11100026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11100026.value: 甲基轉移酶M. Fcohsdm在柱狀黃桿菌毒力中的作用解析及其作為新型減毒活疫苗的可行性探究

11100026.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11100026.value: Prof FU, Bing Prof Zhu, Yongtao

11100026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11100026.value: Flavobacterium columnare is a devastating bacterial pathogen in global aquaculture, responsible for columnaris disease and causing substantial economic losses that threaten sustainable aquaculture development. While bacterial DNA methyltransferases are increasingly recognized as key epigenetic regulators of virulence, their specific functions in F. columnare pathogenesis remain entirely unexplored. In a previous study, we constructed a targeted knockout of a specific Type I methyltransferase (M. Fcohsdm) in F. columnare, and the knockout mutant completely attenuated virulence without impairing growth. Our preliminary RNA-seq data directly link this attenuation to a significant downregulation of the Type VI Secretion System (T6SS), a key virulence apparatus. This mutant provides a unique opportunity to investigate the mechanistic link between MTase function and bacterial pathogenicity. The core objectives of this proposal are to: 1) Identify the mechanism by which MTase knockout dysregulates the T6SS and virulence factors using genetic, bioinformatic and proteomic analyses; 2) Characterize the spatial and temporal dynamics of the MTase activity using the single-molecular super-resolution imaging technique, and 3) Evaluate the immunological potential of this mutant as a modified live vaccine candidate. Our work will reveal how epigenetic modification orchestrates virulence in aquatic bacteria and open a potential transformative new avenue for live attenuated vaccine development through targeted MTase manipulation in aquaculture. 柱狀黃桿菌（Flavobacterium columnare）是全球水產養殖業中一種可引起柱狀病的細菌病原體，其可以造成重大的經濟損失，威脅水產養殖的可持續發展。儘管細菌DNA甲基轉移酶日益被認為是毒力調控的關鍵表觀遺傳因子，但其在柱狀黃桿菌致病機制中的具體功能至今仍未被探索。在前期研究中，我們建構了柱狀黃桿菌中一種特異性 I 型甲基轉移酶（M. Fcohsdm）的定向敲除株，該敲除突變株在不影響生長的情況下完全喪失了毒力。我們的初步RNA-seq數據將此減弱效應直接與VI型分泌系統（T6SS）的顯著下調聯繫起來。該突變株為我們研究甲基轉移酶功能與細菌致病性之間的關聯機制提供了獨特的機會。本申请的核心目标是：1）利用遺傳學、生物資訊學和蛋白質體學分析，解析甲基轉移酶敲除導致 T6SS 及毒力因子失調的機制；2）利用單分子超分辨成像技術，解析甲基轉移酶活性在不同環境影響下的時空動態；3）評估該突變株作為改良型活疫苗候選株的免疫學潛力。我們的工作將揭示表觀遺傳修飾如何調控水生病原菌的毒力，並為透過靶向甲基轉移酶操控開發水產養殖減毒活疫苗開闢一條新途徑。

11100126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11100126.value: 基于G-四链体结构介导的转录后基因调控的L-RNA适配体修饰寡核苷酸的理性设计

11100126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11100126.value: G-quadruplexes (G4s) are four-stranded nucleic acid structures that have been reported in humans and other species. Accumulating data have indicated that they have significant roles in many biological events, including transcription and translation. Emerging studies also highlighted their potential as promising targets for therapeutic interventions. Despite this progress, significant gaps remain in our understanding of the precise targeting of G4 structures and the subsequent regulatory effects on gene activity. To address these issues, developing innovative platforms and tools—particularly with the ability to recognize G4 in the gene/transcript of interest, as well as to investigate the impact of the G4 targeting tool on gene function—are two primary areas for further revealing new G4 biology and developing innovative strategies for exploiting G4s in disease treatment. Our group has an excellent track record and a long-term interest in studying G4 targeting and biology using interdisciplinary strategies. Over the last few years, we have developed novel technologies to investigate the formation and function of G4s, one of which is L-RNA aptamers. These L-aptamers can be further modified with other molecular moieties to enhance the function and performance of the L-RNA aptamer-based tools. Building on our recent work, we will develop novel, non-G4-containing L-RNA aptamers, assess their secondary structures, and evaluate their performance regarding G4 target affinity and selectivity. Moreover, we will design a robust chemical ligation strategy and examine the effects of antisense oligonucleotide length and modifications on the binding and biostability properties of L-RNA aptamer–oligonucleotide conjugates. Finally, we will study the impact of optimized L-RNA aptamer – modified oligonucleotide conjugates on controlling G4-mediated post-transcriptional gene activity in multiple cell lines and under different cellular conditions. Our lab possesses the necessary instruments and capabilities to conduct the research outlined in this proposal. The original methods and L-RNA aptamer–modified antisense oligonucleotide tools developed in this study have great potential for patent filing. Using the cancer-related BCL2 rG4 target, we have demonstrated the feasibility of generating a non-G4-containing L-RNA aptamer and the robustness of the L-aptamer–D-oligonucleotide conjugation platform. The pilot experiments on the developed L-RNA aptamer–modified oligonucleotide tools are promising. We are optimistic that the deliverables from this project will have a significant impact on the advancement of gene regulation via precise rG4 targeting, as well as improve our understanding of rG4 function in biology and disease. G-四链体（G4）是在人类及其他物种中广泛存在的四股核酸结构，被证明在包括转录与翻译在内的多种生物学过程中发挥重要作用。越来越多的研究也表明，G4结构是具有潜力的治疗干预靶点。尽管相关研究已取得重要进展，但关于如何精确地靶向特定G4结构以及其对基因活性所产生的后续调控效应，我们仍然知之甚少。为解决这些问题，开发具有创新性的研究平台与工具——尤其是能够识别特定基因/转录本中的G4结构，并用于系统研究G4靶向工具对基因功能影响的技术——是进一步揭示G4新生物学功能并将G4用于疾病治疗策略开发的两个关键方向。 本课题组长期致力于利用跨学科策略研究G4靶向和生物学问题，并在相关领域建立了出色的研究基础和成果记录。近年来，我们开发了多种用于研究G4形成与功能的新技术，其中之一便是L-RNA适配体（L-aptamer）。这些L-aptamer还可进一步与其他分子基团进行修饰，从而提升基于L-RNA适配体工具的功能与性能。在我们最新研究工作的基础上，本项目将开发新型的、不含G4结构的L-RNA适配体，系统解析其二级结构，并评估其在G4靶标亲和力与选择性方面的表现。此外，我们将设计一套高效且稳健的化学连接策略，并系统考察反义寡核苷酸长度及其化学修饰对L-RNA适配体–寡核苷酸缀合物结合能力和体内稳定性的影响。最后，我们将研究优化后的L-RNA适配体修饰寡核苷酸缀合物在多种细胞系及不同细胞状态下，对G4介导的转录后基因活性调控的作用。 本实验室已具备完成本研究计划所需的仪器平台与技术能力。本项目拟开发的原创方法与L-RNA适配体修饰反义寡核苷酸工具具备良好的专利申请前景。以与癌症密切相关的BCL2 rG4靶标为例，我们已验证了构建非G4结构的L-RNA适配体的可行性，以及L-aptamer–D-寡核苷酸缀合平台的稳健性。针对已开发的L-RNA适配体修饰寡核苷酸工具，我们的初步实验结果十分令人鼓舞。我们有信心，本项目预期产出的成果将显著推动通过精确靶向rG4实现基因调控的研究进展，并进一步加深对rG4在生物学与疾病发生发展中的功能认识。

11100426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11100426.value: 觀察如何調控動機—替代強化的神經機制

11100426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11100426.value: Vicarious reinforcement, where observing another individual’s reward increases one’s own motivation, provides an efficient mechanism for adaptive behavior. As a cornerstone of social learning theory, vicarious reinforcement has shaped research and practice across psychology, education, marketing and other domains. However, the neural processes underlying the transformation from perception to motivational drive remains poorly understood. Our preliminary study demonstrated robust vicarious reinforcement-like behaviors in mouse, an experimentally tractable model that allows us to dissect the underlying circuit and mechanism. Our pilot work also suggests contributions played by the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) and the anterior insular cortex (aIC), with a potential role of midbrain dopaminergic system linking their activities. In this proposal, we hypothesize that the ACC encodes vicarious outcome signals that engage the midbrain ventral tegmental area (VTA), driving dopamine release in aIC to update motivational state representations and invigorate behavior. Specifically, we aim to 1) define the external and internal factors that modulate vicarious reinforcement in mice; 2) establish the ACC-VTA-aIC pathway as a causal driver of vicarious reinforcement; and 3) determine how dopamine signaling in the aIC updates socially modulated motivational state representation. By integrating quantitative behavioral analysis, circuit dissection, pathway-specific manipulations and machine-learning based analyses of single cell and population-level activities, this project will deliver the first mechanistic account of vicarious reinforcement, shedding light on the neurobiological basis of this powerful learning mechanism. 替代強化（Vicarious reinforcement）是指觀察到他人獲得獎勵時，能提升自身的動機，這為適應性行為提供了一種高效的機制。作為社會學習理論（Social learning theory）的核心基石，替代強化深刻影響了心理學、教育學、行銷學等領域的研究與實踐。然而，從感知轉換為動機驅力的底層神經機制至今仍所知甚少。我們的初步研究展現了小鼠中穩健的類替代強化行為，小鼠作為一種實驗上易於操作的模型，使我們能夠剖析其背後的神經迴路與機制。我們的先導工作亦表明，前扣帶皮層（ACC）和前島葉皮層（aIC）發揮了作用，且中腦多巴胺系統可能在連結這兩者活動中扮演潛在角色。在此計畫中，我們假設 ACC 編碼替代結果訊號以活化中腦腹側蓋膜區（VTA），進而驅動 aIC 釋放多巴胺，以更新動機狀態的表徵並激發行為。具體而言，我們的目標為：1）確定調節小鼠替代強化的外部與內部因素；2）建立 ACC-VTA-aIC 通路作為替代強化的因果驅動因素；3）確定 aIC 中的多巴胺訊號如何更新受社會調控的動機狀態表徵。透過結合定量行為分析、迴路剖析、特異性通路操控，以及基於機器學習的單細胞與群體層級活動分析，本計畫將首次提供替代強化的機制性解釋，揭示這種強大學習機制的生物學基礎。

11100726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11100726.value: 深度學習引導之閉環合成與回收：以廚餘為原料製備全生物基非異氰酸酯聚氨酯

11100726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11100726.value: Polyurethane (PU), accounting for ~5.3% of global plastic output, is a versatile material widely applied in industrial and consumer products owing to its excellent strength, thermal stability, and insulation properties. However, PU production faces three fundamental challenges: (1) reliance on fossil-derived feedstocks, which contribute to climate change and resource depletion; (2) dependence on toxic isocyanates, which pose occupational and environmental hazards; and (3) poor end-of-life degradability and recyclability, leading to the accumulation of persistent plastic waste. Collectively, these challenges drive greenhouse gas emissions, pollution, health risks, and sustainability bottlenecks in polymer manufacturing. Therefore, this project aims to develop an innovative PU framework, namely bio-based non-isocyanate polyurethane (NIPU), to address these limitations through three breakthroughs: (1) 100% bio-based and waste-driven production, realised by valorising food waste (FW) as a sustainable carbon source. As Hong Kong generates over 3,300 tonnes/day of FW, thereby transforming an underutilised waste stream into high-value polymer precursors; (2) isocyanate-free synthesis, achieved by converting FW lipids into five-membered cyclic carbonates (5-CCs) and further reacting with bio-based diamines derived from lysine fermentation and enzymatic decarboxylation; and (3) closed-loop recyclability, enabled by deep-learning-guided enzyme evolution to deliver high-efficiency, thermostable PU-degrading biocatalysts. The proposed project will directly align with Hong Kong’s Product Eco-responsibility (Amendment) Bill 2023 and the Global Plastics Treaty’s 2040 zero-pollution target, addressing urgent needs for sustainable materials and circular waste management. Its feasibility is underpinned by four key advances from the PI’s team: (1) a proven FW lipid valorisation platform, with life-cycle and techno-economic viability for polyols and PU production; (2) a robust catalytic system (TBAB/Zn(II)–Salphen) for efficient FW-lipid-to-5-CCs conversion, coupled with high-yield (≥98%) enzymatic diamine production; (3) the DeepDE framework, which integrates advanced protein language models (e.g., ESMC/ESM3 and eUniRep) with droplet microfluidic high-throughput screening for hyper-efficient enzyme engineering; and (4) pre-identified PU-degrading enzymes (CpCut1, CpEst6) as strong starting points for optimisation. By integrating waste valorisation, synthetic biology, and deep-learning-driven enzyme design, the proposed research will (1) establish the first complete route for 100% bio-based NIPU synthesis; (2) advance state-of-the-art enzyme engineering for plastic degradation; and (3) demonstrate a circular FW-to-NIPU recycling system with validated life-cycle sustainability. This transformative work will deliver breakthroughs in sustainable biomanufacturing, provide new pathways for Hong Kong’s waste-to-resource strategy, and contribute globally to a circular, low-carbon plastics economy. 聚氨酯約佔全球塑膠總產量的5.3%，憑藉其優異的機械強度、熱穩定性及隔熱性能，被廣泛應用於工業製造及日常消費產品。然而，現有聚氨酯的生產與應用仍面臨三項根本性挑戰：(1) 高度依賴化石資源作為原料，不僅加劇氣候變化，亦造成不可再生資源的持續消耗；(2) 製備過程依賴具有高毒性的異氰酸酯，對作業人員健康及環境安全構成重大風險；(3) 產品於使用壽命結束後難以降解及回收，導致大量持久性塑膠廢棄物累積。上述問題共同造成溫室氣體排放增加、環境污染、健康風險及聚合物製造可持續發展的重大瓶頸。 本項目旨在建立一套創新的生物基非異氰酸酯聚氨酯技術體系，透過三項核心突破解決上述挑戰。首先，實現完全生物基及廢棄物驅動的聚氨酯製備，以廚餘作為可持續碳源，將香港每日超過3,300公噸的廚餘轉化為高附加值聚合物前驅物，充分發揮其資源化利用潛力。其次，建立無異氰酸酯合成路徑，將廚餘來源脂質轉化為五元環碳酸酯，並與經賴氨酸發酵及酵素脫羧反應製備的生物基二胺進行聚合，實現完全不依賴異氰酸酯的聚氨酯合成。最後，透過深度學習引導的酵素定向演化策略，開發兼具高催化效率及高熱穩定性的聚氨酯降解酵素，建立聚氨酯材料的閉環回收體系。 本項目將直接配合香港《2023年產品環保責任（修訂）條例草案》以及《全球塑膠公約》於2040年實現零塑膠污染的目標，回應可持續材料及循環資源管理的迫切需求。項目的可行性建立於本研究團隊四項前期研究成果之上：(1) 已建立成熟的廚餘脂質資源化平台，並完成聚醇及聚氨酯製備的生命週期評估及技術經濟分析，證實其技術與經濟可行性；(2) 建立高效率的催化體系，可有效將廚餘脂質轉化，並結合高產率的酵素催化二胺製備技術；(3) 自主開發人工智慧蛋白質演化平台，整合先進蛋白質大型語言模型與液滴微流控高通量篩選技術，實現高效率酵素工程改造； (4) 已鑑定出具良好聚氨酯降解能力的候選酵素，可作為後續深度優化的重要起始模板。 本項目將有機整合廚餘資源化利用、合成生物學及深度學習驅動的酵素設計三大前沿技術，預期實現以下三項突破：(1) 建立全球首個全生物基非異氰酸酯聚氨酯完整製備技術路徑；(2) 推動塑膠降解酵素智慧設計及工程改造技術的發展；(3) 建構並驗證具有生命週期可持續性的廚餘至非異氰酸酯聚氨酯閉環循環利用體系。本研究將為可持續生物製造帶來重要突破，為香港廢棄物資源化策略提供全新技術路徑，並為全球建立低碳、循環型塑膠經濟作出重要貢獻。

11100926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11100926.value: 邁向秀麗隱桿線蟲神經系統的完整生物物理圖譜

11100926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11100926.value: Understanding how the brain gives rise to perception, memory, and behavior remains one of the grand challenges of modern science. Achieving a mechanistic understanding of these processes requires a comprehensive view of the nervous system across all levels of organization—from molecules and neurons to circuits and network behaviors. As an essential step toward this ultimate goal, it is critical to first elucidate and model simpler nervous systems, such as that of the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans. With only 302 neurons and an invariant connectome, C. elegans provides a uniquely tractable system for whole-brain analysis. While the complete wiring diagram of its nervous system has been mapped, the absence of detailed biophysical data describing the intrinsic properties and activity dynamics of individual neuron types has prevented the construction of a unifying, mechanistic model of the worm’s neural function. This project aims to fill this critical gap by systematically characterizing the biophysical properties of all C. elegans neuron types and developing accurate mathematical models to simulate their activity. Specifically, we will record from all 106 somatic neuron types using electrophysiological approaches to obtain detailed parameters describing their electrical properties and firing dynamics. These data will be curated into a comprehensive database forming the foundation of a “biophysical atlas” of the C. elegans nervous system. Our preliminary work has already generated electrophysiological recordings for approximately 50% of all neuron types, revealing an unexpected diversity in intrinsic properties and computational functions. These findings demonstrate both the feasibility and scientific value of establishing a complete biophysical atlas of the C. elegans nervous system. Building on this foundation, we will construct conductance-based single-neuron models and integrate them into connectome-informed circuit frameworks to generate anatomically correct and biophysically accurate neural system models. This proposal represents a proof-of-principle effort to assess how biophysically detailed single-neuron models contribute to full-scale simulations of neural dynamics. The results will provide insight into the appropriate levels of abstraction required for whole-system modeling and establish a scalable framework for understanding more complex nervous systems. Ultimately, the knowledge gained from this project will advance our ability to link neural biophysics to emergent behavior, bringing us closer to a mechanistic understanding of brain function. 理解大腦如何產生知覺、記憶與行為，仍是現代科學的重大挑戰之一。要對這些過程取得機制層面的理解，必須從分子、神經元，以至神經迴路與網絡行為等各個組織層次，建立對神經系統的全面認識。作為邁向此終極目標的關鍵一步，我們必須先闡明並建立較簡單神經系統的模型，例如線蟲秀麗隱桿線蟲（Caenorhabditis elegans）的神經系統。該物種僅有 302 個神經元，且具備恆定不變的神經連接組（connectome），因而成為進行全腦分析的獨特而可行的模式系統。雖然其神經系統的完整連線圖已經繪製完成，但由於缺乏描述各類神經元內在特性及活動動態的詳細生物物理數據，至今仍無法建構出統一且具機制解釋力的線蟲神經功能模型。 本計劃旨在填補這一關鍵空白：系統性地描繪秀麗隱桿線蟲所有神經元類型的生物物理特性，並發展精確的數學模型以模擬其活動。具體而言，我們將以電生理學方法記錄全部 106 類體神經元（somatic neuron types），以取得描述其電學特性與放電動態的詳細參數。這些數據將整理成一個綜合資料庫，構成秀麗隱桿線蟲神經系統「生物物理圖譜」的基礎。 我們的前期研究已完成約 50% 神經元類型的電生理記錄，揭示其內在特性與運算功能具有出乎意料的多樣性。這些結果既證明了建立完整生物物理圖譜的可行性，亦彰顯其科學價值。在此基礎上，我們將建構基於電導（conductance-based）的單一神經元模型，並將其整合至以連接組為依據的迴路架構中，從而產生在解剖結構上正確、在生物物理層面上準確的神經系統模型。 本計劃書代表一項原理驗證（proof-of-principle）研究，用以評估具生物物理細節的單一神經元模型，如何有助於神經動態的全尺度模擬。研究結果將闡明全系統建模所需的適當抽象層次，並確立一個可延展的框架，以理解更為複雜的神經系統。最終，本計劃所獲得的知識將提升我們把神經生物物理特性與湧現行為相連結的能力，使我們更接近對大腦功能的機制性理解。

11101626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11101626.value: 双重Ca²⁺传感器调控突触传递的机制解析

11101626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11101626.value: At presynaptic nerve terminals, synaptic vesicles (SVs) undergo docking, priming, and exocytosis to release neurotransmitters. Since Katz and colleagues first revealed that Ca²⁺ triggers neurotransmitter release through ultrafast SV exocytosis, studies have been focusing on the roles of synaptotagmin proteins (Syts) in synaptic transmission. Structural, biochemical, and functional analyses have demonstrated that synaptic transmission at mammalian central synapses is mediated by a dual Ca²⁺ sensor system, consisting of two Syt isoforms, Syt1 and Syt7, which serve as primary and secondary Ca²⁺ sensors promoting synchronous and asynchronous release. These sensors exhibit distinct characteristics, including differences in Ca²⁺ binding affinity and synaptic localization. Despite advances in understanding Syt1 and Syt7, the mechanisms by which they regulate synaptic transmission remain enigmatic. Recent observations of the Syt1-SNARE crystal structure have revealed critical interactions between the Syt1 C2B domain and SNARE proteins, such as syntaxin and SNAP25. These findings have significantly advanced our understanding of Syt1's mechanism of action while raising new questions: Is SNARE interaction critical for both primary and secondary Ca²⁺ sensors? Do they engage other regulatory mechanisms? Are these mechanisms evolutionarily conserved? What underlies their distinct functional contributions in neurotransmission? We aim to address these key questions by utilizing the nematode C. elegans as a genetic model organism. In C. elegans, synaptic transmission is similarly regulated by a dual Ca²⁺ sensor system comprising SNT-1 (the worm homolog of Syt1) and SNT-3. Our previous work has demonstrated that SNT-1 and SNT-3 function as the primary and secondary Ca²⁺ sensors, respectively, triggering evoked fast and slow release at the neuromuscular junction synapses. Notably, the SNT-1/SNT-3 system mirrors the mammalian Syt1/Syt7 system in critical aspects, including differential synaptic localization, redundant roles in SV priming, and specific coordination during neurotransmitter release. Moreover, predicted models of SNT-1-SNARE and SNT-3-SNARE interactions by AlphaFold 3 closely resemble the primary binding interfaces observed in recent crystallographic studies of the Syt1-SNARE complex. These shared features establish C. elegans as a powerful model for dissecting evolutionarily conserved mechanisms of synaptotagmin-mediated synaptic transmission. In this project, we will integrate in vivo electrophysiology, synaptic imaging, genetics, electron microscopy, biochemistry, and behavioral approaches to investigate these questions. Our research will elucidate both conserved and divergent mechanisms by which dual Ca²⁺ sensors regulate synaptic transmission, providing valuable insights into nervous system function. 在突触前神经末梢，突触囊泡（synaptic vesicles，SVs）依次经历停泊、预备和胞吐过程，从而释放神经递质。自Katz及其同事首次揭示Ca²⁺通过触发超快速突触囊泡胞吐介导神经递质释放以来，突触结合蛋白（synaptotagmins，Syts）在突触传递中的作用一直是该领域的研究重点。结构、生化和功能研究表明，哺乳动物中枢突触的突触传递由双Ca²⁺传感器系统介导。该系统由Syt1和Syt7两种Syt亚型组成，二者分别作为主要和次级Ca²⁺传感器，促进同步释放和异步释放。这两种传感器具有不同的特性，包括Ca²⁺结合亲和力和突触定位方面的差异。尽管我们对Syt1和Syt7的认识已取得重要进展，但它们调控突触传递的具体机制仍不清楚。近期对Syt1–SNARE复合物晶体结构的解析揭示了Syt1的C2B结构域与syntaxin、SNAP25等SNARE蛋白之间的关键相互作用。这些发现显著推进了我们对Syt1作用机制的理解，同时也提出了一系列新的问题：SNARE相互作用是否对主要和次级Ca²⁺传感器均至关重要？它们是否还通过其他调控机制发挥作用？这些机制在进化过程中是否保守？两种Ca²⁺传感器在神经递质释放中承担不同功能的机制基础是什么？ 本项目拟利用模式生物秀丽隐杆线虫（Caenorhabditis elegans）回答上述关键问题。在秀丽隐杆线虫中，突触传递同样受到由SNT-1（Syt1的线虫同源蛋白）和SNT-3组成的双Ca²⁺传感器系统调控。我们此前的研究表明，SNT-1和SNT-3分别作为主要和次级Ca²⁺传感器，在神经肌肉接头突触处触发诱发性快速释放和慢速释放。值得注意的是，SNT-1/SNT-3系统在多个关键方面与哺乳动物Syt1/Syt7系统高度相似，包括不同的突触定位、在突触囊泡预备过程中的功能冗余，以及在神经递质释放过程中的特异性协同作用。此外，AlphaFold 3预测的SNT-1–SNARE和SNT-3–SNARE相互作用模型，与近期Syt1–SNARE复合物晶体结构研究中观察到的主要结合界面高度相似。这些共同特征表明，秀丽隐杆线虫是解析突触结合蛋白介导的突触传递进化保守机制的有力模型。 在本项目中，我们将综合运用在体电生理、突触成像、遗传学、电子显微镜、生物化学和行为学等研究方法，系统探究上述科学问题。本研究将阐明双Ca²⁺传感器调控突触传递的保守机制和分化机制，为深入理解神经系统功能提供重要依据。

11102226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11102226.value: 內皮細胞CD93是一種新型機械敏感性炎症介質及防治動脈粥樣硬化的潛在治療靶點

11102226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11102226.value: Prof Huang, Yu Prof Yiu, Kai Hang

11102226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11102226.value: Atherosclerosis, a chronic inflammatory disease of the arterial wall, remains a leading cause of cardiovascular mortality worldwide. Its pathogenesis begins with endothelial dysfunction triggered by atherogenic stimuli, particularly disturbed blood flow and dyslipidemia. Hemodynamic forces exert profound influences on endothelial phenotypes. Oscillatory shear stress in atheroprone regions promotes endothelial activation and inflammation, while laminar shear stress in protected areas maintains endothelial quiescence. Elucidating the molecular mechanisms by which endothelial cells sense and transduce these biomechanical signals may reveal novel therapeutic targets for the prevention and treatment of atherosclerosis. CD93, a transmembrane glycoprotein which is highly expressed in endothelial cells, macrophages, and monocytes, has been implicated in the immune regulation, efferocytosis, and lipid metabolism. Our preliminary multi-omics analysis reveals that CD93 expression is increased in aortic endothelium and plasma of high cholesterol diet-fed ApoE⁻/⁻ mice and correlates with atherosclerosis severity. scRNA-seq identifies CD93-enriched endothelial subclusters with pro-inflammatory signatures. Elevated CD93 is confirmed in mouse and human atherosclerotic vessels, and in plasma from atherosclerotic patients. Notably, CD93 activates the pro-inflammatory YAP/TAZ signaling pathway, promoting endothelial activation and leukocyte adhesion, critical early events in atherogenesis. In vitro, CD93 knockdown suppresses inflammation and monocyte adhesion. In vivo, endothelium-specific CD93 deficiency markedly reduces inflammation and plaque formation in atherogenic mice, thereby supporting its pathogenic role. Mechanistically, CD93 expression is elevated in atheroprone regions and by oscillatory shear stress, while suppressed by KLF2 via direct promoter binding. Based on these promising preliminary findings, we hypothesize that CD93 is a mechanosensitive regulator of endothelial inflammation and a promising biomarker for atherosclerosis. We will test this central hypothesis through three interconnected objectives: (1) To investigate the role of endothelial CD93 in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis. (2) To investigate the mechanisms underlying CD93-induced inflammatory responses in endothelial cells. (3) To define the KLF2-dependent transcriptional mechanism by which oscillatory shear stress upregulates endothelial CD93. We will assess the therapeutic potential of CD93 neutralizing antibodies to inhibit vascular inflammation and plaque progression and evaluate whether circulating soluble CD93 could act as an early diagnostic biomarker for atherosclerotic vascular disease. By illustrating the role of CD93 in translating mechanical stress into vascular inflammation, this study shall deepen our understanding of the critical pathological role of endothelial dysfunction in atherosclerosis and provides scientific basis for the development of novel therapies targeting CD93 to combat atherosclerosis and related cardiovascular disorders, ultimately advancing public health outcomes. 動脈粥樣硬化是一種以慢性血管壁炎症為特徵的疾病，至今仍是全球心血管疾病致死的首要原因。其病理進程始於血管內皮功能障礙，主要由致動脈粥樣硬化性刺激因素（如異常血流動力學與血脂紊亂）所誘發。血流動力學作用對內皮細胞表型具有深遠影響：在易損血管區域，振盪剪切力促進內皮活化與炎症反應；而在保護性區域，層流剪切力則有助於維持內皮靜息狀態。因此，釐清內皮細胞感知與轉導生物力學信號的分子機制，有望為動脈粥樣硬化的預防與治療發掘新穎靶點。 CD93為一型跨膜糖蛋白，高度表現於內皮細胞、巨噬細胞及單核細胞，涉及免疫調控、凋亡細胞清除及脂質代謝等過程。我們前期多組學分析發現，高膽固醇飲食餵養之 ApoE⁻/⁻ 小鼠的主動脈內皮與血漿中 CD93 表达量均上升，且與病變嚴重度呈正相關。單細胞RN 测序進一步鉴定出一個具促炎特徵的CD93⁺內皮細胞亞群。我們亦證實，在小鼠及人類動脈粥樣硬化血管組織，以及患者血漿中，CD93水平皆顯著升高。 值得注意的是，CD93可活化促炎性 YAP/TAZ 信號通路，進而促進內皮細胞活化及白細胞黏附，此乃動脈粥樣硬化早期關鍵事件。體外實驗中，降低CD93表達可抑制炎症反應及單核細胞黏附；體內內皮細胞特異性敲低CD93，則能顯著減輕致動脈粥樣硬化小鼠的血管炎症與斑塊形成，支持CD93在疾病進程中的致病角色。機制層面，CD93 於易損血管區域表現上調，且受振盪剪切力誘導；另一方面，轉錄因子KLF2 可透過直接結合 CD93 啟動子而抑制其轉錄。 基於上述前瞻性結果，我們提出核心假說：CD93 為一機械敏感性調控因子，可促进內皮炎症反應，並可能作為動脈粥樣硬化之潛在生物標誌物。為驗證此假說，我們擬定三項相互關聯的研究目標： 1. 探討內皮細胞CD93在動脈粥樣硬化發病機制中的功能角色； 2. 闡明 CD93 誘導內皮炎症反應的分子機制； 3. 解析振盪剪切力如何經由KLF2依賴性轉錄調控上調內皮CD93表現。 此外，我們將評估CD93中和抗體抑制血管炎症與斑塊進展的治療潛力，並探討循環可溶性CD93是否可作為動脈粥樣硬化性血管疾病的早期診斷生物標誌物。 綜合而言，本研究將揭示CD93如何將機械應力轉化為血管炎症信號，深化對內皮功能障礙在動脈粥樣硬化病理中核心地位的認識，並為開發以CD93為標靶的新型防治策略提供科學依據，最終促進心血管健康與公共衛生。

11102426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11102426.value: 慢性腎臟病相關骨丟失中新型炎症物質的機制研究

11102426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11102426.value: The aim of this project is to determine the functions of fibrotic kidney derived Fstl1 in Chronic kidney Disease (CKD) associated bone loss. CKD affects 16% of the global population and is invariably associated with a debilitating skeletal complication, CKD-Mineral and Bone Disorder (CKD-MBD), which markedly increases fracture risk and mortality. A critical limitation in current treatment is that osteoporosis drugs are either contraindicated or unsafe in CKD patients due to adverse renal effects such as bisphosphonate accumulation or severe hypocalcemia by denosumab. There is a dire need for therapies that target the unique pathophysiology of CKD-MBD without compromising renal function. Our preliminary work identifies the inflammatory glycoprotein Follistatin-like 1 (Fstl1) as a key signal secreted by fibrotic kidneys that directly disrupts bone remodeling. We have demonstrated that Fstl1 is upregulated in CKD, inhibits osteoblast differentiation but promotes osteoclastogenesis, and that its neutralization ameliorates renal fibrosis as well as osteoblast differentiation inhibition. Based on these observations, we propose to study in details the functions of Fstl1 in bone remodeling, the cellular and molecular mechanisms on how Fstl1 disrupts bone homeostasis in CKD and its direct and causal role in driving CKD bone loss. This proposal aims to provide direct in vivo causal evidence that bone being a key target of kidney fibroblast derived Fstl1, which contributes to CKD associated bone loss. The long term goal of this project seeks to establish bone specific inhibition of Fstl1 as a safe, effective, and targeted therapeutic paradigm for CKD-MBD. The central hypothesis is that fibrotic kidney-derived Fstl1 is the main inflammatory factor driving bone loss during CKD. The hypothesis will be tested by pursuing the following aims: 1) To define the functions of Fstl1 in bone remodelling 2) To elucidate the cellular and molecular mechanisms by which Fstl1 disrupts bone homeostasis in CKD 3) To investigate the direct and causal role of fibrotic kidney-derived Fstl1 in driving osteoporosis The proposed research is significant because it is expected to advance the mechanistic understanding of the kidney-bone axis. The knowledge will aid the development of novel therapeutic strategy for chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder. 慢性腎臟病（CKD）影響著全球16%的人口，且必然伴隨一種令人衰弱的骨骼併發症——慢性腎臟病-礦物質與骨代謝異常（CKD-MBD），後者顯著增加骨折風險及死亡率。當前治療的一大關鍵局限在於，骨質酥鬆症藥物在CKD患者中要麼存在禁忌，要麼因對腎臟產生不良影響而安全性欠佳，例如雙膦酸鹽可在體內蓄積，地舒單抗則可誘發嚴重低鈣血症。因此，亟需開發能夠針對CKD-MBD獨特病理生理機制且不損害腎功能的干預策略。我們的前期研究表明，纖維化腎臟分泌的關鍵信號分子，可直接干擾骨重塑。我們已證實，關鍵信號分子在CKD中表達上調，既可抑製成骨細胞分化，又可促進破骨細胞生成；而中和關鍵信號分子不僅可改善腎纖維化，還能減輕對成骨細胞分化的抑制。基於上述發現，我們擬深入探究關鍵信號分子在骨重塑中的功能，闡明其在CKD狀態下擾亂骨穩態的細胞與分子機制，並明確其在驅動CKD骨丟失中的直接致病作用。

11102626.value: 氧感應羥脯氨酸調控丁香假單胞菌的毒力

11102626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11102626.value: Pseudomonas syringae is a globally important gram-negative plant pathogen. P. syringae uses its type III secretion system (T3SS) to drive host invasion and disease. However, how host-derived signals are sensed and are routed to T3SS regulators remains unclear. Building on extensive work defining RhpRS as a central switch, we have recently revealed a novel hydroxyproline (hyp) modification at Pro89 in the RhpS HAMP domain, which is elevated in minimal medium but suppressed by hypoxia. We hypothesise that a conserved prolyl hydroxylase (ProH) catalyzes this modification to repress rhpR and activate T3SS and motility gene expression, while limiting biofilm expression. Based on these preliminary results, we propose a novel signaling pathway of ProH–Hyp–RhpRS–virulence, whose verification is the focus of the proposal. Genetic and biochemical characterizations of this novel signaling pathway is the first step toward identifying signals to which the T3SS responds, and toward the development of new strategies for disease control based on T3SS manipulation. Our long-term goal is to leverage the outcomes of the herein proposed studies to develop better therapies against P. syringae infection. 丁香假單胞菌是一種在全球範圍內具有重要影響的革蘭氏陰性植物病原菌。該菌透過Ⅲ型分泌系統（T3SS）介導宿主侵染並引發疾病。然而，宿主來源信號如何被感知並傳遞至T3SS調控因子，仍尚不明確。在既往大量研究確立 RhpRS 為核心調控開關的基礎上，我們近期發現：RhpS 的 HAMP 結構域中第89位脯氨酸（Pro89）存在一種新型羥脯氨酸（hydroxyproline，Hyp）修飾。該修飾在 MM 培養基中水平升高，但在低氧條件下受到抑制。我們推測，一種保守的脯氨醯羥化酶（ProH）催化這一修飾，從而抑制 rhpR 的表達，並活化 T3SS 及運動性相關基因的表達，同時限制生物被膜相關基因的表達。基於上述初步結果，我們提出了一條新的信號通路：ProH–Hyp–RhpRS–毒力。本研究擬重點驗證該信號通路。 對這一新型信號通路開展遺傳學和生物化學表徵，將是鑑定 T3SS 響應信號的第一步，也將為基於 T3SS 調控開發植物病害防控新策略奠定基礎。我們的長期目標是利用本研究的成果，開發更有效的防治丁香假單胞菌感染的方法。

11103126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11103126.value: 內皮細胞解偶聯蛋白2保護缺血性腦中風小鼠的血腦屏障完整性

11103126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11103126.value: Dr HE, Lei Dr Ip, Bonaventure Yiu-ming Prof Ko, Ho

11103126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11103126.value: Ischemic stroke remains a leading cause of death and disability worldwide, with limited treatment options focused on vascular protection. A pivotal early event is blood-brain barrier (BBB) breakdown, which exacerbates cerebral injury by driving inflammation and neuronal damage; however, no therapies exist to directly stabilize the BBB. Through a bioinformatic analysis of a public single-cell RNA-seq dataset, we made a critical observation: uncoupling protein 2 (UCP2), a key mitochondrial vasoprotective molecule, is profoundly downregulated in brain vascular endothelial cells following experimental stroke. This UCP2 suppression strongly correlated with the loss of tight junction proteins, revealing a novel and potentially causal link to BBB dysfunction. Building on our prior work showing that glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) elevating agents upregulate vascular UCP2, we hypothesize that GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) protect the BBB after ischemic stroke by restoring endothelial UCP2 expression and function. This project will systematically test this hypothesis with three specific objectives: 1. To establish the causal role of endothelial UCP2 in stroke pathogenesis using inducible, endothelial-specific UCP2 knockout mice subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion. 2. To decipher the mechanistic pathway by which UCP2 preserves BBB integrity, with a focus on mitochondrial reactive oxygen species signaling and its impact on tight junction protein dynamics. 3. To validate UCP2-dependent therapeutic efficacy of GLP-1RAs in preserving BBB integrity and promoting functional recovery post-stroke. This research will definitively position endothelial UCP2 as a critical regulator of cerebrovascular health after ischemia. By delineating a novel GLP-1/UCP2 protective axis, our work will provide a robust preclinical rationale for the rapid repurposing of already-approved GLP-1RAs as a novel vascular-protective therapy to improve outcomes for ischemic stroke patients. 缺血性中風仍為全球致死及致殘之主因，現行治療方案有限，且主要集中於血管保護層面。血腦屏障（BBB）破壞乃關鍵早期病變，可觸發炎症反應及神經元損傷，進而加劇腦部損害；惟目前尚無直接穩定血腦屏障的療法。 本團隊透過生物信息學分析單細胞RNA测序公共數據庫，獲得一項重要發現：線粒體關鍵血管保護分子解偶聯蛋白2（UCP2）在實驗小鼠中風後的腦血管內皮細胞中顯著下調。UCP2表達抑制與緊密連接蛋白流失呈高度相關，揭示其與血腦屏障功能障礙間可能存在因果關聯。 基於本團隊前期研究證實胰高血糖素樣肽-1（GLP-1）激動劑可上調血管UCP2表達，本研究提出假說：GLP-1受體激動劑（GLP1RAs）可透過恢復內皮細胞UCP2的表達與功能，於缺血性中風後發揮血腦屏障保護作用。 本項目將透過以下三項具體目標，系統性驗證上述假說： 1. 利用可誘導型內皮細胞特異性UCP2基因敲除小鼠，建立大腦中動脈閉塞模型，確立內皮UCP2在中風病理機制中之因果作用。 2. 闡明UCP2維持血腦屏障完整性的分子機制，重點探討線粒體活性氧信號傳導及其對緊密連接蛋白動態變化的影響。 3. 驗證GLP-1RAs是否透過UCP2依賴途徑，發揮保護血腦屏障及促進中風後功能恢復之療效。 本研究將明確界定內皮UCP2為缺血後腦血管健康之關鍵調控因子。透過揭示全新GLP-1/UCP2保護軸，本項目將為已獲批准之GLP-1RAs藥物重新定位為新型血管保護療法，提供堅實的臨床前依據，以期改善缺血性中風患者的預後。

11103226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11103226.value: 基於電腦視覺的奶牛熱應激相關行為變化特徵分析

11103226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11103226.value: Prof Kenez, Akos Prof LIU, Kai

11103226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11103226.value: Heat stress is a significant challenge faced by the global dairy industry as it impacts animal welfare, health and productivity. These impacts are becoming more widespread as dairy farming expands in Asia, but there is limited research examining heat stress in tropical and subtropical climates. Although numerous methods are used to detect heat stress in cattle, ranging from environmental measures to animal-based assessments, no definitive method has emerged for monitoring dairy cattle thermal status. Computer vision (CV) methods such as multi-object tracking (MOT) algorithms have great potential for use in livestock monitoring as they enable comprehensive identity-linked behaviour analysis with simultaneous tracking of multiple animals in complex environments. However, at present they are underutilized in livestock farming, with most models tested on benchmark datasets of pedestrians or vehicles. Objective 1 of this research will quantify the environmental conditions under which heat stress develops in high-producing dairy cattle in Hong Kong to improve our understanding of heat stress in dairy cattle in the wider Greater Bay Area and Asia. To do this, we will install state-of-the art environmental monitors to collect detailed microclimate data year-round. We will determine heat stress in the cattle based on routine clinical assessments (e.g., rectal temperature, respiratory rate, behaviours), further validated by physiological parameters from serum and faecal samples (e.g., insulin, interleukin 1β), and use these parameters to confirm metabolic impacts of heat stress and evaluate its severity. Objective 2 will characterize behaviours and space use patterns of cattle with and without heat stress using CV techniques to improve on-farm monitoring efficiency in a non-invasive and novel manner. We will continuously record cattle behaviours using pre-installed high-performance cameras during periods of heat stress and in thermoneutral environments. Using CV techniques, we will annotate datasets at individual and herd-level, training a strong backbone using unsupervised learning models with unlabelled data, and identifying specific cattle behaviours (e.g., lying, standing, feeding, brush-use) and spatial usage. As proof of concept, we successfully established spatial location of cattle using triangulation and bundle adjustment of their visible dorsal keypoints in an existing dataset, showing our method is feasible and generalizable. Ultimately, we will create the largest multi-camera tracking dataset in precision livestock farming and facilitate automated behaviour recognition for informed decisions to optimise cattle management under heat stress. 熱應激是全球乳業面臨的壹項重大挑戰，它會影響奶牛的健康狀況、生產性能以及動物福利。隨著乳業養殖在亞洲持續擴張，這些影響也日益普遍。然而，目前針對熱帶與亞熱帶氣候條件下奶牛熱應激的研究仍相對有限。盡管現有用於檢測奶牛熱應激的方法多種多樣，涵蓋從環境監測到動物本體評估等多種途徑，但目前尚未形成壹種能夠對奶牛熱狀態進行明確、可靠監測的“確定性”方法。計算機視覺方法（如多目標跟蹤）在畜牧業監測中具有巨大的應用潛力：它們能夠在復雜環境中同時對多只動物進行跟蹤，從而實現基於個體身份的連續、系統化行為分析。目前這類方法在實際畜牧生產中的應用仍不夠充分，多數模型主要在行人或車輛等基準數據集上完成驗證。 本研究的目標壹是量化香港高產奶牛發生熱應激時對應的環境條件，以加深對大灣區乃至亞洲範圍內奶牛熱應激的理解。為此，我們將安裝先進的環境監測設備，全年連續采集精細的微氣候數據。熱應激判定將基於常規臨床評估，包括直腸溫度、呼吸頻率與行為表現等指標，並進壹步通過血清與糞便樣本中的生理參數進行驗證（例如胰島素、白細胞介素1β等）。這些指標將用於確認熱應激引起的代謝影響，並評估熱應激的嚴重程度。 目標二將利用計算機視覺技術刻畫處於熱應激與熱中性狀態下奶牛的行為特征及空間使用模式，從而以非侵入且創新的方式提升農場端監測效率。我們將在熱應激期間及熱中性環境中，利用預先安裝的高性能攝像機對奶牛行為進行連續記錄。隨後，我們將對數據進行個體與群體層面的標註：在利用未標註數據的基礎上，通過無監督學習訓練強大的“骨幹”特征提取網絡，並識別特定行為（例如臥躺、站立、采食、刷撓鱷擦拭用具等）以及空間活動分布。作為概念驗證，我們已在現有數據集中采用三角測量與束調整方法，實現對奶牛可見背部關鍵點的定位，從而證明該方案具有可行性並具備良好的泛化能力。最終，我們將構建精密畜牧業中規模最大的多攝像機跟蹤數據集，並推動自動化行為識別，為熱應激條件下的科學管理決策提供支持，從而進壹步優化奶牛的飼養管理。

11103426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11103426.value: 微塑膠及其相關化學物質對鰓組織細胞與分子效應的解耦機制研究

11103426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11103426.value: Micro and nanoplastics (MNPs) have become defining environmental contaminants of the Anthropocene, functioning not only as persistent physical pollutants but also as dynamic vectors for tens of thousands of synthetic and natural chemicals in aquatic ecosystems. These small plastic particles, typically less than 5 mm in size, readily adsorb and transport additives and pollutants such as plasticizers, phthalates, metals, pesticides, and persistent organic pollutants, creating complex particle–chemical mixtures that threaten aquatic organisms, food safety, and ecosystem stability. Despite their ubiquity, our mechanistic understanding of how such mixtures become bioavailable, how aquatic species sense and internalize them, and how chemical and particle stressors interact at the cellular level remains critically limited, representing a major frontier in environmental toxicology and ecological risk assessment. This project aims to disentangle particle mediated and chemical specific effects of MNPs by integrating environmentally realistic exposure experiments with state of the art cellular and molecular technologies. Using two evolutionarily distant but functionally analogous “sensory gill systems”—the marine oyster Crassostrea hongkongensis and the freshwater zebrafish Danio rerio—we will investigate how MNPs and their associated chemicals of concern (COCs) are taken up, transformed, and sensed at molecular and cellular scales. Building upon our recently established single cell transcriptomic atlases for oyster and fish gills, the study introduces a mechanistic “cradle to cell” framework to examine interactions between particulate and chemical stressors across biological complexity. Task 1 will quantify the bioavailability and bioaccessibility of representative MNP–COC pairs under environmentally relevant conditions to derive kinetic parameters and exposure models. Task 2 will map MNP uptake and chemical specific transcriptional responses in oyster gills using single cell RNA sequencing, supported by histopathology, oxidative stress biomarkers, and functional validation assays. Task 3 will extend these analyses to zebrafish gills to identify conserved and cell type specific pathways, including copper induced redox switching under combined exposures. Collectively, these studies will reveal cellular processes that distinguish mechanical from chemical toxicity, identify molecular biomarkers of MNP and COC exposure, and deliver predictive understanding of mixture effects in aquatic systems. Overall, this project will identify differential responses of gill sensors to specific MNPs and chemicals at the cellular and molecular levels and contribute to safer plastic design, improved environmental monitoring, and evidence based risk assessment essential for protecting aquatic and human health in rapidly changing coastal ecosystems. 微塑膠和纳米塑膠已成為最具代表性的環境污染物之一。 它們不僅是持久性的物理顆粒污染物，也成為水生生態系統中數萬種合成及天然化學物質的動態載體。 雖然微纳米塑膠在環境中廣泛存在，但我們仍缺乏系統性理解這些複合水生生物如何感知與攝取這些顆粒及其相關化學物質，以及顆粒壓力與化學壓力之間細胞尺度互動機制。 本研究旨在系統性地解耦微纳米塑膠對粒子介導及化學特異性的影響，結合環境情境相關暴露實驗與尖端細胞及分子生物學技術。 專注於分析微纳米塑膠及其分子與細胞尺度上的化學吸收、轉化與感知機制。 本研究依據我們近期構建的牡蠣與魚鰓組織單細胞轉錄組圖譜，提出一套從「環境源到細胞命運」的機制框架，系統性地探討不同生物複雜度下顆粒與化學壓力之間的交互作用。 具體而言：任務一將量化代表性微纳米塑膠-化學組合在環境相關濃度條件下的生物利用度與生物可及性，建立動力學參數，並建立暴露模型，以釐清粒子-化學複合物在環境與生物界面上的遷移與轉化過程。 任務二：利用單細胞RNA定序技術，系統性繪製牡蠣鰓組織中微纳米塑膠的攝取途徑及誘導的化學特異性轉錄反應譜，結合組織病理分析、氧化壓力生物標記檢測及功能驗證實驗，以確認關鍵分子途徑的機制。 任務三：擴展上述魚鰓組織研究，以識別跨物種保守途徑及細胞類型特異性反應機制，重點聚焦於銅離子誘導的氧化還原態轉換等關鍵調控過程，尤其在複合暴露條件下。 透過上述多層次、多尺度整合研究，本計畫將系統性揭示細胞過程層級機械毒性與化學毒性的差異機制，鑑定微纳米塑膠及其相關化學暴露的分子生物標記，並建立對水生系統複合污染效應的預測理解框架。 整體而言，本研究旨在釐清鰓感覺系統在細胞及分子層級對各種微纳米塑膠及特定化學物質的差異反應機制，為安全塑膠材料設計、環境監測系統優化及循證風險評估提供理論基礎，進而為快速變化的沿海生態系統中的水生生態安全與人類健康保護提供科學支持。

11104326.value: 闡明間歇性禁食對疼痛緩解與復發背後之神經膠質細胞異質性的影響

11104326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11104326.value: Neuropathic pain, a chronic condition resulting from nervous system disease or damage, leads to long-term allodynia and hyperalgesia, affecting approximately 17% population globally. Despite the protective nature of pain, the insufficient activation of pain-resolving mechanisms underlies this pathological condition. Currently, there are no effective treatments for neuropathic pain, highlighting the need for developing novel therapies. Intermittent fasting(IF)-cycling between periods of eating and not eating- has shown promise in reducing pain both clinically and pre-clinically, with most studies focusing on inflammatory and acute pain. However, the therapeutic efficacy of IF in alleviating neuropathic pain as well as underlying cellular and molecular changes, particularly those related to pain-resolving mechanisms, remain inadequately understood. Our pilot study found that IF-mediated neuropathic pain relief is not sustainable. The maximal analgesic effects were observed during the 3rd IF cycle, followed by complete pain relapses during the 7th IF cycle. Molecularly, we have identified that initial fasting cycles induce the emergence of beneficial microglia clusters, including CD11c+; Igf1+ subsets and neonatal microglia-like subsets, which are potential contributors to pain relief. Functional analysis confirmed that inhibiting microglia Igf1 signaling leads to early pain relapses, which also negatively impacts neonatal microglia-like subsets crucial for reducing inflammation and aiding in spinal repair, implying a potential reliance of neonatal microglia-like populations on Igf1 signaling. Mechanistically, our preliminary investigations suggest that altered astrocyte properties elevate Igfbp2 production, potentially blocking Igf1 proteins extrinsically, compromising their therapeutic effects, and resulting in pain recurrence at the 7th cycle of IF. Based on these preliminary investigations, we propose that IF influences glial heterogeneity and their associated signaling molecules in the dorsal horn, particularly microglia and astrocytes, which modulate pathological conditions, leading to pain resolution or relapses. In this proposed project, we aim to address these hypotheses by achieving the following objectives: 1) Explore changes in glial heterogeneity in response to intermittent fasting-mediated pain resolution and pain relapse; 2) Determine the role of altered microglia in IF-induced pain resolution and pain relapses; 3) Investigate the Igfbp2/Igf 1 signaling interactions between astrocytes and microglia in IF-induced pain resolution and pain relapses. The successful implementation of this project will not only explain how fasting can relieve pain and why its effects are temporary, but will also uncover novel mechanisms that enhance recovery pathways for developing successful therapeutic strategies. 神經病理性疼痛是一種由神經系統疾病或損傷所引起的慢性疾病，會導致長期的觸摸痛覺過敏和痛覺敏感度上升，全球約有17%的人口受到此病症影響。雖然疼痛本身具有保護作用，但在病理狀態下，身體啟動止痛與修復的機制往往不足，因而導致疼痛持續存在。目前尚無有效治療神經病理性疼痛的方法，因此開發新療法極為迫切。 間歇性禁食在臨床與動物實驗中均顯示出調節疼痛敏感度的潛力，但目前多數研究仍集中在發炎性疼痛與急性疼痛上。至於間歇性禁食對於神經病理性疼痛的療效，以及其在細胞與分子層面上所引發的變化，尤其是與疼痛緩解機制相關的部分，目前仍了解有限。 我們的前期研究發現，間歇性禁食所引發的神經病理性疼痛緩解效果並非持久。最大止痛效果出現在第三次禁食週期，但到了第七次禁食週期時，疼痛則完全復發。在分子層面上，我們觀察到初期禁食週期會誘導出現具有保護作用的小膠質細胞亞群，包括Cd11c+;igf1+亞群及類新生兒小膠質細胞亞群，這些細胞可能是促進疼痛緩解的重要角色。功能實驗證實，若抑制小膠質細胞的igf1信號傳導，會導致疼痛提早復發，同時也對類新生兒小膠質細胞亞群產生負面影響，而這些細胞對於減輕發炎及協助脊髓修復至關重要，這顯示類新生兒小膠質細胞可能依賴igf1信號來維持其功能。 在機制方面，我們的初步研究指出，星形膠質細胞的特性改變會增加igfbp2的生成，而igfbp2可能從細胞外部阻斷igf1蛋白的作用，削弱其治療效果，最終導致疼痛在第七次禁食週期時復發。 基於上述初步發現，我們提出以下假說：間歇性禁食會影響脊髓背角中神經膠質細胞的異質性及其相關信號分子，特別是小膠質細胞與星形膠質細胞，進而調節病理狀態，造成疼痛緩解或復發。在本計畫中，我們將針對以下目標進行研究：（一）探討間歇性禁食在疼痛緩解與復發過程中，神經膠質細胞異質性的變化；（二）確認小膠質細胞的改變在間歇性禁食所引發的疼痛緩解與復發中所扮演的角色；（三）探討星形膠質細胞與小膠質細胞之間，經由Igfbp2/igf信號的交互作用，在間歇性禁食引發疼痛緩解與復發中的影響。 本計畫若順利執行，不僅能增進我們對間歇性禁食在疼痛調控上的療效與分子作用機制的了解，也將發掘出有助於促進疼痛修復路徑的新機制，為未來發展有效的治療策略奠定基礎。

11104526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11104526.value: 齒狀回星狀細胞膽囊收縮素訊號調控認知記憶

11104526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11104526.value: Cholecystokinin (CCK), a peptide hormone and neurotransmitter, plays crucial roles in diverse physiological processes, including memory, anxiety and analgesia. It has been well be documented that vagal afferent nerve fibres express the CCK-A receptor. In the brain, CCK is largely found in GABAergic cells (CCK+-GABA) of the dentate gyrus (DG) in the hippocampus, and is involved in the regulation of a wide range of brain functions. Astrocytes are one of most abundant cell types in the brain and express receptors for a variety of transmitters/neuromodulators; they respond to synaptic activity with changes in cytosolic Ca2+ concentration. Investigations have focused on diverse astrocytes functional receptors of neurotransmitters/neuromodulators including glutamate, acetylcholine, adrenaline and adenosine. Despite extensive investigations into neuronal mechanisms, the bidirectional communication between CCK-expressing interneurons and astrocytes in shaping cognitive function remains largely unexplored. To address this previously unexamined question, we investigated whether astrocytic activity and CCK signaling are functionally coupled and interact with neurons within the dentate gyrus to regulate learning and memory. Using adult CCK-Cre mice combined with optogenetics, calcium imaging, pharmacology, and behavioral assays, we investigated astrocyte function in CCK signaling. We demonstrate that optogenetic activation of CCK interneurons in the DG of freely behaving mice increases local endogenous CCK release, triggering astrocytic Ca²⁺ elevations in response to synaptically released CCK. This response was blocked by CCKBR antagonism and absent in mice with astrocyte-specific CCKBR knockdown. Intriguingly, activating non-CCK interneurons in the DG did not evoke astrocytic calcium elevation. Critically, GABAergic- CCK interneuron activation suppressed calcium activity in nearby neurons. Co-application of the GABA transporter 3 (GAT-3) inhibitor partially attenuated this neuronal suppression without affecting astrocytic responses. Antagonists of the PLC/IP3-signaling cascade significantly reduced CCKB receptor-mediated Ca2+ signaling in astrocytes suggesting that astrocytic CCKBRs in the DG are coupled to the Gq-GPCR signaling pathway. Furthermore, in the novel object recognition task, activating CCK interneurons enhanced recognition memory retrieval, whereas CCKBR inhibition impaired it. Finally, selective inhibition of astrocytic CCKBR receptors disrupted memory retrieval. These findings reveal that astrocytic CCK signaling via CCKBR regulates neuronal network activity and mediates memory retrieval, providing a new framework for targeting neuropsychiatric disorders involving CCK dysregulation through a previously unappreciated astrocyte-dependent pathway.

11105126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11105126.value: 基於 Lrp2 條件性敲除小鼠探討視網膜色素上皮在眼球大小控制與近視發展之角色

11105126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11105126.value: Myopia, or nearsightedness, is a widespread visual disorder caused by excessive axial elongation of the eye, leading to refractive errors. High myopia can result in irreversible pathologies such as retinal detachment, glaucoma, and maculopathy, posing significant public health challenges. Despite its prevalence, the biological mechanisms underlying myopia remain poorly understood, particularly the intricate retina-to-sclera signaling cascade that regulates eye size. The retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), a monolayer of epithelial cells critical for retinal homeostasis, is hypothesized to mediate refractive growth signals from the retina to the sclera. However, the detailed molecular mechanism of the RPE’s functions in regulating eye size is not well characterized. This study focuses on low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 2 (LRP2), a transmembrane protein expressed in the RPE. Mutations in LRP2 are associated with Donnai-Barrow syndrome, a condition characterized by extreme myopia, highlighting LRP2’s critical role in restricting excessive eye growth. Using conditional knockout (cko) mouse models, we demonstrate for the first time that Lrp2 continues to function in the adult RPE to restrict eye growth, with Lrp2 cko leading to myopia. Preliminary data suggest that loss of Lrp2 in the RPE triggers scleral remodeling through paracrine signaling, including the upregulation of the myopia-associated gene Wnt7b. Additionally, lens-induced myopia (LIM) experiments reveal that myopic visual input significantly reduces Lrp2 expression in the RPE, suggesting that it may act as a signal integrator in the retina-to-sclera signaling cascade. Building on these findings, this proposal aims to elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which LRP2 regulates eye size post-development and contributes to myopia development. Our central hypothesis is that LRP2 in the RPE responds to retinal signals and relays these signals to the sclera via signaling molecules such as WNT7b. Our objectives are 1) to investigate how retinal-derived signals, such as dopamine, regulate Lrp2 expression via transcription factor SREBP2 in the RPE; 2) to determine whether Wnt7b upregulation downstream of Lrp2 deficiency contributes to myopia; and 3) to characterize scleral responses to RPE-specific Lrp2 deletion, including changes in extracellular matrix (ECM) composition and fibroblast activity. A combination of genetic models, proteomic analyses, single cell transcriptomic analyses, and advanced imaging techniques will be employed to address these objectives. This study will provide critical insights into the role of the RPE in eye size regulation and myopia, potentially identifying novel therapeutic targets for this increasingly prevalent condition. 近視是因眼軸過長導致的常見視力問題，高度近視更可能引發視網膜剝離等嚴重病變，而視網膜色素上皮細胞被認為在調節眼球大小中扮演關鍵角色 。本研究發現 視網膜色素上皮細胞中的 LRP2 蛋白能限制眼球過度生長，若 LRP2 功能缺失會導致近視，且研究指出近視視覺訊號會抑制 LRP2 的表現 。此項研究旨在解析 LRP2 如何調節眼球發育與近視形成，並探討其機制，期望能為近視治療找到新的標靶。

11105326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11105326.value: 增強雷帕黴素治療後阿茲海默症神經液體及分子變化的影像研究

11105326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11105326.value: We will develop an advanced and comprehensive Chemical Exchange Saturation Transfer(CEST) MRI to evaluate neuropathological changes after enhanced rapamycin treatment non-invasively in Alzheimer’s disease(AD). Imaging provides valuable information to reveal whether the patient is suitable to continue the treatment, such as monitoring edema in lecanemab treatment. If we can image the underlying neurofluid and molecular changes beyond the structural changes, we could assess the treatment timely and perhaps could identify patients who are suitable pior to treatments. Challenges in achieving this goal is the lack of non-invasive and comprehensive imaging of multiple molecular and dynamic changes in the brain, especially imaging multiple neuropathological events simultaneously. Here, we propose to develop a non-invasive imaging platform to monitor key molecular events and neurofluid dynamic changes in AD during rapamycin treatment. The goal is to image key hallmarks sensitively and specifically for evaluating AD and therapeutic efficacy, and to provide evidence to monitor enhanced rapamycin treatment outcomes for AD. We hypothesize that multiple CEST contrasts can reveal important molecular and neurofluid characteristics of AD and therapeutic effects upon our enhanced rapamycin treatment simultaneously and independently. Our previous work has shown that CEST can sensitively detect essential neuropathological hallmarks. CEST-DGE can detect abnormal glucose metabolism, hampered CSF clearance in AD and the effects of rapamycin in tumors. Furthermore, CEST-APT, rNOE can detect altered protein in AD, myelin content in multiple sclerosis and AQP4 activity via MISL. These are essential hallmarks in AD pathology. Collectively, our pilot studies suggested that CEST MRI holds strong promises for assessing key AD hallmarks and for evaluating the therapeutic effects of rapamycin in AD. In this study, we will develop an advanced multi-contrast CEST platform to evaluate the treatment efficacy of enhanced rapamycin treatment using our imaging technologies and intranasal drug delivery. By the three objectives:(1)develop and optimize our advanced MRI for imaging AD neuropathology;(2)characterize the key molecular and neurofluid changes in AD(APP/PS1) mouse models with rapamycin treatment;(3)evaluate the delivery-route and optimize dose-dependent efficacy of rapamycin towards AD pathology. We will image AD-related molecular hallmarks and treatment responses across seven groups of mice, including wild-type and AD with and without rapamycin treatment, together with a comparison study of the intranasal administrative route that could enhance the effective dose in the brain. This simultaneous and independent imaging of multiple neuropathology could provide valued information to study the interplay of key hallmarks in AD, potentially enable prognosis in AD. 我們將開發一套先進且全面的化學交換飽和轉移（CEST）磁力共振成像技術，用以在阿茲海默症（AD）中，以非侵入性方式評估經增強性雷帕黴素治療後的神經病理變化。影像能提供重要資訊，以揭示患者是否適合繼續接受治療，例如在樂卡奈單抗治療中監測水腫情況。如果我們能夠在結構變化之外，進一步造影底層的神經流體與分子變化，便能即時評估治療效果，甚至可能在治療前就篩選出適合的患者。實現此目標的挑戰在於缺乏能夠同時且全面地對腦部多種分子與動態變化進行非侵入性造影的方法，尤其是同時成像多種神經病理事件。為此，我們提議開發一套非侵入性造影平台，用於監測阿茲海默症在雷帕黴素治療過程中的關鍵分子事件與神經流體動態變化。本研究的目標是敏感且特異地對關鍵病理特徵進行成像，以評估阿茲海默症及治療效果，並為監測增強性雷帕黴素治療在阿茲海默症中的療效提供證據。 多種CEST對比能同時且獨立地揭示阿茲海默症在經過增強性雷帕黴素治療後的重要分子與神經流體特徵及其治療效應。我們先前的研究已顯示，CEST能夠敏感地檢測到關鍵的神經病理特徵。例如，CEST-DGE可檢測到阿茲海默症中異常的葡萄糖代謝與受損的腦脊髓液清除能力，以及雷帕黴素在腫瘤中的作用。此外，CEST-APT與rNOE可用於檢測阿茲海默症中改變的蛋白質、多發性硬化症中的髓鞘含量，以及透過MISL檢測AQP4活性。這些都是阿茲海默症病理中的重要表徵。綜合來看，我們的先導研究指出，CEST磁振造影在評估阿茲海默症關鍵病理特徵及雷帕黴素治療效果方面極具潛力。 在本研究中，我們將開發一套先進的多對比CEST成像技術平台，結合我們的造影技術與鼻內給藥方式，評估增強性雷帕黴素治療的療效。透過以下三個目標：（1）開發並優化我們先進的磁振造影技術，以成像阿茲海默症神經病理；（2）表徵接受雷帕黴素治療的阿茲海默症（APP/PS1）小鼠模型中關鍵分子與神經流體的變化；（3）評估給藥途徑並優化雷帕黴素對阿茲海默症病理的劑量依賴性療效。我們將對七組小鼠進行與阿茲海默症相關的分子特徵及治療反應造影，其中包括野生型小鼠、未接受治療及接受雷帕黴素治療的阿茲海默症小鼠，並與能提高腦內有效劑量的鼻內給藥途徑進行比較研究。這種同時且獨立的多重神經病理造影方式，將為研究阿茲海默症中關鍵病理特徵間的交互作用提供寶貴資訊，並有望實現對疾病預後的預測。

11106326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11106326.value: 手性誘導液滴圖案化及其在對映體分離中的應用

11106326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11106326.value: Chirality, the property of an object that cannot be superimposed on its mirror image, is ubiquitous in nature. The influence of molecular chirality is pervasive, such as life science, medicine, food, and agriculture. Over 72% of the chiral market is occupied by pharmaceuticals, where single-enantiomer drugs are critical for achieving precise therapeutic outcomes due to the inherently chiral environment of the human body. For instance, most amino acids in the human body used for protein synthesis are L-configured, whereas drugs containing D-enantiomers may resist metabolism and therefore be toxic. While seminal work recognized by Nobel Prizes in Chemistry 2001 has significantly advanced the synthesis of enantiopure drugs, conventional chiral analysis and separation approaches, such as chromatography and liquid-liquid extraction, are often expensive, technically complex, and challenging to scale up. Over the past decades, enantioselective liquid-liquid extraction has emerged as a promising alternative. However, existing systems are often substrate-specific and inefficient, relying on slow bulk-phase equilibrium processes. While microextraction has been used leveraging its high surface-to-volume ratios to enable rapid mass transfer, it typically requires integration with additional analytical techniques. Furthermore, the hydrodynamic effects induced by chiral interactions during microextraction remain poorly understood, limiting its efficiency and broad practical application. The proposed project is motivated by a newly discovered and pioneering phenomenon: Chirality directs the formation of distinct, visually identifiable patterns during the evaporation of aqueous two-phase system (ATPS) droplets. Such non-equilibrium hydrodynamic processes in confined microdroplets differ significantly from conventional bulk-phase behaviors. The macroscopic visual signals arising from molecular-scale interactions provide a direct readout of chirality. Building on these findings and a thorough understanding of the chirality-directed phase behavior, simple, rapid, and large-scale differentiation of chiral molecules through Artificial Intelligence(AI)-analyzed microcompartmentalization in ATPS can be achieved, thereby overcoming the limitations of complex instruments in conventional chiral analysis. Our objectives are to: (1) Elucidate chirality-driven physicochemical dynamics in ATPS droplets; (2) Decipher the mechanism of chirality directed phase behaviors via modeling droplet dynamics; (3) Enhance chiral molecular isolation with AI-analyzed droplet patterns. In the short term, this project will reveal how molecular chirality influences non-equilibrium soft matter physics at the microscale. In the long term, it will establish a novel paradigm that transforms complex chiral analysis into a simple, direct visual readout, with transformative potential for the pharmaceutical industry and beyond. 手性是指一個物體無法與其鏡像完全重合的性質，這種現象在自然界中普遍存在。分子手性在生命科學、醫藥、食品及農業等領域發揮重要作用。在手性市場中，製藥業佔比超過72%。由於人體本身具有手性環境，單一對映體藥物對於實現安全、精準治療至關重要。例如，人體參與蛋白質合成的大多數氨基酸均為 L-構型，而含有 D-對映體的藥物可能因難以被代謝而具有潛在毒性。儘管2001年諾貝爾化學獎所表彰的開創性手性催化研究極大推動了高純度單一構型藥物的合成，但傳統的手性分析與分離方法（如色譜法及液液萃取法）通常成本高昂、技術複雜，且難以實現規模化應用。過去數十年來，手性對映體選擇性液液萃取逐漸成為傳統手性分離技術的重要替代方案。然而，現有體系通常只適用於特定類型的分子，且其分離過程主要依賴緩慢的體相平衡，分離效率有限。儘管微萃取技術能夠利用其高表面積／體積比加快物質傳遞，但通常仍需結合其他分析手段才能實現手性識別與分離。此外，目前尚不清楚手性相互作用如何影響微萃取過程中的液滴動態及傳質過程，因此限制了分離效率的進一步提升及其廣泛應用。 本項目源於一項原創性發現：手性可誘導雙水相系統液滴在蒸發過程中形成具有明顯差異的可視化特徵圖案。與傳統體相系統不同，微液滴中的非平衡動態過程能夠將分子尺度的手性資訊放大為易於觀察的宏觀訊號，從而為手性識別提供直接而直觀的判讀依據。基於這一發現及對手性調控相變行為機制的深入研究，本項目將結合人工智能技術，解析雙水相系統液滴中的微觀相分離圖案，實現手性分子的快速、高效及規模化識別，從而突破傳統手性分析對複雜儀器設備的高度依賴。 本項目的研究目標為： （1）揭示雙水相微液滴中手性驅動的物理化學動力學過程； （2）基於液滴動力學模型，闡明手性調控相分離行為的作用機制； （3）結合人工智能圖像分析，實現手性分子的高效識別與分析。 短期而言，本項目將揭示分子手性對微液滴中非平衡動態過程及軟物質體系行為的影響規律；長期而言，將建立一種全新的可視化手性分析策略，將複雜的手性檢測轉化為直觀、快速的圖案識別過程，為製藥產業及其他相關領域帶來重要的應用潛力。

11106526.value: 導航變遷：繪製香港瀕危江豚棲息地季節性驅動因素地圖以促進動態海洋保育

11106526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11106526.value: Hong Kong waters host the Indo-Pacific finless porpoise (Neophocaena phocaenoides), a Vulnerable (IUCN Red List; CITES Appendix I) small cetacean. Monitoring surveys since 1996 by various parties provide baseline abundance and distribution data, with peak-season sightings of only 176–220 individuals. Marine Protected Areas (MPAs), often compensatory for infrastructure, lack holistic evaluation of coverage and effectiveness amid seasonal ecosystem fluctuations. Habitat suitability is governed by seasonally varying environmental factors, compounded by human activities and climate change. Statistical models offer a powerful framework to elucidate and forecast population trends by identifying key environmental and anthropogenic drivers of distribution. By revealing spatio-temporal patterns and mechanisms, they inform targeted mitigation, such as dynamic zoning or seasonal fishing restrictions. This project, for the first time, leverages a >30-year dataset (1996–2029) from long-term governmental and agency monitoring programs, complemented by environmental and anthropogenic parameters from diverse sources. Through rigorous integration and advanced modelling, we will address three pivotal conservation objectives. 1. Distribution patterns: Analyze seasonal variations in habitat distribution using long-term data from line-transect surveys. Historical records show seasonal core habitat shifts—offshore in dry season (November–April), inshore in wet season (May–October)—linked to oceanographic changes and prey dynamics. We will unify disparate sighting data, correct for survey effort biases, and use kernel density estimation and hotspot analysis in ArcGIS to quantify spatio-temporal hotspots, revealing seasonal trends and climate-driven displacements. 2. Habitat drivers: Identify key environmental and anthropogenic variables shaping core habitat suitability via Species Distribution Models (SDMs). We will integrate oceanographic variables (bathymetry, chlorophyll-α, dissolved oxygen, salinity, sea surface temperature) with anthropogenic layers (traffic density, fishing intensity, pollution levels) to assess relative importance and cumulative effects of variables through permutation tests and response curves, calculating ensemble habitat suitability indices to uncover degradation thresholds and inform risk maps for threats like vessel strikes and fishery bycatch. 3. Gap analysis: Quantify marine protection deficits relative to dynamic core habitat shifts under the influence of seasonal and climatic changes. We will overlay SDM outputs on existing MPAs to evaluate proportional coverage and efficacy using a panel of statistical tests, integrating threat layers and exposing temporal mismatches to prioritize risk-based adaptations like boundary revisions or dynamic zoning. Evidence-based analyses will empower Hong Kong and Greater Bay Area agencies to implement adaptive measures, delivering recommendations to stakeholder, safeguarding this vulnerable species and fostering sustainable human-wildlife coexistence. 印度太平洋江豚（Neophocaena phocaenoides）棲息在香港水域，屬國際自然保護聯盟（IUCN）紅色名錄易危物種，並列入《瀕危野生動植物種國際貿易公約》（CITES）附錄I的小型鯨豚類。自1996年以來，多方進行的監測調查提供了江豚的基線豐度及分布數據，旺季的目擊數目僅為176至220隻。海岸公園及海岸保護區（MPAs）多為基建項目的補償措施，在季節性生態系統波動下，缺乏對覆蓋範圍及成效的整體評估。生境適宜性受季節性變化的環境因素支配，並受人類活動及氣候變化影響。 統計模型提供強大框架，可透過識別影響分布的主要環境及人為因素，闡明並預測種群趨勢。藉揭示時空模式及機制，有助制定針對性緩解措施，例如動態分區或季節性捕魚限制。本項目首次運用超過30年（1996–2029年）的長期政府及機構監測數據，並輔以來自不同來源的環境及人為參數，透過嚴謹整合及先進建模，本項目將處理三項關鍵保育目標。 1. 分布模式：利用船舶定線調查的長期數據，分析江豚生境分布的季節性變化。歷史記錄顯示季節性核心生境轉移——旱季（11月至4月）偏離岸、雨季（5月至10月）偏向近岸——與海洋學變化及獵物動態相關。我們將統一不同來源的目擊數據、校正調查努力量偏差，並在ArcGIS中運用核密度估計及熱點分析，量化時空熱點，揭示季節趨勢及氣候驅動的位移。 2. 生境因素：透過物種分布模型（SDM）識別塑造江豚核心生境適宜性的主要環境及人為變量。本項目將整合海洋學變量（水深、葉綠素-α、溶解氧、鹽度、海面溫度）與人為因為（交通密度、捕魚強度、污染水平），透過排列檢驗及響應曲線評估變量的相對重要性及累積效應，計算集成生境適宜性指數，揭示退化閾值，並為船舶撞擊及漁業誤捕等威脅製作風險地圖。 3. 缺口分析：在季節及氣候變化的影響下，量化因生境改變而產生的海洋保護缺口。本項目將把SDM輸出結果疊加於現有MPAs，使用一系列統計檢驗評估比例覆蓋及成效，整合江豚面對的威脅，揭示時間錯配，從而優先考慮以風險為本的適應措施，例如邊界修訂或動態分區。以實證為本的分析將協助香港及大灣區相關機構實施措施，向持份者提供建議，保護江豚此易危物種，並促進可持續的人類與野生動物共存。

11200726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11200726.value: 基於結構信息論的單細胞 DNA 拷貝數檢測研究

11200726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200726.value: Single-cell DNA sequencing reveals copy-number alterations (CNAs) at cellular resolution, but fully resolving tumor evolution requires haplotype-aware analysis. Calling single haplotype- and clonal-specific CNA (single hcCNA), by explicitly phasing major and minor copy-number alleles at each locus, haplotype, and subclone, enables assignment of CN changes to parental haplotypes and clearer reconstruction of intratumor heterogeneity and tumor evolution. Tumor evolution begins in diploid cells and proceeds via accumulated hcCNAs, producing clones and subclones. A clonal hierarchy (tumor dendrogram) models this process: leaves are individual cells that group into distinct clones and subclones. Complementing this, a segmental hierarchy captures global-, clone-, subclone-, and cell-specific genome segmentations induced by hcCNAs over time. Inferring the clonal and segmental hierarchies are fundamental for resolving intratumor heterogeneity and reconstructing tumor evolutionary trajectories. Prioritizing complex hcCNA detection (coordinated alterations that involve two or more single hcCNAs across multiple haplotypes, cells, or genomic loci, e.g., copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity [LOH], mirrored-subclonal-CNA) uncovers cooperative alterations that more accurately capture tumor biology otherwise hidden. Precise focal hcCNA detection pinpoints actionable oncogene amplifications, tumor-suppressor deletions, and LOH tracts that unmask recessive alterations on specific haplotypes. Accurately reporting hcCNA recurrence and privacy is crucial for prioritizing candidate driver events (typically recurrent) and for quantifying ongoing mutagenesis and cellular diversity (often reflected by private events). Despite progress, no existing tool jointly models clonal and segmental hierarchies or provides explicit, hierarchical (clone, subclone, cell) annotation of the full spectrum of complex and focal hcCNAs, including recurrence/privacy scoring with calibrated confidence. To fill these gaps, we will infer hcCNAs from scDNA data, grounded in extensions of structural information theory, to deliver global segmentation and haplotype and the clonal and segmental hierarchies. Building on these profiles, we will annotate complex hcCNAs, focal hcCNAs, and their recurrence and privacy across the hierarchy. Preliminary results show promising performance in global phasing and mirrored-subclonal detection at practical coverage. We will conduct comprehensive benchmarking and continue tuning the framework to handle low-pass noise and protocol-specific artifacts. Finally, the team will apply the finalized framework to discover hcCNA biomarkers implicated in tumorigenesis from large, protocol-diverse single-cell cancer genomics cohorts across coverages and cancer types. 單細胞 DNA 測序能在單細胞解析度下揭示拷貝數變異（CNAs），但要徹底解析腫瘤演化，仍有賴於對單倍體（haplotype）的分析。透過明確對每個基因位點、單倍體及亞克隆的主要與次要拷貝數等位基因進行相位分型（phasing），鑑定出單一單倍體及克隆特異性 CNA（single hcCNA），能將拷貝數變化精確歸因至親本單倍體，進而更清晰地重建腫瘤內部異質性與腫瘤演化進程。腫瘤演化始於二倍體細胞，並隨着 hcCNAs 的累積逐步推進，最終形成不同的克隆與亞克隆。克隆層級結構（腫瘤樹狀圖）即是用來模擬此過程：葉節點代表單一細胞，並聚類為特定的克隆與亞克隆。與此互補的是，段落層級結構則捕捉了隨時間由 hcCNAs 所誘發的全域、克隆、亞克隆及細胞特異性基因組分段。因此，推斷克隆與段落層級結構是解析腫瘤內部異質性及重建腫瘤演化軌跡的關鍵基礎。優先檢測複雜 hcCNA（例如：拷貝數中性的雜合性缺失 [LOH]、鏡像亞克隆 CNA），能揭示先前被隱藏且能更精準反映腫瘤生物學特徵的協同變異。精準的局灶性hcCNA 檢測可精確定位具臨床可藥用價值的致癌基因放大、腫瘤抑制基因缺失，以及揭示特定單倍體上隱性變異的 LOH 區域。準確報告 hcCNA 的復發性與私有性對於優先篩選候選驅動事件（通常具復發性），以及量化持續發生的基因突變與細胞多樣性（通常反映於私有事件）至關重要。儘管已有相關進展，目前仍缺乏能同時對克隆與段落層級結構進行聯合建模的工具，也無法針對全譜系的複雜與局灶性 hcCNAs（包含具校準置信度的復發性／私有性評分）提供明確且具層級性（克隆、亞克隆、細胞）的註釋。為填補這些空白，我們將拓展結構信息理論，從單細胞 DNA數據中推斷 hcCNAs，以建立全域分段、單倍體相位，以及克隆與段落層級結構。基於這些圖譜，我們將在整個層級結構中，進一步註釋複雜 hcCNAs、局灶性 hcCNAs，及其復發性與私有性。初步結果顯示，在實用測序深度下，本方法於全域相位分型與鏡像亞克隆檢測方面均展現出優異的性能。我們將進行全面的基準測試，並持續優化演算法框架，以處理低覆蓋率噪聲與特定實驗協定帶來的偽影。最後，團隊將把最終確定的分析框架應用於包含不同深度與癌症類型的多樣化大型單細胞癌症基因組學資料集中，以探勘與腫瘤發生相關的 hcCNA 生物標誌物。

11201126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11201126.value: 3D列印鹼激發水泥複合材料耐火性能研究

11201126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11201126.value: Prof Kodur, Venkatesh Kumar R. Prof Sun, Jinhua

11201126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201126.value: The catastrophic collapse of concrete structures during fires poses a critical and ongoing risk to public safety and economic stability, as starkly illustrated by the 21 November 2022 fire in Henan, China, which claimed 38 lives and caused damages exceeding 123 million RMB (Reuters, CNN, BBC). Such events underscore the urgent need to rigorously evaluate and improve the fire performance of concrete. Simultaneously, the construction industry faces two transformative challenges: reducing its significant carbon footprint and embracing digitalization, both of which demand innovative and sustainable building technologies. One promising pathway is 3D concrete printing (3DCP) with alkali-activated cements (AAC), which offers advantages in automation, design flexibility, and sustainability. AAC formulations can reduce the carbon footprint of concrete by up to 80% compared to traditional Portland cement. However, their adoption is hindered by poor fire resistance, particularly in metakaolin-based systems optimized for buildability. Unlike conventional cast concrete, which typically fails by spalling, 3D-printed AAC structures are especially vulnerable to interlayer delamination under high temperatures—a critical safety concern. This project proposes to address this barrier by reinforcing AAC with recycled carbon fibers (rCFs) recovered from end-of-life wind turbine blades. This approach simultaneously targets improved fire performance and advances circular economy principles by upcycling high-value waste materials. The fundamental thermo-hygro-mechanical (THM) mechanisms that govern the fire response of such 3D-printed, fiber-reinforced composites (3DP-rCFAC) remain almost entirely unknown, representing the central knowledge gap of this research. To fill this gap, we will undertake an integrated experimental–computational program. First, a workable and printable 3DP-rCFAC formulation will be developed, with systematic investigations into its microstructure, moisture transport, and interlayer bond degradation under elevated temperatures. Second, a coupled THM constitutive model will be established to capture these degradation processes. Third, a novel multiscale, multiphysics meshfree simulation framework will be created and validated to predict the structural fire response of 3D-printed concrete. The outcomes will provide the first fundamental understanding of fire behavior in sustainable, digitally fabricated concrete systems. Deliverables will include validated design guidelines and a robust predictive simulation tool to support the engineering of fire-resilient 3D-printed structures. By directly addressing a major safety barrier, this project will accelerate the safe, widespread adoption of 3D printing in construction while contributing to global goals of decarbonization, resource circularity, and resilient infrastructure. 混凝土結構在火災中的災難性倒塌，持續對公共安全與經濟穩定構成重大威脅。2022年11月21日發生於中國河南的火災事故便是一個令人警醒的案例，該事故造成38人死亡，經濟損失超過1.23億元人民幣（来源：Reuters、CNN、BBC）。此類事故凸顯了對混凝土結構的耐火性能進行系統評估與提升的迫切需求。與此同時，建築業正面臨兩項深刻的轉型挑戰：一方面，需要顯著降低其龐大的碳足跡；另一方面，需要加快數位化轉型。這兩項挑戰均迫切需要創新且可持續的建築技術。 採用鹼激發水泥（Alkali-activated cements, AAC）的3D混凝土列印（3D concrete printing, 3DCP）是其中一條極具潛力的技術路徑，其在自動化、設計靈活性及可持續性方面具有顯著優勢。與傳統波特蘭水泥相比，AAC配方可將混凝土的碳足跡降低最高達80%。然而，其廣泛應用仍受到耐火性能不足的嚴重制約，尤其是針對為滿足可建造性而優化的偏高嶺土基體系。不同於傳統澆築混凝土在高溫下通常以爆裂形式破壞，3D列印AAC結構在高溫作用下尤其容易發生層間脫層，從而構成關鍵性的結構安全隱患。 本項目擬採用從退役風力渦輪機葉片中回收的再生碳纖維（Recycled carbon fibers, rCFs）對AAC進行增強，以突破上述技術瓶頸。該方法不僅有望提升材料及結構的耐火性能，同時可透過高附加值廢棄材料的升級再利用，推動循環經濟發展。然而，此類3D列印纖維增強複合材料（3DP-rCFAC）在火災作用下的基本熱-濕-力耦合（Thermo-hygro-mechanical, THM）機制目前幾乎尚未被揭示，這構成了本研究所要解決的核心知識空白。 為填補這一研究空白，本項目將開展一套實驗與計算相結合的整合研究。首先，研發具有良好工作性與可列印性的3DP-rCFAC材料體系，並系統研究其在高溫作用下的微觀結構演變、水分傳輸行為及層間黏結性能退化機制。其次，建立耦合THM本構模型，以準確描述上述多物理場耦合退化過程。第三，開發並驗證一種新型多尺度、多物理場無網格數值模擬框架，用於預測3D列印混凝土結構在火災作用下的整體結構響應。 本項目預期將首次建立對可持續、數位化製造混凝土體系火災行為的基礎性與系統性認識。主要成果將包括經驗證的設計指南，以及一套可靠的預測性數值模擬工具，以支援耐火3D列印混凝土結構的工程設計。透過直接突破制約3D列印建築技術應用的重大安全瓶頸，本項目將有助於加速3D列印技術在建築領域的安全與規模化應用，並同時服務於全球脫碳、資源循環利用及韌性基礎設施建設等發展目標。

11201226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11201226.value: 一种可实现单向传热的新型紧凑式辐射天空冷却器：利用夜间冷却提升白天性能

11201226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11201226.value: Prof Tso, Chi Yan Prof XIAO, Fu

11201226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201226.value: Subtropical rooftops, especially tin shacks housing many elderly residents, are exposed to prolonged, intense solar radiation, causing surface temperatures to exceed 70°C during summer. This drives up cooling energy demand and poses significant health risks. Cooling such rooftops is vital for protecting vulnerable residents, lowering energy use, and mitigating Hong Kong’s urban-heat-island (UHI) effect. As a promising passive cooling technology, radiative sky coolers (RSCs) can generate over 200% more usable cooling at night than during daytime, offering a significant opportunity to harness nighttime-cooling to enhance daytime performance. However, conventional RSCs remain highly inefficient at utilizing nighttime-cooling. The primary reason is as follows. At night, heat transfer must be enhanced to efficiently capture and store cooling under narrow temperature differentials; however, during the day, this enhanced heat transfer causes the stored cooling to be rapidly depleted by solar heat gain, leaving no cooling available to enhance daytime performance. Thus, harnessing nighttime-cooling requires satisfying two opposing requirements simultaneously: HIGH heat transfer at night to capture and store cooling, but LOW heat transfer during the day to prevent stored-cooling loss from solar heat gain. For the first time, we propose a novel RSC that leverages the unidirectional-heat-transfer capability of a heat pipe to meet the opposing requirements. Our preliminary experiments demonstrate a 320.75% enhancement in daytime cooling performance. Building on these promising results, this project aims to address three key limitations of current design and studies: (1) poor compactness, as the bulky 300 mm height severely restricts practical use; (2) absence of an accurate dynamic model, which hinders reliable performance assessment and design optimization; and (3) lack of an effective method to optimize its high-dimensional interacting parameters for maximum daytime cooling. To address the limitations, the project is organized into four tasks. Task-1 will design a novel RSC structure with substantially improved compactness and experimentally investigate its unidirectional heat transfer characteristic. Task-2 will develop a dynamic model to capture the complex multi-phase coupled heat transfer across three major units: cooling generation, delivery and storage. Task-3 will develop a hybrid optimization method to maximize daytime performance while accounting for complex interactions among high-dimensional influencing parameters. Task-4 will conduct real-world experiments to assess its daytime cooling enhancement, long-term durability and cost-effectiveness. By harnessing nighttime-cooling, the proposed RSC can be widely implemented on subtropical rooftops to improve daytime performance, enhancing elderly health, reducing cooling energy use, and mitigating the UHI effect. 亚热带地区的屋顶，尤其是居住着大量老年居民的铁皮屋顶，长期暴露在强烈太阳辐射下，夏季表面温度可超过 70°C。这不仅会推高制冷能源需求，还会带来显著的健康风险。因此，对此类屋顶进行降温，对于保护易受影响的居民、降低能源消耗以及缓解香港城市热岛效应（UHI）至关重要。 作为一种有前景的被动冷却技术，辐射天空冷却器（radiative sky coolers, RSCs）在夜间产生的可用冷量可比白天高出 200% 以上，这为利用夜间冷却来提升白天性能提供了重要机会。然而，传统 RSC 在利用夜间冷却方面效率仍然很低。其主要原因如下：夜间，在较小的温差条件下，必须增强传热，才能有效捕获并储存冷量；但白天，这种增强的传热会使储存的冷量因太阳得热而迅速耗尽，从而无法用于提升白天性能。因此，利用夜间冷却需要同时满足两个相互矛盾的要求：夜间需要高传热以捕获和储存冷量，而白天需要低传热以防止储存冷量因太阳得热而损失。 我们首次提出一种新型 RSC，利用热管的单向传热能力来满足上述相互矛盾的需求。我们的初步实验表明，其白天冷却性能提升了 320.75%。基于这些有前景的结果，本项目旨在解决当前设计与研究中的三个关键局限：（1）紧凑性较差，现有装置 300 mm 的庞大高度严重限制了实际应用；（2）缺乏准确的动态模型，阻碍了可靠的性能评估和设计优化；（3）缺乏有效方法来优化其高维、相互耦合参数，以实现最大的白天冷却效果。 为解决上述局限，本项目分为四项任务。任务 1 将设计一种紧凑性显著提升的新型 RSC 结构，并通过实验研究其单向传热特性。任务 2 将建立动态模型，以刻画三个主要单元——冷量产生、冷量传输和冷量储存——之间复杂的多相耦合传热过程。任务 3 将开发一种混合优化方法，在考虑高维影响参数之间复杂相互作用的同时，最大化白天性能。任务 4 将开展真实环境实验，以评估其白天冷却增强效果、长期耐久性和成本效益。 通过利用夜间冷却，所提出的 RSC 可广泛应用于亚热带地区屋顶，以提升白天冷却性能，从而改善老年人健康、降低制冷能源消耗，并缓解城市热岛效应。

11201326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11201326.value: 低功率應用之直接隔離式 AC-AC 轉換器

11201326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201326.value: Compact, energy-efficient power supplies are essential to meet the rising demand for safe and sustainable consumer electronics. A defining feature of next-generation power supplies is their ability to deliver high-frequency AC power directly from the wall outlet—an innovation that is vital for advancing emerging applications with wireless power transfer (WPT) capability and ultrasonic motor driven products. Currently, offline power supplies for such applications typically rely on multi-stage conversion architectures that are achieved through combination of disparate topologies or the adaptation of legacy designs. Such designs increase system size, power loss, and control complexity, which hinder integration and also increase product cost. To address this challenge, we propose a type of isolated direct offline AC-AC converters that process 50/60 Hz mains voltage directly into high-frequency AC output through a single-stage power conversion. This approach integrates galvanic isolation, simplified structure, and control, offering a compact, efficient, safe, and low-cost solution for powering high-frequency AC loads. The proposed converter delivers several advantages over existing systems: • Higher power transfer efficiency • Smaller size and higher power density • Single active power stage • Simplified control and design • Enhanced integration for modular systems Impact on the Wireless Power Transfer Industry: The converter eliminates intermediate stages in WPT systems, reducing energy loss and system complexity. This enables the development of compact and efficient wireless charging platforms for consumer electronics and medical devices, supporting the growth of WPT adoption fueled by the integration of emerging Qi2 and MagSafe-like standards. Impact on the Ultrasonic Motor Industry: Ultrasonic motors require high-frequency AC drives with precise control and compact form factors. They are commonly used in smart toys, compact robots, wearables, and smart home devices, etc., for their silent, gearless, and low-speed torque features. The proposed converter facilitates direct grid-powered operation, improving energy efficiency and enabling broader deployment in these products. The project will pursue three core objectives: Topology Innovation: Explore advanced AC-AC converter topologies to minimize power stages. Control Development: Create efficient control methods tailored to the proposed topologies. Practical Implementation: Establish design guidelines and component selection strategies for miniaturized, real-world applications. The proposed converter technology reconciles the high demands of direct high-frequency AC power delivery with the limitations of conventional offline systems. This research will pave the way for transformative innovations in WPT and ultrasonic motor applications, contributing to the advancement of power electronics and sustainable technologies. 隨著市場對安全、可持續及高能效消費電子產品的需求持續增長，體積小巧且能源效率高的電源供應器已成為關鍵技術之一。新一代電源供應器的一項重要特徵，是能夠直接將市電轉換為高頻交流電（AC）輸出，而無需經過多重中間轉換級。此技術對於具備無線電力傳輸（Wireless Power Transfer, WPT）功能的產品，以及採用超聲波馬達（Ultrasonic Motor）的新興應用尤為重要。 目前，此類離線式（offline）電源系統大多採用多級功率轉換架構，通常透過組合不同電路拓撲或改良傳統設計而成。然而，這些方案普遍存在體積較大、功率損耗較高及控制複雜等問題，不但限制系統整合能力，亦增加產品成本。 為解決上述挑戰，本研究提出一種新型隔離式直接離線 AC-AC 轉換器，可透過單級功率轉換，直接將 50/60 Hz 市電轉換為高頻交流輸出。該技術同時具備電氣隔離（galvanic isolation）、結構簡化及控制簡化等特點，為高頻交流負載提供一種體積小、效率高、安全可靠且具成本效益的供電方案。相較現有系統，所提出的轉換器具有以下優勢： • 更高的能量傳輸效率； • 更小體積及更高功率密度； • 單一主動功率轉換級； • 簡化的控制策略與系統設計； • 更佳的模組化系統整合能力。 對無線電力傳輸產業的影響 所提出的轉換器能夠消除無線電力傳輸系統中的中間功率轉換級，從而降低能量損耗及系統複雜度。此技術將有助開發更緊湊、更高效率的無線充電平台，廣泛應用於消費電子及醫療設備領域，並支援 Qi2 及類 MagSafe 等新一代無線充電標準的普及與發展。 對超聲波馬達產業的影響 超聲波馬達需要高頻交流驅動，並對控制精度及系統小型化有較高要求。由於具備低噪音、無齒輪傳動及低速高扭矩等優點，超聲波馬達已廣泛應用於智能玩具、小型機械人、穿戴式裝置及智慧家居產品等領域。本研究提出的轉換器可支援直接市電驅動超聲波馬達，提高能源利用效率，並促進其於更多消費產品中的應用。 研究目標: 本項目將圍繞以下三個核心研究目標開展： 拓撲創新（Topology Innovation） 探索先進 AC-AC 轉換器拓撲結構，以實現最少功率轉換級數及最高系統性能。 控制方法開發（Control Development） 針對所提出拓撲設計高效控制策略，以提升轉換效率、輸出品質及系統穩定性。 實際應用實現（Practical Implementation） 建立小型化電源系統設計準則及元件選型方法，推動技術於實際產品中的落地應用。 總括而言，本研究所提出的直接隔離式離線 AC-AC 轉換器，能有效兼顧高頻交流供電需求與傳統離線電源系統的設計限制。預期研究成果將為無線電力傳輸及超聲波馬達應用領域帶來突破性發展，並促進電力電子技術及可持續能源技術的進一步進步。

11201626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11201626.value: 模組化時空分離架構下內嵌線性動力學的工業時空大模型

11201626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201626.value: Many real-world physical processes are spatiotemporal dynamic systems that can be described by partial differential equations, also known as distributed parameter systems. Modeling these spatiotemporal dynamic systems is extremely difficult, let alone the online performance prediction that is crucial in industrial operations. Traditional modeling approaches perform well under specific operating conditions and spatial locations, but such small models struggle to provide comprehensive spatial performance predictions, especially when data is scarce. While large language models have demonstrated great potential across a wide range of industries, they are not specifically designed for physically constrained spatiotemporal dynamic systems and are therefore expensive to train. Industrial scenarios require lightweight large models that can be trained quickly and cost-effectively.
