This proposal aims to develop a linear dynamics-embedded large physical model under modular spatial/temporal separation for industrial spatiotemporal dynamic systems, which can be easily trained at low cost and achieve full-space performance prediction under all operating conditions.  First, the complex spatiotemporal dynamic system will be decomposed through modular design and space/time separation, with linear dynamics as the basic unit. The large model will be constructed hierarchically, containing many small sub-models, each capturing nonlinear dynamics under different operating conditions and spatial locations. This physical structure model will be easy and cheap to train.  Second, the hybrid experiment/simulation dataset will be produced for physics-informed model training and learning. Model learning should adhere to three key principles: first, establish the model structure before learning the parameters; second, define the spatial model prior to developing the temporal model; and third, employ sensitivity-based parameter grouping and coarse-fine coordination techniques for iterative learning in multi-parameter scenarios.  Third, spatiotemporal transfer learning will be introduced for the first time to facilitate model learning in data-scarce conditions. The results of the proposed research, if successful, will produce pioneering work in large model for spatiotemporal processes in industry, and can be generalized to a wider range of spatiotemporal dynamic systems in the real world.

11201726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11201726.value: 用於高效活細胞成像實驗的細胞形狀匹配方法 用於高效活細胞成像實驗的細胞形狀匹配方法 用於高效活細胞成像實驗的細胞形狀匹配方法

11201726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201726.value: Live cell imaging is commonly used to study cell division, in which the cross-sectional images of an embryo are obtained at different time points using a confocal microscope. Starting from the root cell (zygote), we extract and track each cell and its daughter cells during cell division. Through the mother and daughter relationships, we can identify cells in all successive generations, name them and create a lineage tree. If we start image collection at a later stage, for example, when there are 150 cells, we can avoid laser radiation before the 150-cell stage. Thereafter, we can use higher laser power and higher temporal resolution for better image quality. In this way, the total light dose from the laser radiation can be kept under the limit in order not to damage the embryo. The problem with this approach is that we do not have the ancestor information of these 150 cells and cannot identify them. To tackle this problem, we will develop cell shape matching techniques. The strategy is to match these 150 cells’ shapes with those from a standard experiment that started from the root cell and find the corresponding positions in the lineage tree. Cell shape matching is also useful for studying cell dynamics, such as the shape changes between two time points. Another important application is to match cells from standard and gene knockdown experiments to infer gene regulatory functions. In this project, we will extract robust cell features for effective shape matching. Invariant pattern matching techniques will be investigated to allow cell variations in scale, translation and rotation. A high-order compatibility formulation will be developed to deal with non-rigid deformations. Tensor CUR decomposition will be employed to reduce both computing time and storage space. In addition to matching individual cells’ shapes, we will also consider their dynamic morphological features, nucleus trajectories in the temporal direction, and the cells’ neighborhood relations to improve matching accuracy. We will develop a multi-step matching process to solve these problems, one for matching static cell shapes, one for their dynamics, and one for their positions and neighbors. Our project will make it possible to conduct live cell imaging experiments more efficiently and provide innovative techniques to investigate cell dynamics and identify gene functions. Our technology will open the door to developing a new generation of methods for live cell imaging and cell division data acquisition and analysis. 活細胞成像常用於研究細胞分裂，其原理是利用共聚焦顯微鏡在不同時間點取得胚胎的橫斷面影像。從根細胞（受精卵）開始，我們提取並追蹤細胞分裂過程中每個細胞及其子細胞。透過母子關係，我們可以識別所有連續世代中的細胞，對其進行命名並建立譜系樹。 如果我們在較晚的階段開始採集影像，例如在細胞數量達到150個時，我們可以避免在150個細胞階段之前進行雷射照射。之後，我們可以使用更高的雷射功率和更高的時間解析度來獲得更好的影像品質。這樣，雷射輻射的總光劑量可以控制在一定範圍內，從而避免傷害胚胎。這種方法的缺點在於，我們無法獲得這150個細胞的祖先訊息，也無法辨識它們。為了解決這個問題，我們將開發細胞形狀匹配技術。該策略是將這150個細胞的形狀與從根細胞開始的標準實驗中的細胞形狀進行匹配，並在譜系樹中找到相應的位置。 細胞形狀匹配對於研究細胞動力學也十分有用，例如兩個時間點之間的形狀變化。另一個重要的應用是將來自標準實驗和基因敲除實驗的細胞進行匹配，以推斷基因調控功能。 本計畫旨在提取穩健的細胞特徵，以實現高效的形狀匹配。我們將研究不變模式匹配技術，以適應細胞在尺度、平移和旋轉方面的變化。此外，我們還將開發一種擁有高階相容性的方法來處理非剛性形變。張量CUR分解將用於減少運算時間和儲存空間。 除了匹配單一細胞的形狀外，我們還將考慮其動態形態特徵、細胞核在時間方向上的軌跡以及細胞的鄰域關係，以提高匹配精度。我們將開發一個多步驟匹配流程來解決這些問題：第一步用於匹配靜態細胞形狀，第二步用於匹配其動態特徵，還有一步用於匹配其位置和鄰域關係。 我們的研究項目將使活細胞成像實驗更加高效，並為研究細胞動力學和識別基因功能提供創新科技。我們的技術將為開發新一代活細胞成像和細胞分裂資料收集與分析方法打開大門。

11202026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11202026.value: 不確定歐拉–拉格朗日多智能體系統分布式尋源控制

11202026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11202026.value: Cooperative control of networked dynamical systems, known as multi-agent systems, has become a major research focus within the control and robotics communities over the past few decades. These systems enable agents to collaboratively achieve objectives through information sharing. Within this area, distributed source seeking has attracted considerable attention due to its great potential in missions like search-and-rescue, military surveillance, and environmental monitoring. It aims to locate a source of interest using a group of networked dynamical systems. While some distributed source seeking control strategies exist for various networked dynamical systems including integrators and nonholonomic vehicles, most fail to address complex real-world scenarios. For example, in hazardous environments, source seeking often requires diverse robotic platforms, such as unmanned aerial vehicles, ground robots, and underwater gliders, which exhibit nonlinear Euler-Lagrange (EL) dynamics beyond simple integrator models. In addition, existing works suffer from three critical limitations: First, reliance on undirected network topologies ignores practical constraints such as bandwidth limitations and unidirectional links. Second, predominant focus on static sources inadequately addresses moving sources such as wildfire fronts tracking during containment operations. Third, slow convergence prevents time-critical applications like wildfire control where delays may cause catastrophic escalation. Furthermore, a key omission of existing works is the lack of robustness to parametric uncertainties. During operation, robotic parameters can change due to component wear or varying payloads. In fact, recent literature review reveals that there is no existing work on distributed source seeking of multiple uncertain EL systems simultaneously addressing the issues of directed network topologies, moving source seeking, and fixed-time convergence. This project will investigate the distributed source seeking problem of multiple uncertain EL systems under practical and challenging settings. Specifically, it will address three core issues: (i) distributed static source seeking of multiple uncertain EL systems over directed networks; (ii) distributed moving source seeking of multiple uncertain EL systems over directed networks; and (iii) fixed-time distributed moving source seeking of multiple uncertain EL systems over directed networks. This project, by addressing these issues and related challenges, will develop novel robust and fixed-time distributed control strategies. The expected outcomes of this project will enhance the performance of multi-agent systems in distributed source seeking, greatly facilitating their practical applications in real-world scenarios. 分布式尋源控制是多智能體系統協同控制中的重要研究課題，旨在利用多個智能體之間的協同合作，自主搜尋並定位目標源，在搜救、環境監測、災害應急等任務中具有廣泛的應用前景。近年來，針對不同動態模型（如積分型系統及非完整动态系統）的分布式尋源控制已取得不少研究成果。然而，多數現有研究仍難以滿足複雜實際場景的需求。例如，實際任務中應用的無人機、地面機器人等智能體系統具有複雜的非線性歐拉–拉格朗日動力學特性。此外，現有研究主要存在三方面不足：一是大多假設智能體之間採用雙向通信，未充分考慮實際中普遍存在的有向通信拓撲；二是主要針對靜態目標源，難以應對森林火災蔓延等動態目標源的尋源問題；三是收斂速度較慢，難以滿足災害應急等時間敏感任務的需求。另一方面，智能體在運行過程中，其動力學參數可能因設備磨損或載荷變化而產生不確定性，進一步增加了分布式尋源控制的難度。目前，針對不確定歐拉–拉格朗日多智能體系統，同時考慮有向通信拓撲、動態目標源及固定時間收斂等實際因素的分布式尋源控制問題仍缺乏深入研究。 本項目將聚焦於不確定歐拉–拉格朗日多智能體系統的分布式尋源控制問題，重點研究有向通信拓撲下的靜態目標源、動態目標源，以及固定時間收斂的動態目標源尋源三項關鍵問題，並提出兼具魯棒性與固定時間收斂特性的分布式控制策略。預期研究成果將有效提升多智能體系統在分布式尋源任務中的效率、可靠性與環境適應能力，促進其在災害應急、環境監測及其他複雜實際場景中的應用。

11202326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11202326.value: 認識車輛誘導湍流與道路綠化對城市街道中交通污染物擴散的交互影響

11202326.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11202326.value: Dr Gromke, Christof Dr Qin, Peng Dr Zhao, Yongling

11202326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11202326.value: Urban air pollution is a serious health concern in cities. Vehicular pollutants, including exhaust emissions and non-exhaust pollutants such as fine particle matter from tires, brakes, and road surface, continue to pose health risks to citizens, even with the adoption of electric vehicles. In urban street canyons, the dispersion of vehicular pollutants is influenced by two key street elements: vehicles and roadside vegetation. Stationary or moving vehicles interact with the incoming air flow, creating turbulence that redistributes pollutants, while engines and solar-heated urban surfaces generate rising warm air, further complicating pollutant movement. Roadside vegetation acts as a porous barrier that often slows wind and exacerbates pollutant accumulation; however, recent studies found that properly designed and placed roadside vegetation can reduce pedestrians’ exposure to pollutants. Vegetation’s foliage captures particle matter through the deposition effect, while deposited particles can re-enter the air via wind-driven resuspension. The complex and interactive effects of those mechanisms on vehicular pollutant dispersion in street canyons remain unclear, and an integrated understanding is lacking. This project addresses four critical, articulated research gaps: (1) the lack of experimental data on vehicle-induced turbulence under buoyant, weak wind conditions; (2) inadequate understanding on the competing aerodynamic, deposition, and resuspension effects of roadside vegetation on fine particles; (3) the lack of computationally efficient yet reliable Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) approaches for simulating the interactive effects of vehicle-induced turbulence and roadside vegetation; and (4) the lack of rapid, design-oriented surrogate model to guide strategic design of roadside vegetation for pollution mitigation. We will combine real-world measurements, novel wind tunnel experiments, advanced CFD simulations, and physics-informed neural networks to reveal these complex processes. First, we will measure tracer gas and airflow along real roads under typical traffic, buoyant, and weak wind conditions. Then, we will reproduce these conditions in a wind tunnel for detailed analysis of the interactive mechanism. For vegetation, we will develop a novel two-stage wind tunnel experiment to isolate and quantify the aerodynamic, deposition, and resuspension effects of vegetation’s foliage. Next, based on the experimental data, we will develop and validate CFD approaches with both reliability and computational efficiency for simulating the interactive effects of vehicle-induced turbulence and roadside vegetation on the flow pattern and pollutant dispersion. Finally, we will use physics-informed neural networks to develop a fast prediction surrogate model to guide the strategic design of roadside vegetation for mitigating pedestrian exposure to vehicular pollutants. 空氣污染是城市面臨的重大公共健康挑戰。車輛排放的污染物，包括尾氣以及來自輪胎、製動器和路面的細顆粒等非尾氣排放，即使在電動車廣泛採用的情境下，仍持續威脅市民健康。在城市街谷中，車輛污染物的擴散受兩類關鍵街道要素控製：車流與行道綠化。靜止或行駛中的車輛與背景氣流相互作用，産生車輛誘導湍流，改變局部流場並重新分佈污染物；同時，汽車髮動機及受太陽加熱的城市下墊面産生的浮力上昇氣流，進一步強化了流動與傳輸過程的複雜性。行道綠化作爲多孔障礙物，往往削弱近地風速、促使污染物在街谷內累積；然而，最新研究顯示，若在空間配置與形態設計上加以優化，行道綠化亦可有效降低行人對交通污染物的暴露。植被葉片一方面可通過沉積作用捕獲顆粒物，另一方面已沉積顆粒在風力作用下又可能再懸浮回到空氣中。多種機理交織下，街谷內交通污染物的時空分佈及其對公衆暴露的綜合影響仍缺乏系統的定量認知。 本項目旨在彌補以下四個關鍵研究缺口：（1）缺乏關於浮力主導、弱風條件下車輛誘導湍流的系統實驗數據；（2）對行道綠化在細顆粒物控製中氣動阻隔、沉積與再懸浮等相互競爭機理的認識不足；（3）缺少在計算成本與預測精度之間取得平衡、能夠刻畫車輛誘導湍流與行道綠化耦合效應的高效計算流體力學方法；（4）缺乏可快速用於設計決策的代理模型，以支撐行道綠化的策略性配置與優化。本研究將綜合採用實地觀測、新型風洞實驗、高分辨率計算流體力學模擬以及物理約束神經網絡，繫統揭示相關多尺度過程。首先，我們將在典型交通強度、浮力效應與弱風條件下，對真實城市道路沿線的示踪氣體濃度與流場進行同步測量，並在實驗室中複現實地邊界條件，開展風洞實驗以解析車輛與綠化耦合下的細緻流動與輸運機理。針對植被效應，我們將設計兩階段或分離式實驗方案，定量區分並評估植被的氣動影響、顆粒沉積與再懸浮貢獻。隨後，基於觀測與實驗數據，開髮並驗証兼具可靠性與計算效率的數值模擬方法，用於再現車輛誘導湍流與行道綠化對流場結構及污染物擴散的交互作用。最後，我們將構建融入物理約束的神經網絡代理模型，實現對街谷內污染物分佈與行人暴露的快速預測，爲行道綠化的設計佈局優化提供科學依據與定量設計工具。

11202426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11202426.value: 面向集水與淨化一體化的複合內凹剪紙超材料構築

11202426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11202426.value: Achieving sustainable access to clean water and sanitation is a key priority within the United Nations’ 17 Sustainable Development Goals. Atmospheric fog represents a vast and sustainable freshwater resource, yet its large-scale utilization remains hindered by the low collection efficiency due to aerodynamic deflection of fog-laden wind and poor water quality caused by airborne contaminants. Existing fog harvesting and purification technologies that integrate collection surfaces with photocatalysts face inherent trade-offs: sufficient contaminant degradation requires prolonged droplet retention, which in turn impedes droplet drainage and reduces the clean water yield. This project proposes a transformative solution through the composite reentrant kirigami metamaterial design that decouples and independently optimizes fog capture and water purification. The design integrates a geometry-dominant perforated kirigami scaffold at the front with a visible-light-responsive photocatalytic layer at the back. The kirigami scaffold, featuring optimized reentrant geometries, can reshape the aerodynamics near the substrate, suppressing fog deflection and enhancing droplet interception, while the porous photocatalytic layer, with refined material configurations, enables continuous and on-site purification of captured fog droplets. By separating and independently tuning the geometric and material effects of these two layers, the proposed system overcomes the long-standing trade-off between droplet retention and drainage, providing a new pathway for highly efficient and high-yield clean water harvesting. Our preliminary results demonstrated that the composite kirigami produced a clean water yield of 18.1 L/m2/h under an organic contaminant concentration of 0.5 ppm, corresponding to a superior purification efficiency of 96.7% and a high collection efficiency of 39.2%. Building on this foundation, this project will develop a comprehensive framework to characterize and optimize the intertwined processes of fog capture and purification, deepen mechanistic insight, and enable adaptable, scalable implementation. Through a comprehensive experimental-numerical-analytical framework, we will elucidate the aerodynamic mechanisms behind geometry-enhanced fog capture and identify optimal design parameters. Further, we will investigate how the conjunction between scaffold geometry and the photocatalytic layer property coordinates synchronized water transport and contaminant decomposition dynamics for highly efficient and high-yield clean water production. Comprehensive evaluations spanning diverse atmospheric contaminants and environmental conditions will be conducted to validate the versatility and practicality of our approach. Finally, the optimized composite kirigami sample will be scaled up and tested in outdoor environments. The fundamental and technical outcomes generated by this project will establish a new paradigm for high-yield, high-efficiency, and scalable fog harvesting and on-site purification, offering a transformative pathway toward sustainable and decentralized clean-water solutions. 實現可持續的清潔用水獲取與衛生保障，是聯合國17項可持續發展目標中的重要議題。大氣霧蘊含豐富且可持續利用的淡水資源，但其大規模利用仍受到集水效率不足及空氣污染物引起的水質問題所限制。尤其是，傳統集水與淨化功能通常依賴同一界面實現，導致水量與水質難以兼顧。 本項目擬構築一種由內凹剪紙骨架與高效光催化塗層集成的複合剪紙超材料，建立兼具高效霧水收集與原位污染物去除能力的可持續集水平台。不同於傳統單一功能界面，本項目將集水過程中的幾何效應與水處理過程中的材料效應進行空間解耦與獨立調控，以突破傳統霧水收集系統中水量與水質難以同步提升的性能瓶頸。 初步結果表明，在有機污染物濃度為0.5 ppm的條件下，所開發的複合剪紙超材料可實現18.1 L/m²/h的潔淨水產量、96.7%的污染物去除效率及39.2%的霧水收集效率。在此前期基礎上，本項目將結合實驗與理論分析，系統揭示剪紙幾何對霧滴捕獲與排液行為的調控規律，並確定關鍵結構設計參數；進一步研究剪紙骨架與光催化層之間的功能匹配關係，闡明水體輸運與污染物降解的協同動力學，實現高效率、高產量的潔淨水獲取。同時，項目將針對不同大氣污染物及環境條件開展系統評估，驗證其通用性與實用性，並對優化樣品進行尺度放大和戶外測試。預期成果將建立一種高通量、高效率且可規模化的霧水收集與原位淨化新策略，為可持續、分散式潔淨水供應提供新的材料與技術路徑。

11202626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11202626.value: 機器學習設計具梯度介面的多功能共晶高熵合金

11202626.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11202626.value: Prof Guan, Pengfei Prof Zeng, Qiaoshi Dr Zhou, Hao

11202626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11202626.value: Eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs) represent a frontier in advanced materials design, offering an exceptional combination of excellent castability, high strength, and superior ductility. However, the discovery of these alloys is hindered by the immense and uncharted compositional space characteristic of high-entropy systems, for which conventional phase diagrams are unavailable. Traditional trial-and-error experimental approaches are thus rendered impractical due to their inherent inefficiency, high cost, and prolonged timelines. Furthermore, a fundamental materials challenge persists in multiphase alloys: atomically sharp interfaces between phases serve as barriers to dislocation motion, enhancing strength, but also act as stress concentrators that initiate premature failure, enforcing a frustrating trade-off between strength and ductility. This project aims to overcome these limitations through an integrated machine learning (ML) framework that synergizes two advanced computational approaches. First, we will employ our established generative ML model, based on a conditional variational autoencoder algorithm, to enable rapid discovery of novel eutectic compositions within multicomponent systems. Second, we will introduce a physics-informed regression model, utilizing an artificial neural network architecture, to identify EHEA compositions prone to interfacial segregation. This dual strategy allows for the targeted design of alloys amenable to the formation of chemically and structurally graded interfaces (GIs). Our preliminary results have already demonstrated the successful creation of such GIs in an ML-identified EHEA through carefully designed thermomechanical processing. These engineered interfaces exhibit the ability to concurrently enhance microstructural stability, achieve room-temperature strength-ductility synergy, and enable superplasticity at elevated temperatures, although the underlying mechanisms remain to be fully elucidated. On a fundamental level, this research will utilize the ML framework to discover new EHEAs with graded interfaces and will combine advanced characterization techniques with multi-scale atomistic simulations to investigate the formation mechanisms of GIs and their influence on mechanical behavior. The resulting data and physical insights will inform the optimization of thermomechanical processing parameters to tailor GIs for superior mechanical performance. If funded, this work will not only deliver experimentally validated EHEAs with exceptional properties but will also establish a versatile and powerful ML platform applicable to a wide range of alloy systems, thereby accelerating materials discovery for broad engineering applications. 共晶高熵合金代表了先進材料設計的前沿，兼具優異的可鑄性、高強度與出色的延展性。然而，由於高熵體系固有的廣闊且尚未探明的成分空間缺乏傳統相圖參考，此類合金的發現面臨阻礙。因此，傳統的試錯實驗方法因其固有的低效、高成本與長週期而難以為繼。此外，多相合金中仍存在一個根本性的材料科學難題：相間原子級尖銳介面雖可作為位錯運動的障礙從而提高強度，但同時也會成為引發早期失效的應力集中點，導致強度與延展性之間陷入難以調和的矛盾取捨。 本項目旨在通過構建一個融合兩種先進計算方法的一體化機器學習框架來突破上述局限。首先，我們將採用基於條件變分自編碼器算法的既有生成式機器學習模型，在多組元體系中快速發現新型共晶成分。其次，我們將引入基於物理信息的迴歸模型，利用人工神經網絡架構識別易發生界面偏析的共晶高熵合金成分。這一雙重策略使得我們能夠有針對性地設計易於形成化學與結構梯度界面的合金。 我們的初步結果已證明，通過精心設計的熱機械處理，可在機器學習篩選出的共晶高熵合金中成功製備出此類梯度界面。這些經過工程設計的界面能夠同時提升微觀組織穩定性、實現室溫下的強塑積協同增益，並在高溫下賦予超塑性，儘管其深層機制尚待充分闡明。 在基礎層面，本研究將利用該機器學習框架發現具有梯度界面的新型共晶高熵合金，並綜合運用先進的表徵技術與多尺度原子模擬，探究梯度界面的形成機制及其對力學行為的影響。由此獲得的數據與物理洞見將反饋至熱機械處理參數的優化中，以實現針對梯度界面的精準調控並獲得更優的力學性能。若獲資助，本工作不僅將交付經實驗驗證且具備卓越性能的共晶高熵合金，還將搭建一個適用於多種合金體系的通用型強大數據平台，從而加速面向廣泛工程應用的材料研發進程。

11202926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11202926.value: 一種用於無線電能傳輸的全新雙頻三功能原理

11202926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11202926.value: Wireless power transfer (WPT) is rapidly transforming industries such as consumer electronics, electric vehicles and robotics by enabling contactless energy delivery. However, a persistent challenge in WPT systems is achieving soft switching across the full operating range of the transmitter power inverter. This is important because emerging wireless charging standards such as the International Telecommunications Union in Europe set new recommendation in late 2024 to use the Mega-Hertz frequency range for WPT. Soft-switching is essential for minimizing switching losses, reducing electromagnetic interference (EMI), and enhancing system reliability—especially in high-frequency (Mega-Hertz) applications mandated by emerging wireless charging standards. Conventional methods often fail under light-load or no-load conditions, leading to degraded efficiency and compromised performance. This research introduces a new Bi-Frequency Trifunctional Principle that exploits the bifurcation (frequency-splitting) phenomenon between a magnetically coupled Transmitter resonator and a Relay resonator as an “integrated” structure. At bifurcation, two resonant frequencies, namely a low bifurcation frequency (f-) and a high bifurcation frequency (f+), co-exist at a specific magnetic coupling coefficient. By carefully designing f- to be the fundamental frequency and f+ to be close to 3f- (i.e third harmonic frequency), this Bi-Frequency Trifunctional principle skillfully allows: (1) WPT between transmitter and receiver resonators at the fundamental frequency. (2) Soft switching of the transmitter power inverter using coupled current at the third harmonic frequency even under no-load condition. (3) Enhanced effective mutual inductance between the transmitter and receiver resonator, resulting in higher WPT capability and energy efficiency. The proposal requires only the addition of a simple relay resonator, making it an extremely low-cost and scalable solution. It can significantly reduce switching losses, thermal stress, and EMI emissions, thereby extending the lifespan of power electronic components. It is compatible with existing inverter topologies and can be seamlessly integrated into modern WPT architectures without substantial redesign. Preliminary simulations have confirmed its feasibility for full-range soft-switching and improved efficiency under various load conditions. This project will investigate various arrangements of the integrated transmitter and receiver resonator structures using discrete components and/or circuit printing technologies, paving the way for mass production. Since this new principle is applicable to both existing wireless charging standards (100 kHz-1MHz) and emerging standards (1MHz-13.56MHz), this innovation could redefine WPT design principles, offering a resilient, efficient, and scalable solution for existing and next-generation WPT systems. The success of this project will place Hong Kong as a leading innovation hub in WPT technology. 摘要 無線電力傳輸（Wireless Power Transfer, WPT）正迅速改變消費電子、電動車及機器人等產業。然而，在整個操作範圍內實現發射端功率逆變器的全範圍軟切換（Soft Switching），仍然是WPT系統的一項關鍵技術挑戰。隨著國際電信聯盟（ITU）於2024年底建議未來WPT系統採用MHz級頻率，高頻運作下的軟切換變得更加重要，因為它能有效降低開關損耗、減少電磁干擾（EMI）並提升系統可靠性。傳統方法在輕載或空載條件下往往無法維持軟切換，導致效率下降及性能受損。 本研究提出一種創新的「雙頻三功能原理（Bi-Frequency Trifunctional Principle）」。該方法利用發射端共振器與中繼共振器（Relay Resonator）形成整合結構後所產生的分岔（Bifurcation／頻率分裂）現象。在特定磁耦合係數下，系統會同時產生低分岔頻率（f−）及高分岔頻率（f+）。透過精心設計，使f−作為基頻，而f+接近3f−（第三次諧波頻率），該架構可同時達成： 1. 在基頻下實現發射端與接收端之間的無線電力傳輸。 2. 利用第三次諧波耦合電流，使發射端逆變器即使在空載條件下仍能維持軟切換。 3. 提升發射端與接收端之間的有效互感量，進而提高傳輸能力與能源效率。 此方案只需增加一個簡單的中繼共振器即可實現，因此成本低、易於擴展，且可與現有逆變器拓撲結構相容，無需大幅修改現有WPT系統架構。其優點包括降低開關損耗、減少熱應力、降低EMI，並延長電力電子元件壽命。初步模擬結果已驗證其在不同負載條件下具備全範圍軟切換及效率提升的可行性。 未來研究將進一步探討使用離散元件及／或電路印刷技術建構整合式發射端與接收端共振器結構，以推動大量生產。 由於此新原理同時適用於現有無線充電標準（100 kHz至1 MHz）及新興標準（1 MHz至13.56 MHz），有望重新定義WPT系統的設計原則，提供更具韌性、高效率且可擴展的解決方案。若研究成功，將有助於鞏固香港在無線電力傳輸技術領域的國際創新領導地位。

11203726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11203726.value: 面向高性能固態鋰電池的界面工程

11203726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11203726.value: Achieving carbon neutrality within the next few decades is an urgent mission to address global climate change, in which rapid adoption of clean energy and a wholesale switch to electric transport is key to reducing carbon emissions. But current market-dominated lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) cannot meet the needs of automotive and grid-scale energy storage because the specific energy is rapidly reaching a theoretical limit, and the operating safety is unsatisfactory due to the flammable nature of organic liquid electrolyte. These limitations highlight the pressing need for next-generation batteries that are more powerful, reliable, and inherently safe. Solid-state lithium batteries (SSLBs) are promising alternatives with high energy densities due to reduced battery packaging attributable to their bipolar stacking manufacture. Moreover, due to the usage of non-flammable solid electrolyte (SE), SSLBs are free of fire issues with enhanced battery safety. However, currently the presence of various interface issues within SSLBs results in huge battery resistance, low Coulombic efficiency, and rapid capacity decay, hindering their wide real-world application. In this project, we will tackle these issues at various levels via synergistic approaches ranging from atomic structure engineering to surface regulation, materials design and manufacturing. Specifically, stable cathode/SE interfaces within SSLBs will be established via performing tetrahedral site modification at cathode surface to prevent the hazardous interfacial transition metal diffusion, as well as introducing coherent perovskite phases as local oxygen reservoir to eliminate oxygen at the interface. Meanwhile, highly compatible SE interfaces will be developed through the design of polymer electrolytes with characteristics of self-healing ability, high ionic conductivity, and strong adhesion. Furthermore, the long-standing instability issues between the lithium anode and SE will be tackled by creating novel interphases, including intermolecular ionic layers and liquid-metal interphases, that can effectively suppress Li dendrite formation and growth. More importantly, this project will integrate state-of-the-art ex situ and in situ characterization techniques with computational modelling to establish a quantitative correlation between SE, interphase and performance, enabling scientific design principles of SE and interphase, and guiding the development of high-performance solid-state batteries. The anticipated breakthroughs will not only generate patents and new industrial opportunities but also advance interdisciplinary knowledge, redefine the frontiers of energy storage, and revolutionize battery technologies. Ultimately, project outcomes will deliver safer and more powerful energy storage systems for electric vehicles and smart grids, supporting the global transition to a decarbonized economy. 實現碳中和是應對全球氣候變遷的迫切使命，其中快速推廣清潔能源以及全面轉向電動運輸，是減少碳排放的關鍵。然而，目前市場主導的鋰離子電池無法滿足汽車及電網級儲能的需求，因為其比能量正迅速逼近理論極限，且由於有機液態電解質的易燃特性，操作安全性亦不理想。這些局限性突顯出開發下一代更高能量、更可靠且本質安全電池的迫切性。 固態鋰電池是極具前景的替代方案，其具備高能量密度，原因在於雙極堆疊製造方式可減少電池封裝。此外，由於使用不可燃的固態電解質，固態鋰電池無火災疑慮，電池安全性得以提升。然而，目前固態鋰電池內部存在各種界面問題，導致電池阻抗大、庫項目倫效率低，容量快速衰減，阻礙了其廣泛的實際應用。 在本項目中，我們將透過從原子結構工程到表面調控、材料設計與製造等多層級的協同途徑，來解決這些問題。具體而言，我們將透過在陰極表面進行四面體位置修飾，以防止有害的界面過渡金屬擴散，並引入鈣鈦礦相作為局部氧儲存層以消除界面處的氧，從而在固態鋰電池中建立穩定的陰極/固態電解質界面。同時，我們將透過設計具備自癒能力、高離子導電率及強附著特性之聚合物電解質，來開發高度相容的固態電解質界面。此外，我們將透過創造新型界面層來有效抑制鋰枝晶的形成與生長，從而解決鋰陽極與固態電解質之間長期存在的不穩定性問題。更重要的是，本計畫將整合先進的原位表徵技術，並結合計算模擬，以建立固態電解質、界面層與性能之間的關聯，從而確立固態電解質與界面層的科學設計原則，並引導高性能固態電池的開發。 預期之突破不僅將產生專利與新的產業機會，亦將推進跨學科知識、重新定義能源儲存的前沿領域，並革新電池技術。最終，本計畫之成果將為電動車與智慧電網提供更安全且更強大的能源儲存系統，以支持全球邁向脫碳經濟的轉型。

11203926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11203926.value: 利用非線性動力學抑制固有旋轉單元引起的振動

11203926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11203926.value: Rotating machines are everywhere — from the washing machines in our homes to the wind turbines powering our cities, and even the engines and CNC machines driving industry. But these systems often come with a hidden problem: vibration and noise. These disturbances aren’t just annoying — they can cause structural damage, reduce reliability, and shorten the lifespan of the equipment. What makes this issue especially tricky is that these machines operate under constantly changing conditions. The load inside a washing machine shifts unpredictably, and the rotational speed varies widely. Space and cost constraints mean we can’t rely on bulky or expensive vibration control systems. Instead, we need compact, passive solutions that work directly at the source — without interfering with the machine’s function. This project aims to tackle that challenge head-on by harnessing the power of nonlinear dynamics — a field that deals with complex, adaptive behaviors. By designing smart systems with nonlinear stiffness, damping, and inertia, we’re developing innovative vibration suppression technologies like mounts and absorbers that can adjust to real-world conditions. These solutions are not only effective but also easy to implement. Unlike many existing methods that require large space, fixed operating conditions, or active control systems, our approach focuses on practical, scalable designs. We’re building new theoretical foundations and design tools that will lead to benchmark technologies for vibration control — applicable to a wide range of rotating systems including washing machines, wind turbines, centrifuges, engines, and more. 旋轉機械無所不在——從家用的洗衣機到為城市供電的風力發電機，再到驅動工業運轉的引擎和CNC機床。然而，這些系統往往伴隨著一個隱憂：振動與噪音。這些幹擾不僅令人煩惱，還可能導致結構損壞、降低可靠性並縮短設備使用壽命。 這個問題的棘手之處在於，這些機器通常在不斷變化的工況下運作。例如，洗衣機內部的負載會發生不可預測的位移，轉速也會大幅波動。受限於空間和成本，我們無法採用體積龐大或昂貴的振動控制系統；相反，我們需要的是緊湊型被動式解決方案，能夠在不影響機器正常功能的前提下，直接從源頭抑制振動。 本計畫旨在利用非線性動力學（一門研究複雜自適應行為的學科）的力量，直面並解決這項挑戰。透過設計具備非線性剛度、阻尼和慣性特性的智慧系統，我們正在開發創新的振動抑制技術（如減振支座和吸振器），使其能夠適應實際運作工況。這些解決方案不僅成效顯著，而且易於實施。 與許多需要佔用大量空間、依賴固定工況或採用主動控制系統的現有方法不同，我們的方案著重於實用且可擴展的設計。我們正在建構新的理論基礎與設計工具，力求打造振動控制領域的標竿技術，並將其廣泛應用於洗衣機、風力發電機、離心機、引擎等各類旋轉機械系統中。

11204326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11204326.value: 面向高能效無線接取網的淨增益整合微波光子鏈路

11204326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11204326.value: Wireless communication technology has profoundly transformed our daily lives by widespread connectivity. To meet the surging demand for data throughput and spectral efficiency, wireless networks are evolving toward higher-frequency bands, including millimeter-wave and terahertz. However, this shift imposes fundamental limitations in spatial coverage due to the decreasing wavelength of electromagnetics. Increased path loss and reduced propagation range necessitate ultra-dense base station deployments to ensure seamless coverage. Such densification places unprecedented stress on link interconnects from central units to base stations, where conventional copper cable-based solutions suffer from severe frequency-dependent attenuation, bulkiness, and environmental vulnerability. Microwave photonics (MWP) offers a compelling solution by shifting the RF transmission tasks into optical domain, broadly known as radio over fiber (RoF). Leveraging the inherent advantages of photonic systems, this technology has been widely deployed as fronthaul in current 4/5G networks. However, their performance is currently constrained by the limited conversion efficiency of electro-optic (E/O) and opto-electric (O/E) interfaces. The bottleneck results in signal deterioration, driving the extensive deployment of power-hungry electronic amplifiers for loss compensation. This not only increases energy consumption but complicates system design, especially in ultra-dense wireless access scenarios envisioned for future networks. To address these challenges, this project aims to develop highly efficient chip-scale E/O/E interfaces to empower wireless access networks with substantial gain and low noise, eliminating the need for power-hungry amplifiers. The proposed research leverages the PI's expertise in integrated MWP based on thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) platform, where he has previously demonstrated an ultrafast MWP signal processing engine (H. Feng et al., Nature 2024). Specifically, the proposed RoF link involves the optimized E/O conversion circuits based on TFLN platform, and the high-power handling O/E interface based on III-V uni-traveling-carrier photodiode (UTCPD). The exquisite synergy of these building blocks will evolve the RoF links from mere ‘signal pipelines’ to ‘signal booster’. This technology will be accompanied by two proof-of-concept demonstrations, including power amplifier-free data link transmission to achieve energy-efficient fronthaul and electronic-amplifier-free optoelectronic oscillation to provide high-quality carrier sources. These demonstrations highlight the transformative potential of the net-gain MWP link in revolutionizing wireless access architecture. The proposed system aims to deliver green solutions for future wireless communication networks, enabling energy-efficient data transmission and ultra-low phase noise signal generation. This technology could be further extended to millimeter-wave radar and satellite communications, laying the foundation for future Integrated Sensing and Communication and ubiquitous Internet of Things. 無線通訊技術透過廣泛覆蓋的連接能力，深刻改變了我們的日常生活。為滿足資料吞吐量和頻譜效率的爆發式需求，無線網路正朝著毫米波、太赫茲等更高頻段演進。然而，這一趨勢因電磁波波長減少而帶來了空間覆蓋的根本性限制。路徑損耗增加、傳播距離縮短，迫使網路部署超密集基地台以確保無縫覆蓋。這種緻密化給從中央單元到基地台的鏈路互連帶來了前所未有的壓力，傳統銅纜方案在此面臨嚴重的高頻衰減、體積龐大以及易受環境影響等問題。 微波光子學提供了一條極具前景的解決路徑，將射頻傳輸任務移至光域處理，即廣義的光載無線通訊（RoF）技術。借助光子系統的固有優勢，該技術已在目前4G/5G網路的前傳鏈路中廣泛部署。然而，其性能目前受限於電光（E/O）和光電（O/E）轉換效率的瓶頸。這套頸部導致訊號劣化，迫使系統大量部署高功耗電子放大器以補償損耗，這不僅增加了能耗，也使系統設計趨於複雜，尤其是在未來網路所設想的超密集無線存取場景中。 為因應上述挑戰，本專案旨在開發高效能晶片級E/O/E接口，使無線接取網路具備大幅增益和低雜訊特性，因此無需依賴高功耗放大器。擬研究將依托專案負責人在薄膜鈮酸鋰（TFLN）整合微波光子平台方面的專長，團隊先前已在該平台上實現了超高速微波光子訊號處理引擎（H. Feng等，Nature 2024）。具體而言，擬開發的光載無線鏈路包括基於TFLN平台的最佳化電光轉換電路，以及基於III-V族單行載流子光電二極體的高功率處理光電轉換介面。這些建構模組的精妙協同，將使光載無線鏈路從單純的「訊號管道」進化為「訊號增強器」。該技術將配合兩項概念驗證演示，包括：無功率放大器資料鏈路傳輸，以實現高能效前傳；以及無電子放大器光電振盪，以提供高品質載波源。這些演示將充分彰顯淨增益微波光子鏈路在革新無線接入架構方面的變革性潛力。 本專案旨在為未來無線通訊網路提供綠色解決方案，實現高能源效率資料傳輸和超低相位雜訊訊號產生。該技術還可進一步擴展至毫米波雷達和衛星通訊領域，為未來通感整合與泛在物聯網奠定基礎。

11204826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11204826.value: 面向參數多目標最佳化的Top-K集合演化演算法

11204826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11204826.value: In many applications, the objective functions of a multi-objective optimization problem depend not only on the decision variables but also on external (environmental) parameters. For instance, in morphing wing design, aerodynamic performance is determined jointly by shape geometry and flight conditions. The goal is often to find optimal solutions for all possible parameter values. However, there is little effort on such parametric multi-objective optimization problems. Commonly-used multi-objective optimization methodologies are hardly used due to two major challenges: (1) when parameters are continuous variables, there is an infinite number of parameterized multi-objective optimization tasks, and (2) the Pareto optimal set for each task typically forms a manifold, which itself contains infinitely many solutions. Thus, one has to develop and study new concepts and algorithms for addressing this problem. Noting that decision-makers are often only interested in a small subset of top-K solutions for each parameter value, rather than characterizing the entire Pareto set in many real-world settings, this project makes a first attempt to systematically exploit the top-K requirement in parametric multi-objective optimization. Specifically, we will formulate and address two fundamental problems. One is to learn a math model to efficiently approximate the mapping from parameter values to their corresponding top-K solution sets, and the other is to identify the globally optimal top-K solutions under the most favorable parameter value. To achieve these goals, we will integrate techniques from evolutionary computation and machine learning to develop efficient algorithms. The proposed methods will be validated on the shape optimization of morphing wings and non‑morphing underwater gliders, considering flight or gliding conditions such as angle of attack and airspeed as parameters. The outcome of this project will significantly narrow down the gap between multi-objective optimization research and real-world requirements. 在許多應用中，多目標最佳化問題的目標函數不僅依賴決策變量，還依賴外部環境參數。例如，在可變形機翼設計中，機翼的空氣動力學性能由幾何形狀和飛行條件共同決定。此類問題的目標通常是在所有可能的參數取值下尋找最優解，但相關研究仍然較少。其主要挑戰​​在於：（1）當參數為連續變數時，參數多目標最佳化包含無限個最佳化任務；（2）每個任務的帕累托最適解集通常構成一個包含無限多個解的流形。因此，必須開發並研究新的概念和演算法來解決這個問題。鑑於在許多現實場景中，決策者往往只對每個參數值對應的少量 top-K 最適解感興趣，而不是刻畫整個帕累托解集，本項目首次嘗試系統地利用參數化多目標優化中的 top-K 需求。具體而言，我們將提出並解決兩個基本問題：一是學習一個數學模型，高效近似參數值到其對應 top-K 解集之間的映射；二是在最有利的參數值下識別全局最優的 top-K 解集。為實現這些目標，我們將結合進化計算與機器學習技術，開發高效能演算法。所提出的方法將透過可變形機翼和非變形水下滑翔機的外形優化進行驗證，將迎角、空速等飛行或滑翔條件作為參數加以考慮。此計畫的成果將有助於顯著縮小多目標優化研究與現實需求之間的差距。

11205726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11205726.value: 微曝氣厭氧消化（MAAD）實現氮去除與生物能源回收協同突破：效能與生物機制研究

11205726.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11205726.value: Prof Han, Ping Prof HSU, Shu-Chien Prof Li, Xiaoyan

11205726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11205726.value: Globally, energy and environmental sustainability transition are crucial for meeting Net Zero target. This is especially true for mega cities such as Hong Kong, which has placed increased importance on waste treatment facilities to become truly sustainable. Organic solid waste plays a vital role in enabling the energy-environment nexus but is hindered by technological challenges. Anaerobic digestion (AD) technology is widely-applied for the bioconversion of organic solid waste to bioenergy. However, AD has inherent limitations in (1) bioenergy production due to the rate-limiting hydrolysis degradation of recalcitrant compounds, and (2) pollution control due to poor ammonia-nitrogen removal. Hence, it is imperative to seek innovative solutions to enhance pollution control and bioenergy harvesting from organic solid waste. Micro-aerated anaerobic digestion (MAAD), which involves the introduction of oxygen at nano to micromolar levels, is a promising technology to improve bioenergy recovery and pollution control. Our preliminary study demonstrated that compared to AD, MAAD enhanced methane production (0.93 L CH4/d), resulting in an 18% increase in methane yield (0.49 L CH4/g VSS added), achieving 75% of the theoretical yield. Unexpectedly, MAAD produced 5 times more nitrogen gas (~0.2 L N2/d) during a transient period of micro-aeration cessation. Using pure simple glucose and nitrogen substrates, MAAD completely metabolized glucose, producing similar methane yield as AD but showed a twofold increase in ammonia nitrogen removal efficiency and 4.5 times higher nitrogen gas production. This discovery presents the exciting prospect that MAAD could achieve both methane production and ammonia-nitrogen removal under intermittent micro-aeration condition. However, such a coupled process is not well-understood for digester system and many critical aspects necessary to achieve this endeavor are unknown, necessitating a comprehensive study. Using HK’s sewage sludge as substrate, this proposal aims to investigate MAAD’s capacity for simultaneous methane production and ammonia-nitrogen removal. Specifically, this proposal will (1) determine the optimal oxygen dosing regime to maximize concurrent methane production and nitrogen removal, (2) elucidate the biomechanisms underpinning the metabolic coupling of methane production and nitrogen removal, and (3) evaluate MAAD’s economic feasibility and technological benefits for prospective real-world application. The unprecedented first-hand insights gained from this study will form a core scientific knowledge scaffold, crucial for advancing the fundamental understanding of microbial processes in micro-aerated niche environments. These insights will also guide the long-term development of MAAD and other micro-aerated biotechnologies, paving the way for potential pilot trials, commercialization, and industrial applications.

11206426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11206426.value: 城市排水系統的可觀測性與最佳化監測

11206426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206426.value: Urban drainage system (UDS) overflows are a major driver of urban waterway pollution, largely caused by suboptimal use of network conveyance capacity during wet weather. Real-time control (RTC) mitigates overflows by optimizing the use of UDS hydraulic capacity, making it a critical tool for UDS management—but it relies on comprehensive network monitoring. High costs of procuring, installing, and maintaining monitoring equipment for large-scale UDS restrict real-time monitoring to only a limited number of strategic locations, posing key challenges: selecting appropriate sensor types, determining optimal placement, and extracting maximum actionable information from limited data to support RTC. This project aims to develop a theoretical framework and advanced algorithms to address these challenges: (1) optimally design UDS sensor networks (selecting types, quantities, and locations); (2) maximize reconstruction of UDS state variables (e.g., pipe flows, manhole water levels) from data collected via the optimized network. To achieve these goals, we will for the first time develop a UDS-specific observability concept and analysis framework—extending the well-established control domain observability theory to UDS, which are nonlinear networks with both free-surface and pressurized flows. This framework transforms sensor network design into a constrained optimization problem: we select sensor numbers, types, and locations to maximize UDS observability while adhering to resource limits (e.g., cost, device availability). We then construct a hybrid observer by integrating this framework with deep learning: it estimates full UDS states for fully observable systems or critical state subsets for partially observable ones, ensuring robust state reconstruction even with limited data. Finally, we validate these theories/methods via simulations on two benchmark UDS (Astlingen and Chaohu) and a real-life case study in Hong Kong (Shau Kei Wan), in collaboration with local drainage authorities. This project delivers significant value: it addresses a critical gap in the urban water sector, fills a void in UDS observability theory, and resolves longstanding theoretical bottlenecks by accounting for UDS nonlinearity and network topology—pioneering a new research direction. Its approaches also hold transferable value for other engineering systems facing similar nonlinear and topological challenges. The PI and Co-I, with strong expertise in UDS modelling and control, are well-equipped to lead the project to success. The PI’s collaborative ties with Hong Kong’s Drainage Services Department facilitate the real-world implementation and transfer of the project’s technologies. 城市排水系統（UDS）溢流是城市水道污染的主要驅動因素，很大程度上肇因於雨天期間管網輸送容量未能得到最佳化運用。即時控制（RTC）透過最佳化運用城市排水系統的水力容量以減緩溢流，是城市排水系統管理的關鍵工具，然而此技術仰賴完備的管網監測。 大規模城市排水系統之監測設備，其採購、安裝及維護成本高昂，使得即時監測僅能布設於少數策略性位置，衍生出重大挑戰：選取合適的感測器類型、決定最佳布設位置，以及從有限的數據中萃取最多可執行資訊，以支援即時控制。 本計畫旨在建構一套理論架構與進階演算法以解決上述挑戰：(1) 城市排水系統感測器網路之最佳化設計（選定感測器類型、數量與位置）；(2) 透過最佳化感測網路所蒐集的數據，盡可能還原城市排水系統之狀態變數（例如管道流量、檢查井水位）。 為達成上述目標，本研究將首次建立專屬城市排水系統的可觀測性概念與分析架構，將控制領域已發展成熟的可觀測性理論，延伸至同時存在明渠流與壓力流的非線性排水管網。此架構將感測器網路設計轉化為受限最佳化問題：在成本、設備取得等資源限制下，選定感測器數量、類型與布設位置，最大化城市排水系統的可觀測性。接著結合本架構與深度學習建構混合觀測器：針對完全可觀測系統估計完整系統狀態；針對部分可觀測系統則估計關鍵狀態子集，確保即便數據有限仍能穩健重構系統狀態。最後透過兩套基準城市排水系統（Astlingen、巢湖）模擬，並與香港當地排水主管機關合作，於香港筲箕灣進行實務案例研究，驗證本計畫提出的理論與方法。 本計畫具備顯著價值：研究填補城市水領域的關鍵缺口，補足城市排水系統可觀測性理論的空白；透過納入排水系統非線性特徵與管網拓樸，解決長期以來的理論瓶頸，開創全新研究方向。本計畫發展的方法亦可轉移應用至其他面臨相似非線性與拓樸挑戰的工程系統。 本計畫之首席研究員與共同研究員在城市排水系統建模與控制方面擁有扎實專業背景，足以帶領計畫順利完成。首席研究員與香港渠務署維持緊密合作關係，有利本計畫技術於現場落地與成果移轉

11206526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11206526.value: 面向信息物理系統自適應韌性的風險指引與證據驅動防禦規劃框架

11206526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206526.value: Recent cybersecurity surveys report the exponential growth in the frequency and sophistication of cyber threats targeting Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs), driven by advanced system interconnectivity and attackers’ increasing use of AI-powered tools to automate vulnerability identification and exploitation. This produces big economic losses expected to reach US$10.5 trillion in 2025. Among emerging threats, Coordinated Cyber-Physical Attacks (CCPAs) are of particularly concern. CCPAs involve multi-tiered threat actors employing methodical and adaptive strategies to exploit low- to medium-risk vulnerabilities, prioritizing stealth reconnaissance activities that facilitate subsequent attacks on high-risk targets. In practice, the attackers dynamically reconfigure attack paths in response to defensive countermeasures to amplify cascading failures across interconnected infrastructures. This adaptability renders CCPAs highly unpredictable, hindering the development of risk-informed decision-making for proactive defense planning. Moreover, current resource allocation strategies often fail against these challenges because they fragment the coordination between prevention and response systems, ignoring their interdependence required to counter CCPAs. In this project, we propose a risk-informed, evidence-driven framework for adaptive cyber-physical resilience decisions. Built on three interdependent CCPA defense functions—capturing inherent threat behaviors, encoding operational threat contexts, and operationalizing optimal defense resources—the process will convert evidence flows into resilience-oriented investments. First, we will model CCPA scenarios account for inherent uncertainties via Monte Carlo simulation to generate risk-informed empirical evidence on adversarial stealth tactics and their cascade propagation effects. Second, we will encode this evidential knowledge into cross-domain attack path analysis to synthesize defensible vulnerability prioritizations that combines inherent exploitability metrics with dynamic CCPA threat contexts through multi-criteria importance analysis. Finally, we will design a resilience-oriented optimization approach that applies the vulnerability prioritization knowledge to allocate defense resources against CCPAs. By coupling multi-objective deep reinforcement learning with evolutionary game theory, this approach analyzes situational attack paths and co-evolving attacker-defender dynamics to optimize proactive prevention and adaptive response investments within a unified defense system. The proposed framework will be evaluated using established CPS testbeds from our prior research and validated through industry collaboration with our AI/data analytics partner, assessing performance against real-world CCPAs and operational disruption events. 近期網絡安全調查顯示，針對信息物理系統（Cyber-Physical Systems, CPSs）的網絡威脅，其發生頻率及複雜程度均呈指數式增長。這一趨勢主要源於系統互聯程度日益提高，以及攻擊者越來越多地使用人工智能驅動工具自動識別及利用漏洞。由此造成的巨額經濟損失預計於2025年達10.5萬億美元。在各類新興威脅中，協調式網絡物理攻擊（Coordinated Cyber-Physical Attacks, CCPAs）尤其值得關注。CCPA涉及多層級威脅行為者，他們採用系統化且具適應性的策略，先利用低至中等風險的漏洞進行隱蔽偵察，進而為後續針對高風險目標的攻擊創造條件。在實際攻擊中，攻擊者會根據防禦對策動態重構攻擊路徑，從而加劇跨互聯基礎設施的級聯失效。這種自適應能力使CCPA極難預測，嚴重阻礙了以風險為導向的決策制定與主動防禦規劃。此外，現行的資源配置策略往往將「預防系統」與「應對系統」割裂處理，忽略了有效對抗CCPA所需的相互依存關係，削弱了兩者之間的協調性。 本項目提出一個風險感知、證據驅動的信息物理系統自適應韌性決策框架。該框架基於三項相互依存的CCPA防禦功能——刻畫固有威脅行為、編碼運行層面的威脅情境，以及落實最佳防禦資源配置——旨在將動態證據流轉化為具有成本效益、以韌性為導向的投資決策。首先，透過蒙特卡羅模擬，建立涵蓋固有不確定性的CCPA情境模型，針對攻擊者的隱蔽戰術及其級聯傳播效應，生成具備風險資訊的實證依據。其次，將上述證據納入跨域攻擊路徑分析，並結合多準則重要度分析，貫通整合固有可利用性指標與動態CCPA威脅情境，進而輸出具備充分理據的漏洞優先排序結果。最後，設計一套具備情境感知能力、以韌性為導向的優化方法。該方法結合多目標深度強化學習與演化博弈理論，深度分析特定情境下的攻擊路徑及攻防雙方的動態演化關係，從而在統一的防禦體系內，優化主動預防與自適應應對的資源投入。本項目利用先前研究建立的CPS測試平台評估擬議框架，並聯合人工智能與數據分析領域的業界合作夥伴進行實證驗證，以評估該框架在應對真實世界CCPA攻擊及運作中斷事件時的實際表現。

11207126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11207126.value: 磁場輔助製備3D列印水泥基定向自感知複合結構

11207126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11207126.value: Ensuring the long-term durability and safety of concrete structures under service conditions is of paramount importance. To promote intelligent and predictive maintenance, self-sensing cementitious composites incorporating conductive fillers (e.g., graphene) have been developed, allowing real-time detection of stress and crack propagation. However, the widespread adoption of these materials in smart buildings is hindered by the difficulty of achieving uniform filler dispersion while maintaining high sensing efficiency and cost-effectiveness. The integration of self-sensing composites with 3D printing provides a promising route to fabricate customized structural elements with built-in health monitoring capabilities. Despite the potential, this technology still faces challenges related to printability, interlayer bonding, and self-sensing sensitivity. This project will develop magnetically assisted self-sensing 3D printed concrete (3DPC) structures with commercial graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs) and magnetic particles. Leveraging the layer-by-layer deposition characteristic of 3D printing, a magnetic field will be applied during extrusion to induce the alignment of magnetic particles within each deposited layer. The magnetic-driven particle movement is expected to increase extrudability, while the alignment and interconnection of magnetic particles will strengthen buildability and interlayer adhesion. More importantly, the magnetic chains/clusters create conductive bridges for graphene that increase the likelihood of continuous pathways along the field direction, thereby enhancing electrical conductivity and sensing sensitivity. To achieve these objectives, the interactions between GNPs and magnetic particles in cementitious suspensions under magnetic fields will be examined, and their influence on rheological and microstructural evolutions will be clarified. Afterwards, the combined effect of extrusion process and magnetic field on printability, interlayer bonding, mechanical strength, and electrical conductivity of printed filaments will be systematically investigated. Mechanical-electrical models will be developed to correlate structural deformation with piezoresistive response. Through microstructural analyses, the role of magneto-induced particle alignment in anisotropic piezoresistive behavior will be revealed. Ultimately, a framework for designing 3DPC structures with direction-specific sensing behavior will be proposed and validated by the development of structural health monitoring elements. This research introduces innovative opportunities for fabricating self-sensing structures with tailored piezoresistive properties through an in-situ and non-contact manner, even at very low conductive filler concentrations. Beyond serving as self-sensing elements for real-time structural health monitoring in smart prefabricated and modular construction, the developed cementitious materials can also be optimized for use in conductive pavements with possible applications in traffic detection and energy storage. Overall, this project will advance the development of intelligent and sustainable construction materials, supporting the safe operation and maintenance of buildings and infrastructure. 混凝土結構在服役過程中的耐久性和安全性是保障基礎設施可靠運作的關鍵。為滿足智慧預測性維護的需求，摻加導電組分（如石墨烯）的自感知水泥基材料應運而生，可實現對應力狀態和裂紋擴展的即時監測。然而，其在智慧建築中的廣泛應用受到導電組分分散均勻性不足、難以兼顧高感知性能與成本效益等問題的限制。將自感知水泥基材料與3D列印技術結合，為製備具有內建健康監測功能的客製化結構構件提供了新的技術途徑。儘管潛力巨大，該技術仍面臨可列印性、層間黏結性能和自感知靈敏度難以協同提升等關鍵挑戰。 本計畫擬開發磁場輔助製備石墨烯-磁性顆粒複合3D列印自感知混凝土結構。充分利用3D列印逐層沉積的特點，在材料擠出過程中施加磁場，誘導磁性顆粒定向排列。其中，磁場誘導的磁性顆粒移動有望改善可擠出性，而其定向排列與適度團聚將增強可建造性和層間黏結性能。同時，形成的磁性團簇可為石墨烯建構導電橋接結構，提高沿磁場方向形成連續導電網絡的機率，從而顯著提升材料的導電性能和壓阻感知靈敏度。 圍繞著上述目標，本計畫將系統研究磁場下水泥基體系中石墨烯與磁性顆粒的協同作用，闡明其對流變性能和早期微觀結構演變的影響規律；揭示擠出過程與磁場耦合作用對打印性能、層間粘結、力學強度及導電性能的影響機制；建立結構力學與壓阻響應之間的力學-電學模型，實現結構變形與電學訊號的定量關聯；結合微觀結構表徵，揭示磁性顆粒定向排列調控材料各向異性壓阻行為的作用機制。最終，建構面向定向感知功能的3D列印混凝土結構設計理論，並透過自感知結構健康監測元件的開發與驗證，證明其工程應用的可行性。 本研究將為採用原位、非接觸式磁場調控方法，在低導電組分濃度下製備具有定向壓阻特性的自感知結構提供了新的技術途徑。除可作為智慧預製與模組化建築中的結構健康監測元件外，所開發的自感知水泥基材料還有望應用於導電路面、交通檢測及儲能等領域。本計畫將推動智慧化、功能化和永續建築材料的發展，為建築結構與基礎設施的安全服役和智慧維運提供重要的理論基礎和技術支撐。

11207526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11207526.value: 用於活體視網膜成像的高通量、高保真度三維顯微成像平台

11207526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11207526.value: The retina serves as a transparent and accessible window to the central nervous system, enabling direct optical interrogation of neuronal, glial, and vascular networks in living organisms. Two-photon fluorescence microscopy (2PFM) offers unique advantages for retinal imaging, including intrinsic optical sectioning, subcellular resolution, and minimal responsiveness of photoreceptors to near-infrared excitation. However, conventional 2PFM relies on point-by-point scanning, limiting imaging speed and preventing volumetric visualization of fast biological dynamics across large retinal volumes. Moreover, in vivo retinal imaging suffers from severe aberrations, especially under large fields of view where aberrations vary across retinal locations. The fragile nature of the eye further requires low excitation power to minimize photodamage, inevitably resulting in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Together, these limitations hinder 2PFM from capturing rapid structural and functional changes in the living retina. To address these limitations, this project aims to develop a high-throughput, high-fidelity volumetric microscopy platform that integrates Bessel-droplet 2PFM with deep-learning–based adaptive optics (DL-AO) and deep-learning-based denoising. Compared with conventional Bessel-focus-based volumetric imaging, which suffers from strong side lobes and reduced image contrast, the Bessel-droplet excitation employs destructive interference between two concentric illumination rings to suppress side-lobe energy and improve contrast. In parallel, DL-AO and DL-denoising, both designed as self-supervised computational tools, will be implemented to enhance image fidelity. DL-AO will estimate and correct ocular aberrations directly from image data without requiring a wavefront sensor or deformable mirror, while DL-denoising will suppress noise from low-SNR datasets acquired under minimal illumination. Together, these optical and computational innovations will enable high-throughput, high-resolution, and high-SNR volumetric retinal imaging in vivo. Through this project, we aim to establish an integrated platform for high-throughput, high-fidelity volumetric imaging of the mouse retina in vivo. We will (1) construct and characterize a prototype Bessel-droplet 2PFM system designed for retinal imaging, (2) develop an open-source computational toolbox for integrated aberration correction and denoising. As an exemplary application, longitudinal in vivo imaging of retinal angiomatous proliferation will be performed to investigate neurovascular alterations during disease progression. Overall, this project will deliver an imaging framework that unites optical engineering and artificial intelligence for in vivo retinal imaging. Beyond ophthalmic applications in mice, the developed platform can be extended to other tissues or organisms, providing a broadly applicable strategy for high-resolution, large-volume biological imaging. The anticipated outcomes will advance adaptive optical microscopy and computational bioimaging, offering new opportunities to explore neural and vascular function in health and disease. 視網膜是觀察中樞神經系統的重要天然光學窗口，能夠在活體狀態下無創研究神經元、膠質細胞及血管網絡的結構與功能。雙光子螢光顯微鏡具備光學切片能力、亞細胞解析度，以及近紅外激發對視覺感光細胞影響較低等優勢，在視網膜活體成像中具有重要應用價值。然而，傳統雙光子依賴逐點掃描方式，成像速度有限，難以在大範圍視網膜組織中捕捉快速發生的三維生物動態變化。此外，活體視網膜成像亦面臨嚴重像差問題，尤其在大視場成像時，不同視網膜位置所產生的像差具有高度空間變異性。同時，由於眼部組織對光損傷較為敏感，成像通常需要採用較低激發功率，進一步降低影像訊噪比。上述限制使現有雙光子技術難以實現高速、高品質的活體視網膜結構與功能成像。 本項目旨在建立一套高通量、高保真度的活體三維視網膜成像平台，結合貝塞爾液滴光雙光子螢光顯微技術、基於深度學習的自適應光學以及深度學習去噪方法，以突破現有技術限制。相比傳統利用貝塞爾光束進行體積成像的方法容易受到旁瓣干擾及影像對比度下降的問題，貝塞爾液滴光激發模式利用兩個同心照明環之間的相消干涉，有效降低旁瓣能量並提升成像對比度。此外，本項目將開發基於自監督學習的自適應光學及去噪算法，以進一步提升影像質量。其中，深度學習自適應光學可直接根據影像估算並校正眼部像差，無需依賴波前感測器或可變形鏡；深度學習去噪技術則可在低激發功率條件下，有效改善低訊噪比影像的品質。 通過整合先進光學設計與人工智能計算方法，本項目將實現活體視網膜的大範圍、高解析度及高訊噪比三維成像。研究目標包括：（1）建立並系統表徵適用於視網膜成像的貝塞爾液滴光雙光子螢光成像系統；（2）開發用於像差校正及影像去噪的一體化開源計算工具。作為示範應用，本研究將利用長期活體成像技術，研究視網膜血管增生性疾病進展過程中的神經血管變化。 本項目將建立一個融合光學工程與人工智能技術的新型活體視網膜成像框架。除眼科研究應用外，該平台亦有望拓展至其他組織及生物模型，為高解析度、大體積生物成像提供通用技術方案。預期成果將推動自適應光學顯微技術及計算生物成像的發展，並為探索健康及疾病狀態下神經與血管功能提供新的研究途徑。

11207626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11207626.value: AI賦能的構網型光伏系統研究

11207626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11207626.value: The rapid growth of renewable energy, particularly solar photovoltaic (PV), is transforming modern power systems. However, as conventional synchronous generators are gradually phased out, the electrical grid loses its natural stability, inertia, and robustness. Existing PV inverters typically operate in grid-following mode, relying on a strong external voltage source, which limits their ability to support frequency and voltage regulation. To achieve future 100% renewable grids, PV systems must evolve toward grid-forming capability, performing as active, intelligent participants in maintaining grid stability. This project aims to develop a new generation of physics-informed artificial intelligence (AI)-aided control frameworks for grid-forming PV systems and multi-inverter microgrids. By combining physical principles of power electronics with data-driven learning, the proposed research seeks to overcome the limitations of traditional model-based control, which often fails under rapidly changing and uncertain operating conditions. Three main research directions are proposed, which are organized in work packages (WPs). WP1 will develop a physics-informed AI-aided control structure for grid-forming converters, integrating deep reinforcement learning (DRL), transfer learning, and online adaptive tuning to achieve robust, interpretable, and self-learning control. WP2 will apply the framework developed in WP1 to PV systems with and without energy storage, developing adaptive control strategies that optimize both power tracking and system stability under variable sunlight and grid conditions. WP3 will address coordination and compensation in multi-inverter AC microgrids, using AI methods to mitigate voltage imbalances and harmonics at the point of common coupling (PCC), ensuring cooperative and resilient operation among distributed generators. The proposed project will deliver new scientific knowledge in physics-informed machine learning for power electronic converters, bridging the gap between theoretical AI models and practical energy systems. The outcomes will include validated algorithms, real-time hardware prototypes, and an open-source experimental platform to support future development and standardization of grid-forming technologies. Beyond academia, the project will directly benefit renewable energy industry, utilities, and policymakers by providing tools for stable and intelligent renewable integration. Ultimately, it will contribute to building a resilient, carbon-neutral, and AI-empowered power grid, supporting Hong Kong’s long-term “Carbon Neutral 2050” and “Grid 2.0” initiatives. 隨著再生能源，尤其是太陽能光伏（PV）的快速發展，現代電力系統正經歷深刻轉型。然而，隨著傳統同步發電機逐步減少，電網慣性、電壓支撐能力及動態穩定性亦隨之下降。現有光伏逆變器大多採用跟網型（grid-following）控制模式，依賴外部電網提供穩定電壓與頻率參考，其在弱電網環境及高比例再生能源接入場景下，難以有效支撐系統頻率調節、電壓穩定及故障恢復。因此，發展具備主動電網支撐能力的構網型（grid-forming）光伏系統，已成為實現未來高比例甚至百分之百可再生能源電網的重要技術方向。 本研究旨在開發一套基於物理資訊人工智能（physics-informed AI）的智能控制框架，用於新一代構網型光伏系統及多逆變器微電網的穩定運行與協同控制。通過融合電力電子變流器動態模型、電網穩定性約束及數據驅動學習方法，本研究將突破傳統模型控制策略在複雜、不確定及快速變化運行條件下適應能力不足的局限，實現具備自適應、自學習及可解釋能力的智能控制。 本項目將圍繞三個主要研究方向展開： 第一， 建立面向構網型變流器的 AI 輔助控制架構，融合深度強化學習（Deep Reinforcement Learning, DRL）、遷移學習（Transfer Learning）及在線自適應參數調節技術，實現高魯棒性、快速響應及可解釋的構網型控制策略。 第二， 將所提出的 AI 控制框架應用於不同配置的光伏系統，包括獨立光伏系統及光伏儲能系統，研究在變化光照、負載波動及弱電網條件下兼顧最大功率追蹤、頻率支撐及電壓穩定的自適應控制方法。 第三， 研究多逆變器交流微電網中的協同控制與補償技術，利用 AI 方法優化分布式能源單元間的功率共享，降低公共耦合點（Point of Common Coupling, PCC）的電壓不平衡及諧波影響，提升微電網整體韌性與可靠性。 本研究將建立物理資訊機器學習與電力電子控制相結合的新型理論與技術體系，推動 AI 從理論算法向實際能源系統應用轉化。預期成果包括新型 AI 控制算法、實時硬件驗證平台及開源實驗系統，為構網型技術的標準化與工程應用提供重要支撐。 研究成果將直接服務於再生能源產業、電力企業及電網規劃部門，為高比例可再生能源接入提供智能化、可靠及韌性的技術方案。最終，本研究將支持香港「2050 年碳中和」及未來智能電網（Grid 2.0）發展目標，助力建設低碳、高可靠及 AI 賦能的新一代電力系統。

11208126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11208126.value: 數位孿生輔助邊緣運算中感知資訊時效且時延敏感的智慧服務

11208126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11208126.value: With the explosive growth of mobile devices and development of Artificial Intelligent (AI) applications, we now witness unprecedented booming of machine learning model driven intelligent services. The convergence of AI and mobile edge computing (MEC) has catalysed growing interest in edge intelligence to enable intelligent services in the proximity of network edge. Digital twin (DT) as a disruptive technology has been applied for diverse fields such as autonomous driving, smart healthcare and the metaverse, which provides future insights and perceptions to predict physical object behaviours and help humans with decision-making. This project will investigate Age of Information (AoI) aware, delay-sensitive intelligent services based on machine learning models in a DT-assisted MEC network. It aims to maximize the user satisfaction with services that consists of service accuracy and service latency. To enable high accuracy yet low latency intelligent services in edge computing, each service model must be continually retrained using the update data from the model sources to mitigate its service accuracy degrading, due to data drift. Meanwhile, a user satisfaction on a service is determined by whether the actual service delay meets the user's specified delay requirement. The study of AoI-aware, delay sensitive intelligent services in DT-assisted MEC networks poses several important challenges: (1) How to develop novel metrics to measure the service accuracy of each service model and user satisfactions? How to model dynamic resource consumptions of service model retraining and user request admissions? (2) Due to limited computing resource in the MEC network, what is the proportional amount of computing resource allocated for model retraining? should which service models and user requests be chosen for retraining and admissions simultaneously? (3) How to accurately predict future user requests for different service models in order to deploy their requested models in advance? how to utilize DT and machine learning technologies to predict user service demands in future? (4) Should which resolution of a multi-resolution service model be chosen for a request while meeting its service accuracy and delay requirements? This project will conduct cutting-edge research on high service accuracy, delay sensitive intelligent services in DT-assisted MEC networks, and develop a suite of novel solutions for such services. It will substantially contribute to the development of innovative machine learning algorithms and enabling techniques for intelligent services to maximize the user satisfaction. It will also deepen our understanding on jointly choosing service models for retraining and user requests for admissions. 隨著行動裝置的爆發式成長和人工智慧（AI）應用的發展，我們見證了由機器學習模式驅動的智慧服務的空前繁榮。 AI與行動邊緣運算（MEC）的融合激發了人們對「邊緣智慧」的濃厚興趣，旨在網路邊緣附近實現智慧服務。作為一項顛覆性技術，數位孿生（DT）已被應用於自動駕駛、智慧醫療和元宇宙等多個領域，它透過提供前瞻性的洞察與感知，能夠預測物理物件的行為並輔助人類進行決策。本計畫將研究在DT輔助的MEC網路中，基於機器學習模型的、感知「資訊新鮮度」（AoI）且對延遲敏感的智慧服務。其目標是最大化用戶對服務的滿意度，該滿意度由服務準確度和服務時延共同決定。為了在邊緣運算中實現高準確度且低時延的智慧服務，必須利用來自模型來源的更新資料持續重新訓練每個服務模型，以緩解因資料漂移而導致的服務準確度下降問題。同時，使用者對服務的滿意度取決於實際服務延遲是否符合使用者設定的延遲要求。在DT輔助的MEC網路中研究感知AoI且對時延敏感的智慧服務，面臨若干重要挑戰：（1）如何制定新的指標來衡量每個服務模式的準確度及使用者滿意度？如何對服務模型重訓練和使用者請求接納過程中的動態資源消耗進行建模？ （2）鑑於MEC網路中的運算資源有限，應分配多少比例的運算資源用於模型重訓練？應同時選擇哪些服務模型進行重訓練以及接納哪些使用者請求？ （3）如何準確預測針對不同服務模型的未來使用者請求，以便預先部署對應的模型？如何利用DT和機器學習技術預測未來的使用者服務需求？ （4）在滿足服務準確度和時延要求的前提下，針對特定請求應選擇多解析度服務模型中的哪一種解析度？本計畫將針對DT輔助MEC網路中的高準確度、時延敏感型智慧服務進行前沿研究，並開發一套針對此類服務的新穎解決方案。這將大大促進創新機器學習演算法及賦能技術的開發，從而為智慧服務提供支持，最大限度地提升用戶滿意度；同時，這也將加深我們對「聯合選擇用於再訓練的服務模型」與「用戶接入請求」之間關係的理解。

11208226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11208226.value: 在多智能體系統高機率收斂分析下實現去中心化的高效率資料交換的優化與學習

11208226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11208226.value: Decentralized optimization and learning (DOL) have emerged as powerful approaches for large-scale systems, with successful applications in diverse domains such as natural language processing, smart grids, and wireless networks. Unlike centralized methods, DOL enables agents to collaboratively optimize a global objective function using only their local data while exchanging information with neighboring agents. This decentralized framework offers several key advantages, including improved robustness, enhanced data privacy, and strong scalability. Data exchange among agents is critical to guarantee convergence in DOL. However, existing methods face two fundamental challenges: (1) excessively high data-exchange frequency, where agents exchange data at every iteration; and (2) large data-exchange volume, often due to the transmission of multiple complete high-dimensional variables. These issues create significant data-exchange overhead, limiting the scalability and practical deployment of DOL in bandwidth-constrained or resource-limited environments. This proposal aims to address these challenges by developing a unified framework for data-exchange-efficient DOL based on two complementary strategies: -Reducing data-exchange frequency; -Reducing data-exchange volume. The proposed approach supports heterogeneity in the number of local updates across agents and an increasing number of local updates over communication rounds, combined with appropriately designed step-size schemes, to reduce data-exchange frequency. It further introduces stochastic quantization methods and single-variable communication protocols to reduce data-exchange volume. The convergence behavior of the proposed methods will be rigorously analyzed to ensure robust performance across a range of decentralized scenarios. Furthermore, this proposal aims to establish new theoretical foundations and algorithms that offer strong convergence guarantees, with a particular focus on high probability convergence analysis. High probability guarantees provide stronger reliability by ensuring that algorithms perform well with overwhelming likelihood, rather than merely on average. Such guarantees are essential in safety-critical domains and practical scenarios with limited algorithm runtime, where expectation-based guarantees are often insufficient. The research outcomes will enhance the robustness, efficiency, and scalability of decentralized optimization and learning, providing a solid theoretical foundation for practical multi-agent systems. 優化與學習的去中心化（DOL）已成為大規模系統的強大方法，並在自然語言處理、智慧電網和無線網路等多個領域成功應用。與集中式方法不同，DOL 允許智能體僅使用其本地資料協作優化全域目標函數，同時與相鄰智能體交換資訊。這種去中心化框架具有多項關鍵優勢，包括更高的穩健性、更強的資料隱私性和更強的可擴展性。 智能體之間的資料交換對於確保 DOL 的收斂性至關重要。然而，現有方法面臨兩大挑戰：（1）資料交換頻率過高，智能體在每次迭代中都交換資料；（2）資料交換量過大，通常是因為傳輸多個完整的高維變數所致。這些問題會造成顯著的資料交換開銷，限制 DOL 在頻寬受限或資源有限的環境中的可擴展性和實際部署。本提案旨在透過建立一個基於兩種互補策略的統一框架來應對這些挑戰，該框架用於實現高效的資料交換分散式學習（DOL）： 降低資料交換頻率； 降低資料交換量。 所提出的方法支援代理間局部更新數量的異質性，並允許在通訊輪次中增加局部更新的數量，同時結合適當設計的步長方案來降低資料交換頻率。本提案方法還引入了隨機量化方法和單變量通訊協定來降低資料交換量。我們將對所提出方法的收斂行為進行嚴格分析，以確保其在各種去中心化場景下均具有穩健的效能。 此外，本提案旨在建立新的理論基礎和演算法，以提供強大的收斂保證，特別著重於高機率收斂分析。高機率保證透過確保演算法在極高機率下而非僅在平均水準上表現良好，從而提供更強的可靠性。在安全攸關的領域和演算法運行時間有限的實際場景中，此類保證至關重要，因為基於期望的保證往往不足以應對這些情況。研究成果將提升分散式最優化和學習的穩健性、效率和可擴展性，為實際的多智能體系統提供堅實的理論基礎。

11208426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11208426.value: 甲殼類廢棄物資源化製備面向建築應用的高性能可生物降解被動輻射冷卻材料

11208426.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11208426.value: Prof Chopra, Shauhrat Singh Prof Tso, Chi Yan

11208426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11208426.value: Space cooling accounts for up to 40% of total building electricity consumption in dense subtropical cities like Hong Kong. Passive radiative cooling (PRC) offers a zero-energy pathway to relieve the increasing cooling demand by lowering sky-facing surface temperatures through solar reflection and thermal emission. However, most scalable PRC designs rely on petrochemical-derived polymers that are non-biodegradable and persist as pollutants. This creates a critical paradox in which technologies intended to reduce climate impact may themselves pose sustainability challenges. This project aims to tackle this paradox by a "waste-to-cooling" strategy, developing fully biodegradable PRC materials (FB-PRCs) derived exclusively from crustacean shell waste. Chitin, the main component of waste extraction, features a naturally high refractive index in the solar spectrum and strong molecular vibrations in the mid-infrared, making it intrinsically suited for efficient solar scattering and radiative heat dissipation. Its inherent processability enables the scalable fabrication of tunable multiscale structures, allowing controllable engineering of optical properties. Initial experimental validation supports the promise. Without structural optimization, chitin microparticles derived from local shell waste and compacted into a solid achieve a solar reflectance of 90±2% and a thermal emissivity of 93±2%, providing a robust baseline. Despite the compelling potential, the fundamental science governing chitin's optical-thermal performance remains largely unexplored. Critical knowledge gaps persist, specifically in understanding the relationships between waste source, extraction parameters, structural morphology, and the resulting optical constants. This lack of knowledge prevents rational design of FB-PRCs. Furthermore, comprehensive life cycle assessments (LCAs) are absent, leaving the true environmental trade-offs and long-term viability of such bio-derived PRCs unquantified. To address these gaps, this project will systematically examine the influence of biomass origin and processing parameters on extraction’s optical constants, incorporating these findings into a hybrid optical modeling framework that combines the Lorenz–Mie scattering theory and Monte Carlo ray-tracing to predict light–matter interactions. Insights from this model will guide the fabrication and optimization of different FB‑PRC architectures, including packed‑particle solids, porous coatings, and fibrous membranes, through controlled tuning of structural morphology. The coupling between optical‑thermal performance and environmental sustainability will then form the basis for assessing their practical applicability and ecological impact. By bridging materials science, optical modeling, and LCA, this research aims to establish a unified framework for developing sustainable and high‑performance PRC solutions tailored for next‑generation thermal management applications. 在香港這類高密度亞熱帶城市中，室內製冷能耗最高可佔建築總用電量的 40%。被動式輻射冷卻（PRC）透過反射太陽輻射並發射熱輻射，降低朝天表面的溫度，從而以零能耗的方式緩解日益攀升的冷卻需求。然而，多數具備規模化潛力的 PRC 設計仍高度仰賴源自石化原料的聚合物材料。這類材料通常不可生物降解，且可能在環境中長期累積並成為污染物。這造成了一個關鍵悖論：原本旨在緩解氣候危機的技術，其本身卻對永續發展構成壓力。本提案旨在開發完全由甲殼類殼體廢棄物衍生、且可完全生物降解的PRC材料（FB-PRCs），以廢棄物高值化策略回應這一挑戰。幾丁質是此類廢棄殼體中萃取得到的主要成分，其在太陽光譜範圍內具有天然較高的折射率，並在中紅外波段展現強烈的分子振動吸收特徵，因此在材料本質上非常適合用於高效率的太陽光散射與輻射散熱。此外，幾丁質本身具備良好的可加工性，可實現規模化製備，並建構可調控的多尺度結構，進而對其光學性質進行可控設計。初步實驗結果已顯示其具備良好的開發潛力：在尚未進行結構優化的情況下，由本地殼體廢棄物製得的幾丁質微粒經壓實成固體後，即可達到 90±2% 的太陽反射率與 93±2% 的熱輻射率，為後續的結構設計與性能優化奠定了良好的基礎。 儘管其潛力相當引人注目，幾丁質的光熱特性在輻射熱管理領域中仍未被充分探討。尤其對於廢棄物來源、萃取參數、結構形貌與最終光學常數之間關係的理解仍相當有限，這限制了 FB-PRCs 的設計與優化。此外，目前對這類永續熱管理技術仍缺乏完整的生命週期評估；尤其是此類以基於生物質的、可降解的 PRC 材料，其在環境效益方面的優勢及長期應用可行性，仍未被系統性量化。基於上述背景，本提案將系統性探討不同幾丁質廢棄物來源與萃取參數對產物光學常數的影響。以光學常數作為輸入，結合洛倫茲－米氏散射理論與蒙地卡羅光線追跡，構建一套光學數值模型，以預測光與材料之間的交互作用。該模型將被用於指導不同結構形式的FB-PRC的製備與最佳化，包括顆粒組裝材料、多孔塗層以及纖維膜，並透過不同加工工藝中對結構形貌的精準調控達到優化目標性能（如光學性能）的目的。最後，將綜合考量熱管理表現與環境永續性，評估材料的實際應用潛力及其對生態環境的影響。總體而言，本研究將整合材料科學、光學建模與生命週期評估，建立一套統一的研究框架，以研發兼具永續性與高性能的被動式輻射制冷方案，並為下一代熱管理應用材料提供研究參考。

11208826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11208826.value: 資源約束下的基於學習的量子系統表徵

11208826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11208826.value: Quantum computers promise to solve complex problems far beyond the reach of classical machines, yet accurately characterizing quantum systems—understanding how a prepared quantum state or circuit actually behaves—remains a critical scientific challenge. Traditional characterization methods such as quantum state tomography and random measurement protocols require an exponentially increasing number of measurements, labeled data, and computational resources, making them infeasible for large and noisy systems. Recent learning-based approaches offer a potential alternative by using neural networks to infer system properties from measurement data, but they suffer from several key limitations: (i) they often assume access to abundant and ideal training data, which is unrealistic on current quantum devices; (ii) their architectures are directly transferred from classical domains such as vision or language and thus fail to capture the physical structure of quantum systems; and (iii) their performance is inconsistent due to the lack of standard benchmarking and theoretical understanding of efficiency limits. To address these challenges, this project proposes a learning-based framework for quantum system characterization under resource constraints, aiming to systematically study how artificial intelligence can model and verify quantum systems efficiently when measurements, data, and computational resources are limited. To achieve this goal, the project will first construct a standardized benchmarking platform to evaluate characterization methods under unified datasets, model architectures, and performance metrics. It will then develop measurement-efficient protocols that adaptively select measurement bases and purify noisy labels, sample-efficient algorithms that incorporate physical constraints and multimodal pretraining to enhance learning from small and noisy datasets, and computation-efficient simulation models that reformulate classical estimation as a sequential decision process guided by data-driven truncation. Complementing these algorithmic advances, the PI and Co-I will collaborate to establish theoretical efficiency bounds on the computational complexity, providing a rigorous foundation for the proposed framework. The expected outcome is a unified and resource-efficient paradigm for quantum system characterization, delivering both practical algorithms for quantum devices and new theoretical insights into the learnability of quantum systems. The results will enhance Hong Kong’s competitiveness in AI-driven quantum technologies and contribute foundational knowledge toward scalable, intelligent quantum computing. 量子計算有望在分子模擬、材料設計、優化等複雜問題上突破經典計算的能力極限。然而，準確表徵量子系統，即理解製備的量子態或量子線路的實際行為，仍然是一項關鍵的科學挑戰。傳統量子系統表徵方法，例如量子態層析和隨機測量協議，通常需要隨系統規模指數增長的量子測量次數、標註數據數量以及計算資源，因此難以應用於大規模和含噪量子系統。近年來，基於學習的方法為量子系統表徵提供了新的可能，但現有學習方法仍存在幾個關鍵限制：首先，這些方法通常假設能夠獲得大量且理想的訓練數據，而這在當前量子設備中並不現實；其次，其模型架構通常直接借鑒視覺或語言等經典領域的方法，未能充分利用量子系統的物理結構；此外，由於缺乏統一的基準測試體系以及對資源效率邊界的理論理解，不同方法的性能表現難以進行公平比較。針對這些挑戰，本項目提出一個面向資源約束條件下量子系統表徵的學習框架，旨在系統研究當測量、數據和計算資源有限時，如何利用人工智能高效地建模和驗證量子系統。 為實現這一目標，本項目將首先建立標準化基準測試平台，在統一的數據集、模型架構和評價指標下系統評估量子系統表徵方法。隨後，本項目將發展高效測量策略，通過自適應選擇測量基和噪聲標籤凈化方法，降低獲取量子信息和高質量訓練標籤所需的測量成本；進一步結合量子系統物理約束和測量數據與量子線路之間的多模態預訓練方法，提高模型在小規模和含噪數據條件下的學習能力和泛化性能；同時發展計算高效的量子模擬方法，將經典量子系統表徵中的計算過程重新建模為由數據驅動的決策過程，通過智能優化降低大規模量子系統模擬的計算開銷。此外，本項目將從理論角度研究計算複雜度、數據需求和測量資源之間的基本關係，為資源高效的量子系統表徵提供理論基礎。預期成果將建立一個統一且資源高效的量子系統表徵框架，提供適用於不同量子平台的可擴展算法和工具，推動人工智能驅動的量子技術發展，並為未來大規模量子硬件驗證、優化和實際應用提供重要支撐。

11209026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11209026.value: 網絡化多智能體系統的分散式異步約束優化及其應用

11209026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11209026.value: Distributed optimization of networked multi-agent systems has attracted tremendous research interest due to its broad engineering applications, such as distributed control of multiple mobile robots, distributed resource allocation of microgrids, and so on. Many theories and methodologies have been developed for distributed constrained optimization of networked multi-agent systems, but most on decoupled constraints rather than coupled constraints. The recent literature review reveals that existing distributed optimization approaches with coupled constraints only achieve sublinear or asymptotic convergence under clock synchronization. It should be noted that these synchronous algorithms require a relatively large number of iterations to reach optimal solutions and that clock synchronization is very difficult to implement. In addition, these synchronous algorithms often suffer from poor optimization efficiency. It is thus more desirable to develop distributed asynchronous constrained optimization algorithms with linear convergence rates as they not only reduce the number of iterations but also eliminate the need for clock synchronization, thereby improving optimization efficiency. Furthermore, existing distributed synchronous algorithms are developed for networked multi-agent systems without considering cyber-attacks though they often exist in practical communication networks and their presence often leads to performance degradation, or even worse, system failure. One typical cyber-attack is the so-called denial-of-service attacks, which affect the timeliness of information transfer by blocking or destroying the network connectivity. Thus the study of distributed asynchronous constrained optimization for networked multi-agent systems under denial-of-service attacks has both theoretical and practical significance. Motivated by these observations, this project proposes to investigate and develop novel distributed asynchronous optimization algorithms with linear convergence rates for networked multi-agent systems under coupled constraints and denial-of-service attacks. In particular, we will investigate the following three problems: (i) the problem of distributed asynchronous optimization with linear convergence of networked multi-agent systems under coupled constraints over undirected communication graphs; (ii) the problem of distributed asynchronous optimization with linear convergence of networked multi-agent systems under coupled constraints over directed communication graphs; and (iii) the problem of distributed asynchronous optimization with linear convergence of networked multi-agent systems under both coupled constraints and denial-of-service attacks. This project, by addressing these problems, will explore and develop novel distributed asynchronous optimization theories and methodologies for networked multi-agent systems under coupled constraints and denial-of-service attacks over undirected/directed communication graphs. The outcomes of this project are expected to be novel fundamental theories and methodologies which would provide more solid analysis and synthesis tools in distributed asynchronous constrained optimization of networked multi-agent systems. 網絡化多智能體系統的分佈式優化在多機器人的分佈式控制、微電網的分佈式資源配置等領域有著廣泛的工程應用，因而吸引了大量的研究興趣。目前已有許多關於多智能體系統的分佈式約束優化的理論與方法，但多數研究側重於解耦約束而非耦合約束。最近的文獻綜述表明，現有的含耦合約束的分佈式優化算法只有在時鐘同步下才能實現次線性或漸近收斂。需要指出的是，這些同步算法往往需要較多的迭代次數才能收斂至最優解，且時鐘同步在實際中實現困難。此外，這類同步算法由於同步等待，其優化效率通常較低。因此，開發具有線性收斂速率的分佈式異步約束優化算法更具價值。這類算法不僅能減少迭代次數，還能消除對時鐘同步的依賴，從而顯著提升優化效率。不僅如此，現有的分佈式同步算法普遍忽略了網絡攻擊對多智能體系統的影響。網絡攻擊在實際通信網絡中頻繁發生，其存在往往會導致系統性能下降，甚至引發系統癱瘓。拒絕服務（DoS）攻擊是一種典型的網絡攻擊，它通過阻塞或破壞網絡連通性來影響信息傳輸的時效性。因此，研究拒絕服務（DoS）攻擊下網絡化多智能體系統的分佈式異步約束優化問題，兼具重要的理論意義與實際價值。基於上述考量，本項目針對耦合約束和拒絕服務（DoS）攻擊下的網絡化多智能體系統，研究並開發具有線性收斂速率的新型分佈式異步優化算法。具體而言，我們將重點研究以下三個問題：（i）無向通信圖下，含耦合約束的網絡化多智能體系統的分佈式異步線性收斂優化問題；（ii）有向通信圖下，含耦合約束的網絡化多智能體系統的分佈式異步線性收斂優化問題；（iii）同時面臨耦合約束與拒絕服務（DoS）攻擊時，網絡化多智能體系統的分佈式異步線性收斂優化問題。本項目通過解決上述問題，旨在深入探索並開發無向/有向通信圖下，面臨耦合約束與拒絕服務（DoS）攻擊的網絡化多智能體系統的分佈式異步優化新理論與新方法。本項目的預期成果將形成一系列新穎的基礎理論與方法體系，從而為網絡化多智能體系統的分佈式異步約束優化提供更為堅實的分析與設計工具。

11209426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11209426.value: 6G 無線系統中大規模靈活天線的近場感知與通訊

11209426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11209426.value: Every leap in wireless systems from 2G to 5G has been propelled by relentless advancements in antenna technology, progressing from basic single-element antenna designs to today's sophisticated massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems.
