Objective 3: Develop stakeholder-informed decision-support tools for optimizing NEV integration strategies. Generates actionable recommendations across six decision domains: vehicle selection, charging/refueling infrastructure siting, energy mix optimization, route planning, end-of-life disposal, and financial incentive design. Expected Impact: The framework enables Hong Kong's transport planners to make evidence-based decisions that strengthen MPTN resilience while achieving ambitious decarbonization targets. Practical applications include strategic NEV deployment that matches vehicle capabilities to route vulnerabilities, optimal infrastructure placement that maintains service continuity during extreme weather, and sustainable fleet transition strategies that minimize both costs and environmental impacts. 香港公共運輸向新能源車輛（NEVs）的轉型帶來一項複雜挑戰：在加速的氣候變遷下，平衡環境效益與系統韌性。本研究開發一個整合性決策支援架構，以因應規劃香港多模式公共運輸網路（MPTN）時的關鍵權衡取捨。 挑戰：雖然新能源車輛提供比化石燃料更潔淨的替代方案，但它們也帶來現有規劃方法無法充分因應的新氣候脆弱性。電動車依賴電網，而極端高溫會透過降低水力發電效率與增加冷卻需求而損害電網。氫能車在極端天氣事件期間，當配送網路失效時，會面臨供應鏈中斷。若未將韌性考量系統性地納入新能源車輛規劃，這些氣候驅動的風險可能抵消環境效益。 知識缺口：全球城市皆體認到多元能源與運輸組合能增強基礎設施韌性，但現行規劃工具缺乏將此原則轉化為可行新能源車輛整合策略所需的路線層級細部分析。香港的獨特背景——90% 的公共運輸使用率，以及道路基礎設施無法吸收運輸中斷的高密度都市環境——使得系統性韌性規劃對新能源車輛部署的成功格外關鍵。 研究解決方案：本計畫建立一套全面的決策支援架構，同時優化環境績效（減少二氧化碳排放）、經濟永續性（可負擔的生命週期成本）與韌性（整備、應變、復原及調適能力）。該架構以路線層級運作，引導香港各種運輸模式中實際的新能源車輛整合決策。 目標 1：建立香港現有多模式公共運輸網路在路線層級的基線績效指標。 這為對照現有系統績效來評估新能源車輛替代方案建立實證基礎。 目標 2：模擬未來新能源車輛整合情境，以辨識香港運輸網路中的績效權衡取捨。 每個情境都經過嚴格評估，包括生命週期環境影響、經濟成本，以及系統韌性指標的變化，以揭示關鍵權衡。 目標 3：開發經利害關係人意見納入的決策支援工具，以優化新能源車輛整合策略。 在六個決策領域中產生可付諸實行的建議：車輛選擇、充電／加氫基礎設施選址、能源組合優化、路線規劃、報廢處置，以及財務誘因設計。 預期影響：該架構使香港的運輸規劃者能夠做出以證據為基礎的決策，在達成宏大脫碳目標的同時，強化多模式公共運輸網路的韌性。實際應用包括：將車輛能力與路線脆弱性相匹配的策略性新能源車輛部署、在極端天氣期間維持服務持續性的最佳基礎設施配置，以及同時最小化成本與環境影響的永續車隊轉型策略。

11217326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11217326.value: 一个描述非富勒烯受体有机太阳能电池中激发态的能量、动力学和空间信息的统一模型

11217326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217326.value: The escalating global energy demand and achieving carbon neutrality necessitates the rapid development of renewable sources, with solar power holding immense potential to meet this need. Organic solar cells (OSCs) present a promising photovoltaic technology due to their advantages of low-cost solution processability, mechanical flexibility, and tunable optoelectronic properties. The emergence of non-fullerene acceptors (NFAs) has been a revolutionary breakthrough, propelling OSC power conversion efficiencies beyond 20%. However, despite remarkable performance achieved, understanding on the fundamental photophysical mechanisms still lag behind, hindering further enhancement of device efficiency. Currently, two critical and debated focuses are the exact driving force required for efficient charge generation and the energetic levels of excited states that governs open-circuit voltage loss. The major difficulties leading to these controversies are ambiguous energy-level assignment and inconsistent dynamic information observed from different measurement techniques. This lack of a coherent mechanistic understanding represents a major bottleneck to the rational design of next-generation materials and device structures. To address these challenges, in this project we propose a comprehensive investigation method using multiple in-situ spectroscopic techniques, especially including an ultrafast two-photon photoelectron spectroscopy (2PPE) that can simultaneously provide energetic, temporal and spatial information of excited states. By integrating 2PPE with in-situ ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) and transient absorption (TA), we aim to ambiguously resolve the energetic landscapes, interconversion dynamics and spatial locations of these excited states. In our preliminary results, we successfully probe their energetic distribution and dynamics, verifying our method as a powerful tool to address the core difficulties in the photophysical study of NFA systems. With these encouraging findings, we will continue expanding the spectroscopic studies to decipher the charge-generation mechanism and develop guidelines for further enhancing the performance of OSCs based below four sequential tasks: (1) construct well-defined bilayer heterojunctions for in-situ experiments; (2) elucidate the energetic landscapes, dynamics and spatial locations of excited states with our comprehensive in-situ spectroscopic characterizations including 2PPE, UPS and TA; (3) establish a novel three-dimensional model describing the energy, dynamics and spatial location of excited states to analyze the mechanism of charge generation and recombination processes; and (4) develop photophysics-device performance relationships as guidelines for improving OSC performance. The success of this project will provide the crucial mechanistic understanding needed to guide the rational design of next-generation materials and device structures, accelerating the development and eventual commercialization of high-performance organic photovoltaics. 全球能源需求的不断增長以及實現碳中和的目標，迫切要求我們加快發展可再生能源，其中太陽能發電在滿足這一需求方面擁有巨大潛力。有機太陽能電池（OSCs）因其具有低成本溶液加工性、機械柔韌性和可調光電特性等優勢，成為一種頗具前景的光伏技術。近期，非富勒烯受體（NFAs）的出現推動有機太陽能電池的能量轉換效率超過20%，為這一技術帶來了革命性的突破。然而，儘管人們在提升器件效率方面已取得顯著成果，但是對電池的基本光物理過程的理解卻相對滯後，這嚴重制約了器件效率的進一步提高。目前，在光物理研究方向存在兩個關鍵但富有爭議的焦點：（1）實現高效電荷生成所需的確切驅動力，以及（2）決定開路電壓損失的激發態能級。產生這些爭議的主要原因在於激發態能級資訊的不明確，以及不同測量技術獲得的動力學資訊不一致。這種光物理模型的不統一，已成為制約下一代材料和器件發展主要瓶頸。 為應對這些挑戰，本項目擬提出一種綜合性的研究方法，利用多種原位光譜技術，特別是包括一種超快雙光子光電子能譜（2PPE），該技術能同時提供激發態的能量、時間和空間資訊。透過將2PPE與原位紫外光電子能譜（UPS）和瞬態吸收光譜（TA）相結合，我們旨在明確解析這些激發態的能量分佈、相互轉化動力學以及空間位置。在前期實驗結果中，我們已成功探測到部分體系激發態的能量分佈和動力學過程，驗證了我們的方法作為解決NFA體系光物理研究核心難題的有力工具。基於這些令人振奮的發現，我們將繼續擴展光譜研究，以揭示電荷生成機制，並為進一步提升OSC器件性能制定指導方針，具體透過以下四個逐步遞進的任務展開：（1）建構結構明確的雙層異質結用於原位實驗；（2）利用包括2PPE、UPS和TA在內的綜合原位光譜表徵，闡明激發態的能量分佈、動力學和空間位置；（3）建立一個描述激發態能量、動力學和空間位置資訊的新型三維模型，以分析電荷生成和複合過程的機理；（4）建立光物理-器件性能關係，作為提升OSC性能的指導原則。本計畫的成功實施將提供一個用於指導下一代材料和器件合理設計的關鍵模型，從而加速高性能OSC的發展及其最終商業化應用。

11217726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11217726.value: 基於電磁波的無創與微創無線深部腦刺激

11217726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217726.value: Neurobiological disease diseases, such as Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease and emotion disorders, plague tens of millions of patients worldwide. Medicinal and behavioral treatments often have limited efficacy and undesirable side effects. As a treatment method, deep brain stimulation (DBS) has proven capable in alleviating the symptoms of neurobiological diseases. However, up until now, most DBS schemes require a surgical procedure to insert a stimulation probe that connects the deep brain region to outside the patient’s body, causing risks of infection, biological incompatibility, and long-term inconvenience to the patient. In this project, we will conduct research toward non-invasive and minimally-invasive wireless DBS using electromagnetic waves. The proposed key concept is to use an RF carrier wave to wirelessly form a hotspot in the deep brain region. A much slower beat signal is modulated onto the RF carrier to stimulate neuronal activity at the hotspot, thus achieving wireless DBS. Our preliminary result shows that, through proper electromagnetic excitations exterior to the human head, one can form a hotspot in the deep brain region of sufficient strength to excite neural activity, while remaining within commonly accepted safety levels for temperature change and SAR. Further, by implanting a millimeter-sized RF scatterer, one can further concentrate the focal region and reduce power exposure to unintended regions by about 100-fold, greatly enhancing the safety and effectiveness of the treatment method. We will systematically investigate, using full-wave electromagnetic and thermal co-simulation software, how to optimize the focal quality and minimize unwanted exposure using (i) an active metasurface formed from electromagnetic equivalence, and (ii) the apparatus in (i), plus an optimized millimeter-sized scatterer implanted near the intended focal region. We will then conduct experiments with a liquid phantom and on live mice to demonstrate (a) the achievement of a strongly-focused hotspot, (b) wireless stimulation of neural activity and (c) symptom alleviation for mice with Alzheimer’s disease through a wireless DBS treatment. These achievements will strongly demonstrate the viability of wireless DBS as a treatment for neurobiological diseases. This project will be performed at the State Key Laboratory of Terahertz and Millimeter Waves and the Neural Interface Research Laboratory at the City University of Hong Kong, which contain state-of-the-art simulation and experiment facilities the project requires. Our interdisciplinary research team, with experts in electromagnetics, neural stimulation, and animal testing, has the requisite complementary expertise to succeed in this project. 神經生物學疾病（例如阿茲海默症、帕金森氏症以及情緒障礙）正影響全球數以千萬計的患者。現有的藥物治療與行為治療方法往往療效有限，且伴隨不良副作用。作為一種治療方式，深部腦刺激（Deep Brain Stimulation, DBS）已被證實能有效緩解多種神經生物學疾病的症狀。然而，至今大多數 DBS 方案皆需透過外科手術植入刺激探針，將大腦深部區域與體外設備相連接，因而帶來感染、生物相容性問題以及患者長期生活不便等風險。 本項目旨在研究以電磁波實現無創與微創無線深部腦刺激技術。所提出的核心概念為利用無線射頻（RF）載波在大腦深部區域形成能量熱點。在 RF 載波上調變頻率遠低於載波的拍頻訊號（beat signal），以刺激熱點處的神經元活動，從而實現無線深部腦刺激。初步研究結果顯示，透過施加於人體頭部外部的適當電磁激發，可在大腦深部形成足以誘發神經活動的熱點，同時將溫度變化與比吸收率（Specific Absorption Rate, SAR）控制於被廣範接納的安全範圍內。此外，若植入毫米尺度的微型 RF 散射體，則可進一步提升焦點區域的能量集中程度，並將非目標區域的電磁波暴露功率降低約 100 倍，從而大幅提升此治療方法的效能與安全性。 本研究將利用全波電磁與熱傳耦合仿真，系統性探討如何最佳化聚焦品質並最小化非目標區域的能量暴露。研究將從以下兩種架構進行分析：(i) 基於電磁等效原理所構成的有源超表面；以及 (ii) 在前述系統基礎上，額外結合植入於目標聚焦區附近之最佳化毫米尺度散射體的裝置。其後，我們將透過液態仿體（liquid phantom）及活體小鼠實驗，驗證：(a) 高度聚焦熱點的形成；(b) 神經活動的無線刺激；以及 (c) 透過無線深部腦刺激治療改善阿茲海默症小鼠之症狀。上述成果將有力證明無線深部腦刺激作為神經生物學疾病治療方法的可行性。 本項目將於香港城市大學太赫茲與毫米波全國重點實驗室（State Key Laboratory of Terahertz and Millimeter Waves）及神經介面研究實驗室（Neural Interface Research Laboratory）進行。上述研究單位具備本項目所需之先進模擬與實驗設備。研究團隊由電磁學、神經刺激技術及動物實驗等領域專家組成，兼具跨領域且互補之專業知識與關鍵能力，確保項目的成功進行與完成。

11218326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11218326.value: 用於模擬人形機器人的神經形態電子皮膚

11218326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11218326.value: The rapid aging of the global population has intensified the need for humanoid robots capable of assisting in healthcare, elderly care, and daily living. To achieve safe and empathetic human-robot interaction, robots must be equipped with sensory systems that replicate the versatile tactile perception and self-protection of human skin. However, existing electronic skins (E-skins) remain limited by complex wiring, high energy consumption, and the absence of advanced biological functions such as pain and injury perception, restricting their practicality and long-term operation. To address these challenges, we propose a concept of a neuromorphic robotic electronic skin (NRE-skin) that integrates efficient tactile encoding, active pain sensing, and adaptive injury recovery. Inspired by biological neural networks, the NRE-skin employs a pulse-based encoding mechanism to transduce tactile and thermal stimuli into neural-like pulse trains with tunable frequency, width, shape, and amplitude, enabling energy-efficient, event-driven sensing. Building upon this architecture, a pain-evaluation and reflex-arc pathway will be established to trigger rapid protective responses under noxious stimuli, while an active injury-sensing and modular replacement mechanism will allow real-time fault detection and quick physical repair. Through the combination of biomimetic neuromorphic design, low-power sensory encoding, and modular adaptability, the proposed NRE-skin will endow humanoid robots with human-like perception, self-protection, and resilience, marking a significant step toward intelligent, safe, and interactive robotic systems for future caregiving applications. 全球人口的快速老化，大大增加了對能夠在醫療照護、養老服務和日常生活中提供協助的人形機器人的需求。為了實現安全且富有同理心的人機交互，機器人必須配備能夠模擬人類皮膚多功能觸覺感知與自我保護能力的感知系統。然而，現有的電子皮膚（E-skins）仍受限於複雜的電路佈線、高能耗以及缺乏疼痛與損傷感知等高級生物功能，這限制了它們的實用性和長期運行能力。 為了解決這些挑戰，我們提出了一種神經形態機器人電子皮膚（NRE-skin）的概念，它整合了高效的觸覺編碼、主動疼痛感知和自適應損傷修復功能。受生物神經網路的啟發，NRE-skin 採用基於脈衝的編碼機制，將觸覺和熱刺激轉換為頻率、寬度、形狀和振幅可調的類神經脈衝序列，從而實現低功耗、事件驅動的感知。基於此架構，系統將建立疼痛評估與反射弧通路，以在有害刺激下觸發快速保護反應；同時，主動損傷感知與模組化替換機制將實現即時故障檢測與快速物理修復。透過仿生神經形態設計、低功耗感知編碼與模組化自適應性的結合，所提出的 NRE-skin 將賦予人形機器人類似於人類的感知、自我保護與復原能力，為面向未來護理應用的高智能、安全且具有互動性的機器人系統邁出重要一步。

11218726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11218726.value: 基於多模態大語言模型的可信風險感知建築遙控操作

11218726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11218726.value: The construction industry remains a high-risk environment, and teleoperation is increasingly utilized to reduce frontline exposure during hazardous, time-critical tasks. Yet current assistance is hampered by fragmented situational awareness, static interfaces, inconsistent risk communication, and misaligned trust. Rule-based, single-channel alerts do not scale across sites and tasks and rarely account for operator workload, uncertainty, or time to hazard, reducing clarity and reliability. Because risk cues, task context, and operator intent are distributed across video, audio, language, and telemetry, single modality systems cannot jointly ground and reason over these signals. In contrast, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can integrate perception with temporal risk reasoning to produce verifiable, uncertainty-calibrated recommendations. This project develops an AI–human shared risk management framework that couples multimodal risk perception with calibrated communication and aligned human interaction. To address the limitations and research gaps identified above, we pose three research questions: RQ1) how to architect and adapt an MLLM for remote environmental risk perception and coordinated multimodal data processing, jointly estimating risk type, spatial locus, time-to-hazard, and uncertainty while remaining robust to distribution shift; RQ2) how to design operator-centered, multichannel human-computer interaction for complex teleoperation to surface severity, and rationales at appropriate moments and through appropriate channels, while establishing efficient bidirectional risk-feedback mechanisms; and RQ3) how to model, calibrate, and personalize human-AI trust for MLLM-generated risk recommendations to quantify and reduce mismatch risk while governing assistance strength, uncertainty phrasing, and escalation thresholds under safety and fairness constraints. Motivated by these questions, we structure the work into three tasks: developing a domain-specific MLLM, designing an AI–human shared control system, and modeling trust for personalized assistance. Task I builds and validates a domain-specific MLLM via a unified corpus, structured risk-centric annotation, and staged alignment. Task II designs an operational system in which a semantic Safety Agent converts camera and telemetry inputs into structured, evidence-linked risk messages and integrates them into a phase-aware, layered, multi-channel UI with progressive disclosure and formal escalation/handover. Task III models trust and mismatch risk from adherence, overrides, timing, uncertainty phrasing, and rationale quality, then learns safety-bounded policies that personalize communication and intervention thresholds. If successful, the project will provide a calibrated, transparent pathway from multimodal risk understanding to human-centered assistance, reducing near misses and hazard response time, maintaining or improving task efficiency, and lowering cognitive workload. Deliverables will support reproducibility, scalable adoption on existing site infrastructure, and transfer to other safety-critical operations. 建造業一直屬於高風險行業，現時業界愈來愈廣泛採用遙距操作技術，在高危、具時限性的建造工序中減少前線人員暴露風險。惟現有的遙距操作輔助系統仍存在明顯不足，包括情境感知零碎、介面設計僵化、風險資訊傳達不一致，以及操作員與系統之間的信任錯配等問題。傳統固定規則、單一訊號警示模式難以靈活适配不同工地場景與工序，亦未有充分考慮操作員工作負荷、環境不確定性及危險倒數時間，導致系統指引的時效性與穩定性不足。究其原因，建造現場的風險特徵、工序情境及操作意圖分散於影片、音訊、文字及機械遙測等多模態數據，單一模態系統無法有效整合即時分析與風險推理。 本研究以多模態大型語言模型（MLLM）為核心，建立一套人機協作的遙距操作風險管理框架，實現具風險感知能力、以操作員為本的互動模式及可信的決策支援。研究聚焦三大核心問題：如何針對建造場景設計專屬MLLM，實現遙距環境風險感知與多模態數據分析，準確評估風險類型、空間位置、危險時限及不確定性，並具備數據分佈偏移穩健性；如何建構以人為本的多通道人機互動機制，適切展示風險嚴重程度與成因，並建立高效的雙向風險回饋機制；如何建模並校正人機信任關係，優化MLLM風險建議的輔助強度、不確定性表述及風險升級門檻，在安全與公平準則下降低信任錯配風險。 研究工作分為三大部分：第一，透過階段性模型微調與提示詞優化，研發建造領域專屬的MLLM，實現遙距風險理解與智能推理；第二，建構共融風險管理系統，包含標準化風險資訊輸出、多通道互動及風險升級機制；第三，基於安全約束策略建立信任建模與輔助校正機制，實現個人化人機互動優化。本研究成果可有效減少建造工地險肇事故、提升危機應對效率、維持工序執行效率並降低操作員認知負荷，同時提供可通用、可擴展的技術工具與操作規範，適用於各類高安全要求的建造遙距作業場景。

11219426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11219426.value: 面向從頭肽設計的一體化人工智能：超圖引導的序列–結構協同生成與獨立多目標驗證

11219426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11219426.value: Therapeutic peptides offer a promising route to address "undruggable" targets, especially protein–protein interfaces beyond the reach of small molecules. Yet despite advances in deep generative models, a plausibility–functionality gap persists, often yielding experimental failures due to misfolding or weak binding. This gap arises from three oversimplifications: first, molecular representations typically treat atoms as points or residues as pairwise edges, missing many-body residue groups and their conformational changes; second, generative pipelines are split into sequence-first or structure-first tracks, causing cascading errors and biophysical inconsistency; third, there is no standardized verification, and inspection via wet experiments is slow and laborious to reproduce. To overcome these limitations, we propose an integrated, data science-driven framework that places multi-objective optimization at its core, comprising three synergistic tasks. Task 1, the development of the hypergraph representation of protein-peptide interfaces, addresses the oversimplified molecular representations by introducing a hypergraph-based modeling of protein–peptide interfaces, where groups of interacting residues are treated as cooperative units instead of isolated pairs. This provides a more realistic view of how proteins flex and adapt to binding partners. Task 2, the development of the receptor-conditioned sequence–structure co-generation framework, resolves the disconnection between sequence and structure design by jointly generating both within a unified, receptor-guided model. This ensures that the designed peptides are not only diverse but also physically compatible with their targets. Task 3, the development of the independent verification and multi-objective assessment agent, tackles the lack of reliable evaluation by establishing an independent verification and decision agent, which tests each designed peptide using trusted external tools and summarizes the trade-offs among structure, stability, and manufacturability. Together, these tasks form an end-to-end, AI-driven pipeline that advances peptide discovery from theoretical design to experimentally actionable candidates. The project will deliver (i) an open toolkit for dynamic interface hypergraph construction, (ii) a receptor-conditioned sequence–structure generator with controllable guidance, and (iii) an independent verification and decision suite for transparent ranking and risk flagging. Beyond methodological innovation, the expected impact is transformative: enabling reproducible, evidence-backed peptide design that shortens the discovery–validation cycle, reduces costly experimental failures, and expands access to new therapeutics for previously "undruggable" targets. By unifying richer representation, joint generation, and multi-objective verification, this project aims to elevate AI-based peptide design from a proof-of-concept stage to a practical, industry-adoptable framework. 治療性肽為攻克「不可成藥」靶點提供了一條極具前景的途徑，尤其適用於小分子藥物難以作用的蛋白質–蛋白質相互作用界面。然而，儘管深度生成模型已取得顯著進展，其生成結果在合理性與功能性之間仍存在差距，常因錯誤摺疊或結合能力較弱而導致實驗失敗。這一差距主要源於以下三方面的過度簡化：第一，現有分子表示通常將原子視為點，或將殘基間相互作用表示為成對連接，忽略了多體殘基群及其構象變化；第二，生成流程通常被割裂為「序列優先」或「結構優先」兩條路線，容易造成誤差級聯和生物物理不一致；第三，目前缺乏標準化的驗證機制，而依賴濕實驗進行檢驗不僅耗時費力，也難以復現。 為克服上述局限，本項目擬提出一個以多目標優化為核心、由數據科學驅動的一體化框架，包括三個相互協同的任務。 任務一是開發蛋白質–肽界面的超圖表示方法。針對現有分子表示過度簡化的問題，本任務引入基於超圖的蛋白質–肽界面建模方法，將相互作用的殘基群視為協同作用單元，而非彼此孤立的殘基對，從而更加真實地刻畫蛋白質在與結合夥伴相互作用時發生的柔性變化與適應過程。 任務二是開發受體條件引導的序列–結構協同生成框架。針對序列設計與結構設計相互割裂的問題，本任務將在統一的受體引導模型中聯合生成肽的序列與結構，確保所設計的肽不僅具有多樣性，而且能夠在物理層面與其靶標保持良好的相容性。 任務三是開發獨立驗證與多目標評估智能體。針對當前缺乏可靠評價機制的問題，本任務將構建獨立的驗證與決策智能體，利用可信的外部工具對每條設計肽進行測試，並綜合呈現其在結構、穩定性和可製造性等方面的權衡關係。 上述三個任務將共同構成一條端到端的人工智能驅動流程，推動肽類藥物發現從理論設計走向具有實驗可操作性的候選分子。本項目將形成以下成果：（i）用於動態界面超圖構建的開放工具包；（ii）具有可控引導能力的受體條件序列–結構生成器；（iii）用於透明排序和風險標記的獨立驗證與決策工具套件。除方法學創新外，本項目還具有潛在的變革性影響：通過實現可復現且具有證據支持的肽設計，縮短藥物發現與驗證週期，減少代價高昂的實驗失敗，並為過去被認為「不可成藥」的靶點拓展新型治療方案。通過統一更豐富的分子表示、序列–結構聯合生成和多目標驗證，本項目旨在推動人工智能肽設計從概念驗證階段邁向可實際應用並適合產業採用的技術框架。

11219926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11219926.value: 簡化並優化 ATR 技術以用於高性能電光平板波導之全面表徵與界面工程

11219926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11219926.value: The advancement of high-performance electro-optic (EO) materials is imperative for the progression of optical interconnect technology, addressing the increasing demands imposed by cloud computing and artificial intelligence workloads within data centers. Characterization remains a fundamental aspect of materials research, serving as a driving force in the evolution of EO material science and technology. Despite its inception over three decades ago, the traditional Attenuated Total Reflectance (ATR) method encounters significant limitations in accurately detecting and quantifying EO responses. This project seeks to refine and enhance the ATR technique, facilitating comprehensive characterization and enabling the rational design of interface engineering strategies for high-performance EO materials integrated within slab waveguides. The project will explore several research tasks: (1) Developing a thorough optical model and calculation method of ATR technique for multilayer slab waveguides with variable parameters; (2) Integrating optimized coupling layers to enhance optical coupling with sub-micron and ultrathin EO films to excite the surface-plasmon resonance and coupled plasmon waveguide resonance in ATR setup; (3) Employing ATR measurements to evaluate the modulation and bias stability of multilayer EO waveguides under AC, DC, and AC/ DC conditions; (4) Using the surface chemistry and interface engineering of organic semiconductors to address the critical instability problems of EO waveguides that are associated with the band bending, contact resistance, and current–voltage hysteresis of thin-film EO materials as polar dielectrics; (5) Demonstrating high-performance hybrid EO waveguides through collaboration. Our preliminary investigations have effectively combined advancements in thin-film EO material development with a widely used commercial high-precision prism coupler system, providing strong feasibility and solid support for this proposal. The anticipated outcomes include a standardized lock-in-free ATR measurement system and data analysis capable of precisely characterizing thin-film EO coefficients in slab waveguides. Additionally, this work will enable the development of optimized EO materials through interface engineering of cladding layers, enhancing device performance and long-term reliability in silicon-organic hybrid (SOH) and thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) waveguides. These efforts will accelerate the advancement of high-efficiency EO modulators, sensors, and integrated photonic components, driving progress in telecommunications, sensing, and quantum technologies. 高效能電光材料的發展對光互連技術的發展至關重要，以應對數據中心內雲端運算和人工智能工作負載所帶來的日益增長的需求。表徵一直是是材料研究的基礎環節，也是推動電光材料科學與技術演進的關鍵環節。儘管傳統的衰減全反射（ATR）方法已問世三十多年，但在準確檢測和量化電光響應方面仍面臨顯著局限。本項目旨在改進並優化 ATR 技術，以實現對片狀波導中高性能電光材料的全面表徵，並為界面工程策略的理性設計提供支持。 本項目將圍繞以下研究任務展開：（1）針對可變參數的多層平板波導，建立完善的 ATR 技術光學模型及計算方法；（2）整合優化的耦合層，以增強與亞微米及超薄電光薄膜的光學耦合，從而在 ATR 裝置中激發表面等離子體共振和耦合等離子體波導共振；（3）運用 ATR 測量，評估多層電光波導在交流、直流及交直流條件下的調製與偏壓穩定性；（4）利用有機半導體的表面化學與界面工程，可有效解決電光波導运行的不穩定性，該問題主要源於極性介電質之薄膜電光材料所引發的能帶彎曲、接觸電阻與電流–電壓遲滯效應；（5）透過合作展示高性能混合電光波導。 我們的前期研究已將薄膜電光材料開發的進展與廣泛使用的商業高精度稜鏡耦合系統有效結合，為本項目提供了強大的可行性和堅實的支持。預期成果包括一套標準化的無需鎖相放大器的 ATR 測量系統及數據分析方法，能夠精確表徵平板波導中的薄膜電光係數。此外，這項工作將通過包層的界面工程，開發出優化的電光材料，從而提升矽有機混合（SOH）及薄膜鈮酸鋰（TFLN）波導的器件性能和長期可靠性。這些工作將加速高效電光調製器、傳感器和集成光子元件的發展，推動電信、感測及量子技術的進步。

11220126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11220126.value: 面向無創連續血糖監測的耳戴式個人化電磁感測系統

11220126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11220126.value: Dr CHAN, Kam Wa Chris Prof Chow, Yee Kwan Elaine Dr Gong, Zheng Prof Luk, Kwai-man

11220126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11220126.value: Diabetes affects over 500 million people worldwide. Despite recent revolutionary advances in pharmacological therapies, glucose monitoring remains the indispensable cornerstone of effective diabetes management and complication prevention. Reliable feedback is required to guide personalized treatment decisions, detect life-threatening hypoglycemic events, prevent hyperglycemic excursions, and optimize individualized therapeutic dosing regimens. However, existing monitoring methods, whether invasive finger-prick testing or semi-invasive subcutaneous sensors, impose substantial barriers to sustained user adherence through pain, infection risk, skin irritation, and psychological burden. The gap between therapeutic potential and clinical reality demands a transformative solution. To address this challenge, a novel non-invasive glucose monitoring system will be developed and integrated into an earring platform, representing a new approach in wearable biosensor technology. The system will leverage the vascular structure of the earlobe. Its capillary network causes glucose-dependent variations in the tissue dielectric properties, which the system measures as shifts in the resonant frequency of antenna. A novel hardware and software co-design featuring personalized calibration algorithms will be validated using both a post earring for pierced earlobes and a clip-on version for non-pierced earlobes, ensuring broad accessibility and user choice. Miniaturized wideband monopole antennas operating in the S, C, X and Ku bands, which cover commercial Wi-Fi and Bluetooth ranges, will be systematically characterized to determine their sensitivity to glucose-dependent dielectric shifts in tissue. Operating within internationally recognized safety standards, these bands take periodic readings at regular intervals similar to the current continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) devices, making them suitable for daily use. The earring back is repurposed to maximize signal-to-noise ratio by focusing electromagnetic energy into tissue while shielding from external interference. The proposed methodology will begin with identifying optimal sensing frequencies across the physiological glucose range. First, extensive in-silico electromagnetic simulations will model antenna-tissue interactions across the S to Ku bands to identify frequency ranges with maximum glucose sensitivity. Second, these predictions will be validated experimentally using custom-developed, multi-layered tissue-mimicking phantoms where glucose concentration can be precisely controlled. Based on these findings, the antenna design further optimized for the identified frequency band will be engineered. This research will not only deliver fundamental knowledge on microwave-tissue interactions in vascularized tissue but also establish the earlobe as a viable site for non-invasive biosensing, targeting an accuracy comparable to existing commercial CGM systems without any tissue penetration. This will create a platform technology extensible to other biomedical sensing applications, fundamentally reshaping wearable medical devices for millions worldwide. 糖尿病影響全球超過五億人口。儘管近年藥物治療取得顯著進展，血糖監測仍是有效管理糖尿病及預防併發症不可或缺的核心環節。可靠的血糖數據對於制定個人化治療方案、及時識別危及生命的低血糖事件、控制高血糖偏移，以及優化個人化給藥劑量，均屬必要。然而，現有的監測方式，無論是侵入性的指尖採血檢測，或是半侵入性的皮下感測器，均因穿刺疼痛、感染風險、局部皮膚反應及監測相關心理負擔，導致患者依從性偏低。現行監測技術與臨床需求之間的落差，凸顯了開發變革性解決方案的迫切需求。 為應對上述挑戰，本研究將開發一套新型無創血糖監測系統，並將其整合於耳環平台之上，為可穿戴生物感測技術提出全新的技術路徑。該系統利用耳垂的血管結構：其毛細血管網絡使組織的介電特性隨葡萄糖濃度而變化，系統則以天線共振頻率的偏移量測此變化。本研究將採用軟硬體協同設計並結合個人化校準演算法，分別以適用於已穿耳者的耳針式耳環，及適用於未穿耳者的夾式耳環進行驗證，以涵蓋兩類使用族群。 本研究將系統性表徵工作於 S、C、X 及 Ku 頻段（涵蓋商用 Wi-Fi 與藍牙頻率範圍）的小型化寬頻單極天線，以確定其對組織中葡萄糖相關介電變化的靈敏度。上述頻段的運作符合國際公認的安全標準，並可如現行連續血糖監測（CGM）裝置一般，以固定間隔進行週期性量測，適合日常長期使用。耳環後扣將被重新設計利用，藉由將電磁能量聚焦至組織內部並屏蔽外部干擾，以最大化訊噪比。所提出的研究方法將首先確定在生理血糖濃度範圍內的最佳感測頻率：第一，透過大規模電磁仿真（in-silico）建立 S 至 Ku 頻段內天線與組織的交互作用模型，以識別對葡萄糖靈敏度最高的頻率範圍；第二，利用自行研製、可精確控制葡萄糖濃度的多層組織仿體（phantom）進行實驗驗證。在此基礎上，針對所識別的頻段進一步優化並實作天線設計。 本研究不僅將提供有關微波與血管組織交互作用的基礎知識，亦將確立耳垂作為無創生物感測的可行部位，目標是在完全不穿透組織的前提下，達到與現有商用 CGM 系統相當的準確度。由此形成的平台技術可延伸至其他生物醫學感測應用，為穿戴式醫療裝置提供新的設計範式。

11220326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11220326.value: 用於高電流密度陰離子交換膜水電解之分級電極的可編程兩相傳輸與界面力學

11220326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11220326.value: Green hydrogen is central to achieving a carbon-neutral energy future. Operating water electrolyzers at high current densities (≥4 A cm⁻²) lowers the levelized cost of hydrogen by boosting productivity, enabling compact stacks, and reducing balance-of-plant costs. However, such high-rate operation remains constrained by two coupled bottlenecks: bubble-induced transport losses that block ionic pathways and increase overpotential, and mechanical degradation from cyclic bubble detachment that weakens catalyst–substrate adhesion. Existing strategies—micro/nano-texturing for bubble release, ordered porous networks for gas evacuation, and interlayer bonding for adhesion—have been effective individually but remain decoupled. In practice, these approaches address only isolated aspects of the problem: electrodes that remove bubbles efficiently often lose adhesion under stress, while those with strong interfaces trap bubbles and suffer transport losses. Consequently, mass transport and mechanical robustness have rarely been optimized simultaneously, leaving bubble nucleation, detachment, and in-pore transport uncontrolled at high current operation. To overcome these challenges, we propose a three-tier hierarchical electrode integrating a Ni TPMS substrate, a micro-cavity interlayer, and a conformal NiFe-LDH catalyst. This architecture unifies efficient gas evacuation, coalescence-induced early detachment, and robust interfacial anchoring. Preliminary studies demonstrate exceptional AEM-cell performance and durability—achieving 8.5 A cm⁻² @ 2.0 V and 14.8 A cm⁻² @ 2.3 V with stable operation for 6000 h @ 1 A cm⁻²—among the best reported for alkaline anodes, confirming the promise of geometry-driven co-optimization. Nevertheless, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood, particularly the coupling between cavity geometry and bubble kinetics, TPMS topology and in-pore gas transport, and interfacial structure and cyclic stress tolerance. Resolving these gaps requires a unified framework linking geometric design to both transport and mechanical responses under high-rate operation. This project will develop an integrated dual-scale approach combining modeling, fabrication, and characterization to reveal how geometry governs two-phase transport and interfacial mechanics. The modeling framework will link pore-scale transport with cavity-scale bubble evolution, generating predictive design maps for optimized architectures. These predictions will drive the fabrication of hierarchical electrodes via additive manufacturing and electrodeposition, followed by high-speed imaging, electrochemical and nanomechanical tests, and AEM validation—completing a closed loop from modeling to device-level performance. By uniting fundamental understanding and device-scale validation, we will establish geometry-based design rules for durable, high-rate AEM electrolysis—advancing both the science of multiscale bubble–structure interactions and the engineering of scalable green-hydrogen technologies. 綠色氫能是實現碳中和能源未來的核心技術。水電解槽在高電流密度（≥4 A cm⁻²）下運行，可提高產氫效率、縮小電解槽堆體積並降低系統輔助設備成本，從而降低氫氣平準化成本。然而，高倍率運行仍受到兩個相互耦合的瓶頸制約：氣泡會阻塞離子傳輸路徑，增加傳質損失與過電位；週期性氣泡脫離則產生機械應力，削弱催化劑與基底之間的界面黏附。現有微／奈米結構、有序多孔網絡及界面增強策略通常分別針對氣泡傳輸或機械穩定性，尚難實現兩者的同步優化。 本項目提出一種三層級分級電極，由 Ni 三重週期極小曲面（TPMS）基底、微腔體中間層及共形 NiFe-LDH 催化層組成，旨在同時實現快速氣體排出、聚併誘導的氣泡提前脫離及穩固的界面錨定。前期研究已實現 8.5 A cm⁻² @ 2.0 V、14.8 A cm⁻² @ 2.3 V，並在 1 A cm⁻² 下穩定運行 6000 h，顯示出優異的 AEM 電解性能與耐久性。 然而，微腔幾何結構與氣泡動力學、TPMS 拓撲與孔內氣體輸運，以及界面結構與週期性應力耐受之間的耦合機制仍不清楚。本項目將結合雙尺度建模、增材製造、電沉積、高速成像、電化學及奈米力學表徵，建立孔尺度傳輸與微腔尺度氣泡演化的統一模型，形成可預測的幾何設計圖譜，並透過 AEM 電解槽進行器件尺度驗證。最終建立耐久、高電流密度 AEM 水電解的幾何設計準則，推進多尺度氣泡—結構相互作用的基礎研究及可規模化綠色製氫技術的工程應用。

11220426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11220426.value: 以渲染為導向的 3D 數據壓縮：從統一表徵到生成式品質增強

11220426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11220426.value: The rapid advancement of immersive technologies (e.g., metaverse, digital twins) and the emergence of spatial intelligence are driving an exponential demand for high-fidelity 3D data. However, this growth is severely constrained by the fundamental limitations of existing 3D data compression methods that are necessary for transmission and storage. Specifically, current compression approaches for 3D meshes and point clouds struggle with two interconnected challenges: their unstructured representation leads to inefficient and ineffective spatial redundancy elimination; their separate compression pipelines for geometry and texture, and optimization goals not aligned with the final rendered visual quality, result in inefficient compression and inferior visual fidelity. To overcome these bottlenecks, this project proposes a comprehensive framework consisting of three key components for representation, compression, and quality enhancement: 1) We will propose a geometry-texture unified deformable tensor (UniGeT) representation, which adopts deformable distance and color fields to uniformly represent the geometry and texture of a textured 3D mesh as a regular, compact, and sparse volume, capturing fine-grained details and enabling precise surface reconstruction and real-time, differentiable rendering. 2) We will build a rendering-oriented neural compression framework that transforms the above UniGeT representation into a compact latent feature and encodes it into bitstreams using a hierarchical context model. Crucially, this compressor is optimized end-to-end by directly minimizing the rendering distortion, ensuring optimal bitrate allocation and control for visual quality. 3) We will investigate an effective 3D quality enhancement approach that harnesses the powerful generative capability of a 2D foundation model to recover geometric and textural details of decompressed 3D data suffering from inevitable loss. Particularly, a rendering-centric pipeline will be leveraged to transfer 2D generative priors into targeted 3D model refinement, avoiding the complexities of direct 3D manipulation. By integrating a unified representation with rendering-driven compression and generative enhancement, this project can deliver a breakthrough in compression efficiency and visual fidelity, effectively bridging the gap between the high demands of next-generation immersive applications and the constraints of practical network conditions. Building upon our strong research foundation and encouraging preliminary results, we anticipate that this project will achieve transformative breakthroughs in 3D immersive media representation and compression, significantly advance current technical capabilities, and drive the practical implementation of virtual reality applications. Beyond technical innovation, this project is expected to lay an extensible foundation for future research in spatial data processing and contribute to Hong Kong’s key initiatives in digital entertainment and smart city development. 沉浸式技術（如元宇宙、數位雙生）的迅速發展與空間智慧的興起，正推動對高逼真度 3D 資料的指數級需求。然而，現有用於傳輸與儲存的 3D 資料壓縮方法存在根本局限，嚴重限制了此一增長。具體而言，目前的 3D 網格（mesh）與點雲（point cloud）壓縮方法面臨兩個相互關聯的挑戰：第一，其非結構化表徵導致空間冗餘消除的效率與效果不佳；第二，幾何與紋理採用獨立的壓縮管線，且優化目標未與最終渲染的視覺品質對齊，導致壓縮效率低下且視覺逼真度較差。 為突破上述瓶頸，本項目提出一個包含表徵、壓縮與品質提升三大核心模組的全面性框架： 幾何—紋理統一可變形張量（UniGeT）表徵：採用可變形距離場與顏色場，將帶紋理 3D 網格的幾何與紋理統一表示為規則、緊湊且稀疏的體素（volume），以捕捉精細細節，並實現精確的表面重建與即時、可微渲染。 面向渲染的神經壓縮框架：將上述 UniGeT 表徵轉化為緊湊的隱特徵（latent feature），並利用分層上下文模型將其編碼為位元流。關鍵在於，該壓縮器透過直接最小化渲染失真進行端到端優化，確保視覺品質的最佳位元率分配與控制。 高效的 3D 品質提升方法：利用 2D 基礎大模型的強大生成能力，修復解壓縮後 3D 資料中不可避免的幾何與紋理細節損失。具體而言，將運用以渲染為中心的管線，將 2D 生成先驗遷移至目標 3D 模型微調中，從而避免直接進行 3D 操作的複雜性。 透過將統一表徵、渲染驅動壓縮與生成式增強相結合，本項目將在壓縮效率與視覺逼真度上取得突破，有效填補下一代沉浸式應用的高需求與實際網路條件限制之間的鴻溝。 憑藉我們堅實的研究基礎與令人鼓舞的初步成果，預計本項目將在 3D 沉浸式媒體表徵與壓縮領域取得變革性突破，顯著提升現有技術能力，並推動虛擬實境應用的落地實施。除了技術創新之外，本項目亦有望為未來空間資料處理研究奠定可擴展的基礎，並為香港在數位娛樂與智慧城市發展方面的關鍵舉措作出貢獻。

11220826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11220826.value: 自動化算子設計探索：一種大語言模型驅動的演化方法

11220826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11220826.value: Kernels—specify how operations (e.g., matrix multiplication) are executed on hardware (e.g., NVIDIA A100)—are critical for AI performance, cost-effectiveness, and energy efficiency. However, designing optimized kernels remains a major bottleneck: it demands deep expertise in hardware architecture and low-level programming, forcing practitioners to rely on painstaking manual tuning. For instance, the FlashAttention kernel—essential for modern Transformer-based AI models—took five years to develop after the Transformer was introduced, and two additional years to adapt to new hardware. This slow, expert-driven process is increasingly unsustainable amid the rapid growth of AI models and specialized AI hardware, each requiring uniquely tailored kernels. A pivotal question naturally arises: Can we automate the development of high-performance kernels to accelerate AI innovation and democratize hardware efficiency? In this project, we propose a novel framework that re-imagines evolutionary computation for automated kernel design (AKD) by shifting from a numerical to a language-based decision space. Leveraging large language models (LLMs), our approach directly searches for high-performance kernels using language representations: natural language (capturing design intent/rationale) and computer code (delivering executable implementations). This framework resembles the workflow of human experts, offering two transformative advantages for AKD: (i) It circumvents the reliance on expert-crafted parameterization schemes for encoding a kernel into a numerical decision vector; and (ii) it enables seamless infusion of domain knowledge into the search process, e.g., inputting knowledge on kernel design as prompts to aid LLMs for generating high-performance kernels. Our research plan advances through four interconnected tasks: (1) Develop a language-based multi-view representation of a kernel and establish a basic understanding of the resulting search landscape. (2) Develop a LLM-guided evolutionary framework for effectively searching in a language-based kernel decision space. (3) Extend the framework with self-evolution for open-ended exploration of innovative kernel designs. (4) Deploy the framework via industry partnership for kernel design on custom AI accelerators, validating real-world practicality. Our automated kernel design framework promises to revolutionize AI systems development by drastically reducing kernel optimization time from years to days, thus accelerating AI innovation. It democratizes hardware efficiency by enabling non-experts to generate high-performance kernels, breaking the reliance on scarce expertise. Ultimately, this work will sustain the rapid evolution of AI by ensuring that hardware capabilities are fully leveraged across emerging models and accelerators. 算子（kernel）規定了某項運算（例如矩陣乘法）在特定硬件（例如 NVIDIA A100）上的具體執行方式，是決定人工智能（AI）系統性能、成本效益與能源效率的關鍵。然而，高效能算子的設計至今仍是 AI 系統開發中的一大難題：它要求開發者同時精通硬件架構與底層編程，迫使從業者只能依靠費時費力的人手調校。以現代 Transformer 類 AI 模型不可或缺的 FlashAttention 算子為例，它在 Transformer 面世五年後方才問世，此後再過兩年才被適配到新硬件。面對 AI 模型與專用 AI 硬件的急速增長——每一款模型與硬件都需要專門定製的算子——這種緩慢且高度依賴專家的流程已難以為繼。由此引出一個關鍵問題：我們能否令高效能算子的開發自動化，從而加速 AI 創新，讓硬件效能惠及大眾？ 本項目提出一個嶄新框架，重新構想演化計算（evolutionary computation）在自動化算子設計（automated kernel design, AKD）中的應用，把決策空間由數值空間轉移至語言空間。藉助大語言模型（large language models, LLMs），我們直接以語言表徵搜尋高效能算子，當中包括自然語言（承載設計意圖與理據）與程式碼（提供可執行的實作）。此框架貼近人類專家的實際工作流程，為 AKD 帶來兩項變革性優勢：（一）無需再依賴由專家人手設計的參數化方案來把算子編碼成數值決策向量；（二）使領域知識能無縫注入搜尋過程，例如把算子設計知識以提示（prompt）形式輸入，引導 LLM 生成高效能算子。研究計劃透過四項環環相扣的任務推進：（1）建立以語言為本的算子多視角表徵，並對由此形成的搜尋地形建立基本認識；（2）發展由 LLM 引導的演化框架，以在語言化的算子決策空間中進行高效搜尋；（3）以自我演化（self-evolution）擴充該框架，實現對創新算子設計的開放式探索；（4）透過業界夥伴合作部署本框架，針對定製 AI 加速器進行算子設計，驗證其實際應用價值。 本自動化算子設計框架有望徹底改變 AI 系統的開發模式：把算子優化所需時間由以年計壓縮至以日計，從而加速 AI 創新；同時讓非專家亦能產生高效能算子，打破對稀缺專才的依賴，讓硬件效能惠及大眾。最終，本研究將確保各種新興模型與加速器都能充分發揮硬件效能，為 AI 的持續快速發展提供支撐。

11221026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11221026.value: 氫鍵網絡雙重優化構築高性能壓離子離子凝膠壓力感測器

11221026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11221026.value: The future of bio-integrated diagnostics, artificial skin, and skin-wearable bioelectronics hinges on soft, robust pressure sensors that seamlessly conform to biological tissue and autonomously convert pressure into electrical signals. Yet, most current sensors depend on batteries, which are fundamentally unsuited for wearables and implants: battery replacement is often impractical, surgical intervention is risky, and electronic waste is environmentally damaging. There is a pressing need for self-powered, maintenance-free pressure sensors designed for next-generation biomedical and wearable applications. Piezoionic ionogels—soft, ion-conducting gels that generate voltage when deformed—offer a promising path forward. However, existing ionogels typically produce weak electrical signals and lack sufficient mechanical integrity, making them unsuitable for long-term, comfortable use on or within the body. Prior approaches have only addressed electrical or mechanical limitations in isolation; no integrated method has emerged to simultaneously enhance both. This proposal presents a novel “hydrogen bond optimization” strategy, enabling the creation of high-performance piezoionic pressure sensors. By engineering the hydrogen bond network within PVA-polyurea copolymer ionogels, we can finely tune the mechanical properties of the polymer matrix while controlling crystallinity to improve ion transport. This dual optimization is unprecedented—it achieves both stronger piezoionic response and superior mechanical properties, resulting in sensors that are soft, stretchable, tough, and truly comfortable for continuous, bio-integrated use. The PI and his team draw on deep expertise in electronic and ionic materials, as well as pressure sensor design, to execute a research plan comprising: (1) advanced synthesis of tunable ionogels, (2) systematic hydrogen bond network optimization, (3) fabrication of conformable piezoionic pressure sensors, and (4) validation in wearable and biomedical scenarios. Preliminary experiments show a tenfold amplification in piezoionic signal, doubled stretchability and strength, and quadrupled toughness—clear indicators of high feasibility and performance. Upon completion, this project will deliver a fundamentally new class of piezoionic pressure sensors, ideally suited for future bio-integrated diagnostics and soft wearable electronics. By collaborating with clinical researchers and bioelectronics device manufacturers, we will deploy these sensors in real-world health monitoring applications. This innovation will help shift healthcare from centralized, resource-intensive models to decentralized, community-oriented monitoring—critically reducing the strain on healthcare systems facing demographic challenges in Hong Kong and China. The resulting knowledge and technology will catalyze advances in soft robotics, artificial skin, and distributed health diagnostics. 針對生物整合診療、人工皮膚及穿戴式生物電子裝置的發展需求，亟需開發能夠與生物組織高度貼合併實現壓力訊號自主電轉換的柔性高性能壓力感測器。然而，目前大多數壓力感測器仍依賴電池供能，而電池在穿戴式和植入式應用中存在固有局限性，包括更換困難、植入手術風險高以及電子廢棄物造成環境負擔等問題。因此，發展新一代自供能、免維護的壓力感測技術已成為生物醫學電子和智慧穿戴領域的重要研究方向。 壓離子離子凝膠（Piezoionic Ionogels）是一類在受力形變過程中能夠產生電壓輸出的柔性離子導電凝膠材料，為解決上述難題提供了一條極具前景的路徑。然而，現有壓離子離子凝膠普遍存在壓離子響應訊號弱、機械性能不足等問題，難以滿足長期配戴及生物整合應用對於舒適性、可靠性和耐久性的要求。現有研究通常僅針對電學性能或機械性能進行單獨優化，尚缺乏能夠同步提升兩者的系統性設計策略 本計畫提出一種創新的氫鍵網路最佳化策略，用於構築高性能壓離子壓力感測器。透過調控聚乙烯醇（PVA）-聚脲共聚離子凝膠內部的氫鍵交互作用網絡，實現聚合物基體微觀結構及結晶行為的精準調控，進而協同優化離子傳輸過程與機械性質。此雙重優化機制有望突破現有壓離子材料在性能協同提升方面的瓶頸，同時實現壓離子響應增強以及拉伸性、韌性和強度的顯著提升，進而獲得兼具柔軟性、高靈敏度和佩戴舒適性的壓力感測器。 專案負責人及其研究團隊在電子與離子功能材料設計、柔性感測器開發等方面具有紮實研究基礎。計畫研究內容包括：（1）可調控高性能離子凝膠的設計與製備；（2）氫鍵網絡結構的系統優化與調控；（3）柔性貼合式壓離子壓力感測器的構築；以及（4）面向穿戴式生物醫學場景的效能驗證與應用評估。前期研究結果表明，該策略可實現壓離子輸出訊號提高約一個數量級，材料拉伸性能與強度提升約兩倍，韌性提高約四倍，充分驗證了方案的可行性和應用潛力。 工程完成後，將建立一類全新的高性能壓離子壓力感測器體系，為生物整合診療和柔性穿戴電子裝置提供關鍵技術支撐。透過聯合中西醫臨床團隊及生物電子元件企業進行應用驗證，推動相關技術在健康監測領域的實際部署。此成果可望促進醫療健康模式由集中式、資源密集型服務向分散式、社區化連續監測轉變，從而緩解人口老化與慢性疾病高發所帶來的醫療系統壓力。同時，專案所形成的理論認知和關鍵技術也將推動軟體機器人、電子皮膚以及分散式健康診斷等前沿領域的發展。

11221326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11221326.value: 稀疏前沿：以MoE打造資源高效之邊緣LLM

11221326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11221326.value: The deployment of large language models (LLMs) on edge devices represents a growing trend in modern intelligent systems, from personal assistants and wearables to industrial Internet of Things (IoT). This emerging paradigm has been recognized by MIT Technology Review as one of the 10 Breakthrough Technologies 2025 and “the next big thing” in AI. Nevertheless, this edge LLM paradigm remains constrained by limited computation, power, and memory resources. A promising solution is the Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, which activates only a sparse subset of expert subnetworks for each input, greatly reducing computational cost while maintaining performance. However, applying MoE to edge environments introduces new challenges, including expert training with scarce and imbalanced domain-specific data, load balancing, and efficient inference across distributed, heterogeneous devices. To bridge this gap, this proposal aims to develop a comprehensive framework for efficient training and deployment of MoE-based edge LLMs under resource constraints and data scarcity. The proposed work is structured into three tasks: 1) Enabling rapid expert specialization training for edge MoE: This task introduces an upcycling training scheme enhanced by iterative task-reversal data augmentation, which efficiently leverages pre-trained dense models to boost expert specialization and mitigate data scarcity. This is coupled with a domain-adaptive hierarchical structure that functions as a two-level domain-task organization within a single-layer architecture, preventing expert collapse and enhancing specialization under resource constraints. 2) Developing a low-latency MoE deployment strategy for edge: This task introduces a novel stochastic lattice-based quantization scheme that achieves high compression rates and maintains strong task performance with low complexity, outperforming standard parameter-wise methods. Additionally, a proactive expert caching mechanism is designed to optimize inference latency in distributed edge networks. 3) Evaluating edge MoE performance and efficiency on real-world datasets: The framework will be evaluated on complex AI tasks to demonstrate the effectiveness and real-world impact of the developed technologies. Integrating cross-disciplinary expertise in LLMs, distributed systems, and communications, this project aims to establish a comprehensive understanding of MoE mechanisms at the edge and deliver customized approaches that ensure stable, scalable, and robust performance. The outcomes are expected to provide valuable insights for both the research community and industry practitioners, facilitating the next generation of efficient and accessible edge AI. 在邊緣裝置上部署大語言模型（LLM）已成為現代智能系統中日益增長的趨勢，應用範圍涵蓋個人助理、穿戴式裝置乃至工業物聯網（IoT）。此一新興典範已被《MIT科技評論》評為2025年十大突破技術之一，並被譽為AI領域的「下一件大事」。然而，此邊緣LLM典範仍受限於運算、電力及記憶體資源之不足。混合專家模型（MoE）架構是一個具有前景的解決方案，其僅針對每個輸入啟動稀疏的專家子網路，大幅降低運算成本，同時維持模型表現。然而，將MoE應用於邊緣環境帶來了新的挑戰，包括在稀缺且不均衡的領域特定資料下進行專家訓練、負載平衡，以及在分散式異質裝置上實現高效推論。 為填補此一缺口，本提案旨在開發一套全面性框架，用於在資源受限及資料稀缺之條件下，實現MoE架構邊緣LLM的高效訓練與部署。本研究工作規劃為三項任務：1）實現邊緣MoE之快速專家專業化訓練：本任務引入一種透過迭代式任務反轉資料擴增強化的升級訓練方案，有效利用預訓練之稠密模型來促進專家專業化，並緩解資料稀缺問題。此方案搭配領域自適應階層結構，在單層架構中實現兩層式領域－任務組織，防止專家崩潰並在資源受限下強化專業化程度。2）開發適用於邊緣之低延遲MoE部署策略：本任務引入一種新穎的隨機格量化方案，可達成高壓縮率並在低複雜度下維持優異任務表現，優於標準的逐參數方法。此外，設計了一種主動式專家快取機制，以最佳化分散式邊緣網路中的推論延遲。3）在真實世界資料集上評估邊緣MoE之效能與效率：該框架將在複雜AI任務上進行評估，以證明所開發技術之有效性及實際影響力。 本計畫整合大語言模型、分布式系統及通訊等跨領域專業知識，旨在建立對邊緣MoE機制之全面性理解，並提供量身訂製之方法，以確保穩定、可擴充及穩健之效能。預期研究成果將為學術界及業界從業人員提供有價值之洞見，促進下一代高效且普及之邊緣AI發展。

11221726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11221726.value: 大语言模型的可解释微调数据选择

11221726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11221726.value: Instruction fine-tuning is indispensable in making pre-trained large language models (LLMs) effectively follow human instructions and achieve specific purposes. This process involves refining pre-trained models using datasets that consist of instruction-response pairs, bridging the gap between the model's inherent capabilities and user expectations. Despite being important, attributing, selecting, and constructing fine-tuning data are still cumbersome, which requires high-quality instructions and intense computation resources. Although recent studies have managed to identify high-quality fine-tuning data for LLMs, there are still several challenges: 1) lacking adaptive attribution metrics suited for different LLMs; 2) lacking effective approaches to compositely attribute instruction data; 3) lacking efficient schemes to examine data selection strategies and explain the selected instructions. To tackle the aforementioned challenges, we will conduct systematic investigations on the explainable fine-tuning data attribution for LLMs. Generally, our project consists of three major tasks. 1) We plan to develop attribution metrics adapted to various LLMs. We will develop an LLM-aware metric adaptation scheme that calibrates the attribution metric tailored to LLMs' characteristics. Furthermore, we will design dataset-level attribution metrics to ensure fair and comprehensive assessments for instruction-tuning datasets regarding complexity and diversity. 2) We plan to compositely attribute and select the instruction data through advanced techniques. We will resort to mutual information to measure the complementarity of selected instruction data and further enhance the composition. Moreover, we will leverage the Wasserstein distance between datasets to balance the proximity and diversity of selected data. 3) We plan to incorporate the efficient examination of selection strategies and explainability into the instruction tuning. We will design a retraining-free scheme with the influence function to efficiently evaluate candidate data selection strategies. Furthermore, we will investigate explainable instruction tuning with the computationally efficient Shapley value, which will enhance the trustworthiness of selected instructions. With the support from industrial collaborators, our outcomes will establish a practical foundation for the analysis of data attribution in LLMs, provide effective data attribution techniques, enhance the training efficiency of supervised fine-tuning, and push forward the scientific frontier of this research area. 指令微调（Instruction Fine-tuning）对于使预训练大语言模型（Large Language Models, LLMs）能够有效遵循人类指令并完成特定任务至关重要。该过程利用由“指令—响应”对构成的数据集对预训练模型进行进一步优化，从而弥合模型自身能力与用户期望之间的差距。尽管指令微调十分重要，但微调数据的归因、筛选与构建仍然较为繁琐，不仅需要高质量的指令数据，还需要大量计算资源。 尽管近期研究已经能够从大规模数据中识别出高质量的大语言模型微调数据，但仍存在若干挑战：1）缺乏能够适配不同大语言模型的自适应数据归因指标；2）缺乏对指令数据进行综合归因的有效方法；3）缺乏能够高效评估数据选择策略并对所选指令进行解释的方案。 针对上述挑战，本项目拟围绕大语言模型微调数据的可解释归因开展系统研究。总体而言，本项目包括以下三个主要研究任务。 1）面向不同大语言模型设计自适应的数据归因指标。 我们计划提出一种面向大语言模型的指标自适应机制，根据不同大语言模型的特性对数据归因指标进行校准，从而实现针对不同模型的自适应归因。此外，我们还将设计数据集级别的归因指标，从复杂度与多样性等维度，对指令微调数据集进行公平且全面的评估。 2）利用先进技术对指令数据进行综合归因与筛选。 我们将利用互信息（Mutual Information）衡量所选指令数据之间的互补性，并进一步优化数据组合。同时，我们将利用数据集之间的 Wasserstein 距离，在所选数据与目标数据的接近程度和数据多样性之间实现平衡，从而获得更加有效的微调数据子集。 3）将高效的数据选择策略评估与可解释性机制融入指令微调过程。 我们计划基于影响函数（Influence Function）设计一种无需重新训练模型的数据选择策略评估方案，从而高效地评估不同候选数据选择策略。此外，我们还将研究基于计算高效的 Shapley 值的可解释指令微调方法，以提升所选指令数据的可解释性与可信度。 在产业合作伙伴的支持下，本项目的研究成果将为大语言模型中的数据归因分析奠定实用基础，提供有效的数据归因与选择技术，提高监督微调（Supervised Fine-tuning, SFT）的训练效率，并推动该研究方向的科学前沿发展

11221826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11221826.value: 結構再利用廢棄風機葉片FRP複材開發道路護欄

11221826.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11221826.value: Prof FANG, Hai Prof Zhou, Chang

11221826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11221826.value: Roadside barriers are a vital component of transportation infrastructure, playing a crucial role in ensuring driving safety. Existing roadside barriers are typically in the form of rigid concrete barriers or semi-rigid metal-beam guardrails. While concrete barriers offer high stiffness, they have limited capacity for energy dissipation during vehicle impacts, resulting in significant vehicle deformation in collision accidents and potentially causing injuries to occupants. In contrast, flexible steel barriers may suffer from diminished crashworthiness due to the corrosion of steel plates and their joints. In recent years, fibre-reinforced polymer (FRP) materials have been increasingly introduced into roadside barrier applications due to their light weight, high strength, and corrosion/weather resistance, non-conductivity, etc. Harvesting wind power through wind turbines is recognized as a vital source of green energy across the globe. However, the dramatically increasing number of decommissioned wind turbine blades (Decom-WTBs) presents a significant challenge to the natural environment. Traditional disposal methods, such as landfilling, incineration, or chemical recycling, can pollute land, air, or water resources. Therefore, there is an urgent need for a viable physical recycling method capable of effectively handling Decom-WTBs. Fortunately, the majority of these blades are constructed using a sandwich structure with FRP outer layers and wood or foam cores. The outer FRP layers provide strength and stiffness, while the inner core is designed to increase the stiffness. This unique sandwich configuration offers massive potential for repurposing them in the construction of roadside barriers that require high energy absorption. This project proposes using Decom-WTBs to develop roadside barriers by leveraging their unique features, providing a one stone, two birds solution. This innovation aims to upcycle Decom-WTBs, enhancing the energy dissipation capacity of roadside barriers, providing excellent protection for out-of-control vehicles, and improving traffic safety. To translate the above innovative concept into practical application, this project will include comprehensive experimental impact tests at both the material and structural levels, as well as advanced numerical modelling. The containment capability, post-impact vehicle trajectory, and safety risks to occupants during vehicle crash accidents will be investigated in detail for evaluating the protection capability of the Decom-WTB-derived roadside barrier system towards forming a multi-objective optimization design approach. The research will lead to a cost-effective, eco-friendly solution for the design and construction of roadside barriers, contributing to enhanced traffic safety and to national goals of carbon neutrality and the circular economy. 路側護欄是交通基礎設施的重要組成部分，在保障行車安全方面發揮著至關重要的作用。現有的路側護欄通常採用剛性混凝土護欄或半剛性金屬梁護欄的形式。混凝土護欄雖然剛度高，但在車輛碰撞時的能量耗散能力有限，導致車輛在碰撞事故中發生顯著變形，並可能造成車內人員受傷。相較之下，柔性鋼護欄可能會因鋼板及其連接處的腐蝕而降低其耐撞性。近年來，由於纖維增強聚合物（FRP）材料具有重量輕、強度高、耐腐蝕/耐候性好、不導電等優點，其在路側護欄領域的應用日益廣泛。 利用風機收集風能被公認為全球重要的綠色能源來源。然而，退役風機葉片（Decom-WTB）數量的急劇增加對自然環境構成了嚴峻挑戰。傳統的處置方法，例如掩埋、焚燒或化學回收，會導致土地、空氣或水資源污染。因此，迫切需要一種能夠有效處理廢棄風機葉片的可行物理回收方法。幸運的是，大多數此類葉片採用三明治結構，由FRP外層和木材或泡沫芯材構成。外層FRP提供強度和剛度，而內芯則旨在進一步提高剛度。這種獨特的三明治結構使其具有巨大的潛力，可用於建造需要高能量吸收的路邊護欄。 本项目旨在利用廢棄風機葉片的獨特特性開發路邊護欄，實現一舉兩得。這項創新旨在對廢棄風機葉片進行升級再造，增強路邊護欄的能量耗散能力，為失控車輛提供卓越的保護，並提高交通安全。為將上述創新理念轉化為實際應用，將進行材料和結構層面的衝擊試驗，並結合先進的數值建模。研究將詳細檢視碰撞事故中車輛碰撞防護能力、碰撞後車輛軌跡以及乘員安全風險，以評估基於Decom-WTB的路側護欄系統的防護性能，並最終形成多目標最佳化設計方法。該研究將為路側護欄的設計和建造提供一種經濟高效且環保的解決方案，有助於提升交通安全，並協助實現國家碳中和及循環經濟目標。

11221926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11221926.value: 用於超低溫無結晶吸收式熱能儲存之仿生多層次吸濕鰓結構與熱響應離子液體

11221926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11221926.value: Buildings account for 20–40% of the world's energy use and 90% of Hong Kong's electricity consumption. Utilizing renewable/waste energy is promising for building energy saving and emission mitigation. However, the mismatch between intermittent energy supplies and variable building loads results in inefficiency and under-utilization. Thermal energy storage plays a significant role in balancing the mismatch. Thermochemical-based absorption thermal energy storage (ATES) stands out due to high energy storage density/efficiency, adjustable charging temperature, and operational flexibility. Besides energy decarbonization, ATES also merits refrigerant decarbonization by using zero-GWP natural fluids like H2O. All these advantages facilitate more sustainable utilization of renewable/waste energy for buildings. However, major issues preventing wider applications are: (1) poor mass transfer (low efficiency, low density, slow response), (2) high charging temperature (narrow applicability), and (3) high crystallization risk (low reliability). This proposal seeks to address these deficiencies by developing a biomimetic hierarchical moisture absorption gill (HMAG) using thermo-responsive ionic liquid (TIL) for ultralow-temperature and crystallization-free ATES. The ATES enables multi-functionality like heating/dehumidification/cooling to accommodate demands across various climates. Mimicking the tuna's breathing gill, HMAG combines capillary wicking, dual-film encapsulation, and multi-stage interconnection. This codesign offers a large specific area that further increases compactness. TIL features temperature-triggered phase transition between biphasic (hydrophobic, desorption) and homogeneous (hydrophilic, absorption) states. Above transition temperature (e.g., 40 °C), a diluted layer forms with easier desorption, thus realizing ultralow-temperature charging. Besides, TIL's crystallization-free nature enables large concentration glides and thus high energy storage density. Therefore, the synergy between biomimetic HMAG and smart TIL empowers high-performance ATES. Preliminary studies demonstrate high viability and excellent performance of HMAG-ATES. Numerical and experimental methods will be employed to complete the following objectives: (1) Model and prototype development of HMAG using TIL for ultralow-temperature and crystallization-free ATES; (2) Characterization of phase-transition behaviors, sorption kinetics, heat/mass transfer, and cycling stability of TILs fabricated with various transition temperatures; (3) Investigation of dynamic charging/discharging behaviors and energy storage performance of HMAG-ATES under various modes/conditions; (4) Multi-scale absorbent-reactor-building optimization assisted by machine learning to maximize overall long-term performance for different application scenarios. This research is significant for developing high-efficiency, high-density, fast-response, wide-applicability, and high-reliability ATES, offering promising building decarbonization solutions. It's estimated to obtain electricity savings of 60–80%, carbon reduction of 70–90%, with payback periods of 2–4 years. It will contribute towards healthy indoor environment, carbon neutrality, and sustainable development in Hong Kong and worldwide. 建築物佔全球能源消耗的20-40%，在香港則佔用電量的90%。利用可再生能源或廢熱，對於建築節能減排極具潛力。然而，間歇性供能與波動性建築負荷之間存在不匹配，導致效率較低且利用率不足。熱儲能在平衡此不匹配中扮演關鍵角色。其中，熱化學吸收式熱儲能因其儲能密度高、儲能效率高、蓄能溫度可調及操作靈活而脫穎而出。除了有助於能源脫碳，吸收式熱儲能亦能透過使用零全球變暖潛能的自然工質（比如水）來實現製冷劑脫碳。這些優勢皆有助於建築中可再生能源或廢熱的可持續利用。 然而，限制吸收式熱儲能廣泛應用的主要問題包括：（1）傳質性能不佳（效率低、密度低、反應慢）；（2）蓄能溫度過高（適用性低）；（3）結晶風險較高（可靠性低）。本項目擬透過研發仿生多層次吸濕鰓結構，並搭配熱響應離子液體，以實現超低溫無結晶之吸收式熱儲能，從而解決上述缺陷。此吸收式熱儲能具備多功能性，如供暖、除濕、製冷，可因應不同氣候條件下的需求。多層次吸濕鰓模仿金槍魚的呼吸鰓，結合毛細芯吸、雙膜包覆與多級互連結構。此協同設計提供較大的比表面積，進一步提升緊湊度。熱響應離子液體則具有溫度觸發的相轉變特性，可在雙相（疏水、脫附）與均相（親水、吸收）之間切換。當溫度高於轉變溫度（例如40°C）時，會形成稀釋層，更容易脫附，從而實現超低溫蓄能。此外，熱響應離子液體的無結晶特性允許較大的濃度滑移，進而提高儲能密度。因此，仿生多層次吸濕鰓與智能熱響應離子液體的協同作用，可實現高性能吸收式熱儲能。 初步研究已證明多層次吸濕鰓吸收式熱儲能方案具有高度可行性與優異性能。本項目將採用數值模擬與實驗方法，完成以下目標：（1）用於超低溫無結晶吸收式熱儲能的多層次吸濕鰓與熱響應離子液體的模型建立與樣機開發；（2）不同轉變溫度下熱響應離子液體的相變行為、吸收動力學、傳熱傳質特性及循環穩定性表徵；（3）多層次吸濕鰓吸收式熱儲能在不同運行模式與工況條件下的動態蓄能/釋能特性及儲能性能研究；（4）基於機器學習的材料-器件-建築多尺度優化，以實現不同應用場景下的長期整體性能最佳。本研究對於開發高效率、高密度、快速響應、高適用性與高可靠性的吸收式熱儲能技術具有重要意義，並為建築脫碳提供具有前景的解決方案。預估該技術可節省60-80%的電力，減少70-90%的碳排放，投資回收期約為2-4 年。研究成果將有助於促進健康室內環境、實現碳中和目標，並推動香港及全球的可持續發展。

11222126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11222126.value: Robotic systems must increasingly interact safely and intelligently with complex environments. However, their tactile perception still lags far behind that of human skin, which naturally integrates pressure, vibration, and temperature sensing through distributed mechanoreceptors and thermoreceptors. Replicating this multimodal capability in a soft, lightweight, and stable platform remains a major challenge due to signal interference and complex fabrication processes. This project develops "Multi-Tac", a soft tri-modal tactile sensor capable of decoupled detection of three-dimensional (3D) force, vibration, and temperature within a flexible ultra-thin film architecture. The objectives are: 1) to design and optimize a multilayer tactile structure achieving intrinsic physical decoupling of mechanical, vibrational, and thermal stimuli; 2) to engineer high-fidelity signal transduction through advanced material and interface design of ionic and dielectric layers; 3) to enhance tactile resolution and perception precision using AI-driven spatial reconstruction models for contact localization; and 4) to integrate and validate the Multi-Tac system in robotic end-effectors for real-time tactile perception and manipulation. The proposed research integrates materials engineering, flexible electronics, and intelligent sensing algorithms to develop a multilayer thin-film tactile sensor that independently transduces multiple tactile modalities. Finite-element modeling will optimize the mechanical–electrical–thermal coupling and guide material and geometric design. The sensors will be fabricated using scalable soft lithography, laser patterning, and thin-film deposition. A custom signal acquisition circuit with capacitance-, voltage-, and resistance-to-digital converters will enable parallel sensing of tri-modal signals. A microcontroller-based system will process the data through neural-network–based spatial reconstruction models, generating high-resolution tactile maps and improving localization accuracy beyond physical pixel limits. The AI-driven reconstruction will further uncover cross-modal correlations, supporting autonomous adaptation and material recognition in unstructured environments. The expected outcomes and significance include: 1) a validated theoretical and experimental framework for decoupled tri-modal tactile sensing in soft thin-film devices; 2) a scalable fabrication process for soft tri-modal sensors with high sensitivity, low cross-talk, and dynamic stability; 3) an integrated hardware - software architecture for intelligent tactile signal acquisition and interpretation; 4) robotic demonstrations of human-like tactile perception for adaptive gripping, material recognition, and texture differentiation. This project will advance next-generation tactile sensing technologies essential for safe human–robot collaboration, precision manipulation, and smart manufacturing. The outcomes will also contribute to Hong Kong’s strategic development in AI robotics, soft electronics, and advanced materials. 機器人系統在安全、智能和複雜的環境工作的需求與觸覺感知能力仍遠落後於人類皮膚感知能力形成對比。人類皮膚透過分佈式機械與溫度感知，整合壓力、振動與溫度傳感。要在輕薄、穩定且柔軟的平台上複現這種多模態能力，由於訊號干擾與複雜製程等挑戰，至今仍是一大難題。 本項目開發一種柔性三模觸覺傳感器，在超薄膜結構中，對三維力、振動與溫度進行解耦偵測。目標包含：（1）設計並優化多層觸覺結構，實現機械、振動與熱刺激的內在物理解耦；（2）透過離子層與介電層之先進材料與介面設計，實現高傳真訊號轉導；（3）運用AI驅動實現空間重建模型進行接觸定位，提升觸覺解析度與感知精度；（4）將系統整合至機器人末端執行器，驗證其即時觸覺感知與操作能力。 本研究所提出的計畫整合材料工程、電子與智能傳感算法，開發一種多層薄膜觸覺傳感器，能獨立感知多種觸覺模態。將採用有限元素模擬最佳化機械–電–熱耦合效應，並指導材料與傳感器設計。傳感器將以可擴展的軟件微影技術、激光圖案化與薄膜沉積製程進行製作。定制化訊號擷取電路配備電容、電壓及電阻轉換器，可實現三模態訊號並行感測。基於微控制器的系統將透過神經網路空間重建模型處理數據，生成高解析度觸覺分佈圖，並提升定位精度。AI驅動與重建將進一步發掘跨模態關聯，支援非結構化環境中的自主適應與材料辨識。 預期成果包括：（1）建立基於柔性薄膜元件的可解耦三模態觸覺感知的理論與實驗驗證架構；（2）開發可擴展的柔性三模態傳感器製程，具高靈敏度、低串擾與動態穩定性；（3）構建智能觸覺訊號擷取與解譯的整合軟硬件架構；（4）展示機器人具類人觸覺感知，實現自適應抓取、材料辨識與紋理區分。 本項目將推動下一代觸覺感測技術，對安全人機協作、精密操作與智能製造至關重要。研究成果亦將有助於香港在AI機器人、柔性電子與先進材料等領域的發展。

11222226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11222226.value: 面向虛擬現實中肢體動作的隱私洩露研究：理論模型構建與防護

11222226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11222226.value: Virtual Reality (VR) has rapidly expanded, reaching over 200 million active users as of 2025. Its immersive experience inherently relies on continuous body-motion tracking, which has been found exploitable through unrestricted motion-sensor access to infer user privacy, like passwords, blood pressure, and vital signs, for malicious purposes. Although once considered theoretical risks under strict app-entry controls, recent malware side-loading incidents and Meta’s 1.4 billion USD fine for mishandling motion data have undermined previous trust, transforming these risks into real-world threats. Nevertheless, existing studies on motion privacy leakage in VR remain largely empirical and fragmented, offering limited insight into why motion data could inherently expose user privacy. The absence of such theoretical foundations has resulted in insufficient exploration of potential attack surfaces, leaving their risks and impacts largely unknown. Consequently, existing mitigation strategies are ad hoc and lack the generalizability required for widespread adoption. In this proposal, we will investigate the modeling and mitigation of motion privacy leakage in VR, aiming to achieve privacy-preserving body motions through two objectives: (i) understanding why user privacy is fundamentally exploitable through body motions, and (ii) exploring how to systematically mitigate these threats. For the first objective, we will establish a theoretical foundation using the stimulus–organism–response (SOR) framework, whose reliability in causal reasoning is constrained by the difficulty of characterizing the unobservable organism (O). Inspired by recent advances in facial-vibration sensing, we will investigate a neuro-behavioral approach that integrates eye-movement and EEG signals to characterize these internal processes (O); then develop an automated, LLM-guided VR-app exploration framework to overcome the manual bottleneck in systematizing the privacy-related in-app activities (S) and body motions (R); and finally construct a mathematical model that advances qualitative theory to quantitatively explain how body motions encode user privacy. Building upon these insights, the second objective focuses on systematic mitigation. We will first conduct a dataflow-driven exploration across VR’s complex architecture and technical stack to comprehensively uncover potential motion-exposing attack surfaces; then design a motion-adaptive perturbation mechanism at the OS-level to secure motion data at generation, and formulate a lightweight protocol obfuscation strategy to protect motion data in transit, together achieving end-to-end motion privacy without compromising usability. The outcomes of this project are expected to establish a theoretical foundation for exploring the fundamental security in VR's motion-privacy, provide effective mitigation techniques, and push the scientific frontier of this field forward. 虛擬現實技術近年來發展十分迅速，截至 2025 年，其活躍使用者已突破 2 億。其沉浸式體驗本質上依賴於持續的人體動作追蹤；然而研究發現，惡意分子可以利用不受限制的動作感測器存取權限，推斷出密碼、生命徵象等使用者隱私。儘管在嚴格的應用程式准入控制下，這些風險曾僅僅被視為理論上的可行，但近期發生的惡意軟體莫名加載以及 Meta 因不當處理這些動作數據被處以 14 億美元罰款的事件，打破了以往的認知，使這些風險轉變為現實世界中的真實威脅。 然而，現有關於 VR 動作隱私洩漏的研究大多留於表面，對於「動作資料為何本質上會暴露使用者隱私」缺乏深入的機理解釋。這種理論基礎的匱乏導致對潛在攻擊面的探索嚴重不足，導致其風險和影響在很大程度上未知。同時，現有的緩解策略多為針對特定問題的臨時性方案，缺乏廣泛應用所需的通用性。 在本項目中，我們將深入研究 VR 中動作隱私洩漏的建模與緩解機制，旨在透過兩大目標實現具備隱私保護的人體動作互動：(i) 揭示為何使用者隱私本質上可透過人體動作被利用以及(ii) 探索如何系統性地緩解這些威脅。針對第一個目標，我們將基於「刺激-機體-反應」（Stimulus–Organism–Response, SOR）框架建立理論基礎。由於難以對不可觀測的「機體（O）」進行刻劃，該框架在因果推理中的可靠性受到了限制。受面部振動感知最新進展的啟發，我們將探索一種融合眼動與腦電訊號的神經行為學方法，用以刻劃這些內部過程（O）；隨後開發一個由大型語言模型（LLM）引導的自動化 VR 應用程式探索框架，以突破在系統化梳理與隱私相關的應用程式內外部刺激（S）和人體動作（R）時的手動收集的瓶頸；最後建立一個數學模型，闡明人體動作是如何洩露隱私。基於上述理論構建，本項目的第二個目標聚焦於系統性的緩解手段。我們將首先解構 VR 複雜的架構和技術棧，全面揭示可能暴露動作信息的潛在攻擊面；接著在操作系統（OS）層級設計一種動作自適應擾動機制，在數據生成源頭確保其安全；同時制定一種輕量級的協定混淆策略，保護傳輸中的動作數據，在不犧牲可用性的前提下實現端對端的動作隱私保護。 本項目的預期成果將為探索 VR 動作隱私的本質安全性奠定理論基礎，提供有效的緩解於防禦技術，並推動該領域的科學前沿不斷向前發展。

11222326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11222326.value: 從 EXIF 到證據：AI 生成影像的自監督鑑識

11222326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11222326.value: High-quality text-to-image generation systems have made synthetic visuals cheap, fast, and convincing—amplifying misinformation risks and eroding trust in digital evidence. Existing detectors largely chase model-specific artifacts and treat detection as a binary classification task, limiting generalization and accountability. Existing image watermarking methods, while proactive, are often decoupled from detectors or require intrusive model access. In this proposal, we propose a unified framework that anchors both passive detection and proactive provenance to the intrinsic statistics of photographs. First, we learn a forensic feature extractor with a novel self-supervised pretext: classifying and ranking EXIF metadata from photographic images only. This forces the extractor to internalize camera-induced fingerprints that are stable over time, yielding a compact, discriminative feature space agnostic to any specific AI image generator. Second, we align this representation to the downstream task via bi-level optimization: an inner loop fine-tunes on linearly weighted EXIF-based pretexts, while an outer loop optimizes those weights for a proxy detection objective. We then fit Gaussian mixture models to the extracted features to perform likelihood-based anomaly testing for authenticity without re-training classifiers when new models emerge. Third, we extend the extractor for proactive provenance: a trigger token embedded in the text prompt encodes an imperceptible watermark during generation; the extractor, repurposed as a decoder, reliably recovers the message from the image’s forensic statistics, enabling origin verification while preserving visual quality. Preliminary evidence shows (1) tightly clustered, well-separated features across multiple generators vs. photographs, (2) competitive or superior detection accuracy to recent baselines across diverse detectors, and (3) high watermark decoding accuracy under common distortions with negligible perceptual degradation. The project will release a pre-trained forensic backbone and reference implementations for detection and watermark verification. By shifting from chasing synthetic flaws to modeling photographic traces, this work aims to establish a durable foundation for trustworthy media, benefitting the research community and downstream stakeholders in content moderation, platform integrity, and digital forensics. 高品質的文字生成圖像系統令合成視覺內容變得廉價、快速且逼真，從而加劇錯誤資訊的風險，並削弱人們對數碼證據的信任。現有偵測器大多著眼於特定模型的偽影，並將偵測視為二元分類任務，因而限制了其泛化能力與可問責性。現有的圖像浮水印方法雖具主動防禦性，卻往往與偵測器脫節，或需要侵入式存取生成模型。本研究計劃提出一個統一框架，將被動偵測與主動來源溯源共同建基於相片的內在統計特性。 首先，我們提出一項嶄新的自監督預文本任務，僅利用攝影圖像進行 EXIF 元資料的分類與排序，藉此學習鑑識特徵擷取器。這項任務迫使擷取器內化由相機產生、隨時間保持穩定的特徵指紋，從而建立一個緊湊且具判別力的特徵空間，並且不依賴任何特定的 AI 圖像生成器。其次，我們透過雙層最佳化，使該表徵與下游任務對齊：內層迴圈針對經線性加權、以 EXIF 為基礎的預文本任務進行微調；外層迴圈則根據代理偵測目標最佳化這些權重。其後，我們在所擷取的特徵上擬合高斯混合模型，透過基於概似度的異常檢驗判斷圖像真偽；即使出現新的生成模型，亦無須重新訓練分類器。第三，我們進一步擴展該擷取器，以支援主動來源溯源：嵌入文字提示中的觸發詞元會在圖像生成過程中編碼不可感知的浮水印；擷取器經重新配置為解碼器後，可從圖像的鑑識統計特性中可靠地恢復訊息，在維持視覺品質的同時驗證圖像來源。 初步證據顯示：（1）多種生成器產生的圖像與相片在特徵空間中各自高度聚集，且彼此分離清晰；（2）在多種偵測設定下，其偵測準確率可媲美或優於近期基準方法；以及（3）在常見失真處理下仍能維持高浮水印解碼準確率，同時僅造成可忽略的感知品質下降。本項目將發布預先訓練的圖像鑑識骨幹網絡，以及用於偵測與浮水印驗證的參考實作。透過由追逐合成圖像的缺陷，轉向建立攝影痕跡模型，本研究旨在為可信媒體奠定持久的基礎，惠及研究社群，以及內容審核、平台完整性和數碼鑑識等領域的下游持份者。

11222426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11222426.value: 基於觸覺互聯網的觸覺通信優化框架

11222426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11222426.value: In recent years, the Tactile Internet, which enables real-time transmission of tactile data, has emerged as a new network paradigm. Through the Tactile Internet, people and robots can now realize haptic communication at a distance, e.g., physically sense and respond to one through exchanging haptic feedback (e.g., force, vibration). This break-through promises transformative applications in teleoperation, remote surgery, immersive training, and collaborative robotics. The widespread deployment of haptic communication, however, still faces practical challenges, particularly in maintaining interaction stability and reliability when operating over uncertain networks and heterogeneous devices. A key technical hurdle lies in ensuring stable haptic transport and rendering under unstable network conditions such as delay, jitter, and packet losses. Without careful handling, these disturbances can cause force spikes or stiffness discontinuities, which severely impair user experience. Furthermore, haptic signals are often sparse, noisy, and captured by diverse devices with varying sensing capabilities. Extracting meaningful and transferable haptic information from such multimodal inputs requires careful signal modelling, alignment, and redundancy suppression. If not addressed, misinterpretation of haptic signals can lead to erroneous control decisions. In addition, decision-making in real-world environments must be robust to both dynamic physical contexts and fluctuating network conditions, so that haptic communications are not interrupted or degraded. To address these challenges, we propose a layered framework for intelligent haptic communication over the Tactile Internet that jointly enhances stability, perceptual fidelity, and decision robustness through coordinated adaptation across protocol layers. At the transport layer, we will design a predictive and congestion-aware haptic transport protocol that dynamically tunes its packetization, retransmission, and buffering strategies in response to network dynamics. At the application layer, two complementary modules will operate in concert. The perception module will build a multimodal signal modelling pipeline that aligns heterogeneous sensor inputs, suppresses redundancy, and extracts sparse-aware haptic representations. In addition, the decision module will implement an embodied, context-aware robustness strategy that integrates environmental semantics and real-time network feedback into control decisions. Together, the transport and application layers form a closed feedback loop that supports resilient, high-quality haptic interaction over time-varying and heterogeneous networks. In summary, this project aims to deliver an efficient solution that optimizes haptic communication between people and robots over the Tactile Internet, laying an important foundation for scalable, cross-platform tactile systems by enhancing haptic transport stability, perceptual robustness, and decision safety. 近年來，能夠實現觸覺數據即時傳輸的觸覺互聯網已成為一種新的網路典範。透過觸覺互聯網，人和機器人現在可以實現遠距離觸覺通信，例如，透過交換觸覺反饋（如力、振動）來物理感知並響應對方。這一突破有望在遠程操作、遠程手術、沉浸式培訓和協作機器人等領域帶來變革性應用。然而，觸覺通信的廣泛部署仍面臨實際挑戰，尤其是在不確定網路和異構設備上運行時，維持交互穩定性和可靠性的問題尤為突出。一項關鍵技術障礙在於，在時延、抖動和丟包等不穩定網路條件下，如何確保觸覺傳輸和渲染的穩定性。若處理不當，這些干擾可能嚴重損害用戶體驗。此外，觸覺信號通常是稀疏的、帶雜訊的，並且由具有不同感知能力之多種設備採集。從這類多模態輸入中提取有意義的、可遷移的觸覺信息，需要細緻的信號建模、對齊和冗餘抑制。若無法解決，對觸覺信號的誤判可能導致錯誤的控制決策。另外，現實環境中的決策必須對動態物理環境和波動網路條件均具有穩健性，以確保觸覺通信不會中斷或降質。為應對這些挑戰，我們提出了一種面向觸覺互聯網的智能觸覺通信分層框架，通過跨協議層的協同適配，聯合提升穩定性、感知保真度和決策穩健性。在傳輸層，我們將設計一種預測式且擁塞感知的觸覺傳輸協議，能夠根據網路動態動態調整其打包、重傳和緩衝策略。在應用層，兩個互補模塊將協同運行。感知模塊將構建一條多模態信號建模流水線，用於對齊異構傳感器輸入、抑制冗餘，並提取稀疏感知的觸覺表示。此外，決策模塊將實現一種具身的、上下文感知的穩健性策略，將環境語義和即時網路反饋整合到控制決策中。傳輸層與應用層共同構成一個閉環反饋迴路，支持在時變和異構網路上實現具有彈性的高質量觸覺交互。總之，本項目旨在提供一種高效解決方案，優化觸覺互聯網上人與機器人之間的觸覺通信，通過增強觸覺傳輸穩定性、感知穩健性和決策安全性，為可擴展、跨平台的觸覺系統奠定重要基礎。

11222526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11222526.value: Proteins are the fundamental building blocks of life, and determining their precise sequences is crucial for understanding biological function and diseases such as cancer and Alzheimer's. However, directly reading the sequence of a protein—a chain of 20 types of amino acids—remains a formidable challenge. Current methods, such as mass spectrometry and Edman degradation, are slow, costly, and lack single-molecule sensitivity. While nanopore technology, which detects molecules via current disruptions as they pass through a nanopore, has revolutionized DNA sequencing, its application to proteins faces two core obstacles: the substantial signal overlap arising from similar physicochemical properties of many amino acids, and the lack of a robust computational framework to decode these complex signal patterns into an accurate sequence. To overcome these barriers, we propose a groundbreaking research program that integrates molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, rational nanopore engineering, and advanced machine learning (ML). This multi-nanopore approach, employing a tailored array of nanopores to collect multidimensional signal data, combined with a powerful ML-based decoder, will provide the information richness necessary to uniquely identify all 20 amino acid residues. This project is structured into three synergistic phases: (1) Mechanistic Insight through MD Simulation: MD simulations are utilized as a "computational microscope" to observe protein translocation at atomic resolution, elucidating the molecular mechanisms of signal generation and overlap. (2) Rational Nanopore Design and Screening: Guided by these insights, we will design and screen a library of engineered MspA nanopores. The objective is to identify a minimal set of pores that, as an ensemble, generates a unique and robust multi-channel fingerprint for each type of residue. (3) ML-Driven Decoding and Validation: We will construct a comprehensive database by simulating multi-dimensional signals of thousands of protein fragments across our selected nanopore set. This database will train a sophisticated ML model to act as a universal signal decoder, converting electrical fingerprints directly into accurate sequences. These phases directly address the core challenges: Phase 1 tackles the root cause of signal overlap, Phase 2 overcomes it through multi-dimensional fingerprinting, and Phase 3 solves the decoding problem. The success of this project will yield transformative outcomes, providing unprecedented atomistic insights for nanopore optimization, establishing a novel paradigm for multi-dimensional protein signal analysis, and delivering a powerful algorithmic toolkit for protein sequencing. This technology has the potential to democratize protein sequencing, dramatically accelerating advancements in drug discovery, early disease diagnostics, and enzyme engineering. 蛋白質是生命的基本構成單元，確定其精確序列對於理解生物功能以及癌症、阿茲海默症等疾病至關重要。然而，直接讀取蛋白質序列——即由20種胺基酸組成的鏈條——仍然是一項艱鉅的挑戰。現有方法如質譜法和艾德曼降解，不僅速度慢、成本高，且缺乏單分子靈敏度。雖然奈米孔技術（藉由分子通過奈米孔時產生的電流干擾來偵測分子）已徹底改變DNA定序，但其應用於蛋白質時面臨兩大核心障礙：許多胺基酸相似的物理化學性質導致信號大量重疊，以及缺乏強健的計算框架來將這些複雜信號模式解碼為準確序列。為克服這些障礙，我們提出一項開創性的研究計畫，整合分子動力學（MD）模擬、合理的奈米孔工程設計與先進的機器學習（ML）。此多奈米孔策略採用特製的奈米孔陣列收集多維度信號數據，結合強大的ML解碼器，將提供足以唯一識別所有20種胺基酸殘基的豐富資訊。本計畫分為三個協同階段：（1）透過MD模擬獲得機制洞見：將MD模擬用作「計算顯微鏡」，以原子解析度觀察蛋白質易位，闡明信號產生與重疊的分子機制。（2）合理設計與篩選奈米孔：根據這些洞見，我們將設計並篩選一個工程化MspA奈米孔庫，目標是找出最小的一組孔道，使其作為整體能為每種殘基產生獨特且強健的多通道指紋。（3）ML驅動的解碼與驗證：我們將透過模擬所選奈米孔組中數千個蛋白質片段的多維度信號，建立一個綜合資料庫，該資料庫將用於訓練一個精密的ML模型，使其成為通用的信號解碼器，直接將電學指紋轉換為準確序列。這些階段直接針對核心挑戰：第一階段處理信號重疊的根本原因，第二階段透過多維度指紋識別來克服該問題，第三階段則解決解碼難題。本計畫的成功將帶來變革性成果，為奈米孔最佳化提供前所未有的原子級洞見，建立多維度蛋白質信號分析的新典範，並提供一套用於蛋白質定序的強大演算法工具組。這項技術有望使蛋白質定序普及化，大幅加速藥物發現、早期疾病診斷和酵素工程等領域的進展。

11223126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11223126.value: 增強單個手性等離激元納腔的超拉曼光學活性來實現單分子水平對映體識別

11223126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11223126.value: Chirality, the geometric property of an object that cannot be superimposed on its mirror image, lies at the heart of many natural phenomena, including the handedness of amino acids and DNA. Detecting and manipulating chirality at the nanoscale has therefore become a major scientific frontier, underpinning applications in molecular sensing, enantiomer separation, and chiral optoelectronics. Although circular dichroism (CD) has long been employed for characterizing molecular chirality, its inherently weak signals (typically one ten-thousandth of the total absorption) severely limit sensitivity. This limitation becomes critical as modern pharmaceutical and biochemical research increasingly moves toward miniaturized and high-throughput analyses. Recent studies demonstrated that, due to their multi-photon and symmetry-sensitive nature, nonlinear processes offer a promising alternative for probing chirality with much higher sensitivity [Nat.
