Photon. 16, 126-133 (2022)]; hyper-Raman optical activity was experimentally observed via chirality transfer from metallic nanohelices to achiral molecules [Nat. Photon. 18, 982–989 (2024)]. However, these advances remain limited to chirality conferral to achiral molecules, and the nonlinear optical interaction between intrinsically chiral molecules and chiral nano-resonators has yet to be explored. Moreover, current demonstrations of nonlinear chiroptics are limited to ensemble measurements on arrayed structures, where averaging over many elements obscures the direct correlation between local chiral fields and far-field polarization. Achieving strong, controllable nonlinear chiral responses at the single-resonator level still remains a major challenge. In this project, we will investigate nonlinear chiroptical properties of single chiral nanoparticle-on-mirror (c-NPoM) cavities, focusing on processes like second-harmonic generation (SHG) and hyper-Raman scattering (HRS), with the long-term objective of enabling single-molecule enantiomer discrimination. The c-NPoM cavities generate super-chiral fields with significantly enhanced optical chirality, yielding chiral nonlinear polarization and measurable SHG CD. This unique property provide the ideal condition for hyper-Raman optical activity: when a chiral molecule is embedded into the c-NPoM cavity, the super-chiral fields can amplify the intrinsic molecular optical activity. This approach enables direct access to chiral vibrational information that is inaccessible to linear or ensemble-averaged measurements. The extreme local field enhancement (up to 10,000) and significant electron-phonon coupling in the cavity-molecule hybrid open the possibility of single-molecule-level enantiomer discrimination. Overall, this project will establish a versatile platform for controlling chiroptical nonlinear response at the nanoscale, from chiral SHG to hyper-Raman optical activity. By combining experimental and theoretical approaches, we will develop comprehensive understanding of the interplay between local near-field chirality and nonlinear emission and identify promising systems toward highly robust chiroptical sensing. 手性是指物體無法與其鏡像完全重合的幾何屬性，廣泛存在於多種自然現象之中，例如氨基酸和DNA的手性構型。對納米尺度手性的探測與調控已成為重要的科學前沿，支撐著分子傳感、對映體分離及手性光電子學等領域的發展。圓二色性長期被用於表征分子手性，但其信號微弱，通常僅為總吸收信號的萬分之一，因而嚴重限制了檢測靈敏度。隨著現代醫藥和生物化學研究日益向微型化和高通量分析發展，這一局限變得尤為突出。 近期研究表明，得益於多光子過程及其對體系對稱性的高度敏感性，非線性光學過程為實現高靈敏手性探測提供了極具前景的新途徑［Nat. Photon. 16, 126–133 (2022)］。此外，研究人員已通過將金屬納米螺旋結構的手性轉移至非手性分子，實驗觀測到超拉曼光學活性［Nat. Photon. 18, 982–989 (2024)］。然而，現有研究主要局限於向非手性分子賦予手性，本征手性分子與手性納腔之間的非線性光學相互作用仍有待探索。與此同時，當前非線性手性光學研究多基於對陣列結構進行整體測量，大量結構單元的平均化掩蓋了局域手性場與遠場偏振之間的直接關聯。因此，如何在單個諧振腔尺度上實現強且可控的非線性手性響應仍是一項重要挑戰。 本項目擬研究單個手性納米顆粒-鏡面腔（chiral nanoparticle-on-mirror, c-NPoM）的非線性手性光學性質，重點關注二次諧波產生（second-harmonic generation, SHG）和超拉曼散射（hyper-Raman scattering, HRS）等過程，並以實現單分子尺度的對映體識別為終極目標。c-NPoM納腔能夠產生超手性局域近場，從而顯著增強光學手性密度，進而產生手性非線性極化和可測量的SHG圓二色性。這一獨特性質為研究超拉曼光學活性提供了理想條件：當手性分子嵌入c-NPoM腔後，腔內超手性場可顯著放大分子本征的光學活性，從而直接獲取在線性光學測量或系綜平均測量中難以分辨的手性振動信息。腔-分子混合結構中極高的局部近場增強（高達10,000倍）和顯著的電子-聲子耦合為單分子級對映體區分提供了可能。 總體而言，本項目將建立一個可在納米尺度調控非線性手性光學響應的通用平台，涵蓋從手性SHG到超拉曼光學活性等多種特性。通過實驗研究與理論分析相結合，我們將系統揭示局域近場手性與非線性發射之間的相互作用機制，並篩選出有望用於高可靠性手性光學傳感的系統。

11300526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11300526.value: 理解與應對波動水解條件下的電催化劑動態衰減

11300526.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11300526.value: Prof Choi, Chang Hyuck Prof Wang , Ying

11300526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300526.value: Directly coupling electrolyzers with renewable electricity is critical for widespread, cost-effective green fuel production, yet the inherent power variability accelerates electrolyzer degradation. Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), a scalable hydrogen-producing technology, is further limited by the scarcity of iridium as the benchmark oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalyst. While alternatives including ruthenium-based and even noble-metal-free oxides (e.g., Science 2025, 387,48–55, Science 2024, 384, 1373) have emerged, their stability remains inadequate even under steady conditions (e.g., >60 °C, > 1A cm-2). Intermittent operation further challenges these representative OER catalysts, and the underlying degradation mechanisms remain unclear. This project will first elucidate dynamic electrocatalyst degradation under fluctuating water-oxidation conditions by combining multiscale, millisecond-resolution high-speed operando characterizations with tailored power profiles (hold, square-wave, and triangle-wave cycles at varying potentials/frequencies). Using model oxide catalysts spanning both iridium-based and iridium-free oxides (IrO₂, RuO₂, MnO₂, Co₃O₄), we aim to uncover how intermittent operation accelerates degradation through pathways such as active-site dissolution, configurational reconstruction (e.g., by frequent redox cycling), and interfacial deterioration. Temporally resolved operando techniques (down to 100 ms) across catalyst, interface, and cell levels will clarify degradation origins and enable reliable extrapolation for predicting long-term stability. This integrated approach will establish how cycling conditions govern degradation kinetics and distribution and also address electrode-scale heterogeneity, where localized variations in current, temperature, and mechanical stress may lead to spatially non-uniform performance loss. We will then employ a "disorder tailoring" strategy to mitigate dynamic degradation through controlled synthesis and heteroatom doping. This approach enables bidirectional tuning of catalyst disorder (degree, range, distribution)—introducing beneficial disorder or reducing excessive randomness— to optimize structural and electronic properties (e.g., local flexibility). Such modifications optimize interactions with reaction intermediates and electrolytes, improving the OER performance. First-principle calculations will be conducted to model the disordered structure (e.g., via a simulated melt–quench method) and supplement operando characterizations to clarify the modulation mechanisms. Finally, optimized catalysts and membrane electrode assemblies will be validated in PEM electrolyzers under simulated fluctuating conditions (following national standards) and actual solar cell coupling. Our target is a stable hydrogen gas output with <3% degradation over 100 days under fluctuating conditions, setting a benchmark performance. By pioneering the investigation of electrocatalysts under fluctuating power conditions, this project will advance the practical design of catalysts and the development of clean energy technologies. 將電解槽與可再生電力直接耦合對於實現大規模且具成本效益的綠色燃料生產至關重要；然而，再生能源固有的電力波動性會加速電解槽的衰減（degradation）。質子交換膜水電解（PEMWE）作為一種具備擴展性的製氫技術，目前仍受到析氧反應（OER）催化劑——銥（Iridium）稀缺性的嚴重限制。儘管近年已出現包括釕（Ruthenium）基甚至無貴金屬氧化物等替代方案（例如 Science 2025, 387, 48–55；Science 2024, 384, 1373），但這些材料即使在穩定條件下（例如 >60°C，> 1 A cm⁻²）的穩定性依然不足。間歇性運行進一步對這些具代表性的 OER 催化劑帶來挑戰，且其潛在的衰減機制仍不不明確。 本計畫將結合多尺度、毫秒級解析度的原位動態表徵技術（high-speed operando characterizations）與專屬調配的電源曲線（包含不同電位與頻率下的恆定、方波及三角波循環），首次闡明水氧化動態條件下的電催化劑動態衰減機制。我們將採用涵蓋銥基與無銥氧化物（如 IrO₂、RuO₂、MnO₂、Co₃O₄）的模型氧化物催化劑，揭示間歇性運行如何透過活性位點溶解、構型重構（例如由頻繁的氧化還原循環引發）以及界面惡化等路徑加速衰減。透過跨催化劑、界面及電解池層級的時間解析原位動態技術（解析度達 100 ms），本研究將釐清衰減根源，並實現可靠的外推預測以推算長期穩定性。此整合性方法不僅能確立循環條件如何支配衰減動力學與空間分佈，還能解決電極尺度的異質性問題——即電流、溫度與機械應力的局部差異所導致的空間非均勻效能損失。 隨後，我們將採用「無序調控」（disorder tailoring）策略，透過可控合成與雜原子摻雜來緩解動態衰減。此方法能雙向調控催化劑的無序度（程度、範圍與分佈）——引入有利的無序結構或減少過度的隨機性——從而最佳化結構與電子性質（例如局部柔韌性）。此類修飾可最佳化催化劑與反應中間體及電解質之間的相互作用，進而提升 OER 效能。我們將進行第一性原理計算（First-principle calculations）來模擬無序結構（例如透過熔融淬火模擬法），並輔以原位動態表徵以闡明調控機制。 最後，最佳化後的催化劑與膜電極組件（MEA）將在模擬波動條件（遵循國家標準）及真實太陽能電池耦合下，於 PEM 電解槽中進行驗證。我們的目標是在波動條件下運行 100 天後，實現衰減率 <3% 的穩定氫氣輸出，樹立基準效能。 本計畫開創性地探索波動電源條件下的電催化劑行為，將推動催化劑的實用化設計並促進清潔能源技術的發展。

11301026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11301026.value: 分布式计算环境下抗干扰的统计估计方法

11301026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11301026.value: Distributed statistical estimation and learning has received significant attention in recent years. This research proposal addresses the challenges of robust statistical estimation and learning in distributed systems, in the context of data abnormalities and vicious attackers. As the reliance on distributed learning frameworks grows, so does the necessity for methods that can tolerate various types of data contamination, including heavy-tailed distributions, Huber's contamination, and adversarial attacks. Our primary objective is to develop robust distributed algorithms that can effectively handle multiple types of data abnormalities simultaneously. We propose methods that integrate robust statistical techniques into distributed learning architectures, including the master-worker system and the peer-to-peer system. By leveraging recent advancements in robust statistics and machine learning, we aim to create algorithms that not only come with theoretical guarantees but also are computationally tractable/efficient for real-world applications. 近年來，隨著數據規模的爆炸性成長，分散式學習已成為主流典範。然而，現實中的數據往往並不「乾淨」——既可能天生帶有極端值，也可能遭受外部的蓄意破壞。面對種種干擾，傳統的集中式演算法往往不堪一擊，而分散式環境下的不確定性更是放大了這一脆弱性。本課題嘗試跳脫「逐一應對」的慣性思路，轉而探索一套具備廣譜抗干擾能力的分散式學習方案，力求在重尾雜訊、混合污染乃至惡意攻擊交織的複雜場景中，依然保持穩定的估計效能。我們將把經過驗證的穩健統計工具，系統性地嵌入主流的分散式框架（如集中化調度與去中心化協作），並在此過程中尋求理論嚴謹性與計算可行性的平衡，最終為現實部署提供兼具保障與效率的技術路徑。

11301226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11301226.value: 南大洋與南大西洋新生代深海底棲生態系統之演變：以介形蟲化石為模型

11301226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11301226.value: Cenozoic deep-sea evolution and its ties to climate change remain poorly understood, mainly because of the paucity of fossil records, especially those of metazoan invertebrates on which a major part of deep-sea organismal biology has been built. A notable exception is crustacean ostracods, that have excellent fossil records from deep-sea sediment cores. However, the major comprehensive studies on Cenozoic deep-sea ostracod evolution were done decades ago and did not show consistent results with each other, across regions, and compared to other taxa, with only some studies revealing long-term diversification and short-term radiations or extinctions coinciding with periods of global climate change. Since then, there has been no major comprehensive study to reconcile their findings and account for various possible issues, including low abundance, lack of rigorous statistics, different methodologies, and coarse temporal resolution. Here, we plan to study Cenozoic deep-sea ostracods from sediment cores known to have or with high probability of sufficiently high ostracod abundance, focusing on the Southern and South Atlantic Oceans, known as a center of origin and a hotspot of deep-sea biodiversity. By using high abundance samples and sophisticated statistics to further address possible biases, we will reconstruct Cenozoic-through historical dynamics of deep-sea metazoan invertebrate ecosystem and diversity, by using fossil ostracods as a proxy. The role of climate change in driving reconstructed patterns will be evaluated using numerical simulations of past environmental conditions and species ecophysiology. This project will give new insights about fundamental questions in deep-sea biology: When and how have modern type deep-sea fauna and diversity been developed and established? When was and what caused the last major deep-sea extinction? How have Cenozoic paleoclimatic and paleoceanographic changes affected deep-sea ecosystem and biodiversity? 新生代的深海演化及其與氣候變化的關聯至今仍不為人所熟知，這主要是由於化石記錄的匱乏，特別是作為深海生物學主要研究基礎的後生無脊椎動物化石。一個顯著的例外是甲殼類的介形蟲，牠們在深海沉積物岩芯中留下了極佳的化石記錄。然而，過去數十年來針對新生代深海介形蟲演化所進行的主要綜合性研究，其結果在不同區域之間、以及與其他分類群相比時均不一致，僅有少數研究顯示長期的多樣化以及短期的輻射演化或滅絕事件與全球氣候變化時期相吻合。自此以後，便缺乏大型的綜合性研究來調和這些發現，並解決各種潛在問題，包括樣本豐度低、缺乏嚴謹的統計數據、方法學差異以及時間解析度粗糙等。 在本研究中，我們計畫使用已知或極可能具備足夠高介形蟲豐度的深海沉積物岩芯，進行新生代深海介形蟲研究，並聚焦於作為深海生物多樣性起源中心與熱點的南大洋及南大西洋。藉由高豐度樣本與精密的統計方法以進一步消除潛在偏差，我們將以介形蟲化石作為代理指標，重建整個新生代的深海後生無脊椎動物生態系統與多樣性的歷史動態。氣候變化在推動這些重建模式中所扮演的角色，將透過過去環境條件與物種生理生態學的數值模擬進行評估。此項目將為深海生物學的根本問題提供新的見解：現代型深海動物群與多樣性於何時以及如何發展並建立？最近一次重大深海滅絕事件發生於何時及原因為何？新生代的古氣候與古海洋學變化如何影響了深海生態系統及生物多樣性？

11301426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11301426.value: SARS-CoV-2變異株動態早期預測：基於病毒與抗體及ACE2受體之交互作用建模

11301426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11301426.value: The continuous emergence of new SARS-CoV-2 variants presents significant challenges to public health efforts. In response to epidemic outbreaks, one critical challenge is to predict early which variants have a high transmission potential before they spread widely. Early identification allows for timely public health measures, including vaccine development. However, the capacity for early prediction in the current methods is limited. The most widely used predictive approaches, such as multinomial logistic regression (MLR) or mechanistic models (compartmental models for infectious disease transmission), often ignore population immunity or actual viral traits. Current predictive models cannot capture the trade-off between ACE2 binding and immune escape that has been observed. Recent advances in deep mutational scanning have provided valuable data on two important virus traits: immune escape and the binding affinity to the ACE2 receptor. Biophysical modelling can map these two phenotypes to viral fitness in growth. Hence, we aim to develop an early prediction framework for SARS-CoV-2 variant dynamics by embedding a biophysical model based on mutational effects in the spike protein, derived from deep mutational scanning data, alongside population immunity. In this proposal, we first demonstrate how to formulate viral fitness depending on two infection stages: the initial stage after susceptible individuals are exposed to the virus, and the infectious period when infected individuals can transmit the disease. This shows a trade-off pattern between ACE2 binding and immune escape. We then construct a cross-immunity function using these traits and population immunity under biophysical principles in a transmission model. The ACE2 binding of each variant will be estimated using a computational tool accounting for measurement errors and epistasis. We train the model using Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo and perform model comparison. The complexity of the candidate models will be systematically increased along two dimensions: biophysical constraints and human heterogeneity. Model validation will be conducted on unseen (out-of-time) data to assess predictive performance. Finally, we refine the proposed model by incorporating unknown mutational effects outside the receptor-binding domain of the spike protein. Sensitivity analysis will be performed to assess the influence of uncertainties at different levels, from viral trait measurements to heterogeneity in the host population, and to quantify model robustness using failure-rate metrics. Both parameter and structural uncertainties are addressed. The robust early predictive tool, mechanistically guided by biophysical principles, will help ensure timely vaccine production and establish a quantitative framework for understanding viral evolutionary dynamics and the role of host heterogeneity.

11301526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11301526.value: 研究與表徵具選擇性識別 N6‑甲基腺苷之 RNA 結合蛋白

11301526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11301526.value: Inside each cell, some RNA molecules are marked by a chemical tag known as m6A. This tag acts like a sticky note, guiding the cell on how to use the RNA. Special proteins, called "readers" interact with and interpret these sticky notes. These readers are crucial for health, and their malfunction can lead to cancer. However, many of these readers remain undiscovered due to the technical challenges in detecting them. Cancer cells often become resistant to treatments because they excel at repairing damaged DNA. Recent findings suggest that m6A-modified RNAs help cancer cells repair this damage, leading to treatment failure. While we know of a few reader proteins involved, our current detection methods are limited, akin to searching for specific individuals in a crowded stadium using a dim flashlight, likely missing many key players. Our project aims to uncover these hidden readers and characterize them. Our project will introduce a powerful new method called PRICE, which functions like a high-speed searchlight, enabling the rapid testing of hundreds of proteins to identify those attracted to the m6A sticky notes. Initial tests with this method have been successful, identifying 52 readers, including 35 previously unknown ones, such as a protein called HNRNPK. The project has three main objectives: (1) The Big Search: Using PRICE technology, we will screen 500 human proteins to significantly expand the list of known m6A readers. (2) The Deep Dive: We will study the newly identified reader, HNRNPK, to understand its role in helping cancer cells repair DNA and resist treatment. We will test whether inhibiting HNRNPK can make cancer cells more susceptible to existing drugs. (3) The AI Predictor: We will employ Artificial Intelligence to analyze our data and develop a computer model that predicts other potential but untested m6A readers in the human body, guiding future discoveries beyond our project. By achieving these goals, we will enhance our understanding of cellular processes. The readers, like HNRNPK, could serve as targets for new drugs. A medication that blocks a specific reader could impair a cancer cell's repair mechanisms, making treatments like chemotherapy more effective. Our PRICE and AI technology will become invaluable resources for scientists globally, accelerating discoveries not only in cancer but also in other diseases influenced by this hidden RNA language. In essence, we are piecing together a cellular puzzle to develop smarter, more effective means to characterize epitranscriptomic regulators. 在人體每一個細胞之內，RNA 上都刻寫著一套隱藏的語言 ——RNA 是負責傳遞 DNA 關鍵指令的分子。這套語言當中最重要的「詞彙」之一，就是名為 m⁶A 的化學修飾標記。該標記如同便利貼，向細胞傳達 RNA 的運作方式。已知這類閱讀蛋白對維持機體健康至關重要，一旦其功能異常，便會引發癌症。然而，由於檢測技術存在局限，我們推測絕大部分此類閱讀蛋白仍未被發現。本研究計劃旨在找出這些尚未被揭曉的閱讀蛋白，並探究如何運用相關知識研發更優質的癌症治療方案。本計劃將開發一套名為 PRICE 的全新高效技術，可一次性快速篩選數百種蛋白，鑑定哪些蛋白能夠結合 m⁶A修飾。初步實驗已證實該技術可行，成功鑑定出 52 種閱讀蛋白，當中 35 種為全新發現，HNRNPK 即為其中一例。 本計劃設有三大核心目標： (1) 大規模篩查：運用 PRICE 技術篩選 500 種人類蛋白，大幅擴充已知 m⁶A 閱讀蛋白的庫存； (2) 深度機制研究：針對極具研究潛力的新發現閱讀蛋白 HNRNPK 開展研究，釐清其協助癌細胞修復 DNA、產生治療抗藥性的具體機制；同時測試抑制 HNRNPK 能否提升癌細胞對現有藥物的敏感性； (3) 人工智慧預測模型：透過人工智慧（AI）分析實驗數據，建構電腦預測模型，預測人體內其他潛在的 m⁶A 閱讀蛋白，為計劃結束後的後續研究提供指引。 完成本計劃後，我們將為細胞運作機制帶來全新的基礎認知。更重要的是，研究成果可直接惠及病患。舉例而言，本計劃發現的 HNRNPK 等閱讀蛋白，可作為新藥研發的作用靶點。透過藥物抑制特定閱讀蛋白，能夠削弱癌細胞的自我修復能力，令化療等常規治療的效果顯著提升。我們建立的 PRICE 技術與 AI 模型，亦會成為全球科研人員的共用研究資源，不僅加快癌症領域的研究進展，亦推動其他受這套 RNA 隱藏語言影響的疾病研究。簡而言之，本計劃將補全細胞生物學的未知拼圖，為對抗癌症研發更精準、更有效的治療工具。

11302026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11302026.value: 高效直接電解含氧模擬烟氣製備多碳産物

11302026.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11302026.value: Prof Hung, Sung-Fu Dr Xu, Aoni

11302026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302026.value: Electrocatalytic CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) to value-added multi-carbon (C2+) products provides an attractive path for storing intermittent renewables. However, the process typically requires high-purity CO2 as a feedstock, which undermines its economic viability and practical feasibility. Direct utilization of flue gas for CO2RR (i.e. direct flue gas electrolysis) in acidic media is a promising strategy to reduce operating expenses by eliminating the need for energy-intensive CO2 separation and purification from flue gas and to address the CO2 loss issue arising from alkaline/neutral media. The challenge of direct flue gas electrolysis, though, lies in selectively facilitating CO2RR to C2+ products while simultaneously suppressing the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) favored thermodynamically, owing to the low CO2 concentration and the presence of O2 impurities in flue gas. In this project, leveraging our prior research experience in CO2RR-related catalyst design and reaction engineering, based on O2-containing simulated flue gas feeds, we aim to address the aforementioned challenge in direct flue gas electrolysis through integrating catalyst design and system development. On the one hand, we will develop a cation exchange membrane (CEM) based acidic membrane electrode assembly (MEA) electrolysis system for direct O2-containing simulated flue gas electrolysis to C2+ products. On the other hand, we aim to develop molecule-modified Cu-based catalysts to improve C2+ selectivity at high current densities, CO2 utilization efficiency, and stability simultaneously under CEM-based acidic MEA system in direct O2-containing simulated flue gas electrolysis. Our preliminary results show that 3,5-diamino-1,2,4-triazole molecule-modified Cu catalysts deliver a high C2+ selectivity of 50% at 200 mA cm-2 in the proof-of-concept CEM-based acidic MEA system, suggesting that molecule-modified catalysts integrated with a CEM-based acidic MEA system are promising to promote CO2-to-C2+ from O2-containing simulated flue gas. Lastly, by uniting in situ/operando spectroscopic characterization techniques with theoretical calculations, we will establish the structure-property relations of molecule-modified Cu-based catalysts towards direct O2-containing simulated flue gas electrolysis to C2+ products. The successful implementation of this project will generate crucial knowledge for designing high-efficiency CO2-to-C2+ electrocatalysts using O2-containing simulated flue gas. This work will advance the development of direct flue gas electrolysis technology, facilitating its future practical applications and contributing to Hong Kong’s goal of achieving carbon neutrality by 2050.

11302126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11302126.value: 挖掘早期分支真菌中未被開發的生物合成酶與天然產物資源

11302126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302126.value: Fungi are prolific producers of a diverse array of chemicals, generally known as “natural products.” These compounds and their derivatives have benefited human society as pharmaceutical drugs, agrochemicals, and cosmetic ingredients. At the same time, fungi can also produce toxic compounds, or mycotoxins, that cause diseases in humans and other organisms. Notably, these fungal natural products known to date are almost exclusively derived from a major group of fungi, the Dikarya. In contrast, early-diverging fungi outside the Dikarya have received little attention, despite their diverse ecological roles in nature. These lineages represent a promising treasure trove for the discovery of natural products. Recent studies have shown that microbial genomes contain numerous biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs)—sets of genes that work collaboratively to synthesize natural products—that cannot yet be linked to known compounds. Our preliminary analysis revealed that chytrids, representative early-diverging fungi, harbor BGCs with unusual features. Given the markedly limited studies on chytrid natural products, these BGCs may direct the biosynthesis of natural products with unprecedented molecular scaffolds and notable biological activities. This project thus aims to exploit the biosynthetic potential of chytrids, as well as other early-diverging fungi, to uncover previously undescribed natural products. The key questions this project addresses are: (1) What is the biosynthetic potential of early-diverging fungi? (2) What natural products are encoded by their BGCs? (3) What are the biosynthetic mechanisms and biological activities of these compounds? To answer these questions, we will first perform a comprehensive genomic analysis of early-diverging fungi. Selected BGCs will then be heterologously expressed in the fungus Aspergillus oryzae to uncover previously unreported natural products. Subsequently, the biosynthetic pathways leading to these compounds will be elucidated, and in-depth functional analyses of selected biosynthetic enzymes will be conducted. Finally, the biological activities and, where feasible, the ecological roles of the obtained natural products will be examined. In summary, by unlocking the biosynthetic potential of early-diverging fungi, this proposed project seeks to expand the chemical space of natural products and the repertoire of biosynthetic enzymes. It will also deepen our understanding of fungal natural product biosynthesis and facilitate studies on previously overlooked fungal lineages, contributing to drug discovery, biotechnological innovation, and a broader understanding of fungal ecology. 真菌能夠大量產生種類多樣的化學物質，這些物質通常被稱為「天然產物」。這些化合物及其衍生物已作為藥物、農用化學品和化妝品成分造福人類社會。與此同時，真菌也能產生有毒化合物，即真菌毒素，並在人類及其他生物中引起疾病。值得注意的是，迄今已知的真菌天然產物幾乎全部來源於真菌的一個主要類群——雙核菌亞界（Dikarya）。相比之下，雙核菌亞界以外的早期分支真菌儘管在自然界中具有多樣的生態作用，卻很少受到關注。這些譜系因此是發現天然產物的一座極具潛力的寶庫。 近期研究顯示，微生物基因組中含有大量生物合成基因簇（biosynthetic gene clusters，BGCs）——即一組協同作用以合成天然產物的基因——而這些基因簇目前尚無法與已知化合物建立聯繫。我們的初步分析顯示，壺菌作為早期分支真菌的代表，其生物合成基因簇具有異常特徵。鑑於目前對壺菌天然產物的研究明顯有限，這些生物合成基因簇負責合成的天然產物可能具有前所未有的分子骨架和顯著的生物活性。因此，本項目旨在利用壺菌以及其他早期分化真菌的生物合成潛力，以發現此前尚未被描述的天然產物。 本項目所要回答的關鍵問題包括：（1）早期分支真菌具有何種生物合成潛力？（2）其生物合成基因簇編碼哪些天然產物？（3）這些化合物具有怎樣的生物合成機制和生物活性？為回答這些問題，我們首先將對早期分支真菌進行全面的基因組分析。隨後，將在真菌米麴菌（Aspergillus oryzae）中異源表達選定的生物合成基因簇，以發現此前未被報導的天然產物。其後，將闡明產生這些化合物的生物合成途徑，並對選定的生物合成酶進行深入的功能分析。最後，將研究所得天然產物的生物活性，並在可行的情況下研究其生態作用。 總而言之，通過發掘早期分支真菌的生物合成潛力，本擬議項目旨在拓展天然產物的化學空間和生物合成酶的種類。該項目亦將加深我們對真菌天然產物生物合成的理解，並促進對此前被忽視的真菌譜系之研究，從而為藥物發現、生物技術創新以及對真菌生態學更廣泛的理解作出貢獻。

11302426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11302426.value: 面向彈道輸運與鐵電器件的二維金屬單硫族化合物層數依賴型多晶型調控

11302426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302426.value: The exceptional carrier mobility and ferroelectric properties, particularly monolayer intralayer ferroelectricity and interlayer sliding ferroelectricity, of two-dimensional (2D) metal monochalcogenide (MX) materials such as InSe, GaSe, and GaTe have emerged as a prominent subject of investigation. However, a comprehensive understanding of how thickness, pressure, and temperature affect the phase (including stacking order) and polymorphism — and how these, in turn, influence the resulting physical properties — remains lacking. No unified criteria currently exist to correlate structure and properties across various MX polymorphs, resulting in fragmented and often contradictory findings in the literature. Among the different phases, the γ (gamma) and ε (epsilon) phases are often linked with high mobility and promise for ballistic device applications. Notably, the γ phase has been reported to exhibit sliding or intralayer ferroelectricity, while the more thermodynamically stable β (beta) phase dominates under standard conditions. These conflicting observations have led to significant discrepancies in reported results, posing challenges for both fundamental research and practical device integration. This project aims to systematically establish a clear and comprehensive correlation between polymorphic structures and the electronic and ferroelectric properties of MX materials. We will investigate phase stability and transformation mechanisms, as well as methods to regulate and control phase formation. Special emphasis will be placed on the influence of thickness (layer number), temperature, and pressure on phase kinetics. These factors will be explored using advanced techniques such as diamond anvil cell (DAC) experiments, in situ scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), and density functional theory (DFT) simulations. We will distinguish the roles of interlayer and intralayer lattice dynamics in determining the phase stability of MX polymorphs and propose phase engineering strategies tailored for various thickness regimes. Furthermore, we aim to scale up the synthesis of high-quality 2D MX materials, enabling practical device fabrication. To validate structure–property relationships, we will experimentally determine key physical parameters, including carrier mobility and ferroelectric polarization, across different MX phases, using representative materials such as InSe, GaSe, and GaTe. For device applications, we will develop and optimize two types of devices based on MX materials: (1) Ballistic field-effect transistors (FETs) targeting: carrier mobility > 260 cm²/V·s, subthreshold swing (SS) < 75 mV/decade, operating voltage < 0.5 V. (2) Ferroelectric memory devices (FeFETs) with: on/off ratio > 10^6, program/erase ratio > 10^3. This project will provide foundational understanding and practical guidelines for realizing next-generation electronic and memory devices using polymorphic MX materials. 二維（2D）金屬單硫族化合物（MX，如 InSe、GaSe 和 GaTe）因其卓越的載流子遷移率和鐵電特性（特別是單層內的面內鐵電性和層間滑移鐵電性）而成為備受關注的研究熱點。然而，目前對於厚度、壓力和溫度如何影響材料相（包括堆疊順序）及多晶型特徵——以及這些因素如何進而影響材料的物理性質——尚缺乏全面的認識。由於缺乏統一的標準來關聯各種 MX 多晶型的結構與性質，導致現有文獻中的研究結果往往零散且相互矛盾。 在多種物相中，γ（伽瑪）相和 ε（艾普西龍）相常被認為具有高遷移率，在彈道輸運裝置應用方面展現出巨大潛力。值得注意的是，已有研究顯示 γ 相表現出滑移鐵電性或面內鐵電性，而在標準條件下，熱力學穩定性較高的 β（貝塔）相則佔據主導地位。這些相互矛盾的觀測結果導致了報告資料間的顯著差異，為基礎研究及實際裝置整合帶來了挑戰。 本計畫旨在系統性地建立 MX 材料的多晶型結構與其電子及鐵電性質之間清晰且全面的關聯。我們將研究相穩定性和相變機制，以及調控相形成的方法，並著重在厚度（層數）、溫度和壓力對相變動力學的影響。我們將利用鑽石對頂砧（DAC）實驗、原位掃描透射電子顯微鏡（STEM）以及密度泛函理論（DFT）模擬等先進技術手段進行相關研究。 我們將區分層間與層內晶格動力學在決定 MX 多晶型物相穩定性的作用，並針對不同厚度區間提出對應的相工程策略。此外，我們致力於實現高品質二維 MX 材料的規模化製備，從而支援實際裝置的製造。 為驗證結構與性能之間的關係，我們將利用 InSe、GaSe 和 GaTe 等代表性材料，透過實驗測定不同 MX 相的關鍵物理參數，包括載子遷移率和鐵電極化強度。在裝置應用方面，我們將開發並優化兩類基於 MX 材料的裝置：(1) 彈道輸運場效電晶體（FET），目標效能指標為：載子遷移率 > 260 cm²/V·s，亞閾值擺幅（SS）< 75 mV/dec，工作電壓 < 0.5 V； 10⁶，編程/擦除比 > 10³。 本計畫將為利用多態MX材料實現新一代電子與記憶體提供基礎性理解及實用指導。

11302826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11302826.value: 偏振复用的可变焦超构柱透镜用于实现线扫描双光片照明

11302826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302826.value: Live biological imaging demands optical systems that combine high resolution, large field of view, and minimal phototoxicity—qualities that make light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) indispensable for modern bioscience. However, conventional LSFM faces critical limitations: bulky optical components that resist miniaturization, inability to simultaneously capture multi-dimensional information, and the fundamental trade-off between light sheet thickness and illumination area. We propose a transformative solution through a polarization-multiplexing varifocal cylindrical metalens that transcends these constraints. Our innovative device employs two cascaded metasurfaces to generate orthogonal light sheets with independently tunable focal properties—a capability impossible with conventional optics. The metalens exploits a novel design principle combining geometric and propagation phase modulation through carefully engineered anisotropic meta-atoms. Right-handed circularly polarized (RCP) light focuses into a line parallel to the x-axis, while left-handed circularly polarized (LCP) light creates an orthogonal line parallel to the y-axis. Crucially, varifocal functionality emerges from controlled lateral displacement between metasurfaces, enabling continuous and independent tuning of each focal line's position along the optical axis. Our design methodology integrates rigorous phase profile calculations with systematic meta-atom selection using silicon nitride on silica substrates. Numerical validation through Rayleigh-Sommerfeld diffraction algorithms confirms unprecedented control over focal line position, width, and depth of focus—parameters critical for optimized biological imaging. The fabrication strategy leverages state-of-the-art semiconductor manufacturing, including electron-beam lithography and precision etching processes, ensuring nanometric accuracy and structural integrity. Comprehensive optical characterization using custom focusing profile measurement systems will validate theoretical predictions and optimize performance parameters. The culminating innovation integrates this metalens into a line-scanning LSFM system. By mounting metasurfaces on precision two-axis linear stages, we achieve simultaneous illumination of distinct specimen regions without conventional mechanical scanning limitations. This paradigm enables real-time tracking of dynamic biological processes across multiple spatial dimensions, dramatically increasing acquisition speed while reducing data storage requirements by orders of magnitude. This project establishes a new frontier in meta-optical devices, demonstrating how advanced electromagnetic control can revolutionize biological imaging. The successful implementation will provide a compact, versatile platform for next-generation fluorescence microscopy, opening unprecedented opportunities for understanding complex biological dynamics in real-time. Beyond immediate applications, this work establishes design principles for future multi-functional meta-devices across diverse optical applications. 活体生物成像需要兼具高分辨率、大视场和低光毒性的光学系统，这些成像特性使得光片荧光显微镜（LSFM）成为现代生物科学不可或缺的工具。然而，传统的光片荧光显微镜面临着诸多关键限制：光学元件难以小型化、无法同时捕获多维信息，以及光片厚度和照明面积之间存在根本性的权衡。我们提出了一种变革性的解决方案：一种偏振复用的可变焦超构柱透镜。 我们设计的超构柱透镜采用两片级联的超构表面来产生在不同偏振通道上具有独立可变焦特性的正交光片——这是传统光学柱面镜无法实现的。该超构柱透镜利用了一种新颖的设计原理，通过精心设计的各向异性超原子，实现了几何相位和传播相位的调制。右旋圆偏振光（RCP）被聚焦成一条平行于x轴的焦线，而左旋圆偏振光（LCP）则被聚焦成一条平行于y轴的焦线。至关重要的是，可变焦功能源于两片超构表面之间可控的相对横向位移，从而能够沿光轴方向连续且独立地调节两条焦线的位置。 我们的设计方法将严谨的相位分布计算与二氧化硅衬底上的氮化硅超构原子选择相结合。我们使用瑞利-索末菲衍射算法证实了设计的超构柱透镜对焦线位置、宽度和焦深的调控作用，这些焦线性能对于优化生物成像至关重要。我们采用电子束刻蚀等先进的半导体制造技术，确保了纳米级的精度和结构完整性。我们使用定制的聚焦光斑测量系统进行全面的光学性能表征，用来验证理论并优化性能参数。 我们将最终设计的超构柱透镜集成到线扫描光片荧光显微成像系统中。我们将两片超构表面分别安装在两台精密双轴线性平台上，通过调节两片超构表面之间的相对横向位移，实现了对不同维度样本区域的同时照明，突破了传统扫描成像的维度限制。这种方法能够实时追踪跨多个空间维度的动态生物过程，显著提高采集速度，同时将数据存储需求降低多个数量级。 该项目在超构光学器件领域开辟了新的前沿，展示了先进的光束调控如何革新生物成像。该项目成功落地后，将为下一代光片荧光显微镜提供一个紧凑、多功能、多维度的平台，为实时理解复杂的生物动力学开辟前所未有的机遇。除此之外，这项工作建立了一套适用于各种光学应用的多功能超构器件的通用设计原则。

11303126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11303126.value: 脫體激波解之數學研究

11303126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303126.value: This project aims to develop rigorous mathematical theory on a transonic detached shock onto a blunt body for multi-dimensional steady compressible Euler flow or potential flow. The study of the problem of an oblique shock onto a wedge has a long history and is of great interest in both mathematics and aerodynamics (see Anderson [1], Ben-Dor [4], and Courant-Friedrichs [24]). For the problem of the attached shock onto a wedge, there are lots of mathematical results, see [5–9, 12–16, 18, 19, 21–23, 25, 28–34, 36–38, 41–46] for recent progress. However, few results are available for the mathematical analysis of the detached shock, see [2, 3, 17]. Due to the importance of the detached shock problem in the nonlinear analysis and aerodynamics, it deserves more attention on this open problem. This is the theme of this project. Mathematically, this problem is a free boundary value problem in an unbounded domain with corners. The crucial difficulty is that the background solution cannot be a non-zero constant solution due to the boundary conditions on the wedge boundary and the symmetry line. So in [3], the Mach number of the incoming flow is assumed to be large enough so that the strong shock solutions of the potential flow in the subsonic region are almost stagnated. However, it is not true in general for the full Euler flow or for weak shock solutions of the potential flow. Therefore, no results are available for these two cases. We believe the methods and techniques developed in this project can be helpful for the theory of the multi-dimensional conservation laws and nonlinear partial differential equations. We have been working on the related problems for several years. We proved the convexity of self-similar transonic shock for potential flow in [11], validated the hypersonic similarity for potential flow in [13, 31] and for full Euer flow in [12], and established the global stability of three-dimensional attached weak transonic shock for potential flow in [7]; global stability of strong shock with a subsonic jet in [36]; and the global existence and convexity of detached strong shock solution past a blunt body for the potential flow in [3] and for full Euler flow under some conditions in [2]. In this project, we will mainly focus on further developing the techniques used in the works above to study the mentioned objectives. 本項目旨在為多維穩態可壓縮歐拉流或位勢流中鈍體前的跨聲速脫體激波建立嚴謹的數學理論。 關於楔形體上斜激波問題的研究歷史悠久，且在數學與空氣動力學領域均備受關注（見 Anderson [1]、Ben-Dor [4] 及 Courant-Friedrichs [24]）。對於楔形體上的附體激波問題，已有大量數學成果，近期進展可參見文獻 [5–9, 12–16, 18, 19, 21–23, 25, 28–34, 36–38, 41–46]。然而，關於脫體激波的數學分析結果則很少，目前僅見 [2, 3, 17]。鑑於脫體激波問題在非線性分析與空氣動力學中的重要性，此一開放問題值得更多關注，這正是本項目的主題。 從數學上看，該問題是一個定義於帶有角點的無界區域上的自由邊界問題。其關鍵困難在於，由於楔形邊界和對稱線上的邊界條件，背景解不能是非零常數解。因此，在文獻 [3] 中，假設來流馬赫數足夠大，使得位勢流在亞聲速區域中的強激波解幾乎處於停滯狀態。然而，對於完整的歐拉流或位勢流的弱激波解，此一假設通常不成立。因此，這兩種情形目前尚無相關結果。我們相信，本項目中所發展的方法與技術將有助於推動多維守恆律和非線性偏微分方程理論的發展。 我們已在相關問題上研究了數年。我們在文獻 [11] 中證明了位勢流自相似跨聲速激波的凸性；在文獻 [13, 31] 中驗證了位勢流的超聲速相似律，並在文獻 [12] 中將其推廣至完整歐拉流；在文獻 [7] 中建立了位勢流三維附體弱跨聲速激波的全局穩定性；在文獻 [36] 中建立了帶亞聲速射流的強激波的全局穩定性；並在文獻 [3] 中建立了鈍體前方位勢流脫體強激波解的全局存在性與凸性，以及在文獻 [2] 中於若干條件下建立了完整歐拉流的相應結果。在本項目中，我們將主要致力於進一步發展上述工作中所使用的技術，以研究所述目標問題。

11303626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11303626.value: 基於分子界面工程實現全印刷碳電極n-i-p型鈣鈦礦太陽能電池

11303626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303626.value: Printable n–i–p metal halide perovskite solar cells (PSCs) with carbon electrodes represent a compelling route toward cost-effective, scalable, and stable photovoltaic technologies. Unlike typical p-i-n architectures that depend on costly vacuum-deposited transport layers and electrodes, printable n-i-p PSCs can be fabricated entirely from solution under low-temperature (<120 °C) conditions, compatible with high-throughput roll-to-roll slot-die coating and screen-printing processes. However, despite their advantages in manufacturability and durability, their efficiencies remain below those of state-of-the-art vacuum-processed perovskite devices, which have surpassed 27%, while printable carbon electrode-based PSCs typically achieve only around 22%. This proposal aims to close this gap through molecularly engineered interfaces and fully co-designed materials systems that enable both high device performance and scalable process compatibility. The proposed research establishes a molecularly engineered framework that couples precise interface chemistry with fully printable device architectures. Molecular electron transport layers (ETLs) based on n-type self-assembled monolayers (n-SAMs) will replace conventional metal oxide ETLs, enabling controlled energy-level alignment, efficient carrier extraction, and durable defect passivation. Optically thick (>1 μm) α-FAPbI₃ absorbers will be fabricated using a templated, additive-assisted two-step crystallization method to achieve large grain sizes, low trap densities, and enhanced structural and thermal stability. For the hole extraction interface, a complementary interface integration strategy will be employed, in which an ultrathin conjugated passivation layer first suppresses interfacial traps, tunes surface energetics, and induces a controlled quasi-2D reconstruction that promotes efficient charge transfer. Building on this modified surface, a polymeric hole transport layer which is structurally complementary to the passivation layer, such as P3HT or PTAA, will be deposited to extend interfacial coupling, enhance hole extraction, and reinforce long-term interfacial stability without the need for further surface treatments. Finally, printable carbon electrodes processed at temperatures below 120 °C, formulated from graphite, graphene, and MXene hybrid fillers, will deliver high conductivity (<5 Ω/sq), strong adhesion, and robust thermal durability. The proposed work targets fully solution-processed PSCs that achieve certified efficiencies exceeding 25%, a substantial advance beyond the current 22% benchmark, and T90 operational stability of over 2,000 hours at 65-85 °C. The resulting device architecture will deepen the fundamental understanding of how molecularly engineered interfaces govern charge extraction, defect suppression, and long-term stability in perovskite photovoltaics. 本項目旨在透過系統性的分子界面工程與材料協同設計，實現可印刷碳基鈣鈦礦太陽能電池效率的突破性提升，以推動其低成本、規模化製備與高穩定性應用的發展。研究聚焦於n-i-p型適合全溶液法加工的元件結構，核心創新方向主要包括以下方面。首先，在電子傳輸層方面，將採用n型自組裝單分子層來構築高效的電子提取界面；其次，於吸光層製程上，發展模板輔助結晶技術以製備高品質的α-FAPbI₃鈣鈦礦薄膜；再者，針對空穴傳輸界面，提出「互補型界面修飾」策略，透過先沉積超薄共軛鈍化層，再耦合高分子空穴傳輸材料，協同提升電荷收集效率與界面穩定性；最後，在電極材料層面，將開發基於雜化填料的低溫可印刷碳電極配方。透過上述多層次界面與材料的整合設計，本研究預期實現兩大關鍵指標：將可印刷碳基鈣鈦礦太陽能電池之認證光電轉換效率提升至25%以上，並在65–85°C光熱加速老化條件下，達成T90壽命超過2000小時的穩定性表現。本計畫不僅在應用層面致力於高性能、高穩定性全印刷鈣鈦礦光伏技術的產業化推進，亦將從機理層面深入探究界面載流子動力學行為、缺陷調控機制與器件退化路徑，為下一代高效穩定鈣鈦礦光伏技術的發展提供理論依據與技術儲備。

11304126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11304126.value: 不可压缩磁流体动力学方程的无条件能量稳定可混合间断 Galerkin 方法

11304126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304126.value: The incompressible magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) equations, which describe the interaction between magnetic fields and electrically conducting fluids, are fundamental for modeling a wide range of physical phenomena. The governing system couples the Navier-Stokes equations of fluid dynamics with Maxwell's equations of electromagnetism, resulting in a highly nonlinear and multiphysical problem that presents significant challenges for the design and analysis of numerical schemes. Developing innovative numerical algorithms with rigorous mathematical analysis is therefore critical for advancing computational capabilities and enabling a deeper understanding of the underlying physics. This project aims to establish a new computational paradigm for the MHD system, underpinned by comprehensive mathematical analysis. Our project will focus on three main areas of research: (1) the design and optimal error analysis of a semi-implicit, structure-preserving monolithic scheme; (2) the development of an unconditionally energy-stable decoupled scheme; and (3) the design and analysis of a robust block preconditioner tailored to the decoupled system. We will first develop a monolithic scheme employing a semi-implicit, structure-preserving approach. The Navier-Stokes subsystem will be discretized using pressure-robust H(div)-conforming discontinuous Galerkin methods to ensure a divergence-free velocity field. To preserve the solenoidality of the magnetic field, we will utilize H(div)-conforming elements for the magnetic field and H(curl)-conforming elements for the electric field. We will construct first and second-order semi-implicit time-stepping schemes, supported by a rigorous analytical framework to establish parameter-robust error estimates. Subsequently, we will design novel decoupled schemes that achieve unconditional energy stability for both first and second-order time discretizations. The key innovation lies in designing subtle decoupling strategies that circumvent strong coupling without compromising stability and accuracy. Finally, we will construct efficient and parameter-robust block preconditioners for the resulting decoupled formulations. The accuracy, efficiency, and robustness of the proposed schemes will be validated through rigorous mathematical analysis and comprehensive numerical simulations on benchmark problems. We anticipate that this project will establish a new mathematical and computational framework for MHD problems. The methodologies developed are expected to have significant implications for a wide range of scientific and engineering applications beyond magnetohydrodynamics. 不可压缩磁流体动力学（MHD）方程描述了磁场与导电流体之间的相互作用，是模拟众多物理现象的重要数学模型。其控制方程组将流体动力学中的 Navier–Stokes 方程与电磁学中的 Maxwell 方程相耦合，形成了一个高度非线性、多物理场耦合的问题，给数值格式的设计与理论分析带来了重大挑战。因此，发展具有创新性的数值算法，并建立严格的数学分析理论，对于提升计算能力以及深入理解其内在物理机制具有重要意义。本项目旨在建立一个以系统数学分析为基础的磁流体动力学（MHD）新型计算框架。研究将围绕以下三个主要方向展开：(1)设计并进行最优误差分析的半隐式、结构保持整体耦合格式；(2) 发展无条件能量稳定的解耦数值格式；(3) 设计并分析适用于解耦系统的高效鲁棒块预条件器。 首先，我们将构造一种采用半隐式结构保持方法的整体耦合数值格式。对于 Navier–Stokes 子系统，将采用压力鲁棒的 H(div)-保形间断 Galerkin 方法进行离散，以保证速度场满足无散约束。为了保持磁场的无源（无散）性质，将分别采用 H(div)-保形有限元离散磁场，并采用 H(curl)-保形有限元离散电场。我们将构造一阶和二阶精度的半隐式时间推进格式，并建立严格的理论分析框架，以证明所提出方法具有关于模型参数的鲁棒误差估计。随后，我们将设计新型解耦算法，使其在一阶和二阶时间离散下均能够实现无条件能量稳定性。该部分的核心创新在于设计精细的解耦策略，在避免强耦合求解困难的同时，不牺牲数值格式的稳定性与计算精度。 最后，我们将针对所得到的解耦离散系统，构造高效且具有参数鲁棒性的块预条件器，以提升大规模计算中的求解效率。所提出数值方法的精度、计算效率以及鲁棒性将通过严格的数学理论分析和针对基准问题的系统数值实验进行验证。我们预计，本项目将为磁流体动力学问题建立一个新的数学与计算框架。所发展的理论方法和计算技术不仅适用于 MHD 问题，还将对更广泛的科学计算和工程应用领域产生重要影响。

11304726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11304726.value: 進階圖卷積神經網路之逼近理論框架

11304726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304726.value: Graphs--mathematical structures that represent entities (nodes) and their connections (edges)--are everywhere in real life, from social networks and transportation systems to molecular structures and protein interactions. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), especially Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs), are powerful tools for processing this graph-structured data. However, GCNs have a critical flaw: as they become deeper (add more layers), their ability to distinguish between different nodes weakens--a phenomenon called ``over-smoothing''. Deep GCNs blend node information too much, turning unique node representations into nearly identical ones, which hurts performance on tasks like node classification and link prediction. Most existing research on fixing over-smoothing focuses on testing new GCN designs (e.g., adding skip connections to retain information) without clear mathematical explanations for why these designs work. Additionally, current GNNs use ``one-size-fits-all'' filters to process graph data: some filters rely only on graph structure, while others use simple learned parameters, but none truly adapt to individual node features. While advanced architectures like ResGCN, APPNP, and GCNII show empirical success, a rigorous theoretical understanding of when and why they work remains lacking. Critically, existing approximation theory only covers fixed filters, leaving learned topology-based and adaptive filters theoretically unexplored. This research proposes a unified mathematical framework to understand and optimize advanced GCNs, drawing on concepts from ``approximation theory''--a branch of mathematics studying how simple functions represent complex patterns. Our work centers on three interrelated objectives: 1. Equivalence between Moduli of Smoothness and K-Functionals for General Graph Filters: Extend the bidirectional equivalence from classical approximation theory to multi-channel graph signals and general Laplacian-based filters. These extended tools will serve as a core basis for analyzing approximation errors in deep GCN models, clarifying how smoothness constraints influence model performance. 2. Approximation Analysis for Advanced GCN Architectures: Derive architecture-specific approximation bounds for advanced architectures (ResGCN, APPNP, GCNII) to formalize why skip connections mitigate over-smoothing. We will derive upper bounds for approximation errors to quantify the performance gains of these designs, providing provable guarantees for their effectiveness. 3. Investigation on Node Communication Dynamics: Develop a comprehensive theory of feature-dependent Communication Kernels to quantify information flow among nodes. Establish design principles that link spectral localization with feature–topology alignment, and derive feature-aware approximation error bounds to guide adaptive filter design with provable high-frequency preservation. By combining mathematical theory with practical GCN design, this research will theoretically explain why existing GCNs work (or fail) and provide insights for building more powerful, reliable GCNs. 圖是刻畫實體（節點）及其連接關係（邊）的數學結構，圖數據廣泛存在於真實世界，涵蓋社群網路、交通系統、分子結構與蛋白質交互作用等場景。圖神經網路（Graph Neural Networks, GNNs），尤以圖卷積網路（Graph Convolutional Networks, GCNs）為代表，是處理圖結構資料的核心工具。但 GCN 存在關鍵缺陷：網路層數加深時，節點區分能力會逐漸衰減，也就是眾所周知的「過度平滑（over‑smoothing）」現象。深度 GCN 會過度融合節點資訊，讓各節點獨特表徵幾乎趨同，直接降低節點分類、鏈結預測等下游任務的整體效能。 當前多數針對過度平滑的研究，聚焦於設計新型 GCN 架構，例如引入跳躍連接來緩解資訊丟失，卻缺少支撐這些機制的明確數學解釋。另一方面，現有 GNN 普遍使用「一體適用」的濾波器處理圖資料：部分濾波器僅依賴圖拓樸結構，另一些則引入簡單可學習參數，但均無法針對個別節點特徵做自適應調整。雖然 ResGCN、APPNP、GCNII 等架構已獲得不錯的實驗效果，仍缺少嚴謹理論刻畫其生效條件與內在機制。更重要的是，現有逼近理論僅針對固定濾波器展開研究，基於拓樸的可學習濾波器與自適應濾波器尚未得到充分的理論分析。 本研究以逼近理論（研究利用簡單函數近似複雜模式的數學分支）為基礎，建構一套統一數學框架，用以解析並最佳化進階圖卷積網路。延續團隊先前關於固定濾波器 GCN 的工作，本文引入通訊核（Communication Kernels）量化節點間的資訊流，並把理論分析拓展至基於拓樸的可學習濾波器以及自適應濾波器。研究包含三項互為關聯的核心目標： 第一，建立統一數學工具。將經典逼近理論的兩個基礎概念 —— 光滑模（度量節點資訊的變異程度）與 K‑泛函（權衡逼近精度與光滑性）拓展至多通道圖訊號。藉由此套工具，我們可以嚴格度量節點特徵的變異性，完成各類 GNN 濾波器的逼近誤差分析。 第二，從理論層面驗證跳躍連接架構。對 ResGCN、APPNP、GCNII 等模型開展嚴謹理論分析，形式化推導跳躍連接抑制過度平滑的內在機制。透過推導逼近誤差界，說明此類架構在何種條件下可以保留具備區辨能力的高頻資訊，給出可證明的效能保證。 第三，發展自適應通訊核理論。設計同時融合圖拓樸與節點專屬特徵的自適應通訊核，引導節點之間的資訊交互。我們將證明該核函數能夠依據節點特徵相似度動態調整通訊強度，進而減弱過度平滑效應，並由此導出構建高性能 GNN 的可操作設計準則。 本研究結合數學理論與實務模型設計，解釋現有架構成功或失效的底層原因，為研發具可證明效能保證的下一代圖神經網路，提供理論驅動的設計指引。

11305126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11305126.value: 基於機器學習的界面水熱力學反常與液-液相變分子動力學模擬

11305126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305126.value: Water is indispensable to human activity and a fundamental subject of study across science and engineering. Despite its ubiquitous presence and simple molecular structure, liquid water remains enigmatic due to its anomalous behaviors. To explain the thermodynamic anomalies of bulk water, Poole et al. proposed the liquid–liquid phase transition (LLPT) hypothesis and the existence of a “second critical point” in deeply supercooled water. Since then, numerical simulations and experimental studies have provided direct and indirect evidence supporting the LLPT in supercooled water. In reality, water exists not only in bulk form but also in interfacial states (i.e., interfacial water). Although experimental (e.g., femtosecond X-ray laser spectroscopy) and computer simulation studies have reported thermodynamic anomalies and sought evidence of the LLPT in water microdroplets and nanoconfined water (where gas-liquid and solid-liquid interfaces play an important role), the results remain a subject of debate. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulation represents a powerful computational tool for gaining insights into water properties at the molecular level. For example, classical force-field-based MD simulations have been used to obtain pressure–temperature phase diagrams of water and explore LLPT behavior. However, because these classical force fields are predominantly based on bulk water properties, their accuracy for interfacial water is limited and can be model-dependent. Machine-learning force fields (MLFFs) with first-principles-level accuracy have been developed for highly confined water, but their computational speed still lags behind that of classical MD. To address these limitations, the proposed research will be aimed at developing a more efficient MLFF that maintains first-principles-level accuracy while achieving the computational speed necessary for long-duration MD simulations of interfacial water. Our focus will be on two representative systems: nanodroplets and nanoconfined water. We will investigate the potential existence of thermodynamic anomalies in interfacial water and examine how nanodroplet size and the thickness of nanoconfined water influence the LLPT. Additionally, we will explore the applicability of the “two-state water” model to interfacial water by developing a deep-learning framework capable of identifying implicit reaction states between two distinct local microstructures in water. The resulting molecular-level insights will not only advance our understanding, at the molecular level, of interfacial water and offer clarity on the ongoing debates regarding its thermodynamic anomalies but also benefit application interfacial water in various areas, e.g., water transport in biochannels, atmospheric chemistry and cell preservation.

11305526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11305526.value: 調控氧化物光電極上光電化學醇類氧化－產氫反應之電荷傳輸與選擇性

11305526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305526.value: Decarbonization of our society necessitates a transition to a future fossil-free energy infrastructure, with green hydrogen identified as an essential transformation vector. Hydrogen can be directly produced using solar energy through photoelectrochemical (PEC) water-splitting, but technoeconomic analyses show that PEC-generated hydrogen is not cost-competitive. One possible solution is the simultaneous production of valuable chemicals within the same PEC device. PEC oxidation of alcohols (such as glycerol or ethylene glycol) has emerged as a value-adding reaction to replace the less economically viable oxygen evolution. Coupling this alcohol oxidation with water reduction at the cathode generate commercially attractive products such as dihydroxyacetone or glycolic acid alongside hydrogen. However, PEC alcohol oxidations suffer selectivity challenges as the reactions can typically go through various pathways, resulting in multiple products and lowering process efficiency. Controlling the selectivity is key, as a 100% selective reaction can optimize profitability, maximize feasibility, and minimize the need for product separation. This project aims to address these selectivity challenges by developing advanced PEC systems based on oxide-based photoelectrodes. Through the principles of engineered nanoconfinement and molecular surface functionalization to regulate charge transfer kinetics and adsorption/desorption dynamics, the project will steer PEC alcohol oxidation toward desired products with high selectivity. Systematic photoelectrochemical experiments that generate >400 datasets will be used to establish quantitative relationships between surface structure, operating conditions and product distribution. Data-driven modeling, supported by machine learning analysis, will be employed to reveal non-linear correlations among experimental parameters and predict optimized conditions for specific products. In parallel, state-of-the-art in situ time-resolved spectroscopic techniques will offer insights into charge transfer dynamics and adsorption/desorption processes on the photoelectrodes, providing mechanistic validation of data-driven predictions. Overall, the combination of rationally designed interfaces, ML-driven approaches and advanced experimental techniques will provide a new level of understanding in controlling reaction selectivity, which can be implemented for PEC processes beyond alcohol oxidation. This project is poised to accelerate the realization of efficient, selective and durable PEC technologies. Leveraging Hong Kong’s strategic solar-geographical potential and commitment to carbon neutrality, this work positions PEC solar fuel and chemical production as a tangible pathway toward energy resilience and sustainable industrial transformation. 我們社會的脫碳進程，迫切需要轉型至未來無化石能源基礎設施，而綠氫已被視為一項關鍵的轉型載體。氫氣可直接透過太陽能驅動的光電化學（PEC）水分解反應來生成，然而技術經濟分析顯示，PEC產氫在成本上尚不具競爭力。一項可能的解決方案是在同一PEC元件中同時生產具附加價值的化學品。以醇類（如甘油或乙二醇）進行PEC氧化，已成為一項可替代經濟效益較低之析氧反應的加值途徑。將此醇類氧化反應與陰極的水還原反應耦合，可於產氫之際，同時生成具商業吸引力的產品，例如二羥基丙酮或乙醇酸。然而，PEC醇類氧化反應面臨選擇性方面的挑戰，因為此類反應通常可經由多種路徑進行，導致產物複雜，並降低整體製程效率。反應選擇性的控制至關重要，因為達到100%選擇性的反應能極大化獲利能力、提升可行性，並減少產物分離的需求。 本計畫旨在透過開發以氧化物光電極為基礎之先進PEC系統，因應上述選擇性挑戰。借助工程化奈米侷限效應與分子表面官能化等原理，調控電荷轉移動力學及吸附／脫附動態行為，本計畫將引導PEC醇類氧化反應朝特定目標產物進行，並達成高選擇性。系統性光電化學實驗將產生逾400組數據集，用以建立表面結構、操作條件與產物分佈之間的量化關聯性。同時，將運用機器學習分析輔助之數據驅動建模，揭示實驗參數間的非線性相關性，並針對特定產物預測最佳化條件。另一方面，本計畫亦將採用當前尖端之原位時間解析光譜技術，深入探討光電極上的電荷傳移動態與吸附／脫附過程，為數據驅動之預測提供機制驗證。總體而言，透過理性設計之介面、機器學習驅動方法及先進實驗技術的結合，本研究將在反應選擇性控制方面開創全新層次的理解，其成果亦可推廣應用於醇類氧化以外之PEC製程。 本計畫預計能加速實現高效、具選擇性且耐久之PEC技術。結合香港在地理位置上具備之太陽能戰略潛力，以及對碳中和目標之承諾，本研究將確立PEC太陽能燃料與化學品生產，作為邁向能源韌性及永續工業轉型之一條切實可行的路徑。

11305726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11305726.value: 標準平均場博弈的混沌傳播

11305726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305726.value: Many complex systems in nature and society, from the motion of particles in a fluid to the interactions of traders in a market, can be modeled as a large number of interacting individuals. Analyzing such systems directly is often impossible due to their sheer scale. A powerful mathematical idea, known as propagation of chaos, states that the behavior of these complex systems can simplify dramatically as the number of components grows. The interactions between any finite number of specific individuals become negligible, and the system’s overall behavior converges to a predictable average limit, described by a single representative individual influenced by the collective mass. This project focuses on a critically important version of this problem within the framework of Mean Field Games (MFGs), which studies strategic decision-making in massive populations. Here, each individual is a rational agent making choices to optimize their own goal, while being influenced by the decisions of everyone else. The propagation of chaos question becomes: if we have a large but finite game with N players, does its outcome converge to the predicted outcome of the idealized MFG model where a single player interacts with the crowd? And if so, how quickly does this convergence happen? Establishing a fast convergence rate is essential for trusting the MFG model’s predictions in real-world applications with finite, albeit large, populations. While it is known that this convergence occurs qualitatively, a general theory for quantitative convergence—providing explicit speed estimates—remains a major challenge. Current results are confined to models with special "monotonicity" properties, which act as a stabilizer. Outside these special cases, we lack tools to provide concrete convergence rates. This project aims to build a general theory for quantitative propagation of chaos by pursuing two key objectives. First, we will discover more general mathematical conditions that guarantee the stability of the MFG system, which is the cornerstone for deriving explicit convergence rates. Second, we will develop "selection principles" for situations where multiple potential outcomes exist. By systematically choosing specific outcomes, we can restore stability and obtain quantitative results even in these complex scenarios. Successfully creating this unified mathematical framework will significantly enhance the predictive power of MFGs. It will provide rigorous, quantitative guarantees for using these models in practical fields such as economics, finance, and engineering, where reliable predictions of large-scale population behavior are crucial for designing robust systems and effective policies. 自然界與社會中的許多複雜系統，從流體中粒子的運動到市場中交易者的互動，都可以被建模為大量相互作用的個體。由於規模龐大，直接分析這類系統通常是不可能的。一個被稱為「混沌傳播」的強大數學概念指出，隨著組成部分數量的增加，這些複雜系統的行為會急劇簡化。任何有限數量特定個體之間的相互作用變得可以忽略不計，而系統的整體行為會收斂到一個可預測的平均極限，此極限由一個受整體群體影響的單一代表性個體來描述。 本計畫聚焦於平均場博弈（Mean Field Games, MFGs）框架中此問題的一個至關重要的版本，平均場博弈研究大規模人群中的策略決策。在這裡，每個個體都是一個理性代理人，做出選擇以最佳化自身目標，同時又受到其他所有人決策的影響。混沌傳播的問題便成為：如果我們有一個包含 N 個玩家的大型但有限的賽局，其結果是否會收斂到理想化 MFG 模型所預測的結果，即單一玩家與人群互動的結果？若會收斂，此收斂發生的速度有多快？對於在有限（儘管數量龐大）人口的實際應用中信任 MFG 模型的預測而言，建立快速的收斂速率至關重要。 雖然已知此收斂在定性上會發生，但提供明確速度估計的定量收斂一般理論仍然是一項重大挑戰。目前的結果僅限於具有特殊「單調性」屬性的模型，這些屬性扮演穩定劑的角色。在這些特殊情況之外，我們缺乏提供具體收斂速率的工具。本計畫旨在透過追求兩個關鍵目標，建立定量混沌傳播的一般理論。首先，我們將發現能保證 MFG 系統穩定性的更一般數學條件，這是推導顯式收斂速率的基石。其次，我們將針對存在多種潛在結果的情況，發展「選擇原則」。透過系統性地選擇特定結果，即使在這些複雜情境下，我們也能恢復穩定性並獲得定量結果。 成功建立此統一數學框架將顯著增強平均場博弈的預測能力。它將為在經濟學、金融和工程等實際領域中使用這些模型，提供嚴謹的定量保證；在這些領域中，對大規模人群行為的可靠預測，對於設計穩健系統和有效政策至關重要。

11307226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11307226.value: 有机分子修饰单原子电催化剂实现可持续非均相氯化

11307226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11307226.value: The conventional synthesis of organochlorides, vital building blocks in agrochemical and pharmaceutical industries, predominantly relies on thermochemical methods that operate with noble-metal organic ligands and generate stoichiometric hazardous waste, posing significant environmental and economic challenges. Electrocatalysis presents a sustainable alternative by using electricity as a clean and tunable reagent, enabling reactions under mild conditions with reduced ecological footprint. While single-atom catalysts (SACs) offer maximal atom efficiency and unique electronic properties, their practical application in anodic chlorination is severely limited by metal leaching and structural degradation under highly oxidizing potentials, which curtails their long-term usability and industrial relevance. This project aims to develop a novel strategy to stabilize SACs by engineering their coordination microenvironment through covalent modification with tailored organic molecules, forming a class of materials we term organocatalyst supported on single-atom supports (OSASs). We hypothesize that grafting functional organic ligands onto the SAC support will enhance metal anchoring via strong coordination bonds and modify the local electronic structure, thereby promoting charge transfer and reactant activation, leading to superior catalytic stability and activity. The key objectives of this project are: 1) To design and synthesize a library of nitrogen-based organic molecules with tailored electronic and steric properties for modifying carbon-supported non-noble metal based SACs; 2) To systematically characterize the physicochemical properties of the hybrid catalysts using advanced techniques such as X-ray absorption spectroscopy and scanning transmission electron microscopy to unravel the structure-modification relationship; 3) To evaluate the electrocatalytic performance towards chlorination of aromatic compounds and the production of key drug intermediates, with a focus on benchmarking stability against metal leaching and assessing Faraday efficiency and selectivity under continuous operation conditions; 4) To realize the kg-scale synthesis of the key drug molecules, demonstrating scalability and potential for industrial adoption. Till now, we have primarily demonstrated that the SACs and OSASs are efficient in the inorganic chlor-related reactions. The ultimate goal is to demonstrate a proof-of-concept for a new class of robust organic-inorganic hybrid electrocatalysts that combine the advantages of molecular precision and heterogeneous stability. The expected outcome is a stable catalytic system that maintains high performance over extended operation, providing a generalizable platform for applying SACs in other challenging electrocatalytic organic reactions. This research will provide fundamental insights into stabilizing metal sites through molecular-level engineering, advancing the frontier of sustainable electrochemical synthesis for fine chemicals and bridging the gap between academic innovation and industrial application. 有机氯化物是农用化学品和制药工业中至关重要的基础原料。其传统合成主要依赖于热化学方法，这些方法通常使用贵金属有机配体，并产生化学计量比的危险废弃物，从而带来了严峻的环境与经济挑战。电催化利用电能作为一种清洁且可调控的试剂，提供了一种可持续的替代方案，使反应能够在温和条件下进行，并显著降低生态足迹。尽管单原子催化剂（SACs）具备极致的原子利用率和独特的电子特性，但它们在阳极氯化反应中的实际应用却受到严重限制。在高氧化电位下，金属浸出和结构降解问题频发，极大地缩短了其长期使用寿命，也削弱了其工业应用价值。本项目旨在开发一种稳定单原子催化剂的新策略：通过使用定制的有机分子进行共价修饰来调控其配位微环境，从而构建一类被我们称为“单原子载体负载有机催化剂”（OSASs）的新型材料。我们假设，将功能性有机配体接枝到单原子催化剂载体上，将通过强配位键增强金属锚定作用，并改变局部电子结构，从而促进电荷转移与反应物活化，最终实现卓越的催化稳定性和活性。 本项目的主要研究目标包括： 1）设计并合成一个含氮有机分子库，这些分子具有特定的电子和空间位阻特性，用于修饰碳载非贵金属单原子催化剂； 2）利用X射线吸收光谱和扫描透射电子显微镜等先进表征技术，系统地研究杂化催化剂的物理化学性质，以揭示结构与修饰之间的构效关系； 3）评估其在芳香族化合物氯化及关键药物中间体生产中的电催化性能，重点是在连续运行条件下，评估其抗金属浸出的稳定性、法拉第效率以及选择性； 4）实现关键药物分子的公斤级合成，以展示该技术的可放大性及其工业应用潜力。 迄今为止，我们已初步证明SACs和OSASs在无机氯相关反应中具有高效的催化性能。本项目的最终目标是为一类新型、稳健的有机-无机杂化电催化剂提供概念验证，该催化剂结合了分子级精度与多相催化稳定性的双重优势。预期成果是开发出一种在长时间运行中仍能保持高性能的稳定催化系统，为将单原子催化剂应用于其他具有挑战性的电催化有机反应提供一个通用平台。这项研究将为通过分子级工程设计稳定金属活性位点提供基础性见解，推动精细化学品可持续电化学合成领域的前沿发展，并为学术创新与工业应用搭建桥梁。

11307926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11307926.value: 三維磁化矢量的原子尺度成像

11307926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11307926.value: Real-space imaging of three-dimensional (3D) magnetization vectors in materials at the atomic scale, which has not been proposed theoretically and achieved experimentally, is essential on a fundamental level in physics, materials science, and nanotechnology, as well as for applications in spintronics and memory devices. In this project, we propose a methodological breakthrough in the ability to directly visualize the 3D magnetization vectors atomic plane by atomic plane on an individual basis in the example of canted antiferromagnets (AFMs) regarding magnetic moment direction and relative strength. The lateral imaging resolution of 3D magnetization vectors proposed by our approach along a single project direction without sample tilting has been, for the first time, improved to the atomic level by more than one magnitude from 10 nm, which is the best spatial resolution of vector imaging of magnetism achieved by the currently available techniques such as holographic vector-field electron tomography and X-ray vector ptycho-tomography. By correlating this 3D spin information with simultaneously determined atomic positions, we provide the first direct experimental quantification of spin canting, spin reorientation, and the effective Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) between adjacent atomic planes in canted antiferromagnets under magnetic field. Considering the capability to determine 3D magnetization vectors with atomic-plane resolution and quantitative magnetic information such as element-specific orbital and spin magnetic moments, our comprehensive approaches can be applied to the various magnetic orderings in canted/collinear AFMs, ferromagnets, helical magnets, and especially altermagnets, which are recently identified as a new class of magnetic materials combining the advantages of ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic order and exhibiting time-reversal symmetry-breaking magneto-optical responses, vanishing stray fields and high-frequency spin dynamics. Our methodological development paves the way to direct imaging of 3D magnetization vectors on each spin sublattice at the atomic scale when controlling the Néel vectors and canted magnetic moments in altermagnets, which is crucial to the emerging fields such as spintronics, magnonics, ultrafast photonics, and phononics. 原子尺度的三維磁化矢量的實空間成像技術迄今尚未在理論上提出並在實驗上驗證。這一技術不僅對於物理學、材料科學和納米科技等基礎研究具有重要意義，也對自旋電子學和存儲器等應用領域至關重要。 本項目擬實現一項方法學上的突破：以傾斜反鐵磁體為典型體系，提出一種能夠逐層原子面地針對單個原子面上三維磁化矢量進行直接成像技術，從而獲得各原子面上自旋磁矩的方向及相對強度信息。我們所提出的方法僅需沿單一投影方向進行測量，且無需傾轉樣品，即可實現三維磁化矢量的原子面分辨成像。三維磁矢量成像空間分辨率首次由現有所能達到的約10 nm直接提升至原子尺度，實現了超過一個數量級的空間分辨率提高。現有可用于磁矢量成像的先進技術，例如全息矢量場電子斷層成像和X射線矢量疊層掃描斷層成像，其最佳空間分辨率仍約為10 nm。 通過將在同一樣品位置處所獲得的三維自旋信息與的原子位置進行關聯，我們將首次實現針對在外加磁場下傾斜反鐵磁體中自旋傾斜、自旋重取向以及相鄰原子面之間有效Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya 交互作用的實驗表徵。 鑒於我們的方法能夠實現原子面分辨測量三維磁化矢量，並可同時獲取元素選擇性的軌道磁矩和自旋磁矩等定量磁學信息，我們所建立的綜合表征方法可進一步推廣至多種不同類型的磁有序體系，包括傾斜/共線反鐵磁體、鐵磁體、螺旋磁體，尤其是近年來受到廣泛關注的交錯磁體。交錯磁體是一類新近確立的磁性材料，其兼具鐵磁有序和反鐵磁有序的優勢，並表現出時間反演對稱性破缺的磁光響應、近乎消失的雜散磁場以及高頻自旋動力學等獨特性質。 本項目的方法學發展將為各自旋子晶格中三維磁化矢量在原子尺度上地直接成像開闢新的途徑，並有望實現對交錯磁體中奈爾矢量和傾斜磁矩的定量表徵與調控。這對於自旋電子學、磁振子學、超快光子學以及聲子學等新興研究領域具有重要意義。

11308226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11308226.value: 評估生態工程在提升人工海岸生態功能與韌性方面的成效

11308226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11308226.value: Rapid coastal urbanization and reclamation have led to widespread ecological degradation as natural habitats are replaced by simplified artificial structures such as seawalls and breakwaters. To mitigate these impacts, eco-engineering has emerged as a promising approach to enhance biodiversity and restore ecological function on hardened shorelines. Hong Kong’s first large-scale eco-shoreline, constructed at Tung Chung East (TCE), provides a unique opportunity to investigate the ecological mechanisms underpinning biodiversity enhancement, functional complexity, and resilience on urban coastlines. Building on long-term monitoring that has demonstrated higher species richness and abundance on the TCE eco-shoreline compared to traditional seawalls, this project aims to quantify how these biodiversity gains translate into ecological functionality and resilience. The first objective is to evaluate the trophic structure, functional diversity, and redundancy of intertidal communities on the TCE eco-shoreline in comparison to adjacent traditional seawalls and natural rocky shores. We hypothesize that the TCE eco-shoreline exhibits higher ecological functionality than the traditional seawall. Using stable isotope analysis of carbon (δ¹³C) and nitrogen (δ¹⁵N), we will quantify isotopic niche width and overlap to determine the number of trophic levels, degree of niche partitioning, and extent of functional redundancy within communities. Broader δ¹³C–δ¹⁵N ranges and larger isotopic niche areas will indicate greater trophic diversity and ecological connectivity, suggesting that enhanced habitat complexity on eco-shorelines supports more functionally robust and resilient ecosystems. The second objective is to evaluate the resilience and recovery capacity of eco-shoreline communities in response to two types of disturbance. We will assess resilience to natural thermal stress by monitoring biodiversity and mortality before, during, and after summer thermal events, testing whether the eco-shoreline’s water-retaining features buffer against heat-induced biodiversity loss. We will also measure recovery from an experimental physical disturbance by tracking recolonization, species richness, and biomass over a twelve-month period on both eco-engineered and traditional seawalls. These experiments will provide direct empirical evidence on how habitat complexity influences the ability of intertidal communities to resist and recover from disturbance. Together, these studies will integrate community composition, trophic structure, and resilience data to provide the first comprehensive evaluation of the ecological functionality and stability of a large-scale eco-shoreline in subtropical Asia. The results will deliver critical insights for the future design of eco-engineered coastlines in Hong Kong and beyond, supporting the integration of ecological principles and nature-positive design into sustainable coastal urban development. 快速的沿海城市化與填海造地，導致生態系統大規模退化；原本的天然棲地被海堤與防波堤等簡化的人造結構所取代。為了減輕這些影響，生態工程已成為一種具潛力的方法，可在硬質（石屎化）海岸上增進生物多樣性並修復生態功能。香港首個大型生態海岸線於東涌東（TCE）建成，為研究都市海岸上支撐生物多樣性提升、功能複雜性與韌性的生態機制提供了獨特機會。基於長期監測結果顯示，相較於傳統海堤，TCE 生態海岸線具有更高的物種豐富度與族群數量，本研究計畫旨在量化這些生物多樣性增益如何轉化為生態功能與韌性。 本研究的第一項目標，是評估 TCE 生態海岸線的潮間帶群落其營養結構、功能多樣性與功能冗餘，並與鄰近的傳統海堤與天然岩岸進行比較。研究假設為：相較於傳統海堤，TCE 生態海岸線具有更高的生態功能性。研究將使用碳穩定同位素分析（δ¹³C）與氮穩定同位素分析（δ¹⁵N），量化同位素生態位寬度與重疊度，以判定群落中的營養階層數量、同位素生態位分化程度，以及功能冗餘的幅度。較寬的 δ¹³C–δ¹⁵N範圍與更大的同位素生態位面積，將代表更高的營養多樣性與生態連結性，顯示生態海岸線所帶來的棲地複雜性，能支持更具功能韌性與恢復能力的生態系統。 第二項目標，是評估生態海岸群落在兩種擾動情境下的韌性與恢復能力。我們將透過監測生物多樣性與死亡率，在夏季熱壓事件發生前、期間與之後進行追蹤，以評估對自然熱應力的韌性，並檢驗生態海岸的保水特徵是否能緩衝熱致生物多樣性流失。另方面，我們也將透過追蹤再定殖、物種豐富度與生物量，比較生態工程海岸線與傳統海堤，在為期十二個月的期間內衡量其對實驗性物理擾動的恢復情況。 這些實驗將提供直接的實證證據，說明棲地複雜性如何影響潮間帶群落抵抗擾動與從擾動中恢復的能力。綜合而言，本研究將整合群落組成、營養結構與韌性資料，對亞熱帶亞洲大型生態海岸的生態功能性與穩定性進行首次全面評估。研究結果將為未來香港及更廣泛地區的生態工程海岸線設計提供關鍵洞見，支持將生態原則與「以自然為本」的設計理念，納入永續的沿海都市發展。

11308526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11308526.value: 活化過渡金屬氧化物表面過氧物種以提升其酵素感測性能：以氧化鈰為例之探討

11308526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11308526.value: Natural enzymes are essential for catalyzing numerous biological reactions, particularly in metabolic processes. Among them, horseradish peroxidase (HRP) is widely employed with chromogenic substrates such as 3,3’,5,5’-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB), 2,2’-azino-bis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) (ABTS), and o-phenylenediamine (OPD) in various bio-analytical assays for quantitative purposes. For instance, when paired with glucose oxidase, which produces H2O2 in the presence of glucose, HRP utilizes the generated H2O2 to oxidize chromogenic substrates, rendering a measurable color change. Consequently, glucose concentration can be determined by assessing color intensity at specific wavelengths. Other biologically important molecules can also be detected similarly by coupling their specific oxidases with HRP. Despite its widespread use and high activity, HRP is prone to denaturation and costly to produce. These limitations have prompted the development of artificial enzymes, particularly inorganic nanomaterials, which offer advantages such as easier preparation, lower costs, and improved thermal/pH stability, attracting significant interest in recent years. Although these so-called peroxidase nanozymes have successfully replaced HRP in glucose detection and other enzymatic assays, most activate H2O2 through a radical pathway that generates OH radicals for TMB oxidation. The nonselective nature of these radicals makes them easily scavenged by not only H2O2 and the catalyst itself, but also various substances present in biological environments, hindering practical applications. To resolve this, researchers working with advanced oxidation processes are developing catalysts that can selectively convert H2O2 into singlet oxygen, which provides greater selectivity and a longer lifespan than OH radicals. Building on our recent discovery of bromide-mediated singlet oxygen production from Ce-peroxo species on octahedral CeO2, we expect this sample to outperform cube-shaped CeO2, which activates H2O2 solely through a radical pathway, in TMB oxidation and the related H2O2/glucose detection. Alternatively, since ABTS and OPD have lower redox potentials than TMB and can be directly oxidized by Ce-peroxo species, their use as chromogenic substrates enables octahedral CeO2 to mimic HRP’s catalytic behavior. This strategy is expected to further improve sensing performance by minimizing potential interferences from the bromide mediator used in the first approach. Both strategies will be applied to CeO2 and other metal oxides without surface control, where some active sites activate H2O2 via the radical pathway while others via the peroxo pathway, to enhance both substrate oxidation and H2O2 utilization. The ultimate goal is to identify an optimal HRP mimetic for practical applications in glucose detection and other coupled sensing assays in the future.

11308826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11308826.value: 多功能鈦和錫氧簇的分子工程以實現高效穩定的鈣鈦礦單結和疊層太陽能電池

11308826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11308826.value: Currently, the mainstream photovoltaics (PVs) are based on high temperature (>1000 °C) processed crystalline silicon, which require significant energy consumption. In contrast, thin film perovskite solar cells (PSCs) can be solution/vapor processed at relatively low temperatures (<150 °C) with diverse form factors and scalable processes to provide low-cost clean energy. The highest power conversion efficiency (PCE) of single-junction PSCs has already reached 27%, however, it still lags the Shockley-Queisser (S-Q) predicted upper-limit of 33%. Developing all-perovskite tandem solar cells is a potential way to exceed this limit by employing complementary bandgap perovskites. Nevertheless, the easy oxidation and faster crystallization of Sn-based narrow-bandgap (NBG) perovskites significantly prevent the derived devices from achieving desired efficiency and stability for further integration with wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskites for tandems. In a typical planar junction PSC, functional interlayers (ILs) are essential for enhancing device efficiency and stability via optimized charge transport/collection and suppressed ion migration. Current organic/inorganic ILs don’t have the properties needed to fulfil these requirements. Titanium-oxo and tin-oxo clusters (TOCs and SnOCs) are two classes of metal-oxo clusters (MOCs) that possess similar semiconducting properties like TiO2 and SnO2 and can be solution processed into high-quality films to serve as promising ILs. Their unique nano-sizes, well-defined structures, tunable optoelectronic and redox properties, and excellent photo- and thermal-stability have enabled their uses in diverse electroactive and optoelectronic applications. However, these MOCs need to be tailored to have proper structures, energy levels, redox potentials, and charge transport for functioning as efficient ILs for PSCs. In this proposal, we will develop functional MOCs and their hierarchical structures based on four interconnecting tasks: 1) develop cross-linkable and amphiphilic MOCs as interfacial modifiers; 2) develop tailored ammonium-containing MOCs for efficient defect passivation; 3) develop redox-active MOCs to suppress iodide and Sn+2 oxidation for enhancing the performance of different bandgaps PSCs; 4) demonstrate PCE greater than 29%, 22%, and 26% for single junction regular, WBG, and NBG PSC, respectively, and 32% for all-perovskite tandem PSCs, with excellent stability showing <5% decay under accelerated testing conditions at the maximum power point. The outcomes from this project will help PSCs achieve exceptional efficiencies and needed stability to facilitate their practical applications. It will also provide good opportunities for training graduate and undergraduate students as the next generation leaders in printable PVs and positioning Hong Kong as the frontier research hub for affordable and sustainable clean energy. 目前，主流光伏（PV）技術以晶體硅爲主，其製備通常需要高於1000 ℃的高溫，能耗顯著。相比之下，鈣鈦礦薄膜太陽能電池（PSCs）可在相對較低溫度（＜150 ℃）下通過溶液法或氣相法制備，製備方法多樣、工藝可規模化，能夠以低成本提供清潔能源。迄今，單結PSCs的最高光電轉換效率（PCE）已達到27%，但仍低於Shockley-Queisser（S-Q）理論預測的33%上限。利用帶隙互補的鈣鈦礦材料構建全鈣鈦礦疊層太陽能電池，是突破這一上限的潛在途徑。然而，錫基窄帶隙（NBG）鈣鈦礦易氧化且結晶速度過快，嚴重製約了相應器件獲得理想效率與穩定性，也阻礙了其與寬帶隙（WBG）鈣鈦礦集成製備疊層器件。 在典型的平面結構PSCs中，功能界面層（ILs）對提升器件效率和穩定性至關重要，其作用包括優化電荷傳輸/收集和抑制離子遷移。現有有機/無機界面層尚不具備滿足這些要求的特性。鈦氧簇（TOCs）和錫氧簇（SnOCs）是兩類金屬氧簇（MOCs），具有與TiO2和SnO2相似的半導體特性，可通過溶液法加工成高質量薄膜，是極具潛力的界面層材料。憑藉獨特的納米尺寸、明確的結構、可調的光電與氧化還原性質，以及優異的光穩定性和熱穩定性，這兩類金屬氧簇已在多種電活性與光電應用中發揮作用。不過，要使它們成爲PSCs的高效界面層，仍需對結構、能級、氧化還原電位和電荷傳輸性能進行針對性設計。本項目將圍繞四項相互關聯的任務，開發功能性金屬氧簇及其多級結構：（1）開發可交聯、兩親性的金屬氧簇作爲界面修飾層；（2）開發定製化的含銨金屬氧簇，實現高效缺陷鈍化；（3）開發具有氧化還原活性的金屬氧簇，抑制碘離子與Sn2+的氧化，從而提升不同帶隙PSCs的性能；（4）實現單結常規帶隙、寬帶隙和窄帶隙 PSCs的PCE分別超過29%、22%和26%，全鈣鈦礦疊層PSCs超過32%，並在最大功率點加速老化測試條件下展現優異穩定性，效率衰減低於5%。 本項目成果將幫助PSCs實現卓越的效率與所需的穩定性，從而推動其實際應用；同時爲研究生和本科生提供良好的培養機會，使其成長爲印刷光伏領域的新一代領軍人才，並助力香港成爲經濟適用、可持續清潔能源的前沿研究中心。 關鍵詞：鈣鈦礦太陽能電池；鈣鈦礦基疊層太陽能電池；鈦氧簇；錫氧簇；長期穩定性

11309126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11309126.value: 具有二阶边界条件的线性与非线性边值问题的Hessian 估计

11309126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11309126.value: This project investigates boundary regularity for elliptic PDEs with second-order Venttsel-type boundary conditions. The first part concerns the (σ_k, B_k)-Yamabe problem, a fully nonlinear generalization of the classical boundary Yamabe problem. Unlike the classical (semilinear, uniformly elliptic) case, the (σ_k, B_k) problem couples a fully nonlinear, non-uniformly elliptic interior equation with a nonlinear, second-order boundary operator; general solvability remains largely open. Building on our recent Liouville-type theorem, this proposal tackles the next major obstacle --- boundary C^2 estimates --- beginning with the model (σ_2, B_2) setting in the umbilic case. The main analytic difficulty is that the boundary operator includes second-order terms and is both tangentially non-uniformly elliptic and non-uniformly oblique. Motivated by this, the second part develops linear theory for Venttsel boundary value problems. While existing results are mostly "Dirichlet-like", relying on uniform tangential ellipticity, we investigate the complementary "oblique-like" regime, where quantitative obliqueness drives the estimates even when tangential ellipticity may degenerate. Our goal is to obtain sharp C^{2,α} and W^{2,p} estimates on rough domains, extending the "boundary relaxation" phenomenon established for pure oblique derivative problems in my earlier work. Together, these advances aim to provide a more complete picture of second-order boundary operators and the linear tools needed for subsequent nonlinear analysis in conformal geometry. 本项目拟研究具有二阶 Venttsel 型边界条件的椭圆型偏微分方程的边界正则性。第一部分聚焦于(\sigma_k,B_k)-Yamabe 问题，这是经典边界 Yamabe 问题的完全非线性推广。与经典的半线性、一致椭圆情形不同，该问题将全非线性、非一致椭圆的内部方程与非线性二阶边界算子耦合，其一般可解性在很大程度上仍悬而未决。基于我们近期建立的 Liouville 型定理，本项目将进一步研究其中的一个核心障碍——边界C^2先验估计，并首先处理平坦（或umbilic）边界下，k=2的情形。主要分析困难在于，边界算子含有二阶项，其切向椭圆性与斜向性均可能发生退化。 受上述问题启发，第二部分拟发展 Venttsel 边值问题的线性理论。现有结果大多属于“Dirichlet 型”框架，依赖切向一致椭圆性；本项目则研究与之互补的“斜导数型”机制，即在切向椭圆性可能退化的情况下，利用边界条件的一致obliqueness建立相应估计。一个目标是在非光滑区域建立二阶导数估计，将作者本人前期在纯斜导数问题的“boundary relaxation”现象推广到Venttsel边值问题。上述研究将深化对二阶边界算子的整体认识，并为共形几何中后续的非线性分析提供关键的线性理论工具。

11309226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11309226.value: 構建有機半導體電荷轉移特性與基於電吸收光譜提取之激子參數之間的關聯關係

11309226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11309226.value: The excitonic behavior of Coulomb-bound electron-hole pairs in organic molecules plays a pivotal role in determining the performance of organic electronic devices.
