Understanding the correlation between molecular structure and excitonic properties can facilitate more efficient material design to achieve better device performance. However, experimental techniques that can qualitatively assess these excitonic properties are currently limited, and previous studies are mainly based on theoretical calculations which have limitations on resolving systems with interactions of multiple molecules. More importantly, calculations are based on existing established theories or models, which might not be able to explore any new properties of materials. Experimentally, electroabsorption (EA) spectroscopy stands out as a promising method, allowing for the extraction of changes in dipole moment (Δμ) and polarizability (Δp) between the ground and excited states. These parameters are closely linked to the exciton recombination and dissociation processes. Despite its potential, a systematic application of EA across different materials is still lacking, leading to inconsistencies in how Δμ and Δp are interpreted in relation to excitonic properties. Moreover, conventional interpretations often rely on an overly simplified hydrogen-like model, where an electron orbits a stationary hole, overlooking the more complex delocalization of electron and hole scenarios in organic materials. This research proposal aims to address these challenges by investigating the discrepancies in the interpretation of excitonic properties based on EA-derived Δμ and Δp values. EA spectroscopy will be conducted on a series of materials that vary in molecular structure, molecular packing, and interactions with other materials. To ensure accurate correlations, the EA results will be cross-referenced with theoretical calculations and independent transient absorption spectroscopy data. The gained insight will be further applied to investigate the contribution from different molecular packing configurations on the charge transfer, and the charge transfer properties at organic donor/acceptor bulk heterojunctions. The success of this project will significantly enhance the qualitative understanding of excitonic properties in organic electronic materials, offering valuable insights that inform molecular design for improved charge transfer processes. Specifically, the findings will help address current limitations by enabling more accurate evaluations of charge transfer properties at organic interfaces. Furthermore, the development of a quantitative relationship between excitonic properties and molecular structure will support more efficient, AI-driven material development, reducing reliance on empirically driven, holistic approaches traditionally employed only by experienced chemists. 有機分子中受庫侖力束縛之電子–電洞對所形成的激子行為，在決定有機電子元件效能方面扮演關鍵角色。理解分子結構與激子特性之間的關聯，有助於更有效率地進行材料設計，以提升元件性能。然而，目前能夠定性評估這些激子特性的實驗技術仍然有限；既有研究多仰賴理論計算，但此類方法在解析多分子交互作用系統時存在侷限。更重要的是，相關計算通常建立於既有理論或模型之上，可能無法探索材料的全新性質。 在實驗方法方面，電吸收（Electroabsorption, EA）光譜被認為是一項具潛力的技術，可用於萃取基態與激發態之間的偶極矩變化（Δμ）與極化率變化（Δp）。這些參數與激子復合與解離過程密切相關。儘管EA技術具有潛在優勢，但目前仍缺乏針對不同材料進行系統性應用的研究，導致Δμ與Δp在激子特性詮釋上的不一致。此外，傳統詮釋方法往往依賴過度簡化的類氫原子模型，即假設電子繞著靜止電洞運行，忽略了有機材料中電子與電洞更為複雜的離域化行為。 本研究計畫旨在針對基於EA所得Δμ與Δp數值進行激子特性詮釋時所產生的差異與問題進行系統性探討。本研究將對一系列在分子結構、分子堆積方式及與其他材料交互作用方面具有差異的材料進行EA光譜量測。為確保關聯分析的準確性，EA結果將與理論計算以及獨立之瞬態吸收光譜數據進行交叉驗證。所獲得之洞見亦將進一步應用於探討不同分子堆積構型對電荷轉移之貢獻，以及有機給體／受體體異質接面（bulk heterojunction）中之電荷轉移特性。 本計畫之成功將大幅提升對有機電子材料中激子特性的定性理解，並為優化電荷轉移過程之分子設計提供重要指引。具體而言，本研究成果將有助於突破現有評估方法之限制，使有機界面電荷轉移特性的評估更加精確。此外，建立激子特性與分子結構之間的定量關係，將有助於推動以人工智慧為導向之材料開發，提高材料設計效率，並降低對傳統上依賴經驗與整體性嘗試方法（通常僅由資深化學家掌握）的依賴。

11309626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11309626.value: 深化基於分數之擴散模型的數學理論：收斂性、加速與穩健性

11309626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11309626.value: Diffusion models have become a transformative class of generative models, achieving state-of-the-art results across domains such as computer vision, natural language processing, and computational biology. Despite their empirical success, their theoretical foundations remain limited, constraining systematic improvement and reliable deployment. This project advances the theory of score-based diffusion models along two complementary directions. *(1)* Acceleration and convergence of ODE-based diffusion models: We will improve computational efficiency by developing acceleration techniques with provable Wasserstein convergence guarantees, providing a more faithful measure of generative quality. This includes second-order formulations and systematic analysis of discretization schemes for faster and more stable sampling. *(2)* Robustness and generalization of diffusion models: We will develop a minimax framework for score estimation under heavy-tailed data distributions and analyze how estimation errors propagate through the generative process, yielding end-to-end convergence guarantees beyond sub-Gaussian settings. We will further quantify robustness under distributional shifts through a distributionally robust score learning framework, establishing convergence guarantees that link data shifts to score estimation and generative accuracy. Building on the PI and Co-I’s expertise in diffusion models and sampling theory, this project will deepen the mathematical understanding of modern generative modeling. The anticipated outcomes include sharper theoretical insights, improved algorithms, and practical guidance for applying diffusion models to complex real-world data. 擴散模型已成為現代生成模型的重要範式，並在計算機視覺、自然語言處理及計算生物學等領域取得領先成果。儘管其在實際應用中展現出卓越成效，相關理論基礎仍不夠完善，因而限制了模型的系統性改進與可靠應用。 本計畫將從兩個相互補充的方向，推進基於分數的擴散模型之理論研究。 (1) 基於常微分方程之擴散模型的加速與收斂分析：本計畫將發展具有可證明 Wasserstein 收斂保證的加速方法，以提升擴散模型的計算效率，並更準確地刻畫其生成品質。研究內容包括建立二階動力學框架，以及系統性分析不同離散化方法，從而實現更快速且更穩定的採樣。 (2) 擴散模型的穩健性與泛化能力：本計畫將針對重尾資料分佈下的分數估計建立極小極大理論框架，並分析估計誤差如何沿生成過程傳播，進而在次高斯假設之外建立端到端的收斂保證。此外，本計畫將進一步建立分佈穩健的分數學習框架，量化擴散模型在分佈偏移下的穩健性，並建立資料分佈偏移、分數估計誤差與生成準確度之間的理論聯繫。 本計畫將結合計畫主持人與共同研究人員在擴散模型及採樣理論方面的專長，進一步深化對現代生成模型的數學理解。預期成果包括更精確的理論刻畫、更高效且具理論保證的演算法，以及將擴散模型應用於複雜真實世界資料時所需的理論與實務指引。

11309926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11309926.value: 透過無鉛雙鈣鈦礦奈米晶體之能量躍遷設計與結構組裝研發高性能X射線閃爍體

11309926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11309926.value: Metal halide perovskites are semiconductor materials with bright photoluminescence and tunable bandgaps. Aside from more established fields such as energy harvesting and light-emitting devices, perovskites are also promising as X-ray scintillators, i.e., the materials which convert X-ray emission to visible light. Pioneering studies on CsPbX3 (X = Cl, Br, I) perovskites demonstrated their high X-ray light yield and sensitivity, starting a new chapter in the search for a cheap, efficient, and stable alternative to current scintillation materials. Despite those promising results, lead-based perovskites are disadvantageous for commercial applications due to the possible leakage of toxic Pb2+ ions and photon re-absorption losses. Lead-free double perovskites, on the other hand, offer reduced toxicity and large Stokes shifts resulting in weaker re-absorption. This research project aims to advance X-ray scintillation technology through the development of lead-free double perovskite nanocrystals (NCs), specifically Cs2NaScCl6. Previous studies have shown great potential for Cs2NaScCl6 in a macrocrystalline form doped with trivalent cations Sb3+ and Yb3+, which offered high stability, outstanding doping capabilities, and near-unity PL quantum yield. However, studies of Sb/Yb-doped Cs2NaScCl6 in a nanocrystalline form are scarce. Using colloidally stable NCs can simplify the device fabrication process and enhance their X-ray light yield, as previously demonstrated for their lead-based counterparts. In this project, to harness this material’s potential, several research directions will be explored: (i) development of NC synthesis and doping protocols; (ii) surface modification of NCs to enhance emission quantum yield and compatibility with different environments; (iii) refinement of the dopant-mediated energy transitions to enhance X-ray scintillation; (iv) strategies to assemble NCs in polymer films and superlattices. First, we will develop protocols for synthesizing Sb/Yb-doped Cs2NaScCl6 in a nanocrystalline form, a vital step for improving their processability and enabling all-solution device fabrication. Next, we will optimize the surface ligand chemistry to render those NCs stable in both colloidal solutions and as NC-polymer composites. In the next step, we will maximize their X-ray scintillation characteristics by engineering efficient energy transfer from the matrix to dopant, and conduct ultrafast spectroscopy studies to establish the relationship between emission mechanisms and X-ray scintillation efficiency. Finally, we aim to achieve collective emission through assembling NCs into ordered structures (superlattices) to further promote scintillation. As a result of these combined efforts, this project will enable high-performance X-ray scintillators, benefiting the society. 鹵化金屬鈣鈦礦屬於具備高亮度光致發光特性且能隙可調控之半導體材料。除了能量收集、發光元件等發展已相當成熟的領域之外，鈣鈦礦材料亦具備成為X射線閃爍體的潛力；所謂閃爍體，係指可將X射線輻射轉換為可見光的材料。針對CsPbX₃（X = 氯、溴、碘）鈣鈦礦的先驅研究證實此類材料具備極高的X射線光產出率與偵測靈敏度，為尋找可取代現有閃爍材料、兼具低成本、高效率與高穩定性的新型材料開啟了新的研究篇章。 儘管該類材料展現出諸多優異特性，含鉛鈣鈦礦在商業化應用上仍存在顯著缺點：一方面有毒的鉛離子（Pb²⁺）有滲漏風險，另一方面會產生光子再吸收損耗。相對地，無鉛雙鈣鈦礦不僅毒性更低，還具備更大的斯托克斯位移，可有效減弱光子再吸收效應。 本研究計畫旨在透過研發無鉛雙鈣鈦礦奈米晶體（Nanocrystals, NCs，具體為Cs₂NaScCl₆），推進X射線閃爍技術的發展。過往研究已證實，摻雜三價銻離子（Sb³⁺）與鐿離子（Yb³⁺）的巨晶態Cs₂NaScCl₆潛力極佳，擁有高穩定性、優異的摻雜容許度，以及近乎單位一的光致發光量子產率。然而，針對銻/鐿摻雜型Cs₂NaScCl₆奈米晶體的相關研究仍十分匱乏。如同先前含鉛鈣鈦礦的研究結果所示，使用膠體穩定的奈米晶體能夠簡化元件製程，並提升其X射線光產出率。 為充分發揮該材料的潛力，本計畫將從四大研究方向展開探討： (i) 建立奈米晶體的合成與摻雜製程； (ii) 對奈米晶體進行表面改質，以提升發光量子產率，並強化其在不同環境下的相容性； (iii) 最佳化摻雜離子所介導的能量躍遷機制，進而提升X射線閃爍性能； (iv) 開發奈米晶體於高分子薄膜與超晶格結構中的組裝策略。 首先，我們會建立銻/鐿摻雜Cs₂NaScCl₆奈米晶體的合成製程，此步驟是提升材料可加工性、實現全溶液法元件製作的關鍵。接著，我們會最佳化表面配體化學，讓奈米晶體無論在膠體溶液中，或是與高分子複合之後都能維持穩定。下一步，我們會透過調控基質到摻雜離子之間的高效能量傳遞，最大化其X射線閃爍特性，並藉由超快光譜量測，建立發光機制與X射線閃爍效率之間的對應關係。最後，我們將奈米晶體組裝為有序超晶格結構以實現集體發光，進一步強化閃爍表現。 透過上述一系列研究工作，本計畫可望開發出高性能X射線閃爍體材料，並為社會帶來實質應用價值。

11310026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11310026.value: 低溫萊頓弗羅斯特泡沫：流體結構方法用於液滴懸浮

11310026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11310026.value: The Leidenfrost effect, in which a liquid levitates on its own vapor film above a heated surface, has long fascinated researchers in fluid dynamics and interfacial thermophysics. Despite extensive study of single-phase droplets, the phenomenon remains constrained by two key limitations: it typically occurs at temperatures far above the liquid’s boiling point, and lowering the transition temperature generally requires specially engineered or coated surfaces to stabilize the vapor layer. These constraints limit both fundamental understanding and practical application, leaving a fundamental question unresolved: to what extent can the Leidenfrost point be reduced to enable stable droplet levitation at low temperatures without surface modification? Our preliminary experiments have revealed an unconventional phenomenon: liquid foams, composed of gas bubbles dispersed within a continuous liquid phase, can sustain stable Leidenfrost-like levitation at 110°C on unmodified surfaces—close to the boiling point of water and significantly below the ~130°C threshold reported in previous studies employing surface modifications. This striking discovery underscores the crucial roles of bubble dynamics, vapor generation, and interfacial thermofluidics in governing foam–surface interactions. Distinct from conventional single-phase liquid behavior, this finding points to a fundamentally new, fluid-structure-based mechanism for self-sustained levitation at record-low temperatures, representing a paradigm shift from surface engineering to fluid engineering. This project aims to elucidate the physical principles underlying low-temperature Leidenfrost foam levitation and to explore its potential for functional applications. Four interconnected research tasks are proposed. First, liquid foams with precisely controlled bubble size, gas volume fraction, and composition will be generated using microfluidic technique to provide a reproducible experimental platform. Second, systematic studies will quantify how foam and substrate properties affect vapor-film formation and stability, leading to a comprehensive phase map of low-temperature Leidenfrost behavior. Third, predictive models coupling bubble deformation, vapor-layer evolution, and heat transfer will be developed to capture the onset and persistence of foam levitation. Finally, proof-of-concept demonstrations will showcase the use of Leidenfrost foams for effective thermal shielding and contactless cargo transport on heated surfaces. The proposed study will yield a theoretical framework for low-temperature Leidenfrost behavior in multiphase fluids, revealing how foam morphology governs vapor-film dynamics and low-temperature levitation. By uncovering how vapor layers can form and persist at near-boiling temperatures on plain surfaces, the study will lay the scientific foundation for innovative technologies, including effective thermal management and contact-free transport systems, with broad relevance to advanced manufacturing, electronics, and aerospace applications. 萊頓弗羅斯特效應（Leidenfrost effect）是指液體在加熱表面上，受其自身產生的蒸汽膜支撐而懸浮的現象，長期以來一直吸引著流體力學與界面熱物理領域的研究人員。儘管針對單相液滴已有廣泛研究，但該現象仍受限於兩大核心瓶頸：其一，它通常發生在遠高於液體沸點的溫度下；其二，若要降低轉變溫度，普遍需要透過特殊設計或具備塗層的表面來穩定蒸汽層。這些限制不僅制約了基礎理論的理解，也阻礙了實際應用的發展，並留下一個懸而未決的根本問題：在不進行表面改質的情況下，萊頓弗羅斯特點究竟能在多大程度上被降低，以實現低溫下的穩定液滴懸浮？我們的初步實驗發現了一種非傳統現象：由氣泡分散在連續液相中組成的「液體泡沫」，在未經改質的表面上，於 110°C 即可維持穩定的類萊頓弗羅斯特懸浮。這已接近水的沸點，且顯著低於以往採用表面改質研究中所報導的約 130°C 閾值。這項重大發現凸顯了氣泡動力學、蒸汽產生以及界面熱流體力學在主導「泡沫—表面」交互作用中的關鍵角色。有別於傳統的單相液體行為，此發現指出了一種全新的、基於流體結構的自我維持懸浮機制，能創下歷史新低的懸浮溫度，展現了從「表面工程」向「流體工程」的範式轉移。本計畫旨在闡明低溫萊頓弗羅斯特泡沫懸浮背後的物理原理，並探索其在功能性應用上的潛力。對此，我們提出四項相互關聯的研究任務：（1）微流體技術製備——利用微流體技術生成氣泡大小、氣體體積分數及成分皆受精準控制的液體泡沫，以提供高重現性的實驗平台。（2）系統性量化實驗——量化泡沫與基材特性如何影響蒸汽膜的形成與穩定性，進而繪製出低溫萊頓弗羅斯特行為的完整相圖。（3）預測模型建構——開發耦合氣泡變形、蒸汽層演變與熱傳遞的預測模型，以捕捉泡沫懸浮的觸發與持續機制。（4）概念驗證展示——展示萊頓弗羅斯特泡沫在加熱表面上作為高效熱屏蔽，以及進行無接觸貨物運輸的概念驗證。本研究預期將建立多相流體中低溫萊頓弗羅斯特行為的理論框架，揭示泡沫形貌如何主導蒸汽膜動力學與低溫懸浮。透過解構蒸汽層如何在普通表面、接近沸點的溫度下形成並持續存在，本計畫將為創新技術奠定科學基礎，包含高效熱管理與無接觸運輸系統，對先進製造、電子元件及航太應用具有廣泛的參考價值。

11311726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11311726.value: PET塑料的光-酶级联升级再造：耦合酶促解聚、对苯二甲酸酯增值与辅因子原位再生

11311726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11311726.value: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) recycling has largely relied on the alkaline hydrolysis method, which suffers from quality loss and harsh processing conditions. While enzymatic hydrolysis offers a greener alternative, and PET depolymerization to ethylene glycol (EG) and terephthalic acid (TPA) is well-studied, strategies for upcycling TPA into high-value chemicals remain underexplored, limiting the potential of circular bioeconomy frameworks. This proposal introduces a cell-free, light-powered platform for the sustainable upcycling of PET waste into high-value chemicals. The system integrates three core modules: (i) enzymatic depolymerization of post-consumer PET waste into EG and TPA under mild, enzyme-compatible conditions; (ii) oxidation of EG to valuable products like glycolaldehyde (GA) while regenerating 1,4-NADH using a visible-light photocatalyst; and (iii) biocatalytic valorization of TPA through a TPADO–DCDDH cascade to protocatechuic acid (PCA), and then extending to the production of gallic acid with the help of regenerated NADH as a proof-of-concept of photo-biocatalytic self-regeneration. The novelty lies in the integration of in vitro TPA upcycling enzymes with the PET hydrolysis reaction, allowing for the simultaneous regeneration of NADH and oxidation of EG within a single photocatalytic architecture. This eliminates the need for sacrificial donors and minimizes parasitic hydrogen evolution. Employing magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) will ease the process of purification, immobilization, enhance the stability of TPA upcycling enzymes, enable wash–react cycles, and can facilitate semi-continuous bioreactor operation. A membrane-enclosed PETase system is proposed to retain enzyme activity with bulk PET particles while allowing monomer diffusion, extending operational windows, and reducing enzyme loss. To ensure robust performance, the project emphasizes rate matching between photocatalytic and enzymatic modules, as well as dynamic feedback control of light intensity, oxygen supply, and pH, if necessary. The integrated design aims to achieve closed electron and carbon balances, multi-hour stability, and potentially scalable operation. This work introduces a photo-biocatalytic co-reforming strategy that transforms PET waste into value-added aromatics using green materials under mild conditions. By coupling enzyme specificity with solar-driven redox chemistry, the platform establishes a blueprint for next-generation plastic upcycling technologies, bridging the gap between waste mitigation and circular bioeconomy. Note: Unless otherwise stated, NADH in this proposal refers to the enzymatically active 1,4-NADH isomer 聚对苯二甲酸乙二醇酯 (PET) 的回收利用主要依赖于碱性水解法，但该方法存在质量损失和加工条件苛刻等问题。虽然酶水解法提供了一种更环保的替代方案，且PET解聚为乙二醇 (EG) 和对苯二甲酸 (TPA) 的研究已较为深入，但将TPA升级再造为高价值化学品的策略仍未得到充分探索，这限制了循环生物经济框架的潜力。本方案提出了一种无细胞、光驱动的平台，用于将PET废料可持续地升级再造为高价值化学品。该系统集成了三个核心模块：(i) 在温和的、酶相容的条件下，将消费后PET废料酶解聚为EG和TPA；(ii) 利用可见光光催化剂将EG氧化为乙醇醛 (GA) 等高价值产品，同时再生1,4-NADH；(iii) 通过TPADO-DCDDH级联反应对TPA进行生物催化增值，生成原儿茶酸(PCA)，然后借助再生NADH进一步生产没食子酸，以此验证光生物催化自再生的概念。其创新之处在于将体外TPA上循环酶与PET水解反应相结合，从而在单一光催化体系中实现NADH的再生和EG的氧化。这无需牺牲性供体，并最大限度地减少了副产物析氢。采用磁性纳米粒子(MNP)可以简化纯化和固定化过程，提高TPA上循环酶的稳定性，实现洗涤-反应循环，并有助于半连续生物反应器的运行。本文提出了一种膜包裹的PETase系统，该系统在保持酶活性的同时，允许单体扩散，从而延长操作窗口并减少酶的损失。为确保性能稳定，该项目着重于光催化模块和酶模块之间的速率匹配，并在必要时对光照强度、氧气供应和pH值进行动态反馈控制。集成设计旨在实现闭合的电子和碳平衡、数小时的稳定性以及潜在的可扩展运行。这项工作提出了一种光生物催化共重整策略，利用绿色材料在温和条件下将PET废料转化为高附加值芳烃。通过将酶的特异性与太阳能驱动的氧化还原反应相结合，该平台为下一代塑料升级回收技术奠定了基础，弥合了废物减量和循环生物经济之间的差距。

11312326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11312326.value: 亞鐵電體中電控自旋軌道耦合的研究

11312326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11312326.value: Conventional microelectronics, which rely solely on the charge of electrons, are confronting fundamental physical limits as transistor sizes approach the atomic scale. The challenges of excessive heat generation from electric currents, quantum tunneling effects that cause current leakage, and the looming end of Moore's Law are driving an urgent search for a successor technology. This has led to intense research in spintronics, a paradigm that exploits another intrinsic property of the electron—its spin. By utilizing spin as an additional state variable, often in conjunction with charge, spintronic devices promise non-volatile data storage, drastically lower power consumption, and logic operations that are immune to the debilitating charge-based effects plaguing conventional electronics, thereby opening a new pathway for the future of information technology. The key functionalities required for a spin-based device include the generation, control and detection of spin current, each of which presents its own challenges. For example, generation of spin current is usually done by spin injection from a ferromagnetic material, spin Hall effect in heavy metals or thermally induced spin Seebeck effect. These techniques have been studied extensively, but face issues such as low efficiency, large charge current and poor controllability, respectively. Furthermore, manipulation of spin current is usually done by magnetic fields, which is not compatible with modern electronic technologies. Our recent discovery of electric-field controlled spin-orbit-coupling (SOC) in a hybrid ferrielectric crystal offers unique opportunities for both the fundamental study and practical applications of spin-based devices. The spontaneous polarization not only allows for the generation of spin current under circularly polarized light, but also the control of the spin orientation by an electric field. To further explore the tantalizing opportunities brought about by this unique system, we thus propose to conduct a comprehensive study on the electric-field driven structural and electronic evolutions, and explore the effects on light induced circular photogalvanic phenomena in this system. The outcomes of this project have the potential to lay the foundation for future spin technologies, bringing novel light-based method for spin excitations and paving the way for designing advanced photogalvanic spintronic devices. The success of this work would not only lead to novel spin-based technologies but also to devices that consume a fraction of the energy of today's electronics, contributing to a more sustainable digital future. 隨着晶體管尺寸接近原子尺度，依賴電子電荷屬性的傳統微電子學正面臨根本性的物理極限。電流產生的過多熱量、量子隧穿效應導致的漏電，以及摩爾定律即將走到盡頭等挑戰，正推動人們急切尋找替代技術。由此引發了對自旋電子學的深入研究，這一範式利用電子的另一種內稟屬性—自旋。通過將自旋作為狀態變量（通常與電荷結合使用），自旋電子器件有望實現非易失性數據儲存、極低功耗、以及不受困擾傳統電子學的電荷相關效應影響的邏輯運算，從而為信息技術的未來開闢一條新路徑。 自旋器件所需的關鍵功能包括自旋流的產生、調控和檢測，而每個方面都有其自身的挑戰。例如，自旋流的產生通常通過鐵磁材料的自旋注入、重金屬中的自旋霍爾效應或熱致自旋塞貝克效應來實現。這些技術已被廣泛研究，但分別面臨着效率低、電荷電流大和可控性差等問題。此外，自旋流的調控通常依賴磁場，這與現代電子技術不兼容。 我們最近在混合亞鐵電晶體中發現的電場調控自旋軌道耦合效應，為基於自旋器件的基礎研究和實際應用提供了獨特機遇。自發極化不僅使得在圓偏振光照射下產生自旋流成為可能，還允許通過電場調控自旋取向。為了進一步探索這一獨特體系帶來的誘人機遇，我們提議對該體系中電場驅動的結構和電子演化進行系統研究，並探討其對光致圓偏振光電效應的影響。該項目的成果有望為未來自旋技術奠定基礎，為自旋激發帶來新穎的基於光的方法，並為設計先進的光電自旋電子器件鋪平道路。這項工作的成功將催生新型自旋技術，為更加可持續的信息未來作出貢獻。

11312426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11312426.value: 原位席夫鹼驅動亞胺網路設計與含MA鈣鈦礦應變耦合相變–分解機制調控

11312426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11312426.value: Metal halide perovskites combine strong optical absorption, efficient charge transport, and low‑temperature processing, enabling high performance and scalable manufacturing. Incorporating methylammonium (MA) often yields smooth, large‑grained films and dynamic dielectric screening that suppresses nonradiative recombination, underpinning record single‑junction and tandem devices. However, durability remains the central obstacle. Under heat, light, electrical bias, or humidity, these soft lattices distort and undergo phase transitions, ions migrate, and MA can volatilize or decompose. The intertwined processes create defects, shift band alignment, and progressively erode power output. Conventional interface passivation based on weak interactions or ultrathin 2D layers offers partial relief yet can desorb, reorganize, or leave channels for ion transport and MA loss. MA‑free formulations improve stability in some cases but may trade away peak efficiency or still depend on MA‑assisted processing, limiting their generality. A robust, chemistry‑driven interfacial solution that preserves MA‑enabled advantages under operational stress is therefore needed. We propose an in‑situ, surface confined Schiff‑base strategy that constructs an ultrathin imine network precisely at the most vulnerable regions—surfaces and grain boundaries. Tailored carbonyl precursors and gentle activation drive selective C=N formation, yielding a covalently bonded interphase that redistributes local strain, raises barriers to ion migration and deprotonation, and blocks pathways leading to phase transition and decomposition. The research will establish a reaction toolkit encompassing precursor libraries, processing windows, and spectroscopic fingerprints that confirm surface specificity and nanoscale confinement. It will then map where and how the interphase forms and relate topology to electronic quality, including modulation of internal fields, suppression of trap states, and regulation of coupled ionic–electronic transport under light, heat, bias, and humidity. Finally, these insights will be translated into complete devices by co‑optimizing the stack for efficiency and applying harmonized durability protocols to identify and mitigate dominant failure modes. The outcome will be a practical, scalable route to MA‑containing perovskite solar cells that retain top‑tier performance with markedly improved stability, alongside clear processing guidelines, quantitative design rules for interphase formation, and validated benchmarks to accelerate reliable manufacturing. 金屬鹵化物鈣鈦礦具有吸光能力強、電荷傳輸快和低溫製備等優點，適合製造高效能、可規模化生產的太陽能電池。加入甲胺（MA）有助於形成平整、大晶粒的薄膜，減少能量損失，進而提高裝置效率。然而，這類材料在熱、光、電壓和濕氣作用下容易發生結構變形、相變和離子遷移，MA也可能揮發或分解，最終產生缺陷並降低發電性能。現有界面保護方法效果有限，而無MA材料有時會犧牲效率。因此，需要一種更穩定的界面保護方法，在保留MA優勢的同時提升裝置壽命。 本計畫提出一種原位席夫鹼反應策略，在鈣鈦礦表面和晶界形成超薄、牢固的亞胺網絡。此網絡能夠緩解局部應變，阻礙離子移動和MA分解，從而減少相變與材料劣化。本計畫將篩選適當的反應材料和製備條件，研究保護層的形成位置及其作用，並評估其在光、熱、電壓和濕氣下的保護效果。最終，我們將把該方法應用於完整太陽能電池，在保持高效率的同時顯著提升穩定性，並建立適合規模化生產的製備方法和設計準則

11313126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11313126.value: 藻華毒素氣膠的多相氧化：對其大氣生命週期、宿命與毒性之影響

11313126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11313126.value: Harmful algal blooms (HABs), intensified by climate change and eutrophication, occur when photosynthetic organisms proliferate and release toxic metabolites (“HAB toxins”) into the water column. HAB toxins can be ejected from the water surface into the atmosphere through bubble bursting during wave action. Aerosolized HAB toxins can be transported over long distances inland, exposing downwind communities to their inhalation hazards. Previous epidemiological and toxicological studies have linked this exposure to various negative respiratory health outcomes. While previous research has mostly focused on the potential for long-range transport and inhalation toxicity of some HAB toxins, their atmospheric processing remains a critical knowledge gap. Specifically, the multiphase oxidation of HAB toxin aerosols by ubiquitous atmospheric oxidants such as gas-phase hydroxyl radicals (•OH) and ozone (O3) are currently understudied and poorly understood. This oxidative processing can fundamentally alter the atmospheric lifetimes, fates, chemical composition, and inhalation toxicity of aerosolized HAB toxins. Thus, enhancing our knowledge of the multiphase oxidation of HAB toxin aerosols is essential for assessing their evolving public health threat. This project addresses existing knowledge gaps by systematically investigating the multiphase •OH and O3 oxidation of HAB toxin aerosols and its consequent impact on their toxicological characteristics. The project focuses on five prevalent HAB toxins: microcystin LR, saxitoxin, okadaic acid, cylindrospermopsin, and brevetoxin PbTx 2. The overarching goal is to elucidate the chemical transformations of HAB toxin aerosols during oxidation, quantify how aerosol matrices modulate this process, and determine the resulting evolution in their inhalation toxicity. Experiments will be performed using an oxidation flow reactor to simulate atmospheric multiphase oxidation, during which HAB toxin-containing sea spray or lake spray aerosol proxies are exposed to gas-phase •OH and O3. Ultra-performance liquid chromatography coupled to high-resolution mass spectrometry will be used to measure reaction kinetics, identify and track the formation of oxidation products, and elucidate reaction mechanisms. Scanning electron microscopy with energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy will be used to characterize oxidative changes in aerosol morphology and mixing state. To determine how multiphase oxidation modulates the inhalation health risks of HAB toxin aerosols, composition changes will be linked to evolution in their toxicological responses, which will be evaluated using acellular (dithiothreitol) and cellular (human bronchial epithelial BEAS-2B cells) assays. Project findings will provide the fundamental data needed to refine atmospheric exposure models and enable accurate science-based public health risk assessments to protect communities near HAB-prone waterbodies. 有害藻華（HABs）因氣候變遷與優養化而加劇，當光合生物（如藍細菌、甲藻）大量增殖並釋放有毒代謝物（即「藻華毒素」）進入水體時即發生。藻華毒素可透過波浪作用產生的氣泡破裂從水面噴射至大氣中。氣溶膠化的藻華毒素可長距離傳輸至內陸，使下風處社區暴露於吸入性危害。先前的流行病學與毒理學研究已將此暴露與多種負面呼吸道健康結果建立關聯。雖然過去研究多集中於部分藻華毒素的長程傳輸潛力與固有的吸入毒性，但其大氣化學轉化過程仍是一項關鍵知識缺口。具體而言，藻華毒素氣膠經由大氣中普遍存在的氧化劑（如氣相羥基自由基（•OH）與臭氧（O3））進行多相氧化的相關研究目前仍不足且了解有限。此氧化過程可根本性地改變氣膠化藻華毒素的大氣生命週期、宿命、化學組成及吸入毒性。因此，增進我們對藻華毒素氣膠多相氧化的認識，對於評估其對公眾健康日益增長的威脅至關重要。 本計畫旨在透過系統性研究藻華毒素氣膠之 •OH 與 O3 多相氧化及其對毒理特性之後續影響，來填補上述知識缺口。總體目標為闡明藻華毒素氣膠在氧化過程中的化學轉化、量化氣膠基質如何調控此過程，並確定其吸入毒性隨之而來的演變。實驗將使用氧化流動反應器來模擬大氣多相氧化，過程中將含有藻華毒素的海浪或湖泊氣膠模擬物暴露於氣相 •OH 與 O3。將使用超高效液相層析串聯高解析度質譜儀來測量反應動力學、識別並追蹤氧化產物的形成，以及闡明反應機制。同時也將測定氣膠形態與混合狀態的氧化性變化。為確定多相氧化如何調控藻華毒素氣膠的吸入健康風險，將把組成分變化與其毒理反應的演變進行關聯，並透過各種分析方法進行評估。本計畫的綜合研究成果將提供基礎數據，以利於精煉大氣暴露模式，並實現以科學為基礎的準確公共衛生風險評估，從而保護鄰近藻華好發水體之社區。

11313726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11313726.value: 等离子体可压缩欧拉–泊松方程稀疏波的高维稳定性

11313726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11313726.value: This research proposal addresses a fundamental problem in the theory of multidimensional hyperbolic conservation laws: the structural stability of planar rarefaction waves for the compressible Euler-Poisson equations. This system serves as a key hydrodynamical model for a warm, collisional plasma, where the charged particle fluid interacts with a self-consistent electrostatic field. While the stability of multidimensional rarefaction waves has been recently resolved for the compressible Euler equations of gas dynamics, the incorporation of the electric field introduces a profound analytical challenge that this project seeks to overcome. The central difficulty stems from the non-local nature of the electric potential, determined instantaneously across space by the Poisson equation. This non-locality destroys the finite speed of propagation (causality), a foundational property of the homogeneous Euler system. Consequently, the spacetime geometry of the characteristic surfaces that define the rarefaction wave regions becomes globally coupled. The boundaries of these regions are no longer predetermined by the initial data but become "free boundaries," interacting non-locally with the entire solution. This leads to a highly intricate and rich nonlinear coupling that is absent in classical gas dynamics. The primary objective is to establish the local-in-time existence and uniqueness of continuous, piecewise smooth solutions featuring two-dimensional rarefaction waves emerging from discontinuous initial data. We will first tackle the case of irrotational flow, where the vorticity vanishes. Subsequently, we will confront the significantly more complex case where vorticity is present, which deforms the characteristic surfaces and introduces further analytic obstacles. The research plan involves a novel nonlinear iterative scheme that decouples the non-local problem into a sequence of local hyperbolic problems with sources. The convergence of this scheme will be established using a sophisticated acoustic geometric framework pioneered by Christodoulou and adopted by Luo-Yu in the study of multi-dimensional compressible Euler equations. This involves working within a characteristic coordinate system, deriving precise energy estimates for a wave-transport system, and controlling the geometry of the characteristic surfaces to obtain uniform estimates without loss of derivatives. Success in this project will provide the first rigorous mathematical proof of the stability of multidimensional rarefaction waves in a plasma context, significantly advancing our understanding of how long-range forces influence nonlinear wave phenomena. The results will have broad implications for the analysis of non-local hyperbolic systems and contribute to the foundational mathematics of plasma physics. 本研究计划探讨高维双曲守恒律理论中的一个基本问题：可压缩欧拉–泊松方程组平面稀疏波的结构稳定性。该方程组是描述温热碰撞等离子体的一类重要流体动力学模型，其中带电粒子流体与自洽静电场相互作用。尽管近年来气体动力学中可压缩欧拉方程的多维稀疏波稳定性问题已得到解决，但电场的引入带来了深刻的分析挑战，而本项目旨在克服这一困难。 核心难点源于电势的非局部性质：电势由泊松方程决定，并在整个空间中瞬时建立。这种非局部性破坏了有限传播速度（因果性），而有限传播速度正是齐次欧拉方程组的一项基础性质。因此，界定稀疏波区域的特征曲面的时空几何结构变得全局耦合。这些区域的边界不再由初始数据预先确定，而是成为与整体解发生非局部相互作用的“自由边界”。由此产生了一种极为复杂且内涵丰富的非线性耦合，而这种耦合在经典气体动力学中并不存在。 本项目的首要目标是证明：对于不连续初始数据所产生的二维稀疏波，存在唯一的局部时间连续分片光滑解。我们将首先研究无旋流动，即涡量为零的情形；随后处理复杂程度显著提高的有涡情形。在后一情形中，涡量会使特征曲面发生变形，并带来更多分析上的障碍。研究方案将采用一种新的非线性迭代方法，把非局部问题解耦为一系列带源项的局部双曲型问题。该迭代方法的收敛性将借助一套精细的声学几何框架予以证明。这一框架由 Christodoulou 首创，并由 Luo–Yu 用于高维可压缩欧拉方程的研究。具体而言，我们将在特征坐标系中开展分析，为波动–输运系统建立精确的能量估计，并控制特征曲面的几何结构，从而在不发生导数损失的情况下获得一致估计。 本项目一旦成功，将首次严格证明等离子体背景下高维稀疏波的稳定性，显著深化我们对长程力如何影响非线性波动现象的理解。研究结果将对非局部双曲型系统的分析产生广泛影响，并为等离子体物理的基础数学理论作出贡献。

11314226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11314226.value: 打破傳統分子篩分規則：利用分子互動開發高效氣體分離材料

11314226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11314226.value: Dr Gu, Qinfen Prof LIU, ZHE

11314226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11314226.value: The gas separation industry accounts for approximately 10–15% of global energy consumption. Developing energy-efficient adsorbents capable of distinguishing similar-sized molecules remains a grand challenge in chemical engineering. This project aims to establish a new paradigm of molecular sieving by revealing that the extent of door-keeping cation displacement—co-governed by the size and interaction strength of both guest molecules and cations—dictates selective gas admission in molecular trapdoor adsorbents. Building on PI Shang’s discovery of the molecular trapdoor mechanism, in which gas entry is regulated by interaction-driven cation motion rather than rigid pore size, this work transforms the mechanism into a predictive framework integrating size, interaction, and framework–cation environment as mechanistically synergistic design handles. Zeolites are selected as the model platform because their well-defined topologies, atomic-level cation positions, and exceptional thermal and structural stability enable rigorous quantification of cation displacement and adsorption energetics—conditions essential for establishing predictive understanding. Once validated, the mechanistic framework and AI-guided methodology developed here will be readily extendable to hybrid porous materials such as metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) and covalent–organic frameworks (COFs). Through four interlinked aims, the project will: (i) elucidate how molecular size and interaction strength jointly control selective admission in model zeolites (Ag-LTA and Na-LTA), revealing counterintuitive invertible and size-inverse sieving; (ii) identify adjacent cations as remote regulators of the activation barrier and threshold admission temperature; (iii) establish adsorption configuration as an orthogonal handle enabling same-size sieving in flexible zeolites such as PHI; and (iv) integrate these mechanistic insights into an AI-assisted predictive design framework, enabling the synthesis and validation of next-generation trapdoor zeolites for benchmark ‘hard’ separations—CO2/C2H2, C2H4/C2H6, C3H6/C3H8, N2/CH4, and Xe/Kr—where achieving sieving-level selectivity remains challenging. Combining in situ neutron and synchrotron diffraction, X-ray absorption spectroscopy, operando FTIR spectroscopy, molecular simulations, and AI-assisted data integration, the project will map how cation displacement, guest configuration, and energetics jointly determine selective gas admission. The outcomes will establish a unifying mechanistic foundation for counter-intuitive molecular sieving, enabling rational design of next-generation, energy-efficient trapdoor adsorbents. The resulting fundamental insights will not only advance adsorption-based gas separations but also inform related fields—gas storage, sensing, and catalysis—contributing to sustainable chemical manufacturing and global decarbonization. 氣體分離產業約占全球能源消耗的 10–15%。開發能夠區分尺寸相近分子的高能源效率吸附劑，仍是化學工程領域的一項重大挑戰。本計畫旨在建立分子篩分的新典範，揭示「門控陽離子位移程度（extent of door-keeping cation displacement）」——其受客體分子與陽離子的尺寸及相互作用強度共同調控——如何決定分子陷阱門（molecular trapdoor）吸附劑中的氣體選擇性進入。建立於 PI Shang 對分子陷阱門機制的發現之上，本研究將此機制轉化為一套可預測的理論框架：在此機制中，氣體進入並非由剛性的孔徑尺寸所決定，而是受到相互作用驅動的陽離子運動（interaction-driven cation motion）所調控。本研究進一步將尺寸、相互作用以及骨架–陽離子環境整合為可協同調控的設計參數。 透過四項相互關聯的研究目標，本計畫將：(i) 闡明分子尺寸與相互作用強度如何共同控制模型沸石（Ag-LTA 與 Na-LTA）中的選擇性進入，揭示反直覺的可逆型與尺寸反向篩分（invertible and size-inverse sieving）；(ii) 鑑定鄰近陽離子作為活化能障與臨界進入溫度（T₀）的遠端調控因子；(iii) 建立吸附構型作為一項正交調控參數，使得在 PHI 等具柔性沸石中能實現相同尺寸反向篩分（same-size-inverse sieving）；以及 (iv) 透過對一系列具代表性的「困難」氣體對進行分離——CO₂/C₂H₂、C₂H₄/C₂H₆、C₃H₆/C₃H₈、N₂/CH₄ 及 Xe/Kr——驗證此統一框架；對於這些氣體對而言，要達到分子篩分等級的選擇性仍極具挑戰。 本計畫將結合原位中子與同步輻射繞射、X 射線吸收光譜、操作條件下傅立葉轉換紅外光譜（operando FTIR）、分子模擬，以及 AI 輔助資料整合，描繪陽離子位移、客體分子構型與能量學如何共同決定氣體的選擇性進入。研究成果將建立一套可統一解釋反直覺分子篩分現象的機理基礎，進而實現次世代高能源效率分子陷阱門吸附劑的理性設計。 這些基礎研究洞見不僅將推進以吸附為基礎的氣體分離技術，也將為相關領域——包括氣體儲存、感測與催化——提供重要指引，進而促進永續化學製造與全球脫碳。

11314326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11314326.value: 高能量密度与长循环寿命无负极锂金属电池的分级工程化界面理性设计

11314326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11314326.value: Anode-free lithium metal batteries (AFLBs) represent a transformative approach toward next-generation energy storage systems by eliminating the conventional lithium-containing anode, thereby maximizing gravimetric and volumetric energy densities. Despite their promise, practical deployment of AFLBs is impeded by critical challenges, including uncontrolled Li dendrite growth, severe volume fluctuations during plating/stripping, parasitic side reactions, and the formation of an unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). These interrelated issues lead to low Coulombic efficiency, rapid capacity fade, and safety hazards, hindering long-term cyclability. This proposal aims to establish a unified materials design framework to simultaneously address these interfacial instabilities through hierarchical engineering of the anode-side interface. We propose a multi-scale strategy integrating three-dimensional (3D) lithiophilic current collectors, artificial protective interlayers with tailored ion transport channels, and synergistically optimized electrolytes to regulate Li nucleation, suppress dendritic growth, and stabilize the electrode/electrolyte interface. Specifically, we will design porous Cu architectures functionalized with lithiophilic metal alloys (e.g., Sn, Au) or carbon-based coatings to reduce local current density and promote uniform Li deposition. Concurrently, we will engineer ultrathin composite interphases incorporating inorganic LiF-rich domains and polymer matrices to enhance mechanical robustness and ionic conductivity. Coupled with localized high-concentration electrolytes or fluorinated solvents, this integrated interface design is expected to yield dense, dendrite-free Li plating with minimized side reactions. Advanced in situ/operando characterizations, including cryo-TEM and X-ray tomography, will be employed to elucidate dynamic Li deposition behaviors and SEI evolution. The proposed work will not only advance the fundamental understanding of interfacial regulation in anode-free systems but also provide scalable design principles for developing safe, high-energy, and durable AFLBs, paving the way for their commercialization in electric vehicles and portable electronics. 无负极锂金属电池（AFLBs）通过消除传统的含锂负极，从而最大化提升质量和体积能量密度，代表了下一代储能系统的一种变革性方法。尽管发展前景广阔，但AFLBs的实际应用仍受到关键挑战的制约，包括不可控的锂枝晶生长、电镀/剥离过程中的剧烈体积波动、寄生副反应以及不稳定固体电解质界面膜（SEI）的形成。这些相互关联的问题导致库仑效率低下、容量迅速衰减和安全隐患，从而阻碍了长期的循环能力。本提案旨在建立一个统一的材料设计框架，通过对负极侧界面进行分级工程化设计，同时解决这些界面不稳定性问题。我们提出了一种多尺度策略，将三维（3D）亲锂集流体、具有定制离子传输通道的人工保护中间层以及协同优化的电解液相结合，以调节锂成核、抑制枝晶生长并稳定电极/电解液界面。具体而言，我们将设计利用亲锂金属合金（如锡、金）或碳基涂层功能化的孔状铜结构，以降低局部电流密度并促进均匀的锂沉积。同时，我们将构建包含富含无机LiF微区和聚合物基体的超薄复合中间相，以增强机械鲁棒性和离子电导率。结合局部高浓度电解液或氟化溶剂，这种集成界面设计有望实现致密、无枝晶的锂电镀，并最大程度地减少副反应。本研究将采用包括冷冻透射电子显微镜（cryo-TEM）和X射线断层扫描在内的先进原位/实时表征技术，以阐明动态锂沉积行为和SEI演变。拟开展的工作不仅将推进对无负极系统中界面调控的基本理解，还将为开发安全、高能量和耐用的AFLBs提供可扩展的设计原则，为其在电动汽车和便携式电子产品中的商业化铺平道路。

11314526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11314526.value: 基于薄膜铌酸锂平台的波束赋形接收型光学相控阵

11314526.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11314526.value: Prof Hu, Xiaopeng Prof Li, Tao

11314526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11314526.value: Optical Phased Arrays (OPAs) are transformative for next-generation optical beam control, enabling agile, mechanical-free steering and shaping of light. Their impact parallels that of microwave and acoustic phased arrays, which underpin 5G/6G communication, radar, and imaging systems. In optics, OPAs promise advances in solid-state LiDAR, free-space optical communication, deep-space navigation, and quantum sensing, empowering reconfigurable beam steering, target tracking, and precise angle-of-arrival detection. These capabilities are critical for autonomous vehicles, spatial mapping, and global optical communication networks. However, realizing reconfigurable and well-balanced high-performance beamforming OPAs remains challenging due to fabrication-induced errors, the lack of modulators combining high speed, low loss, low power, scalable and thermally stable designs. While transmitter-side OPAs have been widely explored, receiver OPAs, essential for detecting weak signals and reconstructing spatial information, remain underdeveloped, hindering progress toward fully solid-state optical sensing and communication systems. This project aims to develop receiver OPA featured with high side-lobe-suppression-ratio (SLSR) beamforming, fast response, low power consumption, low optical loss, and environmental robustness. We will first develop compact thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) electro-optic phase shifters capable of precise, fast, and low-loss modulation under high-voltage operation. Multiphysics modeling and device-level optimization will explore trade-offs among modulation performance, footprint, and thermal stability. At the component level, a variable splitter tree (VST) beamforming network will be optimized for simultaneous phase and amplitude control, supported by low-noise high-voltage electronics. A two-dimensional OPA will then be designed and fabricated to achieve a wide field of view, low sidelobe levels and high coupling efficiency. Finally, a beamforming receiver OPA prototype system will be experimentally validated through far-field optical and photon-level measurements, demonstrating accurate angle-of-arrival detection and target tracking. The results will establish well-balanced high-performance beamforming OPAs for next-generation optical sensing and free-space communication systems, advancing fully solid-state LiDAR and optical receivers. This project builds upon the PI's previously verified beamforming OPA architecture, enhancing its feasibility. Preliminary studies demonstrated short-length TFLN modulators with linear electro-optic response and developed a hybrid Adam–PSO optimization algorithm that improved VST beamforming, achieving higher sidelobe suppression with reduced complexity and loss. Moreover, both classical and quantum frequency-modulated continuous-wave LiDAR systems have been constructed and validated, providing a robust experimental foundation for subsequent receiver OPA studies and confirming the project's feasibility. 光学相控阵（Optical Phased Array, OPA）是下一代光束调控技术的重要发展方向，可实现无需机械运动的快速、灵活光束扫描与波束赋形。其重要性可类比于微波和声学相控阵，后两者已广泛应用于5G/6G通信、雷达及成像系统。在光学领域，OPA有望推动固态激光雷达（LiDAR）、自由空间光通信、深空导航和量子传感等技术的发展，实现可重构光束扫描、目标跟踪以及高精度到达角（angle-of-arrival）探测。这些能力对于自动驾驶、空间环境测绘以及全球光通信网络等应用具有重要意义。然而，要实现兼具可重构性和综合高性能的波束赋形OPA仍面临诸多挑战，包括制造误差所引起的性能劣化，以及目前缺乏能够同时兼顾高速、低损耗、低功耗、可扩展性和热稳定性的调制器。与此同时，现有OPA研究主要集中于发射端，而对于接收微弱光信号并重构空间信息至关重要的接收端OPA仍发展不足，制约了全固态光学传感与通信系统的进一步发展。 本项目旨在开发一种兼具高旁瓣抑制比（Side-Lobe Suppression Ratio, SLSR）波束赋形能力、快速响应、低功耗、低光学损耗及良好环境鲁棒性的接收型光学相控阵。首先，本项目将开发紧凑型薄膜铌酸锂（Thin-Film Lithium Niobate, TFLN）电光移相器，在高电压驱动条件下实现精确、快速且低损耗的相位调制。通过多物理场建模和器件级优化，系统研究调制性能、器件尺寸和热稳定性之间的权衡关系。在器件与功能模块层面，将进一步优化基于可变分光树（Variable Splitter Tree, VST）的波束赋形网络，实现光学相位和幅度的协同控制，并开发与之配套的低噪声高压驱动电子系统。在此基础上，将设计并制备二维OPA，以实现宽视场、低旁瓣和高光耦合效率。最后，本项目将搭建接收型波束赋形OPA原型系统，并通过远场光学测量及光子级探测实验进行验证，实现高精度到达角探测和目标跟踪。项目研究成果将为下一代光学传感及自由空间光通信系统建立一种综合性能均衡的高性能波束赋形OPA技术平台，并推动全固态激光雷达和光学接收机的发展。 本项目建立在项目负责人此前已验证的波束赋形OPA架构基础之上，因此具有良好的技术可行性。前期研究已经验证了短长度TFLN调制器的线性电光响应特性，并开发了一种结合Adam优化算法与粒子群优化（Particle Swarm Optimization, PSO）的混合优化方法，用于提升VST波束赋形性能，在降低系统复杂度和光学损耗的同时实现了更高的旁瓣抑制能力。此外，项目团队已分别完成经典和量子调频连续波（Frequency-Modulated Continuous-Wave, FMCW）激光雷达系统的搭建与实验验证，为后续接收型OPA研究提供了扎实的实验基础，也进一步验证了本项目整体技术路线的可行性与成熟度。

11314826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11314826.value: 關聯無限層鎳氧化物中磁性與超導態的量子調控設計

11314826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11314826.value: The emergence of superconductivity in infinite-layer (IL) nickelates has reignited fundamental questions regarding the nature of correlated electrons and high‑temperature superconductivity. These nickelates host NiO2 planes analogous to those in cuprates but embed itinerant rare-earth 5d bands, producing a complex multiband environment where magnetism, orbital physics, and superconductivity compete. Through precise epitaxial growth and topochemical tuning, unprecedented control over the valence, dimensionality, and magnetism of the NiO2 planes has become possible. This project aims to establish quantum-design principles governing the coexistence and interaction between magnetic and superconducting states in correlated infinite-layer nickelates. Three tightly connected aims are pursued: (1) controlling lattice dimensionality and A-site chemistry to enhance the pairing strength and stabilise new quantum phases; (2) investigating magnetism-superconductivity interplay via rare-earth-driven exchange coupling and high-field re-entrant phases; and (3) mapping the complete electron-hole-doped phase diagram to identify mechanisms of correlation-driven superconductivity. Combining epitaxial thin-film synthesis, high-field transport, synchrotron spectroscopy, and ab initio theory, this work will illuminate the microscopic interactions underpinning superconductivity and magnetism, while strengthening Hong Kong’s international profile in quantum oxide research. 無限層（infinite-layer, IL）鎳氧化物中超導性的出現，再次引發了對關聯電子本質及高溫超導機制等基本問題的廣泛關注。此類鎳氧化物具有與銅氧化物相似的 NiO2 平面，但同時含有具巡遊特性的稀土 5d 能帶，因而形成一個磁性、軌道物理與超導彼此競爭的複雜多能帶系統。隨着精準外延生長及拓撲化學調控技術的發展，現時已可前所未有地精確控制 NiO2 平面的價態、維度性及磁性。 本項目旨在建立支配關聯無限層鎳氧化物中磁性態與超導態之共存及相互作用的量子調控設計原則。研究將圍繞三個緊密相關的目標展開：（1）透過調控晶格維度性及 A 位化學組成，以增強電子配對強度並穩定新的量子相；（2）利用稀土驅動的交換耦合及高磁場再入相，探討磁性與超導之間的相互作用；以及（3）繪製完整的電子摻雜與空穴摻雜相圖，以辨識關聯驅動超導的機制。結合外延薄膜製備、高磁場輸運量測、同步輻射能譜及第一性原理理論研究，本工作將闡明支撐超導與磁性的微觀交互作用，並進一步提升香港於量子氧化物研究領域的國際影響力。

11500126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11500126.value: Existing research on perishable inventory control typically assumes deterministic issuance rules such as first-in–first-out (FIFO) or last-in–first-out (LIFO), yet growing empirical evidence shows that customers’ freshness preferences and shelf-access costs generate stochastic, heterogeneous purchase patterns that these rules cannot explain. This gap limits both the fidelity of performance evaluation and the effectiveness of inventory policies. We propose a flexible framework that models issuance via a Markov chain choice process over remaining lifetimes, capturing probabilistic substitution across ages and balking. The framework subsumes standard issuance policies (e.g., FIFO, LIFO, and multi-class FIFO) while accommodating realistic behaviors observed in practice. Within this framework, we study the inventory management problem for a periodic-review, lost-sales perishable inventory system. To address the intractability of the dynamic program, we adopt a virtual-product perspective in which each age is treated as a distinct product. This recasts perishable inventory control as a joint inventory-and-assortment optimization problem, enabling us to leverage results from the assortment planning literature. Starting from a fluid approximation, we aim to design implementable policies with provable performance guarantees. We will develop algorithms centered on revenue-ordered assortments and constant-order replenishment, with goals of establishing asymptotic optimality under multinomial logit choice and near-optimality under general Markov chain choice. Using real data, we will evaluate the empirical validity of the modeling framework and develop estimation methods for the choice model. In particular, we will exploit structural patterns in the transition matrix suggested by observed behavior (e.g., sparsity, monotonicity) to improve identifiability, robustness, and sample efficiency. We will also refine guarantees for important special cases (e.g., FIFO, LIFO, and threshold-type rules). Finally, we will extend the framework to more general settings, including positive lead times and joint pricing–inventory decisions. This project develops a unified, data-driven framework that captures realistic issuance behavior in perishable systems and yields implementable, theoretically grounded policies. By integrating a virtual-product formulation, tractable fluid approximations, and structure-exploiting estimation, we aim to close the gap between observed customer behavior and prevailing models. The anticipated outcome is a scalable toolkit—with rigorous performance guarantees and clear implementation guidance—that improves service levels and reduces waste in perishable operations, and equips researchers and practitioners to model, estimate, and optimize perishable inventory systems with realistic customer behavior. 現有關於易腐性存貨控制的研究通常假設確定性的發放規則，例如先進先出（first-in–first-out, FIFO）或後進先出（last-in–first-out, LIFO）；然而，越來越多的實證證據顯示，顧客對新鮮度的偏好以及貨架取用成本會產生隨機且異質的購買模式，而這些模式無法由上述規則加以解釋。此一落差限制了績效評估的真實性，也削弱了存貨政策的有效性。我們提出一個彈性架構，透過剩餘保存期限上的馬可夫鏈選擇過程來建模發放行為，以捕捉不同年齡商品之間的機率性替代以及顧客放棄購買的情形。此架構涵蓋標準發放政策（例如 FIFO、LIFO 與多類別 FIFO），同時也能容納實務中觀察到的真實行為。 在此架構下，我們研究週期性盤點、銷售損失型易腐性存貨系統中的存貨管理問題。為處理動態規劃的難解性，我們採用虛擬產品的觀點，將每一個年齡的商品視為一種不同產品。此做法將易腐性存貨控制重新表述為聯合存貨與品類組合最佳化問題，使我們能夠運用來自品類組合規劃文獻的相關成果。從流體近似出發，我們的目標是設計具有可證明績效保證且可實施的政策。我們將開發以收益排序品類組合與固定訂購量補貨為核心的演算法，目標是在多項羅吉特選擇模型下建立漸近最適性，並在一般馬可夫鏈選擇模型下建立近似最適性。我們將利用真實資料評估此建模架構的實證有效性，並為該選擇模型發展估計方法。特別地，我們將利用觀察行為所揭示的轉移矩陣結構模式（例如稀疏性、單調性）來提升可識別性、穩健性與樣本效率。我們也將針對重要特殊情況（例如 FIFO、LIFO 與門檻型規則）進一步精煉績效保證。最後，我們將把此架構延伸至更一般的情境，包括正前置時間以及聯合定價與存貨決策。 本計畫發展一個統一且資料驅動的架構，用以捕捉易腐性系統中的真實發放行為，並產生可實施且具理論基礎的政策。透過整合虛擬產品表述、可處理的流體近似，以及利用結構特性的估計方法，我們旨在弭平觀察到的顧客行為與現行模型之間的落差。預期成果是一套可擴展的工具組，具備嚴謹的績效保證與清楚的實施指引，可提升易腐性營運中的服務水準並降低浪費，同時協助研究人員與實務工作者在具真實顧客行為的情境下，對易腐性存貨系統進行建模、估計與最佳化。

11500426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11500426.value: 公共服务协同生产中的伙伴或敌人：自主智能体的考量、偏好与人工物设计

11500426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11500426.value: Research on the role and implications of artificial intelligence (AI) in the delivery of public services is evolving rapidly, bringing us closer to what experts call ‘zero bureaucracy’ and ‘intelligent government’. While public administrators are still learning how to ‘dance’ with generative AI, augmenting, automating, or collaborating with it, the arrival of agentic AI – or AI agent – is posing new challenges and opportunities for theory development and practice. AI agent – with its abilities to make independent decisions and self-learn to achieve goals without constantly being told what to do – opens a Pandora’s box of its roles, as either partner or enemy, in co-production and co-creation between citizens and government in public service delivery. As autonomous AI agent becomes gradually integrated into public services, questions arise regarding what its features are deemed valuable to citizens as a ‘partner’ in co-production and co-design. Critically, by having AI agent as a partner, can it actually work to co-create value with citizens as suggested in the literature? We seek to understand how autonomous AI agents may play a role as a partner in the co-production and co-design of public services. As an AI agent has unique characteristics, it is timely to evaluate what technical-values attributes are deemed valuable to citizens as they co-produce and co-design. Taking this a step further, and inspired by the premise of design science, we seek to actualize value co-creation by prototyping and evaluating a real autonomous AI system that draws upon attributes that are important to citizens. Using two complementary studies, we will first conduct a pre-registered discrete choice experiment (DCE) with citizens to examine the relative importance of five major technical-values attributes of AI agent and then use in-depth interviews to probe into citizens’ concerns and preferences. Next, we will design an autonomous AI agent for citizens to report problems and offer suggestions to local (district) governments – Hero Citizen App – and evaluate its efficacy using pre- and post-test design and couple it with in-depth interviews. The content of citizens reporting will be analyzed using topic modeling, corpus linguistics, and inductive coding methods. This proposal aims to make a new breakthrough in the substantive theory of digital transformation and co-production in public administration while attempting to actualize value co-creation with the local (district) service ecosystem to inspire new knowledge creation. 数字化转型正在深刻改变公共行政领域。有关人工智能（AI）在公共服务提供中的作用及其影响的研究正快速发展，推动我们向学者所称的“零官僚主义”与“智能政府”迈进。正当公共管理者还在学习如何与生成式人工智能“共舞”，即对其能力进行增强、实现自动化或与之协作之时，代理型人工智能（即“AI智能体”）的出现，又为理论发展与实践探索带来了新的挑战与机遇。 作为生成式人工智能发展的下一浪潮，AI智能体具备自主决策和自我学习以实现目标的能力，无需时刻依赖指令行事。这开启了一个充满变数的局面：在公共服务的提供过程中，当公民与政府开展合作生产与共同创造时，AI智能体究竟是扮演“伙伴”还是“敌人”的角色？随着自主型AI智能体逐渐融入公共服务领域，一个关键问题随之浮现：作为合作生产与共同设计中的“伙伴”，AI智能体的哪些特质被公民视为具有价值？至关重要的是，将AI智能体作为伙伴，是否真能如相关文献所言，实现与公民的价值共创？ 在本提案中，我们寻求理解自主AI智能体如何在公共服务的共同生产与共同设计中发挥合作伙伴的作用。鉴于AI智能体具有独特特性，评估哪些“技术-价值”属性在公民参与共同生产与共同设计时被视为具有价值，显得尤为适时。在此基础上，受设计科学理念的启发，我们力求通过构建原型并评估一个基于公民所重视属性的实际自主式AI系统，来实现价值共创。 本研究包含两个相互补充的子研究。首先，我们将开展一项预注册的离散选择实验（DCE），考察AI智能体五项主要技术—价值属性对公民选择偏好的相对重要性，并结合深度访谈深入探究公民的关注点与偏好。随后，我们将设计一款名为“英雄市民应用（Hero Citizen App）”的自主型AI代理，供市民向地方（区级）政府报告问题并提出建议，并采用前测—后测研究设计结合深度访谈，对其应用效果进行评估。此外，我们将运用主题建模、语料库语言学及归纳编码等方法，对市民提交的报告内容进行分析。 本提案旨在实现公共行政领域关于数字化转型与协同生产的实质性理论突破，同时力求在地方（区级）服务生态系统中实现价值共创，从而激发新知识的创造。

11500626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11500626.value: Federated learning (FL) is a decentralized machine learning paradigm in which multiple clients collaboratively train a global model without sharing raw data. It is widely applied in privacy-sensitive domains such as healthcare, finance, and mobile applications. However, standard FL models often assume that all data come from the same unknown distribution. In practice, this assumption often fails as decentralized data frequently exhibit heterogeneity. To address this issue, robust FL has been proposed to optimize the worst-case performance across clients, which provides robustness against extreme cases but often results in conservative solutions. On the other hand, for many applications in operations research, decisions are made sequentially over time. Federated Reinforcement Learning (FRL) extends FL to this setting by allowing multiple agents to collaboratively learn the optimal policies. However, differences in client environments, such as variations in system dynamics, pose challenges in learning a global policy that performs well in all clients. Recent approaches, such as agnostic FRL, try to improve performance across diverse clients, but often ignore distributional uncertainty of environments, which is important for adversarial or unknown conditions. To address these limitations, we propose to apply distributionally robust optimization (DRO) to federated learning and federated reinforcement learning. Our goal is to account for both data heterogeneity and distributional ambiguity between clients in decentralized settings. We aim to focus on three main tasks. First, we aim to develop the mathematical foundations of distributionally robust federated learning (DRFL) and design efficient and scalable algorithms with provable convergence guarantees. Second, we extend DRFL to handle sequential decision-making under uncertainty and propose a distributionally robust federated reinforcement learning (DRFRL) framework. We will develop efficient algorithms for solving DRFRL. Third, we will validate the proposed frameworks through case studies in domains such as transportation and inventory management, highlighting its advantages over existing FL methods in the presence of data ambiguity. By directly addressing distributional uncertainty, this work aims to advance robust federated learning and reinforcement learning. In addition, we aim to provide open-source implementations of our algorithms, thereby facilitating their adoption by researchers and practitioners. 聯邦學習是一種去中心化的機器學習範式，其中多個客戶端在不共享原始數據的情況下協作訓練一個全局模型。此方法廣泛應用於醫療、金融及移動應用等對隱私敏感的領域。然而，標準聯邦學習模型通常假設所有數據均來自相同的未知分佈。在實際應用中，這一假設往往並不成立，因為去中心化數據經常呈現異質性。為解決此問題，穩健聯邦學習被提出，旨在優化各客戶端之間的最差情況表現，從而提供對極端情況的穩健性，但這往往導致過於保守的解。 另一方面，在許多運籌學應用中，決策是隨時間依序作出的。聯邦強化學習將聯邦學習擴展至此類場景，讓多個代理能夠協作學習最優策略。然而，客戶端環境之間的差異，例如系統動態的變化，對學習一個能在所有客戶端均表現良好的全局策略構成挑戰。近期方法，例如無知型聯邦強化學習，嘗試提升在多樣化客戶端上的表現，但往往忽略了環境的分佈不確定性，而這對於對抗性或未知條件而言至關重要。 為解決上述限制，我們建議將分佈穩健優化應用於聯邦學習及聯邦強化學習。我們的目標是在去中心化環境中，同時考慮客戶端之間的數據異質性與分佈模糊性。 我們的研究將集中於三項主要任務。第一，我們旨在建立分佈穩健聯邦學習(DRFL)的數學基礎，並設計具備可證明收斂保證的高效且可擴展算法。第二，我們將把DRFL擴展至處理不確定性下的序貫決策問題，並提出分佈穩健聯邦強化學習(DRFRL)框架，同時開發用於求解DRFRL的高效算法。第三，我們將透過交通運輸及庫存管理等領域的案例研究，驗證所提出框架的有效性，並突顯其在數據模糊性存在下相對於現有聯邦學習方法的優勢。 透過直接處理分佈不確定性，本研究旨在推進穩健聯邦學習及強化學習的發展。此外，我們亦計劃提供算法的開源實現，以促進其被研究人員及業界從業者採納。

11500826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11500826.value: 運用預訓練神經網路解析視覺複雜性及其對行為的影響

11500826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11500826.value: Artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms based on deep neural networks (DNNs) have evolved from excelling at specialized tasks such as classification and prediction to demonstrating a deeper, more abstract understanding of unstructured data, including images and videos. These models are now capable of generating human-like responses. Notably, DNNs increasingly resemble lower-level brain functions, as they are explicitly designed to mimic certain aspects of the human brain. Recent neuroscience studies have linked pre-trained DNNs to brain activity, revealing strong correlations between the hierarchical representations of DNN layers and stagewise activations in the human brain. This convergence presents an exciting opportunity to enhance our theoretical understanding of visual cognition by leveraging DNN layers to simulate brain activity triggered by visual stimuli (e.g., images). This project focuses on visual complexity and investigates the potential of pre-trained DNN-powered data augmentation for theory development. Specifically, we use the layered attention matrices of transformer-based models to approximate the visual complexity that emerges during stagewise brain activation in image-based cognition. We then examine how this complexity impacts downstream user behavior. Our approach builds on the assumption—supported by recent neuroscience research—that general-purpose pre-trained vision AI models (e.g., CLIP) encode cognition-relevant representations of hierarchical visual cognition features. The project conducts empirical studies in two contexts. First, we examine social media platforms like Instagram, where images are central to user engagement. While existing research has investigated image features in driving engagement, we propose Hierarchical Attention Entropies (HAEs) to simulate hierarchical visual complexity by analyzing attention entropy across different transformer layers. This study aims to uncover how distinct levels of complexity influence user behavior, such as engagement metrics. Second, we extend these insights to the financial domain by exploring the role of HAEs in investors’ interpretation of stock price movement charts (K-charts). We analyze how HAEs influence stock returns and use additional techniques, such as LASSO regression or CNNs, to extract and predict cognition-relevant features from chart data. This project makes two significant contributions. First, it advances theory discovery by leveraging DNN-powered data augmentation, utilizing attention layers in pre-trained neural networks to approximate brain activity and predict downstream behavior. Second, it enhances the understanding of visual complexity by decomposing it into distinct cognitive layers, providing new insights into how varying levels of complexity relate to user behavior. These contributions advance research in Information Systems (IS), Marketing, and Finance while offering actionable insights for visual content optimization. 基于深度神经网络（DNNs）的人工智能（AI）算法已经从精于分类和预测等专门任务，发展到能够对图像和视频等非结构化数据展现出更深层次、更抽象的理解。这些模型现在能够生成类人的反应。值得注意的是，DNNs被明确设计用于模仿人脑的某些方面，因此其功能日益接近于低层次的脑功能。近期的神经科学研究已将预训练的DNNs与大脑活动联系起来，揭示了DNN各层级的层次化表征与人脑在认知过程中的阶段性激活之间存在强相关性。这种趋同为我们提供了一个激动人心的机会：通过利用DNN的层级结构来模拟由视觉刺激（如图像）引发的大脑活动，从而加深我们对视觉认知的理论理解。 本项目聚焦于视觉复杂性，并探究利用预训练DNN驱动的数据增强在理论构建方面的潜力。具体而言，我们采用基于Transformer模型的层级注意力矩阵，来近似模拟在基于图像的认知过程中，大脑阶段性激活所产生的视觉复杂性。随后，我们检验这种复杂性如何影响下游的用户行为。我们的方法基于一个得到近期神经科学研究支持的假设：即通用预训练视觉AI模型（例如CLIP）编码了与认知相关的、具有层次化结构的视觉认知特征。 本项目在两个情境下展开实证研究。首先，我们考察了像Instagram这样以图像为用户参与核心的社交媒体平台。尽管现有研究已探讨了图像特征在驱动用户参与度方面的作用，我们提出“层次化注意力熵”（Hierarchical Attention Entropies, HAEs）的概念，通过分析不同Transformer层级的注意力熵来模拟层次化的视觉复杂性。本研究旨在揭示不同层级的复杂性如何影响用户行为（如参与度指标）。其次，我们将这些见解延伸至金融领域，探索HAEs在投资者解读股价走势图（K线图）过程中的作用。我们分析HAEs如何影响股票回报率，并运用LASSO回归或卷积神经网络（CNNs）等额外技术，从图表数据中提取并预测与认知相关的特征。 本项目有两项重要贡献。首先，它通过利用DNN驱动的数据增强推动了理论发现，即运用预训练神经网络中的注意力层来近似模拟大脑活动，并预测下游行为。其次，它通过将视觉复杂性分解为不同的认知层面，加深了我们对这一概念的理解，为不同层级的复杂性如何与用户行为相关联提供了新的见解。这些贡献不仅推动了信息系统、市场营销和金融领域的研究，也为视觉内容的优化提供了切实的指导。

11501126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11501126.value: 面向大數據的非線性函數對函數幾何分位數迴歸

11501126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11501126.value: Advances in data acquisition have enabled the widespread use of large-scale functional data across fields. In the big data era, functional datasets bring both opportunities and challenges. Being infinite-dimensional, functional data are more complex to analyze than scalar data, with storage and computational demands often exceeding a single machine’s capacity. These challenges reveal the limitations of traditional statistical methods and the need for new frameworks. Functional Data Analysis (FDA) addresses these issues, with Function-on-Function (FoF) regression, modeling both response and covariates as functional data, proving highly versatile. However, FoF regression remains underexplored due to the computational complexity of infinite-dimensional predictors and responses. Most existing methods focus on conditional mean estimation, while attempts at FoF quantile regression rely on pointwise modeling, overlooking the geometric structure of functional data and key concepts like conditional distribution functions and quantile intervals. Furthermore, most work is restricted to linear models, limiting the ability to capture nonlinear relationships. Practical applications are also constrained by the high computational demands of large-scale datasets. This project has two main goals. First, we aim to develop a systematic framework for nonlinear FoF quantile regression using M-quantiles (including geometric quantiles) in infinite-dimensional spaces. This framework generalizes univariate quantile regression, enabling the modeling of complex nonlinear relationships while retaining key properties of conditional quantiles. The Principal Investigator (P.I.) and Co-Investigator (Co-I.) have already conducted preliminary investigations, focusing on geometric quantiles, with plans to expand to the broader M-quantile framework, encompassing both geometric quantiles and expectiles. Additional planned work includes developing a data-driven criterion for selecting truncation orders in the Karhunen-Loève expansion, adapting estimation procedures for discretely observed data, and integrating neural operators to flexibly model nonlinear relationships. Second, to address the computational challenges associated with large-scale functional data, we will extend this framework to a distributed computing setting. The P.I. and Co-I. have proposed a tentative distributed computing algorithm for estimating the basis functions. Building on this foundation, we will thoroughly examine its theoretical properties and associated statistical inference aspects, refine the algorithm to ensure that the resulting estimator attains efficiency comparable to the global estimator, develop communication-efficient techniques, and design iterative methods to improve both scalability and computational efficiency. The requested funding will primarily be used to hire a research assistant to conduct essential empirical analyses for the project, and supporting a postgraduate research student to explore specific research questions within the project. 資料蒐集技術的進步，使大規模函數型資料在各個領域中得到廣泛應用。在大數據時代，函數型資料集同時帶來機遇與挑戰。由於函數型資料具有無限維度，其分析較純量資料更為複雜，而儲存及計算需求往往超出單一電腦的處理能力。這些挑戰揭示了傳統統計方法的局限性，並突顯了發展新框架的需要。 函數型資料分析（Functional Data Analysis, FDA）正是為應對這些問題而發展。其中，函數對函數（Function-on-Function, FoF）迴歸將反應變數與共變數均建模為函數型資料，展現出高度的靈活性。然而，由於無限維預測變數與反應變數所帶來的計算複雜性，FoF 迴歸仍未得到充分探索。現有大多數方法主要集中於條件平均數估計，而有關 FoF 分位數迴歸的研究則多依賴逐點建模，忽略了函數型資料的幾何結構，以及條件分佈函數和分位數區間等關鍵概念。此外，大部分研究仍局限於線性模型，限制了其捕捉非線性關係的能力。在實際應用中，大規模資料集的高計算需求亦進一步限制了相關方法的使用。 本項目有兩個主要目標。首先，我們旨在於無限維空間中，利用 M-分位數（包括幾何分位數）發展一套系統性的非線性 FoF 分位數迴歸框架。該框架將單變量分位數迴歸加以推廣，使其能夠刻畫複雜的非線性關係，同時保留條件分位數的重要性質。首席研究員（P.I.）及共同研究員（Co-I.）已開展初步研究，重點聚焦於幾何分位數，並計劃進一步擴展至更廣義的 M-分位數框架，涵蓋幾何分位數及 expectiles。後續計劃亦包括：為 Karhunen–Loève 展開中的截斷階數選擇制定資料驅動準則；調整估計程序以處理離散觀測資料；以及結合神經算子，以更靈活地建模非線性關係。 其次，為應對大規模函數型資料所帶來的計算挑戰，我們將把此框架擴展至分佈式計算環境。首席研究員及共同研究員已提出一項初步的分佈式計算演算法，用於估計基底函數。在此基礎上，我們將全面研究其理論性質及相關統計推斷問題，改進該演算法，以確保所得估計量能達到與全域估計量相若的效率，並發展具通訊效率的技術，以及設計迭代方法，以提升可擴展性及計算效率。 所申請的資助將主要用於聘請一名研究助理，以進行本項目所需的關鍵實證分析；同時亦將支援一名研究生，探索本項目內的特定研究問題。

11501426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11501426.value: 無形資本市場中的策略性授權與市場力量

11501426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11501426.value: Patents grant inventors temporary exclusive rights over their technologies in exchange for disclosure, thereby encouraging innovation and knowledge diffusion. The conventional view holds that innovation thrives when firms compete for these patent rents and benefit from technology spillovers. Yet, the same exclusivity can also suppress innovation if holders of foundational patents use them to block or delay follow-on developments—resulting in technological “hold-ups” and costly litigation. Although patent licensing theoretically alleviates such inefficiencies by allowing access to protected technologies, little empirical evidence exists on how licensing transactions reshape market power in the market for intangible capital. This project investigates how patent licensing affects competition and innovation incentives. Using transaction-level data on patent licenses, I test whether licensing serves not merely as a channel for technology transfer but also as a strategic tool to deter rivals’ innovation. Specifically, I hypothesize that licensors strategically license more frequently, or at lower royalty rates, to firms that pose greater competitive threats—thereby discouraging these potential entrants from developing competing technologies and locking them into dependent innovation paths. Such behavior reflects a subtle but potent form of market power operating through control of core intellectual property. To test this mechanism, I will construct a novel dataset combining detailed information on patent licensing contracts (licensors, licensees, royalty terms) with firm-level data on financials, patent portfolios, and R&D outcomes. The empirical analysis will assess whether licensing intensity and pricing vary systematically with indicators of competitive threat—such as technological overlap, product-market proximity, or entry potential. Finding that licensors grant more favorable licensing terms to close competitors would provide evidence consistent with strategic deterrence models of innovation. The project proceeds in three stages. First, I estimate the elasticity of licensing activity and royalty rates with respect to competition metrics. Second, I attempt to establish causality through an identification strategy using plausibly exogenous variation in competitive threats. Finally, I will analyze post-transaction outcomes on licensor-licensee pairs to assess the broader implications for corporate innovation and firm value. This research offers the first large-scale empirical evidence on strategic licensing as a source of market power in intangible assets. The findings will contribute to the academic literatures on industrial organization, innovation economics, and finance, and inform policy debates on antitrust and intellectual property governance in the knowledge economy. 專利制度透過賦予發明人對其技術在一定期間內的專有權，以換取技術公開，從而鼓勵創新與知識擴散。傳統觀點認為，當企業競相爭取專利所帶來的經濟租值，並從技術外溢中受益時，創新活動便會更加蓬勃。然而，同樣的專有權也可能抑制創新：若基礎性專利的持有人利用其權利阻礙或延後後續創新，便可能造成技術上的「挾持」（hold-ups）以及高昂的訴訟成本。理論上，專利授權可透過允許其他企業使用受保護技術，減輕上述低效率問題；然而，目前對於授權交易如何重塑無形資本市場中的市場力量，仍缺乏實證證據。 本研究計畫探討專利授權如何影響競爭與創新激勵。我將利用專利授權交易層級的資料，檢驗授權是否不僅是技術移轉的管道，同時也是企業用以遏制競爭對手創新的策略工具。具體而言，我提出以下假說：面對構成較大競爭威脅的企業，授權方會策略性地更頻繁地提供授權，或給予較低的權利金費率，藉此降低這些潛在進入者自行開發競爭性技術的激勵，並使其鎖定於依賴既有核心技術的創新路徑。這種行為反映了一種較為隱晦但影響深遠的市場力量，其根源在於企業對核心智慧財產權的控制。 為檢驗此機制，我將建立一套新的資料庫，結合詳細的專利授權合約資料（包括授權方、被授權方及權利金條款），以及公司層級的財務資料、專利組合與研發成果。實證分析將評估授權強度與授權定價，是否會隨競爭威脅指標而系統性地變化，例如技術重疊程度、產品市場接近程度，以及潛在進入能力。若研究發現授權方會向關係密切的競爭者提供更優惠的授權條件，將構成與創新策略性遏制模型一致的實證證據。 本研究計畫分為三個階段。首先，我將估計授權活動與權利金費率相對於各項競爭指標的彈性。其次，我將利用競爭威脅中具合理外生性的變異，設計識別策略，以嘗試建立因果關係。最後，我將分析授權交易完成後授權方與被授權方配對層級的結果，以評估其對企業創新與公司價值所帶來的更廣泛影響。 本研究將首次提供大規模實證證據，檢視策略性專利授權如何成為企業在無形資產市場中運用市場力量的來源。研究結果將對產業組織、創新經濟學及金融學等學術文獻作出貢獻，並為知識經濟下有關反壟斷政策與智慧財產權治理的政策討論提供實證依據。

11501726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11501726.value: 动态互补性量化的新方向

11501726.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11501726.value: Prof Chen, Xiaohong Prof Zhou, Kang

11501726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11501726.value: A growing literature documents that skill investment at younger ages generates persistent impacts on later stages of skill development. This finding is based on a fundamental concept in the technology of skill formation: the existence of dynamic complementarity between skill stock and skill investment at different stages. However, current studies often either assume the existence of dynamic complementarity or test it within unique randomized control trial (RCT) settings. This project will develop state-of-the-art nonparametric methods to test this complementarity relationship. Simultaneously, we will provide a novel estimation strategy to quantify the magnitude of dynamic complementarity without imposing normalization across different developmental stages. Furthermore, our proposed framework will enable the evaluation of various policies designed to boost children's skill development at different ages through diverse investment types, thus identifying the most cost-effective policies for enhancing children's skill development and household welfare. 近期的文献认为，对儿童早期的技能投资会对后续技能发展阶段产生持久影响。这一发现基于技能形成技术中的一个基本概念，即不同阶段技能与技能投资之间存在动态互补性。然而，当前研究或者假定动态互补性的存在，或者仅在独特的随机对照试验情境下对动态互补的存在性进行检验。本项目将研究前沿的非参数方法来检验这种互补关系。同时，我们将提供一种新的估计策略，以量化动态互补性的大小，而无需对不同发展阶段的技能测量进行标准化处理。此外，我们提出的框架将能够评估旨在通过不同投资类型促进儿童在不同年龄段技能发展的各类政策，从而识别出最能有效提升儿童技能发展和家庭福利的成本效益最优政策。

11502326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11502326.value: 竞价揽储：美国存款拍卖中的流动性管理与窗口粉饰

11502326.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11502326.value: Prof Williams, Christopher Prof Xue, Weizhi Prof Yin, Xiang

11502326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11502326.value: Since 1999, certain U.S. banks have paid significant premiums in government-run auctions to secure large, short-term deposits. Using a unique hand-collected dataset, we investigate the strategic motives and consequences behind this behavior. We find that bidding strategies are driven by market structure, liquidity management, and window-dressing needs. Banks in more competitive environments bid more aggressively. Furthermore, bidding intensity increases when banks have lower cash reserves. Moreover, banks bid more aggressively as regulatory reporting dates approach. While winning an auction successfully attracts subsequent uninsured deposits, these expensive auction deposits are not retained long after maturity. To offset the high cost of paying deposit premiums, banks temporarily raise rates on loans and interest-bearing cash. Our findings show that deposit premiums are determined not only by fundamental risk but also by transient strategic objectives, shedding new light on bank funding strategies and the information content of deposit rates. 自1999年以来，部分美国银行通过在政府组织的存款拍卖中支付高额溢价，以获取大额短期存款。本文利用独特的手工收集数据，考察这一行为背后的战略动机及其经济后果。研究发现，银行的竞价策略受到市场结构、流动性管理和窗口粉饰需求的共同驱动。在竞争更为激烈的市场环境中，银行的竞价行为更加积极。此外，当银行的现金储备较低时，其竞价强度会有所上升；随着监管报告日临近，银行也会提高竞价积极性。尽管赢得拍卖能够成功吸引后续的非保险存款流入，但这些成本高昂的拍卖存款在到期后并不会被长期留存。为抵消支付存款溢价所产生的高昂成本，银行会暂时提高贷款和生息现金资产的利率。本文的研究结果表明，存款溢价不仅取决于基本面风险，也受到短期战略目标的影响，从而为理解银行的融资策略以及存款利率所包含的信息提供了新的视角。

11502426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11502426.value: 激進型沽空者是否操縱市場？全球證據與反事實基準

11502426.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11502426.value: Prof Stice-Lawrence, Lorien Prof Zhao, Wuyang

11502426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11502426.value: Activist short sellers are influential information intermediaries who release reports on firms they view as fraudulent, mismanaged, or overvalued. Evidence shows they surface problems ahead of analysts, auditors, and regulators; their disclosures improve price discovery, curb excessive optimism, and strengthen governance. Yet reports can trigger sharp price drops, fueling allegations of short-and-distort. A central claim is that 30–50% of targets exhibit V-shaped recoveries—an initial plunge followed by a rebound to pre-report levels—interpreted manipulation and used to justify investigations and tighter rules. These responses have threatened the survival of high-profile activists (e.g., Andrew Left scaling down; Jim Chanos shutting his fund). Two foundational gaps motivate this project. First, we lack evidence on the prevalence of V-shapes in campaigns by prominent activists—the group with the greatest market impact and strong incentives to preserve credibility—since existing evidence largely reflects smaller, lesser-known authors (e.g., pseudonymous Seeking Alpha writers). Second, even if common, V-shapes do not by themselves prove manipulation: good-faith errors and managerial corrective actions can produce rebounds. Hence raw V-shape frequencies are uninterpretable without counterfactuals showing how often reversals occur absent misinformation. We ask: (RQ1) How common are V-shapes after prominent activists’ reports compared with smaller activists? (RQ2) What is a normal V-shape and how can we separate natural reversals from manipulation? (RQ3) Do institutional environments shape V-shape incidence, or is it uniform? For RQ1, we analyze 1,756 campaigns by prominent activists from Activist Shorts Research and Breakout Point, benchmarking against a hand-collected Seeking Alpha sample. A pilot shows 23–38% for prominent activists—about half the rate for smaller activists—yet without a benchmark we cannot infer manipulation. We therefore build three benchmarks: (1) EU net short disclosures, which identify large shorts without public reports and thus without a misinformation channel; (2) U.S. 13F put positions (following Stice-Lawrence et al., 2025), capturing synthetic shorts by investors, again without public reports; and (3) pump-and-dump, a manipulation-heavy setting that provides an upper bound for reversal patterns. We add cross-country tests using a short-selling enforcement index and a regulatory shock: Hong Kong’s October 2016 sanction of Citron Research. Contributions: (1) the first large-sample evidence on V-shapes for prominent activists; (2) the first large-sample counterfactuals for non-manipulative V-shapes; (3) policy guidance to calibrate enforcement to actual risk; and (4) Hong Kong–specific insights via shock and cross-market benchmarks. 激進型沽空者是重要的資訊中介，專門針對其認為涉及欺詐、管理不善或估值過高的企業發布報告。研究顯示，他們往往早於分析師、核數師及監管機構揭露問題，有助促進價格發現、抑制過度樂觀情緒及改善公司治理。然而，報告亦可能引發股價急跌，因而招致「先沽空、後散布失實資訊」（short-and-distort）的指控。 一項核心論點指出，30%至50%的被狙擊企業會出現V形反彈，即股價先急跌，隨後回升至報告發布前水平。這種走勢常被視為市場操縱的證據，並成為調查及收緊監管的理據。相關壓力已威脅知名沽空者的生存，例如Andrew Left縮減業務，以及Jim Chanos關閉基金。 本研究針對兩項缺口。第一，現有證據主要來自規模較小、知名度較低的作者，例如Seeking Alpha的匿名撰稿人；目前仍缺乏知名激進型沽空者的V形反彈數據。這些沽空者市場影響較大，亦更有誘因維護信譽。第二，V形反彈本身並不能證明操縱，因為善意的判斷錯誤或管理層的糾正措施亦可促成股價回升。因此，必須建立反事實基準，衡量不存在失實資訊時價格逆轉的正常頻率。 本研究探討三個問題： （RQ1）與規模較小的激進型沽空者相比，知名激進型沽空者發布報告後出現V形反彈的情況有多普遍？ （RQ2）何謂「正常」的V形反彈？我們應如何區分自然發生的價格逆轉與市場操縱？ （RQ3）制度環境是否會影響V形反彈的發生率，抑或這種現象在不同制度環境下大致一致？ 針對RQ1，我們分析Activist Shorts Research及Breakout Point收錄的1,756宗知名沽空者行動，並與人工蒐集的Seeking Alpha樣本比較。初步結果顯示，知名沽空者的V形反彈比例為23%至38%，約為較小型沽空者的一半，但缺乏基準仍無法判斷是否涉及操縱。 因此，我們將建立三項比較基準： 1. 歐盟的淨短倉披露資料。這些資料能識別大型短倉，但相關投資者並未公開發布報告，因此不存在透過公開報告散布失實資訊的渠道。 2. 美國13F申報中的認沽期權持倉。依循Stice-Lawrence等人（2025）的研究方法，這些資料反映投資者所建立的合成短倉，同樣不涉及公開發布報告。 3.「拉高出貨」（pump-and-dump）事件。這是市場操縱程度較高的情境，可為價格逆轉模式提供一個上限基準。 我們亦會加入跨國分析，使用沽空執法指數，並研究一項監管衝擊事件，即香港於2016年10月對Citron Research作出的制裁。 本研究的貢獻包括： 1. 首次就知名激進型沽空者報告發布後的V形反彈提供大樣本證據； 2. 首次建立有關非操縱性V形反彈的大樣本反事實基準； 3. 提供政策指引，使執法力度能夠按照實際風險作出適當調整；以及 4. 透過監管衝擊及跨市場比較基準，提供香港市場特有的研究見解。

11502726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11502726.value: ETF納入互聯互通股票市場 ETF互聯互通對香港和內地股票市場的影響

11502726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11502726.value: ETFs are exchange-traded products that seek to replicate an underlying index. The global ETF market has experienced exceptional growth in the last 20 years. In China, there is also great demand for ETF products, and the country has now overtaken Japan as Asia’s largest ETF market. The popularity of ETFs arises from the advantages they provide in terms of diversification, transparency, cost-effectiveness, and trading convenience. However, some studies also show that ETFs may harm the market quality of constituent stocks. This project will study the effect of the launch of ETF Connect, implemented in 2022. The ETF Connect scheme allows Mainland investors to access Hong Kong-listed ETFs (Southbound trading) and Hong Kong investors to invest in Mainland-listed ETFs (Northbound trading). I will investigate the effect of the launch of ETF Connect on constituent stocks. I propose to examine how trading activities under ETF Connect will affect the liquidity and volatility of constituent stocks, the pricing efficiency of the ETF, and whether the flows under ETF Connect will have any return predictability. The analysis will be performed for both southbound ETF trading (from Mainland investors) and northbound ETF trading (from Hong Kong investors). This project will make an important contribution to the academic literature. While existing literature has extensively studied the effects of ETFs on domestic markets, this study will deepen our understanding of how ETFs function as conduits of financial integration between Hong Kong and Mainland China. This research will provide empirical evidence to help policymakers and regulators assess whether ETF Connect improves liquidity, market efficiency, and stability, supporting the evaluation of the scheme’s effectiveness. ETF是旨在複製標的指數的交易所交易產品。全球ETF市場在過去20年經歷了非凡的成長。在中國，ETF產品的需求也十分旺盛，中國現已超越日本，成為亞洲最大的ETF市場。 ETF的受歡迎程度源自於其在多元化、透明度、成本效益和交易便利性方面的優勢。然而，一些研究也表明，股票ETF可能會損害成分股的市場品質。 本計畫將研究2022年實施的ETF互聯互通的影響。ETF互聯互通讓內地投資者投資香港上市的ETF（南向交易），也允許香港投資者投資內地上市的ETF（北向交易）。我將研究股票ETF互聯互通推出對成分股的影響。我擬研究ETF互聯互通機制下的交易活動將如何影響成分股的流動性與波動性、ETF的定價效率，以及ETF互聯互通的資金流動是否具有任何收益可預測性。分析將分別針對南向ETF交易（來自內地投資者）和北向ETF交易（來自香港投資者）進行。 本計畫將對學術文獻做出重要貢獻。儘管現有文獻已廣泛研究了ETF對內地市場的影響，但本研究將加深我們對ETF如何作為香港與內地金融整合管道的理解。本研究將提供實證證據，幫助政策制定者和監管機構評估ETF互聯互通是否改善了流動性、市場效率和穩定性，從而支持對該機制的有效性評估。

11502926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11502926.value: 基於生物啟發的強化學習及基於概念解釋的多模態深度偽造檢測方法在金融詐欺預防中的應用

11502926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11502926.value: In his 2025 policy address, the Chief Executive of HK stress that the current government will facilitate wide-scale application and development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) across different sectors in the society to boost overall efficiency. However, malicious usage of AI has also led to widespread Deepfake attacks. The HK Business News reports that there is a 1,900% year-on-year increase in Deepfake-related fraud cases in the first quarter of 2025 in HK, and a 209% rise in synthetic identity document fraud in the city. Accordingly, the proposed GRF project aims to strategically aligned with the HKSAR Government’s long-term goal of promoting legitimate AI-enabled innovation in Hong Kong.
