Specifically, the proposed GRF project will develop a novel biologically-inspired deep reinforcement learning method and a generative concept-based explainable AI (XAI) method for multimodal Deepfake detection (e.g., video, audio, image, text) , and hence to prevent financial frauds such as fraudulent loan applications, AI-generated investment scams, forgery financial transactions, etc. Deepfake technology, which leverages Generative AI (GAI) models, has enabled the creation of highly convincing, fake multimodal contents to impersonate individuals, falsify financial documents, and manipulate communications, leading to substantial monetary losses. For instance, CNN reported that a finance worker in Hong Kong had mistakenly paid out HK$200 million after a video call with the firm’s “chief financial officer” deceptively generated by Deepfake technology on 4th Feb. 2024; Deepfake attacks bring significant risks to the business world, particularly for the financial industry. Existing static multimodal Deepfake detection methods are weak in combating rapidly evolving Deepfakes. Not only should the GAI-based detection models identify Deepfakes, but they should also proactively anticipate possible future attack patterns. Above all, existing detection models fail to explain to fraud investigators (e.g., loan managers) why certain identities or financial records are considered fraudulent based on explicit human understandable “concepts” to avoid risky business decisions (e.g., approving a loan for a fake client). Guided by the Design Science (DS) research methodology, the goal of the proposed GRF project is to address the aforementioned research gaps by designing a novel proactive, continual learning, and explainable multimodal Deepfake detection model which is underpinned by neuroplastic deep reinforcement learning and generative concept activation vector discovery and visualization methods. To ensure short/long term business and societal impacts, we plan for technology transfer of our research outcomes (e.g., a prototype system) through our listed industrial collaborator. 香港行政長官在2025年施政報告中強調，本屆政府將推動人工智慧（AI）在社會各領域廣泛應用與發展，以提升整體效率。然而，人工智慧的惡意使用也導致了深度偽造攻擊的氾濫。 《香港商業新聞》報道稱，2025年第一季度，香港與深度偽造相關的詐騙案件同比激增1900%，合成身分文件詐騙案件也增加了209%。因此，擬議的GRF計畫旨在與香港特區政府推動合法人工智慧創新發展的長期目標策略契合。具體而言，擬議的 GRF 項目將開發一種新型的受生物啟發的深度強化學習方法和一種基於生成概念的可解釋人工智能 (XAI) 方法，用於多模態（例如視頻、音頻、圖像和文本）深度偽造檢測，從而防止欺詐性貸款申請、人工智能生成的投資騙局、偽造金融交易等金融欺詐行為。 利用生成式人工智慧（GAI）模型的深度偽造技術，能夠創造高度逼真的虛假多模態內容，用於冒充個人、偽造財務文件和操縱通信，從而造成巨大的經濟損失。例如，CNN報道稱，2024年2月4日，香港一名金融從業人員在與公司「財務長」進行了一次由深度偽造技術生成的視訊通話後，錯誤地支付了2億港元。深度偽造攻擊給商業世界，尤其是金融業，帶來了重大風險。 現有的靜態多模態深度偽造檢測方法難以應對快速演進的深度偽造技術。基於生成式人工智慧的偵測模型不僅能識別深度偽造內容，還應主動預測未來可能的攻擊模式。更重要的是，現有檢測模型無法向欺詐調查人員（例如貸款經理）解釋為何某些身份或財務記錄會被判定為欺詐，而這些判定是基於清晰易懂的“概念”，以避免做出風險較高的商業決策（例如，批准虛假客戶的貸款）。 在設計科學（DS）研究方法的指導下，所提出的GRF計畫旨在透過設計一種新型的、主動的、持續學習的、可解釋的多模態深度偽造檢測模型來彌補上述研究空白。該模型是建基於神經可塑性深度強化學習以及生成式概念活化向量發現和視覺化方法。為確保短期和長期的商業和社會影響，我們計劃透過已上市的工業合作夥伴進行研究成果（例如，原型系統）的技術轉移。

11503026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11503026.value: 审计师专业多面性：跨学科专长带来的劳动力市场回报

11503026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11503026.value: The auditing profession plays a vital role in maintaining trust in capital markets, where the skills of individual auditors are key to ensuring quality audits. Prior research has focused on depth of auditor expertise, such as industry specialization (see Lennox and Wu, 2018). However, there is a significant gap in understanding the role of breadth of expertise, i.e., interdisciplinary knowledge. This study aims to introduce and explore the concept of Auditor Professional Versatility (APV), an individual auditor’s strategic investment in a range of professional credentials beyond the core Certified Public Accountant (CPA) qualification, including certifications in taxation (Certified Tax Agent), valuation (Certified Public Valuer), and legal matters (Certificate of Lawyer Qualification). This study predicts that APV can enhance an individual auditors’ career outcomes through two channels: (1) Enhanced Competence Channel, where the integration of interdisciplinary knowledge improves the effectiveness and efficiency of audits, particularly when dealing with complex engagements; and (2) Strengthened Independence Channel, where greater external marketability reduces the fear of job loss and strengthens auditors’ ability to resist client pressure, especially concerning reputation and litigation risk. We hypothesize that individual auditors with higher APV will experience greater career stability and success, due to their increased value in managing complex engagements and reducing reputational and litigation risks. This study will utilize China’s unique disclosure environment, providing detailed data on individual auditors and their credentials, and examine whether APV has positive effects on individual auditors’ career outcomes. We will test the two channels by analysing auditor competence and auditor independence. We will examine whether the positive effects (if any) of APV vary with depth of auditor expertise, client complexity, litigation risk, audit firm size, and labor market competition. Additionally, we will employ instrumental variable approach, change model, auditor fixed effects model, and propensity score matching to address endogeneity concerns. This research makes several contributions. Conceptually, it introduces APV as a new dimension of auditor human capital and clarifies how interdisciplinary expertise influences career paths. Empirically, it shifts the focus from audit firm- or office-level factors to individual auditors’ characteristics, responding to calls for research on individual auditors (e.g., Hanlon et al. 2022). Practically, the findings are expected to offer valuable insights for audit firms in talent management and professional development, for individual auditors in making strategic career investments, and for regulators interested in market-based mechanisms that enhance audit quality and auditor independence. 审计职业在维护资本市场信任方面发挥着至关重要的作用，而注册会计师个人的专业技能是保障审计质量的核心要素。现有的研究主要聚焦于审计师的专业知识（我们可以称之为专业知识的“深度”），例如审计师的行业专长(Lennox & Wu, 2018), 但对专业知识的“广度”（即审计师跨学科知识）的作用仍存在显著研究空白。本研究引入并且系统探讨“审计师专业多面性”（Auditor Professional Versatility, APV）这一概念，指的是注册会计师个人在核心的注册会计师资格（CPA）之外，对税务（注册税务师资格）、资产评估（注册资产评估师资格）及法律（律师资格）等专业资质进行的战略性投资程度。 我们预测APV可通过两条渠道促进注册会计师的个人职业发展：（1）能力的提升——注册会计师跨学科知识的融合有助于提升审计服务的有效性和效率。这类渠道在处理复杂业务的时候会表现得尤其明显；（2）独立性的强化——更强的外部市场竞争力降低了审计师对失业的顾虑，从而增强其抵御客户压力的能力。这类渠道在面临声誉与诉讼风险的时候尤为重要。据此，我们假设，和具有较低APV的注册会计师比较起来，具有较高APV的注册会计师将会获得更优的职业稳定性与职业成功，主要因为其在管理复杂业务以及降低声誉与诉讼风险方面具有更高的价值。 依托中国独特的信息披露环境（该环境提供了注册会计师个人及其专业资质的详尽数据），本研究将检验APV对注册会计师职业发展结果的积极影响。我们将分别从审计师能力与独立性两条渠道进行机制检验，并考察APV的正向效应是否会因为审计师专业知识深度、客户复杂性、诉讼风险、事务所规模及劳动力市场竞争程度而存在异质性。此外，本研究将综合运用工具变量法、变化模型、审计师固定效应模型及倾向得分匹配等方法，以缓解潜在的内生性问题。 本研究的贡献体现在三个层面。在概念层面，引入APV作为审计师人力资本的新维度，阐明跨学科专长如何塑造职业发展路径；在实证层面，将研究视角从事务所或分所层面下沉至注册会计师个人特征，积极回应了学界对关注审计师个体层面研究的呼吁（如Hanlon et al. 2022）；在实践层面，本研究的结果有望为会计师事务所的人力资源管理与职业发展规划、注册会计师的战略性职业投资，以及致力于利用市场化机制提升审计质量与独立性的监管机构提供有益启示。

11503726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11503726.value: 賦能抑或阻礙人類認知：全球電商場景下 AI 增強型決策的多層次效應

11503726.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11503726.value: Dr Cai, Shaohan Alan Dr Wang, Wei Dr WANG, Xiaoyan Miss ZHOU, YITING

11503726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11503726.value: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs) and intelligent agents, has profoundly reshaped how individuals and firms make strategic decisions. Among all sectors, cross-border e-commerce has become one of the most dynamic and AI-intensive domains. Platforms such as Alibaba International, Amazon, and TikTok Shop increasingly deploy AI-driven tools to assist sellers in product recommendation, trend analysis, translation, and market forecasting. These technologies have significantly improved operational efficiency and global market reach. However, growing reliance on AI has also raised concerns about its long-term effects on human cognition, learning, and independent decision-making. This project aims to examine how AI influences human cognition and learning in the context of cross-border e-commerce decision-making. At the individual level, it explores whether AI serves as a cognitive catalyst that stimulates reasoning and learning, or as a cognitive substitute that encourages cognitive offloading and metacognitive laziness. Overreliance on AI may reduce users’ ability to think critically and reflect on their own decisions, whereas collaborative engagement with AI may strengthen higher-order thinking and adaptive capacity. At the system level, the project investigates whether prolonged human–AI interaction can lead to convergence in cognitive and decision-making patterns across individuals, creating what we term “cognitive convergence.” It further examines whether dynamic system design—such as periodically varying the perceived role of AI—can reactivate reflective thinking and sustain cognitive diversity and adaptability within the system. Methodologically, the project employs a multi-method research design combining a randomized field experiment with a cross-border e-commerce platform (Xingyun), a controlled laboratory experiment using a self-built simulation platform (Glotra), and agent-based modeling (ABM) to capture emergent collective dynamics. These studies jointly trace how individual cognitive processes evolve and aggregate into system-level patterns of convergence and adaptation. By linking micro-level cognition with system-level evolution, this project provides theoretical and practical insights into how AI can be designed to enhance rather than replace human intelligence. The findings will offer guidance for platform developers and policymakers seeking to promote sustainable, human-centered, and cognitively diverse AI ecosystems in the digital economy. 人工智能（AI）的快速發展，尤其是大型語言模型及 AI 智能體的廣泛應用，正在重塑跨境電商中的決策方式。跨境電商平台日益運用 AI 協助商家進行產品選擇、定價及市場分析，以提升決策效率與經營績效。然而，AI 在提升決策效率的同時，也可能促使使用者將更多認知工作交由 AI 完成，導致認知卸載，並降低其主動認知投入、元認知監控及獨立判斷能力。因此，如何設計既能發揮 AI 效率優勢、又能維持人類認知參與的協作模式，已成為人機協作研究及數碼平台治理的重要議題。 本研究聚焦於 AI 定位（AI positioning）如何影響使用者的認知投入與決策質素，以及這些個體層面的影響如何進一步累積為集體層面的決策趨同。在個體層面，本研究比較 AI 被定位為「工具（Tool）」、「夥伴（Partner）」及「顧問（Advisor）」時，使用者在認知卸載、認知資源再投入、元認知監控及決策質素上的差異，並進一步探討不同 AI 輸出方式如何影響上述關係。在集體層面，本研究進一步考察當 AI 輔助決策被廣泛採用時，個體決策模式是否會逐漸趨同，從而降低商家策略及產品選擇的多樣性與整體適應能力。 為檢驗上述跨層面機制，本研究將結合受控平台實驗與田野實驗。受控平台實驗將系統性操弄 AI 定位、輸出方式及 AI 使用程度，以識別 AI 影響個體認知與決策行為的因果機制，並觀察這些行為如何在重複決策及群體互動中形成集體趨同。進一步而言，本研究將與產業合作夥伴開展田野實驗，在真實商業情境中驗證關鍵機制及相應的 AI 協作設計。透過連結個體認知機制與集體決策結果，本研究旨在深化對 AI 輔助決策雙重效應的理解，並為兼顧決策效率、人類認知參與及平台決策多樣性的 AI 協作與治理設計提供實證基礎。

11504226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11504226.value: 駕馭羊群：動態創業投資融資

11504226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11504226.value: Venture capital plays an essential role in financing innovation, acting as the engine for bringing new technologies to market. This financing serves as a critical screening process, deciding which innovations proceed and which do not. This gatekeeping function is challenging. Assessing the potential of a frontier technology requires specialized, costly effort from experts whose knowledge is often dispersed across different fields and experiences. Even with intensive due diligence, outcomes are difficult to forecast; roughly 75% of venture-backed startups fail to return investor capital, and the industry's returns are skewed, driven by a handful of massive successes. This challenge is amplified by the dynamic, sequential nature of the financing process. An entrepreneur must first convince a pioneer investor to undertake a costly evaluation of a venture that may look unattractive. That investor's public decision to fund---or pass---then becomes a signal that influences the beliefs and actions of subsequent investors. This reality raises critical, yet underexplored, questions: How can an entrepreneur, who needs capital from multiple investors, manage this process? How can they design contracts to first induce an early investor's costly screening and then leverage that endorsement to build momentum and attract future capital more efficiently? Existing research is ill-equipped to answer these questions. The security design literature has studied how contracts can incentivize information acquisition, but its focus is largely static. It fails to capture the dynamic reality of how an early investor's decision creates an informational externality. Conversely, the social learning literature explores these dynamic spillovers but typically in decentralized settings where agents learn passively from each other. Neither stream models the entrepreneur as a strategic agent who uses the dynamic choice of contracts to manage investment incentives and the informational environment. This project bridges that gap by developing a dynamic model of security design that incorporates sequential investors, costly information acquisition, and observable funding decisions. Our analysis conjectures a strategy that mirrors the real-world financing lifecycle of startups. We posit it is optimal for the entrepreneur to first offer high-sensitivity securities (e.g., equity) to induce costly due diligence from pioneer investors. If this round succeeds, the entrepreneur then pivots, offering low-sensitivity securities (e.g., debt) to later investors. This second-stage contract capitalizes on the positive reputation built by the first round, leveraging social learning to secure funding. This research provides a new, information-based explanation for the evolution of startup financing, contributing to contract theory, social learning, and security design.

11504426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11504426.value: 高維因子模型中的因子增广Lasso模型平均（FALMA）：理論與應用

11504426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11504426.value: Modern economic analysis and forecasting require managing complex high-dimensional data. The factor model is a core analytical tool that simplifies this challenge by capturing common unobserved forces that drive numerous variables. However, relying on any single model choice—whether it is selecting the number of factors or identifying the relevant idiosyncratic component—is risky and often leads to unstable predictions. This project addresses this issue by developing a novel, high-dimensional Factor-Augmented Lasso Model Averaging (FALMA) framework that systematically combines multiple plausible models, dramatically reducing estimation risk and delivering more stable and accurate predictions. Our preliminary research provides two critical theoretical findings necessary for successful model averaging in high-dimensional settings. First, instead of imposing strong and unrealistic assumptions of perfect model simplicity (exact sparsity), we establish the sufficient conditions that lead to approximate sparsity, providing the theoretical foundation needed to implement the Lasso method. Second, we introduce a critical technical contrast to the traditional Lasso literature. While conventional theory suggests the Lasso estimator converges to the single true parameter value for an optimally selected tuning parameter, we rigorously established that our models, each chosen with a different sub-optimal tuning parameter, converge to distinct pseudo-true values. This crucial finding provides the necessary theoretical justification for combining these different Lasso estimators, forming the foundation of our model averaging approach. Building on these foundational successes, the full project will complete the theoretical and practical development of the FALMA framework. We will first establish the ultimate convergence guarantees using estimated (feasible) factors and idiosyncratic errors, a key step beyond our preliminary work. We will then prove the asymptotic optimality of our weighting scheme. Finally, we will validate the framework's practical value through an important economic application, including the estimation of the stochastic discount factor. By mitigating model selection risk, our methodology will significantly improve the estimation of stochastic discount factor and portfolio construction. 現代經濟分析與預測需要管理複雜的高維數據。因子模型（Factor model）是一項核心分析工具，它透過捕捉驅動眾多變數的共同未觀測力量，簡化了這一挑戰。然而，依賴任何單一模型的選擇——無論是選擇因子數量還是識別相關的特異成分（idiosyncratic component）——都具有風險，且往往導致預測結果不穩定。本項目旨在解決此問題，開發了一種新型的高維「因子增強Lasso模型平均」（Factor-Augmented Lasso Model Averaging, FALMA）框架，該框架系統性地結合了多個合理的模型，從而大幅降低估計風險，並提供更穩定、更準確的預測。 我們的初步研究提供了在高維環境中成功進行模型平均所必需的兩項關鍵理論發現。首先，我們沒有強加完美模型簡化（精確稀疏性, exact sparsity）這種強烈且不切實際的假設，而是建立了導致「近似稀疏性」（approximate sparsity）的充分條件，為實施 Lasso 方法提供了所需的理論基礎。其次，我們對傳統 Lasso 文獻提出了一個關鍵的技術對比。傳統理論認為，對於最佳選擇的調整參數（tuning parameter），Lasso 估計量會收斂到單一的真實參數值；而我們則嚴格證明了，各個使用不同次佳調整參數所選出的模型，會收斂到不同的「偽真實值」（pseudo-true values）。這一關鍵發現為結合這些不同的 Lasso 估計量提供了必需的理論依據，構成了我們模型平均方法的基礎。 在這些奠基性成果的基礎上，整個項目將完成 FALMA 框架的理論與實踐開發。我們首先將利用估計的（可行的）因子和特異誤差來確立最終的收斂保證，這是超越我們初步工作的重要一步。接著，我們將證明我們權重方案的漸近最佳性（asymptotic optimality）。最後，我們將透過一項重要的經濟應用（包括隨機折現因子 [stochastic discount factor] 的估計）來驗證該框架的實際價值。透過減輕模型選擇風險，我們的方法學將顯著改善隨機折現因子的估計與投資組合的構建。

11504626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11504626.value: 遏制按人頭付費醫療計劃中的向上編碼與風險選擇行為：基遏制按人頭付費醫療計劃中的向上編碼與風險選擇行為：基於委託人—代理人的框架分析

11504626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11504626.value: Curbing Upcoding and Risk Selection in Capitation Health Care Programs: A Principal-Agent Framework This study examines a capitation-based healthcare model in which a government entity contracts with private insurers or providers to deliver a defined set of benefits to enrolled individuals. The U.S. Medicare Advantage (MA) program serves as the primary example, offering a rich context for analyzing the design and performance of public-private partnerships in healthcare. Under MA, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) pays private health plans a fixed, risk-adjusted amount per enrollee, transferring financial risk from the government to the insurer. This payment structure incentivizes cost containment but introduces challenges related to incentive alignment and information asymmetry. Three core components define the MA model: (1) Capitation payments, adjusted via the Hierarchical Condition Category (HCC) model based on demographic and diagnostic data; (2) Enrollment mechanisms allowing Medicare beneficiaries to opt into MA plans, which often include additional benefits beyond traditional Medicare; and (3) Care management strategies employed by insurers, including network design, utilization controls such as prior authorizations, and cost-sharing arrangements. These features collectively shape access, quality, and financial outcomes for enrollees. The capitation arrangement creates a classic principal-agent problem. The government, as principal, delegates service delivery to private insurers, who act as agents with superior information about enrollee health and care utilization. This asymmetry gives rise to moral hazard (e.g., upcoding diagnoses to inflate risk levels), and undertreatment risks (e.g., restricting access to costly services). These behaviors can undermine the goals of equitable access and efficient care delivery. To address these challenges, we propose a principal-agent framework that models insurer incentives and identifies mechanisms to realign them with public objectives. By analyzing how payment structures, monitoring tools, and contract design influence agent behavior, the framework offers insights into mitigating inefficiencies and promoting value-based care. The relevance of this framework extends beyond the U.S. context. Hong Kong’s evolving healthcare reforms, particularly its “strategic purchasing” initiatives, reflect similar dynamics. The SAR government is increasingly subsidizing and procuring services from private providers to alleviate pressure on the public system and improve access. These reforms mirror the MA model’s public-private partnership approach and underscore the broader applicability of our analysis. By drawing lessons from MA, this research informs policy design in Hong Kong and other systems seeking to balance cost, quality, and access through innovative contracting with private healthcare entities. 摘要： 本研究探討一種按人頭付費的醫療模式，在該模式下，政府機構與私人保險公司或醫療服務提供者簽訂合約，為已登記的個人提供一套明確界定的醫療福利。美國聯邦醫療保險優勢計劃（Medicare Advantage, MA）作為主要範例，為分析公私營合作夥伴關係在醫療領域中的設計與表現提供了豐富的背景。在MA計劃下，聯邦醫療保險與醫療補助服務中心（CMS）向私人健康計劃支付一筆固定的、經風險調整的人頭費用，將財務風險由政府轉移至保險公司。此支付結構有助於控制成本，但同時引入了與激勵一致性及資訊不對稱相關的挑戰。 MA模式由三個核心要素所定義：（一）按人頭付費款項，透過層級病症分類（HCC）模型，根據人口統計與診斷資料進行調整；（二）登記機制，允許聯邦醫療保險受益人選擇加入MA計劃，該計劃通常提供傳統聯邦醫療保險之外的額外福利；以及（三）保險公司採用的醫療管理策略，包括網絡設計、使用量管控（如事前授權）以及費用分攤安排。這些特徵共同影響了受益人的服務可及性、醫療品質及財務結果。 按人頭付費安排構成了一個典型的委託人—代理人問題。政府作為委託人，將服務交付委託給私人保險公司，而後者作為代理人，對受益人的健康狀況及醫療服務使用情況擁有更充分的資訊。此資訊不對稱導致了道德風險（例如，透過向上編碼診斷來虛增付款）以及治療不足的風險（例如，限制高成本服務的可及性）。這些行為可能削弱公平可及性與高效醫療服務交付的目標。 為應對這些挑戰，我們提出一個委託人—代理人框架，用以模擬保險公司的激勵機制，並識別可使其與公共目標重新一致的機制。透過分析支付結構、監測工具及合約設計如何影響代理人行為，該框架為減少低效率現象並促進價值導向醫療提供了啟示。 此框架的適用範圍超越美國的情境。香港的醫療改革，特別是其「策略性採購」舉措，反映了類似的動態。特區政府正日益增加對私人醫療服務提供者的補貼與採購，以紓緩公共醫療系統的壓力並改善服務可及性。這些改革與MA模式的公私營合作夥伴關係取向相呼應，凸顯了我們分析的廣泛適用性。透過借鑑MA計劃的經驗，本研究可為香港及其他致力於透過與私人醫療機構創新合約來平衡成本、品質與可及性的醫療系統提供政策設計上的參考。

11505326.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11505326.value: Prof Chen, Hui Prof Li, Jun

11505326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11505326.value: Bank loans serve as a critical channel for firms to raise external capital and are typically considered the first resort in debt financing when firms have difficulty accessing public bond markets. However, because loans are issued in private markets and traded between banks with limited liquidity and transparency, their costs are difficult to assess. In this project, we propose to assess bank loan costs, using the cost of bonds traded in public markets as the benchmark. Using a structural credit risk model and market prices of bonds and loans, we construct a novel measure - the loan-bond spread (LBS) - to evaluate the relative pricing between loans and bonds of the same firm. The LBS is the difference between actual loan spreads and bond-implied loan spreads. Intuitively, actual loan spreads reflect how banks trading in private markets view firms' financial conditions, while bond-implied loan spreads reflect how bond investors trading in public markets view the same firms' financial health. A high loan-bond spread indicates that loan prices in private markets are relatively low compared to the same firm's bonds. In our preliminary results, we first confirm that our loan-bond spread adequately captures the relative mispricing between private loans and public bonds. The loan-bond spread positively relates to future loan returns, with a risk-adjusted spread of 4.01% between high- and low-LBS firms. More importantly, we externally validate our measure through managerial financial decisions. We find that the underpricing of loans relative to bonds induces managers to buy back loans, with an estimate of -0.31(t-statistic = -7.66), while actual loan yields have no effect on debt structure adjustment. This contrast demonstrates that managers time the market and arbitrage both loan and bond markets. Taken together, we make four contributions. First, we construct the first measure to assess the relative mispricing of private loans using publicly traded bonds, for both public and private firms. Second, we provide the first empirical evidence that managers time the market and take advantage of relative mispricing to adjust firms' debt structure. We plan to develop a structural model of debt structure choice that incorporates market segmentation and liquidation risk. Third, our planned extension to private firms and market segmentation analysis will allow us to assess the difficulties of credit access faced by private firms. Fourth, our planned study on debt structure changes in response to monetary shocks will shed light on credit (mis)allocation. 銀行貸款是企業籌集外部資本的重要管道，當企業難以進入公開債券市場時，通常被視為債務融資的首要選擇。然而，由於貸款是在私人市場發行，並在銀行間進行交易，流動性與透明度有限，其成本難以評估。在本計畫中，我們擬以公開市場交易的債券成本為基準，來評估銀行貸款的成本。 透過結構式信用風險模型以及債券與貸款的市場價格，我們建構了一項新穎的衡量指標——「貸款-債券利差」（loan-bond spread, LBS）——用以評估同一家企業貸款與債券之間的相對定價。LBS 為實際貸款利差與債券隱含貸款利差之間的差額。直觀而言，實際貸款利差反映的是在私人市場交易的銀行如何看待企業的財務狀況，而債券隱含貸款利差則反映在公開市場交易的債券投資人如何看待同一家企業的財務體質。較高的貸款-債券利差表示，相較於該企業的債券，其貸款在私人市場的價格相對偏低。 在初步結果中，我們首先確認貸款-債券利差能夠適當捕捉私人貸款與公開債券之間的相對錯誤定價。貸款-債券利差與未來貸款報酬呈正相關，其中高LBS組與低LBS組之間的風險調整後利差為4.01％。更重要的是，我們透過管理階層的財務決策對本指標進行外部驗證。我們發現，貸款相對於債券的定價偏低，會促使管理階層買回貸款，估計係數為 -0.31（t-statistic = -7.66）；而實際貸款殖利率則對債務結構調整無顯著影響。此對比顯示，管理階層確實會掌握市場時機，並在貸款與債券市場中進行套利。 綜合而言，本研究提出四項貢獻。第一，我們建構了首項利用公開交易債券來評估私人貸款相對錯誤定價的衡量指標，且同時適用於公開發行企業與非公開發行企業。第二，我們提供了首個實證證據，顯示管理階層會掌握市場時機，並利用相對錯誤定價來調整企業的債務結構。第三，我們規劃將研究延伸至非公開發行企業，並進行市場區隔分析，將有助於評估非公開發行企業所面臨的信貸取得困難。第四，我們規劃探討債務結構對貨幣衝擊的反應變化，將有助於闡明信貸的（錯誤）配置。

11506326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11506326.value: 具時間依賴協變量之混合治癒模型的分位數迴歸框架

11506326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11506326.value: In credit risk analysis, modeling the time duration until a mortgage loan defaults is crucial to banks, investors, and regulators for risk management. In time-to-event analysis, also known as survival analysis or duration analysis, traditional statistical models assume that every subject will experience the failure event eventually. However, default does not occur for the majority of borrowers in reality. Some borrowers are not susceptible to default throughout the full loan term, representing a ``cure fraction'' of the population that is immune to failure. The coexistence of cure fraction and right-censoring complicates time-to-event analysis, because we cannot determine whether a censored observation (due to early payoff or study end) belongs to the cured or susceptible group. Meanwhile, standard survival methods often overlook the abundance of time-dependent covariates in follow-up studies as data are collected over time. In the mortgage loan context, examples include varying interest rates or loan delinquency histories, which can influence the time to default while evolving over time. Incorporating time-dependent covariates into survival models, particularly censored quantile regression, is nontrivial as the failure time counting process is timed in terms of the individual quantile process. This proposal introduces a quantile regression framework for mixture cure models, tailored for right-censored time-to-event data with a cure fraction and time-dependent covariates. A mixture cure model divides borrowers into two groups: the ``cured'' who never default, and the ``susceptible'' who will if not censored. This allows us to examine how loan origination data such as borrower credit scores affect the probability of being cured, as well as how dynamic factors such as outstanding loan balances or late repayment records accelerate the time to default for susceptible loans. In particular, we consider a quantile regression approach that models the conditional quantile of the failure time, allowing covariate effects to vary across quantiles and offering robustness to error heterogeneity. This quantile framework facilitates analysis of mortgage loans at varying risk levels. We will derive feasible estimation procedures for the model parameters and establish the theoretical properties of the resulting estimators. We will apply our methodology to the Freddie Mac's Single-Family Loan-Level Dataset and access its numerical performance through Monte Carlo simulations. Extensions to other data structures, such as general biased sampling schemes, will be explored. User-friendly software packages will also be developed to facilitate implementation and application in credit risk modeling, medical studies, unemployment research, and other time-to-event analyses. 在信用風險分析中，對房屋抵押貸款違約發生前的時間長度進行建模，對銀行、投資者及監管機構的風險管理至關重要。在事件時間分析（亦稱存活分析或持續時間分析）中，傳統統計模型通常假設每個研究對象最終均會經歷失敗事件，然而，現實中大多數借款人並不會違約。部分借款人在整個貸款期限內均不易發生違約，構成族群中對失敗事件具有免疫性的「治癒比例」。治癒比例與右刪失的共存，使事件時間分析更為複雜，因為我們無法判定一項刪失觀測值（例如由於提前清償或研究結束所致）究竟屬於治癒群體還是易感群體。同時，由於數據會隨時間持續蒐集，標準存活分析方法往往忽略追蹤研究中大量存在的時間依賴協變量。在房屋抵押貸款的情境下，這類變數包括隨時間變動的利率或貸款逾期紀錄；它們在隨時間演變的同時，亦可能影響違約發生的時間。將時間依賴協變量納入存活模型，尤其是刪失分位數迴歸，並非易事，因為失敗時間的計數過程是依據個體分位數過程來計時的。 本計畫書提出一個適用於混合治癒模型的分位數迴歸框架，專為具有治癒比例及時間依賴協變量的右刪失事件時間數據而設計。混合治癒模型將借款人區分為兩組：「治癒者」從不違約；「易感者」則在未被刪失時終將違約。此模型使我們得以檢視貸款起始資料（如借款人的信用評分）如何影響借款人屬於治癒者的機率，以及動態因素（如未償還貸款餘額或延遲還款紀錄）如何加速易感貸款的違約時間。具體而言，我們考慮以分位數迴歸方法建模失敗時間的條件分位數，使協變量效應可隨分位數而改變，並對誤差異質性具有穩健性。此分位數框架有助於分析不同風險程度的房屋抵押貸款。 我們將推導模型參數的可行估計程序，並建立所得估計量的理論性質。我們將把所提方法應用於如房地美的單戶住宅貸款層級數據集，並藉由蒙地卡羅模擬評估其數值表現。我們亦將探討延伸至其他數據結構的可能性，例如一般的偏差抽樣機制。最後，將開發易於使用的軟體套件，以促進本方法在信用風險建模、醫學研究、失業研究及其他事件時間分析中的實踐與應用。

11506826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11506826.value: 催化創新：管理者能動性與人工智慧對比人類生成構想如何驅動創意構想的支持與實施

11506826.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11506826.value: Dr Liu, Yihao Dr Oh, Kyoungjo (Jo)

11506826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11506826.value: In today’s fast-changing organizational environment, innovation is crucial for maintaining competitive advantage and fostering growth (Amabile, 1996). Managers play a vital role in driving innovation by endorsing and implementing creative ideas, leveraging their authority within organizations. As a result, scholars have explored what motivates managers to support creative ideas. One prominent predictor is manager agency, which, based on social cognition theory, suggests that individuals with agentic traits are more effective at persuading others (Abele & Hauke, 2020; Hogan, 1982). This led to the argument that agentic managers feel empowered to enact and endorse creative ideas. However, empirical evidence on the link between agency and idea endorsement is mixed, with some studies indicating positive relationships, others finding no connection, and some suggesting negative effects. We propose two explanations for these inconsistent findings. First, the concept of agency has often been defined too broadly, encompassing various traits such as competence, independence, assertiveness, and confidence (Abele & Wojciszke, 2014). Second, prior research has primarily assumed ideas originate from humans, neglecting the increasing influence of AI-generated ideas in organizational processes. The source of an idea—whether from a human or AI—may influence whether to endorse it, because source cues significantly impact perceptions of intent, credit distribution, and perceived threat (Isaakyan et al., 2021). Therefore, our research aims to clarify these conflicting results in two ways. First, grounded in social cognition theories, we differentiate between competence and assertiveness: competence, an ability-related aspect of agency, is expected to promote endorsement, while assertiveness, a motivational trait, may inhibit it. Second, we examine how the source of the creative idea influences these relationships. AI-generated ideas tend to be perceived as less threatening than human-generated ideas, which may reduce resistance among assertive managers and weaken the negative relationship between assertiveness and creative idea endorsement. To test these hypotheses, we plan two cross-cultural studies involving random assignment to conditions where ideas are generated by either AI or human employees. For Study 1, we will recruit full-time managers in the US through Prolific, an online research platform. Study 2 will involve field experiments with Chinese managers and team members, conducted at three different times. If our hypotheses are supported, this research will shed light on how managerial characteristics and idea sources influence innovation outcomes. Ultimately, findings will clarify the mechanisms behind creative idea endorsement and guide strategies to foster organizational innovation amid broader AI adoption. 在當今瞬息萬變的組織環境中，創新對於維持競爭優勢及促進增長至關重要（Amabile, 1996）。管理者能夠運用自身在組織中的權力，透過支持並實施創意構想，在推動創新方面發揮關鍵作用。因此，學者開始探討促使管理者支持創意構想的因素。其中，一項重要的預測因素是管理者的能動性。根據社會認知理論，具有能動性特質的人更能有效說服他人（Abele & Hauke, 2020；Hogan, 1982）。這促使學者提出，具有能動性的管理者會認為自己有能力實踐並支持創意構想。然而，關於能動性與創意構想支持之間關係的實證證據並不一致：部分研究顯示兩者存在正向關係，另一些研究則未發現任何關聯，還有一些研究指出能動性可能產生負面影響。 我們針對這些不一致的研究結果提出兩種解釋。第一，能動性這一概念過去往往被定義得過於寬泛，涵蓋了能力、獨立性、果斷性及自信等多種特質（Abele & Wojciszke, 2014）。第二，過去的研究主要假設構想源自於人類，因而忽略了人工智慧生成的構想在組織流程中日益增長的影響力。構想的來源——無論來自人類還是人工智慧——都可能影響管理者是否支持該構想，因為來源線索會顯著影響人們對意圖、功勞歸屬及潛在威脅的認知（Isaakyan et al., 2021）。 因此，本研究旨在從兩方面釐清這些相互矛盾的研究結果。第一，以社會認知理論為基礎，我們將能力與果斷性加以區分：能力作為能動性中與個人才能相關的面向，預期將促進管理者對構想的支持；而果斷性作為一種動機性特質，則可能會降低其支持意願。第二，我們探討創意構想的來源如何影響上述關係。相較於人類生成的構想，人工智慧生成的構想往往被視為威脅性較低，這可能降低果斷型管理者的抗拒，進而弱化果斷性與創意構想支持之間的負向關係。 為了驗證上述假設，我們計畫進行兩項跨文化研究，並將參與者隨機指派至不同實驗情境，在這些情境中，創意構想分別由人工智慧或人類員工所提出。在研究一中，我們將透過線上研究平台 Prolific 招募美國的全職管理者。研究二將以中國的管理者及其團隊成員為研究對象，分別在三個不同的時間點進行實地實驗。若研究假設獲得支持，本研究將有助於闡明管理者特徵與構想來源如何影響創新成果。最終，研究結果將釐清管理者支持創意構想背後的作用機制，並為人工智慧日益普及的情況下促進組織創新提供策略指引。

11507026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11507026.value: 智能穿戴设备认知与情感机制的现场实验研究

11507026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11507026.value: Rapid advances in intelligent wearables are transforming frontline work by offering real-time, context-aware assistance. In dynamic and uncertain environments such as last-mile delivery, workers must make quick decisions amid fluctuating demand, variable traffic conditions, and adverse weather. In response, many firms are deploying smart helmets and similar devices to help delivery workers streamline operations. However, empirical evidence on their productivity impact remains mixed. This study investigates a central research question: Can intelligent device assistance improve work efficiency in dynamic delivery settings? If so, through what mechanisms and under what conditions? To address this, we plan to collaborate with a leading food delivery platform in mainland China. In the first phase, we will analyze a dataset of one million delivery orders collected before and after the deployment of smart helmets. Using a difference-in-differences (DID) approach, we will estimate the causal effect of wearable technology on operational efficiency. In the second phase, we will conduct a six-month field experiment with the same platform. Riders will alternate between two interaction modes: touchless prompts and anthropomorphic prompts, with algorithmic control over the timing and frequency of prompt delivery. We will link continuous operational data and detailed helmet usage logs with three waves of rider surveys measuring cognative load, technostress, and anxiety. The resulting data will be analyzed using rigorous statistical models. This study contributes theoretically by extending Cognitive Load Theory to human–AI collaboration in hands-busy, high-variability work; by unifying technostress and workplace anxiety into a coherent mediation model that clarifies the mixed IS and HCI findings; and by advancing a contingency-and-temporal account of human–machine fit that specifies when and why interaction modes help or hinder performance. It contributes to practice by providing causal evidence on net efficiency effects, revealing the cognitive and affective mechanisms that mediate those effects, and deriving actionable design principles such as adaptive mode switching, cadence caps, brevity, and error-recovery flows, to align prompt design with situational demands in high-stakes operational settings. Empirical validation will refine theory and inform scalable, human-centered deployment of intelligent wearables. 智能穿戴设备的快速发展正在通过提供实时、情境感知的辅助功能,重塑一线工作方式。在末端配送等动态且高度不确定的工作环境中,骑手需要在需求波动、路况多变和天气不利等多重压力下迅速做出决策。为此,许多企业开始部署智能头盔等设备,以帮助骑手提升作业效率。然而,现有实证研究关于此类设备对生产效率影响的结论并不一致。本研究旨在回答一个核心问题:智能设备辅助能否提升动态配送场景下的工作效率?若能,其作用机制是什么,又在何种条件下发挥作用? 为回答这一问题,我们计划与中国大陆一家领先的外卖配送平台展开合作。第一阶段,我们将分析该平台智能头盔部署前后共计一百万单配送订单数据,采用双重差分法(DID)估计可穿戴设备对运营效率的因果影响。第二阶段,我们将与该平台合作开展一项为期六个月的现场实验。骑手将在两种交互模式——无接触提示与拟人化提示——之间切换,提示的发送时机与频率由算法控制。我们将把持续采集的运营数据、详细的头盔使用日志,与三轮骑手问卷调查数据(测量认知负荷、技术压力与焦虑水平)相结合,并运用严谨的统计模型进行分析。 本研究的理论贡献体现在三方面:一是将认知负荷理论拓展至"双手繁忙、高度变化"工作情境下的人机协作研究;二是将技术压力与工作场所焦虑整合为一个统一的中介模型,以厘清信息系统与人机交互领域现有研究结论不一致的问题;三是提出一个关于人机匹配的权变与动态理论框架,明确不同交互模式在何时、以何种方式促进或抑制绩效表现。在实践层面,本研究提供了智能穿戴设备净效率影响的因果证据,揭示了驱动这些效应的认知与情感机制,并据此提炼出可操作的设计原则——如自适应模式切换、提示频率上限、简洁化设计与错误恢复流程——以帮助企业在高风险运营场景中,使提示设计更好地契合实际情境需求。本研究的实证验证结果将有助于完善相关理论,并为智能穿戴设备的规模化、以人为本的部署提供实践指引。

11507226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11507226.value: 从合规到沟通：人工智能生成内容的可解释性披露如何影响数字商务中的消费者反应

11507226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11507226.value: AI is transforming how businesses create and present digital content in e-commerce. In the apparel industry, generative AI now enables firms to produce customized and cost-efficient product imagery across different body types, styles, and backgrounds. Given the increasing prevalence of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Content (AIGC), regulatory authorities have begun requiring firms to disclose their involvement with AI to promote transparency and prevent deception. However, emerging evidence shows that general disclosures of AI can trigger a “transparency dilemma,” as it can undermine consumer trust, reduce perceived authenticity, and decrease purchase intentions. While prior studies have attempted to mitigate these negative effects by manipulating the properties of AIGC or considering consumer characteristics, limited attention has been paid to how the design and framing of AIGC disclosure shape consumer trust and behavioral responses. This project addresses this critical gap by investigating how AIGC disclosure design affects consumers’ attitudinal and behavioral responses in e-commerce. Drawing on signaling theory, this study conceptualizes explainable disclosure as an information signal that enhances consumers’ comprehension of AI’s role and purpose. We distinguish between two complementary elements: the how explanations, which clarify which part of the content was created by AI, and the why explanations, which articulate the rationale for using AI (e.g., cost efficiency, sustainability, or inclusivity). Furthermore, we will examine boundary conditions (AI form realism and interactive AI engagement) to understand when and how explainable AIGC disclosure is more effective in mitigating negative consumer responses. The project will conduct four laboratory experiments to examine how explainable disclosure of AIGC influences consumers’ attitudinal and behavioral responses. Experiment 1 will investigate the baseline effects of how explanations by manipulating disclosure type across five conditions (without disclosure, general disclosure, AI-generated background disclosure, AI-adjusted model pose disclosure, and AI-generated model disclosure). Experiment 2 will examine the effects of why explanations and their interactions with how explanations. Experiments 3 and 4 will test moderating roles of AI form realism and interactive AI engagement. As one of the early studies to systematically investigate how explainable AIGC disclosure influences consumer responses, this project will improve theoretical understanding of AI transparency and disclosure design by conceptualizing explainable disclosure as the how and why explanations. The findings will inform online retailers and platform managers on designing AIGC disclosure strategies that comply with transparency regulations while maintaining consumer engagement, offering new insights into effective and responsible AI communication in e-commerce. 人工智能正在重塑电子商务领域数字内容的创作与呈现方式。在服装零售行业，生成式人工智能（Generative AI）已能够以更低成本、高效率地生成适用于不同体型、风格及背景的个性化商品展示图片。随着人工智能生成内容（Artificial Intelligence-Generated Content, AIGC）的广泛应用，监管机构开始要求企业披露AI在内容创作中的参与情况，以提高透明度并防止误导消费者。然而，越来越多的研究表明，笼统的人工智能披露可能引发"透明度困境"（transparency dilemma），它可能会削弱消费者信任、降低感知真实性，并最终抑制购买意愿。既有研究虽尝试通过调整AIGC的内容属性或考察消费者个体特征来缓解上述负面效应，但对于AIGC披露信息本身的设计与呈现方式如何影响消费者信任与行为反应，仍缺乏系统研究。本项目旨在填补这一关键研究空白，探讨AIGC披露设计如何影响消费者在电子商务情境中的态度与行为反应。 本研究以信号理论（signaling theory）为基础，将可解释性披露（explainable disclosure）视为一种能够提升消费者对AI作用及使用目的理解的信息信号，并将其划分为两个相互补充的组成部分：其一为“如何”解释（how explanations），旨在阐明商品内容中哪一部分由人工智能生成；其二为“为何”解释（why explanations），旨在阐述企业采用AI的原因，例如提高成本效率、促进可持续发展或增强包容性等。此外，本研究还将进一步考察AI呈现形式的真实感（AI form realism）与AI交互参与（interactive AI engagement）这两项边界条件，以揭示可解释性AIGC披露在何种情境下能够更有效地缓解消费者对AI生成内容的负面反应。 本项目拟开展四项实验室实验，以系统检验可解释性AIGC披露对消费者态度与行为反应的影响机制。实验一将围绕“如何解释”展开，通过操纵五种披露条件（无披露、一般性AI披露、AI生成背景披露、AI调整模特姿势披露以及AI生成模特披露），考察不同AIGC披露方式的基准效应。实验二将进一步研究“为何解释”的作用，并分析其与“如何解释”之间的交互影响。实验三和实验四则分别检验AI呈现形式真实感及AI交互参与对上述关系的调节作用。 作为系统探讨可解释性AIGC披露如何影响消费者反应的早期研究之一，本项目将通过提出“如何解释”与“为何解释”两个维度，丰富人工智能透明度与披露设计领域的理论体系，深化对AI透明度作用机制的理解。同时，本研究成果将为网络零售商及电子商务平台设计兼顾监管合规与消费者体验的AIGC披露策略提供理论依据和实践指导，为电子商务环境下负责任、有效的人工智能沟通提供新的研究视角与管理启示。

11507526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11507526.value: 高维计数时间序列：泊松回归与因子模型

11507526.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11507526.value: Prof Guo, Shaojun Prof Qiao, Xinghao

11507526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11507526.value: This work introduces a comprehensive methodological framework for analyzing high-dimensional count time series, addressing the critical challenge of modeling complex dependencies in positive integer-valued data while accounting for both temporal dynamics and cross-sectional interdependencies. Our work bridges significant gaps in the current literature by developing a unified approach that specifically respects the discrete, positive integer-valued nature of counts, their evolution over time, and the high-dimensional correlations across series. We propose a novel model that conceptually separates each observed time series into two underlying, latent components. The first component captures series-specific patterns using observed covariates, while the second component models common influences that drive all series simultaneously through a factor structure. This decomposition allows for a principled separation of idiosyncratic effects from market-wide or system-wide co-movements, all while preserving the integer-valued property of the data. To fit this model, we developed an innovative iterative algorithm that tackles the core problem of disentangling these hidden components. The procedure alternates between using a probabilistic technique to allocate observed counts between the two components and then updating the statistical parameters for each component based on this allocation. This creates a refining cycle that progressively improves the separation and accuracy of the estimates. Our preliminary simulations validate the proposed method's core mechanics, showing accurate factor recovery and consistent parameter estimation under idealized settings. These positive results, however, are conditional. They starkly highlight the necessity to generalize the framework to maintain its efficacy in more realistic environments, such as those with endogeneity, as well as other complex dependence structures not captured by the initial model. This work makes several key contributions: it establishes a first-of-its-kind modeling framework for high-dimensional count time series; it develops a powerful estimation procedure to overcome a major technical hurdle; and it demonstrates practical utility through a real-world application to financial trading data. The project's practical relevance is directly ensured by our collaboration with a trader at a hedge fund in Hong Kong. 这项工作提出了一套用于分析高维计数时间序列的综合方法论框架，旨在解决对正整数取值数据中复杂依赖关系建模的关键挑战，同时兼顾时间动态性与截面相互依赖性。我们的工作通过发展一种统一的方法，弥合了当前文献中的重大空白，该方法尤其尊重计数的离散、正整数取值特性、其随时间演化的规律，以及各序列之间的高维相关性。 我们提出了一种新颖模型，从概念上将每条观测到的时间序列分解为两个潜在的隐成分。第一个成分利用协变量和历史取值捕捉序列特有的模式，而第二个成分则通过因子结构刻画同时驱动所有序列的共同影响。这种分解能够原理清晰地将异质效应与市场整体或系统整体的共同波动分离开来，同时保持数据的整数取值属性。 为拟合该模型，我们开发了一种创新的迭代算法，以解决分解这些隐成分的核心难题。该过程交替运用概率技术将观测到的计数分配至两个成分，然后基于该分配更新每个成分的统计参数。这就形成了一个不断精炼的循环，逐步提升分离效果与估计精度。 初步模拟验证了该方法的有效性。在一个代表性场景中，随着可用数据量的增加，模型正确识别公共因子数量的能力显著提升，在较大样本量下达到了完全准确。此外，所有参数的估计误差均随时间序列长度的增加而持续减小，从而验证了我们方法在统计学上的合理性。 本工作作出了若干关键贡献：它为高维计数时间序列建立了一个首创性的建模框架；它发展了一种强大的估计算法以克服重大技术障碍；并且通过对金融交易数据的实际应用展示了其实用价值。为确保即时影响力，我们将借助与金融行业交易团队的长期合作，把这些方法从验证阶段推进至实时市场环境中的实际应用。

11507826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11507826.value: 应对認證的永續資訊設計：漂綠、漂棕与如实披露

11507826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11507826.value: Third-party certification systems—from ESG ratings to eco-labels—represent the conventional solution for building consumer trust in sustainable products. However, these systems may paradoxically worsen the very information asymmetry they aim to resolve. This research investigates a troubling reality: certification can transform from transparency mechanism into strategic playbook, enabling sophisticated firms to secure prestigious sustainability labels through information manipulation rather than genuine environmental merit. Evidence of this paradox abounds globally. High-profile scandals—from Volkswagen's emissions fraud to certified illegal deforestation by various firms in the Amazon—reveal that firms systematically exploit certification weaknesses. For Hong Kong, this crisis holds particular urgency as the government's Climate Action Plan 2050 and HKEX's mandatory ESG requirements fundamentally depend on credible certification. Yet Hong Kong's ecosystem—BEAM Plus, MEELS, Green Label Scheme—faces identical gaming vulnerabilities. The core problem stems from strategic information asymmetry. Firms possess private environmental knowledge while consumers rely on certificates. Certifiers employ belief-based triage: direct approval for strong cases, rejection for weak cases, and costly testing with endogenous accuracy for ambiguous cases. Yet measurement challenges create exploitable loopholes. For instance, the Netherlands Food Authority discovered 25% product mislabeling rates. Major ESG rating agencies exhibit "aggregate confusion" with wildly divergent assessments. Anticipating these weaknesses, firms strategically design sustainability information—choosing among greenwashing (overstatement), brownwashing (understatement), and truth-telling—to pass verification thresholds and capture the premiums consumers pay for sustainable products. This research develops a comprehensive game-theoretic framework modeling how firms strategically design sustainability information in response to certifiers' endogenous testing. We make three significant contributions. First, we provide the first unified theoretical framework treating greenwashing and brownwashing as simultaneous choices, revealing critical strategic interdependencies invisible when studying either in isolation. Second, we formally demonstrate the endogenous certification paradox: under well-defined conditions, improving certification accuracy or tightening standards can decrease transparency and harm consumer welfare—challenging conventional regulatory wisdom. Third, we re-theorize brownwashing as an offensive profit-seeking strategy rather than defensive fear response, showing firms strategically understate credentials to trigger imperfect tests they can exploit. Our findings have direct policy implications for Hong Kong. Through comparative analysis of certification architectures—lenient, strict, error-penalty, and pre-commitment designs—we identify optimal frameworks maximizing transparency and consumer welfare while minimizing manipulation. Our research can provide actionable guidance for designing manipulation-resistant systems supporting Hong Kong's green finance ambitions. 從 ESG 評級到環保標籤等第三方認證系統，是建立消費者對永續產品信任的常規解決方案。然而，這些系統可能會矛盾地加劇資訊不對稱問題。本研究探討了一個令人擔憂的現實：認證可能從「透明度機制」變為「博弈策略」，使老練的企業能透過資訊操弄，而非憑藉真實的環境績效來獲取極具聲望的永續標籤。 此類悖論的證據在全球比比皆是。諸多備受矚目的醜聞（如福士汽車排放造假、企業在亞馬遜獲認證卻非法砍伐）揭示了企業正系統性地利用認證弱點。對香港而言，這場危機尤為緊迫：政府的《香港氣候行動藍圖2050》與港交所（HKEX）的強制性 ESG 披露要求，從根本上依賴可信的認證。然而，香港的認證生態系統（如綠建環評、能源效益與環保標籤計劃）也面臨著可能遭操弄的漏洞。 核心問題源於資訊不對稱。企業擁有私有環境資訊，而消費者依賴認證。認證機構採用基於信念的分類篩選機制：對表現強勁者直接批准，差劣者予以拒絕；對於模稜兩可的案例，則進行成本高昂且具內生準確度的測試。然而，衡量上的挑戰創造了漏洞。例如，荷蘭食品安全局曾發現高達 25% 的產品錯誤標示，各大 ESG 評級機構的評估結果也存在極大的「總體分歧」。在預期到這些弱點時，企業會策略性地設計永續資訊，在漂綠、漂棕和如實披露間做出選擇，以跨越門檻並獲取消費者支付的溢價。 本研究建立了一個全面的博弈論框架，對企業如何因應認證機構的內生測試、策略性地設計永續資訊進行建模。我們做出三項重大貢獻。首先，提供首個將「漂綠」和「漂棕」視為並行選擇的統一理論框架，揭示孤立研究兩者時無法察覺的關鍵策略互賴性。其次，正式論證「內生認證悖論」：在特定條件下，提高認證準確度或收緊標準，反而會降低透明度並損害消費者福祉，這挑戰了傳統的監管思維。第三，對「漂棕」進行了重新理論化，將其視為一種進攻性的逐利策略，而非防禦性反應；這表明企業會策略性地低報資歷，藉此觸發他們可利用的不完美測試。 我們的研究結果對香港具有直接的政策意涵。透過對寬鬆、嚴格、錯誤懲罰及預先承諾等不同認證架構的比較分析，我們找出能將透明度與消費者福祉最大化、同時將資訊操弄最小化的最佳框架。本研究能為設計抗操弄的系統提供具體指導，從而支持香港的綠色金融願景。

11508026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11508026.value: 购物中心消费者行为：动态疲劳、社交互动与数据驱动的布局优化

11508026.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11508026.value: Prof SHIN, Jiwoong Dr Sun, He

11508026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11508026.value: Brick-and-mortar shopping malls play a vital role in retail ecosystems, serving as platforms where tenant layout and design choices significantly influence consumer traffic patterns. These traffic patterns are crucial for determining store-level exposure, rental negotiations, and overall mall profitability. However, predicting granular, store-level consumer traffic remains a challenge due to the complex interplay of human behavior, including physical fatigue, social dynamics, and decision-making under spatial constraints. Existing models often rely on aggregate visitation data, overlooking critical behavioral factors such as how shoppers tire over time or how groups navigate collectively. This leads to suboptimal mall designs and inefficient tenant placements. This project aims to address these gaps by developing a behaviorally grounded structural model of consumer movement that incorporates two key dynamics: (1) physical fatigue and (2) social shopping behavior. Using a unique dataset of 17.3 million second-by-second shopping trajectories collected from four large malls, we will analyze how shoppers' decisions are influenced by accumulating fatigue, rest opportunities, and group coordination costs. The dataset, captured through AI-powered video sensors, provides unprecedented spatial and temporal resolution, allowing us to observe complete shopping journeys, group compositions, and rest patterns while preserving privacy. Our research focuses on three key questions: 1. How do physical fatigue and rest affect shoppers' movement, store choices, and exit decisions? 2. Can we reliably identify social shopping groups from movement patterns, and how do their behaviors differ from solo shoppers? 3. Which tenant layouts and recovery zone placements (e.g., seating and food courts) maximize store-level exposure and overall shopper engagement? To answer these questions, we will develop a structural econometric model that explicitly accounts for fatigue accumulation, recovery, and group heterogeneity. Using this model, we will conduct counterfactual simulations to test how different mall layouts and tenant placements impact shopper behavior. These simulations will provide actionable insights for optimizing mall design, balancing trade-offs between driving store-level exposure and minimizing shopper fatigue. Our findings will help mall operators design layouts that enhance shopper experience, increase dwell time, and improve profitability. By combining advanced modeling techniques with high-resolution trajectory data, this project bridges the gap between behavioral theory and practical retail design, offering a robust framework for data-driven decision-making in the retail sector. 实体购物中心在零售生态系统中发挥着至关重要的作用。作为商业平台，其租户布局与空间设计方案在很大程度上决定了消费者的客流分布模式。这些客流分布特征对于决定门店级别的曝光率、租金谈判以及购物中心的整体盈利能力具有关键意义。然而，由于人类行为（包括体力疲劳、社交动态以及空间约束下的决策过程）之间存在复杂的交互作用，预测精细的门店级消费者客流仍面临巨大挑战。现有模型往往依赖于宏观层面的客访总量数据，从而忽略了关键的行为因素，例如购物者随时间推移产生的疲劳感，或者群体如何进行协同移动。这通常会导致购物中心的空间设计欠佳以及租户布局效率低下。 本项目旨在填补这些研究空白，计划开发一种基于行为学的消费者移动结构模型，该模型将引入两大核心动态机制：（1）体力疲劳与（2）社交购物行为。依托从四家大型购物中心采集的包含1730万条逐秒级购物轨迹的独家数据集，我们将深入剖析购物者的决策如何受疲劳累积、休息机会以及群体协调成本的影响。该数据集由人工智能驱动的视频传感器采集，具备前所未有的空间与时间分辨率，在严格保护个人隐私的前提下，使我们能够观测到完整的购物旅程、群体人员构成以及休息模式。 本研究主要聚焦以下三个核心问题： 1. 体力疲劳与休息如何影响购物者的移动轨迹、门店选择以及离场决策？ 2. 我们能否通过移动特征可靠地识别出社交购物群体？其行为模式与单人购物者有何差异？ 3. 何种租户布局与恢复区（如休息座椅和美食广场）配置能够实现门店级曝光率与整体消费者参与度的最大化？

11508726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11508726.value: 客户政治意识形态分歧与信息不确定性：来自供应商企业管理层预测的证据

11508726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11508726.value: In an era marked by heightened political polarization, individuals’ beliefs and behavior are increasingly shaped by their political ideology. This division affects economic expectations as seen in survey data showing diverging consumer sentiment between Republicans and Democrats following the 2024 election in the United States. While existing literature has explored how partisanship shapes economic expectations and in turn economic decisions in the capital market, this proposed research seeks to investigate the impact of partisanship on interactions within product markets. Specifically, the proposed research aims to examine how political ideology divergence among major customers affects a supplier firm’s information uncertainty, manifesting in its management forecast practices. The product market is characterized by significant economic interdependence between suppliers and customers. Customers, typically, provide advance demand forecasts to upstream suppliers to facilitate their production planning and capacity building. Supplier firms rely on these customer demand forecasts to inform investment and operational decisions, as well as to predict future performance. Since these demand forecasts from customers are based on each customer’s economic expectations – shaped by their political ideologies – political misalignment among customers introduces divergent economic beliefs in their demand forecasts. These demand forecasts in turn, sends mixed signals about the broader economic outlook and future market demand to their suppliers, resulting in heightened information uncertainty for these suppliers. As a result, supplier firms facing politically misaligned customers may face challenges in forecasting future performance, reducing their ability and tendency to issue management forecasts. In addition, such supplier firms are less able to issue precise and accurate management forecasts. The findings of the proposed research will extend existing literature by highlighting the role of customer partisanship divergence as a source of friction in supply chain communication, thereby impacting corporate disclosure through supply chain information transfer. As customer information constitutes a critical input for firm decisions, the findings are expected to offer valuable insights into the broader economic consequences of political polarization for corporate decision making. 在政治极化日益加剧的时代，个人的信念与行为越来越受到其政治意识形态的影响。美国2024年大选后的调查数据显示，共和党人与民主党人的消费者信心走势出现显著分化，反映出政治分歧对经济预期的影响。现有文献已探讨党派立场如何塑造经济预期，并进一步影响资本市场中的经济决策；本研究拟进一步考察党派立场对产品市场上交易合作方信息交流的影响。具体而言，本研究旨在检验主要客户之间的政治意识形态分歧如何影响供应商企业的信息不确定性，并如何体现在其管理层对未来业绩的预测中。 产品市场的一个重要特征是供应商与客户之间存在显著的经济依赖。通常，客户会提前向上游供应商提供需求预测，以协助其进行生产规划与产能建设。供应商企业依赖这些客户需求预测来制定投资和经营决策，并预测未来业绩。由于客户的需求预测建立在各自的经济预期之上，而这些预期又受到其政治意识形态的影响，因此，客户之间的政治立场不一致会使其需求预测反映出分化的经济信念。这些需求预测因此向供应商传递出关于整体经济前景和未来市场需求的混乱信号，从而加剧供应商所面临的信息不确定性。因此，面对政治立场不一致客户的供应商企业，在预测未来业绩时可能面临更大困难，进而降低其发布管理层预测的能力与意愿。此外，此类供应商企业也较难发布精确的管理层预测。 本研究的发现将拓展现有文献，揭示客户党派立场分歧如何成为供应链沟通中的一种负面因素，并通过供应链信息传递影响企业披露。鉴于客户信息是企业决策的重要投入，本研究结果有望为理解政治极化对企业决策所产生的更广泛经济后果提供有价值的见解。

11508926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11508926.value: AI 隊友悖論：設計特性能否緩解AI 的局限並促進工作重塑

11508926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11508926.value: In 2025, the Hong Kong government designated artificial intelligence (AI) as a core driver of the city’s future development and committed to positioning Hong Kong as a global hub for AI innovation. Today, approximately 73% of organizations in Hong Kong have integrated AI into their workplaces, transforming AI from a mere functional tool into an indispensable “teammate” in daily operations. However, as AI teammates become increasingly integrated into work environments, an AI teammate paradox has emerged. This paradox highlights the tension between AI’s ability to enhance efficiency and its lack of human-like social qualities that are vital for sustaining employees’ motivation and engagement in team contexts. One such example is job crafting, which is a self-initiated process through which employees actively redefine and adapt their work roles. This paradox may inadvertently undermine employee engagement and constrain the full benefits of AI integration. To address this challenge, this project aims to explore how AI teammates influence job crafting behaviors and how AI systems can be designed to foster promotion-focused (beneficial) job crafting while mitigating prevention-focused (detrimental) forms. This project comprises four interrelated objectives. First, it identifies two defining characteristics that distinguish AI from human teammates—specifically, lack of self-interest and voice capability—and suggests that these features are critical to understanding employees’ job crafting responses. Second, it examines how the absence of these characteristics influences job crafting through two psychological mechanisms: felt obligation for contribution and perceived personal control. Third, building on these insights, it develops two design features—dynamic contribution tracking and constructive dissent expression—that aim to compensate for AI’s limited social characteristics. These features are designed to enhance employees’ felt obligation for contribution and foster promotion-focused job crafting while reducing prevention-focused behaviors. Fourth, it theorizes and empirically tests the effectiveness of these design features in shaping job crafting through the identified psychological mechanisms. Collectively, by achieving these four objectives, this project will establish a theoretical framework for understanding how AI teammates shape employee perceptions and behaviors. For organizations, it offers practical guidance for deploying AI teammates to improve employee performance and increase team adaptability. For AI system developers, it informs the creation of AI teammates that overcome inherent social limitations and better facilitate collaborative work. For policymakers, it offers support for designing AI governance and workforce development strategies that enhance productivity. 2025 年，香港政府將人工智慧（AI）定為本港未來發展的核心驅動力，並致力把香港打造為全球人工智慧創新樞紐。現今，香港約有 73% 的機構已將人工智慧導入工作場域，人工智慧也從單純的功能工具，轉變為日常營運中不可或缺的「隊友」。然而，隨著人工智慧隊友越來越廣泛地融入工作環境，人工智慧隊友悖論隨之浮現。此悖論凸顯出一項矛盾：人工智慧雖能提升效率，卻欠缺人類特有的社會屬性；而這類社會屬性，對於維持員工在團隊情境下的工作動機與投入度至關重要，其中便包括工作重塑—— 員工主動重新定義、調適自身工作角色的自發性歷程。該悖論可能會無意間削弱員工的工作投入，也讓人工智慧導入無法充分發揮其效益。為應對這項挑戰，本研究計畫旨在探討人工智慧隊友如何影響工作重塑行為，以及人工智慧系統該如何設計，以促進促進導向（有益）的工作重塑，同時緩解預防導向（有害）的工作重塑。 本計畫包含四個相互關聯的研究目標。第一，辨識出人工智慧相較人類隊友的兩項核心特徵：缺乏自我利益動機，以及缺乏表達意見的能力，並主張這兩項特徵是理解員工工作重塑反應的關鍵。第二，檢視當這兩項特徵付之闕如時，會透過兩種心理機制 —— 貢獻感受義務感與知覺個人控制感，進而影響工作重塑。第三，基於上述研究洞見，開發兩項設計特性：動態貢獻追蹤機制與建設性異議表達機制，藉此彌補人工智慧社會屬性的不足。這些設計特性旨在強化員工的貢獻感受義務感，培養促進導向的工作重塑，並減少預防導向的行為。第四，透過前述確認的心理機制，針對這些設計特性對工作重塑的影響效果進行理論建構與實證檢驗。 整體而言，透過達成上述四項目標，本計畫將建構一套理論架構，用以解釋人工智慧隊友如何形塑員工的認知與行為。對企業組織而言，本研究可提供實務指引，協助導入人工智慧隊友，提升員工工作表現與團隊適應力。對人工智慧系統開發者而言，本研究可做為研發人工智慧隊友的參考，使其突破先天的社會屬性限制，更有效地協同合作。對政策制定者而言，本研究可協助制訂人工智慧治理與勞動力發展策略，進而提升生產力。

11509026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11509026.value: We develop a model that endogenizes arbitrageurs' information acquisition decisions within the asynchronous awareness framework of Abreu and Brunnermeier (2002). In their original framework, the synchronization problem combined with individual incentives to time the market leads to delayed arbitrage. We conjecture that these same forces may create an additional layer of inefficiency: arbitrageurs lack sufficient incentives to acquire information about emerging bubbles in the first place. This endogenous information acquisition decision generates delayed awareness, providing a theoretical foundation for observed patterns of investor neglect preceding financial crises. Notably, we find that information acquisition decisions in this environment exhibit neither strategic complementarity nor strategic substitutability, distinguishing our results from standard information acquisition models. 我们在 Abreu 和 Brunnermeier（2002）提出的异步认知框架基础上，构建了一个信息获取决策内生化的套利模型。在原始框架中，同步化问题叠加个体择机入市的动机，共同导致了套利延迟。我们进一步发现，同样的作用机制还带来了另一层效率损失：套利者在泡沫萌芽阶段本身就缺乏足够的动力去主动获取相关信息。这种信息获取的内生性造成了认知上的滞后，从而为金融危机爆发前普遍存在的投资者忽视现象提供了理论解释。

11509626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11509626.value: 在线内容市场中的AI平台竞争与收入模式选择

11509626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11509626.value: Generative AI platforms built on large language models (LLMs) are rapidly becoming de facto gateways to information for many users. This transformation raises some important questions about the sustainability of traditional content platforms and the evolution of digital business models. While some publishers engage in high-stakes legal battles over content rights and others negotiate licensing agreements, there remains a noticeable absence of rigorous economic analysis to guide these decisions and inform policy responses. This project develops an economic model to analyze competition between traditional content platforms and AI-powered alternatives. We study a market where two heterogeneous content platforms (differing in quality) compete with an LLM platform that has been trained on their content and offers perfect personalization to users. Content platforms can choose between subscription-based and advertising-based revenue models, while users are heterogeneous along two dimensions: their horizontal preferences for content and their sensitivity to advertising. The LLM platform's distinctive features (its ability to provide personalized content and its intermediate quality derived from training on existing content) create some novel competitive dynamics that depart from standard platform competition. Our preliminary analysis yields several counterintuitive insights. First, we demonstrate that LLM entry can generate Pareto improvements, simultaneously increasing user welfare and incumbent platform revenues. This can occur when the threat of AI competition induces traditional platforms to switch from subscription to advertising models, creating a more efficient segmentation where some users access ad-supported content while others subscribe to the LLM service. Second, we show that LLM-induced elimination of low-quality platforms can benefit both users and surviving high-quality platforms by reducing competitive pressure and raising average market quality. Third, we characterize how platforms' strategic responses (including aggressive pricing and revenue model switching) depend on the distribution of user types, advertising sensitivities, and quality differentials. Planned extensions include incorporating content licensing agreements between AI and traditional platforms, endogenizing quality investments, and analyzing mixed revenue models for the LLM platform. This research has immediate policy relevance for ongoing regulatory debates about AI platform competition and content licensing requirements. Our framework can inform key decisions about whether AI platforms should compensate content creators for training data and whether AI represents a monopolistic threat or a welfare-enhancing competitive force. By providing an economic analysis of AI platform competition with endogenous revenue model choice, this project aims to guide both business strategy and regulatory design during this pivotal transformation of online content markets. 基于大语言模型（LLMs）的生成式人工智能平台正迅速成为众多用户获取信息的事实上的主要入口。这一变革引发了若干关于传统内容平台可持续性及数字商业模式演进的重要问题。部分出版商围绕内容版权展开高风险法律诉讼，另有部分则寻求达成授权许可协议，然而目前仍明显缺乏严谨的经济学分析来指导上述决策并为政策应对提供依据。 本研究构建了一个经济模型，用以分析传统内容平台与AI驱动的替代平台之间的竞争。模型设定一个市场，其中两个具有异质性的内容平台（质量存在差异）与一个基于其内容训练而成、能够为用户提供完全个性化服务的LLM平台展开竞争。内容平台可在订阅制与广告制收入模式之间进行选择，而用户在两个维度上具有异质性：对内容的水平偏好以及对广告的敏感程度。LLM平台的独特特征——提供个性化内容的能力及其基于既有内容训练所获得的中等质量水平——催生了若干偏离标准平台竞争框架的新型竞争动态。 初步分析揭示了若干反直觉的洞见。第一，本文证明LLM平台的进入可以产生帕累托改进，同时提升用户福利与在位平台收入。这一结果可能出现于如下情形：AI竞争的威胁促使传统平台从订阅制转向广告制，由此形成更为有效的市场分割——部分用户获取广告支持的免费内容，另一部分用户则订阅LLM服务。第二，本文表明LLM平台引致的低质量平台退出可以同时惠及用户和存活的高质量平台，其机制在于竞争压力的减轻及市场平均质量的提升。第三，本文刻画了平台的策略性应对（包括激进定价与收入模式转换）如何取决于用户类型分布、广告敏感度及质量差异。后续拓展计划包括：引入AI平台与传统平台之间的内容授权协议、将质量投资内生化，以及分析LLM平台的混合收入模式。 本研究对当前围绕AI平台竞争与内容授权要求的监管辩论具有直接的政策参考价值。所构建的分析框架可为以下关键决策提供依据：AI平台是否应为训练数据向内容创作者支付补偿，以及AI究竟构成垄断威胁还是增进福利的竞争力量。通过在内生收入模式选择条件下对AI平台竞争进行经济学分析，本研究旨在为在线内容市场这一关键转型期的商业战略与监管设计提供指引。

11509726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11509726.value: 綠色悖論：調和消費者對可持續產品失敗的寬恕與懲罰

11509726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11509726.value: The high failure rate of green startups represents a critical bottleneck in the global transition to a sustainable economy. This problem threatens strategic policy goals, like Hong Kong’s Climate Action Plan 2050, and puts significant public and private capital at risk. This market-level challenge is magnified by a fundamental puzzle in consumer psychology: while consumers often harbor a “sustainability liability,” believing green products are less effective, they can also exhibit a “greenguard effect,” showing greater forgiveness when these products fail. This conflict creates immense uncertainty for innovators, unsure if a product setback will trigger a punitive backlash or a forgiving embrace. This research addresses the core question: Under what conditions do consumers punish, and when do they forgive, green innovation failure? This project advances a new paradigm of “proactive” brand resilience, shifting from the traditional reactive recovery strategies. It proposes that a brand’s proactive value-based positioning, established long before any potential failure, is the key determinant of consumer response. Drawing from system justification theory, the research distinguishes between two brand narratives: a “system-justifying” positioning, which frames a green product as a better choice within the current market system, and a “system-challenging” positioning, which invites consumers to join a movement to change a flawed system. The central thesis is that a system-challenging positioning fosters a communal (vs. exchange) consumer-brand relationship by reframing consumption as a collective effort toward a shared goal, creating a powerful shared identity. This shared identity creates a psychological stake in the brand’s success, motivating consumers to attribute failure to external factors (the difficult struggle against a flawed system) rather than internal incompetence, thereby building resilience. Through a multi-method approach, this project delivers a comprehensive framework to reconcile conflicting findings (sustainability liability vs. greenguard effect) by identifying which brand narratives determine the outcome. In addition, it extends system justification theory by bridging macro- (i.e., proactive positioning) and micro-level analyses (consumers’ mindset). Furthermore, it delineates critical boundary conditions—consumers’ implicit theory (incremental vs. entity) and failure type (performance vs. ethical)—providing a nuanced model of consumer response. This work advances a novel theory of proactive brand resilience and provides green innovators with actionable strategies to craft their brand narratives to survive innovation setbacks. Eventually, this research will help unblock a critical bottleneck in the transition to a sustainable economy.

11600326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11600326.value: 香港華商總會的社會角色與政治參與

11600326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11600326.value: 本計劃以文獻搜集、史料分析為基礎，從社會參與、政商協作、粵港/政商跨界活動以至身份認同等不同議題，研究華商總會於戰前香港的各種活動與發展歷程。自省港大罷工爆發後，華商在中英交惡困境下透過粵港人事網絡和交際手腕，協助粵港雙方解決經濟及政治危機。華總要員佔據社會要津，多被粵港政權體制吸納以助當局改善管治，成為溝通中港的橋樑。但是，1930年代的中國名義上統一，各派勢力爭鬥不休。廣東執政者如走馬燈般來去匆匆，加上全球經濟大蕭條以及接踵而至的日本侵華國難，都為香港政經發展帶來不少挑戰，華總於此不穩定局面下既為港府解決經濟難題，也為中國政府承擔抗日後勤支援的政治角色，值得關注。它未如南洋的商會般因為雙重效忠遭受打壓，所涉及的香港地緣政治、華商的在地殖民協作以及家國、身份認同等複雜問題也是值得研究。要之，研究華總參與在地社會建設、國家建構的角色以及「雙重效忠」的課題，有助我們開拓更深層、更多元的香港史研究。 This research project is grounded in literature review and historical source analysis. By examining diverse themes such as social engagement, government-business collaboration, cross-border activities between Guangdong and Hong Kong, and identity formation, it investigates the wide-ranging activities and developmental trajectory of the Chinese General Chamber of Commerce in pre-war Hong Kong. Following the outbreak of the Canton-Hong Kong Strike, Sino-British relations deteriorated severely. Amid this predicament, Chinese merchants leveraged their Guangdong-Hong Kong interpersonal networks and diplomatic tact to mediate between the authorities, helping to resolve economic and political crises on both sides. Key figures within the Chamber held pivotal social positions and were frequently co-opted into the administrative frameworks of both Guangdong and Hong Kong to help improve governance, thereby serving as a crucial bridge between mainland China and Hong Kong. However, while China was nominally unified in the 1930s, fierce power struggles among various factions persisted. The leadership in Guangdong changed in rapid succession. This instability, coupled with the global Great Depression and the subsequent national crisis brought about by the Japanese invasion of China, posed significant challenges to Hong Kong's political and economic development. Against this volatile backdrop, the Chamber not only assisted the Hong Kong government in tackling economic hardships but also assumed a political role by providing logistical support for China’s anti-Japanese resistance—a dynamic that merits close attention. Unlike the Chinese chambers of commerce in Southeast Asia, which faced suppression due to their "dual loyalty," the Chamber avoided such crackdowns. The complex issues involved—including Hong Kong's geopolitics, the Chinese merchants' local collaboration with the colonial regime, and their intertwined national and cultural identities—also warrant thorough academic research. In conclusion, examining the Chamber’s role in local social development and nation-building, as well as the issue of "dual loyalty," will help us pioneer a deeper and more multifaceted study of Hong Kong history.

11600426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11600426.value: 評測與訓練粵語大語言模型

11600426.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11600426.value: Prof LAI, Yan Ki Jackie Prof Wang, Rui

11600426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11600426.value: Cantonese, a language spoken by over 85 million people worldwide, is being left behind in the current AI revolution. While Large Language Models (LLMs)—the technology behind tools like ChatGPT—are transforming society, there are no high-quality, publicly available models that truly understand Cantonese. This is reflected in a stark research gap: for every 30 academic papers on German language AI, there is only one on Cantonese. This digital inequity means Cantonese-speaking communities, particularly in Hong Kong, lack access to reliable and culturally aware AI tools for education, work, and daily life. This project will systematically solve this problem. First, we will create two foundational resources: 1) a comprehensive exam or evaluation benchmark with 34,000 questions to accurately measure an AI's proficiency in Cantonese, covering everything from everyday slang and cultural nuances to its unique sentence structures; and 2) the largest collection of high-quality Cantonese text of 100 billion tokens for training new AI models. Second, we will use this benchmark to produce a public white paper on the Cantonese abilities of existing major LLMs. Finally, we will train a suite of more than 30 monolingual and multilingual Cantonese LLMs through a series of well-controlled experiments. All datasets and models will be open-sourced under a suitable license. The impact of the project will be twofold. For Hong Kong and the global Cantonese community, it will deliver a new generation of powerful, open-source AI models that are capable and reliable in Cantonese. This will empower developers to build truly useful Cantonese-aware applications. More broadly, our methodical experiments will create a roadmap for developing AI in thousands of other low-resource languages currently neglected by technology. Thus this research will not only secure a vibrant future for Cantonese in the digital world, but also advance the creation of more inclusive and equitable AI in the world. 粵語（廣東話）雖為全球逾八千五百萬人使用之語言，卻在當今人工智能（AI）革命中遭到邊緣化。儘管大型語言模型（LLM，即驅動 ChatGPT 等工具之底層技術）正深刻重塑社會，市場上仍缺乏充分掌握粵語、品質優良且可供公眾使用之模型。此現象反映出嚴峻的研究鴻溝：平均每三十篇探討德語人工智能的學術論文，方有一篇聚焦粵語。這種數碼不平等意味著粵語社群——尤其是香港——在教育、就業及日常生活中，均匱乏可靠且具本土文化認知的人工智能工具。 本項目將有系統地回應此問題。首先，我們將建立兩大基礎資源：（一）一個涵蓋 34,000 條題目之綜合評測基準，用以精準衡量人工智能的粵語能力，內容遍及日常俚語、文化細膩差異，乃至其獨特之句法結構；（二）蒐集總量高達一千億個詞元（token）之全球最大型、高品質粵語文本語料庫，用以訓練嶄新之人工智能模型。其次，我們將運用上述評測基準，發表一份剖析現有主要大型語言模型粵語表現之公開白皮書。最後，我們將透過一系列嚴謹對照之實驗，訓練逾三十個單語及多語粵語大型語言模型。所有數據集與模型均會在適當授權條款下，以開放源碼形式釋出，供公眾使用。 本項目將帶來兩方面之深遠影響。對香港及全球粵語社群而言，我們將提供新一代功能強大、開源且粵語能力穩健的人工智能模型，藉此賦能開發者，協助其建構真正實用且諳熟粵語之應用程式。從更宏觀之視角審視，我們系統化的實驗將為數以千計目前遭科技忽略、數據稀缺之「低資源語言」，勾勒出一套發展人工智能的路線圖。故此，此研究不僅能確保粵語在數碼世界中持續發光發熱，更將推動全球邁向更包容、更公平的人工智能技術。

11600726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11600726.value: 全球想像中的北京：記憶、製圖與轉譯，1912–1949

11600726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11600726.value: China’s Republican era (1912–1949) was a period of transformation for Beijing’s built environment and its international image. While Shanghai’s visible modernity, iconic status, and cosmopolitan treaty-port status have attracted both popular and scholarly attention, historical studies of Beijing during this period are relatively less common. Drawing on English-language and translingual sources and archives, the project examines how genres such as travel writing, maps, guidebooks, and novels position Beijing in the global imagination as a city poised between old and new worlds, where memory, modernity, and power intersect. This project will be organized around three related investigations: (1) George N. Kates’s unpublished papers and his memoir "The Years That Were Fat" (1952), which reveal an embodied, preservationist practice attentive to routes and routines, courtyard typologies, furniture, and the everyday infrastructures of Republican Beijing; (2) maps and tourist guidebooks including L. C. Arlington and William Lewisohn’s "In Search of Old Peking" (1935), Frank Dorn’s “Map and History of Peiping” (1936), and related archival materials, which demonstrate how cartographic and artistic practices framed Beijing as both a navigable spectacle and a site of cultural memory; and (3) novels by authors including Harold Acton, Lin Yutang, and Lao She, which dramatize and translate everyday life within old worlds and newly charted urban spaces. Treating these sources as situated mediations rather than transparent windows, the project links practices of memorializing, mapping, and storytelling to broader geopolitical tensions, cultural anxieties, and imagined futures. Through an interdisciplinary method that engages with multimodal and popular texts, literary works, and historical materials, the project will produce three peer-reviewed articles that contribute to urban cultural history, critical heritage studies, and transnational literary studies. 民國時期（1912–1949）是北京建成環境與其國際形象發生深刻轉變的年代。上海因其可見的現代性、標誌性地位及通商口岸的國際都會身份，長期吸引大眾與學界關注；相較之下，同一時期北京的歷史研究則相對較少。本計劃取材於英語文獻及跨語際的資料與檔案，探討旅行書寫、地圖、旅遊指南與小說等文類如何在全球想像中將北京定位為一座徘徊於舊世界與新世界之間的城市——記憶、現代性與權力在此交會。 本計劃圍繞三項相互關聯的研究展開：（一）喬治·凱茨（George N. Kates）的未刊文稿及其回憶錄《豐年》（The Years That Were Fat, 1952），這些材料呈現出一種身體化的、以保存為念的實踐，關注行走路線與日常作息、四合院的類型、家具，以及民國北京的日常基礎設施；（二）地圖與旅遊指南，包括阿靈頓（L. C. Arlington）與劉易森（William Lewisohn）合著的《尋找老北京》（In Search of Old Peking, 1935）、多恩（Frank Dorn）的〈北平地圖與歷史〉（"Map and History of Peiping," 1936）及相關檔案材料，藉以說明製圖與藝術實踐如何將北京同時框定為可供遊覽的景觀奇觀與文化記憶的場域；（三）哈羅德·艾克頓（Harold Acton）、林語堂與老舍等作家的小說，這些作品將舊世界與新近繪製的城市空間中的日常生活加以戲劇化並予以轉譯。 本計劃不把上述材料視為透明的觀看之窗，而是將其理解為具有特定位置的中介，藉此把紀念、製圖與敘事等實踐，與更廣泛的地緣政治張力、文化焦慮及對未來的想像連結起來。透過兼顧多模態與通俗文本、文學作品及歷史材料的跨學科方法，本計劃將產出三篇同行評審期刊論文，為城市文化史、批判性遺產研究及跨國文學研究作出貢獻。

11600926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11600926.value: 機器人記者為何反噬：人工智能合成新聞中的作者身份、透明度與平台觸達如何塑造受眾的偏見感知與反應

11600926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11600926.value: While five finalists in the 2024 Pulitzer Prize for Journalism acknowledged using artificial intelligence (AI) in their work and Bloomberg’s Cyborg system generates thousands of articles within milliseconds, a paradox emerges from this “AI-turn” in journalism: do users perceive AI-synthesized news as more or less biased than human journalism? Competing arguments emerge: users may view AI as objective due to its rule-based operation and freedom from human prejudices, or conversely, as suspect due to algorithmic opacity and its inability to exercise contextual judgment. In politically polarized environments, even balanced reporting can be perceived as biased—a phenomenon known as hostile media perception (HMP)—which leads to news disengagement, selective avoidance, and diminished trust in the broader media environment. This project examines public perceptions of and responses to AI-synthesized news—AI-powered news curation applications—from socio-psychological and journalism studies perspectives. We examine how source-level (authorship: human vs. AI vs. human-AI hybrid), message-level (editorial transparency disclosure: evidence-based sourcing citations vs. process-based fairness claims), and system-level (platform reach: established commercial application vs. student coursework prototype) factors shape bias perception as stipulated by HMP (Objective 1). Informed by human-computer interaction and self-categorization theory, we explore how this news–perception pathway is moderated by three techno-political dispositions—machine heuristics (mental shortcuts about algorithmic objectivity versus inflexibility), affective polarization (in-group solidarity and out-group animosity), and technological nationalism (belief in one’s nation’s technological superiority)—that condition audience responses to AI-authored content (Objective 2). We also examine how such hostile perception predicts several attitudinal and behavioral outcomes, including news engagement, platform trust, and policy attitudes (Objective 3). To ground this inquiry in high-stakes environments, this project implements two population-based online experiments in the United States and Hong Kong, using U.S. federal AI regulation (Study 1, U.S. sample) and U.S. semiconductor export controls on (Study 2, U.S. and Hong Kong samples) as test cases. Both topics provide ecological validity through their sustained media coverage, concrete economic impacts, and geopolitical importance. The findings aim to advance theories in media effects, political psychology, and human-AI interaction (Objective 4), and offer evidence-based insights for media organizations and policymakers (Objective 5). For practitioners, we identify transparency and platform positioning strategies that build credibility. For policymakers, our findings foster democratic media innovation, aligning with the UN Sustainable Development Goals to promote peace, justice, strong institutions, and responsible innovation. 儘管2024 年普立茲新聞獎（Pulitzer Prize）有五名入圍者明確承認在其工作中使用人工智能（AI）、且美國彭博社（Bloomberg）的 Cyborg系統能在短時間內生成數千篇報導，新聞業的「人工智能轉型」引申出一項悖論：受眾究竟會認為 AI 合成新聞比人類採寫的新聞更具偏見，還是更為客觀？學術界對此存在兩種截然不同的觀點：一方面，用戶可能因 AI 依循規則運作且無人類偏見而視其為客觀；另一方面，用戶亦可能因演算法的不透明性及缺乏語境判斷能力而對其產生懷疑。在政治高度極化的環境下，即便是平衡客觀的報導亦可能被視為帶有偏見——傳播學稱其為「敵意媒體感知」（Hostile Media Perception, HMP）現象，進而引發受眾的新聞疏離、選擇性迴避，並削弱對整體媒體環境的信任。 本研究項目從社會心理學與新聞學研究視角出發，深入探討公眾對 AI 合成新聞的感知與反應。本項目的具體研究目標如下： 目標一：基於敵意媒體感知理論，檢視來源層面（作者身份：人類 vs. 人工智能 vs. 人機協同）、訊息層面（編輯透明度披露：基於證據的出處引用 vs. 基於流程的公正聲明）及系統層面（平台觸達：成熟商業應用程式 vs. 學生課程原型）之因素如何塑造受眾的偏見感知。 目標二：結合人機互動（HCI）與自我歸類理論，探索三種技術政治傾向如何調節上述新聞感知路徑，進而影響受眾對 AI 署名內容的反應。 目標三：考察此類敵意媒體感知如何預測受眾的態度與行為結果，包括新聞參與度、平台信任度及政策態度。 為在高風險、高爭議的議題情境中落實本研究，本項目將在美國與香港兩地開展兩項基於人口代表性樣本的線上實驗，分別以「聯邦人工智能監管」（研究一，美國樣本）與「技術出口管制」（研究二，美國與香港樣本）作為測試案例。這兩個議題具備持續的媒體報導、具體的經濟影響及高度的地緣政治重要性，能為本研究提供顯著的生態效度（Ecological Validity）。 本項目的研究發現旨在推進媒體效果、政治心理學及人機互動領域的理論發展（目標四），並為媒體機構與政策制定者提供基於實證的深刻見解（目標五）。對新聞從業者而言，本研究將梳理出能建立公信力的透明度策略與平台定位策略；對政策制定者而言，研究成果將有助於促進民主化的媒體創新，切合聯合國可持續發展目標（SDGs）中關於促進和平、正義與強大機構以及負責任創新的願景。

11601126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11601126.value: With increasing global movement, Hong Kong’s literary culture in the early 20th century developed through exchanges that linked local writers with those in mainland China and the wider global networks.
