By advancing a comprehensive institutional analysis, the project deepens our understanding of China’s evolving energy governance and provides broader insights for scholars and policymakers examining the complex interactions between state power and market instruments in the energy transition. 中国的净零转型正推动能源治理领域发生战略性制度重构：国家有意识地构建市场机制，以减少对传统命令—控制模式的长期依赖。几十年来，中国能源部门一直通过行政指令、国家融资和集中规划加以管理，这种模式削弱了长期效率。当前在持续国家监管下嵌入市场机制的转型，体现了一种超越传统国家—市场二分法的混合型治理模式，并综合运用供给侧与需求侧干预工具。 这种混合化的一个核心例证是绿色电力证书（绿证）交易体系。尽管初期发展缓慢，但自中央政府于 2023 年决定将绿证 指定为可再生能源电力环境属性的唯一法定证明，并随后出台一系列监管与政策措施以来，绿证市场迅速扩张。考察 绿证交易的演变，有助于理解中国如何在以国家为中心的制度框架内重新校准其能源治理，而该框架仍持续界定并调节市场活动的边界。 尽管 绿证的政策相关性日益增强，但针对中国绿证交易制度的学术分析仍然匮乏。本研究旨在填补这一空白，将 绿证作为案例研究，用以检验并完善制度理论：一方面借鉴Williamson的基础性框架，另一方面吸纳Mahoney and Thelen等后续学者的贡献。研究考察法律与组织创新如何在持续的结构性与规范性挑战，包括监管碎片化、根深蒂固的国家干预以及相互冲突的利益相关者诉求之下，既促成又制约市场改革。尤其值得关注的是，在中国 绿证交易制度中，市场机制与国家干预通过渐进式的制度叠加与制度转换而并存。此外，研究还评估在上述 根深蒂固的监管与结构性挑战背景下，绿证交易规则与政策在多大程度上提升了中国的能源治理能力。 本研究采用多方法路径，将对法律、法规与政策的教义分析，同对中国法学学者、能源监管者、行业参与者以及熟悉中国能源领域的国际专家的访谈相结合。最终，研究力求提出可操作的政策建议，以强化绿证对中国可再生能源发展的贡献，确保其推动实质性脱碳而非仅停留于形式合规。通过推进全面的制度分析，本项目将深化我们对中国能源治理演进的理解，并为研究能源转型中国家权力与市场工具之间复杂互动的学者与政策制定者提供有益启示。

12100226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12100226.value: 研究豕去氧膽酸作為類風濕性關節炎免疫代謝調控因子的作用

12100226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12100226.value: Prof Lyu, Aiping Prof Xiao, Qingzhong

12100226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12100226.value: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic inflammatory disease marked by dysregulated immune responses within the joint microenvironment. Our recent cohort studies have revealed a distinct alteration in the serum bile acid (BA) profile of RA patients, most notably a significant reduction in hyodeoxycholic acid (HDCA) levels. Parallel investigations using the collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) mouse model demonstrated a similar decline in HDCA accompanied by increased pro-inflammatory (M1) macrophage activity. Our preliminary data indicate that this process involves disrupted de novo fatty acid synthesis and heightened production of pro-inflammatory cytokines, particularly nitric oxide (NO), implicating reprogrammed macrophage metabolism in RA pathogenesis. BAs, including HDCA, are increasingly recognized modulators of both innate and adaptive immunity. Our prior research also indicates that HDCA influences enteroendocrine signaling and interacts with nuclear receptors, such as farnesoid X receptor (FXR) and liver X receptor alpha (LXR-α), which are broadly expressed in metabolic and immune-relevant tissues, such as the liver, adipose tissue, and cells of the monocyte/macrophage lineage. Through the activation or inhibition of these pathways, HDCA can exert significant effects on lipid and cholesterol metabolism, as well as on immune cell function and phenotype (Cell Metabolism 2023). Hence, we hypothesize that HDCA serves as an immunometabolic regulator, mediating cross-talk between fatty acid signaling and the FXR/LXR pathway to modulate macrophage driven inflammation in RA. The central goal of this proposed study is to determine: i) the role of HDCA:FXR/LXR signaling using overexpression and knockdown approaches, and its implications for RA development and persistence; ii) the detailed mechanisms by which HDCA, through FXR/LXR cross talk with fatty acid signaling, reprograms macrophage metabolism to curb de novo lipogenesis, cholesterol handling, and reduce iNOS-derived nitric oxide and pro-inflammatory cytokine production; and iii) the links (i+ii) to human RA immunometabolic traits. Possible outcome: The co-applicants have previously demonstrated that hyocholic acid (HCA) upregulates the BA transporter SLC10A7 in human CD4+ T cells (GRF grant, 2023); HDCA alleviates non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (Cell Metabolism, 2023); Metabolic alterations regulate Treg cell migration (Immunity, 2017). We anticipate that HDCA-driven macrophage metabolic reprogramming via FXR/LXR will be a distinctive feature of RA, enabling the identification of actionable mechanistic targets and supporting the development of BA based immunometabolic therapies for RA and related metabolic inflammatory conditions. 類風濕性關節炎（RA）是一種慢性炎症性疾病，其特徵為關節微環境中的免疫反應失調。我們近期的隊列研究顯示，RA 患者的血清膽汁酸（BA）譜出現顯著改變，尤其是豬去氧膽酸（HDCA）水平顯著下降。平行的膠原誘導性關節炎（CIA）小鼠模型研究亦觀察到類似的 HDCA 減少，並伴隨促炎性（M1 型）巨噬細胞活性增加。我們的初步數據顯示，此過程涉及新生脂肪酸合成受阻，以及促炎性細胞激素（特別是一氧化氮 NO）產量升高，提示巨噬細胞代謝重編程在 RA 發病機制中扮演重要角色。 膽汁酸（包括 HDCA）愈來愈被認為是先天與適應性免疫的調節因子。我們先前的研究亦指出，HDCA 影響腸內分泌訊號，並與核受體交互作用，如法尼醇 X 受體（FXR）與肝臟 X 受體 α（LXR-α），這些受體廣泛表達於代謝與免疫相關組織，包括肝臟、脂肪組織，以及單核球/巨噬細胞系。透過啟動或抑制這些途徑，HDCA 能顯著影響脂質與膽固醇代謝，以及免疫細胞功能與表型（Cell Metabolism 2023）。因此，我們假設 HDCA 作為免疫代謝調控因子，透過脂肪酸訊號與 FXR/LXR 路徑的交互作用，調節巨噬細胞驅動的炎症反應。 本研究的核心目標為： i) 探討 HDCA–FXR/LXR 訊號在 RA 發展與持續中的角色，並利用過度表達與基因敲低方法驗證； ii) 詳細闡明 HDCA 如何透過 FXR/LXR 與脂肪酸訊號交互作用，重編程巨噬細胞代謝，以抑制新生脂質生成、正常化膽固醇處理，並降低 iNOS 衍生的一氧化氮與促炎性細胞激素產生； iii) 將上述機制（i+ii）與人類 RA 的免疫代謝特徵建立聯繫。

12100626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12100626.value: 從腸道淋巴吸收與免疫調控的角度研究多糖構效關係以及與 GP2/TLR4 受體的結合作用

12100626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12100626.value: Polysaccharides are major active ingredients in functional foods and herbal medicines, yet their clinical translation is often hindered by poor knowledge such as how they are absorbed and work in body. Our recent studies have identified a novel and highly selective absorption pathway for Radix Astragalus polysaccharide (RAP) through intestinal lymphatics, in which the Glycoprotein 2 (GP2) receptor on M cells in Peyer's patches (PPs) plays the key role as the mediating receptor. Mechanistic study further revealed the role of Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) on dendritic cells (DC) in the activation of DC-B cell axis induced by absorbed RAP, leading to the production of anti-colitis IgA. These findings arise important questions about the structure-activity relationships (SAR) and binding interactions between the key receptors and polysaccharide structures. Previously, RAP was reported to have a complex and undetermined heteropolysaccharide structure, complicating the SAR analyses. We recently identified RAP to be a mixture of four simpler components having clearly determined structures. Interestingly, despite the most absorbable among them, polygalacturonic acid shows no immunomodulatory effects. We hypothesize that specific structural features of these polysaccharides enhance their binding to GP2 and TLR4, facilitating absorption and immune modulation. This hypothesis is supported by the finding of Xylan as another example of lymph-absorbable but non-immunogenic polysaccharide in our screening of reference standard polysaccharides. Our pilot study found that a hexamer of galacturonic acid binds more strongly to GP2 than smaller oligomers. To further test this hypothesis, the current project aims to: 1) prepare a library of oligosaccharides having the bioactive structures by separating and identifying the products of enzyme hydrolysis of these bioactive polysaccharides; 2) characterize their SAR in terms of GP2/TLR4 binding, lymph absorption, and immune modulation; and 3) optimize the saccharide structures using an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted SAR prediction model and validate their bioactivities. If successful, this will be the first project clarifying clear molecular interactions between polysaccharides and their targeting receptors. The expected results will provide significant insights into the lymphatic absorption pathway of polysaccharides and their immunomodulatory effects, paving the way for the development of polysaccharide-based functional foods and herbal medicines. 多糖是功能食品與中草藥的主要活性成分，但由於對其體內吸收及作用機制認知不足，極大阻礙了其臨床轉化。本團隊前期研究發現黃芪多糖可經一條全新高選擇性腸道淋巴通路吸收，派氏淋巴結 M 細胞上的糖蛋白 2（GP2）是介導該過程的關鍵受體。機制研究進一步證實，被吸收的黃芪多糖可激活樹突狀細胞 B 細胞軸，該過程依賴樹突狀細胞表面的 Toll 樣受體 4（TLR4），最終誘導產生抗結腸炎 IgA 抗體。上述研究引出關鍵科學問題：多糖結構與 GP2、TLR4 受體之間存在怎樣的構效關係與分子結合模式。 以往研究認為黃芪多糖為結構複雜且未完全解析的雜多糖，給構效關係研究帶來困難。本團隊近期將黃芪多糖拆分為 4 種結構明確的組分。其中，多聚半乳糖醛酸吸收能力最強，卻無免疫調節活性。據此提出科學假說：多糖特定結構特徵能夠增強其與 GP2、TLR4 的結合能力，進而實現腸道吸收與免疫調控。 課題組對多糖標準品篩選發現木聚糖同樣可經淋巴吸收，但不具備免疫原性，為該假說提供佐證。前期分子對接與分子動力學模擬預實驗表明，糖單元組成、聚合度等結構特徵會顯著影響多糖與 GP2、TLR4 的結合親和力。為驗證該假說，本項目研究目標如下：1）對活性多糖進行酶解分離鑒定，構建具有生物活性的寡糖分子庫；2）從 GP2/TLR4 受體結合能力、淋巴吸收效率、免疫調節活性三個維度解析其構效關係；3）利用人工智能輔助構效關係預測模型對糖結構進行優化，並開展生物活性驗證。 本項目若取得成功，將首次闡明多糖與靶受體之間的分子相互作用機制。研究成果可為理解多糖的淋巴吸收途徑及其免疫調控效應提供重要理論依據，推動多糖類功能食品與中藥的開發應用。

12100726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12100726.value: 從棕櫚油加工廠到市場：連結企業供應鏈承諾與東南亞森林砍伐及生物多樣性風險

12100726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12100726.value: The planet is undergoing profound transformations as human activities increasingly push the Earth system beyond safe planetary boundaries through climate change, biodiversity loss, and ecosystem degradation. Conservation was once considered primarily the responsibility of governments, but there is growing recognition that corporations—given their economic power, control of supply chains, and global reach—are indispensable actors in addressing environmental challenges. A key mechanism to leverage this influence is Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) reporting, which encourages or mandates disclosure of environmental impacts throughout corporate supply chains, thereby fostering accountability and transparency. For example, some corporations now disclose the origins of the palm oil they use by publishing lists of processing mills and their locations, as the oil-palm industry has been criticized as a major driver of deforestation in Southeast Asia. By publishing mill lists, corporations implicitly or explicitly claim an active role in managing their supply chains to achieve zero-deforestation sourcing. However, skepticism persists regarding the actual effectiveness of such initiatives, as robust empirical evidence linking ESG disclosure to measurable sustainability outcomes remains scarce. This project addresses this critical knowledge gap using the oil-palm supply chain as a model system. Specifically, it investigates whether linkages with downstream manufacturers that demonstrate strong environmental commitments (“E-linkages”) effectively reduce deforestation risk upstream, in the sourcing areas of oil palm, through three complementary approaches. First, we will identify the proximate causes of deforestation surrounding oil-palm plantations and assess how downstream manufacturers manage these drivers by integrating satellite image interpretation, field verification, and interviews with local stakeholders. Second, we will test whether mills with E-linkages are associated with lower deforestation rates and biodiversity loss than those without such linkages by modeling annual deforestation and translating these outcomes into biodiversity impacts. Finally, we will evaluate causality by examining whether recent withdrawals of E-linkages—resulting from corporate supply-chain restructuring—lead to increased deforestation risk. Interviews with manufacturers will provide complementary insights into the motivations, processes, and consequences of these changes. By combining fieldwork, geospatial modeling, and qualitative inquiry, this project will provide novel evidence of how supply-chain linkages identified from company-published mill lists (ESG disclosures) translate into measurable reductions in deforestation and biodiversity loss. The findings will inform policymakers and the private sector about the effectiveness and the limitations of ESG reporting, guiding the development of more robust and evidence-based approaches to sustainable supply-chain governance. 隨著人類活動透過氣候變化、生物多樣性喪失及生態系統退化，日益將地球系統推向甚至超越安全邊界，由此地球正經歷深刻的環境變遷。過去，生物多樣性保育主要被視為政府的責任；然而，企業憑藉其龐大的經濟影響力、對供應鏈的控制能力以及全球性的營運範圍，如今已被廣泛認為是應對環境挑戰不可或缺的參與者。發揮企業影響力的一項重要機制，是環境、社會與管治（Environmental, Social and Governance, ESG）報告制度。此類制度鼓勵或要求企業揭露其整體供應鏈的環境影響，以提高企業問責性與透明度。 例如，由於油棕產業長期被指為東南亞森林砍伐的重要驅動因素，一些企業現已開始公開其所使用棕櫚油的來源，包括公布加工廠（palm oil mills）及其地理位置清單。透過公布加工廠名單，企業或明示、或默示地宣稱其正積極管理供應鏈，以實現零毀林採購。然而，這類措施是否確實能帶來預期的環境成效，仍受到質疑，因為目前能將 ESG 揭露與可量化永續成果直接連結的實證證據仍相當有限。 本研究以棕櫚油供應鏈作為模式系統，針對此一關鍵知識缺口進行研究。具體而言，我們將檢驗：與具有高度環境承諾的下游製造商之間的供應鏈連結（以下稱「環境連結」，E-linkages），是否能有效降低上游油棕產地的森林砍伐風險。研究將採取三項相互補充的方法。 首先，我們將辨識油棕種植區周邊森林砍伐的直接驅動因素，並透過衛星影像判讀、實地查證及訪談當地利益相關者，評估下游製造商如何管理這些驅動因素。 其次，我們將檢驗具有 E-linkages 的加工廠，其周邊森林砍伐率及生物多樣性損失是否低於不具此類連結的加工廠。為此，我們將建立年度森林砍伐模型，並進一步將森林損失轉換為可量化的生物多樣性影響。 最後，我們將透過分析近年企業供應鏈重組所造成的 E-linkages 中斷，評估這些連結與森林砍伐風險之間的因果關係：當企業退出某些加工廠的供應鏈後，當地的森林砍伐風險是否隨之上升？同時，我們亦將訪談相關製造商，以進一步了解企業進行供應鏈重組的動機、過程及其後果。 透過結合實地研究、地理空間模型與質性分析，本研究將提供新的實證證據，說明企業所公布的加工廠名單（即 ESG 揭露中的供應鏈資訊）所呈現的供應鏈連結，如何轉化為可量化的森林砍伐及生物多樣性損失降低成效。研究成果將有助於政策制定者及私營部門更準確地評估 ESG 報告制度的成效與侷限，並為建立更健全、以實證為基礎的永續供應鏈治理機制提供依據。

12100926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12100926.value: 探究TFE3在CAPON介導的阿爾茨海默病Tau蛋白病變中的具體作用及鉤藤鹼的治療潛力

12100926.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12100926.value: Dr Iyaswamy, Ashok Prof Shen, Hanming Prof SONG, Juxian

12100926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12100926.value: Tauopathy, characterized by the abnormal accumulation of hyperphosphorylated tau proteins in the brain, has been shown to have the strongest correlation with the progression of cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Autophagy, which removes cellular waste such as misfolded proteins like tau, is impaired in neurodegenerative diseases (NDs) including AD. Clinical studies have shown that mutations in TFE3, an important regulator of autophagy, can lead to intellectual disabilities. However, the relationship between TFE3 deficiency and cognitive decline in tauopathy has not been studied. Exploring this connection could reveal new therapeutic targets for NDs involving tauopathies. In our pilot study, we found for the first time that Tfe3-knockout (KO) mice exhibited cognitive decline. Expectedly, deficient autophagy and lysosomal biogenesis were detected in the hippocampus. Notably, total and phosphorylated Tau were significantly higher in the hippocampus of Tfe3-KO mice, with no changes in Aβ-related proteins, suggesting the memory deficits are likely caused by tauopathy rather than Aβ pathology. Proteomic analysis identified CAPON, a Tau-binding protein, as a possible mediator of tauopathy in Tfe3-KO mice. CAPON colocalized with Tau and accumulated in the hippocampus, and its levels were negatively regulated by TFE3. Importantly, knocking down CAPON in the hippocampus rescued memory deficits and lowered total and phosphorylated Tau levels, indicating CAPON's role in driving the tauopathy and memory decline. Moreover, CAPON accumulation, impaired autophagy flux, and TFE3 inactivation were observed in the hippocampus of tauopathy AD mice (P301S and 3xTg), further supporting the link between TFE3, CAPON, and AD-related tauopathy. To explore the therapeutic potential, we demonstrated that Corynoxine (Cory), a natural autophagy inducer discovered from Chinese medicine, can rescue learning and memory deficits in 3xTg AD mice. Cory reduced both Tau and CAPON in the hippocampus, possibly via promoting TFE3-mediated autophagy. Based on these findings, we hypothesize that TFE3 deficiency causes memory deficits by inducing tauopathy through CAPON accumulation, and that Cory may mitigate tauopathy-related memory impairment by promoting TFE3-mediated autophagic degradation of the Tau-CAPON complex. This study aims to: 1) Investigate the regulatory mechanisms of CAPON via TFE3-mediated autophagy; 2) Explore CAPON's role in tauopathy and memory deficits through TFE3-mediated autophagy; and 3) Validate Cory's protective effects in reducing tauopathy by enhancing TFE3-mediated autophagic degradation of the Tau-CAPON complex. The findings may reveal TFE3's role in tauopathy and provide a promising strategy for new drug development targeting TFE3. Tau蛋白病症（tauopathy）是指在大腦中異常累積過度磷酸化的Tau蛋白，已被證實與阿茲海默症（AD）認知衰退的進展有較強關聯。自噬作用能清除細胞廢物，例如錯誤摺疊的蛋白質如Tau，但在包括阿茲海默症在內的神經退化性疾病中，神經細胞自噬功能受損。臨床研究顯示，自噬重要調節因子TFE3蛋白的突變可導致智能障礙。然而，TFE3功能缺失與Tau蛋白病相關的認知衰退之間的關係尚未被研究。探索這一關聯有望揭示涉及Tau蛋白病變神經退行性疾病的治療新靶點。 我們的研究首次發現，Tfe3基因敲除小鼠出現認知衰退，海馬區神經細胞的自噬及溶酶體生物合成不足。值得注意的是，Tfe3基因敲除小鼠海馬區總Tau蛋白及磷酸化Tau蛋白水準顯著升高，而澱粉樣蛋白及AD相關蛋白未見變化，顯示記憶缺陷極可能由Tau蛋白病變引起，而非澱粉樣蛋白病理。蛋白質組學分析發現CAPON（一種Tau結合蛋白）為Tfe3基因敲除小鼠Tau蛋白病變的潛在介導因子。CAPON與Tau蛋白共定位並在海馬區累積，其表現受到TFE3蛋白的負向調控。重要的是，在小鼠海馬區下調CAPON能恢復記憶障礙、降低總Tau及磷酸化Tau蛋白水準，顯示CAPON在促進Tau蛋白病變及記憶衰退上具有關鍵作用。此外，在Tau蛋白病變AD小鼠（P301S及3xTg）海馬區亦可發現CAPON蛋白累積、自噬流受損及TFE3失活，進一步支持TFE3、CAPON與AD相關Tau蛋白病變間的聯繫。同時，我們發現源於中藥鉤藤的天然自噬誘導劑「釣藤鹼」（Corynoxine）能夠減少海馬區的Tau及CAPON蛋白積聚，可改善3xTg AD小鼠的學習與記憶障礙。釣藤鹼可能是透過促進TFE3介導的神經細胞自噬而發揮作用。 基於以上發現，我們假設TFE3功能缺失會誘導CAPON蛋白積聚，致使Tau蛋白病變引起記憶功能障礙，而釣藤鹼可藉促進TFE3介導的自噬降解Tau-CAPON複合體以減緩Tau蛋白病變導致的記憶損傷。本研究目標為：(1)探討CAPON經由TFE3介導自噬的調控機制；(2)研究CAPON在Tau蛋白病變及記憶缺陷中扮演的角色；(3)驗證釣藤鹼通過促進TFE3介導自噬降解Tau-CAPON複合體減少Tau蛋白病變的神經保護效應。研究結果有望揭示TFE3於Tau蛋白病變中的作用並提供以TFE3為標靶之新藥開發策略。

12101126.value: 脂肪細胞Sclerostin-loop3-LRP4相互作用貢獻硬骨抑素導致全身糖脂代謝紊亂

12101126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12101126.value: Dr JIANG, Hewen Dr LI, Dijie Dr WANG, Luyao Prof ZHOU, Hong

12101126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12101126.value: Serum sclerostin was significantly higher in postmenopausal osteoporosis (POP) patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (POP-T2DM) than either POP or T2DM patients in our epidemic analysis. Sclerostin knock-in/overproduction (SOST-KI/AAV-SOST) impaired whole-body lipid/glucose metabolism, while either sclerostin knock-out (SOST-KO) or the marketed antibody mainly targeting sclerostin-loop2 (Scl-Ab) treatment improved whole-body lipid/glucose metabolism in high-fat diet (HFD)-induced diabetic mice. However, FDA/EMA warned the cardiovascular risk of Scl-Ab in POP patients. We have published that sclerostin-loop3 domain contributes to the antagonistic effect of sclerostin on bone formation, whereas sclerostin-loop2 contributes to its cardioprotective action. Moreover, we found that whole-body lipid/glucose metabolism was improved in loop3-deficient-sclerostin knock-in (Δloop3-SOST-KI) mice compared to SOST-KI mice. Targeting sclerostin-loop3 by sclerostin-loop3-specific aptamer attenuated HFD-induced whole-body lipid/glucose metabolism disorders. This proposal will further address how sclerostin-loop3 contributes to the impairing effects of sclerostin on whole-body lipid/glucose metabolism. We further identified sclerostin-loop3-LRP4 interaction instead of the canonical sclerostin-LRP5/6 interaction. Lrp4 deficiency in adipocytes improved whole-body lipid/glucose metabolism reportedly. To determine whether sclerostin-loop3-LRP4 interaction in adipocytes participated in impairing whole-body lipid/glucose metabolism, Lrp4 mutation (Lrp4m) and blocking peptide (LRP4-BP) was designed to block the sclerostin-loop3-LRP4 interaction in human/mouse adipocytes, respectively. Genetically, Lrp4m improved lipid/glucose metabolism in vitro and in adipocytic (Ad).Lrp4m mice. By injection of AAV-SOST into Ad.Lrp4m mice (n=3) after shielding endogenous sclerostin (SOST-KO), SOST-KO/Ad.Lrp4m mice showed no change in whole-body lipid/glucose metabolism, whereas SOST-KO mice exhibited an impaired whole-body lipid/glucose metabolism. Pharmacologically, adipose tissue-targeting blocking peptide (Ad-LRP4-BP)-induced blockade of sclerostin-loop3-LRP4 interaction attenuated the impairing effects of sclerostin on lipid/glucose metabolism in SOST-KI mice (n=3). Together, we hypothesized that sclerostin-loop3-LRP4 interaction in adipocytes could be required by sclerostin to impair whole-body lipid/glucose metabolism. To test it using the above mouse models with larger sample-size, we have three aims: Aim 1: To determine the role of sclerostin-loop3-LRP4 interaction in adipocytes in sclerostin-impaired whole-body lipid/glucose metabolism by comparing the difference between SOST-KO/Ad.Lrp4m and SOST-KO mice, with/without injection of AAV-SOST. Aim 2: To determine the role of sclerostin-loop3-LRP4 interaction in adipocytes in sclerostin-impaired whole-body lipid/glucose metabolism by comparing the difference between SOST-KI mice with/without Ad-LRP4-BP treatment. Aim 3: To evaluate whether Ad-LRP4-BP could improve whole-body lipid/glucose metabolism in ovariectomized (OVX) mice with HFD by comparing the difference between OVX + HFD mice with/without Ad-LRP4-BP treatment. Translationally, specific blockade of sclerostin-loop3-LRP4 interaction in adipocytes would provide a precise sclerostin inhibition strategy without cardiovascular risk to normalize whole-body lipid/glucose metabolism in POP-T2DM patients.

12101326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12101326.value: 擬南芥PWO 蛋白通過與DXO1互作作為m7G mRNA加帽的新調控因子

12101326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12101326.value: abstract Eukaryotic mRNAs typically carry a 7-methylguanosine (m7G) cap that coordinates key steps in transcription, mRNA processing, and translation. Although m7G capping was long considered constitutive, recent studies suggest that cap formation can be dynamically regulated by developmental and environmental cues. Additionally, some RNAs have been found to carry non-canonical caps, such as the NAD cap, highlighting a more complex role for RNA capping in gene regulation. As sessile organisms continuously exposed to fluctuating conditions, plants rely on highly plastic gene regulatory mechanisms—including dynamic control of m7G capping—to mount rapid, context-specific responses to external stimuli. Recent studies have identified Arabidopsis DXO1 as an important multi-tasking regulatory hub in mediating various transcriptional and post-transcriptional processes. DXO1 was initially identified as a decapping enzyme for non-canonical NAD-capped RNAs and as a 5'–3' exonuclease. We recently discovered that DXO1 also functions as a key regulator of canonical m7G capping: the plant-specific N-terminal extension of DXO1 binds to and activates the RNA cap methyltransferase RNMT1, which catalyzes the formation of the m7G cap. More recently, we found that DXO1 interacts with PWWP-DOMAIN INTERACTOR OF POLYCOMBS (PWO) family proteins, which are known to be involved in chromatin remodeling. Our preliminary data suggest that DXO1 is recruited into PWO condensates within the nucleus, rendering it inaccessible for association with and activation of RNMT1. This indicates that PWOs act as negative regulators of m7G capping. This project aims to reveal the role of PWOs as novel mediators of m7G capping. We will test the hypothesis that PWOs regulate m7G capping through competitive binding, partitioning DXO1 between PWO–DXO1 condensates and a discrete RNMT1–DXO1 capping complex. Additionally, we will identify target genes whose mRNAs undergo PWO-dependent m7G capping and investigate how environmental cues such as light and darkness influence DXO1 sequestration by PWOs. Together, this study will elucidate a plant-specific mechanism for dynamic regulation of m7G mRNA capping in response to environmental signals. 真核生物的 mRNA 通常在 5' 端攜帶 7-甲基鳥苷（m7G）帽，協調轉錄、mRNA 加工與翻譯等關鍵步驟。儘管 m7G 加帽長期被視為組成型的過程，但近期研究表明，帽的形成可受發育與環境線索的動態調控。此外，已有研究發現部分 RNA 攜帶非經典帽（如 NAD 帽），凸顯 RNA 加帽在基因調控中的作用更為複雜。作為長期暴露於多變環境的固著性生物，植物依賴高度可塑的基因調控機制——包括對 m7G 加帽的動態控制——以對外界刺激作出快速且情境特異的反應。 近年的研究將擬南芥 DXO1 鑑定為介導多種轉錄與轉錄後過程的重要多功能調控樞紐。DXO1 起初被發現是非典型 NAD 帽 RNA 的去帽酶，同時也是一種 5'–3' 外切核酸酶。我們近期發現，DXO1 亦是經典 m7G 加帽的關鍵調控因子：其植物特異的 N 端延伸可結合並激活 RNA 帽甲基轉移酶 RNMT1，催化 m7G 帽的形成。更進一步地，我們發現 DXO1 可與 PWWP-DOMAIN INTERACTOR OF POLYCOMBS（PWO）家族蛋白互作，該家族已知參與染色質重塑。我們的初步數據表明，DXO1 被招募至細胞核內的 PWO 凝聚體，使其無法與 RNMT1 結合並被其激活，這表明 PWO 充當 m7G 加帽的負向調控因子。 本項目旨在揭示 PWO 作為 m7G 加帽新型媒介者的作用。我們將檢驗以下假說：PWO 通過競爭性結合，在 PWO–DXO1 凝聚體與 RNMT1–DXO1 加帽複合體之間分配 DXO1，從而調控 m7G 加帽。此外，我們將鑑定其 mRNA 的 m7G 加帽依賴 PWO 的靶基因，並探究光照與黑暗等環境線索如何影響 PWO 對 DXO1 的要抑制。綜上，本研究將闡明一種植物特異的機制，解釋植物如何響應環境信號而動態調控 mRNA 的 m7G 加帽。

12101526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12101526.value: 解密染料木素在帕金森氏症中的神經保護機制

12101526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12101526.value: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a relentlessly progressive neurodegenerative disorder for which no disease-modifying therapy currently exists. Our research identifies the soy isoflavone genistein—a chemical that can be found in many traditional Chinese medicine (TCM)—as a promising neuroprotective agent for dopaminergic neurons in vivo. However, the mechanisms underlying its effects remain unclear. In MPTP-induced Mito-QC mice, daily intraperitoneal administration of genistein (5 or 10 mg/kg body weight) for 4 weeks restored tyrosine hydroxylase–positive neuron counts to 92 % of wild-type levels and reversed motor deficits, as evidenced by open-field, hindlimb clasping, and DigiGait assays. Preliminary pharmacokinetics demonstrated brain concentrations of 4.87 ng/ml following oral dosing (5 mg/kg body weight). Additionally, a solubility-optimized genistein derivative achieved a fivefold increase in brain permeability without toxicity. Mechanistically, analysis of publicly available proteomic datasets revealed mitochondrial dysfunction and impaired mitophagy in neurons from PD patients. A high-throughput mitophagy reporter screening identified genistein as the top flavonoid enhancer of mKeima-Red signal. In N27 dopaminergic cells treated with MPP⁺ or α-synuclein (α-syn), genistein prevented mitochondrial fragmentation, promoted DRP1-Ser616 phosphorylation, and facilitated PINK1 recruitment to depolarized mitochondria, thereby driving LC3-I/LC3-II conversion and facilitating α-syn clearance. Co-immunoprecipitation and proximity-ligation assays demonstrated that α-syn directly sequesters DRP1, and genistein disrupts this interaction, restoring mitochondrial fission-fusion balance. Importantly, CRISPR-mediated DRP1 knockout abolished genistein-induced mitophagy and neuroprotection, confirming dependence on DRP1. Building on these findings, we hypothesize that genistein mitigates mitochondrial fragmentation and restores mitophagy activation in PD, providing a novel treatment strategy for PD. This study aims to further elucidate genistein’s mechanism of action in promoting mitophagy through a multifaceted approach involving molecular, cellular, and transgenic animal models. Our specific objectives are to: 1. Validate genistein's mitophagy-activating potential in A53T-Mito-QC transgenic primary dopamine neurons; 2. Delineate the mechanisms of α-syn-DRP1 modulating mitophagy in N27 dopaminergic and iPSC-derived dopamine neurons; and, 3. Evaluate the therapeutic efficacy and safety of genistein in A53T transgenic PD mice model. We anticipate that this research will decipher the role of genistein in mitigating mitophagy impairment in PD. By uncovering its therapeutic mechanisms, we aim to pave the way for innovative treatments that not only restore mitochondrial function but also slow down the progression of this debilitating neurodegenerative disease. 帕金森病（PD）是一種持續惡化的神經退化性疾病，目前尚無任何能延緩或改變疾病進程的治療方法。我們發現長期作為中藥使用的植物大豆異黃酮「染料木素」（genistein），能在活體內為多巴胺神經元提供強效的神經保護作用。然而，其治療機制仍有待進一步闡明。 在 MPTP 誘導的 Mito-QC 小鼠模型中，每日口服染料木素（每公斤體重 5 或 10 毫克）可將酪氨酸羥化酶陽性神經元數量恢復至野生型的 92%，並透過曠場實驗、後肢抱緊實驗和 DigiGait 步態分析證實其逆轉了運動功能障礙。在機制方面，對公開蛋白質組學數據集的分析一致顯示帕金森病患者神經元中存在線粒體功能障礙和線粒體自噬受損。高通量線粒體自噬報告基因篩選將染料木素確定為增強 mKeima-Red 信號最強的黃酮類物質。在經 MPP⁺ 或 α-絲核蛋白（α-syn）處理的 N27 多巴胺細胞中，染料木素能預防線粒體過度碎片化，促進 DRP1-Ser616 磷酸化，並將 PINK1 招募至去極化的線粒體，從而驅動 LC3-II/LC3-I 轉化並促進 α-syn 的清除。免疫共沉澱和近接標記技術顯示，α-syn 會直接封鎖截留 DRP1；而染料木素打破了這種相互作用，恢復了線粒體分裂與融合的動態平衡。CRISPR 介導的 DRP1 基因敲除阻斷了染料木素誘導的線粒體自噬和神經保護作用，證實了其對 DRP1 的依賴性。初步藥代動力學研究表明，口服給藥後腦內濃度可達 3.2 µM，且一種溶解度優化的染料木素衍生物在無毒性的情況下將腦部滲透率提高了五倍。 基於這些初步發現，我們假設染料木素能減緩帕金森病中的線粒體碎片化並恢復線粒體自噬的激活，從而提供一種治療帕金森病的新型治療策略。本研究旨在透過結合分子、細胞及轉基因動物模型的多維度方法，進一步闡明染料木素促進線粒體自噬的作用機制。 我們的具體目標包括： 1. 在 A53T-Mito-QC 轉基因原代多巴胺神經元中，驗證染料木素激活線粒體自噬的潛力； 2. 確定其分子標靶，並在 N27 多巴胺神經元及 iPSC 誘導分化的多巴胺神經元中，闡明 α-syn-DRP1 調控線粒體自噬的機制；以及 3. 在 A53T 轉基因小鼠和 MPTP 誘導的帕金森病模型中，評估染料木素的治療功效與安全性。 我們預期本研究將明確染料木素在解決帕金森病線粒體自噬障礙中的作用。透過揭示其治療機制，我們旨在為創新治療方案奠定基礎，不僅能恢復線粒體功能，更能延緩這種嚴重神經退化性疾病的病程。

12101626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12101626.value: 布氏線蟲與新鑑定之尼氏線蟲野生分離株間完全外顯性雜交 F1 致死之遺傳與分子機制鑑定

12101626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12101626.value: Speciation, the process by which new biological species arise, is often driven by the accumulation of genetic incompatibilities that cause hybrid dysfunction. While hybrid inviability and sterility are well-documented, the precise genetic elements and molecular mechanisms underlying these postzygotic barriers remain poorly understood. This project aims to dissect the molecular bases of hybrid F1 lethality (HL) between two closely related nematode species, Caenorhabditis briggsae and C. nigoni. We have identified an inbred strain of C. nigoni, ZZY1071, which, when crossed with C. briggsae males, produces 100% lethal F1 hybrid progeny. This complete penetrant phenotype presents a powerful system for dissecting the genetic and molecular bases of the hybrid F1 lethality. Our preliminary data exclude cytonuclear incompatibility as the cause, pointing instead to an epistatic interaction between the nuclear genomes of the two species. The central objective of this proposal is to map, clone, and validate the causative HL genes from both the C. briggsae and C. nigoni genomes. We will employ a sophisticated genetic mapping strategy utilizing a pre-existing library of C. nigoni strains carrying fluorescently marked C. briggsae genomic introgressions in the JU1421 background. The C. briggsae-specific HL locus will be mapped by crossing JU1421 males carrying individual introgressions to ZZY1071 females—a scheme that circumvents the HL unless the introgression fragment contains the HL locus. Conversely, the C. nigoni-specific locus will be mapped by crossing C. briggsae males with ZZY1071 females that carry the C. briggsae introgressions. These females will be achieved by crossing our existing C. nigoni strains carrying C. briggsae introgressions in the JU1421 background to ZZY1071 followed by backcrossing. To overcome the suppression of recombination between these species—a major bottleneck in fine-mapping—we will leverage our established CRISPR/Cas9-mediated targeted recombination technique. This will allow us to narrow the HL loci to intervals small enough for molecular cloning. Candidate genes will be validated through systematic CRISPR/Cas9 knockout and complementation tests in both species' backgrounds. Furthermore, we have designed a novel biochemical contingency approach. Should maternal effects confound genetic analysis, we will use co-immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry to identify protein-protein interactions between the tagged C. briggsae HL gene product and its incompatible partner from C. nigoni. The successful completion of this work will offer profound insights into the mechanisms of hybrid incompatibility and speciation. Our innovative integration of classic genetics, cutting-edge genomics, and biochemistry will establish a new paradigm for dissecting reproductive isolation.

12101726.value: PROTAC策略靶向降解核內uPA以抑制胰腺癌的神經周圍侵襲

12101726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12101726.value: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the most lethal cancers. Over 90% of all PDAC cases exhibit perineural invasion (PNI), which contributes to severe neuropathic pain and significantly decreased survival time. During PNI, a key mediator - Schwann cells (SCs) are activated to remodel the neural microenvironment for facilitating tumor invasion. However, how PDAC cells activate SCs to drive PNI remains poorly understood, and no current therapies are available for targeting PNI. We analyzed PDAC patient transcriptomic datasets and identified urokinase-type plasminogen activator (uPA) significantly associated with PNI severity and poor prognosis. In our murine PNI model of PDAC, the expressions of uPA and SC marker GFAP were positively correlated. In a PDAC-SC coculture system, knockdown of tumor-derived uPA significantly attenuated tumor-induced SCs proliferation and migration. Conventionally, uPA has been widely studied for its degrading the extracellular matrix functions that promotes tumor metastasis. However, we discovered that uPA localizes in the nucleus of PDAC cells, where the nuclear uPA acts as a transcriptional co-activator, binding to the transcription factor c-Jun and promoting the expression of pro-neurogenetic genes. This leads to increased secretion of pro-neural factors from PDAC cells for SC activation. uPA nuclear import is mediated by nucleolin. Excitingly, blocking the uPA–nucleolin interaction with a nucleolin-targeting aptamer significantly reduced uPA nucleus translocation in PDAC cells, and consequently disrupted the uPA’s transcriptional function and decreased secretion of pro-neural factors, leading to inhibited SCs activation both in vitro and in vivo. In contrast, using conventional extracellular uPA protease inhibitor, Upamostat, had no effect on SCs activation, further confirmed the nuclear action of uPA. To target nuclear uPA, we developed a novel PROTAC strategy that directs ubiquitin-mediated degradation of intracellular uPA. PROTAC-uPA-3 effectively decreased uPA level in nucleus, suppressed uPA-driven transcriptional programs, and consequently inhibited SC proliferation and migration in co-culture assays. In a piolet study, PROTAC-uPA-3 treatment dramatically inhibited PNI progression compared with control in our murine PNI model. Therefore, we hypothesize that uPA functions as a transcriptional coactivator in PDAC to drive SC-mediated PNI, and PROTAC-uPA-3-induced degradation of uPA will disrupt this pathogenic signaling axis and effectively inhibit PNI. we will achieve the following aims: 1)To demonstrate the anti-PNI efficacy of PROTAC uPA 3 in our murine PNI model. 2)To define structural determinants of uPA's nuclear translocation and coactivator function. 3)To elucidate how uPA modulates c-Jun's transcriptional functions. 胰腺導管腺癌（PDAC）是最致命的腫瘤之一。超過90%的PDAC病例存在神經周圍侵犯（PNI），這不僅導致嚴重的神經病理性疼痛，還顯著縮短患者生存期。在PNI過程中，關鍵媒介——施萬細胞（SCs）被激活以重塑神經微環境，從而促進腫瘤侵襲。然而，PDAC細胞如何激活SCs以驅動PNI仍不清楚，目前也缺乏針對PNI的有效治療。 我們分析了PDAC患者的轉錄組數據集，發現尿激酶型纖溶酶原激活物（uPA）與PNI的嚴重程度及不良預後顯著相關。在我們的PDAC小鼠PNI模型中，uPA與施萬細胞標誌物GFAP的表達呈正相關。在PDAC–SC共培養體系中，敲低腫瘤來源的uPA顯著減弱了腫瘤誘導的SCs增殖與遷移。 經典研究普遍認為uPA通過降解細胞外基質、促進腫瘤轉移的作用而發揮功能。然而，我們發現uPA定位於PDAC細胞核內，核內uPA作為轉錄共激活因子，與轉錄因子c-Jun結合，促進促神經生成基因的表達。這導致PDAC細胞分泌更多促神經性因子，從而激活SCs。uPA進入細胞核的過程由核仁蛋白（nucleolin）介導。令人振奮的是，利用靶向核仁蛋白的核酸適配體阻斷uPA–核仁蛋白相互作用，顯著減少了PDAC細胞中uPA的入核，從而破壞其轉錄功能並降低促神經性因子的分泌，進而在體內外均可抑制SCs的激活。相反，使用傳統的細胞外uPA蛋白酶抑制劑Upamostat對SCs的激活無影響，進一步證實了uPA的核內作用。 為靶向核內uPA，我們開發了一種新型PROTAC（蛋白降解靶向嵌合體）策略，誘導對細胞內uPA的泛素介導降解。PROTAC-uPA-3可有效降低細胞核內uPA水平，抑制uPA驅動的轉錄程序，並在共培養實驗中抑制SCs的增殖與遷移。在一項初步研究中，在我們的鼠PNI模型中，與對照相比，PROTAC-uPA-3處理顯著抑制了PNI的進展。 因此，我們假設uPA在PDAC中作為轉錄共激活因子，驅動由SCs介導的PNI，而通過PROTAC-uPA-3降解uPA將破壞這一致病性信號軸並有效抑制PNI。我們將實現以下目標：1）在我們的小鼠PNI模型中證明PROTAC-uPA-3的抗PNI療效；2）界定uPA核內轉運及其共激活功能的結構決定因素；3）闡明uPA如何調控c-Jun的轉錄功能。

12103126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12103126.value: 基於 Stereo-seq 和 MiP-seq 空間轉錄組技術解析單、雙子葉植物花序與花發育過程

12103126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12103126.value: Prof Kong, Hongzhi Prof Xia, Yiji

12103126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12103126.value: Both Monocots and Eudicots originated from a common ancestor but have subsequently undergone significant divergence in gene expression patterns, functional constraints, and post-replication fates during their prolonged evolutionary journey. Flowers, especially inflorescence, are the most complex structures in plants and act as a hallmark feature of the evolution from cryptophytes to flowering plants. The origin and diversification of flowers not only helped the angiosperms to reproduce more efficiently, but also tremendously enriched Earth's biodiversity through co-evolution with pollinators. However, the information on structurally-resolved cell-type specific inflorescence and flower gene expression are still largely unknown. Our recent published single-cell multi-omics work reveals possible mechanisms driving rice floral primordium formation. Developmental trajectories showed that ovule, ovarywall, filament and stamen cells occupied distinct terminal positions potentially arising from specific floral meristem subsets. Although these single cell RNA sequencing (ScRNA-seq) information gave us a hint about the cell type heterogeneity during flower development, floral tissues must be digested into single-cell or single-nucleus suspension, which loses the spatial positional information of cells within the original tissue and the neighborhood relationships between cells. The recent rapid advancement of spatial transcriptomics ingeniously integrates molecular-level (gene expression) information with tissue morphology (cell location). Its core value lies in accurately identifying sub-populations of cells with distinct functional regions and their gene expression characteristics within tissues, while also revealing inter-cellular interactions and spatial transmission of cell signals during developmental processes. ‘Stereo-seq’ is a high-throughput, whole-transcriptomic capture platform, which gives whole atlas of the gene expression. While ‘MiP-seq’ is a high-resolution, multi-omics platform optimized for fine-scale mapping. It is used as targeted validation of findings from high-throughput Stereo-seq. This project will systematically apply Stereo-seq and MiP-seq to unravel inflorescence and flower development at different developmental stages of Monocots and Eudicots, providing high-precision spatial heterogeneity of gene expression landscape and regulatory networks. The floral organ development-related genes, such as the MADS-box gene family which are highly conserved in sequence, would be analyzed in the structurally-specific way. It is also expected to discover a new batch of key genes and pathways regulating flower development, and elucidate their spatially specific functions which might be related to the fundamental ABCE model, providing a comprehensive and feasible technical route for in-depth research on plant flower development. This project would provide important genetic resources and theoretical basis for Angiosperm genetic improvement of flower morphology, molecular breeding, and quality improvement. 單子葉植物與真雙子葉植物雖源自共同祖先，但在漫長的演化歷程中，二者的基因表達模式、功能約束以及複製後命運隨後發生了顯著分化。花器官，尤其是花序，是植物體內結構最為複雜的構造，也是隱花植物向開花植物演化的標誌性特徵。花的起源與多樣化不僅讓被子植物具備更高效率的繁殖能力，更透過與傳粉生物的協同演化，極大地豐富了地球的生物多樣性。然而，具備空間結構解析度、細胞類型特異性的花序與花器官基因表達資訊，目前仍有大量內容尚未被闡明。 本團隊近期發表的單細胞多組學研究，揭示了驅動水稻花原基形成的潛在分子機制。發育軌跡分析顯示，胚珠、子房壁、花絲及雄蕊細胞各自處於分化終端的不同位置，推測其源自花分生組織內不同的亞群細胞。儘管單細胞轉錄組測序（ScRNA-seq）數據為我們揭示了花發育過程中的細胞類型異質性，但該技術需要將花組織酶解為單細胞或單細胞核懸浮液，會丟失細胞在原始組織中的空間位置資訊，以及細胞間的鄰接互作關係。 近年空間轉錄組技術飛速發展，該技術巧妙地將分子層級（基因表達）資訊與組織形態（細胞空間定位）相整合。其核心價值在於可精準定位組織內不同功能區域的細胞亞群及其基因表達特徵，同時解析發育過程中的細胞間相互作用與細胞訊號的空間傳遞規律。Stereo-seq 是一款高通量全轉錄組捕獲平台，可構建完整的基因表達圖譜；MiP-seq 則是為微尺度精細定位優化的高解析度多組學平台，用於對高通量 Stereo-seq 的研究結果進行靶向驗證。 本研究計畫將系統運用 Stereo-seq 與 MiP-seq 兩項技術，解析單子葉植物與真雙子葉植物不同發育階段的花序及花器官發育機制，構建高精度的基因表達空間異質性圖譜與調控網路。針對序列高度保守的花器官發育關鍵基因（例如 MADS-box 基因家族）開展結構特異性解析，預期篩選出一批調控花發育的全新關鍵基因與信號通路，並闡述其具空間特異性的生物學功能，探究其與經典 ABCE 花器官發育模型的關聯，為植物花發育的深度研究建立一套完整可行的技術體系。本課題將為被子植物花型遺傳改良、分子育種與品質提升提供重要的遺傳資源與理論依據。

12103926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12103926.value: 探討一種新型滑膜交叉通訊：成纖維樣滑膜細胞外泌體miRNA在類風濕性關節炎中驅動巨噬細胞致病性重編程

12103926.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12103926.value: Prof Chen, Hubiao Prof Liu, Jin

12103926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12103926.value: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an incurable autoimmune disease wherein pathogenic crosstalk between fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLSs) and macrophages perpetuates synovial inflammation. Current therapies inadequately disrupt this microenvironmental dialogue, highlighting the critical need to identify specific mediators for transformative therapies. Despite the established role of exosomes in mediating intercellular communication, the specific function of FLS exosomal miRNAs in the FLS-macrophage dialogue remains largely unknown. We previously observed that FLSs from RA patients secreted significantly more exosomes than normal FLS. MiRNA sequencing of these RA-FLS exosomes revealed a broad upregulation of let-7 family miRNAs. We then performed a comparative miRNA sequencing from an adjuvant-induced arthritis (AIA) rat model and found let-7f-5p (log2FC=1.87), let-7g-5p (log2FC=1.84), and let-7i-5p (log2FC=2.06) also showed marked elevation when compared to normal FLS. These results confirmed our observation in human RA-FLS samples also accrued in AIA rats. GO enrichment analysis suggested a role of such elevated miRNAs in immune cell metabolic reprogramming. In vitro, RA-FLS exosomes traffic into human macrophages to induce pro-inflammatory M1-like phenotype, characterized by elevated CD86 expression, increased TNF-α/IL-6, reduced TGF-β/IL-10, impaired phagocytosis/migration, and a proteomic profile resembling RA patient synovial macrophages. This effect was abolished by global miRNA knockdown. In AIA rats, intra-articular injection of RA-FLS exosomes exacerbated disease and promoted synovial macrophage M1 polarization, with increased TNF-α/IL-6 and reduced TGF-β/IL-10 secretion, which was not observed with exosomes from miRNA-knockdown FLSs. To probe the therapeutic potential of this pathway, we repurposed scopoletin and syringin (Sco+Syr), an anti-RA natural compound combination from our prior research. We found that Sco+Syr specifically reduced RA-FLS exosomal let-7 levels without altering total exosome secretion or direct effects on macrophages. Exosomes from Sco+Syr-conditioned RA-FLSs prevented M1 polarization, an effect reversed by let-7 replenishment, positioning Sco+Syr as a precise pharmacological tool for targeting the synovial crosstalk. It is therefore hypothesized that RA-FLS exosomal miRNAs drive pathogenic macrophage reprogramming and RA progression, and that this axis is a druggable target. Our objectives are: 1) To establish the causal role of RA-FLS exosomal miRNAs in driving macrophage reprogramming and RA pathology, using gain- and loss-of-function exosome approaches in AIA rats; and 2) To validate whether the therapeutic effect of Sco+Syr is dependent on the suppression of RA-FLS exosomal let-7 miRNAs, via let-7 replenishment rescue experiments. This work will elucidate a novel mechanism in RA progression, providing a foundational strategy for precision therapy targeting pathogenic synovial crosstalk. 類風濕性關節炎（RA）是一種目前無法治癒的自體免疫疾病，其病理特徵為成纖維樣滑膜細胞（FLS）與巨噬細胞之間的致病性交叉通訊，持續加劇滑膜組織的炎症反應。現有療法難以有效阻斷此微環境中的細胞對話，因此，識別其中關鍵的介質，對於開發革新性療法至關重要。 外泌體（exosomes）在細胞間通訊中的作用已廣為人知，但FLS外泌體中的微小核糖核酸（miRNA）在FLS與巨噬細胞交互作用中的具體功能仍不清楚。我們的先前研究發現，RA病患的FLS會分泌比正常FLS更多的外泌體，且對這些外泌體進行miRNA測序後，發現let-7家族的miRNA普遍顯著上調。此現象亦在佐劑誘導性關節炎（AIA）大鼠模型中得到驗證。生物資訊學分析提示，這些上調的miRNA可能參與了免疫細胞的代謝重編程。體外實驗證實，RA-FLS外泌體能進入巨噬細胞，誘導其向促炎性的M1表型分化，並抑制其吞噬與遷移能力。此效應可被全面敲降miRNA所消除。 我們假設，RA-FLS分泌的外泌體miRNA是驅動巨噬細胞致病性重編程及RA病程惡化的關鍵因素，且此一信號軸可作為藥物標靶。本研究旨在：1）利用功能增益/缺失的外泌體，在AIA大鼠模型中確立RA-FLS外泌體miRNA在驅動巨噬細胞重編程與RA病理進程中的因果關係；2）透過miRNA回補救援實驗，驗證我們前期研發的抗RA天然藥物組合（東莨菪內酯與紫丁香苷）的療效，是否依賴於其抑制RA-FLS外泌體中let-7 miRNA的能力。 本研究將闡明RA病程進展中的一個新型分子機制，為開發針對滑膜組織致病性交叉通訊的精準療法，提供重要的理論基礎與策略。

12104126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12104126.value: Clinical studies have suggested an association between human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) and biliary atresia (BA), a life-threatening disease in neonates due to cholangiopathy of the bile duct, but it remains poorly understood without a proper study model. The etiology of BA is likely multifactorial, where biological factors such as epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and viral factors from HCMV can contribute to the development of BA. EMT is a characteristic of the bile duct epithelial cells, or cholangiocytes, which can lead to fibrosis and result in cholestasis. Though little is known of the relationship between HCMV and EMT. Interestingly, using an induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived cholangiocyte organoid model, we generated preliminary data that showed HCMV strain TB40/E-eGFP can successfully infect the cholangiocytes and brought drastic effects on the organoid structure and function post-infection. Viral gene expression indicative of productive infection was detected, with a low level of viral replication being detected. Furthermore, our current RNA-seq data showed that the differential expression genes (DEGs) between mock and HCMV-infected organoids are highly enriched in the EMT pathway. RT-qPCR and immunostaining data verified that HCMV infection decreased the E-cadherin expression and increased N- N-cadherin expression. In addition, we found that HCMV infection of cholangiocytes led to the upregulation of TGF-beta, where inhibition of its downstream signalling abrogated the induced EMT genes and organoid deformity, which suggests that HCMV can mediate cholangiopathy. The first aim of the proposed study is to characterise how HCMV affects cholangiocyte organoid defects via the induction of the EMT canonical and non-canonical pathway, as well as TGF-beta signalling. scRNA-seq will be performed to correlate with the results and to define new cell subsets, viral gene expression profiles, and host pathway changes. The second aim involves characterising it by examining the barrier function of the infected organoids, the modulation of the immune pathways by HCMV and correlation studies with glioblastoma, which had been reported to be associated with HCMV-induced EMT. 臨床研究顯示，人類巨細胞病毒（HCMV）與膽道閉鎖（BA）之間具有關聯性。膽道閉鎖是一種因膽管病變所致的新生兒致命性疾病，惟目前因缺乏適當的研究模型，其致病機轉仍不甚明瞭。膽道閉鎖的病因可能為多因素所致，其中生物學因子如上皮間質轉化（EMT）及HCMV病毒因子均可能參與疾病進程。EMT為膽管上皮細胞（即膽管細胞）之重要特徵變化，可能導致纖維化並引起膽汁鬱積。然而，目前對HCMV與EMT之間關聯的了解仍十分有限。 值得關注的是，我們利用誘導型多潛能幹細胞（iPSC）衍生之膽管細胞類器官模型，初步結果顯示HCMV TB40/E-eGFP病毒株可成功感染膽管細胞，並在感染後對類器官之結構與功能產生顯著影響。我們偵測到具有產毒性感染特徵之病毒基因表現，並觀察到低度病毒複製。此外，目前之RNA-seq數據顯示，對照組與HCMV感染組類器官之差異表現基因（DEGs）顯著富集於EMT路徑。RT-qPCR及免疫染色結果證實，HCMV感染可降低E-鈣黏蛋白之表現並增加N-鈣黏蛋白之表現。 進一步研究發現，HCMV感染膽管細胞會導致TGF-β表現上升，而抑制其下游訊息傳導則可消除HCMV誘導之EMT相關基因表現及類器官變形，顯示HCMV可能透過此機制媒介膽管病變。 本研究之第一項目標，旨在闡明HCMV如何透過誘導EMT經典路徑、非經典路徑及TGF-β訊息傳導，造成膽管細胞類器官之缺損。我們將進行單細胞RNA定序（scRNA-seq），以整合分析上述結果，並定義新的細胞亞群、病毒基因表現圖譜及宿主路徑變化。第二項目標則進一步探討感染類器官之屏障功能、HCMV對免疫路徑之調控，並進行與膠質母細胞瘤（已有文獻指出其與HCMV誘導之EMT相關）之相關性研究，以全面釐清其作用機制。

12104326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12104326.value: 從傳統中藥猴棗到功能性食品：尿石素作為兒童呼吸健康的新型干預策略

12104326.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12104326.value: Dr Dai, Xiaoyong Dr Zhang, Quanwei Dr ZHU, Peili

12104326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12104326.value: Respiratory tract infections are highly prevalent among pediatric population worldwide. Existing approaches fail to provide comprehensive protection, highlighting the need for safe and sustainable interventions. Goat Bezoar (Hóu Zǎo, concretion from goat caecum), a traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) valued above gold, has been used for centuries across China and Southeast Asia for treatment of pediatric respiratory inflammation. Today, Goat Bezoar serves as a principal constituent in over 300 pediatric proprietary medicines. Despite its longstanding clinical use and remarkable value, the scientific basis for Goat Bezoar’s therapeutic efficacy, including its chemical constituents and mechanisms of action, remains unclear. Our recent chemical analyses have, for the first time, revealed that Goat Bezoar is a natural reservoir of urolithins. Urolithins are a group of structural analogs well-known for being produced predominantly through gut microbial metabolism of dietary polyphenols in adults, but are rarely generated in infants and children. Urolithins were reported to display anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and mitophagy-enhancing activities, with urolithin A widely used as an anti-aging dietary supplement. Therefore, we hypothesize that urolithins can serve as a novel nutritional intervention to ameliorate pediatric respiratory inflammation. Supporting this, our pilot studies have demonstrated orally-administered total urolithins significantly attenuated lung inflammation in OVA/LPS-induced young mice, with reduced inflammatory cell infiltration (H&E staining), proinflammatory cytokine levels and neutrophil counts in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Single-cell RNA sequencing of lung tissues revealed that urolithins treatment obviously altered neutrophils, notably enriching IL-17 signaling. Further cell–cell communication analysis showed that urolithins enhanced neutrophil-to-T cell signaling and significantly reversed Th17 cell activation, suggesting that neutrophil–Th17 interplay may mediate the therapeutic effects. To further address this hypothesis, we aim to: 1) Identify the key urolithin in vitro using neutrophils combined with drug-seq technology; 2) Validate the anti-lung inflammation efficacy and safety of the key urolithin by animal and human lung organoid models; 3) Elucidate the underlying mechanism of action, focusing on the neutrophil–Th17 crosstalk. If successful, this will be the first scientific study to clarify Goat Bezoar’s active compounds and mechanisms, supporting its safe and effective clinical use in children. In the long run, by bridging traditional wisdom with modern nutritional science, our research will establish an innovative model for studying natural remedies and foster R&D of novel functional foods for pediatric respiratory health. Ultimately, it will also contribute to the modernization of valuable TCM such as Goat Bezoar. 呼吸道感染是全球兒童群體中的常見病。現有治療手段無法提供全面保護，凸顯了開發安全、可持續干預措施的迫切需求。猴棗，一種源自山羊消化道結石的傳統中藥，價值千金。數百年來，在中國及東南亞地區，猴棗一直被廣泛用於治療兒童呼吸道炎症，並且是超過300種兒科中成藥的核心成分。然而，儘管其臨床應用歷史悠久且價值非凡，猴棗發揮療效的科學基礎，包括其化學成分和作用機制，至今仍不明確。 我們的最新化學分析首次揭示，猴棗是尿石素類化合物的天然寶庫。尿石素是一類結構類似物，通常被認為是成年人腸道菌群代謝膳食多酚後的產物，但在嬰幼兒體內極少生成。已有報導證實尿石素具有抗炎、抗氧化和增強線粒體自噬等多種生物活性，其中尿石素A已被廣泛用作抗衰老膳食補充劑。 因此，我們提出科學假說：尿石素可作為一種新型營養干預手段，用於緩解兒童呼吸道炎症。為驗證此假說，我們的初步研究顯示，在OVA/LPS誘導的幼鼠模型中，口服總尿石素能顯著減輕肺部炎症，表現為炎性細胞浸潤減少、支氣管肺泡灌洗液中的促炎細胞因數水準和中性粒細胞計數均下降。對肺組織進行的單細胞RNA測序分析發現，尿石素處理顯著改變了中性粒細胞的功能，特別是富集了白介素-17信號通路。進一步的細胞間通訊分析表明，尿石素增強了中性粒細胞向T細胞的信號傳遞，並顯著逆轉了Th17細胞的活化。這提示，中性粒細胞與Th17細胞的相互作用可能是其發揮療效的關鍵。 為進一步驗證該假說，本研究旨在： 1.結合中性粒細胞體外模型與藥物篩選測序技術（drug-seq），鑒定發揮核心作用的關鍵尿石素單體。 2. 通過動物模型和人源性肺類器官模型，驗證該關鍵尿石素在抗肺部炎症方面的功效與安全性。 3. 聚焦於中性粒細胞與Th17細胞的交互作用，闡明其潛在的作用機制。 本研究將首次從科學層面闡明傳統兒童用藥猴棗的活性成分及作用機制，為其在兒童中的安全有效應用提供依據。長遠來看，通過連接傳統智慧與現代營養科學，推動針對兒童呼吸健康的創新功能性食品的研發，並最終為猴棗等珍貴傳統中藥的現代化發展做出貢獻。

12105026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12105026.value: O-岩藻糖與 O-GlcNAc 糖基化調控植物自噬之機制性剖析

12105026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12105026.value: Intracellular protein O-linked glycosylations such as O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine modification (O-GlcNAcylation) and O-fucose modification (O-fucosylation) are unique monosaccharide modifications of the hydroxyl groups of serine and threonine residues. They are not extended to complex glycans and are almost exclusively found on cytoplasmic and nuclear proteins. Forty years of research in animals has established O-GlcNAcylation as a central nutrient sensing mechanism. Emerging evidence in plants shows that O-GlcNAcylation and O-fucosylation are ubiquitous and essential PTMs that modulate growth and development, signal transduction, and various other cellular activities. Recent reports from us and others have revealed hundreds of O-GlcNAc- and O-fucose-modified proteins in plants. However, only a handful of them have been characterized so far. Importantly, previous work has paid little attention to the regulation of O-GlcNAcylation and O-fucosylation, as well as their potential roles in nutrient homeostasis. Autophagy facilitates the degradation and recycling of cellular components in eukaryotes, ensuring nutrient homeostasis and survival under adverse conditions. In plants, autophagy is essential for stress adaptation, nutrient redistribution, and grain filling. Our proteomic studies identified O-fucosylation on key autophagy-related proteins, including ATG1A and ATG4B, in Arabidopsis. Yeast two-hybrid experiments demonstrated that ATG1 homologs and ATG4 homologs interact with SPY and SEC. Further investigations revealed that SPY specifically localizes to autophagosomes, and that spy mutants exhibit severe autophagic defects and hypersensitivity to nutrient starvation, underscoring the functional importance of spatial regulation of O-fucosylation in autophagy. Building upon these findings, we hypothesize that O-fucosylation and potentially O-GlcNAcylation dynamically modulate autophagy through direct modification of the autophagy machinery, particularly influencing autophagy induction via ATG1 and autophagosome formation through ATG4. The specific localization of SPY to autophagosomes and the pronounced autophagic defects observed in spy mutants suggest that SPY may be a hitherto unknown plant-specific factor required for assembling and regulating the protein complexes involved in autophagy. In this study, we propose to dissect the molecular basis of O-fucosylation- and O-GlcNAcylation-mediated modulation of autophagy induction and autophagosome formation, as well as to investigate the regulatory mechanisms governing O-fucosylation of autophagy proteins in response to changes in nutrient status. Utilizing a combination of proteomics, genetic analysis, microscopy, and molecular and biochemical assays, we will provide new mechanistic insights into the regulation of plant autophagy through O-fucosylation and O-GlcNAcylation. Our work aims to establish O-fucosylation, and potentially O-GlcNAcylation, as integral components of the nutrient-sensitive autophagy pathway, offering new perspectives on how plants coordinate metabolic homeostasis under fluctuating environmental conditions. 胞內蛋白的 O-連接型糖基化, 如O-連接型 β-N-乙醯葡糖胺修飾（O-GlcNAc 糖基化）與 O-岩藻糖修飾（O-岩藻糖基化），是對絲氨酸與蘇氨酸殘基之羥基進行的獨特單醣修飾。這些修飾不會延伸成複雜聚醣結構，且幾乎僅存在於細胞質與核內蛋白質上。動物領域四十年的研究已確立 O-GlcNAc 糖基化為核心的營養感應機制。植物領域的新興證據顯示，O-GlcNAc 糖基化與 O-岩藻糖基化是普遍且必需的翻譯後修飾（PTMs），可調控生長與發育、訊息傳遞，以及多種其他細胞活動。我們與其他團隊的最新報告已在植物中揭示數百種受 O-GlcNAc 與 O-岩藻糖修飾的蛋白質，然而迄今僅有少數被表徵。值得注意的是，以往的研究鮮少關注 O-GlcNAc 糖基化與 O-岩藻糖基化的調控，以及它們在營養穩態中的潛在角色。 自噬在真核生物中促進細胞成分的降解與再循環，確保營養恆定並在逆境下存活。在植物中，自噬對壓力適應、營養再分配與籽粒充實至關重要。我們的蛋白質體學研究在阿拉伯芥的關鍵自噬相關蛋白（包括 ATG1A 與 ATG4B）上鑑定到 O-岩藻糖基化。酵母雙雜交實驗證明，ATG1 與 ATG4 的同源蛋白可與 SPY 與 SEC 相互作用。進一步研究顯示，SPY 特異性定位於自噬體，而且 spy 突變體呈現嚴重的自噬缺陷並對營養飢餓高度敏感，強調 O-岩藻糖基化在自噬中的空間性調控具有重要功能意義。 基於上述發現，我們假設 O-岩藻糖基化，並有可能包括 O-GlcNAc 糖基化，會透過直接修飾自噬機器而動態地調節自噬，尤其是透過 ATG1 影響自噬誘導，並藉由 ATG4 調節自噬體形成。SPY 在自噬體中的特異定位，以及在 spy 突變體中觀察到的顯著自噬缺陷，提示 SPY 可能是迄今未知、且對參與自噬之蛋白質複合體的組裝與調控所必需的植物特異性因子。在本研究中，我們擬剖析 O-岩藻糖基化與 O-GlcNAc 糖基化介導之自噬誘導與自噬體形成的分子基礎，並探究自噬蛋白在營養狀態變化下 O-岩藻糖基化的調控機制。透過結合蛋白質體學、遺傳分析、顯微觀察，以及分子與生化分析，我們將就 O-岩藻糖基化與 O-GlcNAc 糖基化如何調控植物自噬提供新的機制性見解。我們的研究旨在確立 O-岩藻糖基化，以及可能的 O-GlcNAc 糖基化，為對營養敏感之自噬途徑不可或缺的組成部分，並為植物如何在多變的環境條件下協調代謝穩定提供新視角。

12200426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12200426.value: 基於頸部生物特徵認證強化虛擬/擴增實境系統之信息物理安全研究

12200426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12200426.value: Virtual Reality (VR) and Augmented Reality (AR) technologies have great potential to be adopted in diverse industrial sectors, such as creative industries, smart tourism, aviation, maritime, and construction. Despite their huge market values, VR/AR systems have also raised new cyber-physical security and privacy concerns due to their intrinsic vulnerabilities. As a typical cybersecurity countermeasure, authentication can verify users' identities and authorize their access to strengthen the VR/AR system security and protect user privacy. However, existing text/token-based VR/AR authentication schemes suffer from poor user experience and dependence on untrusted third-party devices, while biometric-based authentication approaches have requirements on external devices and special deployment. To bridge these research gaps, this project will investigate an innovative authentication modality (named NeckAuthenticator) on commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) VR/AR systems with built-in motion sensors to collect neck ballistocardiogram (BCG) biometrics from users. The key idea of NeckAuthenticator is to effortlessly place a VR/AR controller at a user's neck to capture neck BCG vibrations, which encompass rich cardiac biological features for reliable authentication biometrics. After effectively processing BCG signals, unique biometrics can be extracted for subsequent authentication. However, it is non-trivial to implement such an authentication system due to several pivotal challenges. First, it is difficult to process distorted BCG signals due to a user's inconsistent posture when placing the VR controller at his/her neck each time, and to determine the boundaries of BCG signals due to inconspicuous peaks. Second, it is challenging to extract inherent biometric features accurately from BCG signals, though this process is crucial for developing a reliable authentication model. Third, it is challenging to develop new lightweight biometric template protection schemes for NeckAuthenticator. To tackle these challenges, our research agenda includes: i) designing new cardiac signal processing algorithms to process neck BCG signals in VR/AR settings, ii) developing the cardiac biometric authentication framework based on contrastive learning, and iii) investigating lightweight biometric template protection methods to protect the privacy of BCG biometric templates. Finally, we will implement NeckAuthenticator and evaluate it over several COTS VR headset suites via extensive experiments. With our extensive research experience in cybersecurity and privacy for Internet of Things (IoT) and VR/AR systems, we believe that the outcomes achieved in this project will help strengthen the security of VR/AR systems and facilitate the rapid adoption of VR/AR technologies in myriad vertical industries. 虛擬實境（VR）與擴增實境（AR）技術在創意產業、智能旅遊、航空、航運及建築等多個工業領域具備極大的應用潛力。然而，儘管 VR/AR 系統擁有巨大的市場價值，其內在的安全漏洞也引發了新的信息物理安全與隱私疑慮。作為一種典型的網絡安全對策，身份認證能夠驗證使用者身份並授權存取，進而強化 VR/AR 系統的安全性並保護使用者隱私。然而，現有的基於文本/口令的 VR/AR 認證方案存在使用者體驗度不足以及依賴不可信第三方設備等問題。此外，現有的生物特徵認證方法則往往需要額外的外接設備或特殊的部署條件。 為了填補這些研究空白，本項目擬研究一種名為 頸部生物特徵認證器（NeckAuthenticator） 的創新認證機制。該機制利用現成商業化VR/AR設備自帶的運動傳感器，收集使用者的頸部心電圖（Ballistocardiogram, BCG）關鍵生物特徵。NeckAuthenticator 的核心思想是將 VR/AR 手柄/控制器放置於使用者的頸部以捕獲頸部 BCG 震動，這些震動蘊含豐富的心臟生物特徵，可用於抽取可靠的生物特徵認證。在經過有效處理 BCG 信號後，系統即可提取用戶獨有的生物特徵以進行後續認證。然而，實現此認證系統面臨多項挑戰：首先，使用者每次將 VR 控制器置於頸部時的姿勢可能不一致，導致 BCG 信號畸變且難以處理，同時因波峰特徵不明顯而難以確定 BCG 信號邊界；其次，準確從 BCG 信號中提取可靠的生物特徵頗具挑戰性，而該過程對構建可靠的認證模型至關重要；第三，為 NeckAuthenticator 開發新型生物特徵模板保護方案亦具難度。為應對上述挑戰，我們的研究規劃包括：i）設計新型心臟信號處理算法，用於處理 VR/AR 情境下的頸部 BCG 信號；ii）開發基於對比學習（Contrastive Learning）的心臟生物特徵認證框架；以及 iii）研究生物特徵模板保護方法，以保護 BCG 生物特徵模板的隱私。最後，我們將實現 NeckAuthenticator的原型，並透過多款現成 VR 頭戴式設備套件進行廣泛的實驗評估。 憑藉我們在物聯網（IoT）及 VR/AR 系統網絡安全與隱私領域的豐富研究經驗，我們相信本項目的成果將有助於強化 VR/AR 系統的安全性，並促進 VR/AR 技術在眾多垂直行業中的快速應用。

12200526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12200526.value: 面向長視頻理解與推理的可擴展多模態智能體

12200526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12200526.value: Videos are now a dominant form of information in everyday life, from security cameras and medical monitoring systems to sports broadcasts, online education, wearable devices, and entertainment. Yet today’s AI struggles to make sense of long videos that span hours. In particular, a one-hour video at standard resolution and frame rate generates tens of millions of tokens, which are far beyond the capacity of current vision-language models (VLMs). Without new advances, AI remains unable to provide meaningful comprehension, reasoning, or interactive assistance over long video content. This project aims to build the next generation of multimodal AI agents: models that can understand, reason over, and interact with long videos through natural language. Three fundamental challenges must be addressed. First, long videos overwhelm current models, which cannot process all the visual tokens at once. Second, existing VLMs lack strong reasoning abilities: they cannot reliably break down complex user queries, decide when to use external tools, or explain their answers. Third, training such large models requires vast computational resources, putting this line of research out of reach for most universities and independent researchers. To address these challenges, first we propose a retrieval-augmented generation framework that enables models to concentrate on the most relevant portions of a video rather than processing every frame, while also equipping them with agent-like abilities such as tool use and step-by-step problem solving. Second, we develop new reinforcement learning methods that give models the flexibility to adapt their reasoning: they are able to switch between quick, efficient responses for simpler tasks and slower, more deliberate reasoning for complex ones, thereby improving both speed and accuracy. Third, we design memory-efficient training strategies that drastically reduce the computational demands of these systems, making it feasible to train advanced multimodal agents on consumer-grade GPUs. The research will generate new scientific knowledge on how to integrate retrieval, reasoning, and resource-efficient training in multimodal AI. By lowering the hardware barrier for training large VLMs, the project will also broaden participation in this fast-moving field, empowering the wider research community and open-source ecosystem. All code will be released on GitHub and trained models will be shared on Hugging Face, ensuring that the project’s outcomes are openly available, reproducible, and beneficial to both academic and open-source communities. 視頻已成為現代生活中不可或缺的資訊載體，廣泛應用於安全監控、醫療照護、運動轉播、線上教育、穿戴式裝置與影音娛樂等場域。然而，現有人工智能仍難以有效理解長達數小時的影片。以一小時、標準解析度與影格率的影片為例，其資料量可轉換為數千萬個視覺詞元，遠超出目前視覺語言模型所能處理的範圍。若無關鍵技術突破，人工智能將難以對長影片進行深入理解與推理，更無法針對影片內容提供有效的互動式協助。 本計畫旨在研發新一代多模態智能體，使模型能透過自然語言理解長影片、推論其中的事件與脈絡，並與使用者進行互動。為達成此目標，本計畫將聚焦於三項核心挑戰。首先，長視頻蘊含的龐大視覺資訊遠超現有模型的處理能力，模型無法一次納入所有內容。其次，現有視覺語言模型的推理能力仍顯不足，往往無法有效拆解複雜問題、判斷何時應調用外部工具，亦難以清楚說明其作答依據。最後，大型模型的訓練高度仰賴昂貴且龐大的運算資源，使多數大學與獨立研究者難以投入相關研究。 針對上述挑戰，本計畫將從三個方向提出創新方法。第一，建構適用於長影片的檢索增強生成架構，讓模型不必逐一處理所有影格，而能主動找出並聚焦於與問題最相關的影片片段；同時，賦予模型工具調用、任務規劃與逐步解題等代理能力。第二，發展新型強化學習方法，使模型能依據任務難度彈性調整推理模式：面對簡單問題時迅速且有效率地回應，遇到複雜問題時則進行更深入、審慎的推理，兼顧運算效率與回答準確度。第三，設計高記憶體效率的訓練技術，大幅降低模型訓練所需的硬體與運算成本，使先進多模態代理得以在消費級圖形處理器上進行訓練。 本研究預期將深化多模態人工智能在資訊檢索、複雜推理與高效訓練整合方面的科學知識，並為長視頻理解建立新的技術基礎。透過降低大型視覺語言模型的硬體與訓練門檻，本計畫亦將促進更多大學、獨立研究者及開源開發者參與此一快速發展的研究領域，進一步拓展多模態人工智能的研究社群與開源生態。計畫所開發的程式碼將公開於 GitHub，訓練完成的模型亦將發布於 Hugging Face，以確保研究成果能夠公開取得、驗證與重現，並廣泛惠及學術界與開源社群。

12201026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12201026.value: 基於存內計算的生成式推薦系統加速架構

12201026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12201026.value: Recommendation systems (RecSys) are the core engine of the modern digital economy, and their architecture is undergoing a transformative shift. Next-generation systems are rapidly adopting a powerful two-stage pipeline: an initial embedding-based retrieval stage selects candidate items from billion-scale catalogs, followed by a Large Language Model (LLM) based generative ranking stage that produces personalized results. This two-stage approach delivers remarkable gains in recommendation accuracy and user engagement. However, this architectural revolution has created a fundamental system efficiency crisis. The problem is twofold. First, while GPUs are the main stream accelerator for RecSys pipeline, their architecture is fundamentally mismatched to the irregular memory access of embedding retrieval, yielding a meager 15-20% peak bandwidth of their High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) and creating a severe retrieval bottleneck. Second, the generative ranking stage introduces a massive Key-Value (KV) cache that contends with embedding data for scarce GPU memory, creating a dual pressure that limits both scale and latency. To overcome this, we propose PiRecSys, a novel hardware-software co-design that leverages the emerging Processing-in-Memory (PIM) architecture to break this memory wall. PIM fundamentally rethinks data movement by placing computation directly inside memory banks, achieving 2.5-3x higher effective bandwidth for memory-bound operations than GPUs. PiRecSys holistically re-architects the two-stage pipeline through three core innovations: (1) a PIM-optimized billion-scale retrieval system that co-designs terabyte-scale embedding storage and ANNS execution to deliver millisecond candidate retrieval latency; (2) a PIM-offloaded KV cache management engine that performs semantic deduplication and pruning in-memory, slashing the GPU cache footprint by 3-5x; and (3) an automated PIM-centric orchestration framework that intelligently schedules the entire pipeline, treating PIM as the primary platform for memory-bound tasks. We will build an open-source PiRecSys prototype to facilitate widespread adoption and academic replication. The outcomes are expected to deliver higher throughput and better energy efficiency while maintaining strict tail-latency Service Level Objectives (SLOs) (e.g., the 99th percentile latency, critical for user experience). By providing one of the first comprehensive demonstrations of PIM for production-scale generative AI, PiRecSys will pioneer a new architectural paradigm, directly influencing future hardware design and establishing essential methodologies for sustainable, large-scale recommendation. To ensure our research addresses real-world production challenges, we are collaborating with ByteDance, a platform serving billions of users, to ground our design in industrial-scale requirements. 推薦系統是現代數位平台的核心技術。隨著大型語言模型（LLM）的興起，新一代生成式推薦系統普遍採用「召回 + 生成式排序」兩階段架構，以提升推薦品質與使用者體驗。然而，此架構亦帶來嚴重的記憶體瓶頸。一方面，大規模嵌入檢索具有高度不規則的記憶體存取模式，難以充分發揮 GPU 的頻寬效能；另一方面，生成式排序所需的鍵值快取（KV Cache）佔用大量 GPU 記憶體資源，進一步限制系統吞吐量與延遲表現。 本計畫提出 PiRecSys，一個基於存內計算（Processing-in-Memory, PIM）的生成式推薦系統加速架構，以突破傳統 GPU 架構面臨的記憶體牆限制。PiRecSys將從三個方面展開研究：（一）設計面向十億級嵌入資料的存內計算召回系統，實現低延遲候選檢索；（二）開發存內計算鍵值快取管理機制，在記憶體側完成快取壓縮與優化，降低 GPU 記憶體需求；（三）建立以存內計算為核心的異質資源協同調度框架，提升整體系統效能與資源利用率。 本計畫將建構開源 PiRecSys 原型系統，並與產業合作，以真實產業工作負載驗證其效能。預期成果可顯著提升生成式推薦系統的吞吐量、能源效率及服務品質，並為未來記憶體中心人工智慧基礎設施的設計奠定重要基礎。

12201426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12201426.value: 增強對話式推薦系統：基於多模態大語言模型的自適應用戶多模態偏好擷取

12201426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12201426.value: Recent advances in LLMs have led to increased attention to Conversational Recommender Systems (CRS). These systems focus on eliciting user preferences through multi-turn dialogues and adapting recommendations based on users' real-time feedback. However, most current CRS are limited to textual interactions and cannot utilize multimodal user input (e.g., images, voice), which often contain complementary information that can help model user preferences more accurately. This project aims to develop a novel multimodal conversational preference elicitation framework for recommender systems. By harnessing the advanced comprehension and generation capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), we seek to enable adaptive and effective multimodal preference elicitation in CRS. In particular, we will propose an MLLM-enhanced CRS model capable of detecting and resolving multimodal preference conflicts. By fine-tuning MLLMs on a curated multimodal conflict dataset, we will aim to identify and resolve conflicts at different levels. Additionally, we will introduce a dynamic modality weighting mechanism that can adaptively adjust each modality's relative importance. It may jointly model modality contribution and reliability through information-theoretic analysis and robustness-aware noise injection, hence improving user preference representation accuracy. We will also design an uncertainty-driven multimodal question generation model based on variational inference and reinforcement learning, using expected information gain to generate appropriate questions for clarifying ambiguous user preferences. A multimodal preference explanation module will further be developed to enhance system transparency, by integrating a structured multimodal preference memory, a reinforcement learning-based textual explanation generator, and a diffusion-based visual explanation model. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work emphasizing a multi-modality driven user preference elicitation framework for conversational recommender systems. It holds strong potential for practical applications in domains like fashion retail, lifestyle e-commerce, tourism, and interactive media, where interactive and visually engaging recommendations are increasingly common. By enabling systems to understand multimodal user preferences and respond proactively and transparently, our research can directly improve conversion rates, user satisfaction, and engagement in commercial recommender systems. From an economic perspective, our contributions will empower businesses to build more intelligent and trustworthy recommender systems, supporting intelligent marketing, personalized shopping experiences, and customer decision automation, all of which can offer significant productivity gains and commercial returns. Moreover, this project will output open-source toolkits and datasets to benefit the academic and developer community. Educationally, postgraduate and undergraduate students will be actively involved in algorithm design, system development, and experimentation, helping cultivate future researchers in recommender systems and multimodal interactive technologies. 大語言模型的進展帶動了對話式推薦系統（CRS）的發展。此類系統重點在於透過多輪對話擷取用戶偏好，並根據用戶的即時回饋調整推薦。然而，目前大多數 CRS 僅限於文字互動，無法利用多模態的用戶輸入（如影像、語音），而這些多模態資訊常包含互補性資訊，有助於更準確地建模用戶偏好。本研究旨在開發一套新穎的多模態對話式偏好擷取框架。藉由發揮多模態大語言模型（MLLMs）在理解與生成上的先進能力，我們期望在 CRS 中實現自適應且有效的多模態偏好擷取。具體而言，我們將提出一個由 MLLMs 強化的 CRS 模型，能夠偵測並化解多模態偏好衝突。此外，我們將引入一種動態模態權重機制，能自適應地調整各模態的相對重要性，從而提升用戶偏好表示的準確性。我們也將設計一個以不確定性為驅動、基於變分推理與強化學習的多模態問題生成模型，利用期望資訊增益來生成適切問題，以釐清模糊的用戶偏好。進一步地，我們會開發一個多模態偏好解釋方法，以提升系統可解釋性，整合結構化的多模態偏好記憶、基於強化學習的文字解釋生成器，以及基於擴散模型的視覺解釋模型。我們相信此多模態驅動的用戶偏好擷取框架具有強大的實務應用潛力，特別是在時尚零售、生活風格電商、旅遊與互動媒體等領域。透過使系統能理解多模態用戶偏好並主動且透明地回應，本研究可直接提升商業推薦系統的轉換率、用戶滿意度與互動黏著度。從經濟角度來看，我們的貢獻將賦能企業建構更智慧且值得信賴的推薦系統，支援智慧行銷、個人化購物體驗與顧客決策自動化。

12201726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12201726.value: 基於鬆散性分析之敏感功能網絡生物標記的阿茲海默症早期偵測與模型優化多靶點干預

12201726.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12201726.value: Prof Li, Min Prof TANG, Qianyuan

12201726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12201726.value: Alzheimer's disease (AD) presents a profound challenge to global health. While no known intervention can cure or halt AD, early detection and treatment can slow progression. However, it is difficult to achieve in practice. Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) offers high spatial resolution measurements of brain dynamical activity, enabling low-cost and non-invasive early detection, but its high dimensionality and variability pose challenges in developing reliable and sensitive markers. This gap in early detection methods makes it difficult to intervene before irreversible brain changes occur. To overcome these challenges, our team will first develop a framework for detecting and validating subtle but crucial variations in the brain through sloppiness analysis of brain network functional connectivity from multiple fMRI and Positron Emission Tomography (PET) datasets, to identify fMRI-based AD stiff network dynamical marker (AD-SNDM). The sloppiness analysis aims to identify stiff directions in large parameter space of network effective connectivity that correspond to sensitive brain networks underlying AD pathology, validated using AD biomarkers like amyloid-beta (Aβ) and phosphorylated tau (τP) via PET. Thus fMRI-based AD-SNDM are potential sensitive markers for early AD detection from accessible and non-invasive fMRI only, and provide targets for neuromodulation therapies. Then we will carry out in Silicon validation of the sloppiness analysis prediction using large-scale brain network dynamical model calibrated by individual fMRI data. We will perturb the network model using the multi-target strategy predicted from the sloppiness analysis of AD-SNDM to simulate the effect of neuromodulation on the dynamical patterns towards those reflecting healthy aging and optimize the modulation parameters. Finally, we will conduct experimental test and validation of our framework using MRI and transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) at HKBU’s Life Science Imaging Centre on aMCI participants (Amnestic Mild Cognitive Impairment with memory decline), demonstrating that muti-target neuromodulation of sensitive network is more effective than typical single site strategies in prior studies. The goal of this project is to use individual data-driven models of patients to identify, simulate and optimize multi-target neuromodulation therapies that shift brain dynamics and underlying parameters from AD-typical states toward those reflecting healthy aging. Experimental test and validation of the efficacy of these interventions will lay the groundwork for future projects on clinical applications for early stage of AD patients through collaboration with medical doctors. 阿茲海默症（AD）對全球健康構成重大挑戰。目前尚無任何已知的干預方法能夠治癒或停止AD，但早期發現與治療可以延緩疾病進程。然而，在實際操作中實現早期發現十分困難。功能性磁共振成像（fMRI）可以高空間解析度測量大腦動態活動，使得低成本、非侵入性的早期檢測成為可能，但由於其高維度和高變異性，開發可靠且敏感的生物標記仍具有挑戰性。這使得在不可逆的大腦改變發生之前及時介入變得困難。 為了克服這些挑戰，我們的團隊將首先開發一套框架，通過對多個fMRI和正電子發射斷層掃描（PET）數據集中的大腦網絡功能連結性進行鬆散性（sloppiness）分析，來檢測並驗證大腦中微妙但關鍵的變化，以識別基於fMRI的AD剛性網絡動態標記（AD-SNDM）。鬆散性分析旨在找出網絡有效連接的大參數空間中與AD病變相關的敏感大腦網絡的剛性方向，並通過PET上的澱粉樣蛋白（Aβ）和磷酸化tau（τP）等AD生物標記進行驗證。因此，基於fMRI的AD-SNDM有潛力作為僅依賴fMRI的敏感早期檢測標記，並可作為神經調控治療的干預目標。 接著，我們將利用根據個體fMRI數據校正的大規模大腦網絡動態模型，在電腦模擬中驗證鬆散性分析的預測。我們將根據AD-SNDM鬆散性分析中預測的多靶點策略擾動網絡模型，模擬神經調控如何使大腦動態模式朝向健康老化的方向發展，並優化調控參數。 最後，我們將在香港浸會大學生命科學影像中心，針對aMCI（記憶障礙型輕度認知障礙）受試者，使用MRI和經顱磁刺激（TMS）進行框架的實驗驗證，展示多靶點神經調控敏感網絡的方法比以往僅針對單一腦區的策略更為有效。 本項目的目標是利用個體化的資料驅動模型，發掘、模擬並優化能將大腦功能與其基礎參數從典型AD狀態調整至健康老化相關狀態的多靶點神經調控治療。這些干預措施的實驗測試和驗證將為未來與醫生合作，應用於早期AD患者臨床治療奠定基礎。

12201826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12201826.value: 面向大規模屬性圖的檢索技術：查詢、嵌入與算法研究

12201826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12201826.value: Graph databases are gaining increasing traction, especially for LLM use cases, with the market projected to hit approximately $4.03 billion in 2025, driven by their strength in modeling relationships and structured knowledge. As a primitive operation therein, graph retrieval seeks to retrieve from the graph database the graphs that are most relevant to a given query graph, which underpins multifarious applications in cheminformatics, software engineering, circuit design, and so on. Despite being extensively studied in the past two decades, the majority of these efforts center on graph isomorphism-based similarity/distance computation for graphs with categorical vertices, which are incompetent for real scenarios due to their costly matchers/approximators, brittle indexes, and inapplicability to rich attributes, e.g., multi-labels, properties, and textual descriptions, at both nodes and edges. To date, there is a lack of systematic studies on queries integrating structural and attribute semantics for flexible conditions over arbitrary attributed graphs, and it remains highly challenging to deliver fast retrieval results, particularly across millions of attributed graphs in large-scale databases. Inspired by the remarkable success of vector databases in real-time semantic search of textual, acoustic, and visual data, this project aims at transforming attributed graph retrieval (AGR) into multi-vector search, thereby enabling highly efficient and effective management of graph-structured data in unified vector stores. Towards this goal, we intend to conduct a systematic study of AGR through a stepwise series of research tasks. First and foremost, we will investigate the definitions of relevant measures that capture both hard and soft graph semantics and the formulations of queries for varied attributed graphs. In the second stage, we will establish theoretical foundations to bridge graph spaces and Euclidean spaces, and focus on devising novel and efficacious algorithms and models to build multi-vector graph embeddings. On top of that, we plan to design a series of theoretically-grounded optimization techniques to accelerate model training and multi-vector search, targeting sub-second query performance over massive sets of attributed graphs. Finally, we will develop a prototype system of attributed graph retrieval and liaise with industry partners for real-world evaluation. With our rich research experience in large graph management and analytics as a backing, we anticipate the outcome of this project to contribute to the advancement of graph data management and improvements of applications and services in the industry. 圖資料庫（Graph databases）正獲得越來越多的關注，特別是在大語言模型（LLM）的應用場景中；得益於其在關係建模與結構化知識表達方面的強項，預計其市場規模將在2025年達到約40.3億美元。圖檢索（Graph retrieval）作為圖資料庫中的一項基礎操作，旨在從圖資料庫中檢索出與給定查詢圖最相關的圖，這為化學資訊學、軟體工程、電路設計等眾多領域的應用提供了關鍵支撐。儘管在過去二十年中圖檢索已被廣泛研究，但絕大多數研究成果仍集中於基於圖同構（Graph isomorphism）的相似度/距離計算，且僅針對具有類別標籤節點的圖。這些方法由於其昂貴的匹配器/近似器、脆弱的索引機制，以及無法處理節點和邊上豐富的屬性資訊（如多標籤、屬性特徵和文字描述），導致其無法滿足真實應用場景的需求。時至今日，針對在任意屬性圖上整合結構與屬性語義以支援靈活查詢條件的系統性研究仍有所缺失，且要在包含數百萬張屬性圖的大規模資料庫中實現快速檢索，依然面臨著極大的挑戰。 受向量資料庫在文字、音訊和視覺資料的實時語義搜尋中所取得的顯著成功所啟發，本項目旨在將屬性圖檢索（Attributed Graph Retrieval, AGR）轉化為多向量搜尋（Multi-vector search），從而在統一的向量存儲中實現對圖結構資料的高效且精準的管理。為實現這一目標，我們計劃通過一系列循序漸進的研究任務對 AGR 進行系統性研究。首先，我們將探索能夠同時捕捉圖的硬性與軟性語義的相關度量定義，並研究針對不同屬性圖的查詢構建方式。在第二階段，我們將建立連接圖空間與歐幾里得空間的理論基礎，並著重設計創新且有效的演算法與模型，以構建多向量圖嵌入（Multi-vector graph embeddings）。在此基礎上，我們計劃設計一系列具備理論保障的優化技術，以加速模型訓練與多向量搜尋，目標是在海量屬性圖集上實現亞秒級（sub-second）的查詢性能。最後，我們將開發一個屬性圖檢索的原型系統，並與工業界夥伴合作進行真實場景下的評估。憑藉我們在大規模圖資料管理與分析領域的豐富研究經驗，我們預計本項目的研究成果將推動圖資料管理技術的進步，並促進相關工業界應用與服務的提升。

12202026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12202026.value: 組件感知精選驅動的基礎模型高效與可信融合

12202026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12202026.value: Foundation models (FMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities and significantly advanced various real-world sectors. For example, a healthcare-oriented FM could influence sectors accounting for about 8% of Hong Kong’s GDP in 2024-2025. However, training an FM (e.g., GPT-4) is expensive, consuming millions of dollars and substantial time. In this context, foundation model merging (FM merging) offers a cost-effective alternative by integrating FMs fine-tuned from the same pre-trained model. In the key stages of an FM merging cycle, including model selection, knowledge correction, and parameter aggregation, current methods widely rely on idealized assumptions: a limited number of candidate FMs, knowledge derived from high-quality data, and non-conflicting parameters. However, this idealization conflicts with the complexity of real-world applications, thereby introducing critical challenges to the efficiency, security, and robustness of FM merging, as manifested in the following aspects: Challenge 1 (Model Selection): How to efficiently select FMs from a large number of candidates? The number of candidate FMs may be large while only a few of them contribute to the target tasks. However, typically selecting FMs by exhaustive performance evaluations is time-consuming, raising efficiency concerns for FM merging. Challenge 2 (Knowledge Correction): How to remove malicious knowledge and avoid privacy leakage for secure FM merging? The candidate FMs may contain malicious knowledge and harmful triggers from inaccessible training data, raising security concerns for FM merging. Challenge 3 (Parameter Aggregation): How to mitigate parameter conflicts for robust FM merging? Candidate FMs are fine-tuned on various tasks. However, parameter conflicts, such as parameter overlap and preference bias, may arise across FMs, raising robustness concerns for FM merging. In this project, we propose a Component aware Curation Model Merging (CoCu-Merging) framework that curates models, knowledge, and parameters to improve the efficiency and trustworthiness of FM merging. Specifically, we propose four tasks for the above three challenges. Task 1: Efficient Foundation Model Merging via Model Routing: It will develop strategies for efficient FM selection (for Challenge 1). Task 2: Secure Foundation Model Merging via Data Selection-based Unlearning: It will develop synthetic data selection-based unlearning algorithms to remove malicious knowledge in FMs (for Challenge 2). Task 3: Robust Foundation Model Merging via Resolving Parameter Conflicts: It will develop parameter selection algorithms to mitigate parameter conflicts and enhance the robustness of FM merging (for Challenge 3).
