Specifically, market makers adjust their delta hedges by trading S&P 500 futures overnight, exerting significant buying or selling pressure on the futures if the adjustment needs are substantial. This pressure then transmits to the underlying market or ETF market when trading opens the next day. By establishing a clear link between 0DTE trading and predictable price dynamics, the project will inform ongoing debates about the market impact of 0DTEs, provide practical insights for risk management and execution, and offer evidence relevant to regulatory policy as similar short-dated products proliferate. 超短期的期權的交易量大幅上升，目前已佔美國指數期權交易量約一半。當投資人買賣這類期權時，造市商會站在對向，並透過交易標的資產來對沖風險。隨著期權接近到期日，即使價格沒有變動，造市商所需的避險部位也可能迅速變化。這種由時間驅動的變化，可能迫使造市商在開盤前買賣標普500指數期貨，進而可能造成標的指數在昨日收盤與今日開盤之間出現可預測的缺口。 本研究探討0DTE期權交易所產生的避險壓力，是否會影響標普500指數隔夜的開盤走勢。我們聚焦於時間衰變避險，此風險捕捉的是因時間流逝而導致的避險需求變化，有別於取決於價格變動的風險。具體而言，造市商會透過在隔夜交易時段買賣標普500指數期貨來調整其delta避險部位，若調整需求較大，將對期貨構成顯著的買進或賣出壓力。而這股壓力會在次日開盤時傳導至標的市場或ETF市場。 透過建立0DTE交易與可預測價格動態之間的明確關聯，本研究將為當前關於0DTE市場影響的討論提供實證依據，為風險管理與交易執行提供實務見解，並在類似短天期產品日益增加的背景下，為交易所設計與監管政策提供相關參考證據。

12502926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12502926.value: 設計能抵禦虛假評論與搭便車競爭者的個人化評分平台

12502926.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12502926.value: Prof Chen, Chia-Hui Prof Lo, Melody Pei-yu

12502926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12502926.value: In this digital economy, recommender and rating systems are everywhere. Google Maps provides a few recommended routes when we want to get from A to B. YouTube and TikTok recommend the next video for us to watch. Hotels.com and Booking.com allow us to looking up the ratings of any hotels we are curious about. Some providers provide both recommendations and ratings at the same time: Amazon allows us to look up the ratings of any books and also recommends what books we may want to buy next. Providers of recommendations and ratings sometimes also play the role of a two-sided marketplace, where a buyer can make a purchases right away after being recommended or after looking up the rating of a specific seller, turning these providers to integrated platforms. There are also standalone providers of recommendations and ratings, such as Google Maps in its role of providing restaurant ratings. Curiously, while most recommender systems provide personalized recommendations, most rating systems stick with impersonalized ratings. Netflix’s recommendations depend on what we have watched and what we liked. But it returns the same rating for any given movie regardless of who is inquiring. There are probably good marketing reasons why ratings, unlike recommendations, remain mostly impersonalized: a frustrated buyer may be more willing to revenge with a bad review if it will damage the seller’s rating universally instead of only among a minority of likeminded fellow buyers; a Michelin star also would not confer much in the way of bragging rights if it were not transparent to connoisseurs how many stars a restaurant actually has; etc. Without dismissing these marketing concerns, it is still interesting to ponder (at least theoretically) what could have happened if more ratings are personalized. This project will investigate exactly that. It is a theoretical project, because it is about a counterfactual. Its primary focuses are the synergy between such a standalone rating provider and a two-side marketplace, and how the thus integrated platform can defend against sham reviews and free-riding rivals. We expect at least one international refereed journal article and several international conference/seminar presentations will be generated from this project. In the longer run, we expect it will enhance our understanding of recommender/rating systems, as well as informing practitioners on different business strategies they can keep in their toolboxes. 在數位經濟中，推薦系統與評分系統無所不在，但兩者存在一個有趣的差異：推薦系統多為「個人化」（如 Netflix 依用戶觀影歷史推薦），而評分系統多為「非個人化」（如 IMDb 對同一電影顯示統一評分）。這種設計可能出於行銷考量——非個人化評分能讓負面評價對賣家造成普遍影響，從而增強評分的威懾力；同時，像米其林星級這樣的榮譽也需透明且一致才具公信力。然而，若理論上假設評分系統也走向「個人化」，將引發一系列值得探討的後果。本專案旨在探討此一反事實情境，特別聚焦於評分提供者（如 TripAdvisor）與雙邊市場平台（如 Amazon、Booking.com）之間的互動將產生甚麼變化。此專案將透過理論建模，分析一個與雙邊市場平台有機整合的「個人化」評分提供者如可比「非個人化」評分提供者更能抵禦虛假評論與搭便車競爭者。

12503026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12503026.value: 選擇抑或被動指派？性別化任務分隔的動態循環

12503026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12503026.value: Despite significant advancements in female education, gender disparities in labor market outcomes persist (Bertrand, Goldin, & Katz, 2010; Van der Lee & Ellemers, 2015). Of particular concern is the enduring vertical gender segregation, where women tend to concentrate in low-level positions while men dominate high-ranking positions (Bertrand & Hallock, 2001; Friendman & Laurison, 2019; Padavic & Reskin, 2002). To better understand this puzzling phenomenon, there has been a growing focus on examining whether the tasks that men and women perform vary, and whether such differences contribute to disparities in workplace advancement (Benschop & Doorewaard, 1998; Chan & Anteby, 2016). This line of research has revealed that women, compared to men, tend to perform more low-promotability tasks (i.e., tasks that benefit the organization, but is given light weight in performance evaluation and promotion decisions, such as service tasks performed by research faculty in research-oriented universities) but fewer challenging and developmental, known as high-promotability tasks (Babclock et al., 2017; De Pater, Van Vianen, & Bechtoldt, 2010; Mitchell & Hesli, 2013). The literature does not directly explain why women’s task portfolios emphasize low-promotability tasks. Common explanations for gender differences in the workplace, such as individual preferences, a disinclination to self-promote, hesitation to negotiate and compete, and gender stereotypes, may provide insights (Dreber, Heikensten, & Säve- Söderbergh, in press; Niederle & Vesterlund, 2007). However, these accounts either come from the demand-side or the supply-side with a static snapshot while overlooking the dynamic nature inherent in the task formation process. We contend that women’s segregation on low-promotability tasks may arise from a leader-follower interactive process involving both self-reinforcing and other-reinforcing mechanisms. Drawing on interdependence theory (Kelly & Thibaut, 1978) and social role theory (Eagly, 1987), we propose that women’s concentration on low-promotability tasks evolves over time, influenced by both leaders’ actions and their own behavioral discretion. Specifically, we theorize that women are likely to volunteer for and be assigned low-promotability tasks due to the alignment with their communal roles. Female employees’ volunteering for and leaders’ allocation of such tasks will influence subsequent task allocation and women’s volunteering, respectively. Furthermore, women’s overall trend of volunteering for low-promotability tasks over time is moderated by the extent of leaders’ allocation, and similarly, leaders’ overall trend of assigning low-promotability tasks to women is moderated by women’s level of volunteering. 儘管女性教育水準大幅提升，勞動力市場的性別差異依然存在（Bertrand et al., 2010；Castilla, 2023；Van der Lee & Ellemers, 2015）。女性多集中於低層職位，男性主導高層職位，即縱向性別隔離（Bertrand & Hallock, 2001；Friedman & Laurison, 2019；Padavic & Reskin, 2002）。研究表明，女性比男性承擔更多低晉升性任務（如服務性工作），更少承擔高晉升性任務（Babcock et al., 2017；De Pater et al., 2010；Mitchell & Hesli, 2013）。現有解釋多從供需兩側靜態分析，忽視任務形成的動態過程（Dreber et al., 待刊；Niederle & Vesterlund, 2007）。我們認為，女性在低晉升性任務上的集中，源於領導者—追隨者互動中的自我強化與他者強化機制。 基於相互依賴理論與社會角色理論（Kelly & Thibaut, 1978；Eagly, 1987），我們提出女性在低晉升性任務上的集中是隨時間演變的，受領導者行為和自身自主性共同影響。具體而言，女性因與其共融性角色契合，更可能自願承擔或被分配低晉升性任務。進一步，女性的自願承擔與領導者的任務分配會相互影響後續行為。同時，女性自願承擔的整體趨勢受領導者分配程度調節，領導者分配的整體趨勢也受女性自願水準調節。

12503126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12503126.value: 國際投資網絡與國際商業周期

12503126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12503126.value: Understanding the source of aggregate fluctuations is crucial for effective monetary policy design. For example, the global negative supply shock in 2020 has advocated the G20’s commitment to coordinated monetary policy. More recently, tariff changes have the potential to trigger global price shocks and inflation surges, prompting the IMF to call for international policy coordination. Research that identifies the nature of shocks and their transmission mechanisms to drive the aggregate fluctuations is known as business cycle analysis. This proposal seeks to contribute to this area. Real Business Cycle theory performs relatively well in a closed economy environment. However, most economies nowadays are connected to the global economy through the exchange of goods and assets. The International Real Business Cycle (Hereafter IRBC) literature, which incorporates these international linkages, struggles to replicate empirical patterns. A prominent puzzle is the “quantity anomaly"—the observation that cross-country consumption correlations are lower than output correlations, contrary to model predictions. In reality, international trade happens for various purposes. Recent IRBC literature, incorporating trade in both consumer goods and the intermediate inputs used in production, studies the shocks at the sector level and explores whether these shocks can propagate through the production networks and drive the GDP comovements. Notably, this literature hasn’t addressed other anomalies or puzzles. We explore the international investment networks--- international linkages in trade for inputs used to produce investment goods such as machinery and equipment. Our framework, building on recent production network literature, explicitly characterizes the sectoral linkages through which capital goods are produced using inputs sourced across countries. Analytical and quantitative methods are used to gauge our model’s ability to match the GDP comovements. Additionally, we evaluate the model’s performance in other business cycle moments and its potential to address some anomalies, such as the “quantity anomaly.” Intuitively, when facing positive technology shocks, the investment networks structure increases the demand for imported investment inputs, crowding out consumption in the foreign country, and thus dampening the excessively high cross-country consumption comovements predicted by the standard model. By utilizing detailed input-output data on investment goods, this project is the first to quantitatively assess investment networks in IRBC studies. Our goal is to enhance the understanding of international shock transmission, offering a more realistic and comprehensive explanation of global economic fluctuations, helping policymakers better understand the deep connections within the global economy. 理解總體經濟波動的來源對貨幣政策設計具有重要意義。例如，2020 年的全球負向供給衝擊促成了 G20 對貨幣政策協調的承諾。近期，關稅變動有可能引發全球價格衝擊與通脹飆升，促使國際貨幣基金組織（IMF）呼籲加強國際政策協調。旨在理解衝擊的性質及其傳導機制如何驅動總體波動的研究被稱為經濟週期分析。本研究計劃擬在這一領域作出貢獻。 真實經濟週期理論在解釋封閉經濟環境下的總體波動方面表現相當出色。然而，多數經濟體通過商品與資產的交換同全球經濟相連。將這些國際聯繫納入考量的國際真實經濟週期（以下簡稱 IRBC）文獻卻難以複製經驗規律。其中一個廣為人知的問題是「數量異象」（quantity anomaly）——即跨國消費相關性低於產出相關性這一現象，與模型的預測相反。 在現實中，國際貿易出於多種目的而發生。近期的 IRBC 文獻同時納入消費品貿易與生產所用中間品貿易，研究部門層面的衝擊，並探討這些衝擊是否通過生產網絡傳播並驅動總體波動。此類研究聚焦於理解 GDP 協動性，而未觸及其他異象與謎題。 我們強調國際貿易在供給投資品（如機器設備）生產所需投入方面的重要作用。投資網絡——即資本品借助跨國投入進行生產所形成的部門間關聯——在我們的框架中得到明確刻畫。我們將運用解析與定量方法，評估模型在匹配 GDP 協動性方面的表現；同時，考察該模型在其他經濟週期矩以及在解釋某些異象（如「數量異象」）方面的潛力。直觀而言，面對正向技術衝擊時，投資網絡結構會推高對進口投資投入品的需求，擠出外國的消費，從而抑制標準模型所預測的過高跨國消費協動性。 借助投資品的詳細投入產出數據，本項目首次對 IRBC 研究中的投資網絡進行定量評估。我們的目標是深化對國際衝擊傳導的理解，為全球經濟波動提供更貼近現實、更為全面的解釋，幫助政策制定者更好地把握全球經濟內部的深層聯繫。

12503226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12503226.value: 資助以性別導向的生物醫學創新

12503226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12503226.value: This study investigates how gender influences startup financing in biomedical innovation, focusing on how the gender orientation of health technologies—whether they target female, male, or gender-neutral conditions—shapes capital allocation and venture capital (VC) behavior. Despite increasing attention to women’s health, female-specific conditions such as endometriosis, menopause, and maternal health remain underrepresented in R&D pipelines and receive disproportionately low levels of private investment. This imbalance reflects deeper frictions in innovation financing, where capital flows are shaped by both demand-side biases and institutional structures. These dynamics echo findings from Aghion et al. (2009, 2013), who show how financial constraints and investor preferences can influence the direction and growth of innovation. To address this gap, we construct a novel dataset linking biomedical patents to their originating startups and classify each patent by its gender focus. Using large language models (LLMs), we develop a scalable method to detect whether a patent targets female, male, or gender-neutral health conditions based on its text. This allows us to systematically analyze the gender orientation of innovation at the firm level. With this dataset, we examine whether startups focused on female health face different financing outcomes—such as funding size, timing, investor composition, and exit performance—compared to those focused on male or gender-neutral conditions. We further explore the role of investors, particularly the gender composition of VC firms. We ask whether firms with greater female representation are more likely to fund female-focused innovations, shedding light on how investor diversity affects the inclusivity of biomedical investment. We also assess whether VC funding shifts a startup’s innovation direction by tracking changes in patent portfolios after investment. This enables us to evaluate whether capital steers innovation pipelines toward or away from gender-specific health needs. To identify causal effects, we exploit organizational and institutional shocks, such as CEO turnovers and gender-focused policy changes within VC firms. Finally, we introduce the Gender Focus Innovation Index (GFII)—a cross-country benchmark that combines patent data, funding outcomes, and investor demographics. The index enables global comparisons of how countries prioritize gender-equitable biomedical innovation. In sum, this study places financing at the center of efforts to reduce gender disparities in health innovation, identifying both market and policy levers to foster a more inclusive biomedical R&D ecosystem. 本研究探討性別如何影響生物醫學創新領域的新創融資，重點在於健康科技的性別導向——亦即其目標是女性、男性或性別中立的疾病／健康狀況——如何形塑資本配置與創投（VC）的投資行為。儘管近年來對女性健康的關注日益增加，針對女性特定疾病的研發主題（如子宮內膜異位症、更年期與孕產婦健康）仍在研發（R&D）管線中代表性不足，且獲得的私人投資金額明顯偏低。此一失衡反映了創新融資中更深層的摩擦：資金流向同時受到需求端偏誤與制度性結構的影響。這些動態亦呼應 Aghion 等人（2009、2013）的研究發現：金融約束與投資人偏好會影響創新的方向與成長。 為填補此一缺口，我們建構一套新的資料集，將生物醫學專利與其原始新創公司連結，並依每件專利的性別焦點進行分類。我們運用大型語言模型（LLMs），發展出一種可擴展的方法，根據專利文本偵測其所針對的健康狀況屬於女性、男性或性別中立。此方法使我們能在公司層級系統性分析創新的性別導向。藉由此資料集，我們檢驗聚焦女性健康的新創公司，在融資結果上——例如募資規模、時點、投資人組成與退出績效——是否與聚焦男性或性別中立健康狀況的新創公司存在差異。 我們亦進一步探討投資人的角色，特別是創投機構的性別組成。我們提出問題：女性代表性較高的創投機構，是否更可能資助女性導向的創新？藉此揭示投資人多元性如何影響生物醫學投資的包容性。我們也評估創投資金是否會改變新創公司的創新方向：透過追蹤投資後專利組合的變化，判斷資本是否會引導研發管線朝向或遠離性別特定的健康需求。為識別因果效果，我們利用組織與制度面的外生衝擊，例如執行長更迭，以及創投機構內部與性別焦點相關的政策變動。 最後，我們提出「性別焦點創新指數」（Gender Focus Innovation Index, GFII）——一項跨國基準指標，整合專利資料、融資結果與投資人（創投）人口結構特徵。該指數可用於全球比較各國如何優先推動性別公平的生物醫學創新。總結而言，本研究將「融資」置於縮小健康創新中性別落差的核心，並辨識可促進更具包容性的生物醫學研發生態系之市場機制與政策槓桿。

12503326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12503326.value: 算法時代的愛：浪漫式人工智能的溝通風格如何塑造人機關係與服務績效

12503326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12503326.value: A growing number of people are forming romantic relationships with AI companions, creating a fast-growing market of romantic AI that uses natural language processing and deep learning to deliver personalized intimate conversations. Current default design of romantic AI, however, usually adopts an overly submissive communication style, leading to undifferentiated product positioning and creating discomfort for users. Little research to date has examined romantic AI (or companion AI in general) through the lens of communication style. This gap is surprising, given that instant dialogue is the primary (and often the only) means by which romantic AI interact with users. The current proposal aims to address this research gap through the following objectives: 1. Determine whether romantic AI that adopts a dominant communication style, compared to a submissive communication style, induces more favorable firm-directed (i.e., subscription, usage frequency, service evaluation) and consumer-directed service outcomes (i.e., consumer well-being). 2. Examine the underling mechanisms in driving the proposed effects of communication style on romantic AI service outcomes. 3. Explore when, how, and for whom the proposed communication style effects on romantic AI service outcomes would be attenuated, amplified, or even reversed. Drawing on mind perception theory, we propose that the romantic AI that adopts a dominant (vs. submissive) communication style improves both firm-directed service outcomes and consumer well-being, though the effect on consumer well-being emerge at a later stage. We propose a serial mediation of consumers’ perceived AI independence and relationship authenticity. We also identified three moderators concerning when (situation factor: post-traumatic distress), how (AI factor: AI response time), and for whom (consumer factor: need for control) the proposed effect would be attenuated, amplified, or even reversed. Two preliminary studies (a survey and an experiment) provided evidence for the research context and the main effect. We will further conduct seven experiments, including a large-scale text-mining study enabled by machine learning technique, a quasi-field and a field experiment with a self-developed romantic AI mobile app, one lab experiment, and three online experiments to test our proposed propositions. The work explains whether, when, how, and for whom a dominant communication style of romantic AI benefits both firms and consumers, offering clear design advice for creating better romantic AI services. This research addresses a cutting-edge AI product type (i.e., romantic AI) that potentially generate large revenue and positively influence consumer well-being. 越來越多的人正與人工智能（AI）伴侶建立浪漫關係，從而催生了一個快速成長的浪漫式人工智能市場。該市場利用自然語言處理與深度學習技術，來提供客製化的親密對話。然而，現今浪漫式人工智能的預設設計通常採用過度順從的溝通風格，導致產品定位缺乏差異化，並引發使用者不適。迄今為止，甚少有研究從溝通風格的視角來探討浪漫式人工智能（或更廣義的伴侶式人工智能）。鑑於即時對話是浪漫式人工智能與使用者互動的主要（且通常是唯一的）手段，此研究缺口令人驚訝。本計畫旨在透過以下目標來填補這一研究空白： 1. 探討相較於順從型溝通風格，採用主導型溝通風格的浪漫式人工智能是否能帶來更有利的企業導向服務績效（即訂閱意願、使用頻率、服務評價）與消費者導向服務結果（即消費者福祉）。 2. 檢驗溝通風格對浪漫式人工智能服務績效之預期影響的底層驅動機制。 3. 探索在何種情況下（when）、透過何種方式（how）以及針對何種群體（for whom），溝通風格對浪漫式人工智能服務績效的預期影響會被削弱、放大甚至反轉。 本研究基於心智感知理論（Mind Perception Theory），提出採用主導型（相較於順從型）溝通風格的浪漫式人工智能能同時提升企業導向服務績效與消費者福祉，儘管對消費者福祉的影響會在較晚的階段才顯現。我們提出了一個由消費者感知人工智能獨立性（AI independence）與關係真實性（relationship authenticity）所構成的序列中介模型。此外，我們還確立了三個干擾變數，分別涉及該預期效應何時（情境因素：創傷後壓力）、如何（人工智能因素：人工智能回應時間）以及對誰（消費者因素：控制需求）會被削弱、放大甚至反轉。 兩項初步研究（一項問卷調查與一項實驗）為研究背景和主效應提供了實證支持。我們將進一步進行七項實驗以驗證研究假說，其中包括一項基於機器學習技術的大規模文字探勘研究、一項準田野實驗與一項利用自主研發之浪漫式人工智能行動應用程式進行的田野實驗、一項實驗室實驗以及三項線上實驗。本研究旨在闡明浪漫式人工智能的主導型溝通風格是否、何時、如何以及對誰能同時使企業和消費者獲益，並為創造更優質的浪漫式人工智能服務提供了明確的設計建議。本研究探討了一種前沿的人工智慧產品類型（即浪漫式人工智能），該產品具備創造巨大營收並對消費者福祉產生積極影響的潛力。

12503426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12503426.value: 運用負責任AI智能體緩解金融顧問服務中的隱性說服風險

12503426.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12503426.value: Prof LI, Xin Prof Xu, Sean Xin

12503426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12503426.value: The deployment of large language models (LLMs) as agentic assistants in high-stakes domains like financial services introduces complex governance challenges. This integration creates two interrelated paradoxes that may amplify hidden persuasive risk: advice that remains formally compliant yet psychologically manipulative. The learning paradox arises because LLMs trained on historical data risk amplifying the very persuasive biases and sales-driven distortions they are meant to correct. The responsibility paradox is a conflict between the AI’s capability and the human advisor’s accountability. This misalignment can cause accountability anxiety and undermine human-AI collaboration. Prevailing AI alignment methods like Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) are ill-suited to this problem, as they are vulnerable to reward hacking and may amplify these biases. This project addresses this gap by designing, constructing, and validating a framework for a responsible AI agent. Following a design science approach and in collaboration with a major commercial bank in China, the research is structured into two main studies. Study 1 constructs and technically validates the agent artifact to solve the learning paradox. It employs a Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning (GCRL) framework trained on a unique, large-scale dataset containing conflicting supervisory signals: regulatory audits and real-world client outcomes. Key technical innovations include an implicit reward mechanism to resist reward hacking and intrinsic interpretability via an attribution graph to ensure its reasoning is auditable. Study 2 addresses the responsibility paradox through a 2×2 factorial field experiment with the bank’s professional advisors. This study investigates how the agent’s interactive design—specifically its internal motivational orientation (prevention vs. promotion) and external communicative stance (collaborative vs. directive)—impacts the effectiveness of human–AI collaboration. This project offers a novel sociotechnical solution that contributes a new perspective on designing AI as an embedded ethical governance mechanism that actively balances information asymmetry. The findings will provide actionable, evidence-based principles for designing systems that foster a responsible financial ecosystem. 隨著大語言模型（Large Language Models，LLMs）逐漸應用於金融服務等高風險決策場景，AI智能體不再只是提供資訊的輔助工具，而開始深度參與金融顧問的判斷、建議生成與客戶溝通。這一轉變帶來新的治理挑戰：某些建議即使在形式上符合監管要求，仍可能透過語言表達和互動方式對客戶產生不當的心理影響，形成難以被傳統合規機制識別的隱性說服風險。本研究認為，這一風險主要源自兩個相互關聯的悖論。首先是學習悖論。大語言模型主要從歷史數據中學習，而這些數據本身可能包含既有的說服偏誤和銷售導向行為。因此，原本旨在改善金融建議的AI智能體，反而可能複製甚至放大其所要糾正的偏誤。其次是責任悖論。AI智能體具備愈來愈強的分析、推薦和溝通能力，但最終的專業及合規責任仍由人類顧問承擔。這種人工智能能力與人類責任之間的錯位，可能增加顧問的問責焦慮，並削弱人機協作成效。 現有人工智能對齊方法，例如基於人類回饋的強化學習，容易受到獎勵操弄及既有偏誤的影響，難以充分應對上述問題。為此，本項目採用設計科學研究方法，並與中國一家大型商業銀行合作，設計、建構及驗證一套面向金融顧問服務的負責任AI智能體框架。研究一聚焦學習悖論，採用目標條件式強化學習框架，利用包含兩類互補但可能相互衝突監督訊號的大規模真實數據進行訓練：一類來自監管及合規審查，另一類來自實際客戶結果。研究將引入隱式獎勵機制，降低模型迎合單一評價標準而產生獎勵操弄的風險；同時建構歸因圖，使AI智能體形成建議的依據和推理過程能夠被追溯及審查，提升系統的可解釋性與可問責性。 研究二聚焦責任悖論，將與銀行的專業金融顧問開展一項2×2因子實驗考察AI智能體的內在動機取向（預防取向或促進取向）以及其對外溝通方式（協作式或指令式），如何影響人機協作成效。本項目將技術設計與人機協作機制結合，提出一套應對金融人工智能隱性說服風險的社會技術方案。研究將拓展負責任人工智能的研究視角，探討如何將AI智能體設計為嵌入金融服務流程中的倫理治理機制，主動緩解資訊不對稱及不當說服。研究結果亦將為金融機構提供具實證基礎且可操作的系統設計原則，以促進更負責任的金融生態系統。

12503626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12503626.value: 元宇宙的消費者品牌互動和選擇

12503626.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12503626.value: Prof Zhang, Kuangjie Prof Zhou, Zhongyun

12503626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12503626.value: Metaverse is becoming a new battleground for brands, but marketing research on metaverse and consumer-brand interaction is still in its infancy. Building on consumer-brand relationship theory and identity literatures, this proposal suggests that the metaverse, an immersive new world with unfamiliar norms, can reduce consumers’ self-concept clarity, compared to other conventional environments such as webpages. To restore self-concept clarity and blend into the metaverse, consumers are motivated to imitate the personalities exhibited by brand mascots, who are the residents of the metaverse. Connecting this process with consumers’ choices, we propose a three-level effect, including within-brand product choice, across-brand product choice, and beyond-brand activity choice. To elaborate, we suggest that consumers in the metaverse (vs. on the webpage) are more likely to choose a brand’s products that align with the personality exhibited by this brand's mascot. Consumers are also inclined to choose a brand’s products that align with the personality of a mascot from another brand they encountered previously. Furthermore, they are more likely to engage in activities (e.g., gaming) that reflect the brand personality of that mascot. While brand mascots strive to imitate humans and fit into the human world, this research proposes a novel process in which consumers behave like brand mascots, thereby influencing their consumption choices. Based on this process, we propose two moderators: self-continuity and shared experience, which are aligned with the two dimensions of self-concept, namely idiosyncratic personal identities and relational social identities. Individuals with high self-continuity are more likely to maintain a clear self-concept under the pressure of environmental changes. And therefore, our proposed effect of the metaverse will be attenuated for consumers with high self-continuity. Furthermore, when close others in consumers’ real lives join the metaverse for a shared experience, it can activate and reinforce consumers’ real-life self-concept, so that their self-concept clarity is less weakened by the metaverse, and the proposed effect would disappear. In collaboration with a company that builds metaverses and webpages, we have successfully completed one pilot study that confirms our main hypothesis, and we propose five more experiments to comprehensively test our theoretical framework. To increase the generalizability, we aim to test six different brand personalities, and a wide range of products that are virtual or real. This work will contribute to literature in metaverse, branding, and identity, and provide cutting-edge practical implications. 元宇宙正成為品牌的新戰場，但關於元宇宙以及當中消費者與品牌互動的研究仍處於起步階段。基於消費者品牌關係理論與身分認同文獻，本研究計畫提出：相較於傳統環境（如網頁），沉浸而又陌生的元宇宙會降低消費者的自我概念清晰度。為了恢復自我概念清晰度並融入元宇宙，消費者會被驅動去模仿作為元宇宙居民的品牌吉祥物所展現的個性。 過去品牌吉祥物致力於模仿人類、融入人類世界，本研究則提出一項新穎機制：消費者會像品牌吉祥物般行為，進而影響其消費選擇。基於此機制，我們提出兩個調節變數：自我連續性與共享經驗，分別對應自我概念的兩個維度，即個人身分與社會身分。自我連續性高的個體在面對環境變遷壓力時較能維持清晰的自我概念，因此，元宇宙所帶來的效應在這些消費者身上將被減弱。此外，當消費者現實生活中的親近他人一同進入元宇宙共享經驗時，會喚起並強化其現實生活的自我概念，使其自我概念清晰度較不易受元宇宙削弱，因而所提出的效應將消失。 我們與一家建構元宇宙與網頁的公司合作，已成功完成一項先導研究，並確認了我們的主要假設。我們亦設計了另外五個實驗，以全面檢驗我們的理論架構。為提高研究的普適性，我們計畫測試六種不同的品牌個性，以及涵蓋虛擬與實體的多樣產品。本研究將對元宇宙、品牌管理與身分認知等領域的文獻做出貢獻，並提供前沿的實務意涵。

12503826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12503826.value: 外商直接投資，投入相似性和企業生產率

12503826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12503826.value: For decades, economies around the world have engaged in policy efforts and global competition to attract foreign direct investment (FDI), driven primarily by the belief that it can foster productivity spillovers for domestic firms. Yet, robust empirical support for these spillover effects remains limited, mostly confined to backward linkages—where FDI benefits local upstream suppliers. In contrast, evidence for horizontal and forward spillovers is mixed and often inconclusive, suggesting that prevailing analytical approaches may overlook critical mechanisms through which FDI impacts wider economic outcomes. This research proposes and rigorously investigates a novel channel through which FDI generates productivity spillovers: shared input markets. With modern production becoming increasingly fragmented and specialized, firms in different industries are more reliant on common inputs. We hypothesize that FDI’s impact permeates more broadly through industries that use similar inputs, even absent direct buyer-supplier relationships. When multinationals enter, they elevate standards for local upstream suppliers, triggering industry-wide improvements in input quality, variety, and cost. This, in turn, benefits all domestic firms relying on those inputs, irrespective of their industry. To identify this causal effect, we leverage China’s 2002 FDI liberalization following its WTO accession as a quasi-natural experiment. We construct a measure of exposure to FDI within input-similar—but not vertically linked—industries, and exploit comprehensive microdata on Chinese firms from 1998 to 2007. Using an instrumental variable strategy, we rigorously test whether input-similar FDI causally increases local firm productivity. Further, we unpack the mechanisms by examining upstream supplier upgrading and downstream firms’ shifts toward domestic inputs and adaptive innovation. Finally, we analyze the moderating role of input specificity, testing whether spillovers are stronger for customized, relationship-specific inputs versus standardized commodities. This study advances the literature on FDI spillovers by shedding light on an economically potent yet overlooked pathway through input-based linkages across unrelated industries. By identifying broader spillover effects beyond direct vertical relationships, our research helps reconcile the tension between widespread policy efforts to attract FDI and the mixed empirical evidence on its local impacts. The importance of this analysis is further underscored by ongoing geopolitical realignments—such as U.S.-China trade tensions and Brexit—which are prompting the global reallocation of FDI and restructuring of supply chains. Understanding how FDI reshapes economic outcomes across interconnected sectors and borders is therefore of heightened policy relevance in this increasingly fragmented global economy. 本研究探討外國直接投資（FDI）對本地企業生產力溢出效果的新機制。過去各國長期競相吸引FDI，主要基於其可帶來技術與生產力外溢的預期，但實證證據多集中於後向溢出（backward spillover），也就是FDI對本地上游供應商的影響；至於水平與前向溢出，結果則分歧且不夠明確，顯示現有分析可能忽略了FDI影響更廣泛經濟結果的重要渠道。 本文提出，FDI除了透過直接買賣關係產生影響外，還會藉由「共享投入市場」擴散生產力。隨著現代生產日益分工與專業化，不同產業的企業愈來愈依賴相似的中間投入品。當跨國企業進入某一市場時，會提高上游供應商的品質、種類與成本標準，進而促使整體投入品市場升級，讓所有使用這些投入品的本地企業受益。這些本地企業不僅可以是跨國企業的同行業者，也可以是更廣泛的其他產業的使用該投入品的生產者。 為識別此因果效果，研究利用中國2002年加入WTO後的FDI放寬政策，作為準自然實驗，並結合1998至2007年中國企業微觀資料，建構「投入相似但無垂直連結」產業中的FDI暴露程度指標，採用工具變數方法檢驗投入相似FDI是否會提升本地企業生產力。研究進一步分析其作用機制，包括上游供應商升級，以及下游企業轉向使用國內投入品與進行調適性創新；同時也檢驗投入特異性是否具有調節效果，亦即客製化、關係專屬投入品的外溢是否強於標準化商品。 本研究擴展了FDI溢出文獻，揭示一條經濟上重要但過去較少被注意的路徑：透過跨產業的投入連結，FDI可對更廣泛的本地企業產生生產力影響。此發現不僅有助於解釋各國為何持續積極爭取FDI，也可回應現有實證結果不一致的問題。在美中貿易緊張與英國脫歐等地緣政治重組持續推動FDI與供應鏈重分配的背景下，理解FDI如何透過相互連結的產業與跨境網絡重塑經濟成果，具有更高的政策意義

12600326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12600326.value: 王夫之詩歌中的語言、情感和自我

12600326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12600326.value: Known primarily as a towering philosopher during the Ming-Qing transition, Wang Fuzhi王夫之 (1619-1692) also wrote poetry and extensive literary critical commentary. A mutually formative relationship between “theory” and “practice” has often been proposed, sometimes even taken for granted, for writers in imperial China who were both poets and critics, but this aspect has been strangely overlooked in modern studies of Wang. His poetry has largely been ignored in the vast body of scholarship seeking to reconstruct his poetic thought. This project proposes to reexamine Wang’s poetics by taking his poetry as the primary text, aimed primarily at addressing two aspects that by studying his literary criticism and philosophical writings alone cannot satisfactorily resolve: its practicality in the world of experience; and the changes over the course of his life. For Wang, poetry confirms the inevitable physicality of human existence but also plays a role in the individual’s efforts to transcend it. His insistence on self-discipline in the face of calamity highlights the opposite pulls in individual selfhood that is both necessary and problematic for his moral universe. This, I argue, is what makes poetry necessary and meaningful for Wang, and what underlies his belief for the role that lyrical expression can uniquely fulfill. Wang’s poetics, developed in the same historical moment when the Ming yimin poets widely claimed narrative and history for the poetic demesne, is a poetry of heightened consciousness of being in the world: the poet feels everything in full force and allows nothing to distract or blunt the impact of the moment. While modern scholarship on Wang’s literary critical writings has provided comprehensive reconstructions of Wang’s poetic paradigm, his poetry sheds fresh insight. First, dated and produced in response to real-life situations, it supplies the immediate context to study the changes in his poetic thought over time. Second, by foregrounding the limitations imposed by the human condition, it furnishes us with the material to focus on the practical orientation of his poetics, which tends to be obfuscated in his literary criticism and philosophical writings. A study of his poetry will present a more nuanced picture on the problem of emotion, selfhood, and language in Wang’s poetry and poetics, and deepen our understanding in the role of literature in his intellectual universe. 本計畫通過王夫之的詩歌為主要文本重新審視其詩學，主要關注僅透過研究他的文學批評和哲學著作無法滿意解決的兩個面向：其詩學理想在經驗世界中的實踐以及在其晚年的變化。結合王夫之的詩歌對其詩學的研究能夠展現在其詩學中關於語言、情感和自我等課題更細緻入微的理解，並更好地認識王夫之的詩歌創作在其學術世界中的位置。

12601526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12601526.value: 香港平台化新聞與科學錯誤資訊：分析與對策

12601526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12601526.value: When scientific information circulates online, accuracy does not always keep pace. In the platformized media landscape, dense with messaging apps, forums, and algorithmic feeds, echo chambers can intensify and accelerate the spread of scientific misinformation. This study maps cross-platform narrative diffusion, identifies the interpretive frames that gain traction, and pinpoints the community and platform characteristics associated with heightened vulnerability. Study 1 will examine the pathways by which scientific reports are interpreted, reframed, and converted into misinformation across social media, news portals, and messaging apps, with attention to variation by topic, subtopic, and community worldview. It will systematically trace the evolution of original reports into misinformation variants, map diffusion pathways across platforms and communities, identify recurrent interpretive frames, and model their dynamics across platforms and over time. Study 2 will implement a survey experiment with Hong Kong residents to assess how online community engagement, news consumption patterns, and science attitudes relate to susceptibility to particular misinformation types. Grounded in the interpretive frames from Study 1 and designed to test echo chamber effects, it will produce actionable insights to reduce susceptibility and mitigate misinformation spread. This research addresses two major gaps in the literature, namely the lack of cross-platform insight into decentralized information flows and limited understanding of susceptibility to diverse forms of scientific misinformation. It contributes to scholarship on platformization and echo chambers by evidencing how platform affordances and community structures intensify particular interpretive frames and accelerate diffusion across platforms. Expected outputs include a typology of interpretive frames in scientific misinformation, topic-specific diffusion maps, and comprehensive susceptibility profiles outlining risk patterns across community worldviews, news diets, platform ecosystems, and interpretive frames. Building on these findings, the research will develop targeted interventions, including pre-bunking and debunking guidance for fact-checkers, media literacy resources tailored to Hong Kong’s platform ecosystem, and recommendations for cross-platform collaboration, to strengthen science outreach and support science-based policymaking. Findings will be disseminated through comprehensive reports and practitioner-facing materials. Ultimately, the project provides actionable pathways to cultivate an informed, resilient public and to bolster accurate perceptions of science within Hong Kong’s dynamic digital landscape. 科學資訊在網上流通時，其準確性未必同步維持。在充斥通訊應用程式、討論區與演算法資訊流的平台化媒體生態中，回音室效應往往強化並加速科學錯誤資訊的擴散。本研究將分析與繪製跨平台敘事擴散圖譜，並辨識具牽引力的解讀框架。 研究一將檢視科學報告在社交媒體、新聞平台及通訊應用程式中如何被解讀、重塑並轉化為錯誤資訊；比較不同主題與社群世界觀的差異；系統追蹤原始報告演變為錯誤資訊的過程；勾勒跨平台與跨社群的擴散路徑；識別常見解讀框架；並建立其跨平台與時序的動態模型。研究二將採用問卷實驗，評估網上社群參與、新聞消費與科學態度如何關聯對特定類型錯誤資訊的受誤導風險，並提出可操作對策，以降低受誤導風險並抑制擴散。 本研究將為去中心化的跨平台資訊流提供整體洞見，並深化對人們為何易受科學錯誤資訊影響的理解，同時闡明平台特性與社群結構如何強化特定解讀框架並加速跨平台擴散。項目產出將包括為事實查核人員提供的預先拆解與闢謠指引、度身訂造的香港平台生態媒體素養資源，以及跨平台協作建議，旨在培養具判斷力與韌性的公眾，並鞏固香港動態數碼生態中的科學正確認知。

12602126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12602126.value: 音樂如何形塑思想與想像：一個數據驅動與概念性框架

12602126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12602126.value: Prof Bhattacharya, Joydeep Prof d'Inverno, Mark

12602126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12602126.value: Listening to music profoundly influences our internal mental experiences, allowing us to immerse ourselves in the narratives of songs, imagine vivid scenarios, and drift between past memories and future anticipations. Many listeners engage with music to support various cognitive functions such as fantasizing, introspecting, and recalling memories, making music an integral part of their inner worlds. The heterogeneity of these mental experiences, such as earworms, absorption, mind-wandering, autobiographical memories, and trance (among others), highlights music’s fundamental role in human cognition, but also presents important challenges for scientific study. Currently, research in music psychology remains fragmented, with diverse terminologies, theories, and methods. Developing a unified conceptual framework that delineates the core dimensions of subjective experience is crucial for advancing the field, resolving terminological ambiguities and operationalization challenges, and providing the foundational setting for future research. Additionally, integrating existing consciousness theories can help create both a comprehensive and parsimonious model. With regard to empirical findings, the influence of music features and listener traits on mental experiences remains unclear and ecological data from naturalistic listening settings are needed to complement traditional lab-based studies, providing a more accurate understanding of music’s impact on consciousness in “real life”. The goal of our project is to develop a novel, conceptual, and data-driven framework for understanding the relationship between music listening and internal mental experiences. Combining expertise from music psychology, cognitive science, and formal modeling, we will undertake comprehensive literature reviews to inform our conceptual modeling, at the same time validating it through systematic empirical data collection. Results will be used to iteratively test and refine the model, ensuring that it captures as much of the full complexity of music-related mental experiences as possible. In four empirical music listening studies, we will employ multidimensional experience sampling to characterize subjective changes, across various music styles, listener profiles, and listening contexts (both naturalistic and laboratory settings). Data analysis will include principal component analysis and psychometric network analysis to identify core dimensions and clarify their relationships. Ultimately, this project will deepen our understanding of how music influences conscious experience in everyday life, thereby impacting research on consciousness, emotion, creativity, and other related areas. Beyond academia, the findings will benefit therapists and health professionals by informing music-based interventions, help the general public use music more intentionally for well-being, and support artists in harnessing music’s power to influence conscious states for creative purposes. 聆聽音樂對我們內在的心理體驗產生深遠影響，讓我們能夠沉浸於歌曲的敍事之中，想像生動的場景，並在過往記憶與未來期盼之間游移。許多聽眾透過音樂來支援各種認知功能，例如幻想、內省和回憶，從而使音樂成為其內在世界不可或缺的一部分。這些心理體驗的異質性，例如耳蟲、沉浸、思緒漫遊、自傳式記憶和恍惚狀態等，既突顯了音樂在人類認知中的基本角色，也為科學研究帶來了重要挑戰。目前，音樂心理學的研究仍然相當零散，涉及不同的術語、理論和方法。建立一個統一的概念框架，以劃定主觀體驗的核心維度，對於推動該領域的發展、解決術語歧義和操作化挑戰，以及為未來研究提供基礎設定，均至關重要。此外，融入現有的意識理論，有助於建立一個既全面又簡潔的模型。就實證研究結果而言，音樂特徵和聽眾特質對心理體驗的影響仍不明確，並且需要來自自然聆聽環境的生態數據，以補充傳統的實驗室研究，從而更準確地理解音樂在「現實生活」中對意識的影響。我們項目的目標是建立一個新穎的、概念性且以數據為驅動的框架，以理解音樂聆聽與內在心理體驗之間的關係。結合音樂心理學、認知科學和形式建模的專業知識，我們將進行全面的文獻回顧，以指導概念建模，同時透過系統性的實證數據收集來驗證該模型。研究結果將用於反覆測試和修訂模型，確保它能盡可能地捕捉與音樂相關的心理體驗的完整複雜性。在四項實證音樂聆聽研究中，我們將採用多維度經驗取樣來描述主觀變化的特徵，涵蓋不同的音樂風格、聽眾特質和聆聽情境（包括自然情境和實驗室情境）。數據分析將包括主成分分析和心理計量網絡分析，以識別核心維度並釐清它們之間的關係。最終，本項目將加深我們對音樂如何在日常生活中影響意識體驗的理解，從而對意識、情緒、創造力及其他相關領域的研究產生影響。在學術界之外，研究結果將惠及治療師和健康專業人員，為以音樂為基礎的干預措施提供參考；幫助公眾更有意識地運用音樂來增進福祉；並支持藝術家善用音樂的力量，以影響意識狀態，達致創作目的。

12602226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12602226.value: 榕樹下的聆聽：藝術與生態中的植物生物電聲化

12602226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12602226.value: Listening Under the Banyan Tree: Plant Bioelectric Sonification in Arts and Ecology is an interdisciplinary project that translates the bioelectrical activity of Hong Kong’s banyan trees into sound. At its core, the project uses listening as both method and outcome, creating new ways of experiencing more-than-human life. Banyans (Ficus microcarpa) are keystone species that provide shade, habitats, and urban cooling, while serving as cultural landmarks and gathering places. Their ecological and cultural presence makes them anchors for exploring how artistic research and ecological science can come together. All plants generate tiny electrical signals as part of their lives, regulating photosynthesis, responding to stress, and adapting to their environments. Normally invisible, these signals can be translated into sound, making plant vitality perceptible. In recent years, artists and scientists have approached this in different ways: some have turned signals into music to spark engagement, while others have used high-fidelity instruments to study physiology in controlled laboratory settings. Artistic approaches risk treating plants as abstract data or performers, while scientific work remains highly specialised. Both perspectives are valuable, yet rarely combined. This project bridges those traditions. It develops a portable, open-source biosensing system to capture banyan bioelectrical activity in real time, with a flexible sonification framework that balances clarity with resonance— combining methods such as parameter mapping, audification, and spatialisation to create immersive soundfields. Fieldwork will focus on ecologically and culturally significant banyans identified through Hong Kong’s Old and Valuable Trees Register, including clusters of trees that allow listening “across” multiple organisms to reveal patterns of interdependence. The project also extends cultural memory. Oral histories gathered under banyan canopies will be recorded in ambisonic format and integrated into the existing 3D Hong Kong Topophonies sound map, a previous funded project. By weaving community stories with real-time plant sonifications, the project creates a layered archive where human and vegetal voices meet. Public listening sessions will share these experiences, inviting communities to gather under banyans once again and explore new forms of empathy, reflection, and dialogue. By combining ecological science, cultural practice, and artistic research, Listening Under the Banyan Tree offers an original model for open, accessible, and situated listening—one that is scientifically grounded, culturally resonant, and widely shareable. 《榕樹下的聆聽：藝術與生態中的植物生物電聲化》是一項跨學科研究計劃，旨在將香港榕樹的生物電活動轉化為聲音。本計劃以聆聽作為方法與成果，創造體驗超越人類生活的新方式。榕樹（Ficus microcarpa）作為關鍵物種，為城市提供遮蔽、棲息地及降溫，同時亦是文化地標與聚集場所。榕樹在生態與文化上的重要性，使其成為探索藝術研究與生態科學融合的核心。 所有植物在生命過程中皆會產生微小的電信號，以調節光合作用、回應壓力及適應環境。這些信號通常不可見，但可轉化為聲音，使植物的活力變得可感知。近年來，藝術家與科學家以不同方式進行相關探索：部分人將信號轉化為音樂以促進參與，而另一些人則使用高保真儀器在受控的實驗室環境中研究生理學。藝術方法有時將植物視為抽象數據或表演者，而科學研究則高度專業化。兩者皆具價值，卻鮮有結合。 本計劃旨在合這些傳統之間的鴻溝，開發一套便攜式、開源的生物感測系統，能即時捕捉榕樹的生物電活動，並以靈活的聲化框架呈現，兼顧清晰度與共鳴，結合參數映射、聲訊化及空間化等方法，創造沉浸式音場。田野調查將聚焦於香港「古樹名木冊」中具生態及文化意義的榕樹，包括群落式樹木，讓聆聽能跨越多個個體，揭示相互依存的模式。 計劃同時延伸文化記憶，於榕樹下收集的口述歷史將以全景聲格式錄製，並整合至現有的「香港聲地圖」3D聲音地圖中（前期資助項目）。透過將社群故事與即時植物聲化交織，計劃創建一個多層次檔案，讓人類與植物聲音相遇。公開聆聽活動將分享這些體驗，邀請社群再次於榕樹下聚集，探索新的共感、反思與對話形式。 結合生態科學、文化實踐及藝術研究，榕樹下的聆聽提供一個開放、易於參與且具本地特色的聆聽模式——既具有科學基礎，又富文化共鳴，並能廣泛分享。

12602526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12602526.value: 邁向大型多模態模型驅動的失明及視力受損人士無障礙服務自動化：透過提示工程生成口述影像腳本

12602526.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12602526.value: Dr LEUNG, Hoi Ching Dawning Prof Pan, Jun

12602526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12602526.value: According to the World Health Organization, “at least 2.2 billion people have a near or distance vision impairment” in the world (WHO, 2023). Population growth, ageing and life expectancy increases are expected to escalate the risk that more people acquire vision impairment. Therefore, the need for accessibility measures for the blind and partially sighted (BPS) will become even more pressing. This project aims to contribute to accessibility measures for the BPS that support digital content understanding and enjoyment. The project will be based in Hong Kong, where over 199,600 citizens or more than 2.7% of the population, have visual impairments of differing degrees (Census and Statistics Department, 2021). Access to information and participation in cultural life are fundamental human rights. Audio description (AD), which uses voiced-out narratives to describe relevant on-screen actions, is a key accessibility measure in a world where video consumption keeps growing exponentially every year (Sandvine, 2025). The limited availability of AD is further compounded by the fact that, currently, AD is a time-consuming and costly process, including script creation and recording or live voice acting. Partially automating the AD process could significantly expand access to audiovisual media for BPS individuals, enhancing their quality of life. This project proposes the use of Large Multimodal Models (LMM), artificial intelligence systems designed to process audiovisual data, to generate AD scripts in the Cantonese language. It will do so via prompt engineering, the practice of designing and refining input prompts to effectively guide the behaviour and outputs of AI models. The project aims to 1. develop prompt engineering guidelines to enhance the innate capabilities of LMMs to generate AD scripts; 2. assess the way LMMs can assist human audio describers to create AD scripts, and 3. evaluate the way LMM-generated AD scripts are received by BPS individuals. The project collaborates closely with The Audio Description Association (Hong Kong) (AuDeAHK), a Hong Kong-based NGO. LMM-generated scripts will be evaluated using a mixed methods approach, including both automatic and human evaluation. A set of prompting guidelines will be drafted according to the findings. Finally, BPS participants will assess different types of AD scripts (LMM-generated, post-edited, and human-generated) in a reception study. Combining the input from AD creators and AD users will provide a comprehensive understanding of the potential of LMM-generated AD scripts. 根據世界衞生組織的資料，全球「至少有 22 億人患有近距離或遠距離視力障礙」（WHO, 2023）。隨著人口增長、人口老化及預期壽命延長，預計將有更多人面臨視力受損的風險。因此，為失明及視力受損人士（blind and partially sighted, BPS）提供無障礙措施的需要將變得更加迫切。 本研究項目旨在推動支援失明及視力受損人士理解及享受數碼內容的無障礙措施。研究將以香港為主要研究場域。香港有超過 199,600 名市民，即超過全港人口的 2.7%，患有不同程度的視力障礙（Census and Statistics Department, 2021）。 獲取資訊及參與文化生活均屬基本人權。口述影像（audio description, AD）透過語音敘述畫面中相關的動作及視覺資訊。在全球影片內容消費量每年持續大幅增長的情況下，口述影像已成為一項重要的無障礙措施（Sandvine, 2025）。然而，目前可提供的口述影像仍然有限，而其製作過程亦耗時且成本高昂，包括撰寫口述影像腳本，以及錄音或現場配音等工作。若能將口述影像製作流程部分自動化，便有望大幅增加失明及視力受損人士接觸影音媒體的機會，從而提升其生活質素。 本研究項目建議運用大型多模態模型（Large Multimodal Models, LMM），即能夠處理影音數據的人工智能系統，生成粵語口述影像腳本。研究將透過提示工程（prompt engineering）實現此目標。提示工程是指設計及不斷優化輸入提示，以有效引導人工智能模型的行為及輸出。本研究旨在：1. 制定提示工程指引，以提升大型多模態模型生成口述影像腳本的內在能力；2. 評估大型多模態模型如何協助人類口述影像撰稿員創作口述影像腳本；以及 3. 評估失明及視力受損人士如何接受及評價由大型多模態模型生成的口述影像腳本。 本研究項目將與香港的非政府組織香港口述影像協會（The Audio Description Association (Hong Kong), AuDeAHK）緊密合作。研究將採用混合研究方法評估由大型多模態模型生成的腳本，包括自動評估及人工評估，並根據研究結果制定一套提示工程指引。最後，失明及視力受損參與者將透過接受度研究，評估不同類型的口述影像腳本，包括由大型多模態模型直接生成的腳本、經後期人工編輯的腳本，以及由人類撰稿員創作的腳本。結合口述影像創作者及使用者雙方的意見，將有助於全面了解大型多模態模型生成口述影像腳本的潛力。

12603126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12603126.value: 無界勞工：中國平台經濟數位前沿的生存現場

12603126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12603126.value: The global proliferation of platform-based work signals a profound transformation in the contemporary labor landscape, creating a reality of what we term “Unbounded Labor.” This shift moves beyond flexible hours to a fundamental re-spatialization of work, transitioning from bounded workplaces to “workplaces as infrastructure.” In this model, the platform becomes the central node, generating the unique and flexible geographies of this digital frontier that actively blur the boundaries between work, home, and social life. While promising new avenues for livelihood, this unbounded reorganization is underpinned by a pervasive regime of algorithmic control, creating a new political economy that inevitably transforms the meanings, practices, and experiences of work. Platform jobs often appear to democratize access, yet algorithms mediate interactions, job dispatching, and performance ranking under a veneer of digital objectivity. This raises a critical question: does the perceived freedom and flexibility genuinely enhance empowerment, or do these systems, despite claims of neutrality, encode and perpetuate social biases? Drawing on theories of intersectionality, we interrogate how gender, age, and socioeconomic class shape experiences on this frontier. Furthermore, the study investigates the erosion or reconfiguration of worker agency, asking how algorithmic management constructs divergent workday realities and fosters new, contingent work identities. To investigate these complex socio-technical relations, this project employs a mixed-methods approach in Jiangsu, China, combining a quantitative questionnaire of 2,000 workers with in-depth qualitative methods: participant observation and mobile interviews with 24 workers across four distinct platform roles (food delivery, ride-hailing, vlogging, and livestreaming). This comparative design is crucial for analyzing three key dynamics: the selection and self-selection into different platform roles; the navigation of intersecting demands like migration and family; and the ways workers’ daily tactics negotiate the tension between the platform’s regime of mobility/fixity and the mobilities/immobilities of personal life. As digital technologies relentlessly remake labor markets worldwide, China’s vast and dynamic platform economy offers a critical, instructive case study of this global shift. Our analysis provides a nuanced understanding of how workers from diverse backgrounds strategize within platform systems, and how new subjectivities are forged at the nexus of technology, space, and labor. The findings aim to generate actionable insights for policymakers and platform designers, contributing to more equitable regulatory frameworks and technological designs that genuinely enhance worker safety and well-being, mitigate embedded biases, and reduce adverse social consequences for this expanding workforce of “unbounded” laborers. 全球平台工作的普及，標誌著當代勞動樣貌的一場深刻轉變，形構出我們所稱的「無界勞工」現象。這場轉變不僅止於工時彈性化，更徹底顛覆了工作的空間邏輯──從過去「有固定邊界的工作場所」，轉變為「作為基礎設施的工作場所」。在此模式下，平台化身為核心節點，在數位前沿上鋪展出獨特而靈活的地理樣態，也同時模糊了工作、家庭與社交生活之間的界線。 平台工作看似開闢了新的謀生管道，背後卻由一套無孔不入的算法控制體系所支撐。這套新的遊戲規則，正悄然改寫工作的意義、執行方式，以及勞動者的主觀感受。平台工作表面上促進了機會的普及，實則從信息交互、工作指派到績效排名，全由算法在幕後調度，且往往披著「數據中立」的合理外衣。這引出了一個關鍵問題：勞動者切身感受到的自由與彈性，是否真能賦予他們更多自主權？抑或這些宣稱中立的系統，實際上是社會既有偏見的數位化身，甚至進一步強化了不平等？ 本研究借鑒交織性理論，探討性別、年齡與社經地位如何在數位前沿上形塑勞動者的不同處境。同時，我們也追問勞動者的能動性究竟是被侵蝕，還是以新的形態重新生成；算法管理如何建構出迥異的工作日常，又如何催生各種臨時性、權宜性的工作身份。 為釐清這些複雜的社會技術關係，本研究在中國江蘇省採行混合研究方法，結合2,000名平台工作者的量化問卷，以及針對24位平台工作者的參與觀察與行動中訪談等深入質性方法。通過比較研究，旨在分析三個關鍵動態：勞動者如何進入不同的平台角色；他們如何調度遷徙、家庭、工作等多重生活需求的交織壓力；以及他們如何在平台體制所要求的流動／固定，與個人生活的流動／不流動之間，發展出日常的協商策略。 隨著數位科技持續席捲全球勞動市場，中國龐大且充滿活力的平台經濟，是理解此全球轉型的重要參照。我們的分析將細緻呈現，來自不同背景的勞動者如何在平台系統中謀劃行動策略，以及新形態的主體性如何在技術、空間與勞動的交匯處逐漸成形。研究成果期望為政策制定者與平台設計者提供具體啟發，推動更公平的制度設計與監管框架，從根本上提升勞動者的安全保障與生活福祉，降低系統性偏見的影響，並避免對這群持續擴張的「無界」勞動者所產生負面社會後果。

12604326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12604326.value: 香港支援長者家庭照顧者的輔助科技之研究

12604326.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12604326.value: Prof BAI, Xue Prof Cheng, Reynold Chun-Kong Prof KAN, Wing Shan Prof LAI, Wing-Leung Daniel Prof Wong, Yu Cheung

12604326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12604326.value: Family caregivers in Hong Kong face heavy strain with insufficient tailored support. While software-based assistive technology may help with accessing community information, reaching out to support services, and peer connections, many caregivers face challenges in adoption due to usability, confidence, cost, and attitudes towards technology. The proposed study will focus on software-based assistive technology in Hong Kong—specifically, mobile apps, websites, and online platforms—to examine how caregiving demands, the nature of the care recipient’s primary impairment (cognitive or physical), and anxiety about technology shape caregivers’ views on usefulness and ease of use. The study will also examine how these views influence caregivers’ actual use of these digital platforms and how such use relates to their well-being. The study will also consider the reasons behind adoption or rejection, as well as what caregivers want from the design and support of these tools. Through an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design, Phase 1 will include a quantitative random telephone survey of 800 Hong Kong caregivers aged 40 and above caring for older adults with long-term needs, technological anxiety, technological perceptions, usage of major assistive platforms in Hong Kong (e.g., HA GO, eHealth, Information Gateway for Carers, OK Care, Evercare, and others), and their well-being. This will be followed by Phase 2, which will comprise qualitative in-depth interviews with 40 family caregivers to identify the contextual barriers and facilitators they experienced in using assistive technologies. The expected outcomes include clear, practical recommendations to improve the design of applications and training, outreach for low-literacy users, and policy actions to reduce barriers—ultimately helping caregivers use digital platforms more easily and thereby enhancing their daily care. 香港的家庭照顧者承受沉重壓力，而現有為他們的針對性支援仍然不足。以軟件為本的輔助科技有望能協助他們獲取社區資訊、接觸支援服務及建立同儕連繫。然而，不少照顧者在採用上面對可用性、信心、成本及對科技態度等方面的障礙。本研究將聚焦在香港的軟件式輔助科技——特別是流動應用程式、網站及網上平台——以探討照顧負荷、被照顧者主要功能障礙的性質（認知或身體）以及科技焦慮等如何形塑照顧者對工具有用性與易用性的看法。研究亦將檢視這些看法如何影響照顧者對相關數碼平台的實際使用，以及使用科技與其福祉之間的關係。本研究亦會探討照顧者採納或拒用的原因，以及他們對相關工具設計與支援配套的期望。 本研究採用解釋性序列混合方法設計。第一階段為定量隨機電話調查，對象為800名年滿40歲、為有長期需要之長者提供照顧的香港照顧者；內容包括科技焦慮、對科技的看法、對香港主要輔助平台的使用情況（例如 HA GO、醫健通、照顧者資訊網、「要回家」OK Care、Evercare 等平台）及其福祉。其後的第二階段為對40名家庭照顧者定性深度訪談，以辨識他們在使用輔助科技時所面對的情境性障礙與促進因素。 預期成果包括提出清晰且可行的建議，以改進應用程式設計與培訓、強化面向低數碼能力使用者的接觸與支援，以及推動減少障礙的政策措施。最終結果有助照顧者更便捷地使用數碼平台，從而改善其日常照顧狀況。

12604926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12604926.value: 基於社交媒體的電子檔案袋對香港高校英語學習者寫作水準和焦慮程度的影響研究

12604926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12604926.value: In English as a second or foreign language (EFL) writing pedagogy, significant attention has been paid to electronic portfolio (e-portfolio) assessment through social networking sites in the past two decades. Nonetheless, little is known about how WeChat (i.e., an instant messaging cum social networking app), which has 1.15 billion active monthly users, can be used as a platform for e-portfolio assessment to identify junior undergraduates’ learning of academic writing and their levels of anxiety when handling programme-based writing tasks. This proposed study intends to investigate the impact of a WeChat-based e-portfolio assessment, one popular social networking tool in Asia, on L2 writing performance and writing anxiety levels among Hong Kong undergraduates, namely in their freshmen and sophomore years, as well as their perceptions of using this assessment tool. A quasi-experimental design will be employed, recruiting 320 freshmen and sophomores from two public-funded, comprehensive universities in Hong Kong, which represent a total of eight public-funded universities in the territory. Participants will be randomly assigned to either an experimental group that adopts WeChat-based e-portfolios (N = 160, comprising four intact classes from one university) or a control group using paper-based portfolios (N = 160, comprising four intact classes from another university). Both groups will undergo pre-test, intervention, and post-test procedures, and their L2 writing performance and anxiety levels will be measured before and after the intervention by using the International English Language Testing System (IELTS) Writing Task 2 with its rubrics and Second Language Writing Anxiety Inventory (SLWAI), respectively. After the post-test, semi-structured focus-group interviews (n = 80) will be conducted to gather insights into participants’ perspectives on utilizing WeChat-based e-portfolio assessment. The quantitative data will be scrutinized via the paired t-test and the independent sample t-test. Concurrently, the qualitative data will adhere to the six prescribed procedures put forth by Creswell and Clark (2011). The findings of this study can enrich the existing knowledge base of e-portfolio assessment, shed new light on the effectiveness of using social media-based e-portfolios for L2 writing assessment, and provide scientific empirical evidence for the use of alternative assessment approaches along with the trend of integrating information and communication technology into L2 writing assessment in the Hong Kong higher education landscape and beyond. 在英語作為第二語言或外語（EFL）寫作教學領域，過去二十年間，學界對基於社交網路平臺進行的電子檔案袋評估給予了高度關注。然而，對於擁有11.5億月活躍用戶的微信（即一款集即時通訊與社交網路功能於一體的應用）如何被用作電子檔案袋評估平臺，以識別低年級本科生在學術寫作方面的學習水準及其在完成基於課程的寫作任務時的焦慮程度，目前仍知之甚少。本研究旨在探究基於微信的電子檔案袋評估（亞洲地區廣受歡迎的社交網路工具）對香港本科生（即大一和大二學生）的二語寫作水準及焦慮程度的影響，以及他們對使用該評估工具的看法。研究採用准實驗設計，從香港兩所公立綜合性大學中招募320名大一及大二學生，這兩所大學代表了香港境內八所公立大學。參與者將被隨機分配到兩組之一：使用基於微信的電子檔案袋的實驗組（n=160，來自一所大學的四個完整班級），或使用紙本學習檔案袋的對照組（n=160，來自另一所大學的四個完整班級）。兩組均將經歷前測、干預和後測流程。干預前後，分別使用國際英語語言測試系統（IELTS）寫作任務二及其評分標準來評估其二語寫作水準，並使用二語寫作焦慮量表（SLWAI）測量其焦慮程度。後測結束後，將開展半結構化焦點小組訪談（n=80），以收集參與者對使用基於微信的電子檔案袋評估的看法和見解。定量數據將採用配對 t 檢驗和獨立樣本 t 檢驗進行詳細分析。 同時，定性數據將遵循 Creswell 和 Clark（2011）提出的六項規定程序處理。研究結果能夠豐富現有電子檔案袋評估領域的知識體系，為基於社交媒體的電子檔案袋在二語寫作評估中的有效性提供新的見解，並為香港高等教育領域乃至更廣泛的二語寫作評估中採用替代性評估方法，及將資訊與通信技術融入二語寫作評估的趨勢提供科學實證依據。

12605226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12605226.value: 被定型，亦反擊？亞洲媒體性別歧視與女性領袖的數位傳播策略

12605226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12605226.value: This project addresses gaps in our understanding of media sexism and the strategies employed by political and business leaders, with a focus on women in South Korea, Taiwan, Singapore, and Hong Kong between 2020 and 2024. Most research on media sexism centres on Western contexts and political figures, leaving the experiences of women leaders in other regions and sectors insufficiently explored. By broadening empirical inquiry to these East and Southeast Asian settings and including both political and business sectors, this study aims to provide a more comprehensive account of gender bias in media. First, the research will undertake a comparative analysis of traditional news media portrayals, examining how key women leaders are depicted relative to male counterparts. Specifically, the project will investigate different facets of gendered coverage, including attention to feminine/masculine policy issues, personal life or appearance, use of gender identifiers, tone, and coverage volume. This multidimensional approach enables a nuanced assessment of media bias. Moreover, the cross-national and cross-sectoral design will reveal whether similar stereotypes persist across democratic and authoritarian regimes or differ between political and business sectors. Second, given the growing influence of digital media platforms, the study also examines how leaders use social media such as Facebook and LinkedIn to respond to biased portrayals in traditional news media. By analysing their digital communication strategies—such as the content they share online—the research explores how women leaders challenge stereotypes and how their approaches differ from those of their male counterparts. For example, they may highlight agentic qualities or emphasize engagement with policy issues that are traditionally associated with men. This analysis will shed light on how digital communication can be leveraged to counter or reshape dominant narratives. Methodologically, quantitative analysis will be applied to the coded dataset of news articles and social media posts, using descriptive statistics and regression models to identify patterns and associations between gender, sector, and coverage characteristics. Qualitative corpus-assisted critical discourse analysis will then be conducted, allowing for a close examination of how language and framing construct or challenge gender stereotypes. The study promises a substantial contribution to understanding media sexism and gendered leadership image management in Asian contexts. Beyond advancing theory, it will produce a new dataset on gendered media coverage and digital self-presentation strategies. The findings will also offer practical guidance for policymakers, media organizations, political parties, and businesses seeking to monitor and mitigate gender bias in leadership representation. 本研究探討2020至2024年間南韓、台灣、新加坡及香港政治與商界領袖所面對的媒體性別歧視，以及女性領袖如何運用數位平台回應、挑戰及重塑帶有性別偏見的媒體敘事。研究首先比較傳統新聞媒體對男女領袖的報道差異，包括政策議題、外貌與私人生活、性別標籤、報道語調及曝光程度，並分析這些差異是否因政治制度、國家及領域而有所不同。其次，本研究將檢視女性領袖在Facebook及LinkedIn等社交媒體上的自我呈現與溝通策略，例如強調領導能力、專業形象，以及參與傳統上被視為男性主導的政策議題。方法上，研究將結合新聞文章與社交媒體帖文的量化分析，以及語料輔助批判論述分析，以揭示性別刻板印象如何被建構、延續或挑戰。本研究將深化對亞洲媒體性別歧視及女性領袖形象管理的理解，並為政府、媒體、政黨及企業減少領導形象中的性別偏見提供實證建議。

12605526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12605526.value: 有特殊學習需要子女家長的雙向聚焦人際情緒調節模型：一項混合方法的縱向網絡分析研究

12605526.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12605526.value: Prof Epskamp, Sacha Prof Hofmann, Stefan G. Prof Kwok Lai, Sylvia Yuk Ching Prof Pan, Jiayan Dr Samson, Andrea
rows: Prof Kwok Lai, Sylvia Yuk Ching

12605526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12605526.value: In Hong Kong, there has been a steady increase in the prevalence of children with reported special educational needs. Internationally and locally, approximately 30% to 40% parents of children with special educational needs experience elevated depressive and anxiety symptoms. High parental stress and mental health problems can lead to negative parenting behaviours and adversely impact children’s development. Unfortunately, several incidents of abuse of children with special educational needs and even homicide due to adverse parental mental health have been reported in Hong Kong in recent years, raising significant concerns about parental stress and mental health. Current interventions for parents of children with special educational needs typically focus on either parental stress management or parenting skills training. These approaches demonstrate inconsistent effectiveness in improving parental mental health and may not adequately secure healthy functioning in the parent-child dyad. Emotion regulation (ER), a crucial transdiagnostic factor linked to mental health and a promising intervention target, remains understudied in this population. Grounded in the recently developed interpersonal ER framework, this study proposes a reciprocal interpersonal model of dual-focused (i.e., self-focused and child-focused) ER for parent-child dyads in families with a child with special educational needs. Using both advanced network analysis and qualitative inquiry, we will investigate the reciprocal mechanisms between parents’ and children’s ER. This is a 3-year mixed-methods research design comprising a 3-wave longitudinal observational study and a qualitative study. Stratified cluster random sampling will be adopted to recruit 650 parents of a child with special educational needs in Hong Kong. Network analysis will be adopted to explore how parents’ self- and child-focused ER strategies connect to children’s ER and parents’ mental health, as well as how parents’ and children’s ER reciprocally impact each other. Semi-structured qualitative interviews will be conducted among 45 parent-child dyads to enhance the richness and in-depth understanding of the contextual factors influencing the interpersonal ER process. This study aims to provide an in-depth understanding of the reciprocal dynamics between parents’ and children’s ER and mental health, contributing to ER theory in parent-child interactions. If supported, this model will address a critical gap in interventions by informing the development of a reciprocal, interpersonal, and dynamic ER coaching programme. This avoids negative consequences, such as family tragedies, and will potentially benefit over 80,000 families in Hong Kong. 在香港，被界定為有特殊教育需要兒童的比率持續上升。無論在國際或本地研究中，大約有 30% 至 40% 的特殊教育需要子女家長出現較高程度的抑鬱及焦慮症狀。家長承受高度壓力及出現精神健康問題，會導致負面的教養行為，並對子女的發展造成不良影響。近年本港更先後出現多宗涉及特殊教育需要兒童的虐兒，甚至因家長精神健康惡化而導致的弒親悲劇，令社會對家長壓力及精神健康問題更為關注。 現時為特殊教育需要子女家長而設的介入，多集中於家長壓力管理或教養技巧培訓其中一方面。這類介入在改善家長精神健康方面的成效並不一致，而且未必足以全面保障親子二元關係的健康運作。情緒調節（emotion regulation, ER）是與精神健康高度相關、跨診斷的重要關鍵因素，也是具潛力的介入目標，然而在此群體中仍然研究不足。基於近年提出的人際情緒調節理論架構，本研究擬建構一個以親子二元互動為本的雙向聚焦（即自我聚焦與子女聚焦）的情緒調節人際模式，並以此說明在有特殊教育需要子女家庭中，家長與子女情緒調節之間的互動機制。本研究將結合網絡分析方法及質性探究，深入考察家長與子女情緒調節之間的互動歷程。 本研究為期三年，採用混合方法研究設計，包括縱向觀察研究及質性研究。我們將以分層整群隨機抽樣方式，在全港招募 650 位照顧一名有特殊教育需要子女的家長。研究將運用網絡分析來探討家長之自我聚焦及子女聚焦情緒調節策略，如何與子女的情緒調節及家長的精神健康互相關聯，以及家長與子女情緒調節之間如何互相影響。另外，我們將對 45 對親子進行半結構式質性訪談，以更豐富及深入地理解影響人際情緒調節歷程的情境因素。 本研究旨在深入剖析家長與子女情緒調節及精神健康之間的互惠動態，從而推進親子互動情緒調節理論之發展。若本研究所提出的模式獲得支援，將可填補現有介入上的重要缺口，為日後發展一套具互動性及動態性的情緒調節教練計劃提供理論基礎，以促進家庭福祉，並有潛力惠及本港逾 80,000 個特殊教育需要兒童家庭。

12606626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12606626.value: 二〇〇〇年後香港電影中老化的再現與文化政治

12606626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12606626.value: Hong Kong cinema has been one of the most widely researched and discussed cinemas, but not many publications take aging and elderhood as the center of inquiry. In order to fill the gap, this book-length project is set to probe the representation of aging in the Hong Kong films produced after 2000 and uncovers the cultural politics involved with respect to the city’s changing socio-political realities in the new millennium. This study poses several questions: first, what are the narrative and aesthetic strategies to represent old age in contemporary Hong Kong films? Second, what concerns, sentiments, and power dynamics evoked by aging are unfolded in those films? Third, in what ways do the cinematically portrayed aging experiences have intersections and dialogues with the wider socio-political and cultural milieus of Hong Kong? Finally, how do the outcomes of study inform and mobilize the theoretical debates in the studies of Hong Kong cinema? These questions need to be answered with the help of systematic research of the cinematic discourse of elderhood in Hong Kong informed by theoretical formations of aging and cinema. Employing a qualitative, textual-cultural approach, the proposed project centrally explores how aging is represented in contemporary Hong Kong films and how the representations intersect and interact with pertinent cultural discourses by unraveling the complexities, perplexes, and tensions involved. By pursuing the methodological lens of age, this project traces and negotiates gerontological imaginaries as a form of texts that prospered in popular entertainment alongside socio-political, cultural, and industrial transformations. The PI renders textual analysis and cultural reading to anlayze the filmic image of aging, in association with theoretical inquiry of disability, fidelity of care, gerontological patriarchy, and gay sexuality. Building on the thriving area of research of Hong Kong cinema, this project intervenes into the current debate of popular representations of late life, which is seriously under-studied. It illuminates an effort to disrupt a Western-inclined critical mobilization of studying aging and cinema, offering an alternative to the existing scholarship in the context of Hong Kong. This project not only recalibrates the discursive vigor of elderhood in cinematic discourse but also reveals the potential to expand the paradigmic trajectory in the study of Hong Kong films. The research outcome leads to one international conference presentation and an academic monograph published by a university press. 香港電影文化一向是最受廣泛研究與討論的電影文化之一，但以「老化」與「老年」為核心探究對象的相關著述卻不多見。為填補此一空白，本專書計畫旨在深入探討二〇〇〇年後香港電影中老化的再現，並揭示其中所牽涉的文化政治，特別是其如何回應新千禧年香港社會政治現實的變遷。為此，本研究提出以下問題：一，當代香港電影在再現老年時，採取何種敘事與美學策略？二，這些電影如何展開由老化所引發的關注、情感與權力動態？三，電影所描繪的老化經驗，如何在與香港更廣泛的社會政治與文化脈絡的互動中，形成交匯與對話？最後，研究結果如何啟發及推動香港電影研究中的理論探討？要回答這些問題，必須透過由「老化與電影」之理論建構所引導的香港老年電影話語進行系統性研究。 本研究採用質性文本-文化研究方法，聚焦探討當代香港電影如何再現老化，以及這些再現如何與相關文化話語交織互動，藉此揭示個中複雜性、彷徨與張力。研究以「年齡」作為方法論視角，追蹤並協商以文本形式呈現的「老年學想像」。這些想像在流行娛樂中蓬勃發展，並與社會政治、文化脈絡及產業轉型的進程並行。研究者將以文本分析與文化詮釋的方法，結合殘障、照護忠誠、老年學父權與同性情欲等的理論查究，採索電影中的老化影像。 本研究建基於香港電影研究的興旺領域，以介入目前被嚴重忽視、關於晚年生活之流行文化再現的討論。它力圖打破帶有西方傾向的老化與電影研究之批判取徑，在香港脈絡中提供可供對照的另類視角。此研究不僅重新校準電影話語中老年的論述動能，更進一步揭示香港電影研究範式軌跡的擴張潛能。研究成果將包括一次國際會議發表及由大學出版社出版學術專書。

12607226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12607226.value: 感知差異：失明、失聰與藝術史正典

12607226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12607226.value: Abstract: The proposed project investigates intersections between art practice and sensory disability in Renaissance and Baroque art. Situated at the crossroads between art history, social history and disability studies, it locates understandings of sensory loss in the context of history, social and religious practices, literature, visual and material culture. By looking at documentary sources, including first-person narratives, legal documents, poetry, sculptures, drawings, and paintings, it interrogates how early modern artists with sensory disabilities navigated their daily lives, professional careers, and personal relationships. While doing so, it highlights the fluidity of disability experiences, challenging enduring stereotypes and emphasising that in premodern societies responses to impairment were shaped by a variety of intersectional factors. While disability studies have recently become a robust aspect of historical research, they remain a neglected topic within early modern art history. Opening a new field of enquiry, the proposed project retraces the life experiences and professional careers of seven artists who experienced congenital or adventitious sensory loss: Benedetto Grazzini (1474–1552), Giovanni Paolo Lomazzo (1538–1592), Girolamo Padulo (ca. 1550–1600), Hans Verhagen (1554–1600), Giovanni Gonnelli (1603–1664), Wolfgang Heimbach (1615-1678), and Giovanni Lo Coco (1667–1721). Each career is presented as a microhistory: a case study that opens a window into broader historical and art historical questions. The project interrogates matters of artistic training, public reception, and patronage. It unravels the strategies adopted by artists with sensory loss to advance themselves both socially and professionally, debunking assumptions that identify them as self-taught outsiders. The study challenges the idea that early modern people with disabilities were necessarily living on the fringes of society and depended on the charity of temporarily abled people. It replaces this ableist notion with individual case studies that highlight the agency of artists with sensory disabilities in the workplace and within their family networks. Through in depth articulation, art historical, visual, cultural, and socio historical analysis, the project (i) challenges the exclusion of artists with disabilities from the canon of art history; (ii) presents a different way to look at how sensory disability was perceived in the early modern period; and (iii) investigates concepts of disability identity and disability gain, supplementing analyses and debates conducted in our contemporary world. 摘要： 本項目旨在探討文藝復興與巴洛克時期藝術實踐與感官缺陷之間的交匯。此研究將聚焦於藝術史、社會史與殘障研究的交叉點，從歷史、社會與宗教實踐、文學、視覺及物質文化的脈絡中，定位對感官喪失的理解。通過檢視文獻資料，包括第一人稱敘述、法律文件、詩歌、雕塑、素描及繪畫等，本研究探討早期現代具有感官殘障的藝術家如何在日常生活、專業生涯及個人關係中自處與應對。研究同時強調殘障經驗的流動性，挑戰根深蒂固的刻板印象，並指出前現代社會對殘障的回應如何由多重交織的因素所形塑。儘管殘障研究近年已成為歷史研究的重要範疇，但在早期現代藝術史領域仍屬較為忽視的主題。本項目開闢新的研究領域，重構七位具有先天或後天感官喪失藝術家的生活經驗與職業生涯，包括：Benedetto Grazzini (1474–1552) 、Giovanni Paolo Lomazzo (1538–1592) 、Girolamo Padulo (ca. 1550–1600) 、Hans Verhagen (1554–1600) 、Giovanni Gonnelli (1603–1664) 、Wolfgang Heimbach (1615-1678) 和 Giovanni Lo Coco (1667–1721)）。每一位藝術家的生涯皆以「微觀史」的方式呈現，作為契機，以更「宏觀」的角度探究歷史與藝術史的相關議題究。項目將探討藝術訓練、公眾觀感與商業贊助等議題，並揭示這些藝術家為提升自身社會與專業地位所採取的策略，駁斥他們僅為自學成才、局外人的假設。本研究質疑早期現代殘障者必然被邊緣化並依賴健全者施惠的觀念，並以個案研究取而代之，凸顯感官殘障藝術家於職場及家庭網絡中的能動性。通過深入的論述、藝術史、視覺、文化及社會歷史分析，本項目：（一）挑戰將殘障藝術家排除於藝術史正典之外的傳統；（二）提供一種理解早期現代社會感官缺陷觀念的新視角；（三）探討殘障認同與殘障優勢等概念，補充當代相關分析與討論。

12607426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12607426.value: 《追憶阿薩亞卡特爾：一位阿茲特克帝王的生命與來生》

12607426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12607426.value: 'Remembering Axayacatl' is a project focused on writing a biography of an important, but little studied, Aztec emperor, Axayactl, and how he was remembered for approximately 130-years after his death. 'Remembering Axayacatl' will utilize sources found in colonial archives, rare and published manuscripts, and frame them within the context of popular Nahuatl language songs. These songs, found in the 'Cantares Mexicanos' manuscript, are central to this project because they are part of an oral tradition which was transcribed in the mid-sixteenth century, but had roots from long before the arrival of the Spanish. Song lyrics, and evidence about their performances from other sources, are ideal for framing this project for two reasons. First, the lyrics capture specific emotional and popular commentaries about Axayacatl that were handed down over generations. Second, these commentaries represent perspectives of a more diverse segment of the Nahua population (audience and performers) than other sources. The majority of other sources about Axayacatl were prepared by Indigenous nobles who wrote for other Nahua intellectuals, friars who focused on conversion efforts, or the second or third generation of mixed-ancestry nobility (Spanish and Nahua) invested in better positioning their home cities in Spanish political debates. The songs provide a unique and little studied entry point to analyze Axayacatl’s life and how it was remembered during the colonial period by people whose perspectives are normally considered to be lost to history. 'Remembering Axayacatl' will trace the communal memory and emotions of the residents of the Aztec city of Tenochtitlan and the transition to the Spanish run Mexico City from the 1460s to the late-sixteenth century. This focus will expand our understanding of how layers of communal memory and rulership worked in Nahua society that bridges the precolonial and colonial periods. Disrupting the commonplace division between colonial and precolonial will promote a new methodology from which to engage with song lyrics as political critiques based on historical memories while acknowledging the traumas of conquest and colonization. By emphasizing Indigenous voices as well as their own structures of historical memory, this study will show how an Indigenous people applied their own traditional knowledge and forms of history keeping to a quickly changing world. 'Remembering Axayacatl' engages the accessibility of a biography to discuss important scholarly conversations related to the knowability of the precolonial period while proposing and applying important theoretical framings in memory studies and the history of emotions. 《追憶阿薩亞卡特爾》項目旨在為一位重要但鮮少被研究的阿茲特克皇帝阿薩亞卡特爾撰寫傳記，並探討在他去世後約130 年間, 人們是如何銘記他的。《追憶阿薩亞卡特爾》將利用殖民時期檔案、珍稀手稿及已出版手稿中的史料，並將其置於納瓦特爾語通俗歌謠的脈絡中進行解讀。這些收錄於《墨西哥詩歌》（Cantares Mexicanos）手稿中的歌曲，是本計畫的項目的核心所在，因為它們屬於一種口述傳統: 該傳統雖於十六世紀中葉被筆錄成文，而其淵源卻遠溯至西班牙人抵達之前的久遠年代。 這些歌詞, 以及其他資料中關於這些歌曲演出的證據，為本項目提供了尤為理想的研究切入框架，原因有二。首先，歌詞保存了圍繞阿薩亞卡特爾所形成的具體情感表達和民間評論，並經由世代相傳。其次，與其他史料相比，這些評論所呈現的視角來自更為多元的納瓦人群體（既包括觀眾，亦包括表演者本身）。關於阿克薩亞卡特爾的其他史料，大多出自以下幾類作者之手：為其他納瓦知識分子撰述的原住民貴族、投身於傳教與皈依工作的修士，以及致力於在西班牙政治辯論中提升其家鄉城邦地位的西班牙—納瓦混血貴族的第二代或第三代后裔。這些歌曲提供了一個獨特且鮮少受到學界關注的切入點，使我們能夠重新考察阿薩亞卡特爾的生平，以及殖民時期人們如何記憶這位人物——尤其是那些其視角通常被視為已湮沒於歷史之中的人群。 《追憶阿薩亞卡特爾》將追溯自以及從15世紀60年代到16世紀末, 阿茲特克城市特諾奇提特蘭居民的集體記憶和情感，以及該城市向西班牙統治下的墨西哥城轉型的歷史進程。這一研究焦點將拓展我們對納瓦社會中層層交織的集體記憶和統治權力如何運作的理解，從而連結前殖民時期和殖民時期。藉由打破殖民時期和前殖民時期之間慣常的二分法，本研究將提出一套新的方法論：在承認征服與殖民所造成之創傷的同時，將歌詞視為植根於歷史記憶的政治批評加以探討。通過強調原住民的聲音, 以及其自身的歷史記憶架構，本研究將展示一個原住民群體如何運用自身的傳統知識和歷史記述方式, 來理解並應對一個急遽變遷的世界。 《追憶阿薩亞卡特爾》藉由傳記此一易於理解與接近的形式，探討與前殖民時期之「可知性」相關的重要學術論辯; 與此同時，本研究亦提出並運用了記憶研究和情感史領域中的重要理論框架。

12607626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12607626.value: 鮮活的影像：近代早期日本形象媒介中的動畫美學

12607626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12607626.value: This project will provide a new understanding of figural media produced in the urban centres of early modern Japan. These included bidimensional figure paintings in manuscript (hanging scrolls, handscrolls, folding screens), figural depictions in print (single-sheet prints, book illustrations), and anthropomorphic three-dimensional media (dolls, puppets, ceramic statuettes). All of these figural media belonged to what came to be known as ukiyo 浮世 (‘the floating world’): a construct that celebrated the cultural practices associated with urban entertainment. The term ‘figural media’ is used because either specific named individuals, such as actors or prostitutes, or generic types were depicted. This project’s working thesis is that the effectiveness and appeal of these figural media relied on a slippage between reality and representation. The phenomenon amounted to an ‘aesthetics of animation’: the appreciation of images as potentially imbued with life, or having ontological potential. The term ‘animation’ is used here in the anthropological sense of attributing qualities of aliveness to inanimate objects, and should not be confused with the term from media and film studies denoting a moving-image medium. The main questions are: what were the roles of figural media in the ‘aesthetics of animation’ of early modern Japan? What were the patterns of interaction between figural media and their users? To investigate the questions above, the PI will deploy an interdisciplinary approach to discussing terms used to describe figural media in this period, such as utsushi, which will enable a theory of ‘floating world’ images. This will be complemented by analyses of stories and images of the time featuring figure paintings interacting with their users as if alive. The main outcome will be the publication of a monograph by a leading academic publisher. This objective will be achieved by applying the PI’s expertise in the history of the art and visual culture of Japan. The first phase of the project (4 months) will involve literature review and fieldwork to consult primary sources in Japan. The second phase (12 months) will consist of conference presentations, writing of the monograph manuscript, and securing the publishing contract, starting by proposing the book to Brill for inclusion in their Japanese Visual Culture series. The third phase (8 months) will comprise rewriting based on peer reviewers’ comments, resubmission of the manuscript and final editing for publication. 本計畫將為早期現代日本都市中心所產製的人物類媒介提供新的理解。這些媒介包括手抄本中的二維人物畫（掛軸、手卷、屏風）、版畫中的人物描繪（單張版畫、書籍插圖），以及擬人化的三維媒介（玩偶、木偶、陶瓷小雕像）。所有這些具象媒介都屬於後來被稱為「浮世」（ukiyo）的範疇：這是一個頌揚與都市娛樂相關的文化實踐的建構概念。之所以使用「具象媒介」一詞，是因為其中描繪的對象，要麼是具名的特定個人（例如演員或妓女），要麼是 某種通用類型。本研究的工作假說認為，這些具象媒體的有效性與吸引力，取決於現實與表徵之間的錯位。此現象實質上構成了一種「動畫美學」：即將圖像視為潛在蘊含生命，或具備本體論潛能的對象。此處「動畫」一詞係採用人類學意義，意指將生命特質歸於無生命物體，不應 與媒體及電影研究中指稱動態影像媒介的術語混淆。主要問題包括：在早期現代日本的「動畫美學」中，具象媒體扮演了什麼角色?形象媒介與其使用者之間的互動模式究竟為何？為探究上述問題，首席研究員將採用跨學科方法，探討用以描述此時期形象媒介的術語，例如「utsushi」，藉此建構「浮世」圖像的理論。此外，本研究亦將輔以對當時故事與圖像的分析，這些作品中描繪的人物畫彷彿活物般與使用者互動。主要成果將是由一家頂尖學術出版社出版專著。此目標將透過運用首席研究員在日本藝術史與視覺文化方面的專業知識來達成。本計畫的第一階段（4個月）將進行文獻回顧及田野調查，以查閱日本境內的一手資料。第二階段（12 個月）將包含會議發表、撰寫專著書稿，以及爭取出版合約，首先將向 Brill 出版社提案，希望將該書納入其「日本視覺文化」系列。第三階段（8 個月）將包含根據同行評審意見進行修改、重新提交書稿 以及為出版進行最終編輯。

12608026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12608026.value: 歐盟擴張的框架建構，2004–2028：地緣政治、理想主義與程序主義之間的歐盟

12608026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12608026.value: Whether, when, and how the EU should expand is among the most pressing questions facing EU policymakers. Russia’s February 2022 invasion of Ukraine put enlargement firmly back on the agenda, following a decade of ‘enlargement fatigue’.
