The post-invasion extension of a membership perspective to Ukraine, Moldova, and Georgia has also brought renewed attention to the Western Balkans candidates, and to the larger issue of the EU’s ‘absorption capacity’. The proposed project will provide a deeper understanding of present trends and likely future directions via the contextualisation of EU actors’ reactions to the invasion in a broader timeframe. Following the insights of discursive institutionalism, the project focuses on enlargement discourses, which constitute the space for political action. Using the method of framing discourse analysis, the project will track changing attitudes towards enlargement in three institutions – the European Council, the Commission, and the European Parliament (EP) – from 2004 to 2028. The EP’s inclusion is particularly novel. Evidence indicates that it is an increasingly important foreign policy actor and that party groups play a central role as inter-institutional mediators. Yet, the EP remains understudied in the enlargement space. Researchers will gather quantitative and qualitative data on the salience of enlargement, sentiment towards it, and the prevalence of identified frames from a range of primary sources, including European Council conclusions, speeches of the Commission President and High Representative, EP party group manifestos, EP resolutions, and semi-structured interviews. Analysis of the data will yield significant insights into attitudes towards enlargement within and across institutions, and how these have changed over time. Researchers will investigate whether and how exogenous shocks, including Russia’s invasion of Georgia (2008), the Russian annexation of Crimea (2014), the full-scale invasion of Ukraine (2022), and Donald Trump’s return to the US presidency (2025) have affected actors’ perspectives on enlargement. Beyond the compilation of a comprehensive dataset on discursive framings of enlargement, the project’s value-added is both empirical and conceptual. First, it will advance scholarly understandings of the EU’s strategic capacity, contributing to efforts to evaluate the EU’s ‘geopolitical turn’ amidst a weakening of the liberal international order. Second, it will investigate the dynamic interaction between enlargement frames, including the shifting construction of ‘merit’ as a geopolitical, normative, and procedural concept.

12608726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12608726.value: 神話與礦藏：梵文醫學與寶石學文獻中寶石神話起源的翻譯

12608726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12608726.value: The project examines alchemical and gemological materials in the Sanskrit language dating from the ninth to seventheenth centuries that focus on the mythological origins and medical usage of nine gems: diamond, pear, coral, garnet/zircon, sapphire, cat eye, topaz, emerald, and ruby. I have identified 20 Sanskrit texts that contain material on the mythological formations, detailed descriptions, and preparations of gems for medicinal applications. The texts range from alchemical works (Rasapaddhati, Rasarnava, Rasendracudamami, and Rasaratnakara) to religious (Garudapurana) to gemological (Manimahatmaya, Manasollasa, Ratnadipika) to ayurvedic (Todaranda, Ayurvedaprakasa), demonstrating textual interconnectedness of works previously studied in isolation. A preliminary examination finds fantastical tales of jewels forming from the mouths and bodies of both gods and demons. Diamonds, for example, are said to have formed during the creation of the universe, when the gods drank the nectar of immortality which arose during the churning of the Ocean of Milk. As they drank, drops of the nectar fell to the ground and became diamonds. This myth uses the standard Hindu creation tale to explain a natural phenomenon in a new and unique way. Alchemical works differ from other medicinal manuals with their rich literary sections that use prevailing religious and mythological themes interwoven with more traditional explanations of disease, plants, and mineral materials. The detailed explanations of the characteristics of gemstones fit into the Hindu mythological worldview but are also analogue with modern scientific understandings of carat, faults, and other qualities. To date few studies have focused on gemological materials in Sanskrit, despite the importance of the Subcontinent to the global gem trade (India is one of the largest centres in the world for the polishing of precious gemstones). The most detailed study of gemological material related to this project is Louis Finot’s French language 1896 work Les Lapidaires Indiens. Dagmar Wujastyk’s 2023 article “Making Gems in Indian Alchemical Literature” discusses the making of artificial gemstones in a 15-17th century alchemical work. Neither of these works explore the myths and usage of medicinal gemstones. Finot is largely an edited edition and partial translation of several gemological works and Wujastyk states artificial gems recipes do not contain any medicinal usages. Through this study, I hope to demonstrate that in fact the alchemical works cross the boundaries of scientific, medicinal, geological, and social traditions that can help us understand the broader significance of healing within Subcontinental history. 本計畫研究了公元9至17世紀梵語煉金術和寶石學文獻，重點關註九種寶石的神話起源和藥用價值：鑽石、梨形寶石、珊瑚、石榴石/鋯石、藍寶石、貓眼石、托帕石、祖母綠和紅寶石。我已找到20篇梵文文獻，其中包含有關神話起源、詳細描述以及寶石藥用製備方法的資料。這些文獻涵蓋了煉金術著作（《Rasapaddhati》、《Rasarnava》、《Rasendracudamami》和《Rasaratnakara》）、宗教著作（《Garudapurana》）、寶石學著作（《Manimahatmaya》、《Manasollasa》和《Ratnadipika》）以及阿育斯育（《吠陀）》中初步研究發現，其中不乏關於寶石由神魔口中或體內形成的奇幻傳說。例如，據說鑽石是在宇宙創世之初形成的，當時眾神飲用了攪動乳海時湧現的不朽甘露。甘露滴落到地上，化作了鑽石。這個神話運用了標準的印度教創世故事，以一種新穎獨特的方式解釋了自然現象。 煉金術著作與其他醫學手冊的不同之處在於，它們擁有豐富的文學部分，將當時盛行的宗教和神話主題與對疾病、植物和礦物材料的更傳統的解釋交織在一起。寶石特性的詳細解釋既符合印度教神話的世界觀，也與現代科學對克拉、瑕疵和其他品質的理解相呼應。儘管印度次大陸在全球寶石貿易中扮演著重要角色（印度是世界上最大的寶石加工中心之一），但迄今為止，鮮有研究關注梵文寶石學文獻。與本計畫相關的最詳盡的寶石學文獻是路易·菲諾 (Louis Finot) 於 1896 年出版的法語著作《印度寶石》(Les Lapidaires Indiens)。達格瑪·伍亞斯提克 (Dagmar Wujastyk) 於 2023 年發表的文章《印度煉金術文獻中的寶石製作》探討了 15 至 17 世紀煉金術著作中人造寶石的製作方法。然而，這兩部著作均未探討藥用寶石的神話傳說及其用途。菲諾的著作主要是對多部寶石學著作的編輯和部分翻譯，而伍亞斯斯蒂克則指出，人造寶石的配方中並未提及任何藥用價值。透過這項研究，我希望證明，煉金術作品實際上跨越了科學、醫學、地質和社會傳統的界限，這可以幫助我們理解治療在次大陸歷史中的更廣泛意義。

12609026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12609026.value: 中國煤礦開采甲烷排放的多尺度評估

12609026.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12609026.value: Prof Lo, Tek Sheng Kevin Prof Lu, Xi Prof Qin, Kai

12609026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12609026.value: This project employs integrated multi-scale monitoring to quantify methane emissions from China’s coal mining sector, where current estimates rely predominantly on IPCC Tier 1 default emission factors with substantial uncertainties. It addresses critical data and knowledge gaps constraining evidence-based mitigation strategies needed to support China’s methane action plan and carbon neutrality commitments. Methane emissions from coal mining are a major climate concern, with CH4 having 80 times the warming potential of CO2 over a 20-year period. China produces nearly half of the world’s coal, yet atmospheric observations show methane levels that exceed inventory-based estimates. The lack of mandatory monitoring creates a regulatory gap, where operators prioritize safety-grade sensors over climate-relevant measurements, and reliance on self-reported data prevents accurate emission quantification. This measurement shortfall hampers China’s ability to establish empirical baselines and set quantitative reduction targets. The research methodology entails three interconnected tasks: (i) establishing empirical emission factors through hierarchical field measurements at 60 strategically selected mines in Shanxi, Inner Mongolia, and Shandong, using vehicle-mounted laboratories and statistical scaling relationships to extrapolate results to unmeasured mines; (ii) validating the multi-scale monitoring framework by reconciling mine-level measurements with regional atmospheric observations, incorporating uncertainty analysis across scales; and (iii) developing science-based policy frameworks that quantify technical reduction potentials using marginal abatement cost curves and evaluate differentiated regulatory pathways by mine size and ownership. Strategies to mitigate potential risks related to methodology and logistics are also proposed. The PI’s preliminary field studies in Shanxi (August 2024) demonstrated the feasibility of the proposed methodology through successful seven-day mobile monitoring campaigns at multiple operational mines, quantifying emissions from ventilation shafts, drainage systems, and coal storage areas. These pilot measurements identified previously unaccounted emission sources, underscoring the need for comprehensive field-based quantification. The PI’s team has the required instrumentation and technical expertise to implement the multi-scale monitoring framework. Established partnerships with local coal mining operators and environmental bureaus ensure site access and operational data sharing across the target mines. The expected outcomes will directly support China’s methane action plan by providing validated emission factor databases, provincial inventories with transparent uncertainty bounds, quantified reduction potentials by mine characteristics, and policy frameworks that guide measurable emission reductions in line with national climate commitments. These methodologies will also advance international climate mitigation efforts, particularly in countries facing similar data gaps when developing comprehensive methane management strategies. 本項目採用整合多尺度監測方法，對中國煤礦行業的甲烷排放量進行量化研究。目前，相關估算主要依賴IPCC第一層級默認排放因子，具有相當程度的不確定性。本研究旨在彌補制約循證減排策略的關鍵數據與知識缺口，進而支持中國甲烷行動計劃與碳中和承諾的落實。 煤礦開採所產生的甲烷排放是氣候變化的重大威脅，甲烷在20年時間尺度內的全球增溫潛勢為二氧化碳的80倍。中國生產了全球近一半的煤炭，然而大氣觀測數據顯示，實際甲烷濃度已超過基於清單的估算結果。強制性監測機制的缺失形成了甲烷監管漏洞：相關運營方慣於優先配置安全級別的傳感器，而非氣候相關的監測設備，加之排放數據依賴自願申報，使甲烷實際排放量的準確量化難以實現。此一監測缺口嚴重削弱了中國以實證數據為依據、設定量化甲烷減排目標的能力。 本研究包含三項相互關聯的任務：（i）在山西、內蒙古及山東三省區的60座精選礦井開展分層次實地測量，以建立實證排放因子；並基於車載移動實驗室採集的現場監測數據，運用統計學方法將測量結果外推至未受監測的礦井；（ii）將礦井級測量結果與區域大氣觀測數據相互比對印證，並結合跨尺度蒙特卡洛不確定性分析，對多尺度監測框架進行系統驗證；（iii）構建以科學與實證為基礎的政策框架，運用邊際減排成本曲線量化甲烷減排技術的潛力，並依據礦井規模與所有制類型，評估差異化的監管路徑。研究亦針對方法論與後勤保障層面的潛在風險，提出相應的應對策略。 項目負責人於2024年8月在山西省開展了前期實地研究，在多個運營礦井成功實施為期七天的移動監測活動，驗證了本研究方法的可行性，並完成了對通風豎井、排水系統及煤炭儲存區域排放量的量化工作。試點測量發現了此前未被納入統計的排放源，進一步凸顯了開展全面實地量化研究的必要性。項目團隊具備實施多尺度監測框架所需的儀器設備與技術能力，並已與當地煤礦運營企業及環境管理部門建立合作關係，可確保對目標礦井的現場進入及相關生產數據的獲取與共享。 預期研究成果將為中國甲烷減排行動計劃提供直接支撐，主要包括：經過驗證的排放因子數據庫、附有透明不確定性區間的省級排放清單、基於礦井特徵的量化減排潛力評估，以及能夠指導可量化減排行動、契合國家氣候承諾的政策框架。上述研究方法亦將推動國際氣候減緩工作的進展，尤其對於在制定綜合甲烷管理策略時面臨類似數據缺口的國家，具有重要的參考借鑒價值。

12609126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12609126.value: 不平等的學位：香港直接入學與銜接入學大學生從學府到職場的過渡研究

12609126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12609126.value: Prof Postiglione, Gerard Dr Tang, Hei Hang Hayes

12609126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12609126.value: Hong Kong’s higher education system has undergone significant structural changes over the past two decades. In the early 2000s, sub-degree programmes were introduced primarily to provide students who fail to enter university some postsecondary education. For many years, only a small proportion of sub-degree graduates successfully transferred into undergraduate programmes. However, since 2014, the expansion and formalisation of articulation pathways have enabled a growing number of students to enter public universities through transfer, steadily increasing their representation within the university population. After more than a decade of policy implementation, it is timely to evaluate the equity implications of this shift. This research project examines whether the increasing presence of transfer students in public universities leads to equitable educational and employment outcomes. Although the expansion of higher education is often linked to greater social mobility, not all students benefit equally. The massification of undergraduate degrees has contributed to credential inflation, allowing students from privileged backgrounds to leverage additional resources and maintain a competitive edge in the labour market. As a degree alone no longer guarantees meaningful employment, unequal access to career preparation and institutional support may deepen existing disparities. This raises important questions: Are students from different entry pathways—direct-entry and transfer—equally prepared for the transition to work? Do their university experiences yield comparable advantages in the labour market? Focusing on the university-to-work transition—a critical phase where inequalities may be reinforced or reduced—this study adopts a qualitative, longitudinal design. It will conduct two rounds of in-depth interviews with both direct-entry and transfer students: first during their final year of university, and again within one year after graduation. This approach captures rich, contextualised narratives and reveals how students prepare for and navigate their post-university trajectories. Unlike quantitative studies that highlight broad trends, this method offers a nuanced understanding of how social, familial, and educational backgrounds shape initial labour market outcomes, providing deeper insight into the lived experiences and institutional dynamics that influence graduate success. By comparing learning experiences, access to resources, and employment trajectories, the study contributes to theoretical debates on the equity implications of higher education expansion. It also offers policy-relevant insights into how universities can better support diverse student populations in preparing for employment. Ultimately, this research seeks to inform institutional practices and policy development that promote more inclusive and equitable outcomes in Hong Kong’s evolving higher education system. 過去二十年間，香港高等教育體系經歷了重大的結構性變革。二十世紀初，副學位課程的設立主要旨在為未能直接升讀大學的學生提供專上教育機會。在相當長的一段時間內，只有少數副學位畢業生能成功銜接至學士學位課程。然而，自2014年起，隨著銜接升學途徑的擴展與制度化，愈來愈多學生透過銜接方式進入公立大學，其在大學學生群體中的比例亦持續上升。在相關政策推行超過十年後，現在正是檢視此轉變對教育公平影響的適當時機。 本研究旨在探討銜接學生於公立大學人數增加，是否能帶來更公平的教育與就業成果。儘管高等教育擴張常被視為促進社會流動的重要途徑，但並非所有學生都能同等受惠。隨著學士學位日益普及，學歷膨脹現象逐漸加劇，使較具社會優勢背景的學生能透過額外資源維持其在勞動市場中的競爭優勢。在學位已不再保證理想就業機會的情況下，不同學生在職涯準備及院校支援方面所面對的不平等，可能進一步擴大既有差距。因此，本研究提出以下問題：來自不同入學途徑（直接入學與銜接入學）的學生，是否同樣具備從大學過渡至職場的準備？他們的大學經歷是否能轉化為相若的勞動市場優勢？ 本研究聚焦於「大學至職場轉銜」這一關鍵階段，因為社會不平等可能在此過程中被強化或緩解。研究採用質性縱向研究設計，對直接入學學生及銜接學生進行兩輪深入訪談：第一輪於大學最後一年進行，第二輪則於畢業後一年內進行。此研究方法能夠蒐集豐富且具脈絡性的生命敘事資料，深入理解學生如何準備及應對畢業後的發展歷程。相較於著重整體趨勢的量化研究，本研究更能細緻呈現社會背景、家庭條件及教育經驗如何影響畢業生初入職場的結果，並揭示影響其就業發展的個人經歷與制度因素。 透過比較不同學生群體的學習經驗、資源獲取情況及就業發展軌跡，本研究將有助於深化有關高等教育擴張與教育公平之間關係的理論討論。同時，研究亦能為大學如何更有效支援多元學生群體的就業準備工作提供實證基礎與政策啟示。最終，本研究期望為香港高等教育體系的制度實踐與政策制定提供參考，促進更具包容性及公平性的教育與就業成果。

12609826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12609826.value: 大型推理模型能否進行批判性和創造性思考？ 忠實推理、擬人化語調和溯因推理的根本評估

12609826.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12609826.value: Prof Beni, Majid D. Prof Copeland, Jack

12609826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12609826.value: Evidence suggests that large reasoning models (LRMs)—AI systems trained to reason—lack robust critical thinking abilities. They produce persuasive chains of thought not faithful to underlying inference, perform inconsistent reasoning, fail to use explicit procedures, overthink with missing premises, and exhibit motivated reasoning fallacies. If AI systems cannot reason critically and logically, the future risks intellectual contamination: confident synthetic text without substance. We will test whether today’s LRMs, which may sound convincing, can truly reason critically and creatively. Our logic-first project asks three questions: Do LRMs follow valid steps from premises to conclusions and handle tricky cases correctly? Can they keep explanations consistent, checkable, and backed by real evidence? Are they capable of abductive reasoning—proposing a plausible hypothesis for a surprising observation and outlining what to check next? We focus on separating faithful reasoning from anthropomorphic tone, ensuring that evaluations reward warranted inference rather than polished rhetoric. We will develop: (A) clear, testable standards for good reasoning—validity, correct use of conditionals and modality, transparency of warrants (why a claim follows), and creative hypothesis making with a concrete inquiry plan; (B) a task suite that separates substance from style by testing LRMs under tone-neutral prompts; (C) faithfulness audits that track each step in a chain of thought, verify outputs, and compile a failure atlas explaining where and why LRMs go wrong (e.g., fallacies or untestable storylines); and (D) “deliberation as inquiry” scaffolds—lightweight prompts requiring a hypothesis, reasons, and a testable next step—to determine whether structure improves reasoning quality beyond mere fluency. Audits will flag missing premises, non sequitur steps, and fabricated tool-traces with scoring protocols. The project will contribute: (1) philosophy and logic benefits—a rigorous account of what should count as reasoning in modern LRMs; (2) education benefits—open exercises, fallacy labs, and rubrics that help value process, verification, and originality; (3) policy and procurement benefits—simple checklists and open benchmarks that distinguish reliable reasoning from polished rhetoric; and (4) dissemination—three peer reviewed open access journal articles, an open repository with tests, scoring scripts, and an educator kit, plus a workshop to support adoption of findings and policy recommendations. We will engage academic, policy, and education communities through active dissemination and outreach. All releases will be open access, and negative results will be documented to build trust and reproducibility. 證據表明，大型推理模型（LRMs）— 即經過訓練進行推理的人工智慧系統—缺乏穩健的批判性思考能力。它們會產生看似有說服力的思維鏈，但這些思維鏈並不忠實於其背後的推論；它們的推論前後矛盾；它們未能使用明確的程序；它們會在缺少前提的情況下過度思考；它們還會犯動機性推理謬誤。如果人工智能系統無法進行批判性和邏輯性推理，未來將面臨知識污染的風險：充斥著缺乏實質內容的自信合成文本。 我們將測試如今那些聽起來頗具說服力的大型推理模型（LRMs）是否真的能夠進行批判性和創造性推理。我們這個以邏輯為先的項目提出了三個問題：大型推理模型（LRMs）是否能遵循有效推理步驟（從前提推論到結論），並正確處理棘手的情況？它們能否保持解釋的一致性、可驗證性，並有真實證據支持？它們是否能夠進行溯因推理（abductive reasoning）—即針對令人驚訝的觀察結果提出合理的假設，並概述下一步需要驗證的內容？ 我們致力於將忠實的推理與擬人化的語氣區分開來，確保評估獎勵的是合理的推論，而不是華麗的辭藻。我們將發展：(A) 清晰、可驗證的良好推理標準－包括有效性、條件句和模態詞的正確使用、論證依據的透明度（即某個論點為何成立），以及提出配以具體的探究計劃的創造性假設；(B) 建立一套通過在語氣中立的提示詞去測試大型推理模型（LRMs）的任務組合，藉此區分實質內容同表達風格；(C)忠實度審核，追蹤思維鏈中的每一步，驗證輸出結果，並編制一份失敗案例圖譜，解釋大型推理模型何處及因何出錯（例如，謬誤或無法驗證的故事情節）；以及 (D) 建立“探究式審議”（ deliberation as inquiry）框架—使用輕量級提示，要求提出假設、給出理由並提出可驗證的下一步—以確定結構是否能提升推理質素。審核將標記缺少的前提、不合邏輯的步驟以及捏造的工具痕跡，並制定評分協議。 本計畫將作出以下貢獻：(1) 哲學和邏輯－提供一套嚴謹的闡述，界定現代大型推理模型（LRMs）中，甚麼才是真正的推理； （2）教育－提供開放練習、謬誤實驗室和評分標準，有助於提高對過程、驗證和原創性的重視；（3）政策和選用－提供簡明清單和公開基準，有助於區分可靠的推理和華麗的辭藻；（4）傳播－發表三篇同儕審查的開放取用期刊文章，一個包含測驗、評分腳本和教師資源包的開放資源庫，並舉辦一場工作坊，推動研究成果同政策建議得以落實。我們將透過積極的傳播和推廣，與學術界、政策界和教育界進行互動。所有發佈內容都將開放取用，並且會記錄所有負面結果，以建立信任和可重複性。

12609926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12609926.value: 提升抗壓韌性：為香港大學生設計『壓力優化心態』訓練及其效果研究

12609926.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12609926.value: Dr HUANG, Yi Prof Jamieson, Jeremy Dr ZHEN, Shanshan

12609926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12609926.value: Academic stress is a pervasive issue in Hong Kong’s competitive educational landscape, with over 40% of university students reporting moderate-to-severe depression and anxiety, directly impairing academic functioning. While traditional interventions focus on stress reduction, contemporary theories suggest that stress can be a pathway for enhanced performance and growth. Our approach is grounded in the synergistic mindset model, which integrates two powerful psychological frameworks: a growth mindset, which reframes challenges as opportunities for development, and a stress-can-be-enhancing mindset, which reinterprets physiological arousal to stress as a source of energy. While effective in Western contexts, a direct application faces limitations due to cultural differences, the transient nature of single-session interventions, and an unclear understanding of its underlying mechanisms. To address these gaps, this project aims to firstly, culturally adapt and deliver a multi-session synergistic mindset intervention. We will reframe the intervention to align with collectivist values, positioning the growth mindset not only as a tool for personal improvement but also a modern embodiment of the Confucian ideal of self-cultivation. We will also conceptualize the stress-enhancing mindset using culturally congruent concepts, portraying the physiological sensations of academic pressure as a state of being inspired and energized. Additionally, the multi-session format will reinforce the mindset over time, embedding it as a habitual response to real-world academic stressors. We will adopt a 3-arm randomized controlled trial with pre-, post-, and 6-months follow-up assessments to examine the effectiveness of the intervention. The primary outcomes include academic achievement, stress mindset, and cognitive stress appraisal, the last of which will be measured via physiological responses (heart rate and skin conductance). Secondly, we will identify key moderators to understand for whom the intervention works best. We will investigate baseline stress levels, socioeconomic factors, and culturally-specific thinking styles to quantify heterogeneity in treatment effects. Thirdly, using fMRI combined with a stress-inducing task, we will uncover the underlying mechanistic evidence for how the intervention works. It allows us to identify the specific neural pathways of change, which is critical for optimizing the intervention’s core components and predicting for whom it will be most effective, thereby enhancing its future application and personalization. By employing a Randomized Controlled Trial combined with physiological and neural measures, this research will not only provide a validated tool for promoting student well-being and academic resilience but will also yield important insights into the brain mechanisms that facilitate stress optimization. 學業壓力喺香港高度競爭嘅教育環境入面，係一個相當普遍問題。超過四成大專生表示有中等至嚴重程度嘅抑鬱同焦慮徵狀，直接影響佢哋嘅學業表現。傳統嘅干預方法多數集中喺減壓，但當代心理學理論就提出，壓力其實可以成為提升表現同促進個人成長嘅途徑。本研究計劃提出一套切合本地文化脈絡嘅干預方案，目標係幫助香港大專生掌握有效應對壓力嘅技巧。方法建基於「協同心態模型」（synergistic mindset model），模型結合咗兩個好有影響力嘅心理學框架：第一個「成長心態」（growth mindset），強調將挑戰重新理解為發展嘅機會；第二個「壓力可增強表現心態」（stress-can-be-enhancing mindset），將面對壓力時嘅生理反應重新詮釋為能量嘅來源。雖然呢個模型喺西方語境下證實有效，但直接套用喺香港會面對限制，包括文化差異、單次介入嘅效果難以持久，以及對其背後機制嘅了解仍然不足。 本項目將「協同心態」介入方案進行文化調適，並以多節課程形式推行。將「成長心態」唔單止詮釋為個人進步嘅工具，同時亦視之為儒家「修養自身」呢個傳統理念嘅現代體現。用本地文化認同嘅概念嚟解釋「壓力增強心態」，將學業壓力所引起嘅生理反應（例如心跳加速）描述為一種「靈感湧現」同「精力充沛」嘅狀態。此外，多節課程嘅設計可以隨時間鞏固參與者嘅心態轉變，令佢哋能夠將新嘅思維模式內化為應對真實學業壓力嘅慣性反應。項目採用三臂隨機對照試驗，並設有前測、後測同六個月追蹤評估，以檢視介入方案嘅成效。主要嘅結果指標包括：學業成績、壓力心態轉變，以及認知壓力評估（後者會透過心率同皮膚電導等生理反應嚟量度）。項目識別關鍵嘅調節變項，以了解呢套介入方案對邊類參與者最有效。具體會探討基線壓力水平、社經因素，以及具文化特殊性嘅思考模式，從而量化治療效果嘅異質性。項目揭示介入方案背後嘅神經認知機制。透過功能性磁共振成像（fMRI）結合壓力誘發任務，我哋會驗證介入方案能夠重構大腦網絡。透過結合隨機對照試驗、生理測量同神經影像技術，本研究唔單止會提供一套經實證驗證嘅工具，用於促進學生身心健康同學業抗壓韌性，同時亦會為「壓力優化」背後嘅大腦機制提供重要嘅新見解。

12610126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12610126.value: 以風險資訊尋求與處理（RISP）模型探討癌症資訊的取得與處理機制

12610126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12610126.value: Prof Griffin , Robert J. Mr ZHU, Yuanxing

12610126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12610126.value: The project is in communication studies’ subfield: health communication. To explain cancer information acquisition and processing behavior, our project adopts a social scientific, etic approach and uses the Risk Information Seeking and Processing (RISP) model as the theoretical framework to conduct surveys with the general public and individuals with cancer experience. To deepen understanding, we also conduct in-depth interviews with both groups to triangulate the survey results. Cancer is a leading cause of death worldwide including Hong Kong. To address this rising cancer burden, Hong Kong’s government formulated the “Hong Kong Cancer Strategy 2019.” One key strategy is to effectively disseminate cancer messages through an approach consistent with the paradigm of people as consumers of information and as active participants in the health decision-making process. However, cancer communicators face the challenges of how to design audience-centered interventions to effectively address different target audience groups’ information needs. Crucial to addressing the challenges is the understanding of how people acquire and process cancer information. People can acquire information through two modes: information seeking (volitionally attend messages from selected communication channels for reaching a desired informational goal) and information scanning (spontaneously obtain information of interest). People can process cancer information also through two modes: systematic processing (more cognitively energetic) and heuristic processing (superficial and less effortful). More or less effort in acquiring and processing information can lead to varying degrees of health behavior engagement. The literature on cancer information acquisition and processing has several weaknesses: (1) lack of theory-driven studies, (2) little research compares the differences of information acquisition and processing behavior across different target audience groups, (3) virtually no research to examine information processing behavior in the cancer domain, (4) lack of a theory-driven audience segmentation tool to design more tailored intervention messaging, and (5) variation in prevention and control behaviors across acquisition and processing modes remains unexplored. Our proposal addresses these research gaps by conducting two surveys and two in-depth interviews—with the general public and individuals with cancer experience. We aim to identify factors influencing modes of cancer information acquisition and processing, and to compare prevention and control behaviors across these modes. This project will not only advance the RISP model by examining its capacity as an audience segmentation tool, but it will also guide cancer communicators to design audience-centered informational campaign to motivate people to acquire and process cancer information. 本研究了解釋癌症資訊的獲取與處理行為，本研究採取社會科學的「外部觀點」（etic approach），並以風險資訊尋求與處理模型（Risk Information Seeking and Processing, RISP）作為理論架構，針對一般民眾及具有癌症經驗者進行問卷調查。此外，為深化研究理解並驗證問卷調查結果，本研究亦對上述兩類受訪者進行深度訪談，以達成資料三角驗證（triangulation）。 癌症是全球各地（包括香港）主要的死亡原因之一。為因應日益沉重的癌症負擔，香港政府制定了《香港癌症策略（Hong Kong Cancer Strategy 2019）》。其中一項核心策略是透過符合「民眾作為資訊消費者，並積極參與健康決策過程」理念的方式，有效傳播癌症相關訊息。然而，癌症傳播工作者面臨的重要挑戰在於：如何設計以受眾為中心的介入措施（audience-centered interventions），以有效回應不同目標群體的資訊需求。而要解決此一挑戰，關鍵在於理解人們如何獲取與處理癌症資訊。 人們主要透過兩種方式獲取資訊：資訊尋求（information seeking）與資訊掃描（information scanning）。資訊尋求是指個體基於特定資訊目標，有意識地透過選擇特定傳播管道來接收資訊；資訊掃描則指個體在非刻意搜尋的情況下，自發性地接觸並獲得感興趣的資訊。同樣地，人們處理癌症資訊也可區分為兩種模式：系統性處理（systematic processing）與捷思式處理（heuristic processing）。前者需要投入較多認知資源與思考努力；後者則較為表層且所需認知投入較少。不同程度的資訊獲取與處理投入，可能進一步影響個體參與健康行為的程度。 現有關於癌症資訊獲取與處理的文獻仍存在若干不足之處：（1）缺乏理論驅動的研究；（2）鮮少研究比較不同目標群體在資訊獲取與處理行為上的差異；（3）幾乎沒有研究專門探討癌症領域中的資訊處理行為；（4）缺乏以理論為基礎的受眾區隔工具，以利設計更具針對性的介入訊息；以及（5）不同資訊獲取與處理模式下，癌症預防與控制行為的差異仍未受到充分探討。 為彌補上述研究缺口，本研究計畫將針對一般民眾及具有癌症經驗者，分別進行兩項問卷調查與兩項深度訪談。我們旨在找出影響癌症資訊獲取與處理模式的因素，並比較不同模式下癌症預防與控制行為的差異。本研究不僅將透過檢驗RISP模型作為受眾區隔工具的潛力，進一步拓展該模型的理論發展，同時亦能為癌症傳播實務提供依據，協助傳播工作者設計以受眾為中心的資訊宣導活動，促使民眾更積極地獲取與處理癌症相關資訊。

12611226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12611226.value: 透過社區翻譯賦能香港的少數語言和少數族裔群體：一項實踐社群框架下的研究

12611226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12611226.value: Dr Bartindale, Tom Dr Neather, Robert John

12611226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12611226.value: This project examines community translation in and for Hong Kong’s South Asian (SA) communities, particularly those whose participation in society is hindered by a lack of proficiency in Chinese and/or English, the city’s official languages. Community translation is important for debates around social inclusion, the relationship between language and identity, and the impact of technology on communication involving minority languages. Research on community translation has hitherto comprised largely product-oriented studies focusing on its social function, power asymmetries between public service providers and minority language speakers, and the modalities of community translation. Translation policies have also gained scholarly attention. However, several issues remain unexamined. These include: the process of community translation as a collaborative act, the ways in which identity is manifested through participant interactions, the power dynamics between majority and minority languages and their speakers, and the meaning of community translation as a practice and a concept. These issues have been particularly under-researched in Hong Kong, not least because multilingualism and multiculturalism are generally less visible than in societies where immigration is more high-profile. This project approaches these issues by focusing on community translation undertaken collaboratively by different stakeholders, including SA communities, a partner NGO, professional minority language translators, and trainee translators. Employing an ethnographic action research methodology, the project investigates community translation from three dimensions – its definition, the collaborative process, and the identity of the participants. It also examines how SA participants’ self-perceptions can be leveraged to develop more effective and inclusive minority language provision. The project will firstly evaluate the needs of SA populations by reflecting on experiences and findings from previous collaborations and discussing with stakeholders. This will inform the subsequent design of translation and research workshops involving human-to-human and human-computer interaction, implemented with the partner NGO and focusing on two key domains: education and healthcare. Thematic analysis, combined with sociolinguistically informed narrative analysis, will be applied to examine the data collected from ethnographic observations, interviews, focus group discussions, written reflections, workshop materials and translated products. ‘Communities of practice’ theory will be applied in interpreting the data. The findings will be communicated through scholarly publications, the project website, and a policy report written jointly with our partner organisation. This project will significantly contribute to expanding existing conceptualisations of community translation and produce a ‘communities of practice’ theoretical framework for studying translation in and for linguistic minority contexts. 香港的官方語言為中文和英文。缺乏對此兩種語言的掌握難免會影響參與各類社會活動。本項目研究社區翻譯，特別關注那些不會中英文的南亞裔背景的少數族裔群體。社區翻譯對許多社會議題的討論都至關重要。這些議題包括：社會包容、語言與身份的關係和科技對使用少數語言來交流的影響。 以往關於社區翻譯的研究主要以翻譯出來的成品為導向，關注其社會功能、公共服務提供者與少數語言使用者之間的權力不對等，以及社區翻譯的模式。翻譯政策也已引起學術界的關注。然而，仍有一些問題尚待深入探討。這些問題包括：社區翻譯作為一種協作行為的過程、身份如何透過參與者的互動得以體現、主流語言和少數語言及其使用者之間的權力動態，以及社區翻譯作為一種實踐和概念的意義。在香港，這些問題的研究尤其不足，這在很大程度上是因為與移民問題更為突出的社會相比，多語言和多元文化在香港缺少關註。 本研究著重探討由不同持份者共同進行的社區翻譯工作。他們包括南亞裔社群、與項目合作的非政府組織、少數語言翻譯人員和實習譯員。本研究採用民族誌行動研究方法，從三個維度——社區翻譯的定義、合作過程和參與者的身份——來研究社區翻譯。此外，本計畫也會探討如何利用南亞裔參與者的自我認識來發展更有效、更具包容性的少數語言服務。本研究首先回顧以往合作的經驗和成果，與持份者討論並評估南亞裔群體的需求。這些經驗總結為後續翻譯和研究工作坊的設計提供基礎。工作坊會與非政府組織共同設計和教授。工作坊的活動涉及人際互動和人機交互，並聚焦教育和醫療保健兩個關鍵領域。研究過程搜集到的資料包括對從民族誌觀察、訪談、焦點小組討論、書面反思、工作坊材料和翻譯成品。這些資料的分析主要採用主題分析法，同時結合社會語言學視角下的敘事分析法。理論方面，我們會運用「實踐社群」理論來解讀分析結果。研究成果會以學術出版物、項目網站，以及與合作機構共同撰寫的政策報告形式出現與傳播。 本研究會顯著拓展現有關於社區翻譯的概念，並建構一個「實踐社群」理論框架，用於研究語言少數群體脈絡下的翻譯工作。

12611926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12611926.value: 城市之間的書寫：香港及大灣區非場所、閾限空間、消失與短暫性的文學探索

12611926.label: Principal Investigator(Chinese)
12611926.value: 帕特里克·戈登·霍蘭教授

12611926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12611926.value: This practice-led research project explores how creative writing might respond to the loss of traditional, anthropological place in the age of supermodernity, when discrete place, and the communitas and identities it generates, has traditionally been the chief driver of story. Hong Kong will be taken as primary focus, as a paradigmatic supermodern city characterizable by proliferating non-places (such as airports, chain hotels and motorways) per Marc Augé’s (2008) designation, characterizable, too, by transience and dis-appearance (due to mobile residents) per the writing of Akbar Abbas (1996). Patrick Shanahan refers to the environs observed by Augé and Abbas—where we never feel estranged, yet never at home—as the ‘post-landscape’; Manuel Castells (1997) adds that a constellation of sleepless nodes he calls the “global capitalist space of flows” has usurped the space of places and traditional cities. The project, then, extends to the post-landscapes of Greater Bay Area—especially to Shenzhen and Macau—to examine how these nodes of global transit communicate and what representational strategies are demanded for sympathetic depiction and understanding of both the built environments and the people who reside in and transit through them. So the project asks: What formal, aesthetic, and stylistic literary strategies might sympathetically depict the supermodern post-landscapes of Hong Kong and Greater Bay Area cities (Shenzhen, Macau), and how might these depictions reveal insights into residents’ reclamation of belonging, identity, telos, and sacred connections in transient urban environments? To address this question, the project adopts a mixed-method approach, developing Narrative-led Spatial Inquiry (NSI), a bespoke adaptation of practice-led research, where interpretive phenomenology and embodied, in situ writing are complemented by iterative storytelling. Combined with stylistic analysis of Greater Bay Area post-landscapes and phenomenological fieldwork, NSI aims to reveal new representational strategies (aesthetic, stylistic, formal), new modes of belonging, and cultural meaning—even the potential re-discovery of sacrality—in apparently banal, cultureless spaces. The findings will be disseminated through two critical papers and an edited volume (Writing Non-places, Bloomsbury/UWA Press) on non-places and transient spaces, and the novel One Thousand & One Nights in Hong Kong. These will inform the PI’s teaching at HKBU, workshops at the Australian International School of Hong Kong, and public talks at such as the Hong Kong International Writers Festival and Brisbane Writers Festival.

12613026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12613026.value: 短影音如何以及在何時影響香港青少年的福祉？一項三波次縱貫研究

12613026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12613026.value: The dominance of short-form video has raised urgent concerns for adolescent well-being, primarily through the rise of “mindless scrolling”—a passive, habitual form of consumption linked to negative mental health outcomes. Adolescents are uniquely vulnerable to this behavior due to neurodevelopmental factors that make them highly susceptible to the platforms’ immersive, reward-driven designs, which can lead to fragmented attention, guilt, and a decline in psychological health. Despite these mounting concerns, a clear understanding of the specific mechanisms through which short video use impacts adolescent well-being remains lacking. Current research is limited by two critical shortcomings: a conceptual gap, where an over-reliance on addiction models pathologizes common behaviors and overlooks both mundane harms and protective behaviors; and a methodological gap, where a lack of longitudinal, within-person studies prevents an understanding of the dynamic, reciprocal, and person-specific effects of short-video use. Drawing on the Differential Susceptibility to Media Effects Model (DSMM) and the Integrative Model of Mobile Media Use and Need Experiences (IM3UNE), this project will provide a more precise, nuanced understanding of how, when, and for whom short-video consumption impacts adolescents in Hong Kong. Specifically, the study will identify key differential-susceptibility variables (trait self-control, habit strength, affiliative tendency) that predict mindless and procrastinatory short-video watching behaviors. It will also investigate potential reciprocal relationships between mindless and procrastinatory short-video use and adolescent well-being overtime. It will further examine the mediating role of media-induced recovery experience and digital harms (distraction, fatigue, time wasting) in this process, while also investigate whether sense of coherence moderate these effects to explain why some adolescents are more vulnerable than others. To achieve these aims, the project will employ a three-wave longitudinal panel design, surveying a sample of adolescents recruited from secondary schools in Hong Kong using a cluster sampling. Findings will clarify the heterogeneous, person-specific, and dynamic effects of short-form video, informing the development of targeted, evidence-based interventions that move beyond blanket bans. Ultimately, this research aims to empower adolescents, parents, and educators with the nuanced knowledge needed to foster healthier digital habits and support adolescent well-being in an increasingly saturated media environment. 短影音的主導地位已對青少年的福祉引發迫切關注，主要原因在於「無意識滑動手機」的興起: 一種被動、習慣性的內容消費形式，並與負面的心理健康結果相關。由於神經發展上的因素，青少年對這種行為尤其脆弱；這些因素使他們更容易受到平台沉浸式、以獎賞為導向的設計所影響，進而導致注意力碎片化、內疚感，以及心理健康下降。儘管這些疑慮日益增加，目前對於短影音使用如何影響青少年福祉的具體機制，仍缺乏清晰理解。現有研究受到兩項關鍵不足所限制：其一是概念上的缺口，即過度依賴成癮模型將常見行為病理化，卻忽略了日常性的傷害與保護性行為；其二是方法上的缺口，即缺乏縱貫性、個體內研究，使得我們無法理解短影音使用的動態、互惠與個人化效應。 本研究將結合媒體效果差異易感性模型（Differential Susceptibility to Media Effects Model）與行動媒體使用與需求體驗整合模型（Integrative Model of Mobile Media Use and Need Experiences），以更精確的方式理解短影音消費如何、在何時、以及對哪些香港青少年產生影響。具體而言，本研究將辨識關鍵的差異易感性變項（特質自我控制、習慣強度、親和傾向），以預測無意識與拖延式的短影音觀看行為。研究亦將檢驗無意識與拖延式短影音使用與青少年福祉之間隨時間可能存在的互惠關係。此外，本研究將進一步探討媒介引發的恢復經驗與數位傷害在此過程中的中介作用，同時也將檢驗條理感是否會調節這些效果，以解釋為何有些青少年比其他人更脆弱。 為達成上述目標，本研究將採用三波次縱貫性追蹤設計，並在香港中學招募青少年樣本進行調查。研究結果將有助於釐清短影音的異質性、個人化與動態效應，並為發展針對性的、以證據為基礎的介入措施提供依據，使相關策略能超越一刀切的禁止方式。本研究旨在賦能青少年、家長與教育工作者，使其具備更細緻的知識，從而在媒體環境中培養更健康的數位習慣，並支持青少年的福祉。

12613126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12613126.value: 立足邊緣，跨越疆界：戰後香港粵語社會寫實片與庶民都市喜劇中既存音樂的跨地域運用，1953–1968

12613126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12613126.value: This project explores the translocal use of preexisting music in postwar Hong Kong Cantonese films from 1953 to 1968, focusing on two contrasting genres: social realist dramas and populist urban comedies. Cantonese films were central to Hong Kong’s popular culture, often surpassing Mandarin and Hollywood productions in local popularity. While the filmmakers often worked under tight budgets and relied heavily on borrowed music, these soundtracks played a key role in storytelling, shaping emotions, and reflecting Hong Kong’s unique translocal cultural identity. Our study challenges the common dismissal of preexisting music as cheap filler or ‘canned music.’ Instead, we position it as a site of translocal creative production. Borrowed music was not simply a cost-saving measure but a dynamic, artistic element shaped by the interplay of political ideologies, market forces, and the visions of directors and music editors. These forces combined uniquely in Hong Kong cinema to create mixed soundscapes that integrated Hollywood scoring techniques with diverse musical traditions including classical, jazz, Latin, pop, and rock. The study uses a purposively selected sample of 30 films—16 social realist dramas from the left-wing Zhong Lian studio and 14 populist urban comedies starring Sun Ma Sze Tsang—to ground our analysis in concrete cases. Building on this foundation, the research articulates two interrelated theoretical advances: first, distinct translocal mix variants—patterns of how borrowed music is selected, adapted, and integrated across genres; and second, the conditions under which these variants arise—political ideologies, market dynamics, directorial visions, and the networks of music editors. Methodologically, our approach combines detailed film-by-film coding of musical cues, close textual analysis, and archival research. The resulting insights connect genre-specific musical practices to broader political and economic contexts, offering a theoretical framework for Cantonese film history built on the overlooked ingenuity embedded in preexisting film music during a pivotal era. It also has broader impact, encouraging re-evaluation of peripheral cultural forms and enriching transnational perspectives on creative production in postwar Asian cinemas. The project will generate open-access outputs, scholarly articles, and public-facing material that illuminate the creative genius hidden at the margins of Cantonese cinema. 本研究探討戰後香港粵語電影在1953至1968年間如何借用不同地域的既存音樂作配樂，並以社會寫實片與庶民都市喜劇作為主要研究片種。戰後粵語片是香港流行文化的重要一環，往往比國語片和荷里活電影更受本地觀眾歡迎。當時粵語片製作資源有限，不少電影大量採用既存音樂，但這些「借來」的音樂並不只是出於製作成本的考慮；它們同時推動敘事、營造情感，並共同構成戰後香港複雜而獨特的跨地域文化面貌。簡言之，本研究希望打破過往將既存音樂視為廉價「罐頭音樂」的看法，並把既存音樂的運用視為一種重要的跨地域創作實踐。電影工作者選取甚麼音樂、如何剪接、重組和配合畫面，除了受製作成本影響，也受到政治立場、市場考慮，以及導演和配樂人員的創作取向影響。這些因素在粵語片製作過程中互相影響，形成複雜而多元的配樂面貌：粵語片一方面借鑑荷里活的配樂手法，另一方面又把古典音樂、爵士樂、拉丁音樂、流行歌曲和搖滾樂等不同音樂傳統廣泛用作配樂素材。 研究將選取30部電影作深入分析，當中包括16部左翼中聯影業公司的社會寫實片，以及14部由新馬師曾主演的庶民都市喜劇。透過這兩組性質不同、但同樣大量運用既存音樂的作品，研究將考察不同類型的電影如何選取、改造和組合來自不同地方的音樂，並歸納其配樂中不同的「跨地域混合模式」。研究亦將探討這些差異如何形成，包括政治意識形態、市場環境、導演以及配樂人員的創作取向，如何影響既存音樂的選擇和運用。 研究方法包括逐片記錄和分析音樂段落、細讀電影文本，以及檔案研究。本研究旨在從具體的配樂方式出發，了解不同片種的音樂運用如何與當時更廣泛的政治和經濟環境互相連繫，並重新發掘既存電影音樂中長期被忽略的創意，從而為理解戰後粵語電影提供新的角度。 本研究的意義亦不限於香港電影史：它引導我們重新評價長期處於文化邊緣的創作形式，並從跨國角度重新認識戰後亞洲電影中其他被忽略的創意實踐。本計畫除發表學術論文外，亦會以開放取用及面向公眾的方式分享研究成果。

12613226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12613226.value: 利用大型語言模型評估客觀與感知的醫療服務可達性及環境暴露的不平等

12613226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12613226.value: Dr Guan, Xiaodong Dr Ou, Yifu

12613226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12613226.value: Since the United Nations introduced Sustainable Development Goal 3, "Good Health and Well‑being," a growing body of urban research has focused on improving healthcare accessibility to reduce public health risks. However, better access to healthcare does not automatically lead to better health outcomes. Areas with strong healthcare access can also suffer from environmental degradation: residents in urban centers may enjoy convenient medical services while facing higher air pollution and intensified urban heat island effects. Objective measures of healthcare accessibility and environmental exposure often diverge from people’s own perceptions, and those perceived measures—shaped by individual experience and judgment—can have a stronger influence on health behaviors and outcomes. Research that systematically quantifies gaps between objective and perceived indicators remains limited, largely because of data and methodological challenges in capturing subjective experience at scale. Moreover, spatial and social inequities can undermine potential public‑health gains. Because populations are unevenly distributed across cities, socially vulnerable groups are more likely to face both limited access to healthcare and greater exposure to environmental hazards, compounding health risks. To address these gaps, this project will: (1) identify spatiotemporal (mis)matches between objective measures of healthcare accessibility and environmental exposure; (2) develop a large language model–based approach to measure perceived accessibility and exposure and compare perceived and objective metrics; and (3) evaluate spatiotemporal and sociodemographic inequalities in the convergence or divergence between accessibility and exposure. Shenzhen is selected as the case study due to its diverse socioeconomic composition, the availability of detailed healthcare, environmental exposure, and population data, and its pronounced spatiotemporal variation in health risks. We will collect multisource data, including remote-sensing imagery, population datasets, points of interest (POIs), multimodal travel times, and healthcare capacity information. Objective healthcare accessibility and environmental exposure will be assessed using the Gaussian two-step floating catchment area (Ga2SFCA) method and resampling techniques, which better capture supply–demand dynamics in medical service allocation and reflect patients’ search behavior than conventional accessibility measures. This research offers two main contributions. Academically, it advances the urban health and social equity literature by uncovering spatiotemporal and sociodemographic inequalities in healthcare accessibility and environmental exposure using both objective and perceived metrics, and it is among the first to leverage large language models to analyze perceived accessibility and exposure. Practically, it provides actionable guidance for creating socially inclusive, healthier cities, shaping urban planning and public health policy. 自聯合國提出永續發展目標3「良好健康與福祉」以來，越來越多的城市研究致力於透過提升醫療服務可達性來降低公共衛生風險。然而，更好的醫療可達性並不必然帶來更好的健康結果。醫療可達性較強的地區同樣可能遭受環境退化：城市中心的居民或許享有便利的醫療服務，但同時面臨更高的空氣污染和更強烈的城市熱島效應。關於醫療可達性與環境暴露的客觀測量常常與人們的主觀感知存在偏差，而這些由個體經驗與判斷塑造的感知指標，往往對健康行為和結果產生更強的影響。系統量化客觀指標與感知指標之間差距的研究仍然有限，主要原因在於在大尺度上捕捉主觀體驗面臨數據與方法上的挑戰。此外，空間與社會不平等可能會削弱潛在的公共衛生利益。由於城市人口分佈不均，社會脆弱群體更可能同時面臨醫療服務取得受限與更高的環境危害暴露，從而疊加健康風險。 為彌補這些差距，本計畫將：（1）識別醫療服務可達性與環境暴露客觀指標之間的時空匹配與不匹配；（2）構建基於大型語言模型的方法來度量感知的可達性與暴露，並對比感知與客觀學不平等指標；（3）評估在可達性與暴露的收斂或背離方面的時空與社會人口學不平等指標。之所以選擇深圳作為個案研究對象，是因為其社會經濟結構多樣，具備詳實的醫療、環境暴露與人口數據可獲得性，且其健康風險在時間與空間上呈現出顯著的變異。我們將收集多源數據，包括遙感影像、人口數據集、興趣點（POI）、多交通方式旅行時間以及醫療服務能力資訊。將採用高斯加權兩步驟浮動捕捉區法（Ga2SFCA）和重採樣技術評估醫療服務可及性與環境暴露的客觀指標，這些方法相較於傳統可達性度量，更能刻畫醫療服務配置中的供需動態，並反映患者的搜尋行為。 本研究主要有兩方面貢獻。學術上，它透過同時採用客觀與感知指標，揭示醫療服務可達性與環境暴露在時空與社會人口學維度上的不平等，推進了城市健康與社會公平領域的研究，並且是率先利用大型語言模型分析感知可達性與暴露的研究之一。實踐上，它為建立一個更包容與健康的城市提供了可操作的指導，幫助塑造城市規劃與公共衛生政策。

12613626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12613626.value: 中國內地與香港文學與電影中的動物再現（20世紀80年代至今）：擬人化與人類世

12613626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12613626.value: This research explores how nonhuman animals are represented in literature and cinema from the 1980s to the present in mainland China and Hong Kong. Drawing on the emerging animal studies and environmental humanities, the project investigates how these representations shape—and are shaped by—human understandings of ecological issues mediated by human-animal relationships in rapidly modernizing societies. As modernization displaced animals from everyday life, their symbolic and material significance underwent a shift. Yet, in China, literary and cinematic portrayals of animals have persisted, reflecting complex societal transformations that extend beyond the Western context. From the resource exploitation of the 1980s to the ecological conservation campaigns of the 2010s, Chinese writers and filmmakers have used animals to allegorize social change, critique industrialization and bureaucracy, and explore human-animal relationships to rethink humanity. These narratives are especially prominent in works by ethnic minorities and rural communities, where human-animal bonds continue to hold cultural significance. In (post)colonial Hong Kong, animals serve more as metaphors for urban alienation, political resistance, and hybrid identities, though animal welfare also matters in some works. Representation, in this context, is not merely about depicting animals but about speaking for and to them—making animals matter in cultural discourse and matter to animals themselves. This project, by examining selected texts and films, seeks to discover new conceptual paradigms and imaginings of the human-animal relationship. By engaging with animals as active subjects rather than passive symbols, Chinese writers and filmmakers challenge anthropocentric worldviews and reimagine the complex connections between species. This project argues that anthropomorphism, often dismissed as unscientific, can be a vital tool for bridging human and nonhuman experiences. Rather than reinforcing human dominance, anthropomorphic representations may reveal affinities and shared vulnerabilities, particularly in an era of uncertainty brought forth by geopolitical tensions, climate crisis, and ecological collapse. Ultimately, this study contributes to environmental humanities by examining how Chinese and Hong Kong cultural producers envision a more-than-human world—one where animals are not just symbols but co-participants and co-agents in shaping ecological and ethical futures. 本研究探討了自1980年代至今，中國内地和香港的文學和電影作品中非人類動物的形象呈現方式。此研究計畫借鑒了新興的動物研究和環境人文學科，考察了這些形像如何塑造——以及如何被塑造——人類對生態問題的理解，而這種理解又受到快速現代化社會中人與動物關係的影響。隨著現代化過程將動物從日常生活中剝離，它們的象徵和物質意義也隨之轉變了。然而，在中國，文學和電影中對動物的描繪依然存在，反映了超越西方脈絡的複雜社會轉型。從1980年代的資源開發到21世紀頭十年的生態保護運動，中國作家和電影人一直運用動物來寓言社會變遷，批判工業化和官僚主義，並探索人與動物的關係，從而重新思考人性。這些敘事在少數族群和農村社區的作品中尤其突出，在這些地區，人與動物之間的連結仍然具有重要的文化意義。在（後）殖民時代的香港，動物更多地被用作城市疏離、政治抵抗和混合身份的隱喻，儘管在某些作品中，爭取動物福利也同樣重要。 在此脈絡下，表徵再現並非僅僅是描繪動物，而是為它們發聲，與它們對話──使動物在文化論述中以及對它們本身而言都具有意義。本研究計畫透過對特定文本和電影的分析，旨在探索人與動物關係的新概念範式和新想像。透過將動物視為積極的主體而非被動的符號，中國與香港作家和電影製作人挑戰了以人類為中心的視角，並重新構想了物種間錯綜複雜的聯繫。本研究計畫認為，擬人化──這種常被視為不科學的手段──可以成為連結人類與非人類經驗的重要工具。擬人化的表徵並非強化人類的支配地位，而是揭示了人與動物之間的親緣關係和共同的脆弱性，尤其是在地緣政治緊張局勢、氣候危機和生態崩潰帶來的不確定時代。 最終，這項研究透過檢視中國和香港的文化生產者如何構想一個超越人類的世界——在這個世界裡，動物不僅是符號，而且是塑造生態和倫理未來的共同參與者和共同行動者——為環境人文領域做出了貢獻。

12614226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12614226.value: 邊緣上的被重視：香港少數族裔數碼創意媒體實踐的文化研究

12614226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12614226.value: Prof Erni, John N Prof Fung, Anthony Ying-him

12614226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12614226.value: This proposed study aims to obtain an in-depth cultural understanding of how South and Southeast Asian ethnic minorities (EM) in Hong Kong utilize digital media for creative purposes and develop content strategies in a hybrid cultural context of Hong Kong. Although EM in Hong Kong are still marginalized from mainstream Chinese society in various aspects, the younger generation have become increasingly active on digital media. New means of digital creative practices have noticeably reshaped the nature, form, and structure of their cultural activities. The young generation of EM have spent their formative years to localize themselves in Hong Kong, and in the process witnessed and participated in the booming development of digital media. Are they becoming adept at utilizing multiple digital tools to create their own forms of mediated storytelling, in order to strive for social recognition? Theoretically, the project fills a research gap by articulating the notions of ‘marginality’ and ‘mattering’ as a critical lens of inquiry to guide the analysis of the EM's active digital practices. Originating in Education research, these interrelated concepts have been widely adopted in different minority studies. ‘Marginality’ is felt when an individual senses separation from others within the larger social system. When the need to matter is not fulfilled by the social environment, individuals may feel pushed to the margin of society and believe that they do not fit in. Meanwhile, ‘mattering’ reflects the relational process of developing one’s positive identity development and encompasses how individuals understand themselves vis-a-vis the others. Adopting a mixed methods approach, this study asks: 1) How do ethnic minorities in Hong Kong develop their sense of mattering through creative digital media use and content strategies despite, and because of, their marginality? 2) How does their participation in creative media help them overcome their social and linguistic limitations and strike alternative social and career pathways on the margin? 3) To what extent do their digital practices inspire their peers in their own search for robust self-understanding, social connectedness, and cultural belonging? The findings will provide important intercultural bearings for understanding the complex interplay among cultural alterity, creativity, active agency, and identity building. By doing so, it will generate a new direction for future societal discussion on the role played by savvy EM digital citizens in Hong Kong’s multicultural development. 本研究計畫旨在深入理解香港南亞及東南亞少數族裔如何在本地混融的文化脈絡中，運用數碼媒體進行創意表達並發展適合自身的內容策略。儘管香港的少數族裔在以華人為主流的社會中的多個層面仍被邊緣化，但其年輕一代在數碼媒體上愈見活躍。新興的數碼創意實踐已顯著重塑其文化活動的性質、形式與結構。少數族裔年輕一代在成長期努力實現自我本地化，並在此過程中見證且參與了數碼媒體的蓬勃發展。他們是否正日益嫻熟地運用多樣的數碼工具，創作屬於自己的媒介化敘事，從而爭取社會認可？ 在理論層面，本研究透過闡明「邊緣性」與「被重視感」兩個概念，以批判性探究視角指引對少數族裔的積極數碼實踐進行分析研究，從而補足相關研究缺口。這兩個相互關聯的概念源自教育研究，並已廣泛應用於不同少數群體研究之中。「邊緣性」指的是個體在更大的社會系統中感到與他人差異時的經驗。當「被重視的需要」未獲社會環境滿足時，個體可能覺得自己被推向社會邊緣，並認為難以融入。與此同時，「被重視感」體現的是一種關係性的歷程，有助於正向的身份發展，並涵蓋個體在與他者互動中如何理解自我。本研究採混合方法，提出以下問題：1）香港少數族裔如何透過具創意的數碼媒體運用與內容策略來建構自身的被重視感？2）他們參與創意媒體如何幫助他們克服社會與語言上的限制，並在邊緣處境中開闢替代性的社會與職涯路徑？3）他們的數碼實踐在多大程度上啟發其同儕，協助他們在追求更為扎實的自我理解、社會連結與文化歸屬感？ 研究發現將為理解文化他者性、創造力、主體能動性與身份建構之間的複雜互動，提供重要的跨文化參照與指引。由此，將為社會未來就精通數碼媒體實踐的少數族裔公民在香港多元文化發展中所扮演的角色展開討論，開拓新的方向。

12614626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12614626.value: 透過AI輔助簡易版能源審計計劃賦能主動型電力消費者

12614626.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12614626.value: Prof Chen, Yi-Ru Regina Dr Cheung, Darren Man-wai Prof LEUNG, Kwok Hi, Michael Prof Tai, Samson Prof Yun, Sun-Jin

12614626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12614626.value: The urgency of climate risks and energy insecurity heightens the importance of Hong Kong's 2050 carbon neutrality goal. Low-carbon technologies alone are insufficient for full decarbonisation. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers potential to scale energy-saving solutions, particularly in the hard-to-reach residential sector. In Hong Kong, while energy audits can address information gaps that hinder behavioural change, a major shortage of certified assessors makes large-scale audits costly and time-consuming. This raises critical questions: Can AI mainstream residential energy auditing to support Hong Kong’s 2050 target? Who, besides professionals, can AI empower to conduct audits effectively? How can Hong Kong leverage AI to deliver economic and environmental benefits while promoting digital inclusion? This interdisciplinary study aims to explore how a voluntary, AI-assisted simplified energy auditing (AI-SEA) programme can mainstream energy saving in the residential sector. Using a participatory mixed-methods approach, we will provide digital green-skill training to approximately 150 members from socially excluded and youth groups (including mentally disabled people, intellectually disadvantaged people, new immigrants, and ethnic minorities). Our trainees will conduct audits in 12 residential sites that represent diverse building and demographic features across Hong Kong. We will develop and test the effectiveness of our collaborative model of AI-assisted voluntary energy auditing, which can be replicated across sectors in Hong Kong. This study is novel in three key areas: First, it will test how integrating five AI methods (i.e. text analysis, object detection, thermal imaging, conversational AI, and natural language generation) can simplify energy audits, making them faster, cheaper, and more collaborative than traditional techno-centric approaches. Second, we will develop a three-stage capacity building and engagement programme that emphasises human inputs to improve the outcomes of AI methods. Thirdly, we will showcase how a voluntary, multi-sectoral collaborative initiative can align diverse interests, and ultimately enhance the government’s governing capacity. Our multiple case study across 12 residential sites will generate robust, new datasets, including real-time electricity profiles, building and occupant metadata, equipment inventories, quantitative survey data, and qualitative data from interviews, community dialogues, and a focus group. These datasets will provide a foundation for benchmarking residential energy performance, and enhancing policy developments. In collaboration with 4 organisational collaborators, a five-member multidisciplinary research team with expertise in AI, big data analytics, smart energy technologies, energy auditing, and science communication will deliver the project. Outputs include training handbooks, toolkits, workshops, focus group meeting, policy action plan, dashboard, and two journal articles. 這項為期兩年的跨學科比較研究，將涵蓋香港12個住宅社區、共150名住戶。本研究將AI輔助簡易版能源審計計劃(AI-assisted simplified energy auditing, AI-SEA) 重新建構為一項推動能源行為改變的社會實驗, 並於賦能培訓計劃中付諸實踐。150名住戶將參與兩階段的介入計劃，結合實踐（實際行動）與持續參與. 在第一階段, 這研究將整合運用五大AI方法(即: 文本分析、物件偵測、熱成像、對話式AI，以及自然語言生成等技術)，以測試運用的效果，包括簡化能源審計的流程、令能源審計更快、更便宜、以及更能促進各界合作。五大弱勢群體的150名住戶將伙拍年青人 接受培訓，並在五個城市進行共200個簡易版能源審計。 在第二階段，這些住戶將參與循序漸進的「審計後」工作坊，工作坊將善用遊戲化（如虛擬實境）、區塊鏈碳幣系統，以及協作式政策設計，從而建構全面的支援系統，支持在家中及社區內激勵並擴大節能行為。

12615326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12615326.value: 探索最優AI增強型同聲傳譯：工具定制化與認知個體差異的融合

12615326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12615326.value: High-quality real-time language services, such as simultaneous interpreting, are essential for effective global communication. While artificial intelligence (AI) has made impressive progress, it still struggles to match human interpreters, especially in situations where accuracy and cultural sensitivity are critical. Current AI interpreting systems often miss subtle cultural meanings or a speaker’s true intent, leading to serious misunderstandings. They also tend to produce longer delays than human interpreters, who typically maintain a brief lag of only a few seconds. Although human interpreters remain vital in high-stakes environments like diplomacy, law, and healthcare, there is growing interest in how advanced AI tools can support them effectively and reduce mental strain. This project aims to explore how different AI-assisted tools and interpreters’ individual skills, such as language proficiency, working memory, and stress levels, affect interpreting quality. The goal is to find the best combination of AI support that helps interpreters perform at their peak. To do this, the study will compare four types of AI tools against a no-tool baseline: live transcription, machine translation, keyword prompting, and an innovative multi-agent system developed by our team that allows interpreters to customize the type(s) of AI assistance they need. Thirty professional simultaneous interpreters from major organizations, including the United Nations and the Hong Kong government, will take part in realistic interpreting simulations to assess how humans and AI can work together most effectively. The study has three main objectives: first, to evaluate the overall effectiveness of each AI tool; second, to measure how these tools influence key aspects of interpreting—latency (speed), accuracy, and fluency; and third, to understand how an interpreter’s personal abilities and cognitive traits interact with these technologies. The findings will help interpreters choose and adapt AI tools that best fit their individual strengths, forming the basis for a new model of global competence in the language profession. This project matters because it will provide solid, research-based guidance to organizations around the world, helping improve communication accuracy in crucial settings like international hearings or courtrooms. It will also support interpreters’ well-being by reducing mental fatigue and the risk of burnout. Led by an experienced interpreter and psycholinguist who developed the customizable AI tool, our team has the expertise and proven methods needed to deliver meaningful insights into the future of human-AI collaboration in interpreting. 高品質的即時語言服務（如同聲傳譯）對促進有效的全球溝通至關重要。儘管人工智慧（AI）已取得顯著進展，其表現仍難以媲美人類口譯員，尤其是在高度重視準確性與文化敏感度的情境中。現有的 AI 口譯系統往往無法掌握細微的文化意涵或講者的真正意圖，因而可能造成嚴重誤解。此外，這些系統產生的延遲通常比人類口譯員更長；人類口譯員一般只會與講者保持數秒的短暫時間差。雖然人類口譯員在外交、法律及醫療等高風險場域中仍不可或缺，學界與業界亦日益關注如何運用先進的 AI 工具有效支援口譯員，並減輕其認知負荷。 本研究計畫旨在探討不同的 AI 輔助工具，以及口譯員的個人能力與特質（例如語言熟練度、工作記憶及壓力水平）如何影響口譯品質。研究目標是找出 AI 支援的最佳組合，協助口譯員發揮最佳表現。 為此，本研究將以不使用任何工具的情況作為基準，並比較四類 AI 工具：即時語音轉寫、機器翻譯、關鍵詞提示，以及由本研究團隊開發的可定制創新多智能體系統。該系統讓口譯員可按照自身需要，自訂所需的 AI 輔助類型及其組合。研究將邀請三十名來自主要機構的專業會議口譯員，參與貼近真實情境的口譯模擬，以評估人類與 AI 如何最有效地協同工作。 本研究有三項主要目標：第一，評估各類 AI 工具的整體成效；第二，衡量這些工具如何影響口譯的三個關鍵面向——延遲時間（速度）、準確度及流暢度；第三，了解口譯員的個人能力與認知特質如何與這些技術相互作用。研究結果將協助口譯員選擇並調整最符合其個人優勢的 AI 工具，並為建立語言專業領域的全新全球勝任力模型奠定基礎。 本研究計畫具有重要意義，因為它將為世界各地的機構提供以實證研究為基礎的可靠指引，有助於提升國際聽證會或法庭等關鍵場域中的溝通準確度。此外，本研究亦可藉由減輕認知疲勞及降低職業倦怠風險，促進口譯員的身心福祉。本研究團隊由一位經驗豐富的口譯員兼心理語言學家領導；該研究者亦是上述可定制化 AI 工具的開發者。憑藉團隊的專業知識及經實證驗證的研究方法，本計畫將能深入揭示人類與 AI 在口譯領域協作的未來發展。

13100526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13100526.value: 食珊瑚背鰓海蛞蝓之宿主選擇與氣候韌性基因體學研究

13100526.label: Co - Investigator(s)
13100526.value: Dr Mehrotra , Rahul Prof Sun, Jin Mr Yiu, Sam King Fung

13100526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13100526.value: Corallivores, organisms that feed on corals, are increasingly recognized as significant threats to coral ecosystems worldwide. By preying on thermally tolerant corals that survive heatwaves, these predators weaken reef resilience under climate change. Among corallivores, Phestilla nudibranchs have drawn particular attention due to recent reports of new species discoveries and population expansions in subtropical reefs. The ecological impact of Phestilla species, coupled with their high host specificity, positions them as an ideal model for studying genomic adaptations behind trophic specialization. Yet their genetic mechanisms for corallivory, host selection, and environmental resilience remain poorly understood, underscoring the need for targeted genomic research to inform coral reef conservation. To address these knowledge gaps, we propose to generate high-quality, chromosome-level genome assemblies for three Phestilla species that are experiencing rising populations in subtropical Hong Kong waters: P. fuscostriata (host: Pavona), P. subodiosa (host: Montipora), and P. goniophaga (host: Goniopora). We will compare these genomes with those of non-corallivorous nudibranchs to identify the genomic basis for the transition to corallivory. To elucidate host specificity, comparative genomic and transcriptomic analyses among the three Phestilla species will identify genetic determinants of host selection for Pavona, Montipora, and Goniopora. Spatial transcriptomics will validate these findings by mapping gene expression in chemosensory, digestive, and epithelial tissues, identifying localized gene patterns critical for coral host recognition and digestion. To further assess climate resilience of Phestilla, we will analyze whole-genome resequencing data from conspecific populations in subtropical and tropical reefs to detect signatures of thermal adaptation. Overall, this study will provide critical insights into the genomic basis of corallivory and host-specific feeding in nudibranchs, enabling better predictions of ecological risks under climate change and informing evidence-based conservation and restoration strategies for subtropical coral reefs. 珊瑚捕食者（以珊瑚為食的生物）正日益被視為全球珊瑚生態系統的重要威脅。它們捕食能在熱浪中存活的耐熱珊瑚，進而削弱珊瑚礁在氣候變遷下的韌性。在眾多珊瑚捕食者中，Phestilla屬背鰓海蛞蝓因近年新種陸續被發現，以及其在亞熱帶珊瑚礁的族群擴張而備受關注。這類海蛞蝓的生態影響與其高度宿主專一性，使其成為研究營養特化背後基因體適應機制的理想模式生物。然而，其珊瑚捕食、宿主選擇及環境韌性的遺傳機制至今仍所知甚少，凸顯針對性基因體研究對於珊瑚礁保育的迫切需求。為填補這些知識缺口，本研究擬針對香港亞熱帶水域族群上升的三種Phestilla海蛞蝓——P. fuscostriata（宿主：葉狀珊瑚屬Pavona）、P. subodiosa（宿主：牡丹珊瑚屬Montipora）及P. goniophaga（宿主：管孔珊瑚屬Goniopora）——產生高品質、染色體層級的基因體組裝。我們將這些基因體與非珊瑚食性背鰓海蛞蝓進行比較，以鑑定轉化為珊瑚捕食的基因體基礎。為釐清宿主專一性，將透過三種Phestilla之間的比較基因體與轉錄體分析，鑑定分別對應葉狀珊瑚、牡丹珊瑚及管孔珊瑚宿主選擇的遺傳決定因子。進一步以空間轉錄體學驗證上述結果，繪製化學感受、消化及上皮組織中的基因表現圖譜，找出珊瑚宿主辨識與消化關鍵的局部基因模式。此外，為評估Phestilla的氣候韌性，將分析亞熱帶與熱帶礁區同種族群的全基因體重定序數據，偵測熱適應的演化特徵。整體而言，本研究將深入揭示背鰓海蛞蝓珊瑚捕食與宿主專一取食的基因體基礎，有助更精準預測氣候變遷下的生態風險，並為亞熱帶珊瑚礁的實證保育與復育策略提供重要依據。

13200826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13200826.value: 自下而上的聯盟：檢視奧斯特羅姆「多層次治理」原則在香港歷史建築保育中的應用

13200826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13200826.value: This research examines how a bottom-up alliance of small-scale built heritage conservation projects could influence these projects’ viability in Hong Kong. In many modern cities, historic buildings are scattered among clusters of newer structures. Many of these older buildings are repurposed for contemporary functions that differ from their original use, resulting in a cityscape dotted with numerous small-scale, adaptively reused heritage buildings. While these efforts contribute to conserving cultural heritage and revitalising urban spaces, this piecemeal approach raises an important question: After they have started operating, do these built heritage conservation projects have sufficient scale and coordination to remain viable over the long term? Nobel Laureate Elinor Ostrom examined a similar question in her work on how communities manage large areas of shared natural resources, such as forests or water bodies. She found that smaller actors in long-enduring resource management regimes tend to be nested in larger organisations—like federations, networks or alliances. By analogy, just as shared natural resources depend on this type of nested governance structure to remain viable, conserving scattered small-scale built heritage projects in a city likewise requires collaborative governance to address the shortcomings of piecemeal urban conservation approaches. Recently, operators behind 21 small heritage conservation projects in Hong Kong formed a self-organised network called the ‘Built Heritage Alliance’. Members come from heritage sites sponsored by various private or government-supported institutions and have different levels of commitment to the alliance. This bottom-up initiative, emerging in one of the world’s most expensive real estate markets, offers investigators a unique and convenient sampling frame for examining the challenges faced by scattered small heritage conservation undertakings. Such an investigation could also assess how being nested into an alliance may or may not enhance the sustainable use and maintenance of these heritage sites. To examine how the alliance evolves, we plan to use case studies of individual members and affiliates of the alliance, producing a timeline and organisational charts over several years—retrospectively tracing from the time members joined the alliance to the end of the study period. Through interviews and field work, we also investigate the members’ dynamics within the alliance, the alliance’s relationships with various external actors, and how this institutional arrangement can reduce inefficiencies in the conservation and utilisation of the heritage resources. 本研究旨在探討一個在香港由小規模歷史建築保育項目自下而上組成的聯盟如何影響其成員的存續能力。在許多現代城市中，歷史建築往往散落於新建建築群之間，其中不少這類建築已被賦予不同於原始功能的新用途，從而形成城市景觀中眾多小型、活化再利用的歷史建築保育項目。儘管這些嘗試有利於文化遺產的保育和市區空間的活化，惟此種零散式的保育方式也引出一個重要問題：當這些歷史建築保育項目進入營運階段後，是否具備足夠的規模和協同效應，以維持項目的長遠存續呢? 諾貝爾經濟學獎得主埃莉諾·奧斯特羅姆（Elinor Ostrom）在其關於社區如何管理森林、水體等大規模共有自然資源的研究中，曾探討過類似問題。她發現，在能夠長期維持的資源管理制度中，規模較小的行動者往往嵌套於較大型的組織架構之內，例如聯合會、網絡或聯盟。類比地，正如共有自然資源的存續有賴這類多層次治理結構，城市中零散的小型歷史建築保育項目同樣需要透過協作治理，來彌補零散保育模式的內在缺陷。 近年來，香港21個小型歷史建築保育項目的營運者，組成了一個名為「歷史建築聯盟」的網絡。其成員分別來自私人機構或政府資助的歷史建築保育項目，他們對聯盟的投入程度各有不同。這種自下而上的舉措在香港這個全球房地產價格最高的城市之一出現，為研究者提供了一個獨特而便利的抽樣框架，用以檢視分散型小型歷史建築保育計劃所面臨的挑戰，同時亦可評估此種聯盟式的嵌套結構是否以及在何種程度上能促進歷史建築的永續利用與維護。

13202426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13202426.value: 有限训练实例下的可泛化并行算法组合协同演化

13202426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13202426.value: Optimisation is ubiquitous. This proposal considers combinatorial optimisation, which has numerous applications, such as smart logistics, energy management, etc. Many algorithms have been developed. In particular, parallel algorithm portfolios (PAPs) have been proposed to tackle hard combinatorial optimisation problems (COPs) with enhanced robustness and solution quality. The core idea of PAPs is to use a diverse population of different algorithms to solve a hard problem co-operatively and in parallel. Automatic design of PAPs has been a research topic in evolutionary computation for many years. However, current research still faces significant challenges. On the problem side, machine learning-based approaches require a large and diverse set of training problem instances, which may not be available in practice. On the algorithm side, existing work focuses on algorithmic parameters only. The algorithm and portfolio spaces explored in the automatic PAP design are limited. The generalisation ability of automatically designed PAPs is limited. Our proposal will tackle the issue of limited training instances for a hard COP with an unknown instance distribution. The overall goal of our project is to enhance the generalisation ability of automatically designed PAPs given limited training instances. The key novelty here is to use the idea of competitive co-evolution to co-evolve PAPs and problem instances. Our preliminary studies have shown very encouraging promises, being able to find the best-known solutions to TSP benchmark problems and to real-world problem instances from JD.com. However, our preliminary work considered algorithmic parameters only when evolving PAPs and did not make any use of the data generated during co-evolution, which is a rich source of information about the relationship between PAPs and problem instances. This project will build upon our preliminary studies and focus on three unresolved research challenges. The first research challenge is to define the representation space of PAPs, in addition to parameters, and efficient search methods in such a space. The second research challenge is to extract useful knowledge from the evolutionary data to gain a better understanding of the relationship between PAPs and problem instances and apply such knowledge to guide more efficient and effective co-evolution. The third research challenge is to speed up the co-evolutionary process by using computationally efficient surrogate models to evaluate the fitness of PAPs as evaluating a PAP is very time-consuming. The project will carry out extensive computational studies and theoretical analyses to evaluate the proposed research. 组合优化问题在智能物流、能源管理等领域具有广泛应用。现有研究工作对组合优化问题已经开发了众多高效算法。其中，并行算法组合（Parallel Algorithm Portfolios，PAPs）通过提高算法的鲁棒性和解的质量，为求解困难组合优化问题（Combinatorial Optimisation Problems，COPs）提供了一种有效途径。PAPs的核心思想是利用由多种不同算法构成的多样化算法组合，以协作且并行的方式求解困难问题。多年来，PAPs的自动设计一直是进化计算领域的重要研究课题。然而，现有研究仍面临诸多重大挑战。在问题层面，基于机器学习的方法需要大量且多样化的训练问题实例，而这些实例在实际应用中难以获得；在算法层面，现有研究仅关注算法参数设计，PAPs自动设计所探索的算法空间和算法组合空间均较为有限。因此，自动设计的PAPs的泛化能力仍然不足。 本项目将针对实例分布未知的困难组合优化问题，解决训练实例有限这一问题。项目的总体目标是：在训练实例有限的条件下，提高自动设计的PAPs的泛化能力。本项目的核心创新在于引入竞争性协同进化思想，对PAPs和问题实例进行协同进化。我们的前期研究已展现出这一思想的强大潜力，不仅能够找到旅行商问题（TSP）基准实例的当前已知最优解，还能够求解来自京东（JD.com）的真实问题实例。然而，在前期工作中，我们在进化PAPs时仅考虑了算法参数的搜索，也尚未充分利用协同进化过程中产生的数据；而这些数据蕴含着有关PAPs与问题实例之间关系的丰富信息。 本项目将在前期研究的基础上，重点解决以下三个尚未解决的研究挑战。第一个挑战是：构建除参数之外的PAPs表征空间，并研究在该空间中进行高效搜索的方法。第二个挑战是：从进化数据中提取有用知识，以深化对PAPs与问题实例之间关系的理解，并利用这些知识引导更加高效、有效的协同进化。第三个挑战是：利用计算成本较低的代理模型评估PAPs的适应度，从而加快协同进化过程，因为对PAP进行直接评估通常非常耗时。项目将通过大规模计算实验和理论分析，对所提出的研究方法进行系统评估。

13202526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13202526.value: 人格感知型對話式人工智能的綜合框架：數據、識別、誘導與驗證

13202526.label: Co - Investigator(s)
13202526.value: Prof Ali, Raian Prof Qiu, Lin Dr Wen, Zhiyuan

13202526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13202526.value: Imagine AI that truly understands you—adapting its teaching style to your introversion, adjusting explanations as your confidence grows, remembering what motivates you. This isn't science fiction. It's the next frontier in conversational AI, and it's worth $32.62 billion by 2030. The potential transforms lives. Students using personality-matched AI tutors perform 0.3-0.4 standard deviations better—vaulting from average to top-third—while cutting course completion time by half. Patients receiving personality-tailored healthcare interventions show 30% higher medication adherence, potentially saving billions. Companies delivering personalized experiences earn 40% more revenue, yet 80% of consumers report frustration with today's generic AI that ignores individual differences. Why doesn't this exist? Three fundamental barriers block progress. First, no datasets capture authentic human-computer conversations with validated personality profiles—researchers lack the training data needed. Existing attempts using AI to generate conversations produce fake positivity and simplified language that destroys authenticity. Second, current systems analyze only words, ignoring how personality manifests through behavior: response timing, turn-taking rhythms, engagement patterns. They recognize personality once, then freeze—blind to how people evolve during conversations. Third, when AI attempts multiple personality traits simultaneously, outputs contradict themselves—friendly one moment, cold the next—breaking user trust. Our breakthrough solves all three. We're creating the first comprehensive dataset of 34,000+ authentic human-computer dialogues with psychologically validated personality annotations. Unlike AI-generated alternatives plagued by positivity bias, our transformation-based approach preserves genuine emotional complexity and linguistic richness that characterize real conversations. We're pioneering dynamic personality recognition that distinguishes momentary "states" from stable "traits"—the difference between someone having a bad day versus genuinely being pessimistic. Our system integrates what people say with how they interact, continuously refining estimates through conversation rather than making one-time judgments. We're developing algorithms that maintain psychologically coherent AI personalities by systematically identifying and eliminating conflicts among personality descriptors. No more simultaneous "warm yet distant" contradictions that frustrate users. The innovation lies in integration grounded in psychological science—the Big Five personality model validated by decades of research. Our framework continuously adapts with uncertainty quantification, enabling AI that genuinely personalizes without superficial customization. The impact spans sectors. Education systems where students learn faster. Healthcare platforms where patients stay healthier. Customer experiences that truly engage. This research transforms conversational AI from frustratingly generic to genuinely understanding—not just smarter technology, but technology that finally understands what makes each of us unique. 試想像，人工智能能真正理解你：因應你的內向性格調整教學方式，隨着你的信心提升改變講解策略，並記住甚麼最能激勵你。這並非科幻構想，而是對話式人工智能的下一個研究前沿；相關市場規模預計將於2030年達326.2億美元。 這類人工智能有望改變生活。使用與自身人格匹配的人工智能導師，學生的學習表現可提升0.3至0.4個標準差，由平均水平躍升至排名首三分之一，完成課程所需時間亦可減半。按人格特質調整的醫療介入可令服藥依從性提高30%，有望節省數以十億美元計的醫療開支；提供個人化體驗的企業，收入可增加40%。然而，80%的消費者對現時千篇一律、忽視個體差異的人工智能感到沮喪。 既然如此，為何這類人工智能仍未實現？ 三項根本障礙令這一願景至今未能實現。第一，尚無數據集同時涵蓋真實人機對話及經心理學驗證的人格資料。現有由人工智能生成的對話往往帶有不自然的正向偏誤，語言亦過度簡化。第二，現有系統大多只分析語言內容，忽略回應時間、話輪交替及參與模式等行為訊號；其人格識別通常只進行一次，無法追蹤對話中的人格狀態變化。第三，人工智能同時呈現多項人格特質時，回應容易前後矛盾，例如前一刻親切、下一刻冷漠，損害用戶信任。 針對上述限制，本項目提出一套整合框架。首先，建立首個綜合數據集，收錄逾34,000段具真實性的人機對話，並配以經心理學驗證的人格標註；同時採用轉換式數據構建方法，保留真實對話的情感複雜性與語言豐富度。其次，開發動態人格識別方法，區分短暫的「人格狀態」與穩定的「人格特質」，亦即辨別一個人只是當天心情欠佳，還是一貫較為悲觀。系統整合言語內容與互動方式，隨對話推進持續修正人格估計，而非只作一次性判斷。最後，研發演算法，識別並消解人格描述詞之間的衝突，確保人工智能所呈現的人格在心理學上連貫一致，避免「既熱情又疏離」等矛盾表達。 本研究以經數十年研究驗證的大五人格模型為基礎，整合數據構建、動態識別與多特質一致性誘導，並量化不確定性，使人工智能實現真正的個人化，而非僅作表層調整。預期成果可應用於教育、醫療及客戶服務，讓學生學得更快、協助患者維持健康，並提升客戶投入度。這項研究將推動對話式人工智能從千篇一律的工具，轉變為真正理解用戶的系統——不僅更加智能，更能理解每個人的獨特之處。

13203826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13203826.value: LEAPformer - 长期误差增强预测器及在智慧大楼冷负荷预测中的应用

13203826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13203826.value: Identifying nonlinear dynamic systems from input–output data is essential in many engineering applications where first-principles models are unavailable or too complex to derive. In real-world scenarios such as model predictive control, accurate long-term prediction is critical. Traditional learning methods often optimize one-step prediction errors, assuming multi-step performance will follow. However, this assumption frequently fails, especially when neural models differ structurally from the data-generating process. In this project, we propose a novel objective for long-term predictors: the Long-term Error Augmented Predictive (LEAP) learning objective, applied to transformers and state space models. The framework extends conventional prediction error minimization by adding terms that capture error propagation over long prediction horizons. Specifically, LEAP minimizes the difference between p-step and (p-1)-step ahead predictions for a sequence of p values. The project aims to: i) develop long-term augmented predictive (LEAP) learning objectives for transformers, termed LEAPformers, to mitigate accumulated prediction errors; ii) design a residual LEAPformer (Res-LEAPformer) that reduces transformer parameters, improving efficiency for periodic data series; and iii) implement and evaluate these algorithms in predicting HVAC cooling loads for commercial buildings in Hong Kong and Shenzhen to reduce energy consumption and carbon footprint. The main tasks include: 1. Developing the LEAPformer with a long-term predictive objective and $p$-step forecasting, minimizing differences between $p$-step and $(p-1)$-step predictions, and analyzing error propagation across multiple steps. The LEAPformer will also be compared with the multi-token DeepSeek approach. 2. Designing the Res-LEAPformer to extract daily cyclic dynamics from long data sequences and apply LEAPformer for near-term dynamics. This decomposition enables more efficient attention with shorter sequences. Linear models will forecast trend-cyclic components, while the transformer handles near-term dynamics. 3. Extending LEAP learning to LSTM networks and developing PEACE learning for transformers as comparative alternatives. 4. Validating LEAPformer and Res-LEAPformer using building cooling load datasets from Hong Kong and Shenzhen. The developed algorithms will be evaluated using two real-world scenarios: first, an 18-month dataset from the operations of two government office buildings in West Kowloon; second, live data from the DAS smart building in Shenzhen. The Shenzhen building data will be released as open source worldwide to support efforts in reducing energy consumption and carbon emissions. 基于输入-输出数据识别非线性动态系统，是许多缺少物理模型或物理模型过于复杂的工程应用中的关键任务。在模型预测控制等真实场景中，准确的长期预测至关重要。传统的学习方法通常只优化单步预测误差，并假设多步预测性能会自动随之提升；然而，当神经网络模型与数据的生成过程存在结构差异时，这一假设往往失效。 本项目提出了一种全新的长期预测学习目标——长期误差增强预测（LEAP）学习目标，并将其应用于 Transformer 和状态空间模型（State Space Models）。该框架在传统的预测误差最小化基础之上，增加了能够捕获长期预测范围内误差传播的附加项。具体而言，LEAP 通过最小化一系列 p 值下 p 步预测与 (p-1) 步预测之间的差异来实现优化。 本项目旨在： 1. 为 Transformer 开发长期增强预测（LEAP）学习目标（称为 LEAPformer），以缓解累积预测误差； 2. 设计残差 LEAPformer（Res-LEAPformer），减少 Transformer 的参数量，从而提高针对周期性数据序列的预测效率；及 3. 将上述算法应用于香港及深圳商业建筑的暖通空调（HVAC）冷负荷预测并进行评估，以降低能源消耗和碳足迹。 主要研究任务包括： 1. 开发具备长期预测目标的 LEAPformer 并实现 p 步预测：最小化 p 步与 (p-1) 步预测之间的差异，分析多步误差传播过程。此外，将 LEAPformer 与Multi-Token DeepSeek 方法进行对比。 2. 设计 Res-LEAPformer：从长序列数据中提取每日周期性动态，并将 LEAPformer 用于近期动态预测。这种分解能够利用更短的序列实现更高效的注意力机制（Attention）。其中，线性模型用于预测趋势-周期分量，而 Transformer 则负责处理近期动态。 3. 扩展与替代方案研究：将 LEAP 学习扩展至 LSTM 网络，并开发用于 Transformer 的累积纠正增强预测误差（PEACE）学习机制作为对比替代方案。 4. 算法验证：利用香港和深圳的建筑冷负荷数据集对 LEAPformer 和 Res-LEAPformer 进行验证。 研发的算法将在两个真实场景中进行评估：一是西九龙两座政府办公大楼运行 18 个月的历史数据集；二是深圳达实智慧大楼的实时数据。其中，深圳大楼的数据将面向全球开源，以助力全球在降低能耗和碳排放方面的努力。

13300126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13300126.value: 用於提升鋰金屬界面化學–機械穩定性的複合固態電解質膜體相–表面協同工程

13300126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13300126.value: This project aims to develop a bulk–surface co-engineering strategy to improve the chemo-mechanical stability between composite solid electrolyte membranes (CSEMs) and lithium (Li) metal, and to reveal the mechanism by which the synergistic effects of bulk and surface properties enhance interfacial stability. All-solid-state lithium-metal batteries (ASSLMBs) have attracted considerable attention because of their intrinsic safety and high theoretical energy density. CSEMs, comprising sulphide solid electrolytes (exemplified by the lithium argyrodite Li6PS5Cl (LPSCl)) and a polymer matrix, serve as a key component in ASSLMBs by enabling ionic conduction and physically separating the cathode and anode. However, inadequate chemo-mechanical stability at the CSEM|Li interface leads to interfacial degradation, dendrite penetration, and capacity fade. These issues have not been effectively resolved by optimizing the bulk properties of the electrolyte or by surface modification alone. To address this challenge, this project proposes to regulate the bulk and surface properties of CSEMs in a coordinated manner and to enhance the chemo-mechanical stability between CSEMs and Li-metal anodes through the co-design of these two components. To implement this co-engineering strategy, we will first synthesise Zn–F–Br co-doped LPSCl and elucidate how such co-doping regulates ionic and electronic transport and chemo-mechanical stability against Li.
