Fluorine introduced into the bulk phase is expected to act synergistically with fluorine in the subsequent surface coating, forming a gradient LiF-rich solid electrolyte interphase that enhances the critical current density. Second, we will reinforce the P(VDF-TrFE) polymeric fibrous membrane by incorporating inorganic nanoparticles to suppress Li dendrite formation. Besides reinforcing the bulk phase, the nanoparticles at the CSEM|Li interface may also strengthen the interfacial layer formed by the reaction between the coated CSEM and Li, further suppressing dendrite penetration. Third, we will thermally evaporate a thin SnF2 coating onto the Li-facing surface of LPSCl–P(VDF-TrFE) CSEMs and investigate the composition and structure of the interfacial layer formed upon reaction with Li. This coating is expected to improve CSEM|Li contact and establish a fast Li-ion conducting interface. Finally, we will elucidate how the integrated bulk–surface approach, combining Zn–F–Br co-doped LPSCl and nanoparticle-reinforced P(VDF-TrFE) fibres with the SnF2 coating, synergistically governs the chemo-mechanical stability of the CSEM|Li interface, thereby enhancing resistance to dendrite growth under high current densities. In summary, this project will provide a robust and generalizable route to stabilizing solid-electrolyte|Li-metal interfaces in sulphide-based ASSLMBs, thereby facilitating their practical deployment. 本项目旨在開發一種體相–表面協同工程策略，以提升複合固態電解質膜與金屬鋰之間的化學–機械穩定性，並揭示體相與表面協同效應增強界面穩定性的作用機制。全固態鋰金屬電池因其本徵安全性與高理論能量密度而備受關注。以硫化物固態電解質（如鋰硫銀鍺礦型Li–P–S–Cl）與聚合物基體構成的複合固態電解質膜，作為傳導離子並物理隔絕正負極的核心組件，在全固態電池中發揮著關鍵作用。然而，複合固態電解質膜與鋰金屬界面處化學–機械穩定性不足，會導致界面衰退、枝晶穿透及容量快速衰減等問題。單純通過優化電解質體相性質或單一的表面改性，均無法有效解決這些瓶頸。為此，本项目提出對複合固態電解質膜的體相與表面性質進行協同調控，通過兩者的協同設計，全面提升複合固態電解質膜與鋰負極之間的化學–機械穩定性。為實施這一協同工程策略，本项目將開展以下四個方面的研究：（1）合成 Zn、F、Br 共摻雜的Li–P–S–Cl電解質，並闡明該共摻雜策略對離子/電子傳輸及對鋰化學–機械穩定性的調控機制。引入體相的氟元素協同後續的表面塗層，形成富含氟化鋰的梯度固態電解質界面相，從而提高臨界電流密度。（2）通過引入無機奈米顆粒增強聚(偏氟乙烯–三氟乙烯)（P(VDF–TrFE)）纖維膜，以抑制鋰枝晶生長。除了強化體相外，分布在界面處的奈米顆粒還能鞏固電解質膜與鋰反應生成的界面層，進一步阻擋枝晶穿透。（3）在複合固態電解質膜表面蒸鍍一層二氟化錫塗層，研究其與鋰反應後生成的界面層成分與結構。該塗層旨在改善電解質膜與鋰的物理接觸，並構建高效的快速鋰離子傳輸界面。（4）揭示“Zn、F、Br 共摻雜的Li–P–S–Cl + 奈米顆粒增強P(VDF–TrFE)纖維 + 二氟化錫塗層”這一體相–表面一體化策略，如何協同調控電解質膜–鋰界面處的化學–機械穩定性，進而顯著提升在大電流密度下抑制鋰枝晶生長的能力。本项目將為穩定硫化物基全固態鋰電池中的固態電解質–鋰金屬界面提供一種穩健且具備普適性的途徑，為其工業化實用進程提供有力支撐。

13300426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13300426.value: 原位分子置換提升反式鈣鈦礦太陽能電池的可擴展性

13300426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13300426.value: Photovoltaic (PV) devices, which can directly convert solar energy into electricity without carbon emissions, play a critical role in the global energy transition toward clean and renewable sources. Among PV technologies, the power-conversion efficiencies (PCEs) achieved by single-junction metal halide perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have recently exceeded 27%, positioning them as a transformative technology. This unprecedented efficiency gain is largely catalyzed by the advent of carbazole-derived hole-selective self-assembled monolayers (SAMs), which are imperative for achieving high efficiency in inverted PSCs (i.e., with p-i-n configuration). To improve their commercial viability, it is urgent to scale up small-area PSCs to large-area perovskite solar modules (PSMs). Nevertheless, state-of-the-art hole-selective SAMs face several critical challenges, including incomplete coverage, low surface energy, and conformational instability. Consequently, the resulting large-area perovskite films exhibit inhomogeneous optoelectronic properties and a high density of defects at the buried interface, leading to a pronounced efficiency gap between PSCs and PSMs. Moreover, metal halide perovskites are vulnerable to electrochemical degradation when in direct contact with the underlying transparent conducting oxides (TCOs). Although these issues have been partially addressed in recent studies, simultaneously achieving high coverage, efficient hole extraction, favorable wettability, and good molecular stability in hole-selective SAMs remains extremely challenging, impeding their real-world applications. In this project, we will develop an in-situ molecular replacement strategy at the buried interface in PSMs to overcome these challenges. Specifically, we will (1) design and synthesize a series of hydrophilic SAMs based on anchoring groups with lower Brønsted acidity (referred to as pre-SAMs hereafter) than that of phosphonic acid; (2) investigate the molecular replacement reactions between pre-SAMs and hole-selective SAMs on TCO surfaces; (3) establish the relationships between the molecular structures of SAMs and the properties of the resulting hole-selective contacts and perovskite films to guide the iterative optimization of pre-SAM molecules and replacement conditions; and (4) demonstrate high-performance PSCs and PSMs based on this optimized strategy. The success of this project will strengthen our fundamental understanding of in-situ molecular replacement between SAM molecules and enhance the efficiency and long-term operational stability of inverted PSMs. Moreover, it will accelerate the commercialization of inverted PSMs and contribute to the large-scale deployment of sustainable energy solutions. 光伏器件能夠在不產生碳排放的情況下直接將太陽能轉化為電能，在全球能源向清潔可再生能源轉型過程中發揮著重要作用。在各類光伏技術中，單結金屬鹵化物鈣鈦礦太陽能電池的光電轉換效率近期已突破27%，使其成為一項具有變革性的光伏技術。這一前所未有的效率提升在很大程度上得益於咔唑衍生物空穴選擇性自組裝單分子層的發展，該類材料對於實現高效率反式鈣鈦礦太陽能電池至關重要。為進一步提升其商業可行性，亟需推動小面積鈣鈦礦太陽能電池向大面積鈣鈦礦太陽能組件的規模化擴展。然而，目前先進的空穴選擇性自組裝單分子層仍面臨覆蓋不完整、表面能低以及分子構象不穩定等關鍵問題。因此，所形成的大面積鈣鈦礦薄膜往往表現出不均一的光電性質，且埋底界面存在高密度缺陷，從而導致小面積鈣鈦礦太陽能電池與大面積鈣鈦礦太陽能組件之間存在顯著的效率差距。此外，當金屬鹵化物鈣鈦礦與底層透明導電氧化物直接接觸時，容易發生電化學降解。儘管近期研究已在一定程度上緩解了上述問題，但對於空穴選擇性自組裝單分子層而言，同時實現高覆蓋率、高效空穴提取、良好潤濕性及優異分子穩定性仍極具挑戰，制約了其實際應用。 本項目擬在鈣鈦礦太陽能組件的埋底界面開發一種原位分子置換策略，以解決上述關鍵問題。具體而言，本項目將：（1）設計並合成一系列可形成親水性自組裝單分子層的分子，其錨定基團的布朗斯特酸性低於膦酸，以下稱為預自組裝單分子層；（2）研究透明導電氧化物表面預自組裝單分子層與空穴選擇性自組裝單分子層之間的分子置換反應；（3）建立自組裝單分子層分子結構與所形成的空穴選擇性接觸及鈣鈦礦薄膜性質之間的結構—性能關係，並以此指導預自組裝單分子層分子及置換條件的迭代優化；以及（4）基於優化後的策略實現高性能鈣鈦礦太陽能電池和鈣鈦礦太陽能組件。 本項目的成功實施將深化對自組裝單分子層分子之間原位分子置換過程的基礎認識，並提升反式鈣鈦礦太陽能組件的光電轉換效率和長期運行穩定性。此外，本項目將推動反式鈣鈦礦太陽能組件的商業化進程，並促進可持續能源技術的大規模應用。

13500126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13500126.value: AI作為數位和平使者：通過轉化型调解方法促進家庭關係健康

13500126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13500126.value: The escalating adolescent mental health crisis, linked to profound societal costs and strained family systems, represents a pressing global challenge. In regions such as mainland China and Hong Kong, this issue is particularly acute, yet cultural stigma and a lack of scalable solutions create significant barriers to seeking help. Evidence suggests that the breakdown in family communication, particularly between parents and children, is a primary driver of this crisis. While Artificial Intelligence (AI) has shown promise for individual mental health screening and support, its application currently fails to address the core problem of fractured dyadic communication, where adolescents’ distress is often generated and sustained. This project addresses this critical gap by designing and empirically testing a theory-driven AI platform that serves as a “digital peacemaker” to enhance parent-child relational health. Drawing on Transformative Mediation Theory (TMT), we propose and evaluate two specific AI transformative mediation designs—AI empowerment and AI recognition—to achieve such outcomes. This project will be conducted in partnership with an educational technology company that operates an AI platform serving over 500,000 students in mainland China. The project involves two major studies (a two-stage AI mediation process) utilizing multiple methodologies, both of which will recruit parent-child dyads from our partner company’s extensive user base to ensure both feasibility and a large, diverse sample. Study 1 will employ a design science approach, beginning with qualitative interviews with parent-child dyads to develop a 2×2 diagnostic framework of dyadic interaction patterns. This framework will be validated through user surveys, which will then guide the design and validation of our proposed AI platform. Study 2 will consist of a field experiment designed to empirically test the causal effects of the two AI transformative mediation designs on dyadic relationship quality. Crucially, this study will also investigate the underlying mechanism of dyadic shared understanding and the moderating role of the dyadic interaction patterns identified in Study 1. To our knowledge, this project will be the first to develop relational AI using transformative mediation theory in the parent-child context and to empirically examine its impact on dyadic relationship quality. The project will yield a set of actionable, evidence-based design principles for creating technologies that foster healthier and more understanding family relationships. 青少年心理健康問題日益加劇，帶來深遠的社會成本，亦令家庭系統承受更大壓力，已成為全球迫切的公共議題。中國內地及香港等地區的情況尤為嚴峻；然而，文化污名及缺乏可大規模推廣的支援方案，往往令有需要者難以及時求助。現有證據顯示，家庭溝通的失衡——特別是父母與子女之間的溝通破裂——是推動此問題的重要原因之一。儘管人工智能（AI）在青少年個人層面的心理健康篩查與支援方面已展現潛力，但現有應用多仍未能處理核心問題：父母與子女這類「雙人互動」的溝通斷裂，而青少年的困擾往往正是在此互動中產生並延續。 本項目旨在填補此關鍵缺口：我們將設計並以實證方式檢驗一個以理論為基礎的AI平台，作為「數位和平使者」，以提升親子關係健康。項目以「轉化式調解理論」為指導，提出並評估兩種AI轉化式調解設計：AI賦權及AI認可，以促進親子溝通並提升親子關係。本項目將與一家教育科技公司合作；該公司在中國內地營運的AI平台服務逾50萬名學生。項目包含兩項主要研究，並採用多種研究方法；兩項研究均將從合作夥伴龐大且多元的用戶群中招募父母—子女配對樣本，以確保研究可行性。 研究一先透過父母—子女配對的質性訪談，建立一個2×2的兩人互動模式辨識框架；再以用戶問卷調查加以驗證，並據此指導我們所提出之AI平台的設計與驗證。研究二為實地實驗，旨在檢驗兩種AI轉化式調解設計對親子關係品質的因果影響；同時探討其背後機制——親子之間的「互相理解」如何形成——以及研究一所辨識之互動模式的調節作用。據我們所知，本項目將為首批在親子情境中以轉化式調解理論發展「關係型AI」，並以實證方式檢驗其對親子雙方關係品質影響的研究。最終，本項目將產出一套理論驅動、可操作的設計原則，為開發能促進更健康、更多理解的家庭關係之科技提供指引。

13500226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13500226.value: 直播中脏话的语用研究

13500226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
13500226.value: Prof CHUNG, Yuho Prof Zheng, Wanyi

13500226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13500226.value: Swear words are increasingly prevalent in everyday language, commonly appearing in casual conversations, media, and online platforms—such as 7.7% of Twitter posts (Wang et al. 2014), 8.9% of Yelp reviews, and 3.5% of Amazon reviews (Lafreniere et al. 2022). Swearing can serve various communicative functions and evoke both positive and negative perceptions of speakers. While previous research has examined the meaning and impact of swearing in text, its effects in live, interactive online settings remain underexplored. Existing profanity filters primarily rely on keyword matching or basic classification, often failing to account for the nuanced pragmatics of swearing. Indiscriminate censorship risks suppressing authentic expression and may disproportionately silence marginalized groups, for whom swearing can signal solidarity, catharsis, or humor. The rise of livestreaming in gaming, sports, and e-commerce underscores the urgent need for context-aware moderation and presents a unique opportunity to study swearing through multimodal, dynamic analysis. Building on prior work in swearing, attribution theory, multimodal affective coherence (MMAC), social identity, and language style matching, this research presents a conceptual framework with related propositions. We posit that high MMAC, involving congruent negative cues, is associated with spontaneous aggression, while low MMAC, involving incongruent cues, reflects non-aggressive functions. To classify swearing functions via MMAC, we employ a neural network with a Multi-Head Attention mechanism, effectively modeling dependencies both within and across modalities. A series of five studies are designed: Studies 1 and 2 use YouTube and Taobao livestream data to assess the impact of swearing on engagement and purchase behavior; Studies 3 and 4 investigate underlying mechanisms; Study 5 explores moderators such as audience gender and social identity. This research makes two key contributions: (1) it theoretically and empirically validates the relationship between swearing functions and MMAC, and (2) it applies Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) to analyze the influence of swearing on viewer engagement. HMMs capture the dynamic, interactive nature of viewer responses to streamer actions, moving beyond static correlations to quantify bidirectional interactivity in livestreams. The findings will inform the development of nuanced, context-sensitive moderation strategies for digital platforms and offer practical guidance to content creators on ethically leveraging communication to enhance engagement. 脏话在日常语言中日益普遍，频繁出现在日常对话、媒体和网络平台中——例如，Twitter帖子中有7.7%，Yelp评论中有8.9%，亚马逊评论中有3.5%包含脏话。脏话可以承担多种交际功能，并会引发听话者对说话者的正面或负面感知。尽管已有研究考察了脏话在文本中的含义与影响，但其在实时交互式在线环境中的作用仍鲜有探讨。 现有的脏话过滤系统主要依赖关键词匹配或基础分类方法，往往无法顾及脏话使用中微妙的语用差异。不加区分的审查制度有可能抑制真实的表达，并可能不成比例地压制边缘群体——对这些人而言，脏话可以传递团结感、情感宣泄或幽默意图。游戏、体育和电商领域直播的兴起，既凸显了对情境敏感型内容审核的迫切需求，也为通过多模态动态分析研究脏话提供了独特契机。 在脏话、归因理论、多模态情感一致性（MMAC）、社会认同和语言风格匹配等前期研究的基础上，本研究提出一个包含相关命题的概念性框架。我们提出，高MMAC（涉及一致的负面线索）与自发性攻击行为相关，而低MMAC（涉及不一致的线索）则反映非攻击性功能。为了通过MMAC对脏话功能进行分类，我们采用带有多头注意力机制的神经网络，有效建模模态内部及模态之间的依赖关系。本研究设计了五项系列研究：研究1和研究2使用YouTube和淘宝直播数据，评估脏话对用户参与度和购买行为的影响；研究3和研究4考察其内在机制；研究5探索受众性别和社会认同等调节变量。 本研究有两项主要贡献：（1）从理论和实证层面验证了脏话功能与MMAC之间的关系；（2）应用隐马尔可夫模型（HMM）分析脏话对观众参与度的影响。HMM能够捕捉观众对主播行为的动态交互式反应，超越了静态相关性分析，从而量化直播中的双向互动性。研究结果将为数字平台制定细腻且情境敏感的审核策略提供参考，并为内容创作者在合乎伦理地运用传播手段提升参与度方面提供实践指导。

13501526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13501526.value: This proposal explores the interplay between CEOs' political ideologies and the ideological orientations of media outlets in shaping corporate strategic responses to media coverage. While existing research highlights the influence of media tone and volume on corporate behavior, it often overlooks the impact of media ideological alignment on CEO perceptions and actions. Drawing on political communication theories, we examine how CEOs’ responses to media coverage vary based on the perceived ideological congruence with news sources. With the rise of media and political polarization, understanding this dynamic is crucial for comprehending corporate governance and strategic decision-making. This project aims to bridge management literature and political communication, addressing the critical question: How do CEOs’ political ideologies and their alignment with media outlets influence corporate strategic change? By doing so, we seek to provide a more comprehensive framework for analyzing the effects of media on corporate behavior, enhancing our understanding of the nuanced role that ideology plays in shaping executive responses to media signals. 13502426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13502426.value: 任务演进中的劳动者职业生命周期

13502426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13502426.value: Technological evolution continuously reshapes the economy by creating, organizing, automating, and destroying tasks. While recent research has documented the short-term labor market effects of this shift, the long-term consequences for workers' careers and the aggregate labor market remain less well understood. A key gap is the lack of a quantitative framework that integrates explicit task evolution with workers' life-cycle decisions. This project aims to fill that void. We develop a general equilibrium model where the set of available tasks for workers evolves exogenously. In this model, workers specialize in tasks, accumulate task-specific human capital, and face the risk that their skills will become obsolete. They can respond by switching jobs (at the cost of losing some human capital) or by leaving the labor force. Multiple cohorts of workers coexist, and premature labor-force exits create fiscal burdens. We then use this model to quantitatively assess how task evolution drives labor force attachment, reshapes human capital, and contributes to wage stagnation. Our work makes two primary contributions. Methodologically, we bridge macroeconomics and labor theory by uniting an explicit model of task evolution with workers' life-cycle choices in a tractable framework. Substantively, we provide a novel quantitative evaluation of the medium- to long-run labor market response to technological change. Our model reveals that an acceleration in task evolution devalues task-specific human capital, increases prime-age labor force exits, and stagnates wages relative to capital income—ultimately leading to a decline in the labor share. 技术演进通过创造、组织、自动化和消灭任务，来持续重塑经济。尽管近期研究记录了这种转变对劳动力市场的短期影响，但其对劳动者职业生涯和总体劳动力市场的长期后果仍较少被理解。一个关键空白是缺乏将明确的任务演进与劳动者生命周期决策相结合的定量框架。本项目旨在填补这一空白。我们构建了一个一般均衡模型，其中劳动者可从事的任务集合外生演进。在该模型中，劳动者专门从事特定任务，积累任务专用人力资本，并面临技能过时的风险。他们可以通过转换工作（代价是损失部分人力资本）或退出劳动力市场来应对。多代劳动者同时存在，过早退出劳动力市场会造成财政负担。随后，我们利用该模型定量评估任务演进如何影响劳动力市场参与、重塑人力资本并导致工资停滞。我们的工作主要有两大贡献。在方法论上，我们通过在一个可处理的框架中，将明确的任务演进模型与劳动者的生命周期选择相结合，架起了宏观经济学与劳动理论之间的桥梁。在实质层面，我们对劳动力市场对技术变革的中长期反应提供了新的定量评估。我们的模型表明，任务演进加速会贬值任务专用人力资本，增加壮年劳动者退出劳动力市场，并使工资相对于资本收入停滞，最终导致劳动份额下降。

13502626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13502626.value: 從私下調查到公眾壓力：美國證券交易委員會《資訊自由法》查詢記錄公開與企業信息披露

13502626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13502626.value: The U.S Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) allows the public to access records of any federal agency. Although initially designed to enhance the transparency of government activities, it has become an important information source for individuals and entities to acquire firms’ undisclosed information (Gargano et al. 2017; Klein et al. 2020; Glaeser et al. 2023). As part of the OPEN Government Data Act, since December 2013, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) began publishing FOIA request log files, which made the act of information acquisition by various parties publicly observable. In this project, exploiting the exogenous publication of FOIA logs by the SEC, we will examine how observing the act of information acquisition affects corporate disclosure. The FOIA logs list all FOIA requests submitted to the SEC, including the requester’s name, organization, request description, and the request date. The requested information, if granted, remains available only to the requester both before and after the FOIA log publication. Anecdotes suggest that investors and managers use FOIA request log files to identify the firms targeted by individuals and entities probing for negative information (Katz and Hancock 2017; Jackson 2020). Prior to the log publication, probe activity was known only to the requester, allowing firms to withhold bad news without external detection. The public observability of information acquisition increases stakeholder awareness and external monitoring, which in turn pressures managers to disclose bad news in a timely manner to avoid litigation and reputational damage. We predict that after the SEC’s publication of FOIA log files, firms targeted by probe requests will be more likely to release bad news. To test our prediction, we will employ a difference-in-differences design and identify the firms targeted (not targeted) by probe requests as the treatment (control) group. Because probe requests are not random, we will apply entropy balancing to construct a control group which is identical to the treated sample with respect to observable covariates. To examine corporate disclosure behavior, we will first focus on a subsample of firms that are undergoing SEC investigations, and analyze firms’ disclosure likelihood and speed of SEC investigations. Next, we will use management guidance and voluntary 8-K items as more general disclosure measures and test firms’ disclosure of negative information.

13502726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13502726.value: 人机之辨：两条证券市场线之谜

13502726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13502726.value: One of the most prominent anomalies in finance is the weak relationship between risk and expected return. There exists compelling evidence that high-beta assets often deliver lower expected returns than low-beta assets. However, the Capital Asset Pricing Model predicts a strong positive relation between market beta and expected returns (i.e., an upward-sloping security market line). This disconnect between empirical evidence and theory has attracted significant academic attention. Many studies have explored the beta-return relation, highlighting weakening factors such as leverage constraints and investor disagreement. As survey-based forecast data have become more prevalent, recent research has documented belief biases and their effects on aggregate market returns. However, their impact on cross-sectional stock returns, such as the beta-return relation, remains underexplored. We address this gap by using machine learning to form rational expectations and measure predictable belief biases in survey expectations of retail investors and analysts. Additionally, understanding beta and its cross-sectional pricing is also crucial for asset allocation and market efficiency. This leads to an important question: Can investor belief bias explain both the unconditional level and conditional variation in the beta-return relation? Preliminary analyses indicate that high-beta stocks outperform (underperform) low-beta stocks following periods when machine learning forecasts of market returns exceed (or fall short of) survey forecasts, as investors are overly pessimistic (optimistic). We will extend the analysis to the firm level by comparing machine and analyst earnings forecasts to identify overly optimistic and pessimistic stocks. We expect that arbitrage asymmetry can explain the unconditionally flatter beta-returns relation: the negative beta-return relation is stronger among overly optimistic stocks, particularly those that are difficult to short, resulting in an overall weak relation. Our project is original in three ways. First, we use machine learning to construct new measures of expectation wedges (machine learning minus survey forecasts) for market returns and firm earnings. Second, this study predicts and explains the conditional variation in the beta–return relation using these expectation wedges. Third, we explain the unconditional relation between beta and expected returns using arbitrage asymmetry, which leads to a more negative relation among stocks with overly optimistic survey forecasts. Eventually, the proposed research aims to elucidate both the level and dynamics of the market risk premium, offering valuable insights for researchers and practitioners in fields including asset pricing, machine learning, and capital markets. 金融学中一个长期存在的重要异象是，风险与预期收益之间的关系弱于经典理论预测。实证证据表明，高贝塔资产的预期收益往往低于低贝塔资产，这与资本资产定价模型（CAPM）所预测的贝塔与预期收益显著正相关相悖。已有研究主要从杠杆约束、投资者分歧等角度解释这一现象。近年来，调查预期数据的广泛应用揭示了投资者信念偏差及其对市场整体收益的影响，但其如何影响股票横截面收益，尤其是贝塔—收益关系，仍缺乏系统研究。 本项目利用机器学习构建理性预期基准，并据此识别散户和分析师调查预期中的可预测信念偏差，研究其能否同时解释贝塔—收益关系的无条件水平及条件变化。初步结果显示：当机器学习预测的市场收益高于（低于）调查预测，即投资者相对悲观（乐观）时，高贝塔股票随后显著跑赢（跑输）低贝塔股票。进一步地，我们将比较机器学习与分析师盈利预测，在公司层面识别过度乐观和过度悲观的股票。 本项目预计，套利不对称能够解释总体上较为平坦的贝塔—收益关系：在投资者过度乐观的股票中，贝塔与未来收益的负向关系更强，且这一效应在卖空受限股票中尤为显著，从而削弱整体样本中的贝塔—收益关系。 本项目的创新主要体现在三方面：第一，利用机器学习与调查预测之差构建市场收益和公司盈利的“预期楔子”新指标；第二，利用该指标预测并解释贝塔—收益关系的时变特征；第三，从套利不对称角度解释贝塔与预期收益之间较弱的无条件关系。研究将深化对市场风险溢价水平及动态变化的理解，并为资产定价、机器学习和资本市场研究及实践提供新的证据。

13503826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13503826.value: 突顯獨特性：增量式獎勵結構在群眾募資中的影響

13503826.label: Co - Investigator(s)
13503826.value: Prof PENG, Ling Prof Zheng, Wanyi

13503826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13503826.value: This research proposal seeks to investigate how different presentation formats of reward menus influence consumer behavior in reward-based crowdfunding. Campaign creators frequently underestimate the impact of reward presentation, which can critically shape campaign outcomes. This study centers on two commonly used reward menu designs: the cumulative structure (CS), wherein each higher-tier reward encompasses all benefits from preceding tiers in addition to new offerings; and the incremental structure (IS), where higher-tier rewards are described primarily in terms of unique, added items, using descriptors such as “with,” “plus,” or “also”, without reiterating the specifics of lower-tier rewards. Guided by salience theory, we hypothesize that the manner in which rewards are presented substantially affects backer preferences and perceptions. To rigorously test these hypotheses, we will employ a mixed-methods research design, incorporating both controlled laboratory experiments and empirical analysis of real-world data from Kickstarter campaigns. Controlled experiments will enable us to isolate causal effects, probe underlying mechanisms, and delineate boundary conditions, while the empirical study will enhance the external validity and contextual relevance of our findings. By integrating principles from behavioral economics with robust empirical methodologies, this research aims to elucidate the mechanisms underlying consumer decision-making in crowdfunding settings. The anticipated findings will yield actionable insights for campaign creators, informing optimal reward menu design strategies, and will contribute to a deeper understanding of consumer behavior in digital marketplaces. Ultimately, this work is poised to offer significant value to both academic researchers and industry practitioners seeking to maximize engagement and effectiveness in crowdfunding campaigns. 本研究計劃旨在探討不同獎勵選單的呈現格式如何影響消費者在群眾募資中的行為。許多募資專案發起人往往低估獎勵呈現方式的影響，而這種影響可能會顯著左右募資成果。本研究聚焦於兩種常見的獎勵選單設計：累積式結構（CS），即每一個更高層級的獎勵包含所有前一層級的利益並額外提供新項目；以及增量式結構（IS），即較高層級的獎勵主要以新增的獨特項目來描述，常使用「附加」、「加上」或「另外」等字眼，而不重複列出低層級獎勵的細節。本研究以顯著性理論為指引，假設獎勵呈現方式會顯著影響支持者的偏好與認知。 為了嚴謹檢驗這些假設，我們將採用混合研究方法，結合控制式實驗室實驗與 Kickstarter 平台的真實數據分析。控制實驗能夠幫助我們隔離因果效應、探究內在機制並界定邊界條件；而實證研究則能提升外部效度並增強研究結果的情境相關性。透過將行為經濟學的原則與嚴謹的實證方法相結合，本研究旨在揭示群眾募資情境下消費者決策的運作機制。 預期的研究成果將為募資專案發起人提供具體可行的洞見，協助設計最佳化的獎勵選單策略，並深化對數位市場中消費者行為的理解。最終，本研究有望為學術研究者與產業實務工作者提供重要價值，協助提升群眾募資活動的參與度與成效。

13504826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13504826.value: 創新價值鏈中的策略性企業創投（CVC）投資：部分垂直持股的協調價值

13504826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13504826.value: Innovation is a critical driver of growth and competitiveness in today’s supply chains, enabling firms to respond to technological change, shifting customer needs, and market uncertainty. As supply chains become increasingly innovation-dependent, downstream firms are looking beyond traditional contracts to influence upstream R&D. One prominent mechanism is corporate venture capital (CVC)—investment arms or subsidiaries established by large corporations to fund and collaborate with innovative startups and suppliers. According to PitchBook (2022), CVC investors participated in around 26% of all U.S. venture capital rounds, underscoring the growing importance of corporate capital in shaping innovation. A 2025 Corporate Venturing Report by the Mack Institute further finds that 50–60% of Forbes 500 companies in each sector engage in CVC. While CVC can serve both financial and strategic purposes, its strategic role—aligning R&D incentives, coordinating supply chain, and shaping supplier capabilities—is particularly salient in supply chain contexts. In this proposal, we investigate a setting where a downstream firm (e.g., a manufacturer) invests in an upstream supplier through its CVC arm, not merely to provide capital but to strategically align innovation efforts and coordinate supply chain operations. However, such investment creates a key tradeoff: a higher equity stake by the manufacturer enhances coordination but may dilute the supplier’s incentive to innovate. To explore this tension, we develop an analytical model by comparing two regimes: one with traditional contracting (no ownership stake) and one involving partial vertical ownership via CVC. Motivated by this tradeoff, the project aims to deepen our understanding the implications of CVC investments in innovation value chains by addressing the following questions: (1) How does CVC investment affect supplier innovation, supply chain coordination, overall efficiency, and consumer surplus? (2) What are the optimal levels of CVC investment and R&D effort? (3) How do these optimal decisions vary with key model parameters? We expect the project to make meaningful contributions in several areas. First, it can generate insights into the strategic role of CVC in supplier innovation and new product coordination, helping supply chain managers design more effective CVC programs. Second, the findings may offer practical guidance on structuring and managing CVC initiatives to optimize collaboration between manufacturers and suppliers. Finally, the research may inform policy development to encourage and regulate CVC investments—particularly in emerging markets such as China, where such policies could support innovation ecosystems and venture capital growth. 創新是當今供應鏈成長與競爭力的關鍵驅動力，使企業能夠回應科技變遷、顧客需求轉移以及市場不確定性。隨著供應鏈日益依賴創新，下游企業正超越傳統契約安排，尋求影響上游的研發（R&D）。其中一項重要機制是企業創投（Corporate Venture Capital, CVC）—由大型企業設立的投資部門或子公司，用以資助並與具創新能力的新創公司與供應商合作。根據 PitchBook（2022），CVC 投資者參與了約 26% 的美國所有創投融資輪次，凸顯企業資本在形塑創新方面的重要性日益提升。Mack Institute 於 2025 年發布的《Corporate Venturing Report》亦指出，各產業中《Forbes》500 大公司有 50–60% 參與 CVC。 CVC 既可服務於財務目的，也可服務於策略目的；而在供應鏈情境下，其策略角色——包括對齊研發誘因、協調供應鏈，以及塑造供應商能力——尤為突出。在本研究提案中，我們探討一種情境：下游企業（例如製造商）透過其 CVC 部門投資於上游供應商，此舉不僅是提供資金，更是為了策略性地對齊創新投入並協調供應鏈營運。然而，這類投資也產生一項核心取捨：製造商持有較高的股權比例有助於提升協調程度，但可能稀釋供應商的創新誘因。 為探究此一張力，我們建立一個分析模型，比較兩種制度：其一為傳統契約（無持股）制度，其二為透過 CVC 進行部分垂直持股的制度。基於上述取捨，本計畫旨在深化對 CVC 投資於創新價值鏈之影響的理解，並聚焦以下問題：（1）CVC 投資如何影響供應商創新、供應鏈協調、整體效率與消費者剩餘？（2）CVC 投資與研發努力的最適水準為何？（3）這些最適決策如何隨關鍵模型參數而變動？ 我們預期本計畫將在多個面向做出具意義的貢獻。首先，研究可就 CVC 在供應商創新與新產品協調中的策略角色提供洞見，協助供應鏈管理者設計更有效的 CVC 計畫。其次，研究結果可對如何建構與管理 CVC 專案以最佳化製造商與供應商之間的合作提供實務指引。最後，本研究亦可為鼓勵與規範 CVC 投資的政策制定提供參考—尤其是在中國等新興市場，此類政策可支持創新生態系並促進創投市場成長。

13505126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13505126.value: 電子遊戲中的戰利品箱：玩家感知、心理機制與行為後果

13505126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
13505126.value: Prof Liu, Yong Ms Zhu, Qiaoqian

13505126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13505126.value: Over the past two decades, the video game industry has increasingly employed loot boxes, which are purchasable game content with randomized outcomes such as characters, weapons, or costumes. Loot boxes have proven highly lucrative but also face growing scrutiny for their gambling-like nature. However, while the similarity between loot boxes and gambling is echoed in a rich body of scholarly research, growing evidence also points to their dissimilarities. This inconsistency highlights a fundamental gap in scholarly understanding of how players actually perceive loot boxes, what psychological processes they engage, and how these perceptions shape behavior. This lack of comprehensive and nuanced understanding of loot boxes may hinder public discourse and regulatory action that are potentially critical to public interest and consumer well-being. To bridge this gap, this project proposes three integrated projects, using real player samples and an interdisciplinary, multi-method approach. Project 1 distinguishes between what loot boxes objectively are and how they are subjectively perceived, and tests whether players construe loot boxes as gambling or as pathways to achievement. Specifically, we leverage the dual-aspect nature of the Big Five trait conscientiousness (self-control vs. achievement) as a theoretically grounded lens. Specifically, we find that loot box engagement is positively associated with conscientiousness (H1), suggesting players do not naturally view loot boxes as gambling (H2) and, consequently, favoring the alternative account of loot boxes as opportunities for achievement (H3). Furthering these findings, Project 2 identifies the types of achievements players pursue via semi-structured interviews, NLP topic modeling, and staggered difference-in-differences estimations (H4). We then experimentally test how elevated achievements (H5) and obscured costs (H6) causally increase spending. Lastly, Project 3 addresses the lack of high-quality, real-world consumption data on loot boxes, and proposes to build a public longitudinal dataset that combinine time-stamped behavioral logs of loot-box activity with player surveys documenting players’ attitudes, traits, motives. Taken together, this proposal is designed to deliver a nuanced, evidence-based account of player psychology and behavior surrounding loot boxes. Our findings will inform theory, guide regulatory policy, and encourage more ethical and sustainable monetization practices in the games industry. The dataset generated from this project will also benefit future academic and policy research. 當前的電子遊戲產業日益廣泛採用「戰利品箱」(loot box) 機制。所謂戰利品箱，是指由玩家購買、但開箱結果隨機的遊戲內容，例如角色、武器或服裝等。戰利品箱雖具有高度商業價值，卻也因其類賭博性質而受到愈來愈多的審視與批評。學術研究而言，儘管現有研究對戰利品箱與賭博之相似性多有論及，但亦有越來越多的證據指向兩者之間的差異。這一矛盾揭示了學術界在理解玩家如何實際感知戰利品箱、其背後涉及哪些心理過程，以及這些感知如何影響行為等方面尚存在不足；而對戰利品箱缺乏全面而細緻的理解，則可能影響與公共利益及消費者福祉息息相關的公眾討論與政策監管。 為此，本計畫提出三個相互整合的子研究，並以真實玩家樣本為基礎，採用跨學科、多方法的研究路徑。研究一區分戰利品箱的客觀屬性與玩家的主觀感知，並檢驗玩家究竟將戰利品箱視為賭博行為，抑或視為達成成就的途徑。具體而言，本研究以「大五人格」中盡責性特質所具備的兩面性（自我控制與成就追求）—作為理論框架。研究結果顯示，戰利品箱的參與程度與盡責性呈正相關（假設一），表明玩家並不天然地將戰利品箱視為賭博（假設二）；而是將其理解為追求成就的機會（假設三）。在此基礎上，研究二透過半結構式訪談、自然語言處理主題建模及交錯雙重差分估計，識別玩家透過戰利品箱所追求的成就類型（假設四），並以實驗方法檢驗提升成就感（假設五）與模糊消費成本（假設六）如何因果性地增加消費支出。最後，針對現有戰利品箱真實消費數據匱乏的問題，擬研究三建立一個數據集，其中包含附有時間戳的戰利品箱行為日誌，并配合玩家調查數據以記錄玩家的態度、人格特質與動機。 綜上所述，本計畫旨在對玩家心理與戰利品箱消費行為進行細緻研究。本研究的發現將有助於豐富相關理論、指導監管政策制定，並推動遊戲產業採取更具倫理性與可持續性的商業化實踐。本計畫所產生的數據集亦將為未來的學術研究與政策研究提供重要資源。

13600626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13600626.value: 移民密度如何影响移民工人的就业匹配？——理论与实证分析

13600626.label: Co - Investigator(s)
13600626.value: Prof Kaushal, Neeraj Prof Pang, Yu Prof Ye, Han

13600626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13600626.value: Migrant density has grown substantially in many Western countries in recent decades, raising an important question: How does rising migrant density affect labor market outcomes for migrant workers? This issue remains underexplored in economics and social policy for two reasons. First, most migration studies focus on impacts to native populations, reflecting political concerns over immigration’s effects on citizens. Second, studies that do examine migrant density’s effect on migrants themselves mostly focus on earnings, with mixed results. Some suggest higher migrant density lowers wages, others find the opposite—likely due to limitations in measuring earnings. To address this gap, our project shifts focus to migrant overeducation—when workers hold qualifications exceeding job requirements. Overeducation is widespread among migrants and often results in lower earnings and underused skills, signaling labor market mismatches that prevent skilled migrants from using their full potential. We examine, both theoretically and empirically, how migrant density influences overeducation. Our theoretical model builds on our earlier work—Fan, Kaushal, and Pang (2025)—which employs a dynamic job search framework incorporating Becker’s theory of taste-based discrimination. That study shows that when wage equality is enforced, higher migrant density can reduce inequality by limiting discriminatory hiring. We extend this framework in two key ways. First, we account for not only employer bias but also potential productivity gaps among migrants due to language or cultural barriers. Second, we introduce educational heterogeneity, assuming that more educated workers are more productive. This forces employers to weigh their biases against potential productivity gains. We hypothesize that when migrant density is low, employers prefer natives and hire only highly educated migrants. As density increases, employers become less selective, narrowing the education gap between migrants and natives—our central hypothesis. Empirically, we use data from the Integrated Public Use Microdata Series (IPUMS) American Community Survey (ACS) from 2005 onward, combined with occupational data from O*NET. These sources allow us to construct two indicators of overeducation. Using instrumental-variable regressions, we will test two hypotheses: (1) Working-age male immigrants in the U.S. are more likely than natives to work below their qualifications; and (2) this overqualification gap narrows as migrant density rises. This approach introduces a novel lens on migrant labor market integration, highlighting how migrant density can shape labor market mismatches and influence the effective use of migrant talent. 过去几十年来，许多西方国家的移民密度显著上升。在此背景下，一个重要问题随之浮现：移民密度的增加如何影响移民工人自身的劳动力市场结果？这一问题在经济学、社会政策及相关学科中仍未得到充分研究，主要出于两个原因。 首先，尽管移民研究文献浩繁，但大多聚焦于移民对本土居民福利的影响。这种侧重可以理解，因为政策辩论常围绕移民是否改善或损害现有公民的福祉展开。其次，少数考察移民密度对移民劳动力市场影响的实证研究，多集中于收入层面，且结论不一——有的发现密度上升导致移民收入下降，有的则得出相反结论。这些分歧可能源于工资数据的测量误差，以及可靠收入信息的经常性缺失。 为弥补这一空白，我们的项目采用了一个替代性指标：移民工人的过度教育，即工人所持资质高于岗位所需的现象。这在东道国移民中普遍存在。当移民接受低于自身技能水平的工作时，不仅压低个人收入，也阻碍了东道国经济对其人力资本的有效利用，反映出高技能移民无法充分施展教育与经验的劳动力错配问题。 本项目将从理论和实证两方面，研究移民密度对过度教育的影响。理论框架基于项目负责人与两位合作者（Fan, Kaushal & Pang, 2025）的前期工作。他们构建了一个工作搜寻模型，用以分析多数群体（本土居民）与少数群体（移民）间的工资差异，并将贝克尔基于偏好的歧视理论拓展至动态情境。在该模型中，雇主可能对移民持有偏见，但受反歧视法律约束——这些法律要求同工同酬，并对解雇设定高昂成本。当工人生产力各异时，带有偏见的雇主需在自身偏见与雇佣高学历移民所带来的生产力收益之间权衡。因此，移民被雇佣的概率随其教育水平提高而上升。 在移民密度较低时，有偏见的雇主可能更倾向于等待本土求职者，并仅考虑高学历移民。然而，随着密度上升，下一名求职者也是移民的可能性增加，从而降低了雇主在教育资质上的筛选严格程度。这一动态过程引出我们的核心实证假设：尽管移民整体受教育水平高于本土居民，但随着移民密度增加，这一教育差距会缩小。 在实证方面，我们将主要使用2005年及之后的美国社区调查（ACS）综合公共使用微观数据系列（IPUMS）数据。为构建稳健的过度教育衡量指标，我们结合O*NET数据库的职业信息对ACS数据进行补充。通过工具变量回归，我们拟检验两个主要假设：第一，美国处于工作年龄的男性移民比本土居民更可能从事低于其教育资质的职业；第二，这一过度任职效应随移民密度增加而减弱。

13601226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13601226.value: 塑造「創意無產階級」：中國數字經濟中的職業教育、抱負與技能

13601226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
13601226.value: Prof Koo, Ching Hua Anita Prof PUN, Ngai

13601226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13601226.value: Amid China's transition to a digital economy, this project investigates a state-led venture: the repurposing of the vast vocational education (VE) system to forge a new 'creative proletariat'. This inquiry is urgent as China confronts the dual imperatives of industrial upgrading and soaring youth unemployment, positioning VE as the primary engine to solve both. Providing the first bottom-up, ethnographic account of this venture, we analyse how VE attempts to transform youth from working-class and rural-migrant backgrounds into precarious digital creative workers. This project highlights vocational education for two critical reasons: 1) the VE system, with its vast scale and role in class stratification, is the key institutional site where the base of the creative economy is being systematically formed; 2) this process raises a core paradox that animates this study: how can an educational system historically oriented toward producing disciplined industrial bodies be radically retooled to cultivate entrepreneurial and creative subjectivities suited for a precarious creative industry that relies heavily on social and cultural capital? We approach this paradox not as a predetermined outcome, but as a complex, power-laden process of contestation. Our inquiry interrogates: 1) how an ethos of entrepreneurialism – encompassing autonomy, self-branding, and risk-taking – is instilled in students whose class background and educational trajectories offer limited safety nets against market precarity; 2) how schools attempt to mass-produce a ‘creative habitus,’ contested by new technologies and the students’ own class-based habitus; 3) how ‘aspirational indebtedness’ is produced and experienced as a precondition for market entry; and 4) what forms of collective consciousness and everyday resistance emerge amidst intense precarity. To answer these questions, this study employs a multi-sited comparative ethnography, contrasting a state-run 'flagship' college in Shenzhen with a private, market-driven one in Chengdu. Through intensive fieldwork, in-depth interviews tracing the student-to-worker trajectory, and innovative qualitative digital diaries, we will capture the textured reality of precarious creative work and the hidden costs of market entry. Academically, this project will substantially contribute to: 1) the global sociology of labour, by advancing an ethnographic theory of creative subjectivity formation outside a middle-class, Global North context and by theorizing ‘aspirational indebtedness’ as a novel mechanism of precarity; and 2) the sociology of education, specifically to the literature on school-to-work transitions and the political economy of skill formation, by offering a critical account of VE’s role in class formation for digital economy. 伴隨中國向數位經濟轉型，本研究旨在考察一項由國家主導的制度實踐：即龐大的職業教育體系如何被重新配置，以鎔鑄出新型的「創意無產階級」（creative proletariat）。當前中國正臨產業升級與青年高失業率之雙重結構性壓力，並將職教體系視為化解上述困境的核心機制，此一宏觀背景更凸顯本研究之學術迫切性。作為首項針對此一進程提供由下而上之民族誌觀點的實證研究，本計畫將剖析職教體系如何試圖將出身工人階級與鄉村流動背景之青年，轉化為就業處境高度不穩定的數位創意勞動者。 本計畫之所以聚焦職業教育，主要基於兩項考量：其一，憑藉其龐大規模及在階級階層化（class stratification）中扮演之角色，中國職教體系已然成為系統性建構創意經濟基座的關鍵制度場域；其二，此一轉型過程衍生出貫穿本研究的核心問題：一個一貫以規訓並生產「工業身體」（industrial bodies）為導向的教育體系，該如何進行根本性的重構，從而培育出具備企業家精神（entrepreneurial）與創意的主體性，以適應高度依賴社會與文化資本且充滿不穩定性的創意產業？ 在這複雜且充滿權力張力的階級塑造過程，本研究將探問：第一，當學生的階級背景與學歷難以提供抵禦市場不穩定性（market precarity）之社會資本與安全網時，涵蓋自主性、自我品牌化及風險承擔的「企業家氣質」（ethos of entrepreneurialism）是如何在職業教育過程中被灌輸與內化的？第二，學校機構如何試圖批量生產「創意慣習」（creative habitus），而此一機制又如何遭遇新興科技與學生既有階級慣習之拮抗？第三，作為市場准入前提的「抱負性負債」（aspirational indebtedness），是如何被生產並形塑個人的生命經驗？第四，在高度不穩定的結構處境中，浮現出何種形式的集體意識與日常應對？ 為回應上述探問，本研究採取多點比較民族誌（multi-sited comparative ethnography）之方法徑路，將深圳一所具指標性的公立院校與成都一所市場驅動型的私立院校進行對照分析。藉由田野調查、追蹤「從學校至職場」生命軌跡之深度訪談，以及創新的質性數位日記，本研究期能精準捕捉不穩定創意勞動之真實肌理，並揭露數位創意勞動力進入市場之隱性成本。 於學術貢獻層面，本計畫將在以下兩大領域產生實質推進：其一，在全球勞工社會學領域，本研究將跨出「全球北方」（Global North）及中產階級之傳統預設，開展關於創意主體性形塑的民族誌理論，並將「抱負性負債」概念化為一種嶄新的不穩定化（precarity）機制；其二，在教育社會學領域，特別是針對「學校到職場過渡」及技能形成政治經濟學之相關文獻，本研究將對職教體系在數位經濟階級形塑過程中所扮演之角色，提出具備深度反思的學術剖析。

13601526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13601526.value: 香港不適切居所與兒童福祉

13601526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13601526.value: This research concerns the links between poverty, housing and neighbourhood deprivation, and the well-being of children during the primary-secondary transitions. Hong Kong is a rich society with some of the least affordable housing in the world and housing inadequacy is one of the most pressing issues in exacerbating disadvantage among children. However, there is a scarcity of local literature incorporating the effect of inadequate housing on child well-being from children’s own perspectives. Since family resources, housing adequacy and employment opportunities have been significantly reduced and constrained due to the pandemic recession, it is believed that child poverty has increased significantly. Based on deprivation and exclusion frameworks, this study aims to fill the research gaps by simultaneously examining the links between child deprivation, deprived home and neighbourhood environments and child outcomes mediated by children’s social relationships. The research aims to examine how the assessment of such a link can be informed by the children’s voices. This study will address three important research questions: (1) What does ‘inadequate housing’ mean to children in middle childhood?; (2) How does poverty and inadequate housing affect children’s social-emotional functioning and self-reported well-being? ?; and (3) What do the empirical findings imply for policy and practice related to child poverty, well-being and housing design in Hong Kong? A mixed-methods approach will be adopted to gather data directly from children aged 11-13 years, through focus groups and school-based surveys for a holistic understanding of their views and lived experience. Focus groups are an integral part of the survey development process and will provide insights into the aspects of housing inadequacy which are of greatest importance to children. A child advisory group will help with interpreting the survey findings. A paired sample design is used. Primary caregivers will be invited to complete a short questionnaire which includes some housing history and affordability questions to obtain some insight into the cumulative effects of deprivation over the life course. This research will capture children’s views about their actual lived experiences and provides robust evidence about how multifaceted disadvantage at the child-, household- and neighbourhood-level shape children’s lives. This study has greater relevance to children themselves and will assist stakeholders from the education, housing, health and social welfare sectors to take evidence-based concerted actions that effectively and efficiently target children who are in the greatest need. 本研究關注貧窮、住房及社區環境匱乏與處於成長過渡期的兒童福祉的關聯性。香港是一個富裕的社會，與此同時，亦是全球樓價最難負擔的城市之一。不適切居所問題亦是加劇兒童貧窮問題的重要因素。然而，本地缺乏從兒童自身角度探討不適切居所對兒童福祉影響的相關文獻。新冠疫情導致的經濟衰退進一步削弱家庭資源、住房條件和就業機會，加劇了兒童貧窮問題。本研究採用匱乏與社會排斥的理論框架，以兒童社會關係為中介，從兒童自身角度探討兒童物質、住房及社區環境匱乏及對其成長影響的關聯性。本研究探討三個重要的研究問題：(1) 中童期兒童如何理解「不適切居所」? (2) 貧困與不適切居所如何影響兒童的社會情感功能和主觀幸福感? 及 (3) 研究結果如何對香港兒童貧窮、福祉及房屋設計作出務實的政策啟示? 本研究將採用混合研究方法，透過焦點小組訪談和學校問卷調查，了解11至13歲兒童的觀點和生活體驗。焦點小組訪談是問卷設計過程中不可或缺的，有助了解不適切居所的不同範疇對兒童成長的重要性。兒童諮詢小組有助解讀問卷調查結果。本研究採用配對樣本設計，主要照顧者將會填寫一份簡短問卷 (包括住房歷史和負擔能力等問題)，了解生命歷程中匱乏的累積效應。本研究聚焦兒童對自身生活經歷的看法，並提供有力的實証，闡明兒童、家庭和社區層面的不利因素如何影響兒童日常生活。研究結果不僅對兒童有切身關係，亦有助教育、房屋、公共衛生及社會福利不同界別的持份者制定出務實的政策措施，以解決兒童生活的迫切需要。

13601726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13601726.value: 意義、價值與人工智能技術

13601726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13601726.value: Many of us find meaning in life through achievements, relationships, pursuing knowledge, creating art, developing skills, moral growth, or contributing to society. Until recently, these activities were uniquely human. Recent advances in AI are changing this picture. AI systems are now advancing science, creating art, even forming relationships with us. AI may increasingly displace humans from many activities which make our lives meaningful. Some theorists even speculate that AIs could eventually surpass us at all tasks (Bostrom, 2024). This raises pressing questions: how can humans live meaningful lives in an AI-dominated world? What becomes of human significance when our characteristic activities are no longer distinctively ours? These questions lie at the intersection of two active areas of philosophy: theories of meaning in life, developed by Wolf (2010), Metz (2013), and others, and the field of AI ethics. Theories of meaning vary, but most agree that (i) meaning in life is good for its own sake (ii) comes in degrees and (iii) is logically distinct from other normative categories, such as happiness or justice. Most theories converge on the idea that meaning arises from active, positive engagement with valuable things beyond ourselves, often characterized as ‘the good, the true, and the beautiful’. A life wholly lacking in meaning - even if filled with pleasure - appears radically impoverished. AI ethics has thus far focused on issues like existential risk, distributive justice, and AI suffering. Only recently has attention turned to the relationship between AI and meaning in life (Danaher, 2019; Nyholm & Rüther, 2023; O’Brien, 2025). While this literature identifies some threats, analyses remain piecemeal, and few solutions have been proposed. This project will address that gap. First, I will introduce the concept of M-Risks - risks that threaten the meaning in human lives - and develop a systematic taxonomy of how AI creates them. Second, I will evaluate the impact of different AI applications on human meaning and propose normative principles for the design, deployment, and governance of AI that safeguard and promote meaning in life. Third, I will address the broader question of how AI may reshape the cosmic significance and distinctive value of humanity itself, a question not yet directly examined in the literature. In doing so, the project aims to advance both philosophical theory and practical policy, ensuring that meaning in life remains central in the age of artificial intelligence. 許多人都從成就、人際關係、求知、藝術創作、技能發展、道德成長，或者社會貢獻等活動中尋見生命意義。一直以來，這些活動都由人類獨有。然而，人工智能（AI）的新近發展正在動搖這局面。AI 系統如今已在推動科學發展、創作藝術，甚至有能力與我們建立人際關係。AI 可能代理愈來愈多賦予人類生命意義的活動。有學者甚至推測，AI 最終可能在所有任務上超越人類（Bostrom, 2024）。因此，以下問題變得迫在眉睫：在AI主導的世界，人類怎樣才能活得有意義？當人類的特有活動獨特不再，人類的存在意義又何去何從？ 這些問題聯合了兩個熱門哲學領域：一是生命意義理論（由 Wolf, 2010；Metz, 2013 等人發展），二是 AI 倫理學。儘管關於生命意義的理論各有差異，但大多贊同：(i) 生命的意義本身即具有價值；(ii) 意義是有程度之分的；(iii) 意義在邏輯上獨立於其他規範範疇（例如幸福或正義）。大多數理論都傾向接受，意義源於積極、正面地參與超越小我的重要之事；有時稱為「真、善、美」。完全無意義的人生——即使十分快樂——似乎也極度貧乏。目前為止，AI 倫理學主要關注存在風險（existential risk）、分配公義，以及 AI 受苦等議題。直到近日，學界才開始關注 AI 與生命意義之間的關係（Danaher, 2019; Nyholm & Rüther, 2023; O’Brien, 2025）。雖然這些文獻指出了一些威脅，但只有零碎分析，亦甚少提出解決方案。 本計劃旨在填補這一空白。第一，我會引入「M-Risks（威脅人類生命意義的風險）」這概念，並就 AI 如何引發這些風險，建立有系統的分類學（taxonomy）。第二，我將評估不同的AI 應用方式對人類生命意義的影響，並針對 AI 的設計、部署與管治，提出規範原則，以保障並促進生命意義。第三，我將探討更宏觀的問題：AI 將如何重塑人類本身的宇宙意義與獨特價值；現有文獻尚未直接審視這問題。經過這些研究，本計劃旨在推動哲學理論與實務政策的發展，確保生命意義在人工智能時代依然保有核心地位。

13601826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13601826.value: 青年吸煙的神經異質性：靜息與任務路徑的脆弱性、心理靈活性的保護作用及已戒煙者驗證

13601826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13601826.value: Smoking is the foremost preventable cause of morbidity, with 70–90% of quit attempts failing even among motivated individuals. This high failure rate suggests that uniform treatments overlook heterogeneous neurobiological mechanisms in tobacco use disorder. Converging evidence points to a Dual‑Route Neural Framework involving two distinct pathways: a Rest (state) route, representing chronic baseline neural dysregulation and internal distress, and a Task (cue/control) route, representing heightened cue reactivity and impaired inhibitory control. While these routes suggest distinct vulnerability profiles, critical gaps remain, which this study aims to address using EEG in young adults (18–25; N≈300): Within‑Person Route Independence and Specificity. No study has measured both routes within the same individuals to determine their partial independence. It remains unknown whether Rest‑ and Task‑route vulnerabilities show differentiated associations with baseline use and 6‑month abstinence. This study will derive stable within‑route Rest and Task composites and use regularized canonical correlation analysis (rCCA) descriptively to quantify cross‑route coupling within individuals and test partial independence. Route‑Matched Protection. Motivation alone is often insufficient. Psychological flexibility (PsyFlex)—the capacity to remain open to difficult experiences while pursuing valued actions—may offer protection. This study will systematically test the hypothesis that the acceptance dimension of PsyFlex preferentially protects the Rest route, while the values‑based action dimension preferentially protects the Task route. Neurobiological Subtyping and Validation in Former Smokers. The field has largely ignored former smokers, missing the opportunity to identify which neural changes normalize with quitting (state‑dependent therapeutic targets) versus persist (trait vulnerabilities). Leveraging unique access to a Youth Quitline, this study will use Gaussian Mixture Modeling to identify distinct subtypes (e.g., Rest‑dominant, Task‑dominant) and compare current, former, and never smokers to validate cessation mechanisms. Originality and impact. The originality of this study lies in its systematic, within‑person dual‑route neural subtyping in a critical developmental population. By including former smokers, we uniquely validate which neural markers enable versus follow successful cessation. This research provides the translational foundation to move beyond one‑size‑fits‑all approaches toward personalized, neuroscience‑informed cessation strategies matched to individual vulnerability profiles. 吸煙是最主要的可預防致病因素。即使戒煙意欲強烈，仍有70%至90%的戒煙嘗試以失敗告終。如此高的失敗率顯示，劃一的治療方式可能忽略了煙草使用障礙背後因人而異的神經生物學機制。多方面的研究證據均指向一個雙路徑神經框架，當中包括兩條不同的路徑：靜息（狀態）路徑，反映長期存在的基線神經調節失衡與內在心理困擾；以及任務（線索／控制）路徑，反映線索反應性增強及受損的抑制控制。這兩條路徑可能代表不同的脆弱性模式，但目前仍有關鍵研究缺口尚待填補。本研究將以18至25歲的年輕成人為對象，運用腦電圖探討以下三方面： 個體內兩條路徑的獨立性與特異性。過往尚未有研究在同一批參與者身上同時測量這兩條路徑，因此兩者在多大程度上彼此獨立，至今仍未明確。靜息路徑與任務路徑的脆弱性，是否分別與基線吸煙情況及六個月後的戒煙狀況呈現不同關聯，同樣有待驗證。本研究將建構穩定的靜息路徑及任務路徑綜合指標，並以正則化典型相關分析進行描述性分析，量化同一個體內兩條路徑的關聯程度，以檢驗兩者是否具有部分獨立性。 與不同路徑相對應的保護作用。單靠戒煙動機往往並不足夠。心理靈活性是指個體能夠以開放態度面對困難的內在經驗，同時繼續採取符合自身價值的行動，可能對戒煙發揮保護作用。本研究將有系統地檢驗以下假設：心理靈活性中的接納向度主要對靜息路徑發揮保護作用，而價值導向行動向度則主要對任務路徑發揮保護作用。 神經生物學分型及在已戒煙者中的驗證。現有研究鮮少納入已戒煙者，因而未能分辨哪些神經變化會隨戒煙而恢復正常，反映與狀態相關的治療靶點；哪些則在戒煙後仍然持續存在，反映較穩定的特質性脆弱因素。透過與青少年戒煙熱線的合作及其招募渠道，本研究將運用高斯混合模型識別不同的神經生物學亞型，例如靜息路徑主導型及任務路徑主導型，並比較現時吸煙者、已戒煙者及從未吸煙者，以驗證與成功戒煙相關的神經機制。 創新性與影響。本研究的創新之處，在於針對正處於關鍵發展階段的年輕成人，從個體內角度有系統地進行雙路徑神經分型。透過納入已戒煙者，本研究得以進一步辨別哪些神經標記有助促成成功戒煙，哪些則是成功戒煙後才出現的改變。研究結果將為戒煙介入的轉化應用奠定基礎，推動現有服務由劃一模式，轉向以神經科學為依據、並切合個人脆弱性特徵的個人化戒煙策略。

13602726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13602726.value: Altruism is fundamentally grounded in empathetic and compassionate concern for the well-being of others. However, ethical discourse concerning our duties of beneficence has tended to prioritise questions about what one ought to do over questions about what kind of person one ought to be when confronted with others’ needs. The growing influence of Effective Altruism, a relatively recent philosophical and social movement which encourages people to use evidence and careful reasoning to do the most good, underscores this tendency. Effective Altruists are notoriously dismissive of the motivational and affective aspects of philanthropy, advocating impersonal, ruthless decision-making, with the heart firmly reined in by the head. This research project seeks to redirect the discussion by shifting from an exclusively action-oriented framework to one that emphasises the moral significance of character and motivation in shaping our obligations of beneficence. Motives for acting have intrinsic significance independent of their outcome, and acting with the right motives is just as crucial to ethics as achieving the right outcomes. By integrating insights from virtue ethics with contemporary debates in normative ethics, the project aims to develop a more nuanced and psychologically informed account of beneficence—one that takes seriously the role of character and affect in ethical life. This philosophical inquiry is situated against the backdrop of overwhelming global and intertemporal suffering. Approximately 800 million people currently live in extreme poverty. At least 1.6 trillion animals suffer annually as a result of human activity, and wild animal suffering, though less well understood, may exceed human-caused suffering by orders of magnitude. Furthermore, if demographic projections prove accurate and the human population stabilises at around 11 billion by the end of this century, the long-term future may contain upwards of 100 trillion people over the next 800,000 years. The moral enormity of these facts raises urgent questions about the scope, content, and prioritisation of our altruistic obligations. The research will be structured around three core questions that will be approached from this alternative perspective: (1) What is the extent of our obligations to others? (2) Who or what should be included within our moral circle? and (3) Should considerations of effectiveness or sheer numbers influence our philanthropic priorities? In addressing these questions, the project aims to offer a comprehensive and virtue-informed account of beneficence that bridges the gap between ethical theory and real-world moral complexity. 行善之核心 利他主義本質上源於對他人福祉的同理心與慈悲關懷。然而，傳統上關於行善義務的倫理學討論，往往側重於「人應該做什麼」，而非在面對他人需求時「人應該成為怎樣的人」。近年興起的「有效利他主義」（Effective Altruism）更推波助瀾了這一趨勢。該哲學與社會運動鼓勵人們利用證據與嚴密推理來實踐最大效益，卻往往對慈善行為中的動機與情感層面不屑一顧，反而倡導由理性主導感性，進行不帶個人情感且不留情面的決策。 本研究項目旨在扭轉這一討論方向。我們試圖將焦點從全然「以行動為導向」的框架，轉移至強調「品格與動機」在構建行善義務時的道德重要性。行善的動機具有獨立於結果之外的內在價值；對於倫理學而言，心懷正確的動機與達成正確的結果同樣至關重要。本項目將美德倫理學的洞見與當代規範倫理學的辯論相結合，致力於發展出一套更細緻、且更符合心理學實情的行善論述，從而正視品格與情感在道德生活中的核心角色。 這項哲學探究的背景，是當前全球與跨時代所面臨的巨大苦難。目前全球約有8億人口生活在極端貧困之中；每年至少有1.6萬億隻動物因人類活動而遭受痛苦，而野生動物承受的苦難雖然較少為人知，但其規模可能比人類造成的苦難還要高出幾個數量級。此外，若人口預測準確，全球人口將在本世紀末穩定在110億左右，這意味著在未來的80萬年裡，長期未來可能會包含超過100萬億人口。這些無比沉重的道德事實，對我們利他義務的範圍、內容和優先順序提出了迫切的詰問。 本研究將圍繞以下三個核心問題展開，並從上述的新視角進行剖析：（1）我們對他人承擔的義務範圍有多大？（2）誰或什麼應該被納入我們的道德關懷圈？（3）行善的效益或單純的受惠人數，是否應該影響我們慈善資助的優先順序？透過解答這些問題，本項目旨在提出一套兼顧美德與全面性的行善論述，以此修補倫理學理論與現實世界道德複雜性之間的鴻溝。

13603926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13603926.value: According to a family of views falling under the heading "desire satisfactionism," well-being consists, somehow or other, in the satisfaction of desire. In other words: what ultimately makes our lives good is getting what we want. This family of views holds pride of place in economics and decision theory, and many consider it the dominant approach among philosophers, economists, and others. Despite countless attempts to offer a more precise version of this approach, however, no attempt has gained widespread acceptance. Most everyone agrees that not every desire is relevant to well-being. The main disagreement--yielding countless versions of the view--concerns which subset of desires is relevant to well-being. My project's first aim is to show that, in fact, every desire is relevant to well-being. I'll thus argue against a fundamental assumption and starting point for theorizing in contemporary debate over well-being. Desires that don't seem relevant to well-being can always be made to seem relevant under appropriate conditions. I'll offer a systematic account of these conditions, and thereby show that all desires are indeed relevant to well-being. My project's second aim is to build on the foundations of the first, and to address one of the most persistent and damaging objections to desire satisfactionism: the problem of "remote desires." Intuitively, some desires--such as desiring that Napoleon's favorite color was blue--seem "too remote" from our lives to affect our well-being. Despite many attempts to solve this problem, no solution has emerged. Rather than proposing yet another solution, I will break the deadlock here by analyzing the problem itself. Specifically, I will provide the first systematic analysis of what makes a desire "remote." I argue that remoteness is a matter of how likely it is that the desirer will form a belief about whether they are getting the thing they want. This analysis reveals why the problem is so difficult to solve, and also provides an adequacy constraint on all desire satisfactionist theories--a constraint that rules out several important versions of desire satisfactionism, including those dominant in economics and decision theory. These contributions have important practical implications. The remote desires analysis shows that economists and decision theorists working on welfare policy may need to reconsider their basic theoretical assumptions. More generally, by clarifying which desires matter for welfare and under what conditions, the project offers both theoretical insights and practical applications for measuring and promoting human flourishing. 根据一系列归于“欲望满足论”的观点，幸福感在某种程度上取决于欲望的满足。换句话说：最终使我们生活美好的，是得到我们想要的东西。这一观点在经济学和决策理论中占据着举足轻重的地位，许多人认为它是哲学家、经济学家和其他领域人士的主流观点。然而，尽管无数人尝试提出更精确的版本，但没有一种尝试被广泛接受。几乎所有人都认同并非所有欲望都与幸福感相关。主要的分歧——也是由此衍生出无数种观点的原因——在于究竟哪些欲望子集与幸福感相关。我的研究项目的首要目标是证明，事实上，所有欲望都与幸福感相关。因此，我将反驳当代幸福感辩论中一个基本的假设和理论出发点：那些看似与幸福感无关的欲望，总能在适当的条件下变得与幸福感相关。我将系统地阐述这些条件，从而表明所有欲望都与幸福息息相关。 我的项目的第二个目标是在第一个目标的基础上，解决对欲望满足论最持久、最具破坏性的反对意见之一：“遥远欲望”问题。直觉上，有些欲望——例如希望拿破仑最喜欢的颜色是蓝色——似乎与我们的生活“太过遥远”，以至于不会影响我们的幸福。尽管人们曾多次尝试解决这个问题，但至今仍未找到解决方案。与其提出新的解决方案，不如通过分析问题本身来打破僵局。具体而言，我将首次系统地分析是什么使一个欲望“遥远”。我认为，遥远性取决于欲望者形成关于他们是否能得到想要之物的信念的可能性有多大。这项分析揭示了该问题为何如此难以解决，并对所有欲望满足论理论提出了充分性约束——这一约束排除了几个重要的欲望满足论版本，包括经济学和决策理论中的主流版本。 这些贡献具有重要的实践意义。远程欲望分析表明，从事福利政策研究的经济学家和决策理论家可能需要重新审视其基本理论假设。更广泛地说，通过阐明哪些欲望对福利至关重要以及在何种条件下至关重要，该项目为衡量和促进人类福祉提供了理论见解和实践应用。

13604726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13604726.value: 值得信賴的穩定幣：實現中心化金融與去中心化金融的大規模協同

13604726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13604726.value: Stablecoins (STC) are digital assets layered on blockchains, on par with and backed by a basket of high quality, liquid traditional assets such as USD or US Treasurys. Licensing regimes for STC have been adopted in 2025 in several jurisdictions, including Hong Kong and the US (UK and the EU are following suit). This opens a broad avenue for STC institutionalization. Can stablecoins be trusted? They are often described as trustworthy because they are backed by high-quality collateral such as Treasurys. Yet in practice, trust in stablecoins cannot be reduced to collateral alone. The real challenge lies in the interface between two fundamentally different systems of finance: centralized ones, where trust is built through reputation, regulation, and professional expertise; and decentralized systems, where trust is anchored in code, cryptographic proofs, and software protocols. Stablecoins connect these two worlds directly: they are digital tokens circulating on blockchains, but they depend on collateral that exists within traditional, centralized finance. This interface generates a new kind of trust problem—one of coordination across systems that operate on different principles and at different scales. Digital wallets and bank accounts must interoperate securely. The parity between digital tokens and their collateral must be maintained continuously across both ledgers, avoiding risks such as double-spending, or deviations from parity. Stablecoins must navigate regulations across jurisdictions, with different expectations about what counts as credible collateral, secure code, or valid reporting. If stablecoins are to be successful, coordination must be achieved on all levels—micro, meso, and macro—and at scale, supporting millions of daily transactions. For social science, this is significant because existing theories of financial trust have largely focused on centralized finance. Much less is known about how trust is built and maintained when two distinct trust regimes must continuously work together. Stablecoins force us to reconceptualize trust not as something embedded in either institutions or code alone, but as a sociotechnical coordination problem spanning both domains. Adopting a mixed methods strategy spanning ethnographic and quantitative approaches, the project focuses on the following objectives: (1) To theorize trust sociologically when it is no longer “inside one domain” but “between radically different domains”. (2) To outline solutions for interfacing two (financial) systems that define, evaluate, and enact trust differently. (3) To identify the conditions under which these solutions work together at scale without breakdown. 穩定幣 (STC) 是構建於區塊鏈之上的數位資產，其價值與一籃子高品質、高流動性的傳統資產（例如美元或美國國債）相當，並以這些資產作為支撐。包括香港和美國在內的多個司法管轄區已於 2025 年通過了 STC 的許可製度（英國和歐盟也正在效仿）。這為 STC 的製度化開闢了廣闊的道路。 穩定幣值得信賴嗎？穩定幣通常因為它們由國債等高品質抵押品支持， 而被解釋爲可信賴的資產。然而，在實踐中，對穩定幣的信任不能只歸結於抵押品的價值。真正的挑戰在於兩種截然不同的金融體系之間的介面：一種是中心化體系，信任建立在聲譽、監管和專業知識之上；另一種是去中心化體系，信任根植於程式碼、加密證明和軟體協議。穩定幣直接連接了這兩個世界：它們一方面是在區塊鏈上流通的數位代幣，但在另一方面，它們依賴來源於傳統中心化金融體系中的抵押品。 這種介面產生了一種新型的信任問題——如何在基於不同原則、規模不同的系統之間進行協調的問題。數位錢包和銀行帳戶必須安全互通。數位代幣與其抵押品之間的對等性必須在兩個帳本上持續保持，以避免如雙重支付或偏離對等性等風險。穩定幣必須應對不同司法管轄區的監管，這些管轄區對可信任抵押品、安全編碼或有效合規報告的期望各不相同。如果穩定幣想要成功，就必須在 所有層面——微觀、中觀和宏觀——實現協調，並達到一定規模，以支持每天數百萬筆 交易。對於社會科學而言，這一點意義重大，因為現有的金融信任理論大多集中於中心化金融。社會科學對在兩個截然不同的信任機制必須持續協同運作的情況下，如何建立和維護信任知之甚少。 穩定幣迫使我們重新思考信任這一概念，它不再僅限於制度或程式碼，而是一個跨越這兩個領域的社會技術協調問題。本計畫採用混合方法策略，結合民族誌和量化研究方法，旨在實現以下目標： (1) 從社會學的角度探討信任，尤其是在信任不再「局限於單一領域」而是「存在於截然不同的領域之間」的情況下。 (2) 為兩個定義、評估和實施信任方式不同的（金融）系統提供介面解決方案。 (3) 確定這些解決方案在何種條件下能夠大規模協同運作而不失效。

13605926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13605926.value: 革命後，敘述後：形式問題與尋根文學的“陌生化”寫作

13605926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13605926.value: What happens to literature when the narrative certainties of revolution fade? This project seeks to answer this question through the frame of developments in 1980s Chinese literature. It does so with particular reference to the roots-seeking group of writers, consisting of writers who, from the mid 1980s, turned towards the resources of the Chinese countryside and ethnic minority communities as a source of inspiration and renewal in their literary experiments. In particular, it examines how, in theoretical writing as well as in their literary experiments, these writers came to re-imagine literature as no longer strictly bound to the category of narrative, meaning the recounting of events in time in their rational causative relations with one another. In place of narration, roots-seeking formal experiments came to imagine literature as possessing a capacity for “de-familiarization”, meaning the critique of established modes of sensation and cognition. In a search for non-narrative modes of writing, they recovered the cultural possibilities of the pre-modern Chinese essay form (sanwen, biji) as that form most adequate to responding to the cultural demands of the post-socialist moment. 本研究項目試圖探索中國現代文學在八十年大中面對的“敘述危機”與它帶來的敘述方式轉變。

13607326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13607326.value: 東亞藝術策展：在全球博物館與當代藝術機構中展覽作為「世界化」的實踐

13607326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13607326.value: This research examines how exhibitions are curated to foster a critical discourse of “worlding” in East Asia, with a focus on Hong Kong and Taiwan. It considers the notion of “worlding” as a critical and creative intervention in knowledge generation, aimed at addressing the unfinished project of decolonizing and de-imperializing, as well as developing post-colonial subjectivity, in the region's global context. Recognizing world-making as practices to reveal multiple geo-cultural perspectives in imagining and pluralizing the “global,” as well as agencies to counter the dominant worlding, this research investigates how world-making has been practised in exhibition, as a critical tactic to de-colonize and develop a “world-in-becoming” that can deconstruct ideological power and radically create new signification for a specific condition. The research will also analyze the historical contexts in which diverse institutional, cultural, and socio-political forces have shaped the role and manifestation of exhibitions. It seeks to assess the impacts of these exhibitions on the "global art" discourse, and the address of new realities and the contemporary condition. This research extends the study of worlding practices to exhibition studies, identifying and constructing a new typology of “worlding” curatorial practice, that represents a significant shift in the region’s exhibitionary discourses in the twenty-first century. The study includes global museums and contemporary art institutions, to see how their exhibitions generate re- or counter-worlding discourses. These areas have received little attention in existing scholarship in Asia or Asia-Pacific, with most studies focused on artwork analysis while overlooking the agency of exhibitions in the region. This research will draw from exhibition case studies in Hong Kong and Taiwan, using ethnographical methods including textual analysis of exhibition-related materials, participant observation, media review analysis, and qualitative analysis of interviews with creative professionals, art communities, and exhibition visitors involved. The research will aid in understanding the contested discourse of worlding curatorial practice in the region. In particular, it will provide a critical understanding of the roles played by key cultural actors and institutions in Hong Kong and Taiwan and their curatorial practice in remaking the world in response to the challenges specific to their regional and global contexts. The studies will contribute to the unfinished project of decolonizing and de-imperializing in East Asia and offer a new point of departure for inter-referencing on counter-worlding activities in the region. 本研究探討展覽如何策劃以促進東亞「世界化」的批判性論述，重點聚焦香港與台灣。 它將「世界化」概念視為知識生成中一種批判性且具創造力的介入，旨在解決未完成的去殖民化與去帝國化計畫，並在該地區的全球脈絡中發展後殖民主體性。 本研究將「世界建構」視為一種揭示多元文化視角、想像力與多元「全球性」的實踐，並探討如何將世界建構作為展覽中實踐，作為去殖民化的關鍵策略，並發展「形成中的世界」以解構意識形態權力並在特定條件下創造新意義。 研究也將分析各種機構、文化及社會政治力量如何塑造展覽在歷史脈絡中的角色與形式。 該展覽旨在評估這些展覽對「全球藝術」話語的影響，以及它們對新現實與當代條件的回應。 本研究將世界化實踐的研究延伸至展覽研究，識別並建構一種新的「世界化」策展實踐，代表廿一世紀區域展覽話語的重大轉變。 該研究涵蓋全球博物館與當代藝術機構，觀察其展覽如何產生或抗衡全球論述。 這些領域在亞洲或亞太地區現有的學術研究中鮮少受到重視;大多數研究聚焦於藝術分析，卻忽略了該地區展覽的能動性。 本研究將借鑑香港、台灣（以至東亞地區內）的展覽案例研究，採用民族誌方法，包括對展覽相關資料的文本分析、參與者觀察、媒體評論分析，以及對創意專業人士、藝術社群與參與展覽觀眾的質性訪談。 本研究將有助理解該地區世界化策展實踐的爭議性論述。 特別是，它將批判性地理解香港與台灣關鍵文化行動者與機構所扮演的角色，以及他們在處理區域與全球特定挑戰中重塑世界的策展實踐。 這些研究將有助於東亞未完成的去殖民化與去帝國化計畫，並為交叉參照該地區世界化活動提供新的起點。

13607426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13607426.value: 愉悅的維度 質化享樂主義再探

13607426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13607426.value: The concept of pleasure features importantly in contemporary philosophical debates about well-being, or about what makes a person’s life go better or worse for them. Almost all philosophers of well-being agree that, at least in general, one’s life goes better for one to the extent that it is pleasant. But philosophers disagree about which experiences of pleasure are most beneficial from the standpoint of well-being. Some hold that only the quantity of pleasure matters, where quantity is traditionally understood as a function of pleasure’s intensity and duration. Others hold that some pleasures are higher quality than others, and are therefore superior to lower quality pleasures of equal intensity and duration. I aim to move this debate forward by bringing together contemporary research on well-being, consciousness, and affective neuroscience. In particular, the pioneering work of Kent Berridge and Morten Kringelbach has uncovered two distinct systems in the brain — the so-called "wanting" and "liking" systems — which are operative in many or all cases in which we pursue pleasurable activities. Roughly, “liking” is responsible for making it the case that mental states are experienced as pleasant, and “wanting” is responsible for producing a feeling of motivation or compulsion. I will argue for a distinction between what I call static pleasures and dynamic pleasures: static pleasures are experiences of pure “liking”, whereas dynamic pleasures are experiences of mixed “liking” and “wanting”. I will further argue that dynamic pleasures are more beneficial, or more conducive to well-being, than static pleasures. The difference in quality is explained by an underlying difference in quantity: if two subjects experience pleasures of equal intensity and duration, but the former subject’s pleasure is dynamic whereas the latter subject’s pleasure is static, the former subject experiences more pleasure. Thus, my project will attempt a grand reconciliation of quantitative and qualitative views about pleasure’s impact on well-being: quality of pleasure matters, because higher quality pleasures involve a greater quantity of pleasure. 愉悅(pleasure)這一概念,在當代關於福祉(well-being)——亦即關於什麼使一個人的生命對其自身而言過得更好或更差——的哲學爭論中佔有重要地位。幾乎所有研究福祉的哲學家都同意:至少就一般情況而言,一個人的生命愈是愉快,對其自身而言便愈好。然而,從福祉的角度看,究竟哪些愉悅經驗最為有益,哲學家之間卻莫衷一是。有些人主張,唯有愉悅的量才是重要的;而量按傳統理解,乃是愉悅的強度與持續時間的函數。另一些人則主張,某些愉悅的質素高於其他愉悅,因此在強度與持續時間相同的情況下,高質素的愉悅優於低質素的愉悅。 本文旨在結合當代關於福祉、意識與情感神經科學的研究,以推進這場爭論。尤其是 Kent Berridge 與 Morten Kringelbach 的開創性研究,揭示了大腦中兩個彼此有別的系統——即所謂的「想要」(wanting)系統與「喜歡」(liking)系統——在我們追求愉悅活動的許多(甚至全部)情況中,這兩個系統均在運作。粗略而言,「喜歡」負責使心靈狀態被體驗為愉快的,「想要」則負責產生一種動機感或強迫感。 我將論證,我們應當區分我所謂的靜態愉悅(static pleasures)與動態愉悅(dynamic pleasures):靜態愉悅是純粹「喜歡」的經驗,動態愉悅則是「喜歡」與「想要」相混合的經驗。我將進一步論證,動態愉悅比靜態愉悅更為有益,亦即更有助於福祉。這種質素上的差異,可由一種潛在的量上的差異來解釋:設有兩個主體,其所經驗的愉悅在強度與持續時間上均相等,但前者的愉悅是動態的,後者的則是靜態的,那麼前者所經驗到的愉悅其實更多。因此,本計劃試圖對「愉悅如何影響福祉」的量化觀點與質化觀點作出一次宏大的調和:愉悅的質素之所以重要,正是因為質素較高的愉悅包含了更大量的愉悅

13607526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13607526.value: 與對話式人工智能（CAI）的情感連結：一項關於CAI依戀如何影響青少年幸福感的混合方法研究

13607526.label: Co - Investigator(s)
13607526.value: Prof Ni, Shiguang Dr Wang, Qi

13607526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13607526.value: Contemporary adolescents, who are growing up with ubiquitous digital technologies, are prone to form an emotional connection to conversational artificial intelligence (CAI) agents—AI systems that mimic human conversation (e.g., ChatGPT, Doubao). As adolescents are often under personal and interpersonal pressure while still developing their cognitive, social, and emotional capacities for coping, there have been public concerns about the risk that such emotional connection may pose to their well-being. However, little is known about how adolescent users’ emotional connection to CAI may influence their well-being. Although preliminary research has suggested that adults’ connections to CAI are associated with both positive and negative well-being outcomes, little research has elucidated the mechanisms through which these divergent outcomes occur. We will address these gaps through an attachment lens, conceptualizing adolescents’ connection to CAI as CAI attachment—an emotional bond that affords a sense of security and safety. Specifically, this research aims to address three questions: (1) How does CAI attachment influence adolescent well-being? (2) Who receives more benefits or fewer harms from CAI attachment? (3) How do attached adolescents experience CAI’s influences in daily life? By integrating attachment theories and media use theories, we propose a dual-path model, positing that CAI attachment will benefit adolescent well-being by enhancing socioemotional competence (i.e., social augmentation path) and impair it by increasing CAI dependence (i.e., social displacement path). Furthermore, we will examine the moderating roles of social richness and AI literacy in the aforementioned paths. Finally, to complement the quantitative evidence, we will qualitatively investigate the lived experiences of adolescents with strong CAI attachment. We will employ a mixed-methods approach by incorporating a three-wave longitudinal study (Study 1) and a semi-structured interview study (Study 2). Study 1 will test the hypothesized dual-path model based on high school students who use CAI (N = 860 at Time 1). Study 2 will provide qualitative evidence on the dual-path model and additional insights beyond the structured survey based on highly attached adolescents (identified from Study 1). The findings of this research will provide a nuanced understanding of how CAI may present developmental opportunities and risks to adolescents. These insights will help construct a novel theory that elucidates the effects of CAI attachment on adolescent well-being. They will inform the design and implementation of prevention and intervention strategies to help adolescents develop healthy relationships with CAI while cultivating technologies that promote their well-being. 當代青少年成長於無所不在的數碼科技環境中，容易與對話式人工智能（CAI）建立情感連結。CAI是能模擬人類對話的人工智慧系統（如ChatGPT和豆包）。由於青少年常處於個人和人際壓力之下，且其認知、社交與情緒應對能力仍在持續發展中，大家非常關注此類情感連結對其幸福感可能產生的風險。然而，關於青少年使用者與CAI之間的情感連結究竟如何影響其幸福感，學界目前所知甚少。儘管已有少量研究指出，成年人與CAI的連結同時與積極和消極的心理健康狀況相關，但鮮有研究闡明這些分歧結果得以產生的機制。本研究將基於依戀理論來填補此一缺口，將青少年與CAI的連結概念化為「CAI依戀」——一種能提供安全感與安適感的情感連結。具體而言，本研究旨在探討三個問題：（1）CAI依戀如何影響青少年幸福感？（2）哪些人從CAI依戀中獲益較多或受害較少？（3）具高度依戀的青少年如何在日常生活中體驗CAI的影響？ 透過整合依戀理論與媒體使用理論，我們提出一個雙路徑模型：CAI依戀一方面可藉由增進社會情緒能力而提升青少年幸福感（即社會增強路徑），另一方面亦可能因增加對CAI的依賴而損及其幸福感（即社會取代路徑）。此外，我們將考察社會豐富性與AI素養在上述路徑中所扮演的調節角色。最後，為補足量化證據，我們將用質性方法深入探究高CAI依戀水平的青少年的真實經歷。 本研究將採用混合方法，結合三波縱向量化研究（研究一）與半結構式訪談研究（研究二）。研究一以使用CAI的高中生為樣本（第一波N＝860），檢驗雙路徑模型。研究二則針對研究一中辨識出具高度依戀的青少年，蒐集有關雙路徑模型之質性證據，并探索結構化問卷調查之外的洞見。 本研究之發現將有助於細緻理解CAI可能為青少年帶來的發展機會與風險。這些研究成果將有助於建構一套新理論，闡明CAI依戀對青少年幸福感的影響；同時亦能為預防與干預策略的設計與實施提供參考，以協助青少年與CAI建立健康的關係，並促進相關技術之發展，使其能增進青少年幸福感。

13607626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13607626.value: 銀縷交織：華語語系文學中的晚年、疾病與身份

13607626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13607626.value: East Asia is undergoing the world’s fastest demographic transformation: by 2050, more than 35% of the populations of Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Singapore will be over the age of 65. Yet modern Chinese and Sinophone literary studies have strikingly neglected aging. For over a century, youth has been celebrated as an emblem of progress and modernity, while the elderly have been cast as obstacles to renewal or symbols of tradition. Their lived experiences are rarely explored, leaving a glaring disconnect between demographic realities and literary scholarship. This project addresses that gap by reframing aging as a critical category in Sinophone literary studies through an interdisciplinary framework that integrates cultural gerontology (the study of aging through cultural perspectives), medical humanities, and literary criticism. It examines how Sinophone writers transform embodied and intersectional experiences of aging into innovative narrative forms. Offering the first comparative study of aging in Sinophone literature, the project focuses on three acclaimed authors: Hong Kong writer Xi Xi, Singapore writer Yeng Pway Ngon, and Taiwan writer Huang Chunming. Their careers exemplify the project’s central argument: that illness and aging, rather than signaling decline, can spark new literary vitality. Each writer confronted serious illness while writing about late life, creating a rare biographical convergence that shows how aging, understood both as a lived condition and literary theme, is experienced, narrated, and can be theorized in Sinophone contexts. Methodologically, the project combines close readings of their literature with intermedial analysis of their broader creative outputs, such as Huang Chunming’s torn-paper collages and Xi Xi’s handcrafted stuffed toys. This approach traces how illness reshapes artistic expression, revealing close links between personal vulnerability and late-life creativity. Drawing on narrative analysis, embodiment studies, and comparative Sinophone analysis, the project shows how illness catalyzes new ways of engaging aging, transforming vulnerability into a site of literary experimentation and self-redefinition. The project has three interrelated aims. Firstly, to reframe aging as a central analytical category in Sinophone literary studies; secondly, to expand cultural gerontology beyond its Euro-American foundations by analyzing how Sinophone literature complicates discourses of aging, illness, and identity; thirdly, to demonstrate how literature illuminates demographic and social transformation by revealing how individual stories of aging yield collective reflections on late life. By linking intimate illness narratives to broader socio-cultural changes, the project highlights aging as an issue of urgent significance. 東亞正經歷全球最快速的人口結構轉型。預計至 2050 年，香港、台灣與新加坡 65 歲以上人口比例均將逾 35%。然而，現當代中國與華語語系文學研究對老年與晚年議題的關注卻明顯不足。逾百年來，「青年」向被視為進步與現代性的象徵而備受頌揚，「長者」則往往被視為革新的阻力或傳統的表徵，其生命經驗鮮獲深入探究，以致文學研究與人口現實之間出現顯著落差。 本研究計畫旨在填補此一缺口，透過結合文化老年學（從文化視角研究老齡化的學科）、醫療人文與文學批評的跨學科架構，重新將「晚年」確立為華語語系文學研究的重要分析範疇。研究將探討作家如何把步入老齡過程中具身且交織多重身分的生命經驗，轉化為新穎的敘事形式。做為首項針對華語語系文學晚年書寫的比較研究，本計畫聚焦三位作家：香港作家西西、新加坡作家英培安、台灣作家黃春明。他們的創作歷程共同印證本研究核心主張：疾病與老齡處境非但不必然意味著生命力與創造力的衰退，反而可能激發全新的文學創作能量。三位作家均於身患重疾之際書寫晚年經驗，使我們得以考察步入晚年做為生命處境與書寫主題，在不同華語語系脈絡下如何被經歷、敘述與理論化。 研究方法上，除對文學文本進行細讀外，亦納入作家跨媒介創作之分析，例如黃春明的撕紙拼貼、西西的手作玩偶，藉此梳理疾病如何影響藝術表達，並揭示個人生命的脆弱體驗與晚年創造力之間的深刻關聯。本研究結合敘事分析、具身研究與華語語系文學的比較視角，探討疾病如何促使作家以全新視角書寫晚年處境，並將生命的脆弱性，轉化為文學實驗與自我重新定義的契機。 本計畫有三項彼此關聯的研究目標：一、將晚年議題提升為華語語系文學研究的核心分析範疇；二、突破文化老年學長期以歐美經驗為主的研究框架，透過華語語系文學的分析，豐富並重思老齡化、疾病與身分之間的論述；三、揭示文學如何透過個人步入晚齡的生命體驗，映照更廣泛的集體晚年處境，從而彰顯文學回應人口與社會變遷的價值。本研究藉由將個人疾病敘事置於廣闊的社會文化變遷脈絡之中，強化老齡化作為當代社會緊迫公共議題的認知。

13609126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13609126.value: 長期照護保險如何重塑中國家庭照顧網絡：一項縱向混合方法研究

13609126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
13609126.value: Prof CHAN , Wing-kit Prof Fernández, José Luis Prof Li, Bingqin

13609126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13609126.value: As China’s population ages rapidly, families face growing pressure in providing care for older relatives, challenging traditional support systems. In response, the Chinese government introduced the Long-Term Care Insurance (LTCI) pilot scheme in 2016, designed to share care costs and alleviate family burdens. After nearly a decade of implementation, a critical question remains: How does LTCI scheme reshape care arrangements? Current research often overlooks the complex reality of multiple caregivers and fails to distinguish between different benefit types, particularly cash benefits versus in-kind services. This study addresses these gaps through a care network perspective, investigating three key questions: How does LTCI reshape care network composition and structure? Does it trigger renegotiation of care roles and responsibilities, and how do family caregivers perceive monetary compensation for care? How do these changes ultimately affect the well-being of both care recipients and caregivers?
