14115626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14115626.value: Gastric cancer (GC) is a major public problem in Hong Kong causing significant mortality. H. pylori is considered a causative factor in GC initiation; however, our recent studies have shown that non-H. pylori gastric microbiome contributes to GC progression (Cell 2024; Cancer Discov 2024; Gut 2019, 2018). Nevertheless, whether beneficial gastric microbes could slow GC progression remains unexplored. To this end, we analyzed gastric mucosa microbiome in correlation with GC prognosis, and identified Bifidobacterium as an important genus linked to favorable survival. Consistent with this, screening of Bifidobacterium strains in GC tumors demonstrated their antitumor properties, with B. breve emerging as the top candidate. B. breve, an FDA-approved probiotic, suppressed GC cell proliferation and induced apoptosis in vitro, and arrested tumor growth in vivo. Single-cell RNA-sequencing further revealed that B. breve significantly activated antitumor immunity by alleviating CD8+ cell exhaustion and enhancing effector functions. Mechanistic studies revealed that B. breve generates the metabolite genistein via the action of β-glucosidase, which in turn exerts anti-GC effect via dual modulation of GC cells and intratumoral CD8+ T cells by. First, B. breve-derived genistein induces tumor p53 signaling in GC cells by binding to HADHA and disrupting HADHA-MDM2 interaction. This leads to inactivation of MDM2, a major p53 E3 ligase. Second, genistein recapitulates B. breve in boosting CD8+ T cell function, as exemplified by reduced expression of exhaustion markers (PD-1, LAG3) together with the upregulation of effector markers (GZMB, IFN-γ). In terms of translational potential, B. breve or genistein supplementation potentiates anti-PD1 in inducing IFN-γ-expressing CD8+ T cells in GC tumors, offering compelling evidence that B. breve might be useful as an adjuvant for GC immunotherapy. Based on these observations, we hypothesize that B. breve could be utilized for GC prevention and improving immunotherapy response, and as a prognostic biomarker for GC patients. To address these, we propose 4 objectives: 1) To elucidate the function of B. breve in suppressing gastric tumorigenesis and modulating tumor immunity; 2) To uncover the molecular mechanisms underlying B. breve-mediated antitumor and immune regulatory effects; 3) To investigate B. breve as an adjuvant to enhance immunotherapy effects; and 4) To evaluate B. breve as a potential biomarker for predicting GC prognosis. We will utilize a multidisciplinary approach to define functional, mechanistic and clinical significance of B. breve in GC, and pave the way for rational development of probiotics for GC prevention and treatment. 胃癌(Gastric cancer, GC)是香港面臨的重大公共衛生問題，其致死率極高。幽門螺旋桿菌(H. pylori)一直被視為引發胃癌的致病因素；然而，我們近期的研究表明，非幽門螺旋桿菌的胃部微生物在胃癌的惡化過程中亦扮演著重要角色(Cell 2024; Cancer Discov 2024; Gut 2019, 2018)。儘管如此，有益的胃部微生物能否減緩胃癌進展目前仍未知。為此，我們分析了胃黏膜微生物與胃癌預後的相關性，並鑑定出雙歧桿菌屬(Bifidobacterium)為與患者良好存活率相關的重要菌屬。與此一致，我們在胃癌腫瘤模型中對多種雙歧桿菌菌株進行篩選，證實其具備抗腫瘤特性，其中短雙歧桿菌(B. breve) 為最具潛力的候選菌株。作為獲美國食品藥物管理局(FDA)認可的益生菌，B. breve 在體外實驗中能抑制胃癌細胞增殖並誘導細胞凋亡，並在體內實驗中有效遏制腫瘤生長。單細胞 RNA 測序進一步揭示，B. breve 透過緩解 CD8+ T 細胞的耗竭並增強其效應功能，顯著激活抗腫瘤免疫反應。機制研究表明，B. breve 透過 β-葡萄糖苷酶(β-glucosidase)的作用產生代謝物金雀異黃酮(genistein)，進而對胃癌細胞及腫瘤內 CD8+ T 細胞進行雙重調控，從而發揮抗胃癌作用。首先，源自 B. breve 的金雀異黃酮透過與 HADHA 結合，破壞 HADHA 與 MDM2 之間的相互作用，從而激活胃癌細胞中的 p53 腫瘤信號通路，導致 MDM2(一種主要的 p53 E3 泛素連接酶)失活。其次，金雀異黃酮重現了 B. breve 提升 CD8+ T 細胞功能的效果，具體表現為耗竭標誌物(如 PD-1、LAG3)表達下降，同時效應標誌物(如 GZMB、IFN-γ)表達上調。在轉化應用潛力方面，補充 B. breve 或金雀異黃酮能增強抗 PD-1 療法在胃癌腫瘤中誘導表達 IFN-γ 的 CD8+ T 細胞的能力， B. breve 作為胃癌免疫治療佐劑的應用潛力提供了有力證據。 基於上述結果，我們提出以下假說：B. breve 可應用於胃癌的預防及改善免疫治療的療效，且有望成為預測胃癌患者預後的生物標誌物。為驗證上述假說，我們提出四項研究目標：1)闡明 B. breve 在抑制胃部腫瘤發生及調節腫瘤免疫中的功能；2)揭示 B. breve 介導抗腫瘤及免疫調節作用的分子機制；3)探討 B. breve 作為佐劑以增強免疫治療療效的潛力；4)評估 B. breve 作為預測胃癌預後潛在生物標誌物的可行性。本研究將採用多學科整合的研究策略，全面確立 B. breve 在胃癌中的功能、機制及臨床意義，並為理性開發應用於胃癌預防與治療的益生菌奠定基礎。

14115826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14115826.value: 植物ATG18蛋白家族非自噬依賴的功能分子解析

14115826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14115826.value: As a fundamental metabolic pathway, autophagy plays important roles in plant growth and development, particularly under stress conditions. A set of autophagy-related (ATG) proteins is recruited for the formation of a double-membrane autophagosome. Though the molecular mechanisms underlying plant autophagy have been characterized extensively in detail in the past decades, whether the ATG machinery plays autophagy-independent functions in plants is still unexplored. ATG18 protein family, which consists of eight ATG18 isoforms in Arabidopsis, is a well-known PI3P binding regulator to promote autophagosome formation. Our recent study showed that under normal condition, ATG18a proteins also localize on late endosomes. Interestingly, our preliminary data showed that during the heat stress recovery, ATG18a proteins are partially associated with the late endosomes and recruited to the vacuole membrane. However, the vacuolar localization of ATG18a is independent of other core ATG machinery, and no overlapping is observed for ATG18a and ATG8 under the same conditions. We hypothesized that Arabidopsis ATG18a plays an autophagy-independent role on the endosome/vacuolar system, likely to facilitate membrane repair by collaborating with other endosomal regulators. Therefore, in this project, we aim to characterize the unconventional role of ATG18a for acute heat stress response as well as the underlying molecular mechanism by using a combination of biochemical, genetics and cellular approaches. 作為細胞內的基礎代謝途徑，自噬在植物生長發育（特別是在逆境條件下）中發揮重要作用。雙層膜結構的自噬體的生物發生需要募集一系列自噬相關（ATG）蛋白。過去研究已對植物自噬的分子機制進行了深入研究，但ATG相關蛋白是否在植物中發揮非自噬依賴的功能目前尚不清楚。我們近期的研究發現，在正常生長條件下，ATG18a蛋白也定位在內體上。初步數據表明，在熱脅迫條件下，部分ATG18a蛋白募集到植物液泡膜上，並且不依賴其他核心ATG蛋白，也不與自噬標靶ATG8共定位，提示擬南芥ATG18a在內體-液泡系統中可能發揮不依賴自噬的功能。因此，本項目旨在通過生物化學、遺傳學及細胞生物學等多種研究手段，解析ATG18a在植物熱脅迫反應中的非典型功能以及相關的分子機制。

14116026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14116026.value: 幽門螺旋桿菌 CagT4SS 的結構與構象動態學

14116026.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14116026.value: Prof Tao, Changlu Prof Uchihashi, Takayuki Prof Zhang, Huawei

14116026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14116026.value: Helicobacter pylori Cag Type IV secretion system (CagT4SS) is a supramolecular nanomachine that mediates the translocation of a broad range of substrates, including the oncogenic effector protein CagA, into host cells. It is tightly associated to the development of gastric cancer. Unlike the prototypical T4SS, CagT4SS possesses a dozen of species-specific proteins that contribute to its structural diversity and adaptation to distinct biological niches. Previous cryo-EM studies have revealed the overall architecture of CagT4SS and the atomic details of the outer membrane core complex (OMCC) and the periplasmic core complex (PRC). However, mechanistically how CagT4SS is assembled, and functions remains unclear. The central cylinder of PRC-OMCC, comprising of CagM, CagX and CagY, is of particular interest as it is critical for the initiation of CagT4SS biogenesis, gateway for the growth of pilus and substrates delivery, and host contact. Recently, our team has uncovered the assembly pathway is initiated by the self-oligomerization of CagX to form a ring scaffold structure. In vitro reconstitution of different subassemblies indicates the coupling of CagY to form the PRC and multimerization of species-specific CagM onto CagX to establish the OMCC periphery. Findings from hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) and high-speed atomic force microscopy (HS-AFM) single molecule imaging analyses further highlight the conformational dynamics of the central cylinder, particularly the structural plasticity of CagM and instability of OMCC region. To elucidate how PRC-OMCC is assembled and functions as a hub for substrate translocation, we will determine the cryo-EM structures of CagM-CagX and CagM-CagX-CagY sub-complexes. We will define the coupling of Cag3 and CagT onto the central cylinder, and the conformational dynamics involved in completing the OMCC by HDX-MS and HS-AFM. Additionally, we will characterize the molecular compositions of the ‘plug’-like structure in the central cavity of PRC-OMCC by molecular genetics and in situ cryo-ET studies. Mechanistic understanding of CagT4SS has been limited in the past, largely due to the structural diversity and complexity imposed by the unique Cag proteins and the technical challenges in separating different subcomplexes for characterization. This proposal will combine biochemical and multiple state-of-the-art biophysical methods to systemically and comprehensively define the structure-function relationship of PRC-OMCC. The findings will provide a critical foundation to explain the underlying mechanism of CagT4SS beyond what a fully assembled static model can disclose. Understanding how CagT4SS is assembled will also guide the development of therapeutics targeting H. pylori and novel design of molecular machines. 幽門螺旋桿菌Cag第四型分泌系統（CagT4SS)是一種超分子奈米機器，可將多種分子（包括致癌效應蛋白 CagA）輸送至宿主細胞，與胃癌發生密切相關。與典型第四型分泌系統不同，CagT4SS 含有多種幽門螺旋桿菌特有蛋白，賦予其獨特結構與適應性。儘管過往冷凍電鏡研究已解析其整體架構及外膜核心複合體（OMCC）和周質核心複合體（PRC）的原子結構，但其組裝與運作機制仍未完全闡明。 PRC-OMCC 的中央圓柱由 CagM、CagX 和 CagY 組成，是系統生物合成、菌毛延伸及底物轉運的核心樞紐。我們近期發現，CagT4SS 的組裝由 CagX 自我聚集形成環狀支架結構啟動，隨後招募 CagY 形成 PRC，而菌種特有的 CagM 則多聚化於 CagX 外圍，建立 OMCC 結構。氫氘交換質譜及高速原子力顯微鏡進一步揭示中央圓柱具有顯著構型動態性，其中 CagM 的高度結構可塑性及 OMCC 的不穩定特徵尤為突出。 本研究將結合冷凍電鏡、氫氘交換質譜、高速原子力顯微鏡、分子遺傳學及原位冷凍電子斷層掃描，解析 CagM-CagX 與 CagM-CagX-CagY 次複合體結構，闡明 Cag3 和 CagT 如何組裝至中央圓柱，並鑑定 PRC-OMCC 中央腔結構的分子組成。 CagT4SS 因結構高度複雜及特有蛋白多樣性，其機制研究長期受到限制。本計劃將系統性解析 PRC-OMCC 的結構與功能關係，揭示動態組裝過程中驅動底物轉運的分子機制。研究成果不僅將深化對幽門螺旋桿菌致病機制的理解，也有助於開發針對 H. pylori 的新型治療策略，並為人工分子機器的設計提供理論基礎。

14117226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14117226.value: 磁控牽引於結直腸內鏡黏膜下剝離術的隨機對比研究

14117226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14117226.value: Prof Chiu, Philip Wai-yan Prof Lau, Louis Ho-shing Prof Li, Zheng Prof Ng , Simon Siu Man

14117226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14117226.value: Introduction As one of the most common cancers in the world, population based endoscopic screening programs for colorectal cancers are increasingly utilized. Early colon neoplasia are thus often being detected, which could be resected via endoscopy. In particular, endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) is a special technique that allows complete resection of large size colon lesions. It has major benefit in achieving curative treatment for early colon cancer, but is technically demanding and associated with higher risk of adverse events. The main technical challenge lies in the lack of effective countertraction to expose the dissection plane during ESD. We have designed a novel magnetic countertraction system that provide simple effective dynamic countertraction that could facilitate ESD. The system demonstrated superior performance over conventional ESD in an ex-vivo randomised crossover study. An ongoing clinical pilot study also proved the clinical safety of the system. We therefore design a multi-center prospective randomized study to investigate the efficacy of the novel magnetic countertraction on the safety and efficacy of colorectal ESD. We postulate that the procedural efficiency could be enhanced by the use of the novel countertraction system. Methods This is a multi-center randomized controlled trial conducted in two high volume centers in Hong Kong SAR. Adult patients with colon neoplasia undergoing ESD would be randomized to undergo ESD with or without novel magnetic countertraction system. The primary outcome is dissection speed of ESD, measured by lesion area (mm2) divided by time (minute). Secondary outcomes include technical success rate of magnetic countertraction, intra-procedure and post-procedure adverse event rate, pain scores, endoscopist workload measured by NASA Task Load Index etc. Sample size calculation Based on the results of clinical pilot study of the novel system as well as existing local data on colorectal ESD, it is estimated that 144 patients would be required to demonstrate an increase in dissection speed from 16.6 to 25.7 mm2/min (±18.5), with 80% power and false positive rate of 0.05, accounting for 10% drop out. Purpose and potential The current study proposal could demonstrate the superiority of the novel magnetic countertraction system in improving the procedural efficiency during colorectal ESD. It could potentially also demonstrate reduction in endoscopists’ workload and enhanced the learning curve of the procedure. It could therefore provide a new effective device of treatment for superficial colon neoplasia, which carries the potential of translation into a commercial product that benefits patients worldwide. 引言 大腸直腸癌是全球最常見的癌症之一，針對該疾病的基於人群的內視鏡篩檢計畫正日益普及。這使得早期結腸腫瘤的檢出率提高，而此類病變通常可透過內視鏡進行切除。其中，內視鏡黏膜下剝離術（ESD）是一項能夠完整切除大面積結腸病變的特殊技術。儘管ESD在實現早期結腸癌根治性治療方面具有顯著優勢，但該技術操作難度大，且伴隨較高的不良事件風險。 ESD操作中的主要技術挑戰在於缺乏有效的反向牽引力來充分暴露剝離層面。我們設計了一種新型磁性反向牽引系統，旨在提供簡單、有效且動態的反向牽引力，從而輔助ESD操作。在一項離體動物模擬隨機交叉研究中，該系統展現了優於傳統ESD的性能；一項正在進行的臨床試驗研究也證實了該系統的臨床安全性。因此，我們設計了一項多中心前瞻性隨機研究，以評估這種新型磁性反向牽引系統對大腸直腸ESD安全性和療效的影響。我們推測，使用此新型反向牽引系統可望提高手術效率。 方法 本研究是一項在香港特別行政區兩家高手術量中心進行的多中心隨機對照試驗。接受ESD治療的結腸腫瘤成年患者將被隨機分配至「使用新型磁性反向牽引系統」組或「不使用該系統」組。主要終點指標為ESD剝離速度，計算方式為病變面積（mm²）除以操作時間（分鐘）。次要終點指標包括磁性反向牽引的技術成功率、術中及術後不良事件發生率、疼痛評分，以及透過NASA任務負荷指數（NASA-TLX）評估的內視鏡醫師工作負荷等。 樣本量計算 基於此新型系統的臨床試驗研究結果以及現有的本地結直腸ESD數據，經估算，若要證實剝離速度從16.6 mm²/min提升至25.7 mm²/min（標準差±18.5），在統計效能為80%、假陽性率（α）為0.05且需考慮10%脫落率的情況下，共144名患者需納入。 目的與潛力 本研究方案旨在證實新型磁性反向牽引系統在提高大腸直腸ESD手術效率的優點。此外，該系統還有望降低內視鏡醫師的工作負荷，並優化此項技術的學習曲線。因此，它有望為淺表性結腸腫瘤提供一種新型有效的治療手段，並具備轉化為造福全球患者的商業產品的潛力。

14117726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14117726.value: 應用青春雙歧桿菌抑制代謝功能障礙相關脂肪性肝炎：機制解析與臨床應用

14117726.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14117726.value: Dr Wong, Chi-chun Prof Wong, Vincent Wai-Sun

14117726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14117726.value: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a significant and growing health challenge, affecting over 30% of the global population. Approximately 23% MASLD patients develop metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), which may further progress to cirrhosis and liver cancer. Despite this alarming prevalence and severity, effective pharmacotherapeutic treatments for MASH remain scarce. Increasing evidence implicates dysregulation of the gut-liver axis as a pivotal driver of MASH pathogenesis, underlining the urgent need to explore therapeutic strategies that focus on gut microbiome modulation. Our shotgun metagenomic sequencing analysis of stool samples from 279 biopsy-confirmed MASH patients and 78 healthy individuals revealed a profound reduction of several beneficial gut microbes in MASH patients, with Bifidobacterium adolescentis (B. adolescentis) being the most significantly depleted species. In preliminary studies, we successfully isolated B. adolescentis strains from healthy donors and demonstrated that B. adolescentis supplementation alleviates diet-induced MASH in mice, as evidenced by improved liver histology and reduced insulin resistance, hepatic lipid accumulation and inflammation. Mechanistic investigations identified that B. adolescentis restores gut barrier integrity and produces protocatechuic acid (PCA), a metabolite enriched in B. adolescentis conditioned medium, portal vein serum and stools of B. adolescentis-gavaged germ-free mice. PCA effectively inhibits lipid accumulation and inflammation in cultured hepatocytes and in a diet-induced mouse model. Furthermore, mutant E. coli engineered to overexpress PCA-synthesizing enzymes showed significant effects in alleviating lipid accumulation and inflammation in cultured hepatocytes. PCA binds to glucose-regulated protein 78 (GRP78) in the cytoplasm of hepatocytes, suggesting a direct intracellular mechanism. For clinical translation, we have developed B. adolescentis dropping pills to assess its therapeutic efficacy in MASH patients. Based on these preliminary data, we hypothesize that B. adolescentis is a novel therapeutic agent for treating MASH, whose beneficial effects are mediated by PCA-dependent mechanisms. To validate our hypothesis, the objectives of this proposed study are to: 1) characterize the therapeutic effect of B. adolescentis on MASH progression in both conventional and germ-free mouse models; 2) elucidate the mechanisms by which B. adolescentis suppresses MASH through its functional metabolites and its interaction with the host; 3) evaluate the therapeutic potential of B. adolescentis in MASH patients by a proof-of-concept study. Leveraging multidisciplinary approaches that integrates metagenomics, metabolomics, multiorgan-on-a-chip platforms, molecular biology, and multiple mouse models with clinical validation, this research will comprehensively define the gut-liver axis interactions mediated by B. adolescentis. These insights will accelerate the development of innovative microbiota-based therapies for effective management of MASH. 代謝功能障礙相關脂肪性肝病（MASLD）是一個日益嚴重的健康挑戰，影響全球超過30%的人口。約有23%的MASLD患者會進展為代謝功能障礙相關脂肪性肝炎（MASH），後者可能進一步惡化為肝硬化及肝癌。儘管此疾病發病率高且嚴重性不容忽視，目前仍缺乏有效的藥物治療方案。越來越多的證據顯示，腸-肝軸失調是MASH致病機轉中的關鍵驅動因素，探索調控腸道微生物的治療策略迫在眉睫。 我們針對279位經肝臟穿刺確診的MASH患者及78位健康個體的糞便樣本進行了宏基因組測序分析，結果發現MASH患者腸道中多種有益菌顯著減少，其中以青春雙歧桿菌的降低最為顯著。在前期研究中，我們已成功從健康捐贈者分離出青春雙歧桿菌菌株，並證實補充該菌可緩解飲食誘導的小鼠MASH，表現為肝臟組織學改善，胰島素抵抗緩解、肝臟脂質堆積與發炎的減輕。機制研究發現，青春雙歧桿菌能恢復腸道屏障完整性，並產生原兒茶酸（PCA），此代謝物在青春雙歧桿菌條件培養基、門靜脈血清及經該菌灌胃之無菌小鼠糞便中皆呈現富集。PCA能有效抑制肝細胞及飲食誘導小鼠模型中的脂質聚積與發炎。此外，過度表達PCA合成酶的突變大腸桿菌可以顯著減輕肝細胞中的脂質聚積與炎症。PCA可與肝細胞質中的葡萄糖調節蛋白78（GRP78）結合。在臨床轉化方面，我們已開發出青春雙歧桿菌滴丸，用以評估其對MASH患者的治療療效。 基於上述前期數據，我們提出假說：青春雙歧桿菌通過產生PCA抑制MASH，可能成為新型MASH防治藥物。為驗證此假說，本項目具體目標如下：1）在SPF小鼠及無菌小鼠模型中，驗證青春雙歧桿菌對MASH的治療效果；2）闡明青春雙歧桿菌經由其功能性代謝物及與宿主交互作用，抑制MASH的機制；3）評估青春雙歧桿菌在MASH患者中的治療潛力。本研究將整合宏基因體學、代謝體學、多器官芯片平台、分子生物學、多種小鼠模型及臨床驗證等跨領域方法，全面定義青春雙歧桿菌所介導的腸-肝軸相互作用。這些研究成果將加速開發以微生物群為基礎之創新療法，以有效治療MASH。

14117926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14117926.value: 腸道微生物衍生羥基苯乳酸在飲食誘導性肥胖中的作用

14117926.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14117926.value: Prof Ng, Siew C. Prof Zhang, Xiang

14117926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14117926.value: Obesity and its related complications are rising health challenges worldwide, imposing a substantial burden on healthcare systems. There is an unmet need for safe, durable and non-invasive strategies for long-term weight management, with microbiome-derived products showing significant potential. Our recent studies have advanced the understanding of the microbiota in obesity in clinical and preclinical models. In a cross-sectional metagenomic study involving 128 obese subjects and 101 lean controls, we found that R. hominis was significantly reduced in individuals with obesity. Moreover, R. hominis was linked to improved LDL and liver CAP scores in a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial with 61 obese T2DM patients. Recently, we demonstrated in a preclinical model that R. hominis administration prevented diet-induced obesity (DIO) by producing metabolites under 3kDa. Through comparative untargeted and targeted metabolomics, we identified hydroxyphenyllactic acid (HPLA), a gut microbiota-derived metabolite, as the most significantly enriched in R. hominis supernatant and the only one consistently elevated in plasma of R. hominis-treated mice. In preliminary investigations, HPLA supplementation in drinking water prevented weight gain in high-fat diet (HFD)-fed mice. Specifically, energy balance assessments using the Promethion system revealed that HPLA reduced food intake and energy absorption by increasing fecal caloric content, with minimal impact on energy expenditure, mirroring R. hominis effects. This suggested a mechanism driven by HPLA-mediated inhibition of intestinal lipid uptake and modulation of satiety signalling. HPLA, when administered via either enema or gavage, was effectively absorbed into the bloodstream, suggesting that HPLA produced by colonic microbiota has the potential to impact the host both locally and systemically. Based on these preliminary data, we hypothesize that HPLA could serve as a beneficial microbiota-derived metabolite for mitigating DIO. To validate this, our objectives are to 1) elucidate the mechanisms of HPLA in mitigating DIO; 2) elucidate HPLA’s colon-specific and microbiota-dependent anti-obesity mechanisms and 3) evaluate the clinical relevance of HPLA and identify novel HPLA-producing therapeutic strains. We will employ a multidisciplinary strategy involving metagenomics, metabolomics, transcriptomics, molecular biology, and immunology, utilizing established high-precision platforms such as the Promethion system and LC-MS/MS to dissect the role of HPLA in DIO. This study is expected to provide insights into the protective role of HPLA and its producing bacteria through gut-mediated metabolic regulation, elucidating its clinical relevance in obesity while facilitating the development of novel therapeutic strategies. 肥胖及其相關併發症已成為全球日益嚴峻之健康議題，對醫療體系構成重大負擔。目前對於安全、持久且非侵入性之長期體重管理策略仍存在明確不足，而源於腸道微生物組之生物活性物質具有應用潛力。 本研究團隊近期之研究發現，於肥胖個體中 R. hominis 丰度顯著降低，且與低密度脂蛋白及肝臟CAP評分之改善相關。動物模型進一步證實R. hominis 可透過產生分子量低於3 kDa代謝產物有效預防飲食誘導性肥胖（DIO）。透過比較性非標靶與標靶代謝體學分析，我們鑑定出羥基苯乳酸（HPLA）—一種腸道微生物來源之代謝物—在 R. hominis 培養上清液中富集。 於初步實驗中，於飲用水中補充HPLA可顯著預防高脂飲食（HFD）餵養小鼠之體重累積。進一步利用Promethion系統進行能量平衡評估，結果顯示HPLA可透過增加糞便熱量排出，進而減少食物攝取與能量吸收，而對能量消耗之影響則相對有限，此作用模式與 R. hominis 之效應一致。此結果提示其作用機制可能經由HPLA介導之腸道脂質吸收抑制及飽足感訊號調控所驅動。無論以灌腸或灌胃，HPLA均能有效被吸收進入循環系統，顯示由結腸微生物群產生之HPLA可能同時對宿主發揮局部及全身性之生理調節作用。 基於上述前期研究成果，我們提出假說，認為HPLA可作為一種具保護效益之微生物衍生代謝物，用以緩解DIO。為驗證此假說，本研究擬達成以下三項目標：1）闡明HPLA緩解DIO之分子與生理機制；2）探討HPLA於結腸特異性及微生物依賴性層面之抗肥胖作用機轉；3）評估HPLA之臨床相關性，並篩選具產HPLA能力之新型治療性菌株。本研究將採用整合性多學科研究策略，涵蓋宏基因體學、代謝體學、轉錄體學、分子生物學與免疫學等技術平台，並搭配已建立之高精度分析系統，以系統性解析HPLA於DIO進程中之功能角色。本計畫預期將能深入闡明HPLA及其產菌透過腸道代謝調控所發揮之保護效應，並建立其於肥胖臨床應用之科學基礎，進而推動新型治療策略之發展。

14118226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14118226.value: 擬南芥雄配子發生過程中花粉內壁形成的分子機制研究

14118226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14118226.value: In angiosperms, mature pollen has a complex wall that consists of exine and intine layers, playing crucial roles in pollen development. The pollen wall protects against environmental stress, aiding germination and tube growth. Since the 1960s, research has focused on pollen exine development, while intine mechanisms are less understood. The intine, a multi-layered structure next to the plasma membrane (PM), is vital for pollen grain integrity and is tightly regulated during pollen development. Cortical microtubules (MTs) play a key role in cell wall component deposition and patterning. These dynamic polymers undergo phases of polymerization and depolymerization, facilitating intracellular transport through vesicle trafficking, which involves the fusion of vesicles with the PM via a trans-Golgi network (TGN)-dependent pathway, which is mediated by plant syntaxins (SYPs), a type of SNARE (Soluble N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive factor activating protein receptor), required for the vesicle and target membrane fusion. During Arabidopsis pollen development, the MT array aids in cell wall formation, cell growth, and organ directional growth. However, the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying intine development during pollen development remain largely elusive. Our preliminary data show that 1) the development of the intine begins at the polarized stage, during which the large vacuole is formed; 2) the intine layer becomes thicker at the pollen mitosis I stage, which coincides with the increase of MTs and development of the phragmoplast; and 3) the intine formation is disrupted in syp42/syp43 double mutant pollen. We thus hypothesize that cortical MT arrays play an important role in regulating intine development via post-Golgi trafficking and aim to illustrate the underlying mechanisms. Our motivation for this project is based on volume TEM (transmission electron microscopy) and cryo-ET (electron tomography) observation of the uniform intine formation and changes during the bicellular stage. We will employ our well-established large-volume ET technology in combination with cellular, molecular, and genetic approaches to identify and characterize candidate regulators in mediating intine formation and post-Golgi trafficking during pollen development with three specific objectives: 1. To investigate the intine development profile of the pollen; 2. To elucidate the mechanisms of the SYP4 protein in regulating the intine development; 3. To investigate the MT-dependent post-Golgi trafficking that regulates intine development. This project aims to address the development of the intine layer in angiosperm pollen grains. Our study will provide new insights into pollen biology and the regulatory mechanisms of cell wall formation, with potential impact on plant fertilization and reproduction. 在被子植物中，成熟花粉具有由外壁和內壁組成的複雜花粉壁結構，這對於花粉的結構完整性和生理功能至關重要。花粉壁能夠保護花粉免受環境脅迫，並促進花粉萌發和花粉管生長。自20世紀60年代以來，研究主要集中於花粉外壁的發育過程，而對於內壁形成機制的了解仍相對有限。花粉內壁是一種緊鄰質膜的多層結構，對維持花粉粒完整性具有重要作用，其形成過程在發育過程中受到嚴格調控。 皮層微管是花粉發育過程中不可或缺的細胞骨架成分，在細胞壁組分的沉積和空間排列中發揮關鍵作用。這些動態聚合物不斷經歷聚合與去聚合過程，並通過囊泡運輸促進細胞內物質轉運。該過程依賴反式高爾基網絡介導的運輸途徑，通過植物 syntaxin 蛋白（SYPs，一類 SNARE 蛋白）調控囊泡與質膜的融合。 在擬南芥花粉發育過程中，微管陣列參與細胞壁形成、細胞生長以及器官定向生長。然而，目前關於花粉壁發育的研究仍然有限，因此發育中花粉內壁形成過程的許多機制尚不明確。我們的前期研究結果表明：1. 花粉內壁的形成始於極化期，此階段伴隨著大型液泡的形成；2. 在第一次花粉有絲分裂階段，內壁層明顯增厚，同時胞質微管數量增加，並伴隨著成膜體的發育；3. 在 syp42/syp43 雙突變體花粉粒中，內壁形成發生異常。 基於這些發現，我們提出假說：皮層微管陣列通過高爾基體後運輸過程調控花粉內壁的形成。 本項目的研究動機來源於體透射電子顯微鏡和冷凍電子斷層成像對雙細胞期花粉中內壁均勻形成及其動態變化的觀察。我們將利用已建立的大體積電子斷層成像技術，結合細胞學、分子生物學和遺傳學方法，鑑定並解析參與花粉內壁形成及高爾基體後運輸調控的候選因子。本研究擬圍繞以下三個具體目標展開： 1. 系統表徵花粉粒內壁的發育過程 2. 闡明 SYP4 蛋白調控內壁發育的功能及作用機制 3. 研究微管依賴的高爾基體後囊泡運輸在內壁發育中的調控作用

14118826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14118826.value: 組蛋白去乙醯酶9作為肝細胞癌治療抗性之新型免疫調節因子

14118826.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14118826.value: Dr Wong, Chi-chun Dr Zhou, Jingying

14118826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14118826.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most malignant and deadly form of primary liver cancers. The majority face a poor prognosis due to the limited efficacy of standard therapies, including tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI) and immune-checkpoint inhibitors (ICI). This treatment failure is largely driven by an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), though the precise cellular mechanisms remain incompletely defined. Our prior work established that TKI-resistant HCC tumors exhibit an immunosuppressive phenotype that confers subsequent ICI resistance. To delineate the mechanisms underlying treatment tolerance, we employed single-cell RNA sequencing and functional studies on lenvatinib-resistant murine HCC models. Our preliminary data reveal a significant upregulation of HDAC9 in resistant tumor cells, which is functionally linked to the immunosuppressive function of tumor-associated neutrophils (TANs), which suppress cytotoxic T cell function and promote ICI failure. Mechanistically, we propose that HDAC9-mediated deacetylation activates the eIF4G2/PPIA axis to enhance neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation in TANs. Based on these findings, we hypothesize that a tumor-intrinsic HDAC9-driven signaling axis remodels the TME to foster ICI resistance. This proposal aims to comprehensively elucidate the novel immunoregulatory function of HDAC9 in orchestrating TANs-mediated immunosuppression in HCC. We will delineate the mechanistic pathway linking HDAC9 to eIF4G2/PPIA pathway and NETosis, and evaluate the potential of targeting HDAC9 using lipid nanoparticles as a novel therapeutic strategy to overcome ICI resistance. Furthermore, we will assess the clinical relevance of HDAC9 and its associated TANs signature as potential biomarkers for patient stratification and prediction of treatment outcome. This work seeks to define a new druggable axis to improve the efficacy of immunotherapy in advanced HCC. 肝細胞癌（Hepatocellular carcinoma, HCC）為原發性肝癌中最具惡性且致死率最高之類型。多數患者因標準療法療效有限而預後不佳，這些療法包含酪胺酸激酶抑制劑（tyrosine kinase inhibitors, TKI）及免疫檢查點抑制劑（immune-checkpoint inhibitors, ICI）。此治療失敗之主因，主要源於腫瘤微環境（tumor microenvironment, TME）之免疫抑制特性，惟其確切之細胞機轉尚未完全釐清。我們先前之研究已證實，具TKI抗藥性之HCC腫瘤會表現出免疫抑制表型，進而導致後續對ICI產生抗性。為闡明治療耐受性之潛在機轉，我們採用單細胞RNA定序（single-cell RNA sequencing）及功能學研究，於樂伐替尼（lenvatinib）抗藥性之小鼠HCC模型中進行探討。我們的初步數據顯示，抗藥性腫瘤細胞中HDAC9表現量顯著上升，且此現象與腫瘤相關嗜中性球（tumor-associated neutrophils, TANs）之免疫抑制功能具功能性關聯，TANs會抑制細胞毒性T細胞功能並促進ICI治療失效。於機轉層面，我們提出HDAC9媒介之去乙醯化作用，可活化eIF4G2/PPIA訊息軸，進而增強TANs中嗜中性球細胞外陷阱（neutrophil extracellular trap, NET）之形成。基於上述發現，我們假設腫瘤內源性之HDAC9驅動訊息軸會重塑TME，進而促成ICI抗性。本計畫旨在全面闡明HDAC9於調控HCC中TANs媒介免疫抑制之新穎免疫調節功能。我們將描繪HDAC9連結至eIF4G2/PPIA路徑及NETosis之機轉途徑，並評估以脂質奈米顆粒（lipid nanoparticles）標靶HDAC9作為克服ICI抗性之新穎治療策略的潛力。此外，我們亦將評估HDAC9及其相關TANs標記作為潛在生物標記之臨床相關性，以用於患者分層及治療結果預測。本研究旨在定義一新型可藥物標靶之訊息軸，以提升晚期HCC免疫治療之療效。

14118926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14118926.value: RSPO1/LGR4信號軸在腦室下區促進少突膠質細胞生成與髄鞘再生的機制研究

14118926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14118926.value: White matter (WM) injury, comprising demyelination and axonal damage, is characteristic of debilitating neurological disorders such as multiple sclerosis (MS). Oligodendrocytes (OLs), which are myelin-producing cells in the central nervous system, are essential for insulating axons, maintaining efficient nerve signal transmission, and preserving neuronal integrity. Effective remyelination, driven by the differentiation of oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs) into mature OLs, is crucial for restoring neural function and reversing neurological deficits. In aging and chronic diseases, parenchymal OPCs often fail to regenerate, leading to progressive disability. The subventricular zone (SVZ), a neurogenic niche in the adult brain, is an alternative endogenous reservoir of neural stem cells (NSCs) capable of generating OPCs and contributing to myelin repair. Although harnessing NSCs may be a promising therapeutic approach, the molecular mechanisms driving SVZ-derived oligodendrogenesis remain poorly understood. R-spondins (Rspos) are secreted growth factors with known roles in stem cell maintenance and embryonic development. Our recent findings reveal that the Rspo1/Lgr4 axis activates non-canonical Sonic hedgehog (Shh)/Gli1 signaling and crucial OL transcription factors such as Olig2 and Sox10. Notably, Rspo1/Lgr4 operates independently of Wnt signaling and involves Egfr/Erk/c-Jun pathway activation. In vivo, Rspo1 promotes SVZ-mediated oligodendrogenesis, increases OL numbers, and enhances remyelination in a demyelination model, highlighting its therapeutic potential. Based on these findings, we hypothesize that the Rspo1/Lgr4 axis activates non-canonical Shh/Gli1 signaling via the Egfr/Erk/c-Jun pathway, providing a novel mechanism for promoting NSC oligodendrogenesis and myelin repair. The aim of the proposed study will be to uncover the mechanisms by which the Rspo1/Lgr4 axis regulates SVZ-NSC mobilization and oligodendrogenesis to promote WM repair. Specifically, we will: (1) identify Rspo1-responsive cell populations and their lineage progression during OL regeneration and remyelination using single-cell RNA-seq and lineage tracing; (2) determine the role of Lgr4 in SVZ-derived oligodendrogenesis during WM development and repair using Nestin-creERT2; Lgr4fl/fl mice; (3) investigate how the Rspo1–Lgr4–Znrf3 complex regulates non-canonical Shh/Gli1 signaling for OL regeneration; and (4) evaluate the therapeutic potential of RSPO1, alone or with EGF, for enhancing myelin repair and functional recovery in a mouse model of demyelination. Despite urgent need, effective therapies to promote OL regeneration and remyelination in demyelinating diseases remain elusive. The proposed study will not only elucidate the previously undefined role of the Rspo1/Lgr4 axis in oligodendroglial development but also provide a strong foundation for developing transformative therapies to repair WM damage and restore neural function. 白質（white matter, WM）損傷，包括去髓鞘與軸突受損，是多發性硬化症（multiple sclerosis, MS）等致殘性神經疾病的典型病理特徵。少突膠質細胞（oligodendrocytes, OLs）為中樞神經系統中負責產生髓鞘的細胞，對於軸突絕緣、維持神經訊號有效傳導及保存神經元完整性至關重要。有效的再髓鞘化過程仰賴少突膠質前体細胞（oligodendrocyte progenitor cells, OPCs）分化為成熟 OL，這對於恢復神經功能具有關鍵意義。在衰老與慢性疾病狀態下，實質區（parenchymal）OPCs 往往喪失再生能力，導致神經功能持續惡化。成人腦中的側腦室下區（subventricular zone, SVZ）作為內源性神經幹細胞（neural stem cells, NSCs）的儲存庫，能夠產生 OPCs 並參與髓鞘修復。儘管活化 NSCs 可能成為具潛力的治療策略，但調控 SVZ 來源少突膠質生成的分子機制仍未被充分闡明。 R-spondin（Rspos）為分泌型生長因子，已知在幹細胞維持與胚胎發育中扮演重要角色。我們近期的研究發現，Rspo1/Lgr4 軸可活化非典型訊號傳導路徑，以及關鍵的少突膠質轉錄因子，如 Olig2 與 Sox10。在體內實驗中，Rspo1 能促進 SVZ 介導少突膠質生成，增加 OL 數量，並在去髓鞘模型中增強再髓鞘化，顯示其潛在治療價值。本研究計畫旨在闡明 Rspo1/Lgr4 軸如何調控 SVZ-NSC 動員與少突膠質生成，以促進白質修復。 儘管臨床需求迫切，目前仍缺乏有效促進 OL 再生與再髓鞘化的治療策略以應對去髓鞘疾病。本研究不僅將闡明 Rspo1/Lgr4 軸在少突膠質發育中的全新功能，也將為開發突破性治療策略奠定堅實基礎，以修復白質損傷並恢復神經功能。

14119726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14119726.value: 誘導 CD8+ Tregs 啟動 Notch 訊號，使血管平滑肌細胞維持靜止，從而減少動脈粥樣硬化

14119726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14119726.value: Previous studies have established that T cells are the most abundant immune cell type within atherosclerotic lesions; however, the effector mechanisms by which they influence vascular cells remain unclear. In particular, the protective effects of CD8+ regulatory T-cells (Tregs) and the strategies for their in vivo induction are not well defined. In our preliminary work, we found that CD8+ T cells are the predominant immune population during the advanced stages of atherosclerosis and can directly interact with vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) via the CD8 alpha coreceptor pathway in human atherosclerotic tissues. Adoptive transfer of CD8+ T cells inhibits Notch signaling in VSMCs, whereas genetic ablation of Notch signaling in VSMCs acclerated atherosclerosis by enhancing their proliferation, inflammation, and phenotypic switching within plaques. Conversely, CD8a blockade alleviated atherosclerosis and inhibited VSMC proliferation and phenotypic switching by inducing CD8+CD44+CD122+ Tregs, which directly activate Notch signaling in VSMCs. These CD8+ Tregs exhibit higher levels of Notch ligands than conventional CD8+ T cells but are greatly reduced in both circulation and vessel adventitia under a high-cholesterol diet. Importantly, adoptive transfer of CD8+CD44+CD122+ Tregs reduced atherosclerosis progression. Building on these findings, this proposal aims to examine how CD8+ T cells drive the loss of Notch activity in VSMCs during atherosclerosis (Objective 1); delineate the molecular mechanisms by which CD8+ Tregs/Notch regulates VSMC behavior to protect against atherosclerosis (Objective 2); and assess the therapeutic potential of increasing/inducing CD8+ Tregs against atherosclerosis (Objective 3). Collectively, our proposal will uncover the CD8+ Tregs/Notch axis as a novel and promising therapeutic target for treating atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. 既有研究已證實，T 細胞是動脈粥樣硬化病灶中最豐富的免疫細胞類型；然而，它們影響血管細胞的效應機制仍不清楚。特別是，CD8+ 調節性 T 細胞（Tregs）的保護作用及其在體內的誘導策略尚未被明確界定。在我們的初步研究中發現，在動脈粥樣硬化的進展期，CD8+ T 細胞為優勢免疫族群，且可在人體動脈粥樣硬化組織中經由 CD8α 輔受體途徑直接與血管平滑肌細胞 (VSMCs）互動。CD8+ T 細胞的過繼轉移會抑制 VSMCs 的 Notch 訊號傳導；相對地，在 VSMCs 中基因性移除 Notch 訊號會因促進其在斑塊內的增殖、發炎與表型轉換而加速動脈粥樣硬化。反之，阻斷 CD8α 可藉由誘導 CD8+CD44+CD122+ Tregs 而減輕動脈粥樣硬化，並抑制 VSMCs 的增殖與表型轉換；這些 Tregs 可直接活化 VSMCs 的 Notch 訊號。與傳統 CD8+ T 細胞相比，CD8+ Tregs 表現較高水準的 Notch 配體，但在高膽固醇飲食下，其於循環與血管外膜中的數量大幅下降。值得注意的是，CD8+CD44+CD122+ Tregs 的過繼轉移可減緩動脈粥樣硬化的進程。基於上述發現，本計畫擬：目標一，檢視 CD8+ T 細胞在動脈粥樣硬化過程中如何驅動 VSMCs Notch 活性喪失；目標二，闡明 CD8+ Tregs／Notch 軸調控 VSMCs 行為以對抗動脈粥樣硬化的分子機制；目標三，評估提升／誘導 CD8+ Tregs 以對抗動脈粥樣硬化的治療潛力。綜合而言，我們的研究將揭示 CD8+ Tregs／Notch 軸作為治療動脈粥樣硬化性心血管疾病的新穎且具前景的治療靶點。

14119926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14119926.value: TRIP6 與 LILRB4 結合以促進結腸癌幹細胞的免疫逃逸，是增強大腸直腸癌免疫治療的治療標靶。

14119926.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14119926.value: Dr Chen, Huarong Dr Wong, Chi-chun

14119926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14119926.value: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the number one cancer in Hong Kong and second leading cause of cancer-related deaths. Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy has shown very promising efficacies in certain malignancies and in hypermutated cancers with microsatellite instability. However, a majority of CRC patients demonstrate intrinsic resistance to ICB therapy. Identification of therapeutic targets that sensitize CRC to ICB therapy is an unmet need. Colon cancer stem cells (CSCs) is a subpopulation of tumor cells considered as key players in chemoresistance, tumor relapse and metastasis in CRC. However, it is unclear whether CSCs might modulate antitumor immunity and its therapeutic implications. Single cell sequencing (scRNA-seq) revealed TRIP6 was enriched in LGR5+ CSCs. High TRIP6 expression was associated with stem-like signatures in CRC. We observed colon stem cell-specific Trip6 knockout (Trip6 cKO) attenuated carcinogen-induced CRC. scRNA-seq on whole tumors from WT and Trip6 cKO mice confirmed that Trip6 cKO decreased LGR5+ CSC frequencies. Primary CRC organoids isolated from Trip6 cKO mice showed suppressed self-renewal ability, cell proliferation, and cancer stemness features. Notably, a dramatic activation of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells was consistently observed in Trip6 cKO mice and TRIP6 knockdown xenografts in humanized mouse model. We further observed co-culture CSCs with or without TRIP6 knockdown and PBMCs derived naïve T cells significantly induced CD8+ T cell proliferation and activation, whereas their conditioned medium showed no effect. We thus inferred CSCs-specific TRIP6 induced suppression of CD8+ T cells through CSCs surface proteins. Mechanistically, immunoprecipitation followed by mass spectrometry identified transmembrane protein LILRB4 was the potential target for TRIP6 in CSCs. The direct interaction between TRIP6 and LILRB4 in CSCs was further confirmed by molecular docking and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assay. Furthermore, TRIP6 knockout in CSCs synergized anti-PD1 efficacy in PBMC- humanized mice. These results lend us to hypothesize that TRIP6 binds to LILRB4 to facilitate immune evasion of colon cancer stem cells and is a therapeutic target for boosting immunotherapy in CRC. To address this, we propose three objectives:1) to evaluate the function of CSCs-specific TRIP6 in driving cancer stemness and immunosuppression in colorectal tumorigenesis; 2) to elucidate the mechanism of TRIP6 binding to LILRB4 to mediate immune evasion of CSCs; and 3) to evaluate the synergy between targeting TRIP6-lLILRB4 axis and immune checkpoint therapy in CRC. The proposed study will unravel novel mechanisms for immune evasion of CSCs through TRIP6-lLILRB4 axis, which inform future approaches for CRC immunotherapy. 大腸直腸癌是香港發生率最高的癌症，也是導致癌症相關死亡的第二大原因。免疫檢查點阻斷療法在某些惡性腫瘤以及具有微衛星不穩定性的高突變癌症中顯示出極佳的療效。然而，大多數大腸直腸癌患者對免疫檢查點阻斷劑療法不敏感。尋找能使大腸直腸癌對免疫檢查點阻斷剂增敏的治療標靶，是目前亟需的臨床需求。結腸癌幹細胞（CSCs）是腫瘤細胞的一個亞群，被認為是大腸直腸癌化療抗藥性、腫瘤復發及轉移的關鍵驅動因素。然而，目前尚不清楚CSCs是否會調節抗腫瘤免疫及其相關的治療意義。單細胞測序結果顯示，TRIP6在LGR5+ CSCs中富集表現。在結直腸癌中，TRIP6的高表現與幹細胞樣特徵相關。我們觀察到，結腸幹細胞特異性敲除Trip6可減輕致癌劑誘導的結直腸癌發生。對野生型（WT）和Trip6 cKO小鼠的完整腫瘤進行單細胞定序證實，Trip6 cKO降低了LGR5+ CSCs的比例。Trip6 cKO小鼠的原代結直腸癌類器官表現出自我更新能力、細胞增殖及癌症乾性受抑制。在Trip6 cKO小鼠以及人源化小鼠模型中的TRIP6敲低異種移植瘤中，均觀察到細胞毒性CD8+ T細胞的顯著活化。進一步研究發現，將經TRIP6敲低處理或未處理的CSCs與源自外周血單核細胞（PBMC）的初始T細胞共培養，可顯著誘導CD8+ T細胞的增殖與活化，而其條件培養基則無此效應。我們推斷，CSCs特異性的TRIP6透過CSCs表面蛋白介導了對CD8+ T細胞的抑製作用。機轉研究方面，透過免疫沉澱合併質譜分析，鑑定出跨膜蛋白LILRB4是CSCs中TRIP6的潛在作用標靶。分子對接及表面等離子體共振（SPR）實驗進一步證實了CSCs中TRIP6與LILRB4之間存在直接交互作用。此外，在人源化週邊血單核細胞（PBMC）小鼠模型中，敲除結直腸癌幹細胞（CSC）中的 TRIP6 增強了抗 PD-1 療法的療效。這些結果提示我們：TRIP6 透過與 LILRB4 結合促進大腸直腸癌幹細胞的免疫逃逸，是增強大腸直腸癌（CRC）免疫療法的潛在治療標靶。為此，我們提出了以下三個研究目標：1) 評估 CSC 特異性 TRIP6 在結直腸癌發生過程中驅動癌乾性及免疫抑制的功能；2) 闡明 TRIP6 與 LILRB4 結合介導 CSC 免疫逃逸的機制；3) 評估靶向 TRIP6-LILRB4 軸與免疫檢查點療法在結直腸癌治療中的協同效應。本研究將揭示 CSC 透過 TRIP6-LILRB4 軸實現免疫逃脫的新機制，從而為大腸直腸癌免疫療法的未來策略提供理論基礎。

14120126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14120126.value: 復發性惡性心包積液之經皮球囊心包切開術治療：多國、多中心隨機臨床試驗

14120126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14120126.value: Prof Chan, Stephen Prof Wong, Hung-Leung Randolph Prof Yan, Bryan

14120126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14120126.value: Background Accumulation of excess fluid around the heart due to disseminated cancer (malignant pericardial effusion, MPE) is a common problem (up to 21%) that often recurs (up to 60%) and requires repeated pericardiocentesis (drainage of the pericardial fluid) and hospital admissions. Untreated, MPE can lead to cardiac tamponade by compressing the heart and impair its ability to pump blood. Traditionally, creation of an opening in the pericardium (sac around the heart) by open surgery allows excess fluid to drain safely into the abdominal or pleural cavity thus preventing re-accumulation. In our experience, the pericardial opening can be created using angioplasty balloon via minimally invasive approach (percutaneous balloon pericardiotomy, PBP) and we have demonstrated this approach is both safe and effective in reducing recurrent MPE in patients who presented with MPE for the first time. Whether PBP confers similar benefits in the setting of recurrent MPE compared with repeat pericardiocentesis is not established. This international, multicenter randomized trial aims to compare the safety, efficacy and cost-effectiveness of PBP with pericardiocentesis in preventing recurrent clinically significant MPE. Patients’ quality-of-life will be assessed. Method This is a multinational, multicenter, open-labelled, randomized pragmatic trial involving patients with significant recurrent MPE secondary to metastatic malignancy following initial pericardiocentesis. Eligible patients will be randomized 1:1 to PBP or repeat pericardiocentesis with extended pericardial drainage. The primary end point of the study will be the rate of recurrence of large pericardial effusion (defined as >20mm) at 3 months. Secondary outcomes include overall survival at 3 months, incidence of cardiac tamponade requiring emergency pericardiocentesis, tamponade-free survival at 3 months, and quality-of-life assessment. The primary safety endpoint is the occurrence of moderate or severe procedural-related complications. Cost-effectiveness in terms of incremental cost per pericardiocentesis avoided will be evaluated. Implications This study will be the first to demonstrate safety and efficacy of PBP for the treatment of recurrent MPE. Results of this study are likely to change clinical practice by establishing minimally invasive approach as first line treatment to prevent cardiac tamponade which is a life-threatening oncological emergency and recurrent MPE which is associated with substantial morbidity and impaired quality-of-life in cancer patients. The findings from this study will provide critical data to support the broader adoption of this treatment strategy in diverse patient populations and international guidelines. In our local context, this study will directly address the urgent need to reduce repeat admission and procedures for recurrent MPE. 摘要 目的 惡性心包積液（MPE）是癌症患者常見的併發症，發生率可達 21%，且復發率高達 60%，常需反覆心包穿刺及住院治療。若未治療，MPE 可導致心包填塞，造成生命威脅。傳統上，開放手術於心包製造小開口以引流液體，避免再度積聚。我們的經驗顯示，經皮球囊心包切開術（PBP）能以微創方式達成相同效果，並在首次 MPE 患者中證明安全有效。然而，PBP 在復發性 MPE 的療效與重複心包穿刺術相比仍未確立。本研究旨在比較 PBP 與心包穿刺術在復發性 MPE 的安全性、療效及成本效益，並評估患者生活品質。 方法 這是一項多國、多中心、開放標籤、隨機化的實用性臨床試驗，納入因轉移性惡性腫瘤導致顯著復發性 MPE 且已接受初次心包穿刺的患者。合資格患者將以 1:1 隨機分配至 PBP 或重複心包穿刺並延長心包引流。主要終點為 3 個月內大心包積液（>20mm）復發率。次要終點包括 3 個月整體存活率、需緊急心包穿刺的心包填塞發生率、3 個月無心包填塞存活率，以及以 FACT-G 問卷評估的生活品質。主要安全終點為中度或重度操作相關併發症。成本效益將以品質調整生命年（QALY）及避免重複心包穿刺的增量成本進行評估。 結果 本研究預期將首次提供 PBP 在復發性 MPE 治療中的安全性與有效性證據，並比較其與心包穿刺術在臨床結局及成本效益上的差異。 結論 研究結果有望改變臨床實踐，將微創方法建立為預防心包填塞及復發性 MPE 的首選治療。此策略不僅能改善癌症患者的生活品質，亦可減少住院及重複操作的需求，並為國際臨床指引提供關鍵數據支持。

14120726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14120726.value: 剪接因子 SF3B4 的細胞間轉移活化癌症相關成纖維細胞並促進肝細胞癌進展的機制研究

14120726.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14120726.value: Prof Ding, XiaoFan Dr Li, Linxian Prof Wong, Nathalie

14120726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14120726.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) exploits dysregulated alternative splicing to drive tumor progression, yet how spliceosomal components influence the tumor microenvironment remains poorly understood. Our recent genome-wide CRISPR screen in HCC organoids identified Splicing factor 3B subunit 4 (SF3B4) as a critical splicing factor essential for HCC progression (Science Advances, 2025). In the present study, we extend this investigation beyond tumor-intrinsic mechanisms to explore how SF3B4 impacts the tumor microenvironment in HCC. Intriguingly, we discovered that SF3B4 is secreted from HCC cells via extracellular vesicles (EVs) and transferred intercellularly to cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs). CAFs are key stromal components that mediate immune interactions, remodel the extracellular matrix, and promote tumor progression in HCC. Transferred SF3B4 induces a pro-tumorigenic phenotype in CAFs, characterized by increased proliferation, enhanced invasiveness, and elevated tumor-promoting capacity in co-culture with HCC organoids. Consistently, elevated serum SF3B4 levels are associated with CAF enrichment in matched HCC tumors. Mechanistically, we found that SF3B4 is a transcriptional target of TP53-R249S, the most common TP53 missense mutation in HCC. Further analyses revealed that HCC tumors harboring TP53 missense mutations exhibit higher SF3B4 levels and increased sensitivity to spliceosome inhibition, revealing a genotype-specific therapeutic vulnerability. Prompted by these findings, we developed antisense oligonucleotide-loaded lipid nanoparticles (ASO-LNPs) that combine isoform-specific modulation with enhanced stability and liver-targeted delivery. As a proof of concept, we validated ASO-LNPs targeting TBX3+2a, an oncogenic splice variant regulated by SF3B4 in HCC cells. These nanoparticles achieved isoform-specific knockdown and significantly suppressed the growth of HCC organoids, with enhanced efficacy in the TP53-mutant genetic background. In the current proposal, we aim to (1) elucidate the molecular composition of SF3B4-enriched EVs and evaluate the function and clinical relevance of secreted SF3B4 in HCC, (2) define SF3B4-driven oncogenic splicing events in CAFs, and (3) assess the therapeutic efficacy of ASO-LNPs targeting SF3B4-dependent splicing variants, particularly in TP53-mutant HCC. Collectively, this study will reveal a previously unrecognized extracellular role for a splicing factor in the tumor microenvironment and lay the foundation for splicing-directed therapy in HCC.

14120926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14120926.value: 細菌微生物組、EBV及宿主基因組學在鼻咽癌免疫治療中的作用

14120926.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14120926.value: Prof Chen, Zigui Dr Stephanie, Wong

14120926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14120926.value: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is an Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV)-driven malignancy prevalent in Southern China and Southeast Asia, and often diagnosed at advanced stages. Although neoadjuvant chemotherapy and chemoradiotherapy enhance NPC survival, complete responses are limited, toxicity is high, and immunotherapy responding to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) shows modest efficacy due to an immunosuppressive tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). Bacterial microbiomes contribute to carcinogenesis and therapy resistance in various cancers, yet in NPC, microbiota dysbiosis and the oral-to-nasopharyngeal translocation, as well as their interactions with EBV and immune responses remain poorly characterized, hindering biomarker development and strategies to augment ICI efficacy. Our preliminary investigation uncovered site-specific microbiota (across the nasopharynx, oral and gut) and pronounced nasopharyngeal dysbiosis in NPC, marked by increased microbial heterogeneity and enrichment of 15 bacterial species compared to controls. A unidirectional oral-to-nasopharyngeal translocation unique to NPC was observed, stratifying patients into high- and low-translocation (NPC^H vs NPC^L) subgroups. Notably, NPC-enriched taxa such as Pseudoprevotella muciniphila and Fusobacterium periodonticum were prominent in NPC^H, yielding high diagnostic accuracy. EBV quantification revealed near-universal positivity in NPC (91%) with correlations to five translocation-linked bacteria, suggesting microbial modulation of viral load. In vitro assay co-cultured F. periodonticum in EBV+ NPC cells showed upregulated immunosuppressive markers like INHBA and PD-L1, consistent with our observation of similar bacterial influences in oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) models, including NF-κB/STAT1 pathway activation, elevated checkpoints (e.g., PD-L1, CTLA4), matrix remodeling, Treg regulators, and reduced CD8+ T-cell activity. These findings indicate that translocation-driven dysbiosis may interact with EBV to foster an NPC TIME, supporting the need for targeted exploration to overcome ICI resistance. We hypothesize that dysbiotic oral microbiota translocate to the nasopharynx, promoting EBV-driven immune dysregulation and ICI resistance in NPC, and that targeting these factors will enhance therapeutic responses. To test this, we will: (1) Quantify translocation and microbial features in NPC patients to identify bacterial signatures and biomarkers associated with EBV and clinical outcomes; (2) Elucidate microbiota-EBV-immune crosstalk via integrated transcriptomic profiling in NPC patient subsets, mapping networks for resistance prediction; (3) Assess immunomodulatory effects of translocated dysbiotic bacteria (e.g., F. periodonticum) on ICI responses in NPC using in vitro and in vivo models, evaluating TME remodeling with interventions combined with ICIs. This prospective study will deliver novel translocation biomarkers, crosstalk networks, and evidence for microbiome modulation, enabling prediction of ICI responses and innovative adjunctive therapies to improve outcomes in NPC populations. 鼻咽癌（NPC）是一種由EB病毒（EBV）驅動的惡性腫瘤，盛行於華南與東南亞地區，且確診時通常已屆晚期。儘管新輔助化療與化學放射治療能提升 NPC 的存活率，但完全緩解率有限且毒性偏高；此外，由於腫瘤免疫微環境（TIME）具有免疫抑制特性，針對免疫檢查點抑制劑（ICIs）的免疫治療療效僅算差強人意。細菌微生物組在多種癌症中會促進癌變與治療抗性。然而，在 NPC 中，微生物菌群失調、口腔至鼻咽的菌群易位（translocation），以及它們與 EBV 和免疫反應之間的交互作用仍未被充分了解，這阻礙了生物標記的開發與提升 ICI 療效的策略。 我們的初步研究發現了特定部位的微生物群（涵蓋鼻咽、口腔與腸道），並觀察到 NPC 患者具有明顯的鼻咽菌群失調；與對照組相比，其特徵為微生物異質性增加，且有 15 種細菌物種顯著富集。我們也觀察到 NPC 特有的「口腔至鼻咽單向菌群易位」現象，並藉此將患者分層為高易位（NPC^H）與低易位（NPC^L）亞群。值得注意的是，在 NPC 中富集的分類群（如 Pseudoprevotella muciniphila 與 Fusobacterium periodonticum）在 NPC^H 亞群中尤為突出，並具備極高的診斷準確率。EBV 定量分析顯示，NPC 患者呈現近乎全面的陽性率（91%），且與五種易位相關的細菌具有相關性，表明微生物可能會調節病毒載量。 在體外試驗中，將 F. periodonticum 與 EBV 陽性 NPC 細胞共培養，結果顯示 INHBA 與 PD-L1 等免疫抑制標記物上調。這與我們在口腔鱗狀細胞癌（OSCC）模型中觀察到相似細菌影響的結果一致，包含 NF-κB/STAT1 途徑活化、檢查點（如 PD-L1、CTLA4）升高、基質重塑、調節性 T 細胞（Treg）調節因子增加，以及 CD8+ T 細胞活性降低。這些發現指出，由易位驅動的菌群失調可能會與 EBV 產生交互作用，進而促成 NPC 的腫瘤免疫微環境，這支持了為克服 ICI 抗性而進行標靶探索的必要性。 我們假設，失調的口腔微生物群易位至鼻咽，促進了 NPC 中 EBV 驅動的免疫失調與 ICI 抗性；而針對這些因素進行干預將能提升治療反應。為了驗證此假設，我們將執行以下步驟： (1) 定量 NPC 患者的易位現象與微生物特徵，以鑑定與 EBV 及臨床預後相關的細菌特徵與生物標記； (2) 透過對 NPC 患者亞群進行整合轉錄組分析，闡明微生物群、EBV與免疫系統間的交互作用，並繪製用於抗性預測的網絡圖； (3) 使用體內與體外模型，評估易位的失調細菌（例如 F. periodonticum）對 NPC 之中 ICI 反應的免疫調節作用，並評估結合 ICI 干預措施後的腫瘤微環境（TME）重塑情形。 這項前瞻性研究將提供新穎的易位生物標記、交互網絡圖，以及微生物組調節的相關證據，從而有助於預測 ICI 反應，並催生創新的輔助療法，以改善 NPC 族群的治療預後。

14121926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14121926.value: 解碼基因調控密碼：基於可解釋多組學方法挖掘癌症驅動基因

14121926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14121926.value: The precise control of gene expression is fundamental to cellular identity, and its dysregulation is a hallmark of cancer. While many individual regulatory components have been cataloged, a central question in biology is how these multi-layered mechanisms are integrated to establish gene expression programs. Progress has been hampered by two key limitations in computational modeling. First, as current studies focus on only one or a few mechanisms at a time, the field’s understanding of the complete regulatory landscape remains fragmented. Second, current methods often force a difficult trade-off between predictive accuracy and interpretability. Simpler models are transparent but lack power, while powerful black-box models are hard to interpret. This severely limits the ability to decipher the complete regulatory code and efficiently pinpoint novel cancer-driving regulatory mechanisms. Building upon our work GEEK in modeling gene regulation (Nature Machine Intelligence, 2020), this project will overcome these barriers by developing and applying GEEK2. GEEK2 is designed as a scalable and interpretable framework to integrate large-scale, heterogeneous, multi-omic data, simultaneously modeling most, if not all, known regulatory mechanisms. Its innovative architecture automatically identifies the dominant regulatory mechanisms (i.e., regulatory codes) that drive gene expression. Our strong preliminary data demonstrate that GEEK2 not only identifies both canonical and higher-order regulatory codes, validating its interpretability, but also achieves state-of-the-art predictive accuracy (Pearson correlation coefficient > 0.85). Crucially, GEEK2’s predictions from in silico perturbation for both a known immune axis and a paradoxical tumor suppressor in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) have been validated by biological experiments, providing a robust proof-of-concept. Upon this foundation, we will systematically apply GEEK2 to extensive bulk and single-cell multi-omic datasets to model their regulatory mechanisms. By performing this integrative modeling, we will define the fundamental predictive limits of gene expression and create a comprehensive atlas of regulatory codes across diverse human cell types. We will then leverage GEEK2 as a predictive engine to perform systematic in silico perturbations in cancer, generating a prioritized list of high-impact candidate regulatory drivers. Finally, in a tight computation-to-validation loop, we will experimentally validate the top candidate drivers for HCC using CRISPR-based technologies to uncover novel, cancer-driving mechanisms. This project will deliver transformative public resources: the atlas of regulatory codes and an open-source GEEK2 framework. By identifying and validating novel regulatory circuits driving cancer, our work will reveal fundamental rules of gene regulation and uncover new therapeutic targets, to ultimately inform precision oncology strategies. 基因表達的精確調控是決定細胞特性的基礎，而其調控失常是癌症的標誌性特徵。儘管目前已鑑定出許多獨立的調控元件，但生物學面臨的一個核心問題是：這些多層次的機制是如何協同整合以建立基因表達程序的。然而，計算建模領域的兩大核心局限阻礙了這一研究進展。首先，當前研究通常一次僅關注一種或少數幾種調控機制，導致學界對完整調控網絡的認知仍處於碎片化狀態。其次，現有方法往往難以兼顧預測準確性與模型可解釋性：簡單模型雖然透明但預測效能不足，而「黑盒」模型又缺乏可解釋性。這限制了我們解碼完整調控密碼以及高效定位新型癌症驅動機制的能力。 基於我們前期在基因調控建模領域的研究基礎（即2020年發表於《自然·機器智能》的GEEK模型），本項目將通過開發和應用全新框架GEEK2來突破上述瓶頸。GEEK2被設計為一個兼具高可擴展性和可解釋性的分析框架，能夠整合大規模、高度異質性的多組學數據，並對已知的大多數甚至全部調控機制進行同步建模。其模型架構能自動識別驅動特定基因表達的主導調控機制（即「調控密碼」）。預實驗數據表明，GEEK2能夠識別經典及高階調控密碼，體現了其可解釋性，並取得了良好的預測準確度（皮爾遜相關係數大於0.85）。此外，針對肝細胞癌中的已知免疫軸及非典型腫瘤抑制因子，GEEK2基於電腦模擬擾動得出的預測結果得到了生物學實驗的驗證，證明了模型的可行性。 在此基礎上，我們將系統性地把GEEK2應用於大規模的常規組織及單細胞多組學數據集，以深入模擬其內在調控機制。通過這種整合建模，我們將界定基因表達預測的基本極限，並構建出一個涵蓋多種人類細胞類型的全面調控密碼圖譜。隨後，我們將依託GEEK2這一預測引擎，在癌症數據中開展系統性的電腦模擬擾動，從而生成一份具有高優先級的候選調控驅動因子列表。最後，在緊密的「計算預測-實驗驗證」閉環中，我們將利用基因編輯技術，對排名前列的肝細胞癌候選驅動因子進行實驗驗證，以期揭示新的癌症驅動機制。 本項目將產出極具價值的公共資源：全面的調控密碼圖譜以及開源的GEEK2軟件框架。通過識別並驗證驅動癌症的新型調控迴路，我們的工作將進一步揭示基因調控的底層法則，發現新的治療靶點，最終為精準腫瘤學策略的制定提供科學依據。

14124026.value: 用於研究卵巢子宮內膜異位症相關不孕症細胞與分子機制及治療標靶的小鼠子宮內膜異位囊腫模型

14124026.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14124026.value: Prof Chung, Pui Wah Jacqueline Dr Hung, Sze Wan Kennes Prof Zhang, Tao

14124026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14124026.value: Endometriosis is a chronic disorder characterized by implantation of endometrium outside uterine cavity. Endometrioma is the most common subtype of endometriosis in ovaries, it affects many women in reproductive age and is the leading cause of infertility. Surgery to remove the endometriotic lesions from the affected ovaries is a common infertility treatment for endometrioma. However the surgical treatment is invasive and costly, it may also remove the underlining follicles, thus further limit the ovarian reserve. In addition, subsequent assisted reproductive treatment may be needed due to the less adequate number and low quality of oocytes available for successful pregnancy. The underlying mechanism of endometrioma-associated infertility on how the endometriotic lesions affect the follicle development and oocyte quality in the ovary remains unclear. Technical issue to obtain both endometriotic and ovarian tissues intact, and also ethical issue to collect additional ovarian tissues from patients with already low ovarian reserve for study are the major limitations. In our pilot studies, we reviewed the impacts of endometrioma in ovarian aging (Front Endocrin 2023, 13: e1073261, doi:10.3389/fendo.2022.1073261), compared various animal models for endometrioma (Biomedicines 2022, 10(7);e1483, doi:10.3390/biomedicines10071483) and then successfully established a unique mouse model of endometrioma in which the endometriotic lesion was only engrafted and grown in ovary, showing characteristic pathology of chocolate cyst-like and impaired folliculogenesis as endometrioma in human (J Vis Exp 2024, 5: e206), doi:10.3791/6624, and video). In this study, we will use the established endometrioma mouse model to characterise the effects of ovarian endometriosis on the follicle development, to dissect the cellular and molecular mechanism of endometrioma-associated infertility, and to identify and evaluate the therapeutic targets of endometrioma-associated infertility in the ovary. The results of this study will provide scientific insights to the infertility due to the ovarian endometriosis for potential clinical translations and therapeutic applications. 關於子宮內膜異位囊腫（卵巢子宮內膜異位症）如何影響卵巢內卵泡發育及卵母細胞質量，進而導致不孕的潛在機制，目前尚不明確。研究面臨的主要限制在於：在技術層面上，難以完整取得子宮內膜異位病灶及卵巢組織；在倫理層面上，難以從卵巢儲備功能已低下的患者體內採集額外的卵巢組織用於研究。 本研究將利用已建立的子宮內膜異位囊腫小鼠模型，闡明卵巢子宮內膜異位症對卵泡發育的影響，解析子宮內膜異位囊腫相關不孕的細胞與分子機制，並識別與評估針對該類不孕症的卵巢治療靶點。本研究結果將為理解卵巢子宮內膜異位症導致的不孕症提供科學依據，並為未來的臨床轉化及治療應用奠定基礎。

14124326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14124326.value: 利用基於多光子的空間微圖案化技術在體外重現與操控平面細胞極性

14124326.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14124326.value: Prof Chan, Michael Chi Wai Prof Gao, Bo Prof Liu, Pengtao

14124326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14124326.value: Planar cell polarity (PCP) is essential for coordinated orientation of epithelial and mesenchymal cells and is critical for tissue morphogenesis and function. Disruption of PCP leads to developmental defects and pathologies including congenital malformation and impaired organ function. Most PCP studies rely on in vivo models, which, while informative, are limited by complexity, and difficulty in dissecting casual mechanisms. PCP regulation is highly complex, with multiple niche factors as extracellular signals implicated; among these, Wnt5a has emerged as a key non-canonical Wnt ligand and candidate global cue for PCP alignment. However, its mechanistic role remains unclear due to the absence of in vitro system capable of generating stable and spatially defined gradient. To address the scientific and technological gaps, we have developed, a multiphoton microfabrication and micropatterning (MMM) platform, which can fabricate protein-based microstructures with sub-micron features, enabling immobilization of bioactive proteins and precise control over mechanical properties, surface topology, extracellular matrix composition, and localized signaling cues. Critically, MMM allows niche factors to be independently tuned and decoupled, making it possible to dissect their individual and combined contributions to cell behavior. With this platform, bioactive morphogens can be immobilized in a sustained and functional form. Here, using MMM capability, we aim to generate stable, bioactive Wnt5a gradients on protein microstructures for in vitro PCP studies. Our preliminary data demonstrated that Wnt5a can be quantitatively and spatially micropatterned on protein substrates, forming gradients of immobilized Wnt5a (iWnt5a), which was also found bioactive. Most importantly, initial evidence showing that iWnt5a gradient can direct Vangl1 asymmetry in human bronchial epithelial cells (HBECs), suggesting the feasibility to establish a robust in vitro model for PCP. This proposal aims to expand on these findings by investigating how Wnt5a gradients regulate PCP in epithelial and mesenchymal cells and coordinate PCP-driven function at tissue level. We hypothesize that stable, bioactive Wnt5a gradient act as directional cue that may control orientation or magnitude of PCP, which is interpreted through defined molecular signatures, and ultimately drive functional consequences. To test this hypothesis, we will pursue three integrated aims: (1) define and optimize Wnt5a gradient geometry controlling PCP (2) map the spatial signaling logic by which Wnt5a gradients are translated into PCP orientation, and (3) determine the functional consequences of Wnt5a‑driven PCP alternation at tissue‑level behaviors. Together, these studies will provide mechanistic insights into PCP regulation and establish a versatile platform for studying morphogen-guided tissue patterning. 平面細胞極性 (PCP) 對於細胞的協調定向至關重要，並且對組織形態發生和功能起著關鍵作用。 PCP 的破壞會導致發育缺陷和病理，包括先天性畸形和器官功能障礙。大多數 PCP 研究都是透過體內模型進行的，雖然這些模型能夠提供有價值的信息，但由於其複雜性以及難以解析其內在機制，因此存在一定的局限性。 PCP 的調控機制非常複雜，涉及多種微環境因子；其中，Wnt5a 已成為一種關鍵的非經典 Wnt 配體，並被認為是 PCP 排列的候選全局訊號。然而，由於缺乏能夠產生穩定且空間明確的梯度的體外系統，其機製作用仍不清楚。 為了彌補這些科學和技術上的不足，我們開發了一種多光子微加工和微圖案化 (MMM) 平台，該平台能夠製造具有亞微米級特徵的蛋白質微結構，從而實現生物活性蛋白的固定，並精確控制其機械性能、表面形貌、細胞外基質組成和局部信號傳導。至關重要的是，生物活性形態發生素可以以持久且功能性的形式固定。 在此，我們利用微分子膜（MMM）旨在在蛋白質微結構上生成穩定的、具有生物活性的Wnt5a梯度，用於體外蛋白質複合物（PCP）研究。 目標1 – 確定並優化控制PCP的Wnt5a梯度幾何結構 目標2 – 從空間上繪製將Wnt5a梯度轉化為PCP取向的分子機制 目標3 – 測試Wnt5a驅動的PCP排列的功能後果

14125126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14125126.value: Mst1介導腎臟保護的YAP/TAZ之外的新機制

14125126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14125126.value: Acute kidney injury (AKI) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) are major health problems. AKI affects up to 20% of all hospitalized patients. CKD affects around 11% of the population worldwide. Renal tubular epithelial cells constitute more than 90% of the kidney mass and play a key role in orchestrating renal inflammation and fibrosis. Mst1 and Mst2 are highly homologous St20-like serine/threonine kinases, and they share similar functions. Within the canonical Mst1/2 pathway, Mst1/2 serve as the catalytic core of the Hippo signaling cascade, which promotes phosphorylation and degradation of the transcriptional coactivators YAP and TAZ, thereby inhibiting cell proliferation. Several non-canonical Mst1/2 pathways including those involving FoxO1 and FoxO3 have been identified that can either induce or suppress cell apoptosis in a context-dependent manner. Our previous work demonstrated that tubule-specific knockout of both Mst1 and Mst2 activates YAP in renal tubules, leading to spontaneous kidney injury in mice. In contrast, our new results show that tubule-specific deletion of 3 alleles of the Mst1/2 genes did not activate YAP/TAZ at baseline and caused only slight activation after unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO). Furthermore, tubule-specific deletion of Mst1 failed to activate YAP/TAZ under either condition. These findings indicate that intrinsic protective mechanisms tightly restrict YAP/TAZ activation in response to Mst1/2 deficiency in the kidney. Notably, tubule-specific ablation of Mst1 promoted tubular cell apoptosis and renal fibrosis induced by UUO. Under hypoxic or serum starvation conditions in vitro, Mst1 knockdown promoted tubular cell apoptosis and activated FoxD3, FoxN1, and NFAT5, without altering FoxO1/FoxO3 activities or YAP/TAZ phosphorylation. In addition, during kidney injury, Mst1 protein was drastically upregulated and its polyubiquitination was decreased, even though Mst1 mRNA levels remained unchanged. We therefore hypothesize that during kidney injury, the inhibition of Mst1 polyubiquitination stabilizes the Mst1 protein, which in turn protects against tubular cell apoptosis and renal fibrosis via YAP/TAZ-independent mechanisms. To test this hypothesis, we will 1) determine the impacts of tubule-specific deletion of two Mst1/2 alleles on YAP/TAZ phosphorylation and kidney injury; 2) investigate the role and mechanisms of action of Mst1 in tubular cell apoptosis; and 3) determine the mechanisms underlying the increased Mst1 protein stability during kidney injury. Our results could advance the understanding of kidney disease pathogenesis and contribute to novel therapeutic development. 急性腎損傷（AKI）和慢性腎臟病（CKD）是主要的健康問題。急性腎損傷影響高達20%的住院患者，而慢性腎臟病則影響全球約11%的人口。腎小管上皮細胞占腎臟質量的90%以上，在調控腎臟炎症和纖維化中發揮關鍵作用。Mst1和Mst2是高度同源的Ste20樣絲氨酸/蘇氨酸激酶，具有相似的功能。在經典的Mst1/2通路中，Mst1/2作為Hippo信號級聯的催化核心，促進轉錄激活因子YAP和TAZ的磷酸化及降解，從而抑制細胞增殖。此外，還發現了幾種包括FoxO1和FoxO3在內的非經典Mst1/2通路，這些通路在不同條件下可誘導或抑制細胞凋亡。我們先前的研究表明，腎小管特異性同時敲除Mst1和Mst2會激活腎小管中的YAP，導致小鼠發生自發性腎損傷。我們現在的新結果顯示，腎小管特異性缺失Mst1/2基因的3個等位基因在基礎條件下並未激活YAP/TAZ，僅在單側輸尿管梗阻（UUO）後引起輕度激活。此外，腎小管特異性缺失Mst1在兩種條件下均未能激活YAP/TAZ。這些發現表明，腎臟中內在的保護機制嚴格限制了對Mst1/2缺失的YAP/TAZ激活反應。值得注意的是，腎小管特異性敲除Mst1促進了UUO誘導的腎小管細胞凋亡和腎纖維化。在體外低氧或血清飢餓條件下，Mst1敲低促進了腎小管細胞凋亡，並激活了FoxD3、FoxN1和NFAT5，但不改變FoxO1/FoxO3活性或YAP/TAZ磷酸化水平。此外，在腎損傷過程中，儘管Mst1 mRNA水平保持不變，Mst1蛋白顯著上調，其泛素化水平降低。因此，我們提出假設：在腎損傷過程中，Mst1泛素化的抑制穩定了Mst1蛋白，進而通過不依賴YAP/TAZ的機制保護腎小管細胞免於凋亡並抗腎纖維化。為驗證這一假設，我們將：1）確定腎小管特異性缺失兩個Mst1/2等位基因對YAP/TAZ磷酸化和腎損傷的影響；2）探討Mst1在腎小管細胞凋亡中的作用及其機制；3）闡明腎損傷過程中Mst1蛋白穩定性增加的機制。我們的研究結果有望加深對腎臟疾病發病機制的理解，並促進新型治療方法的開發。

14125226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14125226.value: 玉米葉片表觀基因組圖譜的單細胞多組學分析

14125226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14125226.value: The establishment of cell-specific gene expression programs is critically dependent upon histone modifications and the accessibility of promoter chromatin. But a major barrier in plant epigenomics is the lack of a robust method for simultaneous multi-omics profiling at single-cell resolution. Existing technologies, reliant on microfluidic chips optimized for mammalian cells, perform poorly with plant nuclei due to low RNA capture efficiency, aggregation, and high cost. We propose to develop a microfluidics-free single-cell multi-omics platform for simultaneous profiling of chromatin accessibility (scATAC-seq) with histone modifications (scCUT&Tag), and transcriptome (snRNA-seq) in the maize leaf, and apply the new metacell analysis strategy to solve the complex regulatory landscape of its C4 photosynthetic genes. We have performed successful pilot experiments to test the feasibility of the proposed microfluidic-free single-cell platform. We obtained high-quality scATAC-seq data with robust cell clustering in different maize and Arabidopsis tissues. Additionally, we have developed a reversible hydrogel encapsulation strategy to prevent nuclei aggregation after ATAC-seq, which enabled us to use scCUT&Tag to profile histone modification H3K4me3 after the scATAC-seq. Furthermore, we have developed an in situ RT-PCR conditions for maize nuclei, enabling efficient cDNA synthesis and laying the groundwork for integrating snRNA-seq to our joint profiling platform. The key objectives of our proposal are: 1) Expand the platform to profile functionally distinct histone marks, such as H3K27me3, which is known to regulate C4 photosynthetic genes in maize. 2) Continue to develop the snRNA-seq methodology based on in situ RT-PCR, and integrate it with scATAC-seq workflow using droplet PCR barcoding. 3) Co-assay chromatin accessibility, histone modifications, and gene expression in the maize leaf, and use metacell analysis to reveal the multi-layer regulatory mechanism controlling C4 genes. We are confident that this scalable, cost-efficient, and robust method will overcome the limitations of existing microfluidic-based single-cell technologies. We will apply it to solve a central question in biology: deciphering the cell-type-specific epigenetic and transcriptional regulation of C4 photosynthesis, which has both scientific and agricultural impact. 細胞特異性基因表達程序的建立，高度依賴於組蛋白修飾與啟動子染色質的開放性。然而，缺乏高穩定性的單細胞分辨率多組學同步分析方法，一直是植物表觀基因組學研究的主要瓶頸。現有技術多依賴針對哺乳動物細胞優化的微流控晶片，用於植物細胞核時常面臨 RNA 捕獲效率低、細胞核凝集及成本昂貴等問題。為此，本計畫擬開發一種免微流控單細胞多組學平台，實現植物染色質開放性（scATAC-seq）、組蛋白修飾（scCUT&Tag）及轉錄組（snRNA-seq）的同步剖析，並結合新型 Metacell 分析策略，解析玉米 C4 光合作用的複雜調控圖景。 前期預實驗已證實該平台的可行性：我們在玉米與擬南芥不同組織中成功獲得高質量的 scATAC-seq 數據並實現穩健的細胞分群；開發了可逆水凝膠包埋策略以防止 ATAC-seq 後的細胞核凝集，進而成功在 scATAC-seq 後接續進行 H3K4me3 的 scCUT&Tag 檢測；此外，我們已優化玉米細胞核的原位 RT-PCR 條件，實現高效 cDNA 合成，為整合 snRNA-seq 奠定了堅實基礎。 本計畫的核心目標包括： 擴展平台能力：剖析具不同功能特性的組蛋白修飾（如已知調控 C4 光合作用基因的 H3K27me3）； 整合技術流程：基於原位 RT-PCR 繼續完善 snRNA-seq 方法，並利用液滴 PCR 條碼技術將其與 scATAC-seq 工作流無縫整合； 解析 C4 光合作用：應用該系統全面剖析玉米葉片的染色質開放性、組蛋白修飾及基因表達，揭示控制 C4 光合作用的多層次調控機制。 此具高度擴展性、高成本效益且穩健的新方法，將突破現有微流控技術的局限，為解密 C4 光合作用的細胞特異性表觀遺傳與轉錄調控提供關鍵工具，兼具深厚的科學意義與農業應用價值。

14125426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14125426.value: 平面細胞極性基因在先天性椎骨畸形中的作用

14125426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14125426.value: Congenital vertebral malformations (CVMs) are structural defects of the spine that arise during early embryogenesis. Uneven growth of malformed vertebrae can lead to congenital scoliosis (CS), a severe, early-onset spinal curvature that often requires complex surgery. While several genes involved in somite development have been implicated in the pathogenesis of CS, most cases remain unexplained, and the frequent co-occurrence of CS with neural tube defects suggests a shared developmental mechanism. Planar cell polarity (PCP) is a conserved pathway that orients cells within the plane of a tissue and is essential for somite development and neural tube closure. Building on our recent multi-center study identifying rare risk variants in core PCP genes VANGL1 and VANGL2 (PNAS 2024), we hypothesize that disruption of PCP signaling, alone or together with prenatal environmental factors, accounts for a substantial subset of human CVMs. In this project, we further identified rare compound heterozygous variants in the core PCP gene CELSR2 and in the global PCP module gene DCHS1 across multiple CS families, further expanding the genetic spectrum of CS. Our preliminary data of functional analyses support their roles in vertebral malformation. To address our hypothesis, we will first expand our family-based whole-genome analyses in an enlarged Hong Kong CS cohort to define the spectrum of risk variants across PCP signaling components and discover additional genes. We will then delineate the molecular consequences of CELSR2 and DCHS1 variants by assessing protein stability, cell-surface presentation, and assembly of PCP complex at cell junctions. Lastly, we will assess the pathogenicity of these variants in animal models and human organoids. The established human axial organoids that co-model somite and neural tube development will provide a rapid, human-relevant system to test patient variants and their interactions with environmental factors. This study will advance our understanding of CS etiology, thereby improving genetic diagnosis and prenatal risk assessment for this birth defect. 先天性椎骨畸形（congenital vertebral malformations, CVMs）是胚胎發育早期形成的脊柱結構缺陷。畸形椎骨的不均衡生長可導致先天性脊柱側彎（congenital scoliosis, CS），這是一種嚴重的早發性脊柱彎曲，患者往往需要接受複雜的外科手術。儘管多個參與體節發育的基因已被證實與先天性脊柱側彎的發病機制相關，但大多數病例的病因仍未明確。此外，先天性脊柱側彎經常與神經管缺陷同時出現，提示兩者可能具有共同的發育機制。 平面細胞極性（planar cell polarity, PCP）是一條高度保守的訊號通路，負責調控細胞在組織平面內的定向排列，並在體節形成及神經管閉合過程中發揮關鍵作用。基於我們近期的一項多中心研究，該研究發現核心PCP基因 VANGL1 和 VANGL2 中的罕見風險變異與先天性脊柱側彎相關（PNAS, 2024），我們提出假說：PCP訊號異常單獨作用，或與產前環境因素共同作用，是相當一部分人類先天性椎骨畸形的致病原因。 在本項目中，我們進一步在多個先天性脊柱側彎家系中發現PCP基因 CELSR2 及 DCHS1 的罕見複合雜合變異，進一步擴展了先天性脊柱側彎的遺傳變異譜。我們初步的功能分析結果亦支持這些基因變異在椎骨畸形形成中的作用。 為驗證上述假說，我們首先將在擴大的香港先天性脊柱側彎隊列中開展以家系為基礎的全基因組分析，以界定PCP訊號通路相關基因的風險變異譜，並鑑定新的致病基因。其次，我們將通過評估蛋白質穩定性、細胞表面定位，以及PCP蛋白複合體在細胞連接處的組裝，闡明 CELSR2 和 DCHS1 變異所造成的分子及細胞功能異常。最後，我們將利用動物模型和人源類器官評估這些變異的致病性。我們已建立能夠同時模擬體節及神經管發育的人源軸向類器官，該模型將提供一個快速且更貼近人類發育的研究平台，用於檢測患者變異的功能及其與環境因素之間的相互作用。本研究將深化我們對先天性脊柱側彎病因及發病機制的理解，從而提升這類出生缺陷的遺傳診斷能力及產前風險評估水平。

14200126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14200126.value: 針對特殊約束結構優化問題的誤差界方法：理論、方法與應用

14200126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200126.value: The notion of error bounds is known to play a fundamentally powerful role in mathematical programming with equilibrium constraints, a challenging class of constrained optimization problems. More recently, error bounds were employed in constant-modulus constrained optimization problems and were found to provide effective algorithmic solutions and elegant theory for a wide class of such problems. In this proposed project, we aim to expand on the aforementioned success to explore a variety of important constrained optimization problems that arise in signal processing, communications, and machine learning. The scope of our study includes bounded integer constraints, sparsity constraints, low-rank matrix constraints, and non-convex quadratic constraints, as well as their combined or generalized forms. They are relevant to applications such as model compression of deep learning models, MIMO detection, compressive sensing and sparse recovery, joint resource allocation and MIMO beamforming optimization of wireless networks, to name a few. This project aims to investigate the theory, methods, and applications of the error bound technique. We will explore the potential of the error bound technique in specific applications, studying how error bounds can leverage application-specific constraint structures, how that leads to application-customized effective algorithms, and how they work in practice and bring merits to the applications through thorough numerical experiments. In parallel we will study the common threads that underlie the applications, seeking to uncover the bigger reasons behind and to establish a framework for a class of constrained optimization problems—which could bring us to a richer scope of applications. The proposed research sets out to provide long-term benefits by advancing an important type of optimization techniques, providing current and future research with new insights and tools to tackle challenging problems in different applications. 誤差界（error bounds）的概念在帶均衡約束的數學規劃（mathematical programming with equilibrium constraints）中發揮着重要而強大的基礎作用；此類問題亦是一類極具挑戰性的約束優化問題。近期的研究進一步將誤差界應用於恆模（constant-modulus）約束優化問題，並發現它能為該類廣泛的問題提供有效的算法解決方案與優雅的理論支撑。本研究計劃擬在上述成果的基礎上進一步拓展，探討一系列源於信號處理、通訊及機器學習的重要約束優化問題。本研究的範圍包括有界整數約束（bounded integer constraints）、稀疏性約束（sparsity constraints）、低秩矩陣約束（low-rank matrix constraints）及非凸二次約束（non-convex quadratic constraints），以及這些約束的組合形式和廣義形式。這些約束與多項重要應用密切相關，包括深度學習模型壓縮、多輸入多輸出（MIMO）檢測、壓縮感知與稀疏恢復，以及無線網絡中的聯合資源分配與 MIMO 波束成形優化等。本研究計劃旨在從理論、方法及應用三方面深入研究誤差界技術。我們將探討誤差界技術在特定應用中的潛力，包括研究如何利用不同應用所特有的約束結構建立誤差界、如何以此設計針對具體應用的高效算法，以及這些算法在實際運作中的表現，並透過全面的數值實驗評估其為相關應用所帶來的效益。與此同時，我們亦將研究不同應用之間的共通脈絡，力求揭示其背後更具普遍性的原理，並為一類約束優化問題建立統一的研究框架，從而有望將有關方法拓展至更廣泛的應用領域。本研究期望透過推進這一重要類型的優化技術，帶來長遠的學術及應用價值，並為當前及未來的研究提供新的見解與工具，以應對不同應用領域中的具挑戰性問題。

14200426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14200426.value: 超高選擇性光譜調變的全陶瓷被動智慧窗

14200426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200426.value: Buildings account for approximately 40% of global energy consumption, which presents a major challenge to sustainable development. Among building envelopes, windows are responsible for nearly half of all heat gain and loss, making them a critical component for improving energy efficiency. In recent years, significant research efforts have been focused on the development of smart windows capable of dynamically modulating sunlight transmission and thermal emission. Various types of smart window have been developed, including active smart windows such as electro- and mechano-chromic windows, and passive smart windows such as photo- and thermos-chromic windows. Among them, cost effective photo- and thermochromic passive smart windows respond to the surrounding temperature and light intensity without requiring additional energy input or integrated control systems. They autonomously adapt to ambient conditions or seasonal changes, making them a highly promising and sustainable option for next-generation building energy savings. However, the energy-saving performance of each system is ultimately bounded by their intrinsic limitations in spectral modulation capability and potential weatherability issues. Herein we propose to integrate all ceramic photochromic and thermochromic materials with meticulously designed various structures, multilayer, meta surface and Fabry-Perot resonators to overcome the intrinsic limitations by leveraging the rarely studied seasonal temperature and radiation difference. Preliminary results show that the multilayer photo-thermochromic structure can effectively modulate solar transmittance (ΔTsol= 12.4%) and long-wave infrared emissivity (ΔεLWIR = 0.48) in response to ambient temperature and light intensity, outperforming the state of the art. The in-depth mechanistic understanding of passive modulation will be investigated aided by theoretical simulations and energy-saving potential of the proposed passive smart windows will be evaluated through field tests and simulations. These new strategies are expected to advance green building technologies and the retrofitting of existing buildings, thereby contributing to green building development and carbon neutrality goals not limited in Hong Kong. 建築物約佔全球能源消耗的40%，這是永續發展面臨的重大挑戰。 在建築外殼中，窗戶消耗近一半的熱量调控，是节能的關鍵組成部分。 近年來，重要的研究工作包括開發具備調變陽光透过與熱輻射的智慧窗，包括主動调控的電致變色與機械變色窗，以及被動调控式如光致變色窗和热致變色窗。 其中，具成本效益的光致與熱致變色被動窗具能回應與周圍溫度及光強差，無需額外能量輸入或整合控制系統。 它們會自主地適應環境條件，或季節性變化，使其成為下一代極具前景且永續的建築節能。 然而，每一種的節能性能系統最終受限於其在頻譜調變上的不足與潛在的耐候性問題。 本文建議整合全陶瓷光致變色與熱致變色材料，以及設計的各種結構比如多層結構、超表面及法布里-佩羅法共振腔， 来利用鮮少研究的季節性效應去克服材料內在局限。 初步結果顯示，多層光熱致變色結構能有效調變太陽透射率（ΔT =12.4% 及長波紅外線發射率（ΔεLWIR = 0.48），超越现有技術水準。 深入探討將透過以下方式進行， 包括被動調變的機制性理解、理論模擬，與實地測試進行評估。 這些新策略預計將推動不限于香港的綠色建築技術及現有改造建築，從而促進綠色建築發展與碳中和的目標。

14200726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200726.value: This project investigates Reinforcement Learning (RL) in Continuous-Time Jump Markov Decision Processes (CTJMDPs), a powerful framework for modelling dynamic decision making in continuous-time stochastic systems with discrete state spaces. RL enables agents to learn optimal policies through trial-and-error interactions with their environment. Despite their significance in operations research, including applications such as queueing control, dynamic pricing, and population process control, RL for finite-horizon CTJMDPs with unknown system dynamics remains a largely underexplored area. The finite-horizon CTJMDP framework poses several unique challenges: the system is continuously observed and controlled, the dynamics can be time-varying, and the state and action spaces can be unbounded. While one can discretize time upfront and apply existing RL algorithms developed for discrete-time problems, this approach is known be highly sensitive to the choice of discretization step and performs poorly with small time steps. To address these challenges, this project has two primary objectives: (1) to develop a comprehensive and rigorous framework for RL in finite-horizon CTJMDPs, encompassing problem formulation, theoretical foundations, algorithm development, and convergence analysis; and (2) to demonstrate the framework's applicability in two distinct domains: operations research (queueing control) and generative AI (discrete diffusion models). By establishing a fundamental understanding of RL in CTJMDPs, this project aims to advance continuous-time RL theory and its application to complex decision-making problems, with potential benefits in operations research, AI, and beyond. 本項目研究連續時間跳躍馬爾可夫決策過程（CTJMDPs）中的強化學習. 強化學習使代理能夠透過與其環境進行試錯互動來學習最佳策略. 儘管它們在運籌學中具有重要意義（包括排隊控制、動態定價和人口過程控制等應用），但在系統動態未知的有限時間CTJMDPs 中的強化學習仍然是一個很大程度上未被充分探索的領域. 有限時間 CTJMDP 框架帶來了幾個獨特的挑戰: 系統受到持續觀察和控制，動態可能隨時間變化，並且狀態和動作空間可以是無界的. 雖然人們可以預先對時間進行離散化，並應用為離散時間問題開發的現有強化學習演算法, 但已知這種方法對離散化步長的選擇高度敏感，並且在小時間步長下表現極差. 為了應對這些挑戰, 本項目有兩個主要目標: (1) 開發一個全面且嚴謹的框架用於有限時間 CTJMDPs 的強化學習, (2) 展示該框架在不同領域包括運籌學和生成式人工智能的適用性. 透過建立對 CTJMDPs 中強化學習的基礎理解，本研究將產生重要的新知識和影響. 該項目將為具有未知動態的複雜連續時間系統實現更高效的控制策略, 并展示基於 CTJMDP 強化學習的實際應用. 最終, 本項目旨在推進連續時間強化學習理論及其在複雜決策問題中的應用，從而在運籌學及其他領域帶來潛在效益.

14201026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201026.value: The rapid progress of AI is increasingly pushing the limits of the von Neumann memory wall bottleneck.
