In-memory computing, by moving the computation into non-volatile memory, is an emergent solution to address this. Realising in-memory computing is critically dependent on the performance of the underlying non-volatile memory. Charge trapping memory with linear memory programming capability appears promising. Despite the promise, it is fundamentally constrained by its slow memory programming speed, typically in an order of μs to ms. Carbon nanotubes with high carrier concentrations and mobilities and the large specific surface exhibit active surface chemistry towards charge trapping dynamics engineering and memory development advancements. In our prior studies, we have reported highly scalable thin-film transistor-based memory devices from PCz-sorted carbon nanotubes. The devices exhibited a non-volatile memory, with linear and symmetric memory states, arising from charge trapping by the sorting polymer. This memory behaviour allowed in-memory computing implementation, with significant efficiency enhancements proved in image processing. Most notably, the devices exhibited an ultrafast memory programming in our preliminary testing, reaching ~100 ns, surpassing other charge trapping memories (including those based on carbon nanotubes). Our hypothesis, based on the Maxwell-Wagner effect and our preliminary results, was that this ultrafast memory did not originate from a bulk charge trapping but instead, a rapid interfacial charge trapping at the molecular-scale crisscross interconnections of the carbon nanotubes. The primary goal of this project is to conclusively investigate this hypothesis and determine the origin of the ultrafast memory effect. We propose comprehensive material, electrical, and spectroscopic characterisations to understand the charge trapping dynamics, aiming to confirm whether indeed the ultrafast memory effect arises from a rapid interfacial charge trapping. On this basis, we propose to establish an ultrafast memory programming protocol (including a spike-timing-dependent plasticity learning rule) for high-precision memory writing and erasing. This protocol will be indispensable for high-efficiency in-memory computing implementation. Moving beyond the electrical approach, we propose to explore memory programming using ultrashort optical pulses. Realising optical programming will not only enhance the flexibility of in-memory computing but also unlock pathways for electro-optical neural networks and AI systems. Upon successful completion of the project, we anticipate our results to advance the research on carbon nanotube electronics. An ultrafast electrical and optical memory programming can position our memory devices as a transformative technology for in-memory computing towards enabling of intelligent technologies including robotics, VR/AR, and autonomous driving. 人工智能的快速發展正日益逼近馮·諾依曼“存儲墻”瓶頸的極限。存內計算通過將計算過程轉移至非易失性存儲器中，成為解決這一問題的新興方案。存內計算依賴於底層非易失性存儲器的性能，具備線性編程能力的電荷捕獲型存儲器展現出了廣闊的應用前景。然而，電荷捕獲型存儲器從根本上受限於其較慢的存儲器編程（寫入）速度，通常在微秒（μs）到毫秒（ms）量級。 碳納米管具有高載流子濃度、高遷移率以及大比表面積等特點，在電荷俘獲動力學工程與存儲器研發方面表現出活躍的表面化學特性。我們此前的研究報道了基於PCz分選碳納米管的高可擴展薄膜晶體管存儲器件。得益於分選聚合物的電荷捕獲效應，該器件表現出非易失性存儲特性，並具有線性和對稱的存儲狀態。這種存儲特性使得存內計算的實現成為可能，並在圖像處理應用中證實了其效率的顯著提升。最為突出的是，在我們的初步測試中，該器件展現了超快的存儲編程速度（達到約 100 ns），超越了其他電荷捕獲型存儲器（包括其他基於碳納米管的存儲器）。基於麥克斯韋-瓦格納效應及初步實驗結果，我們提出假設：這種超快存儲並非源於體相電荷捕獲，而是源於碳納米管分子尺度交叉互連處的快速界面電荷捕獲。 本項目的主要目標是深入驗證這一假設，並確定超快存儲效應的起源。我們計劃開展全面的材料、電學及光譜學表征，以解析電荷捕獲動力學機制，旨在證實該超快存儲效應是否確實源於快速的界面電荷捕獲。在此基礎上，我們擬建立一套超快存儲編程協議（包含脈沖時間依賴可塑性學習規則），以實現高精度的存儲器寫入與擦除。該協議對於實現高效的存內計算將是不可或缺的。除了電學方法，我們還計劃探索利用超短光脈沖進行存儲器編程。實現光學編程不僅能增強存內計算的靈活性，還將為光電神經網絡與人工智能系統開辟新的發展路徑。 本項目順利完成後，預期研究成果將極大推動碳納米管電子學領域的研究進展。超快的電學與光學存儲器編程能力，有望使我們的存儲器件成為存內計算領域的一項變革性技術，進而賦能包括機器人、虛擬現實/增強現實以及自動駕駛在內的各類智能技術。

14201326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14201326.value: 電源管理晶粒的混合式單電感多輸出直流對直流轉換器

14201326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201326.value: Chiplet-based integrated-circuit (IC) systems have been becoming popular in recent years. Multiple individually performance optimized chiplet modules integrated with different IC technologies are combined on the interposers to form a large-scale system. This heterogeneous integration with today’s cutting-edge packaging technologies provides numerous advantages over the system-on-chip approach because each chiplet can be designed and fabricated independently to achieve shorter design cycles, lower defect rates and more add-on choices of different functionalities. This project is to focus on the development of hybrid single-inductor multiple-output (HSIMO) dc-dc converter for power-management chiplets. The use of a single low-profile inductor in HSIMO converter has high potential to reduce both circuit volume and cost concurrently. However, the high inductor current and its conduction loss at the dc resistance of inductor is a major problem in HSIMO converter design. This goal of this project is to develop a HSIMO converter structure and control methods to achieve high efficiency, high stability and fast transient responses simultaneously. Prototypes of proposed HSIMO converter will be realized to verify the functionality and performance of the proposed concepts. 近年來，基於晶粒的積體電路系統日益普及。多個經過個別效能最佳化、採用不同積體電路技術製造的晶粒模組，透過中介層整合形成大型系統。相較於系統單晶片架構，這種結合當今尖端封裝技術的異質整合方式具有多項優勢，因為每個晶粒均可獨立設計與製造，從而縮短設計週期、降低缺陷率，並可更靈活地擴充不同功能模組以滿足多元化需求。 本計畫將聚焦於應用於電源管理晶粒的混合式單電感多輸出（Hybrid Single-Inductor Multiple-Output, HSIMO）直流對直流轉換器之開發。HSIMO 轉換器採用單一低高度電感，具備同時降低電路體積與成本的高度潛力。然而，在 HSIMO 轉換器設計中，較高的電感電流及其流經電感直流電阻所產生的導通損耗，是影響效能的主要挑戰。 本計畫的目標是開發一種兼具高效率、高穩定性及快速暫態響應能力的 HSIMO 轉換器架構及其控制方法。為驗證所提出概念的功能與效能，將實現相關 HSIMO 轉換器原型，並進行實驗測試與性能評估。

14202226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14202226.value: 再生核希爾伯特空間中的連續時間强化學習：理論、算法與金融工程應用

14202226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202226.value: Dynamic financial decision-making remains a core challenge in financial engineering. Traditionally, such problems are approached using model-based methods: a model of the environment is first estimated from historical data, and then an optimal decision policy is derived from that model. However, these methods are vulnerable to model misspecification and estimation errors, often resulting in unsatisfactory empirical performance. Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a powerful and increasingly popular method for addressing complex financial decision-making problems. Unlike traditional model-based approaches, RL seeks to learn optimal decision policies directly through exploration and exploitation, without relying on a predefined model. Its empirical advantages have been demonstrated across various financial applications, including portfolio selection and trade execution. While most RL research focuses on discrete-time settings, there is rapidly growing interest in continuous-time RL, which aligns naturally with many financial applications that involve high-frequency decisions. Recent theoretical advances have enabled policy evaluation, policy gradient methods, and q-learning in continuous time, leading to diverse algorithmic developments. Nonetheless, the current theoretical framework is limited by the assumption that the state process is Markov and the rewards depend solely on the current state as well as by the absence of uncertainty quantification in the learning outcomes. This project aims to advance the theoretical and algorithmic foundations of continuous-time RL by overcoming existing limitations. Departing from conventional function-based learning, we propose a novel operator-based learning paradigm that unifies Markov and non-Markov settings. Specifically, we allow the state process to follow a path-dependent stochastic differential equation, and the rewards may also exhibit path dependence. To facilitate operator learning, we employ vector-valued reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHS) and extend the RKHS theory to address the specific challenges of our framework. Our ultimate goal is to establish a unified theoretical framework that yields useful RL algorithms for financial applications. 動態金融決策制定一直是金融工程中的核心挑戰。傳統上，此類問題通常採用基於模型的方法：先利用歷史資料估計環境模型，再從該模型推導出最優決策策略。然而，這些方法容易受到模型錯誤指定與估計誤差的影響，常常導致不理想的實證表現。 近年來，強化學習（RL）已成為解決複雜金融決策問題的強大且日益受歡迎的方法。與傳統的模型式方法不同，RL 透過探索與利用直接學習最優決策策略，而不依賴預先指定的模型。其在多種金融應用中展現出實證優勢，包括投資組合選擇與交易執行。 儘管大多數 RL 研究聚焦於離散時間設定，對連續時間 RL 的興趣正快速升溫，因為許多涉及高頻決策的金融應用天然地以連續時間為基礎。近期的理論進展已使得連續時間中的策略評估、策略梯度方法與 q-learning 成為可能，並促成多樣化的演算法發展。然而，現有的理論框架仍受限於假設狀態過程為馬可夫過程、獎勵僅依賴當前狀態，以及缺乏對學習結果的不確定性量化。 本研究計畫旨在突破現有限制，推進連續時間 RL 的理論與演算法基礎。我們將跳脫傳統的函數式學習方法，提出一種全新的算子式學習範式，以統一馬可夫與非馬可夫設定。具體而言，我們允許狀態過程遵循路徑相依的隨機微分方程，獎勵亦可呈現路徑相依性。為促進算子學習，我們採用向量值再生核希爾伯特空間（RKHS），並擴展 RKHS 理論以處理本框架中的特殊挑戰。我們的最終目標是建立一套統一的理論框架，並據此設計可用於金融應用的 RL 演算法。

14202526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14202526.value: 基於真實世界二進制檔案的反組譯器基準測試資料集：關鍵技術、研究洞見與應用

14202526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202526.value: Binary code analysis is one of the most important research topics in the area of cybersecurity. It aims to find security problems (like vulnerabilities or malicious behaviour) by analyzing the binary code in executable files (such as malicious software or proprietary software which has no associated source code available). Binary code analysis normally begins with a disassembler that will translate binary executable files into assembly code, thus an accurate disassembler can greatly affect the results of down-stream security analysis. To evaluate disassemblers' accuracy, people have constructed various benchmark (i.e., ground truth) datasets by compiling open-source projects with various combinations of compilers, compiling options (like optimization levels), and code obfuscation techniques (which make code harder for disassembling). However, none of existing benchmark datasets had included real-world binary executable files, and this makes their evaluation results not convincing, because they can only cover a small part of all possible scenarios that security analysts need to handle during their daily jobs. Such a awkward situation is caused by several challenges. First of all, since we do not have the source code, we cannot tell whether the generated assembly code is really correct or not. Secondly, although it is possible to get the true instruction sequence via dynamic execution, it is slow and time consuming to increase the instructions coverage (and it is also unlikely to cover all possible instructions). To address these limitations, in this project we aim to study new techniques to build a benchmark dataset with real-world executable files, which we believe is necessary and useful for the whole cybersecurity community. We plan to achieve this goal by investigating the following three research questions (RQs). RQ 1: How to obtain the true assembly code from the real-world binary executable files? RQ 2: How to use the obtained benchmark dataset to guide the improvements of existing disassemblers. RQ 3: How to enable the cybersecurity community to benefit most from our benchmark dataset and the techniques behind? By the end of this project, we should deliver a disassembler evaluation benchmark dataset consists of real-world executable files, as well as an online multi-agent system that can generate test cases to evaluate and guide a continuous evolution of existing disassemblers. This can lead to better disassemblers and software security analysis in short term, and more secure digital world in the long run. 二進制程式碼分析是網絡安全領域的重要研究方向之一。研究人員透過分析可執行檔案中的二進制程式碼，找出當中可能存在的安全問題，例如軟件漏洞或惡意行為。這些檔案可以來自惡意軟件，也可以是沒有公開原始碼的商業或專有軟件。 二進制程式碼分析一般由反組譯開始。反組譯器會將電腦可以直接執行、但人類難以閱讀的二進制檔案，轉換為較容易分析的組合語言程式碼。因此，反組譯結果是否準確，會直接影響後續的安全分析。 為了評估反組譯器的準確程度，研究人員建立了不同的基準測試資料集。這些資料集通常以開源軟件為基礎，再配合不同的編譯器、編譯設定、最佳化程度及程式碼混淆技術，產生不同版本的可執行檔案。由於原始碼公開，研究人員可以掌握正確答案，並將反組譯結果與之比較。 不過，現有資料集大多以人工編譯的開源軟件為主，未能涵蓋真正來自現實世界的二進制可執行檔案。因此，即使某個反組譯器在現有測試中表現良好，也未必代表它能可靠地處理安全分析人員日常面對的真實軟件。 建立這類資料集主要面對兩項挑戰。第一，許多真實世界的軟件沒有公開原始碼，因此難以確認反組譯結果是否正確。第二，雖然可以透過實際執行程式，記錄運行期間的指令以取得真實指令序列，但這種方法速度較慢，而且要涵蓋所有可能的程式路徑和指令非常困難。 為了解決這些問題，本項目將研究建立真實世界二進制可執行檔案基準測試資料集的新方法，並探討以下三個研究問題： * RQ1：如何從真實世界的二進制可執行檔案中取得可信的組合語言程式碼？ * RQ2：如何利用所建立的資料集，找出現有反組譯器的不足，並為改進提供方向？ * RQ3：如何讓網絡安全社群更有效地使用這個資料集及相關技術？ 項目完成後，我們預計建立一套以真實世界可執行檔案為核心的反組譯器評估基準測試資料集，並開發一個網上多智能體系統，自動產生測試案例，用於評估及持續改進現有反組譯器。 短期而言，這項研究有助提升反組譯器的準確性及軟件安全分析的成效；長遠而言，則有助研究人員和安全從業員更有效地發現軟件安全問題，推動建立更安全的數碼環境。

14202726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14202726.value: 基於扭轉層狀材料的高品質因數超構表面本征手性發射

14202726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202726.value: This proposal aims to realize high-Q intrinsic chiral emission from etch-free hybrid metasurfaces through twist engineering of anisotropic layered 2D materials, e.g., NbOCl₂, As₂S₃, integrated with quasi-bound states in the continuum (qBIC) nanostructures. Chirality, a fundamental asymmetry ubiquitous in nature, enables chiral emission characterized by a high degree of circular polarization (DOP) and quality factor (Q-factor), which is crucial for advancing classical and quantum optics. Key applications include ultrasensitive molecular detection and discrimination, coherent chiral lasing for energy-efficient light sources, and on-chip quantum communications, facilitating secure quantum information processing and entangled photon generation in miniaturized devices. While chiral emitters like valley-contrast excitons in 2D semiconductors offer promise for low-energy, compact systems, their intrinsic chirality is often weak, with broad, incoherent emission limiting practical utility. Metasurfaces provide a pathway to enhance chiral light-matter interactions by confining fields at resonance, yet achieving efficient intrinsic chiral emission—distinct from extrinsic effects reliant on oblique incidence or false chirality—remains experimentally challenging in planar structures. Our innovative approach overcomes these limitations by leveraging twist engineering in anisotropic 2D materials like As₂S₃ to break out-of-plane mirror symmetry without complex 3D fabrication, combined with asymmetric qBIC nanostructures to simultaneously disrupt in-plane symmetry and enable high-Q (>10³) resonances with minimal radiation leakage. This hybrid design introduces an extra degree of freedom via tunable twist angles, allowing precise control over giant circular dichroism (CD ~1) and enhanced chiral field confinement. By integrating 2D semiconductors (e.g., monolayer of WS₂ or MoSe₂) or nonlinear 2D layered materials, we anticipate the first experimental demonstration of low-threshold chiral exciton lasers and nonlinear chiral emission sources, surpassing traditional plasmonic or 3D chiral metasurfaces in DOP, energy efficiency, and Q-factor. This versatile, fabrication-friendly platform—compatible with dry transfer methods and extendable to various layered materials—promises profound impacts on scientific research and technologies, including miniature nanolasers, chiral nanosensors, and integrated photonics for quantum computing and sensing. 手性是自然界中普遍存在的一種基本不對稱性，它賦予了發射體具有高圓偏振度（DOP）和高品質因子（Q因子）的手性發射特性，這對推動經典光學和量子光學的發展至關重要。其關鍵應用涵蓋超靈敏分子檢測與識別、用於節能光源的相干手性激光，以及片上量子通信，從而促進微型器件中的安全量子信息處理和糾纏光子產生。儘管二維半導體中的谷間反差激子等手性發射體在構建低能耗、緊湊型系統方面極具潛力，但其固有本征手性往往較弱，且發射譜域寬、相干性差，限制了實際應用。超表面透過在共振狀態下約束光場，為增強手性光與物質相互作用提供了有效途徑。然而，在平面結構中實現高效的本征手性發射 — 即區別於依賴斜入射或「偽手性」的外在效應，在實驗上仍面臨巨大挑戰。我們提出了一種創新方案，利用各向異性二維材料（如As₂S₃）中的扭轉工程打破面外鏡像對稱性，無需複雜的3D微納加工；同時結合非對稱準束縛態（qBIC）納米結構，打破面內對稱性，從而實現輻射損耗極低的高Q值（~10³）共振。這種混合設計透過可調扭轉角引入額外的自由度，能夠精確調控巨大的圓二色性（CD ~1）並增強手性光場的約束能力。透過集成二維半導體（如單層WS₂或MoSe₂）或非線性二維層狀材料，我們預期將首次在實驗上實現低閾值手性激子激射和非線性手性發射源，其圓偏振度、能源效率和品質因子均優於傳統的等離体激元或3D手性超表面。此功能多樣且易於製備的平台於乾式轉移工藝相兼容，並可擴展至多種層狀材料，將在科學研究和技術應用領域產生深遠影響，其中包括微型化納米激光、手性納米感測器，以及可用於量子計算和感測的集成光子器件。

14203526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14203526.value: 使用自旋鎖磁共振進行腦組織大分子含量與微結構的快速非侵入性同步表徵

14203526.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14203526.value: Dr Abrigo, Jill Dr Choi, Chun Ho Dr Hui, Sai Kam Dr Ip, Bonaventure Yiu-ming Prof So, Tiffany Yuen Tung

14203526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203526.value: Aim To develop and validate a fast, robust, and orientation independent MRI methodology that enables simultaneous characterization of tissue macromolecular content and microstructure, and to apply this technology to the assessment of multiple sclerosis (MS). Background White matter consists of organized bundles of myelinated axons that support structural connectivity and brain function. Noninvasive MRI is central to studying demyelination and remyelination and to developing biomarkers for neuroprotection and repair. Current quantitative approaches that characterize microstructure (e.g., diffusion tensor imaging, inhomogeneous magnetization transfer) and macromolecular content (e.g., myelin water fraction, macromolecular proton fraction) each capture complementary facets of myelin-related pathology. Nonetheless, relatively long scan times, limited specificity, and orientation dependence can constrain their clinical utility. A rapid, robust, orientation-independent method that jointly quantifies microstructure and macromolecular content could help bridge this gap. Project description Building on our spin lock-based MPF imaging (MPF-SL), we will develop a rapid 3D acquisition and quantification framework that simultaneously estimates dipolar order-sensitive microstructural integrity (T1D like contrast) and MPF within a single scan, while preserving orientation independence. The framework integrates biophysical modeling, optimized spin lock preparations, and AI enhanced quantification for joint parameter mapping of MPF and T1D. We will establish repeatability, reproducibility, and cross vendor robustness in phantoms and healthy volunteers, benchmarking microstructural measures against DTI and macromolecular content against MWF. We will then conduct an in vivo clinical study of 100 participants (50 MS patients and 50 age- and gender-matched controls) to assess group differences, abnormalities in lesions and normal appearing tissue, and associations with clinical measures (EDSS plus and SDMT), and to quantify the diagnostic performance of the proposed technology. All acquisition protocols and analysis software will be finalized for clinical translation. Significance This project will deliver a fast, noninvasive, and orientation‑independent quantitative MRI technology for concurrent assessment of microstructural integrity and macromolecular proton fraction in white matter, enabling reliable evaluation of remyelinating and neuroprotective therapies in multiple sclerosis. The method provides whole‑brain coverage in minutes and supports cross‑vendor deployment. Beyond MS, its biophysical specificity and scalability position it as a generalizable platform for biomarker development across neurological and neurodegenerative diseases, accelerating neuroimaging in both clinical trials and routine care. 目的 開發並驗證一種快速、穩定且不受方向影響的磁振造影方法，用以同步表徵組織大分子含量與微結構，並將此技術應用於多發性硬化症的評估。 背景 白質由有髓鞘軸突所構成的有序束狀結構組成，支持大腦的結構連結與功能。非侵入性磁共振造影在研究脫髓鞘與髓鞘再生，以及開發神經保護與修復的生物標誌物方面，扮演核心角色。當前的定量方法分別從微結構（如擴散張量造影、非均勻磁化傳遞）和大分子含量（如髓鞘水份比、大分子質子分數）切入，各自捕捉髓鞘相關病理的不同面向。然而，掃描時間較長、特異性有限以及方向依賴性等問題，可能限制其臨床應用價值。若能建立一種快速、穩定且不受方向影響的方法，聯合定量微結構與大分子含量，將有助於彌補此一差距。 計畫說明 本研究將以我們基於自旋鎖大分子質子分數造影技術為基礎，開發一套快速三維取樣與定量架構，能在單次掃描中同時估算對偶極有序狀態敏感的微結構完整性（類似T1D對比）與大分子質子分數，並保持不受方向影響的特性。此架構整合了生物物理模型、最佳化自旋鎖準備脈衝，以及人工智慧增強的定量方法，以實現大分子質子分數與T1D的聯合參數圖譜繪製。我們將在仿體與健康志願者中，建立重複性、再現性及跨廠牌穩定性，並以擴散張量造影作為微結構指標的基準，以髓鞘水份比作為大分子含量指標的基準。隨後，我們將進行一項納入100位參與者（50位多發性硬化症患者及50位年齡與性別匹配之對照組）的臨床研究，以評估組間差異、病灶與外觀正常組織中的異常、與臨床指標的關聯，並量化所提出技術的診斷效能。所有數據採集協議與分析軟體都將完成最終定稿，供臨床使用。 意義 本計畫將提供一種快速、非侵入性且不受方向影響的定量磁共振技術，用於同步評估白質的微結構完整性與大分子質子分數，進而實現對多發性硬化症中髓鞘再生及神經保護療法之可靠評價。此方法可在數分鐘內完成全腦掃描，並支援跨廠牌部署。除了多發性硬化症之外，其對生物物理特性的敏感度及可擴展性，使其有望成為一個可廣泛應用的平台，用於開發涵蓋各類神經系統及神經退化性疾病的生物標誌物，從而加速精準神經影像技術在臨床試驗及常規醫療照護中的應用。

14204026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14204026.value: 具指定性能之不確定非線性多智能體系統的協同輸出調節

14204026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204026.value: The cooperative output regulation problem (CORP), proposed by the principal investigator in 2012, extends the classical output regulation problem (ORP) from single-agent to multi-agent systems. The CORP aims to design a feedback control law that enables each follower's output to asymptotically track a class of reference trajectories while rejecting disturbances generated by an exosystem (referred to as the leader system). This problem generalizes issues such as leader-following consensus, formation control, and synchronization. The CORP is challenging because the control inputs of various agents are subject to communication constraints imposed by communication networks, requiring the control law to be distributed in the sense that it must satisfy these constraints at all times. The principal investigator has developed two approaches to address the CORP: the adaptive distributed observer (DO) approach and the distributed internal model (DIM) approach. The DO approach effectively handles switching communication networks, but it cannot address uncertainties in the plant or the leader system on its own. On the other hand, the DIM approach can handle uncertain nonlinear multi-agent systems but requires the communication network to remain connected at all times. Recently, the principal investigator combined the DO and DIM approaches, resulting in an integrated approach that can manage uncertain nonlinear multi-agent systems over jointly connected switching networks, that may be disconnected at any instant. However, despite over a decade of research, two critical issues remain unresolved. First, existing approaches cannot address multi-agent systems with uncertain exosystems over jointly connected switching networks. Second, the current problem formulation focuses solely on the steady-state response of the closed-loop system, neglecting its transient response. Since transient performance—measured by rise time, overshoot, and settling time—is as critical as steady-state performance due to physical constraints in practical systems, addressing both is essential. To tackle these challenges, this project proposes a new paradigm that integrates the DO and DIM approaches with an adaptive control mechanism to estimates the unknown parameters in the exosystem. This results in an adaptive integrated control approach for complex uncertain nonlinear systems with uncertain exosystems over jointly connected switching networks. To address the second obstacle, we employ a time-varying barrier Lyapunov function to shape the transient response of the closed-loop system, ensuring it meets prescribed performance requirements. Notably, the CORP over switching networks with prescribed performance has not been studied, even for cases with a known exosystem. 協同輸出調節問題由計劃主持人於 2012 年提出，將經典的輸出調節問題從單智能體系統推廣至多智能體系統。该問題旨在設計一種反饋控制律，使每個跟隨者的輸出能夠漸進跟蹤一類參考軌跡，同時抑制由外生系統，即領導者系統，產生的干擾。該問題涵蓋了諸如領導—跟隨一致性、編隊控制與同步等議題。該問題具有相當的挑戰性，因為各智能體的控制輸入受到通信網絡帶來的約束，這要求控制律必須是分佈式的，即必須始終滿足這些通信約束條件。 計劃主持人已開發出兩種解決 該問題 的方法：自適應分佈式觀測器方法與分佈式內模方法。自適應分佈式觀測器方法能有效處理切換通信網絡，但其本身無法處理受控對象或領導者系統中的不確定性。另一方面，分佈式內模方法方法可以處理不確定非線性多智能體系統，但要求通信網絡始終保持連通。最近，計劃主持人結合了自適應分佈式觀測器方法與分佈式內模方法，提出了一種整合方法，該方法能夠在聯合連通的切換網絡（在任何瞬間都可能斷開）下管理不確定非線性多智能體系統。 然而，儘管經過十多年的研究，仍有兩個關鍵問題尚未解決： 1. 外生系統的不確定性： 現有方法無法處理在聯合連通切換網絡下具有不確定外生系統的多智能體系統。 2. 暫態性能的忽視： 當前的問題表述僅關注閉環系統的穩態響應，而忽視了其暫態響應。由於實際系統受限於物理約束，以上升時間、超調量與調節時間衡量的暫態性能與穩態性能同樣重要，因此同時解決這兩者至關重要。 為應對這些挑戰，本計劃提出了一種新範式，將自適應分佈式觀測器方法與分佈式內模方法與 與自適應控制機制相結合，以估計外生系統中的未知參數。這形成了一種針對在聯合連通切換網絡下、具有不確定外生系統之複雜不確定非線性系統的自適應整合控制方法。為解決第二個障礙，我們採用時變障礙李亞普諾夫函數來塑形閉環系統的暫態響應，確保其滿足指定的性能要求。值得注意的是，即使在外生系統為已知的情況下，具指定性能且基於切換網絡的協同輸出調節問題亦尚未有人研究過。

14204126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14204126.value: 開發關聯式X射線與聲學顯微術以進行鋰離子軟包電池材料表徵

14204126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204126.value: Lithium-ion batteries play a crucial role in modern energy systems, powering electric vehicles and emerging technologies, such as the low-altitude economy in Hong Kong and the Greater Bay Area (GBA) of China. As demand grows for higher energy density, faster charging, and greater reliability, addressing battery degradation has become a critical challenge. However, most existing battery characterization techniques provide only partial insights into the complex, multi-scale, and dynamic processes occurring during battery operation. This limitation hinders the optimization of material performance and the accurate prediction of key battery metrics, such as state of charge and state of health. This project aims to develop a correlative imaging system, AXIS (Acoustic and X-ray Imaging System), to enable real-time monitoring and analysis of battery degradation mechanisms. By seamlessly integrating X-ray and acoustic microscopy while addressing critical challenges such as synchronization and runtime efficiency, AXIS will deliver complementary, high-resolution insights into the structural and mechanical evolution of batteries during operation. To achieve this, we will develop dedicated signal processing and machine learning algorithms to overcome physical limitations in resolution, speed, and sensitivity, facilitating the creation of predictive models for battery health and performance. If successful, AXIS will serve as a versatile tool for battery materials scientists, delivering unmatched precision in multi-modal data analysis under realistic fast-charging conditions. Additionally, this platform has the potential to revolutionize the battery industry by enabling cost-effective and detailed characterization of degradation processes. The insights gained from AXIS will drive innovation in battery materials, designs, and operational protocols, supporting the development of next-generation energy storage techniques. 鋰離子電池在現代能源系統中扮演至關重要的角色，不僅為電動車提供動力，亦支撐香港及粵港澳大灣區低空經濟等新興技術與產業的發展。隨著市場對更高能量密度、更快充電速度及更高可靠性的需求日益增長，電池退化與失效已成為亟待解決的關鍵問題。然而，現有大多數電池表徵技術只能局部揭示電池運行期間複雜、多尺度且持續演變的動態過程，因而制約了材料性能的優化，以及對荷電狀態和健康狀態等關鍵電池指標的準確預測。 本項目旨在開發關聯式成像系統AXIS (Acoustic and X-ray Imaging System，聲學與X射線成像系統)，以實現對電池退化與失效機制的實時監測與分析。AXIS將X射線顯微術與聲學顯微術有機整合，並著力解決系統同步和運行效率等關鍵技術難題，從而以互補方式獲取高分辨率信息，深入揭示電池運行期間的結構與力學演變。為此，我們將開發專用的信號處理及機器學習算法，突破成像分辨率、速度和靈敏度方面的物理限制，並為構建電池健康狀態與性能預測模型奠定基礎。 若項目成功，AXIS將成為電池材料研究的多功能工具，能夠在貼近實際的快速充電條件下實現高精度多模態數據分析。此外，該平台有望以具成本效益的方式對電池退化與失效過程進行精細表徵，為電池產業帶來革新。透過AXIS獲得的研究成果將推動電池材料、結構設計及運行規程的創新，並促進下一代儲能技術的發展。

14204326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14204326.value: 用於建造環境中空氣傳播病原體高效採樣與核酸分析的快速溶解納米纖維過濾網研製

14204326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204326.value: The study of airborne pathogen transmission is critical for mitigating the spread of infectious diseases. Nucleic acid analysis, such as quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) and sequencing, represents a powerful approach for the quantification and characterization of airborne pathogens. However, a significant bottleneck exists: the transfer of pathogens from collection filters (e.g., quartz filters) into a liquid medium for nucleic acid analysis requires a complex elution procedure. This process, which often involves steps such as ultrasonic elution, enrichment into polyethersulfone filters, and cutting those filters into small pieces, is laborious and time-consuming. More critically, this complex elution process results in substantial pathogen loss (over 65%), increasing the risk of false negatives. Therefore, it is crucial to develop advanced air sampling filters that enhance the pathogen recovery rate and simplify the elution process. A potential solution involves fabricating filters from dissolvable polymers, enabling the direct transfer of collected pathogens into a liquid medium by dissolving the filter. Electrospinning can produce high-efficiency nanofiber air filters. Furthermore, these filters possess minimal thickness and a high surface-area-to-volume ratio, which together facilitate rapid dissolution. Therefore, we hypothesize that rapidly dissolving nanofiber filters with high physical collection efficiency can be developed by electrospinning dissolvable polymers. The use of such filters would eliminate the need for the complex elution procedure. We also hypothesize that this rapid dissolution feature will significantly improve the pathogen recovery rate by avoiding the sample losses inherent in traditional elution methods. This project will start with the development of core-shell composite nanofiber filters that can dissolve quickly in a liquid medium while remaining structurally intact in high-humidity environments to facilitate practical applications. The influence of filter parameters on physical collection efficiency, sampling flow rate, and pathogen recovery rate will be systematically investigated. The filters will then be optimized accordingly to balance these performance metrics. Finally, this project will conduct field tests in various built environments to quantify airborne pathogens using these filters with qPCR analysis and evaluate the real-world performance of the proposed method. The proposed project will enhance our understanding of the collection and recovery mechanisms of airborne pathogens by rapidly dissolving nanofiber filters. The development of these filters is expected to improve the pathogen recovery rate and simplify the elution process for nucleic acid analysis. The findings will advance the development of this novel air sampling technology, enabling more accurate and efficient nucleic acid analysis of airborne pathogens in built environments. 病原體空氣傳播的研究對於減緩傳染病擴散至關重要。核酸分析，例如定量聚合酶連鎖反應（qPCR）及定序，是定量與鑑定空氣傳播病原體的強大工具。然而，現有技術存在一個顯著的瓶頸：將病原體從採集過濾網（如石英濾紙）轉移至液體介質以進行核酸分析，需經繁複的溶離程序。此程序常包括超音波溶離、濃縮至聚醚碸濾膜，再將濾膜剪成小片等步驟，不僅費力且耗時。更關鍵的是，此複雜的溶離過程會導致大量病原體流失（超過65%），增加偽陰性風險。因此，開發能提升病原體回收率並簡化溶離程序的先進空氣採樣過濾網至關重要。 一種可能的解決方案是利用可溶解高分子材料製作過濾網，透過溶解過濾網即可將收集到的病原體直接轉移至液體介質中。靜電紡絲技術可製造高效率納米纖維空氣過濾網，且此類過濾網厚度極薄、比表面積高，這些特性均有助於快速溶解。因此，我們假設可透過靜電紡絲可溶解高分子材料，開發出具有高物理收集效率且能快速溶解的納米纖維過濾網。使用此類過濾網將可免除複雜的溶離程序。我們亦假設，此快速溶解特性將可避免傳統溶離方法固有的樣本損失，從而顯著提升病原體回收率。 本研究將首先開發能在液體介質中快速溶解，同時於高濕度環境中保持結構完整的核殼複合納米纖維過濾網，以利實際應用。我們將系統性地探討過濾網參數對物理收集效率、採樣流速及病原體回收率的影響，並據此優化過濾網，以平衡這些性能指標。最後，本研究將於不同建造環境中進行實地測試，利用這些過濾網搭配 qPCR 分析來定量空氣傳播病原體，並評估所提出方法的實際效能。 本研究將增進我們對快速溶解納米纖維過濾網收集與回收空氣病原體機制的理解。此類過濾網的開發預期可提升病原體回收率，並簡化核酸分析的溶離程序。研究成果將推動此新穎空氣採樣技術的發展，實現對建造環境中空氣傳播病原體更準確且高效的核酸分析。

14205926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14205926.value: 非平穩氣候動態下的多模態城市天氣預報

14205926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205926.value: Background and Motivation: Climate change poses a significant threat to humanity, leading to an increase in extreme weather events and natural disasters that cause substantial socioeconomic losses. Accurate urban weather forecasting is critical for mitigating these impacts, especially as more than half of the global population currently resides in cities. However, urban weather prediction remains exceptionally challenging due to the complex microclimates shaped by intricate urban morphologies. Current operational systems predominantly rely on numerical models, which incorporate urban parameterizations to simulate phenomena like urban heat islands. Despite their utility, these models suffer from high computational costs, reliance on simplified physical approximations, and coarse resolutions that limit their accuracy and applicability at the urban scale. Related Work and Challenges: While data-driven weather forecasting methods offer efficiency, they either operate at coarse resolutions (e.g., weather foundation models) or are trained on limited urban observations (e.g., station-based forecasting). With the accumulation of city weather stations, the urban weather forecasting has come into reach. However, there are several challenges: (1) Integrating highly heterogeneous data sources requires an effective multimodal representation learning framework; (2) The inherent chaos in atmospheric systems makes probabilistic forecasting essential for quantifying uncertainty; (3) Urban weather patterns exhibit non-stationary behavior, necessitating continuous model adaptation without incurring prohibitive retraining costs while maintaining accuracy; (4) Translating numerical forecasts into timely and coherent public reports remains reliant on time-consuming manual interpretation. Proposal Objectives: This project aims to build a comprehensive operational system for urban weather forecasting. First, we will develop a Multimodal Spatio-temporal Diffusion Transformer to generate accurate, probabilistic urban weather forecasts, effectively integrating diverse data sources. Second, to tackle the non-stationary behavior of urban weather patterns, we will propose a meta-learning approach for continual model adaptation with Low-Rank Adaptation to efficiently update the model with new data, ensuring long-term accuracy without prohibitive retraining costs or "catastrophic forgetting". Finally, we will leverage Multimodal Large Language Models to automate the generation of clear, actionable, and meteorologically accurate public weather reports, enhancing the efficiency and quality of information delivery and providing better support for public decision-making. Impact: This project will significantly enhance urban resilience and operational efficiency by providing timely, high-resolution weather forecasts. It supports improved disaster preparedness, reduces economic losses from extreme events, optimizes energy and water management, and enables smarter decision-making across transportation, agriculture, and public health sectors, contributing to sustainable urban development. 背景與動機: 氣候變遷對人類社會構成重大威脅，導致極端天氣事件與自然災害日益頻繁，造成巨大的社會與經濟損失。精準的城市天氣預報對於減輕這些影響至關重要，尤其是在目前全球已有超過一半人口居住於城市的情況下。然而，由於城市複雜的地形結構與建築形態所形成的微氣候效應，城市天氣預測仍然是一項極具挑戰性的任務。現行的天氣預報系統主要依賴數值天氣預報模型，透過城市參數化方案模擬都市熱島等現象。儘管此類模型有實用性，但仍存在計算成本高昂、依賴簡化物理近似以及空間解析度較粗略等問題，限制了其在城市尺度上的預報準確度與實際應用。 相關研究與挑戰：雖然資料驅動的天氣預報方法具有運算效率高的優勢，但現有方法大多僅能在較粗解析度下運作（例如天氣基礎模型），或是依賴有限的城市觀測資料進行訓練（例如基於氣象站的預報模型）。隨著城市氣象站的持續增多，高解析度城市天氣預報已逐漸成為可能。然而，仍面臨以下幾項關鍵挑戰：(1) 城市天氣預報涉及多種高度異質的資料來源，需要有效的多模態表徵學習框架，以實現跨資料來源的資訊融合; (2)大氣系統具有混沌特徵，因此機率式預報對於量化不確定性至關重要; (3) 由於城市天氣模式的非平穩性，模型需要具備持續適應新的能力，避免高昂的重新訓練成本並保持準確性; (4) 將數值預報結果轉化為及時、準確的天氣報告，目前仍高度依賴專家的人工解讀與撰寫，耗費大量時間與人力資源。 計畫目標: 本項目旨在建立一套完整的城市天氣預報系統。首先，我們將開發多模態時空擴散轉換器，有效整合多元異質資料來源，生成高精度且具不確定性量化能力的機率式城市天氣預報。其次，為解決城市天氣模式的非平穩特性，我們將提出結合元學習與低秩適應的持續學習框架，以低成本方式利用最新資料更新模型，在維持長期預報準確度的同時，避免全面重新訓練及災難性遺忘問題。最後，我們將結合多模態大型語言模型，自動生成清晰、具可操作性且符合氣象專業標準的公共天氣預報報告，提升資訊發布的效率與質量，並為公眾決策提供更有效的支援。 預期影響：本項目將透過提供及時且高解析度的城市天氣預報，大幅提升城市韌性與運行效率。其成果可應用於災害預警與應變，提升防災準備能力，降低極端天氣造成的經濟損失，同時有助於能源與水資源管理最佳化，支援交通運輸、農業生產及公共健康等領域的智慧決策，進一步促進城市永續發展與社會福祉。

14206026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14206026.value: 局部可指數性於弱耦合馬可夫過程之基礎研究與網路應用：局部可指數性的驗證、快速計算與近似可指數性

14206026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206026.value: Weakly-coupled MDP (Markov Decision Process) can be a powerful tool to model many network control problems with stringent performance requirements. However, large MDPs are also known to suffer from the curse-of-dimensionality, i.e., the complexity increases exponentially as the number of networked agents increases. Index policies, including the classical Whittle index and the recently-developed partial index, promise a framework to decompose a large-scale MDP into much-smaller per-agent MDPs, which can lead to solutions that are scalable, easy-to-interpret, and adaptive to network changes. Compared to the Whittle index, partial index (recently proposed by our team) further extends index policies to systems with multiple resource constraints, and therefore can potentially benefit a much-larger set of network control problems. However, to date the theory of partial index still faces many fundamental technical challenges: (i) partial indexability is difficult to verify; and (ii) computing the partial index incurs high complexity. Without effective solutions to these obstacles, many network control problems modelled as weakly-coupled MDPs will be unable to benefit from the partial index, and thus have to suffer low performance, poor scalability, and difficulty in practical implementation. Research Goals: The goal of this project is therefore to develop the foundational theory and algorithms that overcome these key obstacles to the use of the partial index, so that it can be easily applied to large weakly-coupled MDPs modelling a wide range of network control problems with stringent performance requirements. Specifically, we will develop new active-time conditions that can greatly ease the verification of partial indexability in complex settings, design new algorithms that can significantly speed up the computation of the partial index for real-time implementation, and develop a new notion of approximate indexability that enables the use of partial index even under certain settings when indexability cannot be analytically verified. Further, we will demonstrate the effectiveness and benefits of our partial-index theory by applying it to practical use-cases in time-sensitive wireless systems and caching systems with dynamic content. Impact: The project will impact both theory and practice. On the theory side, the results from our project will significantly enlarge the range of weakly-coupled MDPs and network-control problems that partial index can solve. On the practice side, by applying our theory to network control problems in time-sensitive wireless systems and caching systems with dynamic content, our research will benefit IT systems by providing scalable, easy-to-interpret, and adaptive solutions. 弱耦合馬可夫過程是適用於建模多類網路控制問題的強大工具，特別適合於對性能有嚴格要求的網路控制問題。然而，大規模的馬可夫過程（MDP）複雜度極高。指數策略（index policies），包括經典的 Whittle 指數以及近期提出的局部指數（partial index），提供了一個能將大規模 MDP 分解為各個小 MDP的框架，進而能導出可擴展、易於解釋、並快速適應網路變化的網絡控制算法。相比於 Whittle 指數，由我們團隊近期提出的局部指數更進一步將指數策略擴展至有多類資源限制的網絡系統。但是，迄今局部指數的理論仍面臨許多根本性的技術挑戰：(i) 局部可指數性（partial indexability）難以驗證；以及 (ii) 局部指數的計算複雜度仍很高。如果沒有有效的方法去克服這些障礙，許多以弱耦合 MDP 建模的網路控制問題將無法受益於局部指數，以至於效能低下、可擴展性差，並難以應用于實際系統。 研究目標：針對局部指數（partial index）的技術挑戰，本項目將研究局部指數的基礎理論與算法，使其能更容易地應用於大規模弱耦合 MDP和相應的網路控制問題。我們將提出新的『主動時間條件』（active-time conditions），以大幅降低在複雜網絡問題中驗證局部可指數性的難度；我們將設計新的算法，能快速計算局部指數，使之能達到實時應用的要求；我們將提出新的『近似可指數性』（approximate indexability）概念，即便在局部可指數性無法解析驗證的情境下，仍可以使用相應的近似局部指數策略。以上局部指數的理論與算法， 將透過在實時無線網絡與動態緩存系統中的實際應用，展示其有效性與性能優勢。 研究意義：本項目在理論與實踐上都將帶來重大影響。在理論層面，我們的研究成果將大大擴展局部指數的應用範圍，使其能應用與更多的網路控制問題。在實踐層面，透過將局部指數策略應用於實時無線網絡與動態緩存系統，我們的研究將為各種信息技術系統提供可擴展、易於解釋、並能快速適應網路變化的解決方案。

14206326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14206326.value: 仿生鬚感連續體輸尿管鏡機器人助力上尿路上皮癌早期診斷

14206326.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14206326.value: Prof Ren, Hongliang Dr Teoh, Yuen Chun, Jeremy

14206326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206326.value: Urothelial carcinoma (UC) is the second most common urological malignancy, with upper tract UC (UTUC) accounting for 5–10% of cases, primarily affecting the ureters. Although less common, UTUC is highly malignant and difficult to detect early, as it often presents as carcinoma in situ (also known as “flat tumor”), that are subtle and poorly visualized with current imaging techniques. Clinical studies indicate that two-thirds of newly diagnosed cases have already progressed to the muscle-invasive stage, often requiring ureterectomy (removal of the ureter), which is suboptimal for preserving renal function. Ureteroscopy-assisted biopsy, though commonly recommended, is limited by the narrow ureteral caliber and thin wall—raising perforation risk—and often yields inadequate tissue samples, leading to missed lesions. Building on evidence that cancerous ureteral tissues exhibit markedly reduced stiffness, we propose to develop a miniature intelligent continuum ureteroscopic robot equipped with a bioinspired whisker-like tactile sensing module and Artificial Intelligence (AI) algorithms. This robotic system can navigate transurethrally to perform stiffness-based palpation and generate surface-grade 4D intraluminal stiff maps for in situ detection of visually imperceptible early-stage UTUC, thereby improving the likelihood of kidney- and ureter-sparing management. This work will advance key technologies in multi-material miniature continuum design, constrained flexible robot motion planning and control, optical fiber-based whisker sensing, cost-effective sim2real transfer learning, and physics-informed stiffness reconstruction—aimed at enabling early detection of abnormalities in deep, confined anatomical sites previously inaccessible for in situ diagnosis. Our project's outcomes, scientifically spanning robotic perception, autonomous robotics, and pre-clinical studies on tactile-based deep site abnormality detection, are expected to guide the future development of a broader range of emerging robots for delicate perception and operation in other deep anatomical sites (e.g., bronchi, ovary). This will create opportunities to transfer extensively researched flexible robots and tactile sensing technologies to advanced biomedical applications, leading to significant societal impacts. The beneficiaries of this project are numerous. Its novelty can inspire new case studies in multimodal sensorimotor control, advancing emerging robotic perception and control paradigms. In the long term, UTUC patients will gain from a nondistructive robotic solution for early-stage inspection, improving the likelihood of renal preservation. Urologists will benefit from intelligent navigation and automated ureteral stiffness mapping, reducing workload, enhancing efficiency, and expanding diagnostic capabilities. These outcomes have the potential to transform early-stage UTUC diagnostic protocols. 尿路上皮癌（UC）是第二常見的泌尿系統惡性腫瘤，其中上尿路尿路上皮癌（UTUC）約佔 5–10% 的病例，主要影響輸尿管。雖然較少見，但 UTUC 惡性程度高，且早期難以檢測，因為它常以原位癌（又稱「扁平腫瘤」）形式出現，病灶隱匿，現有影像技術難以清晰顯示。臨床研究顯示，三分之二的新診斷病例已進展至肌層浸潤期，往往需要行輸尿管切除術，這對腎功能保存並不理想。雖然輸尿管鏡輔助活檢常被推薦，但受限於輸尿管管徑狹窄及管壁薄弱，存在穿孔風險，且常常取得的組織樣本不足，導致病灶遺漏。基於癌變輸尿管組織剛度顯著降低的證據，我們提出研發一種微型智能連續體輸尿管鏡機器人，配備仿生鬚狀觸覺感測模組與人工智慧（AI）演算法。該機器人可經尿道導航，進行基於剛度的觸診，並生成表面級四維腔內剛度地圖，用於原位檢測肉眼不可見的早期 UTUC，從而提升腎臟與輸尿管保留治療的可能性。 本項目預期成果涵蓋機器人感知、自主機器人以及基於觸覺的深部異常檢測的臨床前研究，預期將引導更多新型機器人於其他深部解剖區域（如支氣管、卵巢）的精細感知與操作。這將創造將柔性機器人與觸覺感測技術廣泛轉移至高階生醫應用的契機，並帶來潛在社會影響。

14206426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14206426.value: 採用基於VCO的電荷累積電路提升噪聲整形SAR ADC的能效與可重構性

14206426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206426.value: Noise-Shaping Successive-Approximation-Register (NS-SAR) analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) are a leading architecture for power-efficient, high-resolution conversion in low-to-medium bandwidth applications such as biomedical signal acquisition, neural interfaces, and Internet-of-Things sensor nodes. By merging the inherent energy efficiency with the oversampling and noise-shaping benefits of Delta-Sigma modulators, NS-SAR ADCs offer a compelling solution. However, the performance trajectory of NS-SAR ADCs is now facing diminishing returns; achieving the next leap in energy efficiency demands fundamental architectural and circuit-level innovations. Furthermore, advanced NS-SAR designs are predominantly confined to low-pass conversion, excluding them from applications requiring a signal band centered at a high frequency. This project aims to overcome these performance and functional barriers by pioneering a reconfigurable, high-order NS-SAR ADC. Our approach centers on a voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO)-based charge accumulation (CA) circuit as a transformative loop filter. While this technique offers robustness to process-voltage-temperature (PVT) variations and scaling-friendly characteristics, the prior implementation has been constrained by low noise-shaping order and low thermal noise efficiency. To transcend these limitations, we propose two key innovations. First, we will develop a novel nested feedforward NS-SAR architecture, offering superior stability, minimal implementation complexity, and a freely scalable noise-shaping order to achieve a drastically improved signal-to-quantization-noise ratio. Second, we will design a new VCO-CA circuit topology engineered for significantly enhanced thermal noise efficiency while maintaining PVT robustness. We will validate these innovations through two 28-nm CMOS prototypes. The first will demonstrate the VCO-CA-based nested feedforward NS-SAR architecture, aiming to achieve state-of-the-art energy efficiency to set a new benchmark for NS-SAR ADCs. The second will be a reconfigurable low-pass/high-pass version. Crucially, by reusing the core circuitry from the low-pass mode, this prototype will achieve record-breaking energy efficiency in its high-pass configuration, outperforming all existing high-pass noise-shaping ADCs, including discrete-time Delta-Sigma modulators. The successful completion of this project will deliver a versatile, high-performance, and PVT-robust ADC platform that extends the frontiers of power-efficient data conversion. 噪聲整形逐次逼近寄存器（NS-SAR）型模數轉換器（ADC）是低至中等帶寬應用（如生物醫學信號採集、神經接口和物聯網傳感器節點）中實現高能效、高分辨率轉換的領先架構。通過將固有的能效優勢與Delta-Sigma調制器的過采樣和噪聲整形特性相結合，NS-SAR ADC提供了一種極具競爭力的解決方案。然而，NS-SAR ADC的性能提升軌跡正面臨收益遞減的困境；要實現能效的下一階段飛躍，亟需根本性的架構和電路級創新。此外，現有的先進NS-SAR設計主要局限於低通轉換，因此無法應用於信號頻帶中心位於高頻的場景。 本項目旨在通過開創一種可重構的高階NS-SAR ADC來突破這些性能和功能瓶頸。我們的核心技術路徑是採用基於壓控振盪器（VCO）的電荷累積（CA）電路作為變革性的環路濾波器。儘管該技術具有對工藝-電壓-溫度（PVT）變化魯棒性強且工藝縮放友好的特點，但此前實現方案一直受限於較低的噪聲整形階數和較差的熱噪聲效率。 為克服上述局限，我們提出兩項關鍵創新。第一，我們將開發一種新型嵌套前饋NS-SAR架構，該架構具有優越的穩定性、極低的實現複雜度以及可自由擴展的噪聲整形階數，從而大幅提升信號量化噪聲比。第二，我們將設計一種新型VCO-CA電路拓撲，在保持PVT魯棒性的同時，顯著提高熱噪聲效率。 我們將通過兩款28納米CMOS原型芯片來驗證這些創新。第一款原型將展示基於VCO-CA的嵌套前饋NS-SAR架構，旨在實現業界領先的能效水平，為NS-SAR ADC樹立新的性能標杆。第二款原型將是可重構的低通/高通版本。關鍵在於，通過重用低通模式下的核心電路，該原型將在高通配置下實現創紀錄的能效，超越所有現有高通噪聲整形ADC，包括離散時間Delta-Sigma調制器。 本項目的成功完成將提供一個通用、高性能且對PVT魯棒的ADC平台，從而拓展高能效數據轉換的技術前沿。

14206526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14206526.value: 計算具結構雙層優化問題的近似克拉克駐點的可證高效算法

14206526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206526.value: Bilevel optimization (BO), which concerns optimal decision making in processes that involve an upper-level decision maker (the leader) and a lower-level decision maker (the follower), has attracted much interest lately due to its many applications in machine learning and signal processing. One of the current research directions is the design of efficient iterative methods with complexity guarantees for computing approximate stationary points of structured BO problems. However, existing results in this direction either make the restrictive assumption that the lower-level solution mapping is a singleton or only establish the tractability of rather weak stationarity concepts. In a recent study, the PI and his collaborators have introduced a new regularity property of set-valued mappings called set smoothness and shown that if a BO problem has, among other things, a set-smooth lower-level solution mapping, then the task of finding an approximate Clarke stationary point of the problem is tractable. Our results significantly sharpen those in the literature. Moreover, they suggest exciting new research directions, which we intend to explore thoroughly in this project. The outcomes will advance our understanding of the tractability of strong approximate stationarity concepts in BO, provide algorithmic tools to tackle broader classes of structured BO problems that arise in contemporary applications, and give impetus to further research in the design and analysis of iterative methods for tackling BO problems. 雙層優化中一個重要的研究方向是設計帶複雜度保證的高效迭代算法，以找出具結構雙層優化問題的近似駐點。項目負責人及其合作者最近提出一種關於集值映射的新正則性性質，並給出計算帶這種性質的雙層優化問題的近似克拉克駐點的複雜度。這成果揭示了若干新研究方向，而本項目將對這些方向進行深入探索。本項目的研究成果將有助於增進我們對雙層優化中不同駐點概念之可計算性的理解，為求解當代應用中出現的具結構雙層優化問題提供新的算法工具，並進一步推動求解雙層優化問題的算法設計與理論分析研究。

14207126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14207126.value: 自回歸三維組合模型生成與設計：程式建模、組合補全、結構完整性與動態分析

14207126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207126.value: Generating 3D modular assemblies is far more challenging than generating 3D shapes. The generative process needs to attend not only to the overall shape of the assembly but also to its structures, its component parts, the parts connections, structural integrity, and possibly its dynamics. In this research project, we shall perform a comprehensive study in developing a new generative solution for 3D assemblies, considering procedural modeling and generation, assembly completion and refinement, structural integrity, and mechanical dynamics, beyond the capabilities of the existing 3D generative solutions. Importantly, we identify and plan the following five novel research directions concerning 3D assembly generation: (1) To formulate a Multiscale-graph-guided Autoregressive Generative (MAG) framework, integrating our multiscale tokenization scheme and multimodal conditioning to deliver a generalized approach for generating 3D modular assemblies; (2) To develop a hierarchical procedural assembly generation approach, enabling inverse 3D assembly modeling, constraint-aware feedforward grammar, and interactive procedural editing, for efficiently producing a rich variety of 3D assembly models for data training; (3) To introduce controllability into the assembly generative framework, with intelligent 3D assembly completion and refinement to enable interactive and flexible assembly design; (4) To study and incorporate structural integrity considerations (collision-free, parts connectivity, assemblability, and structural stability) into the generative framework; and (5) To extend our framework for generating dynamic assemblies by considering mechanical joints, actuators, and motion ranges, and jointly optimizing the structure and motion. 三維組裝模型生成遠比三維形狀生成更具挑戰性。生成過程不僅需要關注組裝模型的整體形狀，還需注意其結構、部件形狀、部件連接、結構完整性以及可能的動態特性。在本研究計畫中，我們將進行一項全面的研究，旨在開發一種全新的三維組裝模型生成的解決方案，該方案將考慮程序化的程式建模及生成、組合補全及改進、結構完整性與動態分析，超越現有三維模型生成解決方案的能力。重要的是，我們確定並規劃了以下五個與三維組裝模型生成相關的新研究方向： (1) 建構多尺度圖引導的自回歸生成框架，整合多尺度分詞方案和多模態條件化方法，從而提供了一種生成三維組裝模型的通用方法； (2) 發展一種分層過程式組裝產生方法，實現逆向三維組裝建模、約束感知前饋語法和互動式流程編輯，從而高效產生種類豐富的三維組裝模型用於資料訓練； (3) 在組裝生成框架中引入可控性，透過智慧三維組裝完成和優化，實現互動式和靈活的組裝設計； (4) 研究並將結構完整性考量（無碰撞、部件連通性、可組裝性和結構穩定性）納入生成框架；以及 (5) 透過考慮機械關節、致動器和運動範圍，並共同優化結構和運動，擴展我們用於產生動態組裝的框架。

14207626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14207626.value: 面向超大城市韌性的地表沉降知識引導雷達遙感研究

14207626.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14207626.value: Prof Ma, Peifeng Prof Zhang, Li Min

14207626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207626.value: Land subsidence, the gradual lowering of the Earth's surface, has emerged as a significant geohazard, resulting from both natural processes and intensified human activities. In megacities, typically characterized by high population density and extensive infrastructure, this phenomenon is particularly critical due to the excessive groundwater extraction and large-scale underground developments. The interplay of these factors not only compromises the structural integrity of buildings and public infrastructure but also heightens the risk of flooding and diminishes groundwater storage capacity, posing a long-term threat to urban resilience. In recent years, we have seen multiple subsidence-induced tragic events. For instance, the 2021 condominium collapse in Florida led to 97 fatalities, and in 2023 a 20 mm subsidence induced wall cracking at the Sung Wong Toi station in Hong Kong. These events call for advanced early warning systems and proactive risk mitigation strategies in subsidence-prone urban environments. The United Nations 2030 Agenda has also emphasized the importance of building sustainable and resilient cities. This project aims to develop innovative Synthetic Aperture Radar interferometry (InSAR) remote sensing methods with multi-disciplinary knowledge to detect and interpret land subsidence in megacities, addressing the scientific challenge of linking complex deformation mechanisms to their underlying natural and anthropogenic drivers for risk assessment and resilience empowering. InSAR remote sensing offers unique advantages over traditional ground-based methods: (i) large-scale monitoring ability; (ii) high-density measurement points; and (iii) cost-effective without requiring in-situ instrumentation. The integration of artificial intelligence (AI), especially knowledge-guided AI, enables improved understanding of subsidence patterns and their interactions with various environmental factors. The proposed deliverables include: (i) a state-of-the-art millimeter-accuracy InSAR deformation monitoring technique with point density enhancement and high-resolution atmospheric correction; (ii) a novel and intelligent subsidence spatiotemporal pattern recognition method guided by multi-disciplinary geological and hydrological knowledge; (iii) a multi-level and multi-phase urban risk assessment system incorporating domain expertise and geographic information system (GIS) analysis; and (iv) dissemination of research outputs through journal publications, international conferences, and academic workshops. The deliverables developed in this project will be transferable to subsidence-prone megacities worldwide, offering practical value for urban planning and risk mitigation. In addition, the scientific insights gained from this research will contribute to broader geoscience topics like sea-level rise, groundwater dynamics, and Earth surface evolution, where a deeper understanding of land subsidence mechanisms is also essential. 地表沉降是指地表高程持續或漸進降低的地質過程，其形成既受自然因素影響，也與日益增強的人類活動密切相關。對於人口高度集聚、基礎設施密集的超大城市而言，過量地下水開採及大規模地下空間開發等活動使地表沉降問題尤為突出。持續沉降不僅可能威脅建築物及公共基礎設施的結構安全，還會加劇城市洪澇風險、削弱地下水儲存能力，並對城市長期韌性構成重要挑戰。近年，多地發生了與地表沉降及地基變形相關的嚴重事件。例如，2021年美國佛羅里達州公寓倒塌事故造成97人死亡；2023年，香港宋皇臺站附近約20毫米的地表沉降引發牆體開裂。上述事件進一步凸顯了在地表沉降高風險城市地區建立先進監測預警體系和主動風險防控機制的迫切需求。聯合國《2030年可持續發展議程》亦明確提出建設包容、安全、韌性和可持續城市的重要目標。本項目擬融合多學科領域知識，發展面向超大城市地表沉降監測與機理解析的創新合成孔徑雷達干涉測量（InSAR）遙感方法，重點突破複雜地表形變模式與其自然及人為驅動因素之間關聯表徵的科學難題，從而支撐城市地表沉降風險評估與韌性提升。相較於傳統地面監測手段，InSAR具有大範圍覆蓋、高密度觀測及無需大規模地面儀器布設等突出優勢，尤其適合城市尺度地表形變的長時序精細監測。進一步融合人工智能（AI），特別是知識引導人工智能方法，有望充分利用地質、水文及城市環境等領域先驗知識，提升對地表沉降時空演變特徵及其環境驅動機制的識別與理解能力。本項目預期取得以下成果：（一）發展具有毫米級形變探測精度的先進InSAR監測方法，通過提高有效測量點密度及高空間分辨率大氣延遲改正，提升複雜城市環境中的形變監測能力；（二）建立融合地質學、水文學等多學科知識的地表沉降智能時空模式識別方法，揭示不同類型沉降的演變特徵及其潛在驅動因素；（三）構建融合領域知識與地理信息系統（GIS）分析的多層級、多階段城市地表沉降風險評估體系，服務於城市基礎設施安全與風險防控；以及（四）通過高水平學術論文、國際學術會議及專題研討會等形式推廣和交流研究成果。 本項目所形成的方法體系具有良好的可遷移性，可進一步應用於全球其他地表沉降高風險超大城市，為城市規劃、基礎設施管理及地質災害風險防控提供科學依據與技術支撐。同時，本研究對地表沉降形成與演變機制的深入認識，亦將為海平面上升、地下水動力過程及地表演化等相關地球科學問題提供新的研究基礎。

14207726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14207726.value: 基於持續學習的代理式多模態推薦系統

14207726.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14207726.value: Dr Chen, Jianting Dr Song, Zixing Dr Zhang, Zijian

14207726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207726.value: Modern Recommender Systems (RS) are pivotal for digital personalization, yet they are fundamentally constrained by three critical limitations. First, they rely on static, isolated user profiles, failing to capture the dynamic evolution of user preferences and collaborative signals, making the system difficult to scale and vulnerable to data sparsity issues. Second, they lack a holistic understanding of the fragmented multimodal, generic, and one-size-fits-all item representation. Finally, their practical deployment is severely limited by rigid, opaque system architectures that lack intelligent planning and reasoning, resulting in poor adaptability and fundamentally unexplainable recommendations. Recent advancements in Agentic AI offer a transformative paradigm to address these challenges. By reframing the recommender system as an intelligent agent capable of planning, reasoning, and memory, this approach can overcome the limitations of rigid pipelines. Furthermore, integrating principles from continual learning allows the agent to dynamically adapt to evolving user preferences from a continuous stream of interaction data. This proposal aims to bridge this gap by designing a novel framework, AgentRec, which integrates agentic workflows with continual learning and multimodal representation learning. This research is challenging as it requires a fundamental rethinking of the traditional recommendation pipeline. Our research will pioneer this new paradigm by systematically tackling the challenges in the following three-pronged aspects: (1) User Modeling with Dynamic Collaborative Memory: We aim to design and develop a dynamic memory framework for the agent that models continuous preference evolution by integrating individual learning with collaborative intelligence from user cohorts. (2) Unified and Personalized Multimodal Representation: We aim to construct a unified representation space that aligns fragmented multimodal data and enables personalized item projections, where an item's representation is dynamically conditioned on the user's context and persona. (3) Agentic Workflow with Explainability: We aim to architect an agentic workflow guided by dynamic user memory and personalized item representations, whose reasoning process is rendered into a verifiable causal graph for full transparency. In summary, by pursuing this cutting-edge research direction, our objective is to pioneer a new generation of recommender systems powered by agentic AI and continual learning. This proposal delivers a more intelligent, adaptive, and transparent framework capable of handling dynamic user needs and complex multimodal data. The potential applications of this framework are far-reaching, fundamentally changing how personalization is delivered in e-commerce, content streaming, and beyond. 現代推薦系統（Recommender Systems, RS）是數碼個人化服務的核心支柱，然而其發展受到三大關鍵限制的根本制約。第一，現有系統依賴靜態、孤立的用戶畫像，無法捕捉用戶偏好的動態演變及協同信號，導致系統難以擴展，且易受數據稀疏問題影響。第二，系統對零散的多模態、泛化且「一刀切」的物品表徵缺乏整全理解。第三，其實際部署嚴重受限於僵化、不透明的系統架構——此類架構缺乏智能規劃與推理能力，導致適應性欠佳，且推薦結果本質上無法解釋。 近年智能體式人工智能（Agentic AI）的進展，為應對上述挑戰提供了一個變革性的範式。透過將推薦系統重新構建為具備規劃、推理及記憶能力的智能體，此方法可突破僵化流程的限制。此外，融入持續學習（Continual Learning）的原理，可使智能體從持續不斷的互動數據流中動態適應用戶偏好的演變。 本計劃書旨在填補此一研究空白，設計一個嶄新框架——AgentRec，將智能體式工作流程與持續學習及多模態表徵學習相結合。此項研究極具挑戰性，因其需要對傳統推薦流程進行根本性的重新思考。本研究將透過系統性地應對以下三個層面的挑戰，開創此一嶄新範式： （一）基於動態協同記憶的用戶建模：我們旨在為智能體設計並開發一個動態記憶框架，透過整合個體學習與來自用戶群組的協同智能，對用戶偏好的持續演變進行建模。 （二）統一且個人化的多模態表徵：我們旨在構建一個統一的表徵空間，對齊零散的多模態數據，並實現個人化的物品投射，使物品的表徵能夠根據用戶的情境與人物特徵動態調整。 （三）具可解釋性的智能體式工作流程：我們旨在構建一個由動態用戶記憶與個人化物品表徵引導的智能體式工作流程，並將其推理過程轉化為可驗證的因果圖，以實現全面透明。 總括而言，透過推進此一前沿研究方向，我們的目標是開創由智能體式人工智能與持續學習驅動的新一代推薦系統。本計劃書提出一個更智能、更具適應性且更透明的框架，能夠應對動態的用戶需求及複雜的多模態數據。此框架的潛在應用範圍深遠，將從根本上改變電子商務、內容串流等領域提供個人化服務的方式。

14207926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14207926.value: 噬菌體導向之CAR-T細胞浸潤於肝細胞癌以增強標靶免疫治療

14207926.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14207926.value: Prof JIAO, Ju Prof Tse, Eric Wai Choi

14207926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207926.value: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has achieved remarkable success in treating hematopoietic tumors, but its efficacy against solid tumors such as hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains limited. Key challenges include poor tumor targeting/infiltration and undesired exhaustion of CAR-T cells. The PI has extensive expertise in identifying protein-, cell-, or tumor-targeting peptides from phage libraries, site-specifically displaying them on phages, and applying these phages for cancer diagnosis and immunotherapy (Science 2004, Nature Materials 2015, Nature Communications 2024, Nature Nanotechnology 2025). Recently, the PI successfully used fd phages—displaying tumor-homing and PD-L1-binding peptides—to target/infiltrate melanoma and block immune checkpoint recognition between programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) on T cells and its ligand (PD-L1) on cancer cells without side effects (Nature Nanotechnology 2025). Building on these foundations, we propose a novel strategy to functionalize CAR-T cells with filamentous fd phage—a genetically modifiable, clinically safe bionanofiber—to overcome the limitations of CAR-T therapy for HCC. The tip and sidewall of fd phage will be engineered to display two “humanized” peptides, PD-1-binding (PD1b) and HCC tumor-homing/infiltrating (HTH) peptides, identified from a phage library using human PD-1 and humanized HCC mice model as targets, respectively. The PD1b peptide on the tip of the resulting phages (fd-PD1b-HTH) will bind PD-1 overexpressed on CAR-T cells, anchoring the phages in an end-on configuration to create phage-functionalized CAR-T cells (CAR-T@fd-PD1b-HTH). The phage functionalization confers tumor-targeting/infiltrating capabilities to CAR-T cells and pre-emptively blocks PD-1/PD-L1 immune checkpoints to avoid CAR-T cell exhaustion. We hypothesize that CAR-T@fd-PD1b-HTH can specifically home to and infiltrate HCC tumors via HTH peptides on phage sidewall and block PD-1/PD-L1 immune checkpoints through PD1b peptides on phage tip, thereby preventing T-cell exhaustion and achieving efficient immunotherapy without adverse side effects. Aim 1 is to identify and validate humanized HTH peptides by our well-established in vivo/in vitro combination biopanning. Aim 2 is to identify and validate humanized PD1b peptides by microfluidics-assisted in vitro biopanning. Aim 3 is to evaluate CAR-T@fd-PD1b-HTH for HCC immunotherapy. The CAR-T@fd-PD1b-HTH cells, once intravenously injected into the humanized HCC mice models, will home to HCC tumors and infiltrate them. PD-1 on CAR-T@fd-PD1b-HTH cells is pre-blocked by phage tips and thus will not be recognized by PD-L1 on HCC cells, efficiently activating CAR-T cells to attack cancer cells. Successful completion of this project will lead to a new way of engineering CAR-T cells for effective solid tumor therapy. 嵌合抗原受體（CAR）T細胞療法在治療造血系統腫瘤方面已取得顯著成功，但其對肝細胞癌（HCC）等實體瘤的療效仍然有限。主要挑戰包括腫瘤靶向/浸潤能力不佳，以及CAR-T細胞出現非預期的耗竭現象。計畫主持人（PI）在從噬菌體庫中鑑定出可靶向蛋白、細胞或腫瘤的肽、將其定點展示於噬菌體上，以及應用這些噬菌體進行癌症診斷與免疫治療方面，擁有豐富的經驗。近期，PI成功利用展示腫瘤歸巢與PD-L1結合肽的fd噬菌體，靶向/浸潤黑色素瘤，並阻斷T細胞上之程序性細胞死亡蛋白1（PD-1）與癌細胞上其配體（PD-L1）之間的免疫檢查點辨識，且無副作用。在此基礎上，我們提出一新穎策略，以絲狀fd噬菌體——一種可基因修飾且臨床上安全之生物奈米纖維——對CAR-T細胞進行功能性修飾，以期克服CAR-T療法用於HCC之限制。 fd噬菌體的尖端與側壁將被設計為展示兩種「人源化」肽，分別為PD-1結合（PD1b）肽與HCC腫瘤歸巢/浸潤（HTH）肽，此二者係分別以人類PD-1及人源化HCC小鼠模型為標靶，從噬菌體庫中篩選鑑定而得。所得噬菌體（fd-PD1b-HTH）尖端上之PD1b肽將與CAR-T細胞上過度表現之PD-1結合，以末端朝上的構型將噬菌體錨定於細胞上，從而產生經噬菌體功能化之CAR-T細胞（CAR-T@fd-PD1b-HTH）。此噬菌體功能化賦予CAR-T細胞腫瘤靶向/浸潤能力，並預先阻斷PD-1/PD-L1免疫檢查點，以避免CAR-T細胞耗竭。我們假設CAR-T@fd-PD1b-HTH能經由噬菌體側壁上之HTH胜肽特異性地歸巢至HCC腫瘤並浸潤其中，並透過噬菌體尖端之PD1b肽阻斷PD-1/PD-L1免疫檢查點，進而防止T細胞耗竭，並在不產生不良副作用之情況下達成有效之免疫治療。 目標1為透過我們已建立且成熟之活體/體外組合生物篩選（biopanning）技術，鑑定並驗證人源化HTH肽。目標2為利用微流體輔助之體外生物篩選，鑑定並驗證人源化PD1b肽。目標3為評估CAR-T@fd-PD1b-HTH用於HCC免疫治療之成效。將CAR-T@fd-PD1b-HTH細胞經靜脈注射至人源化HCC小鼠模型後，該細胞將歸巢至HCC腫瘤並浸潤其中。CAR-T@fd-PD1b-HTH細胞上之PD-1因被噬菌體尖端預先阻斷，故不會被HCC細胞上之PD-L1辨識，從而有效激活CAR-T細胞以攻擊癌細胞。本計畫之順利完成，將為有效治療實體瘤之CAR-T細胞工程化修飾開闢新途徑。

14208426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14208426.value: 面向多機器人協作多軸增材製造的計算框架開發

14208426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208426.value: Recent advancements in robot-assisted additive manufacturing (AM) are advancing how large-scale and geometrically complex structures can be fabricated. Multi-robot collaboration further extends these capabilities by improving printing efficiency and enabling the creation of functionally sophisticated designs. However, the absence of a unified computational kernel remains a critical barrier to scaling multi‑robot AM systems, as current methods lack tight coupling between spatial printing path computation, task allocation, and motion coordination. This computational limitation also constrains the synchronization between offline planning and online robotic execution, leaving a critical gap between intelligent computation and reliable physical implementation needed to unlock the full potential of multi‑robot AM. This project addresses these research gaps through the development of a unified framework built upon major computational innovations. Firstly, a kernel‑based implicit modeling method will be developed to efficiently represent robots and workpieces for fast, time‑varying collision evaluation, forming the foundation for subsequent planning modules. Subsequently, a field‑guided toolpath generation and graph‑based region assignment strategy will be conducted to improve printing efficiency and quality while respecting kinematic constraints. From the motion planning aspect, a local–global motion planner will explicitly guarantee collision‑free trajectories and optimized dynamic performance for coordinated robot execution. These computational innovations will be tightly integrated with real‑time synchronization between simulation and fabrication, ensuring that virtual planning outcomes are accurately and reliably realized in physical processes. The proposed computational framework will enable intelligent multi‑robot collaboration, optimizing 3D material deposition sequences and ensuring collision‑free, efficient motion planning for multi-robot collaboration. The framework will be validated through two complementary setups: (1) a lab-based platform featuring three collaborating robot arms equipped with fused deposition modeling (FDM) print heads for fabricating topology‑complex structures in a support‑free manner, and (2) an industrial multi‑robot metal directed energy deposition (DED) system for large‑scale fabrication of turbine components with high surface quality. We will evaluate the scalability, geometric accuracy, and process efficiency of the proposed method and compare it with existing approaches to assess its practical advantages. The success of this project will pave the way for a new paradigm that tightly integrates computation and real‑world fabrication, transforming the production of complex structures across aerospace, automotive, and construction applications through robot‑assisted automation. 近年來，機器人輔助增材製造的進展，正持續推動大型複雜結構製造方式的轉變。多機器人協作進一步拓展了這些能力，不僅提升列印效率，也實現功能上更為複雜的設計。然而，目前缺乏統一的計算核心，仍是擴展多機器人增材製造系統的一項關鍵障礙。現有方法在空間列印路徑計算、任務分配與運動協調之間，仍缺乏緊密耦合。此外，這一計算層面的限制，也制約了離線規劃與線上機器人執行之間的同步，使智慧計算與可靠物理實施之間仍存在關鍵缺口；而這正是充分釋放多機器人增材製造潛力所必須解決的問題。 本项目將透過建立一個基於主要計算創新的統一框架，來解決上述研究缺口。首先，將開發一種基於核心函數的隱式建模方法，用以高效表示機器人與工件，從而支援快速且隨時間變化的碰撞評估，並為後續規劃模組奠定基礎。接著，將採用場引導的工具路徑生成方法，以及基於圖論的區域分配策略，在符合運動學約束的同時，提升列印效率與品質。從運動規劃的角度來看，將建立一種局部—全域運動規劃器，以明確保證無碰撞軌跡，並優化協調式機器人執行的動態性能。這些計算創新將與模擬和製造之間的即時同步緊密整合，確保虛擬規劃結果能夠在實體製程中被準確且可靠地實現。 所提出的計算框架將促進智慧化多機器人協作，優化三維材料沉積序列，並確保多機器人協作中的無碰撞且高效率運動規劃。該框架將透過兩種互補的系統配置進行驗證：（1）一個實驗室平台，配置三支協作機械手臂，並搭載熔融沉積成型（Fused Deposition Modeling, FDM）列印頭，用於以免支撐方式製造拓撲結構複雜的構件；以及（2）一個工業級多機器人金屬定向能量沉積（Directed Energy Deposition, DED）系統，用於大規模製造具有高表面品質的渦輪構件。我們將評估所提出方法的可擴展性、幾何精度與製程效率，並與現有方法進行比較，以評估其實際優勢。本計畫的成功將為緊密整合計算與真實世界製造的新範式鋪平道路，並透過機器人輔助自動化，改變航空、汽車與建築應用中複雜結構的生產方式。

14208626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14208626.value: 最大化細胞利用率的通用型液滴微流控單細胞測序平台

14208626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208626.value: Single-cell heterogeneity refers to the natural variation among individual cells, even within a seemingly identical group. Conventional bulk assays measure the ensemble average, often overlooking the specific actions and unique roles of individual cells. In contrast, single-cell sequencing enables the analysis of individual cells, facilitating the systematic dissection of cellular heterogeneity, which is crucial for comprehending how tissues function and why diseases such as cancer develop and resist treatment. Advances in droplet microfluidics have empowered single-cell omics by enabling high-throughput single-cell isolation within well-controlled environments. However, existing platforms achieve this high throughput at the expense of compromised cell utilisation, which hinders sequencing efforts. The proposed project will be aimed at developing a generalisable droplet-microfluidics-based workflow named M3-seq. This framework will maximise cell and data utilisation in single-cell sequencing by combining an innovative strategy for producing barcoded hydrogel beads and a multi-parametric high-fidelity enrichment process for droplets containing single cells. These features will allow M3-seq to achieve an unprecedented combination of high throughput, high cell utilisation efficiency, reduced sequencing efforts, and improved data quality. Once established and validated, M3-seq will allow researchers to clarify the unique functions of rare cell types, especially in plant cells, which are highly responsive to environmental changes during development. In addition to technical advances, the proposed project will involve collaboration with a clinical partner and plant biologist to formulate protocols suitable for clinical applications and genetically modified plant cells and biomass crops, respectively. This combined effort will expedite the transfer of the proposed technology to the identified beneficiaries both locally and globally. If successful, the proposed project will provide a valuable opportunity to translate scientific excellence in Hong Kong into societal impacts, thus helping transform the Greater Bay Area into an international powerhouse for monitoring minimal residual disease after treatment, improving biomass valorisation, and developing tangible bioenergy products. 單細胞異質性，是指即使在一群看似相同的細胞當中，各個細胞之間依然存在的自然差異。傳統的群體分析測量的是整群細胞的平均狀態，往往忽略了個別細胞的專一功能和獨特性。相比之下，單細胞測序能逐一分析單個細胞，讓我們得以有系統地剖析細胞之間的異質性；這對理解細胞組織如何運作，以及癌症等疾病為何會發生、又為何會對治療產生抗藥性等，都至關重要。液滴微流控技術的進步大大推動了單細胞體學的發展，在受到良好控制的環境中，以高通量的方式把單個細胞逐一分隔開來。然而，現有平台雖能達到高通量的要求，卻是以犧牲細胞利用率為代價，因而降低了後續測序的整體效率。 本計劃旨在開發一套以液滴微流控為基礎的通用實驗流程，命名為 M3-seq。這套系統結合了兩項創新：製備「帶條碼水凝膠微珠」的嶄新策略，以及一套多參數、高準確度、能精準挑選出僅含單個細胞之液滴的篩選程序，藉此在單細胞測序中最大化細胞與數據的利用率。憑藉這些特點，M3-seq 能同時實現高通量、高細胞利用效率、更少的測序工作量以及更佳的數據品質。一旦建立並通過驗證，M3-seq 將協助研究人員釐清稀有細胞類型的獨特功能，尤其是在發育過程中對環境變化極為敏感的植物細胞。除了技術上的突破，本計劃亦將與臨床夥伴及植物生物學家合作，分別制定適用於臨床應用，以及適用於基因改造植物細胞與生物質作物的操作規範。這種協同合作的模式，將加快把本技術推廣給本地及全球相關受惠對象。若計劃成功，將為把香港的卓越科研轉化為社會效益提供寶貴契機，協助大灣區發展成為國際重鎮，在治療後監測微量殘存疾病、提升生物質的利用價值，以及開發生物能源產品等方面發揮影響力。

14208826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14208826.value: 基於可編程貝塞爾超聲波束陣列的2.5D高深寬比超表面結構溶膠-凝膠玻璃模壓成形

14208826.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14208826.value: Prof Chen, Shih-Chi Prof Yi, Allen

14208826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208826.value: This proposal aims to develop a high filling ratio sol-gel molding method based on programmable ultrasonic Bessel-beam arrays, suitable for fabricating high aspect ratio (HAR) metasurface structures. Specifically, a custom-made holographic phase plate will be integrated with an ultrasonic transducer to modulate plane wave into a programmable Bessel array, which subsequently generates optimal acoustic fields to drive the sol-gel glass into deep cavities, achieving void-free filling and near-zero-shrinkage densification. Infrared glass with metasurface structures, which typically have arrays of HAR micro- to nanostructures of varying heights and sidewall slopes, offer advanced optical and photonic functions (comparing with conventional refractive/reflective optics and equal-height 2D metastructures). However, most current nanofabrication techniques, e.g., electron-beam lithography and two-photon lithography (TPL), suffer from low yield and high cost. Accordingly, development of low-cost, scalable and precise methods, e.g., sol-gel glass molding, that can replicate and fabricate complex metastructures, are imperative. To achieve the goal, a holographically-controlled Bessel-ultrasonic-assisted sol-gel glass molding (HBUSGM) technology will be developed. First, we will fabricate polymer masters via a custom-built multi-focus TPL system; next, a soft PDMS mold will be replicated and used for positive sol-gel infrared glass molding. To ensure the soft mold can be fully filled by the sol-gel glass, we will develop a holographically-controlled Bessel-ultrasonic system by integrating a phase plate with an ultrasonic transducer that converts plane acoustic wave into programmable Bessel beam arrays. The system will then generate optimal acoustic fields via superposition and order modulation to fully drive the sol-gel glass into each cavity. Finite element analysis and experiments will be designed and performed to understand and predict the filling process and ensure HAR cavity filling. After that, we will perform molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the solvent diffusion pathways and amorphous network formation during densification and to verify the effect of ultrasonic fields on solvent diffusion. Lastly, we will validate the entire fabrication chain and the error budget for each step experimentally; the molded infrared metalens will undergo unit-cell amplitude/phase verification and be evaluated in a dual-plane OAM-multiplexed holography system to confirm practical applicability. The result of this work will establish a general solution for large-scale fabrication of infrared glass with metasurface structures; this work will also enhance fundamental understanding of glass deformation in cavities with extreme aspect ratios under varying ultrasonic fields. The scalable fabrication platform will pave the way for their practical use in next-generation photonic and optical device manufacturing. 本項目旨在開發一種基於可編程貝塞爾超聲波束陣列的高填充率溶膠-凝膠模壓成形方法，以適用於2.5D高深寬比（HAR）超表面結構的製造。具體而言，我們將把定制的全息相位板與超聲換能器相集成，將平面波調製為可編程的貝塞爾超聲波束陣列，進而產生最優聲場以驅動溶膠-凝膠玻璃深入深腔內部，從而實現無空隙填充和近零收縮緻密化。 相較於傳統折射/反射光學元件及等高二維超表面，具有高度和側壁傾角各異的2.5D紅外玻璃超表面結構具備更先進的光學與光子功能。然而，現有的多數納米加工技術（如電子束光刻和雙光子光刻 TPL）均存在良率低、成本高的問題。因此，迫切需要開發如溶膠-凝膠玻璃模壓成形等低成本、可擴展且高精度的方法，以實現複雜超表面結構的複製與製造。 為實現上述目標，本項目將開發全息控制的貝塞爾超聲輔助溶膠-凝膠玻璃模壓成形（HBUSGM）技術。首先，我們將利用定制的多焦點TPL系統製備聚合物母模；隨後，複製PDMS軟模具，並將其用於正性溶膠-凝膠紅外玻璃的模壓成形。為確保溶膠-凝膠玻璃能夠完全填充軟模具，我們將開發一套全息控制的貝塞爾超聲系統，通過集成相位板與超聲換能器，將平面聲波轉換為可編程的貝塞爾超聲波束陣列。該系統將通過聲場疊加與階數調製產生最優聲場，以充分驅動溶膠-凝膠玻璃進入各個微腔。我們將設計並開展有限元分析與實驗，以深入理解並預測填充過程，確保高深寬比腔體的完全填充。此後，我們將進行分子動力學模擬，探究緻密化過程中的溶劑擴散路徑與非晶網路形成機制，並驗證超聲場對溶劑擴散的具體影響。最後，我們將通過實驗驗證整個製造鏈路的可靠性及各環節的誤差分配；模壓成形的紅外超透鏡將進行單元振幅/相位驗證，並在雙平面軌道角動量複用全息系統中進行評估，以確認其實際應用潛力。 本項目的研究成果將為紅外玻璃超表面結構的大規模製造提供一套通用解決方案，同時深化對極端深寬比腔體在不同超聲場作用下玻璃形變機制的基礎理解。該可擴展製造平臺將為下一代光子與光學器件的實際應用與製造鋪平道路。

14209726.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14209726.value: Prof Hu, Wei Prof LONG, Yi

14209726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14209726.value: This multi-disciplinary research project proposes, for the first time, the integration of a multi-functional reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) with energy-saving smart windows. More specifically, the concept of Multi-function transparent Intelligent reconfigurabLe surfacEs on Smart windows for wireless communicaTions, pOwering, seNsing and Energy-efficient smart buildings (MILESTONE) is proposed. RIS, also known as “programmable metasurface” or “software-defined metasurface”, is a promising technology for future generations of wireless systems (such as 6G mobile communication systems), integrated sensing and communications (ISAC), and IOT. RIS can dynamically and flexibly manipulate the EM waves in a programmable way, including the amplitude, phase, polarization and frequency. RIS can also be employed to adaptively control the scattering and reflection of electromagnetic waves, so as to create a smart radio propagation environment desirable for the wireless systems such as communications, sensing, imaging and localization. RIS is also demonstrated to be useful for wireless power transfer (WPT) and wirelessly charging low-power devices of IOT. Billions of IOT devices are used for medicine, industries and smart homes, etc. WPT via RIS can make these IOT devices become battery-free, very important for protecting our environment. Smart windows with dynamic modulation capability on light transmission offer a promising solution to improve energy efficiency and reduce environmental impacts in buildings [4]. Buildings consume about 30% to 40% of total energy, with heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems contributing 50% of building energy usage. Fig. 1b show a smart window. In the hot summer, smart windows can keep the room cool by reducing the sunlight transmitted into the room, hence reducing the energy consumption of air conditioning systems; during the cold winters, smart windows can keep the room warm by increasing the penetration of sunlight entering the room, hence reducing the energy consumption of heating systems. The project aims to investigate the theory, modelling, analysis, design, optimization and practical prototype development of a new generation of RIS, which can achieve multiple radio frequency (RF) functions of RIS as well as the optical and adaptive thermal control functions of energy-saving smart windows. MILESTONE will help tackle the key challenges of sustainable RF wireless systems (communications, sensing, imaging, WPT), energy-efficient smart buildings and sustainable environments simultaneously, bridging the gaps between researchers in the antennas, EM, RIS and wireless communications communities and material science, smart windows and smart building communities 這項跨領域研究計畫首次提出整合多功能可重構智慧表面（RIS）與節能智慧窗戶的方案。更具體地說，提出了多功能透明智慧重構面板的概念，適用於無線通訊、、無線電力傳輸、感知與節能智慧建築。RIS，也稱為軟體定義表面，是一項對未來無線系統（如6G通訊系統）、整合感測與通訊（ISAC）及物聯網（IoT）有前景的技術。RIS能動態且靈活地以可程式方式操控電磁波，包括振幅、相位、偏振及頻率。RIS也可用於自適應控制電磁波的散射與反射，從而創造一個適合通訊、感測、成像及定位等無線系統所需的智慧無線電傳播環境。RIS也被證明可用於無線電力傳輸及無線充電低功耗物聯網裝置。透過RIS的無線電力傳輸能讓這些物聯網裝置免電池，這對保護我們的環境非常重要。具備動態調制光線透射能力的智慧窗戶，提供了提升建築能源效率並減少環境影響的有前景解決方案。建築物約佔總能源的30%至40%，其中暖氣、通風和空調系統佔建築能源使用量的50%。在炎熱的夏季，智慧窗戶能透過減少陽光進入房間來保持涼爽，從而降低空調系統的能源消耗; 在寒冷的冬季，智慧窗戶能透過增加陽光穿透進來保持房間溫暖，從而降低暖氣系統的能源消耗。本計畫旨在探討新一代RIS的理論、建模、分析、設計、優化及實際原型開發，該系統能實現RIS的多重射頻（RF）功能，以及光學功能。這項研究將協助同時解決永續射頻無線系統（通訊、感測、影像、WPT）、節能智慧建築與永續環境的關鍵挑戰，彌合天線、電磁、資訊系統與無線通訊社群與材料科學、智慧窗戶與智慧建築社群之間的鴻溝

14209826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14209826.value: 用於中風後手部復健的液晶彈性體-摩擦奈米發電機自主軟體機器人的研發

14209826.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14209826.value: Prof Li, Wei Prof Liao, Wei-Hsin

14209826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14209826.value: With more than eight million post-stroke patients in Hong Kong and mainland China suffering from hand spasticity, there is an urgent need for effective rehabilitation. Characterized by abnormally elevated muscle resistance, the spasticity severely restricts hand motion and daily functioning, creating a substantial socioeconomic burden. Although clinical practice has shown that slow, periodic finger stretching and relaxation can alleviate spasticity, its long-term application is constrained by limited medical resources and high treatment costs. Soft rehabilitation robots, leveraging their compliance, programmable actuation, and safe human-machine interaction, have emerged as a promising solution capable of autonomously executing therapist-like protocols while reducing dependence on clinical resources and associated costs. Despite recent progress, current soft rehabilitation robots remain constrained by bulky and heavy mechatronic systems, which compromise wearing comfort and portability, reducing their suitability for home-based rehabilitation. In addition, current assessment of spasticity with soft rehabilitation robots relies heavily on physicians’ subjective judgment, lacking objective measures of muscle resistance that undermine accuracy and introduce deviations in intervention. The absence of continuous monitoring and remote feedback further prevents targeted physician guidance and parameter optimization, ultimately constraining rehabilitation outcomes. To address these challenges, this project aims to develop an autonomous soft robotic system for post-stroke hand rehabilitation by integrating smart materials, employing electrothermal liquid crystal elastomers (LCEs) as actuators and flexible triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) as sensors. The robotic system combines high wearing comfort with a fully integrated sensing–control–actuation architecture, enabling quantitative monitoring, autonomous evaluation, and real-time adaptive control to optimize rehabilitation outcomes. The Principal Investigator has extensive expertise and a strong track record in smart materials and soft robotics, providing a solid foundation for the proposed research. Practically, the project will advance through four stages: (i) design, fabrication, and characterization of LCE actuators and TENG sensors; (ii) development of a dynamic mechanical model to optimize nonlinear human–robot interaction; (iii) construction of an integrated sensing–control–actuation framework; and (iv) clinical validation supported by an autonomous evaluation system and a remote smart healthcare platform. Extensive preliminary results already obtained further confirm the feasibility of achieving this objective.
