We believe this innovative design represents a breakthrough in post-stroke hand rehabilitation, integrating recent advances in materials science, applied mechanics, robotics, and artificial intelligence to deliver an efficient, safe, and cost-effective therapeutic solution that accelerates functional recovery, enhances patients’ quality of life, and advances the development of next-generation medical robots. 香港和中國內地有超過八百萬中風後患者患有手部痙攣，因此迫切需要有效的復健治療。痙攣的特徵是肌肉阻力異常升高，嚴重限制了手部活動和日常生活功能，造成了巨大的社會經濟負擔。儘管臨床實踐表明，緩慢、週期性的手指伸展和放鬆可以緩​​解痙攣，但由於醫療資源有限和治療費用高昂，其長期應用受到限制。軟體復健機器人憑藉其柔順性、可編程驅動和安全的人機互動特性，已成為一種很有前景的解決方案，能夠自主執行類似治療師的操作方案，同時減少對臨床資源的依賴和相關成本。儘管近年來取得了一些進展，但目前的軟體復健機器人仍然受到笨重機械系統的限制，這影響了穿戴的舒適性和便攜性，降低了其在家庭復健中的適用性。此外，目前使用軟體復健機器人評估痙攣程度主要依賴醫生的主觀判斷，缺乏肌肉阻力的客觀測量方法，這會影響評估的準確性，並導致幹預措施偏差。缺乏持續監測和遠端回饋進一步阻礙了醫生進行有針對性的指導和參數優化，最終限制了復健效果。 為因應這些挑戰，本計畫旨在開發一種用於中風後手部復健的自主軟體機器人系統。該系統整合了智慧材料，採用電熱液晶彈性體（LCE）作為驅動器，柔性摩擦奈米發電機（TENG）作為感測器。該機器人系統兼具高佩戴舒適性和完全整合的感測-控制-驅動架構，能夠進行定量監控、自主評估和即時自適應控制，從而優化復健效果。專案負責人擁有豐富的智慧材料和軟體機器人領域的專業知識和卓越的研究成果，為本研究奠定了堅實的基礎。計畫將分四個階段進行：（i）LCE驅動器和TENG感測器的設計、製造和表徵；（ii）開發動態力學模型以優化非線性人機互動；（iii）建構整合的感測-控制-驅動框架；（iv）透過自主評估系統和遠距智慧醫療平台進行臨床驗證。目前已獲得的大量初步結果進一步證實了實現該目標的可行性。我們相信，這項創新設計代表了中風後手部復健的突破，它融合了材料科學、應用力學、機器人技術和人工智慧領域的最新進展，提供了一種高效、安全且經濟的治療方案，能夠加速功能恢復，提高患者的生活質量，並推動下一代醫療機器人的發展。

14210126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14210126.value: 智慧吞咽式膠囊機器人操作關鍵技術

14210126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14210126.value: Prof Bakheet, Nader Prof LI, Zhen Prof Tang, Raymond Shing-yan

14210126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14210126.value: Gastrointestinal (GI) diseases, including cancers and obstructive disorders, remain among the most prevalent and deadly conditions worldwide. According to the WHO, GI cancers account for over one-third of global cancer deaths. This high mortality, combined with the burden of non-malignant disorders, highlights the urgent need for advanced diagnostic and therapeutic technologies. Current methods have limitations: (1) flexible endoscopy is invasive, risks bleeding and perforation, and has limited reach in the GI tract; (2) capsule endoscopy, though minimally invasive, is restricted to passive imaging without active navigation or intervention. Thus, next-generation “surgical capsule” platforms capable of both diagnosis and therapy are urgently needed. Prior studies have demonstrated swallowable capsules capable of site-specific inspection and drug release, yet the therapeutic capabilities required for a swallowable robotic platform remain largely unrealized. Key challenges include: 1) active navigation: existing systems depend on passive peristalsis or single-magnet actuation, inadequate for reliable motion in tortuous lumens; 2) lack of haptic feedback: absence of force sensing increases tissue injury risk; 3) vision-only limitation: inability to interpret deformable tissue or subtle lesions without multimodal sensing; 4) workflow isolation: no synergistic framework linking navigation, perception, and surgical decision-making. This project aims to overcome these barriers by: (1) developing a dual-capsule system with decoupled multi-channel magnetic actuation, a three-axis propulsion module, and flexible dual-arm manipulators for grasping, traction, and cutting; (2) enabling wireless multimodal force sensing and closed-loop control for safe, reproducible tissue interaction; (3) achieving multimodal surgical perception through real-time 3D/4D GI reconstruction and fusion of visual–haptic–language modalities; and (4) establishing a hierarchical control framework coordinating task-level control, workflow-level decision-making, and surgeon-in-the-loop collaboration. Together, these advances aim to transform capsules from passive imagers into intelligent surgical partners capable of context-aware, safe, and efficient intra-intestinal intervention. The impact of the proposed study will include the following beneficiaries: 1) R&D community: creation of a reproducible capsule-surgery reference platform integrating actuation, sensing, perception, and control, with open datasets, coordinated IP strategy, and training modules to accelerate research translation. 2) Clinicians & patients: co-designed workflows with GI teams will enable multi-task interventions in fewer insertions, reduce bleeding/perforation risk, shorten procedures, and improve access to challenging anatomy, with staged preclinical/clinical validation aligned to clinical standards. 3) Healthcare & society: reduced complications and hospital stay, and a viable pathway to clinical-grade devices through industrial partnerships and spinoffs, driving innovation in medical robotics and endoscopy. 胃腸道疾病仍是全球最常見、致死率最高的疾病之一，其中胃腸道癌症占全球癌症死因逾三分之一。現有方法局限明顯：軟式內鏡有創、有出血穿孔風險且探查範圍有限；膠囊內鏡雖微創，但僅能被動成像，無法主動導航或干預。因此，亟需兼具診療功能的下一代“膠囊”。 當前可吞服膠囊在治療能力上遠未成熟，主要挑戰包括：主動導航依賴蠕動或單磁驅動，難以適應彎曲管腔；無觸覺回饋，易致組織損傷；僅靠視覺，無法識別細微病變；導航、感知與決策相互割裂。本專案擬攻克這些瓶頸：（1）開發雙膠囊系統，含解耦多通道磁驅動、三軸推進模組及柔性雙臂操作器；（2）無線多模態力感知與閉環控制，實現安全、可重複的組織操作；（3）通過即時3D/4D重建及視覺-觸覺-語言融合，實現多模態手術感知；（4）建立分層控制框架，協調任務、流程與醫生參與。最終將膠囊從被動成像器轉變為情境感知、安全高效的腸內智慧手術助手。 預期受益：對研發社區，提供可複現的膠囊手術參考平臺（含驅動、感知、控制），配套開放資料集、加速轉化；對臨床與患者，通過消化科協同設計，減少插入次數、降低出血穿孔風險、縮短手術時間、改善複雜解剖部位的可達性，並開展分階段臨床前/臨床驗證；對醫療與社會，減少併發症和住院時長，通過產業合作與衍生企業推動臨床級設備落地，促進醫療機器人與內鏡創新。

14210426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14210426.value: 面向安全內視鏡手術的超細長柔性操作臂多模態本體感知和精準閉環力位控制

14210426.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14210426.value: Prof Li, Hongsheng Prof Ren, Hongliang Prof YEUNG, Trevor Ming-Yee

14210426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14210426.value: Endoscopic surgery features a minimally invasive procedure for examining and treating diseases within tubular, confined anatomical cavities, like digestive and urinary systems. To improve its efficacy and efficiency, some flexible endoscopic surgical robots (FESRs) were developed in the last decade. During operation, empowering the robotic instruments with multi-modal proprioceptive sensing (e.g., pose, force) is essential to effectively “move the surgeon's hands to the operational site”. Nevertheless, the development of state-of-the-art FESRs mostly focuses on enhancing mechanical dexterity and motion execution. Because ultra-slender (length > 1200 mm, diameter < 3.5 mm) flexible robotic manipulators (uSFRM) in endoscopic surgery pose formidable challenges on implementing single-modal or even multi-modal sensing. Thus, current uSFRMs have no capability of precise closed-loop position/force control, which hinders the precision of FESR’s control, and ultimately affects the safety of endoscopic surgery. The project aims to develop the world’s first uSFRM and FESR with multi-modal proprioceptive sensing, including shape with twist, pose, traction and grasping force. In detail, the PI proposes to develop a multi-sensory uSFRM based on our previously developed parallel continuum wrist (PCW). The project has four progressive research steps: 1) mechanical structure design, 2) sensing algorithms, 3) closed-loop control and 4) system integration & preclinical validation. In step 1), the PCW will incorporate fiber Bragg grating (FBG) and vision sensors while maintaining its original transendoscopic dimensions (diameter = 2.5~3.0 mm). Besides, learning-based methods will be used to model its kinetostatic in real time and optimize structural parameters. In step 2), a simultaneous hierarchical architecture will be designed to perform four-modality proprioceptive sensing with different strategies: shape with twist - deep learning-based method; pose - marker detection on end-effector’s bottom; traction - model-based traction estimation; grasping force - Hooke’s law on the distal side. In step 3), closed-loop position/force control will be built to improve the end-effector’s motion accuracy and tissue interaction. In step 4), integrating them, a state-of-the-art FESR will be developed and validated by preclinical tests in ex vivo & in vivo. The project has great impacts: First, the research work will achieve technological breakthroughs in the mechanical structure of miniature flexible manipulators, multi-modal sensing for surgical instruments and surgical robotic systems; Second, the FESR has promising potential for clinical translation, which is meaningful for clinical treatment, contributing to more precise intuitive operation for surgeons and safer surgical outcomes for patients.

14210526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14210526.value: 面向檢索增強推理的高效向量數據管理

14210526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14210526.value: Machine learning models, particularly large language models (LLMs), have revolutionized industries by powering applications like question answering and image generation. Recent advances have also created multi-stage pipelines for processing unstructured data (e.g., images, texts, and videos), where models act as operators similar to SQL functions (e.g., filter, join, map). However, these approaches demand immense computational resources, leading to high monetary costs for model inference. To mitigate this, retrieval-augmented inference (RAI) techniques leverage vector similarity search to minimize model invocations. We focus on two key RAI methods: Output Substitution and Semantic Join. Output Substitution predicts a model's output y for input x by mapping x to an embedding vector e(x), then searching a precomputed reference set of similar objects with known outputs. If matches are consistent, x reuses those outputs, skipping inference. Semantic Join identifies related pairs across two sets X and Y (e.g., matching research topics to papers) by embedding objects, searching for similarities, and applying inference only to promising pairs—avoiding exhaustive enumeration. While vector databases and similarity search techniques have been extensively studied, they fall short for RAI due to unique demands. For Output Substitution, reference sets must be dynamic and capacity-limited, balancing representativeness for input objects while keeping high diversity among themselves to maximize reuse. Semantic Join requires on-the-fly index construction, as target sets may emerge from prior operations. RAI also needs advanced queries beyond standard top-k vector retrieval, such as diversity-aware and threshold-based search, or joins on vector datasets. These new challenges motivate us to develop novel algorithms and efficient systems tailored for RAI. Algorithmically, we will create strategies for maintaining reference sets for Output Substitution, building on-demand indexes for Semantic Join, and processing advanced queries in RAI. System-wise, we will develop efficient implementations of our algorithms by considering the hardware characteristics (e.g., memory hierarchies, multi cores, NUMA) and maximizing resource utilization, while exploring disk-based strategies for cost savings, GPUs for acceleration, distributed engines for scaling, and cloud deployment for accessibility. Project outcomes will provide foundational infrastructure for LLM-driven applications, reducing costs and accelerating AI adoption. They will also advance vector database techniques, broadening their utility in data management and AI applications. 機器學習模型，特別是大語言模型（LLMs），已透過賦能問答和圖像生成等應用，為各行各業帶來變革。近期的進展更創造出處理非結構化數據（如圖像、文本和影片）的多階段流水線。在這些流水線中，模型的運作方式類似於 SQL 函數運算子（例如篩選、連接、映射）。然而，這些方法需要巨大的計算資源，導致模型推理的資金成本高昂。 為了緩解這一問題，檢索增強推理（RAI）技術利用向量相似度檢索來盡可能減少模型調用。我們聚焦於兩種核心的 RAI 方法：輸出替代（Output Substitution）與語義連接（Semantic Join）。輸出替代透過將輸入 x 映射為嵌入向量 e(x)，並在一個已知輸出的預計算參考集中檢索相似對象，以此預測模型對輸入 x 的輸出 y。若匹配結果一致， x 即可複用這些輸出而無需進行推理。語義連接則旨在識別兩個集合 X 與 Y 之間的相關對象對（例如將研究課題與論文進行匹配）。它透過對對象進行嵌入、檢索相似度，並僅對具有潛力的對象對執行推理，從而避免了窮舉枚舉。 儘管向量數據庫和相似度檢索技術已得到廣泛研究，但由於 RAI 的獨特需求，現有技術仍有力不從心之處。對於輸出替代，參考集必須是動態且容量受限的，既要平衡對輸入對象的代表性，又要保持自身的高度多樣性，以最大化複用率。對於語義連接，由於目標集合可能源自先前的操作，因此需要即時（on-the-fly）構建索引。此外，RAI 還需要超越標準 top-k 向量檢索的高級查詢，例如具備多樣性感知和基於閾值的檢索，或是在向量數據集上進行連接。 這些新挑戰激發我們開發專為 RAI 定制的新穎算法與高效系統。在算法層面，我們將制定維護輸出替代參考集的策略、構建語義連接的按需索引，並處理 RAI 中的高級查詢。在系統層面，我們將結合硬件特性（如內存層次結構、多核、NUMA）並最大化資源利用率，以此實現算法的高效落地。同時，我們還將探索基於磁盤的成本節約策略、利用 GPU 進行加速、採用分佈式引擎進行擴展，以及通過雲端部署提升可用性。 本項目的研究成果將為大模型驅動的應用提供底層基礎設施，從而降低成本並加速人工智能的普及。此外，這些成果還將推進向量數據庫技術的發展，拓寬其在數據管理和人工智能應用中的實用價值。

14210626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14210626.value: 利用新興的分層記憶體實現虛擬化雲端的現代化

14210626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14210626.value: Due to the scaling limitations of DRAM technology, memory tiering has emerged as a vital solution to address the increasing demand for memory in various applications. Memory tiering involves integrating traditional DRAM with new memory technologies that offer varying capacity, latency, and cost characteristics, such as Non-Volatile Memory (NVM) and Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA)-attached or Compute Express Link (CXL)-attached memory. Due to its nice potential, tiered memory management has attracted extensive research interest, with kernel-based systems leading development. Nevertheless, the system support for the virtualized cloud infrastructure receives relatively less attention. To fill up this void, our recent research study, Demeter, for the first time reveals the significant performance overhead associated with existing hypervisor-based solutions; moreover, it advocates for an innovative guest-delegated approach to foster a productive synergy between the guest and hypervisor. Building on the success of Demeter, this research project aims to further explore how to modernize virtualized clouds with the emerging tiered memory in a broader context. First, for long-running virtual machine (VM) instances, this research will address two critical yet unresolved challenges that could significantly hinder Demeter’s effectiveness in production environments: the performance variability due to memory sharing and hotness skewness within hugepages. Our plan is to reinforce Demeter with a guest-assisted bandwidth monitoring mechanism and a hierarchical dual-tree hotness tracking: the former facilitates the control and throttling on the per-VM bandwidth consumption to prevent memory resource monopolization, while the latter enables selective, fine-grained hotness tracking with low overhead. Second, this research will extend to enable cloud serverless (or Function-as-a-Service (FaaS)) platforms to leverage the cost and capacity advantages of tiered memory, substantially improving the notorious cold start problem. The key innovation lies in proposing a tiered snapshot restoration and a fork-and-replay offline hotness profiling mechanism that classifies function memory into multiple categories based on access patterns and accommodates them in appropriate memory tiers of different characteristics. This research is particularly important for Hong Kong, as its success will pave the way for the modernization of virtualized cloud infrastructures, ensuring that both long-running VM instances and transient serverless functions can benefit from the cost and capacity advantages offered by the emerging tiered memory. This will bring substantial commercial values and benefits to a wide range of service users and providers, including end-users, enterprises, and government entities. 由於動態隨機存取記憶體（DRAM）技術在擴展性方面存在侷限，分層記憶體（Memory Tiering）已成為滿足各類應用日益增長的記憶體需求的一項關鍵解決方案。分層記憶體旨在將傳統的DRAM與具有不同容量、延遲和成本特性的新型記憶體技術相結合，例如非揮發性記憶體（NVM），以及透過遠端直接記憶體存取（RDMA）或快速運算連結（CXL）連接的記憶體。憑藉其巨大的潛力，分層記憶體管理已經吸引了廣泛的研究興趣，其中基於作業系統核心的研究正蓬勃發展。然而，針對虛擬化雲端基礎設施的系統支援卻較少受到關注。為了填補這一空白，我們近期的研究項目Demeter首次揭示了現有基於虛擬機管理程式（hypervisor）的解決方案所帶來的顯著效能開銷；同時，該研究提倡採用一種創新的客體委託（guest-delegation）方法，以促進客體（guest）和虛擬機管理程式（hypervisor）之間的高效協同。 在Demeter取得成功的基礎上，本研究項目旨在進一步探索如何在更廣泛的背景下，利用新興的分層記憶體來實現虛擬化雲端的現代化。首先，針對長時間運行的虛擬機（VM）實例，本研究將解決兩個關鍵且尚未解決的挑戰，這些挑戰可能會嚴重阻礙Demeter在生產環境中的有效性：由記憶體共享引起的效能波動，以及大頁（hugepages）內部的熱度分佈不均。我們的計劃是透過客體輔助的頻寬監控機制和階層式雙樹熱度追蹤技術來強化Demeter：前者有助於控制和限制每個虛擬機的頻寬消耗，避免單一虛擬機獨佔記憶體頻寬資源；後者則能夠以較低的開銷實現選擇性、細粒度的熱度追蹤。其次，本研究將應用範圍擴展至雲端無伺服器（Serverless，或函數即服務）平台，使其能夠利用分層記憶體的成本和容量優勢，從而大幅緩解長期困擾雲端架構的冷啟動（cold start）問題。其核心創新在於提出一種分層快照還原機制，以及一種分叉重放的離線熱度分析機制，從而能夠根據存取模式將函數記憶體分為多個類別，並將它們放置於具有不同特性的適當記憶體層中。 這項研究對香港尤為重要，因為它的成功將為虛擬化雲端基礎設施的現代化鋪平道路，確保長時間運行的虛擬機實例和生命週期短暫的無伺服器函數都能從新興分層記憶體所提供的成本和容量優勢中受益。這將為終端用戶、企業與政府等廣大的服務使用者與提供者，帶來巨大的商業價值與效益。

14211126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14211126.value: 用於全血循環腫瘤細胞檢測的石墨烯霍爾傳感器

14211126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14211126.value: The ability to detect rare circulating cells, especially circulating tumor cells (CTCs, often < 10 cells/mL in whole blood), is of increasing importance in early cancer diagnosis and treatment monitoring. Fluorescence based workflows (e.g., the CELLSEARCH System) are the current gold standard and rely on immunomagnetic capture, enrichment, multiple wash steps, and optical labeling, which can delay turnaround and may lead to the loss of target cells. Here, leveraging the Hall effect, we propose an all-electronic, high-throughput approach that directly reads the magnetic signatures of immunomagnetically labeled cells (no solid phase capture, no enrichment, no wash steps, no fluorescent labeling, and no optical detection) in whole blood flowing over micro graphene Hall sensors (µGHSs) at ≥ 50 mL/h. The proposed research aims to develop scalable µGHS arrays on chemical vapor deposition (CVD) grown hBN-Gr-hBN heterostructures and integrate them with wafer-scale photolithography and multi-channel microfluidics for real-time, high-throughput operation. High-quality hBN-Gr-hBN will be prepared via CVD on Ni-Cu gradient alloys with controlled stacking, followed by transfer and fabrication into six-terminal µGHS arrays. Encapsulating high-mobility graphene in hBN minimizes electron scattering and boosts sensitivity, enabling single-event detection in whole blood. Each chip will host 20 microfluidic channels for high throughput, each with 24 µGHSs organized in three 8-sensor clusters to yield robust spatiotemporal event signatures and suppress false positives. Validation will progress from PBS to human serum to whole blood controls, and finally to clinical ovarian cancer patient samples for a blinded, head-to-head comparison with the CELLSEARCH System. The proposed project is novel and highly notable for multiple reasons: 1) electronic detection of CTCs in whole blood with minimal sample processing and loss; 2) large-area hBN-Gr-hBN growth via a PECVD/CVD route that advances layered 2D carbon nanomaterial synthesis; 3) scalable, wafer-level fabrication of high mobility µGHS arrays suitable for point-of-care integration; 4) a 20-channel, 24-sensor-per-channel architecture that delivers high throughput (≥ 50 mL/h), whole blood operation with built-in consensus logic; and 5) first-of-its-kind blinded benchmarking of graphene Hall sensing against the clinical gold standard for CTCs. The success of the project will lead to applications of µGHSs in rapid and highly sensitive cellular diagnosis of CTCs, and thus early cancer diagnosis. 檢測稀有循環細胞、尤其是循環腫瘤細胞（circulating tumor cells, CTCs；全血中含量通常少於10個/毫升）的能力，對癌症的早期診斷及治療監測日益重要。以螢光為基礎的檢測流程（如CELLSEARCH系統）為現時的臨床金標準，其依賴免疫磁性捕獲、富集、多重清洗步驟及光學標記，不僅延長檢測周轉時間，亦可能造成目標細胞損失。本項目基於霍爾效應（Hall effect），提出一種全電子化、高通量的檢測方法：全血以≥50毫升/小時的流速流經微型石墨烯霍爾傳感器（micro graphene Hall sensors, µGHSs），直接讀取經免疫磁性標記細胞的磁信號特徵，全程無需固相捕獲、富集、清洗步驟、螢光標記及光學檢測。 本研究旨在基於化學氣相沉積（chemical vapor deposition, CVD）生長的hBN-Gr-hBN（六方氮化硼-石墨烯-六方氮化硼）異質結構，開發可規模化的µGHS陣列，並將其與晶圓級光刻技術及多通道微流控系統整合，實現實時、高通量運作。高質量hBN-Gr-hBN將以CVD法於鎳銅梯度合金上製備，並精確調控其堆疊結構，隨後經轉移及微加工製成六端µGHS陣列。以hBN封裝高遷移率石墨烯可將電子散射減至最低並提升靈敏度，從而實現全血中的單一事件檢測。每塊晶片將設有20條微流控通道以達致高通量，每條通道配置24個µGHS，以每8個為一簇、共三簇的方式排列，藉此產生穩健的時空事件信號特徵並抑制假陽性。驗證工作將循序推進：由磷酸鹽緩衝液（PBS）至人血清及全血對照樣本，最終以臨床卵巢癌患者樣本與CELLSEARCH系統進行盲法頭對頭比較。 本項目具有多方面的創新性與重要意義：（1）以電子方式直接檢測全血中的CTC，樣本處理步驟及細胞損失均減至最少；（2）透過等離子體增強化學氣相沉積（PECVD）/CVD路線實現大面積hBN-Gr-hBN生長，推動層狀二維碳納米材料合成技術的發展；（3）可規模化的晶圓級高遷移率µGHS陣列製備，適合臨床現場即時檢測的整合應用；（4）20通道、每通道24個傳感器的架構，實現≥50毫升/小時的高通量全血檢測，並內置共識判定邏輯；（5）首次以盲法將石墨烯霍爾傳感技術與CTC檢測的臨床金標準進行對照基準評估。本項目的成功將推動µGHS於CTC快速、高靈敏細胞診斷中的應用，從而促進癌症的早期診斷。

14211226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14211226.value: 邁向SSD圖ANN搜索新范式：優化I/O瓶頸的SSD存內聚合

14211226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14211226.value: Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search (ANNS) plays a critical role in AI-driven applications. It enables the retrieval of vectors that are close to a given query point within a dataset using an index. Among various ANNS methods, graph-based indexing such as Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) offers exceptional speed and accuracy. However, its high memory consumption makes it prohibitively expensive for large-scale datasets. To address this, SSD-resident graph-based indexing has emerged as a cost-effective alternative, leveraging limited memory and affordable Solid State Drives (SSDs). Yet, the relatively slow I/O performance of SSDs introduces significant overhead, which becomes a bottleneck. Therefore, minimizing I/O overhead is essential for scaling SSD-resident graph-based indexing in ANNS applications. In this project, we present a novel in-SSD aggregation framework that redefines how vector data and neighbor lists are accessed and transferred in graph-based ANNS. Rather than issuing separate I/O requests for each vector and its neighbors, our approach aggregates them directly within the SSD, enabling unified retrieval through a single I/O operation. This significantly reduces the number of I/O requests—especially impactful when each vector is linked to hundreds of neighbors—and mitigates read amplification by eliminating redundant data access. Unlike prior in-SSD solutions that attempt to offload the entire vector search process into SSDs—devices inherently optimized for storage, not processing—our framework strategically shifts only the aggregation logic into SSDs. This targeted design unlocks new performance potential for SSD-resident ANNS systems, paving the way for faster and more scalable similarity search. The proposed framework comprises three core tasks. First, we will design efficient in-SSD aggregation mechanisms to group vectors and their neighbor lists into a single I/O request. Building on this, we will develop prefetching and caching strategies to minimize I/O overhead and integrate them into SSD-resident ANNS workflows. Second, we will architect new SSD software components to support in-SSD aggregation, including a priority-aware task model and queue management system that enables concurrent execution of vector aggregation and storage operations. We will also explore host/SSD interfaces for streamlined command dispatch and result retrieval. Finally, as a system-level research effort, we will implement our techniques on in-SSD development platforms and release the prototype as open-source to foster reproducibility and community engagement. This project is especially relevant to Hong Kong, where vector search powers AI-driven analytics vital to the city’s role as a global center for business, trade, and finance. 近似最近鄰搜尋（ANNS）在人工智慧驅動的應用中扮演著關鍵角色。透過索引技術，它能從大型資料集中快速檢索出與查詢點相近的向量。在眾多 ANNS 方法中，分層可導航小世界（HNSW）等基於圖的索引展現了卓越的速度與精度。然而，這類方法的記憶體消耗極為龐大，處理大規模資料集時成本往往高昂。為了應對此挑戰，基於 SSD 的圖索引技術逐漸受到重視，作為一種經濟高效的替代方案，它充分利用有限的記憶體資源與價格適中的固態硬碟（SSD）。但 SSD 相對較慢的 I/O 效能仍帶來顯著開銷，成為系統瓶頸。因此，在 ANNS 應用中擴展 SSD 基礎的圖索引技術時，如何最大限度降低 I/O 開銷至關重要。 本研究提出一種新穎的 SSD 內部聚合框架，重新定義了基於圖的 ANNS 中向量資料與鄰居清單的存取與傳輸方式。不同於傳統針對每個向量及其鄰居分別發起 I/O 請求的方法，我們的框架直接在 SSD 內部完成聚合，使得單次 I/O 操作即可完成統一檢索。此設計顯著減少了 I/O 請求數量，尤其在每個向量關聯數百個鄰居的場景下效果尤為突出，並透過消除冗餘存取緩解讀取放大問題。與過往嘗試將整個搜尋過程卸載至 SSD 的解決方案不同，我們僅策略性地將聚合邏輯遷移至 SSD 內部，釋放了基於 SSD 的 ANNS 系統新的效能潛力，為更快速且可擴展的相似度搜尋鋪平道路。 該框架包含三個核心任務：(1) 設計高效的 SSD 內部聚合機制，將向量與鄰居清單組合成單一 I/O 請求，並整合預取與快取策略以最小化 I/O 開銷。(2) 建立新的 SSD 軟體元件以支援聚合，包括支援向量聚合與儲存操作並發執行的優先權感知任務模型與佇列管理系統，同時探索主機與 SSD 之間的高效接口。(3) 在 SSD 開發平台上實現相關技術，並開源原型系統，以促進研究可複現性與社群參與。 本計畫對香港具有特殊意義。向量搜尋技術是人工智慧驅動分析的基礎，而這些分析應用對於鞏固香港作為全球商業、貿易與金融中心的地位至關重要。

14211326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14211326.value: 基於各向高分辨OCT與可重構螺旋支點的動態管腔臟器內用遙操作冷凍活檢機器人

14211326.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14211326.value: Prof Ng, Sze Hang Calvin Prof Ren, Hongliang

14211326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14211326.value: Specimens of luminal organs, such as the respiratory and gastrointestinal tracts, are typically collected by single-bite forceps biopsy via the working channel of an endoscope. However, this technique does not allow adequate control of biopsy depth and tissue orientation and may generate crushing artifacts in specimens. Consequently, specimens may be of poor quality, leading to sampling errors and increasing the risk of false negatives, particularly for diseases that are difficult to detect with standard (white-light) endoscopy. Furthermore, physiological motions, such as respiration-induced lung displacement, can degrade imaging quality and destabilize forceps–tissue interactions, reducing biopsy yield. In contrast, cryobiopsy involves freezing the target area to preserve tissue integrity prior to specimen collection and thus affords intact specimens containing minimal artifacts. Moreover, combination of cryobiopsy with real-time, high-resolution lesion visualization by optical coherence tomography (OCT) reduces the risk of false negatives, thereby enhancing the effectiveness of endoscopic disease surveillance. Thus, integration of OCT with a cryobiopsy device could enable the collection of high-quality specimens and thereby enhance diagnostic accuracy. However, current 1300-nm OCT systems do not enable effective detection of subtle pathological changes and performance of high-quality cryobiopsy in clinical settings, as these systems (1) have low (~15-µm) resolution; (2) cannot achieve long-range, isotropic high-resolution imaging across a variety of luminal organ dimensions; (3) lack an adaptive endoscopic fulcrum and thus cannot generate artifact-free images of or accurately localize lesions in moving organs; and (4) do not enable precise telerobotic cryobiopsy and thus do not minimize physicians’ X-radiation exposure during procedures. In this proposed project, we will combine our 1060-nm OCT and robotic endomicroscopy technologies to develop a telerobotic cryobiopsy (TeleCryo) system featuring an ultrasmall (1-mm-diameter) volume-controlled cryobiopsy probe; an isotropic high-resolution ultrathin (0.6-mm-diameter) OCT fiber probe; a robotic endoscope; and a remote-control platform. The cryobiopsy probe will have an adjustable coolant flow, enabling efficient, volume-controlled tissue freezing. The distal tip of the OCT probe will have a three-dimensionally printed glass reflective–diffractive metalens powered by a physics-informed neural network, enabling isotropic high-resolution (~5-µm axial × 10-µm transverse) imaging over a 22-mm range. The robotic endoscope will have a patency-preserving reconfigurable helical fulcrum and a hydraulically actuated soft-robotic tip, enabling stabilized high-resolution imaging and image-guided cryobiopsy in moving luminal organs. The TeleCryo system will be validated in human anatomical and animal models and is expected to afford optimized endoscopic biopsy yields and advance patient management. 管腔器官（如呼吸道與胃腸道）的活檢多以單咬式活檢鉗經內視鏡工作通道取得。然而，此法受限於組織取向難以維持、易產生壓碎偽影，以及活檢深度控制不精確。對於白光內視鏡不易偵測的病變，更因取樣誤差而增加假陰性風險。此外，生理性運動（如呼吸引起的肺部位移）會劣化成像品質並使鉗-組織互作不穩定，降低標本獲取效率。 冷凍活檢透過凍結目標區域以保全組織完整性，可取得偽影最小的完整標本。若結合光學相干斷層成像（OCT）提供即時高解析病灶視覺化，可進一步降低假陰性，提升內視鏡監測效能。將OCT成像功能與冷凍活檢裝置整合，具備改善活檢品質與診斷準確度的潛力。然而，現行技術在臨床上對細微病理變化的偵測與高品質冷凍活檢仍未達最佳，主因包括：(1) 現有1300 nm OCT系統解析度受限（約15 µm）；(2) 需在多種管腔器官尺度下實現長距、等向性高解析OCT成像；(3) 缺乏可適應移動器官的內視鏡支點，導致影像偽影與病灶定位不準；(4) 難以精準執行遙操作冷凍活檢以降低術中醫師的輻射暴露。 基於我們既有的1060 nm OCT與機器人內視顯微技術，我們提出整合式遙操作冷凍活檢（TeleCryo）系統，結合超小體積可控之冷凍活檢探頭、等向性高解析OCT探頭、螺旋支點輔助機器人內視鏡與遠端控制平台。直徑1 mm的冷凍活檢探頭具可調式冷媒流型，可高效凍結組織並精準控制凍結體積。直徑0.6 mm的OCT探頭於遠端端頭整合3D玻璃列印的反射-繞射元透鏡，並結合物理引導神經網路，使其在22 mm成像範圍內達到約5 × 10 µm（軸向與橫向）的近等向性高解析成像。機器人內視鏡採用保持腔道通暢的可重構螺旋支點與液壓驅動柔性端頭，得以在移動中的管腔器官內提供穩定高解析成像並實現影像導引的冷凍活檢。我們將以解剖與動物模型進行遙操作冷凍活檢驗證。TeleCryo系統有望優化內視鏡活檢的標本獲取效率與診斷表現，並促進臨床病患管理的進步。

14211826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14211826.value: 具備宏微激光轉向功能用於軟牽引內鏡黏膜下剝離術的分布式磁驅動機械人系統

14211826.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14211826.value: Prof Lin, Rongfu Prof Yip, Hon-chi Prof Yu, Jiangfan

14211826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14211826.value: Endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) for early colorectal lesion remains a challenging, skill-dependent procedure with high risks of perforation. Most existing robotic solutions rely on conventional cable-driven mechanism and electrosurgical knife, suffering from reduced precision, bulky tethers, lack of stable anchoring, difficult thermal damage control, and steep learning curve. In this project, we will develop a next-generation multi-magnet actuated miniature robot to address key challenges associated with current ESD robots, including enabling robot anchoring for stable operation, directly integrating dual instruments within the robot for tissue traction and lesion resection, and developing a robotic laser with large coverage and fast micro-motion. Specifically, we will develop a distributed-magnet, soft-tethered miniature robot under hybrid external permanent magnet (EPM)-electromagnetic (EM) actuation, an origami-based robotic laser steering module, and a novel theoretical framework featuring workspace analysis and control for selective manipulation of multiple magnetic targets in the confined space of the miniature robot. Overall, the proposed robotic system will be the first soft-tethered robot with multiple embedded magnets capable of performing complex surgical tissue resection, significantly improving robot maneuverability, anchoring stability, coordinated control of fully integrated instrument as well as lesion resection quality. The theoretical workspace and control frameworks not only support practical robot operation for a more effective ESD procedure, but also enhance clinical adoption potential by enabling scalability to higher degrees of freedom with a limited number of EM coils.

14212126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14212126.value: 用於增強心血管分析和訊號解讀的超聲-光電容積脈搏波描記雙模太集成穿戴式平台的研發

14212126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14212126.value: This project aims to develop an integrated wearable platform that combines a "Scan-and-Track" ultrasound module with a multi-wavelength photoplethysmography (PPG) sensing matrix to address the inherent complexities associated with PPG signal interpretation. By enabling in-situ and synchronous acquisition of blood vessel information, this platform will allow characterization and decomposition of signal contributions from arterial, venous, and capillary components, enhancing the reliability, accuracy, and interpretability of PPG signals in wearable devices while providing critical insights into vascular dynamics. PPG is widely used in wearable devices for cardiovascular monitoring due to its simplicity and ability to measure blood volume changes. However, its diagnostic capacity is limited because it cannot independently identify or analyze contributions from different vascular components. This "black-box" nature has hindered its reliability in clinical applications and constrained its use for continuous and comprehensive cardiovascular assessment. The proposed research addresses this critical challenge by integrating ultrasound technology, which provides precise blood vessel localization, with multi-wavelength photoplethysmography (MWPPG) to enable synchronized and contextualized signal acquisition. This innovative approach will overcome current knowledge gaps, allowing for a holistic assessment of arterial-venous interactions and their role in systemic and microcirculatory dynamics. The project will be conducted in three main steps. First, a wearable "Scan-and-Track" ultrasound module will be developed using phased array beamforming to dynamically locate and track arteries and veins in real time. This system will serve as the foundation for extracting the location and waveforms of the big blood vessels under the sensing area. The completed device will be tested at three body sites with different vascular distributions, using the ultrasound module to scan and locate vessels and MWPPG sensors to acquire wavelength- and location-specific PPG signals. This phase will also involve developing a physics-informed analytical model to interpret PPG signals and accurately decouple contributions from different vascular components. Finally, the clinical applications of the platform and model will be explored, with a focus on blood pressure estimation, arterial function evaluation, and disease classification through machine-learning algorithms. Through dual-modality integration, this project introduces a new level of precision and versatility to sensor signal analysis and cardiovascular monitoring. By bridging the gap between advanced sensing technologies and commercial wearable solutions, it will provide systematic guidelines for sensor optimization, improve diagnostic accuracy, and promote wearable health monitoring adoption. 本項目旨在開發一種雙模態集成穿戴式平台，該平台將「掃描追蹤」超聲模組與多波長光電容積脈搏波描記法 (PPG) 傳感器矩陣相結合，以精確解讀分析PPG 訊號。透過實現血管資訊的原位同步採集，該平台能夠表徵和分解來自動脈、靜脈和毛細血管成分的訊號貢獻，從而提高可穿戴設備中 PPG 訊號的可靠性、準確性和可解讀性，同時提供對血管動力學的關鍵洞察。 PPG 因其簡單性和測量血液容量變化的能力而被廣泛應用於心血管監測的可穿戴設備。然而，由於其無法獨立識別或分析來自不同血管成分的貢獻，因此其診斷能力受到限制。這種「黑箱」特性阻礙了其在臨床應用中的可靠性，並限制了其在連續、全面的心血管評估中的應用。本研究透過將能夠精確定位血管的超聲傳感技術與多波長光電容積脈搏波描記法 (MWPPG) 結合，實現了同步和情境化的訊號採集。這種創新方法將彌補缺失的解剖學信息，從而能夠對動靜脈相互作用及其在全身和微循環動力學中的作用進行全面評估。 該項目將分三個主要步驟進行。首先，將開發一種可穿戴的「掃描追蹤」超聲模組，該模組採用相控陣波束形成技術，能夠即時動態定位和追蹤動脈和靜脈。該系統將作為提取感測區域下大血管位置和波形的基礎。其次，將製造一種整合設備，該設備將超聲模組與MWPPG矩陣結合，以實現從多個血管層同步擷取訊號。完成的設備將在三個血管分佈不同的身體部位進行測試，測試中將使用超音波模組掃描和定位血管，並使用MWPPG感測器採集波長和位置特定的PPG訊號。此階段還將開發一個基於生理物理分析模型，用於解釋PPG訊號並準確分離不同血管成分的貢獻。最後，我們將探索該平台和模型的臨床應用，包括血壓估算、動脈功能評估以及透過機器學習演算法進行疾病分類。 透過雙模態融合，本項目將感測器訊號分析和心血管監測的精度和多功能性提升到了新的水平。透過彌合先進感測技術與商用穿戴式解決方案之間的差距，本項目將為PPG傳感器優化提供系統性指導，提高診斷準確性，並促進穿戴式健康監測的普及應用。

14212726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14212726.value: 機械力調控內質網功能的作用機制及其細胞層面效應研究

14212726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14212726.value: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is the central organelle governing protein folding, trafficking, calcium (Ca2+) storage, and lipid metabolism, serving as a cornerstone of diverse cellular processes such as cell proliferation and differentiation. To sustain these functions, the ER relies on the unfolded protein response (UPR), a critical mechanism for resolving stress and restoring proteostasis. ER dysfunction underpins diseases from neurodegeneration to cancer. Emerging evidence reveals that the ER is not only a biochemical powerhouse but also a direct mechanosensitive organelle, capable of sensing and responding to intracellular or extracellular mechanical forces. However, how the ER transduces mechanical inputs to regulate its core functions, which of its many diverse functions are mechanoregulated, and how this impacts cellular physiology remain largely unknown. To address this, we recently developed LIMER (Light-Induced Mechanostimulation of the ER), an innovative, non-invasive, and reversible tool that applies tunable mechanical force directly to the ER with spatiotemporal precision (Dev. Cell., 2024). Using LIMER, we have already demonstrated that ER-specific mechanostimulation elicits rapid Ca2+ efflux, disrupts ER-to-Golgi trafficking, and triggers stress responses, providing the first direct evidence on ER mechanosensitivity and mechanoregulation of some ER functions. This proposal builds on these pioneering findings to address three critical questions: (1) Scope: How does mechanostimulation regulate key ER functions, including trafficking, protein synthesis, and stress responses? (2) Mechanism: What molecular pathways underlie the mechanoregulation of ER functions? (3) Consequence: How does ER influence cellular behaviors, such as intercellular signaling, migration, and differentiation? To systematically map these processes, we will leverage the multidisciplinary expertise of our team, including the PI’s extensive background in ER biology (PNAS, 2023; J. Biol. Chem., 2020; Front. Cell. Dev. Biol., 2022) and the Co-PI’s expertise in mechanobiology and mechanostimulator development (Cell Chem. Biol., 2022; PNAS, 2024; Dev. Cell., 2024). Our novel tool (LIMER) and established experimental platforms for ER function and cell activity assays uniquely position us to uncover those fundamental aspects of ER mechanobiology. This work will provide new insights into how mechanical forces regulate ER and cellular function and create a new framework for understanding how cells integrate physical cues to control their fundamental biology. In the long run, this work has broad implications for understanding mechanoregulation in health and disease, particularly in contexts such as neurodegeneration, cancer, and fibrosis, where ER dysfunction is a hallmark. 內質網是調控蛋白質摺疊與運輸、鈣離子儲存及脂質代謝的核心細胞器，亦是細胞增殖與分化等多種細胞過程的關鍵參與者。內質網依賴於未摺疊蛋白反應來維繫自身的穩態與功能。內質網功能障礙則是神經退行性疾病與癌症等多種疾病的病理基礎。 近年研究揭示，內質網不僅是生化代謝的樞紐，更是一種具機械敏感性的細胞器，能感知並回應細胞內外的機械力。然而，內質網如何將機械訊號轉化為功能調控、其哪些特定功能受機械力影響，以及此過程如何改變細胞生理活性，目前仍不清楚。 為突破上述難題，我們近期開發了「內質網光誘導機械刺激技術」LIMER。LIMER是一種創新、非侵入性且可逆的光控工具，能在時空尺度上精準且直接地向內質網施加可控機械力。利用LIMER，我們發現特異性刺激內質網可迅速誘發鈣離子外流、抑制蛋白質從內質網至高爾基體的運輸，並啟動未摺疊蛋白反應；這些結果首次為內質網的機械敏感性及其部分功能的機械調控提供了直接證據。 基於上述開創性發現，本項目擬系統性回答三個關鍵科學問題：（1）調控範圍——機械刺激如何調控內質網的關鍵功能，包括囊泡運輸、蛋白質合成與未摺疊蛋白反應？（2）調控機制——內質網功能的機械調控由哪些分子通路介導？ （3）調控結果——內質網對機械信號的響應如何影響細胞行為，如細胞間訊息傳遞、遷移與分化？ 為系統解析這些問題，我們將充分發揮團隊的跨領域優勢：項目負責人在內質網生物學方面擁有深厚積累，共同項目負責人在力學生物學與機械刺激裝置開發方面則具備豐富專長。結合新開發的LIMER工具，以及成熟穩定的內質網功能與細胞活性檢測平臺，我們具備獨特條件，可望闡明內質網力學生物學中的這些基本問題。 本研究的成果不僅將為理解機械力如何調控內質網及細胞功能提供新視角，也將建立一個嶄新的研究框架，用以解析細胞如何整合物理訊號來調控基本生物學過程。長遠而言，這項研究對於認識健康與疾病狀態下的力學調控具有廣泛意義，尤其適用於神經退行性疾病、癌症與纖維化等以內質網功能障礙為重要特徵的病理情境。

14213026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14213026.value: 安全的濫用遏制：可密鑰盲化的指數型可驗證隨機函數、定域密鑰暴露及密封元數據通道

14213026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14213026.value: Security on the open internet is subtle and must deter misuse without chilling legitimate use or coercing honest parties. Scenarios include subscriptions to online services, human verification for Tor/VPN users (e.g., a CAPTCHA result bit), code and certificate signing, and privacy-preserving authorization such as private e-cash/e-voting. Current approaches suffer from structural weaknesses, including heavy use of succinct non-interactive arguments of knowledge (SNARKs) for verifiable random function (VRF) relations, forced disclosure of certificate-authority private keys under coercion, and the absence of a verifier-only channel that conveys more than a hidden bit. We address these pain points with three technical contributions, from foundational primitives to improvements toward deployed systems. First, we formalize $d$-exposing anonymous tags ($d$-EAT) that ensure the ($d+1$)-st rate-limit violation reveals a secret key. We construct $d$-EAT from exponent-verifiable random functions (eVRFs) with a key-blinding property so that verifiers avoid checking a zero-knowledge proof (ZKP) of the full VRF relation. A prover instead proves that a committed key matches a blinded key, and the commitment composes with other ZKPs in larger anonymous systems while preserving extraction on misuse. This foundational layer enforces per-epoch $d$-use limits through a simple double-spending equation and supports ring- and group-based variants with fast revocation without heavyweight SNARKs. Second, we design self-menacing signatures (SMS) that reveal only a scoped secret on conflict, while non-conflicting signatures remain valid. Here, a signature binds a pair (context, payload), and conflict means signing two different payloads under the same context. In public-key infrastructures, the context can bind an identity and the payload a public key, so issuing two certificates for one identity triggers scoped exposure that renders impersonating certificates moot rather than a system-wide penalty that harms honest users. SMS introduces support for wildcard certificates and two-level hierarchies to localize penalties. We propose SMS schemes based on Boneh--Lynn--Shacham short signatures and eVRF, with efficient extensions to threshold signing and batched verification. Third, we propose anonymous tokens (AT) that provide sealed metadata channels by signing encrypted commitments and binding issuance to redemption with lightweight non-interactive proofs. The channel conveys verifier-only signals while the AT requester can verify token validity without learning the signals, and we offer a post-quantum construction via lattice-based instantiations. Across the stack, the sealed metadata channel forms the cornerstone for misuse resilience, enabling richer private signals that transport rate-limiting handles and scoped-exposure policies, leading to systems that preserve privacy under compliant use with bounded, auditable exposure under misuse. 互聯網環境開放，安全設計須講求平衡：既要遏止濫用，也要避免過度追蹤或懲罰對正當使用者造成寒蟬效應，並把濫用或脅迫造成的附帶損害限於必要範圍。相關情境包括網上帳戶的使用、洋蔥路由（Tor）用戶或虛擬私人網絡用戶的人機驗證（例如以一個位元表示 CAPTCHA 結果）、程式碼及證書簽署，以及保障私隱的授權機制，例如電子現金及電子投票。現有方法存在若干結構性弱點，包括大量依賴簡潔非互動式知識論證（SNARK）來證明完整的可驗證隨機函數（VRF）關係、現有衝突威懾方法可能在核證機關受脅迫簽發衝突證書時暴露其完整私匙，以及缺乏可傳遞多於一個隱藏位元的驗證者專用通道。本研究針對這些問題提出三項技術貢獻，涵蓋基礎密碼學原語及針對實際部署的設計。 首先，我們提出並嚴謹定義 d-暴露匿名標記（d-EAT），使同一時段內使用超過 d 次時即可提取私匙。我們以可盲化密碼匙的指數型可驗證隨機函數（eVRF）構造 d-EAT，使驗證者毋須檢查完整 VRF 關係的零知識證明（ZKP）。證明者只需證明承諾中的密碼匙與盲化後的密碼匙相符；該承諾可與其他 ZKP 組合，用於更大型的匿名系統，同時保留濫用時提取密碼匙的能力。這項技術以簡單的重複使用偵測方程式實施每個時段最多使用 d 次的限制，可用於環和群組兩類匿名系統，並支援快速撤銷相應的使用權限，而毋須依賴高成本的 SNARK。 其次，我們設計自我威懾簽署（SMS）：僅在衝突時暴露定域秘密，非衝突簽署仍然有效。每個簽署均綁定一對（情境、內容）；同一情境下簽署不同內容即構成衝突。在公匙基建中，可用身分作為情境、公匙作為內容；若為同一身分簽發兩張採用不同公匙的證書，便會觸發定域密碼匙暴露，使該身分的證書失去可信性，而不波及其他身分。SMS 亦支援萬用字元證書及兩級階層，將密碼匙暴露限制在相應範圍。我們提出基於 Boneh–Lynn–Shacham 短簽署及 eVRF 的 SMS 方案，並可高效延伸至門檻簽署及批次驗證。 第三，我們提出具密封元數據通道的匿名權標（AT）框架，透過對加密的承諾作簽署，並以較輕量的非互動式證明綁定權標的發行與後續使用。該通道可傳遞僅供驗證者讀取的訊號，AT 申領者仍可驗證權標有效性，卻無法得知訊號內容。我們亦提出基於格密碼學的後量子構造。 整體而言，密封元數據通道可作為應對濫用的核心機制，承載 d-EAT 標記等更豐富的保密訊號，支援使用限額及定域暴露，使系統在合規使用時保障私隱，並把濫用時的暴露限於必要範圍。

14213326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14213326.value: 面向胃腸疾病診療的智能體式多模態推理系統

14213326.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14213326.value: Prof Chan, Shannon Melissa Prof Meng, Max Qing-Hu

14213326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14213326.value: Gastrointestinal (GI) diseases represent a critical global health challenge, particularly in China, where GI cancers constitute over 50% of all cancer cases and approximately 45% of cancer-related deaths. This severe burden is exacerbated by a notably low early detection rate of less than 10% and insufficient endoscopic screening coverage. Consequently, advancements in accurate GI disease diagnosis and treatment through endoscopy robotics are imperative for enhancing GI healthcare. However, existing robotic systems often treat diagnosis and treatment intervention separately, resulting in suboptimal performance. The key challenges include 1) the inherent difficulty of assessing GI diseases with single modality data; 2) limitations in comprehensive knowledge reasoning of treatment planning, which impedes clinical application; and 3) the insufficient accuracy for autonomous robotic navigation and treatment due to the challenges of precise control in complex, deformable anatomical environments. This project aims to develop an agentic and reasoning intelligent multi-modal robotic system for unified GI disease diagnosis and treatment. Firstly, we will construct a multi-agent multimodal imaging analysis framework that jointly utilizes different imaging modalities (endoscopy, ultrasound, CT, MRI) with a constructed comprehensive GI knowledge graph for automatic report generation. This framework integrates heterogeneous medical data into unified diagnostic information, enhancing the accuracy and reliability of medical reports. Secondly, we develop a clinical tree-of-thought reasoning framework for treatment planning. It systematically decomposes patient assessment into four sequential levels: symptom analysis, cause inference, treatment suggestion, and risk assessment, along with domain-adapted scoring mechanisms to quantitatively validate each step and ensure transparent, interpretable clinical decision-making. Thirdly, for accurate treatment interventions, we propose a dynamic procedure-aware digital twin of the GI tract for simulation-to-reality robotic navigation that combines treatment-oriented dynamic GI tract reconstruction with precise robotic control. This is complemented by an integrated control framework that optimizes both navigation paths and treatment while continuously monitoring procedural safety constraints. Lastly, we will integrate these components into a comprehensive robotic system with a clinical interface, enabling unified diagnosis and treatment in complex GI clinical applications. This research represents a pioneering effort to develop an agentic diagnostic and treatment endoscopic robotic system. Our preliminary results for the proposed research tasks with our already available dataset have confirmed the feasibility and superior performance of this project. The innovative combination of multimodal report generation, knowledge-based reasoning, and digital twin guided navigation promises to advance the field of endoscopic automation, ultimately improving early diagnosis and treatment outcomes for GI diseases. 胃腸道疾病是全球健康領域的一項重大挑戰，尤其是在中國，胃腸道癌症佔所有癌症病例的 50% 以上，並造成約 45% 的癌症相關死亡。這一沉重負擔又因早期檢出率顯著偏低（低於 10%）以及內視鏡篩檢覆蓋不足而進一步加劇。因此，透過內視鏡技術推動胃腸道疾病精準診斷與治療的進步，對提升胃腸道醫療服務至關重要。然而，現有系統往往將診斷與治療介入分開處理，導致整體效能未達最佳。其關鍵挑戰包括：1）僅依賴單一模態資料評估胃腸道疾病本身存在困難；2）治療規劃中全面知識推理能力有限，阻礙其臨床應用；以及 3）由於複雜且可變形的解剖環境中精準控制困難，導航與治療的準確性仍然不足。 本計畫旨在開發一套具備智能體能力與推理智能的多模態系統，用於胃腸道疾病的一體化診斷與治療。首先，我們將構建一個多智能體多模態影像分析框架，該框架結合不同影像模態以及所構建的完整胃腸道知識圖譜，用於自動生成醫學報告。此框架將異質醫療資料整合為統一的診斷資訊，從而提升醫學報告的準確性與可靠性。其次，我們將開發一種用於治療規劃的臨床推理框架。該框架將患者評估系統性地分解為四個連續層級：症狀分析、病因推斷、治療建議與風險評估，並結合領域適配的評分機制，對每一步進行量化驗證，以確保臨床決策過程透明且可解釋。第三，為實現精準治療介入，我們提出一種面向操作流程的胃腸道動態數字孿生重建模型，用於模擬到現實的機器人導航。最後，我們將把上述組件整合為一套具備臨床的綜合機器人系統，使其能夠在複雜的胃腸道臨床應用中實現診斷與治療一體化。

14213526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14213526.value: 繩索驅動摺紙關節式充氣機器人

14213526.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14213526.value: Prof Li, Bing Prof Xu, Dongyan

14213526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14213526.value: Inflatable robots refer to a class of soft robots, made of flexible films that will change its shape when inflated by fluids such as air. This type of robots has been popular in recent years due to a range of attractive advantages, including being naturally lightweight, safe for environment interaction, ability to extend over large distances and the ability to operate within complex or confined spaces. Despite the large number of studies and various types of inflatable robots already developed, they are predominantly pneumatically actuated, and have major drawbacks such as low accuracy, low dexterity and limited controlled range of motion. As such, this limits the range of potential real-world applications for inflatable robots. In this project, a new generalised type of origami-jointed inflatable cable-driven robot (OICR) is proposed. While preserving the advantages of inflatable robots, the proposed system possesses the following unique features and advantages: 1) rather than a “continuous” inflating backbone, the OICR backbone consists of multiple inflatable segments interjoined by origami-structured joints that are formed by sealing the flexible film, resulting in greater dexterity and a larger controllable range of motion; 2) rather than pneumatic actuators, the use of motorised cables will increase accuracy, higher payload capabilities and faster reaction time; 3) extended novel inflating structures such as coupled OIC segments to minimise cable actuators and multiple layer films for joint reconfiguration; 4) novel flexible and stretchable sensors integrated into the film material to provide proprioceptive and exteroceptive sensing for the OICR; and 5) easy to fabricate process that favours customised film and joint design to explore inflating body morphologies for different task requirements. The following major challenges will be addressed in this project: 1) to study the mechanism design for the class of OICRs, including the origami-joint design, cable attachment design, film material and body structure; 2) to model the kinematics and dynamics of the OICR mechanism, particularly in the presence of environment contact; 3) to design the cable setup for different task requirements, including the number and location of cables; 4) control and planning of the complete OICR mechanism; 5) development of film embedded sensors for both origami joint and inflatable body sensing; and finally 6) the development of OICR prototypes to demonstrate the potential for real-world applications. 充氣機器人是一類以柔性薄膜製成的軟體機器人，其結構在空氣等流體充入後會發生形狀變化。近年來，此類機器人因具備多項顯著優勢而受到廣泛關注，包括本質上重量輕、與環境互動時具有較高安全性、可實現長距離延伸，以及能夠在複雜或狹窄空間內作業。儘管目前已有大量相關研究，並發展出多種類型的充氣機器人，但現有系統主要仍採用氣動驅動，並存在精度較低、靈巧性不足及可控運動範圍有限等主要缺點。因此，充氣機器人在實際應用中的潛在應用範圍仍受到限制。 本研究提出一種新型且具一般性的摺紙關節式充氣繩索驅動機器人（OICR）。在保留充氣機器人既有優勢的同時，所提出的系統具備以下獨特特點與優勢：1）不同於「連續式」充氣主體，OICR 的主體由多個充氣節段構成，各節段之間透過由柔性薄膜封合形成的摺紙結構關節相互連接，從而實現更高的運動靈巧性及更大的可控運動範圍；2）不同於採用氣動致動器，系統使用馬達驅動的繩索進行致動，可提高運動精度、負載能力及響應速度；3）進一步發展新型充氣結構，例如採用耦合式 OIC 節段以減少所需繩索致動器數量，以及利用多層薄膜結構實現關節重構；4）將新型柔性及可拉伸感測器整合於薄膜材料之中，為 OICR 提供本體感知與外部環境感知能力；以及 5）採用易於製造的製程，有利於針對不同任務需求進行客製化薄膜與關節設計，從而探索具有不同形態的充氣機器人本體。 本研究將重點解決以下主要挑戰：1）研究 OICR 類機器人的機構設計，包括摺紙關節設計、繩索連接設計、薄膜材料及本體結構；2）建立 OICR 機構的運動學與動力學模型，尤其考慮其與環境接觸時的機械行為；3）針對不同任務需求設計繩索配置，包括繩索的數量與佈置位置；4）研究完整 OICR 機構的控制與運動規劃方法；5）開發嵌入薄膜的感測器，以實現對摺紙關節及充氣本體的感知；以及最後 6）開發 OICR 原型系統，以展示其在實際應用場景中的潛力。

14213826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14213826.value: 研究兩接收器廣播頻道容量區域（capacity region）的內界與外界（inner and outer bounds）

14213826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14213826.value: Computing the capacity region for a two-receiver discrete memoryless broadcast channel is a central open problem in network information theory. Progress on this problem stalled for about a decade, except for two outer bounds introduced in a paper co-authored by the principal investigator. These bounds were part of a broader auxiliary-receiver-based approach, which also advanced other major challenges, such as the Gaussian interference and relay channels. Earlier this year, Yanlin Geng, a former doctoral student of the principal investigator, developed an improved outer bound for the two-receiver broadcast channel using the auxiliary receiver method. This bound enhanced the sum-rate for the binary skew-symmetric broadcast channel, a key setting for understanding inner and outer bounds of the capacity region. This represents the first improvement in the sum-rate outer bound since the late 2000s and the first significant advance since the late 1970s. However, the principal investigator and collaborators showed that Geng’s new bound is actually implied by one of the two recent outer bounds, although the intuition behind Geng’s choice of auxiliary receiver remains non-trivial. The core question of this proposal is to evaluate the effectiveness of the two recent outer bounds and explore possible improvements. Building on recent developments, the principal investigator and a current student demonstrated that one of these bounds can characterize the capacity region for sums of various broadcast channel classes, marking the first such advance since Abbas El Gamal’s work in the early 1980s. They also found that the two seemingly distinct outer bounds are comparable for sum-rate and that combining their ideas could lead to a new, stronger outer bound. This proposal aims to build on this promising progress as the puzzle pieces align. Another focus of the proposal is to study Marton’s inner bound for the two-receiver broadcast channel. The goal is to develop techniques to isolate the extremizers of the associated non-convex optimization problem. Through extensive numerical experiments, a recently published conjecture suggests these extremizers satisfy a particular Markov chain. This insight not only clarifies the maximizers’ structure but also offers a concrete path to tackle this longstanding open problem. In summary, this proposal seeks to address a decades-old challenge by leveraging exciting recent advances in both inner and outer bounds of the capacity region for the two-receiver discrete memoryless broadcast channel. 計算兩接收器離散無記憶廣播頻道（two-receiver discrete memoryless broadcast channel）的容量區域（capacity region）是網路資訊理論領域中一個核心且重要的未解問題。除了由本計畫主持人共同執行的論文中所提出的兩個外界（outer bounds）之外，針對此問題的研究在大約 10 年間陷入停滯。雖然上述發展令人振奮，但它屬於利用基於輔助接收器（auxiliary-receiver-based）方法來建立外界之更廣泛藍圖的一部分，而這種方法也在其他核心未解問題（如高斯干擾頻道與中繼頻道）中取得了成果。 今年早些時候，本計畫主持人的前博士生耿彥林再次基於輔助接收器方法，針對兩接收器廣播頻道開發了一個外界，改善了二元斜對稱廣播頻道（binary skew-symmetric broadcast channel）的和速率（sum-rate）。這種特定的廣播頻道設定間接地是所有關於兩接收器廣播頻道容量區域內界與外界發展的核心。這是自 2000 年代末期以來，針對該頻道和速率外界的第一項改善，也是自 1970 年代末期以來第一項非 trivial（非顯而易見）的改善。然而，計畫主持人及其合作者隨即能夠證明（並私下與耿彥林交流），這個新外界實際上已被最近提出的兩個外界之一所涵蓋。不過，耿彥林所使用的輔助接收器選擇之直覺並非顯而易見。 這引出了本計畫的核心問題：最近提出的兩個外界究竟有多有效？它們是否能進一步被改善？鑑於二元斜對稱廣播頻道最近的發展，計畫主持人與其現指導的一名學生已經證實，其中一個提出的外界同時也能確立各類廣播頻道和的容量區域，標誌著自 Abbas El Gamal 在 1980 年代初期的工作以來，在此方向上的首次改善。在此過程中，我們也發現最近提出的兩個看似不同的外界在和速率方面確實具可比性，並且透過巧妙結合兩者的理念，極有可能為兩接收器廣播頻道推導出一個新的外界。因此，隨著拼圖的各個部分似乎正漸漸到位，本計畫旨在基於這些廣泛的初步工作進一步深入研究。 本計畫的另一部分是研究針對兩接收器廣播頻道的 Marton 內界（Marton's inner bound）。本部分的核心重點在於發展相關技術，以獨立出相關非凸最佳化問題（non-convex optimization problem）之極大化函數（maximizer）的屬性。透過大量的數值實驗，我們剛發表了一項關於 Marton 內界極端點的猜想，即它們滿足特定的馬可夫鏈（Markov chain）。這除了能讓我們深入了解極大化函數之外，也為我們攻克這個長久以來的未解問題提供了明確的途徑。 簡而言之，本計畫希望基於兩接收器離散無記憶廣播頻道容量區域之內界與外界令人振奮的新發展，以攻克這個長久以來的未解問題。

14214026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14214026.value: 基於人類姿態適應示範與擴散生成方法的人形機器人全身多支撐強力操作技能研究

14214026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14214026.value: Recent advances in generative artificial intelligence and humanoid hardware have led to remarkable progress in both locomotion and manipulation. Yet, despite these breakthroughs, intentional contact, the deliberate use of multiple body-environment contacts for support and balancing, remains underexploited in humanoid control. Contact modelling, simulation, planning, and control continue to pose long-standing challenges due to their inherently hybrid nature, combining discrete contact selection with continuous force and posture adaptation under nonlinear dynamics. Consequently, current humanoids still fall short of human-level robustness and versatility. In contrast, humans routinely leverage additional support contacts with the environment, such as bracing a hand on a wall or a knee on the ground, to maintain balance, extend reach, and amplify applied forces in loco-manipulation tasks. These strategies allow humans to safely operate near their physical limits, performing tasks that require stability and strength beyond what limb kinematics alone can provide. Such whole-body, multi-support behaviors are uniquely enabled by the humanoid form factor, which offers both flexible postural adaptation and a wide choice of contact configurations. This proposal, titled “Learning Humanoid Whole-Body Multi-Support Forceful Manipulation Skills From Human Demonstrated Postural Adaptation Strategies Using Diffusion Generative Methods,” seeks to capture, model, and transfer these human capabilities to humanoid robots. By combining recent advances in diffusion-based generative modeling and reinforcement learning, the project aims to endow humanoids with human-inspired, adaptive whole-body manipulation skills that exploit intentional contacts for greater reach, stability, and force. The research plan is organized into four integrated tasks. Task 1 will record and analyze human demonstrations of forceful manipulation involving multi-support postures, creating the first dataset of whole-body human contact adaptation strategies. Task 2 will develop a diffusion-based generative planner that learns from these demonstrations to predict feasible, ergonomic multi-contact configurations for given tasks and environments. Task 3 will design a hybrid whole-body control architecture combining reinforcement learning and model-based optimization to reproduce human-like posture adaptation and dynamic contact reconfiguration in real time. Finally, Task 4 will validate the complete framework on the full-size Tiangong humanoid robot, demonstrating previously infeasible tasks such as heavy object pushing, extended reach with hand support, and forceful overhead operations requiring whole-body stabilization. By integrating human-inspired strategies, generative modeling, and intelligent whole-body control, this project will enable humanoid robots to operate at the frontier of their physical capabilities, achieving robust, forceful, and adaptive manipulation that brings them a step closer to human-level embodied intelligence. 近年生成式人工智能與人形機器人硬件快速發展，推動了機器人在行走與操作能力方面取得顯著進展。然而，在人形機器人控制中，有意接觸，即主動利用身體與環境之間的多個接觸點以增強支撐、平衡與施力能力，仍未被充分利用。由於接觸建模、仿真、規劃與控制涉及離散接觸選擇、連續力控制及姿態適應等混合動態問題，相關研究仍面臨長期挑戰，令現有人形機器人在魯棒性、靈活性及強力操作能力方面仍未達到人類水平。相比之下，人類在搬運、推動、支撐及伸展等任務中，能自然地利用手扶牆面、膝部着地或其他身體支撐方式，以維持平衡、擴展操作範圍並提高施力能力，並能在接近身體極限的情況下安全完成高強度操作任務。本項目「基於人類姿態適應示範與擴散生成方法的人形機器人全身多支撐強力操作技能研究」旨在捕捉、建模並遷移人類在多支撐強力操作中的姿態適應能力，結合擴散生成模型、強化學習及全身控制方法，建立由人類示範到機器人執行的技能學習框架。研究將採集並分析人類在多支撐強力操作任務中的示範數據，建立全身接觸與姿態適應策略數據集；發展基於擴散生成模型的規劃方法，從人類示範中學習可行且符合人體工效的多接觸構型；設計融合強化學習與模型優化的混合式全身控制架構，實現實時姿態適應與動態接觸重構；並在人形機器人平台上進行驗證，展示重物推動、支撐下的遠距離操作及需要全身穩定的高強度操作等任務。本項目將人類姿態適應策略、生成式建模及智能全身控制相結合，有望提升人形機器人在複雜環境中的穩定性、施力能力及操作適應性，推動其在具身智能和高難度實體任務中的應用，並使人形機器人更接近人類水平的全身協作與操作能力。

14214226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14214226.value: 在開放世界中學習自我演進智能體

14214226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14214226.value: Agents built on top of latest large language models have shown great promise in automating digital tasks, acting as assistants that can operate software and navigate websites on our behalf. Such ``computer use agents'' leverage the capabilities of the underlying model to understand and interact with what they see on a screen, aiming to free up human users from repetitive and tedious work. Such agents have great potential of becoming capable digital partners that can seamlessly handle complex tasks by reliably using software on behalf of human beings, thus leading to substantial increase of productivity in the real world. Despite their potential, today’s agents have a critical weakness: they are unable to adapt on their own in an open environment. They are typically trained on static, human-provided examples, which means they are easily broken by minor changes in the digital world. For instance, a simple software update that moves a button or renames a menu can render an agent’s learned knowledge completely useless. For these agents to become truly reliable, they must learn to evolve. This presents two core challenges: 1) the agent must be able to set its own goals and create new learning opportunities and 2) it needs a reliable way to verify if its attempts were actually successful. We propose a novel framework to create self-evolving agents that overcome these limitations. Specifically, we propose to develop a task generator that can autonomously generate a curriculum of progressively more difficult tasks, ensuring the agent expands its capabilities in a steady way. To solve the problem of reliable verification, we propose an agentic reward system, which incorporates external tools to provide objective and accurate confirmation of its performance, thus preventing the agent from getting stuck in loops of error or self-deception. By enabling agents to learn and adapt autonomously in an open environment, this research paves the way for a new generation of more resilient and intelligent digital assistants. The most significant impact of this work lies in its potential to unlock new applications, particularly in the realm of accessibility. We envision creating advanced tools that can dynamically adapt to any user interface they encounter. This would provide a seamless and intuitive experience for individuals with disabilities, as the AI assistant could learn to navigate new and unfamiliar software on the fly, without needing constant reprogramming by a human. 建立在最新大語言模型（LLM）之上的智能體（Agent）展現出在自動化數位任務方面的巨大潛力。它們可作為能代表我們操作軟體、瀏覽網站的助理。這類「電腦使用智能體」運用其底層模型的能力，理解並與螢幕上所看到的內容互動，目標是將人類使用者從重複且繁瑣的工作中解放出來。這類智能體極有潛力成為具備能力的數位夥伴，能夠代表人類可靠地使用軟體，無縫處理複雜任務，從而在現實世界中大幅提升生產力。 儘管具有潛力，現今的代理仍有一項關鍵弱點：它們無法自行適應變化。它們是基於靜態、由人類提供的範例進行訓練，這意味著數位世界中的細微變化就很容易使其失效。例如，一次簡單的軟體更新若移動了某個按鈕或重新命名某個選單，就可能使智能體已學得的知識完全失去作用。若要讓這些智能體變得真正可靠，它們必須學會演化。這帶來了兩項核心挑戰：1）智能體必須能夠自行設定目標並創造新的學習機會；2）它需要一種可靠的方法來驗證其嘗試是否確實成功。 我們提出一個新穎的框架，以建立能克服上述限制的自我演進智能體。為了解決目標設定的挑戰，我們提出一種任務生成器，能夠自主生成一套難度逐步提升的任務課程，確保智能體始終持續學習並擴展其能力。為了解決可靠驗證的問題，我們提出一套獨特的回饋系統。不同於依賴代理自身可能有缺陷的自我評估，我們的方法納入外部工具，以對其表現提供客觀且準確的確認，從而避免代理陷入錯誤循環或自我欺瞞之中。 透過讓智能體能夠自主學習與適應，本研究為新一代更具韌性且更智慧的數位助理鋪平道路。這項工作的最重大影響，在於其有潛力開啟新的應用，尤其是在無障礙領域。我們設想打造先進工具，使其能夠動態適應所遇到的任何使用者介面。這將為身心障礙者提供無縫且直覺的體驗，因為 AI 助理可以即時學習如何瀏覽全新且不熟悉的軟體，而不需要人類不斷重新編程。

14214526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14214526.value: 通過干預選擇實現分佈魯棒社會福利最大化

14214526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14214526.value: This project addresses the critical challenge of welfare maximization under hard budget constraints in targeted interventions such as preventive healthcare, welfare-to-work programs, and social services. Traditional empirical welfare maximization (EWM) methods optimize treatment allocation using experimental data but often fail to guarantee feasibility under fiscal limits and robustness to distributional shifts. These limitations are acute in real-world deployments where heterogeneous treatment effects, covariate shift, and model misspecification undermine policy performance. To overcome these challenges, the proposal introduces a distributionally robust optimization (DRO) framework tailored for constrained welfare maximization. The approach leverages Wasserstein ambiguity sets to hedge against two distinct sources of uncertainty: (i) outcome-model misspecification and (ii) covariate shift affecting budget feasibility. This decoupled ambiguity design reflects operational realities—costs depend on observable covariates at assignment, while welfare depends on counterfactual outcomes. The resulting formulation ensures worst-case welfare guarantees and budget compliance under plausible perturbations of the data-generating process. The methodology comprises four key components: 1. Framework Specification: Formalize a budgeted Wasserstein-DRO model with tractable reformulations via Kantorovich–Rubinstein duality. 2. Nominal Model Construction: Develop a data-driven joint distribution of covariates and potential outcomes using k-nearest-neighbor (kNN) local learning, ensuring statistical consistency under mild conditions. 3. Optimization and Extension: Solve the in-sample robust policy via linear programming and extend it to the full covariate space using a Shapley-type Lipschitz interpolation, preserving feasibility and optimality for infinite-dimensional problems. 4. Deterministic Implementation: Convert randomized allocations into deterministic policies that maintain worst-case budget guarantees and near-optimal welfare, addressing practical requirements for auditability and operational simplicity. The proposed framework advances policy learning theory by integrating robustness, feasibility, and deployability. It delivers treatment allocation rules that are transparent for auditing, stable under population drift, and computationally efficient. The project also contributes novel theoretical results on consistency of kNN-based joint models, tractable DRO reformulations, and Shapley extensions under Wasserstein penalties. Ultimately, this research aims to provide provably robust, budget-compliant policies for agencies operating under uncertainty, bridging the gap between theoretical robustness and practical implementation in welfare-critical programs. 本項目旨在解決預防性醫療保健、就業轉型培訓以及社會服務等標的干預措施中，在硬性預算約束下進行福利最大化的關鍵挑戰。傳統的經驗福利最大化方法利用實驗數據來優化處置分配，但往往無法保證在財政限制下的可行性，也缺乏對分佈偏移的魯棒性。在真實世界部署中，異質性處置效應、共變量偏移以及模型誤設均會削弱政策性能，使上述局限性尤為突出。 為克服這些挑戰，本申請案提出了一套專為受約束福利最大化量身定制的分佈魯棒優化（DRO）框架。該方法利用瓦瑟斯坦模糊集（Wasserstein ambiguity sets）來規避兩種不同的不確定性來源：（i）結果模型誤設，以及（ii）影響預算可行性的共變量偏移。這種解耦的模糊集設計反映了實際營運現狀：成本取決於分配時的可觀測共變量，而福利則取決於反事實結果。由此得到的優化公式能確保在數據生成過程發生合理擾動時，仍具備最壞情況下的福利保證與預算合規性。 本研究方法包含四個核心部分： 框架構建：建立帶預算約束的瓦瑟斯坦-DRO 模型，並透過 Kantorovich-Rubinstein 對偶性實現可計算的公式重構。 名義模型建立：利用 k 近鄰局部學習，開發數據驅動的共變量與潛在結果聯合分佈，並在溫和條件下確保統計一致性。 優化與擴展：透過線性規劃求解樣本內魯棒政策，並利用 Shapley 型 Lipschitz 插值將其擴展至全共變量空間，在無限維問題中保持可行性與最優性。 確定性實施：將隨機化分配轉化為確定性政策，既能維持最壞情況下的預算保證與接近最優的福利，又能滿足可審計性與營運簡潔性的實際需求。 本項目提出的框架透過整合魯棒性、可行性與可部署性，推動了政策學習理論的發展。它能提供審計透明、在總體漂移下保持穩定且計算高效的處置分配規則。本項目還在基於 kNN 的聯合模型一致性、可計算的 DRO 重構以及瓦瑟斯坦懲罰下的 Shapley 擴展方面作出了創新理論貢獻。 最終，本研究旨在為不確定性下運作的機構提供可證明的魯棒且符合預算規範的政策，填補福利關鍵項目中理論魯棒性與實際實施之間的鴻溝。

14214726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14214726.value: 定量生物標記圖譜成像的穩健高品質肝臟擴散加權磁振造影研究

14214726.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14214726.value: Dr CHIU, Wan Hang Prof Dou, Qi

14214726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14214726.value: For over two decades, diffusion-weighted MRI (dMRI) has been an indispensable tool for quantitative dMRI-biomarker assessment in brain applications, such as apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) and fractional anisotropy (FA). Extending this success, dMRI-biomarker mapping shows significant promise in liver applications, providing complementary diagnostic insight for lesion characterization, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) assessment, and fibrosis staging without contrast injection. However, conventional ADC is confounded by microcirculatory perfusion, leading to the development of intravoxel incoherent motion dMRI (IVIM-dMRI). Further advancing this, the T2-IVIM model improves separation of fast and slow diffusion components by correcting for TE-dependent signal, providing a more precise depiction of liver tissue microstructure and pathology. Despite this potential, routine liver dMRI using single-shot echo-planar imaging (DWssEPI) is limited by low resolution and poor geometric accuracy. More critically, advanced IVIM-dMRI, especially the multi-TE T2-IVIM approach, necessitates extensive data acquisition, pushing scantime to clinical limits. These issues are further compounded by pervasive respiratory motion, leading to inconsistent biomarker reproducibility and signal loss in diffusion-encoded images. While multi-shot techniques and free-breathing (FB) methods can enhance image quality and motion robustness, they often incur prohibitive scantime and incomplete motion compensation, hindering the clinical feasibility and robustness of high-quality liver IVIM-biomarker mapping. Therefore, the overall goal of this project is to address these challenges through three interconnected developments: First, we will develop a motion-compensated advanced multi-shot multi-echo dMRI technique based on the DW-Propeller-EPI sequence, incorporating self-referenced artifact corrections for FB liver dMRI acquisition. Second, we will design a deep learning (DL)-based reconstruction framework to accelerate FB liver dMRI for IVIM-biomarker mapping, involving pipeline development for resolving respiratory motion and joint reconstruction of images and biomarker maps from highly undersampled multi-blade data. Third, we will acquire training data and comprehensively evaluate the performance of the developed technique for liver IVIM-biomarker mapping under FB conditions through optimized data acquisition, DL model training, and comparative studies against fully-sampled techniques. Successful completion of this project will provide a comprehensive acquisition and reconstruction framework, making a significant step toward motion-robust, high-quality, and repeatable liver dMRI-biomarker mapping. This framework, with AI-powered reconstruction, will significantly enhance liver dMRI applications. The rigorous evaluation within this study will establish a solid foundation for future clinical translation and patient-focused evaluations, potentially advancing liver dMRI-biomarker mapping for diagnosing and monitoring a wide range of liver diseases. 在過去二十多年來，擴散加權磁共振成像（dMRI）一直是腦部應用中定量dMRI生物標誌物評估不可或缺的工具，例如表觀擴散係數（ADC）和非等向性分數（FA）。延續此一成功經驗，dMRI生物標誌物成像在肝臟應用中展現出巨大潛力，在無需注射對比劑的情況下，為病灶特徵分析、非酒精性脂肪肝病（NAFLD）評估以及纖維化分期提供具互補性的診斷資訊。然而，傳統ADC受微循環灌注的混淆影響，促使了體素內不相干運動dMRI（IVIM-dMRI）的發展。在此基礎上進一步推進的T2-IVIM模型，透過校正與回波時間（TE）相關的訊號變化，改善了快速與慢速擴散分量的分離效果，從而更精確地描繪肝臟組織的微結構及病理特徵。 儘管具有上述潛力，以單次激發回波平面成像（DWssEPI）進行的常規肝臟dMRI仍受限於低解析度及較差的幾何準確度。更為關鍵的是，進階IVIM-dMRI，尤其是多TE 的 T2-IVIM方法，需要大量的數據採集，使掃描時間逼近臨床可接受的極限。這些問題因呼吸運動而進一步加劇，導致生物標誌物的低可重複性以及擴散編碼影像中的訊號丟失。雖然多次激發技術和自由呼吸方法能夠提升影像品質和運動穩健性，但它們往往伴隨著難以承受的掃描時間及不完整的運動補償，阻礙了高品質肝臟IVIM生物標誌物成像的臨床可行性和穩健性。 因此，本計畫的總體目標是透過三個相互關聯的研究內容來解決上述挑戰：第一，我們將開發一種基於DW-Propeller-EPI序列的運動補償進階多次激發多回波dMRI技術，結合自參考式偽影校正，用於自由呼吸肝臟dMRI採集。第二，我們將設計一個基於深度學習（DL）的重建框架，以加速自由呼吸肝臟dMRI的IVIM生物標誌物成像，包括開發用於解析呼吸運動的處理流程，以及從高度欠採樣的多葉片數據中聯合重建影像與生物標誌物分布圖。第三，我們將採集訓練數據，並透過優化數據採集、深度學習模型訓練以及與全採樣技術的對比研究，全面評估所開發技術在自由呼吸條件下進行肝臟IVIM生物標誌物成像的效能。 本計畫的順利完成將提供一個全面的採集與重建框架，為實現運動穩健、高品質且可重複的肝臟dMRI生物標誌物成像邁出重要一步。此框架結合AI驅動的重建技術，將顯著提升肝臟dMRI的應用價值。本研究中的嚴謹評估將為未來的臨床轉化及以患者為導向的驗證研究奠定堅實基礎，有望推動肝臟dMRI生物標誌物成像在診斷和監測各類肝臟疾病中的應用。

14214826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14214826.value: 高熵材料有序-無序相變發現的自驅動智能模型

14214826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14214826.value: High-entropy materials (HEMs) represent a paradigm shift in materials science, leveraging configurational entropy to stabilize novel phases and enable unprecedented property combinations. A key factor influencing these properties is the order-to-disorder transition, which determines the thermodynamic stability, mechanical response, and functional performance of HEMs. However, the vast compositional and configurational space of high-entropy systems presents several challenges for conventional trial-and-error methodologies: 1) Vast Compositional Space: Traditional methods cannot systematically explore the vast space of elemental combinations and local atomic arrangements. 2) Heavy Computational Cost: Atomistically probing transition pathways via molecular dynamics simulations is often computationally prohibitive. 3) Multi-modal Data Alignment: A significant gap exists in integrating multi-modal data—such as material representations, spectroscopy, and textual descriptors—into a unified model. To overcome these challenges, we propose an autonomous platform with self-driving intelligent models for the intelligent discovery of high-performance HEMs. This integrated system comprises: First, a self-evolving multi-agent simulation framework will explore reinforcement learning to navigate the compositional space autonomously, enabling the efficient exploration of atomic structural evolution. This will generate the first comprehensive dataset on order-to-disorder transitions in HEMs. Second, we will develop a novel Transition-informed 3D Diffusion Model. This model moves beyond traditional noise-based processes by explicitly simulating disorder-to-order transitions. Trained on the simulation dataset, it will generalize to predict equilibrium microstructures for arbitrary compositions and temperatures. Finally, we will design a physically-grounded multi-modal alignment to unify material representations, spectral, and textual data. This approach will achieve dynamic, atomic-scale understanding, providing critical experimental validation and advancing the interpretation of local structures. This project will pioneer a closed-loop, AI-robotics-validated research paradigm, delivering a foundational understanding of order-to-disorder transitions and a powerful toolset for designing high-performance HEMs. 高熵材料（High-Entropy Materials, HEMs）代表了材料科學領域的一次範式轉變，其利用組態熵穩定新穎物相，並實現前所未有的性能組合。影響這些性能的一項關鍵因素是有序—無序轉變，該轉變決定了高熵材料的熱力學穩定性、力學響應及功能表現。然而，高熵體系龐大的成分與組態空間，為傳統試錯式研究方法帶來了若干挑戰：1）龐大的成分空間：傳統方法難以系統性探索大量元素組合及其局部原子排列所構成的廣闊空間；2）高昂的計算成本：利用分子動力學模擬在原子尺度上探究轉變路徑，通常需要極高的計算成本；3）多模態資料對齊困難：目前在將材料表徵、光譜資料與文字描述等多模態資訊整合至統一模型方面，仍存在顯著鴻溝。為克服上述挑戰，我們提出一個搭載自驅動智能模型的自主化平台，用於高性能高熵材料的智能發現。該整合系統包括以下三個部分：首先，我們將建立一套自演化多智能體模擬框架，探索利用強化學習自主搜尋高熵材料的成分空間，從而高效探索原子結構的演化過程，並生成首個涵蓋高熵材料有序—無序轉變的綜合性數據集。其次，我們將開發一種新型的轉變感知三維擴散模型（Transition-informed 3D Diffusion Model）。不同於傳統以隨機加噪為核心的擴散過程，該模型將顯式模擬無序—有序轉變。透過在上述模擬数据集上進行訓練，模型將具備良好的泛化能力，可預測任意成分與溫度條件下的平衡微觀結構。最後，我們將設計一套具物理基礎的多模態對齊方法，統一整合材料表徵、光譜資料及文字資訊。該方法將實現對材料動態演化過程的原子尺度理解，為實驗驗證提供關鍵依據，並推進對高熵材料局部結構的解析。本計畫將開創一種由人工智能與機器人實驗共同驗證的閉環研究範式，深化對高熵材料有序—無序轉變機制的基礎理解，並建立一套用於設計高性能高熵材料的強大工具體系。

14300226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14300226.value: 人工非阿貝爾規範場下超冷原子的輸運動力學

14300226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300226.value: Non-Abelian geometric phases are central to topological quantum computing, enabling topologically protected and noise-resilient gates. This proposal outlines a collaborative theory-experiment initiative to investigate the rich transport dynamics of bosonic systems in the presence of synthetic non-Abelian SU(2) gauge fields. In such systems, the adiabatic transport of a quantum state through parameter space results in a path-dependent SU(2) rotation, a direct signature of the underlying non-Abelian geometry. The topology is governed by a non-Abelian Yang monopole, a generalization of the more familiar Dirac monopole. We will start from single-mode approximation and explore how strong interactions fundamentally alter topological phenomena. Our investigation will proceed in three stages, systematically building complexity from few- to many-body systems through close theory-experiment collaboration. First, we will study the dynamics of few interacting bosons in an isolated two-site plaquette under synthetic U(1) gauge fields. To account for the quasi-1D confinement inherent in realistic experiments, we will construct a single-band effective field theory that incorporates renormalized two-body and emergent three-body interactions, which arise naturally from integrating out higher bands in a full multi-band calculation. These confinement-and-excitations induced multi-body interactions qualitatively modify the topology experienced by the spins, deforming the bare Dirac monopole in the non-interacting limit. We will further validate them against exact few-body simulations obtained with first-principle time-dependent explicitly correlated Gaussian techniques, while providing quantitative benchmarks for the experimental realization. Second, we will explore transport dynamics under the non-Abelian SU(2) gauge field by examining a few interacting bosons in an isolated four-site plaquette. The minimal single-particle model is a four by four Hamiltonian describing a Yang monopole in a five-dimensional parameter space, which can be experimentally engineered by our Co-I's team. We will theoretically investigate how traversing paths in the parameter space induces controllable spin rotations, with the degree of rotation determined by the non-Abelian Berry phase, a geometric phase also known as the holonomy. Finally, we will extend our study to the many-body regime by investigating non-Abelian Thouless pump in optical lattices. We design the hopping and detuning of the lattice such that the momentum-space Hamiltonian describes a non-Abelian Yang monopole. This pump directly probes the non-Abelian geometric phase which could couple charge transport with spin flipping. Our theoretical predictions will guide and be validated by the experimental implementations from our Co-I's optical lattice laboratory and could be further tested in other laboratory across various quantum simulation platforms. 非阿貝爾幾何相位是拓撲量子計算的重要基礎，可用於實現具拓撲保護與抗噪能力的量子閘。本計劃結合理論與實驗，研究玻色子在合成非阿貝爾 SU(2) 規範場中的輸運動力學。當量子態沿參數空間中的不同路徑絕熱演化時，會產生路徑依賴的 SU(2) 旋轉，反映系統的非阿貝爾幾何結構。其拓撲性質由楊單極子描述，可視為狄拉克單極子的非阿貝爾推廣。 第一階段將研究合成 U(1) 規範場下，孤立雙格點中少數相互作用玻色子的動力學。為描述實驗中的準一維侷限，我們將建立包含有效二體與三體相互作用的單能帶理論。這些多體效應可能使非相互作用系統中的狄拉克單極子發生形變。我們也將利用高精度少體數值方法驗證理論，並為實驗提供定量預測。 第二階段將研究孤立四格點中少數相互作用玻色子在 SU(2) 規範場下的輸運。其最小單粒子模型由一個 4階哈密頓量描述，對應五維參數空間中的楊單極子，並可由合作團隊實驗實現。我們將分析不同演化路徑如何產生可控制的自旋旋轉，以及非阿貝爾貝里相位如何決定旋轉結果。 第三階段將研究光學晶格中的非阿貝爾 Thouless 泵浦，把研究延伸至多體系統。我們將設計晶格躍遷與失諧，使其動量空間哈密頓量實現楊單極子。此泵浦可直接探測非阿貝爾幾何相位，並可能實現電荷輸運與自旋翻轉的耦合。理論結果將用於指引合作團隊的光學晶格實驗，並可推廣至其他量子模擬平台。

14300626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14300626.value: 量化軸海山地震波速度變化與應變

14300626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300626.value: Over the past two decades, seismic interferometry has revolutionized our ability to monitor subtle changes in the Earth’s subsurface, leading to discoveries such as precursory seismic velocity changes before volcanic eruptions, earthquakes, and landslides. However, a major limitation persists: interpreting the physical causes of these changes remains qualitative and non-unique, as diverse mechanisms such as changes in crustal strain, water saturation, and temperature can all produce similar seismic velocity changes. This project will break this impasse by performing a quantitative calibration of how seismic velocity responds to known applied strain. We will leverage a unique natural laboratory: Axial Seamount, an active submarine volcano ~1.5 km below the ocean surface, monitored since 2015 by a network of eight permanently buried seismometers and supplemented by an additional 15 temporary stations with greater spatial coverage from 2022-2024. This deep-sea, “weather-free” environment, subjected to large periodic tidal loading, offers an ideal setting to isolate and calibrate the seismic velocity-strain relationship. We will use a decade of continuous data to precisely measure how seismic velocity varies with known tidal strain amplitude and rate across different crustal units. Crucially, we will determine for the first time how this relationship evolves with changing background stress and damage state as the volcano inflates towards its next eruption. Furthermore, we will move beyond standard 1-D analysis and perform 4-D (space–time) imaging of relative seismic velocity changes (dv/v) across Axial Seamount before inverting these results based on our obtained seismic velocity-strain calibration to model the spatiotemporal evolution of the underlying deformation source(s). Our work will transform dv/v measurements from a qualitative indicator into a powerful quantitative tool for constraining the evolution of subsurface magmatic systems and forecasting eruptions at active volcanoes. This project will also help build a world-leading geophysics research program in Hong Kong that trains students in cutting-edge techniques. Our developed framework is transferable for monitoring and forecasting various geological hazards in the Asia-Pacific region and beyond, thereby enhancing regional resilience and solidifying Hong Kong's role as a hub for geohazard research. 過去二十年間，地震干涉技術徹底改變了我們監測地球地下微小變化的能力，促成了一系列重要發現，例如火山爆發、地震和滑坡前的地震波速變化異常。然而，該領域仍面臨一個主要限制：對這些變化物理成因的解讀往往停留在定性層面且缺乏唯一性，因為地殼應變、含水飽和度及溫度變化等多種機制都可能引發相似的地震波速變化。本計畫將透過對應變施加條件下地震波速的反應進行定量標定，從而打破這一僵局。我們將利用一個獨特的天然實驗室 - 軸海山。這是一座位於海面以下約1.5公里的活躍海底火山，自2015年起由八台永久埋設的地震儀組成的台網監測，並在2022至2024年間輔以另外15個覆蓋範圍更廣的臨時台站。這種深海且「不受天氣影響」的環境，伴隨著週期性的大幅度潮汐載荷作用，為分離並標定地震波速與應變之間的關係提供了理想條件。 我們將利用長達十年的連續觀測數據，精確測量不同地殼單元內的地震波速如何隨已知的潮汐應變幅度和速率變化。至關重要的是，我們將首次揭示隨著火山因岩漿充注而膨脹並趨向於下一次噴發，這種波速-應變關係如何隨背景應力和介質損傷狀態的變化而演變。此外，我們將突破常規的一維分析方法，對軸海山區域的相對地震波速變化（dv/v）進行時空成像；隨後，利用我們建立的波速-應變標定關係對成像結果進行反演，從而模擬地下形變源的時空演化過程。這項研究將把dv/v測量從定性指標轉變為強有力的定量工具，用於約束地下岩漿系統的演化並預測活躍火山的噴發活動。同時，本計畫也將協助香港建立世界一流的地球物理研究項目，培養掌握尖端技術的人才。我們所發展的架構可推廣應用於亞太地區乃至更廣泛區域各類地質災害的監測與預報，進而增強區域韌性，並鞏固香港作為地質災害研究樞紐的地位。

14301026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14301026.value: 一般三維流形中紐結的拓撲學及拓展研究

14301026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301026.value: When we think of a knot, we usually imagine a loop of string in ordinary three-dimensional space. Mathematicians have studied these classical knots extensively, developing powerful tools to distinguish them and measure their complexity. But what happens when we tie knots inside more exotic, curved 3-dimensional spaces? This project aims to embark on a systematic study of knots in general 3-manifolds, exploring this fascinating frontier where new phenomena emerge that are not seen in the standard 3-space, yet are central to questions in 3- and 4-dimensional topology. Our research focuses on two interconnected themes. First, we study Dehn surgery, a fundamental operation that modifies a space by cutting out a neighborhood of a knot and regluing it in a new way. We will determine when such surgeries are unique in various senses and classify which special, highly structured spaces (e.g., lens spaces) can be created by this process. Second, we tackle minimal genus problems, investigating the simplest surfaces that knots can bound.
