We aim to characterize the knots that achieve this minimal genus and understand how that minimality depends on the ambient 4-manifold. This work directly addresses major open problems in low-dimensional topology, including the longstanding Berge conjecture concerning lens space surgery. It also finds application in DNA topology: when DNA molecules reorganize during cellular processes, they undergo changes mathematically equivalent to the surgeries we study. By developing new mathematical tools for understanding knots in general spaces, we aim not only to advance pure mathematics but also to provide fresh insights into the intricate topology of life's molecules. 當我們提及紐結，通常會聯想到三維空間中的一條封閉繩圈。數學家對這類經典紐結已有深入研究，發展出了強大的工具以區分其結構並度量其複雜度。然而，若我們在更奇異、彎曲的三維空間中打結，情況又將如何？本項目旨在對一般三維流形中的紐結展開系統性研究。此領域預計將湧現許多在標準歐氏三維空間中未曾見過的新現象，會對三維和四維拓撲學的核心問題至關重要。 本研究聚焦於兩個相互關聯的主題。首先，我們研究Dehn手術，這是一種通過切除紐結的鄰域並以全新方式重新黏合來改變空間的基本操作。我們將探討這類手術在各種意義下的唯一性，並對能透過該過程構造的高度結構化的特殊空間（例如透鏡空間）進行分類。其次，我們聚焦於最小虧格問題，探究紐結所能界定的最簡單曲面。我們旨在刻劃達到此最小虧格的紐結，並理解該最小性如何取決於周圍的四維流形。 本工作將直接嘗試解決低維拓撲學中的若干重大未解難題，包括長期懸而未決的 Berge 猜想（關於透鏡空間手術）。此外，該研究在DNA拓撲學中亦具備實際應用價值：當DNA分子進行重組時，其經歷的結構變化在數學本質上正對應於本項目所研究的手術操作。藉由發展一般空間中紐結的數學工具，我們不僅期望推進純數學的前沿發展，亦要洞開生命分子拓撲變幻的奧秘。

14301126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14301126.value: Q-曲率與共形不變方程的新挑戰

14301126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301126.value: Conformal geometry studies angle-preserving transformations on manifolds, using techniques from geometric analysis, which applies the tools of analysis to geometric problems. It plays a vital role in understanding of scalar curvature, $Q$-curvature, Einstein manifolds, etc. Among them, the stability and rigidity of scalar curvature is becoming a trending topic in geometric analysis. Moreover, it has applications in fields like computer graphics, vision, medical imaging, and theoretical physics. This project investigates central questions in conformal geometry concerning the compactness of solution spaces and the rigidity of geometric structures. A fundamental problem is determining the number of constant scalar curvature metrics within a conformal class on a compact manifold, which relates to the compactness of solutions to a second-order semilinear elliptic PDE with critical exponent. Building on the complete resolution by Khuri–Marques–Schoen and Brendle-Marques, which established a dimensional threshold at 24, we develop a robust and systematic framework to study the compactness of solutions for corresponding $2k$-th order PDEs and $Q$-curvature problems. We make new analytic and geometric observations for constructing a precise approximation of the blowing-up solutions. Our current results indicate threshold dimensions of 24 for the fourth-order case and 26 for the sixth-order case, and we plan to extend this analysis to general $2k$-th order operators. Along the way we will also investigate the existence and positive mass theorems for higher order conformally invariant operators. A key model in this study is that of Einstein manifolds, known for their rigidity under conformal deformations preserving constant scalar curvature, as established by Obata. We extend this approach using Gursky’s ideas to derive a higher-order version of Obata’s identity. This new identity will be instrumental in analyzing the rigidity of Einstein manifolds under conformal deformations that preserve constant $2k$-th order $Q$-curvature and may further lead to Liouville-type theorems for $p$-Laplace equations. These techniques may be extended to study the Lane-Emden system and give a complete answer to Lane-Emden Conjecture. 共形幾何（Conformal geometry）研究流形上保持角度不變的變換，並利用幾何分析（geometric analysis）的技術，將分析工具應用於幾何問題中。它在理解純量曲率（scalar curvature）、Q-曲率（Q-curvature）、愛因斯坦流形（Einstein manifolds）等方面發揮著至關重要的作用。其中，純量曲率的穩定性（stability）與剛性（rigidity）正成為幾何分析領域的熱門課題。此外，它在電腦圖形學、計算機視覺、醫學影像以及理論物理等領域皆有應用。本項目深入研究共形幾何中的核心問題，主要聚焦於解空間的緊緻性（compactness）和幾何結構的剛性。一個根本性的問題是確定緊緻流形上共形類中常純量曲率度量（constant scalar curvature metrics）的數量，這與具有臨界指數（critical exponent）的二階半線性橢圓偏微分方程（PDE）解的緊緻性密切相關。在 Khuri-Marques-Schoen 和 Brendle-Marques 建立 24 維度閾值的完整解答基礎上，我們開發了一個穩健且系統化的框架，用以研究相應 \(2k\) 階偏微分方程和 Q-曲率問題之解的緊緻性。我們提出了全新的分析與幾何觀測，以構建爆破解（blowing-up solutions）的精確逼近。我們目前的結果表明，四階情況的閾值維度為 24，六階情況的閾值維度為 26，並且我們計劃將此分析推廣至一般的 \(2k\) 階算子。在此過程中，我們還將研究高階共形不變算子的存在性定理（existence theorems）與正質量定理（positive mass theorems）。 本研究中的一個關鍵模型是愛因斯坦流形，如 Obata 所確立的結論，愛因斯坦流形以其在保持常純量曲率的共形形變下的剛性而聞名。我們借鑒 Gursky 的思想擴展了這一方法，從而推導出高階版本的 Obata 恆等式（Obata’s identity）。這一新的恆等式將在分析愛因斯坦流形於保持常 \(2k\) 階 Q-曲率的共形形變下的剛性時發揮關鍵作用，並可能進一步導出 \(p\)-拉普拉斯方程（p-Laplace equations）的 Liouville 型定理。這些技術亦可推廣至研究 Lane-Emden 系統，從而對 Lane-Emden 猜想（Lane-Emden Conjecture）給出完整的解答。

14301626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14301626.value: 莫法特磁弛豫猜想的數學研究

14301626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301626.value: Moffatt’s magnetic relaxation conjecture is an important theoretical problem in both mathematics and plasma physics. It concerns the long-time relaxation process of the magnetic field of Moffatt’s magnetic relaxation equation (MRE) to a topologically-preserved magnetohydrostatic (MHS) equilibrium, namely the Euler equilibrium (steady-states of the classical incompressible Euler equation). Despite the broad significance of magnetic relaxation across theoretical and applied science, rigorous mathematical results in this area remain scarce. For instance, while the perturbation theory for the two-dimensional MRE near a constant MHS equilibrium is well-established, its applicability to general inhomogeneous MHS equilibria remains an open question in the field. A primary difficulty is that the magnetic equation is an active vector equation. Furthermore, the coupling between the velocity and magnetic fields introduces cubic nonlinearities into the magnetic equation, which obscure any clear relaxation mechanism for the magnetic field. Consequently, the current mathematical understanding of Moffatt’s magnetic relaxation conjecture remains far from satisfactory. This project aims to achieve concrete progress on Moffatt's conjecture in the two-dimensional setting. (The three-dimensional case is distinctly different, as it exhibits nonlinear instabilities even around a constant background magnetic field.) At first, for any non-degenerate sheared magnetic fields, we plan to establish their global-in-time nonlinear stability by developing desired decay estimates for the linearized equation of the dissipative part of the magnetic field. The dynamics of Moffatt’s MRE far from MHS equilibrium are both fascinating and challenging. We observe that Moffatt’s MRE enjoys a scaling-invariance property and therefore propose to study magnetic relaxation conjecture for the solutions that are invariant under this scaling. Our motivation is that the additional symmetry reduces one degree of freedom, eliminates two derivatives from the equation, and thereby leads to a one-dimensional compressible-fluid-type equation, whose solutions are expected to converge to equilibrium as time diverges. Finally, we propose to perform a numerical analysis of Moffatt’s MRE in the multi-dimensional case, aiming to provide effective algorithms and long-time simulation. In summary, this project seeks to validate Moffatt's magnetic relaxation conjecture in several highly non-trivial scenarios, combining novel theoretical strategies with supporting numerical evidence. The strategies developed herein are expected to provide a framework that can be adapted to study magnetic relaxation in other related systems. 莫法特磁弛豫猜想是數學和等離子體物理學中的重要理論問題。它涉及莫法特磁弛豫方程（MRE）中磁場的長時間弛豫過程，直到達到拓樸守恆的磁流體靜力平衡（MHS）狀態，即歐拉平衡（經典不可壓縮歐拉方程的穩態）。儘管磁弛豫在理論和應用科學領域具有廣泛的意義，但該領域的嚴謹數學成果仍匱乏。例如，雖然二維MRE在恆定MHS附近的微擾理論已經相當成熟，但其對一般非均勻MHS的適用性仍然是該領域的一個開放性問題。主要困難在於磁方程式是一個主動向量方程式。此外，速度場和磁場之間的耦合會在磁方程中引入三次非線性，這使得磁場的弛豫機制變得模糊不清。因此，目前對莫法特磁弛豫猜想的數學理解還遠遠不夠令人滿意。 本計畫旨在二維情況下對莫法特猜想取得實質進展。（三維情況截然不同，即使在恆定的背景磁場附近，它也可表現出非線性不穩定性。）首先，對於任意非退化的剪切磁場，我們計劃透過建立磁場耗散部分線性化方程式所需的衰減估計，來建立其全局非線性穩定性。遠離MHS的莫法特磁弛豫方程式的動力學既引人入勝又充滿挑戰。其次, 我們觀察到莫法特磁弛豫方程式具有尺度不變性，因此，我們提出研究在此尺度下不變的解的磁弛豫猜想。我們的動機是，額外的對稱性減少了一個自由度，消除了方程式中的兩個導數，從而導出一個一維可壓縮流體型方程。其解有望隨著時間的發散而收斂到平衡態。最後，我們計劃對多維情況下的莫法特磁弛豫方程式進行數值分析，旨在提供有效的演算法和長時間模擬方法。總之，本計畫旨在驗證莫法特磁弛豫猜想在幾個高度複雜的場景中的有效性，結合新穎的理論策略和數值證據。我們預期本計畫提出的策略可以應用於研究其他相關係統中的磁弛豫。

14301826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301826.value: Left- and right-handed circularly polarized light carrying spin angular momentum can serve as powerful and robust information carriers. The development of chiral light sources has therefore recently sparked intensive attention owing to their diverse applications in three-dimensional display and imaging, enantiomeric analysis, asymmetric organic synthesis, spintronics, and quantum photonics. The ability to generate chiral light at nanoscale is particularly important, as nanoscale light sources are essential for building ultra-compact and energy-efficient devices for sensing, computing, and data storage, paving the way for next-generation photonic circuits. Current strategies for creating chiral light rely on two major approaches. One utilizes chiral luminescent molecules, yet chiral molecules typically suffer from weak chiroptical responses. The other couples light-emitting materials with non-emissive chiral nanostructures to modulate polarization through selective chiral light interactions. Most current nanoscale chiral light sources require external laser excitation, making them bulky and difficult to integrate onto electronic chips. The ultimate goal is to fabricate a nanoscale, electrically powered component capable of emitting bright and pure chiral light under an applied voltage. Circularly polarized electroluminescence has been realized by incorporating chiral nano-entities, such as phosphorescent emitters, metallo-mesogens, and lanthanide complexes, into the emissive layers of light-emitting diodes. However, existing electrically powered chiral light sources remain macroscopic in size, limiting their integration into miniaturized on-chip devices and advanced integrated systems. Herein we propose to develop innovative electrically driven nanoscale chiral light sources by integrating advanced chiral plasmonic nanostructures with two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs). The investigation will center on two types of state-of-the-art hybrid nanostructures. The first comprises chiral Au nanoparticles covered with TMDC monolayers or bilayers, and the second is chiral plasmonic nanocavities constructed out of chiral Au nanoparticles and a pyramided Au mirror and sandwiched with TMDC monolayers or bilayers. The chiral light-matter interactions and chiroptical responses of various two-dimensional excitons will be examined under optical excitation for understanding. Electrically driven circularly polarized light-emitting diodes (CP-LEDs) will further be fabricated by incorporating TMDC p-n junctions within the hybrid nanostructures. Their chiral electroluminescence properties will be systematically evaluated. The major goal is to achieve a type of electrically driven nanoscale CP-LED that can deliver superior electroluminescence dissymmetry factors and high emission efficiencies. Through the successful execution of this project, we will establish a versatile and groundbreaking platform for on-chip integrable chiral light sources, unlocking new opportunities in quantum information technologies, ultra-sensitive chiral molecular sensing, and secure optical communication systems. 攜帶自旋角動量的左旋和右旋圓偏振光可作為強大且穩健的訊息載體；手性光源因其在三維顯示與成像、對映體分析、不對稱有機合成、自旋電子學及量子光子學等領域的廣泛應用，近年來備受關注。在納米尺度上產生手性光的能力尤其重要，因為納米光源是建構用於感測、運算和資料儲存的超緊湊、高能效裝置的關鍵，並為下一代光子電路的發展奠定了基礎。目前產生手性光源的方法主要有兩種：一種是利用手性發光分子，但手性分子通常存在手性光學響應較弱的問題；另一種是將發光材料與非發光手性納米結構耦合，透過選擇性的手性光相互作用來調控偏振態。現有的納米級手性光源大多需要外部雷射激發，導致裝置體積龐大，難以整合到電子晶片上。這個研究方向的最終目標是製造一種納米級、電驅動的組件，使其在施加電壓通電流時能夠發射明亮且純淨的手性光。透過將磷光發射體、金屬介晶和鑭系配合物等手性納米單元引入發光二極體（LED）的發光層中，已實現了圓偏振電致發光。然而，現有的電驅動手性光源尺寸仍處於宏觀量級，這限制了其在微型化片上裝置及先進整合系統中的應用。 本計畫旨在透過將先進的手性等離激元納米結構與二維過渡金屬硫族化合物（TMDC）結合，開發創新的電力驅動納米級手性光源。本研究將聚焦於兩種尖端的混合納米結構：第一種由覆蓋有單層或雙層TMDC的手性金奈米顆粒構成；第二種則是由手性金納米顆粒與金字塔形金反射鏡建構、並夾有單層或雙層TMDC的手性等離激元納米腔。我們將透過光學激發，深入探討各種二維激子的手性光-物質相互作用及手性光學響應。此外，透過在這些混合納米結構中整合TMDC p-n結，我們將製備電驅動圓偏振光發光二極體（CP-LED），並系統評估其手性電致發光特性。本計畫的核心目標是實現一種兼具優異電致發光不對稱因子與高發光效率的電力驅動納米級CP-LED。該計畫的成功實施將建立一個通用且具有突破性的片上整合手性光源平台，為量子資訊技術、超靈敏手性分子感測及安全光通訊系統開闢新的應用前景。

14302126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14302126.value: 物理真空邊界條件下的愛因斯坦-歐拉系統

14302126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302126.value: From a purely mathematical standpoint, this project aims to deepen our understanding of fluid motion where Einstein’s theory plays a significant role. Specifically, we examine the dynamics of relativistic stars in spacetimes governed by the Einstein–Euler system with a physical vacuum boundary. The primary focus is on exploring the distinctive aspects of the Einstein–Euler system with a physical vacuum boundary, which existing literature techniques cannot adequately address by simple adaptation. 從純數學的角度來看，本計畫旨在深化我們對愛因斯坦理論發揮顯著作用之流體運動的理解。具體而言，我們探討在受具物理真空邊界的愛因斯坦–歐拉系統所支配的時空中，相對論性恆星的動力學行為。研究的核心焦點在於探索具有物理真空邊界之愛因斯坦–歐拉系統的獨特特徵，這些特徵是現有文獻技術無法透過簡單修正來妥善解決的。

14302426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14302426.value: 自旋系統及對數凹測度的極限定理

14302426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302426.value: Asymptotic theory serves as a unifying theme in probability and statistics. The central limit theorem (CLT), a renowned classical result in this field, states that the distribution of a sum of n independent and identically distributed random variables, when n is large, can be approximated by a normal distribution. In practical scenarios, data often exhibit dependence. Establishing the CLT for random variables with complex dependency structures is one of the most active research topics in probability theory. In this project, we will study the CLT for spin systems and log-concave random vectors, which are ubiquitous in mathematical physics and statistical inference. While much progress has been made, most existing results are limited to specific situations, such as the total magnetization of special mean-field spin systems and the projection of log-concave random vectors in a random direction, due to technical challenges. We aim to prove general CLTs for low-dimensional projections of large spin systems or high-dimensional log-concave random vectors using Stein's method, which has proven to be a powerful tool for establishing the CLT for dependent random variables. We will first use the generalized exchangeable pair approach to prove the CLT for the projection of mean-field spin systems in an arbitrary direction. We will then apply the density approach and the Stein kernel to handle the projection of log-concave random vectors in a given non-random direction. Finally, we will explore a combination of a new renormalization group method with the results for log-concave random vectors to address spin systems with short-range interactions. The results of this project will address important questions in the study of spin systems and log-concave measures. Moreover, we expect that the new approaches developed in this project will be useful in addressing related problems in other areas of probability and statistics, such as Bayesian posterior inference. 漸近理論是貫穿概率論與統計學的一條重要主線。中心極限定理是此領域中一項著名的經典結果；它指出，當 n 足夠大時，n 個獨立同分佈隨機變量之和的分佈可以用正態分佈近似。然而，在實際情況中，數據往往具有依賴性。為具有複雜依賴結構的隨機變量建立中心極限定理，是概率論中最活躍的研究課題之一。 本項目將研究自旋系統及對數凹隨機向量的中心極限定理。這兩類對象廣泛出現於數理物理及統計推斷之中。儘管相關研究已取得不少進展，但由於技術上的困難，現有結果大多只適用於某些特定情況，例如特殊平均場自旋系統的總磁化量，以及對數凹隨機向量沿隨機方向的投影。 我們擬運用 Stein 方法，為大型自旋系統或高維對數凹隨機向量的低維投影建立一般性的中心極限定理。Stein 方法已被證明是為具依賴性的隨機變量建立中心極限定理的有力工具。首先，我們將採用廣義可交換對方法，證明平均場自旋系統沿任意方向投影的中心極限定理。其後，我們將運用密度方法及 Stein 核，處理對數凹隨機向量沿某個給定非隨機方向的投影。最後，我們將探索如何結合一種新的重整化群方法與對數凹隨機向量的相關結果，以研究具有短程相互作用的自旋系統。 本項目的研究成果將解答自旋系統及對數凹測度研究中的若干重要問題。此外，我們預期，本項目所發展的新方法亦可用於處理概率論與統計學其他領域的相關問題，例如貝葉斯後驗推斷。

14302626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14302626.value: 三維鏡像對稱與族Fukaya理論

14302626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302626.value: 3d mirror symmetry is a mysterious duality for certain pairs of hyperkahler manifolds. When the space is a point, it reduces to the usual mirror symmetry originated in string theory. The PI propose to develop family Fukaya theory to unveil the mystery of 3d mirror symmetry. 三維鏡像對稱性是針對特定 hyperkähler 流形對的一種神秘對偶關係。當空間退化為單點時，它便還原為源自弦論的常規鏡像對稱性。專案負責人計劃發展族Fukaya理論，以揭示三維鏡像對稱性的奧秘。

14302726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14302726.value: 在微納加工金剛石壓力包中對於范德華超導體高壓下的點接觸能譜探測研究

14302726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302726.value: Point-contact spectroscopy (PCS) is a powerful probe of superconductivity as it enables direct measurement of the superconducting gap via Andreev reflection. However, PCS has not yet been systematically implemented for investigating thin flakes of van der Waals superconductors under high pressure. By leveraging microfabrication expertise to pattern gold electrodes onto diamond anvils, we aim to establish reliable point contacts between normal metals and thin superconductors, thereby enabling spectroscopic measurements in diamond anvil cells. A particular focus will be placed on conducting PCS in the tunneling regime and integrating PCS capability with complementary high-pressure transport techniques -- such as Subnikov-de Haas oscillations -- to facilitate multiprobe investigations on the same samples. Our study will target van der Waals superconductors of current interest. The combined strengths of the Hong Kong team’s extensive high-pressure experience and proven track record in thin-flake measurements, together with the France team’s expertise in PCS, will significantly accelerate the advancement of this technique.

14303026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14303026.value: 結構未知之因子增強混合隸屬模型

14303026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303026.value: Mixed membership models (MMMs) offer a powerful framework for capturing complex individual heterogeneity in multivariate longitudinal data by allowing subjects to hold partial membership across multiple latent profiles rather than being confined to a single class, as in traditional finite mixture models. This flexibility enables the identification of nuanced patterns often missed by conventional approaches. However, existing MMMs typically assume fully observed predictors, overlooking latent traits that may influence outcomes and are represented through multiple correlated surrogates. Treating these manifestations as independent predictors disregards their shared structure, induces multicollinearity, and complicates interpretation. Furthermore, the underlying dependence and heterogeneity structures, including the number of latent factors, their manifestations, and the number of extreme profiles, are often unknown, making joint determination of these components computationally challenging and rendering existing information-criterion-based methods inefficient. To address these gaps, we propose a factor-augmented MMM that integrates an exploratory factor analysis component to uncover dependence structures among multiple manifest variables and a mixed-membership component augmented with latent factors to capture complex, heterogeneous associations between outcomes and both observed and latent factors. By extracting lower-dimensional traits from multiple manifestations and allowing partial membership for each individual, the model reduces predictor dimensionality, mitigates multicollinearity, enhances interpretability, and captures both population- and individual-level heterogeneity through subject-specific mixed membership scores. Our goal is to develop rigorous statistical methods for simultaneously estimating latent factors, factor loadings, and extreme profiles within a unified framework that combines model selection and parameter estimation, overcoming the limitations of existing multi-stage approaches. The methodology will be adapted to accommodate diverse outcome types and capture nonlinear associations between outcomes and predictors by leveraging modern machine learning techniques. Key extensions include (i) incorporating functional covariates, (ii) accommodating survival outcomes under semi-competing risks, and (iii) addressing variable-and-time co-clustered structures. For statistical inference, we will develop a Bayesian framework coupled with a hybrid Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm that integrates data augmentation, Gibbs sampling, the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm, and an adjust-bound sampling scheme. Multiple Bayesian penalization strategies will be employed to jointly determine the number of factors, factor loading structures, and extreme profiles. In addition, we will explore alternative inference procedures and investigate the theoretical properties of the proposed estimators under the frequentist framework. Finally, we will develop user-friendly software and apply the proposed methodologies to real-world problems in Hong Kong and beyond. 混合隸屬模型透過允許個體同時對多個潛在剖面具有部分隸屬關係，而非如傳統有限混合模型般僅被歸類至單一類別，為刻畫多變量縱向資料中的複雜個體異質性提供了一個強而有力的框架。此種靈活性使模型能夠辨識傳統方法往往無法捕捉的細緻模式。然而，現有的混合隸屬模型通常假設所有預測變數皆為完全觀測資料，因而忽略了可能影響結果、且需透過多個相關指標加以衡量的潛在特質。若將這些指標視為彼此獨立的預測變數，不僅會忽略其共享的潛在結構，亦可能造成多重共線性問題並降低模型結果的可解釋性。此外，資料中的依賴結構與異質性結構，包括潛在因子的數量、其對應的觀測指標，以及極端剖面的數量，通常皆為未知。要同時決定這些組成要素在計算上相當困難，而現有基於資訊準則的模型選擇方法往往效率不足。為了解決上述問題，本研究提出一種因子增強混合隸屬模型以整合探索性因素分析與混合隸屬模型兩大組件。前者用於發掘多個觀測指標之間的依賴結構，後者則透過引入潛在因子來捕捉結果變數與觀測及潛在因子之間複雜且異質的關聯。透過從多個觀測指標中萃取低維度潛在特質，並允許每位個體同時具有多個潛在剖面的部分隸屬關係，本模型可降低預測變數維度、緩解多重共線性問題、提升結果詮釋性，並透過受試者專屬的混合隸屬分數同時捕捉群體層次與個體層次的異質性。 本研究旨在發展一套嚴謹的統計方法，於單一統一架構下同時估計潛在因子、因子負荷量及極端剖面，並結合模型選擇與參數估計，克服現有多階段方法的限制。所提出的方法將進一步擴展，以適用於不同類型的結果變數，並結合現代機器學習技術以捕捉結果與預測變數之間的非線性關係。主要延伸方向包括：（i）納入函數型共變數；（ii）處理半競爭風險架構下的存活結果；以及（iii）處理變數與時間共同分群結構。在統計推論方面，本研究將建立一套貝葉斯推論框架，並發展混合式馬可夫鏈蒙地卡羅演算法，整合資料增補、Gibbs 抽樣法、Metropolis-Hastings 演算法，以及調整界限抽樣機制。此外，我們將採用多種貝葉斯懲罰化策略以同時決定潛在因子的數量、因子負荷結構以及極端剖面的數目。除貝葉斯方法外，本研究亦將探索其他推論程序，並在頻率學派架構下研究所提出估計量的理論性質。最後，我們將開發易於使用的軟體工具，並將所提出的方法應用於香港及其他地區的實際問題，以展示其理論價值與實務效益。

14303126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303126.value: This proposal is motivated from the frontier of science. By measuring molecular features in its native spatial context, spatial omics technologies have become essential tools in revealing the organization and heterogeneity of biological tissues. New spatial multi-omics technologies, which jointly profiles spatial transcriptome and epigenome/protein markers/metabolome for the same tissue section, have expanded the frontiers of spatial techniques. Compared to single-omics technologies, spatial multi-omics provides additional molecular modality for more comprehensive profiling of the tissue and more importantly the unique opportunity for a deep understanding of the regulation across different molecular modalities within the native spatial context. Following the tide of laboratory developments and commercialized platforms, spatial multi-omics datasets are accumulating fast. However, the complex multi-modal data structure and the scale of information in spatial multi-omics present challenges to realize the potential of analyzing such data. Dimension reduction that extracts the low-dimensional representation of the pixels is crucial in analyzing spatial multi-omics datasets. It facilitates spatial domain identification through clustering and data visualization, revealing the tissue organization and heterogeneity, and is routinely used as a preprocessing step for other analyses. Inferring the cross-modality regulation is also important in analyzing such data. The aim of this proposal is to develop a unified framework that simultaneously performs dimension reduction and models the cross-modality association of the molecular features for spatial multi-omics. One key innovation in our proposed framework is a two-level graph attention autoencoder that simultaneously models the cross-modality association of the molecular features and embeds the pixels in a low-dimensional space, which will both enable deep data integration for the multi-omics features to better extract the low-dimensional embeddings for clustering and data visualization and provide rich insight on cross-modality regulation. The proposed framework will be applicable to different platforms and will leverage the unique advantage powered by spatial multi-omics to infer cis-regulation, trans-regulation, protein-gene association, and gene-metabolite association. We also propose to incorporate reference data to facilitate inferring the cell-type composition of the pixels, which will complement clustering and align the data with the existing knowledge of cell types. Powered by GPU computing, our proposed framework will be scalable to large datasets. Our approach will reveal the spatial organization of the tissue and how cells organize and interact in their native environment, deciphering the complex microenvironment of tissues. The identified cross-modality association of the molecular features will advance the understanding of complex biological systems and human diseases and facilitate drug development. 本研究計畫的提出源自科學前沿的發展。透過在分子所處的原生空間脈絡中測量其分子特徵，空間體學技術已成為揭示生物組織之組織結構與異質性的重要工具。新興的空間多體學技術可在同一組織切片上聯合分析空間轉錄體，以及表觀基因體／蛋白質標記／代謝體，進一步拓展了空間技術的疆界。與單一體學技術相比，空間多體學提供了額外的分子模態，可更全面地描繪組織特性；更重要的是，它提供了在原生空間脈絡下，深入理解不同分子模態之間調控機制的獨特機會。 隨著實驗技術的快速進展與商業化平台的普及，空間多體學資料集正迅速累積。然而，空間多體學中複雜的多模態資料結構以及龐大的資訊規模，使得如何充分發揮這類資料分析潛力面臨重大挑戰。能夠萃取像素低維表示的降維方法，是分析空間多體學資料集的關鍵。它有助於透過分群進行空間區域辨識與資料視覺化，揭示組織的結構與異質性，並且也常被作為其他分析程序的前處理步驟。推論跨模態調控關係同樣是分析此類資料的重要課題。本計畫的目標，是發展一套統一框架，能夠同時執行降維，並建模空間多體學中分子特徵的跨模態關聯。 我們所提出框架的一項核心創新，是一個雙層級圖注意力自編碼器，能夠同時建模分子特徵的跨模態關聯，並將像素嵌入至低維空間中。這不僅能促進多體學特徵的深度資料整合，以更有效地萃取用於分群與資料視覺化的低維嵌入表示，也能提供豐富的跨模態調控洞見。所提出的框架可適用於不同平台，並將善用空間多體學的獨特優勢，以推論順式調控、反式調控、蛋白質—基因關聯，以及基因—代謝物關聯。我們也提出納入參考資料，以協助推論各像素中的細胞類型組成，藉此補充分群分析，並使資料能與既有的細胞類型知識相互對應。在 GPU 運算能力的支援下，我們提出的框架亦可擴展至大型資料集。 我們的方法將揭示組織的空間組織結構，以及細胞如何在其原生環境中進行排列與互動，進而解析組織中複雜的微環境。所鑑別出的分子特徵跨模態關聯，將有助於推進對複雜生物系統與人類疾病的理解，並促進藥物開發。

14303226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14303226.value: 基於光鑷的玻色少體量子體系確定性構建與研究

14303226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303226.value: The few-body problem is a fundamental topic in physics, playing a crucial role in nuclear, chemical, biophysical, and atomic systems. Ultracold atoms, with their unprecedented tunability and control, have become a powerful platform for studying few-body physics. Recent advancements, particularly the development of optical tweezers and re-arranged arrays of ultracold atoms, have enabled the deterministic assembly and manipulation of quantum systems at the single-particle level. While optical tweezer systems have been widely used in advancing quantum computing and quantum simulation with neutral atoms, they also offer a powerful method to investigate few-body physics with precise, atom-by-atom control. This approach has great potential to bridge the gap between few- and many-body systems, serving as a pristine testbed for theoretical models. We propose to construct an optical tweezer apparatus to deterministically assemble few-body systems of bosonic Rb85 atoms in the motional ground state of a single optical tweezer, with tunable interactions enabled by a Feshbach resonance. This platform will allow a systematic investigation of few-body phenomena, such as Efimov resonances, by precisely controlling atom-atom interactions and probing their signatures with high-resolution and single atom sensitivity. Additionally, we plan to explore higher-order phenomena, such as collisional resonances involving four- and five-body systems, by precisely assembling and varying the number of atoms in the tweezer. Furthermore, our approach will facilitate the direct study of the elusive few-body bound states, such as Efimov trimers, free from collisional losses. By gradually increasing the number of atoms in the system, we will investigate the transition from few-body physics to collective many-body behavior, including the formation of a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC). We will measure interaction energy shifts, breathing mode dynamics, and second-order momentum and spatial correlations to map the crossover from discrete few-body spectra to collective behaviors. Importantly, we aim to identify the critical atom number at which many-body effects, such as long-range coherence and symmetry breaking, emerge. The breathing mode frequency, for example, is expected to shift from its few-body value to the hydrodynamic limit as the number of atoms increases, reflecting the collective excitations of the BEC. Our proposed research will provide new insights into the emergence of many-body quantum coherence from few-body interactions for bosons and establish a versatile platform for studying quantum systems atom by atom. By connecting few-body physics to the collective behavior of mesoscopic systems, this work will deepen our understanding of the transition from microscopic to macroscopic quantum behavior. 少體問題是物理學中的核心課題之一，廣泛存在於核物理、化學、生物物理與原子物理等領域。由於超冷原子具有高度可調控性與優異的實驗控制能力，近年來已成為研究少體物理的重要平台。特別是隨著光鑷技術及超冷原子陣列重排的快速發展，研究者已能在單粒子層次上，對量子系統進行確定性的組裝與操控。雖然光鑷系統已廣泛應用於中性原子量子計算與量子模擬，但它同時也為少體物理研究提供了一種極具優勢的方法，使我們能夠逐一控制原子並精確探測其行為。這樣的平台不僅有助於連結少體與多體系統，也為理論模型的檢驗提供了理想而純淨的實驗基礎。 本計畫擬建置一套光鑷實驗系統，在單一光鑷的運動基態中，確定性地組裝由玻色原子85Rb構成的少體系統，並藉由 Feshbach 共振實現原子間相互作用的可調控制。在此平台上，我們將能精確調整原子間相互作用，並以高分辨率及單原子靈敏度量測其物理訊號，從而系統性地研究各種少體現象，例如 Efimov 共振。此外，我們也將透過精準控制光鑷中的原子數，進一步探索更高階的少體效應，例如四體與五體系統中的碰撞共振。更重要的是，此方法有望讓我們在不受碰撞損失干擾的情況下，直接研究過去難以觀測的少體束縛態，例如 Efimov 三聚體。在此基礎上，我們也將逐步增加系統中的原子數，研究物理行為如何由少體區域過渡至集體性的多體區域，包括玻色–愛因斯坦凝聚的形成過程。 本研究將有助於釐清玻色子系統中，多體量子相干如何從少體相互作用中逐步湧現，並建立一個可逐原子操控與研究量子系統的多功能實驗平台。透過連結少體物理與介觀系統中的集體行為，本計畫將進一步深化我們對量子現象由微觀走向宏觀之過渡機制的理解。

14303326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14303326.value: 具有拓撲保護的完美相干吸波器

14303326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303326.value: Absorption is a fundamental process in nature where energy from waves, such as sound and light, is captured and converted into another form, like heat or electrical current. This phenomenon is crucial in many technologies, from noise-canceling headphones to solar panels. Traditional absorbers rely on materials that inherently dissipate energy, but they often struggle to achieve perfect absorption without significant energy loss. A breakthrough in this field came with the discovery of the coherent perfect absorber (CPA). Unlike conventional absorbers, a CPA does not require highly lossy materials. Instead, it exploits wave interference, where carefully tuned incoming waves cancel each other out inside the absorber, leading to 100% energy absorption. CPAs have been demonstrated in various systems, including optical, microwave, and acoustic devices, with potential applications in energy harvesting, signal processing, and quantum optics. However, a major limitation of CPAs is their extreme sensitivity to imperfections. Even tiny deviations in the system, such as slight changes in material properties or misalignment of incoming waves, can drastically reduce absorption efficiency. This fragility makes real-world applications challenging, as perfect experimental conditions are rarely achievable. Recent advances in topological photonics, a field studying topological phases of electromagnetic waves, offer a promising solution. In topological photonic systems, waves can be guided without being scattered by defects and disorders, a phenomenon known as topological protection. This robustness arises from deep mathematical principles (such as the bulk-boundary correspondence) that ensure wave stability as long as the overall structure remains intact. Such topologically protected edge states have been demonstrated in photonic crystals and metamaterials at various frequencies. In this project, we propose merging the concepts of coherent perfect absorption and topological protection to create topological CPAs. The key idea is to design systems where incoming waves are guided to topological modes and directed toward a lossy element that perfectly absorbs them. The topological CPAs represent a paradigm shift in wave absorption, transforming a fragile phenomenon into a robust and practical technology. By harnessing the power of topological protection, we can overcome the key limitations of conventional CPAs, enabling new applications in energy, communications, and sensing. This project not only advances fundamental wave physics but also paves the way for real-world devices that perform reliably under imperfect conditions—an essential step toward next-generation wave-based technologies. "吸收"是自然界中的一項基本過程，聲音與光等波所攜帶的能量會被擷取，並轉換成其他形式，例如熱能或電流。這種現象對許多技術至關重要，其應用範圍涵蓋降噪耳機與太陽能板等。傳統吸收體依靠本身能夠耗散能量的材料，但若沒有顯著的能量損耗，通常很難實現完美吸收。此領域的一項重大突破，是完美相干吸波器的發現。與傳統吸收體不同，完美相干吸波器 不需要使用高損耗材料，而是利用波的干涉效應：經過精確調控的入射波會在吸波器內彼此抵消，從而實現 100% 的能量吸收。 完美相干吸波器已在多種系統中獲得實驗驗證，包括光學、微波及聲學裝置，並具有應用於能量擷取、訊號處理與量子光學的潛力。然而，它的一項主要限制，是其對缺陷極為敏感。即使系統中僅存在極微小的偏差，例如材料特性的輕微變化，或入射波之間未能精確對準，都可能大幅降低吸收效率。這種脆弱性使其難以應用於現實環境，因為在實驗中幾乎不可能始終維持完美條件。 近年來，拓撲光子學的進展為解決這項問題提供了極具潛力的方法。拓撲光子學是一門研究電磁波拓撲相的領域。在拓撲光子系統中，波可以在不受缺陷與無序散射影響的情況下傳播，此現象稱為“拓撲保護”。這種穩健性源自深刻的數學原理，例如體－邊界對應關係。只要系統的整體結構保持完整，這些原理便能確保波的穩定性。此類受拓撲保護的邊緣態，已在不同頻率下的光子晶體與超材料中獲得實驗驗證。 在本項目中，我們提出將完美相干吸波器與拓撲保護的概念相結合，以建立“拓撲完美相干吸波器”。其核心構想是設計一種系統，使入射波被引導至拓撲模態，並進一步導向能夠將其完全吸收的損耗元件。這一器件代表了波吸收領域的一次典範轉移，能將原本脆弱的物理現象轉化為穩健且實用的技術。藉由運用拓撲保護的特性，我們可以克服傳統完美相干吸波器的主要限制，並開創其在能源、通訊與感測領域中的新應用。本計畫不僅將推進基礎波動物理的發展，也將為能夠在非理想條件下可靠運作的實際裝置鋪平道路，而這正是邁向下一代波動技術的關鍵一步。

14303526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14303526.value: 控制增強分散式量子計量

14303526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303526.value: Quantum metrology leverages quantum resources, such as superposition and entanglement, to surpass classical measurement precision limits. In local quantum metrology, which deals with single-probe systems, optimal strategies have been well studied. There is a good understanding of the ideal probe state, optimal control during parameter encoding, and the best measurement scheme, all of which together define the ultimate precision achievable in such settings. Distributed quantum metrology, which employs networks of spatially separated quantum sensors to measure global, spatially extended parameters, introduces new challenges that distinguish it from the single-sensor case. While local metrology focuses on maximizing sensitivity at one location, distributed quantum metrology aims to leverage quantum correlations between sensor nodes to extract collective information inaccessible to any individual sensor. Consequently, a primary research focus has been on identifying optimal entangled states shared across the network to enhance measurement precision. However, the role of quantum control during the sensing process is much less explored. A key distinction stems from the practical architecture of distributed networks: control operations are typically implemented locally at each sensor node. This constraint fundamentally distinguishes distributed control strategies from those used in single-sensor metrology and introduces specific design challenges. For these reasons, the ultimate precision limits attainable by controlled, distributed quantum networks remain significantly less understood than those for their single-sensor counterparts. This project seeks to address this gap by establishing a theoretical framework for control-enhanced distributed quantum metrology. We will derive fundamental precision limits for controlled distributed quantum metrology, design practical control sequences that actively shape parameter encoding dynamics across distributed probes to approach these limits, and validate these strategies in various scenarios involving both static and time-varying fields. The results of this project will advance the understanding and practical capabilities of distributed quantum metrology. By delineating the ultimate precision limits for these systems and developing control strategies to approach them, we will enable the development of high-precision sensor networks for various applications in practice, such as networked magnetometry, distributed imaging, and large-scale gravitational wave detection, where parameters are measured across a spatial field. 量子計量利用量子資源，例如疊加和糾纏，來超越經典測量的精度極限。在處理單探針系統的局域量子計量中，最優策略已被充分研究。人們對理想探針狀態、參數編碼過程中的最優控制以及最佳測量方案都有深入的理解，所有這些因素共同決定了此類情況下可達到的最終精度。 分散式量子計量利用空間分離的量子感測器網路來測量全局的、空間擴展的參數，這帶來了新的挑戰，使其區別於單一感測器情況。局域計量著重於最大化單一位置的靈敏度，而分散式量子計量則旨在利用感測器節點之間的量子關聯來提取任何單一感測器都無法取得的集體資訊。因此，一個主要的研究重點是識別網路中共享的最優糾纏態以提高測量精度。然而，量子控制在感測過程中的作用卻鮮少被研究。一個關鍵的區別在於分散式網路的實際架構：控制操作通常在每個感測器節點上本地執行。這項限制從根本上區分了分散式控制策略與單感測器計量策略，並帶來了特定的設計挑戰。因此，受控分散式量子網路所能達到的最終精度極限遠不如其單感測器對應系統那樣為人所知。 本計畫旨在透過建立一個控制增強型分散式量子計量的理論框架來彌補這一差距。我們將推導出受控分散式量子計量的基本精度極限，設計能夠主動調控分散式探針間參數編碼動態以接近這些極限的實用控制序列，並在涉及靜態和時變場的各種場景中驗證這些策略。 本計畫成果將增進人們對分散式量子計量的理解並提升其應用能力。透過闡明這些系統的最終精度極限並開發相應的控制策略，我們將推動高精度感測器網路在各種實際應用中的發展，例如網路化磁力測量、分散式成像和大規模重力波探測等，這些應用都需要測量空間場中的參數。

14303726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14303726.value: 發展序列式全氟烷基化–脫氟策略以構建新型含氟分子

14303726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303726.value: Fluorinated organic molecules exhibit unique properties in the development of pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and new materials. Approximately 20% of marketed drugs contain at least one fluorine atom. The field of organofluorine chemistry is an integral part of modern organic synthesis. Through the discovery of new reactions, high-value fluorine-containing compounds can be synthesized for important applications in our society. In contrast to well-established carbon-fluorine bond forming reactions, the cleavage and functionalization of carbon-fluorine bonds in perfluoroalkylated compounds can give access to previously unattainable fluorinated motifs. We herein propose a sequential perfluoroalkylation-defluorination strategy to synthesize novel fluorinated molecules while addressing the environmental issues of removing persistent fluoroalkyl substances by C-F bond activation. Prior studies of defluorinative functionalization of perfluoroalkylated compounds have been largely focused on trifluoromethyl groups with limited scope and application. We will introduce pentafluoroethyl group and longer chain perfluoroalkyl groups into non-fluorinated precursors based on the methods and reagents developed in our laboratory. Subsequent defluorofunctionalization of the perfluoroalkylated intermediates such as pentafluoroethyl alkenes and arenes can lead to novel polyfluorinated motifs. Transition metal catalysis and photoredox catalysis will be employed for the selective C-F bond functionalization. Furthermore, asymmetric transformations can facilitate the challenging construction of quaternary stereogenic centres containing both fluorine and trifluoromethyl moieties. The outcome of this project will have an impact on both industrial application and fundamental research. We expect the developed methodology to be widely adopted by practitioners in the fields of medicinal chemistry and materials science for synthesizing useful organofluorine compounds. Research personnel and students will be trained throughout the project who can contribute to the society in the industrial and academic sectors. 含氟有機分子在藥物、農用化學品及新材料的研發中展現出獨特的理化性質。目前，約有 20% 的上市藥物含有至少一個氟原子。因此，有機氟化學已成為現代有機合成中不可或缺的重要領域。透過發展新型化學反應，可高效合成具有重要應用價值的含氟化合物，從而服務於醫藥、材料及其他相關領域的發展。 相較於已相當成熟的碳-氟鍵形成反應，全氟烷基化合物中碳-氟鍵的選擇性斷裂與官能團化，為構建傳統方法難以獲得的新型含氟結構提供了嶄新的途徑。本研究擬提出一項序列式全氟烷基化-脫氟策略，以合成具有新穎結構的含氟分子；與此同時，亦期望透過碳–氟鍵活化，為持久性含氟烷基物質的去除及其所引發的環境問題提供新的化學解決方案。 過往針對全氟烷基化合物進行脫氟官能團化的研究，主要集中於三氟甲基化合物，其底物範圍及實際應用仍存在一定限制。本研究將利用本實驗室所發展的方法與試劑，將五氟乙基及更長鏈的全氟烷基引入非氟化前驅物中；隨後，對所生成的全氟烷基化中間體，例如五氟乙基取代烯烴及芳烴，進行選擇性脫氟官能團化，以構建一系列新型多氟結構。研究將結合過渡金屬催化與光氧化還原催化策略，實現碳-氟鍵的選擇性官能團化。此外，透過發展不對稱轉化反應，有望解決同時含有F與CF₃基團的四級立體中心之高難度立體選擇性構建問題。 針對選擇性C-F鍵官能團化，我們將採用過渡金屬催化與光氧化還原催化技術。此外，不對稱轉化技術能促進同時含有氟（F）與三氟甲基（CF3）之季碳立體生成中心的構建，克服此一具挑戰性的化學難題。 本計畫的研究成果將對工業應用與基礎研究產生深遠的影響。我們預期所開發的方法論將被藥物化學與材料科學領域的從業者廣泛採用，用於合成實用之有機氟化合物。同時，在整個計畫的執行過程中，我們也將致力於培育研究人員與學生，使其未來能在工業界與學術界為社會做出實質貢獻。

14303826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14303826.value: 基於張量網絡的多-多體理論

14303826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303826.value: In recent years, a wave of new ideas is emerging, aiming at studying many quantum many-body systems all together, which might be called the many-many-body theory. Tensor network is a practical tool widely used in the numerical computation of many-body systems. We will develop a candidate framework for the many-many-body theory, based on the graphical calculus of tensor networks. It is necessary to collect all or many tensor networks together, and consider the entire space formed by these tensor networks. This leads to the central notion in this project: protensor network, which refers to the space formed by a certain class of tensor networks. Categorical calculus methods will be employed. Focus will be on the topologically invariant symmetric protensor networks. The theory of (co)limits of protensor networks will be developed to compute various universal invariants of a class of many-body systems. These invariants will give duality dictionaries since the same tensor network admits multiple interpretations under different physical scenarios. Moreover, since tensor network is a unified tool with applications in not only physics, but also mathematics and computer science, it is expected that our investigation leads to broad interdisciplinary applications in these fields. 近年來，一股新的研究思潮正在興起，其目標是將眾多量子多體系統作為一個整體來研究，此方向可稱為多-多體理論（many-many-body theory）。張量網絡是一種廣泛用於多體系統數值計算的實用工具。本項目將基於張量網絡的圖形演算，發展一套多-多體理論的候選框架。為此，我們需要將全部或大量張量網絡匯集起來，並研究由這些張量網絡所形成的整體空間。這引出了本項目的核心概念：升張量網絡（protensor network），即由某一類張量網絡所構成的空間。我們將採用範疇演算的方法進行研究，重點聚焦於具拓撲不變性的對稱升張量網絡。我們將發展升張量網絡的（餘）極限理論，以計算一類多體系統的各種普適不變量。因為同一張量網絡在不同物理情景下可以具有多種詮釋，這些不變量將建立對偶詞典。此外，由於張量網絡是一種統一工具，其應用不僅遍及物理學，亦涵蓋數學與計算機科學，因此預期本研究將在這些領域帶來廣泛的跨學科應用。

14303926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14303926.value: 硫屬元素硼酸鹽的設計、合成及其在催化中的應用

14303926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303926.value: The proposed project will aim to develop a new class of efficient catalytic protocols that employ chalcogenonium borate catalysts as chalcogen-bond donors for diverse chemical transformations. Chalcogen-bond donors based on soft chalcogens (e.g. S, Se, Te) have attracted increasing attention as Lewis acid-type organocatalysts, offering a metal-free alternative in organic synthesis. Among them, cationic chalcogenonium salts have emerged as a particularly potent class, exhibiting superior catalytic performance compared with their neutral counterparts. This enhanced activity arises from their stronger electron-accepting character. However, the development of chalcogenonium catalysts is constrained by several limitations. One of the challenges is the requirement for non-coordinating anions to reduce deactivation of the Lewis acidic site, which requires cumbersome synthetic routes involving stoichiometric silver salts and thereby restricts structural diversification. Furthermore, some chalcogenonium salt catalysts still exhibit limited reactivity and narrow substrate scope, and their potential in asymmetric catalysis remains underdeveloped. Our research group has developed numerous catalytic protocols based on soft chalcogen catalysts (e.g., Y.Y.Yeung et al. Nature Catal. 2020, 3, 993; JACS 2021, 143, 12745; ACIE 2022, e202208009; Chem 2023, 9, 1255; ACS Catal. 2024, 14, 9198; ACIE 2025, e202711770). These protocols have been applied to the synthesis of valuable building blocks and advanced intermediates of drug molecules. Building on this foundation, we hypothesized that a strategic redesign could help overcome existing limitations in chalcogenium catalysis. We envisioned that chalcogenonium borates, which are formed from chalcogen and boron Lewis acids, could provide effective anion isolation, thereby strengthening the chalcogen bond without deactivating the cationic catalytic site, while also offering multiple opportunities for structural tuning. We anticipated that our newly designed chalcogenonium borate catalysts would unlock unprecedented reactivity and selectivity, enabling transformations that are currently inefficient or inaccessible. Our preliminary, unpublished findings validate this hypothesis. We discovered that readily accessible chalcogenonium borates function as effective catalysts across a broad range of valuable transformations. Moreover, we prepared a chiral chalcogenonium borate catalyst that promotes asymmetric reactions, demonstrating the platform’s potential for catalytic enantioselective synthesis. The proposed project will build on these promising preliminary findings to establish chalcogenonium borates as a versatile and powerful catalytic platform. We will explore their scope across diverse organic transformations, optimize their design, and advance them into indispensable tools for synthetic chemistry. The successful implementation of this catalytic strategy will establish a sustainable and efficient methodology for complex molecule synthesis, offering significant benefits for the pharmaceutical and materials science sectors. 本擬議項目旨在開發一類新的高效催化系統，該方案採用硫族元素硼酸鹽催化劑作為硫族鍵供體，用於各種化學轉化反應。 基於軟硫族元素（例如S、Se、Te）的硫族鍵供體作為路易斯酸型有機催化劑，因其在有機合成中提供了一種無金屬替代方案而備受關注。其中，陽離子硫族鎓鹽作為一類特別高效的催化劑，展現出比其對應的中性化合物更優異的催化性能。這種增強的活性源自於其更強的電子受體特性。然而，硫族鎓催化劑的發展受到限制。其中一個挑戰是需要使用非配位陰離子來減少路易斯酸性位點的失活，這需要繁瑣的合成路線，涉及化學計量比的銀鹽，從而限制了結構的多樣性。此外，一些硫族鎓鹽催化劑的反應活性仍有限，底物適用範圍較窄，其在不對稱催化中的應用潛力尚未充分開發。 我們的研究團隊已開發出多種基於軟硫族元素催化劑的催化系統 (e.g., Y.Y.Yeung et al. Nature Catal. 2020, 3, 993; JACS 2021, 143, 12745; ACIE 2022, e202208009; Chem 2023, 9, 1255; ACS Catal. 2024, 14, 9198; ACIE 2025, e202711770)。這些催化系統已被應用於藥物分子重要結構單元和中間體的合成。在此基礎上，我們假設，透過策略性的重新設計，可以克服硫族元素催化中存在的限制。我們設想，由硫族元素和硼路易斯酸形成的硫族元素硼酸鹽能夠有效隔離陰離子，從而在不使陽離子催化位點失活的情況下增強硫族鍵，同時還能提供多種結構調控的機會。我們預期，新設計的硫族元素硼酸鹽催化劑將釋放更強的反應活性和選擇性，從而改善目前效率低下或難以實現的轉化。 我們初步的研究結果證實了這個假設。我們發現，易於取得的硫屬元素硼酸鹽可作為高效催化劑，應用於多種有價值的轉化反應。此外，我們製備了一種手性硫屬元素硼酸鹽催化劑，該催化劑能夠促進不對稱反應，證明了該平台在催化對映選擇性合成方面的潛力。 本計畫將基於這些令人鼓舞的初步研究成果，將硫屬元素硼酸鹽確立為一種用途廣泛且高效的催化平台。我們將探索其在多種有機轉化反應中的應用範圍，優化其設計，並將其發展成為合成化學中的工具。此催化策略的成功實施將為複雜分子的合成建立一種可持續且高效的方法，為製藥和材料科學領域帶來顯著的益處。

14304026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14304026.value: 時序與跨時序聚合：處理時間序列變點檢測中異質性的方法

14304026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304026.value: How to detect a change? Detecting a change point (CP) intuitively involves identifying a moment when the data before and after it exhibit different structures. However, it is unreliable in the presence of data heterogeneity. In this project, we study two types of heterogeneity: changing dependence structures over time and varying change times across components. We frame them as local stationarity and high dimensionality problems. Instead of modeling the varying structures, we propose an alternative principle called "pooling". Pooling offers advantages of simplicity, being model-free, and potentially achieving efficiency comparable to traditional modeling approaches. We introduce two types of pooling: (I) temporal pooling, and (II) cross-temporal pooling. Stage 1: principle for type-I pooling. We develop a sparse subsampling scheme to eliminate the local dependence structure of the time series without directly modeling it. Performing sparse subsampling at different starting points, we create multiple datasets. It yields a series of p-values via applying a CP test on each subsample. We conjecture that these p-values form an approximately stationary time series. It allows us to pool them by treating them as a stationary series and testing for the mean. We call this method stationary pooling. Stage 2: theory and methods for type-I pooling. While sparse subsampling may lead to information loss, we conjecture that stationary pooling efficiently aggregates information across all possible sparse subsamples. A high-level condition is developed for stationary pooling. We demonstrate that this condition is mild by verifying that many existing tests satisfy it. This concept is generalized to CP set estimation and general parameter CP test. Stage 3: principle for type-II pooling. We generalize the standard change point problem to a change interval problem. Traditional methods aggregate change magnitude statistics across components after modeling their long-run variances by estimation or self-normalization. Instead of pooling these change statistics, we propose pooling the estimated individual change times through their empirical distribution. This approach avoids modeling. Thus, it provides a simple and stable way for high-dimensional tests. It is also a natural way to address change interval problems. Stage 4: theory and methods for type-II pooling. The first step involves developing assumptions about dependence across components. We consider an M-dependent framework for high-dimensional components, where M is divergent. The second step develops a functional central limit theorem for the cumulative sum process of the estimated CP times. We address this using graph theory and physical dependence measures. 變點應如何檢測？ 直觀而言，變點檢測旨在識別數據於特定時間點前後，呈現出不同結構的關鍵時刻。然而，當數據存在異質性時，這種傳統的直觀方法往往缺乏可靠性。在本研究中，我們探討兩種類型的異質性：隨時間變化的依賴結構，以及不同分量間變點時間的差異。我們將這兩者分別框架為「局部平穩性」與「高維度」問題。為了解決上述問題，我們並未直接對這些變動的結構進行建模，而是提出一種名為「聚合」的替代原則。聚合方法具備簡單且無須依賴模型的優勢，其潛在的統計效率更可媲美傳統的建模方法。本研究具體引入兩類聚合機制：（甲）時序聚合，以及（乙）跨時序聚合。 第一階段：第一類聚合的原理。我們發展了一套稀疏子抽樣機制，無須直接建模即可消除時間序列中的局部依賴結構。透過在不同起始點執行稀疏子抽樣，我們建構出多個資料子集。對每個子樣本進行變點檢定後，將生成一系列的 p 值。我們推想這些 p 值構成了一個近似平穩的時間序列；基於此，我們能將其視為平穩序列並進行均值檢定，從而實現聚合。我們將此方法命名為「平穩聚合」。 第二階段：第一類聚合的理論與方法。儘管稀疏子抽樣可能伴隨資訊耗損，但我們推證平穩聚合能有效整合所有可能之稀疏子樣本的資訊。我們為平穩聚合建立了一項高階理論條件，並透過驗證眾多現有檢定法均符合此條件，證明了該條件相當寬鬆且易於滿足。此概念亦可進一步推廣至變點集合估計及一般參數的變點檢定。 第三階段：第二類聚合的原理。我們將標準的變點問題推廣為「變點區間」問題。傳統方法通常先透過估計或自正規化來對各分量的長期變異數進行建模，隨後再聚合這些分量的變化幅度統計量。不同於直接聚合這些變化統計量，我們提出透過經驗分布來聚合所估計出的個別變點時間。此方法免除了建模的需要，為高維度檢定提供了一條簡明且穩定的途徑，同時也是處理變點區間問題的自然解法。 第四階段：第二類聚合的理論與方法。第一步涉及建立跨分量依賴性的相關假設。針對高維度分量，我們考慮了一個 M-依賴架構，其中 M 允許是發散的。第二步，我們針對估計變點時間的「累積和過程」建立了泛函中心極限定理。在此過程中，我們運用了圖論與物理依賴性度量來克服相關的理論挑戰。

14304626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14304626.value: 謝爾賓斯基地毯類分形上迪氏型的存在性和唯一性

14304626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304626.value: Analysis on fractals is a mathematical field that emerged from the study of disordered media in mathematical physics. It provides both analytical and probabilistic methods to study the electrical resistance properties of such materials, and has wide applications in stochastic models like percolation clusters and random trees. The field began with the construction of Brownian motion on the Sierpinski gasket and generalized Sierpinski carpets. Since then, a central theme has been the existence and uniqueness of well-behaved diffusion processes, or equivalently Dirichlet forms. Substantial progress has been made on finitely ramified fractals, such as the Sierpinski gasket, which can be disconnected by removing a finite number of points. In contrast, infinitely ramified fractals remain far less understood. Beyond generalized Sierpinski carpets, the only significant advances so far are the recent works by Hua and the PI on unconstrained Sierpinski carpets, and by Kigami on polygon-based self-similar sets. In this project, we plan to further investigate the construction of Dirichlet forms on infinitely ramified fractals, focusing on Sierpinski carpet like fractals. We will also study their uniqueness and apply the results to the homogenization problem on generalized Sierpinski carpets, with the goal of characterizing scaling limits of various processes on their approximating domains. 分形分析是數學物理中為研究無序介質而發展出的一個數學分支。該領域提供分析與機率方法，用以探討此類材料的電阻特性，並在滲透簇、隨機樹等隨機模型中具有廣泛應用。 這一領域的起點，是在謝爾賓斯基墊片及廣義謝爾賓斯基地毯上建構布朗運動。此後，一個核心問題便是良好行為擴散過程的存在性與唯一性，等價地說，即狄利克雷形式的存在性與唯一性。 在有限分叉分形方面，例如謝爾賓斯基墊片，學界已取得相當進展。此類分形只需移除有限個點即可使其不連通。相比之下，無限分叉分形至今仍遠未獲得充分理解。除廣義謝爾賓斯基地毯外，目前僅有的重要進展，包括邱華與本研究計畫主持人近期關於無約束謝爾賓斯基地毯的工作，以及Kigami關於基於多邊形之自相似集的研究。 本計畫擬進一步研究無限分叉分形上狄利克雷形式的建構，重點關注類謝爾賓斯基地毯的分形。同時，我們也將探討其唯一性，並將研究成果應用於廣義謝爾賓斯基地毯的均質化問題，最終目標是刻畫各類過程在其逼近域上的尺度極限。

14304926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304926.value: Chiral organoboron compounds have attracted significant attention due to their diverse applications in catalysis, biomedicine, and material science. To date, most reported chiral organoboron compounds feature chirality-at-skeleton, whereas those with stereogenic boron centers remain scarce due to longstanding challenges in their synthesis. Nevertheless, the limited examples reported so far have already demonstrated promising applications as circular dichroism probes, chiral BODIPY dyes, and chiral catalysts. It is anticipated that the development of efficient preparative methods will greatly advance boron-stereogenic compounds, unlocking new possibilities across various fields. Early approaches to synthesizing boron-stereogenic compounds mainly relied on resolution techniques, such as HPLC or the use of chiral auxiliaries. More recently, transition-metal-catalyzed enantioselective desymmetrization of prochiral organoboron compounds has emerged as a significant advancement. However, these reports remain scattered, and most methods are substrate-specific, with the synthesis of particular substrate classes relying on specific synthetic protocols. Consequently, the development of a more universal and efficient method for synthesizing diverse enantioenriched boron-stereogenic compounds remains an unmet yet critical need. To address this challenge, we propose the development of a versatile chiral boron reagent that can deliver a stereogenic boron center to a wide range of organic substrates. Building on our ongoing efforts in boron-reagent design, we have recently developed an sp2-sp3 diboron reagent, (NHC)BH2‒Bpin, and demonstrated its versatility in the borylation of various organic molecules, including alkynes, allenes, aldehydes, and alkyl/aryl halides. This progress now motivates us to pursue the synthesis of the related sp2-sp3 diboron reagent, (NHC)B(R)H–Bpin, where the four-coordinate (sp³) boron center is stereogenic. In this project, we aim to develop a new catalytic asymmetric synthesis method for the preparation of the first enantioenriched boron-stereogenic diboron reagent (BSDB) and to demonstrate its utility as a versatile chiral boron synthon for the enantiospecific transfer of boron-stereocenters to diverse organic substrates, enabling the synthesis of a broad range of enantioenriched boron-stereogenic compounds. The anticipated outcomes of this project include the successful synthesis of BSDB and the establishment of a general and efficient route to structurally diverse boron-stereogenic compounds. This work will also provide insights into the mechanisms of enantioselective control during both the synthesis and transformation of BSDB. These results are expected to open new possibilities for the application of boron-stereogenic compounds in material science and biomedicine, potentially expanding the frontiers of boron chemistry and organic synthesis. 手性有機硼化合物由於在催化、生物醫藥及材料科學領域的廣泛應用，已受到顯著關注。迄今為止，大多數已報導的手性有機硼化合物僅具有骨架手性（chirality-at-skeleton），而具有硼中心手性（stereogenic boron centers）的化合物，因合成上長期存在的挑戰，仍然相當稀少。然而，目前已報導的有限示例已展現其作為圓二色性探針、手性 BODIPY 染料及手性催化劑的極大應用潛力。可以預期，高效製備方法的開發將大幅推進硼中心手性化合物的發展，從而在各領域中解鎖新的可能性。 早期合成硼中心手性化合物的方法主要依賴於拆分技術，例如高效液相層析（HPLC）或使用手性輔基。近年來，過渡金屬催化的前手性有機硼化合物的對映選擇性去對稱化（enantioselective desymmetrization）已成為一項重大進展。然而，這些報導仍然較為零星，且大多數方法都具有底物特異性，特定底物類別的合成往往依賴於特定的合成方案。因此，開發一種更通用且高效的方法來合成多樣化的對映體富集硼立體中心化合物，仍然是一個尚未滿足但至關重要的需求。 為了應對這一挑戰，我們提出開發一種多功能的手性硼試劑，該試劑可以將硼立體中心傳遞到廣泛的有機底物中。基於我們在硼試劑設計方面持續付出的努力，我們最近開發了一種 sp²-sp³ 型雙硼試劑 (NHC)BH₂‒Bpin，並證實了其在多種有機分子（包括炔烴、丙二烯、醛以及烷基/芳基鹵化物）硼化反應中的多功能性。此進展現在激勵我們進一步追求相關sp²-sp³ 型雙硼試劑 (NHC)B(R)H–Bpin 的合成，其中四配位（sp³）硼中心具有手性（即為硼中心手性）。 在本项目中，我們旨在開發一種新的催化不對稱合成方法，用於製備首個對映體富集的硼中心手性雙硼試劑（BSDB），並證實其作為多功能手性硼合成子（synthon）的實用性，以實現硼立體中心向多種有機底物的專一對映選擇性轉移（enantiospecific transfer），從而合成廣泛的對映體富集硼中心手性化合物。 本項目的預期成果包括成功合成 BSDB，並建立一條通往結構多樣化硼立體中心化合物的通用且高效的路徑。這項工作還將深入揭示在 BSDB 的合成和轉化過程中，對映選擇性控制的機理。這些結果預計將為硼立體中心化合物在材料科學和生物醫藥中的應用開闢新的可能性，並有望拓展硼化學和有機合成的前沿。

14305426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14305426.value: 透過分子模擬與連續介質模型闡明凝聚體穿膜機制

14305426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305426.value: The therapeutic efficacy of biomolecules, such as mRNAs, peptides, and proteins, is critically dependent on their efficient delivery into the cell's interior. A major bottleneck is the inability of these large, often charged, molecules to cross the lipid membrane, compounded by their tendency to become trapped in endosomes. Coacervates are the macromolecule-enriched dense phase formed via liquid-liquid phase separation. Many coacervates are stimuli-responsive and effectively recruit peptides, proteins and nucleic acids, making them ideal candidates for intracellular delivery. Since they typically enter living cells through endocytosis, a major challenge faced by coacervate-based delivery vehicles is to escape from the endosomes in order to release their cargoes into the cytosol. Recent studies have demonstrated the remarkable capacity of certain coacervates to penetrate lipid membranes, allowing them to either directly cross the plasma membrane or readily escape from the endosomes. However, molecular details and the energetic landscape of such penetration are largely missing. In the proposed work, we plan to combine all-atom (AA) and coarse-grained (CG) simulations with continuum modeling, in order to thoroughly elucidate the molecular mechanism of coacervate membrane penetration. The CG simulations, parameterized by AA references and calibrated against our collaborator’s experimental data, will directly model sub-micron coacervate-membrane interactions. The AA simulations and free-energy calculations will yield missing thermodynamic and mechanical parameters for a continuum model, which will quantitatively predict the behavior of physiologically relevant, micron-sized coacervates. Aided by experimental input and validation, our calculations will resolve the fundamental biophysical question of how micron-sized coacervates traverse a lipid bilayer, paving the way for a complete understanding of their cellular entry pathways. By deciphering the molecular grammar of coacervate membrane penetration, the proposed research will also lay the foundation for a rational design strategy of intracellular delivery platforms, producing quantitative design principles for engineering coacervates with optimized delivery efficiency. 生物分子（如mRNA、肽和蛋白質）的治療功效取決於它們能否有效遞送至細胞內部。這一過程的瓶頸在於，這些通常帶有電荷的大型分子難以穿越脂質膜且容易被困在內涵體（endosomes）中。凝聚體（coacervates）是經由液-液相分離所形成的富含巨分子的密集相。許多凝聚體具有刺激響應性，且能有效招募肽、蛋白質與核酸，使其成為細胞內遞送的理想候選載體。由於凝聚體通常透過胞吞作用進入活細胞，因此以凝聚體為基礎的遞送載體所面臨的一項重大挑戰，便是如何逃離內涵體，以將其攜帶的貨物釋放到胞質溶膠中。近期研究顯示，某些凝聚體具有穿透脂質膜的能力，使它們能夠直接穿越細胞質膜，或輕易地從內涵體中逃脫。然而，此類穿透過程的分子細節與能量景觀仍很不明確。在本研究中，我們擬結合全原子（AA）與粗粒化（CG）模擬，以及連續體模型，以徹底闡明凝聚體穿膜的分子機制。以全原子模擬為參數化依據，並根據合作者的實驗數據進行校準的粗粒化模擬，將直接用於模擬亞微米尺度凝聚體與膜之間的作用。全原子模擬與自由能計算則將提供連續體模型所欠缺的熱力學與力學參數，輔助後者定量預測具生理相關性的微米級凝聚體行為。在實驗數據的輸入與驗證輔助下，我們的計算將解決「微米級凝聚體如何穿越脂質雙層膜」這一基礎生物物理問題，為完整理解其細胞進入途徑鋪平道路。透過解譯凝聚體穿膜的分子語法，本研究也將為細胞內遞送平台的合理設計策略奠定基礎，建立用於改造凝聚體以達到最佳遞送效率的定量設計原則。

14305826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14305826.value: 格陵蘭冰蓋積水冰裂隙的季節與年際演化

14305826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305826.value: The Greenland Ice Sheet is the largest single cryospheric contributor to global sea-level rise. Its mass loss and motion are strongly influenced by complex surface hydrological processes. Among these, ponded crevasses—deep surface fractures filled with meltwater—play a critical yet understudied role. They can drain rapidly, routing meltwater to the bed and altering ice dynamics; alternatively, they can retain meltwater that refreezes, temporarily preventing meltwater from reaching the ocean. Their low albedo also enhances surface melt. Despite their importance, current knowledge of Greenland ponded crevasses is limited to a few glaciers and short observational periods, leaving their spatial extent, occurrence frequency, evolution across seasonal and inter-annual time scales largely unknown. This gap hinders our understanding of their key hydrological processes, spatial-temporal variability, climatological and glaciological drivers. This project will address these knowledge gaps through a systematic, ice-sheet-scale survey of ponded crevasses using Sentinel-2 imagery at 10-m spatial resolution and sub-weekly intervals. Our objectives are: (1) to develop an automated, robust, and transferable method for mapping ponded crevasses from Sentinel-2 imagery across diverse climatological and glaciological settings on the Greenland Ice Sheet; (2) to generate a pan-Greenland, fine-resolution, high-frequency time-series dataset of ponded crevasse hydrology (2016–2028) to capture their seasonal and inter-annual evolution; (3) to quantify the influence of surface meltwater runoff, ice stress regime, and subglacial drainage efficiency on the inter-annual variability of ponded crevasse hydrology using statistical modeling. Our method integrates deep learning for crevasse field detection with spectral water indices for ponded crevasses mapping. The resulting dataset will be the first of this kind to quantify ponded crevasses’ key hydrological properties, including peak area, late-summer persistence, expansion/shrinking duration and rates in each melt season, and spatial-temporal variations across 13 years. We will then apply generalized additive models to quantify the nonlinear relationships between the year-to-year changes of ponded crevasse hydrology and key climatological and glaciological drivers, including meltwater runoff output from the polar regional climate model RACMO, ice stress regimes calculated from ice velocity products, and subglacial drainage efficiency inferred from shrinking rates. The developed code and datasets will be openly accessible, promoting transparency, reproducibility, and broad community use. Together, these advances will deliver the first decade-long, ice-sheet-wide record of ponded crevasse hydrology, significantly improving observational capabilities. This project will deepen our understanding of ponded crevasse hydrology and provide critical data for improving ice-sheet hydrology models and sea-level rise projections. 格陵蘭冰蓋是冰凍圈對全球海平面上升貢獻最大的單一要素，其質量損失與運動受控於複雜的表面水文過程。其中，積水冰裂隙, 即被融水填充的冰面深裂縫，扮演關鍵角色。其可迅速排水，從而將融水輸送至冰底並影響冰蓋運動速度；亦可滯留融水並再凍結，從而暫時阻止融水流入海洋。其較低的反照率亦會加強冰蓋表面消融。 儘管其重要性顯著，目前對格陵蘭積水冰裂隙的認識僅限於對少數冰川的短期觀測，而對其空間分布、出現頻率、季節與年際演化缺乏認知。這限制了我們對其關鍵水文過程、時空變異、氣候與冰川驅動因素的理解。 本研究將使用Sentinel-2衛星影像，進行全冰蓋尺度的系統性調查，以填補上述研究空白。具體的研究目標為： (1) 發展一套自動化、穩健、可遷移的積水冰裂隙製圖方法，以適用於格陵蘭冰蓋多樣的氣候與冰川條件； (2) 生產全格陵蘭、高空間分辨率、高觀測頻率的積水冰裂隙水文特徵時間序列數據集（2016–2028），以完整刻畫其季節與年際演化； (3) 利用統計模型量化冰面融水逕流、冰體應力狀態、冰下排水效率對積水冰裂隙水文年際變化的影響。 本方法所得數據集將量化積水冰裂隙關鍵水文特徵：包括峰值面積、夏末存留量、擴張與收縮期時長與速率，以及十餘年的時空變化。我們將應用廣義加性模型，量化積水冰裂隙水文特徵的年際變化與關鍵氣候及冰川因子之間的非線性關係，這些因子包括氣候模式RACMO模擬的融水逕流、由冰流速計算的冰體應力狀態、由積水冰裂隙收縮速率推算的冰下排水效率等。 本研究將生產首套超過十年、涵蓋整個冰蓋的積水冰裂隙水文數據集，顯著提升觀測能力。本項目將深化我們對積水冰裂隙水文的理解，並為改進冰蓋水文模型與海平面上升預測提供關鍵資料。

14305926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14305926.value: 鎳基超導：從探測相互作用到材料設計

14305926.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14305926.value: Prof Si, Liang Prof Zhao, Jun Prof Zhu, Zhihai

14305926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305926.value: The recent discovery of superconductivity in nickelates with critical temperature (Tc) surpassing the nitrogen boiling point, has inspired renewed enthusiasm to address the longstanding problem of high-Tc superconductivity. These nickelate materials exhibit distinct electronic and magnetic properties from cuprate superconductors, suggesting an alternative pathway to high-Tc superconductivity. However, bulk nickelate crystals require high pressures (above 14 GPa) to exhibit superconductivity, posing significant challenges for experimental studies. Key properties, including the intrinsic electronic and magnetic structures, the superconducting gap symmetry, and the defining parameters of superconductivity, remain elusive. The latest realization of superconductivity in nickelate thin films at ambient pressure offers promising opportunities to address these outstanding questions. Yet, the film’s sensitive and complex surface conditions complicate conventional surface-sensitive measurements. To overcome these limitations, we propose to employ resonant X-ray scattering, a bulk-sensitive technique, to probe the electronic, magnetic, and superconducting gap structures of nickelates. These measurements will be complemented by neutron and X-ray scattering studies on bulk crystals for a comprehensive comparison. By systematically exploring the phase diagram, our goal is to identify the key interactions that drive nickelate superconductivity. These insights will guide us to further explore tuning and synthesis of new nickel-based materials, with the goal to achieve even higher superconducting transition temperatures. This project promises to deliver timely and crucial experimental insights into the mechanism of nickelate superconductivity. In addition, it will provide a training platform for young researchers in material synthesis, advanced scattering techniques, and the physics of correlated electron systems. 近期在鎳基超導體中發現了臨界溫度超過液氮沸點的超導電性，這一突破促使我們重新審視高溫超導這一長期未解之謎。與銅基超導體不同，鎳基超導體具有Ruddlesden–Popper（RP）結構，並呈現出不同的電子和磁學性質，表明其可能為實現高溫超導提供一條新的途徑。然而，塊體鎳基材料通常需要在10 GPa以上的高壓條件下才能表現出超導電性，給實驗研究帶來了巨大挑戰。目前，人們對鎳基材料的許多基本性質仍缺乏深入認識，尤其是其電子和磁性基態的本質，以及導致超導電性產生的關鍵相互作用，至今尚不清楚。本項目將重點研究最新發現的、可在常壓下實現超導的鎳基薄膜，以解決上述關鍵科學問題。我們將綜合運用多種X射線散射和譜學技術，系統研究這些材料中的電子和磁性不穩定性；同時，通過非彈性散射測量表徵其元激發，進而揭示材料中的基本相互作用及其在超導電性形成過程中可能發揮的作用。通過對不同鎳基材料體系及不同摻雜區間開展系統研究，本項目旨在闡明驅動鎳基超導的關鍵相互作用。我們將圍繞鎳基超導這一核心問題，開展新材料合成、物性表徵以及元激發譜學測量，從材料製備、實驗表徵和微觀機制等多個層面進行探索，力求揭示鎳基超導的微觀起源。與此同時，本項目還將為青年科研人員提供培養平台，使其在晶體生長、散射實驗、數據分析和學術交流等方面得到系統訓練。依託我們在散射實驗領域的專業積累以及在非常規超導研究方面的豐富經驗，本項目有望為揭示鎳基高溫超導機制提供及時而關鍵的實驗依據。

14306326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14306326.value: 最佳次抽樣之區間設限多狀態資料半參數分析

14306326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306326.value: Interval-censored multi-state data are prevalent in biostatistical and financial applications, such as credit risk modelling, where subjects transition between discrete states over time. While classical approaches often assume time-homogeneous Markov processes, recent semiparametric models have addressed progressive-only transitions or have not incorporated subject-specific covariates. A significant gap remains concerning the identifiability of covariate effects in settings where transitions are bidirectional and potentially non-Markovian. This research addresses this gap by proposing a unified framework for semiparametric intensity models on interval-censored data. Our model extends existing methods by accommodating non-progressive, non-Markovian processes and incorporating covariate effects. Furthermore, we tackle the formidable computational challenges posed by modern large-scale datasets. Motivated by a comprehensive corporate credit rating database spanning over 20 years and 10,000 entities, we integrate a subsampling approach into our framework. This strategy significantly reduces the computational burden while maintaining statistical efficiency. Notably, our construction establishes a general framework for subsampling within the EM algorithm, offering significant potential across a wide range of applications. The proposed methodology is expected to provide a more robust and computationally feasible tool for analysing complex, real-world multi-state data, with preliminary simulations validating its effectiveness. 區間設限多狀態資料（interval-censored multi-state data）廣泛存在於生物統計與金融應用領域（例如信用風險建模），其中個體會隨時間在不同離散狀態之間轉移。傳統方法多假設其遵循時間同質（time-homogeneous）的馬可夫過程，而近期的半參數模型則主要聚焦於單向漸進轉移（progressive-only transitions），或未納入個體特定之協變量（subject-specific covariates）。在轉移具備雙向性且可能為非馬可夫過程的情境下，協變量效應的可識別性（identifiability）仍存在顯著的研究缺口。為解決此問題，本研究針對區間設限資料提出了一個半參數強度模型之統整架構；該模型透過納入非漸進性、非馬可夫過程以及協變量效應，有效拓展了現有方法。 此外，本研究進一步解決了現代大規模資料集所帶來的龐大運算挑戰。奠基於一項涵蓋逾 20 年、涉及 10,000 多家企業的完整公司信用評等資料庫，我們在架構中導入了次抽樣（subsampling）方法。此策略在保有統計效率的同時，大幅降低了運算負擔。值得注意的是，本研究建構之方法為 EM 演算法架構下的次抽樣建立了通用的理論框架，在多元應用領域具備高度潛力。所提出之方法論預期能為分析複雜的真實世界多狀態資料提供更穩健且具運算可行性的工具，且初步的模擬研究已驗證其有效性。

14306426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14306426.value: 基於成像的空間轉錄組數據中轉錄本洩漏的統計建模

14306426.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14306426.value: Prof Chan, Ting-Fung Prof TSE, Gary Man-Kit

14306426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306426.value: This project will aim to develop statistical methods to model transcript leakage in imaging-based spatial transcriptomic data. By simultaneously measuring the transcriptome and spatial location of individual cells, spatial transcriptomics offers unprecedented opportunities to investigate the tissue organization, cell-cell interactions and the tumor microenvironment. Compared with spot-based spatial transcriptomic technologies, which typically assay multiple cells within a single spot and hence yield bulk-level data, imaging-based spatial transcriptomic platforms, such as the MERSCOPE platform that provides Multiplexed Error-Robust Fluorescence in situ Hybridization (MERFISH), CosMx Spatial Molecular Imager (SMI) and the Xenium In Situ platform, achieve cellular resolution and exhibit higher sensitivity in detecting gene expression. However, recent benchmarking studies of imaging-based spatial transcriptomic platforms have reported that some genes appear to be expressed in cell types where such expression is not expected, even after the application of state-of-the-art data processing and filtering methods. Our pilot study suggests that this phenomenon is likely attributable to transcript leakage. Unfortunately, despite active research on the deconvolution of spot-level spatial transcriptomic data, statistical methods for decontaminating imaging-based spatial transcriptomic data affected by transcript leakage are lacking. However, if the transcript leakage problem is not properly adjusted, it can lead to serious consequences for (a) the quantification of expression levels, (b) annotation of cell types, (c) detection of genes differentially expressed between cell types and (d) calling of spatially variable genes. In this proposed project, we will develop a Bayesian hierarchical model to adjust gene expression contamination resulting from transcript leakage from neighboring cells. Our model will allow the level of transcript leakage to vary across genes. We will prove the model identifiability, and our theoretical results will show that contamination due to transcript leakage can be distinguished from the true underlying gene expression. We will develop an efficient parallel Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm for statistical inference and provide it as free software packages. We will apply our proposed methods to systematically assess the magnitude of transcript leakage across various imaging-based spatial transcriptomic platforms and tissue types. Application to spatial transcriptomic data collected from breast cancer patients will address health problems related to Hong Kong. This project will greatly facilitate the analysis of spatial transcriptomic data and reduce the risk of data misinterpretation. By solving a cutting-edge scientific problem in genomics, this project will make profound contributions to statistical modeling, statistical computing, parallel programming and the development of personalized medicine. 本計畫旨在開發統計方法以校正基於成像的空間轉錄組數據中的轉錄本洩漏問題。 透過同時測量單一細胞的轉錄組和空間位置，空間轉錄組學為研究組織結構、細胞間相互作用和腫瘤微環境提供了前所未有的機會。基於成像的空間轉錄組學平台能夠實現細胞尺度的分辨率並在檢測基因表達方面表現出高靈敏度。然而，近期對基於成像的空間轉錄組學平台的數據分析表明即使應用了最先進的數據處理和過濾方法，某些基因似乎仍在預期不會表達的細胞類型中表達。我們的初步研究表明這種現象很可能是由轉錄本洩漏造成的。 遺憾的是針對受轉錄本洩漏影響的基於成像的空間轉錄組數據進行去污染的統計方法仍然匱乏。如果轉錄本洩漏問題無法妥善處理，可能會對以下游分析如 (a) 基因表達量的量化、(b) 細胞類型的註釋、(c) 不同細胞類型間差異表達基因的檢測以及 (d) 空間變異基因的識別造成嚴重影響。 在本計畫中，我們將開發一個貝葉斯分層模型用於校正鄰近細胞轉錄本洩漏造成的基因表達污染。我們的模型允許不同基因的轉錄本洩漏程度不同。我們將證明該模型的可識別性，並且我們的理論結果表明轉錄本洩漏造成的污染可以與真實的基因表達區分開來。我們將開發一種高效的並行馬可夫鏈蒙特卡羅算法用於統計推斷，並將其作為免費軟體包提供。我們將應用我們提出的方法，系統地評估各種基於成像的空間轉錄組平台和組織類型中轉錄本洩漏的程度。 本計畫將大大促進空間轉錄組學數据的分析，並降低数据誤讀的風險。透過解決基因組學領域的前沿科學難題，本計畫將為統計建模、統計計算、並行計算以及個人化醫療的發展做出深遠貢獻。

14306626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14306626.value: 鈣鈦礦光伏自組裝單分子層（SAMs）衰減機制與應對策略研究

14306626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306626.value: Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) have recently become the most popular interfacial layers in perovskite solar cells (PSCs), facilitating favorable energy-level alignment, efficient charge extraction, and improved efficiency for inverted (p-i-n) devices. However, recent studies have revealed that SAMs are not intrinsically stable. In solution, SAM precursors degrade upon storage. In the thin-film state, SAM layers are also prone to morphological and chemical degradation, leading to electronic inhomogeneity, inefficient charge transport, and accelerated perovskite degradation. Despite their widespread use, the degradation mechanisms of SAM at the solution, film, and device levels remain elusive, severely hindering device reproducibility and lifetime, and ultimately the mass production of PSCs. This proposal aims to obtain a comprehensive understanding of SAM degradation mechanisms and to develop effective stabilization strategies for their integration into PSCs. We will pursue three synergistic tasks. In Task 1, we will identify intrinsic molecular features and external environmental factors responsible for SAM solution degradation by systematically varying SAM anchoring groups, linkers, and functional groups, and probing degradation products and aggregation behaviors. In Task 2, we will investigate the degradation of SAM thin films under thermal, light, and ambient stresses, correlating structural and chemical changes with interfacial electronic properties. In Task 3, we will establish the link between SAM degradation and perovskite crystallization, device performance, and operational stability, guiding the fabrication of highly efficient and stable single-junction and tandem devices. Our methodology combines advanced in-situ and in-operando scattering techniques (GIWAXS/SAXS), spectroscopy (NMR, HRMS, EPR, XPS/UPS, NEXAFS), and microscopy (AFM, c-AFM, KPFM) to reveal degradation pathways at multiple scales, complemented by device-level testing under realistic operating conditions. The successful implementation of this project will establish design principles for robust SAM molecules, solvent/additive strategies for solution preservation, and processing protocols that improve both bulk and interfacial film qualities. These advances will not only enhance the reproducibility and operational lifetime of PSCs but will also extend to other thin-film optoelectronic devices. 自組裝單分子層（SAMs）近年來已成為反式（p-i-n）鈣鈦礦太陽能電池中最受歡迎的界面層，能顯著優化能級對齊、促進高效電荷提取並提升器件效率。然而，近期研究表明 SAMs 並非本徵穩定。在溶液中，SAM 前驅體在儲存過程中易發生降解；在薄膜狀態下，SAM 層亦易發生形貌和化學降解，導致界面電學性質不均勻、電荷傳輸效率低下以及加速鈣鈦礦的退化。儘管 SAMs 被廣泛應用，但其在溶液、薄膜和器件層面的退化機制仍不清晰，嚴重限制了器件的可重複性、工作壽命以及最終的工業化生產。 本項目旨在深入且全面地理解 SAMs 的衰減機制，並開發有效的穩定化策略以推動其在鈣鈦礦太陽能電池中的應用。我們將圍繞三個協同任務展開研究：任務一，通過系統改變 SAMs 的錨定基團、連接基團和官能基團，探究其降解產物與聚集行為，從而揭示導致 SAM 溶液降解的分子結構特徵與外部環境因素；任務二，研究 SAM 薄膜在熱、光照及大氣環境等應力作用下的降解行為，建立結構與化學變化與界面電學性質之間的關聯；任務三，建立 SAM 降解與鈣鈦礦結晶、器件性能及運行穩定性之間的聯繫，為製備高效率、高穩定性的單結及疊層器件提供指導。 本項目將結合先進的原位（in-situ）與工況（in-operando）散射技術（GIWAXS/SAXS）、光譜技術（NMR, HRMS, EPR, XPS/UPS, NEXAFS）以及顯微技術（AFM, c-AFM, KPFM），多尺度揭示降解路徑，並配合真實運行條件下的器件級測試。本項目的成功實施將為設計高穩定性 SAM 分子、溶液保存的溶劑/添加劑工程以及優化薄膜質量的加工工藝提供通用準則。這些突破不僅能顯著提升鈣鈦礦太陽能電池的可重複性和運行壽命，亦可推廣至其他薄膜光電器件中。

14306726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14306726.value: 用於深近紅外磷光的異金屬銠-鉑分子的配體工程

14306726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306726.value: Near-infrared (NIR) triplet light-emitting materials are important for next-generation technologies in optoelectronics, bioimaging, and telecommunications. However, developing efficient NIR triplet emitters remains a fundamental challenge due to the "energy gap law" (where longer emission wavelengths reduce emission efficiency) and the difficulty in harnessing spin-forbidden triplet electronic transition for light emission. Our recent developments of heterometallic complexes—the Rh(I)–Pt(II) systems—show promise by combining deep-NIR emission with enhanced phosphorescence efficiency (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2025, 147,19949−19958). However, this design is still limited by relatively weak metal–metal (M–M) orbital overlap and unwanted non-radiative energy loss. This proposal aims to overcome these limitations in hetero-Rh(I)-Pt(II) system through rational ligand design strategy. Our strategy involves employing strong π-acceptor and sulfur-containing ligands to decrease M–M distance and reduce the HOMO-LUMO gap for deep NIR emission, alongside strong σ-donor and deuterated ligands to suppress non-radiative pathways and boost phosphorescence efficiency. The project combines synthesis, photophysical characterization, and computational studies to establish structure-property relationships. Preliminary results confirm the formation of a ³[dσ*→pσ] excited state in a new Rh(I)-Pt(II) double salt complex with emission up to 966 nm. Success in this endeavor will provide a novel design platform for efficient, tunable deep-NIR triplet emitters. In summary, the outcomes of this project will deliver: 1. Ligand design principle for deep NIR triplet emitters based on heterometallic Rh-Pt interactions; 2. A library of high-performance NIR triplet emitters which show potential applications in NIR-OLEDs, biological sensors, and light-based telecommunications. 近紅外（NIR）三線態發光材料對於光電、生物成像和電信通訊等下一代技術至關重要。然而，由於「能隙定律」（即發射波長越長，發射效率越低）以及難以有效利用自旋禁阻的三線態電子躍遷來產生光發射，開發高效率的近紅外三線態發射體仍是一項根本性挑戰。我們近期發展的異金屬配合物——Rh(I)–Pt(II)系統——展現出深近紅外發射與增強磷光效率相結合的潛力（J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2025, 147, 19949–19958）。然而，此設計仍受限於相對較弱的金屬–金屬（M–M）軌道重疊以及不必要的非輻射能量損失。 本提案旨在透過合理的配體設計策略，克服異核Rh(I)-Pt(II)系統中的這些限制。我們的策略包括：採用強π受體和含硫配體，以縮短M–M距離並縮小HOMO-LUMO能隙，從而實現深近紅外發射；同時利用強σ供體和氘代配體，以抑制非輻射途徑並提高磷光效率。本項目結合合成、光物理表徵和理論計算研究，以建立結構-性質關係。初步結果證實，在一種新型Rh(I)-Pt(II)雙鹽配合物中形成了³[dσ*→pσ]激發態，其發射波長可達966 nm。此項研究的成功將為高效率、可調控的深近紅外三線態發射體提供一個新穎的設計平台。 總而言之，本項目的成果將提供： 1. 基於異金屬Rh-Pt相互作用的深近紅外三線態發射體之配體設計原則； 2. 一系列高性能近紅外三線態發射體，這些材料在近紅外有機發光二極體（NIR-OLEDs）、生物感測器和光基電信通訊中展現出潛在應用前景。

14306926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14306926.value: 波茲曼方程的無窮層問題

14306926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306926.value: The infinite layer problem on the Boltzmann equation addresses the motion of rarefied gas flow confined between two parallel infinite planes. This problem presents several complex features in collisional kinetic theory, as it involves not only binary collisions among particles but also interactions with physical boundaries, which influence gas flow within the domain. Unlike classical boundary-value problems in bounded or exterior domains, the infinite layer domain is unbounded with a non-compact boundary, posing significant challenges for the mathematical analysis of global well-posedness in this PDE problem with a non-local nonlinear collision term. The mixed-type spatial domain, which combines unbounded and bounded variables together, results in more intricate behavior of the rarefied gas. As confirmed by studies of the compressible Navier-Stokes equations at the fluid level, the solution to the time-evolutionary problem in a 3D infinite layer behaves as a 2D diffusion wave, exhibiting polynomial decay in the unbounded direction, in contrast with the typical large-time exponential convergence to equilibrium observed in bounded domains. However, there are few results in the mathematical literature regarding the kinetic equation. In this project, we focus on the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation in an infinite layer. The PI, along with collaborators, has developed a solid understanding of large-time stability for the initial-boundary value problem near global Maxwellians. We will further examine inhomogeneous data driven by variable boundary temperatures, moving boundary velocities, self-consistent forces, or additional pressure along the tangent direction of the layer. These considerations are crucial in both physics and mathematics as they characterize non-equilibrium stationary phenomena.
