We aim to develop new analytical techniques specific to the infinite layer domain to gain insights into this fundamental problem on the Boltzmann equation in kinetic theory. 波茲曼方程的無窮層問題，旨在研究侷限於兩片平行無限平面之間的稀薄氣體流動。該問題在碰撞動理學理論中呈現出諸多複雜特徵，因為它不僅涉及粒子間的相互碰撞，還涉及與物理邊界的相互作用，而這些邊界會影響區域內的氣體流動。與經典的有界域或外部域邊值問題不同，無窮層區域是無界的，且邊界非緊緻，這對含有非局部非線性碰撞項的此類偏微分方程問題在全局適定性方面的數學分析構成了重大挑戰。空間區域為混合類型，同時結合了無界變量與有界變量，導致稀薄氣體的行為更為複雜。正如在流體層面上對可壓縮納維-斯托克斯方程的研究所證實的，在三維無窮層中的時間演化問題，其解表現為二維擴散波，並在無界方向上呈現多項式衰減，這與有界域中所觀察到的典型長時間指數收斂至平衡態的行為形成對比。然而，數學文獻中關於此動理學方程的研究結果甚少。在本項目中，我們將聚焦於無窮層中的硬球波茲曼方程。項目主持人及其合作者已針對全局麥克斯韋分佈附近的初邊值問題，建立了穩固的長時間穩定性理解。我們將進一步研究由邊界溫度變化、移動邊界速度、自洽力場、或沿層的切向附加壓力所驅動的非均勻性問題。這些考量在物理與數學上均至關重要，因為它們刻畫了非平衡穩態現象。我們的目標是發展專門針對無窮層區域的新分析技巧，從而深入理解動理學理論中這一關於波茲曼方程的基礎問題。

14307126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14307126.value: 用於複合材料板數值模擬的高效多尺度計算方法

14307126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14307126.value: Composite plates are at the forefront of material design. The typical properties of composite plates include variable thickness, heterogeneous material properties, laminated structure, anisotropy, variable density, thermal/hygroscopic effects, and interfacial properties. These characteristics result in spatial variations in the bending stiffness, thereby increasing the complexity of the mathematical model used to describe the bending behavior of composite plates. From the computational simulation point of view, resolving the aforementioned geometric complexity and material heterogeneity at high resolutions is computationally infeasible. To address this challenge, multiscale model reduction techniques have emerged as a powerful framework, enabling efficient simulation by systematically capturing microscale features while drastically reducing computational costs. Despite significant advancements in multiscale modeling and simulation, existing multiscale methods remain inadequate for addressing challenges in the numerical simulations of composite plates. One reason is that the mathematical model is a fourth order partial differential equation. In addition, for practical application, the boundary condition is nonlinear, and in some cases, some obstacle problems are involved. In this project, our aim is to develop efficient and robust multiscale computational methods for composite plates problems. The proposed multiscale framework is based on the construction of multiscale basis functions for more challenging fourth order partial differential equations with heterogeneous coefficients. The key ingredients are the design of local spectral decomposition, oversampling and energy minimization. The resulting basis functions satisfy exponential decay property and the convergence is robust with respect to the heterogeneity of the material. The proposed methodologies are significantly different from existing techniques due to the higher order nature of the equation. We will also develop stability and convergence results for the composite plates problem with obstacle condition or nonlinear boundary condition. Furthermore, in order to efficiently address different heterogeneity, we will develop adaptive basis enrichment strategies. This is based on a novel error indicator that is robust with respect to the contrast and heterogeneity of the coefficients. The convergence of the proposed adaptive multiscale method will be analyzed. The proposed research provides a new class of multiscale computational methods for applications involving the design of composite plates. The research works contain novel mathematical ideas and computational techniques. We expect that our methodology will provide an accurate and efficient tool for many realistic applications. We also expect that our proposed methods will give significant impacts in both mathematical sciences and application areas where computational modeling composite plates problem plays a vital role. 複合材料板是材料設計領域的前沿課題。複合材料板的典型特性包括厚度變化、材料屬性不均勻、層合結構、各向異性、密度變化、熱/吸濕效應、界面特性。這些特性導致彎曲剛度存在空間變化，從而增加了用於描述複合材料板彎曲行為的數學模型的複雜性。從計算模擬的角度來看，在高解析度下解析上述幾何複雜性和材料不均勻性在計算上是不可行的。為了應對這項挑戰，多尺度模型降階技術應運而生，成為一種強大的框架，它能夠系統地捕捉微觀尺度特徵，從而實現高效的模擬，同時大幅降低計算成本。儘管多尺度建模和模擬取得了顯著進展，但現有的多尺度方法仍然不足以應對複合材料板數值模擬中的挑戰。原因之一是其數學模型是四階偏微分方程。此外，在實際應用中，邊界條件是非線性的，在某些情況下，還會遇到一些障礙問題。 本專案旨在開發高效且穩健的多尺度計算方法，用於解決複合材料板問題。所提出的多尺度框架是基於建立多尺度基底函數，以應對具有異質係數的更具挑戰性的四階偏微分方程。其關鍵要素包括局部光譜分解、過採樣和能量最小化的設計。所得基函數滿足指數衰減特性，且收斂性對材料的異質性具有穩健性。由於方程式的階數較高，所提出的方法與現有技術顯著不同。我們也將針對具有障礙條件或非線性邊界條件的複合材料板問題，推導出其穩定性和收斂性結果。此外，為了有效應對不同的異質性，我們將發展自適應基增強策略。該策略基於一種新型誤差指標，該指標對係數的對比度和異質性具有穩健性。我們將分析所提出的自適應多尺度方法的收斂性。 本研究為複合材料板設計應用提供了一種新的多尺度計算方法。該研究工作包含新穎的數學思想和計算技術。我們預期，我們的方法將為許多實際應用提供準確且有效率的工具。我們也預期，我們提出的方法將在數學科學和計算建模複合材料板問題至關重要的應用領域產生重大影響。

14307226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14307226.value: 由近斷層觀測約束破裂傳播動力學

14307226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14307226.value: Earthquakes remain one of the most destructive natural hazards, yet the physics of rupture propagation—how an earthquake spreads along a fault—remains poorly understood. A major challenge is the lack of high-resolution near-fault data, which are essential for capturing the fine details of rupture dynamics. Traditional seismic networks rely heavily on velocity sensors, which often saturate when placed close to the fault, making near-source recordings rare. Recently, acceleration-sensor-based near-fault data have become available, but only for a limited number of events globally. This scarcity has left a critical gap in our ability to decode rupture behavior and the governing factors, which is essential to improve seismic hazard assessments. This project proposes an innovative framework to systematically decode near-fault data and constrain rupture dynamics in large (M > 7) continental strike-slip earthquakes. By integrating dynamic rupture simulations with waveform analysis—areas where our team has extensive expertise—we will investigate how fault geometry and subsurface structure influence rupture speed, frictional behavior, and near-fault waveform characteristics. Synthetic waveforms will be compared with real observations to extract reliable rupture features. A key innovation is the deployment of a dense seismic array across the Amanos segment of the 2023 Turkey earthquake, which has been done in 2025. This array provides unprecedented resolution of fault zone structure, enabling us to isolate the effects of fault geometry and material properties on rupture propagation. Another breakthrough is our approach to combine near-fault observations, dense-array imaging, and dynamic simulations—an integration rarely achieved due to logistical and technical constraints. We also aim to develop new methods for extracting rupture parameters from limited near-fault datasets, including techniques to estimate rupture speed and frictional strength. These tools will be applicable to other global strike-slip events, creating a transferable framework for future studies. By decoding the physics of rupture from near-fault data, this project will significantly advance earthquake science and contribute to more accurate seismic hazard models. The innovations in data acquisition, simulation, and analysis will not only fill longstanding gaps in earthquake research but also support better societal preparedness in regions prone to large earthquakes. 本項目旨在突破淺源破壞性地震破裂物理研究的瓶頸。近斷層高解析度數據稀缺，傳統速度儀常在近場飽和，限制了對破裂動力學的認識。我們提出整合近斷層波形分析、動態破裂模擬與密集陣成像的新框架，以大陸走滑型地震（M > 7）為研究對象，探討斷層幾何與介質結構對破裂速度、摩擦特性及波形複雜性的影響。依託 2025 年在土耳其阿馬諾斯段布設的密集台陣，我們可綜合解析斷層結構，並發展從近斷層數據中提取破裂速度與摩擦強度的新方法。此框架可推廣至全球走滑型地震，填補長期缺口，提升對震源物理的理解，並為地震危險性評估與防災減災提供更可靠的科學支撐。

14307426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14307426.value: This project addresses a fundamental problem lying at the interface of geometry, differential equations, and mathematical physics. The objects we investigate, spectral networks, are certain graph-like objects consisting of trajectories on a surface, associated to differentials on the surface. They play a central role in the study of four-dimensional N=2 supersymmetric quantum field theories and the asymptotic analysis of linear differential equations, and are expected to form an important part of Donaldson-Thomas and higher Teichmuller theory. Although these objects have been under intense investigation for the past decade and a half, having been initially observed over four decades ago, almost all study has focused on the simplest case of spectral networks arising from quadratic differentials. Despite their importance, results for higher differentials are primarily numerical conjectures, due to the dramatic increase in complexity, since trajectories may now intersect, giving birth to additional trajectories which may intersect and give birth to further trajectories, and so on. The goal of this project is to establish some of the first rigorous results on spectral networks for cubic differentials, including both explicit treatments of concrete examples and general theory, following very recent advances in the field. 本計畫探討一個位於幾何學、微分方程與數學物理交會處的基礎性問題。我們所研究的對象稱為譜網絡（spectral networks）；它們是一類由曲面上的軌跡構成、並與該曲面上的微分相關聯的圖狀結構。譜網絡在四維 N=2 超對稱量子場論的研究，以及線性微分方程的漸近分析中，皆扮演核心角色；此外，它們也被預期將成為 Donaldson–Thomas 理論與高階 Teichmuller 理論的重要組成部分。 儘管這類結構早在四十多年前便已受到注意，並且在過去十五年間成為密集研究的對象，幾乎所有相關研究都集中於最簡單的情形，也就是由二次微分（quadratic differentials）所產生的譜網絡。儘管高次微分所對應的譜網絡十分重要，現有成果卻主要仍停留在數值猜想的層次。其原因在於，問題的複雜度會急遽增加：軌跡此時可能彼此相交，並在交點處生成額外的軌跡；這些新生成的軌跡又可能進一步相交，產生更多軌跡，如此反覆延伸。 本計畫的目標，是承接本領域極近期的進展，建立首批關於三次微分（cubic differentials）之譜網絡的嚴格數學結果；研究內容將同時涵蓋對具體例子的顯式處理與一般理論的建構。

14307526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14307526.value: 實與複 里奇流平滑化的唯一性、穩定性及其在穩態孤立子存在性問題上的應用

14307526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14307526.value: The project aims at studying uniqueness and stability of the Ricci flow which starts from singular initial data weakly. This geometric flow, utilized by Hamilton and Perelman to solve the long-standing Poincare conjecture in topology, has proven to be highly effective in various other problem as well. This proposal revolves around two main themes. The first goal is to investigate the uniqueness and stability of Ricci flow with singular initial data, motivated by the challenge of running the Ricci flow across singularities. Finite-time singularities in Ricci flow are often described using conical singularity models. Angenent-Knopf and Gianniotis-Schulze have suggested that asymptotically conical expanding solitons could help resolve these conical singularities. Building on this, Schulze conjectured the uniqueness of Ricci flow emerging from a cone in the pointed Gromov-Hausdorff sense, under non-negative curvature. Unlike the smooth compact case, finding an appropriate gauge for effectively comparing Ricci flows poses a significant challenge, particularly since the geometry of the Ricci flow is not well-controlled in the classical sense near the initial data. Despite these difficulties, there has been considerable recent progress in understanding uniqueness and stability, notably by the PI in the smooth non-compact case and by Deruelle-Schulze-Simon in the locally Reifenberg case. In this project, the PI proposes to explore uniqueness and stability in a broader context by combining the methods of Cheeger with the new stability estimates developed by the PI and Chan-Lai. Additionally, the PI plans to investigate the Kaehler analogy, which involves less restrictive curvature conditions. The second theme of the project focuses on the existence of gradient steady Kaehler-Ricci solitons. This is motivated by the need to construct more examples to better understand Type II singularities of Ricci flow in general. In a recent collaborative work with Chan-Lai, the PI constructed Riemannian gradient steady Ricci solitons with positive curvature and a general symmetric group, extending Lai’s flying wing construction. In the Kaehler setting, gradient steady Kaehler-Ricci solitons are anticipated to exhibit greater rigidity. The PI proposes to explore the possibility of extending the Riemannian results to the Kaehler case and to construct additional examples of positively curved gradient steady Kaehler-Ricci solitons with general symmetric groups. 本計畫旨在研究從奇異初始資料以弱意義出發之 Ricci 流的唯一性與穩定性。Ricci 流是幾何分析中的重要工具，Hamilton 與 Perelman 曾利用其解決拓撲學中的龐加萊猜想，並已廣泛應用於其他幾何與拓撲問題。 本計畫主要包含兩個研究方向。第一個方向是研究具有奇異初始資料的 Ricci 流之唯一性與穩定性，其動機來自如何使 Ricci 流穿越奇點。Ricci 流的有限時間奇點常可由錐形奇點模型描述。Angenent–Knopf 及 Gianniotis–Schulze 的工作顯示，漸近錐形的擴張 Ricci 孤立子可能有助於消解此類奇點。基於此，Schulze 猜想在非負曲率條件下，從錐形空間以帶基點 Gromov–Hausdorff 意義產生的 Ricci 流應具有唯一性。 此問題的一項主要困難，是在接近奇異初始資料時，Ricci 流的幾何結構缺乏經典意義下的有效控制，因此難以選取適當的規範（gauge）比較不同的 Ricci 流。近年相關研究已有重要進展，包括計畫主持人在光滑非緊緻情形的工作，以及 Deruelle–Schulze–Simon 在局部 Reifenberg 情形的結果。本計畫擬結合 Cheeger 的方法，以及計畫主持人與 Chan–Lai 新近建立的穩定性估計，將唯一性與穩定性理論推廣至更一般的幾何背景。同時亦將研究 Kähler 情形，以期在較弱的曲率條件下得到相應結果。 第二個方向是研究梯度穩態 Kähler–Ricci 孤立子的存在性，其主要動機是構造更多模型，以加深對 Ricci 流 II 型奇點的理解。計畫主持人近期與 Chan–Lai 合作，構造了具有正曲率及一般對稱群作用的黎曼梯度穩態 Ricci 孤立子，推廣了 Lai 的 flying wing 構造。相較於黎曼情形，Kähler 結構通常具有更強的剛性。本計畫將探討能否將上述黎曼結果推廣至 Kähler 情形，並進一步構造具有正曲率及一般對稱群作用的新型梯度穩態 Kähler–Ricci 孤立子。

14307826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14307826.value: 噬菌體引導的脂質體納米載體對感染性肺腫瘤的精準靶向：從分子相互作用到製劑策略

14307826.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14307826.value: Prof CHEN, Sheng Prof To, Kin Wah

14307826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14307826.value: Infection-associated malignancies represent a growing clinical challenge, particularly in lung cancers. Epidemiological studies reported that over half of lung cancer patients develop pulmonary infections, with Klebsiella pneumoniae and Staphylococcus aureus as the predominant gram-negative and gram-positive pathogens, respectively. These bacteria can colonize and persist within the tumor microenvironment (TME), where they interact with cancer cells, evade immune surveillance, and form protective biofilms to hinder antibiotic penetration and compromise therapeutic efficacy. However, whether these tumor-resided pathogenic bacteria can promote tumor growth, modulate immune responses or mediate therapeutic resistance, remains largely unexplored. This knowledge gap provides the impetus for the present study, predicated on our pilot data showing a higher intracellular selectivity of pathogenic bacteria in malignant cells over normal lung epithelial cells. Elucidating such interactions would facilitate the development of more effective treatment strategies to manage infected lung cancers. In this project, we will investigate the biological relevance of our pilot data by performing systematic mechanistic studies to elucidate the molecular interactions between pathogenic bacteria and lung cancer cells. Specifically, we will characterize bacterial invasion, intracellular localization, their impacts on host signaling pathways and immune responses using bacterial recovery assays, transcriptomic profiling, and immunofluorescence imaging. In parallel, we will assess influences of bacterial colonization on anticancer drugs, focusing on drug degradation, uptake, cytotoxicity, and resistance mechanisms in infected versus uninfected cancer cells. Cytokine profiling and immune cell polarization will also be analyzed to clarify roles of intratumoral bacteria in reshaping the immune landscape of the TME. Building on collected insights, we propose a dual-action therapeutic strategy using phage-guided liposomal delivery systems to simultaneously target pathogenic bacteria and cancer cells. Exploiting the inherent specificity of phages for their bacterial hosts, drug-loaded liposomes decorated with phages are designed to achieve selective delivery to infected tumors. Upon localization, phages can eradicate biofilms and lyse host bacteria, while the anticancer drug exerts its cytotoxic effects on malignant cells. To enhance the clinical applicability, we will investigate the feasibility of pulmonary delivery of phage-guided liposomal formulations using mesh nebulization for direct, localized delivery to lung tumors. In-vivo validation will be performed using CDX and orthotopic lung tumor models in mice, with intratumoral or intratracheal administration of phage-guided liposomes. This study will yield critical insights into the clinical implication of pathogenic bacteria on cancer progression. Successful development of phage-guided liposomal formulations can lay a strong foundation for the clinical development of precision-targeted treatment strategies for infection-associated cancers. 感染相關的惡性腫瘤在臨床上日益受到重視，尤其以肺癌的挑戰最為嚴峻。流行病學統計顯示，超過半數肺癌患者會合併肺部感染，常見病原菌中以克雷伯氏肺炎桿菌（革蘭氏陰性）與金黃色葡萄球菌（革蘭氏陽性）最為普遍。這些細菌能在腫瘤微環境中定殖，不僅與癌細胞相互影響，還能逃避免疫攻擊，並形成生物膜阻擋抗生素滲透，進而削弱療效。然而，腫瘤內細菌是否會促進腫瘤生長、調節免疫或誘發抗藥性，目前研究仍相當有限。本項目奠基於致病菌對惡性細胞的侵入偏好高於正常肺上皮細胞的前期發現，旨在釐清背後機制，為開發更有效的合併治療策略提供基礎。 本計畫將針對前期結果進行系統性機制探討，深入解析致病菌與肺癌細胞的分子交互作用。我們將透過細菌侵染實驗、轉錄體分析與免疫螢光染色，釐清細菌入侵途徑、胞內分布，以及其對宿主訊息傳遞與免疫反應的影響。同時比較有無細菌感染下，癌細胞對化療藥物的反應差異，包括藥物降解、細胞攝取、毒性表現及抗藥機轉。此外，也將分析細胞激素變化與免疫細胞分化傾向，以了解腫瘤內細菌如何重塑免疫微環境。 基於掌握的基礎資訊，我們提出一項雙重標靶治療策略：利用噬菌體導向之微脂體載藥系統，同步攻擊致病菌與癌細胞。噬菌體對宿主細菌具高度專一性，我們將化療藥物包覆於經噬菌體修飾的微脂體中，使其精準累積於受感染的腫瘤部位。到達標的後，噬菌體可破壞生物膜並裂解細菌，微脂體釋出之藥物則同步毒殺癌細胞。為提升臨床適用性，我們將測試此製劑是否可透過網式霧化器以吸入方式給藥，直接遞送至肺部腫瘤區域。動物實驗將採用小鼠異種移植與原位肺癌模型，分別以腫瘤內注射或氣管內給藥方式進行驗證。 本研究成果預期能為致病菌在癌症進程中所扮演的角色提供關鍵性的線索。若噬菌體導向微脂體製劑能順利開發完成，將有助於奠定感染相關癌症精準治療的臨床發展基礎，為此類患者帶來更具前景的治療選項。

14308626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14308626.value: 帶有散點隨機測量之次擴散問題參數識別的數值分析

14308626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14308626.value: Over the last few decades, inverse problems of estimating physical parameters in subdiffusion problems have formed a very prominent class of inverse problems for partial differential equations (PDEs) and have attracted much attention in the mathematics community, due to their wide-spread practical applications. This class of problems arises in many practical applications, e.g., in subsurface flow, pollution detection and medical imaging. However, these problems are mathematically and numerically very challenging, due to a lack of the usual well-posedness, especially the continuous dependence on problem data, and the inevitable presence of noise in the measurement data. Nonetheless, there have been significant progresses towards theoretical analysis, in terms of both uniqueness and stability. However, there remain significant challenges in developing effective reconstruction algorithms with rigorous error bounds, due to the high-degree of nonlinearity, and low regularity of the concerned parameters. This project aims to develop effective reconstruction algorithms for a class of nonlinear inverse problems for the subdiffusion model from the observational data at scattered points subject to sub-Gaussian random noise, and to provide relevant mathematical guarantees. The main additional challenge lies in the nonlinearity of the forward model, limited smoothing property of the solution operators, and the random and discrete nature of the measurement. The tools that we will employ include modern regularization theory, advanced tools from PDE theory and probabilistic tools (empirical processes). Specifically, this project is comprised of two work packages, which address two representative inverse problems. First, we investigate the stable recovery of the potential coefficient in the subdiffusion model from the scattered random measurements at a fixed terminal time. We aim at developing novel reconstruction algorithms using the Galerkin FEM in space and time stepping in time (e.g., backward Euler), and providing error bounds on the fully discrete approximation. This will be achieved by combining analytic tools, e.g., conditional stability estimates, with a priori estimates on the direct problem with nonsmooth data. Second, we investigate the recovery of the diffusion coefficient in the subdiffusion model from scattered random measurements at a terminal time. The key challenges include low regularity of the coefficient and the solutions of the associated PDEs. The proposed research will provide new insights into nonlinear PDE inverse problems with random scattered measurements which remain poorly understood in the low regularity regime. 在過去幾十年裡，次擴散模型的參數識別問題已成為偏微分方程反問題中一類突出的反問題，因其廣泛實際應用而廣受數學界的關注。該類問題出現於許多實際應用，如地下水流、污染檢測和醫學成像。然而由於缺乏適定性，尤其是對數據的連續依賴性，以及測量數據不可避免存在噪聲，該類問題在數學上和數值上都頗具挑戰性。儘管如此，唯一性和穩定性理論均已經取得顯著進展。 由於問題的高度非線性和所涉及參數的低正則性，在開發具有嚴格誤差界的有效重建算法方面仍存在重大挑戰。本項目將針對次擴散模型的一類非線性反問題，從函亞高斯隨機噪聲的散點觀測數據出發，開發高效重建算法，並提供相應數學保證。主要挑戰包括正問題的非線性、解算子的有限平滑性質及測量的隨機性和離散性。項目將採用的數學工具包括現代正則化理論、偏微分方程理論以及概率工具（經驗過程理論）。 本項目由兩個工作包組成。首先研究從終端散點隨機測量反演次擴散模型中的勢係數。將利用空間上的伽遼金有限元法和時間上的時間步進法構建重建算法，並為全離散近似提供誤差界。核心在於將分析工具（如條件穩定性估計）與含非光滑數據的正問題先驗估計相結合。其次研究從終端散點隨機測量反演次擴散模型中的擴散係數。關鍵挑戰包括係數及相關偏微分方程解的低正則性。迄今為止，非線性偏微分方程反問題在隨機散點測量的情形下仍鮮為人知，該項目將為此方向的研究提供新見解。

14308726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14308726.value: 運用 G4Earth 探討地球大氣伽馬射線

14308726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14308726.value: Earth atmospheric gamma rays are produced by cosmic rays interacting with the Earth's atmosphere. With the Fermi Gamma-ray space telescope, the Earth atmospheric gamma rays have been studied in detail, especailly on its association to the geomagnetic structure. These gamma rays provide important information about the interactions of cosmic rays with the atmosphere and Earth magnetic fields, both are important for studing the radiation environment of space. However, despite their importance, e.g., to satellite infrastructures and astronauts, there are currently no detailed theoretical studies on the production of these gamma rays that takes into account solar modulation and geomagnetic fields. In this project, I propose to develop a detailed simulation package, G4Earth, based on the popular Geant4 particle interaction simulation suite, to simulate the production of Earth atmospheric gamma rays. The simulation will take into account the effect of solar modulation via force-field models. Then fully 3D particle tracing and interaction modeling will be performed with the Geant4 particle simulation sutit. The geomagnetic fields will be modeled using state-of-the art magnetic field models, such as the IGRF and Tsyganenko models. The simulation will be used to study the spectral and spatial-angular properties of the Earth atmospheric gamma rays, and their correlation with geomagnetic structures. I will also study the time-dependece of the Earth atmospheric gamma rays, which should depends on either solar modulation of primary cosmic rays, time-varying geomagnetic fields, or both. In particular, I will search for transient earth gamma rays associlated with solar energetic particles, which could be a new probe for these explosive events and their effect on the earth atmosphere. At the end of this project, I will have developed a state-of-the-art simulation package that can accurately simulate the production of Earth atmospheric gamma rays, G4Earth. With this code and its results, I will perform detailed comparisons with Fermi data, on the spatial-angular distributions of the earth gamma rays. In particular, I will study, for the first time, the time dependence of the earth atmospheric gamma-ray flux. Effects from both solar modulation and the time-varying geomagnetic fields are expected to be seen. Earth gamma rays being an important bridge between cosmic rays, the Sun, and the earth magnetosphere could be a new way to study the earth and the space weather. 地球大氣伽馬射線是由宇宙射線與地球大氣層相互作用所產生的。藉由費米伽馬射線太空望遠鏡，地球大氣伽馬射線近期已被詳細研究，特別是其在與地磁結構關聯方面的特性。這些伽馬射線提供了關於宇宙射線與大氣層及地球磁場相互作用的重要資訊，而這兩者對於研究太空輻射環境皆至關重要。然而，儘管它們具有重要性——例如對衛星基礎設施與太空人而言——目前仍缺乏針對這些伽馬射線產生機制的詳細理論研究，對太陽調製與地磁場效應的影響的相關研究也沒有。 在本計畫中，我擬開發一套詳盡的模擬套件 G4Earth，此套件係基於廣泛使用的 Geant4 粒子交互作用模擬套件，用以模擬地球大氣伽馬射線的產生過程。該模擬將透過力場模型納入太陽調製的效應，並利用 Geant4 粒子模擬套件進行完整的三維粒子追蹤與交互作用建模。地磁場將採用最先進的磁場模型進行模擬，例如 IGRF 與 Tsyganenko 模型。此模擬將用於研究地球大氣伽馬射線的能譜與空間角向特性，以及它們與地磁結構的相關性。我亦將研究地球大氣伽馬射線的時間性，其應取決於初級宇宙射線的太陽調製、隨時間變化的地磁場，或兩者兼具。 在本計畫結束時，我將開發出一套最先進的模擬套件，能夠精確模擬地球大氣伽馬射線的產生，即 G4Earth。藉由這套程式碼及其模擬結果，我將與費米望遠鏡數據進行詳細比較，針對地球伽馬射線的空間角向分布進行分析。特別是，我將首次研究地球大氣伽馬射線的時間變化，預期可觀察到太陽調製與時變地磁場兩者的效應。此外，我將首次搜尋與太陽高能粒子相關的地球伽馬射線，這可能揭示太陽與地球磁層交互作用的新資訊，並對太空天氣研究具有重要意義。

14309126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14309126.value: 張量網路重整化與廣義對稱性

14309126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14309126.value: Global symmetry plays a foundational role in modern physics, shaping our understanding for quantum phases of matter and the nature of their phase transitions. Traditionally, symmetry refers to reversible transformations of local operators forming a group structure. This underpins the Landau paradigm, where phases are classified by symmetry preservation or spontaneous breaking—successfully explaining phenomena like superconductivity and magnetism. Even in the absence of symmetry breaking, nontrivial symmetry-protected topological phases can emerge, such as topological insulators, protected by symmetries like time-reversal and U(1) charge conservation. In recent years, The traditional concept of global symmetry has been broadened in several directions, including higher-form symmetries, non-invertible symmetries, higher-group symmetries in classifying quantum phases, especially in gapped systems. However, their role in gapless systems—particularly in conformal field theories (CFTs), which describe critical points of phase transitions—remains less understood. Our recent work makes pioneering advances in this direction by applying tensor network renormalization (TNR) to study generalized symmetries in gapless systems. At criticality, the renormalization group flow reaches a fixed point described by a tensor encoding the full structure of a CFT. We demonstrated that this fixed-point (FP) tensor can be reconstructed purely from generalized symmetry data, showing how continuous conformal symmetry emerges from a discrete tensor network. This insight also supports the topological holographic principle, suggesting that a 3D bulk spacetime can emerge from 2D CFT correlations. Beyond CFTs, our framework offers a new algebraic approach to quantum field theory. Unlike the traditional path integral—which suffers from ill-defined measures and perturbative limitations—we treat tensors as fundamental, allowing for a rigorous, discrete reformulation of QFT. In this proposal, we show how the path integral can be replaced by a tensor network that captures key features of CFTs. More general QFTs then emerge from controlled tensor deformations, corresponding to relevant perturbations. The TNR method with generalized symmetry not only enables a deeper understanding gapless systems but also provides a powerful non-perturbative framework for studying strongly correlated quantum systems. More specifically, we will pursue the following directions: 1) TNR with generalized symmetries and topological bootstrap; 2) FP tensors for fermionic CFTs and generalize symmetry for supersymmetry CFT; 3) Tensor network representations of two-dimensional QFTs and non-perturbative method; 4) Experimental implications for non-perturbative QFT. Through these research objectives, we aim to contribute to the systematic understanding of quantum critical systems and their potential applications in various fields. 全域對稱性在現代物理學中扮演著基礎性的角色，構建了我們對量子物質相及其相變本質的理解。傳統上，對稱性指的是局部算符的可逆變換，這些變換構成一個群結構。這一觀點構成了朗道範式的核心，其中相的區分依據對稱性是否被保持或自發破缺——這成功地解釋了超導電性與磁性等現象。即使在對稱性未破缺的情況下，仍可能出現非平凡的對稱保護拓樸相，例如拓樸絕緣體，其受到時間反演及U(1)電荷守恆等對稱性的保護。近年來，傳統的全域對稱性概念已在多個方向上被擴展，包括高形式對稱性、非可逆對稱性、高階群對稱性等，應用於量子相的分類，特別是在有能隙系統中。然而，它們在無能隙系統——特別是在描述相變臨界點的共形場論（CFT）——中所扮演的角色，仍較少被理解。 我們近期的工作在這一方向上取得了開創性的進展，應用了張量網路重整化（TNR）來研究無能隙系統中的廣義對稱性。在臨界點，重整化群流會到達一個由張量描述的不動點（FP），該張量編碼了CFT的完整結構。我們證明了此固定點張量可以僅從廣義對稱性數據中被重建，展示了連續的共形對稱性如何從離散的張量網路中湧現。這一洞見也支持了拓樸全息原理，暗示著三維體時空可以從二維CFT的關聯性中湧現。 除了CFT之外，我們的框架也為量子場論（QFT）提供了一種新的代數方法。不同於傳統的路徑積分——後者受限於定義不良的測度與微擾限制——我們將張量視為基本對象，從而允許對QFT進行嚴謹的離散重構。在本提案中，我們展示了路徑積分如何被一個能夠捕捉CFT關鍵特徵的張量網路所取代。更一般的QFT則可從受控的張量變形中湧現，這些變形對應於相關微擾。具有廣義對稱性的TNR方法不僅促進了對無能隙系統的更深層理解，也為研究強關聯量子系統提供了一個強有力的非微擾框架，甚至在基礎物理學中具有潛在的應用。 更具體地說，我們將朝以下方向進行研究：1）具有廣義對稱性的TNR與拓樸自舉法；2）費米子CFT的不動點張量及超對稱CFT的廣義對稱性；3）二維QFT的張量網路表示與非微擾方法；4）非微擾QFT的實驗意涵。通過這些研究目標，我們期望能為量子臨界系統的系統性理解及其在各個領域中的潛在應用作出貢獻。

14309326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14309326.value: 一個自洽的族群框架以解決重力波透鏡的生日問題

14309326.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14309326.value: Prof Li, Tjonnie Guang Feng Prof Parameswaran, Ajith

14309326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14309326.value: In the 1600s, Newton revolutionised our understanding of Gravity, viewing it as a fundamental force that permeated the Universe. Newton's view continued until the 1900s, when Einstein revolutionised our understanding of gravity a second time. Shortly after formulating his theory of general relativity in 1915, Einstein predicted the existence of gravitational waves—ripples in the fabric of spacetime. Gravitational-wave astronomy now celebrates its 10th anniversary. Since the first Nobel Prize-winning detection in 2015, hundred years after Einstein's prediction, the field has completed four successful observing runs, rigorously tested general relativity, independently measured the Universe's expansion, and revealed new black hole populations, among other breakthroughs. After completing the LVK's latest fourth observing run, the LIGO-Virgo-Kagra gravitational-wave detectors will be further upgraded in anticipation of O5. When this happens, new research avenues will become possible. Several independent forecasts from independent groups worldwide suggest 0.1-1% of gravitational-wave events may be strongly lensed, where massive objects distort and ``copy'' signals by bending spacetime. The expected rate in O4 is around 0.2-2, which makes detections already plausible, though not expected. However, this rate will increase substantially in future runs, such as O5 (starting around late 2027), aided by upgraded detectors. Thus, this proposal aims to develop new technologies for O4, O5, and beyond. Specifically, the goal is to create the first data-driven population inference framework aimed at overcoming the well-known and persistent lensing birthday problem. This framework is a novel approach that addresses a well-known problem through population inference without parametric assumptions--aiming at a paradigm shift from traditional model-dependent methods usually adopted in lensing. Importantly, this framework also advances the rapidly growing field of non-parametric population modeling within LVK, regardless of lensing timelines. The PI and collaborators will first develop an empirical Bayesian mixture framework to infer the population of compact objects across cosmic time. The population will then be lensed and connected with lensing hypothesis testing. The framework will then be validated on realistic mock data and applied to LVK data. These steps aim to confront the primary challenges in the field, while driving connections between lensing and the compact object population analysis communities. Gravitational-wave lensing has been a central part of Hong Kong's research since 2016. Combined with detection and forecasting frameworks, this work positions Hong Kong to advance the field through technologies now standard in LVK. Prior expertise, parallel/past RGC projects, pilot results, and a focus on well-established techniques support feasibility. 西元1600年代，牛頓徹底改變了我們對重力的理解，將其視為一種彌漫於宇宙之中的基本作用力。牛頓的觀點一直延續至1900年代，此時愛因斯坦第二次徹底改變了我們對重力的理解。愛因斯坦在1915年提出廣義相對論後不久，便預言了重力波的存在——即時空結構中的漣漪。 重力波天文學如今迎來十週年。自2015年首次獲得諾貝爾獎肯定的探測以來——距愛因斯坦的預言已逾百年——此領域已完成四次成功的觀測運行，對廣義相對論進行了嚴格檢驗，獨立測量了宇宙的膨脹，並揭示了新的黑洞族群，以及其他諸多突破。在完成LVK最新的第四次觀測運行後，LIGO-Virgo-Kagra重力波探測器將進一步升級，為O5觀測運行做準備。屆時，新的研究途徑將成為可能。 來自世界各地獨立團隊的數項獨立預測表明，0.1%至1%的重力波事件可能受到強透鏡效應影響，即大質量天體通過彎曲時空來扭曲並「複製」訊號。在O4觀測運行中，預期此類事件的數量約為0.2至2次，這使得探測已屬可能，儘管尚未在預期之中。然而，在未來的觀測運行中，例如O5（約於2027年底啟動），得益於探測器的升級，此一比率將大幅提升。 因此，本計劃旨在為O4、O5及後續觀測運行開發新技術。具體而言，目標是創建首個數據驅動的族群推斷框架，旨在克服廣為人知且長期存在的透鏡效應生日問題。此框架是一種新穎的方法，透過族群推斷而無需參數化假設來應對這一著名難題——旨在推動範式轉移，擺脫透鏡效應研究中通常採用的傳統模型依賴方法。重要的是，無論透鏡效應的時間表為何，此框架亦推進了LVK內部快速發展的非參數化族群建模領域。 計劃主持人及其合作者將首先開發一個經驗貝氏混合框架，以推斷緻密天體在宇宙時間尺度上的族群分佈。隨後，將對此族群施加透鏡效應，並與透鏡效應假設檢定相連結。該框架將在符合實際情況的模擬數據上進行驗證，並應用於LVK數據。這些步驟旨在應對該領域的主要挑戰，同時推動透鏡效應研究社群與緻密天體族群分析社群之間的聯繫。 自2016年起，重力波透鏡效應一直是香港研究的核心部分。結合探測與預測框架，此項工作使香港得以透過現已成為LVK標準的技術推動該領域的發展。先前的專業知識、並行/過往的優配研究金項目、初步結果，以及對成熟技術的重視，均為可行性提供了支持。

14309526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14309526.value: 以牛血清白蛋白載運光敏劑實現膠質瘤的靶向清除及膠質瘤相關巨噬細胞的重編程

14309526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14309526.value: Gliomas are among the most common primary brain tumors and are associated with high morbidity and mortality. Being the most aggressive and prevalent form, glioblastoma is characterized by profound heterogeneity, rapid proliferation, therapeutic resistance, and a dismal prognosis, with a median survival of less than 16 months despite aggressive multimodal therapy. The current standard of care—surgical tumor resection followed by radiotherapy and chemotherapy with temozolomide—offers only transient benefits and fails to prevent recurrence. While advancements in treatment alternatives have been made, major barriers to therapeutic success include the restricted permeability of the blood–brain barrier (BBB), inadequate tumor-specific drug delivery, poor intratumoral transport, and the intrinsic resistance of glioma cells to conventional therapies. As a promising antitumor modality, photodynamic therapy (PDT) utilizing light to activate photosensitizers to generate cytotoxic reactive oxygen species (ROS) has gained approval for several localized cancers. Recent clinical investigations suggest that PDT can extend progression-free survival in glioma patients, highlighting its promise as a minimally invasive and mechanistically distinct treatment. However, clinical translation remains limited by poor photosensitizer delivery across the BBB and insufficient tumor selectivity. To address these challenges, we propose the development of a bovine serum albumin-based nanosystem incorporating a boron dipyrromethene (BODIPY)-derived photosensitizer and a cyclic RGD peptide ligand for targeting αvβ3 integrin, which is highly expressed on glioma cells and tumor vasculature. The cyclic RGD-modified BSA not only improves solubility and pharmacokinetics but also promotes BBB penetration and tumor-specific accumulation. Moreover, it shifts the photosensitizing property of the BODIPY-based photosensitizer from a type-II to a type-I mechanism, favoring the generation of radical ROS such as superoxide anion and hydroxyl radical under far-red light excitation. Apart from direct elimination of gliomas, these radical ROS are expected to reprogram brain resident macrophages and microglia, which represent the most abundant non-neoplastic cells in gliomas, from an M2 (immunosuppressive, pro-tumor) to an M1 (pro-inflammatory, antitumor) phenotype, enabling modulation of the immune microenvironment. This dual action combines targeted tumor cell killing with immune reactivation, offering a synergistic strategy against gliomas. This therapeutic platform will be systematically evaluated through cell-line and animal studies to assess its safety, tumor selectivity, immune modulation, and antitumor efficacy. We believe that this approach has the potential to overcome key limitations of current therapies and establish a novel paradigm for precise and immune-activating treatment of gliomas. 膠質瘤是最常見的原發性腦腫瘤之一，具有高發病率和高死亡率。其中，膠質母細胞瘤（glioblastoma）是最常見且惡性程度最高的類型，具有高度異質性、快速增殖、治療抗性及預後極差等特徵。即使接受積極的多模式治療，患者的中位生存期仍不足16個月。目前的標準治療方案主要包括手術切除腫瘤，繼而進行放射治療及替莫唑胺（temozolomide）化學治療，但治療效益往往有限且短暫，亦難以有效防止腫瘤復發。儘管近年膠質瘤治療取得一定進展，其療效仍受到多項關鍵因素限制，包括血腦屏障（blood–brain barrier, BBB）的低通透性、藥物缺乏腫瘤特異性遞送、腫瘤內部傳輸效率不足，以及膠質瘤細胞對傳統治療的內在抗性。 光動力治療（photodynamic therapy, PDT）是一種極具潛力的抗腫瘤治療模式，利用光激活光敏劑產生具細胞毒性的活性氧物種（reactive oxygen species, ROS），目前已獲批准用於治療多種局部腫瘤。近期的臨床研究顯示，PDT有望延長膠質瘤患者的疾病無惡化存活期，顯示其作為一種微創且具有獨特作用機制的治療策略的潛力。然而，光敏劑難以有效跨越BBB以及腫瘤選擇性不足，仍然嚴重限制PDT在膠質瘤治療中的臨床轉化。 為克服上述挑戰，本研究擬開發一種以牛血清白蛋白（bovine serum albumin, BSA）為基礎的納米治療系統，結合硼二吡咯亞甲基（boron dipyrromethene, BODIPY）衍生光敏劑及環狀RGD肽配體，以靶向在膠質瘤細胞及腫瘤血管中高度表達的αvβ3整合素。經環狀RGD修飾的BSA不僅可改善光敏劑的水溶性及藥代動力學特性，亦可促進其跨越BBB並在腫瘤部位選擇性積聚。此外，BSA可使BODIPY光敏劑的光敏化機制由II型轉向I型，從而在遠紅光激發下促進超氧陰離子自由基及羥基自由基等自由基型ROS的產生。 除直接殺滅膠質瘤細胞外，這些自由基型ROS亦有望對腦內常駐巨噬細胞及小膠質細胞進行重編程。這些細胞是膠質瘤中數量最豐富的非腫瘤細胞之一，通常呈現免疫抑制及促腫瘤的M2樣表型。本研究將利用PDT誘導其由M2樣表型向促炎及抗腫瘤的M1樣表型轉變，從而重塑膠質瘤免疫微環境。此雙重作用策略將靶向腫瘤細胞殺傷與抗腫瘤免疫再激活相結合，有望產生協同抗膠質瘤效應。本研究將通過系統性的細胞及動物實驗，全面評估此治療平台的安全性、腫瘤靶向選擇性、免疫調節作用及抗腫瘤療效。我們相信，此策略有望克服現有膠質瘤治療的若干關鍵局限，並為建立一種兼具精準靶向及免疫激活功能的膠質瘤治療新模式奠定基礎。

14309826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14309826.value: 探討不同糧食系統轉型與氣候變化情景下農業活性氮排放對全球空氣質素的影響

14309826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14309826.value: The proposed research aims to assess how agricultural emissions will affect global air quality under different socioeconomic and climate change scenarios from now to the mid-21st century. The rising food production over the past half century has supported population growth and alleviated hunger, but has also induced severe environmental consequences. One of the most pressing issues is the leakage of reactive nitrogen (Nr) compounds from excessive fertilizer use in croplands and unmanaged animal waste in livestock systems. These emissions substantially contribute to the formation of harmful air pollutants such as fine particulate matter and tropospheric ozone, threatening both human health and ecosystems worldwide. With the global population continuing to grow and dietary patterns shifting toward higher meat consumption, food production is expected to intensify further. If pursued through conventional means, this will exacerbate nitrogen pollution. Additionally, climate change is projected to amplify agricultural Nr emissions through warmer temperatures and altered meteorological conditions. Therefore, the pathways countries take to transform their food systems through improved practices, dietary shifts, and technological innovation will critically shape future air quality and environmental health. In this study, we will develop a state-of-the-art, fully coupled climate-chemistry-agriculture modeling system based on the Community Earth System Model, which enables two-way interactions among agricultural emissions, atmospheric chemistry, and climate dynamics. The model will be driven by a machine learning-optimized global agricultural Nr emission inventory, which accounts for crop and livestock types, fertilizer use, manure management, and other food system characteristics. Model simulations will evaluate the impacts of different food system transformation pathways, ranging from business-as-usual to sustainable development scenarios, on global Nr emissions, air quality, and associated health outcomes. We will also assess how climate change may exacerbate emissions and offset mitigation benefits, quantifying the extent of such “climate penalty” and identifying adaptive strategies accordingly. By integrating Earth system modeling, machine learning, and scenario analysis, this study will provide among the first comprehensive assessment of how food system choices influence global air quality under climate change. The findings will offer a vital scientific foundation for policymakers, farmers, and consumers to develop sustainable and resilient food systems that jointly address air pollution, climate challenges, and food security, supporting multiple UN Sustainable Development Goals, including those related to zero hunger, good health and well-being, climate action and responsible consumption. 本研究旨在評估由現在至21世紀中葉，在不同社會經濟與氣候變化情景下，農業排放將如何影響全球空氣質素。過去半個世紀，糧食產量增加支撐了人口增長並減輕饑餓問題，但同時亦帶來嚴重的環境後果。其中一項最迫切的問題，是旱地過量施肥及畜牧系統中未經妥善管理的動物糞便所造成的活性氮化合物流失。這些排放大幅促成細懸浮粒子及對流層臭氧等有害空氣污染物的形成，對全球人類健康及生態系統構成威脅。隨着全球人口持續增長，以及飲食模式逐漸轉向較高肉類消費，糧食生產預計將進一步密集化。若仍採用傳統方式推動生產，氮污染將會加劇。此外，預計氣候變化亦會透過氣溫上升及氣象條件改變，增加農業活性氮排放。因此，各國透過改善生產方式、改變飲食模式及推動技術創新來轉型糧食系統的不同路徑，將對未來空氣質素及環境健康產生關鍵影響。 本研究將以CESM地球系統模型為基礎，建立一套先進的全耦合氣候–化學–農業模擬系統，從而模擬農業排放、大氣化學與氣候動力學之間的雙向相互作用。模型將由一套經機器學習優化的全球農業活性氮排放清單驅動，該清單涵蓋農作物及牲畜種類、肥料使用、糞便管理，以及其他糧食系統特徵。透過模型模擬，我們將評估由維持現狀至可持續發展情景等不同糧食系統轉型路徑，對全球活性氮排放、空氣質素及相關健康影響的作用。我們亦將評估氣候變化如何加劇農業排放並抵銷減排效益，量化這種「氣候懲罰效應」的程度，並據此識別相應的適應策略。 通過整合地球系統建模、機器學習及情景分析，本研究將提供其中一項首批全面評估，探討在氣候變化下，不同糧食系統選擇如何影響全球空氣質素。研究結果將為政策制定者、農民及消費者提供重要的科學基礎，以發展兼具可持續性及韌性的糧食系統，協同應對空氣污染、氣候挑戰及糧食安全問題，並支持多項聯合國可持續發展目標，包括消除饑餓、良好健康與福祉、氣候行動，以及負責任消費等目標。

14310126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14310126.value: 利用量子中心超級電腦研究超越精確可解範疇的二維關聯拓撲相

14310126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14310126.value: This project will develop quantum-classical hybrid algorithms for accurately simulating two-dimensional (2D) correlated topological phases, especially topological orders, at scales beyond exact diagonalization on a near-term quantum-classical hybrid computing platform (a quantum-centric supercomputer) and will apply these algorithms to challenging real-world problems: the Kagome-lattice Heisenberg model and the triangular-lattice Hubbard model. Topological orders (TOs; a class of new states of matter) are promising for impactful applications, most notably fault-tolerant quantum computation. Therefore, searching for appropriate systems that host specific TOs has become an important research topic. However, TOs usually arise in strongly correlated quantum many-body systems. In these systems, accompanying exponential computational complexity (“entanglement barrier”) emerges and makes classical simulation intractable. Quantum simulation (i.e., using quantum devices) offers a path beyond this barrier, but it is not straightforward because current devices suffer from decoherence and other noise. Although some TOs with known wavefunctions from exactly solvable models have been prepared on current quantum devices, it remains unclear how to compute the topological ground state of a non-exactly solvable model on these devices—an important research issue that still needs to be addressed. This project aims to develop a feasible variational quantum algorithm (VQA) to accurately simulate large-scale (beyond exact diagonalization) 2D correlated topological phases on currently accessible quantum devices, with support from well-developed classical high-performance computing (together forming a quantum-centric supercomputer), and to apply it to real-world applications. The PI and Co-I have successful experience in exploiting quantum simulations for non-exactly solvable topological phases and in developing algorithms for simulating large-scale quantum many-body problems on quantum-centric supercomputers. In this project, we will develop efficient algorithms to generate appropriate parametrized quantum-circuit Ansätze, which are the heart of VQA, for topological phases in interacting-electron and frustrated quantum-spin systems, based on fermionic Gaussian states and tensor-network states. A software package for large-scale Hamiltonian diagonalization in selected bases will also be developed to carry out the classical part of the VQA. Meanwhile, to develop and validate the VQA, we will build high-performance quantum-circuit simulators based on tensor-network states. For potential applications, we will investigate the ground states of the Kagome-lattice Heisenberg model and the triangular-lattice Hubbard model using this VQA on real quantum devices. By developing quantum algorithms for realistic correlated topological phases and applying them to challenging problems, this project will contribute to the realization of a fault-tolerant quantum computer. 本項目將開發量子—經典混合演算法，以在近期量子—經典混合計算平台（量子中心超級電腦）上，精確模擬超越精確對角化可處理規模的二維關聯拓撲相，尤其是拓撲序，並將這些演算法應用於兩個具挑戰性的實際問題：Kagome 格子 Heisenberg 模型及三角格子 Hubbard 模型。 拓撲序是一類新穎的物質狀態，在多項重要應用中具有很大潛力，其中尤以容錯量子計算最為突出。因此，尋找能夠實現特定拓撲序的合適物理系統已成為重要的研究課題。然而，拓撲序通常出現在強關聯量子多體系統中，而這些系統中的量子糾纏會導致計算複雜度隨系統尺寸呈指數增長，形成所謂的「糾纏壁壘」，令經典計算模擬變得極為困難。 量子模擬，即利用量子裝置進行計算，為突破這一壁壘提供了新的途徑。然而，由於目前的量子裝置仍受到退相干及其他噪聲的限制，要實現高精度模擬並非易事。雖然一些具有已知波函數、源自精確可解模型的拓撲序已能在現有量子裝置上製備，但如何在這些裝置上計算非精確可解模型的拓撲基態，目前仍是一個尚待解決的重要研究問題。 本項目的目標是開發一套可行的變分量子演算法，結合成熟的經典高性能計算技術，在目前可用的量子裝置上精確模擬大規模、超越精確對角化能力的二維關聯拓撲相，並將其應用於實際物理問題。項目首席研究員及共同研究員在利用量子模擬研究非精確可解拓撲相，以及開發用於量子中心超級電腦的大規模量子多體計算演算法方面均具有相關研究經驗。 本項目將針對強關聯電子系統及受挫量子自旋系統中的拓撲相，分別以費米高斯態及張量網絡態為基礎，開發高效演算法以構造合適的參數化量子電路 Ansatz，作為變分量子演算法的核心。同時，我們亦將開發在選定基底中進行大規模哈密頓量對角化的軟件，以完成量子—經典混合演算法中的經典計算部分。為了開發及驗證上述演算法，我們還將建立基於張量網絡態的高性能量子電路模擬器。最後，我們將在實際量子裝置上應用所開發的演算法，研究 Kagome 格子 Heisenberg 模型及三角格子 Hubbard 模型的基態。 透過開發適用於實際關聯拓撲相的量子演算法，並將其應用於具挑戰性的量子多體問題，本項目將為最終實現容錯量子計算作出貢獻。

14310526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14310526.value: 有機硫化物水系液流電池：設計原則與衰減機制

14310526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14310526.value: This project investigates the fundamental design principles and degradation mechanisms of catalyst-assisted organosulfide-based electrolytes with low crossover rates for high-power aqueous redox flow batteries (RFBs), aiming to advance safe and cost-effective long-duration energy storage. Aqueous RFBs are a promising technology for grid-scale energy storage due to their inherent safety, scalability, and decoupled energy and power capacities. However, the dominant vanadium-based RFBs are limited by high vanadium costs, while polysulfide-based alternatives offer low material costs but suffer from severe crossover of small polysulfide ions, causing rapid capacity decay and electrode passivation. Common mitigation strategies, such as membrane engineering (e.g., increasing thickness, tuning ion channels, or applying surface coatings), often leads to higher membrane resistance and reduced power performance due to the trade-off between selectivity and ionic transport. To address these challenges, this project aims to develop catalyst-assisted, low-crossover organosulfide electrolytes that combine larger molecular sizes to minimize crossover with homogeneous catalysis to enhance reaction kinetics. Through a systematic approach integrating synthesis, characterization, computation, and cell testing, we pursue the following objectives to realize high-power, stable organosulfide-based RFBs. Firstly, we will synthesize a series of organo-tetrasulfides by grafting blocking centers and hydrophilic terminal groups onto polysulfides, thereby increasing molecular size to suppress crossover. We will elucidate structure-property-performance relationships by evaluating the impacts of functional groups on (i) crossover rate, (ii) solubility, (iii) redox potential, and (iv) electrochemical kinetics, using a combination of experimental measurements and theoretical calculations to guide rational molecular design. Secondly, we will design molecular catalysts to accelerate the sluggish reduction kinetics of organosulfides via homogeneous catalysis. Thirdly, we will integrate the optimized low-crossover, catalyzed organosulfide negative electrolytes (negolytes) with ultra-thin ion-exchange membranes to demonstrate stable operation in full organosulfide-ferrocyanide flow batteries at high current densities (>100 mA cm⁻²) and energy efficiencies (≥80%). Lastly, we will employ operando spectroscopic techniques to probe the reaction mechanisms of organosulfides and associated catalytic processes, while analyzing degradation pathways in full cells under practical harsh conditions, such as elevated temperatures and high current densities. By revealing the fundamental structure-property-performance relationships of organosulfides and establishing design principles for catalyst-assisted systems, this project will provide a deep mechanistic understanding of degradation in aqueous RFBs, paving the way for durable, low-cost energy storage solutions. 本項研究專注於開發一種更安全、更平價的水基液流電池技術，特別適合長時間儲存電力（例如電網級應用）。目前主流的釩基液流電池雖然安全，但釩金屬價格高昂。另一種用多硫化物的替代方案成本低，卻有嚴重互串問題：小分子硫化物容易穿過隔膜，導致電池容量快速衰退、電極損壞。一般改善方法（加厚隔膜或改結構）又會增加電阻、降低功率表現。為了解決這些問題，本項目設計「有機硫化物」電解液：把較大的分子結構和親水基團接到硫化物上，讓分子變大，大幅減少互串。希望透過分子設計與催化，找出兼具低成本、低互串、高功率和長壽命的有機硫化物液流電池方案，為大規模長時間儲能提供更實用的技術基礎。

14310626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14310626.value: 生態記憶與植物功能性狀於極端氣候下對草地生態系統的功能與穩定性調控扮演甚麼角色？

14310626.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14310626.value: Dr Hossain, Md Lokman Prof Niu, Shuli Prof Wu, Jin Dr Zhang, Ruiyang

14310626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14310626.value: While grassland ecosystems cover approximately one-third of the land area in China, their coverage is experiencing a notable decline in recent years that could impede the steady provision of ecosystem functions, e.g. biomass production. Although previous studies have investigated the effects of climate extremes on grassland ecosystems, the role of memory effects of climatic conditions (MECC: influence of previous climate on current vegetation) and vegetation growth carryover (VGC: influence of present state of vegetation on future growth) in regulating ecosystem functioning and stability of grasslands remains poorly understood. Moreover, a thorough understanding of how plant community properties and functional traits influence the functioning of these grasslands remains elusive. Using the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau (QTP) as a case study, this research aims to: (i) assess the impacts of plant community properties and plant functional traits on ecosystem functioning of grasslands across different functional groups within individual grassland types; (ii) investigate the underlying abiotic factors that contribute to varying patterns of functional traits and biodiversity-productivity relationships across different grassland types along the altitudinal gradient; (iii) examine the influence of MECC on the ecosystem functioning and stability of various types of grasslands; and (iv) explore the effects of vegetation growth carryover (VGC) on the ecosystem functioning of grasslands across different periods in the growing seasons under varying strengths of climate extremes. We will extract climate and normalized vegetation difference index (NDVI) data (1984-2025) for various grassland types from multiple sources. The NDVI values against preceding climatic conditions will be evaluated to assess the MECC on vegetation, while VGC will be calculated using a linear mixed-effects model that quantifies the effect of prior vegetation state on current productivity after controlling for concurrent climatic conditions. Moreover, for each grassland type, measurements of plant community properties, functional traits and abiotic environmental parameters will be conducted in replicate plots along the altitudinal gradient at 500 m intervals. By separating the climatological memory of past conditions from the biological memory within the vegetation itself to examine how past climatic conditions influence current vegetation functioning and ecosystem stability, this study will deepen our understanding of ecological memory significantly. Furthermore, the study of VGC effect will shed light on how plant performance in the early, peak, and late growing seasons affect future vegetation growth and ecosystem performance. This research will offer evidence-based recommendations for sustainable management strategies for Chinese grasslands and other similar grasslands worldwide in the face of climate extremes. 儘管草地生態系統覆蓋了中國約三分之一的陸地面積，但近年來其覆蓋面積顯著減少，這可能阻礙其生態系統功能（如生物量生產）的穩定發揮。雖然先前研究已探討了極端氣候對草地生態系統的影響，但關於氣候條件記憶效應（即前期氣候對當前植被的影響）和植被生長滯後效應（即植被當前狀態對未來生長的影響）在調節草地生態系統功能與穩定性方面的作用，目前尚缺乏深入了解。此外，對於植物群落特徵和功能性狀如何影響這些草地的生態系功能，目前尚無透徹的認知。 本研究以青藏高原為例，旨在：(一) 評估在不同草地類型及功能群間，植物群落特徵和植物功能性狀對草地生態系統功能的影響；(二) 探究潛在非生物因素對沿海拔梯度不同草地類型間功能性狀格局及生物多樣性-草地關係差異的影響；(三) 調查氣候條件記憶效應如何影響不同草地類型之功能與穩定性；(四) 探討在不同強度的極端氣候條件下，植被生長滯後效應於生長季節不同時期對草地生態系統功能的影響。 我們將從多源資料中擷取各類草地類型的氣候資料和歸一化植被指數資料（1984–2025年）。透過分析歸一化植被指數與前期氣候條件的關係來評估氣候條件對植被的記憶效應，同時利用線性混合效應模型計算植被生長滯後效應，該模型將在控制同期氣候條件的前提下，量化前期植被狀態對當前生產力的影響。此外，針對每種草地類型，我們將沿著海拔梯度以500公尺為間隔設定重複樣地，並測定植物群落特徵、功能性狀及非生物環境參數。 本研究將區分源自過去氣候條件的氣候記憶與植被本身的生物記憶，進而檢視過去的氣候條件如何影響當前的植被功能與生態系統穩定性，這將顯著加深我們對生態記憶的理解。此外，植被生長滯後效應的研究將揭示植物在生長季節初期、盛期和末期的表現如何影響未來的植被生長及生態系統功能。這項研究將針對氣候極端事件背景下中國及全球類似草地的永續管理策略，提供科學證據為本的建議。

14310726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14310726.value: 具有不確定性之薛定諤方程的高效數值方法

14310726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14310726.value: This proposal focuses on numerical approximation of the nucleonic Schrödinger system and its semi-classical approximation models with band-crossing phenomena, which arise from the Bohn-Oppenheimer approximation to N-body Schrödinger equation with inter-band transition, the so-called non-adiabatic quantum phenomena. The problem has three computational challenges: degeneracy of eigenspace, highly oscillatory solutions, and uncertainties. The objectives of the proposal is to develop efficient numerical methods to tackle these challenges. Specifically, our research projects involve the following topics: • developing nonlinear geometric optics (NGO) based particle and high-order semi-Lagrangian methods that are structure-preserving, and allow numerical parameters (time step and mesh size) to be independent of the small wavelength, thus allowing efficient and reliable numerical simulations to non-adiabatic quantum dynamics with highly oscillatory solutions; • developing multi-fidelity methods for nucleonic Schrödinger system with random uncertainties, allowing one to conduct uncertainty quantification efficiently for highly oscillatory, non-adiabatic quantum dynamics. Our projects, if successfully carried out, will provide state-of-the-art numerical and uncertainty quantification techniques to solve important non-adiabatic quantum dynamics, which has broad applications from chemical reaction, semiconductor modeling to graphane simulation. 本計畫聚焦於具有能帶交叉現象之核薛定諤系統及其半經典近似模型的數值逼近。此類系統源自于具有能帶間躍遷的多體薛定谔方程之玻恩-奧本海默近似，所描述的現象通常稱為非絕熱量子現象。此問題面臨三項主要的計算挑戰：特徵空間的簡併性， 高度振盪的解以及不確定性。本計畫的目標是發展高效的數值方法，以克服上述挑戰。 具體而言，本研究計畫包含以下研究主題： 1. 發展基於非線性幾何光學的粒子方法與高階半拉格朗日方法。 這些方法具有結構保持的特性，並使數值參數（時間步長與網格尺寸）能夠獨立於小波長從而實現對具有高度振盪解之非絕熱量子動力學進行高效且可靠的數值模擬； 2. 針對具有隨機不確定性的核薛定諤系統，發展多保真方法， 以便對具有高度振盪特性之非絕熱量子動力學問題進行高效的不確定性量化。 若上述研究能夠順利完成，預期將為重要的非絕熱量子動力學問題提供最先進的數值計算與不確定性量化方法，並具有廣泛的應用前景。

14311226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14311226.value: 了解鈣鈦礦太陽能電池中的降解途徑和電荷積累：從淺陷阱到移動離子

14311226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14311226.value: Perovskite solar cells have demonstrated unprecedented progress in power conversion efficiency, now rivaling established silicon technology. However, their path to commercialization is critically hindered by operational instability, especially under real-world conditions with light, heat, and reverse bias due to partial shading. Therefore, it is essential to gain a comprehensive understanding of the underlying chemical and physical processes occurring during device aging and their effects on device performance. The reasons for this are being extensively investigated. We were recently able to demonstrate that the creation of more and more mobile ions under external stressors in the mixed electronic-ionic perovskite semiconductors leads to increased charge extraction losses with aging, representing a dominant degradation pathway. Nevertheless, a significant part of the total degradation loss under operation remains unaccounted for, and a full breakdown of all major recombination losses has not been achieved yet. The keys to achieving this are understanding the intricate interplay between shallow traps and mobile ions, as well as the massive charge accumulation in the device during degradation, which correlates strongly with the stability. In this project, we aim to gain a deep understanding of the major recombination mechanisms during degradation, not only due to mobile ions and shallow traps, but also due to insufficient charge transport and non-radiative recombination losses. We do so by first separating the losses at fast current-voltage scan speeds, where mobile ions are frozen, from the losses at slow scan speeds. We will then examine the interplay and mobile ions and shallow trapped charges to the degradation losses, building on previous drift-diffusion simulations of various electro-optical measurements, in particular, conductivity, quasi-Fermi level splitting, capacitance, and charge extraction measurements. To quantify losses under ion-freeze conditions, we will assess non-radiative losses as well as charge transport losses through transient surface photovoltage and resistance-dependent photovoltage measurements. The analysis will also be partially corroborated by an AI-assisted performance analysis. Ultimately, the experimental protocol will be applied to different aging operational conditions, including light, heat, and reverse bias. The project's findings address key unsolved fundamental questions and are critical for understanding degradation pathways under prolonged device operation. 鈣鈦礦太陽能電池在光電轉換效率方面展現了前所未有的進展，現已可與成熟的矽基技術相匹敵。然而，其商業化之路仍受到操作穩定性不足的嚴重阻礙，特別是在真實世界的條件下，例如光照、高溫，以及因局部遮蔭所導致的反向偏壓。因此，全面了解元件老化過程中所發生的化學與物理機制，以及這些機制對元件性能的影響，至關重要。目前相關原因正受到廣泛研究。我們最近已能證明，在外加應力條件下，混合型電子-離子鈣鈦礦半導體中會產生越來越多的移動離子，導致老化過程中電荷萃取損失增加，這是一個主要的退化途徑。然而，操作過程中總體退化損失仍有相當大的部分尚未被解釋，且尚未能完整解析所有主要的複合損失。要達成此目標，關鍵在於理解淺層陷阱與移動離子之間的複雜交互作用，以及在退化過程中元件內部大量電荷累積的現象，而此累積現象與穩定性密切相關。在本計畫中，我們旨在深入瞭解退化過程中的主要複合機制，不僅限於移動離子與淺層陷阱所導致者，還包括電荷傳輸不足及非輻射複合損失所造成的影響。為此，我們首先將快速電流-電壓掃描速度下（此時移動離子被凍結）的損失，與慢速掃描速度下的損失分離開來。接著，我們將基於先前對各種電光量測（特別是導電度、準費米能階分裂、電容及電荷萃取量測）的漂移-擴散模擬，進一步探討移動離子與淺層束縛電荷對退化損失的交互作用。為了量化離子凍結條件下的損失，我們將透過暫態表面光電壓及電阻依賴型光電壓量測，來評估非輻射損失與電荷傳輸損失。分析結果也將部分輔以人工智慧輔助性能分析進行驗證。最終，此實驗流程將應用於不同的老化操作條件，包括光照、高溫及反向偏壓。本計畫的研究成果將探討多項未解的基礎關鍵問題，並對於理解元件長時間操作下的退化損失具有關鍵重要性。

14311326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14311326.value: 非阿貝爾移位算子與等變鏡像對稱

14311326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14311326.value: A gauge theory is a type of physical theory whose dynamics does not change under local transformations. The group of such transformations is called the gauge group of the theory. Gauge theories are important in modern day particle physics as well as in explaining gravitation in the theory of general relativity. 3d mirror symmetry arises as a duality between gauge theories. This duality is different from the duality from which classical mirror symmetry (or so-called 2d mirror symmetry) was originated. Over the last 10 years, this new 3d mirror symmetry phenomenon has attracted much attention from mathematicians and mathematical physicists because it turned out to have very interesting relations with a diverse range of subjects including enumerative geometry, algebraic geometry, symplectic topology, representation theory, etc. In this project, the PI plans to apply a recent construction of so-called nonabelian shift operators by himself and collaborators to further understand equivariant mirror symmetry and 3d mirror symmetry, mainly building on the framework proposed by Teleman in his 2014 ICM address. The first main objective of this project is to understand the geometry of a space called the Coulomb branch, which naturally appears in one side of the duality (the space on the other side is called a Higgs branch). The construction of the Coulomb branch is rather complicated. In fact, it has taken mathematicians a long time to arrive at the correct construction. Its structure remains very mysterious. Making use of our new construction of nonabelian shift operators, the PI aims to get some new insight into the structures of these Coulomb branches. The second main objective of this project is to apply the construction of nonabelian shift operators to study 3d mirror symmetry via Teleman’s conjectures on equivariant 2d mirror symmetry. On the one hand, we plan to explore a quantum version of the so-called “quantization commutes with reduction” principle. We plan to use a nonabelian version of Fourier transform in our investigation. We would also like to further generalize the construction of nonabelian shift operators and apply it to 3d mirror symmetry of some important classes of examples. One such class is given by the Springer resolutions, which are important in geometric representation theory. Last but not the least, we plan to explore transformations of 3d branes, which is crucial for an in-depth understanding of 3d mirror symmetry. 規範場論是一套物理理論，其動力學在局部變換下保持不變。這種變換群稱為該理論的規範群。規範理論在現代粒子物理學以及廣義相對論中解釋引力方面都非常重要。 三維鏡像對稱是不同規範場論之間的一種對偶性。這種對偶性不同於經典鏡像對稱或所謂的二維鏡像對稱。過去十年間，這種新的三維鏡像對稱現象引起了數學家和數學物理學家的廣泛關注，因為它與枚舉幾何、代數幾何、辛拓撲、表示論等許多領域有著非常有趣的關聯。 本項目負責人計畫運用其本人及合作者近期構造的所謂非交換移位算子，進一步理解等變鏡像對稱和三維鏡像對稱，主要基於Teleman在2014年國際數學家大會（ICM）演講中提出的框架。 本項目的首要目標是理解Coulomb分支空間的幾何性質。Coulomb分支空間自然地出現在對偶空間的一側（另一側的空間稱為Higgs分支）。Coulomb分支空間的構造相當複雜，事實上，數學家們花了很長時間才找到正確的構造方法。它的結構至今仍是一個謎。利用我們新構造的非交換移位算子，項目負責人旨在深入了解這些Coulomb分支的結構。 本項目的第二個主要目標是將非交換移位算子的構造，並結合Teleman關於等變二維鏡像對稱的猜想，應用於研究三維鏡像對稱。一方面，我們計劃探索所謂的「量子化與約化交換」原理的量子版本。我們計劃在研究中使用非交換傅立葉變換。此外，我們也希望進一步推廣非交換移位算子的構造，並將其應用於一些重要例子的三維鏡像對稱。其中一類例子是Springer分解，它們在幾何表示論中非常重要。最後，我們計劃探索三維膜的變換，這對於深入理解三維鏡像對稱至關重要。

14311426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14311426.value: 基於側翼芳烴骨架的高可調性膦配體在芳基乙酸酯鈀催化交叉偶聯反應中的研究：瞬態協同配位與基礎機制探究

14311426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14311426.value: Catalysis has revolutionized the field of organic synthesis by offering rich opportunity in achieving versatility. At the forefront of catalysis technology, the activation of carbon-oxygen bond remains a central challenge in Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling processes. While aryl acetates (ArOAc) are attractive substrates derived from abundant phenolic feedstocks, their robust nature of C(Ar)-O bonds is notoriously difficult to activate selectively. This proposal aims to overcome this challenge through the rational design of highly tunable phosphine ligands, engineered with flanking arene chassis for exploiting synergistic transient metal ligation and arene substrate pi-pi-coordination. The main focuses of this proposal are: (1) to rationally design phosphine ligands having flanking arene units and to establish efficient synthetic schemes for attaining systematically varied phosphine ligand scaffolds; (2) to comprehensively explore and study the scope of Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling of ArOAc and the enantioselective arylation; (3) to fundamentally elucidate the reaction mechanism and probe the transient ligation catalysis steps using both experimental and computational approaches, for acquiring more in-depth understanding of this new catalysis science. This project is designed to unlock the yet to be solved Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling of aryl acetates. The knowledge gained through the development, refinement and manipulation of catalysts is expected to significantly propelling the field of catalysis sciences forward. The proposed study is based on our encouraging proof-of-concept initial results, proven expertise in the ligand and catalyst design, as well as our extensive experiences in aromatic bond-construction research. The success of this program will not only advance the frontier of chemical bond activation but also establish a pioneering research platform in Hong Kong, aligning with the Greater Bay Area's strategic focus on technological innovation for the fine-chemical industry. 催化技術為有機合成領域帶來了革命性的變化，提供了實現高度多樣化合成的廣泛機會。在催化技術的前沿領域，碳-氧（C-O）鍵的活化一直是鈀（Pd）催化交叉偶聯反應的核心挑戰。雖然乙酸芳酯（ArOAc）是一類源自豐富酚類原料的極具吸引力的底物，但其芳基碳-氧鍵（C(Ar)-O）性質穩定，難以實現選擇性活化。本提案旨在透過合理設計高度可調的膦配體來克服此難題；這些配體將引入側翼芳烴骨架，以協同利用過渡金屬配位作用與芳烴底物間的π-π相互作用。 本提案的主要研究重點包括：（1）合理設計帶有側翼芳烴單元的膦配體，並建立高效的合成路線，以製備結構各異的膦配體骨架；（2）全面探索和研究乙酸芳酯參與的鈀催化交叉偶聯反應及對映選擇性芳基化反應的適用範圍；（3）結合實驗與計算方法，深入研究機制並加深對分析方法，從而加深配位的分析方法，從而深入闡明對計算這一方法，從而深入研究機制並加深對解決這一步驟的分析。 本計畫旨在攻克乙酸芳酯鈀催化交叉偶聯這一尚未解決的難題。透過催化劑的開發、優化與調控所累積的知識，可望顯著推動催化科學領域的發展。本研究建立在我們令人鼓舞的概念驗證初步結果、在配體與催化劑設計方面的成熟專業知識，以及在芳香族化學鍵構建研究方面的豐富經驗之上。該計畫的成功不僅將拓展化學鍵活化領域的前沿，還將在香港建立一個開創性的研究平台，從而契合粵港澳大灣區關於精細化工產業技術創新的戰略重點。

14311626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14311626.value: 多圖表曲面映射問題及其應用

14311626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14311626.value: Surface mapping plays a central role in computer graphics, medical imaging, and shape analysis, providing the mathematical foundation for tasks ranging from registration and texture transfer to geometric modeling. Conventionally, most mapping methods assume simple surfaces that can be parameterized by a single global chart. However, many real-world surfaces, such as anatomical structures, high-genus objects, and shapes with intricate features, often require multiple overlapping charts to parameterize the surface accurately with the least distortions. Some surfaces cannot admit a global parameterization, and even when possible, such parameterizations may introduce large area distortions, leading to numerical errors in downstream tasks. Despite this need, existing methods are not well-suited to handle the challenges of multi-chart surface mapping. In our previous work, we developed efficient numerical frameworks based on quasi-conformal geometry, enabling distortion-controlled parameterizations and robust diffeomorphic surface registration for simple surfaces that can be parameterized by global charts. Building on this foundation, we now seek to address the less-explored and more challenging problems of multi-chart surface mapping. These problems encompass several key aspects. Specifically, this proposal focuses on two important objectives: the mapping problems between two multi-chart surfaces and the embedding problem of a multi-chart surface to an optimized shape in 3D Euclidean space. Our primary research objective is to create robust, learning-based algorithms to address the challenges inherent in these problems, including the discrete nature of chart selection, the need for seamless consistency across chart boundaries, and the preservation of global geometric quality. The research will proceed by tackling several key tasks: (1) developing a general framework for computing multi-chart surface mappings using a novel differentiable chart correspondence network; (2) optimizing multi-chart mappings for surfaces with complex geometries; (3) designing methods for optimizing the canonical parameterization of high-genus closed surfaces by co-optimizing the map and the domain geometry; (4) computing the embedding from a multi-chart surface to an unparameterized shape; (5) applying the proposed frameworks to problems in medical imaging and (6) applying the propsed methods to challenges in computer graphics. The proposed work will integrate the expertise of the PI in computational quasi-conformal geometry with state-of-the-art deep learning methods. The expected outcome is a set of algorithms that will advance the study of multi-chart surface mapping problems, with broad applications in medical imaging and computer graphics. 曲面映射在電腦圖學、醫學影像與形狀分析中扮演核心角色，為從配準、紋理轉移到幾何建模等各類任務提供數學基礎。傳統上，多數映射方法假設曲面較為簡單，可由單一全域圖表進行參數化。然而，許多真實世界中的曲面，例如解剖結構、高虧格物體，以及具有複雜特徵的形狀，往往需要多個相互重疊的圖表，才能在最小失真的情況下準確地參數化曲面。有些曲面無法接受全域參數化；即使可以，全域參數化也可能引入巨大的面積失真，進而導致下游任務中的數值誤差。儘管存在此一需求，現有方法仍不太適合處理多圖表曲面映射所帶來的挑戰。在我們先前的研究中，我們已發展出基於擬共形幾何的高效率數值框架，能夠為可由全域圖表參數化的簡單曲面提供失真受控的參數化，以及穩健的微分同胚曲面配準。基於此一基礎，我們現在希望處理較少被探索且更具挑戰性的多圖表曲面映射問題。這些問題涵蓋數個關鍵方向。具體而言，本計畫聚焦於兩個重要目標：兩個多圖表曲面之間的映射問題，以及將多圖表曲面嵌入至三維歐幾里得空間中最佳化形狀的問題。我們的主要研究目標是建立穩健的、基於學習的演算法，以應對這些問題中固有的挑戰，包括圖表選擇的離散性、圖表邊界之間無縫一致性的需求，以及全域幾何品質的保持。本研究將透過數項關鍵任務來推進：（1）利用一種新穎的可微分圖表對應網路，發展計算多圖表曲面映射的一般框架；（2）針對具有複雜幾何的曲面最佳化多圖表映射；（3）透過共同最佳化映射與域幾何，設計用於最佳化高虧格閉合曲面之典範參數化的方法；（4）計算從多圖表曲面到未參數化形狀的嵌入；（5）將所提出的框架應用於醫學影像問題；以及（6）將所提出的方法應用於電腦圖學中的挑戰。本計畫將整合計畫主持人在計算擬共形幾何方面的專長與最先進的深度學習方法。預期成果將是一套能推進多圖表曲面映射問題研究的演算法，並在醫學影像與電腦圖學中具有廣泛應用。

14311726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14311726.value: 流體動力學液晶理論中的尖銳界面極限

14311726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14311726.value: Periodic stripes are a ubiquitous phenomenon in liquid crystal materials. The physical parameters that may cause the stripes are various. In this project, we focus on the external magnetic fields and surface anchoring constants and investigate the formation of stripes when these parameters are strong. We plan to study the sharp interface limits in certain hydrodynamic systems as the external magnetic field strength and surface anchoring constants tend to infinity. The systems include, but are not limited to, the hydrodynamic sine-Gordon equation, a simplified Ericksen-Leslie system, and the Beris-Edwards system. In experiments, the quadruple junctions are also observed. It is a structurally stable singularity at which four sharp interfaces are joined. We also plan to investigate the persistence of the quadruple junction along the weak formulation of the flow derived from the previously mentioned sharp interface limits. We believe our studies can provide theoretical and rigorous explanations for various singular phenomena occurring on the bulk surfaces of liquid crystals. New mathematical problems may be motivated. Novel techniques may be invented to tackle these problems. The project can attract attention from both pure mathematicians and applied scientists. 週期性條紋是液晶材料中普遍存在的現象。導致條紋形成的物理參數多種多樣。本研究項目重點在於外部磁場和表面錨定常數，並研究當這些參數較強時條紋的形成機制。我們計劃研究某些流體動力學系統中，當外部磁場強度和表面錨定常數趨於無限大時，界面銳利的極限情況。這些系統包括但不限於流體動力學正弦-戈登方程式、簡化的埃里克森-萊斯利系統和貝里斯-愛德華茲系統。實驗中也觀察到了四重交界點。這是一種結構穩定的奇點，四個銳利的介面在此匯合。我們也計劃研究四重交界點在上述界面銳利極限推導出的弱流動形式下的持續性。我們相信，我們的研究可以為液晶體表面發生的各種奇異現象提供理論和嚴謹的解釋，並可能引出新的數學問題，以及解決這些問題的新技術。該計畫可以吸引純數學家和應用科學家的注意。

14311826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14311826.value: 求解帶約束的非線性偏微分方程的預處理剃度型方法的定量數學分析

14311826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14311826.value: This research undertakes a systematic investigation of preconditioned gradient-type methods for solving nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) subject to linear constraints. We are particularly interested in those nonlinear PDEs that can be formulated as constrained optimizations, where the objective functional represents an appropriate energy while the constraints encode some fundamental laws. Projection-based gradient methods are known to be a standard strategy for the constrained nonlinear PDEs, but their performance is frequently hampered by a computational bottleneck: the need to repeatedly compute projections of approximate solutions onto constraint sets, which entails solving large-scale ill-conditioned linear systems. To overcome this bottleneck, practitioners often employ inexact preconditioned projected gradient descent (IPPGD) methods, which relax projection accuracy. However, there are various variants of IPPGD, and there is no existing theoretical or numerical guidance to help practitioners judge which variant is more efficient, how to choose the key parameters involved, and how to find an effective inexact projection operator for a concrete constrained PDE. More importantly, the theoretical foundations of these methods, particularly the construction of effective inexact projectors and their global convergence behavior, remain underdeveloped. This project will make a significant effort to understand and study these basic questions and to build up the theoretical foundations of the IPPGD methods. Our contributions are threefold. First, we introduce a novel framework for constructing inexact projection operators. Second, we model IPPGD algorithms through a novel non-gradient flow; its discretization not only recovers the original method but also yields a new and accelerated variant. Third, we introduce some tailored and appropriately weighted Lyapunov functionals to develop exponential convergence at the continuous level and linear convergence of these methods at the discrete level. We will demonstrate the new theories and their predictions with a class of important constrained nonlinear PDEs, and further improve the methods through numerical experiments and the convergence theory. Ultimately, this work underscores that the design of the inexact projections and effective preconditioners is paramount, and we will propose some efficient and reliable construction strategies and verify their effectiveness and stability numerically through various constrained nonlinear PDEs. 本研究系統性地探討了用於求解受線性約束的非線性偏微分方程（PDEs）的預處理梯度型方法。我們特別關注那些可表述為約束最佳化問題的非線性PDEs，其中目標泛函代表適當的能量，而約束則編碼了一些基本規律。基於投影的梯度方法雖是處理帶約束非線性PDEs的標準策略，但其效能常受到一個計算瓶頸的阻礙：需要反覆計算近似解在約束集合上的投影，而這涉及求解大規模病態線性系統。 為克服此瓶頸，通常採用非精確預處理投影梯度下降（IPPGD）方法，此類方法放寬了投影精度。然而，IPPGD法存在多種變體，目前尚無既有的理論或數值指引來協助我們判斷哪種變體更有效率、如何選擇所涉及的關鍵參數，以及如何針對具體的約束PDE找到有效的非精確投影算子。更重要的是，這些方法的理論基礎，特別是有效非精確投影算子的建構及其全域收斂行為，仍然發展不足。 本計畫將努力理解並研究這些基本問題，並建立IPPGD方法的理論基礎。我們的貢獻有三方面。第一，我們引入了一個建構非精確投影算子的新框架。第二，我們透過一種新的非梯度流來對IPPGD演算法進行建模；其離散化不僅還原了原始方法，而且產生了一種新的加速變體。第三，我們引入一些新穎且適當加權的Lyapunov泛函，以便在連續層面建立指數收斂性，並在離散層面建立這些方法的線性收斂性。我們將透過一類重要的帶約束非線性PDEs來展示我們的新穎收斂性理論，並透過數值實驗和收斂理論進一步改進這些方法。最終，這項工作強調非精確投影和有效預處理子的設計至關重要，我們將提出一些高效且可靠的建構策略，並透過各種帶約束非線性PDEs數值驗證其有效性與穩定性。

14311926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14311926.value: 平均曲率和外蘊幾何中的質量概念

14311926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14311926.value: In this project, the PI proposes to investigate the relation between mean curvature and various notions of mass in extrinsic geometry that are motivated by the concept of mass in general relativity. Since the celebrated work of Schoen-Yau in the resolution of the positive mass conjecture, it is well known that minimal surfaces and mean curvature play an essential role in the study of scalar curvature and other mathematical problems arising in general relativity. On the other hand, another very successful approach towards studying scalar curvature is the spinor method introduced by Witten. It has remained a major mystery to understand the link between these two different approaches. In the past few years, there are some recent advances which shed light on this mystery. Level-set approach based on linear and non-linear potential theory has produced new proofs of the positive mass theorem and Penrose inequality. Moreover, they are powerful enough to reflect more global information on the geometry with precise quantitative estimates. As a result, stability of positive mass theorem and Penrose inequality were obtained in the Riemannian setting. While minimal surfaces and mean curvature have been used as an indispensable tool in the study of mass in general relativity, there was an extrinsic notion of mass introduced by Huisken which can be used to study minimal surfaces and mean curvature in the context of extrinsic geometry. Although it was known in some special cases that the extrinsic mass exhibit similar properties as the notion of mass in general relativity, its refined properties as well as their quantitative relation to mean curvature remains unexplored.The main goal of this project is to initiate a systematic investigation of the extrinsic mass and apply some of the recent state-of-the-art techniques to study its quantitative relation with the geometry of mean curvature. 本項目計畫研究平均曲率與廣義相對論中啟發的外蘊幾何中各種質量概念之間的關係。自從Schoen和Yau在解決正質量猜想方面取得著名成果以來，人們已熟知極小曲面和平均曲率在研究數量曲率及廣義相對論中的其他數學問題時發揮著至關重要的作用。另一方面，Witten引入的旋量方法也是研究數量曲率的有效方法。然而，這兩種不同方法之間的聯繫仍是一個重大未解之謎。 近年來的一些新進展為這一謎團提供了更多的線索。基於線性和非線性位能理論的水平集合方法為正質量定理和Penrose不等式提供了新的證明。此外，這些方法功能強大，能夠透過精確的定量估計反映幾何結構的更多整體資訊。基於這些新進展，Dong和Song已經獲得了在黎曼幾何框架下正質量定理和Penrose不等式的穩定性結果。 儘管極小曲面和平均曲率已成為研究廣義相對論中質量問題的不可或缺的工具，但Huisken引入了一種可用於在外蘊幾何的質量概念。雖然目前已知在某些特殊情況下，這種新的外蘊質量表現出與廣義相對論中的經典質量相似的性質，但我們對其更精細性質的研究，以及與平均曲率之間定量關係的研究，目前尚屬空白。本計畫的主要目標是對這種外​​蘊質量展開系統性研究，並應用一些前沿技術來探討其與平均曲率幾何性質之間的定量關係。

14500226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14500226.value: 美國證監會調查的非預期後果：來自基層員工流動的證據

14500226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14500226.value: This proposal investigates whether confidential Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) investigations result in higher turnover among rank-and-file employees. SEC investigations are intended to be confidential to minimize the potential negative impact on firms because most of the investigations do not result in enforcements (Blackburne et al., 2021). However, even without public disclosure, the ongoing investigations can generate signals, through document holds, data preservation, employee interviews, subpoenas, and internal probes, that affect rank-and-file employees’ perceived job insecurity and uncertainty Anticipating that potential enforcement could harm their compensation or career prospects (Choi et al., 2023), these employees may accelerate exit decisions despite having less information than senior managers about the investigation’s scope and likely outcome. Consequently, the combination of heightened risk perceptions and informational disadvantage can increase voluntary departures of rank-and-file employees during the investigative period. We measure rank-and-file turnover using individual LinkedIn profiles and identify SEC investigations from Blackburne et al. (2021). We use a stacked difference-in-differences design comparing firms that enter investigation with matched non-investigated firms, including firm-cohort and year-cohort fixed effects. To isolate scrutiny from misconduct, we exclude cases that culminate in enforcement or coincide with restatements, internal control weaknesses, or voluntary disclosures. We have the following predictions. First, investigations increase rank-and-file turnover. Second, the effects are concentrated among headquarters employees and in administration and finance, where information exposure is greater. In contrast, there should be no comparable increase in sales and marketing employees. Third, the effects are stronger among entry- and junior-level workers due to lower switching costs and weaker firm-specific capital. In addition, if employees expect potential enforcement to harm their reputations, compensation, or advancement prospects, they may accelerate their departure and shorten their search horizon, which increases the likelihood of accepting offers with weaker progression or employer visibility. Therefore, we predict that these employees are more likely to join private firms and to accept roles that are less prestige relative to their pre departure positions. This project makes several contributions. First, it documents a labor market effect of non-public regulatory scrutiny, adding to evidence on the costs and externalities of SEC investigations. It also demonstrates mechanisms linking SEC scrutiny to human-capital reallocation. In addition, it extends labor-market research beyond ex post enforcement by showing that turnover can arise in anticipatory settings, not only following fraud or restatements. It also provides policy implications that regulators should account for human-capital consequence even for confidential investigations. 本研究計畫探討美國證監會的保密調查是否會導致基層員工出現較高的離職率。美國證監會調查原則上採取保密方式進行，旨在盡量降低對公司可能造成的負面影響，因為大多數調查最終並不會導致執法行動（Blackburne 等人，2021）。然而，即使未向公眾揭露，進行中的調查仍可能透過文件保全通知、資料保存、員工訪談、傳票及內部調查等途徑釋放訊號，進而影響基層員工對工作不安全感與不確定性的認知。基層員工可能預期潛在的執法行動將損害其薪酬或職涯前景，因而加快離職決策；儘管相較於高階管理人員，他們對調查範圍及可能結果所掌握的資訊較少。因此，在調查期間，風險感知升高與資訊劣勢的結合，可能增加基層員工自願離職的情況。 我們使用個人職業社群網站檔案衡量基層員工流動。我們採用堆疊式雙重差分法，將進入調查的公司與配對的未受調查公司進行比較，並納入公司—隊列及年度—隊列固定效果。為將監管審查的影響與實際不當行為區分開來，我們排除最終導致執法行動的案件，以及與財務報表重編、內部控制重大缺失或自願揭露同時發生的案件。 我們提出以下預測。第一，美國證監會調查會提高基層員工的離職率。第二，該影響將主要集中於總部員工，以及行政與財務職能員工，因為這些員工接觸相關資訊的機會較高。相對地，業務與行銷員工的離職率不應出現可比的上升。第三，由於轉職成本較低、公司特定人力資本較弱，該影響在初階與初級職位員工之中將更為顯著。 此外，若員工預期潛在執法行動將損害其聲譽、薪酬或晉升前景，他們可能加快離職步伐並縮短求職期間，從而提高接受職涯發展性或雇主知名度較弱之工作機會的可能性。因此，我們預測，這些員工更可能轉往私人公司，並接受相較於離職前職位聲望較低的職務。 本研究計畫有數項貢獻。第一，本研究記錄非公開監管審查對勞動市場的影響，補充有關美國證監會調查成本與外部性的證據。第二，本研究揭示美國證監會審查影響人力資本重新配置的可能機制。此外，本研究將勞動市場文獻延伸至事前預期的情境，說明員工流動不僅會發生於詐欺或財務報表重編之後，也可能在潛在違規遭執法前便已出現。最後，本研究亦具有政策意涵：監管機關即使在進行保密調查時，也應考量其可能帶來的人力資本後果。

14500326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14500326.value: 生成式金融時間序列：學會「演奏」市場的旋律

14500326.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14500326.value: Prof Ma, Ding Prof Saunders, Michael

14500326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14500326.value: Recent advances in generative AI, particularly diffusion models from image synthesis, offer a new approach to a core challenge in quantitative finance: creating synthetic market data that embeds the economic logic of asset co-movement. A key challenge in this domain is capturing the market’s systemic structure. We introduce a novel diffusion model designed to learn this structure by explicitly modeling the cross-sectional dependencies among assets. We test the economic value of our approach by using synthetic data from our model to augment the training of a quantitative portfolio construction strategy. This data augmentation leads to portfolios with substantially improved out-of-sample performance, delivering significant gains in Sharpe Ratio and information coefficient over multiple benchmarks.
