Our findings suggest that generated data containing learned economic structure provides new, valuable information for asset allocation. 最近在生成式人工智慧方面的進展，特別是從圖像生成領域的擴散模型，為定量金融中的核心挑戰提供了一種新的解決方法：建立嵌入資產共同變化經濟邏輯的合成市場數據。這一領域的一個關鍵挑戰是捕捉市場的系統性結構。我們引入了一種新穎的擴散模型，透過顯式建模資產之間的橫截面依賴關係來學習市場結構。我們透過使用模型生成的合成數據增強定量投資組合建構策略的訓練來測試我們方法的經濟價值。這種生成的數據可以顯著改善投資組合的樣本外表現，該方法對理解金融市場提供了理論和實踐上的全新視角。

14500526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14500526.value: 閉門背後：股東行動主義中私下和解的驅動因素與後果

14500526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14500526.value: This research project investigates the dynamics of private settlements between activist investors and corporate boards, a critical but understudied mechanism in corporate governance. While existing literature has focused on public activist campaigns and their outcomes, the recent and significant shift toward private negotiations has been largely overlooked. This project aims to fill this gap by exploring the drivers and consequences of these discreet settlements, which leave shareholders out of the negotiation process. The study constructs a comprehensive dataset of activist campaigns from 2000 to 2024, expanding on prior work to hand-collect details on settlement types and terms. By leveraging exogenous shocks to directors’ job insecurity—specifically the staggered adoption of Majority Voting laws and the introduction of the Universal Proxy Rule—the research empirically tests whether boards are increasingly opting for private settlements to mitigate career and reputational risks. The project will test two primary predictions rooted in established theories: first, that the likelihood of a private settlement increases with the activist's “credible threat” of winning a proxy fight; and second, that this likelihood also rises when incumbent directors face higher "reputational costs" from a public battle. A Differences-in-Differences (DiD) methodology will be employed to identify causal effects and examine subsequent outcomes on board composition, CEO turnover, and firm performance. Ultimately, this study aims to illuminate the “black box” of how activists achieve their goals outside of public view. The findings will contribute significantly to the discourse on corporate governance by assessing whether private settlements serve as a valuable risk-mitigation tool for directors or a mechanism that sidesteps shareholder accountability, with important implications for investors, regulators, and corporate boards. 本研究項目探討了激進投資者與公司董事會之間私下和解的動態，旨在填補現有文獻多聚焦於公開活動而忽視近期向私人談判重大轉變的研究空白。為揭開激進投資者如何在公眾視野外達成目標的「黑箱」，本研究構建了一個涵蓋2000年至2024年激進投資者活動的新穎手工收集數據集，專門識別並分類私下與公開和解及其詳細條款。透過利用多數決投票法的交錯採用與通用委託書規則引入等對董事工作不安全感造成的外生衝擊，本研究採用雙重差分法（DiD）框架，實證檢驗董事會是否為減輕職業與聲譽風險而日益傾向選擇私下和解。具體而言，本項目測試了私下和解可能性會隨激進投資者贏得委託書爭奪戰的「可信威脅」以及現任董事面臨的「聲譽成本」增加而上升的假設。此外，本研究進一步分析了私下和解對公司治理與企業層面結果的因果影響，包括董事會組成的變化（如擴編與替換）、執行長更替、董事會獨立性、股東派息、收購活動以及長期營運績效（如資產報酬率與托賓Q值）。這些發現將評估私下和解究竟是董事有價值的風險緩解工具，還是規避股東問責的機制，從而為投資者、監管機構與公司董事會提供具備重大意義的公司治理見解。

14500826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14500826.value: 並非總是技術的錯：基於歸因視角的語音用戶界面對任務失敗的解釋

14500826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14500826.value: Voice user interfaces (VUIs), empowered by artificial intelligence (AI), have become a central gateway to smart products in the AI era. However, unlike traditional technological artifacts designed for well-defined task domains, users are often unclear about the service boundaries of VUIs. As such, they may issue requests beyond these boundaries, leading to task failures. In the absence of appropriate explanations for the failures, users will question VUIs’ competence in performing future tasks, ultimately leading to their usage discontinuance. Existing literature has extensively studied the role of explanations in intelligent systems, particularly in demystifying the “black box” of systems that can accomplish user tasks. However, it has yet to examine how explanations for task failures should be provided and what effects they may have on user perceptions. This project aims to investigate the effects of a VUI’s explanations for task failures on users’ competence belief in the VUI. Drawing on attribution theory and the theoretical lens of psychological contract violation (PCV), it examines how explanations across different locus attributions—VUI vs. non-VUI attributions (user or environment)—influence users’ competence belief differently. Furthermore, when comparing the effects of explanations with different attributions (especially VUI vs. users), this project considers the contingent role of failure stability. Specifically, for failures with stable causes, users are likely to resist explanations that attribute the failures to themselves, leading to lower effectiveness compared to explanations that attribute the failures to VUIs. To test the hypotheses, the PI will develop an apologetic response framework for delivering explanations for task failures and employ multi-phase experimental designs to collect data. First, an online experiment will be conducted, followed by a laboratory experiment to capture participants’ think-aloud verbal protocols to validate the theoretical arguments supporting the hypotheses. Second, the PI will collaborate with a company to conduct a field experiment, validating the findings in real-world VUI scenarios and exploring further research areas. This project serves as an initial endeavor in investigating how AI systems—VUIs, in particular—should explain task failures. It will contribute to the IS literature by extending system-provided explanations into an unexplored area of explanations for task failures. By examining the role of attribution and failure stability in shaping the effectiveness of explanations, it will offer valuable insights for designing VUIs for smart products that can foster satisfying and trustworthy user interactions over the long term. 語音用戶界面（VUI），在人工智慧（AI）的助力下，已經成為 AI 時代智能產品的主要入口。不過，與特定任務領域設計的傳統科技產品不同，使用者通常不太清楚 VUI 的服務範圍。因此，用戶可能會提出超出服務範圍的請求，導致任務失敗。如果對失敗沒有適當的解釋，使用者就會質疑 VUI 完成未來任務的能力，最終可能停止使用。既有研究已經廣泛探討了解釋在智能系統中的角色，特別是在揭開能完成使用者任務的系統「黑箱」時。然而，目前還沒有研究探討應該如何對任務失敗提供解釋，以及這些解釋可能對使用者感知產生什麼影響。 本研究的目標關注VUI對任務失敗的解釋如何影響使用者對VUI的能力判斷。我們會運用歸因理論以及心理契約違反（PCV）的理論視角，探討不同歸因來源的解釋—VUI 歸因 vs. 非 VUI 歸因（使用者或環境）—如何對使用者的VUI能力判斷產生不同影響。此外，當比較不同歸因（尤其是 VUI vs. 使用者）的解釋效果時，本研究也會考慮失敗穩定性所扮演的影響。具體來說，對於原因穩定的失敗，使用者通常會抗拒將失敗歸因於自己的解釋，因此這類解釋的效果會比將失敗歸因於 VUI 的解釋差。 為了驗證這些假設，我們將開發道歉式回應框架，用以提供任務失敗的解釋，並採用多階段的實驗設計來收集數據。首先，我們會進行線上實驗，之後再進行實驗室實驗並捕捉參與者的即時口述思考協定，以驗證支持假設的理論論點。接著，我們將與一家公司合作進行實地實驗，在真實的VUI場景中驗證研究結果。 這個項目作為最初的嘗試，旨在研究人工智能系統—特別是語音使用者介面—應如何解釋任務失敗。它將透過將系統提供的解釋延伸至尚未探索的任務失敗解釋領域，為資訊系統文獻做出貢獻。透過研究歸因與失敗穩定性在塑造解釋有效性中的角色，將為設計智慧產品的語音使用者介面提供寶貴的見解。透過檢視歸因和失敗穩定性在解釋效果上的作用，它將為設計智能產品的語音用戶介面提供見解，幫助建立令人滿意且值得信賴的VUI與使用者的互動。

14500926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14500926.value: CPA資深會員身份的網絡效應

14500926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14500926.value: Professional recognition programs serve as crucial quality signals in expert service markets, yet their network-level effects remain unexplored. This study examines how the Chinese CPA Fellowship designation—the highest professional honor awarded by the Chinese Institute of Certified Public Accountants (CICPA)—influences collaborative networks among auditors and creates audit quality spillovers. Using comprehensive Chinese audit data (2008-2025) and advanced social network analysis, we propose to investigate whether professional recognition creates "positive contagion" effects through auditor networks. Our research advances the examination of network-level consequences of professional recognition, contrasting with existing literature that focuses primarily on individual-level effects. China's audit market provides an ideal setting due to unique institutional features that facilitate collaborative networks among individual CPAs. Since the early 1990s, Chinese regulations have mandated that individual CPAs sign audit reports, creating direct accountability and visibility for each auditor. Additionally, audit reports issued to public companies must be co-signed by two CPAs, enabling us to effectively map the networks among these professionals. The CICPA established the Fellow CPA program in 2008, with the first batch of 684 senior members announced in December 2010, providing a clear timeline for empirical analysis. Subsequent batches have been periodically recognized, further shaping the collaborative networks among auditors and enhancing audit practices. We employ a difference-in-differences research design exploiting the staggered timing of fellowship designations, combined with social network analysis to map collaborative relationships among CPAs. Our methodology includes network centrality measures, spillover effect analysis, and robustness tests using alternative network definitions. Expected findings include evidence that CPA Fellowship designation leads to expansion of collaborative networks for designated auditors, with audit quality improvements spilling over from Fellow CPAs to their network partners. The study provides novel insights into how professional bodies can leverage recognition programs to create system-wide quality improvements through network effects. Our research contributes to audit quality literature by introducing network-level analysis of professional recognition effects, offers practical insights for professional bodies designing recognition programs, and informs regulatory policy on audit quality improvement mechanisms. The findings have implications for audit regulation and professional development policies across multiple jurisdictions. 專業認可計劃在專家服務市場中扮演著重要的品質訊號角色，然而，其在網絡層面的影響仍有待探索。本研究考察中國註冊會計師資深會員資格——由中國註冊會計師協會授予的最高專業榮譽——如何影響審計師之間的合作網絡，並產生審計品質的溢出效應。 本研究使用中國審計市場的全面數據，涵蓋2008年至2025年，並結合先進的社會網絡分析方法，擬探討專業認可是如何透過審計師網絡產生「正向傳染」效應。本研究推進了對專業認可在網絡層面後果的考察，並與現有主要聚焦於個體層面影響的文獻形成對比。 中國審計市場因其獨特的制度特徵，為研究個體註冊會計師之間的合作網絡提供了理想情境。自1990年代初以來，中國相關法規要求個體註冊會計師在審計報告上簽字，從而為每位審計師建立了直接問責機制與可見度。此外，上市公司審計報告必須由兩名註冊會計師共同簽署，使我們能夠有效描繪這些專業人士之間的合作網絡。中國註冊會計師協會於2008年設立資深會員制度，並於2010年12月公布首批684名資深會員，為實證分析提供了清晰的時間軸。此後，後續批次的資深會員亦定期獲得認可，進一步塑造了審計師之間的合作網絡，並促進審計實務的提升。 本研究採用雙重差分研究設計，利用資深會員資格授予時間的錯位性，並結合社會網絡分析方法，以描繪註冊會計師之間的合作關係。研究方法包括網絡中心性指標、溢出效應分析，以及使用替代性網絡定義進行的穩健性檢驗。 預期研究結果將顯示，CPA資深會員資格的授予會促使獲認可審計師的合作網絡擴展，而審計品質的提升也會由資深會員註冊會計師向其網絡合作夥伴產生溢出效應。本研究為理解專業機構如何透過認可計劃，借助網絡效應推動系統層面的品質提升，提供了新的見解。 本研究透過引入專業認可效應的網絡層面分析，對審計品質文獻作出貢獻；同時，為專業機構設計認可計劃提供實務啟示，並為審計品質提升機制的監管政策提供參考。本研究結果對多個司法管轄區的審計監管與專業發展政策均具有啟示意義。

14501626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14501626.value: 網路化系統的高效蒙地卡羅方法

14501626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14501626.value: This research aims to develop efficient Monte Carlo methods for estimating risk in networked systems. Modern complex systems, such as financial systems, distribution networks, and supply chains, are fundamentally highly interconnected. Consequently, the distress of a single component can trigger a cascade of widespread, systemic failures. Quantifying risk in these networks is critical; however, standard numerical techniques, particularly crude Monte Carlo simulation, are often too computationally demanding to capture such rare but catastrophic events. While advanced rare-event simulation techniques exist, they are ill-suited for these networked systems, confronting three significant challenges: (1) they fail to handle complex, higher-order network effects; (2) they exhibit poor scalability as networks grow; and (3) they rely on oversimplified models, thereby limiting their applicability to a broad class of real-world systems. To overcome these limitations, this research introduces a novel Monte Carlo method founded on a critical innovation: a reformulation of an individual component's distress condition that effectively decouples it from the network's complex fixed-point dynamics. This approach enables a highly efficient, bi-level sampling estimator, which functions by first sampling the perturbations in the other components and subsequently evaluating the failure of the target component in the second stage. We have found that even without optimizing it, this estimator is both scalable (with computational complexity that grows only linearly with network size) and flexible (accommodating non-linear network models that more accurately represent real-world systems). This project is thus dedicated to the optimal design of this estimator to achieve significant variance reduction and will mathematically prove its accuracy and efficiency, which is expected to establish a new theoretical framework for rare-event simulation in complex networks. The proposed method will subsequently be applied to several important practical problems, including pricing bonds in financial networks, assessing failure risks in distribution networks, and estimating default probabilities in supply chains. Ultimately, this research will deliver a powerful and practical simulation tool for robust risk quantification in networked systems and provide critical insights across these domains. 本研究旨在開發高效的蒙地卡羅方法，用於評估網路化系統中的風險。現代複雜系統（如金融系統、配送網路與供應鏈）在本質上具有高度的互聯性。因此，單一元件的困境可能會引發廣泛的系統性連鎖失效。量化這些網路中的風險至關重要；然而，標準的數值技術（特別是原始蒙地卡羅模擬）往往計算量過大，難以捕捉此類罕見但具有災難性的事件。 儘管目前存在先進的稀有事件模擬技術，但它們並不適用於此類網路化系統，面臨三大嚴峻挑戰：（1）無法處理高階複雜的網路效應；（2）隨著網路規模的擴大，可擴展性較差；（3）過度依賴過於簡化的模型，從而限制了其在廣泛現實系統中的適用性。 為克服這些局限，本研究提出了一種全新的蒙地卡羅方法，其核心創新在於：重新表述單一元件的困境條件，從而有效地將其與網路複雜的不動點動力學解耦。該方法實現了一個高效的雙層採樣估計器，其工作原理是：第一階段對其他元件的擾動進行採樣，第二階段評估目標元件的失效情況。我們發現，即使在未經優化的情況下，該估計器也兼具可擴展性（計算複雜度僅隨網路規模線性增長）與靈活性（能夠容納更準確表徵現實系統的非線性網路模型）。 因此，本計畫致力於對該估計器進行優化設計，以實現顯著的變異數縮減，並將從數學上證明其準確性與高效性，這有望為複雜網路中的稀有事件模擬建立全新的理論框架。隨後，所提出的方法將被應用於若干重要的實際問題，包括金融網路中的債券定價、配送網路中的失效風險評估以及供應鏈中的違約機率估計。最終，本研究將為網路化系統的強健風險量化提供強有力的實用模擬工具，並在相關領域提供關鍵洞見。

14501826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14501826.value: 計量經濟學模型的在線機器學習

14501826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14501826.value: In today's data-driven world, machine learning and artificial intelligence (AI) are transforming economics, finance, and business by analyzing vast amount of information to uncover patterns and insights. However, traditional offline methods, where models are re-trained from scratch each time new data arrives, become computationally expensive and slow, especially with time series data like stock prices or economic forecasts, or large panel datasets tracking multiple entities over time. This research proposes developing online learning techniques for econometrics, allowing models to update incrementally as new data streams in, without re-processing everything. This makes computation faster and more scalable for big data. The research narrows down to two specific models. First, online empirical likelihood handles economic models defined by moment conditions. Instead of cumbersome full re-training, we can use stochastic gradient descent—a simple update rule common in AI—to refine estimates with each new observation. The approach can be consistent and efficient, even with high-dimensional data or time dependency. Second, the panel data interactive Fixed effects (IFE) model accounts for hidden variations across entities and periods. Viewed as a basic neural network, it updates the embeddings for individuals and time points incrementally. We intend to show via asymptotic theory that the panel IFE models converge reliably, and use simulations to demonstrate its speed gains. 在當今數據驅動的世界中，機器學習和人工智能正透過分析海量資訊、揭示其中的洞見，深刻改變着經濟學、金融學和商業實踐。然而，傳統的離線學習方法——即每當新數據到來時便從頭重新訓練模型——運算成本高昂且速度緩慢，在處理股票價格、經濟預測等時間序列數據，或追蹤多個個體隨時間變化的大型面板數據集時，這一問題尤為突出。 本研究提出為計量經濟學開發在線機器學習技術，使模型能夠隨着新數據的流入進行增量式更新，而無需重新處理全部歷史數據。這不僅加快了運算速度，也使方法在大數據場景下更具擴展性。研究具體聚焦於兩類模型。其一是在線經驗似然方法，用於處理由矩條件定義的經濟模型。我們無需進行繁瑣的全量重訓練，而是可以借助隨機梯度下降，利用每一個新觀測值逐步更新估計結果。即使面對高維數據或存在時間依賴性的情形，該方法仍可保持一致性與有效性。其二是面板數據交互固定效應模型，該模型刻畫了不同個體與不同時期之間隱藏的變異。若將其視為一個基礎神經網絡，則個體與時間點的嵌入向量均可實現增量式更新。我們擬透過漸近理論證明面板模型的收斂性，並借助模擬實驗展示其在運算速度上的顯著提升。

14501926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14501926.value: 溫室氣體排放目標對家庭消費的影響：預防性儲蓄渠道與已實現風險渠道

14501926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14501926.value: Amid escalating climate risks, 24 U.S. states and the District of Columbia have enacted legally binding greenhouse gas (GHG) emission targets. While these climate regulations are essential, they may have an unintended effect on the real economy. This project explores whether these GHG targets reduce spending by households in high-carbon industries, where workers face potential job losses or pay cuts. We aim to quantify the magnitude of these effects and uncover the underlying mechanisms. We propose two channels: a precautionary saving channel, where target announcements immediately trigger precautionary savings due to an expected future income risk, and a realized income risk channel, where actual employment and earnings decline during policy implementation. To identify the impacts of GHG targets and separate the channels, we compare households in high-emission industries to others within the same state, before and after announcements (triple-differences design). Using high-frequency home-scan spending data, we trace consumption dynamics from days to years after the announcements. This approach allows us to separate short-term reactions (within two weeks) likely driven by the precautionary saving channel from longer-term changes reflecting actual labor market impacts. Given the critical role of awareness of the announcements, we examine whether attention measures such as Google search trends and local news coverage amplify immediate consumption responses. We also analyze how effects vary by household characteristics, such as liquidity constraints, education, occupation, and industry type. Our study contributes by quantifying both the total impact of GHG targets on household spending and the relative importance of precautionary saving versus realized income risk channels. This will shed light on the magnitude and timing of the transmission from policy announcement to household spending behavior. Our study will offer profound policy implications, as our findings highlight potential unintended economic consequences of green transitions, including reduced consumer activity among affected populations. While we use U.S. policies and data for empirical identification, our insights directly apply to Hong Kong, a global financial center exposed to worldwide climate transitions. In particular, sectors like shipping, aviation, logistics, construction, and energy face similar pressures from decarbonization policies, where workers may reduce spending in response to climate regulations. By documenting how climate policies affect household consumption and identifying the underlying mechanisms, our research helps policymakers in Hong Kong and elsewhere to implement climate regulations effectively. This knowledge allows leaders to minimize economic disruption, support smoother transitions for affected workers, and maintain financial stability while pursuing net-zero goals.

14502226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14502226.value: 弱因子面板數據模型的穩健方法

14502226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14502226.value: Panel data models with interactive fixed effects (IFEs) are widely used to capture unobserved heterogeneity and cross-sectional dependence. Standard estimators such as Common Correlated Effects (CCE) and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) perform well under strong factor conditions, but often exhibit poor performance in the presence of weak factors, a common feature in empirical data. Building on recent work by Lu et al. (2025) and Feng et al. (2025), this project introduces a new estimator and inference procedure within the Generalized CCE (GCCE) framework that accommodates potentially weak factors. The proposed methods are robust across a wide range of factor strengths. Preliminary simulations demonstrate superior finite-sample performance. This project will systematically analyze their asymptotic properties, conduct Monte Carlo experiments to assess finite-sample behavior, and demonstrate their practical relevance through empirical applications. 具有交互固定效應（Interactive Fixed Effects, IFEs）的面板數據模型被廣泛用於刻畫不可觀測異質性與橫斷面相依性。常用的估計方法，如共同相關效應（Common Correlated Effects, CCE）與主成分分析（Principal Component Analysis, PCA），在強因子條件下表現良好，但在存在弱因子的情況下往往表現欠佳，而弱因子是實證數據中的常見特徵。基於 Lu et al.（2025）與 Feng et al.（2025）的最新研究成果，本項目在廣義共同相關效應（Generalized CCE, GCCE）框架下，提出一種能夠處理潛在弱因子的全新估計及推論方法。所提出的方法在不同因子強度下均具有穩健性。初步模擬結果顯示，該方法在有限樣本下具有優異的表現。本項目將系統性分析其漸近性質，透過蒙特卡洛模擬評估其有限樣本表現，並利用實證應用展示其實際價值與應用潛力。

14502426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14502426.value: 組織懷舊表達：概念、測量和影響

14502426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14502426.value: While organizational nostalgia—a sentimental longing for an organization's past—is known to benefit the individual who feels it, we know little about the interpersonal consequences when this nostalgia is expressed to others. This research introduces the concept of expressed organizational nostalgia (EON), defined as the verbal or behavioral communication of fondness for a past experience or era within an organization. Moving beyond the prevailing "expresser-centric" view, we adopt an audience-centric perspective to investigate how coworkers perceive and react to EON. We propose a theoretical model identifying two distinct forms of EON—group-centered and self-centered—and their distinct interpersonal threats. We argue that group-centered EON (longing for past teams/events) can threaten a coworker's sense of group identity continuity, especially when expressed by someone with a high temporal categorization tendency (a tendency to categorize colleagues by tenure). This threat, in turn, reduces organizational citizenship behaviors directed at the organization (OCB-O). Conversely, self-centered EON (longing for one's personal journey) can provoke a status threat in coworkers, particularly when the coworker perceives their own recent career trajectory as more favorable than the expressor's (a favorable temporal social comparison). This status threat subsequently reduces citizenship behaviors directed at the individual expressor (OCB-I). This research will test this model through a multi-method program of three studies: an online experiment to establish causality, a scale development study to create a measure for EON, and a multi-wave, multi-source field survey to validate the hypotheses in a real-world setting. By uncovering the "dark side" of expressed nostalgia and its boundary conditions, this research provides a critical theoretical extension to the nostalgia literature and offers practical guidance for employees on how to share nostalgic reflections without causing unintended interpersonal friction. 雖然組織懷舊——對組織過往的一種感傷性眷戀——已知能為懷有這種情感的個人帶來益處，但對於這種懷舊在向他人表達時所產生的人際後果，我們所知甚少。本研究引入「組織懷舊表達」（EON）這個概念，定義為以口頭或行為方式傳達對組織內過往經歷或時代的喜愛。有別於當前主流「表達者中心」的觀點，我們採納「受眾中心」的視角，來探討同事如何感知及回應組織懷舊表達。 我們提出一個理論模型，辨別出兩種不同形式的組織懷舊表達——群體中心型與自我中心型——及其各自獨特的人際威脅。我們主張，群體中心型組織懷舊表達（對過去團隊／事件的眷戀）可能威脅同事的群體身分延續感，尤其當表達者具有高度時間分類傾向（即傾向依年資來分類同事）時更為明顯。這種威脅進而會降低指向組織的組織公民行為（OCB-O）。相反地，自我中心型組織懷舊表達（對自身個人歷程的眷戀）則可能引發同事的地位威脅，尤其當同事認知到自己近期職涯軌跡比表達者更為有利（即有利的時序性社會比較）時。這種地位威脅隨後會減少指向個別表達者的公民行為（OCB-I）。 本研究將透過三項研究組成的多重方法方案來檢驗此模型：一項線上實驗以確立因果關係，一項量表發展研究以建立表達性組織懷舊的測量工具，以及一項多波次、多來源的實地調查，以在真實場域中驗證各項假設。透過揭示表達性懷舊的「黑暗面」及其邊界條件，本研究為懷舊文獻提供了關鍵的理論延伸，並為員工如何分享懷舊反思而不致引發非預期的人際摩擦，提供實務上的指引。

14503226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14503226.value: 資訊通信技術（ICT）對知識生產和傳播的影響：來自非洲海底電纜部署的證據

14503226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14503226.value: The production and diffusion of scientific knowledge are fundamental drivers of innovation and long-run economic growth. The development in information and communication technologies (ICT) has a profound impact on the economy and society by minimizing information frictions. This project examines the effects of ICT development on the production and diffusion of scientific knowledge, as measured by the publication and citation of scientific research papers. A key challenge in establishing a causal link is the problem of endogeneity. The development of ICT is closely tied to local economic and technological conditions. We utilize the arrival of fast internet connections in Africa through submarine cables as a natural experiment. Africa had lagged behind in digital access for much of the 20th century; however, it experienced dramatic connectivity improvements in the late 2000s and early 2010s with the deployment of fiber-optic submarine cables. In this project, we take advantage of the staggered arrival of these cables to investigate their effects on knowledge production and diffusion across three dimensions. First, we analyze whether better internet access increased the number of research papers published by African institutions. Second, we study changes in collaboration and citation patterns, focusing on whether African researchers collaborate more globally and whether they cite more works from other continents. Third, we look at how quickly African scientists cite global work. To achieve this, the project will construct a robust institution–year panel dataset from OpenAlex publication records and TeleGeography’s submarine cable data. The data is organized to capture institutions’ proximity to both submarine cable landing points and national terrestrial backbone networks. This allows for precise identification of treatment effects using the difference-in-differences (DiD) framework. Key variables include publication counts, intercontinental co-authorship patterns, the flow of intercontinental citations, and the timeliness of citations. This research will fill gaps in the literature regarding the role of ICT in advancing scientific systems in developing regions. Its findings will inform policymakers and development agencies, underscoring the importance of connectivity not only in promoting economic efficiency but also in accelerating scientific progress. This is particularly relevant for regions like Africa, which have historically encountered substantial connectivity challenges. 科學知識的生產和傳播是創新和長期經濟成長的根本驅動力。資訊通信技術（ICT）的發展透過減少資訊摩擦，對經濟和社會產生了深遠的影響。本計畫旨在研究資訊通信技術發展對科學知識生產和傳播的影響，並以科學研究論文的發表和引用量作為衡量指標。 建立因果關係的關鍵挑戰在於內生性問題。資訊通信技術的發展與當地的經濟和技術條件密切相關。我們利用海底光纜為非洲帶來高速網路連線這項自然實驗。在20世紀的大部分時間裡，非洲在數位存取方面一直落後；然而，隨著21世紀初光纖海底光纜的部署，非洲的網路連接得到了顯著改善。本專案利用這些光纜分階段部署的特點，從三個維度研究其對知識生產和傳播的影響。 首先，我們分析更便利的網路存取是否增加了非洲機構發表的科學研究論文數量。其次，我們研究合作和引用模式的變化，重點關注非洲研究人員是否在全球範圍內進行更多合作，以及他們是否引用更多來自其他大洲的文獻。第三，我們考察非洲科學家引用全球文獻的速度。 為實現這一目標，本計畫將利用OpenAlex的出版記錄和TeleGeography的海底電纜數據，建構一個穩健的機構-年份面板數據集。此資料集的組織方式旨在反映各機構與海底電纜登陸點和國家陸地骨幹網路的距離。這使得我們能夠利用雙重差分法（DiD）框架精確辨識處理效應。關鍵變數包括論文發表數量、跨洲合作模式、跨洲引用流量以及引用的時效性。 這項研究將填補現有文獻中關於資訊通信技術（ICT）在發展中地區科學體系發展中所扮演角色的空白。研究結果將為政策制定者和發展機構提供參考，強調互聯互通的重要性，它不僅有助於提高經濟效率，也能加速科學進步。這對於像非洲這樣歷史上面臨許多互聯互通挑戰的地區尤其重要。

14503426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14503426.value: 光環與陷阱：公益廣告中明星代言的神經行銷學調查

14503426.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14503426.value: Prof Chau, Ka Hung Bolton Prof Hung, Kineta Hing-kun Dr SIN, Lok Lam Emily

14503426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14503426.value: Celebrity endorsement (CE) has long been a cornerstone of commercial marketing, where admired public figures are leveraged to attract attention, build trust, and drive consumer behavior. Over time, this strategy has expanded beyond the commercial realm into the public sphere, particularly following the COVID-19 pandemic, which spurred a surge in public service announcements (PSAs) addressing urgent societal issues. Today, celebrities are frequently enlisted to raise awareness in areas such as public health, environmental sustainability, and social inclusion. The rationale is straightforward: familiar and admired spokespersons are believed to amplify message visibility and emotional resonance in an increasingly saturated media environment. Endorsement literature supports this approach, suggesting that celebrities’ reputational capital can be transferred to the causes they represent. However, this project challenges that assumption. While celebrities often command public attention, their influence in PSAs is far less certain. On the one hand, they can amplify message reach and lend social credibility; on the other, they risk distracting audiences from the core message, diluting impact through the “vampire effect”. In an era when societies urgently need effective public service communication, understanding this paradox is not only academically important but also socially critical. Building on our earlier investigation, this proposal pioneers an integrative approach to uncover how and when celebrity endorsement undermines public interest communication. By employing neuromarketing methods, this project provides a comprehensive understanding of both the attentional and neural mechanisms underlying unintended risks in celebrity-driven PSAs. Three studies are proposed. Study 1 employs eye-tracking to investigate the 'vampire effect' posed by a celebrity endorser in PSA contexts. Study 2 examines how message framing interacts with CE, specifically investigating whether negative framing exacerbates the vampire effect. Study 3 utilises fMRI to explore the neural correlates of viewing a celebrity with multiple endorsements, examining whether over-endorsement leads to distrust. The project promises three major contributions. Theoretically, it redefines the boundary conditions of the “halo versus hazard” of CE, advancing advertising and marketing communication scholarship. Methodologically, it pushes the frontier of persuasion research by triangulating behavioral, psychophysiological, and neural evidence. Practically, it delivers actionable insights for governments, NGOs, and campaign strategists who must decide whether celebrities are assets or liabilities in critical public service messaging. The outcomes will help optimize campaign strategies, ensuring that scarce public resources are invested in endorsements that truly change attitudes and behaviors, rather than in star power that merely shines on itself. 名人代言長期以來一直是商業行銷的基石，品牌透過公眾愛戴的名人吸引目光、建立信任並驅動消費者行為。隨著時間推移，此一策略已超越商業領域並擴展至公共領域；特別是在疫情之後，針對緊急社會議題的公益廣告出現爆發性成長。如今，名人常被邀請在公共衛生、環境永續和社會包容等領域提升公眾意識。其背後的邏輯相當直接：在日益飽和的媒體環境中，大眾熟悉且喜愛的代言人被認為能放大訊息的能見度與情感共鳴。 名人代言相關文獻支持這種作法，認為名人的聲譽資本可以轉移至其所代表的公益訴求上。然而，本研究計畫挑戰這一假設。儘管名人往往能吸引公眾注意力，但他們在公益廣告中的影響力卻存在極大的不確定性。一方面，他們能擴大訊息傳播範圍並賦予社會公信力；但另一方面，他們也可能帶來「吸血鬼效應」，分散受眾對核心訊息的注意力，進而稀履宣傳效果。在社會迫切需要有效公共服務溝通的時代，理解這種矛盾現象不僅具有學術重要性，更具備關鍵的社會意義。 承接我們前期的研究，本計畫開創性地採用綜合研究法，旨在揭示名人代言何時以及如何削弱公共利益溝通的效果。透過結合神經行銷學方法，本研究針對名人導向的公益廣告中所產生的非預期風險，提供對其注意力機制與神經機制的全面理解。 本計畫提出三項研究方案- 研究一： 採用眼動追蹤技術 ，探討名人代言人在公益廣告情境下所產生的「吸血鬼效應」。研究二： 檢視訊息框架與名人代言的交互作用，特別是深入調查負面框架是否會加劇吸血鬼效應。研究三： 利用功能性磁振造影探索觀看具多重代言之名人時的神經關聯，檢視過度代言是否會導致大眾的不信任。 本計畫預計帶來三項重大貢獻- 理論層面： 重新定義名人代言「光環與危害」的邊界條件，推動廣告與行銷溝通學術研究的進展。方法論層面： 透過交叉驗證行為學、心理生理學及神經學證據，拓展說服研究的前沿領域。實務層面： 為政府、非政府組織 及活動策劃者提供具操作性的洞察，協助其在關鍵的公共服務宣傳中，精準判斷名人究竟是資產還是負擔。 研究成果將有助於優化宣傳活動策略，確保稀缺的公共資源投入於真正能改變態度與行為的代言上，而非僅是照亮明星自身的星光。

14503626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14503626.value: 利用可解釋文本分析預測股票收益

14503626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14503626.value: Text data has become an important source of information in finance. It contains rich content that reflects both the current state of financial assets and expectations about future investment opportunities. However, the natural property of high dimensionality embedded in text data makes it challenging to extract precise and relevant signals when filtering out useless information. The typical method to extract textual information is to transform text data either into sentiment features representing emotional polarity (e.g., sentiment scores), or into low-dimensional semantic vectors using pretrained language models (e.g., FinBERT). These extracted features are then used to model their relationship with various targets in finance such as stock returns, investors’ trading behavior, and companies’ investment decisions. However, the traditional approaches have notable shortcomings: the model is lack of interpretability. For example, word vectorization is an effective way for semantic representation, but the process of mapping an article to a numerical vector is inherently opaque and not clear what the vector actually signifies. This lack of interpretability is particularly problematic in the context of implications in finance, where understanding how such text data affects the predictive outcome is crucial. Without interpretability, it becomes difficult to assess the reliability of the model’s predictions and trust the implications based on it. To address this limitation, in this project we explore an alternative approach beyond traditional semantic representations: structured event representations (SER). Our key innovation lies in using large language models (LLMs) not merely as embedding tools but as controllable extractors that identify key events from unstructured text data via a carefully designed prompt. To illustrate, we apply LLMs to transfer all sentences in an article to event triplets (i.e., subject+action+object) and treat them as the basic features for model input. By examining these human-readable events, we can learn how they are mapped to stock returns and conduct attribution analyses for our model. We then combine SER with various LLMs to study its implications in finance. For example, we will combine SER with an attention-based deep learning model for stock return prediction and text selection. Compared with traditional word-based or embedding-based models, our SER-based model offers a flexible structure to capture heterogeneity and enhance interpretability by revealing which events are the most relevant to stock returns. By displaying SERs through a knowledge graph, our method can further identify the linkages across firms by textual information and analyze cross-stock connections and common factors. 文字資料已成為金融領域的重要資訊來源。它包含豐富的內容，既反映了金融資產的現狀，也反映了對未來投資機會的預期。然而，文字資料固有的高維度特性使得在過濾掉無用資訊的同時提取精確且相關的訊號變得極具挑戰性。提取文字資訊的常用方法是將文字資料轉換為代表情緒極性的情緒特徵，或使用預先訓練的語言模型（例如，FinBERT）將其轉換為低維語義向量。然後，利用這些提取的特徵來建模其與金融領域各種目標之間的關係，例如股票收益、投資者交易行為和公司投資決策。 然而，傳統方法存在顯著的缺陷：模型缺乏可解釋性。例如，詞向量化是一種有效的語義表示方法，但將文章映射到數值向量的過程本身是不透明的，向量的實際含義並不明確。這種可解釋性的缺失在金融領域尤其突出，因為理解此類文字資料如何影響預測結果至關重要。缺乏可解釋性，就難以評估模型預測的可靠性，也難以信任基於此的推論。 為了克服這一局限性，本計畫探討了一種超越傳統語義表示的替代方法：結構化事件表示（SER）。我們的關鍵創新在於，將大型語言模型（LLM）不僅用作嵌入工具，更用作可控的提取器，透過精心設計的提示從非結構化文字資料中識別關鍵事件。例如，我們應用LLM將文章中的所有句子轉換為事件三元組（即主詞+動作+賓語），並將其作為模型輸入的基本特徵。透過分析這些易於理解的事件，我們可以了解它們如何映射到股票收益，並對模型進行歸因分析。 然後，我們將SER與各種LLM結合，研究其在金融領域的應用。例如，我們將SER與基於注意力機制的深度學習模型結合，用於股票收益預測和文字選擇。與傳統的基於字詞或基於嵌入的模型相比，我們基於SER的模型提供了一種靈活的結構，能夠捕捉異質性，並透過揭示哪些事件與股票收益最相關來增強可解釋性。透過知識圖譜展示SER，我們的方法可以進一步利用文字資訊來識別公司間的關聯，並分析跨股票連結和共同因素。

14503726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14503726.value: 检验最低工资就业效应的地理识别策略 检验最低工资就业效应的地理识别策略 检验最低工资就业效应的地理识别策略 检验最低工资就业效应的地理识别策略

14503726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14503726.value: his project investigates the credibility of geographically based identification strategies in estimating the employment effects of minimum wage policies. A large body of empirical research has used cross-border comparisons—such as contiguous counties straddling state lines—to infer causal effects of minimum wage changes. While this approach has shaped much of the modern minimum wage debate, it faces two central challenges: (i) geographic spillovers, whereby workers or firms respond to wage differentials by commuting or relocating across borders, and (ii) economic incomparability, as nearby counties may nevertheless lie in distinct labor markets with different dynamics. The combination of these forces threatens the validity of commonly used designs and may explain why decades of research have yet to resolve even the basic question of whether minimum wages reduce, increase, or leave employment unchanged. The proposed study advances this debate by systematically testing the assumptions underpinning geographic identification. Specifically, it will quantify the extent of cross-border commuting responses to minimum wage differentials and examine whether such responses vary according to local labor market concentration. Using linked microdata from the American Community Survey, the Current Population Survey, and administrative records on establishments and wages, the project will track how workers adjust across county and commuting-zone boundaries following wage policy shifts. The analysis will combine cross-border difference-in-difference designs with within-market comparisons to higher-wage workers, and then integrate both into a triple-difference framework. This design provides a more comprehensive test of credibility by isolating policy-driven employment effects from confounding trends. The project also speaks to a broader theoretical question: how the employment elasticity of minimum wages varies across competitive versus monopsonistic labor markets. Existing evidence suggests that in competitive markets, binding minimum wages reduce employment, while in monopsonistic markets, moderate increases may raise employment up to the “full-employment wage.” By explicitly linking geographic spillovers with measures of labor market concentration, this project will provide the first direct test of how market structure mediates cross-border responses and bias in control groups. Beyond its academic contribution, the study offers practical policy relevance. Governments continue to debate the merits of regional versus national minimum wage policies, often without clear guidance on spillover effects. By clarifying when and where geographic control groups produce credible estimates, the findings will inform the design of labor market policy evaluations and provide benchmarks for policymakers considering differentiated wage floors. 14503826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14503826.value: 氣候資訊揭露與供應鏈減碳：大型企業排放外溢效應之實證研究

14503826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14503826.value: Climate disclosure regulations such as IFRS S1 and S2 are reshaping corporate environmental accountability. These mandates often require large firms to report Scope 3 emissions, encompassing upstream and downstream supply chain activities. However, beyond reporting changes, evidence on real effects remains limited. This proposal will examine how greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions practices adopted by large firms affect the environmental behavior and emissions reporting of smaller supply chain partners. Building on recent evidence that disclosure regulation and investor demand alter corporate transparency and real decisions, we argue that disclosure requirements, especially those involving Scope 3 emissions, create strong informational and operational linkages between focal firms and their suppliers. These linkages can lead to spillover effects in both reporting behavior and real emissions outcomes, as suppliers adapt to meet the data demands and sustainability expectations of their major customers. We hypothesize that climate disclosures (especially Scope 3) by powerful firms propagate along value chains, affecting smaller partners’ reporting choices, operational emissions, and financing outcomes. We outline a staggered difference-in-differences research design to explore suppliers’ GHG reporting incidence or quality, real emissions intensity, and capital market consequences. This research will contribute to both academic literature and policy debates on how transparency initiatives can drive meaningful decarbonization rather than mere compliance. IFRS S1 與 S2 等氣候揭露準則的推出，正大幅提升企業環境資訊透明度的要求。其中，範疇三排放揭露規定要求企業揭露供應鏈相關排放，使氣候資訊逐漸成為投資決策與公司治理的重要基礎。然而，氣候揭露究竟能否改變企業的實際環境績效與經濟結果，仍有待進一步驗證。 本研究聚焦於大型企業氣候揭露對供應鏈夥伴所產生的外溢效應。我們認為，當大型企業面臨氣候揭露壓力時，將透過資訊需求與業務往來影響其供應商，進而改變供應商的揭露策略、經營決策及排放行為。此一機制可能不僅影響企業的永續表現，也可能進一步影響其資金成本及投資人結構。 為驗證此假說，本研究將利用大型企業範疇三排放揭露的逐步採納作為準自然實驗，並運用分期差異中的差異法分析其對供應商揭露品質、排放強度及資本市場結果的影響。 研究成果將有助於深化會計、財務與永續發展文獻對氣候資訊揭露經濟後果的理解，並為氣候政策與企業治理提供實證依據。

14504226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14504226.value: 利用對抗性逆強化學習對遊戲玩法和遊戲內購買動態進行建模

14504226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14504226.value: Virtual environments — such as games, metaverse platforms, and gamified learning systems — continue to gain in importance both in terms of share of consumer time and money. Within these environments, players make interdependent choices about how much time to spend and when to pay, dynamically allocating time and money choices in response to the changing game states. For firms designing games and in-game interventions, this creates a high-dimensional problem: they must consider not only player states, but also how these states interact with the changing conditions of the game environment, which together create complex and potentially nonlinear feedback loops between players' play and purchase decisions. We address this challenge by developing a novel adversarial inverse reinforcement learning (AIRL) framework that recovers players’ latent reward and policy functions directly from observed behavior, rather than requiring explicit functional forms on the structural parameters. This allows the framework to handle a large number of state variables and their interactions that would be computationally infeasible in traditional dynamic structural estimation. Methodologically we extend the AIRL framework to (i) incorporate latent player heterogeneity, and (ii) establish identifiability of action-dependent utilities through an absorbing action (exit) that preserves structural interpretation for counterfactual analysis. We apply this framework to a large-scale dataset from a mobile golf game covering a 15-month period of around one million play records, comprising every player action and state in the game environment. Model-free analysis suggests different purchase behavior across durable and consumable tools. Durables are purchased midway through each level, as players approach level-up thresholds, consistent with forward-looking behavior, whereas consumables are purchased immediately after leveling up, reflecting more myopic responses to sudden increases in difficulty. Using the model, we conduct counterfactual analysis to design personalized interventions -- such as adaptive difficulty adjustments and targeted timing of product discounts or offerings (e.g., when to discount durables versus consumables) -- to maximize player monetization. In Hong Kong and beyond, the video game industry continue to gain in importance, with its market size projected to reach US $1.8 billion in Hong Kong by 2027. This research provides a scalable and interpretable framework for modeling consumer decision-making in virtual environments. Beyond gaming, our framework generalizes to other digital contexts — such as online learning and health— where user engagement and monetary investment decisions dynamically interact. Methodologically, we contribute to the rapidly growing literature linking dynamic discrete choice models and inverse reinforcement learning. 虛擬環境——例如遊戲, 元宇宙平台和遊戲化學習系統——在消費者的時間和金錢佔比方面持續成長. 在這些環境中, 玩家需要做出相互關聯的選擇, 決定投入多少時間和何時付費, 並根據不斷變化的遊戲狀態動態地分配時間和金錢. 對於設計遊戲和遊戲內幹預措施的公司而言, 這帶來了一個高維度問題: 他們不僅要考慮玩家狀態, 還要考慮這些狀態如何與不斷變化的遊戲環境條件相互作用, 從而在玩家的遊戲和購買決策之間形成複雜且可能非線性的反饋迴路. 為了應對這項挑戰, 我們開發了一種新穎的對抗性逆強化學習 框架, 該框架直接從觀察到的行為中恢復玩家的潛在獎勵和策略函數, 而無需明確地定義結構參數的函數形式. 這使得該框架能夠處理大量狀態變數及其交互作用, 而這些在傳統的動態結構估計中是計算上不可行且難以處理的. 在方法論上, 我們擴展了AIRL框架, 以（i）納入潛在的玩家異質性, 以及（ii）透過吸收動作（退出）建立與動作相關的效用可識別性, 從而保留反事實分析的結構解釋. 我們將此框架應用於一個來自行動高爾夫遊戲的大規模資料集, 該資料集涵蓋了15個月期間約一百萬筆遊戲記錄, 包含了遊戲環境中玩家的每一個動作和狀態. 無模型分析表明, 玩家在耐用品和消耗品上的購買行為存在差異. 耐用品通常在每關中途購買, 此時玩家接近升級閾值, 這與前瞻性行為一致; 而消耗品則在升級後立即購買, 反映了玩家對難度突然增加的短視反應. 利用該模型, 我們進行反事實分析, 以設計個人化幹預措施——例如自適應難度調整和有針對性的產品折扣或優惠時機（例如, 何時對耐用品和消耗品進行折扣）——從而最大限度地提高玩家的盈利能力. 在香港及其他地區, 電子遊戲產業的重要性持續提升, 預計到2027年, 香港的電子遊戲市場規模將達到18億美元. 本研究提供了一個可擴展且易於解釋的框架, 用於模擬虛擬環境中的消費者決策. 除了遊戲領域, 我們的框架還可推廣到其他數位場景, 例如線上學習和健康領域, 在這些領域中, 用戶參與度和資金投入決策之間存在動態的交互作用. 在方法論方面, 我們為快速發展的動態離散選擇模型與逆強化學習相結合的文獻做出了貢獻.

14504526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14504526.value: 金融欺詐、財政壓力和中小企業稅收

14504526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14504526.value: Many prior studies explore corporate tax behaviour for large firms. In this study, we focus on tax behaviour of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), which are economically important yet understudied in the literature. Given that SMEs tend to be young, small, and less resilient than large firms, excessive tax burdens may impair their long-term survival and success. Thus, policymakers face a balancing act to collect legally owned tax revenues from SMEs to finance public services, and at the same time avoid imposing excessive tax burdens that impede SMEs’ growth. In this study, we manually collect the transaction-level data for a large sample of SMEs in China by using the invoice records provided by a fintech firm. We then use financial fraud revelations at listed firms as an exogenous shock to local government fiscal pressure since fraud reduces future tax contributions from the fraudulent firms due to the deterioration of future performance of fraudulent firms. We next examine whether there is lower tax avoidance for SMEs following fraud revelations due to stricter tax enforcement by local officials. Furthermore, we would like to assess the real‐economic impact of the increased tax burdens on SMEs’s future growth by analysing subsequent changes in SMEs’ revenues, employment levels, and capital investment. This study will make several implications. First, we fill the literature gap by examining tax avoidance behaviour of SMEs. Second, we build the link from fraud‐induced fiscal pressure to the changes in tax behaviour of SMEs. Third, we provide evidence into the real effects of stricter tax enforcement on the future performance of SMEs, offering insights for policymakers to balance the tax collection and the possible adverse impact on the growth and survival of SMEs. 許多先前的研究探討了大型企業的企業納稅行爲。本研究則聚焦於中小企業的納稅行爲，中小企業在經濟中扮演着重要角色，但在相關文獻中卻鮮有研究。鑒於中小企業往往成立時間較短、規模較小且抗風險能力較弱，過重的稅負可能會損害其長期生存和發展。因此，政策制定者面臨着兩難的境地：一方面要依法向中小企業徵收稅款以資助公共服務，另一方面又要避免施加過重的稅負，從而阻礙中小企業的發展。 本研究計劃利用一家金融科技公司的相關數據，收集中國大量中小企業的交易層面數據。然後，我們研究上市公司財務欺詐事件的曝光後對地方政府財政壓力的衝擊，因爲欺詐行爲會導致涉案企業未來業績下滑，並且降低涉案企業未來的納稅額。接下來，我們考察在欺詐事件曝光後，由於地方政府加強了稅務執法，中小企業的避稅行爲是否有所減少。此外，我們希望通過分析中小企業收入、就業水平和資本投資的後續變化，評估稅負增加對中小企業未來增長的實際經濟影響。 本研究將産生以下幾個方面的影響。首先，我們通過考察中小企業的避稅行爲填補了現有文獻的空白。其次，我們建立了欺詐行爲引發的財政壓力與中小企業納稅行爲變化之間的聯繫。第三，我們提供了更嚴格的稅收執法對中小企業未來績效的實際影響的証據，爲政策制定者提供了在稅收徵管與可能對中小企業增長和生存造成的不利影響之間取得平衡的參考。

14504626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14504626.value: 非對稱模型設定錯誤的宏觀經濟學

14504626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14504626.value: Macroeconomic environment features complex interactions among various decision makers, which underscores the importance of general equilibrium (GE) effects. Consequently, the decision-making process for economic agents involves not only forming expectations about fundamentals but also considering how others form their own expectations. This, in turn, requires understanding the subjective models held by other agents. For the sake of tractability, standard macroeconomic theories often assume that models are common knowledge among agents, regardless perceived models are misspecified or not. However, in reality, such tractability assumptions rarely hold. Take, for example, the housing market. In the face of rapidly rising property prices, some individuals believe these increases reflect the market's fundamental value, while others interpret them as signs of a speculative bubble. As a result, even if both fundamentalists and bubble-believers anticipate further short-term price increases, their long-term expectations may diverge dramatically. More importantly, a fundamentalist agent cannot be certain how many other market participants share their perspective. In summary, the subjective models that guide agents' decision making are often misspecified, and the extent of this misspecification can vary asymmetrically across individuals. Empirical evidence from survey data on the expectations of firms and households confirms the existence of asymmetric model misspecification in reality. As documented by Candia, Coibion, and Gorodnichenko (2020), firms and households have differing perceptions of the slope of the Phillips curve—and neither group's perception aligns with the relationships observed in actual data. In this project, we theoretically characterize the implications of asymmetric misspecification in environments with general equilibrium (GE) effects. The absence of common knowledge regarding agents' perceived models disrupts the law of iterated expectations because of the interplay between asymmetric misspecification and GE interactions. Within the standard New Keynesian (NK) framework, when households and firms lack common knowledge about the slope of the NK Phillips curve, the optimal pricing strategies of monopolistically competitive firms violate the law of iterated expectations—a key condition for deriving the NK Phillips curve. This lack of common knowledge introduces a correlated wedge into the NK Phillips curve, which alters the transmission mechanism of structural shocks, such as productivity or monetary policy shocks. Furthermore, our project sheds light on the conduct of monetary policy. Since the correlated wedge reflects differences in agents’ perceived models, our findings underscore the importance of monitoring misspecification in the economy when designing monetary policy. 宏觀經濟環境中存在各類決策者之間複雜的互動，這突顯了一般均衡效果的重要性。因此，經濟行為者在決策時，不僅需要對基本面形成預期，也必須考量其他人如何形成其自身預期。進而，這要求他們理解其他行為者所持有的主觀模型。為了使分析易於處理，標準總體經濟理論通常假設，各行為者之間對模型具有共同知識，無論其所認知的模型是否存在錯誤設定。然而，在現實中，這類為求可處理性而設的假設鮮少成立。以房市為例，當房價快速上漲時，有些人認為漲勢反映市場的基本面價值；另一些人則將其詮釋為投機泡沫的徵兆。因此，即使基本面派與泡沫信念者都預期短期內價格會繼續上漲，兩者的長期預期仍可能大幅分歧。更重要的是，持基本面觀點的行為者無法確定，有多少其他市場參與者與其觀點相同。總而言之，引導行為者決策的主觀模型往往存在錯誤設定，而這種錯誤設定的程度可在個人之間呈現非對稱性的差異。 來自企業與家戶預期之調查資料的實證證據，證實現實中確實存在非對稱的模型錯誤設定。正如 Candia、Coibion 與 Gorodnichenko（2020）所記錄，企業與家戶對菲利普斯曲線斜率的認知不同，而且兩個群體的認知皆不符合實際資料中觀察到的關係。 本研究計畫從理論上刻畫，在具有一般均衡效果的環境中，非對稱模型錯誤設定所帶來的影響。行為者對彼此所認知模型缺乏共同知識，會因非對稱錯誤設定與一般均衡互動之間的相互作用，而破壞迭代期望法則。在標準的新凱恩斯架構中，當家戶與企業對 新凱恩斯菲利普斯曲線的斜率缺乏共同知識時，獨占性競爭企業的最適定價策略將違反迭代期望法則；而該法則正是推導新凱恩斯菲利普斯曲線的關鍵條件。這種共同知識的缺失會在新凱恩斯菲利普斯曲線中引入一個具相關性的楔子，進而改變生產力衝擊或貨幣政策衝擊等結構性衝擊的傳導機制。 此外，本研究計畫亦有助於理解貨幣政策的執行方式。由於這個具有相關性的楔子反映了行為者所認知的模型之間的差異，我們的研究結果強調：在設計貨幣政策時，監測經濟體中的模型錯誤設定至關重要。

14504726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14504726.value: 團結一致：激進做空行動對員工對CEO評價的影響

14504726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14504726.value: Activist short-selling campaigns have become increasingly prominent, presenting sudden and significant external threats to targeted firms. In this study, we examine how such short-selling activism impacts employees’ approval of their CEOs. Drawing on the “rally round the flag” effect from political science, we propose that while short-selling activism typically seeks to undermine a strategic leader’s credibility, it may also paradoxically result in increased employee approval of the CEO. This response likely stems from employees’ heightened motivation to protect and defend their organizational identity when the organization’s reputation is challenged by external actors. We further hypothesize that this effect varies depending on the degree to which the CEO is seen as a symbolic representation of the firm. Additionally, we propose that the response is influenced by the country of origin of the activist short seller and the targeted firm. To test these hypotheses, we will employ data from 2011 to 2024 on activist short-selling campaigns, using a propensity score matching–difference-in-differences (PSM-DiD) design. This study contributes to the literature on strategic leadership by demonstrating how external threats can bolster employee support for CEOs. It also advances strategic management research on short-selling activism by showing how and under what conditions such activism can unexpectedly strengthen support for corporate leaders among key stakeholders, even as activists seek to undermine their credibility. The findings offer practical implications for business leaders in managing external threats and for short-selling activists in refining their strategies for selecting targets. 激進做空行動日益受到關注，為被鎖定的企業帶來突然而重大的外部威脅。本研究探討此類做空維權行動如何影響員工對其 CEO 的支持與評價。借鑑政治學中的「旗幟效應」（rally round the flag），我們主張：雖然激進做空行動通常旨在削弱企業領導者的可信度，但它也可能悖論式地提升員工對 CEO 的支持度。此反應可能源於員工在組織名譽受到外部行動者挑戰時，為捍衛組織認同而產生的更強動機。我們進一步假設，這種效果會因 CEO 被視為企業象徵性代表的程度不同而有所差異。此外，我們也提出，激進做空者與被鎖定企業的來源國差異，會影響員工的反應。為檢驗這些假設，我們將使用 2011 至 2024 年的激進做空行動資料，採用傾向分數配對—差異中的差異（PSM‑DiD）研究設計。本研究對策略領導文獻的貢獻在於展示外部威脅如何反而增強員工對 CEO 的支持。同時，本研究也推進策略管理領域對激進做空行動的理解，指出此類行動在何種情況下可能意外地強化關鍵利害關係人對企業領導者的支持，即便做空者的目的在於削弱其可信度。研究結果亦為企業領導者在面對外部威脅時的管理策略，以及做空維權者在選擇目標時的策略調整，提供實務啟示。

14504926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14504926.value: 預見未來：人工智能生成的裝修後效果圖賦能房地產平台

14504926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14504926.value: Real estate platforms such as Zillow and Lianjia have become increasingly central to housing transactions. Recently, several platforms have introduced AI-generated post-renovation visuals, i.e., images that depict how a property might appear after renovation, into online listings. This represents a novel application of generative AI in a two-sided marketplace. By leveraging GenAI technology and rich platform data, these visuals can be personalized to reflect prospective buyers’ preferences. When integrated with virtual reality (VR) tools, they further enrich the buyer experience, shaping expectations and influencing both search and purchase decisions. Despite their growing prevalence, however, little is known about the business implications of AI-generated post-renovation visuals for key market outcomes such as time-on-market and transaction prices. This gap motivates several research questions of both academic and practical significance: • How do AI-generated post-renovation visuals affect core market outcomes, including matching efficiency (time-on-market for buyers and sellers), matching quality (post-sale satisfaction), and transaction prices? • What behavioral mechanisms underlie these effects for both buyers and sellers? • How do such effects vary across property types, buyer segments, and agents with differing professional capabilities? • How can platforms personalize these AI-based features to better target properties and buyers, thereby optimizing buyer experiences and enhancing platform profitability? In collaboration with one of the largest Chinese real estate platforms (“Platform B” hereafter), this study will address these questions through a combination of field experiments and empirical analyses. Drawing on a randomized controlled trial (RCT) conducted in one city, we will first estimate the effects of AI-generated visuals on time-on-market, buyer and seller satisfaction, and transaction prices. As an alternative identification strategy, we propose a staggered difference-in-differences design that exploits the phased rollout of the feature across cities. We will then use Platform B’s extensive transaction data to explore underlying mechanisms from both buyer and seller perspectives. Next, we will investigate heterogeneous effects along three dimensions: property condition, buyer experience, and agent capability. To further advance targeting, we will apply causal machine learning methods to design personalized deployment strategies for AI-generated visuals. Finally, we will conduct an additional field experiment with Platform B to test whether personalized targeting can enhance business outcomes beyond uniform adoption. Zillow與鏈家等房地產平台在住宅交易中日益舉足輕重。近年，若干平台開始在網上樓盤資訊中引入人工智能生成的裝修後效果圖，即描繪物業裝修後可能面貌的圖像，堪稱生成式人工智能在雙邊市場中的嶄新應用。藉助生成式人工智能技術與豐富的平台數據，此類效果圖可按準買家的偏好度身訂造。配合虛擬實境（VR）工具，更能豐富買家體驗，塑造其預期，進而影響搜尋與購買決策。然而，儘管此類功能日趨普及，其對物業在市時間（time-on-market）與成交價格等關鍵市場結果的商業影響，目前所知仍然甚少。 此一研究空白引出多個兼具學術與實踐意義的研究問題：（一）人工智能生成的裝修後效果圖如何影響核心市場結果，包括配對效率（買賣雙方的在市時間）、配對質素（成交後滿意度）及成交價格？（二）這些效應背後，買賣雙方各有何種行為機制？（三）此類效應在不同物業類型、買家群體以及專業能力各異的地產代理之間有何差異？（四）平台應如何將此類人工智能功能個人化，以更精準地投放於合適的物業與買家，從而優化買家體驗並提升平台盈利能力？ 本研究將與中國最大的房地產平台之一（下稱「平台B」）合作，結合田野實驗與實證分析回答上述問題。首先，我們將基於在一個城市開展的隨機對照實驗，估計人工智能生成效果圖對在市時間、買賣雙方滿意度及成交價格的影響。同時，我們將利用該功能在各城市分階段推出的安排，提出交錯雙重差分設計作為替代識別策略。其次，我們將利用平台B的大量交易數據，從買賣雙方視角探究背後的行為機制。繼而，我們將沿物業狀況、買家經驗與代理能力三個維度考察異質性效應。為進一步提高投放的精準度，我們將運用因果機器學習方法，為人工智能生成效果圖設計個人化部署策略。最後，我們將與平台B再進行一項田野實驗，檢驗個人化精準投放能否較劃一採用帶來更佳的商業成效。 關鍵詞：雙邊平台、生成式人工智能技術、房地產市場、平台設計、线上實驗

14505126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14505126.value: 評估型人工智能的流失成本：因果識別、作用機制與傷害防範導向設計

14505126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14505126.value: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly built into platforms that people use to learn, exercise, and upskill. A fast-growing class of “evaluative AI” (EAI) scores or judges users in real time (e.g., form-checking during workouts or pronunciation grading in language learning). While intended to motivate, constant algorithmic evaluation may also discourage participation by making performance gaps salient. This project quantifies the attrition cost of real-time EAI, identifies the mechanisms behind it, and develops harm-aware design principles that sustain engagement without sacrificing guidance. We address three questions: (1) What is the causal impact of introducing real-time EAI on user engagement and retention, and how does it vary with exposure intensity and user characteristics? (2) Through which behavioral and experiential mechanisms does EAI influence motivation? (3) What are the platform-level consequences, including spillovers to non‑AI alternatives and net effects on usage and revenue? Our empirical setting is a leading digital fitness platform that launched real‑time, camera-based form evaluation on a randomly selected subset of courses. Using a difference-in-differences (DID) framework, complemented by text analysis of user reviews, we provide initial evidence that real-time EAI can reduce participation in treated courses by roughly 31%, with stronger declines in longer sessions (greater exposure) and weaker declines among more tech‑savvy users. Effects are heterogeneous by task difficulty: EAI can boost engagement in easier courses but amplifies perceived inadequacy and disengagement in harder ones. We also find positive spillovers to similar non-AI courses, yet a net reduction (around 11%) in activity across the affected categories, raising platform-level concerns. Building on these findings, we will (i) replicate across domains such as language learning, coding, music practice, and tele-rehabilitation; (ii) isolate mechanisms via controlled experiments that vary scoring cadence, message valence, transparency, and reference frames; and (iii) translate mechanisms into harm-aware EAI designs (e.g., baseline‑anchored feedback, cadence budgets, practice-without-grades modes, adaptive difficulty, and privacy controls) and test them in the field. The project will deliver causal evidence on when EAI helps or harms, a mechanism‑to‑design playbook for practitioners, and policy‑relevant guidance for responsible deployment, advancing academic knowledge on feedback and platform economics while protecting user motivation and ecosystem sustainability. 人工智能（AI）日益被整合至人們用於學習、運動及提升技能的數位平台之中。一類迅速發展的「評估型人工智能」（evaluative AI, EAI）會即時對用戶的表現進行評分或評判，例如在運動過程中檢查動作姿勢，或在語言學習中評定發音。儘管此類技術旨在激勵用戶，持續不斷的演算法評估亦可能因凸顯其表現差距而削弱參與意願。本項目旨在量化即時 EAI 所帶來的用戶流失成本，識別其背後的作用機制，並建立傷害防範導向的設計原則，以在不犧牲指導功能的前提下維持用戶參與。 本項目聚焦三個研究問題：（1）導入即時 EAI 對用戶參與度與留存率具有何種因果影響？此影響如何隨接觸強度及用戶特徵而變化？（2）EAI 透過哪些行為與體驗機制影響用戶動機？（3）EAI 會產生哪些平台層面的後果，包括用戶向非 AI 替代方案轉移的溢出效應，以及其對整體使用量與營收的淨影響？本研究以一家領先的數位健身平台為實證場域。該平台在隨機選取的部分課程中推出了基於攝影機的即時動作姿勢評估功能。我們採用雙重差分法（difference-in-differences, DID），並結合用戶評論的文本分析。初步證據顯示，即時 EAI 可使處理組課程的參與量下降約 31%；此下降在時長較長、因而接觸強度較高的課程中更為明顯，而在數位科技素養較高的用戶中則相對較弱。其影響亦因任務難度而異：EAI 能夠提升用戶對較容易課程的參與，卻可能在較困難的課程中加劇能力不足感，進而促使用戶退出。我們亦發現，用戶會轉向相似的非 AI 課程，形成正向溢出效應；然而，在受影響的課程類別中，整體活動量仍淨減少約 11%，反映出值得關注的平台層面後果。 在上述發現的基礎上，本項目將進一步：（i）在語言學習、程式設計、音樂練習及遠距復康等領域進行跨情境驗證；（ii）透過控制實驗，系統性調整評分頻率、訊息效價、透明度及參照框架，以識別 EAI 影響用戶行為的具體機制；以及（iii）將這些機制轉化為傷害防範導向的 EAI 設計，例如以個人基準表現為錨點的回饋、評分頻率限制、無評分練習模式、自適應難度及隱私控制，並透過實地實驗檢驗其成效。本項目將提供有關 EAI 在何種情況下有助或有損用戶參與的因果證據，建立從作用機制到設計方案的實務框架，並為負責任的技術部署提供具政策意義的指引。藉此，本項目不僅將推進回饋機制與平台經濟學領域的學術知識，亦有助於保護用戶動機及維持平台生態系統的長期可持續性。

14505226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14505226.value: Structural transformation has traditionally been conceptualized as a phenomenon driven entirely by local conditions. Conventional wisdom suggests that the rise of the service sector stems from localized factors such as income growth or differential sectoral productivity changes within a specific region. Our project challenges this perspective by introducing a novel mechanism: structural transformation driven by the spatial allocation of consumption across cities. We argue that inflows of external demand expand local service sectors and consequently accelerate sectoral reallocation from manufacturing to services. Crucially, we demonstrate that these effects are more pronounced when demand flows from higher-income to lower-income cities. This asymmetry establishes a previously unexamined mechanism for spatial convergence of economic structures, complementing the well-established channel through income convergence. To formalize this concept, we develop a comprehensive spatial equilibrium model. We calibrate this model to quantify the importance of spatial structural transformation. Given that improvements in transportation infrastructure serve as a key driver for growing external demand for local services, our calibrated model further decomposes the contribution of external demand to spatial structural transformation into transportation and non-transportation channels. China provides an ideal laboratory for our quantitative analysis for two compelling reasons. First, China has undergone dramatic structural transformation, with particularly remarkable growth in services over the past two decades. Second, connectivity within China has improved substantially through enormous infrastructure investments. Our framework addresses a fundamental question: to what extent have these transportation improvements stimulated inflows of external demand and accelerated structural transformation, especially in less-developed regions? Our unique access to transaction records of AlipayHK users offers an unprecedented opportunity to reveal previously undocumented patterns of spatial consumption choices across varieties and expenditure categories. Additionally, using the rich transaction-level data, we can leverage new high-speed rail connections as instrumental variables to estimate the causal effects of improved transportation on spatial consumption allocation. These reduced-form estimations with clear identification strategies are critical for disciplining our calibration parameters and serve as important external validity checks for our quantitative assessments. The policy implications of our analysis are particularly relevant for contemporary China, where the manufacturing sector faces dual challenges from negative external demand shocks and weakening domestic demand. Our spatial structural transformation mechanism illuminates how cross-regional flows of demand can stimulate service sector growth and facilitate the transition from manufacturing to services, potentially reducing China's dependence on foreign demand for manufactured goods while fostering more balanced and sustainable economic development across regions. 結構轉型傳統上被概唸化爲一種完全由本地條件驅動的現象。傳統觀點認爲，服務業的興起源於特定地區內部的收入增長或部門間生産率變化差異等本地化因素。我們的項目通過引入一種新的機製來挑戰這一觀點：由消費在城市之間的空間配置所驅動的結構轉型。我們認爲，外部需求的流入會擴大本地服務業，並進而加速從製造業向服務業的部門再配置。關鍵在於，我們証明，當需求從較高收入城市流向較低收入城市時，這些影響更爲顯著。這種非對稱性揭示了一種此前尚未被考察的經濟結構空間趨同機製，並對通過收入趨同實現經濟結構趨同這一已有充分研究的渠道形成補充。

14505326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14505326.value: 突擊檢查的經濟後果：來自投資顧問的證據

14505326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14505326.value: This study examines the effect of surprise exams on investment advisers. To deter fraudulent conduct, the SEC’s recent custody rule requires that investment advisers holding client assets (i.e., having custody of client assets) undergo annual surprise exams. Unlike financial statement audits of public firms, surprise exams of investment advisers can happen during any time of a year and advisers are not informed in advance. Using a sample of advisers that are subject to the custody rule, I examine the effect of surprise exams on employees’ misconduct. I conjecture that surprise exams that happen at irregular intervals across years (i.e., that could be more of a "surprise" to employees) are more effective in reducing misconduct, relative to exams with regular intervals across years. One possible reason is that when (perpetrator) employees “anticipate” that an exam is coming, they are more likely to cover their tracks in advance by hiding evidence or altering records, which undermines the effectiveness of the exam. In addition, I also examine the effect of surprise exams on investment advisers’ labor market decisions. Prior literature finds that employees with a misconduct record are more likely to be repeated offenders. I thus conjecture that investment advisers subject to the surprise exam requirement are more likely to hire employees with a clean record after the custody rule. To the best of my knowledge, this study is the first that examines whether the “timing” of an accounting exam matters for examinees. The findings of this study may also have practical implications for regulators. 本研究旨在探討突擊檢查對投資顧問的影響。為遏制欺詐行為，美國證監會近期出台的託管規則要求持有客戶資產（即對客戶資產具有託管權）的投資顧問每年接受一次突擊檢查。與上市公司的財務報表審計不同，對投資顧問的突擊檢查可能在一年中的任何時間進行，且投資顧問不會事先收到通知。本研究以受該託管規則要求的投資顧問為樣本，考察突擊檢查對員工不當行為的影響。本研究推測，與時間間隔固定的檢查相比，間隔不規律的突擊檢查（即對員工而言更具「突擊性」）在減少不當行為方面更為有效。一個可能的原因是，當具有不當行為的員工預期檢查即將到來時，他們更有可能通過隱匿證據或篡改記錄等方式提前掩蓋其行為，從而削弱檢查的有效性。此外，本研究還考察突擊檢查對投資顧問勞動力市場決策的影響。已有研究發現，曾有不當行為記錄的員工更有可能再次違規。因此本研究推測，在託管規則實施後，受突擊檢查要求的投資顧問更傾向於聘用無不當行為記錄的員工。據我所知，本研究應為最早探討會計檢查的時間是否會對受查對象產生影響的文章之一。本研究的發現也會為監管機構提供具有實踐意義的啟示。

14505626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14505626.value: 供應網路中的預測與因果關係：ESG 風險的證據與工具

14505626.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14505626.value: Prof Gaur, Vishal Prof Osadchiy, Nikolay

14505626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14505626.value: In an era of heightened scrutiny on corporate responsibility, global supply chains are increasingly vulnerable to reputational risks stemming from Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) issues, such as labor violations, environmental damage, or unethical practices by suppliers. Unlike traditional operational risks (e.g., supply disruptions or cost fluctuations), where diversifying suppliers helps mitigate problems, ESG risks can spread reputational harm across the entire network, making broader supplier bases potentially more exposed. Firms may face backlash for issues involving even distant upstream partners, prompting them to rethink and restructure their supply relationships. This research project investigates the causal impacts of ESG incidents on supply network reconfiguration and develops predictive tools to forecast such risks. Using comprehensive data on firm-to-firm supply links (from FactSet Revere), ESG incidents (from RepRisk), and financial metrics (from Compustat), the study first provides empirical evidence on how buyers respond to ESG shocks. For instance, do firms drop suppliers involved in incidents and switch to better-governed alternatives? How do these shocks create spillovers, such as affecting relationships with indirect (tier-2) suppliers or peers? The analysis explores timelines, variations across industries and risk types, and anticipatory actions to avoid future vulnerabilities. Additionally, the project leverages advanced Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to predict ESG risks by incorporating network structures alongside firm fundamentals. This approach identifies potential risk pathways in deep-tier supply chains, enabling early warning systems for monitoring and stress-testing. By bridging causation and prediction, this research advances understanding of ESG dynamics in volatile global networks. The findings offer practical insights for managers to enhance supplier due diligence and resilience strategies, for investors to assess hidden risks, and for policymakers to design regulations promoting sustainable supply chains. Ultimately, it supports informed decision-making to navigate and mitigate ESG impacts on global operations. 在企業社會責任備受審視的時代，全球供應鏈正日益容易受到源自環境、社會和公司治理（ESG）議題的聲譽風險影響，例如供應商的勞工違規行為、環境破壞或不道德行為。與傳統的營運風險（如供應中斷或成本波動）不同——在傳統風險中，分散供應商有助於減輕問題——ESG 風險可能會將聲譽損害擴散至整個網路，從而使更廣泛的供應商基礎可能面臨更大的風險敞口。 企業甚至可能因為涉及遙遠上游合作夥伴的議題而面臨強烈抵制，這促使它們重新思考並重組其供應關係。本研究專案調查了 ESG 事件對供應網路重組的因果影響，並開發了預測工具來預報此類風險。本研究利用關於企業間供應鏈結（源自 FactSet Revere）、ESG 事件（源自 RepRisk）和財務指標（源自 Compustat）的全面數據，首先提供了關於買方如何應對 ESG 衝擊的實證證據。例如，企業是否會汰換涉及事件的供應商並轉向治理更好的替代方案？這些衝擊如何產生溢出效應，例如影響與間接（第二層）供應商或同業的關係？該分析探討了時間線、不同行業和風險類型的差異，以及為避免未來脆弱性而採取的預防性行動。 此外，該專案利用先進的圖神經網路（GNN），透過結合網路結構與企業基本面來預測 ESG 風險。 這種方法識別了深層供應鏈中的潛在風險路徑，從而為監控和壓力測試建立早期預警系統。 透過連結因果關係與預測，本研究推進了對動盪全球網路中 ESG 動態的理解。研究結果為管理人員加強供應商盡職調查和韌性策略、為投資者評估隱含風險，以及為政策制定者制定促進可持續供應鏈的法規提供了實用的見解。最終，它為引導和減輕 ESG 對全球營運的影響提供了明智決策的支持。

14505726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14505726.value: A substantial share of patented innovations never reach the marketplace, limiting downstream diffusion and social welfare gains. Information frictions—difficulties in accessing and processing patent-related knowledge—play a central role in this “valley of death” between invention and commercialization. This project examines how reducing such frictions influences the timing, likelihood, and locus of patent commercialization. We plan to develop a novel, embedding-based measure that links patent texts with product launch announcements, capturing both internal and external commercialization dynamics. This approach moves beyond conventional proxies such as citations or market reactions by emphasizing realized technology adoption in products. Validation exercises will compare our measure with forward citations, licensing agreements, trademark applications, and search intensity around product launches to ensure robustness and construct validity. To establish causal relationships, we plan to exploit two regulatory reforms that reduced information frictions and improved patent visibility. The American Inventors Protection Act (AIPA) mandated early publication of U.S. patent applications, while the Global Dossier initiative integrated patent information across the world’s five largest intellectual property offices. These settings provide a unique opportunity to examine how earlier and more transparent patent disclosures shape commercialization outcomes, both domestically and across borders. This project contributes to several strands of literature. First, methodologically, it introduces a new textual measure of commercialization that will be made publicly available for use in future research. Second, it enriches the accounting and innovation literature by showing how disclosure affects the diffusion of patented technologies, highlighting the dual role of transparency in both reducing frictions and creating proprietary costs. Third, it sheds light on policy design by illustrating how reforms in patent information regimes can influence the translation of inventions into marketable products and ultimately improve social welfare. 相當一部分已獲專利的創新最終未能進入市場，因而限制了相關技術的後續擴散及其所能帶來的社會福利增益。信息摩擦——即獲取及處理專利相關知識時所面臨的困難——在發明與商業化之間的這一「死亡之谷」中扮演關鍵角色。本項目旨在研究降低此類信息摩擦如何影響專利商業化的時機、可能性及發生位置。 我們計劃開發一項嶄新的、基於文本嵌入技術的衡量指標，將專利文本與產品發布公告相匹配，以捕捉企業內部及外部的商業化動態。與引用次數或市場反應等傳統替代指標不同，該方法聚焦於專利技術在產品中的實際應用。為確保衡量指標的穩健性及構念效度，我們將其與前向引用、專利許可協議、商標申請，以及產品發布前後的搜索熱度進行比較和驗證。 為識別因果關係，我們計劃利用兩項降低信息摩擦並提高專利可見度的監管改革。《美國發明人保護法案》（American Inventors Protection Act，AIPA）要求美國專利申請提前公開，而「全球卷宗」（Global Dossier）計劃則整合了全球五大知識產權局的專利信息。這兩項制度改革為我們提供了獨特的研究情境，以考察更早及更透明的信息披露如何影響本國及跨境的專利商業化結果。 本項目對多個領域的文獻作出貢獻。首先，在研究方法方面，本項目提出一項新的商業化文本衡量指標，並將其公開，以供未來研究使用。其次，本項目通過揭示信息披露如何影響專利技術的擴散，豐富會計與創新領域的文獻，並突顯透明度既能降低信息摩擦，也可能帶來專有成本的雙重作用。最後，本項目亦有助於理解政策設計，說明專利信息制度改革如何影響發明向可銷售產品的轉化，並最終提升社會福利。

14505926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14505926.value: 進階計量經濟工具與高頻金融數據中新典型化事實的湧現

14505926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14505926.value: High-frequency trading now accounts for a large share of activity in modern financial markets, yet many widely used tools for analysing intraday prices rely on assumptions that no longer hold. This project develops new econometric methods tailored to today’s data and applies them to uncover three central findings. First, short-run drifts—systematic price movements over brief intervals—are common and increasing. Contrary to the traditional view that drift is negligible at high frequencies, our new test, applied to raw transaction data for large U.S. stocks between 2013 and 2018, identifies frequent and rising departures from the negligible-drift assumption. Second, market microstructure noise—the difference between traded prices and the underlying efficient price—is often much smaller than suggested by standard realized-variance-based methods. We introduce a multi-horizon double differencing estimator that separates noise from genuine information even in the presence of large drifts. Applied to major exchange-traded funds and blue-chip stocks from 2013 to 2023, this method shows that conventional approaches can overstate noise by orders of magnitude, leading to understated efficient-price volatility and biased assessments of market quality. Third, market efficiency, when scaled by the pace of price discovery, is highest precisely when spreads are wide, including at the open, at the close, and immediately following FOMC announcements. We implement a real-time metric of “frictions per unit of information” using second-by-second transactions and find that, once information flow is accounted for, markets rapidly incorporate news and display lower relative frictions during these periods, despite elevated quoted and effective spreads. These results caution against relying on spreads alone as a proxy for efficiency and call into question common research practices that exclude opening and closing intervals, which may be the most informative segments of the trading day. The proposed methods improve volatility estimation, the measurement of noise and liquidity, and policy evaluation using only transaction data. The evidence indicates that modern intraday prices are shaped by short, intense bursts of information and that true volatility is higher than commonly inferred. For regulators and exchanges considering extended trading hours, the findings suggest that spreading activity over longer sessions risks diluting liquidity and reducing efficiency. Overall, the project delivers practical tools and robust evidence to reassess intraday market quality in the era of high-speed trading. 高頻交易目前在現代金融市場中佔據相當大的活動比重，然而許多廣泛使用的日內價格分析工具所依賴的假設，已不再成立。 本專案開發了針對現今數據量身打造的新計量經濟方法，並將其應用以揭示三項核心發現。第一，短期趨勢——即短暫區間內的系統性價格變動——相當常見且日益增加。與傳統觀點認為在高頻下趨勢可忽略不計相反，我們將新檢定應用於2013至2018年間大型美國股票的原始交易數據，發現偏離可忽略趨勢假設的情況頻繁出現且持續上升。第二，市場微觀結構噪音——即交易價格與潛在有效價格之間的差異——通常遠小於標準實現變異數法所暗示的程度。我們引入了一種多期距雙重差分估計量，即使在存在大幅趨勢的情況下，仍能將噪音與真實資訊分離。將此方法應用於2013至2023年間的主要交易所交易基金及藍籌股，結果顯示傳統方法可能將噪音高估數個數量級，導致有效價格波動性被低估，以及市場品質評估產生偏誤。第三，當以價格發現速度為衡量基準時，市場效率恰好在價差擴大時達到最高，包括開盤時、收盤時，以及聯邦公開市場委員會（FOMC）公告發布後的短暫期間。我們利用逐秒交易數據建構了「每單位資訊的摩擦」即時指標，發現一旦將資訊流納入考量，市場能迅速吸收新聞，且儘管報價價差與有效價差均處於高位，這些時期的相對摩擦反而較低。這些結果提醒不宜單獨以價差作為效率的代理變數，並質疑常見研究中排除開盤與收盤時段的做法，因為這些時段可能是交易日中最具資訊含量的區間。 所提出的方法僅利用交易數據，即可改進波動性估計、噪音與流動性衡量，以及政策評估。證據顯示，現代日內價格受到短暫而劇烈的資訊爆發所形塑，且真實波動性高於一般推論所得。對於考慮延長交易時間的監管機構與交易所，研究結果指出，將交易活動分散至更長時段，可能導致流動性稀釋與效率降低。整體而言，本專案提供了實用工具與穩健證據，以重新評估高速交易時代的日內市場品質。

14506026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14506026.value: 消費者流動性、品牌偏好與電動汽車選擇：基於中國市場的經驗研究

14506026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14506026.value: Promoting the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) is central to reducing carbon emissions and supporting sustainable growth. In China, EV sales have grown rapidly not only in major metropolitan markets but also in second- and third-tier cities, where local policy incentives and firm marketing efforts are limited. This project proposes to investigate a novel demand-side factor: consumer mobility to EV-leading mega-cities generates spillover effects that influence brand preferences and increase EV adoption in less developed markets. To carry out the empirical investigation, we will compile a new dataset from multiple sources. We will link city-level monthly vehicle registration data for over 860 car models across more than 300 Chinese cities in 2018-2022 with intercity travel data from a leading online navigation platform to construct measures of exposure to six EV-leading mega-cities. We also use detailed vehicle characteristics and survey data to augment the analysis of city-level data. After cleaning and organizing the data, we will document key stylized facts on EV adoption patterns and mobility-driven exposure to EV-leading mega-cities. Using a shift-share instrumental variable strategy, we will estimate the causal effect of mobility-driven exposure to EV-leading mega-cities on EV sales in lower-tier cities, while controlling for city-level socio-economic factors and vehicle characteristics. Preliminary analysis shows that cities with higher outbound travel to these mega-cities display stronger EV adoption patterns, consistent with the proposed mobility-driven spillover channel. To uncover the mechanisms behind these spillovers, we will build a structural demand model that incorporates mobility-driven exposure into consumer utility and adoption decisions, accounting for supply-side factors such as EV subsidies. The structural analysis will allow us to quantify how mobility-driven exposure affects brand preferences, consumer choices, and market outcomes. Lastly, we will use counterfactual simulations based on the structural estimates to evaluate how market outcomes and the effectiveness of EV promotion policies would change if mobility-driven exposure were removed, illuminating the interaction between consumer spillovers and conventional policy instruments. This project will provide a first systematic examination on consumer mobility as a driver of EV diffusion, offering insights for understanding brand preferences and designing effective climate policies in emerging markets.

14506626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14506626.value: 當巨人倒下：上市公司財務不當行為對當地小型企業的影響

14506626.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14506626.value: Prof Geng, Lingfeng Mr LIU, WEIQIAN

14506626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14506626.value: We examine the spillover effects of public firms’ financial misconduct on the performance of local small and micro enterprises (SMEs hereafter). Based on detailed invoice-level data of more than 100,000 SMEs, the analysis shows that SMEs located in cities where their public firms’ financial misconducts are exposed, experience significant sales growth. The effect is particularly concentrated among firms operating in the same industry as the misconducting public firm. The spillover effect is stronger when the misconduct is more severe, receives broader media coverage, occurs in industries with low competition and low entry barriers, or involves firms with poorer social performance. We further explore the underlying mechanisms and find that, after the exposure of local public firms’ misconduct, local SMEs experience an expanded customer base, a larger transaction volume, and a more diversified demand of products. In response to this surge in demand, SMEs expand their production capacities through procurement of fixed assets and adjusting pricing strategies to capture the new business opportunities. The study contributes to the literature on the wider impact of corporate misconduct and provides new insights into SMEs’ resilience and local economic dynamics. 我們研究上市公司財務不當行為對當地中小微企業（以下簡稱 SMEs）經營績效的外溢效應。基於超過 10 萬家 SMEs 的詳細發票層級資料，分析結果顯示，當所在地城市的上市公司財務不當行為遭到揭露後，當地 SMEs 的銷售額會出現顯著成長。此效果尤其集中於與發生不當行為之上市公司處於相同產業的企業。進一步分析發現，當不當行為情節更為嚴重、獲得更廣泛的媒體報導、發生於競爭程度較低且進入門檻較低的產業，或涉及社會責任表現較差的企業時，這種外溢效應會更加明顯。我們亦探討其潛在機制，結果顯示，在當地上市公司不當行為被揭露後，當地 SMEs 的客戶基礎擴大、交易量增加，且產品需求結構更加多元化。為因應需求的成長，SMEs 透過採購固定資產來擴充產能，並調整定價策略，以把握新出現的商業機會。本研究擴展了企業不當行為廣泛影響的相關文獻，並為理解中小微企業的韌性以及地方經濟動態提供了新的洞見。

14507326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14507326.value: 個稅政策，貨幣政策與存款市場穩定性

14507326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
