Bamboo’s unique combination of flexibility, strength, and bending resistance has made it a cornerstone of traditional craftsmanship, particularly in woven forms, such as baskets. In traditional bamboo weaving, skilled craftspeople rely on tacit knowledge to introduce singularities – points of changing curvature at which bending stresses are concentrated and therefore at which cracking and failure are likely to occur. However, such craftspeople are vanishing, and nuanced ways of negotiating singularities are being lost, leaving technical and cultural gaps. This loss of knowledge will restrict innovation and impede the use of bamboo weaving in contemporary design applications, such as in architectural use. The proposed study will therefore systematically analyse bamboo’s elastoplastic behaviour, along with its curvature and structural characteristics at singularities in woven architectural structures, to harness its potential for use in structurally reliable and innovative architectural applications. Through experimental testing focusing on bamboo’s bending and elastoplastic behaviour under controlled loading conditions, this study will develop a methodology that bridges traditional craftsmanship and modern engineering to generate foundational knowledge of bamboo’s mechanical properties and structural behaviour. The study will characterise the material properties of bamboo, conduct physical experiments and digital simulations to analyse stress distribution, displacement, and bending limits, and construct prototype structures and mock-ups to validate the experimental findings. It will also develop computational design tools to model the relationship between form and performance, particularly at singularities. This work will both preserve intangible cultural heritage and promote sustainable architectural practices. By systematically testing and analysing the structural behaviour of woven bamboo at singularities, this study will develop evidence-based design principles and reliable guidelines for stable, scalable, and sustainable architectural applications. By transforming tacit knowledge of bamboo crafting into explicit, shareable methods, the project will help preserve traditional bamboo weaving techniques while making them accessible to modern architectural designers and manufacturers for the construction of woven bamboo structures. It will also promote bamboo culture in the Chinese cultural sphere and facilitate the transmission of craft knowledge. These outcomes will align with broader cultural preservation goals, such as those outlined in the Hong Kong government’s cultural policy. The project will also support the development of a sustainable built environment by leveraging bamboo’s exceptional properties as a renewable material, thus contributing to the achievement of global goals for decarbonisation and sustainable development. 社會對可持續材料的興趣與需求正日益增長。竹材兼具柔韌性、強度與抗彎性能，並依憑此獨特性能作為造籃等傳統編織工藝的重要基礎。在傳統竹編中，工匠會根據自己難以言述的經驗控制編織構件間拓撲關係異於別處的奇異點。在這些奇異點的位置，曲率較其他位置更突出，構件的應力會更集中，較容易產生裂紋與失效，因此合理安排奇異點的位置對編織結構事關重大。然而，這些傳統工藝正隨工匠離世而逐漸消失，通過控制構件間關係而處理奇異點的細緻方法也正在流失。這種知識流失將形成技術與文化上的缺失，並阻礙設計者在當代設計實踐中使用竹編，其中包含建築中的應用。 因此，本研究擬系統分析竹材的彈塑性行為，以及建築尺度編織結構中奇異點處的曲率與結構特徵，以發掘竹材在結構可靠且具創新性的建築應用中的潛力。透過聚焦於竹材在受控載荷條件下之彎曲與彈塑性行為的實驗測試，本研究將建立一套連結傳統工藝與現代工程的方法論，以獲取關於竹材力學性能與結構行為的基礎知識。研究將解析竹材的材料性能，通過物理實驗與數位模擬，分析其應力分佈、位移與彎曲極限，並建造原型結構與實體模型，以驗證物理實驗的發現。本研究亦將開發計算設計工具，用以模擬形態與性能之間的關係，尤其著重於奇異點位置。 本研究將同時保存非物質文化遺產並促進可持續建築實踐。透過系統測試與分析編織竹材在奇異點處的結構行為，本研究將制定以證據為基礎的設計原則，以及適用於穩定、可擴展且可持續建築應用的可靠指引。透過將竹工藝中的默會知識轉化為明確且可共享的方法，本項目將有助於保存傳統竹編技藝，同時使現代建築設計師與製造商能夠掌握並應用這些技術，以建造竹編結構。本項目亦將推廣中華文化圈中的竹文化，並促進工藝知識的傳承。這些成果將與更廣泛的文化保育目標相契合，例如香港政府文化政策中所提出的相關目標。本項目亦將透過發揮竹材作為可再生材料的優異性能，支持可持續建成環境的發展，從而為實現全球減碳與可持續發展目標作出貢獻。

14616026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14616026.value: 以給京師：漢代長安銅鏡生產與供應的考古學研究

14616026.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14616026.value: Prof Chen, Jian Li Dr Qiang, Wu Wei

14616026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14616026.value: The aim of this project is to investigate how Chang’an, the capital of the Han dynasty, was materially sustained, using bronze mirrors—an “affordable luxury” widely used across social ranks—as a tracer of production and circulation. Drawing on newly discovered bronze-manufacturing remains found at Ducheng, a major site complex near Chang’an, this study will analyze how mirrors and other associated bronze products were produced and supplied to sustain the capital’s economies. Bronze mirrors were a hallmark of Han material culture, and Chang’an has yielded the largest published assemblage. Earlier scholarship identified the capital region as a key supply centre. However, no direct workshop evidence has been securely tied to mirror production. This absence leaves essential questions unresolved: which mirrors were locally made, how far the capital’s products circulated, and how local and imported products were integrated. Similarities—typological and compositional—between mirrors from Chang’an and other centres, such as Linzi in Shandong, further complicate the assumptions about local manufacture. While isotopic studies of finished mirrors provide useful clues, they cannot fully distinguish local from imported products. A systematic analysis of remains across the operation chain is urgently required. The project proposes an integrated approach to fill the research gap. Main methodologies include: I. metallurgical analysis of bronze-making remains; II. geochemical analysis to trace and compare ore source between waste and finished products; III. 3D scanning of moulds and final mirrors. Although the Guanzhong region was a major production core, the link between workshop remains and finished products has not been systematically explored. With the new data, this study will ask: (1) what are the “fingerprints” of Ducheng’s workshop waste and cemetery mirrors; (2) do these fingerprints align, demonstrating local provisioning, or diverge, suggesting multiple production units or imports; (3) how does Ducheng’s profile compare with legacy datasets from Chang’an and other centres. The outputs of this project will illuminate several broader issues. First, it will provide first-hand data to identify local products in the Chang’an region. Second, it will establish a framework for improving our understanding of how goods were transported to provision the capital. Ultimately, this archaeological study of mirrors will enhance research on the local production, imports, and the ways such interactions underpinned the functioning of the Han state. 本研究旨在探討漢代長安都城地區如何在物質上得以供應，並以銅鏡——一種泛見於不同社會階層的「普及型奢侈品」(affordable luxury)——作為追蹤生產與流通的材料。近年，長安附近的大型遺址群杜城新發現了一批青銅生產遺存。本研究將以此為基礎，分析銅鏡及其他相關青銅製品如何生產和供應，以維持都城經濟的運作。 銅鏡是漢代物質文化的重要組成部分，長安地區出土並已發表的銅鏡數量居全國之首。過去研究已指出，都城地區是重要的供應中心。然而，迄今尚未有作坊遺存能夠明確與銅鏡生產聯繫起來，因此若干重要問題仍未解決：哪些銅鏡屬於本地生產？都城產品的流通範圍有多大？本地與外來產品如何整合，尤其是在都城地區？此外，長安銅鏡與山東臨淄等其他生產中心的產品在類型和成分上的相似性，在多大程度上增加了判斷本地生產的困難，仍不清楚。現有對成品銅鏡的同位素研究雖然提供了重要線索，但尚不能充分區分本地與外來產品，因此有必要系統分析生產操作鏈不同環節的考古遺存。 本研究將採取綜合方法，包括：（一）青銅生產遺存的冶金學分析；（二）地球化學分析，比較生產廢棄物與成品的原料來源；（三）銅鏡陶范與成品的三維掃描。關中地區雖是漢代青銅生產的重要核心區域之一，但作坊生產遺存與附近墓葬出土成品之間的關係尚未得到系統研究。利用杜城新發現的材料，本研究將回答三個問題：（1）杜城作坊生產遺存與附近墓葬出土成品具有哪些可辨識的「指紋」特徵？（2）兩者的特徵是否吻合，從而顯示本地供應，或存在差異，反映不同生產單位或外來輸入？（3）杜城的特徵與長安既有資料及臨淄等其他生產中心有何異同？以杜城遺址群為基礎，結合青銅生產遺存與成品研究，將為回答上述問題提供新的考古資料。 本研究將從更宏觀的層面推進對若干重要問題的認識。首先，研究將提供第一手資料，以辨識長安地區的本地產品。其次，研究將建立進一步追蹤「都城供應」（capital provisioning）及物資運輸的分析框架。最終，通過研究本地生產、外來輸入及兩者之間的互動，本研究將進一步探討這些物質生產與供應體系如何支撐漢代國家的運作。

14616126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14616126.value: 檢驗補償機制在緩解閱讀障礙和預測中英文單字閱讀能力的作用：一項從香港小學到中學階段的縱向研究

14616126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14616126.value: Prof MAURER, Urs Dr Ning, Xiaoran Prof Torppa, Minna Dr Wang, Li-Chih

14616126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14616126.value: Developmental dyslexia (below dyslexia), characterized by unexpected difficulties in word reading, has affected 9~13% of the population. Despite the uniform symptom at diagnosis, longitudinal studies have revealed great individual variation in developmental trajectories of reading in children with dyslexia. While some children show persistently low performance across time, others show an improving trajectory. The explanation of this heterogeneity remains unclear. One account is compensation; the symptoms lessen by cognitive strengths in other domains and engagement of neural networks that are less involved in typical-developing individuals, despite persisting core deficits. Long-term longitudinal studies are needed to reveal parallel development of the brain, cognitive-linguistic strategies, and word reading to test this account. Furthermore, Hong Kong's bilingual context (Chinese and English) provides a unique opportunity to investigate whether compensation mechanisms observed in Chinese dyslexia transfer to English reading. We propose a multiple-cohort long-term longitudinal study, which will be built on our existing representative sample of 258 grade 2-5 children with clinically diagnosed dyslexia recruited from three cohorts (2018-2019, 2020-2021, and 2022-2023), among which 96 children have participated in EEG recordings. We will follow up on this sample when they are in secondary school in 2027-2029. Study one will test the compensation account by examining the development of neural specialization to print and its connections to Chinese reading gain. The participants will be recorded EEG again in secondary schools while performing the same character decision task as primary school. Data analysis will test the moderating role of reading gain on the development of N1 print tuning (print-non print), which we have found with typical developing children. The neural compensation account predicts that more reading gain is linked to higher level and more longitudinal increase in right lateralization of N1 print tuning, while normalization account predicts so in left-lateralization. Study 2 is to confirm the compensation mechanisms identified in study 1 in an independent sample and explore the cross-linguistic generalizability of it. We propose a cross-sectional study of adolescents with Chinese dyslexia to identify common neural activation patterns associated with both English and Chinese word reading ability. Finally, we will build machine learning models predicting dyslexia children’ s secondary school Chinese and English word reading profiles from primary school cognitive-linguistic and neural markers. The final model will indicate the most important primary school risk factors that predict long-term bilingual word reading difficulties. The results in turn suggest possible mitigating pathways. 發展性讀寫障礙（以下簡稱讀寫障礙）以單字閱讀展現出意料之外的困難為特徵，影響了全球 9% 至 13% 的人口。儘管診斷時的症狀一致，但縱向研究顯示，讀寫障礙兒童的閱讀發展軌跡存在巨大的個體差異。部分兒童在不同時期均持續表現不佳，而另一部分兒童則展現出進步的軌跡。這種異質性的成因目前尚不明確。其中一種解釋是「補償機制」——儘管核心缺陷仍然存在，但其他領域的認知優勢，以及大腦中較少參與典型發育個體閱讀的神經網絡之投入，減輕了讀寫障礙的症狀。因此，需要進行長期的縱向研究，以揭示大腦、認知語言策略與單字閱讀的平行發展，從而驗證這一解釋。此外，香港的雙語環境（中文和英文）提供了一個獨特的機會，讓研究人員能夠探討在中文讀寫障礙中觀察到的補償機制是否會遷移至英文閱讀。 我們提出一項多隊列的長期縱向研究，該研究將建基於我們現有具代表性的樣本。該樣本包含 258 名就讀小學二至五年級、經臨床診斷患有讀寫障礙的兒童，他們招募自三個隊列（2018–2019 年、2020–2021 年以及 2022–2023 年），其中有 96 名兒童曾參與腦電圖（EEG）記錄。我們將在 2027–2029 年他們升讀中學時進行追蹤研究。研究一將透過檢視大腦對印刷文字的神經特異化發展，及其與中文閱讀能力提升的聯繫，來驗證補償機制假說。參與者在中學階段將再次接受腦電圖記錄，同時執行與小學時期相同的字形判斷任務。數據分析將檢驗閱讀能力提升在快速腦電文字特異加工（印刷文字對比非印刷文字）發展中的調節作用，而我們在典型發育兒童中已發現了這種加工現象。神經補償機制假說預測，更多的閱讀能力提升與較高水平及更顯著的快速腦電文字特異加工右側化縱向增長相關；而常態化假說則預測左側化會出現上述現象。研究二旨在獨立樣本中確認研究一所發現的補償機制，並探索其跨語言的推廣性。我們提出一項針對患有中文讀寫障礙青少年的橫斷面研究，以找出與英文和中文單字閱讀能力共同相關的大腦激活模式。最後，我們將建立機器學習模型，利用小學時期的認知語言和神經標記，來預測讀寫障礙兒童在中學時期的中文和英文單字閱讀表現。最終模型將指出預測長期雙語單字閱讀困難最關鍵的小學風險因素。這些結果反過來能為潛在的緩解路徑提供啟示。

14616726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14616726.value: 一致百慮，同歸殊途：西漢中前期諸子歸屬之再思

14616726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14616726.value: This research project aims to systematically re-examine the classification and integration of various pre-Qin philosophical schools during the early and middle Western Han period. Traditional academic history has largely relied on the categorical framework of the "Bibliographic Treatise" in the Hanshu, assigning figures and texts to specific philosophical schools. However, this approach often overlooks that the classification system itself was a historical product emerging from the mid-to-late Western Han. These thinkers shared common concerns and were not originally confined by school boundaries. The project will focus on the following aspects: 1. Utilizing both transmitted and newly excavated texts—such as Xinyu by Lu Jia, Xinshu by Jia Yi, Huainanzi, Chunqiu Fanlu, and manuscripts from Yinque Shan and Peking University—to analyze the intellectual content of early and middle Western Han thinkers. Each text contains rich and diverse ideas that resist simple categorization under a single school. 2. Examining key cases—such as the formation of "Daoism," the rise of "Eclecticism," and the blending of Confucian and Legalist ideas—to reveal the complex process of selection, interpretation, and attribution behind the Hanshu classification. Many texts exhibit characteristics of multiple schools, reflecting a tendency toward synthesis rather than distinction. 3. Exploring shared intellectual concerns among Western Han thinkers that transcend school-based analysis. Their philosophies were oriented toward contemporary political and social issues, reflecting the real preoccupations of Han society rather than abstract doctrinal disputes. 4. Re-evaluating prior studies on the classification of Han thinkers, including academic histories and research on the "Masters" traditions, to refine scholarly understanding of school attribution. By integrating newly excavated materials—such as the Warring States bamboo slips housed at Anhui University—and adopting interdisciplinary perspectives from intellectual history, philology, and the sociology of knowledge, this study seeks to:  Analyze the complexity of thought within individual texts;  Identify common ground among different schools;  Examine the relationship between intellectual discourse and the sociopolitical context;  Investigate the historical process of school formation and classification. This research will not only deepen understanding of early Chinese intellectual formation but also offer interdisciplinary insights into the interaction between knowledge classification and political order. 本研究計劃旨在對西漢中前期諸子學說的歸類與整合現象進行系統性再考察。傳統學術史多依賴《漢書．藝文志．諸子略》的分類框架，將人物與典籍歸納為不同的諸子學派，卻在很大程度上忽略了此一分類體系本身是西漢中後出現的歷史產物。諸子有其共同關心的課題，本不以學派之思想囿之。本計劃擬從以下方面著眼： 結合傳世文獻與出土文獻，討論西漢中前期諸子的思想內容。傳世諸子文獻包括陸賈《新語》、賈誼《新書》、《淮南子》、《春秋繁露》等，以及出土文獻如銀雀山漢簡、北大漢簡等。每一部典籍有著極其豐富的思想內容，難以利用一家思想囿之。 深入剖析若干關鍵案例（如「道家」形成、「雜家」興起、儒法合流等），呈現西漢諸子思想在《漢書．藝文志》被選擇、詮釋與歸屬的複雜過程。不同典籍可以同時呈現與多於一個思想學派相合，並不容易區分。諸子思想，重視融合多於區分。 討論西漢諸子共同關心的課題，已超越可用某家派以作分析的情況。諸子的思想，皆為當時政治服務，所關心的也是當時社會的各種問題。西漢諸子的主張並非捏造，他們所關心的正是西漢人所關心的。 前人學者多有討論西漢諸子之學術歸類，包括若干西漢學術史，以及子學研究等，可以重新審視。如此討論，當屬學術史的重新考訂，可以深化諸子學派歸屬問題。 本研究將綜合運用與最新出土材料（如、安徽大學藏戰國竹簡等），突破既往研究的學科壁壘，結合思想史、文獻學與知識社會學的視角，致力於達成以下目標：（1）西漢諸子各自思想的複雜性，一部典籍包括各種思想，難以利用一家囿之，選取其中顯例分析之；（2）各家思想同中有異，異中有同，分析各家相通之處；（3）西漢諸子共同關心的課題，與當時社會、政治的關係；（4）諸子學派在西漢形成與歸納諸子的過程。本研究不僅有助於深化對中國早期思想形成的理解，其關於知識分類與政治秩序互動的討論亦具備跨學科的啟示意義。

14616926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14616926.value: 區劃調整，政策干預與鄉鎮城市化

14616926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14616926.value: For over four decades of economic reforms, the Chinese administrative state has actively intervened in the classification and definition of local government units, while currently incentivizing local officials through numerous policy schemes to accelerate urbanization in their localities. While many units have been formally reclassified as urban districts (市区), county-level cities (县级市), sub-districts (街道), and urban communities (居委会), the long-run consequences of such reclassification have not been evaluated systematically due to the paucity of cumulative data. We do so both qualitatively and quantitatively, in the context of townships and villages in Shandong province. We model the cumulative and multilevel nature of policy shocks affecting townships over time in the event-history framework of local administrative reconfiguration, combining rich administrative data on township organization with information about policy schemes deployed across Shandong province. We collect indicators of socio-economic development from municipalities down to townships and build a corresponding multilevel longitudinal database. We aim to disentangle the relationship between administrative reclassification and urban development, subject to the shocks of state policy ‘treatments’ aimed at (re)shaping and accelerating local urbanization. We argue that two interrelated pathways can accelerate local urbanization: (1) ex ante urban growth motivates officials to seek upgrading the administrative status of their locality to an urban unit as a validation of successful socio-economic transformation. Once administrative reclassification occurs, local urbanization may accelerate further. (2) the state also leverages policy initiatives to spur growth. By reclassifying units as urban regardless of their actual level of urbanization, the state targets policy support to localities chosen for future urbanization. This complex relationship suggests that state intervention is both a cause and an outcome that co-evolves along with local developmental conditions and should therefore be evaluated jointly and over time. We test the microfoundations of our theory using information about the long-term restructuring process among township-units and villages in the cases of Lanshan district and Linshu county in Linyi municipality, where authorities have been implementing multiple rounds of village mergers. We are particularly interested in the way administrative reorganizations have been sequenced and how varying temporalities have influenced ultimate outcomes on the ground. Specifically, we seek to explain why, following efforts to restructure villages in both cases, urbanization in Lanshan accelerated, but not in Linshu and theorize about how long-held urban biases and varying socio-economic conditions mediate this outcome. 在四十多年的經濟改革過程中，中國的行政國家一直積極介入地方治理單元的分類和界定，同時使用大量政策干預激勵官員，以加快當地城市化進程。許多行政單位儘管已被正式劃分為城區（市區）、縣級市、街道和居委會，由於數據的匱乏，此類區劃調整的長期影響尙未得到係統評估。本項目以山東省的鄉、鎮及街道和村、居委會為研究對象，對其進行定性和定量分析。 我們使用事件史的分析框架來研究行政區劃調整，結合大量有關鄉鎮組織運作的行政數據以及山東省各地實施的政策方案，對政策干預長期影響的纍積性和多層次特徵構建模型。我們收集從地級市到鄉鎮各級的社會經濟發展指標，構建相應的多層次縱貫數據庫。 我們的目標是釐清行政區劃調整與城市化之間的關係，同時評估旨在（重）塑和加速地方城市化的國家政策干預所帶來的衝擊。我們認為，加速地方城市化有兩條相互關聯的路徑：（1）事前實現的城市增長會促使官員尋求將本地的行政單元升格為城市單位，以此證明社會經濟轉型的成功。當地一旦實現這類區劃調整，城市化進程可能會因此進一步加速。（2）國家還利用政策干預來刺激增長，通過將部分區域重新劃分為城市單位，錨定那些計劃未來實現城市化增長的地區提供政策支持，無論其當下實際的城市化水平如何。這種複雜的關係表明，國家干預既可以是城市化的原因，也可以是其結果，它與當地的發展條件共同演變，我們因此應從長期對其綜合評估。 臨沂市蘭山區和臨沭縣已實施了多輪“合村併居”，我們利用它們鎮、村級單位長期區劃調整的數據，檢驗本理論的微觀基礎。我們特別關註區劃調整發生的先後順序以及時點層面的差異，評估它們如何影響最終的發展結果。具體而言，我們試圖解釋為何“合村併居”的調整僅在蘭山區實現了城市化的加速，而並未在臨沭縣產生相同的效果。我們還對中國發展進程中長期存在的城市偏向以及不同的社會經濟條件如何調節其效應提出理論解釋。

14617126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14617126.value: 平衡英文授課高等教育中的學術成長與情緒健康：探究人工智能情境下的自我調節學習雙軌系統

14617126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14617126.value: Prof Lai, Chun Prof Liyanage, Indika Prof ZOU, Di

14617126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14617126.value: English-medium instruction (EMI) is a global phenomenon in higher education. However, since EMI often operates in non-English-speaking contexts, it imposes heavy academic difficulties and evokes strong emotional reactions from students who learn complex subject knowledge through a foreign language. Advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) may help students address these challenges. Students use AI to overcome language barriers, manage course workloads, and reduce anxiety to protect their emotional well-being. Yet, misusing AI might deprive students of opportunities for deep learning and hinder long-term academic development. Thus, students urgently need to become self-regulated learners who strategically use AI to support academic growth in EMI contexts. The study will investigate how students in EMI higher education regulate their learning when using AI, and how such self-regulated learning (SRL) affects their academic success. Guided by Boekaerts and Niemivirta’s (2000) dual processing SRL model, the study will unpack how students navigate the affordances provided by AI in EMI course tasks, balancing two SRL pathways: one oriented toward cognitive growth and the other toward emotional well-being. By integrating the important yet often-neglected affective dimension, the study will add a unique perspective to SRL research in EMI contexts. The study will also provide the first systematic account of AI-mediated learning and its impact on EMI academic outcomes. The study will adopt a two-stage, mixed-methods design that triangulates quantitative and qualitative findings from diverse sources of data. Stage 1 will explore students’ use of AI and associated SRL strategies. Data generated by semi-structured interviews and learner-AI interaction logs with 48 purposively selected students will be used to map how students employ AI in EMI learning and to develop a novel AI-mediated SRL strategy questionnaire. Stage 2 will validate the questionnaire with two cohorts of students (N = 400, N = 1,600) selected via stratified random sampling. Using structural equation modelling, this stage will also examine key learner factors that predict SRL strategy use, and the effect of strategy use on EMI academic success. Finally, complementary task-specific stimulated recall interviews with 24 purposively selected students will provide in-depth insights into the situated, complex decision-making behind students’ strategy use. Together, the findings will extend theory on SRL, yield new research instruments, and generate evidence to design training programs for strategic AI use. Ultimately, the study will contribute to the ‘bigger picture’ of cultivating students’ AI literacy and SRL capacity in EMI higher education.

14618226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14618226.value: 電子音樂作為文化外交：讓-米歇爾·雅爾與後毛澤東時代至新千禧年的中法關係

14618226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14618226.value: This project investigates the complex interplay between electronic music and Sino-French cultural diplomacy through Jean-Michel Jarre’s landmark concerts in the People’s Republic of China in 1981 and 2004. I explore the rationale behind China’s collaboration with a Western pop music icon, hypothesizing that Jarre’s performances were strategically leveraged to project an image of openness and modernity in the wake of China’s 1978 reform and opening-up policy. The 1981 concerts, staged with spectacular multimedia displays in Beijing and Shanghai, and broadcast to an alleged audience of over 500 million listeners and 30 million viewers, were followed by global releases of live recordings and a documentary film. While these events are often credited with catalysing the emergence of electronic music in Chinese conservatories, I contend that the influence was more technological than curricular, given the absence of popular music genres in academic institutions at the time. Through a critical analysis of Jarre’s biography, autobiography, and Andrew Piddington’s documentary, I uncover ideological messaging embedded in the 1981 concerts and reveal covert political maneuvers that shaped their reception. Notably, Jarre’s pre-concert visit to China aboard the same flight as François Mitterrand, soon to become France’s first Socialist president, suggests deeper political alignments than registered in dominant historical accounts. I also interrogate the marginalization of other forms of electronic music—such as ethnic synthesizers, rock, and film scoring—and the contributions of individuals and industrial sectors excluded from the official narrative. The 2004 concert, held at the Forbidden City and Tiananmen Square as part of the Year of France, represents a more cautious and ideologically managed form of cultural diplomacy. I analyse Jarre’s evolving role as a “cultural ambassador” in light of his subtle political gestures, including his public dedication to the values of “liberty, equality, and fraternity.” By foregrounding marginalized narratives and reassessing the ideological underpinnings of cultural exchange, I offer a more comprehensive understanding of electronic music’s emergence in the PRC and the broader geopolitical dynamics of the Cold War and beyond. This project ultimately argues that Jarre’s concerts were not merely artistic spectacles but carefully orchestrated diplomatic interventions revealing a nuanced negotiation of identity, ideology, and international visibility. 本研究旨在探討電子音樂與中法文化外交之間複雜互動的關係。通過分析西方流行音樂偶像讓-米歇爾·雅爾前後在1981年及2004年來華的音樂會，探究中國如何策略性地利用雅爾的演出，營造開放與現代化的形象，特別是在中國1978年改革開放後的那一次。1981年雅爾在北京與上海舉行音樂會，配以宏大的多媒體展演，據稱兩場音樂會分別轉播給超過五億及三千萬的觀眾；現場錄音與紀錄片隨即向全球發行。本研究通過對雅爾的傳記、自傳，以及安德魯·皮丁頓的紀錄片作批判性分析，揭示1981年音樂會所傳達的意識形態訊息和政治運作。雅爾在音樂會前先到訪中國，並與即將成為法國首位社會黨總統的弗朗索瓦·密特朗同班機抵達，顯示了其中深層的政治意味。2004年在故宮與天安門廣場舉行的音樂會，是作為法國文化年的一部分，卻顯出相當謹慎，並有意識形態上受管控的文化外交形式的元素。本研究分析雅爾作為「文化大使」的角色轉變，辨明其微妙的政治姿態，其中包括公開宣示獻給「自由、平等、博愛」。透過突顯邊緣化敘事，並重新評估文化交換的意識形態基礎，本研究深入探討電子音樂在中華人民共和國興起，以及冷戰及其後出現的更廣泛地緣政治動態。本研究最終要論證的是雅爾的音樂會不僅是藝術以及宏異的視覺效果，更是精心編排的外交介入，交織出身份、意識形態與國際視角之間的融合爭競。

14618326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14618326.value: 早期中國與歐亞邊界之雙金屬兵器：藝飾與製技

14618326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14618326.value: This project provides the first systematic and interdisciplinary investigation of iron-blade bimetallic weaponry in the Chinese Central Plains and its Eurasian borderlands from their origins (c. 14th century BCE) until 220 CE. It directly challenges the dominant scholarly paradigm that treats bronze and iron technologies as separate, sequential stages of development. Instead, this research reframes these sophisticated composites as active sites of technological and cultural negotiation, probing why they emerged and persisted for over a millennium within a mature bronze-casting tradition. First appearing in the northeastern sector of Tong Enzheng’s “Crescent-shaped Cultural-Communication Belt,” these weapons were not mere technological precursors but were highly valued items consumed by both early Chinese and Eurasian frontier societies, embodying a complex interplay of established techniques and novel materials. The project’s analysis centers on the material and formal properties of these objects—their specific combinations of metals, methods of joinery, and ornamental and morphological features. It investigates how these visible and tangible characteristics functioned as markers of status, identity, and technical prowess within specific social and geographical contexts. To decode this material syntax, the research employs an integrated methodology, combining formal analysis with advanced non-invasive techniques, including 3D scanning and portable X-ray fluorescence, applied to a targeted corpus from key sites. This generates high-resolution data on form, surface treatment, structural integrity, and elemental composition, all systematically integrated with archaeological context within a unified relational database. The investigation is guided by five core objectives: to establish a verified typology and chronology; to classify distinct manufacturing protocols; to correlate technological choices with specific socio-geographic contexts; to trace the provenance of iron components (distinguishing meteoritic from smelted iron); and to develop a new model of technological transmission for the region. By reconstructing the decision-making of early metallurgists, the project aims to reveal a dynamic landscape of interaction. The research aims to explore how technological knowledge across the Eurasian frontier may have been transmitted, reinterpreted, and reconfigured rather than merely passed along through unidirectional diffusion. In pursuing this line of inquiry, the project seeks to situate early China as an active and dynamic participant within broader networks of Eurasian technological exchange, proposing a refined framework for understanding the interconnected art and archaeology of its frontiers. 本計畫首次針對華夏中原及其歐亞邊界地區之鐵刃雙金屬兵器進行系統性跨學科研究,時段涵蓋其起源(約公元前十四世紀)至公元220年。本研究直接挑戰將青銅與冶鐵技術視為獨立且先後承接之發展階段此一主流學術範式。相反,本研究將這些精密複合器物重新界定為技術與文化交涉之能動場域,探討其在成熟青銅冶鑄傳統中為何出現且長期存續逾千年。這些兵器最早出現於童恩正所謂「半月形文化傳播帶」之東北段,並非單純之技術先驅,而是早期中國與歐亞邊區社會共同珍視之消費品,體現既有技術與新穎材料間之複雜互動。 本計畫之分析聚焦於此類器物之材質與形制,具體而言:兩種金屬之組接方式、工藝技法以及造型紋飾。研究探討這些顯性與隱性之特徵,如何在特定社會與地理脈絡中標示地位、身分與技術造詣。為解讀這些物質特徵,本研究整合諸多方法,結合形制分析與先進非侵入性技術,包括三維掃描及便攜式X射線螢光光譜分析,應用於關鍵遺址之目標材料。這些方法就器物形制、器表處理、結構特徵及元素組成生成高解析度數據,並將所得數據連同出土情境等考古資訊,系統整合統一於資料庫中。 本研究設定五項核心目標:建立經驗證之類型學與年代學;分類不同之製作方式;將技術選擇與特定社會地理脈絡相關聯;追溯鐵質構件之來源(區分隕鐵與冶煉鐵);並為該區域建構新的技術傳播模型。通過重構早期冶金工匠之決策過程,本計畫旨在揭示一個互動之動態景觀。本研究探索歐亞邊界之技術知識如何被傳遞、重新詮釋及重新配置,而非僅通過單向擴散傳播。循此研究路徑,本計畫將早期中國定位為歐亞技術交流更廣網絡中主動且具活力之參與者,從而提出理解其邊疆技藝與考古互聯性之新框架。

14618726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14618726.value: 野化願景之爭：從規劃－融資－環境感測關聯視角探討城市再野化的政治

14618726.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14618726.value: Dr Wang, Zheng Prof Xu, Jiang

14618726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14618726.value: Imagine cities where wildflowers reclaim concrete lots, birds nest in abandoned buildings, and native species flourish without human control – this is the vision of urban rewilding, an emerging approach to ecological restoration in urban settings. Unlike conventional greening efforts, urban rewilding aims to reintroduce self-sustaining ecosystems into the urban fabric. It is gaining momentum as a practical nature-based solution to climate change and food insecurity, and as an ethical commitment to restoring space for biodiversity. Yet, despite its growing appeal, urban rewilding continues to raise pressing practical and theoretical questions. They concern not only how rewilding, originally developed as a rural conservation strategy, adapts to the fragmented ecologies of urban environments, but also how it becomes entangled in the political-economic complexities of urban governance. It is this latter dimension that remains poorly understood and forms this project's central concern. Addressing this lacuna requires developing a new conceptual lens that integrates three influential strands of critical urban scholarship – sustainable urbanism, urban financialisation, and smart urbanism – to examine urban rewilding as a politically contested process. Sustainable urbanism highlights the role of spatial planning in advancing urban sustainability, as well as the discursive and institutional struggles over how environmental concerns are addressed through planning. Urban financialisation reveals the growing influence of financial actors and instruments, including green finance, over the trajectories of urban environmental governance. Smart urbanism underscores the increasing centrality of data and environmental sensing technologies in both spatial planning and the financial valuation of nature. These literatures, though insightful, have largely evolved in isolation. Our project breaks down these silos by proposing the perspective of planning-financing-sensing nexus, which captures the entangled processes through which urban rewilding is contested and assembled. This lens enables us to trace how spatial planning, financial imperatives, and environmental sensing co-produce urban nature in complex and often contradictory ways. Through a comparative analysis of London and Shenzhen – two global frontrunners in urban rewilding situated within contrasting contexts – this project will illuminate the varied pathways through which urban rewilding becomes possible. By examining how spatial, financial, and technological dynamics intersect to shape urban rewilding in each city, we uncover the complex barriers to implementing self-sustaining ecological restoration and the levers available to promote it. In doing so, the project contributes to a deeper understanding of how cities can embrace the ‘wild’ as a viable and transformative response to contemporary ecological challenges. 試想像一座城市：野花重新在混凝土空地上扎根，雀鳥在廢棄建築中築巢，本地物種不受人為干預而得以繁衍生息。這正是城市再野化所描繪的願景。作為一種新興的城市生態修復方法，城市再野化有別於傳統的綠化措施，其目標是在城市環境中重建能夠自我維持的生態系統。此方法近年備受關注，既被視為應對氣候變化和糧食安全挑戰的自然為本解決方案，亦體現人類為生物多樣性騰出更多空間的倫理承諾。然而，城市再野化的推展亦引發一系列亟待探討的實務和理論問題。這些問題不僅涉及源自鄉郊保育的再野化理念如何適應生態環境高度碎片化的城市空間，更關乎城市再野化如何受到城市治理中各種政治經濟力量的影響和塑造。相較於前者，後一層面的討論至今仍相對有限，亦正是本研究的核心關注。 為回應這方面研究的不足，本研究提出一個新的視角，整合三個具影響力的批判城市研究取向，即可持續城市主義、城市金融化及智慧城市主義，以探討城市再野化作為一項充滿政治爭議的過程。可持續城市主義強調空間規劃在推動城市可持續發展中的作用，以及圍繞環境議題如何透過規劃加以回應所引發的制度和論述角力。城市金融化揭示金融參與者及金融工具（包括綠色金融）如何日益影響城市環境治理的發展方向。智慧城市主義則指出，數據與環境感測技術在空間規劃及自然環境金融估值中的重要性與日俱增。儘管這些研究各具洞見，但大多沿着不同研究脈絡發展，鮮有置於同一分析框架下加以探討。有見及此，有見及此，本研究提出「規劃－融資－環境感測關聯」的分析視角，以理解規劃、融資與環境感測如何共同塑造城市再野化，並使其成為不同持份者協商與角力的場域。透過此一視角，我們得以探究規劃、融資與環境感測之間錯綜複雜且往往相互矛盾的關係，如何共同塑造城市自然。 透過比較倫敦與深圳兩個在城市再野化發展方面處於領先位置，但發展背景迥異的城市，本研究將闡明城市再野化得以實現的多元路徑。透過分析空間規劃、金融及技術因素如何在兩地相互作用並共同塑造城市再野化的實踐，本研究旨在揭示推動生態系統自我維持的修復實踐所面對的複雜障礙，以及促進其落實的有利條件。藉此，本研究將深化我們對城市再野化政治的理解，並探討城市如何為「野生自然」騰出空間，作為回應當代生態挑戰的一條可行且具變革潛力的路徑。

14619026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14619026.value: 持久的父母責任與中國低生育率現象

14619026.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14619026.value: Prof Gan, Yiqing Prof Wolbring, Tobias

14619026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14619026.value: Aims: We propose a nuanced conceptualization of enduring parenthood responsibilities (EPR) to understand shifts in intergenerational family dynamics and their potential influence on China’s extremely low fertility. By EPR, we mean parents’ lifelong, child-centered, competitive, and high-standard duties toward their children. We hypothesize that parenting responsibilities have become increasingly intensive and prolonged, which may partly contribute to young adults forgoing childbearing in contemporary China. In the proposed study, we will first examine what constitutes EPR and how young adults perceive and understand it. We will then analyze the relationship between EPR and fertility using both Factorial Survey Experimental (FSE) data and longitudinal observation data from the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS). Finally, we will conduct further moderation analyses by considering cultural norms, socioeconomic resources, and the situation of parent-young adult intergenerational interdependence. Significance: Low fertility is one of China’s most contentious demographic issues, with far-reaching implications for aging, the labor market, and related domains. Existing theories, largely developed in Western contexts, are insufficient to explain China’s situation, where strong traditional family values and a pro-natal culture have long prevailed. Historically, strong intergenerational support and familism facilitated childbearing among young adults. In recent years, however, the responsibilities between parents and children have become increasingly imbalanced, resulting in intensive and prolonged transfers from parents to children, rather than the other way around. Parents are now expected to shoulder substantial, lifelong responsibilities under elevated standards. This intensification and prolongation of parenthood, combined with rising individualism among younger generations, may have partially backfired against the pro-natal culture in China. Novelty: First, EPR is a new concept we will develop to capture nuances in the intergenerational dynamics among Chinese families, which is beyond the recent development of intensive parenthood for childhood. Second, mixed methods—including qualitative research, online surveys for developing EPR scales, and Factorial Survey Experiments (FSE) for understanding the relative importance of different factors on EPR and its linkage with fertility, as well as longitudinal data analysis from the CFPS, will complement one another to provide a deeper and more nuanced understanding of EPR and its relationship to fertility. Third, the approach to China’s low-fertility context extends beyond the short-term effects of having children on young adults, prompting a long-term consideration of intergenerational relationships and fertility. Our findings will help clarify paradoxical fertility patterns and strengthen evidence-based policymaking in the Chinese context. 研究目的和方法：在本研究中，我們創造性的提出「持久性的父母責任」（Enduring Parental Responsibilities，EPR）的概念並對其進行細緻化的拆解，以理解代際家庭關係的轉變及其對中國極低生育率的潛在影響。 EPR指父母對其子女所承擔的終身型、以子女為中心、具有競爭性且以高標準為導向的職責。我們假設當代中國父母養育子女的責任日益強化並延長至更長生命週期階段，這一變化可能促使青年人推遲， 減少，甚至放棄生育。在本研究中，我們首先以定性的方法界定EPR的構成要素，並考察青年群體對這個概念的認知與理解；隨後，結合「析因式情境調查實驗」與 「中國家庭追蹤調查」的縱向觀測數據，分析EPR與生育之間的關係；最後，我們納入文化規範、社會經濟資源以及父母與青年之間的代際相互依賴狀況，進行調節效應分析。 研究意義：低生育是當下中國最具爭議的人口議題之一，關涉老化、勞動市場等許多領域。目前的學術討論主要源自於西方脈絡的理論，難以充分解釋中國長期存在的強傳統家庭觀念與鼓勵生育文化之下的現實。歷史上，強而有力的世代支持與家本位價值曾促進生育；然而，近年來父母與子女之間的責任日益失衡，表現為由父母向子女進行更為密集且更持久的資源轉移和情感支持。社會對父母的期待也標準更高，讓父母承擔更沉重且貫穿一生的職責。父母角色的強化與延伸，再加之年輕一代個體主義的上升，可能在某種程度上對中國的传统的積極生育文化產生了反作用。本研究在中國低生育情境下，將焦點從“生育對青年個體的短期影響”拓展到“代際關係與生育的長期聯動”，從而有助於釐清看似矛盾的生育現象，並為中國語境下的循證政策制定提供更堅實的依據

14619426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14619426.value: 不穩定的工作生涯與未來展望：香港外賣員、照顧工作者與社交媒體內容創作者的生命傳記敘事

14619426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14619426.value: It is estimated that over 150 million individuals are involved in platform-mediated gig work, while over 50 million individuals work as social media content creators globally. Despite differences in the nature of their work and levels of privilege, there is a growing consensus among scholars and policy makers that the lived realities of workers are characterized by algorithmic management, precarious working conditions, and limited social protections, contradicting the flexible and entrepreneurial narratives promoted by labor platforms. While these discussions offer invaluable insights into platform governance, we know relatively little about the longer-term social impacts of precarious platform work on workers’ lives beyond the workplace and their capacity to make future plans. Building on the Principal Investigator’s years of qualitative research on the struggles of platform-mediated workers in various geographical contexts, this 30-month qualitative project examines (1) why individuals – despite being aware of and critical towards labor exploitation and precarity – continue to work on platforms, (2) how prolonged precarious platform work experiences extend into other domains of social life and shape workers’ future projections, and (3) how workers’ narratives of precarity vary across different sectors and life stages in Hong Kong. Theoretically, the project sits at the intersection of platform labor studies and sociological research on precarity and future-making. Platform workers often experience not only insecurity at work but also difficulty in envisioning long-term life trajectories. As many enter platform work at different stages of their lives, these experiences can act as “turning points” that prompt workers to reassess their biographies and aspirations. The project also explores how workers’ future projections are shaped by their dynamic life trajectories and unevenly shaped across social groups, potentially reinforcing or reshaping existing patterns of social inequality. Empirically, the project adopts a biographical approach to examine the cultural narratives and future imaginaries of three types of platform-mediated workers in Hong Kong: delivery workers, care workers, and content creators. This project contributes to scholarly debates on the platformization of service, care, and creative labor by theorizing the temporal dimensions of worker agency, precariousness, and cultural narratives. By offering a culturally grounded analysis of how prolonged precarious platform work experiences shape other domains of workers’ lives in Hong Kong, it has the potential to inform policy interventions, particularly around labor protections and future planning support for platform workers. 據估計，全球有逾一億五千萬人從事平台中介的零工勞動，另有超過五千萬人以社交媒體內容創作為職業。儘管兩者的工作性質及所享有的相對優勢各異，學界與政策制定者已逐漸形成共識：這些工作者普遍面對演算法管理、不穩定的勞動條件及有限的社會保障。這與平台所宣揚的「靈活自主」及「創業精神」論述背道而馳。然而，對於不穩定的平台工作如何在工作場所以外，對工作者的生活帶來較長遠的社會影響，以及如何影響其規劃未來的能力，我們所知仍相對有限。本項為期三十個月的質性研究計劃，旨在探討以下三個問題：第一，為甚麼個體即使意識到勞動剝削與就業不穩定，甚至對此抱持批判態度，仍持續從事平台工作？第二，長期不穩定的平台工作經驗如何延伸至社會生活的其他領域，並形塑工作者的未來展望？第三，在香港，工作者對不穩定處境的敘事如何隨行業及人生階段的不同而呈現差異？本計劃建基於平台勞動研究，以及關於不穩定性與未來建構的社會學研究。平台工作者往往不僅在工作中承受不安全感，亦較難構想長遠的人生軌跡。由於不少人在人生不同階段投身平台工作，這些經驗可能成為「轉捩點」，促使他們重新審視自身的生命歷程與人生抱負。本計劃亦探討工作者的未來展望，如何受其動態多變的人生軌跡所形塑，而這種形塑在不同社會群體之間並不均等，有可能強化或重塑既有的社會不平等。本計劃採用生命傳記方法（biographical approach），考察香港三類平台中介工作者（外賣員、照顧工作者及內容創作者）的文化敘事與未來想像。本計劃透過將工作者能動性、不穩定性與文化敘事的時間維度加以理論化，為服務、照顧及創意勞動平台化的學術討論作出貢獻。透過立足香港文化脈絡，分析長期不穩定的平台工作經驗如何形塑工作者生活的其他領域，本計劃有望為平台工作者的勞工保障及未來規劃支援等政策介入提供依據。

14620226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14620226.value: 運用「正向摩擦」在人工智能新聞環境中重拾人類能動性：一項兩階段混合方法研究

14620226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14620226.value: Prof McDonald, Thomas Niall Prof Zhang, Jingwen

14620226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14620226.value: Generative AI (GenAI) is rapidly changing how we access and process information. While the convenience of getting instant answers and summaries is immense, this very efficiency carries a significant risk. The seamless, “frictionless” experience encourages users to passively accept AI-generated content without critical thought. This is especially concerning for news consumption, where it can erode critical evaluation skills, diminish our sense of control (human agency), and increase vulnerability to sophisticated misinformation. This project moves beyond simply debating whether to use AI, and instead asks: how can we interact with it to become smarter and more autonomous news consumers and thinkers? Our research confronts the frictionless design ideal by introducing and testing the concept of “positive friction.” These are small, deliberately designed moments of pause or challenge that interrupt mindless consumption and prompt users to engage more deeply with AI-generated news content. The goal is to transform the user from a passive recipient into an active, critical partner in the information process. Our approach is a two-phase, mixed-methods study. First, a foundational qualitative study will explore how young adults currently integrate GenAI into their daily news routines, providing a rich understanding of their real-world behaviors and perceptions. The insights from this phase will directly inform the design of Phase 2: a longitudinal field experiment. Here, we will develop and empirically test our positive friction interventions over six months to measure their effectiveness in fostering more critical engagement and enhancing human agency. This project will deliver new knowledge on how to design more responsible human-AI interactions. Crucially, we will translate our findings into actionable, evidence-based guidelines for educators teaching news literacy in the AI era, for designers building more human-centric interfaces, and for the general public on how to use these powerful tools wisely. The ultimate aim is to foster a more thoughtful and empowered relationship with AI, ensuring it enhances, rather than erodes, human intellect. 生成式人工智能（GenAI）正迅速改變我們獲取與處理資訊的方式。雖然能即時獲得答案與摘要帶來極大的便利，但這種效率本身卻隱藏著重大風險。這種無縫且「無摩擦」的體驗，會促使使用者在未經批判性思考的情況下，被動地接受AI生成的內容。這在新聞消費領域尤其令人擔憂，因為此現象可能侵蝕批判性評估能力、削弱我們的掌控感（人類能動性），並增加我們受到精巧虛假信息影響的風險。本研究項目不僅止於單純辯論是否該使用AI，而是進一步探問：我們該如何與AI互動，才能成為更聰明、更具自主性的新聞消費者與思考者？ 我們的研究透過引入並測試「正向摩擦」的概念，來挑戰這種無摩擦的設計理想。這些是經過刻意設計的微小停頓或挑戰時刻，旨在中斷無意識的消費行為，並促使使用者更深入地與 AI 生成的新聞內容互動。目標是將使用者從被動的接收者，轉變為資訊處理過程中積極且具批判精神的夥伴。 本研究採用兩階段的混合研究法。首先，將透過基礎性質性研究，探討年輕族群目前如何將生成式AI融入日常新聞閱讀習慣，藉此深入理解他們的實際行為與認知。此階段所得的洞見將直接應用於第二階段——一項縱向田野實驗——的設計。在此階段，我們將耗時六個月開發並實證測試「正向摩擦」干預措施，以衡量其在促進更具批判性的參與及強化人類能動性方面的成效。 本計畫將提供關於如何設計更具責任感的AI互動模式之新知。關鍵在於，我們將把研究成果轉化為可操作且以實證為基礎的指引，供教育工作者在AI時代教授新聞素養、供設計師打造更以人為本的介面，以及供大眾學習如何明智地使用這些強大的工具。最終目標是建立與AI之間更深思熟慮且賦權的關係，確保AI能增強而非削弱人類的智力。

14620526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14620526.value: 關鍵詞的流轉：解析當代中國相關概念的翻譯與傳播（2001–2025）

14620526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14620526.value: This research project explores the evolving landscape of key concepts that are perceived as defining contemporary Chinese culture and society, examining their translation, evolution, and cultural significance. These key concepts will be identified through a search in a large corpus of texts related to China that will identify words that occur significantly more frequently than in a comparable reference corpus of unrelated terms. The study is grounded in the historical use of key concepts as tools for understanding cultural nuances, seeking to move beyond the two dominant perspectives: traditionalists, who reference the canonical texts of Confucianism, and modernists, who advocate for new terms reflecting current realities, believing that there has been a rupture with the past. The project aims to tackle several key questions: How does translation affect the interpretation of key concepts? How have the terms used to reference these concepts evolved over time in both Chinese and English contexts? What differences exist in how these concepts are framed in media from the two languages? This project will first compile two large corpora of texts: one in Chinese and one in English, spanning the years 2001 to 2025. These corpora will be compared against reference corpora in English and Chinese to identify keywords. Then keywords will be subjected to a variety of advanced digital humanities methods—such as data mining, sentiment analysis, and network visualization—to uncover hitherto patterns and connections on both the macro and the micro level. At the macro level, changes in usage over time and across geographic or cultural distance will be investigated to reveal how public perceptions shift over time, influenced by political and social changes. At the micro level, the project will uncover the complexities of individual terms like “China Dream” (zhongguo meng) and “copycat” (shanzhai), which may serve as case studies illustrating the cultural and contextual differences between languages. Ultimately, this research aims to illuminate not just the keywords themselves but the underlying concepts and cultural narratives they represent. By examining these concepts, the project aspires to expose existing stereotypes to foster greater cross-cultural understanding between China and the global community, revealing how language and translation shape our perception of a rapidly changing world. The findings will contribute to ongoing discussions in translation studies, cultural discourse, and digital humanities, offering fresh insights into the dynamics of language and culture in contemporary China. 本研究項目旨在探索那些定義當代中國文化與社會的關鍵概念及其流轉過程，分析這些概念的翻譯、演變及文化意義。研究將[MOU1.1]建立一個涵蓋中國相關文本的大型語料庫，識別出在語料庫中出現頻率顯著高於對照語料庫的詞彙，以提取這些關鍵概念。本研究立足於關鍵概念在歷史中的使用，將其作為理解文化細微差異的工具，試圖突破兩種常見的主要觀點[MOU2.1]：其一是傳統主義者的觀點以儒家經典文本作為參考；其二是現代主義者的觀點提倡新術語以反映當前現實，並主張這代表與過去的斷裂。 本研究聚焦於幾個關鍵問題：翻譯如何影響關鍵概念的解讀？用以表達這些概念的術語在中英語境中如何隨時間演變？這些概念在中英兩種語言媒體中的呈現框架存在哪些差異？為了回應這些問題，本研究將建立兩個大型文本語料庫：分別為中文文本語料庫及英文文本語料庫，涵蓋2001年至2025年的相關資料。這些語料庫將與中英文的參照語料庫進行對比，以提取關鍵詞。隨後，研究將運用多種先進的數字人文方法（如數據探勘、情感分析及網絡可視化），以宏觀及微觀層面揭示未曾發現的模式與聯繫。 在宏觀層面，研究將分析詞彙使用隨時間及地理或文化距離的變化，揭示大眾認知如何受到政治與社會變遷的影響。在微觀層面，研究將深入探討如「中國夢」（China Dream）與「山寨」（copycat）等具體術語[MOU3.1]，透過具體案例展示不同語言之間文化及語境的差異。 本研究的最終目標不僅在於探究關鍵詞本身，亦在於揭示其背後所代表的深層概念及文化敘事。透過對這些概念的檢視，本研究希望挑戰現有的刻板印象，促進中國與國際社會之間更深層次的跨文化理解，並揭示語言與翻譯如何塑造我們對快速變化世界的認知。相關研究成果將助力翻譯研究、文化話語研究及數字人文領域的討論，為解析當代中國的語言與文化提供新穎視角。

14620926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14620926.value: 需求滿足的多重層次：理解人工智能中介學習情境中的學生幸福感

14620926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14620926.value: Background The rapid integration of AI into higher education is reshaping how students learn, communicate, and prepare for future careers. While much scholarship has emphasized risks such as AI-related anxiety and stress, less attention has been paid to how engagement with AI influences students’ broader well-being. Drawing on Self-Determination Theory (SDT), this project argues that the psychological needs of competence, autonomy, and relatedness form a foundation for flourishing in AI-mediated environments. These needs can be satisfied at two levels: a provision-based level, supported by external access, resources, and training provisions, and a self-integrative level, reflecting personal internalization of skills and agency, such as critical evaluation and purposeful engagement for social good. We propose that these layers of need fulfillment differentially associate with well-being, with higher-level satisfaction more strongly linked to eudaimonic outcomes such as purpose, beyond momentary hedonic enjoyment. Purpose The project aims to investigate unique well-being experiences of students in the face of AI, and how psychological need satisfaction shapes students’ hedonic and eudaimonic well-being, and in turn, how well-being influences their engagement with AI. Guided by SDT, the project focuses on the three basic needs and introduces the concept of layered need satisfaction to distinguish between resource-based fulfillment and deeper, self-integrative fulfillment. Methodology The study adopts a mixed-method longitudinal design. Quantitative surveys across three time points will track changes in psychological need satisfaction, AI-related behaviors, and well-being indicators. Complementary qualitative interviews will capture how students experience well-being in AI environments, including the tensions, uncertainties, and opportunities they encounter; and the adaptive strategies they develop for wellbeing. This combination will illuminate both the mechanisms and the lived meanings of flourishing with AI. Contributions Theoretically, the project will advance SDT by introducing layered need satisfaction in the AI era, showing why resource-based level is insufficient and why deeper internalization of competence, autonomy, and relatedness is critical for long-term flourishing. Empirically, it is among the first longitudinal, mixed-method studies to trace how AI engagement shapes, and is shaped by both hedonic and eudaimonic well-being, shifting the focus from short-term risks toward the developmental trajectories of purpose and growth. Practically, the project will provide evidence-based guidance for higher education, moving beyond teaching AI as a technical skill toward creating environments that cultivate flourishing. By centering students’ voices, it will inform policies and pedagogies that prepare students not just to cope with AI, but to thrive with it.

14621826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14621826.value: 融合非因果依賴關係的因果建模、推理與發現

14621826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14621826.value: Causal modelling has proved useful in several research fields, including philosophy and artificial intelligence. In philosophy, it serves as a formal tool for studying important concepts such as causation and explanation and for examining logical and epistemological foundations of causal reasoning. In artificial intelligence, it is applied to automate the discovery of causal relationships from data and to design machine learning models that leverage causal information. The standard framework of causal modelling focuses exclusively on causal dependencies and assumes that variables of interest do not share intimate non-causal relations, such as conceptual, compositional, or constitutive dependencies. While this restriction simplifies many problems and enables elegant theorization, it limits the framework's ability to represent complex systems that involve both causal and non-causal dependencies. In earlier work, the PI proposed a way to generalize Judea Pearl’s structural causal models to incorporate both causal and non-causal dependencies. While still preliminary, this proposal shows promise for being sufficiently flexible to accommodate a variety of philosophical theories and sufficiently expressive to support counterfactual reasoning. Moreover, its use of directed graphs to represent dependency structures makes it plausible to adapt existing causal discovery algorithms to this more general framework. This project aims to systematically develop the proposal to substantiate these merits. The work is divided into three parts. The first part examines the philosophical foundations and interpretations of the formalism and evaluates the compatibility of various philosophical theories with the basic formal setup. The second part studies interventional and counterfactual reasoning within the generalized models and investigates the distinctive features introduced by the new framework. The third part explores methods for inferring dependency structures—both causal and non-causal—from data, guided by several prominent approaches in the causal discovery literature. We adopt a mixed methodology in this project, which integrates philosophical analysis, mathematical investigation, and computational experimentation. Philosophical interpretation and argumentation will be employed to clarify conceptual foundations and examine how the proposed formal setup aligns with or challenges significant theses in metaphysics and the philosophy of science. Mathematical derivation and demonstration will be used to explore the consequences of alternative formal definitions and establish theoretical results about interventional and counterfactual reasoning, as well as algorithms for structural discovery. Finally, experiments on synthetic and real data will be conducted to test and illustrate the behavior of the proposed methods and evaluate their feasibility and reliability. 因果建模已被證明在多個研究領域中十分有用，包括哲學與人工智能。在哲學中，它作為一種形式工具，可用於研究因果性和科學說明等重要概念，並考察因果推理的邏輯與認識論基礎。在人工智能中，因果建模則被應用於自動從數據中發現因果關係，並設計能夠利用因果資訊以改進決策的機器學習模型。 因果建模的標準框架專注於因果依賴關係，並假定相關變量之間並不存在密切的非因果關係，例如概念、組成或構成上的依賴關係。儘管這一限制簡化了許多問題，並促成了優雅的理論建構，但它也限制了該框架表徵複雜系統的能力，因為此類系統往往同時包含因果與非因果依賴關係。 在此前的研究中，我們提出了一種推廣標準因果模型的方法，使其能夠同時納入因果與非因果依賴關係。儘管該方案仍屬初步，但它展現出一定前景：一方面，它具有足夠的靈活性，可容納多種哲學理論；另一方面，它也具有足夠的表達能力，可支持反事實推理。此外，由於該方案使用有向圖來表徵依賴結構，因此有理由認為，現有的因果發現演算法可以被調整並應用於這一更一般的框架。本項目旨在系統發展這一方案，以充分證成上述優點。 本研究分為三個部分。第一部分考察該形式體系的哲學基礎與詮釋，並評估各種哲學理論與其基本形式設定之間的相容性。第二部分研究推廣模型中的干預推理與反事實推理，並探討新框架所引入的獨特特徵。第三部分則在因果發現文獻中若干重要進路的指引下，探索如何從數據中推斷依賴結構，包括因果與非因果依賴結構。 本項目採用混合方法，結合哲學分析、數學推導與計算實驗。研究將運用哲學詮釋與論證來澄清概念基礎，並考察所提出的形式設定如何契合或挑戰形上學與科學哲學中的重要論題；運用數學推導與證明來探索不同形式定義的後果，並建立關於干預推理、反事實推理以及結構發現算法的理論結果；最後，將在合成數據與真實數據上進行實驗，以測試並展示所提出的方法，並評估其可行性與可靠性。

14622826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14622826.value: 建構大型語言模型與人類決策協調的通用框架

14622826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14622826.value: Large language models (LLMs) are transforming how people think, work, and make decisions. Because these models are trained on vast amounts of human data, they can reproduce patterns of reasoning and social behavior that resemble human responses. This capability has motivated researchers to explore whether LLMs can serve as substitutes for human participants in behavioral and management experiments, a methodological approach known as LLM-based simulation. Such simulations offer the potential to make research cheaper, faster, more scalable, and reproducible. However, existing studies suggest that while LLMs can replicate human results in simple and well-structured tasks, they often fail to replicate human behavior in socially complex environments. These are settings that involve interdependent payoffs, uncertainty, or reasoning about others’ intentions. Such divergences limit the validity of LLM-based simulations and highlight the need for a deeper theoretical foundation to understand and improve alignment between human and model reasoning. This project systematically examines and addresses this challenge of aligning LLMs with human behavior in socially complex environments. In Phase I, using Kremer and Debo’s (2016) sequential decision experiment as a benchmark, we replicate the human study with GPT-4o and find that model behavior departs significantly from human data. In Phase II, drawing on Newell and Simon’s (1971) theory of human problem solving, we develop a theory-driven framework that conceptualizes reasoning as structured information processing within a defined problem space. Within this framework, two mechanisms, context formation (how tasks are internally represented) and context navigation (how reasoning proceeds selectively under uncertainty), are formalized to improve LLMs’ behavior. We analytically demonstrate the validity of this framework and automate the prompt generation process to adapt it to specific experimental contexts. In Phase III, we empirically validate the framework using the Kremer and Debo (2016) task, extend it to other socially complex experiments in management, and evaluate its robustness across different models and behavioral profiles to ensure both internal and external validity. Through this three-phase design, the project will generate new insights into why LLMs diverge from human behavior and how alignment can be improved through structured, theory-based interventions. The resulting framework will serve as a roadmap for future research that seeks to align human decision behavior with LLM performance and to enhance the credibility and utility of LLM-based simulations in the behavioral and social sciences. 大型語言模型（LLM）正在改變人們的思考、工作和決策方式。由於這些模型是基於海量的人類資料進行訓練，它們能夠重現類似於人類反應的推理模式和社會行為。這種能力促使研究人員探索LLM是否可以取代人類參與者參與行為和管理實驗，這種方法被稱為基於LLM的模擬。此類模擬可望降低研究成本、加快研究速度、提高可擴展性和可重複性。然而，現有研究表明，儘管LLM能夠在簡單且結構良好的任務中復現人類的結果，但它們往往無法在複雜的社會環境中復現人類行為。這些環境涉及相互依賴的利益、不確定性或對他人意圖的推理。這種差異限制了基於LLM的模擬的有效性，並凸顯了需要更深層的理論基礎來理解和改進人類推理與模型推理之間的一致性。 本計畫系統性地研究並解決LLM在複雜社會環境中與人類行為一致的挑戰。在第一階段，我們以 Kremer 和 Debo (2016) 的序列決策實驗為基準，使用 GPT-4o 復現了人類研究，發現模型行為與人類數據有顯著差異。在第二階段，我們借鑒 Newell 和 Simon (1971) 的人類問題解決理論，建構了一個理論驅動的框架，將推理概念化為在特定問題空間內進行的結構化資訊處理。在這個框架下，我們形式化了兩種機制：情境形成（任務的內在表徵方式）和情境導航（推理如何在不確定性下選擇性地進行），以改進邏輯學習模型 (LLM) 的行為。我們透過分析驗證了該框架的有效性，並實現了提示產生過程的自動化，使其能夠適應特定的實驗情境。在第三階段，我們使用 Kremer 和 Debo (2016) 的任務對該框架進行了實證驗證，並將其擴展到其他社會複雜的管理實驗中，同時評估了其在不同模型和行為模式中的穩健性，以確保其內部效度和外部效度。 透過這個三階段設計，該計畫將深入探究邏輯邏輯模型（LLM）為何偏離人類行為，以及如何透過結構化的、理論為基礎的介入措施來改善二者的一致性。最終形成的框架將為未來的研究提供路線圖，這些研究旨在使人類決策行為與邏輯邏輯模型的表現保持一致，並提升基於邏輯邏輯模型的模擬在行為和社會科學領域的可信度和實用性。

14623126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14623126.value: 冷戰天使：韓國「小天使」兒童民俗芭蕾舞團的少女政治、外交與軟實力

14623126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14623126.value: This research project investigates South Korea’s Little Angels Children’s Folk Ballet as a pivotal case study in the gendered cultural diplomacy of the Cold War. Established in 1962 under the patronage of the Unification Church and the Park Chung-hee regime, the troupe was deployed internationally to project an image of South Korea as a modern, yet tradition-bound, non-threatening ally. This study argues that the Little Angels’ performances constituted a form of jaerong (winsomeness) diplomacy—a distinct mode of soft power that mobilized the affective labor of pre-adolescent girls to aestheticize authoritarian development and facilitate the US-ROK alliance. Through a critical analysis of state-produced newsreels (Daehan News), media archives, and contemporary artistic reinterpretations, the project dissects the visual and performative construction of this “angelic” girlhood. It demonstrates how carefully curated elements—hybridized choreography, traditional costumes, and narratives of purity—served to erase the trauma of war and colonialization, presenting a sanitized national identity for Western consumption. A comparative analysis with the jazz singer Yoon Bok-hee illuminates the state’s preference for a controllable, “traditional” femininity over transgressive modernity. By theorizing the “girled body” as a biopolitical instrument, the research reveals how gendered performance was central to Cold War nation-building. It ultimately traces the discursive legacy of this state-sponsored diplomacy to the contemporary Korean Wave, challenging market-centric narratives of Hallyu by highlighting its roots in a state-initiated tradition of deploying disciplined youth for ideological ends. The project contributes to Cold War studies, visual culture, and gender studies by uncovering the intimate linkages between cultural production, gendered politics, and neocolonial power.
