There are three research questions and one reflection question. Why and how can a wireless ultrasonic motor system solve the aforementioned problems due to the gearbox, brake and inflexible arrangement? Why and how can an integrated encoderless wireless power transfer topology solve the aforementioned problems due to the encoder, energy storage, electronic controller and power converter at the motor side. Why and how can a primary-side control strategy provide all motion controls at the transmitter side without involving any electronic controller at the motor side? How to measure success of the proposed motor system as compared with the existing motor system for exoskeletons? The purpose of this proposal is to propose a novel integrated encoderless wireless ultrasonic motor system for exoskeletons. The corresponding objectives are: (1) develop a novel wireless ultrasonic motor system; (2) develop a novel integrated encoderless wireless power transfer topology; (3) develop a novel primary-side control strategy for the integrated encoderless wireless ultrasonic motor system; (4) perform analytical modeling and finite element analysis of the proposed motor system; (5) construct a prototype of the proposed motor system for experimentation and evaluation as compared with the existing motor system for exoskeletons. 隨著年齡增長或神經肌肉功能受損，通常會伴隨肌肉力量的下降。若未能及時介入，肌肉無力的人容易失去在社區中獨立生活的能力，從而增加家庭與醫療系統的負擔。外骨骼是一種外部穿戴裝置，可以補償肌肉力量的下降，以支援行走與操作。由於全球人口老化趨勢以及對神經肌肉疾病的日益關注，外骨骼的發展極具需求。 由於外骨骼是由電動機驅動，其性能受到電動機的轉矩密度、效率、可控性、成本與靈活性等因素的嚴格限制。現有外骨骼普遍採用直流伺服電動機，並配合齒輪箱與編碼器以獲得高轉矩與反饋控制。然而，它們存在若干主要問題：1) 齒輪箱體積龐大、效率低、噪音大且存在回差；2) 編碼器價格昂貴、結構脆弱且需精密安裝；3) 電動機需以電線連接並永久固定於外骨骼框架，必然降低靈活性與穿戴性；4) 由於外骨骼用於支援肌肉無力者，這些電動機需安裝制動裝置以在斷電或電池耗盡時提供失效保護，導致額外的體積與成本。 因此提出三個研究問題與一個反思問題：為何以及如何透過無線超聲波電動機系統解決齒輪箱、裝制與不靈活佈局所帶來的問題？為何以及如何透過整合式無編碼器無線電力傳輸拓撲解決編碼器、能量儲存、電子控制器與電動機端電力轉換器的問題？為何以及如何透過初級側控制策略，在發射端完成所有運動控制，而無需在電動機端配置電子控制器？如何衡量所提出電動機系統相較於現有外骨骼電動機系統的成功？ 本項目的目的在於提出一種新型整合式無編碼器無線超聲波電動機系統以應用於外骨骼。其具體目標包括：(1) 開發新型無線超聲波電動機系統；(2) 開發新型整合式無編碼器無線電力傳輸拓撲；(3) 開發新型初級側控制策略以應用於整合式無編碼器無線超聲波電動機系統；(4) 對所提出的電動機系統進行解析建模與有限元素分析；(5) 建構所提出電動機系統的原型，並進行實驗與評估，以與現有外骨骼電動機系統比較。

15204826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15204826.value: 面向碳中和建築的可重複使用冷彎型鋼結構

15204826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15204826.value: In high-density urban environments such as Hong Kong, construction activities are major contributors to carbon emissions. Although the Hong Kong Climate Action Plan 2030+ targets a 26-36% reduction in carbon emissions through recycling initiatives, these measures alone are insufficient to meet the city’s sustainability goals. Recycling still requires substantial energy input for remanufacturing components, whereas the direct reuse of building elements demands minimal additional energy. Promoting the direct reuse of building elements, therefore, offers a more impactful strategy, extending the service life of buildings, conserving natural resources, minimising construction waste, and significantly reducing carbon emissions. This project addresses a critical gap in sustainable construction: the lack of safe and practical methods for reusing cold-formed steel (CFS), a lightweight material extensively employed in modern buildings. The research objectives are closely aligned with the Hong Kong Chief Executive’s 2025 Policy Address, Green and Low-carbon Living Environment - Reduce and Recycle Waste to Achieve “Zero Landfill”. The research focuses on two central challenges: first, determining how to reliably predict the strength of CFS structural components for reuse; second, building the trust and confidence necessary for adoption of reuse by industry, regulators, and clients. To meet these challenges, the project will deliver two key innovations. The “Reuse Limit State” will establish an engineering framework to ensure the structural reliability of reused steel components, while the “Reuse Sustainability Index” will provide a user-friendly tool for quantifying environmental, economic, and adaptability benefits similar to a nutritional label on a food product that enables informed decisions. The research approach integrates full-scale testing of CFS frames under repeated loading, disassembly, and reassembly to simulate real reuse conditions, with advanced computational modeling to analyse performance over multiple reuse cycles. It is also proposed to conduct tests on corroded steel frames to assess the reuse potential after long-term exposure. Preliminary investigations already show that CFS connections can withstand several reuse cycles without compromising safety, demonstrating strong potential of CFS reuse. The project will generate new technical knowledge on structural behavior, reuse limit state, and decision-making tools for stakeholders. It will also produce educational resources for future professionals to apply reuse strategies effectively. By advancing the safe direct reuse of CFS structures, this research will deliver both environmental and economic benefits and position Hong Kong as a global leader in carbon-neutral construction, with a better impact on sustainable building practices. 在香港等高密度城市環境中，建築活動是碳排放的主要來源之一。儘管《香港氣候行動藍圖2030+》訂下通過回收利用措施來實現減排26%至36%的目標，但單靠此類舉措並不足以達致本港的可持續發展願景。回收再造仍需耗用大量能源以重新製造建築構件，而直接重用建築元件則僅需極少量額外能源。因此，推廣建築構件的直接重用是更為有效的策略，既可延長建築物的使用壽命，節約自然資源，又能減少建築廢物，並顯著降低碳排放。 本項目旨在填補一項可持續建築領域的關鍵空白——即缺乏安全且實務可行的方法來重複使用冷彎型鋼。此種輕質材料在現代建築中應用甚廣。本研究目標與香港特別行政區行政長官《2025年施政報告》中「建設綠色低碳生活環境——減廢回收，達致零堆填」的施政方針緊密呼應。 本研究聚焦於兩項核心挑戰：其一，如何可靠地預測冷彎型鋼結構構件經重用後的強度；其二，如何建立業界、監管機構及客戶對採用重用方案的信賴與信心。為克服此等挑戰，本項目將推出兩項關鍵創新。其一為「重用極限狀態」，將建立一套工程框架以確保重用鋼構件的結構可靠性；其二為「重用可持續性指數」，此乃一個簡便易用的工具，用以量化環境、經濟及適應性效益，其功能猶如食品上的營養標籤，有助於用家作出知情決策。 研究方法結合了對冷彎型鋼框架進行重複加載、拆卸及重新組裝的全尺寸測試，以模擬真實重新利用的情境，並輔以先進的計算建模技術，分析其歷經多次重用週期後的性能表現。此外，亦擬對鏽蝕鋼框架進行測試，以評估其經長期暴露後的重用潛力。初步研究已顯示，冷彎型鋼連接節點能承受多次重用週期而無損安全性，足見冷彎型鋼重用的巨大潛力。 本項目將在結構力學性能、重用極限狀態及決策輔助方法等方面，產出全新的技術知識，同時亦會編製教育資源，助未來從業人員有效運用重用策略。通過推進冷彎型鋼結構的安全直接重用，本研究不僅能帶來環境與經濟的雙重裨益，更可將香港定位為全球碳中和建築的引領者，對可持續建築實踐發揮更廣泛且深遠的正面影響。

15204926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15204926.value: 面向O-RAN AI 服務的xApp自動生成

15204926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15204926.value: Traditional Radio Access Network (RAN) systems are closed and monolithic, stifling innovation. The openness and programmability enabled by Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) are envisioned to transform traditional cellular networks towards more intelligent and interoperable RAN, with control-plane applications - xApps. The development of xApps, however, remains time-consuming and cumbersome, often requiring months of manual coding and testing, which hinders the roll-out of new network functionalities and AI services. This creates an urgent need for fast and flexible xApp development. This project will develop AutORAN, the first LLM-driven xApp synthesis framework for agile AI services, which fully automates the entire xApp development pipeline. In a nutshell, AutORAN turns high-level user intents into swiftly deployable xApps within minutes, eliminating the need for manual coding or testing. Thus, a network operator can describe desired network functions or AI services in natural language, while AutORAN generates the corresponding xApp to fulfill the requirements. Realizing this vision entails technical challenges that existing solutions cannot address: 1) Under-specified user requirements: Users often struggle to precisely articulate their needs due to the complexity of O-RAN, causing LLMs to misinterpret the true intents. 2) LLMs' lack of O-RAN domain knowledge: general-purpose LLMs lack specialized knowledge of O-RAN standards, leading to hallucinated code or non-compliant API calls. 3) Entangled xApp logic and interfaces: A typical xApp comprises two parts: the core logic code (e.g., AI control logic), and the interfacing code connecting to O-RAN components. Thus, generating an entire xApp in one shot is often error-prone. To tackle these issues, we develop a fully automated xApp program synthesis framework. 1) We will develop a new requirement refinement and structuring module, which defines a structured template to guide users to clearly specify desired xApps (e.g., objectives, inputs, policies). This requirement structuring process helps capture the true intent and provides LLMs an unambiguous specification. 2) We will develop an automated knowledge retrieval module, which retrieves relevant O-RAN documentation. This in-context knowledge injection will greatly improve code generation robustness. 3) We will disentangle the xApp synthesis into a new two-stage generation and validation process. We will first prompt LLMs to synthesize correct control logic, and then integrate and interface with O-RAN to produce complete xApps. We envision that AutORAN will drastically accelerate xApp development (from user intent elicitation to new AI service roll-out) and thereby streamline O-RAN innovation. 傳統無線接取網路（RAN）架構封閉且缺乏彈性，限制了創新發展。O-RAN 透過開放與可程式化架構，引入控制平面應用程式（xApps），推動行動網路朝向更智慧化與互通的方向發展。然而，現有 xApp 開發流程高度依賴人工撰寫程式與測試，往往需耗費數月時間，難以快速部署新的 AI 網路服務。本計畫將開發 AutORAN，首個由大型語言模型（LLM）驅動的自然語言 xApp 開發框架。AutORAN 能將網路營運商以自然語言描述的需求，自動轉換為可部署的 xApp，將開發時間從數月縮短至數分鐘，大幅提升 O-RAN 應用創新效率。 本研究主要面對三項挑戰：(1) 使用者需求描述不完整或不明確；(2) 通用 LLM 缺乏 O-RAN 專業知識，容易產生錯誤程式碼；(3) xApp 核心邏輯與 O-RAN 介面高度耦合，增加生成難度。為解決上述問題，AutORAN 將提出三項核心技術：(1) 需求精煉與結構化模組：引導使用者以標準化方式描述需求，提升意圖理解準確性。(2) 自動化知識檢索模組：自動擷取相關 O-RAN 標準文件與範例，增強 LLM 的領域知識。(3) 兩階段生成與驗證機制：先生成核心控制邏輯，再完成 O-RAN 介面整合，以提高程式碼正確性與可靠性。預期 AutORAN 可大幅加速 xApp 的設計、開發與部署流程，進一步促進 O-RAN 生態系統的創新發展。

15205426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15205426.value: 首次利用5G蜂窩網絡GNSS設備密集觀測水汽數據同化至數值天氣預報模型的區域預報改進實驗

15205426.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15205426.value: Prof Chan, Pak-Wai Dr Xie, Yuanfu

15205426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205426.value: Extreme precipitation events pose severe risks to infrastructure, public safety, and economic continuity in coastal regions like Hong Kong (HK) and Guangdong. The record-breaking rainstorm in HK on 7–8 September 2023, which resulted in billions of dollars in losses, underscores the urgency of improving forecasting capabilities. A critical challenge lies in the scarcity of observational data for key atmospheric variables. One of such key variables is atmospheric water vapor. Current data sources, such as radiosondes and Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) stations in HK and Guangdong, are limited. For instance, HK has only one radiosonde and no GNSS water vapor stations. The PI’s preliminary work using data from Chinese Mainland showed that assimilating more water vapor data into Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) models can significantly improve the accuracy of rainfall forecasting. This project aims to address this water vapor data scarcity gap by exploring a new source of data, which is to derive water vapor from GNSS devices of densely distributed 5th Generation (5G) communication stations. The two collaborators of this project, China Mobile Group and the Huawei Technologies, have installed a dense 5G network in Guangdong. The equipped GNSS devices allow the estimation of water vapor data. The two collaborators agreed to provide the PI GNSS data from at least 1,505 5G stations across the Guangdong Province, which is approximately 20 times more than the 70 GNSS stations available from the China Meteorological Administration (CMA). Water vapor data from these 5G GNSS stations will be estimated using GNSS Precise Point Positioning (PPP) technique. Subsequently the water vapor data will be assimilated into NWP model’s data assimilation system to enhance the initial conditions, with which the NWP models can produce an improved weather forecasting result, particularly an improved rainfall forecasting result. This project will (1) first develop a PPP method to process 5G GNSS data of various quality and evaluate the accuracy characteristics of the derived water vapor data; (2) then identify the optimal data assimilation scheme for different weather conditions; (3) and finally validate the project research findings in Government agency’s operational weather forecasting settings through several extreme weather case studies. This novel project is expected to significantly enhance the precipitation forecasting accuracy for HK and Guangdong region. With the increasing deployment of 5G stations in China and worldwide, the research findings will benefit the residents in a much larger community.

15205626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15205626.value: 面向低電壓、高集成度與高力學输出人工肌肉的多層級紡織介電彈性體致動器

15205626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205626.value: Dielectric elastomer actuators function as artificial muscles, rapidly expanding or contracting under electric field control with high stretchability, energy density, and speed. However, inherent material limitations, such as low electromechanical sensitivity and high viscosity, cause high driving voltages and performance decay at high frequencies. Additionally, conventional dielectric elastomer actuators rely on flat "sandwich" structures, and stacking layers to increase force is inefficient and unscalable, causing integration challenges and limited output force for practical applications. To overcome these challenges, we propose a hierarchical design strategy. At the material level, we will incorporate dielectric nanoparticles with surface carboxyl groups into the polymer. These particles physically increase the dielectric constant, while the carboxyl groups chemically form hydrogen bonds as dynamic crosslinks, partially replacing covalent crosslinks in the polymer network to reduce viscosity and elastic modulus. These effects enable lower driving voltages and improved actuation performance at high frequencies. At the actuator level, we will transcend planar 2D designs by a 1D fiber-based approach, leveraging textile hierarchy (fiber→yarn→ fabric), mirroring the human muscle hierarchy (muscle fiber→fascicle→muscle), to achieve compact, scalable, and robust fabrication and integration. This textile engineering approach enhances the force output of dielectric elastomer actuators while preserving their flexibility, closely mimicking the properties of natural muscle. The project comprises three parts: 1) Material Development: We will optimize the nanocomposite by tailoring nanoparticle size, concentration, and carboxylation to establish structure-property relationships for dielectric constant, elastic modulus, and viscoelasticity; 2) Fiber & Yarn Actuators: We will manufacture fiber actuators and assemble them into yarns. We will experimentally and simulationally characterize their mechanical properties and actuation performance, and develop an analytical model to guide yarn design based on fiber geometry, number, and twist level. We will systematically characterize structural integrity, durability, and resistance to bending, compression, friction, and moisture to evaluate practical usability; 3) Fabric Actuators: We will integrate yarn actuators into woven fabrics and perform comprehensive characterization and modeling, focusing on weaving patterns, yarn densities, float lengths, internal interactions, and overall actuation deformation and force. We will quantify actuation transmission efficiency across hierarchical levels to refine the structural design for higher actuation performance. If successful, this project will advance soft actuator technology by offering a novel hybrid material enhancement strategy, a scalable textile-based integration route, and new theoretical models, paving the way for high-performance artificial muscles in diverse fields like healthcare, rehabilitation, soft robotics, and wearable devices. 介電彈性體致動器如同人造肌肉，在電場控制下能夠快速伸縮，並具有高應變、高能量密度和高速度。然而，其固有的材料局限性，例如低電機械靈敏度和高粘度，導致高致動電壓和高頻下的性能衰減。此外，傳統的介電彈性體致動器依賴平面三明治結構，透過堆疊層數來增加致動力效率低下且難以擴展，這給整合帶來了挑戰，並限制了實際應用中的輸出力。 為了克服這些挑戰，我們提出了一種分層設計策略。在材料層面，我們將表面帶有羧基的介電奈米顆粒引入聚合物中。這些顆粒能夠物理性地提高介電常數，而羧基則透過化學方式形成氫鍵作為動態交聯，部分取代聚合物網絡中的共價交聯，從而降低黏度和彈性模量。這些效應使得致動器能夠在高頻下實現更低的致動電壓和更優異的致動性能。在致動器層面，我們將超越傳統的二維平面設計，採用基於一維纖維的方法，利用紡織品的層級結構，模擬人體肌肉的層級結構，從而實現緊湊、可擴展且穩健的製造和整合。這種紡織工程方法能夠增強介電彈性體致動器的機械輸出，同時保持其柔韌性，使人造肌肉更接近天然肌肉的特性。 本專案包含三個部分：1）材料開發：我們將透過調整奈米顆粒的尺寸、濃度和羧基化程度來優化奈米複合材料，從而建立介電常數、彈性模量和黏彈性等結構-性能關係；2）纖維和紗線致動器：我們將製造纖維致動器並將其組裝成紗線。我們將透過實驗和模擬來表徵其機械性能和致動性能，並開發一個分析模型，以根據纖維的幾何形狀、數量和撚度來指導紗線設計。我們將系統地表徵結構完整性、耐久性以及抗彎曲、抗壓縮、抗摩擦和抗濕性能，以評估其實際應用價值；3）布料致動器：我們將把紗線致動器集成為布料，並進行全面的表徵和建模，重點關注編織圖案、紗線密度、浮線長度、內部相互作用以及整體致動變形和內部相互作用。我們將量化不同層級的致動傳遞效率，以優化結構設計，從而獲得更高的致動性能。 如果成功，本計畫將透過提供一種新型混合材料增強策略、一種可擴展的基於紡織品的整合方法以及新的理論模型，推進軟體致動器技術的發展，為醫療保健、復健、軟體機器人和可穿戴設備等多個領域的高性能人造肌肉鋪平道路。

15205826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15205826.value: 複合材料結構智慧赋能：透過非線性導波實現初期損傷監測的合成換能器層

15205826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205826.value: Composite materials are widely used in aerospace, automotive, energy, and civil engineering, with global market projected to reach USD 169.27 billion by 2030. However, composite structures are inherently susceptible to degradation and damage during service, demanding timely diagnosis via structural health monitoring (SHM) technology. Among existing techniques, nonlinear guided wave-based SHM (NGW-SHM) is particularly promising for early damage detection. While limited studies exist on isotropic materials/structures, nonlinear guided wave dynamics in composites and NGW-SHM for composite structures remain largely unaddressed. Key bottlenecks include insufficient understanding of the elusive generation and propagation mechanisms of nonlinear guided waves in composites, as well as the stringent requirements on SHM-specific wave generation and extraction in such complex media. To address these challenges, this proposal embraces the concept of composite structure intelligence combined with metamaterial design, proposing an embedded synthesized transducer layer (STL) to yield a self-contained composite structure with self-sensing and wave-modulating capabilities. We first investigate the generation and propagation of nonlinear guided waves in composites, elucidating their complex interaction mechanisms with incipient damage. Building on this knowledge, we develop an STL for seamless embedding in composite laminates, enabling selective excitation and reception of nonlinear guided waves. Considering the STL’s impact on the composite’s mechanical properties and wave propagation, we finally design and optimize intelligent composite panels with a dedicated monitoring system. Ultimately, this study leads to a holistic SHM solution for real-time monitoring of incipient damage in intelligent composite structures. From a scientific perspective, this research bridges nonlinear ultrasonics, composite materials science, and metamaterial engineering, expanding the technical boundaries for utilizing nonlinear guided waves in damage detection. Practically, this work will advance the application of composite materials across diverse fields by enhancing structural safety through proactive maintenance, reducing lifecycle costs, and minimizing unplanned downtime. 複合材料廣泛應用於航太、汽車、能源及土木工程領域，預計到 2030 年，全球市場規模將達到 1,692.7 億美元。然而，複合材料結構在使用過程中本質上容易發生劣化與損壞，因此需要透過結構健康監測（SHM）技術進行及時診斷。在現有技術中，基於非線性導波的結構健康監測（NGW-SHM）對於早期損壞檢測尤具潛力。雖然針對各向同性材料／結構的研究已有所進行，但複合材料中的非線性導波動力學，以及針對複合材料結構的 NGW-SHM 技術，目前仍大多未被深入探討。關鍵瓶頸包括：對複合材料中非線性導波難以捉摸的產生與傳播機制理解不足，以及在此類複雜介質中針對 SHM 專用波的產生與萃取所面臨的嚴格要求。為解決這些挑戰，本提案融合「複合結構智慧」概念與超材料設計，提出嵌入式合成換能器層（STL），以打造具備自感測與波調製能力的自足型複合結構。我們首先研究複合材料中非線性導波的產生與傳播，闡明其與初期損傷之間的複雜交互作用機制。基於這些研究成果，我們開發出一種可無縫嵌入複合材料層壓板中的合成換能器層（STL），從而實現對非線性導波的選擇性激發與接收。

15205926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15205926.value: 鋅基液流電池氫氣泡演化與電沉積耦合特性研究

15205926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205926.value: This project aims to develop an in-depth understanding of coupled bubble evolution and electrodeposition phenomena and ultimately create a durable and efficient zinc electrode for zinc-based flow batteries, which offer a promising solution for safe and low-cost grid-scale energy storage. At present, this technology has not yet reached the mainstream market due to certain barriers. A key limiting factor lies in the poor-performing zinc electrodes, which suffer from dendrite formation and side reactions. Typically, porous electrodes with large surface area such as carbon felts and copper foams are used as substrates for zinc deposition to reduce the local current density and thus suppress dendrite formation. However, as the redox potential of Zn2+/Zn is lower than that of standard hydrogen electrode, hydrogen evolution reaction is inevitable during battery operation. The evolved hydrogen will form gas bubbles, which may adhere to the electrode surface or stagnate in the complex porous structure, blocking the active sites for zinc deposition and ion transport pathways. Moreover, the complex bubble dynamics and two-phase flow will result in non-uniform electrolyte distribution, triggering dendrite formation and uneven zinc deposition, which considerably degrades the battery performance. Unfortunately, we are far from thoroughly understanding this complex process, and the lack of knowledge impedes the success in developing highly efficient and durable zinc electrodes for zinc-based flow batteries. In this project, we propose to develop an in-situ nondestructive probing system to reveal the real-world dynamics of bubble evolution and zinc electrodeposition process. We will then develop a robust mathematical model that can accurately describe the coupled fluid flow, bubble evolution, and electrodeposition process to theoretically study the coupled characteristics of bubble dynamics and morphological evolution of zinc deposits. Based on the obtained fundamental understanding, we will design and optimize novel porous electrodes to realize fast bubble removal and uniform ion distributions, thus achieving uniform and dendrite-free zinc deposition. This research will not only significantly advance our fundamental understanding of the bubble dynamics and two-phase flow coupled with zinc electrodeposition, but also address the long-standing challenge of short cycle life in zinc-based flow batteries, thereby facilitating the commercialization of this advanced energy storage technology, which will boost the adoption of intermittent renewable energy. 本計畫旨在深入探討鋅基液流電池中氣泡演化與電沉積的耦合機制，最終開發出兼具高耐久性與高效率的鋅電極。鋅基液流電池具備本質安全與低成本之優勢，是大規模電網儲能的極佳候選方案。然而，受限於若干技術瓶頸，其大規模商業化應用仍面臨挑戰；其中，鋅電極性能受限（如易生長枝晶及伴隨副反應發生）為最核心的制約因素。傳統研究多採用碳氈、泡沫銅等高比表面積之多孔電極作為鋅沉積基材，藉由降低局部電流密度來抑制枝晶生長。然而，由於 Zn²⁺/Zn 的氧化還原電位低於標準氫電極電位，電池充放電過程中不可避免地會伴隨析氫副反應（HER）。生成的氫氣氣泡易附著於電極表面或滯留於複雜的孔隙內，進而阻塞鋅沉積活性位點與離子傳輸通道。更甚者，複雜的氣泡動力學與氣液兩相流會加劇電解液分佈的空間異質性，誘發局部電場不均與枝晶生長，最終導致電池性能顯著衰退。迄今為止，學界對上述氣、液、固多相耦合過程的理解仍相當匱乏，此基礎理論的缺失嚴重阻礙了高效、長壽命鋅電極的研發。針對此知識缺口，本計畫擬開發一套原位、非破壞性觀測系統，以即時揭示實際工況下氣泡演化與鋅電沉積的動態行為。同時，本計畫將建構一套多物理場數學模型，精確描述流體流動、氣泡演化與電化學沉積的耦合交互作用，從理論層面深度剖析氣泡動力學與鋅沉積形貌演化的內在關聯。基於上述實驗觀測與理論認知，我們將進一步設計並最佳化新型多孔電極結構，以促進氣泡的快速排除並實現離子通量的均勻分佈，進而達成高度均勻、無枝晶的鋅沉積形貌。本計畫不僅將大幅深化學界對於氣泡動力學、氣液兩相流與鋅電沉積耦合機制的基礎科學理解，更將為解決鋅基液流電池循環壽命短板提供具體可行的技術路徑。研究成果有望實質推動此先進長時儲能技術的商業化進程，進而助力間歇性再生能源的大規模併網與廣泛應用。

15206126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15206126.value: 供需不確定性下具韌性的骨幹與需求導向公交營運

15206126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15206126.value: Prof Lo, Hong Kam Prof PAN, Kai

15206126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206126.value: Public transport (PT) systems rely on high-capacity trunk services such as metro and bus rapid transit to move cities efficiently. When trunk services are disrupted, passengers often shift to flexible transit (FT) options such as taxis and minibuses, creating significant uncertainty and delays for passengers. Currently, the use of FT in such situations is reactive and uncoordinated. Vehicles are not pre-positioned, operations are not aligned with trunk services, and dispatch and pricing decisions are improvised. This lack of coordination creates inefficiencies for FT operators and uncertainty for passengers, resulting in missed opportunities for timely and effective service. This project develops a coordinated trunk and FT system that proactively maintains service continuity and minimizes operating costs under both normal and disrupted conditions by managing the compound uncertainty of passenger demand and supply-side failures. The research builds a multi-layered optimization framework across three distinct timescales. At the strategic level, a Distributionally Robust Optimization (DRO) model will design resilient FT routes coordinating with trunk line transit, hedging against rare, high-impact disruptions where historical data is sparse. This robust formulation will be made computationally tractable using conic duality and advanced approximation algorithms. At the operational level, a two-stage Stochastic Program (SP) using a time-space network will co-optimize trunk and flexible schedules to enhance reliability and synchronize transfers under daily demand variability, with formulations for both system optimal and user equilibrium conditions. We will develop an innovative dual-reliability decomposition method combined with column generation to solve this large-scale problem. Finally, at the real-time level, we will design a centralized Mobility-as-a-Service (MaaS) platform for the trunk-and-FT service, formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), to dynamically dispatch vehicles, assign passengers, and adjust pricing. This complex MDP will be solved through a simulation-based optimization framework built on differentiable computational graphs. The entire framework will be validated using a simulation with large-scale, real-world multimodal datasets from cities like Hong Kong and New York to quantify performance gains against historical response strategies under realistic disruption scenarios. Theoretically, this project delivers a novel, computationally tractable approach for optimizing large-scale multimodal systems under joint supply-demand uncertainty. Practically, it provides transport authorities with a scalable suite of decision-support tools to enhance system resilience, manage disruptions effectively, and optimize resource utilization. This research aims to provide a blueprint for building public transport systems that are not just efficient in routine operation, but robust for passengers amidst supply-demand uncertainties. 公共交通（PT）系統依賴如地鐵及巴士快速交通（BRT）等大運量的骨幹線路來高效維持城市運作。當骨幹線路受阻時，乘客往往會轉乘的士及小巴等需求導向公交選項，因而為乘客帶來顯著的不確定性與延誤。目前，在此類情況下使用需求導向公交普遍屬於被動應對且缺乏協調：車輛未有預先部署，營運未能與幹線服務對接，調配及定價決策亦屬即興臨時安排。這種缺乏協調的情況導致靈活交通營運商效率低下，亦增加了乘客的不確定性，致使錯失提供及時且有效服務的時機。本項目旨在開發一個協調的幹線與靈活交通系統，透過管理乘客需求與供給側故障的複合不確定性，主動在日常營運及服務中斷情況下維持服務連續性並降低營運成本。 本研究跨越三個不同的時間尺度，構建一個多層次優化框架：首先，在策略層面，分佈魯棒優化（DRO）模型將設計與幹線交通相協調且具韌性的需求導向公交路線，以對衝歷史數據稀疏的罕見、高影響中斷風險。該魯棒公式將透過錐對偶性及先進的近似算法使其在計算上可行。其次，在營運層面，基於時空網絡的兩階段隨機規劃（SP）將共同優化骨幹與需求導向公交班次表，在日常需求波動下提升可靠性並實現轉乘同步，並分別針對系統最佳與用戶均衡條件進行構建。我們將開發一種結合生成列法的創新雙可靠性分解方法，以求解此大規模問題。最後，我們將為骨幹和需求導向公交服務設計一個集中式「出行即服務」（MaaS）平台，將其構建為馬爾可夫決策過程（MDP），以動態調配車輛、分配乘客及調整定價。此複雜的 MDP 將透過基於可微計算圖的模擬優化框架進行求解。整個框架將利用來自香港及紐約等城市的真實大規模多模式數據集進行模擬驗證，以在逼真中斷場景下量化相比歷史應對策略的性能提升。 在理論上，本項目提供了一種在供需聯合不確定性下優化大規模公交系統的新穎且計算可行的途徑。在實踐上，本項目為交通管理部門提供了一套可擴展的決策支援工具，以增強系統韌性、有效管理中斷並優化資源利用。本研究旨在為構建公共交通提供藍圖，使其不僅在日常營運中保持高效，更能在供需不確定性中為乘客提供強韌可靠的服務。

15206226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15206226.value: 正極性放電中流注莖分支特性探測新方法

15206226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206226.value: Positive leader branching is a common feature in both natural lightning and long air gap discharges in power systems. Recent evidence suggests that streamer stems—intermediate structures between streamers and leaders—may play a critical role in triggering leader branching. However, studying stem branching has long been hindered by two challenges. First, stems are easily masked by the bright emissions from surrounding streamers and leaders, making them nearly impossible to distinguish with conventional optical imaging. Second, stems form and evolve on extremely short timescales (hundreds of nanoseconds), which demand observation tools with exceptionally high temporal resolution. As a result, direct and systematic observations of stem branching remain very rare. To overcome these barriers, this project proposes two new approaches: the thermal-signature method and the current-fingerprinting method. The thermal-signature method exploits the temperature differences between streamers, stems, and leaders. By reconstructing the three-dimensional temperature field of the discharge channel, it isolates stems from luminous interference and allows precise identification of their branching structures. This enables the measurement of key geometric parameters such as branching angle, branch diameter, and branch length. The current-fingerprinting method takes advantage of the fact that each stem branch is driven by a characteristic current pulse with a double-exponential shape. Because discharge currents can be recorded continuously with very high temporal resolution, decomposing the measured current waveforms makes it possible to reconstruct the timing of stem branching events and to determine the charge required for stem growth, from which growth velocity can be inferred. To implement these methods, this project will develop an advanced experimental platform combining a three-dimensional Schlieren-based diagnostic for temperature reconstruction with a broadband, high-speed current measurement system. An artificial climate chamber with controllable humidity and pressure, as well as adjustable electrode structures and voltage waveforms, will allow us to systematically examine how background electric fields, their change rates, and environmental factors affect stem branching. This will reveal whether positive streamer stem branching follows universal scaling across conditions, clarify the geometric influence of environmental factors, and elucidate how these branching patterns shape subsequent leader morphology. The successful execution of this project will shed new light on the physical mechanisms of positive streamer stem branching, offering a missing link in our understanding of leader branching. Beyond advancing fundamental plasma physics, the findings will also provide valuable insights for lightning protection and insulation design of power systems. 正極性先導分叉是自然雷電和電力系統空氣絕緣間隙放電中的常見現象。最新證據表明，流注莖在觸發先導分支中扮演關鍵角色。然而，對流注莖分支的研究長期受困於兩大挑戰：其一，流注莖極易被周圍流注和先導的強光輻射所掩蓋，常規光學成像幾乎無法將其區分出來；其二，流注莖形成和演化時間極短（數百納秒量級），需要具備極高時間分辨率的觀測工具。因此，直接、系統地對流注莖分支進行觀測仍非常罕見。 為克服上述困難，本項目提出兩種新方法：熱特徵法和電流指紋法。熱特徵法利用流注、流注莖和先導之間的溫度差異，通過重建放電通道的三維溫度場，將流注莖從光輻射干擾中分離出來，從而精確識別其分支結構，並可測量分支角度、分支直徑和分支長度等關鍵幾何參數。電流指紋法則基於每個流注莖分支均伴隨特徵性的雙指數型電流脈衝這一物理事實，通過測量具有極高時間分辨率的放電電流波形，並對實測電流波形進行分解，便可重建流注莖分支事件的時間序列，並確定流注莖生長所需的電荷量，進而推算出流注莖生長速度。 為實施上述方法，本項目將開發一套先進的實驗平台，集成基於三維紋影診斷的溫度重建系統與寬帶高速電流測量系統。通過配備濕度和壓力可控的人工氣候室，以及可調節的電極結構和電壓波形，我們將系統研究背景電場、電場變化率及環境因素對流注莖分支的影響，從而獲得正極性流注莖分支特性，闡明環境因素對分支幾何特徵的影響，並釐清這些分支模式如何影響後續先導形態。 本項目的成功實施將為正極性流注莖分支的物理機制提供新的認識，為先導分支研究填補關鍵空白。研究成果除了推動基礎等離子體物理學的進展外，還將為電力系統的防雷保護和絕緣設計提供有價值的參考。

15206426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15206426.value: 面向 5G/6G 智能的城市級輻射場重建：基於混合無線電專家架構

15206426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206426.value: Reliable and intelligent wireless connectivity in dense urban environments is a cornerstone of future 5G and 6G systems. However, accurately modeling how radio waves propagate through complex cityscapes remains a fundamental challenge. At high frequencies, signals are strongly influenced by reflections, diffractions, and blockages from buildings, vehicles, and pedestrians. Existing empirical or simulation-based models either oversimplify these interactions or require prohibitive computational resources, making them inadequate for large-scale and data-driven network design. This project aims to develop a new artificial intelligence framework, Mixture of Radio Experts (MoRE), to enable scalable and high-fidelity modeling of city-scale wireless propagation. Building on the research team’s award-winning Neural Radio-Frequency Radiance Field (NeRF2) model, MoRE introduces a modular architecture that divides the city into a collection of specialized neural “experts,” each responsible for modeling local propagation characteristics. Instead of relying on a single monolithic network, MoRE activates only a small subset of relevant experts for each prediction. This design dramatically enhances scalability, allowing the framework to capture fine-grained spatial and frequency-dependent effects across urban environments while maintaining computational efficiency. The proposed framework will deliver the first scalable neural radiance field capable of city-wide wireless modeling with high physical fidelity. It will provide an advanced foundation for adaptive beamforming, interference coordination, spectrum reuse, and intelligent site planning. Beyond communications, the outcomes will benefit emerging applications in wireless sensing, localization, and digital-twin-based automation. Ultimately, this research will advance the scientific and technological basis for future 6G networks, where communication, sensing, and computation are seamlessly integrated to support smarter, more connected cities. 在高密度城市環境中實現可靠、智能的無線連接，是未來 5G 和 6G 系統的重要基礎。然而，如何準確建模無線電波在複雜城市環境中的傳播過程，仍然是一項基礎性挑戰。在高頻段，建築物、車輛和行人所引起的反射、繞射和遮擋等效應會顯著影響無線信號傳播。現有的經驗模型或基於仿真的方法，要麼對這些複雜傳播過程進行了過度簡化，要麼需要極高的計算資源，因此難以滿足大規模、數據驅動的無線網絡設計需求。本項目旨在研發一種新的人工智能框架——無線電專家混合（Mixture of Radio Experts，MoRE），以實現可擴展、高保真的城市級無線傳播建模。基於研究團隊此前獲獎的神經射頻輻射場（Neural Radio-Frequency Radiance Field，NeRF²）模型，MoRE 引入模塊化架構，將城市劃分為多個由專門神經網絡“專家”負責建模的區域，每個專家學習相應局部區域的無線傳播特徵。與採用單一大型神經網絡不同，MoRE 在每次預測時僅激活少量與當前任務相關的專家。該設計能夠顯著提升模型的可擴展性，使其在保持計算效率的同時，捕捉複雜城市環境中精細的空間特性及頻率相關傳播效應。本項目提出的框架將構建首個具備高物理保真度、可擴展至全城市範圍的神經輻射場無線傳播模型，為自適應波束成形、干擾協調、頻譜復用和智能站點規劃等關鍵技術提供先進的建模基礎。除無線通信外，項目成果還將惠及無線感知、定位以及基於數字孿生的智能自動化等新興應用。最終，本研究將推動未來 6G 網絡的科學與技術基礎發展，促進通信、感知與計算的深度融合，為建設更加智能、互聯的城市提供支撐。

15206626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15206626.value: 採用自預應力鐵基形狀記憶合金（Fe-SMA）筋增強的超高性能混凝土（UHPC）用於耐久海洋基礎設施

15206626.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15206626.value: Dr Dong, Zhiqiang Prof Ghafoori, Elyas

15206626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206626.value: Ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC) has emerged as a transformative material in civil engineering, offering exceptional compressive strength, durability, and flowability. Its adoption in thin-walled and complex structural elements, particularly in marine and offshore environments, is limited by its relatively low tensile strength and susceptibility to cracking. Conventional prestressing methods are often impractical for thin-walled or curved UHPC structures due to constraints such as friction loss and complex anchorage requirements. Iron-based shape memory alloys (Fe-SMA) present a novel solution, enabling self-prestressing through temperature-induced shape memory effects, thereby enhancing crack resistance, flexural capacity, and durability without external tensioning systems. It is expected that the proposed project will make breakthroughs in integration of Fe-SMA with UHPC for the development of robust, high-performance structural elements suitable for harsh ocean environments. The proposed project will fill knowledge gaps relating to: (a) the phase transformation mechanism and shape memory effect of Fe-SMA rebars in UHPC matrix; (b) the influence of curvature and thickness of elements on self-prestressing of Fe-SMA rebars in UHPC; (c) bonding mechanism and bond-slip model between Fe-SMA rebars and UHPC considering different thermal activating conditions; and (d) crack control mechanism and predictive model for UHPC reinforced with Fe-SMA rebars. A comprehensive experimental and numerical methodology is proposed, including material-level studies on phase transformation and thermo-mechanical behavior of Fe-SMA, structural-level investigations of prestress distribution in UHPC elements, and advanced characterization of interfacial bonding mechanisms. Pull-out and beam tests, coupled with digital image correlation (DIC), X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), will inform the development of bond-slip models and finite element simulations. Crack resistance will be evaluated through four-point bending tests, 3D-DIC measurement, and phase field modeling. The proposed project will enable a deeper understanding of the self-prestressing mechanism, validated predictive models for prestress and crack resistance, and practical design guidelines for Fe-SMA-reinforced UHPC structures. The integration of Fe-SMA and UHPC is expected to significantly enhance the durability, service life, and sustainability of marine infrastructure by reducing maintenance needs and CO₂ emissions. This research will provide essential insights and tools for the next generation of lightweight, durable, and high-performance concrete structures in challenging environments. Furthermore, the project will provide opportunities to train several young researchers in Hong Kong and increase their awareness and knowledge of high-performance materials in civil infrastructure. 超高性能混凝土（UHPC）作為一種變革性土木工程材料，具有卓越的抗壓強度、耐久性和流動性。然而，由於抗拉強度相對較低且易於開裂，其在薄壁及複雜結構構件（特別是在海洋及近海環境）中的應用受到了一定限制。對於薄壁或曲面UHPC結構，傳統的預應力施加方法往往因摩擦損失和複雜的錨固要求而難以實施。鐵基形狀記憶合金（Fe-SMA）提供了一種創新的解決方案，能夠利用溫度誘發的形狀記憶效應實現自預應力，從而在無需外部張拉系統的情況下，提升結構的抗裂性能、抗彎承載力和耐久性。 本專案旨在實現Fe-SMA與UHPC結合技術的突破，開發適用于惡劣海洋環境的堅固、高性能結構構件。項目將填補以下方面的研究空白：(a) UHPC基體中Fe-SMA鋼筋的相變機理與形狀記憶效應；(b) 構件曲率和厚度對UHPC中Fe-SMA鋼筋自預應力效果的影響；(c) 考慮不同熱啟動條件下的Fe-SMA鋼筋與UHPC間的粘結機理及粘結-滑移模型；以及 (d) Fe-SMA鋼筋增強UHPC結構的抗裂機理與預測模型。 本項目提出了一套綜合性的試驗與數值模擬研究方案，包括針對Fe-SMA相變及熱力學行為的材料級研究、針對UHPC構件預應力分佈的結構級研究，以及對介面粘結機理的先進表徵分析。通過拔出試驗和梁彎曲試驗，結合數位圖像相關技術（DIC）、X射線衍射（XRD）、掃描電子顯微鏡（SEM）及能譜分析（EDS），為粘結-滑移模型的建立和有限元類比提供資料支援。此外，還將通過四點彎曲試驗、3D-DIC測量及相場類比，對結構的抗裂性能進行評估。 本專案的實施將深化對自預應力機理的理解，建立經試驗驗證的預應力及抗裂性能預測模型，並制定Fe-SMA增強UHPC結構的實用設計指南。 Fe-SMA（鐵基形狀記憶合金）與UHPC（超高性能混凝土）的結合，有望通過減少維護需求和降低二氧化碳排放，顯著提升海洋基礎設施的耐久性、使用壽命及可持續性。這項研究將為在嚴苛環境下構建下一代輕質、耐久且高性能的混凝土結構提供關鍵見解與技術手段。此外，該項目還將為香港的多位青年研究人員提供培訓機會，增強他們對土木基礎設施領域高性能材料的認知與瞭解。

15206726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15206726.value: 利用自發性微生物限域構建生物膜微環境實現污水可持續氮去除

15206726.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15206726.value: Prof Nerenberg, Robert Prof YUAN, Zhiguo

15206726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206726.value: Wastewater treatment plants worldwide rely on the conventional activated-sludge process, which consumes energy and chemicals, and emits nitrous oxide, a potent greenhouse gas. Recent efforts to modernise wastewater treatment target five primary goals, including Net-zero emissions, Intensified capacity, Cost-effectiveness, Emerging contaminant control, and Resource recovery, together forming the ‘NICER’ wastewater treatment paradigm. This project aims to demonstrate a simple yet effective technology that supports the ‘NICER’ wastewater treatment paradigm. It leverages the phenomenon of ‘Microbial Confinement’, where microbes naturally self-organise into layered biofilms and create localised microenvironments. Based on this spontaneous phenomenon and our promising preliminary results, we propose a novel strategy to form localised acidic microenvironments in biofilms to realise stable Partial Nitritation-Anammox (PNA), a highly sought-after biological innovation for sustainable nitrogen removal in wastewater, without external chemical dosing or operation under harsh conditions. Beyond process demonstration, the project will generate new insights into microbial ecology in engineered ecosystems, revealing how microorganisms form and interact within layered biofilms. Microelectrodes will profile biofilm microenvironments, while cryosectioned biofilms will enable spatially resolved analysis of nitrous oxide generation and microbial communications across different biofilm layers. The process is developed based on real requirements and conditions in Hong Kong, where 80% of sewage undergoes Chemically Enhanced Primary Treatment (CEPT). As a result, the sewage typically has a low organic content, and thus the anammox process is always desired by local water utilities. We will showcase this process using Hong Kong’s unique saline sewage, expecting to (1) reduce nitrous oxide emissions, (2) increase capacity by reducing sludge yield, (3) lower costs through improved aeration and less oxygen/organic demand, and (4) recover more wastewater organics for biogas production. These outcomes will help wastewater treatment plants evolve into net energy exporters and contribute to the generation of carbon credits, aligning with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and Hong Kong’s 2050 carbon neutrality goal. With extensive experience and excellent relevant track records, the PI and Co-Is are well-equipped to lead this project to success. 全球的污水處理廠普遍依賴傳統活性污泥法，但該工藝需要消耗大量能源與化學藥劑，並會排放一氧化二氮這種高效力溫室氣體。近年來，污水處理現代化的努力主要聚焦於五項目標，包括淨零排放、處理能力強化、成本效益、新興污染物控制及資源回收，並共同構成"NICER"污水處理新範式。 本項目旨在示範一項簡單而有效的技術，以支持"NICER"污水處理新範式。該技術利用"微生物限域"現象，即微生物會自然自組織形成分層生物膜，並在其中建立局部微環境。基於此自然發生的現象，以及我們具潛力的初步研究結果，本項目提出一項創新策略，在生物膜內形成局部酸性微環境，以實現穩定的短程硝化－厭氧氨氧化（PNA）。PNA 是一項備受重視的生物技術創新，可用於可持續的污水脫氮，而本策略毋須投加外部化學藥劑，亦毋須在嚴苛操作條件下運行。 除工藝示範外，本項目亦將深化我們對工程生態系統中微生物生態的理解，揭示微生物如何在分層生物膜中形成、分布及相互作用。研究將利用微電極測定生物膜內的微環境，並通過生物膜冷凍切片，對不同生物膜層中的一氧化二氮生成及微生物通訊進行空間解析。 本工藝是根據香港的實際需求及運行條件而開發。香港約有80%的污水採用化學強化一級處理（CEPT），因此污水通常具有較低的有機物含量，這使厭氧氨氧化工藝一直受到本地水務機構的重視。我們將利用香港獨特的含鹽污水示範此工藝，預期可實現以下效益：（1）減少一氧化二氮排放；（2）通過降低污泥產量提升處理能力；（3）通過改善曝氣效率及降低氧氣和有機物需求，減少運行成本；以及（4）回收更多污水中的有機物，用於沼氣生產。 上述成果將有助於推動污水處理廠由能源消耗者轉型為淨能源輸出者，並促進碳信用的產生，從而配合聯合國可持續發展目標及香港於2050年前實現碳中和的目標。憑藉豐富的相關經驗及卓越的研究往績，項目負責人及共同研究員具備充分能力，帶領本項目取得成功。

15206826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15206826.value: 基於本地化差分隱私的關係挖掘

15206826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206826.value: The big data era is defined by unprecedented data generation, yet the sensitive nature of much of this data—encompassing biometrics, health records, financial transactions, and location trajectories—poses a profound privacy challenge for analytics. Local Differential Privacy (LDP) has emerged as the gold standard for mitigating this risk, allowing entities like Apple and Google to collect aggregate statistics directly from user devices without accessing raw data. However, while LDP effectively secures simple statistical tasks such as counts and means, it is fundamentally incompatible with the recovery of complex relational knowledge, such as social communities or functional associations. The very noise that guarantees privacy catastrophically destroys the subtle statistical dependencies that define relations. The root cause is a fundamental mismatch: LDP injects independent noise, whereas relations are defined by statistical dependence. To resolve this paradox, we are pioneering the first foundational framework for relation-aware LDP. Our research introduces a two-pronged, synergistic approach: (1) developing novel data representations inherently robust to LDP perturbation, and (2) co-designing new LDP protocols that explicitly preserve relational structures for accurate inference. This initiative establishes a new paradigm, shifting the scope of LDP from simple aggregation to the mining of complex relational knowledge. We will create novel methodologies for explicit relation mining on graph data and devise new metrics for explicit relation mining to uncover hidden patterns. To ensure real-world robustness, we will fortify our frameworks through rigorous adversarial analysis and develop potent defense mechanisms against poisoning and inference attacks. By bridging the critical gap between stringent privacy and deep relational insight, this research will unlock the next frontier of private data analysis. It will enable transformative discoveries in fields from social network science to recommendation systems, ensuring that the pursuit of knowledge never comes at the cost of personal privacy. The outcomes of this project will provide a foundational privacy layer for the data-driven and AI industries, delivering significant benefits to the research community, all data-driven industries, and citizens in Hong Kong. 大數據時代的特徵是前所未有的數據生成規模。然而，當中大量數據具有高度敏感性，例如生物特徵、健康紀錄、金融交易及位置軌跡等，為數據分析帶來嚴峻的隱私挑戰。本地化差分隱私（Local Differential Privacy，LDP）已成為重要的隱私保護標準，Apple、Google 等機構亦已成功部署 LDP，直接從用戶裝置收集統計數據，而毋須存取原始數據。然而，儘管 LDP 能有效保障計數、平均值等簡單統計任務，卻從根本上難以支援複雜關係知識的恢復，例如社交社群或功能關聯。用以保障隱私的噪聲，會嚴重破壞界定各類關係的細微統計依賴性。問題的根源在於一項根本性的錯配：LDP 注入的是獨立噪聲，而關係則由統計依賴性所界定。為解決這一矛盾，本項目將首次系統研究關係感知的本地化差分隱私基礎框架，並提出一套雙管齊下、相互協同的方法：（1）開發對 LDP 擾動具有內在穩健性的新型數據表示方法；以及（2）協同設計能明確保留關係結構的新型 LDP 協議，從而實現準確推斷。 本項研究將建立一種嶄新範式，把 LDP 的應用範圍由簡單的數據匯總擴展至複雜關係知識的挖掘。我們將針對圖數據上的顯式關係挖掘，建立創新的方法體系，並設計新型度量指標，以揭示隱藏的關係模式。為確保框架在現實環境中的穩健性，我們將進行嚴格的對抗性分析，進一步強化相關框架，並開發有效的防禦機制，以抵禦數據投毒攻擊及推斷攻擊。本研究將彌合嚴格隱私保障與深層關係洞察之間的關鍵鴻溝，開拓隱私數據分析的新前沿，並推動社交網絡科學、推薦系統等不同領域的突破性發現，確保對知識的探索不會以犧牲個人隱私為代價。本項目的成果將為數據驅動及人工智能產業提供基礎性的隱私保護層，為研究社群、各類數據驅動產業以及香港市民帶來重大裨益。

15207826.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15207826.value: Prof Liu, Yang Prof Lo, Hong Kam

15207826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15207826.value: Efficient coordination between international and neighbouring domestic airports can improve how passengers move between flights across airports, make better use of airport capacity and offer frequent flight schedule. International airports have broad air right but feature stringent immigration controls, separate terminal corridors and customs inspections, while domestic airports are simpler, easier to navigate and convenient check-in procedure under the same air sovereignty. Globally, regions like the San Francisco Bay Area, New York, Los Angeles, Manchester, Moscow, Berlin, Seoul, and Tokyo have similar multiple airport system (MAS) structures. However, the efficiency of passenger transit between international and domestic airports depends on service availability, transport networks, and geographical constraints. In Hong Kong SAR, the “Fly-via-Zhuhai-HK” programme links airports with flexible transport options, including cooperative ferry services (70-90 minutes) and coach or private vehicles (60-120 minutes). Recent advances in regional air mobility (RAM) and electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) flight tests in the Greater Bay Area (GBA) highlight the potential for rapid cross-border MAS transit in about 25 minutes. International passengers are more time-sensitive, while domestic passengers are more vulnerable to delays and rebooking. Competition between RAM and existing transit options, and cooperation with airlines for multi-stop flights, present ongoing challenges for RAM’s market position. This research aims to develop flexible and efficient ways to connect airports within a region, focusing on passengers who need to transfer quickly or when passenger number are uneven or unpredictable. Firstly, we will study a game-theoretic model and find the best vertiport facility location for eVTOL landing sites and plan services that balance the transit time and capacity for time-sensitive passengers. We will also analyse how passenger choose between transit options, and how these choices affect overall demand amid competition among transit providers and cooperation with airliners. Secondly, we will design a learning-to-optimise framework for RAM service and air corridor capacity estimation, considering spatial-temporal traffic flow, transit patterns and the schedules between international and domestic flights. Finally, we will investigate eVTOL service models, including on-demand and scheduled modes, considering empty repositioning or discounted services to address uneven demand from international passengers. The results of this research will help airport authorities and air transport planners design better connections between airports, making travel faster and more reliable for passengers in the GBA. The multi-modal transit solutions developed can also bridge international and domestic air rights in other cooperative MAS around the world. 國際機場與鄰近的國內機場之間的有效協調，能改善旅客在不同機場間轉機的流程，更善用機場容量，並提供更頻密的航班班次。國際機場擁有廣泛的航權，但特點是出入境管制嚴格、客運大樓通道分隔及海關檢查繁複；相比之下，國內機場在同一航空主權下，運作更簡單、指示更清晰，辦理登機手續亦更便捷。放眼全球，三藩市灣區、紐約、洛杉磯、曼徹斯特、莫斯科、柏林、首爾及東京等地區都擁有類似的「多機場系統」（MAS）結構。然而，旅客在國際與國內機場之間的中轉效率，取決於服務供應、交通網絡以及地理限制。在香港特別行政區，「經珠港飛」客運項目透過靈活的交通選項連接兩地機場，包括聯運渡輪服務（需時 70 至 90 分鐘）以及旅遊巴或私家車（需時 60 至 120 分鐘）。近期「區域空中交通」（RAM）的發展，以及在粵港澳大灣區（大灣區）進行的電動垂直起降（eVTOL）飛行測試，突顯了實現約 25 分鐘快速跨境 MAS 轉乘的潛力。國際旅客通常對時間更敏感，而國內旅客則有更大彈性改簽乘坐後續其他航班，延誤成本相對較低。RAM 與現有交通選項之間的競爭，以及與航空公司在多停靠點航班上的合作，均為 RAM 的市場定位帶來持續挑戰。 本研究旨在開發靈活而高效的區域內機場連接方案，重點關注需要快速轉機的旅客，以及應對客流量不均衡或難以預測的情況。首先，我們將研究一個博弈論模型，找出 eVTOL 降落點（垂直起降場）的最佳設施選址，並規劃能為對時間敏感的旅客平衡轉乘時間與載客量的服務。我們亦會分析旅客如何在不同交通選項中作選擇，以及在交通營辦商的競爭與航空公司的合作下，這些選擇會如何影響整體需求。其次，我們將設計一個結合學習與優化的框架（learning-to-optimise framework），用於估算 RAM 服務與空中走廊的容量，當中會考量時空交通流、中轉模式，以及國際與國內航班之間的班次編排。最後，我們將探討 eVTOL 服務模式（包括按需及定時模式），並考慮透過空機調撥（empty repositioning）或提供折扣服務，以應對國際出行及國內出行的旅客不均衡需求。本研究的結果將有助機場管理局與航空交通規劃者設計出更佳的機場接駁方案，讓大灣區旅客的出行更快捷、更可靠。研究所開發的多式聯運方案，亦可為全球其他合作型的多機場系統建立橋樑，連繫國際與國內航權。

15208126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15208126.value: 体力负荷建模与结构钢加工工作规划优化框架

15208126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15208126.value: This research proposes an ontology-driven framework to model physical workload and optimize work planning in structural steel fabrication. This study confronts a pressing challenge in the construction industry: the escalating shortage and aging of its skilled trades workforce. This demographic trend intensifies occupational health risks, undermines labor productivity, and threatens project viability. In response, our research proposes a human-centric framework designed to enhance workforce sustainability by systematically mitigating physical strain and optimizing work planning through posture-time management. Indeed, the prevalence of non-standardized designs in steel construction frequently leads to complex geometries. This forces fitters and welders to maintain awkward and sustained postures while connecting components, a primary risk factor for developing work-related musculoskeletal disorders. Forged through a strategic partnership with Zhejiang & Jinggong Steel Building (Group) Co., Ltd., a leading Chinese fabricator, and BACBUDY, a Hong Kong-based biomechanical startup, this research will develop a core methodology that integrates multi-source data. This approach synergistically combines planning-stage Building Information Modeling (BIM) with real-time worker posture data, captured through computer vision and sensors embedded in BACBUDY's exoskeleton suit, to proactively mitigate the risk of lower-back injuries. This integrated data is transformed into a standardized "posture-time" metric for precise workload analysis. Building on this foundation, the research develops novel workface planning and resource scheduling algorithms that balance physical load—measured through worker exposure times to specific postures—alongside conventional constraints of time, work sequence, and finite crew resources. To materialize proactive work analysis and adaptive scheduling, this research will formalize domain knowledge into a dedicated ontology. This structured knowledge base enables machine-readable reasoning about the complex relationships between workers, tasks, postures, and associated risks. The ultimate goal is to deliver a validated, integrated system that fundamentally reduces musculoskeletal disorder risks and enhances worker well-being. By optimizing workload management from planning to execution, this framework promotes more sustainable and humane construction practices. 本研究提出一个本体驱动的框架，旨在对结构钢加工作业中的体力负荷进行建模，并优化工作规划。研究直面建筑业面临的紧迫挑战：熟练技术工人日益短缺且趋于老龄化。这一人口趋势加剧了职业健康风险，削弱了劳动生产率，并威胁到项目的可行性。为此，本研究提出一个以人为本的框架，通过系统性地减轻体力负担，并借助姿势时间管理优化工作规划，以增强劳动力队伍的可持续性。 钢结构工程中大量存在的非标准化设计常导致构件几何形态复杂，迫使装配工和焊工在连接构件时长时间保持别扭且固定的作业姿势，而这正是引发工作相关肌肉骨骼疾病的主要风险因素。本研究通过与国内领先的钢构企业精工钢构集团及香港生物力学初创公司BACBUDY建立战略合作，开发一套集成多源数据的核心方法。该方法将规划阶段的建筑信息模型（BIM）与实时工人姿势数据协同融合，后者通过计算机视觉及嵌入BACBUDY外骨骼服中的传感器采集，从而主动降低腰部损伤风险。整合后的数据被转化为标准化的“姿势时间”指标，用于精确的负荷分析。在此基础上，本研究开发新型的现场作业规划与资源调度算法，在兼顾时间、工序顺序和有限班组资源等传统约束的同时，平衡以工人暴露于特定姿势的时间来度量的体力负荷。 为实现主动式作业分析与自适应调度，本研究将领域知识形式化为专用本体。这一结构化知识库支持对工人、任务、姿势及相关风险之间复杂关系进行机器可读的推理。最终目标是交付一个经过验证的集成系统，从根本上降低肌肉骨骼疾病风险，提升工人福祉。通过从规划到执行的全过程优化负荷管理，该框架推动更可持续、更人性化的施工实践。

15208426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15208426.value: 開發一種用於提高弛豫鐵電單晶壓電性能的高效極化方法

15208426.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15208426.value: Prof Huang, Houbing Prof Zhang, Shujun

15208426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15208426.value: Enhancing the piezoelectric properties of relaxor ferroelectric single crystals is essential for improving the performance and operational reliability of devices such as sensors, actuators, motors, and transducers. Post-growth treatments, including alternating current (AC) poling and pulse poling, have demonstrated significant potential in enhancing piezoelectric performance by softening ferroelectric domains and domain walls in the relaxor ferroelectric single crystals. However, these methods face challenges such as non-uniform poling, performance fluctuations, susceptibility to ferroelectric fatigue, and crystal cracking due to the alternating and discontinuous nature of the electric field. Consequently, they are less practical for industrial applications compared to direct-current (DC) poling techniques, which often result in lower piezoelectric performance but are more reliable. Mechanical stress is well known for its capability to alter microstructures in ferroelectric materials. Recent studies have demonstrated that mechanical stress can facilitate charge and defect redistribution, as well as ferroelectric domain-switching behavior, potentially aiding the domain-softening process. In light of this, the present proposal aims to combine the DC poling technique with mechanical stress, developing a new method referred to as mechanically assisted direct-current poling. This approach seeks to enhance piezoelectric performance while ensuring high poling efficiency, uniform poling outcomes, and reduced susceptibility to fatigue and crystal cracking in relaxor ferroelectric materials. Based on our preliminary results, the research team aims to achieve at least a 50% increase in the piezoelectric coefficient and dielectric constant of relaxor ferroelectric single crystals compared to those treated with conventional DC methods. Advanced ex-situ and in-situ characterization techniques, alongside modeling tools, will be employed to elucidate the factors and mechanisms contributing to the enhanced performance achieved through this approach. The research will clarify the relationships between the poling process, local structures, and properties in relaxor ferroelectric single crystals. The anticipated outcomes of this project are expected to guide the development of poling technologies to achieve high-performance relaxor ferroelectric materials, significantly impacting industrial practices and driving technological advancements, thereby enhancing the commercial viability of partners in the electronic industry. While the primary focus of this project is on relaxor ferroelectrics, the experimental and analytical techniques developed here are expected to broadly apply to other material forms and systems, including non-relaxor ferroelectrics and lead-free ferroelectrics in the form of single crystals and ceramics in the future. 增強弛豫鐵電單晶的壓電性能，對於提升感測器、制動器、馬達及換能器等裝置之性能與操作可靠性至關重要。後生長處理技術，包括交流電極化與脈衝極化，已展現出透過軟化弛豫鐵電單晶中之鐵電疇與疇壁，以顯著提升壓電性能的潛力。然而，這些方法面臨諸如極化不均勻、性能波動、易受鐵電疲勞影響，以及因電場之交變與不連續特性導致晶體開裂等挑戰。因此，與直流電極化技術相比，這些方法在工業應用上較不實用，儘管直流極化通常導致較低的壓電性能，但較為可靠。 機械應力因其能改變鐵電材料微結構的能力而廣為人知。近期研究顯示，機械應力可促進電荷與缺陷的重新分佈，以及鐵電疇切換行為，可能有助於疇軟化過程。有鑑於此，本提案旨在將直流極化技術與機械應力相結合，開發一種稱為「機械輔助直流極化」的新方法。該方法旨在提升壓電性能，同時確保高極化效率、均勻的極化結果，並降低弛豫鐵電材料對疲勞與晶體開裂的敏感性。根據我們的初步結果，研究團隊期望能將弛豫鐵電單晶之壓電係數與介電常數，相較於傳統直流方法處理者，提升至少50%。 先進的離位與原位表徵技術，搭配建模工具，將用以闡明透過此方法達成性能提升之因素與機制。本研究將釐清弛豫鐵電單晶中極化製程、局部結構與性能之間的關聯性。本專案預期之成果，可望為實現高性能弛豫鐵電材料之極化技術發展提供指引，對工業實務產生重大影響，並推動技術進步，進而提升電子產業合作夥伴之商業可行性。儘管本專案主要聚焦於弛豫鐵電材料，但本研究所開發之實驗與分析技術，預期將廣泛應用於其他材料形式與系統，包括未來之非弛豫鐵電材料及無鉛鐵電材料，其形式涵蓋單晶與陶瓷。

15208726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15208726.value: 基於創新表達系統與液-液相分離（LLPS）介導紡絲的人造蜘蛛絲製備

15208726.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15208726.value: Prof Liu, Wei Prof Zhang, Yaopeng

15208726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15208726.value: Given that they have lived on Earth for almost 400 million years, spiders are incredibly amazing animals. Spiders have several glands, each of which is able to create distinct proteins that form specialised silks for various uses, in contrast to silkworms, which only produce one type of silk. The major ampullate gland exclusively produces two primary proteins (i.e., MaSp1 and MaSp2) to form dragline silk, which is renowned for its exceptional strength and toughness. It is generally acknowledged that MaSp1 adds strength to the silk, whilst MaSp2 gives it flexibility. However, a major scientific challenge persists: Despite knowing the roles of these individual proteins, we have been unable to replicate their synergistic performance in artificial fibers. A central obstacle is our incomplete understanding of how MaSp1 and MaSp2 interact with each other under native-like conditions to form the final silk's intricate structure. The challenges of creating these intricate proteins in their fully functioning forms contribute to this knowledge gap. It is frequently difficult for traditional systems, such as E. coli, to produce big, properly folded spider silk proteins. Our idea uses a unique strategy utilising mammalian cell (the Expi293F system) to get around this. This gives us a crucial starting point for our research by enabling us to create full-domain MaSp1 and MaSp2 proteins that closely resemble their natural counterparts. Our project will carefully study the protein-protein interaction between MaSp1 and MaSp2, and its impact on the liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) behaviors occurred in natural spinning process. With this knowledge, we are building a biomimetic microfluidic spinning system to enable a native-like condition with various triggers involved. The ultimate goal of our project is to uncover how MaSp1 and MaSp2 work together in spider dragline silk, and to expand this research to include remainning spider silk constituents like MaSp3, MaSp4, and MaSp5. By exploring how multiple proteins are integrated within a single spider silk fiber, we hope to explain the subtle combination of tensile strength and toughness for natural spider silk. It provides insight into the spider silk self-assembly mechanism, inspiring the rational design of high-performance materials via biomimicry. This project integrates knowledge from synthetic biology, fluid mechanics, materials science, and fiber engineering. Through this interdisciplinary approach, we aim to advance the development of high-performance artificial spider silk, so-called “dream fiber”, with mechanical properties comparable to those of natural spider silk. 鑑於蜘蛛已在地球上生存近四億年，牠們無疑是極其令人驚奇的生物。與僅能產生單一類型蠶絲的家蠶不同，蜘蛛具有多種絲腺，每一種絲腺皆能合成不同的蛋白質，進而形成具有特化功能、可供不同用途的蜘蛛絲。其中，大壺狀腺（major ampullate gland）專門產生兩種主要蛋白質，即 MaSp1 與 MaSp2，以形成牽引絲（dragline silk）。牽引絲以其卓越的強度與韌性而聞名。一般認為，MaSp1 主要賦予蜘蛛絲強度，而 MaSp2 則提供其柔韌性。然而，一項重大的科學挑戰仍然存在：儘管我們已了解這些單一蛋白質各自的功能，卻仍無法在人造纖維中重現其協同作用所帶來的優異性能。其核心障礙在於，我們對 MaSp1 與 MaSp2 在近天然條件下如何相互作用，並進一步形成最終蜘蛛絲複雜結構的理解仍不完整。 造成此知識缺口的原因之一，在於製備這些複雜蛋白質之完整功能形式仍具有相當挑戰性。傳統表達系統，如大腸桿菌（E. coli），通常難以產生分子量大且正確折疊的蜘蛛絲蛋白。本研究構想採用一種獨特策略，即利用哺乳動物細胞表達系統（Expi293F system）以克服此限制。此方法使我們能夠製備完整結構域的 MaSp1 與 MaSp2 蛋白質，並使其高度接近天然對應物，從而為本研究提供關鍵的起始基礎。 本計畫將系統性研究 MaSp1 與 MaSp2 之間的蛋白質—蛋白質相互作用，並探討其對天然紡絲過程中液—液相分離（liquid–liquid phase separation, LLPS）行為的影響。基於此知識，我們將建立一套仿生微流控紡絲系統，以在多種觸發因子參與下模擬近天然的紡絲環境。本計畫的最終目標是揭示 MaSp1 與 MaSp2 如何在蜘蛛牽引絲中協同作用，並進一步將此研究拓展至其他蜘蛛絲組成蛋白，如 MaSp3、MaSp4 與 MaSp5。透過探討多種蛋白質如何整合於單一蜘蛛絲纖維之中，我們期望闡明天然蜘蛛絲在拉伸強度與韌性之間所呈現的精妙平衡。此研究將有助於深入理解蜘蛛絲的自組裝機制，並啟發透過仿生策略理性設計高性能材料。 本計畫整合合成生物學、流體力學、材料科學與纖維工程等領域之知識。透過此跨學科研究方法，我們旨在推動高性能人造蜘蛛絲—即所謂「夢幻纖維」—的發展，使其具備可媲美天然蜘蛛絲的機械性能。

15208826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15208826.value: 採用輕質UHPC浮體的浮式海上風力機船舶碰撞性能研究

15208826.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15208826.value: Prof HAO, Hong Prof Poon, Chi Sun Dr Sha, Yanyan Dr Yang, Mindong

15208826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15208826.value: Floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs) offer unparalleled access to stronger and more consistent wind resources compared to onshore or fixed-bottom offshore wind turbines (OWTs), unlocking vast untapped energy potential to significantly boost renewable energy output while advancing global decarbonization and energy security goals. However, their wide deployment may introduce critical maritime risks, particularly from ship collisions, which can lead to catastrophic structural failures, environmental disasters, and substantial human and economic losses. Therefore, a thorough investigation into the ship collision performance of FOWTs is needed. Existing research in this field remains limited due to the complexity of coupled aerodynamic, hydrodynamic, and highly nonlinear impact behaviours. Though some numerical studies have been conducted, their accuracy is constrained by the oversimplified assumptions (e.g., calm water), and no experimental work has reasonably replicated these coupled conditions. Moreover, current studies mainly focused on steel-based FOWTs, which face long-term durability challenges such as corrosion. In contrast, lightweight ultra-high-performance concrete (LUHPC) presents a promising alternative, offering superior structural efficiency and durability in harsh marine environments. However, the dynamic material properties of LUHPC are not well understood, hindering its widespread application. This project aims to propose the use of LUHPC with hollow glass microspheres (LUHPC-HGM) for constructing semi-submersible FOWT floaters, and systematically investigate its ship collision performance through an integrated experimental and numerical approach. Key objectives and innovations of the project include: • Developing the first dynamic constitutive model for LUHPC-HGM through a comprehensive series of material tests, and implementing it in commercial software LS-DYNA via a user-defined subroutine for high-fidelity ship collision simulations. • Conducting pioneering ship impact tests in a wave basin under combined wind, wave, mooring, and collision loads, achieving the first experimental replication of ship-FOWT collision in marine environment. • Establishing a high-fidelity coupled numerical simulation framework by integrating LS-DYNA and OrcaFlex, to realistically consider wave excitation and currents, accurately capture the coupled external dynamics and internal mechanics of ship-FOWT collisions, and parametrically assess the influence of critical factors on collision performance. By addressing these research gaps, this project will deliver fundamental insights into the collision mechanics of FOWT while advancing LUHPC-HGM as a transformative material for offshore renewable energy infrastructure. The outcomes will inform safer and more resilient FOWT designs, accelerating the sustainable expansion of offshore wind energy. 浮式離岸風力機（FOWTs）相較於陸域或固定式離岸風力機，能獲得更強勁且穩定的風能，因而得以釋放大量尚未開發的能源潛力，大幅提升再生能源產出，同時也有助於推動全球脫碳進程與能源安全目標。然而，隨著浮式風力機的廣泛佈設，可能衍生出重要的海事風險，特別是船舶碰撞事件，一旦發生，恐將造成結構毀損、環境災害，甚至重大的人員傷亡與經濟損失。因此，深入探討浮式離岸風力機的船舶碰撞性能，實屬必要。 目前這方面的研究仍相當有限，主因在於氣動力、水動力與高度非線性撞擊行為之間的耦合作用極為複雜。雖然已有若干數值分析，但其準確性往往受限於過度簡化的假設（例如忽略波浪影響），而且至今尚無任何實驗能忠實重現這些耦合條件。此外，既有研究多聚焦於鋼製浮式風力機，此類結構在長期使用下容易面臨腐蝕等耐久性問題。相較之下，輕質超高性能混凝土（LUHPC）極具應用潛力，在嚴苛的海洋環境中能展現優異的結構效率與耐久性。不過，目前對LUHPC的動態材料特性瞭解不足，這也阻礙了其廣泛推廣。 本計畫提出以添加空心玻璃微珠之輕質超高性能混凝土（LUHPC-HGM）來建造半潛式浮式風力機浮體，並透過實驗與數值模擬的整合方式，系統性評估其船舶碰撞性能。計畫的主要目標與創新之處包括： 透過一系列完整的材料試驗，建立全球首個LUHPC-HGM的動態組成律模型，並以自訂副程式將其導入商業軟體LS-DYNA中，以進行高精確度的船舶碰撞模擬。 在波浪水槽中，結合風力、波浪、繫泊系統與撞擊載重等多重條件，進行開創性的實體撞擊試驗，首次在實驗室環境中重現船舶與浮式風力機於真實海洋條件下的碰撞情境。 建立一套整合LS-DYNA與OrcaFlex的高保真耦合數值模擬框架，不僅能真實反映波浪與海流的外力作用，更能精確掌握碰撞過程中外部動力與內部力學的耦合行為，並透過參數分析，系統性評估各項關鍵因子對碰撞性能的影響。 本計畫將填補當前的研究缺口，不僅能深化對浮式風力機碰撞力學的基本理解，也有助於將LUHPC-HGM推向離岸再生能源基礎設施的革新材料。研究成果將為更安全、更具韌性的浮式風力機設計提供科學依據，進而加速離岸風能的永續發展。

15210226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15210226.value: 面向精準神經科學的腦內源性分區與自適應圖學習

15210226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15210226.value: Understanding brain organization is essential for linking neural systems to cognition, emotion, and behavior, as well as for uncovering mechanisms of psychiatric and neurological disorders. While population-based atlases have illuminated canonical brain networks, they obscure substantial individual variability in anatomy, function, and connectivity that shapes development, cognition, and vulnerability to mental illness. Existing individualized parcellation methods either impose atlas-derived constraints that suppress meaningful differences or rely on group-informed priors that attenuate subject-specific brain organization. Fully individual-native approaches preserve uniqueness but struggle with inter-subject correspondence, limiting their clinical and machine learning utility. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a theory-driven framework for intrinsic, subject-specific brain parcellation and deep learning analysis that advances precision neuroscience. First, we develop the first geometry-driven, theory-grounded parcellation method, LB-hierarchical cortical parcellation, that leverages Laplace–Beltrami (LB) eigenfunctions and Courant’s nodal domain theorem, providing mathematically principled cortical subdivisions. We resolve the long-standing challenge of eigenvalue multiplicity by introducing a multi-label assignment scheme that aligns naturally with the brain’s overlapping functional organization. Second, we propose the geometric–functional Laplace–Beltrami (GF-LB) operator, the first spectral operator to mathematically unify cortical geometry and functional connectivity within a single framework. Our method generates multi-scale hierarchical parcellations that capture both geometry and function at individual resolution, enabling a deeper characterization of brain organization across scales. Third, we design a subject-specific graph neural network (SS-GNN) that addresses inter-subject and intra-subject variability in brain graphs by generating subject-adaptive spectral filters through a novel filter generation network. We introduce ensemble-based brain network representations, where multiple stochastic graph realizations jointly capture the distributed and individualized nature of human brain organization, moving beyond static atlas-based representations. We rigorously evaluate the reliability of our methods using repeated MRI scans across sessions and across scanners (n=200). Finally, we apply our framework to predict adolescent depression (n=9800) and compare it with state-of-the-art GNN methods, including GCN, GAT, GatedGCN, GPS, on atlas-based brain networks created based on the atlas, demonstrating its clinical utility in precision neuroscience. This work introduces an innovative mathematical framework of intrinsic brain parcellation and adaptive graph learning that advances both fundamental neuroscience and clinical translation. Beyond psychiatry, the framework is versatile and applicable to diverse types of geometric data—including graphs in logistics, computer vision, biology, and chemistry—underscoring its broad scientific and technological impact. 理解大腦組織結構是揭示認知功能及精神與神經系統疾病機制的關鍵。然而，現有腦圖譜主要反映群體平均特徵，難以捕捉個體之間的重要差異，限制了精準醫學的發展。本研究提出一套全新的數學與人工智能框架，實現個體特異性的大腦分區及深度學習分析。我們首次建立具理論基礎的幾何驅動腦區劃分方法，並創新地整合大腦幾何結構與功能連結，建立多尺度個體化腦網絡。同時，我們研發可自適應個體差異的圖神經網路，大幅提升跨個體腦網絡分析及疾病預測能力。透過跨時段及跨掃描儀MRI數據驗證，該方法展現高度可靠性，並成功應用於近萬名青少年憂鬱症風險預測，表現優於現有先進方法。此框架將推動精準神經科學及精神疾病研究，並可廣泛應用於生物醫學、電腦視覺、物流及化學等多個領域，具備重要的科學價值與應用前景。

15211126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15211126.value: 面向耐火及低碳的組裝合成建築（MiC）：利用冷結核殼骨料減緩高強輕質混凝土的高溫爆裂

15211126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15211126.value: Prof Poon, Chi Sun Prof Zhang, Shipeng

15211126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15211126.value: This project aims to develop a green high-strength lightweight concrete (HSLWC) for Modular integrated Construction (MiC) in Hong Kong by engineering artificial lightweight core-shell aggregates (CSA) from local waste glass powder (WGP) and waste expanded polystyrene (EPS). Unlike conventional sintered lightweight aggregates that are energy-intensive, imported, and costly, the proposed CSA uses a porous low-density core and a functional shell to simultaneously reduce density, buffer vapour pressure, and enhance thermal insulation. This design introduces a novel mechanism: increasing effective porosity and improving aggregate-paste thermal uniformity, thereby mitigating internal steam-pressure build-up and reducing the risk of explosive spalling. The research integrates multi-scale material design with advanced experimental and modelling methods. CSA will be fabricated by cold-bonded pelletisation and systematically characterised for their physical, mechanical, and thermal properties. The optimised aggregates will then be incorporated into HSLWC mixes, which will be evaluated for workability, strength, stiffness, and durability in accordance with international standards. Fire resistance of HSLWC will be assessed using instrumented furnace tests under ISO 834 standard fire curves, with both loading and cooling regimes considered to reflect realistic structural fire scenarios. Embedded K-type thermocouples and high-temperature pore-pressure transducers with sintered metal filters will record in-situ temperature and vapour pressure histories, enabling direct observation of spalling mechanisms. In parallel, thermo-hydro-mechanical (THM) simulations will be calibrated to link pore structure, permeability, thermal conductivity, and ITZ behaviour to spalling thresholds. This combined experimental-numerical approach ensures both mechanistic understanding and predictive capability. The project is structured in four stages. First, CSA aggregates will be designed using local waste streams, achieving lightweight efficiency while enhancing ITZ bonding. Second, CSA will be integrated into HSLWC mixes, optimised to meet MiC structural requirements of dry density ≤ 1,800 kg/m³, compressive strength ≥ 60 MPa, and modulus ≥ 20 GPa. Third, the high-temperature performance and anti-spalling mechanisms will be systematically investigated, focusing on vapour-pressure evolution, thermal stress, and post-fire residual capacity. Finally, a life-cycle assessment (LCA) and techno-economic analysis will benchmark CSA-HSLWC against imported sintered aggregates, quantifying reductions in embodied energy, emissions, and cost, while validating industrial scalability. The expected outcomes include validated CSA formulations, a mechanistic anti-spalling framework, calibrated safety maps, and MiC-scale prototype evidence. Overall, the project will deliver a fire-robust and low-carbon HSLWC tailored for MiC, advancing Hong Kong’s Climate Action Plan 2050 pillars on energy efficiency and waste reduction, while providing a transferable model for sustainable construction in dense urban contexts. 本項目旨在利用本地廢棄玻璃粉末（WGP）及廢棄發泡聚苯乙烯（EPS），設計人工輕質核殼骨料（CSA），以開發適用於香港「組裝合成建築」（MiC）的綠色高強度輕質混凝土（HSLWC）。有別於傳統燒結輕質骨料需大量能源、依賴進口且成本高昂，本研究所提出的CSA採用多孔低密度核心與功能性外殼，可同時降低密度、緩衝蒸汽壓力並提升隔熱性能。此設計引入新機制：透過增加有效孔隙率及改善骨料－漿體熱均勻性，以減輕內部蒸汽壓力累積與熱應力發展，進而降低爆裂剝落風險。 本研究整合多尺度材料設計與先進實驗及模擬方法。CSA將以常溫造粒技術製備，並系統性表徵其物理、力學及熱學性質。經優化的骨料掺入HSLWC配比中，並依國際標準評估其工作性、強度及耐久性。HSLWC的耐火性能將採用高溫爐體試驗，依據ISO 834及ASTM E119標準火災升溫曲線進行評估，並同時考慮載重與冷卻階段，以反映真實結構火災情境。內置K型熱電偶及高溫孔隙壓力傳感器將記錄現場溫度與蒸汽壓力歷程，可直接觀察爆裂機制。同時，將校準熱－水－力（THM）耦合模擬，以連結孔隙結構、滲透性、熱傳導係數及界面過渡區（ITZ）行為與爆裂臨界值。此實驗與數值計算並行方法兼具機制理解與預測能力。 本項目分為四個階段。首先，利用本地廢棄物流設計CSA骨料，達到輕量化效率並強化ITZ粘結（鬆散容重 < 1,000 kg/m³，抗壓強度 > 10 MPa）。其次，將CSA整合至HSLWC配比中，優化以滿足MiC結構要求：乾密度 ≤ 1,800 kg/m³、抗壓強度 ≥ 60 MPa、彈性模數 ≥ 20 GPa。第三，系統性探討高溫性能及抗爆裂機制，重點關注蒸汽壓力演化、熱應力及高溫後殘餘強度。最後，進行生命週期評估（LCA）與技術經濟分析，將CSA-HSLWC與進口燒結骨材進行比較，量化隱含能源、排放及成本之減量，並驗證工業規模可行性。 預期成果包括經驗證的CSA配方、機理的抗爆裂理論架構、校準的安全設計圖譜，以及MiC尺度的原型驗證數據。整體而言，本計畫將開發適用於MiC的耐火爆裂且低碳排HSLWC，推進香港《氣候行動計畫2050》中關於能源效率及廢棄物減量兩大支柱，同時為高密度都市環境提供可持續建築的可轉移模式。

15211226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15211226.value: In competitive industries, moving second can sometimes be more advantageous. For example, a firm can benefit from observing early entrants’ experiences when entering a new market, and can capture the market share from competitors who exit an existing market early. Most of the existing literature on real-option games with second-mover advantages assumes that firms have complete information about the entire structure of the game. In reality, however, each firm may possess private information, including proprietary innovation technologies, investment costs, financing costs, and liquidation values. This project aims to model second-mover advantages and incomplete information in differential games. We plan to develop a method to solve for Bayesian Nash equilibria and to examine how incomplete information affects firms’ incentives to become the second mover. By integrating the financial architecture into our game-theoretic framework, we will examine how competition influences firms' strategies, including their leverage policies, liquidity management, default timing, and financing decisions. We will also explore the policy implications and empirical predictions of our game models. In practice, the proposed research will establish guidelines for firms to strategically manage liquidity and optimize capital structures in competitive environments, while providing policymakers with theoretical foundations to redress inefficiencies in market competition. This project fosters interdisciplinary research, integrating methodologies from optimal stopping, stochastic control, partial differential equations, and numerical methods, with applications spanning differential games, real options, capital structure, and liquidity management. 在竞争激烈的行业中，后发者可能更具优势。例如，企业进入新市场时，可以先观察早期进入者的成败经验，减少试错成本；在现有市场中，如果竞争对手过早退出，后行动的企业也可能趁机夺取其市场份额。现有关于具有后发优势的实物期权博弈文献，大多假设企业对整个博弈结构拥有完全信息。但现实中，企业往往掌握各自的机密信息，例如专有技术、投资成本、融资成本以及清算价值等。因此，本项目希望在微分博弈框架下，同时刻画后发优势与信息不完全的问题。我们将尝试建立求解贝叶斯纳什均衡的方法，并分析不完全信息如何影响企业成为后发者的动机。 在此基础上，本项目还将把企业的金融结构纳入博弈模型，研究市场竞争如何影响企业的一系列重要决策，包括杠杆选择、流动性管理、违约时机以及融资安排等。我们也将进一步分析模型所蕴含的政策启示和实证预测。在实践层面，本研究将为企业在竞争环境中更有效地管理流动性、优化资本结构提供指导，同时也为政策制定者理解并纠正市场竞争中的低效率问题提供理论依据。 本项目具有明显的跨学科特点，将结合最优停时、随机控制、偏微分方程和数值计算等方法，服务于微分博弈、实物期权、资本结构和流动性管理等领域的研究。

15211526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15211526.value: 高效零知識證明：新約束系統、重複電路聚合、與應用

15211526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15211526.value: Zero-Knowledge Succinct Non-Interactive Arguments of Knowledge (zk-SNARK) has become a fundamental tool in privacy-preserving technology, providing a powerful way for a prover to demonstrate the correctness of a computation without revealing private information. Their succinct proofs and fast verification make them crucial for secure outsourcing, verifiable computation, and blockchain scalability. However, zk-SNARK proof generation remains both memory-intensive and computation-heavy, limiting its practicality for complex statements. This project aims to overcome these limitations by proposing new zk-SNARK constructions that improve efficiency and applicability through three technical objectives. We first aim to propose a new variant of Plonkish constraint system, which is one of the most adopted constraint systems in building zk-SNARK, to support the free addition gate property as the R1CS (Rank-1-Constraint-System). By replacing the traditional permutation check used for checking wire connections with a new linear check, the proposed new system will allow both wiring connections and addition relations to be verified in a single batched linear equation, and eliminate explicit addition gate representations in the witness polynomial. This will reduce the proof generation complexity in both computation and memory for circuits with a large number of addition gates, while preserving the flexibility of the Plonkish constraint system to support custom high-degree gates. The second objective aims at designing new zk-SNARKs for circuits with repetitive subcircuits. Many large-scale computations, such as zk-rollups and batch signature verifications, rely on circuits with repetitive subcircuits. Building upon the new Plonkish constraint system proposed in objective 1 and R1CS, we will design a zk-SNARK framework that integrates identical subcircuits into a single “aggregated” instance. This approach minimizes redundant proving work, cuts memory consumption, and ensures that both proof size and proving complexity depend on the subcircuit size rather than the total circuit size. In the third objective, to enhance the efficiency of zk-SNARK applications in image provenance, we will design a practical privacy-preserving proof framework for verifying multi-step image transformations. Instead of generating separate proofs for each transformation step, our system will produce a single, succinct proof for the entire transformation chain. To ensure real-world interoperability, the framework will maintain full compatibility with the C2PA (Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity) standard by linking zk-friendly hashes (such as Poseidon) with SHA-256 and ECDSA signatures. Collectively, by proposing a new constraint system, leveraging circuit structure, and bridging zk-SNARKs with real-world image provenance, this project advances zk-SNARKs toward deployability in complex and privacy-critical environments. 零知識簡潔非互動式知識證明（Zero-Knowledge Succinct Non-Interactive Arguments of Knowledge, zk-SNARK）已成為隱私保護技術中的一項基礎工具，使證明者能夠在不洩露私密資訊的情況下證明某項計算的正確性。其證明具有簡潔性，且驗證速度快，因此對安全外包計算、可驗證計算以及區塊鏈擴展等應用至關重要。然而，zk-SNARK的證明生成過程仍然需要大量計算資源，限制了其在複雜實例上的實際應用。本項目旨在透過三個技術目標提升zk-SNARK效率與實用性。 首先，我們旨在提出一種新的Plonkish約束系統。Plonkish 是目前構建 zk-SNARK 時最廣泛採用的約束系統之一。我們希望使其具備類似R1CS的「免費加法閘」特性。對於包含大量加法閘的電路而言，此設計可同時降低證明生成的計算與記憶體複雜度，同時保留 Plonkish 約束系統支援自訂高次數閘的靈活性。 第二個目標是為具有重複子電路的電路設計新zk-SNARK系統。我們將設計一個 zk-SNARK 框架，將相同的子電路整合為單一聚合實例。此方法能夠減少重複的證明生成工作、降低記憶體消耗，並使證明大小以及證明生成複雜度取決於子電路的大小，而非整體電路的大小。 第三個目標旨在提升zk-SNARK在影像來源驗證應用中的效率。我們將設計一套實用且具隱私保護能力的證明框架，為確保與現實世界系統之間的互通性，此框架將透過連結適合零知識證明的雜湊函數與 SHA-256及ECDSA簽章，維持與 C2PA標準的完整相容性。 總體而言，本項目將透過提出新的約束系統、利用電路結構特性，以及建立zk-SNARK與實際影像來源驗證技術之間的橋樑，推動zk-SNARK朝向可部署於複雜且高度重視隱私之應用環境的方向發展。

15211726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15211726.value: 保护数十亿用户：跨移动操作系统的访问控制漏洞系统性检测研究

15211726.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15211726.value: Prof Luo, Xiapu Dr TANG, Yutian

15211726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15211726.value: Mobile operating systems, including Android, iOS, and HarmonyOS, enforce permission-based access control to protect sensitive functions and private data across billions of devices worldwide. Despite this critical security infrastructure, the complexity and massive codebases of these systems lead developers to inadvertently introduce vulnerabilities that enable attackers to launch denial-of-service attacks, brick devices, and steal personally identifiable information. Current security analysis methods exhibit three fundamental limitations: they fail to comprehensively detect access control inconsistencies across platforms, overlook missing privacy protection controls for data access, and cannot identify hidden requirements when permission checks are uniformly absent. This research systematically addresses these gaps through three complementary detection methods targeting distinct vulnerability types. First, our cross-platform function-directed approach identifies access control inconsistencies where sensitive system functions are protected in some execution paths but exposed in others. This method achieves platform independence through adaptive analysis of IPC mechanisms and employs large language models to systematically identify callback relationships in platform-specific asynchronous APIs, enabling comprehensive call graph construction without manual modeling. Second, our universal data-driven method detects missing privacy protection controls when system service interfaces transmit private data to apps without permission enforcement. This approach combines static analysis with LLM-assisted refinement to eliminate imprecise data flows while handling platform-specific propagation patterns. Third, our platform-independent semantic-based approach uncovers hidden access control requirements "invisible" to code analysis.
