By doing so, it will contribute to building secure, reliable, and entirely renewable-based power grids that help achieve carbon neutrality targets in Hong Kong and worldwide. 實現碳中和需要更多基於可再生能源的電力。然而，若是目前廣泛採用的基於跟網型逆變器的并網資源（GFL-IBRs）占比過高，將危及電力系統的穩定性與可靠性。2025 年西班牙大停電便鮮明地證實此風險的存在。構網型（GFM）逆變器是一項強大且具前景的方案。它能模擬同步發電機的并網特性，可為 100% 再生能源供電的電網建立穩定基礎。然而，基於構網型逆變器的并網資源（GFM-IBRs）在物理特性上有別於同步發電機，它的過電流能力顯著較低，且需要專門的控制策略，才能在故障期間維持自身運行並支撐電網。這些差異造成了關鍵知識缺口，使產業界與學術界在相關的設計與運行標準上缺乏共識。 本項目針對此缺口所衍生的兩項核心挑戰展開研究：如何以科學方式設計GFM-IBRs 的過電流容量？以及如何策略性地利用此電流，以最大化 GFM-IBR 在故障期間的存活與電網支撐能力？本項目將透過系統的多階段研究來回答上述問題。首先，我們將建立一套分析框架，評估現有故障穿越策略，定量界定其性能極限與取捨關係。接著，本項目的核心創新在於研發新穎且科學的容量設計框架，可根據特定電網條件與 FRT 目標，決定 GFM-IBRs 的最佳過電流額定值。同時，我們將研發先進的自適應控制策略，使其能在不同 FRT 運行目標之間智能地切換，例如最大化地支撐電壓或同步功率，從而能夠主動且有效地運用 GFM-IBR 有限的資源。最後，這些創新成果將透過電磁暫態仿真與系統性的功率硬件在環（power-hardware-in-the-loop, PHIL）實驗進行嚴謹分析與驗證，以證明其在混合型低慣量電力系統中的有效性。 本項目將有助深化產業界、學術界與監管機構對 GFM-IBR 故障穿越特性的認識。項目成果將能提供清晰、可執行的方案，使GFM 技術對於電網運行與設備製造商而言更加可預測、更具成本優勢。通過推動技術標準的建立，本研究將能促進可再生能源電力的部署，有助於構建安全、可靠且以再生能源為基礎的電力系統，支持香港及全球實現碳中和目標。

15222626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15222626.value: 基於外牆玻璃-火交互作用作為輸入的預測室內火特徵的人工智能模型

15222626.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15222626.value: Prof Chen, Suwen Prof YANG, Bo

15222626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15222626.value: In Hong Kong, each year records around 35000 fire cases. More than 3000 cases are building fires, and around 25000 cases are unwanted fire alarms. Current firefighting operations are based on the experiences and high-risk operation of firefighters inside buildings. To either achieve optimized firefighting to effectively prevent fire spread or to potentially use unmanned firefighting vehicles such as UAVs to fight fires, the first and foremost task is to know “where and how large the fire is in a building”. The emerging smart firefighting research has attempted to use artificial intelligence to predict fire behaviour, which is based on the inversed relation between fire heating impact (e.g., ceiling temperature at different locations) and the size of localised fire. However, this approach requires widely distributed temperature sensors or cameras, which is hardly achievable in modern buildings for the concerns of cost and privacy. In this project, a novel methodology is proposed to resolve these conflicted needs, which aims to predict the size and location of an accident fire inside a building through interpreting external observables captured outside the building. This methodology is motived by the PI’s past research on investigating glass-fire interaction in large compartment fires, which has found that glass temperature rises, fallout patterns, and ejecting smoke/flames are feasible indices to the prediction of fire characteristics such as HRR and flaming area. This project will extend the preliminary success of AI fire prediction to more generalized scenarios, which will characterize the glass-fire interaction as indices to the prediction of fires in Type A residential compartments and Type B large open-plan office compartments. Glass fallout models considering modern glass designs and non-uniform heating will be developed and implemented in integrated CFD fire simulation, which is then deployed to generate a large set of sample cases with various façade observables. Together with the camera captured videos/images in fire tests and fire accidents as cross validation, the simulated images will be interpreted and quantified using Computer Vision tools, and the dataset will be fed to the training of AI models to predict fire characteristics. This project will lead to an AI based Insider-Out fire prediction framework that eliminates the need of in-building sensors and provides the key fire situation information to the firefighting officers and to the automated firefighting UAVs & robots in future. 現代高層建築的火災安全是一個至關重要的課題，尤其是对于香港和中國內地等人口稠密的城市環境。在這些地方，每年都會發生數以千計的建築物火災，並伴隨大量的虛假警報。傳統的消防工程主要集中於小型分隔空間的火災，但大型開放式空間（其特點是非均勻燃燒和局部蔓延的「移動式火災」）所帶來的獨特火災動力學，為預測和緩解火災帶來了新的挑戰。其中一個關鍵但尚未得到充分研究的方面，是火災發展與外牆構件（特別是當代建築中普遍存在的玻璃窗）之間的相互作用。玻璃面板對火非常敏感，其破裂和脫落可以作為內部火災動力學的顯著觀測指標，從而有望實現從外部預測內部火災特徵。本项目提出了一種創新的「由外而內(Inside-Out)」預測框架。該框架利用外部外牆觀測結果（例如玻璃脫落模式、濃煙和火焰溢出），實時推斷關鍵的內部火災特徵（例如熱釋放率、火焰面積、煙霧溫度和火災位置）。該方法整合了先進的計算流體動力學 (CFD) 模擬、火災測試以及人工智能 (AI) 技術（特別是電腦視覺模型），以建立並量化可觀測的外牆現象與內部火災發展之間的相關性。本項目主要聚焦於兩種核心建築類型：具有多個單位和玻璃窗的住宅建築（A型），以及具有大型開放式佈局和框架玻璃外牆的高層辦公大樓（B型）。本项目共分成6个分工作内容：玻璃脫落前分隔空間火災的 CFD 模型建立。開發非均勻受熱下各類現代玻璃類型的簡化「玻璃—火災」相互作用模型。火災與玻璃脫落的整合模擬。透過模擬、真實火災和火災測試，進行外牆觀測指標的特徵分析及數據集生成。利用電腦視覺進行基於 AI 的「玻璃—火災」相互作用解讀與定位。開發 AI 驅動的「由外而內」預測工具。預期成果是一個高效且具擴展性的 AI 框架，能夠提供快速、非侵入式的火災情勢評估，以支援消防決策，並助力無人機 (UAV) 和機械人等先進消防技術的部署。該項目的研究結果和數據集將公開傳播，以促進火災安全工程領域的進一步研究與實際應用。

15223226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15223226.value: 圖形壓縮的後門攻擊：效率、問題與應用

15223226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15223226.value: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have emerged as the leading model for encoding structural information such as social networks, recommender systems, and chemical molecules. However, training GNNs on large graphs presents significant challenges due to high resource demanding and extended training time. Graph Condensation (GC) has emerged as a vital technique for scaling Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to large-scale datasets, condensing large graphs into small yet informative ones for efficient training. However, the prevailing focus on optimizing the trade-off between graph size and model performance has left the security vulnerabilities of GC critically underexplored. This oversight is highly concerning, especially as data providers facilitate model development, introducing potential security risks from untrustworthy sources. This project addresses this significant research gap by comprehensively investigating the security of GC through the lens of backdoor attacks. Our investigation begins by devising a Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) based backdoor attack framework to systematically reveal the security mechanisms inherent in kernel-based GC. To move beyond brute-force poisoning methods, we will develop an effective target node selection method that leverages the NTK output and conflict loss to maximize attack efficacy while minimizing the number of poisoned nodes required, thus preserving the model’s performance on clean data. Furthermore, we will investigate the security of GC in a more practical and challenging threat model by devising a backdoor attack where the adversary only has access to the condensed graph. Moving beyond conventional metrics of attack success, this project will be the first to systematically investigate the unintended side effects of these attacks, which we term “backdoor complications.” We will define a taxonomy of these anomalies and propose a more holistic evaluation metric, “General Behavioral Stealthiness,” to assess the true stealthiness of an attack across diverse and unforeseen tasks. Finally, we will create a prototype of our framework and validate its real-world applicability by designing a kernel-based promotion attack for the link prediction task in graph-based recommendation systems. This comprehensive methodology is anticipated to expose critical security flaws in current GC methods and pave the way for the development of more robust and secure graph condensation techniques for real-world deployment. 圖神經網絡 (GNNs) 已經成為編碼結構信息的主要模型，例如社交網絡、推薦系統和化學分子。然而，在大型圖上訓練 GNNs 面臨著重大挑戰，因為其對資源需求高且訓練時間長。圖凝聚 (GC) 已成為將圖神經網絡擴展到大規模數據集的重要技術，能將大型圖凝縮成小而信息豐富的圖，以提升訓練效率。然而，目前大多集中在優化圖大小和模型性能之間的權衡上，卻對 GC 的安全漏洞關注不足。這個忽略非常令人擔憂，特別是當數據提供者促進模型開發時，可能會帶來來自不可信來源的安全風險。本項目旨在通過後門攻擊的視角，全面調查 GC 的安全性，來填補這一重要的研究空白。我們的研究從設計一個基於神經切線核 (NTK) 的後門攻擊框架開始，旨在系統地揭示基於核的圖卷積（GC）中內建的安全機制。為了超越暴力式的中毒方法，我們將開發一種有效的目標節點選擇方法，利用 NTK 輸出和衝突損失來最大化攻擊效果，同時最小化所需中毒節點的數量，從而保護模型在乾淨數據上的表現。此外，我們還將通過設計一種攻擊者僅能訪問精簡圖的後門攻擊，來探討在更實用且具有挑戰性的威脅模型下，GC 的安全性。超越傳統攻擊成功率的評估指標，這個項目將首次系統性地研究這些攻擊帶來的非預期副作用，我們將其稱為「後門併發症」。我們將定義這些異常的分類法，並提出一個更全面的評估指標——「一般行為隱匿性」，來評估攻擊在各種不同和不可預見的任務中的真實隱匿性。最後，我們會建立我們框架的原型，並透過為圖形推薦系統中的連結預測任務設計一個基於內核的促進攻擊，來驗證其在現實中的適用性。這種全面的方法預計能揭示當前圖神經網路方法的重要安全漏洞，並為開發更穩健、更安全的圖濃縮技術以應用於實際部署鋪路。

15224226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15224226.value: 電力系統可信人工智能：大型語言模型增強的深度強化學習用於大規模安全約束最優潮流求解

15224226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15224226.value: Prof McCalley, James Prof Zhang, Hongcai Prof Zhao, Junhua

15224226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15224226.value: Alternating-current (AC) Optimal Power Flow (OPF) forms the foundation for the operation of autonomous energy systems. Recent studies have shown that deep reinforcement learning (DRL) offers an efficient approach to solving AC OPF problems. However, several critical gaps still hinder the practical deployment of DRL in real-world power systems: 1) Few studies consider N-1 post-contingency scenarios when applying DRL to AC OPF; 2) DRL-based decisions may lack trustworthiness due to the models’ inherent black-box nature and external uncertainties; and 3) DRL algorithms trained on small systems often fail to generalize to large-scale networks. To address these challenges, this project aims to develop a trustworthy artificial intelligence framework for solving large-scale Security-Constrained OPF (SCOPF) problems. The proposed framework focuses on enhancing the robustness, reliability, interactivity, and scalability of DRL models to enable their practical use in SCOPF applications. First, we will develop a robust DRL algorithm capable of maintaining high performance under data uncertainty and system topology changes, including N-1 post-contingency conditions. Next, we will design a reliable DRL framework that enhances model transparency, enabling parameters learned from historical data to generalize effectively across new operating contexts. These two aspects will be integrated into a comprehensive trustworthy DRL-based SCOPF solution framework, combining robustness and reliability. To further strengthen operational trust, we will incorporate human expertise into the decision-making loop through the assistance of large language models, facilitating expert-augmented and interpretable control strategies. Finally, we will develop a consensus-federated DRL approach to efficiently handle large-scale SCOPF problems. The proposed methods will be validated using two synthetic systems—the IEEE 8376-bus system and the Texas 6717-bus system—as well as a real-world Guangdong power system comprising approximately 30,000 buses and over 100,000 electrical elements. We anticipate that the outcomes of this project will benefit not only the global research community but also Hong Kong, which is striving for carbon neutrality through the development of green industries and the promotion of decarbonization technologies and innovation. 交流最優潮流（ACOPF）是自主能源系統運行的基礎。近期研究表明，深度強化學習（DRL）爲求解交流最優潮流問題提供了一種高效方法。然而，在真實電力系統中實際部署DRL仍麵臨若幹關鍵障礙：1）在將DRL應用於ACOPF時，少有研究考慮N-1故障後的場景；2）由於模型固有的黑箱特性以及外部不確定性，基於DRL的決策可能缺乏可信度；3）在小規模系統上訓練的DRL算法往往難以泛化到大規模網絡。爲應對這些挑戰，本項目旨在開髮一種用於求解大規模安全約束最優潮流（SCOPF）問題的可信人工智能框架。所提出的框架重點提昇DRL模型的魯棒性、可靠性、交互性和可擴展性，以支持其在SCOPF應用中的實際使用。首先，我們將開髮一種魯棒DRL算法，使其能夠在數據不確定性和系統拓撲變化條件下保持高性能，包括N-1故障後運行條件。隨後，我們將設計一種可靠的DRL框架，以提昇模型透明度，使從曆史數據中學習得到的參數能夠有效泛化到新的運行場景。這兩個方麵將被集成到一個全麵的、基於可信DRL的SCOPF求解框架中，融合魯棒性與可靠性。爲進一步增強運行可信度，我們將藉助大語言模型（LLMs）將人類專家知識納入決策閉環，從而實現專家增強且可解釋的控製策略。最後，我們將開髮一種共識聯邦DRL方法，以高效處理大規模SCOPF問題。所提出的方法將通過兩個合成系統——IEEE 8376節點系統和Texas 6717節點系統——以及一個真實的廣東電力系統進行驗証；該實際系統包含約30,000個節點和超過100,000個電氣元件。我們預期，本項目成果不僅將惠及全球研究界，也將助力香港通過髮展綠色産業以及推動脫碳技術與創新來實現碳中和目標。

15224726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15224726.value: 用於壓縮、增強及評估AI生成視訊的生成式框架

15224726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15224726.value: The rapid advancement and widespread adoption of AI-generated video (AIGV) technologies have resulted in an exponential growth in AIGV content across various digital platforms. Access and sharing of such massive AIGV contents demand fundamentally new representation strategy that is more suitable for compressing AI-generate video contents. Without new compression strategy, AIGV shall face significant challenges in its practical deployment and scalability. It is therefore imperative to develop new representation and compression frameworks specifically designed fro AI-generated videos. Traditional video coding standards and recent end-to-end neural compression methods are primarily designed for natural videos captured by cameras. They are not suitable for compressing AI-generated videos due to the fundamental differences in generating video contents. Conventional encoding strategy is unable exploit the unique semantic structures and generative priors inherent in AIGVs, resulting in sub-optimal performance. A new compression framework that is tailored for AI-generated videos is urgently needed to achieve breakthrough performance. This project aims to develop a holistic generative framework for AIGV compression and enhancement, and their quality assessment. Specifically, the research agenda includes: (1) Developing a multi-modal collaborative decomposition framework to learn compact semantic representations for video reconstruction; (2) Designing an implicit neural compression system with cross-modal prediction to achieve semantic-preserving compression; (3) Constructing a cloud-based reference-guided enhancement network to restore perceptual quality using retrieved video samples; (4) Establishing a learnable quality assessment model that quantifies semantic fidelity to guide and evaluate the entire framework. The proposed research includes both theoretical analysis and experimental verification. In theoretical analysis, we shall focus on the semantic representation learning and cross-modal redundancy reduction to establish the foundation for efficient AIGV compression. We shall also explore the integration of generative priors and semantic perceptual characteristics into the AIGV enhancement and quality assessment. In experimental verification, we will conduct comprehensive experiments on videos generated by various advanced AIGV models to verify the proposed framework. The outcome of the proposed research will be disseminated via both publications and patents. Source codes of the algorithms developed in this project will be uploaded to an open-source platform for sharing with the research community. A special outcome will be in the form of the contributions to the development of semantic-preserving compression standards specifically tailored for AI-generated videos. We expect that the impact of this research will reach beyond academia to benefit the deployment of AIGC products in various industries.

15224826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15224826.value: 一款可解釋的 AI 驅動腦電圖-功能性近紅外線腦成像頭盔，用於監測建築設備操作員的心理疲勞

15224826.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15224826.value: Dr MEHMOOD, Imran Dr UMER, Waleed

15224826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15224826.value: The construction industry is rapidly adopting digital technologies to enhance efficiency and safety, yet equipment operators face significant challenges due to mentally demanding tasks. Long hours, repetitive tasks, and increased interaction with digital tools elevate cognitive load, leading to mental fatigue that impairs concentration, decision-making, and reaction times, increasing accident risks and reducing productivity. While technologies like EEG, eye-tracking, wristbands, and sweat sensors have been explored for fatigue detection, their practical limitations such as discomfort, sensor dislocation, maintenance needs, privacy concerns, and environmental interference hinder real-world use in construction settings. To address these issues, this project proposes a dual-phase approach integrating multimodal electroencephalography (EEG) and functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy (fNIRS) with explainable AI (xAI) to develop a transparent, trustworthy mental fatigue monitoring system for construction equipment operators. The project will be conducted in two phases. In the discovery phase, the first of its kind, EEG (capturing rapid neural oscillations) and fNIRS (measuring hemodynamic changes in cortical regions) will map neurocognitive patterns and functional connectivity during equipment operation tasks. This will identify fatigue critical brain regions and connections. More importantly, it will provide interpretable insights into fatigue mechanisms, enabling stakeholders to understand why specific AI based fatigue predictions are made. These insights are essential for regulatory compliance and trust in technology. In the development phase, xAI-derived insights will guide the design of a lightweight, PPE-compatible helmet integrating minimal and optimally placed EEG-fNIRS sensors for real-time, interpretable fatigue monitoring. The proposed multimodal system contributes significantly by: (1) advancing neuroscience through xAI-enhanced mapping of fatigue-related functional connectivity and network efficiency, revealing previously opaque brain dynamics in construction-specific contexts; (2) pioneering engineering innovation through xAI-driven sensor optimization that reduces channels from 60+ to ~15 while maintaining accuracy and providing transparent decision rationale; and (3) delivering practical impact with an interpretable system where xAI explains fatigue predictions to operators and managers, facilitating informed safety interventions and building trust in automated monitoring. The prototype will be rigorously evaluated in real-world Hong Kong construction environments to validate its reliability, usability, and interpretability, with xAI ensuring transparent performance metrics. By synergizing EEG-fNIRS with xAI, this project transforms opaque neural data into actionable, explainable safety insights, advancing neuroscientific and engineering knowledge while aligning with Sustainable Development Goals 3, 8, and 9, and addressing Hong Kong's construction industry challenges through transparent, trustworthy technology. 營造業正迅速採用數位科技以提升效率與安全性，然而設備操作員因面臨高心智負擔的任務，仍遭遇重大挑戰。長時間工作、重複性作業，以及與數位工具互動的增加，皆提高了認知負荷，進而導致心智疲勞，削弱專注力、決策能力與反應時間，增加事故風險並降低生產力。儘管已有研究探索運用腦電圖（EEG）、眼動追蹤、手環及汗水感測器等技術進行疲勞偵測，但其在實務上的限制，例如不適感、感測器位移、維護需求、隱私疑慮及環境干擾等，阻礙了其在營造場域中的實際應用。 為解決上述問題，本計畫提出雙階段途徑，整合多模式腦電圖（EEG）與功能性近紅外光譜（fNIRS），並結合可解釋人工智慧（xAI），以開發一套透明、可信賴的營造設備操作員心智疲勞監測系統。本計畫將分兩階段進行。在探索階段，此為同類研究首創，將透過EEG（捕捉快速神經振盪）與fNIRS（量測大腦皮質區域的血流動力變化），繪製設備操作作業期間的神經認知模式與功能性連結，藉此識別與疲勞相關的重要腦區及連結。更重要的是，此階段將提供對疲勞機制的可解釋性見解，使利害關係人能理解為何AI會做出特定疲勞預測。這些見解對於法規遵循及對技術的信任至關重要。 在開發階段，由xAI衍生之見解將引導設計一款輕量化、可搭配個人防護裝備（PPE）的安全帽，整合最少且最佳配置的EEG-fNIRS感測器，以實現即時且可解釋的疲勞監測。本計畫所提出之多模式系統具有以下重要貢獻：（1）透過xAI強化疲勞相關功能性連結與網路效率的繪製，推進神經科學進展，揭示過往在營造特定情境中難以掌握的大腦動態；（2）透過xAI驅動的感測器優化，開創工程創新，將通道數從60多個減少至約15個，同時維持準確度並提供透明的決策依據；（3）提供具實務影響力的可解釋系統，由xAI向操作員與管理者說明疲勞預測結果，促進知情的安全介入措施，並建立對自動化監測的信任。 本計畫的原型系統將在香港的真實營造環境中進行嚴格評估，以驗證其可靠性、實用性與可解釋性，並藉由xAI確保透明的績效指標。透過將EEG-fNIRS與xAI結合，本計畫將不透明的大腦神經數據轉化為可具體行動且可解釋的安全見解，不僅推進神經科學與工程知識，同時呼應永續發展目標第3、8及9項，並以透明且可信賴的技術，回應香港營造業所面臨的挑戰。

15225126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15225126.value: 基於神經展開的可學習演化多目標優化

15225126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15225126.value: Prof TAN, Kay Chen Prof Yang, Ming Dr Yao, Lu

15225126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15225126.value: Evolutionary Multi-objective Optimization (EMO) has long served as a foundational methodology for resolving multiple conflicting objectives in science, engineering, and decision-making. While traditional heuristics have achieved remarkable success in approximating Pareto fronts, the rise of learning-based optimization brings new opportunities for automation, adaptability, and integration with modern AI systems. Yet, the systematic unification of learning and EMO remains an open challenge. First, conventional EMO algorithms rely on fixed heuristic mechanisms such as non-dominated sorting and diversity preservation. These operators are inherently non-differentiable, creating what we term the Differentiability Gap that hinders end-to-end learning and adaptation. Second, emerging learning-based strategies, including algorithm selection, optimizer composition, and LLM-guided operator design, remain largely confined to single-objective or surrogate-assisted contexts where gradient information is readily available, leaving the problem of Multi-objective Scalability unresolved. Third, real-world scientific problems often demand structural generalization across high-dimensional and computationally intensive environments, yet existing methods lack a principled framework to ensure both adaptability and theoretical soundness, highlighting a persistent Structural Generalization challenge. To address these challenges, this project proposes a unified framework of Learnable Evolutionary Multi-objective Optimization (LEMO). First, to bridge the Differentiability Gap, we establish a bilevel learning formulation that embeds EMO operations within a differentiable computational graph supported by theoretical guarantees. Second, to enhance Multi-objective Scalability, we design a neural-unrolling architecture equipped with a modular library of learnable operators for efficient optimization in high-dimensional settings. Third, to achieve Structural Generalization, we develop a system-level platform integrating benchmarks, multi-fidelity evaluations, and AI4Science case studies to support validation and deployment of EMO algorithms. Collectively, these efforts aim to advance EMO from a heuristic-driven paradigm toward a learnable, differentiable, and structure-aware framework. 演化多目標優化（EMO）長期以來一直是處理科學、工程及決策領域中多個相互衝突目標的基礎方法。傳統啟發式方法在逼近帕累托前沿方面已取得顯著成果，而學習式優化的興起，則為自動化、適應能力及與現代人工智能系統的整合帶來了新的機遇。然而，如何系統性地統一學習方法與 EMO，仍然是一項尚未解決的挑戰。 首先，傳統 EMO 算法依賴非支配排序、多樣性維持等固定的啟發式機制。這些運算本質上不可微分，從而形成我們所稱的"可微分性鴻溝"，阻礙端到端學習與自適應。其次，新興的學習式策略，包括算法選擇、優化器組合，以及由大型語言模型引導的算子設計，目前仍主要局限於單目標或代理模型輔助的情境。在這些情境中，梯度資訊通常較容易取得，因此"多目標可擴展性"問題仍未得到解決。第三，現實世界中的科學問題往往要求方法能夠在高維度及高計算成本的環境中實現結構泛化，但現有方法缺乏一套具原則性的框架，以同時確保適應能力與理論嚴謹性，突顯出持續存在的"結構泛化"挑戰。 為應對上述挑戰，本項目提出一套統一的可學習演化多目標優化（LEMO）框架。首先，為彌合可微分性鴻溝，我們建立一套雙層學習建模方法，將 EMO 運算嵌入具理論保證的可微分計算圖之中。其次，為提升多目標可擴展性，我們設計一種神經展開架構，並配備由多個可學習算子組成的模組化算子庫，以支援高維度環境中的高效優化。第三，為實現結構泛化，我們開發一個系統級平台，整合基準測試、多保真度評估及 AI4Science 案例研究，以支援 EMO 算法的驗證與部署。整體而言，這些工作旨在推動 EMO 由啟發式方法主導的範式，邁向一個可學習、可微分且具結構感知能力的框架，從而提升多目標優化方法的適應能力與可解釋性。

15225426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15225426.value: 表面工程強化氣泡脫附實現高效電解製氫

15225426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15225426.value: Electrolytic hydrogen production has gained significant attention as a sustainable alternative to fossil fuels and a leading solution for energy storage. Nevertheless, the persistent formation of bubbles on electrode surfaces continues to pose a common challenge in electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution reactions. These adhered bubbles create localized dry zones that isolate active catalytic sites from the electrolyte, thereby substantially reducing the overall system efficiency. Surface engineering has recently emerged as a promising approach to address this bottleneck, offering the potential to enhance bubble detachment without requiring additional energy input. Yet, current surface engineering strategies remain predominantly focused on reducing bubble-electrode adhesion forces, which face inherent limitations due to the constrained reducibility of electrode surface energy and the scaling effect, where adhesion forces dominate over buoyancy as bubble dimensions decrease. This project explores a largely unexplored alternative: amplifying the bubble detachment forces for efficient electrolytic hydrogen production. Our approach employs rationally designed electrode surfaces featuring superaerophobic thin-walled lattice structures (STLS) that spatially regulate bubble growth and rectify fluid dynamics during bubble coalescence. The optimized bubble coalescence generates substantially enhanced off-plane detachment forces that scale comparably with adhesion forces, enabling bubble jumping at significantly reduced sizes and higher probabilities compared to conventional surfaces, thereby promoting the electrocatalytic reactions. This project builds upon but goes beyond our recent breakthrough in the demonstrations of TLS in enhancing droplet jumping (Nature Communications 2022) and bubble/droplet manipulation for energy conversion (Nature 2020, Science Advances 2022). Preliminary results confirm that STLS achieves significantly smaller bubble detachment sizes and higher detachment frequencies compared to the conventional designs. This enhanced bubble detachment yields a reduced surface bubble coverage and record-low overpotentials of 19.46 mV at 10 mA per square meter and 44.1 mV at 100 mA per square meter, indicative of exceptional hydrogen evolution reaction performance. In this project, we will first systematically investigate bubble statistics on STLS with varying lattice dimensions and establish correlations with electrochemical performance. We will then analyze in detail individual bubble dynamics and theoretically elucidate the bubble detachment mechanism, with particular emphasis on how lattice structures influence bubble growth and coalescence jumping. These insights will further inform generalized design criteria. Finally, we will demonstrate a renewable energy-driven electrolytic hydrogen production device. We anticipate that the STLS-mediated bubble detachment will significantly advance fundamental understanding of coalescence jumping phenomena and pioneer new pathways for designing advanced materials and devices for green energy and environmental applications. 電解製氫作為化石燃料的可持續替代方案，以及能源儲存的重要技術，近年受到廣泛關注。然而，電極表面持續形成氣泡，仍然是電催化析氫反應中普遍存在的挑戰。黏附於電極表面的氣泡會形成局部乾區，使活性催化位點與電解液隔離，從而顯著降低整個系統的效率。近年，表面工程被視為解決此瓶頸的一項具潛力的方法，可在毋須額外能量輸入的情況下促進氣泡脫附。然而，現有的表面工程策略主要集中於降低氣泡與電極之間的黏附力。由於電極表面能可降低的幅度有限，加上尺度效應的影響，當氣泡尺寸減小時，黏附力會逐漸主導浮力，因此相關策略存在固有局限。 本項目將探索一種尚未獲充分研究的替代方案，即透過增強氣泡脫附力，實現高效電解製氫。我們將採用經合理設計、具有超疏氣薄壁晶格結構（superaerophobic thin-walled lattice structures，STLS）的電極表面，以空間調控氣泡生長，並整流氣泡聚併過程中的流體動力學行為。經優化的氣泡聚併過程可產生顯著增強的離面脫附力，而該脫附力與黏附力具有相若的尺度關係。與傳統表面相比，此設計可使氣泡在更小尺寸下以更高概率發生跳躍脫附，從而促進電催化反應。 本項目建基於我們近期取得的突破，並在此基礎上進一步拓展。相關研究包括利用薄壁晶格結構促進液滴跳躍的研究（《Nature Communications》，2022年），以及利用氣泡和液滴操控實現能量轉換的研究（《Nature》，2020年；《Science Advances》，2022年）。初步結果證實，與傳統設計相比，STLS可顯著減小氣泡脫附尺寸，並提高氣泡脫附頻率。經強化的氣泡脫附可降低電極表面的氣泡覆蓋率，並在10 mA m⁻²及100 mA m⁻²的電流密度下，分別實現低至19.46 mV及44.1 mV的過電位，顯示出卓越的析氫反應性能。 在本項目中，我們首先會系統研究不同晶格尺寸STLS表面的氣泡統計特徵，並建立其與電化學性能之間的關係。其後，我們將詳細分析單個氣泡的動力學行為，並從理論上闡明氣泡脫附機制，重點探討晶格結構如何影響氣泡生長及聚併誘導跳躍。相關研究結果將進一步用於建立具普適性的設計準則。最後，我們將展示一套由可再生能源驅動的電解製氫裝置。我們預期，由STLS介導的氣泡脫附機制，將顯著深化對氣泡聚併跳躍現象的基礎理解，並為綠色能源及環境應用中的先進材料與器件設計開拓新的途徑。

15226126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15226126.value: 基于數據、知識和人智互動的協同整合构建AI-XR賦能的經尿道膀胱腫瘤整塊切除術患者個性化手術規劃和術中引導系统

15226126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15226126.value: Dr Teoh, Yuen Chun, Jeremy Prof Wong, Tien-Tsin Prof ZHAO, Shengdong

15226126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15226126.value: Bladder cancer is among the ten most common cancers worldwide. Conventionally, standard resection is performed transurethrally to resect a bladder tumor in a piecemeal manner. However, piecemeal resection results in floating tumor cells, which may reimplant onto the bladder wall and lead to disease recurrence. Recently, transurethral en bloc resection of bladder tumor (ERBT) has been proposed as an innovative alternative technique to overcome this shortcoming. By removing the tumor in one piece, the risk of reimplantation can be reduced. However, ERBT is a very challenging task for surgeons owing to (1) complex (and patient-specific) surgical anatomy, (2) difficulties in identifying optimal operation paths, removing the tumor in one piece without damaging surrounding tissues, and (3) limited range of view and operation under cystoscopy. While some extended reality (XR) based planning and intraoperative guidance techniques/systems have been proposed, they still cannot fulfil ERBT’s demanding requirements. The main shortcomings include suboptimal segmentation due to limited training data and large variation of surgical anatomy, imperfect visualization/reconstruction for precise and efficient planning/guidance, and defective registration between preoperative-intraoperative data under deformations. Particularly, most existing systems largely depend on data-incentive solutions while ignoring to sufficiently incorporate clinical knowledge/experience and human interactions to overcome inherent limitations of data-driven approaches. Afterall, surgery is a highly knowledge- and interaction-intensive procedure. In this project, we aim at developing a set of novel AI models that innovatively and synergistically integrate medical data, clinical knowledge/experience, and human-AI interactions to comprehensively address above challenges, including (1) a novel agentic segmentation model equipped with a memory bank and a mixture-of-experts module for interactive ERBT anatomy segmentation, (2) a novel visualization framework based on a editable Gaussian splatting model and a memory bank for interactive ERBT planning, (3) a novel generalizable human-in-the-loop model for real-time surgical scene reconstruction via a new causal Transformer architecture, and (4) a novel human-in-the-loop biomechanics-informed model for interactive preoperative-intraoperative data registration. Finally, we’ll develop a novel AI-XR empowered ERBT planning and intraoperative guidance system by integrating these new techniques and extensively validate it in clinical settings. In summary, this is a joint project with a strong interdisciplinary team, including experts in medical image computing, XR, visualization, human-computer interaction, and ERBT. The innovative techniques cannot only improve the preciseness and efficiency of ERBT but provide inspiring insights on how to incorporate knowledge/experience and human feedback into an AI-XR empowered computer-assisted surgery system to improve its performance. 膀胱癌是全球十大常見癌症之一。傳統上，標準切除術是經尿道以分塊切除的方式切除膀胱腫瘤。然而，分塊切除會導致殘存漂浮腫瘤細胞，這些細胞可能會重新植入膀胱壁上，導致疾病復發。近年來，經尿道膀胱腫瘤整塊切除術（ERBT）被提出作為一種創新的替代技術來克服這一缺點。透過整塊切除腫瘤，可以降低重新植入的風險。 然而，由於以下原因，ERBT 對外科醫生來說是一項極具挑戰性的任務：(1) 複雜的（且患者個體差異較大的）手術解剖結構；(2) 難以確定最佳手術路徑，在不損傷周圍組織的情況下整塊切除腫瘤；以及 (3) 膀胱鏡下視野和操作範圍有限。 目前，儘管已經開發了一些基於擴展現實（XR）的手術規劃和術中引導技術或系統，但它們仍然無法滿足ERBT的苛刻要求。主要缺陷包括：由於訓練資料有限和手術解剖結構差異大導致分割效果欠佳；可視化/重建不完善，無法實現精確高效的規劃/引導；以及在形變條件下術前-術中數據配準不準確。 尤其值得注意的是，大多數現有系統主要依賴數據驅動的解決方案，而忽略了應充分整合臨床知識、經驗和人智交互，以克服數據驅動方法固有的局限性。畢竟，手術是一個高度依賴知識和互動的過程。 本計畫旨在開發一系列新型人工智能模型，以創新且協同的方式整合醫療數據、臨床知識/經驗以及人智交互，從而全面應對上述挑戰。 這些模型包括：(1) 配備記憶庫和專家混合模組的新型智能分割模型，用於交互式ERBT解剖分割；(2) 基於可編輯高斯滾雪球模型和記憶庫的新型可視化框架，用於可交互ERBT術前規劃；(3) 基於新型因果Transformer架構的新型通用人機交互模型，用於實時手術場景重建。 最終，我們將整合這些新技術，開發一種新型的AI-XR賦能的ERBT術前規劃和術中引導系統，並在臨床環境中進行廣泛驗證。 總而言之，這是一個由強大的跨學科團隊合作開展的項目，團隊成員包括醫學影像計算、擴展顯示、視覺化、人機互動和ERBT等領域的專家。這些創新技術不僅可以提高ERBT的精確度和效率，還可以為如何將知識/經驗和人類反饋融入AI-XR賦能的電腦輔助手術系統以提高其性能提供真知灼見。

15226326.value: Prof Huang, Baoling Prof Wang, Qiuwang

15226326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15226326.value: Maintaining proper indoor humidity levels is essential for ensuring occupant health, enhancing comfort, preserving building materials, and boosting productivity. In hot and humid regions, moisture removal plays a dominant role in the fresh air treatment process, accounting for 50–70% of the total ventilation cooling load. Conventional condensation dehumidification, which is electricity-intensive, removes moisture by cooling air below its dew point. Dedicated solid desiccant dehumidifiers offer a compact and precise way to control indoor humidity by separating temperature and humidity regulation. These systems utilize hygroscopic materials to adsorb moisture driven by low-grade thermal energy rather than electricity, but face challenges like high regeneration temperatures (above 80°C) and high energy use for desorption due to the significant water-vapor phase change enthalpy. Furthermore, the water vapor evaporated during regeneration is discharged outdoors, wasting water. Developing new solid desiccants with high moisture adsorption capacity that can be regenerated using ultra-low-grade heat sources and scaled up to the device level is critical for achieving highly energy-efficient dehumidification. Recently, we successfully fabricated a thermo-responsive hydrogel composite (THC) containing hygroscopic salt with superior water uptake, and its wettability varies with temperatures demonstrating a reversible hydrophilic/hydrophobic wettability transition at 32°C. This enables the possible liquid water release-based regeneration to be powered by low-temperature thermal energy, together with water recovery. We believe these novel desiccants (THC) will usher in a new chapter in the field of dehumidification. Therefore, this project aims to develop a novel THC-based enthalpy exchanger for air dehumidification and water recovery in buildings. Firstly, a multi-physics model will be established to investigate the water sorption kinetics and the hydrophilic-hydrophobic transition mechanism of THC at the micro-/mesoscopic scale. Based on the obtained insights, THCs will be developed with programmable adsorption-desorption properties and tunable hydrophilic-hydrophobic transition temperatures to enhance adaptability. Next, an enthalpy exchanger coated with the developed THC will be fabricated and tested to examine its performance in dehumidification and regeneration integrated with water recovery. In parallel, a heat and mass transfer will be established to predict the prototype performance and guide design optimization. Finally, a THC-based moisture harvesting system will be developed and then comprehensively evaluated in terms of energy efficiency, economic feasibility, environmental impact, durability and climate resilience, thereby demonstrating its practical value for real-world building applications. We believe the thermo-responsive hydrogel composite and module structure will offer new insights into addressing energy-intensive air dehumidification and freshwater scarcity, enhancing energy-water-air nexus. 室內濕度水平，對保障居住者健康、提升熱舒適性、保護建築材料以及提高工作效率至關重要。在炎熱潮濕地區，除濕在新風處理過程中佔據主導地位，其能耗可佔總通風冷負荷的 50–70%。傳統冷凝除濕方法主要通過將空氣冷卻至露點以下來去除水分，因而高度依賴電力，能耗較高。專用固體除濕系統通過將溫度調節與濕度控制相分離，為室內濕度的精準控制提供了一種緊湊而有效的方案。該類系統利用吸濕材料吸附空氣中的水分，並可由低品位熱能而非電能驅動再生。然而，現有固體除濕系統仍面臨一些挑戰，例如再生溫度較高，通常高於 80°C；同時，由於水蒸氣相變焓較大，解吸過程能耗較高。此外，再生過程中蒸發出的水蒸氣通常被直接排放至室外，造成水資源浪費。 因此，開發具有高吸濕容量、可利用超低品位熱源再生，並能夠放大至器件層面的新型固體除濕材料，對實現高能效空氣除濕具有重要意義。近期，我們成功嘗試製備了一種含吸濕鹽的熱響應水凝膠複合材料。該材料具有優異的吸水性能，其潤濕性隨溫度變化而改變，並在 32°C 左右表現出可逆的親水/疏水潤濕性轉變。這一特性使其有可能通過低溫熱能驅動基於液態水釋放的再生過程，同時實現水回收。我們相信，這類新型除濕材料（THC）將為除濕領域開啟新的篇章。因此，本項目旨在開發一種基於 THC 的新型焓交換器，用於建築中的空氣除濕與水回收。首先，項目將建立多物理場模型，從微觀/介觀尺度研究 THC 的水分吸附動力學及其親水—疏水轉變機制。基於所獲得的機理認識，將進一步開發具有可編程吸附—解吸性能以及可調控親水—疏水轉變溫度的 THC 材料，以提升其對不同工況的適應性。 隨後，項目將製備塗覆有上述 THC 材料的焓交換器，並對其除濕性能以及結合水回收的再生性能進行測試。同時，將建立傳熱傳質模型，用於預測原型裝置性能並指導設計優化。最後，項目將開發基於 THC 的水分捕集系統，並從能源效率、經濟可行性、環境影響、耐久性及氣候適應性等方面對其進行全面評估，從而展示其在實際建築應用中的實用價值。 我們相信，該熱響應水凝膠複合材料及其模組化結構將為解決高能耗空氣除濕和淡水短缺問題提供新的思路，並有助於促進能源—水—空氣之間的協同發展。

15227726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15227726.value: 透過動態知識的自適應RAG增強大型語言推薦：模型、效率脆弱性與防禦策略

15227726.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15227726.value: Prof Li, Qing Dr Yin, Dawei

15227726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15227726.value: Recently, there has been growing interest in leveraging large language models to advance next-generation recommender systems (LLMRec). Despite their impressive capabilities, LLMRec faces inherent limitations, particularly hallucinations and a lack of up-to-date, high-quality domain-specific knowledge. These challenges are further exacerbated by the dynamic nature of the web, where user preferences, trending items, and product information evolve continuously, making it difficult for static models to provide accurate and personalized recommendations. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) techniques have shown promise in addressing these issues by integrating external knowledge sources, especially dynamic web knowledge, into the recommendation process. This project aims to explore new frontiers in recommender systems by developing Wrag-LLMRec, a novel web-based RAG framework for LLMRec that leverages dynamic web knowledge to enhance personalized recommendations. Specifically, we introduce a Message Passing-enhanced Attention Head to effectively model long-distance dependencies in noisy web content, enabling timely and context-aware suggestions. To facilitate adaptive retrieval and capture rich relationships among knowledge entities, we design a Mixture-of-Expert RAG framework that intelligently routes user queries to specialized retrieval experts over a web-based knowledge graph. Additionally, to address complex reasoning, we propose a multi-agent reinforcement learning approach that decomposes the recommendation process into collaborative sub-tasks, where three specialized agents (i.e., Selective Retrieval Agent, Knowledge Preference Alignment Agent, and Reasoning-enhanced Recommendation Agent) are jointly optimized within a unified framework, effectively bridging the semantic gap between structured knowledge and natural language understanding. Moreover, the safety vulnerabilities of RAG-enhanced LLMRec--especially efficiency attacks that cause excessive computational consumption without impacting output accuracy--remain largely under-explored. For example, malicious attackers could plant carefully crafted adversarial web content on social media that triggers significant GPU consumption without altering correctness, allowing them to remain stealthy. Thus, we aim to timely investigate the efficiency vulnerabilities of LLMRec. Specifically, we introduce a resource exhaustion attack framework that crafts and injects malicious documents to compel the victim system into excessive, yet stealthy, computational expenditure. Building on insights gained from these attacks, we will investigate countermeasure strategies to enhance the recommendation's robustness. Specifically, we propose a novel detection-based defense framework, where an asymmetric contrastive entropy training objective and a kernel density scoring mechanism are developed to effectively distinguish poisoned from benign retrieved documents in RAG-enhanced LLMRec. Finally, experimental prototype systems will be developed to manifest our frameworks, and extensive testing will be conducted using real-world data to evaluate the effectiveness of our research in industry settings. 近年來，利用大型語言模型推進推薦系統（LLMRec）漸受關注，但其固有侷限（如幻覺、缺乏即時領域知識）因網路動態性而加劇。為此，本專案提出 Wrag-LLMRec，一個基於網路的 RAG 框架，透過動態網路知識增強個人化推薦。我們引入訊息傳遞增強注意力頭以處理嘈雜網路內容的長程依賴；設計專家混合 RAG 框架，將查詢智慧路由至知識圖譜上的專門檢索專家；並提出多重代理人強化學習，以三個協作代理人（選擇性檢索、知識偏好對齊、推理增強推薦）分解推薦任務，橋接結構化知識與自然語言理解。 同時，我們關注 RAG 增強型 LLMRec 的安全性漏洞，尤其是效率攻擊——攻擊者可投放惡意網路內容，誘發大量 GPU 消耗且不影響輸出正確性，難以察覺。為此，我們提出資源耗盡攻擊框架，並基於攻擊洞察發展防禦策略，進一步設計基於偵測的防禦框架，結合非對稱對比熵訓練與核密度評分機制，有效區分惡意與良性檢索文件。最終將開發原型系統，並以真實數據驗證其在產業環境中的有效性。

15227826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15227826.value: 自動駕駛中的開放詞彙三维目標定位

15227826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15227826.value: Reliable 3D grounding is fundamental to autonomous driving, allowing vehicles to recognize, localize and reason about objects in complex, dynamic environments based on human queries. However, current 3D perception systems are constrained by closed-set recognition and limited generalization, struggling to identify rare or unseen objects such as road debris, unique vehicles, or animals. Meanwhile, Vision-Language Models (VLMs) demonstrate strong open-vocabulary recognition in 2D through natural language supervision but still are limited in localizing and reason about their spatial relationships in a 3D context. This mismatch between flexible 2D recognition and rigid 3D grounding hinders their adaptability to real-world autonomous systems. This project aims to bridge this gap by developing an open-vocabulary 3D grounding system capable of flexible semantic understanding, accurate geometric localization, and robust spatial reasoning for autonomous driving in open-world scenarios. In this project, we will pursue three key objectives: (1) Develop a scalable auto-labeling pipeline that transforms 2D predictions from visual foundation models, such as Grounding DINO and the Segment Anything Model (SAM), into reliable 3D bounding boxes. This approach eliminates the need for exhaustive manual labeling and supports recognition of arbitrary object categories. To address unstable training from long-tail distribution of rare and novel objects, we will design occlusion-aware data augmentation techniques to balance the open categories. (2) Develop a multimodal BEV encoder that fuses point cloud and multi-view image features. To address spatial ambiguity in multi-view images, we introduce an Egocentric Position Embedding (EgoPE) that aligns them within a unified ego coordinate system. The encoder is further enhanced through a spatially grounded vision-language pretraining framework, enabling it to locally encode fine-grained, open-vocabulary semantics; accurately understand the underlying spatial relationships and scales of objects; and support downstream 3D grounding tasks. (3) Develop a unified multimodal language model for joint 3D localization and reasoning guided by language instructions. In addition, we will curate driving data and establish a benchmark to evaluate open-vocabulary 3D grounding capabilities of the proposed model. This project will develop an open-vocabulary 3D grounding framework for autonomous driving, capable of recognizing arbitrary objects, localizing and reasoning about their spatial information in open-world scenarios. The proposed multimodal language model will unify visual, spatial, and linguistic cues for robust BEV understanding, enhancing system's safety and adaptability. The automated annotation pipeline and standardized benchmark will further reduce labeling costs and promote reproducible progress in open-world 3D perception. 可靠的 三維目標定位是自動駕駛的基礎，它允許車輛根據人類的查詢，在複雜、動態的環境中識別、定位並推理物體。然而，當前的三維感知系統受限於閉集識別和有限的泛化能力，難以識別道路碎片、特殊車輛或動物等罕見或未見過的物體。與此同時，視覺語言模型通過自然語言監督在二維領域展現出強大的開放詞彙識別能力，但在三維語境中定位物體並推理其空間關係方面仍然存在局限。這種靈活的二維識別與刻板的三維目標定位之間的不匹配，阻礙了它們在真實世界自動駕駛系統中的適應能力。本項目旨在通過開發一種開放詞彙三維目標定位系統來縮小這一差距，該系統能夠在開放世界場景下具備靈活的語義理解、準確的幾何定位以及魯棒的空間推理能力。在本項目中，我們將追求三個關鍵目標：開發一個可擴展的自動標註管線，將來自 Grounding DINO 和 Segment Anything Model等視覺基座模型的二維預測結果轉化為可靠的三維邊界框。該方法消除了對詳盡人工標註的依賴，並支持對任意物體類別的識別。為了解決罕見和新穎物體之長尾分佈導致的訓練不穩定問題，我們將設計遮擋感知的語義數據增強技術來平衡開放類別。開發一個融合點雲和多視角圖像特徵的多模態鳥瞰圖編碼器。為了解決多視角圖像中的空間模糊性，我們引入了一種自車位置嵌入EgoPE，將它們對齊在統一的自車座標系中。通過空間落地的視覺語言預訓練框架，該編碼器得到進一步增強，使其能夠在地化編碼細粒度的開放詞彙語義，準確理解物體的底層空間關係以及比例大小，並支持下游的三維目標定位任務。開發一個統一的多模態語言模型，在語言指令的引導下，實現三維定位與推理的聯合處理。此外，我們將構建駕駛數據集並建立基準標準，以評估該模型在開放詞彙三維目標定位方面的能力。本項目將開發一個用於自動駕駛的開放詞彙三維目標定位框架，該框架能夠在開放世界場景下識別任意物體、對其空間信息進行定位並開展推理。所提出的多模態語言模型將統一視覺、空間和語言線索，以實現魯棒的鳥瞰圖理解，從而增強系統的安全性和適應性。自動標註管線和標準化的基準數據集將進一步降低標註成本，並促進開放世界三維感知領域的可複現性進展。

15228626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15228626.value: 統一多模態世界模型：幾何一致的3D表徵、融合物理的預測與前瞻規劃

15228626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15228626.value: Humans can effortlessly learn mental representations from multiple sensory modalities, such as visual inputs and language descriptions, to comprehend the 3D world, anticipate future changes, and make reasonable actions accordingly to achieve specific goals. Endowing machines with these capabilities - reconstruction, forecasting, and planning - is essential for applications in robotics, healthcare, environmental surveying and monitoring. However, current methods often tackle these challenges in isolation, relying on training task-specific neural networks, which leads to sub-optimal solutions. This project aims to develop a unified algorithmic framework that bridges reconstruction, prediction, and planning, leveraging multiple sensory modalities as input. The research will focus on three core objectives: 1) achieving 3D geometry reconstruction with both spatial and temporal consistency; 2) forecasting 4D dynamics by integrating physical laws; and 3) enabling foresight planning in complex environments for embodied agents. Despite notable progress in existing methods, significant challenges remain, particularly in constructing geometrically consistent and physically compliant world representations, and in learning future-aware action policies grounded in these representations. To address these challenges, we propose several key innovations. First, we will learn a novel ray-based 3D surface distance field from video frames with other modalities. Compatible with prevailing point-based representations such as 3D Gaussians and point maps, our ray-based method will ensure that the reconstructed geometry is both spatially consistent across multiple views and temporally consistent across different time stamps. Second, we will introduce an innovative 3D physics learning technique. Instead of relying on costly human labels or slow physics simulations, our method will directly learn latent codes of physical dynamics from visual observations with audio signals and texts, thus allowing accurate physics-integrated future predictions. Third, we will pioneer a foresight planning approach that harnesses our learned world representations with other modalities such as texts and past actions to guide future actions, rather than relying solely on historical sensory data typically adopted in existing methods. Overall, this project aims to advance 3D world modeling and planning by offering a unified and more effective solution. Preliminary results are highly promising, demonstrating the feasibility of this approach. Importantly, our learned multimodal world models will serve as a foundation for various downstream applications. This work has the potential to significantly impact emerging fields, including robotics, autonomous vehicles, and urban intelligence. 人類能夠毫不費力地從多種感官模態（如視覺輸入與語言描述）中學習心智表徵，藉此理解3D世界、預測未來變化，並據此採取合理的行動以達成特定目標。賦予機器這些能力，重建、預測與規劃，對於機器人技術、醫療保健、環境測量與監控等應用至關重要。然而，現有方法通常孤立地解決這些挑戰，依賴訓練針對特定任務的神經網絡，從而導致次優的解決方案。 本計畫旨在開發一個統一的演算法框架，以多種感官模態為輸入，將重建、預測與規劃串聯起來。本研究將聚焦於三個核心目標：1）實現具備空間與時間一致性的3D幾何重建；2）藉由融合物理定律來預測4D動態；3）讓具身智能體（embodied agents）能在複雜環境中進行前瞻規劃（foresight planning）。 儘管現有方法已取得顯著進展，但仍面臨重大挑戰，特別是在建構幾何一致且符合物理法則的世界表徵，以及在這些表徵的基礎上學習具備未來意識（future-aware）的行動策略方面。為應對這些挑戰，我們提出了幾項關鍵創新： 首先，我們將從視訊影格及其他模態中，學習一種新穎的、基於射線（ray-based）的3D表面距離場。與現行基於點的表徵（如3D高斯和點圖）相容，我們基於射線的方法將確保重建的幾何結構在多個視角上具備空間一致性，且在不同時間戳記上具備時間一致性。 其次，我們將引入一項創新的3D物理學習技術。我們的方法不依賴昂貴的人工標記或緩慢的物理模擬，而是直接從視覺觀察、音訊訊號與文本中學習物理動態的潛在編碼（latent codes），從而實現精確且融合物理的未來預測。 第三，我們將開創一種前瞻規劃方法，利用我們學到的世界表徵與文本、過去行動等其他模態來引導未來行動，而非僅依賴現有方法通常採用的歷史感測數據。 總體而言，本計畫旨在透過提供一個統一且更有效的解決方案，推進3D世界建模與規劃的發展。初步結果極具前景，證明了此方法的可行性。重要的是，我們學到的多模態世界模型將可作為各種下游應用的基礎。這項工作有潛力對機器人技術、自動駕駛車輛與城市智能等新興領域產生深遠的影響。

15229126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15229126.value: 機械智能賦能動態自適應的先進高性能廣義並聯機器人研製

15229126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15229126.value: With the rapid advancement of intelligent manufacturing, aerospace, and precision robotics, industrial requirements for robotic systems have shifted from a primary focus on “high precision” to an increasing emphasis on “high adaptability”. Parallel manipulators, renowned for their high stiffness, accuracy, and high load capabilities, have found widespread application in flight simulators, machining centers, and medical robotics. However, Conventional Parallel Manipulators (CPMs) face several significant limitations: (1) small workspace due to rigid platform structures; (2) Singularity issues caused by kinematic dependencies; (3) Inconsistent stiffness under varying loads; and (4) limited adaptability to dynamic environments or unforeseen tasks. Addressing these challenges necessitates innovative design and advanced control strategies, enabling CPMs to effectively fulfill the evolving demands of adaptive automation in modern industrial environments. This research project is to overcome the limitations of CPMs by developing innovative design methodologies and advanced control technologies for next-generation systems---Generalized Parallel Manipulators (GPMs). GPMs represent a significant advancement over CPMs, and this project will focus on four key areas: (1) developing GPMs with configurable platforms to enhance task adaptability; (2) integrating coupling sub-chains to improve global stiffness; (3) designing articulated moving platforms to expand the workspace; and (4) incorporating mechanical intelligence for dynamic adaptation. By systematically addressing the core limitations of CPMs, GPMs have the potential to revolutionize manufacturing applications. This project aims to establish a comprehensive design and control framework for GPMs, empowering them to execute complex, high-precision, and adaptive tasks in dynamic industrial environments. Ultimately, GPMs are poised for deployment in high-precision assembly, rapid product handling, milling, surface finishing, and a wide range of other industrial applications. This research project will contribute significantly to new design methodologies and control technologies for next-generation high-performance GPMs for manufacturing applications such as high-precision assembly, rapid product handling, milling, and surface finishing. Additionally, it will have applications in other industries. This proposed research promises to make substantial contributions to GPMs design and practical applications across contemporary technical sectors, notably augmenting China's manufacturing economy. By enhancing performance, efficiency, quality, and flexibility while simultaneously reducing costs and lead times for robotic manufacturing systems, this research has the potential to revolutionize advanced manufacturing, particularly in the semiconductor, automotive, aerospace, medical device, and biomedical microsystem industries. 隨著智能製造、航空航天和精密機器人技術的快速發展，工業界對機器人系統的需求已從主要關注“高精度”轉向日益重視“高適應性”。並聯機器人以其高剛度、高精度和高承載能力而著稱，已廣泛應用於飛行模擬器、加工中心和醫療機器人等領域。然而，傳統並聯機器人（CPMs）仍面臨若干顯著局限：（1）剛性平台結構導致工作空間較小；（2）運動學約束導致奇異位形問題；（3）不同負載條件下的剛度不一致；（4）對動態環境或未預見任務的適應能力有限。解決這些問題需要創新設計方法和先進控制策略，使傳統並聯機器人能夠有效滿足現代工業環境中自適應自動化不斷發展的需求。 本項目旨在通過為下一代系統——廣義並聯機器人（GPMs）開發創新設計方法和先進控制技術，克服傳統並聯機器人的局限。廣義並聯機器人代表了相對於傳統並聯機器人的一項顯著進步。本項目將重點研究四個方面：（1）開發具有可重構平台的廣義並聯機器人，以提高任務適應性；（2）集成耦合子鏈，以提高全局剛度；（3）設計鉸接動平台，以擴大工作空間；（4）融入機械智能，以實現動態自適應。通過系統解決傳統並聯機器人的核心局限，廣義並聯機器人有望革新製造業應用。本項目旨在建立一套完整的廣義並聯機器人設計與控制框架，使其能夠在動態工業環境中執行複雜、高精度和自適應任務。最終，廣義並聯機器人有望部署於高精度裝配、產品快速搬運、銑削、表面精加工以及其他廣泛的工業應用中。 本項目將為下一代高性能廣義並聯機器人的新設計方法和控制技術作出重要貢獻。相關成果可用於高精度裝配、產品快速搬運、銑削和表面精加工等製造應用，並可進一步應用於其他行業。擬開展的研究有望為廣義並聯機器人的設計及其在現代技術領域中的實際應用作出重大貢獻，並顯著促進中國製造業經濟發展。通過提高機器人製造系統的性能、效率、質量和柔性，同時降低成本並縮短交付週期，本研究具有革新先進製造業的潛力，尤其是在半導體、汽車、航空航天、醫療器械和生物醫學微系統等行業。

15229326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15229326.value: 用於肩袖修復的多尺度雙相肌肉—肌腱移植物

15229326.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15229326.value: Prof Ling, Samuel Ka-kin Prof Mao, Chuanbin Prof WANG, Huating

15229326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15229326.value: Severe muscle-tendon injuries such as large-to-massive rotator cuff tears are common with poor recovery[1]. Although state-of-the-art treatments exist, prior advances have focused on the bone-tendon junction. This has left the muscle-tendon unit, which powers shoulder function, largely overlooked. Within this context, key unaddressed challenges include high tendon re-tear rates and inadequate muscle-tendon regeneration along with excessive levels of intramuscular fat[2]. Indeed, rotator cuff tears with significant muscle-tendon retraction and fatty tissue are clinically ‘irreparable’. Attaining stable biomechanical repair and biological healing of the muscle-tendon unit will restore shoulder movement and minimize reinjury[3,4]. Therefore, we propose a coordinated strategy that biomechanically and biologically restores the muscle-tendon unit. This strategy is conceptually innovative and vital to functional joint recovery. Specifically, we will develop a biphasic muscle-tendon graft that is adequately strong to biomechanically support muscle-tendon forces and contains a pro-regenerative cocktail to biologically combat multi-tissue loss and intramuscular fat. An advanced multi-scale drug delivery system will target the muscle and tendon compartments to deliver the pro-regenerative cocktail, comprised of polyhedrin (PH)-encapsulated FGF-2 and IGF-1, and black phosphorous-polydopamine (BP-PD) nanosheets bound with TGF-β agonist (FITag). FITag cocktail is inexpensive and up to 8,400× cheaper than equivalent counterparts. This work leverages on our well-established expertise with musculoskeletal spatial patterning (Advanced Functional Materials,2018[5]; Biomaterials,2011a[6]; Biomaterials,2011b[7]), tendon-promoting growth factor cocktails (Biomaterials Advances,2023[8]), and mechanically strong biomaterials (Bioactive Materials,2024[9]. Aim 1 will develop in vitro pathophysiological models mimicking muscle fatty degeneration to systematically assess FITag cocktail’s efficacy and study its mechanism-of-action, and develop a strong and biopatterned multi-tissue graft for muscle-tendon healing. Pilot studies indicate that a combination of FGF-2, IGF-1, and TGF-β3 (FIT) signaling promoted tendon and muscle differentiation, enhanced adipocyte apoptosis and transdifferentiation while compartment-specific delivery of FITag was demonstrated ex vivo and in vivo. Aim 2 will assess the efficacy of FITag muscle-tendon graft in vivo via our chronic-like rabbit rotator cuff injury model (JOVE,2023[10]) for biomechanical restoration (tendon tensile attributes and muscle force generation) and biological healing (histology and spatial RNA-seq). Pilot studies with FIT or FI-FITag demonstrated up to ~65% or ~3-fold higher muscle force production relative to no cocktail treatment, increased muscle-tendon tissue healing, and reduced fatty degeneration. Successful completion will establish a new multi-tissue muscle-tendon paradigm for cost-effective treatment of large-to-massive rotator cuff injuries. This work has broad applications for regenerating musculoskeletal and non-musculoskeletal tissues with fatty degeneration (e.g., heart and liver). 嚴重的肌肉—肌腱損傷，例如大型至巨大型肩袖撕裂，十分常見且復原效果不佳[1]。儘管目前已有最先進的治療方法，過往研究進展主要集中於骨—肌腱交界處，因而使驅動肩關節功能的肌肉—肌腱單元在很大程度上被忽略。在此背景下，尚未解決的關鍵挑戰包括肌腱再撕裂率高、肌肉—肌腱再生不足，以及肌肉內脂肪含量過高[2]。事實上，伴隨顯著肌肉—肌腱回縮及脂肪組織浸潤的肩袖撕裂，在臨床上被視為「不可修復」。實現肌肉—肌腱單元穩定的生物力學修復與生物性癒合，將有助於恢復肩關節活動並最大限度降低再次受傷風險[3,4]。因此，我們提出一項協同策略，從生物力學與生物學兩方面恢復肌肉—肌腱單元。此策略在概念上具創新性，且對關節功能恢復至關重要。 具體而言，我們將開發一種雙相肌肉—肌腱移植物，其具備足夠強度，可在生物力學上支撐肌肉—肌腱受力，並含有促再生雞尾酒配方，以在生物學上對抗多組織缺損及肌肉內脂肪堆積。一套先進的多尺度藥物遞送系統將靶向肌肉與肌腱區室，遞送促再生雞尾酒配方；該配方由多角體蛋白（polyhedrin, PH）包封的 FGF-2 與 IGF-1，以及結合 TGF-β 激動劑（FITag）的黑磷—聚多巴胺（black phosphorous-polydopamine, BP-PD）奈米片組成。FITag 雞尾酒配方成本低廉，較同等替代方案最高可便宜 8,400 倍。本研究將借助我們在肌肉骨骼空間圖案化（Advanced Functional Materials, 2018[5]；Biomaterials, 2011a[6]；Biomaterials, 2011b[7]）、促肌腱生長因子雞尾酒配方（Biomaterials Advances, 2023[8]）以及高機械強度生物材料（Bioactive Materials, 2024[9]）方面已建立的專業基礎。 目標 1 將建立模擬肌肉脂肪變性的體外病理生理模型，以系統性評估 FITag 雞尾酒配方的療效並研究其作用機制，同時開發一種具高強度且具生物圖案化特徵的多組織移植物，用於肌肉—肌腱癒合。初步研究顯示，FGF-2、IGF-1 與 TGF-β3（FIT）訊號的組合可促進肌腱與肌肉分化，增強脂肪細胞凋亡與轉分化；同時，FITag 的區室特異性遞送已在離體與體內實驗中獲得證實。目標 2 將利用我們建立的慢性樣兔肩袖損傷模型（JOVE, 2023[10]），在體內評估 FITag 肌肉—肌腱移植物在生物力學恢復（肌腱拉伸特性與肌肉力量產生）及生物性癒合（組織學與空間 RNA-seq）方面的療效。採用 FIT 或 FI-FITag 的初步研究顯示，與未接受雞尾酒配方處理相比，肌肉力量產生最高提高約 65% 或約 3 倍，肌肉—肌腱組織癒合增加，且脂肪變性減少。 本研究若成功完成，將建立一種新的多組織肌肉—肌腱治療範式，用於具成本效益地治療大型至巨大型肩袖損傷。此研究亦具有廣泛應用潛力，可用於再生伴隨脂肪變性的肌肉骨骼及非肌肉骨骼組織（例如心臟與肝臟）。

15230026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15230026.value: 用於深腦成像且具細胞級解析度的超快光纖整合型顯微鏡

15230026.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15230026.value: Dr LAI, Cora Sau Wan Prof Qu, Junle

15230026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15230026.value: The rising global prevalence of neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's, underscores an urgent need to decipher the fundamental mechanisms of neural circuit function deep within the brain. A critical barrier to this goal is the limitations of current neuroimaging technologies. None can simultaneously achieve the essential combination of minimal invasiveness, deep penetration (>2 mm), cellular spatial resolution, and millisecond temporal resolution required to observe rapid neural signaling in their native, deep-brain environments. This gap severely hampers our ability to understand brain function and the circuit-level dysfunctions that underlie neurological disorders. This project proposes a transformative solution via development of a fully validated, next-generation microscope-on-a-fiber. Our strategy is built on a synergistic optical-computational approach designed to overcome existing bottlenecks. In System Engineering (Task 1), we will create an ultrafast fluorescence imaging platform centered on a minimally invasive multimode fiber (~100 μm diameter). The core optical innovation is a wavefront shaping technique that integrates a Digital Micromirror Device (DMD) with a resonant scanner. This design fundamentally bypasses the speed limitation of conventional DMD systems, achieving an unprecedented focal point scanning rate of 17.7 MHz. This enables volumetric imaging at speeds >1 kHz, providing the temporal resolution necessary to capture fast action potentials and synaptic transmissions deep inside the brain. We recognize that such extreme imaging speeds can compromise image quality. Therefore, our Computational Enhancement (Task 2) employs a dedicated deep learning framework, an Attention-Guided Dual-Branch Sampling Neural Network. It is specifically engineered to perform real-time, nonlinear reconstruction of the acquired low-signal images, effectively restoring spatial detail and contrast to produce high-fidelity maps of neural activity without sacrificing the critical temporal resolution. The Biological Validation (Task 3) will prove the system's utility. Through rigorous ex-vivo experiments, we will first correlate the optical signals with simultaneous gold-standard patch-clamp electrophysiology, providing quantitative verification of the >1 kHz temporal fidelity. Subsequently, in-vivo experiments in mouse models will demonstrate the system's practical capability to monitor real-time functional dynamics in deep neuronal populations at a penetration depth >2 mm. Upon successful completion, this project will deliver a groundbreaking and essential tool to the global community. It will establish a new benchmark for minimally invasive, high-speed neuroimaging, opening new frontiers for investigating neural coding and disease progression. By providing unparalleled access to deep-brain dynamics, this technology will accelerate the identification of novel therapeutic targets and pave the way for groundbreaking treatments for complex neurological disorders. 全球神經退化性疾病（如阿茲海默症與帕金森氏症）日益盛行之趨勢，凸顯了亟需解構深層腦部神經迴路功能之基本機制的迫切性。然而，當前神經影像技術存在重大瓶頸，構成了達成此目標的關鍵障礙。現有技術中，無一能同時兼具微創、深層穿透（>2 mm）、細胞級空間解析度，以及毫秒級時間解析度——而這些正是於原生深腦環境中觀察快速神經訊號傳遞所必備之條件。此一技術缺口嚴重限制了我們對大腦功能及神經疾病中迴路層級失調之理解。 本計畫提出一項變革性解決方案，即開發一套經過完整驗證的次世代「光纖整合型顯微鏡」。我們的策略奠基於光學與計算協同之創新途徑，旨在突破現有瓶頸。在系統工程（任務一）中，我們將打造一套以微創多模光纖（直徑約100 μm）為核心的超快螢光顯微成像平台。其關鍵光學創新在於一種波前整形技術，該技術整合數位微鏡裝置（DMD）與共振掃描器。此設計從根本突破傳統DMD系統的速度限制，達成史無前例的17.7 MHz焦點掃描速率，從而實現大於1 kHz的體積成像速度，提供捕捉深腦內快速動作電位與突觸傳遞所需的時間解析度。 我們認知到，極高的成像速度可能影響影像品質。因此，在計算增強（任務二）中，我們將採用專屬的深度學習架構——注意力引導雙分支取樣神經網路。該網路專為即時、非線性重建所獲取的低訊號影像而設計，能有效恢復空間細節與對比度，從而在不犧牲關鍵時間解析度的前提下，產出高保真度的神經活動圖譜。 生物驗證（任務三）將證明此系統之實用性。首先，透過嚴謹的離體實驗，我們將光學訊號與同步進行的金標準膜片鉗電生理記錄進行比對，以量化驗證大於1 kHz之時間保真度。隨後，在齧齒動物模型的活體實驗中，我們將展示此系統在穿透深度大於2 mm下，即時監測深層神經族群功能動態之實際能力。 本研究若順利完成，將為全球學術社群提供一項開創性且至關重要的研究工具。它將為微創高速神經影像樹立新標竿，開啟探索神經編碼與疾病進程的新前沿。透過提供前所未有的深腦動態觀測途徑，此技術將加速新穎治療標靶的發掘，並為複雜神經系統疾病之突破性療法鋪路。

15230126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15230126.value: 解構高密度城市中建成環境、可步行性與行人安全之關係：基於多源數據的空間分析

15230126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15230126.value: Hong Kong’s compact urban form, high density, and mixed land use make walking the primary mode of access to work, education, commerce, healthcare, and leisure. Enhancing walkability is crucial for promoting sustainability by reducing car dependency and lowering carbon emissions. However, frequent conflicts between vehicles and pedestrians in urban areas pose significant safety risks, particularly as pedestrians are among the most vulnerable road users. To create a safer and more liveable city, it is essential to identify the environmental, traffic, and human factors influencing pedestrian safety. This research project investigates the roles of the built environment, traffic flow characteristics, and pedestrian perception in shaping pedestrian safety within Hong Kong’s urban context. First, built environment data, including urban planning, road infrastructure, buildings, transport facilities, and landscaping, will be integrated using geographical information systems (GIS). While previous studies have explored the relationship between land use, transport, and pedestrian safety at broad spatial scales, the impact of street-level environments remains underexplored. To address this gap, the project will employ advanced computer vision techniques to analyse street view images, capturing the visual elements of streets as experienced by pedestrians. Second, state-of-the-art data fusion and deep learning methods will be used to estimate both vehicle and pedestrian exposures. Pedestrian volumes at the street level will be assessed using object detection algorithms applied to dashcam video data, while probe vehicle data will provide estimates of network-wide traffic volume and speed. These exposure metrics are critical for understanding the likelihood of pedestrian crashes. Third, the project will examine how personal characteristics, walking experiences, and street environments influence perceived walkability. This will be achieved through transfer learning applied to a crowdsourced dataset of global urban imagery and human-labelled data, accounting for urban design and socio-cultural factors specific to Hong Kong. A hierarchical spatial model, combining deep learning and econometric techniques, will be developed to estimate pedestrian safety levels and the influence of potential factors at both micro and macro scales. This approach addresses challenges such as imbalanced crash data, spatial dependency, and unobserved heterogeneity. Additionally, an agent-based model will be used to evaluate the effectiveness of policy interventions and mass-action plans in improving pedestrian safety. This research will provide actionable insights into how urban form, road infrastructure, street environments, and traffic management can be optimized to enhance walkability and support sustainable transport development in Hong Kong. 香港緊湊的城市形態、高密度的發展以及混合土地利用，使步行成為市民出行、就學、商業活動、醫療和休閒的首要方式。提升可步行性對於減少汽車依賴和降低碳排放以推動可持續發展至關重要。然而，市區中車輛與行人之間頻繁的衝突帶來了顯著的安全隱患，尤其是行人在道路使用者中屬於最脆弱的群體。為了構建一個更安全、更宜居的城市，必須識別影響行人安全的環境、交通及人為因素。本研究項目旨在探討在香港城市背景下，建成環境、交通流特徵以及行人感知對行人安全所起的作用。 首先，本研究將利用地理資訊系統整合包括城市規劃、道路基礎設施、建築物、交通設施和綠化景觀在內的建成環境數據。過往研究雖已在較宏觀的空間尺度上探討了土地利用、交通與行人安全之間的關係，但街道微觀環境的影響仍有待深入研究。為填補這一空白，本項目將採用先進的計算機視覺技術分析街景圖像，以捕捉行人所體驗的街道視覺元素。其次，本研究將應用前沿的數據融合與深度學習方法，估算車輛與行人的暴露量。研究將利用目標檢測算法分析行車記錄儀的視頻數據，以評估街道級別的行人流量；同時，利用探針車數據估算全網的交通量與車速。這些暴露量指標對於理解行人撞車事故的發生概率至關重要。第三，本項目將探討個人特徵、步行體驗和街道環境如何影響感知可步行性。這將通過遷移學習應用於全球城市圖像的眾包數據集和人工標註數據來實現，並充分考慮香港特有的城市設計與社會文化因素。本研究將開發一個結合深度學習與計量經濟學技術的層次空間模型，以評估微觀和宏觀尺度下的行人安全水平及潛在因素的影響。該方法有效解決了撞車數據不平衡、空間相關性以及未觀測異質性等挑戰。此外，本項目亦將利用基於模擬模型，評估政策干預措施和集體行動計劃在改善行人安全方面的成效。本研究將提供具操作性的科學見解，闡明如何優化城市形態、道路基礎設施、街道環境和交通管理，以提升可步行性並支持香港可持續交通的發展。

15230826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15230826.value: 城市交通源PM2.5與噪聲復合暴露：基於小鼠模型的腦–肺–心血管軸研究

15230826.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15230826.value: Prof Kang, Jian Prof Li, Xiang-dong Prof Wexler, Anthony

15230826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15230826.value: This proposed research project addresses critical knowledge gaps in urban environmental health by investigating the cerebro-pulmonary-cardiovascular consequences of co-exposure to traffic-derived PM₂.₅ and noise in Hong Kong—a model subtropical metropolis with over 7.5 million residents, high population density, dense traffic, and pronounced seasonal pollution peaks (PM₂.₅: 10–40 μg/m³ in winter vs. 5–10 μg/m³ in summer). The study will yield transformative insights for global urban policy and preventive health strategies amid rising cross-organ toxicological burdens. By integrating site-specific sampling from high-traffic zones such as the Cross-Harbor Tunnel in Hung Hom (70–85 dB noise; PM₂.₅: 50–100 μg/m³ rich in trace metals and vehicular emissions), we will simulate real-world co-exposure in C57BL/6 murine models to assess the independent, additive, or synergistic effects of PM₂.₅ and noise. The project will bridge large-scale Hong Kong epidemiological observations with controlled acute and subchronic exposures to reveal combined toxicities across the lung–blood–brain axis, ultimately informing integrated co-exposure health risk assessments for Asian megacities and reducing underestimation in current air-quality models. Then, the underlying toxicological and pathological mechanisms affecting health along the cerebro-pulmonary-cardiovascular axis will be investigated systematically. Using biosamples collected from co-exposed mice, we will quantify biomarkers of systemic oxidative stress, cardiopulmonary inflammation, and neuroinflammation, alongside pathological changes in the brain (hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, BBB integrity), lungs, and vascular endothelium. Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses will be applied to identify shared molecular pathways and confirm mechanistic targets across organs. Finally, we will examine vulnerable subgroups with pre-existing metabolic syndromes (e.g., obesity, high BMI) using high-fat diet-induced murine models. Low-cost, practical interventions—such as air filtration and noise reduction—will be evaluated through biomarker and functional endpoints to identify personalized protective strategies for susceptible populations. Building on our team’s expertise in environmental medicine, toxicology, and environmental engineering, this research will establish verifiable multi-organ toxicological pathways and sensitive biomarkers for cross-organ, co-exposure health risks. The outcomes will empower evidence-based interventions, positioning Hong Kong as a leader in preventive environmental health research for rapidly urbanizing regions facing multiple environmental stressors. 研究目標1：評估交通源PM2.5與噪聲複合暴露對小鼠腦–肺–心血管軸的聯合毒性效應 香港等高密度城市居民長期同時暴露於交通源PM2.5與噪音，兩者均與肺部炎症、血管功能障礙及神經炎症相關。隨著人口老化及心血管代謝性疾病增加，相關公共衛生風險日益突出。然而，既往動物研究多聚焦單一暴露，對PM2.5與噪音複合暴露及跨器官效應了解有限。本研究將以 C57BL/6 小鼠為模型，利用新建立的複合暴露系統，結合香港主要道路採集的PM2.5樣本與真實交通噪音（70–85 分貝），系統比較單獨及聯合暴露對腦–肺–心血管軸的毒性效應。 研究目標2：闡明交通源PM2.5與噪聲複合暴露擾亂腦–肺–心血管軸的共同機制 兩類暴露均可誘導全身性炎症與氧化應激，進一步造成血管內皮及血腦屏障功能障礙。PM2.5可由肺部啟動炎症反應並擴展至全身循環；噪音則可激活交感神經及應激反應，放大炎症與氧化通路。基於目標1獲得的組織及生物樣本，本研究將檢測全身性氧化應激、心肺炎症及神經炎症標誌物，評估肺、心臟及腦組織病理改變與 HPA 軸相關反應，並結合轉錄組及蛋白質組分析，識別PM2.5與噪音在炎症、氧化應激、內皮功能障礙及神經血管損傷中的共同分子網絡。 研究目標3：探討既存代謝風險對複合暴露毒性的易感性，並評估實際可行的干預策略 肥胖及代謝綜合徵人群本身存在慢性低度炎症與氧化應激，可能放大PM2.5與噪音的聯合毒性。本研究將建立高脂飲食誘導的肥胖小鼠模型，與健康對照比較跨器官毒性與功能障礙；並依據前述機制結果，評估便攜式空氣淨化及噪音衰減等低成本措施對炎症、內皮功能障礙及神經毒性的緩解效果，為城市高風險人群提供具實證基礎的預防策略。

15230926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15230926.value: 結合現場多方向分佈式光纖聲波感測與實驗室試驗的岩土工程勘察概率框架

15230926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15230926.value: The Hong Kong Government recently announced the “Northern Metropolis Development Strategy”, which involves expansion of existing towns in the northern part of Hong Kong, development of underused areas in their neighbourhood, and enhancing connectivity among these regions and with Chinese Mainland through major infrastructure projects. These strategies are important drivers of development in Hong Kong in the next 15 to 20 years, but there are important geotechnical challenges due to complexities in geologic conditions. In particular, the rock types in these parts of Hong Kong include meta-sedimentary rocks and their weathering products, and there is limited prior knowledge on their properties and variability. Some areas are underlain by marble and limestone, which may dissolve to form underground cavities that jeopardise the stability of structures founded on them. These represent “known unknowns” as the existence of such rocks is well-recognised but their impacts on future developments are not well-understood. Construction in the underdeveloped areas also entails “unknown unknowns”, as information of the subsurface domain is limited in regions with few previous developments. Subsurface imaging by distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) represents a novel and promising approach for efficient and cost-effective site investigation, and is particularly suitable for exploration of large areas that are under-developed. The approach involves fibre-optic sensors laid close to the ground surface or inserted vertically into the ground, enabling estimation of shear wave velocities in the subsurface domain. The existence of underground cavities or boulders, which may jeopardize or obstruct infrastructure developments, can be readily detected without the need of drilling closely-spaced boreholes. However, the current technology suffers from the issue of non-uniqueness in data interpretation process, meaning that multiple solutions of potential underground profiles may lead to the observed DAS measurements. Therefore, this study proposes DAS measurements in multiple directions, utilizing both surface wave analysis and crosshole travel-time tomography techniques to provide additional sources of information in the data analysis. Moreover, these can be combined with traditional geotechnical investigation measures such as borehole drilling, soil and rock sampling and laboratory testing, with the difference data types integrated through a Bayesian framework to rationally quantify the uncertainty and spatial variability in the ground profiles. As this framework aims to overcome geotechnical challenges of the Northern Metropolis, the infrastructure works also present opportunities to validate and refine this tool, contributing to the construction of smart cities in other parts of the world. 香港特區政府近期公佈了《北部都會區發展策略》，內容涵蓋擴建香港北部現有新市鎮、開發週邊未充分利用的土地，以及透過大型基建項目加強這些區域內部及與中國大陸的互聯互通。這些策略是香港未來15至20年發展的重要動力，但複雜的地質條件也帶來了嚴峻的岩土工程挑戰。具體而言，該區域的岩石類型包括變質沉積岩及其風化產物，而工程業界對這些岩石的特性及變異性的了解相對有限。另外, 部分區域的基岩為大理岩和石灰岩，這些岩石可能發生溶蝕形成地下空洞，危及建於其上的結構物的穩定性。這類情況屬於「已知的未知」— 即雖已知此類岩石的存在，但對其對未來發展帶來的影響尚缺乏充分了解。此外，在開發程度較低的區域進行建設也涉及「未知的未知」，因為這些地區過往開發活動較少，關於地下地質狀況的資料也十分有限。 利用分佈式光纖聲學感測（DAS）技術進行地下成像，是一種高效且經濟的場地勘察新方法，尤其適用於大面積未開發區域的勘探。此方法透過在地表附近鋪設或垂直埋入光纖感測器，實現對地下剪切波波速的估算。無需進行高密度鑽孔，即可探測到可能危及或阻礙基礎設施建設的地下空洞或孤石。然而，目前技術在資料解譯過程中存在非唯一性問題，即多種可能的地下剖面形態均可能產生相同的DAS觀測結果。因此，本研究提出採用多方向DAS測量，結合面波分析與跨孔走時層析成像技術，為資料分析提供更多維度的資訊。此外，此方法可與鑽孔、土石取樣及室內試驗等傳統岩土勘察手段結合，並透過貝葉斯框架整合各類數據，從而合理量化地下剖面的不確定性與空間變異性。鑑於該框架旨在應對「北部都會區」建設中的岩土工程挑戰，相關的基礎設施工程也為驗證和完善這項技術提供了契機，進而助力全球其他地區的智慧城市建設。

15231026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15231026.value: 深海採礦軟黏土力學行為的機制驅動建模：一種創新的實驗與數值整合方法

15231026.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15231026.value: Prof CHEN, Qiushi Prof CHEN, Xu-Guang

15231026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15231026.value: The deep-sea harbors vast deposits of minerals, energy, and biological resources typically hosted in clayey sediment layers, making their development a strategic priority for global progress. This has driven the emergence of deep-sea mining. However, the safety and stability of mining operations depend critically on the vehicle-seabed interaction, as the mobility stability of a mining vehicle on the soft seabed is directly governed by the bearing capacity of the underlying soil layer. Inadequate bearing capacity can lead to equipment subsidence, overturning, or even larger failures. Consequently, accurately assessing the mechanical properties of deep-sea shallow soft soils is an essential requirement for ensuring the safety and reliability of deep-sea mining. Current research primarily relies on conventional soil mechanics, which has limited applicability under the deep sea's ultra-high hydrostatic pressure. This pressure significantly alters the soil's microstructure and hydromechanical properties, causing mechanical responses with time and cyclic effects subjected to vehicle operation-induced loadings. However, understanding these complex processes and their engineering impacts remains limited. This project aims to establish a comprehensive experimental and computational framework, progressing from the development of cutting-edge laboratory instrumentation to sophisticated multiscale modeling and practical engineering applications, to achieve a deep understanding of soft clay behavior under the ultra-high hydrostatic pressures in the deep sea. A novel ultra-high-pressure triaxial system will probe the effect of ultra-high hydrostatic pressure on both time-dependent monotonic and frequency-dependent cyclic behaviors with microstructural evolutions of soft clay. Concurrently, an MD-DEM-CFD (Molecular Dynamics - Discrete Element Method - Computational Fluid Dynamics) based upscaling numerical approach will be developed to elucidate fundamental mechanisms of ultra-high hydrostatic pressure and establish quantitative fabric evolution rules. These insights will inform a novel multiscale constitutive model that unifies broad pressure ranges, implemented within a new large-deformation numerical framework for realistic soil-structure interaction simulations under complex conditions. The framework will undergo rigorous validation via innovative mini-CPT (Cone Penetration Test) model tests and prototype tests of vehicle-seabed interactions for practical deployment. This project will be the first systematic effort to bridge high-fidelity experimentation under deep-sea pressure with multiscale computational modeling for the deep-sea shallow soft seabed. It will offer not only a series of valuable experimental data, but also an advanced numerical framework. The established integrated multiscale framework is expected to enable more accurate and efficient simulations of deep-sea geotechnical systems, contributing to innovations in design methodologies and safeguarding the sustainable development of ocean resources in Hong Kong and beyond. 深海黏土質沉積層中蘊藏豐富的礦產、能源和生物資源。實現這些資源的開發已成為全球發展的策略重點。這項需求推動了深海採礦技術的興起。然而，採礦作業的安全性與穩定性在很大程度上取決於採礦車與海床的相互作用——採礦車在鬆軟海床上的穩定性直接受控於下伏土層的承載力。承載力不足可能導致設備沉陷、傾覆甚至更大規模的破壞。因此，準確評估深海淺層軟土的力學特性，是確保深海採礦安全可靠的必要前提。 現有研究主要依賴傳統土力學理論，但在深海超高靜水壓力環境下的適用性十分有限。此壓力顯著改變土的微觀結構及水力-力學性質，使土體在採礦車作業荷載下呈現複雜的時效與循環力學響應。然而，目前對這些複雜過程及其工程影響的理解仍十分有限。 本計畫旨在建構一個集前沿試驗裝備研發、精細多尺度建模與工程應用於一體的綜合研究框架，以深入理解深海超高靜水壓力下軟黏土的力學行為。本計畫將發展新型超高壓三軸試驗系統，以探討超高靜水壓力對軟黏土時間相關單調特性、頻率相關循環特性及其微觀結構演化的影響。同時，將發展基於MD‑DEM‑CFD（分子動力學-離散元法-計算流體動力學）的升尺度數值方法，揭示超高靜水壓力的作用機制，並建立定量的組構演化法則。在此基礎上，建構適用於常壓至超高壓範圍的新型多尺度本構模型，並將其嵌入新開發的大變形數值框架中，以模擬複雜條件下真實的土-結構相互作用。最後，透過創新的微型靜力觸探（mini‑CPT）模型試驗及採礦車-海床交互作用原型試驗，對上述框架進行嚴格驗證，為其實際工程部署提供可靠依據。 本計畫首次將深海高壓環境下的高保真試驗與多尺度數值模擬結合，針對深海淺層軟海床進行系統性研究。研究成果不僅將產出一系列寶貴的試驗數據，還將建構先進的數值計算架構。此綜合多尺度架構可望實現對深海岩土工程系統更精確、高效的模擬，進而推動設計方法的創新，並為香港及更廣泛區域的海洋資源永續發展提供科學支撐。

15231926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15231926.value: 基於通用第一性原理原子力場的極端燃燒真實流體效應量子與人工智能協同解密

15231926.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15231926.value: Prof Curran, Henry Prof ZHANG, Xiaoge

15231926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15231926.value: This project aims to overcome the fundamental scientific and technological barriers in characterizing and understanding real-fluid behaviors in extreme-pressure combustion, and to construct, validate, and deliver a transformative quantum-AI-enabled framework that redefines high-pressure combustion research. Precise characterization of real-fluid phenomena under high- to extreme-pressures is critical for designing next-generation propulsion and energy systems. However, this remains a formidable challenge due to the complex and intensified interactions between multiple molecules and reactive radicals that occur under such conditions. Existing approaches heavily rely on empirical equations of state and property correlations, which are limited in accuracy and species coverage, lack generalizability to large and non-spherical molecules, and fail to capture the intricate physics governing real-fluid phenomena. Direct quantum mechanics calculations, while rigorous, are computationally prohibitive for complex species, which are commonly seen for combustion applications. To address these challenges, this project unites leading experts in quantum chemistry, AI, combustion modeling, and extreme-pressure experimental diagnostics to pioneer a synergistic quantum-AI methodology. The core innovation is the development of a universal ab initio-based atomic force field, augmented by machine learning (ML), to rapidly and accurately determine intermolecular potentials and high-order Virial coefficients for a wide range of species, including large hydrocarbons and radicals where existing methods fall short. This enables dynamic reconstruction of real-fluid thermodynamic and transport properties, which will be integrated into a comprehensive modeling framework within OpenFOAM for high-fidelity real-fluid combustion simulations. Key project tasks and innovations include: (1) Establishing a generalized quantum-AI workflow for atomic force field and real-fluid property determination, achieving computational acceleration by orders of magnitude; (2) Implementing and validating a novel high-dimensional combustion modeling framework in OpenFOAM with ML-driven dynamic property correction; (3) Conducting new combustion experiments at unprecedented high- to extreme-pressure conditions to reveal qualitative and quantitative trends in real-fluid effects across diverse fuels and diluents with different molecular structure and properties; (4) Rigorously validating the developed framework against both new and existing experimental data, quantifying for the first time the individual impacts of multi-body and radical interactions, and benchmarking against conventional methods; and (5) Delivering a standardized methodology and toolset that overcomes current limitations. By breaking through bottlenecks in real-fluid characterization, this project will set a new benchmark with unprecedented accuracy, efficiency, and applicability in characterizing real-fluid phenomena, not only for high-pressure combustion research, but also for broader applications such as advanced waste treatment, chromatographic analysis, biomass processing, and planetary atmospheric studies. 本項目旨在克服極限壓力燃燒中表徵與理解真實流體行為的底層科學與技術屏障，構建並驗證一套具有變革性的量子-人工智能融合框架。在高壓至極限壓力下進行精準表徵，是設計下一代推進與能源系統的關鍵；然而，由於此類工況下多分子與活性自由基之間存在複雜且劇烈的相互作用，這依然是一項極具挑戰性的課題。現有方法高度依賴經驗狀態方程和物性關聯式，在準確度與組分覆蓋率上受到限制，且無法捕捉主導真實流體現象的複雜底層物理。直接進行量子力學計算雖然嚴謹，但對於燃燒應用中常見的複雜組分而言，其計算運算量高昂得難以承受。 為了應對這些挑戰，本項目匯聚了量子化學、人工智能、燃燒建模以及極限壓力實驗診斷領域的頂尖專家，率先開創了一套「量子-人工智能」協同方法學。其核心創新在於開發一套基於初算（ab initio）的通用原子勢場，並藉由機器學習進行增強，從而快速且精準地確定廣泛組分的分子間勢能與高階維里係數，其中包括現有方法無法處理的大型烴類與自由基。這實現了真實流體熱力學和輸運性質的動態重構，並將其整合至 OpenFOAM 內的一體化建模框架中，用於高保真度的真實流體燃燒模擬。 本項目的關鍵任務與創新點主要涵蓋五個維度：一是建立通用的量子-人工智能工作流以確定原子勢場與真實流體物性，實現計算速度數個數量級的飛躍；二是在 OpenFOAM 中實現並驗證一套引入機器學習驅動、具備動態物性修正的新型高維燃燒建模框架；三是在史無前例的極限壓力工況下開展全新燃燒實驗，揭示不同分子結構燃料與稀釋劑中真實流體效應的定性與定量演化趨勢；四是結合全新與現有實驗數據進行嚴謹驗證，首次定量評估多體與自由基相互作用的獨立影響；五是交付一套標準化的方法學與工具集以突破現有局限。 通過打破真實流體表徵的技術瓶頸，本項目將在表徵真實流體現象方面樹立具備前所未有準確度、效率與適用性的全新標竿。這項具有里程碑意義的變革性成果，其戰略效益不僅將徹底顛覆傳統的高壓燃燒研究，還將廣泛延伸並輻射至先進廢物處理、超高壓色譜分析、生物質高效加工以及行星大氣物理研究等更廣闊的尖端科學與工業領域。

15232326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15232326.value: 廢棄鋰離子電池誘發陰燃火災的基礎研究

15232326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15232326.value: Lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries are widely used in most electronic devices and electric vehicles (EVs), meanwhile the quantity of disposed battery cells also rises rapidly. After their disposal, the fire risk of these high-energy batteries remains and even increases, because they suffer from unintended impacts and damages during waste collection, storage, transportation, and processing. However, the ignition mechanisms of disposed batteries are not fully studied, posing a significant knowledge gap. Under mechanical, thermal, and electrical impacts, thermal runaway of batteries will occur, releasing intense heat that may ignite surrounding solid fuels in landfills and wildlands. In particular, the combustible nature of other disposed fuels makes it highly susceptible to smoldering combustion, which can propagate slowly and persist undetected for long periods, producing toxic emissions and transitioning into flames.
