Despite past research on Li-ion battery thermal runaway and smoldering fires, there is a fundamental gap in linking battery failure to its consequent initiation of fires in nearby fuels, as well as in addressing their coupled interactions. Therefore, our scientific understanding remains insufficient to support the development of reliable prevention, detection, and suppression strategies for battery-induced fires and the life-cycle battery safety management. This research aims to reveal the underlying mechanism of the ignition of smoldering fires in typical solid fuels induced by disposed Li-ion batteries and identify critical ignition conditions. Small-scale laboratory experiments will first be conducted to examine the thermal impact of disposed batteries under both internal and external short-circuit failure modes. The influence of battery properties and solid-fuel properties will be quantified. Gas analysis will provide emission signatures associated with ignition events. Then, numerical models will be developed and verified by lab-scale ignition tests, which will further simulate large-scale ignition risks of smoldering fires in waste processing and wildland. Eventually, this work will establish a scientific risk evaluation framework and provide practical guidelines for the detection, prevention, and suppression of fires induced by disposed Li-ion batteries. This research will benefit the scientific community and society through (1) Advancing scientific understanding of the mechanism of smoldering fire in waste and wildland fuels induced by disposed Li-ion batteries; (2) Enriching the knowledge of battery fire hazards, supporting safer strategies for the collection and recycling of end-of-life Li-ion batteries; (3) Providing a multi-parameter framework for assessing fire risks in modern waste processing systems containing disposed Li-ion batteries; (4) Informing safety management across waste battery recycling, contributing to the development of fire prevention standards. 鋰離子電池廣泛應用於各類電子設備和電動車，隨之而來的是廢棄電池數量的急劇增加。廢棄後的高能量電池在收集、儲存、運輸和處理過程中易遭受意外撞擊與損壞，導致其起火風險仍存在甚至加劇。然而，目前針對廢棄電池起火機制的研究尚不充分，且有顯著的認知空白。 在機械、熱或電應力的作用下，電池可能發生熱失控並釋放大量熱量，進而引燃垃圾掩埋場或野外環境中的固體可燃物。特別是廢棄物中存在的其他可燃材料，極易發生陰燃火災；這種燃燒過程緩慢蔓延且難以被察覺，可持續很長時間，不僅產生有毒排放物，還可能演變為明火燃燒。 儘管先前研究已涉及鋰離子電池熱失控及陰燃火災，但在建立「電池失效」與「引發週邊可燃物火災」之間的因果聯繫，以及闡明兩者間的耦合相互作用方面，仍存在根本性的研究缺失。因此，現有的科學認知尚不足以支撐針對電池引發火災的可靠預防、偵測及救援策略的製定，也難以滿足電池全生命週期安全管理的需求。 本研究旨在揭示廢棄鋰離子電池引發典型固體燃料陰燃的內在機制，並明確關鍵的起火條件。首先，將進行小規模實驗室實驗，檢視廢棄電池在內部和外部短路失效模式下的熱效應，量化電池特性及固體燃料特性對起火過程的影響，並透過氣體分析取得與起火事件相關的排放特性。隨後，將建立數值模型並利用實驗室規模的起火實驗進行驗證，進而模擬廢棄物處理場景及野外環境中的大規模陰燃起火風險。最終，本研究將建構科學的風險評估框架，並為廢棄鋰離子電池引發火災的偵測、預防及救援提供實用指導。本研究將透過以下方式造福科學界與社會： (1) 深化對廢棄鋰離子電池引發廢棄物及野外燃料陰燃火災機制的科學認知； (2) 深化對電池火災隱患的認識，支持更安全的廢棄鋰離子電池收集與回收策略； (3) 建構多參數評估框架，用於評估含有廢棄鋰離子電池的現代廢棄物處理系統中的火災風險； (4) 為廢棄電池回收過程中的安全管理提供指導，協助火災預防標準的製定。

15232726.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15232726.value: Prof Liu, Chuan Qi Prof Ng, Charles Wang Wai

15232726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15232726.value: Landslides pose serious risks to human life and infrastructure worldwide, causing 4,933 fatalities in 2024. This threat is expected to intensify due to climate change and extreme rainfall. Vegetation is increasingly used to mitigate shallow landslide risk, alone or with other techniques, supporting global efforts toward carbon neutrality and climate change mitigation. Extensive evidence demonstrates that vegetation effectively enhances slope stability through mechanical and hydrological reinforcement. In Hong Kong, statistics reveal a 63% reduction in landslide occurrences in areas where vegetation has recovered, compared to those without recovery. Analysing the behaviour of vegetated slopes is important yet challenging. In vegetated slopes, rooted soils are typically unsaturated with varying moisture conditions and exhibit anisotropy due to both soil fabric and root network. Accurate analysis is hindered by a lack of test data and constitutive models for unsaturated, anisotropic rooted soils. Furthermore, existing analysis methods mainly address pre-failure behaviour, leaving post-failure dynamics largely unexplored. Understanding post-failure behaviour is crucial for risk assessment and disaster mitigation, especially in densely populated cities like Hong Kong, where numerous buildings and roads are constructed along hillsides. Therefore, there is an urgent need for research that advances the analysis of both pre-failure and post-failure behaviour of unsaturated vegetated slopes. This project is timely in addressing these challenges through two interrelated tasks. The first focuses on laboratory testing and constitutive modelling of unsaturated rooted soils, with emphasis on anisotropic strength and dilatancy that are crucial for slope analysis. Advanced hollow cylinder torsional shear tests will be conducted on three types of rooted soils under varying principal stress magnitudes, directions, and suction levels. The unique data will support the development and validation of a novel constitutive model for unsaturated rooted soils that explicitly captures the interplay between fabric and root network anisotropies. Building on this new model, the second task will develop an advanced MPM-FEM coupled computational platform to simulate both pre-failure and post-failure behaviour of vegetated slopes, explicitly incorporating the distinct hydro-mechanical roles of fine and coarse roots within complex root architectures. To validate this platform, large-scale physical model tests of vegetated slopes subjected to rainfall will be conducted. The results from these tests and the validated numerical simulations will be analysed to assess the effects of root characteristics on slope stability and post-failure dynamics. The success of this project will deepen understanding of rooted soils and provide reliable tools for analysing vegetated slopes, supporting safe, low-carbon development. 滑坡是全球範圍內威脅人類生命財產安全與基礎設施營運的主要地質災害之一，僅2024年即導致4,933人遇難。在全球氣候變化加劇、極端降雨事件頻發的背景下，滑坡災害風險預計將進一步上升。植被護坡作為一種綠色低碳的生態工程手段，既可獨立應用，亦可與傳統工程措施聯合使用，契合全球碳中和目標與氣候變化減緩策略。大量研究表明，植被可透過力學加筋與水力調控雙重機制顯著提升邊坡穩定性。以香港為例，統計數據顯示，植被恢復區域的滑坡發生率相較未恢復區域大幅降低63%。 植被邊坡的水力–力學耦合行為極為複雜，分析難度較大。在實際條件下，根系土通常處於非飽和狀態，水分條件動態變化，並同時受土體原生組構與根系空間分佈影響，表現出顯著的非飽和各向異性特徵。當前，由於缺乏系統性試驗數據，以及能夠準確描述非飽和根系土各向異性行為的本構模型，植被邊坡精細化分析面臨關鍵瓶頸。此外，現有研究多集中於邊坡失穩前的穩定性評價，對其失穩後大變形演化過程的關注尚顯不足。而深入理解邊坡破壞後的動力學行為，對於風險評估與防災減災具有重要意義，尤其是在香港這類高密度山地城市，大量建築物與交通設施依山而建，災害後果尤為嚴重。因此，亟需開展能夠涵蓋非飽和植被邊坡失穩前–失穩後全過程的系統性研究。 針對上述挑戰，本項目擬圍繞兩項相互關聯的研究任務展開工作。第一項任務聚焦於非飽和根系土的室內試驗與本構模型研究，重點分析對邊坡穩定性起關鍵作用的強度各向異性與剪脹特性。透過採用先進的空心圓柱扭剪儀，針對三類典型根系土開展不同主應力幅值、主應力方向及基質吸力水平下的多場耦合試驗，獲取系統性試驗數據，支撐並驗證新建的非飽和根系土本構模型，該模型將顯式考慮土體組構各向異性與根系網絡各向異性的耦合機制。第二項任務基於該本構模型，開發先進的MPM-FEM耦合數值計算平台，用於模擬植被邊坡從失穩前到失穩後的全過程破壞演化，並精細刻畫複雜根系結構中細根與粗根各自不同的水力–力學作用。為驗證平台可靠性，項目將開展降雨條件下植被邊坡的大比例尺物理模型試驗。基於試驗成果與數值模擬結果，系統評估根系特徵對邊坡穩定性及失穩後大變形動力學行為的影響規律。本項目的順利實施，將深化對非飽和根系土力學行為的理解，並為植被邊坡分析提供科學可靠的計算工具，從而支持安全、低碳的可持續發展路徑。

15233026.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15233026.value: Prof Shen, Shihui Prof ZHAO, Qi

15233026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15233026.value: Bottom-up fatigue cracking is a major failure mode of flexible pavements. The crack initiates at the bottom of the asphalt layer interfaced with a granular base layer. Yet, little attention has been paid to the interfacial behaviors of the two materials under traffic loading. In fatigue testing of asphalt mixtures, samples are unsupported by granular materials. In pavement design and analysis, both layers are treated as homogeneous materials with only their respective moduli being considered. Both material characterization and structural analysis ignore meso/micro-scale interactions between asphalt and granular materials. Consequently, knowledge is lacking on (1) how the characteristics of granular material affect stress concentration of the contacted asphalt mixture, (2) whether there are any compatibility issues between asphalt mixture design and granular material design, (3) how interactions between the two layers affect fatigue cracking of flexible pavements, (4) whether, and to what extent, interface optimization enhances the fatigue life of asphalt pavement. Addressing such critical questions will enable pavement engineers to improve material and structural designs to enhance pavement durability without significantly increasing cost. To address these knowledge gaps, this study aims to investigate the fundamental mechanisms governing load-induced interactions between asphalt and granular materials at their interface. We propose four integrated objectives across modeling, laboratory testing, generalization, and field validation: 1) to model and simulate load-induced interactions between asphalt mixtures and granular materials at the interface, and calibrate/validate the results using a micro-CT equipped with an in-situ loading and instantaneous scanning system; 2) to develop a new laboratory sample preparation method and a new test method to evaluate the failure of composite asphalt-granular samples under repeated loading; 3) to identify the general trends of the effects of interfacial characteristics on stress/strain distributions and fatigue performance; 4) to validate the interactive effects between asphalt and granular materials on pavement performance through full-scale accelerated pavement testing. The research outcomes include: 1) new asphalt-granular analysis models calibrated by a micro-CT equipped with a novel in-situ loading and instantaneous scanning system, 2) a new sample preparation apparatus and method, 3) a new test method for composite asphalt-granular samples, and 4) key insights into the relationship between interfacial characteristics and asphalt fatigue. These outcomes will advance our knowledge of asphalt pavement behaviors and performance in actual loading situations, reveal the fundamental mechanisms of load-induced asphalt-granular material interactions, and improve pavement durability through optimized material and structural designs. 「底部疲勞裂縫」是路面最常見的壞損方式，通常發源於瀝青層與底下碎石基層的「接觸面」。然而，傳統的路面設計與測試都將兩者視為獨立且質地均勻的材料，完全忽略了它們在微觀細節上的相互影響。這導致我們過去無法掌握碎石特性對瀝青受力的影響、兩種材料設計是否不相容，以及接觸面如何影響路面壽命。只要能釐清並優化這個接觸面，就能在不顯著增加成本的前提下，大幅提升路面的耐用度。 為了補足這些知識缺口，本研究結合電腦模擬、新型實驗與真實路面測試，深入探討瀝青與碎石層在受力時的互動機制。我們將利用高精度的微電腦斷層掃描（micro-CT）進行即時動態觀察與模型校正，並研發全新的瀝青-碎石複合樣品製作與測試方法，最後透過模擬真實車流長期壓打的「加速路面測試」來驗證成果。本研究將提供全新的分析模型與測試設備，揭開材料互動的根本機制，幫助工程師優化材料與結構設計，打造更堅固耐用的道路。

15233126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15233126.value: 面向宽幅薄壁轻合金构件先进多筒挤压技术的多尺度变形机理与智能模具设计研究

15233126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15233126.value: The growing demand for lightweight and high-performance transportation structures has driven rapid development of ultra-wide and thin-walled light-alloy extrusions. The recently invented multi-container extrusion (MCE) technology by the PI has demonstrated, at both laboratory and industrial scales, a threefold breakthrough in extrudable width, enabling the integrated forming of large and complex components without subsequent welding. Despite these advances, MCE still faces two critical challenges: mechanical property degradation induced by peripheral coarse grains (PCG) formation and the lack of a mechanism-based, predictive, and transferable die design framework. These challenges fundamentally arise from the insufficient understanding of the coupled deformation-microstructure interactions under extrusion-representative conditions, especially the transient strain-rate jumps near the die orifice and the immediate post-extrusion thermal exposure before quenching. Moreover, the absence of effective multi-scale finite element (FE) and artificial intelligence (AI) tools for predictive design and optimisation further limits industrial implementation. To address these challenges, this project proposes a mechanism-informed and data-driven strategy to bridge the gap between fundamental science and intelligent design for MCE. Through integrated hot-deformation tests, MCE experiments, multi-scale characterisation, FE simulations, and AI-assisted framework development, the project aims (i) to elucidate the underlying microstructural evolution mechanisms in MCE process under transient deformation and post-deformation thermal exposure, and (ii) to establish an FE-AI integrated system for automated die-design optimisation towards optimal macro-micro extrusion performance. Specifically, this project will clarify the coupled mechanisms between microstructural evolution and mechanical response, including work hardening, dynamic and static recovery/recrystallisation, and grain growth, under extrusion-representative conditions. Quantitative dominance maps of competing mechanisms will be established, leading to a physically based, multi-scale constitutive model that captures material thermomechanical behaviour. This model will be implemented into a customised FE platform for MCE to enable accurate prediction of extrusion indices such as PCG thickness, metal-flow uniformity, recrystallised fraction, grain-size deviation, and die stress. Validated through extrusion trials of representative Al-Li alloy wide-thin components, the simulation-experiment datasets will be digitalised into a machine-interpretable, sequence-encoded, profile-agnostic knowledge base. By combining this knowledge with FE-based data generation, data augmentation, and reinforcement learning, an AI-assisted die design system will be established to autonomously propose optimal die geometries satisfying multiple objectives of metal flow uniformity, microstructural property, and tooling reliability. Through this mechanism-informed, simulation-supported, and data-driven research, the project will deliver an integrated scientific-engineering platform that advances the fundamental understanding of multi-scale extrusion mechanisms while transforming die design from an experience-driven practice into an intelligent and predictive process. 随着交通运输装备向轻量化、高性能及大型一体化方向发展，超宽薄壁轻合金挤压构件的应用需求日益迫切。项目负责人发明的多筒挤压技术突破了传统挤压工艺的成形宽度极限，使构件可成形宽度提高至传统工艺的约3倍，为大型复杂轻合金构件的无焊缝一体化成形提供了新途径。 然而，多筒挤压过程中仍存在两个亟待解决的关键问题：一是制品表层易形成周边粗晶组织，造成力学性能劣化；二是现有模具设计仍主要依赖经验，缺乏基于成形机理、具有预测能力且可适用于不同截面构件的设计方法。上述问题主要源于对多筒挤压过程中变形行为、热历史与微观组织演化之间耦合关系的认识尚不充分，尤其是模具出口区域应变速率瞬态跃迁及挤出后淬火前短时热暴露对组织演化的作用机制尚不明确。同时，面向多筒挤压过程的有限元预测与人工智能优化方法尚未形成有效融合，制约了模具设计效率、成形质量调控及该技术的规模化工程应用。 针对上述问题，本项目拟采用机理研究与数据驱动相结合的研究思路，综合开展热变形实验、多尺度组织表征、有限元模拟与人工智能辅助设计，主要实现以下两个目标：1. 揭示瞬态变形及变形后热暴露条件下多筒挤压组织演化机制；2. 构建有限元-人工智能融合的模具优化方法，实现成形质量与组织性能的协同调控。具体而言，项目将围绕加工硬化、“动态与静态回复、动态与静态再结晶及晶粒长大等机制，研究典型挤压条件下微观组织演化与力学响应的耦合关系，建立不同竞争机制的定量主导区间图及多尺度本构模型。进一步将该模型嵌入多筒挤压有限元平台，实现对周边粗晶层厚度、金属流动均匀性、再结晶体积分数、晶粒尺寸偏差及模具应力等关键指标的预测，并通过典型铝锂合金宽幅薄壁构件挤压试验进行验证。在此基础上，将模拟与实验数据构建为机器可识别、可迁移的知识库，并结合有限元数据生成、数据增强和强化学习，建立面向多目标优化的智能模具设计系统。 通过机理引导、模拟支撑和数据驱动的综合研究，本项目将建立一个集基础研究与工程设计于一体的科学-工程平台，深化对多尺度挤压变形与组织演化机制的理解，同时推动挤压模具设计由依赖经验的传统方式转变为智能化、可预测的设计过程。

15233426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15233426.value: 面向桥梁网络主动健康监测的新一代智能体研究

15233426.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15233426.value: Prof Sun, Hao Prof Xia, Yong

15233426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15233426.value: Long service bridges inevitably suffer from degradation. Structural health monitoring (SHM) systems have been installed on many long-span bridges to monitor structural conditions. However, these systems predominantly function as passive, isolated data collectors. As a result, vast and heterogeneous data resources (e.g., long-term sensor measurements, inspection records, and physical models) remain unstructured and fragmented. The subsequent tasks from data analysis to decision making are characterized by manual expert-driven processes. Consequently, bridge condition assessment and management remain reactive, inefficient, and unable to harness decades of collective knowledge. The advent of agentic artificial intelligence (AI), driven by large language models (LLMs), offers transformative potential for automating data synthesis and complex reasoning. Currently, the application of LLMs in SHM is still in the nascent stage, focused on isolated tasks such as visual inspection interpretation. The full potential of agentic AI operating on a continuous perceive-think-plan-act loop (e.g., autonomously mining data, learning through complexity, and planning tasks) remains largely unexplored. This project aims to pioneer an integrated agentic AI for intelligent, proactive, and network-scale bridge health assessment. By synthesizing cutting-edge agentic AI technologies, the project will transform fragmented data archives into a unified actionable intelligence core. The following tasks will be undertaken: (1) construct a novel spatiotemporal knowledge graph as the agent’s digital brain to autonomously structure multi-source data; (2) develop a novel LLM-to-finite element model chain in the multiphysics object-oriented simulation environment (MOOSE) to empower the agent with autonomous, on-demand physical simulation; (3) leverage physics-based simulation to connect statistical patterns with bridge condition assessment, and enable temporal knowledge transfer from data-rich to data-scarce bridges; and (4) integrate these capabilities into a unified AI agent for automated prognostics, condition assessment, and physically-explained early warning. The developed system will be demonstrated and validated on world-class long-span bridges in Hong Kong. The project holds significant academic and practical value. Academically, the project pioneers a holistic cognitive framework for bridge engineering agents. It contributes the spatiotemporal knowledge graph for contextual memory, the LLM-to-MOOSE chain to automate physical simulation, and temporal transfer learning for generalized intelligence, defining a new class of AI that can reason and act in complex physical domains. Practically, this project will deliver the first operational agentic AI for proactive network-scale bridge health assessment, establishing a valuable reference model for infrastructure management worldwide. 长期服役过程中，桥梁结构不可避免地会出现性能退化。目前许多大跨桥梁已安装结构健康监测系统，用于持续评估其服役状态。然而，现有系统大多仅承担数据采集与平台运行功能，缺乏主动分析和协同决策能力。长期传感监测数据、人工检测记录和物理模型等海量异构资源仍然分散存储，尚未得到有效组织与融合；从数据分析到决策制定，也高度依赖人工操作和专家经验。因此，现有桥梁状态评估与管养模式仍以事后响应为主，不仅效率较低，也难以充分利用数十年来积累的监测数据、专业知识与工程经验。 大语言模型驱动的智能体技术迅速发展，为多源数据自动融合和复杂工程推理提供了新的可能。目前，大语言模型在结构健康监测领域的应用尚处于起步阶段，相关研究主要聚焦于视觉检测结果解读等单一任务。对于能够形成“感知—思考—规划—行动”闭环的智能体，例如自主挖掘数据、从复杂信息中学习规律并规划和执行任务，其在结构健康监测领域的潜力尚未得到充分挖掘。 本项目旨在构建一套集成化智能体框架，实现智能、主动的桥梁群健康评估。项目将融合前沿智能体技术，把分散、碎片化的数据资源转化为统一、可推理并可执行的智能中枢。具体研究内容包括：（1）构建新型时空知识图谱，作为智能体的“数字大脑”，自主汇集、组织和结构化多源数据；（2）依托多物理场面向物理仿真平台，开发“大语言模型—有限元模型”协同链路，使智能体能够根据任务需求自主开展物理仿真；（3）借助物理机理驱动的仿真，建立监测数据统计特征与桥梁结构状态之间的关联，并将数据丰富桥梁积累的时序知识迁移至数据稀缺桥梁；（4）集成上述能力，构建统一的桥梁工程智能体，实现性能自动预测、状态智能评估以及具有因果解释能力的早期预警。最终，所开发的系统将在香港具有代表性的世界级大跨桥梁上开展示范应用与验证。 本项目兼具重要的学术价值与工程应用价值。在学术方面，项目将构建面向桥梁工程智能体的整体认知框架，提出支持上下文记忆的时空知识图谱、面向自动化物理仿真的“大语言模型—物理仿真”协同链路，以及提升跨桥梁泛化能力的时序知识迁移方法，由此探索一类能够在复杂物理环境中自主推理并采取行动的新型人工智能范式。在工程应用方面，项目将研制面向主动式桥梁群健康评估的可运行智能体系统，为全球基础设施的智能管养提供可推广、可借鉴的示范方案。

15233926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15233926.value: 月球永久陰影區葉瓣狀邊緣撞擊坑的先進測圖與特徵分析及其於揮發物探測之應用

15233926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15233926.value: The Moon’s rotation axis is slightly tilted relative to the Sun, resulting in permanently shadowed regions (PSRs) in deep craters at the poles. These PSRs remain extremely cold, allowing them to trap volatiles such as water ice and hydroxyl, which can alter the regolith and form distinctive landforms. The most notable landform consistent with subsurface volatiles is the lobate-rimmed crater (LRC), which is characterized by features such as low depth-to-diameter ratios, subdued rim heights, and limited ejecta dispersal. LRCs have only recently been identified through high-sensitivity imaging by the newly deployed ShadowCam in lunar orbit, which can capture faint, indirect illumination within PSRs. Traditional techniques, including photogrammetry and laser altimetry, are inadequate for generating detailed 3D topographic models in the PSRs, hindering the ability to detect LRCs. To date, there has been no comprehensive study of the distribution, morphology, or volatile associations of LRCs. This project will address these gaps by developing advanced methodologies for high-resolution 3D mapping, systematic classification, and detailed characterization of LRCs within PSRs and by integrating these findings with complementary remote sensing results to enable synergistic exploration of lunar volatiles. The objectives of the proposed project are: 1) To develop a novel shape-from-shading method that leverages indirect illumination to achieve pixel-wise, high-resolution 3D topographic mapping of PSRs in the lunar polar regions, utilizing ShadowCam imagery. 2) To develop a novel multi-modal active deep-learning approach for the detection and classification of LRCs within PSRs, using both 2D and 3D features derived from images and topographic models. 3) To investigate the distribution and morphological characteristics of LRCs in the lunar polar regions and correlate these findings with the abundance of volatiles inferred from complementary remote sensing data to advance the synergistic exploration of lunar volatiles. The PI is actively involved in China’s forthcoming lunar missions, including Chang’E-7 (2026) and Chang’E-8 (2029), both of which will land at the lunar south pole to explore water ice and other resources. This engagement will provide privileged access to mission data, and the research outputs will directly support these missions. The results will deepen our understanding of lunar volatiles and their implications for lunar geology and potential habitation. Furthermore, the developed methods will have significant potential for technology transfer to civilian applications such as 3D city mapping, urban remote sensing, landform analysis, and artificial intelligence, benefiting Hong Kong, mainland China, and the global community. 月球自轉軸相對於太陽光照方向僅稍有傾斜，使得其兩極較深撞擊坑內形成永久陰影區（permanently shadowed regions, PSRs）。這些永久陰影區長期維持極低溫環境，因而能夠捕集水冰、羥基等揮發物；這些揮發物可改變月壤性質，並形成獨特的地貌特徵。其中，最顯著且被認為與地表淺層揮發物相一致的地貌為葉瓣狀邊緣撞擊坑（lobate-rimmed crater, LRC），其特徵包括較低的深徑比、較不明顯的坑緣高度，以及有限的噴射物擴散範圍。LRC 是近期才透過新近部署於月球軌道上的 ShadowCam 高靈敏度成像數據被識別出來的。ShadowCam 能夠捕捉永久陰影區內微弱的間接光照信號。然而，傳統技術，包括攝影測量和激光測高，難以在永久陰影區生成精細的三維地形模型，從而限制了 LRC 的探測能力。迄今為止，尚未有針對 LRC 分佈、形態特徵或其與揮發物關聯性的系統研究。本項目將通過研發先進方法，對永久陰影區內 LRC 進行高分辨率三維測圖、系統分類和精細特徵分析，並將結果與相關遙感分析結果相結合，以推動月球揮發物的協同探測。 本項目的研究目標如下： 1）研發一種利用間接光照的新型明暗恢復形狀方法，基於 ShadowCam 影像，實現月球極區永久陰影區逐像素、高分辨率三維地形測圖。 2）研發一種新型多模態主動深度學習方法，利用由影像和地形模型提取的二維與三維特徵，對永久陰影區內的 LRC 進行檢測與分類。 3）研究月球極區 LRC 的分佈及形態特徵，並將其與相關遙感數據推斷出的揮發物豐度進行關聯分析，以推進月球揮發物的協同探測。 項目負責人正積極參與中國即將開展的月球探測任務，包括嫦娥七號（2026）等。這些任務將著陸於月球南極，以探測水冰及其他資源。這將為本項目提供獲取任務數據的有利條件，而研究成果亦將直接支持上述任務。項目成果將深化對月球揮發物及其對月球地質和潛在居住環境意義的理解。此外，本項目所研發的方法在應用方面亦具有重要的技術轉移潛力，例如用於三維城市測圖、城市遙感、地貌分析和人工智能等，將惠及香港、中國內地及國際相關領域的技術進步。

15234226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15234226.value: 力學驅動閉環觸覺系統用於觸感感官復健：從基礎模型到轉譯應用

15234226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15234226.value: Prof Chen, Zuobing Prof Liu, Jun

15234226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15234226.value: Stroke is a major neurological condition, with over 12 million new cases and 100 million survivors globally each year. By 2025, stroke is expected to affect 60,000 people in Hong Kong, with the majority being seniors. Among them, nearly half of survivors experience somatosensory disorders, which impede motor recovery and independence, yet these complications remain largely undertreated. Existing therapies often lack mechanistic understanding and specificity. This project will create a mechanics-driven, closed-loop framework that links stimulus design, skin mechanics, receptor activation, and brain responses for personalized rehabilitation. To lay the foundation for this framework, Task I develops a nonlinear continuum mechanics model of skin tissue, coupled with receptor-specific neural response fitting. This model quantitatively relates external stimulation parameters such as frequency, amplitude, and spatial distribution to the stress and strain fields that govern the firing patterns of four mechanoreceptor subtypes. Building on this modeling, we further employ Bayesian optimization to iteratively fit electroencephalography (EEG) responses with varying stimulation parameters, thereby establishing a correlation between the stimuli, the neural response patterns, and EEG responses. Task II further applies Task I’s insights to develop practical rehabilitation systems. We will develop a bimodal tactile stimulation system featuring electroadhesion-based friction modulation for superficial receptors to support texture discrimination training, and a 3D vibrotactile array that delivers high-frequency stimulation to deep mechanoreceptors for vibration perception training. Adaptive signal generation algorithms, guided by models from Task I, drive both modalities to achieve receptor-selective activation and maximized therapeutic efficacy. To further enhance adaptability, Task III focuses on developing a closed-loop personalized tactile rehabilitation methodology that tailors therapy based on EEG feedback and stratified database, with a large language model translating natural language therapeutic instructions into stimulation parameters. The system will be refined iteratively using performance metrics, user feedback, and statistical analysis to ensure efficacy and safety. By unifying mechanical modeling, neural signal interpretation, and intelligent control, this project addresses a fundamental barrier in sensory neurorehabilitation: the lack of quantitative, receptor-targeted, and personalized tactile feedback. The resulting system will transform tactile rehabilitation from empirical practice into a precision discipline grounded in real-time and personalized neural monitoring. Beyond stroke, this project provides a foundation for sensory restoration across neurological disorders, injuries, and neuroprosthetics, offering evidence-based tactile therapy for millions worldwide. 中風是一種主要的神經系統疾病，全球每年新增病例超過 1,200 萬宗，並有約 1 億名中風倖存者。到 2025 年，預計香港將有 60,000 人受中風影響，其中大多數為長者。在這些患者當中，近半數倖存者會出現軀體感覺障礙，這些障礙會阻礙運動功能恢復及獨立生活能力；然而，相關併發症在很大程度上仍未得到充分治療。現有療法往往缺乏對作用機制的深入理解及明確針對性。本項目將建立一個由力學驅動的閉環框架，連結刺激設計、皮膚力學、感受器激活與大腦反應，以實現個人化康復。 為奠定此框架的基礎，任務一將建立皮膚組織的非線性連續介質力學模型，並結合針對特定感受器的神經反應擬合。該模型將外部刺激參數，如頻率、振幅及空間分佈，與決定四種機械感受器亞型放電模式的應力與應變場進行定量關聯。在此建模基礎上，我們將進一步採用貝葉斯優化，針對不同刺激參數下的腦電圖（EEG）反應進行迭代擬合，從而建立刺激、神經反應模式與 EEG 反應之間的相關性。 任務二將進一步應用任務一所得見解，開發實用的康復系統。我們將研發一套雙模態觸覺刺激系統，其中包括基於電黏附的摩擦調制，用於激活表層感受器並支援紋理辨識訓練；以及一個 3D 振動觸覺陣列，用於向深層機械感受器傳遞高頻刺激，以進行振動感知訓練。在任務一模型的指導下，自適應訊號生成演算法將驅動上述兩種模態，以實現感受器選擇性激活並最大化治療效果。 為進一步提升適應能力，任務三將聚焦於開發一種閉環個人化觸覺康復方法，根據 EEG 反饋及分層數據庫定制治療方案，並利用大型語言模型（LLM）將自然語言治療指令轉化為刺激參數。該系統將透過效能指標、使用者回饋及統計分析進行迭代優化，以確保療效與安全性。 通過整合力學建模、神經訊號解讀與智能控制，本項目旨在解決感覺神經康復中的一項根本障礙：缺乏定量化、針對感受器且個人化的觸覺反饋。最終形成的系統將把觸覺康復從經驗性實踐轉變為一門以即時、個人化神經監測為基礎的精準學科。除中風外，本項目亦將為神經系統疾病、損傷及神經假體中的感覺恢復奠定基礎，為全球數以百萬計的人士提供以實證為本的觸覺治療。

15234326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15234326.value: 高壓縮導電氣凝膠自適應調控：高性能CFRP複合材料的非熱壓罐快速與規模化製造

15234326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15234326.value: Carbon fibre-reinforced polymer (CFRP) composites are of great interest in aerospace and other engineering fields due to their excellent strength-to-weight ratio and multifunctional potential. However, their widespread application is limited by manufacturing challenges, particularly achieving uniform fibre compaction and consistent resin curing. Traditional autoclave curing, while effective, is energy-intensive and costly, making it difficult to scale to large structures. Out-of-autoclave methods, such as vacuum-assisted resin infusion (VARI), offer more sustainable alternatives but still struggle to achieve high fibre volume fractions required for optimal mechanical properties. Furthermore, these methods often require oven curing to fully crosslink the resin. Although out-of-oven solutions, including heat blankets for localized heating and conductive interleaves for in-situ heating, have been explored, they result in uneven temperature distribution and do not address the fundamental issue of fibre compaction, respectively. To overcome these challenges, we propose a highly compressible and electrically conductive aerogel-based interleave as adaptive compaction media between carbon fabrics. This interleave can dynamically respond to pressure changes during the VARI process, enabling fast and scalable out-of-autoclave production of CFRP composites through multiscale mechanisms. At macroscales, they collapse under vacuum to fill gaps and irregularities between carbon fibres before resin infusion, converting localized point pressures into evenly distributed surface pressures. As such, pressure is transferred more uniformly to the underlying layers for uniform compaction, enabling high fibre volume fractions comparable to autoclave-processed composites. During infusion, the interleaves continuously act as adaptive buffers to redistribute local pressure fluctuations, minimizing the negative effects of fibre relaxation. After infusion, the intimate contact achieved by compressible structures promotes the formation of a hybrid 3D conductive network, leveraging the through-thickness conductivity of aerogel interleaves and the in-plane conductivity of carbon fabrics to enable programmable, uniform electrical heating for energy-efficient out-of-oven curing. At microscales, vertical pore channels within aerogel interleaves facilitate rapid resin transport, enabling effective wetting of all carbon fabrics and minimizing void content. At nanoscales, tailored surface chemistry of aerogels improves wettability and interfacial adhesion with epoxy resin, further enhancing impregnation and mechanical integrity. The quality and energy consumption of the final CFRP products will be quantitatively compared to those produced by traditional methods, laying the foundation for out-of-autoclave manufacturing of CFRP composites. The PI brings extensive expertise in multifunctional CFRP composites and advanced freeze-casting technologies for scalable composite manufacturing. Successful implementation of this project will enable alternative out-of-autoclave manufacturing methods, significantly enhancing the versatility and sustainability of CFRP composite production. 碳纖維增強樹脂基（CFRP）複合材料是航空航天等高端製造領域的關鍵支撐材料。然而，傳統熱壓罐固化工藝的高能耗、高成本，極大地限制了其在大型結構件上的規模化應用；而現有的非熱壓罐 (Out-of-autoclave) 成型工藝，則面臨因纖維壓實不足導致的低纖維體積含量，以及因固化溫度不均誘發的熱應力缺陷雙重瓶頸。為此，本項目提出引入一種高壓縮性導電形變氣凝膠插層作為自適應壓實介質。該插層在真空輔助樹脂灌注過程中，通過以下多尺度協同機制，實現高性能CFRP的低能耗、無爐化（Out-of-oven）製造： • 宏觀尺度（協同壓實與原位固化）：插層在真空負壓下自適應壓實，填充纖維層間空隙並實現壓力的均勻傳遞，以獲得媲美熱壓罐工藝的高纖維體積含量；同時，利用插層與纖維構建的三維混合導電網絡，通過程序化自阻發熱，實現高效、均勻的無爐原位固化。 • 微觀尺度（樹脂高效輸送）：利用氣凝膠內部高度定向的垂直孔道結構，構築低阻力流道，加速樹脂在厚度方向的滲透與充分潤濕，從而顯著降低製品孔隙率。 • 納觀尺度（界面鍵合調控）：通過精細調控氣凝膠的表面化學活性，增強其與環氧樹脂基體的界面相容性與分子間作用力，保障複合材料優異的整體力學性能。 本項目將定量評估新工藝在製品質量提升與能耗控制上的雙重優勢，為高性能CFRP的非熱壓罐製造奠定堅實的物理機制與工程技術基礎。項目負責人（PI）在多功能複合材料及定向凍結鑄造領域積累深厚，項目的實施將顯著提升複合材料製造的綠色化與多功能化水平。

15234426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15234426.value: 鑽石超精密加工中亞表面損傷多尺度檢測、機制與製程優化的智能分子動力學的整合系統研發

15234426.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15234426.value: Dr Ho , Lai Ting Prof Wang, Chunjin Dr Yuan, Song Prof ZHAO, Haitao

15234426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15234426.value: Diamond possesses high hardness and exceptional multifunctional properties, making it indispensable for high energy and semiconductor applications. However, ultra-precision machining of diamond through grinding, mechanical polishing and chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) inevitably induces surface/subsurface damage (SSD) in diamond, encompassing microcracks, dislocation networks, amorphous layers, and point defects, which critically limits the performance and lifetime of diamond-based quantum devices, high-power optics, and high-frequency electronics. Current technologies for detecting SSD in diamond face significant bottlenecks, and our fundamental understanding of SSD evolution are still far from complete. There is a lack of single detection method that covers the entire scale range of SSD. It suffers from limited spatial resolution, incomplete scale coverage, or destructive operation, while the coupled thermo–mechano–chemical mechanisms underlying SSD evolution during ultra-precision machining remain not well understood with a lack of dynamic in-situ models to capture the full damage evolution process. This project aims to propose a unified AI–molecular dynamics (MD) system to achieve in-situ, multi-scale, and non-destructive characterization of SSD, quantitative mechanism modeling, and process optimization for CMP of diamond. The research is formulated in six phases which include: (i) development of an AI-assisted multi-modal data fusion platform integrating Raman spectroscopy, photoluminescence, X-ray diffraction, TEM, and MD simulations for holistic SSD mapping; (ii) a study of crystallite size and orientation effects on material removal; (iii) development of an AI-driven mechanistic inference system to extract atomistic pathways of damage evolution from large-scale MD trajectories; (iv) mechanistic dissection of mechanical–chemical synergy and competition in CMP through combined experiments and reactive MD simulations, establishing SSD phase diagrams; (v) construction of predictive machine learning models for SSD prediction and process optimization, supported by interpretability analysis; and (vi) deployment of a real-time AI-guided CMP control system validated on a laboratory testbed and scaled toward industrial application. The project, if successfully, will provide an AI-assisted multi-modal data fusion framework that enables better scientific understanding of SSD evolution, full-scale, non-destructive characterization of SSD in diamond. It will also provide an important means for the development of the first predictive, physics-informed, and adaptive control strategy for minimizing SSD in ultra-precision machining of diamond. Hence, a smart molecular dynamics integrated system will be established for multi-scale detection, mechanism elucidation, and process optimization of SSD in ultra-precision machining of diamond. The outcomes will enhance manufacturing reliability, extend component lifetime, and set new benchmarks for non-destructive evaluation in extreme manufacturing environments. 鑽石具有超高硬度、超高熱導率、寬禁帶等優異物理性能，是高功率電子裝置、半導體裝置及極端服役光學系統的核心材料。然而，在研磨、機械拋光及化學機械拋光（CMP）等超精密加工過程中，不可避免地產生微裂紋、位錯網絡、非晶層及點缺陷等亞表面損傷（Subsurface Damage, SSD），嚴重製約金剛石器件的服役性能、可靠性及使用壽命。目前，鑽石亞表面損傷檢測仍面臨多尺度表徵能力不足、空間分辨率有限、檢測手段具有破壞性等關鍵瓶頸，尚缺乏一種能夠涵蓋原子尺度至微米尺度的統一無損檢測方法。同時，超精密加工過程中熱—力—化學多場耦合作用下亞表面損傷的形成、演化及去除機制尚未完全闡明，缺乏能動態揭示損傷演變全過程的理論模型與智能分析方法。 本項目擬建構人工智慧（AI）與分子動力學（MD）深度融合的智慧分子動力學整合系統，實現鑽石亞表面損傷的原位、多尺度、無損檢測，揭示損傷形成與演化機制，並建立面向化學機械拋光製程的智慧優化方法。本計畫圍繞六個面向進行研究：（1）建構融合拉曼光譜、光致發光（PL）、X射線衍射（XRD）、透射電子顯微鏡（TEM）及分子動力學模擬的AI多模態資料融合平台，實現亞表面損傷全尺度重構與定量表徵；（2）研究晶粒尺寸及晶體取向對材料去除法素和損傷形成規律的影響結構的影響（3）路徑及關鍵機制；（4）結合化學機械拋光實驗與反應分子動力學模擬，系統揭示機械作用與化學反應的協同及競爭機制，建構亞表面損傷形成與演化相圖；（5）建立具有物理約束和可解釋性的機器學習預測模型，實現亞表面損傷預測及加工參數智能優化；（6）開發即時AI智能控制系統，實現化學機械應用拋光製程。 項目實施後，將形成以鑽石超精密加工亞表面損傷的AI多模態融合檢測與智慧分析新框架，實現從原子尺度到微米尺度的全尺度無損表徵，深化對亞表面損傷形成與演化規律的科學認知；建立首個融合物理機理、人工智慧和分子動力學的亞表面損傷預測與自適應控制體系，實質現超精密加工過程的智慧優化與損傷最小化控制，最終建構鑽石超精密加工亞表面損傷多尺度檢測—機械理解析—製程優化一體化智慧分子動力學系統，為高階半導體、精密光學及量子裝置製造提供關鍵理論基礎與核心技術支撐，並推動極端製造領域無損檢測與智慧製造技術的發展。

15234826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15234826.value: 物理机理和人工智能双驱动的长期气溶胶参数反演研究

15234826.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15234826.value: Prof Wong, Charles Man-sing Prof Yuan, Qiangqiang

15234826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15234826.value: Atmospheric aerosols exert critical impacts on the Earth’s radiative balance by absorbing and scattering solar radiation, which are also essential for environmental and climate-related studies. Thus, how to realize aerosol parameter estimation accurately and reliably at finer spatio-temporal resolution has attracted extensive attention. Numerous studies have been conducted for satellite-based aerosol optical depth (AOD) retrieval, which is a key parameter to describe the effect of aerosol on light attenuation. However, other aerosol parameters (e.g., Single Scattering Albedo (SSA), Fine Mode Fraction (FMF), aerosol types) are generally neglected, rendering it difficult to comprehensively characterize the aerosol properties, thereby introducing substantial uncertainties in aerosol-climate interaction models. The research team proposes to develop a novel physics-guided artificial intelligence (AI) dual-driven model to achieve aerosol composition retrieval at finer spatio-temporal resolution based on Fengyun-4 (FY-4) and Advanced Himawari Imager (AHI) observations. The proposed project is structured by three inter-related work programs: (i) a decadal Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Function (BRDF)-corrected land surface reflectance (LSR) dataset will be constructed by synergizing multi-angle and multi-spectral satellite data; (ii) a pioneering physics-guided AI dual-driven model will be developed by introducing physical constraints of Radiative Transfer Model (RTM) to an Attention-augmented Random Forest Transfer Learning (ARFTL) architecture for multiple aerosol parameter estimations; (iii) a Multi-Dimensional Aerosol Fingerprint Classification (MDAFC) method will be developed to enable dynamic aerosol type identification at pixel level by leveraging the derived multi-dimensional aerosol fingerprint database. This project will fill the research gap of lacking a methodology to realize multiple aerosol parameter retrievals at finer spatio-temporal resolution and the classification approach for pixel-level aerosol type identification. Deliverables from this project, especially for the proposed several novel algorithms, a long-term BRDF-corrected LSR dataset, a comprehensive aerosol fingerprint database and decadal dynamic pixel-level aerosol type maps, are expected to significantly advance satellite-based aerosol retrieval techniques. They will provide vital data for air quality monitoring, climate model calibration, and informed policy-making, supporting Hong Kong and the global community in achieving environmental sustainability and climate resilience. 大气气溶胶通过吸收和散射太阳辐射，对地球辐射能量平衡、空气质量及气候变化产生重要影响。如何准确、可靠地获取高时空分辨率的气溶胶参数，是大气环境遥感和气候研究领域的重要科学问题。现有卫星气溶胶遥感研究主要集中于气溶胶光学厚度（Aerosol Optical Depth，AOD）反演。AOD能够表征气溶胶对光辐射的整体衰减程度，但难以充分反映气溶胶的吸收特性、粒径结构和类型差异。单次散射反照率（Single Scattering Albedo，SSA）、细模态比例（Fine Mode Fraction，FMF）及气溶胶类型等关键参数仍缺乏高精度、高时空分辨率的长期观测产品，制约了对气溶胶综合特性的准确刻画，也增加了气溶胶—气候相互作用模拟的不确定性。 本项目拟综合利用风云四号（FY-4）卫星和Himawari卫星（Advanced Himawari Imager，AHI）的高频观测优势，构建物理机理与人工智能双驱动的气溶胶参数反演方法，实现多种气溶胶参数的高时空分辨率协同反演。主要研究任务如下： （1）融合多角度、多光谱卫星观测，分析地表反射率随观测几何和光谱波段的变化特征，构建经过双向反射分布函数（Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Function，BRDF）校正的长期陆表反射率（Land Surface Reflectance，LSR）数据集，为气溶胶参数反演提供长期、稳定且具有时空一致性的地表反射率基准； （2）将辐射传输模型（Radiative Transfer Model，RTM）所描述的大气辐射传输机理引入注意力增强随机森林迁移学习（Attention-augmented Random Forest Transfer Learning，ARFTL）框架，构建物理机理与人工智能双驱动的反演模型。通过发挥物理模型在机理表达的优势，以及人工智能在复杂非线性关系建模和快速计算方面的能力，实现AOD、SSA、FMF等多种气溶胶参数的协同反演； （3）构建多维气溶胶分类（Multi-Dimensional Aerosol Fingerprint Classification，MDAFC）方法，综合表征不同气溶胶类型在光学特性、粒径结构、光谱响应及环境条件等方面的差异，建立多维气溶胶参数数据库。在此基础上，实现像元尺度气溶胶类型的动态识别，揭示不同类型气溶胶的长期时空演变特征。 本项目旨在突破高时空分辨率多气溶胶参数协同反演和像元尺度气溶胶类型动态识别中的关键技术瓶颈。预期形成一套物理机理与人工智能双驱动的气溶胶参数反演方法，开发长时间序列BRDF校正陆表反射率数据集和多维气溶胶参数数据库，生成长期、像元级动态气溶胶类型分布产品。相关成果将进一步提升卫星气溶胶遥感的参数反演能力和综合表征水平，为空气质量监测、气候模式评估与校准，以及大气环境管理和气候政策制定提供科学依据与数据支撑，并为香港及其他地区提升环境可持续发展能力和气候韧性提供技术支持。

15235126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15235126.value: 協作式超越對角型可重構智能表面輔助的無線通信：信道估計、本質極限及最優化

15235126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15235126.value: Wireless communication is a crucial component of the digital economy. Current fifth-generation (5G) wireless technologies will stimulate 13.2 trillion dollars in global sales activities by 2035 according to Qualcomm. Poised to embrace various immersive applications such as 16K/32K video streaming and extended reality (XR), sixth-generation (6G) wireless technologies are anticipated to further achieve a quantum leap in data rate. Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) has emerged in the past few years as a disruptive technology for data rate enhancement, due to its capability of proactively altering the wireless channel. The original form of RIS, or conventional diagonal RIS, has a strictly diagonal scattering matrix under unit-modulus constraints due to the lack of connections among its elements, and can only reflect signals within a half-space. Recently, beyond-diagonal RIS (BD-RIS) was developed as a new technology which overcomes these limitations. By adding inter-element connections via reconfigurable admittance components, BD-RIS enjoys a more general block-diagonal scattering matrix with each block being a unitary matrix, as well as 360-degree full-space coverage by mounting connected elements on both sides of the plane. Nevertheless, the capability of a single BD-RIS to change the channel is fundamentally limited by the number of elements therein, and the only single-scattered link that it can create. To unleash the full potential of wireless channel reconfiguration especially in rate-demanding and heavy-blockage scenarios, cooperation among multiple BD-RISs is necessary. This project will investigate a novel paradigm of cooperative BD-RISs aided communication, where multiple BD-RISs collaboratively change the wireless channel via both single-scattered links and multi-scattered links. The multi-scattered links provide new link diversity gains and offer opportunities for new multiplicative scattering gains with coherent scattering matrices designs. However, the complex signal flows among elements on each BD-RIS and through multiple BD-RISs pose new technical challenges in harnessing these gains. This project will conduct a comprehensive theoretical study to unveil and harvest the fundamental gains of cooperative BD-RISs aided communication. We will: i) establish a low-overhead cascaded channel estimation framework to enable coherent scattering matrices design, by innovatively exploiting essential channel correlations; ii) characterize fundamental capacity limits of cooperative BD-RISs aided single-antenna, multi-antenna, and multi-user channels via optimization and bounding techniques; iii) devise BD-RIS scattering strategies and optimization algorithms for wideband systems under the challenging frequency-dependent scattering model. The outcomes of this project are envisioned to lay a solid theoretical foundation for cooperative BD-RISs aided communication and pave the way for ultra-high-speed data transmission. 無線通信是數字經濟的重要組成部分。根據 Qualcomm 的資料，現行第五代（5G）無線技術預計將在 2035 年前帶動全球 13.2 兆美元的銷售活動。為迎接各種沉浸式應用，例如 16K/32K 影片串流與延展實境（XR），第六代（6G）無線技術有望進一步在信息傳輸速率上實現大幅躍升。近年來，具備主動改變無線信道能力的可重構智能表面（reconfigurable intelligent surface, RIS）已成為提升信息傳輸速率的一項顛覆性技術。RIS 的原始形式，即傳統對角型 RIS，由於其元件之間缺乏相互連接，因此其散射矩陣為嚴格的受恆模約束限制的對角矩陣，且其僅能在半空間內進行信號反射。最近，一項名為超越對角型可重構智能表面（beyond-diagonal RIS, BD-RIS）的新技術被提出，用以克服上述限制。通過引入由可重構導納實現的元件間連接，BD-RIS 具備更一般化的分塊對角散射矩陣，其中每個塊均為酉矩陣；此外，通過將相連元件安裝於平面的兩側，BD-RIS 可實現 360 度全空間覆蓋。然而，單個 BD-RIS 改變信道的能力從根本上受限於其內部元件數量，以及其所能建立的唯一單次散射鏈路。為了充分釋放無線信道重構的潛力，尤其是在傳輸速率要求高或環境遮擋嚴重的場景中，多個 BD-RIS 之間的協作是必要的。 本項目將研究一種由協作式 BD-RIS 輔助的新型通信範式，其中多個 BD-RIS 通過單次散射鏈路與多次散射鏈路協同改變無線信道。多次散射鏈路可提供新的鏈路分集增益，並通過相干散射矩陣設計帶來新的乘性散射增益機會。然而，每個 BD-RIS 上元件之間以及多個 BD-RIS 之間複雜的信號流動為實現這些增益帶來了新的技術挑戰。 本項目將進行全面性的理論研究，以揭示並獲取協作式 BD-RIS 輔助通信的本質增益。我們將：i) 通過創新性地挖掘與利用關鍵信道相關性，建立低開銷的級聯信道估計框架，以支持相干散射矩陣設計；ii) 通過最優化與定界技術，刻畫協作式 BD-RIS 輔助的單天線、多天線與多用戶信道的本質容量極限；iii) 在極具挑戰性的頻率依賴散射模型下，為寬帶系統設計 BD-RIS 散射策略與最優化算法。本項目的成果預計將為協作式 BD-RIS 輔助通信奠定堅實的理論基礎，並為超高速信息傳輸鋪平道路。

15236026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15236026.value: 污染大氣中硝酸鹽光解產生Cl2的機制研究

15236026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15236026.value: Chlorine (Cl) atoms are long known to destroy stratospheric ozone (O3), a beneficial trace gas that absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation in the stratosphere. In the lower atmosphere, however, Cl can play a contrasting role by increasing the production of O3 and secondary aerosols, which damage human health and affect the Earth’s climate. Molecular chlorine (Cl2) is an important Cl precursor; it can be photolyzed quickly to release two Cl atoms during the daytime. Recent studies have found elevated concentrations of Cl2 during daytime in multiple areas across China, including Hong Kong. These studies reveal the presence of a strong photolytic source and a large impact of Cl2 on the production of ozone and PM2.5 in Hong Kong and other polluted areas of China. Our previous research has shown strong evidence for Cl2 production from photodissociation of particulate nitrate. However, the underlying mechanisms of Cl2 formation remain uncertain, which hinders the prediction of Cl2 production and impact in major air quality models. This proposal aims to elucidate the detailed mechanisms and key factors governing Cl2 production from nitrate photolysis through an integrated approach combining advanced laboratory experiments and theoretical calculations. We will conduct photolysis experiments on both laboratory-generated and field-collected nitrate aerosols to identify the chemical and environmental parameters that influence Cl2 formation, and elucidate the role of HCl through heterogeneous reactions. Theoretical calculations, including quantum chemical calculations, classical molecular dynamics simulations, and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, will be employed to investigate the detailed reaction pathways and kinetics of nitrate photolysis in the bulk aqueous phase and at aerosol surfaces, providing molecular-level insights into the underlying mechanisms. By integrating experimental and theoretical results, we will develop a mechanistic parameterization of nitrate-driven chlorine activation and implement it into the widely used multiphase model RACM2-CAPRAM. The updated model will be validated using our historical Cl2 observations in polluted atmospheres to quantify the contribution of this pathway to ambient Cl2 levels. This study will advance the fundamental understanding of nitrate photolysis as a source of reactive chlorine in the troposphere. More importantly, it will improve the representation of multiphase halogen chemistry in atmospheric models, thereby enhancing their predictive capability for atmospheric oxidation capacity and secondary pollution formation. 氯（Cl）原子長期以來被認為是導致平流層臭氧（O3）損耗的重要活性物種，從而削弱平流層對有害紫外輻射的吸收與屏蔽作用。然而，在對流層大氣中，Cl原子則可能發揮截然不同的作用，可促進臭氧和二次氣溶膠的生成，危害人體健康並影響全球氣候。分子氯（Cl2）是Cl原子的重要前體物之一，在太陽輻射作用下能夠迅速光解並釋放兩個Cl原子。近期研究在包括香港在內的中國多個地區觀測到日間高濃度的Cl2，表明其在大氣中可能存在強烈的光化學來源。我們已開展的研究為顆粒態硝酸鹽光解產生Cl2提供了有力證據。然而，Cl2的具體生成機制目前仍不明確，制約了現有大氣化學模式對其生成及環境影響的準確描述與預測。 本研究擬結合先進的實驗室實驗與理論計算，闡明硝酸鹽光解產生Cl2的詳細機制及其關鍵影響因素。我們將對實驗室生成及外場採集的硝酸鹽氣溶膠開展光解實驗，識別影響Cl2生成的重要環境因素，通過非均相反應實驗闡明氯化氫（HCl）的作用。理論計算將包括量子化學計算和分子動力學模擬，用以研究硝酸鹽光解的詳細反應路徑與動力學，從分子層面揭示其作用機制。通過整合實驗與理論計算結果，我們將建立硝酸鹽驅動氯活化過程的機理參數化方案，並將其納入廣泛應用的多相化學模式 RACM2-CAPRAM。我們將利用過往在污染大氣中獲得的分子氯觀測資料驗證更新後的模式，定量評估該途徑對環境大氣中Cl2濃度的貢獻。本研究將深化對硝酸鹽光解作為對流層活性氯來源的基礎認識，改善大氣模式對多相鹵素化學過程的表徵，提升其對大氣氧化能力及二次污染形成的預測能力。

15236526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15236526.value: 基于实时健康状态估计与预测的复杂退化下车队级电池再分配与更换联合优化

15236526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15236526.value: Lithium-ion batteries have been widely used for Electric Vehicle (EV) and have a huge potential for the low altitude economy utilizing Electric Vertical Take-off and Landing Aircraft (EVTOL). Battery swapping has become one of the mainstream refuelling methods in fleet operations due to its short service time. However, battery heterogeneity and uneven workloads lead to divergent degradation. Most companies use batteries until retirement without reallocating them based on real-time health status, posing safety and reliability risks. Existing fleet-level reallocation studies often overlook complex battery degradation, accelerating overall degradation and raising operational costs. This project aims to develop a systematic framework for operators to optimize their reallocation and replacement decisions for batteries by considering batteries’ real-time health status and complex degradation. To achieve such an objective, the following challenges need to be tackled. First, real-time health assessment is difficult. Physical measurements are impractical, while data-driven methods often require complete charge/discharge curves under low current rates, which is hard to meet in real operations. Battery heterogeneity also limits model generalizability. Second, battery degradation is complex, involving coupled calendar and cycling aging. The coupling effect’s acceleration mechanism is not fully understood. Third, large-scale decision-making is challenging. With numerous batteries and task types, reallocation choices grow exponentially. Uncertainties in health estimation and degradation prediction further complicate decisions. To tackle the first challenge, we use probabilistic generative model, such as Gaussian mixture model, to represent the joint distribution of charge curves and health status, handling data incompleteness. Online model updating based on sufficient statistics is introduced to adapt to different batteries. For the second challenge, we employ hypothesis testing to verify this coupling effect and model degradation using Wiener process, with the coupling effect represented as a stress factor via a shape-constrained non-parametric function. For the third challenge, we formulate the problem as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process and develop a solution based on Centralized Training with Decentralized Execution. This study is among the first to offer a systematic methodology for fleet-level battery reallocation and replacement, based on real-time health estimation and degradation prediction. It helps extend battery life, reduce costs, and enhance operational safety and reliability. The findings will be integrated into an engineering asset management framework to support practical decision-making. 锂离子电池不仅在电动汽车（EV）领域应用广泛，在利用电动垂直起降飞行器（eVTOL）发展低空经济方面也蕴藏着巨大潜力。由于换电模式耗时短，它已成为车队运营的主流补能方式之一。然而，电池的个体差异和不均衡的工作负荷会导致它们的退化程度出现分化。目前，大多数公司在电池退役前都不会根据其实时健康状态进行重新分配，这带来了安全和可靠性隐患。而现有的车队级电池重新分配研究往往忽略了复杂的电池退化机制，这不仅会加速电池整体老化，还会推高运营成本。 本项目旨在开发一套系统性的框架，帮助运营商在综合考量电池实时健康状态与复杂退化规律的前提下，优化电池的重新分配与更换决策。为实现这一目标，我们需要攻克以下三大挑战： 首先是实时健康评估的难题。物理测量在实际操作中并不现实，而数据驱动的方法通常需要完整的低倍率充放电曲线，这在真实运营场景中很难满足。此外，电池的个体差异也限制了模型的泛化能力。其次是电池退化的复杂性。这涉及日历老化与循环老化的耦合效应，而目前对这种耦合加速机制的理解尚不充分。第三是大规模决策的困难。面对海量的电池和多样化的任务类型，重新分配的选择呈指数级增长。再加上健康评估与退化预测中存在的诸多不确定性，让决策变得更为棘手。 针对第一个挑战，我们采用概率生成模型（如高斯混合模型）来表征充电曲线与健康状态的联合分布，从而解决数据不完整的问题。同时，引入基于充分统计量的在线模型更新机制，以适应不同电池的特性。针对第二个挑战，我们运用假设检验来验证这种耦合效应，并利用维纳过程（Wiener process）对退化过程进行建模，通过形状约束的非参数函数将耦合效应转化为应力因子。针对第三个挑战，我们将该问题构建为去中心化部分可观测马尔可夫决策过程（Dec-POMDP），并开发了基于“集中训练、分散执行”（CTDE）的求解算法。 本研究率先提出了一套基于实时健康评估与退化预测的车队级电池重新分配与更换系统性方法。该方法有助于延长电池寿命、降低成本，并提升运营的安全性和可靠性。相关研究成果将被整合到工程资产管理框架中，以支持实际的决策制定。

15237226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15237226.value: 带有输入约束的部分观测正倒向随机系统的最优控制及其金融应用

15237226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15237226.value: Partially observed optimal stochastic control problems have important applications across a wide range of fields, including science, engineering, economics, and financial investment. In recent years, there has been a surge of interest in studying these problems and exploring their practical applications. While significant progress has been made in the analysis of partially observed stochastic dynamic systems without input constraints, new challenges arise in financial investment models, particularly when input constraints and backward systems (such as those encountered in option pricing) are present. This situation highlights the urgent need for research on partially observed forward-backward stochastic systems with input constraints and random coefficients. The introduction of both input constraints and random coefficients brings major technical difficulties, including the failure of many existing methods due to increased randomness and complexity. In this research proposal, we aim to investigate optimal control problems for partially observed forward-backward stochastic systems with control input constraints, motivated by practical challenges in financial investment. Although fully observed stochastic control problems with input constraints have been extensively studied, the partially observed case, especially for forward-backward systems, remains largely unexplored, despite its significance in finance, engineering, and economics. Our research is structured in three parts: First, we will develop a rigorous theoretical foundation for the optimal control of partially observed forward-backward stochastic systems with random coefficients and input constraints. This will involve the use of Girsanov’s transformation, Ekeland’s variational principle, and projection analysis to derive necessary and sufficient stochastic maximum principles. Second, we will focus on stochastic linear-quadratic optimal control problems for partially observed forward-backward linear systems with quadratic cost functionals and linear input constraints. This includes analyzing the associated backward stochastic differential Riccati equations and developing efficient numerical algorithms for their solution. Third, we will apply these theoretical advances to continuous-time mean-semi-variance portfolio selection problems under partial observation and no-shorting constraints, addressing practical issues such as capital flows and random market dynamics. This model is expected to help investors better understand and manage risk, enabling them to achieve higher returns over a finite investment horizon. Overall, by bridging advanced stochastic control theory with real-world financial applications, this project aims to provide new insights and effective strategies for portfolio management under uncertainty and constraints. 部分观测最优随机控制问题在科学、工程、经济学和金融投资等广泛领域中具有重要应用。近年来，学术界对研究这类问题及其实际应用表现出日益浓厚的兴趣。尽管在不含输入约束的部分观测随机动态系统分析方面已经取得了显著进展，但在金融投资模型中，尤其是当存在输入约束以及后向系统时，例如期权定价中出现的后向系统，新的挑战随之产生。这一现状凸显了研究带有输入约束和随机系数的部分观测正倒向随机系统的迫切需求。输入约束和随机系数的同时引入带来了重大的技术困难，包括由于随机性和复杂性的增加，许多现有方法不再适用。在本研究计划中，我们拟以金融投资中的实际挑战为动机，研究带有控制输入约束的部分观测正倒向随机系统的最优控制问题。尽管带有输入约束的完全观测随机控制问题已经得到了广泛研究，但部分观测情形，尤其是正倒向系统的部分观测最优控制问题，仍然在很大程度上尚未被充分探索，尽管其在金融、工程和经济学中具有重要意义。 我们的研究分为三个部分：第一，我们将为带有随机系数和输入约束的部分观测正倒向随机系统的最优控制建立严格的理论基础。这将涉及使用 Girsanov 变换、Ekeland 变分原理以及投影分析，推导随机最大值原理的必要条件和充分条件。第二，我们将重点研究部分观测正倒向线性系统的随机线性二次最优控制问题，其中成本泛函为二次型，并带有线性输入约束。这包括分析相关的倒向随机微分 Riccati 方程，并开发用于求解这些方程的高效数值算法。第三，我们将把这些理论进展应用于部分观测和禁止卖空约束下的连续时间均值-半方差投资组合选择问题，处理资本流动和随机市场动态等实际问题。该模型有望帮助投资者更好地理解和管理风险，使其能够在有限投资期限内获得更高收益。 总体而言，本项目旨在将先进的随机控制理论与现实金融应用相结合，为不确定性和约束条件下的投资组合管理提供新的见解和有效策略。

15238426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15238426.value: 基於主動式防禦之區塊鏈 Rollup 生態系安全加固研究

15238426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15238426.value: Rollups are becoming the backbone of scalable blockchain systems: total value locked in major Ethereum rollups now exceeds $50B, and their throughput reaches up to 20× Ethereum’s main chain. Yet their growing complexity introduces new security risks, and their thriving ecosystems attract diverse attacks. At the same time, because all rollup transactions pass through the sequencer, it is well positioned to mount effective defenses. Although many studies assess the security of layer‑1 (L1) blockchains and their smart contracts, few examine vulnerabilities in rollup platforms, and no systematic study of rollup ecosystem security exists. Existing work struggles to handle the complexity of modern rollups, relies heavily on manual analysis, and either misses advanced malicious contracts or fails to leverage the sequencer’s vantage point for proactive defense. In this project, we take a first step toward filling in this gap by proposing novel methods and building practical systems to fortify rollup ecosystems through proactive defenses. First, we will develop new methods to systematically uncover weaknesses that threaten rollup availability and reliability, and to detect soundness and completeness issues in zero-knowledge virtual machines (zkVMs) used by zkRollups—bugs that can permit invalid state transitions or reject valid ones. Second, to counter advanced malicious smart contracts, we will assess whether existing machine-learning detectors can be bypassed and, if so, design robust defenses. We will also analyze code deltas between contract versions to identify “Trojan updates” that introduce malicious behavior. Our techniques will enable sequencer-side screening as soon as a contract deployment or update transaction is received. Third, to protect DeFi—the dominant class of rollup applications—we will propose novel approaches to accelerate MEV risk assessment and detect exploitable weaknesses in DeFi applications. This research will deliver new systematic methodologies for uncovering security issues in rollup platforms, sequencer‑integrated proactive defenses against malicious smart contracts and updates, and practical risk assessment tools for DeFi. Together, these advances will raise the security baseline of rollup ecosystems, inform best practices and standards, and deliver safer, more trustworthy blockchain infrastructure for users and developers. The project will yield publications in top‑tier venues and train the next generation of experts in blockchain and security. Rollup 正逐渐成为可扩展区块链系统的骨干支柱，例如以太坊 Rollup 的总锁仓量（TVL）目前已突破 500 亿美元，其吞吐量达到了以太坊主链的 20 倍。然而，其日益增加的复杂性引发了新的安全风险，繁荣的生态系统也吸引了各式各样的攻击。与此同时，由于所有 Rollup 交易都需要经过排序器（Sequencer），这使得排序器具备了部署有效防御措施的绝佳位置优势。 尽管现有许多研究评估了L1区块链及其智能合约的安全性，但鲜有研究探讨 Rollup 平台自身的漏洞，针对 Rollup 生态系统安全性的系统性研究更是空白。现有的工作难以应对现代 Rollup 的复杂性，过度依赖人工分析，且要么遗漏了复杂的恶意智能合约，要么未能充分利用排序器的位置优势来进行主动防御。 在本项目中，我们通过提出创新方法并构建实用系统，以主动防御来强化 Rollup 生态系统安全，迈出了填补这一空白的第一步。首先，我们将开发新方法，系统性地挖掘威胁 Rollup 可用性和可靠性的弱点，并检测 zkRollup 所使用的zkVM的可靠性（Soundness）与完备性（Completeness）问题——这些漏洞可导致允许无效的状态转移，或拒绝有效的状态转移。其次，为了对抗複雜恶意智能合约，我们将评估现有的机器学习检测器能否被绕过；若存在被绕过的风险，我们将设计更健壯的防御机制。我们还将分析合约版本之间的代码差异，以识别引入恶意行为的後門更新。我们的技术将在合约部署或更新的第一时间内，利用排序器的優勢來审查。第三，为了保护 Rollup 中最主要的应用——去中心化金融（DeFi），我们将提出全新方法来加速 MEV风险评估，并检测 DeFi 应用中可被利用的漏洞。 本研究将提供一套用于發現Rollup 平台安全隐患的新型系统性方法论、集成于排序器的针对恶意智能合约及更新的主动防御机制，以及面向 DeFi 的实用风险评估工具。这些研究成果将提升 Rollup 生态系统的安全基线，指导最佳实践与标准的制定，并为用户和开发者提供更安全、更值得信赖的区块链基础设施。此外，该项目将在顶尖学术平台发表研究成果，并为区块链与安全领域培养新一代专业人才。

15238526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15238526.value: 面向智能體的隱私代理智能體研究

15238526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15238526.value: The rapid emergence of Agentic AI systems, which perform complex, multi-step tasks autonomously by interacting with various tools and data sources, presents a profound and unprecedented privacy challenge. Unlike single-query models, these agents operate over extended contexts, making iterative API calls and processing vast amounts of potentially sensitive personal information. This continuous data ingestion creates an expansive attack surface for privacy violations, including membership inference, attribute inference, and data reconstruction attacks. Current privacy-preserving techniques, predominantly designed for static datasets or single model inferences, are ill-suited to the dynamic, sequential, and compositional nature of agentic workflows. This research proposes the design, development, and evaluation of a "Privacy Agent" — a novel, dedicated AI agent that acts as a proactive guardian for user privacy within an Agentic AI system. The core of this research is to develop an autonomous and adaptive agent system that: (1) perceives privacy violations through contextual integrity graphs and sensitive attention heads, (2) mitigates them with synthetic data generated by differentially private (DP) finetuned LLMs using personal data, and (3) balances privacy-usability through RLHF-based parameter optimization on latent user preferences. In essence, this project will pioneer a holistic framework where the Privacy Agent intelligently selects from a portfolio of new privacy-enhancing technologies (PETs) for privacy perception, protection, and utility enhancement. In particular, this framework will synergistically combine new DP finetuning methods such as DP-LoRA and DP-finetuned MoE models, with new usable privacy methods such as contextual integrity graph learning, and synthetic data generation in the context of AI agent systems. By minimum assumption on the agent’s types and tasks, the framework is general and can adapt to future generation of Agentic AI. With our extensive research experience in data privacy (especially differential privacy), LLM privacy, and adversarial machine learning, we believe this project will successfully contribute to the privacy foundation for Agentic AI, providing a scalable, adaptive, and formally-grounded architecture for preserving user privacy in the age of Agentic AI. We also expect this project to spark endeavors in related research fields, from retrieval-augmented generation to AI wellbeing, where user privacy is crucial. The outcomes will benefit the research community, the AI industry, and Hong Kong, which aims to be a “world-class smart city” as outlined in the government’s blueprint. 智能體系統的快速湧現帶來了深刻而全新的隱私挑戰。這類系統能夠透過與各種工具和資料來源交互，自主執行複雜的多步驟任務。與單查詢模型不同，智能體在擴展的上下文中運行，進行迭代式 API 調用，並處理大量潛在的敏感個人資訊。這種持續的資料攝取為隱私侵犯創造了廣闊的攻擊面，包括成員推斷、屬性推論和資料重構攻擊。目前主要針對靜態資料集或單一模型推斷設計的隱私保護技術，並不適用於智能體工作流程的動態、順序和組合特性。 本研究提出設計、開發和評估一種「隱私代理」——一種新型的專用智能體，旨在主動守護智能體生態系統中的用戶隱私。本研究的核心是開發一個自主自適應的智能體系統，該系統能夠：(1) 利用上下文完整性圖和敏感注意力頭感知隱私侵犯；(2) 利用基於個人數據的差分隱私 (DP) 微調（MoE 或 DP-LoRA）LLM 生成的合成數據來緩解基於隱私侵犯；(3) 透過基於 RLHF 的參數優化，在用戶偏好的基礎上平衡性和隱私性侵犯；(3) 在用戶偏好的基礎上進行基於 RLHF 的參數優化。 本項目將開創一個整體框架，使隱私智能體能夠從一系列隱私增強技術 (PET) 中進行智慧選擇，以實現隱私感知、保護和效用提升。該框架將 DP-LoRA 和 DP 微調 MoE 模型等新型 DP 方法與上下文完整性圖學習和合成資料生成等新型可用隱私方法在智能體系統的背景下協同結合。由於對智能體的類型和任務的假設極少，該框架具有通用性，並能適應未來一代智能體人工智慧的發展。 憑藉我們在資料隱私（特別是差分隱私）、LLM隱私和對抗性機器學習領域的豐富研究經驗，我們相信本項目將成功為智能體的隱私基礎做出貢獻，為智能體時代的用戶隱私保護提供可擴展、自適應且形式化的架構。我們也期望本項目能激發相關研究領域的探索，例如檢索增強生成和人工智慧福祉等，在這些領域，使用者隱私至關重要。計畫成果將惠及研究界、人工智能產業以及香港——香港正致力於成為政府藍圖中規劃的「世界級智慧城市」。

15239026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15239026.value: 基於多模態數據融合的震後性能定量預測數字孿生框架

15239026.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15239026.value: Prof WEN, Chih-Yung Prof Xia, Yong

15239026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15239026.value: Rapid and reliable post-earthquake building assessments are often hindered by subjective visual inspections and sparse measurements, leading to delays in recovery and unnecessary social and economic costs. This project proposes a transformative approach by advancing a predictive digital twin—a physics-based computational model calibrated to a structure’s post-damage condition through fused multimodal sensing (accelerations, video, and UAV imagery). By converting heterogeneous, raw measurements into validated structural response estimates and damage states, the framework aims to shift post event evaluation from ad hoc judgment to defensible, data-driven decision-making. The integrated methodology addresses three critical research gaps: 1. Physics-informed data fusion: We will employ structured matrix completion to fuse sparse accelerometer records with dense, video-derived motion fields, yielding spatially continuous, high resolution dynamic properties (natural frequencies and full-field mode shapes) accurate in both space and time. 2. Automated damage quantification: We will develop a semantic to mechanical pipeline that applies a fine-tuned deep learning model to UAV-based 3D reconstructions (Structure-from-Motion) to detect and quantify damage, translating geometric indicators into engineering parameters such as localized stiffness and strength loss. A large-scale experimental benchmark will link visual metrics to mechanical degradation, producing a machine readable, mechanically quantified 3D damage map for direct model integration. 3. Hierarchical hybrid model updating: We will embed quantified local damage into a nonlinear finite-element model and then calibrate global parameters against the fused dynamic response using constrained particle swarm optimization, producing a unified model consistent with all multimodal evidence. The framework will be rigorously validated through multi-phase shake-table experiments on a large-scale reinforced-concrete specimen, culminating in a blind-prediction protocol that compares digital-twin forecasts with withheld measurements. Upon validation, the project will release open-source software, a public multimodal benchmark dataset, and actionable safety metrics (including residual drift, aftershock collapse probability, and recovery time). This project will directly enable a paradigm shift toward faster, safer, and more resilient post-disaster recovery. 建築結構震後性能評估的效率與可靠性往往受限於主觀目視檢查和測量數據稀疏等因素，不僅延緩災後恢復進程，還可能造成不必要的社會與經濟損失。本項目擬研發一種預測型數字孿生，為解決上述問題提供變革性技術路徑。該數字孿生以物理機理模型為核心，通過融合加速度、視頻及無人機影像等多模態感知數據，依據結構震後損傷狀態對計算模型進行校准。通過將異構原始數據轉化為經驗證的結構響應與損傷狀態估計，本項目旨在推動震後評估由依賴經驗的主觀判斷轉向科學、可靠且可追溯的數據驅動決策。 本項目將重點解決以下三個關鍵科學問題： 1. 物理信息驅動的多模態數據融合 本項目將采用結構化矩陣補全方法，融合稀疏的加速度傳感器記錄與基於視頻提取的高密度運動場數據，重構空間連續、高分辨率的結構動態響應，進而准確識別結構自振頻率和全場振型等動力特性，實現結構響應在時間與空間維度上的高精度表征。 2. 基於機器視覺的結構損傷自動量化 本項目將構建從損傷語義識別到力學參數量化的分析流程。利用微調後的深度學習模型，對基於無人機影像和運動恢復結構技術生成的三維重建模型進行分析，實現結構損傷的自動檢測與定量表征，並將損傷幾何特征轉化為局部剛度折減、強度退化等工程力學參數。 同時，本項目將依托大尺度結構試驗建立基准數據庫，揭示視覺損傷指標與結構力學性能退化之間的定量映射關系，最終生成機器可讀、力學參數化的三維損傷圖譜，為損傷信息直接嵌入計算模型提供支撐。 3. 分層混合模型更新 本項目將首先把量化後的局部損傷信息嵌入非線性有限元模型，隨後采用約束粒子群優化算法，基於融合後的結構動力響應對模型全局參數進行校准，最終構建與多模態觀測數據相一致的統一數字孿生模型，實現局部損傷識別與整體結構響應校准的有機融合。 本項目將通過大型鋼筋混凝土試件的多階段振動台試驗，對所提出的理論方法與技術框架進行系統驗證。在研究後期，將采用盲預測驗證方案，把數字孿生模型的預測結果與未參與模型校准的實測數據進行對比，以客觀評估其預測精度與可靠性。 項目將研发相应軟件、形成多模態基准數據集，並提供可直接服務於結構安全決策的性能指標，包括殘余層間位移角、余震作用下的倒塌概率及災後恢復時間等。項目預期推動建築結構震後性能評估由經驗驅動向數據與物理機理協同驅動轉變，為實現更加快速、安全且具有韌性的災後恢復提供理論基礎與技術支撐。

15239126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15239126.value: 基于现场监测、试验测试与数值模拟的大跨度钢桥多场耦合效应下腐蚀疲劳行为研究

15239126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15239126.value: Dr Fan, Zhihong Dr Ma, Yan

15239126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15239126.value: Steel bridges experience the combined actions of corrosion and alternating loads during operation, leading to fatigue damage, accelerated corrosion, and eventual component cracking or failure. This phenomenon, known as corrosion–fatigue, exhibits a complex coupling effect that substantially weakens bridge durability and safety. However, most current research focuses on separated corrosion and fatigue behaviors of steel bridges, neglecting their coupling effects, which may lead to an underestimation of crack growth risks and impacts on service life. Additionally, most corrosion–fatigue experimental tests are conducted on material or small-scale specimens in accelerated corrosive environments, lacking a clear correlation to the actual corrosion–fatigue behavior of bridges. Furthermore, while structural health monitoring (SHM) technologies have been developed to assess performance of long-span bridges, most SHM systems have only several years of data, failing to capture the corrosion–fatigue process that may take decades. This project aims to investigate the multifield coupling of corrosion–fatigue behavior and the performance degradation of long-span steel bridges by integrating super-long-term field monitoring data, experimental tests, and advanced simulations. The Hong Kong Tsing Ma Bridge, equipped with a real-time SHM system since 1997, will serve as the testbed. (1) Corrosion–fatigue coupling laboratory tests will be conducted on full-scale truncated rib-to-deck specimens to analyze corrosion–fatigue behavior and identify key influencing factors. (2) Mechanical–chemical–thermal coupling analyses of the tested specimens will be conducted and validated by test data to reveal the corrosion–fatigue degradation mechanism and establish a multiphysics response–thickness loss analytical model. (3) The multiphysics response–thickness loss analytical model will be applied to the Tsing Ma Bridge and finetuned from the SHM data. By integrating the finetuned analytical model and global finite element model of the bridge, a comprehensive predictive framework will be established to predict the corrosion–fatigue performance of the bridge. (4) Long-term condition prognosis of the bridge’s behavior will be conducted progressively by updating structural damage, thickness reduction, and crack growth within the predictive framework. As monitoring progresses, additional data will be collected, allowing the predictive framework to be continuously updated. Consequently, condition assessment and prognosis of corrosion–fatigue performance of the Tsing Ma Bridge will become more and more accurate. It serves as a valuable reference for the durability assessment and maintenance optimization of similar long-span steel bridges under varying service environments. 钢桥在服役期间承受腐蚀与交变荷载的共同作用，导致疲劳损伤、腐蚀加速，并最终引发构件开裂或失效。这种“腐蚀-疲劳”的现象呈现出复杂的耦合效应，显著削弱了桥梁的耐久性与安全性。 然而，目前大多数该领域的研究将钢桥的腐蚀与疲劳行为独立分析，忽视了二者的耦合效应，这可能低估了对裂纹扩展风险及使用寿命影响。此外，大多数腐蚀-疲劳试验是在加速腐蚀环境下材料级或小尺寸试件上进行的，缺乏与桥梁结构级别实际腐蚀-疲劳行为的明确关联。再者，尽管结构健康监测技术已用于评估大跨度桥梁的性能，但多数结构健康监测系统仅积累了数年的数据，无法捕捉可能历时数十年的腐蚀-疲劳演化过程。 本项目旨在通过整合超长期现场监测数据、试验研究和数值模拟，探究大跨度钢桥腐蚀-疲劳行为的多场耦合机理及其性能退化规律。本研究将采用香港青马大桥（自1997年起配备实时SHM系统）作为依托工程。 (1) 针对足尺截断式“加劲肋-桥面板”连接试件开展腐蚀-疲劳耦合试验，分析其腐蚀-疲劳行为并识别关键影响因素。 (2) 对试验试件进行力学-化学-热耦合分析，并利用试验数据进行验证，以揭示腐蚀-疲劳退化机理，建立多物理场响应与厚度损失之间的解析模型。 (3) 将该多物理场响应-厚度损失解析模型应用于青马大桥，并利用结构健康监测数据进行参数修正。通过整合修正后的解析模型与桥梁整体有限元模型，构建综合预测框架，以评估桥梁的腐蚀-疲劳性能。 (4) 在预测框架内动态更新结构损伤、厚度减薄及裂纹扩展信息，对桥梁行为进行长期的状态演化预测。 随着监测工作的持续推进，将不断采集新的数据，从而实现预测框架的持续更新与优化。因此，对青马大桥腐蚀疲劳性能的状态评估与预测将变得愈发准确，为不同服役环境下类似大跨度钢桥的耐久性评估及维护优化提供了宝贵的参考。

15239526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15239526.value: 一種利用可移動壓電傳感器測量混凝土板原位強度的新型無基線檢測技術

15239526.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15239526.value: Prof Marzani, Alessandro Prof Poon, Chi Sun

15239526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15239526.value: Concrete is the backbone of modern construction and extensively used in buildings, bridges, roads, and other infrastructure. The mechanical properties of concrete (such as compressive strength, modulus of elasticity, etc.) are critical parameters determining the integrity and longevity of concrete structures. Evaluating these concrete properties plays a vital role throughout both the construction and maintenance phases. For instance, during construction, regular assessment of concrete compressive strength is necessary to ensure construction quality and compliance with relevant standards. Timely and precise determination of early-age concrete strength directly informs key engineering decisions, such as formwork removal, application of post-tension, and progression to the next construction stages. Conversely, any inaccurate estimation may result in premature loading, leading to excessive cracking and deflection, and ultimately compromising structural durability and safety. Industrial standard testing methods include compressive testing on field-cured specimens (such as standard concrete cubes or cylinders) or drilled cores from existing concrete elements. These tests are generally performed in laboratories using specialized compressive testing machines, rather than directly on-site, resulting in costly and inefficient processes. Furthermore, the inherently destructive nature of core testing makes it unsuitable for widespread applications across entire structures, preventing comprehensive assessment of spatial variability in concrete strength. Therefore, developing a rapid, accurate, and mobile nondestructive testing (NDT) technique suitable for in-place non-intrusive measurement of concrete strength is highly desirable in the global construction industry. While various NDT techniques have been introduced to characterize concrete properties, most are limited to small-sized concrete specimens in laboratories and are not readily applicable to full-scale structural elements. Some NDT techniques have seen in-place measurement applications, such as rebound hammer and ultrasonic pulse velocity methods for surface hardness and pulse velocity, respectively. However, their indirect estimation of concrete strength lacks sufficient accuracy. As a result, the above-mentioned testing of standard specimens and drilled cores remains the dominant approaches, despite their inherent limitations. The proposed project aims to develop a novel baseline-free (BF) electromechanical impedance (EMI) technique for evaluating in-place strength of concrete slabs by leveraging the capability of movable piezoelectric sensors. This new NDT technique, termed movable BF-EMI, represents a paradigm shift from traditional baseline-dependent EMI methods to baseline-free methods. It is particularly suitable for in-place assessment of concrete slabs and offers a versatile tool for characterizing modulus of elasticity, Poisson’s ratio, and compressive strength. The anticipated outcome of this project will be a promising alternative to conventional semi-destructive core testing methods. 混凝土被廣泛應用於建築、橋樑、道路等基礎設施，其抗壓強度、彈性模量等力學性能直接關係到結構安全與耐久性。在施工和維護階段，準確評估混凝土力學特性對品質控制、模板拆除、後續施工決策具有重要意義；若估算不准，可能導致過早加載並引發開裂、大變形和耐久性問題。而現行標準方法主要依賴現場養護試件抗壓試驗或原位鑽芯測試，通常只能在實驗室完成，成本高、效率低；同時鑽芯本身具有破壞性，只能少量進行，難以全面反映結構中混凝土強度的空間差異。 因此，發展快速、準確、便攜且適用於現場的無損檢測技術十分必要。儘管傳統無損檢測技術如回彈法、超聲脈衝速度法等已有應用，但其對混凝土強度的間接估算精度仍有限，上述標準試件和鑽芯測試因而仍占主導地位。本項目擬開發一種基於可移動壓電傳感器的新型無基綫機電阻抗技術，用於混凝土板原位強度評估。該方法有望實現對彈性模量、泊松比和抗壓強度的無損表徵，並為傳統半破壞性鑽芯測試提供可靠替代方案。

15239826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15239826.value: 用於極端熱管理的純銅的微尺度增材制造

15239826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15239826.value: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and High-Performance Computing (HPC) is facing a critical physical bottleneck: heat. Next-generation AI chips, such as NVIDIA's Rubin, will exceed 2000W of power, generating unprecedented heat and rendering traditional air-cooling obsolete. To solve this power density crisis, the industry is urgently shifting to Micro-Channel Liquid Cooling Plates (MLCP)- metal plates with fine internal channels mounted directly on the chip. However, current manufacturing methods (e.g., skiving or etching) are limited to simple 2D parallel channels, which are at their thermal limit and cannot produce theoretically superior, complex 3D structures like bio-inspired or TPMS lattices. 3D printing is the only technology capable of fabricating these complex 3D structures. However, existing metal 3D printing techniques for pure copper (the best thermal conductor) suffer from low precision (only ~100 microns) and insufficient material density. This project aims to establish a world-leading platform for the micro-scale 3D printing of pure copper to manufacture revolutionary, high-performance heat exchangers. We are not starting from zero; our lab has already established the core end-to-end printing process for pure copper, reliably producing components with 97% relative density and 94% IACS conductivity, placing us at the field forefront. Building on this strong foundation, this project will solve the final critical engineering science problems. First, we will engineer a novel copper nanocomposite slurry and pioneer an effective light-field feedback printing system. This system will use co-axial vision monitoring to actively compensate for light scattering in real-time, pushing printing resolution from our current 80 microns to below 10 microns. Concurrently, we will establish fundamental sintering science for these micro-structures. This will allow us to precisely control the material's densification process, increasing the relative density from 97% to >99% and conductivity to >99% IACS, matching the performance of wrought copper. Finally, we will integrate this platform to fabricate and validate a high-performance micro-heat exchanger featuring complex 3D lattices or bio-inspired design. The success of this project will create a key technological advantage for Hong Kong in the AI hardware and advanced manufacturing sectors, addressing a critical need for next-generation chip development. 人工智能（AI）与高性能计算（HPC）的飞速发展正面临一个严峻的物理瓶颈：散热问题。以英伟达（NVIDIA）Rubin架构为代表的下一代AI芯片，功耗将突破2000瓦，产生前所未有的热量，传统的风冷技术已无法胜任。 为了解决这一功率密度危机，业界正迫切转向微通道液冷板（MLCP）技术，即将内部带有精细流道的金属板直接贴合在芯片上。然而，现有的制造工艺（如铲齿或蚀刻）仅能加工简单的二维平行流道，其散热性能已达物理极限，无法制造出理论上更优的复杂三维结构（如仿生结构或TPMS三周期极小曲面晶格）。目前，3D打印是唯一能够制造这类复杂三维结构的技术。 不过，现有的纯铜（导热性能最佳的材料）金属3D打印技术存在精度低（仅约100微米）和材料致密度不足的问题。本项目旨在建立一个全球领先的纯铜微纳3D打印平台，用于制造革命性的高性能热交换器。 我们并非从零起步。目前，我们实验室已成功打通纯铜端到端打印的核心工艺，能够稳定制造出相对密度达97%、导电率达94% IACS（国际退火铜标准）的部件，处于该领域的前沿水平。 依托这一坚实基础，本项目将攻克最后的关键工程科学难题： 首先，我们将研发新型铜纳米复合浆料，并首创高效的光场反馈打印系统。该系统将通过同轴视觉监测，实时主动补偿光散射效应，将打印分辨率从目前的80微米提升至10微米以下。 同时，我们将建立针对这些微结构的底层烧结科学理论，从而精确控制材料的致密化过程，将相对密度从97%提升至99%以上，导电率提升至99% IACS以上，使其性能媲美锻压铜。 最后，我们将整合该平台，制造并验证一款采用复杂三维晶格或仿生设计的高性能微热交换器。 该项目的成功将为香港在AI硬件和先进制造领域确立关键的技术优势，满足下一代芯片研发的迫切需求。

15240226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15240226.value: 基於機率型人工智慧-物理融合預報的登陸熱帶氣旋災前風險評估研究

15240226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15240226.value: Prof Xia, Yong Prof ZHANG, Jize

15240226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15240226.value: Tropical cyclones (TCs) are among the most destructive weather phenomena, posing severe threats to human lives and property. The Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Great Bay Area (GBA), one of the most typhoon-prone regions worldwide, is frequently affected by landfalling TCs originating in the western North Pacific. With global warming projected to increase the occurrence frequency, peak intensity, and duration of strong TCs, there is an urgent need for reliable, high-resolution, real-time wind field forecasts to support effective pre-disaster risk assessment and management. In recent decades, the accuracy of TC track forecasting over short lead times has substantially improved due to major advancements in global numerical weather prediction (NWP) models. Additionally, newly developed AI-based global models have shown considerable potential to compete with conventional physics-based NWP models. However, both traditional and AI-based global models face limitations due to their coarse spatiotemporal resolution, restricting their capability to accurately assess TC intensity. In contrast, high-resolution regional weather forecasting models have demonstrated advantages in resolving this problem, motivating the development of AI-physics hybrid modelling. Despite these advances, current AI-physics hybrid models remain deterministic and lack clear guidance on selecting optimal AI models for forecasting landfalling TCs under diverse scenarios. Given the chaotic nature of the complex Earth system, TC behaviour is inherently uncertain. Effective pre-hazard risk assessment and management, such as evaluating the structural performance of civil infrastructure and ensuring the driving safety of road vehicles, requires uncertainty-aware forecasts of wind conditions. Moreover, previous model evaluations simply treated all TC events as a homogeneous group, overlooking potential variations due to landfalling behaviour and irregular tracks. This project will address these gaps through the following tasks. (1) Identify the best-performing deterministic AI-based models for global weather forecasting of landfalling TCs through comprehensive categorical performance evaluation; (2) Develop and validate the physics-constrained perturbation strategy, and integrate it with the optimal deterministic AI models and the robust WRF-based regional model to establish the probabilistic AI-physics hybrid forecasting system; (3) Forecast probability-based, time-evolving, high-resolution local wind fields under ensemble forecasts, and demonstrate the system’s practical value through case studies on structural performance and traffic management for the Tsing Ma Bridge. This proposed research aims to deliver a reliable and uncertainty-aware local weather forecasting system to mitigate TC-induced risks.
