Its success will deepen our understanding of TC dynamics and provide high-resolution probabilistic forecasts, contributing to a smart, climate-resilient, and sustainable society in the GBA region. 熱帶氣旋是最具破壞性的天氣現象之一，對人民生命財產安全構成嚴重威脅。粵港澳大灣區是全球受颱風影響最頻繁的地區之一，經常受到源自西北太平洋並登陸的熱帶氣旋影響。隨著全球暖化，強烈熱帶氣旋的發生頻率、峰值強度及持續時間預計將進一步增加，因此，亟需發展可靠、高解析度、即時的風場預報技術，為災前風險評估與管理提供有效支撐。 近幾十年來，隨著全球數值天氣預報（NWP）模式的快速發展，短預報時效下熱帶氣旋路徑預報的準確性得到了顯著提升。同時，新近發展的以人工智慧（AI）為基礎的全球天氣預報模型展現出與NWP模式競爭的巨大潛力。然而，無論傳統全球NWP模式或AI全球預報模型，均受到較粗時空解析度的限制，限制了其對熱帶氣旋強度的準確刻畫。相較之下，高解析度區域天氣預報模式在解決此問題上展現出明顯優勢，由此推動了AI與區域物理模式融合預報方法的發展。 儘管取得了上述進展，現有AI-物理融合預報模型仍主要採用確定性預報方式，對於不同情境下登陸熱帶氣旋預報中如何選擇最優AI模型，尚缺乏明確的指導。鑑於複雜地球系統所具有的混沌特性，熱帶氣旋的演變過程本身就具有顯著的不確定性。對於大型土木基礎設施結構性能評估、道路車輛行車安全保障等災前風險評估與管理而言，需要能夠充分錶徵不確定性的風環境預報結果。此外，已有模型評估通常將所有熱帶氣旋事件視為同一類型進行統一分析，忽略了不同登陸特徵及異常路徑可能導致的預報表現差異。 針對上述問題，本計畫擬進行以下研究： （1）透過系統的分類性能評估，識別並遴選適用於登陸熱帶氣旋全球天氣預報的最優確定性AI模型； （2）發展並驗證物理限制的擾動策略，與最優確定性AI模型及穩健的WRF區域模式融合，建構機率型AI-物理融合天氣預報系統； （3）基於集合預報進行機率型、時變、高解析度局部風場預測，並以青馬大橋結構性能與交通管理為工程案例，驗證所建立預報系統的實際應用價值。 本計畫旨在建立一套可靠、能夠表徵不確定性的局部天氣預報系統，以降低熱帶氣旋災害所造成的潛在風險。計畫的成功實施將進一步深化對熱帶氣旋動力學及其演變規律的認識，並提供高分辨率概率預報信息，為粵港澳大灣區建設智慧、氣候韌性和可持續發展的社會與基礎設施體系提供科學與技術支撐。

15240926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15240926.value: 無釩錳基NASICON型正極之反位缺陷調控及其應用於高能量密度鈉離子電池

15240926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15240926.value: Energy storage technologies are critical for large-scale renewable energy deployment. Among diverse storage possibilities, rechargeable batteries achieve superior energy storage ability through efficient electrochemical reactions. Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) have realized widespread applications in electric vehicles and portable devices, owing to their exceptional performance and reliability. Yet the high price of LIBs and safety issues hinder the widespread application of LIBs in grid-scale energy storage. Vanadium-free Mn-based Na superionic conductor (NASICON) has emerged as an attractive cathode material for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) in grid-scale energy storage owing to its low cost of raw materials and superior structure stability that enables ultra-long-time cycling. However, intrinsic anti-site defects (IASDs) are easily formed, where Mn ions occupy the Na-sites during sintering. The IASDs severely retard the reactivity and kinetics of redox couples, causing abnormal voltage hysteresis, fast capacity loss, and poor low-temperature kinetics. In this proposed project, we aim to address the issue of IASDs in NASICON-type materials by selective atomic occupancy at the Na vacancy site. We take Na3MnTi(PO4)3 (NMTP) as a representative NASICON cathode material for SIBs due to its non-toxicity (V-free) and low-cost (Mn-based). By preferential doping of Li on the Na vacancy site, we expect to suppress the formation of IASDs and accelerate the Na diffusion kinetics. At the same time, the Mn/Ti ratio will be increased to create a Na-rich environment to further suppress IASD formation. Through a combined approach of theoretical calculations and experimental validation, we will clarify the formation mechanism of IASDs and identify the effect of IASDs on the electrochemical performance of the cathode. We expect to achieve an energy density exceeding 500 Wh/kg, reaching over 30% improvement compared with pristine NMTP material. Meanwhile, due to the effective suppression of IASDs, the material’s reaction kinetics and cycling stability will be significantly enhanced, enabling wide-temperature operation (-40 ~ 80 °C) and long lifespan (>10,000 cycles). This research will advance the understanding of IASDs regulation and mechanisms in NASICON-type cathode materials, promoting the development and application of low-cost NASICON cathodes for high-energy-density SIBs working in a wide temperature range. 儲能技術對大規模可再生能源的部署至關重要。在多種儲能方案中，可充電電池透過高效的電化學反應，實現優越的儲能表現。鋰離子電池憑藉其卓越性能與可靠性，已在電動車及流動裝置中獲得廣泛應用。然而，鋰離子電池的高昂成本與安全問題，阻礙了其在電網級儲能領域的普及應用。無釩錳基鈉超離子導體（NASICON），由於原材料成本低廉，加上具備優異的結構穩定性而能夠實現超長循環壽命，已成為鈉離子電池用於電網級儲能中備受矚目的正極材料。然而，該材料容易形成本徵反位缺陷，即在燒結過程中，錳離子會佔據鈉位點。本徵反位缺陷會嚴重減慢氧化還原對的反應活性與動力學，導致異常電壓滯後、容量快速衰減以及低溫動力學表現欠佳等問題。本研究項目旨在透過在鈉空位進行選擇性原子佔位，解決NASICON型材料中本徵反位缺陷的問題。本研究選用Na₃MnTi (PO₄)₃（NMTP）作為代表性的NASICON型鈉離子電池正極材料，原因在於其無毒（不含釩）且成本低廉（錳基）。透過在鈉空位優先摻雜鋰離子，預期可抑制本徵反位缺陷的形成，並加快鈉離子擴散動力學。同時，本研究將提高錳/鈦比例，以創造富鈉環境進一步抑制反位缺陷的產生。透過理論計算與實驗驗證相結合的方法，本研究將闡明本徵反位缺陷的形成機制，並確定該缺陷對正極電化學性能的影響。研究目標為達到超過500 Wh kg⁻¹ 的能量密度，較原始NMTP材料提升30%以上。同時，由於本徵反位缺陷得到有效抑制，材料的反應動力學與循環穩定性將顯著增強，可實現寬溫度範圍運作（−40 ~ 80 °C）及長壽命（>10,000 次循環）。是項研究將加深學術界對NASICON型正極材料中本徵反位缺陷調控與機制的理解，推動低成本NASICON正極在寬溫域、高能量密度鈉離子電池中的研發與應用。

15241326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15241326.value: 基於天空計算平台的新型分佈式大規模模型訓練與微調系統

15241326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15241326.value: Recent years have witnessed the rapid evolution of large-scale models for achieving high accuracy. Training such large-scale models becomes a time- and resource-consuming task. As the size of AI models grows, the demand for computing resources doubles every 2-3 months, outpacing Moore's law and leading to global computational resource exhaustion. Sky computing has emerged as an effective solution to the global challenge of computing resource exhaustion by harnessing various computational resources from different data centers, regions, and cloud vendors. Training/fine-tuning large-scale AI models over such multidimensional heterogeneous computational resources has become a critical yet underexplored area of research. Several crucial challenges have been observed. Firstly, most existing all-reduce training frameworks are optimized for homogeneous computational environments and exhibit inefficiency when deployed on heterogeneous clusters. This project proposes designing a distributed framework that enables large-scale models to be trained across multidimensional, heterogeneous resources, encompassing diverse training frameworks (TensorFlow and PyTorch) and heterogeneous accelerators (NVIDIA and AMD GPUs) sourced from various data centers, geographic regions, and cloud vendors. Secondly, recent studies have reported low resource utilization in large-scale model training due to substantial communication overhead. We have explored parameter compression techniques and demonstrated that high compression ratios can be achieved while reducing communication overhead and preserving model accuracy. However, our solutions still suffer from sub-optimal resource utilization problems. Thirdly, deploying large-scale training lacks guidelines for how to schedule the tasks over sky computing platforms to achieve performance and cost efficiency. Fourth, as training scales increase, checkpointing has garnered significant attention, and designing an efficient checkpoint strategy remains a challenging task. To address these challenges, we will develop a distributed framework, SkyPS, which supports the entire life-cycle of large-scale model training over heterogeneous computational resources. We propose enhancing training performance through three key strategies: (1) designing a parameter compression algorithm that achieves a high compression ratio and is executable on various chip types; (2) provide a scheduling strategy for training/fine-tuning tasks over heterogeneous resource across cloud vendors to achieve performance and cost efficiency by packaging the compression as a service and integrate it to the training system; and (3) developing an efficient checkpoint strategy to facilitate rapid recovery from training failures. This project holds both academic and practical significance. It makes a unique contribution to the foundational research on training large-scale models over heterogeneous computational resources across cloud vendors (Sky Computing Platform). 近年來，大規模人工智能模型得到了快速發展。然而，此類模型的訓練通常需要消耗大量時間與計算資源。隨著人工智能模型規模的持續增長，其對計算資源的需求約每 2—3 個月翻倍，已超過摩爾定律的發展速度，並進一步導致全球計算資源緊張。Sky Computing通過整合來自不同數據中心、地理區域和雲服務商的多樣化計算資源，為緩解全球計算資源枯竭問題提供了一種有效方案。在此類多維異構計算資源上開展大規模人工智能模型的訓練與微調，已成為一個重要但尚未被充分探索的研究方向。 當前，該領域仍面臨若干關鍵挑戰。首先，現有大多數基於 All-Reduce 的訓練框架主要針對同構計算環境進行優化，當部署於異構集群時往往效率較低。本項目擬設計一種新型分佈式框架，使大規模模型能夠在多維異構資源上進行訓練，涵蓋來自不同資料中心、地理區域和雲服務商的多種訓練框架（如 TensorFlow 和 PyTorch）以及異構加速器（如 NVIDIA 和 AMD GPU）。其次，近期研究表明，大規模模型訓練中顯著的通信開銷會導致資源利用率較低。我們將探索參數壓縮技術，並證明其能夠在保持模型精度的同時實現較高壓縮率並降低通信開銷。再次，在Sky Computing平台上部署大規模訓練任務時，如何進行任務調度以同時實現性能與成本效率，目前仍缺乏系統性指導。最後，隨著訓練規模不斷擴大，檢查點機制受到越來越多關注，而設計高效的檢查點策略仍是一項具有挑戰性的任務。 為應對上述挑戰，我們將開發分佈式框架 SkyPS，以支持異構計算資源上大規模模型訓練的完整生命週期。具體而言，本項目擬通過三項關鍵策略提升訓練性能：（1）設計實現一種可在多種晶片類型上執行、並能夠實現高壓縮率的參數壓縮算法；（2）將壓縮機制封裝為服務並整合至訓練系統中，為跨雲服務商異構資源上的訓練與微調任務提供調度策略，以實現性能與成本效率的協同優化；（3）開發高效的檢查點策略，以支持訓練故障後的快速恢復。 本項目兼具重要的學術價值與實踐意義。其將對跨雲服務商異構計算資源（即Sky Computing平台）上的大規模模型訓練基礎研究作出獨特貢獻，並為未來大規模人工智能模型的高效訓練與微調提供系統性技術支撐。

15241526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15241526.value: 開發用於PM2.5空氣污染控制與健康風險評估的分子層面自由基分析工具

15241526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15241526.value: While fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is widely linked to cardiovascular and respiratory disease, the critical question is which chemical components drive this risk. Oxidative stress induced by radical species is increasingly recognized as a central pathway. Existing methods have provided important insights: common oxidative potential assays give bulk reactivity measures and, in some cases, target specific radicals such as hydroxyl (•OH), while electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy directly detects unpaired electrons. However, both approaches face limitations in complex particle mixtures. OP assays do not resolve the full radical spectrum, and EPR, while powerful, offers limited molecular detail and often requires high radical concentrations. As a result, practical methods that can reveal both short-lived reactive oxygen species (ROS) and longer-lived environmentally persistent free radicals (EPFRs) with molecular-level specificity are urgently needed to connect PM2.5 chemistry with health outcomes. This project develops a practical platform to identify and measure radicals in PM2.5. We first establish a rapid liquid chromatography-ion mobility-mass spectrometry (LC-IM-MS) method using spin-trapping agents to capture short-lived ROS. We then extend the same tools to EPFRs, generating two linked reference libraries that store retention time, collision cross section, and mass spectral fingerprints. These resources enable reliable recognition of radicals in complex particle mixtures. Next, leveraging previously confirmed EPFRs features, we move beyond radical trapping agents to create a reagent-free approach for direct EPFRs detection, reducing artifacts from chemical additives. Together, these methods make radical measurements faster, more specific, and transferable to instruments already available in many laboratories. In the final phase, we apply these methods to multi-site, multi-season samples from Hong Kong. We integrate radical data with standard composition, oxidative potential assays, and cell-based cytotoxicity tests. Machine-learning models are used to highlight EPFRs patterns and identify which radical species contribute most to oxidative potential and cytotoxicity. We further trace hazardous EPFRs contributors using source apportionment model. The expected outputs are (i) two validated analytical methods for ROS and EPFRs, (ii) two complementary reference libraries, one for radical-trapping agent adducts and another for native EPFRs, that will be accessible to other researchers, (iii) a workflow to identify the most toxic radicals, and (v) source attributions for Hong Kong. Beyond local applications, the methods and resources can be readily adopted by other cities facing more severe air pollution. In this way, the project advances radical-specific monitoring as a foundation for cleaner air policies and improved protection of public health worldwide. 微細懸浮粒子（PM2.5）已被廣泛證實與心血管及呼吸系統疾病相關，但關鍵問題仍在於：究竟哪些化學組分驅動這些健康風險？由自由基物種引起的氧化應激，日益被視為其中一條核心作用途徑。 現有方法已提供重要見解：常用的氧化潛勢測試可測量整體反應性，部分測試亦可針對羥基自由基（•OH）等特定自由基；電子順磁共振（EPR）光譜則可直接檢測未成對電子。然而，這兩類方法在複雜顆粒物混合物中均存在局限。氧化潛勢測試無法解析完整的自由基譜，而EPR雖然功能強大，所提供的分子層面資訊有限，且通常需要較高的自由基濃度。因此，亟需可在分子層面特異性地揭示短壽命活性氧物種（ROS）及較長壽命環境持久性自由基（EPFRs）的實用方法，從而將PM2.5的化學特性與健康效應聯繫起來。 本項目將建立一個用於鑑定和測量PM2.5中自由基的實用分析平台。首先，我們將利用自旋捕獲劑建立一種快速液相色譜－離子遷移－質譜（LC–IM–MS）方法，以捕獲短壽命ROS。其後，我們將把相同的分析工具擴展至EPFRs，建立兩個相互關聯的參考資料庫，記錄保留時間、碰撞截面及質譜指紋。這些資源將有助於在複雜顆粒物混合物中可靠地識別自由基。下一步，我們將利用先前已確認的EPFR特徵，進一步建立無需自由基捕獲劑的直接EPFR檢測方法，以減少化學添加劑所造成的分析偽影。整體而言，這些方法將使自由基測量更快速、更具特異性，並可移植至許多實驗室現有的分析儀器。 在最後階段，我們將把這些方法應用於香港多個地點及不同季節採集的PM2.5樣品。我們會把自由基數據與常規化學組成、氧化潛勢測試及細胞毒性測試相結合，並利用機器學習模型識別EPFR模式，以及確定哪些自由基物種對氧化潛勢和細胞毒性的貢獻最大。我們亦將利用源解析模型追蹤有害EPFR的可能來源。 預期成果包括：（i）兩種經驗證的ROS及EPFR分析方法；（ii）兩個互補並可供其他研究人員使用的參考資料庫，其中一個收錄自由基捕獲劑加合物，另一個收錄本徵EPFR；（iii）一套識別毒性最強自由基的工作流程；以及（iv）香港PM2.5中有害EPFR的來源解析結果。除香港的應用外，這些方法及資源亦可供空氣污染更嚴重的其他城市採用。藉此，本項目將推動以自由基為特異性指標的監測，為制定更有效的清潔空氣政策及改善全球公共健康保護奠定基礎。

15300026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15300026.value: 高雷諾數極限下三維邊界層的穩定性分析

15300026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300026.value: Understanding the behaviour of high-Reynolds-number flows near physical boundaries is a fundamental yet challenging problem in mathematical fluid mechanics. The primary theoretical framework for this is Prandtl's boundary layer theory, which asymptotically describes fluid motion near rigid walls. Since its introduction, this theory has played an essential role in the development of aerodynamics and fluid mechanics. Due to its importance, numerous studies have investigated its mathematical foundations. While significant progress has been made in understanding 2D boundary layers, the mathematical analysis of 3D boundary layers is still at an early stage. The presence of crossflow introduces significant complexity to stability mechanisms in three dimensions. In particular, our recent work [29] identified an instability in 3D boundary layers caused by crossflow effects, which is stronger than the classical Tollmien-Schlichting instability observed in 2D flows. This project aims to provide a rigorous stability analysis of boundary layers in the more realistic and complex three-dimensional setting. The research is divided into two main objectives. First, we will analyse the stability of parallel boundary layer profiles without crossflow. In this simplified scenario, our goal is to prove stability for the 3D Navier-Stokes equations within the critical Gevrey-3/2 class. Second, we will investigate the full problem, including crossflow effects. A key observation is that crossflow instability is directional: the associated unstable mode propagates only in centain directions. To maintain optimal regularity requirements, we will establish the stability of 3D boundary layer using a framework of anisotropic function spaces. This approach involves imposing stronger analytic regularity only in the singular direction of the crossflow modes, while preserving Gevrey regularity elsewhere. By addressing these mathematical challenges, this research will enhance our understanding of the stability characteristics of 3D boundary layers, and contribute to the broader field of mathematical fluid mechanics. Furthermore, the mathematical tools developed in this project are expected to be applicable to other hydrodynamic stability problems in higher dimensions with anisotropic structures. 理解高雷諾數流動在物理邊界附近的行為是數學流體力學中一個基本且具挑戰性的問題。對此最主要的理論框架是普朗特邊界層理論，該理論漸近地描述了剛性壁面附近的流體運動。自提出以來，這一理論在航空動力學與流體力學的發展中扮演了關鍵角色。鑑於其重要性，許多研究深入探討了其數學基礎。 儘管在理解二維邊界層方面已取得顯著進展，但三維邊界層的數學分析仍處於早期階段。橫向流（crossflow）的出現，為三維空間中的穩定性機制帶來了極大的複雜性。特別地，我們最近的研究 [29] 發現了由橫流效應引起的三維邊界層不穩定性，這種不穩定性比在二維流動中觀察到的傳統的Tollmien-Schlichting不穩定性更為強烈。 本項目旨在為更真實且複雜的三維情境下的邊界層提供嚴謹的穩定性分析。研究分為兩個主要目標： 1. 分析不含橫流的平行邊界層剖面之穩定性。在這種簡化情境下，我們的目標是在臨界 Gevrey-3/2 函數空間內，證明三維 Navier-Stokes equations的穩定性。 2. 探討包含橫流效應的邊界層穩定性。一個關鍵的觀察是，橫流不穩定性具有方向性：相關的不穩定模式僅沿特定方向傳播。為了保持臨界的正则性要求，我們將利用各向異性函數空間（anisotropic function spaces）的框架來確立三維邊界層的穩定性。該方法僅在橫流模式的奇異方向上施加更強的解析正则性，同時在其他方向保留 Gevrey 正则性。 本研究將深化我們對三維邊界層穩定性特徵的理解，並對更廣泛的數學流體力學領域做出貢獻。此外，本項目所開發的數學工具預計亦可應用於高維度中具有各向異性結構的其他流动穩定性問題。

15301026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15301026.value: 非利普希兹非光滑隨機零階優化及其複雜度分析

15301026.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15301026.value: Prof Li, Guoyin Prof Takeda, Akiko

15301026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301026.value: Optimization problems in contemporary applications are becoming increasingly complex. These problems usually involve an objective whose first-order information such as gradient or subgradient is prohibitively expensive to compute, and while its function value is obtainable, it can also be expensive. Thus, zeroth-order methods that only access function values in each iteration are suitable for solving these problems. In addition, since function value query is expensive, an important concern in the study of zeroth-order method is the worst-case complexity for obtaining a point that satisfies certain approximate stationarity measure. Up to date, most existing worst-case complexity results rely on various Lipschitzian assumptions, which fail to hold for important applications such as neural network training and fine-tuning problems, as well as many simulation-based optimization problems. In this project, the PI and his collaborators will go beyond the standard Lipschitzian setting and develop and analyze zeroth-order methods for objective functions that are possibly non-Lipschitz and nonsmooth. Specifically, leveraging the recent work of the PI, we will study a class of functions known as subdifferentially polynomially bounded (SPB) functions, which is general enough to cover all Lipschitz functions, all polynomial functions, and the possibly nonsmooth functions that arise in neural network training problems. In addition, we will focus on Gaussian-smoothing based methods, which have well-established worst-case complexity analysis for Lipschitz and nonsmooth objectives. Our study will be conducted along three directions. First, we will investigate how extrapolation and variance reduction techniques can be incorporated to develop accelerated variants of Gaussian-smoothing based methods for SPB functions, and analyze their worst-case complexities for achieving approximate Goldstein stationarity. Second, we will develop new Gaussian homotopy type methods for SPB functions, and establish their worst-case complexities for obtaining a stationary point. Finally, to obtain a more complete understanding of the algorithmic performances, we will also analyze the local convergence rates of the methods developed above under the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz property. Our study will result in new zeroth-order optimization methods with worst-case complexity guarantees for SPB functions, which are ubiquitous in contemporary applications. 本項目將研究一類零階最優化方法的（最壞情況）複雜度。這類方法在日益複雜的當代應用中愈發重要。現有理論多依賴 Lipschitz 假設，無法應用於神經網絡訓練等重要領域。本計畫將突破傳統 Lipschitz 設定，針對非 Lipschitz 非光滑的次微分多項式有界函數，基於高斯光滑方法展開三個方向研究。首先我們將結合外插等技術，開發新型高斯光滑算法並分析其複雜度。我們亦會針對次微分多項式有界函數開發新型高斯同倫算法並分析其複雜度。最後，我們將利用 Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz 性質分析上述新算法的局部收斂率。本研究將發展出具複雜度保證的高效零階最優化方法。

15301126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15301126.value: 生物醫學研究中處理代理變量、機器學習預測與缺失數據的統計方法

15301126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301126.value: With the increasing availability of electronic health record (EHR) data from large and diverse populations, there is growing interest in using these records to advance research on health and disease. However, EHR data are often subject to inaccuracies arising from issues in data collection, representation, and preprocessing. In many studies, only a small subset of subjects have precise measurements obtained through manual chart reviews, while most rely on proxy values that are often inaccurate. Machine learning and artificial intelligence methods have been developed to improve phenotype derivation from EHR data, but these predictions remain error-prone, and the underlying processes are often treated as a black box. The integration of EHR data with multi-omics data further complicates analysis, as it typically results in high-dimensional datasets with substantial missingness. A key research challenge is to effectively incorporate proxy variables and incomplete data to perform valid inference. In this project, we will develop a unified two-step "update estimation" framework for estimation and inference with missing and error-prone data. First, we will propose update estimation methods for semiparametric transformation models for censored survival data, incorporating proxy data to improve inference for regression coefficients and nonparametric functions. We will then consider high-dimensional regression models, focusing on inference and variable selection in the presence of many covariates and proxy variables. Finally, we will consider blockwise missing covariate patterns, which commonly arise in multi-omics data. We will conduct comprehensive theoretical analyses of the proposed methods and evaluate their performance through extensive simulation studies. In addition, we will apply these methods to real-world studies. To facilitate broad adoption, we will develop and distribute efficient and user-friendly statistical software packages. 隨著來自大型且多元族群的電子健康紀錄（electronic health record, EHR）資料日益普及，研究人員對利用這些紀錄來推進健康與疾病研究的關注也不斷增加。然而，EHR 資料常因資料蒐集、詮釋與處理過程中的問題而存在不準確性。在許多研究中，只有少數受試者具有透過人工病歷審查取得的精確測量值，而大多數受試者則依賴通常並不精確的代理值。機器學習與人工智能方法雖已被用於改善 EHR 資料的表型推導，但這些預測仍易出錯，且其流程往往被視為黑盒子。EHR 資料與多組學資料的整合進一步增加了分析的複雜性，因為這通常會產生具有大量缺失值的高維度資料集。研究的關鍵挑戰在於如何有效納入代理變量與不完整資料，以進行有效的推論。 在本計畫中，我們將發展一個統一的兩步「更新估計」框架，用於具有缺失與易出錯資料之估計與推論。首先，我們將針對刪失生存變量的半參數轉換模型提出更新估計方法，並納入代理資料，以改善對迴歸係數與非參數函數的推論。接著，我們將考慮高維度迴歸模型，著重於在存在大量協變量與代理變量的情況下進行推論與變量選擇。最後，我們將考量區塊式缺失的協變量結構，這類結構常見於多組學資料中。我們將對所提出的方法進行全面的理論分析，並透過廣泛的模擬研究評估其效能。此外，我們也將把這些方法應用於真實世界研究。為促進廣泛採用，我們將開發並發布高效率且易於使用的統計軟體套件。

15301226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15301226.value: 動態隨機系統中的多個非光滑最佳化問題

15301226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301226.value: Nonsmooth optimization problems have numerous applications in data science including signal reconstruction, variable selection, image restoration, etc. Nowadays, many applications of Artificial Intelligence (AI) use static, dynamic and random data in different forms including digital, images, text and sound to make time-dependent decisions. For example, embodied intelligence systems for the health of elderly people use data from wearable devices, medical records, video cameras, etc. However, most existing nonsmooth optimization methods have limitations to solve multiple nonsmooth optimization problems constructed from different data sources in different forms simultaneously and efficiently. This project aims to establish new optimization theories and algorithms for finding solutions of multiple nonsmooth optimization problems in a dynamic stochastic system simultaneously and efficiently. The solution set of each optimization problem may have infinitely many solutions. It is crucial to select some special solutions from the optimal solutions sets to make the dynamic system have a meaningful solution. We will study continuous selections from the solution sets of the multiple nonsmooth convex optimization problems and establish new existence theorems for solutions of the dynamic stochastic system. Moreover, we will develop discrete approximation schemes with sample average approximation and time-stepping approximation. Finally, we will develop computer codes for implementation of the new optimization algorithms with the discrete approximation schemes on high-performance computers to solve multiple nonsmooth optimization problems in dynamic stochastic systems. Real data from wearable devices and health care records will be used to demonstrate the applications of the new theories and algorithms. The outcomes of this project will have a long-term and significant impact, because multiple nonsmooth optimization problems in dynamic stochastic systems arise from many applications in data science and AI, and urgently need efficient algorithms for implementation. The new optimization theories and algorithms developed in this project will attract attention from the international scientific community through excellent collaboration with world leading researchers and publications in leading journals and conferences. 非光滑最佳化問題在數據科學領域有廣泛的應用，涵蓋訊號重構、變數選擇、影像修復等場景。如今，許多人工智慧（AI）應用利用數字、圖像、文字和音訊等多種形式的靜態、動態及隨機數據，來製定依賴時間變化的決策。例如，旨在保障老年人健康的具身智慧系統，便利用了來自穿戴式裝置、醫療記錄及視訊監控等多種管道的數據。然而，現有的多數非光滑最佳化方法在同時且有效率地求解由不同形式、不同來源的資料所構成的多重非光滑最佳化問題時，往往有其限制。 此研究計畫旨在建立新的最優化理論與演算法，以便有效地同時求解動態隨機系統中的多個非光滑最優化問題。每個最優化問題的解集可能包含無限多個解；從最優解集中選取特定的解，對於確保動態系統獲得有意義的解至關重要。我們將研究這些非光滑優化問題解集的連續選擇問題，並建立動態隨機系統解的存在性新定理。此外，我們還將開發基於樣本平均逼近和時間步進逼近的離散近似方案。 最後，我們將利用離散逼近方案，在高效能電腦上編寫程式碼以實現這些新的最優化演算法，從而求解動態隨機系統中的多類非光滑最優化問題。我們將使用來自穿戴式裝置和醫療保健記錄的實際數據，來展示這些新理論與演算法的應用。 此研究計畫的成果將產生深遠且重大的影響，因為動態隨機系統中的多類非光滑最優化問題源自於數據科學和人工智慧領域的廣泛應用，且極需高效演算法來實現求解。透過與世界頂尖研究人員的卓越合作，以及在頂尖期刊和會議上發表研究成果，本研究計畫所發展的創新優化理論與演算法將引起國際科學界的廣泛關注。

15301426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15301426.value: 等熵可壓縮納維-斯托克斯方程的定量正則性與弱解

15301426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301426.value: Despite of its importance in physics and engineering, on one hand, the existence theories of weak solutions of isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with low adiabatic constants remain as challenging open problems in mathematics, even though the global weak solution had been established pioneerly by Lions in his monograph and by Feireisl-Novotny-Petzeltova two decades ago as the adiabatic constant is large. On the other hand, the quantitative regularity of compressible Navier-Stokes equations with large initial data in critical spaces remains open, and hence attracts a lot of attentions in the past decades. The first topic in this proposal aims to address the quantitative regularity of classical solutions to multi-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes equations with large initial data in critical spaces. Away from the initial layer, the velocity is expected to be bounded because of the parabolicity; while the density is expected to be bounded for all time due to the hyperbolicity. The decay mechanisms in the linearised hyperbolic-parabolic coupling system provide the necessary control on the growth of norms of solutions. The success of this proposed problem relies on a better understanding of the smoothing effect of velocity and the damping effect of density with the help of ``effective viscous fluxes", and will pave the way to the quantitative regularity of other hyperbolic-parabolic models with large initial data in critical spaces. The second topic in this proposal focuses on concentration phenomenon and existence of weak solutions of isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations in multi-dimensional spaces with large initial data as the adiabatic constant is low. This proposed problem is interesting and challenging because of the lack of a priori estimates, and the non-compatibility between the weak convergence and the nonlinearity. Precisely due to the lack of a priori estimates, the concentration of density would appear and it makes the compactness of the pressure hard to be established. This proposal will study the concentration of density in terms of Newtonian potential of density. As a consequence, an improvement on the integrability of density will be established. Moreover the ``effective viscous flux" will be applied to deal with the possible oscillation of approximating solutions. The success of this proposed problem needs a careful analysis of both concentration and oscillation phenomena with the help of the relation between Newtonian potentials of density and a Sobolev embedding with weights, and will in turn shed lights on understanding better the weak convergence method in compressible fluids. 本提案的第一個主題旨在探討臨界空間中具有大初始資料的高維可壓縮Navier-Stokes方程式經典解的定量正則性。遠離初始層時，由於拋物性，速度預計是有界的；而由於雙曲性，密度預計始終是有界的。本提案的成功取決於對速度平滑效應和密度阻尼效應的更深入理解，而這需要藉助「有效黏滯通量」來實現。 本提案的第二個主題聚焦於高維空間中具有大初值的等熵可壓縮Navier-Stokes方程式的弱解的集中現象和存在性，尤其是在絕熱常數較低的情況下。由於缺乏先驗估計以及弱收斂性和非線性之間的不相容性，本提案的問題非常具有挑戰性。由於缺乏先驗估計，密度集中現象才會出現，這使得壓力的緊緻性難以確定。此問題的成功需要對集中和振盪現象進行仔細分析。

15301626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15301626.value: 開發粒線體標靶配體與臨床抑制劑協同作用的新型組合療法以克服BRAF突變癌症

15301626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301626.value: Cancer remains a major global health challenge, causing nearly 10 million deaths in 2020. The BRAFV-600E mutation is a key genetic driver, found in 40–60% of melanomas, 8–12% of metastatic colorectal cancers, and ~50% of papillary thyroid cancers. Targeted therapies, especially BRAF and MEK inhibitor combinations, are now standard for BRAF-V600E-mutant cancers. In colorectal cancer, encorafenib plus cetuximab has set a new therapeutic benchmark. However, acquired resistance, mainly via MAPK pathway reactivation and compensatory signaling, often limits long-term clinical efficacy. Emerging evidence highlights the role of mitochondrial dysfunction in cancer progression and therapy resistance. Mitochondria are well-known to influence tumor behavior through retrograde signalling involving reactive oxygen species (ROS), calcium flux, and mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) stress responses. These processes contribute to cellular adaptation and survival under therapeutic pressure. Recent studies suggest that certain small-molecule ligands, such as disulfiram (a copper ionophore), capable of inducing mitochondrial damage, particularly through the TXNIP/TRX2 axis, when combined with BRAF inhibitors, may help overcome resistance to the inhibitors by inducing mitochondrial damage and oxidative stress and disrupting tumor cell survival mechanisms. Despite this promise, the development of mitochondria-targeting agents that are both selective and potent remains a significant challenge. Moreover, the therapeutic potential of combining such agents with clinically approved inhibitors (e.g., BRAF, MEK, and EGFR inhibitors) has not been fully explored in the context of BRAF-V600E-driven cancers. For these reasons, this project aims to address these gaps by: (i) Designing mitochondria-specific small-molecule ligands that selectively impair mitochondrial function and activate retrograde signalling through interactions with mitochondrial DNA in cancer cells. (ii) Evaluating the synergistic potential of these ligands in combination with existing clinical inhibitors in BRAF-V600E-mutant melanoma, colorectal, and thyroid cancers. By co-targeting mitochondrial integrity and oncogenic signalling pathways, such as the MAPK pathway, using tailor-made small-molecule ligands developed in this project, this strategy aims to overcome drug resistance, enhance therapeutic efficacy, and improve clinical outcomes in BRAF-V600E-driven cancers. We have developed two mitochondria-targeting lead compounds with potent anticancer activity for this project. These ligands will be further advanced through rational design to selectively impair mitochondrial function and disrupt compensatory survival mechanisms, thereby sensitizing tumor cells to existing therapies. Anticipated benefits include improved pharmacodynamic profiles, greater precision in targeting resistant cancer cells, and a robust foundation for future clinical translation. Ultimately, this research seeks to advance the development of next-generation combination therapies for melanoma, colorectal, and thyroid cancers harbouring BRAF-mutations. 癌症仍然是全球重大公共衛生挑戰之一，於2020年造成近1,000萬人死亡。BRAF-V600E 突變是一種重要的致癌驅動基因變異，存在於約 40–60% 的黑色素瘤、8–12% 的轉移性大腸直腸癌，以及約 50% 的乳頭狀甲狀腺癌中。目前，以 BRAF 與 MEK 抑制劑聯合治療為代表的標靶療法，已成為 BRAF-V600E 突變癌症的標準治療方案。在大腸直腸癌方面，encorafenib 聯合 cetuximab 的治療組合更已建立新的治療標竿。然而，治療後產生的後天抗藥性，特別是經由 MAPK 訊號傳導途徑再活化及補償性訊號網絡所引起的抗藥機制，往往限制了這些療法的長期臨床效益。 愈來愈多研究證據顯示，粒線體功能失調在癌症進展及治療抗藥性形成中扮演關鍵角色。眾所周知，粒線體可透過涉及活性氧（reactive oxygen species, ROS）、鈣離子通量（calcium flux）及粒線體 DNA（mtDNA）壓力反應的逆向訊號傳導（retrograde signalling），調控腫瘤細胞的生物學行為。這些機制有助於癌細胞在治療壓力下維持適應與存活。近期研究指出，某些能夠誘導粒線體損傷的小分子配體，例如具有銅離子載體（copper ionophore）活性的雙硫崙（disulfiram），可藉由 TXNIP/TRX2 訊號軸引發粒線體損害。當其與 BRAF 抑制劑併用時，可能透過增加粒線體損傷與氧化壓力並破壞腫瘤細胞存活機制，而克服對 BRAF 抑制劑的抗藥性。儘管此策略展現出良好前景，兼具高度選擇性與強效活性的粒線體標靶藥物之開發仍面臨重大挑戰。此外，在 BRAF-V600E 驅動癌症中，將此類粒線體標靶藥物與已獲臨床核准的抑制劑（例如 BRAF、MEK 及 EGFR 抑制劑）進行聯合治療的潛力，迄今尚未被充分探索。因此，本研究計畫擬藉由下列兩項目標填補現有研究缺口： (1). 設計具粒線體專一性的小分子配體，透過與癌細胞粒線體 DNA 的相互作用，選擇性損害粒線體功能並啟動逆向訊號傳導機制； (2). 評估此類配體與現有臨床抑制劑的協同治療潛力，並應用於 BRAF-V600E 突變之黑色素瘤、大腸直腸癌及甲狀腺癌。 本項目將利用自行開發的客製化小分子配體，同時針對粒線體完整性及 MAPK 等致癌訊號傳導路徑進行雙重標靶治療，以期克服藥物抗性、提升治療效果，並改善 BRAF-V600E 驅動癌症患者的臨床預後。我們目前已開發出兩種具有顯著抗癌活性的粒線體標靶先導化合物，將在本計畫中透過理性藥物設計進一步優化，以選擇性抑制粒線體功能並破壞癌細胞的補償性存活機制，從而提高腫瘤細胞對現有療法的敏感性。本項目的預期成果包括改善藥物藥效動力學特性、提高針對抗藥性癌細胞的治療精準度，以及建立穩固的臨床轉譯基礎。本研究期望推動新一代聯合治療策略的發展，為帶有 BRAF 突變的黑色素瘤、大腸直腸癌及甲狀腺癌提供更有效的治療選擇。

15302126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15302126.value: 基於二維半導體的垂直超短溝道晶體管研究

15302126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15302126.value: The continuous reduction in transistor size revolutionizes the semiconductor industry. However, silicon-based transistors are now approaching atomic scale. Further miniaturization faces significant physical limitations, including short channel effects, quantum effects, and thermal challenges. For instance, the channel lengths of transistors at 3 nm technology node remains around 10 nm, indicating that the technology node names no longer reflect their historical physical significance. According to the International Roadmap for Devices and Systems (IRDS), future performance improvements in the semiconductor industry will depend on the integration of new materials and innovative transistor structures. Two-dimensional (2D) materials have emerged as promising candidates due to their atomic thickness and dangling-bond-free surface, which can mitigate short channel effects and enable further transistor miniaturization, allowing for higher density integration on chips. To explore the miniaturization limits of transistors, we aim to achieve channel lengths of less than 10 nm, which imposes stringent requirements on fabrication techniques. While extreme ultraviolet lithography, utilized in advanced semiconductor foundries, offers precise patterning capabilities, it is hindered by high complexity and substantial costs. As a result, exploring innovative transistor structures that can be fabricated using more accessible and conventional equipment emerges as a promising alternative. By leveraging existing technologies, we aim to overcome the barriers imposed by advanced lithography, paving the way for more efficient and cost-effective manufacturing processes in the field of nanoelectronics. In this research project, we will focus on designing and fabricating vertical ultrashort-channel transistors using two-dimensional (2D) materials, exploring their applications in logic circuits and neuromorphic computing. We aim to achieve channel lengths below 10 nm by designing a vertical ultrashort-channel device using 2D semiconductors, where the channel length is defined by a vertical metal-insulator-metal configuration. We will address the challenges of performance verification and large-scale preparation of these vertical ultrashort-channel devices. After the construction of the vertical ultrashort-channel devices, we will optimize its performance by straining engineering, study its ballistic transport characteristics, demonstrate its logic circuit functions, and investigate the physical characteristics and circuit operation modes, ultimately evaluating their performance through theoretical analysis supported by experimental data. 晶體管尺寸的持續縮小引領了半導體產業的革命性變化。然而，矽基晶體管目前已接近原子尺度，進一步微縮面臨着嚴重的物理限制，包括短溝道效應、量子效應以及熱挑戰。例如，在 3 納米技術節點下，晶體管的溝道長度仍維持在 10 納米左右，這表明技術節點的名稱已不再反映其歷史上的物理意義。 根據《國際器件與系統路線圖》（IRDS），半導體產業未來的性能提升將依賴於新材料的集成與創新晶體管結構的引入。二維（2D）材料憑藉其原子級厚度和無懸鍵表面，成為極具前景的候選材料；它們能夠緩解短溝道效應並推動晶體管的進一步微縮，從而實現晶片上更高密度的集成。 為了探索晶體管微縮的極限，我們旨在實現小於 10 納米的溝道長度，這對製備技術提出了極其嚴苛的要求。儘管先進半導體晶圓廠所採用的極紫外線光刻技術具備精準的圖案化能力，但其複雜度高昂且成本巨大。因此，探索可利用更通用且易於獲取的設備進行製備的創新晶體管結構，成為了一項極具前景的替代方案。通過利用現有技術，我們旨在克服先進光刻技術帶來的障礙，為納米電子學領域鋪平更高效、更具成本效益的製造路徑。 在本研究項目中，我們將專注於設計和製備基於二維（2D）材料的垂直超短溝道晶體管，並探索其在邏輯電路與類腦神經形態計算中的應用。我們計劃通過設計一種採用二維半導體的垂直超短溝道器件，由垂直的金屬-絕緣體-金屬結構來定義溝道長度，從而實現 10 納米以下的溝道長度。我們將攻克這些垂直超短溝道器件在性能驗證和大面積製備方面的挑戰。在建構垂直超短溝道器件後，我們將通過應變工程優化其性能，研究其彈道輸運特性，展示其邏輯電路功能，並深入探究其物理特性與電路運行模式，最終結合實驗數據與理論分析對其性能進行綜合評估。

15302326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15302326.value: 透過二維鈣鈦礦超晶格破除手性與遷移率的權衡關係，開發新式自旋電子元件

15302326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15302326.value: Chiral semiconductors leverage the chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect to generate spin polarization in transported charges—critical for spintronics—yet face a core barrier: strong chiral order (needed for reliable CISS) and efficient charge transport (vital for practical devices) are mutually exclusive. This trade-off has stalled lab-to-real-world translation, demanding chiral materials that boost both. This proposal builds on promising preliminary work: we synthesized highly ordered, vertically aligned, transferable 2D chiral perovskite superlattices (SLs) with breakthrough traits—large CD anisotropy factor (0.21), high mobility (12.6 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹), ~90% spin-polarized current—plus observation of room-temperature magnetoresistance and spin photocurrent in devices. Still, gaps remain to unlock their full potential of these SLs for chiral spintronics applications. The proposed research will address three key unresolved questions: (1) What is the spin lifetime of these chiral perovskite SLs, and what mechanisms (e.g., DP or EY) limit it? (2) How does adjusting the number of inorganic layers (n-value) in SLs modulate chiral order, mobility, and spin lifetime—and can we find an optimal n that synergizes these properties? (3) How do SL architectural parameters (vertical thickness and density) tune device performance (e.g., magnetoresistance, spin polarization in electrical/optical currents)? To answer these questions, we will execute an integrated experimental-theoretical research plan: (1) Experimentally, use ultrafast circularly polarized transient absorption (CP-TA) and optical pump terahertz probe (OPTP) to measure spin lifetime and carrier momentum relaxation time; theoretically, collaborate on DFT calculations and NAMD simulations to distinguish DP/EY spin relaxation mechanisms. (2) Synthesize SLs with n=1–5, characterize their chiral order, mobility, and spin lifetime; pair with DFT modeling of n-dependent properties to find the optimal n. (3) Fabricate vertical spin valves and opto-spin devices, adjust SL thickness and density, and characterize key device metrics to validate structure-performance links. By resolving these questions, this project will overcome key bottleneck in chiral spintronics and establish design principles for next-generation vertical spintronic technologies, with broad implications for advanced computing, data storage, and optoelectronic applications. 手性半導體可透過手性誘發自旋選擇效應（CISS）使傳輸電荷產生自旋極化，該特性為自旋電子學的核心要素，然而現今存在一項核心困境：穩定 CISS 效應所需的高手性有序度，與實用器件不可或缺的高效率電荷傳輸兩者互為衝突。此一取捨問題阻礙了該技術由實驗室走向實際產業應用，亟待開發可同時提升兩項屬性的手性材料。本研究提案立基於已有的優異先期成果：本團隊合成出高有序度、垂直排列、可轉移之二維手性鈣鈦礦超晶格（SLs），具備多項突破性參數，包含 0.21 的圓二色性各向異性因子、12.6 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ 的高遷移率、近 90% 的自旋極化電流，並已在器件上檢測到室溫磁阻與自旋光電流訊號。即便如此，此類超晶格要完整實現在手性自旋電子學的應用潛力，仍存在不少研究缺口待補足。本計畫研究將解決三項尚未釐清的關鍵問題：(1) 該手性鈣鈦礦超晶格的自旋生命期數值為何，以及受狄亞可諾夫–佩雷爾（DP）、艾略特–亞菲特（EY）何種機制所限制；(2) 調整超晶格的無機層數（n 值）會如何改變手性有序度、遷移率與自旋生命期，是否能求得讓各項物性產生協同作用的最佳 n 值；(3) 超晶格結構參數（垂直厚度、堆積密度）如何調控器件性能，例如磁阻、電流與光電流的自旋極化程度。為解決上述議題，我們將執行實驗與理論整合之研究架構：(1) 實驗方面運用超快圓偏振瞬態吸收光譜（CP-TA）與光泵浦太赫茲探測（OPTP）量測自旋生命期與載子動量鬆弛時間，理論部分則合作進行密度泛函理論（DFT）計算與非平衡分子動力學（NAMD）模擬，辨識 DP 與 EY 兩種自旋鬆弛機制的主導貢獻；(2) 製備 n＝1 至 5 的一系列超晶格樣品，檢測其手性有序度、遷移率及自旋生命期，搭配 DFT 建模分析物性隨 n 值的變化規律，篩選出最適層數；(3) 製作垂直自旋閥與光自旋元件，調控超晶格厚度與密度，量測各項器件指標，驗證材料結構與器件表現的對應關係。藉由厘清上述科學問題，本計畫將突破手性自旋電子學的重要瓶頸，建立新一代垂直式自旋電子技術的設計準則，對於先進運算、資料儲存與光電元件領域皆具備廣泛的應用價值。

15302826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15302826.value: 探索補償反鐵磁體中的非線性電自旋產生與非線性自旋/軌道霍爾效應

15302826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15302826.value: The predominant technology for information storage relies on ferromagnetic materials. Importantly, recent advancements have highlighted the potential of compensated antiferromagnets (AFMs) to outperform ferromagnets, due to their lack of stray fields, resilience to external magnetic fields, and ultrafast operational speeds. This has spurred the emerging field of AFM spintronics, which seeks to leverage AFMs for next-generation information technologies. A comprehensive understanding of the physical response properties of AFMs is essential to realize this potential. Current research in AFM spintronics primarily focuses on linear response regimes, leaving the nonlinear responses of AFM systems largely uncharted. These nonlinear responses are critical for several reasons: (i) they exhibit distinct symmetry properties, becoming dominant where linear responses are symmetry-forbidden; (ii) they enable functionalities unattainable with linear responses; (iii) their nonlinear properties reveal intriguing quantum geometric features of band structures, offering valuable insights into fundamental physics. For instance, from simple symmetry analysis, we note that AFMs with inversion symmetry cannot be effectively switched by an electric field in the linear regime, but this becomes feasible through nonlinear responses. Thus, exploring nonlinear physics in AFMs is imperative for both foundational knowledge and practical applications. This project aims to address this gap by theoretically investigating key nonlinear effects in compensated AFMs, including nonlinear electric spin generation, nonlinear spin Hall effect, and nonlinear orbital Hall effect. The study is structured around three objectives. (A) Developing microscopic theories with quantitative predictive capability. This will be based on the approach of extended semiclassical theory, pioneered by the PI’s group and collaborators. (B) Identifying suitable AFM materials for studying these nonlinear effects. This is by screening material databases based on symmetry conditions obtained from group theoretical analysis. (C) Developing computational approach to quantify nonlinear effects of candidate materials. Based on these findings, we will also suggest possible schemes to harness these nonlinear effects for AFM spintronic applications. This project will advance our fundamental understanding of nonlinear physics in AFMs, predict novel effects and material platforms for experimental validation, and pave new pathways for utilizing AFMs in advanced information storage technologies. 目前資訊儲存的主流技術依賴於鐵磁材料。近年來的研究進展已凸顯出補償反鐵磁體（AFMs）超越鐵磁體的潛力。這歸因於其無雜散磁場、對外加磁場具有抗擾性，以及具備超快的操作速度。這些優勢推動了新興的反鐵磁自旋電子學領域，旨在利用反鐵磁體實現下一代資訊技術。全面理解反鐵磁體的物理響應特性，對於實現這一潛力至關重要。當前反鐵磁自旋電子學的研究主要集中於線性響應區間，而反鐵磁系統的非線性響應仍大多未被探索。這些非線性響應之所以關鍵，有以下幾個原因：（i）它們展現出獨特的對稱性質，在線性響應被對稱性禁戒的情況下可成為主導；（ii）它們能夠實現線性響應無法達成的功能；（iii）其非線性特性揭示了能帶結構中的量子幾何特徵，為基礎物理提供寶貴洞見。例如，從簡單的對稱性分析可知，具有反演對稱性的反鐵磁體無法在線性區間有效地被電場切換，但透過非線性響應則變得可行。因此，探索反鐵磁體中的非線性物理，無論對於基礎知識還是實際應用，都至關重要。本計畫旨在透過理論研究補償反鐵磁體中的關鍵非線性效應，包括非線性電自旋產生、非線性自旋霍爾效應及非線性軌道霍爾效應，以填補此缺口。研究圍繞三個目標展開。(A) 發展具有定量預測能力的微觀理論。這將基於 PI 研究團隊與合作者所開創的擴展半經典理論方法。(B) 識別適合研究這些非線性效應的反鐵磁材料。(C) 發展計算方法以量化候選材料的非線性效應。基於這些發現，我們亦將提出可能的方案，以利用這些非線性效應於反鐵磁自旋電子學應用。本計畫將增進我們對反鐵磁體中非線性物理的基礎理解，預測新穎效應與可供實驗驗證的材料平台，並為利用反鐵磁體於先進資訊儲存技術開闢新途徑。

15303126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15303126.value: 白噪声色散随机非线性薛定谔方程的保结构数值方法

15303126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303126.value: The stochastic nonlinear Schrödinger equation (SNLSE) with white noise dispersion is a fundamental model for describing wave propagation in complex media, with significant applications in nonlinear optics, quantum mechanics, and materials science. While the theoretical analysis of the SNLSE has advanced in recent years, obtaining explicit analytical solutions is extremely difficult, if not impossible, due to the equation’s inherent complexity and randomness. As a result, the development of robust and structure-preserving numerical methods for these equations remains in its infancy, particularly in the presence of white noise dispersion. This project aims to bridge this gap by developing and analyzing novel numerical schemes that preserve key geometric and physical structures of the SNLSE, such as mass conservation and stochastic symplecticity, even under minimal regularity assumptions on the initial data. Our research will focus on three main objectives. First, we will investigate the well-posedness and longtime dynamics of SNLSE with white noise dispersion, employing multiscale analysis and perturbation techniques to uncover hidden structures and regularity properties of the solutions. Second, we will design and rigorously analyze structure-preserving numerical methods, including resonance-based schemes via the Wong-Zakai approximation and stratified Monte-Carlo methods, to accurately capture the stochastic dynamics and geometric features of the SNLSE. Special attention will be given to the development of stochastic low-regularity integrators that remain effective even when the initial data or coefficients lack smoothness. Third, we will conduct a comprehensive error analysis of the proposed numerical methods, establishing strong and weak convergence rates and providing quantitative error bounds for longtime simulations. We will also explore the longtime behavior of numerical solutions, including scattering properties and the impact of random dispersion on the qualitative dynamics of the system. The effectiveness of our framework will be demonstrated through applications of SNLSEs with various nonlinearities and in different physical settings. The results of our research have strong potential for applications in various fields. For example, in optical fiber communications, they may be used to simulate the propagation of nonlinear waves under random dispersion effects. In quantum physics, the proposed methods could help analyze the dynamics of Bose-Einstein condensates in disordered environments. Overall, this research will advance numerical analysis by providing robust and efficient tools for simulating SNLSEs with white noise dispersion. By preserving the structures of the original equations, our methods will enable more accurate and reliable simulations, paving the way for new discoveries and practical applications across multiple disciplines. 白噪声色散作用下的随机非线性薛定谔方程，是描述复杂介质中波传播现象的一类重要数学模型，在非线性光学、量子物理和材料科学等领域具有广泛应用。近年来，相关方程的理论研究取得了显著进展，但与之相配套的数值计算方法仍不够成熟。特别是在白噪声色散的影响下，如何设计既稳定可靠、又能保持原方程重要几何与物理性质的数值方法，仍是一个具有挑战性的研究问题。本项目旨在发展一套适用于白噪声色散随机非线性薛定谔方程的保结构数值方法，并建立相应的严格理论分析。所构造的方法将重点保持方程的质量守恒和随机辛结构等关键性质，同时尽可能降低对初始数据光滑性的要求，从而提高数值模拟的准确性、稳定性和适用范围。 本项目包括三个主要研究方向。首先，我们将研究该类方程解的存在唯一性、正则性以及长时间动力学行为。通过多尺度分析和摄动方法，进一步揭示随机色散作用下解的内在结构及其演化规律。其次，我们将设计并分析多类保结构数值方法，包括基于 Wong–Zakai 逼近的共振型数值格式和分层蒙特卡罗方法，以有效刻画方程中的随机效应、非线性相互作用以及几何结构。项目将特别关注随机低正则性积分方法的构造，使数值方法在初始数据或方程系数不够光滑时仍能保持良好的稳定性和计算精度。然后我们将对所提出的数值方法进行系统的误差分析，建立强收敛与弱收敛结果，给出明确的收敛速度和长时间误差界。同时，我们还将研究数值解的长期演化特征，包括波的散射行为，以及随机色散对系统整体动力学性质的影响。 本项目将通过具有不同非线性形式和物理背景的模型验证所提出方法的有效性。相关成果具有较好的应用潜力。例如，在光纤通信中，这些方法可用于模拟随机色散环境下非线性光波的传播；在量子物理中，可用于研究无序环境中玻色–爱因斯坦凝聚体的动力学行为。总体而言，本项目将为白噪声色散随机非线性薛定谔方程的数值模拟提供一套稳定、高效且可靠的理论与计算工具。通过保持原方程的关键结构，所提出的方法有望提高长时间数值模拟的准确性和可信度，并为相关领域的理论研究和实际应用提供新的方法与技术支持。

15303326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15303326.value: 两相MHD流的Cahn-Hilliard-MHD模型的有限元方法与数学分析

15303326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303326.value: In recent years, the study on the interaction of electromagnetic fields with two incompressible, immiscible and electrically conducting fluids is of great signification in the engineering, such as the Aluminum electrolysis cells, metallurgical industry, pump accelerators, MHD generators and fusion reactors. In this project, we consider a Cahn-Hilliard-MHD model with varying or constant density for the two-phase MHD flows. This model consists of Cahn-Hilliard equation (free interface), Navier-Stokes equations (hydrodynamics) and Maxwell equations (magnetic field) which are nonlinearly coupled through convection, stresses, and Lorentz forces. One straightforward idea to develop and analyze the numerical methods of the Cahn-Hilliard-MHD models is to combine the available approaches for the Cahn-Hilliard equation and MHD equation. However, the fact is that this combination idea only works partially since significant difficulties and technical issues arise from the strong coupling, nonlinearity, stiffness, and the varying density of the fluid. In this project, we plan to develop and analyze both coupled and decoupled numerical methods with both first and second order accuracy in time. We plan to utilize the energy analysis framework to carry out the optimal convergence analysis for these finite element methods. In addition to the regular Ritz projection and Maxwell projection, we plan to utilize the Ritz quasi-projection and Stokes quasi-projection, which was recently introduced in the literature, as a critical tool in the error estimates. Other critical analysis techniques include mathematical induction, superconvergence, different appropriate sets of test functions, and operator transformation. To efficiently and accurately solve the coupled nonlinear Cahn-Hilliard-MHD system, we need to develop a discretization scheme which is second order in time, unconditionally stable, linearized, and satisfying a discrete energy law. This is by no means an easy task as we have to conquer a few significant challenges including: (i) the coupling of the velocity and pressure through the incompressibility constraint; (ii) the stiffness of the phase equation associated with the interfacial width; (iii) the costly solver that involves varying density, and (iv) the coupling of the phase field variables, flow field variables, and magnetic field variables through nonlinear convection, stresses, and varying density. The key idea is based on a novel unified framework of zero-energy-contribution (ZEC) method and the scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) method. The scheme will integrate the second-order backward differential formula with the ZEC method to decouple the phase field, flow field, and magnetic field, and the second-order pressure-correction projection method to decouple velocity and pressure.

15303426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15303426.value: 調控手性傳遞以實現手性準二維雜化鈣鈦礦中自旋壽命的延長

15303426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303426.value: Spin-optoelectronic devices promise ultralow power consumption, nonvolatile information storage, and fast switching beyond conventional electronics by exploiting both electron charge and spin. Chiral quasi-2D hybrid perovskites are strong candidates for such devices because the heavy-element inorganic framework provides intrinsically strong spin-orbit coupling, while chiral ligands break inversion symmetry and imprint spin-textured bands, enabling magnet-free spin filtering through chirality-induced spin selectivity. In addition, their quasi-2D architecture adds multiple practical merits, including low-temperature solution processing, tunable Rashba or Dresselhaus splitting, dielectric confinement, and improved environmental stability under light, humidity, and heat. However, device performance is still hindered by short spin lifetimes, due to the limited understanding in how organic ligands transfer their chirality to the inorganic framework and influence the spin dynamics. Therefore, there is a critical need for an in-depth investigation and strategic manipulation of chirality transfer in chiral quasi-2D hybrid perovskites to prolong the spin lifetime. This project builds on our recent studies demonstrating that rationally engineering chirality transfer can deliver long-lived spin polarization in chiral 2D and quasi-2D hybrid perovskites. Using our well-established theory-guided investigation workflow, we aim to elucidate the mechanism of chirality transfer and the corresponding impact on spin dynamics, thereby strategically amplifying spin lifetime in chiral quasi-2D hybrid perovskites. By tackling these key parameters, the deliverables of this project include: (i) a unified descriptor network for quantitative evaluation of chirality transfer from organic ligands to the hybrid perovskites; (ii) a roadmap for modulating chirality transfer and spin dynamics through halogenated chiral ligands engineering; and (iii) a set of mechanism-grounded design principles for achieving substantially amplified spin lifetime in chiral quasi-2D hybrid perovskites. Our preliminary results demonstrate that n = 5 quasi-2D perovskites functionalized with fluorinated chiral ligands can effectively enhance the chirality transfer, strengthen spin splitting, and increase out-of-plane spin polarization, delivering substantially prolonged spin lifetime. This project will elucidate the mechanisms that control chirality transfer and translate them into actionable design guidelines for prolonging spin lifetimes in hybrid perovskites. Beyond advancing fundamental understanding, the resulting framework will enable rational materials selection and process optimization, shorten iteration cycles between computation and synthesis, and accelerate device development in perovskite spin-optoelectronics. 自旋光電子器件通過協同利用電子的電荷與自旋自由度，有望突破傳統電子器件的性能瓶頸，實現超低功耗、非揮發性資訊儲存及高速開關切換等關鍵功能。手性準二維雜化鈣鈦礦因其獨特的結構與性質，成為構建此類器件的理想候選材料。其含有重元素的無機骨架可提供本徵強自旋–軌道耦合，而手性有機配體則能打破空間反演對稱性，並在能帶中誘發特定的自旋織構，進而通過手性誘導自旋選擇性效應實現無需外加磁場的自旋過濾。此外，該類材料兼具低溫溶液加工性、可調的自旋劈裂、顯著的介電限域效應，以及在光照、濕度和熱應力條件下較優的環境穩定性。然而，目前基於此類材料的器件性能仍受到自旋壽命較短的嚴重制約，根本原因在於對有機配體如何將手性有效傳遞至無機骨架，以及這一過程如何影響自旋動力學的認識尚不充分。因此，亟需深入探究並精確調控手性準二維雜化鈣鈦礦中的手性傳遞行為，以實現自旋壽命的大幅提升。 我們前期的研究表明，通過合理設計手性傳遞路徑，可在手性二維及準二維雜化鈣鈦礦中實現長壽命自旋極化。本項研究擬系統揭示手性傳遞的微觀機制及其對自旋動力學的影響規律，並據此發展提升手性準二維雜化鈣鈦礦自旋壽命的有效策略。具體預期成果包括：（i）建立統一描述符，實現對有機配體向雜化鈣鈦礦骨架手性傳遞程度的定量評估；（ii）構建基於鹵代手性配體工程的調控策略，明確手性傳遞與自旋動力學之間的關聯；（iii）提出一套基於微觀機制的材料設計準則，顯著延長手性準二維雜化鈣鈦礦的自旋壽命。本項目將釐清決定手性傳遞及自旋動力學的關鍵因素，並將這些認識轉化為具有實踐指導意義的鈣鈦礦材料設計原則。除了深化對手性雜化鈣鈦礦自旋物理本質的基礎理解，所建立的理論框架還將有效助推材料的理性篩選與合成工藝優化，縮短理論預測與實驗驗證間的迭代週期，從而加速鈣鈦礦自旋光電子器件的研發進程。

15303526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15303526.value: 求解非光滑优化约束问题的一阶方法复杂度界

15303526.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15303526.value: Prof LIU, Xin Prof QI, Houduo

15303526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303526.value: Many problems in artificial intelligence (AI) and operations research (e.g., fairness constrained learning and Boolean quadratic programs) remain challenging because they are nonconvex, potentially nonsmooth, and involve nonlinear function constraints. While first-order methods are extensively adopted in practice, the theoretical understanding of their oracle complexity for solving these function-constrained problems remains incomplete: existing upper and lower complexity bounds do not align, leaving uncertainty about how close current algorithms are to optimal performance. This project aims to bridge the existing theoretical gap through a two-fold strategy. First, we will develop a smoothed exact penalty approach, strategically integrating the robustness and exactness benefits of fixed-parameter penalties with the computational efficiency of quadratic penalties. Preliminary analysis demonstrates that this approach yields improved oracle complexity upper bounds in deterministic optimization scenarios. We will further extend this complexity analysis to the more general expectation-valued settings widely encountered in AI. Second, we will rigorously establish complexity lower bounds by constructing a hard problem instance. This theoretical investigation will clarify the precise conditions under which optimal oracle complexity can be achieved, thereby providing a complete and informative characterization of algorithmic performance limits. To facilitate immediate practical impact and wider adoption, we will deliver an open-source software package featuring a user-friendly interface, comprehensive documentation, rigorous testing, and reproducible benchmark problems drawn from representative function-constrained nonconvex tasks. Overall, this work will establish clearer, tighter theoretical foundations for first-order methods under function constraints, accompanied by practical tools that significantly enhance the applicability, reliability, and computational efficiency of constrained optimization in AI and operations research. 人工智能与运筹学中的许多问题（如公平性约束学习、二次规划）至今仍具挑战性，原因在于它们非凸、可能非光滑，且涉及非线性函数约束。尽管一阶方法在实践中被广泛采用，但对其求解此类函数约束问题的谕示复杂度的理论理解仍不完善：现有的上下界并不吻合，导致我们无法确知当前算法与最优性能之间的差距。 本项目旨在通过双重策略弥合这一理论鸿沟。其一，我们将发展一种平滑精确罚方法，策略性地将固定参数罚方法的鲁棒性与精确性优势，同二次罚方法的计算效率融为一体。初步分析表明，该方法在确定性优化场景下可给出更优的复杂度上界。我们还将把这一复杂度分析进一步推广到人工智能中广泛存在的期望值场景。其二，我们将通过构造困难问题实例，严格建立复杂度下界。这项理论研究将厘清能够实现最优复杂度的精确条件，从而为算法性能极限提供完整的刻画。 为推动即时实际影响与更广泛的应用，我们将交付一个开源软件包，包含用户友好的接口、完整的文档、严格的测试，以及取自代表性函数约束非凸任务的可复现基准问题。总体而言，本工作将为函数约束下一阶方法奠定更清晰、更紧致的理论基础，并提供实用工具，从而显著提升约束优化在人工智能与运筹学中的适用性、可靠性和计算效率。

15303826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15303826.value: 針對細胞核內微蛋白譜的時空刻畫和機制研究

15303826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303826.value: Microproteins (MPs), encoded by small open reading frames, represent a vast, underexplored dimension of the human proteome with critical implications for cancer, development, and immunity. Despite their significance, nuclear MPs remain poorly characterized due to limitations in predictive methods that fail to capture their localization and dynamic behaviour. Leveraging our previously developed proteogenomic platform, which optimizes proteomics workflows for MP detection, this project aims to map the spatiotemporal landscape of nuclear MPs and elucidate their roles in fundamental cellular processes. Our preliminary spatiotemporal proteomics identified 153 nuclear MPs, including 51 with potential chromatin association and 41 exhibiting cell cycle-dependent dynamics. Orthogonal validation via immunostaining and imaging confirmed nuclear residency, while select MPs were implicated in regulating cell proliferation, cycle progression, and tissue-specific functions. Through three integrated aims, we will construct the first comprehensive, temporally resolved atlas of nuclear MPs and decode their mechanistic contributions to cell-cycle control: (1) systematically profile and validate nuclear MP translation across cellular states; (2) dissect MP-driven regulation of cell morphology and phenotypes using multi-omics integration; and (3) uncover MP-specific interactions with proteins and genomic loci to reveal regulatory mechanisms. These aims will be supported by robust bioinformatics to assess evolutionary conservation, pathway integration, and clinical relevance. This project will yield novel insights into MPs that shape chromatin architecture and checkpoint control, alongside openly accessible datasets and analytical tools. Responding to recent calls from Nature and Science, our work addresses a pivotal gap in proteome research, laying the groundwork for innovative drug targets, biomarkers, and therapeutic strategies in translational medicine. 微蛋白（MPs）由小型開放閱讀框編碼，代表了人類蛋白質組中一個廣闊且尚未被充分探索的維度，對癌症、發育和免疫具有重要影響。儘管意義重大，但由於現有預測方法難以捕捉其定位和動態行為，細胞核微蛋白的特徵仍不明確。依託我們先前開發的蛋白質基因組學平台——該平台優化了用於微蛋白檢測的蛋白質組學工作流程，本項目旨在繪製細胞核微蛋白的時空分佈圖譜，並闡明其在基本細胞過程中的作用。我們的初步時空蛋白質組學研究鑑定出153種細胞核微蛋白，其中51種具有潛在的染色質關聯，41種表現出細胞週期依賴的動態變化。通過免疫染色和成像進行的正交驗證確認了其細胞核定位，同時發現部分微蛋白參與調控細胞增殖、週期進程及組織特異性功能。通過三個整合性研究目標，我們將構建首個全面的、具有時間分辨率的細胞核微蛋白圖譜，並解析其在細胞週期調控中的機制性貢獻：（1）系統性地分析和驗證不同細胞狀態下細胞核微蛋白的翻譯情況；（2）利用多組學整合技術，剖析微蛋白對細胞形態和表型的調控作用；（3）揭示微蛋白與蛋白質及基因組位點的特異性相互作用，以闡明其調控機制。這些目標將得到強大的生物信息學支持，以評估進化保守性、通路整合及臨床相關性。本項目將產生關於塑造染色質結構和檢查點控制的微蛋白的新見解，同時提供開放獲取的數據集和分析工具。響應《自然》和《科學》雜誌近期的呼籲，我們的工作將填補蛋白質組研究中的一個關鍵空白，為轉化醫學中的創新藥物靶點、生物標誌物和治療策略奠定基礎。

15304226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15304226.value: 嫦娥五號與嫦娥六號月壤樣品中膠結質的研究

15304226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15304226.value: Humanity is entering a new era of lunar exploration, marked by the Chinese Chang’e-5 (CE-5) and Chang’e-6 (CE-6) missions, which returned the youngest lunar samples to date and the first samples from the farside of the Moon, respectively. These samples offer an unprecedented opportunity to understand the evolution of the Moon. The next phase of lunar exploration will involve establishing a lasting human presence and utilizing lunar resources. These activities require a thorough understanding of the engineering properties of the surface of the Moon, which is covered by a layer of fine-grained soil, termed lunar regolith. Agglutinates – small, glassy, porous grains formed by micrometeorite impacts – are a major component of lunar regolith, comprising up to 60-70% of its volume and significantly influencing its physical, thermal, and mechanical properties. However, the processes governing agglutinate formation and their effects on regolith properties are not yet well understood. This project leverages access to multiple batches of CE-5 and CE-6 samples to conduct a detailed comparative analysis of lunar regolith, focusing on agglutinates. We will employ non-destructive, high-resolution three-dimensional X-ray computed tomography imaging and machine learning methods to automatically identify agglutinate particles from millions of lunar regolith particles. This will create a unique dataset that allows robust statistical comparisons between the agglutinates in CE-5 and CE-6 samples. Our goal is to reveal how agglutinates characteristic change over the geological history, providing new insights into how the surface of the Moon evolved. Furthermore, we will use an integrated experimental and computational approach to evaluate how agglutinates influence the engineering properties of the lunar regolith. This involves: a) Creating highly realistic replica lunar regolith(known as the lunar regolith simulant) that includes agglutinates matching the characteristics of real samples; b) Measuring the thermal and mechanical properties of the lunar regolith simulants in ground-based lab tests; c) Performing innovative ground-based Moon gravity experiment to study the porosity of the lunar regolith; d) Building, calibrating, and upscaling numerical models that can predict lunar regolith behaviour under coupled thermal-mechanical conditions. Uniquely positioned with access to precious lunar regolith samples, our previous experience in sample analysis, and advanced research facilities, this project is highly feasible. The outcomes will advance our understanding of the Moon surface evolution process, guide the design and execution of future missions, and enable the use of lunar resources, directly contributing to humanity's sustainable return to the Moon. 人類正進入月球探索的新時代，其中以中國嫦娥五號和嫦娥六號任務尤為重要；兩者分別帶回了迄今最年輕的月球樣品，以及首批來自月球背面的樣品。這些樣品為理解月球的演化提供了前所未有的機會。下一階段的月球探索將涉及建立長期人類駐留能力及利用月球資源。這些活動需要我們深入了解月球表面的工程性質；月球表面覆蓋著一層細粒土壤，稱為月壤。膠結質是月壤的主要組成部分，為由微隕石撞擊形成的小型玻璃質多孔顆粒，佔月壤體積可达超過50%，並顯著影響其物理、熱學及力學性質。然而，控制膠結質形成的過程及其對月壤性質的影響，目前仍未得到充分理解。 本項目將利用多批次嫦娥五號和嫦娥六號樣品，對月壤進行詳細的比較分析，重點聚焦於膠結質。我們將採用非破壞性、高解像度三維 X 射線電腦斷層掃描成像技術，以及機器學習方法，從數以百萬計的月壤顆粒中自動識別膠結質顆粒。這將建立一個獨特的數據集，使我們能夠對嫦娥五號與嫦娥六號樣品中的膠結質進行可靠的統計比較。我們的目標是揭示膠結質特徵如何隨地質歷史而變化，從而為理解月球表面的演化提供新的見解。 此外，我們將採用結合實驗與計算的綜合方法，評估膠結質對月壤工程性質的影響。具體包括：製備高度逼真的月壤複製樣品，即月壤模擬物，並使其中的膠結質特徵與真實樣品相匹配；通過地面實驗室測試，量測這些複製月壤的熱學及力學性質；建立、校準並尺度提升數值模型，以預測月壤在熱—力耦合條件下的行為。 本項目的獨特優勢，包括已經獲取的珍貴月壤樣品、團隊以往在樣品分析方面的經驗，以及先進的研究設施，因此具有高度可行性。項目成果將推進我們對月球表面演化過程的理解，為未來月球任務設計提供指引，並促進月球資源利用，從而直接助力人類可持續重返月球。

15304326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15304326.value: 帶邏輯增長源之趨化模型行波解的非線性穩定性

15304326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15304326.value: This proposal is dedicated to establishing the nonlinear stability of traveling wave solutions for the aggregation-type chemotaxis models with a logistic source on the cell density, encompassing both attractive and repulsive scenarios, as well as the parabolic-elliptic case (where one component follows a parabolic equation and the other an elliptic equation) and the parabolic-parabolic case (where both components are governed by parabolic equations). Over the past decade, extensive research has been conducted on the existence of traveling wave solutions for such models; however, the stability of these solutions, a question of fundamental significance to the field, remains entirely unexplored. This proposal thus represents an initial and critical step toward addressing this profound and long-standing research gap. A key challenge in this endeavor stems from the cross-diffusion structure inherent to chemotaxis models, which severely limits the availability of mathematical tools for analyzing nonlinear stability of traveling wave solutions with no proven and empirical methods currently existing. Notably, addressing the complex strong couplings induced by cross-diffusion constitutes a novel challenge that has not been confronted in existing literature, requiring innovative analytical approaches beyond traditional methodologies. To overcome this barrier, this proposal will employ a comprehensive analytical framework, integrating weighted energy estimates with carefully chosen weight functions and sophisticated coupling intertwined estimates alongside the strategic application of various functional inequalities. Prior to conducting the stability analysis, it is imperative to derive several novel auxiliary results that are indispensable to the stability analysis yet have not been established in existing works. These include, but are not limited to, the monotonicity properties and comparative pointwise estimates of traveling wave solutions, presenting a second critical challenge to be addressed. By leveraging a diverse suite of mathematical tools to tackle these challenges, this research project aims to not only achieve its immediate goals but also open a new and rigorous avenue for future investigations into the traveling wave solutions of chemotaxis-growth models. 本研究計劃旨在建立帶有邏輯增長源（作用於細胞密度）之聚集型趨化模型行波解的非線性穩定性，研究範圍同時涵蓋吸引與排斥兩種情形，以及拋物‑橢圓情形（其中一個分量遵循拋物型方程，另一個分量遵循橢圓型方程）與拋物‑拋物情形（兩個分量皆由拋物型方程所支配）。過去十年間，已有大量研究針對此類模型之行波解的存在性展開探討；然而，對該領域具根本重要性的行波解穩定性問題，至今仍完全未獲探索。因此，本研究計劃是邁向填補此一重大且長期存在之研究缺口的首要關鍵步驟。 本研究面對的一項核心挑戰源自趨化模型固有的交叉擴散結構，此結構大幅限制可用於分析行波解非線性穩定性的數學工具，目前既無已驗證也無經驗性的處理方法。值得注意的是，處理由交叉擴散所引發的複雜強耦合效應，是現有文獻尚未面對過的嶄新難題，需要運用超越傳統方法的創新分析手段。為克服該障礙，本計劃將採用一套完備的分析框架：結合選取合適權重函數的加權能量估計、精巧的耦合交織估計，並策略性運用各類泛函不等式。 在開展穩定性分析之前，必須先推導若干嶄新的輔助結果。該等結果對穩定性分析不可或缺，但現有研究中尚未建立，當中包括（但不限於）行波解的單調性質以及逐點比較估計，這構成本計劃需要處理的第二項關鍵挑戰。透過運用多樣的數學工具處理上述各項難題，本研究項目除力求達成直接研究目標外，亦旨在為日後探討趨化‑增長模型的行波解開闢一條嚴謹的全新研究路徑。

15305326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15305326.value: 具有非光滑数据的偏微分方程 Parareal 算法收敛性分析

15305326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15305326.value: The numerical solution of evolution partial differential equations (PDEs) often requires extensive computational time, particularly in long-time simulations, due to the inherently sequential nature of traditional time-stepping methods. The parareal method, a leading parallel-in-time (PinT) algorithm, offers a promising solution by introducing parallelism in the time domain. While its practical success has been demonstrated across various applications, several theoretical aspects remain unresolved. This project aims to address key gaps in the convergence theory of the parareal method, particularly for nonlinear parabolic equations with low-regularity data. Such scenarios frequently arise in inverse problems and optimal control, making the developed methods highly applicable to these areas. This project is divided into three key parts. First, we aim to establish a rigorous convergence analysis of the parareal algorithm for nonlinear parabolic equations with nonsmooth initial data. While previous studies have observed that the convergence behavior of the parareal algorithm for nonlinear problems often mirrors that of linear problems when the coarse propagator has sufficient resolution, there are currently no theoretical guarantees to support this observation. By refining existing frameworks for the analysis of nonlinear ODEs and incorporating error analysis techniques designed for nonsmooth data, we intend to show the linear convergence of the parareal iteration and provide a comprehensive analysis of its optimal convergence factor. Second, we will explore the use of linear multistep methods, such as the high-order backward differentiation formula (BDF), as fine propagators within the parareal algorithm. While most existing studies assume the fine propagator to be either an exact solver or a single-step method, linear multistep methods, which are particularly effective for parabolic equations, introduce additional challenges due to their dependence on multiple previous steps for initialization. To address these challenges, we will develop a novel initialization strategy to ensure the stable convergence of parareal iterations for parabolic equations with nonsmooth data and analyze the convergence factor using the generating function technique. Finally, we will explore the application of parareal algorithms to inverse problems, focusing on parameter identification in evolution PDEs. To accelerate the computation of repeatedly solving the direct problem during iterative inversion, we will integrate iterative inversion algorithms with the parareal method, improving computational efficiency while rigorously proving the global convergence rate. Besides, we aim to develop an error analysis framework that combines the conditional stability of inverse problems with the numerical analysis of the fully discrete scheme and the parareal method. 演化型偏微分方程（PDE）的数值求解通常面临显著的计算挑战，尤其是在长时间模拟中，这是由于传统时间步进方法具有内在的顺序执行特性。Parareal 方法作为一种重要的时间并行（parallel-in-time, PinT）算法，通过在时间方向引入并行性，为此类问题提供了一种有前景的解决方案。尽管其在多种应用中的实际效果已得到验证，但若干理论问题仍有待解决。本项目旨在弥补 Parareal 方法收敛理论中的关键不足，特别关注具有低正则性数据的非线性抛物型方程；这类问题常见于反问题和最优控制中。 首先，我们拟针对具有非光滑初始数据的非线性抛物型方程，建立 Parareal 算法的严格收敛性分析。已有研究观察到，当粗传播算子具有足够分辨率时，Parareal 算法在非线性问题中的收敛行为往往类似于线性问题中的情形，但目前尚无理论保证支持这一观察。通过改进现有的非线性常微分方程分析框架，并结合针对非光滑数据的误差分析技术，我们计划证明 Parareal 迭代的线性收敛性，并对其收敛因子进行细致分析。 其次，我们将研究在线性多步方法作为 Parareal 算法中精细传播算子时的应用，例如高阶后向差分公式（BDF）。现有大多数研究通常假设精细传播算子为精确求解器或单步方法，而线性多步方法对抛物型方程尤为有效，但其初始化依赖多个前序时间步，因此会带来额外挑战。为解决这些问题，我们将发展一种新的初始化策略，以确保具有非光滑数据的抛物型方程在 Parareal 迭代中的稳定收敛，并利用生成函数技术分析其收敛因子。 最后，我们将探索 Parareal 算法在反问题中的应用，重点研究演化型偏微分方程中的参数识别问题。为加速迭代反演过程中对正问题的反复求解，我们将把迭代反演算法与 Parareal 方法相结合，在提高计算效率的同时，严格证明其全局收敛速率。此外，我们还旨在建立一个误差分析框架，将反问题的条件稳定性、全离散格式的数值分析以及 Parareal 方法的误差分析有机结合起来。

15305926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15305926.value: 三維張量對象的統計學習與推斷及其在超廣角影像中的應用

15305926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15305926.value: The ultrawide-field (UWF) fundus image is an advancing ocular image that provides most compressive information of the retina. School of Optometry of PolyU possesses the Optos Daytona device for UWF fundus scanning, and has collected two datasets: the pair-eye UWF fundus images for high myopia screening, and repeated measured UWF fundus scans of diabetic retinopathy patients for progression monitoring. Ophthalmologists look for more efficient ophthalmic diagnosis based on UWF fundus biomarkers, and hence raise the need of new statistical learning methodologies and theories. Topic 1 studies a deep multivariate regression that associates multiple mixed-type responses with dependent tensor/image covariates through the Vision Transformer (ViT). The motivation is the classification of high myopia of both eyes based on pair-eye images. We derive a new copula loss for mixed-type multiple responses and adapt it to a ViT to incorporate conditional dependence information among responses given the image inputs. To the proposed AI model, we plan to overcome overfitting issue and establish interpretable asymptotic theories and demonstrate the theoretical optimality. The outcomes are expected to activate automatic myopia screening to save the costs and human resources, and contribute to inference of deep multi-task learning. Topic 2 aims to monitor diabetic retinopathy progression through UWF fundus image series. We treat 3D images as high-dimensional 3-way tensor-valued observations, and turn the problem into detecting multiple change-points of the tensor-variate sequence. We propose a 3-dimensional binary latent vector to model change-point scheme so as to capture the inherent 3-mode structure under the Tucker-type tensor latent structure. We plan to explore the estimation procedure and establish the corresponding inferential theories. Such results are expected to fill the research gap in change-point detection for tensor-valued sequences, besides faciliating the practical diabetic retinopathy progression monitoring. Topic 3 aims to develop a novel latent tensor factor structure with inferential theories. Tucker tensor factor model is widely employed though it may not be the optimal choice for downscaling tasks. We plan to derive a CP-type tensor factor model that assumes the vector-factor-model structure on the basis fibers. The spirit is motivated by the PI’s success in presenting a low-order tensor latent structure that is optimal in 2D-image reconstruction. We will explore quasi-likelihood estimation on the components of the proposed latent tensor structure, and establish the necessary inferential theory, providing new sharper tools for analyzing tensor-valued data. The above works, once completed, is also applicable beyond the ophthalmic science. 超廣角（UWF）眼底影像是一種先進的眼科影像，可提供較全面的視網膜資訊。香港理工大學眼科視光學院配備 Optos Daytona 超廣角眼底掃描設備，並已收集兩個數據集：一是用於高度近視篩查的雙眼配對超廣角眼底影像，二是用於監測糖尿病視網膜病變進展的患者重複測量超廣角眼底掃描資料。眼科醫生期望基於超廣角眼底影像生物標誌物實現更高效的眼科診斷，因而產生了對新的統計學習方法與理論的需求。 研究主題一研究一類深度多變量迴歸模型，通過視覺 Transformer（ViT）將多個混合類型反應變量與具有相依性的張量/影像協變量建立關聯。其研究動機是基於雙眼配對影像對雙眼高度近視進行聯合分類。我們將構建一個適用於混合類型多重反應變量的新型 Copula 損失函數，並將其引入 ViT，以納入在給定影像輸入條件下各反應變量之間的條件相依資訊。針對所提出的人工智能模型，我們計劃解決過度擬合問題，建立具有可解釋性的漸近理論，並證明其理論最優性。預期成果將有助於推動基於影像的自動化近視篩查，從而節省成本和人力資源，並對深度多任務學習的統計推斷理論作出貢獻。 研究主題二旨在通過超廣角眼底影像序列監測糖尿病視網膜病變的進展。我們將三維影像視為高維三階張量值觀測，從而將該問題轉化為檢測張量值序列中的多個變點。我們提出一個三維二元潛在向量來刻畫變點機制，以捕捉 Tucker 型張量潛在結構所具有的內在三模態結構。我們計劃研究相應的估計程序並建立相關的統計推斷理論。預期研究成果將填補張量值序列變點檢測領域的研究空白，同時有助於糖尿病視網膜病變進展的實際監測。 研究主題三旨在發展一種新型潛在張量因子結構，並建立相應的統計推斷理論。Tucker 張量因子模型已被廣泛應用，但在降尺度任務中未必是最優選擇。我們計劃構建一個 CP 型張量因子模型，在基底纖維上引入向量因子模型結構。這一研究思路源於項目負責人此前提出的、在二維影像重建中具有最優性的低階張量潛在結構。我們將研究所提出潛在張量結構各組成部分的準似然估計，並建立必要的統計推斷理論，從而為張量值數據分析提供新的、更精確的工具。上述研究完成後，亦可拓展應用至眼科學以外的領域。

15306326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15306326.value: 高性能三元鹵化銅發光材料的AI輔助設計與合成

15306326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15306326.value: Material innovations have remained a critical task advancing lighting and display technologies in the last decades, propelled by the rapid growth of the light-emitting diode (LED) market (China’s LED lighting exports approach US$50 billion annually). Conventional LED emitters such as GaN-based semiconductors and CdSe quantum dots have achieved commercial success, but they are limited by issues of either high material/processing cost or environmental and health concerns. Next-generation light-emitting semiconductors have thus been identified as a strategically critical research area with a focus on new materials and high-efficiency devices. In this context, metal-halide perovskites have emerged as promising luminescent materials due to their high brightness, narrow emission linewidth (high color purity), and tunable bandgaps covering the full visible spectrum. However, critical challenges remain: conventional lead-halide perovskites contain toxic Pb and suffer from poor long-term stability, and achieving a tunable bandgap without sacrificing photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) is difficult due to issues like halide phase segregation and nonradiative recombination. These limitations hinder the realization of high-performance perovskite LEDs (PeLEDs), and it remains an important and urgent task to develop lead-free light emitters that simultaneously deliver high efficiency, high luminance, and long operational lifetimes. This project aims to overcome these challenges by developing lead-free ternary copper-halides (TCH) with tunable bandgaps and high PLQY through an AI-assisted materials design strategy. TCH are low-toxicity and cost-effective, but a systematic and innovative methodology is needed to fully exploit their compositional flexibility and structural diversity for optimal optical performance. We will integrate large language models (LLM) and machine learning (Bayesian optimization) with automated high-throughput synthesis and characterization in a closed-loop platform to rapidly identify, optimize, and produce high-performance TCH emitters. Key tasks include screening potential copper halide compositions for desirable bandgaps, optimizing synthesis conditions (e.g., ligand chemistry, solvent, temperature) to improve crystallinity and reduce defects, performing high-throughput optical/electrical characterization to evaluate PLQY and stability, and ultimately fabricating prototype PeLED devices with high external quantum efficiency (EQE). This AI-driven closed-loop approach enables a paradigm shift from trial-and-error experimentation to rapid, data-guided optimization, dramatically accelerating the innovation cycle. The expected outcomes include not only novel, low-toxicity, high-efficiency light-emitting materials but also a general AI-enabled paradigm for accelerating materials discovery. Successful completion of this project will advance the emerging lead-free lighting and display technologies, positioning Hong Kong as a leader in this field with a crucial technological edge, training the much-needed talents for sustainable development. 在過去幾十年裡，受發光二極體（LED）市場快速成長（中國LED照明年出口額已接近500億美元）的推動，材料創新一直是推動照明與顯示器技術進步的關鍵任務。儘管傳統的LED發光材料（如氮化鎵半導體和硒化鎘量子點）已實現商業化應用，但它們仍受限於高昂的材料或加工成本，以及環境與健康的隱患。因此，開發新型材料與高效能裝置的下一代發光半導體技術，已成為具有戰略意義的研究重點。在此背景下，金屬鹵化物鈣鈦礦因其高亮度、窄發射線寬（高色純度）以及覆蓋全可見光光譜的可調帶隙特性，成為極具潛力的發光材料。然而，該領域仍面臨嚴峻挑戰：傳統的鉛鹵鈣鈦礦含有毒性鉛元素且長期穩定性較差；此外，受鹵化物相分離和非輻射複合等問題影響，要在不犧牲光致發光量子產率（PLQY）的前提下實現帶隙調節，難度極大。這些限制阻礙了高性能鈣鈦礦LED（PeLEDs）的實現，因此，開發兼具高效率、高亮度和長使用壽命的無鉛發光材料，仍然是一項重要且緊迫的任務。 本計畫旨在透過人工智慧輔助的材料設計策略，開發出具有可調帶隙和高光致發光量子產率（PLQY）的無鉛三元鹵化銅（TCH）材料，從而克服現有挑戰。儘管鹵化銅材料具有低毒性和成本效益，但仍需採用系統化且創新的方法，充分利用其成分靈活性和結構多樣性，以實現最佳的光學性能。我們將把大語言模型（LLM）和機器學習（貝葉斯優化）與自動化高通量合成及表徵技術整合於閉環平台中，以快速篩選、最佳化並製備高性能的滷化銅發光材料。關鍵任務包括：篩選具有理想帶隙的鹵化銅成分；優化合成條件（如配體化學性質、溶劑、溫度）以提高結晶度並減少缺陷；開展高通量光電表徵以評估PLQY和穩定性；以及最終製備出具有高外量子效率（EQE）的鈣鈦礦發光二極管（PeLED）原型器件。這種由人工智慧驅動的閉環方法將推動研究範式從傳統的「試誤法」轉變為快速、數據導向的最佳化模式，從而顯著縮短創新週期。 預期成果不僅包括新型、低毒、高效的發光材料，還涵蓋一種由通用人工智慧賦能的、旨在加速材料發現的新典範。該計畫的成功實施將推動新興無鉛照明與顯示技術的發展，確立香港在該領域的領先地位與關鍵技術優勢，並為永續發展培養急需的人才。

15306426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15306426.value: 適用於高性能電子器件的二維半導體設計

15306426.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15306426.value: Prof Wu, Jing Prof YANG, Shengyuan

15306426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15306426.value: Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors such as monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have emerged as promising candidates for post-Moore electronic devices. Despite their potential, the application of 2D semiconductors in high-performance electronics has been hampered by their low carrier mobility at room temperature, which is primarily attributed to strong electron-phonon scattering. Recent studies have demonstrated that introducing rippled lattice structures in 2D MoS2 can significantly enhance its room-temperature carrier mobility. However, the understanding of underlying mechanisms responsible for this improvement remains limited, and the applicability of this strategy to other 2D semiconductors has not been systematically explored. In this proposal, we aim to investigate the mechanisms underlying the improved carrier mobility in rippled 2D semiconductors and translate the understanding to develop high-performance 2D field effect transistor (FET) devices. To achieve this, we plan to employ a combination of advanced high-throughput first-principles calculations, transport simulation, and experimental validation.
