First, we will perform in-depth electronic, phonon, and transport calculations to reveal the effects of rippled lattice structures on the carrier mobility in 2D MoS2, in which various contributions such as electronic structure, phonon dispersion, strain gradient, and dielectric screening will be examined; Second, we will identify the optimum rippled configurations such as ripple shape, height, and length to maximize the room-temperature carrier mobility; Third, building on insights gained from 2D MoS2, we will explore ripple effects in other promising 2D semiconductors such as WSe2, black phosphorene, and InSe, which exhibit diverse lattice symmetries, electronic band features, and electron-phonon interaction, providing a broad platform to validate the generalizability of the ripple engineering strategy; Finally, we will fabricate 2D FET devices using the optimized rippled 2D semiconductors and evaluate their performance. By combining high-throughput calculations and experimental validation, this proposed research is expected to deepen our understanding of ripple-induced mobility enhancement and accelerate the development of high-performance 2D FET devices. Successful implementation of this research could pave the way for transformative advancements in 2D electronics, enabling their applications in areas such as integrated circuits, flexible electronics, and next-generation computing devices. 二維（2D）半導體，如單層過渡金屬二硫屬化物（transition metal dichalcogenides, TMDs），已成為後摩爾時代電子器件的有前景候選材料。儘管其潛力巨大，二維半導體在高效能電子器件中的應用仍受到其室溫下低載子遷移率的限制，而這主要歸因於強烈的電子－聲子散射。近期研究已證實，在二維 MoS₂ 中引入彎曲晶格結構，可顯著提升其室溫載子遷移率。然而，對於造成此一提升的底層機制，目前理解仍相當有限；此外，該策略是否適用於其他二維半導體，也尚未被系統性地探討。 在本計畫中，我們旨在研究彎曲二維半導體中載子遷移率提升的內在機制，並將相關理解轉化為高效能二維場效應管（field-effect transistor, FET）器件的開發。為達成此目標，我們計畫結合先進的高通量第一原理計算、輸運模擬與實驗驗證。首先，我們將進行深入的電子、聲子與輸運計算，以揭示彎曲晶格結構對二維 MoS₂ 載子遷移率的影響；其中將檢視電子結構、聲子色散、應變梯度及介電屏蔽等各項貢獻。其次，我們將辨識最佳的彎曲結構配置，例如彎曲形狀、高度與長度，以最大化室溫載子遷移率。第三，基於從二維 MoS₂ 所獲得的洞見，我們將進一步探討其他具潛力之二維半導體中的彎曲效應，例如 WSe₂、黑磷烯與 InSe。這些材料具有多樣的晶格對稱性、電子能帶特徵與電子－聲子交互作用，可作為廣泛的平台，用以驗證彎曲工程策略的一般適用性。最後，我們將利用最佳化後的彎曲二維半導體製作二維 FET 器件，並評估其效能。 透過結合高通量計算與實驗驗證，本研究預期將深化我們對結構彎曲誘發之遷移率提升機制的理解，並加速高效能二維 FET 器件的發展。本研究若能成功實施，將有望為二維電子學帶來突破性進展，推動其在積體電路、柔性電子與下一代運算器件等領域中的應用

15306626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15306626.value: 環保無鉛鈣鈦礦高效太陽能電池材料

15306626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15306626.value: To search the solutions for decarbonization, renewable solar energy utilization stands out as one of the most promising solutions. Lead-based perovskite solar cells as a low-cost alternative of silicon-based photovoltaics (PV) have achieved remarkable power conversion efficiencies in the past decade. However, their commercial viability is significantly hindered by the use of highly toxic heavy metal lead. Tin-based perovskites are promising lead-free options due to their non-toxic nature and favourable optoelectronic properties, but they currently suffer from rapid oxidation of Sn(II) to Sn(IV), which creates defects (Sn vacancies) and unwanted p-doping in the materials. These problems cause poor efficiency and short device lifetime. As a result, the efficiencies and operational stability of current Sn-perovskite cells remain far below their lead-based counterparts. This project aims to develop eco-friendly tin-based high-efficiency perovskite solar cells by innovating perovskite composition and interfacial engineering to overcome these limitations. Built on our recent success in achieving certified record efficiency in tin-based solar cells, we will innovate materials engineering strategies including designing suitable additives and compositional modifications to suppress Sn (II) oxidation and improve the crystallinity of the perovskite films. By forming a robust perovskite/charge transport interface, the devices will better resist moisture, oxygen, and thermal stress. This project will combine experimental fabrication and characterization to provide a unique perspective on the degradation mechanisms of Sn-perovskites and how our innovations enhance their ion transport and stability. Through this, we seek to establish a clear structure–function relationship that guides the design of stable lead-free perovskite materials for indoor PV application. The target outcome is to achieve tin-based perovskite solar cells with new record power conversion efficiencies above 20% and the ability to operate under continuous illumination for over 3000 hours. The expected outcomes will lead to next-generation lead-free perovskite PV technology one step closer to commercialization. Such solar cells are expected to be a game changer in renewable energy, eliminating the environmental hazard of lead and enabling lightweight, high-performance solar cells that offers sustainable energy applications with minimal environment impact. The successful implementation of the project will significantly contribute to a decarbonized local economy and the “Hong Kong’s Climate Action Plan 2050” in promoting the utilization of renewable energy and the growth of clean energy industry sectors. 為尋求減碳解決方案，可再生太陽能的利用無疑是最具前景的途徑之一。鉛基鈣鈦礦太陽能電池作為矽基光伏（PV）的高性價比替代方案，在過去十年間取得了卓越的光電轉換效率。然而，因其含有高毒性的重金屬鉛，嚴重阻礙了其商業化進程。錫基鈣鈦礦因其無毒特性及優異的光電性質，成為極具潛力的無鉛替代方案。但目前錫基材料面臨二價錫（Sn(II)）易快速氧化為四價錫（Sn(IV)）的難題，這會產生缺陷（錫空位）並導致不必要的 p 型摻雜。這些問題導致器件效率低下且壽命較短。因此，現有錫基鈣鈦礦電池的效率和運行穩定性仍遠落後於鉛基電池。 本項目旨在透過創新鈣鈦礦成分及界面工程來克服上述局限，開發出環保、高效的錫基鈣鈦礦太陽能電池。基於我們近期在錫基太陽能電池中取得認證世界紀錄效率的成功基礎，我們將創新材料工程策略，包括設計合適的添加劑與成分改性，以抑制 Sn(II) 的氧化並提升鈣鈦礦薄膜的晶體質量。透過構建穩固的鈣鈦礦/電荷傳輸界面，器件將能更好地抵抗水汽、氧氣及熱應力。 本項目將結合實驗製備與表徵技術，為錫基鈣鈦礦的降解機制以及我們的創新技術如何提升其離子傳輸與穩定性提供獨特視角。在此基礎上，我們致力於建立清晰的「結構—功能」關係，以指導用於室內光伏應用的穩定無鉛鈣鈦礦材料之設計。本項目的目標成果是實現光電轉換效率突破 20% 新紀錄的錫基鈣鈦礦太陽能電池，並能在持續光照下穩定運行超過 3000 小時。預期成果將推動下一代無鉛鈣鈦礦光伏技術向商業化邁進重要一步。此類太陽能電池有望成為可再生能源領域的顛覆性技術，在消除鉛環境危害的同時，實現輕質、高效的太陽能電池，以最低的環境影響提供可持續的能源應用。 本項目的成功實施，將顯著推動本地經濟脫碳，並助力《香港氣候行動藍圖2050》，促進可再生能源的應用及清潔能源產業的發展。

15307026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15307026.value: 二維半金屬性過渡金屬二硫族化合物修飾隔膜及其在高性能鋰硫電池中的應用

15307026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15307026.value: Energy storage systems are fundamental to modern industry, supporting the rapid market growth of portable electronics and electric vehicles. Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), which are the main power source in today’s storage landscape, provide a reasonable energy density (100~250 Wh kg-1). However, they have reached theoretical energy density limit and are almost unlikely to surpass 300 Wh kg-1, which is a basic requirement for future electric vehicles, robotic, flexible electronics, and aerospace transportation. Lithium-sulfur batteries (LSBs) have been considered as one of the most promising alternative high-energy battery technologies because of their high theoretical energy density (2600 Wh kg-1) as well as the high natural abundance of sulfur. However, practical application of LSBs is hindered by several challenges, including the poor electrical conductivities of sulfur and its discharge product Li2S, sluggish redox kinetics, and the shuttling of intermediate lithium polysulfides (LPSs), leading to rapid capacity fading and low coulombic efficiency. Thus, the development of advanced materials combining high intrinsic conductivity, strong LPSs adsorption, and superior catalytic activity is essential to achieve high-performance LSBs. This project proposes the systematic exploration of two-dimensional (2D) semi-metallic transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) modified separator in LSBs. The 2D semi-metallic 1T′-TMD nanosheets (NSs) with high intrinsic conductivity and abundant exposed catalytically active sites for absorption and conversion of LPSs will be prepared by an efficient electrochemical intercalation and exfoliation process, which are used to modify separators for the fabrication of high-performance LSBs. We aim to address three critical questions: (1) Development of low-cost and high-efficiency preparation of clean 2D semi-metallic TMDs with abundant exposed active sites; (2) Are 2D semi-metallic 1T′-TMDs suitable for LSBs? (3) What is the mechanism of 2D semi-metallic TMDs for enhancing the performance of LSBs? To systematically tackle these questions, this project is divided into four tasks: (1) To develop low-cost and large-scale method for the synthesis of various 2D semi-metallic 1T′-TMD bulk crystals; (2) To achieve controlled preparation of clean 2D semi-metallic 1T′-TMD NSs exposing abundant active sites; (3) To investigate the electrical, adsorption and catalytic properties of 2D semi-metallic 1T′-TMDs and mechanism for LSBs; (4) To fabricate and optimize high-performance LSBs for practical applications. The success of this project will pave the way for future development of high-performance LSBs, facilitating their practical application in a wide range of fields, including renewable energy storage, electric vehicles, and portable electronics. 儲能系統是現代工業的基礎，支撐著便攜式電子產品和電動車市場的快速增長。目前作為主流的鋰離子電池（LIBs）具備合理的能量密度（100~250 Wh kg⁻¹），但已觸及其理論極限，且難以突破 300 Wh kg⁻¹，無法滿足未來電動車、機器人、柔性電子和航空航天運輸的基本需求。 鋰硫電池（LSBs）因具有極高的理論能量密度（2600 Wh kg⁻¹）以及硫的天然豐富性，被認為是最具前景的新一代高能電池技術之一。然而，其實際應用面臨诸多挑戰，包括硫及其放電產物（Li₂S）導電性差、氧化還原動力學緩慢，以及多硫化鋰（LPSs）中間體的穿梭效應，這些問題導致電池容量快速衰減和庫侖效率低下。因此，開發兼具高本徵電導率、強LPSs吸附能力及優異催化活性的先進材料，對於實現高性能鋰硫電池至關重要。 本項目提出在鋰硫電池中系統性地探索二維半金屬性過渡金屬二硫族化合物（TMD）修飾隔膜的應用。我們將透過高效的電化學插層與剝離工藝，製備出具有高本徵電導率並暴露豐富催化活性位點的二維半金屬性1T′-TMD納米片，用以吸附與轉化LPSs，並將其應用於修飾隔膜以構建高性能鋰硫電池。 我們致力於解決三個關鍵科學問題：(1) 開發低成本且高效的方法以製備表面潔淨且富含活性位點的二維半金屬性TMDs；(2) 二維半金屬性1T′-TMDs應用於鋰硫電池的適用性；(3) 二維半金屬性TMDs提升鋰硫電池性能的作用機制。為系統性解決上述問題，本項目規劃了四項具體任務：(1) 開發低成本、大規模合成多種二維半金屬性1T′-TMD塊體晶體的方法；(2) 可控制備表面潔淨且暴露豐富活性位點的二維半金屬性1T′-TMD納米片；(3) 研究二維半金屬性1T′-TMDs的電學、吸附與催化特性及其在鋰硫電池中的作用機制；(4) 構建並優化適用於實際應用的高性能鋰硫電池。本項目的成功將為高性能鋰硫電池的未來發展鋪平道路，並促進其在可再生能源存儲、電動車及便攜式電子產品等廣泛領域的實際應用。

15307126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15307126.value: 內蘊幾何流的有限元方法

15307126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15307126.value: This project aims to develop efficient computational techniques and rigorous numerical analysis for intrinsic geometric flows by pursuing the objectives outlined below. First, we will address the open problem of convergence and error estimates for finite element methods for the Ricci flow on two-dimensional manifolds. We will achieve this by reformulating the Ricci flow as a solution-driven metric evolution, in which the metric is driven by the Gaussian curvature and the Gaussian curvature satisfies a parabolic equation coupled to the evolving metric. By fully exploiting the parabolic nature of the system, we will establish error estimates of arbitrary polynomial order for both the Gaussian curvature and the Riemannian metric. Second, an important feature of intrinsic geometric flows is that they evolve the metric intrinsically—without reference to an embedding—raising the fundamental question of how to visualize these flows in Euclidean space. To address this question, we will propose a novel formulation for computing an isometric embedding by reformulating the problem as an embedding flow in Euclidean space. A high-accuracy numerical scheme with rigorous error analysis will be established based on this formulation. Finally, we will extend the numerical analysis techniques developed above to more challenging higher-dimensional and higher-order intrinsic geometric flows. For example, we will study the three-dimensional Ricci flow, in which curvature singularities may occur. We will also consider the Calabi flow—a fourth-order intrinsic geometric flow—and develop corresponding discretizations and error analyses. 本項目旨在針對內蘊幾何流，發展高效的計算技術與嚴謹的數值分析方法，具體目標如下。首先，我們將研究 Ricci 流有限元方法的收斂性與誤差估計這一尚未解決的問題。為此，我們將把 Ricci 流重新表述為一個以解為驅動的度量演化繫統。透過充分利用該繫統的拋物型結構，我們將為黎曼度量建立高精度計算的誤差估計。其次，內蘊幾何流的一個重要特徵是，它在不依賴任何嵌入的情況下，以內蘊方式演化度量。這自然引出一個基本問題：如何在歐幾裡得空間中將此類幾何流視覺化？為解決這一問題，我們將透過把等距嵌入問題重新表述為歐幾裡得空間中的嵌入流，提出一種計算等距嵌入的新穎方法。基於這一表述，我們將建立一種高精度數值格式，並對其進行嚴謹的誤差分析。最後，我們將把上述數值分析技術推廣至更具挑戰性的高維或高階內蘊幾何流，例如 Calabi 流（一類四階內蘊幾何流），並發展相應的離散化方法與誤差分析。

15307326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15307326.value: 多組分膜相場模型的能量穩定高效數值方法

15307326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15307326.value: This project aims to develop efficient and accurate numerical methods for a coupled diffuse-interface system modeling multicomponent membranes. We will design both first- and second-order exponential time-differencing schemes for the phase field variable and for the membrane-associated Ohta–Kawasaki dynamics. We will conduct rigorous energy-stability analyses and convergence proofs for the proposed schemes. To reduce computational cost, we will introduce a narrow-band surface-Poisson solver for the operator arising in the membrane-bound Ohta–Kawasaki model, assembling operators only in the region near the interface. The developed algorithms will be validated on canonical benchmarks, compared with established pattern-formation results, and released as a scalable software package suitable for large-scale simulations. These advances address the limitations of existing first-order time discretizations in cell biology modeling, providing tools that are both accurate and computationally efficient. Furthermore, we will extend the current model to a self-consistent framework that couples a relaxed transport equation for interface motion, a Stokes-type viscous flow for the surrounding fluid, and a membrane-associated Ohta–Kawasaki model for protein segregation. This coupled system will simultaneously resolve cell velocity, membrane morphology, and protein density, reproducing experimental domain patterns and predicting the associated velocity fields. The formulation is flexible and can accommodate adhesion, actin-related effects, and external forces, enabling in-depth studies of how flow and substrate interactions regulate phase separation and membrane remodeling. Asymptotic analysis will be performed to connect the diffuse-interface model to its sharp-interface limit as the interfacial width vanishes, elucidating the roles of bending energy, surface and line tension, biochemical forcing, and viscous stresses. We will design energy-stable, provably convergent discretizations for the fully coupled system. Collectively, the proposed methods and models will establish a predictive mathematical platform for studying multicomponent cell motility and related membrane processes. 本項目旨在構建一套高效、高精度數值方法，用於求解描述多組分膜體系的擴散界面耦合方程組。研究擬針對相場變量以及膜相關 Ohta–Kawasaki 動力學，構造一階與二階指數時間差分格式；並對所構造數值格式開展嚴格的能量穩定性與收斂性分析。為降低計算開銷，針對膜約束 Ohta–Kawasaki 模型中出現的曲面泊松問題，引入窄帶求解器，僅在界面鄰近的狹長區域組裝離散算子。所開發的算法將通過基準算例完成驗證，與已有的圖樣生成結果開展對比，並封裝為適用於大規模數值模擬的程序。上述成果可突破當前細胞生物建模中一階時間離散格式存在的局限，提供兼具精度與計算效率的數值工具。 在此基礎上，本研究將拓展現有模型，建立一套自洽耦合框架：耦合刻畫界面演化的鬆弛輸運方程、描述外圍流體的斯托克斯型黏性流動方程，以及用於模擬蛋白分相的膜相關 Ohta–Kawasaki 模型。該耦合方程組能夠同步求解細胞運動速度、細胞膜形態與蛋白濃度分佈，重現實驗觀測的區域分相圖樣，並預測對應的流場分佈。模型框架具備良好擴展性，可納入黏附作用、肌動蛋白相關效應以及外部作用條件，從而深入探究流體與基底相互作用如何調控相分離行為與細胞膜形態演化。本研究還將開展漸近分析，刻畫當界面寬度趨於零時，擴散界面模型收斂至尖銳界面極限的過程，闡明彎曲能、面張力、線張力、生化驅動力與黏性應力各自發揮的作用。綜上，本項目提出的數值方法與理論模型將搭建一套具備預測能力的數學平台，支撐多組分細胞運動及相關細胞膜動力學過程研究。

15307626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15307626.value: 预测中国登革热、基孔肯雅热和寨卡病毒的风险：调查蚊媒病毒暴发的内在机制和异质性、气候和社会经济阈值以及相互作用

15307626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15307626.value: The project is aimed at understanding the inner mechanisms of real outbreaks of viruses spread by Aedes mosquitoes – dengue, chikungunya, Zika. This will enable better estimations of risks of future outbreaks and better designing of intervention strategies. The problem with the viruses in China is emphasised by the recent significant outbreaks of dengue (Guangdong and Yunnan, 2014, 2019, and 2023) and chikungunya (Foshan and Jiangmen in Guangdong, 2025). The real outbreaks of the viruses are characterised by extreme heterogeneity: often, outbreaks are limited to small towns or villages, while in the neighbouring villages sporadic cases of infection are present, but do not “explode” into an outbreak. Climate factors, which are known to affect mosquito-borne infections, are the same in both villages. The current mathematical models of spread of mosquito-borne viruses do not explain this, and usually work on much higher geographic scale. Dengue, chikungunya, and Zika not only are transmitted by the same mosquitoes, but also have intricate interactions on the level of immune systems of the affected humans. Certain sequences of infections and reinfections of the same person can produce much more severe diseases. In highly-endemic countries like Brazil, consequent waves of dengue are often caused by different serotypes of the virus, which, due to partial immunity between the serotypes, is another driving factor behind the epidemiological dynamics of dengue. In this project, our research goal is to build a realistic and real-data-based mathematical model of spread and co-circulation of dengue, chikungunya, and Zika that will seamlessly explain both localised outbreaks (like in Southern China) and high-prevalence scenarios (like in Brazil). A very important new development will be a sub-model that, through climate, socio-economic, demographic, and other indicators, will quantify the risk of outbreaks or significant local transmission in the given geographic locality, thus answering the question why the outbreaks are so localised. This project’s applied goal is, by utilising the above model, to assess and optimise the effectiveness of intervention strategies (mosquito control, vaccination, etc) for Southern China and other countries. We will produce estimates of risk of dengue, chikungunya, and Zika outbreaks in Southern China (including Hong Kong and Macau) on a fine geographic scale and both for the current climate and under different future climate change scenarios. This will improve the preparedness for the future outbreaks and epidemics of the Aedes-borne viruses. 该项目旨在深入理解由伊蚊（Aedes mosquitoes）传播的病毒性疾病——登革热、基孔肯雅热和寨卡病毒病——在实际疫情中的]内在传播机制。研究成果将有助于更准确地评估未来疫情暴发风险，并优化干预策略。近年来，这些蚊媒病毒性疾病已对中国造成显著影响。例如，2014年广东发生了大规模登革热暴发；2019年云南和广东均报告了较多病例；2023年疫情再次上升，本地病例主要集中在云南，其次为广东。2025年，广东发生了较大规模的基孔肯雅热疫情，病例主要集中于佛山，并波及江门等地，凸显了中国南方地区面临的持续风险。 这些疾病的实际暴发呈现高度的空间异质性（extreme heterogeneity）：许多疫情仅局限于某些小城镇或村庄，而邻近地区即使出现散发病例，也未必进一步发展为疫情暴发。然而，影响蚊媒传染病传播的主要气候因素在这些相邻地区通常相似。目前针对蚊媒病毒传播的数学模型尚无法解释这种局部化暴发现象，并且通常仅适用于较大地理尺度的传播分析。登革热、基孔肯雅热和寨卡病毒病不仅由相同的蚊媒传播，而且在人类免疫系统层面还存在复杂的相互作用。某些特定的感染和再次感染组合可能导致更加严重的疾病。在巴西等登革热高度流行的国家，后续疫情波次往往由不同血清型的登革病毒引起；不同血清型之间的部分交叉免疫会进一步影响登革热的流行动态。 本项目的研究目标是建立一个基于真实数据、能够反映实际传播过程的登革热、基孔肯雅热和寨卡病毒共同传播数学模型。该模型将能够同时解释中国南方地区的局部暴发模式，以及巴西等高流行地区的大规模传播情景。项目的一项重要创新]是建立暴发风险预测子模型（submodel），过综合考虑：气候因素；社会经济指标；人口结构特征；其他环境和地理相关指标；定量评估特定地区发生疫情暴发或显著本地传播的风险，从而回答一个关键科学问题：为什么蚊媒病毒疫情往往呈现高度局部化的暴发特征？在应用层面，本项目将利用上述模型评估并优化中国南方及其他地区的蚊媒控制、疫苗接种和其他公共卫生干预措施。 研究将建立覆盖中国南方地区（包括香港和澳门）的精细地理尺度登革热、基孔肯雅热和寨卡病毒病暴发风险评估体系，分别评估当前气候条件下的传播风险，以及未来不同气候变化情景下的潜在风险。该研究将提升对未来伊蚊传播病毒疫情的监测、预警和应对能力，为制定更加精准和有效的公共卫生防控策略提供科学依据。

15308426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15308426.value: 二氧化碳捕集與轉化一體化：協同催化界面的設計與工程應用

15308426.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15308426.value: Dr Wu, Tai-Sing Prof Yang, Ming

15308426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15308426.value: Integrated CO2 capture and utilisation (ICCU) streamlines carbon management by eliminating energy-intensive CO2 compression and transport, offering clear advantages over conventional CCU process. ICCU is especially compelling for high-temperature flue gases, where thermal energy can be directly harnessed to drive CO2 conversion, improving overall energy efficiency. ICCU performance hinges on dual-functional materials (DFMs) that co-locate CO2 adsorption and catalytic sites. However, prevalent CaO-based DFMs paired with Ni/Fe/Ru catalysts face two core barriers. First, temperature mismatches between capture and conversion, particularly acute in high-temperature ICCU-DRM and ICCU-RWGS, often force stepwise operation, destroying stability and inducing energy penalty. Second, the molecular basis of sorbent-catalyst synergy remains unresolved, including whether captured CO2 reacts directly at adsorption sites via carbonate pathways or must desorb/spillover and convert on separate catalytic sites. This project addresses these gaps through an integrated plan spanning computational discovery, interface-engineered synthesis, and operando mechanism elucidation. Activity 1 applies high-throughput screening of oxides and their carbonates to identify sorbents with reversible carbonate cycling and capture windows overlapping RWGS/DRM (600-800 °C). A custom Python reaction enumerator and selective first-principles calculations will rank candidates by capture-conversion temperature matching, cycling thermodynamics, and compatibility with active metals, yielding a top-tier shortlist with phase-stability results. Activity 2 fabricates and benchmarks proximity-controlled DFMs at three scales: dual/multi-bed, physical mixtures, and nano-level metal@sorbent core-shell architectures. A thermal synthesis route will generate robust shells (e.g., aluminates, silicates, alkaline-earth oxides) that cycle carbonates and CO2 conversions at the target temperature while suppressing sintering and coking. Shell thickness, core size, and promoter chemistry will be tuned to achieve isothermal uptake-conversion at 650-750 °C with > 200 h stability under realistic mixed feeds. Activity 3 resolves carbonate-mediated pathways and durability under realistic conditions using ex situ and operando characterisation tools, augmented by DFT models of metal-sorbent junctions. The work will construct a comprehensive understanding of the reaction mechanism, and translate findings into quantitative design rules for the sorbent family, shell composition/thickness/porosity, promoter identity, and operating windows. Outcomes include a temperature-matched materials shortlist, validated proximity architectures with long-term stability, operando-probed mechanisms, and predictive material design rules. Collectively, these advances enable durable, energy-efficient DFMs for high-temperature ICCU to syngas, supporting scalable pathways to carbon neutrality. 整合式二氧化碳捕集與利用（integrated CO2 capture and utilisation, ICCU）可免除高能耗的 CO2 壓縮與運輸步驟，從而簡化碳管理流程。對於高溫煙道氣而言，ICCU 尤具吸引力，因其可直接利用煙氣中的熱能驅動 CO2 轉化，進而提升整體能源效率。 ICCU 的效能關鍵在於雙功能材料（dual-functional materials, DFMs），其可在同一材料系統中整合 CO2 吸附位點與催化活性位點。然而，現有以 CaO 搭配金屬催化劑的 DFM 系統面臨兩項核心障礙。首先，CO2 捕集與轉化的適用溫度不匹配；此問題在 ICCU 甲烷乾重整（ICCU-DRM）及 ICCU 逆水煤氣變換反應（ICCU-RWGS）中尤其嚴重，往往迫使系統採取分步操作，因而損害操作穩定性並帶來額外能耗。其次，吸附劑與催化劑之間協同作用的介面機理尚未釐清，包括被捕集的 CO2 是否會透過碳酸鹽中間體，直接於吸附位點上反應；抑或必須先脫附或經由溢流遷移，再於獨立的催化位點上完成轉化。 本計畫將透過整合性研究策略回應上述挑戰，涵蓋計算篩選、界面工程合成，以及催化反應條件下的機理解析。工作項目一將對氧化物及其碳酸鹽進行高通量篩選，以辨識具可逆碳酸鹽循環特性、且 CO2 捕集溫度範圍與 RWGS/DRM 反應區間重疊的吸附材料。計畫將建立客製化 Python 反應列舉程式，依據捕集與轉化溫度匹配性、循環熱力學，以及與活性金屬的相容性對候選材料進行排序，最終產出具相穩定性分析結果的優先候選材料清單。工作項目二將製備並評估不同尺度的DFM 架構：雙床/多床系統、物理混合，以及奈米尺度的 metal@sorbent 核殼結構。透過熱合成方法，建構具高穩定性的外殼材料，在目標操作溫度下進行碳酸鹽循環與 CO2 轉化，同時抑制燒結與積碳。藉由調控殼層厚度、核心粒徑及助催化劑化學組成，目標是在 650–750 °C 下實現等溫 CO2 吸附與轉化，並在真實混合進料條件下維持超過 200 小時的穩定操作。工作項目三將運用非原位與原位表徵技術，結合金屬與吸附劑接面之密度泛函理論模型，在反應條件下解析碳酸鹽介導反應途徑與材料耐久性，以建立完整的反應機理理解。 本計畫預期成果包括：具溫度匹配特性的候選材料清單、經驗證且具長期穩定性的鄰近性控制 DFM 架構、透過操作中表徵驗證的反應機理，以及可預測材料表現的設計準則。整體而言，這些成果將促成適用於高溫 ICCU 製合成氣、兼具耐久性與能源效率的雙功能材料開發，並支持邁向碳中和的可規模化技術途徑。

15308826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15308826.value: 機器學習調製線性醚類電解液用於高效低溫無負極鈉電池

15308826.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15308826.value: Prof LIU, ZHE Prof Zhao, Yan

15308826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15308826.value: Developing rechargeable batteries capable of high-energy delivery under low-temperature (LT) conditions (below 0 °C) is essential for applications in cold climates. Anode-free sodium batteries (AFSBs) are particularly promising for LT operation due to the low desolvation energy, small Stokes radius of Na+, non-diffusion-controlled plating/stripping behavior, and maximized energy density. However, conventional linear ether-based electrolytes exhibit a sharp decline in ionic conductivity and form unstable solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs) at LT, leading to poor Coulombic efficiency during Na deposition/dissolution. Although cyclic ether-based electrolytes show better LT resistance, their oxidative stability is significantly compromised due to the nucleophilic attack of oxygen and ring-opening polymerization. Thus, designing advanced linear ether electrolytes that overcome kinetic barriers and promote stable SEI formation at LT is of great importance. Conventional trial-and-error methods are inefficient and inaccurate, underscoring the need for a more precise and accelerated electrolyte design strategy. This project aims to achieve precise formulation of linear ether electrolytes for LT AFSBs via a data-driven workflow. A comprehensive dataset of candidate linear ethers with tailored chain length and ether oxygen/alkyl fluoride functionalization will first be constructed. Subsequently, elemental composition, atomic location, and electron configuration of solvent molecules will be selected as features for multi-algorithm machine learning modeling. Candidates with optimal properties including rapid Na+ mobility, low binding energy, and high LUMO energy level will be identified and synthesized based on organic fluorine chemistry. Their solvation structures will be examined using molecular dynamics simulations and spectral techniques, alongwith key physicochemical properties including Na+ diffusion and desolvation kinetics to be evaluated. The electrochemical performance of the synthesized electrolytes will then be assessed, with a focus on sodium plating/stripping efficiency and stability at LT. Furthermore, the formation pathway of the SEI and its fundamental correlation with sodium reversibility will be probed through integrated computational simulations and multi-technique characterization. Finally, practical anode-free pouch cells will be fabricated, and their electrochemical performance optimized to validate the applicability of the formulated electrolytes for LT AFSBs. Directed by Prof. Xiaoliang Yu, our team at The Hong Kong Polytechnic University has extensive experience in developing high-performance AFSBs, including the first demonstration of stable cycling at −40 °C. The proposed data-driven strategy will open new avenues for precise electrolyte molecular design in LT metal batteries. This project will also further enhance our understanding of the interface regulation mechanism of metal-electrolyte interphases and provide guidelines for designing high performance electrolytes for anode-free batteries. 開發能在低溫（低於 0°C）條件下高效放電之可充電電池，對於寒冷氣候應用至關重要。無負極鈉電池（AFSB）因具備低去溶劑化能、鈉離子斯托克斯半徑小、非擴散控制之沉積/剝離行為，以及最大化能量密度等特性，於低溫運作上尤具潛力。然而，傳統線性醚類電解液在低溫下離子導電度急遽下降，且形成不穩定之固體電解質介面（SEI），導致鈉沉積/溶出過程中之庫侖效率不佳。儘管環狀醚類電解液對低溫耐受性較佳，但其氧化穩定性因氧之親核攻擊及開環聚合而顯著受損。因此，設計能克服動力學障礙並促進低溫下穩定 SEI 形成之先進線性醚電解液至關重要。傳統試誤法效率低且不精確，凸顯出更精準且加速電解質設計策略之迫切需求。 本項目旨在藉由數據驅動流程，實現低溫無負極鈉電池用線性醚電解液之精確設計。首先，將建構涵蓋不同鏈長及醚氧/烷基氟官能基修飾之候選線性醚的全面數據集。接著，選取溶劑分子之元素組成、原子位置及電子組態作為特徵，進行多演算法機器學習建模。從中辨識出具備快速鈉離子遷移率、低結合能及高 LUMO 能階之最適候選物，並基於有機氟化學進行合成。隨後，利用分子動力學模擬與光譜技術檢視其溶劑化結構，同時評估鈉離子擴散與去溶劑化動力學等關鍵物理化學性質。進一步評估合成電解質之電化學性能，特別著重於低溫下鈉沉積/剝離效率及穩定性。再者，透過整合計算模擬與多重表徵技術，探討 SEI 之形成途徑及其與鈉可逆性之根本關聯。最後，組裝實際無負極軟包電池，並優化其電化學性能，以驗證所配製電解液於低溫無負極鈉電池之適用性。 本團隊由於曉亮教授指導，在開發高性能無負極鈉電池方面累積豐富經驗，包括首次展示在 -40°C 下穩定循環。本項目之數據驅動策略將為低溫金屬電池之精準電解液分子設計開創新途徑。同時，此計畫亦將深化我們對金屬-電解質介面調控機制之理解，並為高性能無負極電池電解液設計提供指導方針。

15308926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15308926.value: JAK2假激酶-酪氨酸激酶結構域的構象動力學：基於氫/氘JAK2假激酶-酪氨酸激酶結構域的構象動力學：基於氫/氘交換質譜與計計算方法的新啟示

15308926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15308926.value: Janus kinase 2 (JAK2) is a multi-domain protein essential for regulating cell growth and division, particularly for blood cell production within the bone marrow. In the absence of signal stimulation, the pseudokinase (PK) domain of JAK2 binds to its tyrosine kinase (TK) domain, keeping JAK2 in an inactive state through autoinhibition. Upon signal stimulation, JAK2 undergoes substantial conformational transformations into an active state for catalytic activities and downstream signal transduction. Pathogenic mutations such as V617F lead to constant activation of JAK2, causing overproduction of blood cells and consequently severe blood diseases. Various inhibitors have been developed to inhibit the hyperactivity of JAK2. JAK2 is large, dynamic and prone to aggregation and degradation, making it difficult to be studied by techniques such as X-ray crystallography, Cryo-EM or NMR spectroscopy. So far, the molecular mechanisms of autoinhibition, mutation-induced activation and inhibitor interactions of JAK2 are still fragmented. In this project, hydrogen/deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS), molecular dynamics simulation, molecular docking and homology modeling will be employed to investigate the conformational dynamics of the human JAK2 tandem PK-TK domains. Particularly, we will use pulsed-labeling HDX-MS to detect and characterize the autoinhibited, active, and potential transition states of the PK-TK domains, to understand how two domains interact to facilitate the autoinhibition. We will also examine the conformational dynamics changes caused by documented mutations at the autoinhibitory interface and dimerization interface to determine whether the pathogenic activation is achieved by destabilizing the autoinhibited state, stabilizing the active state, or through other mechanisms. Additionally, we will investigate the effects of binding of three types of inhibitors on the conformational dynamics of the PK-TK domains, to gain a comprehensive understanding of their inhibition mechanisms and to discover potential new allosteric sites for inhibitor development. This project focuses on the conformational dynamics of JAK2, which is crucial for its biological functions but not yet experimentally studied. Our preliminary study has revealed two distinct conformational states of the protein system, which may correspond to the autoinhibited and active states of the JAK2 conformational transition, and obtained intriguing information on the conformational dynamics of the wild-type and mutant PK-TK domains and their changes upon the inhibitor binding. The implementation of this project will enable us to acquire new knowledge on the molecular mechanisms of this important protein and obtain new insights for design of JAK2 inhibitors.

15309226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15309226.value: 基於原位和離位掃描透射電鏡探究氧化鉿薄膜的鐵電性及其穩定性

15309226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15309226.value: Ferroelectrics are promising candidates for future memory devices, but their applications are hindered by the inability of downscaling, due to degraded ferroelectricity at reduced thickness for conventional ferroelectrics. The emerging hafnia-based ferroelectrics, with exceptional ferroelectricity down to nanometer thickness, offers an exciting solution to this downscaling bottleneck. Combining with the full compatibility with silicon technology, hafnia (HfO2) holds the tantalizing potential of realizing ultra-dense low-power memory devices. Nonetheless, the application of HfO2-based devices is currently hampered by instability issues, namely the ferroelectric wake-up and fatigue effects. Diminishing these instabilities requires better understanding on the complex nature of HfO2-based ferroelectricity involving phase transitions and oxygen vacancy (Vo) migration driven by the electric field, the detailed mechanism of which still remains elusive. We aim to fill this knowledge gap by establishing characterization techniques that can reliably measure various HfO2 phases, Vo, and polarization states, as well as their evolution under device operation conditions, based on cutting-edge scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM). Our state-of-the-art STEM facility enables i) spatially-resolved electron diffraction via 4D-STEM to quantify various phases at multiscale, ii) electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) to measure the distribution of Vo, iii) differential phase-contrast imaging with atomic resolution to resolve off-center shift of oxygen anions and resultant ferroelectric polarization, iv) operando observation under device operation conditions enabled by electrical holders that can apply an electric field inside STEM. Combining these unique capabilities with our expertise in both STEM characterization and HfO2-based thin film growth, we have an unprecedented opportunity to unravel the intricate behavior of HfO2-based ferroelectricity. Our preliminary results on HfO2 phase and polarization mapping have demonstrated the feasibility of the proposed work. With optimized phase mapping by 4D-STEM, we will compare phase content in HfO2-based thin films grown at different conditions, to interpret their distinct ferroelectric properties. Further correlating with Vo mapping by STEM-EELS allows us to derive the effect of Vo on the formation and stabilization of ferroelectric phases. Conducting such phase and Vo mapping on samples made from operated devices, the ex situ characterization will elucidate the roles of phase transitions and Vo distribution in the ferroelectric instabilities, and shed light on their origins. Moreover, we will use operando STEM to directly capture electric-field-driven HfO2 phase transitions and polarization switching at atomic scale. The exclusive insight obtained from this work will substantially advance the understanding of HfO2-based ferroelectricity and its instabilities, and pave the way for future ferroelectric device applications. 鐵電材料是未來存儲器件極具前景的候選材料。由於傳統鐵電材料在厚度減小時鐵電性能會發生退化，導致其無法製備小尺度器件，從而阻礙了其應用。新興的鉿基鐵電材料在納米級厚度下仍具有優異的鐵電性，為這一尺寸縮減瓶頸提供了令人興奮的解決方案。結合其與硅工藝的完全兼容性，氧化鉿具有實現超高密度、低功耗存儲器件的巨大潛力。然而，目前基於氧化鉿的器件在應用中仍有不穩定性問題，包括鐵電喚醒和疲勞效應。減少這些不穩定性需要深入理解鉿基鐵電性的複雜本質，尤其是電場驅動下的相變和氧空位遷移。 我們的目標是基於尖端的掃描透射電子顯微術 (STEM)，實現能夠可靠測量各種氧化鉿相、氧空位和極化狀態，以及它們在器件工作條件下演變過程的表徵技術，來填補這一知識空白。我們先進的 STEM 設備能夠實現：1) 通過 4D-STEM 進行空間分辨電子衍射，以在多尺度上定量分析各種相；2) 利用電子能量損失譜（EELS）測量氧空位的分佈；3) 利用具有原子級分辨率的微分相位襯度（DPC）成像來解析氧陰離子的偏心位移及由此產生的鐵電極化；4) 利用可在 STEM 內部施加電場的電學原位樣品台，在器件運行工況下進行原位觀測。 將這些獨特的能力與我們在 STEM 表徵和鉿基薄膜生長方面的專業知識相結合，我們擁有前所未有的機會來揭示鉿基鐵電性複雜的行為。我們在氧化鉿相和極化分佈成像方面的初步結果已經證實了這一工作的可行性。通過 4D-STEM 優化的相分佈成像，我們將對比在不同條件下生長的鉿基薄膜中的相含量，以闡釋它們不同的鐵電性能。進一步與 STEM-EELS 的氧空位成像相結合，使我們能夠推導氧空位對鐵電相形成和穩定性的影響。對運行后的器件樣品進行此類相和氧空位分佈成像，這種非原位（ex situ）表徵將闡明相變和氧空位分佈在鐵電不穩定性中的作用，並揭示其起源。此外，我們將利用原位STEM 在原子尺度上直接捕捉電場驅動下的氧化鉿相變和極化翻轉。這項工作所獲得的獨到理解將顯著推進對鉿基鐵電性及其不穩定性的理解，並為未來的鐵電器件應用鋪平道路。

15309426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15309426.value: 基於半参数生成模型的表征学习与统计推断

15309426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15309426.value: Learning data representations and modeling conditional distributions are foundational tasks in statistics and are central to modern machine learning and generative AI. Representation learning aims to produce low-dimensional, informative encodings of high-dimensional inputs for downstream tasks (supervised learning, transfer learning, domain adaptation, generative modeling, etc.), while conditional distribution estimation characterizes how outcomes depend on inputs. These tasks are typically treated separately: representation methods focus on representation quality without directly targeting conditional distribution estimation, and predictive models often rely on preconstructed features. Because the main purpose of representation learning is frequently to enable accurate prediction and reliable uncertainty quantification, a unified framework that jointly learns representations and conditional distributions can yield substantial gains in statistical efficiency, robustness, and interpretability. We propose Generative Sufficient Representation Learning (GSRL), a novel framework that integrates sufficient representation learning with flow-based generative modeling. GSRL learns low-dimensional mappings of predictors that are sufficient for outcomes, retaining all outcome-relevant information, while simultaneously modeling the conditional distribution of outcomes given predictors. By embedding sufficiency within the generative model, GSRL produces representations optimized for both sufficiency and faithful conditional generation, addressing a key methodological gap. Based on this basic formulation, we introduce semiparametric generative models that pair parametric components for interpretable treatment effects with nonparametric generative components for flexible conditional modeling. These semiparametric models expand the literature and create a new class of semiparametric generative models suited to biostatistics, econometrics, and other domains requiring principled inference and realistic data synthesis. We also apply GSRL with continuous normalizing flows to construct distribution-free prediction regions for multivariate outcomes. By concentrating predictive information into a compact representation, GSRL mitigates the curse of dimensionality in conformal calibration under a manifold structure for the covariates, leading to tighter and well-covered regions. The project will deliver rigorous theoretical guarantees and practical tools. Theoretical contributions include non-asymptotic generalization bounds for GSRL and its extensions, showing that GSRL mitigates the curse of dimensionality when the data are concentrated near a low-dimensional manifold, an assumption aligned with many real-world high-dimensional datasets. We will also analyze statistical properties of the semiparametric estimators and investigate converage guarantees and efficiency properties of the GSRL-based conformal prediction procedure. On the practical side, we will develop three open-source Python packages: GSRL (generative sufficient representation learning), SGMI (semiparametric generative model inference) and GCPR (generative conformal prediction), accompanied by documentation and reproducible experiments. 学习数据表征和建模条件分布是统计学中的基础任务，也是现代机器学习和生成式人工智能模型的核心。表征学习旨在为下游任务（如监督学习、迁移学习、领域自适应、生成建模等）生成高维输入的低维、信息丰富的编码，而条件分布估计则刻画结果如何依赖于输入。这两类任务通常被分开处理：表征方法关注表征质量，而不直接针对条件分布估计；预测模型则往往依赖于预先构建的特征。由于表征学习的主要目的通常是实现准确预测和可靠的 uncertainty quantification，一个能够联合学习表征和条件分布的统一框架可以在统计效率、鲁棒性和可解释性方面带来显著提升。 我们提出生成式充分表征学习（Generative Sufficient Representation Learning, GSRL），这是一个将充分表征学习与基于流的生成建模相结合的新颖框架。GSRL 学习预测变量的低维映射，这些映射对结果变量是充分的，即保留了所有与结果相关的信息，同时建模给定预测变量下结果的条件分布。通过将充分性嵌入生成模型，GSRL 产生的表征在充分性和忠实条件生成两方面均得到优化，从而填补了一个关键的方法论空白。基于这一基本框架，我们引入了半参数生成模型，将用于可解释治疗效应的参数化组件与用于灵活条件建模的非参数生成组件相结合。这些半参数模型拓展了现有文献，并创建了一类适用于生物统计学、计量经济学及其他需要原则性推断和真实数据合成领域的新型半参数生成模型。我们进一步将 GSRL 扩展到多任务学习和迁移学习中，通过建模跨任务的共享表征，使所有任务共同为表征提供信息，从而在学习任务特定条件分布的同时提高统计效率和泛化能力。我们的半参数生成建模与推断框架同样适用于这些场景。 本项目将提供严格的理论保证和实用工具。理论贡献包括 GSRL 及其扩展的非渐近泛化界，证明当数据集中在低维流形附近时, 这一假设与许多真实世界的高维数据集相符, GSRL 能够缓解维度灾难。我们还将分析半参数估计量的统计性质，包括治疗参数的渐近正态性和效率考量。在实践方面，我们将开发开源 Python 软件包：GSRL（生成式充分表征学习）和 SemiGM（半参数生成建模），并附有完善的文档和可复现的实验。

15309526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15309526.value: 大規模半定規劃的 GPU 加速增廣拉格朗日方法

15309526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15309526.value: Semidefinite programming (SDP) is a fundamental framework in modern optimization, with broad applications in operations research, data science, and machine learning. However, the scalability of existing CPU-based solvers for SDP problems such as SDPT3, MOSEK, and SDPNAL+ is severely constrained by the O(n^3) cost of repeated eigendecompositions, which become impractical for large-scale problems. Meanwhile, modern graphics processing units (GPUs) provide massive parallelism and high memory bandwidth ideally suited for large-scale linear algebra computations. Although there is growing interest in leveraging this capability to design efficient algorithms for general SDP problems, existing approaches with rigorous theoretical guarantees remain limited. This project aims to develop a unified, GPU-accelerated augmented Lagrangian method (ALM) framework with provable convergence guarantees for efficiently solving large-scale SDP problems. Specifically, we will investigate the theoretical properties of SDP problems—focusing on sparsity and low-rank structures—and establish conditions under which these structures are inherited by ALM subproblems. Building on these insights, for SDP problems with block-wise sparse structures, we will first exploit this property to decompose the positive semidefinite (PSD) constraint into a set of smaller, coupled semidefinite constraints. We will then introduce general matrix–matrix multiplication (GEMM)–based polynomial iterations to approximate PSD projections within the ALM framework, thereby avoiding costly eigendecompositions that are inherently sequential and difficult to parallelize on GPUs. For SDP problems with low-rank structures, we will reformulate the ALM subproblems in a nonconvex factorized form and develop accelerated factorized Frank–Wolfe schemes to solve them efficiently. Additional accelerations, including adaptive rank reduction and Halpern Peaceman–Rachford warm starts, will be incorporated to further enhance convergence and scalability. The resulting open-source GPU solver will establish a new benchmark for large-scale SDP computation and expand the practical frontier of mathematical programming in control, machine learning, and data science. 半定規劃（Semidefinite Programming, SDP）是現代優化中的基礎性框架，在運籌學、數據科學和機器學習等領域具有廣泛應用。然而，現有基於中央處理器（CPU）的 SDP 求解器，如 SDPT3、MOSEK 和 SDPNAL+，其可擴展性受到重複特徵值分解所需 O(n^3) 計算成本的嚴重制約，使其在大規模問題上的應用變得十分困難。與此同時，現代圖形處理器（GPU）具有大規模平行運算能力和高記憶體頻寬，非常適合大規模線性代數計算。儘管近年來利用 GPU 設計高效通用 SDP 演算法日益受到關注，但兼具高計算效率與嚴格理論保證的方法仍然有限。 本項目旨在建立一個統一的 GPU 加速增廣拉格朗日方法（Augmented Lagrangian Method, ALM）框架，並給出嚴格的收斂性保證，以高效求解大規模 SDP 問題。具體而言，我們將研究 SDP 問題的理論性質，重點分析其稀疏結構和低秩結構，並建立這些結構可由 ALM 子問題繼承的條件。在此基礎上，對於具有分塊稀疏結構的 SDP 問題，我們將首先利用其結構將正半定（PSD）約束分解為一組規模更小且相互耦合的半定約束，然後在 ALM 框架中引入基於通用矩陣乘法（GEMM）的多項式迭代，以近似計算 PSD 投影，從而避免代價高昂、具有較強串行特性且難以在 GPU 上充分並行化的特徵值分解。對於具有低秩結構的 SDP 問題，我們將 ALM 子問題重新表述為非凸因子化形式，並發展加速的因子化 Frank–Wolfe 方法進行高效求解。此外，我們還將結合自適應秩約簡和 Halpern–Peaceman–Rachford 熱啟動等加速技術，以進一步提升算法的收斂速度和可擴展性。最終，本項目將開發一個開源的 GPU 大規模 SDP 求解器，力求建立大規模 SDP 計算的新性能基準，並拓展數學規劃在控制、機器學習和數據科學等領域中的實際應用範圍。

15310226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15310226.value: 適用於質子陶瓷燃料電池的高性能、長壽命錯配層狀陰極材料

15310226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15310226.value: Protonic ceramic fuel cells (PCFCs) are promising clean power sources, but their wide adoption is hindered by the unsatisfactory performance of the cathode and the poor durability caused by thermal expansion coefficient (TEC) mismatch between the cathode and the electrolyte. The TEC mismatch can cause delamination of cathode from the electrolyte, degrading cell performance or causing cell failure. Misfit-layered Ca3Co4O9 (CCO) is a promising PCFC cathode material due to its good electrical conductivity and compatible TEC with the electrolyte. However, the performance of CCO-based materials is still unsatisfactory, due to their low oxygen vacancy concentration and proton conductivity. Our previous research on ABO3-type perovskites showed that A-site deficiency could enhance oxygen vacancy concentration and anion (F) doping could weaken the metal-oxygen bonding, leading to enhanced ionic conductivity. In addition, doping of suitable cations such as Cs at the A-site and Y, Hf, and Sn at the B-site could improve the electrocatalytic activity of ABO3-type cathode of solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs). However, no study has been conducted to evaluate how these strategies influence the electrocatalytic activity of misfit-layered CCO-based materials, whose layered structures are very different from those of ABO3-type perovskites. Thus, it’s still unknown: (1) what’s the effects of Ca-site deficiency and anion (F) doping on the electrocatalytic activity of the CCO-based cathodes? (2) what’s the synergistic effects of both Ca-site deficiency and anion (F) doping on the bulk transport and surface exchange properties of CCO-based cathodes? and (3) what’s the effects of cation doping (Cs for Ca-site and Y, Hf, and Sn for Co-site) on the electrocatalytic activity of CCO-based cathodes? This project is purposely designed to address these scientific questions by developing novel misfit-layered CCO-based cathodes with (1) Ca-site deficiency, (2) anion doping, and (3) suitable cation doping (Cs for Ca-site and Y, Hf, and Sn for Co-site). 16 new materials will be synthesized, characterized, tested, and theoretically studied with the density functional theory (DFT). Multiphysics model will be developed for simulating and optimizing the PCFC with the new cathode materials. In this project, new materials will be developed and new knowledge on how the different strategies influence the bulk transport and surface exchange kinetics of CCO-based new cathode materials will be generated. If successfully implemented, the project will contribute significantly to the development of high performance and durable PCFC for clean power generation. 質子陶瓷燃料電池（PCFCs）是極具發展前景的清潔能源裝置，但陰極性能欠佳，加之陰極與電解質之間熱膨脹係數（TEC）不匹配導致耐久性較差，阻礙了PCFC的大規模應用。熱膨脹係數不匹配會造成陰極從電解質表層剝離，降低電池性能，甚至導致PCFC失效。 錯配層狀Ca₃Co₄O₉（CCO）具備優異的電導率，且熱膨脹係數與電解質良好適配，是極具潛力的質子陶瓷燃料電池陰極材料。然而，受限於較低的氧空位濃度與質子電導率，CCO性能依然未如理想。 團隊前期針對 ABO₃型鈣鈦礦材料的研究表明：A 位缺空位能夠提升氧空位濃度；陰離子（氟離子）摻雜可以削弱金屬‑氧化學鍵，最終提高離子電導率。除此之外，在 A 位摻入銫，在 B 位摻入釔、鉿、錫等適配陽離子，能夠改善固體氧化物燃料電池（SOFCs）ABO₃型陰極的電催化活性。 但錯配層狀CCO基材料的層狀晶體結構和 ABO₃型鈣鈦礦差異極大，目前尚且沒有相關研究探究上述改性手段對於CCO基材料電催化性能的作用。 因此仍存在三項待解決的科學問題：（1）鈣位點缺位與氟陰離子摻雜，會對CCO基陰極材料的電催化活性產生何種影響？（2）鈣位點缺位和氟陰離子摻雜二者協同作用，會怎樣改變CCO基陰極的體相傳輸性能與表面交換特性？（3）陽離子摻雜（鈣位點摻雜銫、鈷位點摻雜釔、鉿、錫）對CCO基陰極電催化活性有何作用？ 本課題擬圍繞以上科學問題展開研究，製備三類新型錯配層狀CCO基陰極材料：（1）鈣位點缺位型、（2）陰離子摻雜型、（3）適配陽離子摻雜型（鈣位點摻銫，鈷位點摻釔、鉿、錫）。研究將合成 16 種全新材料，完成材料表徵、性能測試，並結合密度泛函理論（DFT）開展理論分析；同時建立多物理場模型，對使用新型陰極材料的質子陶瓷燃料電池進行模擬模擬與參數優化。 本專案旨在研發新型陰極材料，並厘清各類改性策略如何調控CCO基陰極材料的體相傳輸能力以及表面交換動力學。項目的順利推進，將會為高性能、長壽命質子陶瓷燃料電池清潔能源發電技術的發展提供重要支撐。

15310426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15310426.value: 基於液態基底定向（002）鋅沉積的長壽命水系鋅金屬電池的研究

15310426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15310426.value: Aqueous zinc (Zn) metal batteries (AZMBs) are highly desirable for large-scale energy storage due to their inherent safety, environmental sustainability, and cost-effectiveness. However, uncontrolled Zn deposition leads to dendritic growth and side reactions, resulting in rapid capacity decay and short battery life. Among various strategies, achieving highly oriented (002) Zn deposition is recognized as an essential route toward long-lasting AZMBs, as (002) plane naturally resists corrosion and promotes stable, planar growth of Zn. Although some preferential (002) texture growth are reported, existing methods remain largely constrained by two fundamental shortcomings: 1) achieved (002) texture ratio are generally below 60%; 2) (002) texture are easy to be disrupted under practical operating conditions. These limitations stem from the intrinsic nucleation and growth behavior of Zn on conventional solid substrates (such as Cu, Ti), where polycrystallinity, defects, and grain boundaries induce heterogeneous nucleation that is strongly dependent on plating kinetics. Consequently, even slight variations in operating parameters can disrupt crystallographic alignment. To address this challenge, this project aims for developing a liquid-substrate-direct growth strategy to produce high-purity (002) Zn in practical battery operation conditions. Unlike solid substrates, liquid substrates composed of low-melting-point alloys are defect-free and self-smoothing, which should benefit the uniform Zn deposition. We aim to achieve (002) Zn over 99% purity across diverse electrolytes, current densities, and areal capacities. Through a combination of experimental and numerical approaches, the project is structured into three integrated tasks: 1) preparation of liquid substrates and investigation of the Zn deposition mechanism behavior on liquid substrates; 2) study of the electrochemical performance of liquid-substrate-mediated Zn metal anodes in a wide range of electrochemical conditions including diverse electrolytes, current densities, areal capacities, and calendar conditions; and 3) demonstration of stable Ah-level AZMBs under practical conditions such as low N/P ratios and lean electrolyte. The success of this project will result in a paradigm shift from conventional solid-state nucleation and growth of Zn to a new liquid-substrate-direct mechanism. It will deliver not only a set of first-hand fundamental knowledge on Zn’s electrochemistry on liquid surfaces, but also novel technologies on how to fabricate high-purity (002) Zn metal anodes. These will lead to significant breakthroughs in improving the corrosion resistance, mitigating the dendrite formation, and extending the cycling stability of Zn metal anodes, which paves the way to safe and cost-effective AZMBs for a wide variety of applications in green energy, smart city, and AI data center. 水系鋅金屬電池憑藉本質安全、環境友好及低成本優勢，在大規模儲能領域展現出廣闊應用前景。不同於使用易燃有機電解液的傳統電池，水系鋅金屬電池採用含水系電解液，極大降低了火災隱患，使其成爲電網儲能等應用的理想選擇。然而，鋅金屬負極是制約其商業化進程的主要瓶頸：不均匀的鋅沉積極易誘發枝晶生長及析氫等副反應，造成容量快速衰減與循環壽命受限。誘導鋅抗腐蝕性強且易於平面生長的（002）晶面擇優取向沉積是關鍵解題思路，但受限於固態基底的固有缺陷，現有的晶面調控策略難以在不同電流密度或高比容量等實際工況下實現高純度的（002）鋅取向生長。為此，本項目提出一種基於低熔點合金（如鎵基合金）的液態基底。利用液態表面無缺陷且具自平滑的特性，均化界面離子游，以實現均匀鋅沉積。項目旨在多樣化電解液體體系、寬電流密度（0.1~100 mA cm⁻²）及寬面積容量比（0.1~25 mAh cm⁻²）條件下，實現突破性的高純度（>99.9%）（002）晶面定向沉積。結合實驗與計算模擬，揭示液態基底誘導（002）鋅定向沉積機制，豐富水系鋅電化學基礎理論。 本項目圍繞三大任務展開：設計並優化液態基底組成及鋅沉積工藝；利用原位/非原位表徵手段與理論計算闡明界面沉積動力學；在低負極/正極容量比（<3）及貧電解液體積（<40 μL mAh⁻¹）等實用化約束條件下構建並驗證安時級（>1 Ah）軟包電池性能。項目將構建鋅沉積動力學新理論框架，研製出兼具優異機械性能和抗腐蝕性能力的高純（002）織構化鋅負極，並開發出長循環壽命（>500次循環，容量保持率>80%）的全電池原型，為電網級儲能電池提供可行技術路綫。成果將涵蓋學術突破（論文、專利）、中期工業應用（電網及消費電子儲能）以及長期社會效益（保障能源安全與降低環境風險），加速水系鋅金屬電池的產業化落地。

15310726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15310726.value: 超越平滑性：現代經濟下大額突發消費行為的隨機跨期建模框架

15310726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15310726.value: Consumption is central to economic and financial analysis, offering crucial insights into individual welfare, savings, asset pricing, and macroeconomic outcomes. For decades, economic models have been built on the principle of consumption smoothing: the idea that people prefer a stable path of spending over time. This has long been the standard for understanding how we spend, save, and respond to economic changes. However, this classic view is increasingly challenged by the emergence of lumpy, non‑smooth consumption behaviors driven by modern economic forces. The rapid growth of e‑commerce and digital platforms has concentrated significant spending into short windows through limited-time offers such as 6.18 and Singles' Day, while the COVID‑19 pandemic reinforced these patterns with stockpiling and a lasting shift to online shopping. Even in the post‑pandemic period, ongoing uncertainty and inflation have made consumption more volatile rather than smoother. This shift brings new risks, including over‑indebtedness from “binge” spending and greater volatility in aggregate demand, which can disrupt household financial planning and spill over to the wider economy. The core research challenge is that existing theories were not designed to capture dual behavior of steady day‑to‑day spending and infrequent large outlays, due to their systematic differences. Moreover, consumption spikes are often misread in data observed infrequently, which is typical for economic data measurement. As a result, we lack a coherent framework of theory and empiric to explain what drives non‑smooth consumption and to assess its consequences. This project aims to fill this gap by developing a comprehensive framework for studying non-smooth consumption that integrates flexible intertemporal preferences, frequency‑aware measurement, and interactions with regular spending and habits. Our results will provide a quantitative basis for understanding such modern spending behavior, valuable for assessing the effects of stimulus design and macroeconomic shocks on household welfare and aggregate demand. Beyond its practical implications, this research is methodologically innovative: spikes in spending break smooth temporal evolution, motivating path‑based preferences (on accumulated consumption) and singular control optimization. Considering economic uncertainty and observation frequency, this leads to novel formulations of stochastic differential utility and recursive utility on cumulative consumption paths, and to discrete–continuous bridges with convergence guarantees. This research is at the forefront of stochastic control, with substantial novelty in modeling, theoretical derivations, and mathematical methodologies. 消費是經濟與金融分析的核心，為理解個人福利、儲蓄、資產定價以及宏觀經濟結果提供了重要洞見。數十年來，經濟模型一直建立在"消費平滑"原則之上，即人們傾向於在不同時期保持穩定的支出路徑。長期以來，這一原則始終是理解人們如何消費、儲蓄以及應對經濟變化的標準範式。 然而，隨著現代經濟力量驅動下大額突發性消費、非平滑消費行為的湧現，這一經典觀點正日益受到挑戰。電子商務與數字平台的迅猛發展，通過"6·18"和"雙十一"等限時促銷活動，將大量支出集中於極短的時間窗口內；與此同時，新冠疫情期間的恐慌式囤積行為，以及消費者向線上購物的持續轉移，進一步強化了這一模式。即便在疫情之後，持續的不確定性與通貨膨脹也使消費變得更加波動，而非趨於平滑。這一轉變也帶來了新的風險，包括"衝動式"消費所引發的過度負債，以及總需求波動性的加劇，二者可能擾亂家庭財務規劃，並外溢至更廣泛的經濟領域。 核心研究挑戰在於：由於日常穩定支出與偶發性大額支出之間存在系統性差異，現有理論在設計之初並未考慮如何刻畫這種雙重行為。此外，消費高峰在低頻觀測數據中往往被誤讀，而低頻觀測正是經濟數據測量的典型特徵。因此，我們尚缺乏一套連貫的理論與實證框架，以解釋非平滑消費的驅動因素並評估其影響。 本項目旨在填補這一空白，通過構建一個研究非平滑消費的綜合框架，融合靈活的跨期偏好、頻率感知的測量方法，以及與常規支出和消費習慣之間的相互作用。研究成果將為理解此類現代消費行為提供量化基礎，對於評估刺激政策設計與宏觀經濟衝擊對家庭福利及總需求的影響具有重要價值。 除實踐意義外，本研究在方法論上亦具創新性：消費高峰打破了平滑的時間演化過程，從而促使我們採用基於路徑的偏好（即建立在累積消費之上）以及奇異控制優化方法。在綜合考慮經濟不確定性與觀測頻率的基礎上，這一思路引出了針對累積消費路徑的隨機微分效用與遞歸效用的新穎表述，並構建具有收斂性保證的離散—連續橋接方法。本研究處於隨機控制領域的前沿，在建模、理論推導以及數學方法論方面均具有顯著的創新性。

15311526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15311526.value: 大面積原子級厚度二維錫基鈣鈦礦單晶的溶液法生長

15311526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15311526.value: Atomically thin two-dimensional (2D) metal halide perovskite crystal films exhibit a range of unique physical properties, including tunable bandgap energies, adjustable exciton binding energies, high carrier mobilities, and pronounced spin-orbit coupling effects. These characteristics make them highly promising candidates for next-generation optoelectronic applications. However, their practical implementation is severely hindered by halide ion migration, a phenomenon intrinsically associated with the soft ionic lattice of halide perovskites. Incorporation of tin (Sn) into the perovskite lattice has been shown to effectively suppress ion migration by increasing the diffusion barrier of halide ions. Despite this, the synthesis of large-area, few-layer 2D perovskite single-crystal films remains a significant challenge. To date, the maximum lateral size reported in the literature is limited to approximately 10 µm, which restricts their utility in electronic and optoelectronic devices. Our preliminary studies demonstrate that high-quality, atomically thin two-dimensional (2D) Sn-based perovskite single-crystal films can be synthesized via a novel solution-shearing technique. This approach enables precise control over film thickness, achieving bilayer structures with exceptionally low surface roughness. Remarkably, the lateral dimensions of the resulting crystals exceed 1 millimeter, corresponding to a record-high aspect ratio of 10⁶. Building upon this unique method, we aim to synthesize large-area 2D Sn-based perovskite single crystals with varied chemical compositions and fabricate field-effect transistors (FETs) to investigate their intrinsic physical properties. The proposed research will focus on the following objectives: (1) To elucidate the growth mechanism of 2D perovskite single-crystal films synthesized via the solution-shearing method. (2) To improve the film quality, including crystal size, thickness uniformity, and crystallinity, by optimizing the growth parameters. (3) To grow 2D Sn-based perovskite crystals incorporating different organic ligands, thereby tuning their structural and electronic properties. (4) To fabricate 2D Sn-based perovskite FETs and systematically investigate their charge transport characteristics. The fabricated perovskite transistors will be characterized over a broad temperature range to elucidate the conduction mechanism of carriers in atomically thin 2D perovskite crystals. The success of the proposed study will lead to a convenient method for the fabrication of large-area and high quality 2D perovskite crystal films with a few atomic layers. This technique will enable us to develop both the fundamental research on the physical properties of 2D metal halide perovskites and the applications of the 2D perovskites. This is a multidisciplinary research project that will provide an excellent opportunity for the research students to work on physics, materials science and electrical engineering.

15311926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15311926.value: 實現用於高能量密度鈉離子電池的微米級錫負極：衰退機制與性能改善

15311926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15311926.value: The growing demand for rechargeable batteries has placed sustainability at the forefront of energy storage research, inspiring intensive investigation into sodium-ion batteries (NIBs). Over the past fifteen years, significant advancements have enabled the development of industry-scale NIBs, which exhibit remarkable stability and unique features, such as impressive low-temperature performance, positioning them as complementary alternatives to lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). The future market share of NIBs within the battery industry will depend largely on their cost-performance ratio. LiFePO4-based LIBs, which avoid the use of precious or toxic elements, could be strong contenders, currently offering around 20% higher energy density than NIBs. Research into new insertion chemistries on cathodes is being rigorously explored to narrow this gap for enhancing NIB competitiveness. In addition to cathode innovation, there remains substantial opportunity for advancement in anode materials. The technology roadmap for LIBs suggests that incorporating alloy anodes with carbon can significantly improve energy density, as demonstrated by the adoption of Si/C anodes in advanced LIBs. It is a delight to note that each Sn atom can accommodate up to 3.75 Na ions via alloying reactions, delivering more than twice the capacity of commonly used hard carbon anodes. Encouragingly, stable cycling of Sn microparticles, which is favored in practical applications due to their low manufacturing cost and high tap density, has been realized in our previous works. However, while these electrodes exhibit high stability in half-cell configurations (Sn vs. Na metal), they degrade rapidly in full cells (Sn vs. cathode). This project aims to elucidate the underlying causes of this abnormal behavior through a comprehensive evaluation of cathode/electrolyte/anode interactions. Preliminary results indicate significant crosstalk between cathode and anode interfaces, exacerbated by the catalytic effect of Sn in reducing electrolyte. We will investigate the decomposition products formed at high voltages using advanced spectroscopic techniques, followed by an exploration of the Sn poisoning mechanism resulting from the migration of these species to the anode. Performance will be enhanced through: (i) electrolyte optimization to suppress the generation of detrimental species; (ii) separator modification to capture crossover species; and (iii) electrode surface coating to improve resistance against degradation. This study will provide potential solutions to the long-existed crosstalk issues between cathode and anode, thereby enhancing the stability of rechargeable batteries. 隨著對二次電池的需求日益增長，永續性已成為儲能研究的核心考量，進而帶動了學界對鈉離子電池的深入探討。過去十五年來的顯著進展，成功推動了工業級鈉離子電池的發展；其具備卓越的穩定性與獨特優勢（如優異的低溫性能），被視為鋰離子電池的理想互補方案。未來，鈉離子電池在市場中的佔有率將在很大程度上取決於其性價比。目前，磷酸鐵鋰基鋰離子電池仍是極具競爭力的對手，其能量密度約比鈉離子電池高出 20%。為縮小此差距並提升鈉離子電池的競爭力，學界正積極探索正極的新型嵌入化學反應。除了正極材料的創新，負極材料同樣具備極大的發展潛力。參考鋰離子電池的技術發展藍圖，將合金負極與碳材料複合能顯著提升能量密度，這點已由先進鋰電池導入矽碳負極的實例中得到證實。值得一提的是，每個錫原子可透過合金化反應容納多達 3.75 個鈉離子，其提供的容量是常規硬碳負極的兩倍以上。微米級錫顆粒因製造成本低且振實密度高，在實際應用中極具潛力；令人振奮的是，我們先前的研究已成功實現了此類微米顆粒的穩定循環。然而，儘管這些電極在半電池系統（錫對金屬鈉）中展現出優異的穩定性，但在全電池（錫對正極）的測試中卻面臨快速衰退的瓶頸。本計畫旨在透過全面評估正極/電解液/負極之間的交互作用，深入探明此異常衰退的根本原因。初步研究結果顯示，正負極界面間存在顯著的串擾效應，而錫對電解液還原的催化作用更進一步加劇了此一現象。我們將利用先進光譜技術，分析高電壓下形成的分解產物，並探討這些產物遷移至負極後所引發的錫中毒機制。本計畫將從以下三個維度來提升電池性能：電解液優化，以抑制有害物質的生成；隔膜改性，以攔截穿梭物質；電極表面塗層處理，以強化抗衰退能力。本研究將為長期困擾正負極的串擾問題提供可行的解決方案，進而全面提升二次電池的穩定性。

15312226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15312226.value: 復發事件過程之非參數假設檢定方法

15312226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15312226.value: In this research project, we investigate nonparametric estimation and inference for recurrent event processes involving irregularly observed panel count data, a common scenario in modern medicine, econometrics, and social science. The unique nature of these data presents substantial challenges for analysis, often leading to severe consequences when the model is misspecified. To address these challenges, we propose innovative nonparametric methodologies for drawing statistical inference for such complex data. We first construct the least squares estimator for a conditional mean function of a recurrent event process given predictors using deep neural network function approximation, and study the theoretical properties of the proposed estimator. Specifically, we derive the nonasymptotic error bound and establish the asymptotic normality for functionals of the proposed estimator. Building on this new theoretical framework, we then develop a class of multi-sample tests for treat comparisons, a class of novel tests for model diagnostics, and variable selection procedures for identifying important predictors. For goodness-of-fit assessments, we examine various panel count models, including three commonly used types: proportional mean models, additive mean models, and accelerated mean models. These models incorporate both univariate and multivariate functions, with the accelerated mean models featuring bundled parameters. We utilize a combination of B-splines and deep neural networks for approximations, deriving non-asymptotic error bounds and establishing asymptotic normality for functionals of these estimators to meet the requirements of the proposed general testing framework. We design computational algorithms to effectively implement the proposed methodologies. The performance of the proposed innovative nonparametric inference procedures will be demonstrated through extensive simulation studies and illustrated with panel count data from studies on bladder tumors, skin cancer, and healthy aging. Initial simulation results demonstrate the strong performance of the proposed nonparametric estimation method when recurrent event processes are generated from different types of conditional mean models. Ultimately, the proposed project will provide a novel theoretical and methodological framework for statistical inference of panel count data. 在本研究計劃中，我們針對涵蓋不定期觀測之面板計數數據的重複事件過程，探討其非參數估計與統計推斷。這類數據常見於現代醫學、計量經濟學及社會科學中。此類數據的獨特性質為數據分析帶來重大挑戰，當模型設定錯誤時，往往會導致嚴重的後果。為解決這些挑戰，我們提出創新的非參數方法，對此類複雜數據進行統計推斷。我們首先利用深度神經網絡函數近似法，針對給定預測變量下的重複事件過程之條件均值函數建立最小二乘估計量，並研究該估計量的理論性質。具體而言，我們導出非漸近誤差界限，並建立該估計量泛函的漸近正態性。以此新理論框架為基礎，我們進一步開發用於處理多樣本比較的檢定方法、用於模型診斷的全新檢定方法，以及用於識別重要預測變量的變量選擇程序。 在擬合優度評估方面，我們檢視了多種面板計數模型，包括三種常用的模型類型：比例均值模型、加性均值模型以及加速均值模型。這些模型同時包含單變量與多變量函數，其中加速均值模型更具有捆綁參數的特徵。我們結合 B-樣條與深度神經網絡進行函數近似，導出非漸近誤差界限，並建立這些估計量泛函的漸近正態性，以滿足所提通用檢定框架的要求。 我們設計了計算演算法以有效執行所提出的方法。我們將透過廣泛的模擬研究，並結合來自膀胱腫瘤、皮膚癌和健康老齡化研究的面板計數數據，展示所提創新非參數推斷程序的優異性能。初步模擬結果表明，當重複事件過程由不同類型的條件均值模型生成時，我們所提出的非參數估計方法展現出強大的效能。最終，本研究計劃將為面板計數數據的統計推斷提供一個全新的理論與方法框架。

15500026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15500026.value: 透過開發一套經過驗證且標準化的酒店ESG績效評估指數體系（HESGPEI），為酒店ESG績效評估提供標準化指引

15500026.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15500026.value: Prof Back, Ki-Joon Prof Lee, Seoki

15500026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15500026.value: Environmental, social and governance (ESG) initiatives contribute to protection against climate change, and encourage sustainability performance, co-creation, social stability, and human prosperity (UN Tourism, 2025). Some international consulting institutions (GRI, SASB, UNGC, WTTC) provide organizations with consultant-created general principles, which guide the compilation of ESG/CSR/Sustainability reports. However, these guidelines do not provide a standardized ESG performance evaluation scale, including domains and indicators and their relative weightings, because most of them were simply developed by consulting groups based on literature reviews and interviews with industry/academy experts (Ye et al., 2025). Even though some tourism or sustainable development indices were developed, including the Sustainable Development Index and Sustainable Tourism Indicators, there has been almost no effort to develop a validated, holistic ESG performance evaluation index in the hospitality and tourism field (Bernard et al., 2025; UN Tourism, 2025). Since there are no standardized guidelines, hotels’ self-ESG reports currently tend to demonstrate only their good performances (Lee et al., 2023). This study aims to develop a validated and standardized hotel ESG performance evaluation index (HESGPEI) including domains in each pillar and indictors in each domain. The index will be developed and verified as a single unified scale that reflects the views of hotel ESG research, implementation, and top management groups with regard to the level of importance of the domains in each ESG pillar and the indicators in each domain. The index will help hotel ESG teams to write their ESG reports more accurately, using standardized HESGPEI guidelines, and improve ESG performance. This study will involve seven rigorous stages: (1) extensive review of reports and academic papers; (2) in-depth interviews; (3) a Delphi study to determine domains and indicators; (4) an AHP study to identify the relative importance of the domains and the indicators; (5) main surveys; (6) dimensionality of the HESGPEI, validity and reliability checks, cross-national/cultural validation, generalization, and further analyses; and (7) overall assessment of the developed HESGPEI. The results will enable the development of new solutions/policies/programs/systems for organizations, including organizational culture change, contributions to society, sustainable and environmental applications, responsibility, fairness, and diversity. The standardized instrument will guide the preparation of reports on all hotels’ ESG performances and enable comparison of hotels’ ESG performance levels. Because this multidisciplinary investigation using mixed methods is pioneering and urgently needed, the results will contribute to helping hotels worldwide to enhance their ESG performance, and transfer new knowledge to other industries.

15500126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15500126.value: 組織團隊賦能對一線員工服務創新及客戶滿意度結果的多層次影響：一種角色認同範式

15500126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15500126.value: Prof Bai, Billy Prof Lu, Lin

15500126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15500126.value: Hospitality firms increasingly rely on employees’ innovation to provide new products and services with an ultimate goal is to enhance customers’ satisfaction and retention. Service innovation is a process of an individual developing a new way of service during interaction with customers. It is critical to examine how and when firm empowerment, in which human capital are embedded, instigate innovation on service. Curiously, firm empowerment has noticeably received little attention, and should have important implications for employee service innovation as it conveys role expectations to frontline staff and speaks to the elemental underpinnings of innovation (e.g., self-direction and information sharing). More importantly, current research has taken the intrinsic motivation perspective to understand how workplace empowerment such as leadership/culture influences service innovation, especially in hospitality context, and those that did have generated mixed results, suggesting that firm empowerment needs to further explore and examine in hotel and tourism industry. In view of the controversy surrounding the intrinsic motivation perspective, it is important to examine whether other mechanism(s) explains the influence of firm empowerment on employee service innovation. Our first research question therefore is: does firm empowerment exert cross-level influence on employee service innovation via a mechanism beyond intrinsic motivation? Second, little research has examined the roles of cultural values in the process linking firm empowerment and employee service innovation. This omission is problematic because it leaves unexamined an important boundary condition for the effect of firm empowerment. Theory on empowerment that would remain incomplete if the cultural boundary condition remains unknown. Hotel managers would act with little guidance when managing employee innovation with different cultural values. Our second research question therefore is: do employees’ cultural values strengthen or weaken the mechanism linking firm empowerment to service innovation? Building on role identity theory, we posit creative role identity (i.e. a self-view or internalized set of role expectations that innovation is important and one should be innovative) as a cross-level mechanism linking firm empowerment and employee innovation. Furthermore, we conduct the study in China, a high-power distance and relational culture where interdependent self-construal prevails over independent self-construal. In this context, the concern for others’ expectations is high and role expectations from leaders and members are key sources of an individual’s role identity and behaviors. We therefore consider China an appropriate setting for examining the mechanism. 酒店與旅遊業企業日益依賴員工的創新來提供新產品與服務，最終目標是提升顧客滿意度與留存率。服務創新是指員工在與顧客互動的過程中發展出新服務方式的過程。探討企業賦能（即蘊含人力資本的賦能型領導與組織文化）如何以及何時激發員工的服務創新，具有至關重要的意義。 值得注意的是，企業賦能這項議題先前鮮少受到關注，而它理應對員工服務創新產生重要影響。 基於角色認同理論，我們提出「創造性角色認同」作為連結組織/團隊賦能與員工創新的跨層級機制。此外，本研究在中國進行；中國是一個高權力距離和重關係的文化環境，其中相互依賴型自我構念佔據主導地位，而非獨立型自我構念。

15500226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15500226.value: 情緒光譜：基於大語言模型人格驅動分歧指標的資産定價研究

15500226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15500226.value: Prof Han, Bing Prof Zhan, Xintong, Eunice

15500226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15500226.value: Personality plays a crucial role in shaping financial behavior by influencing how individuals process information and make investment decisions. Even when presented with identical information, investors with different personality traits often interpret it in distinct ways, leading to investor disagreement. While previous research has primarily attributed investor disagreement to variations in information sets, model specifications, or demographic factors such as gender, age, education, and wealth (Hong and Stein, 2007; Cookson and Niessner, 2020; Bali, Kelly, Mörke, and Rahman, 2023), the impact of personality-driven disagreement remains largely unexplored. This study seeks to address this gap by investigating how personality traits contribute to investor disagreement and assessing their potential effects on stock market outcomes. To implement this idea, we employ Large Language Models (LLMs) to simulate diverse investor personalities at scale. LLMs are increasingly used in financial research for sentiment analysis, risk assessment, and prediction generation from textual data. While most studies treat LLMs as objective tools, recent evidence suggests they can adopt distinct perspectives and exhibit human-like biases when appropriately prompted (Bybee, 2023). We leverage this capability by incorporating personality traits into LLM prompts using the Big Five framework, which encompasses Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, and Neuroticism. For each firm-specific news item, we prompt the LLM to act as an investor with varying Big Five profiles, generating sentiment and risk scores with concise reasoning. This approach yields a set of sentiment–risk evaluations for each news item, which we aggregate at the firm-date level to construct measures of personality-driven disagreement in both sentiment and risk. Our framework is flexible and can accommodate alternative personality models, such as the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI), enabling broader behavioral insights and cross-framework comparisons. To validate our LLM-based measures, we will conduct surveys with real investors to capture their personality profiles and interpretations of identical news items. This approach enables a direct comparison between human responses and LLM-simulated outputs. We will then analyze how personality-driven disagreement correlates with stock market outcomes, contributing to the literature on investor disagreement in asset pricing (Miller, 1977; Diether, Malloy, and Scherbina, 2002; Cookson and Niessner, 2020). Further analyses will assess the relative importance of specific personality traits in shaping sentiment and risk perceptions, and investigate how these influences vary across different market environments. By integrating personality theory with LLMs, our study introduces a novel, scalable, and replicable method for quantifying personality-driven disagreement, advancing research in behavioral asset pricing. 人格在塑造金融行為方面扮演著關鍵角色，因為它會影響個人處理資訊以及做出投資決策的方式。即使面對相同資訊，具有不同人格特質的投資者往往也會以不同方式加以解讀，進而導致投資者分歧。過去研究主要將投資者分歧歸因於資訊集合、模型設定，或性別、年齡、教育程度與財富等人口統計因素的差異，然而，由人格驅動的分歧所造成的影響仍大多未被探討。本研究旨在填補此一缺口，透過探究人格特質如何導致投資者分歧，並評估其對股票市場結果的潛在影響。 為實現此構想，我們採用大型語言模型（Large Language Models, LLMs）以大規模模擬多樣化的投資者人格。LLMs 在金融研究中日益被用於情緒分析、風險評估，以及從文本資料中生成預測。儘管多數研究將 LLMs 視為客觀工具，近期證據顯示，在適當提示下，LLMs 能夠採納不同觀點並展現類似人類的偏誤。我們利用此一能力，透過大五人格框架（Big Five framework）將人格特質納入 LLM 提示中；該框架涵蓋開放性、盡責性、外向性、宜人性與神經質。針對每一則公司特定新聞，我們提示 LLM 扮演具有不同大五人格特徵的投資者，並生成情緒分數與風險分數，同時提供簡潔推理。此方法可為每一則新聞產生一組情緒—風險評估，接著我們在公司—日期層級進行彙整，以建構由人格驅動的情緒分歧與風險分歧衡量指標。 我們的框架具有彈性，可容納其他人格模型，例如邁爾斯—布里格斯性格分類指標（Myers-Briggs Type Indicator, MBTI），從而促進更廣泛的行為洞察與跨框架比較。為驗證我們基於 LLM 的衡量指標，我們將對真實投資者進行問卷調查，以蒐集其人格特徵及其對相同新聞項目的解讀。此方法能夠直接比較人類回應與 LLM 模擬輸出。接著，我們將分析由人格驅動的分歧如何與股票市場結果相關聯，從而對資產定價中投資者分歧的文獻做出貢獻。 進一步分析將評估特定人格特質在塑造情緒與風險感知方面的相對重要性，並探討這些影響如何在不同市場環境下產生變化。透過結合人格理論與 LLMs，本研究提出一種新穎、可擴展且可複製的方法，用以量化由人格驅動的投資者分歧，進而推進行為資產定價領域的研究。

15500726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15500726.value: 旅遊預訂中的人工智慧推薦：探究演算法說服對銀髮族旅客決策的影響

15500726.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15500726.value: Prof Liu, Tingting Prof Xu, Jun

15500726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15500726.value: The rapid growth of the senior traveller sector, driven by global demographic shifts and rising life expectancy, has positioned older adults as a strategically significant market for the tourism industry. According to the Hong Kong Chief Executive's 2025 Policy Address, people aged 65 and above will account for 36% of the total population by 2046. Seniors not only represent a substantial proportion of the population but also possess higher disposable incomes and flexible travel schedules, making them an attractive segment for travel businesses. Despite their increasing engagement with digital technologies, research on artificial intelligence (AI) in tourism has largely overlooked the unique needs and challenges faced by senior travellers. This project addresses this gap by investigating how seniors perceive, trust, and adopt AI-powered travel services, with a particular focus on algorithmic persuasion. Drawing on theoretical frameworks such as the Persuasion Knowledge Model and the Elaboration Likelihood Model, the research explores the interplay between algorithmic cues, trust, aversion, and behavioral outcomes in travel decision-making. Four key research questions guide the inquiry: (1) How do senior travellers’ perceptions of AI recommendations influence their decision-making across different stages of the travel journey? (2) What factors contribute to the effectiveness of AI’s algorithmic persuasion among seniors? (3) What strategies can effectively guide the design of AI-powered travel services to build trust and promote adoption among senior travellers? (4) Do seniors prefer “senior-friendly AI” tailored to their needs, or general AI, and what factors shape these preferences? A multi-stage, mixed-methods approach is employed. Phase I involves a comprehensive literature review and industry consultation to inform research instruments. Phase II uses in-depth interviews and focus groups to qualitatively explore seniors’ experiences, trust dynamics, and aversion towards AI in travel planning. Phase III quantitatively examines predictors of algorithm aversion and trust through structured surveys, experimental studies, and real-behavior studies in controlled environments to capture objective usage patterns and preferences. Findings from this research will advance understanding of seniors’ interactions with AI in tourism, identify key factors influencing trust and adoption, and inform the design of inclusive, effective AI-powered travel services. By integrating qualitative insights and behavioral data, the project aims to support the development of digital travel solutions that foster trust, satisfaction, and adoption among senior travellers, ultimately contributing to more accessible and user-centered tourism experiences. 受全球人口結構變化和預期壽命延長等因素推動，老年遊客群迅速成長，已成為旅遊業中具有戰略意義的市場。根據香港行政長官2025年《施政報告》，到2046年，65歲以上人口將佔總人口的36%。老年族群不僅人口佔比高，而且擁有較高的可支配收入和靈活的旅行時間，這使其成為旅遊企業極具吸引力的目標客群。儘管老年人對數位科技的接觸日益增多，但現有的旅遊人工智慧（AI）研究在很大程度上忽略了這群人獨特的各種需求與挑戰。本計畫旨在填補此研究空白，重點探討老年人如何認知、信任並採納由AI驅動的旅遊服務，並特別關注「演算法說服」（algorithmic persuasion）這個機制。 本研究借鑒「說服知識模型」（Persuasion Knowledge Model）和「精細可能性模型」（Elaboration Likelihood Model）等理論框架，探討旅遊決策過程中演算法提示、信任、抵觸情緒與行為結果之間的相互作用。研究主要圍繞著以下四個問題：（1）老年遊客對AI推薦的認知如何影響其在旅遊全過程各階段的決策？ （2）哪些因素決定了AI演算法說服在老年族群的有效性？ （3）應採取何種策略來指導AI驅動旅遊服務的設計，從而建立信任並促進老年遊客的採納？ （4）老年人更傾向於使用針對其需求量身定制的“適老化AI”，還是通用型AI？哪些因素塑造了這些偏好？ 本研究採用多階段混合研究法。第一階段包括全面的文獻綜述和產業諮詢，為研究工具的設計提供基礎。第二階段透過深度訪談與焦點小組，定性探討老年人在旅遊規劃過程中與AI相關的體驗、信任動態及抵觸心理。第三階段透過結構化問卷調查、實驗研究、受控環境下的真實行為研究，量化分析演算法抵觸與信任的預測因素，進而捕捉客觀的使用模式與偏好。 本研究的成果將深化對旅遊情境下老年人與AI互動關係的理解，識別影響信任與採納的關鍵因素，並為設計包容性強且高效的AI驅動旅遊服務提供指導。該計畫旨在透過整合定性洞察與行為數據，支持開發能夠提升老年遊客信任度、滿意度及使用意願的數位旅行解決方案，從而最終助力打造更具無障礙性且以用戶為中心的旅遊體驗。

15501626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15501626.value: 摒弃儿童菜单 “一刀切” 模式：结合发育阶段定制餐厅儿童菜单，打造健康外出就餐方案

15501626.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15501626.value: Dr LUO, Anqi Prof SHIN, Seunghun Prof Stantic, Bela

15501626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15501626.value: Child obesity and family dining outside home are the two common phenomena across the globe. In the United States (US), approximately 20 percent of children and adolescents have obesity. Child obesity may give burden to the health care system. In 2019, the medical cost associated with child obesity was 1.3 billion US dollars. One of the major causes of child obesity is eating behaviour, particularly eating away from home. In this connection, some restaurants have children’s menus or offer children a reduced portion size from regular menus with a lower price. However, the current restaurant practice on children’s menus does not consider different nutritional needs based on physiological development of children. For example, pre-schoolers (4-6 years) may have different nutritional needs from toddlers (1-3 years). Thus, we should rethink one-menu-fits-all approach in the current practice. Furthermore, this study investigates how parents can encourage children to choose nutritious menus based on their psychosocial development. For example, since toddlers often seek independence and autonomy, parents can help them make their own menu choices rather than imposing decisions. This project proposes a framework that integrates child development stages to menu design and nutritional provision in the out-of-home dining context. To do so, we propose three studies. Phase I involves an analysis of the nutritional profile of children's menus in restaurants and how they vary based on child developmental stages. We will use review texts and images from OpenRice and Google Maps and conduct field observations of kitchen staff. Phase II involves interviews with restaurant operators to investigate how they can design and promote children’s menus to improve nutritional benefits based on child developmental stages. Finally, Phase III explores how parents can encourage children to choose nutritious menus based on child developmental stages. We will conduct interviews with parents who will be recruited from playgroups, restaurants, and the research team’s networks. The current project extends previous work on family dining and nutritional quality of children’s menus by accounting for physiological and psychosocial development of children.
