This integrative approach will address fundamental questions in marine microbial ecology while developing predictive capacity for ecosystem responses to climate change, generating the first quantitative forecasts of population genetic shifts in marine carbon cycle organisms under future environmental conditions and establishing methodological frameworks applicable to diverse marine systems. 海洋浮游植物貢獻了全球約半數的初級生產力，然而儘管其在海洋碳循環中扮演關鍵角色，我們對其演化動態的理解仍相當有限。青綠藻綱（Mamiellophyceae）為全球廣泛分布且數量豐富的微微型真核綠藻類群，其與綠藻病毒（prasinovirus）之間長期處於協同演化的軍備競賽之中，此一互動不僅驅動快速的遺傳變異，也維繫著生態系的多樣性。雖然實驗室研究已證實宿主與病毒的協同演化能促成快速的物種分化，但如何將這些受控環境下的觀察結果外推至自然海洋族群，仍是當前重要的科學前沿課題。 本計畫擬整合全球性總體基因體調查、高解析度時序基因體學分析，以及以培養株進行的機制性驗證，建立首個全面且跨尺度的架構，用以理解並預測海洋宿主—病毒系統的協同演化動態。研究方法將運用先進的菌株層級總體基因體分析工具、來自南海為期五年的獨特時間序列資料，以及主持人所建立之具地理連結性的豐富分離株庫，藉以銜接區域性演化過程與全球生物地理格局。 我們將檢驗有關隱蔽族群結構、季節性遺傳循環，以及關鍵功能基因座上頻率依賴型選汰等假說，並最終將此多尺度資料集整合為機器學習模型，以預測族群對未來氣候情境的遺傳反應。此一整合性研究途徑不僅可回應海洋微生物生態學中的根本問題，亦能發展出預測生態系對氣候變遷反應的能力，首次針對未來環境條件下海洋碳循環生物之族群遺傳變化提出量化預測，並建立可廣泛應用於各類海洋系統的方法學框架。

16102026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16102026.value: 靶向視覺環路重塑治療青光眼：基於組合光遺傳學的結構與功能重建策略

16102026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16102026.value: Glaucoma is a leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide, characterized by progressive degeneration of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and their axons. Current treatments can slow disease progression but cannot reverse vision loss, particularly in advanced stages with significant RGC degeneration and demyelination. Inspired by axon sprouting-mediated recovery in spinal cord injury and stroke models, we propose that targeted reinnervation of visual centers by surviving RGCs offer a promising restorative strategy. However, uncontrolled axon sprouting may produce non-functional or maladaptive connections, and the chronic, variable progression of glaucoma necessitates interventions that are both potent and tunable. To address this, we require a tool capable of precise temporal control and potent stimulation of axon regrowth. The BDNF-TrkB pathway, a central regulator of neuronal growth and plasticity, is limited for therapeutic use by the poor stability and specificity of BDNF. To overcome these, we employ an optogenetic TrkB system (LiTrkB), which enables reversible and precise activation of TrkB using blue light. Our preliminary data demonstrate that LiTrkB activation enhances RGC survival and axonal regeneration in an optic nerve injury model. In an excitotoxicity model, post-injury LiTrkB activation enhanced RGC dendritic regrowth, promoted axon sprouting in visual centers, and partially restored visual function. While promising, these findings remain preliminary in mechanisms and clinical relevance. This proposal aims to bridge these gaps using LiTrkB in a severe, silicone oil-induced glaucoma model that mimics advanced human disease. Additionally, our published study showed that enhancing visual pathway activity via melanopsin overexpression improved pupillary light reflex recovery mediated by regenerated axons after optic tract injury. We hypothesize that pairing LiTrkB activation with melanopsin-guided activity boosting will refine visual circuit synaptic connection for improved vision recovery. In Aim 1, we will activate LiTrkB post-injury in a glaucoma model to investigate visual recovery and the underlying mechanisms. In Aim 2, we will co-express LiTrkB with melanopsin in RGCs and implement patterned light stimulation to promote structural growth and activity-dependent synapse refinement. Building on these, aim 3 will integrate a pro-remyelination therapy with this dual-optogenetic approach, evaluating the synergistic potential of combined axonal sprouting, synaptic refinement, and remyelination to restore structural integrity and visual function. Together, this work represents a paradigm shift from neuroprotection to active circuit reconstruction and myelin repair. By establishing a non-invasive, light-controlled therapeutic platform that coordinates multiple repair mechanisms, we aim to develop a powerful treatment capable of restoring meaningful vision in glaucoma. 青光眼是全球範圍內導致不可逆性失明的主要原因之一，其特徵為視網膜神經節細胞（RGCs）及其軸突的進行性退變。現有治療方法雖能延緩疾病進程，但無法逆轉已受損的視覺功能，尤其在RGC大量死亡並伴發脫髓鞘病變的晚期階段。受脊髓損傷和腦卒中模型中軸突出芽介導功能恢復的啟發，利用殘存RGC的軸突對視覺中樞進行靶向性再支配，被認為是一條極具前景的修復路徑。然而，不受調控的軸突出芽可能導致無功能或錯誤配對的突觸連接，加之青光眼病程的多變性與慢性進展，要求干預措施兼具高效性和可調性。因此，極需一種能夠在時間維度上精確控制、並能高效激發軸突再生的工具。 BDNF‑TrkB通路是調控神經元生長與可塑性的核心信號軸，但BDNF本身穩定性差、特異性不足，限制了其臨床應用。為克服這些限制，我們採用光遺傳學TrkB系統（LiTrkB），通過藍光照射實現TrkB信號通路的可逆、精准啟動。前期實驗表明，在視神經損傷模型中，LiTrkB啟動可提高RGC存活率並促進軸突再生；在興奮性毒性模型中，損傷後啟動LiTrkB能促進RGC樹突再生長，增強視覺中樞的軸突出芽，並部分恢復視覺功能。儘管這些結果令人振奮，但其作用機制及與臨床疾病的相關性尚待深入闡明。本項目擬在模擬人類晚期青光眼的矽油誘導重度青光眼模型中應用LiTrkB，以填補上述研究空白。此外，我們以往發表的研究顯示，過表達黑視蛋白可增強視覺通路活性，從而改善視束損傷後由再生軸突介導的瞳孔對光反射恢復。據此，我們擬將LiTrkB啟動與黑視蛋白介導的視覺通路活性增強相聯合，以優化視覺環路的突觸連接，最終實現更優的視力恢復。 本項目具體包含以下三個研究目標： 目標1：在青光眼模型誘導損傷後啟動LiTrkB，系統評估視力恢復效果並探究其潛在分子機制。 目標2：在RGC中共表達LiTrkB與黑視蛋白，並施加特定模式的光刺激，以促進軸突出芽生長及活動依賴性突觸精細化重建。 目標3：將促髓鞘再生治療與上述組合光遺傳學策略聯用，綜合評估軸突出芽生長、突觸精細化重建和髓鞘再生三者協同的治療潛力，以恢復視覺通路的結構完整性與視覺功能。 總體而言，本工作代表了從神經保護向主動環路重建和髓鞘修復的範式轉變。通過建立一種非侵入性、精細光調控且能協同多種修復機制的治療平臺，我們旨在開發一種能夠有效恢復青光眼患者視覺功能的強效治療策略。

16102426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16102426.value: 解析人源DICER切割特异性：RNA茎长、开放末端及3’末端碱基配对的调控作用

16102426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16102426.value: MicroRNAs and siRNAs produced by human DICER mediate precise, sequence- and position-dependent gene silencing, yet the rules by which DICER interprets RNA duplex features to choose 21- versus 22-nt products (DC21 vs. DC22) remain incompletely defined, limiting mechanistic insight and shRNA design. We investigate how three prevalent duplex features, stem length, open-end configurations (e.g., 1–3, 2–4, 3–5 overhangs), and terminal base-pairing with 3′ tails, converge to bias cleavage-site selection. Preliminary high-throughput dicing data indicate that longer stems shift products toward DC22 in a dsRBD-dependent manner, with open-end architectures further amplifying DC22 selection. Cryo-EM structures of DICER bound to long-stem RNA in a cutting state reveal distinct dsRBD engagement relative to short stems, suggesting a cooperative mechanism that repositions the catalytic center to favor 22-nt products; we also capture a previously unobserved pre-dicing state on long-stem substrates. Building on these findings, we will (i) quantify how stem length, end openness, and terminal pairing/3′ tails influence DC21/DC22 selection using high-throughput assays with wild-type and domain-perturbed DICER; (ii) validate determinants in vitro with pre-miRNAs/shRNAs and in human cells, linking cleavage outcomes to mature small-RNA profiles and target repression; and (iii) resolve cryo-EM structures of DICER bound to representative substrates to visualize how these RNA features reposition the catalytic center and enforce DC21 vs. DC22 outcomes. By unifying large-scale functional mapping with structural visualization, this work will establish a mechanistic framework for how human DICER reads RNA ends and counts stem length, clarify how natural variation in these features tunes miRNA maturation and function, and yield actionable design rules for shRNAs with improved precision and potency. 人源 DICER 酶切割产生微小RNA（miRNA）与小干扰RNA（siRNA），二者可介导高精确的、依赖序列和位置的基因沉默。然而目前DICER如何解读RNA双链结构特征以选择生成21-nt还是22-nt产物（即DC21与DC22）的规则尚不完全清楚，这限制了对其作用机制的深入理解以及shRNA的合理设计。本研究探究三种常见的双链结构特征：茎长、开放末端构型（如1–3nt、2–4nt、3–5nt突出端）以及带有3′尾的末端碱基配对，如何协同调控切割位点的选择偏好。前期高通量切割测序数据表明：RNA茎长更长时，产物倾向DC22，该效应依赖双链RNA结合结构域（dsRBD），而开放末端构型则进一步放大这种对DC22的选择。对处于切割状态下的DICER与长茎RNA底物形成的cryo-EM结构解析，发现其dsRBD结合模式与短茎底物时明显不同，提示存在一种协同机制，通过重新定位催化中心从而偏向生成22-nt产物。此外，我们还捕获了此前未被观察到的对于长茎底物的切割前构象。基于上述发现，我们将开展三方面工作：（1）利用野生型及结构域突变型DICER开展高通量酶切实验，定量解析茎长、末端开放程度、3‘端末端配对程度对DC21/DC22产物比例的影响；（2）以pre-miRNA、shRNA为底物开展体外实验，在人体细胞内验证关键决定因素，将切割结果与成熟小RNA图谱及靶基因抑制水平相关联；（3）解析DICER与代表性底物结合的冷冻电镜结构，以直观展示这些RNA特征如何重新定位催化中心并决定DC21与DC22的生成。通过整合大规模功能图谱与高分辨结构观测，本研究将构建一套完整的分子机制框架，阐明人源DICER如何识别RNA末端并计量茎长，明确RNA自然结构变异如何调控miRNA成熟过程与生物学功能，并为提高shRNA精准度和效力的设计提供可操作的规则。

16102526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16102526.value: 研究TruB1在肌肉干细胞中的作用

16102526.label: Co - Investigator(s)
16102526.value: Prof Wu, Zhenguo Prof Zhang, Lisheng

16102526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16102526.value: Adult muscle satellite cells (MuSCs) are responsible for both embryonic and postnatal muscle growth, as well as injury-induced muscle regeneration. Under normal conditions, MuSCs are quiescent with minimal turnover. In response to injury, they exit quiescence, re-enter the cell cycle to proliferate, and subsequently differentiate and fuse to repair the damaged muscle fibers. Each stage of myogenic lineage progression is tightly regulated by intrinsic and extrinsic factors. Disruption of these regulatory mechanisms can impair MuSC function and hinder muscle regeneration. N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modification, the most prevalent and abundant modification in eukaryotic mRNA, has been shown to play a crucial role in regulating MuSC functions. However, the role of pseudouridine (Ψ), the second-most abundant modification in mRNAs, in MuSCs remains poorly understood. Recently, the development of the bisulfite-induced deletion sequencing (BID-seq) has enabled the quantitative and transcriptome-wide mapping of Ψ, providing an excellent opportunity to explore its role across diverse biological processes. We are particularly interested in understanding its role in regulating MuSC functions. Our preliminary data indicated that the expression levels of several pseudouridine synthases (e.g., TruB1 and Pus7), the Ψ modification writer proteins, decreased during myogenic differentiation. Consistently, knockout of these writers in C2C12 cells promoted differentiation. Furthermore, through BID-seq analysis of proliferating myoblasts and differentiating myotubes, we demonstrated a close association between Ψ modification patterns and cellular states. These findings suggest that Ψ modification plays an important role in regulating myogenic differentiation. However, its role in regulating MuSC functions in vivo remains unknown. Genome-wide analysis indicated that TRUB1 and PUS7, two Ψ writer proteins, collectively account for ~60% of the high-confidence pseudouridylation sites in human mRNA. TruB1 has been reported to suppress cell proliferation by promoting let-7 maturation. To further understand the role of TruB1 in MuSCs in vivo, we have generated a MuSC-specific TruB1 knockout mouse line. Our preliminary data showed that MuSC-specific TruB1 deletion impaired muscle regeneration. In this proposed project, we will carefully characterize the behavior of TruB1-null MuSCs in the mutant mouse line and investigate the underlying mechanisms. Additionally, to broaden the scope of our study, we will also explore the role of Ψ modification in regulating MuSC aging. Our work will deepen our understanding of the impact of Ψ modification on MuSC functions and aging, with potential implications for the future development of novel regenerative medicines. 肌肉干细胞是调控胚胎和出生后骨骼肌发育，介导肌肉损伤后再生修复的核心细胞。生理稳态下，肌肉干细胞维持静息状态且更新缓慢。当肌肉受损后，它们迅速退出静息态，重新进入增殖周期，并通过分化融合修复受损的肌纤维。肌源性谱系发育的全过程均受内源性信号和外源性因子的精密调控，调控网络紊乱将直接导致肌肉干细胞功能下降，进而阻碍骨骼肌再生。 N6-甲基腺苷（m6A）作为真核mRNA中最丰富的表观转录修饰，已被证实对肌肉干细胞功能具有重要调控作用。然而，假尿苷（Ψ）作为 mRNA 中第二高丰度的修饰，其在肌肉干细胞中的生物学功能仍未被深入解析。最近，BID-seq技术的建立实现了 Ψ 修饰在转录组水平的精准定量与定位，为揭示其在多种生物过程中的功能提供了关键技术支撑。本研究聚焦Ψ修饰在肌肉干细胞功能调节中的潜在作用。前期实验结果显示，多种假尿苷合成酶（例如 TruB1，Pus7）的表达水平在肌源性分化过程中显著下降，且在 C2C12 细胞中敲除上诉分子可显著促进分化。同时，基于BID-seq的分析证实，Ψ修饰图谱与成肌细胞状态高度相关，提示Ψ修饰在肌源性分化中发挥重要调控作用，但其体内生理作用仍有待阐明。 全基因组分析表明，TRUB1 和 PUS7共同介导人类 mRNA 中近60%的高置信度假尿苷化位点。已有研究表明，TruB1可通过促进 let-7 成熟抑制细胞增殖。为深入解析 TruB1 在肌肉干细胞中的生理功能，我们已成功构建肌肉干细胞特异性TruB1 敲除小鼠模型，初步结果显示，肌肉干细胞特异性TruB1显著损害肌肉再生能力。在本项目将系统解析TruB1 对肌肉干细胞功能的调控作用及潜在分子机制，并进一步探索Ψ 修饰在肌肉干细胞衰老进程中的调控作用。本研究将首次阐明Ψ修饰在肌肉干细胞功能维持及衰老调控中的关键作用，为推动再生医学新策略的开发提供重要理论依据。

16102726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16102726.value: 探索睫狀體與視網膜信號軸在青光眼發病過程中的作用

16102726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16102726.value: Our eyes are a vital sensory organ that transmits information from the outside world to our brain. Glaucoma is the second leading cause of blindness, affecting approximately 80 million people worldwide. It is caused by the gradual loss of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), whose axons form the optic nerve connecting the retina with the brain. There are two major types: hypertension glaucoma (HTG), which is associated with elevated intraocular pressure (IOP), and normal-tension glaucoma (NTG), where the IOP is normal. Lowering the IOP effectively slows the vision loss in 50-60% HTG patients, but it is not effective for NTG. Because the molecular mechanisms underlying RGC death in glaucoma are largely unknown, there are no other effective treatments for it. Our previous study proposed that the ciliary body (CB) forms the intraocular "niche" for maintaining various eye tissues, including the retina, through its secretion. Our preliminary studies indicate that mice with a TGF-β-signaling-defective CB exhibit an NTG-like phenotype, characterized by age-dependent RGC loss without elevated IOP. The TGF-β signaling-defective CB upregulates WIF1, which is secreted into the vitreous to bind WNT7b and inhibit WNT signaling in RGCs, causing their loss. This demonstrates, for the first time, an important role of the CB-to-retina signaling axis in NTG pathogenesis. Therefore, this project will not only benefit the vision field but also contribute to local healthcare, biotech communities, and the general Hong Kong public in the long run. 我們的眼睛是至關重要的感覺器官，負責將外界信息傳遞給大腦。青光眼是全球第二大致盲原因，影響著全球約 8,000 萬人。它的成因是視網膜神經節細胞（RGC）的逐漸流失，而這些細胞的軸突構成了連接視網膜與大腦的視神經。青光眼主要分為兩大類：一種是與眼壓（IOP）升高相關的高眼壓性青光眼（HTG）；另一種是眼壓正常的正常眼壓性青光眼（NTG）。降低眼壓能有效減緩 50-60% 高眼壓性青光眼患者的視力喪失，但對正常眼壓性青光眼卻不奏效。由於青光眼導致 RGC 死亡的分子機制在很大程度上尚不明確，目前臨床上缺乏其他有效的治療方法。 我們以往的研究提出，睫狀體（CB）通過其分泌作用，構成了維持包括視網膜在內的多種眼部組織的眼內「微環境」（niche）。我們的初步研究表明，睫狀體 TGF-β 信號傳導缺陷的小鼠會表現出類似正常眼壓青光眼的表型，其特徵為年齡依賴性的 RGC 流失，且不伴隨眼壓升高。TGF-β 信號傳導缺陷的睫狀體會上調 WIF1 的表達，WIF1 被分泌到玻璃體中與 WNT7b 結合，進而抑制 RGC 中的 WNT 信號傳導，導致其流失。這首次證明了「睫狀體-視網膜」信號軸在正常眼壓青光眼發病機制中的重要作用。 這是一項具有創新性和顛覆範式（paradigm-shifting）的研究，因為我們檢驗了一個全新的假說—即「睫狀體-視網膜」信號軸在青光眼發病機制中起著關鍵作用，這將為揭示人類青光眼的病因開闢一條新途徑。本研究的發現將有助於揭示關鍵的發病機制，用以開發新的青光眼治療策略，並證實「睫狀體-視網膜」信號軸直接參與了青光眼的發病過程。因此，從長遠來看，該項目不僅將造福眼科視覺領域，還將對本地醫療保健、生物科技界以及香港廣大市民做出貢獻。

16103426.value: 海洋藍細菌的囊泡與噬菌體相互作用的結構機制

16103426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16103426.value: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are nanoscale particles released by bacteria that play critical roles in intercellular communication, nutrient acquisition, horizontal gene transfer, and host-pathogen interactions. Two major types of EVs have been identified: B-type EVs, formed via outer membrane blebbing during normal growth, and E-type EVs, generated through explosive cell lysis triggered by bacteriophage infection. In marine ecosystems, cyanobacteria like Prochlorococcus and Synechococcus are dominant primary producers that can release a large amount of EVs. By carrying DNA and RNA, cyanobacterial EVs can potentially act as key vectors for horizontal gene transfer, promoting genetic exchange within marine microbial communities. Cyanobacterial viruses (cyanophages) are estimated to infect ~15% of marine cyanobacteria on a daily basis, playing important roles in cyanobacteria-mediated marine carbon cycle. Cyanophages also interact with EVs, though the functional and structural basis of these interactions remains poorly understood, limiting our ability to model marine microbial processes accurately. While previous studies have shown that EVs can either inhibit or promote phage infection, most have focused on B-type EVs from uninfected bacterial cells. It remains unclear how E-type EVs produced during phage infection differ in composition and function, and how both EV types influence phage infection of bacteria. Moreover, the molecular and structural mechanisms underlying EV–phage interactions are largely unknown. This proposal aims to address these gaps by systematically comparing EV types and their dynamic roles during phage infection of marine cyanobacteria. Our preliminary work has established a strong foundation for this study. We have characterized the proteome of Prochlorococcus MED4 B-type EVs, resolved the high-resolution structure of cyanophage P-SCSP1u, and developed a vesicle-based method for structural studies of membrane proteins. We have also shown that phage infection increases EV production and that EVs can inhibit phage infectivity. This project will characterize B-type and E-type EVs from infected and uninfected cyanobacteria using proteomics, quantify their effects on phage infectivity, and employ advanced cryo-electron microscopy and tomography to visualize EV biogenesis and EV-phage interactions at near-atomic resolution. By elucidating the molecular and structural basis of EV-phage dynamics, this research will provide critical insights into microbial defense strategies, horizontal gene transfer, and virus-driven mortality, ultimately improving models of genetic exchange and carbon cycling in the global ocean. 胞外囊泡（Extracellular vesicles）是細菌釋放的奈米級顆粒，在細胞間通訊、營養獲取、水平基因轉移以及宿主－病原體相互作用中發揮關鍵作用。目前已鑑定出兩種類型的胞外囊泡：B型囊泡，在正常生長過程中透過外膜出芽形成；以及E型囊泡，由噬菌體感染引發的爆炸性細胞裂解產生。在海洋生態系統中，原綠球藻（Prochlorococcus）和聚球藻（Synechococcus）等藍細菌是佔主導地位的初級生產者，能夠釋放大量胞外囊泡。藍細菌囊泡攜帶DNA和RNA，因而可能成為水平基因轉移的關鍵載體，促進海洋微生物群落內的基因交換。據估計，藍細菌病毒（噬藻體）每天感染約15%的海洋藍細菌，在藍細菌介導的海洋碳循環中發揮重要作用。噬藻體也與囊泡相互作用，然而這些相互作用的功能和結構基礎至今仍知之甚少，這限制了我們準確模擬海洋微生物過程的能力。 雖然已有研究表明囊泡可抑制或促進噬菌體侵染，但多數研究聚焦於未侵染細菌細胞產生的B型囊泡。目前尚不清楚噬菌體侵染期間產生的E型囊泡在組成和功能上有何差異，以及這兩種囊泡類型如何影響噬菌體對細菌的侵染。此外，囊泡–噬菌體相互作用的分子和結構機制在很大程度上仍屬未知。本課題旨在透過系統比較囊泡類型及其在噬菌體侵染海洋藍細菌過程中的動態作用，來彌補這些空白。我們的前期工作已為這項研究奠定了堅實基礎：我們鑑定了原綠球藻MED4 B型囊泡的蛋白質組，解析了噬藻體P-SCSP1u的高解析度結構，並開發了一種基於囊泡的膜蛋白結構研究方法。我們還發現噬菌體侵染會增加囊泡的產生，且囊泡能夠抑制噬菌體的侵染活性。 本計畫將利用蛋白質組學技術，對侵染和未侵染藍細菌的B型和E型囊泡進行表徵，量化它們對噬菌體侵染性的影響，並採用先進的冷凍電子顯微鏡和斷層掃描技術，在近原子解析度下可視化囊泡生物發生及囊泡–噬菌體相互作用。透過闡明囊泡–噬菌體動態變化的分子和結構基礎，本研究將為微生物防禦策略、水平基因轉移以及病毒驅動的死亡率提供關鍵認識，從而改進全球海洋中基因交換和碳循環的模型預測。

16103826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16103826.value: 非典型基因組複製起始許可

16103826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16103826.value: Faithful genome duplication requires the precise assembly of pre-replication complex (pre-RC) at thousands of replication origins. This licensing process is orchestrated by the Origin Recognition Complex (ORC) together with Cdc6 and Cdt1 to load two MCM2-7 complexes into an inactive head-to-head double hexamer (DH). Dysregulation of this process is linked to human diseases[1], including cancer[2-4] and Meier-Gorlin syndrome[5,6], underscoring its biological significance. While the canonical licensing pathway has been extensively characterized in vitro using purified components and model DNA templates, it remains unclear how this process is executed across the native chromatin landscape in vivo. Emerging evidence suggests the existence of alternative, non-canonical licensing mechanisms that operate under specific genomic or chromatin contexts. Here, we propose an integrative approach to systematically identify and characterize noncanonical pathways of MCM-DH assembly in yeast cells. Leveraging unique ORC mutants that selectively disrupt canonical licensing pathway while sparing a subset of replication origins, we will (1) classify replication origins by their pathway dependency, (2) define the chromatin features and auxiliary factors that enable noncanonical licensing, and (3) determine high-resolution structures of key intermediates in this alternative assembly route. The outcome of this research will redefine the mechanistic landscape of replication licensing, providing fundamental insights into how cells ensure complete and accurate genome duplication in the face of chromatin complexity. 忠實的基因組複製需要複製前期複合物被準確組裝在染色體上的複製起點。這一過程由複製起始位點識別複合物（ORC）協同 Cdc6 與 Cdt1 所調控，從而將兩個 MCM2-7 複合物裝載為頭對頭的MCM雙六聚體複合物（DH）。此過程調控的紊亂，會導致相關疾病的發生，包括癌症 及 Meier-Gorlin 侏儒症。這也凸顯這一過程調控在生物學上的重要性。值得注意的是，這一過程的典型調控途徑，已利用體外純化組裝進行了廣泛研究。然而在細胞體內內源染色質環境中此過程如何執行仍不清楚。目前新的證據也顯示，在特定基因組或染色質背景下，存在替代性、非典型的複製起始許可機制。在此研究中，我們計畫系統性地研究酵母細胞中 MCM-DH 組裝的非典型途徑。本研究的成果將重塑真核生物複製起始許可的機制，提供細胞如何在染色質複雜環境下確保完整且精確的基因組複製的關鍵機制。

16104026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16104026.value: 水螅蟲綱逆向發育機制之分子與細胞學機制

16104026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16104026.value: While the biological "arrow of time" typically dictates a one-way path from embryo to aged adult, a few hydrozoan jellyfish defy this principle through ‘reverse development.’ This remarkable process, where a mature adult medusa, under stress, reverts to a juvenile polyp, effectively resets its life cycle, offers a profound opportunity to decode the fundamental mechanisms of cellular reprogramming, regeneration, and aging. However, progress has been critically hampered because the species with the highest reverse ability, the so-called "immortal jellyfish" Turritopsis dohrnii, is difficult to culture. This has prevented the in-depth mechanistic studies required to understand what drives this potential biological rejuvenation, leaving its molecular and cellular basis largely unknown. To overcome this critical bottleneck, we have established Cirrholovenia aeternusa sp. nov., a novel hydrozoan species, as a robust and accessible model for reverse development. We have developed stable, long-term culturing methods and a highly reproducible protocol that induces synchronous reverse development on demand. Using this unique organismal system, this project aims to elucidate the fundamental molecular and cellular mechanisms that orchestrate this process by addressing three key questions: (1) What is the genomic basis for this ability? (2) What is the cellular choreography of the transformation? (3) Which genes are functionally required? To answer these questions, we will pursue three integrated aims. First, we will define the genomic and epigenetic architecture by integrating a chromosome-level genome assembly with multi-omic analyses (RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, Hi-C) to build a predictive gene regulatory network. Second, we will construct a high-resolution spatiotemporal atlas of cellular dynamics by combining advanced imaging of cell proliferation, apoptosis, and migration with single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to map cell fate reprogramming pathways. Finally, we will functionally validate the causal roles of key candidate genes using pharmacological inhibition, RNA interference, and CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing to test their necessity for reverse development. Collectively, this research will produce a comprehensive, systems-level model of ontogenetic reversal, spanning genome architecture, cellular choreography, and functional gene validation. By identifying the core molecular machinery that enables an animal to reverse its life cycle, this work will provide unprecedented insight into developmental plasticity. It may unlock new avenues of research into aging and regeneration. 生物學上的「時間之箭」通常規定了一條由胚胎走向衰老成體的單向路徑，然而少數水螅蟲綱水母卻透過「反向發育」打破了這項原則。在這個極為特殊的過程中，成熟的水母體在遭受逆境時可逆轉回幼年的水螅體，實質上重置了自身的生命週期；這為解讀細胞重編程、再生與老化的根本機制提供了難得的契機。然而，相關研究進展受到嚴重阻礙——具有最強反向發育能力的物種、即所謂的「不死水母」多氏燈塔水母難以人工培養。這使得深入的機制性研究無從展開，我們也因此無法理解究竟是什麼驅動了這種潛在的生物性回春，其分子與細胞基礎至今大多仍屬未知。 為突破此關鍵瓶頸，我們已建立新種水螅蟲，將其發展為穩健且易於操作的反向發育模式生物。我們已開發出穩定的長期培養方法，以及可依需求誘導同步化反向發育的高度可重複實驗流程。借助這一獨特的生物體系統，本計畫旨在闡明統籌此過程的根本分子與細胞機制，並著眼於三個核心問題：（1）此能力的基因體基礎為何？（2）此轉變過程中的細胞動態編排為何？（3）哪些基因是功能上不可或缺的？為回答上述問題，我們將推進三項相互整合的研究目標： 界定基因體與表觀遺傳架構——整合染色體層級的基因體組裝與多體學分析（RNA-seq、ATAC-seq、Hi-C），建構具預測力的基因調控網路。 建構高解析度的細胞動態時空圖譜——結合細胞增生、凋亡與遷移的先進影像技術，以及單細胞與空間轉錄體學，繪製細胞命運重編程的路徑。 功能性驗證關鍵候選基因的因果作用——運用藥理抑制、RNA 干擾與 CRISPR-Cas9 基因編輯，檢驗這些基因對反向發育的必要性。 總體而言，本研究將產出一個涵蓋基因體架構、細胞動態編排與基因功能驗證的全面性、系統層級的個體發育逆轉模型。透過鑑定使動物得以逆轉其生命週期的核心分子機制，本工作將為發育可塑性帶來前所未有的洞見，並可能為老化與再生研究開啟全新的途徑。

16104126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16104126.value: 外周APOE對大腦功能和阿爾茲海默症病理的影響

16104126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16104126.value: The apolipoprotein E gene (APOE) is the strongest genetic risk factor for Alzheimer’s disease (AD) with the APOE4 allele increasing risk and APOE2 allele providing protection relative to the common APOE3 allele. As a lipid carrier, APOE is abundantly expressed both in the brain and periphery. Interestingly, clinical and epidemiological studies have supported an association of both the amount and type of peripheral apoE protein with AD risk. However, how periphery apoE impacts brain functions and AD pathology in an isoform-dependent manner remains a knowledge gap. Since the blood-brain barrier (BBB) separates peripheral and central apoE, conventional humanized APOE knock-in mouse models are unable to specifically address the role of peripheral apoE. Our previous work, using a genetic mouse model with inducible APOE expression, demonstrated that peripheral apoE4 impairs brain cognition and increases AD pathology by compromising cerebrovascular function. Building on this, we recently developed a more versatile and therapeutically relevant AAV-based gene delivery method using a liver hepatocyte-specific albumin promoter to express APOE in the periphery. Preliminary studies confirmed the robust, brain-excluded expression of different APOE genotypes in the liver and blood, successfully recapitulating the effects of apoE isoforms on plasma lipoprotein profiles. For the current proposed studies, we hypothesize that, compared to apoE3, peripheral apoE2 enhances brain function and reduces AD pathology by modulating lipid metabolism and vascular function, while apoE4 exerts the opposite effects. We will test this hypothesis through three specific aims. In Aim 1, we plan to express apoE isoforms in the periphery of both Apoe-KO and APOE4 knock-in mice without AD pathology. Effects on brain cognition, gene expression, lipid profiles, and vascular integrity and function will be examined. In Aim 2, we will introduce peripheral apoE expression in mice with amyloid pathology using Apoe-KO;5xFAD and APOE4;5xFAD mouse models. To evaluate therapeutic potential, we will introduce apoE expression either before (prevention) or after (treatment) amyloid plaque development. In addition to the outcome measures in Aim 1, effects on amyloid pathology will also be evaluated. In Aim 3, we will investigate the effects of peripheral apoE isoforms on tau pathology and tau-mediated neurodegeneration using Apoe-KO;PS19 and APOE4;PS19 mouse models. Our proposed research will provide critical molecular and pathological insights into how peripheral apoE impacts brain health and AD pathology in an isoform-dependent manner, information essential for the mechanism-based design of apoE-targeted therapies. 載脂蛋白 E 基因（APOE）是阿爾茲海默症（Alzheimer’s disease, AD）最重要的遺傳風險因子，其中 APOE4 等位基因會增加 AD 發病風險，而 APOE2 等位基因相較於最常見的 APOE3 等位基因則具有保護作用。作為腦內與外周最重要的脂質載體之一，APOE 在中樞神經系統及外周組織中均有豐富表達。臨床與流行病學研究顯示，外周 apoE 蛋白的含量及其亞型與 AD 風險密切相關，但外周 apoE 如何以影響腦功能及 AD 病理仍未完全闡明。由於血腦屏障（BBB）將外周與中樞神經系統中的 apoE 分隔，傳統人源化 APOE 基因敲入小鼠模型無法特異性解析外周apoE 的作用。我們先前利用可誘導 APOE 表達的小鼠模型證明，外周 apoE4 可透過損害腦血管功能而導致認知障礙並加劇 AD 病理。在此基礎上，我們進一步建立了一套以肝細胞特異性白蛋白啟動子驅動的 AAV 基因遞送平台，實現外周組織特異性的 APOE 表達。初步研究證實，不同 APOE 基因型可在肝臟及血液中穩定且高效表達，而不進入腦組織，並成功重現 apoE 各亞型對血漿脂蛋白譜的已知影響。本研究假設，相較於 apoE3，外周 apoE2 可透過調節脂質代謝及血管功能改善腦部健康並減輕 AD 病理，而 apoE4 則產生相反作用。為驗證此假說，我們將首先在無 AD 病理的 Apoe-KO基因敲入小鼠中表達不同 apoE 亞型，評估其對認知功能、腦部轉錄體變化、脂質代謝以及血管完整性與功能的影響；其次，在 Apoe-KO;5xFAD 及 APOE4;5xFAD 類澱粉蛋白病理模型中，於斑塊形成前或形成後導入外周apoE 表達，以評估其預防及治療潛力，並分析其對 AD 病理及相關生物學指標的影響；最後，在 Apoe-KO;PS19 及 APOE4;PS19 tau 病理模型中，探討外周 apoE 各亞型對 tau 病理及 tau 介導神經退化的調控作用。本研究將系統性揭示外周 apoE 如何透過亞型特異性的機制影響腦部健康及 AD 病理進程，並為開發以 apoE 為標靶的精準治療策略提供重要的理論基礎與轉譯依據。

16104226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16104226.value: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a common neurodegenerative disorder that is characterized by movement impairment which is caused by degeneration of dopaminergic neurons (DA neurons) in the substantia nigra (SNc) of the midbrain with the presence of pathological hallmark designated as Lewy bodies (LBs). PD is mostly sporadic, but familial linked (FPD) cases have been reported. The first gene mutation that is associated with FPD is α-synuclein (α-syn) and it is soon found that α-syn is also the major component of LBs. The discovery of α-syn as the major component in LBs has also raised interest in its role in dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) which is the second most common dementia in the population. PD and DLB are both classified in the category of Lewy body disease or synucleinopathies, however, limited studies have been done on the role of α-syn in the development and pathogenesis of DLB. In this proposal, we will generate transgenic mouse models of PD and DLB based on our previous studies to address how α-syn aggregation can contribute to the pathogenesis of PD and DLB with the formation of LBs in an age-dependent process. We hypotheses that unfolded α-syn fibrils and aggregates with different size and number will slowly accumulate in the neurons along with aging which can affect the neuronal function and hence disease phenotype in various degree. These fibrils and aggregates will be targeted by the ubiquitin and proteasomal system (UPS) and the autophagy and lysosomal pathway (ALP) for degradation, however with aging and other contributing factors, UPS and ALP will be overwhelmed and lead to further accumulation of these aggregates. To minimizes the interference with normal cellular processes, these aggregates will be localized to a cellular compartment such as the perinuclear region and resulted in the formation of LBs. With the newly generated mouse models of PD and DLB, our study will provide new insights into how these α-syn fibrils, aggregates and/or LBs can contribute to the clinical symptoms and pathogenesis in PD and DLB. 16104326.value: 基于高通量单细胞成像技术解析细菌基因表达时序调控及抗生素胁迫适应机制

16104326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16104326.value: Over the past two decades, research in microbial systems biology and synthetic biology has demonstrated that seemingly complex cellular dynamics, such as biological rhythms, temporal signal filtering, and phenotypic memory, can often emerge from, and even be rationally engineered using, a small set of molecular and genetic building blocks. These insights have largely come from studies that record single-cell dynamics of a limited number of specifically designed bacterial strains at a time. However, large-scale discovery of single-cell dynamic phenotypes still remains severely constrained by the lack of suitable experimental tools. Given the stochastic nature of bacterial gene expression and its causal role in the emergence of population heterogeneity within otherwise isogenic communities, discovering and characterizing novel temporal gene expression pattern is of immediate importance for advancing both fundamental microbiology and synthetic biology, from elucidating antibiotic tolerance to enhancing production yields in industrial processes. This proposal seeks to leverage an emerging high-throughput imaging technique to track gene expression dynamics in single bacterial cells under diverse environmental conditions, including chemostatic growth, antibiotic assault, and fluctuating nutrient regimes. By combining microfluidics-based live-cell time-lapse microscopy with seqFISH-enabled in situ genotyping, the expression dynamics of hundreds to thousands of genes as well as cell growth dynamics can be recorded in parallel at single-cell resolution, overcoming the inherent trade-offs among temporal resolution, single-cell information, and experimental throughput that limit existing mainstream techniques such as DNA sequencing, bulk assays, and conventional microscopy. The resulting large-scale single-cell datasets, encompassing the expression dynamics of thousands of bacteria genes together with single-cell growth patterns, will provide unprecedented insight into the temporal heterogeneity and signal-processing capabilities of bacterial gene regulatory networks, as well as their adaptive roles under stress. Ultimately, this work will establish a generally applicable framework for high-dimensional phenotypic discovery, enabling predictive modeling of bacterial dynamics and guiding the rational design of robust genetic circuits and antibiotic treatment strategies. 過去二十年來，系統微生物學與合成生物學研究表明，看似複雜的細胞動態行為（如生物節律、時序信號過濾及表型記憶等）往往產生於簡單的基因調控網絡，並可通過理性設計人工基因迴路實現。這些重要認識主要來源於對少量經過特定設計的細菌菌株開展的單細胞動態研究。然而，由於缺乏適用於大規模動態表型研究的實驗技術，對單細胞動態表型的系統性發現與解析仍受到嚴重制約。鑒於細菌基因表達具有顯著的隨機性，而這種隨機性又是遺傳背景相同細胞群體產生表型異質性的主要機制，系統發現並解析新的基因表達時序模式，對於揭示細菌抗生素耐受等重要生命過程、深化基礎微生物學研究以及推動合成生物學發展（包括提高工業生物製造產率）均具有重要科學意義。 本項目擬利用一種新興的高通量單細胞成像技術，在恆定培養、抗生素脅迫以及營養條件動態變化等多種環境下，系統追蹤細菌單細胞中的基因表達動態。項目將微流控活細胞延時螢光顯微成像與基於seqFISH的原位基因分型技術相結合，並行測量上千個基因表達及對應的單細胞生長分裂的動態表型，通過兼顧時間分辨率、單細胞信息獲取能力和實驗通量，克服現有DNA測序、群體水平檢測及傳統顯微成像等主流技術所面臨的固有限制。 項目最終將構建涵蓋數千個細菌基因表達動態及對應單細胞生長行為的大規模數據集，以前所未有的分辨率揭示細菌基因調控網絡的時序異質性、動態信號處理能力及其在環境脅迫適應中的功能機制。通過結合定量分析與數學模型，本研究將建立一種具有廣泛適用性的高維動態表型發現框架，為細菌動態行為的預測建模提供理論基礎，並為基因迴路的理性設計及抗生素治療策略的優化提供新的理論依據和技術支撐。

16104726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16104726.value: 介導載脂蛋白 E 分選與分泌的分子機制

16104726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16104726.value: Apolipoprotein E (APOE) orchestrates lipid transport, neuronal support, and immune signaling. Its common isoforms, APOE3 and APOE4, differ by single amino acid substitutions yet display distinct biochemical behaviors and disease associations; notably, APOE4 is the strongest genetic risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer's disease. Despite its clinical importance, the intracellular mechanisms that govern the sorting and secretion of APOE remain poorly defined. This process is initiated at the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), where COPII coats, guided by SEC24 isoforms and transmembrane cargo receptors, selectively package soluble cargo into transport vesicles. However, the specific COPII components and receptors that mediate APOE ER exit, and how these steps are influenced by APOE's disease-relevant isoforms, are unknown. To address this, we leveraged a systematic ER export platform combining vesicle reconstitution with quantitative mass spectrometry. Our investigation revealed a conserved Cardin-Weintraub (CW) motif in APOE that is essential for its secretion, as its mutation reduced the secretion of both APOE3 and APOE4, with a more pronounced effect on APOE3. We further identified the ER cargo receptor SURF4 as required for APOE3 secretion and demonstrated that SURF4 localizes to a subset of ER exit sites, with its vesicles specifically enriched for the SEC24B COPII subunit. In contrast, APOE4 follows a divergent route. Vesicle formation assays show APOE3 packaging is COPII-dependent, whereas APOE4 incorporation is insensitive to COPII disruption. Consistently, brefeldin A strongly suppresses APOE3 secretion but does not significantly inhibit APOE4 release. Moreover, APOE4 overexpression diminishes lysosomal proteolytic capacity, linking its altered trafficking to degradative defects. Based on our preliminary analyses, we propose a canonical SURF4-to–proteoglycan (PG) relay for APOE3 export, analogous to our prior model for Sonic hedgehog: SURF4 recognizes the APOE CW motif to drive SEC24B-dependent ER export, followed by handoff to PGs in the Golgi. We hypothesize that APOE4 engages distinct cellular factors to access unconventional routes, with downstream consequences for lysosomal degradative activity. To test this model, we will: define the SURF4-PG relay and determine how early lipid association modulates receptor engagement and ER exit (Objectives 1-2); quantify isoform-specific differences in COPII dependence and lipidation, and identify APOE4-specific trafficking factors (Objective 3); and validate these mechanisms in human iPSC-derived astrocytes (Objective 4). By mapping canonical and unconventional pathways for APOE export, this work provides a molecular blueprint of APOE trafficking and reveals how APOE4 rewires secretory–lysosomal networks relevant to neurodegeneration, highlighting new therapeutic targets in APOE handling. 載脂蛋白 E（APOE）協調脂質運輸、神經元支援及免疫訊號傳遞。其常見異構型 APOE3 與 APOE4 僅相差單一胺基酸置換，卻表現出不同的生化特性及疾病相關性；其中，APOE4 是遲發性阿茲海默症最強的遺傳風險因子。 儘管 APOE 具有重要臨床意義，調控其細胞內分選與分泌的機制仍未被充分釐清。此過程始於內質網（endoplasmic reticulum, ER），在此 COPII 外被蛋白會在 SEC24 異構型及跨膜貨物受體的引導下，選擇性地將可溶性貨物包裝進運輸囊泡。然而，哪些特定 COPII 組件及受體介導 APOE 離開內質網，以及這些步驟如何受 APOE 與疾病相關的異構型影響，目前仍未清楚。 為了解決此問題，我們運用一個系統性的內質網輸出平台，結合囊泡重組與定量質譜分析。研究發現 APOE 中存在一個保守的 Cardin-Weintraub（CW）基序，對其分泌至關重要；當此基序發生突變時，APOE3 與 APOE4 的分泌均下降，而對 APOE3 的影響更為明顯。我們進一步鑑定出內質網貨物受體 SURF4 對 APOE3 分泌是必需的，並證明 SURF4 定位於一部分內質網出口位點，而其囊泡特別富集 SEC24B 這一 COPII 亞基。 相比之下，APOE4 採用一條不同的路徑。囊泡形成實驗顯示，APOE3 的包裝依賴 COPII，而 APOE4 的納入則對 COPII 破壞不敏感。與此一致，布雷菲德菌素 A（brefeldin A）可強烈抑制 APOE3 分泌，卻不會顯著抑制 APOE4 釋放。此外，APOE4 過度表達會降低溶酶體蛋白水解能力，將其異常運輸與降解缺陷聯繫起來。 根據我們的初步分析，我們提出 APOE3 輸出採用一條經典的 SURF4 至蛋白聚醣（proteoglycan, PG）接力機制，類似我們過往就 Sonic hedgehog 所建立的模型：SURF4 辨認 APOE 的 CW 基序，以驅動依賴 SEC24B 的內質網輸出，隨後在高爾基體中轉交予 PG。我們假設 APOE4 會利用不同的細胞因子進入非典型運輸路徑，並對溶酶體降解活性造成下游影響。為驗證此模型，我們將會：界定 SURF4–PG 接力機制，並釐清早期脂質結合如何調控受體參與及內質網輸出（目標 1–2）；定量分析不同異構型在 COPII 依賴性及脂質化方面的差異，並鑑定 APOE4 特異性的運輸因子（目標 3）；以及在人類誘導多能幹細胞（iPSC）衍生的星形膠質細胞中驗證這些機制（目標 4）。 透過繪製 APOE 輸出的典型與非典型路徑，本研究將提供 APOE 運輸的分子藍圖，並揭示 APOE4 如何重塑與神經退化相關的分泌—溶酶體網絡，從而突顯 APOE 處理過程中的新治療靶點。

16105226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16105226.value: 透過促進軸突出芽生長來增強中樞神經系統損傷後的功能恢復

16105226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16105226.value: The limited capacity for axon regeneration in the central nervous system (CNS) of adult mammals often results in permanent functional deficits following injuries such as spinal cord injury (SCI) or stroke. Current therapeutic strategies targeting key signaling molecules, including PTEN and various transcription factors, have shown promise but are hindered by oncogenic risks and insufficient regenerative responses. This proposal aims to explore the role of lipin1, a phosphatidic acid phosphatase, in promoting axon regeneration through its modulation of the mTOR and STAT3 signaling pathways. Our preliminary data indicate that lipin1 knockdown enhances corticospinal tract (CST) sprouting and serotonergic axon regeneration in clinically relevant animal models. We propose to investigate the effects of lipin1 knockdown in adult mice following stroke and contusion spinal cord injuries, focusing on functional recovery and axon sprouting. Using a combination of behavioral assessments, immunostaining, and viral delivery methods, we will assess the regenerative capacity of both CST and serotonergic axons. Our research may reveal critical insights into the mechanisms of axon regeneration and establish lipin1 as a promising target for therapeutic intervention in CNS injuries. Successful outcomes could pave the way for new strategies to enhance recovery and functional restoration in patients. 腦部和脊髓損傷（如中風和脊髓損傷）常常會導致永久性殘疾，這是因為成年人的中樞神經系統受損後，神經纖維自身再生的能力非常有限。現有治療方法雖然顯示出一定潛力，但效果通常較為有限，部分方法可能增加罹癌風險。 本計畫將研究降低一種名為 lipin1 的蛋白質能否促進受損神經纖維再生。我們的初步結果顯示，在動物模型中，降低lipin1的水平能夠促進與運動及其他重要功能相關的神經纖維生長。我們將在成年小鼠的中風和脊髓損傷模型中測試此方法，並利用行為學測試、組織成像和病毒靶向遞送等技術，評估神經纖維的再生情況以及運動和身體功能的改善程度。這項研究將幫助我們了解lipin1如何影響神經修復，並評估其能否成為一個安全有效的治療標靶。最終，這些研究結果可能為腦和脊髓損傷患者帶來新的治療策略，促進功能恢復並改善生活品質。

16200226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16200226.value: 光鏈路陣列之時脈產生與分發技術

16200226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200226.value: The explosive growth in data generated by cutting-edge information technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud computing is driving upgrades to data center interconnects for high-speed, low-power, and low-latency data delivery. Conventional electrical interconnects face bottlenecks in link speed and communication distance due to their limited bandwidth and the high loss inherent to their copper-based medium. In contrast, optical interconnects with low-loss and high-bandwidth fiber as the medium have become the mainstream choice for communication scenarios with bandwidth–distance product exceeding 100 Gb/s·m. Optical link arrays enable multi-terabit-per-second throughputs for AI and high-performance computing workloads via parallel channels implemented in pluggable or co-packaged optics (CPOs). Pluggable transceivers, including digital signal processing-based modules for long reach and high loss compensation and low-power linear pluggable optics for short-reach links, provide multivendor interoperability, flexible I/O routing, and high data rates through multilane architectures. CPOs integrate optics near application-specific integrated circuits, which reduce electrical losses through simpler mechanisms and denser integration, and are gaining traction in AI data centers as packaging technologies mature. Both approaches must overcome critical signal integrity and thermal management challenges in dense, multilane configurations. Clock generation for optical arrays presents a significant bottleneck, requiring precise timing to support high baud rates while minimizing power consumption. Effective clocking must achieve low jitter to maintain low bit error rates amid channel noise and distortion. Clocks are typically produced on-chip using phase-locked loops (PLLs), but they must contend with noise and thermal variations that degrade performance and elevate energy demands. On-chip clock distribution across these links further complicates the design, necessitating minimal lane-to-lane skew to avoid data misalignment between channels. While properly terminated electrical traces allow for uniform propagation over equal distances, driving many terminated lines requires multiple stages of buffers, leading to increased energy overhead in these compact, high-density designs. The proposed project will focus on clock generation and distribution for optical link arrays that meet stringent jitter and power efficiency requirements. Our novel approach utilizing standing-wave-based clock distribution with double-side driving and loss compensation results in a synchronized clock along the distributed line with equalized amplitude. Building on our prior work in high-speed electrical and optical communication ICs, we will incorporate the clock distribution into a PLL, resulting in ultra-low-jitter clock generation and distribution, which is in high demand for both pluggable and co- packaged optical link arrays. The proposed design will be fabricated using 28-nm CMOS technology. 由人工智慧（AI）與雲端運算等尖端資訊技術所引發的資料量爆發性成長，正推動資料中心互連系統升級，以實現高速率、低功耗與低延遲的傳輸。傳統電互連因銅基介質頻寬有限且損耗高，在速率與距離上面臨瓶頸。相較之下，利用低損耗、高頻寬光纖的光互連，已成為頻寬距離積（bandwidth–distance product）超過 100 Gb/s·m 場景的主流選擇。 光鏈路陣列（Optical link arrays）透過可插拔光模組或共封裝光學（CPO）中的平行通道，可為 AI 與高效能運算（HPC）工作負載提供每秒數 Terabit 的吞吐量。可插拔光收發器（包含長距離 DSP 模組與短距離低功耗 LPO）具備多廠商互操作性與高資料速率。CPO 則將光學元件緊密整合至 ASIC 附近，以更低電損耗與高整合度逐漸受到 AI 資料中心青睞。然而，兩者皆須克服高密度多通道配置下的訊號完整性與熱管理挑戰。 光陣列的時脈產生（clock generation）為關鍵瓶頸，需要精確定時以支援高鮑率並降至最低功耗。有效的時脈機制須實現低抖動（low jitter），以在通道雜訊中維持低位元誤碼率（BER）。時脈通常由晶片上鎖相迴路（PLL）產生，但須面對降低效能並增加能耗的雜訊與溫飄。此外，跨鏈路的晶片上時脈分發（clock distribution）需要極小的通道間時脈偏移（lane-to-lane skew），以避免資料對齊失誤。雖然適當終端的電傳輸線有利於均勻傳播，但驅動多級終端線路所需的緩衝器會帶來額外的能源開銷。 基於本團隊在設計高速光與電資料鏈路（如 56 Gb/s PAM-4 VCSEL 驅動器、100 Gbaud 驅動器及 48 Gb/s PAM-4 無電感接收器等）的豐富經驗，我們已奠定堅實的光電介面基礎。在時脈產生方面，我們近五年展示了數款 12 GHz 至 30 GHz、抖動遠低於 70 fs 的前沿低功耗 PLL；在接收端抖動抑制上，我們近年實現了 32 Gb/s 至 60 Gb/s 的低抖動與具抖動韌性技術；在時脈分發上，我們具備在地（local）處理及大型晶片（如 28 GHz 相位陣列發射器）全域（global）分發的設計能力。 本計畫旨在研究光鏈路陣列的時脈產生與分發，以滿足嚴格的抖動與能效要求，開發具可擴充性（scalable）與可升級性（upgradable）的高效方法，滿足日益增長的鏈路速率與吞吐量需求，推進下一代光互連技術發展。

16200326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16200326.value: 具保證之軌跡串流簡化演算法

16200326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200326.value: There are efficient algorithms that process trajectories in important tasks, such as measuring similarity, simplification, clustering, and approximate nearest neighbor search, that offer mathematical guarantees. Almost all such algorithms work exclusively in the offline setting. Due to the widespread use of sensors, a moving object or a time series of multidimensional data can continuously generate a long sequence of data points, which is known as a trajectory stream. Many trajectory streams can be monitored simultaneously. The traditional strategy of sending all vertices in a trajectory stream to a remote server for processing is becoming unattractive because it puts a heavy demand on the communication network and the remote server for subsequent processing. It is beneficial to simplify a trajectory stream on the sensor side so that only a simplified curve of a much smaller size is sent. Simplification is also a basic problem that often appears in trajectory analysis. The trend for analyzing trajectories in the streaming setting will become stronger as data becomes more massive and ubiquitous. It is timely to advance our knowledge on simplifying trajectory streams with provably good guarantees on the solution quality and computational efficiency. 在處理軌跡資料的重要任務中（例如測量相似度、簡化資料、分類群組以及快速搜尋最近鄰居），目前已有許多高效的演算法，且這些演算法都能提供可靠的數學理論支持。然而，幾乎所有這類演算法都只能在「離線」狀態下運作。隨著感測器的廣泛應用，移動的物體或多維度的時間序列資料會源源不絕地產生一連串漫長的數據點，這也就是所謂的「軌跡串流」。目前我們可以同時監控許多條這樣的軌跡串流。過去傳統的做法是將軌跡串流中的所有數據全部傳送到遠端伺服器進行處理，但這種方式對通訊網路和後續負責運算的伺服器都會造成沉重負擔，因此已逐漸過時。更理想的做法是在感測器端就先對軌跡串流進行簡化，這樣一來，就只需要傳送體積小很多的精簡曲線即可。在軌跡分析領域中，「數據簡化」一直是一個核心的基本問題。隨著數據量變得越來越龐大且無所不在，直接在「即時串流」環境下分析軌跡已成為必然的趨勢。因此，現在正是我們深入研究如何簡化軌跡串流的最佳時機，進而提出在處理品質與運算效率上都兼具實證保障的解決方案。

16200526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16200526.value: 凍融作用對非飽和根系土熱-水-力學特性影響的實驗研究

16200526.label: Co - Investigator(s)
16200526.value: Prof Chen, Xunwen Prof Pei, Xiangjun

16200526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200526.value: Post-thawed slope failure has been commonly reported in cold regions of China, Europe, US, and Canada. Existing research has shown that cyclic phase changes in soil pore water due to freezing and thawing results in the formation of periodic ice lenses in shallow soils driven by interfacial tension at the ice–water interface. This phenomenon alters the thermohydromechanical (THM) properties of unsaturated soils and thus affects slope stability. Soil bioengineering using vegetation is a nature-based solution mitigating slope instability problems. However, the effectiveness of applying this solution in cold regions has rarely been evaluated because of the lack of a fundamental understanding of soil–root–water–ice interactions and evolution of the THM properties of unsaturated rooted soils during freezing and thawing. The proposed project will use experimental methods to comprehensively investigate, for the first time, the THM behaviour of unsaturated rooted soils under freeze/thaw cycles and evaluate freeze/thaw-induced changes in root reinforcement. A novel oedometric freeze/thaw chamber will be developed to monitor the in situ evolutions of the microstructure of rooted soils and identify the mechanisms of pore water redistribution during freezing and thawing by X-ray micro-computed tomography. Compacted soils cultivated with cold-tolerant species will be subjected to controlled environmental conditions relevant to a cold region in China. After each freeze/thaw cycle, the unsaturated rooted soils will be tested for (1) shearing properties using a newly-modified suction-controllable simple-shear device; (2) thermal properties (heat capacity and thermal conductivity functions) using a thermal needle probe; and (3) hydraulic properties (soil freezing characteristic curves, water retention curves and hydraulic conductivity functions) using a modified instantaneous profile method. After testing, the root systems of each specimen will be exhumed for measuring the THM properties and vitality of the roots. Any freeze/thaw-induced degradation of the THM properties of unsaturated rooted soils at element scale and effects of suction on such degradation will be investigated, modelled and explained using the pore-scale observation of soil–root–water–ice interaction mechanisms. The newly-developed experimental and analysis tools will enhance our ability to more effectively quantify pore-scale soil–root–water–ice interactions, creating new means to explore the THM behaviour of unsaturated rooted soils upon freeze/thaw cycles, a topic that has rarely been explored internationally. The newly-generated data will shed light on the effectiveness of using vegetation as a nature-based solution for reinforcing shallow soils in cold regions. 在中國、歐洲、北美等寒冷地區，凍融誘發的邊坡失穩屢見報道。已有研究表明，凍融過程中土體孔隙水發生週期性相變，在冰-水界面張力驅動下，淺層土內週期性形成冰棱，由此改變非飽和土的熱-水-力學（THM）特性，進而影響邊坡穩定性。利用植被的土壤生物工程是一種基於自然的邊坡失穩防治方案。然而，由於對土-根-水-冰相互作用以及非飽和根系土在凍融過程中THM性質演化規律缺乏基本認識，該方案在寒冷地區的有效性尚鮮有系統評估。 本項目擬採用實驗手段，首次系統性揭示凍融循環作用下非飽和根系土的THM行為，並評估凍融作用所引起的根系加強效應變化。項目將自行研發側限固結凍融實驗裝置，結合X射線CT斷層掃描技術，原位監測根系土微觀結構演化，並辨識凍融過程中孔隙水重分佈機制。項目將耐寒植物種植於壓實土中，在模擬我國寒冷地區實際環境條件的受控環境下培養。每次凍融循環後，分別測定非飽和根系土的下列性質：（1）採用改良的吸力可控單剪儀測定剪切特性；（2）採用熱針法測定熱特性（熱容和導熱係數函數）；（3）採用改良的瞬態剖面法測定水力特性（土壤凍結特性曲線、持水曲線和滲透係數）。實驗結束後取出根系，測定根係自身的THM性質及根系活力。基於孔隙尺度土-根-水-冰相互作用機制的觀測，對單元尺度凍融所致的根系土THM性質退化規律及吸力對其的影響進行系統研究、建模與闡釋。 所研發的新型實驗與分析工具將提升對孔隙尺度土-根-水-冰相互作用進行有效量化的能力，為探索國際上鮮有涉及的非飽和根系土凍融THM行為提供新手段。所獲得的實驗數據將揭示採用植被作為基於自然的解決方案來加強寒冷地區淺層土體的有效性。

16200826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16200826.value: 包含外連接的無環查詢的最佳最壞情況高效處理

16200826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200826.value: Databases power everything from online shopping to social media, allowing us to ask questions—or "queries"—to extract useful information from vast amounts of data. A common operation in these queries is "joining" tables, which combines related records, like matching customer orders with product details. However, standard joins, known as "inner joins" ignore records that don't match perfectly, leading to incomplete results. That's where "outer joins" come in: they include those non-matching records, filling in gaps with nulls. Surprisingly, over 80% of real-world database queries use outer joins, for reasons like generating full reports, data cleaning, integration, or simply ensuring nothing is missed. Despite their prevalence, outer joins lack strong theoretical foundations and efficient processing methods compared to inner joins. This grant proposal aims to bridge that gap by developing new theories and algorithms to make these queries faster and more reliable. We focus on addressing the following three key questions. (1) Fast processing for acyclic queries: For acyclic queries (those without loops in their structure), we extend existing linear-time techniques to handle queries with mixed inner and outer joins, as well as aggregations like summing revenues. (2) Handling cyclic queries: For more complex cyclic queries that require more time, we will design worst-case optimal algorithms, building on bounds for output sizes and advanced decompositions. (3) Real-world integration: We'll implement these ideas in open-source systems like DuckDB and SparkSQL, testing them on benchmarks to optimize practical SQL queries. 數據庫驅動著從線上購物到社交媒體的各種應用，使我們能夠發起詢問（即「查詢」），從海量數據中提取有價值的資訊。這些查詢中的一個常見操作是「連接」（join）資料表——它能夠將相關的記錄組合在一起，例如將客戶訂單與產品詳情進行比對。然而，被稱為「內連接」（inner joins）的標準連接方式會忽略未能完全比對的記錄，導致結果不夠完整。這正是「外連接」（outer joins）發揮作用之處：它們能夠包含那些未比對的記錄，並用空值（nulls）來填補空白。令人驚訝的是，在真實世界的數據庫查詢中，超過 80% 都會用到外連接，其原因包括生成完整報告、數據清洗、數據整合，或者單純是為了確保沒有任何數據遺漏。 儘管外連接被廣泛使用，但與內連接相比，它缺乏堅實的理論基礎和高效的處理方法。本資助計劃旨在透過開發新的理論和演算法來彌補這一空白，從而使這類查詢變得更快、更可靠。我們將重點解決以下三個核心問題： 1. 無環查詢的高效處理：針對無環查詢（即結構中不包含環路的查詢），我們將擴展現有的線性時間技術，以處理混合了內連接與外連接的查詢，以及諸如計算總營收等聚合操作。2. 處理有環查詢：針對需要更多計算時間的複雜有環查詢，我們將基於輸出大小的界限和先進的分解技術，設計出最壞情況下的最佳演算法（worst-case optimal algorithms）。3. 真實世界中的整合應用：我們將在 DuckDB 和 SparkSQL 等開源系統中實現這些構想，並在基準測試中對其進行驗證，以最佳化實際應用中的 SQL 查詢。

16201026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16201026.value: 二維 MoS₂ 奈米帶電晶體之尺寸縮減效應與緊湊模型研究

16201026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16201026.value: This project investigates the fundamental scaling effects in MoS₂ nanoribbon transistors, with a particular emphasis on how atomic-scale features—such as crystallographic orientation and edge termination—influence electronic transport and overall device performance. As transistor dimensions shrink to just a few atomic layers, conventional bulk properties no longer dominate behavior. Instead, edge chemistry, ribbon geometry, and directional anisotropy become critical factors affecting carrier mobility, threshold voltage, subthreshold swing, and contact resistance. The objective of this research is to systematically analyze these small-dimension effects and develop a physics-based compact model that accurately captures their impact for use in circuit-level design. To achieve this, the project integrates quantum mechanical simulations, experimental fabrication, and compact modeling. Ab initio methods, including density functional theory (DFT) and non-equilibrium Green’s function (NEGF), will be employed to study how different ribbon orientations and edge terminations modulate band structure, density of states, and transmission characteristics. These theoretical insights will be validated through the fabrication of MoS₂ nanoribbon transistors using focused electron beam-induced etching (FEBIE), a technique that enables precise control over ribbon width and edge quality. Experimental characterization will provide critical data to refine simulation parameters and ensure model accuracy. A key deliverable of the project is the development of a modular compact model implemented in Verilog-A, compatible with standard circuit simulators. This model will incorporate quantum confinement, edge-induced bandgap modulation, and orientation-dependent transport, enabling predictive design of 2D material-based electronic systems. Beyond modeling, the project will explore novel transistor architectures—such as edge-engineered and orientation-sensitive designs—that leverage the unique properties of MoS₂ nanoribbons. These concepts will be evaluated for feasibility and performance through both simulation and prototype fabrication. Unlike many studies that focus on isolated device demonstrations, this project emphasizes in-depth analysis and knowledge integration. By capturing and synthesizing a wide range of reported findings, the research aims to establish a comprehensive framework that supports long-term innovation in 2D nanoelectronics. The outcomes will contribute to the advancement of ultra-scaled, energy-efficient, and flexible electronic technologies, offering a viable path forward as silicon-based devices reach their physical limits. 本研究計劃旨在探討 MoS₂ 奈米帶電晶體的尺寸縮減效應，重點研究晶體方位、邊緣終止型態等原子尺度結構特徵如何影響電子傳輸機制及整體元件性能。當電晶體尺寸縮減至數個原子層尺度時，傳統體材料特性已不再主導元件行為；取而代之的是邊緣化學特性、奈米帶幾何結構以及晶向異向性等因素，對載子遷移率、臨界電壓、次臨界擺幅及接觸電阻等關鍵電性產生決定性影響。本計劃的目標是系統性分析這些小尺寸效應，並建立一套具備物理基礎的緊湊模型，以準確描述其對元件特性的影響，供電路層級設計與模擬使用。 為達成上述目標，本研究將結合理論模擬、實驗製作及緊湊模型開發。研究將利用第一原理計算方法，包括密度泛函理論（Density Functional Theory, DFT）及非平衡格林函數法（Non-Equilibrium Green's Function, NEGF），探討不同奈米帶晶向與邊緣終止結構對能帶結構、態密度以及傳輸特性的影響機制。理論分析結果將透過聚焦電子束誘導蝕刻（Focused Electron Beam-Induced Etching, FEBIE）技術所製備之 MoS₂ 奈米帶電晶體進行驗證。該製程能精確控制奈米帶寬度與邊緣品質，有助於建立結構與電性之間的直接關聯。實驗量測所得結果將進一步用於校準模擬參數並驗證模型準確性。 本計劃的重要成果之一為建立一套以 Verilog-A 實現的模組化緊湊模型，並可直接相容於標準電路模擬器。該模型將納入量子侷限效應、邊緣誘發能隙調變以及晶向依賴載子傳輸等物理機制，使其能夠準確預測二維材料電子元件於電路層級的行為。此外，本研究亦將探索新型電晶體架構，例如邊緣工程化（edge-engineered）及晶向敏感（orientation-sensitive）設計，以充分發揮 MoS₂ 奈米帶獨特的電子特性。相關架構將透過模擬分析及原型元件製作進行可行性與性能評估。 有別於許多僅著重於單一元件展示的研究工作，本計劃強調深入的物理分析與知識整合。透過系統性整理與統合相關研究成果，本研究將建立一個完整的分析框架，以支持二維奈米電子元件的長期發展與創新。研究成果將有助於推動超微縮、高能效及柔性電子技術的發展，並在傳統矽基元件逐漸接近物理極限的背景下，為下一世代電子系統提供可行的發展方向。

16201826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16201826.value: 近乎無緩衝網路層之傳輸中包控制：超可靠低延遲視訊通訊

16201826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16201826.value: To enable the future immersive applications such as virtual reality (VR) and cloud gaming, ultra-reliable low-latency video communication is critical. Current systems prioritize control signals and sparse sensor data at minimal data rates, which cannot support high-bandwidth applications such as live video feeds, real-time passenger analytics, or synchronized sensor streams. These applications demand end-to-end latency below 100 ms to ensure seamless safety and responsiveness. While recent advancements – including edge computing, 5G/WiFi-7 networks, and protocol optimizations – have reduced network latency, integrated systems still exceed the 100 ms threshold at the 99th percentile due to transient bufferbloat during network fluctuations. The main reason is the network change – when the change happens, the amount of in-flight packets cannot immediately converge to the new network conditions, where the excess packets become the bufferbloats that increase the latency. This latency spike arises from a critical gap: the lack of proactive coordination between in-network routers and video senders. Existing passive backpressure mechanisms fail to adapt swiftly to dynamic network conditions, causing packet overflows and delayed sender responses that compound latency during round-trip time (RTT) intervals. For example, when network fluctuates, it takes at least a RTT for the sender to react to the network changes, during when the stall has already happened. This proposal addresses the transient bufferbloat at its root by introducing a near-bufferless network layer design. We target two key contributors to latency: (1) the time during the sender’s reaction to network changes, and (2) the time during the congestion information arrives at the sender. Our approach integrates three innovations: adaptive smooth queue management to stabilize buffer occupancy during congestion, proactive jammed packet clearance to eliminate stalled data during network transitions, and timely packet duplication from the sender to ensure uninterrupted data flow. By synchronizing router and sender actions at the network layer, our solution dynamically aligns packet rates with fluctuating bandwidth, preventing buffer buildup and ensuring sub-100 ms latency even at the 99.9th percentile. The outcome of this proposal will enable ultra-low latency video communications, which will improve users' experiences and safety in many applications such as VR and AR. 為了支援虛擬實境（VR）和雲端遊戲等未來沉浸式應用，超可靠、低延遲的視訊通訊至關重要。目前的系統主要以最低資料速率優先傳輸控制訊號和稀疏的感測器資料，無法支援即時視訊串流、即時乘客分析或同步感測器資料流等高頻寬應用。這些應用要求端到端延遲低於 100 毫秒，才能確保流暢的操作、安全性與即時反應能力。儘管邊緣運算、5G／Wi-Fi 7 網路及通訊協定最佳化等近期技術進展已降低網路延遲，整合式系統在網路波動期間仍會因暫態緩衝區膨脹（bufferbloat），導致第 99 百分位延遲超過 100 毫秒的門檻。 主要原因在於網路狀況的變化：當網路發生變化時，傳輸中的封包數量無法立即收斂至符合新的網路條件，多餘的封包因而形成緩衝區膨脹並增加延遲。這種延遲突增源自一項關鍵缺口：網路內路由器與視訊傳送端之間缺乏主動協調。現有的被動式反壓機制無法迅速適應動態網路條件，造成封包溢出及傳送端反應延遲，並在往返時間（RTT）內進一步加劇延遲。例如，當網路發生波動時，傳送端至少需要一個 RTT 才能對網路變化作出反應，而此時資料停滯早已發生。 本提案透過引入近乎無緩衝區的網路層設計，從根本上解決暫態緩衝區膨脹問題。我們針對兩項造成延遲的主要因素：（1）傳送端對網路變化作出反應所需的時間；以及（2）壅塞資訊抵達傳送端所需的時間。我們的方法整合三項創新技術：採用自適應平滑佇列管理，在壅塞期間穩定緩衝區占用量；主動清除阻塞封包，以消除網路狀態轉換期間停滯的資料；以及由傳送端及時複製封包，以確保資料流不中斷。透過在網路層同步協調路由器與傳送端的動作，我們的解決方案能根據頻寬波動動態調整封包傳輸速率，防止緩衝區累積，並確保即使在第 99.9 百分位，延遲仍低於 100 毫秒。本提案的成果將實現超低延遲視訊通訊，進而改善使用者在 VR、AR 等眾多應用中的體驗與安全性。

16202126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16202126.value: 推進相變合金相容性理論，邁向百萬周次可逆性

16202126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16202126.value: Materials with strong first-order phase transformations have great potential for emerging applications in medical devices, actuation and solid-state refrigeration. The lack of phase reversibility for these materials is a persistent obstacle. Under repeated stress-induced phase transformations, the superelastic strain decreases with accumulation of plastic deformation and gradual loss of functionality. A mathematical design principle by compatibility theory [Song et al., Nature (2013)], later confirmed in [Chluba et al., Science (2015)], enabled the discovery of alloys with low hysteresis and improved reversibility. This approach identified compatibility metrics and demonstrated their role in suppressing functional fatigue, exemplified by CuAuZn alloys retaining 6% superelastic strains for 100,000 cycles. Despite these advances, discoveries of new alloys with high reversibility remain scarce. Relying on precise lattice parameter tuning, the development is time consuming and experimentally demanding, even with high-throughput facilities. Small compositional variations rapidly increase thermal hysteresis, but their impact on mechanical reversibility remains unclear. Our observations suggest a new opportunity: alloys near compatible compositions may still achieve enhanced stress-induced reversibility, even when thermal hysteresis is elevated. This opens a broader design space beyond strict satisfaction of cofactor conditions. Moreover, applications such as medical implants rely primarily on superelasticity, making mechanical reversibility under million-level cycling critically important. Under repeated loading, dislocation activity, precipitates and grain boundary effects strongly influence fatigue resistance, yet no unified framework connects these microstructural mechanisms with crystallographic compatibility. In this project, we will establish a mechanics based framework to advance the basic understanding of reversibility in phase transforming alloys. We propose to extend compatibility theory incorporating non-transforming defects, and generalize guidelines for alloy development. The orientation-dependent fatigue resistance will be studied using nanomechanical experiments testing micropillars with optimized grain orientations and bi-crystal pillars with compatible grain boundary. In addition, we will investigate dissipative mechanisms of stress-induced transformations in micropillars and will associate the slip events with loading curves toward million cycles. Finally, we will address a long-standing theoretical question: how closely must compatibility metrics be satisfied to ensure practical reversibility? To demonstrate this framework, we will revisit the classic shape memory alloy family NiTi–X (X = Cu, Co, Ta) with many works published on thermomechanical properties, but not systematically benchmarked under micro/nanomechanical tests, particularly at miniature sizes. With modern experimental tools, we will show how tailored grain boundary properties enhance reversibility and fatigue resistance toward million cycle performance even under moderate compatibility without fine tuning of compositions. 具強一階相變的材料在醫療器械、致動與固態製冷等領域極具應用潛力，惟其可逆性不足始終是主要瓶頸：反覆的應力誘導相變會累積塑性變形，令超彈性應變衰減、功能逐漸喪失。基於相容性理論的設計原則 [Song et al., Nature (2013); Chluba et al., Science (2015)] 曾成功指導低遲滯、高可逆性合金的開發，例如 CuAuZn 合金經十萬次循環仍保持 6% 超彈性應變。 然而，此類新合金至今仍屬罕見。其開發依賴晶格參數的精確調控，即使有高通量設施亦相當耗時；成分的微小偏差便會顯著增大熱遲滯，但對力學可逆性的影響卻未有定論。我們的初步觀察顯示，成分接近相容條件的合金，即使熱遲滯偏高，仍可能具備良好的應力誘導可逆性——這意味着設計空間遠比嚴格滿足輔因子條件（cofactor conditions）更為廣闊。對於醫療植入物等以超彈性為主的應用，百萬次循環下的力學可逆性尤為關鍵，而位錯、析出相與晶界等微觀機制如何與晶體學相容性相互作用，目前尚無統一框架可循。 本計劃旨在建立一個基於力學的理論框架，深化對相變合金可逆性的認識。具體工作包括：(一) 擴展相容性理論以納入非相變缺陷，提出更普適的合金設計準則；(二) 以納米力學實驗研究疲勞抗力的取向依賴性，測試優化取向的單晶微柱及具相容晶界的雙晶微柱；(三) 探究應力誘導相變的耗散機制，將滑移事件與加載曲線關聯分析至百萬次循環；(四) 解答一個懸而未決的理論問題——相容性指標須滿足到何種程度，方足以保證實際可逆性。我們將以經典的 NiTi–X（X = Cu、Co、Ta）形狀記憶合金為驗證體系：其熱力學性能雖有大量文獻，卻缺乏系統的微納力學基準測試。藉助現代實驗手段，我們將證明透過調控晶界特性，即使成分僅屬中等相容、無需精細調配，亦可實現百萬次循環級的可逆性與抗疲勞性能。

16203226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16203226.value: 人工智能與物理協同驅動之颱風風暴潮概率預報系統：強度校正，高效採樣及空間可解釋同化

16203226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
16203226.value: Prof Xi, Dazhi Prof ZHU, Xujia

16203226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203226.value: Typhoon-induced storm surges are among the world’s most devastating coastal hazards. With climate change and rapid coastal development, even historically rare surge events are becoming more frequent and severe. To protect lives and infrastructure, decision-makers need more accurate and timely storm surge forecasts, ideally that also quantify uncertainty for better emergency response, land-use planning, and insurance risk profiling. Yet, current forecasting methods face critical limitations. Typhoon-wise, the AI-driven weather foundation models excel in speed but often struggle to capture extreme typhoon intensity evolution. For storm surge, high-fidelity hydrodynamic simulators (e.g. ADCIRC) accurately resolve surge dynamics but are too slow to run for the dozens of typhoon scenarios needed in real time for forecasting. Additional, Hong Kong’s tidal gauge network is limited, making data assimilation (linking simulation to reality) challenging with such sparse data. In this project, we tackle those technical gaps. First, we will enhance the latest AI-based weather foundation models to better capture extreme typhoon intensity. We will plug in a novel two-stage correction to quality-control the AI-predicted wind fields driving our surge model. Second, we develop a hybrid data and physics co-driven workflow for storm surge forecasting. Our solution is based on a Neural Field-based deep-learning surrogate trained on an extensive library of simulated storms and adapted for the incoming storm. To maintain accuracy on the interested ensemble of incoming storms, we employ a novel “anchor” strategy: for each forecast, a small selection of ensemble members are still simulated with the full physics model, and their results are used to calibrate and update the surrogate in real-time. This ensures the predictions never drift far. Third, we introduce an innovative data assimilation scheme using Non-Negative Matrix Factorization (NMF) to continuously correct and refine surge forecasts with sparse real-time tidal gauge data. Our NMF distills the surge field into a few dominant spatial patterns learned from simulations. As a storm unfolds, any new gauge readings are translated into adjustments of those basis patterns, effectively spreading point observations into a full-region correction, finally allowing on-the-fly forecast updates that stay consistent with observations. Ultimately, bringing these components together, the project will deliver an operational probabilistic storm surge forecasting system that significantly upgrade to Hong Kong’s coastal resilience for emergency managers, engineers and urban planners. 颱風引致的風暴潮是全球最具破壞力的海岸災害之一。隨着氣候變化與沿海地區的急速發展，即使是歷史上罕見的風暴潮事件，其發生頻率與嚴重程度亦不斷上升。為保障生命財產與基礎設施安全，決策者需要更準確、更及時的風暴潮預報，並且最好能同時量化不確定性，以支援應急響應、土地用途規劃及保險風險評估。然而，現行預報方法仍面對關鍵局限。在颱風方面，人工智能驅動的氣象基礎模型雖然運算速度極快，卻往往難以刻劃極端颱風強度的演變過程。在風暴潮方面，高保真度的水動力數值模擬器雖能準確解析風暴潮動力過程，但運算過於緩慢，無法在實時預報所需的數十個颱風情景下逐一運行。此外，香港的潮汐測站網絡覆蓋有限，在稀疏的觀測條件下進行資料同化極具挑戰。 本項目針對上述技術缺口展開研究。第一，我們將改良最新的人工智能氣象基礎模型，使其更佳地捕捉極端颱風強度，並嵌入一套創新的兩階段校正方法，對驅動風暴潮模型的 AI 預測風場進行質量控制。第二，我們建立一套資料與物理協同驅動的混合式風暴潮預報流程：該方案以神經場為基礎的深度學習代理模型為核心，先在大規模模擬風暴資料庫上訓練，再針對來襲風暴進行自適應調整。為確保對來襲風暴集合預報的準確度，我們提出創新的錨定策略。每次預報時，仍以完整物理模型模擬少數集合成員，並利用其結果對代理模型進行實時校準與更新，從而確保預測結果不會出現顯著偏移。第三，我們引入一套創新的資料同化方案，運用非負矩陣分解，以稀疏的實時潮汐測站數據持續修正並精化風暴潮預報。可將風暴潮場提煉為若干由模擬資料學習所得的主導空間模態；當風暴持續發展時，任何新增的測站觀測值均可轉化為對這些基底模態的調整，從而把單點觀測有效擴散為全區域的修正，最終實現與觀測保持一致的即時預報更新。 綜合上述各項組件，本項目將交付一套可業務化運行的概率式風暴潮預報系統，為應急管理人員、工程師及城市規劃者提供有力支援，顯著提升香港的海岸韌性。

16203326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16203326.value: 可靠且泛化的无线射频感知系统与应用

16203326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203326.value: Device-free wireless sensing leverages variations in radio signal induced by human motion and environmental changes to infer dynamic physical phenomena such as localization, activity recognition, vital signs, etc. Despite significant academic developments, practical adoption remains limited due to three unaddressed challenges: (1) spatiotemporal fading that causes blind spots and unreliable sensing, (2) poor generalizability across people and environment, and (3) the lack of unified multi-task capability. This project aims to develop a reliable, generalizable, and unified wireless sensing framework that bridges such a gap. The proposed research integrates three synergistic tasks: (1) improving signal reliability through active signal enhancement for robust sensing, (2) developing a physics-informed sensing paradigm for generalizable wireless sensing, and (3) enabling multi-modal, multi-task sensing capability through a unified sensing system design. The project will use elderly care as a vehicle to experimentally study the performance of the proposed framework. The project builds on the PI’s extensive experiences in wireless and mobile sensing research. The project is expected to deliver a reliable and generalizable sensing framework that supports practical application in healthcare and everyday intelligent environment. 无设备无线感知利用由人体运动和环境变化引起的无线电信号变化，来推断诸如定位、活动识别、体征监测等动态物理现象。尽管学术界取得了显著进展，但由于如下三个尚未解决的挑战，其实际应用仍然受限： (1) 无线射频信号的时空衰落易引发不可靠的感知盲区； (2) 跨人员、设备与环境的泛化能力较差； (3) 缺乏统一的多任务能力。 本项目旨在开发一个可靠、可泛化且统一的无线感知框架，以填补这些研究差距。拟进行的研究集成了三个协同任务：(1) 通过主动信号增强提高信号可靠性，实现稳健感知；(2) 开发物理启发的感知方式，实现可泛化的无线感知；(3) 通过统一的感知系统设计，实现多模态、多任务的感知能力。本项目将以健康护理为载体，对所提框架的性能进行实验研究。

16203926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16203926.value: 朝向穩健的鐵路缺陷監測：具備分佈外檢測能力的持續學習框架

16203926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203926.value: Rail surface defects are a leading cause of derailments, posing significant risks to public safety and infrastructure integrity. While Machine Vision-based Inspection Systems (MVIS) offer automation potential, their real-world deployment is hindered by dynamic operational environments. While innovative approaches have been developed to mitigate performance degradation from "domain shifts" (e.g., changes in rail type, weather, or imaging hardware), they fail to address a critical challenge: the emergence of novel, unseen defect types over time, known as Out-of-Distribution (OOD) data. Compounded by the high cost of data labelling, complex visual scenarios and the multi-label nature of the problem, this limits the long-term adaptability of current AI systems. This project aims to overcome these limitations by developing a novel, self-improving AI framework for robust rail defect monitoring. Our core innovation is a comprehensive continual learning system that integrates four key novel components: • Confidence-Free, Energy-Based OOD Detector: We will develop a novel OOD detection module that identifies novel defects. This unsupervised method requires only in-distribution data for training, making it suitable for real-world applications. • Domain-Invariant Feature Extractor: We will design and implement a robust backbone network to learn generalized feature representations resilient to domain shifts. This involves leveraging advanced Domain Generalization techniques to ensure consistent performance across diverse and unseen operational environments. • Diagnostic Latent Attention Classifier (LAC): We will build a novel multi-label classifier that not only accurately categorizes known defects but also functions as a self-diagnostic module. Its integrated latent attention mechanism will work synergistically with the OOD detector to facilitate anomaly detection and low-confidence flagging. • Dynamic Continual Learning Mechanism: We will create a human-in-the-loop system that enables the framework to learn continuously from new data without forgetting previously acquired knowledge. This is the core engine for long-term model adaptation and improvement. To rigorously trained and validated the proposed framework, we will establish a comprehensive, multi-source dataset of by collecting and labelling real rail images covering diverse rail types, environmental conditions, and temporal periods. A dedicated web-based application will be developed to facilitate the implementation of the framework for real-world monitoring. The successful execution of this research will deliver a deployable software tool that enables railway operators to move from manual, periodic inspections to automated, continuous monitoring. The developed AI technology is also readily adaptable for inspecting other critical infrastructures, such as bridges, and pipelines, creating a broader societal impact. 鐵路表面缺陷是導致出軌事故的主要原因之一，對公共安全與基礎設施完整性構成重大風險。雖然基於機器視覺的檢測系統（MVIS）具備自動化潛力，但其在現實世界中的部署卻受到動態操作環境的阻礙。儘管已有創新方法被開發出來以緩解「領域轉移」（例如鐵路類型、天氣或成像硬體的變化）所導致的性能下降，但這些方法未能應對一項關鍵挑戰：隨著時間推移，新型且未曾見過的缺陷類型的出現，即所謂的「分佈外」（OOD）數據。再加上數據標註成本高昂、視覺場景複雜以及問題本身的多標籤性質，這些因素限制了當前人工智慧系統的長期適應能力。 本計畫旨在通過開發一種新穎且具備自我改進能力的人工智慧框架，以實現穩健的鐵路缺陷監測，從而克服上述限制。我們的核心創新在於一個全面的持續學習系統，該系統整合了四個關鍵的新組成部分： • 無需置信度、基於能量的分佈外檢測器：我們將開發一個新穎的分佈外檢測模組，用於識別新型缺陷。此非監督式方法僅需分佈內數據進行訓練，因此適合現實世界的應用。 • 領域不變特徵提取器：我們將設計並實現一個穩健的主幹網路，以學習能抵抗領域轉移的泛化特徵表示。這將涉及利用先進的領域泛化技術，以確保在各種未見過的操作環境中保持一致的性能。 • 診斷性潛在注意力分類器（LAC）：我們將構建一個新穎的多標籤分類器，該分類器不僅能準確分類已知缺陷，還能作為自我診斷模組。其整合的潛在注意力機制將與分佈外檢測器協同運作，以促進異常檢測和低置信度標記。 • 動態持續學習機制：我們將創建一個「人機協作」（Human-in-the-loop）系統，使該框架能夠持續從新數據中學習，而不會遺忘先前獲得的知識。這是實現模型長期適應與改進的核心引擎。 為了對所提出的框架進行嚴格的訓練與驗證，我們將通過收集和標註涵蓋不同鐵路類型、環境條件和時間段的真實鐵路圖像，建立一個全面且多源的數據集。此外，還將開發一個專用的網頁應用程式，以促進該框架在實際監測中的實施。 本研究的成功執行將提供一個可部署的軟體工具，使鐵路運營商能夠從手動、週期性的檢測轉向自動化、連續性的監測。所開發的人工智慧技術際亦可輕鬆調整應用於其他關鍵基礎設施的檢測，例如橋樑和管道，從而產生更廣泛的社會影響。

16204126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16204126.value: 利用電磁自由度概念提升無線通訊系統的效能

16204126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204126.value: An ongoing challenge in wireless communication is how to meet the relentless growth in wireless communication demand. For example, wireless communication traffic is expected to double between 2025 and 2030 (Ericsson Mobility Report, June 2025) and there are also plans for advanced new services. To meet these demands, new technologies need to be developed and harnessed. One area that has received renewed attention is the harnessing of electromagnetic structures to enhance wireless communications. Examples include, fluid antenna systems, moveable antennas, extremely large MIMO, holographic MIMO and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces. On the other hand there have been breakthroughs in our understanding of the electromagnetic degree-of-freedom (DoF) concept. DoF analysis provides us with fundamental bounds on size, feed ports and bandwidth tradeoffs in electromagnetic structures and therefore provides targets for the performance possible in wireless communications. However there remain significant challenges in utilizing the DoF concept and reaching the targets DoF predict in wireless communication systems. In this research proposal the goal is to harness the electromagnetic DoF concept to develop systematic approaches to the design of electromagnetic structures that can reach the DoF target bounds and enhance wireless communications. While much work on the analysis and estimation of DoF targets has been performed, designs and methods that can achieve those targets are much less investigated. A key effort will therefore be to develop techniques to link the DoF concept to the design of implementable electromagnetic structures. Particular tradeoffs to be investigated are between their size, feed ports and bandwidth and whether these structures have useful advantages. These designs and tradeoffs will be used to provide performance enhancements to wireless communication systems that harness the proposed electromagnetic structures. Particular areas of focus will be fluid antenna systems and reconfigurable antennas for wireless communications. Prototypes of the proposed structures will also be developed to verify the findings and performance bounds. The importance of the research proposed lies in its application to wireless communication and its use in future systems. In the development of future 6G wireless communication new electromagnetic structures are being proposed. As such the design of implementable electromagnetic structures that can reach the predicted DoF bounds will be critical and can have significant impact. If the developments proposed prove practical and meet their potential, the approaches could become utilized in millions of wireless communication base and mobile stations. Therefore, there could be significant opportunities for technology transfer and impact beyond academia. 無線通訊領域持續面臨的挑戰是如何滿足不斷增長的無線通訊需求。例如，無線通訊流量預計將在2025年至2030年間翻倍（愛立信行動報告，2025年6月），並且還有計劃推出先進的新服務。為了滿足這些需求，我們需要開發和利用新技術。其中一個重新被受到關注的領域是利用電磁結構來增強無線通訊。例如，流體天線系統、可移動天線、超大規模MIMO、全像MIMO和可重構智慧表面。另一方面，我們對電磁自由度（DoF）概念的理解也取得了突破性進展。 DoF分析為我們提供了電磁結構中尺寸、饋電端口和頻寬權衡的基本界限，從而為無線通訊的性能目標提供了基礎。然而，在無線通訊系統中應用DoF概念並達到DoF預測的目標仍存在重大挑戰。 本研究提案旨在利用電磁自由度（DoF）概念，開發系統化的電磁結構設計方法，以達到DoF目標範圍並增強無線通訊性能。雖然對DoF目標的分析和估計已進行了大量工作，但能夠實現這些目標的設計和方法的研究卻相對較少。因此，一項關鍵工作是開發將DoF概念與可實現的電磁結構設計相結合的技術。需要研究的具體權衡因素包括結構的尺寸、饋電端口和頻寬，以及這些結構是否具有實際優勢。這些設計和權衡因素將用於提升所提出的電磁結構的無線通訊系統性能。研究重點領域將是用於無線通訊的流體天線系統和可重構天線。我們還將開發所提出結構的樣機，以驗證研究結果和性能範圍。 本研究的重要性在於無線通訊領域的應用以及在未來系統中的應用。在未來6G無線通訊的發展中，新型電磁結構正在被提出。因此，設計能夠達到預期自由度範圍的可實現電磁結構至關重要，並可能產生重大影響。如果所提出的方案被證明是實用且能發揮其潛力，這些方法可望應用於數百萬個無線通訊基地台和行動站。因此，技術轉移和影響範圍將擴大到學術界之外，以及存在巨大的機會。

16204926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16204926.value: 基于模型上下文协议生态的大模型智能体精度和效率优化

16204926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204926.value: The integration of Large Language Model (LLM) agents with external tools is propelling LLMs to large-scale, real-world agentic AI applications. Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides a standardized interface akin to “USB-C for the LLM agent world”, greatly facilitating the integration of LLM agents with external tools. We have seen explosive growth in the use of MCP servers, which forms a vast ecosystem consisting of massive number dynamically changing tools. This expands LLM capability while also posing critical challenges in tool selection and system performance optimization. To characterize and optimize the LLM performance with tool usage, existing work has considered small-scale static tool benchmark and selection. In large-scale dynamic MCP environment, however, several critical questions remain underexplored: (1) what are the critical factors that influence selection accuracy when agents execute MCP tool calls? (2) how can an LLM agent identify the most suitable set of tools from a potentially large number of dynamically changing tools placed across different MCP servers? (3) in complex MCP task chains involving multi-step, multi-tool calls, how to minimize the task end-to-end (E2E) latency? This project aims to systematically investigate and optimize the performance of LLM agents within large-scale dynamic MCP environment. We plan to start with empirical analysis to characterize the intrinsic behavior in agent tool calls. We will design and develop techniques for optimizing tool selection accuracy and minimizing task execution latency. To achieve our objectives, this project will proceed as follows: (1) We will conduct large-scale empirical study to capture the behavior of LLM agents in dynamic MCP environment, to understand the accuracy and fine-grained system performance bottlenecks of LLM agents during large-scale MCP tool calls. (2) We will design a feedback-driven hierarchical tool retrieval framework to optimize the selection precision of LLM agents among the vast, dynamically changing tools to satisfy user requests. (3) We will build an intelligent proxy layer to support tool caching and parallel scheduling to minimize the task execution time in complex agent task chains involving multi-step tool calls. We will incorporate these optimization techniques into an efficient, flexible, and user-friendly LLM agent MCP system to enhance its performance in the large-scale dynamic MCP ecosystem. To showcase the effectiveness and practicality of our proposed optimization methods, we will make our framework and evaluation scripts open source, supporting efforts within the scientific community to develop new LLM agents and interactions via the MCP protocol.

16205026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16205026.value: 質子交換膜燃料電池三相界面與質子、電子及質量傳輸同步最大化的研究

16205026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205026.value: The large-scale deployment of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) is constrained by the high cost of platinum catalysts and severe performance losses when platinum loading is reduced, primarily due to small triple-phase boundaries (TPBs) and insufficient transport to the active sites, where protons, electrons and mass converge. The main challenges arise from both intrinsic and extrinsic trade-offs. Intrinsically, a sufficient amount of ionomer is necessary to establish TPBs and facilitate proton transport. However, local excess of ionomers may increase mass transport resistance due to strong interfacial adsorption and bulk agglomeration. Extrinsically, pursuing a thinner catalyst layer can shorten transport distances, thereby enhancing bulk transport in electrodes. However, this also intensifies volumetric water generation, significantly increasing the risk of severe water flooding.
