To break these trade-offs and obtain high-performing PEMFCs, it is essential to reconstruct the transport pathways of both TPB microstructure and electrode macrostructure, thus simultaneously maximizing TPBs and coupled transport by multiscale optimization. In this proposed project, we will develop novel interconnected macroporous channels in the ultrathin catalyst layer, integrating an open mesoporous carbon support with a thin interface capable of transporting protons and mass. Specifically, we will 1) design an open mesoporous carbon support with in-situ grown proton-conducting covalent organic frameworks under ultralow platinum loadings, 2) fabricate interconnected macroporous channels for improved two-phase transport in ultrathin catalyst layers, 3) optimize multiscale electrode structures from the molecular interface to macroporous water channels by machine learning, and 4) demonstrate high-performing PEMFCs with reduced Pt loading and enhanced durability by simultaneously maximizing TPBs and transport. The design and optimization of TPB microstructure and electrode macrostructure will be accomplished through multiscale modeling with machine learning surrogate models and optimization algorithms to capture key coupling effects and overcome the computational limitations. The results will provide fundamental insights into not only construction and distribution of TPBs but also coupled two-phase transport phenomena across microscopic and macroscopic scales. Thus, our project will provide a bottom-up strategy for electrode design and deliver high-performing PEMFCs with reduced affordable platinum loading and improved durability. This research will help advance hydrogen fuel cell technologies in low-carbon transportation and the emerging low-altitude economy, directly supporting Hong Kong’s path to net-zero emission while strengthening its innovative role in air mobility.

16205526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16205526.value: 面向邊緣設備的高效、自適應與可擴展視覺生成模型

16205526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205526.value: On-device visual content generation, such as creating social media avatars or editing videos instantly on a smartphone without a cloud connection, represents a key frontier in user experience innovation. This transition from cloud-based processing to edge deployment offers significant advantages in latency, cost efficiency, and data privacy. However, state-of-the-art visual generative models (VGMs), particularly those based on diffusion processes, remain computationally prohibitive for resource-constrained edge environments due to their substantial model size, slow inference speed and limited adaptive learning ability. Three fundamental scalability challenges impede effective edge deployment of VGMs. First, the massive size of foundation models prohibits direct deployment and requires compression, while existing compression techniques yield significant performance degradation, highlighting a Model Scalability gap. Second, even compressed diffusion models suffer from slow inference due to the iterative nature of diffusion sampling, with existing acceleration methods becoming ineffective in low-step regimes, creating an Inference Scalability problem. Third, these models must continuously adapt to evolving concepts without forgetting previous knowledge, a requirement for Conceptual Scalability that current personalization techniques cannot efficiently meet. This project aims to break down these barriers with a comprehensive framework for efficient and adaptive visual generation on edge devices. We will first introduce a new method to compress large models into compact, high-performance versions suitable for phones and IoT devices. Next, we will develop a novel distillation technique to drastically reduce the number of steps needed to generate content, paired with a smart caching strategy to speed up each step. Finally, we will create a lightweight adaptation framework that allows the model to continuously learn new concepts and trends from the world, ensuring it stays current without extensive retraining. Together, these innovations form a unified pipeline that supports the entire lifecycle of on-device visual generative models, from compression and fast inference to continuous adaptation. The proposed research will be rigorously tested against the best available methods through technical benchmarks, user studies, and edge device deployment verification. By solving the challenges of model, inference, and conceptual scalability in a synergistic way, this project will establish a new foundation for high-quality, fast, and intelligent visual generation directly on edge devices, unlocking new possibilities for consumer applications, creative tools, and personalized media experiences. 面向邊緣設備端視覺內容生成——例如在無需雲連接的智能手機上即時創建社交媒體頭像或編輯視頻——代表了用戶體驗創新的關鍵前沿。從雲端處理向邊緣部署的轉變，在延遲、成本效率和數據私隱方面帶來了顯著優勢。然而，最先進的視覺生成模型（VGM），尤其是基於擴散過程的模型，因其龐大的模型規模、緩慢的推理速度和有限的自適應學習能力，在資源受限的邊緣環境中仍面臨巨大的計算障礙。 三大基礎性可擴展性挑戰阻礙了VGM在邊緣端的有效部署。第一，基礎模型體積過大，無法直接部署，需進行壓縮，而現有壓縮技術會導致顯著的性能下降，凸顯出模型可擴展性的差距。第二，即使經過壓縮，擴散模型由於擴散採樣的迭代性質，推理速度依然緩慢，現有加速方法在低步數場景下效果不佳，形成了推理可擴展性問題。第三，這些模型必須持續適應不斷演進的新概念，同時不遺忘已有知識，這是概念可擴展性的要求，而當前的個性化技術無法高效滿足。 本項目旨在通過一套面向邊緣設備的高效自適應視覺生成綜合框架，打破上述障礙。我們首先將引入一種新方法，將大型模型壓縮為適用於手機和物聯網設備的緊湊、高性能版本。其次，我們將開發一種新穎的蒸餾技術，大幅減少生成內容所需的步數，並配合智能緩存策略加速每一步的執行。最後，我們將構建一個輕量級自適應框架，使模型能夠持續從世界中學習新概念和新趨勢，確保其在不需大規模重新訓練的情況下保持時效性。 這些創新共同構成一個統一的流水線，覆蓋設備端視覺生成模型的整個生命週期，從壓縮、快速推理到持續自適應。本項目將通過技術基準測試、用戶研究和邊緣設備部署驗證，與現有最佳方法進行嚴格對比。通過協同解決模型、推理和概念可擴展性方面的挑戰，本項目將為直接在邊緣設備上實現高質量、快速且智能的視覺生成建立新的基礎，為消費應用、創意工具和個性化媒體體驗解鎖新的可能性。

16205826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16205826.value: 集成CMOS毫米波全双工无线电的自干扰消除技术

16205826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205826.value: 5G/6G applications have emerged as potential solutions in response to the growing demand of higher data rates (>10Gbps) for wireless communications. In particular, full-duplex (FD) communication has become increasingly attractive due to its ability to provide simultaneous transmitting and receiving of data at the same carrier frequency and thus to double spectral efficiency and to reduce latency. However, in such a full-duplex radio, a large continuous signal from the output of the transmitter directly appears at the input of the receiver as strong unwanted self-interference, either through on-chip coupling between the transmitter and the receiver or through non-zero-delay reflections from close-by objects. Typically, such self-interference can be as large as 100dB above the wanted signals and results in serious problems limiting the TRX’s system performance in terms of sensitivity and dynamic range. Many solutions have been proposed, but most of them were developed for applications in radio frequencies around 1GHz to 10GHz, which are not suitable for millimeter-Wave frequencies at 60GHz or above. The objective of this proposed project is to leverage the investigator’s expertise and strengths in mm-Wave and sub-THz integrated circuits and systems to develop some effective design techniques to cancel self-interference in integrated CMOS full-duplex radios in millimeter-wave frequency bands. To achieve the proposed self-interference cancellation, four different cancellation mechanisms will be developed and combined, including not only a feed-forward path of a replica and a feedback cancellation path from baseband but also offset cancellation and a high-order N-path notch filter at the baseband. The radio’s front-end will be designed, laid out, fabricated, and measured to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed cancellation techniques. 随着无线通信对更高数据速率（>10Gbps）的需求日益增长，5G/6G应用已成为潜在的解决方案。特别是，全双工（FD）通信因其能够在同一载波频率上同时进行数据发送和接收，从而提高频谱效率并降低延迟，而变得越来越有吸引力。然而，在这样的全双工无线电中，来自发射机输出的强连续信号会直接以强烈的自干扰形式出现在接收机的输入端，这可能是由于发射机和接收机之间的片上耦合，也可能是由于附近物体的非零延迟反射造成的。通常，这种自干扰可能比所需信号高出100dB，从而导致严重的问题，限制收发器（TRX）的系统性能，例如灵敏度和动态范围。虽然已提出多种解决方案，但大多数方案是针对1GHz至10GHz左右的射频应用而开发的，并不适用于60GHz及以上的毫米波频率。 本项目旨在利用研究人员在毫米波和亚太赫兹集成电路及系统方面的专业知识和优势，开发一些有效的设计技术，以消除毫米波频段集成CMOS全双工无线电中的自干扰。为实现所提出的自干扰消除方案，我们将开发并组合四种不同的消除机制，不仅包括来自基带的副本前馈路径和反馈消除路径，还包括偏移消除和基带高阶N路陷波滤波器。我们将设计、布局、制造和测量无线电前端，以验证所提出的消除技术的有效性。

16206326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206326.value: Dealloying transforms an alloy into bi-continuous nanoporous (BNP) metal, boosting the specific area for applications in electrocatalysis, sensing, and energy storage. The process typically occurs in a liquid electrolyte (e.g., an acid) that percolates through the evolving nanopores while selectively removing the more reactive component of the alloy. Recent work reveals that the same transformation occurs when the electrolyte is solid. Such solid-electrolyte dealloying (SED) underlies the discharging of alloy anodes in all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) and contributes to contact loss, a key failure mechanism preventing ASSBs from fulfilling their safety and high energy density. Yet SED also brings a new opportunity for liquid-free fabrication, enabling spatially confined dealloying and patterned nanostructures with enhanced functionalities. However, we can neither prevent the failure nor design the fabrication without understanding the formation mechanism of BNP metal. Classic theory ties it to liquid-electrolyte percolation, which does not apply to SED. We hypothesize that surface diffusion governs SED, transporting atoms through the nanopores to the solid electrolyte. This kinetics pathway predominates over alloy bulk diffusion due to the large, connected surface area in BNP metal, whose formation, in turn, maintains the dominance of surface diffusion. The hypothesis suggests that BNP metal formation in SED can be generalized beyond the current focus on lithium alloys and inorganic solid electrolytes. It also reveals a route toward high-rate alloy anodes for ASSBs, as the evolution of BNP metal may be harnessed to overcome the limit of bulk diffusion. This project aims to elucidate the mechanism underlying the evolution of BNP metal in SED. We will first examine SED under rigorously controlled conditions and establish parametric bounds for forming BNP metal. We will then analyze SED rates to determine the controlling kinetics, investigate the morphological dependence of diffusivity via galvanic intermittent titration, and develop a continuum model to predict SED processes. Finally, insights from the mechanism will inform the design of patterned BNP metals as mechanically robust electrodes for flow cells and the optimization of lithium alloy anodes for high-rate ASSBs. The success of the project will deepen our understanding of kinetics-controlled morphology evolution, offer new approaches to nanomaterial fabrication, and shed light on alloy/solid-electrolyte interfaces underpinning advanced electrochemical devices like ASSBs. 脫合金可將合金轉化為雙連續奈米多孔金屬，提升比表面積來滿足電催化、傳感與能量儲存等應用。此過程通常發生於液態電解質（例如酸溶液）中，通過液態電解質滲透逐漸演化的孔隙，來選擇性移除合金中較活潑的組分。近期研究顯示，當電解質為固態時，同樣的轉化亦可發生。此類固態電解質脫合金是全固態電池中合金負極的放電過程，可能導致接觸喪失，妨礙固態電池穩定運行。同時，固態電解質脫合金為無溶劑製備新型奈米結構提供了可能性。 然而，經典理論將多孔金屬結構演化歸因於電解質滲流，並不適用於 固態電解質脫合金。我們則假設其為表面擴散主導 ，具有大面積且連通奈米孔表面將原子輸運至固態電解質進行脫合金。此假設不僅闡明固態電解質脫合金可以從鋰合金等體系進一步推廣至其他合金，亦揭示了一條通往高倍率固態電池電極的可行路徑。 本計畫旨在闡明固態電解質脫合金中的多孔金屬演化的底層機制。我們將首先在嚴格控制的條件下研究 此過程，並建立形成 多孔金屬的參數範圍。隨後，我們將分析脫合金速率以確定其動力學，透過恆電流間歇滴定技術研究合金相擴散率對形貌的依賴性，並建立連續體模型以預測 結構演化。最後，對機制的理解將用於指導多孔金屬的設計，應用於流體池電極，和高倍率固態電池的鋰合金負極的優化。

16206526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16206526.value: 海洋搜索和救援中視覺搜索和地圖構建的研究

16206526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206526.value: Maritime search and rescue (SAR) remains a significant public safety challenge, particularly in Hong Kong, where nearly 40% of SAR cases in the past 15 years occurred within local waters. Current SAR practices are largely reactive, relying on distress reports and human visual observation, which are inefficient in complex maritime environments with changing weather, poor visibility, and high risks to personnel. This project aims to transform SAR operations by introducing a vision-based autonomous framework that proactively integrates environmental modeling and search. Using Remotely Operated Vehicles (ROVs) and Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs), the system will fuse seabed video and motion data to create high-fidelity 3D reconstructions of underwater environments and dynamic ocean flow models. These models will support an autonomous vision-based search system that leverages image cues to efficiently locate silent or unreported targets under resource constraints. By unifying mapping and search, this framework reduces human risk, enhances situational awareness, and enables rapid, autonomous responses, marking a paradigm shift in maritime safety and advancing applications in SAR, seafloor inspections, and marine ecological monitoring. 海事搜索與救援（SAR）一直是公共安全領域的重要挑戰，尤其在香港，過去 15 年近 40% 的搜救個案發生於本地水域。目前的搜救行動大多仍以被動應對為主，主要依賴求救訊息及人工目視觀察；然而，在天氣多變、能見度低且作業風險高的複雜環境中，這種模式不僅效率有限，也對救援人員構成較大安全威脅。本項目旨在引入一套以視覺感知為核心的自主搜救框架，將環境建模與目標搜索主動整合，推動海事搜救由被動響應轉向智能化、自主化作業。項目將利用遙控水下航行器（ROVs）及無人水面載具（USVs），融合海床影像與運動資訊，建立高精度的水下環境三維重建模型，以及動態海洋流場模型。在此基礎上，項目將進一步支援自主視覺搜索，利用影像線索，在有限時間與資源條件下高效定位未能發出求救訊號或位置未知的目標。透過將環境建圖與自主搜索統一於同一框架之中，本項目有望降低人員直接參與高風險搜救工作的需求，提升對海上與水下環境的態勢感知力，並實現更快速、更自主的應急響應。整體而言，本項目將推動海事搜救作業模式由人工、被動搜救轉變為智能、自主搜索，並可進一步拓展至海床巡檢、海洋生態監測等相關應用。

16207126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16207126.value: 芯联网：面向智能、可扩展物联网的超低功耗无线总线架构

16207126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207126.value: The rapid expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) envisions a world in which billions of interconnected devices are embedded throughout infrastructure, the environment, and even the human body. Traditionally, these IoT devices have been designed according to the Von Neumann architecture—an approach centered on the microprocessor. In this model, each device, regardless of its size or cost, functions as an independent embedded computer equipped with its own computing capabilities. However, as the IoT ecosystem continues to scale, the Von Neumann model has increasingly become a bottleneck in optimizing energy consumption across end devices. Microprocessors operating at milliwatt (mW) levels must continuously handle sensing, control, and computation tasks. These frequent operations disrupt low-power states, leading to constrained battery life and increased maintenance demands—particularly problematic for devices that are deeply embedded or difficult to access. This project rethinks the conventional IoT design by proposing a novel Internet-of-Microchips architecture, where IoT gateways have direct wireless access to sensor chips deployed on the end device for control and data collection purposes, which would allow high deployment flexibility and significantly reduce the energy consumption of end devices. In this architecture, the gateway performs centralized data processing, control, and diagnostic functions, thereby significantly reducing the end device’s power consumption to the microwatt (µW) level while enhancing adaptability and intelligence through gateway-driven computation. The proposed research tackles three major technical challenges: (1) establishing direct wireless-to-bus communication between gateways and sensor chips to offload computation and control; (2) developing computing-less mechanisms for remote device management and status diagnosis through nano-power parasitic communication and channel-based inference; and (3) ensuring robust and scalable wireless communication via asymmetric modulation/coding schemes and meta-surface-assisted channel enhancement. A comprehensive experimental testbed will be built to validate the architecture, integrating multiple sensor types, low-power circuits, and software-defined gateways. The success of the proposed study will revolutionize IoT system design by enabling ultra-low-power, maintenance-free devices that operate at the µW level. By removing the on-device microprocessor and shifting computation, control, and diagnostics to the gateway through a wireless bus, the project will achieve intelligent, adaptive, and energy-efficient sensor operation. It will further realize computing-free remote management, while ensuring robust and scalable connectivity. Validated using a comprehensive experimental testbed, the outcomes will establish a new generation of sustainable and intelligent Internet-of-Microchips systems, with broad impact on smart infrastructure, healthcare, and environmental monitoring. 物联网的快速发展正在推动一个由数十亿互联设备构成的世界。这些设备广泛嵌入基础设施、自然环境，甚至人体之中。传统上，物联网设备通常基于冯·诺依曼体系结构进行设计，其核心是微处理器。在这种模式下，每个设备无论尺寸或成本如何，都被设计为一台独立的嵌入式计算机，并具备自身的计算能力。 然而，随着物联网生态系统不断扩展，冯·诺依曼架构逐渐成为进一步优化终端设备能耗的瓶颈。工作功耗处于毫瓦级的微处理器需要持续执行感知、控制和计算任务。频繁的处理操作会不断打断设备的低功耗状态，从而限制电池寿命并增加维护需求。对于深度嵌入系统内部或难以接触的设备而言，这一问题尤为突出。 本项目重新思考传统物联网的设计范式，提出一种新型“芯联网”架构。在该架构中，物联网网关可直接通过无线信号访问部署于终端设备上的传感器芯片，并对其进行控制和数据采集。该设计能够提高设备部署的灵活性，并显著降低终端设备的能耗。网关集中承担数据处理、控制和故障诊断等功能，从而将终端设备的功耗降低至微瓦级。同时，通过由网关驱动的计算和控制，系统可进一步提升其适应性和智能化水平。 本项目将重点解决三个主要技术挑战：（1）建立网关与传感器芯片之间的无线总线通信机制，将计算和控制功能从终端设备卸载至网关；（2）利用纳瓦级寄生通信和基于无线信道的状态推断，开发无需终端计算参与的远程设备管理与状态诊断机制；（3）通过非对称调制与编码机制以及超表面辅助的信道增强技术，实现可靠且可扩展的无线通信。项目还将搭建一个综合实验测试平台，集成多种传感器、低功耗电路和软件定义网关，以验证所提出架构的可行性和性能。 本项目的成功实施有望推动物联网系统设计范式的变革，实现工作于微瓦级、超低功耗且近乎免维护的终端设备。通过移除终端设备上的微处理器，并借助无线总线将计算、控制和故障诊断功能迁移至网关，本项目将实现智能、自适应且高能效的传感器运行机制。同时，该架构还可支持无需终端计算参与的远程设备管理，并保障无线连接的可靠性和可扩展性。通过综合实验测试平台的系统验证，本项目将为构建新一代可持续、智能化的芯联网系统奠定基础，并有望广泛应用于智能基础设施、医疗健康和环境监测等领域。

16207326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16207326.value: 用於實現耐久型鈣鈦礦光伏的層壓結構異質界面工程

16207326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207326.value: This project focuses on mechanism-driven molecular engineering of laminate-structured heterointerfaces (LSHs) to enhance the chemo-mechanical reliability of perovskite solar cells and modules. The LSH strategy addresses the intrinsic shortcomings of conventional interface engineering by overcoming the poor structural persistence of engineered interfaces under device operational conditions, thereby enabling more durable and scalable PSCs. Recent advancements in PSCs have sparked intense interest in their commercialization. Extensive efforts have been devoted to interface engineering of PSCs, resulting in state-of-the-art power conversion efficiencies (PCEs). Nevertheless, the inherent durability of those engineered interface microstructures has frequently been overlooked and thus understudied, leading to an inevitable tradeoff between high PCEs and stability. In this context, laminate-structured heterointerfaces (LSHs) have been reported as a novel type of interface microstructure, recently pioneered by the PI (Nature Synthesis 2025, 4, 1078-1087). LSHs are formed by the interdiffusion reaction between two-dimensional (2D) passivation salts and the perovskite surface, spatially mediated by a pre-deposited phenyl-C61-butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM) molecular interlayer. The interaction of diffusing ions with interlayer molecules plays a vital role in determining the overall reaction kinetics, and the resultant interface features a tailorable lamination of a 2D molecular passivation layer, the interlayer, and a 2D perovskite capping layer. Unlike conventionally engineered interfaces, the unique triple-layer passivation microstructures of LSHs exhibit long-term resistance to both chemical and mechanical degradations upon PSC operation. There is a promising opportunity to engineer LSHs to optimize their optoelectronic, chemical, and mechanical properties by leveraging a fundamental understanding of LSH structural formation and dynamics. The overall approach of this project entails three interrelated tasks: (i) using advanced multimodal characterizations to elucidate the atomic details and structural dynamics of LSHs; (ii) implanting ion-mediating interlayers (IMIs) toward engineered LSHs (E-LSHs) that can lead to perovskite films with improved optoelectronic, chemical, and mechanical properties; and (iii) fabricating stable, efficient PSCs and mini-modules to demonstrate the technological impact of E-LSHs. The PI has adequate expertise and resources to perform all these tasks. Strategies to mitigate potential risks associated with the characterization, materials synthesis, and device development in each task are proposed. The outcome of this project will directly impact the development of PSCs toward commercial viability. Meanwhile, the importance of LSHs is generic to all types of thin-film devices; thus, the engineering sciences developed through this project will have a broad impact on numerous other optoelectronic technologies, including, but not limited to, light-emitting devices, memristors, and sensors.

16207626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16207626.value: 按需出行服務的去中心化定價與匹配

16207626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207626.value: Although on-demand mobility platforms like DiDi, Uber, and Lyft have revolutionized urban transportation, they primarily rely on centralized systems for ride-matching and dynamic pricing. This conventional approach limits the agency of passengers and drivers, reducing their roles to accepting or declining algorithmically generated offers. The resulting lack of transparency raises concerns about fairness and equity, as passengers may face surge pricing without clear justification, while drivers often receive lowball offers. Additionally, these platforms struggle to balance system-wide efficiency with individual user preferences, which necessitates more adaptive and transparent systems that cater to all stakeholders, ensuring sustainable development in on-demand mobility markets. To address these challenges, the proposed research will introduce a decentralized pricing and matching mechanism that actively involves all parties in decision-making. In this model, the platform will transition from a central dispatcher to an information hub, facilitating transactions primarily through commission charges. Matching and pricing decisions will be made through a structured negotiation process, where passengers declare their maximum budget and preferred destination, while nearby drivers bid for the ride. Passengers will evaluate bids based on price, driver ratings, and estimated arrival times before selecting their preferred provider. A key innovation of this model will be its consideration of the spatial distributions of passengers and drivers, as pickup distance significantly impacts operational costs and waiting times. We will initially develop game-theoretic models to analyze optimal bidding strategies for drivers and budget-setting strategies for passengers, with spatial distribution as a core parameter. We will then explore the emergent formation of mutually agreeable prices, matching probabilities, and pickup durations at a systemic level, focusing on market equilibrium conditions to assess how decentralized strategies influence overall system performance, including matching rates and social welfare. The models will be calibrated using extensive anonymized datasets from the HKUST–DiDi Joint Research Laboratory. The proposed decentralized mechanism will be comprehensively compared against existing centralized models using a high-fidelity simulator developed by the joint lab. We will also conduct case studies jointly with industry partners DiDi and Hong Kong Taxi, utilizing real-world operational data from mainland China and Hong Kong. In summary, the proposed project will have significant theoretical and practical implications, offering insights for platform managers and policymakers aiming to create fairer and more efficient mobility markets. The proposed methodologies are expected to contribute to advancements in market mechanism design and promote sustainable, user-centric mobility solutions in Hong Kong, mainland China, and beyond. 儘管滴滴、優步和來福車等按需出行平台已深刻改變了城市交通，但它們主要依賴集中式系統來完成乘車匹配和動態定價。這種傳統做法限制了乘客和駕駛者的自主選擇權，使其只能被動接受或拒絕演算法產生的方案。由於缺乏透明度，公平性問題隨之凸顯：乘客可能在毫無明確解釋的情況下遭遇高峰加價，而司機則時常收到被壓低的訂單報價。此外，這些平台也難以在系統整體效率與個別使用者偏好之間實現平衡，因此亟需更具適應性和透明度的機制，以兼顧各方利益，推動按需出行市場的永續發展。 為因應上述挑戰，本研究擬提出一個去中心化的定價與匹配機制，讓乘客與駕駛者都能積極參與決策過程。在這個機制下，平台的角色將從中央調度員轉變為資訊中介，主要依靠收取佣金來促成交易。配對和定價將透過結構化的協商流程完成：乘客首先申報自己的最高預算和首選目的地，附近司機則針對該行程給出報價。乘客將綜合價格、司機評分和預計到達時間等因素評估報價，最終選擇心儀的服務提供者。該模型的一大創新點在於，它明確考慮了乘客與駕駛者的空間分佈，因為接駕距離會直接影響營運成本和等待時間。 研究初期，我們將建構博弈論模型，以空間分佈為核心參數，分析司機的最優報價策略與乘客的預算設定策略。隨後，我們將從系統層面探討可成交價格、匹配機率和接駕時長的湧現規律，重點考察市場均衡條件，從而評估去中心化策略對匹配率和社會福利等整體系統性能的影響。 模型將利用香港科技大學-滴滴聯合研究實驗室提供的大規模匿名資料集進行校正。我們也將藉助此聯合實驗室開發的高保真模擬器，將建議的去中心化機制與現有集中式模型進行全面比較。同時，我們計劃與產業夥伴滴滴和香港的士合作，基於中國內地和香港的實際營運數據進行案例研究。 總之，本計畫具有重要的理論與實務價值，可為平台管理者和政策制定者提供參考，協助建構更公平、更有效率的旅遊市場。預期研究成果將推動市場機制設計領域的發展，並為香港、內地乃至更廣區域提供可持續的、以使用者為中心的出行解決方案。

16208226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16208226.value: 面向下一代居家醫療保健的通用毫米波感知基礎模型

16208226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16208226.value: The aging population in Hong Kong is exerting unprecedented pressure on its healthcare system, creating an urgent need for scalable, long-term in-home monitoring solutions. While millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar sensing offers a promising, privacy-respecting alternative to cameras because of its high sensitivity and contactless nature, its adoption is hindered by a critical limitation: poor generalizability. Current systems are typically narrow, task-specific models trained on limited data from a single perspective that fail to adapt to the diverse sensing tasks required for comprehensive health monitoring. This project proposes a paradigm shift from task-specific models to a unified foundation model for mmWave sensing. Our central hypothesis is that a model pre-trained on a large, multi-task corpus of mmWave data can learn universal representations of human activity and physiology, enabling it to adapt robustly to various downstream healthcare applications. The project's goal is to develop, pre-train, and validate this first-of-its-kind foundation model, capable of generalizing from meter-level macro-movements (e.g., fall detection, activity recognition) to millimeter-level micro-motions (e.g., vital sign monitoring for Parkinson's tremor or hypertension). This project will encompass data curation, model design, pretraining, and deployment, facilitating trustworthy in-home healthcare services. We plan to achieve our objectives in two stages. First, we will create a mmWave pretraining pipeline to unify data from diverse tasks and analyses using a spectrum- aware transformer model. This hybrid pipeline will yield a powerful pretrained mmWave sensing model with four key components: (1) Integration of data from various tasks and hardware into a cohesive physical space; (2) Development of a customized spectrum- aware AI model to enable feature extraction from mmWave; (3) Cross-dataset self-supervised learning for pretraining; and (4) Cross-modality knowledge transfer to incorporate insights from other modalities. Second, we will adapt and deploy the pretrained mmWave foundation model on resource-constrained edge devices for real-world applications. We anticipate that this project will have significant social impact. By creating a generalized, non-contact, and privacy-preserving in-home monitoring system, we aim to alleviate the daily challenges faced by seniors managing chronic diseases and enhance their overall quality of life. This initiative will promote continuous awareness of various age-related conditions, such as Parkinson's disease and hypertension, ultimately reducing long-term care costs, minimizing hospital visits, and easing the burden on Hong Kong's healthcare system. By providing a scalable and user-friendly solution, our work will empower the aging population to live more independently and safely in their homes. 香港人口老齡化正對其醫療保健系統帶來了前所未有的壓力，因此迫切需要可擴展的長期居家監測解決方案。 毫米波雷達傳感技術因其高靈敏度和非接觸式特性，成為一種極具潛力且尊重隱私的攝像頭替代方案，但其應用卻受到一個關鍵限制：泛化能力差。目前的系統通常是基於單一視角、僅使用有限數據訓練的狹隘、特定任務模型，無法適應全面健康監測所需的各種傳感任務。 本項目提出了一種從特定任務模型到統一基礎模型的毫米波傳感範式轉變。我們的核心假設是，在大型多任務毫米波數據集進行訓練的模型可以學習人體活動和生理的通用表徵，從而使其能夠穩健地適應各種下游醫療保健應用。該項目的目標是開發、預訓練並驗証這一首創的基礎模型，該模型能夠從米級宏觀運動（例如，跌倒檢測、活動識別）泛化到毫米級微觀運動（例如，帕金森震顫或高血壓的生命體徵監測）。該項目將涵蓋數據整理、模型設計、預訓練和部署，從而促進值得信賴的居家醫療保健服務。 我們計劃分兩個階段實現目標。首先，我們將創建一個毫米波預訓練流水線，利用頻譜感知Transformer模型整合來自不同任務和分析的數據。該混合流水線將生成一個強大的預訓練毫米波傳感模型，該模型包含四個關鍵組件：(1) 將來自不同任務和硬件的數據集成到一個統一的物理空間中；(2) 開發定製的頻譜感知AI模型，以實現從毫米波中提取特徵；(3) 跨數據集進行自監督學習預訓練；以及 (4) 跨模態知識遷移，以整合來自其他模態的見解。其次，我們將對預訓練的毫米波基礎模型進行適配，並將其部署到資源受限的邊緣設備上，以應用於實際場景。 我們預計該項目將産生顯著的社會影響。通過創建一個通用、非接觸式且能保護隱私的居家監測系統，我們旨在減輕老年人在應對慢性疾病時面臨的日常挑戰，並提昇他們的整體生活質量。這項計劃旨在持續提升公衆對各種與年齡相關的疾病（例如帕金森病和高血壓）的認知，最終降低長期護理成本，減少就醫次數，並減輕香港醫療保健系統的負擔。通過提供可擴展且易於使用的解決方案，我們的工作將幫助老年人在居家生活中更加獨立和安全。

16208626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16208626.value: 聊天機器人真的能設計晶片嗎？大型語言模型輔助 RTL 設計生成之基準評估

16208626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16208626.value: Chip design complexity continues to escalate rapidly, with modern integrated circuits (ICs) exceeding 100 billion transistors and estimated IC design costs surpassing USD 500 million for 3nm technology nodes. This trajectory has created an urgent demand for next-generation electronic design automation (EDA) techniques. Recently, large language models (LLMs) have emerged as a transformative technology for chip design, with the most prominent application being RTL code generation based on natural-language specifications. Despite the rapid development of LLM solutions by academia and industry, appropriate quantitative evaluation infrastructures (i.e., benchmarking) remain underdeveloped, hindering progress in this field. This project addresses three fundamental limitations in existing benchmarks on LLM-assisted chip design: (1) Static benchmarks lack systematic maintenance, leaving flawed test cases unresolved and being susceptible to overfitting as LLMs evolve. (2) Current benchmarks focus on small, isolated design modules rather than project-level designs that reflect realistic industrial development scenarios. (3) Existing evaluations primarily assess functional correctness in RTL generation while mostly neglecting other crucial capabilities such as design optimization and semantic comprehension. We will deliver three key milestones to establish a dynamic, scalable, and comprehensive evaluation infrastructure. (1) Benchmark Enhancement and Maintenance: We will develop an innovative agentic AI framework that systematically analyzes and maintains existing benchmarks, identifying and resolving ambiguous specifications, syntax errors, and diagram inconsistencies. This framework will enable regular updates through both variation (describing identical functionality differently to detect overfitting) and augmentation (generating challenging new cases), ensuring benchmarks evolve alongside advancing LLM capabilities. (2) Project-Scale Benchmarks: We will create unprecedented project-level benchmarks encompassing both RTL revision (500+ cases requiring bug localization and fixes across multi-file codebases) and hierarchical RTL generation (200+ cases spanning 100-2K lines of code with complete project context). (3) Optimization and Comprehension Benchmarks: We will expand the evaluation scope beyond functionality to assess genuine design improvement capabilities through 100+ optimization cases capturing realistic patterns that synthesis tools cannot address, plus 200+ comprehension cases evaluating LLMs' semantic understanding across different abstraction levels. Our research group is uniquely positioned to execute this project, having pioneered widely-adopted benchmarks (RTLLM, AssertLLM) in LLM-assisted chip design. We will also collaborate closely with UniVista and the National Innovation Center for EDA, both are actively developing LLM-assisted chip design products and have existing collaborations with us. This project will establish the evaluation foundation necessary for advancing reliable, efficient, and democratized LLM-driven chip design, ultimately contributing to more efficient and cost-effective IC design processes. 晶片設計的複雜度持續快速攀升，凸顯出對次世代電子設計自動化（EDA）技術的迫切需求。近年來，大型語言模型（LLM）已成為晶片設計的變革性技術，其中最受矚目的應用即為基於自然語言規格的 RTL 程式碼生成。然而，相較於解決方案的快速發展，適當的量化評估基礎設施（即基準測試）仍嚴重不足，阻礙了此領域的進展。 本項目針對現有基準測試的三項根本限制：（1）靜態基準缺乏系統性維護，瑕疵案例未獲修正且易受過度擬合影響；（2）過度著重孤立的小型模組，而非反映真實產業情境的項目層級設計；（3）評估多僅衡量功能正確性，忽略設計優化與語意理解等關鍵能力。 為此，我們將達成三項關鍵里程碑：（1）基準強化與維護——開發創新的代理式 AI（agentic AI）框架，系統性辨識並修正規格模糊、語法錯誤及圖表不一致等問題，並透過「變體」與「擴充」進行定期更新，使基準隨 LLM 能力同步演進；（2）項目規模基準——建立涵蓋 RTL 修訂（500 個以上案例）與階層式 RTL 生成（200 個以上案例）的項目級基準；（3）優化與理解基準——以 100 個以上優化案例及 200 個以上理解案例，評估 LLM 的設計改善與跨抽象層級的語意理解能力。 我們的團隊曾率先開發出廣受採用的基準測試（RTLLM、AssertLLM），將推動可靠、高效且普惠化的 LLM 驅動晶片設計，最終促成更具成本效益的 IC 設計流程。

16209426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16209426.value: 基於穿戴式智慧胸針與多模態時間序列分析之兒童哮喘控制追蹤

16209426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209426.value: Asthma affects over 20% of children in many urban, high‑income settings. Effective asthma management requires regular assessment of symptom control; however, this is challenging in practice with children. Brief clinical consultations offer only a narrow snapshot and can be distorted by the white-coat effect, and children and their caregivers may struggle to recognize and accurately recall symptoms across days, leading to observation and recall biases. Consequently, many children are misclassified, live with uncontrolled asthma, and face heightened risks of exacerbations, irreversibly impaired lung development, sleep disturbance, and mental health comorbidities, which have long‑term impacts on growth and well-being. The proposed project will address this challenge using a new pediatric asthma control tracking (PACT) framework: a child‑friendly smart pin that attaches to clothing and quietly works in the background to estimate asthma control passively, continuously, and objectively. To this end, we will execute the following five tasks. First, we will design a compact wearable pin that captures telltale signs of breathing difficulties and everyday activities without disrupting normal routines while protecting privacy. Second, we will develop methods for reliably recognizing relevant symptoms and patterns during daily life—at home, at school, and during play—so that the system remains useful, even amid noise and distractions. Third, we will translate these daily observations into a simple, familiar control score aligned with the ACT using a novel multivariate time-series analysis method that accounts for subject heterogeneity and potential label scarcity. Then, after the development of PACT, we will test the system in a small‑scale pilot study with our collaborating hospital to assess its usability and clinical value in daily living settings. Finally, we will evaluate and summarize our findings and open-source the research outcomes. The significance of the proposed work will lie in delivering an end‑to‑end, low‑burden, privacy‑aware tool that turns real-world daily living signals into actionable assessments for clinicians and families. By replacing sporadic, subjective recall with continuous, objective evidence, PACT will enable earlier and more precise therapy adjustments, reducing exacerbation risks and healthcare reliance while improving children’s daily lives. We will also release the first open dataset linking everyday symptoms and activity patterns to pediatric asthma control, encouraging further research and paving the way for larger-scale trials and integration into routine care. 在許多城市化且高收入的地區，超過20%的兒童受哮喘影響，需接受治理並要定期評估症狀以有效控制狀況。然而，在兒童族群中，實際執行往往相當困難。短暫的臨床問診只能呈現有限的片段資訊，且可能受到白袍效應的影響。此外，兒童及其照顧者可能難以辨識症狀，也難以準確回憶數日之間的症狀變化，因而產生觀察偏差與回憶偏差。因此，許多兒童的哮喘控制狀況遭到錯誤分類，長期處於控制不佳的狀態，並面臨較高的急性惡化風險、不可逆的肺部發育受損、睡眠障礙，以及精神健康共病等問題，對其生長與整體福祉造成長期影響。 本研究計畫將提出一套全新的兒童哮喘控制追蹤框架（Pediatric Asthma Control Tracking, PACT）以應對上述挑戰。PACT 採用一款適合兒童、可固定於衣物上的智慧胸針，在不干擾日常生活的情況下於背景中運作，以被動、持續且客觀的方式評估哮喘控制狀況。為此，本計畫將執行以下五項工作。首先，我們將設計一款小型穿戴式智慧胸針，在保障使用者隱私的前提下，擷取呼吸困難的代表性徵象與日常活動資訊，同時避免干擾兒童的正常生活。其次，我們將開發可在居家、學校及遊戲等日常情境中可靠辨識相關症狀與行為模式的方法，使系統即使處於噪音及各種干擾之中，仍能維持實用性。第三，我們將運用一種新穎的多變量時間序列分析方法，將每日觀察所得轉換為簡單、易於理解，且與哮喘控制測驗（Asthma Control Test, ACT）一致的控制分數；該方法亦將考量受試者之間的個體異質性，以及可能存在的標籤資料稀缺問題。在完成 PACT 系統的開發後，我們將與合作醫院進行小規模先導研究，評估系統在日常生活環境中的可用性與臨床價值。最後，我們將系統性評估並總結研究結果，並將相關研究成果開源。 本研究的重要性在於提供一套端到端、低負擔且重視隱私的工具，能夠將真實日常生活中的訊號轉化為可供臨床人員與家庭採取行動的評估資訊。透過以持續且客觀的證據取代零散而主觀的症狀回憶，PACT 將有助於更早且更精確地調整治療方案，降低哮喘急性惡化風險及對醫療服務的依賴，並改善兒童的日常生活品質。此外，我們亦將發布首個連結兒童日常症狀、活動模式與哮喘控制狀況的開放資料集，以促進相關研究發展，並為未來更大規模的臨床試驗及整合至常規照護流程奠定基礎。

16209526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16209526.value: 結合理論與實驗方法研究部分類液態晶體中的熱輸運

16209526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209526.value: Partially liquid-like crystals (PLLCs), i.e., A2B (A = Cu+, Ag+; B = S2-, Se2-, Te2-), have been regarded as promising thermoelectrics that can directly convert heat to electricity. The figure of merit of PLLCs can reach 1.5 at 1000 K, which is among the highest efficiencies for any bulk crystals (Figure 1) and stems from their low thermal conductivity. Further increasing their figure of merit to the 3-4 range, which may be achieved by tuning their thermal transport properties, will enable PLLC-based thermoelectrics to compete with conventional electricity-producing methods. Understanding the thermal transport in PLLCs is therefore critical in designing the corresponding thermoelectrics. Unlike atoms or ions in conventional crystals (e.g., crystalline Si) that vibrate around lattice sites, anions in PLLCs form a rigid sublattice while cations are highly disordered with liquid-like mobilities. Cations can largely diffuse within the anion sublattice, which makes the thermal transport properties of PLLCs nontrivial. Our recent preliminary results show that the diffusion of liquid-like cations in PLLCs can contribute around 50% of the total thermal conductivity (Figure 2), suggesting that thermal transport channels resulting from both vibrations of anion lattice sites and diffusion of cations should be considered. However, conventional theoretical methods assume all atoms vibrate around their lattice sites and therefore they exclude the diffusion of liquid-like cations. This limitation has prevented a quantitative microscopic understanding of the scattering mechanisms in PLLCs. This project aims to elucidate the thermal transport in PLLCs considering contributions from both lattice vibrations and cation diffusion. A combination of state-of-the-art advanced theoretical methods and experimental techniques will be applied, including atomistic simulations and thermal transport property measurements. We will construct interatomic potentials to describe the dynamics of thermal transport and heat carriers in PLLCs based on first-principles calculations. We will then quantitatively characterize the contributions to the total thermal conductivity from various thermal transport channels including the influences of temperature and chemical composition. In addition, we will characterize the structural and thermal transport properties of the synthesized PLLCs to validate our theoretical analysis. New PLLCs (e.g., adjusting the chemical composition) with lower thermal conductivity (Figure 1) and improved figures of merit may then be designed based on these fundamental insights. This project will not only enhance the understanding of thermal transport mechanisms but also facilitate real-world applications of PLLCs in sustainable energy conversion technologies. 部分類液態晶體（PLLCs），即 A2B 型化合物（A = Cu+, Ag+; B = S2-, Se2-, Te2-），被視為極具潛力的熱電材料，能夠實現熱能向電能的直接轉換。 PLLCs 的熱電優值（ZT）在 1000 K 時可達 1.5，處於各類塊體晶體材料的最高水準之列（圖 1），這主要歸功於其極低的熱導率。若能透過調控熱輸運特性將其熱電優值進一步提升至 3–4 的範圍，基於 PLLCs 的熱電技術將具備與傳統發電方式競爭的實力。因此，深入理解 PLLCs 中的熱輸運機制對於設計高性能熱電材料至關重要。與傳統晶體（如晶體矽）中原子或離子在晶格格點附近振動的行為不同，PLLCs 中的陰離子構成剛性子晶格，而陽離子則處於高度無序狀態，表現出類似液體的遷移特性。陽離子能夠在陰離子子晶格內顯著擴散，使得 PLLCs 的熱輸運特性呈現出複雜的特性。我們近期的初步研究結果表明，PLLCs 中類液態陽離子的擴散貢獻了約 50% 的總熱導率（圖 2），這提示我們在分析熱輸運時，必須同時考慮陰離子晶格振動和陽離子擴散所形成的熱輸運通道。然而，傳統的理論方法通常假設所有原子均在晶格格點附近振動，因此忽略了類液態陽離子的擴散行為。這一限制阻礙了對 PLLCs 中散射機制的定量微觀理解。本計畫旨在綜合考慮晶格振動和陽離子擴散的貢獻，以闡明 PLLCs 中的熱輸運機制。我們將結合最先進的理論方法與實驗技術，包括原子尺度模擬和熱輸運特性測量。我們將基於第一原理計算構建原子間相互作用勢，以描述 PLLCs 中熱輸運及熱載流子的動力學行為；隨後，我們將定量表徵不同熱輸運通道（包括溫度和化學組分的影響）對總熱導率的貢獻。此外，我們也將對合成的 PLLCs 樣品進行結構與熱輸運特性表徵，以驗證理論分析結果。基於這些基本見解，可以設計出具有更低熱導率（圖1）及更高品質因數的新型PLLC（例如透過調整化學成分）。該計畫不僅將加深對熱輸運機制的理解，還將推動PLLC在可持續能源轉換技術的實際應用。

16209726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16209726.value: 一种在增强现实中生成自适应情境可视化的智能体可视化框架

16209726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209726.value: Situated visualizations in Augmented Reality (AR) provide a transformative way to interact with data by seamlessly linking it to physical referents. It has the potential to revolutionize many high-impact domains rooted in physical and digital world integration, such as environmental analysis, urban exploration, and heritage preservation. Most existing research on situated visualization focuses on predefined tasks under fixed user preferences and spatial contexts (e.g., locations, environments). However, real-world scenarios require constantly switching between various user tasks performed in diverse spatial contexts with different user preferences on the attributes of visualizations (e.g., visual encodings). This project proposes a versatile framework that can generate AR situated visualizations adaptive to a user's evolving tasks, preferences, and contexts. It leverages emerging agentic AI, a paradigm where multiple specialized agents collaborate. This framework decomposes high-level user goals into subtasks executed by a team of specialized agents (e.g., for chart generation, layout, and narration), achieving a level of distributed intelligence beyond single agents. Key challenges within this architecture involve dynamically assigning agents to user tasks that could be ambiguous, inferring user preferences from implicit signals, and enabling the efficient selection of heterogeneous spatial context. To tackle these challenges, we propose the following research tasks (T1-T4), systematically organized together to build and evaluate the framework. First, we construct a dedicated library of specialized execution agents and develop a novel anchor-based task-agent alignment estimator to dynamically assign agents to ambiguous tasks, achieving robust task adaptivity (T1). Second, we enable user adaptivity (T2) by creating a mechanism to continuously infer dynamic user preferences from implicit behavioral signals and integrate them into a personalized agent orchestration process. Third, we achieve context adaptivity (T3) by introducing a human-in-the-loop spatial context selection mechanism, which resolves ambiguity through editable context representations and multimodal AR interactions for refinement. Finally, we validate the integrated framework's cross-domain utility through real-world applications (T4), demonstrating its societal impact by empowering low-vision individuals with accessible urban navigation and its economic and environmental impact by advancing in-situ scientific discovery for marine researchers. All algorithms, agent libraries, and systems will be openly shared to accelerate future research in visualization, AI, AR, etc. 增强现实（AR）中的情境可视化（situated visualization）通过将数据无缝连接到物理参照物，提供了一种变革性的数据交互方式。它有可能彻底改变众多高影响力领域，特别是深深依赖物理与数字世界融合的领域，例如环境分析、城市探索和遗产保护。大多数现有的情境可视化研究侧重于在固定的用户偏好和空间上下文（如位置、环境）下执行预定义任务。然而，现实世界场景要求用户不断在多样化的空间上下文中切换执行各种任务，并且对可视化的属性（例如视觉编码）有着不同的偏好。 本项目致力于提出一个框架，能够生成自适应的AR情境可视化，以响应用户不断变化的任务、偏好和上下文。该框架采用了智能体人工智能（Agentic AI）这一新兴范式，让多个专业化智能体协同工作。具体而言，该框架能将用户的高级目标分解为子任务，交由一组专业化智能体（例如分别负责图表生成、布局和叙述的智能体）执行，从而实现单个智能体无法达到的分布式智能。然而，该架构的设计与实现面临一些关键挑战，包括：如何将智能体动态分配给模糊的用户任务、如何从隐式信号中推断用户偏好，以及如何高效地选择异构空间上下文。 为应对这些挑战，我们提出以下研究任务（T1–T4），以系统性地构建并评估该框架。首先，我们将构建一个专门的执行智能体库，并设计一种新颖的基于锚点的任务-智能体对齐估计器，以动态地将智能体分配给模糊任务，实现任务适应性（T1）。其次，我们将通过创建一种机制来持续从隐式行为信号中推断动态用户偏好，并将其融入个性化智能体编排过程，从而实现用户适应性（T2）。第三，我们将通过引入一种人在回路中的空间上下文选择机制来实现上下文适应性（T3），该机制通过可编辑的上下文表示以及多模态AR交互来减少歧义。最后，我们将通过真实世界应用来验证框架的有效性（T4），展示其带来的社会、经济与环境影响，例如助力海洋研究人员的科学发现。所有算法、智能体库和系统都将开源，以加速可视化、人工智能、增强现实等领域的未来研究。

16209826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16209826.value: 非均勻的都市風環境中基於物理的小型無人機聲傳播建模

16209826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209826.value: The rapid advancement of small unmanned aircraft (SUA) has driven economic and social transformations in recent years. However, public concerns remain a major obstacle to their seamless integration into urban environments. The inhomogeneous urban airflow physics and the complexity of SUA noise pose severe challenges in evaluating sound transmission (see Figure 1). Conventional prediction models cannot fully and efficiently account for phenomena encountered in urban acoustic propagation, e.g., refractions and diffractions, nor the rich nature of noise sources in frequency content and directivity. Methods based on partial differential equations are computationally expensive. Substantial gaps exist in our scientific understanding of SUA noise and in developing accurate and efficient methods for assessing sound transmission in complex wind environments. This project aims to develop a new physics-based method for SUA sound transmission in inhomogeneous urban wind environments with the aim of correctly capturing relevant physics. Advances will be made on several fronts, including new theoretical methods & models, and accurate SUA noise source reconstruction by experimental and numerical approaches using indoor & field tests, and high-fidelity simulations. First, a computational framework based on a new variant of Gaussian beam tracing (GBT) method will be developed to assess the impact of inhomogeneous mean flow on multi-frequency sound transmission. This work advances PI’s research on single-frequency GBT. Given the rich nature of real SUA noise, a new variant of GBT and task-parallel algorithm across multiple frequencies will be developed and validated by benchmark cases. Second, a new acoustic scattering model based on high-order beam series is proposed to assess the impact of inhomogeneous local flow structures on sound transmission. This model will also be validated by benchmark cases to ensure that acoustic scattering effects are adequately considered. Third, the complex SUA sound radiation sphere (see Figure 1) for the new GBT methods, typically generated by SUA under 25 kg, will be established by custom-designed anechoic chamber and outdoor field experiments. High-fidelity simulations of SUA noise will be conducted in aid of sound field construction for the GBT computation. Finally, the new framework will be employed to evaluate SUA sound transmission in typical urban canyon scenarios under inhomogeneous airflows at various SUA flight conditions. High-fidelity simulations will be conducted to simulate urban wind environments. The research will enhance our understanding and ability to assess SUA sound transmission in complex urban wind environments. Outcome can benefit regulation and standard development. 小型無人機（SUA）的快速發展，近年來推動了經濟與社會的轉型。然而，公眾的關注仍是其順利融入都市環境的主要障礙。城市氣流物理的不均勻性以及單體噪聲的複雜性，對評估聲音傳播造成嚴重挑戰。傳統預測模型無法完全且有效地涵蓋都市聲學傳播中遇到的現象，例如折射與繞射，也無法涵蓋噪音源在頻率內容與指向性的豐富特性。基於偏微分方程的方法計算量大。我們對SUA雜訊的科學理解，以及在複雜風環境中評估聲波傳播的精確且高效方法上，存在重大空白。 本計畫旨在開發一種基於物理的新方法，用於非均勻都市風環境中的SUA聲波傳輸，並正確捕捉相關物理現象。本計畫將在多個方面將取得進展，包括新的理論方法與模型，以及透過實驗與數值方法，利用室內與實地測試，以及高保真模擬，精確重建單聲噪聲源。 首先，我們將開發基於高斯束追蹤（GBT）新變體的計算框架，以評估非均勻平均流對多頻聲波傳播的影響。這項工作推動了PI在單頻率GBT的研究。鑑於真實 SUA 雜訊的豐富特性，我們將開發並由基準案例驗證一個跨多頻率的 GBT 變體及任務平行演算法。其次，我們提出基於高階光束系列的新聲學散射模型，以評估非均勻局部流動結構對聲音傳播的影響。此模型也將透過基準案例驗證，以確保聲學散射效應被充分考量。第三，我們為新GBT方法設計的複雜SUA聲波輻射球，通常由25公斤以下的SUA產生，將透過客製化設計的消聲室及戶外實地實驗建立。我們將進行高保真模擬 SUA 雜訊，以協助 GBT 計算的聲場建構。最後，新框架將用於評估在不同單空飛行條件下，於非均勻氣流下的典型都市峽谷情境中，SUA聲波傳輸。並進行高保真模擬以模擬都市風力環境。 這項研究將增進我們對複雜都市風力環境中SUA聲波傳播的理解與評估能力。 結果有助於法規與標準制定。

16210026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16210026.value: 針對水中全氟及多氟烷基物質循環去除的工程生物炭分子級設計：基於熱驅動的 PFAS 礦化與生物炭再生

16210026.label: Co - Investigator(s)
16210026.value: Prof Lo, Man Chi Prof Tsang, Dan Chiu Wa

16210026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16210026.value: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent industrial chemicals, and their high stability and durability in the environment make them “forever chemicals”. PFAS contaminate water systems worldwide, posing a threat to human health due to their high toxicity and bioaccumulation. The common treatment process uses either an ion-exchange resin or activated carbon (AC), with AC generally preferred for its ease of use in practical applications. However, AC technology has the following disadvantages: (1) it merely removes a fraction of PFAS from water, primarily long-chain compounds; (2) it cannot support complete PFAS mineralization during thermal treatment, and toxic by-products are generated; and (3) the regeneration of AC for PFAS adsorption requires high-temperature treatment (>700°C) with extra activation, which is cost-, energy-, and carbon-intensive. Additionally, the adsorption efficiency of PFAS cannot be fully regenerated. To overcome these disadvantages, the proposed project will pioneer the use of engineered biochar derived from biomass waste for cyclic PFAS removal through adsorption and mineralization. Our engineered biochar is expected to outperform conventional approaches by adsorbing a broad spectrum of PFAS, thermally mineralizing the adsorbed PFAS, and thermally regenerating itself, enabled by the scientific modification of porosity, functional groups, and metal oxide clusters. First, the pore structure, functional groups, and metal oxide clusters will synergistically adsorb a broad spectrum of PFAS with different headgroups and chain lengths. Second, a suitable pore structure will confine PFAS molecules associated with designed functional groups and metal oxide clusters to form a “mineralization-ready” pattern. This process is expected to lower the energy of strong PFAS bonds, retain the short-chain by-products, and enable near-complete catalytic mineralization at lower temperatures than the current method (200–500°C). Finally, the thermally stable structure of biochar, including the stable pore structure with graphitic carbon, aromatic functional groups, and metal oxide clusters anchored by functional groups, can potentially enable the reuse of biochar. Our sustainable biochar for cyclic PFAS removal will aim to achieve the following breakthroughs: (1) it will adsorb and mineralize a broad spectrum of PFAS; (2) it will turn PFAS into non-toxic by-products without secondary pollution; and (3) the full regeneration of biochar at a low temperature is expected to allow its cyclic usage with a low cost, low energy consumption, and a low carbon footprint. By developing a circular, sustainable biochar-based strategy for PFAS removal, we will provide a solution for safeguarding global water security. 全氟及多氟烷基物質 (PFAS) 是一種持久的工業化學品，其在環境中具有高度的穩定性及耐久性，因而被稱為「永久化學品」。PFAS 廣泛存在於全球水體中，並因其高毒性及生物累積性而對人類健康構成威脅。常見的處理程序採用離子交換樹脂或活性炭，其中活性炭因在實際應用中較易操作而通常更受青睞。然而，活性炭技術存在以下缺點：(1) 僅能去除水中一小部分的 PFAS，且主要為長鏈化合物；(2) 在熱處理過程中，無法達致 PFAS 的完全礦化，並且會產生有毒副產物；(3) 用於吸附 PFAS 的活性炭需要經過高溫處理及額外活化才能再生，此過程會消耗大量成本與能源，並產生大量碳排放。此外，其對 PFAS 的吸附效能亦無法完全恢復。 為了克服上述缺點，本擬議項目將採用由生物質廢料轉化而成的「工程生物炭」，透過吸附與礦化作用來循環去除 PFAS。透過對孔隙率、官能基及金屬氧化物簇進行科學改性，我們的工程生物炭預期將超越傳統方法，能夠吸附種類廣泛的 PFAS，透過熱化學過程對已吸附的 PFAS 進行熱礦化，並實現自身的熱再生。首先，孔隙結構、官能基與金屬氧化物簇將發揮協同作用，吸附具有不同頭基和鏈長的各種 PFAS。其次，合適的孔隙結構會將與特定官能基及金屬氧化物簇結合的 PFAS 分子限制於其中，使其處於「易礦化」狀態。預期此過程將削弱 PFAS 穩固的化學鍵能，固定短鏈副產物以進行深度脫氟，並在比現有方法更低的溫度下 (200–500°C) 實現近乎完全的催化礦化。最後，生物炭具備熱穩定的結構（包括帶有石墨化碳的穩定孔隙結構、芳香族官能基，以及由官能基錨定的金屬氧化物簇），使其具有被重複使用的潛力。 我們用於循環去除 PFAS 的可持續生物炭旨在實現以下突破：(1) 吸附並礦化種類廣泛的 PFAS；(2) 將 PFAS 轉化為無毒副產物，且不產生二次污染；(3) 預期生物炭能在低溫下完全再生，從而以低成本、低能耗及低碳足跡實現循環使用。透過開發這種以生物炭為基礎、循環且可持續的 PFAS 去除策略，我們將為保障全球水資源安全提供一項解決方案。

16210426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16210426.value: 氣候變化下降雨誘發邊坡滑坡的機器學習輔助分析

16210426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16210426.value: Recent climate changes have caused significant economic losses, injuries, and casualties, highlighted by the record-breaking heatwaves in Europe and China in 2023, and the extreme rainstorms in Hong Kong in September 2023 and Beijing in July 2025. The September 2023 rainstorm brought over 800 mm of precipitation to Hong Kong within 24 hours, leading to the failure or instability of 180 slopes in Hong Kong. Evaluating and enhancing the safety and resilience of slopes against the effects of climate change is crucial, particularly for those important slopes affecting dense populations or critical infrastructure (e.g., major highways). However, accurately assessing slope safety under climate change is challenging because of the difficulty in developing high-fidelity models for specific slopes, stemming from a lack of slope-specific information (e.g., slope-specific projection of future rainfall patterns and subsurface geological details such as soil stratigraphy and property spatial variability). Emerging machine learning (ML) offers a new approach to this issue, although developing geotechnical ML poses challenges. Extensive training databases are essential for ML success, but geotechnical data are often limited and site-specific, making it difficult to compile suitable geotechnical databases for ML. To address these challenges, this proposed project will create a slope-specific training database using existing knowledge and numerical modeling and will develop knowledge-guided ML methods for high-fidelity analysis of rainfall-induced instability on a specific slope under the effects of climate change. The database will encompass both site-specific data collected from the slope (e.g., slope geometry, sparse site investigation data, past rainfall records at or near the slope) and domain knowledge (e.g., soil mechanics, numerical analysis principles, prior geological knowledge, regional projections of future rainfall patterns). The database will be used to train ML models for evaluating the safety of the specific slope against projected rainfall patterns with quantified uncertainty. The PI has developed a preliminary ML method for slope stability analysis without considering rainfall and has obtained promising results. In this project, the method will be further developed to incorporate rain infiltration and triggering of slope instability and slope-specific projection of future rainfall patterns. The methods developed will be calibrated using real slope case histories, and software will be developed to facilitate their applications. This project will provide effective ML methods and software that could revolutionize slope engineering practice worldwide. This will have tremendous economic and societal impacts for many landslide-prone areas around the world, including Hong Kong, under changing climate conditions. 近期氣候變遷已造成顯著的經濟損失及人命傷亡，例如2023年9月的暴雨在24小時內為香港帶來超過800毫米的降雨，導致香港有180處邊坡發生滑坡。評估並提升邊坡面對氣候變遷效應的安全性和韌性至關重要，特別是對於影響人口稠密地區或關鍵基礎設施（如主要高速公路）的重要邊坡。然而，由於缺乏邊坡的具體資訊（如未來降雨模式在目標邊坡的預測，以及地下土層和土工參數空間變異性等），建立邊坡的高保真模型十分困難，準確評估邊坡在氣候變遷下的安全極具挑戰性。為了解決這些挑戰，本項目將利用現有知識和數值模擬來創建一個邊坡專屬的訓練資料庫，並開發知識導引的機器學習方法，對氣候變遷影響下目標邊坡的降雨誘發滑坡進行高保真分析。該資料庫將涵蓋從邊坡收集的場地數據（如邊坡幾何形狀、稀疏的地勘數據、邊坡的過去降雨記錄等）以及專業知識（如土力學、數值分析原理、先驗地質知識、未來降雨模式的區域預測等）。該資料庫將用於訓練機器學習模型，量化不確定性，評估目標邊坡在預測降雨模式下的安全狀況。

16210526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16210526.value: 基於物質點法、計算流體動力學和離散元耦合與機器學習對都市天坑地質災害評估的多尺度數字孿生

16210526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16210526.value: Sinkholes are among the most severe geohazards, posing substantial threats to infrastructure, public safety, and economic sustainability worldwide. These phenomena arise from complex interactions between natural and human-induced factors, including groundwater extraction, internal soil erosion, geological weaknesses, and loading from urban development. In rapidly urbanizing regions, sinkholes are particularly unpredictable, and their sudden emergence can have catastrophic consequences. Despite the widespread use of monitoring techniques, their effectiveness remains limited due to incomplete spatial and temporal coverage, and uncertainties in interpreting subsurface indicators. From a computational perspective, existing models often fail to capture the highly nonlinear, multiscale, and multiphysics processes that drive sinkhole formation and evolution, particularly in environments with heterogeneous subsurfaces and complex fluid–soil-structure interactions. To address these limitations, the aim of the proposed research is to develop an innovative multiscale, multiphysics computational framework that can predict sinkhole initiation, progression, and associated risks with greater accuracy and efficiency. In this proposal, we will develop a multiscale, multiphysics digital twin system for prediction and risk assessment of urban sinkholes, using a tightly integrated framework comprising three components. First, macroscale hydro-mechanical modeling using the material point method will capture regional groundwater flow, stress redistribution, and large-scale deformation. This component will identify potential sinkhole-prone zones and provide initial and boundary conditions for mesoscale analysis. Second, fully resolved mesoscale CFD-DEM simulations will address fluid-particle-structure interactions within these critical zones, capturing key processes such as soil erosion, arching effects, and cavity collapse. These simulations will feed localized constitutive responses and failure mechanisms back into the macroscale model to enhance predictive accuracy. Finally, machine learning-based data integration and surrogate modeling will assimilate multisource information, including MPM outputs, CFD-DEM data, and field observations, to calibrate model parameters and train surrogate models. These models can either be embedded into MPM for hybrid simulation or serve directly as fast macroscale predictors of sinkhole initiation and evolution. The framework will be validated through laboratory experiments, field measurements, and analytical benchmarks to ensure reliability and generalizability. The outcomes of this research will deliver a robust digital twin system for sinkhole prediction, advancing fundamental understanding of coupled hydromechanical processes. Beyond geotechnical applications, the framework will be generalizable to address broader geohazard challenges, such as internal erosion in dams and coastal subsidence. This work will provide transformative tools for sustainable urban development, infrastructure resilience, and disaster risk mitigation, offering long-term benefits to both scientific research and engineering practice. 天坑是最嚴重的地質災害之一，對基礎設施、公共安全及全球經濟永續性構成重大威脅。此類現象源於自然因素與人為因素（包括地下水抽取、內部土壤沖蝕、地質弱帶及都市開發荷載）之間的複雜交互作用。在快速都市化的地區，天坑尤其難以預測，其突然發生可能帶來災難性後果。儘管監測技術已廣泛使用，但因空間與時間覆蓋範圍不完整，以及對地下指標解釋的不確定性，其有效性仍然有限。從計算角度來看，現有模型往往無法捕捉驅動天坑形成與演化的高度非線性、多尺度及多物理場過程，特別是在地下介質非均質且存在複雜流體–土壤–結構交互作用的環境中。為克服這些限制，本研究旨在發展一套創新的多尺度、多物理場計算框架，以更精確且更有效率地預測天坑的起始、進展及相關風險。 在本計畫中，我們將開發一套用於都市天坑預測與風險評估的多尺度、多物理場數位孿生系統，該系統採用緊密整合的三個組成部分。首先，使用物質點法進行巨觀水力–力學模擬，以捕捉區域地下水流、應力重新分佈及大尺度變形。此部分將識別潛在的天坑易發區，並為中尺度分析提供初始條件與邊界條件。其次，在中尺度關鍵區域內，將進行完全解析的CFD-DEM模擬，以處理流體–顆粒–結構交互作用，捕捉土壤沖蝕、拱效應及空洞崩塌等關鍵過程。這些模擬將把局部組成律響應與破壞機制回饋至巨觀模型，以提高預測精度。最後，基於機器學習的資料整合與代理模型建模將同化多來源資訊，包括MPM輸出、CFD-DEM數據及現場觀測資料，以校驗模型參數並訓練代理模型。這些代理模型可嵌入MPM中進行混合模擬，或直接作為天坑起始與演化的快速巨觀預測器。本框架將通過實驗室試驗、現場量測及解析基準進行驗證，以確保其可靠性與通用性。 本研究成果將提供一套穩健的天坑預測數位孿生系統，增進對耦合水力–力學過程的基礎理解。除了大地工程應用之外，該框架亦具有通用性，可推展至更廣泛的地質災害挑戰，例如壩體內部沖蝕與海岸地層下陷。本研究將為永續都市發展、基礎設施韌性及災害風險減緩提供變革性工具，對科學研究與工程實務帶來長期效益。

16211326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16211326.value: 全球地震滑坡風險快速評估

16211326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16211326.value: Earthquake-induced landslides are a significant global hazard in mountainous regions, causing substantial infrastructure damage, fatalities, and economic losses. For example, the 2015 Mw7.8 Gorkha earthquake in Nepal triggered 24,915 landslides and the 2008 Mw7.9 Wenchuan earthquake in China induced over 197,000 landslides that killed 6,727 people. However, existing landslide risk assessment models remain largely site-specific and slow to deploy. These devastating events underscore the urgent need for a rapid global landslide risk assessment system capable of supporting worldwide emergency response, infrastructure planning, and disaster preparedness. This proposed project will develop a multi-scale system for the rapid assessment of global earthquake-induced landslide risks. The system will provide rapid, quantitative evaluations of landslide hazards, including the locations, counts, sizes, and runout distances. In addition to hazard assessment, the system will evaluate the impacts of potential landslides on populations, infrastructure, river systems, and economies. It is designed to offer critical information to stakeholders ranging from emergency responders to engineers, urban planners, and the public. The key scientific challenges that will be addressed include: (1) advancing from qualitative susceptibility analysis to quantitative hazard assessment (e.g., determining locations, counts, sizes and runout distances) across local, regional, and global scales; (2) characterizing potential cascading hazards to support engineering design and risk mitigation; and (3) identifying global risk patterns and hotspots for future seismic scenarios. Four key deliverables are expected from the proposed project: (1) A multi-scale statistical framework for rapidly evaluating global earthquake-induced landslide locations, counts, sizes and runout distances. (2) A near-real-time risk assessment system capable of assessing the spatial distribution of landslide impacts, such as fatalities, economic losses, and transportation disruptions within an hour after a major earthquake. This system would allow stakeholders to understand the full picture of a disaster before ground-truth observations become available. (3) An overview of global earthquake-induced landslide risk patterns that identify historical hotspots and evaluate potential economic losses and fatalities from future earthquakes. Such information will inform disaster mitigation strategies and help prioritize response efforts and resource allocation in seismically active regions. (4) Risk-informed decision-making tools to enhance the resilience of critical infrastructure projects in earthquake-prone regions. The proposed rapid risk assessment system will significantly advance global earthquake-induced landslide risk assessments, enhance emergency response and disaster preparedness, save lives, reduce economic losses, and enhance the infrastructural resilience in seismically active areas. 地震滑坡是全球面臨的山區重大自然災害，常造成嚴重的人員傷亡、經濟損失及基礎設施破壞。例如，2015年Mw 7.8 級尼泊爾廓爾喀地震引發滑坡約 2.5 萬處；2008年Mw 7.9 級中國汶川地震誘發滑坡超 19.7 萬處，致 6,727 人死亡。然而，現有滑坡風險評估模型多局限於特定區域，且部署響應滯後，難以滿足全球應急響應、基礎設施規劃和防災減災的迫切需求。 本項目擬構建全球地震滑坡風險多尺度快速評估系統。系統不僅能對滑坡位置、數量、規模及運移距離進行快速定量評估（危險性評估），還能綜合評估其對人口、設施、水系與經濟的影響（風險評估），為救援決策、工程建設及公眾提供關鍵資訊支撐。 本項目擬解決的關鍵科學問題包括：（1）實現跨尺度（局地-區域-全球）由「定性易發性分析」向「定量危險性評估（滑坡位置、數量、規模與運移距離）」的跨越；（2）表徵潛在的鏈生災害，為工程設計與風險控制提供支撐；（3）識別未來地震情景下的全球風險格局與高風險區。 本項目預期取得以下四項關鍵成果：（1）多尺度統計框架：用於快速評估全球地震滑坡的位置、數量、規模與運移距離；（2）近即時風險評估系統：可在強震後 1 小時內估算人員傷亡、經濟損失及交通中斷的空間分布，實現無現場數據時的災情快速預測；（3）全球地震滑坡風險圖：用於識別歷史高風險區並評估未來地震的潛在損失，為制定防災減災策略及分配救援資源提供決策依據；（4）基於風險的決策工具：用於提升強震易發區關鍵基礎設施的抗災韌性。 本項目的實施將推動地震滑坡風險評估理論與技術的發展，提升應急響應與災害防範能力，減少人員傷亡與經濟損失，並增強地震活躍區基礎設施的抗災韌性。

16211526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16211526.value: 探索開放場景中跨模態對齊、編輯與生成的流匹配技術

16211526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16211526.value: Diffusion models, a powerful new family of models with astonishing visual generation ability, have revolutionized today's generative AI research. Unlike previous single-step generative models (such as GANs or VAEs), diffusion models utilize an iterative process: it first gradually adds noise to data through a forward process, and learns the reverse process in multiple small, denoising steps (i.e., multi-step). Following this idea, flow matching (FM) theory offers a simplified and more general framework by using linear interpolation to bridge any two distributions. Despite its theoretical versatility, current flow-based methods remain largely confined to generating images and videos from a standard noise distribution (e.g., Gaussian). In this proposal, we aim to unlock the broader potential of FM in handling various cross-modal tasks. We posit that beyond their multi-step nature, flow-based models possess several under-explored characteristics that are critical and helpful for multimodal understanding and generation tasks, 1) Compositional: Velocity vectors inherently possess a compositional nature, allowing for the combination of multiple velocities into a composite velocity. 2) Invertible: Unlike other uni-directional mapping functions, learned flows are naturally invertible: We can easily invert the learned velocities, to transform from the target distribution back to the source distribution. 3) Deterministic and Unique: In theory, a "perfect" probability-flow ODE ensures that each flow trajectory is deterministic and unique, with no intersections. Leveraging these properties, we will develop a series of novel flow-based approaches. Specifically, we will study four multimodal tasks from an easy-to-difficult manner: 1) We propose the first compositional zero-shot learning method based on the compositional nature of velocity fields. 2) We develop a new cross-modal retrieval paradigm based on its invertible characteristic. 3) We propose a consistent flow learning strategy for complex text-based visual editing. 4) We investigate the potential of flow matching in dynamic visual tokenization learning, and its application towards unified multimodal LLM. We anticipate that this research will establish a new foundation for flow-based models in multimodal AI, paving the way for next-generation content generation and understanding systems. 擴散模型作為一類強大的新型模型，憑藉其驚人的視覺生成能力，為當今的生成式人工智能研究帶來了革命性的變革。與以往的單步生成模型（如 GAN 或 VAE）不同，擴散模型採用的是一個疊代過程：它首先透過前向過程向數據中逐漸添加噪聲，並在多個微小的去噪步驟（即多步）中學習逆向過程。沿襲這一思路，流匹配（Flow Matching, FM）理論透過使用線性插值來連接任意兩個分佈，提供了一個更簡化且更具通用性的框架。儘管流匹配在理論上具有廣泛的通用性，但目前基於流的方法很大程度上仍侷限於從標準噪聲分佈（例如高斯分佈）生成圖像和影片。 在本提案中，我們旨在釋放流匹配在處理各種跨模態任務中的更大潛力。我們認為，除了多步特性之外，基於流的模型還擁有若干尚未被充分探索的特性，這些特性對於多模態理解與生成任務至關重要且大有裨益： 1. 可組合性： 速度向量本質上具有可組合的特性，允許將多個速度組合成一個複合速度。 2. 可逆性： 與其他單向映射函數不同，學習到的流天然具有可逆性：我們可以輕鬆地反轉學習到的速度，從而由目標分佈變換回源分佈。 3. 確定性與唯一性： 在理論上，一個“完美”的概率流常微分方程能確保每條流軌跡都是確定且唯一的，彼此不會相交。 利用這些特性，我們將開發一系列全新的基於流的方法。具體而言，我們將按照由易到難的方式研究四個多模態任務：1) 利用速度場的可組合特性，提出首個基於流的可組合零樣本學習方法；2) 基於其可逆特性，開發一種全新的跨模態檢索範式；3) 針對複雜的基於文本的視覺編輯，提出一種一致性流學習策略；4) 探討流匹配在動態視覺Token化學習中的潛力，及其在統一多模態大模型中的應用。我們預計這項研究將為多模態 AI 中的基於流的模型奠定新的基礎，為下一代內容生成與理解系統開闢道路。

16213126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16213126.value: 基於智能體人工智能與擴散大型語言模型的時序推理

16213126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213126.value: Time series data underpin high-stakes decisions across finance, energy, transportation, and industrial operations; yet, most deployed models remain sophisticated time series pattern matchers. This project advances a new paradigm of time series reasoning, moving beyond "System 1" fast pattern matching to "System 2" reasoning that decomposes tasks, integrates domain knowledge with numerical evidence, and exposes explicit intermediate steps. By generating natural-language rationales tied to executable computations, our approach enables auditability, improves trust and actionability, and aligns explanations with the operations that produced them. We identify three obstacles towards time series reasoning: (1) Large language models (LLMs) are optimized for discrete tokens, whereas time series are often continuous and numerically precise; (2) Real-world time series exhibit auto-correlation, seasonality, and multi-scale structure, making time series LLMs and time series diffusion models ineffective and slow during inference; (3) Time series often co-occur with text and images that are early, late, or irrelevant. Latent alignment without lead-lag handling can promote spurious correlations and lead to brittle decisions. We address these challenges via an integrated architecture with three novelties: (i) Agentic architecture for time series reasoning: Instead of a single monolithic model, the project will build a modular, agent-based system that decomposes tasks and selects the right tool for each subproblem; (ii) Diffusion LLMs (dLLMs) for time series: Instead of using LLMs and diffusion models, we adapt diffusion large language models, which are traditionally designed for the generation of text, to continuous sequences using hybrid representations (vector-quantized local codes plus residual continuous channels) and parallel, bidirectional denoising over multiple temporal rates; (iii) Lag-aware, gated cross-modal alignment: A backbone-agnostic module that performs differentiable lag search and learns to abstain when auxiliary signals are noisy, optimizing for causal utility rather than mere correlation. 時間序列數據支撐著金融、能源、交通和工業運營中的高風險決策；然而，大多數已部署的模型仍然只是複雜的時間序列模式匹配器。本項目推進了一種新的時間序列推理範式，從「系統 1」快速模式匹配邁向「系統 2」推理，後者能夠分解任務、將領域知識與數值證據相結合，並展示顯式的中間步驟。通過生成與可執行計算相關聯的自然語言合理化解釋，我們的方法實現了可審計性，提高了信任度和可操作性，並使解釋與產生它們的運營操作相一致。我們指出了實現時間序列推理的三大障礙：（1）大語言模型（LLM）針對離散 Token 進行了優化，而時間序列通常是連續且數值精確的；（2）現實世界的時間序列表現出自相關性、季節性和多尺度結構，導致時間序列 LLM 和時間序列擴散模型在推理過程中效果不佳且速度緩慢；（3）時間序列通常與超前、滯後或不相關的文本和圖像共同出現。在不處理超前-滯後關係的情況下進行隱空間對齊，可能會促進虛假關聯並導致脆弱的決策。我們通過一個具有三項創新的集成架構來解決這些挑戰：（i）用於時間序列推理的架構：該項目將構建一個模塊化的系統，而不是單一的龐大單體模型，該系統可以分解任務並為每個子問題選擇合適的工具；（ii）用於時間序列的擴散大語言模型：我們不直接使用 LLM 和擴散模型，而是將傳統上設計用於文本生成的擴散大語言模型進行改造，使其通過在並行、雙向去噪來適應連續序列；（iii）通過使用可微分、感知滯後且帶門控的跨模態對齊機制，搜索並學習不同模態間的時間滯後，從而即使在輔助信號含有噪聲時也能提升性能。

16213326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16213326.value: 基于生成与理解三维物体的统一学习表达

16213326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213326.value: This project seeks to advance the generation and understanding of 3D objects, a major technology development in modern 3D assets creation across digital entertainment, virtual reality and industrial design. Although the very rapid progress in 2D images and 1D language generative modeling have been made, achieving a unified framework for 3D object generation and understanding is still an open problem. The complex and diverse representations of 3D data pose the challenges for learning while scaling, as each computable representation involves the trade-off between the fidelity of detailed geometries, the spatial coherence, and the computability. Consequently, the current 3D generative models struggle to produce fine geometry details in sufficient resolution, to enable editing, or to maintain consistency across different input modalities. For these limitations, we identify the two key challenges for 3D generation: the non-unified 3D representations in both raw data and variational autoencoder latent space, and the not-well-understood conditional mechanisms involving different nature of the paired data. To address these challenges, we perform watertight data preprocessing and introduce two novel 3D representations to establish an effective generative architecture. First, a flexible cube voxel grid captures non-axis-aligned sharp features and supports local geometry editing. A variational autoencoder compresses this representation by enabling a probabilistic modeling in latent space via diffusion. Second, a sparse signed-distance function voxel grid offers higher memory efficiency while preserving essential geometry details, with a dedicated 3D sparse convolutional variational autoencoder achieving the state-of-the-art reconstruction quality. In addition to geometry, we extend the architecture to learning material property directly on 3D surfaces. By conditioning on the surface, our texture generation model ensures realistic and consistent appearance, mitigating therefore the common inconsistencies in the existing approaches. The generation is fundamental in completing a reconstruction, which is never sufficiently complete for the finite input data. Though a generative model produces more complete, it is often less view-consistent. To balance this trade-off, our framework can integrate reconstruction into 3D generative modeling through conditioning, enhancing geometry reasoning from input views, completing missing structures, and leveraging pretrained 2D and 3D priors to improve the spatial understanding and visual alignment. This enables the generation of 3D objects that are both geometrically complete and visually consistent with incomplete observed views. By unifying the understanding, generation, and reconstruction of 3D objects within a unified framework, this project takes a significant step toward holistic 3D world modeling and the advancement of the spatial intelligence. 该项目旨在推进3D物体的生成与理解。这是一项关键的技术进展，对数字娱乐、虚拟现实和工业设计中的现代3D资产创作至关重要。尽管2D图像和1D语言生成模型已经取得了突飞猛进的进展，但实现一个统一的3D物体生成与理解框架仍是一个亟待解决的难题。3D数据复杂且多样化的表达形式给大规模学习带来了挑战，因为每种可计算的表达形式都需要在精细几何体的逼真度、空间连贯性以及可计算性之间做出权衡。因此，目前的3D生成模型难以产出足够分辨率的精细几何细节，无法实现编辑，也难以在不同的输入模态之间保持一致性。针对这些局限性，我们确定了3D生成的两个关键挑战：原始数据与变分自编码器（VAE）潜空间中不统一的3D表达形式，以及涉及不同性质配对数据的条件机制尚未被充分理解。 为了应对这些挑战，我们进行了水密（watertight）数据预处理，并引入了两种新颖的3D表达形式，以建立高效的生成架构。首先，一种柔性的立方体体素网格（cube voxel grid）能够捕捉非轴对齐的尖锐特征，并支持局部几何编辑。变分自编码器压缩该表达形式，从而能够通过扩散模型在潜空间中进行概率建模。其次，稀疏带符号距离函数（SDF）体素网格在保持核心几何细节的同时，提供了更高的内存效率，并配合专用的3D稀疏卷积变分自编码器实现了行业领先（SOTA）的重建质量。除几何结构外，我们还将该架构扩展到直接在3D表面上学习材质属性。通过以表面为条件，我们的纹理生成模型确保了逼真且一致的外观，从而缓解了现有方法中常见的冲突问题。 生成是完成重建的基础，而由于输入数据有限，重建永远无法做到足够完整。虽然生成模型能产生更完整的结构，但其视角连贯性通常较差。为了平衡这种权衡，我们的框架可以通过条件机制将重建整合到3D生成建模中，从而增强输入视角的几何推理能力，补全缺失结构，并利用预训练的2D和3D先验来提升空间理解和视觉对齐。这使得生成的3D物体既具有几何完整性，又在视觉上与不完整的观测视角保持一致。通过将3D物体的理解、生成和重建整合到一个统一的框架中，该项目向全面3D世界建模和空间智能的发展迈出了重要一步。

16213426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16213426.value: 利用金屬–生物炭催化將生物質廢物轉化為可持續航空燃料

16213426.label: Co - Investigator(s)
16213426.value: Prof Yeung, King Lun Prof Yuan, Xiangzhou

16213426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213426.value: Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is widely recognized as a promising pathway to aviation decarbonization. Singapore, Malaysia, and Japan have all implemented the SAF blending mandate. As announced in its Climate Action Plan 2050, Hong Kong will attempt to reduce carbon emissions by 50% before 2035. The requirement for airlines to use SAF at Hong Kong International Airport has been accelerated, e.g., the Cathay Group has set a target of incorporating SAF into 10% of its overall consumption by 2030. Although waste oils and animal fats account for ~70% of global SAF production, their regional supply is currently limited. This situation highlights the urgent need to diversify feedstock sources and develop efficient conversion technologies tailored to these alternatives. Lignocellulosic biomass offers a regionally accessible feedstock for SAF production. However, its heterogeneous composition introduces challenges for efficient processing and consistent quality. To innovate the biomass-to-SAF production pathway, this project will develop highly adaptive processing via artificial intelligence (AI)-empowered catalysis, with metal–biochar as the target class of catalytic materials, building on the PI’s expertise in biochar engineering and Co-I’s expertise on AI and green catalysis. Biochar, a product of carbon fixation through wood waste pyrolysis locally in Hong Kong, can reduce up to 3.3 kg of CO2 per kg, thus further cutting SAF’s carbon footprint. Using machine learning (ML), we will model metal–biochar catalyst properties to guide adaptive designs that cater for variability in SAF feedstock. By streamlining material screening processes, we can improve the design of efficient catalysts while reducing trial-and-error experimentation required for SAF production. The project will be conducted in four interlinked phases—(1) development of ML models for biochar synthesis and catalytic performance evaluation; guiding (2) catalyst fabrication, multiscale characterization, and validation in hydrodeoxygenation reactions of bio-oils obtained from hydrothermal liquefaction of horticultural waste and spent coffee grounds; followed by mechanistic investigation with (3) in-situ analysis and computational chemistry to provide a rigorous scientific foundation for ML findings; and supported by (4) life-cycle and technoeconomic assessments to evaluate sustainability merits in comparison with existing SAF routes. We will uncover key design principles for upgrading diverse bio-oils and guide smarter catalyst development and feedstock selection to stabilize processes and SAF products against variability in feedstock. Our project outcomes will promote lignocellulosic SAF as a long-term, scalable solution. 可持續航空燃料（Sustainable Aviation Fuel, SAF）被廣泛視為推動航空業減碳的重要途徑。隨着亞洲多個經濟體加快SAF的政策部署，以及香港持續推進航空業低碳轉型，業界對可持續航空燃料的需求預期將持續增長。現有SAF主要依賴廢食用油及動物脂肪等脂質原料，但其區域供應有限，難以滿足長期增長的需求，因此亟需拓展可持續原料來源並發展相應的高效轉化技術。木質纖維素生物質在本地及區域內來源廣泛，具有作為SAF替代原料的潛力；然而，其組成差異及季節性波動會影響轉化效率和產品質量的一致性。 本項目將以金屬–生物炭催化劑為核心，建立人工智能輔助的自適應生物質–SAF轉化策略。生物炭可由香港本地木材廢物熱解製備，兼具固碳潛力以及可調控的孔隙結構和表面化學特性，可作為金屬活性位點的穩定載體。項目將利用機器學習（Machine Learning, ML）建立金屬–生物炭催化劑性質與催化性能的預測模型，識別影響反應的關鍵材料特徵及操作參數，從而因應不同生物質原料的組成變化優化催化劑設計，並減少傳統試錯式材料篩選。 研究將分為四個相互關聯的階段：(1) 建立用於生物炭合成及催化性能評估的ML模型；(2) 製備並進行多尺度表徵金屬–生物炭催化劑，利用園藝廢物及廢咖啡渣經水熱液化所得的生物油進行加氫脫氧反應驗證；(3) 結合原位分析及計算化學，闡明催化活性位點、界面反應和反應機理，為ML預測提供科學依據；以及(4) 通過生命周期評估及技術經濟評估，與現有SAF生產路徑比較其環境及經濟可持續性。 本項目將揭示不同生物油升級過程中的關鍵催化劑設計原理，並建立更智能的催化劑設計與原料選擇策略，以降低生物質原料波動對轉化過程及SAF產品一致性的影響，從而為木質纖維素生物質轉化為可持續航空燃料提供具科學基礎、可適應原料變異並具有長期規模化潛力的技術路徑。

16213526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16213526.value: 面向視覺-語言模型應用且能耗受限的無人機任務規劃的邊緣計算

16213526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213526.value: Low-altitude Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly being deployed for complex tasks, e.g., payload delivery that requires onboard video understanding. For example, in a precision environmental remediation application (e.g., by Zenatech), a UAV will fly in an area to disperse remediation payloads (e.g., Algaecides). This mission requests for searching for the disperse locations in this area that maximize the remediation effectiveness. UAVs need to hover in a location to capture a video sequence, perform reasoning with vision-language models (VLMs) to identify the growth of algal blooms, and make disperse decisions. Similar applications include oil spill relief, invasive species management, and precision agriculture. UAVs are critically limited in their battery resources. The energy consumption of UAVs is influenced by the flight trajectory. In particular, UAVs need to hover to capture a video of certain length; so that video-language analysis can explore the long-term temporal dependencies within the video sequence. A longer observation period increases the accuracy; yet this also requires a longer hovering period and more energy; thus restricting the coverage of future areas. The energy consumption of UAVs is also affected by weather; in particular, wind can have an impact of 40%. The UAV mission planning requires onboard computing and potential interactions with the cloud, a typical edge-computing scenario. Current UAVs are equipped with edge computing hardware and software platforms. However, existing edge-computing frameworks, UAV mission planning algorithms, and wind forecasting models; are insufficient to support the new UAV applications. In this project, we plan to develop EdgeVLM-UAV (Edge Computing for UAVs with VLM applications), a new edge-computing framework for UAVs with missions that involve VLM-based applications. We will develop new (1) edge-cloud vision-language analysis algorithms that is computing and communication efficient. We plan to develop algorithms based on scene-graph to efficiently explore long-term temporal dependencies, (2) wind forecasting models. We plan to explore the recent weather foundation models (e.g., GraphCast from Google, Pangu from Huawei, etc.) and develop new models through physics-informed knowledge distillation techniques, and (3) mission planning algorithms. We plan to develop algorithms on the UAV trajectory given energy constraints. Given the uncertainty from the wind forecasting, we further develop robust mission planning algorithms. Our project proposes new edge computing problems and develops new techniques on weather foundation model distillation, scene-graph-based algorithms, and robust optimization algorithms.
