We will implement an open source EdgeVLM-UAV prototype, evaluate EdgeVLM-UAV through simulators, e.g., AirSim from Microsoft, and enhance existing software platforms. 低空無人機（UAV）正越來越多地被部署用於執行複雜任務，例如需要機載視訊理解能力的負載投放任務。以Zenatech所進行的精準環境修復應用為例，無人機需在特定區域飛行並投放修復藥劑（如除藻劑）；此任務要求無人機在區域內尋找能達到最佳修復效果的投放點。具體而言，無人機需要在特定位置懸停以採集視訊序列，利用視覺-語言模型（VLM）進行推理以識別藻類水華的生長情況，並據此做出投放決策。類似的應用場景還包括溢油緊急處置、入侵物種治理以及精準農業。 無人機的電池資源極為有限，其能耗受飛行軌跡影響。具體而言，無人機需要懸停以拍攝特定時長的視頻，從而支持視頻-語言分析技術挖掘視頻序列中的長期時間依賴關係。觀測時長越長，分析準確度越高，但這同時也意味著更長的懸停時間和更高的能耗，進而限制了無人機對後續區域的覆蓋能力。此外，天氣狀況也會影響無人機的能耗，尤其是風力因素，其影響幅度可達40%。無人機任務規劃涉及機載運算以及與雲端的潛在交互，屬於典型的邊緣運算應用場景。儘管目前的無人機已配備邊緣運算軟硬體平台，但現有的邊緣運算框架、任務規劃演算法及風力預測模型，已無法滿足新型無人機應用的需求。 本計畫旨在開發 EdgeVLM-UAV（面向搭載 VLM 應用的無人機邊緣運算框架），這是一個專為執行涉及視覺語言模型（VLM）相關任務的無人機而設計的新型邊緣運算框架。我們將開發以下內容：(1) 兼具計算與通訊效率的邊緣-雲協同視覺語言分析演算法，計劃利用基於場景圖（scene-graph）的演算法來高效挖掘長時序依賴關係；(2) 風力預測模型，計劃探索最新的氣象基礎模型（如 Google 的 GraphCast、華為的「盤古餾」等），並透過物理研究開發新的知識模型；(3)任務規劃演算法，計劃在考慮能量限制的前提下開發無人機軌跡規劃演算法，並針對風力預測的不確定性，進一步開發穩健的任務規劃演算法。 本計畫提出了一系列新的邊緣運算問題，並針對氣象基礎模型蒸餾、基於場景圖的演算法以及穩健最佳化演算法開發了新技術。我們將實現一個開源的 EdgeVLM-UAV 原型系統，利用模擬器（如微軟的 AirSim）進行評估，並對現有軟體平台進行改進。

16214126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16214126.value: 面向大語言模型的多芯片混合推測解碼可重構存算一體處理器

16214126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16214126.value: Large Language Models (LLMs) have revolutionized the AI field, enabling machines to understand and generate human language. However, the autoregressive decoding nature of LLMs leads to repeated model loading with high inference latency and energy. This poses a significant bottleneck for deploying LLMs on resource-constrained devices. Computing-in-Memory (CIM) is a promising architecture that reduces data movement by performing computation inside memory, but it alone cannot fully resolve the latency and energy issues in LLM decoding. Algorithm innovations offer two promising directions: Speculative decoding uses a small draft language model (DLM) to predict multiple tokens and verifies them in parallel with the large target language model (TLM), reducing the number of TLM executions. Meanwhile, quantization techniques like vector quantization (VQ) can drastically reduce the loaded modelsize. Our preliminary study identifies that a mixed-quantization scheme with uniform quantization (UQ) for DLM and VQ for TLM can balance model loading reduction and speculation quality. However, implementing this scheme on CIM processors faces challenges in CIM architecture, performance scaling, and processor scheduling: 1) Conventional CIM architectures are designed for UQ and lack efficient support for VQ. 2) The performance gain of speculative decoding is limited by draft token rejection and frequent off-chip memory access. 3) Existing processors lack the scheduling flexibility for diverse DLM-TLM pairs. This project proposes a reconfigurable CIM-based LLM processor with multi-chip hybrid speculative decoding (HSD) to address these challenges. Three tasks will be completed: 1) [Reconfigurable CIM Architecture] Design a dual-mode reconfigurable CIM macro supporting both UQ and VQ. Develop an intra-core spatial grouping architecture and an inter-core search-compute pipeline to maximize VQ throughput. 2) [Multi-Chip HSD System] Develop an HSD scheme that dynamically optimizes the draft strategy. Implement a memory-compute-coupling multi-chip mapping approach and a workload-decoupled HSD controller for efficient multi-chip execution. 3) [Processor and Verification] Design and fabricate the HSD-based LLM processor. Develop an automated CIM explorer and a scheduling framework for model mapping. Validate the proposed techniques using a fabricated chip and a multi-chip verification system. The completion of this project will establish a cross-stack co-design methodology that integrates algorithm and hardware innovations to realize high-performance and energy-efficient LLM processors. The proposed technology will significantly contribute to the AI computing infrastructure, enabling advanced intelligent applications on edge devices in Hong Kong and beyond. Beyond academia, the proposed technology will significantly contribute to the AI computing infrastructure, fostering intelligent applications across various domains in Hong Kong and globally. 大語言模型（LLM）已深刻改變人工智能領域，使機器能夠理解並生成人類語言。然而，LLM的自回歸解碼機制導致模型參數反覆加載，帶來嚴重的推論延遲與能耗開銷，成為部署於資源受限設備上的主要瓶頸。存算一體（CIM）通過在存儲器內部完成計算，可有效減少數據搬移，但僅靠CIM架構本身無法完全解決LLM解碼階段的延遲與能耗問題。 算法層面的創新提供了兩個重要方向：推測解碼利用小型草稿語言模型（DLM）預測多個詞元，再由大型目標語言模型（TLM）並行驗證，從而減少TLM的執行次數；同時，向量量化（VQ）等壓縮技術可大幅降低模型加載量。前期研究發現，對DLM採用均勻量化（UQ）、對TLM採用VQ的混合量化方案，能在降低模型加載量與維持推測質量之間取得良好平衡。然而，將該方案部署於CIM處理器仍面臨三大挑戰：1）傳統CIM架構通常針對UQ設計，缺乏對VQ的高效支持；2）推測解碼的性能增益受制於草稿詞元的拒絕率與頻繁的片外訪存；3）現有處理器缺乏應對多樣化DLM-TLM組合的調度靈活性。 本項目將提出一種支持多芯片混合推測解碼（HSD）的可重構存算一體LLM處理器，通過三項任務解決上述挑戰：1）可重構CIM架構：設計支持UQ與VQ雙模可重構的CIM宏單元，開發核內空間分組架構與核間搜索-計算流水線，最大化VQ吞吐率；2）多芯片HSD系統：開發動態優化推測解碼策略的HSD方案，實現存算耦合的多芯片映射方法與任務解耦的HSD控制器，以支持高效多芯片執行；3）處理器設計與驗證：設計並流片實現基於HSD的LLM處理器，開發自動化CIM探索工具與模型映射調度框架，利用流片芯片與多芯片驗證系統對所提技術進行全面驗證。 本項目的完成將建立一套涵蓋算法與硬體創新的跨層級協同設計方法，推動高性能高能效LLM處理器的實現。本項目所提出的技術將顯著促進AI計算基礎設施建設，為香港乃至全球邊緣智能應用提供有力支撐。

16214326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16214326.value: 用於可程式化螺旋度顯示器的手性鈣鈦礦界面

16214326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16214326.value: Despite rapid progress in chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) emitters, there is no room-temperature, magnet-free platform that can electrically programme photon helicity at the pixel scale. Prior circularly polarised electroluminescence (CP-EL) demonstrations typically fix handedness and rely on large devices. Here, we target true programmability: left/right helicity switched electrically in III-V micro-LED pixels and scaled to uniform arrays. To achieve this, our route couples transparent, defect-minimal chiral-perovskite injectors to micro-LED stacks, so spin-polarised carriers are generated via CISS and read as CP-EL without sacrificing brightness or colour. Our team’s expertise in vacuum-evaporated perovskite growth, polarimetric imaging, and micro-LED commercialisation positions us to deliver a manufacturable platform. As near-term context, Omdia projects micro-LED display shipments will reach 34.6 million units by 2031, driven by applications in extended reality and smartwatches. This growth presents a promising entry point for implementing pixel-level helicity control. We hypothesise that oriented chiral 2D-perovskite injectors provide CISS spin filtering, while interfacial dipole passivators stabilise band alignment, enabling room-temperature CP-EL flipped on demand. We will form optically neutral, Fermi-level-equilibrated contacts by facet-directed co-evaporation and vapour-phase passivation that suppresses traps while preserving chirality and retaining micro-LED advantages: high luminance, nanosecond switching, and dense pixelation. At the single-pixel level, we map how the degree of circular polarisation (DOCP) evolves with bias, wavelength, and temperature; time-resolved EL/photoluminescence and Hanle measurements separate recombination from spin randomisation to extract the spin lifetime. Ultimately, we will realise electrically programmable pixels by patterning dual-domain R/S enantiomer-specific injectors with independent contacts for addressable arrays using a multiplexed driver. All performance will be referenced to 100 candela per square metre in luminance, a display-relevant brightness that prevents inflated polarisation at dim output. For single pixels, we target a DOCP of 20~30 per cent, producing separable left/right states that exceed polarimetric uncertainty and optics bias. We will toggle helicity at least 60 hertz with a change in DOCP greater than ten percentage points per electrical flip. In arrays, we target tight per-pixel DOCP with negligible optical/electrical crosstalk so that each pixel can be addressed independently. We will test our devices over one million toggles across a calibrated thermal range to demonstrate robustness. By meeting the display-relevant operating point, this platform becomes a practical building block for high-brightness displays, polarisation-encoded links, and on-chip photonic processing, transforming spin control into manufacturable micro-LED tiles.

16214626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16214626.value: 範德華鐵電體中極化耦合熱與載流子傳輸的應變梯度工程研究

16214626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16214626.value: Van der Waals ferroelectrics (vdW FEs) enable transformative advances in low-power logic, flexible electronics, and polarization caloritronics exploiting ferrons—collective polarization fluctuations that carry dipole and heat. High-performance devices demand precise control of thermal conductivity (κ) and carrier dynamics, which are strain-sensitive and critically influenced by ubiquitous thermomechanical strains and flexoelectric excitations under operational conditions. Although strain gradients (∇ε) powerfully control polar order via flexocoupling (polarization-∇ε bidirectional interaction), how polarization couples to thermal and carrier transport under strain fields remains unexplored in vdW FEs. Systematic experimental studies on how ∇ε alter ferron and phonon contributions to κ, and how polarization mediates phonon-carrier scattering under ∇ε, are entirely absent. First-principles predictive frameworks linking κ and carrier dynamics to polarization variation under ∇ε and electric fields are likewise lacking. These combined experimental and theoretical gaps critically hinder thermal design for strain-engineered devices. This proposal experimentally explores ∇ε effects on κ and phonon-carrier coupling in symmetry-contrasting vdW FEs (α-In2Se3, NbOX2, 3R-MoS2) through spatially-resolved phonon spectroscopic and thermal measurements, while building continuum and first-principles models to achieve predictive understanding of κ-polarization coupling and carrier-phonon interplay under strain engineering. We will integrate programmable strain platforms (patterned-substrate imprinting, bending, wrinkling) with spatially-resolved frequency-domain thermoreflectance, Raman, ultrafast coherent phonon spectroscopy, and polarization mapping under controlled ∇ε and electric fields. Kinetic continuum Landau-Ginzburg-Devonshire-Khalatnikov-Tani (LGD-KT) models with flexocoupling—established for FE electromechanics but never applied to thermal transport—will be combined with Boltzmann transport equation (BTE), offering a framework with physical clarity for predicting ferronic κ. First-principles simulations will systematically compute ∇ε and field dependent κ, scattering rates, and carrier lifetimes for curved vdW FE device. We will introduce mode-resolved polarization weights to decompose polar phonon contributions to κ. Our preliminary work establishes the foundation: deterministic strain control via patterned-substrate imprinting achieved 33-50% κ suppression in bent MoS2 films; coherent phonon spectroscopy resolved unique resonantly enhanced soft transverse-optic modes in NbOCl2; first-principles calculations revealed distinctive 36-67% κ reduction and strengthened electron-phonon coupling under controlled ∇ε in α-In2Se3 and NbOI2; LGD-KT modeling fitted to first-principles data captured phonon softening due to flexocoupling in CuInP2S6. This work will deliver foundational understanding of polarization-thermal-mechanical coupling in vdW FEs, enabling electronic-thermal co-design of strain-engineered devices for ultralow-power ferroelectric logic with tunable thermal management and polarization caloritronics. 範德華鐵電體（vdW FEs）利用鐵子（攜帶偶極矩與熱量的集體極化漲落），為低功耗邏輯器件、柔性電子器件及極化熱電學（卡路里電子學）帶來了變革性突破。高性能器件亟需對熱導率（κ）與載流子動力學進行精準調控，而兩者對應變高度敏感，且在工作條件下極易受到泛在的熱機械應變與撓曲電激發的顯著影響。儘管應變梯度（∇ε）可通過撓曲耦合（極化與 ∇ε 的雙向相互作用）強效調控極化有序，但在應變場下極化如何與熱及載流子傳輸發生耦合，在範德華鐵電體中仍屬空白。關於 ∇ε 如何改變鐵子和聲子對 κ 的貢獻，以及極化在 ∇ε 下如何介導聲子-載流子散射，目前完全缺乏系統性的實驗研究；同樣，將 κ 和載流子動力學與 ∇ε 及電場下極化演變相聯繫的第一性原理預測框架亦付諸闕如。上述實驗與理論空白，嚴重阻礙了應變工程器件的熱設計。本項目旨在通過空間分辨的聲子光譜和熱測量，實驗探索具有對稱性對比的範德華鐵電體（α-In₂Se₃、NbOX₂、3R-MoS₂）中 ∇ε 對 κ 及聲子-載流子耦合的影響；同時構建連續介質與第一性原理模型，以實現對應變工程下 κ-極化耦合及載流子-聲子相互作用的預測性理解。我們將把可編程應變平台（圖案化襯底壓印、彎曲、起皺）與受控 ∇ε 及電場下的空間分辨頻域熱反射（FDTR）、拉曼光譜、超快相干聲子光譜及極化映射相結合。項目將首次把包含撓曲耦合的動態連續介質 Landau-Ginzburg-Devonshire-Khalatnikov-Tani（LGD-KT）模型（該模型在鐵電電機械學中已成熟應用，但此前從未用於熱傳輸研究）與玻爾茲曼輸運方程（BTE）相結合，為預測鐵子熱導率 κ 提供一個物理圖像清晰的理論框架。第一性原理計算將系統模擬彎曲範德華鐵電器件中依賴於 ∇ε 和電場的 κ、散射率及載流子壽命。我們還將引入模態分辨的極化權重，以解耦極性聲子對 κ 的貢獻。項目組的前期工作奠定了堅實基礎：通過圖案化襯底壓印實現了確定性應變調控，在彎曲 MoS₂ 薄膜中實現了 33-50% 的 κ 抑制；相干聲子光譜解析出 NbOCl₂ 中獨特的共振增強軟橫塊光學模（TO 模）；第一性原理計算揭示了 α-In₂Se₃ 和 NbOI₂ 在受控 ∇ε 下顯著降低 36-67% 的 κ 以及增強的電子-聲子耦合；基於第一性原理數據擬合的 LGD-KT 模型成功捕捉到 CuInP₂S₆ 中因撓曲耦合引起的聲子軟化。本項目將提供範德華鐵電體中極化-熱-機械耦合的基本物理理解，為應變工程器件實現電子-熱協同設計鋪平道路，從而助力開發具有可調控熱管理功能、基於極化熱電學的超低功耗鐵電邏輯器件。

16214726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16214726.value: 面向边缘开放域自适应机器人作业的弹性VLA模型服务

16214726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16214726.value: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are transforming embodied intelligence by enabling robots to perceive, reason, and act through multimodal understanding of their environments. Unlike conventional task-specific systems, VLA-based robots are expected to operate in open-ended scenarios, where task objectives, object properties, and environmental contexts evolve continuously. This shift toward open-ended robotic manipulation presents unprecedented opportunities for autonomous service, manufacturing, and assistive robotics. Yet, achieving such autonomy at the edge—where computation is constrained but proximity to data offers low latency and privacy advantages—introduces critical challenges for model serving, adaptation, and reliability. In open-ended edge environments, robotic tasks are characterized by high uncertainty and variability, demanding VLA models that can flexibly adapt to new instructions and conditions without the need for extensive re-training. Traditional end-to-end trained VLAs, while powerful, often fail to generalize under such evolving data distributions. Their reasoning process, primarily anchored in the language domain, further limits efficiency and overlooks spatial reasoning inherent in visual inputs. Moreover, edge-native deployment must contend with heterogeneous hardware capabilities, fluctuating resources, and unstable communication links, all of which hinder consistent inference. In addition, edge robots’ exposure to dynamic multimodal inputs and user interactions raises significant security and safety concerns, amplifying the need for resilient defense mechanisms. This proposal aims to develop an elastic VLA model serving framework for open-ended and adaptive edge robotic manipulation. The framework integrates retrieval-augmented reasoning to dynamically incorporate external demonstrations and contextual knowledge, enhancing adaptability to novel tasks. The framework introduces prompt-based elastic knowledge learning to strengthen spatial-temporal reasoning on demand, and latent multimodal reasoning to integrate visual insights efficiently into the inference process. In addition, it further employs multimodal latent reasoning and stage-wise distributed coordination to balance resources and sustain low-latency inference under edge constraints. To ensure safe operation, a self-introspective defense mechanism will detect and elastically mitigate open-world vulnerabilities during robotic inference. By unifying elasticity across knowledge, reasoning, and defense, this research seeks to establish a scalable and trustworthy foundation for open-ended edge intelligence. The outcomes will enable embodied agents to autonomously perform diverse manipulation tasks with robustness, efficiency, and safety in dynamic real-world environments. 视觉-语言-动作（Vision-Language-Action, VLA）模型通过对环境的跨模态理解，使机器人能够具备感知、推理和执行能力，从而正在深刻改变具身智能的技术格局。与传统的特定任务系统不同，基于 VLA 的机器系统被期望在开放域（Open-ended）场景下运行，在此类场景中，任务目标、物体属性以及环境上下文均处于持续变化之中。这种向开放域机器人作业的范式转变，为自主服务、智能制造及辅助机器人领域带来了前所未有的机遇。然而，在边缘端实现此类作业自主性—即在计算资源受限但靠近数据源（具备低时延与隐私保护优势）的环境中—对模型的服务部署、自适应能力与可靠性提出了严峻挑战。 在开放域边缘环境中，机器人作业任务具有极高的不确定性与多变性，这要求 VLA 模型能够在无需大规模重新训练的前提下，灵活自适应全新的指令与环境条件。传统的端到端训练虽然功能强大，但在面对不断演化的数据分布时往往难以有效泛化；同时，其推理过程主要锚定在语言域，这不仅限制了计算效率，也忽视了视觉输入中固有的空间推理能力。此外，边缘原生部署必须应对异构硬件算力、波动资源容量以及不稳定通信链路等客观限制，这些因素严重阻碍了持续稳健的推理服务。不仅如此，边缘机器人暴露于动态多模态输入与人机交互环境中，带来了显著的安全与隐私隐患，进一步放大了对弹性防御机制的迫切需求。 针对上述挑战，本项目旨在构建一个面向边缘开放域自适应机器人作业的弹性 VLA 模型服务框架。该框架融合了检索增强推理，动态引入外部示教数据与上下文知识，从而大幅提升对新任务的自适应能力；提出了基于提示词的弹性知识学习以按需增强时空推理能力，并引入隐空间多模态推理，将视觉感知高效融入推理链中。同时，本项目进一步采用多模态隐空间推理与分阶段分布式协同，在边缘资源约束下实现算力平衡并保障低时延推理。为确保运行安全，本项目设计了自反思/自省防御机制，用于在推理过程中实时检测并弹性化解开放世界下的安全漏洞。通过统一知识、推理与防御三个层面的弹性机制，本研究致力于为开放域边缘智能奠定可扩展且可信赖的技术根基。项目成果将使具身智能体能够在动态复杂的现实世界环境中，具备高鲁棒性、高效率与高安全性地自主完成多样化的作业任务。

16215026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16215026.value: 數據導向的動態可調控帶電界面特異性離子效應研究框架

16215026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16215026.value: Ions are essential to life and technology, yet their behaviour near charged surfaces often defies classical electrostatic expectations. Ions of identical charge can produce opposite effects depending on their size, hydration, and affinity for interfaces. These specific ion effects determine selectivity and efficiency in energy storage, desalination, and iontronic devices, but remain difficult to predict because existing studies generally rely on isolated observations under non-comparable conditions. Our recent work revealed that electrical control can actively reshape interfacial water and, in turn, influence ion transport. Using multilayered graphene membranes with precisely tuneable nanoconfinement, we discovered that negative gate voltages of certain intensity reorganise interfacial water, restructuring ion clusters that overscreen surface charge and enable co-ion transport. This behaviour extends far beyond the predictions of classical electrostatic theory and demonstrates that specific ion effects are dynamically reversible processes governed by coupled hydration, confinement, and electric field interactions. Building on these insights, this project will establish a data-informed experimental and analytical framework for decoding specific ion effects at dynamically tuneable electrified interfaces. By combining an automated high-throughput electrochemical platform with interpretable machine learning analysis and molecular simulation, the project will systematically quantify how voltage, confinement, and ion identity jointly modulate transport and charge storage behaviour. Complementary migration, diffusion, and capacitance measurements will yield reproducible, information-rich datasets from which key physical descriptors such as voltage-dependent diffusivity, hydration asymmetry, and ion selectivity can be extracted and benchmarked against continuum and molecular models. The outcome will be a validated, theory- and data-integrated framework that links interfacial water dynamics with ion specificity, transforming empirical trends into predictive understanding. Beyond advancing fundamental interfacial chemistry, the project will provide new insights and design principles for selective ion separations, efficient energy storage systems, and emerging iontronic devices, turning specific ion effects from a persistent experimental complexity into a controllable functional parameter. 離子對生命過程與現代技術均不可或缺，然而它們在帶電界面附近的行為往往偏離經典靜電理論的預期。即使具有相同電荷，不同離子亦可因尺寸、水合狀態及界面親和力的差異而呈現截然不同，甚至相反的行為。這些特異性離子效應深刻影響能源儲存、海水淡化及離子電子器件中的離子選擇性、傳輸效率與功能表現。然而，現有研究多建基於不同材料、尺度及實驗條件下的孤立觀測，缺乏可直接比較的系統數據，因此相關效應至今仍難以統一描述和可靠預測。 本團隊近期研究顯示，電調控可主動改變界面水及離子組織，從而重塑納米限域中的離子傳輸行為。利用限域尺度可精確調控的多層石墨烯膜，我們發現特定強度的負柵極電壓可顯著改變界面水與離子團簇結構，導致超越經典電荷屏蔽預期的過度屏蔽行為，並促進同離子傳輸。這些結果表明，特異性離子效應並非僅由離子電荷或尺寸等靜態參數決定，而可能源於水合作用、納米限域、界面結構與外加電場之間的動態耦合。因此，帶電界面可被視為一個可由電位主動調控的離子環境，為系統研究及利用特異性離子效應提供新的切入點。 在此基礎上，本項目將建立一套數據導向的實驗與分析框架，以解析動態可調控帶電界面中的特異性離子效應。項目將結合自動化高通量電化學測量、可解釋機器學習、連續介質模型及分子模擬，系統研究電位、納米限域、離子種類及濃度等因素如何共同調控離子傳輸與電荷儲存。互補的遷移、擴散及電容測量將形成具可比性、可複現性及高信息密度的多維數據集，並用於辨識及量化電位依賴擴散、離子水合不對稱性、選擇性及界面響應等關鍵物理描述符。這些數據驅動所得的關聯將進一步與物理模型及分子尺度模擬相互驗證，以區分表觀相關性與具機理意義的控制因素。 最終，本項目將建立一套經實驗驗證、由數據與物理機理共同約束的研究框架，把界面水、離子特異性及電場調控之間的關係由零散的經驗規律轉化為具可比較性及預測能力的理解。除深化對帶電界面離子行為的基礎認識外，研究亦將為選擇性離子分離、高效能源儲存及新興離子電子器件提供可轉移的設計原則，推動特異性離子效應由長期被視為難以控制的實驗複雜性，轉化為可理解、可調控並可用於功能設計的物理參數。

16215826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16215826.value: 用於視覺生成模型的數據高效示例獎勵模型

16215826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16215826.value: In this proposal, we will study a data-efficient reward model to enhance visual generative models during post-training. Existing reward models for visual generation often rely on large-scale human-annotated preference data or require carefully engineered image quality metrics, which are costly and labor-intensive. To address these challenges, we will study our proposed Exemplar Reward Model (ERM), a reward model that significantly alleviates the need for large-scale human preference annotation or manually-designed image quality metrics. ERM is a reward model trained to differentiate between a small set of representative exemplar samples and the raw outputs generated by the generative model. As suggested by preliminary experiments, ERM requires only a few hundred exemplar samples, significantly fewer than those required by baselines (e.g., DiffusionDPO). ERM can also assess the quality of generated samples, thereby supporting test-time scaling via Best-of-N sample filtering. We will conduct extensive experiments, including multi-round post-training, to progressively improve both ERM and the generative model. In summary, there are three project objectives: 1. Data Construction for ERM. To construct data for training the proposed Exemplar Reward Model (ERM), we will create an initial training dataset using user-provided Exemplar Data and raw outputs from the generative model. Then, we will augment this dataset with additional pseudo-positive and pseudo-negative samples derived from the model's outputs to form the final training dataset for ERM. 2. Implementation and Optimization of ERM. We will develop and optimize the implementation of ERM. We will implement and compare different architectures for the CLIP-Vision model and the Reward Projection Layer (RPL) to distinguish between Exemplar Data and generation outputs by minimizing a simple binary cross-entropy loss. Next, we will develop rank-based bootstrapping by generating and scoring additional samples with ERM, incorporating confident positive and negative examples into the training set to enhance model performance. Finally, we will implement the algorithm to use ERM for optimal sample selection during inference and post-training via STF or DPO, with iterative updates to the reward model. 3. Proposed experiments. We have conducted some preliminary experiments, which suggest that ERM can achieve a performance comparable to or even superior to the performance of a competitive baseline DiffusionDPO with significantly fewer data (3 orders of magnitude fewer). We will conduct further experiments on sample selection using ERM, perform user studies, and experiment with extensions to video generation and different training strategies. Based on the experimental results, we will further optimize the model. 在本項目中，我們將研究一種數據高效的獎勵模型，以在後訓練階段提升視覺生成模型的性能。現有用於視覺生成的獎勵模型通常依賴大規模人工標註的偏好數據，或需要精心設計的圖像質量評價指標，因此成本高且耗費大量人力。為應對這些挑戰，我們將研究所提出的示例獎勵模型（Exemplar Reward Model，ERM）。該獎勵模型能夠顯著降低對大規模人工偏好標註或手工設計圖像質量指標的需求。 ERM 通過區分少量具有代表性的示例樣本與生成模型產生的原始輸出進行訓練。初步實驗表明，ERM 僅需數百個示例樣本，遠少於基線方法（例如 DiffusionDPO）所需的數據量。ERM 還能夠評估生成樣本的質量，從而支持通過 Best-of-N 樣本篩選實現測試時擴展。我們將開展廣泛實驗，包括多輪後訓練，以逐步提升 ERM 和生成模型的性能。總體而言，本項目包括以下三個目標： ERM 的數據構建。 為構建訓練所提出的示例獎勵模型（ERM）所需的數據，我們將首先利用用戶提供的示例數據以及生成模型的原始輸出，建立初始訓練數據集。隨後，我們將基於模型輸出構造額外的偽正樣本和偽負樣本，對該數據集進行擴充，最終形成用於訓練 ERM 的完整數據集。 ERM 的實現與優化。 我們將開發並優化 ERM 的實現方案。首先，我們將實現並比較 CLIP-Vision 模型及獎勵投影層的不同架構，通過最小化簡單的二元交叉熵損失，使模型能夠區分示例數據與生成輸出。接下來，我們將開發一種基於排序的自舉方法：利用 ERM 生成並評估額外樣本，將高置信度的正樣本和負樣本加入訓練集，從而提升模型性能。最後，我們將實現使用 ERM 在推理階段進行最優樣本選擇的算法，並將其用於基於 STF 或 DPO 的後訓練過程；在此過程中，獎勵模型將得到迭代更新。 擬開展的實驗。 我們已經進行了一些初步實驗，結果表明，ERM 在使用顯著更少數據的情況下，能夠達到與競爭性基線方法 DiffusionDPO 相當甚至更優的性能，所需數據量可減少約 3 個數量級。後續我們將進一步開展基於 ERM 的樣本選擇實驗、用戶研究，並探索其在視頻生成任務及不同訓練策略中的擴展應用。我們將根據實驗結果持續優化模型。

16215926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16215926.value: 用於閉環腦機接口中刺激偽影消除的背景校準集成電路

16215926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16215926.value: Neural frontend ICs that can both read neural activity and deliver precise electrical stimulation are critical components for future brain–computer interfaces (BCIs). Its capability to deliver dosage-controlled stimulation promises unprecedented efficacy across different individuals to treat neurological disorders such as stroke and Parkinson’s disease, which affects 168 million people chronically on a global scale. Closing the loop requires immediate observation of the neuronal activities captured by the recording electrodes; however, when stimulating, electrical artifacts saturate the recording analog signal chain, producing significant artifacts that hide the underlying neural spikes and incapacitate effective feedback. This problem drives ongoing research to develop effective, miniaturized solutions to remove on-chip stimulation artifacts. This project aims to advance existing adaptive-replica-filter-based predictive artifact cancellation methods and improve their practicality for in vivo use. The foundational idea of the predictive artifact cancellation is to capture the stimulator-to-recorder coupling path and replicate it in the digital domain. Upon stimulation, the replica digital filter, via a digital-to-analog converter (DAC), subtracts the predicted artifact waveform from the input in the analog domain, preventing the analog signal chain from saturating. Compared to existing implementations, the key innovation this project brings is the addition of tiny, safe, charge-balanced, and pseudo-randomly modulated “dither” signals to enable continuous calibration in the background after implantation. Here, the use of pseudo-random dithers allows effective separation of the calibration stimulus from actual neural signals, enabling incremental real-time corrections to the replica filters’ coefficients. This feature offers significant value, as neural frontends experience drifting electrode impedance over time, rendering one-time calibrations used in the prior arts subject to reliability concerns. This project contributes to the development of the next-generation BCI by the following perspectives: 1) the construction of a quantitative framework incorporating both software and hardware to evaluate the efficacy of artifact cancellation methods systematically; 2) the exploration of distributed filter designs to enable scalable artifact removal solutions; and 3) design a piece of integrated circuits with on-chip artifact cancellation capability for performance verification. By the end of the three years, this project expects to generate new integrated-circuit design modules that serve as solid references for the integrated-circuit academic community and have direct translational value for future BCI designs. 能夠同時記錄神經活動並提供精準電刺激的神經前端集成電路，是未來腦機接口（brain–computer interfaces，BCIs）的關鍵組件。這類電路能夠提供劑量可控的刺激，有望實現針對病患的因病施治，協助治療中風及柏金遜症等影響全球約1.68億人的神經系統疾病。 要實現閉環操作，系統必須即時監察記錄電極所擷取的神經元活動。然而，在施加電刺激時，所產生的電刺激偽影會令記錄端的模擬訊號鏈飽和，形成嚴重干擾，掩蓋原有的神經尖峰訊號，令系統無法提供有效回饋。因此，如何利用有效而小型化的晶片內置方案消除刺激偽，是一項重要的研究課題。 本項目旨在改進現有以自適應複製濾波器為基礎的預測式偽影消除技術，並提升其在活體應用中的實用性。預測式偽影消除的基本原理，是擷取刺激器與記錄器之間的耦合路徑，並在數碼域中建立相應的複製模型。施加刺激時，複製數碼濾波器會透過數碼／模擬轉換器（DAC），在模擬域中從輸入訊號扣除預測的偽影波形，從而防止模擬訊號鏈出現飽和。 相較於現有方案，本項目的主要創新，是加入幅度極低、安全、電荷平衡且經偽隨機調制的「抖動」（dither）訊號，使系統在植入體內後仍可於背景持續進行校準。偽隨機抖動訊號可將校準刺激與實際神經訊號有效分離，使系統能夠實時逐步修正複製濾波器的係數。相較現有的一次性校準技術，這項技術可以有效應對神經前端的電極阻抗會隨時間發生漂移，有效提升腦機接口的可靠性。 本項目將從以下三方面開展： 1)建立一套打通軟件及硬件的量化框架，系統地評估不同偽影消除方法的成效； 2)探索分佈式濾波器設計，以開發可擴展的偽影消除方案； 3)設計一款具備晶片內置偽影消除功能的集成電路，並對其效能進行驗證。 預計在三年項目期結束時，本項目將研發出一系列新的集成電路設計模組。這些成果不但可為集成電路學術界提供具參考價值的設計方案，亦可直接轉化並應用於未來的腦機接口設計。

16216126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16216126.value: 面向 6G 的可重構 MIMO：通感一體化系統的高效空間採樣方法

16216126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16216126.value: The fifth generation (5G) of wireless technology has enabled transformative applications such as industrial automation and remote healthcare. Looking ahead, sixth generation (6G) networks promise even more immersive and intelligent services by tightly integrating communication, sensing, computing, and learning. At the heart of this vision lies the integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) paradigm, which empowers wireless systems to simultaneously deliver high-capacity connectivity and extract real-time environmental information. Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technology is a cornerstone of ISAC, exploiting spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs) to enhance both sensing and communication. Scaling up antenna arrays further improves spectral and energy efficiency for communication while boosting target detection accuracy for sensing. However, such scaling also increases hardware complexity, signal processing demands, and energy consumption. Reconfigurable MIMO (RMIMO) systems offer an efficient means of achieving spatial DoFs by dynamically adjusting antenna characteristics, including their positions and radiation patterns. A key technique in this context is dynamic spatial sampling, which involves real-time adjustment of antenna positions to optimize the capture of electromagnetic (EM) waves. By tailoring the spatial sampling pattern to the environment, RMIMO radar can synthesize virtual apertures that exceed the physical constraints of conventional arrays, enhancing target detection accuracy. Similarly, RMIMO communication can flexibly adapt spatial sampling to maximize spectral efficiency and link reliability. These capabilities position RMIMO as a promising enabler for next-generation ISAC systems. However, despite this potential, several open challenges remain: (i) the fundamental limits (capacity) of RMIMO-empowered ISAC (RMIMO-ISAC) systems are not yet established; (ii) joint sensing and channel estimation are hindered by dynamic spatial sampling and the novel mutual coupling effects it introduces; and (iii) conflicting spatial sampling requirements for sensing and communication complicate transceiver design. This project aims to unlock the potential of RMIMO for 6G ISAC systems. Specifically, we will: (1) establish the fundamental limits of RMIMO-ISAC and quantify the impact of dynamic spatial sampling; (2) develop effective algorithms for joint sensing and channel estimation to strengthen the synergy between sensing and communication under the RMIMO framework; and (3) design efficient transceiver architectures that approach these limits using both model-based and machine learning–driven optimization. The successful execution of this project will demonstrate the transformative potential of RMIMO-ISAC systems and enable innovative applications in autonomous driving, smart cities, and environmental monitoring. By advancing both sensing and communication capabilities, this research aims to contribute to a more efficient, responsive, and interconnected society.

16216326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16216326.value: 基於細粒度異構存儲集成的存算一體AI加速器之宏單元與架構設計

16216326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16216326.value: Energy-efficient hardware accelerators are essential for advancing AI and machine learning. However, the Von Neumann bottleneck limits performance and energy consumption due to the need to transfer data between memory and processors. Computing-in-Memory (CIM) paradigm addresses this by enabling computations within memory, reducing energy-hungry data movement. Existing CIM designs typically utilize a single type of memory, which limits their effectiveness. For example, SRAM(Static Random Access Memory)-CIM is fast and reliable but has a larger cell size that limits on-chip data storage and often requiring supplementary off-chip memory. Conversely, DRAM (Dynamic Random Access Memory) has a smaller footprint but its dynamic nature makes it hard to provide reliable and accurate computation in the memory. Emerging memory technologies like ReRAM (Resistive Random Access Memory) offer benefits such as non-volatility and compact size but come with challenges, including the need for costly digital/analog conversions, as well as issues with low writability and resistance variability that affecting computational reliability. Recognizing that no single memory technology can meet all requirements, we ask: Can we harness the strengths of various memory types by integrating them into a unified CIM system? This proposal seeks to develop a hybrid CIM design that seamlessly integrates multiple memory technologies, including ReRAM, DRAM, and SRAM. Our innovative architecture will feature compute-memory cells that incorporate multiple small storage units, such as DRAM for local caching, allowing for efficient storage and fast updating, and SRAM for accurate and reliable computations. By restructuring traditional crossbar configurations, we will facilitate the organization of diverse memory types into smaller, independently accessible segments. The SRAM cells also act as sensing units so that their content can be updated from their local cache simultaneously providing an ultra-high weight updating bandwidth. At the same time content in the local cache can be re-written while the SRAM cells are participating in CIM computation, minimizing the idling time and increasing the hardware utilization. Our research will investigate this hybrid CIM system at the circuit, architectural, and system levels. We will design various hybrid memory cells and develop hierarchical arrays that support parallel read/write operations across various memory types. Additionally, we will develop strategies to efficiently map computations from targeted neural networks onto this advanced hybrid architecture. The effectiveness of the proposed architecture will be showcased using state-of-the-art Large Models as benchmark studies, demonstrating its potential for more powerful and sustainable AI applications. 高能效的硬體加速器對於推動人工智慧和機器學習至關重要。然而，馮·紐曼瓶頸由於需要在記憶體和處理器之間傳輸資料，限制了效能並增加了功耗。存算一體（CIM）範式透過在記憶體內部進行計算來解決這一問題，進而減少了耗能的資料搬移。現有的存算一體設計通常採用單一類型的記憶體，這限制了其成效。例如，靜態隨機存取記憶體（SRAM）-CIM 速度快且可靠，但其較大的晶胞尺寸限制了晶片上的資料儲存空間，且通常需要額外的晶片外記憶體。相反地，動態隨機存取記憶體（DRAM）的佔用空間較小，但其動態特性使其難以在記憶體中提供可靠且精確的計算。如電阻式隨機存取記憶體（ReRAM）等新興記憶體技術雖然具有非揮發性和緊湊尺寸等優勢，但也面臨挑戰，包括需要高成本的數位/類比轉換，以及可寫入性低和電阻變異性影響計算可靠性等問題。意識到沒有任何單一記憶體技術能夠滿足所有需求，我們提出疑問：我們是否能透過將多種記憶體類型整合到一個統一的存算一體系統中，來發揮各自的優勢？本計畫旨在開發一種混合式存算一體設計，將 ReRAM、DRAM 和 SRAM 等多種記憶體技術無縫整合。我們創新的架構將以運算記憶體晶胞為特色，其中包含多個小型儲存單元，例如用於本地快取的 DRAM（以實現高效儲存和快速更新）以及用於精確可靠計算的 SRAM。藉由重構傳統的交叉陣列配置，我們將促進把不同類型的記憶體組織成更小、可獨立存取的區段。SRAM 晶胞同時也作為感測單元，使其內容可以同步從本地快取中更新，從而提供超高的權重更新頻寬。與此同時，當 SRAM 晶胞參與存算一體計算時，本地快取中的內容可以被重新寫入，進而最小化閒置時間並提高硬體利用率。我們的研究將在電路、架構和系統層級對此混合式存算一體系統進行探討。我們將設計多種混合式記憶體晶胞，並開發支援跨多種記憶體類型進行平行讀/寫操作的分層陣列。此外，我們將開發相應的策略，以高效地將目標類神經網路的計算映射到此先進的混合架構上。所提架構的效益將使用頂尖的大型模型作為基準測試進行展示，證明其在更強大且永續的人工智慧應用中的潛力。

16216626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16216626.value: 面向下一代邊緣大語言模型的內存高效智能

16216626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16216626.value: Large language models (LLMs) are commonly deployed on powerful cloud servers. However, through optimizations at the model, algorithm, and application levels, they have made significant advances in edge environments—where computational resources, memory, and energy are limited, such as on mobile phones, IoT devices, and embedded systems. LLMs now deliver practical value across a variety of edge scenarios, including portable medical devices, smart homes, and autonomous driving. As edge environments grow increasingly complex and progress in mobile device memory stagnates, the need for efficient memory utilization in edge LLMs has become more urgent. The tasks performed by edge LLMs have evolved from earlier classification and detection functions to more complex ones, such as logical reasoning, complex decision-making, content generation, and multi-turn dialogues. These advanced tasks require models with more parameters, larger KV caches, and the ability to retain historical task information. At the same time, while the computational power of edge devices continues to improve rapidly, growth in memory capacity has lagged, constrained by power consumption and cost limitations. As a result, memory has become a critical bottleneck hindering the advancement of edge LLMs. This challenge motivates our research, which aims to develop a new framework for efficiently deploying next-generation LLMs on edge devices while maintaining performance in complex task scenarios. Deploying next-generation LLMs in edge environments presents multiple challenges, requiring efficient memory optimization across the model, algorithm, and application levels. First, to run larger LLMs on edge devices, more extensive model compression is necessary to maintain acceptable performance while ensuring low latency. Second, at the algorithm level, efficient and dynamic compression of the KV caches in LLMs is essential to achieve a flexible trade-off between accuracy and memory usage. Finally, at the application level, an efficient memory management system must be designed for LLM agents to accurately retrieve concise yet useful historical data. These insights form the basis for the design of our Memory Efficient Intelligence framework. As a foundational architecture for next-generation edge LLM deployment, this research plan will comprehensively explore the development of high-performance structures for memory-efficient intelligence, address practical design challenges, propose potential solutions, and identify feasible directions for future research. Ultimately, the proposed framework will integrate various edge resources to enhance the performance and operational efficiency of LLMs in resource-constrained environments. 大語言模型（LLM）通常部署在功能强大的雲端服務器上。 然而，通過對模型、算法和應用層面的優化，LLM在邊緣環境（例如移動電話、物聯網設備和嵌入式系統等計算資源、記憶體和能源有限的環境）中取得了顯著進展。 如今，LLM已在各種邊緣場景中展現出實際價值，包括可攜式醫療設備、智能家居和自動駕駛。 隨著邊緣環境日益複雜，移動設備記憶體增長停滯不前，邊緣LLM對高效記憶體利用的需求變得愈發迫切。 邊緣LLM執行的任務已從早期的分類和檢測功能演變為更複雜的任務，例如邏輯推理、複雜決策、內容生成和多輪對話。 這些高級任務需要具有更多參數、更大鍵值緩存以及保留歷史任務資訊能力的模型。 與此同時，儘管邊緣設備的計算能力持續快速提升，但由於功耗和成本的限制，記憶體容量的增長卻相對滯後。 因此，記憶體已成為制約邊緣層級邏輯模型（LLM）發展的關鍵瓶頸。 這一挑戰促使我們開展研究，旨在開發一種新的框架，以便在複雜任務場景下高效地在邊緣設備上部署下一代LLM，同時保持效能。 在邊緣環境中部署下一代LLM面臨多重挑戰，需要在模型、算力和應用層面進行高效的記憶體優化。 首先，為了在邊緣設備上運行更大的LLM，需要進行更廣泛的模型壓縮，以在保證低延遲的同時維持可接受的效能。 其次，在算力層面，高效且動態地壓縮LLM中的鍵值緩存對於在準確性和記憶體使用之間實現靈活的權衡至關重要。 最後，在應用層面，必須為LLM代理設計一個高效的記憶體管理系統，以便準確檢索簡潔而有用的歷史資料。 這些見解構成了我們高效記憶體智慧框架設計的基礎。 作為下一代邊緣LLM部署的基礎架構，本研究計畫將全面探索高效記憶體智慧的高性能結構開發，解决實際設計難題，提出潛在解決方案，並確定未來研究的可行方向。 最終，所提出的框架將綜合各種邊緣資源，以提升LLM在資源受限環境下的效能和運行效率。

16217126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16217126.value: 利用CRISPR介導的整合酶體系在植物乳桿菌中構建具有位點特異性的多重基因組整合系統

16217126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16217126.value: Engineered probiotic microorganisms are emerging as a field of research with great promise for medical and environmental applications. Extending the range of organisms that can express genes in diverse environments would broaden the potential applications for this field. Plasmids, extrachromosomal, self-replicating DNA molecules found in many bacterial species, are widely used to introduce and express heterologous genes. However, their inherent limitations compromise the stability, safety, and long-term expression of the plasmid-borne genes, particularly under complex environmental conditions such as the human gut. Previously, inspired by sourdough starter, we created SINERGY (Sourdough-INspired Engineering of Reconstructed Gut-beneficial bacteria and Yeast consortia) by genetically engineering Lactiplantibacillus plantarum (L. plantarum), one of the two constituent species of the starter, to express and secrete plasmid-encoded therapeutic payloads in situ. SINERGY effectively treated inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) in a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced model of colitis. However, the development of this promising technology is hampered by a lack of efficient genome integration tools in probiotic L. plantarum. Our proposed study aims to establish a suite of urgently needed genome integration tools for L. plantarum strains, including an optimized prime editor, newly identified high-efficient large serine recombinases (LSRs), and fused site-specific and multiplex genome integration systems. We anticipate that our proposed work will not only enable one-step genomic incorporation of multiple therapeutic payloads into defined ‘safe harbor’ loci, to achieve the long-term and stable expression of genetic circuits in probiotic bacteria but also provide new insights and potential solutions to the critical challenges facing live biotherapeutic products (LBPs) as they progress toward real-world clinical and industrial applications. 工程化益生菌微生物是近年來快速發展的研究領域，在醫療與環境應用方面具有廣闊前景。拓展可在不同環境中穩定表達外源基因的微生物種類，將進一步擴大工程化益生菌的應用潛力。質粒是廣泛存在於細菌中的染色體外自主複製DNA分子，目前被廣泛用於導入及表達異源基因。然而，質粒系統本身存在局限性，可能影響所攜帶基因的穩定性、安全性及長期表達，尤其是在人體腸道等複雜環境中。此前，我們受到酸麵團發酵種的啟發，對其中兩種主要組成微生物之一的植物乳桿菌進行基因工程改造，建立了SINERGY（Sourdough-INspired Engineering of Reconstructed Gut-beneficial bacteria and Yeast consortia）系統，使植物乳桿菌能夠在體內表達並分泌由質粒編碼的治療性功能分子。在葡聚糖硫酸鈉誘導的結腸炎模型中，SINERGY能夠有效改善炎症性腸病。然而，益生菌植物乳桿菌目前缺乏高效的基因組整合工具，限制了這一技術的進一步發展與應用。本研究旨在建立一套植物乳桿菌亟需的基因組整合工具，包括優化的Prime編輯器、新鑑定的高效絲氨酸重組酶，以及位點特異性多重基因組整合系統。預期本研究將實現多個治療性功能分子一步整合至預定的「安全港」基因組位點，從而使遺傳迴路能夠在益生菌中實現長期且穩定的表達。同時，本研究亦有望深化我們對活體生物治療產品在邁向實際臨床及工業應用過程中所面臨關鍵挑戰的理解，並為解決這些挑戰提供新的思路與潛在方案。

16217226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16217226.value: 地形表面上精度可調的距離查詢及其應用

16217226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16217226.value: Due to widespread geo-positioning technologies, digital terrain data has gained popularity, attracting significant research in academia and industry (e.g., Microsoft's Bing Maps and Google Earth). Computing distances on terrain surfaces is a key problem with applications in geographical information systems and scientific studies. Since online terrain distance computation is time-consuming, many studies propose index-based algorithms to enhance query processing using pre-computed indexing structures, providing e-approximate distances, where e is a user-defined error parameter set during preprocessing. However, these algorithms face high indexing costs and poor scalability. Experiments show that they consume over 256GB memory for a small terrain dataset with 150,000 vertices. In addition, different applications have different error tolerances and consequently, the accuracy requirement varies in the query phase. Unfortunately, the accuracy guarantees of existing index-based algorithms are pre-determined in the preprocessing phase and cannot answer the query with more stringent accuracy requirements in the query phase. Motivated by this, in this proposal, we consider the adjustable-accuracy distance queries on terrain surfaces, where the user can online ask for the geodesic distance between two given points with any adjustable accuracy. As an initial attempt, we propose an indexing structure, namely Multi-Layer Structure (MLS), which can answer adjustable-accuracy distance queries on terrain surfaces efficiently with a small indexing cost when the terrain is represented by the irregular triangular network (TIN) model. Our theoretical analysis shows that the preprocessing time and the space consumption of MLS are O(N log^2 N) and O(N), respectively, where N is the size of the terrain surface. Our preliminary experiments demonstrate that our algorithm can scale up to terrain datasets with millions of vertices, in which none of the existing index-based algorithms are capable of. Moreover, the MLS algorithm demonstrates a remarkable superiority over all other index-free algorithms in regard to the query processing time, surpassing them by several orders of magnitude. The preliminary results are encouraging and motivate us to continue working on this proposal with 3 objectives. Objective 1 is to study distance queries in different 3D model representations (e.g., the TIN model and the point cloud model) of terrain surfaces. Objective 2 is to study its applications (e.g., k-nearest neighbor queries) on terrain surfaces. Objective 3 is to support dynamic cases on terrain surfaces. 隨著地理定位技術的普及，數位地形資料日益受到重視，並在學術界和工業界（如微軟 Bing Maps 和 Google Earth）引發了廣泛的研究興趣。計算地形表面上的距離是地理資訊系統及科學研究的關鍵問題。由於在線計算地形距離耗時較長，許多研究提出了基於索引的演算法，利用預先建立的索引結構來加速查詢處理，從而提供 e-近似距離（其中 e 是預處理階段設定的用戶自訂誤差參數）。然而，這些演算法面臨著索引建構成本高昂和可擴展性差的問題。實驗表明，對於僅包含 15 萬個頂點的較小地形資料集，這些演算法就需要消耗超過 256GB 的記憶體。此外，不同應用情境對誤差的容忍度各不相同，因此在查詢階段對精確度的要求也存在差異。遺憾的是，現有基於索引的演算法所提供的精度保證是在預處理階段預先設定的，無法滿足查詢階段提出的更高精度要求。 有鑑於此，本研究探討地形表面上精度可調的距離查詢問題，即允許使用者在線上查詢任何兩點間的測地距離，並可靈活調整精度要求。作為初步嘗試，我們提出了一種名為「多層結構」（Multi-Layer Structure，簡稱 MLS）的索引結構；當採用不規則三角網（TIN）模型表示地形時，該結構能以較低的索引構建成本高效地處理精度可調的地形距離查詢。理論分析表明，MLS 的預處理時間和空間消耗分別為 O(N log^2 N) 和 O(N)，其中 N 為地形表面的規模。初步實驗結果顯示，我們的演算法能夠擴展支援包含數百萬個頂點的地形資料集，而現有的各類基於索引的演算法均無法達到此規模。此外，在查詢處理時間方面，MLS 演算法表現出顯著優於所有非索引類別演算法的效能，其效率高出數個數量級。 這些初步成果令人鼓舞，促使我們繼續推進該研究計劃，具體包含兩個目標。目標 1 是研究針對不同地形表面三維模型表示形式（例如 TIN 模型和點雲模型）的距離查詢問題。目標 2 是研究其在地形表面上的應用（例如 k-近鄰查詢）。

16217326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16217326.value: 面向容错量子计算系统的架构支持

16217326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16217326.value: The fault-tolerant performance of quantum computers, specifically quantified by the logical error rate or the fault-tolerant threshold, depends on various factors including the choice of QECCs, underlying hardware technology, quantum ISA, efficiency of QEC stabilizer circuit implementations, and error syndrome decoding methods. Optimizing these aspects is crucial for advancing practical FTQC. However, existing research focused on individual components in isolation, such as improving physical qubit quality or developing new QECCs. Few studies have integrated these elements from a system-driven perspective to holistically enhance fault-tolerant performance This research plan will bridge that gap by focusing on optimizing QEC stabilizer circuits and decoding techniques to boost overall fault-tolerant performance. We will leverage fundamental quantum control protocols and the power of parallel classical computing to systematically explore and integrate advanced quantum ISAs, compiler optimizations, QECC-hardware co-design, and parallel real-time decoding techniques. By pursuing this integrated strategy, we aim to significantly improve the error-correction capabilities and scalability of quantum computing systems, which is essential for unlocking the full potential of quantum computing to solve complex problems. The proposed research plan has four main tasks, collaboratively addressing a critical aspect of advancing FTQC—improving the error-correction performance, through architectural innovations and optimizations. Task 1 investigates how advanced quantum ISAs (e.g., iSWAP, continuous gates) enable more efficient QEC circuit designs and perform experimental validation on real quantum computers. Task 2 focuses on implementing the end-to-end compiler optimization to lower high-level QEC circuits into basic control instructions, with applicability to diverse quantum ISAs. Task 3 explores the design trade-offs for different QECC and hardware topology selections, offering guidance for gate scheduling optimization, logical qubit information protection, noise effect suppression, by leveraging the circuit design protocols and compilation tools developed in Task 1 and Task 2. Task 4 aims to build a real-time, scalable QEC decoding system leveraging GPU parallel computing to meet the stringent timing requirements of FTQC 量子计算机的容错性能（具体由逻辑错误率或容错阈值来量化）取决于多种因素，包括量子纠错码（QECC）的选择、底层硬件技术、量子指令集架构（ISA）、量子纠错（QEC）稳定子电路的实现效率，以及错误伴随式（error syndrome）解码方法。优化这些方面对于推进实用的容错量子计算（FTQC）至关重要。然而，现有的研究大多孤立地关注单个组件，例如提高物理量子比特的质量或开发新的QECC。很少有研究从系统驱动的角度整合这些元素以全面提升容错性能。本研究计划将重点优化QEC稳定子电路和解码技术，以提升整体的容错性能，从而填补这一研究空白。我们将利用基础量子控制协议和经典并行计算的强大能力，系统地探索和整合先进的量子ISA、编译器优化、QECC与硬件的协同设计，以及并行实时解码技术。通过奉行这一综合策略，我们旨在显著提高量子计算系统的纠错能力和可扩展性，这对于释放量子计算解决复杂问题的全部潜力至关重要。 拟议的研究计划包含四个主要任务，这些任务将协同解决推进FTQC的一个关键问题——即通过架构创新与优化来提高纠错性能： 任务 1 研究先进的量子ISA（例如 iSWAP门、连续门）如何赋能更高效的QEC电路设计，并在真实的量子计算机上进行实验验证。 任务 2 侧重于实现端到端的编译器优化，将高级QEC电路向下转换（降级）为基础控制指令，并使其能够适用于多种量子ISA。任务 3 利用在任务1和任务2中开发的电路设计协议与编译工具，探索不同QECC和硬件拓扑选择下的设计权衡，从而为门级调度优化、逻辑量子比特信息保护以及噪声效应抑制提供指导。任务 4 旨在利用GPU并行计算构建一个实时、可扩展的QEC解码系统，以满足FTQC极其严格的时序（timing）要求。

16217526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16217526.value: 結合噴嘴形變與聲學激勵的全局不穩定射流進化控制

16217526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16217526.value: Jets are central to various technological and environmental processes, including fuel injection in gas turbines, exhaust dispersion from chimneys, and plasma spraying for advanced manufacturing. Under certain conditions, however, jets can become globally unstable, developing large-scale self-excited oscillations that profoundly influence their mixing, dynamics, and stability. These oscillations arise from intrinsic hydrodynamic feedback rather than extrinsic disturbances, making them far more difficult to control. Effective control of globally unstable jets therefore remains a major challenge with direct implications for combustion efficiency, pollutant dispersal, and noise mitigation in modern energy and propulsion systems. This project aims to develop a new data-driven framework for controlling globally unstable jets by combining two complementary actuation modalities - nozzle morphing and acoustic forcing - under the guidance of evolutionary algorithms. The jet will be formed by discharging a low-density gas mixture into quiescent air, producing a self-excited global mode representative of many practical hydrodynamic oscillators. A flexible rubber nozzle, actuated by stepper motors, will enable quasi-steady modification of the exit geometry, while a circumferential ring of loudspeakers will provide distributed acoustic forcing. Together, these two actuation systems will permit simultaneous manipulation of the mean vorticity distribution and shear-layer instabilities, achieving a level of control unattainable by either mechanism alone. Optimization will be performed using evolutionary algorithms, specifically genetic algorithms (GAs) and genetic programming (GP), which can discover interpretable control laws directly from data without reliance on reduced-order models. The experimental program will proceed through four stages: (1) baseline characterization of convectively and globally unstable jets issuing from standard nozzle shapes; (2) GA-based optimization of nozzle morphing for enhanced mixing or global-mode suppression; (3) open-loop application of symmetric and asymmetric acoustic forcing; and (4) hybrid optimization of both actuation modalities using GP. These experiments will yield interpretable open- and closed-loop control laws that reveal the physical synergy between nozzle deformation and spatiotemporal perturbations, providing new insights into nonlinear global-mode dynamics. The expected outcomes include the first systematic demonstration of hybrid nozzle-morphing and acoustic-forcing control of a globally unstable jet, new physical understanding of how the mean and fluctuating flow components interact under multi-modal actuation, and the discovery of model-free control laws for self-excited flow systems. Positioned at the intersection of experimental fluid mechanics, active flow control, and machine learning, this project will advance both the fundamental understanding of globally unstable jets and the broader application of evolutionary algorithms for data-driven control across scientific and engineering disciplines. 射流在多種工程技術與環境過程中發揮關鍵作用，包括燃氣輪機的燃料噴射、煙囪廢氣的擴散，以及先進製造中的等離子噴塗。然而，在特定條件下，射流可能呈現全局不穩定性，產生大尺度自激振盪，並深刻影響其混合特性、動力學行為與穩定性。這些振盪源自流體動力系統的內在反饋機制，而非外部擾動，因此更難以控制。有效控制全局不穩定射流，至今仍是一項重大挑戰，並直接關係到現代能源與推進系統的燃燒效率、污染物擴散及噪聲抑制。本項目旨在發展一套新穎的數據驅動框架，在進化算法的引導下，結合噴嘴形變與聲學激勵兩種互補的致動方式，以控制全局不穩定射流。本研究將低密度混合氣體噴入靜止空氣中形成射流，藉此產生可代表多種實際流體動力振盪系統的自激全局模態。由步進馬達驅動的柔性橡膠噴嘴可對出口幾何形狀進行準穩態調整；同時，由多個揚聲器組成的環形陣列將提供分佈式聲學激勵。這兩套致動系統相互配合，可同時調控平均渦量分佈與剪切層不穩定性，達到任一機制單獨作用時均無法實現的控制效果。優化將採用進化算法，尤其是遺傳算法（genetic algorithms, GAs）與遺傳編程（genetic programming, GP）。此類方法無須依賴降階模型，即可直接從數據中發掘具可解釋性的控制律。實驗計劃將分為四個階段進行：（1）對由標準形狀噴嘴產生的對流不穩定及全局不穩定射流進行基準特性分析；（2）利用遺傳算法優化噴嘴形變，以增強混合或抑制全局模態；（3）以開環方式施加對稱及非對稱聲學激勵；以及（4）運用遺傳編程，對兩種致動方式進行聯合優化。這些實驗將產生具可解釋性的開環與閉環控制律，揭示噴嘴形變與時空擾動之間的物理協同作用，並為非線性全局模態動力學提供新的見解。預期成果包括：首次系統地展示利用噴嘴形變與聲學激勵的聯合控制方式調控全局不穩定射流；深入理解在多種致動方式共同作用下，平均流與脈動流分量之間的相互作用；以及發掘適用於自激流動系統的無模型控制律。本項目位於實驗流體力學、主動流動控制與機器學習三大領域的交匯處，不僅將深化對全局不穩定射流基本物理機制的理解，亦將推動進化算法在不同科學與工程領域中數據驅動控制方面的廣泛應用。

16218026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16218026.value: 真空條件下水的相變與輸運機制研究：面向可靠的空間昇華冷卻

16218026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16218026.value: Long-duration lunar and deep-space missions require thermal control systems capable of rejecting large, transient heat loads in vacuum environments with exceptional reliability. Water sublimators, which utilize the latent heat of phase change from sublimation of a consumable working fluid in porous media exposed to space, are uniquely suited to this need due to their efficient phase change heat transfer and compact design. However, they are vulnerable to “breakthrough” failures, where liquid penetrates the ice layer in the porous media, rapidly depleting consumables and collapsing thermal regulation. Current research on sublimation cooling predominantly focusses on simplified modelling approaches and system-level performance validations, yet the inability to accurately characterize and control the microscale liquid-solid-vapor transitions remains a key barrier to the systematic design of advanced sublimator systems. This project aims to bridge this knowledge gap by elucidating the underlying physics of liquid–solid–vapor transitions near the triple point and translating these insights into architected, breakthrough-resistant sublimators. Building on our prior research on microfluidics, surface topography and wettability, we have gained critical insights into tunable phase change and controlled heat and mass transfer. Our preliminary observations from a needle-based flash boiling and freezing experiment indicate that the phase change dynamics are strongly dependent on pore size, inspiring a shift from homogeneous porous media to micro-engineered architectures. The focus of this research proposal has two folds: First, we will integrate experimental and theoretical approaches to sublimation cooling. By establishing a dynamic interface-resolved model coupled with microscale experimental investigations in confine geometries under vacuum conditions, we will examine ice-front propagation, interfacial dynamics, and liquid-vapor transport at the microscale. Our goal is to decipher the mechanisms responsible for instability at the pore scale and identify the critical conditions that lead to the breakthrough failures. Second, we will achieve phase-front stabilization through engineered microporous architectures. We will translate our mechanistic understanding into stabilization strategies by engineering microstructures and surfaces to decouple liquid wicking from vapor venting and to pin and guide the ice front. We will fabricate microporous architectures with hierarchical pore networks, Laplace-pressure barriers, and heterogenous wettability patterns, reframing the sublimator design from a pressure-driven mechanism to a capillary-governed, surface-dominated system. Expected outcomes include a mechanistic framework for microscale phase-front stability, validated models and diagnostics tools for triple-phase dynamics, and design rules for breakthrough-resistant, reliable sublimators that advance space thermal management. 長週期月球與深空探測任務要求熱控系統能夠在真空環境中排散大幅瞬態熱負荷並具備極高的可靠性。水昇華器利用暴露於太空環境的多孔介質中消耗性工質昇華相變的潛熱進行散熱，憑藉其高效的相變換熱能力和緊湊的結構設計，成為滿足這一需求的獨特選擇。然而，水昇華器易發生「擊穿」失效， 即液體穿透多孔介質中的冰層，導致消耗性工質迅速耗竭，熱調節功能隨之崩潰。目前關於昇華冷卻的研究主要集中在簡化建模方法和系統級性能驗證，但仍難以準確表徵和調控微觀尺度的液–固–汽相變過程，這已成為先進昇華器系統化設計的關鍵瓶頸。 本計畫旨在闡明三相點附近液–固–汽相變的內在物理機制，並將這些機制認知轉化為具有抗擊穿能力的結構化昇華器的設計。基於我們在微流控、表面結構與潤濕性方面的研究積累，我們已在可調相變與受控熱質傳遞方面獲得了關鍵認知。我們利用針尖閃蒸沸騰與凍結實驗的初步觀測表明，相變動力學強烈依賴於孔隙尺寸，這啟發我們突破均質多孔介質的傳統路線，轉向微納工程化結構設計。 本研究包含兩個面向：第一，將實驗與理論方法結合進行昇華冷卻研究。透過建立動態界面解析模型，並結合真空條件下受限幾何結構中的微觀尺度實驗，我們將考察微觀尺度上的冰鋒面推進、界面動力學以及液–汽輸運過程，目標是解析孔隙尺度失穩的物理機制，並識別導致擊穿失效的臨界條件。第二，透過工程化微孔結構實現相變鋒面的穩定性。我們將把機理認知轉化為穩定化策略：透過微觀結構與表面特性，實現液體毛細輸運與蒸氣排放過程的解耦，並對冰鋒面進行釘扎與引導。我們將製備具有分級孔隙網絡、拉普拉斯壓力屏障和非均勻潤濕性圖案的微孔結構，從而將昇華器設計範式從壓力驅動機制重新建構為毛細主導、表面調控的體系。 預期成果包括：針對微觀尺度相界面穩定性的機理框架，針對三相動力學的經過驗證的模型與診斷工具，以及面向抗擊穿、高可靠昇華器的設計準則，從而推動空間熱管理技術的發展。

16218126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16218126.value: 單晶片整合電流感測器的垂直結構氮化鎵（GaN）功率MOSFET

16218126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16218126.value: The global demand for electricity is surging exponentially, driven by the digital revolution (AI data centers, 5G/6G communication systems) and the clean energy transition (electric vehicles, renewable grids). At the heart of this transformation are semiconductor power chips that manage and convert electricity efficiently. However, low-cost silicon chips that have been used for decades are bulky, energy inefficient, and limiting system progress. Gallium Nitride (GaN) semiconductors represent a monumental leap forward, capable of handling more power, switching faster, with less energy loss as heat. While lateral GaN HEMTs have been adopted commercially such as in small chargers (adapters), their broader application is limited by some inherent challenges, including the absence of avalanche breakdown leading to catastrophic failure, performance-reliability issues from trapping effects, inefficient thermal management, and low threshold voltages risking false turn-on. In contrast, vertical GaN power MOSFETs offer a fundamentally superior architecture. They provide enhanced robustness through true avalanche capability, greater reliability by being less susceptible to surface traps, and safer operation with intrinsically higher threshold voltages. Furthermore, their vertical design enables more efficient heat extraction through the substrate and supports a higher current handling capability, making them a more resilient and powerful solution for next-generation power electronics. Real-time current sensing is crucial for over-current protection and operational safety in power systems. While conventional sense resistors incur significant power loss and parasitic inductance, an effective alternative is the use of sense FETs in a current mirror configuration to monitor the main FET current—a technique validated in both Si MOSFETs and GaN lateral HEMTs. Although discrete vertical GaN power MOSFETs have been demonstrated with excellent performance, no implementation of integrated current sensing has been reported for this technology to date. Based on our expertise and experience in GaN power devices and integration technology. We propose to demonstrate vertical GaN power MOSFETs with monolithically integrated current sensors. The sense FETs will be fabricated and monolithically integrated with the main power FETs using the same fabrication process. We aim to demonstrate vertical GaN power transistors with current sensing function for future energy-efficient power system applications. 在數位革命（如人工智慧資料中心、5G/6G通訊系統）和清潔能源轉型（如電動車、再生能源電網）的推動下，全球電力需求正呈指數級增長。這項變革的核心在於能夠高效管理和轉換電能的半導體功率晶片。然而，沿用數十年的低成本矽基晶片存在體積大、能效低等問題，限制了系統的進一步發展。氮化鎵（GaN）半導體代表了重大的技術飛躍，它不僅能處理更高的功率，還具備更快的開關速度，且能量損耗（以熱能形式）更低。 基於我們在氮化鎵（GaN）功率元件及整合技術領域的專業知識與經驗，我們計劃開發並展示整合有晶片電流感測器的垂直結構GaN功率MOSFET。其中的感測型FET（sense FET）將與主功率FET採用相同的製程進行製造並實現單晶片整合。我們的目標是開發出具備電流感測功能的垂直結構GaN功率電晶體，以滿足未來高效能電力系統應用的需求。

16218526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16218526.value: 地震邊坡穩定與破壞分析：從基於物理的模擬到機器學習

16218526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16218526.value: Earthquake-induced slope failure is a major cause of damage to infrastructure and poses a significant threat to human safety. Analyzing seismic slope stability and slope failure is one of the most important topics in geotechnical earthquake engineering. Recently, methods for seismic slope analyses have evolved from simple rigid/flexible sliding block models to more advanced stress-deformation simulations. This proposal aims to advance several key technologies to improve the efficiency and accuracy of physics-based simulations for seismic slope stability and large-deformation analyses of slope failure, with an overarching goal to develop advanced machine-learning methods for rapid prediction. Four interrelated tasks are proposed. Tasks 1 and 2 develop an advanced Material Point Method (MPM) to realistically simulate the large deformation failure process of soil slopes under various earthquakes and hydraulic conditions. Task 1 will develop an innovative mesh-grading MPM to efficiently refine the mesh resolution for dynamic shear band simulation and large deformation analyses. A stress-based dynamic boundary will also be developed as a general and practical method to input ground motions. Task 2 will develop a hybrid scheme to couple hydrological modeling with MPM. A semi-implicit u-p formulation will be developed to increase the robustness of slope failure simulation under various hydraulic and rainfall conditions. In Task 3, the developed numerical model will be calibrated and validated. A comprehensive set of physics-based simulations will be performed to investigate the fundamental mechanisms of seismic stability and slope failure under various slope geometries, soil properties, water levels, and input motions. Based on these extensive numerical analyses, in Task 4, several machine learning methods will be investigated to develop surrogate models for rapid prediction of seismic slope stability and slope failure. The proposed work will generate efficient advanced computational tools to study seismic slope failure mechanism, and innovative machine-learning models for practical engineering applications. It will have significant impact on seismic design of embankments, slopes, levees, and dams in seismically active regions around the world. The project also has significant local impact. Historically, all soil slopes in Hong Kong have not been designed or checked for seismic safety. Considering topographic amplification and heavy rainfall conditions, the risk of seismic slope failure in such a highly populous region cannot be underestimated. To date, there is no consensus on developing a code standard for seismic slope stability analyses. Therefore, the research has high local relevance and is urgently needed. 地震引起的邊坡破壞是基礎設施損壞的主要原因，並對人員安全構成重大威脅。分析地震邊坡穩定與破壞，是岩土地震工程中最為重要的課題之一。近年來，地震邊坡分析方法已從簡單的剛性/柔性滑動塊體模型，演進至更為先進的應力-變形模擬。本提案旨在推進幾項關鍵技術，以提升基於物理模擬的地震邊坡穩定及破壞大變形分析的效率與準確性，最終開發先進的機器學習方法以進行快速預測。 本項目提出四項相互關聯的工作任務。任務 1與任務2將發展先進的數值方法，以真實模擬土壤邊坡在各種地震與水文條件下的大變形破壞過程。任務 1將開發一種創新的網格分級物質點法，有效細化動態剪切帶模擬與大變形分析所需要的網格解析度；同時，發展基於應力的動態邊界，作為地震波輸入的實用方法。任務 2開發混合數值方法，以耦合水文模擬與物質點法，並開發半隱式u-p公式，以提升在不同水文與降雨條件下邊坡破壞模擬的穩健性。任務 3校準並驗證所開發的數值模型，進行一系列基於物理的模擬，以探討在不同邊坡幾何形狀、土壤性質、水位及地震動輸入下，地震邊坡穩定性與破壞的基本機制。根據以上大量的數值模擬，任務 4將研究多種機器學習方法，開發代理模型，用於快速預測地震邊坡穩定性及破壞。 本研究項目將產出高效而先進的計算工具，以研究地震邊坡破壞機制，並開發具有實用價值的創新機器學習模型。 這將對全球地震活躍地區的堤防、邊坡、防波堤及水壩的抗震設計產生重大影響。該項目也具有顯著的本地影響力。歷史上，香港的土質邊坡均未經抗震安全設計或檢查。考慮到地形放大效應和強降雨條件，在如此人口稠密的地區，地震導致邊坡失穩的風險不容低估。迄今為止，對制定地震邊坡穩定性分析的規範標準尚未達成共識。因此，這項研究具有高度的本地相關性，且需求極為迫切。

16218626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16218626.value: 港無機碘的研究：總量、種類、多相光化學及影響

16218626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16218626.value: Atmospheric iodine is a major contributor to ozone destruction in the troposphere and to new particle formation and growth impacting human health and the radiative balance of Earth. Iodine is also a critical micronutrient whose availability is partly mediated by the atmosphere. Measurements of atmospheric iodine have generally focused on oxides which are active in photochemical ozone destruction and on oxoacids central to particle formation and growth. There have not been reports on atmospheric iodine levels in Hong Kong in over twenty years and the likely terrestrial sources of iodine indicated at the time remain unidentified. Recent years have seen major advances in our understanding of the atmospheric chemistry of iodine and revisions of its speciation and chemical mechanism. Preliminary investigations in Hong Kong have identified the consistent presence of several gaseous iodine species, possibly including some previously unreported in the atmosphere indicating understanding likely remains incomplete. A major gap in current understanding is that several lines of evidence indicate that particulate reservoirs of iodine are not stable and that there is extensive and active multiphase chemistry. However, the mechanism by which this occurs remains uncertain and so far there have been only limited investigations. We propose to employ online and offline techniques to measure total and speciated inorganic iodine in gas and particles. Aerosol Mass Spectrometry (AMS), Chemical Ionization Mass Spectrometry (CIMS) using nitrate (NO3) and bromide (Br) ions and a Volatilization Inlet for Aerosol (VIA), and Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). Cross-sensitivity between species and phases will be checked in calibrations with an Aerosol Flow Tube (AFT). The AFT will further be used to investigate specific multiphase chemical reactions simultaneously monitoring iodine in both phases, with a particular focus on heterogenous reduction of iodate, understood to be the most stable reservoir. The AFT will also be used to investigate the chemical features and identity of the potentially novel species identified in existing ambient data. The same instruments will be used to collect ambient data in two coordinated campaigns and iteratively inform lab experiments. Ambient campaigns will also include a Long Path (LP) Differential Optical Absorption Spectroscopy (DOAS), to assess spatial homogeneity and connect with remote sensing data elsewhere. Measurements from both campaigns and experiments will be examined in chemical box models to update chemical mechanisms and to assess impacts on ozone, particulate matter, and human health; as well as global models to additionally examine transport of iodine. 大氣碘是對流層臭氧耗損的重要誘因，同時參與新粒子的生成與增長過程，進而影響人體健康與地球輻射平衡。碘也是一種關鍵微量營養素，其可利用性部分受大氣過程調控。大氣碘的觀測研究大多聚焦於參與光化學臭氧耗損的碘氧化物，以及在新粒子生成和增長過程中扮演核心角色的含氧碘酸。香港已有二十餘年沒有大氣碘濃度的相關報導，而其潛在的陸地碘源至今仍未得到確認。近年來，學界對碘的大氣化學認知取得重大進展，碘的存在形態與化學反應機理也得到重新修正。我們在香港的初步觀測已經檢出多種氣態碘組分，其中包含部分此前尚未在大氣中報導過的物質，這說明目前對該體系的認知仍存在短板。當前研究的一大空白是：多項證據表明顆粒物結合態碘並不穩定，存在大量活躍的多相化學反應，但該過程的發生機理尚不明確，相關研究開展十分有限。 本專案擬採用線上與離線聯用技術，測定氣相與顆粒物相中的總無機碘以及識別各種碘的組分。所使用儀器包括氣溶膠質譜儀（AMS）、採用硝酸根（NO₃⁻）與溴離子（Br⁻）作為試劑離子的化學電離質譜儀（CIMS）搭配氣溶膠揮發進樣裝置（VIA），以及電感耦合電漿質譜儀（ICP-MS）。將利用氣溶膠流動管（AFT）開展標定實驗，檢驗不同組分、不同相態之間的干擾。氣溶膠流動管還將用於探究特定多相化學反應，同步監測兩相中的碘組分，重點針對碘酸鹽的非均相還原反應。同時藉助氣溶膠流動管，解析現有環境觀測數據中發現的潛在新型碘物種的化學特徵。將利用同一套儀器開展兩次協同外場觀測，觀測結果將迭代指導實驗室實驗。此外，外場觀測還將搭載多軸差分吸收光譜儀（MAX-DOAS），評估污染物空間均一性，並與其他地區的遙感觀測數據建立關聯。結合外場觀測與實驗測量數據，利用化學箱模式更新反應機理，評估碘對臭氧、顆粒物及人體健康產生的影響；同時結合全球模式，進一步研究碘的大氣輸送過程。

16218826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16218826.value: 月面机器人的原位月壤增材制造：智能化材料与能量沉积研究

16218826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16218826.value: This project proposes a novel, in-situ additive manufacturing (AM) process for lunar construction using unsorted regolith, designed to minimize payload through a unique, oscillation-based sieving technique. The method circumvents the need for pre-processing by employing a cyclic process: (1) pouring raw regolith onto a pre-heated and electrostatically charged surface, (2) inverting and vibrating the structure to selectively retain a fine layer of particles via affiliation forces, (3) sintering this layer using concentrated solar energy, and (4) a closed-loop, cyber-physical system subsequently uses in-situ metrology to dynamically adapt the AM parameters and trajectory in subsequent layers. To realize this vision, the research tackles three foundational challenges. First, it will establish the granular dynamics governing field-induced sieving, creating a predictive model for particle retention under combined electrostatic, thermal, and vibrational fields in lunar gravity. Second, it will develop a stochastic sintering model that links concentrated energy deposition and heterogeneous particle distributions to the resulting microstructure and mechanical strength on non-planar surfaces. Finally, it will pioneer a dynamic control framework that integrates in-situ metrology with multiple views from the robot’s in-hand camera with adaptive, non-planar slicing and trajectory planning to compensate for inherent process uncertainties. The scientific merit of this work lies in establishing first-principle understandings of regolith dynamics under combined physical fields, creating an analytical model for sintering over curved geometries, and pioneering an intelligent feedback loop for AM in highly uncertain environments. Collectively, this research provides the foundational knowledge and a viable framework for robust, resource-efficient robotic construction on the Moon. The proposed research is uniquely positioned for potential validation in upcoming space missions. The proposed AM method is designed to be within the capabilities of the Hong Kong Lunar Operation Robot in the upcoming Chang’e-8 mission scheduled to launch in 2029. This strategic alignment enables a new in-situ construction capability without the burden of additional mission payload. Success in this endeavor would not only validate a novel manufacturing paradigm but also solidify Hong Kong's distinctive contribution to pioneering the sustainable utilization of lunar resources. 本项目提出一种面向月面建造的新型原位增材制造方法，利用未经分选的月壤作为原材料，并通过一种基于振荡的独特筛分机制降低任务载荷需求。该方法无需传统预处理步骤，而是采用循环式制造流程：首先，将原始月壤倾倒至预热且带静电荷的表面；随后，通过翻转与振动结构，利用颗粒间及颗粒—表面间的吸附作用选择性保留一层细颗粒月壤；接着，采用聚光太阳能对该颗粒层进行烧结；最后，闭环信息物理系统基于原位测量结果，动态调整后续层的增材制造参数与运动轨迹。 为实现这一构想，本研究将重点解决三个基础性科学问题。首先，建立由外场诱导筛分过程所主导的颗粒动力学机制，构建在月球重力条件下、静电场、热场与振动场耦合作用下颗粒保留行为的预测模型。其次，发展随机烧结模型，揭示聚光能量输入与非均匀颗粒分布如何共同决定非平面表面上的微观结构演化与力学强度。最后，构建动态控制框架，将原位计量信息与机器人手眼相机的多视角感知相结合，并集成自适应非平面切片与轨迹规划方法，以补偿该制造过程中的固有不确定性。 本研究的科学价值在于：建立月壤颗粒在多物理场耦合作用下运动与筛分行为的第一性原理认知；形成适用于曲面几何烧结过程的解析建模方法；并开创一种面向高度不确定环境的智能反馈式机器人增材制造框架。总体而言，本研究将为月面稳健、高效、低载荷的机器人建造提供基础科学认知与可行技术路径。 本项目所提出的研究还具有在未来空间任务中开展验证的独特潜力。该增材制造方法的设计与计划于2029年发射的嫦娥八号任务中香港月面作业机器人的能力相契合。这一战略契合有望在无需增加额外任务载荷的前提下，实现新的原位建造能力。若本研究取得成功，不仅将验证一种全新的月面制造范式，也将进一步巩固香港在可持续月球资源利用前沿领域中的独特贡献。

16218926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16218926.value: 大氣微細懸浮粒子中的一次有機碳和二次有機碳濃度的長期變化趨勢與空間分佈：三個東亞地區的比較研究

16218926.label: Co - Investigator(s)
16218926.value: Prof Lee, Jiyi Prof Ying, Qi Prof Yu, Jianzhen Dr Zhu, Shuhui

16218926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16218926.value: Organic aerosols constitute a significant portion of airborne fine particulate matter (PM2.5) and are of high scientific interest due to their complex composition and diverse properties. Numerous studies have discussed their adverse health effects and impacts on the atmospheric environment. Organic carbon (OC) serves as a convenient surrogate for total organics, as it can be easily measured and is routinely monitored. OC is categorized into primary organic carbon (POC), which does not undergo chemical changes after emission, and secondary organic carbon (SOC), which is formed through secondary reactions in the atmosphere. Therefore, POC and SOC components have different chemical structures and distinct physiochemical properties, such as light absorption and hygroscopicity. Quantifying POC and SOC in ambient aerosols is essential for understanding pollution patterns and formulating effective control measures. Long-term data of POC and SOC are valuable for evaluating the efficacy of historical environmental regulations and guiding improvements in numerical air quality models. Nonetheless, reliable long-term observations of these two components are scarce to absent in many regions. To address this gap, we propose the following research project. First, we will determine the concentrations of POC and SOC using series of long-term measurement data of major PM2.5 components collected at monitoring stations in three East Asian regions, namely the Pearl River Delta region, the Yangtze River Delta region, and Korean Peninsula. A novel Bayesian inference (BI) approach has been proposed and proven to be robust and credible in previous publications. Our goal is to modify the BI method to enhance its versatility, which will enable us to obtain the long-term estimates of POC and SOC in these regions for the first time. Second, spatiotemporal variations and determining factors for POC and SOC concentrations shall be investigated. We will use time series decomposition techniques and non-parametric estimators to quantify the changing rates of ambient concentrations of POC and SOC in aforementioned regions throughout the monitoring periods. Information of source indicators, control measures, and meteorological events will be collected to elucidate the driving forces behind these variations. Third, we will conduct numerical simulations and source apportionment for POC and SOC using a regional air quality model and compare modeling results to measurements. A hybrid model that integrates measurement data into numerical modeling is developed and will help refine the emission inventories for POC, while sensitivity tests on secondary reaction mechanisms will provide insight for improving SOC modeling. 有機氣溶膠是大氣微細懸浮粒子（PM2.5）的重要組成部分，其化學組分複雜、理化性質多樣，因此備受科學界關注。大量研究已探討了其對人體健康的危害以及對大氣環境的影響。有機碳（OC）常被用作總有機物的替代指標，它易於測量且目前已經被包含在常規監測裡。OC可分為一次有機碳（POC）和二次有機碳（SOC），前者從污染源排放出來後不發生化學變化，後者則是經過大氣中的二次反應生成。因此POC與SOC組分具有不同的化學結構及迥異的理化性質，如光吸收特性和吸濕性。定量解析環境氣溶膠中的POC與SOC，對於理解污染規律和制定有效的控制措施至關重要。POC與SOC的長期數據對於評估歷史環境法規的成效、指導空氣質量數值模型的改進具有重要價值。然而，在許多地區，這兩類組分可靠的長期觀測數據可謂稀缺甚至於完全缺失。為了填補這一空白，我們提出以下研究計畫。 首先，本研究計劃利用在東亞三個地區——即珠江三角洲、長江三角洲和朝鮮半島——監測站收集的PM2.5主要組分的長期測量數據，計算推導POC與SOC的濃度。此前的研究已提出並驗證了一種新型的貝葉斯推斷（BI）方法，該方法具有較好的穩健性和較高的可信度。本研究的目標是對該BI方法進行改進以增強其通用性，從而計算出上述地區POC與SOC的長期變化趨勢。 其次，本研究計畫將討論POC與SOC濃度的時空變化特徵及其決定因素。通過採用時間序列分析技術和非參數估計方法，量化上述地區在整個監測期間，環境中POC與SOC濃度的變化速率。同時，匯總包括排放源指示物濃度、污染調控措施及氣象事件等相關信息，闡明驅動POC和SOC濃度變化的關鍵因素。 第三，本研究將利用區域空氣質量模型開展POC與SOC的數值模擬和源解析，並將模擬結果與實際測量數據進行對比。我們擬開發一種將實測數據與數值模擬結合的混合同化模型，以幫助優化POC的排放清單，同時對二次反應機理進行敏感性測試，為改進SOC模擬提供實際依據。

16219026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16219026.value: 基于类型推断与细化的高级编程语言数据结构编译与优化

16219026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16219026.value: High-level programming languages have become a hallmark of the software engineering industry, underpinning much of the modern software development infrastructure. However, while high-level languages provide expressive abstraction capabilities and ease of programming, this often comes at the cost of reduced performance: programs written in these languages tend to allocate more memory and use more indirection, incurring significant runtime overheads -- and commonly performing several times worse than low-level counterparts for identical tasks. This results in immense amounts of wasted computational resources and energy consumption. Therefore, as Moore's law is tapering off and the needs of the software industry continue to grow, the problem of optimizing high-level languages is becoming ever more critical. A major cause of inefficiency in current high-level languages is that existing compiler optimization techniques are mainly focused on low-level code generation aspects (function inlining, loop tiling, instruction selection, register allocation, etc.), and are not well-suited to optimize high-level abstractions, which require a higher-level understanding of the program's semantics. In particular, current compilers are unable to take into account non-local information relating to the direct and indirect uses of data structures in a program, which limits their ability to optimize data representation, memory usage, and access patterns. In this research, we propose to design new compilation techniques that allow users to write high-level code without necessarily sacrificing performance. We argue that compilers of the future should focus on compiling not only function bodies in isolation, but also the data structures through which functions interact non-locally, by tailoring data representations to the specific usage patterns of each part of the program. We propose to achieve this by developing several new techniques, including an approach based on type inference and elaboration, which leverages type inference technology to automatically infer the most suitable data representations for each separable program fragment, and then use a correct-by-construction elaboration process to transform the program accordingly. We will also investigate ways to compile uses of immutable data structures, which are common in high-level programming, into more efficient mutable ones. Finally, we will study ways of scaling such techniques to large codebases. The successful completion of this research could have a significant impact on the software engineering industry, as it could help bridge the performance gap between high-level and low-level programming languages and therefore produce more efficient software systems, leading to tangible economic and environmental benefits. 高级编程语言已成为软件工程行业的重要标志，并支撑着现代软件开发基础设施的很大一部分。然而，高级语言在提供强大抽象表达能力和良好编程便利性的同时，往往也以性能下降为代价：使用这些语言编写的程序通常需要分配更多内存，并采用更多层次的间接访问，由此带来显著的运行时开销；在执行相同任务时，其性能通常比低级语言实现低数倍。这造成了大量计算资源和能源的浪费。因此，随着摩尔定律逐渐趋于极限，而软件行业的需求仍在持续增长，如何优化高级语言正变得愈发关键。 当前高级语言效率不高的一个主要原因在于，现有的编译器优化技术主要集中于低级代码生成层面，例如函数内联、循环分块（loop tiling）、指令选择和寄存器分配等，而并不适合优化高级抽象，因为后者需要从更高层次理解程序的语义。尤其是，当前编译器无法充分利用与程序中数据结构的直接和间接使用方式有关的非局部信息，从而限制了其优化数据表示、内存使用以及数据访问模式的能力。 本研究拟设计一系列新的编译技术，使用户能够在编写高级代码的同时，不必以牺牲性能为代价。我们认为，未来的编译器不应仅仅孤立地编译各个函数体，还应对函数之间进行非局部交互所依赖的数据结构进行编译，并根据程序各个部分的具体使用模式，为其定制相应的数据表示方式。 为实现这一目标，我们计划开发多项新技术，其中包括一种基于**类型推断与细化（elaboration）的方法。该方法利用类型推断技术，自动为程序中各个可分离的片段推断最合适的数据表示方式，随后通过一个由构造保证正确性（correct-by-construction）**的细化过程，对程序进行相应的转换。我们还将研究如何把高级编程中常见的不可变数据结构的使用编译为更高效的可变数据结构实现。最后，我们将研究如何使这些技术能够扩展并应用于大型代码库。 本研究若能成功完成，将可能对软件工程行业产生显著影响。它有望缩小高级编程语言与低级编程语言之间的性能差距，从而构建更加高效的软件系统，并进一步带来切实的经济与环境效益。

16219326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16219326.value: 微米級間隙精準調控的原位轉移與組裝光聚合三維列印技術

16219326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16219326.value: Recent advances in additive manufacturing have enabled unprecedented geometric freedom in component fabrication. Yet, the ability to produce high-resolution engineering systems with precisely controlled gap sizes remains limited by fundamental constraints in vat photopolymerization (VPP): pixel blending and light over-curing. This phenomenon leads to uncontrolled polymerization and clogging of micro-gaps smaller than 100 µm in the lateral (XY) and vertical (Z) directions, restricting the development of functional lab-on-chip and biomedical devices. Building upon the recently demonstrated In-situ Transfer Vat Photopolymerization (IsT-VPP) process, this project aims to establish a new additive manufacturing paradigm for high-precision microsystems fabrication with micron-size gaps and multiple materials. The core idea of IsT-VPP is the decoupling of energy delivery and resin photocuring through a secondary auxiliary platform that enables in-situ formation and transfer of channel-roof layers. This mechanism suppresses excess light penetration and allows fabrication of microchannels as small as 10 µm using standard transparent resins. The proposed research will advance this concept through three integrated thrusts: (1) develop an interfacial adhesion model and library between polymer layers and coated substrates and develop suitable reconfigurable interface mechanisms to enable selective layer attachment or release on demand; (2) establish an In-situ Transfer and Assembly Vat Photopolymerization (IsTA-VPP) process with multi-platform and multi-tank, enabling assembly of multi-material components using an integrated and automated process; and (3) demonstrate functional biomedical and microfluidic devices with unique capabilities and create design guidelines for functional microsystems that may benefit from precise gap control. This research will establish the scientific foundation and engineering platform for addressing one of the key bottlenecks in microsystem and microfluidic device fabrication. Integrating multiple tanks, coatings, and toolpath coordination introduces a paradigm shift, from static layer-by-layer printing to a dynamic, intelligent, and material-aware assembly process.
