The expected research outcomes include a fully operational multi-material VPP prototype capable of producing microsystems with sub-50 µm gaps, quantitative models of layer adhesion across different coatings, a toolpath planning and process control software for adaptive layer switching and component transfer, functional demonstration of biomedical and microfluidic devices, and an open-access dataset and design guidelines for microdevice developers. Overall, this project will not only advance academic knowledge but also provide practical tools to Hong Kong’s advanced manufacturing ecosystem, enabling new applications in biomedical diagnostics, chemical sensing, and optical communication. 近年來，增材製造技術的快速發展，為製造具有複雜形狀的元件帶來了前所未有的設計自由。然而，要製造具備精確間隙尺寸的高精度工程系統，仍受到光聚合三維列印技術中兩項基本問題的限制，即像素融合和光照過度固化。這些問題會導致樹脂在不需要固化的位置發生聚合，使橫向和垂直上小於100微米的微小間隙被堵塞，因而限制了微系統和功能性裝置的發展。基於近期成功展示的原位轉移光聚合技術，本項目旨在建立一種全新的增材製造方法，用於製造具有微米級間隙和多種材料的高精度三維列印系統。 原位轉移光聚合三維列印的核心概念，是利用一個輔助平台，將能量輸入與樹脂光固化分開進行，從而在打印過程中原位形成微通道的頂蓋層，並將其轉移至目標結構上。這種方法可以減少多餘光線穿透樹脂，並可使用一般透明樹脂製造尺寸小至10微米的微通道。本項目將從三個相互配合的研究方向進一步發展這項技術：（1）建立聚合物層與不同塗層基板之間的界面黏附模型和資料庫，並開發可重新配置的界面機制，使材料層能夠根據需要選擇性黏附或釋放；（2）建立具有多平台和多材料槽的原位轉移與組裝光聚合技術，透過一體化和自動化流程完成多材料元件的製造與組裝；以及（3）製作具有獨特功能的生物醫療和微流體裝置，並建立適用於精密間隙控制之功能性微系統的設計指引。 本研究將建立必要的科學基礎和工程平台，以解決微系統和功能性裝置製造中的一項關鍵技術瓶頸。透過整合多個材料槽、不同表面塗層及打印路徑協調控制，本項目將推動三維打印由傳統的靜態逐層製造方式，轉變為動態、智能且能配合不同材料特性的組裝過程。預期成果包括：一套可實際運作的多材料增材製造原型系統，能夠製造間隙小於50微米的微系統；不同表面塗層與材料層之間的定量黏附模型；可進行材料層自動切換和元件轉移的打印路徑規劃與製程控制軟件；生物醫療和微流體裝置的功能展示；以及供微型裝置開發人員使用的開放數據集和設計指引。整體而言，本項目不僅能推動相關學術研究，亦將為香港的先進製造生態系統提供實用工具，促進生物醫療診斷、化學感測和光學通訊等領域的新應用。

16219726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16219726.value: 一個用於可重構數據流架構通用加速的統一且可重定目標的編譯框架

16219726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16219726.value: Reconfigurable Dataflow Architectures (RDAs) represent a critical advancement in computer hardware, offering a powerful combination of the high performance and energy efficiency seen in specialized chips (like ASICs) with the flexibility of general-purpose processors. This makes them highly promising for accelerating demanding applications, from artificial intelligence to scientific computing, especially in the post-Moore era where traditional performance scaling has slowed down. However, a major roadblock prevents RDAs from reaching their full potential is the fundamental difficulty in compiling conventional programs, which rely heavily on sequential control flow (like loops and branches), onto hardware that is designed to execute the data-driven execution model. This mismatch forces current RDA compilers into inefficient compromises. Some approaches use external controllers to manage program flow, but this serializes execution and creates performance bottlenecks. Others try to flatten the entire program into one large static configuration, but this scales poorly and struggles with complex logic, leading to performance degradation. Even techniques like predication, which convert some control decisions into data operations, fail when faced with the nested and hierarchical control structures commonly existed in real-world programs. Consequently, much of the inherent parallelism that RDAs could exploit remains locked away, limiting performance and hindering wider adoption. This project tackles this foundational challenge by developing a novel, end-to-end compilation framework. At its core, we propose a new unified dataflow intermediate representation (IR). This IR is specifically designed to represent an entire program --- including intricate, nested control flow --- as a single, pure dataflow graph. By systematically encoding control dependencies as data dependencies using an innovative predicated type system, our approach eliminates the problematic mismatch at the compiler level. We will develop a systematic methodology to automatically translate standard program representations into this unified IR. The project will deliver a complete compiler, built on the modern MLIR infrastructure, featuring multi-level optimizations and a retargetable backend capable of generating efficient configurations for diverse RDA designs (including both spatial-only and spatio-temporal execution models). This research will produce a powerful, open-source toolchain poised to unlock the true performance of reconfigurable dataflow computing. 可重構數據流架構（RDAs）是電腦硬體的一項重要進展，它結合了專用晶片（像是 ASIC）所具備的高效能和能量效率，以及通用處理器的靈活性。這讓它們在加速各種高需求應用方面非常有潛力，從人工智慧到科學計算都適用，特別是在後摩爾時代，傳統的效能提升已經放緩的情況下。不過，阻礙 RDA 發揮全部潛力的一大障礙，是將傳統程式（通常依賴順序控制流程，比如迴圈和分支）編譯到面向數據驅動執行模型的硬體上。這種不匹配迫使現有的 RDA 編譯器做出效率低下的折衷。一些做法會使用外部控制器來管理程式流程，但這會讓執行變成串行，造成性能瓶頸。其他方法試圖把整個程式壓縮成一個大型的靜態配置，但這種方法擴展性很差，遇到複雜邏輯時會很吃力，最終導致性能下降。即使像“謂詞化”這種把部分控制決策轉成數據操作的技術，面對現實程式中常見的巢狀和階層控制結構時，也會失敗。因此，RDAs 本可以利用的很多固有平行性仍然被鎖住，這限制了性能並阻礙了更廣泛的使用。 這個專案透過開發一個新的端到端編譯框架來解決這個基礎性的挑戰。我們的核心是提出一種新的統一數據流中間表示（IR）。這個 IR 專門設計用來將整個程式呈現出來—包括複雜、嵌套的控制流程—作為一個單一的純數據流圖。透過使用創新的預測類型系統，將控制相依系統性地編碼成數據相依，我們的方法消除了編譯器層級上常見的不匹配問題。我們將開發一套系統化的方法來自動將標準程式表示轉換成這個統一的 IR。 這個專案將提供一個完整的編譯器，建立在現代 MLIR 基礎架構上，具備多層次優化功能和可重定向後端，能生成高效配置以支援各種 RDA 設計（包括純空間和時空執行模型）。這項研究將產出一個強大且開放原始碼的工具鏈，有助於真正釋放可重配置數據流運算的效能。

16219826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16219826.value: SSS 3D 壓電材料：面向高效能量俘獲的一種綠色可編程加工平臺

16219826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16219826.value: High-performance piezoceramics play a pivotal role in the next-generation energy harvesters and smart devices. However, their potential is not fully released due to the challenge in fabricating such brittle ceramics into 3D complex geometries. Existing manufacturing methods, including 3D printing, are plagued by their slow, costly, and multi-step processes. The polymer binders used in 3D printing sacrifice the final material density and significantly extend production time to tens of hours. It is thus urgent to develop a new technology that can rapidly manufacture high density and complex-shaped ceramics from powder in a single step. We here propose a new, integrated manufacturing platform that achieves the simultaneous sintering and shaping (SSS) of complex-geometry piezoelectric ceramics. Leveraging our extensive research experience in piezoelectric materials and advanced manufacturing, we will introduce a field-assisted thermo-mechanical process that combines rapid Joule heating with a programmable multipoint loading system. This binder-less approach enables the fast (within 5 minutes per piece) and precise fabrication of 3D piezoelectric architectures with superior density (>98%) and performance. Central to our approach is the unification of shaping and sintering. The project is structured into four focused tasks. It will commence with the design and construction of the new SSS manufacturing platform (Task 1). We will then conduct a fundamental study to answer a key scientific question: how can brittle ceramics undergo large deformation? This will involve establishing and validating a viscoplastic theoretical model (Task 2). Based on this understanding, we will proceed to the optimization of key manufacturing parameters, such as temperature, loading rate, and sintering time, to control the final geometry and properties of the ceramics (Task 3). Finally, we will demonstrate the platform's capability by fabricating a novel, multi-wave piezoelectric energy harvester and benchmarking its superior performance (Task 4). The anticipated outcomes include a new SSS platform, a fundamental quantified understanding of the ceramic viscoplasticity, a set of optimized processing parameters, and the creation of complex-shaped piezoelectric materials with near-theoretical density and high piezoelectric coefficients (d33 > 450 pC/N), and high-efficiency 3D energy harvesters. This advancement will not only contribute to the field of materials processing but also pave the way for a new class of highly efficient, reliable, and geometrically optimized energy harvesters, acoustic transducer and sensors. 高性能壓電陶瓷在下一代能量收集器和智慧型設備中發揮關鍵作用。然而，由於難以將這種脆性陶瓷加工成複雜的三維幾何形狀，其潛力尚未充分發揮。現有的製造方法，包括3D列印，都存在速度慢、成本高、步驟繁瑣等問題。 3D列印中使用的聚合物黏合劑會降低最終材料的密度，並顯著延長生產時間至數十小時。因此，迫切需要開發一種能夠一步快速製造高密度、複雜形狀陶瓷粉末的新技術。本文提出了一種新型整合製造平台，實現了複雜幾何形狀壓電陶瓷的同步燒結和成型（SSS）。憑藉我們在壓電材料和先進製造領域的豐富研究經驗，我們將介紹一種場輔助熱機械工藝，該工藝結合了快速焦耳加熱和可編程多點加載系統。這種無黏結劑方法能夠快速（每件僅需5分鐘）且精確地製造出密度（>98%）和性能優異的三維壓電結構。此方法的核心在於成型和燒結的統一。項目分為四個重點任務。首先是設計和建構新型SSS製造平台（任務1）。然後，我們將進行一項基礎研究，以解答一個關鍵的科學問題：脆性陶瓷如何承受大變形？這將涉及建立和驗證黏塑性理論模型（任務2）。基於此，我們將優化關鍵製造參數，例如溫度、加載速率和燒結時間，以控製陶瓷的最終幾何形狀和性能（任務3）。最後，我們將透過製造一種新型多波壓電能量收集器並對其卓越性能進行基準測試，來展示該平台的能力（任務4）。

16220726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16220726.value: 從奈米級機製到系統級智慧：擴展鹵化物鈣鈦礦憶阻器以實現整合感測器內計算和神經形態處理

16220726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16220726.value: The advent of artificial intelligence and edge computing has created an urgent need for hardware that can process complex data with high efficiency, moving beyond the limitations of the von Neumann architecture. Halide perovskite memristors have emerged as a promising candidate for such neuromorphic hardware, offering excellent switching speed and tunability. However, their transition from laboratory devices to scalable computing systems is critically hindered by three fundamental challenges: profound instability and unreliable filamentary switching, an inability to achieve large-scale, uniform integration with transistor-based control, and a lack of conclusive understanding of the underlying ionic mechanisms. This project aims to bridge this gap by delivering a comprehensive pathway to transform perovskite memristors from a promising material into a robust, scalable computing technology. We propose a multi-thrust research program that systematically addresses these bottlenecks. First, we will engineer stable, three-dimensional perovskite nanowire arrays to achieve unprecedented analog control, targeting over 256 distinct conductance states with minimal variability. This will form the basis of a high-density 64x64 crossbar array for implementing a physical neural network. Second, we will pioneer a novel monolithic fabrication process to integrate a perovskite memristor with a transistor selector in a 1T1R configuration directly atop a CMOS backplane. This crucial step will eliminate sneak-path currents and enable individual cell access, allowing us to build a 128 × 128 array for high-accuracy medical image diagnostics. Third, leveraging this integration, we will create a groundbreaking million-pixel vision sensor that fuses sensing and processing. This sensor will demonstrate real-time, single-shot high-dynamic-range imaging and instant convolutional edge detection, performing computation at the speed of light within the sensor itself. Underpinning this entire hardware development is a parallel sub-project dedicated to a fundamental breakthrough: the direct, real-time visualization of ionic switching dynamics using in situ transmission electron microscopy. This will definitively resolve the mechanism debate and guide the development of effective material passivation strategies. By unifying fundamental science with scalable engineering, this project will establish a new paradigm for intelligent, low-power computing systems, with transformative applications in autonomous robotics, real-time biomedical diagnostics, and next-generation edge intelligence. 人工智慧和邊緣運算的出現令市場更迫切需要能夠高效處理複雜資料、超越馮諾依曼架構限制的硬體。鹵化物鈣鈦礦憶阻器已成為此類神經形態硬體的有前途的候選者，提供出色的開關速度和可調諧性。然而，它們從實驗室設備到可擴展計算系統的轉變受到三個基本挑戰的嚴重阻礙：嚴重的不穩定性和不可靠的絲狀開關、無法實現大規模與基於晶體管的控制的統一集成，以及對潛在離子機制缺乏決定性的理解。該計畫旨在透過提供一種全面的途徑來彌合這一差距，將鈣鈦礦憶阻器從一種有前途的材料轉變為一種強大的、可擴展的計算技術。我們提出了一個多重點研究計劃，有系統地解決這些問題瓶頸。首先，我們將設計一個穩定的三維鈣鈦礦奈米線陣列，以實現前所未有的模擬控制，目標是超過 256 種不同的電導狀態，且變異性最小。這將構成用於實現物理神經網路的高密度 64x64 交叉陣列的基礎。其次，我們將開創一種新穎的單片製造工藝，將鈣鈦礦憶阻器與晶體管選擇器以 1T1R 配置直接整合在 CMOS 背板上。這一關鍵步驟將消除潛行電流並實現單一細胞訪問，使我們能夠建立用於高精度醫學影像診斷的 128 × 128 陣列。第三，利用這種集成，我們將創建一個突破性的百萬像素視覺感測器，融合感測和處理。該感測器將展示即時、單次高動態範圍成像和即時卷積邊緣偵測，在感測器本身內以光速執行計算。支援整個硬體開發的是一個平行子項目，致力於實現根本性突破：使用原位透射電子顯微鏡直接即時可視化離子開關動力學。這將徹底化解該機制引致的辯論並推動有效材料鈍化策略的發展。透過將基礎科學與可擴展的工程相結合，該計畫將為智慧、低功耗運算系統建立新的範式，並在自主機器人、即時生物醫學診斷和下一代邊緣智慧方面實現變革性應用。

16300126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16300126.value: 二維人工超莫爾晶格的實驗研究：製備、輸運表徵及概念驗證器件探索

16300126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
16300126.value: Prof Meng, Zi Yang Prof Wang, Ning

16300126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300126.value: Moiré superlattices have opened new frontiers in quantum materials research by expanding characteristic length scales from angstroms to nanoscale periods, flattening electronic bands and amplifying correlations, enabling the emergence of correlated insulators and superconductivity. Yet single-moiré systems face a fundamental limit in pursuing stronger correlation effects: While very small twist angles are necessary to achieve flatter bands that enhance electron correlations, they also drive strong lattice distortions and reconstructions, disrupting long-range order and yielding pronounced inhomogeneity. This undermines the uniformity required for exotic quantum phases, making these phases more difficult to observe. This proposal aims to systematically investigate a novel hierarchical material platform: the super-moiré lattice, which can overcome this limit. This structure arises from the superposition of two distinct moiré patterns, forming a "moiré of moiré" with periodicities extending to hundreds of nanometers. This platform is expected to generate ultra-flat bands with enhanced correlation, introduce new, independent tuning parameters, and significantly suppress structural inhomogeneity, thereby creating an ideal environment for stabilizing exotic quantum states. Our research plan focuses on four interconnected objectives: (1) Achieving precise fabrication and cross-scale structural characterization to ensure homogeneity and long-range periodicity across diverse super-moiré stacks; (2) Understanding how the super-moiré potential reshapes band structure and quantum geometry (especially Berry curvature and its dipole) in weakly correlated regimes, laying groundwork for topological phenomena in strongly correlated systems; (3) Investigating novel transport phenomena such as quantized valley Hall effect and giant nonlinear Hall effect in strongly correlated super-moiré systems, with a focus on the interplay between enhanced electron interactions and engineered quantum geometry; (4) Exploring functional devices such as valleytronic components and terahertz rectifiers based on the unique electronic properties of super-moiré lattices, validating underlying physical mechanisms through prototype measurements. The proposed research will deepen our fundamental understanding of super-moiré physics and the rich interplay between correlation and topology, paving the way for a new paradigm in quantum materials engineering and opening a new chapter in the rational design of next-generation quantum electronic devices. 莫爾超晶格通過將特徵長度尺度從埃米量級拓展至奈米量級，為量子材料研究開闢了新的前沿。其能夠顯著壓平電子能帶並增強電子關聯，從而催生關聯絕緣態和超導等新奇量子現象。然而，單一莫爾體系在追求更強關聯效應時面臨一個根本性限制：極小扭轉角是獲得更平坦能帶、進而增強電子關聯所必需的，但與此同時，它也會引發強烈的晶格畸變與結構重構，破壞長程有序並導致顯著的空間非均勻性。這種結構非均勻性削弱了新奇量子相形成所需的均一環境，使相關量子相更難被穩定和觀測。 本項目擬系統研究一種新型層級化材料平台——超莫爾晶格，以突破上述限制。該結構由兩個不同莫爾圖樣疊加形成，可視為「莫爾之莫爾」，其週期可延伸至數百奈米尺度。預期這一平台不僅能夠形成關聯效應更強的超平坦能帶，還可引入新的、相互獨立的調控參數，並顯著抑制結構非均勻性，從而為穩定新奇量子態提供理想環境。 本研究計劃圍繞四個相互關聯的目標展開：（1）實現多種超莫爾堆疊結構的精準製備與跨尺度結構表徵，確保其均勻性和長程週期性；（2）研究在弱關聯區間內超莫爾勢如何重構能帶結構並調控量子幾何性質，特別是貝里曲率及其偶極矩，為進一步探索強關聯體系中的拓撲現象奠定基礎；（3）研究強關聯超莫爾體系中的新型輸運現象，如量子化谷霍爾效應和巨非線性霍爾效應，重點揭示增強的電子相互作用與人工調控量子幾何之間的協同作用；（4）基於超莫爾晶格獨特的電子性質，探索谷電子學器件和太赫茲整流器等功能器件，並通過原型器件測量驗證其內在物理機制。 本項目的實施將深化對超莫爾物理及關聯與拓撲相互作用機制的基礎認識，為量子材料工程建立新的研究範式，並為下一代量子電子器件的理性設計開闢新的方向。

16300326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16300326.value: 自組裝單分子層實現高效穩定的混合錫鉛鈣鈦礦太陽能電池及全鈣鈦礦疊層電池

16300326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300326.value: The development of efficient and affordable solar cells is essential for accelerating the global shift to renewable energy. Metal halide perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have emerged as a leading technology owing to their simple fabrication, low cost, and remarkable power conversion efficiencies. Their tunable light-absorption properties through composition adjustment enable bandgap engineering. Specifically, replacing some of the lead with tin allows the bandgap to be narrowed for single-junction cells or tailored for use in tandem architectures, which can effectively overcome the efficiency limits of conventional single-junction solar cells. Despite this promise, mixed Sn-Pb narrow‑bandgap (NBG) PSCs face two major challenges: (i) intrinsic materials instability arising from rapid Sn2+ oxidation and asynchronous Sn/Pb crystallization, which induce compositional heterogeneity and high defect densities; (ii) performance and durability limitations associated with the widely used hole‑transport layer (HTL), PEDOT:PSS, which exhibits parasitic near‑infrared absorption and the hygrothermal instability of the PSS component. While progress has been made in suppressing Sn2+ oxidation and controlling crystallization, the inherent drawbacks of HTL remain a bottleneck. This underscores the urgent need for robust HTLs that offer high broadband transparency and environmental stability to fully realize the potential of mixed Sn-Pb perovskites and facilitate their seamless integration into tandem architecture. Self‑assembled monolayers (SAMs) have shown promise as hole‑selective contacts for high‑efficiency Pb‑based PSCs, delivering excellent transparency, tunable energy levels, and defect passivation. In this project, we will develop a new class of hole‑selective contact layers based on SAMs tailored for mixed Sn-Pb NBG sub‑cells and all‑perovskite TSCs. The research is organized into four interlinked tasks: (1) design and synthesis of functional SAMs tailored for mixed Sn-Pb NBG sub‑cells; (2) optimization of SAMs through intramolecular coupling and controlled cross-linking for enhanced interfacial stability; (3) development of mixed-SAMs and co‑SAMs strategies to form densely packed interconnecting layers for all‑perovskite TSCs; and (4) demonstration of highly efficient and stable mixed Sn-Pb PSCs and all‑perovskite TSCs enabled by optimized SAM‑based interfaces. The outcomes of this project will advance perovskite photovoltaics toward exceptional efficiency and stability, thereby facilitating future commercialization. The program will also offer strong training opportunities for students, cultivating next‑generation leaders in printable photovoltaics and positioning Hong Kong as a leading research hub for affordable, sustainable clean energy. 開發高效且可負擔的太陽能電池，對於加速全球轉向再生能源及減少對化石燃料的依賴至關重要。金屬鹵化物鈣鈦礦太陽能電池（PSCs）因其製程簡易、材料成本低廉及優異的光電轉換效率，已成為領先的光伏技術之一。其主要優勢之一在於可透過調整化學組成來調控光吸收特性。具體而言，以金屬錫部分取代鉛可縮窄帶隙以應用於單結電池，或調整帶隙以用於疊層電池結構，從而有效突破傳統單結太陽能電池的效率極限。 儘管前景可期，目前混合錫鉛窄帶隙（NBG）鈣鈦礦太陽能電池仍面臨兩大挑戰：（i）材料本徵不穩定性，源於 Sn²⁺ 快速氧化及錫／鉛結晶動力學不同步，導致組成不均勻與高缺陷密度；以及（ii）與廣泛使用的空穴傳輸層（HTL）PEDOT:PSS 相關的性能與耐久性限制，因其具有寄生近紅外吸收及 PSS 成分的濕熱不穩定性。儘管在抑制 Sn²⁺ 氧化及控制結晶方面已取得進展，PEDOT:PSS 的固有缺點仍是瓶頸。這凸顯了開發具有高透明性與環境穩定性的強韌空穴傳輸層的迫切需求，以充分發揮混合錫鉛鈣鈦礦的潛力，並促進其無縫整合至疊層電池結構中。 自組裝單分子層（SAMs）作為高效鉛基鈣鈦礦太陽能電池的空穴選擇性接觸已展現潛力，具備優異透明性、可調能級及缺陷鈍化能力。本計畫將開發一類基於 SAMs 的新型空穴接觸層，專為混合錫鉛窄帶隙子電池及全鈣鈦礦疊層太陽能電池量身設計。本研究規劃為四項相互關聯的任務：（1）設計與合成專用於混合錫鉛窄能隙子電池的功能性 SAMs；（2）透過分子內偶合與受控交聯闡明並優化 SAMs，以提升界面穩定性；（3）開發混合 SAMs 與共 SAMs 策略，形成緻密堆積的互連層，用於全鈣鈦礦疊層太陽能電池；以及（4）展示由優化 SAM 基界面所實現之高效且穩定的混合錫鉛鈣鈦礦太陽能電池與全鈣鈦礦疊層太陽能電池。 本計畫成果將推動鈣鈦礦光伏技術邁向卓越效率與工作穩定性，從而促進未來商業化。本計畫亦將為學生提供完善的培訓機會，培育可印刷光伏技術的下一代領導人才，並使香港成為可負擔且永續清潔能源的領先研究中心。

16300726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16300726.value: 氣態巨行星潮汐流動的弱非線性理論

16300726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300726.value: In recent years, efforts to explore Jupiter and Saturn have intensified, marked by the launch of several deep space missions. As the prototypical gas giants of our solar system, these planets present unique opportunities to investigate fundamental planetary processes, e.g., tidal flows within the fluid envelopes. These flows are driven by the planets' gravitational interactions with their moons and are dissipated by internal friction, thereby playing a crucial role in the spin-orbit evolution of planet-moon systems via angular momentum exchange. They are generally classified as equilibrium tides and dynamical tides, with the latter manifesting as wave motions that are highly sensitive to tidal frequency, planetary rotation, and internal structure. These distinct tidal regimes represent different pathways for tidal dissipation of energy. Theoretical studies of tidal dissipation aim to model tidal flows by fluid dynamics principles and generate predictions consistent with astrometric data from recent and upcoming missions to Jupiter and Saturn. Such studies are essential for advancing our understanding of planetary interiors and long-term orbital dynamics. Most existing theoretical models of tidal dissipation are based on linear theory, which neglects nonlinear effects, as small tidal amplitudes are observed for Jupiter and Saturn. Nevertheless, recent fully nonlinear simulations have revealed significant deviations from linear predictions, primarily due to the generation of mean zonal flows via the self-interaction of inertial waves. However, such simulations are typically conducted at artificially high Ekman numbers (measuring the importance of viscosity relative to rotation)—much larger than those in planetary interiors—raising concerns about the reliability of extrapolating simulation results to realistic conditions. To address this problem, we propose a weakly nonlinear theoretical framework that incorporates nonlinear effects perturbatively while operating at Ekman numbers closer to planetary values than those in previous simulations. Specifically, we will extend our established methodology for analyzing mechanically driven flows in rotating spherical shells to include tidal forcing. First, we will construct a weakly nonlinear theory for tidally excited waves in an idealized one-layer background flow. Second, we will apply this theory to a realistic multi-layer internal structure of Jupiter to evaluate the impact of nonlinear effects on tidal flows and associated dissipation. Finally, we will investigate how weakly nonlinear effects influence tidal resonances, where dissipation is significantly enhanced. We will assess the accuracy and applicability of our framework through comparisons with fully nonlinear simulations, obtaining a comprehensive understanding of tidal dissipation in gas giants. 近年來，隨著多項深空探測任務相繼啟動，人類對木星和土星的探測工作日益深入。作為太陽系中典型的氣態巨行星，木星和土星為研究行星的基本物理過程提供了獨特機會，例如其流體包層內部的潮汐流動。這些流動由行星與其衛星之間的引力相互作用所驅動，並透過內部摩擦而耗散能量。因此，潮汐流動藉由角動量交換，在行星－衛星系統的自轉－軌道演化中發揮著關鍵作用。潮汐流動通常分為平衡潮和動力潮，其中動力潮表現為波動運動，並對潮汐頻率、行星自轉以及內部結構具有高度敏感性。這兩類不同的潮汐形態代表了潮汐能量耗散的不同途徑。潮汐耗散的理論研究旨在基於流體動力學原理建立潮汐流動模型，並作出與近期及未來木星和土星探測任務所得天體測量資料相一致的預測。此類研究對於增進我們對行星內部結構及其長期軌道動力學的理解至關重要。 現有的大多數潮汐耗散理論模型均以線性理論為基礎。由於觀測顯示木星和土星的潮汐振幅較小，這些模型通常忽略非線性效應。然而，近期的完全非線性數值模擬揭示了與線性理論預測之間的顯著偏差，其主要原因是慣性波透過自相互作用產生了平均緯向流。然而，此類數值模擬通常採用人為設定的高埃克曼數。埃克曼數用於衡量黏性相對於旋轉效應的重要程度，而數值模擬中採用的埃克曼數遠高於行星內部的真實值。因此，將模擬結果外推至真實行星條件下是否可靠，仍然存在疑問。 為解決這一問題，本項目擬建立一套弱非線性理論框架，以攝動方式納入非線性效應，並採用比以往數值模擬更接近行星真實值的埃克曼數。具體而言，我們將拓展已建立的旋轉球殼內機械驅動流動分析方法，使其能夠處理潮汐強迫問題。首先，我們將針對理想化的單層背景流動，建立潮汐激發波動的弱非線性理論。其次，我們將該理論應用於木星較為真實的多層內部結構，以評估非線性效應對潮汐流動及其相關能量耗散的影響。最後，我們將探討弱非線性效應如何影響潮汐共振，因為在潮汐共振條件下，能量耗散會顯著增強。我們將透過與完全非線性數值模擬進行比較，評估本理論框架的準確性與適用範圍，從而全面理解氣態巨行星中的潮汐耗散機制。

16300926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16300926.value: 利用碎片對齊分子軌道（FAMO）分析探究複雜化學體系的結構與成鍵

16300926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300926.value: Understanding how atoms bond together to form molecules lies at the heart of chemistry. However, the numerous tools used to study bonding often struggle to capture the complexity of large or unusual molecular systems. To tackle this challenge, we recently developed a new method, fragment aligned molecular orbital (FAMO) analysis, which offers a fresh and intuitive way of visualizing and understanding chemical bonding in complex structures and has shown great promise when applied to Au clusters in our recent publication in a leading theoretical/computational chemistry journal. In the proposed project, we will expand the reach of FAMO analysis by applying it to new and important classes of chemical systems, including rare-earth metal clusters, metallofullerenes, and reaction transition states. These systems are not only scientifically intriguing but also relevant to areas such as catalysis and materials science. By applying and refining our technique across diverse chemical scenarios, we will make it a broadly useful tool for the chemical community and contribute to the prestige of the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology. 理解原子如何彼此成鍵並形成分子，是化學研究的核心課題。然而，目前用於研究化學鍵的眾多方法，往往難以充分揭示大型或特殊分子系統中的複雜電子結構。為了應對這項挑戰，我們最近開發了一種新的分析方法──碎片對齊分子軌域（Fragment Aligned Molecular Orbital, FAMO）分析。此方法提供了一種嶄新且直觀的方式，用以理解複雜化學結構中的鍵結本質。近期，我們已於國際理論與計算化學期刊發表相關研究成果，並成功展示 FAMO 在金團簇電子結構分析中的應用潛力。 在本計畫中，我們將進一步拓展 FAMO 分析的應用範圍，將其推廣至多類重要且具挑戰性的化學系統，包括稀土金屬團簇、金屬富勒烯（metallofullerenes）以及化學反應的過渡態。這些系統不僅具有重要的科學研究價值，也與催化及材料科學等領域密切相關。透過在不同化學系統中的應用與持續發展，我們將使 FAMO 成為化學界廣泛採用的重要研究工具，推動化學鍵結理論的發展，並進一步提升香港科技大學在理論與計算化學領域的國際聲譽及學術影響力。

16301126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16301126.value: 多齒硫屬元素膦醯胺：有機鈰配合物的多功能配體平台

16301126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301126.value: Cerium is an earth-abundant element, and its salts are relatively non-toxic. In this context, developing catalytic processes based on molecular cerium complexes holds both academic and practical significance. To design new cerium-catalyzed organic transformations, a comprehensive understanding of the organometallic chemistry of cerium is essential. Cerium(IV) alkyl and aryl complexes are rare, partly owing to incompatibility between the oxidizing cerium(IV) ion and the reducing anionic carbon ligands. Although two cerium(IV) alkyl complexes were isolated recently, the reactivity of the cerium(IV)–carbon sigma bonds toward small molecules and organic substrates has not yet been investigated. Our preliminary work has demonstrated that chalcogenophosphinic amide chelates can stabilize the cerium(IV) oxidation state and serve as effective ligand platforms for organocerium complexes. In the proposed research project, we will synthesize organocerium complexes supported by polydentate chalcogenophosphinic amide ligands and investigate their redox chemistry. Cerium(IV) alkyl and aryl complexes will be synthesized, and their reactivity toward small molecules such as carbon dioxide and unsaturated organic substrates such as heterocumulenes will be investigated. Moreover, bimetallic cerium–transition metal complexes featuring phosphinic amide bridging ligands will be synthesized to explore their potential application in the catalytic oxidation of hydrocarbons. Finally, the catalytic performance of organocerium chalcogenophosphinic amide complexes in the ring-opening polymerization of lactide will be evaluated. The factors influencing the efficiency and controllability of cerium-initiated polymerization will also be elucidated. The results of this study will lead to the development of new organic synthesis strategies using earth-abundant lanthanide catalysts. 鈰是一種地殼豐度較高的元素，其鹽類毒性相對較低。在此背景下，發展基於分子型鈰配合物的催化過程兼具重要的學術意義與實用價值。要設計新型鈰催化的有機轉化反應，必須對鈰的有機金屬化學有全面而深入的理解。四價鈰烷基和芳基配合物十分罕見，部分原因在於具有氧化性的四價鈰離子與具有還原性的陰離子碳配體之間存在著本徵的不相容性。儘管近期已成功分離得到兩例四價鈰烷基配合物，但四價鈰–碳σ鍵對小分子及有機底物的反應性尚未被系統性研究。 我們的前期工作表明，硫屬元素膦酰胺螯合配體能夠有效穩定四價鈰的氧化態，並可作為構建有機鈰配合物的優良配體平台。在本擬進行的研究計畫中，我們將合成由多齒硫屬元素膦醯胺配體支撐的有機鈰配合物，並系統性研究其氧化還原化學。擬合成四價鈰烷基及芳基配合物，考察其對二氧化碳等小分子及雜累積二烯等不飽和有機底物的反應性。此外，還將合成以膦酰胺為橋聯配體的鈰–過渡金屬雙金屬配合物，探索其在烴類催化氧化反應的潛在應用。最後，將評估有機鈰硫屬元素膦醯胺配合物在丙交酯開環聚合中的催化性能，並闡明影響鈰引發聚合效率與可控性的關鍵因素。本研究結果將為利用地球豐產鑭係金屬催化劑發展新型有機合成策略奠定基礎。

16301326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16301326.value: 超越16種優先控制多環芳烴：分子識別、全國表徵及氧化潛勢研究

16301326.label: Co - Investigator(s)
16301326.value: Prof Yu, Jianzhen Prof Zimmermann, Ralf

16301326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301326.value: While the 16 U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) priority polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) have been extensively studied for their long-term carcinogenic, teratogenic, and mutagenic risks, far less attention has been paid to the broader class of polycyclic aromatic compounds (PACs), including PAHs and their derivatives such as alkylated PAHs (APAHs), oxygenated PAHs (OPAHs), nitrated PAHs (NPAHs), heterocyclic PAHs (HPAHs), and halogenated PAHs (XPAHs). Amid rapid socioeconomic development, China faces increasing challenges from PAC pollution, threatening both environmental sustainability and public health. However, insufficient measurement capability and the lack of nationwide monitoring have left persistent gaps in knowledge of PAC molecular composition, spatiotemporal variability, and health risks, thereby constraining model simulation accuracy and evidence-based air pollution control strategies in China. In this project, we will develop molecular-level identification of PACs using state-of-the-art thermal-desorption comprehensive two-dimensional gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (TD-GC×GC-MS) and a hyphenated system that couples a thermal-optical carbon analyzer with a resonance-enhanced multiphoton ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (TOCA-REMPI-ToF-MS). We will characterize particle-bound PAC compositions from typical sources, including biomass burning, coal combustion, cooking emissions, vehicle exhaust, and industrial emissions, and we will quantify chemical compositions, spatiotemporal distributions, and drivers of PACs across China. By combining source-oriented PAC inventories with nationwide measurements, we will apply the positive matrix factorization (PMF) receptor model to apportion sources. Oxidative potential (OP) will be assessed for model compounds and selected field samples, and dose-OP and structure-OP relationships will be established to quantify PAC contributions to particle-bound OP. This study will establish a molecular-level identification workflow through advanced mass-spectrometry techniques and will provide insights into the chemical compositions, spatiotemporal characteristics, primary sources, influencing factors, and the oxidative potential of particle-bound PACs across China. The methodologies developed will facilitate further analysis of PACs globally and provide evidence to support future mitigation strategies in China and other rapidly developing countries. 美國環境保護署（EPA）優先控制的16種多環芳烴（PAHs）因具有致癌、致畸和致突變等長期健康風險，已受到廣泛關注。相比之下，包括母體PAHs及其烷基化、含氧、硝基、雜環和鹵代衍生物在內的多環芳香族化合物（PACs），尚未得到充分研究。隨着我國社會經濟快速發展，PACs污染問題日益突出，已對生態環境安全和公眾健康構成潛在威脅。然而，受制於檢測手段不足和全國尺度監測數據缺乏，我國對PACs分子組成、時空變化及健康風險的認識仍十分有限，這不僅影響大氣化學模式的模擬準確性，也制約了大氣污染精準防控措施的制定。 本項目擬依託熱脫附全二維氣相色譜—質譜（TD-GC×GC-MS）以及熱光碳分析—共振增強多光子電離飛行時間質譜聯用技術（TOCA-REMPI-ToF-MS），建立顆粒物中PACs的分子水平識別方法。圍繞生物質燃燒、燃煤、機動車尾氣等典型來源，解析顆粒態PACs的組分特徵；結合全國觀測，闡明PACs的化學組成、時空分佈規律及其主要影響因素。在此基礎上，進一步測定典型PACs標準物質及環境樣品的氧化潛勢（OP），構建劑量—氧化潛勢關係，定量評估PACs對顆粒物氧化潛勢的貢獻。 本研究將建立顆粒物中PACs的分子識別與表徵技術體系，系統揭示其在我國的化學組成、時空分佈、影響因素及氧化潛勢特徵。研究結果將為深化PACs污染認識、提升大氣污染模擬能力和優化污染防控策略提供科學依據，並可為其他快速發展國家開展相關研究與治理提供參考。

16301926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301926.value: Two-dimensional (2D) melting, characterized by an intermediate hexatic phase, is a fundamental process distinct from its three-dimensional counterpart due to enhanced long-wavelength fluctuations. Despite the extensive literature on this subject, our unpublished preliminary simulations reveal two unexpected phenomena in 2D melting, plus a third anomaly in small confined systems. (1) Anti-hyperuniformity in the hexatic phase. We find that the highly ordered hexatic phase exhibits anti-hyperuniformity at large length scales. This counterintuitive finding, which we will confirm across various model systems, raises critical questions about the role of long-wavelength fluctuations and defect dynamics in disrupting hyperuniform order, forging a novel link between the two active fields of hyperuniformity and 2D crystal melting. (2) Anomalous melting in a binary mixture. In a 1:4 mixture of paramagnetic and nonmagnetic spheres, we observe that increased repulsion induces anomalous melting instead of the usually expected solidification. Furthermore, we have identified a re-entrant transition (crystal → liquid → hexatic → solid) with increasing magnetic field. We will investigate the mechanism of this unusual phase behavior. This system, with its tunable particle interactions, serves as a novel platform for studying compositional order-disorder transitions in a crystalline lattice, analogous to those in binary alloys. (3) Collective opposite rotations in confined systems. For 15-25 spherical particles confined in a circular cavity, we observe that particles in different shells rotate collectively and that neighboring shells may rotate in opposite directions. This phenomenon, critical for the stability of small crystallites, appears to arise from the interplay between interlayer interactions and geometric frustration. We will explain its mechanism and explore the effects of particle number, cavity size and geometry. The results will shed new light on small atomic clusters and nanodevices under confinement. These counterintuitive phenomena are discovered in simple systems of spherical particles with isotropic pairwise interactions under thermal equilibrium and quasi-static processes. These underscore their novelty and fundamental importance. They raise new questions that warrant exploration. We will investigate them using complementary computer simulations and colloidal experiments. The above preliminary results come from computer simulations designed to model both atomic and colloidal systems. The experimental approach is particularly powerful, as optical microscopy can track individual particle motions—a capability not feasible in atomic systems—providing unique insight into the underlying mechanisms. This work is of significant interest to condensed matter physics, materials science, and nanotechnology. 本項目聚焦於單層球形膠體粒子這一簡單系統中，我們最近初步發現的兩個意想不到的行為。1. 六角相中的「反超均勻性」：在高度有序的六角相宏觀尺度上，發現了反直覺的反超均勻性波動，首次在「反超均勻性」與「二維熔化」兩個前沿領域間建立關聯。2. 受限微系統中的「層間反向集體旋轉」：當15-25個粒子受限於微圓形腔體時，不同同心殼層的粒子呈現集體旋轉，且相鄰層旋轉方向相反。該現象源於層間相互作用與幾何挫折的協同效應，對微小晶簇的穩定性有重要意義。本項目將結合計算機模擬與膠體實驗。利用光學顯微鏡實時追蹤單粒子運動，從根本上揭示上述現象的微觀機制，並探究粒子數、腔體尺寸及幾何形狀的影響。研究成果具有基礎意義，且能為受限原子團簇和納米器件設計提供思路。

16302326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16302326.value: 以人工智慧輔助掃描隧道顯微技術自動製備與表徵自旋結構化

16302326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302326.value: Scanning tunnelling microscopy (STM) is a powerful technique to image single atoms and molecules and characterize their electronic and magnetic properties with atomic resolution. STM is also able to manipulate single atoms and molecules to build artificial structures. However, using STM to create large size artificial structures with thousands of constituent atoms/molecules is a daunting task since the STM manipulation is a highly labor-intensive operation which is prone to human errors. The recent fast development of artificial intelligent (AI) technologies has shown great potential in executing automated tasks. Several pioneering groups have implemented AI to STM operation, such as automated recognition, autonomous assessing the quality of acquired images, and reliably conditioning the state of the probe, automated fabricating single-molecule quantum π-magnets with single-bond precision and predicting the atomic structure directly from an STM image. These results demonstrate the tremendous potential of using AI techniques in STM research. To date, all the reported AI-related STM works focus on recognizing and manipulating individual atomic or molecular species. We propose to expand to recognize and manipulate structures that contain hundreds even thousands of molecules. Recently, our lab has developed a metal-organic framework (MOF) platform which comprises a triangular lattice of triphenylmethyl (TPM), a protype carbon-centered radicals. We will develop and apply an AI-assisted recognition and dehydrogenation framework to create predesigned artificial spin structures on this platform. These artificial spin structures represent interesting systems exhibiting quantum entangled phases. Moreover, we will develop an AI-assisted automated data acquisition algorithm to conduct tunneling spectroscopy on the single molecules of the artificial structures to probe the signatures of the entangled phases. This is a highly interdisciplinary project that incorporates expertise in self-assembly, scanning tunnelling microscopy and spectroscopy, and AI technologies. We believe the rich experience of the individual participating teams as well as the proposed close collaboration will allow us to achieve the proposed goals, which will open a new avenue for AI applications in quantum spin research. 掃描穿隧顯微鏡（STM）是一種強大的技術，能夠以原子級分辨率對單個原子和分子進行成像，並表徵其電子和磁學性質。 STM 也能操縱單原子和分子以建構人工結構。然而，利用 STM 來建構包含數千個原子或分子的大型人工結構是一項艱鉅的任務，因為 STM 操縱過程高度依賴人工操作，容易出現人為失誤。近年來，人工智慧（AI）技術的快速發展在執行自動化任務方面展現了巨大潛力。一些研究團隊已將 AI 應用於 STM 操作，例如實現自動識別、自主評估成像品質、調節探針狀態、以單鍵精度自動製備單分子量子 π 磁體，以及直接根據 STM 影像預測原子結構。這些成果展示了在 STM 研究中應用 AI 技術的巨大潛力。 迄今為止，所有已報導的與 AI 相關的 STM 研究主要集中在識別和操縱單原子或分子。我們計劃將研究範圍擴展到識別和操縱包含數百甚至數千個分子的結構。近期，我們實驗室開發了一種金屬有機框架（MOF）平台，該平台由三苯甲基（TPM）——一種碳中心自由基——構成的三角晶格組成。我們將開發並應用一套 AI 輔助的識別與脫氫框架，以便在該平台上建立預先設計的人工自旋結構。這些人工自旋結構展現量子糾纏相。此外，我們將開發一種 AI 輔助的自動資料擷取演算法，對人工結構中的分子進行隧道譜測量，以探測量子糾纏相。 這是一個跨學科的項目，融合了自組裝、掃描隧道顯微和譜學以及 AI 技術領域的專業知識。我們相信，憑藉著各參與團隊豐富的經驗以及擬議的緊密合作，我們將能夠實現既定目標，從而為 AI 在量子自旋研究中的應用開闢一條新途徑。

16302426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16302426.value: 一些非线性退化椭圆方程解的正则性

16302426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302426.value: A wide range of natural phenomena—such as the propagation of sound, the diffusion of heat, and the motion of fluids—are governed by partial differential equations (PDEs), which relate an unknown function of several variables to its partial derivatives. PDEs are central not only to the physical sciences and engineering, but also interact deeply with other mathematical fields, including geometry and probability. While explicit, closed-form solutions are desirable, they are available only in special cases. A central challenge is therefore to determine whether solutions exist at all and, if so, to understand their properties. For elliptic equations, existence is often established first in a weak sense—via variational methods or viscosity techniques—before addressing regularity: are these weak solutions sufficiently smooth to satisfy the equations in the classical sense? This proposal focuses on the latter question. The regularity of solutions to PDEs is a cornerstone of mathematical analysis, reflecting the smoothness and predictability of solutions to complex problems. Regularity results ensure that solutions behave well, avoiding pathological cases that can render equations intractable or meaningless in applications. This aspect is crucial in physics, where PDEs describe fundamental laws. We intend to study the regularity of solutions to certain nonlinear, degenerate elliptic equations, where degeneracy can arise either in the interior of the domain, or at its boundary, or from the irregularity of the boundary. Such degeneracy leads to the breakdown of standard elliptic estimates and presents significant analytical challenges. Our goals are to develop new techniques tailored to these settings, to identify sharp conditions under which improved regularity holds, and to clarify the quantitative relationship between the structure of the degeneracy and the smoothness of solutions. 广泛的自然现象，例如声音的传播、热的扩散以及流体的运动，都由偏微分方程（PDEs）所支配。偏微分方程将一个关于多个变量的未知函数与其偏导数联系起来。偏微分方程不仅在物理科学和工程领域中具有核心地位，也与其他数学领域（包括几何和概率论）有着深刻的相互作用。尽管显式的闭式解是人们所期望的，但它们只在特殊情形下才存在。因此，一个核心挑战在于确定解是否存在；若存在，则进一步理解其性质。对于椭圆方程而言，通常首先通过变分方法或粘性解技术，在弱意义下建立解的存在性；随后再研究正则性问题：这些弱解是否足够光滑，从而能够在经典意义下满足方程？本项目将重点关注后一个问题。 偏微分方程解的正则性是数学分析的基石，反映了解对复杂问题的光滑性与可预测性。正则性结果确保解具有良好的行为，避免出现可能使方程在应用中变得难以处理或失去意义的病态情形。这一点在物理学中尤为关键，因为偏微分方程刻画了基本自然规律。我们计划研究某些非线性退化椭圆方程解的正则性，其中退化性可能出现在区域内部，也可能出现在区域边界，或源于边界的不规则性。这类退化会导致标准椭圆估计失效，并带来重大的分析挑战。我们的目标是发展适用于这些情形的新技术，确定使更高正则性成立的尖锐条件，并阐明退化结构与解的光滑性之间的定量关系。

16302526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16302526.value: 開發基於 Achmatowicz 重排的化學合成 2-酮醣酸的方法

16302526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302526.value: This research project aims to revolutionize the way scientists build a crucial family of complex sugar molecules, known as 2-ulosonic acids. These are not common sugars but sophisticated molecules that act as unique identification cards on the surfaces of cells. In bacteria, they are essential components of their protective outer layer and are fundamental to how they cause infections and evade our immune system. In humans, similar sugars are involved in cell-to-cell communication, immune regulation, and cancer progression. Because of their pivotal role in health and disease, these molecules are high-value targets for developing new antibiotics, vaccines, and cancer therapeutics. A major hurdle in this field is the extreme difficulty of synthesizing these molecules in the laboratory. Current methods are long, inefficient, and inflexible, often requiring more than 16 steps to produce a single target. This inefficiency severely limits the ability of researchers to obtain enough material for biological testing or to create subtle variations to study their function. Our project proposes an innovative solution by adapting a powerful chemical process called the Achmatowicz rearrangement. Think of this as a molecular origami technique that can rapidly fold a simple, flat structure into a complex, three-dimensional one. We start with furan alcohols, which are simple compounds that can be sourced sustainably from plant materials. Our key breakthrough, which has already been demonstrated in preliminary work, is successfully applying this technique to a specific type of furan that was previously believed to be incompatible with the process. This critical step allows us to efficiently create a versatile central building block that already contains the defining chemical feature of all 2-ulosonic acids. From this central building block, we can then use a suite of additional chemical tools to carefully add the remaining parts of the molecule, like adding specific branches to a tree. This flexible approach will allow us to create not only natural sugars like Kdo (a target for novel antibiotics) and pseudaminic acid but also to create custom-designed analogues. This will enable a new wave of research into how these sugars function. By providing an efficient and versatile supply of these important molecules, our work will open new doors for discovering future medicines and understanding the fundamental sugar code of life. 這項研究計畫旨在創新地構建一群關鍵複雜糖分子——2-酮糖酸的方式。這些不是常見的糖，而是細胞表面獨特的識別卡的複雜分子。在細菌中，它們是保護外層的重要成分，是它們引發感染和逃避免疫系統的關鍵。在人類中，類似的糖類參與細胞間的通訊、免疫調控及癌症進展。由於這些分子在健康與疾病中扮演關鍵角色，是開發新抗生素、疫苗及癌症治療藥物的高價值目標。 此領域的一大障礙是實驗室合成這些分子極為困難。現有方法冗長、效率低且缺乏彈性，常常需要超過16步驟才能產生單一目標。這種低效率嚴重限制了研究人員取得足夠材料進行生物測試或製造微妙變異以研究其功能的能力。 我們的計畫提出一種創新解決方案，採用一種名為阿赫馬托維茲重排的強大反應作為關鍵步驟。阿赫馬托維茲重排以簡單且可持續地從植物材料中取得的呋喃醇作為起始原料。我們的創新解決方案可以看作是一種分子摺紙技術，能快速將簡單平坦的結構摺疊成複雜的三維結構。我們的關鍵突破，已在初步工作中證明，是成功將此技術應用於先前被認為與該過程不相容的特定呋喃類型。這個關鍵步驟使我們能有效打造一個多功能的中心組件，該組件已包含所有2-酮糖酸的決定性化學特徵。 從這個核心組件出發，我們可以利用一系列額外的化學工具，小心地添加分子的剩餘部分，就像在樹木上添加特定的分支一樣。這種彈性的方法不僅能創造像Kdo（新型抗生素的靶點）和偽胺酸這類天然糖類，還能創造客製化的類似物。這將促成新一波關於這些糖類功能的研究。透過提供這些重要分子的高效且多功能供應，我們的工作將為未來藥物的發掘及理解生命的基本糖分密碼開啟新大門。

16302626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16302626.value: 沿海環境有機氣溶膠來源和生成機制：多相化學及海陸交互作用的影響

16302626.label: Co - Investigator(s)
16302626.value: Prof Chen, Qi Prof Wang, Zhe

16302626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302626.value: Organic aerosols (OA) exert significant impacts on air quality, radiative forcing, and human health. However, their sources, formation pathways, and chemical evolution remain poorly constrained, particularly in coastal environments where marine and continental emissions strongly interact. These regions are characterized by complex and rapidly changing air masses, high humidity, and variable chemical regimes, all of which complicate current understanding and modeling of secondary organic aerosol (SOA) formation. In particular, the roles of multiphase chemistry and marine-continental interactions in controlling SOA composition and variability remain among the least understood aspects of atmospheric chemistry. This project aims to unravel the sources and formation mechanisms of OA in Hong Kong, a subtropical coastal environment located at the dynamic interface between the South China Sea and the Pearl River Delta. With its persistently high humidity, frequent air-mass shifts, and abundant anthropogenic, biogenic, and marine precursors, Hong Kong provides an ideal natural laboratory to investigate how multiphase processes and air-mass interactions shape SOA formation and transformation. The study adopts a fully integrated approach combining year-round field observations, in-situ oxidation experiments with ambient air, laboratory simulations, and regional chemical transport modeling. A suite of advanced mass spectrometers, including several chemical ionization mass spectrometers and a high-resolution aerosol mass spectrometer, will be deployed to achieve near full-volatility coverage of organic compounds. These instruments will enable the molecular-level characterization of key precursors, intermediates, and oxidation products, offering direct insights into SOA chemistry. Field observations will capture the temporal and seasonal variability of OA sources under varying marine and continental influences, while laboratory experiments will simulate representative multiphase processes under controlled humidity, oxidant, and temperature conditions to validate field-based interpretations and identify dominant chemical pathways. By integrating observational and experimental findings with chemical transport model simulations, this project will establish a mechanistic and quantitative framework for predicting coastal OA behavior under current and future climatic conditions. The results will elucidate the contribution of multiphase chemistry and marine-continental interactions to OA variability, reduce uncertainties in the parameterization of SOA processes in regional and global models, and provide scientific evidence to support air-quality management and climate-mitigation strategies. The outcomes will also advance our broader understanding of how coastal environments respond to simultaneous changes in anthropogenic emissions and climate, offering implications for air-pollution control across East and Southeast Asia. 有機氣溶膠（organic aerosol, OA）對空氣質素、輻射強迫及人體健康具有重要影響。然而目前對其來源、生成途徑及化學演化過程的認識仍很不足，尤其是在海洋與陸地排放強烈交互作用的沿海環境中。沿海地區氣團來源複雜多變，且具有高濕度和多變的化學反應環境，使二次有機氣溶膠（secondary organic aerosol, SOA）的生成過程更加複雜，並增加了機制解析和模式模擬的難度。其中，多相化學過程及海陸交互作用如何調控SOA的化學組成與時空變化，仍是當前大氣化學研究中認識較為不足的重要問題之一。 本項目旨在揭示香港有機氣溶膠的來源及形成機制。香港地處南海與珠江三角洲的動態交界區，是典型的亞熱帶沿海環境。持續高濕度、頻繁的氣團轉換，以及豐富的人為源、生物源和海洋源前體物排放，使香港成為研究多相化學過程與氣團交互作用如何影響SOA生成及轉化的理想地點。本研究將採用結合外場觀測、氧化實驗及區域化學傳輸模式的綜合方法。研究計劃使用一系列先進質譜儀器以實現對不同揮發性有機化合物的廣泛覆蓋，以實現對覆蓋不同揮發程度有機化合物的測量，並在分子層面表徵關鍵前體物、中間產物及氧化產物，進而實現對SOA生成過程的解析。外場觀測將刻畫不同海洋及陸地氣團影響下OA來源的時間及季節變化特徵；氧化實驗則將在可控的濕度、氧化劑及溫度條件下模擬具有代表性的多相化學過程，以驗證外場觀測所揭示的機制並識別主導化學反應途徑。進一步結合觀測、實驗結果與化學傳輸模式模擬，本項目將建立一套綜合框架，用於預測當前及未來氣候條件下沿海地區OA的生成與演變。 本研究將闡明多相化學及海陸交互作用對沿海環境OA的貢獻，降低模式模擬中SOA過程參數化的不確定性，並為空氣質素管理及氣候變化減緩策略提供科學依據。同時，研究成果將深化對沿海大氣環境如何響應人為排放與氣候同步變化的認識，並為東亞及東南亞地區的空氣污染防控提供科學參考。

16302726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16302726.value: 海平面上升對紅樹林土壤中鐵氧化物介導的有機碳固存的影響

16302726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302726.value: The impact of sea-level rise on soil carbon pool dynamics is an emerging frontier in carbon cycling research within land-water ecotones and a core focus of coastal carbon cycling research under the international Future Earth program. Soil organic carbon (SOC) in estuarine wetlands constitutes a critical component of coastal "blue carbon". The sequestration of SOC by iron oxides, forming Fe-bound organic carbon (Fe-OC), is a vital stability pathway for the long-term burial of coastal blue carbon, known as the "rusty sink" function. However, sea-level rise, which raises the baseline water table and allows seawater to move further inland through subsurface flow and tidal inundation, may alter Fe-OC formation pathways and associated microbial processes, thereby modulating the effectiveness of the rusty sink. Salinity and inundation induced by seawater intrusion modify soil physicochemical conditions, and restructure soil aggregates, both of which affect Fe-OC adsorption and coprecipitation processes. Moreover, seawater intrusion reshapes soil microbial communities and enzyme activities. However, how the "iron gate" evolves to regulate Fe-OC formation and stabilization remains unclear. Given the abundant Fe-OC interactions in subtropical estuarine wetlands and the unique hydrological dynamics imposed by seawater intrusion superimposed on tidal processes, the proposed project will present a novel perspective by focusing on Fe-OC transformation trends and stabilization mechanisms. We hypothesize that "expected seawater intrusion linked to rising sea-level will reduce terrestrial-derived carbon inputs, weaken the efficient coprecipitation pathway of Fe-OC, reduces Fe-OC stability, and diminish the 'rusty sink' function". Taking Hong Kong's Mai Po mangrove wetland as a representative system, we will integrate stable isotope analyses, three-dimensional fluorescence spectroscopy, ultrahigh-resolution mass spectrometry, and molecular biology techniques to (1) compare Fe-OC formation processes under varying seawater intrusion scenarios, distinguishing shifts in the relative contributions of coprecipitation versus adsorption pathways; (2) elucidate the mechanisms underlying Fe-OC stabilization, including physical protection from aggregate formation, molecular structure integrity, and microbial-enzyme regulation; and (3) identify key drivers of Fe-OC formation and persistence, thereby elucidating the intrinsic links between seawater intrusion and "rusty sink" functionality at process and mechanistic levels. By unraveling how Fe-OC interactions respond to seawater intrusion, the project will yield new insights into the resilience of blue carbon sinks as sea levels rise in response to a warming climate. The findings will address a globally important scientific frontier and provide a robust scientific basis for assessing the coastal carbon-climate feedback and advancing strategies to achieve "carbon neutrality". 海水入侵對土壤碳庫動態的影響是水陸交錯帶碳循環研究的前沿課題，也是國際「未來地球」計劃下海岸帶碳循環研究的重要組成部分。河口濕地土壤有機碳是海岸「藍碳」的核心組分，而鐵氧化物透過形成鐵結合態有機碳（Fe-OC）對其進行固存，是土壤碳庫的重要穩定模式，可透過「銹匯」功能直接貢獻海岸藍碳，為土壤有機碳固存的關鍵途徑。然而，海水入侵透過提高土壤鹽度與淹沒程度，可能改變Fe-OC的形成路徑及相關微生物過程，進而調控「銹匯」功能。一方面，海水入侵引發的鹽度與淹沒脅迫改變土壤物理化學條件，重塑土壤團聚體結構，進而影響Fe-OC的吸附與共沉澱過程；另一方面，海水入侵重塑土壤微生物群落及酵素活性，惟「鐵門」如何演變以調控Fe-OC的形成與穩定仍不清楚。鑑於亞熱帶河口濕地中豐富的Fe-OC交互作用，以及海水入侵疊加潮汐過程所形成的獨特水文動力學，本研究以全新視角聚焦Fe-OC轉化趨勢與穩定機制，提出「海水入侵減少陸源碳輸入，削弱Fe-OC的高效共沉澱途徑，降低其穩定性，最終削弱『銹匯』功能」之假說。以香港米埔紅樹林濕地為代表性系統，整合穩定同位素探針、三維螢光光譜、超高解析質譜及分子生物學技術，擬：（1）比較不同海水入侵情境下Fe-OC的形成過程，區分共沉澱與吸附途徑相對貢獻的轉變；（2）闡明Fe-OC的穩定機制，包括團聚體物理保護、分子結構完整性及微生物-酵素調控；及（3）解析Fe-OC形成與持留的關鍵驅動因子，從過程與機制層面揭示海水入侵與「銹匯」功能之間的內在聯繫。本項目旨在回應一項具有全球意義的科學前沿問題，具開創性意義。透過揭示Fe-OC交互作用如何響應海水入侵，本項目將為全球變化下海岸濕地碳匯的韌性提供創新性見解，並為評估海岸碳-氣候反饋及推進「碳中和」策略提供堅實的科學依據。

16302926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16302926.value: 面向原子級精度可擴展電子元件的低溫磊晶二維材料生長

16302926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302926.value: This proposed project aims to develop process-driven synthetic routes to make two- dimensional (2D) materials with atomically sharp interfaces aiming for ultralow contact resistance. In addition, all processes will be designed to be compatible with back-end-of-the-line (BEOL) processing. Consequently, the developed method will allow 2D materials to be grown below ~450 ºC, preventing damage to the underlying chip and advancing the mass production of 2D materials for next-generation electronics and optoelectronics. The ultraclean interfaces achieved will eliminate issues arising from Fermi-level pinning and work function mismatches in conventional metal electrodes, which have high Schottky barriers that drastically increase contact resistance and heavily degrade electrical properties. We will demonstrate low-temperature van der Waals epitaxial synthesis by growing lattice-matched 2D metal single crystals directly on transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs). The proposed epitaxial growth mechanism will take advantage of the space-confined synthesis protocol we have already developed, combined with the in situ generated bismuth-based metal halide hetero-anionic precursors that we are proposing here, guided by our computational results. We will use thermodynamics-integrated simulation to predict and experimentally validate atomic-scale interfaces, and to probe the transport of effective electro-optical properties. The successful completion of the project will significantly advance our control over chemical vapor deposition at industry-compatible temperatures by identifying novel precursor formulations that can be introduced controllably during growth. It will also clarify the interface chemistry and how it controls electrical contact resistance, which is critical for short-channel transistors. Beyond applications in classical electronic and optoelectronic devices, these epitaxially grown 2D materials will find applications in quantum devices, excitonic devices, and platforms for quantum information processing, using their novel charge transport behavior at ultraclean interfaces. 本項目旨在開發工藝驅動的合成方法，製備具有超低接觸電阻界面且與後端製程相兼容的二維材料，以顯著降低半導體材料生產能耗。通過創新性工藝，我們將在低於450℃的條件下實現二維材料生長，避免對底層芯片的損傷，推動新一代電子與光電器件用二維材料的規模化製備。這種新型界面將解決傳統金屬電極中費米能級釘紮與功函數失配問題——這些缺陷會形成高肖特基勢壘，導致接觸電阻激增與電性能惡化。我們將通過在WSe2和MoS2半導體襯底上製備二維金屬鎘、鈀單晶，演示低溫範德華外延合成技術。該生長機制利用我們新研發的前驅體材料，以範德華半導體為襯底實現二維金屬單晶的可控生長。項目成功實施後，將通過揭示生長過程中可精準調控的新型前驅體組合，顯著提升在工業兼容溫度下對化學氣相沉積的掌控能力。研究還將闡明界面化學特性及其對接觸電阻的調控機制，這對短溝道晶體管至關重要。除傳統電子與光電器件應用外，這類外延二維材料憑藉其在超潔淨界面處展現的新型電荷傳輸特性，還將在量子器件、激子器件及量子信息處理平台等領域展現應用潛力。

16303026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16303026.value: 利用引力波探测器直接探测暗物质

16303026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303026.value: The discovery of gravitational waves has opened an unprecedented window into the Universe, providing not only a powerful probe of astrophysical phenomena but also a transformative opportunity to explore physics beyond the Standard Model. Ultralight dark matter candidates, such as dark photons, are theoretically well motivated and can be probed through their coherent wave-like behavior. Gravitational-wave detectors provide a unique platform with which to search for these candidates. This proposal aims to establish gravitational-wave observatories as precision laboratories to detect ultralight dark matter. Following the theoretical proposal by the PI, the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) collaboration has started research in this direction. However, current searches primarily rely on simple “bump-hunting” strategies in frequency space, which do not fully benefit from theoretical predictions of dark matter signal properties. We propose to go beyond this approach by developing optimized template-based searches that incorporate realistic dark matter velocity distributions and Earth's rotational modulation. These refinements will significantly improve the sensitivity and enhance our ability to distinguish signals from noise. This proposal will take three related directions. First, we will construct a comprehensive theoretical framework for signal templates that incorporates fine spectral features, detector orientation effects, and a realistic dark matter velocity distribution. Second, we will develop a dedicated analysis module, validated within the LVK collaboration, to implement these optimized methods in future searches. This effort will extend beyond dark photons to encompass a broad class of ultralight dark matter candidates, enabling a unified and systematic approach. Third, we will broaden the scope of dark matter searches to the rapidly expanding global network of gravitational-wave observatories, with particular emphasis on future space-based missions such as LISA, TianQin, and Taiji. These detectors, which are sensitive in the millihertz frequency band, will complement terrestrial experiments by probing previously inaccessible regions of dark matter parameter space. By combining particle physics and gravitational-wave astronomy, this proposal will deliver both theoretical innovation and experimental impact. It will establish optimized and broadly applicable search strategies, maximize the scientific reach of current and future gravitational-wave observatories, and significantly advance our ability to discover the nature of dark matter. 引力波的发现为我们打开了一扇前所未有的通往宇宙的窗口，它不仅为探测天体物理现象提供了强有力的工具，也为探索超越标准模型的物理学提供了变革性的机遇。 超轻暗物质候选者，例如暗光子，在理论上具有充分的理论依据，并且可以通过其相干的波动行为进行探测。引力波探测器为寻找这些候选者提供了一个独特的平台。 本提案旨在将引力波天文台建立为探测超轻暗物质的精密实验室。在申请人提出理论方案之后，LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) 合作组已开始朝这个方向开展研究。 然而，目前的搜索主要依赖于频域中简单的“寻找峰值”策略，这种策略未能充分利用暗物质信号特性的理论预测。我们建议超越这种方法，开发优化的基于模板的搜索策略，该策略将纳入真实的暗物质速度分布和地球自转调制。这些改进将显著提高灵敏度，并增强我们区分信号与噪声的能力。 本提案将从三个相关方向展开。首先，我们将构建一个全面的信号模板理论框架，该框架包含精细的光谱特征、探测器方向效应以及真实的暗物质速度分布。其次，我们将开发一个专用的分析模块，并在LVK合作组内进行验证，以便在未来的搜索中应用这些优化方法。这项工作将超越暗光子，涵盖一类广泛的超轻暗物质候选者，从而实现统一且系统的方法。第三，我们将扩大暗物质搜索的范围，将其扩展到快速发展的全球引力波天文台网络，尤其关注未来的空间任务，例如LISA、天琴和太极。这些在毫赫兹频段具有高灵敏度的探测器将通过探测此前无法触及的暗物质参数空间区域，来补充地面实验。 通过结合粒子物理学和引力波天文学，该提案将带来理论创新和实验影响。它将建立优化的且广泛适用的搜索策略，最大限度地发挥现有和未来引力波天文台的科学作用，并显著提升我们发现暗物质本质的能力。

16303426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16303426.value: 聯邦張量學習：隱私、算法與統計推論

16303426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303426.value: Tensor data typically contain abundant information, much of which is sensitive in many applications. Often, multiple local clients hold their own tensor data and aim to train a global model without directly sharing their private data. Differential privacy is a mathematical framework that rigorously formalizes data privacy by limiting the risk of re-identifying individuals in a dataset. Federated tensor learning is a decentralized machine learning paradigm in which local clients communicate with a central server to promote efficient tensor learning while preserving data privacy. This project aims to investigate federated tensor learning with three primary objectives: (1) develop methods and study the statistical limits for differentially private tensor learning; (2) investigate federated gradient descent and a direct approach for tensor learning under heterogeneous sample sizes and privacy budgets at local clients; and (3) develop methods and theory for statistical inference in low-rank tensor models subject to privacy constraints. Achieving these objectives will advance our understanding and application of large-scale tensor data analysis in privacy-constrained and decentralized platforms. 張量數據通常包含豐富的信息，其中許多在各類應用中屬於敏感信息。通常，多個本地客戶端各自持有其張量數據，並希望在不直接共享私人資料的情況下訓練一個全域模型。差分隱私是一種數學框架，透過限制數據集中個體被重新識別的風險，嚴謹地形式化數據隱私的概念。聯邦張量學習是一種去中心化的機器學習範式，其中本地端客戶端與中央伺服器進行溝通，以在保護數據隱私的同時促進高效的張量學習。本項目旨在研究聯邦張量學習，並有三個主要目標：（1）發展方法並研究差分隱私張量學習的統計極限；（2）在本地客戶端具有異質樣本大小與隱私預算的情況下，探討用於張量學習的聯邦梯度下降法與一種直接聯邦學習方法；以及（3）針對受隱私約束的低秩張量模型，發展統計推論的方法與理論。達成這些目標將推進我們對於在隱私受限與去中心化環境中進行大規模張量數據分析的理解與應用。

16303726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16303726.value: 超哈伯擾動的邊界有效場論

16303726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303726.value: How do galactic and larger-scale structures arise in our universe? The seeds of these structures are the fluctuations from the primordial universe. In the simplest scenario, these fluctuations started from an initial vacuum state and were stretched beyond the Hubble horizon by cosmic inflation. Once the wavelengths of these fluctuations exceed the Hubble length (dubbed “super-Hubble”), these fluctuations stop evolving in the simplest “single clock” inflation models. But when richer physics are considered, the super-Hubble fluctuations may still evolve. Known examples include the curvaton scenario, modulated reheating, and the light mass parameter regime of cosmological collider signals. We propose to study the late time evolution of these super-Hubble fluctuations using a new approach, that we refer to as a boundary effective field theory (BEFT). Some hints of the BEFT have already been seen from past studies, especially a recent work by the PI, on the boundary terms of inflationary cosmic perturbation theory. In this proposal, we propose to study BEFT systematically. We would like to first set up BEFT on firmer theoretical grounds, by deriving BEFT from both bottom-up and top-down approaches. Specifically, we propose to show how BEFT terms generally arise from curved reheating surfaces from the bottom-up; and study how these BEFT terms arise from coarse-graining of particle decay details in the modulated reheating scenario. After carefully setup BEFT, we will write down all possible terms of a two-field BEFT up to a given dimension, arrange the terms of BEFT by power counting, and study their non-Gaussianities, starting with the most important ones. Through the study of BEFT non-Gaussianities, we will be able to address some interesting questions in cosmic perturbation theory. For example, the PI and collaborators have noted in a recent work that total energy poles can arise from a boundary term, which can be considered as one of the terms in the BEFT. We propose to trace its origin. We will also classify the bulk terms into reducible and irreducible ones, depending on whether they can be transformed into a term of the BEFT. BEFT provides a much simpler way to compute the reducible terms since it does not involve time integration. Finally, we will also compare the coefficients of BEFT with observational data, providing observational constraints on the BEFT. 銀河以及更大尺度的宇宙結構是如何形成的？這些結構的種子來自原初宇宙中的漲落。在最簡單的情境下，這些漲落起始於一個初始真空態，並在宇宙暴脹期間被拉伸至哈伯視界之外。 當這些漲落的波長超過哈伯尺度（稱為「超哈伯尺度」，super-Hubble）之後，在最簡單的「單時鐘」（single-clock）暴脹模型中，這些漲落便停止演化。然而，若考慮更豐富的物理機制，超哈伯尺度漲落仍可能繼續演化。已知的例子包括 curvaton 情境、調制再加熱（modulated reheating），以及宇宙對撞機訊號中的輕質量參數區域。 我們提出一種新的方法來研究這些超哈伯尺度漲落的晚期演化，並將其稱為邊界有效場論（boundary effective field theory, BEFT）。過去的研究中已經出現了一些 BEFT 的跡象，特別是在計畫主持人（PI）近期一項關於暴脹宇宙微擾理論中邊界項的工作中。在本研究計畫中，我們將對 BEFT 進行系統性的研究。 首先，我們希望從更紮實的理論基礎建立 BEFT，分別從自下而上（bottom-up）與自上而下（top-down）兩種途徑推導 BEFT。具體而言，在自下而上的方向，我們將展示 BEFT 項如何普遍地由彎曲的再加熱曲面（curved reheating surfaces）產生；在自上而下的方向，我們將以調制再加熱情境為例，研究在對粒子衰變的微觀細節進行粗粒化（coarse-graining）之後，這些 BEFT 項如何產生。在仔細建立 BEFT 的理論架構之後，我們將寫出二場 BEFT 在給定維度以下所有可能的項，利用冪次計數（power counting）對這些項進行系統排序，並從最重要的項開始研究它們所產生的非高斯性。 透過對 BEFT 非高斯性的研究，我們將能夠處理宇宙微擾理論中的一些有趣問題。例如，計畫主持人及其合作者在近期工作中指出，總能量極點（total energy poles）可以由一個邊界項產生，而該邊界項可被視為 BEFT 中的一個項。我們將進一步追溯這類總能量極點的來源。我們也將把體積項（bulk terms）分類為可約（reducible）與不可約（irreducible）兩類，其判準在於這些體積項是否能夠轉換為 BEFT 中的邊界項。對於可約項，BEFT 提供了一種遠為簡單的計算方法，因為這種方法不需要進行時間積分。最後，我們還將把 BEFT 的係數與觀測資料進行比較，從而對 BEFT 給出觀測上的限制。

16303826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16303826.value: 通过纳米晶与配体的设计突破三线态-三线态湮灭上转换的“红外屏障”

16303826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303826.value: Photon upconversion (PUC), i.e., the conversion of multiple low-energy photons to a high-energy photon, holds promise for various applications, including solar cells, bioimaging, and photocatalysis. In particular, the conversion of invisible near-infrared (NIR) photons to visible light holds promise for deep tissue bioimaging, scalable photocatalysis, and more efficient energy conversion. Triplet fusion upconversion, also known as triplet–triplet annihilation upconversion (TTA-UC), is a photophysical process that converts incident low-energy photons into high-energy excited states and can potentially enable NIR PUC. Colloidal quantum dots (QDs) have emerged as ideal triplet sensitizers for TTA-UC because of their compositional diversity and spectral tunability. However, nanocrystals capable of sensitizing NIR-to-visible upconversion remain scarce, and existing systems cannot efficiently convert NIR-II photons to visible light. There is a pronounced efficiency “red wall” in TTA-UC, where the upconversion quantum yield (UCQY) rapidly declines to below 2% for NIR-II excitations. To address these challenges, we propose a phonon-assisted TTA-UC mechanism to overcome current efficiency limits. We hypothesize that the rate of triplet energy transfer at the QD–molecule interface is strongly dependent on the quantum confinement, the surface states of QDs, and the strength of electronic coupling between QDs and surface ligands. Building on our recent success with AgBiS₂ QDs as triplet sensitizers, which achieved a UCQY of 10.5% for NIR-I-to-visible upconversion, we will develop novel NIR QDs featuring low thermal conductivity and strong quantum confinement. Additionally, we will create novel triplet mediator ligands to modulate the electronic coupling strength at the QD–molecule interface. The proposed project will employ several key strategies, including (1) the precise synthesis of NIR ternary and III–V QDs with tunable sizes, compositions, and surface chemistries; (2) the design and synthesis of novel surface ligands acting as triplet transmitters; and (3) the fabrication of TTA-UC systems coupled with ultrafast dynamics analysis using time-resolved spectroscopy. We aim to develop robust NIR-II-to-visible upconversion systems with efficiencies markedly surpassing those of current technologies. Our preliminary results reveal an intriguing phonon-assisted TTA-UC mechanism that significantly enhances UCQY under NIR-II excitations. The success of this project has the potential to break through the current “red wall” of TTA-UC, paving the way for innovative photochemical systems that enable more precise bioimaging, scalable photocatalysis, and improved energy conversion technologies. 光子上转换（PUC），即利用多个低能光子转换成一个高能光子的过程，在太阳能电池、生物成像和光催化等诸多领域展现出广阔的应用前景。特别是将“不可见”的近红外（NIR）光子转换为可见光，有望应用于深层组织生物成像、可放大光催化以及更高效率的能量转换。三重态聚变上转换（亦称三重态-三重态湮灭上转换，TTA-UC）是一种能将入射低能光子转化为高能激发态的光物理过程，为实现近红外光子上转换（NIR PUC）提供了可能。 胶体量子点（QDs）凭借其组成的多样性和光谱可调性，已成为TTA-UC中理想的三重态敏化剂。然而，能够敏化近红外到可见光上转换的纳米晶体依然十分匮乏，且现有体系无法高效地将近红外二区（NIR-II）光子转换为可见光。在TTA-UC中存在一个明显的效率“红外屏障”（或称“红墙”），即在NIR-II激发下，其上转换量子产率（UCQY）会急剧下降至2%以下。 为了应对这些挑战，我们提出了一种声子辅助的TTA-UC机制，以期突破目前的效率极限。我们假设，量子点-分子界面处的三重态能量传递速率高度依赖于量子限域效应、量子点表面态以及量子点与表面配体之间的电子耦合强度。基于我们近期在AgBiS₂量子点作为三重态敏化剂方面的成功经验（该体系实现了10.5%的近红外一区到可见光上转换量子产率），我们将开发具有低热导率和强量子限域效应的新型近红外量子点。此外，我们还将设计新型三重态介导配体，以调控量子点-分子界面的电子耦合强度。 本项目拟采用以下几项关键策略： 1. 精准合成尺寸、组分及表面化学性质可调的近红外三元和III-V族量子点； 2. 设计与合成作为三重态传输介质的新型表面配体； 3. 构建TTA-UC体系，并结合时间分辨光谱进行超快动力学分析。 我们的目标是开发出性能稳健的近红外二区到可见光上转换体系，其效率将显著超越现有技术。 我们的初步结果揭示了一种新颖的声子辅助TTA-UC机制，该机制能显著提高NIR-II激发下的上转换量子产率。本项目的成功有望突破目前TTA-UC所面临的“红外屏障”，为开发能够实现更精准生物成像、可放大光催化以及更高效能量转换技术的创新光化学体系奠定基础。

16303926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16303926.value: 鋅動力學於甲藻生產二甲硫基丙酸（DMSP）及二甲硫醚（DMS）中之作用

16303926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303926.value: Dimethylsulfoniopropionate (DMSP) and its enzymatic product, dimethyl sulfide (DMS), serve important physiological functions in phytoplankton, including protection against osmotic stress, cryoprotection, and scavenging of reactive oxygen species. Additionally, they play a crucial role in regulating the Earth's climate. The production of DMSP by marine phytoplankton is influenced by light and temperature, as well as by the availability of the trace metal zinc (Zn), which is essential for various biological pathways related to sulphur metabolism. However, the effects of these environmental factors on the biological production of DMS(P) remain poorly understood. To address this gap, the proposed project will be aimed at examining how Zn limitation affects DMSP and DMS production in several model dinoflagellate species under varying light and temperature conditions. Additionally, we will also identify the potential mechanisms that control DMS(P) production under those conditions. The proposed research will provide a comprehensive understanding of dinoflagellate responses to Zn availability across different oceanic regions, particularly in the context of their DMS(P) production. Ultimately, our findings will be incorporated into a biogeochemical model to explore how Zn influences DMS(P) dynamics in the modern ocean and how these processes may evolve in the future under climate change. 二甲硫基丙酸（DMSP）及其酶促產物二甲硫醚（DMS）在浮游植物中具有重要的生理功能，包括抵抗滲透壓逆境、低溫保護，以及清除活性氧物質（ROS）。此外，它們在調節地球氣候方面也扮演著關鍵角色。海洋浮游植物生產DMSP的過程會受到光照、溫度，以及微量金屬鋅（Zn）可利用性的影響，而鋅對於與硫代謝相關的多種生物途徑至關重要。然而，這些環境因子對DMS(P)生物生產的影響尚未被充分研究。在本項目中，我們擬探討在不同光照與溫度條件下，鋅限制如何影響數種模式甲藻物種的DMSP與DMS生產量。我們也將釐清在這些條件下控制DMS(P)生產的潛在機制。本研究旨在提供對於不同海洋區域中甲藻因應鋅可利用性之反應的全面性理解，特別是在其DMS(P)生產方面。最終，我們的研究結果將納入生物地球化學模型中，以探討鋅如何影響現代海洋中的DMS(P)動態，以及這些過程在未來氣候變遷下可能如何改變。

16304926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16304926.value: 正表示論的量子哈密頓約化

16304926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304926.value: The finite-dimensional representation theory of compact quantum groups has been a cornerstone in both mathematics and physics, providing profound insights and applications for nearly four decades. Despite its successes, the extension to the split real case, which holds significant implications for quantum field theory, remains underdeveloped due to persistent analytical challenges. This project aims to further develop the theory of positive representations of split real quantum groups Uq(gR) developed by the PI, which was originally motivated by a special class of representations of Uq(sl(2,R)) studied in the physical context of quantum Liouville’s theory, utilizing positive self-adjoint operators. Recent findings have revealed connections between the cluster algebraic structure of positive representations and non-compact integrable systems, as well as the quantum geometry in higher Teichmüller theory. In prior projects, the PI has successfully generalized the positive representations, including parabolic positive representations and representations at zero Casimirs of split real quantum groups, as well as their modular doubles. These were achieved through combinatorial techniques, specifically embedding quantum groups into certain quantum cluster algebras associated with a punctured disk with two marked points, using a "truncation" method. The current project seeks to formalize this method as a quantum Hamiltonian reduction, focusing on the action of quantum groups on invariant slices of Hilbert spaces. By refining algebraic relations between quantum cluster variables, this approach may extend to broader contexts, particularly quantum cluster algebras linked to G-local systems on various surfaces. An immediate application of this work is a formula for the scalar action of generalized Casimirs under parabolic positive representations, achieved through analytic continuation of representation parameters, enhancing previous combinatorial methods. 有限維緊緻量子群的表示論在數學與物理中一直扮演著基石的角色，近四十年來提供了廣泛的應用。儘管如此，量子場論中具有重要意義的實分裂(split real)情況的推廣，仍因持續存在的解析難題而發展不足。 本研究項目旨在進一步發展首席研究員所建立的實分裂量子群 U_q(g_R) 的正表示論(positive representations)。該理論最初源於對U_q(sl(2,R))的一個特殊表示論的研究，此類表示論以正自伴算子為工具，在量子Liouville 理論的物理背景中出現。近期的研究結果揭示了正表示論的叢代數結構與非緊緻可積系統以及高階Teichmüller理論中的量子幾何之間的聯繫。 在既有的研究項目中，首席研究員已成功推廣正表示理論，包括實分裂量子群的拋物正表示、零Casimir 情形下的表示以及其對偶。此類推廣是透過組合技巧完成的，採用截斷方法，將量子群嵌入到與帶有兩個標記點之穿孔圓盤相關的量子叢代數之中。 本項目擬將上述方法形式化為量子哈密頓量約化，重點研究量子群在Hilbert 空間不變切片上的作用。透過細化量子叢變數之間的代數關係，該方法有望延伸至更廣泛的背景，特別是與各種曲面上的 G-局部系統相關的量子叢代數。此工作的直接應用之一，是給出廣義Casimir在拋物正表示下的純量作用公式，此公式是藉由表示參數的解析延拓而獲得，並進一步提升了先前的組合方法。

16305026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16305026.value: 用於單細胞蛋白質體學研究的高通量、超靈敏微流控二維凝膠電泳晶片的開發

16305026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305026.value: Single-cell proteomics remains one of the most challenging frontiers in molecular biology due to the ultra-low abundance and vast diversity of proteins within individual cells. Existing methods often rely on antibody-based detection or peptide inference, limiting sensitivity and proteome coverage—especially for rare or uncharacterized proteins. To address these limitations, we propose a novel platform that integrates high-throughput microfluidic 2D gel electrophoresis with a triple-focusing signal enhancement strategy. This approach enables direct, antibody-free quantification of proteins at the sub-femtogram level, allowing spatially resolved proteomic mapping of single cells. Our method combines high-throughput protein separation microfluidics, protein electro-elution microfluidics, and multi-level signal amplification to achieve billion-fold sensitivity enhancement. This work would be the first worldwide to directly analyze low-abundance proteins from individual cells, including those with only a few thousand copies. This breakthrough will unlock new capabilities in cancer biology, neuroscience, and organoid research by enabling the detection of rare proteins and revealing cellular heterogeneity with unprecedented resolution. The platform also offers broad applicability for general 2D PAGE analysis, cell-cell interaction studies, and organoid profiling, paving the way for transformative advances in diagnostics, therapeutics, and personalized medicine. 由於單一細胞內蛋白質豐度極低且種類繁多，單細胞蛋白質體學仍然是分子生物學中最具挑戰性的前沿領域之一。現有方法往往依賴基於抗體的檢測或基於肽段的推斷，這限制了靈敏度和蛋白質組覆蓋範圍——對於稀有或未被表達的蛋白質尤其如此。為了克服這些局限性，我們提出了一種新型平台，將高通量微流控二維凝膠電泳與三重聚焦訊號增強策略相結合。這種方法能夠實現亞飛克（sub-femtogram）水平蛋白質的直接、無抗體定量，從而實現單細胞的空間分辨蛋白質體圖譜繪製。 我們的方法結合了高通量蛋白質分離微流控技術、蛋白質電洗脫微流控技術以及多層次訊號放大技術，實現了靈敏度高達十億倍的提升。這項工作將成為全球首個能夠直接分析單一細胞中低豐度蛋白質（包括拷貝數僅為數千的蛋白質）的技術。這項突破將透過檢測稀有蛋白質並以空前的分辨率揭示細胞異質性，為癌症生物學、神經科學和類器官研究開闢新的能力。該平台也廣泛適用於常規二維聚丙烯酰胺凝膠電泳（2D PAGE）分析、細胞間相互作用研究以及類器官圖譜分析，為診斷、治療和個人化醫療領域的變革性進展鋪平道路。

16305226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16305226.value: 透過層級調控構建發光共價有機框架

16305226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
16305226.value: Prof Sun, Jianwei Prof Tang, Ben Zhong

16305226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305226.value: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as a revolutionary class of crystalline porous materials distinguished by their structural precision, extensive surface areas, and finely tunable functionalities. Since the pioneering work by Yaghi and colleagues in 2005, the field has witnessed remarkable progress under the guidance of reticular chemistry, giving rise to diverse architectural motifs such as two-dimensional layers, three-dimensional networks, and intricately woven structures. The inherent modularity of COFs enables the straightforward integration of functional moieties into molecular building blocks, thereby facilitating their application across broad domains including chemical sensing, gas storage, photocatalysis, asymmetric catalysis, molecular separation, energy storage, and photodetection. Particularly promising is their potential in photoluminescence, where the crystalline frameworks allow for precisely controlled extension of π-conjugation along predefined directions, providing ideal platforms for the development of advanced luminescent materials. However, achieving highly emissive COFs remains challenging due to the ubiquitous problem of aggregation-caused quenching. Even when constructed from emissive building blocks, most COFs exhibit limited fluorescence because their π-π stacked structures, which promote non-radiative decay of photoexcited states. The choice of linkage chemistry is therefore critical, as exemplified by the contrasting behavior (highly emissive vs no emission) of tetraphenylethene units showing aggregation-induced emission (AIE) connected via rigid boronate ester linkages versus flexible imine bonds. Building on our previous breakthrough in constructing an sp² carbon-conjugated COF incorporating AIE luminogens (AIEgens) as effective pyroptosis inducers for cancer immunotherapy, in this work, we propose a comprehensive hierarchical modulation strategy to address these challenges systematically. Our approach integrates three fundamental levels: (1) linkage chemistry for the restriction of intramolecular motions through the introduction of rigid conjugated linkage groups; (2) ligand chemistry for incorporating AIEgens into COF structures to maximize the light emission in the aggregate state and impart unique material properties and (3) topological chemistry for controlling the framework dimensionality from 2.5D to 3D architectures while tailoring particle morphology. This integrated methodology will enable systematic elucidation of structure–property relationships and overcome the fundamental limitations of fluorescence quenching. Successful implementation of this strategy will establish a versatile platform for the creation of bright, tunable luminescent materials with significant potential in advanced sensing, high-resolution bioimaging, innovative therapeutic applications, and next-generation optoelectronic devices. By bridging fundamental material design with practical applications, this research seeks to unlock the full potential of COFs in photoluminescence and related fields, thereby paving the way for transformative technological breakthroughs. 共價有機框架（COFs）已成為一類創新的結晶多孔材料，以其結構精確性、廣泛的表面積和可精細調節的功能性而聞名。自2005年Yaghi及其同事的開創性工作以來，該領域在網狀化學的引導下取得了顯著進展，衍生出多種結構樣式，如二維層狀、三維網狀及複雜編織結構。COFs 固有的模組化特性，使其能直接將功能基團整合至分子構建基元中，從而推動其在化學感測、氣體儲存、光催化、非對稱催化、分子分離、能量儲存及光電檢測等廣泛領域的應用。特別值得注意的是它們在光致發光方面的潛力，晶體框架允許沿預定方向精確控制π-共軛的延伸，成為發展先進發光材料的理想平台。然而，實現高發光效率的COFs仍然面臨挑戰，因為聚集引起的淬滅（ACQ）是普遍存在的問題。即使由發光基團建構的COFs，由於其π-π堆疊結構促進了光激發狀態的非輻射衰減，展現的螢光亦相當有限。因此，連接化學的選擇至關重要；正如具備聚集誘導發光（AIE）特性的四苯基乙烯單元所示，其通過剛性硼酸酯鍵與柔性亞胺鍵連接時展現出鮮明的發光對比（高發光 vs 無發光），恰好印證了這一點。 基於我們之前在構建摻入AIE發光團的sp2碳共軛COF中取得的突破，這項工作提出了一個全面的層級調控策略，以系統性地解決這些挑戰。我們的方法整合了三個基本層次：（1）通過引入剛性共軛連結基團來限制分子內運動的連結化學；（2）通過將AIE發光團整合進COF結構中，顯著提升聚集狀態下的發光並賦予獨特材料性能的配體化學；（3）透過控制框架維度從2.5D到3D架構並調整顆粒形態的拓撲化學。這一綜合方法將系統性地闡明結構和性能之間的關係，並克服螢光淬滅的基本限制。該策略的成功實施將建立一個多功能平台，用於創造明亮、可調的發光材料，在進階傳感、高解析度生物成像、創新治療應用和下一代光電裝置中具有重要潛力。通過將基礎材料設計與實際應用相結合，本研究旨在充分發揮COFs在光致發光及相關領域的潛力，為變革性技術的重大突破奠定基礎。

16305526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16305526.value: 结构化随机图的谱分析

16305526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305526.value: Random graphs are central objects in modern mathematics, computer science, and data science, providing flexible models for networks and powerful testing grounds for theoretical ideas. This proposal will explore two broad classes of structured random graphs with a unifying focus on their spectral and expansion properties, which capture how well-connected and robust these networks are. The first direction for research concerns random geometric and latent kernel graphs, where nodes are associated with hidden feature vectors and edges are formed according to geometric similarity or probabilistic kernels. These models include classical random geometric graphs, Gaussian mixture graphs, and the widely studied stochastic block model. They are highly relevant to modern data analysis, where data points often lie in high-dimensional feature spaces. However, despite much progress, existing results largely focus on asymptotic limits and provide little guidance for finite, practical settings. We propose to develop precise spectral guarantees for algorithms based on eigenvalues and eigenvectors, which are the main tools for revealing hidden community structure in such networks. In addition, we will establish sharp concentration results for small subgraph counts such as edges and triangles, which are central to statistical testing and motif-based methods in network science. The second direction of research will investigate the robustness of expansion in random regular graphs, one of the most important families of graphs in combinatorics and theoretical computer science. Random regular graphs are known to be nearly optimal expanders, and recent breakthroughs have shown that a positive fraction are exactly optimal Ramanujan expanders. A central question is how this remarkable property behaves under perturbations that reduce randomness. We will study edge percolation, where edges are randomly deleted, and analyze how the spectral gap is affected as the graph becomes sparser. We will also study algebraic constraints such as rotation or reflection symmetries, which restrict randomness and lead to structured families of graphs that remain regular but may lose their property of expansion.
