Together, these two lines of inquiry will apply new tools from random matrix theory, probability, and spectral analysis to central questions in combinatorics, while deepening connections with network science and data analysis. 随机图是现代数学、计算机科学和数据科学中的核心研究对象，它们为网络提供了灵活的建模工具，也为各种理论思想提供了强有力的检验平台。本项目将研究两大类结构化随机图，并以其谱性质与扩张性质为统一的核心关注点——这些性质刻画了网络的连通程度与稳健性。 第一个研究方向关注随机几何图与隐核图，其中每个节点关联着一个隐藏的特征向量，边则根据几何相似度或概率核来生成。这类模型包括经典的随机几何图、高斯混合图，以及被广泛研究的随机块模型。它们与现代数据分析高度相关，因为数据点往往位于高维特征空间之中。然而，尽管已有诸多进展，现有结果大多聚焦于渐近极限，对有限规模的实际应用场景几乎没有提供指导。我们计划为基于特征值与特征向量的算法建立精确的谱理论保证——这些正是揭示此类网络中隐藏社群结构的主要工具。此外，我们还将为小型子图计数（如边和三角形）建立锐利的集中不等式，而这类计数在网络科学中的统计检验和基于模体的方法中占据核心地位。 第二个研究方向将考察随机正则图中扩张性的稳健性。随机正则图是组合数学与理论计算机科学中最重要的图族之一，已知它们是接近最优的扩张子，而近期的突破性成果表明，其中有正比例的图恰好是最优的 Ramanujan 扩张子。一个核心问题是：当施加削弱随机性的扰动时，这一卓越性质将如何变化。我们将研究边渗流，即随机删除边的过程，并分析随着图变得更加稀疏，谱隙会受到怎样的影响。我们还将研究诸如旋转或反射对称性之类的代数约束，这些约束限制了随机性，从而产生结构化的图族——它们保持正则性，但可能会失去扩张性。 这两条研究主线将把随机矩阵理论、概率论与谱分析中的新工具应用于组合数学的核心问题，同时深化其与网络科学和数据分析之间的联系。

16306226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16306226.value: 利用 N-雜環卡賓催化開拓不對稱烷基化新方法

16306226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306226.value: The aim of the proposed project will be to transform how chemists build chiral molecules by developing new strategies for enantioselective alkylation using N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) catalysis. Chiral alkyl groups are essential components of many pharmaceuticals and bioactive molecules, yet current methods for their introduction are limited in scope and efficiency. Although NHCs are powerful and versatile catalysts, their potential in asymmetric alkylation remains largely untapped. The proposed study will address this gap through three complementary approaches. 1. Radical-based alkylation of non-Breslow intermediates: We will design dual catalytic systems combining chiral NHCs with transition-metal mediators to enable direct enantioselective radical alkylation of homoenolates using common alkyl electrophiles. This strategy will overcome key thermodynamic barriers, offering high stereocontrol in the formation of β-branched chiral carboxylates. 2. Closed-shell SN2 alkylation: Building on recent breakthroughs, we will expand the scope of SN2-type alkylation beyond activated substrates. By isolating and characterizing stable homoenolate intermediates, we will use mechanistic insights and computational tools to design catalysts capable of accommodating simple enals and unactivated alkyl halides, creating a broadly applicable platform for stereoselective bond formation. 3. Non-covalent activation: We will explore an alternative paradigm in which NHCs will function as strong Brønsted bases to organize reactive partners through non-covalent interactions, eliminating the need for covalent adduct formation. This approach will provide access to a wider range of pronucleophiles and offer a complementary route to asymmetric alkylation. The proposed project will integrate experimental studies with computational modeling and data-driven optimization to achieve precise control over the site and stereoselectivity. By addressing long-standing challenges of reactivity and selectivity, the proposed project will offer new catalytic principles and practical methods for constructing chiral building blocks. These advances will not only expand the chemical space accessible to NHC catalysis but also provide powerful tools for drug discovery and complex molecule synthesis, redefining the possibilities in asymmetric alkylation. 本計劃旨在開創合成手性分子的新方法，透過發展以N-雜環卡賓（NHC）催化為核心的不對稱烷基化反應，改變化學家建構手性分子的方式。手性烷基是許多藥物及生物活性分子的關鍵組成部分，但現有合成這些結構的方法仍受到適用範圍及效率的限制。儘管 NHC 是一類功能強大且用途廣泛的催化劑，其在不對稱烷基化方面的潛力至今仍未被充分發掘。本研究將透過三個相輔相成的研究方向來突破這項瓶頸。 首先，我們將開發以自由基反應為基礎的烷基化方法。我們會結合手性 NHC 催化劑與過渡金屬媒介劑，建立雙催化系統，使常見的烷基化試劑能夠直接與特定反應中間體發生不對稱自由基反應。此策略有望克服現有方法的重要限制，並高效製備具有精確三維結構的手性羧酸衍生物，而這些化合物是藥物研發中十分重要的分子骨架。 其次，我們將拓展不對稱 SN2 的烷基化反應。目前這類反應主要適用於少數經特別活化的反應物。我們將分離並研究關鍵反應中間體，結合反應機理分析及電腦模擬，設計新型催化劑，使簡單及更常見的原料也能順利參與反應。這將建立一個更具普適性的技術平台，用於精準構築具有特定立體結構的化學鍵。 第三，我們將探索一種新的催化模式。在這個模式下，NHC 不再透過與反應物形成共價鍵來發揮作用，而是利用非共價作用力將反應物組織及活化，從而促進反應進行。這種方法可望擴展可使用原料的種類，並為不對稱烷基化提供一條全新的途徑。 本研究將結合實驗研究、電腦模擬及數據驅動的優化策略，以精確控制反應發生的位置及所形成手性分子的立體結構。透過解決長期困擾有機合成領域的反應性與選擇性問題，本計劃將建立新的催化原理，並發展實用的手性分子合成方法。研究成果不僅將拓展 NHC 催化的應用範圍，更有望為新藥研發及複雜分子合成提供重要工具，為不對稱烷基化領域開啟新的可能性。

16306426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16306426.value: 形塑內波驅動珊瑚礁氣候避難所的生物地球化學動態

16306426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306426.value: Coral reef ecosystems, together with the extraordinary biodiversity and ecosystem services they support, are increasingly threatened by climate change, deoxygenation, and coastal pollution. These pressures are especially acute within the Coral Triangle (CT) – the global centre of coral diversity and home to more than 120 million people who depend on reefs for food, livelihoods, and coastal protection. While the decline of shallow reefs has been widely documented, deeper reef habitats remain poorly understood, even though they may serve as climate refuges that help sustain coral ecosystems during marine heatwaves. In these deeper zones, internal waves – powerful subsurface oscillations driven by tides – can bring cooler, nutrient-rich water upward onto reefs, potentially protecting corals from heat stress. Yet such upwelling can also transport low-oxygen or particle-laden water, altering light, oxygen, and food conditions in ways that may either enhance or compromise reef resilience. The biogeochemical functionality of these potential refuges, whether they provide conditions that support coral growth and productivity, remains largely unknown. Building on an ongoing Research Grants Council (RGC) project that is quantifying internal-wave-driven temperature variability across reef depths in Indonesia, this study will extend the framework to investigate biogeochemical dynamics essential to reef function. Guided by high-resolution ocean models, long-term instruments will be deployed across reef slopes (10–100 m) in Bali to record dissolved oxygen, chlorophyll, turbidity, and light with fine temporal resolution. These observations will capture how internal-wave activity influences oxygen supply, particulate food availability, and light penetration, revealing trade-offs between physical buffering and biological sustainability. The field data will be integrated with state-of-the-art numerical ocean models to improve predictions of where and when coral reef refuges can persist under changing climatic and oceanographic conditions. By combining advanced physical and biogeochemical monitoring with modelling, the research will create a new framework for identifying functionally viable coral refuges – those that are not only thermally protected but also biogeochemically sustainable. This pioneering study will generate the first continuous, depth-resolved biogeochemical records from internal-wave-dominated reefs in the CT. Its results will directly inform regional conservation and restoration planning, enhance understanding of how reefs respond to ocean heating and deoxygenation, and contribute to global efforts to safeguard coral ecosystems in an increasingly hot, oxygen-poor, and darkened ocean. 珊瑚礁生態系及其所支撐的高度生物多樣性與生態系服務，正日益受到氣候變遷、海洋缺氧與沿岸污染的威脅。此等壓力在珊瑚大三角區（Coral Triangle, CT）尤為顯著；該區為全球珊瑚多樣性的核心區域，亦有超過 1.2 億人口仰賴珊瑚礁提供食物、生計來源與海岸防護。儘管淺水珊瑚礁的退化現象已受到廣泛記錄，較深水層的珊瑚礁棲地仍缺乏充分了解；然而，這些深層棲地可能作為氣候庇護區，在海洋熱浪發生期間協助維繫珊瑚礁生態系。 於這些較深水域中，內波（一種由潮汐所驅動的強烈次表層振盪）可將較低溫且富含營養鹽的海水向上輸送至珊瑚礁區，因而具有降低珊瑚熱壓力的潛在作用。然而，此一湧升過程亦可能伴隨低溶氧或富含懸浮顆粒之水團的輸送，進而改變光照、氧氣與食物供應條件；這些改變可能促進，也可能削弱珊瑚礁的韌性。因此，這些潛在庇護區是否具備支持珊瑚生長與生產力的環境條件，亦即其生物地球化學功能性，目前仍大多未知。 本研究奠基於一項進行中的研究資助局（Research Grants Council, RGC）計畫；該計畫正量化印尼珊瑚礁不同水深間由內波所驅動的溫度變異。本研究將進一步擴展此研究架構，探討維持珊瑚礁功能所需之關鍵生物地球化學動態。在高解析度海洋模式的指引下，本研究將於峇里島珊瑚礁斜坡不同水深（10–100 公尺）布放長期觀測儀器，以高時間解析度記錄溶解氧、葉綠素、濁度與光照。這些觀測資料將用以捕捉內波活動如何影響氧氣供應、顆粒性食物可利用性與光線穿透，進而揭示物理性熱緩衝作用與生物永續性之間的權衡關係。 野外觀測資料將進一步與先進數值海洋模式整合，以提升對珊瑚礁庇護區在變動的氣候與海洋環境條件下，於何處及何時得以持續存在的預測能力。透過結合先進的物理與生物地球化學監測及模式模擬，本研究將建立一套新的分析架構，用以辨識具功能可行性的珊瑚礁庇護區——亦即不僅具有熱環境保護效果，同時亦能維持生物地球化學永續性的庇護區。 本開創性研究將產出珊瑚大三角區內首批來自內波主導珊瑚礁環境、且具連續性與深度解析度的生物地球化學紀錄。研究成果將可直接為區域保育與復育規劃提供寶貴意見，深化對珊瑚礁如何回應海洋升溫與缺氧現象的理解，並有助於全球在日益高溫、低氧且光照減弱的海洋環境中，維護珊瑚礁生態系的相關努力。

16306626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16306626.value: 关于Zetterberg型纠错码的覆盖半径问题的研究

16306626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306626.value: In this proposal, we investigate the covering radius problem for Zetterberg-type codes, a prominent family of cyclic codes renowned for their desirable properties in practical applications and their deep connections with various areas of mathematics such as number theory and algebraic geometry. By employing new techniques from number theory, we have obtained both preliminary and original results on the covering radius of generalized Zetterberg codes over finite fields of even and odd characteristic, thereby identifying an infinite family of quasi-perfect and maximum codes. Building upon these findings, we plan to further explore related problems, such as the covering radius of subcodes of generalized Zetterberg codes and the generalized covering radius of Zetterberg codes -- a topic that has recently attracted growing research interest. 在本项目中，我们研究 Zetterberg 型纠错码的覆盖半径问题。Zetterberg 型纠错码是一类著名的循环码，因其在实际应用中的优良性质以及与数论、代数几何等诸多数学分支之间的深刻联系而备受关注。借助受数论启发的新方法，我们已在偶特征和奇特征域上广义 Zetterberg 码的覆盖半径方面获得了若干初步且具有原创性的结果，并由此确定了一个无穷的拟完美码与极大码族。在这些成果的基础上，我们计划进一步探讨相关问题，例如广义 Zetterberg 码的子码的覆盖半径，以及 Zetterberg 码的广义覆盖半径----这是当代编码理论中一个活跃且迅速发展的研究方向。

16307226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16307226.value: 低秩求解器与数据驱动模型降阶求解辐射输运方程的统一框架探索

16307226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307226.value: Radiative transfer equation (RTE) describes particles that propagate through and interact with a background medium, with applications in medical imaging, astrophysics, and nuclear engineering. In parametric settings such as sensitivity analysis and optical tomography, RTE must be solved repeatedly, posing significant computational challenges due to its high dimensionality. Low-rank solvers and data-driven reduced order models (ROMs) are two main dimensionality reduction strategies. Low-rank solvers for RTE utilize phase-space low-rank structures by representing solutions as low-rank matrix or tensor decompositions, but typically do not exploit low-rank structures in the parameter space of parametric RTE. Conversely, data-driven ROMs exploit parameter-space low-rank structures but rely on full-rank data that ignore phase-space low-rank structures, demanding substantial offline resources in its construction. The complementary strengths of these two methods suggest potential integrations, but such integrations have not been systematically investigated for RTE. This proposal aims to fill this gap by integrating low-rank sovlers with data-driven ROMs to exploit low-rank structures in both the phase and parameter spaces of parametric RTE. First, we propose low-rank ROMs (LR-ROMs) that construct reduced bases from low-rank data offline and leverage low-rank solvers online to fully exploit phase-space structures while bypassing the need for full-rank data. Additionally, we will establish error estimates for LR-ROMs by analyzing projection errors and errors from online low-rank solvers. Second, to develop more efficient and flexible low-rank iterative solvers for RTE, we propose a rank-adaptive source iteration with diffusion synthetic acceleration (SI-DSA) by designing a novel projection-based angle sampling approach to enable rank-adaptive transport sweeps. The convergence rate of the proposed method will be analyzed by extending the Fourier convergence analysis for full-rank SI-DSA to the low-rank setting. Finally, building on the proposed LR-ROMs and rank-adaptive iterative solver, we propose a low-rank ROM-enhanced SA preconditioner (LR-RESA) to accelerate iterative solvers for parametric RTE by exploiting low-rank structures in both the phase and parameter spaces. We will establish the convergence theory of low-rank iterative solvers with LR-RESA preconditioner by analyzing how LR-ROMs and low-rank truncations affect the convergence rate, leveraging theories of inexact and low-rank iterative methods. This analysis will guide the selection of truncation tolerances. The proposed research will establish a foundation for efficient dimensionality reduction of RTE, advancing computational tools for applications in related fields such as optical tomography and proton therapy. Our framework also has the potential to be extended to other kinetic equations. 辐射输运方程（RTE）描述粒子在背景介质中的传播与相互作用，在医学成像、天体物理学和核工程等领域具有广泛应用。在敏感性分析和光学成像等参数化场景中，RTE需要被反复求解，其高维特性带来了巨大的计算挑战。 低秩求解器和数据驱动的降阶模型（ROM）是两种主要解决这一挑战的降维策略。低秩求解器利用相空间中的低秩结构，将解表示为低秩矩阵或张量分解，但通常不利用参数化RTE在参数空间中的低秩结构。相反，数据驱动的ROM利用参数空间的低秩结构，却依赖忽略相空间低秩结构的全秩数据，导致离线构建阶段需要大量计算资源。 这两种方法的互补优势暗示了潜在的融合可能，但此类努力尚未在RTE降维中得到系统探索。本提案旨在填补这一空白，通过整合低秩求解器与数据驱动ROM，充分利用参数化RTE在相空间和参数空间中的低秩结构。 首先，我们提出低秩降阶模型（LR-ROMs），直接利用低秩数据离线构建降阶基，并在线借助低秩求解器以充分挖掘相空间结构，同时避免对全秩数据的需求。此外，我们将通过分析投影误差和在线低秩求解器引入的误差，为LR-ROMs建立误差估计。 其次，为了开发更高效、灵活的低秩迭代求解器用于RTE，我们提出一种结合扩散综合加速（SI-DSA）的秩自适应源迭代方法，通过设计一种新颖的基于投影的角度采样方法，以非侵入方式实现秩自适应输运扫描。我们将通过扩展全秩SI-DSA的傅里叶收敛分析，研究该方法的收敛速度。 最后，基于所提出的LR-ROMs、秩自适应迭代求解器以及我们初步发展的全秩ROM增强SA预处理器，我们提出一种低秩ROM增强SA预处理器（LR-RESA），通过利用相空间和参数空间中的低秩结构来加速参数化RTE的迭代求解。其收敛理论将结合非精确迭代求解器和低秩迭代方法的分析来建立，为LR-ROMs及低秩分解中截断容差的选择提供理论指导。 本项研究将通过整合低秩求解器与ROM，为RTE的高效降维奠定基础，推动医学成像与应用物理（如光学层析成像、质子治疗和聚变能源）领域计算工具的发展。所构建的框架还有潜力拓展至其他动理学方程。

16307326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16307326.value: 球面值偏微分方程之保結構快速掃描法

16307326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307326.value: Many modern scientific and engineering problems involve data that represent directions or orientations, rather than simple numerical values. Examples include the direction of magnetization in magnetic materials, the alignment of molecules in liquid crystals, the orientation of colors in digital images, and the paths of seismic waves as they travel through the Earth. In mathematics, such quantities are described as functions that always lie on the surface of a sphere. This spherical structure is essential for capturing the physics of the problem, but conventional numerical methods often ignore it. As a result, standard computations can drift away from the sphere, producing unstable solutions or results that lack physical meaning. This project develops new computational methods that are structure-preserving. That is, they are carefully designed to respect the spherical geometry at every step of the calculation. We will begin by developing efficient solvers that can handle large-scale problems where speed is critical, and then extend them to high-order methods capable of capturing fine details with high accuracy. These new algorithms will be applied to practical challenges such as seismic imaging, where accurately reconstructing the Earth’s subsurface structure from recorded wave signals is vital for resource exploration and earthquake hazard assessment. At the same time, we will establish the mathematical foundations of these methods, proving when and why they work, and ensuring that their predictions are both stable and reliable. By combining theoretical analysis, algorithmic innovation, and real-world applications, this project will create robust tools for simulating systems in which orientation and direction play a central role. The outcomes will have an impact across multiple fields, including physics, materials science, geophysics, and imaging, and will contribute to the broader goal of developing computational techniques that faithfully capture the geometry of the natural world. 現代科學與工程中的許多重要問題，都涉及描述方向或取向的資料，而非單純的數值。例如，磁性材料中的磁化方向、液晶分子的排列方向、數位影像中的色彩方向，以及地震波在地球內部傳播的路徑等。在數學上，這些量可表示為取值於球面上的函數（球面值函數）。此球面幾何結構對於正確描述相關物理現象至關重要，但傳統數值方法往往忽略此幾何限制，使得計算結果偏離球面，進而導致數值不穩定，甚至產生不具物理意義的解。 本計畫旨在發展一系列保結構的數值計算方法，在整個計算過程中嚴格維持球面幾何結構。我們將首先發展適用於大規模問題的高效率快速求解演算法，以滿足高效能運算的需求，並進一步建立高階數值方法，以兼顧高精度與細部結構的解析能力。所提出的方法將應用於多項重要實務問題，例如地震成像，透過分析量測到的地震波訊號，精確重建地下介質結構，進而支援天然資源探勘及地震災害評估。同時，本計畫亦將建立完整的數學理論基礎，證明所發展方法的收斂性、穩定性及可靠性，確保其計算結果具有嚴謹的理論保證。 本計畫結合理論分析、演算法創新與實際應用，將建立一套適用於方向與取向主導問題的穩健數值計算工具。預期研究成果將廣泛應用於物理、材料科學、地球物理、醫學與科學影像等領域，並促進兼顧幾何結構與物理特性的下一代數值計算技術發展，為自然界幾何現象的高精度模擬提供新的理論與方法。

16307426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16307426.value: 多水平因素下的协变量自适应随机化方法研究

16307426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307426.value: Clinical trials are the gold standard for learning whether new treatments truly help patients, yet modern trials often face a practical obstacle: participants come from many different clinics or hospitals, and each site may enroll only a few people. When researchers try to balance treatment assignments across a large number of sites, along with important characteristics such as age, sex, or biomarker levels, standard tools can struggle. Groups within each site can become uneven, results less precise, and the evaluation of treatment effect may be obscured. This project develops a coherent toolkit that improves both how trials are designed and how the data are analyzed when there are factors with many levels (“sites” or other long-factor variables). First, we provide principled methods that treat site-to-site variation in a statistically efficient way by utilizing mixed-effect models. Rather than fitting a separate fixed parameter for every site or ignoring site differences entirely, we use models that “borrow strength” across sites. This stabilizes estimates when some sites are small, preserves fair comparisons between treatment groups, and clarifies how modern randomization procedures that actively balance key variables during enrollment translate into higher power and reliable error control. Second, we address the challenge of having too many categories by grouping levels that behave similarly. We begin with a fine-grained view, estimating how much each site appears to differ, and then merge sites whose patterns align. A robust version safeguards against imperfect groupings so that an occasional misclassified site does not distort results. The outcome is a simpler, more interpretable structure that retains the signal while reducing noise. Third, we extend these ideas to continuous covariates such as age or laboratory values. Instead of relying on a single threshold (for example, “under 65” versus “65 and over”), we form small bins and then merge bins, even when they are not adjacent, if they show similar relationships to outcomes. This produces a small set of data-driven categories that are easy to explain, improve balance when assigning treatments, and enhance precision at the analysis stage. By unifying smarter design with robust, interpretable analysis, the project aims to make trials more informative without increasing participant burden. The expected impact is clearer results, better use of available data, and practical guidance that trial teams can adopt immediately in protocols and statistical analysis plans. 临床试验是判断新疗法是否真正惠及患者的黄金标准，但现代试验常面临一个现实难题：受试者来自众多诊所或医院，而每个中心可能只招募少量患者。当研究者希望在大量中心以及年龄、性别、生物标志物等重要特征之间平衡治疗分配时，传统方法往往力不从心，可能导致中心内组别不均衡、估计精准度下降，并影响治疗效果评估。 本项目拟建立一套统一工具，用于处理含有多水平因素（如研究中心或其他长因子变量）的试验设计与数据分析问题。首先，我们利用混合效应模型，以统计上更有效的方式刻画中心间差异。相比为每个中心单独拟合固定参数或完全忽略中心差异，该方法可在中心之间“借力”，从而在小样本中心中稳定估计，保持治疗组间公平比较，并阐明现代动态平衡随机化如何提升检验效能并保证错误率控制。 其次，我们通过合并表现相似的水平来应对类别过多的问题。具体而言，先细致估计各中心的差异，再将模式相近的中心合并；同时引入稳健版本，避免少数误分中心对结果造成明显干扰。这样可得到更简洁、可解释的结构，在保留信号的同时降低噪声。 第三，我们将上述思想推广到年龄、实验室指标等连续协变量。不同于仅使用单一阈值划分，我们先构造小区间，再将与结局关系相似的区间合并，即使它们并不相邻。由此得到少量数据驱动、易解释的类别，既有助于治疗分配时的平衡，也能提高分析精度。 通过统一更智能的设计与稳健、可解释的分析，本项目旨在不增加受试者负担的前提下提升试验信息量。预期成果包括更清晰的结论、更充分的数据利用，以及可直接写入试验方案和统计分析计划的实践指南。

16307526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16307526.value: 有機化學反應機理之自動資訊提取以應用於預測建模與機理數據分析

16307526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307526.value: Understanding organic chemical reaction mechanisms, i.e., the stepwise electron-flow pathways that govern chemical transformations, is essential for predicting product formation and optimizing reaction conditions, driving innovation in pharmaceuticals, chemical manufacturing, and materials science. However, progress in data-driven mechanistic modeling has been limited by the absence of large-scale, structured datasets. While mechanistic information is abundant in textbooks and journals, extracting it automatically remains a major technical challenge. The complexity and stylistic diversity of electron-pushing diagrams make them difficult for computational tools to parse. Previous semi-automatic efforts have relied on encoding mechanistic templates by experts and applying them to reaction instances. While valuable, these approaches are inherently constrained by the scope of manually coded templates and cannot capture the diversity of mechanisms discussed in the broader literature. Our project aims to address this bottleneck by developing an end-to-end pipeline for automated extraction of mechanistic data from the literature. Building on our prior success in chemical image understanding (MolNexTR, RxnIM, ChemEAGLE) and supported by expert collaborators in organic chemistry and AI, we are well-positioned to accomplish this goal. First, we will train a U-Net model for precise arrow segmentation and integrate its output with large language models capable of multimodal reasoning to interpret mechanism information embedded in chemical diagrams. We will deliver a validated pipeline that can automatically convert mechanistic diagrams into step-wise, machine readable data, with the following features: (i) accurately detecting and interpreting electron-pushing arrows, and (ii) handling the heterogeneity of diagram styles and quality. We will then use this pipeline to process raw diagrams with various reaction classes and layouts in chemistry textbooks and publications, constructing a high-quality, large-scale database of reaction mechanisms. Building on this dataset, we will explore predictive modeling of electron flow and perform data analyses to identify trends and patterns in mechanistic reasoning, moving beyond individual reactions to uncover generalizable mechanistic knowledge. The ultimate outcome of this work will be a suite of user-friendly tools, including the software for mechanism data extraction and hypothesis generation, and a website hosting the extracted mechanism data for easy navigation. These tools will assist chemists in formulating reaction hypotheses, rationalizing unsuccessful outcomes, and making more informed choices in synthetic planning, thereby accelerating progress in fields such as drug discovery and materials science. 理解有機化學反應機理，即控制化學轉化的逐步電子流動路徑，對於預測產物生成及優化反應條件至關重要。這項知識是製藥、化學製造及材料科學創新的基石。然而，數據驅動的機理建模進展一直受到缺乏大規模、結構化數據集的限制。機理資訊在教科書和學術期刊中俯拾皆是，但由於電子推動圖複雜多樣、風格各異，且難以被計算工具自動解讀，因此從中自動提取資訊在技術上仍極具挑戰。過往的半自動化方法依賴專家編碼機理模板，再將其應用於反應實例。儘管此類方法極具價值，但其成效本質上受限於手動編碼模板的涵蓋範圍，無法捕捉更廣泛文獻中所討論的機理多樣性。 我們的項目旨在開發一個端到端的自動化提取流程，從文獻中系統性地抽取機理數據，以突破上述瓶頸。基於我們在化學圖像理解方面的既有成果（MolNexTR、RxnIM、ChemEAGLE），並在有機化學及人工智能領域的專家協作下，我們已具備充分條件應對兩大核心挑戰：(i) 準確檢測並解讀電子推動箭頭，以及 (ii) 處理圖表風格與畫質上的差異性。為此，我們將訓練一個 U-Net 模型以進行箭頭的精確分割，並將其輸出與具備多模態推理能力的大型語言模型整合。這種綜合方法能將複雜的機理圖轉化為逐步、機器可讀的表示形式，從而捕捉中間體及電子流動的完整資訊。其後，我們會設計一個穩健的工作流程，用於處理來自教科書及學術出版物的多樣化反應類別與版面配置。 本研究主要成果將包括 (i) 一套經實證驗證的機理數據提取流程，以及 (ii) 一個高品質、大規模的反應機理數據庫。借助此資源，我們將探索電子流動的預測建模，並進行數據分析，以識別機理推理中的趨勢與規律，從而超越個別反應的範疇，歸納出更具普遍性的機理知識。雖然此框架初期建基於既有文獻知識，但它將為生成及排列合理機理假設提供一個可擴展的基礎，最終有助於以更理性、更高效的方式進行反應設計與發現。

16307726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16307726.value: 基於隨機照明的反散射問題之理論與計算框架

16307726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307726.value: Inverse scattering theory underpins imaging modalities such as radar, sonar, medical imaging, and non-destructive evaluation, where the aim is to infer the presence of unknown scatterers from measured scattered waves. Despite major progress, devising inverse methods with provable resolution guarantees that may break the classical diffraction limit remains a challenging task. Recent super-resolution results for inverse source problems show that the diffraction limit can be surpassed for point sources under favorable signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), but comparable theory for extended scatterers under realistic data constraints is far less developed. This proposal seeks to build a theoretical and computational framework for the inverse scattering problem of extended targets when only far-field patterns are available and the incident fields are unknown but statistically characterized. Such settings arise naturally under passive or opportunistic illumination, including ambient-noise tomography driven by microseisms and passive ultrasound/photoacoustics. The goal is to localize the support of the scatterers and to determine, with theoretical guarantees, when distinct components are resolvable, especially below the classical diffraction limit. The PI will analyze two representative scenarios: 1) multiple penetrable scatterers; 2) multiple impenetrable scatterers. For each case, the PI will develop an efficient localization method and establish rigorous resolution bounds, demonstrating the super-resolution capability of the proposed method in certain regimes. The results will provide a theoretical foundation as well as efficient high-resolution imaging methods for passive remote sensing, seismology, ocean acoustics, biomedical imaging, and nondestructive evaluation. 反散射理論是雷達、聲納、醫學成像與無損檢測等成像技術的基礎，其目標是透過量測散射波來推斷未知散射體的存在。儘管該領域已取得重大進展，但如何構建具有可證明解析度保證、並有望突破經典繞射極限的反演方法，仍然是一項具挑戰性的任務。近期關於反源問題的超解析研究顯示，在有利的訊噪比（SNR）條件下，可以突破點源的繞射極限；然而，針對延展散射體的相應理論研究仍相當不足。 本計畫旨在建立一套理論與計算框架，用於研究延展目標的反散射問題，其中僅能取得遠場散射圖樣，且入射場未知但具有統計特性。此類情境自然出現在被動或機會式照明條件下，包括由微震驅動的環境雜訊層析成像，以及被動式超音波／光聲成像等。研究目標是在理論保證下定位散射體的支撐區域，並確定在何種條件下不同組成部分可以被解析，特別是在低於經典繞射極限的情況下。 計畫主持人將分析兩類具有代表性的情境：（1）多個可穿透散射體；（2）多個不可穿透散射體。針對每一種情況，將發展高效率的定位方法並建立嚴格的解析度界限，在特定參數區間內證明所提方法具備超解析能力。研究成果將為被動遙測、地震學、海洋聲學、生物醫學成像以及無損檢測等領域提供理論基礎與高解析度、高效率的成像方法。

16307926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16307926.value: 從高分辨率空間轉錄組學中提取單細胞信息的統一框架

16307926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307926.value: Recent advancements in spatial transcriptomics (ST) technologies have opened new avenues for investigating the architecture of organs and tissues at subcellular resolution. Sequencing-based methods achieve spatial resolutions ranging from 0.5 to 2 µm, while imaging-based techniques can reach resolutions as fine as 0.1 to 0.2 µm. Given that cells are the fundamental units of life, extracting single-cell information from these high-resolution ST measurements is crucial. However, this task presents significant challenges due to the limitations of subcellular measurements. Sequencing-based ST technologies often suffer from low transcriptional abundance per spot, while imaging-based approaches typically measure only a few hundred genes. This limited data can hinder accurate delineation of cell boundaries and cell type annotation. Furthermore, the integration of multimodal information, such as staining images and transcript measurements, remains underexplored. The computational burden of analyzing millions of cells in high-resolution ST data adds another layer of complexity, underscoring the urgent need for innovative statistical and computational methodologies to fully leverage ST technologies for understanding biological processes and disease mechanisms. In response to these challenges, we propose CellART, a unified framework designed to extract single-cell information from high-resolution ST data. Our primary objectives are to accurately segment cell and nucleus boundaries and to annotate cell types. In our pilot study, we demonstrate that CellART outperforms existing methods in both cell segmentation and cell type annotation for both sequencing-based and imaging-based ST data. By integrating deep neural networks with probabilistic models, CellART effectively addresses the challenges posed by imperfect subcellular measurements, learning high-resolution representations from multimodal information. These representations provide precise data for cell segmentation and type annotation. Importantly, CellART is scalable and capable of handling millions of cells efficiently. Our pilot study results highlight the superior performance of CellART compared to current approaches. Building on these promising findings, we aim to extend the CellART framework to characterize cell niches in condition-agnostic studies and to explore disease-relevant niches in case-control settings. The novelty of our method lies in its seamless integration of deep learning and probabilistic modeling, allowing for effective utilization of multimodal data, including staining images, transcript measurements, and scRNA-seq reference data. We believe that this project will establish a reliable platform for cell segmentation, type annotation, and niche characterization in high-resolution ST data, addressing significant data science challenges in the field and advancing our understanding of biological processes and disease mechanisms. 空間轉錄組學技術的進展為以亞細胞分辨率研究器官和組織的結構打開了新的路徑。這些基於測序的方法實現的空間分辨率在0.5到2微米之間，而基於成像的技術則可達到0.1到0.2微米。由於細胞是生命的基本單位，從這些高分辨率數據中提取單細胞信息變得至關重要。然而，亞細胞測量的局限性使這一任務面臨顯著挑戰。測序型空間轉錄組技術通常在每個點的轉錄丰度較低，而成像方法一般僅測量數百個基因，這限制了細胞邊界和類型注釋的準確性。此外，整合多模態信息（如染色圖像和轉錄測量）也尚未得到充分探索。為應對這些挑戰，我們提出了CellART框架，旨在從高分辨率空間轉錄組數據中提取單細胞信息，主要目標是準確分割細胞與細胞核邊界並進行細胞類型注釋。我們的初步研究表明，CellART在細胞分割和細胞類型注釋方面均優於現有方法。CellART通過結合深度神經網絡與概率模型，有效解決了亞細胞測量的不完美性，能夠高效處理百萬級細胞數據。因此，這一研究有望在細胞分割、類型注釋及細胞生態位特徵描述等方面建立可靠的平台，為生物過程及疾病機制的理解提供重要支撐。

16308126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16308126.value: 以大型強子對撞機的完整數據集研究希格斯玻色子的特性

16308126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308126.value: The world’s most powerful particle accelerator, the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is currently approaching the end of its main operation period. It started in 2011 and will be concluded at the second half of 2026. About two thirds of the total dataset planned to be obtained by the ATLAS experiment during the LHC lifetime has been presently collected. One of the major scientific goals of ATLAS are searches for the new physics effects, extending the Standard Model (SM), presently established theory of elementary particles and their interactions. At present, the SM successfully describes the fundamental interactions at accessible energy scale, while lacking explanation for several important observations, such as the presence of Dark Matter and dominance of baryonic matter in our Universe. The explanations for these effects are normally attributed to hypothetical Beyond the Standard Model (BSM) physics, which is yet to be discovered. While the biggest part of the LHC dataset has already been collected, no significant evidence for the BSM physics is reported. This may indicate that the BSM energy scale lies significantly higher than the LHC reach. In such case, the new physics may manifest itself through small deviations in the precision measurements of well-predicted SM parameters. The full LHC dataset to be obtained by the second half of 2026 thus needs to be used for two main purposes: producing the LHC “legacy” measurements of least measured SM parameters, and observing rare SM effects, not accessible with previously small statistics. This project is an extension of a previously funded GRF project, which addresses searches for BSM physics in Higgs boson sector using the partial LHC dataset. In this project the results obtained in our previous investigations will be used. We will further enhance our studies of Higgs boson couplings to other Standard Model particles using the full LHC dataset, applying novel measurement techniques, developed in the frame of our previous projects. The full LHC dataset will allow us to access the Quantum Entanglement in Higgs decays and to assess its sensitivity to possible BSM physics. Having positioned itself as the expert of the corresponding studies, in the next three years the Hong Kong group expects to significantly enhance their precision by exploring the new dataset to be collected by the LHC. The work on all mentioned directions has already started and the HKUST ATLAS group is currently playing the leading role in it. 全球最大的粒子加速器——大型強子對撞機（LHC）的主要運行期目前已接近尾聲。該加速器於2011年起運行，而本輪運行將於2026年下半年結束。作為LHC主要實驗之一的ATLAS亦已收集了其計劃獲取數據的約三分之二。ATLAS實驗的主要科學目標之一，是尋找標準模型（SM）之外的物理理論。標準模型是目前描述基本粒子及其相互作用的既定理論，其雖能成功描述可及能量尺度下的基本相互作用，卻未能解釋宇宙中的暗物質及重子不對稱性等重要現象。現今已有不少理論嘗試解決這些難題，儘管目前已累積了龐大的數據量，卻仍未出現超出標準模型（BSM）理論的顯著證據。這可能意味着BSM理論的能量尺度遠高於LHC的探測範圍。在此情況下，新物理或會透過精確測量標準模型中的參數而顯現。因此，2026年下半年前獲取的LHC數據集，需用於兩個主要目的：對精確度較低的標準模型參數進行高精度測量，以及探索過去因統計量不足而無法觸及的罕見物理過程。本項目為先前獲優配研究金資助項目的延伸，先前項目利用部分LHC數據集，在希格斯玻色子領域搜尋BSM物理。本項目將沿用過往研究結果，進一步運用先前項目開發的新穎測量技術，以完整的LHC數據集深化希格斯玻色子與其他標準模型粒子耦合的研究。完整數據集將允許我們探討希格斯衰變中的量子糾纏，並評估其對BSM物理的敏感度。在過去數年，我們已在相關研究確立專家地位，未來三年我們預期透過LHC新數據集大幅提升測量精度。相關的各項前沿工作現已全面展開，香港科技大學的小組正在ATLAS實驗中發揮領導作用。

16308226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16308226.value: 金屬鹵化物鈣鈦礦材料中電子-聲子相互作用的太赫茲光譜學研究

16308226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308226.value: Metal-halide perovskite (MHP) has emerged as a leading candidate for next-generation photovoltaic technologies, with single-junction perovskite solar cells demonstrating significant advancements in its efficiency, rising from 3.8% to 26.7% in just a decade. However, it is quite challenging to further raise the figure of merit of MHP compounds to the theoretical limit. The ultimate solution may lie in the microscopic details of the generation and transport of charge carriers and their interaction with the local environment, intrinsically and extrinsically. A salient inherent characteristic of MHP, that is fundamentally important and distinguishes it from conventional solar cells made from III-V inorganic semiconductors, is the pronounced electron-phonon interaction, which intricately intertwines the lattice and charge degrees of freedoms. As such, charge carriers in MHP become essentially polaronic, i.e., greatly renormalized by phonon dressing. This intrinsic interaction imposes upper limits to mobility and underlies the non-equilibrium cooling and recombination pathways of the charge carriers. Therefore, to break the present bottleneck, a comprehensive investigation of electron-phonon coupling at fundamental energy and time scales is essential, yet this area is still not fully resolved. To elucidate electron-phonon coupling, we propose to investigate ultrafast dynamics of both charge and the lattice degrees of freedom by the state-of-the-art ultrabroadband THz spectroscopy (0.5-23 THz) for a near exhaustive tracking of the relevant low-energy dipole-active modes, at the femtosecond temporal resolution. Furthermore, we will leverage the powerful concept of mode-selective excitation in ultrafast spectroscopy, that is, to resonantly excite specific lattice modes, aiming to dynamically modify the properties of polarons. The resultant polaronic carrier dynamics will be tracked by THz time-domain spectroscopy. The proposed research into the electron-phonon interactions on fundamental time and energy scales, alongside the exploration of phonon-engineered polaron dynamics, could provide significant insights for the future rational design of perovskite-based solar cell materials and devices. 金屬鹵化物鈣鈦礦已成為下一代光伏技術的重要候選材料。近年來鈣鈦礦太陽能電池的效率實現了顯著跨越。然而，要將其品質因數進一步提升至理論極限，依然面臨著巨大挑戰。該解決方案可能取決於電荷載流子的產生、輸運及其與局部環境（包括內在和外在環境）相互作用的微觀細節。金屬鹵化物鈣鈦礦因為具有極強的電子-聲子相互作用，使其有別於基於無機半導體的傳統太陽能電池。晶格與電荷自由度交織在一起，從而使得金屬鹵化物鈣鈦礦中的電荷載流子以極化子的形式存在，即因聲子綴飾的自由電荷。這種本徵相互作用不僅限制了遷移率的上限，也決定了電子和空穴的非平衡態弛豫和複合的動力學過程。為了突破現有瓶頸，在本徵能量和時間尺度上對電子-聲子耦合進行全面研究至關重要，但這一領域的研究目前尚未充分展開。為了闡明電子-聲子耦合機制，將利用太赫茲光譜技術，在飛秒級時間分辨率下，對電荷和晶格自由度的超快動力學進行研究，從而近乎詳盡地追蹤相關的低頻偶極活躍模式。此外，我們將利用超快光譜學中的模式選擇激發概念，即共振激發特定的晶格模式，旨在動態調控極化子的性質，並追蹤由此產生的極化子載流子動力學過程。這將為未來鈣鈦礦太陽能電池材料與器件的設計和性能提升帶來重要指導信息。

16308426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16308426.value: 嵌合腺相關病毒衣殼的工程化設計及其免疫逃逸性能優化

16308426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308426.value: Gene therapy holds great promise for treating diseases by delivering healthy replacement genes to patients’ cells, typically using adeno-associated viruses (AAVs) as the delivery vehicle. Recombinant AAV vectors are pivotal in gene therapy, evidenced by nearly 10 clinical therapy approvals in the past six years. However, pre-existing immunity, present in 40–70% of the human population due to prior natural AAVs exposure, poses significant challenges by eliciting neutralizing antibodies (NAbs) that reduce therapeutic efficiency and trigger dose-dependent inflammation or toxicity. Current clinical solutions relying on immunosuppression remain inadequate for long-term use. As gene therapy expands from rare, life-threatening disorders to more prevalent conditions, there is an urgent need to develop AAVs that evade NAbs and host immune responses, thereby improving safety, efficacy, and the potential for repeat dosing. Natural AAV capsid is composed of three protein subunits, which contains multiple immunogenic epitopes both in linear and complex conformations as binding sites of NAbs. It is challenging to rationally design and predict the mutations needed for a “neutralization-free” vector. In this study, we propose to design chimeric AAV capsids with superior immune evasion while preserving their assembly and infection capabilities. Specifically, to improve the state-of-the-art AAV recombination library, we apply a protein language model (pLM)-based approach to optimize crossover positions with diversified AAV parent types. Unlike previous algorithms, which yield only ~10% functional AAV variants after recombination, our pLM-guided approach achieves more than 80% functional capsids, enhancing library diversity and utility for downstream therapeutic applications. These libraries will then enable selection and enrichment for capsid variants via iterative directed evolution against human intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), which serves as a clinically relevant model of population-level NAbs. Using the AAV sequence-to-function dataset, we propose to develop a generalizable machine-learning framework for the prediction and design of a recombination library that balances multiple key functions simultaneously, such as immune evasion, assembly, and diversity. To translate our design into clinical application, this newly designed library will be validated using a mouse model pre-treated with IVIG. By comprehensively characterizing host immune responses following systemic administration, we anticipate boosting delivery efficacy through reduced immunogenicity. By leveraging our interdisciplinary expertise and prior work at the nexus of bioengineering, virology, and computational biology, we envision providing valuable tools in the fields of gene therapy, paving the way for broadening patient therapeutic access, facilitating personalized gene therapies, and advancing nucleic acid-based modalities for diverse genetic disorders. 基因治療透過將功能性基因遞送至患者細胞，為遺傳性及其他難治性疾病提供重要的治療策略。腺相關病毒（AAV）因其良好的安全性及體內遞送能力，已成為目前最主要的基因治療載體之一，近六年間已有近十項相關療法獲得臨床批准。然而，由於人群曾自然暴露於AAV，約40–70%人體內存在針對AAV衣殼的預存中和抗體（NAbs），不僅降低基因遞送效率，亦可能加劇高劑量給藥相關的免疫反應及毒性。現有免疫抑制策略難以從根本上解決此問題，並限制AAV載體的重複給藥。因此，開發兼具高效免疫逃逸與病毒功能的新型AAV載體，是拓展基因治療臨床應用的重要需求。 AAV衣殼表面包含多個線性及構象性免疫表位，其序列同時影響抗體識別、衣殼組裝及細胞感染能力，使傳統突變或理性設計難以預測可廣泛逃逸中和抗體的功能性載體。本研究擬結合蛋白質語言模型（pLM）、嵌合衣殼工程、定向演化及機器學習，建立新型AAV免疫逃逸設計框架。 首先，我們將利用pLM優化不同AAV血清型之間的重組交叉位點，建立高功能性及高多樣性的嵌合衣殼文庫。傳統重組方法產生的功能性AAV比例僅約10%，而我們的前期研究顯示，pLM引導策略可將功能性衣殼比例提升至80%以上。在此基礎上，我們將以人靜脈注射免疫球蛋白（IVIG）作為具臨床相關性的人群中和抗體模型，透過多輪定向演化篩選，富集具有廣泛免疫逃逸能力的嵌合衣殼。 進一步地，本研究將利用大規模AAV序列—功能數據建立可泛化的機器學習模型，解析嵌合序列與免疫逃逸、衣殼組裝及病毒功能之間的關係，並設計同時兼顧免疫逃逸、組裝效率及序列多樣性的精煉重組文庫。最終將於IVIG預處理的小鼠模型中進行體內驗證，系統評估候選AAV在預存抗體環境下的基因遞送效率、宿主免疫反應及安全性。 本研究旨在突破AAV免疫逃逸與病毒功能難以兼顧的核心瓶頸，建立從嵌合文庫構建、抗體壓力篩選、序列功能學習至多目標設計及體內驗證的閉環工程平台，為開發低免疫原性AAV載體、擴大基因治療適用人群及實現未來重複給藥提供新的技術基礎。

16308526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16308526.value: 醇-胺偶聯電合成酰胺：催化劑創新、微環境工程與反應器放大的協同策略

16308526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308526.value: Amide electrosynthesis from oxidative alcohol-amine coupling represents a sustainable route to high-value chemicals. However, its practical application is hindered by three key challenges: competing side reactions leading to low selectivity, corrosive anodic environments causing electrode instability under industrial current densities, and mass transfer limitations restricting substrate scope. To address these limitations, this proposal develops a synergistic strategy that integrates catalyst innovation, microenvironment engineering, and reactor scale-up. First, we will employ a theory-guided screening approach to design Cu-alloy-based catalysts that selectively stabilize key intermediates for C−N coupling while suppressing over-oxidation, enabling efficient formamide electrosynthesis from methanol and ammonia. These candidates will be precisely synthesized and engineered using plasma technology to optimize their surface chemistry and electronic structures. Second, to enhance durability, we will implement a dual-protection strategy combining electronic structure modulation via alloying with physical protection via plasma-etched porous carbon coating. The stability and evolution of the real active sites will be assessed under ampere-level current densities. Finally, we will generalize this platform for diverse amide electrosynthesis by expanding the substrate scope to various alcohol-amine pairs. A surfactant-tailored interfacial engineering strategy will be developed to overcome the mass transfer limitation for organic substrates in aqueous electrolytes. These innovations will be integrated into an optimized membrane electrode assembly flow reactor for scalable production of amides. The success of this project will establish a foundational framework for advancing the electrosynthesis of valuable organic compounds through the synergistic integration of catalyst design, interfacial control, and reactor engineering. 醇-胺氧化偶聯電合成酰胺是一條可持續的高值化學品製備路線。然而，其實際應用受到三大關鍵挑戰的制約：競爭性副反應導致選擇性低、工業電流密度下腐蝕性陽極環境引發電極不穩定性、以及傳質限制縮小了底物適用範圍。為應對這些侷限，本項目提出一種整合催化劑創新、微環境工程與反應器放大的協同策略。首先，我們將採用理論指導的篩選方法，設計Cu合金基催化劑，使其選擇性地穩定C−N偶聯的關鍵中間體，同時抑制過氧化，從而實現甲醇與氨高效電合成甲酰胺。這些候選催化劑將經精確合成，並藉助等離子體技術進行結構調控，以優化其表面化學性質及電子結構。其次，為提升耐久性，我們將實施雙重保護策略，即通過合金化實現電子結構調控，並結合等離子體刻蝕多孔碳塗層提供物理保護。在安培級電流密度下評估真實活性位點的穩定性及其演變規律。最後，我們將底物範圍拓展至各類醇-胺組合，從而將該平台拓展至多種酰胺的電合成。針對水性電解質中有機底物的傳質限制，將發展表面活性劑調控的界面工程策略。上述創新將整合至優化的膜電極組裝流動反應器中，以驅動酰胺的放大製備。本項目的成功實施，將通過催化劑設計、界面調控與反應器工程的協同融合，為高值有機化合物電合成奠定基礎性框架。

16308626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16308626.value: 快速構建複雜分子的有機不對稱催化策略

16308626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308626.value: Rapid generation of complex molecules with intricate architecture from simple ones represents a primary goal of modern organic synthesis. Traditionally, this has been achieved by a sequence of multiple steps, which may cause additional waste and more cost. Therefore, the development of efficient strategies that can construct complex molecules by a short sequence would be ideal in this regard. Meanwhile, chirality is another fundamental feature of many organic molecules often vital to human life, such as amino acids, DNAs, proteins. Asymmetric catalysis that employs a small amount of chiral catalyst to induce chirality represents essentially the most efficient way to produce enantioenriched products in large quantity. Chiral bridged seven-membered carbocycles are unique pharmacophores widely present in biologically active molecules and drug candidates. Their complex architecture, often containing multiple stereogenic centers, poses substantial synthetic challenges. [5+2] Cycloaddition provides rapid access to diverse seven-membered bridged skeletons of this type. However, current efforts have been focused on racemic version or those from enantioenriched starting materials. Efficient catalytic enantioselective strategies with chirality induced by catalyst remain very scarce. Here we plan to continue our efforts in developing general and efficient catalytic enantioselective and diastereoselective [5+2] cycloadditions for the assembly of diverse seven-membered bridged skeletons. Specifically, two types of reactions, namely [5+2] cycloaddition of oxidopyryliums and perezone analogs, will be systematically explored. Both intermolecular and intramolecular reactions with different types of internal tethers at different positions will be developed to deliver different levels of structural complexity and concomitantly generate multiple stereogenic centers with both absolute and relative stereocontrols. New organocatalysts and catalytic strategies will be developed, some enabled by our own backbone (e.g., SPHENOL), to achieve high chemical efficiency and stereoselectivity. Some of our preliminary results have been reported (Nat. Synth. 2025, doi:10.1038/s44160-025-00803-w and J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2025, 147, 10.1021/jacs.5c14484). These catalytic strategies can be applied to the improved synthesis of natural products and drug candidates with a shorter sequence and better efficiency. The employment of organocatalysis is complementary to metal catalysis and may contribute to green synthesis and a sustainable environment. 從簡單分子快速建構結構複雜的分子是現代有機合成的主要目標之一。傳統方法通常依賴多步驟反應序列，這往往導致額外的廢棄物產生並增加成本。因此，開發能夠透過簡短步驟建構複雜分子的高效策略顯得特別理想。同時，手性是許多對人類生命至關重要的有機分子（如胺基酸、DNA和蛋白質）的另一個基本特徵。不對稱催化利用少量手性催化劑誘導手性，是實現對映體富集產物大規模生產最有效的方法。 手性橋聯七元碳環是一類獨特的藥效團，廣泛存在於生物活性分子和候選藥物中。由於其結構複雜且通常包含多個立體中心，這類分子的合成極具挑戰性。 [5+2]環加成反應為快速建造此類多樣的七元橋聯骨架提供了有效途徑。然而，目前的研究多集中於外消旋系統或使用對映體富集的起始原料；利用催化劑誘導手性的高效催化對映選擇性策略仍十分匱乏。 本計畫旨在繼續致力於開發通用且高效的催化對映和非對映選擇性 [5+2]環加成反應，以建構多樣的七元橋聯骨架。具體而言，我們將系統探討兩類反應：氧化吡喃鎓（oxidopyrylium）與佩雷酮（perezone）類似物的[5+2]環加成。我們將發展涉及不同類型內連橋及不同連接位置的分子間與分子內反應，從而建構不同複雜程度的結構，並同時產生具有絕對和相對立體化學控制的多個立體中心。我們將開發新型有機催化劑及催化策略（部分基於我們自主研發的骨架，如SPHENOL），以實現高化學效率和立體選擇性。這些催化策略可應用於天然產物及候選藥物的改良合成，進而縮短合成步驟並提高效率。有機催化的應用與金屬催化形成互補，並有助於實現綠色合成與環境的可持續發展。

16308726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16308726.value: 時間反演和晶格對稱性共同保護的內稟平均對稱性保護拓撲序的分類與構造

16308726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308726.value: A central goal of condensed matter theory is prediction of new phases of matter. While phases are classified by symmetries, experimentally relevant platforms, from solid-state materials with inevitable defects to noisy quantum simulators, rarely possess perfect symmetries. One natural question is that can the imperfect symmetries play the symmetry principle to classify phases? Recent theory shows the answer to be positive. More remarkably, it predicts that disorder and decoherence can enable fundamentally new family of quantum phases of matter—intrinsic average symmetry-protected topological phases (iASPTs)—that can only exist in the presence of disorder or noise. Unlike conventional symmetry-protected topological phases (SPT) phases, which rely on exact symmetries in perfectly clean systems, iASPTs are protected by symmetries that hold only on average across many disorder realizations (e.g., time-reversal (TRS) or crystalline symmetries that are locally broken by impurities but restored statistically). These phases exhibit robust, symmetry-protected boundary phenomena even though each sample may look trivial. Yet a complete classification and practical construction for iASPTs with TRS and crystalline symmetries, two most relevant symmetries for realistic platforms, are still missing, especially in 3D interacting fermion systems. In this project, we focus on interacting fermionic systems in two and three dimensions with TRS and crystalline symmetries. The goals are: 1. To classify 2D and 3D ASPTs jointly protected by TRS and crystalline symmetries. 2. To identify which ASPT phases are iASPT. 3. To construct explicit real-space models that realize these phases. Methodologically, we combine two powerful approaches: 1. Algebraic classification via spectral-sequence tools that consistently organize symmetry domain walls or defects decorated with lower dimensional SPTs or invertible phases into topological phase under average symmetries. 2. Real-space “topological crystal” constructions that place lower-dimensional SPTs or invertible phases on symmetry-related cells of a lattice. The project leverages recent advances by the PI and collaborators that generalize these tools to generic anti-unitary symmetries and crystalline symmetries, enabling systematic treatment of internal-spatial symmetry mixes. Outcomes will map the full landscape of iASPTs protected by TRS and crystalline symmetries, provide practical construction recipes, and furnish indicators to guide experiments. Broadly, the work shows that disorder and decoherence are not merely detrimental—they can be essential resources for realizing fundamentally new topological states with potential applications to robust quantum information and advanced semiconductor technology. 凝聚態理論的核心目標之一是預言物質的新物相。物相依據對稱性進行分類，但實驗上的實際研究體系 —— 從存在不可避免缺陷的固態材料，到受雜訊干擾的量子模擬器 —— 幾乎都不具備完美對稱性。一個很自然的問題是：非理想的對稱性能否做為分類物相的對稱性原理？近期理論研究給出了肯定的答案。更值得關注的是，理論預言無序與退相干可以催生一類全新的量子物相：內稟平均對稱性保護拓撲相（iASPT），這類物相僅在存在無序或雜訊的條件下才能存在。 傳統的對稱性保護拓撲相（SPT）依賴於理想無雜質體系中的嚴格對稱性；與之不同，內稟平均對稱性保護拓撲相由僅在大量無序樣本統計平均意義下成立的對稱性所保護（例如時間反演對稱性、晶格對稱性，這類對稱性會被雜質局域破壞，但在統計平均層面得以恢復）。即便每一個獨立樣本都表現為平庸體系，這類物相仍會展現出受對稱性保護的穩健邊界效應。然而，針對時間反演與晶格對稱性（現實體系中兩類最重要的對稱性）共同保護的內稟平均對稱性保護拓撲相，目前還缺少完整的分類與可行的構造方案，對於三維有相互作用費米子體系而言該問題尤為突出。 本專案研究二維、三維具有時間反演對稱性與晶格對稱性的有相互作用費米子體系，研究目標如下： 1. 對時間反演和晶格對稱性聯合保護的二維、三維平均對稱性保護拓撲相（ASPT）開展分類。 2. 甄別哪些平均對稱性保護拓撲相屬於內稟平均對稱性保護拓撲相（iASPT）。 3. 建構可以實現上述物相的顯式實空間模型。 研究方法上，我們結合兩種強有力的研究手段： 基於譜序列工具的代數分類：將修飾有低維對稱性保護拓撲相或可逆相的對稱疇壁、缺陷，在平均對稱性框架下自洽地歸為拓撲相。 實空間「拓撲晶體」建構：將低維對稱性保護拓撲相或可逆相放置於晶格中由對稱性關聯的原胞上。 本專案依託計畫主持人及其合作者的最新研究進展：已將上述工具推廣至一般反么正對稱性與晶格對稱性，能夠系統處理內部‑空間混合對稱性。預期成果將完整刻畫由時間反演與晶格對稱性保護的內稟平均對稱性保護拓撲相全貌，給出可實際使用的建構方案，並提供可指導實驗的判據指標。從更廣泛的意義來看，本研究表明無序與退相干並非只有破壞作用，它們也可以做為實現全新拓撲態的關鍵資源，有望應用於高魯棒性量子資訊與先進半導體技術。

16308926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308926.value: What is the origin of our Universe? This ultimate question has puzzled humankind for thousands of years. Today, advances in theoretical physics and cosmology allow us to approach this mystery with unprecedented scientific rigour. Remarkably, what happened at the birth of everything left behind characteristic “fossils” imprinted in the structure of today’s cosmos. Therefore, cosmic inflation—the modern version of the Big Bang—acts as a natural laboratory where unknown physics in the microscopic world can be tested through cosmic-scale observations. As an increasing amount of data is arriving within the next decade, now is the perfect time to get prepared for potential revolutionising discoveries. I will integrate cutting-edge ideas from theoretical high energy physics to explore fundamental physics in the primordial Universe. Specifically, I will develop the wavefunction formalism to gain more precise understandings about the physics of inflation. Pioneered by Hartle and Hawking in the 1980s, the wave function of the Universe (WFU) is expected to contain all the information of our cosmos, but is impossible to solve in practice. In recent advances on the theory frontier, it has been more and more appreciated that the field-theoretic wavefunction, as a simplification of the full WFU, is a very helpful framework for studying quantum field theories in cosmological spacetime. Using this approach, significant progress has been made on the analytic understanding of the tree-level perturbation theory in the flat de Sitter spacetime. This proposal aims to extend the current analysis of the simplest setup above to incorporate richer physics in the cosmological wavefunction. I will first analyse loop-level correlators using the cosmological bootstrap method. With this preparation, I will go beyond perturbation theory and study the behaviour of large-size fluctuations at the tail of the probability distribution. Meanwhile, I will also go beyond the flat de Sitter background and consider the effects of different spacetime geometries on the field-theoretic wavefunction. I will focus on two concrete examples: the Hartle-Hawking state from the no-boundary proposal and the bubble geometries from open inflation. With promising implications for both theoretical high energy physics and inflationary cosmology, my investigation will bridge the gap between the two and open up new lines of research for further exploration. 我们的宇宙起源于何处？这个终极问题千百年来一直困扰着人类。如今，理论物理学和宇宙学的进步使我们能够以空前严谨的科学态度来探讨这一谜题。值得注意的是，万物诞生之时所发生的一切，在当今宇宙的结构中留下了独特的“化石”印记。因此，作为大爆炸理论现代版的“宇宙暴胀”，正扮演着一个天然实验室的角色——在这里，我们可以通过宇宙尺度的观测，来检验微观世界中未知的物理规律。随着未来十年内海量观测数据的陆续到来，目前我们应做好准备，迎接可能具有革命性的新发现。 我将融合理论高能物理学的前沿思想，以探索极早期宇宙中的基本物理学。具体而言，我将发展宇宙学波函数，以对暴胀物理学获得更精确的理解。起初，宇宙波函数由哈特尔（Hartle）和霍金（Hawking）在 20 世纪 80 年代提出，它被认为包含了我们宇宙的所有信息，但在实际中却无法求解。在理论前沿的最新进展中，人们越来越认识到，作为完整宇宙波函数的简化版，量子场论波函数（field-theoretic wavefunction）是研究宇宙时空中量子场论的一个非常有效的框架。利用这一方法，人们在解析理解平坦德西特时空中的树图级微扰论方面，已经取得了显著进展。 本研究旨在推广上述最简单模型的现有分析，将更丰富的物理内容引入到宇宙学波函数中。首先，我将利用宇宙学自展法来分析圈图级的关联函数。在此基础上，我将超越微扰论，研究概率分布尾部的长波涨落行为。同时，我亦将超越平坦德西特背景，考虑不同时空几何对场论波函数的影响。我将重点关注两个具体实例：源自无边界假说的哈特尔-霍金态，以及源自开放暴胀的宇宙泡几何。这项研究不仅对理论高能物理学和暴胀宇宙学都具有广阔的应用前景，还将搭建起两者之间的桥梁，并为进一步的探索开辟新的研究方向。

16309026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16309026.value: 利用衛星資料研究東南亞生物質燃燒對香港微量氣體影響

16309026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309026.value: Biomass burning is a major source of trace gases and aerosols, with significant impacts on air quality, climate, biogeochemical cycles, and public health. While its role in atmospheric composition is well-established, the spatiotemporal variability of biomass burning emissions and their transport mechanisms remain poorly understood. Therefore, characterizing emission dynamics and pollutant transport from biomass burning across different global regions is essential. In Southeast Asia (SEA), extensive biomass burning occurs primarily through agricultural land clearing and conversion, with fire activity intensified during El Niño–Southern Oscillation-associated droughts. Transboundary pollutants from SEA biomass burning affect surrounding regions and have attracted international attention, particularly regarding air quality in Hong Kong and the Pearl River Delta. Despite considerable research on biomass burning contributions to air pollution, most studies in Hong Kong have focused on particulate matter, including black carbon and secondary organic aerosols. Accurately quantifying the impacts of SEA biomass burning on trace gas pollutants remains challenging due to limited in-situ measurements in Hong Kong. This project addresses these gaps by integrating satellite remote sensing observations with in-situ measurements to assess the impacts of SEA biomass burning on trace gases in Hong Kong, specifically CO, CO₂, CH₄, alkyl nitrates, and halocarbons. Satellite data will be used to characterize biomass burning intensity in SEA and to investigate trace gas emissions and transport patterns. Long-term in-situ measurements will monitor trace gas distributions to identify the specific contributions from SEA biomass burning. Statistical analyses and model simulations will quantify pollutant contributions from different emission sources and clarify transport processes. The resulting long-term datasets and emission estimates will advance atmospheric chemistry and climate change research while providing scientific support for air quality policy evaluation and improvement. 生物質燃燒是微量氣體和氣溶膠的主要來源，對空氣品質、氣候、生物地球化學循環及公共衛生有顯著影響。儘管其對大氣成分的影響已廣為人知，但生物質燃燒排放的時空變化及其傳輸機制尚不完全明確。因此，研究全球不同地區生物質燃燒的排放動態及污染物傳輸特性至關重要。在東南亞地區，大規模的生物質燃燒主要源自於農業用地的清理與轉化，且在與厄爾尼諾-南方濤動相關的乾旱期間，火災活動尤其劇烈。源自東南亞生物質燃燒的跨界污染物影響著週邊地區並引發了國際關注，特別是對香港及珠江三角洲地區空氣品質的影響。 儘管已有大量關於生物質燃燒對空氣污染貢獻的研究，但香港地區的大多數研究主要集中在顆粒物（包括黑碳和二次有機氣溶膠）。由於缺乏足夠的實地觀測數據，準確量化東南亞生物質燃燒對香港微量氣體污染物的影響仍面臨挑戰。本計畫旨在透過整合衛星遙感觀測與實地測量數據，彌補上述研究空白，評估東南亞生物質燃燒對香港微量氣體的影響。本計畫將利用衛星數據來表徵東南亞生物質燃燒的強度，並探討微量氣體的排放與傳輸模式；透過長期的實地觀測監測微量氣體的分佈，以識別東南亞生物質燃燒的具體貢獻；利用統計分析和模型模擬，量化不同排放源對污染物的貢獻並闡明傳輸過程。由此獲得的長序列資料集和排放估算結果，不僅將推動大氣化學與氣候變遷領域的研究進展，也將為空氣品質政策的評估與改進提供科學基礎。

16309326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16309326.value: 模擬人為與生物質燃燒排放之粒狀有機硝酸鹽的形成與歸宿

16309326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309326.value: Organic nitrates (ONs) are key atmospheric compounds that link the cycles of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and nitrogen oxides (NOₓ), exerting a complex influence on tropospheric ozone (O₃) and secondary organic aerosol (SOA) formation. While ON formation from biogenic VOCs is relatively well-studied, significant knowledge gaps remain regarding their sources, formation pathways, and fate in polluted regions influenced by anthropogenic emissions and open biomass burning. Current chemical transport models (CTMs) substantially underpredict observed particulate organic nitrate (pON) in these environments, hindering an accurate assessment of their impacts on air quality and health. This research addresses these gaps by investigating three interconnected questions: (1) What is the contribution of anthropogenic VOCs to observed gaseous and particulate ON in polluted urban atmospheres? (2) How much ON is formed during extensive Southeast Asian (SEA) biomass burning episodes? (3) To what extent do condensed-phase decay processes of pON feed back into gas-phase chemistry, affecting O₃, atmospheric oxidation capacity, and SOA? To address these questions, we propose a three-part research plan using the Community Multiscale Air Quality (CMAQ) model. In Task 1, we will incorporate two enhanced chemical mechanisms (SAPRC-22 and the Master Chemical Mechanism) to better represent ON formation from anthropogenic and biogenic VOCs. This will be coupled with advanced treatments of multiphase processes, including gas-particle partitioning and condensed-phase reactions (hydrolysis, aqueous OH oxidation, and photolysis). The model will be rigorously evaluated against field measurements from multiple East Asian campaigns. In Task 2, we will quantify the contribution of SEA open biomass burning to regional pON, assessing the sensitivity of predictions to VOC speciation profiles and plume-rise algorithms, and exploring non-linear interactions with urban anthropogenic emissions. In Task 3, targeted sensitivity simulations will isolate and quantify the feedback of pON condensed-phase decay on O₃ and SOA formation, critically examining uncertainties in reaction products and oxidant concentrations. This project will deliver a robust, evaluated modelling framework that can accurately simulate pON in polluted atmospheres, thereby addressing critical gaps in current models. By quantifying the relative contributions of anthropogenic and biomass burning sources, and by resolving key uncertainties in the multiphase fate of organic nitrates, the research will provide valuable mechanistic insights into the complete lifecycle of ONs. Ultimately, this will enable more accurate assessment of their impact on regional O₃ and particulate matter pollution, providing a scientific foundation for informed air quality management strategies. 有機硝酸鹽（ON）是大氣中的重要化合物，連接揮發性有機化合物（VOCs）與氮氧化物（NOx）的循環，並對對流層臭氧（O₃）及二次有機氣溶膠（SOA）的形成產生複雜影響。儘管源自生物源VOCs的ON生成已有較多研究，但在受人為排放和露天生物質燃燒影響的污染地區，其來源、生成途徑及歸宿仍存在顯著知識缺口。現有的化學傳輸模型（CTMs）在這些環境中對觀測到的顆粒態有機硝酸鹽（pON）大幅低估，妨礙了對其空氣質素及健康影響的準確評估。本研究旨在填補這些缺口，圍繞三個相互關聯的問題進行探討：（1）人為源VOCs對污染城市大氣中觀測到的氣態及顆粒態ON有多大貢獻？（2）在東南亞（SEA）大規模生物質燃燒事件期間會生成多少ON？（3）pON的凝縮相衰減過程在多大程度上會反饋至氣相化學，進而影響O₃、大氣氧化能力及SOA？ 為解答上述問題，我們提出一個三部分的研究計劃，採用社區多尺度空氣質素（CMAQ）模型。在任務一中，我們將納入兩個增強型化學機制（SAPRC-22及Master Chemical Mechanism (MCM)），以更佳地模擬人為及生物源VOCs生成的ON。同時，我們會結合先進的多相過程處理，包括氣－粒分配及凝縮相反應（水解、水相羥基氧化及光解）。模型將利用多個東亞觀測活動的實測數據進行嚴格驗證。在任務二中，我們將量化東南亞開放式生物質燃燒對區域pON的貢獻，評估預測對VOCs物種組成輪廓及煙羽抬升算法的敏感性，並探討其與城市人為排放之間的非線性交互作用。在任務三中，針對性敏感度模擬將分離並量化pON凝縮相衰減對O₃及SOA生成的反饋作用，並重點審視反應產物及氧化劑濃度方面的不確定性。 本項目將提供一個穩健且經評估的模擬框架，能夠準確模擬污染大氣中的pON，從而填補當前模型的關鍵缺口。通過量化人為源及生物質燃燒源的相對貢獻，並釐清有機硝酸鹽多相歸宿中的關鍵不確定因素，本研究將為ON的完整生命週期提供寶貴的機理見解。最終，這將有助於更準確地評估其對區域O₃及顆粒物污染的影響，為基於科學的空氣質素管理策略提供堅實基礎。

16309526.value: 合成穩定的三元硼環及反應性研究

16309526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309526.value: Boron-containing drugs have recently garnered significant research interest due to the unique interactions of organoboron compounds with biologic targets and valuable nuclear properties of 10B, particularly its neutron capture capability for cancer therapy. Despite their potential, the application of boron in pharmaceuticals remains relatively limited, with only five boron-based molecules approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). This limitation primarily stems from synthetic challenges: (1) many organoboron scaffolds lack robust and generalizable synthetic routes; and (2) the poor air stability of certain organoboron molecules hinders their practical use in biosystems. Therefore, the development of new synthetic strategies to access structurally diverse and bench-stable organoboranes is both highly desirable and scientifically meaningful. Boracycles have emerged as important pharmacophores, with two out of the five FDA-approved boron drugs featuring the benzoxaborole scaffold. Current studies largely focus on five- and six-membered boracycles, which typically exhibit good air stability. In contrast, smaller boron-containing rings remain underexplored in medicinal chemistry due to the scarcity of reliable synthetic methods and inherent stability issues. Recently, our group developed a photochemical method to access four-membered, bench-stable boracyclobutenes (Nat. Chem. 2025, 17, 663). These strained boracycles display versatile reactivities, enabling the synthesis of benzothiaboroles with potent ferroptosis-inhibitory activity and thereby demonstrating the importance of accessing new molecular architectures in the discovery of novel biological functions. In this proposal, we plan to challenge the smallest boracycles, three-membered boriranes. Our preliminary studies have revealed a visible-light photocatalytic approach to boriranes that show good air stability and allow for purification via chromatographic techniques. Further optimization of this photocatalytic strategy is expected to yield a broad range of three-membered boron rings. Their high ring stain may render them versatile synthons for accessing structurally diverse boracycles, many of which are difficult or not able to synthesize via conventional methods. Mechanistic studies will be carried out to deepen our understanding of reaction pathways and inspire the design of more efficient synthetic methodologies. Beyond expanding the accessible chemical space of bench-stable boracycles, this research aims to explore their valuable applications across a range of scientific disciplines. 含硼藥物近期因與生物靶點的獨特相互作用，以及硼-10同位素在癌症治療中獨特的中子捕捉能力，引起了廣泛的研究興趣。儘管其具備發展潛力，硼在製藥領域的應用仍相對有限，目前僅有五款有機硼分子獲得美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准。這一限制主要源於合成上的挑戰：（1）許多有機硼骨架缺乏高效且具普適性的合成路徑；（2）某些有機硼分子較差的空氣穩定性阻礙了其在生物系統中的實際應用。因此，開發全新的合成策略以獲取結構多樣且對空氣穩定的有機硼烷，不僅極具實用價值，亦富含科學意義。 硼雜環已成為重要的藥效團，在五款獲 FDA 批准的硼藥物中，就有兩款具有苯並氧硼唑（benzoxaborole）骨架。目前的科學研究主要集中在五元和六元硼雜環，這類環狀化合物通常展現出良好的空氣穩定性。相比之下，由於缺乏可靠的合成方法以及其固有的穩定性問題，較小硼環化合物在藥物化學中的探索仍然不足。近期，我們課題組開發了一種光化學方法，成功合成了性質穩定的四元硼雜環丁烯（Nat. Chem. 2025, 17, 663）。這些具環張力的硼雜環展現出多樣的反應活性，能夠用於合成具有強效鐵死亡抑制活性的苯並硫硼唑，從而證實了在發現新型生物功能過程中，獲取全新分子結構的重要性。 在此提案中，我們計劃挑戰最小的硼雜環——三元硼雜環丙烷（boriranes）。我們的初步研究發現了一種利用可見光光催化合成硼雜環丙烷的方法，該化合物展現出良好的空氣穩定性，並可透過層析技術進行純化。進一步優化此光催化策略有望產出多種三元硼環。其高的環張力能使其成為多功能合成子，用以獲取許多透過傳統方法難以或無法合成的結構多樣化硼雜環。我們亦將進行機理研究，以深化對反應路徑的理解，並啟發更高效合成方法的設計。本研究除了擴展穩定有機硼雜環的化學空間外，更旨在探索其在多個科學學科中的重要應用。

16309626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16309626.value: 提取强关联2维拓扑物相中的晶体不变量

16309626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309626.value: This proposal targets an important challenge in condensed matter: extracting crystalline invariants in interacting topological phases where band-theory tools fail. While quantized responses such as the Hall conductance and Chern number have long served as robust invariants, spatial symmetries—translations, rotations—stabilize a richer set of symmetry-protected and symmetry-enriched topological phases that are enriched by interactions. Recent theory established that crystalline defects (disclinations, dislocations) and partial symmetry operations encode universal data—discrete shift, polarization, and symmetry fractionalization—yet there remains no broadly applicable, interaction-ready toolkit to compute these invariants in microscopic models. The discovery of topological phases with crystalline symmetry in 2D materials and quantum simulators renders it even more pressing to fill the gap. This proposal addresses the issue with a unified field-theoretic, analytical and numerical program aimed at practical diagnostics. The scientific significance is threefold. First, it operationalizes crystalline gauge-field responses in interacting lattice systems: we will compute charges bound to disclinations/dislocations to extract discrete shift and polarization in fractional Chern insulators, relevant to moiré superlattices and cold-atom platforms. Second, it classifies rotation invariants in topological phases and elevates partial rotation operations from conceptual probes to computation-ready estimators in two-dimensional numerics. With tensor network techniques, the project establishes stable procedures that extract partial rotation expectations, benchmarked on Z2 topological order with exact agreement. Third, it extends crystalline diagnostics to quantum criticality: monopole quantum numbers in Hofstadter-Hubbard models will be computed using analytical and numerical methods, predicting pairing symmetry of anyon superconductors. Methodologically, the proposal integrates: (i) topological field theory with crystalline background fields, relating symmetry fluxes to quantized responses and bulk–boundary relations; (ii) lattice constructions of symmetry-enriched topological orders to engineer symmetry-fractionalization patterns; (iii) scalable numerical pipelines (DMRG for defect embedding; tensor network for partial symmetry operations). Preliminary results demonstrate high-precision extraction of defect-bound charges and exact partial-rotation expectations, de-risking the numerical core. The impact is broad and immediate. For theory, it delivers a bridge between crystalline responses, symmetry fractionalization, and topological field theory, enabling classification and detection beyond free-particle paradigms. For numerics, it supplies a reusable toolbox to quantify crystalline topology in interacting phases and to potentially validate PEPS descriptions of chiral phases.For experiments on moiré and synthetic platforms, the framework provides measurable crystalline invariants,linking lattice defects, and spatial probes to topological data. Collectively, the program promises a standardized, quantitative pathway to compute and measure crystalline invariants in correlated quantum matter. 该提案聚焦于凝聚态物理中的一个重要挑战：在电子相互作用主导的拓扑相中提取晶体不变量，此类系统超出了传统能带理论工具的适用范围。虽然霍尔电导、陈数等量子化响应长期以来是拓扑相的稳健不变量，但空间对称性（如平移、旋转）能够稳定更丰富的对称保护拓扑相（SPT）和对称丰富拓扑相（SET），并且可因相互作用而得到拓展。最新理论表明，晶体缺陷（如旋转畸变、位错）以及部分对称操作可以编码通用数据，诸如离散位移偏移、极化、对称分数化等。然而，目前尚缺乏适用于相互作用系统的广泛而高效的工具，以在显微模型中计算这些不变量。随着二维材料与量子模拟器中晶体对称拓扑相的突破性发现，该领域亟需填补这一空白。为此，本提案提出了一个统一的场论、解析与数值研究框架，目标是开发实际可行的诊断工具。 本研究的科学意义体现在三方面： 实现晶体规范场响应的计算：针对相互作用的晶格系统，我们将计算与晶体缺陷（如旋转畸变和位错）绑定的电荷，提取离散位移偏移和极化，这对于研究摩尔超晶格和冷原子平台中的分数陈绝缘体尤为重要。 分类并量化拓扑相中的旋转不变量：我们将部分旋转操作从理论探针提升为二维数值计算中的实用估算器。通过张量网络技术，建立稳定的提取部分旋转期望值的方法，并通过对Z2拓扑序的验证取得精确一致的结果。 将晶体诊断拓展至量子临界性：利用解析和数值方法计算Hofstadter-Hubbard模型中单极子对称量子数，预测任意子超导体的配对对称性，包括SU(4)扩展的一般化情况。 方法论上，提案整合了以下技术： (i) 基于晶体背景场的拓扑场论，揭示对称性磁通与量子化响应及体-边界关系之间的联系； (ii) 在晶格中构建对称丰富拓扑序，以设计对称分数化模式； (iii) 可扩展的数值方案，包括用于嵌入缺陷的DMRG方法和针对部分对称操作的张量网络技术。 初步研究结果已验证了缺陷绑定电荷的高精度提取与部分旋转期望值的精确计算，为核心数值方法提供了可靠性保障。

16309726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16309726.value: 含高功能化酪氨酸的RiPPs的全面全合成

16309726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309726.value: Reflecting on roughly two centuries of human progress in synthetic organic chemistry, the field has devoted much of that time to the stereochemical control of small molecules such as terpenes and alkaloids. More recently, however, advances in genome mining have led to the identification of numerous ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs) featuring distinctive topologies of cyclic amide linkages. Among these are highly strained cyclic peptides that cannot be formed by conventional amide-coupling methods, as well as macrocycles with characteristic topologies exemplified by lasso peptides. Despite often displaying potent biological activities, the structural complexity and synthetic constraints associated with these motifs render their de novo chemical synthesis a persistent challenge. To address this challenge, the present research project aims to develop a convergent, modular synthetic platform that enables the late-stage incorporation of arbitrary biaryl units directly into oligopeptide linkers, and to apply this platform to comprehensive total syntheses of RiPPs containing highly functionalized tyrosine residues. Specifically, we will combine electrochemical cross electrophilic coupling (XEC) with Walczak–Suzuki cyclization to enable the convergent construction, in the late stages of a synthesis, of macrocyclic peptides bearing either native or non native biaryl linkages. This strategy proceeds under mild conditions and can achieve macrocyclization from readily available oligopeptide linkers in only a few steps, delivering highly distorted atropisomeric macrocycles in high efficiency. By extending this platform, we plan exhaustive, divergent total syntheses of RiPPs that contain highly functionalized tyrosine residues and that feature both biaryl and aryl ether linkages. Construction of these macrocyclic cores will be accomplished through a sequence of electrochemical cross electrophilic coupling, Walczak–Suzuki cyclization, and electrochemical oxidative coupling to forge Tyr–Tyr linkages. Because these transformations do not require prefunctionalized aryl building blocks, the approach affords enhanced synthetic flexibility and practicability. Overall, this synthetic platform offers a unified and scalable route to rapidly access structurally diverse macrocyclic peptides and their analogues. Its modularity and efficiency will facilitate comprehensive structure–activity relationship (SAR) studies and accelerate the discovery of novel bioactive scaffolds in peptide therapeutics. Moreover, it will provide a new, practical, and systematic synthetic methodology for RiPPs, a class for which general synthetic strategies remain largely undeveloped. 回顾人类在有机合成化学领域近两个世纪的进展，该领域的大部分时间都致力于萜类、吲哚生物碱等小分子的立体化学控制。然而，近年来随着基因组挖掘技术的发展，已鉴定出大量核糖体合成并经翻译后修饰的肽类（RiPPs），其特征在于具有独特的环状酰胺拓扑结构。其中包括无法通过常规酰胺偶联方法形成的高应变环肽，以及以套索肽为代表的具有特殊拓扑的巨环结构。尽管这些分子常常表现出强大的生物活性，但其结构复杂性和合成限制使得其从头化学合成仍然是一个长期挑战。 为应对这一挑战，本研究项目旨在开发一种收敛性、模块化的合成平台，使得在合成后期能够直接将任意双芳基单元引入寡肽连接体，并将该平台应用于含高功能化酪氨酸残基的RiPPs的全面全合成。具体而言，我们将结合电化学交叉亲电偶联（XEC）与Walczak–Suzuki环化反应，实现合成后期的收敛构建，从而获得含有天然或非天然双芳基连接的巨环肽。该策略在温和条件下进行，仅需少数步骤即可由易得的寡肽连接体实现宏环化，且能够高效地生成高度扭曲的轴手性宏环。 通过扩展该平台，我们计划开展含高功能化酪氨酸残基的RiPPs的全面、发散性全合成，这些分子同时具有双芳基和芳醚连接。其宏环骨架的构建将通过电化学交叉亲电偶联、Walczak–Suzuki环化以及电化学氧化偶联来实现Tyr–Tyr连接。由于这些转化不需要预先功能化的芳基构件，该方法提供了更高的合成灵活性和实用性。 总体而言，该合成平台为快速获取结构多样的巨环肽及其类似物提供了一条统一且可扩展的途径。其模块化与高效性将有助于全面开展构效关系（SAR）研究，并加速新型肽类治疗分子的发现。此外，它还为RiPPs这一尚缺乏通用合成策略的分子类别提供了一种新的、实用的、系统化的合成方法学。
