Publication, patent, and policy analysis trace how governance principles diffuse into standards and market practices, while comparison with EU and U.S. frameworks situates the Chinese case in global perspective. These form a unified analytical pipeline linking governance architectures, organizational behavior, and innovation outcomes. Three questions guide the research: (1) How do firms internalize and operationalize governance requirements in design architectures and strategic decisions? (2) How do these governance-mediated strategies influence innovation direction—channeling development toward incremental optimization or enabling paradigm-shifting breakthroughs? (3) How are governance principles codified into standards and market practices that institutionalize legitimacy and shape long-term innovation pathways? Theoretically, the study conceptualizes regulation as an ambivalent force enabling innovation through coordination while constraining it through conformity pressures. Empirically, it establishes the first systematic, multi-dimensional evidence base examining how coordination-intensive governance shapes innovation outcomes. Rather than prescribing models, it develops assessment frameworks allowing policymakers to evaluate trade-offs between short-term performance and long-term sustainability. By producing open-access comparative datasets and analytical protocols, the project builds transferable methodological infrastructure for examining governance-innovation dynamics across sectors and jurisdictions, advancing scholarly understanding and policy capacity to align governance with sustainable innovation. 中國生成式人工智能企業僅用五年便躍升至國際前沿水平，這一發展軌跡挑戰了傳統創新理論關於治理約束與技術突破之間關係的基本假設。產業發展處於一個強調安全與管控的協調密集型治理體制之下，與傳統觀點「嚴格監管易抑制技術突破」形成張力。這種嵌入治理體系之中的創新模式，究竟代表一種可持續的適應性發展路徑，還是一種可能導致制度鎖定的階段性動員機制，目前仍缺乏系統性解釋。該議題不僅關係中國AI產業走向，亦對全球變革性新興技術治理具有重要理論與政策啟示。 本研究探討中國 AI 企業平衡治理要求與創新目標的組織機制，重點考察前瞻性合規、效率優化、制度創業三種機制，分析治理協調在何種條件下可成為創新催化劑，而非單純的約束條件。研究提出「治理 — 創新權衡模型」，剖析治理在提升技術表現的同時，亦可能壓縮探索性創新空間，並識別區分適應性協調與制度僵化的邊界條件。 本研究採取整合式多方法設計，從組織、技術、制度三層面交叉驗證。透過中國領先 AI 企業個案，結合過程追蹤與精英訪談，還原企業內化治理規範、落實至技術架構、研發布局與管理實務的機制。針對前沿模型開展計算基準測試與價值審計，評估安全、準確度與適應性的技術權衡。藉由論文、專利與政策文本分析，追蹤治理原則如何擴散並沉澱為技術標準與市場慣例。研究對比歐盟、美國 AI 治理框架，將中國案例置於全球視野對照，搭建銜接治理架構、組織行為與創新成效的綜合分析框架。 研究聚焦三大核心問題：第一，AI 企業如何內化治理要求，落實至技術架構與戰略決策；第二，治理形塑的企業策略如何引導技術發展，偏向漸進式改良或範式轉換的重大突破；第三，治理原則如何納入標準與市場實踐，實現合法性制度化並形塑長期創新路徑。 在理論層面，本研究將治理視為雙重效應機制：既可透過協調整合資源、降低不確定性、提升創新效率，亦會因規範趨同與制度約束壓縮探索性創新空間。在實證層面，本研究建立系統、多維的證據體系，解析高協調型治理對 AI 創新過程與成果的影響。本研究並非試圖提出普適性的治理模式，而是建構分析框架，用以識別不同治理安排影響創新過程與長期可持續性的條件。 本項目將建構可複用的分析框架與研究資源，支持跨產業、跨制度的 AI 治理比較研究，深化學界對治理與創新互動機制的理解，為政策者評估治理布局與創新可持續性提供分析依據。

16603126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16603126.value: 科學史與科學哲學在現代科學社會中的作用

16603126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16603126.value: In the 20th century the significance of scientific inquiry intensified across all levels of social, political, and intellectual life. After the Second World War especially, governments across the globe drastically augmented their financial support for scientific research. This increased the need to reflect on science as an intellectual and social force in modern society. One important field of inquiry, which arose in the Western world out of this, is History and Philosophy of Science (HPS) - a field aimed at integrating insights from history and philosophy to improve our understanding of what science is and how its results should be implemented. Until now, scholars in HPS have conceived the emergence of their field as a purely intellectual response to the tradition of logical empiricism. Logical empiricists used formal logic to model scientific language which resulted in an understanding of scientific inquiry abstracted from actual experimental and theoretical practice. In the 1960s, scholars like Norwood Hanson and Thomas Kuhn advocated that the history of science would prove the best resource to provide interesting cases to understand science as it is actually performed. Traditionally, their work is understood as the main inspiration for the rise of HPS departments, programs and journals ever since then. The traditional narrative, however, has a problem of scope: it focuses only on the 1960s, on a limited set of actors, and is centered around the American context. This project intends to broaden the historical narrative by looking at both intellectual and institutional developments in the early 1940s and 1950s in the USA and Europe which led to the emergence of HPS as a field of study. The project will also expand available oral recollection about the emergence of HPS by interviewing important scholars from these various regions about their early training and work in this field. This enriched narrative will not only be significant for the history of philosophy, but also aims to refocus attention to the explicitly social motivations, of administrators, philosophers and scientists, to improve how scientific knowledge is received and used in our modern societies. Contemporary work in HPS is faced with challenges to reach beyond its disciplinary confines and have a significance on education and broader culture. This project will reflect on those challenges by recovering past problems earlier scholars and administrators faced and by extending these problems to our contemporary situation. 在20世紀，科學探究的重要性在社會、政治和知識生活的各個層面都日益凸顯。尤其是在第二次世界大戰之後，世界各國政府大幅增加了科學研究的財政支持。這使得人們更需要反思科學作為現代社會中一股知識和社會力量的角色。由此，西方世界興起了一個重要的研究領域－科學史與科學哲學（HPS）。這個領域旨在整合歷史和哲學的洞見，以增進我們對科學本質及其成果應用方式的理解。 迄今為止，科學史與科學哲學領域的學者一直認為，該領域的出現是對邏輯經驗主義傳統的一種純粹的理性回應。邏輯經驗主義者運用形式邏輯來建構科學語言模型，導致他們對科學探究的理解脫離了實際的實驗和理論實踐。在1960年代，諾伍德·漢森和托馬斯·庫恩等學者提出，科學史將是提供有趣案例的最佳資源，有助於我們理解科學的實際運作方式。傳統上，他們的工作被認為是此後人文與社會科學（HPS）系所、計畫和期刊興起的主要靈感來源。然而，傳統的敘述存在範圍上的限制：它只關注20世紀60年代，涉及的行動者有限，且以美國為中心。本計畫旨在拓展歷史敘述，考察20世紀40年代和50年代初美國和歐洲的知識和製度發展，正是這些發展促成了人文與社會科學作為一門學科的出現。本計畫也將透過採訪來自不同地區的重要學者，了解他們早期在該領域的學習和工作，從而豐富現有的人文與社會科學興起的口述回憶。 這種更豐富的敘述不僅對哲學史意義重大，而且旨在重新聚焦於管理者、哲學家和科學家為改善現代社會對科學知識的接受和運用所採取的明確的社會動機。當代人文與社會科學的研究面臨著超越學科界限、對教育和更廣泛的文化產生影響的挑戰。本計畫將透過回顧早期學者和管理者面臨的過去問題，並將這些問題擴展到我們當今的情況，來反思這些挑戰。

16603726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16603726.value: 夢境：一種嶄新的敘述歷史與現實的角度

16603726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16603726.value: This project centers on dreamscape—a core component of surrealist writing—in 21st-century Chinese novels, examining its narrative construction and ideological role in key works: Yan Lianke’s The Lingering Soul, Su Tong’s Good Weather, Mo Yin’s Ritual Paper Figure, Du Li’s Ripple, Hon Lai-chu’s Empty Face. While scholars like Robert Ford Campany (Campany 2020) have conducted systematic studies on dreams and dreaming in early medieval Chinese literature, contemporary Chinese literary research has largely overlooked this vital representational approach. This gap is closely tied to Max Weber’s concept of “disenchantment”: modernity’s emphasis on secularization and rationalization has sidelined dream-focused inquiry, reducing surreal dream worlds to dismissible superstition rather than recognizing their literary value. Dream research itself presents unique challenges, as no single, universally applicable theory exists to unpack its complexity—even Buddhist, Daoist, or Confucian frameworks alone fail to fully explain the intricate relationship between dreams and literature. Yet dreamscape has long been a defining motif: it anchors classical Chinese masterpieces (e.g., Dream of the Red Chamber, The Peony Pavilion, Strange Tales from a Chinese Studio) and modern works like Lu Xun’s Wild Grass, while Western authors such as Jorge Luis Borges, Roberto Bolaño (2666) and Ismail Kadare (The Palace of Dreams) also deploy dreams extensively. This study poses critical questions: How does the dreamscape in 21st-century Chinese novels differ from those of Eastern and Western traditions? Do contemporary writers develop innovative approaches to depicting dreams, and does the inherent unverifiability of dreams grant them a distinct form of “alternative truth”? Furthermore, this project will take into account the representation of the dreamscape in cultural production such as films, web-novels, TV series, and other media. Focusing on dreamscape’s concrete manifestations—including immersive dream realms and spirit journeys shaped by dream logic—the project argues this element engages with, intervenes in, and even rewrites historical narratives and lived reality more powerfully than realist techniques. Methodologically, the study combines close textual analysis of dreamscape representations with cultural studies inquiries into the social-political contexts shaping these narratives. It positions dreamscape as a vital aesthetic innovation for 21st-century Chinese surrealist fiction and media. Research outputs will include peer-reviewed journal articles, presentations at international conferences, and a potential monograph exploring supernatural literary representations. 本研究項目以夢境敘事作為二十一世紀中國小說超現實書寫的核心載體，選取閻連科《日熄》、蘇童《好天氣》、默音《甲馬》、劉亮程《長命》、杜梨《漪》、韓麗珠《裸山》六部代表性作品，剖析夢境敘事的敘事建構方式與思想內涵。當下學界雖有羅伯特・福特・康帕尼（Robert Ford Campany，2020）針對中國中古文學夢書寫展開體系化研究，但當代漢語文學領域仍長期忽視夢境這一關鍵書寫手段。此研究空白與馬克斯・韋伯提出的「除魅」概念深度相關：現代性崇尚世俗化與理性化的認知邏輯，使得以夢為核心的文學書寫備受邊緣化，學界往往將超現實夢境貶為無足輕重的迷信敘述，未能發掘其獨特文學價值。 夢境研究本身存在理論層面的天然難題：目前尚未形成一套可通用、能完整解釋夢敘複雜性的統一理論體系，單獨依靠儒、釋、道的思想框架，無法完整地梳理中國當代小說夢與文學之間錯綜複雜的關聯。但夢向來是文學經典的核心母題，從中國古典文學《紅樓夢》《牡丹亭》《聊齋誌異》，到魯迅《野草》等現代文學作品，夢境敘事始終佔據重要地位。西方文學經典如博爾赫斯〈循環廢墟〉、羅貝托・波拉尼奧《2666》、伊斯梅爾・卡達萊《夢宮》等西方經典亦大量運用夢境書寫。本研究由此提出核心研究問題：二十一世紀中國小說的夢境敘事，相較中西文學傳統存在何種差異？當代作家是否開拓出獨特的夢境書寫美學？夢境本身具備的不可驗證性，是否賦予文學一類異質的「另類真實」？除此以外，本研究亦納入電影、網路小說、電視劇等大眾文化文本，考察夢意象在跨媒介文化生產中的呈現樣貌。 本研究聚焦沉浸式夢境場域、依循夢邏輯展開的靈魂遊歷等夢敘具體形態，提出核心論點：相較現實主義敘事手法，夢境書寫能夠更強有力地介入、干預乃至重構歷史敘述與個體的精神真實。研究方法上，本文結合夢境文本細讀法與文化研究視角，考察塑造夢敘的社會、政治語境。總體而言，本研究試圖論證：夢境敘事是二十一世紀中國超現實文學與跨媒介創作極為關鍵的美學創新，而該領域迄今仍未獲足夠學術關注。本研究預期成果包含外審期刊論文、國際學術會議發表，並計劃撰寫一部學術專著，系統梳理超自然文學書寫的內涵與形態。

16604126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16604126.value: 賦能藝術創意：AI輔助的藝科構想支援研究

16604126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16604126.value: Art-tech, the convergence of art and technology, harnesses technological advancements to create, enhance, and inspire artistic expression. Recognizing its potential, Hong Kong's 2020 Policy Address identified art-tech as a strategic priority for driving creative innovation. Yet artists often face significant obstacles when engaging with emerging technologies, due to technical complexity, fragmented resources, and communication gaps between artistic and scientific communities. Although generative artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT, holds great promise for enhancing artistic ideation, its creative potential and cultural implications within art-tech practice remain largely unexamined. This project examines how generative AI can assist artists in accessing, interpreting, and integrating emerging technologies into innovative artworks. It addresses four interrelated challenges: (C1) limited understanding of how artists conceptualize art-tech ideas and the difficulties they encounter, even with AI support; (C2) lack of a structured dataset and taxonomy to systematically organize art-tech knowledge; (C3) absence of dedicated AI-assisted tools that facilitate open-ended creative exploration, while preserving artistic authorship; and (C4) insufficient empirical evidence on the impact of AI-assisted systems in art-tech ideation. We propose a systematic and human-centered research framework that bridges technological innovation and artistic creation. First, a formative study with practicing artists will analyze arttech ideation processes and identify design requirements for effective creativity-support tools (C1). Second, we will construct a research-driven dataset of art-tech works, with a validated taxonomy, which integrates the multimodal information into a knowledge-linked resource to support analysis, comparison, and generative creativity, shifting from event-based documentation in existing archives (C2). Third, we will design and develop an AI-assisted platform for iterative and exploratory art-tech ideation, powered by multimodal LLMs and knowledge-augmented reasoning (C3). The system will respect artistic context, personal style, technological nature, creative intent, and copyright. Finally, we will evaluate its effectiveness through benchmarking, user studies, participatory workshops, and a public exhibition to assess its creative, educational, and cultural impact (C4). By lowering technological barriers and fostering AI-supported creative ideation, this project will deepen understanding of human-AI collaboration in art-tech practice. Expected outcomes—the findings of the formative study, a curated dataset, and a creativity support platform—will advance research in art-tech, digital humanities, and computational creativity. Beyond academia, the project will enhance art and design education, empower creative practitioners, and nurture AI literacy in the cultural sector, positioning Hong Kong as a key player in interdisciplinary art-tech research and education. 藝術科技（Art Tech）強調藝術與科技的匯聚，透過科技創新拓展藝術表達與創意產業的可能性。 香港特區政府在《2020年施政報告》中將藝術科技列為推動創意創新的策略重點之一，但藝術家在接觸新興科技時，仍面對技術複雜、資源零散，以及藝術與科技社群溝通不足等障礙。 生成式人工智能（AI），尤其大型語言模型（如 ChatGPT），為藝術構想與人機協作帶來新契機，然而其在藝術科技實踐中的創意潛力與文化意涵，仍有待深入研究。 本研究探討生成式AI如何協助藝術家理解、串聯及運用新興科技於創作構想，並回應四項關鍵挑戰：（C1）目前對藝術家如何構思藝術科技創作及其在過程中所面對的困難（即使已有 AI 協助）缺乏深入了解；（C2）尚未建立具結構化的資料集及分類架構；（C3）缺乏專為開放式創意探索而設計、同時維護藝術家作者性與創作主體性的 AI 輔助工具；以及（C4）對 AI 輔助系統在藝術科技構想過程中的實際影響，仍缺乏充足的實證研究。 研究將採用以人為本的框架：首先，透過與藝術家的前期研究，分析藝術科技構想流程並歸納設計原則（C1）；其次，策劃並建構具多模態資訊與分類的藝術科技作品資料集，作為分析與生成構想的知識資源（C2）；再者，以多模態大型語言模型與知識強化推理為基礎，開發支援反覆及探索式構想的 AI 平台，並在設計上尊重創作脈絡、個人風格與著作權（C3）；最後，透過用戶研究評估平台在創意實踐與教育現場的效用（C4）。 該項目將深化對人機協作於藝術科技實踐的理解，並產出前期研究洞見、具多模態資訊與分類的藝術科技作品資料集與創意構想支援平台三項核心成果。 在學術層面，研究將推動藝術科技、數位人文與計算創意等領域的發展；在社會與文化層面，研究將促進藝術與設計教育、賦能創意工作者，並提升文化界對 AI 的理解與批判思維，強化香港在跨領域藝術科技研究與教育上的關鍵地位。

16604526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16604526.value: 國之利器：國有資本如何驅動中國科技競賽中的創新

16604526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16604526.value: China's pursuit of technological supremacy has given rise to a new policy arsenal: Government-Guided Investment Funds (GGIFs), state-backed vehicles that mobilize trillions of RMB to finance strategic technology firms. While existing research often analyzes such policy tools in isolation, the proposed study places GGIFs at the core of China's state capital mobilization strategy and situates them in the broader innovation ecosystem, including the role of state-sponsored science exemplified by the National Key Laboratories (NKLs). In principle, these mechanisms are designed to function in coordination, forming a cohesive pipeline that translates scientific discovery into commercial innovation and technological advancement. In practice, however, China's high-profile successes, including notable technological breakthroughs and rapid industrial scaling, coexist with persistent challenges such as capital misallocation, bureaucratic inefficiencies, and fragmented implementation. These mixed outcomes prompt a central research question: Under what conditions does state capital effectively align with state-sponsored science to foster impactful innovation, and when does it fail? Answering this question is crucial for assessing China's technological capabilities and envisioning the future of global technology competition. This project employs a sequential mixed-methods research design that integrates quantitative analysis with qualitative insights. It begins by establishing the statistical association between GGIF–NKL synergy and innovation performance. A panel dataset will be constructed to track thousands of Chinese technology firms, GGIF investments, and NKL affiliations from 2014 to 2023. Using statistical methods, the impact of this synergy on innovation outcomes, such as patent filings, will be assessed. This analysis will be complemented by Social Network Analysis (SNA) to map the structural features of these innovation ecosystems, focusing on the interplay between GGIFs and NKLs. Guided by these quantitative findings, the project will explore the mechanisms underlying these patterns. Through fieldwork interviews with GGIF managers, NKL scientists, and government officials, the qualitative study will uncover the political, institutional, and organizational mechanisms that facilitate success or contribute to failure. This integrated mixed-method approach enables the project to move from identifying statistical patterns to generating rich, contextually grounded explanations. This study will advance the understanding of state-led innovation and industrial policies, by revealing how institutional synergies between GGIFs and NKLs shape innovation outcomes. It will also provide policymakers with evidence-based insights to design more targeted and adaptive innovation strategies, relevant to both Chinese mainland and economies like Hong Kong, which is pursuing government-led innovation policies and positioning itself as an international innovation hub under the Greater Bay Area initiative. 中國對科技優勢的追求催生了一套新的政策武器庫:政府引導基金。這是一種由國家支持的投資載體,動員數以萬億計的人民幣資金,為戰略性科技企業提供融資。既有研究多將此類政策工具孤立分析,而本研究則將政府引導基金置於中國國有資本戰略的核心,並將其放置在更廣泛的創新生態系統中加以考察,包括以國家重點實驗室為代表的國家資助科學體系的角色。就制度設計而言,這些機制本應協調運作,形成一條連貫的管道,將科學發現轉化為商業創新與技術進步。然而在實踐中,中國廣受矚目的成功案例,包括重大技術突破與快速的產業規模化,與資本錯配、官僚體系低效、政策執行碎片化等長期挑戰並存。這種喜憂參半的結果引出了本研究的核心問題:國有資本在何種條件下能夠有效地與國家資助的科學體系協同配合,從而催生具有影響力的創新?又在何種情況下會歸於失敗?回答這一問題,對於評估中國的科技實力、展望全球科技競爭的未來格局,都至關重要。 本項目採用循序推進的混合研究方法,將定量分析與定性洞察相結合。研究首先確立政府引導基金與國家重點實驗室之間的協同效應與創新績效之間的統計關聯。項目將構建一個面板數據集,追蹤2014至2023年間數千家中國科技企業、政府引導基金的投資活動以及企業與國家重點實驗室的關聯情況,並運用統計方法評估這種協同效應對專利申請等創新產出的影響。在此基礎上,研究將輔以社會網絡分析, 繪製這些創新生態系統的結構特徵,重點考察政府引導基金與國家重點實驗室之間的互動關係。在定量研究結果的引導下,項目將進一步探究這些模式背後的作用機制:通過對政府引導基金管理者、國家重點實驗室科學家及政府官員的實地訪談,定性研究將揭示促成成功或導致失敗的政治、制度與組織機制。這種整合性的混合研究方法,使本項目得以從識別統計模式,推進到生成豐富且紮根於具體情境的解釋。 本研究將通過揭示政府引導基金與國家重點實驗室之間的制度協同如何塑造創新結果,深化學界對國家主導型創新與產業政策的理解;同時也將為政策制定者提供基於實證的洞見,以設計更具針對性和適應性的創新戰略。這不僅適用於中國內地,也適用於香港等經濟體:香港正推行政府主導的創新政策,並在粵港澳大灣區倡議下致力於打造國際創新樞紐。

16604926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16604926.value: 手繪與生成式人工智慧繪圖如何影響人類的視覺認知？

16604926.label: Co - Investigator(s)
16604926.value: Prof Chan, Antoni B. Prof Hsiao, Janet Hui-wen Prof LC, Ray

16604926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16604926.value: Artists exhibit superior visual information extraction and processing capabilities as compared with novices, such as improved global-local attentional flexibility. This flexibility involves both global attention to overall structure and local attention to detailed features. However, it remains unclear whether these differences result from drawing training or inherent characteristics as previous studies have primarily focused on comparing novices with experts. This research aims to test the hypothesis that drawing training leads to enhanced visual object identification performance associated with changes in attention strategies and internal perceptual representations through both computational modeling and human experiments. We also hypothesize that these benefits may be limited to hand-drawing training but not drawing with generative AI tools. Computationally, we will integrate the DNN (Deep Neural Network) + HMM (Hidden Markov Model) model with a drawing module to learn attention strategies and perceptual representations for both identifying the input object and reproducing the details of the object image. Experimentally, we will employ simultaneous eye tracking and EEG recording to measure human attention strategies and neural activities in visual object identification tasks to verify the modeling predictions. We hypothesize that drawing training may enhance several aspects of visual cognition, including enhanced object identification performance, attentional flexibility to adopt global and local processing, reduction in holistic processing of visual objects, and enhancement of neural representations of visual stimuli with higher fidelity. However, these effects may be weakened when drawing with generative AI tools through text prompts as opposed to traditional hand-drawing methods. The outcomes of this research will contribute to a deeper understanding of expert visual processing strategies and representations, and elucidate how these can be achieved through drawing training. Importantly, advancements in generative AI technology have revolutionized the workflows of art practitioners and facilitated art creation in the general population with minimal drawing expertise required. However, it is crucial to consider its potential negative impacts while embracing the great capabilities of the technology. The findings of this study are expected to have significant implications for various fields, including psychology, education, neuroscience, human-computer interaction, and human-centric AI. 相較於新手，美術家具備更強的視覺資訊提取與處理能力，例如擁有更好的全局-局部注意靈活性。這種靈活性既包括針對整體結構的全局注意力，也包括針對細節特徵的局部注意力。然而，過去研究大多僅比較新手與專家，因此尚無法確認此類差異究竟源自繪畫訓練，還是個體先天特質。本研究結合計算建模與人類行為實驗，檢驗如下假設：繪畫訓練能夠提升視覺物體識別表現，該提升與注意策略以及內在知覺表徵的改變相關。我們同時假設，上述提升效果僅限於手繪訓練，並不適用於使用生成式人工智慧工具進行繪圖。 計算層面上，我們將把深度神經網路（DNN）與隱馬可夫模型（HMM）相結合的模型，加入繪圖模組，用以學習注意力策略與知覺表徵，同時實現輸入物體的識別以及物體圖像細節的復現。實驗層面上，我們將同步採用眼動追蹤與腦電（EEG）記錄，測量受試者在視覺物體識別任務中的注意力策略與神經活動，驗證模型的預測結果。我們假設，繪畫訓練可從多個方面提升視覺認知能力，包括改善物體識別表現、提升全局-局部加工的注意力靈活性、降低視覺物體的全局加工程度，以及強化視覺刺激的神經表徵，使其擁有更高保真度。但相較於傳統手繪方式，透過文字提示使用生成式人工智慧工具繪圖時，上述各項效果將會減弱。 本研究的研究成果將有助於更深入地理解專家視覺加工策略與表徵機制，並闡明透過繪畫訓練何以實現此類能力。重要的是，生成式人工智慧技術的進步已經革新了美術從業者的工作流程，也讓幾乎沒有繪畫基礎的大眾能夠輕鬆進行美術創作。然而，在接納該技術強大能力的同時，也必須重視其潛在的負面影響。本研究的預期成果將對心理學、教育學、神經科學、人機交互以及以人為本的人工智慧等多個領域具有重要啟示。

17100626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17100626.value: 多配体蛋白聚糖4（Sdc4）在缺血性腦中風血腦屏障破壞中的關鍵調控角色：分子機制與治療前景

17100626.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17100626.value: Prof Chang, Junlei Prof Xu, Aimin

17100626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17100626.value: Ischemic stroke (IS)-induced breakdown of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) is associated with poorer clinical outcomes. Brain microvascular endothelial cells (BMECs) play a crucial role in maintaining BBB integrity by forming specialized tight junctions that restrict paracellular passage between blood and brain tissue. Additionally, BMECs regulate transcellular transport by limiting vesicle trafficking and transcytosis, thereby preserving the selective permeability of the BBB. Syndecan-4 (Sdc4) is a heparan sulfate proteoglycan receptor composed of an intracellular domain, a transmembrane domain, and an ectodomain. It can function as a receptor or co-receptor to modulate cellular activities upon ligand binding. Under pathological conditions, increased shedding of the Sdc4 ectodomain occurs, which can exert detrimental effects on cells. Our preliminary data demonstrated that cerebral Sdc4 expression and its ectodomain shedding were significantly upregulated in mice subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO). Infiltrating macrophages and microglia were identified as the primary cellular sources of cerebral Sdc4. Macrophage-specific Sdc4 deficiency protected mice against MCAO-induced BBB disruption, associated with alleviated neurological deficits and reduced endothelial vesicle formation. Treatment of BMECs with recombinant Sdc4-ectodomain increased plasmalemma vesicle-associated protein (PLVAP) expression, a facilitator of transcytosis-without affecting tight junction proteins, indicating enhanced endothelial permeability via transcytosis. Additionally, Sdc4 alone or with VEGF exerted a synergistic effect on PLVAP expression in BMECs. Sdc4 also interacts with integrin Itgb1, suggesting a potential pathway for its effects. Sdc4 deficiency also attenuated MCAO-induced cerebral macrophage infiltration, and Sdc4-deficient macrophages displayed reduced migratory capacity in response to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion. Preliminary treatment with Sdc4-ectodomain-neutralizing antibody showed trends toward reduced BBB leakage and alleviated neurological deficits. VEGF and integrin-α5β1 independently induce PLVAP, contributing to increased endothelial permeability. Sdc4 has been shown to crosstalk with VEGF and integrin-α5β1, thereby promoting their functions in pathological conditions. Based on the evidence, we hypothesize that during IS, increased shedding of Sdc4-ectodomain acts through integrin-α5β1 to induce PLVAP expression, or as a co-receptor for VEGF, synergistically upregulating PLVAP via VEGFR2. Elevated PLVAP then promotes transcytosis, leading to increased endothelial permeability, BBB disruption, and worsens IS outcomes. Intact Sdc4 may modulate macrophage infiltration through CCL2-CCR2 chemotactic axis. This study will investigate how Sdc4 contributes to IS and assess the therapeutic potential of targeting its ectodomain with specific antibodies. The findings aim to clarify Sdc4's role in macrophage-endothelial interactions, BBB disruption, and macrophage infiltration, highlighting its promise as a therapeutic target for IS. 缺血性腦中風（IS）會破壞保護大腦的血腦屏障，這種破壞與較差的臨床結果有關。大腦微血管的內皮細胞（BMECs）在維持血腦屏障的完整性方面扮演著非常重要的角色。它們會形成特殊的緊密連接，限制血液與腦組織之間的物質通過。此外，這些持續的內皮細胞還調控物質穿越血管的方式，通過限制小泡的活動，保持血腦屏障的選擇性通透性。 一個名為多配体蛋白聚糖4 ( Sdc4）的蛋白質，是一種帶有糖胺聚糖的受體，具有細胞內、跨膜和外部部分。它可以作為一個受體或协同受體，在與配體結合時調節細胞的活動。在疾病狀況下，Sdc4的外部部分會被過度釋放 (（稱為碎片化），這可能對細胞產生不良影響。 我們的初步研究發現，在用來模擬中風的老鼠身上，腦內Sdc4的表達和外部碎片化變得明顯增加。這些Sdc4主要來自進入腦部的巨噬細胞和微膠細胞。我們發現，讓這些巨噬細胞缺乏Sdc4可以減少血腦屏障破壞，同時改善神經功能，並減少內皮細胞的小泡形成。此外，將重組的Sdc4碎片加入腦內皮細胞，會增加一種叫做PLVAP的蛋白質的表現，這種蛋白質促進細胞內的小泡形成，幫助物質穿越血管，並沒有影響緊密連接蛋白，顯示血管的通透性增加是由轉運作用引起的。另外，Sdc4還會與VEGF和一種名為整合素Itgb1的蛋白相互作用，暗示這些蛋白可能在血管通透性增加的過程中扮演角色。缺乏Sdc4也減少了大腦中的巨噬細胞浸潤，並且在缺氧-再灌流的實驗中，缺乏Sdc4的巨噬細胞移動能力也較弱。初步用抗Sdc4的抗體治療，也展現出減少血腦屏障破壞和改善神經狀況的趨勢。 進一步來說，VEGF和整合素α5β1都會促進PLVAP的表現，導致血管變得更通透。Sdc4則可能與這些蛋白交流協同作用，促進它們在疾病中的功能。根據這些證據，我們推測在腦中風發生時，Sdc4的外部碎片化可能通過與整合素α5β1作用，誘導PLVAP的表現；也可能作為VEGF的協同受體，與VEGFR2一同促使PLVAP上升。這會增加血管的轉運能力，使血腦屏障破裂，從而惡化腦中風的結果。完整的Sdc4可能也會通過調控特定化學訊號，影響巨噬細胞的進入。 本研究將探討Sdc4在腦中風中扮演的角色，並評估用特定抗體阻斷Sdc4外部部分的治療潛力。我們希望找到，Sdc4在血管與免疫細胞互動、血腦屏障破裂，以及巨噬細胞滲透中的角色，並促使它成為未來治療腦中風的新目標。

17101126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17101126.value: 粒線體轉移介導膠質母細胞瘤化療抗藥性的表觀遺傳機制

17101126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17101126.value: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most common and aggressive primary brain tumor in adults, characterized by inevitable recurrence and a dismal prognosis. Despite standard multimodal treatment including maximal surgical resection, concomitant radiotherapy, and adjuvant temozolomide chemotherapy, patients often develop chemoresistance, leading to tumor relapse. This regimen has been the standard since 2005 and provides survival benefits, however, treatment guidelines for recurrent glioblastoma remain lacking. Our team has been focusing on understanding the clinical emergence of chemoresistant tumor cells, which represents a key factor in tumor recurrence. In recent years, emerging studies have demonstrated the important role of intercellular mitochondria transfer (MT) in conferring the bioenergetic advantage to recipient cells. Our team found that GBM cells can exploit MT to hijack mitochondria from astrocytes in the brain tumor microenvironment, primarily via tunnelling nanotubes (TNTs), enhancing mitochondrial function, metabolic potential and proliferation in recipient tumor cells. We also revealed that a MT phenotype in tumor cells correlates with poorer prognosis in GBM patients. More importantly, we found that tumor cells receiving mitochondria were less responsive to the chemotherapy temozolomide compared with non-recipient cells, accompanied by epigenetic changes on DNA methylation, suggesting that MT may contribute to chemoresistance through metabolic-epigenetic regulation. Based on these observations, we hypothesize that MT to cancer cells is a key pathological mechanism underlying the development of chemoresistance in glioblastoma. In this proposed study, treatment responders and non-responders from our in-house patient cohort will be used to evaluate the prognostic significance of MT in predicting treatment response. The mechanisms by which MT drives chemoresistance will be elucidated by characterizing the metabolic and epigenetic changes in the DNA methylome, and the associated gene signatures and pathways will be identified. We will also explore the therapeutic potential of targeting MT to overcome chemoresistance using preclinical animal models. This study aims to define the role and mechanisms of MT in contributing to chemoresistance by integrating clinical, basic and translational research platforms. Understanding how MT influences treatment response will facilitate the prediction of clinical outcomes by uncovering the metabolic-epigenetic links. The epigenetic signatures that characterize treatment-resistant cells will further guide patient stratification and treatment planning. In light of the emerging concept of MT, our study will open new avenues for drug development and improve patient survival by reducing tumor recurrence. 膠質母細胞瘤是成人最常見且惡性程度最高的原發性腦腫瘤，具有高度化療抗藥性及復發率，臨床預後極差。目前雖以手術切除合併放射治療及替莫唑胺化療作為標準治療，但針對復發性膠質母細胞瘤仍缺乏有效治療策略。本研究團隊發現，膠質母細胞瘤細胞可透過奈米管從星形膠質細胞獲取粒線體，提升粒線體功能、代謝活性及腫瘤生長能力。更重要的是，接受粒線體的腫瘤細胞對替莫唑胺的治療反應較差，並伴隨DNA甲基化等表觀遺傳改變，顯示粒線體轉移可能透過代謝與表觀遺傳重塑促進化療抗藥性的形成。本研究假設星形膠質細胞來源的粒線體轉移是膠質母細胞瘤化療抗藥性的關鍵致病機制。我們將利用本團隊建立的病人樣本及臨床前動物模型，評估粒線體轉移與治療反應的關聯，解析其引發的代謝及DNA甲基體變化，並鑑定相關分子機制與訊息傳遞路徑。此外，本研究亦將探討抑制粒線體轉移作為克服化療抗藥性的潛在治療策略。本研究將整合臨床、基礎及轉化研究，闡明粒線體轉移促進膠質母細胞瘤化療抗藥性的分子機制，並建立其作為預測治療反應生物標誌及治療標的的可行性。研究成果將有助於發展新的精準治療策略，降低腫瘤復發，並改善膠質母細胞瘤患者的臨床預後。

17101426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17101426.value: 整合污水監測以指導新發傳染病預警與防控決策

17101426.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17101426.value: Prof Lam, Tsan Yuk Prof Wu, Joseph Tsz Kei Prof ZHANG, Tong Dr Zheng, Xiawan

17101426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17101426.value: Background During the recent COVID-19 pandemic, numerous efforts were made to control the spread of this emerging respiratory disease. In the last decade, wastewater surveillance (WWS), as a novel approach, has been widely implemented to supplement existing case-based epidemiological surveillance for monitoring the transmission of various infectious diseases. However, the results from WWS have rarely been used for evidence-based decision-making for public health measures. Methods In this project, we propose to integrate well-characterized mathematical models for infectious disease transmission and WWS to create a framework for simulation and study how WWS data can best inform public health measures. First, we will extend WWS models to consider faecal shedding dynamics, shedding behaviour, population mobility, and pathogen-specific characteristics such as types of pathogens, viral concentration and decay. Second, we will integrate infectious disease and WWS models to simulate wastewater signals with high spatiotemporal resolution and variations at multiple levels. Lastly, we will examine the value of utilizing WWS to inform potential public health measures triggered by results from integration of existing surveillance systems and WWS, using COVID-19 and chikungunya as case studies. Expected outcomes and implication The proposed project will leverage our previous WWS data and experience at different levels. The proposed integrated model framework, comprising infectious transmission models, WWS models, and public health measures feedback loops, will create a simulation platform to explore the impact of various public health measures and identify data gaps in WWS-based decision-making. The simulation results will improve the understanding of this novel data source for disease surveillance and enhance communication of WWS results to stakeholders of health decision-making. 背景 在近期的2019新型冠狀病毒病（COVID-19）大流行期間，各界為控制這種新發呼吸道疾病的傳播作出了大量努力。過去數年間，污水監測作為一種新興方法已被廣泛應用以補充現有的基於病例的傳統流行病學監測，用於監測各種傳染病的傳播。然而，污水監測的結果鮮少被用於公共衛生措施的循證決策。 方法 在本項目中，我們將整合經過已有的傳染病傳播數學模型與污水監測模型，以建立模擬框架研究污水監測數據如何最有效地為公共衛生措施提供依據。首先，我們將擴展污水監測模型，以考慮糞便病毒動力學、個體病毒釋出行為、人口流動性，以及病原體特異性特徵（如病原體類型、病毒濃度及衰減等）。其次，我們將整合傳染病模型與污水監測模型，模擬具有高時空分辨率及多層次變異的污水信號。最後，我們將以COVID-19和基孔肯雅熱為案例研究，探討利用污水監測結果，為現有監測系統與污水監測整合後所觸發的潛在公共衛生措施提供決策依據的價值。 預期成果與意義 本項目將充分利用我們此前在不同層面積累的污水監測數據與經驗。所提出的整合模型框架涵蓋傳染病傳播模型、污水監測模型及公共衛生措施反饋迴路，我們將建立一個模擬平台，以探索各種公共衛生措施的影響，並識別基於污水監測決策中的數據缺口。模擬結果將加深對這一新型疾病監測數據來源的理解，並促進污水監測結果向衛生決策持份者的有效傳達。

17101926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17101926.value: 標靶跨物種染色質相互作用治療EB病毒相關鼻咽癌

17101926.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17101926.value: Prof Chen, Honglin Dr Chung, Lai Shun Dittman Prof Kwong, Lai Wan Dora Prof Lee, Ho Fan Victor Dr Tsang, Anna Chi Man

17101926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17101926.value: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is a ubiquitous human herpesvirus implicated in the pathogenesis of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), a malignancy with high metastatic potential. Despite decades of research, the molecular mechanisms by which EBV contributes to NPC progression remain incompletely understood. Our recent studies have uncovered that EBV episomes act as mobile transcriptional regulators, interacting with host chromatin and reprogramming enhancer landscapes through a process termed “enhancer infestation”. Central to this mechanism is the hijacking of KDM5B, an epigenetic regulator, which facilitates EBV-host chromatin tethering and drives oncogenic transcriptional programs. We identified a robust epigenomic signature, named as EBVIR-enhancer-KDM5B, that predicts metastasis independent of clinical stage and EBV DNA levels and demonstrated that disrupting this axis suppresses tumour growth and EBV persistence. Building on these findings, we propose a multi-phase study to dissect the molecular basis of EBV-host chromatin interactions and evaluate novel therapeutic strategies. First, we will employ multi-omics approaches including 4C-seq, CUT&RUN-seq, and HiChIP to map EBV-interacting regions (EBVIRs), KDM5B and EBNA1 binding sites, and histone modifications in EBV+ patient-derived xenografts and clinical samples. Functional perturbation via CRISPR-mediated enhancer deletion and KDM5B overexpression will be used to assess the impact on chromatin accessibility, enhancer activity, and tumour invasiveness. Protein complex analyses and spatial proteomics will further elucidate the role of EBNA1-KDM5B interactions in chromatin tethering. Second, we will evaluate the next-generation BET inhibitor with a favourable safety profile, for its ability to disrupt EBV-driven enhancer activation. In vitro and in vivo studies will assess its effects on tumour growth, EBV DNA load, and expression of metastasis- and stemness-related genes. Finally, we will integrate multi-omics data using an AI-driven drug screening platform to identify novel therapeutic targets dysregulated by EBV-host chromatin interactions. This study aims to provide comprehensive preclinical evidence for targeting cross-species chromatin interactions as a transformative strategy for EBV-associated solid tumours. By elucidating the molecular underpinnings of EBV enhancer reprogramming and validating the BET inhibitor therapeutic potential, we seek to advance precision medicine approaches for high-risk NPC patients. EB病毒是一種普遍存在的人類皰疹病毒，與鼻咽癌的發病機制密切相關，而鼻咽癌是一種具有高度轉移潛能的惡性腫瘤。儘管經過數十年的研究，EBV促進鼻咽癌進展的分子機制仍未完全闡明。我們近期的研究發現，EBV遊離體可作為可動式轉錄調節因數，與宿主染色質相互作用，並透過稱為增強子侵襲的過程重塑增強子分佈。此機制的核心在於劫持表觀遺傳調節因數 KDM5B，從而促進 EBV 與宿主染色質的錨定，並驅動致癌轉錄過程。我們識別出一個表觀基因組特徵，命名為 EBVIR-enhancer-KDM5B，該特徵能獨立於臨床分期和 EBV DNA 水平來預測轉移，並證明抑制這個過程可抑制腫瘤生長和 EBV 的持續存在。 基於這些發現，我們提出一項多階段研究，旨在解析 EBV 與宿主染色質相互作用的分子基礎，並評估新型治療策略。首先，我們將採用多組學方法（包括 4C-seq、CUT&RUN-seq 和 HiChIP），在 EBV 陽性病人來源的異種移植瘤（PDX）及臨床樣本中，繪製 EBV 相互作用區域、KDM5B 與 EBNA1 結合位點以及組蛋白修飾圖譜。我們將利用 CRISPR 介導的增強子刪除和 KDM5B 過表達等功能干預手段，評估其對染色質可及性、增強子活性及腫瘤侵襲性的影響。蛋白質複合物分析與空間蛋白質體學將進一步闡明 EBNA1-KDM5B 相互作用在染色質錨定中的作用。 其次，我們將評估具有良好安全性特徵的新一代 BET 抑制劑，以探討其破壞 EBV 驅動的增強子活化的能力。體外與體內研究將評估其對腫瘤生長、EBV DNA 載量以及轉移和幹細胞相關基因表達的影响。最後，我們將利用人工智能方法為基礎的藥物篩檢平台整合多組學數據，以識別受 EBV 與宿主染色質相互作用失調的新型治療標靶。 本研究旨在為針對跨物種染色質相互作用作為 EBV 相關實體瘤的變革性治療策略提供全面的臨床前證據。透過闡明 EBV 增強子重編程的分子基礎並驗證 BET 抑制劑的治療潛力，我們力求為高危鼻咽癌病人提供精準醫療方法。

17102526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17102526.value: 口腔潛在惡性疾病的診斷與癌變風險預測：基於大样本多中心真實數據的多模態深度學習模型

17102526.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17102526.value: Prof Fan, Li Jie Dr Shen, Yuehong Prof Zhang, Dan

17102526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17102526.value: Background: Oral squamous cell carcinoma represents the most common head and neck malignancy, frequently arising from a prolonged pre-malignant phase characterized by oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMDs). These disorders exhibit significant clinical heterogeneity and a widely variable risk of malignant transformation (MT), underscoring the critical need for early detection and surveillance. Key Issues: Current OPMDs management faces several challenges: i) considerable variation in reported MT rates due to population and methodological heterogeneity, ii) significant diagnostic difficulty, especially in primary care, due to clinical overlap among OPMDs subtypes, iii) the limitations of existing unimodal and static prediction models that fail to integrate multifaceted data and capture the time-varying nature of cancer risk, and iv) the "black box" nature of many advanced models, which hinders clinical trust and adoption. Objectives: This research project aims to: 1) Establish a large-scale, multi-center cohort to create a standardized evidence base for OPMDs, clarifying MT rates and key determinants; 2) Develop and validate an interpretable, multimodal deep learning framework that simultaneously provides accurate OPMDs subtype classification and time-to-event cancer risk prediction by fusing clinical data with lesion images. Methods: We will recruit a retrospective cohort of patients diagnosed with five major OPMDs from four university-affiliated hospitals. Comprehensive data on demographics, lifestyle, clinical manifestations, histopathology, treatment, and high-resolution clinical photographs will be systematically collected. Our technical approach involves building upon our previously validated SANN and a tailored U-Net/VGG16 architecture integrated via a multimodal fusion layer with an attention mechanism. The model will be trained for multi-class classification and discrete-time survival analysis, and its generalizability will be rigorously assessed through both internal cross-validation and external validation on a held-out dataset. Significance: This project will deliver the clinically deployable, multimodal decision-support tool that bridges OPMDs subtype diagnosis with individualized cancer risk stratification. By incorporating state-of-the-art explainability techniques, it will function as a transparent partner for clinicians, aiding differential diagnosis and enabling personalized, risk-stratified surveillance. The establishment of a large, standardized OPMDs database will serve as a foundational resource for the field, ultimately aiming to improve diagnostic precision, optimize patient management, and enhance outcomes on a global scale. 背景：口腔鱗狀細胞癌（OSCC）是頭頸部最常見的癌症類型。OSCC的發展涉及一個較長的前病理階段，這一階段發生在最初接觸風險因素與癌症發生之間。此階段常伴隨具有較高惡變風險的口腔潛在惡性病變（OPMD）的進展。 關鍵問題：由於缺乏高度特異的臨床和病理特徵，診斷某些OPMD對臨床醫生，特別是非專科醫生而言是一大挑戰。缺乏可靠的風險分層系統來預測癌變風險，使管理變得困難。雖然機器學習已經提升了對惡性轉化風險的評估，但現有模型主要進行二元分類（惡性或非惡性），未考慮時間變化的風險概率，限制了模型提供詳細、時間相關的病變發展趨勢風險評估的能力。此外，現有預測模型通常依賴單一模態，而OPMD作為口腔黏膜病變，受到臨床症狀、外觀形態、患者人口特徵、生活習慣、潛在醫療狀況及組織病理特徵等多方面因素的影響，呈現多維度的複雜性。 目標：1）調查OPMD的癌變發生率，並探討特定患者特徵與癌變風險之間的相關性；2）利用實際數據開發一個深度學習模型，協助臨床醫生有效診斷OPMD並預測癌變風險。 方法：本研究將涵蓋2005年至2025年間在四所大學附屬醫院診斷的六種類型OPMD患者資料。將提取患者的人口統計資料、症狀、生活習慣、檢查結果、治療資訊及病變的視覺特徵。將利用定制的深度學習演算法，建立一個多模態框架，整合多源資料以進行OPMD診斷及癌變風險預測。 意義：此多模態深度學習模型將為專科醫師及一般醫療人員提供一個可靠的工具，以準確診斷OPMD並評估癌變風險。建立一個全面的OPMD資料庫亦將促進全球相關研究。對這些疾病的深入了解將改善OPMD的管理，對患者、臨床醫生及社會整體皆有裨益。

17103326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17103326.value: Yop1p寡聚的冷凍電鏡結構研究及其在內質網管化中的作用

17103326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17103326.value: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is a continuous membrane-bound organelle, morphologically classified into sheets and highly curved tubules. The ER tubules are vital for various biological processes, including lipid synthesis and calcium homeostasis, and their morphology is also suggested to influence ribosome distribution. The tubular architecture is shaped by integral membrane proteins, such as reticulons and Yop1p, which oligomerize into scaffolds that stabilize the high membrane curvature by counteracting the energy barrier associated with membrane bending. Understanding how integral membrane proteins maintain ER tubule morphology is a fundamental biological question. However, a lack of structural data on these proteins and their higher-order assemblies has left the underlying molecular mechanisms elusive. This project aims to elucidate the molecular mechanism of ER tubule shaping by Yop1p, an essential integral membrane protein in ER morphology dynamics, through an integrative structural and cell biology strategy. We will employ single-particle cryo-EM and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) to reveal the structural basis of Yop1p and its high-order assemblies on membrane tubules. These structural insights will guide mutagenesis and in vitro functional studies of membrane tubule formation and stabilization through Yop1p polymerization. Ultimately, by correlating these molecular findings with in vivo analysis of ER morphology via live cell imaging, this project will establish a molecular-level mechanistic understanding of ER tubule shaping. 17103826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17103826.value: Glaucoma, the leading cause of irreversible blindness, affected approximately 80 million individuals worldwide in 2020, with numbers expected to rise due to an aging population. Ocular hypertension (OHT) represents an early stage in the glaucoma continuum, characterized by accelerated retinal ganglion cell axon loss without detectable retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) damage. While lowering intraocular pressure (IOP) can reduce the risk of developing glaucoma in OHT patients, there is no consensus on when to initiate treatment, as 90% of untreated patients may not develop glaucoma within five years, raising concerns about unnecessary treatment burden, costs, and potential adverse effects in low-risk individuals. The Ocular Hypertension Treatment Study (OHTS) and European Glaucoma Prevention Study (EGPS) 5-year glaucoma conversion risk calculation provide the only validated approach to guide treatment decisions. However, risk calculations derived from the OHTS-EGPS model are imprecise, creating a critical need for more reliable biomarkers to guide clinical management. We recently devised ROTA, an algorithm that integrates retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness and reflectance data from optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans to reveal axonal fiber bundle trajectories across a wide field, identifying RNFL defects often missed by clinical examination and conventional OCT thickness analysis. These ROTA-detected RNFL defects likely represent the earliest discernible signs of glaucomatous damage, providing a potential biomarker for targeted treatment decisions. We propose a 5-year prospective, multicenter, randomized clinical trial to investigate the impact of ROTA in managing OHT. A total of 418 OHT patients will be randomly assigned to two management strategies: IOP-lowering treatment initiated upon detecting RNFL defects on ROTA (Strategy I), or when the 5-year OHTS-EGPS glaucoma conversion risk exceeds 15% (Strategy II). Patients will undergo clinical examination, RNFL imaging, and visual field (VF) testing every 4 months for 60 months. The primary objective is to compare time to IOP-lowering treatment initiation between strategies. Secondary objectives include comparing the rates of change in VF mean deviation (MD) using a non-inferiority design and time to VF defect development between strategies. We hypothesize that Strategy I will demonstrate delayed treatment initiation while maintaining non-inferior visual function compared to Strategy II, thereby identifying patients who truly require treatment while safely deferring therapy in those at lower risk. 17104226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17104226.value: Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) induces varying degrees of disease severity in young and adult individuals, predominantly affecting young individuals due to their unique physiological characteristics. Our preliminary data examining histological cell arrangement and biological marker expressions have confirmed that our 2D multi-layer nasal organoid model accurately replicates the essential features and mucociliary clearance (MCC) functions of the human nasopharynx, exhibiting age-dependent variations. Our proposal aims to fully characterize the effects of MCC and structural organization in young-aged- and adult-derived nasal organoids on enterovirus infectivity. Preliminary data indicate that EV-D68 targeted specific cell types, which we will explore further to understand their impacts across different age groups. Despite the significant role of enterovirus in causing respiratory diseases, the specific biological pathways disrupted by the virus in the upper respiratory tract remain largely unknown. Therefore, we propose to study the molecular changes induced directly and indirectly by enterovirus using our human nasal organoids. Additionally, the structured and MCC-equipped nasal organoids offer a novel platform to evaluate the effectiveness of anti-enterovirus drugs in a physiologically relevant context. We plan to assess the efficacy of known anti-enterovirus drugs, determining the optimal half maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) values under conditions that closely mimic human physiology. 17104926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17104926.value: 變動的營養景觀：草食動物生態位變異作為養分通量的驅動因子

17104926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17104926.value: Coral reefs, arguably the most biodiverse of all marine ecosystems, are dying at an alarming rate. Globally, nearly 50% of coral cover has been lost over the past five decades due to anthropogenic pressures. Conversely, algae have proliferated, replacing corals that they outcompete for space, a process exacerbated by the overfishing of herbivorous fish that would otherwise control algal growth. Herbivorous fish, by grazing on harmful algae and by facilitating the recycling of nutrients within these ecosystems, are the cornerstone of coral reef maintenance and resilience. Their importance is such that some countries have implemented national bans on herbivore fishing. Despite their recognized roles, how individual species within diverse herbivorous communities contribute to coral reef resilience remains surprisingly unknown. While for many years, herbivorous fish within broad functional groups were considered to have largely overlapping and “static” diets (or trophic niches), recent detailed feeding observations, some of our own, suggest that every species may in fact eat different macroalgal species, forage in distinct microhabitats and adjust what and where they eat based on available resources. The implications are far-reaching because it means that every species may contribute uniquely to maintaining reef health, and that the loss of even a single species could have cascading effects on ecosystem resilience. We propose to leverage traditional and cutting-edge approaches - morphological and molecular gut content analysis (what fish ingest), compound-specific stable isotope analysis of essential amino acids (what fish assimilate), and feeding observations (where fish eat) - and the gradient of environmental conditions in Hong Kong’s coral reefs to ask (1) how the trophic niche of co-occurring herbivorous species differ in their breadth and overlap, (2) how these differences manifest across gradients of habitat condition and resource availability, and (3) how changing diets influence the contribution of herbivorous fish species to the recycling and redistribution of nutrients across reefs. The complementary datasets will be used to compute multi-dimensional niche hypervolumes that correspond to the “ecological space” occupied by each species at each site. The maintenance of coral reefs, an ecosystem upon which many coastal communities depend for livelihood, is inextricably linked to the diverse functional roles of herbivorous fish that have so far been completely overlooked. Our results on the nuanced and context-dependent roles of individual herbivore species will transform how conservation and management strategies are developed and implemented to bolster reef resilience and ecosystem services. 珊瑚礁，可能是海洋中生物多樣性最高的生態環境，正在以驚人的速度消亡。在過去五十多年間，全球有將近一半的珊瑚礁因人類壓力而消失。然而藻類卻大量繁殖，取代了在生存空間戰中落敗的珊瑚。草食性魚類本可控制藻類的繁殖，但由於過度捕撈，使藻類替代珊瑚的情況更加惡化。草食性魚類透過啃食有害藻類並促進這些生態系統內養分的循環再利用，成為維持珊瑚礁生態系統穩定及保持其復原力的基石。因此，有些國家已在全國範圍内禁止捕撈草食性魚類。雖然草食性魚類的重要性已得到認可，令人驚訝的是，在物種豐富的草食性魚類中，我們尚未清楚每個物種是如何影響珊瑚礁復原力。儘管多年以來，同屬廣義功能群的草食性魚類一直被認為擁有大幅重疊且「靜態」的食性（即營養生態位），根據近期他人及我們詳盡的攝食觀察，我們推測每個物種實際上有其的獨特微生境並取食與其他物種不同的大型藻類。其覓食地與食物也會根據可獲取的資源有所調整。這觀察可能具有深遠的影響，因爲其説明了每種草食性魚類對維持珊瑚礁的健康或許有其獨特的功能，即便僅僅失去一個物種，也有可能對生態復原力產生連鎖效應。結合香港珊瑚礁環境條件的梯度，我們計劃探討1. 共存草食性魚類間營養生態位在廣度與重疊程度上的差異；2. 此差異在棲地條件與資源可獲性的梯度差異上如何呈現；以及3. 食性的改變如何影響草食性魚類物種循環利用與重新分配珊瑚礁間的養分。我們計劃結合傳統與尖端方法來分析魚類攝入的食物、其吸收的營養物質以及其攝食地。具體方法包括形態學、魚類腸道內容物分子成分分析、化合物特異性氨基酸穩定同位素分析，以及攝食觀察。這些互補的數據將用于計算對應於每一物種在每一地點所佔據的「生態空間」的多維度的生態位超體積。珊瑚礁是眾多沿海社區賴以維生的生態系統，其維繫與草食性魚類迄今完全被忽視的多樣化功能角色密不可分。我們關於草食性魚類具體物種所扮演的細微且因情境而異之角色的研究成果，將徹底改變保育與管理策略的制定與實施，從而強化珊瑚礁的復原力與生態系統服務。

17105126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17105126.value: 醫生魚互動行為的網絡神經機制與細胞構成

17105126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17105126.value: Interactions between species are central to shaping community dynamics and ecosystem functions, with facilitative and mutualistic relationships playing pivotal roles in ecosystem productivity. Despite extensive ecological insights into these behaviours, their underlying neurological, neuromolecular, and cellular mechanisms remain largely unexplored due to the complexity of linking behaviour with specific brain processes within contexts. The cleaner wrasse (Labroides dimidiatus) serves as an ideal model for investigating these mechanisms, given its intricate interspecific cleaning behaviour, social decision-making, and demonstrated cognitive capabilities such as self-recognition. This study aims to elucidate the neural substrates underpinning species interactions by integrating neuroanatomical, sensory, and molecular approaches. We will localize brain regions involved in interaction behaviours through immunohistochemistry, focusing on neural activation patterns in the forebrain during cleaner-client interactions. Additionally, we will identify sensory perception pathways—vision, olfaction, touch, and taste—that facilitate recognition and decision-making, leveraging genomic data indicating evolved sensory gene signatures. Finally, employing single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), we will characterize the cellular landscape and cell-type-specific gene expression profiles associated with social interactions. Through this innovative and comprehensive approachwe will provide critical insights into the cellular and molecular basis of complex ecological interactions shedding light on the intricate relationships between brain, behaviour, and the natural world. 物種間的互動對於塑造群落動態與生態系統功能至關重要，其中促進性與互利性關係在生態系統生產力中扮演著關鍵角色。儘管針對這些行為已有廣泛的生態學見解，但由於將行為與特定情境下的腦部過程建立關聯極為複雜，其背後的神經學、神經分子及細胞機制仍大多未被探索。清潔鯛（Labroides dimidiatus）憑藉其複雜的異種間清潔行為、社會決策能力，以及已證實的認知能力（如自我辨識），成為探究這些機制的理想模型。本研究旨在透過整合神經解剖學、感官及分子方法，闡明支撐物種互動的神經基礎。我們將透過免疫組織化學技術定位參與互動行為的大腦區域，並著重於清潔魚與受潔魚互動期間前腦的神經活化模式。此外，我們將利用顯示感官基因演化特徵的基因組數據，闡明促進識別與決策的感官知覺路徑——包括視覺、嗅覺、觸覺及味覺。最後，透過單細胞 RNA 定序（scRNA-seq），我們將闡明與社會互動相關的細胞景觀及細胞類型特異性基因表達模式。透過這種創新且全面的方法，我們將針對複雜生態互動的細胞與分子基礎提供關鍵見解，從而闡明大腦、行為與自然世界之間的錯綜複雜關係。

17105226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17105226.value: 研究T細胞免疫記憶對冠狀病毒突變動態的影響

17105226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17105226.value: Coronaviruses, such as SARS-CoV-2 that is responsible for the COVID-19 pandemic, continue to circulate and cause illness worldwide. Most people now have immunity to the original virus, either through vaccination or previous infection. However, SARS-CoV-2 has changed over time, including some evading the immune system’s memory, partially shaped by antibodies. T cells, another part of our immune system, help clear infected cells and often targets regions of the virus that are less likely to mutate. Therefore, T cells may offer broader protection against different coronavirus strains, including SARS-CoV-2 and those that cause seasonal infections. Although some viral mutations that escape T cell recognition have been reported, it remains unclear how T cell immune memory influences which viral mutations arise, especially in people whose antibody responses are impaired, such as those with blood cancers. Currently, various COVID-19 vaccines are available, with some focus only on the spike protein, while others include additional viral proteins. It is unknown whether vaccines that target more diverse viral proteins create broader T cell memory, resulting in lower chance of viral mutations that evade T cell recognition. This study addresses this gap by assessing whether vaccines that include both spike and other viral proteins can generate broader T cell responses and limit the emergence of mutations in the spike protein. In Project Module 1, we will combine and analyse publicly available SARS-CoV-2 sequences along with vaccination history, to identify mutations associated with different vaccine types. T cell responses to these mutated regions will be further assessed. In Project Module 2, we will vaccinate mice that are unable to produce antibodies with spike protein alone or with additional viral proteins. After vaccination, the mice will be infected with SARS-CoV-2 or a related seasonal coronavirus. Viral sequences from the infected mice will be analysed to identify mutations distinct to each vaccine type. In Project Module 3, both normal mice and mice unable to produce antibodies will be vaccinated the same way as described above. We will then assess their T cell responses to the identified mutations and examine the breadth of their T cell populations. Overall, findings from the proposed study will provide valuable insights into how T cell immunity shape coronavirus evolution and inform vaccine design, especially for individuals with impaired antibody responses. Ultimately, this work will guide healthcare professionals and policymakers in improving vaccine strategies for those at higher risk from viral infections. 冠狀病毒，如導致新冠大流行的新冠病毒，仍在全球持續傳播並引發疾病。大多數人現在已透過疫苗接種或先前感染對原始病毒具有免疫力。然而，新冠病毒已隨著時間變化，包括一些可逃脫免疫系統記憶的變化，而這些變化部分受到抗體的塑造。T細胞是我們免疫系統的另一個組成部分，有助於清除被感染的細胞，並且通常針對病毒中較不容易突變的區域。因此，T細胞可能針對不同冠狀病毒毒株提供更廣泛的保護，包括新冠病毒和引起季節性感染的冠狀病毒。雖然一些可逃脫T細胞辨識的病毒突變已被報導，但T細胞免疫記憶如何影響病毒突變的產生仍不清楚，尤其是在抗體反應受損的人群中，例如血液癌症患者。 目前，已有多種新冠疫苗可供使用，其中一些僅聚焦於刺突蛋白，而另一些則包含額外的病毒蛋白。現在尚不清楚，針對更多樣病毒蛋白的疫苗是否能夠建立更廣泛的T細胞記憶，從而降低病毒產生逃脫T細胞識別突變的可能性。 本研究旨在填補這一空白，評估同時包含刺突蛋白及其他病毒蛋白的疫苗是否能夠產生更廣泛的T細胞反應並限制刺突蛋白中突變的出現。 在項目模組1中，我們將整合並分析公開可取得的新冠病毒序列及其對應的疫苗接種史，以鑑定與不同疫苗類型相關的突變。隨後，我們將進一步評估針對這些突變區域的T細胞反應。在項目模組2中，我們將為無法產生抗體的小鼠接種僅含刺突蛋白的疫苗或接種同時包含額外病毒蛋白的疫苗。接種後，這些小鼠將被感染新冠病毒或相關的季節性冠狀病毒。我們將分析感染小鼠體內的病毒序列以辨識各疫苗所特有的突變。在項目模組3中，我們將依照上述相同方式對正常小鼠及無法產生抗體的小鼠進行免疫。隨後，我們將評估其針對所辨識突變的T細胞應答，並考察其T細胞群體的廣度。 總體而言，本研究的預期發現將為理解T細胞免疫如何塑造冠狀病毒突變提供重要見解並為疫苗設計提供依據，尤其是對於抗體應答受損的個體。最終，這項工作將為醫療專業人員和政策制定者改善病毒感染風險更高人群的疫苗策略提供指導。

17105326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17105326.value: 應用於種植牙規劃的多模態人工智能輔助決策系統：整合硬組織與軟組織評估

17105326.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17105326.value: Prof Nalley, Andrew Kyle Dr Zhou, You

17105326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17105326.value: Dental implants have become among the most reliable treatments for replacing missing teeth lost due to trauma, disease or age-related conditions. Their long-term success, however, depends critically on accurate presurgical planning. This requires careful and thorough evaluation of both hard tissues, such as bone volume, mandibular canals, and maxillary sinuses, and soft tissues, including gum (gingival) thickness and overall characteristics (phenotype). Current clinical workflows rely heavily on dentists’ manual expertise, which is time-consuming, prone to variability, and often neglects systematic soft tissue assessment. These limitations increase the risk of complications, including implant failure, nerve damage and compromised aesthetics, highlighting the need for more precise and efficient planning solutions. This project addresses this gap by developing a multimodal AI-assisted clinical decision support system that integrates cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and intraoral scanning (IOS). CBCT provides three-dimensional visualization of bone and anatomical structures, whereas IOS captures fine details of the crowns and gingiva. By combining both modalities, our system automatically will consider both hard and soft tissues, and automatically distinguish and label (segment) teeth, jawbones, nerves, and gingiva; quantify the gingival thickness; and generate prosthetic-driven, personalized implant plans. A unique open-source dataset of registered CBCT–IOS images will be created to train and validate advanced deep learning models. Automated segmentation, registration, and planning, including the precise determination of implant sites in three-dimensional space (position, orientation, and depth), will be systematically benchmarked against expert-designed plans using multicentre datasets. Preliminary evidence indicates that the system can achieve high accuracy in CBCT segmentation while reducing time and variability. Importantly, by incorporating CBCT and IOS segmentation results and gingival phenotype analysis, the framework introduces a novel dimension of risk assessment and aesthetic predictability, moving beyond bone-centred planning towards a more comprehensive and patient-centred approach. No open datasets pairing the two modalities currently exist. The project will yield several impactful outcomes. First, it provides new knowledge on how multimodal imaging and AI can be integrated to address long-standing challenges in digital dentistry. Second, it will provide a high-quality open dataset that enables reproducibility and fosters global innovation in AI-driven implantology. Finally, it will support clinical translation by reducing dentists’ workload, improving patient understanding through visualized planning, and enhancing surgical safety and both functional and aesthetic outcomes. By advancing both science and clinical practice, this work has the potential to transform digital implant workflows and set a new standard for precision oral health care. 種植牙已成為修復缺牙最可靠的方式之一，適用於因外傷、疾病或年齡相關狀況而引起的缺牙情況。然而，其長期成功率高度依賴於術前規劃的精準性。此規劃需對硬組織（如骨量、下頜神經管及上頜竇）和軟組織（包括牙齦厚度及整體表型）進行細緻且全面的評估。現行臨床工作流程多仰賴牙醫的手動專業技能，不僅耗時、易產生變異，且常忽略系統性的軟組織評估。這些局限增加了併發症風險，包括種植體失敗、神經損傷及美學效果不佳，凸顯出對更精確、高效規劃方案的迫切需求。 本項目為填補此缺口，開發一套整合錐狀射束電腦斷層掃描（CBCT）與口內掃描（IOS）的多模態人工智能輔助臨床決策支持系統。CBCT可呈現骨骼及解剖結構的三維影像，而IOS則能捕捉牙冠與牙齦的精細細節。透過結合這兩種模態，本系統將自動整合硬、軟組織信息；自動區分並標記（分割）牙齒、頜骨、神經及牙齦；量化牙齦厚度；並生成以修復為導向的個性化種植方案。我們將建立一個獨特的開源數據庫，內含已配準的CBCT–IOS影像，用於訓練和驗證先進的深度學習模型。我們亦會利用多中心數據庫，將本系統的自動分割、配準及規劃（包括在三維空間中精確確定種植體的位置、方向和深度），與專家設計的方案進行系統性基準比較。 初步證據顯示，本系統在CBCT分割上可達到高準確度，同時縮短時間並減少變異性。更重要的是，通過納入CBCT與IOS分割結果及牙齦表型分析，本框架引入了風險評估與美學可預測性的新角度，將規劃重點從以骨為中心的傳統模式，推進至更全面且以患者為中心的模式。目前尚沒有配對這兩種模態的公開數據庫。 本項目將取得多項重大成果。首先，它將貢獻關於整合多模態影像與人工智能的新知識，以應對數字化牙科的長期挑戰；其次，它可提供高質量的開源數據庫，以支持可重複性，並推動全球種植領域在人工智能驅動下的創新；最後，它將在不同方面支持臨床轉化，包括：減輕牙醫工作負擔，以視覺化規劃幫助患者理解，提升手術安全性，以及改善種植牙功能及美學。通過推動科學進展與臨床實踐，此項工作有望優化數字化種植工作流程，並為精準口腔健康照護建立新標準。

17105826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17105826.value: 多中心國際心臟磁振造影4D血流、心房大小及心房應變，評估射血分數保留型心臟衰竭之研究

17105826.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17105826.value: Prof Lee, Alex Pui-wai Dr Leung, Chun Yu Dr Montero Barril, David Prof Nadig, Vidya Dr Patel, Hena Prof Wong, Chun Ka Dr Yun, Chun-Ho

17105826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17105826.value: Heart failure (HF) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in Hong Kong and worldwide (ie. ~20,000 discharges or deaths in Hong Kong during a 1-year period from 2015-2016; 1-2% prevalence worldwide). Briefly, HF is separated, based on the left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), into HF with reduced ejection fraction, heart failure with mildly impaired ejection fraction and HF with preserved ejection (HFpEF). HFpEF comprises about 50% of HF patients and remains difficult to diagnose. Echocardiography is the first line non-invasive imaging modality and current standard to assess suspected HFpEF patients. However, echocardiography has well known limitations and our previous work shows that ~50% of suspected HFpEF patients after NT-proBNP and echocardiography assessment were indeterminate for HFpEF. In addition, other diagnoses were identified such as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy during CMR examination. Currently, CMR is not part of the diagnostic work-up to diagnose HFpEF. It is only at best used for identifying underlying aetiology if other aetiologies like hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or cardiac amyloidosis are suspected. Based on previous studies conducted by our group there are several CMR parameters which are most promising for diagnosing HFpEF. However, as these were single centre studies, a larger study comprising of patients from different international locations and demographics is required to confirm these results in a wider population. In our previous studies, left atrial reservoir strain, left atrial volume index, 4D direct flow and 4D residual volume showed good to very good area under the curve results for diagnosing HFpEF of 0.804, 0.776, 0.781 and 0.740. We propose to undertake an international multicentre prospective case-control study comprising 6 hospitals recruiting suspected HFpEF patients to determine: 1. The diagnostic accuracy of CMR derived 4D direct flow, 4D residual volume, left atrial strain and/ or left atrial volume indexed to diagnose HFpEF. 2. What proportion of patients referred for CMR assessment of suspected HFpEF, have alternative diagnoses? By undertaking a multicentre international study case-control design, we hope to establish CMR parameters that can be used in international guidelines for diagnosing HFpEF. 心臟衰竭（HF）是香港及全球範圍內發病及死亡的主要原因之一（例如，在2015至2016年的一年期間，香港約有20,000宗出院或死亡個案；全球患病率約為1–2%）。 簡而言之，心臟衰竭根據左心室射血分數（LVEF）分為射血分數降低型心臟衰竭、射血分數輕度受損型心臟衰竭及射血分數保留型心臟衰竭（HFpEF）。HFpEF約佔心臟衰竭患者的50%，且至今仍難以診斷。超聲心動圖是第一線非侵入性影像檢查方式，亦是當前評估疑似HFpEF患者的標準工具。然而，超聲心動圖存在眾所周知的局限性，我們先前的研究顯示，約有50%的疑似HFpEF患者在接受NT-proBNP及超聲心動圖評估後，仍無法確診HFpEF。此外，在心臟磁振造影（CMR）檢查中亦發現其他診斷，例如肥厚型心肌病變。目前，CMR尚未納入HFpEF的診斷流程；充其量僅在用於懷疑其他病因（如肥厚型心肌病變或心臟類澱粉沉積症）時，用來鑑別潛在病因。 根據我們團隊先前進行的研究，有數項CMR參數極具診斷HFpEF的潛力。然而，由於這些均屬單中心研究，仍需進行一項納入不同國際地區及人口學特徵患者的大型研究，以在更廣泛的族群中驗證這些結果。在我們先前的研究中，左心房儲存應變、左心房體積指數、4D直接血流及4D殘餘容積在診斷HFpEF方面均顯示出良好至非常良好的曲線下面積（AUC）結果，分別為0.804、0.776、0.781及0.740。 我們擬進行一項國際多中心前瞻性病例對照研究，納入6家醫院，招募疑似HFpEF患者，旨在確定： 1. CMR衍生之4D直接血流、4D殘餘容積、左心房應變及／或左心房體積指數在診斷HFpEF方面的診斷準確性； 2. 轉介接受CMR評估的疑似HFpEF患者中，有多少比例存在其他替代診斷？ 透過進行此項多中心國際病例對照研究，我們期望建立可用於國際指引中診斷HFpEF的CMR參數。

17106626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17106626.value: 協調腸神經系統與腸道發育的訊號傳導動態

17106626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17106626.value: Bowel innervation is essential for establishing functional gastrointestinal activity. Disruptions in the enteric nervous system (ENS) can lead to various bowel disorders, including diarrhea and constipation, affecting individuals across different age groups. Severe conditions, such as Hirschsprung disease (HSCR), pose life-threatening risks if untreated. HSCR results from the absence of neurons in the distal colon, often accompanied by muscular defects. Therapeutic strategies involving the transplantation of ENS progenitor cells to regenerate functional ganglia hold promise for ENS repair. Nonetheless, the effect of such interventions on the muscle layer's recovery remains uncertain, potentially limiting overall treatment efficacy. Therefore, a comprehensive understanding of the molecular mechanisms governing interactions between the ENS and the muscle layer for the formation of functional bowel is crucial for advancing therapeutic approaches. Through a genome-wide genetic screen of HSCR patients, we identified seven loss-of-function mutations in the Vinculin (VCL) gene. Mice with conditional deletion of Vcl (Vcl cKO) in ENS exhibited hypoganglionosis accompanied by muscular defects, resembling HSCR phenotypes. Subsequent spatial transcriptomic analysis revealed impaired interactions between the ENS and mesenchyme (MES), with pleiotrophin (Ptn) and Ncam1 showing the most significant disruptions. Ptn-null mice also displayed both ENS and muscular defects, albeit less severe than Vcl cKO mice, indicating the involvement of additional factors mediating ENS and muscle layer development. All of these observations demonstrate that signal cross-talk between the ENS and MES cells is critical for the proper development of the bowel's muscle layers. We hypothesize that factors mediating ENS-MES interactions are essential for muscle layer formation and may serve as potential therapeutic targets to improve bowel function following cell-based therapies. To test this hypothesis, we aim to (1) elucidate the mechanisms by which ENS directs muscle layer development in mice; (2) investigate the roles of the Ptn pathway in ENS and muscle layer formation to assess its therapeutic potential; and (3) characterize the signaling dynamics between ENS and MES during gut development using multiomic approaches, with the goal of identifying novel pathways that promote muscle layer recovery. Defining the key regulatory pathways underlying the ENS-MES interactions will deepen our understanding of bowel development and aid in the discovery of new pharmacological strategies to enhance functional recovery after cell therapy. 腸道神經支配對於建立功能性胃腸道活動至關重要。腸神經系統（ENS）的異常可能導致多種腸道疾病（包括腹瀉和便秘），影響各年齡層。嚴重病症（如先天性巨結腸症，HSCR）若不及時治療，可危及生命。 HSCR 是由遠端結腸神經元缺失引起的，常伴隨肌肉層缺陷。利用 ENS 祖細胞移植再生功能性神經節的治療策略，為 ENS 修復帶來了希望。然而，此類幹預措施對肌肉層恢復的影響尚不明確，這可能限制了整體治療效果。因此，全面了解調控 ENS 與肌肉層之間相互作用以形成功能性腸道的分子機制，對於推動治療方法的進步至關重要。 透過對 HSCR 患者進行全基因組遺傳篩選，我們鑑定出了 Vinculin (VCL) 基因的七種功能缺失突變。在 ENS 中條件性敲除 Vcl (Vcl cKO) 的小鼠表現出神經節減少症（hypoganglionosis）並伴有肌肉層缺陷，其表型與 HSCR 相似。隨後的空間轉錄組分析顯示，ENS 與間質（MES）之間的相互作用受損，其中多效生長因子（Ptn）和 Ncam1 的變化最為顯著。 Ptn 缺失小鼠也表現出 ENS 和肌肉層缺陷，儘管嚴重程度低於 Vcl cKO 小鼠，但這表明還有其他因素參與介導 ENS 與肌肉層的發育。上述所有觀察結果均表明，ENS 與 MES 細胞之間的訊號交互作用對於腸道肌肉層的正常發育至關重要。我們推測，介導 ENS-MES 相互作用的因子對於肌肉層形成必不可少，並可能作為潛在的治療靶點，以改善基於細胞療法後的腸道功能。為驗證此假說，我們旨在：(1) 闡明小鼠體內 ENS 引導肌肉層發育的機制；(2) 探究 Ptn 通路在 ENS 和肌肉層形成中的作用，以評估其治療潛力；以及 (3) 利用多組學方法表徵腸道發育過程中 ENS 與 MES 之間的信號傳導動態，從而鑑定出肌肉層恢復的新通路。明確介導 ENS（腸神經系統）與 MES（間質）相互作用的關鍵調控通路，將加深我們對腸道發育的理解，並有助於發現新的藥理策略，以促進細胞治療後的功能恢復。

17106826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17106826.value: 基於新型疾病模型探究新興人畜共通病原體——大鼠戊型肝炎病毒

17106826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17106826.value: Rocahepevirus ratti genotype 1 (rHEV), also known as rat hepatitis E virus, is a ubiquitous pathogen of street rats globally. Rats frequently shed rHEV; approximately 10% of street rats are actively infected at any time. Therefore, there is a vast reservoir of rHEV in rodents, which have a close commensal relationship with humans. In 2018, we reported for the first time that rHEV can infect humans. Cases have since been described in mainland China, Thailand, Spain, France, Germany, and Canada - fostering recognition that rHEV is a sporadic but geographically widespread zoonosis. Although rat hepatitis E infection is generally milder than conventional hepatitis E virus (HEV) infection, solid organ transplant recipients (SOTRs) appear uniquely susceptible and frequently develop chronic infections. Besides discovering that rHEV is a human pathogen and describing the clinical and epidemiological features of this zoonosis, we have also established infection models of rHEV using wildtype strains isolated from rats and humans. In vitro, we have developed a robust primary rat hepatocyte infection model to complement established human hepatocyte models. We have also developed an experimental rat model of rHEV infection. In this project, we will build on pilot data from these models to explore host immune responses to rHEV infection with an aim of addressing pressing questions regarding rat enzootics and human infections. Specifically, we will a) assess how rat livers respond to rHEV infections at the cellular and tissue level and the kinetics of immune responses following infection and b) compare innate immune transcriptomic responses of human hepatocytes to rHEV infection in comparison to conventional HEV infection under various conditions of immunosuppression. These experiments will provide insight into a) how rHEV enzootics are sustained in rodent populations (e.g. weak immune responses may foster high virus load infections and susceptibility to reinfections enabling spread) and b) why rHEV infections are clinically distinct to conventional HEV infections in having a milder hepatitis phenotype and predilection for SOTRs (e.g. weaker innate immune activation, direct potentiation of infection with calcineurin inhibitors). Addressing these will give us vital knowledge of rHEV infections in the natural host and potentially inform rodent surveillance and disinfestation strategies. The insights into pathogenesis of rHEV will provide a mechanistic framework to the clinical and epidemiological significance of this emerging zoonotic threat and inform immunosuppression management strategies in infected SOTRs. 大鼠戊型肝炎病毒（rHEV，基因1型）是全球城市野鼠中普遍存在的病原體。野鼠排毒現象十分常見，日常感染率約為10%。由於齧齒動物與人類生活環境高度重疊，這構成了一個巨大的rHEV潛在傳播風險庫。2018年，本團隊首次證實rHEV可感染人類。此後，中國大陸、泰國、西班牙、法國、德國及加拿大等地相繼有病例報導，使人們逐漸認識到rHEV是一種散發性但地理分佈廣泛的人畜共通傳染病。儘管rHEV感染通常較傳統戊型肝炎病毒（HEV）感染症狀輕微，但實體器官移植受者（SOTR）對此病毒高度易感，且易發展為慢性感染。除發現rHEV的人類致病性並描述其臨床與流行病學特徵外，我們還利用從大鼠和患者體內分離的野生型毒株，建立了rHEV感染模型：在體外，我們構建了穩定的原代大鼠肝細胞感染模型，以補充現有的人肝細胞模型；同時，我們還建立了實驗大鼠rHEV感染模型。本計畫將在這些模型的初步數據基礎上，深入探究宿主對rHEV感染的免疫應答，旨在解決大鼠地方性流行和人類感染中的關鍵問題。具體內容包括：a）在細胞和組織層面上評估大鼠肝臟對rHEV感染的應答特徵，並明確感染後免疫應答的時相變化；b）在不同免疫抑制條件下，比較人肝細胞感染rHEV與傳統HEV後的先天免疫轉錄組學應答差異。本研究將有助於闡明：a）rHEV如何在齧齒動物種群中持續維持地方性流行（例如，弱免疫應答可能導致高病毒量感染和再感染易感性，從而促進病毒擴散）；b）為何rHEV感染在臨床上有別於傳統HEV感染——肝炎表型較輕，但對SOTR有特殊傾向性（例如，先天免疫激活較弱，或鈣調神經磷酸酶抑制劑直接增強病毒感染）。回答這些問題將為我們理解rHEV在自然宿主中的感染規律提供重要理論依據，並有望為齧齒動物監測和滅鼠策略提供參考。同時，關於rHEV致病機制的深入認識，將為這一新興人畜共通威脅的臨床和流行病學意義提供機制層面的解釋，並為SOTR感染者的免疫抑制管理策略提供指導。

17106926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17106926.value: 小型隔離種群能否避免滅絕？

17106926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17106926.value: Human induced habitat destruction and fragmentation has caused dramatic population size declines of many organisms around the world. The distribution ranges of many species have become severely fragmented leading to reduced gene flow and isolation among the remaining subpopulations. One unfortunate and detrimental consequence of this isolation is the reduction in effective size of subpopulations. Small effective population size entails increased strength of genetic drift, reduced efficiency of selection against deleterious genetic variants, as well as increased likelihood of inbreeding and loss of fitness due to inbreeding depression. All these negative genetic consequences of isolation will increase the extinction/extirpation risk of local populations, as well as compromise their ability to adapt to changing environmental conditions. However, by purging the loads of deletrious mutations, some unknown fraction of populations may avoid extripation risk, but how frequently this will occur is not known as quantitative data on mutation loads from large number of small wild population isolates is lacking. We have recently demonstrated that the Hong Kong populations of the flat-headed loach (Oreonectes platycephalus) have extremely small effective population sizes, show low degree of genetic diversity and an extreme degree of population subdivision not seen in any comparable study of freshwater fishes. These findings suggest that the loach system can serve as a well replicated model system to study consequences of small effective population size and the prospect of genetic restoration of fitness through purging of mutation loads. We propose to quantify the loads of realised and potential deleterious mutations in a large number of small loach populations to see how often and to what extent purging has occured. We will further test experimentally if the reduction of these loads (by crossing individuals from different populations) leads to restoration of their fitness (i.e. to genetic rescue), alternative, outbreeding depression. To enable this research, we will first assemble a high quality telomere-to-telomere reference genome of the flat-headed loach which will be the foundation for accurate characterisation of deleterious mutation loads from a large number of replicate populations. The main novelty of this study would be a quantitative estimate how frequently small populations have or have not managed purge their loads of deletrious mutations, and how this relates to their levels of inbreeding and effective populations size. 人類活動引致棲地破壞與破碎化，已在全球造成眾多生物種群數量的顯著下降。許多物種的地理分布已高度碎片化，導致基因流動受限及加劇殘存種群之間的隔離。種群隔離會引致物種的有效群體大小（effective population size）下降的嚴重後果。較小的有效群體數量會增強基因漂變，降低自然選擇清除有害遺傳變異的效率，並提高近親繁殖的機率，從而引發近交衰退（inbreeding depression）及適應度降低。上述因隔離引致的負面遺傳效應，將進一步提高本地種群滅絕（extinction/extirpation）的風險，並削弱其適應環境變化的能力。 透過清除（purging）有害的突變負荷，部分種群或有可能降低滅絕風險。然而，由於目前缺乏針對大量小型野生隔離種群之突變負荷的量化資料，因此此現象發生的頻率仍未明。我們近期的研究顯示，香港平頭嶺鰍（Oreonectes platycephalus）具有極小的有效群體數量、低遺傳多樣性，以及在淡水魚類相關研究中罕見的高度種群分化。上述發現表明，該物種能作為一個可複製的模型系統，用以探討小型有效群體的遺傳效應，以及如何透過清除突變負荷以恢復適應度。 本研究擬針對多個小型嶺鰍群體，量化其已表現（realised）及潛在（potential）的有害突變負荷，以評估清除發生的頻率及程度。此外，我們將透過實驗測試降低突變負荷（例如不同群體間個體交配）是否能促進適應度恢復（即基因救援，genetic rescue），或相反導致遠交衰退（outbreeding depression）。為支援上述研究，我們將首先構建平頭嶺鰍之高品質端粒至端粒（telomere-to-telomere）參考基因組，以作為準確分析多個群體中有害突變負荷的基礎。本研究創新之處，在於量化評估小型群體能否以及多大程度成功清除有害突變負荷，並闡明其與近親繁殖程度及有效群體大小之間的關聯。

17107426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17107426.value: 闡明全著絲粒調控與可塑性的表觀遺傳機制

17107426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17107426.value: The centromere serves as an essential element on all chromosomes to ensure equal chromosome segregation and genome stability. Despite centromeres’ conserved functions, the DNA sequence and size of centromeres differ widely among organisms, and centromeres are primarily governed by epigenetics. Among the diverse types of centromeres, holocentromeres, diffused along the entire length of chromosomes, are observed in over 350,000 species, including nematodes, some insects and plants, and have evolved over 13 times. Holocentric chromosomes are potentially more resistant to DNA damages, as broken chromosomal fragments retain functional centromeres. The ability to form de novo holocentromeres on artificial chromosomes containing exogenous sequences in the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans indicate that holocentromeres possess remarkable plasticity, adaptable to various DNA sequences, developmental stages and environmental conditions. Nonetheless, the intricate mechanisms for regulating holocentromere locations remain unclear. We previously identified the genome-wide permissive locations for CENP-A, the epigenetic mark of centromere, in C. elegans embryo population through chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by DNA sequencing (chIP-seq). CENP-A is permissive to bind to ~35% of the genome; however, the locations are neither random nor enriched in repetitive sequences. The locations of CENP-A display a positive correlation with histone H3K27me3 and a negative correlation with gene transcription. Live-cell imaging analyses reveal that AuroraB/AIR-2 kinase, Argonaute CSR-1 and maternal germline gene transcription can negatively influence embryonic CENP-A binding. Yet, the impact of these factors on CENP-A genomic locations remains unknown. We propose that only a subset of these CENP-A-permissive sites are utilized as the holocentromere in individual cells, wherein the specific sites used exhibit plasticity, provided that the size, density and interval of CENP-A domains are maintained. Alterations in these parameters could cause malfunctioning of holocentromeres. To elucidate the impacts of epigenetic pathways, parental origins, multiple generations and developmental stages on CENP-A locations, and to examine individual heterogeneity of CENP-A patterns, we will apply low-input methodologies (CUT&Tag and DamID) to determine CENP-A genomic locations. Next, we will utilize single-molecule long-read sequencing methods (Nanopore-DamID and DiMeLo-seq) to map CENP-A locations and density on individual chromosomes. Furthermore, we will investigate the spatial locations of all CENP-A-permissive regions by single-cell Oligopaint fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH) on mitotic chromosomes. The results will illuminate the effects of epigenetic factors on CENP-A locations, and clarify the determinants necessary for functional holocentromeres. The knowledge will enhance the understanding of chromosome organization and promote the use of holocentric artificial chromosomes in synthetic biology and biotechnology.

17107526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17107526.value: 當成本效果分組決策可以被實施時，公平性值多少？：將異質性的價值納入分布式成本效果分析

17107526.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17107526.value: Prof Chan, Esther Wai Yin Prof Li, Xue Prof Zhao, Jie

17107526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17107526.value: Health systems worldwide face the persistent challenge of being unable to provide full coverage for all effective technologies, necessitating prioritization in resource allocation. Cost-effectiveness analysis (CEA) has traditionally served as a tool to guide these decisions, following a distributional justice principle of maximizing population health within budgetary constraints. However, standard CEA is limited in its capacity to address equity concerns and all potential efficiency gains. It overlooks individual heterogeneity and fails to account for the distributional consequences of health outcomes across the population. To address these limitations, two complementary approaches have emerged: the Value of Heterogeneity (VoH) and Distributional Cost-Effectiveness Analysis (DCEA). While each offers valuable insights, they operate independently and answer distinct questions, which may not optimally consider both goals simultaneously. This project aims to develop and implement a novel method that integrates DCEA and VoH to inform coverage decisions for new technologies. The resulting framework, termed DCEA-H, seeks to simultaneously address equity concerns and enhance efficiency in resource allocation. The method will be applied using a microsimulation-based CEA of pharmacological treatments for patients with type 2 diabetes, from the perspective of the Hospital Authority (HA) in Hong Kong. The project is expected to generate several key research outputs: (1) Individual-level cost-effectiveness estimates for all available hypoglycaemic pharmaceutical products used in the treatment of type 2 diabetes in Hong Kong, from the HA perspective (case-base); (2) an enhanced VoH application, incorporating multiple comparators across diverse subgroups—a methodological advancement in itself; (3) an estimate of the distribution of opportunity costs associated with health budget allocations in Hong Kong’s public health system, stratified by socioeconomic status; (4) an estimate of societal aversion to health inequalities within the Hong Kong population; (5) a DCEA to produce equity-informed resource allocation decisions using the case-base; and (6) the results of the implementation of the DCEA-H, compared to the independent application of DCEA and VoH, in terms of gains in population health and social welfare due to inequality reduction.
