DCEA-H expects to contribute significantly either locally or globally to enhance the current methods of economic evaluation in healthcare. 世界各地的醫療衛生體系均面臨著難以為所有具有療效的醫療科技提供全面保障的挑戰。成本效果分析（cost-effectiveness analysis, CEA）有助於指導資源配置，但通常依賴平均估計值，因而忽略了人口異質性及公平性影響。「異質性價值（value of heterogeneity, VoH）」框架評估針對不同亞組制定決策如何影響整體人口健康，而分布式成本效果分析（distributional cost-effectiveness analysis, DCEA）則評估由某項公平性考量所界定的不同亞組之間，總體健康收益與公平程度之間的平衡。儘管 VoH 可以改善資源配置效率，而 DCEA 能夠處理公平性問題，但將兩者分開使用可能導致較不理想的結果。本研究旨在建立一個整合性框架（DCEA-H），結合兩種方法，以支持醫療資源配置決策。我們將建立其理論基礎，並將其應用於 2 型糖尿病治療，同時開展一系列循序漸進的研究工作，包括模型開發，以及分別應用 VoH 和 DCEA 進行分析，最終藉此展示採用新方法所帶來的健康收益。我們相信，該方法將能更有效地支持全球醫療衛生決策，並預期香港將成為首批受益於此方法應用的地區之一。

17107726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17107726.value: 利用脂質納米粒子（Lipid Nanoparticles）遞送 CRISPR-Cas9系統介導 ATXN2 / SARM1 雙基因敲除，以逆轉小鼠肌萎縮性脊髓側索硬化症（Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis）表型之治療效應研究

17107726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17107726.value: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease that causes progressive paralysis and eventually death. It often links with frontotemporal dementia (FTD). Global cases are projected to rise 70% by 2040 due to population ageing burden. Only 10% ALS cases are genetic and remaining 90% are sporadic. Current therapies such as Riluzole or Edaravone provide only modest benefits. Tofersen, a recently approved gene therapy, benefits a small subset of ALS patients with specific genetic mutations. Thus, treatments that address the majority of ALS/ALS–FTD cases should be urgently developed. TDP-43 is a potential therapeutic target linked to nearly all ALS cases. Directly targeting TDP-43 is challenging due to its essential role in healthy neurons. An alternative approach considers indirectly targeting it via its modifiers. The ATXN2 gene, which encodes ataxin-2 protein, drives neurodegeneration in ALS by promoting the formation of toxic TDP-43 protein aggregates causing progressive neuronal damages. The SARM1 gene, encoding the sarm1 protein, is essential in driving destructive processes in neuron fibres during stress. We have proposed targeting those two genes to attain two different functional benefits linked to improving ALS phenotypes in mice. We deliver a gene editing tool co-targeting two distinct target genes in the same cell to perform two different functions to improve ALS phenotypes. Here, we combined two parallel hypotheses to deliver our novel lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) system encapsulating CRISPR/Cas9-based gene editing tools to attain dual knockout (KO) in the same target cell directing for therapeutic benefits in ALS. Dual targeting of ATXN2 and SARM1 presents a transformative approach to address the root causes of ALS. Combining two distinct but complementary pathways to treat ALS could offer a powerful and comprehensive new therapeutic strategy. In our previous work, LNPs, developed as drug carriers, demonstrated excellent stability in living systems and effectively protected encapsulated Cas9 mRNA and sgRNAs. These LNPs achieved a 20%–40% reduction in ataxin-2 and sarm1 proteins in the brain and spinal cord of healthy mouse following intranasal, intracerebroventricular, and intracisternal magna injections. Here, we proposed to examine ATXN2 and SARM1 dual KO effects on TDP-43 aggregation, neuronal health, reversal of ALS phenotypes, and behavioural improvement using humanized TDP-43 mice representing ALS phenotypes and comparing them with healthy mice. The findings of the proposed project will provide additional mechanistic insights to comprehend the therapeutic effects of CRISPR-Cas9-mediated ATXN2/SARM1 dual KO in reversing ALS phenotypes in mice. 肌萎縮性脊髓側索硬化症（amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, ALS），簡稱 ALS，俗稱「漸凍人症」是一種致命的神經退化性疾病，會導致患者出現漸進性癱瘓並最終死亡。ALS 亦常與額顳葉認知障礙症（frontotemporal dementia，簡稱 FTD）相關。受人口老化影響，至 2040 年全球 ALS 患者人數預計將增加近 70%。其中僅約 10% 的 ALS 屬於遺傳性，其餘 90% 均為缺乏明顯的家族遺傳病史的散發性案例。現有治療 ALS 的藥物，如利魯唑（Riluzole）及依達拉奉（Edaravone），所能帶來的臨床效益仍然有限。近期獲批的基因治療药物Tofersen，亦僅能惠及少數具備特定遺傳突變的 ALS 患者。因此，迫切需要開發能涵蓋絕大多數 ALS 及 ALS–FTD 患者的全新治療策略。 TDP-43 是與幾乎所有 ALS 病例相關的潛在治療靶點。然而，由於 TDP-43 在健康神經元中扮演關鍵角色，直接針對 TDP-43 進行干預極具挑戰性。另一替代策略，是藉由靶向其修飾因子（modifiers）來達到間接調節的效果。其中，編碼 ataxin-2 蛋白的 ATXN2 基因會透過促進具神經毒性的 TDP-43 蛋白聚集體形成，從而驅動 ALS 的神經退化，並導致漸進性神經元損傷。編碼 sarm1 蛋白的 SARM1 基因，則在神經元纖維處於應激狀態時引發的破壞性過程中發揮關鍵作用。因此，我們提出同時針對這兩個基因進行干預，以實現兩種不同且具互補性的功能效益，進而改善小鼠的 ALS 表型。結合這兩條截然不同但具互補性的途徑來治療 ALS，有望建立一套強大且全面的全新治療方案。 我們遞送了一套能在同一細胞內共同靶向兩個不同目標基因的基因編輯工具，以透過執行兩種不同功能來改善 ALS 表型。在此，我們結合了兩個平行假設，利用包裹 CRISPR-Cas9 基因編輯工具的新型脂質納米粒子（lipid nanoparticles，簡稱 LNPs）遞送系統，在同一目標細胞內實現雙重敲除，從而達致治療 ALS 的效益。同時靶向 ATXN2 與 SARM1，為應對 ALS 的根源病因提供了一種具變革性的策略。 在我們先前的研究中，作為藥物遞送載體的 LNPs 在活體系統中展現出極佳的穩定性，並能有效保護所包裹的 Cas9 mRNA 及向導 RNA（single-guide RNAs，簡稱 sgRNAs）。在健康小鼠中，經鼻內給藥、腦室內注射及小脑延髓池注射後，這些 LNPs 成功使腦部及脊髓內的 ataxin-2 及 sarm1 蛋白水平降低 20%–40%。在本研究中，我們擬採用能重現 ALS 表型的人源化 TDP-43 小鼠模型，並與健康小鼠進行比較，藉此檢測 ATXN2/SARM1 雙重敲除對 TDP-43 聚集、神經元健康、ALS 表型逆轉以及行為學改善的影響。本計畫的研究結果將提供進一步的機制性見解，以深入理解 CRISPR-Cas9 介導的 ATXN2/SARM1 雙重敲除在逆轉小鼠 ALS 表型方面的治療效應。

17108026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17108026.value: POSTN⁺ CAF-TGF-β訊號軸在口腔鱗癌轉移與免疫逃逸中的機制及靶向干預研究

17108026.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17108026.value: Prof Chen, Zigui Prof Pu, Jingya Prof Su, Yuxiong

17108026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17108026.value: Lymph node metastasis (LNM) remains the primary cause of mortality in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), yet the stromal mechanisms driving this process are incompletely understood. This project investigates the pivotal role of a specific periostin-expressing cancer-associated fibroblast (POSTN⁺ CAF) subpopulation in orchestrating both pro-metastatic signaling and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) to facilitate LNM. Our integrated approach will leverage primary cell co-cultures, multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) staining, CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, and orthotopic mouse models to functionally interrogate this axis in vitro and in vivo. Our interconnected objectives will first validate the POSTN/TGF-β axis as a key driver of invasion, then dissect its mechanistic role in TME remodeling and immune exclusion, and finally identify novel downstream targets amenable to therapy. By delivering novel mechanistic insights and a robust preclinical rationale, this work will establish a new paradigm for stroma-targeted therapy, offering a clear path toward preventing metastasis and improving survival for patients with this devastating disease. 淋巴結轉移是導致口腔鱗狀細胞癌患者死亡的主要原因，但驅動該過程的間質微環境機制目前尚不完全明確。本項目旨在探究一類特異性表達骨膜蛋白的腫瘤相關成纖維細胞（POSTN+ CAF）亞群，剖析其如何通過協同激活促轉移信號及重塑免疫抑制微環境來促進腫瘤發生淋巴結轉移。 研究將結合原代細胞共培養、多重免疫螢光、CRISPR-Cas9 基因編輯以及原位小鼠模型等多種手段，在體內外層面系統解析該信號軸的功能。具體研究內容分為三個遞進階段：首先，驗證 POSTN/TGF-β 信號軸在腫瘤侵襲過程中的核心驅動作用；其次，闡明該信號軸在微環境重塑及免疫排斥中的具體機制；最後，篩選並鑑定具有臨床干預潛力的新型下游靶點。 本研究不僅有望為口腔鱗狀細胞癌的轉移機制提供新的理論見解和扎實的臨床前數據，還將為靶向腫瘤間質治療確立新思路，最終為阻斷腫瘤轉移、改善患者生存預後提供科學依據。

17108426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17108426.value: 浮萍沃爾菲亞屬（Wolffia）快速生長的分子機制

17108426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17108426.value: Wolffia species are the fastest-growing species among known angiosperms. Revealing the mechanism of their rapid growth is of great significance for research on plant productivity. The major objective of this study is to reveal the physiological, biochemical, and molecular mechanisms of Wolffia’s rapid growth rate, which is expected to involve higher efficiency of photosynthesis, energy conversion, and inter-organellar energy flux. Our preliminary data showed that the rate of photosynthetic oxygen release in Wolffia was three times higher than that of Arabidopsis. Our previous studies proved that mature Arabidopsis chloroplasts do not express ATP transporters (NTT transporter), and thus need to balance the stromal ATP/NADPH ratio and to regenerate NADP+, which is the electron acceptor of linear electron flow (LEF), by exporting surplus reducing equivalents from excess NADPH via the malate valve. We hypothesize that Wolffia chloroplasts express NTT transporter to enable importation of cytosolic ATP. This can quickly balance the stromal ATP/NADPH ratio and enable faster regeneration of stromal NADP+. If this is the case, Wolffia will have a high oxygen evolving rate during photosynthesis, as we observed in our experiment. The rapid growth of Wolffia may also be attributed to its higher ability to fix CO2 via the anaplerotic pathway and the subsequent carbon-concentrating mechanism (CCM). Floating on the water surface, the degree of O2 fixation by Rubisco in Wolffia chloroplasts is expected to be lower than that of land plants like Arabidopsis. The minimization of photorespiration will reduce energy and carbon loss from the photorespiratory flux to support the fast growth rate of Wolffia. We will examine the above mechanisms by carrying out promoter-GUS studies, in situ hybridization, enzyme assays, oxygraph analysis, pyridine nucleotides measurements, and spatial transcriptomic and metabolomics studies, etc. In addition to measuring physiological parameters like growth rate, photosynthesis, and respiration, we will also study inter-organellar energy fluxes between chloroplast and mitochondria using in planta ratiometric energy sensors. We will study the chloroplasts and mitochondria in detail, including oxygraph study, and enzymatic capacities of key metabolic enzymes in these two organelles. The new findings generated from this project will be useful for exploiting these species for use in green energy and biotechnology, as well as applications in synthetic biology and plant biotechnology. 浮萍沃爾菲亞屬（Wolffia）是已知被子植物中生長速度最快的物種。闡明其快速生長的機制，對於植物生產力研究具有重大意義。本研究的主要目標是闡明沃爾菲亞快速生長的生理、生化及分子機制，預期這將涉及高效率的光合作用、能量轉換以及細胞器間的能量流動。我們的初步數據顯示，沃爾菲亞屬的光合作用釋氧速率是擬南芥的三倍。我們先前研究證實，成熟的擬南芥葉綠體不表達 ATP 轉運蛋白（NTT 轉運蛋白），因此需要透過「蘋果酸閥門」將過剩的 NADPH 中的還原當量輸出，藉此平衡基質中的 ATP/NADPH 比值，並再生作為線性電子流（LEF）電子受體的 NADP+。我們假設浮萍沃爾菲亞屬的葉綠體會表達 NTT 轉運蛋白，以利於將胞質中的 ATP 轉運至葉綠體。此機制能迅速平衡葉綠體基質中的 ATP/NADPH 比例，並加速葉綠體基質中 NADP+ 的再生。若情況果真如此，沃爾菲亞屬在光合作用期間將具有較高的氧氣釋放速率，這也與我們實驗中的觀察結果相符。沃爾菲亞屬的快速生長，亦可能歸因於其透過PEPC 碳固定補充途徑及隨後的碳濃縮機制（CCM）進行二氧化碳固定的能力較強。由於沃爾菲亞屬漂浮於水面，其葉綠體中Rubisco的氧氣固定效率將低於擬南芥等陸生植物，減少因光呼吸造成的能量與碳損失，從而支持沃爾菲亞屬的快速生長速率。我們將透過啟動子-GUS研究、原位雜交、酶活性測定、氧氣圖譜分析、吡啶核苷酸測量，以及空間轉錄組學與代謝組學研究等方法，探討上述機制。除了測量生長速率、光合作用和呼吸作用等生理參數外，我們還將利用植體內比值能量感測器，研究葉綠體與線粒體之間的細胞器間ATP能量流。我們將對葉綠體與線粒體進行詳細研究，包括氧氣記錄法分析，以及這兩種細胞器中關鍵代謝酶的酶活性測定。本計畫所產生的新發現，將有助於開發這些物種在綠色能源與生物技術領域的應用，並可應用於合成生物學及植物生物技術。

17109126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17109126.value: JAK2V617F與CALR突變骨髓纖維化治療應答的分子及生物學機制研究

17109126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17109126.value: Background. Myelofibrosis (MF), the most severe subtype of MPN, is characterized by reticulin fibrosis, abnormal cytokine mediated systemic symptoms, anaemia, hepatosplenomegaly and a propensity for progression to acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The Janus kinas (JAK) inhibitor Ruxolitinib is the mainstay of treatment for most patients with MF but treatment failure is common and represents an unmet medical need. We performed the world’s first study of Ruxolitinib in combination with the novel agent Bomedemstat. Clinical benefit in terms of reduction of symptom burden and spleen volume reduction was observed in both treatment ruxolitinib naïve and ruxolitinib-refractory patients with MF. In addition, reduction in JAK2V617F and CALR allele burden by next generation sequencing (NGS) was observed in 57.5% and 77.8% of patients respectively. Nevertheless, the biologic basis of such responses are largely unknown. Objectives. 1. To elucidate clonal evolution and mutation dynamics in response to therapy 2. To investigate molecular signatures of responders versus non-responders Methods. Droplet digital polymerase reaction (ddPCR) for JAK2V617F and CALR mutations will be serially assessed. This will be further complemented with single-cell multi-omic analyses. The infrastructure and expertise is established in our team to ensure technical feasibility. Expected outcome and impact. This project will transform the therapeutic landscape for patients with MF by uncovering the biological basis of molecular responses in persons with myelofibrosis. By evaluating the molecular and biological basis of response and non-response to treatment, we will advance the understanding of MPN pathobiology with the ultimate goal to optimise therapeutic strategies and improve clinical outcomes for patients.

17109326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17109326.value: 探究核心蛋白聚糖（Decorin）在腹膜透析中對腹膜結構炎症、細胞衰老及纖維化的作用

17109326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17109326.value: Peritoneal dialysis (PD) is an important renal replacement modality for patients with end-stage kidney disease. Increased life expectancy in developed countries has seen a rise in chronic kidney disease in the elderly. The success of long-term PD and favorable clinical outcome of patients are dependent on the structural integrity and normal transport function of the peritoneal membrane. Mesothelial cells line the surface of the peritoneal membrane and they constitute the first line of defense against chemical or bacterial injury. Mesothelial cells perform physiological homeostatic functions, but upon injury can also contribute to peritoneal inflammation and fibrosis through epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and cellular senescence. There is no treatment for peritoneal fibrosis. Decorin is a small leucine-rich dermatan sulphate proteoglycan that possesses anti-fibrotic and anti-angiogenic properties. It is the predominant proteoglycan synthesized and secreted by human peritoneal mesothelial cells (HPMC) and its expression is reduced in HPMC exposed to TGF-beta1 and IL-1beta. The role of decorin in peritoneal inflammation and fibrosis in the setting of PD has not been defined. Results from our preliminary studies showed that dialysate decorin level is reduced with increasing time on PD (Figure 1). In the normal murine peritoneum, decorin expression is present in the mesothelium while fibronectin is absent. In a murine PD model, peritoneal mesothelial denudation and submesothelial thickening is associated with induction of fibronectin and depletion of decorin expression (Figure 1). Peritoneal fibrosis is exacerbated in decorin knockout (KO) mice on PD and is accompanied by increased expression of mediators of inflammation, EMT, cellular senescence and fibrosis compared to their wild-type (WT) counterpart. Decorin supplementation reduced submesothelial thickening that was induced by PD fluid. These findings suggest altered decorin synthesis in PD, and decorin supplementation may attenuate peritoneal fibrosis. The project aims to investigate the role of decorin in peritoneal inflammation, cellular senescence and fibrosis in a murine model of PD using young and aged WT and decorin KO mice. The therapeutic potential of decorin supplementation on peritoneal inflammation and fibrosis and its ability to deplete senescent cells in the peritoneum will also be investigated, and compared to senolytics. Progressive deterioration of the peritoneal membrane is universal in long-term PD, and there is no effective measure to prevent peritoneal fibrosis in PD patients. Elucidating the role of decorin in peritoneal inflammation and fibrosis addresses a crucial knowledge gap in the pathogenic mechanisms, which is prerequisite to novel therapeutic approaches to improve clinical outcomes.

17109426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17109426.value: 首发精神分裂症谱系障碍患者自我参照凝视知觉的计算认知机制：一项为期五年的纵向随访研究

17109426.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17109426.value: Prof Hsiao, Janet Hui-wen Prof Lui, Sai Yu Simon Dr Olivia Louise , Calvin-Rawls Dr Wong, Hoi Yan Gloria Dr Wong, Ting Yat

17109426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17109426.value: Social cognition deficits are characteristic in patients with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders (SSD) and are major drivers to their social and vocational impairments above and beyond the general cognitive deficits, with limited effective treatment modalities. One of the key domains of social cognition is the ability to infer intentions, emotions and beliefs of others. Awareness of others' attention and intention through gaze perception, including self-referential gaze perception (SRGP) - judging whether others are looking at us, is an essential element of social interaction and social cognition. Studying the nature and cognitive mechanisms of the SRGP in patients could thus improve our understanding of social cognitive deficits and support the development of effective interventions in this population. Benefiting from our previous study, we have 100 patients with first-episode schizophrenia spectrum (FES) disorders and 88 health controls who have been well characterised with clinical, cognition, functioning and social cognition at baseline. We proposed to conduct a 5 year follow-up study of this population and answer three research questions. First is the stability of the social cognitive function, in particular the cognitive process of SRGP in the FES compared with the healthy control. Two computational modeling will be applied to facilitate a quantitative understanding of the cognitive and visual information processing strategies during the tasks. Since the gaze's intentional judgement is essential and fundamental to social cognition, the cognitive strategies during the task could be basic cognitive units for social cognition, building blocks of more complex social cognitive function and social functioning, thus could be considered an interventional target. The second research question is to examine the predictability of the cognitive strategies of the SRGP to the long-term clinical and functional outcomes. The third research question is to understand the link between these cognitive strategies of the SRGP and the cognitive process of more complex social cognition such as facial emotion recognition and comic strip. Results of this study will enhance our understanding of mechanisms and nature of social cognitive function impairments and pave a way for establishing low-cost and scalable digital tools for routine assessment of patients to facilitate objective and informative clinical assessment and treatment monitoring. 社會認知缺陷是精神分裂症譜系障礙（schizophrenia-spectrum disorders, SSD）患者的典型特徵，也是導致其社會功能與職業功能受損的重要因素，其影響程度甚至超過一般性認知缺陷，而目前有效的治療方式仍相當有限。社會認知的一個關鍵領域，是推斷他人意圖、情緒與信念的能力。透過凝視知覺來理解他人的注意方向與意圖，包括自我參照凝視知覺（self-referential gaze perception, SRGP），亦即判斷他人是否正在注視自己，是社會互動與社會認知的基本組成部分。因此，探討患者 SRGP 的特徵及其認知機制，有助於深化我們對此族群社會認知缺陷的理解，並支持有效介入措施的發展。 基於我們先前的研究，目前已建立包含 100 名首發精神分裂症譜系障礙（first-episode schizophrenia-spectrum disorders, FES）患者及 88 名健康對照者的研究隊列。所有參與者皆已於基線階段接受系統性評估，涵蓋臨床症狀、一般認知、社會功能及社會認知等面向。我們擬對此隊列進行為期 5 年的追蹤研究，並探討以下三個研究問題。 第一個研究問題是：相較於健康對照組，FES 患者的社會認知功能，尤其是與 SRGP 相關的認知歷程，是否具有穩定性。本研究將採用兩種計算模型方法，量化分析參與者於任務執行過程中的認知策略與視覺資訊處理策略。由於凝視意圖判斷是社會認知中基礎且關鍵的能力，個體在此任務中所採用的認知策略，可能構成社會認知的基本認知單元，並作為更複雜社會認知功能與社會功能的基礎組成部分，因此亦可視為潛在的介入標的。 第二個研究問題是：探討與 SRGP 相關的認知策略是否能夠預測患者的長期臨床結果與功能性結果。 第三個研究問題是：闡明與 SRGP 相關的認知策略，與較複雜社會認知歷程之間的關聯，例如在臉部情緒辨識及連環漫畫理解任務中的認知加工過程。 本研究的結果將有助於加深我們對社會認知功能障礙之機制與本質的理解，並為建立低成本、可擴展的數位化評估工具奠定基礎，以應用於患者的常規評估，促進更客觀且資訊豐富的臨床評估與治療監測。

17110026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17110026.value: 甲硫胺酸代謝的肝癌免疫編輯機制與干預策略

17110026.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17110026.value: Prof Cheung, Tom Hiu Tung Prof Wong, Chun Ming

17110026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17110026.value: Metabolic reprogramming is a key feature of cancer, with tumour cells heavily reliant on amino acids for their growth and function. Among these, methionine stands out as essential for critical processes like translation, methylation, and redox balance. The role of methionine uptake in Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC), as well as strategies to exploit this dependency, remain underexplored. Here, we identified two methionine transporters, SLC7A6 and SLC43A2, that were significantly upregulated in human HCC tumours and were associated with poor patient outcomes. Knockdown of either or both transporters impaired the proliferation and survival of HCC cells in vitro. Similar results were observed in multiple HCC cell lines when we depleted methionine from the culture medium. We established an in vivo isotopic tracing approach with 13C515N1-methionine and confirmed the impairment of methionine uptake in tumours lacking the two methionine transporters. As diet is the primary nutrient source for tumours, we aimed to target this vulnerability using dietary methionine restriction (MR). Indeed, we demonstrated that short-term intermittent MR regimens effectively restricted HCC development. Interestingly, tumours from MR-treated mice were generally less immunosuppressive with decreased levels of M2-like tumour-infiltrating macrophages, suggesting the potential of MR in activating antitumor immune responses. However, we discovered that the macrophage polarization is not a direct consequence of MR but rather indirectly by decreased expression of Tgfb1 in cancer cells during MR. Mechanistically, MR decreases the availability of S-adenosyl-methionine (SAM), reducing m6A methylation which is crucial for mRNA stability. Site-specific m6A methylome profiling showed that MR significantly reduced m6A at two sites on the TGFB1 transcript. Based on these findings, our research aims to: (1) elucidate the mechanisms and clinical relevance of methionine transport in HCC, (2) define how methionine depletion regulates TGFB1 expression via m6A modification, and (3) assess the impact and therapeutic potential of methionine depletion on the HCC tumor microenvironment and response to immunotherapy. Through integrated in vitro, in vivo, and clinical analyses including isotopic tracing, CRISPR-based gene editing, m6A epitranscriptomic profiling, and functional immune studies, we will advance our understanding of methionine metabolism in HCC and identify novel strategies to enhance immunotherapy by targeting the methionine-m6A-TGFB1 axis. This work will provide new mechanistic and translational insights into the metabolic control of tumor immunity in HCC, and inform the development of metabolic interventions to improve patient outcomes. 癌症的發展與代謝異常密切相關，其中肝癌細胞高度依賴甲硫胺酸來維持生長。研究發現，肝癌中兩種負責運輸甲硫胺酸的蛋白含量越高，患者預後越差；而阻斷這些蛋白或減少甲硫胺酸供應，可顯著抑制肝癌細胞的生長。透過短期、間歇性的飲食限制甲硫胺酸，不僅能抑制小鼠肝癌發展，還能改變腫瘤微環境，減少抑制免疫的M2型巨噬細胞，從而激活抗腫瘤免疫。進一步研究發現，甲硫胺酸限制會降低細胞內SAM水平，進而減少RNA上的m6A修飾，最終下調免疫抑制因子TGFB1的表現。基於以上發現，本研究旨在闡明甲硫胺酸運輸在肝癌中的具體作用，揭示甲硫胺酸限制如何透過m6A修飾調控TGFB1，並評估甲硫胺酸限制對腫瘤免疫微環境的影響及其與免疫治療結合的潛力。這項研究為肝癌治療提供了新思路，表明透過飲食或藥物干預甲硫胺酸代謝，可能成為增強免疫療效的新策略。

17110326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17110326.value: 可溶性 β-Klotho 介導的 FGF21 反式信號通路的鑒定與表徵：從分子機製到臨床意義

17110326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17110326.value: Obesity and its associated metabolic disorders have become prominent public health challenges, underscoring an urgent need for the development of targeted therapeutic interventions. Extensive animal studies and clinical trials have demonstrated the therapeutic potential of fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21) in treating obesity-related conditions, notably hyperlipidemia and fatty liver disease. However, the issue of FGF21 resistance remains unresolved and the functioning mechanisms of FGF21 and its receptors remain incompletely understood. Traditionally, FGF21 is believed to signal through a membrane-bound receptor complex comprising FGF receptor-1 (FGFR1) and the obligate co-receptor β-Klotho (KLB). Remarkably, our preliminary study identified two soluble forms of KLB (sKLB), a long form (~140 kDa) and a short form (~85 kDa), likely generated via a dual-site proteolytic cleavage mechanism. Notably, the long form of sKLB exhibits biological activity capable of facilitating FGF21 signaling in both KLB-expressing and KLB-null cell lines. These observations suggest a novel mode of FGF21 action, where the long sKLB forms a circulating complex with FGF21 that potentially interacts with FGFR1 on target cells, initiating trans-signaling distinct from the classic membrane-bound pathway. This project aims to (1) elucidate the mechanisms underlying sKLB generation, including identifying specific cleavage sites and proteolytic enzymes involved. We will also investigate how sKLB facilitates FGF21 trans-signaling. (2) We will employ multi-omics approaches to dissect the intracellular signaling networks activated by sKLB alone and in conjunction with FGF21, thereby uncovering the molecular effectors of sKLB/FGF21-mediated signaling. (3) We will quantify circulating sKLB levels in plasma samples from human cohorts with obesity-related conditions such as type 2 diabetes and fatty liver, utilizing our validated in-house ELISA kits. Parallel assessments in corresponding mouse models will help identify tissue sources and dynamics of circulating sKLB, with the goal of establishing sKLB as a novel biomarker for metabolic disorders. (4) We will investigate the capacity of sKLB to sensitize endogenous or exogenous FGF21 and thereby elicit metabolic benefits in diet-induced obese mice, which may identify sKLB-based therapeutics and help develop novel approach to overcome FGF21 resistance and enhance therapeutic efficacy of FGF21. To our knowledge, this research will be the first to report the discovery of FGF21 trans-signaling mediated by sKLB, potentially leading to a quantum jump in FGF21 biology. Our findings have the potential to position sKLB as a critical biomarker and therapeutic target for obesity-related metabolic diseases, thereby advancing the understanding and treatment of these prevalent conditions. 肥胖及其相關的代謝紊亂已成為重大的公共衛生挑戰，開發有效的靶向性治療手段迫在眉睫。大量的動物研究和臨床試驗已證實成纖維細胞生長因子21（FGF21）在治療肥胖相關疾病（特別是高血脂和脂肪肝）方面具有卓越潛力。然而，FGF21抵抗的問題尚未解決，且FGF21及其受體的作用機制也尚未完全闡明。 傳統觀點認為，FGF21透過一種由FGF受體1（FGFR1）和必需的輔助受體β-Klotho（KLB）組成的膜結合受體複合物來傳遞信號。我們的初步研究發現了兩種可溶性KLB（sKLB）形式：長型（約140 kDa）和短型（約85 kDa），它們很可能是透過雙位點蛋白水解切割機制產生的。特別是長型sKLB表現出生物活性，能夠在表達KLB和不表達KLB的細胞系中促進FGF21信號傳導。這些發現提示了一種新的FGF21作用模式：長型sKLB與FGF21形成循環複合物，可能與目標細胞上的FGFR1相互作用，從而啟動一種不同於經典膜結合途徑的「反式信號傳導」（trans-signaling）。 本計畫旨在：（1）闡明sKLB生成的機制，包括確定特定的切割位點和相關的蛋白水解酶；同時研究sKLB如何促進FGF21的反式信號傳導。 （2）利用多組學方法解析sKLB單獨作用或與FGF21聯合作用所啟動的細胞內信號網絡，從而揭示sKLB/FGF21介導信號傳導的分子效應元件。 （3）利用我們自主研發並經過驗證的ELISA試劑盒，定量檢測患有肥胖相關疾病（如2型糖尿病和脂肪肝）的人群隊列血漿樣本中的循環sKLB水準。透過在相應小鼠模型中進行平行評估，確定循環sKLB的組織來源及動態變化，最終目標是將sKLB確立為代謝紊亂的一種新型生物標記物。 (4) 我們將研究 sKLB 增強內源性或外源性 FGF21 敏感性並由此在飲食誘導的肥胖小鼠中產生代謝獲益的能力；這項研究有望發掘基於 sKLB 的治療藥物，並有助於開發克服 FGF21 抵抗及增強 FGF21 療效的新策略。 該項研究將首次報導由 sKLB 介導的 FGF21 反式信號傳導現象，有望推動 FGF21 生物學研究實現跨越式發展。我們的研究結果可望確立 sKLB 作為肥胖相關代謝疾病的關鍵生物標記及治療靶點，從而推動對這些常見疾病的理解與治療。

17110726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17110726.value: 長程神經活動傳播與大腦狀態：一項光遺傳學功能性磁振造影研究

17110726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17110726.value: An outstanding question plaguing neuroscience is synthesizing our understanding of brain circuits and their multiple functions to elucidate their dysfunction in disease states. Converging evidence at the cellular and micro-circuit level suggest temporal patterns of neural activity are critical to underlie basic sensory and motor processing, behavior and learning. However, these frameworks are slow to accommodate highly complex, interconnected neural structures architecture that utilize parallel and hierarchical circuits and networks distributed within and between neural systems. The challenge is further compounded with recent works demonstrating that underlying brain states (i.e., distributed neural activity patterns that are recorded during sleep/wake and/or behavioral state) do affect the characteristics of neural activity propagation in local microcircuits. To fill this gap in knowledge, we must elucidate whether and how neural activity propagates in long-range polysynaptic neural circuits, brain networks and systems at various distinct brain states. Blood-oxygen-level-dependent (BOLD) fMRI constitutes a powerful neuroimaging platform that is widely used by both basic and clinical research communities to map brain-wide functions in response to a specific sensory or cognitive task. However, fMRI only reflects the gross outcome of complex and cascaded activities of various cell types and networks, posing significant limitations to dissect circuit properties and their underlying temporal basis at different brain states. In this project, we aim to uncover whether and how brain states alter long-range propagation pathways and their intended targets. By deploying an integrative neuroimaging approach combining optogenetics and functional MRI (fMRI), we will systematically (i) initiate and interrogate temporal patterns of neural activity within long-range sensory systems via optogenetics, (ii) determine and characterize subsequent brain-wide, long-range downstream neural activity propagation pathways and their targets using fMRI, and (iii) delineate the underlying brain states and the neural mechanisms mediating elicited long-range neural activity propagation using simultaneous electrophysiological recordings. In our preliminary studies, we have implemented a simple design of optogenetic pulse train stimulation to examine neural activity propagation in somatosensory, olfactory and vestibular systems. Our initial experimental findings demonstrated the specificity and sensitivity to characterize brain-wide neural activity propagation pathways and their targets across three different sensory systems. However, the preliminary optogenetic fMRI works were conducted in anesthetized rats and without simultaneous neural activity recordings to classify brain states. Here, we will advance our research by examining long-range neural activity propagation under distinct brain states in awake rats.

17110926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17110926.value: 解析微管蛋白密碼與腔內酵素調控微管復合力學性質的分子機制

17110926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17110926.value: Microtubules are not only intracellular tracks but also force-bearing components in diverse mechanotransduction machineries across evolution, including human motile cilia, D. melanogaster larval proprioceptive organs, and C. elegans touch receptor neurons. In these architectures, microtubules undergo cycles of force-driven deformation to power fluid flow, coordinate the crawling behavior, or transduce touch sensation. However, the molecular mechanism by which microtubules respond to forces of different magnitudes and timescales remains unresolved. In particular, the structural elements that couple microtubule’s mechanical properties to the strength of inter-tubulin lattice interactions are unknown. This knowledge gap is mainly due to the long-overdue biochemical, biophysical, and structural characterization of microtubules that have physiologically relevant compositions and exhibit a broad range of mechanical properties. The compositions of alpha/beta-tubulin subunits in cellular microtubules can vary significantly due to the presence of tubulin family proteins (i.e., isotypes) and post-translational modifications (PTMs). The combination of tubulin isotypes and PTMs forms codes that regulate microtubule organization and functions in specific biological contexts. In particular, mutations in specific tubulin isotypes and the disruption of the alpha-tubulin lysine 40 (K40) acetylation have been associated with mechanosensing defects in mice, flies, and nematodes. However, we lack a mechanistic insight into how tubulin isotypes and acetylated alpha-tubulin confer critical microtubule properties for maintaining the integrity of the force-sensing microtubule architectures. The presence of tubulin acetyltransferases, which are responsible for K40 acetylation, further complicates the scenario of how multi-protofilament-bound luminal enzymes regulate the mechanical properties of microtubules. The challenge of reconstituting microtubules with a defined composition of tubulin isotypes and acetylation states has limited the approach to dissecting how tubulin acetyltransferase-bound microtubules respond to forces as a composite material. To overcome this challenge, we have developed a state-of-the-art strategy for the structural and mechanical characterization of microtubules reconstituted with a defined composition of tubulin isotypes and acetylation states. Supported by preliminary data, we have (i) generated recombinant alpha/beta-tubulin isotypes that are enriched in mechanosensing cells across evolution, (ii) employed amber suppression to incorporate acetyl lysine into K40 of recombinant α-tubulin, and (iii) established the cryo-electron microscopy workflow to obtain the structural reconstruction of isotypically pure microtubules at ~2.3 Å resolution. Together, we are well-positioned to elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which microtubules adapt to diverse mechano-environments for the needs of biological processes. Our study will open a new avenue toward unraveling some of the greatest mysteries in the biological functions of tubulin codes. 微管不僅是細胞內的運輸軌道，也是演化過程中多種機械轉導機制中的承力組成部分，包括人類運動纖毛、黑腹果蠅（D. melanogaster）幼蟲本體感覺器官，以及秀麗隱桿線蟲（C. elegans）觸覺受器神經元。在這些結構中，微管會經歷由力驅動的變形循環，以驅動液體流動、協調爬行行為，或轉導觸覺感受。然而，微管如何回應不同大小與時間尺度的作用力，其分子機制仍未明瞭。特別是，將微管機械性質與微管蛋白晶格間交互作用強度相連結的結構元素，目前仍屬未知。這一知識缺口主要源於長期缺乏對具有生理相關組成、且展現廣泛機械性質範圍之微管的生化、生物物理與結構特徵分析。 細胞中微管的 α/β-微管蛋白次單元組成，會因微管蛋白家族蛋白（即同種型，isotypes）與轉譯後修飾（post-translational modifications, PTMs）的存在而顯著不同。微管蛋白同種型與轉譯後修飾的組合形成「微管蛋白密碼」（tubulin codes），可在特定生物情境中調控微管的組織與功能。尤其是，特定微管蛋白同種型的突變，以及 α-微管蛋白第 40 位離胺酸（K40）乙醯化的破壞，已被發現與小鼠、果蠅和線蟲的機械感知缺陷相關。然而，我們仍缺乏機制層面的理解，尚不清楚微管蛋白同種型與乙醯化 α-微管蛋白如何賦予微管關鍵特性，以維持力感測微管結構的完整性。負責 K40 乙醯化的微管蛋白乙醯轉移酶之存在，進一步使多條原絲結合的管腔內酵素如何調控微管機械性質的情境更加複雜。由於難以重組具有明確微管蛋白同種型與乙醯化狀態組成的微管，限制了我們以複合材料的角度，解析與微管蛋白乙醯轉移酶結合之微管如何回應作用力。 為克服此挑戰，我們已發展出一套先進策略，用於對具有明確微管蛋白同種型與乙醯化狀態組成的重組微管進行結構與機械特徵分析。在初步資料的支持下，我們已經：（i）產生在演化上各類機械感知細胞中富集的重組 α/β-微管蛋白同種型；（ii）利用琥珀密碼子抑制技術，將乙醯化離胺酸導入重組 α-微管蛋白的 K40 位點；以及（iii）建立冷凍電子顯微鏡工作流程，以約 2.3 Å 的解析度取得同種型純化微管的結構重建。綜合而言，我們已具備有利條件，可闡明微管如何因應多樣化的機械環境以滿足生物過程需求的分子機制。本研究將開啟一條新途徑，以揭示微管蛋白密碼在生物功能中一些最重大的謎團。

17111026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17111026.value: 面向超低场全身磁共振成像临床应用的脂肪抑制与定量技术

17111026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111026.value: MRI has greatly impacted modern healthcare with its non-invasive, non-ionizing, multi-parametric and quantitative properties. However, after five decades of development, the accessibility of MRI remains limited and highly uneven, primarily due to the cost-prohibitive nature and infrastructural requirements associated with existing standard high-field (1.5 Tesla or 3 Tesla) superconducting MRI scanners. Consequently, there has been a growing interest in developing ultra-low-field (ULF; below 0.1 Tesla) MRI scanners to address the global healthcare disparities. Our team has been a pioneer in ULF MRI, being the first to successfully design and construct a 0.05 Tesla whole-body MRI scanner and demonstrate its wide applicability for imaging various anatomical structures. Clinically, fat suppression and quantification are of indispensable value for pathology visualization and tissue characterization, particularly in body imaging where organs are surrounded by or composited with adipose tissue (e.g., for diagnosing fatty liver disease). However, while several fat suppression techniques have been developed and routinely used in clinical high-field MRI, robust fat suppression and quantification at ULF remain challenging due to inherently low SNR and extremely small chemical shift between water and fat. Here, we propose to develop a new water-fat separation method to tackle the fat suppression challenges in ULF MRI for whole-body clinical applications. It consists of multi-echo chemical shift encoded imaging and deep learning based water-fat separation (Deep-FATS). Our general hypothesis states that the fat suppression challenges associated with drastic field strength reduction can be overcome through high-efficiency data acquisition and by leveraging high-quality high-field MRI data and advanced computational modelling. We believe that a versatile neural network model that integrates physics priors can better estimate water and fat components from multi-echo chemical shift encoded images for reliable fat suppression and quantification. To test our hypothesis, we will first develop our proposed Deep-FATS method, which allows accurate estimation of water and fat components from chemical shift encoded images at minimal echo times, even in presence of high level of image noise. Second, we will optimize and comprehensively evaluate our proposed method in various human imaging applications on our experimental ULF MRI platforms. Finally, we will explore preliminary clinical applicability of our proposed method by direct comparison to clinical 3 Tesla results for both normal subjects and patients. The proposed method is expected to provide an effective and robust solution for fat suppression and quantification, to advance ULF MRI towards truly accessible, simplified and point-of-care clinical applications at whole-body level. 磁共振成像（MRI）凭借其无创、无电离辐射、多参数及定量化的特性，对现代医疗卫生领域产生了深远的影响。然而，历经五十年的发展，MRI的可及性依然有限且分布高度不均。这主要是由于现有的标准高场（1.5特斯拉或3特斯拉）超导磁共振扫描仪成本高昂，且对场地基础设施（如屏蔽室、液氦冷却等）有着极高的要求。因此，开发超低场（ultra-low-field, ULF；低于0.1特斯拉）磁共振扫描仪以解决全球医疗资源分配不均的挑战，正受到国际学术界和临床医学界的广泛关注。申请人团队致力于超低场磁共振成像（ULF MRI）研究，率先成功设计并研发了0.05特斯拉无屏蔽全身磁共振原理样机，并证实了其在多种人体解剖结构成像中的广泛应用价值。 在临床磁共振成像应用中，脂肪抑制与定量对于病灶的影像及组织特征表征具有不可替代的价值，特别是在体部成像中，许多器官被脂肪组织包绕或含有脂肪成分（例如，用于诊断脂肪性肝病）。然而，尽管多种脂肪抑制技术已被开发并广泛应用于常规临床高场磁共振成像中，在超低场下实现稳健的脂肪抑制与定量仍极具挑战。这主要是由于超低场强下固有的极低信噪比（SNR）以及水和脂肪质子之间极其微小的化学位移。 为此，本研究提出开发一种新型的水脂分离方法，以攻克超低场磁共振在全身临床应用中所面临的脂肪抑制与精准定量难题。该方法由多回波化学位移编码（chemical shift encoding, CSE）成像和基于深度学习的水脂分离技术（Deep-FATS）组成。我们的核心科学假设是：通过高效的数据采集方案，结合高质量的高场磁共振先验数据与先进的计算建模，可以克服由磁场强度大幅降低所带来的物理局限性。我们认为，一个融合了磁共振物理先验知识的通用神经网络模型，能够更精准地从超低场多回波编码图像中解耦并估计出水和脂肪成分，从而实现可靠的脂肪抑制与质子密度脂肪分数（proton density fat fraction, PDFF）定量。 为验证该假设，我们首先将开发所提出的Deep-FATS方法，该方法能够在极短回波时间下，从化学位移编码图像中精确估算水和脂肪成分，即使在图像噪声水平较高的情况下也能保持精准。其次，我们将在实验性超低场MRI平台上，针对多种人体成像应用，对该方法进行优化与全面评估。最后，我们将通过把健康受试者及患者在超低场下的结果与临床3特斯拉MRI结果进行直接对比，探索该方法的初步临床适用性。所提出的方法有望为脂肪抑制与定量提供一种高效且稳健的解决方案，进而推动超低场MRI技术朝着真正普及化、极简化及床旁（point-of-care）全身临床应用的方向发展。

17111426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17111426.value: 護理評估後青黴素激發測試（PANDA）：前瞻性隨機對照研究比較護理主導與標準療法於低風險青黴素過敏之療效

17111426.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17111426.value: Prof Chan, Sophia Siu Chee Prof Hung, Ivan Fan Ngai Prof Leung, Agnes Sze-yin Dr Li, Timothy Chun-Man Prof Trubiano, Jason

17111426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111426.value: Penicillins are the most prescribed medication and common culprits of drug “allergy”, but ~90% of penicillin allergy labels are found to be incorrect after formal testing. These incorrect labels are associated with poorer outcomes, greater healthcare burden and development of multidrug resistant organisms (MDRO). The current standard of care (SoC) for assessment is based on local guidelines with assessments primarily conducted by physicians. Nonetheless access to allergist/physician-led services remains limited in many countries, creating a critical bottleneck to more efficiently “delabel” incorrect diagnoses. We recognize the potential of the latest regional guidelines that propose nurse-directed penicillin allergy assessments locally and internationally. We propose to conduct this study to provide conclusive evidence for the efficacy, safety and longitudinal impact of nurse-directed direct provocation testing in patients with “low-risk” penicillin allergy. To evaluate this approach, we propose the PANDA (Provocation After Nurse-Directed Assessment) study: a prospective, randomized, non-inferiority trial comparing nurse-led direct provocation testing against standard physician-led care in patients with low-risk penicillin allergy. We aim to enroll over 408 low-risk (as defined by local (HK-DADI) and regional (APAAACI) guidelines) participants from two allergy centers in Hong Kong, randomizing them 1:1 into either the PANDA or standard-of-care pathway. In the standard-of-care arm, patients undergo a clinical history review by a physician, followed by skin testing (if indicated) and supervised oral penicillin challenge for those deemed low risk, all performed according to local protocols. In the PANDA arm, trained allergy nurses conduct a structured assessment using a validated algorithm based on HK-DADI and APAAACI criteria. Patients classified as low risk by the nurse then proceed directly to a supervised oral amoxicillin challenge without prior skin testing, consistent with current international guidance for low-risk cases. All challenges are conducted in a controlled clinical setting with immediate access to emergency treatment. The primary outcome is the delabelling rate, while secondary outcomes include safety (measured by frequency and severity of reactions), longitudinal impacts on MDRO acquisition, penicillin reuse, and quality of life over at least six months. An independent, international expert (randomization and safety monitor) will oversee the trial and halt/intervene the study if safety concerns arise. We hypothesize that PANDA will be non-inferior to standard-of-care in delabelling efficacy, with comparable safety and longitudinal outcomes. If successful, we are confident that PANDA can be implemented throughout Hong Kong and internationally, via collaboration with the Hospital Authority, and national/international societies. 背景： 青黴素為最常處方之藥物，亦為藥物「過敏」之常見成因，然經正式檢測後，約有九成被標記為青黴素過敏之個案實屬錯誤。此等錯誤標籤不僅導致病人預後欠佳，亦加重醫療體系負擔，更促使多重耐藥性微生物（MDRO）之產生。目前之標準評估程序係依據本地指引，主要由專科醫師執行。惟各地區對於過敏科專科醫師服務之可及性普遍有限，形成瓶頸，阻礙錯誤診斷之有效「除標」。鑑於最新區域性指引建議由護理人員主導青黴素過敏評估，本團隊擬進行此項研究，以提供確切實證，驗證由護理人員主導之直接激發測試，對於低風險青黴素過敏病人（依據本地HK-DADI及區域APAAACI指引之定義）之療效、安全性及長期影響。 目的： 進行一項前瞻性、隨機分派、頭對頭比較之非劣效性研究，旨在比較護理主導之直接激發測試與現行標準治療，應用於低風險青黴素過敏之情形，即所謂「護理評估後激發測試」（PANDA）。 主要指標： PANDA相較於標準治療在青黴素「除標」率方面之療效。 次要指標： 評估PANDA之安全性（以陽性反應之次數及嚴重程度為指標） 評估PANDA之長期影響（涵蓋多重耐藥性微生物之發生率、青黴素之重新使用情形及生活品質），追蹤期間不少於六個月 研究假說： PANDA在青黴素除標率方面不劣於標準治療，且安全性及長期影響亦屬相當。 研究設計／對象： 納入逾四百零八名病人，以隨機分配方式按一比一比例分為兩組（PANDA組二百零四人，標準治療組二百零四人），收案來源為香港兩所過敏中心。 介入措施： 標準治療組之病人依常規由醫師進行評估及青黴素激發測試，以達除標之目的。 PANDA組之病人則由受過培訓之護理人員依據國際建議所訂定之規範進行評估。經確認屬於「低風險」之病人，將接受受監督之青黴素激發測試，以進行除標。 資料分析： 比較PANDA組與標準治療組之主要及次要指標結果。本研究將委任外部專家擔任獨立安全監測員，若出現安全性疑慮，其有權暫停試驗進行。 預期成果： 相較於標準治療，經PANDA途徑評估之病人，其青黴素過敏除標率及安全性表現相當；同時在抗菌藥物管理及生活品質方面亦有所改善。本研究完成後，配合本團隊過往之經驗，我們有信心可將PANDA推展至全港及國際層面，並透過與醫院管理局及各國內外過敏醫學會之合作，落實此項服務。

17111526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17111526.value: G3PP 介導甘油分流於抑制代謝相關脂肪性肝炎所致肝細胞癌抗腫瘤免疫的影響

17111526.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17111526.value: Prof Feng, Yibin Prof Xian, Yanfang

17111526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111526.value: Metabolic-associated steatohepatitis (MASH)-driven hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is particularly characterised with its immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment (TME) driven by underlying metabolic dysregulation. However, the key immunometabolic mediator that facilitates this immune evasion remains poorly understood. Our pilot study performed an untargeted metabolomic analysis of HCC patients of different aetiologies, which revealed a dominant metabolic signature called glycerol shunt, an alternative pathway to produce glycerol, centred on the dysregulated pathways in patients with MASH-HCC. Spatial metabolomic analysis confirmed this signature, identifying reduced levels of intracellular glycerol-3-phosphate (Gro3P) and increased glycerol release as hallmarks of glycerol shunt in HCC tissues. Clinically, glycerol-3-phosphate phosphatase (G3PP), the speed-limiting enzyme involving glycerol shunt process, was uniquely and highly expressed in tumour cells of MASH-HCC, and was associated with shorter progression-free survival. Using an immunocompetent MASH-HCC mouse models, we found that G3PP overexpression potently accelerated tumour growth in vivo, whereas its genetic knockout suppressed tumour growth. Crucially, this protumour effect was entirely abrogated in T-cell-deficient mice, indicating that G3PP drives HCC progression in a T-cell-dependent manner. Single-cell RNA sequencing of tumours revealed that G3PP knockout remodelled the TME by expanding CD8+ cytotoxic T cells (CTLs) and shifting their differentiation from a terminally exhausted (Tex) state towards a progenitor exhausted (Ptex) phenotype. In vitro coculture models showed that G3PP-derived glycerol from HCC cells was sufficient to induce CD8+ T-cell exhaustion. Mechanistically, we found that glycerol uptake directly by T cells triggered intracellular calcium influx, leading to calcineurin activation, NFAT1 dephosphorylation, and the subsequent transcription of exhaustion-related genes. Chinese Medicine Magnolia officinalis-derived honokiol was identified as G3PP inhibitor by compound library screening, which can dose-dependently suppresses glycerol shunt in HCC cells in vitro and tumour growth in a mouse MASH-HCC model. With the literature review and our pilot study, we therefore hypothesize that G3PP is a novel immunometabolic checkpoint in MASH-HCC, where its induces a glycerol release from HCC cells, suppresses CD8+ T-cell immunity via the calcium/calcineurin/NFAT1 axis and hence promotes tumour progression. This proposal aims to (1) systematically evaluate the clinical significance and pathological function of the G3PP-induced glycerol shunt in mediating MASH-HCC progression; (2) investigate the role of the G3PP-induced glycerol shunt in limiting CD8+ T-cell antitumour immunity; (3) explore the mechanism by which the G3PP-induced glycerol shunt affects CD8+ T-cell exhaustion; and (4) identify honokiol as an adjuvant therapy for MASH-HCC. This work will establish a mechanistic basis for a transformative diagnostic and therapeutic strategy for MASH-HCC. 由代謝功能障礙相關脂肪性肝炎（MASH）引發的肝細胞癌（HCC）對抗PD-1（aPD1）免疫治療反應不佳，但其潜在機制尚不明確。我們對患者樣本及MASH-HCC模型的初步多組學分析鑒定出一個顯著的代謝特徵：由G3PP（甘油-3-磷酸磷酸酶）介導的甘油分流途徑，表現爲甘油-3-磷酸（Gro3P）减少而甘油升高。臨床上，G3PP高表達與非病毒性HCC的不良預後特异性相關。在功能上，儘管調控G3PP在體外不影響HCC細胞生長，但其過表達顯著加速、基因敲除則抑制了免疫健全MASH-HCC小鼠的腫瘤生長，而在T細胞缺陷小鼠中無此效應，提示其具有免疫調節作用。 在機制上，單細胞測序和共培養分析表明，G3PP驅動的腫瘤細胞甘油釋放可在腫瘤微環境中誘導CD8+ T細胞耗竭。具體表現爲終末耗竭T細胞（TCF1⁻PD1hi）與前體耗竭T細胞（TCF1⁺PD1int）的比例增加。轉錄組學和生化研究顯示，CD8+ T細胞攝取甘油後會抑制PI3K/Akt/β-catenin/TCF1信號軸，而該通路是維持T細胞幹性和效應功能的關鍵。此外，我們發現中藥活性成分和厚樸酚（源自厚樸）是一種强效且直接的G3PP抑制劑。和厚樸酚治療可抑制甘油分流、减輕CD8+ T細胞耗竭，幷在MASH-HCC模型中顯著抑制腫瘤生長。 基于上述發現，我們提出假說：G3PP誘導的甘油分流通過代謝抑制PI3K/Akt/β-catenin/TCF1軸，驅動CD8+ T細胞耗竭，從而促進MASH-HCC進展；而靶向該通路的和厚樸酚可恢復抗腫瘤免疫幷提高免疫治療療效。本課題擬：1）系統闡明G3PP在MASH-HCC中的臨床意義及其驅動的代謝重編程；2）揭示G3PP來源的甘油損害CD8+ T細胞免疫的作用；3）解析從甘油攝取到T細胞耗竭的詳細分子級聯反應；4）評估和厚朴酚作爲新型輔助療法增强MASH-HCC對aPD1應答的潜力。本研究將揭示MASH-HCC中一種新型代謝-免疫檢查點，幷爲克服這一日益高發癌症的免疫治療耐藥性提供具有轉化前景的策略。

17111926.value: TLR4-M細胞軸在活體肝移植術後侵襲性真菌感染中的腸黏膜免疫調控機制
