17111926.value: Prof Chen, Zhiwei Prof Man, Kwan Nancy Dr Wong, Cho Lam Tiffany

17111926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111926.value: Invasive fungal infection (IFI) is a devastating complication of liver transplantation, with mortality rates reaching 70%. Living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) is the major type of transplantation in Hong Kong, is more prone to gut-derived IFI due to the smaller graft size which could induce more severe intestinal mucosal injury. However, the risk factors and mechanisms remain unclear. We preliminarily found a 17.9% incidence of post-LDLT IFI in our local cohort, predominantly invasive candidiasis (93%). The occurrence of IFI significantly reduced patient survival and elevated the rates of short-term complications, indicated by elevated serum creatinine and urea, as well as the Clavien-Dindo score. Additionally, reduced-size (GRWR<0.8%) grafting was identified as an independent risk factor. In a rat model of liver transplantation with Candida albicans colonization, reduced-size grafts increased the IFI rate and mortality. Histological analysis revealed specific damage to the follicle-associated epithelium (FAE), characterized by a 50% reduction in Microfold cells (M cells) and disrupted tight junctions. Functionally, antibody-mediated M cell depletion in healthy animals increased their susceptibility to IFI, confirming the protective role of M cells in safeguarding the gateway from gut-derived IFI. Mechanistically, we observed a significant transcriptional upregulation of Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) within the FAE of the reduced-size liver transplantation subgroup. TLR4 knockout significantly decreased IFI incidence, preserved FAE integrity, and maintained M cell population. Specifically, an increase of CD8+ T cell infiltration was revealed in the wild-type, but its population was diminished after TLR4 knockout, suggesting that reduced-size graft injury triggered a TLR4-mediated autoimmune response that disrupted the M cell-associated mucosal immunological barrier against IFI. However, in-depth investigation for the interaction between M cell and TLR4-related immune microenvironment is warranted for the development of novel diagnostic marker and therapeutic strategy. This project aims to: 1) comprehensively analyze the clinical liver transplant data to define IFI risk factors; 2) characterize the mucosal immune atlas and gut-liver axis communication in post-transplant gut-derived IFI; and 3) explore TLR4-M cell-related mucosal immunological mechanisms and the therapeutic strategies. Elucidating the TLR4/M-cell axis will provide a foundation for understanding the mucosal immunology during gut-derived IFI, as well as for developing novel diagnostics and interventions to prevent life-threatening infections in transplant recipients. 侵襲性真菌感染是肝臟移植術後極為嚴重的併發症，可引起70%的致死率。香港的活體肝臟移植由於使用減體積的肝臟可導致更嚴重的腸粘膜損傷，從而對腸源性真菌感染更為易感。但其中的特定危險因素和致病機制尚不清楚。 我們前期發現香港本地活體肝移植隊列中侵襲性真菌感染發生率為17.9%，其中約93%為侵襲性念珠菌病。侵襲性真菌感染的發生使得病患短期併發症明顯增加而生存期顯著縮短，主要表現為血清肌酐和尿素水平與併發症Clavien-Dindo評分升高。另外我們發現小體積供肝（供肝體重比小於0.8%）的使用是獨立危險因素。我們在大鼠中建立了肝臟移植手術後白色念珠菌腸道定植的動物模型，發現減體積供肝可引起侵襲性真菌感染發生率和總死亡率的升高。組織學分析顯示，發生腸源性真菌感染的動物腸濾泡上皮損傷加重，表現為約50%的微皺褶（M）細胞減少和細胞間緊密連接缺失。進一步通過特異性抗體阻斷M細胞生成實驗證明了M細胞減少可直接引起腸源性真菌感染發生率升高，從而證實了M細胞在保護腸源性真菌感染中的關鍵作用。 機制研究顯示，在減體積肝移植動物的腸濾泡上皮中的Toll樣受體4（TLR4）的轉錄水平顯著升高。而基因敲除TLR4可顯著降低侵襲性真菌感染的發生率，並維持了M細胞數量和腸濾泡上皮的完整性。在黏膜免疫方面，我們發現發生腸源性真菌感染的動物中CD8+T細胞明顯增多，而在TLR4敲除後又減少，表明減體積肝移植可能誘發TLR4介導的腸黏膜自身免疫，進而導致M細胞相關的腸屏障功能障礙。而進一步研究M細胞與TLR4分子相關的腸黏膜免疫微環境之間的相互作用對於研發新型診斷標誌物和治療策略至關重要。 因此，該項目旨在：1.全面分析臨床肝移植術後侵襲性真菌感染的特異性危險因素，2.解析腸黏膜免疫特征與腸肝軸互作在移植後腸源性真菌感染中的作用機制，3.探索TLR4-M細胞相關黏膜免疫機制的轉化潛質。深度闡釋TLR4-M細胞軸將為理解腸源性真菌感染的黏膜免疫調控機制提供理論基礎，並為開發新型診斷標誌物和探索新型治療策略提供思路，最終可極大優化移植病患的併發症預防與診治。

17112326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17112326.value: 远端创伤诱导的神经元自噬对果蝇行为改变及创伤愈合的影响

17112326.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17112326.value: Prof Chang, Raymond Chuen Chung Prof Cheung, Martin Chi Hang Prof Hirano, Yukinori

17112326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17112326.value: Wound-healing mechanisms following skin injuries, such as severe punctures, are crucial for maintaining physiological balance. Because the skin is the primary barrier protecting organisms from environmental threats, defects in wound healing can lead to a range of pathological conditions, from infection to death. Whereas local cellular processes at the wound site, including clot formation and inflammation, are well characterized, the systemic inter-organ communication that coordinates wound repair remains unclear. In particular, there is limited understanding of the brain's role in wound healing, as a master organ governing systemic homeostasis and behavior. Surprisingly, our established Drosophila injury model with a puncture wound in the thoracic cuticle showed robust induction of autophagy, a cellular process that degrades cytoplasmic organelles, specifically in brain neurons. A distal wound rapidly activated neuronal autophagy, which was initiated within 5 minutes. Furthermore, neuronal autophagy was required to trigger behavioral changes, such as repeated proboscis extension/retraction and reduced leg movement. These behavioral changes were beneficial to proper wound healing and the survival of injured flies. Our preliminary results are striking because they strongly support a novel concept: rapid neuronal autophagy in the brain controls distant wound-healing processes through behavioral changes. However, the detailed mechanisms of (i) how a distant wound triggers neuronal autophagy, (ii) how neuronal autophagy changes behavior, and (iii) how autophagy-dependent behavioral changes promote wound healing remain to be elucidated. We will leverage our Drosophila model to investigate the fundamental mechanisms underlying the crosstalk among a distal wound, neuronal autophagy, and behavioral changes. Objective 1 will determine functions of wound-driven factors that rapidly trigger neuronal autophagy in the brain, and examine the roles of pain sensation and oxidative stress in the induction of neuronal autophagy. In Objective 2, we will investigate the targets of autophagic degradation and their functions in behavioral changes, and focus on the endoplasmic reticulum and vesicles containing neurotransmitters, putative autophagic targets that regulate neuronal activity. Objective 3 will elucidate the effects of behavioral changes on innate immune cell recruitment at the wound site, stimulating clot formation. The proposed research will elucidate a critical axis of inter-organ communication, which is essential for survival following injury. In particular, we will characterize wound-induced neuronal autophagy as a novel and rapid signaling mechanism that modulates brain function and regulates organismal homeostasis. These findings will provide new insights into the integration of nervous and immune responses to tissue damage. 皮肤遭受严重穿刺伤等损伤后的伤口愈合机制，对于维持生理平衡至关重要。皮肤是保护机体免受环境威胁的主要屏障，因此伤口愈合过程中的缺陷可能导致一系列病理状况，轻则引发感染，重则危及生命。尽管人们对伤口局部的细胞过程（如血栓形成和炎症反应）已有深入了解，但协调伤口修复的系统性器官间通讯机制尚不明确。特别值得注意的是，作为调控机体稳态与行为的统领性器官，大脑在伤口愈合中发挥着何种作用，目前人们对此知之甚少。 令人惊讶的是，我们建立的果蝇胸部表皮刺伤模型显示，大脑神经元中发生了强烈的自噬诱导——这是一种降解细胞质细胞器的细胞过程。远端伤口能迅速激活神经元自噬，且该过程在5分钟内即被启动。此外，神经元自噬对于触发某些行为改变（如反复伸缩口器和腿部活动减少）至关重要；这些行为改变有利于伤口的有效愈合及受损果蝇的存活。我们的初步结果十分引人注目，因为它们有力地支持了一个新颖的观点：大脑中的快速神经元自噬通过改变行为来调控远端伤口的愈合过程。然而，以下具体机制尚待阐明：(i) 远端伤口如何触发神经元自噬；(ii) 神经元自噬如何改变行为；以及 (iii) 依赖于自噬的行为改变如何促进伤口愈合。 我们将利用果蝇模型，探究远端伤口、神经元自噬与行为改变之间相互作用的潜在基本机制。目标1旨在明确那些能迅速诱导脑内神经元自噬的伤口相关因子的功能，并考察痛觉及氧化应激在诱导神经元自噬过程中的作用。在目标2中，我们将研究自噬降解的靶标及其在行为改变中的功能，重点关注内质网和含有神经递质的囊泡——这两者是调节神经元活动的潜在自噬靶标。目标3将阐明行为改变如何影响伤口部位的固有免疫细胞募集，进而促进血凝块的形成。 拟议研究将阐明一条关键的器官间通讯轴，该轴对于损伤后的生存至关重要。具体而言，我们将揭示创伤诱导的神经元自噬是一种调节脑功能及机体稳态的新型快速信号传导机制。这些发现将为理解针对组织损伤的神经与免疫反应的整合机制提供新见解。

17113126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17113126.value: 針對接受非共軛反義寡核苷酸 AHB-137 治療者以反應為導向且序貫使用 聚乙二醇化干擾素 𝛼 的療法：一項開放標籤的 II 期臨床研究

17113126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17113126.value: Prof Cheung, Ka Shing Michael Prof Seto, Wai Kay Walter Prof Yuen, Richard Man Fung

17113126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17113126.value: Chronic hepatitis B infection (CHB) cannot be cured by current therapies due to viral persistence and associated immune alterations, with a number of new treatments being developed. Antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) is a class of compound that targets a specified sequence of viral transcripts and induce their degradation by host cellular mechanisms to inhibit the virus. Bepirovirsen is an example of unconjugated ASO, which is the only drug that has entered phase III clinical trials based on the favourable data to induce hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) seroclearance in 9-10% recipients. AHB-137 is a more potent ASO with superior preclinical and clinical antiviral efficacy compared to bepirovirsen, achieving HBsAg seroclearance in ~70% recipients in an ongoing phase II trial. While PEG-IFN-alpha is an approved treatment for CHB, it has not been widely utilized, despite its potential to sustain HBsAg seroclearance in bepirovirsen recipients. The strategy of response-guided sequential PEG-IFN-alpha following ASO knockdown of HBsAg should be explored to enhance functional cure. We propose to conduct a single-center, prospective, investigator-initiated, open-label, phase II clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of AHB-137 with response-guided sequential PEG-IFN-alpha in 165 patients with chronic hepatitis B infection on stable oral antiviral therapy. The study is composed of two phases. The first phase (week 1 to week 24) involved 24 weeks of weekly subcutaneous injection with 300mg AHB-137 which is an unconjugated ASO. The second phase (week 25 to week 72) begins after completing 24 weeks of AHB-137, which adopts a response-guided approach of PEG-IFN-alpha dosing (none, 12 weeks or 24 weeks). Oral antiviral therapy will be maintained throughout unless specific cessation criteria is met to assess for functional cure. Research-related investigations include peripheral blood for virological biomarkers, peripheral blood mononuclear cells, and liver biopsy at baseline and week 48. The findings from this study will be potentially practice-changing to become the optimal strategy to boost functional cure to reach 60% in chronic hepatitis B infection. Patients will be able to achieve finite therapy, can stop their long-term antiviral agent, and significantly reduced risk of liver cancer and liver cirrhosis from achieving functional cure. The project will provide solid scientific basis to catalyse drug development and ultimately influence treatment strategies.

17113626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17113626.value: 靶向 CENP-A 在肝細胞癌表觀遺傳矯正及藥物開發中的作用 - 治療機制與精準模型建構

17113626.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17113626.value: Dr Lee, Nikki P Prof LO, Kenneth Kam-Wing Prof Man, Kwan Prof Sung, Wing Kin Prof Wang, Weiping

17113626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17113626.value: [Rationale] Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common liver cancer globally, characterized by high mortality rates due to ineffective treatments. Current targeted therapies - a main type of personalized treatment - aim to correct specific genetic deregulations in tumors to suppress tumorigenesis, but they benefit only a limited number of patients. The high genetic diversity of tumors complicates treatment options. This highlights the need for new drug classes that can target alternative deregulations critical to HCC. This research aims to increase the number of patients who can be treated effectively. [Background] HCC exhibits significant epigenetic deregulation, presenting a therapeutic opportunity through epigenetic correction to address its root causes. [Problem] However, there are currently no drugs specifically designed for epigenetic correction in HCC. Existing epigenetic drugs (epi drugs) tend to have broad-spectrum effects and are not targeted. [Solution] In this drug development program, we focused on a novel therapeutic strategy to suppress a specific epigenetic regulator, CENP-A (centromere protein A), which is critical in HCC. This approach aims to achieve robust and targeted epigenetic correction. Our evidence (prognostic/pathological/biological/functional/phenotypic) supports CENP-A as a promising drug target. This proposal will validate this hypothesis through pharmacodynamics studies and generate data to prepare clinical deployment. The effectiveness of CENP-A suppression will be assessed via examining treatment efficacy using clinically relevant experimental models. The safety and specificity of CENP-A suppression will be evaluated through mechanism of action analysis in a chromatin biology- and epigenetics-focused approach. Additionally, we will compare the effectiveness and specificity of CENP-A suppression with existing epi drugs and first-line HCC drug to determine its therapeutic usefulness. [Deliverables/Impact/Potential] This research aims to elucidate the novel mechanism of action of CENP-A suppression, contributing valuable insights into epigenetics. It will support the development of a first-in-class epi drug for robust and targeted epigenetic correction, potentially replacing the use of existing epi drugs with higher specificity. This innovative drug will address previously untargeted disease mechanisms, complement existing HCC drugs, and increase patient eligibility for drug treatment, ultimately transforming therapeutic practices. It will particularly benefit advanced-stage patients with CENP-A overexpression by achieving tumor control, enhancing quality of life with minimal side effects, and improving prognosis. Additionally, this approach enhances the cost-efficiency of healthcare systems, especially in high HCC incidence regions like the Asia-Pacific including Hong Kong. It also has potential applications across various cancers, given that CENP-A overexpression is found in over 44% of cases. 為解決肝細胞癌（HCC）藥物療效有限且作用短暫的問題，需要開發具不同治療機制的新藥。在本藥物開發計劃中，我們採用多模式方法（臨床／生物學／功能／表型／機制），鑑定出表觀遺傳調控因子 CENP-A（著絲粒蛋白 A），作為用於矯正 HCC 表觀遺傳異常的新候選治療靶點。基於以下事實：（一）HCC 是一種表觀遺傳疾病，而現有 HCC 藥物並非針對表觀遺傳矯正；（二）我們的數據顯示 CENP-A 是 HCC 的關鍵表觀遺傳調控因子；（三）表觀遺傳藥物作用範圍廣泛；我們假設，抑制單一靶點 CENP-A 以矯正表觀遺傳異常，可能較現有表觀遺傳藥物更具特異性。此方法可能較現有 HCC 藥物更有效，並可透過阻斷腫瘤替代性存活途徑而提高藥物敏感性。 透過整合跨學科團隊（臨床／癌症生物學／機制／臨床前研究）的專長與資源，以及目前正在進行的一線 HCC 藥物樂伐替尼臨床試驗，我們將產生 CENP-A 抑制治療 HCC 的臨床前數據，以驗證上述假設。我們將以 HCC 細胞株（體外及體內）及具臨床相關性的 HCC 患者來源腫瘤類器官（在有／無樂伐替尼治療下；離體）作為研究平台，並以可誘導式 RNA 干擾系統抑制 CENP-A，以模擬人類癌症及基因治療。 在目標一中，我們將透過闡明作用機制，鑑定受 CENP-A 抑制影響的關鍵分子及終點效應，作為臨床試驗的藥效學（pharmacodynamic）生物標誌物。為進一步鞏固我們關於 CENP-A 抑制可透過鐵死亡誘導細胞死亡這一新發現的數據，我們將研究染色質重塑及基因轉錄程序調控，並評估其對腫瘤表型和功能的終點效應，以釐清相關機制。 在目標二中，我們將產生可靠的療效數據，支持將 CENP-A 抑制用作單一治療及聯合治療。我們會把其治療結果的成效（抑制腫瘤的效能和存活率）及特異性（靶內及脫靶的分子效應），與用於 HCC 臨床試驗的表觀遺傳藥物及現有 HCC 藥物作比較，並研究其對 HCC 藥物的增敏作用。 本研究將揭示 CENP-A 抑制如何矯正 HCC 的表觀遺傳失調。了解 CENP-A 抑制的特性，將支持利用這種基因治療方法，針對 HCC 中 CENP-A 過度表達的根本原因。鑑於超過 44% 的人類癌症存在 CENP-A 過度表達，此策略極具應用於多種癌症的潛力。

17113826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17113826.value: EV-A71 3C蛋白酶介導ISG15裂解以拮抗宿主抗病毒反應的分子機制研究

17113826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17113826.value: ISGylation, mediated by the ubiquitin-like protein ISG15 through a cascade involving E1 (UBE1L), E2 (UBCH8), and E3 (HERC5) enzymes, modifies both host and viral proteins to inhibit viral replication and enhance immune responses. ISG15 exists in conjugated, free, and secreted forms, each contributing to immune regulation, including activation of sensors like MDA5 and IRF3. It also impairs viral proteins’ functions, such as influenza NS1 and HPV capsid proteins, disrupting viral assembly and immune evasion. EV71, a virus causing hand, foot, and mouth disease, encodes a 3C protease critical for immune evasion. This protease cleaves key immune molecules and disrupts inflammatory signaling pathways, facilitating viral replication. Understanding these mechanisms offers potential for developing targeted antiviral therapies and vaccines to combat EV71 and other viral infections. We identified EV-A71 3C protease suppresses ISGylation. Using immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry, our study showed that the 3C protease, especially the catalytically inactive mutant 3C-C147A, binds strongly with ISG15, suggesting that 3C binds to and degrades ISG15. Co-immunoprecipitation confirmed this interaction, and Western blotting demonstrated that EV-A71 3C protease degrades ISG15 in a dose-dependent manner. Further experiments revealed that wild-type 3C, but not the inactive mutant, inhibits ISGylation. A deeper understanding of the interplay between EV-A71 3C and ISG15 is warranted, providing insights for potential therapeutic strategies targeting 3C and ISG15 and the potentially the related ISGylation pathway. In this proposal, we aim to elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which EV-A71 3C protease mediates the cleavage of ISG15 and modulates host immune responses. We will validate the cleavage of ISG15 by EV-A71 3C, identify the precise cleavage site on ISG15, and map the interaction interface between these two proteins. We will further confirm ISG15 cleavage within EV-A71-infected cells and conduct a comparative analysis of viral main proteases to understand specificity. Building on these findings, mechanistic insights will be explored to determine how 3C modifies ISG15 during viral replication, including potential ISG15 modification of 3C itself. The impact of cleaved or secreted ISG15 on EV-A71 replication and innate immunity will be assessed, alongside the influence of 3C on ISGylation, especially regarding conjugated ISG15. Furthermore, the study will investigate how ISG15 enhances the antiviral efficacy of rupintrivir, aiming to provide a comprehensive understanding of how EV-A71 manipulates host antiviral pathways through 3C-mediated ISG15 processing. Together, these studies will provide comprehensive insights into how EV-A71 employs 3C to counteract host antiviral defenses and may identify novel therapeutic targets. ISGylation 是一種由類泛素蛋白 ISG15 介導的蛋白質修飾過程，透過 E1（UBE1L）、E2（UBCH8）及 E3（HERC5）酵素所組成的級聯反應，將 ISG15 共價連接至宿主或病毒蛋白質，進而抑制病毒複製並增強宿主抗病毒免疫反應。ISG15 可分別以結合型、游離型及分泌型等形式存在，並在免疫調控中發揮多重功能，包括活化 MDA5 與 IRF3 等抗病毒訊號分子。此外，ISG15 亦可干擾多種病毒蛋白質的功能，例如流感病毒 NS1 蛋白及人類乳突病毒衣殼蛋白，從而影響病毒組裝、複製及免疫逃逸。腸病毒 A71 型（enterovirus A71, EV-A71）是引起手足口病及嚴重神經系統併發症的重要病原體，其編碼的 3C 蛋白酶在病毒複製與免疫逃逸過程中扮演關鍵角色。既有研究顯示，EV-A71 3C 蛋白酶可裂解多種宿主免疫相關分子，進而促進病毒複製。然而，EV-A71 3C 蛋白酶是否透過調控 ISG15 或 ISGylation 路徑來拮抗宿主抗病毒反應，目前仍有待深入釐清。 我們的前期研究發現，EV-A71 3C 蛋白酶可顯著抑制 ISGylation。透過免疫沉澱結合質譜分析，我們發現 3C 蛋白酶，尤其是催化失活突變體 3C-C147A，能與 ISG15 產生強烈交互作用，提示 3C 可能直接結合 ISG15 並介導其降解或裂解。進一步的共同免疫沉澱實驗亦確認了 EV-A71 3C 與 ISG15 之間的結合關係。這些結果支持 EV-A71 3C 蛋白酶可能透過靶向 ISG15，干擾 ISGylation 及相關抗病毒免疫路徑，從而協助病毒逃避免疫監控。本研究旨在闡明 EV-A71 3C 蛋白酶介導 ISG15 裂解並調控宿主抗病毒免疫反應的分子機制。我們將首先驗證 EV-A71 3C 對 ISG15 的裂解作用，鑑定 ISG15 上的精確裂解位點，並解析 3C 與 ISG15 之間的交互作用界面。接著，我們將進一步確認 EV-A71 感染細胞中 ISG15 的裂解情形，並透過比較不同病毒主蛋白酶對 ISG15 的作用，評估此一調控機制的特異性。基於上述結果，本研究將深入探討 3C 在病毒複製過程中如何調控 ISG15 的功能，包括 3C 本身是否可能受到 ISG15 修飾，以及此修飾對 3C 蛋白酶活性與病毒複製的影響。此外，我們亦將評估裂解型或分泌型 ISG15 對 EV-A71 複製及先天免疫反應的影響，並分析 3C 對整體 ISGylation，特別是結合型 ISG15 形成的調控作用。進一步地，本研究將探討 ISG15 是否能增強 3C 蛋白酶抑制劑 rupintrivir 的抗病毒效果，以評估其潛在治療應用價值。 綜上所述，本研究將系統性解析 EV-A71 如何透過 3C 蛋白酶介導 ISG15 降解與 ISGylation 調控，進而拮抗宿主抗病毒防禦。本研究成果不僅有助於深化對 EV-A71 免疫逃逸機制的理解，也可能為開發針對 EV-A71 感染的新型抗病毒策略與治療標的提供重要依據。

17113926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17113926.value: 預測首發性思覺失調長期臨床及功能的成果：延伸早期介入治療的隨機對照試驗的16年追蹤研究

17113926.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17113926.value: Dr Chan, Sherry Kit-wa Prof Chen, Eric Yu-hai Dr Hui, Christy Lai Ming Dr Lee, Edwin Ho-ming Dr Lui, Sai Yu Simon Prof Sham, Pak-Chung

17113926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17113926.value: Psychotic disorders are a group of severe mental illness which affects approximately 3% of the population and constitutes one of the leading causes of disability worldwide, incurring substantial healthcare expenditure and indirect societal cost. Evidence indicates superior effectiveness of early intervention (EI) for first-episode psychosis (FEP) on short-term outcome improvement than standard care. However, a significant proportion of FEP patients still experience persistent functional impairment even in the presence of symptom remission. There is limited prospective research examining long-term clinical and functional outcomes in FEP. Even fewer studies have evaluated the longitudinal trajectories of various symptom dimensions and psychosocial functioning in FEP samples on a longer-term basis. In particular, whether and to what extent the early-course symptom and functional trajectory patterns can enhance prediction of long-term outcomes remain to be clarified. Recently, an increasing body of research has assessed both clinician-based functional recovery and patient-based personal recovery in early psychosis. However, there is a paucity of long-term follow-up research on FEP simultaneously investigating both recovery constructs. To address the knowledge gap, in the current proposal, we will conduct a 16-year follow-up study of a randomized-controlled trial (RCT) on extended EI (3-year) for Chinese FEP patients in Hong Kong, which comprises multiple serial assessment time-points (namely at baseline, 6-month, 1-year, 2-year, 3-year, 12-year and 16-year of follow-up), to systematically examine a comprehensive range of illness outcomes encompassing various symptom dimensions, psychosocial functioning, subjective quality of life, relapse of psychotic episodes and risk behaviors, mortality, service utilization, and treatment characteristics. This is the longest follow-up study of post-RCT on extended EI for FEP. Specifically, we aim to evaluate rates and predictors of symptomatic remission, functional recovery and personal recovery at 16-year follow-up; to delineate longitudinal trajectories of various symptom dimensions and psychosocial functioning over 16 years; to identify early-course symptom and functional trajectory patterns and their predictive capacity on long-term clinical and functional outcomes; and to characterize relapse, self-harm, hospitalization, and treatment patterns over the study period. The study findings will facilitate identification of key therapeutic targets in the initial course of illness, and derivation of individual-based symptom-specific and functional trajectory patterns for risk stratification and more accurate outcome estimation, as well as development of sophisticated prediction models for long-term clinical and functional outcomes. This will in turn pave the way for future implementation of personalized psychiatric care in the framework of specialized EI service to enhance treatment outcomes of first-episode population. 思覺失調是一組嚴重精神疾病，約影響全球3%人口，亦是導致殘疾的主要原因之一，造成龐大的醫療開支及間接社會成本。研究顯示，針對首發性思覺失調的早期介入較常規治療更能改善短期成果。然而，即使症狀得到緩解，仍有相當比例的首發性思覺失調患者持續出現功能受損。目前針對首發性思覺失調長期臨床及功能成果的研究數量有限；而長期評估不同症狀及心理社會功能縱向軌跡的研究則更少。尤其是早期病情中的症狀及功能軌跡模式在多大程度上提升對長期成果的預測能力上仍有待釐清。近年來，越來越多研究同時關注由臨床人員角度出發的功能康復，以及由患者角度出發的個人康復。然而，長期追蹤研究中同時探討這兩種康復概念者仍然不足。 為填補上述知識缺口，本研究計劃將針對香港華人首發性思覺失調患者中進行一項有關延伸早期介入服務（三年）的隨機對照試驗的16年的追蹤研究。這項研究包含多個評估時間點，包括基線、6個月、1年、2年、3年、12年及16年的追蹤研究。本研究將系統地檢視一系列全面的疾病結果，包括不同症狀、心理社會功能、主觀生活質素、精神病復發、風險行為、死亡率、服務使用情況及治療情況。這將是目前針對首發性思覺失調的延伸早期介入治療隨機對照試驗中最長追蹤年期的研究。具體而言，本研究旨在評估患者在這16年其間的症狀緩解、功能康復及個人康復的比率及其成因；描繪16年間不同症狀及心理社會功能的縱向軌跡；識別早期症狀及功能軌跡模式，並評估其對長期臨床及功能結果的預測能力；以及描述研究期間精神病復發、自我傷害、住院及治療模式。研究結果將有助識別思覺失調早期病程中的關鍵治療目標; 建立個人化、症狀特異及功能相關的軌跡模式，以進行風險分層及更準確的成果估算，並發展更精細的長期臨床及功能成果預測模型。最終，本研究將為日後在專門早期介入服務框架下推行個人化精神科照護奠定基礎，從而改善首發性思覺失調患者的治療成果。

17114426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17114426.value: 胰高糖素樣肽-1受體激動劑類藥物在常染色體顯性多囊腎病患者中的應用

17114426.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17114426.value: Prof Bae, Kyongtae Tyler Prof Chan, Daniel Tak Mao

17114426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17114426.value: Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD) is the commonest monogenic kidney disease, resulting in end stage kidney failure and diminished quality of life. Real-world adoption of the only existing disease-modifying treatment is limited due to intolerance and cost. Abnormal lipid and glucose metabolism is a key feature in ADPKD patients identified by pre-clinical models. Metabolic syndrome accelerates kidney disease progression. There is mounting evidence of targeted metabolic reprogramming in slowing disease progression in ADPKD. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RA) mimic actions of incretin hormone GLP-1 and have been shown to reduce risk of clinically important kidney outcomes in patients with type II Diabetes. Studies using ADPKD mouse models showed semaglutide (a GLP-1 RA) delayed kidney cyst growth and reduced total kidney volume, the most sensitive prognostic biomarker for disease progression acceptable by overseas Regulatory Agencies in the United States and Europe. There is only one newly-started clinical trial of GLP-1 RA in patients with ADPKD registered on ClinicalTrials.gov to-date. As targeted metabolic reprogramming is one of the key therapeutic directions in ADPKD management, GLP-RA show great promise in ADPKD patients. Our study is an investigator-initiated, randomized, single-arm, open-label study. Eighty ADPKD patients with evidence of active disease progression or risk factors of disease progression will be prospectively recruited over 1 year from Genetic Kidney Disease clinics at Queen Mary Hospital. Eligible participants will be randomized to either injectable semaglutide plus standard of care, or standard of care alone in a 1:1 ratio. Intervention group will be started on semaglutide according to standard titration protocol. Clinical, anthropometric, laboratory assessment will be performed at baseline, weeks 4, 12, 24 and 52. Magnetic resonance imaging for height-adjusted total kidney volume (htTKV) will be performed at week 52 ± 4 weeks. The primary outcome is change in htTKV at week 52 from randomization in ADPKD patients using semaglutide compared to standard of care alone. Secondary outcomes include the difference in composite renal outcomes of estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) reduction ≥30%, kidney failure, all-cause mortality, change in eGFR, eGFR decline slope, change in anthropometric parameters at week 52 between intervention and control groups and the safety outcomes of semaglutide in ADPKD patients. Our study aims to show the clinical efficacy and safety of GLP-1 RA in ADPKD patients with evidence or at risk of rapid disease progression. With plausible scientific rationale and evidence, our study can potentially identify new treatment for ADPKD patients. 常染色體顯性多囊腎病（ADPKD）是最常見的單基因腎臟疾病，會導致末期腎衰竭及生活質量降低。由於耐受性問題和成本限制，現有唯一的疾病治療在實際應用中有限。臨床模型顯示，ADPKD患者的異常脂質與葡萄糖代謝是其一個關鍵特徵。代謝症候群會加速腎臟疾病的進展。越來越多的證據顯示，有針對性的代謝重編程能延緩ADPKD的疾病進展。胰高糖素樣肽-1受體激動劑（GLP-1 RA）模擬促胰素激素GLP-1的作用，已被證明能降低2型糖尿病患者腎臟衰退風險。ADPKD小鼠模型研究顯示Semaglutide（一種GLP-1 RA）能延緩腎臟囊腫生長並降低腎臟總體積（國際監管機構普遍接受的疾病進展預後生物標記）。目前在ClinicalTrials.gov註冊的針對ADPKD患者的GLP-1 RA新臨床試驗有限。由於有針對性的代謝重編程是ADPKD管理中的一個重要治療方向，GLP-1 RA在ADPKD患者中展現巨大潛力。我們的研究是一項隨機單臂開放標籤的研究。將在瑪麗醫院的遺傳腎病門診招募80名高風險的ADPKD患者，為期一年。符合資格的參與者將以1:1的比例被隨機分配至注射用Semaglutide加標準治療組，或僅接受標準治療組。干預組將按照標準漸增方案開始使用Semaglutide。基線、4週、12週、24週及52週時，將進行臨床、人體測量及抽血化驗評估。第52週（±4週）將進行磁共振成像評估身高調整的總腎體積（htTKV）。主要觀察指標是使用Semaglutide的ADPKD患者在第52週時的htTKV變化，與僅接受標準治療的對照組相比。次要觀察指標包括估算腎小球過濾率（eGFR）降低≥30%的綜合腎臟結果差異、腎衰竭、全因死亡率、eGFR變化、eGFR下降坡度、週52時干預組與對照組的身體測量參數變化，以及Semaglutide在ADPKD患者中的安全性。 本研究旨在證明GLP-1 RA在高風險的ADPKD患者中的臨床療效與安全性。憑藉合理的科學理論與證據，我們的研究有望為ADPKD患者帶來新的治療選擇。

17114526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17114526.value: 以深度學習超解像技術推進超低場心臟磁力共振成像

17114526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17114526.value: Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of death worldwide, accounting for ~17.9 million (32%) deaths each year. This necessitates effective, reliable and accessible imaging modalities for diagnosis and management. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) cine imaging is the gold standard for non-invasive, radiation-free and dynamic evaluation of cardiac anatomy and function with high inter-rater reliability. However, widespread clinical adoption of high-field (1.5/3Tesla) CMR and MRI in general is hindered by high costs and infrastructure requirements. The limited accessibility, especially in resource-constrained or remote settings, contributes to significant global health inequities. Ultra-low-field (ULF) MRI systems (<0.1T) present a promising solution, offering the potential for affordable and point-of-care cardiac imaging. Yet, current ULF MRI technologies face substantial technical limitations, including reduced signal-to-noise ratio, prolonged acquisition times and compromised spatial and temporal resolution, which diminish their clinical utility for cardiac applications and widespread adoption. Recent advances in deep learning (DL) powers a paradigm shift in MR image reconstruction and restoration at clinical high-field-strengths (1.5/3T). However, the integration of ULF MRI and DL techniques for cine CMR remains unexplored. Building on our pilot study using a shielding-free 0.05T ULF whole-body MRI scanner, which demonstrated effective noise reduction and improved spatial resolution in free-breathing 3D short-axis cine CMR images, this project seeks to address important remaining limitations such as lack of temporal enhancement and limited validation. We propose to develop and rigorously validate novel data-driven DL-based reconstruction and super-resolution (SR) methods tailored to the challenges of ULF cine CMR. Our approach will leverage a motion-guided 4D (3D+time) DL framework to reconstruct and enhance noisy, low-resolution, subsampled ULF cine data, aiming to reduce scan times and improving ULF image quality and diagnostic utility. The proposed model will be trained and optimised using synthetic ULF-like datasets derived from high-field MRI and systematic validated on first simulated ULF-like healthy and pathological data, then on real, in-vivo free-breathing 0.05T ULF whole-heart cine data acquired with our custom-built whole-body ULF MRI system. DL-enhanced ULF MRI will be rigorously evaluated through qualitative and quantitative analyses, comparing its reliability and image quality to gold-standard 3T clinical references across cardiac morphological and functional measures in heathy volunteers and patients. This project will address key barriers in ULF cine CMR, laying the foundation for rapid, high-quality CMR in diverse clinical settings, including point-of-care environments. Ultimately, we seek to extend the reach of cardiac imaging to underserved populations, paving the way for equitable cardiovascular care worldwide. 心血管疾病是全球最主要的死亡原因，每年約造成1,790萬人死亡，佔全球死亡人數約32%。因此，發展有效、可靠而且普及的心臟影像檢查技術十分重要。動態心臟磁力共振成像 (CMR cine) 能在無輻射情況下清晰觀察心臟結構及評估其跳動和功能，是臨床評估心臟的重要影像標準。然而，現時高場磁力共振 (1.5/3T MRI) 設備昂貴，並需要大型場地及專門基建，令不少資源有限或偏遠地區難以使用，造成醫療服務差距。 超低場磁力共振 (低於0.1T) 具有成本較低、設備要求較少及可作即場檢查等優勢，有望提升心臟影像檢查的普及程度。不過，現有超低場系統仍面對訊號較弱、掃描時間較長，以及影像空間和時間解像度不足等技術限制，影響其心臟臨床應用及普及。 本研究將建基於我們利用0.05T、毋須屏蔽的全身超低場磁力共振系統所進行的先導研究，進一步運用深度學習改善動態心臟影像。我們將開發一套以心臟運動資訊為導向的四維 (三維立體＋時間) 深度學習影像重建及超解像框架，從低訊噪比、低解像度及較少取樣的數據中重建更清晰、更連貫的動態心臟影像，目標是縮短掃描時間，同時提升影像質素及診斷價值。 模型將先利用高場MRI數據模擬超低場影像進行訓練及測試，包括正常及病理個案，再於我們自建的0.05T全身系統取得的自由呼吸動態心臟影像上驗證。研究亦會將深度學習增強後的超低場影像與臨床3T MRI作系統比較，評估心臟形態、功能及影像可靠性。 本研究有望突破超低場心臟磁力共振在速度和影像質素方面的限制，為快速、低成本及更普及的心臟檢查奠定基礎，長遠讓更多資源不足地區及基層醫療環境受惠，促進更公平的心血管醫療服務。

17115526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17115526.value: 乳酸鏈球菌素类抗菌肽之發掘與生物工程改造：抗藥性病原體的新剋星

17115526.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17115526.value: Prof Gao, Peng Dr Guo, Longcheng Prof Li, Jian

17115526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17115526.value: Discovery and Bioengineering of Nisin-like Antimicrobial Peptides to Combat Antibiotic-Resistant Pathogens The escalating crisis of antibiotic-resistant demands innovative therapeutic solutions. Nisin-like peptides (NLPs), a natural product class of ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs), especially those derived from complex microbiomes, represent a promising source of next-generation antibiotics. These peptide natural products offer a compelling combination of potent bactericidal activity, narrow-spectrum targeting, and a low historical incidence of resistance, positioning them as ideal candidates for combating antibiotic-resistant pathogens with minimal impact on commensal flora. This proposed research is powered by our established high-throughput discovery platform, which synergistically integrates AI-driven genome mining, cell-free peptide synthesis (CFPS), and bioassays. This pipeline enables the rapid translation of genetic blueprints from complex microbiota into functionally characterized antimicrobial compounds. Preliminary application of this platform has already uncovered a diverse repository of novel NLPs with confirmed antibacterial activity, providing a robust foundation for this proposal. We hypothesize that systematic mining and engineering of this NLP reservoir will yield lead candidates for narrow-spectrum anti-infectives or microbiome modulators. To test this, we will execute an integrated strategy to: 1. Discover Novel NLPs by expanding our high-throughput platform to screen hundreds of candidates from the complex microbiota. 2. Evaluate Therapeutic Efficacy by quantifying NLP potency against a panel of priority antibiotic-resistant pathogens through in vitro and animal model studies. 3. Optimize Pharmacological Properties through closed-loop design–build–test bioengineering to enhance metabolic stability, solubility, and in vivo potency. 4. Elucidate Mechanisms of Action by defining specific bactericidal targets and characterizing selective microbiome modulation. By creating a closed-loop cycle from computational prediction to experimental validation and optimization, this work will establish a versatile pipeline for antimicrobial discovery. The outcome will be a portfolio of optimized antimicrobial NLP candidates, offering a powerful, targeted strategy to address the antibiotic-resistant crisis. 抗生素耐藥性危機持續加劇，亟需發展具有全新作用機制、精準抗菌譜和低耐藥誘導風險的新型抗感染策略。乳酸鏈球菌素類肽（nisin-like peptides, NLPs）是一類重要的核糖體合成及翻譯後修飾環肽類天然產物（ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides, RiPPs），廣泛存在於複雜微生物群及其相關微生物基因組中。此類肽類天然產物兼具強效殺菌活性、窄譜靶向選擇性以及極低的耐藥發生率，使其成為抗擊抗生素耐藥病原體、同時最大限度降低對共生菌群干擾的理想候選分子。 本研究依託本團隊已建立的高通量 NLP 發現平台。該平台整合人工智慧驅動的基因組挖掘、無細胞蛋白／肽合成體系（cell-free protein synthesis, CFPS）以及生物活性篩選，實現了從複雜微生物群遺傳資訊到功能性抗菌分子驗證的快速轉化。前期研究已基於該平台發現並驗證了一批具有明確抗菌活性的新型 NLPs，為本項目進一步開展系統性挖掘、功能評價與分子優化奠定了堅實基礎。 本項目的核心假設是：複雜微生物群中蘊含大量尚未被開發的 NLP 分子資源，通過高通量發現與閉環式生物工程優化，可獲得兼具高效抗感染活性、優良藥理性質和選擇性微生物群調節功能的新型抗菌候選分子。圍繞這一假設，本研究擬開展以下工作： 一、新型 NLPs 的系統發現與資源庫構建 進一步拓展高通量發現平台，結合 AI 輔助基因組挖掘、序列特徵分析和 RiPP 生物合成基因簇識別，從複雜微生物群中系統篩選並構建數百個候選 NLP 分子庫。通過無細胞合成與初步活性篩選，快速獲得具有潛在抗菌活性的候選分子。 二、NLPs 抗耐藥病原體活性的定量評價 針對 MRSA、VRE 等重點多重耐藥病原體，開展體外抑菌、殺菌動力學、最低抑菌濃度（MIC）測定及抗菌譜分析。進一步利用動物感染模型評估候選 NLPs 的體內抗感染效力及初步安全性，為後續先導化合物篩選提供依據。 三、基於閉環「設計–構建–測試」流程的藥理性質優化 建立閉環式生物工程優化體系，通過計算設計、序列改造、結構優化和高通量功能驗證，迭代提升 NLPs 的代謝穩定性、水溶性、血清穩定性、組織分布特徵及體內藥效。 四、作用機制解析及微生物群選擇性調節功能表徵 闡明 NLPs 的殺菌機制及其分子靶標。進一步利用體外菌群模型及動物微生物群分析，解析其潛在微生物群調節功能。 本研究將構建一條的新型抗菌肽藥物發現與生物工程優化管線。預期將獲得一系列具有明確作用機制、優良藥理性質和精準抗菌活性的 NLP 候選分子，為開發下一代窄譜抗菌藥物及微生物群精準干預策略提供重要技術平台和分子基礎，並為緩解全球抗生素耐藥性危機提供新的解決方案。

17115626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17115626.value: 鉴定ACSL4是否通过富含CEACAM1的细胞外囊泡，在肝细胞癌肿瘤间质液中塑造免疫抑制的肿瘤微环境

17115626.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17115626.value: Prof Ng, Irene Oi Lin Dr Tian, Lu Dr Zhang, Vanilla Xin

17115626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17115626.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, particularly in China and Hong Kong, due to its high recurrence rates and resistance to conventional therapies, which are driven by the aggressive nature of liver cancer stem cells (LCSCs) and their complex interactions within the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). Current understanding of these interactions is limited, impeding the development of effective targeted and immunotherapeutic strategies. To address this gap, our study focuses on analyzing tumor interstitial fluid (TIF), which more accurately reflects the local tumor microenvironment than systemic blood samples, as it preserves non-cellular tumor-derived components often diluted in circulation. Our preliminary data from proteomic analyses of paired TIF and non-tumor interstitial fluid (NTIF) samples from our HCC patients have identified ACSL4 as a critical regulator associated with LCSC-related gene expression, tumor invasion, and immunosuppression. Notably, our preliminary data also show that ACSL4 correlates positively with cancer stemness marker expression and PD1 expression in the TCGA cohort. Knockdown of ACSL4 suppresses sphere formation. As demonstrated through spatial transcriptomics and through in vitro HCC knockdown cell models, and in vivo mouse models, ACSL4 is implicated in modulating T cell exhaustion and infiltration. These findings suggest that ACSL4 plays a dual role in promoting both liver cancer stemness and immunosuppression within the tumor microenvironment in HCC. Furthermore, we identified the secretion of CEACAM1-enriched small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) as a route for ACSL4 to inhibit anti-tumor T cell activity and promote an immunosuppressive niche in HCC. Building on these insights, our proposed research aims to elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which secretory ACSL4 influences CEACAM1 packaging into sEVs, assess the inhibitory effects of CEACAM1-positive sEVs on T cell functions, and evaluate the therapeutic potential of targeting ACSL4 and CEACAM1 to enhance immunotherapy efficacy in HCC, ultimately aiming to uncover novel immunomodulatory pathways and improve clinical outcomes. 由于肝细胞癌（hepatocellular carcinoma, HCC）复发率高和对常规治疗有抵抗性，其仍然是中国和香港，乃至全球與癌症相关死亡的主要原因之一。肝癌干细胞（liver cancer stem cells, LCSCs）的侵袭性特性及其在肿瘤免疫微环境（TIME）中的相互作用复杂。目前对这些相互作用的理解有限，阻碍了有效靶向及相关免疫治疗策略的开发。为弥补这一空白，我们集中研究分析肿瘤间质液（tumour interstitial fluid, TIF），因为當中肿瘤衍生的非细胞性成分未在体內循环中稀释，比全身血液样本更能准确反映局部肿瘤微环境的。我们对来自肝细胞癌患者的肿瘤间质液和非肿瘤间质液（NTIF）的配对样本进行蛋白质组学分析，初步发现ACSL4是与LCSC相关的基因表达、肿瘤侵袭和免疫抑制的关键调控因子。值得注意的是，我们的初步数据显示，ACSL4在TCGA数据集中与癌症干性标志物表达和PD1表达呈正相关。敲低ACSL4可以抑制肝癌细胞的成球能力。通过空间转录组学、体外HCC敲低细胞模型以及体内小鼠模型的研究表明，ACSL4涉及调节T细胞耗竭状态和浸润。这些发现表明，ACSL4在促进肝癌干性和肿瘤微环境中的免疫抑制方面具有双重作用。此外，我们还发现ACSL4通过富含CEACAM1的小型细胞外囊泡（small extracellular vesicles, sEVs）抑制抗肿瘤T细胞活性和促进免疫抑制微环境。基于这些发现，我们的研究旨在阐明分泌性ACSL4如何影响CEACAM1被包装入sEVs的分子机制，评估CEACAM1阳性sEVs对T细胞功能的抑制作用，以及评估靶向ACSL4和CEACAM1以增强HCC免疫治疗效果的潜力，最终旨在揭示新的免疫调节途径并改善临床治疗效果。

17115826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17115826.value: 利用先進成像技術研究合成脂質的細胞處理過程

17115826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17115826.value: In human physiology, lipid nutrients are efficiently transported and metabolized as nanosized lipoprotein particles, with cells having sophisticated systems to process these endogenous packages for energy, signaling, and storage. Modern medicine has ingeniously adopted this principle, creating packages with non-natural synthetic lipids that mimic lipoproteins for biomedical applications. However, introducing these non-natural lipid species into the cell’s complex metabolic network presents a fundamental biological challenge: how do cells process and metabolize these lipids, and what are the functional consequences? Numerous adverse effects have been reported in both clinical and preclinical studies, indicating a significant yet poorly understood disruption of cellular homeostasis. This research program addresses this critical knowledge gap by investigating the metabolic fate and biological impact of synthetic lipids. We aim to reveal where these lipids go at the organelle level, what these lipids do to cells that disrupts vital cellular processes. A key focus will be to determine how cells sense this disruption and process these lipids to restore homeostasis, thereby revealing potential strategies to mitigate adverse effects. We are uniquely positioned to address this challenge. Our lab has established a suite of advanced technologies, including unique imaging capabilities in correlative light, ion, and electron microscopy. This enables us to precisely track the subcellular journey of synthetic lipids at 50-nm resolution and high sensitivity, providing unprecedented insights into their cellular processing. Already, our innovative approaches have generated extensive high-quality preliminary data, revealing previously unknown aspects of the cellular and subcellular fate of synthetic lipids. Combined with molecular and genetic approaches, the goal of this proposal is to map their distribution, quantify their impact on organelle function, and identify the key cellular machinery responsible for their processing and detoxification. Ultimately, we will explore novel strategies that target these mechanisms for the safer use of synthetic lipids. The insights from this work will establish a new paradigm for understanding the biological interactions of lipids. By defining how these lipids disrupt and are handled by cellular systems, we will provide a foundational roadmap for designing safer and more effective synthetic lipid formulations for biomedical applications. This knowledge is essential for advancing treatments across a wide spectrum of human diseases, from genetic disorders to cancer and infectious diseases. 在人體生理學中，脂質營養物質以納米級脂蛋白顆粒的形式被高效運輸和代謝，細胞擁有複雜的系統來處理這些內源性顆粒，用於能量、信號傳導和儲存。現代醫學巧妙地借鑒了這一原理，利用非天然合成脂質製造模擬脂蛋白的顆粒，用於生物醫學應用。然而，將這些非天然脂質引入細胞複雜的代謝網絡帶來了一個根本性的生物學挑戰：細胞如何處理和代謝這些脂質，其功能後果是什麼？大量臨床和臨床前研究已報道了許多不良效應，表明細胞穩態受到了顯著但尚不清楚的破壞。 本研究計劃通過探究合成脂質的代謝命運和生物學影響來填補這一關鍵知識空白。我們旨在揭示這些脂質在細胞器水平上的去向，以及這些脂質對細胞產生了何種作用，從而擾亂重要的細胞過程。一個關鍵重點是確定細胞如何感知這種擾亂，並處理這些脂質以恢復穩態，從而揭示減輕不良效應的潛在策略。 我們在應對這一挑戰方面具有獨特優勢。我們的實驗室已建立了一套先進技術，包括在關聯光學、離子和電子顯微鏡方面的獨特成像能力。這使我們能夠以50納米分辨率和高靈敏度，精確追蹤合成脂質的亞細胞旅程，為其細胞處理過程提供前所未有的見解。我們的創新方法已經產生了大量高質量的初步數據，揭示了合成脂質在細胞和亞細胞水平命運中此前未知的方面。結合分子和遺傳學方法，本提案的目標是繪制其分布圖譜、量化其對細胞器功能的影響，並鑒定負責其處理和解毒的關鍵細胞機制。最終，我們將探索以這些機制為靶點的新策略，以實現合成脂質的更安全使用。 這項工作的見解將建立理解脂質生物學相互作用的新範式。通過闡明這些脂質如何擾亂細胞系統，以及如何被細胞系統處理，我們將為設計更安全、更有效的生物醫學應用合成脂質制劑提供基礎性路線圖。這一知識對於推進從遺傳疾病到癌症和傳染病等廣泛人類疾病的治療至關重要。

17115926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17115926.value: 探索氟化氨銀與唾液薄膜對抗牙齒酸蝕的雙重防禦作用

17115926.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17115926.value: Prof Chu, Chun Hung Prof Hannig , Matthias Prof Wang, John Junwen

17115926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17115926.value: Background Erosive tooth wear affects approximately 30%-50% of adults worldwide. It damages tooth enamel and exposes dentine, leading to hypersensitivity and irreversible tooth structure loss, which is difficult to restore. The current standard care for dental erosion using stannous chloride/amine fluoride/sodium fluoride(SNF) offers only limited protection and pain relief. Silver diamine fluoride(SDF) is a potent anti-hypersensitivity agent. Recent laboratory studies show that SDF can reduce erosive tooth damage by ~50% compared to standard treatment, owing to its synergistic interaction with the salivary pellicle—a natural protein layer that coats teeth and shields the tooth from acid attack. However, the precise mechanism of this interaction remains unclear. A comprehensive understanding of how SDF alters the pellicle's structure, composition, and function is essential for unlocking its full therapeutic potential and guiding the development of next-generation preventive strategies for dental erosion. Objectives This project aims to determine the multi-dimensional mechanism by which SDF interacts with salivary pellicle. The specific objectives are to: (1) analyze the structure and chemical composition of SDF-modified pellicle; (2) map its proteomic profile; and (3) evaluate its functional efficacy and stability as an anti-erosive barrier. Methods This study will use an in-situ model of human enamel blocks mounted on custom intraoral appliances worn by healthy participants. For each objective, pellicles formed on SDF-treated, SNF-treated and control enamel blocks will be analyzed as follows: 1. The ultrastructure of the pellicle will be assessed using transmission electron microscopy. The distribution and integration of silver and fluoride within the pellicle matrix will be analysed using energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy. 2. Harvested pellicles will be analysed using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry to identify and quantify differential protein expression and post-translational modifications. Bioinformatic analysis will be performed. 3. The in-situ-formed pellicle will be assessed for its functional efficacy as a barrier by quantifying the net mineral ion release across the pellicle during in vitro acid exposure using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry. The pellicle’s surface characteristics after acid exposure will be assessed using atomic force microscopy and scanning electron microscopy. Significance and implications This will be the first study to mechanistically link the structural, compositional, and functional properties of the SDF-modified pellicle. The findings will provide fundamental insights into its superior anti-erosive action, creating a foundation for refining clinical protocols to maximize protection by SDF. This knowledge will also guide the bio-inspired design of novel and effective preventive therapies for dental erosion. 酸蝕性牙齒磨耗影響全球約 30%–50% 的成年人。其會損害牙釉質並暴露牙本質，導致牙齒敏感及不可逆的牙體結構喪失，且難以修復。目前針對牙齒酸蝕的標準治療——氯化亞錫／胺氟化物／氟化鈉（SNF）——僅能提供有限的保護與疼痛緩解。氟化氨銀（SDF）是一種強效的抗敏感藥劑。近期實驗室研究顯示，與標準治療相比，SDF 可將酸蝕性牙齒損傷減少約 50%，這歸因於其與唾液薄膜之間的協同作用；唾液薄膜是一層覆蓋於牙齒表面的天然蛋白質層，可保護牙齒免受酸性侵蝕。然而，這種交互作用的確切機制仍不清楚。全面了解 SDF 如何改變唾液薄膜的結構、組成與功能，對於發揮其完整治療潛力，以及指導下一代牙齒酸蝕預防策略的發展至關重要。 本研究旨在闡明 SDF 與唾液薄膜相互作用的多面向機制。具體目標包括：（1）分析經 SDF 改變之唾液薄膜的結構與化學組成；（2）繪製其蛋白質體圖譜；以及（3）評估其作為抗酸蝕屏障的功能效能與穩定性。 本研究將採用原位模型，將人類牙釉質塊固定於健康受試者配戴的客製化口內裝置上。針對各研究目標，將分析形成於 SDF 處理、SNF 處理及對照組牙釉質塊上的唾液薄膜，方法如下： 將使用穿透式電子顯微鏡評估唾液薄膜的超微結構。並以能量色散 X 射線光譜分析銀與氟在薄膜基質中的分布及整合情形。 採集所得的唾液薄膜將以液相層析串聯質譜法進行分析，以鑑定並定量差異性蛋白質表現及轉譯後修飾，並進行生物資訊學分析。 將透過體外酸暴露期間，利用感應耦合電漿質譜法定量穿越唾液薄膜的淨礦物離子釋放量，以評估原位形成之唾液薄膜作為屏障的功能效能。酸暴露後的薄膜表面特性將使用原子力顯微鏡及掃描式電子顯微鏡進行評估。

17116126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17116126.value: 超聲響應性單原子修飾植入物催化表面實現適應性活性氧調控以增強生物膜清除和骨整合

17116126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17116126.value: Dr Guan, Shiwei Prof LIN, Sien Prof Liu, Xuanyong Prof Yeung, Kelvin Wai-Kwok

17116126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17116126.value: Titanium (Ti) and its alloys are the most widely used implantable materials, yet periprosthetic infection and insufficient osteointegration remain common causes of failure. Although antibacterial surface coatings have been explored, clinical management still relies on systemic antibiotics and invasive debridement. Antibiotic therapy is limited by subtherapeutic local drug levels, biofilm induced tolerance, and multidrug resistance, while debridement risks incomplete clearance or excessive tissue loss. Current surface modification strategies often lose efficacy over time and pose safety concerns as bound agents degrade. These limitations, together with the lack of implant surfaces capable of actively and dynamically regulating the osteoimmune microenvironment, highlight an urgent need for designs combining noninvasive antibacterial activity with adaptive immune modulation to improve osseointegration. Stimuli-responsive generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) is a validated route for rapid bacterial killing. We previously demonstrated that defect engineered titanium oxide honeycomb nanostructures produce ROS under 808 nm near-infrared (NIR) light to eliminate infection and, via unique topography, modulate macrophage polarization. However, shallow NIR penetration limits deep orthopaedic use, and passive topography mediated modulation cannot adapt to changing infection and healing stages. We propose a clinically translatable approach using therapeutic ultrasound (US) and a sensitizer free catalytic Ti surface to achieve noninvasive biofilm elimination together with adaptive osteoimmune regulation. We hypothesize that the high surface area of the honeycomb structures will anchor atomically dispersed bioessential metals (e.g., Fe-Co single atoms) as catalytic centers, enabling robust US-triggered ROS generation via oxidase- and peroxidase-like activities under infection mimicking conditions, followed by catalase- and superoxide dismutase-like activities to attenuate excess ROS once infection is cleared. This dynamic modulation is expected to coordinate macrophage phenotype transitions and enhance osseointegration. Preliminary data show ROS output can be tuned by single-atom sites and amplified by US stimulation, supporting the feasibility of the proposed approach. We propose the following specific aims: (1) to fabricate an US-responsive, sensitizer free surface with atomically dispersed single atoms and characterize its physicochemical and sonocatalytic properties; (2) to achieve noninvasive elimination of biofilms, re-infection, and dynamically modulate ROS levels to direct osteoimmunomodulation in vitro; and (3) to comprehensively evaluate in vivo antibacterial efficacy and osseointegration outcomes using a biofilm implant infection animal model. 17116226.value: 靶向 ADAT2 介導之 tRNA A-to-I 編輯以干擾肝細胞癌之絲胺酸/甘胺酸/單碳代謝

17116226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17116226.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, characterized by limited treatment options and poor prognosis due to late diagnosis and therapy resistance. This underscores the urgent need to develop novel therapeutic strategies. Beyond genetic mutations, epigenetic alterations play critical roles in HCC development, with RNA modifications emerging as key regulators of translation and cellular function in cancer. Transfer RNAs (tRNAs) are essential for protein synthesis, and their function is modulated by post-transcriptional modifications, including adenosine-to-inosine (A-to-I) editing at the wobble position mediated by ADAT2. This editing expands codon recognition and influences translation efficiency; however, its role in HCC remains unclear. Our preliminary data reveal that ADAT2 is frequently upregulated in HCC tissues and correlates with aggressive tumor features. Functional studies show that ADAT2 knockdown reduces HCC cell proliferation, colony formation, migration, and metastasis both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, ADAT2-mediated A-to-I editing is critical for the efficient translation of proteins enriched in inosine-dependent codons. Notably, ADAT2 is essential for the translation of key enzymes in the serine/glycine/one-carbon (SGOC) metabolic pathway, which supports nucleotide synthesis, methylation, and redox balance, which are vital for tumor growth. To address knowledge gaps regarding the role of ADAT2 role in HCC, we propose three research objectives: (1) characterize ADAT2 expression and its impact on tRNA A-to-I editing in human HCC samples; (2) define how ADAT2 regulates the SGOC metabolic network at the translational level and its effects on metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming in HCC; and (3) develop novel small-molecule inhibitors targeting ADAT2 and assess their anti-tumor efficacy alone and in combination with tyrosine kinase inhibitors. This study aims to elucidate the mechanistic role of ADAT2 in translational control and metabolic reprogramming in HCC, establishing it as a prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target. By integrating molecular biology, metabolomics, epigenetics, and drug discovery, our work seeks to uncover new vulnerabilities in HCC and advance targeted therapies to improve patient outcomes. 肝細胞癌（HCC）是全球癌症相關死亡的主要原因之一，其治療選擇有限，且因晚期診斷與治療抗性導致預後不佳，凸顯了開發新型治療策略的迫切需求。除了基因突變之外，表觀遺傳變異在肝癌發展中扮演關鍵角色，其中RNA修飾作為翻譯調控與癌細胞功能的重要調節因子日益受到重視。 轉運RNA（tRNA）是蛋白質合成不可或缺的分子，其功能受到轉錄後修飾的調控，包括由ADAT2介導、發生於反密碼子擺動位置的腺苷轉肌苷（A-to-I）編輯。此編輯能拓展密碼子識別範圍並影響翻譯效率，然而其在肝癌中的角色仍不清楚。我們的初步數據顯示，ADAT2在肝癌組織中經常上調，且與侵襲性腫瘤特徵相關。功能性研究證實，無論在細胞實驗或動物模型中，降低ADAT2表現均可抑制肝癌細胞的增殖、群落形成、遷移與轉移。機制上，ADAT2所介導的A-to-I編輯對於富含肌苷依賴性密碼子的蛋白質之高效翻譯至關重要。尤其值得注意的是，ADAT2對絲胺酸/甘胺酸/單碳（SGOC）代謝路徑中關鍵酵素的翻譯是必需的，該路徑支援核苷酸合成、甲基化及氧化還原平衡，為腫瘤生長所仰賴。 為填補ADAT2在肝癌中角色之知識缺口，我們提出三項研究目標：（1）於人類肝癌檢體中，描繪ADAT2的表現及其對tRNA A-to-I編輯的影響；（2）釐清ADAT2如何在轉譯層次上調控SGOC代謝網絡，以及其對肝癌代謝與表觀遺傳重塑的作用；（3）開發靶向ADAT2的新型小分子抑制劑，並評估其單獨使用及與酪胺酸激酶抑制劑聯合使用的抗腫瘤效果。 本研究旨在闡明ADAT2於肝癌轉譯調控與代謝重塑中的機制角色，將其確立為預後生物標記及治療標靶。透過整合分子生物學、代謝體學、表觀遺傳學與藥物開發，我們的工作將揭示肝癌的新弱點，並推進標靶治療以改善患者預後。

17116326.value: 人工智能驅動的抗牙齦炎代謝物從頭發現與功能驗證

17116326.label: Co - Investigator(s)

17116326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17116326.value: Background and Rationale Gingivitis and periodontitis are pervasive global health issues, closely linked to systemic diseases like diabetes and cardiovascular conditions. Current treatments, primarily mechanical debridement and antibiotics, often fail to sustainably correct microbial imbalance, leading to high recurrence rates and exacerbating antibiotic resistance. This underscores an urgent need for precise, ecology-friendly therapies that simultaneously modulate host inflammation and pathogenic microbes. Our team has pioneered the development and multi-omics analysis of the clinical gingivitis retrogression-progression model. Through longitudinal multi-omics investigations, we have identified 572 inflammation-associated metabolites after curation, and developed a high-throughput screening platform driven by single-cell Ramanomics technology coupled with a deep learning model (GINEConvNet) that achieves 92.7% accuracy in classifying anti-inflammatory metabolites based on chemical structures. Aim This project aims to discover and validate novel anti-gingivitis metabolites by establishing and integrating a transformative discovery pipeline that combines deep mechanistic investigation, high-throughput functional screening, and AI-powered prediction, ultimately delivering new therapeutic candidates for precise oral inflammatory disease management. Objectives 1. Establishment of a Validation Technology Platform for Core Functional Anti-inflammatory Metabolites and Exemplar Validation 2. High-Throughput Functional Validation of Anti-inflammatory Metabolites 3. AI Model-Driven Prediction, Discovery, and Validation of Novel Compounds Methodology We will employ an integrated experimental-computational strategy. Mechanistic studies will use an in vitro host-microbe co-culture model analyzed via single-cell Ramanomics, transcriptomics, and metabolomics. High-throughput functional screening of candidate metabolites will utilize our established FlowRACS platform and a quantitative Ramanomic Index of Metabolic Stress (RIMS). The AI component will involve training and optimizing our GINEConvNet model on experimental data to perform virtual screening, with top AI-predicted candidates validated in vitro and in a mouse periodontitis model. Expected Results We expect to deliver a fully validated AI-powered discovery pipeline, a core set of functionally verified anti-gingivitis metabolites, and novel AI-predicted lead compounds with demonstrated efficacy. The established platform and discovered compounds will provide a strong foundation for developing next-generation, non-antibiotic oral care formulations and targeted therapeutics. Significance and Impact This research will directly benefit patients by paving the way for more effective and precise treatments for gingivitis and periodontitis. It will also provide clinicians with new therapeutic strategies and offer oral care industries novel lead compounds. By enabling a shift away from broad-spectrum antibiotics, the project contributes to combating antimicrobial resistance. In the long term, reducing the burden of oral inflammation can lower the associated risks of systemic diseases, improving public health and reducing healthcare costs. 背景與理據 牙齦炎與牙周炎是普遍的全球健康問題，並與糖尿病、心血管疾病等全身性疾病密切相關。現行治療以機械清創及抗生素為主，往往未能持續糾正微生物失衡，導致復發率高，並加劇抗生素耐藥性。因此，迫切需要精準且對生態友善的療法，同時調控宿主炎症反應與致病微生物。本團隊率先建立臨床「牙齦炎消退—進展」模型並進行多組學解析，經整理後鑑定出 572 種與炎症相關的代謝物，並建立以單細胞拉曼組學結合深度學習模型（GINEConvNet）驅動的高通量篩選平台，該模型基於化學結構分類抗炎代謝物的準確率達 92.7%。 研究目的 本項目旨在建立並整合一條變革性的發現流程，融合深入的機制研究、高通量功能篩選與人工智能預測，以發現並驗證新型抗牙齦炎代謝物，最終為口腔炎症性疾病的精準管理提供新的治療候選物。 研究目標 一、建立核心功能性抗炎代謝物的驗證技術平台並完成範例驗證；二、抗炎代謝物的高通量功能驗證；三、人工智能模型驅動的新化合物預測、發現與驗證。 研究方法 採用實驗與計算相結合的整合策略。機制研究以體外宿主—微生物共培養模型為基礎，並以單細胞拉曼組學、轉錄組學及代謝組學進行分析。候選代謝物的高通量功能篩選將採用本團隊已建立的 FlowRACS 平台及定量指標「代謝壓力拉曼組指數」（RIMS）。人工智能部分將以實驗數據訓練並優化 GINEConvNet 模型進行虛擬篩選，排名最前的候選化合物將在體外及小鼠牙周炎模型中驗證。 預期成果 預期交付一條完整驗證的人工智能驅動發現流程、一組經功能驗證的核心抗牙齦炎代謝物，以及具實證療效的人工智能預測先導化合物。所建立的平台與所發現的化合物，將為開發新一代非抗生素口腔護理配方及標靶治療奠定基礎。 意義與影響 本研究將為牙齦炎與牙周炎提供更有效、更精準的治療途徑，直接惠及患者，並為臨床醫生提供新的治療策略、為口腔護理產業提供新的先導化合物。透過減少對廣譜抗生素的依賴，本項目有助於應對抗菌素耐藥性問題。長遠而言，減輕口腔炎症負擔可降低相關全身性疾病風險，改善公共衞生並降低醫療成本。

17116526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17116526.value: 年龄依赖性促翻译淀粉样蛋白丧失导致果蝇记忆受损

17116526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17116526.value: How transient experiences produce persistent memories remains unsolved. The physical substrate of memory has been explored at the neuronal network level, establishing the synapse as the unit of memory. Encoding and maintaining new memories involve persistent synaptic changes, yet the molecules driving these changes remain largely unknown. Among these, the aggregated state of the cytoplasmic polyadenylation element-binding (CPEB) protein has emerged as a substrate of long-lasting memories across species. Local protein synthesis at synapses is essential for memory persistence. While monomeric CPEB represses translation, aggregated CPEB activates translation of synaptic mRNAs, playing a key role in converting transient memories into lasting ones. Using cryo-EM and functional assays, we reported the structure and activity of aggregated CPEB from 3-to-7-day-old Drosophila heads. This work showed that Drosophila CPEB, Orb2, forms a translationally active amyloid that enhances translation of synaptic mRNA targets implicated in memory. Unlike hydrophobic, disease-related amyloids, the hydrophilic nature of Orb2 amyloid reveals how it could serve as a stable, yet malleable substrate of memory whose integrity is influenced by the environment. This raises critical questions: How do long-lived memories decay with age? Does the aging brain foster a cellular environment that alters the active conformation of Orb2 amyloid, impairing synaptic function and contributing to age-related memory impairment (AMI)? This project aims to provide insight into the molecular basis of AMI—which affects over 40% of individuals over age 60—since the mechanisms by which aging leads to loss or altered accessibility of memory substrates remain unknown. To support this proposal, we have isolated Orb2 from Drosophila heads at different ages and found preliminary evidence that allows us to hypothesize that Orb2 aggregates undergo age-dependent structural and functional changes—from a translation-activating polymorph to a form unable to promote translation, with the prevalence of the latter increasing with age and potentially contributing to AMI. To investigate this and establish a causal link between Orb2 amyloid conformation and AMI, we will examine the functional properties of Orb2 aggregates during aging, determine the structure of Orb2 amyloid isolated from Drosophila heads at different ages, and assess how overexpression of CG10375—a memory-promoting chaperone—in aged flies with severe AMI, and CG6693—a memory-impairing chaperone—in young flies with robust long-term memory, affects Orb2 amyloid activity and structure. These findings will provide insight into the molecular basis of AMI and guide the development of prevention strategies. 摘要 短暂经历如何产生持久记忆是一个尚未解决的问题。记忆的物理基础已在神经网络层面得到探索，并将突触确立为记忆的基本功能单元。新记忆的编码与维持伴随持续性的突触变化，但驱动这些变化的分子在很大程度上仍是未知的。在这些分子中，胞质多聚腺苷酸化元件结合蛋白（CPEB）的聚集状态已被认为是跨物种长期记忆的一种物理基础。 突触处的局部蛋白质合成对记忆的持久性至关重要。单体形式的 CPEB 抑制翻译，而聚集形式的 CPEB 则激活突触 mRNA 的翻译，对于将短暂记忆转化为持久记忆至关重要。我们利用低温电子显微镜结合功能实验，揭示了来自 3 至 7 日龄果蝇头部中聚集态 CPEB 的结构及其生化活性。该研究表明，果蝇 CPEB，即 Orb2，可形成一种具有翻译活性的淀粉样蛋白，增强与记忆相关的突触 mRNA 靶标的翻译。与疏水性的致病性淀粉样蛋白不同，Orb2 淀粉样蛋白的亲水特性揭示了它如何能够作为一种稳定但又可塑的记忆基质，且其完整性会受到环境影响。 这引出了一些关键问题：长期记忆如何随年龄增长而衰退？衰老的大脑是否会产生一种细胞环境，改变Orb2 淀粉样蛋白的活性构象，从而损害突触功能并导致年龄相关性记忆障碍（AMI）？本项目旨在阐明 AMI 的分子基础。AMI 影响超过 40% 的 60 岁以上人群，而衰老如何导致记忆基质的丧失或可及性改变，其机制仍然未知。 为支撑本研究计划，我们已从不同日龄的果蝇头部中分离出 Orb2 淀粉样蛋白，并获得了初步证据，我们据此提出如下假设：Orb2 聚集体会发生年龄依赖性的结构和功能变化——从一种具有翻译激活能力的结构多形体，转变为一种无法促进翻译的形式；后者（无活性形式）的比例随年龄增长而增加，并可能导致 AMI。为研究这一假设并建立 Orb2 淀粉样蛋白构象与 AMI 之间的因果关系，我们将考察衰老过程中 Orb2 聚集体的功能特性，解析从不同年龄果蝇头部中分离出的 Orb2 淀粉样蛋白结构，并评估在严重 AMI 的老年果蝇中过表达 CG10375（一种促进记忆形成的分子伴侣），以及在具有稳固长期记忆的年轻果蝇中过表达CG6693（一种损害记忆的分子伴侣），如何影响 Orb2 淀粉样蛋白的活性和结构。这些发现将有助于深入理解 AMI 的分子基础，并为预防策略的开发提供理论依据。

17117326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17117326.value: 視黃酸透過Alx家族轉錄因子調節神經嵴細胞的位置身份

17117326.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17117326.value: Prof Cox, Timothy Chilton Prof Liu, Huan Prof Wang, John Junwen

17117326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17117326.value: Midfacial defects are a group of congenital conditions ranging from hypoplastic midfacial structures to a cleft in the facial midline splitting the nose into two halves. Midfacial defects pose a detrimental impact on the physiological and social-psychological wellbeing of affected patients and are highly challenging to correct surgically. Deficiency in retinoic acid (RA) signalling — either due to dietary vitamin A deficiency or mutations in the genetic components of the RA signalling pathway — is a known aetiology of midfacial defects. However, our current understanding of the functions of RA during midfacial development is incomplete. The building blocks of the skeletal framework of the face are neural crest cells (NCCs), which are transient, migratory, multipotent embryonic progenitor cells. To develop the complex structure of the face, it is imperative for NCCs to “know” their locations in the embryo by acquiring correct positional identities. As a diffusive signalling molecule, RA is known to function as an environmental cue to set up positional identities along the anterior-posterior axis of the body plan by regulating a combinatorial expression of Hox family genes. However, the major skeletal elements of the face are derived from Hox-negative NCCs. Whether RA signalling also provides environmental cues for establishing the positional identity for those Hox-negative cells is completely unknown. Our preliminary results demonstrated that inhibition of RA signalling causes incorrect assignment of first pharyngeal arch (PA1)-like identity to NCCs in the frontonasal prominence (FNP) of chick embryos. We found that in anterior NCCs where Hox genes are not expressed, RA regulates the expression of a different family of transcription factors — the Alx genes. Therefore, we hypothesize that RA acts as an environmental cue to instruct the identity of FNP by regulating the expression of Alx genes. This hypothesis will be tested rigorously using cutting-edge techniques in different but complementary models. We aim to characterize the global effect of RA on NCCs through multi-omics approaches; to elucidate the regulatory mechanism of RA on Alx genes by identifying and characterising RA-responsive Alx enhancers; and to define the 3D chromatin conformation features enabling the RA-responsiveness of Alx genes. The expected outcomes of the study will not only fill a longstanding gap in our understanding of the fundamental biology of midfacial development and NCC patterning, but also provide critical insight into risk factors for craniofacial defects that interact with RA signalling. 中面部缺陷是一組先天性疾病，其表現涵蓋從中面部結構發育不良，到面部中線裂隙（將鼻子分成兩半）等不同程度。中面部缺陷對患者的生理和社會心理健康造成嚴重的影響，且通過外科手術矯正的難度極高。視黃酸（RA）信號傳導不足——無論是源於膳食維生素 A 缺乏，還是 RA 信號通路基因組分的突變——均為已知的中面部缺陷病因。然而，我們目前對於 RA 在中面部發育過程中的功能瞭解仍不完整。 構成面部骨骼框架的基礎單元是神經嵴細胞（NCCs），這是一群具備暫時性、遷移性及多能性的胚胎祖細胞。為了發育出複雜的面部結構，NCCs 必須透過獲取正確的位置身份，來「感知」其在胚胎中的位置。作為一種可擴散的信號分子，過往研究表明RA 能發揮環境訊號的作用，透過調控 Hox 家族基因的組合表達，建立沿著體軸前後軸的位置身份。然而，面部的主要骨骼元件卻是由不表達Hox的NCCs 衍生而來。RA 信號傳導是否同樣為這些 Hox 陰性細胞提供確立位置身份的環境訊號，目前完全未知。 我們的初步結果顯示，抑制 RA 信號傳導會導致雞胚胎前額鼻突（FNP）中的 NCCs 被錯誤賦予類似第一咽弓（PA1）的身份。我們發現，在不表達 Hox 基因的前端 NCCs 中，RA 調控著另一個轉錄因子家族——Alx 基因的表達。因此，我們假設 RA 作為一種環境訊號，透過調控 Alx 基因的表達來指引 FNP 的身份確立。 這項假設將在不同的模型中，運用前沿技術進行嚴謹的驗證。我們旨在透過多組學方法系統性地闡明 RA 對 NCCs 的影響；透過鑑定並解析響應 RA 的 Alx 增強子，來揭示 RA 對 Alx 基因的調控機制；並通過描述3D染色質構象特徵解釋為何在NCC中Alx可以響應RA的刺激。 本研究的預期成果不僅將填補我們對中面部發育與 NCC 模式形成（patterning）基礎生物學長久以來的認知空白，還將幫助我們理解與 RA 信號傳導相互作用的環境風險因素（例如孕期酒精及特定藥物的攝入）對胎兒面部發育的影響。

17117526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17117526.value: 針對牙酸蝕症的仿生礦化策略：開發一種pH響應性納米複合水凝膠

17117526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17117526.value: BACKGROUND Dental erosion causes irreversible loss of dental hard tissue, often leading to sharp pain and significant challenges for restoration. Current treatment provides limited protection, as frequent exposure to high-level acids overwhelms saliva’s remineralisation capacity. To overcome these limitations, we developed a pH-responsive quaternary ammonium chitosan-tannic acid/nano amorphous calcium phosphate hydrogel (QCS-TA/NACP) to manage dental erosion through biomimetic mineralisation. Pilot studies have demonstrated that QCS-TA/NACP releases nano amorphous calcium phosphate (NACP) in acidic environments, counteracting erosion. Additionally, QCS-TA/NACP promotes remineralisation by forming enamel-like prismatic crystals. Its low cytotoxicity makes it suitable for daily application, further research is needed to confirm its efficacy. OBJECTIVE To develop and evaluate a pH-responsive nanocomposite hydrogel (QCS-TA/NACP) for dental erosion management. METHODS Synthesis and characterisation: We will synthesise QCS-TA using the one-pot method, incorporating NACP to form QCS-TA/NACP. Characterisation will include morphology (scanning electron microscopy, SEM), crystallinity (X-ray diffraction, XRD), chemical structure (X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, XPS) and bond formation (Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, FTIR). We will also investigate its wet adhesion on tooth surface (mechanical testing), release kinetics of calcium and phosphorus (inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry) and cytotoxicity (mitochondrial dehydrogenase activity assay). Erosive model: We will section extracted sound human molars into enamel blocks. The blocks will be subjected to demineralisation with citric acid (pH 3.2) to simulate erosion, followed by daily QCS-TA/NACP treatment. One-hour post-treatment, the blocks will receive five two-minute citric acid erosive challenges, each separated by one-hour intervals, in an artificial mouth system for 21 days. Sodium fluoride (5,000 ppm) toothpaste and deionised water will serve as positive and negative controls. Biomimetic mineralisation: We will perform the mineralisation assessment of the QCS-TA/NACP-treated enamel, including its surface morphology (SEM), surface loss (profilometry), surface hardness (nanoindentation) and mineral density (micro-computed tomography). We will also perform structure characterisation to study crystal structure (XRD), molecular bonds (FTIR), crystalline phases (Raman spectroscopy) and binding state (XPS). We will repeat the study on the QCS-TA/NACP-treated dentine. The protective effects for dentine collagen will be investigated by evaluating the morphology (TEM), collagen content (hydroxyproline assay), chemical structure (FTIR) and molecular interactions (molecular dynamics simulation). EXPECTED OUTCOMES AND IMPLICATIONS We anticipate that QCS-TA/NACP will prevent dental erosion by promoting biomimetic mineralisation and inhibiting dentine-collagen degradation. If translated to clinical care, this innovative approach will offer a practical and effective solution for billions affected by dental erosion worldwide, thereby improving oral health and quality of life. 目標 開發並評估一種用於管理牙酸蝕症之pH響應性奈米複合水凝膠（QCS-TA/NACP）。 方法 合成與表徵：我們將採用一鍋法合成QCS-TA水凝膠，並摻入NACP以形成QCS-TA/NACP。表徵項目將包括形態（掃描式電子顯微鏡，SEM）、結晶度（X射線繞射，XRD）、化學結構（X射線光電子能譜，XPS）以及鍵結形成（傅立葉轉換紅外光譜，FTIR）。我們也將研究該水凝膠在牙齒表面的濕式附著力（機械測試）、鈣與磷的釋放動力學（感應耦合電漿光學發射光譜儀）以及細胞毒性（使用人類牙齦纖維母細胞進行粒線體脫氫酶活性測定）。 酸蝕模型：我們將拔除之健康人類臼齒切片分割為琺瑯質試塊。這些試塊將以檸檬酸（pH 3.2）進行去礦化以模擬酸蝕，隨後每日接受QCS-TA/NACP處理。處理後一小時，試塊將在人工口腔系統中，於21天內接受五次為時兩分鐘的檸檬酸酸蝕挑戰，每次挑戰之間間隔一小時。氟化鈉牙膏（5,000 ppm）及去離子水將分別作為陽性對照組與陰性對照組。 仿生礦化評估：我們將對經QCS-TA/NACP處理之琺瑯質進行礦化評估，包括其表面形態（SEM）、表面損失量（表面輪廓測定法）、表面硬度（奈米壓痕試驗）以及礦物密度（微型電腦斷層掃描）。同時也將進行結構表徵，以研究晶體結構（XRD）、分子鍵結（FTIR）、晶相（拉曼光譜）及鍵結狀態（XPS）。 我們將在經QCS-TA/NACP處理之牙本質上重複上述研究。針對牙本質膠原蛋白的保護作用，將透過評估形態（穿透式電子顯微鏡，TEM）、膠原蛋白含量（羥脯胺酸測定法）、化學結構（FTIR）以及分子交互作用（分子動力學模擬）來進行探討。 預期成果 我們預期QCS-TA/NACP能透過促進仿生礦化及抑制牙本質膠原蛋白降解，達到預防牙酸蝕症的效果。 應用與意義 若能將此創新方法轉化至臨床照護，將為全球數十億受牙酸蝕症影響的人口提供實用且有效的解決方案，進而改善口腔健康與生活品質。

17117626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17117626.value: 估算經死亡位移調整後與新冠肺炎相關的疾病負擔及對加強疫苗接種策略的影響

17117626.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17117626.value: Prof Cowling, Benjamin John Dr Presanis, Anne Margaret Prof Wu, Peng

17117626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17117626.value: Background: The emergence of SARS-CoV-2 has caused a substantial mortality burden in Hong Kong and across the world. It is well established that deaths among laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infections underestimate the “true” mortality impact, and it is possible to statistically estimate excess mortality attributable to a pathogen as the difference between observed mortality and the mortality expected in the absence of that pathogen. However, it has been challenging to estimate the baseline mortality for COVID-19 infections accurately in the long term due to a proportion of deaths that were premature and brought forward by the pandemic, a phenomenon known as “mortality displacement”. Obtaining estimates of mortality burden based on an accurate baseline mortality have important implications for booster vaccination strategies that minimize transmission and disease burden. Purpose: We propose to conduct a comprehensive study using statistical modeling of administrative and surveillance data to determine the mortality impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and to optimize vaccination strategy. We aim to conduct a years-of-life-lost analysis based on individual COVID-19 case data. Then, we will construct a statistical model to quantify the excess mortality associated with the COVID-19 pandemic while accounting for mortality displacement. We will also conduct extensive simulations to optimize age-based booster vaccination strategies based on simulated excess mortality. Methods: We will develop a statistical model to predict life expectancy using data from specific cohorts and estimate the distribution of mortality displacement. Then, we will develop a full probability model to estimate excess mortality under a Bayesian synthesis framework while accounting for mortality displacement in the estimation of baseline mortality. Finally, we will conduct extensive simulations by extending the Bayesian models to incorporate the distribution of mortality displacement, estimate the mortality impact and evaluate the population-level effectiveness of booster vaccination strategies. Data from the COVID-19 waves from 2020 through 2025 will be analyzed using these approaches. Implications: This study proposes a novel methodology to estimate the distribution of mortality displacement, which fills an important gap in COVID-19 epidemiology and control measures, particularly for interventions that focus on high burden groups. Robust modeling of the population-level mortality impact, while accounting for mortality displacement, allows for an accurate estimation of excess mortality and the optimization of population-level effectiveness for booster vaccination strategies. Public health policies for COVID-19 infection control may need to target the reduction of burden in health-care settings. This approach can be extended to other infectious diseases. 背景：新冠病毒在香港和世界各地造成極大的死亡負擔。利用確診新冠病毒感染的死亡數字會低估實際的死亡負擔，而我們可以透過統計方法來估算與指定病毒相關的超額死亡人數，即是實際死亡數字與在沒有病毒流傳的假設下的預期死亡數字的差額。可是，「死亡位移」的現象會導致一部分的患者因為新冠疫情提早死亡，因此增加估算與新冠肺炎相關的長遠預期死亡數字的難度。掌握準確的預期死亡數字估算出的死亡負擔能促進加強疫苗接種策略的規劃，有助減少傳播與疾病負擔。 目的：我們計劃透過統計模型對行政與監測數據進行分析，估算與新冠肺炎相關的死亡負擔，並優化疫苗接種策略。首先，我們會利用新冠患者的數據進行生命損失年數分析。然後，我們會建立統計模型估算經死亡位移調整後與新冠肺炎相關的超額死亡數字，並利用估算得來的數值進行模擬分析，用於優化以年齡為主的加強疫苗接種策略。 方法：我們計劃建立統計模型對特定群組的數據進行分析，估算預期壽命與死亡位移的統計分佈。然後，我們會建立機率模型，在貝氏理論框架下估算預期死亡數字時把死亡位移的現象納入考量，經調整後估算超額死亡數字。最後，我們會利用延伸模型進行深入的模擬分析，納入死亡位移的統計分佈，估算與新冠肺炎相關的死亡影響，並評估不同加強疫苗接種策略的有效性。以上提及的統計方法會被應用到2020至2025年新冠疫情相關數據的分析。 意義：此研究對死亡位移統計分佈的估算提供了一個新穎的研究方法論，有助於填補與新冠病毒相關流行病學與疾病控制政策的研究缺口，特別是用於保護高危群組的干預措施。估算與新冠肺炎相關的死亡影響時納入死亡位移的現象可以更準確地估算超額死亡數字與優化加強疫苗接種策略的有效性。控制新冠疫情的公共衛生政策需要針對減輕醫療機構負擔。這個方法可以應用於其他傳染病。

17117726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17117726.value: 可解釋多模態機器學習系統於初中學童精神健康風險早期識別之開發與驗證：一項前瞻性隊列研究

17117726.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17117726.value: Prof Fung, Hong Dr Huizhi, Liang Prof Jing, Qi Dr Ni, Michael Yuxuan Dr Qian, Mengjie

17117726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17117726.value: Adolescent mental health has become one of the most urgent public-health challenges in China and Hong Kong. National surveys indicate that roughly one in four middle-school students experience symptoms of depression, anxiety, or obsessive-compulsive disorder. Yet most schools still depend on self-report questionnaires and teacher observations—methods that identify difficulties only after they become visible. As a result, many young people remain undetected until their distress escalates into crisis. To address this systemic gap, the proposed study will be conducted in Shandong Province, mainland China, where strong partnerships with local schools and hospitals allow for rigorous, low-cost data collection under controlled ethical oversight. The project will develop and validate an interpretable, multimodal machine-learning (MML) system that integrates three complementary data sources—short surveys, students’ essays, and drawings—to identify early signs of mental-health risk in school settings. The study will recruit near 1300 students aged 12–15 and their parents or guardians, following them across baseline, 3-month, and 6-month assessments. Diagnostic interviews will provide the gold-standard reference for model training and testing. Using state-of-the-art AI methods, the team will first construct separate models for each data modality and then merge them into a unified MML framework. Explainable-AI (XAI) techniques will ensure transparency, allowing educators and counsellors to interpret which features—such as linguistic tone, visual composition, or survey patterns—drive each prediction. The project unites an interdisciplinary team from the School of Public Health, The University of Hong Kong, the Shandong Second Medical University, and international collaborators at the University of Cambridge (Department of Engineering) and the Newcastle University (School of Computing). All procedures will comply fully with China’s Personal Information Protection Law (PIPL) and international research-ethics standards. By combining technological innovation with cultural sensitivity, the project will deliver a scientifically validated, ethically grounded early-warning system for schools. The findings can also be used to inform youth-mental-health strategies in Hong Kong, where similar academic pressures exist, and offer a scalable framework adaptable to other East-Asian societies with shared educational and cultural contexts. Ultimately, this work aims to transform school mental-health screening from a reactive process into a proactive, data-driven system—shortening the “time-to-care” for at-risk adolescents and promoting emotional well-being across the region. 青少年精神健康已成為中國內地及香港最迫切的公共衞生議題之一。全國性調查顯示，約四分之一的初中學生出現抑鬱、焦慮或強迫症狀。然而，目前大多數學校仍主要依賴自陳式問卷及教師觀察，此等方法往往只能在問題已顯性化後方能識別困難，導致不少學生在情緒困擾惡化至危機階段之前，始終未被察覺。 為填補此一系統性缺口，本研究擬於中國內地山東省進行。該地與本地學校及醫院建立了穩固的合作關係，可在嚴謹的研究倫理監督下，以較低成本開展高質素的資料收集工作。本項目將開發並驗證一套可解釋多模態機器學習（interpretable multimodal machine learning, MML）系統，整合三類互補的資料來源——簡短問卷、學生作文及繪畫作品——藉以識別校園情境中精神健康風險的早期徵象。 研究將招募約1,300名年齡介乎12至15歲的學生及其家長或監護人，並於基線、第三個月及第六個月進行追蹤評估。診斷性訪談將作為模型訓練與測試的金標準參照。研究團隊將運用當前最先進的人工智能方法，先就各項資料模態分別建構模型，繼而整合為統一的多模態機器學習框架。研究並將採用可解釋人工智能（explainable AI, XAI）技術以確保模型的透明度，使教育工作者及輔導人員能夠理解何種特徵——例如語言語氣、視覺構圖或問卷作答模式——驅動個別預測結果。 本項目匯聚跨學科研究團隊，成員來自香港大學公共衞生學院、山東第二醫科大學，以及英國劍橋大學工程學系與紐卡素大學計算機學院的國際合作夥伴。所有研究程序將全面遵循《中華人民共和國個人信息保護法》（PIPL）及國際研究倫理準則。 透過結合技術創新與文化敏感度，本項目將為學校提供一套經科學驗證、並具備倫理基礎的精神健康預警系統。研究結果亦可為香港的青少年精神健康策略提供實證參考——香港學生同樣面對相近的學業壓力——並可為具有相似教育與文化脈絡的其他東亞社會，提供一套可擴展、可調適的框架。本研究的最終目標，是推動學校精神健康篩查由被動應對模式轉型為主動而以數據為本的系統，縮短高風險青少年由出現徵狀至獲得專業支援的「求助至照護時間」（time-to-care），從而促進區內青少年的情緒健康。

17118226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17118226.value: 流感病毒神經氨酸酶抗體在禽流感病毒傳播與擴散中的作用

17118226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17118226.value: Prof Peiris, Joseph Sriyal Malik Prof Poon, Leo Lit Man Prof Zanin, Mark Phillip

17118226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17118226.value: Avian influenza viruses (AIV) in poultry pose a significant public health threat due to their potential to cause outbreaks with severe economic, food security, and social impacts. Notably, the emergence and spread of highly pathogenic Clade 2.3.4.4b H5Nx AIV have intensified vaccination efforts in poultry. However, the current global vaccine landscape is complex, relying on regional vaccine seed strains and various platforms that differ in neuraminidase (NA) content and types. We previously found that exposure to avian NA subtypes in humans through the pandemics of avian-origin 1918 (N1) and 1957 (N2) boosted the breadth of anti-NA reactivity to include its phylogenetic neighbours. Here, we hypothesize that NA-antibodies can influence the AIV shedding and transmission pattern and we seek to examine this in the context of AIV poultry vaccines. In this proposal, we will examine the cross-reactivity conferred by NA-antibodies using the highly sensitive enzyme-linked lectin assay (ELLA) after vaccination in experimental and field samples. In collaboration with several groups, we will test this hypothesis through the following aims i) to determine the magnitude and breadth of NA-antibodies elicited by major commercial poultry vaccines in experimental and field settings, ii) to determine the role of NA-antibodies in protecting against homologous and heterologous avian NA virus infection in chickens and iii) to determine the impact of vaccine-elicited NA-antibodies in infection susceptibility by heterologous avian NA virus type in chickens. In Aim 1, we will investigate whether major poultry vaccines will elicit significant NA-antibodies in vaccinated chickens and the breadth of such reactivity. In Aim 2, we will use a NA-only virus like particle (VLP) (specifically expressing N2 or N8) to immunize chickens. We will then determine the morbidity and virus after homologous infection by the highly pathogenic H5N8, a low pathogenic H9N2 virus and another heterologous NA type virus. In Aim 3, we will determine the role of NA antibodies in infection susceptibility to viruses bearing different NA. Here we will immunize chickens with the commercial, trivalent AIV vaccine that elicits high titers of NA antibodies. These chickens will be challenged with a panel of nine isogenic viruses that differ only in the NA to assess the degree of viral shedding. We will then validate our hypothesis in a contact transmission experiment and another challenge experiment using wildtype viruses. 17118326.value: 轉形生長因子活化的遺傳失調及肝星狀細胞相互作用於膽管發育及膽道閉鎖發病機制中的角色

17118326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17118326.value: Biliary Atresia (BA) is a life-threatening fibroinflammatory obstruction of bile ducts, with the highest incidence in Asians. Though the precise etiology remains largely unknown, compelling evidence suggests that genetic defects impairing cholangiocyte development may increase the vulnerability of immature bile ducts to perinatal biliary injury. The injury can trigger abnormal immune responses, eventually leading to atresia of the biliary tree. Unfortunately, the current prognosis for BA is poor, with less than 60% of patients achieving long-term native liver survival. In fact, BA is the primary indication for paediatric liver transplantation, highlighting the need for alternative therapies to improve clinical outcomes.
