Functional characterization of BA-associated mutations in TGF-β activators, including the hub gene, THBS1, demonstrated inhibition of TGF-β activation. Analysis of single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data of human fetal liver showed that these ECM genes are primarily expressed in fetal hepatic stellate cells (HSCs). Additionally, knockout of Thbs1, which is also mainly expressed in HSCs, in zebrafish led to abnormal biliary network formation and impaired biliary function, supporting the critical role of HSC-mediated TGF-β activation in bile duct development. Given these findings, we hypothesize that genetic predisposition to TGF-β signaling dysregulation may disrupt hepatocyte-cholangiocyte bifurcation and cholangiocyte differentiation/maturation via paracrine effects of HSCs, which leads to increased susceptibility to perinatal biliary injury and hence BA. Here we propose to use our established human stem cell-based transwell coculture and transgenic BA mouse models to evaluate the impact of reduced TGF-β activation on cholangiocyte development and susceptibility to perinatal insults, respectively. We will elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms by scRNA-seq. The Thbs1-associated factors involved in the pathogenic pathways or cellular crosstalk will serve as promising targets for therapeutic intervention. In conclusion, our study will provide valuable insights into the roles of TGF-β activation in cholangiocyte differentiation, immune cell crosstalk, and fibrogenesis during injury and BA progression. The knowledge gained could enhance genetic risk prediction and patient stratification for better clinical management. Importantly, we will identify critical ECM/TGF-β-associated factors as novel therapeutic targets, ultimately contributing to improved clinical outcomes for BA. 膽道閉鎖（BA）是一種致命的纖維發炎性的膽管阻塞性疾病，在亞洲人群中發病率最高。儘管其確切的病因至今尚不明確，但有證據表示，損害膽管上皮細胞發育的遺傳缺陷，可能會增加發育未成熟之膽管對圍產期膽道損傷的易感性。此種損傷可進一步誘發異常的免疫反應，最終導致膽道閉鎖。目前膽道閉鎖患者的臨床預後依然不理想，僅有不到六成的患者能夠實現長期的自體肝臟存活。事實上，膽道閉鎖是兒童肝臟移植的首要病因，這突顯出開發新型替代療法以改善臨床預後的迫切需要。本研究團隊最近開展了迄今為止規模最大的基因測序研究，分析了 303 名膽道閉鎖患者的基因數據，發現調控TGF-β訊號路徑的細胞外基質（ECM）相關基因中，存在著罕見破壞性突變的顯著富集。我們進而對與膽道閉鎖相關的 TGF-β 活化因子（包括核心樞紐基因 THBS1）進行功能表徵分析，證實了這些基因突變會抑制 TGF-β 的活化。通過分析人類胚胎肝臟的單細胞 RNA 測序數據，我們進一步發現這些ECM主要表達於胚胎時期的肝星狀細胞。在肝臟發育過程中，胚胎肝星狀細胞與肝母細胞之間存在多種相互作用，其中超過三分之一的相互作用是透過ECM相關配體或受體介導的。此外，我們在斑馬魚模型中敲除了同樣主要在肝星狀細胞中表達的 Thbs1 基因，結果導致了斑馬魚出現膽道網絡形成異常及膽道功能受損，此發現證實了由肝星狀細胞介導的 TGF-β 活化在膽管發育中發揮關鍵作用。基於上述科研發現，我們提出以下假說：TGF-β訊號通路失調的遺傳易感性，可透過肝星狀細胞的旁分泌效應，干擾肝細胞與膽管上皮細胞的分化分流以及膽管上皮細胞的成熟進程，從而增加個體對圍產期膽道損傷的易感性，引發膽道閉鎖。為此，本項目計劃將採用基於人類幹細胞的共培養體系，以及轉基因膽道閉鎖小鼠模型，分別評估TGF-β活化水平降低對膽管上皮細胞發育及圍產期損傷易感性的影響。我們將透利用單細胞 RNA 測序，闡明其背後的分子機制。參與致病通路或細胞間相互作用的Thbs1相關因子，將有望成為未來臨床治療干預的重要潛在靶點。總括而言，本研究將深入揭示 TGF-β 活化在膽管上皮細胞分化、免疫細胞交互作用與膽道閉鎖病理進程形成中所扮演的角色。研究所獲成果可望提升遺傳風險預測與患者臨床分層，以優化臨床管理。更重要的是，我們將鑑定出關鍵的 ECM/TGF-β 相關因子作為新型治療靶點，最終幫助改善膽道閉鎖患者的臨床預後及生存率做出貢獻。

17119126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17119126.value: 構建下一代豬多潛能幹細胞

17119126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17119126.value: Prof Huang, Yuanhua Prof Lin, Jiangwei

17119126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17119126.value: The derivation of stable and developmentally potent porcine pluripotent stem cells (pPSCs) in naïve and totipotency states remains a unmet goal in stem cell biology, with broad implications for biomedical research and agriculture. As large-animal models, pigs offer unique advantages due to their close anatomical, physiological, immunological, and genetic similarities to humans, surpassing traditional rodent models. Authentic naïve pPSCs and totipotent stem cells would enable rigorous cross-species comparisons of human and porcine development, facilitate precise genome engineering, support studies of zoonotic pathogens, and serve as renewable cell sources for xenotransplantation. Although recent advances have yielded pig expanded potential stem cells (pEPSCs) and primed pPSCs such as pESCs, EDSCs, and pgEpiSCs, these cell lines exhibit limited chimeric contribution and uncertain germline competency. Establishing naïve pPSCs capable of robust, multi-lineage chimerism remains challenging, primarily due to the apparent requirement of MEK/ERK signaling for porcine pluripotency in vitro. This is at odds with naïve-promoting regimens commonly used in other species, which rely on MEK inhibition. Indeed, culture systems for pEPSCs and primed pPSCs are optimized to exclude PD0325901, a selective MEK/ERK pathway inhibitor that blocks MEK activation and downstream signaling, highlighting potential species-specific signalling requirements. Building on our preliminary findings, this project proposes an innovative strategy to derive and characterize naïve-like pPSCs by modulating key cell stress pathways during the transition to naïve states. In parallel, we have identified CBL0137, a small molecule that binds to DNA and influences chromatin dynamics, as a potent inducer of totipotency- associated gene expression in mouse, human, and porcine PSCs. These findings suggest promising strategies for generating versatile and developmentally potent next-generation porcine stem cells. We will employ an integrative approach combining transcriptomic, epigenomic, and functional analyses to derive and characterize novel porcine stem cells in defined naïve and totipotent states. The developmental potency of these cells will be rigorously assessed through chimera formation, and ultimately, germline transmission assays. Successful establishment of such cell lines will open new avenues for modeling human development and disease, accelerating regenerative medicine, and advancing agricultural biotechnology. These principles may also be applicable to stem cells of other large animal species, such as cattle and sheep/goats. By addressing a critical gap in stem cell biology, this project will advance both fundamental understanding and translational applications in biomedical and agricultural research, aligning closely with the RGC’s mission to support high-impact, innovative scientific inquiry. 獲得處於原始態（naïve）和全能性（totipotency）狀態、且具備穩定發育潛能的豬多潛能幹細胞（pPSCs），仍是幹細胞生物學領域中一項尚未實現的目標，這對於生物醫學研究和農業發展具有深遠的意義。作為大型動物模型，豬在解剖結構、生理機能、免疫系統以及遺傳特徵上與人類高度相似，其優勢顯著超越了傳統的齧齒類動物模型。真正的原始態 pPSCs 和全能幹細胞將有助於對人類與豬的發育進行嚴謹的跨物種比較、促進精準基因組工程、支持人畜共通傳染病原體的研究，並為異種移植提供可再生的細胞來源。 儘管近年來的進展已成功培育出豬擴展潛能幹細胞（pEPSCs）和始基態（primed）pPSCs（例如 pESCs、EDSCs 和 pgEpiSCs），但這些細胞株在體內嵌合貢獻（chimeric contribution）上表現有限，且其生殖系傳遞能力（germline competency）仍不確定。要建立能實現高效、多譜系嵌合的原始態 pPSCs 依然充滿挑戰，這主要是因為豬的體外多潛能性維持似乎高度依賴 MEK/ERK 信號通路的激活。這與其他物種中常用於誘導/維持原始態、依賴於抑制 MEK 通路的培養方案背道而馳。事實上，現有的 pEPSCs 和始基態 pPSCs 培養系統均特意排除了 PD0325901（一種阻斷 MEK 激活及其下游信號傳導的選擇性 MEK/ERK 通路抑制劑），這凸顯了豬可能存在獨特的物種特異性信號調控需求。 基於我們的初步研究結果，本項目提出了一種創新策略：在細胞向原始態轉變的過程中調控關鍵的細胞壓力（應激）通路，以此建立並鑑定「類原始態」（naïve-like）的 pPSCs。與此同時，我們發現小分子化合物 CBL0137（能與 DNA 結合並影響染色質動力學）在小鼠、人類和豬的 PSCs 中均能強效誘導全能性相關基因的表達。這些發現為培育具備高分化潛能且用途廣泛的下一代豬幹細胞開闢了極具前景的途徑。我們將採用整合轉錄組學、表觀基因組學及功能分析的綜合研究方法，在確定的條件下建立並鑑定新型的原始態和全能性豬幹細胞。這些細胞的發育潛能將通過嵌合體形成實驗、以及最終的生殖系傳遞（germline transmission）檢測進行嚴謹評估。成功建立這些細胞株將為模擬人類早期發育和疾病、加速再生醫學進程以及推動農業生物技術發展開闢全新途徑。此外，這些調控原理亦有望應用於牛、羊等其他大型家畜的幹細胞研究中。 本項目針對幹細胞生物學領域的關鍵空白進行攻關，將大幅推進生物醫學與農業研究中的基礎認知與轉化應用，這與研究資助局（RGC）支持具高影響力、創新性科學探索的宗旨高度契合。

17120526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17120526.value: 小細胞外囊泡中的MED8調控肝細胞癌進展的作用及機制研究

17120526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17120526.value: The liver plays a crucial role in maintaining redox balance, which is essential for physiological homeostasis. Increasing evidence highlights the vital effect of oxidative stress within the tumor microenvironment in the development of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) have been implicated in driving HCC progression through multiple pathways, yet their role in oxidative stress remains poorly understood. Our findings revealed that sEV derived from metastatic cells increased cellular ROS level and induced DNA damage in recipient cells. To elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying sEV-mediated oxidative stress and genomic instability in HCC, we conducted proteomic profiling and identified Mediator Complex Subunit 8 (MED8) as significantly upregulated in sEVs from HCC cells compared to those from normal liver cells. MED8 is a component of the mediator complex, which regulates transcription. While aberrant MED8 expression has been linked to various diseases, its presence and function in sEVs have not been documented. We show that sEVs from metastatic cells promoted increased ROS levels and DNA fragmentation in recipient cells, effects that are mitigated by MED8 knockdown. Furthermore, sEVs with reduced MED8 levels exhibited diminished capacity to induce cell growth, motility, and tumor development, underscoring the pivotal role of sEV-MED8 in HCC progression. RNA sequencing of cells treated with sEVs from control and MED8 knockdown cells revealed an enrichment of genes involved in mitochondrial calcium transport, a process critical for redox homeostasis. We postulate that sEV-MED8 promotes mitochondrial ROS production by enhancing Ca²⁺ influx into the mitochondria. Indeed, sEV-MED8 was found to elevate mitochondrial superoxide levels and increase mitochondrial Ca²⁺ concentrations. Furthermore sEV-MED8 upregulated the expression of mitochondrial calcium uniporter (MCU) and increases mitochondrial membrane potential, which mediates Ca²⁺ transport from the cytosol into the mitochondria. Collectively, our findings suggest that sEV-MED8 induces mitochondrial oxidative stress by promoting MCU-mediated Ca²⁺ influx into the mitochondria. Based on these preliminary data, we hypothesize that sEV-MED8 enhances mitochondrial superoxide production, leading to DNA damage and an aggressive cancer phenotype via mitochondrial Ca²⁺ dysregulation. This study aims to 1) elucidate the mechanistic basis of sEV-MED8 in regulating mitochondrial Ca²⁺ influx, 2) characterize the role of sEV-MED8 in oxidative stress through its regulation of MCU, and 3) assess the clinical relevance of MED8 in HCC. Our findings will advance the understanding of sEV-mediated redox imbalance and provide insights into the development of therapeutic strategies targeting the dynamic regulation of ROS in HCC. 肝臟是維持機體氧化還原平衡的核心器官，對於維持生理功能穩態至關重要。近年來，越來越多研究證實，腫瘤微環境中的氧化應激反應在肝細胞癌（Hepatocellular Carcinoma, HCC）發生發展中發揮關鍵作用。小細胞外囊泡（small extracellular vesicles, sEVs）是細胞間物質傳輸與信號傳遞的重要載體，已被證實可通過多種通路驅動HCC進展，但目前其在腫瘤氧化應激調控中的具體作用尚不明確。 本研究前期結果顯示，高轉移潛能的HCC細胞所分泌的sEVs可提高受體細胞內活性氧（Reactive Oxygen Species, ROS）水平，誘導DNA損傷，提示sEVs可能通過介導氧化應激及DNA損傷而參與HCC進展。爲了深入解析sEVs介導HCC氧化應激、DNA損傷及基因組不穩定的分子機制，我們通過蛋白質組學分析對比正常肝細胞與 HCC 細胞來源的 sEVs 蛋白表達差異，發現中介體複合物亞基8（Mediator Complex Subunit 8, MED8）在 HCC 細胞分泌的 sEVs 中顯著高表達。MED8作爲中介體複合物的核心組分之一，參與基因轉錄調控，目前已有研究證實其異常表達與多種疾病的發展密切相關，但MED8在sEVs中的存在及具體功能尚未見報道。實驗證實，轉移性 HCC 細胞來源的 sEVs 可顯著誘導細胞內ROS累積及 DNA 片段化，而在HCC中敲低MED8從而降低其分泌的sEVs內MED8水平後，上述效應被明顯逆轉；類似地，轉移性HCC細胞分泌的sEVs可促進細胞增殖、遷移侵襲及腫瘤進展，而這些效應在敲低MED8後均明顯減弱，進一步證實sEVs攜帶的MED8（sEV-MED8）是促進HCC進展的關鍵分子。 爲了明確sEV-MED8作用機制，我們對對照組及MED8敲低組sEVs處理後的細胞進行RNA測序分析，結果顯示差異表達基因富集於線粒體鈣轉運通路，而該通路是調控細胞氧化還原穩態的關鍵環節。據此我們推測：sEV-MED8可通過促進線粒體鈣離子內流，誘導線粒體ROS過量產生，進而導致肝細胞氧化應激損傷及惡性表型轉化。進一步的實驗驗證顯示，sEV-MED8可提高線粒體超氧化物水平與鈣離子濃度；同時我們也發現，sEV-MED8可上調線粒體鈣單向轉運體（Mitochondrial Calcium Uniporter, MCU）表達，並提高線粒體膜電位水平，而MCU正是介導鈣離子從胞質向線粒體轉運的關鍵蛋白。 綜上，本研究證實sEV-MED8通過調控MCU介導的線粒體鈣離子內流，誘導線粒體氧化應激。基於前期研究基礎，我們提出假說：sEV-MED8通過擾亂線粒體內鈣離子穩態，增強線粒體超氧化物產生，導致DNA損傷，促進HCC進展。本項目擬開展以下三方面研究：1）解析sEV-MED8調控線粒體鈣離子內流的分子機制；2）明確sEV-MED8通過調節MCU表達從而調控氧化應激、驅動HCC進展的具體作用；3）評估MED8在HCC臨牀樣本中的表達特徵及臨牀意義。本研究將進一步完善sEVs介導氧化還原失衡的調控機制，爲開發靶向動態調控ROS的HCC治療新策略提供理論依據和實驗基礎。

17120626.value: Aberrant glycosylation is a hallmark of cancer progression, profoundly impacting cell signaling, adhesion, and interactions with the immune system. Among these modifications, fucosylation—the attachment of fucose sugars to glycan termini—stands out for its strong association with metastatic disease and poor outcomes in diverse cancers. While elevated fucosylation correlates with aggressive malignancies, the mechanisms by which it drives tumor progression, and in particular, which protein substrates are involved, remain incompletely understood. Our prior research identified FUT5 (fucosyltransferase 5), a Golgi-resident enzyme mediating α1-3/4 fucose addition to terminal glycans, as a key driver of peritoneal dissemination in ovarian cancer. Ultimately, this work will establish fucosylated, extracellular PODXL as a promising biomarker and therapeutic target, unveiling new insights for how aberrant fucosylation rewires protein secretion and cancer biology. 異常醣基化是癌症進展的重要特徵，深度影響細胞訊號傳遞、細胞黏附及其與免疫系統之交互作用。在眾多醣基化修飾中，岩藻糖化（fucosylation，即在醣鏈末端接上岩藻糖）因與多種癌症之轉移及不良預後高度相關而備受關注。儘管岩藻糖化程度升高普遍見於高侵襲性腫瘤，其驅動腫瘤惡化之確切分子機制，尤其所牽涉之關鍵蛋白受質，至今仍未完全闡明。我們先前之研究發現，FUT5（岩藻糖轉移酶5）—— 種位於高基氏體、負責催化α1-3/4岩藻糖接合至末端醣鏈的酵素——為卵巢癌腹腔擴散之關鍵驅動因子。更重要的是，我們現有數據顯示FUT5之表現量與高惡性度漿液性卵巢癌（最常見且侵襲性最強之亞型）的晚期分期及較差存活率密切相關。然而，由於癌細胞中醣蛋白具高度結構異質性與複雜性，鑑定FUT5特異性下游受質蛋白仍具相當挑戰。 為彌補此研究缺口，我們運用已建立、可強制表現FUT5之卵巢癌轉移模型，藉此富集經FUT5修飾之蛋白質。透過結合凝集素親和層析純化與定量質譜分析，系統建構出依賴 FUT5 修飾的醣蛋白體圖譜。在眾多顯著富集的候選蛋白中，我們鎖定足萼蛋白（PODXL）——一種高度醣基化、且在多種癌症中皆與不良預後相關的唾液黏蛋白——確認其為FUT5之受質。生化實驗進一步證實，FUT5專一性地在PODXL之黏蛋白型O-醣鏈結構上進行岩藻糖化修飾。值得注意的是，我們發現一種前所未見的分泌型PODXL，其釋放至細胞外之過程受FUT5介導之岩藻糖化顯著促進，並透過一條先前未被揭示、依賴鈣離子的胞吐途徑進行，此機制截然不同於傳統蛋白酶剪切釋放或胞外囊泡包裝之分泌模式。初步蛋白質體學分析顯示，此分泌型、經岩藻糖化修飾之PODXL，可能在功能上穩定與血管新生相關之生長因子，進而重塑腫瘤微環境，提升腫瘤之轉移潛能。 基於上述具開創性之發現，我們提出以下假說：FUT5透過催化PODXL之O-型岩藻糖化，促使產生並分泌一種具腫瘤特異性之PODXL醣型，促進腫瘤血管新生，進而驅動卵巢癌之轉移進展。據此，本研究計畫將：（1）闡明FUT5所驅動之岩藻糖化如何改變PODXL在卵巢癌細胞中之運輸分子機制；（2）鑑定細胞外PODXL之醣型特徵及其分泌機制；（3）釐清分泌型PODXL在血管新生及臨床預後中所扮演之角色。本研究成果將確立經岩藻糖化修飾之細胞外PODXL，作為極具潛力之生物標誌物與治療標的，並為異常岩藻糖化如何重編蛋白質分泌與癌症生物學提供新見解。

17120726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17120726.value: The crosstalk between gut and adipose tissues plays an important role in maintaining metabolic health by fine-tuning energy homeostasis, glucolipid metabolism and inflammation. Furthermore, TFF2-deficient mice are resistant to diet-induced obesity, insulin resistance and glucolipid dysregulation, whereas elevating plasma TFF2 exacerbates obesity-induced metabolic disorders. On the basis of these findings, we propose TFF2 as a key component of gut-adipose axis, in which gut-secreted TFF2 exerts its endocrine actions on adipocytes regulating lipid metabolism and adipokine production. Additionally, gut-secreted TFF2 acts locally modulating immune micro-environment, which in turn alters gut microbiota composition and/or metabolism. In obesity, augmented production of gut-derived TFF2 impairs the gut-adipose tissue crosstalk through its direct actions on adipocytes and indirect effects by disrupting gut microbiota balance, thus triggering adipose tissue dysfunction, metabolic inflammation, insulin resistance and glucolipid dysregulation. This project aims to validate this hypothesis by comprehensively investigating the impact of global and gut-selective ablation of TFF2 on adipose tissue pathophysiology, whole-body metabolism and insulin sensitivity in obese mice. The findings from this study are expected to provide scientific evidence for developing novel peptide hormone-based pharmacotherapies by targeting gut-adipose tissue axis. 腸道與脂肪組織之間的相互對話，透過精確調節能量穩態、糖脂代謝和炎症反應，在維持代謝健康中發揮著重要作用。這兩個器官之間的雙向溝通是由脂肪分泌的脂肪因子和腸道分泌的激素所介導，而這些激素又受到腸道菌群及其微生物代謝產物的調節。腸道—脂肪組織軸的失調（通常由激素產生/功能異常以及腸道菌群失衡引起）是導致肥胖及其相關代謝併發症的重要因素。 三葉因子2（Trefoil factor 2, TFF2）是一種主要在胃黏膜細胞中表達的分泌蛋白。在功能上，它與保護胃黏膜屏障以及調節炎症和免疫反應密切相關。我們對病態肥胖個體進行的基於Olink技術的蛋白質組學分析顯示，TFF2是血漿蛋白中排名靠前的標誌物，在減重手術引起的體重減輕後顯著下降。在患有糖尿病前期的超重/肥胖華人中，我們亦發現為期12週的高強度運動干預所引起的血漿TFF2水平變化，與胰島素敏感性及血糖控制的改善密切相關。此外，TFF2缺陷小鼠對飲食誘導的肥胖、胰島素抵抗和糖脂代謝紊亂具有耐受性，而提高血漿TFF2水平則會加劇肥胖引起的代謝障礙。通過體內追蹤螢光標記的TFF2、體外結合實驗以及功能分析，我們發現 TFF2可直接作用於脂肪細胞，從而調節脂肪分解和脂聯素的分泌。基於這些發現，我們提出TFF2是腸道—脂肪軸的核心組成部分：在該軸中，腸道分泌的TFF2對脂肪細胞發揮內分泌作用，調節脂質代謝和脂肪因子的產生；同時，腸道分泌的TFF2亦在局部發揮作用，調節免疫微環境，進而改變腸道菌群的組成和/或代謝。在肥胖狀態下，腸道來源的TFF2產量增加，一方面直接作用於脂肪細胞，另一方面通過破壞腸道菌群平衡發揮間接影響，從而損害了腸道與脂肪組織之間的對話，進而引發脂肪組織功能障礙、代謝性發炎、胰島素抵抗和糖脂代謝紊亂。 本項目旨在通過全面研究全身性及腸道特異性敲除TFF2對肥胖小鼠脂肪組織病理生理學、全身代謝和胰島素敏感性的影響，進一步驗證這一假設。此外，我們計劃闡明TFF2在脂肪細胞中發揮多重作用的受體及細胞內信號通路，並探討腸道菌群及其代謝產物在TFF2誘導的代謝紊亂中的角色。我們還將進行概念驗證研究，評估通過抗體介導中和循環系統中的TFF2在對抗肥胖相關代謝併發症中的治療潛力。這項研究的發現有望為開發靶向腸道—脂肪組織軸的新型肽類激素藥物療法提供科學依據。

17121126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17121126.value: Accurate completion of DNA replication and faithful chromosome segregation are crucial for cell viability and genome stability. Replication stress, a key driver of chromosomal instability in early tumorigenesis, impedes replication fork progression, leading to incomplete DNA replication and persistent DNA intermediates linking sister chromatids. Common fragile sites and early replication fragile sites are genomic regions that are inherently difficult to replicate and serve as hotspots for cancer-associated genome alternations, such as deletions and translocations. Structure-selective endonucleases (SSEs), including SLX1-SLX4, XPF-ERCC1, MUS81-EME1, and GEN1, play essential roles in processing DNA joint molecules and resolving replication intermediates to facilitate chromosome segregation. However, the precise coordination of these SSEs in cleaving under-replicated DNA and the downstream repair pathways remain incompletely understood. Our preliminary data reveal that GEN1 plays a distinct role in mitigating aphidicolin-induced replication stress, acting downstream of MUS81 to prevent fragile site instability. Specifically, GEN1-deficient cells, but not MUS81-deficient cells, exhibit elevated fragile-site ultrafine anaphase bridges and enhanced fragility at an AT-rich FLEX1 sequence. Whole-genome sequencing further revealed that loss of GEN1 leads to increased structural variations, especially deletions enriched in late-replicating and centromere-proximal regions. This project aims to elucidate how SSEs safeguard the genome under various sources of replication stress. First, using a comprehensive panel of SSE-deficient cell lines, we will characterize their responses to replication stress induced by low-dose aphidicolin, oncogene overexpression (Cyclin E and c-Myc), and BRCA2 depletion. Second, we hypothesize that SSE-mediated cleavage of under-replicated DNA trigger mitotic DNA synthesis (MiDAS) through distinct mechanisms. We will investigate the roles of DNA polymerases delta and zeta, as well as DNA end resection factors, in MiDAS and sister chromatid exchanges. Finally, whole-genome and MiDAS sequencing in SSE-deficient backgrounds will generate high-resolution maps of structural variations and MiDAS sites, providing new insights into the genomic consequences of impaired DNA cleavage and processing. Together, this research will advance our understanding of how SSEs process unreplicated DNA during replication stress and clarify their coordinated roles in maintaining fragile site integrity and genome stability. Ultimately, this work will shed light on fundamental mechanisms that prevent chromosomal instability, a key driver of cancer development. DNA 複製的精確完成與染色體的忠實分離，對細胞存活與基因體穩定性至關重要。複製壓力是早期腫瘤發生中染色體不穩定性的關鍵驅動因素，會阻礙複製叉前進，導致 DNA 複製不完整，並產生持續連結姐妹染色單體的 DNA 中間體。常見脆弱位點與早期複製脆弱位點是先天難以複製的基因體區域，也是癌症相關基因體變異（如缺失與易位）的熱點。結構選擇性核酸內切酶，包括 SLX1-SLX4、XPF-ERCC1、MUS81-EME1 與 GEN1，在處理 DNA 連接分子與解決複製中間體以促進染色體分離方面扮演關鍵角色。然而，這些 SSE 如何精確協同切割未完整複製 DNA，以及其下游修復路徑為何，仍未完全釐清。 我們的初步資料顯示，GEN1 在緩解 aphidicolin 誘發的複製壓力中具有獨特功能，並在 MUS81 下游作用以防止脆弱位點不穩定。具體而言，GEN1 缺失細胞（但非 MUS81 缺失細胞）呈現更高比例的脆弱位點超細後期橋，且在富含 AT 的 FLEX1 序列處顯示更高脆弱性。全基因體定序進一步顯示，GEN1 缺失會增加結構變異，特別是富集於晚期複製區域與著絲點近端區域的缺失。 本計畫旨在闡明 SSE 在不同來源複製壓力下如何維護基因體。首先，我們將利用完整的 SSE 缺失細胞株面板，系統性解析其對以下複製壓力來源的反應：低劑量 aphidicolin、致癌基因過度表現（Cyclin E 與 c-Myc）以及 BRCA2 耗竭。其次，我們假設 SSE 介導的未完整複製 DNA 切割，會透過不同機制啟動有絲分裂 DNA 合成（MiDAS）。我們將探討 DNA 聚合酶 delta 與 zeta，以及 DNA 末端切除因子，在 MiDAS 與姐妹染色單體交換中的作用。最後，我們將在 SSE 缺失背景下進行全基因體定序與 MiDAS 定序，建立高解析度的結構變異與 MiDAS 位點圖譜，以提供 DNA 切割與處理受損之基因體後果的新見解。 綜上所述，本研究將推進我們對 SSE 在複製壓力期間處理未複製 DNA 之機制的理解，並釐清其在維持脆弱位點完整性與基因體穩定性上的協同角色。最終，本研究將闡明預防染色體不穩定性的基礎機制，而此不穩定性正是癌症發展的重要驅動因子。

17121226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17121226.value: 闡明雙殼綱生物礦化在演化、發育及生態尺度上的功能調控

17121226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17121226.value: Bivalves are marvels of nature. These animals are fundamental ecosystem engineers that have influenced human culture, activities and nutrition since prehistoric times. Now, their exploitation represents a 20 billion US$ industry that provides food for a growing global population. Most people have an acquired taste for their soft bodies but consider their shells a waste product. However, shells are not just inert objects. These complex biological structures are key players in important coastal ecosystems services and provide ecofriendly building materials to humans as well as valuable information about their environment. Despite of this, bivalves, their shells and their socio-ecological value are under threat due to overexploitation and climate change. In order to preserve them, we need first to understand them, uncovering the diversity of blueprints and mechanisms by which bivalves make and regulate their shells. The architecture of these biological structures is based on CaCO3 crystals (calcite/aragonite) that form complex biominerals and biocomposites with proteins that determine shell microstructures (i.e., prismatic, nacreous, foliated, crossed-lamellar, composite-prismatic, and homogeneous). Nevertheless, most of the knowledge regarding bivalve shell biomineralization is limited to few model species, and large knowledge gaps remain in how bivalve molluscs construct and maintain their shells. While the general framework behind the biological control of these processes is well-established, Bivalve biomineralization is hypothesised to vary as a function of the evolutionary history of the species (Objective 1), their developmental backgrounds (Objective 2), and their sensitivities to environmental changes (Objective 3). Therefore, understanding the functional regulation underpinning these phenotypic differences is vital for elucidating the mechanisms that contribute to shell diversity and resilience in bivalves, and their ability to adapt to environmental changes. While the inventories of molluscan shell-forming proteins continue to grow at an exponential rate, the mechanisms by which these proteins are regulated and the underlying gene regulatory networks that have evolved to coordinate these processes remain less understood. Harnessing this knowledge can help us to develop a sustainable use of these biological resources, particularly in developing countries such as those across the Indo-Pacific. For many coastal communities in this region, bivalves and their shells are an integral part of their culture (e.g., arts, religion), well-being (e.g., traditional medicine), economy (e.g., tourism, aquaculture), and development (e.g., housing material). Moreover, by filling this major knowledge gap, we can open up novel research areas that integrate the diverse sectors interested in biominerals and biomaterials for both basic and translational research. 雙殼綱是自然界的奇蹟。這些動物是基本的生態系統工程師，自史前時代以來就一直影響著人類的文化、活動和營養。如今，對牠們的開發已發展成一個價值200億美元的產業，為全球不斷增長的人口提供糧食。大多數人對其柔軟的身體情有獨鍾，卻將其貝殼視為廢棄物。然而，貝殼並非僅是惰性物體。這些複雜的生物結構在重要的海岸生態系統服務中扮演著關鍵角色，既能為人類提供環保的建築材料，也能提供有關其環境的寶貴資訊。儘管如此，由於過度開發和氣候變化，雙殼綱、其貝殼及其社會生態價值正面臨威脅。為了保護牠們，我們首先需要了解牠們，揭示雙殼綱製造和調控其貝殼的多樣化藍圖與機制。這些生物結構的建築學基礎是碳酸鈣（CaCO3）晶體（方解石/文石），它們與蛋白質一起形成複雜的生物礦物和生物複合材料，從而決定了貝殼的微細結構（即稜柱狀、珍珠層狀、葉狀、交叉層狀、複合稜柱狀和均質結構）。然而，目前關於雙殼綱貝殼生物礦化的多數知識僅局限於少數模式物種，而在雙殼綱軟體動物如何構建和維持其貝殼方面，仍存在巨大的知識空白。雖然這些過程背後生物控制的總體框架已確立，但有假說認為，雙殼綱的生物礦化會隨着物種的演化歷史（目標1）、其發育背景（目標2）以及對環境變化的敏感性（目標3）而有所不同。因此，理解支持這些表型差異的功能調控，對於闡明有助於雙殼綱貝殼多樣性與韌性，以及牠們適應環境變化能力的機制至關重要。雖然軟體動物成殼蛋白質的清單正以指數級速度增長，但這些蛋白質的調控機制，以及為協調這些過程而演化出的底層基因調控網絡，至今仍不甚明瞭。利用這些知識可以幫助我們發展這些生物資源的可持續利用，特別是在印太地區等發展中國家。對於該地區的許多沿海社區而言，雙殼綱及其貝殼是其文化（如藝術、宗教）、福祉（如傳統醫學）、經濟（如旅遊業、水產養殖業）和發展（如建材）不可或缺的一部分。此外，透過填補這一重大的知識空白，我們可以開闢全新的研究領域，將對生物礦物和生物材料感興趣的不同領域整合起來，以進行基礎研究和轉化研究。

17121326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17121326.value: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a genetic neuromuscular disease caused by homozygous deletion of the survival motor neuron 1 (SMN1) gene, which encodes the ubiquitously expressed SMN1 protein crucial for the survival and homeostasis of spinal motor neurons (MNs). The disease severity inversely correlates with the copy number of the backup gene, SMN2, which predominantly produces truncated, non-functional protein due to splicing defects, with only a small fraction being functional. Insufficient SMN protein results in progressive, selective degeneration of motor axons and impaired muscle innervation, compromising neuromuscular junction integrity. Consequently, SMA patients suffer from impaired gross motor skills, muscle atrophy, and in severe cases, early mortality. Current FDA-approved treatments (Nusinersen, Zolgensma, and Risdiplam) that elevate SMN protein levels have improved motor function and survival but are not curative. Ongoing clinical trials primarily target muscle weakness rather than addressing the underlying motor axon deficits. A deep understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying MN vulnerability in SMA could facilitate the development of better therapies aimed at regenerating spinal MNs and their axons, potentially altering disease progression. Our pilot studies demonstrate that the MN-specific Rho GTPase-activating protein (RhoGAP), Deleted in Liver Cancer 1 isoform 1 (DLC1-i1), is essential for motor neuron survival and axon outgrowth. Reduced expression of DLC1-i1 impairs neuromuscular junction formation in neuromuscular organoids (NMOs) derived from SMA patients, while overexpression of DLC1-i1 rescues these deficits. In an SMA mouse model, DLC1-i1 gene therapy outperforms SMN1 gene therapy in extending lifespan, improving locomotor function, and restoring SMN protein levels in the spinal cord, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target. These findings lead us to hypothesize that decreased DLC1-i1 expression increases MN vulnerability in SMA, and that DLC1-i1 gene therapy could potentiate the therapeutic effects of existing SMN-enhancing treatments. In this proposal, we will test this hypothesis by investigating: (i) the regulation of MN-specific DLC1-i1 expression and whether DLC1-i1 functions as a RhoGAP during MN development, (ii) the molecular mechanisms by which DLC1-i1 regulates SMN expression and promotes motor axon outgrowth; (iii) the combined effects of DLC1-i1 gene therapy with SMN-enhancing drugs in patient-derived NMOs and SMA mouse model. Successful completion of this project will address the long-standing question of MN vulnerability in SMA by elucidating how MN-specific DLC1-i1 links global SMN deficiency to motor axon degeneration, thereby establishing it as a promising target for more effective therapies.

17121926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17121926.value: 闡明葡萄糖調節蛋白78於SARS-CoV-1、SARS-CoV-2及HCoV-NL63感染中的差異性作用

17121926.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17121926.value: Dr Chan, Jasper Fuk Woo Dr Li, Cun Prof Ni, Tao

17121926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17121926.value: To date, seven coronaviruses are known to infect and spread in humans. Infection by the highly-pathogenic coronaviruses (MERS-CoV, SARS-CoV-1, and SARS-CoV-2) may result in severe manifestations and can be lethal, while the seasonal coronaviruses (HCoV-229E, HCoV-OC43, HCoV-NL63, and HCoV-HKU1) result in much milder infections. More recently, the porcine deltacoronavirus (Hu-PDCoV) and canine coronavirus human pneumonia 2018 (CCoV-HuPn-2018) have been reported in humans, but their characteristics and impact remain poorly understood. The increasing frequency of coronavirus spillover events into human populations underscores the critical need to understand the underlying mechanisms of coronavirus tropism and replication fitness within host tissues, which remain incompletely characterized. In this context, SARS-CoV-1, SARS-CoV-2, and HCoV-NL63 serve as excellent models for comparative studies. Although all three viruses utilize angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) as their primary receptor for infection, they differ significantly in tropism and pathogenicity. Our pilot studies have revealed that while glucose-regulated protein 78 (GRP78) facilitates the infection of SARS-CoV-1 and SARS-CoV-2, it potently inhibits HCoV-NL63 infection. We further demonstrated that GRP78 is more abundantly expressed in human lung cells than in human nasal epithelial cells, a difference that may contribute to the divergent tissue replication fitness among these viruses. Mechanistically, our preliminary results indicate that while the spike S1 region of all three viruses binds to GRP78, the protein reduces cell-cell fusion and ACE2-spike interaction specifically for HCoV-NL63, with no such effect observed for SARS-CoV-1 or SARS-CoV-2. Overall, these results indicate a potential role of GRP78 in contributing to the divergent tropism and pathogenicity of SARS-CoV-1 and SARS-CoV-2 when compared HCoV-NL63. While the intrinsic differences among these viruses imply that additional host and viral factors must regulate their distinct virological features, precisely dissecting the contribution of GRP78 will represent a meaningful step forward in exploring the differential characteristics of highly-pathogenic and seasonal coronaviruses. Building on the findings from our preliminary studies, this proposal aims to further investigate the distinct functional role of GRP78 in the life cycle of SARS-CoV-1, SARS-CoV-2, and HCoV-NL63. We will then dissect the mechanism underlying the differential utilization of GRP78 by HCoV-NL63 compared to SARS-CoV-1 and SARS-CoV-2. Collectively, our proposed work will advance our understanding on the entry, tropism, and tissue replication fitness of these viruses, thereby elucidating key differences between the highly-pathogenic and seasonal coronaviruses. 至今已知有七種冠狀病毒可以感染人類並在人群中傳播。高致病性冠狀病毒（MERS-CoV、SARS-CoV-1及SARS-CoV-2）感染可引發嚴重臨床病徵包括死亡，而季節性冠狀病毒（HCoV-229E、HCoV-OC43、HCoV-NL63及HCoV-HKU1）一般僅引起輕微的上呼吸道感染。近年來，豬冠狀病毒Hu-PDCoV及犬冠狀病毒CCoV-HuPn-2018也有人類感染的報導，但其病毒學特性與影響目前仍所知甚少。冠狀病毒跨物種傳播至人類的頻率日漸增加，突出了深入探究冠狀病毒感染嗜性及複製適應性的重要性，但其中機制至今仍未完全闡明。 在此前提下，SARS-CoV-1、SARS-CoV-2及HCoV-NL63這三個病毒可以作為一個有效的比較模型。儘管此三種病毒均利用血管收縮素轉化酶2（ACE2）作為其主要感染受體，但它們在感染嗜性與致病性方面卻有顯著差異。我們的前期研究顯示，葡萄糖調節蛋白78（GRP78）可促進SARS-CoV-1及SARS-CoV-2的病毒入侵，卻強烈抑制HCoV-NL63的病毒入侵。後續研究進一步證實，GRP78在人類肺細胞中的表達量顯著高於人類鼻上皮細胞，此差異與這三種病毒在不同組織中的複製適應性有所關聯。在機制層面，我們的研究結果顯示儘管三種病毒的Spike蛋白S1區域均可與GRP78結合，但GRP78只抑制HCoV-NL63的細胞融合及ACE2-Spike蛋白互作，而對SARS-CoV-1及SARS-CoV-2則無此抑制效果。整體而言，我們的前期發現指出GRP78在SARS-CoV-1及SARS-CoV-2與HCoV-NL63的感染嗜性及致病性差異中扮演重要角色。雖然三個病毒之間還存在不少本質上的區別，但精準解析GRP78的貢獻將為探究高致病性與季節性冠狀病毒之間的差異性跨出重要一步。 延伸於我們前期的研究發現，本計畫將進一步探討GRP78在SARS-CoV-1、SARS-CoV-2及HCoV-NL63感染中所擔當的功能。我們將進一步解析HCoV-NL63與SARS-CoV-1及SARS-CoV-2在利用GRP78上的差異機制。綜上所述，本研究的工作將深化我們對冠狀病毒的入侵、感染嗜性及複製適應性的理解，進而闡明高致病性與季節性冠狀病毒之間的關鍵性差異。

17122426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17122426.value: ROR1⁺肝癌细胞通过BSG（CD147）调控CAF活化促进肿瘤干性与耐药的机制研究

17122426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17122426.value: Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC) remains one of the most prevalent and aggressive malignancies in the region, with limited treatment options and poor prognosis. Tumor cell plasticity enables HCC cells to undergo molecular and phenotypic changes that promote stem-like states, which are associated with therapy resistance and tumor relapse. Beyond intrinsic mechanisms, the tumor microenvironment (TME) supports these stem-like phenotypes, underscoring the need for targeted therapeutic strategies that address both tumor cells and their niche. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), representing the most abundant cell type in the TME, have been reported to play a pro-tumorigenic role in multiple cancers including HCC. In HCC, more than 80% of cases develop within the context of cirrhosis, which is always accompanied by an enrichment of CAFs due to chronic inflammation. Therefore, it is crucial to dissect the potential crosstalk between CAFs and HCC cells. Our preliminary data reveal that the oncofetal protein ROR1 is highly expressed in HCC, correlating with tumor aggressiveness, poor prognosis, and stemness features. ROR1 expression peaks during fetal liver development and is enriched in hepatic progenitor-like tumors, suggesting its role in maintaining cancer stemness. Functional studies involving CRISPR activation of ROR1 in vivo demonstrate that it promotes tumor-initiating potential and recruits and activates CAFs, further fueling tumor progression. Mechanistically, our pilot data suggests ROR1 to bind to BSG to activate FAK signaling, enhancing the secretion of CXCL1/IL-8, which in turn drives CAF-mediated remodeling of the TME to promote HCC progression in a positive feed-forward manner through collagen-mediated signaling. While ROR1 has been previously reported in HCC, the identification of BSG as a key binding partner, the delineation of the ROR1/BSG/FAK signaling axis, and its specific role in orchestrating CAF-mediated TME remodeling represent novel and previously uncharacterized mechanisms. This project aims to elucidate the functional role and underlying mechanisms of ROR1 in CAF-mediated remodeling of the TME to promote HCC progression and stemness. Additionally, we will evaluate the prognostic potential of ROR1, BSG, and CAF-associated markers, and explore the therapeutic feasibility of targeting ROR1 using neutralizing antibodies or liver-directed AAV8-shRor1 gene therapy to abrogate the cancer stemness niche. Findings of this study will deepen our understanding of phenotypic plasticity within the HCC microenvironment, offering new avenues for precision-targeted therapies to curb tumor progression, prevent recurrence, and improve clinical outcomes. The importance of what can be achieved cannot be overemphasized given the high incidence and mortality of HCC in the local community and beyond. 肝细胞癌（HCC）在亚太地区仍是最常见且最具侵袭性的恶性肿瘤之一，其治疗选择有限，预后较差。肿瘤可塑性促使HCC细胞发生分子及表型改变，获得干性细胞样特性，从而驱动治疗耐药与复发。除内在机制外，肿瘤微环境（TME）同样支持这些干性表型，故治疗策略需同时靶向肿瘤细胞及其所处微环境。 肿瘤相关成纤维细胞（CAF）是TME中数量最多的细胞类型，已被证实在包括HCC在内的多种恶性肿瘤中发挥促癌功能。在HCC中逾80%的病例发生于肝硬化基础上，而肝硬化因慢性炎症常伴随CAF大量浸润。因此，阐明CAF与HCC细胞间的交互作用尤为关键。 前期数据显示，癌胚蛋白ROR1在HCC中的表达水平与肿瘤侵袭性、不良预后及干性特征呈正相关。ROR1于胎儿肝脏发育期高表达，并在肝祖细胞样肿瘤中高度富集，提示其与癌症干性维持相关。基于CRISPR技术调控小鼠肝肿瘤内ROR1的功能研究显示，过表达ROR1可增强HCC细胞成瘤能力，并招募及活化CAF，进而驱动肿瘤进展。机制上，ROR1结合BSG (CD147) 激活FAK，促进CXCL1/IL-8分泌以激活CAF；CAF继而分泌胶原蛋白并与肿瘤细胞表面受体结合，正反馈强化FAK信号，驱动TME重塑，促进HCC进展。尽管ROR1在HCC中的作用已有报道，但BSG作为其结合伙伴的鉴定、ROR1/BSG/FAK轴的阐明及其在CAF介导TME重塑中的角色，均为新发现。本研究旨在解析ROR1在CAF介导的TME重塑中的作用，并揭示其驱动HCC进展与干性维持的分子机制。此外，我们将评估ROR1、BSG及CAF标志物在预测HCC预后中的价值。探索以中和抗体或肝靶向AAV8-shRor1基因疗法清除ROR1，从而破坏HCC细胞干性维持微环境治疗方案的可行性。本研究将加深对HCC微环境可塑性的理解，为精准靶向治疗抑制肿瘤进展、预防复发及改善预后提供新途径。鉴于HCC在香港本地及周边地区的高发与高致死率，本研究具有重要的现实意义与临床转化价值。

17122726.value: 揭示 MDM2 在著床前發育及滋養層幹細胞分化中的作用：對著床成功的啟示

17122726.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17122726.value: Prof Chiu, Chi Ngong Dr Han, Dong Prof Liu, Pengtao Prof Ng, Ernest Hung Yu

17122726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17122726.value: Embryo implantation failure is a major hurdle in assisted reproductive technology (ART), with only 30-50% of embryo transfers leading to successful pregnancies, even with advanced genetic screening. While preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A) identifies embryos with chromosomal issues, many genetically normal embryos still fail to implant. This suggests other factors affect an embryo’s ability to successfully attach to the uterus, a critical step for pregnancy. Our research investigates MDM2, a key regulator of the p53 pathway, which has emerged as an essential determinant in early embryogenesis and trophoblast lineage specification. Our pilot clinical studies using DNA/RNA co-sequencing of trophectoderm (TE) biopsies revealed significant MDM2 upregulation in failed implantations compared to successful ones. Our initial study analyzed trophectoderm biopsies (the embryo’s outer layer) from 12 successful and 13 failed implantations, identifying 472 differently expressed genes, with MDM2 significantly higher in failures. Larger studies with 46 genetically normal embryos (23 successful vs. 23 failed) and 73 abnormal embryos (45 successful vs. 28 failed) confirmed 31 key genes, including consistent MDM2 upregulation, which correlated with lower implantation success. Crucially, functional validation in a mouse model confirmed that MDM2 upregulation specifically impairs implantation without affecting blastocyst development. Higher MDM2 levels were also found in placental tissues from patients with recurrent miscarriages, highlighting its role in pregnancy challenges. To understand how MDM2 affects implantation, we used innovative lab models, including human expanded potential stem cell (hEPSC)-derived blastoids (embryo-like structures) and trophoblast stem cells, alongside mouse embryos. Our findings show that high MDM2 levels disrupt the development of key placental cells (syncytiotrophoblasts and extravillous trophoblasts) and interfere with a signaling pathway (Hippo) critical for implantation. By manipulating MDM2 and its related protein p53, we are uncovering the molecular mechanisms behind these effects. To apply these findings, we will validate MDM2 as a predictive marker for implantation success in 100 patients undergoing PGT-A (50 implantation successful vs. 50 implantation failed). In addition, we will also prospectively test MDM2 as a clinical biomarker in a cohort of 70 patients undergoing PGT-A, assessing performance metrics against morphology- and aneuploidy-based selection. This integrated approach aims to establish MDM2 as a molecular signature for implantation potential, addressing the unmet need for physiological markers beyond genomic screening. By revealing how MDM2 affects implantation and developing a new way to identify viable embryos, this research aims to enhance ART success rates, offering hope to couples facing infertility. 胚胎著床失敗是輔助生殖技術（ART）中的主要障礙，即使採用先進的基因篩檢，胚胎移植後成功懷孕的比例仍僅有30-50%。雖然胚胎著床前染色體非整倍體基因檢測（PGT-A）能找出帶有染色體異常的胚胎，但許多基因正常的胚胎依然無法著床。這表明還有其他因素影響胚胎成功附著子宮的能力，而這正是懷孕的關鍵步驟。 我們的研究將探討MDM2，它是p53路徑的關鍵調控因數，已在早期胚胎發育與滋養層譜系分化中表現為重要決定因素。我們利用滋養外胚層（TE）切片進行DNA/RNA共定序的先導臨床研究發現，與成功著床者相比，著床失敗者的MDM2表達水準顯著上調。初步研究分析了12例成功與13例失敗著床的滋養外胚層切片（胚胎的外層），鑑定出472個差異表達基因，其中MDM2在失敗組中顯著較高。後續較大規模研究通過納入46顆基因正常胚胎（23顆成功 vs. 23顆失敗）與73顆異常胚胎（45顆成功 vs. 28顆失敗），確認了31個關鍵基因，包括MDM2持續上調，且與較低的著床成功率相關。關鍵的是，小鼠模型的功能驗證證實，MDM2上調會特異性損害著床過程，但不影響囊胚發育。反覆性流產患者的胎盤組織中也發現較高的MDM2表現量，顯示其在懷孕相關困難中的角色。 為了瞭解MDM2如何影響著床，我們使用創新的實驗室模型，包括由人類擴展潛能幹細胞（hEPSC）衍生的類囊胚（類胚胎結構）和滋養層幹細胞，以及小鼠胚胎。我們的研究結果顯示，高MDM2表現量會幹擾關鍵胎盤細胞（合體滋養層細胞與絨毛外滋養層細胞）的發育，並影響對著床至關重要的Hippo信號通路。透過調節MDM2及其相關蛋白p53，我們正逐步揭示這些效應背後的分子機制。 為將這些發現應用於臨床，我們將在100位接受PGT-A的患者（50例著床成功 vs. 50例著床失敗）中驗證MDM2作為著床成功預測標誌物。此外，我們也將在70位接受PGT-A的患者所組成的前瞻性隊列中測試MDM2作為臨床生物標誌物的能力，並與基於形態學及非整倍體的篩選方式進行比較。這套整合性方法旨在確立MDM2作為著床潛能的分子特徵，以填補基因體篩檢之外對生理標誌物的需求。 透過揭示MDM2如何影響著床，並開發辨識具有存活能力胚胎的新方法，本研究旨在提升ART的成功率，為面對不孕的夫婦帶來希望。

17123126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17123126.value: 超越重編程的年輕化：無需山中因子的細胞更新表觀遺傳開關

17123126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17123126.value: During ageing, cells accumulate damage, and the epigenetic boundaries of cellular identity get blurred, causing functional decline. Yet, embryos from ageing parents reprogram to regain their youth. Analogously, during somatic cell reprogramming toward induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) via the overexpression of the four Yamanaka factors — Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, and c-Myc (OSKM) —the age of the cells is reset to an embryonic–like state. The time-restricted expression of OSKM in specific organs in mice leads to rejuvenation, the reversal of damage, and organ repair. This so-called partial reprogramming presented the captivating possibility that age can be reset to a youthful state without changing cellular identity. However, sustained OSKM expression would lead to the formation of oncogenic cells, and even brief expression periods may lead to a dangerous destabilization of cell identity. Here, we propose to discover and validate alternative rejuvenation factors that drive the epigenetic age reset without reprogramming cell fates. Our team has previously expanded the repertoire of reprogramming factors, discovered and characterized new reprogramming technologies, developed stem cell models for age-related diseases, redesigned more powerful reprogramming factors, and extended the lifespan of prematurely aging mice. Our success in these areas encouraged us to perform multiplexed assays to rejuvenate aged human fibroblasts using genome-wide transcription factor libraries, leading to a candidate set of 35 new rejuvenation factors. In this project, we will evaluate whether this set of factors alone or in combination can rejuvenate human cells using a panel of molecular, cellular, and epigenetic tests established in our laboratory. To enhance safety and reduce off-target risks, we will de-prioritise rejuvenation factors facilitate pluripotency reprogramming. As an orthogonal rejuvenation assay, we will investigate whether our factors can activate quiescent neural stem cells to generate new neurons, thereby providing a potential avenue to combat brain aging. Top-performing and safe factors will be tested for their ability to repair tissues and extend lifespan in mouse models. Lastly, we will leverage our insights into the sequence-structure-function relationships of reprogramming factors and utilize a structure-aware artificial intelligence workflow to redesign rejuvenation factors, thereby enhancing their fidelity and performance. Our vision is to discover safe alternatives for the oncogenic Yamanaka factors that revert aged cells to a youthful and active state without destabilising their identity. This work will lay the foundation for the removal of a major barrier for the application of cellular rejuvenation for organ repair and healthspan extension. 在衰老過程中，細胞會累積損傷，細胞身份的表觀遺傳邊界將變得模糊，從而導致功能衰退。然而，當細胞經歷受精和胚胎發育後，下一代個體會重獲青春。類似地，在通過表達四個山中因子——Oct4、Sox2、Klf4和c-Myc（OSKM）——將體細胞重編程為誘導多能幹細胞（iPSCs）的過程中，細胞的年齡也被重置為類似胚胎的狀態。在小鼠特定器官中限時表達OSKM可誘導年輕化、損傷逆轉和器官修復，這被稱為部分重編程。這些研究結果展現了在不改變細胞身份的情況下將年齡重置為年輕狀態的可能性。然而，持續的OSKM表達會導致致癌細胞的形成，即使是短暫的表達也可能導致細胞身份的不穩定。在此，我們將發現並驗證能夠驅動表觀遺傳年齡重置，而不改變細胞命運的替代性年輕化因子。我們的團隊此前已擴展了重編程因子的能力，發現並表徵了新的重編程技術，開發了年齡相關疾病的幹細胞模型，重新設計了更強大的重編程因子，並延長了早衰小鼠的壽命。我們在這些領域的成功鼓勵我們進行多重實驗，利用全基因組轉錄因子文庫使衰老的人類成纖維細胞年輕化，從而獲得了一個包含35種新年輕化因子的候選集合。在本項目中，我們將利用本實驗室建立的一系列分子、細胞和表觀遺傳學檢測方法，評估這組因子單獨或聯合使用是否能使人類細胞年輕化。為增強安全性並減少脫靶風險，我們將排除年輕化因子促進多能性重編程的可能性。作為正交檢測，我們將研究我們的因子是否能激活靜息神經幹細胞以產生新的神經元，從而為大腦的抗衰老提供潛在途徑。表現最佳且安全的因子將進行動物實驗，以評估其在小鼠模型中修復組織和延長壽命的能力。最後，我們將利用我們對重編程因子序列-結構-功能關係的深入理解，並運用人工智能工具來重新設計再生因子，從而提高其性能。我們的願景是發現致癌性山中因子的安全替代因子，這些替代因子能將衰老細胞恢復至年輕且活躍的狀態，同時不破壞其身份穩定性。這項工作將為細胞年輕化在器官修復和健康壽命延長方面的應用掃除一個主要障礙。

17123226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17123226.value: 組織胺在滋養層細胞分化中的作用及其與早發型子癇前症病理生理之關聯

17123226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17123226.value: Prof Chiu, Chi Ngong Dr Zhang, Qingqing

17123226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17123226.value: Preeclampsia (PE) is a common gestational disease affecting 2% to 5% of all pregnancies and is the leading cause of prenatal mortality and morbidity, resulting in heavy burdens on healthcare systems. PE is associated with a high incidence of fetal growth restriction, and short- and long-term maternal and perinatal complications. PE can be classified into early- or late-onset PE. Early-onset PE (EOPE) occurs before 34 weeks of gestation and is the most severe clinical variant of the disease. The etiology of EOPE involves defective trophoblast differentiation and functions, leading to abnormal placental development. Currently, there are no reliable prediction or treatment strategies for EOPE, mainly due to a lack of understanding of the underlying pathophysiology. The molecular mechanisms regulating human trophoblast differentiation are poorly understood. Histamine is a biogenic diamine abundantly expressed in early pregnancy. Amine oxidase copper containing 1 (AOC1) is the main histamine-degrading enzyme in the feto–maternal interface. Although data from animal models and clinical association studies support a role of histamine in placental development, its action in human pregnancy is unknown. Our unpublished data demonstrated that the level of both AOC1 in chorionic villi and circulating AOC1 cell-free RNA (cfRNA) are higher in first-trimester pregnant women who later develop EOPE compared to normotensive pregnancy. Furthermore, exogenous histamine and trophoblastic AOC1 can function to regulate trophoblast differentiation in vitro and in vivo. However, the mechanism underlying the function of histamine remains to be studied. We hypothesize that histamine regulates placental development in humans by modulating trophoblast differentiation and that dysregulation of histamine catabolism contributes to the pathophysiology of EOPE. To test this hypothesis, we will investigate the role and mechanism of histamine on regulating trophoblast differentiation using the latest technologies in transcriptomics, stem cells, organoids, and nanotechnology in vitro and in vivo, and correlating the findings with the clinical phenotypes of EOPE. We will also investigate the use of placenta-specific nanoparticle-based histamine signaling molecule as a treatment for EOPE. The outcome of this project will provide novel evidence of dysregulated histamine signaling in the pathology of EOPE, specifically the role of histamine on the differentiation and function of trophoblasts and on normal placental development. Clinically, the results will indicate the possible use of the level of histamine signaling molecules as an early prediction of EOPE and as a possible therapeutic target. 子癇前症（Preeclampsia, PE）是常見的妊娠併發症，發生率約 2% 至 5%，為導致孕產婦與胎兒發病及死亡的主因，對醫療體系造成沉重負擔。PE 常引發胎兒生長遲滯，並伴隨短、長期的母體與周產期併發症。臨床上，發生於妊娠 34 週前的「早發型子癇前症」（Early-onset PE, EOPE）是該疾病最嚴重的亞型。其病因與滋養層細胞（trophoblast）的分化及功能缺陷有關，進而導致胎盤發育異常。然而，由於對其潛在的病理生理機制認識不足，目前仍缺乏可靠的 EOPE 預測與治療策略。 目前，學界對調控人類滋養層細胞分化的分子機制仍所知有限。組織胺（Histamine）是一種在妊娠早期會大量生成的生物胺；而含銅胺氧化酶 1（Amine oxidase copper containing 1, AOC1）則是母胎介面（feto-maternal interface）主要的組織胺降解酶。儘管動物模型與臨床關聯研究均指出組織胺參與了胎盤發育，但其在人類妊娠中的具體作用尚未釐清。我們的初步數據顯示，與血壓正常的孕婦相比，後來發展為 EOPE 的第一孕期孕婦，其絨毛膜絨毛內的 AOC1 表現量，以及血液循環中的 AOC1 游離 RNA（cfRNA）濃度均顯著較高。此外，體內外實驗亦顯示，外源性組織胺與滋養層細胞的 AOC1 能調控滋養層細胞的分化。然而，組織胺發揮此功能的具體機制仍有待深入探討。 基於上述發現，我們假設：組織胺能透過調節滋養層細胞分化來影響人類胎盤發育，而組織胺代謝降解的失調則是促進 EOPE 病理發展的關鍵。為驗證此假說，本計畫將結合轉錄體學、幹細胞、類器官與奈米科技等尖端技術，在體內、外模型中探討組織胺調控滋養層細胞分化的具體作用與機制，並將研究結果與 EOPE 的臨床表型進行關聯性分析。同時，我們也將評估利用「胎盤特異性奈米顆粒」遞送組織胺相關訊號分子，作為 EOPE 潛在治療策略的可行性。 本計畫預期將為「組織胺訊號失調參與 EOPE 的病理發展」提供嶄新證據，進一步釐清組織胺在滋養層細胞分化、功能及正常胎盤發育中的關鍵角色。在臨床應用上，本研究成果有望將組織胺相關訊號分子的濃度作為 EOPE 早期預測的生物標記，並為其提供極具潛力的全新治療標靶。

17123526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17123526.value: SRSF9 作爲肝細胞癌中 CD8⁺ T 細胞功能障礙及 PD-L1/VEGF-A 雙重阻斷耐藥的藥物靶向調控因子的表徵研究

17123526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17123526.value: Although atezolizumab plus bevacizumab targeting PD-L1 and VEGF-A is the standard first-line therapy for advanced disease, many patients particularly those harboring CTNNB1 mutations, exhibit intrinsic resistance that limits durable responses. In our preliminary work, an unbiased, genome-wide in vivo CRISPR/Cas9 knockout screen in an orthotopic HCC mouse model treated with anti-PD-L1 plus anti-VEGF-A identified the splicing factor SRSF9 (mouse ortholog Srsf9) as a central driver of resistance. Clinical validation in HCC specimens implied that high tumor SRSF9 expression correlates with shorter survival after dual immunotherapy, whereas low SRSF9 levels, together with abundant cytotoxic T lymphocyte infiltration, predicts improved outcomes. Functional assays, using antigen-specific OT-1 cocultures, indicated that genetic ablation of SRSF9 in HCC cells boosted CD8⁺ T-cell cytotoxic perforin and granzyme B levels, and enhanced their cytolytic activity against target cells. In a spontaneous MYC-lucOS;CTNNB1 HCC model, SRSF9 deletion combined with dual-antibody therapy profoundly suppressed tumor growth and extended survival, elevated intratumoral cytokines IFN-γ and TNF-α, promoted proliferation and effector functions of CD8⁺ T cells and NK cells, and reduced immunosuppressive M2 macrophages. Moreover, integrated bulk and single-cell RNA-seq of treated tumors revealed increased T cell infiltration and enrichment of IFN-γ response and MHC-Ⅰ antigen presentation pathways. Initial mechanistic studies suggested that SRSF9 regulates HCC cell-surface MHC-Ⅰ expression and that MHC-Ⅰ blockade abrogates CD8⁺ T-cell cytotoxicity. Alternative splicing analysis implicated SRSF9 in promoting exon 5 inclusion in CSDE1 transcripts, indicating a splicing-dependent mechanism that may stabilize CSDE1 mRNA and facilitate immune evasion. Importantly, apigenin (API), a common dietary flavonoid, directly bound to and potently inhibited SRSF9, selectively induced cytotoxicity in HCC cells while sparing normal hepatocytes, and converted immunologically “cold” tumors (MYC-luc;CTNNB1) into “hot” ones. To further delineate the mechanism and regulatory roles of SRSF9, I propose to address following 3 questions in this proposal: 1) to elucidate how SRSF9-mediated CSDE1 splicing modulates mRNA stability, MHC-Ⅰ surface expression and downstream CD8+ T cell function; 2) to determine whether API reverses SRSF9-driven aberrant splicing and restores tumor immune surveillance via the STAT1-MHC-I-CTL axis; and 3) to evaluate the safety and efficacy of API monotherapy and of API in synergy with atezolizumab-bevacizumab in preclinical HCC models. These studies will clarify how SRSF9-associated splicing orchestrates immune escape in HCC and provide a solid preclinical rationale for an API-atezolizumab-bevacizumab regimen to overcome resistance and improve patient outcomes. 肝細胞癌（HCC）仍是全球緻死率最高的噁性腫瘤之一。儘管針對PD-L1和VEGF-A的阿替利珠單抗（atezolizumab）聯合貝伐珠單抗（bevacizumab）療法已成爲晚期HCC的標準一線治療方案，但許多患者（尤其是攜帶*CTNNB1*突變的患者）表現出固有耐藥性，從而限製了療效的持久性。在我們的前期研究中，利用抗PD-L1聯合抗VEGF-A藥物治療的原位HCC小鼠模型，我們開展了一項無偏倚的全基因組體內CRISPR/Cas9敲除篩選，鑒定出剪接因子SRSF9（小鼠同源物爲Srsf9）是導緻耐藥的關鍵驅動因素。對HCC臨床樣本的驗証分析顯示，腫瘤中SRSF9的高表達與雙重免疫治療後的較短生存期相關；相反，SRSF9低表達聯合豐富的細胞毒性T淋巴細胞浸潤則預示着更好的預後。利用抗原特異性OT-1細胞共培養體繫進行的功能實驗表明，在HCC細胞中基因敲除SRSF9可提高CD8⁺ T細胞內穿孔素（perforin）和顆粒酶B（granzyme B）的水平，並增強其針對靶細胞的細胞毒活性。在自髮性*MYC-lucOS;CTNNB1* HCC模型中，SRSF9缺失聯合雙抗治療顯著抑製了腫瘤生長並延長了生存期；該聯合策略提高了腫瘤內IFN-γ和TNF-α細胞因子的水平，促進了CD8⁺ T細胞和NK細胞的增殖及效應功能，同時減少了具有免疫抑製作用的M2型巨噬細胞。此外，對經治療腫瘤進行的批量（bulk）與單細胞RNA測序分析顯示，T細胞浸潤增加，且IFN-γ應答及MHC-Ⅰ抗原呈遞通路顯著富集。初步機製研究表明，SRSF9調控肝細胞癌（HCC）細胞表麵的MHC-Ⅰ表達，且阻斷MHC-Ⅰ會消除CD8⁺ T細胞的細胞毒性作用。可變剪接分析提示，SRSF9促進了CSDE1轉錄本中外顯子5的保留（inclusion），揭示了一種依賴於剪接的機製：該機製可能通過穩定CSDE1 mRNA來促進腫瘤免疫逃逸。值得注意的是，芹菜素（API）——一種常見的膳食黃酮類化合物——能直接結合並強效抑製SRSF9；它在選擇性誘導HCC細胞死亡的同時不損傷正常肝細胞，並將免疫“冷”腫瘤（MYC-luc;CTNNB1）轉化爲“熱”腫瘤。爲進一步闡明SRSF9的機製及其調控作用，本研究擬探討以下三個問題：1) 闡明SRSF9介導的CSDE1剪接如何調控mRNA穩定性、MHC-Ⅰ表麵表達及下遊CD8⁺ T細胞功能；2) 確定API是否能逆轉由SRSF9驅動的異常剪接，並通過STAT1-MHC-I-CTL軸恢複腫瘤免疫監視；3) 在HCC臨床前模型中評估API單藥治療以及API與阿替利珠單抗（atezolizumab）聯合貝伐珠單抗（bevacizumab）協同治療的安全性和療效。這些研究將闡明SRSF9相關的剪接過程如何介導HCC中的免疫逃逸，並爲採用“API-阿替利珠單抗-貝伐珠單抗”聯合方案以克服耐藥性並改善患者預後提供堅實的臨床前理論依據。

17123626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17123626.value: 探究人類 ESCRT 蛋白 ALIX 作為正鏈 RNA 病毒促病毒因數的全新功能

17123626.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17123626.value: Dr Chan, Chi Ping Dr Zou, Jiahui

17123626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17123626.value: Background: Targeting a universal host protein exploited by common and medically important viruses would be a game-changing strategy that offers broad-spectrum solution and rapid pandemic control. Membrane-bound replication organelles (ROs) are a unifying feature among diverse positive-strand (+) RNA viruses, providing a protective niche for viral genome replication. Preliminary findings: We identified an endosomal sorting complex required for transport (ESCRT) protein ALIX that is a proviral factor of different human pathogenic (+) RNA viruses, including SARS-CoV-2, Zika virus (ZIKV), and Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71). While ALIX has been documented to facilitate virus budding particularly in HIV, here we uncovered a novel and unified function of ALIX to coordinate viral polymerase machinery of these (+) RNA viruses. We identified Nsp12 of SARS-CoV-2, 3D of EV-A71, and NS3 of ZIKV as ALIX-interactive proteins. We found these interactions consistently drive viral proteins to ROs, where replication-transcription complexes (RTC) are typically assembled. Of note, blocking each ALIX-viral protein interaction via the same peptide inhibitor can achieve antiviral efficacy across all three viruses. Hypothesis: Based on functional similarity of the identified viral proteins as well as consistent subcellular sites of the visualized host-virus colocalizations, we hypothesis that ALIX is a shared proviral factor of (+) RNA viruses by modulating viral ROs formation and RTC assembly. Competitive blocking of ALIX-viral protein binding may serve as a broad-spectrum antiviral strategy. Research plan: We will strengthen the biological phenotype and physiological relevance of the observed host-virus interaction in different cellular and mouse models (Objective 1). We also aim to perform a series of mechanistic studies to dissect the biological consequences of ALIX and viral RTC-associated proteins interaction, as well as elucidating the binding interface on both counterparts (Objective 2). To achieve more translational impact, we will fully document the therapeutic potential of the identified peptide inhibitor and/or its better analogues in COVID-19 and Zika animal models (Objective 3). Expected outcomes: We expect to obtain new knowledge on the interplay between host ALIX and viral RTC-associated proteins, which will shed important light on how (+) RNA viruses host factors to fuel their replication machinery. This common mechanism of viral pathogenesis may render new targets for broad-spectrum antiviral development with less concern of antiviral resistance. 研究背景：靶向一種可被多種病毒共同利用的宿主蛋白，有望成為突破性的抗病毒策略。膜性複製細胞器是多種正鏈RNA 病毒的共同特徵，可為病毒基因組複製提供受保護的微環境。 初步研究結果：我們發現宿主蛋白 ALIX是多種人類致病性正鏈 RNA 病毒的促病毒因數，包括新冠病毒、寨卡病毒及腸病毒 A71 型。過往研究顯示，ALIX 可促進人類免疫缺陷病毒的出芽；本研究則揭示了 ALIX 的一項全新功能，即協調上述正鏈 RNA 病毒的聚合酶活性。我們鑑定出新冠病毒的Nsp12、腸病毒的 3D及寨卡病毒的 NS3 蛋白均可與 ALIX 相互作用。這些相互作用均可促使相關病毒蛋白定位至複製細胞器。值得注意的是，利用同一種多肽抑制劑阻斷上述 ALIX 與各病毒蛋白的相互作用，可對上述三種病毒產生抗病毒效力。 研究假說：我們推測 ALIX蛋白可透過調控病毒複製細胞器的形成及從而影響病毒複製－轉錄複合體的組裝和活性。以競爭性方式阻斷 ALIX 與病毒蛋白的結合可成為一種廣譜抗病毒策略。 研究計劃：我們將利用不同的細胞及小鼠模型，進一步確證所觀察到的宿主－病毒相互作用之生物學表型及生理相關性（研究目標一）。我們亦將進行一系列機制研究，以解析 ALIX 與病毒複製－轉錄複合體相關蛋白之間的相互作用所引致的生物學效應，並闡明雙方的分子結合介面（研究目標二）。為進一步提升本研究的轉化應用價值，我們將在新冠及寨卡病毒感染動物模型中，全面評估肽類抑制劑及／或其經優化的類似物的治療潛力（研究目標三）。 預期成果：本研究將揭示宿主蛋白 ALIX 與病毒複製－轉錄複合體相關蛋白之間相互作用的新機制，從而深化我們對正鏈 RNA 病毒如何利用宿主因數驅動其複製系統的理解。這種為不同病毒所共有的致病機制，有望提供嶄新的廣譜抗病毒藥物開發靶點，並降低產生抗病毒藥物耐藥性的風險。

17124626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17124626.value: 腸道微生物在IgA腎病自身免疫中的潛在驅動作用

17124626.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17124626.value: Dr Lam, Kong Dr Yiu, Stella Wai Han

17124626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17124626.value: Despite advances in the treatment of IgA nephropathy (IgAN), the leading glomerular disease causing kidney failure worldwide, patients only achieve partial remission and many showed proteinuria rebound upon immunomodulatory treatment cessation. Achieving sustained complete remission remains a challenge due to our incomplete understanding of disease pathophysiology. GWAS-identified risk loci linked to mucosal immunity shifted focus toward the gut-kidney axis in IgAN, however, they explain only a fraction of disease risk. We recently reported that IgAN patients exhibited a significantly higher proportion of gut bacteria coated with galactose-deficient (Gd)-IgA1, and that their stool bacterial isolates could deglycosylate human IgA1 into Gd-IgA1, which was also recognized by anti-Gd-IgA1 IgG autoantibodies in patients’ sera. Our further preliminary data showed that orally administered Gd-IgA1 is detectable in mouse serum after four hours, followed by formation of IgG targeting Gd-IgA1 at day 14 and glomerular deposition of bacteria-derived Gd-IgA1, mouse IgG and C3 at 3 weeks; importantly, in human colonic tissue obtained via colonoscopy from IgAN patients, there are high levels of Gd-IgA1. Thus, the gut lumen is a plausible continuous source of Gd-IgA1 antigens that could prime a systemic autoimmune response in IgAN. To define the causal mechanisms linking gut microbiota, mucosal immunity and autoimmunity in IgAN, we will 1) characterize individual gut Gd-IgA1-producing bacterial strains from IgAN patients’ stool using comprehensive culturomics and sequencing approaches to isolate and characterize IgA1-deglycosylating bacteria, 2) define the role of such bacteria in disease pathogenesis by gavaging germ-free IGHA1+/+ mice with a defined bacterial consortium and then determining kidney injury and the spatial location of the Gd-IgA1-producing bacteria within gut tissue, with a subset of mice receiving a targeted oral antibiotic regimen, and 3) investigate the autoimmune response to bacteria-derived Gd-IgA1 in wild-type C57BL/6 or germ-free IGHA mice receiving oral gavage of Gd-IgA1 or Gd-IgA1-producing bacteria, followed by single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of the ileum, colon, kidney, and peripheral blood mononuclear cells to map systemic changes in immune landscape and identify Gd-IgA1-responsive cell populations, and by flow-cytometry to evaluate the change in specific T cell and DC subtype populations in the intestine; finally an ex-vivo model to investigate if the antigen-load DCs can initiate a pathogenic T cell response. Findings from our study will therefore unravel mechanisms by which gut microbiota-derived antigens (i.e. Gd-IgA1) trigger a systemic autoimmune response that leads to kidney inflammation and injury, and pave the way for a new therapeutic paradigm.

17125226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17125226.value: 從轉錄組學重塑精神健康療法：藥物開發與再利用的應用

17125226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17125226.value: Dr Mak, Christopher Chun-Yu Prof SHAM, Pak-Chung Prof Zhang, Weixiong Dr Zhao, Jie

17125226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17125226.value: Mental disorders affect 970 million people worldwide, representing a major challenge to global health. Current medications do not deliver effective relief, underscoring the urgent need for innovative and accelerated drug development strategies. Traditional approaches are hindered by the complexity of brain biology and the limited translatability of animal models to human conditions. While randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are the gold standard for demonstrating treatment effects in evidence-based medicine, they are costly and time-consuming. Mendelian randomization (MR) harnesses the power of big data and human omics to pinpoint promising drug targets, providing the second-best evidence to RCTs from real-world genetic information. Among various analyses to support MR, colocalization confirms that suggested drug targets are truly implicated for mental disorders. This project aims to leverage MR and analyses, such as colocalization, to discover and prioritize brain-based, druggable genes linked to mental disorders, opening new avenues for drug development and repurposing. By analyzing genetic variations as natural experiments, we will assess how changes in 1,263 druggable targets impact 16 mental health outcomes, drawing from the latest, large-scale datasets. This cutting-edge approach enables us to predict the effects of targeting these genes, making drug discovery more efficient, relevant, and less reliant on animal testing. Promising targets will be further evaluated through comprehensive reviews of publicly available clinical trial data. In our preliminary data for schizophrenia (one of the 16 outcomes), we found that our approach can reduce the time from research to clinical application by up to 60-fold, thus accelerating the identification of existing drugs suitable for repurposing. Our multidisciplinary team brings expertise in clinical genetics, psychiatric genomics, pharmacogenetics, transcriptomics, biostatistics, bioinformatics, and MR; ensuring a rigorous and forward-thinking approach. By integrating large-scale human omics data and examining multiple mental disorders, we expect to uncover drug targets that could benefit several conditions at once. In the short term, we would identify drug repurposing candidates, and in the long term, we would identify candidate targets for drug development. 精神疾病影響全球約9.7億人口，對全球公共衛生構成重大挑戰。現有藥物治療未能提供有效的症狀緩解，凸顯了對創新且加速之藥物開發策略的迫切需求。傳統研究方法受限於腦部生物學的複雜性，以及動物模型轉譯至人類疾病狀態的局限性。儘管隨機對照試驗（randomized controlled trials, RCTs）為實證醫學中證明治療效果的黃金標準，但其成本高昂且耗時費力。孟德爾隨機化（Mendelian randomization, MR）運用大數據與人類體學（omics）的力量，精準定位具潛力的藥物標靶，自真實世界遺傳資訊中提供僅次於RCT的實證等級。在支持MR的各項分析中，共定位分析（colocalization）可確認所建議的藥物標靶確實與精神疾病存在因果關聯。 本計畫旨在運用MR及共定位等分析方法，發現並優先排序與精神疾病相關、源自腦部且具可成藥性（druggable）的基因，為藥物開發與藥物重新定位（drug repurposing）開闢嶄新途徑。藉由將遺傳變異視為天然實驗（natural experiments）進行分析，我們將運用最新的大規模數據集，評估1,263個可成藥標靶的變化對16種心理健康結果之影響。此尖端方法使我們得以預測靶向這些基因的效果，使藥物發現更具效率、更貼近臨床相關性，並降低對動物實驗的依賴。具潛力的標靶將透過對公開臨床試驗數據的全面性回顧進行進一步評估。 在精神分裂症（16種結果之一）的初步數據中，我們發現此方法可將研究至臨床應用的時間縮短達60倍，從而加速識別適合重新定位的現有藥物。我們的跨領域團隊具備臨床遺傳學、精神基因體學、藥物遺傳學（pharmacogenetics）、轉錄組學（transcriptomics）、生物統計學、生物資訊學及孟德爾隨機化之專業知識，確保研究方法嚴謹且具前瞻性。透過整合大規模人類體學數據並檢視多種精神疾病，我們預期能發掘可同時惠及多種疾病的藥物標靶。短期而言，本計畫將識別藥物重新定位的候選藥物；長期而言，則將確立藥物開發的候選標靶。

17125826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17125826.value: 探究高血糖誘導之中性粒細胞重編程如何促進第二型糖尿病相關腫瘤進展

17125826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17125826.value: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is a chronic metabolic disease that is highly prevalent in the Chinese population. Hyperglycemia (HG) is the hallmark of T2D, driving the link between T2D and numerous comorbidities, with cancer emerging as a critical concern. Notably, HG not only worsens cancer prognosis but is also associated with immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy resistance, indicating that HG-driven immune dysfunction is central to tumor aggressiveness in T2D patients. Yet, our knowledge in this regard is limited, hampering effective treatment for this vulnerable population. To address this, we performed scRNAseq analysis on resected tumors from patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) – an aggressive cancer type strongly correlates with T2D and has a high prevalence in Hong Kong. In stage-matched HCC samples, we observed a significant increase in tumor-associated neutrophils (TANs), particularly the pro-angiogenic subset, in patients with T2D. Our HCC murine model further confirmed that HG drives pro-tumor TAN enrichment. TANs are key components of the tumor microenvironment (TME), where they often promote tumorigenesis and impede ICB responses. Indeed, to fully harness the pro-tumor capacity of this immune population, tumors rewire neutrophils from birth. Emerging evidence suggests that tumors exert distal control over granulopoiesis in the bone marrow (BM), biasing neutrophil production and priming them with increased susceptibility to pro-tumor reprogramming in the TME. Building on this paradigm, our results showed that HG compromised the BM vasculature and increased hypoxic stress in the granulopoiesis niche. Consequently, a distinct metabolic imprint was imposed during tumor-driven granulopoiesis: In response to hypoxic stress, neutrophil progenitors and their progeny upregulated HIF-1a, which induced HILPDA and promoted lipid droplet (LD) accumulation. These LD-enriched neutrophils were metabolically adapted to hypoxic and nutrient-deprived TME. As a result, TANs in T2D patients and HG mice survived longer, providing an extended window for reprogramming into pro-tumor subsets. Thus, our preliminary data support a new framework for the enrichment of pro-tumor TANs in T2D, as HG-induced BM remodeling alters tumor-driven granulopoiesis and imprints neutrophils with a metabolic trait that facilitates their differentiation into pro-tumor TANs. In this proposal, we will delineate the molecular basis of the HG-BM-TAN axis, and mechanistically link it to tumor aggression. Finally, we will evaluate strategies to target LD accumulation in TANs to combat tumor growth in T2D hosts. This highly translatable knowledge will pave the way for the development of improved strategies to mitigate cancer risk in T2D patients. 第二型糖尿病（T2D）是一種慢性代謝性疾病，在中國人群中具有極高的患病率。高血糖（HG）是T2D的標誌性特徵，它驅動了T2D與多種併發症之間的關聯，其中癌症正日益成為關鍵問題。值得注意的是，高血糖不僅會惡化癌症預後，還與免疫檢查點阻斷（ICB）治療耐受相關，這表明由高血糖驅動的免疫功能失調是T2D患者腫瘤侵襲性增強的核心因素。然而，我們在這方面的認識仍十分有限，嚴重阻礙了對這一易感人群的有效治療。 為了解決這一問題，我們對接受切除術的肝細胞癌（HCC）患者腫瘤樣本進行了單細胞RNA測序（scRNAseq）分析。HCC是一種與T2D高度相關的侵襲性腫瘤類型，在香港的患病率也較高。在分期匹配的HCC樣本中，我們觀察到T2D患者的腫瘤相關中性粒細胞（TANs）顯著增加，尤其是促血管生成的亞群。我們的HCC小鼠模型進一步證實，高血糖可驅動促腫瘤TAN的富集。TAN是腫瘤微環境（TME）的關鍵組成部分，通常促進腫瘤發生並削弱ICB療效。事實上，為了充分利用這一免疫細胞群的促腫瘤能力，腫瘤從源頭就對中性粒細胞進行「重編程」。最新證據表明，腫瘤可在遠端調控骨髓（BM）中的粒細胞生成過程，使中性粒細胞的產生出現偏倚，並在其生成過程中提前「預處理」，使其在TME中更易被誘導為促腫瘤表型。 基於這一理論，我們的結果顯示，高血糖損害了骨髓血管系統，並增加了粒細胞生成微環境中的缺氧應激。其結果是在腫瘤驅動的粒細胞生成過程中形成了獨特的代謝印記：在應對缺氧應激時，中性粒細胞祖細胞及其後代上調了HIF 1α表達，從而誘導HILPDA的表達並促進脂滴（LD）的積累。這些富含脂滴的中性粒細胞在代謝上更適應缺氧和缺營養的TME。因此，在T2D患者和高血糖小鼠中，TAN生存時間延長，為其被重編程為促腫瘤亞群提供了更長的時間窗口。由此，我們的初步數據支持一個新的理論框架：在T2D的背景下，高血糖誘導的骨髓重塑改變了腫瘤驅動的粒細胞生成過程，並在中性粒細胞上刻下有利於其分化為促腫瘤TAN的代謝特徵，從而導致促腫瘤TAN的富集。 本研究之成果，預期將揭示「高血糖-骨髓造血-腫瘤免疫微環境」軸線在T2D相關癌症中的關鍵作用機制，為開發以中性粒細胞為靶點、兼具代謝調控與免疫治療意義的新型聯合策略提供理論基礎，最終有望改善T2D患者的癌症預後。

17126926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17126926.value: 原位研究巨病毒感染過程中“病毒染色質”結構

17126926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17126926.value: Giant viruses are a group of large double-stranded DNA viruses belonging to the phylum Nucleocytoviricota, also known as nucleocytoplasmic large DNA viruses (NCLDV). Studies suggest that they may share a common origin that predates the emergence of eukaryotes. The Melbournevirus, which belongs to the Marseilleviridae, has been reported to encode unique viral histone doublets that assemble into nucleosome-like particles (NLPs) with a more relaxed conformation compared to eukaryotic nucleosomes. This “viral nucleosome” structure could possibly act as a missing link for the “nucleosome evolution”, which both challenged the general concept that “viruses do not have their own nucleosome” and filled the gap between prokaryotic and eukaryotic nucleosomes. Intriguingly, current research on viral NLPs remains largely focused on in vitro structural studies, while the in situ characterization and functional analysis of these “viral nucleosomes” or even “viral chromatin” are still lacking. This study aims to investigate the in situ characteristics of “viral chromatin” using cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) in the Melbournevirus-infected Amoeba, and to further explore their native biological functions through the construction of histone-deficient viruses via targeted protein degradation techniques (SMASh). This work will enhance our understanding of chromatin formation by virus-encoded histones and expand the range of ‘‘unique organisms’’ that utilize chromatin structure to organize their genomic DNA. 巨病毒是一類屬於核質病毒門的大型雙鏈DNA病毒，也被稱為核質大型DNA病毒。研究表明，它們可能具有共同的起源，早於真核生物的出現。據報導，屬於馬賽病毒科的墨爾本病毒具有獨特的病毒組蛋白雙聚體，能組裝成類核小體，其構象比真核生物的核小體更為鬆散。這種“病毒核小體”結構或許可以作為“核小體演化”的一個缺失環節，既挑戰了“病毒沒有自己的核小體”的普遍觀點，也填補了原核生物和真核生物核小體之間的空白。 令人感興趣的是，目前對病毒核小體的研究大多集中在體外結構分析，而對這些“病毒核小體”甚至“病毒染色質”的原位表徵與功能分析仍然匱乏。本研究旨在利用冷凍電鏡斷層成像技術，在墨爾本病毒感染的變形蟲中研究“病毒染色質”的原位特徵，並通過靶向蛋白降解技術構建缺失組蛋白的病毒，進一步探索其原生的生物功能。本項工作將增進我們對病毒編碼組蛋白形成染色質的理解，並拓展利用染色質結構組織基因組DNA的“獨特生物體”範疇。

17127126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17127126.value: 生態瞬時評估驅動的流動健康干預對產後抑鬱高危孕婦的隨機對照研究

17127126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17127126.value: Prof Chan, Sophia Siu Chee Dr Cheung, Ka Wang Prof KOWK, Jojo Yan Yan Dr Lee, Chi Kei Dr Luk, Tzu Tsun Prof Suen, Yi Nam Prof Wang, Man Ping

17127126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17127126.value: Postpartum depression (PPD) remains a leading complication of childbearing with substantial risks for both mother and child, affecting around 15% of mothers worldwide. Early detection and timely intervention may reduce adverse maternal and child health outcomes. Although mHealth interventions have shown promise, many programs are passive or non-personalized, limiting engagement and effectiveness. Ecological momentary assessment (EMA) is a data collection method that allows the collection of multiple real-time data on mood, psychological status, and detailed lifestyle daily, and thus provides a reference for further intervention based on individualized triggers and stressors of negative emotions. This proposed trial aims to test the effectiveness of a proactive intervention model that enhances lifestyle-based mHealth support via the Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA) to reduce postpartum depression (PPD) in at-risk pregnant women. This is an individual randomized, two-arm randomized control trial conducted in Hong Kong. Pregnant women between 20-and 28-weeks’ gestation attending regular antenatal care will be screened at the time of the first oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT, required for all) using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS-10; score 0-30). Eligible participants are those with EPDS-10≥5 and no history of psychiatric/psychological disorders or current psychiatric treatment. Both groups receive brief psychological counseling and health education with self-help material at baseline. The intervention group will receive 2 weeks of EMA assessment followed by 10 weeks of mHealth personalized lifestyle guidance (nutrition, physical activity, sleep, stress management, social support), with adaptive feedback, and culturally tailored content via instant messaging. The control group continues with usual care. Follow-up assessments will be conducted at post-intervention (12 weeks after enrolment), and at 2 weeks and 1, 3, and 6 months postpartum. The primary outcome is the between-group difference in EPDS-10 score at 3 months postpartum. Secondary outcomes include onset of PPD; changes in EPDS-10 and validated measures of stress, anxiety, and insomnia; health-related behaviors; and family well-being at 3 and 6 months postpartum. Engagement metrics such as usage frequency and adherence will be analyzed. Semi-structured individual qualitative interviews assessing the attitudes, experiences, and perceived effectiveness of the intervention will be conducted after the 6-month postpartum follow-up. An exploratory economic evaluation will assess cost per unit improvement and potential cost savings. This will be the first trial to improve the early detection of PPD in prenatal clinics in Hong Kong. Using EMA-enhanced mHealth personalized intervention, the study will facilitate lifestyle management during pregnancy and prevent PPD post-childbirth. 產後抑鬱症（Postpartum Depression, PPD）是生育期最常見的嚴重併發症之一，全球約15%的產婦受其影響，對母親及嬰兒的健康均構成重大風險。早期識別與及時干預可有效減低母嬰不良健康結局。儘管流動健康（mHealth）干預已顯示出一定潛力，惟現有方案多屬被動式或非個人化，限制了用戶參與度及干預成效。生態瞬時評估（Ecological Momentary Assessment, EMA）是一種實時數據採集方法，能夠在日常環境中多次收集有關情緒、心理狀態及生活方式的動態數據，從而為基於個體化觸發因素及負面情緒壓力源的進一步干預提供參考依據。本研究旨在測試一種由生態瞬時評估驅動的主動式干預模式，透過強化生活方式為本的流動健康支援，以減低高危孕婦的產後抑鬱症狀。 本研究為一項在香港進行的個體隨機、雙臂隨機對照試驗。妊娠20至28週、於常規產前檢查期間接受口服葡萄糖耐量測試（OGTT）的孕婦，將以愛丁堡產後抑鬱量表（EPDS-10，評分範圍0至30分）進行篩查。符合納入條件的參加者為EPDS-10評分達5分或以上，且無精神／心理疾病病史或正接受精神科治療者。兩組參加者均於基線接受簡短心理輔導、健康教育及自助材料。干預組將接受為期2週的生態瞬時評估，其後進行10週的個人化流動健康生活方式指導（涵蓋營養、體能活動、睡眠、壓力管理及社會支援），並透過即時通訊軟件提供適應性反饋及文化適切內容。對照組則維持常規護理。 跟進評估將於干預後（入組後12週）、產後2週、以及產後1個月、3個月及6個月進行。主要結局指標為兩組參加者在產後3個月的EPDS-10評分差異。次要結局指標包括產後抑鬱症的發生率、EPDS-10評分變化、經驗證的壓力、焦慮及失眠量表評分變化、健康相關行為、以及產後3個月及6個月的家庭福祉。使用頻率及遵從性等參與度指標亦將納入分析。於產後6個月跟進完成後，將進行半結構式個別質性訪談，以了解參加者對干預的態度、體驗及感知成效。此外，將進行探索性經濟評估，估算每單位改善的成本及潛在成本節省。 本研究將是本港首個在產前診所推展產後抑鬱症早期識別的臨床試驗。透過以生態瞬時評估強化個人化流動健康干預，本研究將有助促進孕期生活方式管理，並預防產後抑鬱症的發生。

17127626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17127626.value: 利用人源多譜系類呼吸道器官研究DZIP1L於氣道發育過程中的機制

17127626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17127626.value: Respiratory diseases are leading causes of mortality and morbidity worldwide. Despite their prevalence, our ability to develop effective therapies is critically hampered by a lack of preclinical models that accurately predict human responses. For decades, research has relied on animal models; however, significant species differences in physiology and immunity often lead to findings that fail to translate. This is especially true for the lung, where mice lack the terminal bronchioles and their associated human-specific distal airway cell types. This fundamental divergence highlights the challenge in pre-clinical research in which animal models often fail to recapitulate the full spectrum of human pulmonary disease, creating a major bottleneck in translational research. Our project directly addresses this long-standing challenge by leveraging an innovative human-based model: multi-lineage human airway organoids derived from pluripotent stem cells (PSC). This cutting-edge platform achieves characteristic airway morphology, cellular diversity, and physiological function. Most importantly, this system facilitates modelling lung development and disease in vitro and provides an experimentally tractable platform to investigate organ-specific mechanisms underlying disease complexity. By using state-of-art imaging platforms and proteomics, we recently demonstrated a critical function for ciliary transition zone (TZ) in regulating motile cilia assembly and function. TZ localizes to the cilia base in both primary and motile cilia and regulates the ciliary trafficking of membrane and structural proteins. Using a series of mouse models, we demonstrate that correct TZ assembly is essential for the structural integrity and motility of mammalian respiratory cilia. Given that variants in TZ genes are frequently identified in human ciliopathies, our finding has broad implications in understanding ciliopathies with disease heterogeneity and limited therapeutic interventions. In this proposal, we will combine innovate human PSC-derived airway organoids together with our expertise in motile cilia biology to investigate pulmonary defects of autosomal recessive polycystic disease (ARPKD), a major ciliopathy with kidney involvement. More than 30% of ARPKD affected individuals die at birth due to pulmonary dysplasia. It remains unknown whether pulmonary dysplasia is caused by tissue-specific cilia defects and which aspects of human airway development and cilia function are affected. In this project, we will investigate whether DZIP1L, an ARPKD/ciliopathy gene, is required for motile cilia assembly and airway morphogenesis using human PSC derived airway organoids. The outcome from this project will provide much-needed mechanistic insight into the pathophysiology of pulmonary dysplasia associated with ARPKD patients and advance our understandings for genetic disorders with organ-specific defects. 呼吸系統疾病是全球發病和死亡的主要原因。然而，由於缺少能準確預測人體反應的臨床前模型，有效療法的研發嚴重受阻。傳統動物模型受限於物種間生理和免疫差異，研究結果常無法轉化至臨床；尤其肺部，小鼠缺乏終末細支氣管及相關人特異性遠端氣道細胞，難以重現人類肺病全貌，成為轉化研究的關鍵瓶頸。本項目採用創新性人源模型，由多能幹細胞（PSC）分化的多譜系氣道類器官，該平台具備典型氣道形態、細胞多樣性和生理功能，可在體外模擬肺發育與疾病，並為探究器官特異性機制提供便捷的實驗系統。我們前期結合先進成像和蛋白質體學，發現纖毛過渡區（TZ）在調控運動纖毛組裝和功能中起關鍵作用：TZ定位於纖毛基部，調控膜蛋白和結構蛋白的纖毛運輸。透過小鼠模型，我們證實TZ的正確組裝對哺乳動物呼吸道纖毛的結構完整性和運動性不可或缺。鑑於TZ基因變異頻繁見於人類纖毛疾病，該發現對於理解異質性強、治療手段有限的纖毛病具有重要意義。本項目將利用上述人PSC源性氣道類器官，結合我們在運動纖毛生物學方面的專長，研究體染色體隱性遺傳多囊腎病（ARPKD）是一種累及腎臟的主要纖毛病——的肺部缺陷。超過30%的ARPKD患者因肺發育不良在出生時死亡，但該肺發育缺陷是否源於組織特異性纖毛異常，以及具體影響氣道發育和纖毛功能的哪些環節，尚不清楚。我們將重點探究ARPKD致病基因DZIP1L是否參與運動纖毛組裝和氣道形態發生。研究成果將為ARPKD相關肺發育不全的病理機制提供關鍵見解，並深化對器官特異性遺傳病本質的認識。

17128926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17128926.value: 以易用型關聯式體積成像平台推動 3D 生物學研究普及化

17128926.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17128926.value: Prof Chiu, Chi Ngong Dr Ruan, Degong Dr Sugimura, Rio

17128926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17128926.value: Understanding biology now demands three-dimensional (3D) organ-scale visualization that preserves native spatial context and tracks dynamics in living specimens. However, there are still two key unmet needs: (1) It is increasingly essential to obtain correlative 3D readouts that combine molecular specificity with biophysical context. Fluorescence imaging provides molecularly specific cell identity and state, but not the physical state of tissues; 3D quantitative phase imaging (QPI), on the other hand, provides the missing context by mapping refractive index and dry mass—metrics linked to density, growth, compaction, and proxies of mechanics. Acquiring fluorescence and QPI together in the same volume and at matched speeds yields correlative features that are more robust and predictive than either alone, capturing early biophysical events that often precede reporter changes. Yet existing 3D imaging (fluorescence or QPI) are fragmented across separate instruments, hindering tightly co-registered and synchronized dynamical studies. (2) State-of-the-art 3D microscopes are expensive, alignment sensitive, and challenging to operate, limiting adoption and making reconfiguration for multimodal imaging, e.g., fluorescence-QPI, impractical. There is thus a pressing need for high-performance 3D correlative imaging that is affordable, reconfigurable, robust, and easy to use. To address these challenges, we propose an accessible 3D correlative imaging platform that pairs a new form of 3D fluorescence imaging, coined Aberration-assisted Scheimpflug Oblique Plane Microscopy (AS-OPM), with simultaneous 3D-QPI. Inspired by the Scheimpflug photography principle, AS-OPM flexibly controls aberrations to ensure high-fidelity 3D fluorescence image capture without the popular, but complex, remote refocusing optics. Built from off-the-shelf components, it maintains volumetric resolution and low phototoxicity while remaining alignment-tolerant and readily reconfigurable. Hence, the 3D-QPI module can be readily integrated with AS-OPM to provide continuous, label-free biophysical maps alongside molecularly specific fluorescence. Built upon our forefront expertise multimodal bioimaging, image analytics and organoid research, we will explore two critical biological applications in immune-oncology and developmental biology: (i) to quantify CAR-T cell engagement, persistence, and exhaustion in 3D glioblastoma organoids, testing whether mass density dynamics predict cytotoxicity beyond fluorescence reporters; and (ii) to assess mouse blastoids, using 3D QPI to evaluate viability and morphological dynamics while fluorescence imaging benchmarks lineage fidelity - provide comprehensive maps of biophysical signatures and biochemical specificity during development. This integrated platform will democratize advanced 3D imaging and accelerate the discovery of mechanistically grounded biomarkers for diagnostics and therapy response. 了解生物學如今需要在器官尺度上進行三維（3D）可視化，以保留原生空間脈絡，並追蹤活體樣本中的動態變化。然而，目前仍有兩項關鍵需求尚未被滿足：（1）取得具關聯性的 3D 讀出結果已日益重要，這類結果需能結合分子特異性與生物物理脈絡。螢光成像可提供具分子特異性的細胞身分與狀態資訊，但無法揭示組織的物理狀態；另一方面，3D 定量相位成像（quantitative phase imaging, QPI）則可透過映射折射率與乾質量來補足這一缺口，而這些指標與密度、生長、壓實程度，以及力學性質的代理指標密切相關。在同一體積中、並以匹配的速度同步取得螢光與 QPI 資訊，可產生比任一單一模態更穩健且更具預測力的關聯特徵，並捕捉常早於報導基因變化出現的早期生物物理事件。然而，現有 3D 成像技術（無論是螢光或 QPI）多分散於不同儀器平台之中，阻礙了高度共定位與同步化的動態研究。（2）目前最先進的 3D 顯微鏡價格昂貴、對光路校準高度敏感，且操作困難，因而限制了其普及應用；同時，也使其難以重新配置為多模態成像系統，例如螢光-QPI 整合成像。因此，亟需一種高效能、可負擔、可重新配置、穩健且易於使用的 3D 關聯成像技術。 為解決上述挑戰，我們提出一套易於取得的 3D 關聯成像平台，將一種新型 3D 螢光成像方法——稱為像差輔助 Scheimpflug 斜平面顯微術（Aberration-assisted Scheimpflug Oblique Plane Microscopy, AS-OPM）——與同步 3D-QPI 相結合。AS-OPM 的設計靈感來自 Scheimpflug 攝影原理，能靈活控制像差，以確保高保真度的 3D 螢光影像擷取，同時避免使用目前常見但複雜的遠端重新聚焦光學系統。該平台由現成商用元件搭建而成，可維持體積解析度並降低光毒性，同時具備對校準誤差的容忍度，且易於重新配置。因此，3D-QPI 模組可便利地整合至 AS-OPM 中，在提供具分子特異性的螢光資訊之餘，同步產生連續、免標記的生物物理圖譜。 基於我們在多模態生物成像、影像分析與類器官研究方面的前沿專長，本計畫將探索免疫腫瘤學與發育生物學中的兩項關鍵生物應用：（i）在 3D 膠質母細胞瘤類器官中，量化 CAR-T 細胞的接合、持續性與耗竭狀態，並檢驗質量密度動態是否能在螢光報導指標之外進一步預測細胞毒殺作用；以及（ii）評估小鼠胚泡樣體（blastoids），利用 3D QPI 評估其存活能力與形態動態，同時以螢光成像作為譜系保真度的基準，從而在發育過程中建立涵蓋生物物理特徵與生化特異性的完整圖譜。此整合平台將使先進 3D 成像技術更普及，並加速發現具有機制基礎的生物標誌物，以應用於診斷與治療反應評估。

17129326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17129326.value: 基於生物協同DNA框架實現內源性幹細胞選擇性捕獲與功能性牙髓再生

17129326.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17129326.value: Prof Duncan, Henry F. Prof Li, Xin Prof Tian, Taoran

17129326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17129326.value: Pulp revascularization/revitalization is a regenerative endodontic procedure (REP) that induces bleeding into the canal space to form a blood clot that serves as a scaffold to recruit endogenous stem cells from the apical papilla (SCAPs), thereby promoting pulp regeneration. Although evidence shows continued root formation and revitalization, clinical outcomes remain unpredictable. One major challenge is the nonspecific recruitment of heterogeneous cell populations, especially periodontal ligament stem cells (PDLSCs).
