This often results in the formation of cementum or osteoid-like tissue instead of functional pulp-dentin tissue, leading to suboptimal root strengthening or even canal obliteration. Additionally, the quality and stability of the blood clot are critical for successful treatment. The clot serves as a bioactive scaffold and a reservoir of growth factors, but poor clot formation or early degradation can impair stem cell recruitment and tissue regeneration, ultimately causing REP failure. To address these challenges, we propose utilizing tetrahedral framework nucleic acids (tFNAs). These are novel DNA nanostructures that enable precise, high-affinity, multivalent ligand-receptor interactions, thereby efficiently and selectively recruiting SCAPs during REPs. Following a comparative analysis of SCAPs and PDLSCs, we will identify an optimal marker or combination for targeting SCAP subpopulations with superior odontogenic potential. Next, we will synthesize and characterize tFNA constructs functionalized with cell-specific aptamers. These will be tested for their cell-capturing and recruitment efficacy, as well as their influence on nuclear mechanosensing pathways involved in cell migration and odontogenic activation. Leveraging the blood clot formation process, we propose a bio-cooperative approach to bond tFNA to the fibrin mesh in situ, effectively creating an endogenous “SCAP-catcher” that enhances SCAP recruitment and stabilizes clot formation. We will evaluate and optimize three strategies for bonding tFNAs to blood clot components to achieve the desired biochemical stability and mechanical properties. Furthermore, a pulp-revascularization-on-a-chip microfluidic model will be developed to recreate the multi-step, dynamic process of cell homing during REP under dynamic flow. The migratory and odontogenic capacity of cells recruited by various configurations of tFNA-blood-clot-fibrin cell-catchers will be evaluated and optimized. The effectiveness of the novel 'tFNA-blood-clot-fibrin cell-catcher' system for selectively recruiting endogenous SCAPs and promoting dentin-pulp tissue formation and root completion will be examined in vivo using a mini-pig REP model, thereby evaluating its predictability and efficacy. This innovative bio-cooperative, tFNA-based strategy and the dual validation processes will set a new standard for selective cell recruitment, significantly advancing functional dental pulp regeneration and the regenerative dentistry field. 牙髓血運重建／再活化為一種牙髓再生性治療（Regenerative endodontic procedure，REP），其原理係誘導機體出血進入牙齒內部的根管空間，形成血凝塊作為支架，以招募來自根尖部位的內源性牙乳頭幹細胞（Stem cells from the apical papilla，SCAPs），進而促進牙髓組織再生。儘管有證據顯示其可促進牙根持續形成與牙髓再活化，惟臨床成效仍難以預測。其中一大挑戰在於其非特異性招募異質性細胞族群，尤其是牙周韌帶幹細胞（Periodontal ligament stem cells，PDLSCs）。此常導致形成牙骨質或類骨組織，而非功能性牙髓–牙本質組織，這不僅不利於牙根持續形成及強化，甚至可能造成根管閉鎖。此外，血凝塊之品質與穩定性亦為治療成敗之關鍵。血凝塊不僅作為生物活性支架及生長因子儲存庫，若血塊形成不佳或過早降解，將影響幹細胞招募與組織再生，最終導致REP失敗。 本研究擬利用四面體框架核酸（Tetrahedral framework nucleic acids，tFNAs）來應對上述挑戰。tFNAs是一種新型的DNA纳米結構，能實現精確、高親和力且多價的配體–受體交互作用，從而在REP過程中高效且選擇性地招募SCAPs。首先，經由比較SCAPs與PDLSCs的生物功能，本研究將鉴別出最適的單一或組合的細胞表面標記物，以靶向具優異成牙本質分化潛力之SCAP亞群；其次，本研究將合成並鉴定修飾有細胞特異性配體的tFNA框架結構，並測試其SCAP細胞亞群捕獲與招募效率，以及其對引發細胞遷移與激活成牙本質向分化的細胞核機械力感知路徑之影響；藉由血凝塊形成過程，本研究提出一種生物協同策略，將tFNA框架材料原位連結至纖維蛋白網狀結構，藉此形成內源性「SCAP捕捉器」，以加強SCAP招募並穩定血凝塊形成。本研究將評估並優化所提出的三種將tFNA鍵結至血凝塊組分之策略，以達成REP所需之生化穩定性與機械性質；此外，本研究亦將構建牙髓血運重建微流控模型裝置，以再現REP過程中於動態流動條件下細胞歸巢之多步驟動態過程，並用於評估並優化由不同組態之tFNA–血塊–纖維蛋白細胞捕捉器所招募細胞之遷移與成牙本質能力。最後，將利用迷你豬REP模型進行體內試驗，驗證新型「tFNA–血塊–纖維蛋白細胞捕捉器」系統用於選擇性招募內源性SCAPs及促進牙本質–牙髓組織形成與牙根完成之有效性，並評估其可預測性與效能。 本創新性的生物協同、基於tFNA之策略及雙重驗證流程，將為細胞選擇性招募樹立新標竿，並有力地推動功能性牙髓再生及再生牙科學領域之發展。

17129526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17129526.value: 社区及医疗环境听力与认知快速测试的验证

17129526.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17129526.value: Prof Chang, Wai-tsz Prof Fritzgerald, Mathew Prof Kwok, Timothy CY Dr Ng, Iris Hoi-Yee Dr Tsoh, Joshua Dr Wang, Shangqiguo

17129526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17129526.value: Hearing loss (HL) and cognitive decline are common among older adults. Over 42% of those aged ≥60 live with some degree of HL, and around 16% of individuals over 50 have mild cognitive impairment (MCI). Older adult population is anticipated to double between 2015 and 2050. By 2025, people aged ≥60 will constitute 40% of Hong Kong's total population. While dementia care costs $1 trillion in 2018 globally, the increase in older population will double this cost by 2030. Likewise, total global economic costs of HL exceeded $981 billion in 2019. While HL is a modifiable risk factor for dementia, both negatively impact communication. Early interventions can potentially reduce the impacts of these conditions, enhance communication and well-being, and prepare patients and caregivers for better management. While hearing is screened in a few countries, cognitive screening is hindered by limitations of existing tests, such time involved, the need for trained personnel, and results are biased by education level or coexisting perceptual impairments such as HL. Importantly, both conditions are hard to differentiate from each other. In response, Wang and Wong (2023) devised the integrated Digit-in-Noise test (iDIN), to rapidly screen both functions; and is the world’s only test that could decipher their effects on speech understanding. The iDIN evaluates the ability to repeat 2- to 5-digit sequences in noise. Recognizing 2- or 3-digit sequences is relatively easy and when the threshold for recognizing them is significantly elevated compared to normal hearing listeners, a HL is indicated. When cognitive function is declined, the thresholds to recall longer digit sequences (e.g., 5 digits) or backward recall them would elevate significantly because of the increased cognitive load; but when cognitive function is normal, recognition thresholds are not affected. Thus, a significant difference in threshold between easy (2- or 3-digit) and hard conditions (5-digit or backward recall) would indicate cognitive decline. The Mandarin version yielded a sensitivity and specificity of >.90, against outcomes on the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA, a general cognitive screening test) (Wang & Wong, 2023; 2004). These findings are supported by a pilot study conducted at our lab on 107 Cantonese-speaking older adults, effectively differentiated HL and cognitive decline. The study will validate the Cantonese iDIN, examine the relationships with various cognitive domains and provide further evidence on the clinical use of the iDIN test to simultaneously evaluate and differentiate hearing and cognitive decline. 聽力損失（HL）與認知功能衰退是長者常見的健康問題。60歲或以上人士中，逾42%有不同程度的HL；50歲以上人士約16%有輕度認知障礙（MCI）。全球長者人口預計於2015至2050年間倍增；到2025年，60歲或以上人士將佔香港人口40%。全球認知障礙症照護成本於2018年達1兆美元，隨人口老化，預計2030年將倍增；2019年HL造成的全球經濟成本亦逾9,810億美元。HL是認知障礙症的可改變風險因素，兩者均會影響言語理解與日常溝通。 及早識別及介入可減輕這些問題的影響、改善溝通能力與福祉，並協助患者及照顧者及早制訂管理策略。部分國家雖已推行聽力篩查，但認知篩查仍受現有工具限制，包括測試需時、依賴受訓人員，以及結果容易受教育程度或HL等共存感知障礙影響。更重要的是，HL與認知衰退均可表現為言語理解困難，臨床上往往難以區分。 為此，Wang與Wong（2023）研發整合式噪聲中數字測試（integrated Digit-in-Noise test，iDIN），以快速同時篩查聽力與認知功能；據研究團隊所述，這是目前唯一可區分兩者對言語理解影響的測試。iDIN評估受試者在噪聲中複述2至5位數字序列的能力。辨識2或3位序列相對容易；若受試者在此條件下的辨識閾值較聽力正常者顯著升高，提示可能有HL。認知功能衰退者在複述5位序列或倒序複述時，會因認知負荷增加而出現顯著較高的閾值；認知功能正常者的閾值則不會明顯改變。因此，簡單條件與高認知負荷條件之間的閾值差異，可作為認知衰退的指標。 普通話版iDIN以蒙特利爾認知評估（Montreal Cognitive Assessment，MoCA）結果為參照，敏感度及特異度均高於0.90。團隊其後對107名粵語長者進行的先導研究亦支持上述結果，顯示iDIN能有效區分HL與認知衰退。 本研究將驗證粵語版iDIN，探討測試結果與不同認知功能範疇的關係，並提供更多有關臨床應用的證據，評估其作為快速篩查工具的可行性，以支持在社區及醫療環境中同時評估及區分HL與認知衰退。

17130126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17130126.value: 設計和開發牙科氧化鋯的熱輻射超快速燒結技術（TRUST）

17130126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17130126.value: The clinical adoption of dental 3Y, 4Y, 5Y and 3D-printed zirconia is limited by the inefficiencies of conventional sintering, a process requiring hours to days at high temperatures. This creates a significant bottleneck in digital dentistry, preventing same-day prostheses and increasing costs for both laboratories and patients.This project proposes a paradigm shift by developing a novel Thermal Radiation Ultra-fast Sintering Technique (TRUST). This method is designed to achieve rapid, dense sintering in minutes instead of hours, without compromising the mechanical integrity and optical properties that are essential for clinical success, thereby addressing a critical technological barrier in modern dental care. This project will be executed through a systematic, two-phase methodology. First, we will establish the theoretical basis thermal radiation sintering technique using a multiphysics modelling approach. We will investigate the fundamental relationships between key parameters of radiative heat source and thermal response of various zirconia specimen using computation technique to optimize the design of the TRUST furnace. After understanding the relationship between radiation power, exposure time, and atmosphere of the TRUST furnace chamber and the densification kinetics of various zirconias (3Y, 4Y, 5Y, 3D-printed), in second phase the project will optimize the furnace and the process for each material. The sintered samples will be rigorously characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) for microstructure, X-ray diffraction (XRD) for phase analysis, a universal testing machine for biaxial flexural strength, and a spectrophotometer for optical properties (translucency parameter and colour), comparing them against conventionally sintered controls, as well as dimension parameters for dental prostheses. Ultimately, this research will establish the first theoretical framework for the TRUST method, optimize a protype furnace design to demonstrate the feasibility of this technology for rapid sintering dental zirconia, and develop a set of optimized, validated protocols for rapidly sintering of different generation of zirconia materials. Therefore, the successful development of this technique has the potential to revolutionize dental workflows in dental technology and digital dentistry, enabling same-day delivery of reliable zirconia prostheses, and strengthening the knowledge base in advanced dental manufacturing technology. 牙科3Y、4Y、5Y及3D列印氧化鋯需要燒結，而傳統燒結製程需要在高溫下耗費數小時甚至數天時間。這種低效性限制了牙科用氧化鋯在臨床上的廣泛應用，亦構成了數字化牙科領域的重大瓶頸，既阻礙了「當日修復」服務的實現，也增加了技工所和病患的成本。本計畫旨在透過開發一種創新的熱輻射超快速燒結技術（TRUST），實現產業範式的轉變。此方法將燒結時間從數小時縮短至數分鐘，同時確保材料具備臨床應用所需的機械完整性和光學性能，從而攻克現代牙科診療中的關鍵技術難題。本計畫將分兩個階段系統性地進行：首先，利用多物理場建模方法建立熱輻射燒結技術的理論基礎；透過計算方法研究輻射熱源關鍵參數與各類氧化鋯試樣熱響應之間的基本關係，進而優化TRUST技術燒結爐的設計。在明確了TRUST燒結爐腔體內的輻射功率、輻照時間和環境與各類氧化鋯（3Y、4Y、5Y及3D列印）緻密化動力學之間的關係後，工程將在第二階段針對每種材料優化燒結爐及製程參數。我們將對燒結樣品進行嚴格表徵，包括利用掃描電子顯微鏡（SEM）分析微觀結構、X射線衍射（XRD）進行物相分析、萬能試驗機測試雙軸彎曲強度，以及分光光度計測量光學性能（半透明度參數和顏色），並將其與傳統燒結樣品及牙科修復體的尺寸標準進行對比。最終，本研究將建構TRUST方法的首個理論框架，優化原型爐設計以驗證該技術用於牙科氧化鋯快速燒結的可行性，並制定一套針對不同代際氧化鋯材料的、經優化的快速燒結製程規範。因此，該技術的成功開發有望徹底變革牙科技工與數字化牙科的工作流程，實現可靠氧化鋯修復體的當日交付，並充實先進牙科製造技術的理論與實踐基礎。

17130326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17130326.value: 闡明亞鐵離子觸發中性粒細胞陷阱治療多發性硬化症治療靶點及松果菊苷的治療意義

17130326.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17130326.value: Prof Chan, Koon Ho Prof Pan, Weidong Dr Wu, Meiling

17130326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17130326.value: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a debilitating autoimmune disorder of central nervous system (CNS) characterized by demyelination, axonal damage, and progressive neurological decline. Current therapeutics exhibit limited efficacy and significant adverse effects, underscoring the critical need for novel mechanism-based strategies. While T-cells are established mediators of MS pathology, the roles of neutrophils have been overlooked. Meanwhile, iron accumulation is a hallmark of MS lesion that correlates with disease severity. Iron overload mediates oxidative stress related ferroptosis, an iron-dependent cell death. However, whether iron overload could mediate neutrophil infiltration and CNS damages in MS pathology remains unknown. Elucidating this mechanism has potentials to developing novel therapeutic targets for MS treatment. Our preliminary data reveal that: (1) Ferrous iron was accumulated in circulating neutrophils from both MS patients and experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) mice. (2) Intracellular iron overload promoted neutrophil migration and neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in the CNS lesions; (3) Iron chelation with deferoxamine markedly reduced NETs and ferroptosis, and attenuated EAE severity; (4) Inhibition of NETs formation with DNase I treatment inhibited STING expression and mitigated ferroptosis in active EAE mice; (5) Echinacoside, a compound from medicinal plant Radix Rehmanniae used in Traditional Chinese Medicine, alleviated neurological dysfunctions, and down-regulated STING and inhibited ferroptosis in active EAE mice. Thus, we hypothesize that iron overload promotes neutrophil migration and NETs formation, subsequently inducing mitochondrial dysfunctions and ferroptosis, and aggravating neurological deficits through activating cGAS-STING signaling pathway. To test the hypothesis, the study is coached with three specific objectives: First, we will determine how iron overload in peripheral neutrophils facilitates their migration and NETs formation, and their implications for inflammatory demyelination and neurological deficits during MS/EAE pathogenesis. Second, we will investigate whether iron and NETs synergistically aggravate neuronal mitochondrial dysfunction and ferroptosis through cGAS-STING activation. Third, we will evaluate the effects of Echinacoside on modulating “iron-NETs-ferroptosis axis” and cGAS-STING signaling pathway, and ameliorating neuroinflammation and disease severity in MS/EAE pathogenesis. By establishing this paradigm in MS pathogenesis, we will identify new therapeutic targets and advance the fundamental understanding of how peripheral immune mechanisms driving CNS autoimmunity through iron-mediated pathways. The success of this project will provide a strong preclinical rationale for developing Echinacoside as a promising plant-derived drug candidate with significant translational value, offering new hope for MS patients facing limited treatment options. Therefore, the study has long-term implication globally and locally for developing advanced biotechnology platform and training young scientists. 多發性硬化症（MS）是一種以髓鞘脫失和神經功能衰退為特徵的中樞神經系統自身免疫病，現有療法療效有限且副作用明顯，亟需新機制藥物。T細胞雖被認為是主要致病細胞，但中性粒細胞的作用長期被忽視。腦內鐵沉積是多發性硬化症的典型病理改變，與疾病嚴重度相關，並可誘發鐵依賴性細胞死亡。然而，鐵超載是否驅動中性粒細胞向腦內浸潤並加重損傷尚不清楚。實驗性自身免疫性腦脊髓炎（EAE）是國際公認的多發性硬化症經典動物模型，能類比其脫髓鞘和神經功能障礙，為本研究提供關鍵體內驗證平臺。我們的前期研究表明：MS患者和EAE小鼠外周中性粒細胞中存在亞鐵離子顯著積累；鐵超載促進中性粒細胞向病灶遷移並釋放NETs（由DNA和蛋白組成的促炎網狀結構）；去鐵胺（鐵螯合劑）或DNA酶I（抑制NETs）均可減少NETs、鐵死亡並減輕EAE病情；中藥活性成分松果菊苷能改善EAE小鼠神經功能，並抑制STING表達和鐵死亡。基於此我們提出假說：鐵超載驅動中性粒細胞遷移和NETs釋放，通過啟動cGAS-STING信號通路誘導線粒體功能障礙和鐵死亡，從而加重神經缺損。為驗證該假說，本研究利用EAE模型設定三項目標：①闡明鐵超載如何促進中性粒細胞遷移及NETs形成及其在脫髓鞘損傷中的作用；②探究鐵與NETs協同啟動cGAS-STING通路加劇鐵死亡的機制；③評估松果菊苷調控“鐵—NETs—鐵死亡軸”及該通路的療效。本研究首次系統建立該致病鏈條，將揭示外周免疫通過鐵介導途徑驅動中樞自身免疫的新機制，為MS治療發現新靶點。項目成功後將為松果菊苷作為具有轉化價值的植物源候選藥物提供EAE模型中的堅實臨床前證據，為治療選擇有限的多發性硬化症患者帶來新希望，同時推動生物技術平臺建設和青年人才培養。該工作不僅有望發現MS治療的新靶點，還將拓展對中樞神經系統自身免疫性疾病外周驅動機制的理解，具有重要的基礎科學價值和臨床轉化潛力。

17131026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17131026.value: 開發正顎手術中用於診斷、手術規劃及長期穩定性預測的多模態大型語言模型框架

17131026.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17131026.value: Dr Leung, Yiu Yan Prof Peng, Yifan Prof Shan, Zhiyi Prof Yu, Lequan

17131026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17131026.value: Orthognathic surgery corrects severe jaw deformities to improve chewing, breathing, and facial appearance. However, its success is currently limited by three persistent challenges: the limitations of 2D X-rays, the difficulty of combining different types of patient data, and the inability to predict long-term stability, where the jaws can gradually shift back toward their original position—a problem known as relapse. This project aims to transform this field by creating a specialized Artificial Intelligence (AI) assistant for surgeons. We will develop a novel "large language model" (the technology behind advanced chatbots) specifically trained to understand the language of jaw surgery. Unlike standard models that process only text, our system will be "multimodal," meaning it can simultaneously analyse numerical data from complex 3D anatomy, textual clinical notes, and sequential patient records. The core goal is to build a "digital surgical expert" that can perform three critical tasks. First, it will integrate all available patient data to provide an objective, automated diagnosis. Second, it will generate a personalized surgical plan equivalent to an expert's plan. Finally, and most innovatively, it will analyse a patient's unique profile to forecast their individual risk of post-operative relapse, enabling proactive, personalized care. We will train and test this AI using a large, multi-centre dataset of past surgical cases. Its performance will be rigorously validated against the consensus from an expert panel and compared to actual patient outcomes. A pilot study with junior surgeons will also be conducted to measure if the AI tool improves their planning speed, confidence, and accuracy. By integrating disparate data streams with powerful AI reasoning, this project will shift orthognathic surgery from an experience-dependent art towards a predictable, data-driven science. The outcome will be a clinically robust decision-support system that empowers surgeons to achieve unprecedented levels of precision and long-term success, ensuring more stable and predictable care for every patient. 正頜手術可矯正嚴重的頜骨畸形，從而改善咀嚼、呼吸及面部外觀。然而，目前手術成效仍受三項長期存在的挑戰所限制：二維 X 光片的局限、整合不同類型病人數據的困難，以及未能準確預測長遠穩定性。當長遠穩定性不足時，頜骨有機會在術後逐漸移回原來位置——這種情況稱為復發。 本項目旨在透過建立一個專為口腔頜面外科醫生而設的人工智能（AI）助手，推動正頜手術領域的革新。我們將開發一個新型「大型語言模型」（即先進聊天機械人背後的核心技術），並針對正頜手術的專業語言進行特定訓練。與只處理文字的標準模型不同，我們的系統將具備「多模態」能力，即能夠同時分析來自複雜三維解剖結構的數值數據、文字形式的臨床紀錄，以及病人的連續病歷資料。 本項目的核心目標，是建立一位「數碼手術專家」，能執行三項關鍵任務。首先，它會整合所有可用的病人數據，提供客觀、自動化的診斷。其次，它會生成個人化手術方案，其水平可媲美專家制定的計劃。最後，亦是最具創新性的部分，它會分析病人的個別情況，預測其術後復發的個人風險，從而有助提供更主動、更個人化的臨床護理。 我們將利用來自多間中心的大型既往手術病例數據集，對此人工智能系統進行訓練及測試。其表現將與專家小組的共識進行嚴格驗證，並與病人的實際治療結果作比較。此外，項目亦會進行一項針對初級外科醫生的先導研究，以評估此人工智能工具能否提升他們的手術規劃速度、信心及準確度。 透過整合不同來源的數據，並結合強大的人工智能推理能力，本項目將推動正頜手術由依賴經驗的技藝，轉向可預測、以數據驅動的科學。最終成果將是一套具臨床可靠性的決策支援系統，協助外科醫生達至前所未有的精準度及長遠成功率，為每位病人提供更穩定、更可預測的治療。

17131326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17131326.value: CYLD去泛素化酶在EB病毒感染中作用的研究

17131326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17131326.value: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) persistently infects 95% of adults in the world and causes cancers of lymphoid and epithelial origin in a small subset of infected people, including about 10% of gastric carcinoma (GC) worldwide and almost all cases of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) in Hong Kong and southern China, where the incidence of NPC is substantially higher. The life cycle of EBV switches between lytic and latent states, both of which are necessary for viral maintenance and epithelial carcinogenesis. New knowledge about EBV life cycle and the host restriction factors required for EBV replication might provide new strategies for anti-EBV and anticancer therapy. CYLD deubiquitinase is a tumor suppressor known to play a critical role in viral infection, host innate immunity and carcinogenesis. By next-generation sequencing, inactivating mutations of CYLD have been repetitively found in EBV-associated NPC and other epithelial cancers. A similar trend has also been seen in human papillomavirus-associated head and neck tumors. These mutations result in aberrant activation of NF-κB as well as cell proliferation and invasion. However, exactly how CYLD deficiency impacts EBV infection remains to be elucidated. In our pilot study, we found that knockdown of CYLD promotes EBV lytic reactivation. In addition, knockdown of CYLD induces PD-L1 and synergizes with chemotherapeutic agents such as 5-fluorouracil to induce EBV lytic cycle. In this project, we will fully characterize the roles of CYLD deubiquitinase in EBV infection cycle. First, we will delineate the mechanism by which CYLD suppresses EBV lytic replication. The requirement of the deubiquitinase activity of CYLD for the effect on lytic control will be determined. Viral and cellular targets of CYLD will be identified and characterized. The expression, phosphorylation and activity of CYLD during the EBV life cycle will be assessed. Second, we will define the impact of CYLD on host interferon response against EBV. The requirement of the deubiquitinase activity of CYLD and the influence of CYLD on interferon response in relation to EBV infection will be investigated. The interplay between CYLD and EBV-encoded interferon antagonists will be characterized. Finally, we will explore how CYLD deficiency might affect sensitivity of infected cells to chemotherapy, radiotherapy and immune checkpoint blockade. The disease burden of EBV-associated cancers in Hong Kong remains high. Our findings will derive new knowledge of EBV pathogenesis. Our work might help to develop an improved version of EBV producer cells and provide improved strategies for anti-EBV and anticancer therapy. EB病毒在全世界95%的成人中成功建立持續感染，但在極少數感染者中引起淋巴及上皮系統的腫瘤，包括全球約10%的胃癌以及香港及華南近乎所有的鼻咽癌，而鼻咽癌在香港及華南的發生率則遠高於外地。EB病毒的生命周期包括裂解期及隱性期，這兩個階段都對病毒感染的維持及致癌必不可少。有關EB病毒生命周期以及EB病毒複製所需宿主限制因子的新發現，將為抗EB病毒及抗腫瘤藥物的研製提供新思路。 CYLD去泛素化酶具有腫瘤抑制活性，在病毒感染、宿主先天免疫及腫瘤發生中都有重要作用。新一代測序的結果表明CYLD基因的突變重複出現於EB病毒相關鼻咽癌及其他上皮癌中，類似情況也見於人乳頭瘤病毒相關的頭頸腫瘤中。這些突變可引起NF-κB的激活及細胞增殖或侵襲性增强，但CYLD缺損對EB病毒的影響仍有待闡明。 我們在前期研究中發現CYLD的敲低可刺激EBV裂解性復活，CYLD敲低也會誘導PD-L1的表達並對化療藥物如5-氟尿嘧啶所誘導的EBV裂解性感染有促進作用。在本項研究中，我們將全面深入地研究CYLD在EB病毒感染周期中的作用。首先，我們將闡明CYLD抑制EB病毒裂解性複製的分子機制，並揭示CYLD所作用的病毒及宿主靶蛋白及CYLD的表達、磷酸化及活性在EB病毒生命周期中的動態變化。其次，我們將闡明CYLD在宿主對EB病毒所產生的干擾素應答中的作用特別是CYLD與EB病毒編碼的干擾素拮抗蛋白之間的相互作用；再次，我們將探索CYLD缺損是否可以使感染細胞對化療、放療及免疫治療更敏感。 因EB病毒感染而引起的腫瘤在香港造成很高的醫療負擔。我們的研究可揭示有關EB病毒致病的新知識，並為構建EB病毒高效產毒細胞及制定抗EB病毒感染及抗腫瘤治療的新方向奠定重要基礎。

17200226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17200226.value: 通過混合火災模擬與數值方法探討高層模塊化建築之火災與火後性能

17200226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200226.value: This research aims to reveal the structural fire response of high-rise Modular Integrated Construction (MiC) buildings and provide a theoretical basis for performance-based fire design and post-fire structural evaluation for these buildings. The MiC has been rapidly adopted as an innovative technology to address the housing needs from increasing urbanization by delivering improved quality, construction speed, and resource efficiency. High-rise MiC projects are built internationally, including in Hong Kong, where policy initiatives have accelerated deployment and over 100 government and private projects have adopted the MiC. In June 2025, the Development Bureau and the Construction Industry Council published the MiC Annual Demand Forecast, which shows that approximately 2.5 million square meters of floor area for MiC buildings will be completed between 2025 and 2030. Despite this momentum, the structural fire and post-fire performance of high-rise modular buildings remains insufficiently understood. MiC’s volumetric approach introduces numerous interfaces and joints, which are primarily designed for construction efficiency. The fire resistance is only considered for the modules as separate units. The global structural fire behaviors of the high-rise MiC buildings are often overlooked, and the designs fail to consider the building system as a whole. The thermomechanical behavior of the MiC buildings during fire and their post-fire performance need to be quantified and investigated. Existing guidance in Hong Kong emphasizes the deployment of MiC rather than structural integrity under fire and post-fire structural performance, underscoring the need for performance-based fire design informed by whole-building response. Conventional fire performance evaluations are based on component-level fire tests, which do not capture the global structural behavior. In the meantime, numerical simulations are not accurate enough to capture the high nonlinearity at the elevated temperature, while full-scale fire tests are costly and not feasible for parametric studies. To overcome the limits, this project will develop and apply hybrid fire simulations (HFS). The critical structural component subjected to fire is either presented as a specimen that is physically tested in the lab (NP-HFS) or as a high-fidelity numerical model (NN-HFS), while the rest of the structure is modeled numerically as the integration model. Both validation tests using NP-HFS and parametric studies with NN-HFS are to be carried out. The project outcomes will support the regulatory development in MiC high-rise buildings in Hong Kong, the Greater Bay Area, and internationally by delivering an innovative HFS framework and theoretical basis for performance-based fire design of MiC high-rise buildings. 本研究旨在揭示高層模塊化建築（Modular Integrated Construction, MiC）在火災中的結構反應，並為此類建築的性能化防火設計與火後結構評估提供理論基礎。隨著城市化加速帶來的住房需求上升，MiC 作為一項創新技術正被快速採用，並在品質、施工速度及資源效率方面展現優勢。高層 MiC 項目已於全球多地落地，包括香港；在政策推動下，香港已有超過 100 個政府及私營項目採用 MiC。2025 年 6 月，發展局與建造業議會發布《MiC 年度需求預測》，顯示 2025 至 2030 年間將完成約 250 萬平方米的 MiC 建築樓面面積。儘管發展迅速，高層模塊化建築在火災及火後階段的結構性能仍缺乏充分認識。MiC 的體積模組方式引入大量介面與接頭，而這些部位主要以施工效率為設計導向；防火性能往往僅以單一模組為單位考慮。高層 MiC 建築在整體系統層面的結構火災行為常被忽視，設計亦未將建築作為整體系統加以評估。因此，亟需量化並研究 MiC 建築在火災期間的熱—力耦合行為及其火後性能。香港現有指引較著重 MiC 的推廣應用，對火災下結構完整性與火後結構性能關注不足，凸顯了以整體建築響應為基礎之性能化防火設計需求。傳統防火性能評估主要依賴構件層級耐火試驗，難以捕捉結構整體行為。同時，數值模擬在高溫條件下難以準確反映高度非線性，而足尺火災試驗成本高昂，亦不適合參數化研究。為克服上述限制，本項目將開發並應用混合火災模擬（Hybrid Fire Simulations, HFS）方法。受火關鍵構件將以兩種方式表徵：其一為在實驗室進行實體測試的試件（NP-HFS）；其二為高保真數值模型（NN-HFS）。其餘結構則以數值方式建模，形成整合模型。項目將同時開展基於 NP-HFS 的驗證試驗與基於 NN-HFS 的參數化研究。研究成果將透過創新的 HFS 框架及 MiC 高層建築性能化防火設計理論基礎，支持香港、粵港澳大灣區及國際層面的 MiC 高層建築監管與規範發展。

17200326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17200326.value: 基於抗運動、高解析度級聯波超聲的冠狀動脈微血管成像

17200326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200326.value: Coronary microvascular disease, characterized by structural and functional abnormalities within the microcirculation, is a major contributor to angina and adverse cardiovascular events, particularly prevalent among women. Despite its high prevalence and clinical significance, current diagnostic tools lack the spatial resolution, sensitivity, and patient compatibility necessary to directly image microvascular flow dynamics during the cardiac cycle. This hampers early detection and targeted intervention, underscoring the urgent need for noninvasive, efficient, and reliable imaging methods capable of resolving microvascular function in vivo. Ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) has emerged as a transformative and promising technique that overcomes the diffraction limit by detecting, localizing, and tracking microbubbles with micrometer resolution to map microcirculation. Recent advances have enabled ULM to visualize cardiac microvascular networks and quantify coronary flow. However, clinical translation faces significant challenges: the lack of validated, realistic microvascular phantoms that replicate the hierarchical and micron-scale architecture of native vessels, and the difficulty in compensating for large heart muscle deformation that obscure microbubble signals. These barriers hinder the reliable application of ULM for routine clinical use. This project therefore aims to address these limitations by developing MoRe-ResCU (Motion-Resistant, high-Resolution, Cascaded-wave Ultrasound), an imaging technology designed for noninvasive visualization and functional assessment of coronary microvasculature. MoRe-ResCU combines our patented ultrafast cascaded-waves ultrasound imaging method with deep learning-based motion estimation algorithms. The cascaded-wave approach will enhance sensitivity and resolution to depict flow within vessels down to tens of microns at frequencies above 25 MHz. The deep complex-valued neural network will be trained to accurately estimate heart wall motion from beamformed in-phase and quadrature data, effectively extracting MB signals despite large heart motion. This project will evaluate and optimize MoRe-ResCU through computer simulations and an in vitro validation workflow which is directly built upon our recently established fabrication protocol of realistic microvascular phantoms. Subsequently, ex vivo isolated rodent heart experiments, where microvascular flow can be precisely controlled, will optimize imaging parameters, map coronary microvascular dynamics across cardiac phases, and assess performance under different physiological pressure loads. The compatibility of MoRe-ResCU with existing ultrasound probes and systems will facilitate rapid translation into clinical settings. By achieving spatiotemporal resolution surpassing current methods, MoRe-ResCU aims to fill critical knowledge gaps in microvascular physiology and pathology. It has the potential to enable early detection of microvascular dysfunction, guide personalized therapies, and prevent progression to heart failure. Ultimately, this project strives to rescue more lives through early noninvasive microvascular assessment by MoRe-ResCU.

17200626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17200626.value: 用於衝擊感知機械人動態操作的高時空解像度觸覺感知

17200626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200626.value: This research aims to revolutionize robotic manipulation by transitioning from conventional impact avoidance toward impact-aware exploitation—effectively enabling robots to utilize high-speed contact as a strategic resource rather than viewing it as a system failure. While humans interact dynamically and seamlessly with their environment, state-of-the-art robots remain constrained by inefficient strategies such as "zero-velocity contact," significantly limiting their operational speed and adaptability. The fundamental challenge stems from the lack of tactile sensing systems capable of capturing microsecond-scale transient dynamics—including impact velocity, indentation depth, and contact forces—at a sufficiently high spatiotemporal resolution. To address this gap, we propose the development of a novel neuromorphic optical tactile sensor that synergistically integrates circularly bent soft optical fibers and a dual event-camera architecture embedded within a deformable elastomer. Operating at 1 kHz, this sensor delivers real-time, high-fidelity measurements of transient contact events, providing unprecedented insights into fast interaction dynamics. These rich, high-speed tactile data streams will facilitate the development of a new suite of algorithms capable of learning data-driven contact models and supporting real-time planning and control strategies that are robust to discontinuous state transitions induced by impacts. The outcomes of this research will include three key contributions: a high-speed sensing technology that exceeds current methods in both bandwidth and accuracy; a set of impact-aware manipulation algorithms designed to actively exploit impulsive interactions; and extensive validation across five categories of dynamic tasks characterized by distinct contact/impact state transition patterns, such as catching free-falling objects and enabling compliant human-robot collaboration. By effectively bridging high-frequency physical interaction with responsive and adaptive control, this work lays the foundation for applications hitherto impossible in robotics, spanning high-speed logistics, advanced industrial assembly, and fluid collaborative robotics, thereby significantly advancing automation in domains requiring speed, versatility, and physical intelligence. 本研究旨在推動機械人操作的革新，將傳統的「避免衝擊」模式轉向「感知並善用衝擊」，讓機械人能夠把高速接觸視為一種策略性資源，而非系統故障。人類能夠與周遭環境進行流暢而靈活的動態互動，然而，現今最先進的機械人仍受制於「零速度接觸」等低效策略，嚴重限制其操作速度和適應能力。 這項根本挑戰源於現有觸覺感測系統無法以足夠高的時空解像度，捕捉微秒尺度的瞬態動力學資訊，包括衝擊速度、壓入深度和接觸力。為填補這項技術缺口，我們提出研發一款嶄新的神經形態光學觸覺感測器，將環形彎曲的柔性光纖與雙事件相機架構協同整合，並嵌入可變形彈性體之中。該感測器以 1 kHz 的頻率運作，能夠實時、高保真度地量測瞬態接觸事件，為理解快速互動的動力學特性提供前所未有的深入資訊。 這些豐富的高速觸覺數據流將有助於開發一系列嶄新演算法，以學習數據驅動的接觸模型，並支援實時規劃與控制策略，使系統能夠穩健應對由衝擊所引發的非連續狀態轉換。 本研究預期帶來三項主要貢獻：第一，研發一項在頻寬和準確度方面均超越現有方法的高速感測技術；第二，建立一套能夠主動善用脈衝式互動的衝擊感知操作演算法；第三，針對五類具有不同接觸／衝擊狀態轉換模式的動態任務進行廣泛驗證，包括接住自由下落的物件，以及實現具柔順性的人機協作。 透過有效銜接高頻物理互動與快速回應、自適應控制，本研究將為以往機械人技術無法實現的應用奠定基礎，涵蓋高速物流、先進工業裝配及流暢靈活的人機協作，從而大幅推動講求速度、靈活性和物理智能領域的自動化發展。

17201526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17201526.value: 動態系統在網絡攻擊下的綜合：補償與恢復

17201526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201526.value: Modern dynamic systems—such as industrial control networks, power grids, and autonomous vehicles—depend on network communication between sensors, controllers, and links to function properly. However, their open, shared nature exposes these networked systems to cyber attacks such as data manipulation, communication blocking, and node hijacking. Successful attacks can cause a loss of critical data or corruption of state information, leading to severe performance degradation, instability, or even total system failure. Communication failure and false data injection can result in significant economic and human losses in applications such as vehicle platooning or power grid control. Traditional pre-defined defenses often fail in dynamic environments where attack types are unknown and evolve in time. Thus, there is an urgent need for online modeling and rapid attack identification methods to enable effective compensation and recovery strategies, restoring and enhancing estimation and control performance. This project will investigate the synthesis of dynamic systems under adversarial attacks, focusing on compensation strategies and recovery mechanisms to ensure resilient operation. A comprehensive framework will be developed to identify and estimate the dynamic parameters of cyber attacks that occur during system operation. The interactions between these attack characteristics and key performance metrics will be systematically analyzed to facilitate the design of effective estimators and controllers. Under varying attack severity and channel degradation conditions, resilient compensation mechanisms for networked systems will be devised through an adaptive dual-mode architecture combining intelligent retransmission with long short-term memory-based prediction, complemented by an event-triggered coding estimation strategy and a multi-mode switching control scheme. A hierarchical recovery mechanism for multi-agent systems (MASs) strategically restores nodes via Nash equilibrium selection and reconfigures topology through reinforcement learning optimization, while Koopman operator-based estimation and adaptive control ensure desired performance. To mitigate the effect of modeling errors and uncertainties, set-based techniques involving zonotopes and newly developed ellipsotopes will be employed to enhance the robustness of control and estimation strategies for uncertain systems subject to adversarial attacks. Furthermore, the attack-resilient control will be extended to open MASs by developing a signal-heartbeat communication scheme for reliable departure/attack detection and a learning-based adaptive framework that dynamically adjusts control parameters and network topology through local estimators and compensation mechanisms to maintain stability under frequent agent arrivals/departures and cyber attacks. The foundational results derived from this project promise to significantly enhance the performance of MAS applications across extensive engineering domains, including intelligent transportation systems, smart grid technologies, and multi-robot coordination efforts. 現代動態系統——如工業控制網絡、電網和自動駕駛汽車——依賴於感測器、控制器和鏈路之間的網絡通訊來正常運作。然而，其開放和共享的本質使這些網絡化系統容易受到網絡攻擊，例如數據篡改、通訊阻塞和節點劫持。成功的攻擊會導致關鍵數據遺失或狀態資訊損壞，進而造成嚴重的效能下降、不穩定，甚至系統全面癱瘓。在車輛編隊或電網控制等應用中，通訊故障和虛假數據注入可能會導致重大的經濟損失與人員傷亡。在攻擊類型未知且隨時間演變的動態環境中，傳統預先定義的防禦機制往往會失效。因此，迫切需要線上建模和快速攻擊識別方法，以實現有效的補償與恢復策略，從而恢復並提升估測與控制效能。 本計畫將研究遭受對抗性攻擊之動態系統的韌性設計方法，著重於補償策略與恢復機制的開發，以確保系統在攻擊環境下仍能維持可靠且具韌性的運作。我們將開發一個綜合框架，用於識別和估測系統運作期間所發生網絡攻擊的動態參數。將系統化地分析這些攻擊特徵與關鍵效能指標之間的交互作用，以利於設計出有效的估測器和控制器。在不同的攻擊嚴重程度和通訊通道劣化條件下，將透過結合智慧重傳與基於長短期記憶預測的適應性雙模式架構，為網絡化系統設計具韌性的補償機制，並輔以事件觸發編碼估測策略與多模式切換控制方案。針對多智能體系統的分層恢復機制，將透過納什均衡選擇策略性地恢復節點，並透過強化學習優化來重新配置拓撲結構，同時基於庫普曼算子的估測與適應性控制則可確保達到預期效能。為了減輕建模誤差與不確定性的影響，將採用包含帶狀多面體與新開發之橢圓多面體的集合技術，以提升遭受對抗性攻擊之不確定系統在其控制與估測策略上的魯棒性。此外，開發訊號-心跳通訊機制，以實現可靠的節點離線／受攻擊偵測，以及一個基於學習的適應性框架（該框架能透過局部估測器和補償機制動態調整控制參數與網絡拓撲），抗攻擊韌性控制將被擴展至開放型多智能體系統，以在智能體頻繁加入/離開及網絡攻擊下維持系統穩定。從本計畫中得出的基礎成果，有望顯著提升多智能體系統應用在廣泛工程領域中的效能，包括智慧交通系統、智慧電網技術以及多機器人協同作業。

17201726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17201726.value: 無人駕駛與人類駕駛並存的網約車市場監管政策設計

17201726.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17201726.value: Prof Wang, Hai Prof Xiao, Feng Prof Yan, Xintao

17201726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201726.value: Recent breakthroughs in autonomous driving technology have accelerated the transition of self-driving vehicles from experimental prototypes to commercially viable services. This progress has catalyzed the emergence of shared autonomous vehicle (SAV) services—commonly known as robotaxis—which are rapidly becoming a compelling alternative to traditional ride-hailing services provided by human drivers. Pioneering companies such as Waymo and Tesla in the United States, along with Baidu Apollo Go in China, have already demonstrated the feasibility of robotaxis, collectively serving millions of passengers across multiple cities. By 2040, projections indicate that robotaxis could account for approximately half of all on-demand rides, underscoring that SAVs and human drivers will coexist on urban roads for the foreseeable future. While robotaxis offer increased convenience and accessibility for passengers, their widespread adoption is expected to introduce several significant challenges. First, the proliferation of SAVs could threaten the livelihoods of millions of professional ride-hailing drivers, potentially causing substantial social and economic disruption. Second, current autonomous vehicle technologies still encounter difficulties navigating complex traffic scenarios, raising critical safety concerns. Third, the large-scale deployment of SAVs may exacerbate traffic congestion in already crowded urban areas. These challenges highlight the urgent need for robust government regulatory frameworks to ensure a smooth and equitable transition from human-driven vehicles to SAVs within on-demand mobility markets. To address these issues, this project will develop three targeted policy measures to regulate on-demand mobility markets with mixed fleets of SAVs and human drivers. The first policy will limit SAV fleet size through license management, aiming to mitigate the negative impacts of rapid SAV deployment while maintaining high service quality. The second policy will designate specific operational regions and time slots for SAVs, reserving profitable rides for human drivers to help safeguard their earnings and employment opportunities. The third policy will restrict SAV operations on selected road segments, particularly those characterized by heavy traffic or complex driving conditions, to alleviate congestion and enhance safety. As autonomous driving technology matures and human drivers adapt or transition to new roles, these regulations can be gradually relaxed in a phased manner. To evaluate the effectiveness of these regulatory strategies, we will develop a comprehensive simulation platform calibrated with real-world mobility data. Ultimately, by providing actionable and evidence-based guidance for policymakers, this project aims to facilitate the seamless integration of SAVs into on-demand ride service markets and promote an efficient, sustainable, and equitable future for urban mobility systems. 近年來，自動駕駛技術的重大突破加速了自駕車輛從實驗性原型邁向商業化服務的轉型。這一進展催生了共享自動駕駛車輛（SAV）服務，即俗稱的「無人駕駛的士（robotaxi）」，其正迅速成為傳統人類駕駛網約車服務的有力替代方案。美國的Waymo與Tesla，以及中國的百度Apollo Go等先驅企業，已成功驗證了無人駕駛的士的可行性，在多個城市累計服務數百萬名乘客。預計至2040年，無人駕駛的士將佔所有網約車服務的約半數，這意味著在可預見的未來，自動駕駛車輛與人類司機將長期並存於城市道路上。 儘管無人駕駛的士為乘客提供了更高的便利性與可達性，其大規模普及預計將帶來若干重大挑戰。首先，自動駕駛車輛的大量湧入可能威脅數以百萬計的專業網約車司機的生計，造成嚴重的社會與經濟衝擊。其次，現行自動駕駛技術在面對複雜交通情境時仍存在困難，引發嚴重的安全疑慮。第三，自動駕駛車輛的大規模部署可能加劇原已擁擠的城市地區的道路擁堵問題。面對這些挑戰，政府亟需建立完善的監管框架，以確保網約車市場從人類司機向自動駕駛車輛的過渡過程平穩且公平。 為解決上述問題，本研究將針對自動駕駛車輛與人類司機混合營運的網約車市場，提出三項具針對性的監管政策措施。第一項政策透過牌照管理限制自動駕駛車輛的車隊規模，旨在減緩其快速部署所帶來的負面影響，同時維持高品質的服務水準。第二項政策為自動駕駛車輛指定特定的營運區域與時段，將獲利較高的訂單保留給人類司機，以保障其收入與就業機會。第三項政策限制自動駕駛車輛在特定路段的營運，尤其是交通流量大或駕駛條件複雜的路段，以緩解道路擁堵並提升安全性。隨著自動駕駛技術日趨成熟，以及人類司機逐步適應或轉換到新工作，這些管制措施可依階段逐步放寬。 為評估上述監管策略的成效，本研究將開發一套以真實運營數據校準的綜合模擬平台。最終，本研究期望為政策制定者提供具可操作性且基於科學證據的決策指引，促進自動駕駛車輛順利融入網約車市場，並推動城市出行系統朝向高效率、可持續且公平的未來發展。

17201826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17201826.value: 高密度城市中的外送服務：評估風險並提升外送員安全

17201826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201826.value: The recent, rapid expansion of food delivery services, accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic, has fundamentally reshaped urban mobility worldwide. In cities such as Hong Kong, this transformation has had significant implications for road safety, with motorcyclists now among the most at-risk groups. Food delivery riders account for over 90% of motorcycle-related casualties. The risks facing these riders are shaped by the city’s dense road networks, adverse weather, and algorithm-driven management systems that emphasize delivery speed and efficiency. Intense job-related pressures, including tight delivery times, unstable income, and commission-based pay, often compel riders to engage in risky behaviors like speeding, running red lights, and violating traffic rules. Such actions are closely linked to increased crash rates and injury severity, creating a serious public concern. Despite the essential nature of their work, food delivery riders’ occupational safety and well-being remain largely overlooked in academic research and policy discussions, which typically focus on consumer satisfaction and market competition. The interplay between environmental, infrastructural, and organizational factors creates hazardous conditions for these workers. In response, this proposed project will adopt a comprehensive mixed-methods approach, combining accident data analysis, extensive surveys and interviews, and advanced driving simulation experiments, to systematically examine the challenges food delivery riders face. By synthesizing quantitative and qualitative findings, this study aims to develop evidence-based policy recommendations for transportation authorities, delivery platforms, and policymakers. The research will first examine working conditions in the food delivery industry, focusing on factors such as long hours, tight deadlines, pay structures, and occupational stress. Second, it will investigate infrastructural risks, including road design, pedestrian safety measures, and the effects of dense urban environments on delivery operations. Building on these insights, the study will assess both actual and perceived driving performance of food delivery riders, with particular attention to risk-taking behaviors and safety outcomes. The perspectives of key stakeholders regarding delivery rider safety will also be incorporated. Ultimately, by highlighting the critical issue of rider safety, this study seeks to raise safety standards, enhance platform accountability, and promote a more supportive environment for both riders and consumers, contributing to the overall health, safety, and resilience of urban communities as platform-based delivery services continue to evolve. 近年來，外送服務迅速擴張，而 COVID-19 疫情更進一步加速了這一趨勢，從根本上改變了全球城市的出行模式。在香港等城市，這種轉變對道路安全帶來了重大影響，當中電單車騎士已成為最容易面臨風險的群體之一。外送員佔所有電單車相關傷亡個案超過九成。這些外送員所面對的風險，受到城市密集道路網絡、惡劣天氣，以及強調配送速度與效率的演算法管理系統等因素共同影響。工作上的強大壓力，包括緊迫的送餐時限、不穩定的收入，以及以佣金計酬的薪酬制度，往往驅使外送員採取超速、衝紅燈及違反交通規則等高風險行為。這些行為與交通事故發生率上升及傷害嚴重程度增加有密切關聯，已構成嚴重的公共安全問題。儘管外送員的工作對社會運作不可或缺，但其職業安全與福祉在學術研究及政策討論中仍長期受到忽視，相關討論通常更著重於消費者滿意度及市場競爭。環境、基礎設施及組織管理等因素之間的交互作用，進一步為這些工作者形成危險的工作條件。為回應上述問題，本研究計劃將採用全面的混合研究方法，結合交通事故數據分析、大規模問卷調查與訪談，以及先進駕駛模擬實驗，系統性探討外送員所面臨的各項挑戰。透過整合量化與質化研究結果，本研究旨在提出具實證基礎的政策建議，供交通管理部門、外送平台及政策制定者參考。研究首先將檢視外送行業的工作條件，重點分析長工時、緊迫時限、薪酬結構及職業壓力等因素。其次，研究將探討基礎設施相關風險，包括道路設計、行人安全措施，以及高密度城市環境對外送作業的影響。在此基礎上，研究將評估外送員的實際及感知駕駛表現，特別關注其風險承擔行為及相關安全結果。同時，研究亦會納入不同持份者對外送員安全議題的觀點與看法。最終，本研究希望透過凸顯外送員安全這一重要議題，提高相關安全標準、強化平台企業的責任承擔，並促進建立一個對外送員與消費者均更具支持性的環境。隨著平台經濟下的外送服務持續發展，本研究亦期望能夠促進城市社區整體的健康、安全與韌性。

17202226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17202226.value: 基於多模態學習的脊柱畸形自動化手術規劃系統

17202226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17202226.value: Prof Cheung, Jason Prof Qi, Xiaojuan Prof Zhang, Teng

17202226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17202226.value: Spinal deformity is a three-dimensional abnormality of the spine with high prevalence (32–68% in adults), insidious early presentation, and substantial physical and psychological burden. Spinal fusion surgery is the most effective treatment for spinal deformities. However, owing to the anatomical and biomechanical complexity of the spine, these operations demand precise pre-operative planning and carry nontrivial risk. In current clinical practice, surgical planning is largely manual, time-consuming, and highly dependent on surgeon experience. Therefore, automatically formulating personalised and reliable surgical plans based on patients' multimodal clinical data is of great significance for improving surgical success rates, patient recovery, and reducing complications. This project addresses these clinical needs. Existing learning-based studies typically targets planning specific parameters or isolated steps, and are typically relies on a single data modality, limiting scope and clinical applicability. Multimodal learning has been applied mainly to disease management and outcome prediction, offering indirect decision support rather than actionable operative plans. Although state of the art multimodal large-language models and latent diffusion models (LDM) are emerging for surgical scene understanding (e.g., phase recognition, instrument detection), clinically usable pre-operative planning for spinal deformity remains largely unexplored. This project proposes a clinically oriented, multimodal automated planning system for spinal deformity surgery with following novel ideas: 1. Text-guided multimodal feature integration: A novel feature integration module that aligns imaging features based on textual semantics to effectively address multi-source heterogeneity and sparsity in medical data, enabling robust cross-modal feature fusion. 2. Standardised post-operative report generation: A retrieval-augmented generation enhanced text generation module that produces standardised and reliable surgical planning reports, providing text-related, surgery-actionable parameters. 3. Interactively controllable, text-guided LDM: A novel LDM-based framework that embeds interactive control within a mutual self attention mechanism to enable user-guided, anatomically accurate synthesis of post-operative imaging results, providing image-related, surgery-actionable parameters. To our knowledge, this project is among the first to systematically plan the principal intraoperative parameters for spinal deformity surgery within a multimodal learning framework. The resulting system will enable automatic, end-to-end planning of comprehensive surgical schemes for deformity correction, presented in multimodal outputs. Although centred on spinal deformity, the proposed advances are readily generalisable to surgical planning for other spinal conditions, including spondylolisthesis and spinal stenosis. 脊柱畸形是一種脊柱的三維異常，具有高盛行率（成人為 32–68%）、早期表現隱匿，以及顯著的生理與心理負擔。脊柱融合手術是治療脊柱畸形最有效的方法。然而，由於脊柱在解剖與生物力學上的複雜性，此類手術需要精確的術前規劃，並伴隨不可忽視的風險。在目前的臨床實踐中，手術規劃主要依賴人工完成，不僅耗時，而且高度依賴外科醫生的經驗。因此，基於患者的多模態臨床資料，自動制訂個人化且可靠的手術方案，對於提高手術成功率、促進患者康復及減少併發症具有重要意義。本項目旨在回應上述臨床需求。 現有以學習為基礎的研究通常僅針對特定規劃參數或孤立步驟，並且多依賴單一資料模態，因而限制了其研究範圍與臨床適用性。多模態學習目前主要應用於疾病管理與結局預測，所提供的多為間接決策支援，而非可直接執行的手術方案。儘管目前最先進的多模態大型語言模型及潛在擴散模型（latent diffusion models, LDMs）正逐步應用於手術場景理解，例如手術階段識別及器械檢測，但可供臨床實際使用的脊柱畸形術前規劃仍基本尚未被探索。 本項目提出一套面向臨床的脊柱畸形手術多模態自動化規劃系統，包含以下創新構想： 1. 文字引導的多模態特徵整合： 提出一種新型特徵整合模組，基於文字語義對影像特徵進行對齊，以有效處理醫療資料中的多來源異質性與稀疏性，從而實現穩健的跨模態特徵融合。 2. 標準化術後報告生成： 提出一種由檢索增強生成技術強化的文字生成模組，用於產生標準化且可靠的手術規劃報告，並提供與文字相關、可直接用於手術決策的參數。 3. 可互動控制的文字引導式 LDM： 提出一種基於 LDM 的新型框架，將互動控制嵌入互相自注意力機制之中，以實現由使用者引導、符合解剖結構的術後影像結果合成，並提供與影像相關、可直接用於手術決策的參數。 據我們所知，本項目是最早在多模態學習框架下，系統性規劃脊柱畸形手術主要術中參數的研究之一。最終形成的系統將能夠以多模態輸出形式，自動且端到端地規劃完整的脊柱畸形矯正手術方案。儘管本項目以脊柱畸形為核心，所提出的技術進展亦可直接推廣至其他脊柱疾病的手術規劃，包括脊椎滑脫及脊柱管狹窄。

17202726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17202726.value: 廢舊鋰離子電池的新型直接再生技術：結合機械化學處理與低溫共晶熔融鹽的閉環方法

17202726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17202726.value: The rapid adoption of electric vehicles has led to a mounting accumulation of spent lithium-ion batteries, posing serious environmental and resource challenges. Conventional recycling methods, such as pyrometallurgical and hydrometallurgical processes, are to a large degree limited by hazardous emissions and high energy consumption. More importantly, these approaches entail the smelting or dissolution of batteries, which degrade high-value cathode materials into low-value recovery products like Li2CO3 and CoCO3. To address these issues, this project presents a novel closed-loop technology that couples low-temperature eutectic molten salts with mechanochemical synthesis to directly regenerate spent lithium-ion batteries. Specifically, after battery disassembly and binder removal, the degraded graphite anode is delithiated through leaching with hot acetic acid, followed by activation via calcination with sodium hydroxide. Lithium extracted is recovered as lithium acetate via temperature-dependent precipitation. The resulting dehydrated lithium acetate is then combined with other lithium salts (e.g., lithium nitrate, lithium chloride) to form a low-temperature eutectic molten salt (eutectic point estimated <200 °C). During temperature-controlled wet ball milling with degraded cathode materials, the mechanical energy introduced induces localized high-pressure and high-temperature points at particle impact sites, which drive lithium insertion, facilitate phase transformations, and restore microcracks at a mild bulk processing temperature. This low-temperature ball milling operation can prevent lithium volatilization and heterogeneous reactions in high-temperature methods , ensuring precise stoichiometric control. In-situ characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations will be conducted to understand the structural and crystalline differences of the electrode material before and after regeneration and explore the lithiation mechanisms. The regenerated graphite anode and cathode materials are reassembled into anodes and cathodes, validating their electrochemical performance in regenerated lithium-ion batteries. Additionally, a quantitative techno-economic and environmental assessment will be conducted to highlight the industrial potential of this technology compared to conventional pyrometallurgy, hydrometallurgy, and other reported direct regeneration methods. This project is promising to advance the significant sustainable potential of spent LIB regeneration in Hong Kong. 隨着電動車的快速普及，退役鋰離子電池的累積量不斷增加，對環境及資源利用帶來嚴峻挑戰。傳統回收方法，例如火法冶金及濕法冶金，在很大程度上受到有害排放及高能耗的限制。更重要的是，這些方法通常涉及電池材料的熔融或溶解，會將高價值的正極材料降解為碳酸鋰及碳酸鈷等低價值回收產物。為應對上述問題，本項目提出一種新型閉環技術，將低溫共晶熔融鹽與機械化學合成相結合，以直接再生退役鋰離子電池。具體而言，電池經拆解及去除黏結劑後，先以熱醋酸浸出，使劣化石墨負極脫鋰；其後再透過與氫氧化鈉共同煅燒進行活化。浸提出的鋰將透過溫度依賴性沉澱，以醋酸鋰形式回收。所得無水醋酸鋰將與其他鋰鹽（例如硝酸鋰及氯化鋰）混合，形成低溫共晶熔融鹽，其共晶點估計低於 200 °C。在溫度受控的濕式球磨過程中，劣化正極材料與該共晶熔融鹽共同處理。機械能在顆粒碰撞位置產生局部高壓及高溫區域，從而促進鋰嵌入、相變，並在較溫和的整體加工溫度下修復微裂紋。與高溫方法相比，低溫球磨操作可減少鋰揮發及非均相反應，有助於實現更精確的化學計量控制。本項目將結合原位表徵及密度泛函理論（DFT）計算，闡明再生前後電極材料在結構及晶體學方面的差異，並探討其嵌鋰機理。再生後的石墨負極及正極材料將重新組裝成電池的負極及正極，並透過電化學測試驗證再生鋰離子電池的性能。此外，項目亦將進行定量技術經濟分析及環境評估，並與傳統火法冶金、濕法冶金，以及其他已報道的直接再生方法作比較，以評估該技術的工業應用潛力。整體而言，本項目有望推動香港退役鋰離子電池再生利用的可持續發展，並進一步釋放其可觀的資源及環境效益。

17203126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17203126.value: 優化室內空氣分布策略

17203126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17203126.value: Dr Kabanshi, Alan Prof Sandberg, Mats

17203126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17203126.value: Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems consume 10%–20% of global energy, driven by rising cooling demands in a warming climate. These systems comprise an upstream air treatment system and a room distribution system, with distribution being the critical “last mile.” Ineffective distribution wastes the energy expended on upstream pumping, heating, and cooling. On the other hand, effective distribution can significantly reduce energy expenditure. For example, displacement ventilation saves around 30% compared to widespread mixing ventilation. If fully realized, optimal air distribution alone could potentially save 3%–6% of global energy. Yet mixing ventilation remains the norm. A fundamental “old” question persists: which air distribution method is truly optimal over a full year of operation, and could there be even better solutions? Current optimization tends to prioritize indoor air quality and thermal comfort, while overlooking a key metric of thermodynamic efficiency, entropy generation. Our recent finding that displacement ventilation generates 30%-35% less entropy than mixing ventilation points to a major opportunity for optimization. Through a single-objective optimization, we identified a novel displacement-like configuration that also meets air quality and comfort constraints. We hypothesize that the optimal strategy is not just about objectives, but fundamentally depends on the statistical distribution of dynamic parameters like occupancy and heat gain, which fluctuate daily and seasonally. This project will develop a new framework for the stochastic, full-year optimization of air distribution. We will begin by defining and evaluating complete objectives/constraints for energy, comfort, and health. Computational fluid dynamics with a gradient-based Lagrangian optimization approach will be used to identify optimal strategies under fixed conditions, which will be verified in a full-scale test room. To handle realistic and dynamic scenarios, we will develop a stochastic approach using Monte Carlo simulations and machine learning to create fast and accurate surrogate models for airflow. The framework will be validated using a three-year dataset of thermal and environmental parameters from two classrooms and two restaurants. Real-world distributions of heat load, occupancy, and transients from this dataset will be used for optimization. The resulting optimal strategies will be compared against the actual energy use by existing mixing systems to quantify the savings. Ultimately, this project will provide the methodology and evidence needed to assess the integration of realistic air distribution optimizations into ventilation standards like ASHRAE 62.1, paving the way for a new energy-conscious standard for indoor environments. 暖通空調（HVAC）系統消耗全球能源的10%–20%，主要受氣候變暖背景下製冷需求上升的驅動。這些系統由上游空氣處理系統和室內空氣分布系統組成，其中分布環節是關鍵的「最後一公里」。無效的空氣分布會浪費上游泵送、加熱和冷卻所消耗的能源；而有效的分布則可顯著降低能耗。例如，與廣泛採用的混合通風相比，置換通風可節省約30%的能源。若能充分實現，僅優化空氣分布就有望節省全球能源的3%–6%。然而，混合通風仍是當前主流。一個根本性的「老」問題依然存在：在全年運行條件下，哪種空氣分布方法真正最優？是否還存在更優方案？ 當前優化往往優先考慮室內空氣品質和熱舒適，而忽視了熱力學效率的關鍵指標——熵產。我們最近發現，置換通風的熵產比混合通風低30%–35%，這揭示了重大優化機會。通過單目標優化，我們識別出一種新型類置換配置，該配置同時滿足空氣品質和舒適約束。我們假設，最優策略不僅取決於優化目標，更從根本上依賴於佔用率和得熱等動態參數的統計分布，這些參數會隨日變化和季節變化而波動。 本項目將開發一套新的隨機全年空氣分布優化框架。首先定義並評估涵蓋能源、舒適與健康的完整目標／約束。採用計算流體力學結合基於梯度的拉格朗日優化方法，識別固定條件下的最優策略，並在全尺寸試驗室中驗證。為處理現實動態場景，將開發基於蒙特卡羅模擬和機器學習的隨機方法，構建快速準確的氣流代理模型。該框架將利用兩間教室和兩家餐廳三年熱環境參數數據集進行驗證。優化將基於該數據集中熱負荷、佔用率和瞬態過程的實際分布進行。所得最優策略將與現有混合系統的實際能耗進行比較，以量化節能效果。最終，本項目將提供評估將現實空氣分布優化納入ASHRAE 62.1等通風標準所需的方法論與證據，為制定面向室內環境的新型節能標準奠定基礎。

17203426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17203426.value: 公共交通、無樁式共享單車與網約巴士系統協同共存的策略設計、定價及管理

17203426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17203426.value: Free-floating bikes are very popular nowadays. Users can return them anywhere to reduce their last-mile walking distance. Nevertheless, the main problem is inconsiderate bike returns, causing safety issues or blocking pedestrian/vehicle movements. To address the problem, countries such as Singapore have introduced geofencing areas for bike parking and parking fines for inconsiderate bike returns. However, no methodology has been developed to jointly design them. Moreover, to correctly evaluate the benefit of the joint design, an accurate bike repositioning cost should be considered. Other than free-floating bikes, on-demand buses can also be used for the first- and last-mile problem. They co-exist in some transport systems and complement fixed-route trunk transit services, but compete for travel demand if both bike-sharing and bus operators are private. The private bus operator can have a bigger competitive advantage if it further offers trunk services. How to design and manage the coexisting systems under different market regimes is an imperative issue for the government and the operators. Moreover, how to set bus and bike fares to maximize profit is an important issue for private operators. However, no methodology has been proposed to address these issues simultaneously. This project will aim to develop a methodology to strategically design fixed-route bus services, on-demand bus services, and a free-floating bike-sharing system. The methodology will determine (1) the locations and sizes of geofencing areas, (2) the parking fine and bike rental fare, (3) repositioning truck routes and loading/unloading quantities in visited areas by solving a bike repositioning sub-problem, (4) the station locations, routes, and frequencies of fixed-route bus lines, (5) the service area and fleet size of each on-demand bus line, and (6) zone-based bus fare tables without a predetermined number of zones. Based on logit-based stochastic user equilibrium and Nash equilibrium principles, a bilevel modeling framework will be proposed considering competition between on-demand buses and free-floating bikes, travel demand stochasticity, and the common line and mode choice of travelers. A hybrid algorithm based on artificial bee colony, the self-regulated averaging method, Monte Carlo simulation, and parallel computing will be developed. Problem properties will be examined theoretically and demonstrated in numerical studies. Case studies on Hong Kong Island will be conducted to identify critical factors that affect the choice between free-floating bikes and on-demand buses, and to give policy and managerial insights to the government on how to manage and improve the coexisting systems under different market and cooperation regimes. 現今無樁式共享單車非常流行，用戶可在任何地方還車以縮短最後一公里的步行距離。然而其核心問題在於隨意歸還單車，這不僅造成安全隱患，還會阻礙行人或車輛通行。為解決此問題，新加坡等國家已引入電子圍欄停放區域，並對亂停單車的行為處以罰款，但目前尚未發展出共同設計電子圍欄與罰款機制的方法論。此外，單車調度成本應被準確地納入考量用以正確評估協同設計的效益。除了無樁式共享單車外，網約巴士亦可用於解決首末一公里的接駁問題。此兩類交通工具共同存在於部分交通系統中，並與固定路線的幹線公共交通服務形成互補。但若二者營運商皆屬私營，他們將會互相爭奪客運需求。若該私營巴士營運商進一步提供幹線服務，則可獲得更大的競爭優勢。如何在不同的市場體制下設計與管理這些共存的交通工具，是政府與營運商亟待解決的關鍵課題。此外，如何制定巴士與單車票價以實現利潤最大化，亦是私營營運商面臨的重要問題。然而目前尚未有方法論能同時解決上述所有問題。本項目旨在提出一套方法論用以對固定路線巴士服務、網約巴士服務及無樁式共享單車系統進行策略性研究。該方法論將確定：（1）電子圍欄區域的位置與規模；（2）單車亂停罰款與租賃費用；（3）單車調度子問題求解而得的調度卡車的行駛路線及各經過區域的裝卸數量；（4）固定路線巴士線路的站點位置、路線與班次；（5）每條網約巴士線路的服務範圍與車隊規模以及（6）在不預設分區數量的情況下基於分區的巴士票價表。基於對數幾率模型的隨機用戶均衡與納許均衡原理，本項目將提出一個雙層規劃模型框架，其中同時考慮了網約巴士與無樁式共享單車之間的競爭、出行需求的隨機性以及出行者在共同線路上不同交通工具的選擇。項目亦將開發一種基於人工蜂群演算法、自適應平均法、蒙地卡羅模擬與並行計算的混合算法。研究問題的特性將從理論上被檢驗，並在數值研究中進行驗證。本項目將對港島進行案例研究，以找出影響出行者在無樁式共享單車與網約巴士之間進行選擇的關鍵因素，並就不同市場與合作體制下如何管理及優化此協同共存的交通系統，向政府提出政策和管理建言。

17203726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17203726.value: 具重調預算之突發性資料串流下的穩定且具隱私保障的線上最佳化

17203726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17203726.value: Real-time systems make decisions under evolving data, but current methods treat stability and privacy as separate concerns. When inputs spike, algorithms often respond by either adjusting their solutions too abruptly or adding excessive noise to mask the disruption. Current approaches have several shortcomings: (i) the lack of a unified theory linking stability concepts across different online optimization algorithms; (ii) privacy mechanisms that fail to account for decision latency, potentially revealing sensitive information prematurely; and (iii) an absence of modular, composable tools for building private systems, necessitating ad hoc integration. The proposed study will introduce a unified framework to address these gaps with a single, deployable solution. Our central contribution is a unified, primal-dual framework that introduces dynamic dual costs for solution changes, compelling the algorithm to prioritize only high-value local edits and adapt these costs over time. This perspective elegantly captures diverse stability methods, providing practitioners with intuitive controls—such as per-step limits and total budgets—and clear cost accounting for every adjustment. The result is more than a theoretical simplification; it transforms existing algorithms into stable variants with provably predictable behavior. Complementing our stability framework is a latency-aware layer for differential privacy, specifically designed for the continual release setting. Rather than allowing privacy loss or error to surge with an input spike, our method amortizes the impact over a configurable horizon. By strategically spreading the spike and injecting calibrated noise, we ensure early outputs maintain strong privacy, while accuracy recovers predictably. We will formalize time-indexed privacy/error profiles, develop modular composition theorems, and establish lower bounds tying achievable accuracy to spike size, latency, and stability budgets. A key goal is sublinear error scaling against spike magnitude, ensuring graceful degradation under stress. We will demonstrate the power of our framework by building essential latency-aware private primitives, such as prefix sums and heavy hitters, and packaging them into a practical composition toolkit. We will evaluate these tools on real-world applications in finance and federated learning, using both public and realistic synthetic data. Our evaluation will rigorously measure empirical performance—tracking accuracy, stability, and privacy loss—and verify the fundamental tradeoffs predicted by our theory. This project will provide a unified framework for building systems that are both stable and private, which will redefine the operation of online services, analytics, and learning platforms, ensuring they are reliable by design with proven, time-indexed guarantees for both utility and privacy. 即時系統需要根據不斷演變的資料作出決策，但現有方法往往將穩定性與隱私視為彼此獨立的問題。當輸入出現突增時，演算法通常要麼過於劇烈地調整解決方案，要麼加入過量雜訊以掩蓋擾動。現有方法存在若干不足：（i）缺乏一套統一理論，以連繫不同線上最佳化演算法中的穩定性概念；（ii）隱私機制未有考慮決策延遲，可能過早洩露敏感資訊；以及（iii）缺乏用以建構隱私系統的模組化、可組合工具，因而必須採取臨時拼湊的整合方式。本研究將提出一個統一框架，以單一且可部署的方案填補上述缺口。 本研究的核心貢獻是一個統一的原始—對偶框架，引入針對解決方案變動的動態對偶成本，促使演算法只優先執行高價值的局部修改，並隨時間調整這些成本。這一觀點能以簡潔方式涵蓋多種穩定性方法，為實務人員提供直觀的控制方式，例如每一步的變動上限及整體預算，並清楚核算每次調整的成本。其成果不僅是理論上的簡化，更能將現有演算法轉化為具有可證明、可預測行為的穩定版本。 作為穩定性框架的補充，我們將建立一個具延遲感知能力的差分隱私層，專門用於持續發布的情境。當輸入出現突增時，我們的方法不會任由隱私損失或誤差急劇上升，而是將其影響攤分至一段可設定的時間範圍。透過策略性地分散突增的影響並注入經校準的雜訊，我們可確保早期輸出維持強效的隱私保障，同時讓準確度以可預測的方式恢復。我們將形式化隨時間變化的隱私及誤差概況，建立模組化的組合定理，並證明把可達準確度與突增幅度、延遲及穩定性預算連繫起來的下界。一項關鍵目標是使誤差相對於突增幅度呈次線性增長，從而確保系統在壓力下仍能平穩退化。 我們將建構前綴和及高頻項目等重要的具延遲感知能力之隱私基本元件，並將其整合為一套實用的組合工具包，以展示本框架的效能。我們將利用公開資料及具真實性的合成資料，在金融及聯邦式學習的實際應用中評估這些工具。我們的評估將嚴謹量度實證表現，包括追蹤準確度、穩定性及隱私損失，並驗證理論所預測的基本權衡關係。 本項目將提供一個統一框架，用以建構同時具備穩定性與隱私保障的系統。此框架將重塑線上服務、分析系統及學習平台的運作方式，使其從設計之初便具備可靠性，並在效用與隱私兩方面提供經證明且隨時間明確界定的保障。

17204226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17204226.value: 以整合性深度學習進行腫瘤克隆性與可塑性之細胞核級空間分析

17204226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204226.value: Cancer heterogeneity and plasticity pose significant challenges to effective diagnosis and treatment. Understanding tumor clonality at 2D and 3D tissue space and unraveling its cellular plasticity require high-resolution, spatially-resolved data that integrate molecular and morphological information. However, current spatial omics technologies suffer from either low spatial resolution (for example, Visium) or high technical sparsity (for example, VisiumHD and Stereo-seq). On the other hand, histological images are available on the same section or consecutive sections, making them readily available for enhancing the spatial omics data, on both their resolution and signal-to-noise ratio. Therefore, it urgently demands computational methods that can effectively integrate both spatial transcriptomics and histology images to dissect these complex features comprehensively. This project aims to develop innovative multimodal deep learning approaches to integrate spatial transcriptomics and histology images, enabling nuclei-resolved analysis of tumor clonality and plasticity. Our first goal is to develop FineST, a novel deep learning framework designed to perform high-quality imputation of spatial transcriptomics data at the nuclei level. By fusing spatial RNA-seq and histological imaging, FineST will achieve nucleus resolution, capturing cellular heterogeneity with greater accuracy than existing methods. This will facilitate detailed mapping of tumor cell populations and their spatial organization. The second goal is to develop XCloneST, a computational tool designed to detect copy number variations (CNVs) from spatial transcriptomics data enhanced by histological features. XCloneST will utilize a customized variational autoencoder framework to disentangle CNV-related signals from other sources of cellular variability in lower-dimensional embeddings. Additionally, it will incorporate a graph neural network to accurately capture space-aware clonal distributions. Combined with FineST, this framework aims to provide deeper insights into the genetic alterations that drive tumor evolution and heterogeneity. Finally, to ensure robustness and applicability, we will validate both models using a newly developed reads simulator that generates realistic, multimodal sequencing data, alongside diverse publicly available datasets. This validation pipeline will assess model accuracy, scalability, and generalizability across different tumor types and data modalities. Overall, this project will produce cutting-edge computational tools that integrate molecular and morphological data at single-nucleus resolution. These methods will enable researchers and clinicians to better understand tumor clonality, heterogeneity, and plasticity, ultimately informing more precise diagnostics and targeted therapies. The integration of spatial transcriptomics and histology via multimodal deep learning methods holds transformative potential for advancing cancer research and personalized medicine. 癌症的異質性與可塑性對臨床上的有效診斷和治療構成了重大挑戰。若要理解二維和三維組織空間中的腫瘤克隆性，並揭示其細胞可塑性，亟需整合分子與形態學信息與空間組學數據。然而，現有的空間組學技術面臨著兩大瓶頸：空間解像度過低（例如 Visium），或技術性數據稀疏性過高（例如 VisiumHD 和 Stereo-seq）。另一方面，相同或連續切片上的組織學圖像極易獲取，使其非常適合用於提升空間組學數據的解像度與信噪比。因此，目前迫切需要能有效整合空間轉錄組學與組織學圖像的計算方法，以全面剖析這些複雜特徵。 本項目旨在開發創新的多模態深度學習方法，以整合空間轉錄組學與組織學圖像，實現細胞核級解析度的腫瘤克隆性與可塑性分析。我們的首要目標是開發一個新型深度學習框架，旨在進行細胞核水平的高質量空間轉錄組數據填補。通過融合空間 RNA-seq 與組織學圖像，此方法 將達到單細胞核解像度，能比現有方法更精準地捕捉細胞異質性。這將有助於精確繪製腫瘤細胞群落及其空間架構的圖譜。第二個目標是開發 XCloneST，這是一套計算工具，旨在從經組織學特徵增強的空間轉錄組數據中檢測拷貝數變異。XCloneST 將採用定制的變分自編碼器框架，在低維嵌入中，將 CNV 相關信號與其他細胞變異來源進行解耦。此外，它將結合圖神經網絡以精確捕捉具空間感知的克隆分佈。此框架與 FineST 結合，旨在對驅動腫瘤演化與異質性的基因變異提供更深層的見解。最後，為確保模型的穩健性與適用性，我們將利用新開發的測序讀段模擬器產生逼真的多模態測序數據，並結合多種公開數據集，對上述兩種模型進行驗證。此驗證流程將評估模型在不同腫瘤類型與數據模態下的準確性、可擴展性及泛化能力。 整體而言，本項目將開發出尖端的計算工具，在單細胞核解像度下整合分子與形態學數據。這些方法將協助研究人員與臨床醫生更深入地理解腫瘤克隆性、異質性與可塑性，進而為更精準的診斷和靶向治療提供決策依據。通過多模態深度學習方法將空間轉錄組學與組織學進行整合，對於推動癌症研究與個人化醫療具有變革性的潛力。

17204426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17204426.value: 短波紅外聲致發光成像：實現超過一厘米深度的腫瘤免疫治療亞聲學分辨率追蹤

17204426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204426.value: Background and challenges: Optical fluorescence imaging, known for its high spatiotemporal resolution, molecular specificity, and sensitivity, is extensively utilized in the research and development of cancer therapies. However, its spatial resolution in deep tissue imaging rapidly deteriorates with increasing depth owing to light scattering. Only blurred images that lack structural details of the sample can be observed at imaging depths beyond the optical diffusion limit, confining visible (400–700 nm) or near-infrared I (700–900 nm) high-resolution imaging to within ~1 mm in tissues. Achieving high-resolution imaging at tissue-penetration depths greater than one centimeter remains challenging, limiting the observation of interactions between immune cells and tumors and hindering tumor diagnosis and treatment. Acoustoluminescence (AL)—the light emission observed from materials subjected to acoustic vibrations and discovered after sonoluminescence in the 1930s—offers a promising alternative. Because ultrasound undergoes less scattering in tissues, AL has the potential to enable centimeter-depth molecular imaging with acoustic resolution, a capability that remains challenging for fluorescence imaging. However, despite being first reported almost 100 years ago, the use of AL for high-resolution molecular imaging in vivo remains unexplored owing to (1) a lack of AL materials with high acousto-optic conversion efficiency, (2) the limited penetration depth confined by the visible AL emission, and (3) a lack of suitable imaging modalities for high-resolution imaging. This proposal: Our aim is to develop novel AL materials and imaging modalities in the shortwave infrared/near-infrared II (SWIR/NIR-II, 1000–3000 nm) region for molecular imaging with sub-acoustic resolution and penetration depths greater than one centimeter, facilitating high-resolution, deep-tissue imaging in vivo. NIR-II light enables deeper tissue penetration than visible light, as longer wavelengths experience less scattering within biological tissues. Acousto-optic conversion probes, nanonization and surface coating strategies will be developed for in vivo imaging. NIR-II scanning focused-ultrasound acoustoluminescence (SFUAL) imaging systems will be constructed, with improved resolution and speed achieved through artificial intelligence (AI) networks. To experimentally validate this imaging modality, we will perform molecular imaging with SFUAL imaging in tumor immunotherapy. Impacts: The primary issue this project seeks to address is the current limitation in achieving high-resolution molecular imaging in live tissues beyond ~1 mm, leading to the development of novel imaging modalities with great potential to empower biological and medical investigations. Such a breakthrough would significantly impact cancer treatment by driving progress in the diagnosis, treatment, and the development of various tumor therapy strategies. 背景與挑戰： 光學螢光成像因具有高時空分辨率、分子特異性和高靈敏度，被廣泛應用於癌症治療方法的研究與開發。然而，在深部組織成像中，由於光散射隨深度增加而加劇，其空間分辨率會迅速下降。當成像深度超過光學擴散極限時，只能觀察到缺乏樣本結構細節的模糊圖像，這使得可見光波段（400–700 nm）或近紅外一區（near-infrared I, NIR-I；700–900 nm）的高分辨率成像在組織中的成像深度被限制在約 1 毫米以內。在大於 1 厘米的組織穿透深度下實現高分辨率成像仍然具有挑戰性，這限制了對免疫細胞與腫瘤相互作用的觀察，並阻礙了腫瘤診斷與治療的發展。 聲致發光（acoustoluminescence, AL）是指材料在聲振動作用下產生的光發射現象，其發現晚於 20 世紀 30 年代發現的聲致發光/聲致發光現象（sonoluminescence）。聲致發光為解決上述問題提供了一種有前景的替代方案。由於超聲在組織中的散射較弱，AL 有望實現具有聲學分辨率的厘米級深度分子成像，而這仍是螢光成像難以實現的能力。然而，儘管 AL 早在近 100 年前就已有報導，其在體內高分辨率分子成像中的應用仍未得到充分探索，主要原因包括：（1）缺乏具有高聲光轉換效率的 AL 材料；（2）可見光 AL 發射限制了組織穿透深度；（3）缺乏適用於高分辨率成像的成像模式。 本項目內容： 本項目旨在開發短波紅外/近紅外二區（shortwave infrared/near-infrared II, SWIR/NIR-II；1000–3000 nm）區域的新型 AL 材料與成像模式，以實現具有亞聲學分辨率、穿透深度超過 1 厘米的分子成像，從而促進體內高分辨率深部組織成像。與可見光相比，NIR-II 光由於波長更長，在生物組織中的散射更弱，因此能夠實現更深的組織穿透。我們將開發用於體內成像的聲光轉換探針、納米化策略以及表面包覆策略。同時，將構建 NIR-II 掃描聚焦超聲聲致發光（scanning focused-ultrasound acoustoluminescence, SFUAL）成像系統，並通過人工智能（AI）網絡提升其分辨率和成像速度。為實驗驗證該成像模式，我們將在腫瘤免疫治療中利用 SFUAL 成像開展分子成像研究。 影響： 本項目擬解決的核心問題是目前活體組織中超過約 1 毫米深度後難以實現高分辨率分子成像的限制，並由此發展具有巨大潛力的新型成像模式，為生物學和醫學研究提供有力工具。這一突破將通過推動腫瘤診斷、治療以及多種腫瘤治療策略的發展，對癌症治療產生重要影響。

17205026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17205026.value: 捕碳沸石與LDHs協同碳中和膠凝材料實現廢棄物資源化用於可持續建築

17205026.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17205026.value: Prof Jin, Fei Prof Ye, Hailong

17205026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205026.value: As Hong Kong strives for carbon neutrality by 2050 and aims to cut its carbon emissions by 50% by 2035, sustainable alternatives to traditional construction materials have become critical. The city is also grappling with significant waste management challenges, generating about 11,100 tonnes of municipal solid waste (MSW) daily. Incineration is commonly used to reduce the volume of waste, but this process produces byproducts like bottom ash (BA) and fly ash (FA), which pose environmental concerns. Finding solutions for recycling and utilizing these waste materials while also developing eco-friendly construction materials presents a significant challenge. This research focuses on transforming these municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) residues into functional materials, specifically zeolites and layered double hydroxides (LDHs), that have the ability to capture CO2. By integrating these materials into one-part alkali-activated slag (AAS) systems, the project aims to develop carbon-neutral binders that not only reduce CO2 emissions but also enhance the overall sustainability of Hong Kong’s construction sector. The integration of these innovative materials seeks to address both waste management issues and the environmental impacts of traditional cement use, reducing reliance on high-carbon materials like ordinary Portland cement (OPC). The research will proceed through three main tasks: (1) synthesizing porous zeolites from MSWI bottom ash (BA) to act as CO2 capture agents, (2) fabricating CO3- LDHs from MSWI fly ash (FA) and red mud to enhance CO2 storage, and (3) developing carbon-neutral AAS binders by incorporating zeolites and LDHs. The project will evaluate the CO2 sequestration capabilities of these materials, their influence on the geopolymerization process, and their impact on the mechanical properties and performance of the resulting binders. This approach, which adheres to the principles of a circular economy, holds significant potential for advancing green construction practices in Hong Kong, promoting waste recycling, and reducing the environmental footprint of construction materials. By addressing both carbon emissions and waste disposal, this research offers a promising solution to the city’s dual challenges of waste management and the push for sustainable construction materials. 隨着香港致力於在2050年前實現碳中和，並計劃於2035年前將碳排放量減少50%，尋找傳統建築材料的可持續替代品已變得至關重要。與此同時，香港亦正面對嚴峻的廢物管理挑戰，每日產生約11,100公噸都市固體廢物（MSW）。焚化是減少廢物體積的常用方法，但此過程會產生底灰（BA）及飛灰（FA）等副產品，並帶來環境隱患。因此，如何回收及善用這些廢棄物，同時開發環保建築材料，已成為一項重大挑戰。 本研究旨在將都市固體廢物焚化（MSWI）殘餘物轉化為具實際功能的材料，具體包括能夠捕集二氧化碳的沸石及層狀雙氫氧化物（LDHs）。透過將這些材料引入單組分鹼激發礦渣（AAS）系統，本項目擬開發碳中和膠凝材料，不但可減少二氧化碳排放，亦可提升香港建造業的整體可持續性。這些創新材料的整合有望同時紓緩廢物管理問題及傳統水泥使用所帶來的環境影響，並減少對普通波特蘭水泥（OPC）等高碳材料的依賴。 本研究將圍繞三項主要工作展開：（1）利用都市固體廢物焚化底灰（BA）合成多孔沸石，並將其用作二氧化碳捕集劑；（2）利用都市固體廢物焚化飛灰（FA）及赤泥製備碳酸根型層狀雙氫氧化物（CO3-LDHs），以提升二氧化碳儲存能力；（3）透過摻入沸石及層狀雙氫氧化物，開發碳中和型鹼激發礦渣膠凝材料。本項目將評估這些材料的二氧化碳封存能力、它們對地聚合反應過程的影響，以及其對最終膠凝材料力學性能及整體表現的作用。 本研究方案遵循循環經濟原則，在推動香港綠色建築實踐、促進廢物資源化利用，以及降低建築材料環境足跡方面具有重大潛力。透過同時應對碳排放及廢物處置問題，本研究為香港所面對的廢物管理與可持續建築材料發展兩大挑戰，提供一個具潛力的解決方案。

17205126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17205126.value: 先進多天線技術驅動的下一代無線通訊與感知

17205126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205126.value: The success of fifth-generation (5G) networks has set the stage for sixth-generation (6G) systems, which are envisioned to deliver ubiquitous connectivity, ultra-high capacity, and integrated sensing capabilities. To achieve these goals, 6G must overcome two fundamental limitations of existing multiantenna technologies: severe large-scale path loss and blockage sensitivity, particularly in high-frequency bands envisioned for 6G. The pinching-antenna system (PASS), recently proposed by NTT DOCOMO, offers a promising solution. PASS employs low-loss dielectric waveguides with reconfigurable pinching antennas (PAs) that act as flexible radiation points. This enables electromagnetic beamforming and the creation of stable line-of-sight (LoS) links. Early prototypes and theoretical studies confirm that PASS can alleviate path loss and mitigate blockage more effectively than conventional reconfigurable-antenna technologies such as reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, fluid antennas, and movable antennas. However, practical deployment of PASS remains hindered by three critical bottlenecks: (i) the absence of a tractable uplink signal model due to inter-antenna radiation (IAR), (ii) severe in-waveguide propagation loss in long-waveguide designs, and (iii) high maintenance cost with low reliability. Moreover, most existing works simply adapt methods from fluid or movable antennas rather than exploiting the unique physical characteristics of PASS. Motivated by these challenges, this project proposes an engineering-feasible PASS architecture that guarantees reliability and maintainability and establishes a comprehensive framework for the design and analysis of communications and sensing based on it. First, to break the three bottlenecks of existing long-waveguide architectures, the project will develop a segmented waveguide-based design in which several short dielectric segments are arranged end-to-end, each with its own feed point. This segmented PASS eliminates IAR in uplink and effectively mitigates in-waveguide attenuation and maintenance costs. Second, electromagnetic coupled-mode theory and multiport circuit theory will be used to establish two physically consistent yet mathematically tractable signal models for the segmented architecture under three practical operating protocols. These models will then support the characterization of channel capacity limits and network-level coverage performance. Third, PASS-tailored beamforming methods will be developed, beginning with optimal PA placement to reveal fundamental limits and extending to efficient algorithms that address wideband waveguide dispersion and imperfect channel state information. Finally, the study will extend to PASS-enabled sensing and its integration with communications, including waveform and beamforming design for enhanced sensing accuracy, as well as velocity-sensing-assisted communications for predictive beamforming. Through these contributions, the proposed project will overcome the key bottlenecks of PASS and pave the way for its deployment in future networks. 第五代移動通信（5G）的成功爲第六代（6G）系統奠定了基礎。6G被期望實現泛在連接、超高速率與通感一體化。然而，要實現這些願景，6G必須突破現有多天線技術的兩大根本瓶頸：嚴重的大尺度路徑損耗以及易受阻擋的問題，尤其是在6G所規劃的高頻段。 NTT DOCOMO公司近期提出的夾持天線系統（PASS）提供了一條具有前景的解決路徑。PASS採用低損耗介質波導和可重構的夾持天線（PA）作爲柔性輻射點，能夠實現電磁波束賦形並建立穩定的視距鏈路。早期原型驗證與理論研究表明，與智能反射面、流天線和移動天線等現有可重構天線技術相比，PASS能更有效地緩解路徑損耗和抗阻擋。然而，PASS的實際部署仍受制於三大關鍵瓶頸：（i）天線間輻射效應導致上行信號模型難以建立；（ii）長波導設計中波導內傳播損耗嚴重；（iii）維護成本高且可靠性低。此外，現有研究大多簡單套用流天線或移動天線的分析方法，未能充分利用PASS獨特的物理特性。 針對上述挑戰，本項目提出一種工程可行的PASS架構，兼具可靠性與可維護性，並在此基礎上建立通信與感知的一體化分析設計框架。首先，爲突破現有長波導架構的三大瓶頸，本項目將開發基於分段波導的設計方案——將若干短介質波導段首尾相接，每段獨立饋電。該分段式PASS消除了上行中的天線間輻射效應，同時有效抑制了波導內傳播損耗和運維成本。其次，本項目將基於電磁耦合模理論與多端口電路理論，針對三種實際工作協議，建立兩個物理自洽且數學上易處理的分段架構信號模型，並據此刻畫信道容量極限與網絡級覆蓋性能。再次，將發展面向PASS的定製化波束賦形方法，從最優PA佈局入手揭示性能極限，進而推廣至應對寬帶波導色散和非理想信道狀態信息的高效算法。最後，研究將拓展至PASS賦能的感知功能及其與通信的融合，包括面向高精度感知的波形與波束設計，以及基於速度感知輔助的預測波束賦形。 通過以上研究，本項目將突破PASS的關鍵瓶頸，爲其在未來網絡中的部署鋪平道路。

17205226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17205226.value: 基於創新數字孿生的多模態大型建築工程運輸方法

17205226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17205226.value: Prof Besklubova, Svetlana Prof Brilakis, Ioannis Prof Skibniewski, Miroslaw J.

17205226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205226.value: The Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) is experiencing an unprecedented pipeline of urban renewal and infrastructure megaprojects. In recent Chief Executive's 2025 Policy Address, accelerating the development of the Northern Metropolis is highlighted in Chapter III to further advance Hong Kong’s economy and improve people’s livelihood. In this context, large-scale construction projects including University Town, Kwu Tung and Hung Shui Kiu MTR Stations structurally depend on sea–land multimodal transport. The GBA holds natural advantages for multimodal transport approach: deep-sea container gateways, a dense river barge system, and expanding regional rail corridors that connect modular integrated construction (MiC) components and project sites. However, fragmented data and uncoordinated operations across maritime, rail, and road networks undermine efficiency, reliability, and sustainability. This study addresses some fundamental issues in large-scale construction projects using MiC principle by advancing digital and intelligent approaches to facilitate multimodal transport.
