The novelty of this project lies in establishing a unified Digital Twin–enabled framework for sea–land multimodal transport. Firstly, a spatial-temporal analytics framework is developed to process Internet of Things (IoT)-captured data for modeling various stakeholders such as suppliers, MiC hubs, and construction sites as interconnected nodes and material flows as four-dimensional entities including item, location, time, and status. This enables behavioral modeling of creation, storage, transport, and installation during the multimodal transport processes. Secondly, a Digital Twin–enabled bilevel optimization model is proposed to coordinate multimodal transport decision-making, such as scheduling and coordination of sea-land operations. The upper level aims to assist policymakers to balance environmental and capacity constraints, and the lower level supports project managers in minimizing waiting time and cost under uncertainty. Thirdly, large language models (LLMs) are adopted through parameter-efficient fine-tuning on historical megaproject data sponsored by industrial collaborators to provide strategic support, handling fragmented information flows and offering adaptive exception management strategies. The proposed approach will be validated using real-world datasets from collaborative leading construction enterprises. Evaluation metrics include efficiency, on-time delivery, resource utilization, and emissions. The key findings and observations will be translated into managerial implications and strategic policies for guiding construction industry for large-scale project management using collaborated and intelligent approaches when contemplating multimodal transport. 粵港澳大灣區正經歷前所未有的大型基礎設施計畫建設熱潮，在近期行政長官的2025年施政報告中，第三章重點指出加速北部都會區的發展，以進一步推動香港經濟發展並改善民生。在此背景下，包括大學城、鼓洞和紅水橋地鐵站在內的大型建設項目須依賴海陸多式聯運模式，大灣區擁有發展多式聯運的天然優勢：深水貨櫃港口、密集的內河駁船系統以及連接模組化建築（MiC）組件和項目現場的不斷擴展的區域鐵路走廊；然而，海路、鐵路和公路網路的數據分散和營運缺乏協調，影響了效率、可靠性和永續性。本研究旨在透過數字化和智慧化方法，使數據共享及基於數據驅動的決策成爲可能，以促進多式聯運，從而解決採用MiC的大型建設項目中存在的一些根本性問題。 首先，本文開發了一個時空分析框架，用於處理物聯網 (IoT) 收集的數據，將供應商、MiC 樞紐和施工現場等各相關持份者建模為相互連接的節點，並將物料流建模成包含物品、位置、時間和狀態的四維實體，爲多式聯運過程中的創建、儲存、運輸和安裝等行為建模奠定基礎；其次，本項目提出了一個基於數字孿生（DT）的雙層優化模型，用於協調多式聯運決策，包涵海陸作業的調度和協調：上層模型旨在幫助政策制定者平衡環境和運力約束，下層模型則支持在不確定性條件下最大限度地減少等待時間和成本；第三，本項目擬採用大語言模型 (LLM)，透過對產業夥伴提供的歷史大型專案資料進行參數的微調，提供策略性支持、處理碎片化的數據流、提供自適應異常管理策略。 本項目提出的方法將使用龍頭建築企業的真實資料集進行驗證，評估指標包括效率、準時交貨率、資源利用率和碳排放量等，項目關鍵發現和觀察結果將轉化為管理啟示和策略政策，以指導建築業在考慮多式聯運時，採用何種協作和智能方法進行大規模專案項目管理。

17205626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17205626.value: 基於三維人體點雲重建的隱私保護泛在熱感知

17205626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205626.value: Device-free contactless sensing has emerged for human-centric applications, particularly in eldercare and healthcare. However, existing modalities face a fundamental conflict between sensing fidelity and user privacy. Visual modalities (e.g., RGB/depth cameras) offer high resolution but are too intrusive for private spaces, whereas privacy-friendly RF sensing (e.g., Wi-Fi, radar) suffers from low spatial resolution, rendering it insufficient for fine-grained or multi-user sensing. This project investigates a significantly underexplored modality, low-cost infrared thermal arrays, which offer an excellent balance between sensing resolution and privacy. These sensors, which capture coarse heat signatures at a few hundred pixels, are fully passive, cost-effective, and provide spatial resolution an order of magnitude higher than RF modalities without compromising user privacy. However, exploiting these sensors for thermal sensing is non-trivial. The data is textureless, extremely low-resolution, noisy, and prone to ambient thermal interferences. These unique characteristics prevent the direct adoption of existing vision models. This project aims to overcome these challenges and enable thermal sensing for ubiquitous human perception via 3D human body point cloud generation from a single, low-cost thermal array. We propose a novel physics-informed design for 3D point cloud reconstruction, which will integrate a forward thermal physics model with two modules: 1) multi-primitive estimation for self-supervised joint recovery of depth and other thermal properties such as emissivity, surface temperature, and reflection, and 2) geometric perspective fusion for suppressing interference and disentangling multiple people. We will then build models for human sensing using thermal point clouds and explore exciting applications, including fall detection for elderly care and fine-grained occupancy monitoring for smart buildings. To support comprehensive evaluation and foster future research, we will create and open-source a large-scale thermal sensing dataset. This project will be the first study on privacy-first low-cost thermal sensing through human body point cloud reconstruction. The outcomes of this research promise to inspire a new subfield of "thermal computing" and improve human-aware eldercare and smart buildings. The PI's recent works, such as TADAR (Thermal Array-based Detection and Ranging), pioneer this emerging field of thermal computing, and this project will build on these efforts to tackle the far more challenging problem of full-body 3D point cloud reconstruction. Our extensive experience in both RF and thermal sensing, coupled with strong industry partnerships (e.g., Meridian Innovation, West China Hospital, and HKU CSE), will facilitate the success of this project and ensure practical, reliable solutions for real-world applications. 無設備非接觸式感知技術在以人為中心的應用（特別是長者照護與醫療健康領域）中快速發展。然而，現有感知模態在「感知精度」與「用戶隱私」之間存在著根本性的矛盾。視覺模態（如 RGB/深度攝影機）雖能提供高解析度，但在臥室、浴室等私密空間中侵犯隱私風險極高；而具備隱私友善特性的無線射頻感知（如 Wi-Fi、雷達）則因空間解析度極低，無法滿足精細化或多用戶感知的需求。為此，本計畫深入探索一種被嚴重忽視的感知模態——低成本紅外線熱陣列感測器。該感測器能在感知解析度與隱私保護之間取得極佳平衡：其僅擷取幾百個像素的粗粒度熱特徵，具有完全被動式、低成本的優勢，且能在絕不洩漏用戶隱私的前提下，提供比無線射頻高出一個數量級的空間解析度。 然而，利用此類感測器進行熱感知面臨著巨大挑戰。其採集的數據無紋理、解析度極低、雜訊大，且極易受到環境熱源干擾，這些獨特特質導致現有的電腦視覺模型無法直接套用。本計畫旨在克服上述挑戰，透過單一低成本熱陣列感測器重構三維人體點雲，實現無感泛在的人體感知。我們提出一種全新的物理導向（physics-informed）三維點雲重構架構，將前向熱力學物理模型與兩個核心模組結合：1）自監督多原語估計，用於深度以及發射率、表面溫度、反射等熱學特性的聯合恢復；2）幾何透視融合，用於抑制環境干擾並解耦多目標人體。在此基礎上，我們將建立基於熱點雲的人體感知模型，並探索兩項具重要應用價值的場景：用於長者照護的高隱私防跌倒檢測，以及用於智慧建築的精細化空間佔用監測。此外，我們將建置並開源大規模熱感知數據集，以支援全面評測並推動後續研究。 本計畫為首個透過人體點雲重構實現低成本、隱私保護熱感知的研究，其成果有望開闢「熱力計算（Thermal Computing）」的研究，並顯著提升長者照護與智慧建築的智能化水平。計畫主持人（PI）近期研發的 TADAR（基於熱陣列的檢測與測距系統）開創了熱力計算的先河，本計畫將在此基礎上進一步攻克難度更高的全三維人體點雲重構課題。我們在無線射頻與熱感知領域的豐富經驗，結合強大的產業與機構合作夥伴，將確保本計畫的順利實施，並為真實世界應用提供實用且可靠的解決方案。

17206126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17206126.value: 基於圖語言模型的模塊化集成建築多智能體生產調度系統

17206126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17206126.value: Dr Wu, Chengke Prof Yang, Zhile

17206126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17206126.value: Hong Kong faces a critical infrastructure paradox: the urgent need to deliver 440,000 housing units by 2034 coincides with a projected deficit of 45,000-55,000 construction workers by 2028, alongside land scarcity and carbon neutrality pressures. Modular Integrated Construction (MiC) presents a transformative approach with demonstrated benefits, including 50-80% on-site labor reduction, 45-80% less waste, and 35-45% faster assembly. However, the factory production stage—where most value is created—remains plagued by inflexible scheduling systems that cannot adapt to customized projects (e.g., housing, hospitals, schools), supply chain disruptions, or complex human-robot collaboration scenarios. This project addresses these challenges by developing GLM-MAPS: a novel Graph Language Model-based Multi-Agent Production Scheduling system that bridges the gap between natural language (NL) instructions and mathematically rigorous, executable production schedules. GLM-MAPS integrates advanced AI with human expertise through three breakthroughs. First, we develop semantic intelligence capabilities where a domain-adapted large language model (LLM) interprets NL commands like “minimize worker fatigue while meeting hospital module deadlines” and converts them into structured optimization problems. Second, we implement domain-specific scheduling through dual-layer knowledge graphs (KGs) that embed MiC expertise, including task dependencies, resource constraints, ergonomic risks, and disruption patterns, ensuring that generated schedules are both technically valid and operationally practical. Third, we develop a multi-agent system (MAS) with continual learning in which specialized AI agents collaborate to parse intentions, configure scheduling models, and incorporate real-time human feedback through an interactive visual interface. The project’s deliverables include: (1) a triplet-based knowledge base with an open corpus framework featuring 300+ structured instances linking NL descriptions to mathematical models and solver code; (2) a fine-tuned MiC-LLM and MAS with dual KGs validation and human feedback integration; and (3) a deployable GLM-MAPS platform enabling NL interaction, real-time schedule visualization, and proactive disruption management. We anticipate measurable impacts, including throughput gains through optimized resource leveling, faster rescheduling under disruptions, enhanced worker safety through ergonomic constraint enforcement, and seamless adaptation across diverse MiC projects without workflow re-engineering. By transforming production scheduling from a reactive, expert-dependent process to a proactive, AI-augmented workflow, GLM-MAPS directly supports Hong Kong’s policy initiatives in advanced MiC factories and cross-border production. The GLM-MAPS methodology also establishes a transferable framework for human-AI collaborative scheduling that has significant potential applications across manufacturing sectors involving human-robot teams, from aerospace to shipbuilding to custom fabrication. 香港正面臨嚴峻的基建挑戰：既要於2034年前交付44萬個住宅單位，又要應對預計至2028年高達45,000至55,000名建築工人的短缺，同時還要兼顧土地匱乏與碳中和壓力。模塊化集成建築（MiC）雖能顯著減少現場勞工（50–80%）、建築廢料（45–80%）並加快組裝進度（35–45%），但其工廠生產階段——即創造最大價值的環節——仍依賴僵化的調度系統，難以適應不同類型項目（如住宅、醫院、學校）、供應鏈中斷或複雜的人機協作場景。 為此，本項目研發「GLM-MAPS」系統——一個嶄新的基於圖語言模型的多智能體生產調度系統，旨在填補自然語言指令與嚴謹、可執行生產調度之間的鴻溝。GLM-MAPS融合先進人工智能與人類專業知識，實現三大突破：一、語義智能——經領域適應的大型語言模型能理解如「在滿足醫院模塊限期下，盡量減低工人生理疲勞」等自然語言指令，並轉化為結構化優化問題；二、領域專屬調度——透過雙層知識圖譜嵌入MiC專業知識（包括工序依賴、資源限制、人體工學風險及干擾模式），確保生成的調度既技術有效亦具實際操作性；三、持續學習的多智能體系統——多個專門AI智能體協作解析用戶意圖、配置調度模型，並透過互動可視化界面吸納即時人類反饋。 項目成果包括：（1）一個三元組知識庫及開放語料庫框架，含300多個結構化實例，連結自然語言描述、數學模型及求解器代碼；（2）經微調的MiC專用大型語言模型及多智能體系統，配合雙層知識圖譜驗證與人類反饋機制；（3）可部署的GLM-MAPS平台，支援自然語言互動、實時調度可視化及主動式干擾管理。預期效益包括：透過優化資源平準提升產能、干擾下加快重新調度速度、藉人體工學約束加強工安，以及無需重新設計流程即可適應各類MiC項目。 GLM-MAPS將生產調度由被動、依賴專家經驗的工序，轉化為主動、AI輔助的工作流程，直接支援香港在先進MiC工廠及跨境生產方面的政策倡議。其方法論更可推廣至其他涉及人機協作的製造行業（如航天、造船、定制製造），建立可轉移的人機協作調度框架。

17206426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17206426.value: 可適配且可重複使用的鋼結構單邊螺栓互鎖連接節點的研發

17206426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17206426.value: The construction and building industry significantly impact natural resource consumption and carbon emissions. According to 2024/2025 Global Status Report for Buildings and Construction, the sector plays a key role in the climate crisis, consuming 32% of global energy and contributing to 34% of global CO2 emissions. To meet the UN Environment Programme’s climate goal of halving emissions by 2030, the construction sector must prioritise circular practices and building reuse. This is essential for shifting to low-carbon, sustainable models. Echoing this vision, the Hong Kong Chief Executive’s 2025 Policy Address emphasises the importance of industry transformation through innovation, professionalisation, and revitalisation. Under this strategy, it is imperative to develop innovative construction forms that outperform traditional ones in terms of demountability, reusability, economic efficiency, and environmental sustainability. In steel construction, connections between structural members are critical to enabling reuse, representing around 50% of total construction costs and determining the feasibility of disassembly and reassembly. High-performance demountable connections, especially bolted-connections rather than welded-connections, facilitate the reuse of structural members. Within steel-framed structural systems, circular hollow sections offer superior resistance and also provide aesthetically appealing form. However, due to their curved surface, traditional connections between beams and circular hollow section columns typically employ welding rather than bolting, complicating the future dismantling and recycling of structures. Therefore, a universally applicable connection that is both easy to demount and adapt for various column geometries is highly valuable for improving the uniformity of steel-framed systems as well as promoting reuse. This project introduces an innovative adaptable and reusable steel blind bolted interlocking connection, in which all components are assembled using demountable blind bolts and adaptable configurations, which achieves a fully demountable and widely adaptable connection between the beams and tubular columns with various cross-sections, including circular, square, and octagonal shapes. Experimental and numerical investigations will be implemented to evaluate the flexural performance of the proposed connection. Practical design guidelines and recommended reuse approach will be developed to promote its adoption in engineering applications. Furthermore, a life cycle assessment will be conducted to quantify the potential reductions in carbon emissions associated with the novel adaptable and reusable connecting design compared to conventional connections. By addressing the challenges of adaptability, demountability, and reusability in structural connections, this project aims to promote innovative construction practices in Hong Kong and beyond, facilitating circularity in construction and development of sustainable built environment. 建築業對自然資源消耗和碳排放有顯著影響。根據《2024/2025年全球建築與施工現況報告》，該產業在氣候危機中扮演關鍵角色，消耗了全球32%的能源，並排放了全球34%的二氧化碳。為了實現聯合國環境規劃署提出的2030年將碳排放量減半的氣候目標，建築業必須優先考慮循環經濟實踐和建築再利用。這對於向低碳、永續模式轉型至關重要。香港特首2025年施政報告也呼應了這個願景，強調透過創新、專業化和振興實現產業轉型的重要性。在該策略下，必須開發在可拆卸性、可重複利用性、經濟效益和環境永續性方面優於傳統建築形式的創新建築形式。在鋼結構建築中，結構構件之間的連接對於實現再利用至關重要，這些連接約佔總建築成本的50%，並決定了結構拆卸和重新組裝的可行性。高性能可拆卸連接，尤其是螺栓連接而非焊接連接，有利於結構構件的再利用。在鋼框架結構體系中，圓形空心截面具有優異的抗彎強度，且外形美觀。然而，由於其曲面特性，傳統的梁與圓形空心截面柱之間的連接通常採用焊接而非螺栓連接，這增加了結構未來拆卸和回收的難度。因此，開發一種通用型可適配連接，既易於拆卸又能適應各種柱的幾何形狀，對於提高鋼框架系統的統一性以及促進結構再利用具有重要意義。本項目提出了一種創新的可適配、可重複使用的鋼結構單邊螺栓互鎖連接，其所有組件均採用可拆卸單邊螺栓和可調整的適應性裝置進行組裝，實現了梁與各種截面形狀（包括圓形、方形和八邊形）的管狀柱之間的完全可拆卸且廣泛適用的連接。本項目將透過實驗和數值模擬研究來評估此連接的抗彎性能。將制定實用設計指南和建議的再利用方法，以促進其在工程應用中的推廣。此外，還將進行生命週期評估，量化與傳統連接相比，這種新型可適配、可重複使用的連接設計在減少碳排放方面的潛在優勢。透過解決結構連結中適配性、可拆卸性和可重複使用性方面的挑戰，本計畫旨在促進香港及其他地區創新建築實踐，推動建築業的循環發展，並建立可持續的建築環境。

17207026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17207026.value: 非常規環境下的可微分聲學-視覺協同成像

17207026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17207026.value: This proposal aims to establish the differentiable acoustic-visual coded-modulation synergy perception, that lifts limitations of sole visual/acoustic systems in “unconventional” environments, such as underwater and light-deficient scenarios. This multi-modal sensory capability combines “coded” optics and electronics with deep-learning-based image reconstruction algorithms. Anticipated applications include industrial scanning, security screening, robot navigation, VR/AR platforms, as well as marine ecosystem monitoring. Classical approaches to developing coded imagers rely on “legacy designs” through the intuition combination of experienced engineers and “local optimization” on signal energy distributions, without directly optimizing for post-processed image quality. Recent AI advancements facilitate an efficient interpretation of differentiable imaging. Yet, most “neural coded-aperture” research typically optimizes one single modulation unit, restricting the design space and limiting scene representation fidelity. Noteworthy, visual-sole imaging fails to work robustly when there’s a lack of light or in scattering medium. Acoustic-sole imaging resolves a sparse depth map regardless of environmental condition, while spectral information that encodes rich scene attributes is lost. Integrating both sensory modalities can be valuable. Not to be confused with traditional photoacoustic techniques that aim mostly for near-field biomedical imaging, our synergy utilizes a combination of “adaptive coded-modulations” in shaping optical and acoustic functionality over a volume space. The acoustic modulation unit hereby entails one or multiple sound (sonic) emitters/receivers. Likewise, the optics entails but is not limited to coded refractive/diffractive lenses and color filters. The encoding-flexibility and adaptive-configuration are significant because leveraging all available degrees of freedom of manipulating both light and sonic waves greatly aids higher-dimensional operations in many research disciplines. The core objective is to explore a unified imaging paradigm that mimics the propagation of both light and sound. With our preliminary derivation & experimental results, these modulations can be represented via wave propagation and geometric rendering, both differentiable. Parameters of these two modulations and those of image-processing neural networks are learned in an end-to-end manner with domain-specific loss. Accordingly, two representative unconventional perception scenarios --underwater imagery; low-light depth perception-- are to be experimentally conducted with expert collaborators. Overall, our proposed "Differentiable Acoustic-Visual Synergy" shifts imaging design from single-modality heuristics to intelligent, jointly optimized, multi-modal sensing, and is supported by wide academic and industrial interest internationally (11 letters). Once established, it can revolutionize classical imaging schemes widely used in academic research and industrial product development, leading to intelligent perception solutions tailored for unconventional environments. 本研究旨在建立一個可微的聲光協同感知設計範式，以解決單一視覺或聲學感測在缺光等非常規環境中的局限性。這種多模態感測能力結合了編碼光學和電子學，並與現代圖像重建算法相融合。其具備廣闊的應用前景，包括工業掃描、安全篩查、機器人導航、VR/AR平台以及海洋生態系統監測等。傳統的編碼成像器開發方法（無論是視覺還是聲學）很大程度上依賴於“傳統設計”，即通過經驗豐富的工程師的直覺組合，並利用信號能量分佈的代理指標進行局部優化，而非考慮後處理後的圖像質量。因此，如何確定最佳編碼圖案仍是一個懸而未決的問題。近期的AI進展促進了對可微成像的高效詮釋。然而，針對“神經編碼孔徑”的研究通常僅優化單個調製單元，並與神經網絡相結合。這種有限的設計空間可能無法忠實地還原場景保真度。值得注意的是，純視覺成像在缺乏光線或處於散射介質中時無法穩定工作。而純聲學成像雖然可以在任何環境條件下解析出稀疏的深度圖，卻會丟失編碼豐富場景屬性的光譜信息。因此，將這兩種感測模態進行整合具有重要價值。 本研究所提出的協同感知有別於主要用於近場生物成像的傳統光聲方案，它利用自適應編碼調製的組合，在三維空間中創造光學和聲學功能。其中，聲學調製單元包含一個或多個聲音（聲波）發射器/接收器。同樣地，光學單元包括但不限於編碼折射/衍射透鏡以及濾色片。這種編碼靈活性意義重大，利用操縱光波和聲波的所有可用自由度，有助於在許多研究學科中實現更高維度的操作。核心目標是探索一個能夠模擬光和聲音傳播的統一成像範式。根據初步推導和實驗結果，兩者均可通過可微波傳播和幾何渲染來表示。這兩類編碼的參數以及圖像處理神經網絡的參數將通過領域特定損失以端到端的方式進行學習。據此，本計畫將對兩個具代表性的非常規感知場景進行探索：水下成像與低光深度感知。整體而言，所提出的“可微聲光協同”是從現成單模態感測設計向前邁出的重大研究一步，並已獲得學術界和工業界眾多合作者/支持者的認可。一旦成功建立，它將顛覆學術研究和工業產品開發中廣泛使用的傳統成像方案，為非常規環境量身定製出智能感知解決方案。

17207226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17207226.value: 優化基於LLM的AI智能體系統的分佈式後訓練和推理

17207226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17207226.value: This project studies distributed post-training optimization, inference expedition and output self-correction of LLM-based AI agent systems. Modern AI agents use large language models (LLMs) to handle various complex tasks, including browser/OS manipulation, deep research and coding copilot, driving various human-assisting applications. Training and serving AI agents are resource and cost intensive, and agentic output is often error-prone to use in critical scenarios. We study key issues in optimizing distributed post-training and inference efficiencies of AI agent systems. LLM-based AI agents are characterized by: (1) Multi-round interactions with the environment: the AI agent may retrieve information/receive feedback from the environment (e.g., third-party tools) iteratively, leading to complex workflows whose execution time is unknown beforehand; (2) Costly agent post-training and serving: they involve multi-round LLM calls and environmental interactions, incurring significant time and resource costs; (3) Error-proneness of agentic output: due to the well-known hallucination of LLMs, output of LLM-based agents is often erroneous, challenging their real-world application in high-stakes scenarios. We address challenges brought by these characteristics in distributed post-training, agent serving and output self-correction. First, reinforcement learning (RL) has been successfully used in LLM post-training, attaining high model-tuning performance. Agentic systems involving diverse modules are more complex than single-LLM systems. Enabling highly-efficient RL post-training of agentic systems is crucial to empower LLM-based agents to successfully handle complex tasks. Second, serving LLM-based AI agents involves huge resource costs. An agent can call external tools, produce actions, reflect on past steps, and refine its reasoning/actions with multi-round LLM invocations until the final answer is produced, leading to diverse workflows and non-deterministic end-to-end workflow serving time. Efficient agent serving that maximizes resource utilization and minimizes serving time is the key towards practical success of agentic applications. Next, automatic self-correction of agentic output is crucial for enabling AI agents in high-stakes applications. A primary mechanism for LLM self-correction is through iterative generation: output is verified and feedback is organized into refined prompts to invoke the LLM again, soliciting more accurate responses. Revealing key principles in prompt optimization that ensure corrected output is important for effective agent self-correction. We study efficient algorithms and system designs to optimize RL post-training of LLM-based AI agent systems and enable their cost-effective serving with serving time minimization. We also investigate principled prompt optimization for effective agent self-correction. We build agent post-training and serving systems incorporating our designs, and evaluate them on training/serving workloads in real-world AI clouds. 本項目研究基於大語言模型（LLM）的智能體系統的分佈式後訓練優化、推理加速和輸出自糾錯。現代智能體系統利用大語言模型（LLM）處理各種複雜任務，包括瀏覽器/OS操作、深度研究和編碼輔助等，從而驅動各種輔助人類的應用。訓練和運行智能體系統需要耗費大量資源和成本，而智能體的輸出往往容易出錯、不能使用在關鍵場景下。我們研究優化智能體系統分佈式後訓練和推理效率的關鍵問題。 基於LLM的AI智能體具有以下特點：(1) 與環境的多輪互動：AI智能體可能需要迭代地從環境（例如第三方工具）中檢索資訊和接收反饋，從而導致複雜的流程，其執行時間事先未知；(2) 智能體後訓練和服務成本高昂：這涉及多輪LLM調用和環境交互，會產生大量的時間和資源成本；(3) 智能體輸出易出錯：由於LLM的固有缺陷，基於LLM的智能體的輸出經常出錯，這給其在高風險場景中的實際應用帶來了挑戰。我們針對這些特點，研究分佈式後訓練、智慧體服務和輸出自糾錯方面的解決方案。 首先，強化學習（RL）已成功應用於LLM的後訓練，並取得了優異的模型調優表現。包含多個模組的智能體系統比單一LLM系統更為複雜。因此，實現高效的RL後訓練對於賦能基於LLM的智能體成功處理複雜任務至關重要。 其次，服務基於LLM的AI智能體需要耗費大量資源。智能體可以調用外部工具、生成動作、回顧過往步驟，並透過多輪LLM調用不斷完善其推理/動作，直至得出最終答案，這導致了多樣化的工作流程和不確定的端到端工作流服務時間。高效率的智慧體服務，即最大化資源使用率並最小化服務時間，是智慧體應用實際成功的關鍵。 再次，智能體輸出的自動自糾錯對於在高風險應用中運用AI智能體至關重要。LLM自糾錯的主要機制是透過迭代產生：驗證輸出並將反饋組織成更精細的提示詞，再次調用LLM，從而獲得更準確的回應。揭示確保輸出正確性的提示詞優化關鍵原則對於有效的智能體自糾錯至關重要。 我們將研究高效的算法和系統設計，以優化基於LLM的智慧體系統的強化學習後訓練，並以最小的服務時間進行經濟高效的智慧體服務。我們也將研究用於有效智能體自糾錯的原則性提示詞優化。我們將構建包含我們設計的智慧體後訓練和服務系統，並使用真實世界AI雲平台上的訓練/服務工作負載進行評估。

17207426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17207426.value: 納米列印膠體量子點紅外光電探測器實現光子增強與動態可調響應度

17207426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17207426.value: This project aims to address fundamental challenges in printing multi-layer colloidal quantum dots (QDs) with nanoscale morphology control to enhance infrared (IR) photodetection. Advances in sensing and communication technologies urge more efficient, adjustable near-IR photodetectors. Static photoconductive or photovoltaic operation alone cannot support computational spectroscopy and high-dimensional imaging. Colloidal QDs promise low-cost, CMOS-compatible IR devices through solution processing and programmable optoelectronic properties. However, QD photodetectors exhibit an external quantum efficiency (EQE) lower than 50% beyond 1500 nm. The core challenge is mismatched film thickness requirements for IR absorption and charge transport. Therefore, new architectures and fabrication methods must integrate photonic structures to maximise IR photon utilization and semiconductor junctions to facilitate charge separation. Conventional plasmonic and photonic enhancements rely on lithography for metal patterning, adding optical loss, fabrication complexity, and scale-up cost. As on-demand manufacturing, inkjet printing has not yet achieved the flexibility to assemble photoresponsive QDs into designer structures. State-of-the-art QD printing is hindered by modest printing resolution (>10 µm), insufficient to trigger photonic enhancements, and cross-layer interference during multi-material deposition. Consequently, fully printed QD photodetectors are rarely reported, and simple device architectures limit overall performance and functionalities. We propose a nano-printing platform to create multi-dimensional IR QD nanostructures beyond standard lithography, achieving photonically enhanced and tunable photoresponsivity. This method couples high-resolution electrohydrodynamic (EHD) printing with in-situ surface chemical treatment to deliver design freedom and nanoscale precision. We will first study morphology control in printing IR-absorbing PbS, HgTe, and InSb QDs and electron-transport ZnO QDs. Preliminary studies support the feasibility of printing nano-lines and nano-walls of these QDs with sub-300-nm linewidth. Room-temperature chemical treatments favor layer-by-layer printing of electronically coupled QD structures. We will design photonic structures by directly printing IR QDs, guided by electromagnetic modeling to align photonic resonances with QD absorption. We will also suppress droplet drift across inhomogeneous surfaces and morphology deviations during multi-layer printing. Finally, we will print QD lateral field-effect photodiodes to study tunable IR photoresponse via geometry modification, electrostatic gating, and photodoping. We will improve the reliability of bias-dependent device characteristics to build responsivity matrices for IR spectrum reconstruction and expand QD photodetector arrays for hyperspectral imaging. This research will deepen our understanding of microstructure evolution in printed QD assemblies during EHD printing and subsequent chemical treatment and provide insights for creating photon-managing structures and tunable photodetection modes. The lateral field-effect photodiode with switchable photoresponse provides a new paradigm for developing multi-functional photodetectors. 本計劃旨在解決多層膠體量子點（QDs）在納米級形貌控制列印過程中的挑戰，以增強紅外（IR）光電探測能力。感測與通訊技術的進步對高效率、可調控的近紅外光電探測器提出了更迫切的需求。單靠靜態的光電導或光生伏打模式已無法滿足計算光譜學與高維成像的要求。膠體量子點憑藉溶液加工特性及可程式化的光電性質，為低成本、兼容 CMOS 的紅外元件帶來了廣闊前景。然而，量子點光電探測器在 1500 nm 以上波段的外量子效率（EQE）仍低於 50%。其核心挑戰在於紅外光吸收與載流子輸運對薄膜厚度要求的矛盾。因此，必須開發新型元件架構與製造方法，結合光子學結構以最大化紅外光子利用率，並整合半導體結以促進載流子分離。 傳統的等離激元及光子增強方法依賴微影技術進行金屬圖案化，這增加了光學損耗、製備複雜性及量產成本。噴墨列印作為一種按需製造技術，目前尚未具備將光響應量子點組裝成客製化結構的靈活性。現有最新的量子點列印技術受限於較低的列印解析度（>10 µm），不足以觸發光子增強效應；同時在多材料沉積過程中還面臨跨層干擾問題。因此，全列印量子點光電探測器的報導極為罕見，且簡陋的元件架構限制了其整體效能與功能。 我們提出一種納米列印平台，用於建構突破傳統微影限制的多維紅外量子點納米結構，實現光子增強及可調控的光響應度。該方法將高解析度電流體動力學（EHD）列印與原位表面化學處理相結合，賦予設計自由度與納米級精度。我們將首先研究吸光型 PbS、HgTe、InSb 量子點以及電子輸運型 ZnO 量子點在列印過程中的形貌控制。初步研究證實了列印線寬小於 300 nm 的量子點納米線與納米牆的可行性。室溫化學處理有助於逐層列印具備電子耦合的量子點結構。我們將在電磁模擬的指導下，透過直接列印紅外量子點來設計光子學結構，使光子共振與量子點吸收峰精準對齊。我們亦將抑制液滴在非均質表面上的漂移，以及多層列印過程中的形貌偏差。最後，我們將列印量子點橫向場效光電二極管，透過結構微調、電場柵極調控及光摻雜來研究可調控的紅外光響應。我們將提升偏壓依賴性元件特性的可靠性，以建構用於紅外光譜重建的響應度矩陣，並拓展量子點光電探測器陣列用於高光譜成像。 本研究將深化我們對 EHD 列印及隨後化學處理過程中，列印量子點組裝體微觀結構演化的理解，並為創制光子管理結構與可調光電探測模式提供新見解。具有可切換光響應特性的橫向場效光電二極管，為開發多功能光電探測器開闢了全新範式。

17207826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17207826.value: 邊緣端大模型的輕量級分割聯邦微調：基礎與應用

17207826.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17207826.value: Prof FANG, Yuguang Prof Lee, Tatia Mei Chun

17207826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17207826.value: On-device large language models (LLMs) enable users to access LLM services with data privacy, but unlocking their full potential in private domains requires on-device/federated fine-tuning, which demands prohibitive computing and memory resources beyond the reach of most edge devices. Split federated learning (SFL), which partitions a model between devices and a server for co-training, offers a promising path forward. Yet, its application to LLMs remains in its infancy, confronted by three fundamental challenges: prohibitive communication costs at the model split point, on-device computing bottlenecks, and the difficulty in preserving both input data and label privacy. This project introduces SplitTune, a lightweight split federated fine-tuning (SFFT) framework to overcome these barriers through three core innovations. First, to combat the communication bottleneck, we will pioneer an inter-epoch temporal compression module for activation/gradient transmissions at the model split point, borrowing the wisdom from video compression. We further extend this framework to learning-oriented transmission protocols over unreliable wireless channels. Second, to mitigate the computing barrier, we will design a client-backpropagation-free hybrid SFFT architecture, enabling clients to perform forward-only zeroth-order optimization while the server performs regular backpropagation during split fine-tuning. We further enhance computing efficiency via a novel expert-wise model partitioning to flexibly adjust trainable parameters on each client. Third, to enhance user privacy, we will develop a lightweight privacy-preserving SFFT by detaching loss calculation from where labels are located and altering representation-token mapping, thereby keeping both data and labels securely on-device during split fine-tuning. To demonstrate tangible impact, we will develop a SplitTune-powered on-device LLM system for mental well-being, addressing a critical need in high-stress modern society. This application, defined by its strict communication, computing, and privacy constraints, will serve as a powerful validation of SplitTune's capacity to provide efficient, private, and context-aware AI support at the network edge. Beyond this, SplitTune is expected to advance the broader field of edge learning, unlocking other mission-critical and privacy-sensitive applications such as healthcare, elderly care, and home robots. 裝置端大型語言模型（LLM）讓用戶能夠在保障數據私隱的情況下使用 LLM 服務；然而，要在私有領域釋放其潛力，則需要進行裝置端／聯邦式微調，而這對運算及記憶體資源的要求極高，超出大多數邊緣裝置的能力範圍。分割式聯邦學習（SFL）將模型分割於裝置與伺服器之間並進行協同訓練，為此提供了一條具前景的路徑。然而，將其應用於 LLM 仍處於起步階段，並面臨三項根本挑戰：模型分割點的通訊成本高昂、裝置端運算瓶頸，以及難以同時保護輸入數據與標籤私隱。 本項目提出 SplitTune，一個輕量級分割式聯邦微調（SFFT）框架，透過三項核心創新克服上述障礙。首先，為應對通訊瓶頸，我們將率先開發一個用於模型分割點之激活值／梯度傳輸的跨訓練輪次時間壓縮模組，借鑑視頻壓縮的智慧。我們亦會進一步將此框架擴展至不可靠無線信道上的面向學習的傳輸協議。其次，為緩解運算障礙，我們將設計一種無需客戶端反向傳播的混合式 SFFT 架構，使客戶端在分割式微調期間僅執行前向傳播的零階優化，而伺服器則執行常規反向傳播。我們亦會透過一種新的按專家劃分模型分割方法，靈活調整各客戶端上的可訓練參數，進一步提升運算效率。第三，為加強用戶私隱，我們將開發一種輕量級的私隱保護 SFFT，透過將損失計算與標籤所在位置分離，並改變表徵與詞元之間的映射，從而在分割式微調期間確保數據與標籤均安全地保留於裝置端。 為展示實際影響，本項目將開發一個由 SplitTune 驅動、面向心理健康的裝置端 LLM 系統，以應對高壓現代社會中的迫切需要。此應用具有嚴格的通訊、運算及私隱限制，將有力驗證 SplitTune 在網絡邊緣提供高效、私密且具情境感知能力的 AI 支援之能力。除此之外，SplitTune 預期亦將推動更廣泛的邊緣學習領域發展，釋放其他私隱敏感應用的潛力，例如醫療保健、長者照護及家用機械人。

17208326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17208326.value: 面向高速具身智能的動態容錯模擬脈衝神經網絡與自適應時間縮放神經元

17208326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17208326.value: The explosive demand for real-time artificial intelligence (AI) in power-constrained edge devices is severely limited by the high energy consumption and latency of conventional digital hardware, a problem known as the von Neumann bottleneck. While brain-inspired neuromorphic computing offers a promising solution, the field has largely diverged from its foundational principles, often resulting in digital simulators that lose the richness of biological computation or simplified analog systems that fail to scale. This project answers the call for a neuromorphic renaissance, aiming to build a fully analog, continuous-time system that eliminates the expensive data converters (ADCs/DACs) bottlenecking mixed-signal designs. Our idea, demonstrated in an integrated system with dense 1T1R memristor synapses and custom CMOS neurons, is the hardware analog Spike Response Model (SRM) neuron. It uses simple passive RC circuits to implement its temporal convolution, exhibiting rich bio-plausible dynamics, like adaptive thresholds and bursting behavior. Because of our custom kernel, the neuron exhibits a proportional time-scaling property, which decouples the hardware’s fast operational speed from the slower timescale of real-world signals. Our preliminary result, as attached to this proposal, has validated this approach, demonstrating a clear computational advantage over standard Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) neurons, and promising significant hardware benefits. Our research plan begins by characterizing and optimizing our neuron design (Task 1). We will explore its design space, determine optimal RC kernel parameters, investigate the use of RRAM for reconfigurable dynamics, and build a high-fidelity hardware model. This foundation enables two complementary research thrusts. The first, focused on spiking AI acceleration (Task 2), will engineer a highly efficient and resilient perception module by developing hardware-aware training, adopting hardware compensation techniques in the spiking domain, and exploring neuromorphic hardware-friendly local learning rules. The second, a more bio-inspired path (Task 3), will use our hardware to emulate a computational neural manifold, a physical, continuous-time recurrent spiking neural network model of the brain’s head-direction system, providing a tool for neuroscience and a practical navigation unit. Finally, the project’s outcome will be demonstrated in a tangible embodied intelligence demonstration where the perception and bio-inspired navigation modules are integrated into a single mobile robot. By performing quantitative benchmark against a conventional digital implementation, we will deliver proof of our approach’s system-level advantages. While this project uses RRAM, the outcomes are also applicable to a wide range of emerging non-volatile memory technologies, e.g., FeRAM, STT/SOT-MRAM, PCM, and Flash memories. 邊緣設備對實時人工智能（AI）的需求急速增長，但傳統數字硬件的高能耗與高延遲，即所謂馮諾依曼瓶頸，嚴重限制了大型 AI 模型在功耗受限場景下的部署。受大腦啟發的神經形態計算被視為可行的出路，然而該領域近年已大致偏離其原初理念，其成果往往是失去生物計算豐富性的數字模擬器，或是難以擴展的簡化模擬系統。 本項目回應「神經形態復興」的呼籲，目標是構建全模擬、連續時間的計算系統，從而免除在混合信號設計中構成瓶頸的高成本數據轉換器（ADC／DAC）。我們的核心構思是硬件模擬脈衝響應模型（SRM）神經元，並已在一個由高密度 1T1R 憶阻器突觸與定製 CMOS 神經元構成的整合系統中得到驗證。該神經元以簡單的無源 RC 電路實現時域卷積，展現出自適應閾值與叢發放電等豐富的類生物動力學。由於採用定製的響應核，神經元具備比例時間縮放特性，使硬件的高速運行與真實世界信號較慢的時間尺度得以解耦。隨本申請提交的前期結果已驗證此方法，證明其相對於標準洩漏積分發放（LIF）神經元具有明確的計算優勢，並可帶來顯著的硬件效益。 研究計劃首先對神經元設計進行表徵與優化（任務一），包括探索其設計空間、確定最優 RC 響應核參數、研究以阻變記憶體（RRAM）實現可重構動力學，並建立高保真硬件模型。在此基礎上展開兩條互補的研究路線。其一以邊緣端 AI 加速為目標（任務二），透過發展硬件感知訓練、將硬件補償技術移植至脈衝域，以及探索適合神經形態硬件的局部學習規則，構建高效且具容錯能力的基於脈衝神經網絡的感知模組。其二為更具生物啟發性的路線（任務三），利用本硬件模擬計算神經流形，即以物理、連續時間的循環脈衝神經網絡再現大腦頭朝向系統，既為神經科學提供實驗平台，亦可作為實用的導航單元。 最後，本項目將把感知模組與生物啟發的導航模組整合於同一移動機械人，完成具身智能的實體演示，並與傳統數字實現進行定量對比，以驗證本方法在系統層面的優勢。雖然本項目以阻變記憶體（RRAM）為實現載體，研究成果亦適用於其他新興非揮發性記憶體技術，例如鐵電記憶體（FeRAM）、自旋轉移矩／自旋軌道矩磁性記憶體（STT／SOT-MRAM）、相變記憶體（PCM）及快閃記憶體。

17208526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17208526.value: Relay：提升關鍵任務軟件應用的地理分布式資料庫事務的一致性保證與性能

17208526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17208526.value: Global Internet connectivity is pushing almost every mission-critical software application (e.g., Robo-taxi) to deploy beyond one single geo-graphic region: typically, one city/town, with fast Round-Trip Time (RTT) of only several milliseconds between two computer hosts (e.g., two cars). While an application’s database tables are split or replicated across regions, the application’s users naturally desire strong consistency guarantees on the database’s transactions (i.e., all users concurrently invoking transactions from different regions can read the effect of the same sequential order of all these transactions). Unfortunately, preliminary study in this proposal identified severe research problems regarding the ``frequent mutual-blocking between intra-region transactions (IRTs) and cross-region transactions (CRTs)’’, causing the 90-percentile user-perceived latency of intra-region transactions to be deferred by 32.18X. Existing relevant academic and industrial databases (e.g., Google’s Spanner and MongoDB) incur limitations in tackling these problems, as these databases either stick with strong consistency guarantees but ignore the severe latency deferment, or these databases compromise to much weaker consistency guarantees (however, weaker consistency guarantees could easily cause an auto-drive application such as Robo-taxi to generate different scheduling actions for cars on the nearby streets/regions, leading to inconsistent accidents among cars). To tackle these problems, this proposal will develop Relay, a new software system for the concurrency control of a geo-distributed database to support mission-critical applications (e.g., Robo-taxi and Apollo Go, Poly HK auction, and eToro trading), including three objectives. First (Relay-T), we will solve the mutual-blocking problems between intra-region and cross-region transactions, by proposing new distributed algorithms for simultaneously enabling two slightly variant but still strongly consistent guarantees within the same database deployment instance. Second (Relay-R), we will develop the first user-perceived-deterministic transaction replication protocols, greatly reducing transactions’ cross-region RTT on tolerating computer host failures. Third (Relay++), we will integrate the first and second objectives with advanced satellitebased, host-clock synchronization techniques to alleviate transactions’ deferment caused by Internet instability. Our preliminary research prototypes with the proposed theoretically-proof methods of the algorithms/protocols from this proposal show that, all prototypes theoretically enforce the variant strong consistency guarantees, with an empirical improvement of 31.05X on 90-percentile transaction latencies. These promising results are published/accepted by VLDB-2025 and SIGMOD-2026. The success of this proposal will nurture new theoretical methods and practical deployments for mission-critical software applications across more regions (in HK and world), with strong consistency guarantees and high performance on database transactions. 全球網際網路連線推動幾乎所有關鍵任務軟體應用程式（例如，Robo-taxi）以部署於單一地理區域之外：通常，一個城市/城鎮，且快速往返時間（RTT）僅相差數毫秒兩個電腦主機（例如兩台車）。 雖然應用程式的資料庫資料表會被分割或複製於不同區域，但應用程式使用者自然希望資料庫的一致性有強保證交易（即所有同時呼叫來自不同區域的交易的使用者，可以請閱讀所有這些交易相同順序的效果）。很遺憾，本提案的初步研究指出，關於「區域內交易（IRT）與跨區域間頻繁的相互阻塞交易（CRT）」，導致區域內用戶感知的90百分位延遲交易將延後至32.18X。現有相關的學術與產業資料庫（例如 Google 的 Spanner 和 MongoDB）在處理這些問題時會受到限制，問題在於這些資料庫要麼堅持強一致性保證，要麼忽略嚴重延遲，或這些資料庫會被妥協到更弱的程度一致性保證（然而，較弱的一致性保證很容易導致自動駕駛應用程式如 Robo-taxi 以產生不同的排程動作附近街道或區域的車輛，導致車輛間發生不一致的事故）。 為了解決這些問題，本提案將開發 Relay，一套用於並行控制地理分布式資料庫以支援關鍵任務應用程式（例如 Robo-taxi 和 Apollo Go、Poly HK 拍賣及 eToro 交易），其中包括三個目標。首先（Relay-T），我們將解決相互阻塞的問題在區域內與跨區域交易間，透過提出新的分散式交易同時實現兩個略有變化但仍高度一致的演算法保證在同一資料庫部署實例內。第二（Relay-R），我們會大幅開發首個使用者感知確定性交易複製協議降低交易跨區域 RTT，以容忍電腦主機故障。第三（Relay++），我們將把第一和第二目標與先進的衛星整合，主機與時脈同步技術，以減輕因網路不穩定造成的交易延遲。 我們初步研究原型採用理論證明的方法及對本提案中的演算法/協議顯示，所有原型理論上皆適用強制執行變體強一致性保證，並帶來經驗上的改進90百分位交易延遲的31.05倍。這些令人鼓舞的結果已由VLDB-2025及SIGMOD-2026發表/接受。 本提案的成功將培育新的理論方法與實務在更多地區（如香港及世界），具備強大的一致性保證與高效能資料庫交易。

17208826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17208826.value: 車–場合作：共享自動駕駛車隊與停車設施的協同規劃與動態運營

17208826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17208826.value: Shared Autonomous Vehicle (SAV) services are progressing from pilot trials to early commercial deployment, with over 14 million rides delivered in China by 2024. However, a significant operational bottleneck persists as SAV services scale up. SAVs spend 8-16 hours daily idle for parking or charging, often in remote depots far from customers. This forces SAVs to make long, empty “deadheading” trips, wasting energy, adding congestion, and increasing costs. Meanwhile, many well-located parking facilities are not fully used. If SAVs could be assigned to these facilities for parking or charging, vehicles would remain closer to customers and reduce empty miles. Moreover, this offers parking operators a new revenue stream from otherwise underutilized assets. This project investigates the potential Fleet-Facility Partnership (FFP) between SAV and parking operators, quantifies its benefits and impacts, and outlines pathways to transform parking facilities into smart “partner platforms” for SAV operations. Despite its potential benefits, the FFP between SAV and parking operators has not yet been studied. The FFP synergy involves interdependent and interactive decision-making by SAV and parking operators. On the parking side, facilities serve both the SAV partner and regular customers, requiring efficient strategies for time-dependent parking capacity allocation/reservation across user groups, and corresponding pricing policies, in response to SAV allocation and dispatching decisions. Simultaneously, the SAV operator must jointly optimize passenger service provision and fleet allocation/dispatching across a network of facilities, considering parking operator’s capacity allocation and pricing strategies. Optimizing these interdependent decisions is further complicated by two-sided uncertainties in mobility and parking demand. This project will tackle these challenges by developing innovative analytical and optimization methodologies to support collaborative planning and operation within an FFP. The novelty of this project is threefold. First, we will develop the first game-theoretic model to identify conditions where FFP benefits both SAV and parking operators, and to establish optimal long-term strategies for both operators. Second, we will establish a network model to optimize the SAV and parking operators’ resource allocation and pricing in a facility network under spatiotemporally varying supply-demand conditions. Third, we will develop real-time optimization strategies for SAV and parking operators under two-sided uncertainty in parking and mobility demand. In collaboration with industry partners (major SAV and parking operators), the developed methodologies will be validated in realistic case studies. Overall, this project will generate new methodologies and actionable insights for the integration of mobility services and urban infrastructure. 共享自動駕駛出行服務正從試點試驗邁向早期商業部署，截至二零二四年，中國已提供超過一千四百萬次自動駕駛出行服務。然而，隨着服務規模擴大，一個顯著的運營瓶頸持續存在。共享自動駕駛服務車輛每日需花費八至十六小時閒置以進行停車或充電，而這些活動往往在遠離乘客的偏遠停車場進行。這迫使共享自動駕駛車輛進行長距離的空駛行程，浪費能源、加劇交通擁堵並增加成本。與此同時，許多位置優越的停車設施並未得到充分利用。若共享自動駕駛車輛能在這些離乘客更近的設施進行停車或充電，可以有效減少空駛里程；此外，這亦能為停車場營運商從原本未被充分利用的資產中開闢新的收入來源。本項目旨在探討共享自動駕駛車隊營運商與停車場營運商之間「車隊–設施合作」的潛力，量化其效益與影響，並勾勒將停車設施轉型為共享自動駕駛車隊營運之智慧「協作平台」的路徑。 儘管「車隊–設施合作」模式具有潛在效益，共享自動駕駛車隊與停車場營運商之間的此類合作至今尚未得到系統性的研究。此合作模式涉及共享自動駕駛車輛與停車場營運商之間相關聯的互動決策過程。就停車場而言，設施需同時服務共享自動駕駛車隊合作夥伴和一般客戶，因而需要制定高效的針對不同用戶群體的容量分配與預約策略及定價策略，以應對共享自動駕駛車隊的分配與調度決策。與此同時，共享自動駕駛車隊營運商須在考慮停車場營運商容量分配與定價策略的前提下，於設施網絡中聯合優化乘客服務供應及車隊分配與調度。而優化這些相互依存的決策，更因出行需求與停車需求兩端的雙重不確定性而變得愈發複雜。本項目將開發創新的分析與優化方法論，以支持「車隊–設施合作」框架下的協同規劃與運營。 本項目的創新性體現在三個方面。第一，我們將建立首個博弈論模型，識別「車隊–設施合作」能使共享自動駕駛車隊與停車場營運商雙方受益的條件，並為雙方營運商制定最優的長期策略。第二，我們將建立一個網絡模型，以在時空變化的供需條件下，優化設施網絡中共享自動駕駛車隊與停車場營運商的資源分配與定價。第三，我們將在停車需求與出行需求雙向不確定性下，為共享自動駕駛車隊與停車場營運商開發實時優化策略。總體而言，本項目旨在為出行服務與城市基礎設施的融合提供新的方法論及指導建議。

17208926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17208926.value: 基於複合時間尺度和物理資訊驅動的生成式深度學習的海上風電場的動態尾流建模與性能提升

17208926.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17208926.value: Prof YANG, Hong-xing Prof Zhao, Lin

17208926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17208926.value: The turbine wake refers to the trail left by the upstream turbines with the decreased wind speed and the increased turbulence intensity. The adverse wake effect, which correspondingly results in less energy production and triggers earlier fatigue failure of downstream turbines, may significantly impact the overall performance of offshore wind farms. However, current studies on lifecycle wake mitigation strategies, i.e., layout optimization in the design stage and cooperative yaw control in the operation stage, mostly adopt steady-state wake solutions. Accurate characterization of the wake dynamics in wind farms poses great technical challenges, including: (1) The fatigue wind load is overlooked in most of the layout optimization frameworks based on the maximization of power generation so the design layout may not be optimal in reality in terms of structural safety. The low-fidelity analytical model does not fully account for the dynamic variations in wind speed and direction nor accurately capture the transient loads on turbines that result from such variability; (2) most previous cooperative yaw wake control studies assume a time-invariant inflow to determine optimal yaw settings. This approach not only ignores the rapid fluctuations in wind speed and direction but also assumes an instantaneous impact of yaw actions on downstream turbines, which diverges significantly from engineering reality. (3) The high-fidelity LES simulations are capable of capturing the complex wake meandering behavior, but their computational efficiency is too low to adapt to real-time yaw control. The primary objective of the project is to establish an innovative hierarchical physics-informed generative adversarial network (HPIGAN) deep-learning (DL) framework for dynamic wake modeling of wind farms, which strikes a balance of efficiency and accuracy. The HPIGAN framework will be deployed in the following lifecycle application scenarios: (1) Coupling layout optimization based on power and fatigue life, where a two-stage framework, including simplified design recommendation and a fine-tuned machine-learning (ML) based LGBM (light gradient-boosted model), to assess the peak and fatigue loads are proposed; (2) Dynamic wake cooperative control for overall power maximization, where both unsteady inflow and process of yaw angle change accompanied with the wake propagation are considered; (3) Joint optimization combining layout optimization and cooperative yaw control. Finally, the proposed HPIGAN framework and dynamic cooperative control strategy will be validated by the wind tunnel testing. The project is expected to promote the energy efficiency of offshore wind farms by improving energy production and reducing the structural risk downtime through incorporating dynamic wake interactions. 風機尾流是指上游風機後方形成風速降低且湍流強度增加的區域。不利的尾流效應會導致發電量減少，並引發下游風機的早期疲勞破壞，從而顯著影響海上風電場的整體性能。然而，目前關於全生命週期尾流減緩策略的研究（即設計階段的佈局優化和運行階段的協同偏航控制），大多採用穩態尾流求解方案。 在風電場中準確表徵尾流動態面臨著巨大的技術挑戰：（1）忽視疲勞風載荷：絕大多數以發電量最大化為目標的佈局優化框架忽視了疲勞風載荷，因此在結構安全性方面，設計出的佈局在實際應用中可能並非最優。低保真度的解析模型無法充分考量風速和風向的動態變化，也無法準確捕獲由此引發的風機瞬態載荷。（2）假設入流時不變：大多數以往的協同偏航尾流控制研究均假設入流條件時不變來確定最佳偏航設置。這種方法不僅忽略了風速和風向的快速波動，還假設偏航動作對下游風機產生即時影響，這與工程實際嚴重偏離。（3）計算效率極低：高保真度的大渦模擬（LES）能夠捕獲複雜的尾流蜿蜒行為，但其計算效率過低，無法適應實時偏航控制的需求。 本項目的首要目標是建立一種創新的分級物理資訊生成對抗網絡（HPIGAN）深層學習（DL）框架，作為風電場的動態尾流模型，在效率與精度之間取得平衡。非平穩且非線性的尾流場的時空演化可以看作是一個時序圖像生成任務：當前時間步的流場狀態（圖像輸出）取決於上一個時間步的尾流場以及當前時間步的環境風場（圖像輸入）。因此，本項目提出了一種條件生成對抗網絡（cGAN）架構作為替代的一步求解器，在施加物理資訊邊界條件約束下執行圖到圖的轉換任務，並將同一時刻尾流與環境風場之間的不變性關係引入損失函數中。通過對不同時間尺度上的上述深度學習模型進行分級時間聚合，可以減少長期預測中的累積誤差。此外，HPIGAN 框架將部署於以下全生命週期應用場景中：（1）結合功率與疲勞壽命的佈局優化：提出一個包含簡化設計建議和精細化基於機器學習（ML）的輕量級梯度提升模型（LGBM）的兩階段框架，用於評估峰值和疲勞載荷。（2）以整體功率最大化為目標的動態尾流協同控制：同時考慮非穩態入流以及伴隨尾流傳播的偏航角變化過程。（3）結合佈局優化與協同偏航控制的聯合優化。最後，所提出的 HPIGAN 框架和動態協同控制策略將通過風洞實驗進行驗證。本項目預計通過引入動態尾流相互作用來提高發電量並減少結構風險停機時間，從而提升海上風電場的能源效率。

17209126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17209126.value: 截留微塑膠只是起點：生物滯留系統中的積累、沖刷及管理策略

17209126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17209126.value: Microplastics—synthetic particles 1 µm to 5 mm in size—are persistent pollutants entering urban waterways mainly via stormwater runoff from tire wear, synthetic fibers, and litter. Bioretention systems, which are landscaped areas designed to capture and filter stormwater runoff using soil and plants, effectively trap microplastics during routine rain, acting as temporary sinks. However, long-term accumulation and transformations can lead to remobilization during intense storms, turning these systems into secondary pollution sources. Climate change exacerbates this risk by increasing extreme rainfall frequency and intensity, yet current designs lack strategies for long-term retention or washout prevention. This project addresses this gap by examining how microplastic type, size, and shape evolve across bioretention layers over time, identifying hydraulic thresholds that trigger washout, and developing practical inlet controls and maintenance protocols. It integrates laboratory experiments, predictive modeling, and field validation to deliver actionable solutions for sustainable urban drainage. In the first part, laboratory experiments will simulate two years of microplastic buildup in bioretention systems within six months. The study will track how much and where microplastics—both buoyant and non-buoyant—accumulate at different depths. Following this, flume experiments will assess how intense storms wash out these particles, identifying rainfall conditions that trigger significant release. In the second part, a predictive model will be developed to simulate both gradual accumulation during dry periods and sudden washout during storms. It will switch between the two modes based on rainfall conditions and be calibrated with laboratory data to forecast long-term microplastic behavior under varying climate conditions. In the third part, practical flow-control devices—such as adjustable valves—will be tested in the laboratory and deployed at a pilot site in Foshan, China. The ability of these inlet control strategies to reduce microplastic washout while maintaining stormwater management performance will be evaluated over six months in comparison with a standard system without the inlet control strategies. The project will also propose an adaptive maintenance protocol that uses model predictions to schedule media cleaning or replacement according to actual microplastic accumulation levels, rather than relying on fixed time intervals. Building on the team’s prior research in sustainable urban drainage systems, this project will deliver the first integrated framework for managing microplastics in bioretention systems, directly informing engineering practice and stormwater policy—ensuring these systems remain as effective sinks, not hidden sources, of microplastic pollution under changing climate. 微塑膠是指尺寸介乎 1 微米至 5 毫米的人造塑膠微粒，屬於持久性污染物，主要經由輪胎磨損、合成纖維及塑膠垃圾等途徑，隨雨水徑流進入城市水體。生物滯留系統是一種利用土壤和植物來收集並過濾雨水徑流的景觀設施，能在日常降雨中有效截留微塑膠，發揮臨時匯集庫（sink）的作用。然而，長期積累及形態變化可能導致微塑膠在暴雨期間再次釋放，使此類系統反過來成為二次污染源。氣候變化加劇了極端降雨的頻率與強度，進一步擴大此風險，惟現有設計尚未針對長期截留或防止沖刷提出相應對策。 本項目旨在填補上述研究空白，具體包括：探討不同類型、尺寸和形狀的微塑膠在生物滯留系統各層中隨時間的演變規律；識別觸發微塑膠沖刷的水力閾值；以及開發實用的進水口控制裝置和維護方案。本項目結合實驗室實驗、預測模型及現場驗證，為可持續城市排水系統提供可操作之解決方案。 第一部分為實驗室實驗，將在六個月內模擬生物滯留系統中為期兩年的微塑膠積累過程，追蹤不同密度（浮力型與非浮力型）的微塑膠在不同深度的累積量與分佈位置。隨後，透過水槽實驗評估暴雨如何沖刷此類微粒，從而識別觸發大量釋放的降雨條件。第二部分將開發一個預測模型，用以模擬旱季期間的逐步積累過程與暴雨期間的突發性沖刷過程。該模型將根據降雨條件在兩種模式之間切換，並以實驗室數據進行校準，從而預測不同氣候條件下微塑膠的長期行為。第三部分將在實驗室測試實用的流量控制裝置（如可調節閥門），並於中國佛山市的一個試驗場地進行實地部署。透過與無進水口控制策略的標準系統進行為期六個月的對比，評估上述進水口控制策略在維持雨水管理效能的同時，能否有效減少微塑膠的沖刷。此外，本項目還將提出一套適應性維護方案，利用模型預測結果，根據微塑膠的實際累積水平來安排濾料清理或更換，而非依賴固定時間間隔。 本項目建基於團隊過往在可持續城市排水系統方面的研究成果，將構建首個針對生物滯留系統中微塑膠管理的整合框架，直接為工程實踐與雨水管理政策提供依據——確保此類系統在氣候變化的背景下，始終作為微塑膠污染的有效匯集庫，而非隱蔽的排放源。

17209626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17209626.value: 延展性范德華半導體冷焊的納米力學機制與功能器件應用

17209626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17209626.value: Cold Welding represents a highly promising solid-state nano-manufacturing method, particularly for the integration, repair, and additive manufacturing of functional devices and structures, which has been widely investigated and applied in metallic systems owing to the nondirectional metallic bonds that facilitate atomic diffusion across interfaces. However, applying cold welding to conventional inorganic semiconductors remains challenging due to their rigid covalent/ionic crystal structures, which resist deformation and interfacial bonding without high-temperature processing. The recent discovery of ductile van der Waals (vdW) crystals, with strong in-plane covalent bonding and weak out-of-plane interactions, has opened new pathways for cold welding in semiconductors. Ductile vdW semiconductors exhibit key characteristics, including multicenter diffuse interlayer bonding, the continuous dynamic breaking and re-forming of chemical bonds during deformation, and phase transformation-mediated plasticity. Collectively, these properties suggest that ductile vdW semiconductors may serve as an ideal platform for advancing cold welding techniques, which is a highly promising, yet underexplored, nanomanufacturing route for monolithic integration, as it bypasses the need for melt-recrystallization or adhesive interlayers. Progress in both cold welding and deformable electronics has been constrained by a reciprocal set of challenges: the former by a scarcity of suitable material systems, and the latter by a lack of compatible nanofabrication techniques for emerging ductile semiconductors. This project seeks to address these intertwined limitations by establishing cold welding as a viable nanomanufacturing method for deformable vdW devices. Through an integrated methodology combining in situ nanomechanical testing, advanced microscopy, multi-physics characterization, and device demonstration, the research aims to achieve the following objectives: (i) Establish the fundamental criteria and critical parameters, such as size limit and crystallographic orientation dependence, for achieving pristine cold-welded junctions in representative vdW semiconductors (e.g., InSe and GaSe). (ii) Elucidate the atomic-scale mechanisms and nanomechanics governing the cold welding process, with particular emphasis on plastic deformation behavior, interfacial adhesion, and the effect of crystallographic misorientation on bond strength and quality. (iii) Quantify the mechanical integrity, interfacial property, and structural reliability of cold-welded junctions across multiple scales and under varied service conditions. (iv) Demonstrate functional vdW meta-devices fabricated via cold welding and characterize their coupled mechanical, electrical, and thermal-electric performance, focusing on the interrelationship between strain, deformed structures, and functional properties. This project will establish the foundational process-structure-property relationship for cold welding of ductile vdW semiconductors, translating this knowledge into practical device applications and guiding future design and manufacturing of high-performance deformable electronics systems. 冷焊是一種極具潛力的固態納米製造技術，特別適用於功能器件與結構的集成、修復及增材製造。由於金屬材料具有非方向性的金屬鍵，能有效促進原子在界面間擴散，因此冷焊技術在金屬領域已獲得廣泛的研究與應用。然而，將冷焊技術應用於傳統無機半導體仍面臨嚴峻挑戰；這主要歸因於其剛性的共價鍵或離子鍵晶體結構，導致材料在未經高溫處理的情況下，難以發生塑性變形及實現有效的界面鍵合。 近年來，具備延展性的范德華晶體相繼被發現；其面內強共價鍵與面外弱范德華力的獨特結構，為半導體冷焊技術開闢了全新途徑。這類延展性范德華半導體展現出多項關鍵特性，包含多中心彌散的層間相互作用、變形過程中化學鍵的連續動態斷裂與重組，以及由相變介導的塑性變形。綜合而言，上述特性使其成為推進冷焊技術應用的理想材料平台。 當前，冷焊技術與可變形電子學的發展正面臨相互制約的瓶頸：前者受限於缺乏合適的材料體系，後者則缺乏適用於新興延展性半導體的納米製造工藝。本項目旨在將冷焊技術發展為可變形范德華器件的有效納米製造方法，從而突破上述技術壁壘。通過結合原位納米力學測試、先進顯微技術、多物理場表徵及器件展示等綜合研究手段，本研究旨在確立以 InSe 等為代表的范德華半導體在冷焊過程中的基礎準則與關鍵參數，揭示該過程中的原子尺度機制與納米力學行為，量化冷焊節點在多尺度及不同服役條件下的結構可靠性，並最終展示基於納米冷焊技術製造的功能性范德華器件，深入表徵其機械、電學及熱電耦合性能。本項目將建立延展性范德華半導體冷焊工藝—結構—性能的內在關聯，為未來高性能可變形電子系統的設計與微納製造提供科學指導。

17210226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17210226.value: 基於藥效學引導的魯棒強化學習的慢性骨髓性白血病停藥策略優化

17210226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17210226.value: Prof Chen, Frank Youhua Prof HO, Chin Pang Prof Li, Jing Xi Joshua Prof Li, Weiming Prof Singh Gill, Harry

17210226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17210226.value: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) is largely controllable with targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), but many patients require long‑term therapy with substantial costs, side effects, and frequent monitoring. A growing subset of patients who achieve very deep molecular responses can stop treatment and remain in treatment‑free remission (TFR), yet predicting who will sustain TFR and how to taper or stop safely remains an open clinical challenge. Key biological drivers—residual stem‑cell burden, immune control within an “immune window,” and stochastic emergence of resistant clones—are patient-specific and difficult to infer from observations alone. Existing modeling approaches do not jointly incorporate these mechanisms while accounting for real‑world measurement error, imperfect adherence, irregular monitoring, and structural model uncertainty. We will develop and validate a pharmacodynamics‑guided, robust reinforcement learning (robust RL) platform that combines a novel mechanistic model (immuneCML) with decision algorithms that explicitly account for worst‑case perturbations. immuneCML couples quiescent and proliferating leukemic compartments, immune effector dynamics, TKI pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics, and stochastic mutation seeding to constrain learning and improve interpretability. Our proposed Robust RL algorithm optimizes sequential dosing, dose reduction, and cessation policies under worst‑case perturbations in measurements, adherence, and model structure, using offline clinical data and clinician‑seeded training to guide learning toward safe, clinically relevant strategies. %under adversarial measurement, adherence, and model perturbations, training offline on clinician‑seeded trajectories to bias learning toward safe, clinically relevant strategies. We will pretrain and fine‑tune models on multinational trial and registry data and harmonized local cohorts from Wuhan Union Hospital and Queen Mary Hospital, then perform retrospective validation using clinically meaningful endpoints: 12‑ and 24‑month TFR rates, time to molecular relapse, adverse dosing events, and predictive accuracy and calibration versus standard‑of‑care and RL baselines. Robustness will be quantified by stress tests simulating assay noise, bias, monitoring gaps, and structural uncertainty, and clinician review of policy traces and interpretability analyses will guide acceptability and implementation. If successful, the project will deliver a validated, safety‑aware decision framework for individualized TKI dose reduction and cessation, protocolized recommendations for prospective testing, and mechanistic insights into how immune control and resistance shape durable remission. 慢性骨髓性白血病（chronic myeloid leukemia, CML）目前大多可通過標靶酪氨酸激酶抑制劑（tyrosine kinase inhibitors, TKIs）得到有效控制。然而，許多患者仍需長期接受治療，並承受高昂費用、副作用及頻密監測所帶來的負擔。愈來愈多達至深度分子反應的患者能夠停止治療，並維持無治療緩解（treatment-free remission, TFR）。然而，如何預測哪些患者能夠持續維持TFR，以及如何安全地逐步減量或停藥，仍是尚待解決的臨床難題。影響停藥結果的關鍵生物學因素，包括殘餘白血病幹細胞負荷、「免疫窗口」內的免疫控制，以及耐藥克隆的隨機出現，均具有顯著的個體差異，且難以僅憑臨床觀察準確推斷。現有建模方法尚未能在整合上述機制的同時，充分考慮真實世界中的測量誤差、用藥依從性不足、監測時間不規則及模型結構不確定性。 本研究將開發並驗證一套由藥效學引導的魯棒強化學習（robust reinforcement learning, robust RL）方法immuneCML，並將其與能夠明確應對最壞情境擾動的決策演算法相結合。immuneCML模型整合靜止期與增殖期白血病細胞群、免疫效應細胞動力學、TKI藥代動力學與藥效學，以及隨機突變等機制，從而約束學習過程並提高模型的可解釋性。本研究提出的魯棒強化學習演算法，將在測量、用藥依從性及模型結構受到最壞情境擾動的條件下，優化序貫給藥、劑量遞減及停藥策略。演算法將利用離線臨床數據，並通過臨床醫生提供的初始引導進行訓練，使學習過程聚焦於安全且具有臨床意義的治療策略。 我們將利用跨國臨床試驗數據，以及來自武漢協和醫院和瑪麗醫院、經標準化整合的本地患者隊列，對模型進行預訓練與微調。其後將採用具臨床意義的終點進行回顧性驗證，包括停藥後12個月及24個月的TFR率、分子學復發時間、不良給藥事件，以及相較於標準治療和其他強化學習基準方法的預測準確度與校準度。模型的魯棒性將通過壓力測試進行量化，包括模擬檢測雜訊、系統性偏差、監測缺失及模型結構不確定性。此外，臨床醫生將審查模型的策略軌跡及可解釋性分析結果，以評估並改善其臨床可接受性與實施可行性。 若本研究取得成功，將建立一套經驗證且以安全性為核心的個體化TKI減量與停藥決策框架，提出可供前瞻性臨床測試的標準化建議，並深入揭示免疫控制與耐藥機制如何共同影響持久緩解。

17210326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17210326.value: 應用於大規模地圖建構的高效分佈式多感測器光束法平差法

17210326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17210326.value: Large-scale, dense, and colorized 3D maps are critical for various fields such as Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Building Information Modeling (BIM), and autonomous systems. Modern mobile mapping platforms, combining Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR), cameras, Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs), and Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS), have become the dominant means of acquiring the rich, complementary data needed to construct such maps. These platforms produce vast numbers of scans, images, and auxiliary measurements. To convert this heterogeneous data into accurate, globally consistent maps, bundle adjustment (BA) is the central tool. Despite substantial progress in BA, existing methods still fall short of real-world, large-scale requirements. Two gaps are particularly limiting. First, most BA formulations and solvers target a single sensor modality (e.g., camera-only or LiDAR-only). In contrast, building dense, colorized maps at city scale requires tightly coupled fusion of cameras, LiDAR, IMU, and GNSS within a unified BA formulation, which are capabilities that remain largely unexplored. Second, large-scale deployments produce data volumes that exceed the compute and memory of a single device, making distributed optimization a practical necessity. However, most prior work assumes single-machine execution, and a unified distributed BA framework for multi-sensor platforms is still lacking. While these gaps are challenging, recent work applying majorization–minimization (MM) to BA opens a new opportunity. Prior results show that MM can enable distributed optimization for camera BA. Building on this line of work, we have proposed a distributed LiDAR BA approach based on MM. In our latest exploration, we extend analogous MM-based constructions to incorporate IMU and GNSS factors, suggesting a principled route toward a unified, distributed multi-sensor BA. Based on these findings, we propose to develop and validate a scalable, distributed BA framework that jointly optimizes camera, LiDAR, IMU, and GNSS measurements for dense, colorized mapping. We will (i) derive tight upper-bound surrogate functions that decouple pose updates across modalities with provable convergence, (ii) design communication- and compute-efficient distributed solvers, and (iii) release an open-source implementation integrated into a complete mapping stack. We will rigorously evaluate convergence, accuracy, and scalability in simulation and extensive real-world experiments. 大規模、高密度及彩色化的三維地圖，對地理資訊系統（GIS）、建築資訊模型（BIM）以及自主系統等多個領域至關重要。現代移動測繪平台結合光達（Light Detection and Ranging, LiDAR）、相機、慣性測量單元（Inertial Measurement Units, IMUs）及全球導航衛星系統（Global Navigation Satellite Systems, GNSS），已成為獲取建構此類地圖所需豐富且互補資料的主要方式。這些平台會產生大量掃描資料、影像及輔助量測。為了將這些異質資料轉化為精確且具全域一致性的地圖，光束法平差（Bundle Adjustment, BA）是其中的核心工具。 儘管 BA 已取得顯著進展，現有方法仍未能充分滿足真實世界大規模應用的需求，其中有兩項限制尤為突出。首先，大多數 BA 的建模方式與求解器主要針對單一感測器模態，例如僅使用相機或僅使用 LiDAR。相較之下，要在城市尺度上建構高密度且彩色化的地圖，必須在統一的 BA 框架下對相機、LiDAR、IMU 及 GNSS 進行緊密耦合與融合，而這方面的能力目前仍缺乏深入研究。其次，大規模部署所產生的資料量往往超出單一運算裝置的計算能力與記憶體容量，因此分散式最佳化在實際應用中已成為必要手段。然而，現有大多數研究仍假設在單一機器上執行，目前尚缺乏一套適用於多感測器平台的統一分散式 BA 框架。 雖然上述問題極具挑戰性，近期將主函數–最小化（Majorization–Minimization, MM）方法應用於 BA 的研究，帶來了新的突破契機。先前研究結果顯示，MM 可支援相機 BA 的分散式最佳化。在此研究方向的基礎上，我們已提出一種基於 MM 的分散式 LiDAR BA 方法。在最新的探索中，我們進一步將類似的 MM 架構延伸至 IMU 及 GNSS 因子，顯示出建立統一分散式多感測器 BA 的一條具原理性且可行的路徑。 基於上述研究成果，我們提出開發並驗證一套具可擴展性的分散式 BA 框架，聯合最佳化相機、LiDAR、IMU 及 GNSS 的量測資料，以支援高密度彩色化地圖建構。我們將：（i）推導緊密的上界替代函數，使不同感測模態之間的位姿更新得以解耦，並提供可證明的收斂性；（ii）設計兼具通訊效率與計算效率的分散式求解器；以及（iii）發布開源實作，並將其整合至完整的地圖建構系統中。我們將透過模擬實驗及廣泛的真實世界實驗，嚴謹評估所提出方法在收斂性、準確度及可擴展性方面的表現。

17210426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17210426.value: Atmospheric profiles within the planetary boundary layer (PBL) are crucial for the Earth’s climate system and weather processes. These profiles provide detailed information on the atmospheric variations with altitude, which are of significant importance in various fields, such as weather forecasting and climate monitoring. In China, an average 3.9% increase in city-level forecast accuracy generates a considerable social benefit of 25.3 billion Yuan (4.03 billion USD) per year. Currently, atmospheric detection technologies are categorized into 2 types. One type is ground-based detection, such as Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) instruments and Atmospheric Infrared Sounder Spectrometer (ASSIST), but the complicated and bulky components constrain their large-scale deployments and thus wide spatial coverage. The other type is satellite-based sounder, which has wide spatial and high horizontal resolution. However, spaceborne technologies remain insufficient for resolving structures within the PBL. Unfortunately, both types are costly and thus difficult for large-scale deployment. This proposal aims to develop a Smart Microclimate Probe Technology (SMiT) to overcome issues in current technologies. The SMiT mainly relies on a machine learning-based algorithm and a customized multispectral capture device. The algorithm will be developed that incorporates physical models and restrictions to potentially reduce the searching parameter space by multi-fold. The dataset, utilized for training the algorithm, will be constructed by applying the local atmospheric data and the developed radiative transfer models. Preliminary results of virtual experiments have confirmed the feasibility of the SMiT. For hardware, we will focus on compact, lightweight, and highly integrated device designs to guarantee portability and facilitate deployment under challenging field situations. To reduce the number of filters for lightweight while remaining highly accurate detection, a group of selective infrared filters will be carefully designed and fabricated to precisely capture key multispectral information of the atmosphere. Other essential factors, including the choice of low-power, high-performance sensors and compact processor/data acquisition boards that harmonize capabilities with energy efficiency, will also be optimized. The SMiT, due to its low-cost and highly integrated features, enables to construct a city-level detection network, providing a new platform to establish ground-based 2D mesh grids for the reconstruction of high-resolution 3D information about the atmosphere. Real-time and continuous microclimate monitoring for the entire city will substantially improve the accuracy of weather forecasting and climate monitoring, facilitate the initialization of global weather models, and enhance understanding of energy and water cycles. 高解析度、即時連續的大氣探測對於地球氣候系統與天氣演進過程至關重要，大氣性質隨高度的變化情形在天氣預報、氣候監測等諸多領域都具備重大價值。在中國，若城市等級預報準確度平均提升 3.9%，每年可創造高達 253 億元人民幣（折合 40.3 億美元）的龐大社會效益。 目前大氣探測技術主要可分為兩大類：第一類為地面探測，例如傅立葉轉換紅外光譜儀（FTIR）、大氣紅外探空光譜儀（ASSIST）；然而這類設備結構繁瑣、體積龐大，難以大規模佈建，也就無法實現廣闊的空間覆蓋。第二類是衛星載探空儀，雖具備廣闊覆蓋範圍與優異的水平解析度，但星載設備仍不足以解析行星邊界層內部的精細結構。不巧的是，上述兩種技術的建置與運作成本都居高不下，因此很難進行大規模部署。 本研究計畫旨在開發「智慧微氣候探測技術（SMiT）」，解決現有技術存在的各項瓶頸。SMiT 核心運用結合機器學習的演算方法，以及特製的多光譜擷取裝置；本研究將開發一套納入物理模型與約束條件的演算法，可將待搜尋的參數空間大幅壓縮數倍。演算法訓練所需的資料集，將整合當地大氣觀測數據與本研究建構的輻射傳輸模型來建立。虛擬實驗的初步成果已驗證 SMiT 技術的可行性。 在硬體開發方面，我們將著重設計體積精簡、輕量化且高度整合的裝置，確保設備便於攜帶，可在條件艱鉅的野外環境順利佈署。為了在維持高精準度探測能力的同時減少濾片數量、實現輕量化，我們會精心設計並製作一系列選擇性紅外濾片，精準擷取大氣關鍵多光譜資訊。此外，我們也會優化其他關鍵環節：挑選低功耗高效能感測器、體積小巧的處理器與資料擷取板卡，在運算效能與用電效率之間取得最佳平衡。 SMiT 憑藉低成本、高整合度的特性，可協助建構城市等級的大氣探測網路，為搭建地面二維網格觀測陣列提供全新技術平臺，藉此重建高解析度的三維大氣資訊。透過對整座城市開展即時、連續的微氣候監測，不僅能顯著提升天氣預報與氣候監測的準確度，還可協助全球天氣數值模式完成初始場設定，同時深化人類對於地球能量循環與水文循環機制的科學認知。

17210926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17210926.value: 面向快速多材料製造的液體約束槽式光固化工藝

17210926.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17210926.value: Prof Fang, Nicholas Xuanlai Prof Xi, Ning

17210926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17210926.value: Multi-material additive manufacturing (MMAM) refers to 3D printing processes that integrate multiple materials to produce a single object. As a key branch of additive manufacturing (AM), MMAM is revolutionizing the traditional manufacturing paradigm featured by single-material processing and assembly by enabling 3D structures with heterogeneous properties, such as elasticity and conductivity. This capability drives the development of smart products with superior performance in healthcare, electronics, and robotics. However, current MMAM techniques, especially multi-material vat photopolymerization (MM-VPP), face significant challenges in achieving high-throughput production. A major bottleneck lies in the time-consuming cleaning process required to remove un-crosslinked material residue and prevent cross-contamination during material switches. This step, which typically takes several minutes, is unavoidable for layers containing multiple materials and significantly hampers efficiency, given that the actual curing time per layer is only a few seconds. The challenge becomes even more pronounced with frequent material changes across hundreds of layers, a common scenario for larger or more complex parts. Addressing this issue is crucial for advancing MMAM's applications in academia and industry, unlocking new opportunities for innovation and commercialization. Inspired by traditional floating lacquer craftsmanship, we propose a novel High-throughput Liquid-constrained MM-VPP process (HLM-VPP) to achieve unprecedented multi-material (MM) printing speed with exceptional printability, fidelity, and robustness. Unlike conventional methods that accelerate material switching, our key idea is to minimize material switches by employing immiscible fluorinated oil as a constrained surface. Specifically, by synchronizing the build platform's immersion movement with dynamic fluid control, the vertical printing process is decoupled from horizontal material switching. This innovation reduces material switches by orders of magnitude, enabling high-resolution sectional-continuous printing—a breakthrough previously unattainable. To realize this approach, we will: 1) quantitatively analyze the thermo-chemo-hydrodynamic behaviors at the curing surface to uncover the mechanism of printability underpinning the proposed HLM-VPP. A machine learning framework will be established to map comprehensive parameters to printability; 2) maximize MM printing throughput by investigating its unique correlation with process parameters, ensuring both speed and printability; and 3) fully harness HLM-VPP through machine vision-assisted closed-loop control to regulate the dynamic process, ensuring consistent fidelity and system robustness. This project will make a major paradigm shift in MMAM through theoretical innovations and practical solutions, representing a key milestone in intelligent manufacturing. It will generate authentic datasets to accelerate machine intelligence development, support Hong Kong's re-industrialization, and deliver bespoke smart products to the public. 多材料增材製造（Multi-material Additive Manufacturing, MMAM）是指在三維打印過程中集成多種材料以製造單一零件的技術。作為增材製造（Additive Manufacturing, AM）的重要分支，MMAM 能夠製備具有彈性和導電性等異質性能的三維結構，從而突破以單一材料加工和裝配為特徵的傳統製造模式，推動醫療健康、電子和機器人等領域高性能智能產品的發展。然而，現有 MMAM 技術，尤其是多材料槽式光固化（Multi-material Vat Photopolymerization, MM-VPP）工藝，在實現高通量生產方面仍面臨顯著挑戰。其核心瓶頸在於材料切換過程中必須進行耗時的清洗，以去除未交聯的材料殘留並避免交叉污染。對於包含多種材料的打印層，這一清洗步驟通常難以避免，且往往需要數分鐘；相比之下，每層的實際固化時間僅為數秒，因此清洗過程嚴重制約了整體打印效率。對於尺寸更大或結構更複雜的零件，數百個打印層之間往往需要頻繁切換材料，使這一問題更加突出。解決該瓶頸對於推動 MMAM 在學術研究和工業應用中的發展至關重要，也將為技術創新和商業化應用開闢新的機遇。受傳統漂漆工藝啟發，我們提出一種新型高通量液體約束多材料槽式光固化（High-throughput Liquid-constrained MM-VPP, HLM-VPP）工藝，旨在實現前所未有的多材料打印速度，同時兼具優異的可打印性、成形精度和工藝魯棒性。不同於傳統方法側重於加快材料切換速度，我們的核心思路是通過採用不互溶的氟化油作為約束界面，最大限度減少材料切換次數。具體而言，通過同步控制構建平台的浸沒運動與動態流體調控，將垂直方向的打印過程與水平方向的材料切換過程解耦。該創新可使材料切換次數降低數個數量級，從而實現此前無法實現的高分辨率連續打印。為實現上述目標，本項目將開展以下研究：1）定量分析固化表面的熱—化學—流體動力學行為，揭示 HLM-VPP 工藝可打印性的內在機制，並建立機器學習框架，構建多維工藝參數與可打印性之間的映射；2）研究多材料打印通量與工藝參數之間的關聯，以最大化打印通量，並在確保打印速度的同時兼顧可打印性；3）借助機器視覺輔助閉環控制，充分發揮 HLM-VPP 工藝優勢，對動態打印過程進行實時調控，以保證穩定的成形精度和系統魯棒性。本項目將通過理論創新與工程實踐方案，推動 MMAM 領域實現重要範式轉變，成為智能製造發展的關鍵里程碑。同時，項目將生成真實可靠的數據集，促進機器智能發展，助力香港再工業化，並為公眾提供定制化智能產品。

17211126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17211126.value: 複雜城市環境中暴雨、城市形態、連通性和洪水之間的相互關聯

17211126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17211126.value: Dr Chen, Xunlai Dr Gao, Yao

17211126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17211126.value: Extreme flooding is a major concern for cities in the Greater Bay Area (GBA), such as Hong Kong, Shenzhen and Guangzhou. Addressing these extreme flood challenges is crucial for the region’s economic and social development, as well as environmental sustainability. Recent notable events include a flood triggered by sequential heavy rains in August 2025, with over 330 mm of rainfall in a single day, and an event caused by a record-breaking rainfall of 158.1 mm/hour in early September 2023. These events exemplify a characteristic rainfall pattern in subtropical climate, known as the “train effect,” caused by mesoscale convective systems. Such convective subsequential rainstorms with successive peaks may result in inundation overlap, thereby flood hazard intensification. The frequency and severity of such subtropical rainfall extremes are likely to increase under climate change. Urban form in megacities presents complex surfaces with varying building layouts, street geometries, and drainage infrastructures, all of which shapes the pathways and processes of an extreme flooding. The complexity of urban environments significantly affects the magnitude and dynamics of flood responses to subtropical rainfall patterns. Additionally, underground drainage connectivity affects the efficiency of floodwater discharge and can contribute to the accumulation of floodwaters in urban surface areas. Therefore, it is essential to disentangle how rainstorm patterns, urban form, flood connectivity and flooding in complex urban settings interact. Improved understanding will support the enhancement of flood resilience and mitigation strategies, particularly in high-density, highly developed cities like Hong Kong. Hence, the proposed project aims to systematically investigate the mechanisms of extreme flooding in complex urban settings by disentangling the interactions among rainstorm feature, urban form, and flood connectivity across urban surface and underground drainage systems. The overarching goal is to explore the multiple mechanisms of extreme flooding generated and developed in complex urban environments, considering the interplay of these key factors. The research tasks will be conducted in various flood-prone urban/suburban areas within Hong Kong, which will be selected rigorously based on proposed methods. Multi-sourced data collection, field monitoring, high-resolution flood modelling and comprehensive numerical experiments will be performed to achieve the goal. 極端暴雨和洪水是粵港澳大灣區城市（如香港、深圳和廣州）面對的重要挑戰。有效應對這些洪水風險，對區域的經濟發展、社會安全及環境可持續性都十分重要。近年，大灣區已出現多次嚴重暴雨事件，例如2025年8月連續強降雨引發的洪水，單日雨量超過330毫米；以及2023年9月初錄得每小時158.1毫米破紀錄雨量的暴雨事件。這類暴雨常見於亞熱帶氣候，其特點是雨帶像列車般一波接一波經過同一地區，形成所謂的「列車效應」。連續多輪強降雨可能令不同時段的積水範圍互相疊加，從而加劇洪水災害。隨着氣候變化，這類極端降雨事件的頻率和強度預計將會上升。 在高密度城市中，城市形態十分複雜，包括不同的建築物佈局、街道形狀、地面高低起伏及排水設施等。這些因素都會影響雨水在城市中的流動路徑、積水位置及洪水發展過程。同時，地下排水系統的連通性亦會影響雨水排走的效率；若排水不暢，便可能導致地面積水加劇。因此，我們有必要深入了解暴雨特徵、城市形態、地面與地下排水連通性，以及城市洪水之間如何相互影響。相關研究成果將有助提升城市防洪能力，並支援制定更有效的洪水風險管理和減災策略，特別是對香港這類高度發展和高密度的城市尤為重要。 本研究項目旨在系統地探討複雜城市環境中極端洪水的形成及發展機制，重點分析暴雨特徵、城市形態，以及地面與地下排水系統連通性之間的相互作用。項目將在香港多個易受洪水影響的市區及近郊地區開展研究，研究地點將根據科學方法嚴謹選定。研究團隊將結合多來源數據收集、現場監測、高分辨率洪水模擬，以及一系列數值實驗，全面分析極端暴雨在複雜城市環境中引發洪水的關鍵因素和過程。研究成果可為香港及其他大灣區城市提升防洪韌性、優化排水規劃和制定氣候適應策略提供科學依據。

17211426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17211426.value: 誰願與公共住房為鄰？評估公共住房對鄰里住房市場的溢出效應

17211426.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17211426.value: Dr Cheung, William K.S. Dr Zheng, Jingwen

17211426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17211426.value: Public housing remains a cornerstone of equitable urban development in cities marked by soaring property prices and widening income divides. In Hong Kong, where half of the population depends on public rental or subsidized ownership schemes, the government’s renewed expansion of Public Rental Housing (PRH) and Home Ownership Scheme (HOS) highlights an urgent policy question: how does public housing affect surrounding neighborhoods? Despite its social mandate, public housing often provokes “not-in-my-backyard” (NIMBY) resistance among nearby private homeowners who fear falling property values and declining neighborhood quality. Yet, public housing can also generate positive externalities through improved infrastructure and amenities. Understanding the conditions under which these effects emerge is crucial for achieving inclusive and sustainable urban development. This project develops a quasi-causal framework to quantify the neighborhood spillovers of public housing, and to investigate their heterogeneity and underlying mechanisms using multi-source urban big data. First, we employ spatial difference-in-differences (DID) design, event study, repeat sales modelling, and quasi-experiment to identify the spillover effects of public housing developments on adjacent private property values. Second, we assess how these spillover effects vary across public housing schemes (e.g., PRH, HOS) and neighborhoods with different socioeconomic profiles (e.g., income levels). By integrating these dimensions, the research will reveal when public housing functions as an amenity that revitalizes local areas and when it is perceived as a disamenity that reinforces spatial segregation. Beyond quantification, the project innovates methodologically by linking urban big data to spatial economics to unravel the physical and social mechanisms behind spillover effects. Two mechanisms will be examined. The amenity mechanism tests whether facilities such as malls and open spaces associated with public housing can enhance positive spillovers, leveraging high-frequency mobile location data to measure visitor catchments and external visitation. The sociodemographic mechanism analyses how public housing alters the income composition and social mix of neighborhoods, drawing on granular census data. Together, these analyses disentangle the physical and social pathways through which public housing shapes urban neighborhoods. The study will fill a major empirical and theoretical gap in housing economics by offering quasi-causal evidence and mechanism-based insights into public housing spillovers. Our findings will inform policymakers in designing people- and place-based housing strategies – optimizing site selection, amenity planning, and community integration. Ultimately, this research advances a policy vision of public housing that enhances both affordability and neighborhood vitality, contributing to the global agenda of sustainable and inclusive cities. 在房價高企且收入差距懸殊的當代城市中，公共住房始終是實現公平城市發展的基石。香港近半數家庭依賴公共租賃住房或資助置業計劃，政府近期重啓公屋和居屋計劃的大規模建設，突顯出一個緊迫的政策問題：公共住房如何影響周邊社區？儘管具有社會公益性，公共住房經常引發鄰近私人業主的「鄰避效應」——他們擔憂房產貶值及社區品質下降。但公共住房亦能透過提升基礎設施及配套設施產生正向外部效應。釐清這些效應產生的條件，對實現包容性及可持續的城市發展至關重要。 本研究建構準因果框架量化公共住房的鄰里溢出效應，並利用多源城市大數據探究其異質性及內在機制。首先，我們使用空間雙重差分、事件研究法、重複銷售模型及準自然實驗，識別公共住房開發對周邊私有房產價值的溢出效應。其次，評估這些溢出效應如何因公共住房類型（如公屋、居屋）及社區社會經濟特徵（如收入水平）產生差異。透過多維度整合，本研究將揭示公共住房何時作為提升區域活力的積極要素，何時又被視為加劇空間分異的負面因素。 在量化溢出效應之外，本研究透過融合城市大數據及空間經濟學，創新性地解析溢出效應的物理環境及社會機制。我們具體探討兩種機制：其一是便利設施機制，透過高頻手機定位數據測量訪客集水區及外部到訪率，檢驗公共住房配套的商場、開放空間等設施能否加强正向溢出；其二是社會人口機制，借助細粒度人口普查數據，分析公共住房如何改變社區收入結構及人口構成。這些分析將共同揭示公共住房塑造城市社區的物理環境及社會路徑。 本研究透過提供公共住房溢出效應的準因果證據及機制解釋，填補住房經濟學領域的重大實證及理論空白。研究成果可為政策制定者設計「以人為本」與「因地制宜」的住房策略提供參考——包括優化選址決策、配套設施規劃及社區融合方案。最終推動實現兼具可負擔性及社區活力的公共住房政策願景，為全球可持續及包容性城市議程作出貢獻。

17211726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17211726.value: 鈦基橡膠金屬之相穩定性與變形行為的原子尺度模擬

17211726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17211726.value: Titanium Gum Metals (GMs) are a remarkable class of body-centered cubic (BCC) alloys with an unusual combination of properties, including high strength, exceptional ductility, low elastic modulus, and excellent corrosion resistance. These characteristics make them promising candidates for diverse applications in aerospace, automotive engineering, and biomedical implants. Despite their promise, the fundamental mechanisms governing their phase stability and mechanical behavior remain insufficiently understood. In particular, predicting which crystal phases are stable/metastable, how they transform under temperature or stress, and how crystal defects such as dislocations and twins control deformation is a major scientific and technological challenge. This knowledge gap limits the design of new titanium alloys with tailored properties. Atomistic modeling is a powerful route to uncover the fundamental mechanisms that dictate alloy behavior. Accurate quantum-mechanical methods are computationally prohibitive for complex multi-component systems, while traditional molecular dynamics simulations are efficient but limited by the accuracy of their interatomic potentials. Recent advances in foundation atomic models (FAMs), artificial intelligence-based models trained on large-scale quantum-mechanical datasets, offer a transformative opportunity.
