Finally, we will develop precise dynamic prediction methods for future disease progression, leveraging individuals' evolving clinical histories and imaging profiles. The proposed methodologies will be applied to the ADNI study to tackle key scientific questions about transition-specific biomarkers and latent subgroups. 阿茲海默症（Alzheimer’s disease, AD）是一種進行性腦部疾病，影響全球數以百萬計的人口。及早且準確地預測 AD 風險，對於及時介入及制定有效的照護方案至關重要。近年來，腦部影像技術，尤其是磁力共振成像（magnetic resonance imaging, MRI）的快速發展，使研究人員得以偵測與 AD 相關的細微腦部變化，為理解及預測疾病進程帶來新的契機。 儘管目前已發展出多種以影像資料為基礎的預測工具，現有方法仍存在重要限制。這些方法普遍假設 AD 的確切發病時間已知，或僅處理右設限資料。然而，AD 在早期通常沒有明顯症狀，其發病時間只能透過定期臨床評估加以判定，因此在真實世界研究中往往形成區間設限資料。此外，過往研究主要聚焦於由輕度認知障礙（mild cognitive impairment, MCI）進展至 AD 的轉變，因而排除了相當大比例仍處於認知正常（cognitively normal, CN）狀態的個體。此一狹窄的研究視角限制了對初始認知衰退的預測能力，也忽略了疾病完整進程中潛在的生物學與臨床異質性。 本計畫旨在填補上述研究缺口，透過結合影像及臨床資料，發展創新的統計方法，以預測 AD 由 CN 進展至 MCI，再由 MCI 進展至 AD 的完整疾病軌跡。受阿茲海默症神經影像倡議（Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, ADNI）研究所啟發，本計畫將在間歇性觀察的情境下，將 AD 的疾病進程建模為多狀態過程，即區間設限多狀態資料。我們亦將探索 ADNI 參與者中可能存在的潛在次群體，並建立群體特異性的預測模型。相較於現有方法，本計畫所提出的方法將能為所有受試者提供更具資訊性、個人化且準確的預測，而不受其目前所處疾病狀態的限制。這些方法學進展將有助於更早識別 AD 風險，並促進更及時且個人化的介入措施。 在方法學方面，本計畫將針對區間設限多狀態資料發展半參數函數型模型，並將影像資料納入為函數型協變量。我們將提出具嚴謹理論基礎的新型估計與假設檢定方法。此外，本計畫將發展適用於縱向影像資料與區間設限多狀態資料的函數型聯合混合模型，以處理潛在次群體歸屬可能缺失的情況。為克服相關計算挑戰，我們將探索高效率的頻率學派估計方法，而非採用傳統的貝葉斯方法。最後，本計畫將充分利用個體隨時間演變的臨床病史及影像特徵，發展精確預測未來疾病進程的動態預測方法。所提出的方法將應用於 ADNI 研究，以探討與不同疾病轉移階段相關的生物標誌物及潛在次群體等重要科學問題。

17308926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17308926.value: 二維共軛框架基電催化劑的可控合成及其高效CO₂電還原製甲醇

17308926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17308926.value: CO₂ electrolysis offers a promising route for producing clean methanol fuels and can be integrated with renewable power systems for energy storage and conversion. However, the co-electrolysis of CO₂ and H₂O—using protons from water as the hydrogen source—at ambient temperature to methanol still suffers from high energy consumption, low single-pass conversion, and poor selectivity. There is an urgent need to deepen the atomic-scale understanding of methanol formation pathways, the structure of catalyst surfaces/interfaces, and the influence of external fields on electrolyzer efficiency, in order to guide the development of high-performance CO₂-to-methanol electrolysis systems. To address these challenges, this project (named as CFuel) aims to develop conductive two-dimensional conjugated framework materials (2D c-FMs) with tunable molecular units and well-defined interfaces, including 2D conjugated metal-organic frameworks (2D c-MOFs) and covalent organic frameworks (2D c-COFs). The research will systematically integrate three aspects: rational design and precise construction of electrocatalysts, mechanistic understanding and optimization of interfacial reaction kinetics, and development of an efficient co-electrolyzer prototype. Major research objectives of this CFuel project include: 1) Synthesizing conductive 2D c-FMs with tailored interface composition, electronic structure, porosity, and redox activity, focusing on the cascade/synergistic effects of spatially isolated mono-/bimetallic sites in modulating CO₂ reduction pathways toward highly selective and stable methanol production. 2) Developing external field-assisted kinetic optimization strategies, combining electrochemical analysis and machine learning, to investigate the dynamic response of the catalytic system to temperature, pressure, proton concentration, and electric field, thereby revealing the dynamic evolution of catalyst surface/interface structures and key reaction intermediates, and clarifying structure–activity relationships and underlying mechanisms. 3) Designing a high-performance co-electrolyzer with optimized triple-phase boundaries to enhance mass and energy transport, enabling stable operation at industrial-scale current densities. As a consequence, this CFuel project will develop at least six types of 2D c-FMs with precisely controlled interfacial structures. The final co-electrolyzer is expected to achieve Faraday efficiency (FE) >70%, current density >150 mA/cm², CO₂ single-pass conversion >30%, and stable operation for over 300 hours with selectivity maintained above 50%. 二氧化碳電催化還原是製備清潔甲醇燃料的重要途徑，亦可與可再生能源系統耦合，用於能源儲存與轉化。然而，常溫下以水為氫源的CO₂/H₂O共電解製甲醇過程，仍面臨能耗高、單程轉化率低及選擇性差等瓶頸。亟待從原子尺度深化對甲醇生成路徑、催化劑表面/界面結構及外場因素對電解器性能影響機制的認識，以指導高性能CO₂製甲醇電解系統的理性設計。針對上述挑戰，本項目（簡稱CFuel）旨在開發具有可調分子基元和精準界面結構的二維共軛框架材料（2D c-FMs），涵蓋二維共軛金屬有機框架（2D c-MOFs）與共價有機框架（2D c-COFs）。研究內容將圍繞以下三個方面系統開展：電催化劑的理性設計與精準構築、界面反應動力學的機理解析與優化、高效共電解原型器件的開發。CFuel項目的主要研究目標包括：（1）合成界面組成、電子結構、孔隙率及氧化還原活性可調的導電2D c-FMs，並探究空間隔離的單/雙金屬活性位點在調控CO₂還原路徑以實現高選擇性、高穩定性甲醇生成過程中的級聯/協同效應；（2）發展外場輔助的動力學優化策略，結合電化學分析與機器學習，系統考察催化體系對溫度、壓力、質子濃度及電場等參數的動態響應，進而揭示催化劑表面/界面結構及關鍵反應中間體的動態演化規律，闡明構效關係與微觀機制；（3）設計三相界面優化的高性能共電解器，強化傳質與能量傳輸，實現在工業級電流密度下的長期穩定運行。最終，CFuel項目將開發出至少六種界面結構精確可控的2D c-FMs電催化劑。預期所製電催化劑可實現法拉第效率（FE）>70%、電流密度>150 mA/cm²，並能在300小時以上穩定運行，選擇性保持在50%以上。

17309126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17309126.value: 利用噬菌体展示技术发现针对病理靶蛋白的支架式微蛋白结合剂

17309126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17309126.value: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) play important role in biological processes under both health and disease conditions. Disease relevant PPIs emerge as appealing targets for drug discovery. Development of PPIs inhibitors are challenging task due to the broad and flat interaction interfaces and lack of well-defined binding pockets. Current on-market PPIs inhibitors are mainly monoclonal antibodies, which suffer from high production cost and requirement of injection. In recent years, miniproteins with molecular size ranging from 3 kDa to 10 kDa start to attract scientists' attention as a new type of molecules with therapeutic potential. In this project, we plan to develop novel scaffolded miniproteins as PPIs inhibitors via phage display. New template structures derived from cyclic peptides will be employed to generate phage displayed miniprotein libraries with conformationally rigid cage-like structures. The libraries will be applied to the discovery of inhibitors for PD-1/PD-L1 interaction, which is the leading target for cancer immunotherapy. 蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用在健康和疾病状态下的生物过程中均发挥重要作用，并已成为极具吸引力的药物研发靶点。由于该类相互作用界面广泛且平坦，缺乏明确的结合口袋，因此开发针对该类作用的抑制剂极具挑战性。目前市售的蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用抑制剂以单克隆抗体为主，生产成本高昂且需要注射给药。近年来，分子量在三千至一万道尔顿的微蛋白作为一种具有治疗潜力的新型分子，逐渐引起学界关注。本项目计划利用噬菌体展示技术开发新型支架化微蛋白作为蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用抑制剂。我们将采用源自环肽的新型模板结构，构建具有刚性构象笼状结构的噬菌体展示微蛋白库。这些蛋白库将用于作为当前癌症免疫治疗的主要靶点之一的PD-1/PD-L1相互作用的抑制剂发现。

17309326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17309326.value: 構造超壓是否致使垂直構造環境中得以發生地殼循環？

17309326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17309326.value: Understanding how Earth's earliest crust recycled and evolved is central to explaining the planet's long-term habitability. Today, the cycling of water, carbon, and rocks is primarily driven by plate tectonics, where surface materials are buried into the mantle via subduction and re-emerge through volcanism. In contrast, geologic evidence from the Earth's first billion years suggests an "vertical tectonic Earth", where subduction was absent, and crustal recycling was accomplished by gravity-driven processes such as the peeling away of the deep crust (delamination) or the sinking of dense rock drips through lighter crustal layers (crustal dripping or sagduction). The viability of crustal recycling through vertical tectonics, however, has been recently challenged by laboratory experiments and numerical simulations, which suggest that the rocks of early Earth may not have been dense or strong enough to sink under their own weight. Our proposal aims to resolve this dilemma by introducing a new factor into models of vertical tectonics: the non-lithostatic pressure. Non-lithostatic pressure occurs in active deformation zones to balance stresses from various tectonic-related forces. Modeling and geologic evidence both indicate that tectonic "overpressure" (i.e., pressure exceeding lithostatic pressure) can reach hundreds of megapascals and even approach gigapascal levels, thereby facilitating the formation and sinking of dense, garnet-rich high-pressure rocks, making vertical tectonics a viable engine of crustal recycling. To test this, we will integrate field and laboratory studies with geophysical modeling. We will utilize rocks from the East Pilbara Terrane of Western Australia, a place interpreted to have formed by vertical tectonics, to provide key constraints on composition, deformation conditions, strength, and paleostress. Using microscopy, electron backscatter diffraction, and high-temperature-high-pressure experiments, we will quantify paleostress conditions and rock strengths. Thermodynamic modeling coupled with geophysical modeling will predict the extent of non-lithostatic pressure and how the rocks would have behaved in vertical tectonics, and whether tectonic overpressure could have been necessary for crustal recycling. This research has broad implications. If vertical tectonics aided by overpressure could have operated effectively and driven crustal recycling on the early Earth, it would reshape our understanding of how the first continents formed, how volatiles such as water and carbon were cycled, and how habitable environments emerged. Conversely, if overpressure proves insufficient or irrelevant, the results would strengthen the case for an earlier onset of plate tectonics. Either outcome will significantly advance our knowledge of the forces that shaped the young Earth and set the stage for life. 理解地球最初的地殼如何循環與演化，是解釋這顆行星長期宜居性的核心關鍵。現今，水、碳與岩石的循環主要由板塊構造驅動，地表物質透過俯衝作用被埋入地幔，再經由火山活動重新出露地表。相對地，來自地球最初十億年的地質證據則暗示著一個「垂直構造地球」，當時俯衝作用尚未發生，地殼循環是透過重力驅動的過程來完成，例如深部地殼的剝離（拆沉作用），或是緻密岩塊穿越較輕地殼層向下沉陷（地殼滴落或重力凹沉作用）。然而，這種透過垂直構造進行地殼循環的可行性最近受到了實驗室實驗與數值模擬的挑戰；這些研究指出，早期地球的岩石可能既不夠緻密，也不夠堅固，無法憑藉自身重量下沉。 我們的研究提案旨在解決此一困境，方法是在垂直構造模型中引入一個新的因子：非靜岩壓力。非靜岩壓力通常出現於活躍變形帶中，用以平衡來自各種構造相關作用力的應力。模擬與地質證據皆顯示，構造「超壓」（即超過靜岩壓力的壓力）可達數百兆帕，甚至接近十億帕等級，從而有助於形成並下沉富含石榴石的高壓緻密岩石，使垂直構造得以成為地殼循環的可行引擎。 為驗證此一假說，我們將結合野外及實驗室研究與地球物理模擬。我們將利用來自西澳東皮爾巴拉克拉通（East Pilbara Terrane）的岩石——該地區被解釋為由垂直構造所形成——以提供關於成分、變形條件、強度與古應力的關鍵約束。透過顯微分析、電子背向散射繞射以及高溫高壓實驗，我們將量化古應力條件與岩石強度。熱力學模擬搭配地球物理模擬，則將預測非靜岩壓力的範圍、岩石在垂直構造中可能的行為，以及構造超壓是否為在非板塊構造體系下地殼循環的必要條件。 這項研究具有廣泛的意涵。若在超壓輔助下的垂直構造能有效運作，並驅動早期地球的地殼循環，將重塑我們對最初大陸如何形成、水與碳等揮發性物質如何循環，以及宜居環境如何湧現的理解。反之，若超壓被證明不足或不具關鍵作用，其結果將強化板塊構造更早啟動的論點。無論何種結果，都將大幅推進我們對於塑造年輕地球、並為生命奠下基礎的各種作用力的認識。

17309426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17309426.value: 火星地殼磁場（CMF）周圍的等離子體波動及其對離子逃逸的影響

17309426.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17309426.value: Dr Chai, Lihui Prof Zhang, Binzheng

17309426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17309426.value: Mars is a cold and dry planet with a tenuous atmosphere, yet much geology evidence suggests that its climate was once much warmer and wetter. The ion escape caused by Mars-solar wind interaction is thought to have played an important role in Mars’ climate evolution. Mars does not have a global magnetic field now, but have strong crustal magnetic fields (CMF), mostly concentrated in the southern hemisphere. These CMF can interact with the solar wind and ionosphere, potentially generating a variety of plasma waves. These waves are capable of transferring energy to ions through wave-particle interactions, which may enhance ion acceleration and contribute to atmospheric escape. Our previous case studies have shown that plasma waves are related to CMF, and the enhancement of planetary ions with escape coincides with plasma waves. However, the global statistical properties of CMF-related waves and their direct contribution to ion escape remain poorly constrained. The pathway from crustal field to plasma waves, ion energization and ultimately ion escape has not been systematically characterized. Thus, a comprehensive statistical and mechanism understanding of the CMF effect on ion escape through wave-particle interaction is still lacking. This project combines MAVEN/Tianwen-1 observations and test particle simulations to address the following goals: (1) characterize the global properties (spatial-temporal distribution, polarization) of CMF-related plasma waves (proton cyclotron waves, magnetosonic waves, and ULF waves); (2) quantify wave-particle interactions (WPI) driven ion escape by correlating plasma waves with H⁺/O⁺/O₂⁺/CO₂⁺ flux enhancements; (3) evaluate the effects of solar wind activities (e.g. ICME events) on CMF-wave-escape chain. Observations will use magnetic field and particle data to build a statistical wave database, and simulations will track ion trajectories to quantify WPI efficiency. The scientific results will be critical for understanding wave-driven ion escape in CMF-formed magnetospheres. 火星是一顆寒冷乾燥、大氣稀薄的行星，然而大量地質證據表明其氣候曾經更為溫暖濕潤。火星與太陽風相互作用所引起的離子逃逸，被認為在火星氣候演化過程中發揮了重要作用。火星目前沒有全球性磁場，但擁有較強的地殼磁場（CMF），且主要集中在南半球。這些地殼磁場可與太陽風及電離層相互作用，可能激發多種等離子體波動。這些波動能夠通過波粒相互作用將能量傳遞給離子，從而可能增強離子加速並促進大氣逃逸。 我們此前的個例研究表明，等離子體波動與地殼磁場相關，且逃逸行星離子的增強與等離子體波動同時出現。然而，與地殼磁場相關的波動的全球統計特性及其對離子逃逸的直接貢獻仍缺乏有效約束。從地殼磁場到等離子體波動、離子加熱加速並最終導致離子逃逸的完整鏈條尚未得到系統性的刻畫。因此，目前仍缺乏對地殼磁場通過波粒相互作用影響離子逃逸的全面統計和機制性理解。 本項目將結合MAVEN／天問一號的觀測數據與試驗粒子模擬，實現以下目標：（1）刻畫與地殼磁場相關的等離子體波動（質子迴旋波、磁聲波及超低頻波）的全球特性（時空分佈、偏振特性）；（2）通過將等離子體波動與H⁺／O⁺／O₂⁺／CO₂⁺通量增強進行關聯分析，定量研究由波粒相互作用（WPI）驅動的離子逃逸；（3）評估太陽風活動（如行星際日冕物質拋射（ICME）事件）對“地殼磁場—波動—逃逸” 鏈條的影響。觀測方面將利用磁場和粒子數據建立波動統計數據庫，模擬方面將追蹤離子軌跡以定量評估波粒相互作用的效率。相關科學成果對於理解地殼磁場所形成的微型磁層中由波動驅動的離子逃逸具有重要意義。

17309926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17309926.value: 風暴誘發的地下空間內地下水與空氣中氡氣的激增

17309926.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17309926.value: Dr Luo, Xin Dr Mao, Rong

17309926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17309926.value: Radon-222 is a naturally occurring radioactive gas generated from uranium decay in soil and bedrock. Though invisible and odorless, prolonged exposure to elevated radon levels is the second leading cause of lung cancer after smoking. In densely populated Hong Kong—where land scarcity drives extensive use of underground spaces such as tunnels, metro lines, and utility caverns—understanding radon behavior in these enclosed environments is a growing public health priority. Preliminary monitoring at the Poshan drainage tunnel system has revealed dramatic, short-lived spikes in both groundwater and tunnel-air radon during typhoons: groundwater concentrations can surge up to eightfold, while airborne levels jump by 60–80% within hours of intense rainfall. These anomalies coincide with rapid changes in rainfall intensity, hydraulic pressure, and groundwater flow—conditions typical of Hong Kong’s frequent tropical cyclones. This project will uncover the hydrogeological and geochemical mechanisms driving these storm-induced radon surges through six high-resolution field campaigns timed with typhoon landfalls. By continuously monitoring radon in soil gas, groundwater, and tunnel air alongside hydrometeorological variables—and applying concentration–discharge (C–Q) analysis and coupled vadose zone–groundwater–tunnel modeling—we will test the hypothesis that heavy rainfall rapidly saturates fractures in weathered bedrock, expanding the water–rock interface and enhancing radon release via alpha-recoil from radium-bearing minerals. The resulting insights will advance fundamental understanding of how extreme weather modulates subsurface gas transport in fractured-rock systems and directly inform engineering solutions—such as adaptive ventilation, pressure control, and real-time radon alarms. While focused on Hong Kong, this research provides a globally applicable framework for managing radon risk in underground infrastructure located in storm-prone regions with crystalline or uranium-enriched bedrock. By bridging geoscience, public health, and resilient urban design, the project addresses an overlooked but significant hazard at the intersection of climate extremes and subterranean urbanization. 氡-222（Radon-222）是一種天然存在的放射性氣體，由土壤和基岩中的鈾衰變所產生。儘管它無色無味，但長期暴露於高濃度的氡氣環境中，是僅次於吸菸的第二大肺癌成因。在人口稠密的香港，由於土地稀缺，促使人們廣泛使用隧道、地鐵線路和公用設施地下空間等；因此，了解這些封閉環境中的氡氣行為，已成為日益重要的公共衛生首要任務。對寶珊（Po Shan）排水隧道系統的初步監測顯示，在颱風期間，地下水和隧道空氣中的氡氣都會出現劇烈且短暫的激增：地下水中的氡濃度可飆升至高達八倍，而空氣中的氡濃度在強降雨後的數小時內會猛增 60% 至 80%。這些異常現象與降雨強度、水壓和地下水流的快速變化同時發生——這正是香港頻繁出現的熱帶氣旋的典型特徵。 本專案將透過配合颱風登陸時段進行的六次高解析度野外調查，揭示推動這些風暴誘發氡氣激增的水文地質學與地球化學機制。藉由持續監測土壤氣體、地下水和隧道空氣中的氡氣以及水文氣象變數，並應用濃度-流量（C-Q）分析與非飽和帶-地下水-隧道耦合模型，我們將驗證一項假設：強降雨會迅速使風化基岩中的裂隙達到飽和，從而擴大水岩介面，並透過含鐳礦物的阿爾法反衝（alpha-recoil）作用增強氡氣的釋放。由此獲得的見解將促進我們對極端氣候如何調節裂隙岩石系統中地下氣體傳輸的基礎了解，並直接為工程解決方案（如自適應通風、壓力控制和即時氡氣警報）提供參考。儘管本研究聚焦於香港，但它為管理位於易受風暴侵襲且具有結晶岩或富鈾基岩地區的地下基礎設施中的氡氣風險，提供了一個全球適用的框架。透過連結地球科學、公共衛生與具備韌性的城市設計，本專案解決了一個在極端氣候與地下城市化交會處被忽視卻又極具重大意義的危害。

17310026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17310026.value: 系外巨行星的動力學與起源

17310026.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17310026.value: Dr Reffert, Sabine Dr Trifonov, Trifon Prof Wong, Louis Ngai Yuen

17310026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17310026.value: Extrasolar planet searches have discovered many Jupiter-mass giant planets. We propose to investigate several problems related to the dynamics and origins of Jupiter-mass planets in mean-motion resonances in multi-planet systems, in binary star systems, and around low-mass stars. (1) We will analyze the radial velocity and astrometric data of the 4-planet system around the low-mass star GJ 876 to determine whether the 4:2:1 Laplace resonance of the outer three planets in this system is chaotic or regular and to constrain the inclinations of the planetary orbits. The properties of the Laplace resonance will be used to place constraints on the amount of turbulence in the protoplanetary disk. (2) We will analyze high-resolution adaptive optics image of the star HD 59686 to determine whether its binary companion is a low-mass main-sequence star. We will also analyze new radial velocity measurements to determine whether the giant planet orbiting the primary star is on a prograde or retrograde orbit. The orbital properties of the planet will allow us to constrain the origin of the planet, including the possibility that it was captured from a circumbinary orbit or that it was captured into apsidal alignment with the binary by interactions with the protoplanetary disk. (3) Jupiter-mass planets are rare around low-mass stars. We will perform numerical simulations to investigate the conditions under which Jupiter-mass planets could form around low-mass stars via pebble accretion. (4) We will investigate observed multi-planet systems with Jupiter-mass planets to determine the fraction of planet pairs that are in first-order mean-motion resonances, the fraction that are near but outside such resonances, and the fraction that are far from resonances. The dynamical properties of the pairs in and near resonances will be used to constrain the migration of giant planets during formation and the processes that subsequently drive planet pairs away from resonances. Our investigation will lead to a better understanding of the role played by planet-disk interactions (in particular, disk-induced migration) in shaping the architecture of planetary systems containing giant planets. 系外行星的搜尋已經發現了許多木星質量的巨行星。我們提議研究幾個與木星質量行星的動力學和起源相關的課題，包括處於共振軌道、雙星系統中以及圍繞低質量恆星運行的木星質量行星。(1) 我們將分析圍繞低質量恆星 GJ 876 運行的四行星系統的徑向速度和天體測量數據，以確定該系統外側三顆行星的 4:2:1 拉普拉斯共振是混沌的還是規則的，並約束行星軌道的傾角。我們會利用拉普拉斯共振的性質來約束原行星盤的湍流強度。（2）我們將分析恆星 HD 59686 的高解析度自適應光學影像，以確定其雙星伴星是否為低質量主序星。我們還將分析新的徑向速度數據，以確定圍繞主星運行的巨行星的軌道是順行還是逆行。我們會利用行星的軌道特性來約束其起源，包括它是否可能從圍繞雙星的軌道被捕獲，或者是由於與原行星盤的相互作用而被捕獲到現有軌道。（3）圍繞低質量恆星運行的木星質量行星較為罕見。我們將進行電腦模擬，研究木星質量的行星需要哪些條件才能在低質量恆星周圍透過卵石吸積形成。(4) 我們將研究已觀測到的含有木星質量行星的多行星系統，以確定處於一階共振軌道、接近但不處於共振狀態以及遠離共振狀態的行星對的比例。我們會利用處於共振狀態和接近共振狀態的行星對的動力學特性，來約束巨行星在形成過程中的遷移，以及隨後導致行星對遠離共振狀態的過程。我們的研究將有助於更好地理解行星-原行星盤相互作用（特別是原行星盤引起的遷移）在塑造含有巨行星的行星系統的結構所扮演的角色。

17310226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17310226.value: 綠脫石-微生物相互作用的短波紅外光譜識別指標及其在火星探測中的應用

17310226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17310226.value: The search for life on Mars represents a primary objective in planetary exploration and necessitates the identification of robust biosignatures. Given that microbial life likely represents the most plausible form of life that may have existed on Mars, microbe-modified minerals, defined as those chemically and structurally altered by microbial metabolism, offer a durable and detectable record. Microbial reduction of structural Fe3+, a process that yields energy and may represent one of Earth’s earliest metabolic strategies, can be preserved in such mineralogical signatures. Clay minerals are particularly susceptible to microbial alteration, with nontronite (an Fe3+-rich smectite) serving as a representative example. Notably, nontronite is also one of the most widely distributed hydrous minerals on Mars, making it an ideal target for investigating potential mineral-microbe interactions on the planet. Detecting specific mineral modifications associated with microbial activity could thus provide compelling evidence for past Martian life. Short-wave infrared (SWIR; 1.0-2.5 μm) spectroscopy, the primary mineralogical method employed by Martian orbiters and rovers, exhibits high sensitivity not only to hydrous mineral types but also to their crystal chemistry and structure. Building upon the distinctive mineralogical evolution pathway of microbially modified nontronite and its SWIR spectral expression, this project aims to develop a SWIR spectral proxy capable of identifying microbe-altered nontronite in both orbital remote-sensing and rover datasets. To achieve this objective, we will (1) conduct laboratory experiments to synthesize microbe-modified nontronite across a wide range of reaction degrees; (2) delineate the mineralogical evolution pathway induced by microbial activity; (3) characterize SWIR spectral responses to microbial alteration and establish a diagnostic spectral proxy for distinguishing biotically altered nontronite from its abiotic counterparts; and (4) apply this proxy to rover and orbital hyperspectral data to search for potential microbe-modified nontronite on Mars. The development and application of these spectral and mineralogical biosignatures will assist in landing-site selection for China's Tianwen-3 Mars sample-return mission, guide ongoing and future rover investigations (e.g., NASA's Perseverance and ESA's Rosalind Franklin rovers), and support future analyses of returned Martian samples—collectively advancing efforts to determine whether life ever existed on Mars. 生命遺跡探尋探測是火星探測的核心目標之一，且亟需建立穩健可靠的生命標誌物。鑒於微生物是火星上最有可能存在過的生命形式之一，經微生物改造的礦物，即在微生物代謝過程中在化學和結構上發生改變的礦物，是一種火星上潛在且可探測的生命記錄。礦物晶體中 Fe3+ 的微生物還原過程可產生能量，這是地球上最早的生物代謝形式之一，且這個過程可以被保存在礦物的晶體特徵中。黏土礦物對微生物改造尤為敏感，其中綠脫石（一種富含 Fe3+ 的蒙脫石族礦物）是一個具有代表性的例子。值得注意的是，綠脫石也是火星上分佈最廣的含水礦物之一，這使其成為研究該行星上潛在礦物-微生物相互作用的理想目標。因此，與微生物活動相關的特定礦物改造，可為火星過去的生命提供可靠的證據。短波紅外（1.0–2.5 μm）光譜學是火星軌道器和著陸巡視器所採用之主要的礦物學方法，它不僅對含水礦物類型表現出高靈敏度，對其晶體化學和結構也同樣如此。基於微生物改造綠脫石獨特的礦物學演化路徑及其 短波紅外光譜表征，本項目旨在開發一種 短波紅外光譜學指標，能夠從軌道器遙感和巡視器數據集中識別出經微生物改造的綠脫石。為實現這一目標，我們將：(1) 開展室內實驗，合成不同反應程度的微生物改造綠脫石；(2) 刻畫出由微生物活動誘導的礦物學演化路徑；(3) 表征對微生物改造的 短波紅外光譜響應，並建立用於區分生物改造與非生物改造綠脫石的診斷性光譜指標；以及 (4) 將該指標應用於巡視器和軌道器高光譜數據，以搜尋火星上潛在的微生物改造綠脫石。這些光譜與礦物學生物標誌物的開發和應用，將有助於中國天問三號火星採樣返回任務的著陸區選址，指導當前及未來的巡視器探測（例如美國太空總署的「毅力號」與歐洲太空總署的「羅莎琳德·富蘭克林號」巡視器），並支持未來對返回火星樣品的分析——共同推進旨在確定火星上是否曾存在過生命的工作。

17310826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17310826.value: 关于非交换组合的两个问题

17310826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17310826.value: We consider two problems in non-commutative combinatorics. The first one concerns Zaremba’s conjecture, which is phrased in number theory but has significant implication in numerical integration. Zaremba’s conjecture says that every natural number q is a denominator of a reduced fraction r/q whose continued fraction expansion has all partial quotients bounded by an absolute constant A. We aim to prove a weaker version of Zaremba’s conjecture, by allowing A to mildly depend on q (specifically, we require A ≪ log(q)/loglog(q)), which will strengthen a recent work by Moshchevitin-Murphy-Schkredov. A key ingredient is to prove a product theorem over SL_2(Z/qZ) for an arbitrary integer q. The second problem is a two dimensional analogue of Waring’s problem. Let Γ be a finitely generated Zariski dense subgroup of SL_2(Z) and v ∈ Z^2 a primitive vector. Can we generate the whole lattice Z^2, or a large subgroup, by performing only finitely many summation of the set Γ.v by itself? 17310926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17310926.value: 利用量子资源推动哈密顿量模拟鲁棒性

17310926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17310926.value: Quantum computation has demonstrated potential advantages in specific tasks, with Hamiltonian simulation standing out as a leading candidate for practical quantum applications. It promises to unlock quantum dynamical phenomena beyond the reach of classical computers, with broad implications for materials science, quantum chemistry, and fundamental physics. However, progress has been hindered by the pervasive presence of errors—from algorithmic approximations in digital simulation to hardware imperfections in analog platforms. A fundamental question remains poorly understood: how do intrinsic quantum resources such as entanglement and magic shape the performance and robustness of quantum simulation? Conventionally viewed as necessary for quantum advantage yet costly to maintain, these resources have been analyzed exclusively through pessimistic, state-independent error bounds. Counterintuitively, the PI's recent work revealed that entanglement can suppress Trotterization errors in digital simulation, tightening worst-case bounds toward average-case performance and reducing quantum implementation overhead. However, this promising discovery remains confined to a narrow context: it applies primarily to digital Trotterization involving pure state evolution in the Schrödinger picture. Critical gaps persist regarding its applicability to the more general and physically relevant Heisenberg picture, its robustness in noisy analog quantum simulators, and its interplay with other non-stabilizer resources such as magic. Without a systematic understanding of how to leverage these resources across different simulation paradigms, we cannot realize their full potential for practical, robust simulation. This project aims to bridge this gap by developing a comprehensive set of principles and strategies to harness quantum resources for enhanced Hamiltonian simulation. We will systematically transcend current limitations across three frontiers: 1. Entanglement-Driven Enhancement in Simulating Operators: Generalizing our findings to the Heisenberg picture, where we will develop theory and methods to leverage operator entanglement for efficient and accurate observable simulation. 2. Entanglement-Enhanced Robustness in Quantum Dynamics: Building a theoretical foundation demonstrating how entanglement can be harnessed to improve the robustness of analog quantum simulation and control under realistic noise conditions. 3. Taming the Statistical Behavior of Hamiltonian Simulation by Quantum Resources: Quantifying how magic and entanglement reshape the statistical distribution of simulation errors-suppressing tail events and reducing variance for more predictable performance. By integrating theoretical advances with numerical validation, this research will provide a predictive framework for exploiting quantum resources to enhance simulation accuracy and robustness. Our results are expected to directly benefit Hamiltonian simulation efforts in chemistry and materials science, offering new strategies for future experimental realization. 量子计算已在特定任务中展现出潜在优势，其中哈密顿量模拟是最有希望实现实际量子应用的方向之一。它有望揭示经典计算机难以触及的量子动力学现象，并对材料科学、量子化学和基础物理产生广泛影响。然而，该领域的发展一直受到各种误差的阻碍——从数字模拟中的算法近似误差，到模拟量子平台中的硬件缺陷，误差无处不在。一个根本性问题仍未得到充分理解：纠缠和魔性等内禀量子资源如何影响量子模拟的性能与鲁棒性？ 传统观点认为，这些量子资源是实现量子优势所必需的，但同时也难以维持、代价高昂。以往对这些资源的分析几乎完全依赖于悲观的、与具体量子态无关的误差界。与直觉相反，我们近期的研究发现，纠缠可以抑制数字模拟中的 Trotter 化误差，使最坏情形误差界更接近平均情形性能，并降低量子实现的开销。然而，这一有前景的发现目前仍局限于较窄的情境：它主要适用于薛定谔绘景下纯态演化的数字 Trotter 化模拟。关于其是否适用于更一般且具有物理相关性的海森堡绘景、在含噪模拟量子模拟器中的鲁棒性，以及它与魔性等其他非稳定子资源之间的相互作用，仍存在关键空白。如果不能系统理解如何在不同模拟范式中利用这些资源，我们就无法充分发挥它们在实用、鲁棒量子模拟中的潜力。 本项目旨在弥合这一差距，通过发展一套全面的原理和策略，利用量子资源来增强哈密顿量模拟。我们将从以下三个前沿方向系统性突破当前局限： 1. 算符模拟中的纠缠驱动增强：将我们已有发现推广到海森堡绘景，发展相关理论与方法，利用算符纠缠实现高效且精确的可观测量模拟。 2. 量子动力学中的纠缠增强鲁棒性：建立理论基础，阐明在现实噪声条件下，如何利用纠缠提高模拟量子模拟与量子控制的鲁棒性。 3. 利用量子资源调控哈密顿量模拟的统计行为：量化魔性和纠缠如何重塑模拟误差的统计分布——抑制尾部事件并降低方差，从而实现更可预测的性能。 通过结合理论进展与数值验证，本研究将提供一个预测性框架，用于利用量子资源提升模拟精度与鲁棒性。我们的研究结果有望直接促进化学和材料科学中的哈密顿量模拟工作，并为未来实验实现提供新的策略。

17311326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17311326.value: 利用ATLAS Run 3 數據集搜索輕帶電希格斯玻色子

17311326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17311326.value: This proposal describes a comprehensive analysis building upon the ATLAS Run 2 search for light charged Higgs bosons (H±) produced in top quark decays (t →H±b) with subsequent decay H± →cb. The previous analysis reported an intriguing excess near mH± = 130 GeV with a local significance of approximately 3σ. Using the complete Run 3 dataset (√s= 13.6 TeV, L ≈300fb−1), this study aims to conclusively investigate this anomaly while extending sensitivity to branching fraction products B(t→H±b) ×B(H± →cb) below 0.1%. The analysis includes several key improvements: next-generation heavy flavor tagging algorithms, sophisticated machine learning techniques, and en- hanced data-driven background estimation methods. This search will probe complementary parameter spaces in multi-Higgs-doublet models where the H± →cb decay channel dominates. The expected outcomes include either world-leading exclusion limits or compelling evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model.

17311426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17311426.value: 模曲線上相對格拉斯曼流行的泊松幾何

17311426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17311426.value: Elliptic Poisson structures form a class of quadratic Poisson structures on projective spaces, first constructed by Sklyanin in the early 1980s and subsequently generalized by Feigin and Odesskii. These structures are fundamental objects in Poisson geometry and quantum algebra. Building on the work of Polishchuk and the PI, it has become evident that projective spaces equipped with elliptic Poisson structures can be viewed as components of the moduli space of complexes over an elliptic curve. In this project, we will focus on those components that are isomorphic to Grassmannians. Unlike the well-studied case of projective spaces, much less is known about the quantization of elliptic Poisson structures on Grassmannians. While traditional approaches often analyze the Poisson and quantum geometry of a fixed Grassmannian, we adopt a relative perspective. Since the moduli space of complexes can be constructed for a flat family degenerating elliptic curves, we consider a Grassmannian bundle over a parameter space. A natural choice for this parameter space is the compactified modular curve which parametrizes generalized elliptic curves in the sense of Deligne and Rapoport. Our previous work indicates that over the cusps, the Poisson structure on the fiber is semi-standard. By the work of Gekhtman, Shapiro and Vainshtein it admits a compatible cluster structure. The machinery of cluster algebras enables us to construct canonical bases on Grassmannians, leading to a canonical quantization. The main focus of this project will be the construction of log canonical coordinates and the analysis of their behavior under deformation and degeneration. This represents a crucial step toward developing elliptic analogues of quantum Grassmannians and Grassmannian cluster algebras. 橢圓泊松結構是一類定義於射影空間上的二次泊松結構，最早由 Sklyanin 於 20 世紀 80 年代初構造，隨後由 Feigin 與 Odesskii 加以推廣。這些結構是泊松幾何與量子代數中的基本研究對象。在 Polishchuk 以及本人相關工作的基礎上，人們逐漸認識到，帶有橢圓泊松結構的射影空間可以視為橢圓曲線上複形模空間的某些分支。在本計畫中，我們將專注研究其中與 Grassmann 流形同構的那些分支。 相較於射影空間上橢圓泊松結構已被廣泛研究的情形，目前對於 Grassmann 流形上橢圓泊松結構的量子化仍知之甚少。傳統方法通常研究固定 Grassmann 流形上的泊松幾何與量子幾何性質，而本計畫採取相對化的觀點。由於複形模空間可以構造於橢圓曲線平坦退化族之上，我們考慮定義在一個參數空間上的 Grassmann 流形叢。一個自然的參數空間選擇是緊化模曲線，它按照 Deligne 與 Rapoport 關於廣義橢圓曲線的意義，參數化廣義橢圓曲線。我們先前的工作顯示，在尖點處，纖維上的泊松結構是半標準型（semi-standard）的。根據 Gekhtman、Shapiro 與 Vainshtein 的工作，這類結構具有相容的叢代數結構（cluster structure）。叢代數理論所提供的工具，使我們能夠在 Grassmann 流形上構造典範基，從而導出一種典範量子化。 本計畫的主要目標是構造對數正則坐標（log canonical coordinates），並分析其在變形與退化過程中的行為。這將成為發展橢圓型量子 Grassmann 流形以及 Grassmann 流形叢代數理論的重要一步。

17311526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17311526.value: 闡明超窄帶隙有機半導體中激子動力學與電荷產生機制，以實現高靈敏度的短波紅外檢測

17311526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17311526.value: Short-wave infrared (SWIR) detection is critical for emerging applications in biomedical imaging, environmental monitoring, and machine vision, yet incumbent InGaAs photodetectors are expensive to fabricate and difficult to integrate with flexible electronics. Organic photodetectors (OPDs) offer a promising route to low-cost, lightweight, and flexible SWIR detection. Although OPDs can already match inorganic device performance across the visible to near-infrared (~0.4-1.0 μm), attempts to extend detection into the SWIR have typically suffered from reduced responsivity and detectivity beyond ~1 μm. Promisingly, a new class of non-fullerene acceptors (NFAs) featuring strong quinoid resonance effect has recently achieved record-breaking SWIR-OPD performance. Building upon the development of novel NFAs for efficient organic photovoltaics, the introduction of quinoid resonance further reduces the bandgap by enhancing intramolecular charge transfer and electronic delocalization, pushing the absorption onset into the SWIR. However, the fundamental electron-hole (exciton) dynamics and charge generation mechanism in these benchmark quinoid-NFAs have remained unclear. This knowledge gap limits rational design of new quinoid-NFAs with even better OPD performance in the SWIR. A comprehensive investigation to address this knowledge gap will be performed in this project. We plan to employ advanced in-situ ultrafast optical techniques to characterise exciton and charge dynamics in these materials. Our preliminary results reveal for the first time that excitons created in benchmark quinoid-NFAs can synergistically exhibit: (1) suppressed non-radiative decay rates, and (2) fast separation at donor-acceptor interfaces. These early results provide new insights on how these materials can achieve high-performance despite their ultranarrow-bandgaps (~0.8 eV), and indicate that we can improve their performance by further optimizing the kinetics of these competing physical processes. Besides transient optical studies, X-ray scattering measurements and quantum chemical calculations will be used to identify the key intrinsic chemical, structural and electronic factors of narrow-bandgap quinoid-NFAs that promote exciton dissociation yields and suppress dark and noise currents in devices. The project outcome will be a mechanistic model that unifies chemical structure, electronic coupling, and energy landscapes to explain and predict charge generation in SWIR-OPDs based on quinoid-NFAs. From this, we will propose rational design rules to guide new SWIR-OPD material development. Working closely with our chemist collaborators (Professor Chunhui Duan at SCUT), we will design, synthesize, and test new quinoid-NFAs guided by these rules, targeting further extension of absorption range and achieve record-breaking SWIR-OPD performance. Our results will promote fundamental organic semiconductor research, and accelerate the development of commercially-viable SWIR OPD technology. 短波紅外（SWIR）檢測在生物醫學成像、環境監測和機器視覺等新興應用中具有關鍵作用，而現有的InGaAs光電探測器則在製造成本高、難以與柔性電子器件集成方面存在挑戰。有機光電探測器（OPD）為實現低成本、輕便且柔性的SWIR檢測提供了一條有前途的途徑。雖然目前的OPD在可見光至近紅外（約0.4-1.0微米）範圍內已能與無機器件的性能相媲美，但在拓展到SWIR波段的試驗中，通常會因響應度和探測率降低而受阻，特別是在波長超過約1微米時。 令人鼓舞的是，最近一種醌類非富勒烯受體（NFA）分子材料，在SWIR-OPD性能方面取得了突破性進展。基於開發高效有機光伏新型NFA的研究，通過引入醌醚共振，進一步降低了帶隙，這主要通過增強分子內電荷轉移和電子離域實現，從而將吸收起點移動到SWIR範圍內。然而，這些醌類-NFA中的電子空穴（激子）動力學及載子生成機制仍然不清楚。這一知識空白限制了在設計具有更優性能的新型醌類-NFA方面的理性指導，也阻礙了在SWIR範圍內實現更高性能的OPD的開發。 本項目將進行一項全面的研究，以彌補這一知識空白。我們計畫採用先進的原位超快光學技術，表徵這些材料中的激子和電荷動力學。初步結果首次揭示了在醌類-NFA中產生的激子可以協同表現出：(1) 非輻射弛豫速率的抑制；(2) 在給體-受體界面上的快速分離。這些早期發現為理解這些材料在極窄帶隙（約0.8 eV）條件下仍能實現高性能的原因提供了新見解，表明通過進一步優化這些競爭性物理過程的動力學，可以提升器件性能。除了瞬態光學研究外，我們還將利用X射線散射測量和量子化學計算，識別促進激子解離效率並抑制暗電流和噪聲的窄帶隙醌類-NFA的內在化學、結構和電子關鍵因素。 該項目的成果將構建一個機制模型，結合化學結構、電子耦合和能量景觀，用以解釋和預測基於醌類-NFA的SWIR-OPD中的電荷生成過程。基於此，我們將提出合理的設計原則，指導新型SWIR-OPD材料的開發。我們將與合作的化學研究人員緊密合作，旨在進一步延長吸收範圍並實現突破性的SWIR-OPD性能。這些研究不僅將推動有機半導體基礎科研的發展，也將加速商業化SWIR光電探測技術的實現。

17311626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17311626.value: 从极端环境探究未来：适应海洋升温与酸化能否帮助珊瑚礁物种抵御海洋热浪？

17311626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17311626.value: Marine species are increasingly being impacted by compound environmental stressors under climate change. Long-term ocean warming (OW) and ocean acidification (OA) are occurring relatively slowly, potentially enabling some organisms to adapt. In contrast, Marine Heatwaves (MHWs) are rapid and intense increases in temperature that can last for months. More extreme events have the potential for devastating, large-scale reorganization of ecosystems and mass-mortality if organisms are unable to acclimate quickly. However, long-term exposure to gradual OW and OA could lead to selection for beneficial phenotypes, and eventually genotypes, that are more resilient to the effects of climate change. This selection could bring about population adaptation and allow organisms to persist in areas outside of their normal environmental niche, as well as potentially make them more resilient to MHWs. However, the capacity for plasticity and adaptive evolution is unknown for many species. Subsequently, natural analogues for future ocean conditions (e.g., warm and more acidic semi-enclosed bays), have become important tools for investigating the consequences of increased compound stressors for organism physiology and provide an opportunity to study the genetic mechanisms underpinning local acclimation or adaptation. The semi-enclosed coral reef lagoon system of Palau provides the opportunity to study natural assemblages of species that are thriving in more extreme marine conditions, comparing their physiology with the same species living in more ‘average’ conditions. The inner-lagoon in Palau is ~1-2°C warmer and more acidic (pH ~7.8 cf. 8.1) than outer-lagoons. Currently, little is known about how these already extreme environments, and their associated biota, will be impacted by MHWs – will marine species within Palau be more resilient to these events due to their long-term exposure to higher temperatures, or are they already near their physiological tolerance limits? We propose to address this overarching question by using the natural gradient of Palau’s lagoons to study the phenotypic physiological response of model species (sea urchins) to MHWs and identify the genotypic markers that make it possible to live in these more extreme environments. By using natural analogues, we can provide important insights into the future of coastal ecosystems because the long-term exposure of local populations means we can study the ecological mechanisms of adaptation through genotypic markers. Such understanding allows us to project how entire coastal regions could be affected by ocean warming, acidification, and extreme MHWs, all key changes that are occurring because of anthropogenic climate change 气候变化下，海洋生物面临多重胁迫。长期升温与酸化较缓，部分生物或可适应；海洋热浪急剧且持续数月，若无法快速适应，可致生态系统重构与生物大量死亡。长期暴露于渐进升温和酸化可筛选出耐性表型与基因型，增强热浪抵御力，但多数物种表型可塑性与适应进化能力未知。更暖更酸的半封闭海湾等自然类比环境，为研究复合胁迫生理与局地适应遗传机制提供天然平台。 帕劳半封闭珊瑚礁潟湖即为典型代表，可研究极端环境中稳定生存的自然群落，并与常态环境同种个体比较生理。内潟湖温度较外高约1–2°C，pH约7.8（外约8.1）。尚不清楚这些极端环境生物群如何响应热浪：长期高温暴露增强其耐受性，还是已近生理极限？本项目以海胆为模式生物，利用帕劳潟湖自然环境梯度，研究其对海洋热浪的表型与生理响应，探究支撑适应极端环境的基因型标记，揭示其生态适应机制，进而预测沿海生态系统在人为气候变化所致海洋升温、酸化及极端热浪影响下的未来变化。

17311826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17311826.value: 层级建模的鞅后验分布

17311826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17311826.value: Bayesian hierarchical modelling is ubiquitous in many fields including ecology, economics, medicine and social science. The key benefit of hierarchical modelling is the ability to model multiple distinct groups of data, whilst sharing information between them, increasing the efficiency and robustness of statistical inferences. Both parametric and nonparametric Bayesian hierarchical models have been proposed in the literature, with broad applications. However, all methods require the use of Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) for posterior computation, which is computationally expensive and particularly unreliable in hierarchical settings due to the complex posterior geometry. The martingale posterior (MP) framework replaces the Bayesian prior and likelihood with a sequence of predictive densities, and completely avoids MCMC for posterior computation, instead relying on an imputation scheme known as predictive resampling. Thus far however, the MP has only been developed for the setting of a single dataset. This project considers the natural extension of the MP framework to the hierarchical setting, where novel predictive rules will be developed that allow for the sharing of information between multiple groups of data. In particular, the promising scalability of the MP approach will allow Bayesian hierarchical modelling to scale to much more complex settings. 贝叶斯层级建模广泛应用于生态学、经济学、医学和社会科学等众多领域。层级建模的主要优势在于，它能够对多个不同组别的数据进行建模，同时在组别之间共享信息，从而提高统计推断的效率与稳健性。已有文献提出了参数化和非参数化的贝叶斯层级模型，并在诸多领域得到广泛应用。然而，所有这些方法都需要使用马尔可夫链蒙特卡罗（MCMC）进行后验计算；该方法计算成本高昂，并且由于层级模型中的后验几何结构较为复杂，在层级设定下尤其不稳定。 鞅后验分布（martingale posterior, MP）框架以一系列预测密度取代贝叶斯先验和似然，并完全避免使用 MCMC 进行后验计算，转而依赖一种称为预测重抽样的插补方案。然而，到目前为止，MP 仅在单一数据集的情境下得到发展。本项目将考虑把 MP 框架自然扩展到层级设定中，并开发新的预测规则，使其能够在多个数据组别之间共享信息。特别地，MP 方法所展现出的良好可扩展性，将使贝叶斯层级建模能够扩展到更加复杂的应用场景。

17312326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17312326.value: 原初恒星与巨星的潮汐瓦解事件：高红移及非典型核暂现源的理论基础

17312326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17312326.value: The field of tidal disruption events (TDEs) is rapidly expanding beyond the canonical disruption of a main-sequence star by a supermassive black hole. This proposal seeks to confront and characterize these new frontiers by developing sophisticated theoretical models to interpret a growing menagerie of exotic transients. We will focus on two previously understudied areas: TDEs of metal-poor stars in the early universe and repeating partial TDEs of red giants. Our methodology will combine state-of-the-art stellar evolution codes (MESA) with high-performance hydrodynamic simulations (FLASH) to predict the unique observational signatures of these events. This work will determine the distinctive fallback rates and light curves that differentiate these TDEs from the canonical class, providing crucial templates for their identification. The modeling results will be critical for guiding and interpreting discoveries from flagship observatories like the Vera C. Rubin Observatory and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, and possibly explaining the physical origin of newly discovered and puzzling nuclear transients. 潮汐瓦解事件（TDEs）领域正迅速扩展，超越了过去对主序星被超大质量黑洞瓦解的经典图景。本课题旨在通过发展精细的理论模型，来应对和刻画这些新前沿，从而阐释日益多样化的非典型的星系核区暂现源现象。我们将重点研究两个此前未受充分关注的领域：早期宇宙中贫金属星的TDEs，以及红巨星重复性部分TDEs。我们的方法将结合前沿的恒星演化代码（MESA）与高性能流体动力学模拟（FLASH），以预测这些事件独特的观测特征。这项工作将确定区别于经典TDEs的独特回落速率和光变曲线，为其识别提供关键模板。建模结果将对指导并解读薇拉·鲁宾天文台和南希·格雷斯·罗曼空间望远镜等旗舰观测设备的发现至关重要，并可能解释新发现且令人费解的核区暂现源的物理起源。

17312526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17312526.value: 混合精度量化優化的理論基礎：訓練動力學、隱式偏置與尺度律

17312526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17312526.value: Low-precision training has become an indispensable technique for scaling deep learning, enabling the creation of large-scale models on current hardware by reducing memory footprint and computational costs. In practice, this is realized via mixed-precision optimization, where different components, such as model weights, gradients, and optimizer states, are quantized to various bit-lengths. However, despite extensive empirical breakthroughs, the theoretical foundation of mixed-precision quantized training has remained underdeveloped. Existing theoretical analyses, while providing important convergence guarantees, suffer from critical limitations that render them disconnected from practical realities. They predominantly focus on training loss convergence, overlooking the more crucial question of how quantization affects learning performance. Furthermore, these studies often rely on worst-case assumptions, yielding pessimistic bounds that fail to capture the nuanced benefits of mixed-precision schemes. This gap impedes a systematic understanding of quantized training and hinders the principled design of next-generation algorithms. This project aims to mitigate this gap by developing a holistic learning theory for training under mixed-precision quantization, moving beyond convergence analysis to characterize the entire learning process and its effect on generalization. The project has three core objectives. First, it will establish a theoretical framework to analyze the learning dynamics and implicit bias of quantized SGD algorithms, providing instance-specific learning guarantees explicitly formulated in terms of key algorithm and quantization parameters. Second, it will establish learning guarantees for adaptive optimizers in mixed-precision settings, precisely identifying the effects of quantization errors in different optimizer components to guide new co-designs of algorithms and precision allocation strategies. Finally, it will build a theory of low-precision training scaling laws to rigorously quantify the interplay between model size, data volume, and the bit precision of various components, enabling the design of optimal training recipes under fixed resource budgets. Our team has already established preliminary theoretical results on the learning dynamics of quantized SGD and the convergence of quantized adaptive optimizers (e.g., Adam and Muon), providing a set of useful technical tools and precise intuitions for the proposed projects. Overall, this project will deliver a rigorous theoretical framework, novel optimization algorithms, and principled scaling laws. The resulting algorithms will be disseminated as open-source software, and the theoretical insights will be integrated into course materials to train the next generation of researchers in efficient deep learning. Moreover, the developed research is expected to trigger a series of further theoretical explorations in resource-limited scenarios involving LLMs, such as post-training, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and quantization-aware training. 低精度訓練已成為擴展深度學習不可或缺的技術，其透過減少記憶體佔用與計算成本，使得在現有硬體上建立大規模模型成為可能。在實務上，此目標係經由混合精度優化來實現，其中模型權重、梯度與優化器狀態等不同組件分別量化至不同的位元長度。然而，儘管已有大量實證上的突破，混合精度量化訓練的理論基礎至今仍發展不足。現有的理論分析雖提供了重要的收斂性保證，卻存在關鍵性限制，使其與實際應用脫節。此類研究主要聚焦於訓練損失的收斂性，忽視了更為核心的問題，亦即量化如何影響學習表現。此外，這些研究常依賴於最壞情況假設，所給出的悲觀界線無法捕捉混合精度方案所帶來的細緻效益。此落差阻礙了對量化訓練的系統性理解，也制約了下一代演算法之原則性設計。本計畫旨在透過發展一套針對混合精度量化下訓練之整體性學習理論來填補此一缺口，不僅超越收斂性分析，更進一步刻畫整體學習過程及其對泛化能力之影響。本計畫包含三項核心目標。第一，建立一套理論框架，用以分析量化隨機梯度下降（SGD）演算法之訓練動力學與隱式偏置，並以關鍵演算法及量化參數明確表達出特定於實例之學習保證。第二，針對混合精度設定下之自適應優化器建立學習保證，精確辨識不同優化器組件中量化誤差之影響，以指導演算法與精度分配策略之新穎協同設計。第三，建構低精度訓練之尺度律理論，嚴謹量化模型規模、資料量及各組件位元精度之間的交互作用，從而在固定資源預算下實現最優訓練配方的設計。

17312826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17312826.value: The Transformer architecture has emerged as a foundational model for achieving state-of-the-art performance in complex sequential data domains such as audio, video, and natural language, and, most notably, serving as the core architecture for large language models such as ChatGPT in generative AI. Despite its impressive empirical success, statistical understanding of these models-particularly in explaining why Transformers can achieve such performance-remains underdeveloped. Central to their success is the attention mechanism, yet current theoretical explanations are largely heuristic in nature, offering limited insight into why "attention is all you need". Moreover, current theoretical studies primarily focus on in-context learning perspectives and do not provide a framework for uncertainty quantification. This project aims to establish a probabilistic interpretation of the Transformer through the lens of kernel-based models, particularly Gaussian processes (GPs). This perspective will yield an elegant and principled probabilistic variant of the Transformer, enabling the application of Bayesian methodology to analyze its representational and inferential capabilities. Such a framework will offer a deeper probabilistic understanding of why and how Transformers perform so well in practice. Building on this formulation, we will investigate the theoretical properties of the resulting model--most notably, its generalization properties, and establishing posterior contraction rates and other asymptotic guarantees. This analysis will lay the statistical foundations for understanding why and how Transformer models achieve state-of-the-art performance. Moreover, GP-based perspective of the Transformer will naturally facilitate the modeling of complex correlations among features and outputs without added computational complexity, compared to baseline methods. Beyond theoretical insights, the proposed framework will guide the design of computationally efficient training algorithms for Transformer models that are substantially faster than existing algorithms. Modern implementations often involve models with millions or billions of parameters-demanding enormous computational, financial, and energy resources. Contrary to the prevailing paradigm in the AI community that trains the large possible models with available computational power and financial resources, we seek to develop computationally efficient algorithms grounded in the statistical understanding of the transformers. Transformer 架構已成為在音訊、視訊和自然語言等複雜序列資料領域實現最先進效能的基礎模型，尤其值得一提的是，它也是生成式人工智慧中 ChatGPT 等大型語言模型的核心架構。儘管在實證研究中取得了令人矚目的成功，但對這些模型的統計理解——特別是解釋 Transformer 為何能夠達到如此卓越的性能——仍然不夠深入。注意力機制是其成功的關鍵，但目前的理論解釋大多是啟發式的，對「注意力機制就是一切」的原則缺乏深入的詮釋。此外，目前的理論研究主要集中於上下文學習視角，而沒有提供不確定性量化的框架。 本計畫旨在透過基於核函數的模型，特別是高斯過程，建立 Transformer 的機率解釋。這種視角將產生一個優雅且符合邏輯的 Transformer 機率變體，從而能夠應用貝葉斯方法來分析其表徵和推理能力。這樣的框架將提供對Transformer模型在實踐中表現如此出色的原因和機制的更深入的機率理解。 基於此框架，我們將透過建立後驗收縮率和其他漸近保證，研究得出模型的理論特性──尤其是其泛化特性。這項分析將為理解Transformer模型為何以及如何達到最先進的效能奠定統計基礎。此外，與基線方法相比，基於高斯過程的Transformer視角將自然而然地促進特徵和輸出之間複雜相關性的建模，而不會增加額外的計算複雜度。 除了理論見解之外，所提出的框架還將指導設計計算高效的Transformer模型訓練演算法，這些演算法的速度將遠超現有演算法。現代實現通常涉及擁有數百萬甚至數十億個參數的模型——這需要龐大的計算、資金和能源資源。與人工智慧領域目前普遍採用的利用現有運算能力和資金訓練盡可能大的模型的範式相反，我們致力於開發基於對Transformer模型統計理解的計算高效演算法。

17313126.value: 七元环嵌入的开壳纳米石墨烯：间隔基介导的自旋调控、多自旋结构及手性诱导自旋选择性

17313126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17313126.value: Open-shell nanographenes are emerging as promising candidates for applications in spintronics, organic electronics, and quantum information technologies, owing to their unique ability to manipulate spin at the molecular level. However, most reported studies have focused on alternant benzenoid frameworks, while nonalternant systems containing heptagons remain scarcely explored due to synthetic challenges and limited stability. Developing stable heptagon-embedded radicals is therefore crucial, as they can reshape electronic structures, extend spin lifetimes, and enable advanced spin regulation. This project aims to construct a new class of heptagon-embedded nonalternant polycyclic hydrocarbon (PH) radicals and systematically explore their potential for applications in molecular spintronics and quantum information science. The research is structured around three core objectives (Fig. 3): (i) Systematically investigating the influence of alternant (1) vs. nonalternant (2) spacers on electronic structures, spin-spin interactions, and spin lifetimes, thereby establishing transferable design principles for spin regulation at the molecular level; (ii) Synthesizing novel multi-spin architectures embedding seven-five-seven (7-5-7) motifs, including spin-frustrated triradicals (3), tetraradicals (4), and hexaradicals (5), to expand the structural diversity of molecular radicals and address prevailing challenges such as instability and poor solubility; and (iii) introducing chirality into 7-5-7 radical frameworks (compounds 6 and 7) to probe the chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect and explore their potential applications as molecular spin filters, spin valves, and quantum information units. These objectives follow a coherent progression from molecular design, through fundamental property evaluation, to functional application, thereby closing the loop from concept to implementation and paving the way for novel spin-based materials and devices. Anticipated outcomes of this project include the creation of unprecedented heptagon-embedded higher-order polyradicals, the establishment of foundational structure-property-function relationships, and the demonstration of topology- and chirality-mediated spin control. Beyond expanding the structural diversity of open-shell systems, this work will establish general design principles for molecular-level spin manipulation and deliver stable, tunable molecular platforms for investigating spin entanglement and CISS. Ultimately, the project will provide robust, designer molecular systems and transferable design guidelines for advancing organic spintronics and quantum information technologies, bridging fundamental molecular design with future device-oriented applications. 開殼層奈米碳材料憑藉其在分子層級上操控自旋的獨特能力，正逐漸成為自旋電子學、有機電子學和量子資訊技術領域極具前景的應用候選材料。然而，目前已報導的大多數研究集中於交替苯型骨架，而含有七元環的非交替體系則因合成挑戰和穩定性有限而鮮有探索。因此，發展穩定的七元環嵌入自由基至關重要，因為它們能夠重塑電子結構、延長自旋壽命，並實現更先進的自旋調控。本項目旨在構建一類新型的七元環嵌入非交替多環碳氫（PH）自由基，並系統探索其在分子自旋電子學和量子資訊科學中的應用潛力。研究圍繞三個核心目標展開（圖1）：（i）系統研究交替型（1）與非交替型（2）間隔基對電子結構、自旋-自旋相互作用及自旋壽命的影響，從而建立分子層級自旋調控的可推廣設計原則；（ii）合成嵌入七-五-七（7-5-7）結構單元的新型多自旋體系，包括自旋阻挫三自由基（3）、四自由基（4）和六自由基（5），以拓展分子自由基的結構多樣性，並解決不穩定性與溶解性差等當前面臨的挑戰；（iii）在7-5-7自由基骨架中引入手性（化合物6和7），以探究手性誘導自旋選擇性（CISS）效應，並探索其作為分子自旋過濾器、自旋閥和量子資訊單元的應用潛力。這些目標遵循從分子設計到基礎性質評價再到功能應用的連貫遞進過程，從而完成從概念到實施的全鏈條閉環，並為新型自旋基材料與器件的發展鋪平道路。 本項目的預期成果包括：創製前所未有的七元環嵌入高階多自由基，建立基礎的結構–性質–功能關係，並驗證拓撲和手性介導的自旋調控能力。除拓展開殼層體系的結構多樣性外，這項工作還將為分子層級的自旋操控建立通用設計原則，並提供穩定、可調的分子平台，用於研究自旋糾纏和CISS效應。最終，本項目將為推動有機自旋電子學和量子資訊技術的發展，提供堅固、可設計的分子系統及可轉移的設計準則，從而在基礎分子設計與未來面向器件的應用之間架起橋樑。

17313426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17313426.value: 競爭中的非對稱性與資訊聚合

17313426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17313426.value: In many AI-powered systems, decisions can become unbalanced due to asymmetry – where certain errors, user groups, or information sources are prioritized over others. This proposal examines asymmetry in two contexts: algorithmic competition in markets and information aggregation in social networks. In the first context, we study algorithmic personalization in competitive markets. Companies may converge on serving the largest user group – a phenomenon of “algorithmic monoculture” that leaves minority needs underserved. A key challenge is determining whether competition will encourage variety or lead to uniform, majority-focused strategies. To address this, we will develop a new metric to measure algorithmic monoculture and build theoretical models of how firms compete in personalization. By analyzing these models, we aim to pinpoint conditions under which providers either differentiate their algorithms or all chase the same majority segment. We will also examine how these outcomes affect user experience and fairness for majority versus minority groups. The findings will inform strategies and policy interventions such as diversity requirements or market incentives to promote algorithmic diversity and ensure AI-driven services benefit a broader range of users. The second context looks at how information is shared and learned in society, especially in networks where influence is one-directional (for example, popular influencers sway many followers without reciprocal influence). The challenge here is understanding how such directional influence impacts collective learning. Will the community reach a consensus, and if so, is it an accurate “wisdom of the crowd” or a biased outcome shaped by a few voices? Our approach extends social learning models to directed networks. Through theoretical analysis and simulations, we will examine whether these networks reach a stable consensus and, if so, whether that consensus reflects true information or is skewed by a few influencers. We will identify conditions leading to a quick but flawed consensus versus those that enable the crowd to aggregate information wisely. By addressing these two problems through the lens of asymmetry, the project will generate new knowledge about what drives uniformity or diversity in complex systems. The anticipated results have broad implications – from guiding AI regulations and fostering healthier competition in digital markets to informing the design of social networks that promote more balanced information exposure. Ultimately, this research will provide both theoretical insights and practical recommendations to help make digital services and online communities more fair, diverse, and beneficial to society. 在許多由AI驅動的系統中，決策可能因「不對稱性」而失衡——亦即某些錯誤、使用者群體或資訊來源被賦予高於其他對象的優先地位。本計畫將在兩種情境下探討不對稱性：市場中的演算法競爭，以及社會網絡中的資訊匯集。 在第一個情境中，我們研究競爭市場中的演算法個人化。企業可能趨同於服務規模最大的使用者群體——此即「演算法單一文化」（algorithmic monoculture）現象，使少數群體的需求未獲充分滿足。這裡的關鍵挑戰，在於判斷競爭究竟會鼓勵多樣性，還是導致一致且以多數為導向的策略。為此，我們將發展一項衡量演算法單一文化的新指標，並建立理論模型以刻畫廠商如何在個人化服務上競爭。透過分析這些模型，我們期望明確指出在何種條件下，服務提供者會使其演算法彼此差異化，或全都追逐同一個多數客群。我們也將檢視這些結果如何影響多數與少數群體的使用者體驗與公平性。研究發現將為策略與政策干預提供依據——例如多樣性要求或市場誘因——以促進演算法多樣性，並確保AI驅動的服務能嘉惠更廣泛的使用者。 第二個情境關注資訊在社會中如何被分享與學習，特別是在影響力為單向的網絡中（例如，知名的意見領袖左右眾多追隨者，卻不受其反向影響）。此處的挑戰在於理解這種單向影響力如何衝擊集體學習：社群是否會達成共識？若會，這一共識是準確的「群眾智慧」（wisdom of the crowd），還是由少數聲音塑造的偏頗結果？我們的方法是將社會學習模型擴展至有向網絡。透過理論分析與模擬，我們將檢驗這些網絡是否會達成穩定的共識；若會，該共識反映的是真實資訊，還是被少數具影響力者所扭曲。我們將辨識哪些條件會導致快速但有缺陷的共識，哪些條件則能讓群眾明智地匯集資訊。 透過不對稱性的視角處理這兩個問題，本計畫將就複雜系統中驅動一致性或多樣性的因素產生新知識。預期成果具有廣泛意涵——從指引AI監管、促進數位市場更健康的競爭，到為設計能促進更均衡資訊接觸的社群網絡提供參考。最終，本研究將提供理論洞見與實務建議，協助數位服務與線上社群變得更公平、多元，且更有益於社會。

17313726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17313726.value: Despite formidable challenge in metallodrug development, several metal-based compounds are established in clinical practice for diagnostic and therapeutic applications. Amid the escalating global threat of antimicrobial resistance (AMR), there is increasing focus on repurposing metal compounds to combat resistant pathogens. These efforts, leveraging the unique molecular mechanisms of metallodrugs, are under active investigation to address AMR crisis effectively. Bismuth has been a cornerstone of medical treatment for centuries, notably for gastrointestinal disorders caused by Helicobacter pylori infections. Despite H. pylori’s susceptibility to antibiotics, increasing antibiotic resistance hinders effective eradication. Bismuth-based drugs—bismuth subsalicylate (BSS), colloidal bismuth subcitrate (CBS), and ranitidine bismuth citrate (RBC)—are clinically utilized. Combining bismuth drugs with antibiotics is a well-established first-line treatment, effectively targeting even antibiotic-resistant strains. Beyond H. pylori, bismuth demonstrates efficacy against various pathogenic bacteria. Recently, bismuth compounds have been repurposed to combat drug resistant bacterial infections including metallo-β-lactamase-positive bacterial infections, Cefiderocol-resistant P. aeruginosa and B. cepacia infections. These findings highlight bismuth’s significant potential in addressing AMR crisis. Streptococcus pyogenes (S. pyogenes), a bacteria commonly known as “flesh-eating bacteria” can cause a wide spectrum of infections, from mild pharyngitis and skin infections to life-threatening invasive diseases like necrotizing fasciitis and streptococcal shock syndrome. Despite of efficacy of certain antibiotics, treatment failures occur in clinical practice. Thus, development of effective therapy is urgently needed. Our preliminary screening of bismuth compounds against S. pyogenes revealed that select bismuth compounds exhibit potent antimicrobial and anti-virulence activity. This promising discovery provides a robust foundation for the proposed project. We aim to identify more effective bismuth compounds, and elucidate their molecular mechanisms. Specifically, we will synthesize a diverse library of bismuth compounds and conduct further screening to identify those with superior activity. We will examine potential synergistic interaction between bismuth compounds and antibiotics and assess their efficacy in a murine model of S. pyogenes infection. Subsequently, we will study molecular mechanism of bismuth compounds against S. pyogenes by integrating transcriptomics with metalloproteomics. We will functionally categorize identified proteins (altered genes) by bioinformatics, followed by experimental validation of key protein targets or biological pathways influenced by Bi(III) compounds by various assays. These findings will deepen our understanding on molecular mechanism of antimicrobial and anti-virulence of Bi(III) compounds against S. pyogenes infection including resistant strains. This project will provide a foundation for developing novel bismuth-based therapies to combat S. pyogenes infections.

17313926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17313926.value: 面向科學預測的基函數信息Transformer：方法、理論與應用

17313926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17313926.value: The emerging field of "AI for Science", with deep learning at its core, is transforming scientific discovery by enabling rapid analysis and predictive modeling of complex datasets. However, scientific tasks present unique challenges compared to conventional deep learning applications. Many scientific prediction tasks are governed by underlying physical systems, for which numerical methods and physics-informed neural networks can facilitate modeling and inference. Yet, when the available data are incomplete and insufficient to fully characterize these physical systems, traditional approaches may not be directly applicable. Furthermore, scientific data are often irregularly distributed. For example, ocean measurements collected by ships or floats are typically scattered unevenly across geographic locations. Consequently, data collected at different time points often differ in both number and location, lacking direct correspondence across time, which limits the applicability of standard deep learning methods. In this research, we propose the development of basis-informed transformers, a novel class of deep learning models specifically designed to address the unique challenges of scientific prediction tasks with incomplete and irregular data. Unlike conventional transformers, our approach integrates prior scientific knowledge through efficient basis representations, bridging the gap between data-driven methods and physical understanding, and enabling effective modeling under challenging data conditions. We will develop two key model classes: basis-informed masked transformers for scientific reconstruction and basis-informed spatio-temporal transformers for scientific forecasting. Both models have demonstrated promising performance in our preliminary empirical studies and will be further supported with rigorous learning theory guarantees. Comprehensive validation will also be conducted on a range of prediction tasks drawn from multiple scientific domains such as oceanography and climatology. Success in the proposed research will lead to novel deep learning-based methods for scientific prediction. The resulting algorithms will be integrated into open-access software packages, which can potentially be utilized across a range of scientific domains. 以深度學習為核心的新興領域「AI for Science」正在透過對複雜數據集進行快速分析與預測建模，推動科學發現方式的變革。然而，與傳統深度學習應用相比，科學任務具有其獨特挑戰。許多科學預測任務受底層物理系統支配，針對這類問題，數值方法與物理信息神經網路可以促進建模與推斷。然而，當可用數據不完整，且不足以充分支撐對這些系統的建模時，傳統方法可能無法直接適用。此外，科學數據通常呈現不規則分佈。例如，由船舶或浮標收集的海洋觀測數據，通常在地理位置上分散且分佈不均。因此，不同時間點收集到的數據往往在數量與位置上均不相同，且缺乏跨時間的直接對應關係，這限制了標準深度學習方法的適用性。 在本研究中，我們提出發展基函數信息Transformer，這是一類新型深度學習模型，專門用於應對具有不完整與不規則數據的科學預測任務所面臨的獨特挑戰。不同於傳統Transformer，我們的方法透過高效的基函數表示整合先驗科學知識，彌合數據驅動方法與物理理解之間的差距，並使模型能夠在具有挑戰性的數據條件下進行有效建模。我們將發展兩類核心模型：用於科學重建的基函數信息掩碼Transformer，以及用於科學預報的基函數信息時空Transformer。這兩類模型已在我們的初步實證研究中展現出良好的性能，並將進一步以嚴謹的學習理論保證加以支撐。我們還將在來自海洋學、氣候學等多個科學領域的一系列預測任務上進行全面驗證。 本研究若能成功，將形成基於深度學習的全新科學預測方法。所得演算法將被整合到開放取用的軟體套件中，並有望應用於多個科學領域。

17314026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17314026.value: 融合遺傳發現與泛化推斷的統一貝葉斯框架：多族群 TWAS 精細定位與經驗貝葉斯遷移學習

17314026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17314026.value: Statistical genetics is transitioning from association discovery to mechanistic understanding. Transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) represent a key methodology for understanding mechanisms by integrating genome-wide association studies (GWAS) with gene expression data. However, TWAS face two fundamental challenges: the difficulty in identifying causal genes from correlated signals, and limited statistical power in underrepresented populations. This proposal presents a cohesive, two-tiered research strategy to address these bottlenecks through novel Bayesian methodologies. First, we will develop MACHINE-T, a novel multi-ancestry TWAS fine-mapping framework. Existing methods face challenges in reliably controlling false discovery rate (FDR) with out-of-sample linkage disequilibrium (LD) reference panels and have limited capacity to leverage ancestry-specific genetic differences for higher resolution. MACHINE-T addresses these issues by employing a unified continuous global-local shrinkage prior that jointly models gene expression and direct SNP effects across diverse populations. Additionally, by incorporating a latent variable calibration to explicitly account for and correct mismatches between summary statistics and reference panel LD, MACHINE-T ensures calibrated FDR control, significantly enhancing reliability. Furthermore, by integrating functional genomic annotations directly into its prior, MACHINE-T improves biological interpretability, offering a statistically rigorous and biologically insightful tool for causal gene discovery. Second, motivated by the sample size limitations inherent in Aim 1 and other high-dimensional settings, we will create EBTL (Empirical Bayesian Transfer Learning), a general statistical framework for high-dimensional inference. EBTL innovatively leverages auxiliary summary-level data from large source studies to empower inference in target studies with limited samples. By constructing data-driven empirical conjugate priors grounded in established theoretical principles, EBTL provides a computationally efficient, privacy-aware, and robust platform for integrative analysis. Unlike existing transfer learning methods that require individual-level data or rely on unrealistic assumptions about source-target similarity, EBTL offers a practical and flexible solution. This framework directly enhances the power of our TWAS fine-mapping efforts but is designed as a versatile tool with broad applicability to risk prediction and meta-analysis. The aims are deeply synergistic: Aim 1 delivers an immediate, powerful method for improving causal gene identification in genetic studies, while Aim 2 provides a generalizable approach to overcome the pervasive challenge of limited data. Together, they form a transformative methodological pipeline that will advance the rigor and resolution of post-GWAS inference, facilitate more equitable genetic research across ancestries, and provide a robust statistical foundation for future discoveries in biomedical science. 統計遺傳學正從關聯發現邁向機制性理解。全轉錄組關聯研究（transcriptome-wide association studies, TWAS）是透過整合全基因組關聯研究（genome-wide association studies, GWAS）與基因表達資料來理解生物機制的一項關鍵方法。然而，TWAS 面臨兩項根本挑戰：其一，如何從彼此相關的訊號中識別因果基因；其二，在代表性不足族群中統計效能有限。本研究計畫提出一套連貫的雙層研究策略，透過新穎的貝葉斯方法學來突破這些瓶頸。 首先，我們將開發 MACHINE-T，一種新型的多族群 TWAS 精細定位框架。現有方法在使用樣本外連鎖不平衡（linkage disequilibrium, LD）參考面板時，往往難以可靠地控制假發現率（false discovery rate, FDR），且在利用族群特異性遺傳差異以提升解析度方面能力有限。MACHINE-T 透過採用統一的連續型全域—局部收縮先驗，對不同族群中的基因表達效應與 SNP 直接效應進行聯合建模，以解決上述問題。此外，MACHINE-T 納入潛在變數校準機制，明確考慮並修正摘要統計量與參考面板 LD 之間的不匹配，從而實現經校準的 FDR 控制，大幅提升結果的可靠性。進一步地，MACHINE-T 還將功能基因組註釋直接納入其先驗分布中，以增強生物學可解釋性，提供一種兼具統計嚴謹性與生物洞察力的因果基因發現工具。 其次，考量到目標一以及其他高維場景中固有的樣本量限制，我們將建立 EBTL（經驗貝葉斯遷移學習，Empirical Bayesian Transfer Learning），一個用於高維推論的通用統計框架。EBTL 的創新之處在於，利用來自大型來源研究的輔助性摘要層級資料，來增強樣本有限之目標研究中的推論能力。透過建立以既有理論原則為基礎、且由資料驅動的經驗共軛先驗，EBTL 提供了一個計算高效、兼顧隱私且穩健的整合分析平台。不同於現有遷移學習方法往往需要個體層級資料，或依賴來源與目標研究高度相似這類不切實際的假設，EBTL 提供了一種更具實用性與靈活性的解決方案。此框架不僅可直接提升我們 TWAS 精細定位工作的統計效能，也被設計為具有廣泛適用性的工具，可應用於風險預測與統合分析（meta-analysis）。 這兩項研究目標具有深度協同效應：目標一提供了一種可立即應用且效能強大的方法，以提升遺傳研究中的因果基因識別能力；目標二則提供了一種具可泛化性的途徑，以克服資料有限這一普遍存在的挑戰。兩者共同構成一條具有變革性的研究方法流程，將推進 GWAS 後推論的嚴謹性與解析度，促進不同族群間更公平的遺傳研究，並為未來生物醫學科學中的新發現奠定堅實的統計學基礎。

17314126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17314126.value: 針對鐵穩態的金屬基策略用於對抗抗藥性鮑曼不動桿菌

17314126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17314126.value: Metal-based compounds predate organic antibiotics and offer untapped potential to combat antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Increasing evidences have shown that metal complexes may represent promising sources to combating antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Bismuth(III) (Bi(III)) and sideromycins, like cefiderocol, exploit bacterial iron homeostasis, offers a promising strategy against multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens. Acinetobacter baumannii (A. baumannii), a WHO critical priority Gram-negative pathogen, causes severe nosocomial infections in ICU patients, with MDR and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) strains driving 40-60% mortality due to limited treatment options. Its clinical importance is amplified by its remarkable ability to develop and acquire resistance to multiple antibiotics, especially in the context of AMR. MDR and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) A. baumannii infections often require combination therapies, which are associated with limited efficacy and emerging resistance even to these last-line agents. Novel therapies are urgently needed. Our prior work demonstrated that Bi(III) compounds restore antibiotic susceptibility in Escherichia coli and Pseudomonas aeruginosa by inhibiting metallo-β-lactamases and disrupting iron homeostasis, mimicking Fe(III)/Zn(II) biochemistry. Our discoveries pinpoint the potential of Bi(III)-based strategies to be utilize to fight against A. baumannii infections solely or together with clinically used antibiotics. Leveraging these findings, our unique platform of well-characterized A. baumannii clinical isolates and laboratories for animal tests (SKL on Emerging Infectious Diseases), this project aims to develop Bi(III)-based therapies through targeting iron homeostasis against MDR A. baumannii. Specifically, we will: (i) design and synthesize a series of thiol-containing ligands and mono-catecholate sideromycin mimetics of acinetobactin, A. baumannii’s primary siderophore; and synthesize Bi(III) complexes conjugated with these ligands. (ii) We will subsequently evaluate synergy of Bi(III) complexes with key antibiotics, and efficacy of Bi(III)-sideromycin mimetics in bacterial and macrophage infection models; (iii) We will then test the lead compounds’ efficacy in a lung infection model, targeting >80% bacterial clearance. (iv) Finally, we elucidate mechanisms of action using various biophysical techniques including a home-made metalloproteomics, focusing on key iron uptake targets (e.g., BauA/BasD, FhuE) to optimize lead compounds both in vitro and in vivo. This project will generate novel therapeutic insights, train early-career researchers, and advance biological and medicinal chemistry of Bi(III), and importantly Bi(III)-based therapies toward clinical translation. By building on successes like cefiderocol and Bi(III)/Ga(III)-based strategies for E. coli and P. aeruginosa, our long-term goal is to deliver a transformative therapy for MDR A. baumannii infections, reduce AMR-associated mortality, and foster biopharmaceutical innovation Hong Kong and Greater Bay Area. 早在抗生素出現金屬類化合物就用於治療細菌感染，它在應對抗生素抗藥性（AMR）方面的潛力尚未被充分挖掘。越來越多的證據表明，金屬配合物有望成為對抗抗生素抗藥性的重要手段。鉍(III)（Bi(III)）及諸如頭孢地爾（cefiderocol）等鐵載體藥物（sideromycins）利用細菌的鐵穩態機制，為對抗多重抗藥性（MDR）病原體提供了一種極具前景的新策略。 鮑曼不動桿菌（Acinetobacter baumannii）被世界衛生組織列為亟需應對的重點革蘭氏陰性病原體，常導致重症監護病房患者發生嚴重醫院獲得性感染。由於治療方法有限，由多重抗藥性（MDR）及廣泛抗藥性（XDR）菌株引起的感染死亡率高達40%至60%。該菌具有極強的產生及獲得多種抗生素抗藥性的能力，這使其臨床危害性尤為突出，特別是在當前抗生素抗藥性問題日益嚴峻的背景下。針對MDR及XDR鮑曼不動桿菌感染，臨床上常需採用聯合治療方案，但這些方案往往療效有限，且即便使用「最後一道防線」藥物，也可能出現抗藥性。因此，開發新型治療策略迫在眉睫。 我們前期的研究表明，鉍(III)的化合物能夠通過抑制金屬-β-內醯胺酶並幹擾鐵穩態（模擬Fe(III)/Zn(II)的特性），恢復大腸桿菌（Escherichia coli）和銅綠假單胞菌（Pseudomonas aeruginosa）對抗生素的敏感性。我們的研究結果凸顯了基於鉍(III)的策略在對抗鮑曼不動桿菌感染方面的潛力，無論是單獨使用還是與臨床常用抗生素聯合使用，均具有應用前景。 基於既有研究成果，並依託我們擁有的鮑曼不動桿菌臨床菌株平台及動物實驗設施（新興傳染病國家重點實驗室），本研究計畫旨在透過靶向鐵穩態機制，開發針對多重抗藥性（MDR）鮑曼不動桿菌的鉍(III)基療法。具體研究內容包括：(i) 設計並合成一系列含巰基配體及模擬鮑曼不動桿菌主要鐵載體（acinetobactin）的單兒茶酚型鐵載體藥物類似物，並製備與這些配體偶聯的鉍(III)配合物；(ii)評估鉍(III)配合物與關鍵抗生素的協同作用，以及鉍(III)-鐵載體藥物類似物在細菌及巨噬細胞感染模型中的療效；(iii) 在肺部感染模型中測試先導化合物的療效，以實現超過80%的細菌清除率；(iv) 最後，將利用各種生物物理技術包括自主開發的金屬蛋白質組學技術闡明其分子機制作用 (如集中在BauA/BasD、FhuE），從而在體外和體內層面優化先導化合物。 本計畫旨在產生新的治療方案，培養青年研究人員，推進鉍(III)的生物化學和藥物化學研究，尤其重要的是，推動基於鉍(III)的療法向臨床轉化。借鑒頭孢地洛和基於鉍(III)/ 鎵(III)的策略在治療大腸桿菌和銅綠假單胞菌方面的成功經驗。我們的長期目標是為耐多藥鮑曼不動桿菌感染提供變革性療法，降低抗藥性相關死亡率，並促進香港及大灣區的生物製藥創新。

17314326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17314326.value: 使可逆Cl₂/Cl⁻電化學於高安全性、低成本離子液體電解質中成為可能：邁向實用化Li/Cl₂電池。

17314326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17314326.value: The rechargeable lithium-chlorine (Li–Cl₂) battery, a high-energy-density storage technology first reported by our group in Nature in 2021, has attracted significant interest due to their exceptionally high theoretical energy density, yet their development has long been hampered by the reliance on toxic, volatile, and highly corrosive thionyl chloride (SOCl₂)-based electrolytes. This project aims to overcome this fundamental limitation through a groundbreaking innovation in the electrolyte system. We propose to develop a novel, safe chloroaluminate ionic liquid electrolyte based on low-cost triethylamine hydrochloride (TEAC) and AlCl₃, buffered with LiCl, ultimately realizing high-performance Li/Cl₂ batteries completely free of SOCl₂. Our preliminary research has successfully validated this approach. We have established a baseline electrolyte of LiCl-buffered AlCl₃/TEAC (1.5:1) ionic liquid and demonstrated that precisely controlling a minimal amount of SOCl₂ as a sacrificial additive enables the in-situ generation of active LiCl (for subsequent Cl₂/Cl⁻ redox reaction during cycling) within the cathode pores during the first discharge. Building on this foundation, the project will systematically pursue several key objectives: optimizing the carbon/polymer cathode for Cl₂ trapping, and AlCl₃/TEAC molar ratio and SOCl₂ dosage to balance ionic conductivity and interfacial stability; addressing the compatibility challenges between the lithium metal anode and the ionic liquid through fluorine/boron-based additives and the construction of artificial SEI layers (e.g., Nafion coatings, ALD-Al₂O₃); elucidating the Cl₂/Cl⁻ redox reaction mechanism in the non-SOCl₂ system using advanced characterization techniques like in-situ Raman and cryo-TEM; and extending the electrolyte platform to sodium/potassium-chlorine battery systems while assessing its industrialization potential. The successful implementation of this project will establish a new technological pathway and a solid scientific foundation for developing safe, efficient, and low-cost alkali metal- Cl₂ batteries, representing a significant step toward the practical application of next-generation high-energy-density storage devices. 可充電鋰-氯（Li–Cl₂）電池是我們課題組於2021年首次在《Nature》上報導的高能量密度儲能技術，因其極高的理論能量密度而備受關注。然而，其發展長期受到依賴有毒、易揮發且具有強腐蝕性的亞硫醯氯（SOCl₂）基電解質的限制。本項目旨在通過電解質體系的突破性創新，從根本上克服這一瓶頸。我們擬開發一種基於低成本三乙胺鹽酸鹽（TEAC）與AlCl₃、並以LiCl作為緩衝劑的新型安全氯鋁酸鹽離子液體電解質，最終實現完全無SOCl₂的高性能Li/Cl₂電池。 我們的初步研究已成功驗證了該方案的有效性。我們建立了以LiCl緩衝的AlCl₃/TEAC（1.5:1）離子液體作為基準電解質，並證明精確控制微量SOCl₂作為犧牲添加劑，可在首次放電過程中於正極孔道內原位生成活性LiCl（用於後續循環中的Cl₂/Cl⁻氧化還原反應）。 在此基礎上，本項目將系統性地開展以下關鍵目標：優化碳/聚合物正極以提升Cl₂的捕獲能力，優化AlCl₃/TEAC摩爾比及SOCl₂用量，以兼顧離子電導率和界面穩定性；通過氟/硼基添加劑及構建人工SEI層（如Nafion塗層、ALD-Al₂O₃）來解決鋰金屬負極與離子液體之間的相容性問題；利用原位拉曼光譜、冷凍透射電鏡（cryo-TEM）等先進表徵技術，闡明非SOCl₂體系中Cl₂/Cl⁻氧化還原反應機理；並將該電解質平台拓展至鈉/鉀-氯電池體系，同時評估其產業化潛力。 本項目的成功實施，將為開發安全、高效、低成本的鹼金屬–Cl₂電池建立新的技術路線和堅實的科學基礎，從而為下一代高能量密度儲能裝置的實際應用邁出重要一步。

17314526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17314526.value: 基於對ENSO與全球氣候遙相關關係認知的深化解析千年ENSO變率

17314526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17314526.value: The El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is a leading ocean-atmospheric mode that affects worldwide weather and climate. Understanding stationarity of ENSO teleconnections and millennial ENSO variability is of crucial importance for weather forecast, climate prediction, and sustainable development under global warming. However, it remains unclear how robust and stable ENSO teleconnection patterns are under external perturbations. The stationarity assumption applied in previous studies may have misled ENSO simulations in Earth System Models (ESMs) and caused uncertainties in ENSO reconstructions based upon paleoclimate proxies from ENSO teleconnection regions. This project aims to: 1) evaluate the stationarity assumption in ENSO teleconnections and unveil the spatiotemporal changes in ENSO teleconnections; 2) reveal the mechanisms driving the changes in ENSO teleconnections and diagnose the abilities of ESMs in simulating ENSO teleconnection patterns. 3) reconstruct millennial ENSO variability from proxy records showing stationary relationships and appraise the perturbations due to non-stationary teleconnections. 4) unveil ENSO responses to external forcings and constrain simulations on ENSO variability. This project will be accomplished in four phases: 1) The stationarity of ENSO teleconnections on climate variables will be quantified by correlation analysis, sensitivity test, and comparison between years with and without external forcings. The results will delineate regions with marked changes in ENSO teleconnections. 2) The mechanisms behind the non-stationarity of ENSO teleconnections will be revealed by separating the impacts of atmospheric circulations and oceanic variability. The findings will be examined in ESMs to reveal the key processes modulating ENSO teleconnections. 3) Proxy records that show stationary relationships with ENSO observations will be selected as predictors for developing a millennial ENSO reconstruction. Alternative ENSO reconstructions incorporating non-stationary proxy records will be compared to appraise the errors in our current understanding. 4) We will quantify ENSO response to external forcings in the millennial reconstruction using superimposed epoch analyses, and new findings will serve as a constraint for benchmarking ENSO simulations and reducing uncertainties in future climate projections. This project is the first attempt to reconstruct ENSO after rigorous test and selection of proxy records showing stationary relationships with ENSO. The results will provide a new perspective to decipher the indigenous ENSO variability and its teleconnections under external forcings. The outcomes of this project will directly foster weather forecast in Hong Kong and many parts of the world. The forced ENSO changes revealed in the millennial reconstruction will facilitate ENSO simulations and guide future climate projections under global warming. 厄爾尼諾-南方濤動（ENSO）是影響全球天氣與氣候的主要海氣耦合模態。理解ENSO遙相關的穩定性及其千年尺度上的變率特徵對於天氣預報、氣候預測以及全球變暖背景下的可持續髮展至關重要。然而，ENSO遙相關模態在外部擾動下的穩健性與穩定性尚不明確。既往研究中採用的穩定性假設可能導緻了地球繫統模型（ESM）中ENSO模擬出現了偏差，也導緻了基於遙相關區域古氣候代用指標的ENSO重建的不確定性。 本項目旨在：1) 評估ENSO遙相關穩定性的假設，揭示ENSO遙相關的時空變化特徵；2) 揭示驅動ENSO遙相關變化的機製，並診斷地球繫統模型（ESM）模擬ENSO遙相關模態的能力；3) 利用表現出穩定關繫的代用記錄重建千年ENSO變率，並評估遙相關非穩定性所誘髮的幹擾；4) 揭示ENSO對外強迫的響應，並用以約束對ENSO變率的模擬。 本項目將分四個階段實施：1) 利用相關性分析、敏感性試驗以及有無外部強迫年份的對比，量化ENSO對氣候變量遙相關的穩定性，識別出ENSO遙相關髮生顯著改變的區域。2) 通過分離大氣環流與海洋變率的影響，揭示ENSO遙相關非穩定性的機製；利用地球繫統模型（ESM）檢驗上述髮現，從而闡明調控ENSO遙相關的關鍵過程。3) 篩選出與ENSO觀測記錄具有穩定關繫的代用指標，用於重構千年ENSO序列；同時，構建並對比納入非穩定代用指標的替代重建方案，以評估當前認知中存在的偏差。4) 採用時序疊加分析法量化千年重建序列中ENSO對外部強迫的響應，將所得結果作爲約束條件，校準ENSO模擬並降低未來氣候預估的不確定性。 本項目繫首次嚐試在嚴格驗証篩選與ENSO具有穩定關繫的代用記錄的基礎上，重建ENSO的變化曆史。研究結果將爲解析ENSO內在變率及其在外部強迫下的遙相關機製提供新視角。本項目成果將直接助力香港及世界各地的天氣預報。基於千年重建所揭示的外強迫驅動下的ENSO變化特徵將有助於改進ENSO模擬，並爲全球變暖背景下的未來氣候預估提供指引。

17500126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17500126.value: 人類與人工智慧邏輯推理能力的大規模客觀比較

17500126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
