The research offers new insights into how governance architecture shapes the evolution of digital platforms and the long-term sustainability of the creator economy. 創作者經濟的快速崛起，深刻改變了數碼平台中創作者、品牌與消費者之間的互動與交易模式。隨着平台愈來愈多採用集中化治理及演算法配對機制以管理合作、提升交易效率，相關制度如何影響市場效率、公平性及各方福利，已成為亟待研究的重要議題。本研究聚焦於創作者經濟中集中化平台治理的行為與福利影響，探討演算法協調如何作用於品牌與網紅／創作者合作的形成、定價與績效。研究將基於某大型數碼平台的海量交易與行為數據，結合準實驗研究設計與結構計量經濟模型，識別集中式演算法配對對市場結果的因果效應。同時，本研究將進一步分析平台層面的干預措施，如排序演算法、流量分配及激勵重置，如何改變創作者與品牌的策略行為，並評估其可能帶來的意外後果，包括市場集中度上升、價值分配不均及創意內容供給變化。透過比較不同創作者類型、產品類別及市場細分中的異質性效應，本研究旨在揭示集中化治理在何種條件下能提升整體福利，同時兼顧公平、透明與包容性。理論上，本研究將融合產業組織、行為經濟學、數碼市場設計與營銷分析等視角，深化對多邊平台中演算法治理如何重新分配價值與影響力的理解，並回應有關演算法公平與效率之間權衡的學術討論。方法上，本研究將完善評估演算法干預的因果識別框架，為分析複雜數碼生態系統提供嚴謹的實證工具。實務上，研究成果將為平台營運者及監管機構提供政策與管理啟示，協助其設計更具效率、包容性及可問責性的治理架構，推動創作者—品牌生態系統的可持續發展，並促進演算法決策在數碼市場中的負責任應用。

17507426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17507426.value: 大模型驱动的因果推断：方法与实证

17507426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17507426.value: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are the gold standard for estimating treatment effects and are widely used in product management. Yet they often fail to explain why interventions work, for whom, or how effects generalize. To address this, we propose a novel framework that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) with Bayesian inference, combining natural-language reasoning with statistical rigor to identify, interpret, and generalize causal mechanisms from large-scale historical experimental data. This project aims to unleash the value of AI—specifically LLMs—from experimental data, opening a new era of AI-driven causal inference that advances business research and practice. Our framework introduces two complementary agents: a reasoning agent that generates interpretable hypotheses about potential causal pathways or factors, and a feedback agent that evaluates these hypotheses through Bayesian updating. Within this multi-agent structure, Bayesian inference serves as the coordinating principle that continuously updates the credibility of the reasoning agent’s hypotheses in light of new data, transforming subjective conjectures into probabilistically grounded causal beliefs. This design converts the open-ended reasoning capacity of LLMs into a disciplined inferential process rooted in probability theory. To ensure validity, users are first partitioned into heterogeneous groups with stable and consistent treatment effects in certain area, enabling the discovery of subgroup-specific causal pathways. Because individual-level inference is infeasible—each individual yields only one observable outcome—group-level inference preserves interpretability while maintaining statistical credibility. Subgroup posteriors are then aggregated through hierarchical modeling to derive population-level causal insights, allowing both fine-grained understanding and scalable generalization. Empirical validation will use extensive WeChat experimental data on testing content preferences, focusing on two goals: (1) assessing whether the discovered subgroup-specific causal factors can serve as effective user features that improve predictive accuracy in downstream tasks, and (2) evaluating whether subgroup- and population-level inferences can predict outcomes of new interventions. Beyond methodological development, the project will produce open-source software, scholarly publications, and industry collaborations to ensure practical relevance and replicability. By combining the reasoning flexibility of LLMs with the inferential rigor of Bayesian methods, this research advances causal inference methodologically, deepens empirical understanding of heterogeneous treatment effects, and establishes a generalizable framework for interpretable and adaptive causal discovery. The expected outcomes will benefit both academic research—by linking causal inference with language-based reasoning—and industry practice—by enabling organizations to move from measuring what works to understanding why it works and predicting what will work. 摘要 随机对照试验（RCTs）是估计处理效应的黄金标准，并被广泛应用于产品管理。然而，它们往往无法解释干预为何有效、对谁有效，以及效应如何推广。为解决这一问题，我们提出一个新颖的框架，将大型语言模型（LLMs）与贝叶斯推断相结合，融合自然语言推理与统计严谨性，从大规模历史实验数据中识别、解释并推广因果机制。本项目旨在从实验数据中释放 AI，特别是 LLMs 的价值，开启 AI 驱动因果推断的新阶段，从而推动商业研究与实践的发展。 我们的框架引入两个互补的智能体：一个推理智能体，用于生成关于潜在因果路径或影响因素的可解释假设；一个反馈智能体，用于通过贝叶斯更新对这些假设进行评估。在这一多智能体结构中，贝叶斯推断发挥协调作用，根据新数据持续更新推理智能体所提出假设的可信度，将主观推测转化为具有概率基础的因果信念。该设计将 LLMs 开放式的推理能力转化为一个植根于概率论的规范化推断过程。为确保有效性，我们首先将用户划分为在特定方面具有稳定且一致处理效应的异质性群体，从而发现子群体特定的因果路径。由于个体层面的推断并不可行，因为每个个体只能产生一个可观测结果，群体层面的推断既能保持可解释性，又能维持统计可信度。随后，我们通过层级建模聚合子群体的后验分布，以推导总体层面的因果洞见，从而同时实现细粒度理解与可扩展推广。 实证验证将使用大规模微信实验数据，重点考察内容偏好测试，并围绕两个目标展开：（1）评估所发现的子群体特定因果因素能否作为有效的用户特征，用于提升下游任务中的预测准确性；（2）评估子群体与总体层面的推断能否预测新干预的结果。除方法论发展外，本项目还将产出开源软件、学术论文和行业合作，以确保其实践相关性与可复现性。 通过将 LLMs 的推理灵活性与贝叶斯方法的推断严谨性相结合，本研究将在方法论层面推进因果推断，深化对异质性处理效应的实证理解，并建立一个可推广的、可解释且自适应的因果发现框架。预期成果将同时惠及学术研究与行业实践：在学术上，本研究将因果推断与基于语言的推理相连接；在实践中，它将帮助组织从衡量“什么有效”迈向理解“为何有效”并预测“什么将会有效”。

17507526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17507526.value: 土壤污染信息披露与住房市场动态：来自全国性实地实验的证据

17507526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17507526.value: Soil pollution is an increasingly serious but often overlooked environmental problem. Unlike air or water pollution, soil contamination is usually invisible and poorly monitored. Public awareness remains low, and information about polluted sites is fragmented across government documents, short-lived local announcements, and technical reports. As a result, this information rarely reaches the general public or the housing market, even when the pollution is serious. Such informational gaps can delay effective responses, weaken incentives for cleanup, and perpetuate inequities in exposure and property values. This project investigates how making soil pollution information more transparent influences decisions in the housing market, where information and trust play central roles. We focus on China, where we have gathered a new, nationwide database of soil contamination sites—the most comprehensive of its kind to date—by compiling and cleaning data from hundreds of official and semi-official sources. Although these data are, in principle, public, they remain practically inaccessible to ordinary citizens. To understand the behavioral and market consequences of transparency, we will conduct a large-scale randomized controlled trial (RCT) in collaboration with two major online housing platforms. We will randomize cities into high and low treatment intensity groups, and within cities, assign neighborhoods to different disclosure treatments that vary in the recipient and visibility of pollution information: public release to all platform users, private information to homeowners, and private information to brokers. This design allows us to identify both direct and spillover effects and to study how partial transparency shapes expectations and strategic interactions. Using platform data and follow-up surveys, we will track outcomes such as property prices, listing and transaction patterns, buyer engagement, and information sharing behavior. The results will provide rare causal evidence on how environmental information affects housing market functioning. By revealing how different forms of disclosure can amplify or mitigate public concern, this study will inform more effective environmental governance. The findings will be valuable for policymakers seeking to strengthen risk communication, enhance regulatory credibility, and promote safer, more transparent urban land markets. 土壤污染是一个日益严重但却常常被忽视的环境问题。与空气或水污染不同，土壤污染通常是隐形的，且缺乏有效监测。公众意识仍然较低，关于污染场地的信息分散在政府文件、短暂的地方公告和技术报告中。因此，即使污染严重，这些信息也很少能传达给公众或房地产市场。这种信息缺失会延误有效的应对措施，削弱清理工作的积极性，并加剧暴露风险和房产价值方面的不平等。 本项目旨在研究提高土壤污染信息的透明度如何影响房地产市场的决策，因为信息和信任在房地产市场中扮演着至关重要的角色。我们以中国为例，通过收集和清理来自数百个官方和半官方来源的数据，建立了一个全新的全国性土壤污染场地数据库——迄今为止最全面的同类数据库。尽管这些数据原则上是公开的，但普通民众实际上仍然难以获取。 为了解信息透明度对行为和市场的影响，我们将与在线住房平台合作，开展一项大规模随机对照试验（RCT）。我们将随机把城市分为高处理强度组和低处理强度组，并在每个城市内，将各个社区分配到不同的信息披露处理方案中，这些方案在污染信息的接收者和可见性方面有所不同：向所有平台用户公开、向房主提供私密信息、以及向经纪人提供私密信息。这种设计使我们能够识别直接效应和溢出效应，并研究部分信息透明度如何影响预期和策略性互动。 我们将利用平台数据和后续调查，追踪诸如房价、房源挂牌和交易模式、买家参与度以及信息共享行为等结果。研究结果将提供关于环境信息如何影响住房市场运作的难得的因果证据。通过揭示不同形式的信息披露如何放大或缓解公众的担忧，这项研究将为更有效的环境治理提供参考。研究结果对于寻求加强风险沟通、提升监管公信力以及促进更安全、更透明的城市土地市场的政策制定者来说具有重要价值。

17507926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17507926.value: 財政政策，債券市場流動性和匯率：宏觀金融關係

17507926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17507926.value: This project studies how fiscal policies impact exchange rate via bond market liquidity and convenience yield. We start with empirically documenting the exchange rate response to fiscal shocks and examine the underlying economic mechanisms. We highlight the role of dominant currencies in shaping how fiscal policy impacts exchange rates. We then develop a dynamic stochastic general equilibrium model that features frictional bond market liquidity through search and matching mechanism to interpret the empirical pattern. We emphasize the importance of the micro foundation of convenience yield by showing the feedback loop from convenience yield to exchange rate, macro aggregates, international capital flows and fiscal policy. Not capturing such feedback loop would lead to biased evaluation of fiscal policy. 當下的時代，各國債務高企，使得研究財政政策與匯率之間的關係成為最重要的問題之一。在學術文獻中，財政政策如何同時影響匯率和宏觀經濟並未被充分研究闡述。本課題首先使用最新的局部投影方法研究美國和其他發達國家（例如英國）的匯率如何對財政政策做出反應。儘管美元和英鎊匯率在減稅以後的變化方向相似，但其持久性卻有差異。美元的變化持續數個季度，而英鎊的變化僅持續數天。我們認為，它們的差異來自於美元儲備貨幣的地位。 研究了匯率對財政政策反應之後，我們研究其中的經濟學機制，亦即本課題的主要內容。我們計畫研究債券的便利收益、市場流動性、宏觀經濟活動和國際資本流動對財政政策的反應。這一分析有助於我們設計準確、適合的經濟模型來研究財政政策與匯率之間的關係。 我們試圖建立一個定量的開放宏觀經濟模型，其中包括有摩擦的債券市場交易和便利收益，並以此模型來解釋我們發現的實證結果。便利收益和債券市場流動性由一個搜尋匹配模型內生產生。這一微觀基礎使我們得以對匯率反作用於宏觀經濟活動和財政政策的放大作用進行建模。當一國減稅時，債務供給增加，便利收益下降，本幣貶值，刺激經濟，使經濟有更多的減稅空間。我們試圖展示這一放大作用對於評估財政政策是至關重要的。

17508126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17508126.value: 了解與優化數碼平台上數量選擇工具的視覺佈局

17508126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17508126.value: Ms Li, Xinyi Prof Sevilla, Julio

17508126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17508126.value: Purchase quantity (i.e., how many units of a product to purchase) is an important shopping decision that consumers regularly make. Accordingly, to facilitate purchase quantity decisions, online shopping interfaces provide quantity selection tools, which are in various formats, such as “plus/minus” buttons and “up/down” buttons. As two common and equivalent visual formats of quantity selection tools on digital retail platforms, “plus/minus” buttons and “up/down” buttons are essentially the same, such that consumers can incrementally adjust a quantity by one unit every time they click on a button. Despite such an essential commonality, we propose that “plus/minus” buttons and “up/down” buttons lead to different decision outcomes. Specifically, we predict that compared to “plus/minus” buttons, “up/down” buttons will result in fewer product units that consumers purchase. This effect is explained by the greater perceived effort associated with clicking on “up” buttons. Based on this perceived effort mechanism, we further predict that the negative effect of “up/down” buttons (vs. “plus/minus” buttons) on the purchase quantity of product units will be attenuated on mobile devices, for energy-boosting products, and for “up/down” buttons with a lower color saturation or a hollow visual structure. Theoretically, by revealing how “plus/minus” buttons and “up/down” buttons as two common and equivalent visual formats of quantity selection tools affect consumers’ purchase quantity decisions, the proposed research is expected to contribute novel insights into how visuals and numbers interplay with each other in impacting consumer behavior on digital platforms. Managerially, the proposed research develops an integrative and comprehensive managing framework of the visual design of quantity selection tools on digital platforms. First, the proposed research uncovers a disadvantage of “up/down” buttons over “plus/minus” buttons, in terms of reducing purchase quantity. Taking it one step further, the proposed research provides theory-informed, easy-to-implement solutions to optimize the visual design of “up/down” buttons to mitigate this disadvantage. 購買數量（即購買多少件產品）是消費者經常需要作出的重要購物決定。因此，為協助消費者決定購買數量，網上購物介面提供不同形式的數量選擇工具，例如“加/減”按鈕和“上/下”按鈕。 作為數碼零售平台上兩種常見且功能相同的數量選擇工具視覺格式，“加/減”按鈕和“上/下”按鈕本質上相同，消費者可透過每次點擊按鈕將數量逐個單位調整。儘管存在這種基本共通點，本研究提出“加/減”按鈕和“上/下”按鈕會導致不同的決策結果。 具體而言，本研究預測與“加/減”按鈕相比，“上/下”按鈕會令消費者購買的產品數量減少。此效應可透過點擊“上”按鈕所需感知的較大努力來解釋。基於這種感知努力機制，本研究進一步預測，“上/下”按鈕（相對“加/減”按鈕）對產品購買數量的負面影響，會在流動裝置上、針對能量補充型產品，以及當“上/下”按鈕的色彩飽和度較低或具有空心視覺結構時減弱。 從理論上講，本研究通過揭示“加/減”按鈕和“上/下”按鈕這兩種常見且功能相同的數量選擇工具視覺格式如何影響消費者的購買數量決策，有望為視覺元素與數字如何在數碼平台上相互作用影響消費者行為提供新見解。 在管理實踐方面，本研究為數碼平台上數量選擇工具的視覺設計建立了一個綜合全面的管理框架。首先，本研究揭示了“上/下”按鈕在減少購買數量方面相比“加/減”按鈕的劣勢。進一步而言，本研究提供了基於理論、易於實施的解決方案，以優化“上/下”按鈕的視覺設計來減輕此劣勢。

17508326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17508326.value: 基于绩效透明度的跨期参照点设计

17508326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17508326.value: Employees and service users frequently receive performance feedback relative to their own past performance or to that of their peers. While such feedback can be motivating—especially when individuals aim to reclaim their previously high performance or catch up with others—it can also be demotivating when the opposite occurs. This raises two key questions: When does performance transparency (i.e., performance feedback relative to others) facilitate performance improvement? And how should a service provider dynamically balance relative feedback to self and others over time to enhance performance? In this project, we develop a dynamic model to identify optimal feedback policies in order to improve long-term performance by dynamically shaping users’ references through personal performance histories and the performance of peers. We find that users tend to reduce effort when their own past performance (intrapersonal reference) is consistently strong but increase effort when peers (interpersonal reference) are performing well. Given this, we conjecture that managers should focus on providing intrapersonal feedback when users are performing well and shift toward interpersonal feedback—by, for example, launching real-time leaderboards in a sales competition—when users are underperforming. Ultimately, this project aims to provide actionable guidance on the intertemporal design of performance transparency, with broader implications for user grouping decisions and context-specific feedback strategies. 员工和服务用户经常会收到有关其表现的反馈，这些反馈通常以其自身过去的表现或同伴的表现为参照。此类反馈可能具有激励作用，尤其是当个体希望重回自己过去的高水平，或努力追赶他人时；但另一方面，它也可能削弱个体的积极性。由此引出两个关键问题：在何种情况下，绩效透明度—即提供相对于他人的绩效反馈—能够促进绩效改善？服务提供者又应如何随时间动态平衡以自身和他人为参照的反馈，从而提升长期绩效？ 在本项目中，我们构建了一个动态模型，通过个人绩效历史和同伴绩效动态塑造用户的参照点，进而识别能够改善长期表现的最优反馈政策。我们的研究发现，当用户自身过去的表现—即个体内参照—持续较好时，他们往往会降低努力水平；而当同伴—即个体间参照—表现优异时，他们反而会增加努力水平。基于这一发现，我们推测，管理者应当在用户表现良好时侧重提供个体内反馈；而在用户表现不佳时，则应转向个体间反馈，例如在销售竞赛中启用实时排行榜。 最终，本项目旨在为绩效透明度的跨期设计提供具有可操作性的管理建议，并进一步揭示其对用户分组决策以及情境化反馈策略的广泛启示。

17509726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17509726.value: In economics, understanding how decisions and outcomes change with underlying factors—such as costs, technologies, or information—is crucial. A key tool is monotone comparative statics, which predicts how optimal choices or equilibrium outcomes shift as conditions change. In Bayesian environments, economists typically rely on the monotone likelihood ratio (MLR) order: If a piece of news is “better” than another under MLR, updating beliefs with it leads to higher confidence in favorable outcomes—that is, the updated belief is higher under first-order stochastic dominance (FOSD). This supports many applications, such as auctions and contracting, where higher confidence directly translates to decisions like bidding more or hiring a candidate. However, MLR and FOSD have limitations. Many real-world problems involve risks or uncertainties that are not captured by simple “higher is better” logic. For instance, regulators care about avoiding financial crashes (lower-tail risks), behavioral models account for irrational preferences, and fairness policies might prioritize balancing outcomes rather than maximizing averages. These require comparing beliefs and distributions using criteria beyond FOSD, such as higher-order stochastic dominance (which considers risk dispersion) or quantile-based rankings. MLR cannot handle these scenarios, limiting its usefulness. This project aims to develop a unifying framework that starts from any desired way to rank updated beliefs (for example, “less downside risk” or “smaller tail probability”) and then constructs a corresponding way to rank pieces of evidence so that, no matter what someone initially believed, seeing a “better” signal moves their updated beliefs in the desired direction. For example, if a policymaker evaluates policies by a quantile‑based order, we identify signal properties that guarantee this ranking regardless of prior beliefs, enabling an advocate to structure evidence accordingly. For example, if a policymaker ranks policies by their worst-case outcomes (a quantile-based order), the framework would identify the signal properties that guarantee this ranking holds regardless of prior beliefs, enabling an advocate who does not know the policymaker's prior beliefs to structure evidence accordingly. In essence, the research expands the economist’s toolkit to tailor comparisons of signals and beliefs across diverse objectives—portfolio choice, policy design, and equitable decision‑making. We aim to deliver practical, checkable conditions and to develop algorithms for inducing monotone updates in settings where traditional methods fall short. 許多經濟與政策問題都在探討，當人們收到「更好」的資訊時，決策會如何改變。一項經典法則（單調似然比，MLR）保證了利好消息會引導人們以一致的方式提高期望，這有助預測拍賣、合約設計與資訊設計等領域中的選擇。然而，現實世界中的目標往往超越了單純的「更高期望」。監管機構可能更關心如何降低下行風險或尾部損失；分析師可能針對分位數；而一些行為模型所看重的結果，並無法簡單地以「越多越好」來排序。在這些情況下，MLR 可能會顯得太過狹隘。 本項目旨在開發一個統一的框架，從任何期望的更新信念排序方式（例如「較少的下行風險」或「較小的尾部機率」）出發，進而建構出相對應的證據排序方式；如此一來，無論某人最初的信念為何，只要看到「更好」的訊號，就能使其更新後的信念朝預期的方向移動。該提案表明，對於更新後信念的任何目標排序，都存在一個最大、最具資訊量的訊號排序，能夠在所有初始信念中一致地產生該結果。這將關於 MLR 的經典結果作為一個特例包含在內，並為考量風險、尾部、分位數以及更廣泛偏好模型的比較靜態（comparative-statics）工具打開了大門。 在技術層面上，該方法將訊號標準化，使每個訊號都能被視為一種信念，從而揭示了該理論所利用的貝葉斯法則（Bayes' rule）中一個簡單的代數結構。在此基礎上，這項工作旨在提供實用且可檢驗的條件，並為與隨機佔優（stochastic dominance）、多重效用表示法（multi-utility representations）相關的排序，以及像是對收到相同證據的候選人進行公平排序等應用，開發出演算法。預期的成果是提供一套廣泛適用的工具包，用於遠超越傳統 MLR 設定、具穩健性且與政策相關的推論。

17600226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17600226.value: 使用經顱直流電刺激改善重大人生負面事件後的心理韌性：效應、多模態機制及個體層面調節因素

17600226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17600226.value: Major life stress (MLS) is a primary cause of mental health issues. We previously showed a 63% prevalence of MLS and elevated mood symptoms in Hong Kong following the COVID-19 pandemic. Thus, it is critical to enhance individuals' resilience, defined as the capacity to withstand the negative impact of MLS and maintain good mental health. Existing intervention studies on resilience suffer from the important limitations of inconsistent definitions and measurements of resilience that fail to reflect the outcomes of stress coping; these limitations also contribute to the discrepant findings across studies. Transcranial direct current stimulation (TDCS) has emerged as an effective, inexpensive and safe neuromodulation method for improving emotion functions and mental health. While limited evidence supports the effectiveness of TDCS on resilience, very few studies have examined whether the effect can be long-lasting. Also, the emotion and neural mechanisms underpinning the TDCS effect, and individual-level factors that modulate the TDCS effect, remained unclear. Therefore, we propose a randomized controlled trial to test both immediate and persistent 10-session TDCS effects in improving MLS resilience, which utilizes an outcome-based approach that defines and measures resilience as a person's emotion health outcomes following her/his specific MLS history. Since both positive and negative emotion systems are implicated in MLS and resilience, we will study whether resilience is enhanced via improved function of either the positive or the negative emotion and brain pathways, which are respectively triggered by TDCS on the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (lDLPFC) or on the right ventrolateral prefrontal cortex (rVLPFC). We will also test whether individuals' baseline emotion functions, locus-of-control style, and social support would modulate the TDCS effects. Adults (N=207, 23-45 years, both sexes) with MLS will be screened and randomly allocated to the lDLPFC TDCS, rVLPFC TDCS or sham control group. At each of 4 timepoints (baseline, post-intervention, 1-month and 3-month follow-up), participants will complete questionnaires and tasks that assess MLS, emotion symptoms, emotion functions and the associated neural patterns, and psychosocial variables. At each timepoint, a resilience index will be computed for each participant based on MLS number and emotion symptoms. The TDCS effects on resilience, emotion functions and neural patterns will be evaluated using mixed-effect linear and latent growth modelling. The mediating effects of emotion and neural variables will be tested using longitudinal mediation analysis and cross-lagged structural equation modelling. The modulating effects of baseline emotion functions and psychosocial variables will be tested using moderation analysis. 重大人生負面事件（Major life stress, MLS）是引發心理健康問題的主因之一。我們過往研究揭示在COVID-19新冠疫情後，香港的MLS發生率高達63%，且居民的情緒症狀水平上升。因此，提升個體的心理韌性（即其承受MLS負面影響並維持良好心理健康的能力）至關重要。現今已有的心理韌性干預研究存在重要不足，主要包括對心理韌性的定義與測量方式不一致；並且，這些定義與測量方式未能反映個體應對MLS後的情緒健康結果（mental health outcome)）。經顱直流電刺激（transcranial direct current stimulation, TDCS）已成為一種有效、低成本且安全的神經調節干預手段，可用於改善情感功能與心理健康。雖然有限證據支持TDCS改善心理韌性的效應，但極少研究檢視此效應是否能夠持久。此外，支撐TDCS效應的情感與神經機制，以及調節TDCS效果的個體層面因素，尚未明確。 因此，我們提出一項隨機對照試驗（RCT），旨在測試十次TDCS干預對改善MLS心理韌性的即刻與持續效果。本試驗將韌性定義並測量為個體在特定MLS經歷後所展現的情緒健康結果。由於正向與負向情感系統均參與MLS及心理韌性過程，我們將探討TDCS是否通過改善正向或負向情緒調節及相關大腦通路功能而增強心理韌性；這些大腦通路分別由左側背外側前額葉皮質（lDLPFC）或右側腹外側前額葉皮質（rVLPFC）的TDCS刺激所觸發。我們也將檢驗個體的基線情感功能、控制取向（locus-of-control style）及社會支持是否會調節TDCS效應。該試驗將篩選有MLS經歷的成年人（總樣本量為207，年齡23-45歲，男女皆有），並將合資格人士隨機分配至lDLPFC TDCS組、rVLPFC TDCS組或偽刺激對照組。該試驗共包括4個時間點。在每個時間點（基線、干預後、一個月隨訪及三個月隨訪），參與者將完成問卷與電腦任務範式以評估其過往MLS歷史、情緒症狀、情感功能及相關腦神經模式，以及社會心理功能。在每個時間點，我們將基於每位參與者過往經歷的MLS事件數量及其當前的情緒症狀為其計算心理韌性指數。我們將使用混合效應線性模型及潛在成長模型評估TDCS對心理韌性、情感功能和腦神經模式的干預效應，並採用縱貫中介分析及交叉滯後結構方程模型檢驗情感和腦神經因素對干預效應的中介作用。我們還將使用調節分析手段檢驗基線情緒功能與社會心理因素對TDCS干預的調節效應。

17600526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17600526.value: 描繪自發性神經動態活動與感官及認知神經反應之間的關係

17600526.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17600526.value: Dr Lorenz, Romy Prof Northoff, Georg Prof Zhou, Changsong

17600526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17600526.value: Brain activity across different scales exhibits patterns indicative of active, self-coordinating dynamic systems. A defining feature of such systems is that their response to external input is jointly shaped by both the input itself and the brain's ongoing states. This principle suggests that variability in brain responses is not mere noise but a mechanistic window into neural function, with direct implications for understanding cognition and developing cognitive enhancement technologies. Substantial research has established a correlation between ongoing brain activity, evoked responses, and cognitive performance, substantiating the link between spontaneous neural dynamics and cognitive functions. However, we have identified three unresolved issues in this field. First, the correlational analysis of neurophysiological signals is complicated by an intrinsic signal dependence between ongoing activity and evoked responses. The statistical relationship between pre-stimulus brain states and post-stimulus responses is confounded by the simple continuity of spontaneous neural activity across time windows, creating potential circularity in the analysis. Second, the brain's response is not a unitary signal, but a composite of multiple sub-components generated by distinct functional systems. This complexity obscures the specific sources of variability in measured responses. Third, a circulatory interaction exists between ongoing brain activity and neural cognitive responses: a response may generate a carry-over effect that influences the ongoing signals preceding the next trial. This issue is more pronounced in experiments with short inter-stimulus intervals (ISIs). To address these challenges, this project will employ a multi-method approach using human EEG/MEG and neuron spike recordings in macaques. The proposed project is structured around three key aims: 1) Develop and apply advanced signal processing methods to examine the relationship between ongoing dynamics and neural responses while controlling for intrinsic signal dependence. 2) Decompose neural responses into distinct sub-components associated with different functional and cognitive processes to investigate their individual relationships with spontaneous dynamics. 3) Implement an online neural state-dependent experiment to actively test these relationships by triggering stimuli based on specific pre-stimulus brain states with sufficiently long ISI. This project brings together experts in neural signal analysis, dynamical systems theory, brain-computer interfaces, and cognitive neuroscience. The findings are expected to elucidate the fundamental principles of neural dynamics and identify key determinants of cognitive variability, providing a foundation for future research on cognitive enhancement. 不同尺度上的大腦活動都展現出特徵，顯示其為活躍且自我協調的動態系統。這類系統的核心特徵在於，它們對外部輸入的反應是由輸入本身與大腦當前的持續狀態共同塑造成的。這一原理表明，大腦反應的變異性並非單純的雜訊，而是探視神經功能機制的一扇窗口，對於理解認知及發展認知增強技術具有直接的啟示。大量研究已證實持續的大腦活動、誘發反應與認知表現之間存在相關性，從而支持了自發性神經動態與認知功能之間的聯繫。然而，我們在該領域中發現了三個尚未解決的問題。首先，神經生理訊號的相關性分析受到持續活動與誘發反應之間「內在訊號依賴性」的干擾。刺激前大腦狀態與刺激後反應之間的統計關係，會受到自發性神經活動在不同時間窗之間單純連續性的混淆，從而在分析中產生潛在的循環論證。其次，大腦的反應並非單一訊號，而是由不同功能系統產生的多個子成分所組成的複合體。這種複雜性模糊了測量反應中變異性的具體來源。第三，持續的大腦活動與神經認知反應之間存在循環互動：某次反應可能會產生殘留效應，進而影響下一次測試前的持續訊號。在刺激間隔較短的實驗中，這個問題尤為顯著。為了應對這些挑戰，本項目將採用多種方法相結合的策略，利用人類腦電圖/腦磁圖以及獼猴的神經元放電記錄進行研究。擬定的項目圍繞三個核心目標展開：開發並應用先進的訊號處理方法，以在控制內在訊號依賴性的同時，檢視持續動態與神經反應之間的關係。將神經反應分解為與不同功能及認知過程相關的獨立子成分，以探討它們各自與自發性動態的關係。實施線上神經狀態依賴性實驗，透過在特定的刺激前大腦狀態下觸發刺激（並保持足夠長的刺激間隔），來主動測試這些關係。本項目匯聚了神經訊號分析、動態系統理論、腦機介面及認知神經科學領域的專家。研究結果有望闡明神經動態的基本原理，並找出認知變異性的關鍵決定因素，為未來認知增強的研究奠定基礎。

17600726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17600726.value: 隱形安置：二十世紀後期香港越南難民的地方創造

17600726.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17600726.value: Prof Phu, Thy Dr Tran, Ann Ngoc

17600726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17600726.value: Ever since Hong Kong’s founding in 1841, successive waves of migrants and refugees have remade the city. Until recently, much of the scholarship on this topic has focused on the circular migration flows that have always connected mainland China and Hong Kong. Building on the PI’s current research that explores how the Vietnamese boat people left their mark on Hong Kong in the late 1970s and early 1980s as unskilled workers in local factories, this project tracks forward to broach the thorny question of local resettlement. It asks: what happened to the Vietnamese boat people who resettled in Hong Kong? How did they carve out a place for themselves in a city that, by the mid-90s, was keen to put this 20-year crisis in its rear-view mirror? Motivated by a dearth of studies on the Vietnamese boat people community in post-handover Hong Kong, the PI will combine conventional archival research with public history and digital humanities methods to track the production of a Vietnamese sense of place across the city’s (sub)urban landscapes. This project takes as its starting point the fact that, unlike Kowloon City’s “Little Thailand” or the “Sunday gatherings” of Filipina and Indonesian domestic workers, resettled boat people have not claimed urban space in similarly obvious ways. This project hypothesizes that these decentralized geographies of refugee resettlement cannot be understood in isolation from a broader politics of difference-making that unfolded along racialized, classed, and gendered lines. To test this hypothesis, this project considers how resettled boat people accessed subsidized housing; navigated various forms of racial and ethnic stigmatization; and exploited gendered household arrangements to stake a claim on the city. Drawing on material sourced from archives in Hong Kong, London, and Los Angeles, as well as 15 oral history interviews with boat people and their descendants, this project will advance scholarly and public conversations on migrant and refugee place-making in Hong Kong. By foregrounding the everyday survival practices that made it possible for resettled boat people to establish a foothold, it further unsettles the long-standing distinctions between migrants and refugees that have historically defined scholarly work and policy interventions on the topic. In addition to providing valuable insights on the challenges of refugee integration to local non-governmental organizations, this project will lay the groundwork for future studies that will expand it to other Pacific Rim contexts. 自從1841年香港成立以來，接連不斷的移民和難民浪潮一直在重塑這座城市。在此之前，有關這個主題的學術研究多集中於一直連結中國大陸與香港的循環移民流動。本項目基於研究員目前的研究，探討1970年代末至1980年代初越南船民作為本地工廠的非技術工人，如何在香港留下痕跡，並進一步追蹤他們的安置問題，探討：那些在香港重新安置的越南船民究竟發生了什麼？他們又是如何在一個到90年代中期已經著手將這場長達20年的危機拋在腦後的城市中為自己找到位置的？ 由於缺乏關於香港回歸後越南船民社群的研究，研究員將結合傳統的檔案研究、公共歷史以及數字人文的方法，追蹤這個社群在城市（次）都市景觀中形成越南認同感的過程。本項目的出發點是，與九龍城的“泰國村”或菲律賓和印尼家政工人的“星期日聚會”不同，重新安置的船民並未以同樣明顯的方式聲索城市空間。該項假設這些分散的難民安置地理空間，不能孤立於更廣泛的身份政治中理解，這些政治沿著種族化、階級化和性別化的線索展開。為驗證這一假設，項目將考察重新安置的船民如何獲得補貼住房；如何應對各種形式的種族和族裔歧視；以及如何利用性別化的家庭安排來爭取在城市中的立足點。 本研究將利用來自香港、倫敦和洛杉磯的檔案資料，以及15次與船民及其後代的口述歷史訪談，推動學術界與公共社會對香港移民與難民地方創造的討論。通過突出這些重新安置的船民得以立足的日常生存策略，進一步挑戰長久以來在學術研究與政策干預中對移民與難民的區分。此外，該研究將為非政府組織提供關於難民融合挑戰的寶貴見解，並為未來擴展到其他太平洋沿岸地區的相關研究奠定基礎。

17601426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17601426.value: 清華簡虛詞研究：古文字學、語法學與文獻學的跨學科考察

17601426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17601426.value: 清華簡於2008年入藏清華大學，總數約2500枚，內容涵蓋經、史、子多類文獻。除少數篇章有今本對照外，多為失傳已久的佚籍。清華簡年代屬於戰國中晚期，除了部分內容年代可能較早之外，反映的語言現象大致屬於東周時期的上古中期漢語。隨著近世紀地下文獻大量出土，學者普遍認為出土材料年代相對明確，可避免傳抄過程的竄改與錯譌，能夠較準確反映當時的語言面貌。楚簡文獻陸續出土促使研究者開始重視其語法價值，但相較甲金文，楚簡語法研究尚處於初步階段，特別是清華簡發現較晚，相關研究較少。本計劃從跨學科視野，結合古文字學、語法學、文獻學，對清華簡虛詞作全面研究。本計劃從古文字研究，分析清華簡虛詞的字詞關係，解決文字釋讀，結合語法學考察其語法功能和體系，追蹤虛詞的歷時變化，揭示楚方言特點，探討其時代與地域特徵，展示虛詞與語體的關係。本計劃在虛詞研究基礎上，探討清華簡文獻的思想內容、文本的地域與歷史來源，以及文獻形成問題。 The Tsinghua Bamboo Slips, acquired by Tsinghua University in 2008, comprise approximately 2,500 bamboo strips representing a diverse range of literary genres, including Confucian canonical texts, historical records, and philosophical treatises. Most of these manuscripts consist of works that are absent from the extant literature, with only a few parallels to transmitted texts. As such, they offer unprecedented insights into early Chinese history. Dated primarily to the late Warring States period, although some contents might be compiled earlier, the linguistic features reflected in these slips predominantly correspond to Middle Old Chinese, the stage of the language used during the Eastern Zhou period. Alongside the significant discovery of unearthed manuscripts in the twentieth century, scholars have widely acknowledged that these excavated texts provide relatively precise chronological dating and are less affected by scribal corruptions that often accompany transmission over time. Consequently, they serve as more reliable sources for studying the linguistic phenomena and characteristics of their period. However, compared to oracle bone and bronze inscriptions, the grammatical analysis of Chu bamboo texts remains in its nascent stages, especially concerning the Tsinghua Bamboo Slips, which were discovered relatively recently. This project employs an interdisciplinary methodology, combining paleography, grammar, and philology to systematically analyze the grammatical system of function words in the Tsinghua Bamboo Slips. The research will begin with paleographic analysis to examine the relationship between graph and word forms, addressing interpretive challenges related to the decipherment and annotation of the scripts associated with function words. Following this, the project will investigate the grammatical properties of these function words to clarify their roles within the manuscripts’ grammatical framework and identify diachronic and regional features. This analysis aims to shed light on linguistic evolution and the unique characteristics of the Chu dialect. Additionally, the study will explore how function words relate to stylistic and register variations. It will also enhance our understanding of the manuscripts’ intellectual content through the analysis of the grammatical meanings of these function words. By elucidating their regional, temporal, and stylistic distinctions, the research seeks to provide insights into the texts’ regional origins and historical stratification, ultimately contributing to broader knowledge about the formation, development, and transmission of early Chinese writings.

17601726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17601726.value: 社區為基礎的參與式研究（CBPR）在提升老年人精神健康知識的成效

17601726.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17601726.value: Prof Choi, Edmond Pui Hang Prof Chui, Cheryl Hiu-kwan Dr Fong, Daniel Yee Tak Prof Leung, Kiu Yi Dara Prof Liu, Tianyin Prof Lu, Shiyu Prof Lum, Terry Yat Sang

17601726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17601726.value: Community-based participatory research (CBPR) is a bottom-up approach that enhances the validity and relevance of interventions by integrating community practices and cultural knowledge into evidence-based strategies to address locally identified issues. However, most existing theoretical frameworks and empirical studies originate from the United States, anglophone countries, and among racial minority populations. As CBPR is inherently culturally sensitive, its applicability and effectiveness within the Hong Kong context, particularly among community-dwelling older adults, remain uncertain. Two key research gaps are identified. First, current theoretical paradigms developed in the U.S. may not be directly applicable in Hong Kong due to significant cultural differences. Second, existing mental health literacy interventions in Hong Kong have predominantly employed top-down approaches, with limited utilization of CBPR methodologies. Although CBPR is increasingly used globally to promote mental health literacy, there is a lack of systematic evaluation of its effectiveness and overall impact. This study aims to address these gaps with two phases. Phase 1 involves co-creating a localized CBPR model with multiple stakeholders in Hong Kong. This will be achieved through co-creation workshops and a Delphi survey involving 30 local stakeholders—comprising 10 older adults, 10 social workers from non-governmental organizations (NGOs), and 10 academic researchers—to collaboratively develop a culturally appropriate model. Phase 2 adopts a longitudinal, mixed-methods design to assess the effectiveness of the localized CBPR model in promoting mental health literacy and improving mental health outcomes among older adults. A district action committee will be established in three districts in Hong Kong, each comprising 5-10 older adults, 1-2 social workers, and 1-2 researchers. These committees will operate according to the localized CBPR framework, engaging in joint activities such as research design, participant recruitment, data collection, intervention development and implementation, data analysis, and dissemination of findings. The proposed sample includes 400 older adults for a three-time-point quantitative survey, complemented by focus group discussions with 15 older adults for qualitative insights. The final sample size will be determined collaboratively with the district action committees. The resulting localized CBPR model will serve as a valuable reference for future bottom-up mental health literacy promotion initiatives in Hong Kong. Empirical findings from this study will provide scientific evidence on the effectiveness of a culturally adapted CBPR model, informing the development of sustainable mental health intervention policies tailored to the local context. 社區為基礎的參與式研究（Community-based participatory research, CBPR）是一種由下而上的方法，透過融合社區實踐和文化知識，針對本地健康問題制定實證策略，以提升干預措施的有效性和針對性。然而，現有的理論架構和研究多來自美國、英語國家及少數族裔群體，缺乏針對香港特定文化背景的驗證。由於CBPR具有高度的文化敏感性，其在香港，尤其是在居住於社區的長者群體中的適用性與成效尚未明確。本研究旨在填補兩個主要空白：第一，受文化差異影響，西方國家發展的理論模型未必能直接應用於香港；第二，香港現行的精神健康推廣介入多採用由上而下的方法，對於CBPR方法的應用較為有限，且缺乏系統性評估其成效。 研究將分為兩個階段進行。第一階段將與香港多方持份者共同建構一個本土化的CBPR模型，包括10位長者、10位來自非政府組織的社工及10位研究人員，透過共創工作坊與德爾菲調查，共同設計並完善模型。第二階段則採用混合研究方法，評估該模型在提升長者精神健康知識和改善其心理健康狀況的效果。研究將在香港三個不同地區成立“地區行動委員會”，每個委員會由5至10位長者、1至2位社工及1至2位研究人員組成。這些委員會將依據本土化模型，進行合作活動，包括設計研究方案、招募參與者、資料收集、介入措施的執行、資料分析及研究成果的推廣。預計樣本包括約400位長者，將在三個時間點進行量化調查，同時進行15位長者的焦點小組討論，以獲取深層質性資料。最終樣本數將根據各地區委員會的協商結果確定。 此本土化CBPR模型的建立，將為香港未來以社區為核心的精神健康推廣提供寶貴的實務經驗與理論依據。同時，研究的實證結果也將為CBPR模式在香港的應用成效提供科學證據，促進本地持續且有效的精神健康干預策略與政策制定。

17601926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17601926.value: 母系譜線：抹除、模糊性與斯里蘭卡族群身分的塑造

17601926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17601926.value: “Motherlines" will draw on a wide range of published and unpublished sources to offer a multigenerational and multiethnic exploration of ethnic identity and conflict in Sri Lanka. Although the country’s thirty-year civil war features prominently in political, historical, and aesthetic works on Sri Lanka, not enough consideration is given to the life experiences of multiethnic communities exposed to violence across multiple generations. While the colonial, post-colonial, and modern periods of history are often studied in isolation, the primary focus tends to be the development of the Sinhala-Tamil ethnic split. As a result, significantly less attention is paid to how multiethnic families navigated the sharp dualisms that ultimately structured society. “Motherlines” studies the evolution of the ethnic conflict in Sri Lanka by displacing the dominant frameworks of analysis that have made the nation’s local histories legible to a global audience. I do not begin my study with the war, in its aftermath, or by privileging the historical tensions between the Sinhalese and the Tamils. Rather, I venture into the margins where labels, identities, and facts are simultaneously more evasive and multilayered. To work at and through the margins, I have developed a method of study that blends scholarship with storytelling, one that is vigilant about the various forms of silence, erasure, and disappearance that haunt Sri Lanka’s history. I begin my investigation with an individual, my paternal grandmother, a second-generation Indian Tamil born in Sri Lanka, whose exposure to ethnic violence in an earlier, pre-war period resulted in a form of self-exile from community, language, and culture. Choosing not to pass down her heritage, my grandmother cut off the rest of her multiethnic family from a critical part of their cultural inheritance. “Motherlines” engages with this painful decision not to pass down as a pathway into Sri Lankan history. Experimental in nature, “Motherlines” seeks to diversify the categories of knowledge through which the complexities of ethnic conflicts are comprehended. The project will achieve this by blending autoethnography with literary and cinematic analysis, and archival study with travel writing and personal interviews. “Motherlines,” in its final form, will be a visually rich and narratively diverse monograph about the minor histories that trace their outlines around and across the major events that shape a nation’s processes of remembering and forgetting.

17602126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17602126.value: 超越數學課堂：大學生的課外學習如何形塑其對數學的論述

17602126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17602126.value: Dr Law, Ka Ho Prof LEUNG, Frederick Koon-Shing Prof NG , Oi Lam Prof Weber, Keith

17602126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17602126.value: Mathematics is essential for Science, Technology, and Engineering. STEM majors typically study several mathematics courses, and many mathematical topics are discussed in specialised courses. Research into practices that are common to undergraduate mathematics will generate evidence to enhance the preparation of STEM cadres. Lecturing dominates undergraduate mathematics instruction. Little is known about how students navigate the acknowledged challenges of courses that involve lectures (CILs), and especially, how students mobilise technology to advance their learning. This knowledge is essential for improving first-year courses, where many students decide to leave their STEM majors. Research emphasizes the importance of self-regulated practices that undergraduates implement outside of lecture halls. This research will investigate these practices to identify fine-grained mechanisms that foster and hinder students’ attempts to advance their grasp of the course material. The research will attend to students’ use of AI-based tools as a novel subset of learning practices among modern students. This research extends the PI’s expertise in university mathematics education to Hong Kong (HK). Thirty STEM undergraduates taking first-year mathematics CILs will partake in four sessions throughout a semester. The students will engage in their regular learning practices during the sessions. Sfard’s (2008) discursive theory of learning will analyse how specific practices foster micro-level changes in students’ mathematical discourses. The analysis will track student discourses throughout the semester to identify key developmental phases. The follow-up phase will validate the findings at scale through focus groups and questionnaires (N=430). This study will fill a gap in the research understanding of how students learn outside contact hours in CILs, as the predominant setting in undergraduate mathematics. This will be among the first longitudinal studies in undergraduate mathematics education. It will test Sfard’s theory by exploring learning of mathematically mature students over time. The analysis of data from HK with attention to the cultural context will add an original perspective to the research discourse on mathematics lecturing. The research will develop practical resources that will enable STEM departments to enhance their course design and instruction. The research will establish partnerships between mathematicians and educational researchers. The partnerships will impact curricular and policy reforms in schools and universities to better prepare the next generations for academic studies and careers in STEM. 數學是科學、科技與工程不可或缺的基礎。STEM 專業的學生通常會修讀數門數學課程，而許多數學主題亦會在專門課程中進一步探討。針對本科數學課程中常見教學實踐所進行的研究，可提供相關證據，有助於提升 STEM 人才培育的質素。講授式教學是本科數學教學的主流模式。然而，目前對於學生如何應對涉及講座的課程（CIL）的已知挑戰，尤其是學生如何運用科技來促進學習，所知甚少。此方面知識對改善大一課程尤為關鍵，因為許多學生正是在這一階段決定放棄 STEM 專業。研究顯示，大學生在課堂之外實施的自主學習實踐具有重要意義。本研究將探討這些教學實踐，藉此釐清哪些細微機制有助於或阻礙學生深化對課程內容的理解。同時，研究也將著眼於學生對AI工具的應用，將其視為現代學生學習實踐中的一種新興子類別。本研究會將首席研究員在大學數學教育方面的專業知識延伸至香港。三十名修讀大一數學 CIL 課程的 STEM 系大學生，將在整個學期內參加四次研究。在研究期間，學生將進行日常的學習活動。分析將運用 Sfard（2008）的學習論述理論檢視特定實踐如何促成學生數學論述中的微觀層面變化。該分析將全程追蹤學生在整個學期中的言論，以確定關鍵的發展階段。後續階段將透過焦點小組及問卷調查（N=430），對研究結果進行大規模驗證。由於CIL是本科數學課程的主要教學形式，本研究將填補學界對學生如何在課外時間於該環境中學習的認知缺口。該研究亦將是本科數學教育領域中最早的縱向研究之一。該研究將透過探討數學能力較成熟學生隨時間推移的學習過程，來驗證 Sfard 的理論。此外，對來自香港的數據進行分析，並著眼於文化脈絡，將為數學授課的研究論述增添嶄新的視角。該研究將開發實用資源，協助 STEM 相關系所提升課程設計與教學質素。該研究亦將促進數學家與教育研究者之間的合作。這些合作將對學校及大學的課程與政策改革產生影響，以更好地為下一代做好準備，使其在STEM領域的學術研究和職業發展取得成功。

17602426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17602426.value: 生成式人工智慧背景下的評估改革：設計旨在促進學生投入與真實存在的大學評估

17602426.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17602426.value: Dr Chen, Julia Dr MOORHOUSE, Benjamin Luke

17602426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17602426.value: Assessment design and implementation has long been a vexing issue. Redesigning assessment to cater for the realities of student use of generative AI (GenAI) represents one of the most compelling, and intractable, challenges currently facing higher education. Principled assessment re-design is needed so that universities can be confident that students are able to achieve learning outcomes independently without over-reliance on support from GenAI. The rapid developments of GenAI have outpaced institutional and teacher abilities to redesign assessments. Critical analysis of practice in context and related theoretical principles are needed to frame teachers’ attempts to address the challenges of assessment needing to cater for GenAI realities. The project is grounded in literature on assessment design and implementation; teacher assessment literacy; and recent research at the interface of GenAI and assessment. GenAI represents a new challenge for teacher assessment literacy because students may use GenAI productively or instead out-source assignments, resulting in minimal learning. The project addresses an urgent need in terms of understanding the complexity of how to design and implement assessment in the context of GenAI. The essence of the project is to carry out nine case studies of assessment design and implementation in different disciplines across three participating universities. Data collection for the case studies involves iterative teacher interviews to understand rationales for assessment design and implementation details; student interviews to elicit their views and experiences; classroom observations to provide snapshots of how assessment is communicated and prepared; and study of artefacts, such as course outlines and assessment guidelines. Beyond the nine case study teachers, we also elicit broader teacher perspectives through an open-ended online qualitative survey collecting views of assessment design and implementation from a wider sample of university teachers. Through cross-case analysis of the case studies and thematic analysis of the qualitative survey data, we develop insights into assessment design and implementation in the context of GenAI. The value of the project lies in addressing the challenge of assessment design and implementation within the context of ubiquitous student use of GenAI. Its intended outcomes are: contextualized understandings of assessment design and implementation in different disciplines; new theoretical implications for assessment design and implementation in the context of GenAI; understandings of student responses to assessment design and implementation; a framework for teacher assessment literacy in the context of GenAI; a set of practice-oriented principles for assessment design and implementation; and recommendations for assessment and GenAI policy. 評估的設計與實施長期以來一直是個棘手的問題。如何重新設計評估以適應學生使用生成式人工智慧（GenAI）的現實，是高等教育目前面臨的最引人注目且難以解決的挑戰之一。我們需要基於原則進行評估重構，以確保大學確信學生能夠獨立實現學習成果，而不會過度依賴 GenAI 的輔助。 GenAI 的快速發展已超越了大學和教師重新設計評估的能力範疇。我們需要對具體情境下的實踐及相關理論原則進行批判性分析，從而為教師應對 GenAI 時代評估挑戰的嘗試提供指導框架。 本計畫立基於評估設計與實施、教師評估素養以及 GenAI 與評估交叉領域最新研究的文獻。 GenAI 對教師評估素養提出了新挑戰，因為學生既可能利用 GenAI 促進學習，也可能將其用於「外包」作業，從而導致學習成效微乎其微。本計畫旨在滿足一個迫切需求：理解在 GenAI 背景下設計與實施評估的複雜性。 本計畫的核心是在三所參與大學的不同學科中開展九項關於評估設計與實施的案例研究。個案研究的資料收集包括：與教師進行多次訪談，以了解評估設計的依據及實施細節；與學生訪談，以獲取其觀點與體驗；進行課堂觀察，以捕捉評估溝通與準備過程的實況；以及分析課程大綱和評估指南等相關資料。 除了這九位參與個案研究的教師外，我們還將透過開放式線上質性調查，徵集更廣泛的大學教師群對評量設計與實施的看法。透過對個案研究進行跨案例分析，並對質性調查資料進行主題分析，我們將深入探討 GenAI 背景下的評估設計與實施問題。 本計畫的價值在於應對學生普遍使用 GenAI 這一背景下的評估設計與實施挑戰。其預期成果包括： 對不同學科中評估設計與實施的情境化理解； GenAI 背景下評估設計與實施的理論新啟示； 對學生針對評估設計與實施之反應的理解； GenAI 背景下教師評估素養的架構； 一套面向實務的評估設計與實施原則。以及評估和生成式人工智慧（GenAI）政策的建議。

17602526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17602526.value: 融合感知的生物—地理資訊框架：促進香港長者友善環境建設

17602526.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17602526.value: Prof Chang, Hue Fung Dorita Prof DeJohn, Amber

17602526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17602526.value: As Hong Kong faces an unprecedented aging population, with the proportion of older adults projected to reach 36% by 2046, addressing mental health challenges within this demographic is a pressing public health priority. Recent statistics indicate a significant rise in mental health disorders, including severe depression, and a record-high suicide rate among individuals over 60, accounting for approximately 41% of all suicides in 2024. Contributing factors include poor infrastructure, neighborhood deprivation and social isolation. It is crucial to address the mental health issues in this vulnerable group. Existing research links age-friendly communities to better mental health among older adults, but largely relies on self-reports, which are biased and time-consuming, meanwhile overlooking the immediate effect of environments on mental health. Studies using wearable biosensors offer continuous data but are limited by small samples and short experimental time, neglecting cumulative effects of outdoor exposure and indoor activities. Additionally, most of these experimental studies are conducted in pre-defined environments, restricting environmental variability and potentially missing key interactions and behavior diversity present in real-life settings. To address the research gaps, we propose a perception-integrated bio-geo informatics framework to investigate the dynamic interactions between environmental exposure and mental health in Hong Kong’s aging population. The novelty of this project includes: 1) synergistically collect and integrate novel data types for individuals, including minute-level biomarkers, GPS trajectories, survey questionnaires, and accelerometer measurements, with multi-source environmental data. 2) examine the minute-level relationship between environmental exposures and digital biomarkers and identify environmental features that elevate stress responses among older adults. 3) leverage data bias from both subjective reports and objective measures from digital biomarkers and GPS records to provide evidence for developing more effective interventions. 4) develop standardized metrics for assessing age-friendly neighborhood characteristics and their associations with mental health to promote healthy aging in place. Our pilot study and preliminary results have certified the project feasibility. Our proposed research offers a promising avenue to improving mental healthcare in older adults by examining the impact of their living environment, providing evidence-based strategies for personalized care and effective interventions. The research insights will advance geospatial data science for social good and wellness, and lay foundations for future implementation of Just-In-Time Adaptive Intervention theory. The findings will inform health professionals in recommending age-friendly environments that promote the well-being of older adults, further improving the quality of life of this vulnerable group in Hong Kong. 隨著香港面對前所未有的人口老齡化，預計到2046年長者比例將達36%，應對此人口群體的精神健康挑戰已成為迫切的公共衛生優先事項。近期統計數據顯示，精神健康障礙，包括嚴重抑鬱症，呈顯著上升趨勢；同時，60歲以上人士的自殺率亦創下新高，約佔2024年所有自殺個案的41%。相關因素包括基礎設施不足、社區資源匱乏以及社交孤立。因此，針對這一弱勢群體的精神健康問題採取應對措施至關重要。 現有研究指出，長者友善社區與長者較佳的精神健康狀況相關。然而，相關研究大多依賴自我報告資料，不僅容易產生偏差，且耗時較長，同時亦忽略了環境對精神健康的即時影響。使用可穿戴式生物感測器的研究雖可提供連續數據，但往往受限於樣本量較小及實驗時間較短，未能充分考慮戶外暴露與室內活動的累積效應。此外，這些實驗研究大多在預先界定的環境中進行，限制了環境變異性，並可能忽略真實生活情境中存在的關鍵互動與行為多樣性。 為回應上述研究缺口，本研究提出一個融合感知的生物—地理資訊學框架，以探討香港老齡人口中環境暴露與精神健康之間的動態互動關係。本項目的創新之處包括：1）協同收集並整合個體層面的新型數據，包括分鐘級生物標誌物、GPS軌跡、問卷調查及加速度計測量數據，並與多來源環境數據進行融合；2）檢視環境暴露與數碼生物標誌物之間的分鐘級關係，並識別會提升長者壓力反應的環境特徵；3）利用主觀報告以及來自數碼生物標誌物和GPS記錄的客觀測量資料所呈現的數據偏差，為制定更有效的干預措施提供證據；4）建立標準化指標，用於評估長者友善社區特徵及其與精神健康的關聯，從而促進健康的原居安老。 我們的試點研究及初步結果已證實本項目的可行性。本研究透過考察長者生活環境對其精神健康的影響，為改善長者精神健康照護提供一條具前景的研究路徑，並為個人化照護及有效干預策略提供循證依據。研究成果將推動地理空間數據科學在社會福祉與健康促進方面的應用，並為未來實施「即時適應性干預」（Just-In-Time Adaptive Intervention）理論奠定基礎。研究發現亦將有助於醫療及健康專業人員提出有利於長者福祉的長者友善環境建議，進一步提升香港這一弱勢群體的生活質素

17603126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17603126.value: 居家個⼈化連結組經顱交流電刺激結合⼈⼯智能⾔語治療之系統性評估：中⾵後失語症治療研究

17603126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17603126.value: Aphasia is an acquired neurogenic language disorder after stroke-induced disruption of the brain’s language processing network. While behavioral-based speech therapy remains the mainstay of aphasia management, its effectiveness is constrained by inherent limitations, including the significant gap between evidence-based recommended therapy dosage and what is routinely provided in clinical practice, high cost and patient-therapist ratio (making it difficult to close the dosage gap), and the inability to directly address underlying neural mechanisms causing aphasia. To address these issues, the use of neuromodulation alongside speech therapy has attracted growing interest. However, existing research has yielded suboptimal efficacy owing to dosage constraints and use of one-size-fits-all stimulation approaches. To improve treatment efficacy in neuromodulation, preliminary evidence supports an innovative approach that uses EEG-guided individualized connectomic transcranial alternating current stimulation (IC-tACS) to provide model-guided, network-based stimulation targeted at one’s language network hub, promote oscillatory network reorganization, and enhance language recovery. This approach not only advances individualized neurorehabilitation methodology, but the accessible technologies it uses are also suitable for implementation in home settings to release dosage capacity. Because tACS is most effective when combined with active language engagement, integrating AI-powered computerized speech therapy presents a unique opportunity for high-dosage, self-administered rehabilitation at home, where early evidence has demonstrated as safe and practical but rigorous large-scale clinical trials remain lacking worldwide. Our primary aim is to systematically investigate the clinical advantages of this home-based neurorehabilitation model for neural and language outcomes in aphasia. Specifically, we compare the treatment effects at 2-week, 4-week, and follow-up among different treatment conditions involving home-based vs. center-based, real vs. sham tACS plus AI-assisted vs. traditional therapy at high vs. traditional dosage. This design will isolate the respective contributions of neuromodulation, therapy modality, and treatment dosage to neural and language recovery. The secondary aim is to develop operational guidelines for implementing home-based neurorehabilitation model by analyzing patient and caregiver experiences and identifying the most effective training and support strategies based on user feedback. These guidelines will include clinician’s manual, clinician/caregiver training materials, user eligibility assessment tool, recommended supervision strategies, and remote monitoring procedures. This project represents the first large-scale clinical trial to rigorously evaluate both the efficacy and practical implementation of a home-based neurorehabilitation model for aphasia. By leveraging cost-effectiveness, scalability, and neural precision, the model has the potential to accelerate language recovery, optimize recourse allocation, and transform the standard of care for aphasia management. • 失語症是一種後天性神經源性語言障礙，由中風引起的腦語言處理網路功能失調所致。儘管行為療法仍然是治療的主要手段，但其療效受到許多固有局限性的限制，包括循證推薦的治療劑量與臨床實踐中常規提供的劑量之間存在顯著差距，以及無法直接調節導致失語症的潛在神經機制。此外，面對面治療的高昂費用和不理想的醫病比例進一步限制了傳統治療模式的治療劑量。為了解決這些問題，近年來，將神經調控技術與言語治療結合引起了越來越多的關注。然而，劑量限制和「一刀切」式刺激方案的使用等挑戰仍然是現有神經調控研究中阻礙療效的主要障礙。為了提高神經調控的治療效果，一種創新方法利用腦電圖引導的個⼈化連結組經顱交流電刺激（IC-tACS），提供基於模型的、針對個⼈語言網絡樞紐的刺激，以促進語言功能恢復。早期證據表明，單次IC-tACS治療即可促進網絡重組並提升語言能力，提示重複應用適當劑量可能帶來持久的康復益處。鑑於其便攜性和易用性，tACS非常適合融入家庭環境，從而擴大治療的可及性並解決當前劑量限制的問題。此外，由於tACS與積極的語言參與相結合時療效最佳，因此將其與人工智慧驅動的電腦化言語治療相結合，為高強度、居家自主復健提供了前景。一款本地開發名為SpeechOn的人工智慧命名治療應用程序，支援自主命名練習，其特色在於個⼈化訓練項目、自動語音識別、提示和反饋。初步證據表明，SpeechOn 與傳統言語治療具有相當的療效，使其成為與居家 IC-tACS 療法相結合的理想工具。我們提出將 IC-tACS 與 SpeechOn 結合，建構一種經濟高效、可擴展且個體化客製化的居家神經復健模式，有望克服傳統失語症療法的關鍵限制。然而，目前尚缺乏失語症居家神經調控療法的大規模臨床試驗。本研究的主要目的是系統性地探討與傳統言語治療相比，此居家復健在改善失語症患者的神經和語言功能方面的臨床優勢。我們旨在比較五種治療方案在2週、4週和隨訪時的治療效果，包括：(i) 居家高劑量真實tACS聯合AI療法；(ii) 居家高劑量假tACS聯合AI療法；(iii) 診所常規劑量真實tACS聯合治療中心；(iv) 診所常規劑量假tACS聯合AI療法；(v) 診所常規劑量言語治療；透過比較不同方案，我們將分別分析神經調控、治療模式和治療劑量對神經和語言功能恢復的貢獻。本研究的次要目標是透過分析患者和照顧者的體驗，並根據使用者回饋來確定最有效的訓練和支持策略，從而製定居家神經復健模式的操作指南。這些指南將包括臨床醫生手冊、臨床醫生和照顧者培訓材料、使用者資格評估工具、建議的督導策略以及遠端監測程序。

17603226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17603226.value: 工作中的日本：當代日本文學中的資本主義勞動、自主性與後工作想像

17603226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17603226.value: Japan’s economy and workplaces have changed dramatically since the 1980s. Financialization, flexible hiring, aging demographics, and automation have reordered daily life and unsettled what “work” means. This project asks how contemporary Japanese literature (1980s–2020s) has registered and reimagined those changes, and what kinds of futures of work it helps us think about. The study’s central claim is that work in contemporary Japan shapes how stories are written. Narrative devices and techniques mirror shift work, platform piecework, and managerial metrics. Reading formal features alongside socioeconomic changes shows how narratives both comply with and critique prevailing work norms. While scholarship has acknowledged precarity as a trope in contemporary Japanese literature, little research has been conducted how work has shaped and formalized literary writings by numerous Japanese authors. The project spans six topics: (1) the late-1970s/1980s “post-revolutionary” turn, when confidence in grand political horizons waned and class identities began to dissolve (2) day labor, youth unemployment, and caregiving as competing forms of work (3) office fiction that either exposes overwork and petty coercion or defends teamwork (4) migrant, Nikkei, and refugee labor that reframes who counts as a worker and what solidarity can look like (5) gig and platform labor where ratings, dashboards, and delivery timetables set the tempo of life (6) AI and automation futures that shift humans toward supervision, allocation, and quality control Four guiding questions organize the analysis: • How do literary works depict changing perceptions of work and propose alternatives? • How do forms of storytelling emulate or resist policy imaginaries? • How does “postwork” and “antiwork” appear as techniques, including delay, non-event, withdrawal, refusal, and rest? • How are automation, datafied oversight, and AI translated into plot, pacing, and voice? Methodologically, the project combines close reading with cultural history and political economy, draws on both Japanese- and English-language scholarship, and reperiodizes the field's consensus by starting before the 1990s postbubble and “lost decade.” The outcome is a new cultural history of work in Japanese literature and framework for reading labor as form that extends beyond Japan to East Asia and other contexts facing similar pressures. In place of productivity metrics and monetary value alone, the project offers humanities criteria for judging work arrangements and imagining viable models of (post)work, and contributing to comparative cultural studies and labor studies. 日本的經濟與職場自1980年代以來因金融化、彈性僱用、人口高齡化與自動化而急劇改變，也重新塑造了人們對「工作」的理解。本研究探討1980年代至2020年代日本當代文學如何記錄並重新想像這些變化，以及文學如何幫助我們思考工作的未來。 本研究主張，工作不只是文學描寫的主題，也形塑敘事形式本身。輪班、平台零工與績效管理等工作模式，會反映在作品的節奏、結構與敘事技巧中。既有研究雖已關注日本文學中的不穩定勞動，卻較少探討工作如何具體塑造文學形式。 研究涵蓋六個主題：（1）1970年代末至1980年代「後革命」時期的階級與政治想像轉變；（2）日薪勞動、青年失業與照護勞動；（3）描寫過勞、職場壓迫、團隊合作與專業技藝的辦公室小說；（4）移民、日裔人士與難民勞動，以及勞動者身分與團結；（5）由評分、平台與配送時間支配的零工經濟；（6）人工智能與自動化下人類工作的轉型。 研究將分析文學如何呈現工作觀念的變化與替代方案，如何回應工作改革、照護與移民政策，以及「後工作」與「反工作」如何透過延宕、拒絕、退出與休息等形式出現。同時探討自動化、數據化監管與人工智能如何轉化為情節、節奏與敘事聲音。 方法上，本研究結合文本細讀、文化史與政治經濟學，並將研究起點提前至「失落十年」之前。最終將提出一部新的日本文學工作文化史，以及「勞動作為形式」的分析框架，並從人文學角度重新思考工作價值與可能的「後工作」未來。

17603926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17603926.value: 開發互動式流向圖，用於大灣區中國新型「特種兵式」遊客的即時管理

17603926.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17603926.value: Dr CHEN, Jinyan Prof KAN, Zihan Dr LUO, Anqi

17603926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17603926.value: A new form of tourism is sweeping across China. ‘Special Forces’ style tourism is a new form of domestic budget tourism performed by social media savvy young people. ‘Special Forces’ tourists are indicative of new social, cultural, economic, technological and tourism developments emerging in China, but they have not been theorized adequately or examined in a comprehensive way. Major uncertainties associated with these new tourists include their lack of spending, their social media-driven movement patterns causing overtourism, their unpredictability, and their unusually intense itineraries and unconventional destinations. As tourism is central to the integration and development of the Greater Bay Area, more needs to be learned about the mobilities, motivations, social media usage and economic capacity of these new tourists. The proposed research will explore the characteristics of ‘Special Forces’ tourists in the context of China’s Greater Bay Area – a region of 86 million people centered around the Pearl River Delta, as it attempts to become a globally recognized tourism destination. The proposal will test and validate a theory of ‘Special Forces’ tourism and produce an interactive digital flow map of their mobilities to facilitate real-time tourism management. The objectives are: (1) Build a theory of ‘Special Forces’ tourism that explains their movement patterns, their social media usage, and their spending; (2) Test and validate our theory among ‘Special Forces’ tourists in the Greater Bay Area and ; (3) Operationalize our theory by developing the Spatiotemporal Tourist Environment Map (STEM) to visualize the movement patterns of ‘Special Forces’ tourists across the Greater Bay Area. The project will build on the PI’s research on tourism mobility, GBA tourism, and mixed methods – including a recent pilot study in Hong Kong. It applies an integrated exploratory sequential mixed methods-big data analytics approach involving tourists in four major GBA cities (Hong Kong, Macau, Shenzhen, Guangzhou). Using a theoretical framework informed by time-geography and twelve components of tourist mobility identified via an in-depth literature search, this proposed project builds on the considerable research experience and scholarly networks established by the PI and Co-Is across the GBA over the past decade. The project will contribute new knowledge of China’s tourism geography and tourist movement patterns, develop a theory of ‘Special Forces’ tourism, and operationalize our theory for policy makers and tourism practitioners. 一種新型旅遊方式正席捲中國。 「特種兵式」旅遊是擅長使用社群媒體的年輕人所進行的一種新型國內低成本旅遊模式。 「特種兵式」遊客群體反映了中國在社會、文化、經濟、技術及旅遊領域湧現的新發展態勢，但目前學界尚未對其進行充分的理論闡釋或全面的考察分析。圍繞這類新型遊客有許多不確定因素，包括其消費水準較低、受社群媒體驅動的出行模式引發「過度旅遊」問題、行為難以預測，以及行程安排異常緊湊、目的地選擇不落俗套等特點。鑑於旅遊業在粵港澳大灣區融合發展中處於核心地位，有必要深入了解這類新型遊客的流動特徵、行動機器、社群媒體使用習慣以及經濟消費能力。 本研究計畫探討中國粵港澳大灣區（以珠江三角洲為核心、擁有8,600萬人口的區域，正致力於成為全球知名的旅遊目的地）背景下「特種兵式」遊客的特徵。該研究將檢驗並驗證關於「特種兵式」旅遊的理論，並製作展示其流動軌跡的互動式數位流動地圖，以輔助即時旅遊管理。具體目標包括：(1) 建構「特種兵式」旅遊理論，闡釋該類遊客的移動模式、社交媒體使用習慣及消費行為；(2) 在粵港澳大灣區的「特種兵式」遊客群體中對該理論進行檢驗與驗證；(3) 透過發展「時空遊客環境」（STEM）將遊客化為中心化的地方性遊客模式。 本計畫將基於計畫負責人（PI）在旅遊流動性、粵港澳大灣區（GBA）旅遊及混合研究方法領域既有的研究成果－包括近期在香港進行的一項試驗研究－展開工作。本計畫採用一種綜合性的「探索性順序混合方法與大數據分析」結合的研究路徑，以大灣區四大城市（香港、澳門、深圳、廣州）的遊客為研究對象。本計畫將依托時間地理學理論框架，並結合透過深入文獻綜述所確定的遊客流動性十二項構成要素；同時，計畫也將充分利用計畫負責人及共同研究人員（Co-Is）過去十年間在大灣區積累的豐富研究經驗與學術網絡。本計畫旨在為中國旅遊地理及遊客流動模式研究貢獻新知，建構「特種兵式」旅遊（「Special Forces」 tourism）理論，並將該理論轉化為可供政策制定者及旅遊從業者實際應用的指導方案。

17604026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17604026.value: 亞太地區之基礎設施諮商

17604026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17604026.value: Global conventions and legal instruments increasingly advocate for the use of consultation prior to the initiation of infrastructure investment projects to advance sustainable development objectives (see ILO Convention 169, 1989; Aarhus Convention, 2001; Equator Principles, 2003; UN Guiding Principles, 2011; OECD Due Diligence Guidelines, 2017). However, differing understandings and implementations of the consultation process inhibit the establishment of a common framework. While scholarship into the underlying dynamics of arbitration, mediation and negotiation across societies is well developed, commensurate research examining the underlying principles, values and conceptualization of consultation in the context of global infrastructure development remains limited. This research project represents a pioneering examination of the legal definition of "consultation" as a core international law obligation in order to explore how its meaning and associated practice may vary depending on the context in which it arises. Drawing on a qualitative triangulation methodology including the use of case studies, interviews and surveys, the project will analyze treaty language, case studies, interviews, and surveys of stakeholders—including non-governmental community groups and legal professionals—to explore the gap between consultation policy ‘in the books’ and the approaches that shape consultation ‘practice’ in infrastructure development programs funded by multilateral development banks in the Asia Pacific region. The aim will be to identify both the challenges and insights that contribute to successful consultation processes addressing complex, polycentric challenges while advancing sustainable infrastructure development objectives. The research will generate policy recommendations for enhancing community engagement in Asia Pacific infrastructure development and provide valuable insights that can inform future multi-jurisdictional dispute resolution research and practice. The findings will be written up in the form of a research monograph, journal articles and conference presentations. 全球各項公約與法律文書日益提倡在啟動基礎設施投資計畫之前進行 諮商，以推動可持續發展目標（可參見《土著和部落人民公約（第169號）》（1989 年）、《奧爾斯公約》（2001 年）、《赤道原則》（2003 年）、《聯合國工商企業與人權指導原則》（2011 年）、《經濟合作暨發展組織盡職調查指南》（2017 年））。 然而，各界對諮商程序之理解與執行方式存在分歧，阻礙了共同框架 的確立。儘管仲裁、調解與談判之跨社會研究已相當廣泛，惟針對全球基礎設施諮商之根本原則、核心價值及概念的探討仍屬有限。 本研究將檢視「諮商」作為核心國際法義務之法律定義，進而探討其意義及相關實踐如何因所處背景不同而有所差異。透過採用質性三角檢證法（包括案例研究、訪談與問卷調查等），針對條約用語、實際案例、訪談內容，以及非政府組織與法律專業人士等持份者的問卷進行分析，本研究旨在探討亞太地區由多邊開發銀行資助之基礎設施發展計劃中，諮商政策的理論「法條規範」與促成諮商的實際運作兩者的落差。 本研究目標在於發掘成功諮商程序所面臨的挑戰與可供借鑑的經驗，如何在回應複雜多元的挑戰之際，同時推進可續基礎設施發展的目標。本研究將提出政策建議，以強化亞太基礎設施發展中的社區參與，並提供可為未來跨司法管轄區爭議解決的研究與實務參考的見解。 研究成果將以專書、學術期刊論文及會議發表等形式呈現。

17604226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17604226.value: 數位時代的育兒至關重要：探討香港兒童數位福祉的實現路徑

17604226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17604226.value: Prof King, Ronnel Bornasal Dr Lee, Amelia Nam Yuk Dr Tao, Sisi

17604226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17604226.value: This research project explores the intricate dynamics between digital parenting practices and Primary 4-6 children’s digital wellbeing in Hong Kong. It seeks to achieve three primary objectives: to develop a comprehensive conceptualization of digital parenting practices and children’s digital wellbeing, to construct survey instruments for measuring these constructs, and to unravel the nuanced relationships between specific digital parenting practices and various facets of children's digital wellbeing. With parents grappling to adapt to the rapid evolution of digital technologies and concerns about the detrimental effects of excessive screen time on children, the project will provide invaluable insights and practical guidance for enhancing children's digital experiences and safeguarding their digital wellbeing. The project is significant for Hong Kong, given the city's high smartphone and Internet penetration rates, societal emphasis on children’s mental health, and the need for evidence-based policies to inform effective digital parenting. By bridging knowledge gaps in the digital parenting and children’s digital wellbeing scholarship, this project will pioneer the integration of emerging (including AI-assisted) digital parenting practices into the mainstream discourse, provide a comprehensive updated understanding of digital parenting practices and children’s digital wellbeing, develop refined survey instruments for measuring these constructs, and provide actionable policy insights into specific digital parenting practices fostering positive digital experiences for children while mitigating online risks. The research methods employed include a systematic review, and interviews and surveys (in an exploratory sequential design) involving Primary 4-6 students and their parents in Hong Kong. First, the systematic review and interviews will provide insights on different conceptualizations, dimensionality, and measurement and inform the survey development. The research will then analyze the survey data to obtain factor structures of digital parenting and children’s digital wellbeing. Lastly, structural equation modelling will be used to determine relationships between digital parenting practices and children’s digital wellbeing. The pathway to impact includes disseminating research findings poised to empower parents, inform policymakers, guide educators in digital parenting and promoting children's digital wellbeing, and advance the scholarship on digital parenting and children’s digital wellbeing. Given the project’s expected impact in enhancing the quality of digital parenting and supporting children’s digital wellbeing, funding this project represents a significant investment in our children’s digital future. Therefore, the project is not only important but necessary to be funded.

17604726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17604726.value: Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) initiatives implemented by corporations are increasingly viewed as essential responses to pressing environmental and social challenges in China. However, the role of corporate law in advancing ESG efforts remains underexplored in current academic and policy discourse. This project seeks to fill that gap by examining how corporate law—through its design, interpretation, and enforcement—can support and shape corporate ESG performance. Corporate law influences ESG outcomes through several key mechanisms. First, it defines the legal framework governing the corporate charter, including how authority is distributed among corporate organs such as the board of directors and shareholders. Within this framework, firms can adopt various provisions—such as staggered boards, limitations on shareholders’ rights to nominate or remove directors, and golden parachutes for executives—that alter the internal balance of power. Corporate law determines the permissibility and enforceability of these provisions, thereby shaping corporate governance structures that may support or hinder ESG initiatives. Second, corporate law sometimes directly regulates the powers and duties of directors. By influencing fiduciary duties and board discretion, corporate law can thus play a central role in enabling or constraining ESG-focused decision-making. Third, corporate law affects the composition of the board of directors. Notably, recent amendments to China’s corporate law require the inclusion of employee representatives on corporate boards. These employee directors often bring different priorities and perspectives compared to shareholder-appointed directors, which can significantly affect a company’s approach to ESG-related matters. Fourth, corporate law also governs the rights of different categories of shareholders. For example, institutional investors—who frequently prioritize long-term ESG concerns—may find their influence limited in firms where controlling shareholders dominate. The legal structure surrounding shareholder rights can either amplify or dilute the voice of ESG-conscious investors. This research project will investigate how variations in corporate law rules—and changes in those rules—impact ESG outcomes and related metrics such as corporate environmental pollution. Furthermore, the project will assess the influence of regulatory interventions by the China Securities Investor Services Center (CSISC) and judicial decisions that interpret corporate law on the ESG practices of publicly listed firms. The findings are expected to guide Chinese regulators, courts, and policymakers in refining corporate law to better support the country’s growing commitment to ESG principles. 企业所实施的环境、社会和治理（ESG）倡议，日益被视为应对中国紧迫环境与社会挑战的必要举措。然而，在当前学术与政策讨论中，公司法在推进ESG工作中的作用仍未得到充分探讨。本项目旨在弥补这一空白，研究公司法——通过其设计、解释与执行——如何支持并塑造企业的ESG表现。 公司法通过若干关键机制影响ESG成效。首先，它界定了规范公司章程的法律框架，包括董事会、股东等公司机关之间的权力分配方式。在该框架内，公司可采纳多种章程条款——例如交错董事会、限制股东提名或罢免董事的权利、以及高管金色降落伞安排——这些条款会改变公司内部的权力平衡。公司法决定了这些条款的合法性与可执行性，从而塑造出可能促进或阻碍ESG倡议的公司治理结构。 其次，公司法有时直接规制董事的权力与义务，包括其在何种程度上可以考虑股东以外利益相关者（如员工、客户或环境）的权益。通过影响信义义务和董事会裁量权，公司法可在推动或限制以ESG为重心的决策方面发挥核心作用。 第三，公司法影响董事会的构成。值得关注的是，中国公司法近期修订要求公司董事会中包含职工代表。这些职工董事往往具有与股东委派董事不同的优先关注点和视角，这可能显著影响公司在ESG相关事务上的做法。 第四，公司法还规范不同类别股东的权利。例如，机构投资者——通常优先关注长期ESG议题——在控股股东主导的公司中，其影响力可能受到限制。围绕股东权利的法律结构，既可以增强也可能削弱具有ESG意识的投资者的声音。 本研究项目将考察公司法规则之间的差异——以及这些规则的变化——如何影响ESG成效及相关指标（如企业环境污染）。它将分析将权力在董事会与股东之间进行分配的特定章程条款对ESG表现的影响。此外，项目还将评估中证中小投资者服务中心的监管干预措施，以及解释公司法的司法裁判，对上市公司ESG实践的影响。同时，将评估证券交易所关于公司章程修订的监管规则的影响，探讨这些规则如何塑造与ESG相关的公司治理实践。 通过生成关于公司法与ESG成效之间关系的实证证据，本研究将为制定更有效的法律与监管框架提供信息。研究结果预计将为中国监管机构、法院和政策制定者提供指导，助其完善公司法，以更好地支持中国对ESG原则日益增强的承诺。

17605126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17605126.value: 高血壓患者動脈粥樣硬化性心血管疾病風險預測模型的構建與驗證：基於四項大規模前瞻性隊列的整合分析

17605126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17605126.value: Dr Bennett, Derrick Dr Du, Huaidong Prof Griffin, Simon Prof Luo, Ruibang Dr Wan, Eric Yuk Fai Prof Yang, Yijian

17605126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17605126.value: Background Currently, there are no atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk (ASCVD) risk prediction models specifically developed for individuals with hypertension. Traditional risk prediction models, including Pooled Cohort Equations and China-PAR, demonstrate poor predictive accuracy when used in individuals with hypertension, limiting clinical utility for lifestyle modification and therapeutic interventions. Objective To derive and externally validate machine-learning enhanced ASCVD risk prediction models incorporating the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (LE8) score (derived based on 8 behavioral and cardiometabolic risk factors) for European and East Asian adults with hypertension using 4 large-scale prospective cohorts. Methods We will use UK Biobank (n>500,000) and China Kadoorie Biobank (n>500,000) as derivation cohorts, with external validation in EPIC Norfolk, and China Health and Nutrition Survey. The study populations comprise individuals with hypertension without baseline cardiovascular disease. A hybrid machine learning approach will employ LASSO regularization for feature selection and XGBoost algorithms to generate enhanced risk scores, integrated with LE8 components using Cox regression. Model performance will be assessed through 5-fold cross-validation, evaluating discrimination via C-statistics and calibration. Conclusion This research will yield rigorous ethnicity-specific ASCVD prediction models and provide evidence on the external validity of these models specifically for individuals with hypertension. The new risk prediction models integrating modifiable LE8 components will enable dynamic risk assessment and serve as broadly applicable self-monitoring instruments. External validation will ensure generalizability across other populations of the same ethnicity, informing evidence-based lifestyle modification strategies for prevention of ASCVD in individuals with hypertension. 背景：目前尚無專為高血壓患者發展之動脈粥樣硬化性心血管疾病（ASCVD）風險預測模型。傳統模型如Pooled Cohort Equations與China-PAR，在高血壓人群之預測準確性欠佳，使得臨床應用和生活型態調整與治療的介入受限。 目標：本研究利用四項大型前瞻性队列，納入美國心臟協會（AHA）之生命八要素（LE8）評分（基於八項行為與心血管代謝风险因子），針對歐洲及東亞裔高血壓成人，發展並外部驗證基於機器學習強化的ASCVD風險預測模型。 方法：以英國生物銀行（UK Biobank, n>500,000）與中國慢性病前瞻性研究（China Kadoorie Biobank, n>500,000）為推導队列，並以EPIC-Norfolk及中國健康與營養調查（CHNS）進行外部驗證。研究對象為基線無心血管疾病之高血壓個體。採用混合機器學習途徑，以LASSO正則化進行特徵篩選，並以XGBoost演算法產生強化風險評分，同時透過Cox迴歸整合LE8組分。模型效能以五折交叉驗證評估，區辨力以C統計量評估，校準度則以校準圖檢視。 結論：本研究將產出嚴謹的種族特異性ASCVD預測模型，並提供該等模型於高血壓患者人群的外部效度之實證。我们建立的整合可修飾LE8組分之新型風險預測模型，可實現動態風險評估，並有望做為廣泛適用之自我監測工具。外部驗證可確保於相同種族的群體之泛化能力，進而為高血壓患者預防ASCVD之“實證生活型態改善策略”提供依據和参考。

17606426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17606426.value: 朋輩帶領的「延後憂慮」方法對減輕癌症復發恐懼的效果：一項隨機對照試驗

17606426.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17606426.value: Prof Chan, Karen Kar Loen Dr Chan , Wendy Wing Lok Dr Foo, Chi Chung Prof Kwong, Ava Prof Ng, Simon Siu Man Dr Ng, Wing Lam Dr Quan, Jianchao

17606426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17606426.value: While mild concern about cancer recurrence is a normal response, high fear of cancer recurrence (FCR) can affect quality of life and functional capacity. Locally, one in four cancer survivors reported high FCR. Patients with high FCR experience intrusive thoughts lacking identifiable triggers, making them difficult to dismiss. FCR manifestations share characteristics with anxiety and depression. Therefore, applying a theoretical model may explain FCR development and maintenance. The Self-Regulatory Executive Function (S-REF) model uses a transdiagnostic approach to identify features across emotional disorders. The S-REF model suggests metacognitive beliefs about negative thinking are essential in emotional disorders' development, as these beliefs promote intrusive thinking. Our recent work showed maladaptive metacognition is associated with high FCR. A manualized intervention, ConquerFear, has been shown effective in reducing FCR. However, its clinical utility in real-world settings has been questioned, as therapist-led interventions are resource-intensive and likely constrain reach. Hence, there is a need to develop an accessible, scalable FCR care model to reach more cancer survivors while minimizing resource constraints. While brief peer-delivered digital FCR interventions could enhance reach and sustainability, their effectiveness remains untested. Furthermore, current metacognitive interventions employ multiple techniques. Investigating individual components of these interventions can provide better understanding of their mechanisms and therapeutic benefits. One technique, worry postponement within a metacognitive framework, guides individuals to defer worries to a designated period, which may increase their sense of control rather than engaging worrisome thoughts. However, the effect of worry postponement as a stand-alone intervention for managing FCR has yet to be tested. This study aims to conduct a randomized controlled trial assessing the effect of peer-delivered digital ConquerFear multimodal intervention and digital ConquerFear worry postponement single modal intervention on FCR among Chinese cancer survivors with subclinical FCR levels. The study will also assess cost-effectiveness of peer-delivered digital interventions for FCR. Eligible patients are Cantonese- or Mandarin-speaking patients diagnosed with curable cancer who completed treatment within two years, aged ≥ 18 years, with subclinical FCR. A total of 450 eligible patients from trial sites will be randomly allocated to peer-led digital ConquerFear multimodal intervention, peer-led digital ConquerFear worry postponement single-modal intervention, or digital health maintenance intervention (active control). The primary outcome is FCR change between baseline and four post-intervention assessment points; the process outcome is metacognition score change. For cost-effectiveness analysis, we will measure changes in health-related quality of life (HRQoL) using the EQ-5D-5L version. 雖然對癌症復發有輕微憂慮屬於正常反應，但若對癌症復發的恐懼程度較高，便可能影響患者的生活質素及日常功能。本地研究顯示，大約每四位癌症康復者中便有一位報告有高度FCR。高恐懼程度患者往往會出現反覆入侵性的想法，而且這些想法通常沒有明顯誘因，因此難以自行排除。癌症復發的恐懼 的表現亦與焦慮及抑鬱症狀有不少相似之處。因此，運用理論模型有助解釋癌症復發的恐懼的形成及持續機制。 自我調節執行功能模型（S-REF）採用跨診斷取向，辨識不同情緒障礙中的共同特徵。S-REF模型指出，個體對負面思維的後設認知信念是情緒障礙發展的重要因素，因為這些信念會促進入侵性思維的產生。我們近期的研究發現，不良的後設認知與較高癌症復發的恐懼的水平有關。 一項具標準化治療手冊的介入方案「慮而不累」自主計劃課程已被證實能有效減低癌症復發的恐懼。然而，其在真實臨床環境中的實用性受到質疑，因為由治療師主導的介入方式需要大量人力及資源，限制了服務覆蓋範圍。因此，有需要建立一套更容易獲取及具擴展性的癌症復發的恐懼照護模式，在盡量減少資源限制的同時，惠及更多癌症康復者。 雖然由朋輩支援員提供的短期數碼化癌症復發的恐懼介入有望提升服務覆蓋率及可持續性，但其成效仍有待驗證。此外，現時的後設認知介入通常結合多種治療技巧。若能研究這些介入的個別組成部分，將有助更深入了解其運作機制及治療效益。其中一項技巧是後設認知框架下的「延後憂慮」，透過引導個體將憂慮延至指定時段處理，而非即時投入憂慮思緒之中，從而增加其掌控感。然而，將延後憂慮作為單獨介入措施以管理癌症復發的恐懼的效果，至今仍未經驗證。 本研究旨在進行一項隨機對照試驗，評估由朋輩支援員提供的數碼化「慮而不累」自主計劃課程多模式介入，以及數碼化「慮而不累」自主計劃課程單一模式「延後憂慮」介入，對華人癌症康復者亞臨床癌症復發的恐懼水平的影響。研究亦會評估朋輩支援員提供的數碼化癌症復發的恐懼介入方案的成本效益。

17606726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17606726.value: 法治與價值之爭：全球防外國干預法的比較研究

17606726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
