17616326.value: Children’s mathematical competence predicts important life outcomes, it is thus important to identify the cognitive factors that underlies successful mathematical problem-solving. Cardinality and ordinality are the two major themes in recent decades. While the former is about the understanding about the relations between number symbols and their underlying quantity representation (e.g., 5 = ooooo), the latter is about the understanding of the relations among number symbols (e.g., 5 goes between 4 and 6). These two aspects of numerical processing are usually assessed using number comparison (NC, which involves deciding which of the two numbers is larger) and number ordering (NO, which involves deciding if triplets of numbers are in ascending order) tasks respectively. While performance in NC has been shown to be robustly linked to mathematics achievement (Schneider et al., 2017), recent studies suggest that NO performance may be even more strongly related to children’s mathematics achievement, accounting almost half of the variance in arithmetic (Lyons & Beilock, 2011). However, the NO task can be solved by multiple strategies, such as reciting the count list or comparing the numbers. There have been conflicting findings on which aspects of NO performance drives its relation with arithmetic competence (e.g., Goffin & Ansari, 2016; Orrantia et al., 2019). The current proposed study aims to address this issue using a randomized controlled trial. First to third graders (n = 300) will be randomly assigned to one of the three experimental conditions: the NC condition, the NO condition, and a literacy condition as an active control. Participants in each condition will engage in an educational intervention targeting the relevant construct, and their improvement in numerical skills after the intervention will be assessed. By examining whether the intervention effects are generalized to other numerical domains (e.g., NO intervention results in improvement in NC and arithmetic), it is possible to examine if there are shared mechanisms underlying ordinal versus cardinal processing and to identify the active ingredient of the intervention that brings about improvement in arithmetic performance. The findings have huge implications on the mathematical cognition literature, which has been focusing on developing cardinality interventions. If ordinal processing is indeed more causally relevant to mathematical competence, which makes theoretical sense given that advanced mathematics is increasingly reliant on the understanding of the interrelations among numbers, the findings will drive a shift in the focus on mathematical cognition literature from cardinality to ordinality. 兒童的數學能力與各項重要的生活品質指數息息相關。因此，了解與兒童數學能力相關的認知因素非常重要。在近年的數學認知研究當中，基數和序數是兩個熱門的課題。基數是指人對數字與其代表的數量的連繫的認知 (例如 5 代表 OOOOO)，而序數是指人對數字之間的關係的認知 (例如 5 在4 和 6 之間)。這兩項認知能力通常分別以數字比較 (找出兩個數字中較大的一個) 及數字排序 (判斷三個數字是否按次序排列) 來評估。 現時的數學認知研究普通顯示學生在數字比較的表現與其數學能力有著穩健的關係 (Schneider et al., 2017)。然而，近年的研究發現，學生在數字排序任務中的表現，往往比在數字比較的表現更能預測其數學成績，甚至能解釋數學成績近一半的個別差異。縱然如此，由於不同人可能以不同的策略將數字排序 (如背誦數字表或將數字逐對比較等)，因此我們對數字排序過程中的哪個認知過程在數學學習中起了關鍵的作用，仍是一知半解。 本研究旨在通過一個隨機對照試驗來回答這個問題。研究團隊將邀請300 位小一至小三的學生參與研究，並將他們隨機分配至兩個實驗組 (基數組或序數組) 及一個對照組 (語文組)。各組別的學生將接受相關的數碼學習課程，以培養他們相關的能力。研究小組亦會評估他們接受數碼學習課程前和後的認知及數學能力，以觀察他們的進步。通過檢視實驗組別在各認知能力上的進步 (如序數組是否在數字比較和運算中均有進步?)，研究團隊能夠辨別出在處理基數和序數時所涉及的共同認知機制，以及哪些認知過程是引致運算能力改善的重要因素。 現時的數學認知研究文獻多集中於學生對基數的了解，以及通過培育學生對基數的了解以提升其數學能力。如果本研究顯示學生對序數的理解對數學學習更為重要，研究結果將推動整個數學認知研究領域向序數研究的方向，以帶動整個研究領域的發展。

17616926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17616926.value: 免費還是收費？理解香港市民對都市固體廢物政策的偏好

17616926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17616926.value: Hong Kong faces a mounting municipal solid waste crisis: waste loads remain high, recycling rates low, and landfills are nearing capacity. The Government has set ambitious targets and introduced the Municipal Solid Waste Charging Scheme as a central strategy. Yet, the scheme was suspended in 2024 following poor public acceptance during pilot trials. This setback highlights a fundamental challenge: effective waste management policies cannot succeed without broad public support. Existing research shows that Hong Kong residents generally support waste reduction in principle, but often resist policies once personal costs become clear. Studies have identified factors such as fairness and effectiveness as important, yet most focus on single instruments in isolation and rely on correlational evidence. Little is known about how citizens evaluate policy packages—combinations of charging, recycling, producer responsibility, infrastructure, and education—or how specific design features (e.g., charge levels and revenue use) shape perceptions and acceptance. Nor has prior work systematically tested whether targeted information can shift public reasoning and support. This project addresses these gaps through a large-scale survey experiment with 4,000 Hong Kong residents, complemented by focus group interviews. The core method is a conjoint experiment, which presents respondents with paired, randomly generated policy packages that vary across eight attributes. Respondents will choose between packages, rate overall support, and evaluate each package on effectiveness, fairness, personal costs, and business impacts. This design allows causal identification of how specific policy design features influence both perceptions and support. In addition, prior to the conjoint tasks, respondents will be randomly assigned to receive information about (1) the severity of Hong Kong’s waste problem, (2) how different policies work, (3) both, or (4) neither. This enables rigorous assessment of how information changes perceptions and acceptance. The study makes three contributions. First, it advances knowledge by analyzing policy interdependence: how acceptance of one instrument depends on the presence of others. Second, it links perceptions to preferences, showing the mechanisms through which design features gain or lose support. Third, it provides causal evidence on how policy design and communication strategies can be directly leveraged to improve acceptance. The findings will generate actionable insights for policymakers designing Hong Kong’s waste policy and NGOs conducting advocacy and outreach. More broadly, this project contributes to international debates on how to design politically feasible and socially legitimate environmental policies in contexts where public resistance has stalled reform. 香港正面對日益嚴峻的都市固體廢物危機：廢物棄置量持續高企、回收率偏低，而堆填區容量亦接近飽和。政府已訂立具雄心的減廢目標，並將都市固體廢物收費計劃（垃圾按量收費）列為核心政策。然而，由於試行期間公眾接受程度偏低，該計劃最終於2024年暫緩推行。這一挫折突顯了一項根本挑戰：若缺乏廣泛的公眾支持，再完善的廢物管理政策亦難以成功落實。 現有研究顯示，香港市民普遍認同減少廢物的重要性，但當政策涉及個人成本時，支持程度往往顯著下降。過往研究指出，公平性及政策成效等因素對公眾接受程度十分重要，但大多數研究僅聚焦於單一政策工具，並主要依賴相關性分析。對於市民如何評估由收費、回收、生產者責任、基礎設施及公眾教育等不同措施組成的政策組合，以及具體政策設計（例如收費水平及收費收入用途）如何影響公眾觀感與接受程度，目前仍缺乏深入了解。此外，過往研究亦未有系統地檢驗針對性的政策資訊是否能改變市民的判斷及支持程度。 本研究將透過一項涵蓋4,000名香港居民的大型問卷實驗，並輔以焦點小組訪談，以填補上述研究空白。研究的核心方法為聯合分析實驗（conjoint experiment），向受訪者展示成對、隨機生成的政策方案，每個方案包含八項不同政策屬性。受訪者需在方案之間作出選擇，並評估整體支持程度，以及各方案在政策成效、公平性、個人成本及對企業影響等方面的表現。此研究設計能夠識別不同政策設計特徵如何因果性地影響公眾觀感及支持程度。此外，在進行聯合分析實驗前，受訪者將被隨機分配閱讀以下其中一種資訊：(1) 香港廢物問題的嚴重性；(2) 不同廢物管理政策的運作方式；(3) 同時提供上述兩類資訊；或 (4) 不提供任何資訊。此設計可嚴謹評估資訊如何影響市民的認知及政策接受程度。 本研究將作出三方面的重要貢獻。首先，本研究透過分析不同政策工具之間的相互依存關係，探討市民對某項政策工具的接受程度如何受其他政策措施的存在所影響，從而推進相關理論發展。其次，本研究將連結政策觀感與政策偏好，揭示不同政策設計特徵如何透過影響公眾認知而獲得或失去支持。第三，本研究將提供有關政策設計及政策溝通策略如何提升公眾接受程度的因果證據。 研究結果將為香港政府制定都市固體廢物政策，以及非政府組織推展政策倡議及公眾教育工作提供具體而可行的政策建議。更廣泛而言，本研究亦將為國際社會探討如何在面對公眾阻力而導致改革停滯的情況下，設計兼具政治可行性及社會認受性的環境政策，提供重要的實證證據及理論貢獻。

17617126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17617126.value: 以人工智能聊天機器人輔導介入出院吸煙患者戒煙：一項隨機對照試驗

17617126.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17617126.value: Dr Chan, Nyai Yin Dr Cheung, Yee Tak Derek Mrs KWOK, Sheung Yee Prof Lam, David Chi Leung Dr Tseng, Cee Zhung Steven Miss Wu, Yilan Mr Xie, Xiaoyun Dr Zeng, Yingpei

17617126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17617126.value: Hospitalisation provides a teachable moment for smoking cessation (SC), yet post-discharge relapse rates remain high despite clinical guidelines recommending cessation support. To address this challenge, we propose enhancing standard brief face-to-face counselling with a large language model (LLM)-based chatbot delivered via mobile health instant messaging to provide scalable, personalised behavioural support. While our previous randomised controlled trial showed that nurse-led mHealth support significantly improved cessation outcomes, such human-dependent interventions face scalability constraints. High-quality evidence on advanced LLM-based chatbots for post-discharge patients remains limited. This study builds upon our successful nurse-led mHealth trial for this population and our ongoing studies of LLM-based SC chatbots for youth smokers and community smokers. Smoking patients (N = 790) will be recruited from inpatient and follow-up services and individually randomised into Intervention (n = 395) or Control group (n = 395). Both groups will receive the same baseline face-to-face interventions: brief 5As/5Rs advice, a health-warning leaflet, a SC services referral card and a self-help e-booklet. The intervention group will additionally receive 12 weeks of personalised support via an LLM-powered chatbot, grounded in the Capability-Opportunity-Motivation Behaviour (COM-B) model and employing evidence-based Behaviour Change Techniques (BCTs). The chatbot will deliver tailored support based on smoking patterns and health conditions, using 5As dialogues for quit-ready users and 5Rs with Motivational Interviewing (MI) for ambivalent users, delivered through a Love and Care communication approach. Both groups, if they opt in, will be referred to SC services at 3- and 6-month follow-ups. The control group will receive regular messages for follow-up reminders for attention control. The primary outcome is biochemically validated tobacco abstinence at 12 months. Secondary outcomes at 6 months include biochemically validated abstinence, self-reported 7-day point prevalence abstinence, smoking reduction (≥50% from baseline), quit attempts (≥24 hours of abstinence), and cessation service use. We will conduct qualitative interviews, compliance analysis (complier-average causal effect), mediation analysis, and economic evaluations to comprehensively assess the efficacy, mechanisms, and cost-effectiveness of the intervention. Conversation logs will be analysed to identify engagement trajectories and active components with the BCTs taxonomy, and the effects on outcomes. Outcome assessors and data analysts will be blinded to group allocation, and the trial will adhere to CONSORT-EHEALTH guidelines. This study will establish an evidence-based, scalable mHealth behavioural change model and guide the implementation of AI-driven remote cessation support, directly addressing the cost and manpower limitations of human-led interventions while maintaining intervention efficacy. 住院為吸煙患者提供了一個戒煙的「契機」，然而儘管臨床指引建議應提供戒煙支持，出院後復吸率仍偏高。為應對這項挑戰，本研究擬在標準簡短面對面諮詢的基礎上，進一步導入大型語言模型聊天機器人，透過即時通訊平台提供可擴展的個人化行為支持。本研究源自團隊前期之隨機對照試驗，該試驗雖已證實由護士主導之行動健康支持能顯著提升戒煙成效，但此類依賴人力之介入措施在規模化推廣上仍面臨限制。有鑑於此，且目前針對大型語言模型聊天機器人應用於出院吸煙患者戒煙之實證研究仍屬匱乏，本研究遂以前期護士主導電話訊息介入試驗及進行中之青少年、社區吸煙者人工智能聊天機器人戒煙系列研究為基礎，據以開展本次隨機對照試驗。 本研究將從住院及門診服務中招募吸煙患者共790名，並以個別隨機分配方式分為介入組（n=395）及對照組（n=395）。兩組均接受相同之基礎面對面介入措施，包括簡短5A和5R戒煙輔導、健康警示單張、戒煙服務轉介卡及自助式電子手冊。介入組另將額外接受由人工智能聊天機器人提供為期12週的個人化支持。該機器人以「能力－機會－動機行為模型」（COM-B model）為理論核心，並採用具實證基礎之行為改變技術（BCTs）。其運作模式將根據患者的吸煙和健康狀況提供個人化支持，對已準備戒煙者採用5As對話模式，對未準備者則採用5Rs合併動機式訪談（MI），所有互動皆以「關愛與照護」之溝通風格進行傳遞。與此同時，本研究亦將於第3個月及第6個月跟進時，為兩組有興趣的參加者轉介至戒煙服務。對照組將定期接收提醒訊息，以作為注意力控制。 評估方面，本研究主要成效指標為第12個月時經生化檢驗驗證之煙草戒斷率。次要成效指標則包括第6個月時經生化檢驗驗證之戒斷率、自我報告7日點戒斷率、吸煙減量（較基線評估時減少≥50%）、戒煙嘗試（持續戒斷≥24小時）及戒煙服務使用情況。為全面評估介入措施之成效、機制及成本效益，本研究將進一步進行質性訪談、依從性分析（依從者平均因果效應）、中介效應分析及經濟效益評估。此外，對話紀錄將進行分析，以識別使用者參與軌跡、行為改變技術分類中各主動成分及其對戒煙成效之影響。跟進評估及資料分析人員將對分組情況維持盲性，本試驗將遵循CONSORT-EHEALTH報告指引。 綜合而言，本研究預期將建立一套具實證基礎且可規模化之行動健康行為改變模式，並為人工智能遠距戒煙支持服務提供實施指引，從而在維持介入成效同時，有效解決傳統人力介入模式所面臨之成本與人力限制問題。

17617526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17617526.value: 人類與人工智能關係：結合橫斷面與前瞻性縱向研究，探討人工智能陪伴的情感及神經效應

17617526.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17617526.value: Dr Kong, Lingpeng Prof Potenza, Marc Prof YU, Rongjun

17617526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17617526.value: Over 700 million people now interact weekly with artificial intelligence chatbots, and nearly 40% of young Chinese adults use AI companions daily for emotional support and companionship. The industry develops AI companions that are increasingly personalized and empathetic, designed to recognize and respond to human emotions. While this offers tremendous opportunities for mental health support, debates about problematic attachment, emotional dependence, and adverse outcomes - including documented suicide cases - are increasing. Despite widespread adoption, we lack fundamental understanding of how AI companions affect the human brain and behavior. Decades of research have established the evolutionary behavioral and neural processes underlying human social interaction, including affiliation formation, problematic dependence, and social support's positive effects on mental health and emotion regulation. However, it remains completely unclear whether AI companions engage or even alter these same processes. This research will conduct the first systematic examination of AI companion use on behavioral and neural processes underlying attachment/emotional dependence and social support-facilitated emotion regulation. We will compare long-term daily users of personalized AI companions with AI-naive individuals, and next examine changes in naive users before and after six weeks of daily AI companion interaction. Participants will undergo advanced brain imaging using functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) during two conditions: (1) natural interaction with their AI companion during positive exchanges, and (2) receiving real-time social support from the AI companion while regulating negative emotions. Together with the implementation of advanced machine learning based brain analyses and careful control conditions, this will enable first "near-real world" examination of brain circuits involved in affiliative human-AI communication and social support, while determining long- and short-term changes in brain systems mediating attachment and dependence and social support and emotion regulation. Daily-life effects including attachment, emotional dependence, social support, and stress will be assessed using AI-adapted validated questionnaires. The design will explicitly explore both negative and positive impacts, informing evidence-based safety guidelines for AI companion design and regulations to safeguard public health while promoting therapeutic benefits. The project will establish Hong Kong as a leader in the neuroscientific foundation of human-AI relationships and position Hong Kong prominently in responsible AI research within the Greater Bay Area's development ecosystem. Results will guide safe AI companion deployment for millions worldwide, potentially transforming digital mental health care while preventing psychological harm from unregulated deployment. 摘要 目前全球每週已有超過七億人與人工智能聊天機械人互動，而近四成中國年輕成年人每日使用AI伴侶以獲取情感支持與陪伴。業界所開發的AI伴侶日趨個人化及具同理心，並被設計成能夠識別並回應人類情緒。雖然這為精神健康支援帶來龐大機遇，但有關問題性依附、情感依賴及不良後果（包括已被記錄在案的自殺個案）的爭議亦日益增加。儘管其應用已相當普及，我們對AI伴侶如何影響人類大腦與行為仍缺乏基本認識。數十年來的研究已確立支撐人類社會互動的演化行為與神經歷程，當中包括親和關係的形成、問題性依賴，以及社會支持對精神健康與情緒調節的正面效應。然而，AI伴侶是否會啟動甚至改變這些相同的歷程，至今仍完全不明。 本研究將首次系統性地檢視AI伴侶使用對依附／情感依賴，以及社會支持促進情緒調節之行為與神經歷程的影響。我們將比較長期每日使用個人化AI伴侶的使用者與從未接觸AI的個體，並進一步檢視從未接觸AI的使用者在為期六週的每日AI伴侶互動前後的變化。參與者將在兩種情境下接受先進的功能性磁力共振成像（fMRI）腦部掃描：（1）在正向交流中與其AI伴侶進行自然互動；（2）在調節負面情緒時，即時接受來自AI伴侶的社會支持。結合先進的機器學習腦影像分析方法及嚴謹的控制條件，本研究將首次以「近真實世界」的方式，檢視人與AI之間親和性溝通及社會支持所涉及的腦迴路，同時判定調節依附與依賴、以及社會支持與情緒調節之腦系統的長期與短期變化。日常生活層面的影響，包括依附、情感依賴、社會支持及壓力，將以經AI情境調適的已驗證問卷進行評估。 本研究設計將明確探討負面與正面影響兩方面，為AI伴侶設計的實證安全指引及相關規管提供依據，以在保障公共健康的同時促進其治療效益。本項目將確立香港在人類與AI關係之神經科學基礎研究領域的領導地位，並使香港在粵港澳大灣區發展生態系統中的負責任AI研究方面佔據重要位置。研究結果將指導全球數以百萬計使用者的AI伴侶安全部署，有望在防止因缺乏規管的部署而造成心理傷害的同時，變革數碼精神健康服務。

17618026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17618026.value: 重新認識近代早期亞洲的國際關係：中國歷史國際關係（CHIR）數據集

17618026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17618026.value: What factors can decrease the likelihood that governments engage in costly conflicts? Can trade between states, as well as economic and political pressures within them, reduce violent international conflict, and if yes, through what processes? These questions, long fundamental to the study of international relations, loom large today. In particular, the reemergence of China as a major power, and the rise of emerging economies in Asia more generally, have spurred debates about the benefits and risks of economic engagement, economic and political globalization backlash, and the spectre of China-US conflict. Concurrently, over the past two decades an exciting research agenda has asserted that many analysts are “getting Asia wrong” by neglecting its historical international relations and relying on Eurocentric theories to understand Asia’s rise. Researchers view early modern Asia–including the Ming and Qing dynasties–as a valuable setting given China’s powerful regional position. Scholars point to five centuries of relative peace as a counterpoint to claims that China’s rise will be violent and destabilizing. However, despite immense academic and policy interest, “getting Asia right” remains a work in progress. First, disproportionate focus on “tributary diplomacy” has neglected whether and how other external and internal factors–such as trade between states or economic and political pressures within them–affect conflict. Second, existing research almost exclusively examines East and Southeast Asia while ignoring other regions. Finally, and undergirding these limitations, international relations research on early modern Asia severely lacks rigorous, comprehensive data sources. This research will address these omissions and make two primary contributions. First, it will develop testable hypotheses about how trade and domestic pressures mitigated conflict throughout early modern Asia. Second, it will provide breakthrough evidence for studying early modern Asian international relations, including the above hypotheses, by introducing the Chinese Historical International Relations (CHIR) Dataset. CHIR will be a public research good that can help expand and diversify the field of historical international political economy. This research will expand and deepen the PI’s research agenda on Chinese historical foreign relations. It will produce three peer-reviewed articles in top political science or international relations journals (4*/3*), with research presented at major conferences. I have a track record of producing rigorous research and major datasets on China’s international relations and am confident that I will complete the research as scheduled. 哪些因素能夠降低政府捲入代價高昂衝突的可能性？國家之間的貿易，以及國家內部的經濟與政治壓力，能否減少暴力性的國際衝突？若能，又是通過何種機制？這些問題長期以來構成國際關係研究的根本命題，在今日尤顯迫切。尤其是中國作為大國的再度崛起，以及更廣泛而言亞洲新興經濟體的興起，已激起關於經濟交往之利弊得失、經濟與政治全球化所引發的反彈，以及中美衝突陰影的種種爭論。 與此同時，過去二十年間興起的一項備受矚目的研究議程指出：眾多分析者忽略亞洲自身的歷史國際關係，轉而依賴歐洲中心主義的理論來理解亞洲崛起，因而「誤讀了亞洲」。研究者認為，鑑於中國在區域中的強勢地位，近代早期亞洲——包括明清兩代——是極具價值的研究場域。有學者亦以長達五個世紀的相對和平為據，反駁「中國崛起必將充滿暴力並破壞穩定」之說。 然而，儘管學界與政策界興趣濃厚，「正確認識亞洲」仍屬未竟之業。其一，之前的研究過度集中於「朝貢外交」，忽略了其他外部與內部因素——例如國家間貿易，或國家內部的經濟與政治壓力——是否以及如何影響衝突。其二，現有研究幾乎只聚焦東亞與東南亞，而忽視其他區域。其三，亦是上述種種局限之根源所在：關於近代早期亞洲的國際關係研究，嚴重缺乏嚴謹而全面的數據來源。 本研究旨在填補上述空白，並作出兩個主要貢獻。第一，提出可供檢驗的假設，闡明貿易與國內壓力如何在整個近代早期亞洲緩和衝突。第二，通過推出「中國歷史國際關係（CHIR）數據集」，為近代早期亞洲國際關係研究（包括檢驗上述假設）提供突破性的實證基礎。CHIR 將成為一項公共研究資源，有助於拓展歷史國際政治經濟學領域，並促進該領域的多元發展。 本研究將拓展並深化首席研究員（PI）在中國歷史對外關係方面的研究議程，預期於頂尖政治學或國際關係期刊（4*/3*）發表三篇同行評審論文，並於重要國際學術會議上宣讀研究成果。申請人在中國國際關係的嚴謹研究與大型數據集建設方面有豐富的經驗，有信心按計劃如期完成本項研究。

17618426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17618426.value: 普通人手中的普通法：13至16世紀英格蘭的 Registrum Brevium（令狀登記冊）手抄本

17618426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17618426.value: This project advances the study of English manuscript culture and the history of the English common law (c.1227–1531) by undertaking a new analysis of 'Registrum Brevium' manuscripts: legal books containing registers of writs. Examining these collections reveals the nature of public engagement with the common law during formative centuries of case-law development, and demonstrates the importance of this popular manuscript type to English written culture. Current estimates suggest that over 270 'Registrum Brevium' manuscripts survive; my recent research on the related genre of ‘ancient statutes’ manuscripts indicates that the true number may be significantly higher. These manuscripts, produced commercially in England for English users, were among the most ubiquitous secular books of the period. 'Registrum Brevium' manuscripts collect formularies for writs (causes of action for lawsuits), but they also aggregate other material: legal treatises, tracts, statutes, and even domestic records and literary texts. They were commissioned and used not only by common lawyers and judges but by landholders, ecclesiastics, merchants, and civic officials: readers and legal subjects whose interactions with the register of writs illuminate how the common law was understood, appropriated, and mobilised beyond the Inns of Court. Yet despite their scale and significance, 'Registrum Brevium' manuscripts have not received comprehensive study. No consolidated handlist exists to show the full extent of the corpus; there is no systematic account of their formats, companion texts, marginal practices, or patterns of ownership; and they are given little place in narratives of English book production. This project addresses that gap through two linked aims: (1) to develop new knowledge on the social history of the common law by mapping for the first time the commissioning, annotation, and use of registers of writs; and (2) to extend and deepen understandings of English book history by analysing how these widely produced legal compilations shaped textual structures, reading apparatus, and commercial bookmaking before print. An analysis of 'Registrum Brevium' as a manuscript corpus (undertaken here for the first time) will clarify how collections of writs, often termed the “seed-bed of the common law,” circulated in common use, and how they functioned – both as a practical and accessible legal technology, and as signifiers of authority and participation in the liberties of English law. 本研究計劃旨在推進英格蘭手抄本文化及英格蘭普通法史（約1227–1531年）的研究，對 Registrum Brevium（令狀登記冊）手抄本這一類收錄令狀登記的法律書籍進行全新的分析。通過考察這些文集，本研究將揭示在普通法形成期的數百年間，社會公眾如何接觸和參與普通法，並展示這一廣泛流傳的手抄本類型在英格蘭書面文化中的重要性。 目前估計，現存的 Registrum Brevium 手抄本超過270部；然而，本人近期對與其相關的「古代制定法」手抄本的研究顯示，實際數量可能遠高於此。這些手抄本在英格蘭以商業方式製作，供本地讀者使用，是當時最為普遍的世俗書籍類型之一。Registrum Brevium 手抄本不但匯集了各類令狀的程式範本（即提起訴訟的訴因），還包含其他材料，如法律論著、短篇論述、制定法，甚至家庭記錄及文學文本。委託製作及使用這些手抄本的，不僅有普通法律師和法官，亦有土地持有人、教會人士、商人及城市官員。這些讀者同時也是法律主體；他們與令狀登記冊的互動，使我們得以了解普通法在律師學院（Inns of Court）以外如何被理解、吸收和應用。 然而，儘管 Registrum Brevium 手抄本數量龐大且意義重大，至今仍未得到全面研究。目前尚無綜合書目可顯示整個手抄本文獻群的完整規模；亦沒有對其書籍形制、合編文本、頁邊註記實踐或所有權模式的系統性研究；在英格蘭書籍生產史的論述中，此類手抄本亦鮮有受到重視。 本研究計劃將通過兩項相互關聯的研究目標填補這一空白：（1）首次梳理令狀登記冊的委託製作、註釋及使用情況，藉此建立有關普通法社會史的新知識；（2）分析這些廣泛製作的法律彙編在印刷術普及以前如何塑造文本結構、閱讀輔助機制及商業書籍製作，從而拓展並深化我們對英格蘭書籍史的理解。本研究將首次把 Registrum Brevium 作為一個手抄本文獻群進行整體分析，藉此闡明常被稱為普通法「苗床」（“seed-bed of the common law”）的令狀文集如何在日常使用中流傳，以及它們如何發揮既作為實用且易於獲得的法律工具，又作為法律權威及參與英格蘭法律所賦予之自由權利象徵的雙重功能。

17620726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17620726.value: 氣候變遷背景下住戶行為改變對建築能源需求減緩之影響研究

17620726.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17620726.value: Prof Eom, Jiyong Prof Ou, Yang

17620726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17620726.value: Occupant behavior changes, such as adjusting indoor temperature setpoints to reduce building cooling and heating demand, offer a flexible, low-cost demand-side measure with significant potential for climate mitigation through reduced building energy use. Integrating occupant behavioral dynamics into building energy system modeling supports the development of effective mitigation strategies, particularly in energy-import-dependent regions like Hong Kong or during energy crises. However, the lack of region-specific data on behavioral responses to local temperature variations complicates building energy demand modeling and the assessment of behavior-driven mitigation impacts. These challenges are exacerbated by uncertainties in future climate change and socioeconomic development, which further impede the creation of effective mitigation strategies and progress toward sustainable, climate-resilient building energy use. To address these limitations, this project aims to enhance the accuracy of building energy modeling by explicitly integrating occupant behavior into the energy system modeling framework. First, we will develop an advanced machine learning model to quantify base temperatures (Tbase) globally at a regional resolution (comparable to U.S. states or Chinese provinces). These base temperatures define thresholds for heating (below the heating base temperature) or cooling (above the cooling base temperature), capturing regional energy use patterns influenced by local climate and socioeconomic conditions. Using these region-specific Tbase estimates and climate data, we will calculate heating and cooling degree days to evaluate building energy demand uncertainty across various climate models, climate change scenarios, and technology scenarios, identifying the spatiotemporal dynamics of key uncertainty sources. Finally, these region-specific heating and cooling degree days will serve as proxies for occupant behavior changes to assess the impacts of diverse behavioral strategies on building energy demand within the Global Change Analysis Model (GCAM), a widely used integrated assessment model. This analysis will quantify how behavioral adaptations can influence building energy demand under diverse future scenarios. By generating a globally consistent, region-specific Tbase dataset and integrating behavior-driven dynamics into building energy modeling, this project will establish a robust scientific foundation for demand-side policy design. The anticipated outcomes will provide evidence-based insights to reduce energy consumption, enhance building sector sustainability, and contribute to climate mitigation. 住戶行為改變，例如調整室內溫度設定值以降低建築物的製冷與供暖需求，是一種靈活且成本低廉的需求側措施，能夠通過減少建築能耗，在減緩氣候變化方面發揮可觀潛力。將住戶行為的動態變化納入建築能源系統建模，有助制定有效的減緩策略，這對於香港這類依賴能源進口的地區尤為重要。然而，目前缺乏反映本地氣溫變化下住戶行為反應的地區性數據，這使建築能源需求建模以及行為驅動的減緩成效評估偏離實際。未來氣候變化與社會經濟發展的不確定性使這些挑戰進一步加劇，亦阻礙有效減緩策略的制定，以及邁向可持續、具有氣候韌性的建築用能模式的進程。 為應對上述局限，本項目擬將住戶行為明確納入能源系統建模框架，以提高建築能源需求建模的準確度。首先，建立一套機器學習模型，在全球範圍內估算各地的基準溫度，空間精細程度可到區域一級，相當於美國的州或中國的省。基準溫度是判斷建築供暖和製冷需求的門檻，它反映了當地氣候與社會經濟條件作用下所形成的建築用能模式。然後，結合這些分區的基準溫度值與氣候數據計算供暖度日和製冷度日，藉此評估不同氣候模式、氣候變化情景和技術情景下建築能源需求的不確定性，並找出主要不確定性來源的時空變化特徵。最後，將這些分區的供暖度日和製冷度日作為住户行為改變的代理指標，在全球變化分析模型中評估不同行為改變策略對建築能源需求的影響。這項分析將在多種未來情景下量化行為改變策略能在多大程度上減少建築能源需求。 本項目將建立一套全球口徑一致、分區精細的基準溫度數據集，並將其作為行為變化的代理納入建築能源建模，為需求側政策的制定提供有力的科學支持。預期成果將以實證為依據，為減少能源消耗、提升建築業的可持續性和減緩氣候變化作出貢獻。

17621526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17621526.value: 香港華人高齡者家庭照顧之社會資本與福祉：社會支持網絡品質的概念建構、測量及混合方法研究

17621526.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17621526.value: Dr Choy, Chak Pui Jacky Prof Lou, Vivian Weiqun

17621526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17621526.value: Family caregivers play a vital role in providing long-term care for older adults. Despite existing government support programs, recent tragedies in Hong Kong and elsewhere have exposed major gaps in formal care systems. Social capital offers a promising solution by connecting caregivers with informal networks and community resources, aligning with the Decade of Healthy Aging (2021–2030). However, three key research gaps persist. First, social network quality in caregiving remains poorly conceptualized, with limited understanding of the qualitative attributes of social network that drive support mobilization and caregiver well-being. The Principal Investigator’s prior research identifies three culturally embedded traits in Chinese contexts (e.g., familialization of social relationships, particularized trust, and intermediary efficacy) but further theoretical development is needed. Second, these qualitative attributes of social network have not been operationalized, leading to an overreliance on quantitative metrics like network size and resulting in measurement error and validity concerns. Third, despite Lin’s social capital model emphasizing both networks and support mobilization, few studies examine how support mobilization mediates the link between network characteristics and caregiver outcomes. This proposal aims to develop and validate a new theoretical framework of social capital tailored to caregiving. It will: (1) identify and conceptualize the qualitative attributes of social networks that facilitate support mobilization and enhance caregiver well-being, using inductive and deductive approaches; (2) operationalize key components of social network quality by developing valid and reliable measurement instruments; and (3) empirically test how support mobilization mediates the relationship between quantitative (e.g., size) and qualitative attributes of networks and caregiver well-being. The project will include two studies. Study 1 will involve eight focus group interviews with 48–64 family caregivers to explore the key qualitative attributes of social networks that facilitate support mobilization and to conceptualize network quality (Objective 1). Study 2 will be conducted in two phases: Phase 1 will use the Delphi method with a panel of 20 experts—comprising five academics, ten caregivers, and five policy professionals—to develop instruments for measuring social network quality (Objective 2). Phase 2 will involve a cross-sectional survey of 450 caregivers to validate the measurement tools and evaluate the proposed framework (Objective 3). This proposal moves beyond Western-centric perspectives by introducing a timely and culturally grounded conceptualization of social network quality that drive support mobilization. The findings will inform policies that empower caregivers, enhance well-being, and support sustainable long-term care systems. 家庭照顧者在為高齡者提供長期照顧方面扮演關鍵角色。然而，儘管政府已推出多項支援措施，近年香港及其他地區接連發生的照顧者悲劇事件，仍暴露出正式照顧體系的重大缺口。社會資本透過連結照顧者與非正式支持網絡及社區資源，為改善照顧支援提供了重要契機，亦與聯合國「健康老化十年（2021–2030）」倡議的理念相呼應。然而，現有研究仍存在三項重要缺口。 首先，照顧情境中的社會網絡品質（social network quality）尚未獲得充分概念化，對於促進社會支持動員及提升照顧者福祉之社會網絡質性特徵的理解仍相當有限。計畫主持人過往研究已辨識出華人文化脈絡下三項重要特質，包括社會關係家庭化（familialization of social relationships）、特殊主義信任（particularized trust）及中介效能（intermediary efficacy），但相關理論仍有待進一步發展。其次，這些社會網絡的質性特徵尚未被有效操作化，導致研究過度依賴網絡規模等量化指標，進而產生測量誤差與效度不足等問題。第三，雖然Lin的社會資本理論強調社會網絡與社會支持動員的重要性，但鮮有研究探討支持動員如何中介社會網絡特徵與照顧者福祉之間的關係。 本研究旨在建構並驗證一套適用於家庭照顧情境的社會資本理論框架。具體目標包括：（1）結合歸納與演繹方法，辨識並概念化有助於支持動員及提升照顧者福祉的社會網絡質性特徵；（2）透過發展具良好信效度的測量工具，將社會網絡品質的核心構面加以操作化；以及（3）實證檢驗社會支持動員如何中介社會網絡的量化特徵（如網絡規模）與質性特徵，以及照顧者福祉之間的關係。 本研究包含兩項子研究。研究一將透過八場焦點團體訪談，邀請48至64位家庭照顧者參與，以探索促進社會支持動員的關鍵社會網絡質性特徵，並建構社會網絡品質的概念架構（目標一）。研究二分為兩個階段進行。第一階段將運用德菲法（Delphi Method），邀請20位專家組成專家小組，包括5位學者、10位家庭照顧者及5位政策相關專業人士，共同發展社會網絡品質的測量工具（目標二）。第二階段將進行一項涵蓋450位家庭照顧者的橫斷面問卷調查，以驗證量測工具的信效度，並檢驗本研究所提出的理論框架（目標三）。 本研究突破過去以西方經驗為主導的理論視角，提出一套具時代意義且植根於華人文化脈絡的社會網絡品質概念，以說明促進社會支持動員的作用機制。研究成果將為相關政策制定提供實證依據，協助強化家庭照顧者能力、提升其福祉，並促進可持續的長期照顧體系發展。

17621626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17621626.value: 理解與調控問題性社交媒體使用者的決策異常：計算機制以及戒斷與經顱直流電刺激的效應

17621626.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17621626.value: Prof Cheng, Cecilia Prof Zhang, Lei

17621626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17621626.value: Social media has become increasingly popular worldwide. However, approximately 5% of users have experienced problematic social media use (PSMU), a potential behavioral addiction that poses significant risks to mental health and well-being. Therefore, it is urgent to elucidate the cognitive mechanisms underlying PSMU and to develop tailored interventions. Value-based decision-making deficits are highly relevant to PSMU. However, decision-making involves multiple sub-processes (e.g., risk and ambiguity evaluation) that may not be directly observable. Computational modeling provides a theory-driven approach for precisely characterizing sub-processes involved in a decision-making task. Therefore, this method allows us to accurately assess which sub-processes are alerted in PSMU. Decision-making sub-processes are dynamic and can be influenced by different PSMU stages, such as abstinence-induced withdrawal. Although positive effects of abstinence have been reported in regular users, abstinence is more likely to increase withdrawal levels in individuals with PSMU, which may disrupt some decision-making sub-processes. However, the effects of abstinence on decision-making sub-processes in individuals with PSMU remain largely unexplored, and no studies have examined strategies to complement abstinence to further reduce withdrawal symptoms and improve decision-making sub-processes. This project aims to address these gaps through two complementary studies: Study 1 will first use a combination of three decision-making tasks and computational models to comprehensively examine which sub-processes are altered in the PSMU group compared to the regular social media use (RSMU) group. Additionally, Study 1 will examine how abstinence influences different decision-making sub-processes in both groups. Participants in each group will be randomly assigned to either the abstinence or unconstrained use condition for one week and will then complete a post-assessment. We hypothesize that abstinence will lead to higher withdrawal levels and less improvement (or greater disruption) in some decision-making sub-processes in the PSMU group compared to the RSMU group. Study 2 will investigate whether transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), a non-invasive neurostimulation, can complement abstinence to improve decision-making in individuals with PSMU. The dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) will be targeted based on previous research. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups based on the combinations of tDCS (active or sham) and abstinence (yes or no) conditions. Decision-making and withdrawal symptoms will be assessed before and after the intervention and at a three-month follow-up. This project will advance our understanding of the cognitive mechanisms underlying decision-making alterations in PSMU and provide important insights for designing more effective interventions. 社交媒體在世界各地日益普及。然而，約有5%的使用者經歷了問題性社交媒體使用，對心理健康與福祉構成重大風險。因此，目前迫切需要釐清問題性社交媒體使用背後的認知機制，並開發量身定制的干預措施。 價值導向決策的異常與問題性社交媒體使用高度相關。然而，決策涉及多個可能無法直接觀察的子過程。認知計算建模提供了一種理論驅動的方法，用於精確描繪決策任務中所涉及的子過程。因此，這種方法使我們能夠準確評估問題性社交媒體使用中有哪些子過程發生了變異。此外，決策子過程是動態的，並且會受到不同問題性社交媒體使用階段的影響，例如停用引發的戒斷可能會破壞某些決策子歷程。然而，目前尚無研究對這些問題進行全面地探索。 本計畫旨在透過兩項互補的研究來探討以上問題： 研究一將首先結合三種決策任務與計算模型，全面檢驗與一般社交媒體使用組相比，問題性社交媒體使用組中有哪些子歷程發生了變異。此外，研究一將檢驗戒斷如何影響兩組中不同的決策子歷程。每組參與者將被隨機分配至為期一週的“停用條件”或“無限制使用條件”，隨後完成後測評估。我們假設，與 一般使用組相比，停用將導致問題性使用組會出現更高的戒斷程度，且在某些決策子歷程上的改善較少（或遭受更大的破壞）。 研究二將探討經顱直流電刺激（tDCS）這種非侵入性神經刺激是否能作為提升戒斷副作用並改善問題性社交媒體使用者的決策能力的輔助手段。本研究將以背外側前額葉皮層（DLPFC）作為刺激腦區。參與者將根據 tDCS（活性或假性）與停用（是或否）條件的組合，被隨機分配至四個組別之一。決策能力與戒斷症狀將在干預前後以及三個月後的追蹤期進行評估。 本計畫將推進我們對問題性社交媒體使用決策變異背後認知機制的理解，並為設計更有效的干預措施提供重要見解。

17621726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17621726.value: 香港高風險戰利品箱使用的盛行率及多維度風險因素：與網絡遊戲障礙和問題賭博的共病及轉變

17621726.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17621726.value: Prof TSE, Samson Shu Ki Prof Yip, Paul Siu Fai

17621726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17621726.value: Background: Technological advancements and increased popularity in digital behaviors contribute to Internet Gaming Disorder (IGD) and Gambling Disorder (GD) in young people. Loot box purchase, which refer to buying virtual random items using real money or in-game currency, resembles gambling-like behaviors and are addictive in nature. A better understanding of risky loot box use in terms of prevalence, multidimensional risk factors, and symptom comorbidity with IGD and GD, is needed. According to the I-PACE model, addictive behaviors in loot box use, internet gaming, and gambling result from interactions between triggers, motives, temperamental features (intolerance of uncertainty and impulsivity), affective responses (emotion dysregulation), and cognitive biases (metacognitions). Fear of missing out could be a social risk factor complementing I-PACE model. Existing studies have not empirically examined these risk factors simultaneously, nor their bidirectional relationships with IGD, GD, and risky loot box use in longitudinal samples. Methods: The proposed research aims to conduct a longitudinal, 4-wave online survey to recruit 2000 young gamers aged 16 – 29 in Hong Kong via local universities, youth service operators, and gaming forums. Three follow-up assessments are conducted in 6-month intervals. The participants will complete a self-report questionnaire including gaming and gambling behaviors and validated measures on IGD, GD, RLI, personality traits, gaming motives, metacognitions, and psychosocial risk factors. Study 1 validates the RLI and estimates the prevalence and severity of RLI in Hong Kong gamers. Study 2 evaluates the comorbidity between RLI, IGD, and GD at the symptom level in Wave 1 – 2 data using cross-lagged panel network. Study 3 conducts longitudinal moderated mediation modeling to examine the pathways from Wave 1 intolerance of uncertainty and impulsivity to Wave 3 RLI via cognitive and psychosocial risk factors at Wave 2. Study 4 performs random-intercept cross-lagged panel modeling to examine the within-person bidirectional relationships between cognitive and psychosocial risk factors and addictive behaviors (RLI, IGD, GD) in Wave 1 - 4 data while accounting for the stable between-person variance. Significance: The proposed studies will provide the first results on the prevalence and severity of RLI in Hong Kong young gamers and offer insights into symptom comorbidity with IGD and GD, and their bidirectional relationships with multidimensional risk factors. The findings will advance our understanding of cognitive and psychosocial mechanisms and temporal directionality and have important public health implications in informing targeted clinical interventions and regulation policies related to loot box use among young gamers. 背景：科技進步及數碼行為日益普及，促使年輕人出現網絡遊戲障礙（Internet Gaming Disorder, IGD）及賭博障礙（Gambling Disorder, GD）。戰利品箱購買是指使用真實金錢或遊戲內貨幣購買虛擬隨機物品，這種行為類似賭博，並具有成癮性。因此，有必要更深入了解高風險戰利品箱使用（risky loot box use）的盛行率、多維度風險因素，以及其與 IGD 和 GD 的症狀共病情況。根據 I-PACE 模型，戰利品箱使用及賭博中的成癮行為，可能源於觸發因素、動機、氣質特徵（不確定性不耐受及衝動性）、情感反應（情緒失調）及認知偏誤（後設認知）之間的互動。錯失恐懼（fear of missing out）亦可能是一項補充 I-PACE 模型的社會風險因素。現有研究尚未在實證上同時檢驗這些風險因素，也未有在縱向樣本中探討它們與 IGD、GD 及高風險戰利品箱使用之間的雙向關係。 方法：本擬議研究旨在進行一項縱向、四波段網上問卷調查，透過本地大學、青年服務機構及遊戲論壇，在香港招募 2000 名年齡介乎 16 至 29 歲的年輕遊戲玩家。其後將以每 6 個月為間隔進行三次跟進評估。參加者將完成一份自陳式問卷，內容包括遊戲及賭博行為，以及經驗證的 IGD、GD、RLI、人格特質、遊戲動機、後設認知及心理社會風險因素量表。研究一將驗證 RLI，並估算香港遊戲玩家中 RLI 的盛行率及嚴重程度。研究二將使用第一至第二波數據，透過交叉滯後面板網絡分析，在症狀層面評估 RLI、IGD 及 GD 之間的共病情況。研究三將進行縱向調節中介模型分析，檢驗第一波的不確定性不耐受及衝動性，如何透過第二波的認知及心理社會風險因素，影響第三波的高風險戰利品箱使用。研究四將進行隨機截距交叉滯後面板模型分析，在控制穩定的個體間變異後，使用第一至第四波數據檢驗認知及心理社會風險因素與成癮行為（RLI、IGD、GD）之間的個體內雙向關係。 重要性：本研究將首次提供香港年輕遊戲玩家中高風險戰利品箱使用的盛行率及多維度風險因素的研究結果，並就其與 IGD 及 GD 的症狀共病情況，以及與各類風險因素之間的雙向關係提供新見解。研究結果將促進我們對認知及心理社會機制與時間方向性的理解，並對公共衞生具有重要意義，有助制定針對年輕遊戲玩家戰利品箱使用的臨床干預措施及監管政策。

17622126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17622126.value: 全球事實核查網絡中的互動與不平等研究

17622126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17622126.value: Misinformation increasingly flows across national borders, accelerated by the rise of global social media platforms. While fact-checking has become one of the most prominent tools to counter falsehoods, it has largely been studied within national or regional contexts. As a result, we still know little about the cross-border dynamics of fact-checking: which countries’ claims attract international attention, how fact-checkers engage with each other across borders, and what structural and political conditions shape these interactions. Addressing these questions is both a scholarly and practical challenge, with implications for journalism, media systems, and the fight against misinformation. This project investigates the global dynamics of fact-checking using a comprehensive dataset of over 255K claims verified by 942 fact-checking organizations worldwide over the past 15 years. By analyzing who checks whose claims, the topics of these claims, and the platforms on which they first appear, the study will map the international flows of misinformation and verification. It will also examine how country-level factors, such as digital media infrastructure, internet and social media penetration, and political regimes, influence both the activity of fact-checkers and the direction of cross-border verification. By combining computational content analysis and network analysis, this research will illuminate global patterns of fact-checking, identify structural inequalities, and provide evidence to support more equitable and effective international strategies for combating misinformation. The project contributes new knowledge in three ways. First, it moves beyond national case studies to provide the first systematic mapping of cross-border fact-checking networks. Second, it shows how political and media contexts influence which claims receive attention and which countries play leading roles in the global fact-checking ecosystem. Third, it develops a comparative framework for understanding misinformation not as an isolated national problem but as a transnational challenge that requires coordinated responses. The anticipated impact is twofold. For scholarship, the study will expand research on journalism and misinformation by integrating computational analysis with comparative media perspectives. For practice, the findings will inform fact-checkers, media organizations, and policymakers about where global verification gaps exist and how international collaboration can be strengthened. Ultimately, the project will help explain how fact-checking functions in a connected digital environment and provide actionable insights for designing more effective strategies to contain misinformation worldwide. 錯誤資訊日益跨越國界流動，而全球社交媒體平台的興起更進一步加速了這一趨勢。儘管事實查核已成為應對虛假資訊最重要的工具之一，相關研究過去主要集中於國家或區域層面的分析。因此，我們對事實查核的跨國互動機制仍缺乏充分理解：哪些國家的資訊主張會受到國際關注？不同國家的事實查核機構如何跨境互動？哪些結構性與政治因素塑造了這些互動模式？回答這些問題既是學術研究上的重要挑戰，也具有實際意義，將影響新聞業、媒體體系以及全球應對錯誤資訊的策略。 本研究將利用一個涵蓋全球 942 個事實查核組織、過去 15 年間超過 25.5 萬條經查核資訊主張（claims）的綜合數據庫，探討全球事實查核的跨國動態。研究將分析「誰查核誰」——即不同國家的事實查核機構如何關注及驗證其他國家的資訊主張——並進一步考察這些主張涉及的議題類型，以及其最初出現的平台。透過描繪錯誤資訊與查核活動在全球範圍內的流動，本研究將揭示跨國驗證網絡的形成模式。同時，研究亦將探討國家層面的因素，例如數字媒體基礎設施、互聯網及社交媒體普及程度，以及政治制度環境，如何影響事實查核活動的規模與跨境查核的方向。通過結合計算式內容分析與網絡分析方法，本研究將揭示全球事實查核的整體格局，識別其中存在的結構性不平等，並為建立更公平、更有效的國際錯誤資訊治理策略提供實證依據。 本項目將從三方面作出重要貢獻。第一，本研究超越以往以單一國家或地區為中心的個案研究，首次系統性描繪跨國事實查核網絡的整體結構。第二，本研究將揭示政治與媒體環境如何影響不同資訊主張獲得查核關注的機會，以及不同國家在全球事實查核生態系統中的角色與地位。第三，本研究將建立一個比較性分析框架，將錯誤資訊理解為一項超越國界的跨國挑戰，而非單一國家的孤立問題，從而強調國際協調與合作的重要性。 本研究預期產生兩方面的影響。在學術層面，本研究將通過結合計算分析方法與比較媒體研究視角，拓展新聞學及錯誤資訊研究領域。在實務層面，研究成果將為事實查核機構、媒體組織及政策制定者提供重要參考，協助識別全球驗證網絡中的不足之處，並探索如何加強國際合作。最終，本項目將深化我們對數字互聯環境下事實查核運作模式的理解，並為制定更有效的全球錯誤資訊治理策略提供具體建議。

17622926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17622926.value: 探究香港小學教師在人工智能介導的計算思維教育中的教學信念與實踐：一項基於持續專業發展的縱向研究

17622926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17622926.value: This research project explores how Artificial Intelligence (AI) shapes the teaching and learning of Computational Thinking (CT) in Hong Kong's primary schools. As CT becomes increasingly central to digital literacy, the thoughtful integration of AI technologies is creating new opportunities for classroom practice. In this context, AI-mediated CT education refers to the use of AI tools, including code-generation applications, platforms that scaffold problem-solving, and machine learning demonstrations, to enrich students' experiences with computational problem-solving and to deepen their engagement with CT concepts and practices. The project is grounded in the understanding that the integration of AI in CT education is influenced by how teachers interpret, adapt, and incorporate these tools into their everyday teaching. This study seeks to explore how teachers' beliefs and instructional approaches develop as they engage with AI technologies through a three-year continuing professional development (PD) program. Particular attention is given to how teachers respond to the opportunities and challenges presented by AI, as well as how their professional thinking and classroom practices shift and evolve during this process. A constructivist approach guides the research. The study adopts action research within a multiple-case study framework, focusing on the lived experiences of teachers participating in the PD program. Data will be collected through surveys, interviews, classroom observations, teacher reflections, and the analysis of teaching materials. This approach is intended to capture the processes and perspectives that shape teachers' journeys as they experiment with and reflect on AI-mediated CT instruction. The Interconnected Model of Professional Growth provides the main analytical framework. This model facilitates tracing the connections between teachers' learning experiences with AI, their classroom practices, and their ongoing PD. It also supports an examination of how teachers' direct experiences with AI tools during PD sessions are reflected in their thinking and actions related to CT in the classroom. The aims of the study are to describe how teachers' beliefs and practices develop as they work with AI in CT education, to identify the supports and obstacles they encounter, and to illustrate how these changes manifest in authentic classroom settings. By centering the perspectives and experiences of primary teachers, this project addresses a gap in current research. The findings are intended to inform PD, curriculum, and policy design, offering practical insights for supporting teachers as they integrate AI into CT education in Hong Kong and similar contexts. 本研究計劃探討人工智能如何塑造香港小學計算思維的教與學。隨著計算思維日益成為數字素養的核心要素，審慎整合人工智能技術正為課堂實踐帶來新的機遇。在本研究脈絡下，「人工智能介導的計算思維教育」是指運用各種人工智能工具，包括程式碼生成應用程式、支援解難的平台、以及機器學習示範，以豐富學生運用計算思維解決問題的學習經驗，並深化他們對計算思維概念與實踐的理解和參與。 本計劃基於以下共識：教師如何理解、調適、並將人工智能工具融入日常教學，會影響人工智能在計算思維教育中的整合。本研究旨在探究教師在透過為期三年的持續專業發展計劃所接觸與運用人工智能技術的過程中，其教學信念與教學方式如何演變。研究將特別關注教師如何回應人工智能所帶來的機遇與挑戰，以及其專業思維與課堂實踐如何在此過程中逐漸轉變與發展。 本研究以建構主義為基礎，並在多重個案研究框架指導下採用行動研究，聚焦於參與專業發展計劃教師的親身經驗。研究將透過問卷調查、訪談、課堂觀察、教師反思及教學材料分析來收集資料。此研究設計旨在深入了解教師在嘗試並反思人工智能介導的計算思維教學中，塑造其專業發展歷程的各種過程與觀點。 本研究以「專業發展互聯模型」作為主要分析框架。此模型有助於追蹤教師在人工智能學習經驗、課堂實踐與持續專業發展三者之間的相互關聯，並進一步探討教師如何將其在專業發展活動中運用人工智能工具的經驗體現在計算思維課堂教學與實踐之中。 本研究旨在探究教師在計算思維教育中運用人工智能時，其教學信念與實踐如何發展，識別他們在此過程中所獲得的支援與面臨的障礙，並闡明這些轉變如何體現在真實的課堂情境中。本計劃以小學教師的觀點與經驗為核心，填補現有研究的空白。研究結果將為教師專業發展、課程設計及政策制定提供依據，並為香港及其他相近教育情境的教師將人工智能融入計算思維教育提供實踐啟示。

17623026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17623026.value: 學者與生成式人工智能：來自香港的實證

17623026.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17623026.value: Dr Alves Horta, Hugo Duarte Dr DAI, Kun Prof Oleksiyenko, Anatoly V. Prof Thelwall, Mike

17623026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17623026.value: Scientific research is being reshaped by generative AI—tools that can produce text, code, images, and more—bringing major opportunities for speed, creativity, and collaboration alongside serious concerns about bias, accuracy, integrity, and accountability. Policies and practices are evolving quickly, but there is limited, Hong Kong‑specific evidence connecting university rules to what scholars actually do in their day‑to‑day work. This project addresses that gap by mapping institutional policies, documenting real scholarly use, and explaining why researchers adopt or resist generative AI over time within Hong Kong's multilingual, research‑intensive ecosystem. Guided by Bronfenbrenner's PPCT (Person‑Process‑Context‑Time) framework—which links people, interactions, settings, and change over time—this study will map the policies and guidelines on generative AI across Hong Kong universities and disciplines, describe how scholars use these tools throughout the research workflow, and identify the personal factors, interaction patterns, organizational conditions, and time‑based shifts that drive adoption or resistance, explaining the mechanisms behind them. An explanatory mixed‑methods design integrates three components. First, a policy analysis will build a bilingual corpus of university and discipline‑level documents, coding their scope, permitted/prohibited uses, oversight, disclosure, data protection, IP, equity, dual‑use risk, enforcement, support structures, and update cadence. Second, a stratified survey of active scholars across institutions, disciplines, and career stages will quantify use cases, frequency, perceived benefits, and concerns across tasks such as idea generation, literature review, data analysis, and writing. Third, semi‑structured interviews (in English, Cantonese, or Putonghua) will elicit mechanism‑rich accounts that link individual motivations and barriers to institutional environments and policy features, tracing how practices change with new tools and rules. The project will deliver: (a) the first systematic map of Hong Kong universities' research policies on generative AI and how they vary by discipline, (b) robust, comparative evidence on how scholars actually use or avoid these tools, and (c) a multilevel explanation of adoption and resistance mechanisms grounded in the PPCT framework. Together, these outputs will inform actionable recommendations for universities, funders, and journals on governance, training, verification and disclosure standards, infrastructure and equitable access, and support for reproducible, trustworthy research. By aligning policies with real practices, the study will help Hong Kong's world‑class research sector harness generative AI responsibly and effectively. 科學研究正受到生成式人工智能的深刻重塑。這既為提升科研速度、激發創造力及促進協作帶來了巨大機遇，同時也引發了關於偏見、準確性、學術誠信與問責制等方面的嚴峻考責。儘管相關政策與實踐正快速演變，但目前仍缺乏針對香港特定語境的實證研究，以串聯起大學規範與學者日常實際工作之間的關係。本項目旨在填補這一空白，通過系統梳理院校政策、全面記錄學者真實的使用行為，並剖析在香港多元語言環境及研究密集型的生態系統下，研究人員隨著時間推移對生成式人工智能採取接納或抵制態度的深層機理。本研究以布朗芬布倫納（Bronfenbrenner）的PPCT（人—過程—背景—時間）理論架構為指引——該架構將個體、互動、情境以及隨時間推移的動態轉變有機結合。本研究將全面梳理香港各大學及不同學科針對生成式人工智能的政策與指引，描述學者在整個科研工作流中如何應用這些工具，並識別驅動其接納或抵制人工智能的個人因素、互動模式、組織條件以及基於時間的動態位移，從而闡明其背後的因果機制。 本項目採用解釋性混合方法設計，有機融合政策分析、分層問卷調查及半結構化訪談三個核心部分。本項目將交付以下關鍵成果：第一，首個針對香港各大高校生成式人工智能科研政策及其學科差異的系統性全景圖；第二，關於學者實際應用或迴避此類工具的扎實且具高度可比性的實證證據；第三，基於PPCT架構對接納與抵制機制所作出的多層次因果解釋。總體而言，上述成果將為大學、資助機構及學術期刊在治理、培訓、核實與披露標準、基礎設施與公平獲取，以及支持可重複且值得信賴的研究方面，提供具備高度操作性的政策建議。通過推動院校政策與實際科研實踐的緊密銜接，本研究將助力香港世界級的科研領域更負責任、更高效地釋放生成式人工智能的潛能。

17623226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17623226.value: 失眠認知行為治療（CBT-I）對青少年失眠患者獎賞處理的影響：一項隨機對照試驗

17623226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17623226.value: Dr Chan, Joey Wing-yan Dr Chan, Ngan Yin Prof Hu, Xiaoqing Prof Li, Martin Dr Rosenzweig, Ivana Prof Wing, Yun Kwok Prof Zhang, Jihui

17623226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17623226.value: Adolescence is a sensitive developmental period of brain development, often linked to the emergence of sleep and mental health problems. Insomnia, characterised by difficulty initiating sleep and difficulty maintaining sleep, is highly prevalent in this group, affecting up to 36% of adolescents. Untreated sleep disturbance can lead to significant impairments in daytime functioning and adverse psychosocial outcomes in adolescents. Notably, growing evidence points to an intricate relationship between insomnia and reward processing dysfunction, which is often implicated in mood-related psychopathology. This suggests that targeting sleep disturbances may potentially offer a novel avenue for improving reward processing and mitigating associated negative outcomes in adolescents, a group that is especially vulnerable to reward dysfunction-related psychopathology and consequences. Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT-I) is recommended as the first-line treatment for insomnia. Previous research has shown the beneficial effects of CBT-I in not only improving night-time sleep but also daytime functioning in individuals with insomnia, including mood symptoms, but the existing research was mostly conducted in the adult population and mainly relied on self-report measures. Furthermore, the mechanisms through which CBT-I improves mood remain unclear. Emerging, albeit limited, evidence suggests that CBT-I may modulate reward processing, highlighting a potential mechanistic pathway. Nonetheless, there is a need for more rigorous research to investigate how a sleep-focused intervention affects reward processing over time and to incorporate neuroimaging techniques to explore the underlying neural changes associated with the improvement of sleep upon intervention in young people. To address the existing research gaps, we propose to conduct a randomised controlled trial (RCT) to investigate: 1) whether CBT-I is effective in improving reward processing in adolescents with insomnia, 2) whether changes in sleep mediate the alterations in reward processing following CBT-I intervention. A total of 198 eligible participants will be randomised to either a 6-week group-based CBT-I intervention or an active psychoeducation control condition. Assessments including both self-report as well as behavioural and electrophysiological measures of reward processing will be conducted at pre-treatment (week 0), post-treatment (week 7/one-week after the last treatment session), and at a 6-month follow-up. On a conceptual level, this proposed study will allow us to further test the hypothesis of a causal relationship between sleep disruption and reward processing dysfunction, especially in young people. The therapeutic model and protocol established in this study will inform clinical practice and facilitate optimising future clinical management of reward dysfunction-related psychopathology in this vulnerable population.

17623626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17623626.value: 从文本到对话：以生成式人工智能促进科学探究学习

17623626.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17623626.value: Dr Chen, Chen Logan Prof Su, Cai Prof Zhen, Yuanyi

17623626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17623626.value: Science education aims to cultivate students’ scientific literacy, moving beyond memorization to foster inquiry and critical thinking. However, learning is often constrained by static science textbooks and teacher-dominated instructional methods, which limit opportunities for dynamic, student-led exploration. While research highlights the profound benefits of dialogic interaction for developing reasoning skills, creating authentic environments for such interaction remains a major challenge. This project addresses this critical gap by proposing an innovative solution that complements traditional textbook-based learning. We will design, develop, and evaluate T2Metaverse, a system that leverages cutting-edge Generative AI to automatically transform frontier scientific findings from leading journals like Nature and Science into immersive, interactive Metaverse learning experiences. This approach moves beyond the static presentation of science as a collection of settled facts to allow students to actively and collaboratively explore the very process of scientific discovery. The project’s feasibility is grounded in the PI’s extensive expertise in using AI for dialogue analysis and enhancement and is supported by a strong interdisciplinary team. A functional prototype of the T2Metaverse workflow developed by the team already demonstrates technical viability. Further, a rigorous human-in-the-loop protocol involving researchers, teachers, and students will ensure all generated content is scientifically accurate, pedagogically sound, and age-appropriate. The project’s effectiveness will be rigorously assessed through a quasi-experimental study involving 20 secondary science teachers and approximately 1,000 of their students in Hong Kong over one semester. Using a pre- and post-test design, we will compare a treatment group using the T2Metaverse environments with a comparison group receiving conventional instruction. To strengthen the design, comparisons will be made between classes taught by the same teacher, providing a robust control for teacher- and school-level confounding variables. A mixed-methods approach will be used to collect and analyze quantitative data (questionnaires, tests, system logs) and qualitative data (interviews, video recordings) to measure the impact on students’ scientific literacy, learning engagement, collaborative learning skills, and problem-solving abilities. The statistical analysis will employ a two-level linear mixed model to account for the nested data structure. The research holds significant potential to innovate technology-supported science education. By demonstrating a scalable method for automatically creating dialogic inquiry-based learning environments, the T2Metaverse system promises to enhance student learning engagement and outcomes. The project will yield deep insights into designing effective learning experiences for students. Findings will inform AI-enhanced education across disciplines and provide evidence-based guidance for educational policy. 科學教育的核心目標是培養學生的科學素養，使其超越單純的死記硬背，進而發展探究與批判性思維能力。然而，現實教學往往受限於靜態的科學教材以及以教師為主導的講授方式，從而限制了學生開展動態、自主探索的機會。儘管既有研究表明對話式互動對培養學生的推理能力具有顯著益處，但創設支持此類互動的真實情境依然是一大挑戰。本項目針對這一關鍵研究空白，提出了一種能夠補充傳統教材式學習的創新解決方案。我們將利用前沿的生成式人工智能技術，將來自學術期刊的前沿科學發現自動轉化為沉浸式、交互式的學習體驗（T2Metaverse 環境）。這種方法突破了將科學知識呈現為現成事實集合的傳統靜態模式，使學生能夠在協作中主動探索科學發現的完整過程。本項目的有效性將通過一項為期一學期的準實驗研究進行系統評估，採用前後測設計，對比使用 T2Metaverse 環境的實驗組與接受傳統教學的對照組。研究將採用混合方法收集並分析量化數據（問卷、測試、系統日誌等）與質性數據（訪談、課堂錄像），測量該系統對學生科學素養、學習投入度、協作學習技能等的影響。本研究通過展示一種自動化構建對話式探究學習環境的可擴展方法，望顯著提升學生的學習投入與成效。同時，項目將深化對如何為學生設計有效學習體驗的理論認識，其研究成果亦將為跨學科的人工智能賦能教育提供借鑑，並為教育政策制定提供實證依據。

17624226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17624226.value: 願景型民族主義：效仿、敵意與近代中國民族認同的形成

17624226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17624226.value: Dr He, Yingtian Prof Peng, Peng

17624226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17624226.value: We develop a new theory of aspirational nationalism to explain how national identity is built not only through resistance to outsiders but also through learning from them. Existing theories of nationalism emphasize war, modernization, or elite manipulation, focusing on the politics of enmity. We argue that national identity also evolves through emulation, a forward-looking process in which elites and publics treat foreign powers as models of reform. Aspirational nationalism, therefore, operates through two pathways: an enmity pathway, grounded in threat and exclusion, and an emulation pathway, grounded in admiration and adaptation. Together, they explain how nationalism can both oppose and imitate its perceived rivals. Our study theorizes these dual pathways and tests them in the context of modern China between 1850 and 1949, a century of imperial decline, foreign invasion, and rapid reform. We ask three questions. First, how do national narratives vary along the three dimensions of pathway, referent, and issue of interest? Second, how do external threats, such as wars and crises, alter the balance between enmity and emulation? Third, how do elites shape the content and trajectory of aspirational nationalism, and which elites have the power to redefine the nation? From these questions, we derive hypotheses linking external shocks, elite experiences, and ideational change. Empirically, we combine large-scale computational text analysis with historical interpretation to examine how Chinese elites reimagined "China" across a century of transformation. Drawing on digitized archives of newspapers, journals, and biographical records, we build the most extensive dataset of elite writings containing the keyword Zhongguo (中国), the linguistic marker of modern nationhood. The corpus includes about 679,000 newspaper titles and 80,000 journal titles, each linked to biographical information about their authors. Using an AI-assisted workflow, we annotate each entry in the rich archive along three theoretical dimensions of aspirational nationalism: pathway, referent, and issue of interest. We then analyze the annotated documents with a mixture of computational and qualitative methods: We use time series analysis to trace how the national narratives evolved over time, network analysis to map how nation-building ideas circulated among elites, and qualitative readings of selected archives to provide interpretive depth and historical grounding. Our study has both theoretical and empirical contributions. Theoretically, it re-conceptualizes nationalism as a politics of aspiration. Empirically, it shows how computational methods can track ideational change at a scale once inaccessible to traditional research methods.

17625326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17625326.value: 橋樑抑或障礙？人工智能自我披露對本港大學生求助路徑的雙刃作用

17625326.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17625326.value: Dr Alan, Dougherty Dr Chen, Zhong Eric Dr Habibi, Mojtaba Dr Qin, Lili Prof Williams, Jo Dr Yeung, Wing Fai

17625326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17625326.value: In Hong Kong, more than one in four experience depression, yet only a quarter ever seek help. After COVID‑19, social withdrawal has surged. It leaves many to face their struggles alone. At the same time, a new trend has emerged: young people are increasingly talking to generative AI chatbots about their feelings and problems. For some, talking to AI feels safer than opening up to friends or professionals. But does this habit encourage help‑seeking, or could it replace human connection and delay care? Current research overlooks three critical gaps. First, no validated tool measures AI substitution (swapping human chats for AI), unlike social media scales. Second, studies ignore whether AI disclosure boosts or kills help-seeking, skipping why (mechanisms) and relying on weak snapshots. Third, traits like low life meaning (which worsens risks) or self-compassion (which protects) are ignored. This project tackles that urgent question through a new Twin‑Mechanism Model explaining how conversations with AI affect real‑world help‑seeking. It identifies two linked processes. The first, AI‑Perceived Partner Responsiveness (AI‑PPR), is a psychological process in which users feel understood and validated by AI, which may boost confidence and reduce stigma around seeking professional help. The second, the AI Substitution Index (ASI), is a behavioural process that measures how much time and emotional energy shift from people to AI, potentially lowering real‑life help‑seeking. Whether AI acts as a bridge or a barrier depends on how these two forces interact. The project unfolds in two phases. Phase 1 will develop and test short, reliable tools to measure AI‑PPR and ASI through in‑depth interviews with university students. Phase 2 will apply these tools in a three‑wave longitudinal study of 360 students, tracking how self‑disclosure to AI predicts later help‑seeking, connectedness, well‑being, and dependency. Advanced statistical models will identify genuine change, ensuring results are rigorous and replicable. This study is unprecedented in testing the Twin‑Mechanism Model, linking psychological theory to behaviour over time. Its novelty lies in showing how emotional comfort with AI might inspire formal, real-world help‑seeking or, instead, substitute digital talk for human care. This project will help guide Hong Kong and the world toward safer uses of AI for youth mental health. 在香港，超過四分之一的人曾經歷抑鬱，但當中僅約四分之一會尋求協助。新冠疫情之後，社交退縮的情況有所增加，令不少人更傾向獨自面對困擾。與此同時，一種新的求助模式正在浮現：愈來愈多年輕人向生成式人工智能聊天機械人傾訴感受和煩惱。對部分人而言，向人工智能傾訴可能比向朋友或專業人士坦白更有安全感。然而，這種做法究竟會促進日後求助，還是逐漸取代人際連繫，甚至延誤接受適切的支援？ 現有研究存在三個關鍵缺口。第一，與社交媒體研究已有相關量度工具不同，目前仍缺乏經驗證的工具量度「人工智能替代」，即使用人工智能對話取代與真人交流的程度。第二，過往研究尚未充分探討向人工智能自我披露究竟會促進還是削弱其後的求助行為，既缺乏對相關機制的檢驗，也大多依賴橫斷面數據，難以了解隨時間發生的變化。第三，生活意義感偏低等風險因素，以及自我關懷等保護因素，在這一研究領域亦一直未獲充分重視。 本計劃提出一個全新的「雙機制模型」，探討與人工智能的對話如何影響現實世界中的求助行為。模型提出兩個相互作用的過程。其一是「人工智能感知伴侶回應性」（AI-PPR），即使用者感到自己被人工智能理解、重視和回應的程度。這種心理經驗可能提升求助信心，並減低與求助相關的污名感。其二是「人工智能替代指數」（ASI），反映使用者在多大程度上把原本投放於人際互動的時間和情感轉移至人工智能，因而可能減少現實中的求助。人工智能最終成為通往人際支援的橋樑，還是取代人際支援的障礙，取決於這兩種機制如何共同發揮作用。 計劃分兩個階段進行。第一階段將透過大學生深度訪談，發展並驗證簡短而可靠的AI-PPR和ASI量度工具。第二階段將把這些工具應用於360名大學生的三波追蹤研究，考察向人工智能自我披露如何預測其後的求助行為、社會聯繫感、心理健康及對人工智能的依賴程度。研究將採用縱向統計模型分析個體隨時間的變化，並提高研究結果的嚴謹性和可重複性。 本研究將首次系統檢驗這一雙機制模型，把人工智能互動中的心理經驗與其後的人際行為變化連繫起來。其核心創新，在於釐清對人工智能的情感投入究竟會成為通往現實世界求助的橋樑，還是逐漸以數碼互動取代人際支援。研究結果將為香港以至其他地區如何更安全地運用生成式人工智能支援年輕人的精神健康提供實證基礎。

17625526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17625526.value: 人工增強的正義：探討法律程序中的人工智慧與人類互動

17625526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17625526.value: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into law promises greater efficiency but also threatens to undermine fundamental values of human justice. Past studies have documented a judicial human-AI fairness gap: people consistently perceive adjudication by algorithms as less fair than adjudication by humans, even when the outcomes are the same. This project investigates how the public perceives and responds to the deployment of AI in the legal field. It builds on past studies by examining assistive rather than adjudicative uses of AI. It also innovates by considering uses of AI inside and, critically, outside the courtroom. This shift in attention is important since most disputes do not proceed to trial. Three axes of inquiry are presented. First, this project examines whether human oversight can eliminate the human-AI fairness gap. It explores whether and why minimal human review might render algorithmic decisions acceptable to the public. Second, it investigates how people process AI-generated legal advice, testing whether uniqueness neglect—the fear that AI cannot appreciate their unique circumstances—causes them to second-guess or reject correct information given by a machine. Third, it analyzes how individuals interpret the probabilistic outputs of AI, e.g., a 70% chance of winning, and how these interpretations shape their legal strategies and expectations. By using experimental methods to explore these questions across different jurisdictions, this project seeks to uncover the normative and psychological mechanisms that influence how we interact with AI technology in law. The findings will provide a crucial evidence base for designing legal systems that are not only efficient and accessible but also perceived as fair and legitimate by the people they serve. 將人工智慧（AI）融入法律體系，雖有望提升效率，卻也可能動搖人類司法的基本價值。過往研究已證實存在「人與AI的司法公平性落差」：即使裁決結果相同，人們仍普遍認為由演算法作出的裁決不如人類裁決公平。本研究旨在探討公眾如何看待並回應AI在法律領域的應用。本研究在既有研究基礎上，將研究重點從人工智慧的裁決應用轉向輔助應用。此外，本研究亦具創新性，不僅考量法庭內的應用，更關鍵的是將法庭外的應用納入探討。此關注焦點的轉變至關重要，因為多數糾紛並未進入審判階段。本研究提出三大探究軸線。首先，本研究探討人類監督是否能消除人與人工智慧之間的公平性差距，並探究最低限度的審查是否以及為何能使演算法決策為公眾所接受。其次，本計畫探究人們如何處理由人工智慧產生的法律建議，並測試「獨特性忽視」——即擔心人工智慧無法體察其獨特處境——是否會導致人們對機器提供的正確資訊產生質疑或予以拒絕。第三，本計畫分析個人如何詮釋人工智慧的機率性輸出結果（例如「勝訴機率為70%」），以及這些詮釋如何形塑其法律策略與預期。本計畫透過實驗方法，在不同司法管轄區探討上述問題，旨在揭示影響我們在法律領域中與人工智慧技術互動方式的規範性與心理機制。研究結果將為設計法律體系提供關鍵的證據基礎，使這些體系不僅高效且易於使用，更能被其服務對象視為公平且合法。

17626226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17626226.value: 跨境旅行與跨境區域消費：誰被遺落，原因何在？

17626226.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17626226.value: Prof Yin, Ling Dr Zhao, Ya

17626226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17626226.value: While residents of regions like the Schengen Area (Europe) enjoy seamless travel across internal borders, many elsewhere still face significant barriers, e.g., the obligation to use specific ports of entry, along with the associated costs and bureaucratic formalities. Despite these barriers, the post-COVID era has witnessed a surge in cross-border travel and consumption (CBTC) in many cross-border regions, such as the Hong Kong-Shenzhen cross-border region. Yet, amid this trend, a segment of the population thereof remains within their borders. Who are they? Why do they choose—or are they compelled—to stay? Furthermore, how is their wellbeing affected compared to that of cross-border travelers? Notably in Hong Kong, more and more residents face dwindling local amenities. The rise of CBTC—driven by cheaper and often superior options—is drawing customers away from local businesses, reducing the supply of amenities like restaurants and grocery stores. This research focuses on residents of cross-border regions who seldom or never cross the border over different time intervals, e.g., 2, 4, 6 months. We hypothesize that a segment of these stayers are willing to travel and consume abroad but are deterred by significant perceived barriers; we term this group constrained stayers. Consequently, their wellbeing may suffer compared to their cross-border peers, who benefit from access to cheaper and more diverse goods and services. Utilizing a mixed-method approach and drawing on concepts and theories from disciplines like transport, positive psychology, economics, and philosophy, the proposed research will gather and utilize both primary and secondary data in Hong Kong to address the following research questions: • Whether and how does the profile of constrained stayers vary when they are defined over different time intervals—for example, 2, 4, and 6 months? • What motivates or deters (different) constrained stayers from undertaking CBTC? • How do the negative effects of CBTC influence the wellbeing of constrained stayers? • Based on the answers to the above questions, what theories and policies can be proposed to support constrained stayers? In short, this research will investigate the impacts of CBTC on the constrained stayers’ wellbeing by developing theories, measurement tools, and predictive models. Its ultimate goal is to provide decision-makers with evidence-based recommendations to improve the constrained stayers' wellbeing. 雖然像申根區（歐洲）等地區的居民享有暢通無阻的跨境旅行，但許多其他地區的人們仍然面臨重大障礙，例如必須使用指定口岸，以及由此產生的費用和繁瑣的行政手續。儘管存在這些障礙，後疫情時代許多跨境地區（例如港深跨境地區）的跨境旅行與消費（CBTC）仍呈現激增態勢。然而，在這一趨勢中，有一部分人口卻滯留境內。他們是誰？為何他們選擇——或被逼——留下？此外，與跨境旅行者相比，他們的福祉狀況如何？特別是在香港，越來越多的居民面臨本地設施日益減少的問題。CBTC的興起——由更便宜且通常更優質的選擇所驅動——正將顧客從本地商家吸引走，從而減少了餐廳、雜貨店等設施的供應。 本研究聚焦於跨境地區中在不同時間間隔（例如2個月、4個月、6個月）內很少或從未跨境移動的居民。我們假設，這些「留守者」中有一部分人願意到境外旅行和消費，但被顯著的感知障礙所阻礙；我們將這群體稱為「受限留守者」。因此，他們的福祉可能不如那些能獲得更便宜、更多元商品與服務的跨境同儕。 本項研究將採用混合研究方法，並借鑑交通、正向心理學、經濟學和哲學等學科的概念與理論，在香港收集並運用初級與次級資料，以回答以下研究問題： • 當受限留守者依不同時間間隔（例如2個月、4個月、6個月）來定義時，其群體特徵是否有差異？如何差異？ • 是什麼因素促使或阻礙（不同的）受限留守者進行CBTC？ • CBTC的負面影響如何影響受限留守者的福祉？ • 基於上述問題的答案，可以提出哪些理論與政策來支持受限留守者？ 簡言之，本研究將透過發展理論、測量工具和預測模型，探討CBTC對受限留守者福祉的影響。其最終目標是為決策者提供以實證為基礎的建議，以改善受限留守者的福祉。

17626326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17626326.value: 碎片書寫：檔案和手稿中的張愛玲

17626326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17626326.value: “Writing in Fragments” continues my earlier and ongoing work to situate the study of Eileen Chang (1920-1995) in archives and manuscripts. Given Chang’s steady rise in global recognition in recent decades, I argue for the need to expand what we consider as “texts” to include manuscripts, papers, correspondences, photographs, drawings, and other documents and objects. I have already begun this work and am now seeking support to allow me to broaden the scope of my research to include a greater variety of material housed outside of Hong Kong. My goal is to lift Chang out of a linear Chinese literary historiography, to place her in the larger context of twentieth-century literary and cultural production, and to define her in precise terms as a major figure in world literature. In Anglophone and Francophone literary studies of recent decades, major figures such as Virginia Woolf, James Joyce, and Emily Dickinson have been reexamined in light of a vast amount of papers, manuscripts, and other documents that have newly emerged. Returning canonical texts to their original state as manuscripts becomes imperative in current scholarly discourse. Similarly, taking writings that were previously considered incomplete, informal, and fragmented as texts proper has enriched and complicated our understandings of familiar literary contours. My work responds directly to this “archival turn” in global literary studies. While Chang’s early works have been canonized and thoroughly researched, her later works, particularly those written during the last three decades of her American life, call for more archive-based research. After Chang died in 1995, her manuscripts that were relatively complete were published posthumously, some with substantial reconstruction and editorial input. She also left behind much material that would be deemed unpublishable, as it was too fragmentary. In her later years, Chang was increasingly writing for a future audience, going at her own pace, one fragment at a time. I define Chang’s “late style” as a form of “future writing,” as she had provided many beginnings of what would have been longer narratives. Studying Chang’s later works in their draft form and in a state of perpetual incompleteness becomes important. Significantly broadening the scope of Eileen Chang studies, my new project will paint a thorough and more nuanced portrait of a global writer who persisted with her experiments till her last days. 本項目旨在繼續將張愛玲研究完整置於檔案和手稿的脈絡中，系統梳理她晚期寫作的樣貌。此項工程已初具規模，下一步的計畫是將研究範圍擴大到香港以外的更多樣化的資料，目標是打破線性的中國文學史的書寫模式，將張愛玲置於二十世紀文學和文化生產的語境中，並精準定義她在世界文學中的位置。 當今的西方文學研究中，對於經典作家比如維珍尼亞·伍爾夫、詹姆斯·喬哀斯和艾米莉·狄金生等的研究，皆因大量的原始手稿和相關資料的重新呈現而得到重啟和拓展。將經典文本還原到其原始手稿的狀態已成為必須。手稿狀態的文字也包括大量的碎片寫作，它們的不完整性恰恰是文學現代性的精髓。本項目正是對近幾十年來全球文學研究中的「檔案轉向」的直接回應。 晚年張愛玲留下了大量的碎片文字。她的「晚期風格」是一種「未來書寫」，留下的文字更多顯示了寫作的可能性，一種永無止境的未完成狀態成為她晚年寫作的常態。本項目力圖拓展「文本」的範疇，擴大張愛玲研究的版圖，在對碎片的梳理中描繪出一位直至生命盡頭都未曾放棄寫作實踐的二十世紀女性作者的形象。

17626426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17626426.value: 利用閉環標靶記憶再激活方法於睡眠期間重激活正向記憶以削弱負向記憶的研究

17626426.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17626426.value: Prof Li, Shirley X. Dr Ngo-Dehning, Hong-Viet

17626426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17626426.value: Sleep offers a unique window for consolidating daily experiences, shaping what we remember and how we feel. Yet not all memories are equally welcome. When negative memories dominate over positive ones, people may develop pervasive negative schemas that distort attention, memory, and interpretation of events, thereby heightening vulnerability to psychiatric disorders including depression, anxiety, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). In contrast, reinforcing positive memories and positive thinking can yield cascading benefits: boosting mood, reducing stress, and ultimately enhancing psychological resilience. However, how to strengthen positive memories and positive thinking during sleep while weakening negative ones remains an open challenge. We propose to address this critical question using targeted memory reactivation (TMR)—a technique that unobtrusively delivers acoustic cues linked to prior daytime learning during sleep to modulate memories. Specifically, we will employ TMR to reactivate and thus strengthen positive memories during sleep while weakening competing negative memories. To enhance efficacy, we will employ closed-loop algorithms to deliver memory cues precisely during the up-state of slow oscillations in non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep, a transient window optimal for memory reactivation. Addressing this question is essential for understanding the mechanisms of emotional memory consolidation, and for developing novel sleep interventions to promote mental well-beings. Across three experiments, the current proposal aims to address the following research questions: 1) how pre-TMR retrieval of positive memories would modulate TMR’s impact on strengthening positive memories and weakening negative memories, both immediately and after a delay. 2) whether reactivating positive reappraisals of negative autobiographical memories during sleep can weaken these memories; and 3) whether the sleep-based memory modulation protocol improves emotional well-being among individuals with subthreshold depression in daily life. Our proposal offers unique advantages. First, initiating memory reactivation during sleep will bypass conscious effort. This particularly benefits vulnerable populations (e.g., depression, anxiety) who often show difficulties in retrieving and maintaining positive emotional memories. Second, employing innovative memory modulation techniques such as closed-loop TMR and positive reappraisal to weaken real-world negative autobiographical memories, our proposal bears high ecological validity. Third, by testing the protocol’s effectiveness in memory modulation among individual with subthreshold depression, the proposal will inform scalable, non-invasive, drug-free interventions that complement existing therapies. In sum, by harnessing sleep’s intrinsic processes, this research could pave the way for innovative strategies to promote psychological resilience and reduce the burden of psychiatric disorders at a population level. 睡眠是記憶鞏固的獨特窗口：睡眠不僅塑造了我們記住什麼內容，也影響著我們的情緒感受。然而，並非所有記憶都是我們想記住的：當負向記憶強於正向記憶時，個體可能逐漸形成廣泛的負向認知模式，進而扭曲其對生活事件的注意偏向、記憶與解釋方式，增加罹患憂鬱症、焦慮症及創傷後壓力症候群（PTSD）等精神疾病的風險。相較之下，強化正向記憶與正向思維則能帶來諸多益處，包括提升情緒、減緩壓力，並最終增強心理韌性。然而，如何在睡眠期間增強正向記憶，同時削弱負向記憶，至今仍是一項尚待解決的重要挑戰。 本研究擬運用標靶記憶再激活（Targeted Memory Reactivation, TMR）技術來探討該關鍵問題。TMR在睡眠期間呈現與白天學習內容相關聯的聲音線索，從而以非侵入的方式在睡眠中進行記憶調控。具體而言，我們將利用TMR於睡眠期間重新激活並強化正向記憶，同時削弱與其相關聯的負向記憶。為進一步提升效果，我們將採用閉環（closed-loop）算法，在非快速眼動的慢波睡眠（non-rapid eye movement, NREM slow wave sleep）中的慢波振盪（slow oscillations）上升相位（up-state）精準呈現記憶線索。此一窗口被認為是記憶再激活的最佳時機。探討此問題對於理解情緒記憶鞏固的神經機制，以及發展促進心理和情緒健康的新型睡眠干預策略，都具有重要意義。 本研究將開展三項實驗回答以下研究問題：（1）在TMR實施之前重複提取正向記憶，將如何調節TMR對於強化正向記憶及削弱負向記憶的效果，並進一步探討此效應在即時與延遲測量中的表現；（2）在睡眠期間重新激活針對負向自傳式記憶所形成的正向評估（positive reappraisal），探討是否能有效削弱負向自傳式記憶；以及（3）是否能提升亞臨床憂鬱（subthreshold depression）個體於日常生活中的情緒健康。 本研究的獨特優勢如下。首先，在睡眠期間啟動記憶再激活無需個體的有意識努力。這對於憂鬱或焦慮等易感人群尤其重要，因為他們往往較難提取並維持正向情緒記憶。其次，本研究結合閉環TMR與情緒調節的正向評估等創新的記憶調節技術，以削弱真實世界中的負向自傳式記憶，因此具有高生態效度。第三，透過檢驗該記憶調節方案對亞臨床憂鬱個體的效果，本研究將為開發可擴展、非侵入性且非藥物的干預方法提供實證基礎，使其能作為現有治療方式的重要補充。 總而言之，本研究旨在善用睡眠的記憶處理機制，為提升心理韌性與降低精神疾病負擔開闢新的研究方向，並有望發展出可推廣的創新策略來促進心理健康。

17627026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17627026.value: 雙系統之說：自閉症與神經典型兒童的母子疼痛共情的神經與行為研究

17627026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17627026.value: Pain empathy, the ability to perceive another’s pain, is a vital skill that fosters mutual understanding and deepens emotional bonds during social interaction. However, due to atypical neural activity patterns, autistic children exhibit significant difficulties in pain empathy. To help them acquire proficient empathy skills, this study will delineate the neural dynamics underlying their empathic dysfunction. Specifically, our three-year longitudinal, electroencephalography (EEG)-behavioural, and mother-child dyadic design will examine (1) the neural mechanisms of empathy to physical and social pain in autistic and neurotypical children, (2) the empathic neural responses to others' pain in mothers of autistic children, and (3) the mother-child empathic links at both neural and behavioural levels. These objectives stem from three identified gaps. Our recent (Wang & Tong, 2025) and other EEG studies (e.g., Liu et al., 2023) have (1) overlooked the multidimensional nature of pain by focusing exclusively on physical pain, but not social pain; (2) neglected the impact of raising an autistic child on the mother’s empathic pain response, and how that potentially altered response may shape the child’s empathic development; and (3) omitted the mother-child connection in empathy development by relying on a cross-sectional design of a specific age group without integrating behavioral measures of empathy. For each of three consecutive years, we will track two mother-child dyadic groups: 87 autistic children aged 6-7 and their 87 neurotypical mothers; and 87 neurotypical peers and their 87 mothers. All will complete a behavioral assessment of cognitive and affective empathy. Mothers will complete questionnaires on their and their children’s anxiety and stress. EEG recordings will be conducted during the first and final year, with mother-child dyads viewing animated videos depicting real-life physical and social pain situations to elicit their empathic responses.
