This research follows a prototype-development and characterization approach. It makes contributions in six areas: (1) Develop a classification system for irregular tile shapes and create a dataset using real-world floor plans combined with simulated setting-out strategies. (2) Developing structured-light scanning procedures for edge-shape acquisition. (3) Designing and building a compact computer-controlled wet saw prototype. (4) Developing a human-machine interface that supports scan-to-cut workflow. (5) Evaluating system performance under lab-simulated renovation conditions. (6) Developing floor pattern design guidelines for future deployment. This project will integrate construction craftsmanship, mechatronics expertise, and computational design methods to develop on-site robotic systems that enhance construction worker productivity. It will align with the Hong Kong government’s policy of promoting building technology for enhancing construction efficiency and contribute to reducing workers’ exposure to dust by encouraging the use of wet saws. Moreover, the sensing, data processing, and on-site cutting technologies developed in this research will be transferable to other fitting tasks (e.g. cabinetry and plumbing) beyond tiling. 瓷磚因耐用、美觀選擇多樣，是世界各地常見的地面裝修材料。近年建築機械人技術不斷發展，但現有研究主要集中於在寬敞、沒有障礙物的空間鋪設大型及形狀規則的瓷磚，仍未能有效處理需要因應現場環境而切割的不規則瓷磚，因此限制了相關技術在住宅室內裝修中的應用。 香港住宅單位普遍空間較小，房間及走廊亦較狹窄，因此需要使用大量不規則形狀的瓷磚。根據本研究對公共房屋平面圖的初步分析，以60厘米瓷磚計算，不規則瓷磚可佔鋪設數量約40%。在整個鋪磚工序中，量度及切割這些不規則瓷磚是最耗時，亦最容易出錯的工作。由於瓷磚必須準確配合牆邊、牆角及其他現場邊界，其形狀不能單靠數碼建築圖則可靠地推算，因此必須在施工現場進行量度。目前的機械人鋪磚研究大多未有處理這個問題，這些不規則瓷磚仍主要依靠工人以傳統方法逐一量度、切割及鋪設。 本研究提出一套人機協作方法，改善兩項主要工序的效率：（1）利用近年價格逐漸普及的高精度3D掃描器，量度施工現場的地面邊界；以及（2）研發一部由電腦控制的濕式瓷磚切割機，按照掃描所得的形狀自動切割瓷磚。整套系統將以便於運送及在工地使用為設計目標，並盡量配合工人現有的施工流程，在毋須大幅改變工作方式或重新培訓的情況下提高生產力。 研究將透過原型開發及性能評估，從六方面展開：（1）建立不規則瓷磚形狀的分類方法，並利用真實住宅平面圖及模擬不同瓷磚鋪設排列方式建立數據集；（2）研究利用結構光3D掃描技術準確取得地面邊界形狀的方法；（3）設計及製作小型電腦控制濕式瓷磚切割機原型；（4）開發人機操作介面，建立由現場掃描至瓷磚切割的完整工作流程；以及（5）在實驗室模擬的裝修環境中測試及評估系統性能。 本研究將結合傳統建築工藝、機電系統及電腦輔助設計方法，研發能夠在施工現場使用的機械人技術，以提升建築工人的生產力。研究亦配合香港政府推動建築科技及提高施工效率的政策，並透過推廣濕式切割，減少工人在瓷磚切割過程中接觸粉塵。此外，本研究所開發的現場掃描、數據處理及自動切割技術，未來亦可應用於其他需要因應現場尺寸進行加工的裝修工作，例如訂製櫃體及水喉工程。

21200926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21200926.value: 從稀疏軌跡到完整出行鏈：基於移動大數據的AI賦能人類流動行為重構

21200926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21200926.value: The rise of big mobility data (BMD), i.e., location data passively collected from smartphones, has transformed how we understand when, where, and why people travel. BMD can track the movements of millions of individuals in near real time and is increasingly used in traffic management, urban planning, environmental assessment, and related fields. In Hong Kong and China's Greater Bay Area (GBA), where population density and travel intensity are among the highest in the world, BMD serves as an essential complement to traditional travel surveys and fixed traffic sensors, enabling 24/7 visibility of human mobility at both the individual level and city scales. However, BMD has inherent limitations that hinder its broader use. At the trip level, it lacks travel semantics such as stays and activity types. At the device level, it is extremely sparse because locations are collected opportunistically, leaving many real-world trips unrecorded. At the population level, it covers only part of the residents, and the coverage rates vary significantly across regions. Existing studies either ignore these limitations or address them separately, which can lead to distorted findings and potentially misleading policy implications. This project proposes a unified, AI-driven framework to jointly address the limitations of BMD and ultimately, reconstruct complete, population-representative daily trip chains from raw BMD. First, we will infer activity types for each trip using machine learning and Hidden Markov Models that integrate spatial context and temporal transition patterns. Second, we will recover missing trips through Transformer-based models that learn mappings from masked to full activity sequences, followed by a location assignment module that integrates exploration and revisit probabilities to identify the most likely locations. Finally, we will estimate zone-level population scaling weights using an integrated optimization+assignment model, which minimizes discrepancies between assigned and observed road traffic counts. These scaling weights will then be used to scale trip observations from partial devices to the full population via generative AI. Building on an extensive dataset that includes local travel surveys (~500,000 respondents) and BMD (~9 million smartphones), we will train this framework in Shenzhen and Hong Kong, two of the largest cities in the GBA. The project will set a new benchmark for human mobility research by releasing a set of high-quality, representative mobility datasets and a ready-to-use toolkit for BMD bias correction and missing data recovery, providing robust evidence and practical tools for both academic research and policymaking in Hong Kong, the GBA, and beyond. 智能手機被動採集的移動大數據（Big Mobility Data, BMD）徹底改變了我們對人群「何時、何地、為何」出行的認知。BMD 能夠近乎實時地追蹤數百萬人的流動軌跡，在交通管理、城市規劃及環境評估等領域發揮著日益重要的作用。在人口密度與出行強度均居世界前列的香港及粵港澳大灣區，BMD 成為傳統出行調查與固定交通傳感器的關鍵補充，實現了跨個人與城市尺度的全天候流動性監測。 然而，BMD 固有的局限性阻礙了其更廣泛的應用。在出行層面，數據缺乏停留時間與活動類型等語義信息；在設備層面，由於採樣具有隨機性，數據極為稀疏，遺漏了大量真實世界的出行記錄；在人口層面，數據僅覆蓋部分居民，且覆蓋率在不同區域間存在顯著差異。現有研究往往忽視或孤立處理這些問題，容易導致分析偏差並產生具誤導性的政策建議。 本項目提出一個一體化、由人工智能（AI）驅動的框架，系統性解決 BMD 的上述局限，最終從原始數據中重構出具全人群代表性的完整全日出行鏈。研究首先結合空間上下文與時序轉移特徵，構建機器學習與隱馬爾可夫模型（ML-HMM）融合框架以精準推斷活動類型；接著建立基於 Transformer 的深度學習模型，學習從掩碼序列到完整活動序列的映射以恢復缺失出行，並結合探索與重訪概率模組精確分配具體空間位置；最後構建優化與交通分配一體化模型，通過最小化路網分配交通量與實際觀測流量的誤差來估算分區人口擴展權重，進而利用生成式 AI（Generative AI）將樣本觀測外推至全量人口。 本項目將基於包含本地出行調查（約50萬受訪者）及移動大數據（約900萬部智能手機）的大規模數據集，在香港與深圳進行訓練與驗證。項目將發布一組高質量、具代表性的流動性數據集，並開源一套開箱即用的數據偏差校正與缺失修復工具包，為香港、大灣區乃至全球的人類流動性學術研究與公共政策制定提供堅實的科學數據與實用工具支撐。

21203026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21203026.value: 針對汗液中肺炎標誌物持續監測的可穿戴雙電極傳感器

21203026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21203026.value: Pneumonia is an inflammatory condition that remains a leading cause of global mortality even after COVID-19 pandemic, particularly among vulnerable populations, necessitating innovative strategies for early detection, continuous monitoring and precision treatment. Traditional diagnostic methods, typically reliant on blood and imaging tests, are insufficient for delivering timely insights into disease progression. Wearable bioelectronics represents a promising alternative; however, most existing biosensors suffer from poor repeatability, signal drift, and limited robustness under dynamic physiological conditions. To address these challenges, this proposal introduces a novel wearable dual-electrode biosensor that decouples target recognition from signal detection, allowing reliable multi-cycle operation through programmed voltage control. It supports continuous monitoring of two pneumonia-specific sweat proteins, C-reactive protein (CRP) and procalcitonin (PCT), with high sensitivity and selectivity. By integrating biosensors with an iontophoresis-microfluidics module for on-demand sweat induction and dynamic collection, and flexible circuit for wireless data transmission, the proposed wearable bioelectronics aim to bridge the gap between laboratory diagnostics and personalized pneumonia management. This research expands the capabilities of wearable biosensors in three steps. The first task centers on materials-engineered electrode for selective recognition of CRP and PCT. The synthesized metal-organic framework/antimonene quantum dots nanocomposites could be loaded onto porous laser-engraved graphene electrodes to form stable interfaces, further functionalized with redox probe-loaded dual aptamers. The second task investigates biosensing mechanism of dual-electrode design, where the recognition electrode captures proteins while the detection electrode produces clean readouts via electrochemical analysis. Through voltage-programmed adsorption, desorption and probe deactivation, it enables repeatable protein measurements over 20 cycles. The final task is to validate dual-electrode biosensors through on-body trials, continuously monitoring sweat CRP and PCT alongside physiological parameters. A cohort study of 60-80 participants, involving healthy volunteers and pneumonia patients across different subtypes, could correlate sweat and serum protein levels, confirming accuracy, reliability and practical usability. Building on our previous success in developing multimodal wearable bioelectronics with validated human studies and high-impact publications, this project leverages accumulated expertise to ensure technical feasibility and translational potential. Upon completion, this research will establish a robust framework for wearable monitoring of pneumonia-specific sweat biomarkers, paving the way for broader chronic disease management. The key scientific contributions include: (i) a materials-engineered approach for highly stable and selective biosensing, (ii) a dual-electrode design for continuous monitoring of sweat proteins, and (iii) integrated wearable bioelectronics for non-invasive health management under real-world conditions. Together, these outcomes will accelerate progress toward digital medicine and personalized healthcare. 肺炎是一種炎症性疾病，即使在COVID-19大流行之後，它仍然是導緻全球死亡的主要原因，尤其是在弱勢群體中。傳統的診斷方法通常依賴於血液和成像測試，不足以及時了解疾病的進展情況。可穿戴生物電子是一種很有前景的替代方法，然而，大多數現有的生物傳感器都存在重複性差、信號漂移以及在動態生理條件下穩定性有限等問題。 爲了應對這些挑戰，本項目介紹了一種新型可穿戴雙電極生物傳感器，它將目標識別與信號檢測分離開來，通過編程電壓實現可靠的多週期運行，實現兩種肺炎特異性汗液蛋白(C-反應蛋白(CRP)和降鈣素原(PCT))的連續監測，並具有高靈敏度和高選擇性。通過將生物傳感器與用於按需誘導和動態收集汗液的微流體模塊以及用於無線數據傳輸的柔性電路相集成，所提出的可穿戴生物電子設備旨在彌合實驗室診斷與個性化肺炎管理之間的差距。 這項研究分三步擴展了可穿戴生物傳感器的功能，第一項任務的核心是選擇性識別CRP和PCT的材料工程電極，合成的金屬有機框架/銻烯量子點納米複合材料可負載到激光刻蝕石墨烯電極上形成穩定的界麵，並進一步與負載氧化還原探針的雙適配體相結合。第二項任務是研究雙電極設計的生物傳感機製，其中識別電極捕獲蛋白質，而檢測電極則通過電化學分析産生信號讀出。通過電壓編程的吸附、解吸和探針失活，實現20個週期內重複測量蛋白質。第三項任務是通過人體試驗驗証雙電極生物傳感器，在連續監測生理參數的同時監測汗液CRP和PCT，開展由60-80名參與者(包括健康誌願者和不同亞型的肺炎患者)組成的隊列研究，將汗液和血清中的蛋白水平聯繫起來，從而確認其準確性、可靠性和實際可用性。 基於我們之前在開髮多模態可穿戴生物電子設備方麵取得的成功，以及經過驗証的人體研究，本項目將利用積累的專業知識，確保技術可行性和轉化潛力。這項研究完成後，將爲肺炎特異性汗液生物標誌物的可穿戴監測建立一個強大的框架，爲更廣泛的慢性疾病管理鋪平道路。主要科學貢獻包括1)用於高穩定性和選擇性生物傳感的材料工程方法，2)用於連續監測汗液蛋白質的雙電極設計，以及3)用於現實場景下無創健康管理的集成可穿戴生物電子學。這些成果將共同加速數字醫學和個性化醫療的髮展。

21210026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21210026.value: 貫通體內外的磁啟淨血：仿生磁性納米機器人介導的膿毒症及時治療策略

21210026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21210026.value: Sepsis is a major global health burden with high incidence, mortality, and healthcare costs. In Hong Kong, it accounts for about one-quarter of adult deaths over the past decade. Current treatments focus on extracorporeal blood purification and intracorporeal micro/nano therapeutic systems, yet both face critical limitations. Extracorporeal devices require complex setups and bulky equipment that delay intervention, while micro/nano systems, though effective at clearing toxins, pose risks of long-term toxicity, off-target effects, and clinical translation challenges. Patient heterogeneity in inflammation and coagulation further complicates in vivo performance. This project bridges the advantages of extracorporeal purification and intracorporeal nanotherapy to create an innovative strategy for rapid detoxification and timely removal of nanomaterials in sepsis treatment. Biomimetic magnetic nanorobots, modified with blood cell membranes and specific peptides, are engineered with controlled ligand density and spatial organization to minimize steric hindrance and nonspecific binding. These nanorobots selectively capture bacterial toxins, pathogens, and inflammatory cytokines while maintaining excellent blood compatibility and immune evasion. Administered intravenously during early sepsis, they provide rapid systemic detoxification without the delay of extracorporeal setup. Binding specificity and efficiency will be validated in complex matrices under multi-target challenge conditions. After detoxification, blood will circulate through an extracorporeal circuit integrating a portable magnetic separator. Within this device, nanorobots are captured as blood flows through parallel medical-grade PVC channels aligned above an NdFeB magnet array, forming localized high-gradient zones (∇B·B ≈ 10⁴–10⁵ T·m⁻¹). This configuration enables efficient nanoparticle capture under clinically acceptable flow and shear conditions, while viscosity and pump pressure are continuously monitored to prevent hemodynamic stress. Compared with traditional purification systems, the proposed platform enables faster response, greater flexibility, and simpler operation. Unlike conventional intracorporeal nanotherapies, it eliminates concerns about long-term nanoparticle retention and toxin redistribution through magnetically assisted retrieval. The system can be personalized to individual inflammatory and coagulation profiles and incorporates predefined immune monitoring for safety. Beyond sepsis, this versatile platform could be extended to other toxin-related diseases. The project also outlines a realistic roadmap for regulatory approval and clinical translation. Overall, this hybrid extracorporeal–intracorporeal strategy offers a promising new direction for sepsis management, with the potential to reduce disease severity, improve survival, and minimize complications of existing treatments. 敗血症是全球重大公共衞生負擔，具有高發病率、高死亡率及高醫療成本。在香港，過去十年間約四分之一的成人死亡與敗血症有關。現有治療主要包括體外血液淨化及體內微／納米治療系統，但兩者均存在明顯局限。體外血液淨化通常依賴複雜的操作流程及大型設備，可能延誤治療；體內微／納米系統雖能有效清除毒素，卻可能帶來長期毒性、非靶向作用及臨床轉化困難。此外，不同患者在炎症及凝血狀態方面存在顯著差異，進一步增加了體內治療效果的不確定性。 本項目旨在結合體外血液淨化與體內納米治療的互補優勢，建立一種可快速解毒並及時移除納米材料的敗血症治療策略。我們將開發以血細胞膜及特異性肽修飾的仿生磁性納米機器人，並精確調控其表面配體密度及空間分佈，以減少位阻效應及非特異性吸附。這些納米機器人可選擇性捕獲細菌毒素、病原體及炎症細胞因子，同時保持良好的血液相容性及免疫逃逸能力。在敗血症早期，納米機器人可經靜脈注射快速進入全身血液循環，在毋須等待體外設備準備的情況下即時進行全身性解毒。我們亦將在多靶標競爭及複雜生物介質條件下，驗證其結合特異性與清除效率。 完成體內解毒後，患者血液將通過整合便攜式磁分離器的體外循環系統。血液流經排列於釹鐵硼永磁體陣列上方的多條醫用級聚氯乙烯管道，局部形成高梯度磁場區域，從而在臨床可接受的流速及剪切條件下高效捕獲磁性納米機器人。系統將持續監測血液黏度、循環流量及泵壓，以避免額外的血流動力學負擔並保障治療安全。 相較於傳統體外血液淨化系統，本平台具有反應更迅速、操作更靈活及設備更簡化等優勢；相較於傳統體內納米治療，本策略可通過磁力回收納米機器人，降低納米材料長期滯留及所攜毒素重新釋放的風險。系統亦可根據患者的炎症及凝血特徵調整治療方案，並設置免疫反應監測及緊急回收機制，以提升個體化治療的安全性。除敗血症外，此模組化平台亦有望拓展至其他涉及循環毒素或炎症介質的疾病。本項目同時規劃了清晰的法規審批及臨床轉化路徑。總體而言，這種體內解毒與體外磁回收相結合的混合治療策略，將為敗血症管理提供一個嶄新的方向，並有望降低疾病嚴重程度、提高患者存活率及減少現有療法所引起的併發症。

21211126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21211126.value: 人工智能增強的多模態眾源地理資訊用於極端天氣下城市雨水系統的評估與維護

21211126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21211126.value: Extreme weather events, intensified by climate change, are increasingly threatening urban environments worldwide, necessitating the development of resilient cities as prioritized by the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals. Hong Kong, to align its efforts with these goals, faces an urgent need for next-generation interventions for extreme weather events following the “Black Rainstorm of the Century” in 2023. The city's Urban Stormwater System (USS) is currently under strain, facing insufficient capacity to handle escalated rainfall levels. Additionally, operational inefficiencies, such as aging infrastructure, further impede drainage performance. Consequently, how to effectively assess the working conditions of USS and develop maintenance strategies to withstand extreme weather has become a critical issue. Current assessment of USS typically relies on routine inspections, such as scheduled inlet and pipeline inspections. However, these approaches suffer from limited spatial coverage and retrospective observations, and therefore may fail to identify the actual USS failure points during extreme precipitation events. To address this gap, the project proposes leveraging Volunteered Geographic Information (VGI) from social media platforms for the assessment of USS. In this vision, VGI offers a complementary approach: citizens act as distributed sensors, generating geo-tagged flood posts that directly correspond to locations where the USS is not functioning properly, particularly in areas of high public concern. When properly extracted and analyzed, such flood-related VGI could provide timely, failure-tagged data for effective USS assessment. The research flow is designed as follows: (i) An AI-empowered toolbox will be developed to identify, geolocate, and quantify real-time flood-related data from multimodal VGI, including text, images, and videos. This toolbox will quantify flood extents, identify flood locations, and assess public sentiment to inform maintenance strategies. (ii) The vulnerability of local drainage units will be evaluated using the extracted flood extents, which will also serve as labels to train a Bayesian Graph Neural Network (BGNN). The BGNN will probabilistically reveal how vulnerability propagates across the entire USS network, especially in areas lacking VGI coverage. (iii) USS failure risk across the network will be quantified by integrating failure probabilities (from the BGNN) with estimated failure consequences, encompassing social, economic, and public sentiment impacts. Targeting risk mitigation, an explainable LLM-driven agent for USS management will be developed. Following comprehensive validation and evaluation in real-world city settings, the developed AI agent is expected to enhance both short-term emergency response and long-term maintenance planning, and, more broadly, to support the development of climate-resilient cities. 極端天氣事件因氣候變化而加劇，正日益威脅全球城市環境，因此聯合國永續發展目標已將建設韌性城市列為優先事項。香港為與這些目標接軌，在2023年「世紀黑雨」之後，迫切需要針對極端天氣事件的新一代干預措施。該市的城市雨水系統（Urban Stormwater System, USS）目前正面臨越來越大的挑戰。此外，基礎設施老化等營運效率低下問題，進一步阻礙了排水效能。因此，如何有效評估USS的運作狀況，並制定能抵禦極端天氣的維護策略，已成為關鍵議題。 目前USS的評估通常依賴定期檢查，例如預定的入水口及管道巡查。然而，這些方法存在空間覆蓋範圍有限及僅能進行事後觀察的缺陷，因而可能無法識別極端降水事件期間實際的USS故障點。為填補此缺口，本項目提出利用來自社交媒體平台的眾源地理資訊（Volunteered Geographic Information, VGI）來評估USS。在此構想中，VGI提供一種互補方法：市民可作為分散式感測器，產生帶有地理標籤的洪水貼文，這些貼文直接對應USS功能異常的位置，特別是公眾高度關注的區域。若能妥善提取並分析此類與洪水相關的VGI，即可為有效的USS評估提供及時且標註故障的數據。 研究流程設計如下：（i）將開發一套人工智能賦能的工具箱，用於從多模態VGI（包括文字、圖像及影片）中識別、地理定位並量化即時洪水相關數據。此工具箱將量化洪水範圍、識別洪水位置，並評估公眾情緒，以協助制定維護策略。（ii）利用所提取的洪水範圍評估本地排水單元的脆弱性，並將其作為標籤，訓練貝葉斯圖神經網路（Bayesian Graph Neural Network, BGNN）。BGNN將以機率方式揭示脆弱性如何在整個USS網路中傳播，尤其是在缺乏VGI覆蓋的區域。（iii）透過整合故障機率（來自BGNN）與估計的故障後果（涵蓋社會、經濟及公眾情緒影響），量化整個網路的USS故障風險。為實現風險緩解，將開發一個可解釋的大型語言模型（LLM）驅動的USS管理代理。在真實城市環境中進行全面驗證與評估後，所開發的AI代理預期能同時強化短期應急響應及長期維護規劃，並更廣泛地支援氣候韌性城市的發展。

21212526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21212526.value: 基於視覺證據的大型視覺語言模型可靠推理的不確定性估計方法研究

21212526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21212526.value: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have recently emerged as powerful tools for a wide range of tasks, including visual question answering, multimodal reasoning, and image captioning. By coupling high-capacity vision encoders with large language models, LVLMs such as LLaVa demonstrate impressive capabilities in high-impact domains such as education, healthcare, and scientific research, where reliability and trust are critical. However, while LVLMs generate fluent and contextually rich responses, their expressions of uncertainty are always miscalibrated, exhibiting overconfidence even when predictions are incorrect. Such unreliable answers undermine user trust and limit the safe deployment of these models in real-world decision-making scenarios. Despite significant progress in model calibration that aligns predicted confidence with true accuracy in traditional classification tasks, a provable path to well-calibrated LVLMs remains an open problem. Unlike traditional closed-set classification with a single modality, LVLM tasks are inherently open-set and multimodal, where visual evidence and textual reasoning interact in complex ways. Existing calibration techniques follow standard training pipelines that rely on deterministic image-text pairs, implicitly teaching models that the world is certain, which introduces an intrinsic posterior error in confidence estimation. Furthermore, current methods cannot generalize calibration across diverse multimodal downstream tasks. In this project, we emphasize that seeing is believing, i.e., every textual claim generated by LVLMs should be grounded in reliable visual evidence. Based on this foundation, we investigate a roadmap towards reliable LVLMs, which contains three major tasks. 1) We will theoretically study the posterior error in existing training pipelines and explicitly control it for provable calibration. By inverting the difficult posterior estimation problem, a new task of generating images conditioned on posterior probabilities can be introduced, which theoretically reduces calibration error with low sample complexity. 2) We will leverage the synthetic data to pretrain a well-calibrated vision encoder in LVLMs. After parsing LVLM answers into unified claims, the uncertainty of each claim can be accurately quantified via reliable visual features from this vision encoder. 3) We will integrate calibrated confidence into LVLMs for reliable inference, including visual reasoning that performs high-resolution reinspection for low-confidence regions and uncertainty expression with user interaction via confidence-guided clarification. We fulfill the research gap by investigating a new roadmap towards reliable LVLM instead of traditional calibration within limited scopes. A new data-driven paradigm for calibration research is introduced with theoretical guidance, which has the potential to accelerate the advancement of this research field. 大型視覺語言模型（LVLMs）近年來成為支援視覺問答、多模態推理和圖像描述等任務的重要工具。透過結合視覺編碼器與大語言模型。 LVLM在教育、醫療和科學研究等高影響力領域展現出強大能力，而這些領域對模型可靠性與可信度提出了關鍵要求。然而，儘管LVLM能產生流暢且具有豐富上下文資訊的響應，但其不確定性表達始終存在校準失準問題，即在預測錯誤時仍表現出過高置信度。這類不可靠回答削弱使用者信任，並限制模型在真實決策場景中的安全部署。儘管模型校準技術已在傳統分類任務中實現預測置信度與真實準確率的匹配，但如何建立具有理論保證的LVLM校準方法仍是開放性問題。不同於單模態封閉集合分類，LVLM任務天然具有開放性與多模態特徵，視覺證據與文本推理有複雜交互作用。現有校準方法依賴確定性的圖像-文字訓練數據，隱式假設世界具有確定性，從而在置信度估計中引入內在後驗誤差。此外，現有方法難以將校準能力泛化至多樣化的多模態下游任務。本計畫提出基於視覺證據的研究理念，即LVLM產生的每個文本聲明均應建立在可靠視覺證據之上，並探索可靠LVLM的系統研究路徑，包括三個主要任務：（1）理論研究現有訓練範式中的後驗誤差，並進行明確控制以實現可證明校準。透過反向建構後驗機率條件下的影像生成任務，將困難的後驗估計問題轉化為可控的資料生成問題，從理論上以較低樣本複雜度降低校準誤差。 （2）利用合成資料預訓練具有良好校準能力的視覺編碼器。透過將LVLM輸出解析為統一聲明，並結合可靠視覺特徵，實現對每個聲明不確定性的準確量化。 （3）將校準置信度融入可靠推理過程，包括針對低置信區域的高解析度視覺重檢，以及透過置信度引導澄清實現不確定性表達與使用者互動。本研究突破傳統校準方法僅在有限任務範圍內優化的局限，提出面向可靠LVLM的新研究路徑，並建立具有理論指導的數據驅動校準範式，推動不確定性估計與可信多模態人工智慧的發展。

21213626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21213626.value: Autonomous systems, from self-driving cars to industrial robots, are poised to revolutionize society, yet their widespread deployment is critically hindered by the challenge of uncertainty. While deep learning models excel in controlled environments, their potential for rare but catastrophic failures in the unpredictable real world makes them untrustworthy for safety-critical applications. This creates an urgent need for advanced artificial intelligence systems that do not just perform well on average, but can provide rigorous, provable guarantees on their safety. Current research often addresses uncertainty in isolated components of the autonomy stack: perception, prediction, or decision-making, leaving a critical blank in creating an integrated, certifiably safe pipeline. This project introduces a unified, principled framework that leverages advanced Conformal Prediction (CP) theory to provide rigorous, distribution-free safety guarantees across the entire autonomy stack. We directly confront three fundamental challenges. First, to move beyond perception models for semantic segmentation with only "average-case" guarantees, we will develop novel methods that achieve more robust conditional risk control, adapting their uncertainty estimates to the difficulty of each specific scene. Second, to address the multi-modal nature of agent behavior, we will design a novel trajectory prediction method that generates planner-friendly geometric sets such as convex polytopes and alpha-shapes that are simultaneously guaranteed to be valid in coverage rate, geometrically simple for downstream planning use, and tight enough to be efficient and practical. Third, and most critically, we will move from guarantees to action by designing an online risk controller. This controller operationalizes Conformal Decision Theory (CDT) in a closed-loop system, dynamically adjusting the planner's conservatism based on realized outcomes to provably steer the system's long-term average safety performance to a user-defined target, ensuring robustness even under distribution shifts. By creating a principled and complete pipeline, this project marks a fundamental shift from static uncertainty avoidance to dynamic, adaptive risk control. The outcomes will provide a foundational methodology for building the next generation of trustworthy autonomous systems, accelerating their safe and reliable deployment in society. 本項目旨在為自動駕駛等安全攸關（Safety-Critical）的自主系統建立一個從感知到決策直到最終行動的風險可控框架，以解決傳統深度學習模型僅能在平均意義上提供性能保證、無法應對分佈外數據與長尾極端場景（Edge Cases）安全隱患的致命缺陷。針對不確定性在系統管線中引發的級聯放大風險，本項目創新性地引入共形預測（Conformal Prediction）技術，構建貫穿全流程且具備嚴謹統計安全保證的自主系統架構，研究內容涵蓋四大核心模組：首先研發共形風險適應（CRA）與共形自適應閾值（COAT）模型，在動態場景下導出邊界可控的語義預測集以實現穩健條件安全感知；其次構建面向軌跡預測的共形自適應幾何集合（CAGES），生成既具備統計安全保證又易於規劃器調用的多模態幾何預測集；隨後開發基於共形決策理論的在線閉環風險控制器（OCRC），結合時序共形預測與李雅普諾夫控制理論實現長遠平均風險的動態實時調控；最後在高仿真模擬環境與真實數據集中對“感知-預測-決策-行動”全流程進行端到端集成與極端場景驗證，其成果將打破傳統單點預測的局限，為下一代高可靠自主系統的落地提供計算開銷低且具數學安全證明的堅實理論與技術支撐。

21213726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21213726.value: 用於評估阻燃木結構隔間防火性能的人工智能驅動多尺度模擬平台

21213726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21213726.value: The global construction sector faces an urgent challenge: reducing its carbon footprint to combat climate change. Engineered wood products (EWPs), such as cross-laminated timber, offer a sustainable alternative to concrete and steel by storing carbon and enabling circular economy practices. However, their widespread adoption in tall buildings is hindered by one critical issue - fire safety. Timber is combustible, and current fire protection strategies rely heavily on costly, destructive full-scale tests, which limit innovation and confidence in design. This project proposes a transformative solution: a high-fidelity multiscale fire modelling and risk assessment framework that integrates advanced computational techniques with experimental validation. At the material level, Reactive Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations will reveal how timber and flame-retardant coatings behave under extreme heat, uncovering the chemical pathways that govern charring, gas emissions, and self-extinguishing potential. These insights will be used to extract accurate thermal degradation kinetics and material properties. At the structural level, these data will feed into Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) models to simulate realistic compartment fires in mass timber buildings. This approach will capture complex interactions between heat, smoke, and structural elements under various ventilation and loading conditions—critical for predicting flashover and burnout scenarios. By coupling MD and CFD, the framework will bridge the gap between microscopic chemistry and large-scale fire dynamics, enabling unprecedented predictive accuracy. Finally, the project will leverage machine learning (ML) to develop a rapid fire risk assessment tool. This tool, designed as a Building Information Modelling (BIM) plug-in, will allow architects and engineers to instantly evaluate fire performance indicators—such as temperature, smoke layer height, and radiation—during the design phase. This capability will empower performance-based fire safety design and accelerate the safe adoption of timber construction in Hong Kong and beyond. By combining cutting-edge simulation, experimental validation, and AI-driven design tools, this research will deliver a robust, scalable platform for fire safety engineering. The outcome will not only enhance confidence in sustainable timber construction but also contribute to global efforts in decarbonising the built environment. 全球建築業正面臨一項迫切挑戰：降低碳足跡以應對氣候變化。工程木製品（EWP），例如正交膠合木，能透過固碳及推動循環經濟，成為混凝土與鋼材的可持續替代方案。然而，其在高層建築中的廣泛應用，主要受限於防火安全這一關鍵問題。木材具有可燃性，加上現行防火策略高度依賴昂貴且具破壞性的足尺試驗，從而限制了設計創新與工程信心。 本項目提出一項變革性方案：結合先進計算技術與實驗驗證，建立高保真的多尺度火災模擬與風險評估框架。在材料微觀層面，反應分子動力學（MD）模擬將揭示木材及阻燃塗層在極端高溫下的行為，釐清主導炭化、氣體釋放及自熄潛力的化學路徑；所得數據將用於提取準確的熱降解動力學參數及材料特性。在結構巨觀層面，有關數據將輸入計算流體力學（CFD）模型，以模擬工程木結構建築中的真實隔間火災，捕捉熱、煙與結構構件在不同通風及荷載條件下的複雜相互作用，這對預測閃燃及燃盡情景至關重要。 透過耦合分子動力學（MD）與計算流體力學（CFD），該框架將銜接微觀化學與大尺度火災動力學，實現前所未有的預測精度。此外，本項目將運用機器學習（ML）開發快速火災風險評估工具，並將其設計為建築資訊模型（BIM）插件，讓建築師及工程師在設計階段即時評估各項防火性能指標，例如溫度、煙層高度及熱輻射。此能力將促進性能化防火安全設計，並加快木結構建築在香港及全球的安全應用。 本研究結合前沿數值模擬、實驗驗證及人工智能驅動的設計工具，將提供一套穩健且具擴展性的防火工程平台。研究成果不僅能增強對可持續木結構建築的信心，更將為建築環境的全球減碳目標作出重要貢獻。

21214426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21214426.value: 复杂载荷下的软结构非线性接触力学及其矢量场力学感知应用

21214426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21214426.value: Perception of mechanics cues (termed mechano-perception) underpins a wide range of leading-edge engineering fields, including human-machine interaction, dexterous robotic manipulation, and advanced biomedical systems. The rapid development of these fields increasingly depends on high-resolution, multidimensional vector-field mechanics information perception. However, existing Vector-Field Mechano-Perception (VFMP) approaches based on electro- or magneto-transduction commonly suffer from structural complexity, environmental susceptibility, and computationally intensive inference. In contrast, vision-based mechano-perception derives contact mechanics quantities by optically tracking the deformation of soft materials, offering notable advantages in simplicity, robustness, and integrability. Yet the absence of a comprehensive theoretical understanding of the nonlinear contact mechanics of soft structures under complex loadings remains a key bottleneck that constrains the advancement of vision-based VFMP technologies. To overcome this limitation, the project will establish a systematic theoretical framework describing the nonlinear contact mechanics of soft structures under coupled complex loadings, including compression, shear, and torsion, to enable next-generation VFMP. Building on the applicant's prior work on nonlinear contact theory of soft elastic spheres under large-deformation compression, we will develop mechanics models that accurately capture essential contact behaviors such as contact force and contact area under complex loadings. A VFMP prototype will then be constructed to experimentally verify and refine the proposed theoretical framework. On this validated foundation, a mechanics-guided (physics-informed) VFMP system will be developed to achieve high-resolution, multidirectional mechano-perception and to explore its potential in representative scenarios such as dexterous robotic manipulation, immersive human–machine interaction, and biomechanical monitoring. The implementation of this proposal is expected to establish an in-depth understanding of the nonlinear contact behaviors and multiaxial mechanical responses of soft structures, thereby advancing the fundamental mechanics of coupled large deformations. Furthermore, it will provide a rigorous scientific basis for the design of intelligent VFMP systems with high accuracy, robustness, and adaptability, offering a general theoretical framework for intelligent mechanical perception that can benefit broad engineering fields such as soft robotics, health monitoring, adaptive materials, and human–machine interfaces. In the long term, the outcomes of this research will contribute to Hong Kong's strategic vision of developing itself into an international hub for advanced manufacturing, smart robotics, and biomedical engineering, fostering cross-disciplinary innovation and talent cultivation in the Greater Bay Area. 力学信息感知（Mechano-Perception，简称力学感知）是人机交互、机器人灵巧操作以及先进生物医疗系统等前沿领域的重要基础。这些领域的快速发展，日益依赖于对高分辨率、多维度矢量场力学信息的精确感知。然而，现有基于电学或磁学原理的矢量场力学感知（Vector-Field Mechano-Perception, VFMP）技术普遍存在结构复杂、易受环境干扰以及推理计算成本高等问题。相比之下，基于视觉的力学感知技术，通过光学手段追踪软材料接触变形，从而获取接触力学信息，在结构简洁性、环境鲁棒性及系统集成性等方面具有显著优势。然而，目前对于复杂载荷作用下的软结构非线性接触力学行为尚缺乏系统性的理论认识，这已成为制约视觉式VFMP技术进一步发展的关键瓶颈。 为此，本项目拟建立复杂耦合载荷（包括压缩、剪切和扭转）作用下软结构非线性接触力学的系统理论框架，为下一代VFMP技术提供理论基础。基于申请人在软弹性球体大变形压缩非线性接触理论方面的前期研究，本项目将构建能够准确描述复杂载荷下关键接触行为（如接触力、接触面积等）的力学模型。在此基础上，搭建VFMP实验原型系统，对所提出的理论框架进行实验验证与模型修正。依托验证后的理论模型，进一步开发力学引导（物理信息驱动，Physics-informed）的VFMP系统，实现高分辨率、多维力学信息感知，并探索其在机器人灵巧操作、沉浸式人机交互以及生物力学监测等典型应用场景中的应用潜力。 本项目的实施将加深人们对软结构非线性接触行为及其多维力学响应机制的理解，推动耦合大变形接触力学基础理论的发展。此外，将为构建具有高精度、高鲁棒性和强环境适应性的智能VFMP系统提供坚实的科学依据，并形成适用于智能力学感知的通用理论框架，为软体机器人、健康监测、自适应材料及人机交互等多种前沿领域的发展提供理论支撑。长远而言，本研究成果将为香港建设“国际领先的先进制造、智能机器人和生物医学工程创新高地”提供有力支撑，并为粤港澳大湾区的跨学科科技创新及高层次人才培养发挥积极推动作用。

21215026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21215026.value: 用於新一代超低介電常數材料的分子工程多孔二維聚合物

21215026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21215026.value: In the current information-driven era, integrated circuits (ICs) constitute the cornerstone of modern electronic technologies and everyday devices. With the development of ICs, integration and miniaturization have become more prevalent. As device dimensions continue to scale in line with Moore’s law, transistor density doubles roughly every two years. The resulting increasement in device density forces concomitant downscaling of interconnects, which increases interconnect resistance (R) and capacitance (C), leading to bigger crosstalk noise, delay in signal propagation speed and increasing power consumption. To mitigate these issues, low dielectric constant (low-k) materials are essential, as they can effectively reduce interconnect crosstalk and signal delay. The semiconductor industry has successively introduced carbon-doped oxides (k ≈ 3) and SiCOH-based materials (k ≈ 2.5–2.7) as interlayer dielectrics. However, these materials remain insufficient for the ultralow-k (< 2) regime demanded by advanced technology nodes. More critically, most current low-k dielectrics suffer from poor thermal conductivity and inadequate mechanical robustness due to their disordered or highly porous microstructures, leading to film damage and cracking during backend processing. These limitations highlight an urgent need for next-generation ultralow-k dielectrics that combine exceptionally low permittivity with superior mechanical, thermal stability and processibility. In this proposal, we aim to bridge this critical gap by developing ultralow-k dielectrics based on two-dimensional polymers (2DPs)-crystalline, molecularly ordered networks with precisely tunable porosity. Our preliminary results demonstrate that the ordered porous architecture of 2DPs can achieve dielectric constants as low as ~1.8 while maintaining exceptional mechanical robustness and favorable thermal conductivity. To realize this potential, we will (i) design and synthesize wafer-scale 2DP thin films, (ii) systematically quantify their dielectric, mechanical, and thermal properties to establish clear structure–property relationships, and (iii) elucidate the molecular mechanisms governing low-k behavior in 2DPs through theoretical simulations. This project aims to establish a new materials platform for ultralow-k, mechanically robust interlayer dielectrics, supported by experimentally validated structure–property design rules that enable rational control of porosity, crystallinity, and interfacial integrity without compromising reliability. By integrating molecular design, wafer-scale synthesis, and multiscale characterization, the proposed research will elucidate how nanoscale architecture governs the dielectric, mechanical, and thermal behaviors of two-dimensional polymeric frameworks. These insights will form the foundation for a predictive design framework toward next-generation ultralow-k dielectrics that simultaneously achieve mechanical integrity, thermal stability, and process compatibility, while providing a scalable and manufacturable pathway for faster, more reliable, and energy-efficient integrated circuits. 在當前資訊驅動的時代，積體電路（IC）構成了現代電子技術與日常裝置的基石。隨著半導體技術的發展，元件的高度整合與微型化已成為必然趨勢。在摩爾定律的推動下，電晶體密度約每兩年翻倍，元件尺寸的持續微縮導致互連線間距大幅縮小。這不僅增加了互連電阻（R）與電容（C），更引發了嚴重的電阻-電容（RC）延遲、串音雜訊及功耗攀升。為緩解上述問題，導入低介電常數（low-k）材料以降低互連串音與訊號延遲至關重要。目前，半導體產業已廣泛採用碳摻雜氧化物（k ≈ 3）及 SiCOH 基材料（k ≈ 2.5–2.7）作為層間介電質。然而，面對先進製程節點對超低k（< 2）材料的嚴苛要求，現有材料已難以滿足需求。更關鍵的是，多數傳統低k介電質因具備無序或高孔隙的微觀結構，導致熱傳導率低落且機械強度不足，在後段金屬化製程（BEOL）中極易發生薄膜損傷或破裂。這些限制凸顯了業界對兼具極低介電常數、優異機械特性、高熱穩定性及製程相容性的新一代超低k介電質的迫切需求。在本計畫中，我們旨在透過開發基於二維聚合物（2DP）的超低k介電質來填補此一關鍵技術缺口。該材料具備晶體有序的分子網絡，且其孔隙率可進行精確調控。我們的初步研究結果顯示，2DP 的有序多孔結構能實現約 1.8 的超低介電常數，同時維持優異的機械強度與良好的熱傳導性。為充分發揮此材料潛力，本計畫將執行以下重點工作：（i）設計並合成晶圓級 2DP 薄膜；（ii）系統性地量測其介電、機械及熱學性質，以建立明確的「結構-性能」關聯；（iii）結合理論模擬，闡明 2DP 中展現低k行為的分子層級機制。本計畫期望為超低k且具備機械穩固性的層間介電質研發建立一個全新的材料平台。我們將提出經實驗驗證的結構-性能設計準則，以實現在不犧牲可靠性的前提下，對薄膜的孔隙率、結晶度及界面完整性進行精準調控。透過整合分子設計、晶圓級合成與多尺度表徵，本研究將揭示奈米尺度結構如何支配二維聚合物框架的介電、機械及熱學行為。最終，本研究將為新一代超低k介電質的預測性設計架構奠定基礎，確保其同時滿足機械完整性、熱穩定性及製程相容性，進而為打造更高速、更可靠且具高能源效益的積體電路，提供一條具擴展性與量產可行性的新途徑。

21215726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21215726.value: 基于多模态影像引导传感与自主递药的可降解器件研究

21215726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21215726.value: Monitoring physiological parameters and providing timely interventions, especially in deep tissues and complex anatomical structures, is crucial for advanced healthcare. In recent years, development of bio-integrated devices enables real-time, noninvasive monitoring and targeted drug delivery on demand. However, attenuation in biological tissues limits the use of existing sensing mechanisms to shallow depths, while drug delivery systems relying on wireless near-field coupling or batteries face limitations in functional lifetime or operation distance. It remains challenging to achieve comprehensive diagnosis and personalized therapeutic intervention on demand at arbitrary anatomical locations. In this context, medical imaging modalities including ultrasound, computed tomography (CT), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are of growing interest due to their deep-tissue penetration capabilities with high spatiotemporal resolution. While these modalities are highly capable for clinical diagnosis, their potential to monitor biophysical and biochemical signals remains largely unexplored. Meanwhile, although stimuli-responsive soft materials can transduce physiological signals into physical changes such as shape transformation or volumetric changes, their integration into devices for autonomous therapeutic intervention remains largely unexplored. To address the above challenge, this project aims to develop a bioresorbable, multi-parameter responsive, integrated platform for simultaneous multimodal imaging-guided sensing and autonomous drug delivery in any anatomical locations of interest, using pH, temperature and glucose as three representative physiological parameters. The Principal Investigator has extensive expertise and a relevant track record in functional materials (PNAS, 2020) and bio-integrated devices (Science, 2024). Specifically, the project aims to achieve the following: (i) Comprehensive sensing of both chemical and physical parameters including pH, temperature, and glucose by converting the dimensional changes of responsive materials into quantifiable signals across ultrasound, CT, and MRI, leveraging the complementary advantages of all three modalities. (ii) Autonomous, location-independent drug release triggered directly by internal biosignals, using the actuation of responsive hydrogels to rupture a sealed reservoir. This design also enables miniaturization and potential operation in the long term. (iii) Comprehensive sensing of multiple physiological parameters with autonomous, biosignal-responsive therapeutic intervention simultaneously. We choose temperature, pH, and glucose to validate monitoring and autonomous regulation in mouse models of fever, intestinal leakage, and type 1 diabetes mellitus. Success in these goals is essential for timely treatment of complex conditions and could potentially depress disease progression. This integrated platform provides new insight into the fundamental understanding of functional materials and device design, as well as the broad application potential in precision medicine. 对生理参数进行持续监测并及时实施干预，尤其是在深部组织和复杂解剖结构中，是现代医疗中的关键问题。近年来，生物集成器件的发展使实时、无创监测与按需靶向药物递送成为可能。然而，生物组织中的信号衰减使现有传感机制的有效作用深度多局限于浅层；依赖无线近场耦合或电池供能的药物递送系统，则在功能寿命或工作距离方面存在限制。因此，在任意目标解剖位置实现综合诊断与按需个体化治疗干预，仍面临重要挑战。在此背景下，超声、计算机断层扫描和磁共振成像等医学影像技术因兼具深部组织穿透能力与较高时空分辨率而日益受到关注。尽管这些影像模态已广泛用于临床诊断，其用于监测生物物理与生化信号的潜力仍未得到充分开发。与此同时，刺激响应型软材料虽可将生理信号转化为形状变化或体积变化等物理响应，但其进一步集成至器件并用于自主治疗干预，仍缺乏系统探索。 针对上述挑战，本项目拟开发一种可生物吸收、多参数响应的一体化器件平台，在任意目标解剖位置同步实现多模态影像引导传感与自主药物递送，并以酸碱度、温度和葡萄糖作为三类代表性生理与生化参数。申请人在功能材料和生物集成器件方面具有丰富经验和相关研究基础。具体拟实现以下目标：（1）充分发挥超声、计算机断层扫描和磁共振成像三种影像模态的互补优势，将响应材料的尺寸变化转化为可在不同影像模态中定量读取的信号，实现对酸碱度、温度和葡萄糖等化学与物理参数的综合传感；（2）利用响应水凝胶的致动形变破坏密封储药单元，实现由体内生物信号直接触发、且不受解剖位置限制的自主药物释放，该设计同时有利于器件微型化，并具备长期运行潜力；（3）在同一平台中同步实现多生理参数的综合传感与生物信号响应型自主治疗干预，并选取温度、酸碱度和葡萄糖，分别在发热、肠道泄漏和一型糖尿病小鼠模型中验证其监测与自主调控能力。上述目标的实现对于复杂病症的及时治疗至关重要，并有望抑制疾病进展。该一体化平台将深化对功能材料与器件设计基本规律的认识，并在精准医疗中展现广泛的应用潜力。

21216926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21216926.value: 開發具有目標力學性能與自適應特性的可機械訓練超材料

21216926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21216926.value: The revolutionary concept of metamaterials that uses geometry rather than composition to control material properties has profoundly influenced modern materials science and engineering. Owing to their high programmability, rich nonlinearity, and intrinsic scalability, mechanical metamaterials have enabled a wide range of applications, spanning aerospace, robotics, and biomedical engineering. Despite these advances, a critical challenge persists: most metamaterials remain monofunctional, where a single topology or morphology yields only one type of mechanical response, lacking the reprogrammability and post-fabrication adaptability essential for deployment in unstructured and dynamic environments. Moreover, inverse design of metamaterials with desired functionalities remains computationally demanding, as current machine learning approaches require extensive datasets, substantial energy consumption, and accurate constitutive models that often fail to capture experimental complexities. This project aims to overcome these limitations by establishing a new paradigm of physically trainable metamaterials—materials that can gain, retain, and reprogram mechanical properties through mechanical training, without relying on external power, active control, or computational optimization. The core innovation lies in a multistable metaspring unit that exhibits state-dependent stiffness, allowing mechanical systems to autonomously evolve toward target behaviors through repeated loading. Through synergistic integration of theoretical modeling, numerical simulation, and experimental validation, this project will: (1) employ finite-element simulations and experimental testing to identify how geometric parameters affect the properties of metaspring units; (2) systematically elucidate how lattice topology and metaspring properties govern training efficiency, capacity, and reversibility across diverse target responses, including auxeticity, programmable anisotropy, and shape morphing; (3) develop training protocols that maximize the material training capacity and accuracy while ensuring reproducibility and scalability; and (4) experimentally demonstrate and validate training capabilities in both 2D and 3D metamaterial networks, and translate these findings into proof-of-concept applications such as adaptive medical mattresses for bedsore prevention and personalized assistive devices. This research will deliver a universal and pluripotent metamaterial platform capable of expressing multiple, reprogrammable mechanical properties within a single design, fundamentally bridging the gap between passive structural materials and self-adaptive intelligent matter. By enabling materials to learn from mechanical experience rather than computational design, this work provides adaptive systems that require no external power, computing infrastructure, or active control. The outcomes will advance both fundamental understanding of physical learning in mechanical systems and practical deployment of next-generation adaptive structures, allowing for innovative applications in robotics, biomedical devices, and reconfigurable engineering systems. 超材料利用幾何結構而非材料成分來調控材料性能，這一概念已深刻影響了現代材料科學與工程。憑藉高度的可編程性、豐富的非線性以及內在的可擴展性，機械超材料已廣泛應用於航空航天、機器人技術與生物醫學工程等眾多領域。然而，儘管取得了上述進展，一個關鍵挑戰依然存在：大多數超材料仍屬單功能材料，單一拓撲或形態只能產生一種力學響應，缺乏在非結構化動態環境中部署所必需的可重編程性與製造後自適應能力。此外，針對特定功能對超材料進行逆向設計，其計算代價依然高昂，因為當前的機器學習方法需要海量數據集、可觀的能耗、以及精確的本構模型，而這類模型往往難以刻畫實驗中的複雜性。 本項目旨在建立一種全新的物理可訓練超材料範式，以克服上述局限：此類材料能夠通過機械訓練獲得、保持並重編程其力學性能，而無需依賴外部動力、主動控制或計算優化。其核心創新在於一種具有狀態依賴剛度的多穩態超彈簧單元，可使機械系統通過反覆加載自主演化至目標行為。本項目將理論建模、數值仿真與實驗驗證協同結合，開展以下工作：(1)運用有限元仿真與實驗測試，釐清幾何參數對超彈簧單元性能的影響；(2)系統闡明晶格拓撲與超彈簧性能如何決定多種目標響應下的訓練效率、訓練容量及可逆性，目標響應包括負泊松比、可編程各向異性與形狀變形；(3)開發訓練方案,在確保可重複性與可擴展性的同時，最大化材料的訓練容量與精度；(4)在二維與三維超材料網絡中實驗驗證訓練能力，並將研究成果轉化為概念驗證應用，例如用於預防褥瘡的自適應醫用床墊及個性化輔助器具。 本研究將交付一個通用且多能的超材料平台，能夠在單一設計中表達多種可重編程的力學性能，從根本上填補被動結構材料與自適應智能物質之間的空白。通過讓材料從機械加載歷史中學習而非依賴計算設計，本研究提供了無需外部動力、計算模型或主動控制的自適應系統。研究成果將同時深化對機械系統中物理學習的基礎理論認識，並推動下一代自適應結構的實際部署,從而為機器人技術、生物醫學器件與可重構工程系統開闢創新應用。

21217426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21217426.value: 增材制造铝合金高疲劳抗力的本征起源：胞状结构的关键作用

21217426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21217426.value: To meet the growing demand for energy efficiency and climate sustainability, developing high-strength and lightweight structural components is vital for modern industries such as aerospace and transportation. Metal additive manufacturing (AM), with its unique ability for freeform fabrication and topology optimization, enables the creation of next-generation lightweight and high-efficiency structures. However, the widespread industrial adoption of AM alloys remains limited by their inferior fatigue properties compared with conventional wrought counterparts, primarily due to process-induced defects such as pores and lack-of-fusion regions. Since over 80% of structural material failures in dynamic components are caused by fatigue, overcoming this limitation is crucial for improving the reliability and accelerating the adoption of AM alloys in advanced engineering applications. Recent breakthroughs have begun to overturn this paradigm. The as-printed ultrafine microstructures inherent to AM have been found to provide exceptional fatigue resistance, surpassing that of conventional counterparts across different alloy systems. Notably, the fatigue resistance of void-free AM Ti-6Al-4V alloy has been reported in Nature to reach 1 GPa. Likewise, the PI’s previous study published in Nature Materials demonstrated that the as-printed eutectic Si cellular structures in AM AlSi10Mg alloys exhibit intrinsically ultrahigh fatigue strengths up to 85% of their tensile strength. Nevertheless, the underlying mechanisms governing the high fatigue resistance of these microstructures remain to be fully understood. In this project, the PI aims to elucidate the intrinsic fatigue-resistant mechanisms of the eutectic cellular structures in AM AlSi10Mg alloys. By integrating multiscale experimental techniques with theoretical analysis, the project will systematically investigate (i) the evolution of dislocations within the cellular network during cyclic loading, (ii) the deformation compatibility between the cellular boundaries and the aluminum matrix, and (iii) the critical stress conditions that govern fatigue failure. These efforts are expected to reveal a new fatigue mechanism distinct from conventional cumulative damage. Furthermore, the proposed fatigue-resistant design strategy will be extended to other AM eutectic aluminium alloys to verify its universality. The successful completion of this project will establish a solid theoretical foundation for advancing the understanding of fatigue mechanisms and improving the fatigue performance of AM aluminum alloys. The resulting insights can be further extended to other AM alloy systems, thereby promoting the broader application of AM components. Ultimately, these outcomes will be instrumental in enhancing the structural reliability and energy efficiency of lightweight components across diverse industrial sectors. 面向能源高效利用与气候可持续发展的迫切需求，研制兼具高强度与轻量化特征的先进结构构件，已成为航空航天、交通运输等领域的重要发展方向。金属增材制造（AM）凭借复杂构件自由成形、拓扑优化及多功能一体化制造等优势，为新一代高结构效率轻量化构件提供了重要技术途径。然而，受孔隙、未熔合等工艺缺陷影响，增材制造合金的疲劳性能通常低于传统变形加工合金，严重制约其在关键承载构件中的工程应用。鉴于工程结构服役失效中超过80%与疲劳相关，突破增材制造合金的疲劳性能瓶颈，是保障其长期服役可靠性的关键科学问题。 近年来的研究进展正在改变增材制造合金疲劳性能受缺陷主导的传统认识。研究表明，增材制造过程中形成的打印态超细组织可赋予钛合金和铝合金优异的本征疲劳抗力。例如，无孔洞打印态Ti-6Al-4V合金的疲劳强度可接近1 GPa。申请人的前期研究进一步发现，增材制造铝合金中的打印态共晶胞状结构具有显著的本征抗疲劳能力，其疲劳强度最高可达到抗拉强度的85%。然而，此类胞状结构如何协调循环塑性变形、抑制局部应变集中并延缓疲劳损伤萌生，仍缺乏系统深入的机制认识。 本项目拟围绕增材制造铝合金共晶胞状结构的本征抗疲劳机制开展研究。通过结合多尺度原位实验、微观组织表征与理论分析，系统揭示循环载荷下共晶胞状网络与铝基体之间的协同变形、界面相互作用及组织演化规律，阐明其对局部塑性、应变集中和疲劳损伤萌生的调控机制。在此基础上，识别控制疲劳失效的关键临界应力条件，探索区别于传统累积损伤模式的新型疲劳机制，并建立适用于打印态胞状结构的疲劳理论框架。进一步将该抗疲劳设计策略拓展至其他增材制造铝合金，以验证其普适性。 本项目有望揭示打印态非平衡微观组织实现高疲劳抗力的关键物理机制，推动增材制造合金疲劳研究由“缺陷控制”向“组织调控与临界应力控制”拓展，并为高可靠、轻量化增材制造构件在航空航天和交通运输等领域的应用提供理论基础与设计准则。

21218026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21218026.value: Worldwide, over 200 million people live with severe visual impairment, including roughly 0.2% of the population in Hong Kong, underscoring it as a persistent scientific and societal challenge. Embodied visual navigation provides a compelling domain for advancing theoretical models of visual intelligence that unify perception and action. Existing multimodal systems frequently rely on large language models (LLMs) or cloud-based computation, presuming that high-level reasoning must be expressed through discrete linguistic token streams. This assumption imposes structural limitations: biological vision operates through continuous, structured perceptual processes integrating geometry, semantics, and motion, without serializing cognition into language for real-time spatial decision-making. This project investigates an embodied visual navigation framework in which navigation competence emerges directly from visual representations grounded in embodiment. Language is retained purely as an interface for human interaction rather than as the central reasoning substrate. Our preliminary results indicate that navigational inference can be grounded directly within the visual pathway, without detouring through language. These observations challenge the prevailing reliance on patch-based tokenization and language-driven reasoning, suggesting that current paradigms are fundamentally misaligned with the intrinsic structure of spatial intelligence. We propose a unified multimodal architecture advancing in two tightly integrated phases. Phase-I introduces object-centered, multi-granular visual representations realized through a hybrid graph-and-patch formulation, enabling explicit modeling of relational structure, affordances, and motion dynamics within a coherent model. The language module serves only as an interaction interface (speech I/O), rather than as the reasoning engine. Phase-II develops principled techniques for theoretical soundness under computational constraints, contributing methods in model compression, resource-bounded optimization, and provable safety guarantees during real-time inference, especially under distributional shifts. The anticipated outcome is a foundational shift in multimodal intelligence: core cognition for navigation becomes native to vision itself, eliminating dependence on linguistic intermediaries or external computation. By grounding decision-making directly in structured visual representations and deploying models that maintain robustness and privacy under real-world constraints, this project establishes a scalable theoretical and practical basis for reliable embodied visual navigation. The broader theoretical significance lies in establishing a rigorous framework for multimodal intelligence in which perceptual structure, rather than symbolic transcription, governs decision-making. By departing from grid-based discretization toward object-centric reasoning and grounding action selection directly within visual computation, this research aims to inform next-generation embodied AI. The resulting theories and models provide a blueprint for scalable, privacy-preserving perception–action systems while advancing fundamental understanding of how intelligent agents interpret and navigate the physical world. 全球逾2億人深受嚴重視力障礙困擾（香港約佔本地人口的0.2%），這是亟待攻克的重大社會與科學課題。具身視覺導航作為統合感知與行動的關鍵途徑，是推動視覺智能理論發展的核心前沿。然而，現有主流系統多依賴大語言模型（LLM）或雲端算力，預設高級空間推理必須經由離散文本符號完成。這一做法脫離了生物視覺的本質：真實的生物視覺是通過融合幾何、語義與動態信息的連續感知直接進行空間決策，無需將認知過程轉化為語言。為此，本項目提出一種全新的具身視覺導航架構，使空間決策能力直接內生於視覺表徵本身，語言僅作為人機交互接口而非底層推理核心。前期預研表明，導航推理可完全在視覺通路內部自主完成，無需繞道語言中介。本項目分為兩個階段展開：（1）構建以目標為中心的多粒度視覺表徵：通過融合“圖結構與圖像塊”（Graph and Patch），顯式建模場景中的空間關係、環境可交互性與動態運動特性，語言模塊僅負責語音交互；（2）突破端側受限條件下的可信計算機制：針對邊緣端算力約束，研發輕量化模型壓縮與資源自適應優化算法，並建立在真實環境分布偏移下具備理論安全保障的實時推理機制。本項目旨在推動多模態智能由“語言中介主導”向“視覺原生驅動”的基礎範式轉變，擺脫對雲端算力與文本轉譯的依賴，在真實物理約束下實現兼顧低延遲、高魯棒性與隱私保護的端側智能，為下一代具身感知-行動系統提供堅實的理論與技術支撐。

21300426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21300426.value: 透過難度可控強化學習優化大型語言模型之數學推理能力

21300426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21300426.value: Training large language models (LLMs) to solve mathematical problems is a critical step towards developing advanced general reasoning capabilities. While reinforcement learning (RL) offers a powerful training paradigm, its effectiveness is heavily dependent on the quality, especially the difficulty distribution, of the training questions. Current RL algorithms, like GRPO, rely on contrasting correct and incorrect solution attempts for the same problem. If a question is too easy, all attempts are correct; if it is too hard, all are incorrect. In both cases, the training signal vanishes, hindering learning. This project addresses this fundamental problem by proposing a novel framework to optimize the data used in RL training. We focus on two core research questions: (1) How to find the optimal distribution of question difficulties for the RL training of a given LLM? and (2) How to efficiently generate a diverse and valid set of questions that match this target distribution? To answer the first question, we will perform a systematic analysis of how questions of varying difficulty levels influence learning dynamics and final model performance, aiming to derive an optimal difficulty profile. For the second question, we will develop novel methods to generate questions with controlled difficulty, moving beyond simple rejection sampling from existing datasets. Our approach includes decomposing complex problems into simpler sub-questions to aid smaller models and using constrained self-play to create novel, highly challenging problems to push the boundaries of state-of-the-art models. The outcomes of this project will deliver both theoretical insights and practical algorithms to significantly enhance the mathematical reasoning of LLMs. This work has profound implications beyond the AI industry, as the automated creation of novel problems offers powerful new tools for mathematical research and education. 訓練大型語言模型（LLM）求解數學問題，是建構高階通用推理能力的關鍵步驟。強化學習（RL）雖為效能卓越的訓練範式，然而其訓練成效高度取決於訓練試題的品質，尤以試題的難度分佈最為關鍵。現時 GRPO 等主流強化學習演算法，透過比對模型針對同一道題目產生的正確作答樣本與錯誤作答樣本進行優化。倘若試題過於淺易，模型所有作答輸出皆為正解；若試題難度過高，則所有作答均會出錯。上述兩種情況都會令模型失去有效的訓練訊號，繼而妨礙模型的學習過程。 本研究針對此一根本難題，提出一套全新架構以優化強化學習訓練所使用的數據。研究圍繞兩大核心研究議題展開探討：（1）針對特定的大型語言模型，應如何求出適配其強化學習訓練的最佳試題難度分佈？（2）如何高效率建構一套多元且有效的試題庫，並使其精準對應前述的目標難度分佈？針對首項研究議題，本研究系統分析不同難度的試題對模型學習動態以及最終效能表現的影響規律，藉此推導出最適的難度分佈曲線。針對第二項議題，本研究設計可管控難度的試題生成嶄新方法，捨棄僅依賴現有資料集進行簡單拒絕取樣的傳統做法。 本方法包含兩項核心技術方向：把複雜的數學問題拆解成多個簡易子問題，協助小型模型完成訓練；運用約束式自我對弈機制產生創新且高難度的數學題目，持續突破當下最先進模型的性能極限。本計劃的研究成果除了可提供理論層面的理據支援，亦可產出具備實用價值的演算法方案，顯著提升大型語言模型的數學推理能力。是項研究的價值不單只適用於人工智慧產業：透過自動化生成全新數學試題的技術，可為數學研究及數學教育範疇提供強大的嶄新工具，具備深遠的應用價值。

21300826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21300826.value: 基於動力學朗之萬方法的無偏高維採樣

21300826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21300826.value: Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) is a class of algorithms aimed at sampling from probability distributions, which arise in many real-world applications such as finance, numerical weather prediction and machine learning. MCMC methods rely on simulating a Markov chain which, through a proposal and acceptance probability, will converge towards the distribution of interest. However, MCMC suffers from biases which include the burn-in bias, related to the choice of the initalization, and a discretization bias assuming the proposal arises form a continuous process. These issues can cause challenges for scalability, to ensure an adequate acceptance probability. As a result, there has been a huge development of unbiased methods, focused on removing the burn-in bias. Most of them are based on coupling two Markov chains, where the bias is eliminated once they meet. A recently proposed methodology (by the applicant), entitled UBUBU, aimed to remove both forms of bias is an unbiased estimator exploiting the kinetic Langevin dynamics, combined with a variance reduction scheme. Given this combination, it is shown that both biases can be eliminated which avoid the requirement of the acceptance probability. This provides a key benefit, as with high-dimensional settings it is often cumbersome to balance the acceptance probability and the step-size. The variance reduction technique that is adopted is multilevel Monte Carlo. Numerical verification has demonstrated the improved efficiency of this approach, over (unbiased) MCMC methods. Despite the success of the aforementioned methods, there are limitations related to conducting unbiased estimation in more complex and challenging scenarios. Examples include sampling on confined spaces, and in a non-convex and high-dimensional setting, which are non-trivial tasks. This project will look to consider developments in this area through a combination of generalizing analytical results, developing new methodology and high-dimensional experiments, based on the methodology of UBUBU. Specifically, we will introduce a new algorithms aimed at sampling on confined domains. A careful construction is required related to the discretization scheme, and the coupling. We aim to derive error bounds and validate this numerically. We then aim to apply unbiased methods to diffusion models for generative modelling purposes. To do so, we require to construct a new stepsize stability analysis for reverse diffusion's, testing the effect of the bias and stepsize. This potentially can reduce computational time, which we will test on high-dimensional datasets. Finally we will extend the current analysis of those methods to more complex settings, that include a non-convex setting. 馬可夫鏈蒙地卡羅（MCMC）是一類用於從機率分佈中進行採樣的演算法，廣泛應用於金融、數值天氣預報和機器學習等實際領域。 MCMC 方法透過模擬馬可夫鏈來運作；該鏈利用「提議（proposal）」和「接受機率」機制，最終收斂於目標分佈。然而，MCMC 存在偏差問題，主要包括與初始狀態選擇相關的「預熱（burn-in）」偏差，以及假設提議源自連續過程時產生的離散化偏差。這些問題給確保足夠的接受機率以及演算法的可擴展性帶來了挑戰。 因此，旨在消除預熱偏差的無偏方法得到了長足發展。其中大多數方法是基於兩條馬可夫鏈的耦合（coupling），即一旦兩條鏈相遇，偏差便得以消除。申請人近期提出了一種名為 UBUBU 的方法，旨在同時消除上述兩種偏差；該方法是一種利用動力學朗之萬（kinetic Langevin）動力學並結合方差縮減方案的無偏估計器。研究表明，這種組合能夠消除兩種偏差，從而無需依賴接受機率。這項特性具有重要意義，因為在高維度場景下，平衡接受機率與步長往往十分困難。此方法採用的變異數縮減技術為多層蒙地卡羅（multilevel Monte Carlo）。數值驗證顯示，與現有的（無偏）MCMC 方法相比，此方法效率更高。 儘管上述方法取得了成功，但在更複雜、更具挑戰性的場景下進行無偏估計仍面臨限制。例如，在受限空間、非凸及高維度環境下的採樣，均屬於極具挑戰性的任務。本計畫將基於 UBUBU 方法，透過推廣分析結果、開發新方法以及開展高維度實驗，探索該領域的進一步發展。具體而言，我們將引入一種針對受限域採樣的新演算法，並需精心設計離散化方案與耦合機制。我們的目標是推導出誤差界並進行數值驗證。隨後，我們將把無偏方法應用於擴散模型，以實現生成式建模。為此，我們需要針對反向擴散過程建立新的步長穩定性分析，以評估偏差和步長對演算法的影響。該方法預計將縮短計算時間，我們將在高維資料集上對此進行測試。最後，我們將把針對這些方法的現有分析擴展到更複雜的情形，其中包括非凸情形。

21301326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21301326.value: 针对缺陷高对比介质中麦克斯韦特征值问题的定量数学分析及其应用

21301326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21301326.value: The confinement and control of electromagnetic waves at scales much smaller than their operating wavelength, known as the subwavelength regime, is a long-standing goal with profound implications for robust information transport, high-resolution imaging, and the design of complex optical devices. All-dielectric artificial materials, composed of high-refractive-index dielectric resonators, have emerged as a powerful platform for achieving this goal. These materials often incorporate compact defects or non-compact structural perturbations with specific symmetries into periodic configurations, enabling strong subwavelength wave localization or robust waveguiding with low energy loss that surpasses traditional physical limitations. Despite significant experimental progress, a rigorous mathematical theory remains absent. This project aims to mathematically uncover the underlying mechanisms of these extraordinary wave localization phenomena through spectral analysis of the Maxwell equations in complex structured high-contrast media. We consider three closely related yet complementary spectral problems of Maxwell operators. First, classical wave localization via compact defects in periodic bandgap structures is constrained by the diffraction limit, which requires defect sizes comparable to the wavelength, thereby limiting subwavelength applications. High-index dielectric materials have experimentally demonstrated the potential to overcome this limitation. We will mathematically prove that perturbing only a few resonators within the periodic configuration suffices to generate localized modes near defects, by exploiting their unique local resonant properties. Quantitative estimates for the associated resonances and localization lengths will be provided. Second, while localized modes from compact defects are relatively easy to create, they are sensitive to fabrication imperfections. We will investigate topologically protected modes, which are robust against disorder but require specific configurational symmetries. Specifically, we will establish the existence of double Dirac points, a special type of conical band singularity, for Maxwell equations in an experimentally realized configuration with super-honeycomb symmetry, and analyze their stability and topological properties under symmetry-breaking deformations. We will then explore the emergence of robust edge states localized at interfaces between two topologically distinct deformed high-index lattices. Finally, while infinitely extended lattice structures are commonly used for mathematical analysis, real physical media are necessarily finite. We will address this gap by rigorously analyzing how resonances of localized modes in infinite systems approximate those in defective finite structures. These results are expected to advance the mathematical analysis of exotic wave propagation in all-dielectric metamaterials, facilitate the development of numerical algorithms for computing subwavelength localized modes, and inspire further practical applications. 电磁波在远小于工作波长的尺度上实现局域与调控，即所谓亚波长调控，是波动科学中的长期目标，对稳健信息传输、高分辨成像及复杂光学器件设计具有重要意义。近年来，由高折射率介电谐振子构成的全介电人工材料为突破传统衍射极限提供了新的途径。通过在周期结构中引入局域缺陷，或施加具有特定对称性的非局域结构扰动，可以实现强亚波长局域以及低损耗、抗扰动的波导传输。然而，与快速发展的实验研究相比，对其背后数学机制的严格理解仍十分有限。本项目拟以复杂结构高对比介质中的 麦克斯韦方程为基础，通过谱理论与渐近分析，系统研究上述异常电磁波局域现象的数学机制。项目主要研究三个相互关联的 麦克斯韦谱问题。首先，针对周期带隙结构中的缺陷局域模，传统机制受衍射极限制约，通常要求缺陷尺度与波长相当。我们将利用高折射率介电谐振子的局域共振特性，证明仅扰动周期结构中的少量谐振子即可产生亚波长缺陷局域模，并建立相应共振频率及局域长度的定量估计。其次，针对普通缺陷模对制造误差较为敏感的问题，我们将研究具有拓扑保护性质的稳健局域态。具体而言，将在具有超蜂窝对称性的实验结构中严格证明 麦克斯韦谱的双狄拉克点存在性，分析其在对称性破缺形变下的稳定性与拓扑性质，并进一步研究两个拓扑不同的高折射率晶格界面上稳健边缘态的产生机制。最后，针对理论上常用无限周期结构而实际器件必为有限尺寸这一差距，我们将研究无限体系中的局域模共振如何定量逼近有限缺陷结构中的共振，从而建立无限介质模型与有限器件之间的严格联系。

21303526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21303526.value: 利用新型非線性光學效應實現高效量子調控

21303526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21303526.value: Light-matter interaction lies at the heart of many modern technologies, such as lasers and solar cells, which have profoundly shaped our daily lives. Building on this foundation, nonlinear optical (NLO) effects, which occur when intense light interacts with matter in a non-proportional way, have emerged as a powerful tool for achieving precise control over quantum systems. Quantum control technologies based on NLO effects offer unique advantages – they are ultrafast, highly precise, and non-contact. These capabilities hold great promise for driving transformative advances in diverse fields, including information processing, sensing, and energy technologies. Despite their promise, quantum control strategies based on NLO effects face some challenges. First, the exploration of novel and unconventional NLO phenomena is still in its infancy. Once established, these exotic NLO effects would enable advanced quantum technologies, such as the highly sought-after optical control of nuclear spins for integrated quantum systems. Second, the typically weak magnitude of certain NLO responses limits their practical applications. However, researchers from different fields often focus on distinct aspects of NLO effects, highlighting the need for a more unified theoretical framework that could integrate diverse perspectives and stimulate novel breakthroughs. In this regard, this project aims to develop and harness novel NLO effects for more robust and versatile quantum control. Our approach is to take advantage of the interaction between electrons and phonons (i.e., atomic vibrations) to design and amplify unconventional NLO effects. This electron-phonon interaction is ubiquitous in materials, but it is often treated as a nuisance. We, however, view it as a critical resource. To unlock this potential, we will first develop new computational frameworks to incorporate electron-phonon coupling in the calculation of NLO responses (Task 1). Using this tool, we will explore novel NLO effects involving phonons, especially how they can enable efficient optical control of nuclear spins (Task 2). We will also explore how electron-phonon coupling can be utilized to enhance the magnitude of NLO responses. This can be especially useful in materials with high spatial symmetry, such as silicon (Task 3). This project will deliver a fundamental advance in understanding and predicting novel phonon-driven NLO responses. Beyond the timeline of this project, the computational frameworks developed here can be generalized to incorporate other interactions, enabling the discovery of further novel optical phenomena. Ultimately, this work paves the way for next-generation quantum technologies, with applications spanning high-tech industries and broader society. 光與物質的相互作用是許多現代科技（例如激光和太陽能電池）的核心機理，這些科技深刻地改變了我們的日常生活。在此基礎上，非線性光學效應（即強光與物質相互作用時所發生的現象）已成為對量子系統進行精確調控的強大工具。基於非線性光學效應的量子調控技術具備超快、高精度和非接觸等獨特優勢，因而極具潛力，有望推動資訊處理、感測和能源科技等多個領域的革命性突破。 儘管前景廣闊，基於非線性光學效應的量子調控策略仍面臨諸多挑戰。首先，對新型、非常規的非線性光學現象的探索仍處於起步階段。這些特殊的非線性光學效應一旦被建立起來，將能賦能先進的量子科技，例如在整合量子系統中扮演重要角色的核自旋光學調控。其次，非線性光學響應通常較為微弱，這限制了它們的實際應用。然而，來自不同領域的研究人員往往只關注非線性光學效應的特定面向，這凸顯了建立一個更統一的理論框架，以融合不同視角並激發新突破的必要性。 為此，本計畫旨在開發並利用新型非線性光學效應，以實現更具穩健性與通用性的量子調控。我們的方法是利用電子與聲子（即原子振動）之間的相互作用，來設計並放大非常規的非線性光學效應。這種電-聲耦合相互作用在材料中無所不在，但往往被視為噪音的來源。然而，我們將其視為一種關鍵資源。為了釋放这一潛力，我們將首先開發新的計算框架，將電-聲耦合納入非線性光學響應的計算中（任務 1）。利用这一工具，我們將探索涉及聲子的新型非線性光學效應，特別是探討如何利用它們作為媒介，以實現對核自旋的高效光學調控（任務 2）。我們亦將探索如何利用電-聲耦合來增強非線性光學響應的強度，這在具有高對稱性的材料（如矽）中將尤為有效（任務 3）。 本計畫將在理解與預測新型聲子驅動的非線性光學響應方面取得基礎性進展。在本計畫週期之外，此處所開發的計算框架還可推廣、應用於其他相互作用，進而推動更多新型光學現象的發現。最終，這項工作將為下一世代的量子科技鋪平道路，其應用將涵蓋高科技產業及更廣泛的社會層面。

21306326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21306326.value: 寬溫域電解液設計：透過陽離子-陰離子溶劑化工程提升高比能電池性能

21306326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21306326.value: The development of wide-temperature electrolytes is essential for advancing high-energy batteries capable of reliable operation in both cold and hot environments. Despite lithium metal’s ultrahigh theoretical capacity, its practical application is hindered by electrolyte limitations, including sluggish ion transport, high desolvation energy, and unstable solid–electrolyte interphases (SEI/CEI) that lead to rapid degradation under extreme conditions. Building upon our recent studies on cation–anion solvation engineering, this project seeks to further address these challenges by designing and optimizing solvents with moderate binding energy and lithium salts containing borate-based anions that enable stable electrochemical performance across a broad temperature range. Specifically, this project will focus on three key tasks: (1) developing and screening a new family of borate-based lithium salts paired with selected solvents to tailor cation–anion coordination and reduce Li+ binding energy; (2) elucidating the interfacial chemistry and ion transport mechanisms via advanced characterization techniques and DFT, establishing relationships among solvation structure, interphase composition, and battery performance; and (3) applying the optimized electrolytes in Li metal pouch cells, targeting a high specific energy density of over 500 Wh/kg, a cycle life exceeding 500 cycles, fast charging (10–80 % SOC within 15 min), and stable operation from -40°C to +60°C. Preliminary studies have demonstrated that ternary borate-based electrolytes with regulated cation–anion solvation structures can form dense, inorganic-rich CEI layers and sustain high-voltage operation (4.6 V) over 450 cycles and robust performance across wide temperature ranges (from -35°C to +45°C). Building on this foundation, the proposed project will establish new electrolyte design principles based on cation–anion solvation regulation, paving the way for next-generation lithium metal batteries with wide-temperature capability, high energy density, and enhanced safety. 要發展出喺嚴寒同酷熱環境下都可靠運作嘅高比能電池，研發寬溫度電解液係不可或缺嘅一環。雖然鋰金屬擁有極高嘅理論電容量，但實際應用受阻於電解液嘅局限，例如離子傳輸慢、去溶劑化能高，以及固態電解質界面（SEI/CEI）唔穩定，令電池喺極端溫度下好快衰減。在我哋近來對陽離子－陰離子溶劑化工程嘅研究基礎上，呢個項目會進一步應對上述難題，重點係設計同優化一啲具有適中結合能嘅溶劑，同埋含有硼酸根基團嘅鋰鹽，從而以達致喺寬闊溫度範圍內都有穩定嘅電化學表現。項目會聚焦三大任務：（1）開發同篩選一系列新型硼酸基鋰鹽，配合特定溶劑，調控陽離子－陰離子嘅配位作用，並降低鋰離子嘅結合能；（2）利用先進嘅表徵技術同DFT計算，釐清界面化學同離子傳輸機制，建立溶劑化結構、界面成分同電池性能之間嘅關聯；（3）將優化後嘅電解液應用於鋰金屬軟包電池，目標係實現超過500 Wh/kg嘅高比能量、超過500次嘅循環壽命、快速充電（15分鐘內由10%充到80%電量），以及喺-40°C至+60°C範圍內穩定運作。前期研究已經顯示，透過調控陽離子－陰離子溶劑化結構嘅三元硼酸基電解液，能夠形成緻密、富含無機物嘅CEI層，並且喺高電壓（4.6 V）下維持超過450次循環，仲有喺寬溫度範圍（-35°C至+45°C）內表現強韌。基於呢個基礎，本項目將會建立一套以陽離子－陰離子溶劑化調控為核心嘅電解液設計新原則，為下一代具備寬溫度適應力、高能量密度同更高安全性嘅鋰金屬電池鋪路。

21308126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21308126.value: 再生核希爾伯特空間中對抗訓練的統計性質

21308126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21308126.value: While machine learning models and artificial intelligence systems have grown increasingly powerful, researchers have observed that even small perturbations in input data can lead to significantly unreliable outputs. To address this issue, adversarial training has been proposed as a method to improve the model robustness by optimizing the worst-case loss under bounded input perturbations. While extensive research has focused on adversarially trained parametric models, adversarial training in nonparametric models, which are capable of capturing more complex data structures, has not been well understood. This project aims to investigate adversarially trained nonparametric models within the framework of Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RKHS). The resulting problem is a min-max optimization problem, which can be considered as a new statistical estimation problem within the RKHS framework. The research question is to analyze the statistical properties of the associated estimates. The first task is to characterize the asymptotic behavior of the adversarially trained RKHS estimates, based on which the statistical inferences can be developed accordingly. The second task will focus on the finite-sample convergence rate of the generalization error of the estimates and evaluate the conditions for which the statistical optimality can be proven. To facilitate more efficient applications of the nonparametric adversarial training, possible improvements will be explored to strike a tunable balance between the adversarial robustness and estimation accuracy in the RKHS. Finally, to make our analysis applicable for broader topics, extension to more general robust optimization will be considered. By delivering the tasks mentioned above, both the asymptotic and non-asymptotic behavior of adversarial training estimates in the RKHS will be characterized. Then, the bias induced by adversarial robustness can be analytically evaluated through asymptotic analysis. Also, the finite-sample analysis helps us identify the conditions under which the estimates can be statistically optimal, i.e., the accuracy is not sacrificed for robustness. Together with explorations of the trade-off techniques, these insights contribute to a deeper depiction and solution of the central challenge in adversarial training—the trade-off between adversarial robustness and estimation accuracy—in the RKHS scheme. The main challenge in this project lies in analyzing the new framework of the RKHS-based min-max optimization problem. The challenges can be addressed by bridging the work on parametric min-max optimization problems, including the P.I.'s previous research, and the classical RKHS-based empirical risk minimization framework. 隨著機器學習模型和人工智能系統能力的不斷提升，研究者也發現，即使輸入數據受到很小的擾動，也可能導致模型輸出出現明顯的不穩定甚至失真。為解決這一問題，對抗訓練通過在有界輸入擾動下優化最壞情形損失，提高模型的魯棒性。現有研究主要集中於參數模型，而對於能夠刻畫更複雜數據結構的非參數模型，對抗訓練的統計性質仍缺乏系統研究。本項目擬在再生核希爾伯特空間框架下研究非參數模型的對抗訓練問題。由此得到的估計問題具有極小極大優化結構，可以看作再生核希爾伯特空間框架下一類新的統計估計問題。本項目將重點研究相應估計量的統計性質：首先刻畫對抗訓練估計量的漸近行為，並在此基礎上研究相關的統計推斷問題；其次分析估計量泛化誤差的有限樣本收斂速度，並考察其達到統計最優性的條件；同時，為提高非參數對抗訓練的實際適用性，進一步探索能夠在對抗魯棒性與估計精度之間實現可調節權衡的改進方法；最後，將相關分析推廣到更一般的魯棒優化問題。通過上述研究，本項目希望從漸近和非漸近兩個方面系統刻畫再生核希爾伯特空間中對抗訓練估計量的統計行為，其中漸近分析可用於評估對抗魯棒性所引入的偏差，有限樣本分析則有助於識別估計量能夠達到統計最優性的條件，即在提高魯棒性的同時盡可能避免估計精度的損失。結合對魯棒性與精度權衡方法的研究，本項目將進一步理解和改善對抗訓練中的核心問題，即對抗魯棒性與估計精度之間的權衡。項目的主要難點在於再生核希爾伯特空間下這一新型極小極大優化問題的理論分析，我們將嘗試連接參數模型中極小極大優化問題的已有理論，包括項目負責人此前的相關研究，與經典再生核希爾伯特空間經驗風險最小化理論，從而建立適用於非參數對抗訓練的統計分析方法。

21309026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21309026.value: 手性低維/三維鈣鈦礦異質結構耦合及其自旋光電應用

21309026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21309026.value: Spin-optoelectronics, which exploit the spin degree of freedom in addition to charge, offer transformative advantages including ultrafast response, nonvolatile memory retention, and reduced power consumption. Chiral metal halide perovskites have recently emerged as promising candidates for spin-optoelectronic devices, where spin transport is facilitated by the combined effects of molecular chirality and strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC), primarily driven by the distortion of inorganic lattices. However, purely chiral low-dimensional (low-D) perovskites exhibit low conductivity and short spin coherence, while 3D perovskites, though highly conductive, lack inversion asymmetry for efficient spin polarization. To overcome these trade-offs, this project proposes coherent chiral low-D/3D perovskite heterostructures that integrate the spin-filtering ability of chiral perovskites with the transport efficiency of 3D lattices. Such coherent coupling is promising for surpassing the limitations of isolated chiral low-D or 3D systems by achieving long spin transport lifetimes and large spin polarization at ambient conditions. We will first design and synthesize coherent chiral low-D/3D perovskite heterostructures through a ligand diffusion-driven growth strategy, considering lattice matching, 3D component ligand diffusion, as well as nucleation control. The heterostructure will be characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD), Grazing-Incident Wide-Angle X-Ray Scattering (GIWAXS), and Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) to confirm lattice coherence and extract structural chiral metrics. Then, we will characterize the chirality penetration depth from chiral low-D to 3D perovskite using circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) spectroscopy. Spin-dependent transport will also be quantitatively analyzed using magnetic conductive (mc)-AFM, and helicity-resolved photocurrent, while ultrafast circularly polarized light pump–probe experiments will probe transient spin dynamics. First-principles calculations will link structural chirality metrics with experimental spin polarization and lifetime, providing a predictive framework for optimizing SOC. Ultimately, this study will enable the rational design of next-generation spin-optoelectronic devices, such as circular photogalvanic effect (CPGE)-based photodetectors and circularly polarized (CP)-LEDs, advancing perovskite-based spintronics toward room-temperature energy-efficient devices. The proposed work will establish a new paradigm in coherently coupled chiral heterostructures, providing both a synthesis strategy and a mechanistic model linking structural chirality, SOC, and spin dynamics. Beyond advancing fundamental understanding, this project is expected to unlock applications in future spin-optoelectronic development. 自旋光電子學（spin-optoelectronics）在電荷自由度之外進一步利用電子自旋，具有超快響應、非易失資訊儲存及低功耗等潛在優勢。手性金屬鹵化物鈣鈦礦因結構反演對稱性破缺與強自旋－軌道耦合（spin–orbit coupling, SOC）的協同作用，可產生顯著的自旋選擇性，近年成為自旋光電材料的重要候選體系。然而，手性低維鈣鈦礦通常受限於較低的載流子傳輸效率，而三維鈣鈦礦雖具有優異的電荷傳輸能力，卻缺乏足夠的結構不對稱性以實現高效自旋極化。針對此關鍵取捨，本計畫提出構築手性低維／三維鈣鈦礦異質結構，通過異質界面耦合整合低維手性晶格的自旋選擇性與三維鈣鈦礦的高效載流子傳輸，探索在室溫下實現高自旋極化與長壽命自旋傳輸的新途徑。 本計畫首先採用配體擴散驅動的生長策略，結合晶格匹配、配體擴散與成核調控，構築連續手性低維／三維鈣鈦礦異質結構。利用X射線繞射（XRD）、掠入射廣角X射線散射（GIWAXS）及穿透式電子顯微鏡（TEM）解析晶格連續性、界面結構及晶格畸變；進一步結合圓二色性（CD）與圓偏振發光（CPL）光譜，解析手性由低維層向三維晶格的傳遞與空間延伸。隨後，利用磁導電原子力顯微鏡（mc-AFM）及螺旋度解析光電流定量評估自旋選擇性傳輸，並結合超快圓偏振泵浦－探測光譜揭示自旋產生、傳輸與弛豫動力學。第一原理計算將進一步建立分子構型、界面堆積、晶格畸變、SOC與自旋輸運之間的定量關聯，形成可指導異質結構優化的結構－自旋關係。 本計畫預期建立連續手性低維／三維鈣鈦礦異質結構耦合調控自旋輸運的新策略，揭示結構手性、界面耦合與SOC共同調控自旋選擇性傳輸的物理機制，並以圓偏振敏感光偵測器、圓偏振發光二極體等原型器件驗證其自旋光電功能。研究成果將為突破手性低維鈣鈦礦中自旋選擇性與電荷傳輸之間的性能取捨提供新的材料設計原理，並為室溫、低功耗鈣鈦礦自旋光電元件的發展奠定科學基礎。

21311426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21311426.value: 面向高耐久質子交換膜水電解的低銥析氧催化劑降解路徑與穩定化策略研究

21311426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21311426.value: The development of proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) technology holds strategic importance for the global transition toward a carbon-neutral future, and significantly contributes to decarbonizing various sectors while creating new economic opportunities in the Hong Kong’s emerging green technology market. To date, the large-scale deployment of PEMWE is critically constrained by its dependence on scarce and expensive noble metal iridium. Current research focuses on developing catalysts with reduced iridium loadings, but these materials typically fail to simultaneously achieve high activity and adequate stability in the anodic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in acidic environments. While the recently discovered oxygen coupling mechanism (OPM) offers a promising path to overcome the limitations of conventional adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) and lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM), its practical implementation in OER faces a critical challenge: the OPM-following catalysts experience gradual performance decay during long-term operation. The fundamental origins of this instability, particularly the potential degradation pathways, remain poorly understood, hindering the rational design of durable low-iridium OER catalysts. Our preliminary research has established a robust platform to address these challenges. We have successfully synthesized a model catalyst featuring atomically dispersed iridium on a manganese oxide support, creating well-defined paired active sites facilitating the OPM pathway. Critically, we have also observed preliminary evidence of performance degradation through transformation from OPM to LOM pathway in less stable catalyst configuration, providing a unique opportunity to systematically elucidate the degradation pathways and stabilization strategies of low-iridium OER catalysts. Based on these preliminary data, this project aims to fundamentally understand and ultimately suppress the degradation of low-iridium OER catalysts through an integrated research approach. First, we will employ controlled synthesis to create catalysts with tunable active-site structures, establishing precise relationships between atomic configuration and OER stability. Second, we will combine isotope-labelled mass spectrometry with operando spectroscopy to identify the OER mechanism and capture its evolution during degradation. Third, we will utilize in-situ elemental analysis and microscopic techniques to track active site dissolution and structural changes, elucidating the structural triggers for the degradation. Finally, the fundamental insights gained will guide the development of stabilization strategies, with the optimized catalysts being demonstrated in practical PEMWE devices.
