This project will provide fundamental insights into the stability limitations for OER electrocatalysts at the atomic scale. The findings will establish essential theoretical foundations for designing durable low-iridium catalysts, ultimately supporting the advancement of cost-effective green hydrogen production technology in Hong Kong. 質子交換膜水電解（PEMWE）是綠氫製備的重要技術，但其大規模應用受制於陽極析氧反應對稀缺貴金屬銥的高度依賴。低銥催化劑雖可降低成本，卻往往難以兼顧高活性與長期穩定性。新近提出的氧耦合機制（OPM）為突破傳統反應機制的性能限制提供了新方向，但其催化劑在長期運行中的衰減機制仍缺乏深入理解。 本項目將構築具有明確 Ir-O-Mn 活性位點的低銥催化劑，結合同位素標記、原位光譜及結構分析，揭示 OPM 催化劑的反應機制、降解路徑及關鍵結構因素，並據此提出針對性的穩定化策略。所開發的高性能催化劑將進一步在 PEMWE 器件中進行驗證。 本研究預期建立 OPM 催化劑活性與穩定性的原子尺度設計原則，為開發高效、耐久及低銥用量的 PEMWE 催化劑提供理論基礎和技術支持，並推動低成本綠氫技術的發展。

21312926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21312926.value: 面向二元优化的原始-对偶算法与理论

21312926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21312926.value: Binary optimization, where variables take 0-1 values, is central to network design, scheduling, circuit layout, and machine learning. However, existing solvers face a persistent trade-off. Exact methods provide guarantees yet scale poorly, while heuristics scale but lack certificates. Our recent work shows that many unconstrained binary optimization problems admit a principled primal‑dual minimax reformulation. We then developed a simultaneous gradient descent-ascent (GDA) scheme that converges in linear time to epsilon-binary solutions. This approach is well-suited for GPU deployment, achieving state-of-the-art quality within seconds on benchmarks including Max-Cut, Max-SAT, and Maximum Independent Set with up to 50,000 variables. This project develops the mathematical foundations and scalable algorithms for a gap-certified framework for constrained binary optimization. We will extend the primal-dual formulation and GDA method to handle convex constraints, including budgets, norm bounds, and semidefinite structures. This is achieved via a semi-boxed Lagrangian formulation whose dual variables evolve to enforce both feasibility and integrality. We will derive tight dual lower bounds by combining diagonal shifting (to convexify objectives) with convex envelopes. By analyzing when each approach dominates, we will provide strong certified optimality gaps. We will also convert the resulting primal-dual structure into effective cut families that integrate with branch-and-cut algorithms, yielding exact or epsilon-optimal solutions. Our theoretical agenda includes iteration complexity guarantees for reaching near-feasible, near-binary points by GDA. We will also establish structural dominance conditions determining when each bounding technique provides the tightest bounds. Finally, we will develop cut generation policies that combine concavity cuts with integrality cuts through parallel computation to ensure measurable gap decay in branch-and-cut. The project will deliver significant advances in both theory and practice. We will establish a unified primal-dual scheme for constrained binary optimization, provide rigorous analysis of hybrid bounding techniques with provable dominance regimes, and develop concavification-based cutting planes that accelerate branch-and-cut algorithms. Our GPU-accelerated solver will return high-quality solutions together with certified optimality gaps on instances far beyond the reach of classical exact methods, while retaining branch-and-cut integration for applications requiring exact solutions. These tools will enable faster, trustworthy optimization for large-scale discrete modeling, with theoretical guarantees appropriate for scientific and industrial deployment. By blending continuous optimization, combinatorial structure, and modern hardware, this project aims to make reliable large-scale binary optimization both mathematically rigorous and practically accessible.

21313926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21313926.value: 透過世界線有效場論與格林函數方法研究非線性黑洞微擾：潮汐Love數與振鈴尾部

21313926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21313926.value: Black holes and gravitational waves now offer precision tests of strong-field gravity. This proposal targets two nonlinear regimes of black-hole perturbations that directly impact gravitational-wave (GW) science: (i) nonlinear tidal responses during inspiral, and (ii) nonlinear late-time tails in ringdown. On the inspiral side, we apply the gauge invariant worldline effective field theory (EFT) for compact objects that systematically organizes higher-order tidal interactions. Building on recent evidence for vanishing quadratic Love numbers and infinitely many vanishing even sector Love numbers, we will test the conjecture that all static nonlinear tidal Love numbers of four-dimensional black holes in general relativity vanish, including mixed electric–magnetic sectors. Our strategy solves the stationary, axisymmetric vacuum Einstein equations in Weyl–Lewis–Papapetrou form (encapsulated by the Ernst equation and its SL(2,R)/SO(2) sigma-model structure) for a Kerr black hole tidally deformed by distant matter, enforces horizon regularity and global charge conservation, and matches the large-distance solution to worldline operators. The resulting Wilson coefficients yield clear yes/no diagnostics for nonlinear Love numbers and feed directly into two-to-two scattering amplitudes to derive post-Minkowskian two-body potentials and waveform corrections. On the ringdown side, we analyze late time nonlinear tails in Kerr using the Teukolsky formalism. The nonlinear Teukolsky equation is analyzed using a perturbative expansion in general relativity. By studying the small-s (small frequency) structure of Green-function/source products in Laplace (Fourier) space, we will predict power-law exponents and amplitudes of the late time tails due to mode couplings, then validate them with targeted time-domain evolutions of the nonlinear sourced Teukolsky equation. Together, these efforts deliver a unified treatment of nonlinear black-hole dynamics—quantifying whether (and how) nonlinear tides modify inspiral waveforms and whether spin reshapes nonlinear ringdown tails. The outcomes will sharpen GW templates for next-generation detectors (LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA, ET, CE, LISA, TaiJi, Tianjin) and provide robust null tests that distinguish black holes from other compact objects, while training students in EFT, perturbation theory, and numerical relativity. 黑洞與重力波（gravitational waves）現已為強場重力提供精密的檢驗。本計劃針對黑洞微擾中直接影響重力波科學的兩個非線性領域：（i）旋進（inspiral）階段的非線性潮汐響應，以及（ii）振鈴（ringdown）階段的非線性後期尾部（late-time tails）。在旋進方面，我們應用針對致密天體的規範不變世界線有效場論（gauge invariant worldline effective field theory, EFT），系統性地整理高階潮汐相互作用。基於近期關於二階 Love 數（quadratic Love numbers）以及無窮多個偶數區塊（even sector）Love 數為零的證據，我們將測試以下猜想：在廣義相對論中，四維黑洞的所有靜態非線性潮汐 Love 數（static nonlinear tidal Love numbers）皆為零，包括電-磁混合區塊（mixed electric–magnetic sectors）。我們的策略是針對受到遠方物質潮汐形變的 Kerr 黑洞，求解以 Weyl–Lewis–Papapetrou 形式（由 Ernst 方程及其 SL(2, R)/SO(2) sigma-模型結構所封裝）呈現的穩態軸對稱真空愛因斯坦方程，並強制執行事件視界正規性（horizon regularity）與全域荷守恆（global charge conservation），最後將遠距離解與世界線算子（worldline operators）進行匹配。由此得到的 Wilson 係數為非線性 Love 數提供了明確的「是/否」判斷依據，並可直接輸入至二對二散射振幅（two-to-two scattering amplitudes）中，以推導出後閔考夫斯基（post-Minkowskian）二體位能與波形修正。在振鈴方面，我們利用 Teukolsky 形式體系（Teukolsky formalism）分析 Kerr 黑洞的後期非線性尾部。我們透過廣義相對論中的微擾展開法來分析非線性 Teukolsky 方程。藉由研究Laplace（Fourier）空間中格林函數與源項乘積（Green-function/source products）的小頻率結構，我們將預測由模式耦合（mode couplings）引起的後期尾部的冪律指數（power-law exponents）與振幅，接著透過具源項非線性 Teukolsky 方程的針對性時域演化（time-domain evolutions）來進行驗證。綜合這些努力，本計劃對非線性黑洞動力學提出了統一的處理方法——定量評估非線性潮汐是否（以及如何）修正旋進波形，以及自旋是否會重塑非線性振鈴尾部。本研究成果將提升下一代探測器（LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA、ET、CE、LISA）的重力波模板精度，並提供強韌的零測試（null tests），用以區分黑洞與其他致密天體，同時培育學生在有效場論（EFT）、微擾理論及數值相對論方面的專業能力。

21502826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21502826.value: 耐心资本的影响力：来自风险投资的证据

21502826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21502826.value: Patient capital is essential for breakthrough innovation, yet little is known about the origin of such patience in venture capital (VC). We examine whether long-horizon limited partners (LPs) induce general partners (GPs) to adopt more patient investment strategies and the impact on portfolio company outcomes. Our setting exploits a 2014 reform in China that allowed insurers---canonical long-term investors---to invest in RMB-denominated VC funds, while USD-denominated funds managed by the same GPs remained unaffected. Using a within-GP difference-in-differences design, we show that insurer entry crowds out shorter-horizon investors such as individuals. This investor base change shifted RMB funds toward earlier-stage investments and lengthened holding periods, with positive impact on portfolio company exits and innovation. These effects are not driven by a pure capital supply effect or unobserved market conditions. Complementary survey experiments with Chinese GPs reveal that managers explicitly adjust strategies in response to LP horizon, shedding light on the mechanisms of transmission. Together, the results demonstrate that patient capital from LP investors can pass through intermediation frictions to reshape VC behavior, highlighting how investor composition shapes the patience of delegated asset management. 耐心资本对突破性创新至关重要，但风险投资（VC）中这种“耐心”的源头尚不明确。 本研究探讨长期限有限合伙人（LP）是否会促使普通合伙人（GP）采取更有耐心的投资策略，以及这一转变对被投企业绩效的影响。 本研究利用中国2014年的一项政策改革作为准自然实验。该改革允许保险资金（典型的长期投资者）投资人民币风险投资基金，而同一GP管理的美元基金则不受影响。基于GP内部的双重差分（Within-GP Difference-in-Differences）设计，研究发现保险资金的进入挤出了个人投资者等较短期限的资金来源。这种投资者结构的改变促使人民币基金转向更早期的投资并延长了持股周期，同时对被投企业的退出成果与创新能力产生了积极影响。上述效应并非由单纯的资本供给效应或不可观测的市场环境所驱动。 结合针对中国GP的补充性问卷实验，研究进一步揭示基金管理者会根据LP的资金期限明确调整其投资策略，从而阐明了耐心的传递机制。综合而言，研究结果表明来自LP的耐心资本能够穿透中介摩擦，重新塑造VC的投资行为，阐明了投资者结构对委托资产管理“耐心程度”的塑造作用。

21505226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21505226.value: Dark pools have become an integral component of modern capital markets, accounting for a substantial share of trading volume. While the lack of pre-trade transparency allows investors to conceal trading intentions from the market, dark pool operators retain privileged access to order flow information. As many dark pools are operated by financial institutions that also manage investment funds, concerns have emerged that affiliated funds may exploit this information for trading advantages, undermining the fairness and integrity of capital markets. This study aims to investigate whether funds affiliated with dark pool operators utilize order flow information to improve their trading performance. By uncovering this underexplored channel of information leakage and exploitation, this study would inform the regulatory oversight of dark pools and promote stronger safeguards for confidential trading information. 暗池已成为现代资本市场的重要组成部分，在市场交易量中占据相当大的比重。尽管交易前信息的不透明性使投资者能够向市场隐藏其交易意图，暗池运营商却可以优先获取订单流信息。由于许多暗池由同时管理投资基金的金融机构运营，人们担忧其关联基金可能利用这些信息获取交易优势，从而损害资本市场的公平性与完整性。本研究旨在考察暗池运营商的关联基金是否利用订单流信息提升其交易表现。通过揭示这一尚未得到充分研究的信息泄露与利用渠道，本研究将为暗池监管提供参考，并推动加强对机密交易信息的保护。

21505526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21505526.value: The past two decades have seen a substantial growth in index mutual funds and exchange-traded funds (ETFs), which accounted for 51% of the assets in the fund markets by 2024. These funds typically employ passive investing strategies to replicate certain indices. Investors in these funds tend to buy and hold, rather than engaging in frequent trading. The structural shift toward the rising dominance of passive investing in financial markets presents two offsetting effects on firms' investment decisions. On the one hand, passive ownership can be considered as a potential source of stable capital supply, incentivizing firm investment. On the other hand, information from financial markets feeds back into firms' investment decision-making. A high level of passive ownership reduces the responsiveness of prices to information, which may lead to less efficient investment. This project develops a theoretical model to study the implications of these offsetting channels for firm investment and to characterize the optimal level of passive ownership. Specifically, we develop a multi-period noisy rational expectations equilibrium model, building on Grossman and Stiglitz (1980). Our model features two investor types: passive investors, who maintain a buy-and-hold portfolio, and active investors, who trade on new information. Furthermore, we endogenize firm investment, allowing the firm's initial investment and future investment adjustments to depend on its level of passive ownership and feedback from financial markets. The model jointly determines the equilibrium proportion of passive investors and the firm's investment choice. We further test the empirical implications of the model in the context of U.S. monetary policy. This project aims to provide a theoretical framework for understanding the consequences of the two offsetting effects of passive ownership on firms' real decisions. Our findings will clarify how firms make decisions in modern financial markets and provide crucial insights for policymakers evaluating the real impact of ETFs and other passive investment vehicles. 過去二十年來，指數型共同基金(index mutual funds)和交易所交易基金(ETFs)出現了顯著增長，截至2024年，這兩類基金已佔基金市場資產的51%. 這些基金通常採用被動投資策略，以複製某些指數。此類基金的投資者傾向於買入並持有，而非頻繁交易。金融市場中被動投資日益主導地位的結構性轉變，對企業的投資決策產生了兩種相互抵銷的影響。一方面，被動所有權可被視為穩定資本供給的潛在來源，從而激勵企業投資。另一方面，金融市場的資訊會反饋至企業的投資決策中。被動所有權比例過高會降低價格對資訊的反應程度，進而可能導致投資效率降低。本計畫建構一個理論模型，以研究這些相互抵銷的管道對企業投資的影響，並刻畫被動所有權的最適水準。具體而言，我們以Grossman and Stiglitz (1980)為基礎，建立一個多期雜訊理性預期均衡模型。我們的模型包含兩類投資者：被動投資者，其維持買入並持有的投資組合；以及主動投資者，其依據新資訊進行交易。此外，我們內生化企業投資，允許企業的初始投資與未來投資調整取決於其被動所有權水準及金融市場的反饋效應。該模型同時決定被動投資者的均衡比例與企業的投資選擇。我們進一步在美國貨幣政策的背景下，檢驗該模型的實證意涵。本計畫旨在提供一個理論框架，以理解被動所有權的兩種相互抵銷效應對企業實質決策的影響。我們的研究結果將闡明企業在現代金融市場中如何做出決策，並為政策制定者在評估ETFs及其他被動投資工具的真實影響時，提供關鍵性的見解。

21508126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21508126.value: 人類訓練機器而機器創作藝術：重構生成式 AI 時代的版權機制

21508126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21508126.value: The rapid rise of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has transformed creative production, giving rise to a new form of human–AI co-creation in which human creators rely on AI tools to enhance creativity, while AI models depend on vast repositories of human-generated content for training. This reciprocal relationship challenges the foundations of copyright law, raising two interdependent policy questions: whether AI-generated content should qualify for copyright protection (output regulation) and whether copyrighted human works may be lawfully used to train AI models (input regulation). Although these two debates have been widely discussed in legal and policy circles, existing research largely examines them in isolation, overlooking their dynamic interaction and the resulting welfare implications for creators, AI developers, and consumers. This project aim to fill this critical gap by developing a dynamic game-theoretical framework that integrates the input and output dimensions of AI copyright regulation into a unified analytical model. The model captures the strategic interactions among three key stakeholders—a GenAI platform, human creators, and consumers—within an evolving creative ecosystem. Specifically, the study investigates how granting copyright to AI-generated content influences the optimal level of restriction or compensation for using copyrighted human materials as training data, and vice versa. The framework aims to further identify welfare-maximizing policy combinations that balance human creative effort, AI technological progress, and social welfare. Methodologically, the project models the creative economy as an N-period dynamic game. In each period, the GenAI platform sets a training data price, creators decide their creative effort and data-sharing proportion, and consumers choose between human- and AI-generated content based on perceived quality and authenticity. The equilibrium outcomes under four policy regimes—ranging from full openness to full restriction—are compared in terms of human effort, model quality, and total welfare. The findings will offer both theoretical and policy contributions. Theoretically, the project extends classic copyright economics by incorporating the co-creative nature of GenAI and the feedback loop between input and output regulation. Practically, it provides timely policy guidance for jurisdictions such as Hong Kong, which currently adopts an AI-friendly regime allowing unrestricted training data use while granting copyright to AI outputs. By identifying the optimal balance between innovation and fairness, this research informs sustainable policy design for the global AI-driven creative economy. 生成式人工智能（GenAI）的迅速崛起改變了創意生產模式，衍生出新型的「人機共創」形態：人類創作者依賴 AI 工具提升創造力，而 AI 模型則依賴大量人類創作的內容進行訓練。這種互惠關係對版權法的根基提出了挑戰，並引申出兩個相互關聯的政策問題：AI 生成的內容是否應獲得版權保護，以及使用受版權保護的人類作品訓練 AI 模型是否合法。儘管這兩大爭議在法律與政策領域已被廣泛討論，但現有研究多將其孤立看待，忽視了兩者之間的動態互動及其對創作者、AI 開發者與消費者帶來的福利影響。 本項目旨在填補這一關鍵空白。通過構建一個動態宏觀博弈論框架，本項目將 AI 版權規管的輸入與輸出維度整合至統一的分析模型中，以捕捉生成式 AI 平台、人類創作者與消費者這三大關鍵利益相關者在演進中的創意生態系統內的策略互動。具體而言，本研究探討向 AI 生成內容授予版權將如何影響使用人類版權材料作為訓練數據的最佳限制或補償水平，反之亦然。該框架旨在進一步找出能夠平衡人類創作努力、AI 技術進步與社會整體福利的最佳宏觀政策組合。 在研究方法上，本項目將創意經濟建模為一個N期的動態博弈。在每一期中，生成式 AI 平台設定訓練數據價格，創作者決定其創作投入與數據共享比例，而消費者則根據感知質量與真實性在人類創作與 AI 生成內容之間做出選擇。本研究將對比從「完全開放」到「完全限制」等四種政策機制下的均衡結果，評估指標涵蓋人類創作投入、模型質量及總社會福利。 本研究成果將帶來理論與政策雙重貢獻。在理論層面，項目通過納入生成式 AI 的共創特性以及輸入與輸出規管之間的反饋回路，拓寬了傳統版權經濟學的研究範疇。在實踐層面，本研究為香港等地區提供了及時的政策指導——香港目前採用對 AI 友好的規管機制，既允許無限制地使用訓練數據，又向 AI 輸出內容授予版權。通過明確創新與公平之間的最佳平衡點，本研究將為全球 AI 驅動型創意經濟的可持續政策設計提供科學依據。

21509426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21509426.value: 基於 Transformer 的有限數據下多地點報童系統庫存決策研究

21509426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21509426.value: *Project Background* In classical inventory models, decisions are optimized based on a well-specified stochastic model that characterizes the real system, which yields clear structure and theoretical insights. This approach, however, often comes at the cost of flexibility and tractability. Recent advancement in artificial intelligence (AI) offers a compelling alternative, but its reliance on large datasets, black-box nature, and lack of theoretical guarantees limit its adoption in practice. *Project Description* The project aims to bridge the classical and the AI paradigms by proposing a transformer-based inventory policy that embeds inventory-specific domain knowledge into generative AI, which enables efficient decision-making with limited data. Our approach is threefold: 1. We design a transformer architecture tailored for inventory decision-making based on historical observations that allows efficient optimization. The transformer takes historical demand-covariate pairs as inputs and automatically generates an inventory decision for the next period in real time. 2. We embed inventory-specific domain knowledge into the transformer decision by training the transformer model on simulated demand trajectories drawn from a series of demand models. The demand trajectories are properly augmented through certain transformations, which align the learned policies with the newsvendor solution structure known from classical inventory theory. 3. For multi-location inventory decision, we exploit the cross-attention mechanism to pool information across sites, which enables cross learning between different locations. We further incorporate capacity constraints through Lagrangian relaxation. Our model can thus make efficient real-time decisions for large-scale newsvendor systems faster than conventional methods. *Preliminary Results and Significance* We have developed a preliminary transformer model and an algorithm for the single-location newsvendor problem. Under a linear demand model, we can show that our approach leads to a uniformly optimal solution among a broad class of decision rules developed in the literature. The project will result in a scalable tool that automates data-driven decision making for large inventory systems, and accelerate the adoption of AI-driven inventory optimization in real-world operations. By bridging classical operations management (OM) insights with modern generative AI, this project advances both theory and practice in data-driven inventory management. 項目背景 在傳統庫存模型中，決策是基於能刻劃真實系統的明確隨機模型進行優化，從而提供清晰的結構與理論見解。然而，這種方法往往以犧牲靈活性和易處理性（tractability）為代價。人工智能（AI）的最新進展提供了一種具吸引力的替代方案，但其對大數據集的依賴、黑箱特性以及缺乏理論保障，限制了其在實際中的應用。 項目描述 本項目旨在通過提出一種基於 Transformer 的庫存策略，將傳統模式與 AI 模式相結合。該策略將庫存領域的專屬知識嵌入生成式 AI 中，從而在有限數據下實現高效決策。我們的方法分為三個層面： 一、設計專屬 Transformer 架構： 我們設計了一款專為庫存決策打造的 Transformer 架構，能根據歷史觀測數據進行高效優化。該模型以歷史需求—共變量對（demand-covariate pairs）作為輸入，並自動實時生成下一階段的庫存決策。 二、嵌入庫存領域專屬知識： 我們通過由一系列需求模型生成的模擬需求軌跡來訓練 Transformer 模型，從而將庫存專屬知識嵌入決策中。這些需求軌跡經過適當的變換增強，使學到的策略與傳統庫存理論中的報童解結構保持一致。 三、實現多地點決策與約束處理： 針對多地點庫存決策，我們利用交叉注意力機制匯集各據點的信息，實現不同地點之間的交叉學習（cross learning）。我們進一步通過拉格朗日鬆弛法納入產能/容量約束。因此，我們的模型能夠為大規模報童系統實時做出高效決策，速度優於傳統方法。 初步成果與重要意義 我們已針對單地點報童問題開發出初步的 Transformer 模型及算法。在線性需求模型下，我們可以證明本方法在文獻所開發的廣泛決策規則類別中能導出一致最優解（uniformly optimal solution）。本項目將產出一個具擴充性的工具，實現大規模庫存系統數據驅動決策的自動化，並加速 AI 驅動的庫存優化在真實營運中的應用。通過將傳統營運管理的洞察與現代生成式 AI 相結合，本項目將推動數據驅動庫存管理在理論與實踐上的雙重進步。

21601926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21601926.value: 連接社區與個體：香港粵語變異與變化的雙重研究路徑

21601926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21601926.value: Variability and change are fundamental features of human language. Language is always changing and no two people speak in exactly the same way. However, variability and change are not random. They follow systematic rules. For instance, in Hong Kong Cantonese, the two sounds /n/ and /l/ are merging so that the word for YOU can be pronounced as either nei5 or lei5. But the choice of nei5 or lei5 is not random and can be shaped by many social and linguistic factors. A Cantonese speaker in casual conversations with their local friends may prefer lei5. The use of /l/ may also be preferred before one vowel over another. However, a major mystery remains: Where do these systematic rules come from? What knowledge do individual speakers need to have for these patterns to manifest at the community level and how do their own production patterns and perceptual abilities contribute? To tackle these questions, this project adopts a dual approach, utilizing both corpus analysis and behavioral experiments to understand ongoing sound changes in Hong Kong Cantonese, bridging community-level patterns and individual-level processes. Hong Kong Cantonese is a perfect living laboratory because it is currently undergoing several rapid sound changes within a vibrant multilingual environment, offering a fresh perspective beyond studies focused only on English or other Indo-European languages. This project uses the aforementioned n-l merger as a test case. First, a large-scale corpus of natural speech from 120 native speakers of Hong Kong Cantonese will be compiled to map production patterns at both the community and individual levels. Subsequently, three perception experiments will be conducted with the same 120 participants to probe how individuals leverage their sociolinguistic knowledge of language contact to resolve ambiguity. This approach bridges the gap between community-level patterns and individual cognitive processes, and critically, forges a direct link between production and perception in sound change. The results of this project will document ongoing sound changes in Hong Kong Cantonese amidst rapid socio-cultural shifts, informing theories of language change by bridging patterns observed at community and individual levels. Additionally, this project will have the long-term potential to train Large Language Models to better accommodate the linguistic variability used by diverse speakers and to select socially appropriate variants to meet the communicative needs of users in different social situations. Ultimately, this work will contribute to scientific and cultural understanding of how humans communicate across a diverse range of language backgrounds. 語言的變異與演變是人類語言的基本特徵。語言無時無刻不在變化，世上亦沒有兩個人說話的方式完全相同。然而，這種變異與演變並非隨機發生，而是有跡可尋、遵循著系統性的規律。以香港粵語為例，/n/與/l/兩個聲母正逐漸合併，導致表示「你」的字既可讀作 nei5，亦可讀作 lei5。但發音的選擇並非隨意，而是受制於多種社會與語言因素。例如，當說話者與本地朋友閒聊時，可能更傾向發 lei5 音；在某些特定的元音前，發 /l/ 音的機率也可能較高。儘管如此，學界仍面臨一個重大謎團：這些系統性的規律從何而來？說話者需要具備怎樣的認知，這些語言模式才會在整個社群（community）中顯現？而說話者自身的發音習慣與語音感知能力，又在其中扮演甚麼角色？ 為探究上述問題，本項目將雙管齊下，結合語料庫分析與行為實驗，以剖析香港粵語正在發生的語音演變，從而在「社群整體的語言模式」與「個體的認知過程」之間建立連結。香港粵語身處充滿活力的多語環境，正同時經歷多項快速的語音演變，堪稱完美的「天然實驗室」；這也為過往多局限於英語或印歐語系的研究，提供了嶄新的視角。本項目將以 /n/ 與 /l/ 合併現象作為測試案例。首先，我們會建立一個包含120名香港粵語母語者自然對話的大型語料庫，藉此描繪社群與個體層面的發音模式。隨後，我們將邀請該120名參與者進行三項語音感知實驗，探討個體如何運用與語言接觸相關的社會語言學知識來消除語意歧義。此研究方法不僅彌合了社群模式與個體認知之間的鴻溝，更重要的是，它在語音演變的研究中，直接確立了「發音產出」與「語音感知」之間的關聯。 本項目的研究成果將如實記錄香港粵語在急劇社會文化變遷下的語音演變軌跡，並透過連結社群與個體層面的語言模式，為語言演變理論提供實證基礎。此外，本研究亦具備長遠的應用潛力：其數據可用於訓練大型語言模型（LLM），使其更能適應不同說話者的語言變異，並能根據社交情境選擇得體的用語，滿足用戶多元的溝通需求。總括而言，本研究將有助我們從科學與文化雙重維度，深入理解人類如何在豐富多樣的語言背景下進行交流。

21602626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21602626.value: 香港對類賭博電子遊戲「戰利品箱」的監管：高風險產品特徵與相關條例的合規性

21602626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21602626.value: Playing video games is now a highly popular activity worldwide and in Hong Kong (HK) specifically: 94% of secondary school students play at least weekly. Video games may cause harm to young people: 15.6% of students experienced ‘video game addiction.’ Many video games sell gambling-like ‘loot boxes.’ Players can buy these virtual items with real-world money to get random rewards allowing them to look cooler and fight more powerfully. Players obtain desirable rewards very rarely (less than 1% chance) and so must spend large sums of money to guarantee obtaining what they want. These products are psychologically similar to gambling but are not regulated as such by governments, meaning young people who are not permitted to participate in traditional gambling are currently allowed to purchase loot boxes. More than 50% of HK video game players likely buy loot boxes. Some reported extreme spending of over HK$100,000 monthly. Besides financial harms, these products may exacerbate video game addiction and encourage children to gamble. Other countries have regulated loot boxes, including bans and minimum age requirements to better protect players. However, these products have not been regulated in HK. This project provides crucial, but presently lacking, local evidence on loot box availability, product characteristics, and regulation. Firstly, relevant HK laws will be identified. Consumer protection and gambling laws will be reviewed to identify how they apply and what obligations they place on companies. For example, the Trade Descriptions Ordinance requires that sellers must not hide important information, which when applied to the loot box context means that companies must tell players the probabilities for getting specific random rewards. Secondly, we will examine the 100 most popular games in HK through gameplay to identify how many of them sell loot boxes and how, thus providing evidence on how widely available these products are. Thirdly, we will assess whether the loot boxes identified comply with applicable HK law. For example, are players given information about their probabilities of winning rare rewards as required? We will also assess video game advertising materials published on HK social media as to whether they comply with consumer law. Our findings will be shared with regulators to encourage stricter enforcement against companies that do not follow rules. We will also create a public website that shares information about how loot boxes are regulated in different regions globally to help companies understand their regulatory obligations. 玩電子遊戲已成為全球（尤其是中國香港）一項極受歡迎的活動：94%的中學生至少每週玩一次。電子遊戲可能對青少年造成危害：15.6%的學生曾經歷過「電子遊戲成癮」。許多電子遊戲銷售類似賭博性質的「戰利品箱」（loot boxes）。玩家可用現實貨幣購買這些虛擬物品，以獲取隨機獎勵，讓角色外觀更酷或戰鬥力更強。由於獲得心儀獎勵的幾率極低（不足1%），玩家往往需投入大量資金才能確保獲得所需物品。從心理層面來看，這些產品與賭博無異，但政府並未將其歸類為賭博進行監管；這意味著，被禁止參與傳統賭博的青少年目前卻可以購買戰利品箱。超過50%的香港玩家可能曾經購買過戰利品箱，部分玩家甚至每月花費超過10萬港元。除了經濟損失外，這些產品還可能加劇電子遊戲成癮，並誘導兒童參與賭博。其他國家已對戰利品箱實施監管（包括禁止銷售或設定最低年齡限制），以更好地保護玩家；然而，香港尚未對此類產品進行監管。本計畫旨在提供關於戰利品箱的普及程度、產品特性及監管現狀的本地實證數據——這些資訊至關重要，但目前尚付闕如。首先，我們將整理香港相關法律，審查消費者權益保護法及賭博法規，以明確其適用範圍及對企業規定的義務。例如，《商品說明條例》規定銷售者不得隱瞞重要資訊；若應用於戰利品箱，這意味著企業必須向玩家揭露獲得特定隨機獎勵的幾率。其次，我們將透過實際遊玩，檢視香港最受歡迎的100款遊戲，分析其中有多少款遊戲銷售戰利品箱及其銷售模式，從而揭示此類產品的普及程度。第三，我們將評估已識別的戰利品箱是否符合香港現行法律規定。例如，遊戲是否按要求向玩家告知獲得稀有獎勵的幾率？我們也將評估在香港社群媒體上發布的電子遊戲廣告素材，檢查是否符合消費者權益保護法規。我們將與監管機構分享研究結果，推動其對違規企業採取更嚴格的執法行動。此外，我們將建立一個公開網站，分享全球不同地區關於戰利品箱的監管資訊，幫助企業了解其應盡的監管合規義務。

21602826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21602826.value: 魯迅思想與文學中的復仇

21602826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21602826.value: This project examines a crucial yet underexplored dimension of Lu Xun’s thought and writing: the theme of revenge. Lu Xun has often been portrayed as an advocate of vengeance—an image shaped by his uncompromising stance toward adversaries, his later leftist orientation, and the combative tone and fascination with revenge narratives evident in his fiction. Yet this dimension has frequently been oversimplified or distorted. Scholarship has tended either to collapse his reflections on revenge into a generalized discourse of struggle, sometimes conflating it with revolution, or to abstract the theme into a vague notion of poetic justice. Moreover, few studies have situated Lu Xun within the comparative and world‑literary framework, exploring how he reworked Chinese and foreign traditions of revenge writing and how this process informed the making of Chinese modernity. Focusing on Lu Xun is particularly vital. As the central figure of modern Chinese literature and a thinker deeply attuned to the ethical and political crises of his time, he offers a unique vantage point for examining how revenge—at once a moral impulse and a narrative form—mediated tensions between tradition and modernity, individual development and social reform, Enlightenment ideals and Anti‑Enlightenment critiques. Unlike many of his contemporaries, Lu Xun not only reinterpreted classical Chinese motifs of vengeance but also actively engaged with global literary and philosophical traditions, embedding the theme of revenge into the very fabric of modern Chinese literature and intellectual history. To pursue these questions, the project combines intellectual history, literary analysis, and political philosophy to reconstruct the genealogy of revenge in Lu Xun’s thought, clarifying its content and distinctive features. Through comparative readings of Chinese and Western sources, it investigates how revenge intersects with issues of justice, responsibility, sincerity, and authenticity, and how it illuminates the ethical and political conditions of modern life. Ultimately, by reassessing Lu Xun’s place in both Chinese and global traditions of revenge literature, the study not only recovers a neglected aspect of his oeuvre but also demonstrates how the problem of revenge opens new horizons for understanding the formation of Chinese modernity. 本計畫旨在以「魯迅思想與文學中的復仇」為核心議題，全面探討魯迅如何在思想與 文學創作中構築、轉化與再現復仇的主題。魯迅長期以來被歸類為主張報復的復仇論者，一方面源於他對敵人不寬恕的態度及後期思想的左傾，另一方面則來自其作品中鮮明的抗爭姿態與對復仇故事的迷戀。然而，既有研究往往將魯迅的復仇觀簡化為一般性的抗爭或與革命混同，抑或將其文學裡的復仇主題抽象化為無具體指涉的詩性正義；此外，學界亦較少從比較文學與世界文學的視野，分析魯迅如何轉化中外復仇文學傳統，以及這一過程如何影響中國現代文學的形成。 為填補上述空白，本研究將結合思想史、文學研究與政治哲學的路徑，重新梳理魯迅 復仇思想的譜系，辨析其內涵及特質，比較中西思想資源與文學文本，探討復仇在傳統與現代性、啟蒙與反啟蒙間的深層辯證關係。同時，本研究亦將魯迅作品置於復仇的倫理政治語境中，檢視復仇的條件、責任與後果，考察其涉及的報復性正義與個體真誠性諸議題，並重新評估魯迅思想與文學中的復仇對中國現代性的影響。

21604326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21604326.value: 受自然啟發的高性能建築懸臂結構設計

21604326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21604326.value: The research proposal aims to revolutionize structural design by drawing inspiration from the geometric and mechanical properties of natural structures. Natural structures, such as insect wings and plant rhizomes, exhibit lightweight yet highly efficient structural networks, characterized by primary and secondary veins in a statically determinate system optimized for their in-plane and out-of-plane stiffness. This study proposes to adapt these natural principles to the design of cantilevered building structures, a critical architectural element that often faces challenges in balancing weight, stiffness, and load-bearing capacity. Building upon recent advancements in machine learning and graphic statics, this research will employ Maxwell's reciprocal diagrams to analyze and replicate the force equilibrium of natural structural networks. These diagrams will be used to train artificial intelligence models capable of generating structural networks for arbitrary boundary geometries, specifically, cantilevered structures. The machine learning framework will integrate image-text-based Diffusion Models to predict form and force diagrams, ensuring that the generated designs maintain static equilibrium and geometric efficiency. The generated structural patterns will be evaluated for their mechanical performance under point loads and distributed loads, simulating real-world conditions such as wind and seismic forces. Our preliminary studies on scaled-down 3D-printed prototypes of dragonfly-inspired wing cores have demonstrated up to a 25% improvement in out-of-plane stiffness compared to traditional designs, with a significant reduction in material usage. The proposed research seeks to extend these findings, focusing on developing lightweight, high-performance cantilever designs that optimize stiffness-to-weight ratios while maintaining architectural flexibility. This work has broader implications for sustainable construction practices, as it leverages bio-inspired principles to minimize material usage without compromising structural integrity. The methodology is also adaptable to other natural structures, such as the vein networks of grasshopper wings or the rhizomes of Amazon water lilies, opening avenues for further exploration. The project will culminate in the development of a computational design platform, enabling architects and engineers to generate efficient cantilever structures based on user-defined boundary geometries. By bridging biology, computational design, and structural engineering, this research aims to redefine how we design lightweight and efficient cantilever systems, contributing to more sustainable and resilient architectural innovations in the built environment. 本研究旨在透過借鑒自然結構的幾何和力學特性，革新結構設計。昆蟲翅膀和植物根莖等自然結構展現出輕盈而高效的結構網絡，其特點是具有主脈和次脈，構成一個靜定係統，並針對其面內和麵外剛度進行了優化。本研究擬將這些自然原理應用於懸臂式建築結構的設計。懸臂式建築結構是建築設計中的關鍵元素，在平衡重量、剛性和承載能力方面常常面臨挑戰。 基於機器學習和圖形靜力學的最新進展，本研究將利用麥克斯韋互易圖來分析和重現自然結構網絡的力平衡。這些圖將用於訓練人工智慧模型，使其能夠為任意邊界幾何形狀（特別是懸臂式結構）產生結構網路。此機器學習框架將整合基於圖像-文字的擴散模型來預測形狀和力圖，從而確保生成的結構設計保持靜力平衡和幾何效率。 我們將評估產生的結構模型在點載荷和分佈載荷下的機械性能，以模擬風力和地震力等真實世界條件。我們先前對蜻蜓翼芯的縮比3D列印原型進行的初步研究表明，與傳統設計相比，其面外剛度提高了高達25%，同時顯著減少了材料用量。本研究旨在拓展這些發現，重點在於開發輕盈、高性能的懸臂梁設計，在保持建築靈活性的同時優化剛度重量比。 這項工作對永續建築實踐具有更廣泛的意義，因為它利用仿生原理在不損害結構完整性的前提下最大限度地減少材料用量。此方法也適用於其他自然結構，例如蚱蜢翅膀的脈絡網絡或亞馬遜睡蓮的根莖，為進一步探索開闢了道路。該專案最終將開發出一個計算設計平台，使建築師和工程師能夠根據用戶自訂的邊界幾何形狀生成高效的懸臂結構。 透過融合生物學、計算設計和結構工程，這項研究旨在重新定義我們設計輕量化高效懸臂系統的方式，為建築環境中更具永續性和韌性的建築創新做出貢獻。

21611026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21611026.value: 由心而護：家庭照顧者的人際情緒調節、睡眠與健康之間的關係及文化價值觀的作用

21611026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21611026.value: Background: Aging societies worldwide, including Hong Kong, face increasing care demands, with family caregivers playing a vital role. Supporting their well-being is therefore increasingly critical. The dual emotional burden of caregiving—regulating one’s own emotions while managing those of care recipients—may contribute to the high prevalence of sleep problems that further undermine health. This study will be the first to examine how family caregivers’ engagement in interpersonal emotion regulation (IER)—specifically, intrinsic IER (managing one’s own emotions through others) and extrinsic IER (helping others manage theirs)—affects sleep and, in turn, physical and psychological well-being. Recognizing that emotion regulation is shaped by cultural values, this study will also leverage Hong Kong’s multicultural context to examine how interdependence (vs. independence), a cultural value that emphasizes social connectedness and harmony, influences caregivers’ intrinsic and extrinsic IER and their implications for sleep and health. This study includes three key research questions: Q1) Are higher levels of intrinsic IER associated with better sleep, and higher levels of extrinsic IER associated with worse sleep? Q2) Do sleep patterns mediate the relationships between intrinsic and extrinsic IER and caregivers’ physical and psychological well-being? Q3) Does interdependence (vs. independence) influence caregivers’ engagement in intrinsic and extrinsic IER, which in turn are linked to sleep and health? Methods: The study will adopt a multimethod, three-part design involving family caregivers in Hong Kong. (1) A cross-sectional survey will measure intrinsic and extrinsic IER, sleep quality, physical and psychological health, and the cultural values of interdependence and independence. (2) A two-week daily diary (i.e., daily surveys) will capture caregivers’ everyday experiences of intrinsic and extrinsic IER, self-reported sleep and health, and objective sleep indicators via actigraphy watches. (3) A two-month follow-up survey will reassess sleep quality, and physical and psychological health. Together, these complementary assessments will provide cross-sectional, daily, and longitudinal perspectives to address the research questions. Expected Deliverables: This project will generate a unique dataset on family caregivers’ IER, sleep, and health. The findings will enhance family caregivers’ awareness of how emotion regulation influences sleep and health, and will offer practical guidelines for community organizations and health professionals to strengthen caregiver support. Ultimately, the study will inform culturally sensitive practices and interventions, support policies that sustain family caregiving, and contribute to a healthier aging society in Hong Kong and beyond. 背景：包括香港在內的全球許多地區正面臨人口老齡化所帶來日益增加的照護需求，而家庭照顧者在其中扮演著重要角色。因此，如何支持家庭照顧者的身心健康變得愈加重要。照顧者在照顧過程中不僅需要調節自身情緒，亦需要協助照顧對象調節情緒。這種雙重情緒負擔可能增加睡眠問題的風險，並進一步影響其身心健康。本研究將首次探討家庭照顧者的人際情緒調節（interpersonal emotion regulation, IER）如何影響睡眠，以及睡眠如何進一步影響其身體及心理健康。具體而言，本研究將區分自我導向的人際情緒調節（intrinsic IER；通過他人協助調節自身情緒）與他人導向的人際情緒調節（extrinsic IER；協助他人調節情緒）。鑑於情緒調節亦受到文化價值觀的影響，本研究將結合香港多元文化的社會背景，進一步探討互依型自我（interdependent self-construal；相對於獨立型自我，independent self-construal）如何影響照顧者運用自我導向及他人導向的人際情緒調節策略，以及這些情緒調節方式與睡眠及健康之間的關係。 本研究包括三個主要研究問題：Q1）較高水平的自我導向人際情緒調節是否與較佳睡眠相關，而較高水平的他人導向人際情緒調節是否與較差睡眠相關？Q2）睡眠是否在自我導向及他人導向人際情緒調節與照顧者身心健康之間發揮中介作用？Q3）互依型自我（相對於獨立型自我）是否會影響照顧者的自我導向及他人導向人際情緒調節，並進而影響其睡眠及健康？ 方法：本研究將招募香港家庭照顧者，採用三階段研究設計，並結合多種研究方法進行數據收集。（1）首先進行橫斷面問卷調查，了解家庭照顧者的人際情緒調節方式、睡眠質素及身心健康狀況，並評估其互依型自我與獨立型自我。（2）隨後進行為期兩週的每日紀錄研究，透過每日問卷記錄照顧者日常生活中的自我導向及他人導向人際情緒調節，以及每日自陳的睡眠和健康狀況，並通過腕戴式活動記錄儀（actigraphy watches）收集客觀睡眠指標。（3）兩個月後進行追蹤問卷，再次評估其睡眠質素以及身體和心理健康。三個階段的研究將相互補充，從橫斷面、日常生活及縱向追蹤三個層面，更全面地探討上述研究問題。 預期成果：本研究將建立一個獨特的家庭照顧者人際情緒調節、睡眠與健康數據集。研究結果將加深家庭照顧者對情緒調節如何影響睡眠與健康的認識，並為社區機構及醫護及相關專業人士提供實用指引，以加強對家庭照顧者的支援。本研究將有助於發展具備文化敏感度的實務措施與介入方案，為制定支持家庭照護的相關政策提供依據，並為香港及其他地區應對人口老齡化、促進健康老齡社會的發展作出貢獻。

22200926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22200926.value: 透過垂直廓線觀測與模式模擬為香港臭氧減排策略提供科學支撐

22200926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22200926.value: Ozone (O3) pollution continues to impair air quality across major city clusters in China, accounting for over 70% of non-attainment days in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau Greater Bay Area. In Hong Kong (HK), sustained reductions in primary air pollutant emissions have not translated into declines in surface O3 levels, underscoring a persistent “O3 puzzle.” This project seeks to address this challenge by exploring the vertical dimension of O3 distribution, chemistry, and dynamics, an area that is significantly understudied in HK. Our central hypothesis is that a limited understanding of residual, imported, and locally produced O3 obscures surface O3 attribution and results in sub-optimal precursor control strategies. The specific objectives are to: (i) characterize vertical distributions of O3, its precursors, and key meteorological parameters at multiple times of day under various O3-conducive weather conditions; (ii) elucidate differences in in-situ photochemistry between altitudes and the overall photochemistry integrated over the boundary layer; and (iii) reveal the evolution of the three-dimensional O3 budget driven by the coupled effects of atmospheric dynamics and chemistry along the vertical dimension. We propose an integrated observation–model framework that combines high-cadence unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) vertical profiling (0–800 m), layer-resolved photochemistry simulations, and observation-informed chemical transport modeling. UAV-based measurements will capture air stratification, vertical profiles of O3 and its precursors including volatile organic compounds, residual-layer O3 and precursor reservoirs, and post-sunrise entrainment fluxes. The observational data will be used to constrain layer-resolved box models to simulate O3 formation regimes (sensitivities) and other photochemical metrics across altitudes. An observation-informed chemical transport model will elucidate how the coupling of atmospheric dynamics and chemistry influences vertical O3 redistribution and the relative roles of entrainment of residual O3, in-situ photochemical production, and horizontal/aloft transport in shaping surface O3 levels. Sensitivity simulations will further assess the responses of different forms of O3 to sector- and region-specific precursor emission reductions under typical O3-conducive weather conditions in HK. By explicitly incorporating vertical processes that are underrepresented in current monitoring and modeling efforts, the project will reduce uncertainties in O3 source apportionment and deliver actionable guidance for effective regional O3 mitigation. Key deliverables will include a UAV-based measurement and sampling system, publicly accessible processed UAV vertical profiles, harmonized model–observation O3 budget products, methodological toolkits for entrainment quantification, and policy briefs integrating vertical perspectives. Ultimately, this project aims to inform O3 mitigation strategies in HK under a changing climate. 臭氧污染持續影響中國主要城市群的空氣質素。在粵港澳大灣區，臭氧污染導致的空氣質素不達標日數佔比超過 70%。在香港，儘管一次空氣污染物排放量已持續下降，地面臭氧濃度卻未隨之降低，凸顯出一個持續存在的「臭氧難題」。本項目擬透過探索臭氧分佈、化學過程和動力過程的垂直維度來應對這一挑戰；而這一方向在香港仍明顯缺乏系統研究。 本項目的核心假設是：目前對殘留臭氧、外來輸送臭氧以及本地生成臭氧的認識不足，掩蓋了對地面臭氧來源歸因的準確判斷，並導致臭氧前體物控制策略未能達至最優。項目的具體目標包括：在不同臭氧易發氣象條件下，於一天中的多個時段，刻畫臭氧、其前體物以及關鍵氣象參數的垂直分佈特徵；闡明不同高度層的原位光化學過程差異，以及邊界層整體積分光化學過程的特徵；揭示在垂直維度上，由大氣動力過程與化學過程耦合作用驅動的三維臭氧收支演變。 本項目擬構建一個綜合的「觀測 - 模式」研究框架，結合高時間分辨率無人機垂直廓線觀測（0 - 800 米）、分層光化學模擬，以及觀測約束的化學輸送模式。基於無人機的觀測將捕捉空氣層結、臭氧及其前體物 - 包括揮發性有機物 - 的垂直廓線、殘留層臭氧和前體物儲庫，以及日出後夾卷通量等關鍵資訊。觀測數據將用於約束分層箱式模式，以模擬不同高度層的臭氧生成機制、敏感性及其他光化學指標。進一步，觀測約束的化學輸送模式將用於闡明大氣動力過程與化學過程的耦合如何影響臭氧的垂直再分佈，並量化殘留臭氧夾卷、原位光化學生產以及水平／高空輸送在塑造地面臭氧濃度中的相對作用。敏感性模擬亦將進一步評估在香港典型臭氧易發氣象條件下，不同類型臭氧對分行業、分區域前體物減排措施的響應。 透過明確納入當前監測和模擬工作中代表不足的垂直過程，本項目將降低臭氧來源解析中的不確定性，並為制定有效的區域臭氧減排策略提供可操作的科學依據。主要交付成果將包括：基於無人機的測量與採樣系統、公開可獲取的經處理無人機垂直廓線數據、協調一致的模式 - 觀測臭氧收支產品、用於夾卷量化的方法工具包，以及融合垂直視角的政策簡報。最終，本項目旨在為氣候變化背景下香港臭氧污染防控策略的制定提供科學支撐。

22201926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22201926.value: 用於建構具有可調光學特性和轉變溫度智能窗的工程化熱響應聚醚體系

22201926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22201926.value: Buildings in dense urban regions like Hong Kong account for 90% of generated electricity and contribute over 60% of carbon emissions. Among building components, windows are recognised as the least energy-efficient, responsible for 47% of undesired heat exchange across the building envelope—equating to 4% of total primary energy consumption in the United States. Addressing this energy inefficiency is crucial for meeting local and national climate goals and realising the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals. Although recent advances in thermochromic smart windows have achieved temperature-responsive solar regulation, they are still limited by inherent performance trade-offs, high transition temperatures, undesirable tints, mechanical fragility, and slow response times. These challenges hinder real-world deployment and commercial scalability. This project aims to develop a novel thermochromic polymer system based on the water-soluble polyether with performance tuning via the Hofmeister effect, i.e., ion-specific modulation of polymer and water interactions. We will combine physics- and optics-based experimental methods—including scattering techniques, in situ spectroscopy, and thermal analysis with simulation approaches, including ab initio molecular dynamics simulations and density function theory simulations—to bridge nanoscale structural evolution to macroscale performance. Prototype windows will be fabricated and validated through building energy simulations and real-world thermal testing. By investigating the thermal-optic coupling mechanism through establishing the structure-optical properties relationship in polyether during phase change, investigating the effect of Hofmeister ions on the thermochromic performance of polyether, and evaluating the energy-saving potential of polyether-based smart window, we will produce an emerging smart window with tunable transition temperatures, high luminous transmittance and solar modulation, excellent cycling stability, and promising energy-saving performance. As an early-career faculty member, the Principal Investigator has established a reputation in smart materials development and smart window design. With the pioneering design of multi-wavelength modulation vanadium dioxide smart window (Science 2021, 374, 1501.) and heat storage smart windows based on thermo-responsive hydrogels (Joule 2020, 4, 2458.), the research output of the PI has been featured in more than 70 international media platforms and won the international Green Award (London 2022 TOP 3 in Energy category). The outcomes of this project will deliver new insights into responsive polymer systems and a scalable design strategy for high-performance smart windows. This research will directly support energy-efficient building technologies, Hong Kong’s Climate Action Plan 2050, and UN SDGs, while fostering industry-academic collaboration toward sustainable urban infrastructure. 在香港這樣的建築密集都市地區，建築物消耗了本地區發電量的90%，並排放超過60%的二氧化碳。在建築組件中，窗戶被認為是最不節能的，它導致建築外殼內外47%的非預期熱交換——相當於美國主要能源消耗的4%。解決窗戶的能源效率問題，對於實現地方及國家氣候目標以及聯合國永續發展目標至關重要。 儘管熱致變色智能窗近年來達成溫度響應式的太陽能調節，但仍受限於固有的性能缺陷：如高轉變溫度、不良色調、機械脆弱性及反應時間緩慢等。這些性能缺陷阻礙了智能窗的實際部署與商業擴展。本研究旨在開發一種基於水溶性聚醚的新型熱致變色聚合物系統，並透過霍夫邁斯特效應（即聚合物與水相互作用的離子特異性調控）進行性能調諧。我們將結合物理與光學實驗方法——包括散射技術、原位光譜學及熱分析，與模擬方法，包括分子動力學模擬與密度函數理論模擬——以銜接顯微尺度結構演化與宏觀性能。原型窗戶將透過建築能源模擬與熱測試來製造與驗證其節能性能。透過建立聚醚相變期間結構-光學性質關係，研究熱光耦合機制，探討霍夫邁斯特離子對聚醚熱致變色性能的影響，並評估聚醚基智能窗的節能潛力，我們將打造出具備可調轉變溫度、高透光率與太陽調制能力、優異循環穩定性的新興智能窗。 作為早期職涯的教職員，本項目的首席研究員在智能材料開發與智能窗戶設計方面建立了良好聲譽。憑藉多波段調變二氧化釩智能窗（Science 2021， 374， 1501）及基於熱響應水凝膠的熱能儲存智能窗（Joule 2020， 4， 2458）的開創性設計，首席研究員的研究成果已在超過70個國際媒體平台上刊登，並榮獲國際綠色獎（倫敦2022能源類別前三名）。本項目成果將帶來關於響應式聚合物系統及可擴展設計策略的新見解，以實現高性能智能窗戶。這項研究將直接支持節能建築技術、香港2050年氣候行動計畫及聯合國永續發展目標，同時促進產學合作，推動永續城市基礎設施。

22202126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22202126.value: 大型基礎模型的高效預訓練：協同參數、內存與數據高效技術

22202126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22202126.value: The success of ChatGPT and other large foundation models highlights their transformative potential across research, industry, and society. However, training such models remains extremely resource-intensive. For instance, GPT-4 reportedly required around 25,000 A100 GPUs over 100 days, consuming more than 62 million kilowatt-hours of electricity. These prohibitive costs limit pre-training to a few large organizations, raising concerns about sustainability and technological monopoly. As the demand for increasingly larger models grows, there is a pressing need to develop more efficient pre-training methods. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods have been extensively explored, but they rely on pretrained knowledge, making them less applicable during the pre-training phase or only capable of limited improvements. The challenge of improving pre-training efficiency lies in the complex interplay between several factors: parameters, optimizers, memory, and data. Existing research primarily focuses on only one of these factors in isolation, often neglecting their interdependencies, which leads to suboptimal performance. For example, while parameter-efficient architectures reduce the number of parameters, they impose optimization constraints that are often overlooked. Memory-efficient optimizers, although designed to reduce memory overhead from storing optimizer states, often fail to preserve sufficient gradient information, harming model performance. Additionally, data-efficient methods typically ignore the synergies between parameter- and memory-efficient methods. This project aims to develop synergistic techniques for efficient pre-training by jointly advancing parameter, memory, and data efficiency. Specifically, we will: 1) Design parameter-efficient architectures paired with memory-efficient, compressed structure-aware optimizers to achieve performance comparable to full-parameter models at significantly lower computational cost. 2) Develop dynamic model expansion strategies that adaptively increase model capacity as training progresses, while preserving parameter efficiency. 3) Develop data-efficient pre-training algorithms that integrate parameter- and memory-efficient techniques, adaptively allocating computation to the most informative samples through data utility estimation and dynamic selection. 4) Complement these methods with theoretical analysis and extensive empirical studies to provide solid, actionable insights. By reducing pre-training costs while maintaining high performance, this research will make 7B or even 13B models pre-training feasible on a single consumer-grade GPU, such as the RTX 4090. Ultimately, the proposed methods aim to promote sustainable AI development and lower the entry barrier for foundation model research, paving the way for broader participation beyond a few large organizations. ChatGPT 等大型基礎模型的成功展現了其在科研、產業和社會應用中的巨大潛力。然而，這類型的訓練需要大量計算資源。例如，據報導，GPT-4 的訓練使用了約 2.5 萬張 A100 GPU，持續約 100 天，耗電超過 6200 萬千瓦時。高昂的訓練成本使大規模預訓練主要集中在少數大型機構，也帶來了可持續性以及技術資源過度集中的問題。 現有的量化、剪枝和低秩近似等模型壓縮技術可以降低推理成本，但往往會造成一定的性能損失。同時，這些方法主要面向推理效率，對預訓練階段的效率提升相對有限。模型預訓練的效率受到參數、優化器、梯度和訓練數據等多個因素影響，而現有研究通常只針對其中某一方面進行優化。不同方面也存在各自的困難。例如，參數高效的模型結構會帶來新的優化問題，而現有的內存高效優化器尚不能充分利用模型的壓縮結構，因而難以達到理想的訓練效果。 本項目擬研究面向大型基礎模型預訓練的協同增效技術，同時提升參數、內存和數據三個方面的效率。具體包括：1）設計參數高效的模型結構，並研究與之配套的內存高效、面向壓縮結構的優化方法，在顯著降低計算成本的同時達到與全參數訓練相當的性能；2）研究數據高效的預訓練算法，使模型能夠利用更少的數據快速收斂；3）引入數據集蒸餾方法，提高海量數據條件下的訓練效率；4）結合理論分析和系統實驗，進一步理解這些方法的作用機制和效果。 通過降低預訓練成本並保持模型性能，本項目希望使與傳統全參數 70 億參數模型相當規模、甚至更大規模的模型能夠在單張消費級 GPU（如 RTX 4090）上進行預訓練。相關研究有望推動更加可持續的大規模技術發展，降低基礎大規模研究的資源門檻，使更多科研團隊能夠參與大規模模型的預訓練研究。

22301326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22301326.value: 利用分子表徵方法理解單分散有機混合導體的分子結構性質關係

22301326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22301326.value: Organic mixed conductors (OMIECs) conduct both ions and electronic charges, a unique property enabling them to interface with biological systems and demonstrate great potential in a wide range of bioelectronics applications. However, the optimization of OMIECs is hampered by the inherent variability arising from polydispersity and impurities found in polymers. Such variability can lead to order-of-magnitude performance differences, posing a significant challenge for consistent and scalable applications. A shift towards monodisperse OMIEC oligomers offers a promising avenue to mitigate these inconsistencies, allowing for a more controlled and predictable performance. However, a fundamental understanding of structure-property relationships in these oligomers remains elusive, especially for key properties such as mobility and transconductance at the single-molecule scale. Here, we propose a novel molecular characterization approach that overcomes the limitations of existing single-molecule techniques. Our technical innovation is a platform that integrates a Scanning Tunneling Microscope-Break Junction (STM-BJ) with a semiconductor characterization system, enabling dynamic, transistor-like measurements that are fundamentally different from the static control offered by conventional methods. This unique platform will be used to investigate the fundamental coupling between electronic and ionic conduction at the single-molecule level. We will synthesize a series of monodisperse thiophene-based oligomers with systematically varied backbone (for electronic conduction) and side-chain (for ionic conduction) lengths using a rapid microwave-assisted approach. Our automated measurement platform is designed to perform the first direct characterization of single-molecule mobility and transconductance. Additionally, the influence of diverse electrolytes on molecule-ion interactions and dynamics will be examined to understand their impact on performance. These studies will provide fundamental insights into the design principles for high-performance OMIECs. Specifically, we will quantify how molecular structure and the ionic environment affect key bioelectronic metrics such as response speed, and we will assess the potential for in-situ signal amplification by measuring the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) using artificial ECG and EEG signals. The outcome of this proposal will advance our fundamental understanding of OMIECs and guide the rational design of materials for more compact, rapid, and high-performance bioelectronic devices. 有機混合離子電子導體能同時傳導離子與電子，此獨特性質使其得以與生物系統進行介面接觸，並在廣泛的生物電子學應用中展現出巨大潛力。然而，由於聚合物中普遍存在的多分散性與雜質，所導致的固有變異性極大地阻礙了此類材料的優化。這種變異性可能導致性能出現高達數個數量級的差異，對實現穩定的應用構成了重大挑戰。轉向研究單分散的有機混合導體寡聚物，為降低此類不一致性提供了一條極具前途的途徑，從而能實現更具可控性與可預測性的性能表現。然而，目前對這些寡聚物的結構與性質關係之基礎理解仍相當有限，特別是在單分子尺度下的遷移率與跨導等關鍵特性。在此，我們提出一種全新的分子表徵方法，用以克服現有單分子技術的局限性。我們的技術創新是一個將掃描隧道的顯微鏡斷裂結技術與半導體分析系統整合的平台，能夠進行動態、類似晶體管的測量，這與傳統方法提供的靜態控制有著根本上的不同。此獨特平台將用於深入探討單分子層面上電子傳導與離子傳導之間的基礎耦合機制。我們將採用快速的微波輔助合成法，合成一系列具有系統性變化主鏈（用於電子傳導）與側鏈（用於離子傳導）長度的單分散噻吩基寡聚物。我們設計的自動化測量平台旨在對單分子的遷移率與跨導進行首次直接表徵。此外，我們也將探討不同電解質對分子離子相互作用與動力學的影響，以理解其對性能的具體作用。這些研究將為高性能有機混合導體的設計原則提供關鍵的基礎洞察。具體而言，我們將定量分析分子結構與離子環境如何影響響應速度等關鍵生物醫學電子指標，並透過使用人工心電圖與腦電圖信號測量信噪比，評估原位信號放大的潛力。本提案的研究成果將推動對有機混合導體的基礎理解，並指引材料的理性設計，以開發出更緊湊、快速且高性能的生物電子裝置。

22500226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22500226.value: 鄰里黨派歸屬信念與父母社會化努力：來自一項隨機資訊實驗的證據

22500226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22500226.value: Political polarization has grown across many democracies and now reaches into daily life. Parents play a central role in shaping how children learn about politics: they decide whether to discuss public affairs at home, what news to share or filter, and how to handle disagreements. This project poses a causal question at the heart of those choices: when parents change their beliefs about the partisan composition of their neighborhood, do they also change the effort they devote to socializing their children? I will conduct a two-wave online study of U.S. parents. At baseline, each parent reports their prior belief about the local partisan composition. A randomly selected group then sees a page with concise, source-cited statistics about their area's copartisan share; a control group sees a visually matched page without factual content. After a brief neutral buffer, I elicit posterior beliefs and record a set of pre-specified behaviors that capture parental socialization effort in concrete ways, such as conversation frequency, media curation and gatekeeping for the child, a short plan for a civics activity together, and a simple narrative video choice that distinguishes balanced, civics-first materials from one-sided partisan framing. A follow-up survey four to eight weeks later re-measures beliefs and behaviors to test whether any changes persist beyond the survey session and to reduce the surveyor demand effect. The experiment design follows the best practices in information experiments and maintains strictly non-partisan content. Random assignment supports a clean causal interpretation: differences in behaviors between the treatment and control groups can be attributed to the information. To directly link belief changes to actions, I use assignment as an instrumental variable for the posterior belief. Because information can move beliefs upward for some parents and downward for others, I will report effects separately by the sign of the initial misperception, and I will examine treatment heterogeneity by parent gender, socioeconomic status, and the child's age. This project provides evidence on a household channel through which polarization can be reproduced or buffered: parents adjusting socialization effort in response to perceived local context. It contributes to the literature on cultural transmission by treating the perceived neighborhood partisan share as the state variable in a simple investment problem and by estimating how effort responds when the belief of that state is credibly updated. This project advances our understanding of the formation and persistence of political identities. 政治極化已在許多民主國家加劇，並逐漸滲透到日常生活之中。父母在形塑子女如何認識政治方面扮演核心角色：他們決定是否在家中討論公共事務、分享或過濾哪些新聞，以及如何處理意見分歧。本計畫提出一個置於這些選擇核心的因果問題：當父母改變對其所在社區黨派組成的信念時，他們是否也會改變投入於子女社會化的努力？ 我將對美國父母進行一項兩波線上研究。在基線階段，每位父母報告其對當地黨派組成的事前信念。隨機選取的一組隨後看到一頁附有簡潔、註明來源之統計資料的頁面，內容關於其居住地區的同黨支持者比例；對照組則看到視覺設計相匹配、但不含事實內容的頁面。經過短暫的中性緩衝之後，我將引出事後信念，並記錄一組事先設定的行為，以具體方式捕捉父母的社會化努力，例如對話頻率、為子女進行的媒體策展與把關、一項共同公民活動的簡短計畫，以及一個簡單的敘事影片選擇——用以區分平衡、以公民教育為主的材料與片面的黨派框架。四至八週後的追蹤調查將重新測量信念與行為，以檢驗任何變化是否能延續至調查當次之外，並降低調查者需求效應。實驗設計遵循資訊實驗的最佳實務，並嚴格維持非黨派內容。 隨機分派支持清晰的因果詮釋：處理組與對照組之間的行為差異可歸因於該資訊。為直接連結信念變化與行動，我將以分派作為事後信念的工具變數。由於資訊可能使部分父母的信念上調、另一些下調，我將依初始錯誤認知的符號分別報告效應，並檢視處理異質性——依父母性別、社經地位與子女年齡。 本計畫提供關於家庭管道的證據：透過此一管道，極化可能被再製或緩衝——亦即父母因應所感知的地方脈絡而調整社會化努力。本計畫對文化傳遞文獻的貢獻，在於將所感知的鄰里黨派比例視為一個簡單投資問題中的狀態變數，並估計當該狀態的信念獲得可信更新時，努力如何回應。本計畫推進我們對政治認同形成與持續的理解。

22501226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22501226.value: 揭露資訊與確認資訊的決策有用性：來自財務分析師預測型的證據

22501226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22501226.value: This project examines whether recognition, as opposed to disclosure, changes the decision usefulness of accounting information in the context of operating leases from the perspective of key users of accounting information: financial analysts. The disclosure-versus-recognition question is central to accounting standard setting; indeed, FASB (1984) explicitly states that disclosure should not be a substitute for recognition, and this paper serves as an evaluation of that statement. Although the topic has received sustained attention in the academic literature, prior studies have primarily relied on market-based outcomes—such as stock returns, the market value of equity, and the cost of capital—which, while informative to both academics and standard setters, provide only indirect evidence. These measures do not directly reveal whether users actually employ the disclosed information in their decision processes, nor do they identify which specific users are affected by a shift from disclosure to recognition of accounting information. In other words, they speak to market-level consequences but not to the mechanics of information use by particular stakeholders. This study addresses this gap by using a unique, direct measure to examine whether financial analysts—key stakeholders in capital markets—incorporate operating lease information into their forecasting decisions. The empirical setting is ASC 842, a recent accounting standard that requires firms to recognize operating leases on the balance sheet that had previously been disclosed only in the footnotes. I leverage a unique dataset from Visible Alpha, which allows its users to observe whether and when financial analysts incorporate operating lease information into their forecasting models. I expect that recognition under ASC 842 will increase analysts’ propensity to use operating lease items in their forecasting models. In addition, I examine whether this shift in modeling behavior translates into improvements in forecast quality—specifically, higher forecast accuracy and lower dispersion across analysts—once operating leases are recognized. Finally, prior literature suggests two primary mechanisms through which recognition may enhance usefulness: an increase in the reliability of the information and a reduction in information-processing costs. Because financial analysts are relatively sophisticated users who can often overcome information processing barriers, I expect the reliability channel to be the dominant driver in the setting. To test this mechanism, I conduct cross-sectional analyses based on the ex-ante reliability of disclosed operating leases. 本計畫從會計資訊關鍵使用者－財務分析師－的視角出發，探討在經營租賃背景下，將資訊「確認」（而非僅「揭露」）是否會改變會計資訊的決策有用性。 「揭露與確認」之爭是會計準則制定中的核心議題；事實上，FASB（1984）明確指出揭露不應取代確認，而本文正是對此觀點的評估。儘管學術界對此議題持續關注，但先前研究主要依賴以市場為基礎的指標（如股票報酬率、權益市場價值和資本成本）；這些指標雖對學者和準則制定者俱有參考價值，卻僅能提供間接證據。它們既無法直接揭示使用者是否在決策過程中實際利用了揭露的訊息，也無法識別哪些特定使用者會受到會計資訊處理方式從「揭露」轉變為「確認」的影響。換言之，這些指標反映的是市場層面的後果，而非特定利害關係人使用資訊的具體機制。本研究透過採用獨特的直接衡量指標來填補這一空白，考察資本市場中的關鍵利害關係人——財務分析師——是否將經營租賃資訊納入其預測決策之中。 本研究的實證背景為ASC 842準則。該準則要求企業將先前僅在附註中揭露的經營租賃事項在資產負債表中進行確認。我利用了Visible Alpha提供的獨特資料集，該資料集允許觀察財務分析師是否以及何時將經營租賃資訊納入其預測模型。我預期，在ASC 842準則下進行的「確認」操作，將提高分析師在其預測模型中使用經營租賃項目的傾向。此外，我還檢視了這種建模行為的轉變是否轉化為預測品質的提升——具體表現為更高的預測準確度和更低的分析師間預測分歧度。最後，先前文獻指出，「確認」可能透過兩種主要機制增強資訊有用性：提高資訊可靠性以及降低資訊處理成本。鑑於財務分析師屬於相對成熟的使用者，通常能夠克服資訊處理障礙，我預期「可靠性」機制將成為本研究情境下的主導驅動因素。為了驗證這個機制，我基於已揭露經營租賃資訊的「事前可靠性」進行了截面分析。

22503726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22503726.value: 你正在小憩五分鐘嗎？探討同事微休息所引發的矛盾反應，以及哪些因素能緩解這些反應

22503726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22503726.value: Scholarly research on employee recovery has overwhelmingly demonstrated the intrapersonal benefits of taking microbreaks, establishing them as a key tool for maintaining well-being and performance. In contrast, the popular discourse has also hinted at the negative interpersonal consequences of microbreaks, which may inadvertently deter employees from accessing the full benefits documented in academic research. Thus, the purpose of this study is to provide a more comprehensive and balanced perspective on the social consequences of taking microbreaks at work. Drawing on emotional appraisal theory, we argue that observing a coworker take microbreaks can elicit two competing emotional and behavioral pathways in an observing employee. On one hand, the microbreaks taken by the coworker may be appraised as an obstacle and uncertainty to smooth task completion, triggering irritation and instigating antisocial responses like incivility. On the other hand, the same microbreaks may be appraised as a sign of distress and need for recovery, generating sympathy and prompting prosocial actions like helping. Further, we contend that the observers’ interpretation is not random but shaped by relational context. Specifically, we hypothesize that coworker self-disclosure—coworkers sharing personal information about themselves—weakens the irritation and incivility pathway while strengthening the sympathy and helping pathway. By illuminating the potential for both negative and positive social consequences, as well as highlighting what coworkers can do to alleviate detrimental consequences, this research provides a more complete picture of recovery in organizations, highlighting the social consequences of “taking five.” 關於員工恢復力的學術研究已壓倒性地證實，短暫休息能帶來顯著的個人層面益處，並將其確立為維持身心健康與工作表現的關鍵工具。相較之下，主流輿論也暗示了短暫休息可能帶來的負面人際影響，這可能會無意間阻礙員工充分享有學術研究中記載的各項益處。因此，本研究旨在針對工作時進行「微休息」所帶來的社會後果，提供更全面且平衡的觀點。基於情緒評估理論，我們認為，目睹同事進行「微休息」的行為，可能會在觀察者身上引發兩種相互對立的情緒與行為路徑。一方面，同事所做的微休息可能會被視為順利完成任務的障礙與不確定因素，從而引發煩躁情緒，並誘發不禮貌等反社會行為；另一方面，相同的微休息也可能被視為陷入困境及需要恢復的徵兆，從而引發同情，並促使人們採取幫助他人等親社會行為。此外，我們主張觀察者的詮釋並非隨機產生，而是受人際關係脈絡所形塑。具體而言，我們假設同事間的自我揭露——即同事分享關於自身的個人資訊——會削弱「煩躁與無禮」途徑的影響，同時強化「同理心與協助」途徑的影響。透過闡明可能產生的負面與正面社會後果，並強調同事們可採取哪些措施來緩解不利後果，這項研究為組織中的復原過程提供了更完整的圖景，同時突顯了「休息五分鐘」所帶來的社會後果。

22601426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22601426.value: 東亞與西方老齡化社會中父母喪偶期間的代際支持

22601426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22601426.value: East Asian societies are rapidly aging, and widowhood is becoming a major social challenge. Losing a spouse brings profound psychological distress, with adverse effects on mental and physical health, and often threatens financial security. These risks are especially acute in East Asia, where high rates of poverty and depression in later life intersect with rigid gender norms that make adaptation after widowhood more difficult. Across countries, children are generally regarded as the primary source of support for widowed parents, but this expectation is even stronger in societies with deeply rooted familial cultures. Existing research has tended to frame widowhood primarily as a personal crisis and, less often, as a social problem. What has been largely overlooked, however, is a family-level perspective—how widowhood reorganizes the relationships between parents and all their adult children. We know that widowhood generates enduring financial, caregiving, and social needs, but far less is understood about how siblings in families collectively or unequally share these responsibilities, how these patterns evolve across different stages of widowhood, and why some families arrive at more balanced and intensive support arrangements than others. This project pioneers a family-centered approach to widowhood, reframing it as a multistage process that reshapes relationships both between generations (parents and children) and within generations (among siblings). By harmonizing large, nationally representative aging surveys from Europe, the United States, the Chinese Mainland, South Korea, and Japan, it will examine intergenerational support across four stages: pre-widowhood, pre-terminal phase (before parental death), early widowhood, and later widowhood. The study has three goals: (1) to map how adult siblings share practical and social support for their parents across these stages; (2) to identify factors that shape these support patterns at both the family level (e.g., sibling composition) and the societal level (e.g., policy and cultural contexts); and (3) to understand how widowhood and support across generations are influenced by gender. The project will make both theoretical and practical contributions. First, by examining how siblings share support for widowed parents, it will shed light on fairness and intergenerational solidarity, with implications for family conflicts, family caregivers’ well-being, and older adults’ mental health. Second, it will examine how different welfare systems and cultural contexts shape family support, offering insights into the balance between strong family obligations and expanding social welfare in East Asia. This will inform discussions on meeting the needs of widowed older adults and their families. 東亞社會正面臨快速高齡化，喪偶亦逐漸成為一項重大的社會挑戰。喪失配偶會帶來深重的心理困擾，不僅對身心健康造成負面影響，亦往往威脅到長者的經濟保障。這類風險在東亞尤為嚴峻：老年貧困與抑鬱發生率居高不下，再加上僵化的性別規範，令喪偶長者更難適應生活的轉變。儘管將子女視為喪偶父母的主要支持來源在各個國家都是一種普遍的觀念；但是在一些家族文化根深蒂固的社會中，大眾對子女承擔支持責任的期望會更為強烈。 現有研究大多將喪偶主要界定為個人層面的危機，較少將其視為社會議題。研究較少觸及家庭層面的研究視角被極大地忽視 —— 喪偶如何重構父母與全體成年子女之間的互動關係？我們已知喪偶會衍生持續的經濟、照顧與社交需求，但我們考慮到的還遠遠不夠：家庭內的兄弟姊妹是共同地還是不平等地承擔著家庭責任？這種分工模式如何在喪偶的不同時段發生變化？部分家庭爲什麽能平衡好資源，為喪偶者提供充分的支持？ 本研究開創一種以家庭為中心的喪偶研究取向，將喪偶重新界定為一個多階段的過程，並探討這一過程如何重塑代際之間（父母與子女）以及同代之間（兄弟姊妹）的關係。透過整合歐洲、美國、中國內地、南韓及日本具全國代表性的大型高齡化調查資料，本研究將分析四個階段的代際支持：喪偶前、臨終前階段（父母去世前）、喪偶初期及喪偶後期。本研究有三項目標：（1）描繪成年兄弟姊妹在不同階段如何分擔對父母的實務照護與情緒社交支持；（2）識別在家庭層次（例如兄弟姊妹組成）及社會層次（例如政策及文化背景）塑造這些支持模式的因素；以及（3）了解喪偶及代際支持如何受到性別因素影響。 本研究將帶來理論與實務雙重貢獻。第一，透過考察兄弟姊妹如何為喪偶父母提供各項支持行爲，本研究能夠深化我們對於公平性與代際團結的理解，對於剖析家庭衝突、家庭照顧者的福祉以及長者的心理健康具有啟示。第二，本研究探討不同福利體系與文化脈絡如何形塑家庭支持，剖析東亞社會如何在濃厚的家庭責任觀與持續擴張的社會福利之間求取平衡。研究成果亦可供政策討論參考，協助社會回應喪偶長者及其家庭的各項需求。

22603326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22603326.value: 以擴增實境及生成式人工智能促進香港紮作技藝：互動式文化遺產保存與傳承

22603326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22603326.value: The Hong Kong Government's 2025 Policy Address highlights strengthening district-based promotion of Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) and advancing the "ICH Around Town" initiative. Hong Kong's traditional paper craft technique, known as Za-zo, is a form of dynamic handcrafting that combines bamboo frameworks and colored paper to produce decorative structures for festivals and rituals. Recognized as Hong Kong's ICH in 2014 and officially inscribed on the Representative List in 2017, Za-zo has received growing attention through government and stakeholder initiatives. Despite these efforts, significant challenges remain in its preservation and transmission: (C1) lack systematic understanding of its under-documented dimensions and difficulties hinders broader transmission; (C2) current documentation inadequately represents its 4D information (3D form and dynamic process); (C3) crafting heavily relies on 2D references and intensive mentorship, hindering easy grasp of 4D forms, limiting scalability, broader participation, and personalized learning/creation; (C4) unclear criteria and methods to evaluate the new digital preservation and transmission tools. This project therefore aims to explore how Za-zo crafting techniques be better preserved and transmitted with emerging technologies, especially Augmented Reality (AR) and Generative AI (GenAI), to address the challenges. First, we will conduct literature review and in-depth interviews with key Za-zo stakeholders to identify under-documented dimensions of Za-zo and current transmission challenges (C1). Second, we will construct a multimodal 4D dataset to digitally represent and archive 3D Za-zo works and techniques, capturing external geometry and appearance, internal bamboo frameworks, and dynamic crafting processes through automatic reconstruction methods and interactive mobile AR capture (C2). Third, we will design an interactive tool with AR and GenAI to support easy, customizable 3D Za-zo creation and learning (C3). It will accept multimodal inputs (e.g., text descriptions, image references) and generate editable 3D Za-zo designs with decomposable components and AR-guided crafting instructions, allowing users to in-situ design and practice Za-zo in virtual and physical forms. Input and feedback from artisans, learners, and general users will be incorporated throughout. For validation, we will co-organize Za-zo creation and transmission activities with practitioners and industries, embedding them into common practice (C4). With strong local support, promising preliminary results, and solid expertise, this project aims to set a benchmark for digital heritage preservation of 3D and dynamic handcrafting. Through easy, customizable AR and GenAI solutions, we envision broader participation, craftsmanship revitalization, and new opportunities for cultural tourism and creative practice of Hong Kong–specific applications. 香港政府在《2025年施政報告》中強調加強以地區為本推廣非物質文化遺產（非遺），並推進「香港處處有非遺」計劃。香港傳統紙紮工藝「紮作」是一種結合竹篾骨架與彩紙的動態手工技藝，用以製作節慶及儀式所需的裝飾性結構。紮作於2014年獲列入香港非物質文化遺產清單，並於2017年正式納入代表作名錄；近年亦透過政府及不同持份者的倡議而受到日益重視。儘管如此，紮作的保存與傳承仍面對多項重大挑戰：（C1）對其尚未被充分記錄的內容及傳承困難缺乏系統性理解，阻礙其更廣泛的傳播；（C2）現有記錄方式未能充分呈現其四維資訊，即三維形態與動態製作過程；（C3）紮作學習高度依賴二維參考資料及密集式師徒指導，令學習者難以掌握四維形態，限制了其可擴展性、廣泛參與及個人化學習與創作；（C4）缺乏明確準則與方法，以評估新興數碼保存與傳承工具的成效。 因此，本計劃旨在探討如何運用新興科技，尤其是擴增實境（AR）及生成式人工智能（GenAI），更有效地保存及傳承紮作技藝，並回應上述挑戰。首先，我們將進行文獻回顧，並與主要紮作持份者進行深入訪談，以識別紮作尚未被充分記錄的內容，以及現時傳承所面對的挑戰（C1）。其次，我們將建構一個多模態四維數據集，以數碼方式呈現及保存三維紮作作品與相關技藝。該數據集將透過自動重建方法及互動式流動擴增實境採集，記錄作品的外部幾何形態與外觀、內部竹篾骨架，以及動態製作流程（C2）。第三，我們將設計一套結合擴增實境及生成式人工智能的互動工具，支援易於理解且可自訂的三維紮作創作與學習（C3）。系統將接受多模態輸入，例如文字描述及圖像參考，並生成可編輯的三維紮作設計；設計將包含可拆解的組件，以及由擴增實境引導的製作指示，讓使用者能夠在虛擬及實體環境中進行紮作設計與練習。工藝師、學習者及一般使用者的意見與回饋，將在整個研究及設計過程中持續納入。 在驗證方面，我們將與紮作從業者及相關業界共同舉辦紮作創作與傳承活動，並將系統嵌入日常實踐情境中，以評估其效能（C4）。憑藉本地社群的有力支持、具潛力的初步成果及紮實的研究專長，本計劃旨在為三維及動態手工藝的數碼文化遺產保存建立具參考價值的典範。透過易用、可自訂的擴增實境及生成式人工智能方案，我們期望促進更廣泛的社會參與、活化工藝傳承，並為具香港特色的文化旅遊及創意實踐開拓新機遇。

22603826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22603826.value: 處方圖像：早期現代中國以畫為藥的實踐及其在當代藝術中的激活

22603826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22603826.value: This project investigates the practice of using visual art as medicine—what I term “art as prescription”—in early modern Chinese print culture and proposes its continued transhistorical influence in contemporary Chinese art. As early as the 14th century, the dietary and nutritional manual Yinshan zhengyao (YSZY, Proper and Essential Things for the Emperor’s Food and Drink) documented the practice of prescribing art as medicine. Originally dated 1330, though surviving only in a Ming printed edition of 1456, this manual vividly depicts the act of looking as a form of embodied care, most strikingly in several illustrated scenes showing pregnant women admiring paintings of carp, peacocks, eagles, jade, and etc, designating various effects on the unborn child such as intelligence, beauty, and strength. It suggests that observing certain objects, and equally the images of these objects, would help the maternal body to internalize and transfer the qualities of those objects to her offspring. This practice became increasingly popular thanks to Ming imperial sponsorship and a booming print industry, which together spurred rapid commercialization and democratization of medicinal knowledge through visual imagery. Similar prescriptions also appear in later Ming pharmacopeias, such as those illustrated in the seminal sixteenth-century text Bencao gangmu (BCGM, Compendium of Materia Medica). Although art as prescription has rarely been noted by art historians, contemporary Chinese art has reactivated this inheritance. Works by artists such as Huang Yongping and Cai Guo-Qiang directly borrow from these early modern sources, applying their medicinal imaginations to new socio-political and cultural contexts. This project therefore takes a transhistorical approach to examine this early modern practice and its afterlife in contemporary art. Drawing extensively on primary sources such as medical treatises, nutritional manuals, encyclopedias, illustrated guides, and painting manuals, this project is comprised of three parts: 1) tracing and analyzing the discourse of art as prescription illustrated in YSZY along with other Ming-era canonical texts; 2) establishing a visual archive of paintings prescribed as medicine in these sources; 3) recontextualizing and analyzing this phenomenon as it appears in contemporary Chinese art in light of this long lineage of belief in the medicinal function of art. To do so, this project takes an interdisciplinary approach to reveal the medicinal meanings and values embedded in images and acts of visualization, shedding light on the enduring connections between Chinese medicine and visual art. 本研究考察在早期現代中國視覺文化中以圖像為藥方的實踐, 並主張這一實踐在當代中國藝術中具有持續的跨歷史影響。早在14世紀,飲食與營養手冊《飲膳正要》就已經記錄了以畫為藥的做法。此書原定於1330年成書,但僅以1456年明代刊本存世,書中生動地將"觀看"這一行為描繪為一種具身的調養方式,其中最為鮮明的例證,是若干幅描繪孕婦欣賞鯉魚、孔雀、鷹、玉等圖畫的插圖場景,並指出這些對腹中胎兒的種種效用，如聰慧、美貌與強健。這意味著觀看某些物象（同樣也包括這些物象的圖像）能夠幫助母體將這些物象的品質內化並傳遞給她的後代。由於明代皇室的讚助與蓬勃發展的印刷業,這一實踐日益盛行;二者共同推動了醫學知識經由視覺圖像而迅速商品化與大眾化。類似的藥方也出現在明代後期的本草著作中,例如16世紀具有奠基意義的《本草綱目》所附插圖之中。儘管這一現象鮮少受到藝術史學者的關注,當代中國藝術卻已重新激活了這份遺產。黃永砯、蔡國強等藝術家的作品借鑒這些早期文獻,並將其中的醫藥想像施用於新的社會政治與文化脈絡。因此,本研究採取跨歷史的視角,考察這一早期現代實踐及其在當代藝術中的餘緒。本研究廣泛依據醫學論著、營養手冊、類書、圖說指南與畫譜等第一手文獻,由三個部分組成: 1) 追溯並分析《飲膳正要》及其他明代經典文本中所呈現的以畫為藥的話語流轉; 2) 建立一份在這些文獻中被作為藥方開列的圖像的檔案; 3)在這一源遠流長的、關於圖像具有醫藥功能之信念的脈絡下,對當代中國藝術中出現的這一現象加以重新語境化與分析。為此,本研究採取跨學科的方法揭示圖像與觀看行為中所蘊含的含義與價值,從而闡明中國醫學與視覺藝術之間歷久彌新的關聯。

22606526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22606526.value: 公共交通站點步行範圍內的行人二氧化氮暴露預測

22606526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22606526.value: Background: Ambient nitrogen dioxide (NO2), largely from vehicular emissions, is a critical urban health challenge, with each 10 μg/m³ increase in annual NO2 exposure associated with a 12.7% rise in all-cause mortality. Among urban populations, pedestrians are uniquely vulnerable to NO2 exposure due to their proximity to traffic emissions without physical protection. This vulnerability intensifies in transit walksheds (areas around public transit stations), where concentrated pedestrian activity coincides with heterogeneous pollution patterns, creating potentially elevated exposure risks. Despite this critical nexus of mobility and health, existing research focuses on ambient concentrations or residential population-based exposure, overlooking the collective exposure burden experienced by pedestrians on urban sidewalks. Understanding the distribution of pedestrian exposure in transit walksheds is therefore essential for identifying priority hotspots and informing targeted interventions for public health protection. Objective and Methodology: This research aims to develop a methodological framework to estimate pedestrian-weighted exposure to nitrogen dioxide (PEND) in transit walksheds. Leveraging our expertise, the framework will integrate mobile sensing, computer vision, and graph-based deep learning for accurate exposure modeling. First, a mobile sensing workflow will collect fine-grained data on NO2 concentrations and pedestrian volumes, delivering PEND measurements across extensive spatial coverage at high resolution. Second, a hierarchical feature engineering pipeline will integrate predictors across multiple spatial and temporal scales, including features extracted from multi-modal data (e.g., 3D urban models, road network graphs), to capture overlooked exposure factors. Third, a graph-based deep learning model will predict sidewalk PEND by explicitly capturing spatial dependencies of pedestrian mobility and pollution dispersion across road networks. The framework will be applied in Shenzhen's Futian District across transit walksheds with diverse built environments. Impact: By advancing pedestrian-focused exposure assessment in transit walksheds, this research will reveal micro-scale exposure hotspots overlooked by conventional assessments and identify key determinants of PEND patterns. These findings will enable targeted interventions tailored to specific exposure mechanisms (e.g., pollution-driven or activity-driven), maximizing public health protection with efficient resource allocation. This research can also inform transit-oriented development (TOD) by guiding design strategies that reduce exposure risks while promoting walkability and urban vitality. The replicable framework can be adapted to similar regions, contributing to a new paradigm for pedestrian-centered planning that safeguards air quality and public health in transit environments.

22607526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22607526.value: 從地中海到珠江：19–20世紀希臘人的移民、海事網絡及其香港社群的形成

22607526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22607526.value: In the late nineteenth century, widespread economic hardship prompted many Greeks to seek opportunities abroad—a classic example of push-pull migration. While most European migrants set out for their colonies, the Greeks had to take a different path. In Hong Kong the Greeks built a distinct community among various ethnic groups, positioned between British rulers and the local Chinese. They fostered an identity that balanced integration and disintegration, assimilation and preservation, internationalism, and diasporic nationalism. Hong Kong’s stable business and political environment attracted Greek merchants from Greece, established diaspora regions, and even the Chinese mainland, where Greek communities were already present by the nineteenth century. The Greeks distinguished themselves among colonial ethnic groups due to their unique religious and cultural identity, situated between East and West. As a cosmopolitan trade diaspora, Greeks shared more similarities with Jewish or Armenian communities than with Western imperialists. Lacking support from a nation-state, they depended on close-knit kinship ties and familiar commercial norms to survive (Cohen, 2023). Most Greeks in Hong Kong worked as merchants, sailors, and business owners in Victoria (Central), thriving in spaces where intense commercial activity and cross-cultural interactions abounded, blurring ethnic distinctions and fostering a sense of belonging to the colony. Colonial capitalism provided minorities with economic opportunities while keeping them politically subordinate.
