For example, an HR business partner brings managers and staff together to co-design a new shift rota, but handles early misconduct reports in confidential one-to-ones until facts are established. Existing research, however, tends to view these brokers through a static lens (e.g., Burt, 2012; Soda et al., 2018): people are seen as naturally inclined either to keep parties apart (Separation brokerage; Burt, 1992) or to bring them together (Joining brokerage; Obstfeld, 2005). Prior research has compared the two orientations’ effects on performance (Soda et al., 2018) and innovation (Obstfeld, 2017), and examined their associations with burnout and abusive behavior (Lee et al., 2024). While this framework has offered useful insights, it overlooks a critical reality in organizational life: coordination needs shift from situation to situation (e.g., Kellogg, 2014; Lingo & O'Mahony, 2010), and the ability to adapt one’s approach accordingly may be just as important as the approach itself. To address that issue, the main purpose of this proposed research is to advance the social network literature by introducing and testing a novel concept of brokerage flexibility: the ability to read situational cues and switch brokerage behavior accordingly. We tackle three challenges: (1) Does brokerage flexibility predict higher individual performance above and beyond one's network position and preferred networking orientations? (2) Can flexibility reduce the common trust penalty faced by people in brokerage roles (e.g., Iorio, 2022)? (3) Where does this capability come from? Specifically, does working with a wider variety of counterpart roles cultivate it? We propose to conduct a three-wave longitudinal field study in a knowledge-intensive technology firm in Hangzhou, China. We have established access relationships with multiple local firms there. From them, we will select one where employees coordinate across functions or project squads and have discretion in how they manage work relationships. The research will substantially enrich organizational theory. It will also inform diagnostics and manager guides (e.g., when to separate vs. join), helping organizations design roles, rotate staff, and train leaders to coordinate adaptively across boundaries. 组织中越来越依赖那些能够跨越团队与职能边界、促成问题解决与工作推进的员工(Quintane et al., 2024)。这些"中间人"常常面临一个现实的两难:有时候正确的做法是让双方保持分离(例如为保护信息保密性,或维持观点的多样性);而在另一些情况下,正确的做法则是促成双方的联结(例如为了统一行动、协同执行)。举例来说,一位人力资源业务伙伴(HRBP)会召集经理与员工共同设计新的排班方案,但在处理早期的不当行为投诉时,却会通过保密的一对一沟通,直到事实查清为止。 然而,现有研究往往以一种静态视角看待这类中间人(如 Burt, 2012; Soda et al., 2018):要么将其视为天生倾向于让双方保持分离("分离型中间人"策略;Burt, 1992),要么天生倾向于促成双方联结("联结型中间人"策略;Obstfeld, 2005)。已有研究比较了这两种取向对绩效(Soda et al., 2018)与创新(Obstfeld, 2017)的影响,也探讨了它们与职业倦怠、恶意行为之间的关联(Lee et al., 2024)。这一框架虽有其价值,却忽视了组织生活中的一个关键现实:协调需求会因情境而不断变化(如 Kellogg, 2014; Lingo & O'Mahony, 2010),而能否根据情境灵活调整自己的中间人策略,或许与策略本身同样重要。 针对这一问题,本研究拟提出并检验一个全新概念——"关系调适力"(brokerage flexibility),即个体识别情境线索、并据此切换中间人行为方式的能力,以此推进社会网络领域的理论发展。具体而言,本研究拟回答三个问题:(1)在控制个体的网络位置与其固有的协调倾向后,关系调适力是否仍能预测更高的个人绩效?(2)调适力能否缓解身处中间人角色者普遍面临的"信任折损"问题(如 Iorio, 2022)?(3)这种能力从何而来?具体而言,与更多元的合作对象共事,是否有助于培养这种调适力?

25600226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25600226.value: 「抱團取暖」：中國欠發達地區殘障兒童家長的社會身份與積極適應

25600226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25600226.value: Globally, the prevalence of intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD) is 3.1%, with 80% of them living in the Global South contexts. In China’s economically disadvantaged areas (and many Global South contexts), family care is overwhelmingly drained as the default source of support for children with IDD (CwIDD), as formal and informal support is often compromised by inadequacies in social welfare and social stigma. It is hence critical to explore alternative forms of coping resources for these underserved families. The social identity approach to health literature suggests that meaningful social identification derived from social group connection can be a form of community-level coping resource that facilitates individuals’ adaptive growth following adversities. Inspired by the community’s rich self-help and mutual aid experiences in under-resource contexts, this study proposes a social identity model to family adaptation to examine the “social cure” potential of social identification derived from meaningful social connections with fellow parents of CwIDD in promoting positive adaptation. The study aims to develop a rich, contextualized, and rigorous understanding of the characteristics, socio-familial determinants, influence, and changing pathways of parents’ social identification in China’s economically disadvantaged areas. A community-engaged, three-phase explanatory sequential mixed-methods design is proposed. In Phase I, a quantitative study will examine the characteristics and socio-familial determinants of parents’ social identification, as well as the relationships among caregiving demands, social identification, and adaptation outcomes. To explain why and how social identification can be enacted as a collective coping resource and to inform service development, Phase II will conduct a qualitative constructivist grounded theory inquiry to theorize the pathways to parents’ social identity changes in the caregiving journey, focusing on the meanings, stages, triggers, and precipitating events of identity transformation. In Phase III, a co-production workshop will be organized to co-create a social identification-building service model. Partnership with three community partners will enhance the sustainable community benefits of the study. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to examine social identification as a community-level coping resource in the context of the family care of CwIDD. Academically, this study will contribute to the theoretical understanding of the social identity processes among socially stigmatized population. Practically, it will inform the development of a culturally competent social service intervention that is grounded in the community’s internal strengths and assets for underserved families in the Global South. 在全球範圍內，智力與發展性障礙的流行率為 3.1%，其中 80% 生活於全球南方地區。在中國的經濟欠發達地區以及許多全球南方社會中，由於社會福利體系的不足與社會污名化，正式與非正式社會支持往往難以獲得，家庭照顧無奈成為智力與發展性障礙兒童的唯一支持來源，導致家庭照顧者被極度消耗。因此，探索適合這些缺乏服務支援的家庭的替代性應對資源至關重要。 健康的社會身份理論指出，來源於社會群體連結的有意義的社會身份可能是一項社群層面的應對資源，能幫助面對困境的個人實現積極適應和成長。受到欠發達地區中家長社群豐富的自助與互助經驗啟發，本研究提出了一個「家庭適應的社會身份模型」，探討智力與發展性障礙兒童家長間透過建立良好社群連結所產生的社會身份，在促進家長的積極適應方面的「社會療癒」潛力。本研究旨在獲得對於中國經濟欠發達地區家長社會身份的特征、社會家庭決定因素、影響及其改變路徑的豐富、情景化及嚴謹的理解。 本社區參與式研究採納三階段解釋性順序混合方法設計。第一階段為量化研究，將探討家長社會身份的特徵與社會家庭決定因素，以及照顧負擔、社會身份與適應結果之間的關係。為了進一步解釋社會身份為何以及如何能轉化為社群應對資源，並為服務開發提供依據，第二階段將採用建構主義扎根理論進行質性研究，聚焦於家長社會身份轉變的意義、階段、觸發因素，建構家長在照顧歷程中社會身份轉變路徑的理論。第三階段將舉辦一個共創工作坊，與社群夥伴共同打造一個建立社會身份的服務模式。本研究透過與三個社群夥伴合作，將能提升本研究對社群的可持續效益。 據我們所知，這是首個將「社會身份」作為社群層面應對資源、並應用於智力與發展性障礙兒童家庭照顧情境的研究。在研究層面，本研究將有助於深化對受社會污名化群體之社會身份過程的理論理解；在實務層面，本研究將為全球南方缺乏資源的家庭，提供以社群內部優勢與資產為本、具備文化適應性的社會服務干預模式。

25602626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25602626.value: 線上癌症照顧者意義為本心理治療（MCP-C）對緩解中國晚期癌症患者照護者抑鬱症狀之療效：一項隨機對照試驗

25602626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25602626.value: Informal caregiving for advanced cancer patients is a global public health issue. Although sometimes valuable, long hours of caregiving are generally detrimental to the physical and psychological health of caregivers. Caregiving is complex and challenging, and associated with significant depression (42.3%), exceeding rates observed in other caregiver groups. Poor caregiver mental health could diminish care quality and negatively impact outcomes for care recipients. Current interventions have shown some effects on improving the mental well-being of caregivers of advanced cancer patients. However, these were not sustained over time, as the interventions did not address the root cause of persistent depression in this population—namely, existential distress. A culturally appropriate and novel Meaning-Centered Psychotherapy for Cancer Caregivers (MCP-C) was adapted for Chinese caregivers of patients with advanced cancer and pilot-tested by our team. The feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary effects of the MCP-C have been confirmed. A potential intervention mechanism on meaning in caregiving and positive appraisal of caregiving were supported by a theoretical model and pilot study, but have not been fully explored. The proposed two-arm randomized controlled with a sequential mixed-methods design will examine the effects of an online Chinese MCP-C on depressive symptoms and health-related outcomes. One hundred and fifty caregivers will be randomized to receive 7 weekly online MCP-C sessions delivered by trained interventionists or dosage-matched online psychoeducation sessions as the active control. Outcome measures include depressive symptoms (primary outcome), anxiety, meaning in caregiving, caregiver appraisal, spiritual well-being, and benefit finding. A linear mixed-effects model will be used to compare the effects of the intervention immediately post-intervention (T1) and at the 3-month follow-up (T2). Both quantitative (path analysis) and qualitative methods (semi-structured individual interviews) will be used to explore the mechanism of change. It is hypothesized that the MCP-C participants will experience significantly greater improvements in depressive symptoms and in several secondary outcomes at T1 and T2. Caregivers will experience enhanced meaning in caregiving and positive appraisal of caregiving. The changes in meaning in caregiving and positive appraisal of caregiving will mediate the effects of the MCP-C on caregiver depressive symptoms. This culturally appropriate and novel approach can be adopted by community mental healthcare services, incorporated into online caregiver support services in Hong Kong, and replicated in other Asian populations in other countries, to improve the mental health of informal caregivers of advanced cancer patients, which in turn will benefit the patients’ quality of care. 對晚期癌症患者的非正式照顧是一項全球公共衛生議題。儘管照顧有時可帶來價值感，但長時間的照顧工作一般會損害照顧者的身心健康。照顧工作既複雜又具挑戰性，並與顯著的抑鬱症狀（42.3%）相關，其發生率已超越其他照護群體之報告數值。照顧者心理健康不佳，可能降低照顧品質，並對被照顧者的預後產生負面影響。現有干預措施對改善晚期癌症患者照顧者的心理健康雖具若干成效，但成效未能長期維持，原因在於這些干預措施並未針對該群體持續性抑鬱的根本原因——即存在性困擾。 本研究團隊針對中國晚期癌症患者之照護者，改編了一種符合文化背景且嶄新的「癌症照顧者意義為本心理治療」（MCP-C），並進行先導測試。MCP-C的可行性、可接受性及初步成效已獲確認。理論模型與先導研究均支持該療法在「照護意義」及「照護的正向評價」方面可能發揮的介入機制，但相關機制尚未被充分探討。 本研究擬採用雙組隨機對照試驗，結合序貫混合方法設計，以探討線上中文版MCP-C對抑鬱症狀及健康相關結果的成效。將有一百五十名照護者被隨機分組，一組接受由受過訓練的干預人員進行的 7 週線上 MCP-C 課程，另一組則接受劑量匹配的線上心理教育課程作為積極對照組。結果測量指標包括抑鬱症狀（主要結果）、焦慮、照顧意義、照顧評價、靈性安康及獲益感。本研究將採用線性混合效應模型，比較介入後即時（T1）及三個月追蹤（T2）之效果。本研究亦會同時採用量化方法（路徑分析）及質性方法（半結構式個別訪談），以探討改變機制。本研究假設，MCP-C組參加者於T1及T2的抑鬱症狀及多項次要結果，將有顯著較佳的改善。照顧者的照顧意義及對照顧的正面評價將有所提升；而照顧意義及對照顧的正面評價之變化，將中介MCP-C對照顧者抑鬱症狀的影響。 這項切合文化背景且嶄新的方法可供社區心理健康服務機構採用，並可納入香港的線上照顧者支援服務體系，亦可推展至其他國家的亞洲族群，藉此改善晚期癌症患者非正式照顧者的心理健康，從而提升患者所獲得的照護品質。

25605826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25605826.value: 香港印度尼西亞外籍家庭傭工的跨國敘事網絡與健康話語研究

25605826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25605826.value: Hong Kong employs over 367,000 migrant domestic workers (MDWs), mostly from Indonesia and the Philippines, who provide indispensable care and household labour. Yet despite their centrality to the city’s economy and households, MDWs face disproportionate health vulnerabilities. Indonesian MDWs, in particular, encounter restrictive employment structures, limited healthcare access, and linguistic barriers that render them “information poor,” especially concerning health. In the absence of equitable institutional support, MDWs turn to transnational storytelling agents: interpersonal ties, community organisations, and media outlets across Hong Kong and Indonesia that circulate health-related discourses. These networks provide solidarity and information, yet they also expose workers to misinformation and harmful practices. Hence, understanding what these discourses are, how MDWs evaluate the reliability of these agents and their discourses, and how such evaluations influence their everyday health practices, is particularly important. Guided by the frameworks of migration linguistics and communication infrastructure theory (CIT), this study examines three interrelated dimensions: (1) the storytelling agents across Hong Kong and Indonesia in migrants’ networks, (2) health discourses within these networks, and (3) how MDWs evaluate the quality of both agents and discourses, and how these evaluations shape their health experiences. The interdisciplinary and intersectoral team will employ a sequential mixed-methods design, combining a cross-sectional survey with in-depth interviews. Phase 1 involves a survey of 300 Indonesian MDWs to map their storytelling agents, information needs, structural conditions, language repertoires, and health outcomes. Phase 2 consists of narrative interviews with 40 participants, allowing for a discourse analysis of how health narratives are constructed, assessed, and enacted. Thematic analysis combined with analysis of stance-taking will illuminate how migrants evaluate health information, position themselves within networks, and align with or resist particular sources of advice. Theoretically, the project contributes significantly to the development of CIT, which has long been used to analyse (im)migrant consumption of health information. More specifically, by gathering empirical data related to migrants’ evaluations of storytelling networks and using discourse analytic tools to analyse the stories themselves, this research illuminates how CIT can be used, not only to understand the links between different agents, but to demonstrate the actual impact these links have on the lives and health of marginalised migrants. Practically, it informs best practices for the development of health communication programmes targeting migrant communities, especially regarding the effective delivery of health messages and the use of effective communication channels to disseminate health information. 香港現有逾 36.7 萬名外籍家庭傭工，主要來源為印尼與菲律賓，該群體承擔著不可或缺的照護與家務勞動。然而，儘管外籍家庭傭工對香港的經濟與家庭運作至關重要，她們仍面臨較高的健康風險。印度尼西亞外籍家庭傭工處境尤為嚴峻，限制性僱傭制度、醫療資源取得受限與語言障礙導致其資訊匱乏，此問題在健康議題上尤為突出。 由於缺乏公平的制度性支持，外籍家庭傭工轉向多元跨國敘事載體，包括香港與印尼兩地的人際網絡、社區組織及媒體平台，藉此獲取各類健康資訊。這些網絡在提供社群互助與資訊的同時，也會將她們暴露於錯誤資訊與有害行為之中。因此，理解此類話語內容，外籍家庭傭工如何評估這些敘事載體及其話語的可信度，以及該類評估如何影響其日常健康實踐，尤為重要。 在移民語言學與傳播基礎設施理論的框架指引下，本研究探討三個相互關聯的維度：(1) 移民網絡中分佈於香港和印尼的敘事載體 (2) 這些網絡中的健康相關話語 (3) 外籍家庭傭工如何評估這些敘事載體和話語的質量，以及這些評估如何塑造其健康體驗。這支跨學科與跨部門的研究團隊將採用序列混合方法設計，把橫斷面問卷調查和深度訪談相結合。第一階段對 300 名印尼外籍家庭傭工進行問卷調查，以梳理其敘事載體、資訊需求、結構性處境、語言資源與健康結果。第二階段對 40 名參與者開展敘事訪談，藉此對其健康敘事的建構、評估及踐行進行話語分析。將主題分析與立場表述分析相結合，可闡明移民如何評估健康資訊，在網絡之中定位自我，以及認同或抵觸特定建議來源。 理論層面上，本研究對傳播基礎設施理論的發展具有重要貢獻，該理論長期以來被用於分析移民對健康資訊的取用行為。具體而言，透過收集移民對敘事網絡評估的實證數據，並運用話語分析工具剖析敘事文本本身，本研究闡明傳播基礎設施理論不僅可用於理解不同敘事載體之間的關聯，還能夠揭示此類關聯對邊緣化移民的生活與健康所產生的實際影響。實務層面上，本研究可為面向移民社群的健康傳播項目的制訂提供最具實踐性的參考，尤其是關於健康資訊的有效傳遞，以及透過合適傳播渠道予以發布。

25616226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25616226.value: 針對睡眠與晝夜節律紊亂以減輕中風後抑鬱症狀：隨機對照試驗

25616226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25616226.value: Post-stroke depression (PSD) affects approximately 33% of stroke survivors, over twice the rate observed in age-matched adults without stroke (13%). PSD is strongly associated with a higher recurrence rate, increased mortality, and reduced quality of life. Affecting over half of stroke survivors, sleep and circadian disturbance represents a key modifiable contributor to PSD that predicts depressive symptoms and often remains as a residual problem after depression treatments, increasing relapse risk. Existing sleep interventions, such as cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia (CBT-I), demonstrate reduced efficacy in stroke populations. Our qualitative work highlights that the distinct and multifaceted nature of post-stroke sleep and circadian disturbances precludes easy alignment with disorder-focused sleep interventions. To address this gap, we developed a transdiagnostic intervention targeting shared behavioural mechanisms across diverse sleep and circadian disturbance in stroke survivors, guided by the National Institutes of Health’s Stage Model for Behavioural Intervention Development. The intervention integrates evidence-based approaches: CBT-I (stimulus control, sleep restriction, and cognitive strategies), chronotherapy (regularisation of sleep–wake timing and other non-photic zeitgebers), behavioural activation (scheduling and self-monitoring of meaningful daytime activity), and self-determination theory (enhancing self-determined motivation). The intervention is delivered over six weeks via modular-format 1-hour sessions comprising cross-cutting, core, and optional modules. Pilot data provide preliminary support for the hypothesized target engagement. Depressed stroke survivors who received the intervention showed reduced depressive symptoms and sleep disturbances, increased engagement in actigraphy-measured daytime activities, and improved circadian alignment, indexed by the dim light melatonin onset (DLMO)-to-bedtime phase angle. To confirm the intervention’s efficacy and the antidepressant mechanism, we propose an assessor-blinded, two-arm randomised controlled trial involving 118 community-dwelling stroke survivors with clinically significant depressive symptoms and sleep and circadian disturbance. The participants will be randomly assigned (1:1) to the intervention or an attention-matched control, with assessments conducted at baseline, post-intervention, and a three-month follow-up. The primary outcome is depressive symptom severity. Secondary outcomes include subjective and objective circadian and sleep metrics from questionnaires, actigraphy, and sleep diaries, and biological circadian phase measured by DLMO. The analyses will follow intention-to-treat linear mixed models for efficacy and mediation models to examine the antidepressant mechanism. If effective, this intervention will provide a cost-efficient and low-stigma approach for reducing PSD by addressing the often-overlooked domain of sleep and circadian health.

25616526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25616526.value: 殘疾人士路口通行安全的理解與強化研究

25616526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25616526.value: Disability has become a prominent global social issue, with an estimated 1.3 billion people worldwide experiencing significant disabilities, including over 534,200 in Hong Kong. For many people with disabilities, walking with or without aids and wheelchair use are essential for daily mobility, providing a means to access destinations and serving as a first- and last-mile connection to public transport. However, these activities often require crossing roads, which presents significant safety concerns that can discourage people from leaving their homes. Pedestrian crossings are particularly hazardous, accounting for nearly one-third of all injury-related traffic collisions in Hong Kong. International research confirms that disabled pedestrians face disproportionately high risks, which transforms a routine activity into a dangerous obstacle course and a barrier to independent living. Although Hong Kong has established policies and design manuals to promote barrier-free access, their implementation is inconsistent. Empirical studies indicate that existing interventions are often ineffective, yet the prevalence and nature of the safety concerns faced by disabled pedestrians at road crossings remain poorly understood. This project addresses this gap by developing a novel, human-centred, and AI-powered framework to systematically assess and improve the safety of road crossings for people with disabilities, focusing on Hong Kong's two most prevalent impairments: visual and mobility impairments. The research is structured around three core objectives. First, working closely with 40 participants (20 for each impairment group), it will utilise multiple qualitative approaches, such as video diaries, go-along interviews, and in-depth interviews, to explore their lived experiences. This aims to identify the specific physical, social, and environmental barriers they encounter at different types of crossings, determine which factors facilitate or deter their mobility, and understand their design preferences for safer crossings. Second, building on these insights, this project will co-design potential interventions with participants and use advanced AI algorithms, such as controllable diffusion models, to propose actionable, context-sensitive design improvements. Finally, the project will integrate multiple geographic data sources to characterise the key features of road crossings that participants identify as concerning. By building upon the qualitative findings and integrating quantitative data sources, the research will develop a scalable, data-driven assessment tool. This tool will evaluate and map the inclusivity of road crossings across Hong Kong, visually identifying those that are unsafe or unsuitable. The outcome will be tangible, evidence-based improvements, fostering a safer and more equitable transport system for all. 殘疾已成為一項全球性的社會議題。據估計，全球約有13億人患有顯著殘疾，其中香港約有534,200人。對許多殘疾人士而言，無論是否借助輔助器具行走，或使用輪椅，均為日常出行的基本方式，既是直達目的地的手段，亦擔當連接公共交通系統的「首末一公里」角色。然而，此類活動往往需要橫過馬路，由此產生的安全隱患可能影響其出行意願。行人過路設施的風險尤为值得關注--香港近三分之一的傷害性交通碰撞事故發生於行人過路處。國際研究顯示，殘疾行人面臨的風險高於一般行人，對其獨立生活構成影響。儘管香港已制定相關政策及設計手冊以推動無障礙環境建設，惟執行層面存在不一致之處。實證研究指出，現有干預措施的成效常未達預期，而殘疾行人在過路時所面臨安全問題的普遍性與具體性質，至今仍有待深入探討。 為填補上述研究空白，本項目擬構建一套以人為本並結合人工智能技術的評估框架，用於系統性地評估與改善殘疾人士的過路安全，重點聚焦於香港最常見的兩類障礙--視障與行動障礙。本研究設有三項核心目標：第一，與40名參與者（每類障礙組別各20人）緊密協作，運用影片日記、伴行式訪談及深度訪談等多種定性方法，深入探究其真實生活體驗，旨在識別他們在不同類型過路設施中所面對的實體、社會及環境障礙，釐清促進或制約其出行的因素，並了解其對更安全過路設施的設計偏好。第二，在上述發現的基礎上，本項目將與參與者共同設計潛在的干預方案，並運用人工智能算法（如可控擴散模型），提出具體可行且因應情境的設計改進建議。第三，本項目將整合多項地理數據來源，系統性地分析參與者所關注的過路設施的關鍵特徵。在質性研究結果的基礎上，結合定量數據，本研究將開發一個可擴展且由數據驅動的評估工具。該工具可用於評估全港過路設施的包容性，並以視覺化方式標示不安全或不適宜的過路點。研究成果將轉化為基於實證的改善建議，推動構建一個更安全、更公平的交通體系。

25616926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25616926.value: 利用人工智慧驅動之計算設計平台提升數學建模成效：一項在香港中學的隨機對照試驗研究

25616926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25616926.value: Solving many problems in our world (e.g., wars, floods, climate change) requires mathematical modelling (MM) of real-world situations, but most students lack such skills. Only 9% of 15-year-old students can model complex situations (PISA, 2022). Although the Hong Kong Education Bureau introduced MM into the curriculum in 2017, many students do not understand MM, and teachers do not teach it effectively. Additionally, most current educational technologies primarily address fixed MM problems rather than supporting MM processes. Hence, we urgently need to construct a theoretical framework to guide MM learning and teaching. As computational design (CD) is closely aligned with MM, I enhanced a CD theoretical framework that blends design thinking, computational thinking, and mathematical modelling. Then, I used it to create a prototype of an AI-powered platform, CD2MM, to help learn MM. This platform will co-create teaching materials with teachers by converting real-world situations into different phases of MMs in both visual and analytical formats. Then, students will work on these materials to co-create models with multiple agents on CD2MM. This project has two stages. First, I will develop the CD2MM platform based on the current prototype by adding the main features of visual-logical scaffoldings and multi-agent studios. I will conduct eight rounds of agile development cycles involving feature development, rapid user testing, and collaborative evaluation to enhance the platform. Then I will conduct the feasibility study to test the CD2MM. Second, I will partner with the “Operation SoInno” program by Jockey Club Design Institute and local secondary schools for a field experiment. 300 junior secondary students from 12 classes across 3 schools will participate in a randomized controlled trial with pre- and post-tests conducted in the schools’ project-based learning courses. The classes will be randomly assigned to the CD2MM group or the traditional MM group. I will analyse their MM competency, self-efficacy, and experiences with multilevel linear models to evaluate the effectiveness of the CD2MM platform. I will further understand students’ epistemic patterns on the platform using ordered network analysis. This study will advance theory, practice, and policy in MM education. It will deliver (1) a CD theoretical framework for education, and (2) an evidence-based platform, CD2MM, to enhance MM education in Hong Kong’s secondary schools, with potential for global adoption. Our findings will benefit students, teachers, future employers, and educational policy makers by promoting creative mathematical education powered by AI at scale. 解決世界上許多問題（例如戰爭、洪水、氣候變遷）需要對真實情境進行數學建模（Mathematical Modelling， MM），但多數學生缺乏此類能力。根據 PISA（2022），僅有 9% 的 15 歲學生能夠建模複雜情境。雖然香港教育局自 2017 年起將數學建模納入課程，然多數學生仍不理解數學建模，教師在教學上亦未能有效落實。此外，現行教育科技多數僅支援固定的數學建模題型，而非整體的數學建模流程。因此，迫切需要建構一套理論框架以指導數學建模的學習與教學。鑑於“計算設計”（Computational Design，CD）與數學建模密切相關，我擴充並整合了一套 CD 理論框架，融合設計思維、計算思維與數學建模，並據此開發出以人工智慧驅動之原型平台 CD2MM，以協助數學建模學習。該平台將透過將真實情境轉換為可視與分析並存的不同建模階段，與教師協同共創教學資源；學生則在平台上以多代理方式共同建構模型。本研究計畫分兩階段進行。第一階段：我將在現有原型基礎上發展 CD2MM 平台，加入視覺—邏輯支架（visual–logical scaffoldings）與多代理工作室（multi-agent studios）等主要功能，並以八輪敏捷開發循環（包含功能開發、快速使用者測試與協同評估）強化平台，接著進行可行性研究以測試 CD2MM。第二階段：我將與賽馬會設計學院之“Operation SoInno”計畫及本地中學合作，進行實地實驗。研究將邀請來自 3 所學校、12 個班級之 300 名初中學生參與，以隨機對照試驗（RCT）方式於校內之專題式學習課程中進行前測與後測。各班級將被隨機分配至 CD2MM 組或傳統數學建模組。我將運用多層次線性模式分析學生之數學建模能力、自我效能及學習經驗，以評估 CD2MM 平台之成效；並透過有序網絡分析（ordered network analysis）進一步理解學生在平台上的知識認知模式。本研究將促進數學建模教育在理論、實務與政策層面的發展，並產出：（1）一套適用於教育場域之 CD 理論框架；（2）一個具實證基礎之 CD2MM 平台，以提升香港中學的數學建模教育，且具可擴展至國際之潛力。本研究成果將惠及學生、教師、未來雇主及教育決策者，推動以人工智慧大規模促進之創造性數學教育。

26100426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26100426.value: 黏附GPCR GPR125的結構與機制研究

26100426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26100426.value: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are crucial cell surface receptors in humans, mediating various physiological functions and serving as key drug targets (1,2). Adhesion GPCRs (aGPCRs) comprise a group of 33 receptors that remain among the least understood (3). Notably, there is limited knowledge regarding the ligands, three-dimensional structures, and physiological roles of aGPCRs (3). Among them, Subfamily III aGPCRs, including GPR123, GPR124, and GPR125, represent a group of receptors with essential regulatory functions and, yet untapped, translational potential (4). Loss of GPR125 in mice has been linked to obstructive azoospermia and vaginal malformations, underscoring its critical role in development (5,6). Interestingly, GPR125 is highly expressed in the central nervous system, yet its regulatory functions in neuronal development are largely unexplored (7). Additionally, there is currently no structural information available for its large extracellular domain, and the mechanisms underlying its signal transduction and regulatory functions remain to be elucidated. This proposal aims to address these knowledge gaps through a comprehensive investigation of GPR125. First, we will assess the effects of GPR125 deletion on neuronal development using a conditional GPR125 knockout mouse strain. We will evaluate the impact of GPR125 loss on axon and neurite growth, synapse formation, and synaptic transmission using a combination of morphological and electrophysiological techniques. Additionally, we will utilize human-induced neuronal cultures to analyze the effects of GPR125 on neuronal function, allowing us to draw parallels between mouse models and human neuronal development (8). Second, we will conduct GPCR signaling assays to investigate GPR125 activation mechanisms, focusing on G protein signaling pathways (9). Importantly, we will perform GPR125 rescue experiments using a GPR125-G protein null mutant to elucidate the regulatory function of GPR125-G protein interactions. Lastly, we will determine the structure of GPR125's extracellular domain using single-particle cryo-electron microscopy, which will facilitate ligand identification and enhance our understanding of receptor-ligand interactions. The successful completion of this project will enhance our understanding of GPR125's role in neuronal development, provide insights into its activation mechanisms, elucidate the relationship between G-protein signaling and regulatory functions, and offer direct structural visualization of GPR125. This research paves the way for future therapeutic strategies targeting this important aGPCR. G蛋白偶聯受體（GPCRs）是人體中至關重要的細胞表面受體，介導著各種生理功能，並作為臨床上關鍵的藥物標靶。黏附型G蛋白偶聯受體（aGPCRs）是其中一個家族，包含33個受體。關於aGPCRs的配體、三維結構，信號轉導及生理作用，目前的了解有限。其中，第三亞家族的aGPCRs，包括GPR123、GPR124和GPR125，是一類具有重要調節功能及潛在轉化應用價值的受體。GPR125在小鼠中的缺失與阻塞性無精症及陰道發育異常有關，這突顯了其在發育中的關鍵作用。有趣的是，GPR125在中樞神經系統中高表達，然而其在神經發育中的調節功能卻鮮有探究。此外，其細胞外結構域的結構信息，信號傳導及調節功能的機制也仍待闡明。 本提案旨在透過對GPR125的全面研究，來解決這些知識上的空白。首先，我們將利用條件性GPR125基因敲除小鼠品系，評估GPR125缺失對神經發育的影響。我們將結合形態學及電生理學技術，評估GPR125缺失對軸突與神經突生長、突觸形成及突觸傳導的調控作用。此外，我們將利用人類誘導神經元系統，分析GPR125對神經元功能的影響，以便在小鼠模型與人類神經發育之間建立關聯。其次，我們將進行GPCR信號傳導測定，以探究GPR125的激活機制，重點關注G蛋白信號傳導通路。重要的是，我們將進行GPR125挽救實驗，使用GPR125-G蛋白缺陷型突變體，以闡明G蛋白信號傳導的調節功能。最後，我們將利用單粒子低溫電子顯微鏡技術，確定GPR125細胞外結構域的結構，這將有助於配體識別並增進我們對受體-配體相互作用的理解。本研究的成功完成，將增進我們對GPR125在神經發育中作用的理解，提供其激活機制的見解，闡明G蛋白信號傳導與調節功能之間的關係，並提供GPR125的直接結構可視化。本研究為未來針對此重要aGPCR的治療策略鋪平道路。

26102826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26102826.value: CD4+ T細胞在肌萎縮側索硬化症中的作用

26102826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26102826.value: Neurological disorders represent one of the leading causes of disease burden worldwide. Among them, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a particularly devastating neurodegenerative disease characterized by the progressive loss of motor neurons in the spinal cord, leading to paralysis and death within a few years of onset. Despite decades of research, effective treatments remain elusive. The central nervous system (CNS) was once considered an immune-privileged organ, as the blood–brain barrier was thought to prevent infiltration by peripheral immune cells. Consequently, traditional studies on neurodegeneration have focused primarily on neuron-intrinsic mechanisms, such as protein aggregation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and oxidative stress. However, mounting evidence now indicates that the immune system plays an active and dynamic role in modulating disease onset and progression. T cells, the principal effectors of adaptive immunity, have recently been detected within the CNS in diverse pathological contexts, including CNS injury, Alzheimer’s disease and ALS. While CD8⁺ T cells are often associated with cytotoxic and pathogenic functions, the roles of CD4⁺ T cells in neurodegeneration remain poorly understood. In cancer immunology, CD4⁺ T cells have been shown to orchestrate a wide spectrum of responses, from supporting cytotoxic immunity to mediating tissue protection, depending on their activation state and cytokine profile. Our recent work in models of spinal cord injury revealed that distinct subsets of CD4⁺ T cells can exert either neuroprotective or neurotoxic effects, and that engineering antigen-specific CD4⁺ T cells can promote functional recovery following CNS damage. Building on these findings, this proposal seeks to elucidate the multifaceted roles of CD4⁺ T cells in ALS. We will first define the phenotypic and transcriptional landscape of T cells across different stages of ALS progression, and then determine how antigen specificity influences CD4⁺ T cell recruitment, phenotype, and function, and last, identify and mechanistically validate the signaling pathways through which CD4⁺ T cells interact with CNS-resident cells to modulate neuroinflammation. Together, these studies will uncover how adaptive immune responses shape ALS pathogenesis and will provide mechanistic foundations for developing T cell based immunotherapies for ALS and related neurodegenerative diseases. 神經系統疾病是全球疾病負擔的主要來源之一。其中，肌萎縮側索硬化症（amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, ALS，俗稱漸凍症）是一種嚴重的神經退行性疾病，以脊髓運動神經元進行性丟失為主要特徵，最終導致癱瘓甚至死亡，目前仍缺乏有效治療手段。傳統觀點認為，中樞神經系統（central nervous system, CNS）具有“免疫豁免”特性，因此既往神經退行性疾病研究主要聚焦於神經元內在病理機制，包括蛋白聚集、線粒體功能障礙和氧化應激等。然而，越來越多的研究表明，免疫系統積極參與神經退行性疾病的發生與進展。 T細胞是適應性免疫的重要效應細胞。近年來研究發現，在中樞神經系統損傷、阿茲海默病及ALS等多種病理狀態下，T細胞可進入CNS並參與疾病進程。相比具有明確細胞毒性和潛在致病作用的CD8⁺ T細胞，CD4⁺ T細胞在神經退行性疾病中的功能尚未得到充分闡明。我們近期研究發現，在脊髓損傷模型中，不同CD4⁺ T細胞亞群可分別發揮神經保護或神經毒性作用；進一步通過工程化改造抗原特異性CD4⁺ T細胞，可有效促進CNS損傷後的功能恢復。 基於上述研究基礎，本項目擬系統解析CD4⁺ T細胞在ALS發生發展中的多重作用。首先，描繪ALS不同疾病階段T細胞的表型及轉錄特徵；其次，闡明抗原特異性如何影響CD4⁺ T細胞的募集、表型及功能；最後，鑑定並驗證CD4⁺ T細胞與CNS駐留細胞相互作用、調控神經炎症的關鍵信號通路。本研究將揭示適應性免疫應答調控ALS疾病進程的機制，並為開發針對ALS及相關神經退行性疾病的T細胞免疫治療策略提供理論和機制基礎。

26201126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26201126.value: 邁向可擴展垂直供電：用於大規模人工智能處理器的網格化可擴展供電架構與複合磁芯集成設計

26201126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26201126.value: Power delivery has become a critical bottleneck for next-generation artificial intelligence (AI) processors. As computational demand and chip size continue to increase, the required supply current is expected to exceed 3,000 A per chip, with transient slew rates above 10,000 A/µs. Conventional lateral power delivery, which routes current horizontally across the circuit board before reaching the chip, is now approaching its physical limits. Long current paths cause significant conduction losses, high parasitic impedance, and routing congestion that interfere with high-speed signal channels. To sustain the continued scaling of AI processors, a paradigm shift toward vertical power delivery (VPD) is needed. By supplying current directly beneath the processor, VPD shortens the power path, reduces losses, and improves both power and signal integrity. However, realizing practical VPD still faces three major challenges that current research often overlooks. First, large AI chips require hundreds of converter phases distributed across non-uniform load regions, leading to more severe current imbalance and thermal concentration. Second, the limited footprint beneath the processor demands extremely high power density (> 2 A/mm², including passives). While magnetic components occupy most of the converter volume, burst-like power profiles and peak currents impose stringent saturation and loss constraints, making it difficult to design compact and efficient magnetics. Third, the vertically embedded voltage regulators occupy space originally used for decoupling capacitors, resulting in greater voltage droop during fast load transients that can cause chip malfunction. Overcoming these challenges requires advances in circuit architecture, magnetic design, and control strategy. This project proposes a scalable, compact, and fast-response VPD system built on three key innovations: (1) A mesh-extendable hybrid switched-capacitor point-of-load (MESH-PoL) architecture that enables two-dimensional circuit extension and inherent current balancing to support AI chip scaling. Deep-cycled capacitors with marginal capacitance enhance compactness, guided by a systematic modeling framework to analyze multi-resonant LC dynamics; (2) A composite-core coupled magnetic design that integrates ferrite and alloy-powder layers, supported by a learning-based hysteresis model for accurate characterization of nonlinear behavior in the sub-saturated region; (3) A distributed and coordinated control strategy featuring decomposed control paths, low-latency loops, and AI-chip-aware feedforward control to suppress voltage droop under extreme transients. The completion of this project will establish a new foundation for scalable VPD in large-scale AI processors. The developed technologies will deepen understanding and provide modeling and design methodologies for massive PoL converter systems and high-density coupled magnetics, supporting the continued evolution of high-performance AI chips. 電源供應已成為下一代人工智能（AI）處理器發展的關鍵瓶頸。隨着計算需求與芯片尺寸持續增長，單顆芯片供電電流預計將超過3,000 A，瞬態電流變化率達10,000 A/µs以上。傳統水平供電需將電流沿電路板水平傳輸後再進入芯片，長供電路徑帶來導通損耗、寄生阻抗及佈線擁塞，並干擾高速信號通道。為支撐AI處理器持續擴展，供電架構亟需向垂直供電（Vertical Power Delivery, VPD）轉變。VPD從處理器正下方直接供電，可縮短供電路徑、降低損耗，並改善電源與信號完整性。 然而，在實際應用中實現VPD仍面臨三項關鍵挑戰：1）大尺寸AI芯片需要數百相變換器分佈於非均勻負載區域，易造成相間電流不均衡與局部熱集中；2）處理器下方空間有限，要求供電系統實現極高電流密度（>2 A/mm²，包括無源元件）。磁性元件佔據變換器大部分體積，而突發式功率需求與高峰值電流對磁芯飽和及損耗提出嚴苛要求；3）垂直嵌入的電壓調節器佔用去耦電容空間，會加劇快速負載瞬態下的電壓跌落，甚至造成芯片功能異常。解決上述挑戰，需要在電路架構、磁集成設計與控制策略三方面協同突破。 本項目將研究可擴展、高密度、快速響應的VPD系統，圍繞三項關鍵創新開展研究：1）【網格化可擴展供電架構】提出網格化可擴展混合開關電容負載點（Mesh-Extendable Hybrid Switched-Capacitor Point-of-Load, MESH-PoL）架構，支持二維擴展並利用內在均流特性支撐大尺寸AI芯片擴展；採用深度充放電與低電容量設計提升緊湊度，並建立建模框架分析大規模LC網絡的多諧振動態。2）【複合磁芯磁集成】提出融合鐵氧體與合金粉芯的複合磁芯耦合磁性元件，兼顧高頻低損耗與峰值電流承載能力；建立基於深度學習的磁滯模型，準確表徵亞飽和區域的非線性特性，支撐複合磁芯磁集成建模與優化。3）【分佈式協同控制】提出面向大規模多相供電系統的分佈式協同控制策略，通過控制路徑分解、低延遲控制環路及AI芯片感知的前饋控制，抑制極端負載瞬態下的電壓跌落並提升動態性能。 本項目的完成將為大尺寸AI處理器的規模化可擴展垂直供電建立新基礎。所研究的電路架構、磁集成與控制技術將建立大規模PoL變換器系統及高密度耦合磁性元件的建模、分析與設計方法，為高性能AI芯片持續發展提供關鍵供電技術支撐。

26202326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26202326.value: 強化學習的理論基礎：基於模型方法與無模型方法的權衡

26202326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26202326.value: This proposal is dedicated to advance the theoretical foundations of reinforcement learning (RL). Due to its flexibility, RL has been adopted to solve a wide range of significant real-world problems, such as robotics, healthcare, game playing and large language models. RL algorithms are primarily developed within the Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework and can be broadly divided into two paradigms. Model-based approaches learn a policy by first estimating the underlying MDP dynamics from samples. This typically requires storing an estimated transition model, which often leads to high space complexity. In contrast, model-free methods directly learn a value function or policy without explicitly reconstructing the environment model. Consequently, they are typically more memory-efficient and amenable to function approximation, but often require more samples to learn effectively. This dichotomy naturally raises the question of a fundamental trade-off between memory efficiency and sample efficiency. A central open question is whether an intrinsic performance gap exists between these paradigms, which the PI will investigate across multiple problem settings. This proposal aims to deliver unique insights and a novel methodological toolkit for developing optimal reinforcement learning algorithms for both model-based algorithms and model-free ones. First, it will significantly advance our understanding of the trade-off between space complexity and sample complexity in reinforcement learning. To establish lower bounds that capture the fundamental difficulty imposed by memory limitations, the PI will connect RL problem instances to information theory and complexity theory. Success in this direction will yield a principled, information-theoretic framework to generate hard instances for reinforcement learning, demonstrating a powerful new application of complexity theory in machine learning theory. Second, this proposal will introduce new techniques for designing algorithms that are both statistically and computationally efficient. The PI plans to adapt techniques from information theory—including posterior analysis, graphical model, and divergence analysis—to develop sample- and computation-efficient RL methods. The success of this approach will substantially expand the toolbox available to RL researchers, with broad applicability beyond the specific problems considered here. Ultimately, by deriving tighter upper and lower bounds on sample complexity, this work will provide a clear characterization of the statistical limits of reinforcement learning, offering practical insights for selecting the most appropriate algorithms in real-world applications.

26204426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26204426.value: 利用视频视频生成模型实现通用的机器人控制

26204426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26204426.value: Robotic intelligence and manipulation are among the core challenges for deploying AI in the physical world. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) have led to video-language-action (VLA) models that bridge perception and action. However, these approaches rely heavily on massive, labor-intensive video–language–action pairs, making them difficult to scale. Moreover, current VLA models are predominantly reactive and imitation-driven, with limited modeling of future dynamics or long-horizon reasoning, resulting in poor generalization. To address these limitations, we propose a new paradigm that builds video generative models as a dynamic interface for generalist robotic manipulation. Instead of directly predicting actions from input images, our approach learns to simulate 4D future dynamics through video synthesis. This formulation unifies video generation and policy learning within a single generative framework, transforming the conventional VLA pipeline. The proposed framework introduces three key innovations: 1) Geometry Perception. A general geometry perception module that infers accurate and smooth 3D structures from RGB or RGB-D inputs. It leverages video diffusion models as strong priors to unify geometry reconstruction across modalities, providing a 3D foundation for manipulation. 2) 4D Dynamics Modeling. An autoregressive 4D video generative model that maintains strict 3D consistency under complex, long-horizon scenarios, enabling robust simulation and world modeling for robot control. 3) Unified Video–Action Learning. A joint framework that pretrains the generative model to estimate flow as a proxy for action supervision, followed by fine-tuning for action prediction. This design greatly reduces reliance on costly action-labeled data and enhances data efficiency. Overall, our approach addresses three fundamental weaknesses of existing generalist robot control systems: the lack of 3D awareness (causing inaccurate actions), limited foresight (leading to unstable long-horizon control), and high data dependence (hindering generalization). We will benchmark the proposed system against existing ad-hoc methods in both simulation and real-world robotic environments, and open-source our models to benefit the computer vision and robotics communities. 机器人智能与操作是人工智能在物理世界落地的核心挑战之一。近年来，大语言模型与视觉语言模型的进展催生了打通感知与动作的视觉-语言-动作模型。然而，这类方法严重依赖大规模、高人力成本的视频、语言与动作配对数据，难以规模化。此外，现有视觉-语言-动作模型大多是反应式、模仿驱动的，对未来动态与长时程推理的建模能力有限，导致泛化性能不佳。 针对上述局限，我们提出一种新范式：将视频生成模型构建为通用机器人操作的动态接口。不同于从输入图像直接预测动作，我们的方法通过视频合成来学习模拟四维未来动态。这一表述将视频生成与策略学习统一在单一生成式框架之内，重塑了传统的视觉-语言-动作流水线。 该框架包含三项关键创新： 一、几何感知。一个通用几何感知模块，可从彩色或彩色加深度输入中推断准确且平滑的三维结构。它利用视频扩散模型作为强先验，统一了跨模态的几何重建，为操作任务提供三维基础。 二、四维动态建模。一个自回归的四维视频生成模型，在复杂、长时程场景下保持严格的三维一致性，为机器人控制提供鲁棒的模拟与世界建模能力。 三、统一的视频-动作学习。一个联合框架：先以光流估计作为动作监督的代理任务对生成模型进行预训练，再针对动作预测进行微调。该设计大幅降低了对昂贵动作标注数据的依赖，提升了数据效率。 总体而言，我们的方法针对现有通用机器人控制系统的三个根本性弱点：缺乏三维感知，导致动作不精确；缺乏前瞻能力，导致长时程控制不稳定；以及高度依赖数据，阻碍泛化。我们将在仿真与真实机器人环境中，将所提系统与现有的专用方法进行基准对比，并开源我们的模型，以惠及计算机视觉与机器人学社区。

26205226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26205226.value: 從診所到家庭：運用多模態感知與大語言模型支援自閉症兒童照顧者進行居家干預

26205226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26205226.value: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition characterized by impairments in communication and social interaction alongside restricted and repetitive behaviors. ASD is increasingly prevalent worldwide; in Hong Kong, 2.57% of youth are affected. For children diagnosed with ASD, caregiver-delivered early intervention is effective, but implementation still largely relies on clinician supervision. At home, caregivers often struggle to identify and respond to intervention-worthy moments, leading to increased caregiver stress. Existing research largely focuses on children, overlooking caregiver stress that critically affects long-term outcomes. These realities motivate a shift in autism intervention from clinic to home with in-the-moment assistance for caregivers. This project proposes ASDLens, a caregiver-centric multimodal AI platform that supports caregivers in delivering just-in-time, clinically-grounded interventions during everyday routines (e.g., playtime and bedtime). The ASD home setting raises specific technical challenges: low tolerance for wearables among autistic children restricts sensor placement, and substantial motion during interactions makes robust signal capture challenging; privacy expectations at home demand on-device operation under tight computing budgets; scarce and heterogeneous ground-truth from experts for in-the-moment interventions constrains supervised adaptation of generative models. To overcome these challenges, the proposed research includes three tasks. Task 1 develops caregiver-worn smart glasses that capture conversational cues, dyadic behaviors (e.g., gaze, joint attention, posture), and physiology (e.g., heart rate and heart rate variability) through proposed vision-based algorithms, while keeping the child device-free. These signals, identified in our pilot study involving 63 families, are indicative of intervention-worthy moments. Task 2 builds an efficient fusion model that ingests sensing embeddings and operates on edge devices to detect and predict intervention-worthy moments, lowering privacy concerns. Task 3 proposes an ASD-specific large language model (LLM) trained with data-efficient learning algorithms on expert-annotated intervention corpora. When the detection model indicates a need, the LLM employs sensing embeddings as context to generate concise audio feedback as caregiver guidance, supplemented by post-session feedback to reinforce learning and confidence. Finally, in partnership with ASD experts, we will evaluate the platform with 70 families, assessing short-term gains in caregiver responsiveness, longer-term effects on child development, and caregiver confidence, using quantitative and qualitative measures. By combining unobtrusive egocentric sensing, efficient edge AI, and domain-tuned language models, ASDLens provides a home-based intervention pathway that reduces reliance on clinic-based care and enhances daily life for autistic children and their caregivers. While centered on ASD, the sensing-and-guidance framework is extensible to other neurodevelopmental conditions, enabling broader caregiver-mediated support at home. 自閉症譜系障礙（Autism Spectrum Disorder，ASD）是一種神經發展障礙，其主要特徵包括溝通及社交互動方面的困難，以及局限或重複的行為、興趣或活動模式。ASD 在香港和全球都日益普遍。對已確診 ASD 的兒童而言，早期干預已被證實有效，但目前的干預治療仍主要在醫院或診所，由臨床專業人員督導完成。在家庭環境中，照顧者往往難以及時辨識並適當回應一些值得干預的時刻，因而也承受很大的心理壓力。現有研究大多聚焦於兒童本身，較少關注會顯著影響干預治療長期效果的照顧者的壓力。因此，有必要將自閉症干預治療由診所延伸至家庭，並為照顧者提供即時、切合當下情境的干預治療指導。 本項目提出 ASDLens，一個以照顧者為中心的多模態人工智能平台，旨在為照顧者在家中提供及時且符合臨床原則的干預治療指導。自閉症居家照護場景帶來了多項獨特的技術挑戰：自閉症兒童對穿戴式裝置的接受度較低，限制了感測器的放置方式；家庭環境對私隱保障有較高要求，因此系統必須在有限的運算資源和能源條件下於裝置端本地運行。此外，專家針對當下干預所提供的標準標註數據既稀缺又具異質性，加大了對生成式模型的監督式調適難度。為克服上述挑戰，本研究包括三項任務。任務一將開發由照顧者佩戴的智能眼鏡，透過本項目提出的視覺感知算法，在毋須兒童佩戴任何裝置的情況下，擷取對話線索、照顧者與兒童的雙人互動行為以及心率和心率變異性等生理訊號。我們對 63 個家庭進行的先導研究顯示，這些訊號可反映值得干預的關鍵時刻。任務二將建立高效的多模態融合模型，以感知數據為輸入，在邊緣裝置上運行，以即時偵測及預測關鍵干預時刻，同時減少私隱方面的疑慮。任務三將利用數據高效學習算法，在由專家整理的干預語料庫上訓練自閉症專用大型語言模型。該模型將感知數據作為情境資訊，以簡潔的語音或視覺回饋形式向照顧者提供干預建議，並在每次互動結束後提供總結性回饋，以鞏固照顧者的學習並提升其信心。最後，我們將與自閉症專家合作，在現實家庭中評估此平台，結合定量與定性方法，評估照顧者回應能力的短期提升、兒童發展及照顧者信心所受到的長期影響，以及系統本身的準確性與可靠性。 雖然本研究以自閉症為核心，其感知與指導框架亦有潛力拓展至其他神經發展障礙，例如專注力不足／過度活躍症（ADHD），從而支援更廣泛、由照顧者主導的居家干預治療場景。

26205726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26205726.value: 實用的伺服器客戶端安全計算：以私隱資訊查詢為核心的方法

26205726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26205726.value: Modern digital infrastructure relies on server-client computation for tasks like database queries and AI inference, but current systems force clients to reveal sensitive data to servers, posing major privacy risks. Existing cryptographic solutions (e.g., garbled circuits, multi-party computation, homomorphic encryption) offer strong privacy but are too computationally intensive for practical use in general. This project explores a new secure computation paradigm based on private information retrieval (PIR), which lets clients access server data without revealing their queries. By splitting secure computation tasks into PIR-based memory access and lightweight cryptographic processing, this modular paradigm could overcome the efficiency limitations of traditional methods and enable practical privacy-preserving applications. Previously, PIR was considered too costly for real-world deployment. However, recent advances led by the PI and collaborators (Eurocrypt 2023-2025, IEEE S&P 2024, 2026) have made preprocessing-based PIR (Corrigan-Gibbs and Kogan 2022) nearly 1000x more efficient, enabling near real-time retrieval after the preprocessing phase. This creates a unique new opportunity and a solid foundation to explore the new secure computation paradigm. As an initial demonstration of this paradigm's potential, the PI designed a privacy-preserving vector search solution (ICLR 2025) within this paradigm that achieves industry-grade accuracy (90%+ recall@10) and sub-2-second queries on 100M-scale databases, opening up new use cases like private legal and biomedical search. Several challenges remain before this paradigm can see widespread adoption. Although recent works continue to improve the efficiency of the PIR primitive (e.g., Ren et al. CCS 2024, Nguyen et al. PETS 2025), current schemes still face high preprocessing costs, significant client storage requirements, and lack key features like dynamic updates and private access control. Moreover, system- and hardware-level integration is still largely unexplored, with a concrete blueprint for real-world applications yet to be developed. This project aims to close the gaps by developing fundamental algorithmic improvements in the PIR building block and system/hardware integration for industry-grade performance. We expect to produce high-quality academic publications in top-tier security and cryptography conferences and also release open-source libraries for practitioners. The project will also investigate real-world use cases, including a full-fledged private vector database system and a private AI inference pipeline. Two PhD students will be recruited and trained over the course of the project. With a strong track record of high-impact research and the demonstrated promise of this approach, the project is well-positioned to deliver both academic results with broad commercial and societal impact. 現代數碼基礎設施廣泛依賴伺服器—客戶端計算，以執行資料庫查詢及人工智能推理等任務。然而，現有系統往往要求客戶端向伺服器披露敏感資料，帶來重大的私隱風險。現有密碼學方案（例如混淆電路、多方安全計算及同態加密）雖然能提供強大的私隱保障，但其計算成本過高，難以廣泛應用於實際場景。 本項目將探索一種以私隱資訊檢索（Private Information Retrieval，PIR）為基礎的新型安全計算範式。PIR 允許客戶端在不洩露查詢內容的情況下存取伺服器資料。透過將安全計算任務分解為以 PIR 為基礎的記憶體存取，以及輕量級的密碼學處理，這種模組化範式有望突破傳統方法的效率限制，實現具實用性的私隱保護應用。 過往，PIR 一直被認為成本過高，難以在現實環境中部署。然而，項目負責人及其合作者近年取得的一系列進展（Eurocrypt 2023–2025、IEEE S&P 2024、2026），已將由 Corrigan-Gibbs 和 Kogan（2022）提出、以預處理為基礎的 PIR 效率提升近 1,000 倍，使系統能在完成預處理後實現近乎即時的資料檢索。這些成果帶來了獨特的新機遇，亦為探索上述安全計算範式奠定了堅實基礎。 作為展示此範式潛力的初步成果，項目負責人已按照這一思路設計了一套私隱保護向量搜尋方案（ICLR 2025）。該方案能在一億規模的資料庫上達到產業級準確度（Recall@10 超過 90%），並將單次查詢時間控制在兩秒以內，為私隱法律文件搜尋及生物醫學搜尋等新應用開拓了可能性。 然而，要推動此範式的廣泛應用，仍有多項挑戰尚待解決。儘管近期研究持續提升 PIR 基礎元件的效率（例如 Ren 等人，CCS 2024；Nguyen 等人，PETS 2025），現有方案仍面對預處理成本高、客戶端儲存需求龐大，以及缺乏動態更新和私密存取控制等關鍵功能的問題。此外，系統及硬件層面的整合仍未得到充分探索，亦尚未形成可供實際應用採用的具體技術藍圖。 本項目旨在填補上述研究缺口：一方面，從基礎演算法層面改進 PIR 核心元件；另一方面，推動系統與硬件整合，以達到產業級效能。我們預期在頂尖資訊保安及密碼學會議發表高質素學術成果，並推出開源軟件庫供研究人員及業界使用。本項目亦將探索具體的現實應用，包括構建一套功能完整的私密向量資料庫系統，以及一條私隱保護人工智能推理流程。項目期間將招募並培訓兩名博士研究生。 項目負責人在高影響力研究方面具有優秀的往績，以及此技術路線目前所展現的潛力，本項目具備良好基礎，有望同時產出重要的學術成果，並帶來廣泛的商業及社會影響。

26207426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26207426.value: 廢棄物轉製資源：以納濾技術實現廢鋰電池中鋰的高效回收與再利用

26207426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26207426.value: With the rapid expansion of lithium-ion battery (LIB) usage in mobile electronics, electric vehicles, and renewable energy storage, the improper disposal of spent LIBs poses serious environmental and resource challenges. Efficient lithium recovery from spent LIBs is essential for advancing circular resource management and reducing reliance on landfilling. In recent years, nanofiltration (NF)-based lithium-ion (Li⁺) recovery has emerged as a promising and cost-effective strategy. However, current NF systems and membranes face critical limitations: (1) insufficient mechanistic understanding of Li⁺ transport and lack of system-level modeling; (2) poor acid tolerance of commercially available NF membranes; and (3) degraded separation performance under high feed salinity. These issues result in low Li⁺ selectivity and poor recovery efficiency. In our recent study published in April 2025, we developed the first rigorous system-scale model for NF-based Li⁺ recovery and identified the key mechanism behind negative Li⁺ rejection. This work revealed how intrinsic membrane properties influence Li⁺ purity and system stability. Building on this framework, the proposed project will aim to develop a systematic approach to address deficiencies in Li⁺ purity and recovery. Our strategy will involve three key steps: (1) establishing a comprehensive modeling framework for NF systems, (2) synthesizing acid-tolerant NF membranes, and (3) fine-tuning membrane properties to optimize performance under high salinity conditions. By leveraging the newly identified mechanism of negative Li⁺ rejection and enhancing membrane acid tolerance, both Li⁺ purity and recovery can be significantly improved. The project will integrate advanced modeling, membrane fabrication, and performance optimization to achieve a holistic enhancement of Li⁺ extraction efficiency. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will be employed to investigate ion–membrane interactions at the molecular level. For the first time, an analytical model will be developed to establish a benchmark for NF-based lithium recovery from spent LIB. By simultaneously improving Li⁺ product purity and reducing energy consumption, the proposed project has the potential to enable sustainable lithium recycling in Hong Kong and other regions facing lithium supply constraints. The novel NF system and membranes developed are expected to achieve over 98% Li⁺ purity and over 90% recovery, with a projected 50%-80% reduction in energy consumption. Moreover, the acid in the leachate can be recycled as a sustainable leaching agent, marking a breakthrough in NF-based lithium recovery technology. 隨著鋰離子電池在電子產品、電動車及再生能源儲能系統中的快速普及，廢舊鋰離子電池處置不當所帶來的環境污染與資源浪費問題日益嚴重。高效回收廢舊鋰離子電池中的鋰資源，對推動循環經濟及降低對掩埋處理的依賴至關重要。近年來，基於納濾（NF）的鋰離子回收技術因具備高效率及低成本潛力而受到廣泛關注。然而，現有NF系統與膜材料仍面臨三項關鍵挑戰：(1) 對鋰離子傳輸機制缺乏深入理解，且缺少系統層級的模型分析；(2) 商業NF膜的耐酸性不足；以及 (3) 在高鹽度進料條件下分離性能顯著下降。這些問題導致鋰離子選擇性較低，回收效率受限。在我們於2025年4月發表的最新研究中，首次建立了適用於NF鋰回收的系統尺度模型，並揭示了鋰離子負截留現象背後的關鍵機制。該研究闡明了膜本徵特性如何影響鋰產品純度與系統穩定性。基於此研究基礎，本計畫旨在建立一套系統化策略，以解決目前鋰純度及回收率不足的問題。項目包含三個相互關聯的工作包：(1) 建立完整的NF系統模擬與分析框架；(2) 開發具優異耐酸性的NF膜材料；以及 (3) 精準調控膜性質，以提升其在高鹽度環境下的分離效能。透過運用新發現的鋰離子負截留機制並提升膜耐酸性能，可望同步提高Li⁺產品純度與回收率。本計畫將整合系統建模、膜材料製備及性能優化等研究內容，全面提升鋰回收效率。此外，研究團隊亦將利用分子動力學模擬深入探討離子與膜之間的分子尺度作用機制，並首次建立解析模型，作為廢舊鋰離子電池鋰回收技術的理論基準。通過同時提升鋰產品純度並降低能耗，本研究有望為香港及其他面臨鋰資源供應壓力的地區提供可持續的鋰循環利用方案。預期所開發的新型NF系統與膜材料可實現超過98%的鋰純度及超過90%的鋰回收率，同時將能耗降低50%至80%。此外，浸出液中的酸亦可循環再利用作為永續浸出劑，為基於NF技術的鋰回收領域帶來突破性進展。

26207926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26207926.value: 具有確定性約束隨機最佳化問題的新型增廣拉格朗日方法

26207926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26207926.value: Stochastic optimization provides a powerful mathematical framework for decision-making under uncertainty and plays a central role in modern applications such as machine learning, power systems, and data-driven engineering. Despite significant theoretical and computational progress, existing stochastic optimization algorithms remain fundamentally limited in their ability to handle deterministic constraints. Most existing methods enforce feasibility only in expectation, meaning that they can still be significantly violated in individual realizations. This limitation is critical in many real-world applications where constraints encode essential safety, reliability, or ethical requirements that must be satisfied with certainty. This project aims to overcome these limitations by developing a novel class of stochastic optimization algorithms that ensure deterministic or almost sure feasibility guarantees. Achieving this goal presents substantial challenges due to the need to manage stochastic noise while rigorously maintaining feasibility throughout the optimization process. The proposed research builds upon recent theoretical advances by the applicant and introduces a novel stochastic augmented Lagrangian (AL) framework that integrates efficient single-loop algorithmic structures with advanced variance-reduction techniques. This framework explicitly separates the stochastic and deterministic components of the problem, enabling the development of algorithms with provable convergence and improved computational complexity for finding approximate solution with strong convergence guarantee. The project will establish the theoretical foundations of the proposed methods and extend them to practical settings involving hybrid deterministic–stochastic constraints and heavy-tailed noise distributions. In particular, scalable and implementable algorithmic variants will be developed, together with efficient implementations tailored for large-scale constrained stochastic optimization problems. The performance of these algorithms will be systematically evaluated through extensive numerical experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets. The anticipated outcomes of this research include new theoretical insights into constrained stochastic optimization, the development of algorithms with state-of-the-art complexity guarantees while ensuring strong feasibility guarantees, and practical tools that enhance the safety and reliability of stochastic decision-making systems. Ultimately, this work will bridge the gap between stochastic optimization algorithms and deterministic operational requirements, contributing to the advancement of optimization theory and its applications in engineering, data science, and artificial intelligence. 隨機最佳化為不確定性環境下的決策提供了一個強大的數學框架，並在現代應用中扮演核心角色，例如機器學習、電力系統以及資料驅動工程等領域。儘管隨機最佳化在理論與計算方面已取得顯著進展，現有的隨機最佳化演算法在處理確定性約束方面仍存在根本性的限制。大多數現有方法僅能在期望意義下維持可行性，這意味著在個別隨機實現中，約束條件仍可能出現嚴重違反的情況。此限制對許多實際應用而言至關重要，因為在這些場景中，約束條件往往代表必須確實滿足的安全性、可靠性或倫理要求。 本研究旨在克服上述限制，通過開發一類新型隨機最佳化演算法，確保確定性可行性或幾乎必然可行性的保證。實現此目標面臨重大挑戰：在最佳化過程中嚴格維持可行性的同時，有效處理隨機噪聲的影響。本研究將建立於申請人近期取得的理論成果之上，提出一種新型隨機增廣拉格朗日框架，將高效的單循環算法結構與先進的方差縮減技術相結合。該框架能夠明確分離問題中的隨機部分與確定性部分，從而設計具有可證明收斂性以及更優計算複雜度的演算法，用於尋找具備強收斂保證的近似解。 本計畫將建立所提出方法的理論基礎，並進一步將其拓展至包含混合確定性–隨機約束以及重尾噪聲分佈的實際情境。具體而言，本研究將開發具備可擴展性與可實現性的演算法變體，並針對大規模受約束隨機最佳化問題設計高效的實作方法。此外，將通過大量數值實驗，在合成資料集與真實世界資料集上系統性評估所提出演算法的效能。 本研究預期成果包括：對受約束隨機最佳化理論的新見解；在確保嚴格可行性保證的同時，發展具有最先進計算複雜度保證的新型演算法；以及為提升隨機決策系統安全性與可靠性的實際工具。最終，本研究將彌合隨機最佳化演算法與確定性操作需求之間的差距，推動最佳化理論及其在工程、資料科學與人工智能領域中的應用發展。

26210826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26210826.value: 雙光子聚合低電壓驅動軟體機器人微致動器的致動機理

26210826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26210826.value: Micrometer-scale actuators are fundamental components that define the motion, adaptability, and intelligence of miniature robotics. In nature, motile cilia — hair-like soft filaments found on many cells—serve as ideal models of such actuators. These densely packed microactuators enable various critical physiological functions, such as predation, locomotion, and cell trafficking, in living organisms and the human body. However, replicating these capabilities in artificial systems remains challenging due to the lack of effective and scalable microscale actuation mechanisms. Among emerging approaches, ion-gradient-driven hydrogel deformation could offer a promising solution. In theory, precise micrometer geometry and nanometer confinement can strengthen and accelerate net ionic redistribution, thereby enabling fast and effective shape change under low-voltage electrical stimuli. Nevertheless, this mechanism remains poorly understood because no existing technique can simultaneously sculpture both the microscale topology and nanoscale porosity of the hydrogel. To address this gap, we propose employing two-photon polymerization (TPP) to accurately engineer both the micro- and nanostructures of electroactive hydrogels, thereby enabling direct investigation of the underlying electro-chemo-mechanical mechanism. Our preliminary studies have uncovered a previously unachieved fast electrical response in micrometer-scale hydrogels. Building upon this result, we fabricated gel microcilia arrays on soft substrates. Each microcilium, down to 2 µm × 18 µm, can be actuated by 1.5 V without hydrolysis and exhibits dynamically reconfigurable 3D motion up to 40 Hz, closely mirroring natural cilia. Compared with conventional millimeter-scale hydrogel actuators, the actuation voltage is 20 times lower and the response time is 100 times faster. Additionally, these gel microcilia operate reliably well above 330,000 cycles, facilitating their long-term use. While the preliminary results are promising, a unified framework to harness both material and structural factors of hydrogel actuators to quantitatively push their performance limits has yet to be established. This project aims to bridge this gap through three objectives: (1) Fabrication - establish the process–structure relationship of TPP-fabricated hydrogels to define their achievable porosity and topology; (2) Mechanistic Study – experimentally elucidate the electro-chemo-mechanical coupling mechanisms with nanometer pore confinement and within multi-cation environments; (3) Modeling, Validation and Inverse Design - develop a physics-informed, data-driven model that integrates porosity, ion transport, and nonlinear mechanics for predictive simulation and design optimization. Through an iterative process combining fabrication, characterization, modeling, validation, and designing, these efforts will lay the foundation for future microscale actuators that are fast, effective, programmable, and robust, ushering in soft robotic systems that rival their natural counterparts. 微米尺度致動器是微型機器人系統的核心組件，決定其運動能力、適應性及智能水平。在自然界中，運動纖毛——存在於多種細胞表面的毛髮狀柔性絲狀結構——是此類致動器的理想仿生模型。這些密集排列的微型致動器在生物體及人體內執行多種重要的生理功能，包括捕食、運動及細胞運輸。然而，由於目前缺乏有效且具可擴展性的微尺度致動機制，要在人工系統中重現這些能力仍極具挑戰。 在各種新興方法中，由離子梯度驅動的水凝膠形變提供了一個具潛力的解決方案。理論上，精確的微米尺度幾何結構及納米尺度限域效應可增強並加快離子的淨重新分佈，從而使材料在低電壓電刺激下快速而有效地改變形狀。然而，由於現有技術無法同時塑造水凝膠的微尺度拓撲結構及納米尺度孔隙結構，這一機制目前仍未得到充分理解。 為填補這一研究空白，本項目擬採用雙光子聚合技術，精確調控電活性水凝膠的微觀及納米結構，從而直接研究其內在的電－化學－力學耦合機制。我們的初步研究發現了以往未能實現的微米尺度水凝膠快速電響應。基於此成果，我們在柔性基底上製備了水凝膠微纖毛陣列。每根微纖毛的尺寸可小至2微米 × 18微米，並可在不引發水解的情況下以1.5伏特驅動，實現最高40赫茲、可動態重構的三維運動，高度模擬天然纖毛。與傳統毫米尺度水凝膠致動器相比，其驅動電壓降低了20倍，響應速度提高了100倍。此外，這些水凝膠微纖毛在超過33萬次循環後仍能可靠運作，有利於長期應用。 儘管初步結果令人鼓舞，目前仍缺乏一個能夠同時運用水凝膠致動器的材料與結構因素，並定量推進其性能極限的統一框架。本項目將通過以下三個目標填補這一空白：（1）製造——建立雙光子聚合水凝膠的製程－結構關係，界定其可實現的孔隙結構及拓撲形態；（2）機制研究——通過實驗闡明納米孔隙限域及多陽離子環境下的電－化學－力學耦合機制；（3）建模、驗證及逆向設計——開發一個融合孔隙結構、離子傳輸及非線性力學的物理知識驅動數據模型，用於預測模擬及設計優化。 通過結合製造、表徵、建模、驗證及設計的迭代研究過程，本項目將為開發快速、高效、可編程且穩健的未來微尺度致動器奠定基礎，推動性能可媲美天然系統的軟體機器人技術發展。

26210926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26210926.value: 隐性努力下的最优契约设计：HJB 方程的理论与计算

26210926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26210926.value: Contracts that align incentives between different parties are essential to the efficient functioning of modern economic and engineering systems. In financial and operational settings—such as investment management, project outsourcing, and supply-chain coordination—principals delegate tasks to agents whose actions cannot be directly observed. This lack of observability gives rise to a hidden-action problem, in which optimal decision making requires the design of an incentive-compatible contract that motivates efforts. This project develops a unified theoretical and computational framework for solving such contract design problems. By reformulating the principal–agent interaction as a stochastic control problem, we characterize the optimal contract through a Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman (HJB) equation. A key mathematical challenge arises because this HJB equation may involve unbounded coefficients, which prevents the direct use of standard optimization or PDE techniques. We first establish rigorous existence and regularity results for the value function, guaranteeing that the partial derivatives required to define the optimal contract are well-behaved. Building on this theoretical foundation, we design a numerical algorithm that provably converges even under degeneracy, enabling robust computation of optimal contracts in multi-dimensional settings where closed-form solutions are unavailable. Numerical experiments will then be conducted to quantify how risk preferences, cost structures, and exogenous uncertainties shape contract outcomes. The proposed methodology integrates ideas from stochastic control, partial differential equations, and computational optimization, contributing to the broader field of optimization under uncertainty. Beyond its theoretical significance, the project provides practical tools for decision design in financial engineering and management science—helping investors, firms, and regulators better understand how to structure incentives in environments with asymmetric information. The framework is flexible enough to be extended to other engineering applications, thereby offering a systematic foundation for contract optimization. 能够协调不同参与方利益与激励的契约，是现代经济体系和工程系统高效运行的重要基础。在投资管理、项目外包和供应链协同等金融与运营场景中，委托人往往需要将任务交由代理人执行，却无法直接观察其实际行动或努力水平。由此产生了典型的隐藏行动问题：委托人必须设计满足激励相容条件的契约，引导代理人付出恰当的努力，从而实现整体决策目标。 本项目拟建立一套统一的理论与计算框架，用于求解此类最优契约设计问题。我们将委托人与代理人之间的互动重新表述为随机控制问题，并通过 Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman（HJB）方程刻画最优契约。该方法面临的核心数学困难在于，所得 HJB 方程可能含有无界系数，使得传统的优化方法和偏微分方程理论难以直接应用。 项目首先将严格研究价值函数的存在性与正则性，确保构造最优契约所需的偏导数具有良好的数学性质。在此基础上，我们将进一步设计具有严格收敛保证的数值算法。即使 HJB 方程存在退化，该算法仍能实现稳定、可靠的计算，从而求解缺乏闭式解的多维最优契约问题。随后，我们将通过数值实验，定量分析风险偏好、成本结构和外生不确定性等因素如何影响最优契约的形式及其实施效果。 本项目融合随机控制、偏微分方程与计算优化等领域的方法，旨在推动不确定性环境下优化理论的发展。除理论贡献外，项目还将为金融工程和管理科学中的机制与决策设计提供可操作的计算工具，帮助投资者、企业和监管机构更好地理解如何在信息不对称条件下设计有效的激励机制。所提出的框架具有较强的通用性，并可进一步拓展至其他工程应用，为复杂环境中的契约优化提供系统的理论与计算基础。

26213626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26213626.value: 基於計算機視覺的混凝土與砌體結構震後損傷評估

26213626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26213626.value: Earthquakes pose severe threats to human safety and socio-economic development. For example, the 2023 Turkey Earthquake caused the collapse of about 280,000 buildings, affecting over 13 million people. Timely and accurate post-earthquake building inspection is critical for safety and recovery. As per China’s National Standards and guidelines for post-earthquake building damage assessment, a rapid and comprehensive evaluation should be conducted with “qualitative” and “quantitative” measures, including assessment of global building conditions and local component damage. Traditional manual on-site inspection is inefficient, labor-intensive, and highly dependent on the skills of inspectors. In recent years, computer vision-based damage detection has shown great potential to partially automate the inspection process. Despite the achievements, existing computer vision algorithms have not sufficiently embedded domain-specific knowledge, and face several challenges, such as dataset limitations, insufficient accuracy and efficiency, and limited research scopes (e.g., only qualitative assessment or laboratory validation), which may not meet the comprehensive requirements of post-earthquake building damage assessment. Within this context, this research aims to develop domain-specific computer vision methods for accurate and efficient post-earthquake damage assessment of concrete and masonry buildings (two dominant damaged building types in China’s high-seismicity regions). The project will involve three key tasks: 1) develop a novel deep learning (DL)-driven 3D reconstruction method for building structures; 2) develop a computer vision and 3D point cloud-based building damage evaluation method; and 3) conduct field validation of the proposed methodology in a post-earthquake heritage site in western China. The proposed research project will be executed through dataset curation, theory derivation, model training, laboratory validation, and field tests with the support of the China Earthquake Administration (Institutional Support Letter attached). The main scientific novelties and contributions include the development of domain-specific computer vision models, which embeds domain knowledge of China’s National Standards and guidelines for post-earthquake building assessment, as well as building seismic damage characteristics, for rapid and accurate “qualitative” and “quantitative” vision-based 3D reconstruction and damage assessment in post-earthquake scenarios. The practical contributions to the field include validation of the proposed methodology using extensive sources of real-world post-earthquake data previously collected, as well as rigorous field tests in post-earthquake heritage site based on the related National Standards and guidelines, in collaboration with the China Earthquake Administration. Successful completion of the research will provide new theory development and enhance the existing practice in post-earthquake building damage assessment. 地震對人類生命安全與社會經濟發展構成嚴峻挑戰。以 2023 年土耳其大地震為例，該地震導致約 28 萬棟建築物毀損倒塌，受災人口逾 1,300 萬。因此，開展及時且高精度的震後建築物結構檢測，對於保障公共安全與推動災後重建至關重要。根據中國國家標準及震後建築結構破壞評估指南，震後評估應秉持 “定性分析”與 “定量量測”相結合的原則，實施快速且系統性的全面評估，其內容涵蓋建築物整體結構狀態與局部構件損傷。然而，傳統的人工現場檢測方法不僅效率低、勞動強度大，且評估結果高度依賴檢測人員的工程經驗。近年來，基於計算機視覺的損傷檢測技術在推動檢測流程半自動化方面展現出巨大潛力。儘管現有研究已取得一定進展，但現有的計算機視覺算法普遍缺乏對學科領域知識的深度融合，且面臨諸多技術瓶頸，例如：基準數據集規模受限、檢測精度與運算效率不足，以及研究場景過於單一（如僅侷限於定性評估或實驗室環境驗證），因而難以滿足震後建築結構損傷全面評估的實質工程需求。 在此背景下，本研究旨在開發融合領域知識的計算機視覺方法，以實現對混凝土結構與砌體結構（此為中國高烈度地震區的兩種主要震損建築類型）精確且高效的震後損傷評估。本項目核心研發任務包含以下三點：1) 開發基於新型深度學習驅動的建築結構三維重建方法；2) 建構基於計算機視覺與三維點雲的建築物結構損傷評估體系；3) 在中國西部震後歷史遺產保護地開展示範性現場實車/原位驗證。在中國地震局的鼎力支持下，本項目將有機結合數據集構建、理論公式推導、模型訓練、實驗室試驗驗證及原位現場測試等學術路徑，確保研究的系統性與科學性。 本項目的核心學術創新與科學貢獻在於：首次開發了融合領域知識的計算機視覺模型。該模型深度嵌入了中國現行國家標準、震後建築評估指南的核心要義，以及建築結構地震損傷的物理破壞特徵，從而實現在震後複雜場景下，基於視覺的快速、高精度 “定性”與 “定量”三維重建和損傷評估。在工程應用與實踐貢獻方面：本項目將與中國地震局開展深度合作，利用前期累積的大量真實震後歷史數據進行模型驗證，並依據相關國家標準規範，在震後遺產地進行嚴格的原位測試。本研究的順利實施，不僅能開拓震後建築物結構損傷評估的理論邊界，亦將顯著提升現階段防災減災工程的技術實踐水平。

26217426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26217426.value: 面向真實環境探索的軟體無肢系統瞬態與快速運動動力學

26217426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26217426.value: Soft limbless creatures such as snakes, exhibit remarkable performance in traversing highly heterogeneous and cluttered environments while maintaining speed, precision, and adaptability. These capabilities hold tremendous promise for applications across scales, including exploration, inspection, defense, and healthcare. However, the understanding and engineering realization of soft limbless locomotion have largely been constrained to stereotypical, low-speed, and periodic motions such as crawling or lateral undulation. The diverse repertoire of transient and rapid behaviors that fundamentally constitute the high-level motility and intelligence of limbless animals remains largely unexplored, hindering their practical deployment. This gap arises from significant challenges, from modeling the nonlinear, high dimensional body dynamics to developing effective control strategies in complex, unpredictable environments. While studies leveraging theoretical, empirical, or robophysical approaches have offered important insights, individual efforts remain limited by the lack of generality, scalability, and flexibility. Recognizing these challenges, and seizing upon recent biological insights into mechanical intelligence and hierarchical control, this project aims to develop a systematic computational framework that advances the motility of soft limbless systems toward robust real-world traversal. Through a synergistic combination of mechanics-based modeling, optimization, control, and learning, three key research tasks will be conducted. First, we will investigate the underlying physical principles of diverse transient and rapid motor behaviors and derive a collection of enabling neuromuscular activation strategies. Second, we will formulate a hierarchical control framework that integrates multimodal sensing, high-level decision-making, and lower-level motion execution, driving adaptive traversal in complex and heterogeneous landscapes. Third, we will construct high-fidelity, realistic environments to contextualize these strategies and advance their translation to high-impact applications of strategic importance. Together, these efforts will establish a computational foundation that unifies biological, theoretical, and robotic insights. To further extend impact, the outcomes of this project will be consolidated into OpenSoftEnv, an open-source, accessible, and modular software platform that accelerates discovery, fosters community-driven contributions, and promotes cross-disciplinary deployment and engineering education. In conjunction, this platform will further enable us to initiate the physical realization by leveraging it as a testbed for sim-to-real transfer, laying the foundation for continued robotic development, and advancing the embodied intelligence in soft systems toward adaptive, robust real-world deployment. 蛇類等軟體無肢生物能夠在高度異質、障礙密集的複雜環境中靈活穿行，同時保持卓越的運動速度、精準度與環境適應能力。這類運動能力在不同尺度的探索、巡檢、國防及醫療健康等領域具有廣闊的應用前景。然而，目前對軟體無肢運動的科學認知與工程實現，仍主要局限於爬行、側向蜿蜒等典型、低速且週期性的運動模式。相比之下，構成無肢動物高階運動能力與智能基礎的多樣化瞬態與快速運動行為，至今仍缺乏系統性研究，嚴重制約了相關軟體機器人在真實複雜環境中的實際應用。其核心挑戰涵蓋從非線性、高維度柔性體動力學建模，到複雜、不可預測環境下高效控制策略的建立。儘管理論分析、實驗研究及機器人物理模型等不同研究方法已取得重要進展，單一方法仍普遍受限於通用性、可擴展性及靈活性，難以形成統一而系統的研究框架。 針對上述挑戰，並結合近年生物力學智能與分層控制方面的新認知，本項目旨在建立一套系統性的計算研究框架，推動軟體無肢系統由典型週期運動向複雜真實環境中的高機動、自適應運動拓展。項目將協同融合基於力學的建模、優化、控制與學習方法，開展三項核心研究任務。首先，系統研究多樣化瞬態與快速運動行為背後的基本物理機制，揭示身體動力學、環境交互與驅動之間的耦合關係，並建立一系列實現不同運動行為的神經肌肉激活策略。其次，構建融合多模態感知、高階決策與底層運動執行的分層控制框架，使軟體無肢系統能夠根據環境與任務需求自主選擇、組合及切換不同運動模式，實現在複雜異質地形中的自適應穿行。第三，建立具有高保真度與真實物理特徵的複雜環境模型，在接近實際應用場景的條件下系統評估及優化所提出的運動與控制策略，並推動其向具有重要戰略價值的高影響力應用轉化。 通過上述研究，本項目將建立一套融合生物學、理論力學與機器人學認知的統一計算基礎。為進一步擴大研究成果的影響力，項目將整合相關模型、算法、環境及計算工具，開發 OpenSoftEnv—一個開源、易用且模組化的軟體平台，以加速軟體無肢運動研究中的科學發現，促進研究社群共同開發，並推動跨學科應用與工程教育。同時，該平台亦將作為模擬到現實轉移的測試與驗證平台，進一步啟動軟體無肢機器人的實體化研究，為後續機器人系統的持續開發奠定基礎，最終推動軟體系統的具身智能向自適應、高魯棒性的真實環境應用邁進。

26220226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26220226.value: 面向高效、自適應即時配送優化的新型深度強化學習框架

26220226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26220226.value: On-demand delivery has transformed urban logistics globally, which has become critical urban infrastructure with platforms like Meituan processing over 30 million daily orders within tight 30-60 minute timeframes. This rapidly growing sector has significant economic and societal impact, influencing urban sustainability and quality of life through timely delivery of meals, medications, groceries, and emergency supplies. On-demand delivery optimization represents a complex sequential decision-making process coordinating users, merchants, couriers, and the centralized platform in real-time. At its core, it needs to determine order-courier matching (dispatch: who delivers) and pickup-delivery sequence optimization (routing: how to deliver) efficiently. Despite its growing importance, on-demand delivery optimization remains understudied compared to traditional logistics problems that operate with longer timeframes or more stable patterns, which leads to fundamental challenges, including (1) high system dynamicity with continuously evolving order streams and highly fluctuating courier availability; (2) exponentially growing complexity at scale requiring efficient decision-making within milliseconds; and (3) complex uncertainties throughout the “dispatch-prepare-pickup-deliver” cycle. Although existing research has made strides in dispatch or routing in on-demand delivery, it often considers simplified setups that overlook real-world complexities and requirements, sacrifices long-term solution quality for computational efficiency, or relies heavily on high-quality datasets. Our project aims to bridge this open research gap for efficient and adapative dispatch-routing optimization with an innovative deep reinforcement learning (RL) framework through three interconnected objectives targeting its core components, that collectively tackle these key challenges. First, we develop a novel RL dispatch approach that efficiently handles large-scale orders and couriers in dynamic decision space with reduced computational complexity, enabling efficient long-term performance optimization. Second, we design an uncertainty-aware adaptive routing optimization that accounts for delivery time uncertainties and intelligently selects computational strategies based on situational demands, leading to adaptive, robust route planning under high uncertainty. Finally, we develop integrated dispatch-routing optimization within a coordinated learning framework enabling continuous system-wide improvement. Our preliminary results in a case study are promising (16% improvement in delivery solution quality considering delivery delay and travel distance), validating our methodology’s potential. The research will deliver both practical improvements in delivery efficiency and solution quality with reduced costs (through our established industry partnership with Meituan), and fundamental algorithmic advances in RL for complex decision-making. Ultimately, this project has the potential for establishing foundations for last-mile logistics systems applicable to diverse time-critical scenarios (e.g., medical supplies, emergency services), and creates efficient, sustainable delivery ecosystems with broad societal impact.

26301826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26301826.value: 設計氫原子轉移光酶用於對映選擇性脂肪族C-H鍵官能化

26301826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26301826.value: The selective transformation of inert aliphatic carbon-hydrogen (C–H) bonds is a fundamental and long-standing challenge in synthetic chemistry. Mastering this transformation would provide a streamlined approach to constructing complex molecules, with profound implications for pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and materials science. While enzymes perform such reactions with exquisite precision, their native substrate scope and reaction types are limited. Conversely, synthetic small-molecule hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) photocatalysts offer broad reaction versatility but typically fail to control product stereochemistry. To bridge this gap, the Principal Investigator (PI) proposes to create a new class of artificial enzymes, termed Photo-HATzymes, that merge the versatile reactivity of HAT photocatalysis with the precise stereocontrol of enzymatic environments. A key innovation is the supramolecular anchoring of a mechanistically distinct photocatalyst, eosin Y, inside diverse sophisticated protein hosts to enable high-throughput screening. This approach is supported by computational modeling, compelling preliminary data, and the PI's proven expertise in artificial enzyme design and radical chemistry. The central outcome of this project will be a general biocatalytic platform for the enantioselective Giese-type alkylation of aliphatic C–H bonds—a long-standing challenge in both synthetic chemistry and biology. We will then extend this platform to other valuable C–H transformations, including deracemization, fluorination, and azidation. The utility of Photo-HATzymes will be demonstrated through applications in pharmaceutical ingredient synthesis, bioconjugation, and biocascade reactions. By uniting the power of abiotic HAT photocatalysis with the specificity and evolvability of biocatalysis, this research will establish a novel and sustainable platform for synthesizing valuable chiral molecules from simple C–H starting materials. The Photo-HATzyme technology is poised to open new frontiers in green chemistry and synthetic biology. 惰性脂肪族碳氫（C–H）鍵的選擇性轉化，是合成化學中一項基礎且長久以來的挑戰。掌握此轉化反應，將能提供建構複雜分子的簡化途徑，對醫藥、農化及材料科學具有深遠影響。雖然酵素能以極高的精確度執行此類反應，但其天然受質範圍與反應類型卻有所侷限。相對地，合成小分子氫原子轉移（HAT）光觸媒雖具備反應多樣性，但通常無法控制產物的立體化學。 為填補此一缺口，計畫主持人（PI）擬創造一類新穎的人工酵素，命名為Photo-HATzymes，其結合了HAT光催化之廣泛反應性與酵素環境的精確立體控制能力。其中一項關鍵創新，在於以超分子錨定方式，將一具獨特機制之光觸媒——伊紅Y（eosin Y）——安置於多種複雜的蛋白質主體中，以實現高通量篩選。此研究途徑獲得計算模型模擬，初步實驗數據，以及PI在人工酵素設計與自由基化學專業知識的支持。 本計畫的核心成果，將建立一個通用的生物催化平台，用於脂肪族C–H鍵的對映選擇性Giese型烷基化反應——此為合成化學與生物學中長期存在的難題。我們隨後將把此平台擴展至其他具價值的C–H轉化反應，包括去消旋化、氟化及疊氮化。Photo-HATzymes的實用性將透過在藥用成分合成、生物共軛及生物級聯反應中的應用加以驗證。 藉由整合HAT光催化的優勢與生物催化之特異性及可演化性，本研究將建立一個新穎且可進化的平台，用於從簡單的C–H起始物合成具價值的手性分子。Photo-HATzyme技術可望開創綠色化學與合成生物學的新前沿。

26304226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
