26304226.value: 基于小批量采样的经验似然贝叶斯推断

26304226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26304226.value: Traditional Bayesian analysis defines the likelihood function by specifying a probabilistic model for the data-generating process. However, this likelihood-based Bayesian approach can be sensitive to model misspecification, leading to credible intervals that fails to accurately reflect estimation uncertainty. Bayesian pseudo-inference based on empirical likelihood, such as Bayesian empirical likelihood (EL), Bayesian exponentially tilted empirical likelihood (ETEL), and Bayesian jackknife empirical likelihood (JEL), offer a desirable alternative that retain many advantages of standard Bayesian inference, including consistent point estimation and valid uncertainty quantification, while do not require full model specification. This project aims to develop a theoretically grounded mini-batched Metropolis–Hastings framework for empirical-likelihood–based Bayesian inference, with non-asymptotic guarantees. We design mini-batch approximations to EL/ETEL objectives so that the resulting mini-batch pseudo-posteriors closely match their full-data targets. We analyze a relatively “naive” approximation, for which we provide new theoretical results showing that it yields accurate point estimates, while fails to provide valid uncertainty quantification. This, in turn, motivates a more refined, variance-reduced method that leverages point-estimator information for improved posterior inference. We will provide rigorous theoretical justification for the developed method, including explicit finite-sample bounds on posterior approximation error and principled mini-batch size selection. We will also analyze convergence of the mini-batch MH algorithm via perturbation and conductance arguments, connecting the mixing properties of the mini-batch chain to those of the full-data counterpart. The methodology applies to both smooth and non-smooth moment conditions and extends to settings with intractable moment functions/estimating equations. 传统贝叶斯分析通过为数据生成过程设定概率模型来定义似然函数。然而，这种基于似然的贝叶斯方法可能对模型设定错误较为敏感，导致所得可信区间无法准确反映估计的不确定性。基于经验似然的贝叶斯伪推断方法，如贝叶斯经验似然、贝叶斯指数倾斜经验似然和贝叶斯刀切经验似然，提供了一种理想的替代方案。这类方法无须完整设定概率模型，同时保留了标准贝叶斯推断的诸多优势，包括一致的点估计和有效的不确定性量化。本项目旨在构建一个具有坚实理论基础和非渐近保证的小批量采样框架，用于基于经验似然的贝叶斯推断。我们将为经验似然和指数倾斜经验似然的目标函数设计小批量近似，使由此得到的小批量伪后验分布能够紧密逼近其全数据目标分布。我们首先分析一种相对“朴素”的近似方法，并给出新的理论结果，证明该方法虽然能够产生准确的点估计，却无法实现有效的不确定性量化。这一发现进一步促使我们开发一种更为精细的方差缩减方法，利用点估计量所包含的信息来改进后验推断。我们将为所提出的方法提供严格的理论依据，包括后验近似误差的显式有限样本界，以及具有理论依据的小批量规模选择方法。此外，我们还将运用扰动分析和传导率论证研究小批量采样算法的收敛性，并建立小批量马尔可夫链与全数据马尔可夫链混合性质之间的联系。该方法既适用于光滑和非光滑矩条件，也可扩展至矩函数或估计方程难以直接计算的情形。

26305626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26305626.value: 級聯量子糾錯碼的容錯電路與解碼

26305626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26305626.value: Achieving practical, large-scale quantum computers remains a formidable challenge due to the inherent susceptibility of quantum bits (qubits) to environmental noise. Current quantum platforms suffer from high error rates, necessitating fault-tolerant quantum computation. Quantum error-correcting codes (QECC) address this issue by encoding logical qubits into a larger ensemble of physical qubits, thereby safeguarding information against errors. Among these codes, concatenated quantum codes have historically been less favored compared to alternatives, primarily due to practical limitations such as non-local connectivity requirements, low error thresholds, and substantial qubit overhead. However, recent advancements in quantum hardware that enhance connectivity are prompting a reevaluation of concatenated codes' potential. This proposal aims to fully explore the capabilities of concatenated codes by focusing on the enhancement of global decoding schemes and the improvement of fault-tolerant measurement of error information. Our research endeavors to deepen the understanding of quantum fault tolerance and deliver meaningful advancements to the field of quantum computation. 由於量子位元極易受環境噪聲影響，實用化大規模量子計算機仍是一項嚴峻挑戰。量子糾錯碼透過將邏輯量子位元編碼到更大規模的物理量子位元集合中，藉此保護資訊免受錯誤影響。在各類量子糾錯編碼中，級聯碼過往因存在非局域連通性要求、容錯閾值較低以及量子位元開銷龐大等實際限制，與表面碼等替代方案相比不受青睞。然而，近期量子硬件在連通性方面的提升，正促使人們重新審視級聯碼的潛力。本項目旨在透過強化全域解碼方案以及改進錯誤資訊的容錯測量，來全面解鎖級聯碼的性能。我們的研究致力於加深對量子容錯機制之理解，並為量子計算領域帶來實質性的進展。

26305726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26305726.value: 高電荷凝聚體中聚合物動力學與相互作用的介觀尺度模擬

26305726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26305726.value: Coacervates, macromolecular liquids arising from liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) of highly charged biopolymers, play a vital role in essential biological functions and are driving the development of next-generation biomaterials for artificial cells, nanoreactors, and biomedicines. Coacervates typically comprise multispecies biopolymers with both positive and negative charges, along with small ions and significant amounts of water. This unique composition creates a highly charged, viscous, and hydrated environment, enabling coacervates to selectively encapsulate guest biomolecules, facilitates bioreactions, and regulates intracellular organization. The functionality of coacervates is largely governed by the mesoscale (1 nm to 1 μm) behavior of their constituent and guest polymers, including single-chain dynamics, chain-chain interactions, and many-chain assembly. Despite extensive research, our fundamental understanding of polymer behavior within coacervates remains limited, hindering practical design of coacervate-based systems. Coarse-grained simulation is currently the most effective approach in capturing polymer behavior across mesoscale length and time scales in macromolecular fluid systems. However, existing coarse-grained methods commonly used in modeling coacervate systems do not incorporate hydrodynamic interactions and often exclude explicit electrostatic interactions. These two long-range interactions are expected to be critical for the polymer behavior within the highly charged and hydrated coacervates, which typically contain 15%~45% charged polymers and 55%~85% water. While there exist approaches to couple these long-range interactions, they are too computational extensive to capture polymer-scale behavior within dense coacervates. The proposed project will aim to develop a new coarse-grained modeling method that efficiently integrates long-range interactions, to systematically investigate polymer behavior across mesoscale length and time scales in typical coacervate environments. The key results will be validated via experimental collaborations. The project consists of four main tasks: (i) Develop an efficient modeling method that integrates long-range forces to study polymer behavior in coacervates; (ii) Unravel the length-scale-dependent viscosity of coacervates and its relationship with the charge structure of constituent polymers; (iii) Elucidate how the intrinsic charged network in coacervates governs two-body guest polymer interactions; and (iv) Explore the multichain self-assembly of guest polymers within coacervates and its implications for novel applications. The success of this project will provide significant insights for the design of novel coacervate-based materials, particularly for applications centered on encapsulations. Furthermore, the method developed in this project can be adapted to model a broader range of aqueous charged polymer systems, facilitating the mesoscale study of many emerging fields such as biophysics, aqueous electrochemical devices, and soft robotics. 凝聚體（Coacervates）是由高電荷生物聚合物經液-液相分離（LLPS）產生的高分子液體，在基本生物功能中發揮著至關重要的作用，並正推動著用於人造細胞、奈米反應器和生物醫學的下一代生物材料之發展。凝聚體通常由帶有正電荷與負電荷的多種生物聚合物，以及小離子和大量的水所組成。這種獨特的組成創造了一個高電荷、黏稠且水合的環境，使凝聚體能夠選擇性地包覆客體生物分子、促進生物反應並調節細胞內的組織。凝聚體的功能在很大程度上取決於其組成聚合物和客體聚合物在中尺度（1 奈米至 1 微米）的行為，包含單鏈動力學、鏈間交互作用以及多鏈組裝。儘管已有廣泛的研究，但我們對凝聚體內聚合物行為的基本認識仍然有限，這阻礙了基於凝聚體系統的實際設計。 粗粒化模擬（Coarse-grained simulation）是目前捕捉高分子流體系統中，跨越中尺度長度與時間尺度之聚合物行為最有效的方法。然而，目前常用於模擬凝聚體系統的粗粒化方法並未納入流體動力學交互作用（hydrodynamic interactions），且通常排除了顯式的靜電交互作用（electrostatic interactions）。這兩種長程交互作用預計對高度帶電且水合的凝聚體內的聚合物行為至關重要，因為這些凝聚體通常含有 15%~45% 的帶電聚合物和 55%~85% 的水。雖然目前存在結合這些長程交互作用的方法，但它們的計算成本過於龐大，無法用來捕捉緻密凝聚體內的聚合物尺度行為。 本擬議計畫旨在開發一種能有效整合長程交互作用的新型粗粒化建模方法，以系統性地研究典型凝聚體環境中跨中尺度長度與時間尺度的聚合物行為。關鍵結果將透過實驗合作進行驗證。本計畫包含四項主要任務：(i) 開發一種整合長程作用力的高效建模方法，以研究凝聚體中的聚合物行為；(ii) 揭開凝聚體中依賴於長度尺度的黏度，及其與組成聚合物之電荷結構的關係；(iii) 闡明凝聚體中固有的帶電網路如何支配雙體客體聚合物的交互作用；以及 (iv) 探索客體聚合物在凝聚體內的多鏈自組裝現象，及其對新穎應用的影響。 本計畫的成功將為新型凝聚體材料的設計提供重要見解，特別是在以包覆（encapsulations）為核心的應用上。此外，本計畫所開發的方法將可進一步調整，用於模擬更廣泛的水性帶電聚合物系統，從而促進生物物理學、水性電化學元件以及軟體機器人等許多新興領域的中尺度研究。

26310126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26310126.value: 絕對稜鏡上同調的算術應用

26310126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26310126.value: This research proposal explores new connections between geometry and arithmetic related to a fixed prime number p. Just as classical Hodge theory studies the geometry of complex manifolds through linear algebraic structures, the p-adic Hodge theory aims to study p-adic varieties through p-adic Hodge structures. A crucial and poorly understood aspect of this theory is its "integral" version, which is central to many unanswered questions in number theory. Recent work by Bhatt and Scholze introduced a powerful new theory called prismatic cohomology, which offers a unified geometric perspective on these integral structures. The PI will use this innovative theory to study two fundamental objects: the Emerton—Gee stacks, which are spaces classifying representations of certain Galois groups, and the crystalline deformation rings, which track how these representations vary. The Emerton—Gee stacks are expected to play a key role in the categorical p-adic Langlands correspondence, while the crystalline deformation rings are fundamental to the Breuil–Mézard conjecture. These questions are deeply interrelated and have significant applications, for example to the Fontaine—Mazur conjecture and modularity lifting results. By applying the prismatic theory, the work seeks to develop new approaches to advance our understanding in these two areas. 這份研究計劃探討了關於固定質數 p 的幾何與算術之間的新聯繫。正如經典霍奇理論透過線性代數結構研究複流形的幾何一樣，p 進霍奇理論旨在透過 p 進霍奇結構研究 p 進簇。該理論中一個關鍵且人們了解甚少的方向是其「整」版本，這對於數論中許多未決問題至關重要。Bhatt 和 Scholze 近期的工作引入了一種名為稜鏡上同調的有力新理論，為這些「整」結構提供了統一的幾何視角。本計劃將運用這項創新理論來研究兩個基本對象：Emerton–Gee 疊，它們是分類某些伽羅瓦群表示的空間，以及晶體形變環，它們追蹤這些表示如何變化。Emerton–Gee 疊預計將在範疇性 p 進朗蘭茲對應中扮演關鍵角色，而晶體形變環則是 Breuil–Mézard 猜想的基礎。這些問題深度相關，並具有重要應用，例如在 Fontaine–Mazur 猜想和模性提升結果方面。透過應用稜鏡理論，本工作旨在發展新方法，以推進我們在上述兩個領域中的理解。

26310426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26310426.value: 球面與環面乘積流形上的純量曲率及中間曲率剛性

26310426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26310426.value: This project explores how geometric curvature shapes the global structure of space. In differential geometry, curvature measures how a surface or a higher-dimensional space bends. Among the many curvature types, positive scalar curvature plays a central role because it links geometry, topology, and even physics, especially in Einstein’s theory of general relativity. Two classic milestones illustrate this deep connection. The first is Geroch’s conjecture, which asserts that a flat torus cannot be bent to have positive scalar curvature. This was proved by Schoen and Yau using minimal-surface methods in low dimensions and by Gromov and Lawson using analytic tools based on the Dirac operator. The second is Llarull’s rigidity theorem, which shows that any curved space that can be smoothly and non-stretchingly mapped to a sphere of the same dimension must in fact be a perfect sphere itself. These theorems stand at opposite ends of the curvature spectrum: one forbids positive curvature, while the other enforces rigidity when curvature is maximal. This project aims to bridge these two extremes by studying spaces that are part spherical and part toroidal (that is, products of spheres and tori). It seeks a unified framework for understanding when such “mixed” spaces must exhibit rigidity or curvature obstruction. The research has three objectives. First, it will combine geometric slicing methods and analytic tools from spin geometry to investigate scalar curvature rigidity for closed spaces that resemble a sphere in some directions and a torus in others. Second, it will extend these ideas to spaces with boundaries, developing quantitative “bandwidth” inequalities that generalize existing results on spherical and toroidal regions. Third, it will introduce a new approach to intermediate curvature—an idea that connects different notions of positive curvature—by introducing a level–set slicing scheme generated by ε–minimal potentials. Through this work, the project will create new tools that unify two of the most powerful methods in modern geometry and extend them beyond current dimensional limitations. The anticipated results will clarify how curvature governs the shape and topology of spaces, with implications ranging from pure mathematics to the geometric foundations of general relativity. 本計畫研究曲率如何決定空間的整體幾何與拓撲結構，重點探討兼具球面與環面特徵的乘積流形。計畫希望建立一個統一框架，連結球面的純量曲率剛性與環面上的正純量曲率障礙。研究將結合加權切片、Dirac算子及新建立的調和對稱化方法，探討閉流形及帶邊界流形的曲率剛性、寬度估計與正中間曲率障礙。此研究旨在建立新的幾何分析工具，進一步理解曲率、拓撲與全局幾何之間的深層關係。

26500626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26500626.value: 异质性货币政策冲击：来自数据修订的证据

26500626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26500626.value: Central banks base policy decisions on real-time data that are often preliminary and subject to subsequent revisions. These misperceptions of economic conditions can lead to policy rates that are either too restrictive or too accommodative, generating unintended monetary policy "shocks". Importantly, not all misperceptions are created equal: errors in gross domestic product (GDP) data may exhibit very different properties from errors in inflation due to differing forecastability and thus may have very different macroeconomic consequences. This project aims to identify and analyze the effects of "heterogeneous monetary policy shocks" arising from data revisions. Specifically, we identify these shocks by comparing the data available to policymakers in real-time against final revised figures. This allows us to trace how misperceptions about specific economic indicators translate into different policy paths and macroeconomic outcomes. The analysis of these heterogeneous monetary policy shocks provides novel insights into longstanding puzzles in monetary economics, such as why inflation sometimes rises after unexpected interest rate hikes. Moreover, we develop a novel econometric framework for policy counterfactual analysis using this rich, high-dimensional shock data. This project will deliver four key outputs: First, we will construct and publicly release a comprehensive dataset tracking the Federal Reserve's real-time information set, which will enhance transparency in monetary policymaking. Second, we will create a novel dataset of heterogeneous monetary policy shocks to help researchers better understand monetary policy transmission. Third, we will develop a novel econometric framework for policy counterfactual analysis with high-dimensional instrumental variables, which is applicable in various empirical macro research contexts beyond this study. Fourth, we will apply this framework to historical episodes like the Great Inflation of the 1970s to shed light on the interaction between monetary policy and oil price shocks. 中央银行依据实时数据制定政策，而这些初步数据通常面临后续修订。对经济状况的这类误判，可能导致政策利率过度紧缩或过度宽松，从而产生非预期的货币政策“冲击”。重要的是，不同类型的误判并非同质：由于可预测性存在差异，国内生产总值（GDP）的数据误差可能与劳动力市场或通胀指标误差截然不同，由此造成不同的宏观经济后果。本项目旨在识别并分析由数据修订所产生的“异质性货币政策冲击”。具体而言，我们将实时比较政策制定者当时能够获得的数据与最终修订后的数据。借此，我们可以追踪政策制定者对特定经济指标的误判如何转化为不同的政策路径及宏观经济结果。对这些异质性货币政策冲击的分析，将为货币经济学中的长期难题提供新的认识，例如，为何通胀有时会在意外加息后反而上升。此外，我们还将利用这些丰富的高维冲击数据，构建一种新的政策反事实分析计量经济学框架。本项目将形成四项主要成果：第一，我们将构建并公开发布一个全面追踪美联储实时信息集的数据集，以提高货币政策制定过程的透明度。第二，我们将创建一个异质性货币政策冲击数据集，帮助研究者更好地理解货币政策传导机制。第三，我们将发展一种基于高维工具变量、用于政策反事实分析的新型计量经济学框架。该框架还可应用于本研究之外的各种实证宏观经济学场景。第四，我们将把这一框架应用于“大通胀”等历史时期，以揭示货币政策与油价冲击之间的相互作用。

26504626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26504626.value: 电子商务中促销优惠券的有效定向投放

26504626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26504626.value: In the last five years, Hong Kong’s digital market has been thriving, with an 8.3% annual growth rate. Its market volume reached USD11 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD26 billion by 2030. In increasingly competitive online markets, e-commerce retailers rely heavily on promotional strategies to attract consumers. Sales promotions are key tools that marketers use to spur sales, accounting for a large proportion of companies’ marketing budgets. For example, over 80% of Hong Kong companies’ marketing budgets are weighted toward digital channels, with brands using a mix of online and offline promotions to target a market segment volume of USD745 million worth. However, although promotions are powerful incentives for consumers to spend more, practitioners still lack of concrete, evidence-based guidelines for designing effective sales promotion strategies. Recent studies have shown that 20–50% of promotions generate no noticeable lift in sales, while approximately 30% of promotional strategies erode operative margins. Although many promotions are ineffective, e-commerce companies still run thousands of promotional campaigns, such as discount codes and fixed-value coupons, primarily because they struggle to properly design effective online promotions. Improving promotional effectiveness has become a significant challenge for e-commerce retailers worldwide. Most existing research focuses on analyzing the correlation between the characteristics of promotional strategies and strategic objectives, without considering the impact of promotions on customers’ behavior. Such limitations are mainly due to the complexity of estimating causal effects, together with the challenges involved in accessing high-quality experimental data. The proposed project will expand this emerging empirical research through collaboration with an international e-commerce retailer selling beauty products. By implementing large-scale randomized control trials, the e-commerce retailers assigned to its customers various compliance coupons, namely discount promotions with minimum purchase levels. The randomization of the treatments provides an ideal setting in which to analyze the impact of compliance coupons on purchase behavior and to measure the effectiveness of promotional campaigns in several dimensions, such as customer heterogeneity, willingness to spend, and past purchase behavior. In this project, I aim to fill some gaps in the empirical marketing research by providing new evidence-based results that can offer an original contribution to a predominantly theoretical literature. The findings will ultimately support marketers in optimizing their marketing budget allocation by designing effective promotional schemes and potentially saving billions of dollars on campaign budgets. 近年来，香港数字经济持续快速发展，过去五年市场年均增长率达到8.3%。2025年市场规模已达110亿美元，预计到2030年将增长至260亿美元。随着电子商务市场竞争不断加剧，促销活动已成为电商企业吸引消费者、提升销售业绩的重要营销工具，并占据企业营销预算的重要比例。例如，香港超过80%的企业营销预算投向数字营销渠道，线上与线下促销市场规模已达到约7.45亿美元。 然而，尽管促销活动被广泛采用，其实际效果却存在较大的不确定性。目前企业在制定促销策略时仍缺乏系统、科学且基于实证证据的决策依据。已有研究表明，约20%至50%的促销活动无法带来显著的销售增长，约30%的促销策略甚至会降低企业利润率。尽管如此，电子商务企业仍持续开展大量优惠券、折扣码等促销活动，其根本原因在于企业尚未充分理解不同促销方案对消费者购买行为的真实影响。 提升促销策略的有效性已成为全球电子商务企业面临的重要挑战。现有研究主要关注促销工具与企业营销目标之间的关系，而对促销策略如何影响消费者决策行为的因果机制研究仍然不足。这主要是由于消费者行为的因果效应难以识别，同时高质量随机实验数据十分稀缺。 本项目将依托与一家国际知名美妆电子商务平台的合作，利用大规模随机对照实验（Randomized Controlled Trials, RCT）数据开展研究。合作企业随机向消费者发放不同类型的门槛优惠券（即设置最低消费金额要求的优惠券），为识别促销策略对消费者购买行为的因果影响提供了理想的实验环境。基于该实验数据，本项目将系统分析不同优惠券设计对消费者购买决策的影响，并进一步考察消费者异质性、消费意愿以及历史购买行为在促销效果中的作用机制。 本项目旨在弥补促销策略实证研究中的重要不足，为营销领域提供具有因果识别基础的新证据，丰富现有以理论研究为主的相关文献。同时，本研究将为电子商务企业制定更加精准、高效的促销策略提供科学依据，帮助企业优化营销资源配置，提高促销投资回报率，实现企业收益与消费者福利的共同提升。

26504826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26504826.value: 证券集体诉讼的变革：事件驱动型证券诉讼的兴起

26504826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26504826.value: This project studies the rise of Event-Driven Securities Litigation (EDSL) and its implications for corporate disclosure policies. In accounting, litigation is viewed as a governance mechanism disciplining managers' disclosure choices. Historically, securities class action lawsuits involved misstated financial results or misleading forward-looking statements. Recently, however, the number of misstatements has fallen, while class-action filings have increased, prompting claims that securities fraud litigants have widened legal arguments of what constitutes securities fraud. Legal scholars link this to the rise of EDSL, where lawsuits follow operational events (e.g., industrial accidents, product failures, regulatory breaches) that primarily harm parties other than shareholders. EDSL differs in several dimensions from traditional Disclosure-related Securities Litigation (DSL), which the accounting literature has focused on. First, DSL typically follows corrective disclosures about misstatements, whereas EDSL follows stock drops after adverse operating events. Relatedly, EDSL allegations often target prior “soft” statements about risks, safety, or compliance. The cited sources also differ: DSL complaints mostly rely on earnings announcements, press releases, and 10-Qs, whereas EDSL complaints center on risk factors and Management Discussion and Analysis (MD&A) disclosures in 10-Ks. Considering these significant differences between EDSL and DSL, and EDSL’s growing share of securities class action lawsuits, it is important to examine whether firms assess litigation risks differently and, in turn, adjust their disclosure policies accordingly within this evolving private enforcement landscape. This project begins with descriptive analyses of EDSL and DSL. Using Stanford’s Securities Class Action Clearinghouse (SCAC) database to identify EDSL cases, we will first document the rising trend in EDSL filings. We will then examine which companies get sued for EDSL cases and how the market responds. Specifically, we will test whether operational risk measures predict EDSL cases, considering that these cases follow negative operational events. We will also test whether the market reacts differently to EDSL and DSL cases. We will then assess how EDSL risk shapes firms’ risk disclosures. Using peer EDSL events to capture salient, industry-level shifts in perceived litigation risk, we will examine changes in the volume (word counts) and specificity (text-based measures) of risk disclosures before and after peer EDSL lawsuits. Collectively, these analyses will provide evidence on the determinants, market consequences, and disclosure adjustments associated with the growing EDSL environment. 本项目研究事件驱动型证券诉讼（Event-Driven Securities Litigation，简称EDSL）的兴起及其对企业信息披露政策的影响。在会计领域，诉讼被视为一种约束管理层披露决策的治理机制。历史上，证券集体诉讼通常涉及财务数据错报或误导性前瞻性陈述。然而近年来，错报案件数量有所下降，而集体诉讼案件的提起数量却持续上升，这促使外界认为证券欺诈诉讼方已扩大了对"证券欺诈"构成要件的法律解释。法律学者将这一现象与EDSL的兴起相联系——此类诉讼往往发生于运营事件（如工业事故、产品缺陷、违反监管规定）之后，而这些事件造成的主要损害对象并非股东。 EDSL与传统的披露相关证券诉讼（Disclosure-related Securities Litigation，简称DSL）在多个维度上存在显著差异，而会计文献迄今主要聚焦于后者。首先，DSL通常发生于涉及错报的更正性披露之后，而EDSL则发生于不利运营事件引发股价下跌之后。与此相关，EDSL的指控往往针对此前有关风险、安全或合规方面的"软性"陈述。两类诉讼所引用的信息来源也有所不同：DSL投诉主要依赖盈利公告、新闻稿及10-Q报告，而EDSL投诉则侧重于10-K年报中的风险因素披露及管理层讨论与分析（MD&A）部分。 鉴于EDSL与DSL之间存在的上述重大差异，以及EDSL在证券集体诉讼中占比不断上升的趋势，有必要深入研究以下问题：企业是否会以不同方式评估诉讼风险，并进而在这一不断演变的私人执法环境中相应调整其信息披露政策。 本项目首先对EDSL与DSL展开描述性分析。我们将利用斯坦福大学证券集体诉讼信息库（SCAC）识别EDSL案例，记录EDSL案件提起数量的上升趋势，并考察哪类企业成为EDSL诉讼的对象以及市场对此的反应。具体而言，鉴于EDSL案件源于负面运营事件，我们将检验运营风险指标能否预测EDSL案件的发生，同时测试市场对EDSL与DSL案件是否存在差异化反应。此后，我们将评估EDSL风险如何影响企业的风险信息披露行为。通过以同行业EDSL事件来捕捉感知诉讼风险在行业层面的显著变化，我们将考察企业在同行遭遇EDSL诉讼前后，风险披露的数量（词频统计）与具体程度（基于文本的度量指标）的变化情况。上述分析将共同为理解EDSL环境持续扩展背景下的诉讼决定因素、市场影响后果及信息披露调整行为提供实证依据。

26505026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26505026.value: 數據驅動穩健機會約束的序列凸近似：理論、算法及應用

26505026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26505026.value: Uncertainty is inherent in modern decision-making. From supply chains to energy networks and financial portfolios, organizations must undertake critical decisions in the presence of uncertainty and incomplete information regarding future outcomes. In renewable energy systems, for example, operators must allocate reserves and schedule generation despite sudden drops in wind or solar output as such fluctuations can cause blackouts or costly emergency interventions. To manage such risks, regular chance constrained programs are widely used because they ensure that critical requirements are satisfied with high confidence and are thus particularly suitable for applications where reliability is paramount. A major limitation of regular chance constrained programs is their reliance on exact knowledge of probability distributions, an assumption rarely satisfied in practice. A common approach is to replace the unknown distribution with one estimated from limited data, but such solutions can be unstable: even small deviations between the estimated and true distributions may lead to unreliable decisions. Distributionally robust chance constrained programs (DRCCPs) relax this assumption by requiring feasibility across a family of distributions, thereby providing stronger protection against uncertainty. This robustness is especially valuable in data-driven settings such as renewable energy scheduling under uncertain weather, financial portfolio management in volatile markets, and supply chain design under disruptions. Among distributional models, Wasserstein ambiguity sets have recently attracted significant attention due to their data-driven construction and strong theoretical properties, which make them well-suited for practice. However, solving Wasserstein DRCCPs remains challenging. Exact approaches scale poorly to large instances, while convex approximations such as Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) often produce conservative solutions that sacrifice efficiency. This project will develop new reformulations and algorithms for Wasserstein DRCCPs that achieve a balance among scalability, efficiency, and solution quality. The goal will be to develop sequential convex approximation (SCA), which iteratively replaces nonconvex constraints with convex approximations, for the Wasserstein DRCCPs. We will establish convergence guarantees, compare the approach systematically with CVaR, and investigate special structures such as Gaussian and right-hand-side uncertainty, to yield new explicit insights. To further enhance scalability and efficiency, we will design decomposition strategies that integrate SCA with modern optimization solvers. The project also emphasizes practical validation. We will conduct computational studies on benchmark instances and real-world applications in supply networks, finance, and energy systems. These studies will highlight the ability of the proposed methods to deliver scalable, reliable, and high-quality solutions, advancing the theoretical and computational foundations of DRCCPs for robust data-driven decision-making under uncertainty. 不確定性普遍存在於現代決策之中。無論是供應鏈、能源網絡，還是金融投資組合，決策者往往需要在未來結果不明朗及資訊不完整的情況下作出關鍵決定。以可再生能源系統為例，營運者需要在風力或太陽能發電量可能突然下降的情況下配置備用容量及安排發電。這些波動可能導致停電，或需要採取成本高昂的緊急措施。為管理相關風險，傳統機會約束規劃被廣泛採用。這類模型要求關鍵限制以較高概率獲得滿足，因此特別適合對可靠性要求較高的應用。然而，傳統機會約束規劃通常假設決策者準確掌握不確定因素的概率分佈，而這項假設在實際情況中往往難以成立。一種常見做法是利用有限數據估計未知分佈，並以估計分佈取代真實分佈。但由此得到的決策可能並不穩定：即使估計分佈與真實分佈之間只有輕微偏差，也可能導致不可靠的結果。分佈穩健機會約束規劃（distributionally robust chance constrained programs，DRCCPs）放寬了對準確分佈資訊的依賴。這類模型要求決策在一組可能的概率分佈下均保持可行，從而為不確定性提供更有力的保障。這種穩健性對數據驅動的決策尤其重要，例如不確定天氣下的可再生能源調度、波動市場中的投資組合管理，以及面對突發中斷的供應鏈設計。在不同的分佈模型中，Wasserstein 模糊集合近年備受關注。這類集合可直接根據數據建立，並具有良好的理論性質，因此適合實際應用。然而，Wasserstein DRCCPs 的求解仍然十分困難。精確方法通常難以應用於大規模問題，而條件風險值（Conditional Value-at-Risk，CVaR）等凸近似方法則往往過於保守，可能以犧牲決策效率為代價換取可靠性。 本項目將為 Wasserstein DRCCPs 研究新的模型重構及求解方法，以在可擴展性、計算效率和解的質素之間取得更佳平衡。項目的核心目標是發展適用於 Wasserstein DRCCPs 的序列凸近似方法（sequential convex approximation，SCA）。該方法會反覆以凸近似取代非凸約束，逐步求解原有問題。我們將建立相應的收斂保證，系統比較所提出方法與 CVaR 方法的表現，並研究高斯不確定性及右端項不確定性等特殊結構，以取得更清晰和具實際意義的理論結果。為進一步提升可擴展性和計算效率，我們亦會設計分解方法，將 SCA 與現代優化求解器有效結合。本項目亦重視實際驗證。我們將利用標準測試算例，以及供應網絡、金融和能源系統中的實際應用，進行全面的計算研究。研究結果將展示所提出方法在大規模問題中提供可靠、高質素決策方案的能力，並推動分佈穩健機會約束規劃在理論和計算方法方面的發展，為不確定環境下的穩健數據驅動決策提供更有效的工具。

26507226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26507226.value: 通过在线优化方法加速大语言模型推理

26507226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26507226.value: The widespread deployment of large language models (LLMs) in applications such as AI assistants, search engines, and customer service has created a critical bottleneck: the high computational cost and latency of LLM inference. During inference, the model generates text responses to user prompts, a process that demands efficient resource management to meet user expectations for instant interaction while reducing exorbitant financial and energy costs. Current inference systems rely on simple heuristic scheduling policies that fail to address the unique operational challenges of LLMs. The primary challenge is managing the key-value (KV) cache, a memory-intensive component that accelerates processing but introduces complex, stateful resource constraints incompatible with classical scheduling algorithms. The proposed project will aim to fundamentally advance the efficiency of LLM inference systems by developing a novel mathematical framework from the operations research (OR) and management science (MS) perspective. We will address two core problems: The first problem is online scheduling on a single GPU worker. We will develop efficient, fully online algorithms for scheduling requests on a single GPU, generalizing existing semi-online approaches that assume full prior knowledge of requests. Our approach will adapt established OR techniques, such as online relaxed linear programming with rounding, to the realistic scenario where prompts arrive sequentially and unpredictably. The second problem is online global assignment. We will develop a sophisticated assignment strategy to route prompts from a global dispatcher to a cluster of parallel GPU workers. Our approach will overcome the limitations of naive policies (e.g., round-robin) by integrating output length prediction and real-time modeling of reusable KV cache memory. We will adapt established OR techniques, such as online linear programming with gradient descent, to create a dynamic and provably efficient resource allocation mechanism. The proposed research will develop a rigorous OR-based scheduling and assignment methodology tailored to the constraints of LLM inference. By introducing theoretically grounded algorithms with strong performance guarantees, the research will address a key gap in the computer systems literature, which emphasizes creative system architectures but lacks principled algorithmic approaches to online scheduling and assignment problems. The outcomes have the potential for transformative impact, enabling substantial reductions in operational costs and energy consumption for AI services deployed at a global scale. 大语言模型在人工智能助手、搜索引擎和客户服务等应用中的广泛部署，已引发一个关键瓶颈问题，即大模型推理所带来的高昂计算成本和延迟。在推理过程中，模型根据用户提示生成文本回复，这一过程需要高效的资源管理，以满足用户对即时交互的期望，同时降低过高的财务成本和能源消耗。 当前的推理系统依赖于简单的启发式调度策略，难以应对LLM所特有的运行挑战。其主要挑战在于对键值（KV）缓存的管埋——这是一种内存密集型组件，虽能加速处理过程，但引入了复杂且具有状态性的资源约束，与经典调度算法不相兼容。 本项目拟从运筹学与管理科学的视角出发，通过构建一种新颖的数学框架，从根本上提升LLM推理系统的效率。我们将聚焦于以下两个核心问题： 第一个问题是单GPU工作节点上的在线调度。我们将开发用于单GPU上请求调度的高效、完全在线算法，推广现有的假设具有请求完整先验信息的半在线方法。我们的方法将把成熟的运筹学技术，如带舍入的在线松弛线性规划，适配至提示顺序到达且不可预测的现实场景中。 第二个问题是在线全局分配。我们将开发一种精细化的分配策略，用于从全局调度器将提示路由至一组并行的GPU工作节点。我们的方法将通过集成输出长度预测和可重用KV缓存内存的实时建模，克服朴素策略（如轮询调度）的局限性。我们将借鉴成熟的运筹学技术，如基于梯度下降的在线线性规划，构建一种动态且具有可证明效率的资源分配机制。 本研究将发展一套基于运筹学的、专为LLM推理约束而设计的调度与分配方法体系。通过引入具有强性能保证的理论基础算法，本研究将填补计算机系统文献中的一项重要空白——该领域虽强调创新性的系统架构，却缺乏针对在线调度与分配问题的系统性算法方法。研究成果有望产生变革性影响，显著降低人工智能的运行成本和能源消耗。

26508726.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26508726.value: 後布雷頓森林時代：香港作為金融中心的興起

26508726.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26508726.value: International financial centres now play a substantial economic role in the countries and cities that host them. Understanding how financial centres form is important for assessing the advantages of existing centres and for designing policies to maintain their status. The emergence of financial centres depends on economic fundamentals (Wójcik et al., 2017), historical legacies (Cassis, 2006), and deliberate policy choices (Schenk, 2020). However, only a few candidate cities ultimately become major financial centres, and little is known about how large global shocks influence their rise. To answer the question, this project examines how the increase in foreign‑currency volatility following Nixon’s suspension of the dollar’s convertibility into gold affected foreign banks’ decisions to find correspondent banks that help foreign banks conduct business in Hong Kong. In the 1960s, Hong Kong already had an open and active foreign‑exchange market. The pre‑existing strengths may have attracted international banks after the shift to floating exchange rates. I will estimate the effect of post‑1971 exchange rate volatility on the number of correspondent banking relationships between foreign banks and Hong Kong banks using a difference‑in‑differences (DID) design. This project aims to assemble a bank-level panel dataset of about 4,000 international banks covering the period from 1965 to 1978, when foreign banks relied on correspondent banks to access Hong Kong’s financial market due to restrictions on new bank licences. The main explanatory variable is a shift-share variable that combines pre-1971 trade shares with trading partners’ currency volatility against the U.S. dollar after 1971. It captures how exposed different countries were to the risks of floating exchange rates following Nixon’s decision based on their historical trade patterns. Building on the baseline estimates, I will test several mechanisms. The first mechanism is that individual foreign banks might choose Hong Kong banks that had a presence in their countries as bridges to access Hong Kong. The second is geography, as countries farther from contemporary major financial centres, London and New York, may have been more likely to link to Hong Kong. The third is legal origin, because banks from Common Law jurisdictions may have faced lower entry barriers. Finally, I will construct a network database of banks to examine Hong Kong’s centrality in the international banking network in the 1960s and 1970s. 如今，國際金融中心對所在國家和城市具有重大的經濟影響，理解金融中心的形成對於評估既有中心的優勢以及制定政策以維持其地位均至關重要。金融中心的興起取決於經濟基礎因素（Wójcik 等，2017）、歷史遺產（Cassis，2006）以及審慎的政策選擇（Schenk，2020）。然而，只有少數具備條件的候選城市最終能成為主要金融中心，而且目前學界對於大型全球衝擊如何影響其崛起所知甚少。 為回答此問題，本研究探討尼克松暫停美元兌換黃金之後，外幣波動性增加，如何影響外國銀行尋找代理銀行（correspondent banks）以協助其在香港開展業務的決策。在 1960 年代，香港已擁有開放且活躍的外匯市場，這種既有的優勢可能在匯率轉向浮動制後吸引了國際銀行。 我將採用雙重差分法（difference‑in‑differences，DID），估計 1971 年後匯率波動性對外國銀行與香港銀行之間代理銀行關係數量的影響。本研究旨在建立一個銀行層級的追蹤資料集，涵蓋約 4,000 家國際銀行，時間範圍為 1965 年至 1978 年，此期間因新銀行牌照受限，外國銀行須依賴代理銀行才能進入香港金融市場。 主要解釋變量為一個移動-份額變量，這一變量綜合了一個經濟體在 1971 年之前與各貿易夥伴的貿易份額，以及 1971 年後各貿易夥伴貨幣對美元的匯率波動性。該變量捕捉了不同國家因歷史貿易結構，而在尼克松決策後所暴露於浮動匯率風險的程度。 在基礎估計之上，我將檢驗幾項機制。第一項機制是，外國銀行可能選擇那些已在該國設有據點的香港銀行，作為進入香港的橋樑。第二項是地理因素，因為距離當時主要國際金融中心（倫敦和紐約）較遠的國家，可能更傾向於與香港建立聯繫。第三項是法律淵源，因為普通法管轄區的銀行可能面臨較低的進入障礙。最後，我將建構一個銀行網絡資料庫，以檢視香港在 1960 及 1970 年代國際銀行網絡中的中心性。

26508826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26508826.value: AI搜索概览对互联网的影响

26508826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26508826.value: This research proposal explores the impact of Generative AI (GenAI) on the World Wide Web, with a particular emphasis on the role of AI search overviews in influencing user behavior, content supply dynamics, web structure, and business implications. Our analysis leverages the staggered introduction of Google AI search overviews across different regions over time. Preliminary findings indicate that these AI overviews on search engines reduce the overall volume of traffic to websites, suggesting a substitution effect on the demand side. However, conditional on each search and click, we observe an increase in the duration of stay and depth of interaction, indicating that AI overviews help filter out less interested viewers, resulting in a more engaged audience and targeted visits. To advance the project, we aim to conduct robustness and heterogeneity analyses to further understand the underlying mechanisms. Following the examination of demand-side dynamics, we will investigate the supply-side implications, including content creation practices and technological adoption among websites. We hypothesize that AI search overviews will lead to changes in the technological use of websites, the variety of content formats, and the differentiation of content substance. Additionally, we plan to explore how these AI-driven changes affect overall connectivity and clustering within the World Wide Web. While the demand-side substitution impairs interconnectivity, the increased engagement depth and the active responses from supply-side potentially lead to a more clustered network among specialized subsets of the web. Finally, after examining the effects on both the demand and supply sides, as well as the network structure, we aim to assess the commercial ramifications, specifically focusing on the effectiveness of advertisements in relation to user engagement with advertising content. This project seeks to provide empirical insights into the aforementioned questions. Utilizing a comprehensive dataset from SimilarWeb, which captures global internet traffic dynamics, including traffic shares, user engagement metrics, and referral sources, we plan to conduct an in-depth analysis of the effects of AI search overviews. By employing a staggered difference-in-differences methodology to rigorously evaluate the causal effects of AI search overviews across various regions and timeframes, this research aims to offer critical insights for stakeholders in the digital ecosystem. Our findings will inform strategies for adaptation in an increasingly AI-driven landscape, addressing both the opportunities and challenges presented by this technological evolution. 本研究计划探讨生成式人工智能对互联网的影响，尤其侧重于AI搜索概览在影响用户行为、内容供给动态、网络结构以及商业层面的作用。我们的分析利用了谷歌AI搜索概览在不同地区随时间推移分阶段推出这一背景。初步研究结果表明，搜索引擎上的这些AI概览减少了流向各网站的总体流量，这意味着在需求端存在替代效应。然而，在每次搜索和点击的条件下，我们观察到停留时长和互动深度有所增加，这表明AI概览有助于筛除兴趣较低的浏览者，从而带来更具参与度的受众和更有针对性的访问。为推进本项目，我们计划开展稳健性分析和异质性分析，以进一步理解其背后的作用机制。 在考察需求端动态之后，我们将研究供给端的影响，包括各网站的内容创作实践和技术采用情况。我们假设，AI搜索概览将导致网站在技术使用、内容形式多样性以及内容实质差异化方面发生变化。此外，我们计划探讨这些由AI驱动的变化如何影响整个互联网的连通性与聚类特征。尽管需求端的替代效应削弱了相互连通性，但更深的互动参与度以及供给端的积极响应，有可能在互联网中专业化的子集之间形成更为聚集的网络结构。最后，在考察了需求端与供给端的影响以及网络结构之后，我们旨在评估其商业影响，尤其关注广告投放的有效性与用户对广告内容参与度之间的关系。 本项目力求就上述问题提供实证性的洞见。我们将利用来自SimilarWeb的综合数据集（该数据集捕捉了全球互联网流量动态，包括流量份额、用户参与度指标以及引荐来源）对AI搜索概览的影响进行深入分析。通过采用分阶段双重差分方法，严谨评估AI搜索概览在不同地区和不同时间段的因果效应，本研究旨在为数字生态系统中的各利益相关方提供关键洞见。我们的研究结果将为在日益由AI主导的环境中制定适应性策略提供参考，从而应对这一技术演进所带来的机遇与挑战。

26510226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26510226.value: 多尺度重交通框架下乘積形式近似與工程應用的銜接

26510226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26510226.value: Modern computing infrastructures, such as data centers, cloud platforms, and AI inference systems, must process massive, heterogeneous workloads under stringent latency and efficiency requirements. With the rapid rise of large-scale AI models and data-driven services, these systems now often operate near capacity, where even small inefficiencies lead to substantial costs and performance degradation. Designing effective and theoretically grounded control policies is therefore increasingly important. Yet most existing algorithms remain heuristic, lacking formal performance guarantees. This project aims to build a rigorous theoretical foundation for the control of large-scale computing systems through the lens of multiclass queueing networks. Leveraging recent advances in multi-scale heavy-traffic theory, it will develop a unified approximation and optimization framework that bridges asymptotic analysis with practical control design. This research will proceed in three stages. In the first stage, we will develop a rigorous policy optimization framework for multiclass queueing networks within the Queue-Ratio policy class, a broad family that includes static buffer priority and MaxWeight service policies. Central to this stage is the construction of stability-aware and convex-approximate algorithms that translate the asymptotic product-form limit under the multi-scale heavy traffic regime into computationally tractable and theory-backed control schemes. Next, we will focus on assessing the accuracy of the product-form approximations. Building on recent advances in Stein’s method, we will derive explicit non-asymptotic convergence rates for multi-class networks to their limit under the multi-scale heavy traffic regime, thereby establishing formal convergence rates and error bounds that quantify when the limiting models provide accurate performance predictions for real systems. Lastly, we will extend the analysis to closed networks to capture feedback-coupled infrastructures such as GPU clusters and thread-pool servers. This generalization will unify open and closed network behaviors within a single theoretical framework, providing comprehensive analytical tools for performance management in large-scale computing systems. Together, these advances will deliver the first non-asymptotic performance guarantees for multi-scale product-form approximations in multiclass queueing networks, providing a principled foundation for robust and distributionally informed control in large-scale computing systems. 當今的計算基礎設施，例如數據中心、雲端平台及人工智能推理系統，需要在滿足嚴格的延遲目標和效率要求的同時，處理大規模且高度異質的工作負載。隨着大型人工智能模型及數據驅動服務的快速發展，這些系統往往在接近容量上限的狀態下運行，即使輕微的效率損失也可能導致顯著的成本增加及性能下降。因此，設計可靠且具有嚴謹理論基礎的控制策略日益重要。然而，現有大多數算法仍主要依賴啟發式方法，缺乏嚴格的性能保證。 本項目旨在以多類別排隊網絡為分析框架，為大規模服務與計算系統的控制建立嚴謹的理論基礎。基於近年來多尺度重交通理論的發展，本項目將構建一體化的近似與優化框架，將漸近分析與實際控制策略設計相銜接。本研究將分三個階段進行。 在第一階段，我們將針對多類別排隊網絡中的隊列比例控制策略，建立嚴謹的近似與優化框架。本階段的核心是構建兼顧控制策略穩定性且採用凸近似的算法，將多尺度重交通下的漸近乘積形式極限轉化為計算上可行且具有理論依據的控制策略。 接下來，我們將重點量化這些近似方法的準確性。基於近年來 Stein 方法的發展，我們將推導多類別排隊網絡在多尺度重交通框架下趨近其極限分佈的顯式非漸近收斂速率，從而建立嚴格的收斂速率與誤差界，以判定極限近似在何種條件下能夠為實際系統提供準確的性能預測。 最後，我們將把分析推廣至封閉網絡，以刻畫 GPU 叢集和線程池伺服器等具有反饋耦合特性的計算基礎設施。這一推廣將為開放網絡與封閉網絡提供統一的理論分析框架，並為大規模計算系統的性能管理提供新的分析工具。 綜合上述研究，本項目旨在推動建立多尺度重交通下乘積形式近似的非漸近性能保證，並為大規模計算系統中穩健且基於分佈信息的控制策略提供嚴謹的理論基礎。

26600926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26600926.value: 亞洲移民對美國人如何看待自己的認知及其對政治參與的影響

26600926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26600926.value: Asian immigrants are one of the fastest-growing groups in the United States, yet questions about their acceptance and belonging remain. During the COVID-19 pandemic, anti-Asian hate crimes spiked after rhetoric about the “China virus,” and East Asian communities—especially Chinese, Korean, and Japanese Americans—have faced suspicion as U.S.–China tensions spill into domestic politics. These moments highlight the persistence of the “perpetual foreigner” stereotype, even as Asian Americans become a more visible part of American life. Research shows that inaccurate beliefs about immigrants—such as inflated estimates of their numbers or misconceptions about crime and welfare—fuel prejudice and restrictive policies. But most work examines only how native-born Americans misunderstand immigrants. Much less is known about how immigrants themselves view the majority population. This project centers on meta-perceptions—what Asian immigrants believe Americans think of them. These beliefs matter: they shape whether immigrants feel accepted, trust institutions, and engage politically. Studies in partisan politics show that people often exaggerate how negatively others see them. If Asian immigrants similarly overestimate prejudice, they may feel excluded and powerless, even when majority views are more favorable. Such distortions could dampen participation and deepen marginalization. East Asians are a critical case. They account for the largest share of recent Asian immigration, are highly visible in education and the economy, and sit at the center of debates over globalization and national security. Their status is paradoxical: celebrated as a “model minority” yet treated with suspicion in times of geopolitical strain. This tension makes East Asians uniquely positioned to reveal how belonging and exclusion operate side by side. The project uses surveys and experiments to measure Asian immigrants’ perceptions of how Americans view them, compare these perceptions to actual opinion, and test whether correcting misperceptions shifts outcomes. Corrective information will allow evaluation of whether greater accuracy reduces perceived discrimination, strengthens belonging, bolsters dual identification as Asian and American, and increases political engagement. By uncovering how distorted meta-perceptions shape immigrant incorporation, the study advances research on misperceptions and democratic inclusion. It shows that fostering integration requires not only reducing majority prejudice but also addressing how immigrants themselves imagine they are seen. 亞洲移民是美國人口增長最快的群體之一，但他們是否被接納、是否具有歸屬感，仍是重要問題。新冠疫情期間，在「中國病毒」等言論出現後，針對亞裔的仇恨犯罪急劇上升；隨著中美緊張關係延伸至美國國內政治，東亞裔社群——尤其是華裔、韓裔和日裔美國人——也面臨更多猜疑。這些現象凸顯了「永遠的外國人」這一刻板印象的持續存在，即使亞裔美國人在美國社會中的能見度日益提高。 既有研究顯示，對移民的不準確認知——例如高估移民人口比例，或對移民犯罪和福利使用情況抱有錯誤觀念——會加劇偏見，並增加對限制性移民政策的支持。然而，大多數研究只關注美國本土出生人口如何誤解移民；相較之下，我們對移民如何看待主流群體所知甚少。 本研究聚焦於後設知覺（meta-perceptions），即亞洲移民認為美國人如何看待自己。這些認知十分重要，因為它們會影響移民是否感到被社會接納、是否信任制度，以及是否參與政治。政黨政治研究發現，人們往往會誇大他人對自己的負面看法。如果亞洲移民也同樣高估美國社會對他們的偏見，即使主流群體的實際態度較為正面，他們仍可能感到被排斥和缺乏政治效能感。這類認知偏差可能進一步降低政治參與，並加深其邊緣化。 東亞裔是研究這一問題的重要群體。他們在近年來的亞洲移民中佔有重要比重，在教育和經濟領域具有高度能見度，同時也處於全球化與國家安全相關政治辯論的核心。他們的社會地位具有一種矛盾性：一方面被視為「模範少數族裔」，另一方面在地緣政治緊張時期又容易受到猜疑。這種張力使東亞裔成為理解歸屬與排斥如何同時存在的重要案例。 本研究將運用問卷調查與實驗，測量亞洲移民對美國人如何看待自己的認知，將這些認知與美國人的實際態度進行比較，並檢驗矯正錯誤認知是否會改變相關結果。透過提供更準確的資訊，本研究將評估提升認知準確性是否能降低移民對歧視的感受、增強歸屬感、提升其作為亞洲人與美國人的雙重身份認同，並增加政治參與。 透過揭示扭曲的後設知覺如何影響移民融入，本研究將推進有關錯誤認知與民主包容的研究。研究指出，促進移民融入不僅需要減少主流群體的偏見，也需要關注移民如何想像他人看待自己。

26601126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26601126.value: 迈向法律服务中的可信生成式人工智能：一种具有可解释性与可验证性的治理导向法律推理系统

26601126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26601126.value: Generative AI often makes errors in legal contexts, such as providing false information, outdated or incorrect references, or reasoning that does not align with the legal system. This project aims to develop Verified Professional Services (VeriPS) to address these issues in legal AI systems. VeriPS will ensure that AI-generated legal answers are accurate, clear, and trustworthy. Unlike traditional AI, VeriPS focuses on delivering evidence-based answers. This approach will help reduce errors, improve accuracy, and make the system reliable and easy for people to review. The research involves four key stages. First, VeriPS will develop a system to verify AI-generated legal claims by linking them to authoritative sources, with strict adherence to jurisdictional and temporal parameters. Second, a bilingual legal knowledge base for Hong Kong will be created, featuring version histories and benchmarks for consistency. Third, the system will break down complex legal questions into smaller, verifiable components, using specialized tools to improve reasoning and precision. In the third stage, only outputs that meet high-confidence thresholds will be approved, with uncertain cases flagged for human review to prevent unsupported claims. Finally, in the fourth stage, the project will focus on governance and real-world application, integrating risk assessment tools, audit trails, and pilot testing with legal and corporate partners. The platform will be open sourced to promote transparency and broad adoption. Expected research outputs of the project is six-fold: 1) a governing framework will ensure that all outputs are legally sound and compliant with Hong Kong law; 2) a bilingual knowledge base comprising approximately 50,000 legal documents will be provided, with clear versioning, update histories, and timelines; 3) two datasets, Legal Verify with over one million real-world legal scenarios and Legal Decomp with over 150,000 expert-validated legal questions, will support the development and rigorous evaluation of AI systems for legal reasoning, enhancing accuracy, reliability, and practical applicability; 4) a suite of user-friendly tools will decompose legal problems, detect errors, and generate clear, accurate responses. 5) an AI platform (VeriPS), developed in partnership with industry, will offer risk management features, decision explanations, APIs, pilot deployments, security testing, and an open-source variant; and 6) an educational program will train lawyers, law students, and related professionals to effectively integrate these AI tools into legal practice. While tailored for Hong Kong's unique bilingual common law system, the framework is adaptable to other jurisdictions, providing a scalable model for trustworthy AI in legal and regulated environments. 生成式人工智能在法律场景中经常出现错误，例如提供虚假信息、过时或不正确的引用，或产生与法律体系不一致的推理。本项目旨在开发 Verified Professional Services（VeriPS），以解决法律人工智能系统中的这些问题。VeriPS 将确保人工智能生成的法律回答准确、清晰且值得信赖。不同于传统人工智能，VeriPS 强调提供以证据为基础的答案，从而减少错误、提高准确性，并使系统更可靠、更便于人工审查。 本研究包括四个主要阶段。第一，VeriPS 将开发一个系统，通过将人工智能生成的法律主张与权威来源相连接，并严格遵守司法管辖和时间参数，来验证这些法律主张。第二，项目将建立一个面向香港的双语法律知识库，包含版本历史和一致性基准。第三，系统将把复杂法律问题分解为更小且可验证的组成部分，并使用专门工具提升推理能力和准确性。在这一阶段，只有达到高置信度门槛的输出才会被批准，不确定的情况将被标记并交由人工审查，以防止无依据的主张。最后，第四阶段将聚焦治理和实际应用，整合风险评估工具、审计轨迹，并与法律和企业合作伙伴开展试点测试。该平台将以开源方式发布，以促进透明度和广泛采用。 本项目预期产生六方面研究成果：第一，建立一个治理框架，确保所有输出在法律上可靠，并符合香港法律；第二，提供一个包含约 50,000 份法律文件的双语知识库，并具备清晰的版本记录、更新历史和时间线；第三，建设两个数据集，即包含超过一百万个真实法律场景的 Legal Verify，以及包含超过 150,000 个经专家验证的法律问题的 Legal Decomp，用于支持法律推理人工智能系统的开发和严格评估，提升其准确性、可靠性和实践适用性；第四，开发一套用户友好的工具，用于分解法律问题、检测错误并生成清晰准确的回答；第五，与业界合作开发人工智能平台 VeriPS，提供风险管理、决策解释、应用程序接口、试点部署、安全测试和开源版本；第六，建立教育项目，培训律师、法律学生及相关专业人士，使其能够有效地将这些人工智能工具应用于法律实践。 虽然本项目针对香港独特的双语普通法体系设计，但该框架也可适用于其他司法管辖区，为法律及其他受监管环境中的可信人工智能提供可扩展的模型。

26605326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26605326.value: 中國的「斷」與「連」：1937–1957年西北地區的數碼探索

26605326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26605326.value: This project investigates the transformation and significance of Northwest China from 1937 to 1957, a period shaped by the Sino-Japanese War and its aftermath. As the war forced a re-imagination of the country’s centre and peripheries, the Northwest emerged as the critical “rear area” (houfang) in Chinese discourse. To address gaps in existing research, this study focuses on the interplay between infrastructural actors, spatial discourses, and material infrastructures, all of which influenced the region’s development. By employing digital methods such as network analysis, topic modelling, and transport simulation, the project examines how personal and institutional relationships, historical narratives, and material infrastructures intersected to shape the spatial dynamics of national integration during this transformative period. Central to the research is the exploration of how key actors shaped and were shaped by spatial imaginations and infrastructural development. The project traces these interrelationships through archival sources, historical maps, and generated datasets, reconstructing transportation routes and uncovering the dynamics of movement and interaction in and with the Northwest. By combining spatial analysis with historical network studies, the project provides a systematic account of the Northwest’s evolving role under changing geopolitical conditions. Thereby, the study aims to demonstrate how historical ruptures influence imaginations and materialisations of space and infrastructure. It uncovers the Northwest’s strategic importance in fostering national integration and highlights the reciprocal influences between spatial discourse and material outcomes. The use of innovative digital methods enhances traditional historical research and offers new insights to the broader field of digital humanities. By examining the historical context of spatial relations, the project provides a framework for understanding how the dynamics of infrastructure, discourse, and space continue to influence contemporary practices. Ultimately, this project advances our understanding of the Northwest’s historical significance and demonstrates the transformative potential of integrating digital methods with historical inquiry. 本項目旨在探討 1937 至 1957 年間中國西北地區的轉型與歷史意義，這段時期深受中日戰爭及其後續影響所形塑。隨著戰爭迫使人們重新想像國家的「中心」與「邊緣」，西北地區在中國的論述中躍升為關鍵的「後方」。為填補現有研究的空白，本研究聚焦於基礎設施行動者、空間論述與實體基礎設施之間的相互作用，這些因素共同影響了該地區的發展。 本項目運用網絡分析、主題建模與交通模擬等數碼方法，檢視在這段轉型期內，個人與機構關係、歷史敘事以及實體基礎設施如何交織，進而形塑國家整合的空間動態。本研究的核心在於探討關鍵行動者如何形塑空間想像與基礎設施的發展，同時又如何受其影響。項目透過檔案史料、歷史地圖及生成的數據集來追溯這些相互關係，重建交通路線，並揭示在西北地區內部及其對外流動與互動的動態。 透過結合空間分析與歷史網絡研究，本項目系統性地闡述了西北地區在不斷變化的地緣政治條件下持續演變的角色。因此，本研究旨在展示歷史斷裂如何影響空間與基礎設施的想像及實體化。它揭示了西北地區在促進國家整合中的戰略重要性，並突顯了空間論述與實體成果之間的相互影響。 創新數碼方法的運用不僅提升了傳統歷史研究，亦為更廣泛的數碼人文領域提供了新見解。透過檢視空間關係的歷史脈絡，本項目提供了一個分析框架，有助於理解基礎設施、論述與空間的動態如何持續影響當代實踐。最終，本項目深化了我們對西北地區歷史意義的理解，並展示了將數碼方法與歷史探究相結合所具備的變革潛力。

27103426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27103426.value: 個別化即時通訊之身體活動數位教練與訓練介入對肺癌倖存者癌症相關認知障礙之成效：務實型隨機對照試驗

27103426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27103426.value: Lung cancer is the most common cancer in Hong Kong and survival rate is continuing to rise. Lung cancer survivors often have cancer-related cognitive impairment (CRCI), which has significant impacts on their treatment decision-making, treatment adherence, overall survival, and quality of life. However, research on CRCI, particularly nonpharmacological intervention, is insufficient, resulting in limited options and lack of high-quality evidence. The aim of the proposed research project is to investigate the effectiveness of physical activity e-coaching through instant message-delivered ecological momentary intervention for improving objective cognitive performance in lung cancer survivors. The project will randomly assign eligible participants (n = 270) to either the intervention group or self-management control group. The intervention will involve physical activity e-coaching messages tailored to the participants’ physical activity levels and preferences delivered in plain language via instant messaging application (WhatsApp). The messages will introduce behavioral goals and action plans, encourage participants to adopt various tactics, and remind them to exercise regularly. In addition to regular messages, participants will also receive real-time, chat-based support. Self-determination theory and information-motivation-behavioral skills model will be used as a theoretical framework to guide the intervention’s development and delivery. The self-management control group will not receive physical activity e-coaching messages. Participants in both groups will be provided with a wearable fitness tracker. The primary outcome will be objective cognitive performance. The secondary outcomes include perceived cognitive complaints, physical activity, active minutes, and daily step count, fatigue, anxiety, depression, quality of life, self-efficacy, and cost-effectiveness assessed at baseline, 3, 6, and 9 months. We will also perform post-trial qualitative assessment for process evaluation. The project holds significant promise as the first randomized controlled trial to examine the effectiveness of ecological momentary intervention in enhancing objective cognitive performance among lung cancer survivors. The study will contribute not only to the fields of cancer care and public health guidance, but also to the research on neuropsychiatric conditions and mHealth interventions for promoting physical activity. Furthermore, the project outcomes will provide insights into the application of ecological momentary interventions for lung cancer survivors. If proven effective, the proposed intervention could become an efficient, real-time, real-world, cost-effective approach for improving CRCI in lung cancer survivors. The project will address the lack of nonpharmacological interventions for lung cancer survivors with CRCI and inform the development of future interventions for this population. 肺癌為香港最常見之癌症，其存活率持續上升。肺癌倖存者常出現癌症相關認知障礙，對其治療決策、治療依從性、整體存活率及生活品質產生重大影響。然而，針對癌症相關認知障礙之研究，尤其是非藥物介入研究，仍顯不足，導致可用選項有限且缺乏高質量實證。 本研究計劃旨在探討透過即時通訊遞送之生態瞬間介入進行身體活動數位教練，對改善肺癌倖存者客觀認知表現之成效。本計劃將符合資格之參與者（n = 270）隨機分配至介入組或自我管理對照組。介入組將接收以參與者身體活動水平及偏好為基礎個別化設計之身體活動數位教練訊息，透過即時通訊應用程式（WhatsApp）以通俗語言傳送。訊息內容包括設定行為目標與行動計劃、鼓勵參與者採用多元策略，並提醒其規律運動。除定期訊息外，參與者亦將獲得即時通訊為基礎之支援。本研究將以自我決定理論及資訊─動機─行為技能模型作為理論架構，指導介入之設計與執行。自我管理對照組將不接收身體活動數位教練訊息。兩組參與者均將獲配發可穿戴式健身追蹤器。主要結果指標為客觀認知表現；次要結果指標包括主觀認知抱怨、身體活動量、活動分鐘數、每日步數、疲勞、焦慮、抑郁、生活品質、自我效能及成本效益，並分別於基線、3 個月、6 個月及 9 個月進行評估。本研究亦將於試驗結束後進行質性評估，以進行過程評價。 本計劃具重要意義，將以隨機對照試驗檢驗生態瞬間介入對提升肺癌倖存者客觀認知表現之成效。本研究不僅將貢獻於癌症照護與公共衛生指引領域，亦將豐富神經精神疾病及促進身體活動之行動健康照護（mHealth）介入研究。此外，本計劃成果將為生態瞬間介入於肺癌倖存者群體之應用提供實證依據。 若證實有效，本擬議介入可成為改善肺癌倖存者癌症相關認知障礙之高效、即時、貼近真實世界且具成本效益之方法。本計劃將填補肺癌倖存者 癌症相關認知障礙非藥物介入之不足，並為未來針對此群體之介入發展提供指引。

27106126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27106126.value: 新型納米塗層工程化口腔益生菌靶向治療牙周病的作用機制研究

27106126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27106126.value: Background: Periodontal diseases are common and crucial oral health issues that closely connect to systemic comorbidities through shared risk factors and immuno‑inflammatory pathways, thereby impairing general wellbeing, quality of life and increasing enormous healthcare costs. Porphyromonas gingivalis (Pg), the keystone pathogen, drives disease progression by disrupting oral polymicrobial balance and subverting host immune-inflammatory responses. An integrative therapy concurrently eradicating Pg, modulating immune responses, and re‑establishing a resilient oral microbiota, would be ideal to treat periodontal disease effectively. Research gap: Existing therapies (e.g., biofilm removal and antibiotic application) fail to integrate these actions. Probiotics are attractive alternative approaches for periodontal treatment, while the transient colonization of gut‑derived probiotics significantly limits their applications in oral healthcare. How to develop functional oral-resident probiotics remains challenging. Likewise, the feasibility of using nanotechnology like metal-phenolic network coatings to enhance the functionality of oral-resident probiotics has not been reported. Importantly, lack of biomimetic 3D models for recapitulating the host–microbe interactions in periodontal niches restricts mechanistic discovery and therapeutic innovation. Rationale & objectives: Our preliminary work demonstrates: i) bismuth‑based nano/micromaterials selectively eliminate Pg and restore Pg-perturbed immuno-inflammatory responses; ii) the oral commensal Streptococcus dentisani shows ecological advantages in restoring oral microbial symbiosis; and 3) our developed cavitated oral epithelial spheroids provide a biomimetic 3D infection model for precisely evaluating host–pathogen/probiotic interactions. Herein, we introduce the first functional oral-resident “cyborg” probiotic by arming the surface of S. dentisani with bismuth–tannic acid nanocoating (Bi‑TA‑Sd). This novel approach strategically integrates ecological benefits of an oral-resident commensal with antipathogenic and immunomodulatory properties of our recently constructed bismuth-based nanoparticles, enabling a powerful triple-targeting therapy tackling periodontal diseases. Specifical objectives are to i) develop Bi-TA-Sd and evaluate its antimicrobial/antibiofilm efficacy against periodontal pathogens; ii) assess its immunomodulatory effects on Pg-infected cells; iii) evaluate its barrier protective and pathogen colonization resistant effects using 2D and 3D oral epithelial models; and iv) validate its therapeutic potential in a rat periodontitis model. Perspectives: This pioneering strategy addresses the critical limitations of current periodontal treatments by introducing a sustainable triple-targeting therapeutic approach to restoring microbial balance, strengthening host defenses, and reducing disease recurrence. The innovation establishes a versatile platform technology to endow probiotics with multifunctional therapeutic effects, making it applicable to other dysbiosis‑induced and inflammation-driven systemic comorbidities for enhancing oral and general health. 牙周病作為一種高發的口腔慢性感染性疾病，通過共同的危險因素與多種全身系統性疾病密切相關。當前牙周炎的臨床治療手段較為單一，多依賴機械生物膜清除和局部抗生素應用，這類方法僅能暫時降低局部細菌負荷，難以從根本上恢復牙周組織的免疫穩態與微生態平衡。近年來益生菌療法在重塑微生態方面展現出巨大潛力，有望成為理想的替代方案，但受限於複雜的口腔環境和定植障礙，極大限制了其臨床應用。因此，亟需開發具有強效定植與多維治療功能的新型活體生物藥。同時，現有研究多依賴二維（2D）細胞模型，缺乏能夠真實重現牙周微環境中“宿主-微生物”互作網絡的三維（3D）仿生模型，也制約了相關療法的機制探究與療效評估。 基於此，本項目擬在口腔共生菌 Streptococcus dentisani（Sd）表面原位包覆鉍基納米塗層，首次提出並構建新型“表面工程化口腔益生菌”。為進一步闡明其作用機制與有效性，本項目擬開展以下研究：1）開發工程化益生菌，並評估其針對牙周病致病菌的抗菌與抗生物膜功效；2）評估工程化益生菌對受牙周致病菌感染細胞的免疫調節作用；3）利用2D和3D口腔上皮模型，評估工程化益生菌屏障保護及抵抗病原體定植的作用；4）在大鼠牙周炎模型中驗證工程化益生菌的治療潛力。 本項目創新性地提出了一種可持續的靶向干預策略，有望突破當前牙周臨床治療復發率高的局限，實現微生態平衡重塑與宿主免疫防禦增強。同時，本研究建立的益生菌表面工程化平台技術，不僅賦予了傳統益生菌多維度的治療潛力，也為干預其他由菌群失調或免疫炎症驅動的全身系統性併發症提供了全新的通用型策略，對助力全民口腔與全身健康具有重要的科學價值與臨床轉化前景。

27110426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27110426.value: 基於人工智慧的增強現實在電腦輔助腓骨瓣手術中的應用：一項隨機對照臨床試驗

27110426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27110426.value: Background: Computer-assisted surgery has reshaped functional jaw reconstruction, allowing immediate rehabilitation of form and function. The fibula free flap (FFF) is the workhorse of computer-assisted jaw reconstruction. Accurate and efficient localization of skin-perforating vessels (perforators) is critical for safe and efficient computer-assisted FFF harvest, as the perforators need to be carefully protected to avoid kinking or twisting during flap inset, especially when a complicated fibula configuration and immediate dental rehabilitation are desired for optimal aesthetics and occlusion. However, with current methods, such as color Doppler ultrasonography (USG), incorporating the perforator course into virtual surgical planning is challenging. The technique can also be operator-dependent and time-consuming for inexperienced operators during surgery. Artificial intelligence (AI) and augmented reality (AR) offer promising alternatives by automating 3D modeling of perforators to incorporate into planning and real-time projection of perforators onto the patient’s leg during surgery. Work done so far: We recently developed an integrated AR-AI workflow to streamline computer-assisted jaw reconstruction. Our publication (Pu et al, PRS, 2025) demonstrated the high accuracy of perforator identification using the AI tool. However, its effectiveness and efficiency remain to be compared with the current top-standard technique via a randomised controlled trial. Objective: This randomized controlled clinical trial aims to evaluate whether an integrated AI-AR guidance system offers more efficient perforator identification with non-inferior accuracy and skin paddle survival when compared with the gold standard USG technique. Methods: Patients requiring computer-assisted FFF jaw reconstruction will be randomised 1:1 to either the AI-AR or USG group. Both groups will receive the same computer-assisted surgery workflow established by our team. The AI-AR group will have AI-based segmentation and AR projection of perforators. The USG group will receive colour Doppler USG mapping. Primary endpoints include the time spent on perforator identification, accuracy, and skin paddle survival rates. Secondary endpoints comprise total time spent for FFF harvest, free flap ischemic time, inter-rater reliability, and factors affecting the performance of both systems. Expected Outcomes: We anticipate that the AI-AR system will increase the efficiency of surgery by facilitating the easy identification and incorporation of perforators with non-inferior accuracy and skin paddle survival rates. Significance: This study will provide Level I evidence on the AI-AR system for computer-assisted FFF harvest. It will establish a new standard for computer-assisted jaw reconstruction, enhance surgical predictability and workflow efficiency, and streamline virtual surgical planning and real-time surgery. 背景： 電腦輔助手術已徹底重塑功能性顎骨重建，使形態與功能得以即時復健。腓骨游離瓣（FFF）是電腦輔助顎骨重建的主力。準確且有效率地定位皮膚穿支血管（穿支）對安全、高效的電腦輔助腓骨游離瓣採集至關重要，因為在皮瓣置入時必須小心保護這些穿支，避免扭曲或扭結，尤其當需要複雜的腓骨構型並進行即時牙科復健以達到最佳美觀與咬合時。然而，目前的方法（如彩色都卜勒超聲）難以將穿支路徑納入虛擬手術規劃，且對經驗不足的手術者而言，操作可能依賴個人經驗且耗時較長。人工智慧（AI）與增強現實（AR）提供了有前景的替代方案，可自動建立穿支的三維模型並納入虛擬手術規劃，並在手術中即時將穿支投影到病人小腿上。 目前已完成的工作： 我們已經開發了一套整合的AI-AR工作流程，以簡化電腦輔助顎骨重建。我們的論文（Pu et al, PRS, 2025）已證明該AI工具在穿支辨識上具有較高準確性。然而，其有效性與效率仍需透過隨機對照試驗與目前的黃金標準技術進行比較。 目的： 本隨機對照臨床試驗旨在評估整合的AI-AR導引系統，與黃金標準的彩色都卜勒超聲技術相比，是否能更有效率地辨識穿支，同時準確性與皮島存活率不劣於對照組。 方法： 需要接受電腦輔助腓骨游離瓣顎骨重建的病人將以1:1比例隨機分配至AI-AR組或超聲組。兩組皆採用本團隊既有的電腦輔助手術流程。AI-AR組將使用AI進行穿支分割並以AR投影；超聲組則接受彩色都卜勒超聲定位。主要終點包括穿支辨識所需時間、準確性及皮島存活率。次要終點則包括腓骨游離瓣採集總時間、游離皮瓣缺血時間、評分者間信度，以及影響兩種系統表現的因素。 預期結果： 我們預期AI-AR系統能透過簡化穿支的辨識與納入規劃，提升手術效率，同時準確性與皮島存活率不劣於對照組。 意義： 本研究將為電腦輔助腓骨游離瓣採集的AI-AR系統提供一級證據，建立電腦輔助顎骨重建的新標準，提升手術可預測性與工作流程效率，並簡化虛擬手術規劃與手術過程。

27123326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27123326.value: 解碼人類軀幹類器官中的 WNT–FGF 訊號傳導，以闡明驅動脊索特化與成熟的發育因子。

27123326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27123326.value: The notochord is an essential embryonic structure located at the center of all chordate embryos. Besides a structural scaffold supporting embryo growth, the notochord is a source of signals that pattern surrounding tissues originating cell populations such as motor neurons, cartilage and bone. Notochordal cells are critical for intervertebral disc formation and later give rise to the nucleus pulposus, the gelatinous cushion at the center of the discs, whose decline with age stands as the main culprit behind intervertebral disc disease – a major clinical burden in an ageing population. Undifferentiated cells can also undergo malignant transformation and generate rare but aggressive cancers. Despite its importance, our understanding of notochord formation and maturation, and how it shapes surrounding tissues in human embryos remains very limited. Our work investigating trunk development in vertebrates led us to hypothesize the importance of TGFb family inhibition in notochord formation. Our findings revealed that timed inhibition resulted in the intermediate levels of NODAL signaling required for notochord induction in 2D micropatterned colonies of human embryonic stem cells and 3D spheroids. This signaling logic was used to generate for the first time a “trunk-organoid” juxtaposing the three major lineages of the human trunk: neural, somitic and notochordal. This in vitro notochord can pattern surrounding cell populations generating ventral neural and sclerotome (cartilage and bone) tissues. However, the molecular and cellular mechanisms governing the formation of trunk tissues remain elusive. Preliminary data from trunk-organoids suggests a plethora of endogenous signaling and morphogenetic events steer cell fate decisions, as in the embryo. This offers a unique, mid-complexity, and readily-accessible system to further dissecting the molecular principles of human trunk formation. This project has two major goals. First, to undertake a comprehensive investigation of human embryonic trunk formation and, second, to find the signals required for each of the trunk’s major cell populations, focusing on FGF signaling. For this, we will use trunk-organoids to perform live-imaging of signaling reporters together with time-resolved single-cell transcriptomics of the organoid’s earlier stages. These data will further be useful to compare with recent snapshots of in vivo data. In parallel, we will further mature trunk-organoids into cell populations relevant to adult human diseases. The project outcomes will have wide ranging translational implications: a deeper understanding of cartilage, bone and notochordal cells signaling requirements and developmental checkpoints will improve current limitations in direct differentiations relevant to regenerative medicine. 脊索是位於神經管腹側的棒狀結構，也是所有脊索動物胚胎的核心結構之一。它一方面像支架一樣支撐着胚胎的生長，另一方面，脊索細胞會釋放化學訊號，指引鄰近的細胞——這些細胞隨後會發育成運動神經元、軟骨和骨骼。脊索細胞對椎間盤的形成不可或缺，日後更會發育成髓核——即椎間盤中央的膠狀緩衝組織。髓核隨年齡退化，是椎間盤疾病的主要成因；在人口老化的社會，這類疾病帶來沉重的醫療負擔。此外，未分化的脊索細胞也可能發生惡性轉變，形成罕見但極具侵襲性的脊索瘤。 儘管脊索如此重要，我們對它在人類胚胎中如何形成與成熟、以及如何塑造周圍組織，所知仍然非常有限。 我們過往研究脊椎動物軀幹發育的經驗，令我們推測：適時抑制 TGF-β 這一組細胞訊號，是脊索形成的關鍵。研究結果證實，這種「定時抑制」能把細胞之間傳遞的化學訊號維持在誘導脊索所需的中等強度——無論在體外合成的平面微型組織，或立體的細胞聚集體中皆然。 我們運用這套訊號原理，首次培育出「軀幹類器官」：一個在培養皿中生長的迷你軀幹模型，同時包含人類軀幹的三大細胞譜系——神經、體節（肌肉與脊骨的前身）與脊索。當中的體外脊索細胞確實能指引周圍的細胞，令它們發育成腹側的神經組織，以及日後形成軟骨與骨骼的組織。 不過，主導軀幹組織形成的分子與細胞機制仍然不明。初步數據顯示，類器官內部同樣有大量自發的訊號傳遞與形態變化在引導細胞的命運選擇，一如真正的胚胎。這使它成為一個複雜程度適中、又容易操作的獨特系統，可用來進一步剖析人類軀幹形成的分子原理。 本計劃有兩大目標：第一，全面研究人類胚胎軀幹的形成過程；第二，找出軀幹各主要細胞群所需的訊號，並以 FGF 訊號為重點。為此，我們會利用軀幹類器官，一方面以活細胞實時成像追蹤細胞內訊號的變化，另一方面在類器官發育初期進行逐時的單細胞基因表達分析。這些數據亦可與近期取自真實人類胚胎的資料互相比對。與此同時，我們會令軀幹類器官進一步成熟，培育出與成年人疾病相關的細胞類型，以探究致病機制與潛在治療靶點。 本計劃的成果具廣泛的臨床轉譯意義：更深入了解軟骨、骨骼與脊索細胞所需的訊號和發育關卡，將有助改善目前以幹細胞直接培育特定細胞的技術瓶頸，推動再生醫學的發展。

27129426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27129426.value: 解析LytR調控因子FN0219在具核梭桿菌生物膜形成中的作用，並闡明其抑制劑化合物S的作用機制

27129426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27129426.value: Fusobacterium nucleatum is a keystone pathogen in oral biofilms, acting as a critical bridge between early and late colonizers. Its control is vital for treating periodontitis and preventing associated systemic diseases like colorectal cancer. Our pilot work using a CRISPRi screen identified FN0219, a LytR-type regulator, as essential for F. nucleatum biofilm formation. Objective 1: Elucidate the Regulatory Mechanism of FN0219. FN0219 is annotated as part of a two-component system (YpdB) and autolysin regulator. Intriguingly, it remains essential for biofilm in an autolysin-deficient strain, suggesting it operates through novel pathways. Our comparative proteomics of a ΔFN0219 mutant revealed significant dysregulation, including the down-regulation of key peptide transporters, lysine degradation enzymes (KamA, KamD), metal import systems, and virulence factors (FadA, FplA). To define its regulon, we will: 1) Identify FN0219's direct DNA binding sites via DNase I footprinting; 2) Validate the functional contribution of downstream genes to biofilm using inducible knockdown and promoter replacement assays; and 3) Evaluate the importance of FN0219 in relevant cell based assays and in vivo models of periodontitis and tumorigenesis. Objective 2: Decipher the Mode of Action of Inhibitor Compound S. We have identified Compound S, a non-bactericidal inhibitor that targets FN0219. Supporting this, FN0219 overexpression diminishes Compound S's anti-biofilm effect, and a direct physical interaction has been confirmed by waterLOGSY NMR. We will now: 1) Profile the transcriptomic changes induced by Compound S treatment; 2) Assess its anti-biofilm spectrum across diverse F. nucleatum clinical isolates; and 3) Confirm target specificity through comprehensive chemical genetics, classic genetics approach and mutagenesis screens. This research is paramount as it will unravel a novel regulatory network controlling a key pathogen's virulence. By validating FN0219 as a drug target and characterizing a promising inhibitor, this work paves the way for developing innovative anti-virulence strategies to combat periodontitis and Fn-associated systemic diseases. 具核梭桿菌（Fusobacterium nucleatum）是口腔生物膜中的關鍵病原菌，連接早期與晚期的定殖菌。控制此菌對治療牙周炎及預防相關全身性疾病（如大腸直腸癌）非常重要。我們先前的CRISPRi篩選發現，FN0219這個LytR家族調控因子，是具核梭桿菌形成生物膜所必需的。 目標一：了解FN0219的調控機制。 FN0219被歸類為雙組分系統（YpdB）和自溶素調控因子。有趣的是，在缺乏自溶素的菌株中，FN0219仍然影響生物膜形成，表示它可能透過新的機制發揮作用。我們比較了ΔFN0219突變株的蛋白質組學表現，發現多個基因表現異常，包括肽轉運蛋白、賴氨酸分解酶（KamA、KamD）、金屬攝取系統及毒力因子（FadA、FplA）皆下降。為釐清FN0219調控的基因，我們將：（1）用DNase I足跡法找出FN0219的DNA結合位置；（2）用基因靜默和啟動子置換實驗驗證下游基因對生物膜的影響；（3）在細胞實驗和動物模式中評估FN0219的重要性。 目標二：釐清抑制劑化合物S的作用方式。 我們找到化合物S，它能抑制FN0219但不會殺死細菌。FN0219過量表達會降低化合物S的效果，且NMR實驗也證實兩者可直接結合。接下來我們將：（1）分析化合物S處理後的基因表現變化；（2）測試它對不同臨床菌株的抗生物膜效果；（3）用化學遺傳學、經典遺傳學和突變篩選確認它的專一性。 總結來說，這項研究將揭示一個調控此病原菌毒力的新網絡。 同時，我們也驗證FN0219可作為藥物靶點，並初步確認化合物S的潛力，為未來開發抗毒力療法來對抗牙周炎和具核梭桿菌相關疾病打下基礎。

27201226.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27201226.value: 基於足尺實驗和精準仿真的鋼-混凝土組合組裝合成建築抗震設計優化

27201226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27201226.value: Modular integrated Construction (MiC) is the most advanced form of prefabrication technology and has achieved significant savings in construction labor, time, and costs. However, current MiC buildings in Hong Kong were not required to meet seismic design requirements, whereas all other infrastructure in Hong Kong has incorporated seismic design. Chinese National code also designates Hong Kong buildings with a Design Basis Earthquake Peak Ground Acceleration of 0.15g. There is an urgent need to develop seismic resilient modular structures for Hong Kong and beyond. This project will develop novel seismic-resilient steel-concrete composite modular structures combining large-scale experiments, high-fidelity Finite Element (FE) simulation, and differentiable Artificial Intelligence (AI) solver. The proposed system will combine the advantages of steel and concrete materials to achieve disaster resilience under severe wind or seismic loads. The tensile strength of steel and the compressive strength of concrete will be fully utilized, and steel buckling will be mitigated by concrete. Efficient module-to-module connection details will be investigated to achieve the rigid diaphragm effect and ensure the stiffness, ductility, and durability of the composite modular structural system under extreme seismic excitations and severe wind loads. Our preliminary study achieved seismic design and nonlinear FE simulations for a 32-story high-rise composite modular building. Our preliminary study developed a Recurrent Physics Operator (RPO) based on Fourier Neural Operators (FNO) and Newmark-β time integrator for differentiable AI simulations of structural seismic performance, achieving significant speedup over nonlinear FE simulations. The proposed project will develop a novel steel-concrete composite modular structural system and a high-fidelity simulation platform for structural resilience under wind and seismic disasters. A full-scale experimental program will be conducted at the module-to-module connection level and module level via static hysteretic tests and shake table tests. The research outcomes of this project include: (1) a full-scale experimental dataset to discover the force transfer mechanism and seismic performance of module-to-module connections and module sub-structures. (2) High-fidelity FE simulation framework for full-process disaster performance prediction of composite modular structures validated by full-scale experiments. (3) Differentiable AI Digital Twin to simulate seismic response of composite modular structures combining the Newmark-β time integrator and Neural Operators. (4) Efficient design optimization framework for modular composite structures combining gradient-based optimization and differentiable AI Digital Twin. The proposed research will promote computational design optimization of composite modular structures with notably reduced material usage and construction costs and significantly improved resilience under severe disasters. 組裝合成建築（Modular Integrated Construction，MiC）是最先進的預製建築技術形式，已實現了節省建築人力、時間及成本方面取得顯著成效。然而，目前香港的組裝合成建築並未被要求符合抗震設計規定，而香港其他各類基礎設施均已納入抗震設計。中國國家規範亦規定，香港建築的設計基準地震峰值地面加速度為 0.15g。因此，香港及其他地區亟需發展具抗震韌性的組裝合成結構。本項目將結合大型實驗、精準有限元分析及可微分人工智能（AI）求解器，開發新型具抗震韌性的鋼—混凝土組合模塊化結構。本研究將結合鋼材與混凝土材料的優勢，充分發揮鋼材的抗拉強度與混凝土的抗壓強度，且混凝土可抑制鋼材屈曲，從而在強風或地震荷載作用下實現模塊化組合結構災害韌性。本研究將探討高效的模塊間連接構造以實現剛性樓板效應，並確保組合模塊化結構系統在極端地震激勵及強風荷載作用下具備足夠的剛度、延性及耐久性。 我們的初步研究已完成一棟 32 層高層組合模塊化建築的抗震設計及非線性有限元分析。我們亦開發了一種基於傅立葉神經算子（Fourier Neural Operators，FNO）和Newmark-β 時間格式的循環物理算子（Recurrent Physics Operator，RPO），用於結構抗震性能的可微分人工智能模擬。相較於非線性有限元分析，該方法實現了顯著的計算加速。 本擬議項目將開發一套新型模塊化鋼—混凝土組合結構系統和一個用於評估結構在風災與地震災害下韌性的精準模擬平台。研究將在模組間連接層面及模組層面開展足尺實驗計劃，包括靜力滯回試驗及振動台試驗。本項目的研究成果包括：（1）足尺實驗數據集，用於揭示模組間連接及模組子結構的傳力機制與抗震性能；（2）精準有限元分析框架，用於組合模塊化結構全過程災害性能預測，並通過全尺寸實驗驗證；（3）可微分人工智能數字孿生系統，結合 Newmark-β 時間格式與神經算子，以模擬模塊化組合結構的地震反應；（4）高效設計優化框架，結合梯度式優化方法與可微分人工智能數碼孿生系統，用於組合模塊化結構的設計優化。本研究將推動組裝合成組合結構的計算設計優化，在顯著減少材料用量及建造成本的同時，大幅提升組裝合成結構的災害韌性。

27202626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27202626.value: 小鼠著床前胚胎微管網絡組織模式的力學調控機制

27202626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27202626.value: Early mammalian development relies on a precisely organised cytoskeleton, involving actin filaments and microtubules (MTs). While actin filaments mediate cell contractility, microtubules (MTs) are rigid polymers that provide structural support, guide intracellular transport, and assemble the spindle for chromosome segregation. In addition to these homeostatic functions, in vitro studies suggest that MTs are also mechanical elements that can both respond to and generate forces. Importantly, proper MT organisation is essential for embryonic development, as its disruption can lead to rapid developmental arrest. In preimplantation mouse embryos, a striking feature is the absence of centrioles—the scaffold of centrosomes that normally serve as major MT-organising centres. Centrioles only emerge later through de novo assembly, but the timing, mechanisms, and consequences of this process remain poorly characterised. Recent studies further indicate that, during morphogenesis, preimplantation embryos are shaped by coordinated forces through processes such as compaction and blastocoel formation. However, how MT network organisation is mechanically regulated in this context, particularly in relation to the appearance of centrioles, remains largely unknown. Emerging progress in MT mechanics and expansion microscopy (ExM) now offers the opportunity to address these fundamental questions. Developing ExM for in vitro cell lines reveals the ultrastructural assembly of daughter centrioles during the cell cycle, while advanced live-cell imaging can characterise MT dynamics with high spatiotemporal resolution. Optical tweezers and complementary methods also provide powerful tools to measure the mechanical properties of cells. By combining these methodologies, this project aims to uncover the mechano-regulatory mechanisms underlying MT network organisation in preimplantation mouse embryos. The outcomes will advance our understanding of the fundamental principles of embryonic morphogenesis, which in turn can contribute to combating infertility and promoting stem cell research and organ engineering. 生殖力直接關係到國家人口發展戰略和國民健康。輔助生殖技術ART作為臨床調控生育力的核心手段，目前仍面臨約半數胚胎發育停滯的風險，其主要成因是染色體分離錯誤。而染色體分離高度依賴微管骨架組織模式和紡錘體組裝。中心粒作為微管網絡主要的組織中心，在很多哺乳動物早期胚胎中，經歷了“從無到有”的組裝過程。然而，我們對該過程發生的時間節點、調控機制及其對發育穩態的影響知之甚少。再者，早期胚胎形態建成過程中伴隨著大量的內源性機械力信號。例如，8-細胞階段卵裂球皮質層出現的週期性機械波和囊胚期的肌動蛋白膜泡化。這些力學信號如何影響中心粒的形成和微管網絡的組織模式仍不清晰。針對上述科學問題，本項目將融合膨脹顯微鏡和雙視野光片顯微鏡等高分辨率成像技術，繪製小鼠胚胎中微管網絡和中心粒超微結構的時空演化圖譜；採用光鑷和胚胎宏觀力学表徵技術，在不同尺度對活體胚胎的生物力學特性進行測量和擾動；通過整合這些前沿方法，本項目旨在揭示著床前胚胎中微管網絡組織模式的力學調控機制。研究結果將完善我們對早期胚胎形態建成的理解，進而在優化ART，對抗不孕不育症、幹細胞研究以及器官工程技術等領域產生重要影響。

27203526.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27203526.value: 用於高能量密度電池的分子電解質設計

27203526.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27203526.value: As the core carrier of new energy technologies, high-energy-density batteries are the key to promoting multi-scene applications (drones, robotics, EVs). Materials such as Li/Na metals, silicon anodes, and Ni-rich cathodes are ideal candidates due to their high specific capacity, abundant resources, and low cost. However, these materials are incompatible with current commercial electrolytes due to the formation of organic-rich electrode-electrolyte interphases. The organic-rich interphases are prone to fracture upon continuous charging/discharging. This interphase breakdown triggers electrolyte depletion, promotes the growth of metal dendrites, and causes electrode particle cracks, resulting in rapid cell failure and significant safety hazards. One feasible approach is to construct inorganic-rich interphases through electrolyte design. For example, high-concentration and localized high-concentration electrolytes are used to regulate the anion-enriched solvation for inorganic-rich interphase formation, however, the eye-catching drawbacks are the high cost and low ionic conductivity. Inspired by this working principle, strategies have been developed to fine-tune the electrolyte solvation structure with different diluents and solvents. Another successful approach is the use of fluorinated electrolytes, where both solvents and salts have abundant fluorine for metal fluoride interphase formation.
