Prior research has leveraged the learning-by-teaching approach to build teachable bots/agents (software “students” that learn from what human students teach them). Although these bots showed learning benefits, they were costly to build and limited to fixed design rules. GenAI offers opportunities to create teachable bots that simulate peer students and embody diverse student characteristics, including different levels of prior knowledge and communication styles (e.g., questioners or answer-givers). These variations create learning conditions that require students to adapt explanations, monitor understanding, and regulate strategies; the dialogue with the bots also gives students practice with communication and self-reflection. The project aims to develop and test design principles and methods for using GenAI-powered teachable bots that function as peer students. By calibrating GenAI behaviour, the bots will reflect variations in prior knowledge and communication styles. Their effectiveness will be evaluated through randomised controlled trials in university classes that test learning gains, motivation, metacognition, and how students participate and explain ideas in both one-to-one tutoring and triads. Triads will include both two students with one bot and one student with two bots. The trials will also examine how variations in the bots’ prior knowledge and communication styles affect learning processes and outcomes. The project will investigate interaction patterns over time to guide adaptive mechanisms that sustain engagement and support regulation. The contributions of this research will be multifold. Conceptually, it will extend the learning-by-teaching approach into GenAI settings. Methodologically, it will provide design principles for configuring GenAI models to simulate diverse student characteristics, together with process-sensitive measures that capture how students teach and interact with simulated peers. Empirically, it will offer evidence from randomised trials on effects for learning gains, metacognition, and communication. Practically, it will produce design principles for teachable bots and guidelines for integrating them into classes. All contributions will be implemented in an open-source platform to maximise impact in higher education and strengthen students’ collaborative learning in the AI era. 生成式人工智能（GenAI）正在重塑高等教育學生完成課業的方式。ChatGPT 等 GenAI 系統讓學生可在甚少與同儕互動的情況下獨自完成作業，或會削弱其溝通及自我反思能力，而這兩項能力對學生未來的學習及職業發展均十分重要。「以教為學」為回應這項風險提供了一條具潛力的途徑。研究顯示，當學生需要向新手同儕解釋概念並進行教學時，往往能取得較佳的學習成效，同時促進社交互動及元認知發展。 過往研究曾按「以教為學」理念開發可教導智能代理，即能從學生的教學中學習的「模擬學生」。雖然這類系統能帶來一定的學習效益，但其開發成本高昂，而且大多受預設規則所限制。GenAI 為建構可模擬同儕學生的可教導智能代理帶來新機遇，並可呈現多元的學生特徵，包括不同的先備知識水平及溝通風格，例如傾向提問或傾向直接提供答案。這些差異可形成不同的教學情境，促使學生因應對方的理解程度調整解釋方式、監察理解情況，並調節其教學及學習策略。與智能代理進行對話，亦可讓學生鍛鍊溝通及自我反思能力。 本研究項目旨在發展並驗證以 GenAI 驅動的可教導智能代理作為同儕學生的設計原則及實施方法。透過校準智能代理的行為，系統將呈現不同的先備知識水平及溝通風格。項目將於大學課堂進行隨機對照試驗，評估其對學生學習成效、學習動機及元認知的影響，並分析學生在一對一教學及三方互動情境中的參與模式和概念解釋表現。三方互動將包括兩種組合：兩名學生與一名模擬學生，以及一名學生與兩名模擬學生。試驗亦會探討模擬學生在先備知識及溝通風格上的差異如何影響學生的學習過程和成果。項目同時會分析互動模式隨時間的變化，以支援適應性機制的設計，從而維持學生投入並促進自我調節。 本研究將帶來概念、方法、實證及實務四方面的貢獻。概念上，研究將把「以教為學」延伸至 GenAI 支援的學習環境；方法上，研究將提出配置 GenAI 模型以模擬多元學生特徵的設計原則，並發展能反映學生如何教導模擬同儕及與其互動的過程導向測量指標；實證上，研究將透過隨機對照試驗，就學習成效、元認知及溝通表現提供實證證據；實務上，研究將提出可教導智能代理的設計原則，以及將其融入大學課堂的實施指引。所有研究成果將整合至一個開源平台，以促進研究成果在高等教育中的應用和推廣，並在人工智能時代加強學生的協作學習能力。

27610826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27610826.value: 交易與匿名之外：唐代代筆現象考論

27610826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27610826.value: Although widespread, ghostwriting tends to be regarded as a somewhat underhanded practice in contemporary society. In contrast, under the Tang 唐 dynasty (618–907), the practice of daibi 代筆 or daizu 代作—literally, “writing on behalf of another” and commonly translated as “ghostwriting”—permeated all strata of literate society. A significant portion of surviving Tang literature consists of ghostwritten works by a diverse array of authors, catering to diverse putative authors, and serving distinct purposes. Among them, indeed, are literary masterpieces. However, this significant Tang phenomenon remains under-researched, perhaps due to our contemporary disparagement of ghostwriting. This project, as the first comprehensive examination of Tang ghostwriting, attempts to reveal its prevalence, literary features, sociopolitical roles, and broader cultural implications. By undertaking a close reading of representative texts across genres, combined with theoretical frameworks and comparative perspectives, this study will uncover the literary and rhetorical features of Tang ghostwritten works. It will thoroughly investigate ghostwriters from diverse social backgrounds and, given that their identities were often known to the public, reveal the dual voices—that of the putative author and their own—conveyed in their works. Additionally, this project will demonstrate that ghostwriting extended beyond a mere service for the literarily unskilled or commercial transaction of literary expertise. By exploring the roles played by ghostwriting in Tang dynasty society and politics, this study will reveal the vital functions it served, such as seeking patronage, consolidating friendships, and legitimizing authority. Highlighting the roles of delegation, cooperation, and negotiation in Tang dynasty ghostwriting, the study will also draw parallels with contemporary discussions of authorship, authenticity, and the nature of writing. These insights will in turn contribute to modern debates on ghostwriting, including the emergence of ghostwriting facilitated by large language model (LLM)-based agents. Ultimately, this project will enhance our understanding of a neglected area of Tang literature and culture, the practice of ghostwriting, and the concepts of authorship and authenticity in both premodern and modern contexts. 現代社會往往將日常生活中普遍存在的代筆現象視為不甚光彩的行為。然而，代筆並非現代社會所獨有。早在唐代（618–907），代筆或代作之風便已滲透到文人社會的各個層面。現存唐代文獻中，有相當比例的作品由不同背景的文人代笔；他們在各种語境下，為不同身份的人操刀，其中不乏文學傑作。或許正因現代社會對代筆行為的輕視，這一重要的唐代文化現象至今未獲充分研究。 作為系統研究此現象的首次嘗試，本課題旨在揭示唐代代筆實踐的普遍性、文學屬性、社會政治功能及其更廣泛的文化意涵。研究將結合理論框架與比較視野，通過細讀不同文體的代表性文本，剖析唐代代筆作品的文學與修辭特徵。鑒於許多代筆者的身份在當時往往為公眾所知，本研究將在考察不同背景代筆者身份的基礎上，揭示代筆作品中名義作者與代筆者雙重聲音的交織與共振。同时，它將論證唐代代筆絕非僅限於為文采欠缺者提供的文字服務，亦非單純以文字換取錢財的交易行為。通過探究代筆在唐代社會政治中所起的不同作用，本研究將展現代筆具有獲取政治提攜、鞏固情誼、賦予權力正當性等重要功能。在強調委託、協作與協商於唐代代筆實踐中地位的同時，也將與當代關於作者身份、文本真實性與寫作本質的討論展開對話。這些觀點亦將為現代代筆議題——包括基於大語言模型的智能體所催生的新型代筆現象——提供有價值的歷史參照。 最終，本課題將深化學界對代筆這一長期被忽視的重要唐代文學現象的認識，並重新審視古代與現代語境中關於作者身份與文本真實性的核心命題。

27614926.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27614926.value: 評估香港設立判刑委員會的必要性與可行性

27614926.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27614926.value: Sentencing decisions are one of the most public-facing acts of the judiciary. Yet in many common law jurisdictions including Hong Kong, sentencing and its reform remain opaque, inconsistently structured, and undertheorised at the institutional level. The proposed project examines the necessity, feasibility and desirability of establishing a sentencing council or similar body in Hong Kong. Sentencing councils are bodies that provide guidance, advice, and information on sentencing to courts, governments, and the public. Sentencing Councils have been established in England and Wales, Scotland, Australia, and elsewhere to enhance consistency, transparency, and public confidence in the criminal justice system. However, jurisdictions such as Canada, New Zealand, and Hong Kong have either resisted such reforms or failed to institutionalise them. The reasons for this divergence and their implications remain underexplored. The proposed project fills in the literature gap. Drawing on legal doctrinal analysis and comparative studies, the project will map the institutional design and functions of sentencing bodies across selected jurisdictions. The proposed project will: 1) analyse why sentencing councils have emerged in some jurisdictions and not others; (2) develop a typology of existing sentencing institutions and evaluate their structures, functions, and limitations; (3) assess the existing sentencing framework in Hong Kong and identify institutional gaps; and (4) propose reform models suitable for Hong Kong’s legal and constitutional context. The research will map the institutional design, membership and mandate of sentencing bodies worldwide. Empirical methods, including surveys of participants in the criminal justice system and interviews, will examine stakeholder attitudes towards sentencing reform. The project will create a normative typology of sentencing institutions by categorising them according to structural and functional criteria, evaluating each jurisdiction with its unique sentencing reform mechanisms. The typology will assess indicators of institutional success, such as sustainability, adaptability, and insulation from short-term political pressures. Findings will be used to assess whether Hong Kong possesses the structural prerequisites for adopting a statutory sentencing council, a non-statutory advisory body, or a hybrid model to help the city develop its own unique path for sentencing reform. Hong Kong’s sentencing system, while rooted in appellate guidelines and precedent, lacks clear mechanisms, a data information system, or avenues for public consultation. Debates about sentencing consistency, transparency, and judicial discretion have intensified in recent years. By exploring feasible institutional reform options, this research will contribute significantly to both legal scholarship and sentencing reform development. 量刑決定是司法機構最直接面向公眾的行為之一。然而,在香港及眾多普通法司法管轄區,量刑及其改革至今仍鮮為人知、結構迴異,且在制度層面理論建構不足。本研究計劃旨在探討香港設立量刑委員會或類似機構的必要性、可行性與可取性。量刑委員會旨在就量刑事宜向法院、政府及公眾提供指引、意見及資訊。英格蘭及威爾斯、蘇格蘭、澳洲等地已相繼設立量刑委員會以提升刑事司法制度的一致性、透明度及公信力。然而,加拿大、新西蘭及香港等司法管轄區或對此類改革有所保留,或未能將其制度化。當中分歧的原因及其影響迄今仍未獲充分探討。本研究計劃正可填補此一文獻空白。本計劃將透過法律教義分析及比較研究,梳理選定司法管轄區量刑機構的制度設計與職能。 本計劃將:(一)分析量刑委員會何以在部分司法管轄區出現,而在其他地區則未有設立;(二)建構現有量刑機構的類型學,並評估其架構、職能及局限;(三)檢視香港現行量刑框架,識別其制度缺口;及(四)提出切合香港法律及憲制環境的改革模式。本計劃將梳理各地量刑機構的制度設計、成員組成及職權範圍,並透過實證研究,包括對刑事司法制度參與者進行問卷調查及訪談,以考察持份者對量刑改革的態度。 本計劃將按結構性及功能性準則對量刑機構進行分類,建構規範性類型學,並就各司法管轄區獨有的量刑改革機制作出評估。該類型學將評估制度成功的各項指標,包括可持續性、適應性,以及免受短期政治壓力影響的程度。研究結果將用以評估香港是否具備相應的結構性先決條件,以採納法定量刑委員會、非法定諮詢機構或混合模式,從而協助香港開拓其獨有的量刑改革路徑。香港的量刑制度植根於上訴法院量刑指引及判例,惟欠缺清晰機制、量刑數據資訊系統及公眾諮詢渠道。近年有關量刑一致性、透明度與司法酌情權的討論日益熾熱。透過探索切實可行的制度改革方案,本研究將對法律學術及量刑改革的發展作出重要貢獻。

27617326.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27617326.value: 砂漿：物質的脆弱與科學價值

27617326.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27617326.value: This project applies a history of science and knowledge approach to the weak material mortar. Mortar is a mixture of sand, water, and lime/cement, which hardens to bind masonry blocks, seal holes and gaps, and cover the surfaces of structures. Mortar joints, fillings, and coatings often appear to be the weakest points in buildings and sites in the inevitable processes of deterioration and damage. While industrial interests have driven scientific research to produce stronger mortar materials since the 18th century, conservation activities have also uncovered the diversity of natural knowledge in making and using mortars in human history. Yet this body of conservation knowledge remains on the margins of major sciences and the historiography of science. This project will revisit and recontextualise this body of knowledge anew. There are two problems the project aims to tackle. The first is the conceptual framework of “weak knowledge” discussed by some historians of science, which has overlooked material weakness as an epistemic dimension in knowledge production. The second concerns scientific value, which historians have often characterised through discourses on precision, quantification, and reproducibility—such concepts that reflect modern Western epistemology. Focusing on weak mortar, this project will conduct a historical examination of mortar technology not only within spheres of modern science but also in the conservation experiences of late imperial China. It will demonstrate how material weakness generated new knowledge and innovation under distinct epistemic conditions, and argue that care for vulnerability is a key value integral to the productions of scientific and rational knowledge under examination. Two primary sources will be used, complemented by fieldwork. The first is a little-studied corpus produced by modern scientists and engineers since 1839, focusing on weathering, erosion, decay, degradation, and deterioration of built environments. The second consists of Chinese local gazetteers compiled by literati elites in the 8th-20th centuries, containing records of decay, damage, and maintenance of historic sites. Historical methods and digital techniques will be employed to explore links between these sources. Fieldwork aims to situate the interplay of local and global knowledge and to further decolonise Western epistemologies. Particular attention will be paid to the World Heritage site The Palace Museum of Beijing and the marginalised countryside areas of Hong Kong. This project will historicise different perceptions and understandings of material weakness, decolonise sciences in China, and make a case for an inclusive historiography of knowledge. 本項目從科學史與知識史視角，探討「砂漿」作為建築材料的脆弱性。砂漿通常由砂、水與石灰或水泥混合而成，硬化後具備粘合磚石、填補孔隙、塗刷表層之功能。然而，在構築物與人造環境無可迴避的老化與壞損過程中，砂漿接縫、填料及塗層往往顯現為最脆弱之處。自十八世紀以來，工業需求與科學研究共同驅動了更強韌、耐久、高效的砂漿材料的研發；與此同時，文化資產保存的現代實踐與研究，亦展現出人類在歷史上製作與使用砂漿時所產生的多樣化的自然知識。遺憾的是，這套知識至今仍徘徊在主流科學與科學史書寫的邊緣，有必要對其進行全新的探討與脈絡重構。 有兩個宏觀問題構成本研究之核心關切。首先是部分科學史學家所論及的「弱知識」理論框架，該框架並未將「物質的脆弱性」列為知識生產中的一個重要認識論維度。二則是「科學價值」，主流科學史論述往往用精確性、量化性、可複製性等反映現代西方認識論的特徵與模式來加以界定。圍繞砂漿的物質脆弱性，本項目將比對現代科學範疇及中華帝國晚期以降的文物保存經驗，藉此在兩種知識體系內對砂漿技術進行歷史追蹤。通過論證物質的脆弱性如何在不同的知識和認識條件下激發新知與創新，我將闡明為何「對脆弱性的關懷」乃是研究所涉科學及其他理性知識生產中不可或缺的核心價值。 研究素材主要含兩大類基礎文獻、並輔以新的田野考察信息。自1839年以來，科學家與工程師針對歷史環境中的風化、侵蝕、腐朽、降解與退化現象進行過大量探討，但這類文獻至今少有人問津，此其一。其二則是八至二十世紀由中華文人士大夫編纂的地方志，亦對歷史環境和遺跡的退化、損毀與修繕有詳實紀錄。在歷史學方法的宏觀架構之下，我將運用多學科混合的數位技術與田野考察方法，來探尋上述知識體系間的關聯。田野考察將側重於在地知識與全球化知識體系間的溝通與裂縫，從而展開認識論層面的去殖民化探討。世界文化遺產地北京紫禁城與香港鄉郊地區是本項目重點關注的田野對象。 透過上述設計，我將對不同文化關於物質脆弱性的認知展開歷史書寫、推動中國科學史的去殖民化，並為構建更具包容性的全球知識史做出貢獻。

27617426.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27617426.value: 《抒情引擎：浪漫主義與維多利亞早期女性詩歌及工業想像》

27617426.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27617426.value: This project situates women’s poetry in Britain within the industrial, scientific, and technological transformations of the Romantic and early Victorian periods. While scholarship on literature and the Industrial Revolution has tended to foreground male authors and prose genres, women’s poetic engagements with industrialisation, mechanisation, and expanding knowledge networks remain critically underexplored. By bringing together better-known figures, such as Joanna Baillie and Elizabeth Barrett Browning, with lesser-known poets, many of whom are from the labouring classes, this study reconstructs the various ways in which women challenged the nineteenth-century masculinisation of technology and probed the imagined boundaries between human and nonhuman minds and bodies. Methodologically, the project combines close reading, archival recovery, and historicist contextualisation with perspectives from feminist theory, posthumanism, and the history and philosophy of technology. It examines how women’s poetry reimagined the relationship between humans and machines by using lyric (and other poetic) modes as a kind of technology, with rhythms and rhetorical framings that could both reflect and resist the age’s increasingly mechanical culture. Case studies range from the mythologised industrial landscapes of Anna Seward’s ‘Colebrook Dale’ (1810) and Eleanor Anne Porden’s 'The Veils' (1815); to descriptions of energetic bodies in Mary Robinson’s 'The Progress of Liberty' (1801) and Ann Yearsley’s 'A Poem on the Inhumanity of the Slave-Trade' (1788); to poetry by Letitia Elizabeth Landon, Caroline Norton, and Caroline Bowles Southey denouncing the factory system’s dehumanisation of women and children (Bowles, using the orientalist image of the Juggernaut in her poems, further brings wider questions about empire into the frame); to comparisons between industrial labour and poetic production in Elizabeth Barrett Browning’s 'Aurora Leigh' (1856) and poetry by women factory workers; to speculations about the “poetical science” of algorithms in the ground-breaking work of Ada Lovelace. By historicising nineteenth-century intersections of gender, imaginative writing, and technology, the study reframes contemporary debates on artificial intelligence, creativity, authenticity, and agency, revealing their deep Romantic roots. It contributes to the growing field of literature and technoscience, to the recovery of women’s writing, and to feminist and posthumanist understandings of our technological condition. Ultimately, it argues that Romantic thinking, defined not by nostalgia but by imagination and productive uncertainty, offers vital resources for engaging with the machines of our present and future. 本計畫將英國女性詩歌置於浪漫主義與維多利亞早期工業、科學與技術變革的脈絡之中。雖然探討文學與工業革命的學術研究往往側重於男性作家，但女性詩歌對工業化、機械化以及擴大中的知識網絡之介入，在學術界仍嚴重缺乏探討。藉由將較為知名的詩人（如喬安娜·貝利 [Joanna Baillie] 與伊麗莎白·巴雷特·白朗寧 [Elizabeth Barrett Browning]）與較不知名的詩人（其中許多來自勞工階級）並置，本研究重構了女性挑戰十九世紀科技男性化、並探索人類與非人類心靈及身體之間想像邊界的各種方式。 在方法論上，本計畫結合了文本細讀、檔案發掘與歷史主義脈絡化，並融入女性主義理論、後人類主義，以及科技史與科技哲學的視角。本計畫檢視女性詩歌如何將抒情（及其他詩歌）模式視為一種科技，藉由既能反映、亦能抵制該時代日益機械化文化的節奏與修辭框架，進而重新想像人與機器之間的關係。

27619126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27619126.value: 運用大型語言模型捕捉與理解日常決策中的人類式表徵

27619126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27619126.value: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming societies and industries, and it is also reshaping how cognitive and behavioral scientists study the mind. The advent of Large Language Models (LLMs) provides researchers with unprecedented opportunities to develop theories and tools that extend beyond human cognition. We argue that two key properties of LLMs make them especially valuable for understanding human decision-making and for training intelligent agents that behave in more human-like ways: (i) their capacity to rapidly simulate human decisions in silico, enabling scalable human experiments, and (ii) their flexibility to adapt quickly to specific scenarios through in-context learning and lightweight interventions that can steer behavior without retraining. Building on these properties, we aim to leverage LLMs to unlock large-scale human data collection in more naturalistic decision-making scenarios, without imposing additional time or effort on participants. Specifically, we will examine decisions with real-world relevance that involve risk, time, morality, and social interaction. To accomplish this, we will develop automation tools for running online behavioral experiments at scale, use crowdsourcing platforms for participant recruitment, and integrate LLMs to provide informative priors that guide human data collection. Our focus will be on characterizing how uncertainties are represented in these decisions and on using Bayesian models both to optimally design human experiments and to provide mechanistic accounts of human and LLM behavior. The resulting human data will also support closer alignment between humans and LLMs. We will explore sample-efficient and parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods to distill human data into LLMs, creating a mutually reinforcing research cycle: better-aligned LLMs will further accelerate human experimentation, while realigning AI models on improved human data will promote safer and more effective deployment in real-world contexts. Ultimately, the proposed project seeks to advance our theoretical understanding of both LLM and human behavior, enhance the design of automated behavioral experiments, and improve the human-likeness of LLMs, thereby contributing to the development of safer and more robust AI systems. The PI’s prior experience --- spanning (i) Bayesian models of cognition, (ii) large-scale online experiments on human strategic decisions, (iii) eliciting latent representations from humans and LLMs using Markov chain Monte Carlo, (iv) post-training LLMs with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, and (v) activation editing to steer LLM behavior --- provides a strong foundation for carrying out the proposed research. 人工智能（AI）正迅速改變社會與各行各業，同時亦重塑認知與行為科學家研究心智的方式。大型語言模型（LLM）的出現，為研究人員開發超越傳統人類認知研究範疇的理論與工具帶來了前所未有的機遇。我們認為，LLM 的兩項關鍵特性，使其特別有助於理解人類決策，以及訓練行為更接近人類的智能體：（1）能夠在計算環境中快速模擬人類決策，從而支援可擴展的大規模人類實驗；以及（2）能夠透過情境內學習和輕量級干預，迅速適應特定情境，並在毋須重新訓練的情況下引導其行為。建基於上述特性，本項目旨在運用 LLM，推動在更自然、更貼近日常生活的決策情境中大規模收集人類數據，而毋須參與者投入額外的時間或精力。具體而言，我們將研究涉及風險、時間、道德及社會互動，並與現實生活密切相關的決策。為實現此目標，我們將開發自動化工具，以大規模進行網上行為實驗；利用眾包平台招募參與者；並整合 LLM，以提供具資訊性的先驗分布，從而引導人類數據的收集。本項目將重點探討不確定性在這些決策中如何被表徵，並運用貝葉斯模型，一方面以最佳方式設計人類實驗，另一方面為人類與 LLM 的行為提供機制性解釋。所得的人類數據亦將有助於促進人類與 LLM 之間更緊密的對齊。我們將探索具樣本效率及參數效率的微調方法，將人類數據中的知識蒸餾至 LLM，從而建立一個相互促進的研究循環：與人類更妥善對齊的 LLM 將進一步加快人類實驗，而利用更優質的人類數據重新對齊 AI 模型，則有助於促進 AI 在現實情境中更安全、更有效地部署。總體而言，本項目旨在深化我們對 LLM 與人類行為的理論理解，改進自動化行為實驗的設計，並提升 LLM 的類人性，從而推動更安全、更穩健的 AI 系統發展。項目主持人過往在以下方面的研究經驗，為開展本項目奠定了堅實基礎：（1）認知的貝葉斯模型；（2）有關人類策略性決策的大規模網上實驗；（3）運用馬爾可夫鏈蒙地卡羅方法，提取人類與 LLM 的潛在表徵；（4）透過監督式微調及基於可驗證獎勵的強化學習，對 LLM 進行後訓練；以及（5）透過激活值編輯引導 LLM 的行為。

27619626.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27619626.value: 日本在北海道的殖民統治（1869–1905）

27619626.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27619626.value: My project examines the history of settler colonialism in Hokkaido: today Japan’s northernmost island and the unceded territories of the Indigenous Ainu people. While the Ainu were long recognized by the Tokugawa bakufu, in 1869 Japan's new Meiji government annexed Hokkaido outright, claiming their territories as terra nullius (“empty” or “ownerless” land). Thereafter, Japan’s colonization functioned through the dislocation and displacement of the Ainu. This included violent forms of physical removal such as forced migrations. However, it also took the form of discursive erasures including romantic pioneer myths that claimed settlers were heroically “reclaiming” the “virgin soil” of Ainu villages and tropes of the Ainu, spread throughout popular media and national textbooks, as stateless “barbarians”. I argue that, because the Ainu’s continuing presence revealed a fundamental contradiction at the heart of the terra nullius doctrine and thus undermined Japanese sovereignty in Hokkaido, this discourse became a crucial means for the Japanese state and common settlers alike to reaffirm claims to Ainu territories. In turn, it served to naturalize the forced removal of the Ainu from the land and legitimize the presence of Japanese settlers. Troublingly, conventional scholarship on Japanese colonialism in Hokkaido focuses overwhelmingly on the experiences of settlers, ignoring the Ainu or treating them purely as victims. Such scholarship, I argue, often tacitly reproduces the logics of terra nullius. Challenging received historiography, my research demonstrates that the Ainu not only persisted on the land but actively resisted Japanese colonization. Drawing on newspaper articles, petitions, interviews, and 20th century Ainu memoirs, I document the often-overlooked history of Ainu resistance against and non-compliance with colonial policy. This included physical confrontations between the Ainu and settlers, sizable organized protests in Hokkaido and Tokyo, and patterns of deliberate subversion. This resistance constituted a tangible threat to Japanese rule and, as a result, prompted the state to intensify its suppression of Ainu sovereignty. This led to other forms of dislocation which aimed to suppress the emerging Ainu anti-colonial movement, such as the state’s designation of the Ainu as “former aborigines” in need of “protection” and, on this basis, its suppression of their civil rights. 本項目旨在探討北海道（即日本最北端的島嶼，也是原住民愛努人的未經割讓領土）的定居者殖民主義歷史。愛努人雖長期為德川幕府所承認，但一八六九年日本新成立的明治政府直接兼併北海道，並將其領土宣稱為「無主之地」。其後，日本的殖民統治通過遷徙與驅逐愛努人來推行，當中包括強制移住等暴力形式的物理驅離，也包含論述性的抹除，例如浪漫化的開拓神話將定居者描繪成英勇「開墾」愛努村莊「處女地」的英雄，以及透過大眾媒體與國家教科書，將愛努人塑造成無國籍的「野蠻人」。 筆者主張，由於愛努人的持續存在，揭示了「無主之地」學說的核心矛盾，進而動搖了日本在北海道的主權；因此，這類論述便成為日本政府與一般定居者用以重申其對愛努領土主張的關鍵工具。此論述進而使強行驅離愛努人變得理所當然，並合法化了日本定居者在當地的存在。 令人遺憾的是，關於北海道日本殖民史的傳統學術研究，過度側重於定居者的經驗，而忽略愛努人，或僅將他們視為純粹的受害者。筆者認為，此類研究往往在無意間複製了「無主之地」的邏輯。為挑戰此種主流史觀，本研究證明了愛努人不僅持續生存在這片土地上，更積極抵抗日本的殖民統治。透過運用報紙文章、請願書、訪談及二十世紀愛努人的回憶錄，筆者記錄了長久被忽視的愛努族反抗與不服從殖民政策的歷史，其中包括愛努人與定居者之間的肢體衝突、在北海道與東京舉行的大規模有組織抗議，以及刻意顛覆殖民體制的行動。這些反抗行動對日本的統治構成了實質威脅，因此促使國家加強鎮壓愛努人的主權，進而引發其他形式的遷徙措施，旨在壓制新興的愛努族反殖民運動，例如國家將其指定為需要「保護」的「舊土人」，並以此為由剝奪其公民權利。

27619826.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27619826.value: 當工作擾亂生物時鐘：工作時間安排、生物時鐘失調、表觀遺傳老化與基因－環境交互作用

27619826.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27619826.value: Working-time arrangements, including nonstandard work schedules (e.g., evenings, nights, split/rotating shifts, and irregular hours) and long hours, are increasingly prevalent in 24/7 economies in the world and important contributors to health disparities. Yet our understanding of how such schedules “get under the skin” remains limited. Existing research has focused largely on self-reported outcomes such as stress, sleep quality, or subjective wellbeing, leaving molecular pathways to accelerated ageing and chronic disease in the dark. Moreover, most studies treat work schedules as static, single-point exposures and neglect household dynamics that lead to changes in work time arrangements over the life course. Much less is known on how the health risks of working-time arrangement interact with genetic predispositions across diverse social and demographic contexts. This project addresses these limitations through two complementary, interdisciplinary studies. We focus on two interrelated outcomes: (1) biological ageing, measured with epigenetic clocks capturing cumulative physiological wear-and-tear, and (2) obesity, a chronic disease with strong genetic underpinnings and established links to work stress and schedules. Study 1 investigates how trajectories of working-time arrangements, captured through repeated measures of weekly hours and timing over 18 years, relate to biological ageing. Using sequence analysis, we identify patterns such as stable standard hours, persistent long hours, or irregular shifts, and link these to DNA methylation data from about 3,600 participants in the UK Household Longitudinal Study. Study 2 examines whether long-run working-time trajectories moderate genetic susceptibility to higher body mass index (BMI). The BMI polygenic score, derived from UK Household Longitudinal Study genetic data, aggregates the weighted effects of 480 genome-wide significant genetic variants associated with BMI, providing a validated measure of genetic propensity to adiposity. The contribution of this project is threefold. First, it provides the first evidence on how dynamic, long-term work schedules affect molecular ageing and obesity, moving beyond static, self-reported outcomes. Second, it advances theories of life course inequality by demonstrating whether working-time arrangements accelerate biological wear-and-tear. Third, it generates evidence relevant for policy, including labour regulation, occupational health, and family wellbeing in societies with 24/7 economies. The insights offer a valuable test case for Hong Kong, where employees work the longest hours among OECD economies, while recognising institutional differences may shape how patterns are perceived. The project fills a critical gap in understanding how work and biology intersect and makes a unique contribution by bridging social science and molecular genetics to inform scholarship and practice. 隨著全球二十四小時運作經濟的發展，非標準工作時間安排（如晚班、夜班、輪班、拆班及不規則工時）以及長工時日益普遍，並逐漸成為健康不平等的重要來源。然而，目前對於工作時間安排如何透過生物機制影響健康的理解仍然有限。現有研究大多聚焦於壓力、睡眠品質及主觀幸福感等自陳健康指標，對其如何影響生物老化及慢性疾病等分子層面的機制仍缺乏系統性證據。此外，多數研究將工作時間視為單一時間點的靜態暴露，忽略家庭生命事件及生命歷程中工作時間安排的長期變化，也較少探討工作時間安排如何與個體的遺傳傾向交互作用，共同影響健康。 本研究透過兩項相互補充的跨學科研究，探討工作時間安排如何影響健康。研究聚焦於兩項密切相關的健康結果：（一）以表觀遺傳時鐘衡量的生物老化，反映個體長期累積的生理耗損；以及（二）肥胖，一種受遺傳因素影響顯著，且與工作壓力及工作時間安排密切相關的慢性疾病。 第一項研究利用英國家庭縱向研究（UK Household Longitudinal Study）上千名參與者長達18年的重複追蹤資料，結合每週工時及工作時段資訊，運用序列分析方法辨識不同的工作時間軌跡，例如穩定標準工時、持續長工時及持續輪班等，並分析其與DNA甲基化所測量之表觀遺傳老化的關聯。 第二項研究探討長期工作時間軌跡是否會改變個體對肥胖的遺傳易感性。研究將利用英國家庭縱向研究的基因資料建構身體質量指數（BMI）多基因風險分數，該分數整合480個與BMI顯著相關之全基因組遺傳變異，以評估個體的遺傳傾向，並檢驗不同工作時間安排是否會放大或減弱此遺傳風險。 本研究具有三項主要貢獻。首先，首次從長期、動態的工作時間安排角度，探討其對分子層次生物老化及肥胖的影響，突破過去依賴靜態及自陳健康指標的研究限制。其次，本研究將深化生命歷程健康不平等理論，闡明工作時間安排是否會加速生理耗損及影響遺傳風險的表現。最後，本研究將為勞動政策、職業健康及家庭福祉提供科學證據，支持二十四小時經濟下健康工作環境的政策制定。 研究結果亦將為香港提供重要參考。香港是全球工時最長的地區之一，雖然不同制度背景可能影響工作時間安排的形成與健康影響，本研究仍可為理解工作時間、生物老化及慢性疾病之間的關係提供重要啟示。透過結合社會科學與分子遺傳學方法，本研究將深化對工作與健康生物機制交互作用的理解，並為未來研究與政策制定提供新的實證基礎。

27620126.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27620126.value: 基層醫療促進肝臟篩查：成年糖尿病患者肝臟早期風險分層評估及精準轉診研究

27620126.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27620126.value: Liver disease is a rising but under-recognized burden among adults with diabetes, often progressing silently to advanced stages such as cirrhosis or hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Despite high prevalence—73% with fatty liver and 18% with fibrosis in Hong Kong Diabetes Register data—adherence to liver assessment remains poor, and hospital imaging capacity is constrained. Earlier precise referrals of liver assessment (for liver scarring or cancer risk) from primary care clinics—where people with diabetes already attend (e.g., RAMP-DM)—can overcome poor adherence and limited hospital capacity, raise timely scan completion and yield. The RAISE Liver Triage project proposes a scalable, risk-stratified referral pathway embedded within current RAMP-DM primary care program to address these gaps, by leveraging routine diabetes visits to prioritize liver assessment referrals using readily available clinical data. Objective 1 describes current liver assessment referral processes for adults with diabetes in Hong Kong Hospital Authority (HA) settings. This includes identifying who is referred, from which care settings (e.g., RAMP-DM, GOPC, Family Medicine Clinics), for which tests (e.g., ultrasound, FibroScan, biomarkers), and how long it takes to complete assessment. Objective 2 characterizes downstream outcomes among referred patients, including diagnosis stage, waiting time, treatment delays, hospital length of stay, readmission, and mortality. Objective 3 develops and validates a machine learning–based risk score and nomogram using routine data to guide precise referrals. The score will be embedded in the EHR to auto-populate referral forms and trigger reminders. Internal validation will include calibration, discrimination, and decision-curve analysis, while external validation will be conducted across three partner hospitals: HKU–Shenzhen Hospital, Guangdong Second Provincial General Hospital, and Gansu Wu Wei Traditional Chinese Medicine Hospital. Objective 4 evaluates equity and subgroup differences in referral completion and outcomes by sex, age, socioeconomic status, comorbidity profiles, and care setting. Stratified models and fairness checks will guide targeted interventions and safeguard against disparity amplification. Analytical methods will include descriptive statistics and multivariable models suited to outcome types—linear, logistic, Cox, and Poisson/negative binomial upon fitting. Success will be measured by increased scan adherence, reduced diagnostic delays, and improved patient outcomes. Dashboards will track key metrics to support continuous improvement and budget-impact planning. Aligned with the Primary Healthcare Blueprint and CDCC initiatives, this project offers a data-driven, policy-relevant solution to enhance liver health risk early detection and management from primary diabetes care.

27620226.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27620226.value: Human relationships are foundational to living a good life. Yet it is becoming increasingly difficult to know what good human relationships look like. How should one relate to others amidst deep political uncertainty or the likely significant social changes that will come with the implementation of new technologies like generative AI? To effectively answer questions like these it is necessary to conduct a philosophical investigation into the nature of human relationships and to articulate their ideal moral foundations. In this project, I will conduct such an investigation and articulate a philosophical framework for human relationships based on the work of Immanuel Kant. This framework will produce a monograph outlining character traits that are crucial to human flourishing and applying them to key features of everyday life. Kant’s published work is known for its emphasis on human dignity and rational thought. The framework developed here is grounded in these elements. Chapter one extends them further, reconstructing a virtue of rational sympathy based on material from Kant’s lectures and lesser-known texts. I argue that rational sympathy is an intellectual master virtue and is central to good moral character in the Kantian sense. In chapter two, I articulate an account of moral habit and improvement consistent with this account of sympathy, showing that Kantian ethics has the resources to explain ordinarily desirable features of the good life, contrary to objections from historical and contemporary thinkers. Chapter three then develops a novel account of moral worth, the core of virtuous action, consistent with this. Chapter four reconstructs an account of forgiveness as an imperfect duty and Kantian virtue that requires the development of humility, self-respect, and sympathy. Chapters five through seven focus on the moral features of everyday life: family, friendship, and professional roles. Chapter five reconstructs Kant’s account of marriage and the family to illuminate what Kantian moral psychology can say about these topics today. Chapter six examines the role of pleasure alongside moral duty in friendship. In it, I argue that Kantian duty is necessary to maintain worthwhile friendships and does not threaten or diminish their non-moral value. Chapter seven examines what it looks like to live with integrity in professional environments with significant moral uncertainty and distress, arguing that a Kantian conception of conscience is both necessary and well-suited to establish boundaries for moral action and responsibility. 人际关系是过上美好生活的基石。然而，要理解何为良好的人际关系，正变得日益困难。在政治局势充满深刻不确定性，或生成式人工智能等新技术应用将引发重大社会变革的背景下，人们应当如何与他人相处？要有效回答这些问题，必须对人际关系的本质进行哲学探究，并阐明其理想的道德基础。本项目将开展此类探究，并基于伊曼努尔·康德（Immanuel Kant）的著作构建一个关于人际关系的哲学框架。该框架将形成一部专著，概述对人类蓬勃发展至关重要的性格特质，并将这些特质应用于日常生活中的关键方面。康德的著作以强调人的尊严与理性思维而闻名；本文构建的框架正是建立在这些要素之上的。第一章进一步拓展了这些要素，利用康德的讲座记录及较少为人所知的文本，重构了“理性同情”（rational sympathy）这一德性。我主张，理性同情是一种统摄性的理智德性，对于康德意义上的良好道德品格至关重要。第二章阐述了与上述同情观相契合的道德习惯与道德提升理论，表明康德伦理学具备解释美好生活中那些通常被视为可贵特质的能力——这反驳了历史上及当代思想家提出的异议。第三章在此基础上，提出了一种关于“道德价值”（moral worth）——即德性行为之核心——的新颖解读。第四章将宽恕重构为一种“不完全义务”（imperfect duty）及康德式德性，指出其需要谦逊、自尊与同情心的培养。第五至七章聚焦于日常生活中的道德面向：家庭、友谊与职业角色。第五章重构了康德关于婚姻与家庭的论述，旨在阐明康德的道德心理学在当今语境下对这些议题的启示。第六章探讨了友谊中快乐与道德义务的关系。我主张，康德式的义务对于维系有价值的友谊是必要的，且并不会威胁或削弱友谊的非道德价值。第七章探讨了在充满重大道德不确定性与困境的职业环境中，如何保持正直操守；我主张，康德关于“良知”（conscience）的观念，对于确立道德行为与责任的界限既必要又适切。

27621026.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27621026.value: 職涯發展學習是否影響早期職涯成功？探討大學生過渡至職場的縱向研究

27621026.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27621026.value: University students today face an increasingly competitive and unpredictable economic environment. Given the role of higher education in shaping young people’s career trajectories and life plans, are universities dedicating the right resources to career development learning (CDL)? Does behavioural, cognitive, and affective engagement in CDL activities, such as internships and career coaching, effectively equip students with career development self-efficacy, clarify their career goals, and help them achieve early career success? Conversely, are students who are less proactive in CDL at a disadvantage, or do they achieve early career success via other pathways and experiences? In light of the rapidly evolving career landscape, there is an urgent need to update our understanding of CDL experiences, career development self-efficacy and early career success and setback, particularly from the perspectives of students and graduates. These key stakeholders can provide first-hand insights into the dynamic changes occurring within contemporary society. This proposed project will be a longitudinal mixed-methods study to investigate the impact of CDL on Hong Kong (HK) university students’ early career success/setback. Survey data will be collected in two waves from 1800 university students across four universities. A quantitative approach will be used to examine the relationship between students’ engagement in CDL, their self-efficacy in career development, career goal clarity, and early career success. At the same time, a qualitative multiple case study approach will be used to examine the university-to-work transition experiences of at least 13 students exhibiting different levels of engagement in CDL. These students will be tracked for a year, during which video reflections will be collected using an innovative online platform (i.e. Indeemo), which allows for the collection of real-time insights into the lived experiences of graduates navigating the early stages of their career. The analysis will focus on their paths to achieving early career success or their experiences with early career setback,and how these outcomes are influenced by their level of engagement with CDL,their self-efficacy in career development,and their career goal clarity. While previous research tends to focus on career success,the proposed project challenges this “success-only” narrative by exploring both early career success and setbacks. Findings will not only contribute to the conceptualization of youth career development in HK but can also inform education and government policy recommendations.This will ensure resources are directed in a targeted and meaningful way to better assist the next generation in realizing their aspirations and potential.
